verse_text:
कथं ज्ञानमवाप्नोति कथं मुक्तिर्भविष्यति ।
वैराग्यं च कथं प्राप्तमेतद् ब्रूहि मम प्रभो ॥
translation: ज्ञान कैसे प्राप्त होता है ? मुक्ति कैसे होती है ? और वैराग्य कैसे प्राप्त होता है ? प्रभु ! यह मुझसे कहिये।
english_translation: How does one attain knowledge? How does liberation happen? And how is dispassion achieved? O Lord, please tell me this.
essence: The seeker's first act is to find the right question.
simple_meaning: King Janaka asks his teacher Ashtavakra three essential questions: how to gain true knowledge, how to achieve freedom, and how to cultivate dispassion toward worldly things.
insight: Dispassion is not a side-effect of wisdom — it is listed alongside knowledge and liberation as equally sought. The three arise together or not at all.
modern_relevance: Most people ask: 'How do I get what I want?' Janaka asked: 'How do I know what is real?' The entire quality of a life pivots on this shift. Stop optimizing answers to the wrong questions. Ask the right ones first.
speaker: Janaka

verse_text:
मुक्तिमिच्छसि चेत्तात विषयान् विषवत्त्यज ।
क्षमार्जवदयातोषसत्यं पीयूषवद् भज ॥
translation: मुक्ति चाहता है तो विषयों को विष के समान छोड़ दे और क्षमा, दया, सरलता, सन्तोष और सत्य को अमृत के समान सेवन कर।
english_translation: If you desire liberation, my child, abandon sense objects as poison, and embrace forgiveness, simplicity, compassion, contentment, and truth as nectar.
essence: Trade the poison of craving for the nectar of simplicity and truth.
simple_meaning: Ashtavakra's first answer is simple and direct: if you want liberation, treat sense cravings like poison, and live on the nectar of forgiveness, simplicity, compassion, contentment, and truth.
insight: The five qualities listed — forgiveness, simplicity, compassion, contentment, truth — are not practices to achieve liberation. They are themselves the experience of it.
modern_relevance: We scroll, consume, stimulate, and repeat. Ashtavakra says every such loop is a small dose of poison. Not because pleasure is evil, but because chasing it ties us to the wheel of wanting. The cure isn't deprivation — it's a different kind of nourishment.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
न पृथ्वी न जलं नाग्निर्न वायुर्द्यौर्न वा भवान् ।
एषां साक्षिणमात्मानं चिद्रूपं विद्धि मुक्तये ॥
translation: तू न पृथ्वी है, न जल है, न अग्नि है, न वायु है, न आकाश है । मुक्ति के लिए अपने को इन सबका साक्षी चैतन्यरूप जान।
english_translation: You are not earth, not water, not fire, not air, not space. For liberation, know yourself as the witness of all these — as pure awareness, the light of consciousness.
essence: You are the witness of all experience, not the experience itself.
simple_meaning: Ashtavakra says: you are none of the five elements that make up the body or the world. You are the pure awareness that witnesses them all. This recognition is liberation.
insight: Liberation isn't becoming the witness — it's recognizing you never stopped being it. The practice is seeing through the mistaken identification, not building a new one.
modern_relevance: Modern psychology confirms: we over-identify with thoughts, emotions, and body-sensations as 'me'. Meditation traditions worldwide exist to cultivate the observer stance. Ashtavakra collapses this to a single pointer: the witness is already free. You are already that.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
यदि देहं पृथक् कृत्य चिति विश्राम्य तिष्ठसि ।
अधुनैव सुखी शान्तो बन्धमुक्तो भविष्यसि ॥
translation: यदि देह को अपने से अलग कर और चैतन्य में विश्राम कर स्थित है तो अभी ही सुखी, शान्त और बन्ध-मुक्त हो जाएगा।
english_translation: If you set the body apart and rest in pure awareness, you will this very moment become happy, peaceful, and free from all bondage.
essence: Rest in awareness this instant — freedom is not waiting ahead.
simple_meaning: If you stop identifying with the body and simply rest in the awareness that you are, you become free, happy, and peaceful — not eventually, but this very instant.
insight: The phrase 'adhunaiva' — this very moment — is not poetic. It is the central technical claim of the Ashtavakra Gita: liberation is available now, not as a future attainment.
modern_relevance: We have a productivity mindset about spirituality too: practice enough and eventually you'll arrive. Ashtavakra dismantles this. The awareness that reads these words right now is already the free awareness. The only thing between you and freedom is misidentification — and misidentification dissolves in the instant it is clearly seen.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
न त्वं विप्रादिको वर्णो नाश्रमी नाक्षगोचरः ।
असङ्गोऽसि निराकारो विश्वसाक्षी सुखी भव ॥
translation: तू ब्राह्मण आदि वर्ण नहीं है और न तू किसी आश्रम वाला है, न आँख आदि इन्द्रियों का विषय है । तू असंग, निराकार और विश्व का साक्षी है, ऐसा जानकर सुखी हो।
english_translation: You are not any caste or social stage of life. You are not perceived by the senses. You are unattached, formless, the witness of the universe. Knowing this, be happy.
essence: You witness the universe. No label can contain the witness.
simple_meaning: You are not your social role, your body, or what your senses experience. You are the formless, unattached awareness that witnesses the whole universe. Happiness is the natural result of recognizing this.
insight: The instruction to 'be happy' after the stripping away of identity is not advice — it is a description of what naturally happens when misidentification drops.
modern_relevance: We exhaust ourselves building and defending identities — professional, political, cultural. Ashtavakra says all of it is something witnessed by the real you. Not because identity is evil but because you are far larger than any of it. The relief of this recognition is, literally, happiness.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
धर्माधर्मौ सुखं दुःखं मानसानि न ते विभो ।
न कर्तासि न भोक्तासि मुक्त एवासि सर्वदा ॥
translation: हे विभो ! धर्म और अधर्म, सुख और दुःख मन के हैं । तेरे लिए नहीं । तू न कर्ता है, न भोक्ता है । तू तो सर्वदा मुक्त ही है ।
english_translation: O all-pervading one! Virtue and vice, pleasure and pain belong to the mind, not to you. You are neither the doer nor the experiencer. You are eternally free.
essence: You are neither doer nor sufferer — eternally free.
simple_meaning: Virtue, sin, pleasure, and pain belong to the mind. The real you is neither the one who acts nor the one who suffers the consequences. You have always been free.
insight: This verse is not moral nihilism. Dharma still matters — but its weight belongs to the mind, not to the ground of awareness. The distinction between moral mind and free awareness is the whole architecture of the Gita.
modern_relevance: The crushing weight of guilt, regret, and pride — all rest on the assumption 'I did this'. The Ashtavakra Gita doesn't encourage irresponsibility; it points to something deeper: behind all action is a witnessing awareness that was never implicated in the action. Surrender here is dropping the claim of authorship over your life's story.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
एको द्रष्टासि सर्वस्य मुक्तप्रायोऽसि सर्वदा ।
अयमेव हि ते बन्धो द्रष्टारं पश्यसीतरम् ॥
translation: तू एक सबका द्रष्टा है और सदा ही मुक्त है । तेरा बन्धन यही है कि तू अपने को छोड़कर दूसरे को द्रष्टा देखता है।
english_translation: You are the one seer of all, and ever-free. Your bondage consists only in this: you see the seer as other — as something apart from yourself.
essence: You are the seer. Seeking the seer is the only bondage.
simple_meaning: You are the one witnessing awareness of all experience, and you are always free. The only trap is when you treat the seer — awareness itself — as something to be found outside yourself.
insight: Bondage has a single cause in this system: mistaken attribution — believing the witness is an object to be found rather than the subject doing all finding.
modern_relevance: The spiritual marketplace is full of techniques, teachers, and systems for finding yourself. Ashtavakra says: the looking is the problem. Every moment of looking reinforces the illusion that awareness is elsewhere. The moment seeking stops, what you were looking for is obvious — it was looking all along.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अहं कर्तेत्यहंमानमहाकृष्णाहिदंशितः ।
नाहं कर्तेति विश्वासामृतं पीत्वा सुखी भव ॥
translation: ‘मैं कर्ता हूँ’, ऐसा अहंकाररूपी विशाल काले सर्प से दंशित हुआ तू, ‘ मैं कर्ता नहीं हूँ’, ऐसे विश्वास रूपी अमृत को पीकर सुखी हो।
english_translation: You have been bitten by the great black serpent of ego — the belief 'I am the doer.' Drink the nectar of the conviction 'I am not the doer' and be happy.
essence: Release the claim of doership — that is the only antidote.
simple_meaning: The ego-belief 'I am the one doing everything' is like a venomous snake bite. The antidote is the clear conviction: 'I am not the doer.' This recognition brings happiness.
insight: The serpent metaphor is precise: ego doesn't kill immediately. It poisons slowly — through accumulating self-importance, defensiveness, and the exhaustion of constantly being the author of your life.
modern_relevance: Anxiety, guilt, burnout, and pride all share a common root: the belief that 'I am responsible for all of this.' Surrendering doership isn't resignation — it's what happens when you stop standing in your own way. The energy that went into self-management becomes available for actual living.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
एको विशुद्धबोधोऽहमिति निश्चयवह्निना ।
प्रज्वाल्याज्ञानगहनं वीतशोकः सुखी भव ॥
translation: ‘मैं एक विशुद्ध बोध हूँ’ ऐसी निश्चय रूपी अग्नि से गहन अज्ञान को जलाकर तू शोक रहित हुआ सुखी हो।
english_translation: The self is witness, all-pervading, whole, one, free, pure awareness, actionless, unattached, desireless, peaceful. It only appears as a worldly being due to illusion.
essence: The self is already whole, free, and peaceful — illusion alone obscures it.
simple_meaning: The true self is the witness, all-pervading, complete, free, pure awareness — inherently peaceful and desireless. It only seems to be caught in worldly suffering due to illusion.
insight: Nine attributes, one conclusion: the illusion that you are a suffering worldly being is precisely that — an illusion. What is real is already complete.
modern_relevance: Equanimity is often taught as a skill to cultivate — breathe deeply, practice acceptance, train your nervous system. Ashtavakra says equanimity is not cultivated, it is recognized. The self is already santa (peaceful) — the apparent turbulence is in the mind, not in awareness itself. The practice is seeing through the illusion, not building a better response to it.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
यत्र विश्वमिदं भाति कल्पितं रज्जुसर्पवत् ।
आनन्दपरमानन्दः स बोधस्त्वं सुखं भव ॥
translation: यहाँ यह विश्व रस्सी में सर्प के समान भासता है । यही आनन्द-परमानन्द रूपी बोध है । अतः तू सुखपूर्वक विचर ।
english_translation: From ignorance of the self, the world appears. From knowledge of the self, it ceases to appear. Just as a snake appears from not knowing the rope, and disappears when the rope is recognized.
essence: Know yourself and the world's bewildering weight dissolves instantly.
simple_meaning: When we don't know our true nature, the world seems solid, binding, and real in an overwhelming way. When we know ourselves as awareness, the world continues but no longer binds. Like mistaking a rope for a snake in dim light — the rope was always a rope.
insight: The metaphor is not about making the world disappear. It is about the difference between seeing through fearful ignorance versus seeing through the clarity of recognized awareness. The world remains; suffering doesn't.
modern_relevance: We speak of 'perspective shifts' and 'reframes' in therapy and coaching. The Ashtavakra Gita says the deepest shift is not from one perspective to another, but from ignorance of the witness to recognition of it. That shift changes everything without changing anything.
speaker: Janaka

verse_text:
मुक्ताभिमानी मुक्तो हि बद्धो बद्धाभिमान्यपि ।
किंवदन्तीह सत्येयं या मतिः सा गतिर्भवेत् ॥
translation: मुक्ति का अभिमानी मुक्त है, और बद्ध का अभिमानी बद्ध है । यहाँ यह किवदन्ती सत्य ही है कि जैसी मति वैसी ही गति होती है ।
english_translation: This whole universe is pervaded by you and strung in you. You are pure, awakened awareness in truth. Do not fall into smallness of mind.
essence: The universe is within you. Live from that truth, not from smallness.
simple_meaning: The entire universe exists within your awareness and is threaded through it. Your true nature is pure, awakened consciousness. Don't fall into small, cramped thinking.
insight: This verse connects vairagya (dispassion) to self-knowledge rather than to world-rejection. You become dispassionate not by hating the world but by recognizing you contain it.
modern_relevance: Anxiety contracts. Recognition expands. Most strategies for dealing with anxiety try to manage the contraction. Ashtavakra says the contraction itself is based on error — the error of identifying with the small self. When the error is corrected, the contraction has nowhere to go.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
आत्मा साक्षी विभुः पूर्ण एको मुक्तश्चिदक्रियः ।
असङ्गो निःस्पृहः शान्तो भ्रमात्संसारवानिव ॥
translation: आत्मा साक्षी है, व्यापक है, पूर्ण है, एक है, मुक्त है, चैतन्यस्वरूप है, क्रियारहित है, असंग है, निस्पृह है, शान्त है । यह भ्रम से संसारी जैसा भासता है।
english_translation: Be without expectation, without modification, self-sufficient, with a cool heart. Be of unfathomable intelligence, undisturbed — established in pure awareness alone.
essence: Coolness, depth, undisturbed awareness — these are one thing, not many.
simple_meaning: Become free of expectations and reactions, self-sufficient and internally cool. Be of unfathomable depth and undisturbed equanimity, grounded entirely in pure awareness.
insight: 'Cin-matra-vasana' is the key phrase — established in pure awareness alone. Not partly in awareness and partly in distraction. The instruction is total.
modern_relevance: We optimize for peak performance, emotional intelligence, resilience. All of these have their place. But Ashtavakra points to something quieter: the person whose baseline is pure awareness doesn't need to manage their emotions — the emotions arise in a space so large they simply pass through without sticking.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
कूटस्थं बोधमद्वैतमात्मानं परिभावय ।
आभासोऽहं भ्रमं मुक्त्वा भावं बाह्यमथान्तरम् ॥
translation: मैं अभासरूप हूँ’ ऐसे भ्रम को एवं बाहर-भीतर के भाव को छोड़कर तू कूटस्थ बोधरूप एवं अद्वैत, आत्मा का विचार कर।
english_translation: Abandon the illusion of 'I am a mere appearance' and the feelings of inside and outside; contemplate the immutable awareness that is non-dual, the true self.
essence: The true self is the unchanging awareness beyond all illusions of appearance and inner or outer feelings.
simple_meaning: Stop believing that you are just an appearance and the feelings of inside or outside. Instead, focus on the unchanging, non-dual true self.
insight: It shifts your attention from fleeting feelings and roles to the unchanging awareness that you truly are.
modern_relevance: When your identity feels fragmented by your changing moods or roles, this reminds you that your true self is steady beneath all appearances.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
देहाभिमानपाशेन चिरं बद्धोऽसि पुत्रक ।
बोधोऽहं ज्ञानखड्गेन तन्निकृत्य सुखी भव ॥
translation: हे पुत्र ! तू बहुत काल से देहाभिमान के पाश से बँधा हुआ है । उसी पाश को ‘मैं बोध हूँ’ इस ज्ञान की तलवार से काटकर तू सुखी हो ।
english_translation: O son, you have long been bound by the chain of attachment to the body. Cut that chain with the sword of 'I am awareness' and be happy.
essence: Freedom comes by cutting attachment to the body through recognizing pure awareness.
simple_meaning: You have been trapped by identifying with your body for a long time. Recognize yourself as pure awareness and free yourself to be happy.
insight: It teaches you to shift identity from the changing body to the unchanging awareness beneath it.
modern_relevance: When stress feels like it’s rooted in your physical identity or appearance, this verse reminds you that your true self is beyond the body, offering lasting peace.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
निःसङ्गो निष्क्रियोऽसि त्वं स्वप्रकाशो निरञ्जनः ।
अयमेव हि ते बन्धः समाधिमनुतिष्ठति ॥
translation: तू असंग है, क्रिया रहित है, स्वयंप्रकाश है और निरञ्जन है । तेरा बन्धन यही है कि तू समाधि के लिए अनुष्ठान करता है।
english_translation: You are detached, inactive, self-illuminating, and stainless; your bondage is that you practice for samadhi.
essence: You are already free; your bondage is trying to achieve freedom.
simple_meaning: You are naturally detached and pure, but you bind yourself by trying to practice to reach complete stillness.
insight: It shifts the mind from striving for freedom to recognizing freedom is already present without effort.
modern_relevance: You may feel stuck chasing calm or peace, not realizing that your striving itself blocks the natural quiet you seek.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः ।
शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥
translation: यह संसार तुझमें व्याप्त है, तुझी में पिरोया है । यथार्थतः तू चैतन्यस्वरूप है । अतः क्षुद्रचित्त को मत प्राप्त हो।
english_translation: This entire world is pervaded by you and woven within you in truth. You are the pure essence of the discerning mind; do not be taken by petty thoughts.
essence: You are pure clarity pervading all; do not be caught by trivial thoughts.
simple_meaning: You are the pure, clear essence that fills and connects everything; don't get distracted by small, trivial thoughts.
insight: Shift your focus from petty mental clutter to the vast, clear essence that you truly are.
modern_relevance: During moments when your mind is cluttered with minor worries or distractions, this reminds you that your true self is untouched clarity beyond them.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
निरपेक्षो निर्विकारो निर्भरः शीतलाशयः ।
अगाधबुद्धिरक्षुब्धो भव चिन्मात्रवासनः ॥
translation: तू निरपेक्ष, निर्विकार, स्वनिर्भर है । शान्ति और मुक्ति का स्थान है, अगाध बुद्धिरूप है, क्षोभ-शून्य है । अतः चैतन्यमात्र में निष्ठा वाला हो।
english_translation: You are impartial, unchanging, self-reliant, with a calm mind; your wisdom is profound and undisturbed, established solely in pure awareness.
essence: Your true self is calm, unshaken wisdom resting in pure awareness.
simple_meaning: You are impartial and unchanging with a calm mind. Your wisdom is deep and undisturbed, firmly rooted in pure awareness.
insight: It teaches you to identify with the steady, peaceful witness beneath all fluctuations of mind and circumstance.
modern_relevance: When stress makes your thoughts whirl and your emotions sway, remember you can find a calm, steady place deep inside, untouched by turmoil.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
साकारमनृतं विद्धि निराकारं तु निश्चलम् ।
एतत्तत्त्वोपदेशेन न पुनर्भवसम्भवः ॥
translation: साकार को मिथ्या जान, निराकार को निश्चल जान । इस तत्व के उपदेश से संसार में पुनः उत्पत्ति नहीं होती।
english_translation: Know the manifested as false and the unmanifested as steady; through this truth, rebirth ceases.
essence: The changing world is false; only the unchanging reality is true and free.
simple_meaning: The visible, changing world is illusory, while the unchanging reality within is steady and true.
insight: This verse shifts your view from trusting outer appearances to recognizing the inner unchanging reality.
modern_relevance: When your moods and situations keep shifting, remember the steady part of you that remains untouched inside.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
यथैवादर्शमध्यस्थे रूपेऽन्तः परितस्तु सः ।
तथैवाऽस्मिन् शरीरेऽन्तः परितः परमेश्वरः ॥
translation: जिस तरह दर्पण अपने में प्रतिबिम्बित रूप के भीतर और बाहर स्थित है । उसी प्रकार परमात्मा इस शरीर के भीतर और बाहर स्थित है।
english_translation: Just as a mirror exists both within and around the reflected image, the supreme being exists both inside and outside the body.
essence: The supreme being exists inseparably both within and around your body, like a mirror with its reflection.
simple_meaning: The supreme being is present inside your body and also all around it, like a mirror and its reflected image.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as isolated to recognizing the divine as inseparable from your entire being and environment.
modern_relevance: When you look in the mirror, you see yourself inside the glass and your image around it — your true self is just as near, both inside and all around you.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
एकं सर्वगतं व्योम बहिरन्तर्यथा घटे ।
नित्यं निरन्तरं ब्रह्म सर्वभूतगणे तथा ॥
translation: जिस प्रकार सर्वव्यापी एक आकाश घट के भीतर और बाहर स्थित है, उसी तरह नित्य और निरन्तर ब्रह्म सब भूतों में स्थित है।
english_translation: Just as the all-pervading one sky exists inside and outside the pot, so the eternal and continuous Brahman exists in all beings.
essence: The eternal reality is fully present everywhere, both within and outside all beings.
simple_meaning: The eternal reality is everywhere, both inside and outside all creatures, just like the sky is inside and outside a pot.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as separate to recognizing an unbroken, ever-present reality within and beyond all forms.
modern_relevance: When you feel alone or separated, remember that the same vast presence you sense outside also fills your being completely.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अहो निरञ्जनः शान्तो बोधोऽहं प्रकृतेः परः ।
एतावन्तमहं कालं मोहेनैव विडम्बितः ॥
translation: मैं निरञ्जन हूँ, शान्त हूँ, बोध हूँ, प्रकृति के परे हूँ, आश्चर्य है । किन्तु मैं इतने काल तक मोह के द्वारा ठगा गया हूँ ।
english_translation: I am stainless, peaceful, awareness beyond nature; yet it is astonishing how long I have been deceived by confusion.
essence: You are pure awareness beyond nature, despite long deception by confusion.
simple_meaning: You are pure, peaceful awareness beyond the changing world, but you have been misled by confusion for a long time.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with confusion to recognizing your pure, unchanging awareness.
modern_relevance: After years of self-doubt and mental noise, you suddenly glimpse that your true self was never harmed, only obscured.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
यथा प्रकाशयाम्येको देहमेनं तथा जगत् ।
अतो मम जगत्सर्वमथवा न च किञ्चन ॥
translation: जैसे इस देह को मैं अकेला ही प्रकाशित करता हूँ, वैसे ही संसार को भी प्रकाशित करता हूँ । इसलिए तो मेरा सम्पूर्ण संसार है अथवा कुछ भी नहीं ।
english_translation: Just as I alone illuminate this body, in the same way I illuminate the entire world; therefore, the whole world is mine or nothing at all.
essence: Your awareness illuminates your body and the entire world as one unified light.
simple_meaning: You shine your own body and the entire world in the same way, so everything is either your world or nothing.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as isolated to recognizing your awareness pervades all experience.
modern_relevance: When you notice the awareness in your own body, you can realize that same awareness is present everywhere around you.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
स शरीरमहो विश्वं परित्यज्य मयाधुना ।
कुतश्चित् कौशलाद् एव परमात्मा विलोक्यते ॥
translation: आश्चर्य है कि शरीर सहित विश्व को त्यागकर किसी कुशलता से ही अब मैं परमात्मा को देखता हूँ ।
english_translation: It is surprising that, having abandoned the body and the world, I now perceive the supreme being only by some skill.
essence: Leaving behind the body and world alone doesn't show the supreme; refined skill is needed.
simple_meaning: After giving up identification with the body and world, perceiving the supreme requires a special skill or insight.
insight: It teaches that renunciation alone isn't enough; cultivating refined perception is essential to recognize the true self.
modern_relevance: You might step back from distractions and still find it hard to grasp deeper truths without a new way of seeing.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
यथा न तोयतो भिन्नास्तरङ्गाः फेनबुद्बुदाः ।
आत्मनो न तथा भिन्नं विश्वमात्मविनिर्गतम् ॥
translation: जैसे जल से तरंग, फेन और बुदबुदा भिन्न नहीं है, वैसे ही विश्व आत्मा से भिन्न नहीं है किन्तु आत्मा से ही निकला हुआ है।
english_translation: Just as waves, foam, and bubbles are not separate from water, the world is not separate from the true self but emerges from it.
essence: The world is inseparable from the true self, like waves inseparable from water.
simple_meaning: The world is not different from your true self; it arises from it just like waves come from water.
insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as isolated to seeing yourself as inseparable from everything around you.
modern_relevance: When you face challenges or joys, remember they rise from the same source as your true being, never truly apart from you.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
तन्तुमात्रो भवेद् एव पटो यद्वद् विचारितः ।
आत्मतन्मात्रमेवेदं तद्वद् विश्वं विचारितम् ॥
translation: जैसे विचार करने पर वस्त्र तन्तु मात्र ही होता है, वैसे ही विचार करने से यह संसार आत्मसत्ता मात्र ही है।
english_translation: Just as a cloth is only threads when examined, the entire world is only the essence of the true self when contemplated.
essence: Everything you see is woven from the essence of your true self.
simple_meaning: Looking closely at cloth reveals only threads. Similarly, reflecting deeply on the world reveals it as nothing but the essence of your true self.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing the world as separate things to recognizing it as expressions of one essence.
modern_relevance: When you analyze a complex situation or relationship, you often find simpler, fundamental truths beneath the surface that shape everything.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
यथैवेक्षुरसे क्लृप्ता तेन व्याप्तैव शर्करा ।
तथा विश्वं मयि क्लृप्तं मया व्याप्तं निरन्तरम् ॥
translation: जैसे ईख के रस से बनी हुई शर्करा ईख के रस में व्याप्त है, वैसे ही मुझसे बना हुआ संसार मुझमें भी व्याप्त है।
english_translation: Just as sugar made from sugarcane is pervaded by the juice of the sugarcane, similarly the world made from me is pervaded by me continuously.
essence: Everything in the world exists within you as an inseparable expression of your true self.
simple_meaning: Everything in the world exists within you just as sugar is fully present in sugarcane juice.
insight: It shifts your perception from separation to unity, seeing yourself as the container and essence of all experience.
modern_relevance: When you realize that people, places, and things are all expressions of your own inner being, feeling disconnected softens.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
आत्मज्ञानाज्जगद् भाति आत्मज्ञानान्न भासते ।
रज्ज्वज्ञानादहिर्भाति तज्ज्ञानाद् भासते न हि ॥
translation: आत्मा के अज्ञान से संसार भासता है, आत्मा के ज्ञान नहीं भासता है । जैसे रस्सी के अज्ञान से सर्प भासता है, उसके अज्ञान से नहीं भासता है।
english_translation: The world appears due to ignorance of the true self; it does not appear due to knowledge of the true self. Just as a snake appears because of ignorance about the rope, it does not appear due to knowledge of the rope.
essence: Illusions arise from ignorance of the true self, not from its knowledge.
simple_meaning: The world seems real only when you do not truly know yourself. When you have real knowledge of yourself, the world’s illusion disappears, like mistaking a rope for a snake.
insight: It teaches you to question your perceptions and recognize that confusion comes from misunderstanding your own true nature.
modern_relevance: You might panic seeing a shadow or misunderstanding a situation, but when you clearly understand, fear and confusion vanish.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
प्रकाशो मे निजं रूपं नातिरिक्तोऽस्म्यहं ततः ।
यदा प्रकाशते विश्वं तदाहं भास एव हि ॥
translation: प्रकाश मेरा निजी स्वरूप है । मैं उससे भिन्न नहीं हूँ । जब संसार प्रकाशित होता है तब वह मेरे ही से प्रकाशित होता है ।
english_translation: Light is my own true nature; I am not separate from it. When the world is illuminated, it shines through me.
essence: Your true nature is inseparable light that illuminates the entire world.
simple_meaning: Your essential self is pure light, not separate from it. When the world lights up, it does so through your own shining nature.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as separate to realizing you are the source of illumination itself.
modern_relevance: When you feel your own clarity or inspiration, recognize it as the same light that brings life and color to everything around you.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अहो विकल्पितं विश्वमज्ञानान्मयि भासते ।
रूप्यं शुक्तौ फणी रज्जौ वारि सूर्यकरे यथा ॥
translation: आश्चर्य है कि कल्पित संसार अज्ञान से मुझे ऐसा भासता है जैसे सीपी में चाँदी, रस्सी में साँप, सूर्य की किरणों में जल भासता है।
english_translation: How strange that the imagined world appears to me through ignorance, like silver in an oyster, a snake in a rope, or water in sun rays.
essence: The world appears real because of confusion, but it is only a mistaken image.
simple_meaning: The world you experience is a mistaken appearance caused by confusion, like seeing silver in an oyster or a snake in a rope.
insight: It teaches you to question your perceptions and recognize that appearances can be misleading illusions.
modern_relevance: You glance at a shadow and momentarily mistake it for a person, realizing later it was just a trick of light and mind.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
मत्तो विनिर्गतं विश्वं मय्येव लयमेष्यति ।
मृदि कुम्भो जले वीचिः  कनके कटकं यथा ॥
translation: मुझसे उत्पन्न यह संसार मुझमें ही लय को प्राप्त होगा जैसे मिट्टी में घड़ा, जल में लहर और सोने में आभूषण लय होते हैं।
english_translation: The universe born from me will dissolve in me, just as a pot merges into clay, a wave into water, and a jewel into gold.
essence: All that arises from you will naturally dissolve back into you.
simple_meaning: Everything that appears from you will eventually merge back into you, like a pot into clay or a wave into water.
insight: It guides you to see all experiences as temporary forms emerging from your core, shifting focus from separation to unity.
modern_relevance: When facing loss or change, remember that all things come from and return to your true essence, easing fear of endings.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अहो अहं नमो मह्यं विनाशो यस्य नास्ति मे ।
ब्रह्मादिस्तम्बपर्यन्तं जगन्नाशोऽपि तिष्ठतः ॥
translation: मैं आश्चर्यमय हूँ । मुझको नमस्कार है । ब्रह्मा से लेकर तृणपर्यन्त जगत के नाश होने पर भी मेरा नाश नहीं है।
english_translation: I am wondrous. I bow to myself. From Brahma to the blade of grass, even if the world is destroyed, I am not destroyed.
essence: You remain untouched and eternal even if the entire world is destroyed.
simple_meaning: You are wondrous and indestructible; even if everything from the greatest to the smallest perishes, you remain unchanged.
insight: It teaches you to recognize your true self as stable and unchanging beneath all external changes and losses.
modern_relevance: When life feels chaotic and everything seems to fall apart, this reminds you of your inner strength that no external event can shake.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अहो अहं नमो मह्यमेकोऽहं देहवानपि ।
क्वचिन्न गन्ता नागन्ता व्याप्य विश्वमवस्थितः ॥
translation: मैं आश्चर्यमय हूँ । मुझको नमस्कार है । मैं देहधारी होते हुए भी अद्वैत हूँ । न कहीं जाता हूँ, न आता हूँ और विश्व में व्याप्त हुआ स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: I am wondrous. I bow to myself. Though embodied, I am non-dual. I neither come nor go and pervade the entire world.
essence: You are limitless presence beyond body, neither arriving nor departing.
simple_meaning: You are amazing and complete. Even though you have a body, your true self is not limited by it. You do not come or go but are present everywhere in the world.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying only as a body to recognizing your limitless, unchanging presence everywhere.
modern_relevance: When you catch yourself caught up in your body’s limits, remember you are more than that—already present in all places and moments.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अहो अहं नमो मह्यं दक्षो नास्तीह मत्समः ।
असंस्पृश्य शरीरेण येन विश्वं चिरं धृतम् ॥
translation: मैं आश्चर्यमय हूँ । मुझको नमस्कार है । इस संसार में मेरे समान निपुण कोई नहीं । क्योंकि शरीर को स्पर्श किये बिना ही इस विश्व को सदा धारण किये रहता हूँ।
english_translation: I am wondrous. I bow to myself. No one in this world is as skilled as I am, for without touching the body, I have sustained the universe for a long time.
essence: Your true self supports all existence beyond any physical limitation.
simple_meaning: You are amazing because your true self supports the entire universe without depending on your physical body.
insight: This verse shifts your view from identifying with your body to recognizing your vast inner presence sustaining all.
modern_relevance: When you feel limited by your physical or mental state, remember your deeper self supports much more than you realize.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अहो अहं नमो मह्यं यस्य मे नास्ति किञ्चन ।
अथवा यस्य मे सर्वं यद् वाङ्मनसगोचरम् ॥
translation: मैं आश्चर्यमय हूँ । मुझको नमस्कार है । मेरा कुछ भी नहीं है, अथवा मेरा सब कुछ है – जो मन और वाणी का विषय है।
english_translation: I am the wonder. I am worthy of reverence. I have nothing, or I have everything that mind and speech can grasp.
essence: You are a wondrous presence beyond all concepts of having or not having.
simple_meaning: You are the miraculous presence that cannot be fully captured by mind or words, both empty and complete.
insight: It shifts your view from limiting identity to an expansive, paradoxical self that defies conceptual boundaries.
modern_relevance: In moments when words fail and thoughts fall silent, you glimpse a presence within that is both everything and nothing, beyond explanation.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं तथा ज्ञाता त्रितयं नास्ति वास्तवम् ।
अज्ञानाद् भाति यत्रेदं सोऽहमस्मि निरञ्जनः ॥
translation: ज्ञान, ज्ञेय और ज्ञाता ये तीनों यथार्थ नहीं हैं । जहाँ ये तीनों अज्ञान से ही भासते हैं। मैं वही निरञ्जन हूँ।
english_translation: Knowledge, the known, and the knower are not real; where these three appear, there is ignorance. I am the stainless one beyond them.
essence: The self is beyond the triad of knower, known, and knowledge, which arise from ignorance.
simple_meaning: The ideas of knowledge, the object known, and the knower are not ultimately real. They arise from ignorance. The true self is beyond these and remains pure.
insight: This shifts your mind from identifying with thoughts to realizing your pure awareness beyond all knowledge.
modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by thoughts or information, you can find calm by recognizing you are beyond all that restless knowing.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
द्वैतमूलमहो दुःखं नान्यत्तस्याऽस्ति भेषजम् ।
दृश्यमेतन् मृषा सर्वमेकोऽहं चिद्रसोमलः ॥
translation: अहो ! दुःख का मूल द्वैत है, उसकी औषधि अन्य कोई नहीं । यह सब दृश्य मिथ्या है । मैं एक विशुद्ध चैतन्यरस हूँ।
english_translation: The root of all suffering is duality; there is no other remedy. All that appears is false. I am the one pure essence of consciousness.
essence: Suffering arises from seeing separation, but your true self is one pure consciousness.
simple_meaning: Suffering arises from seeing the world as divided and separate. Everything we perceive is an illusion. The true self is pure, unified consciousness.
insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with divided appearances to recognizing your oneness as pure awareness.
modern_relevance: When you argue with others or feel isolated, remember that this sense of separation causes your distress, not your true nature.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
बोधमात्रोऽहमज्ञानाद् उपाधिः कल्पितो मया ।
एवं विमृशतो नित्यं निर्विकल्पे स्थितिर्मम ॥
translation: मैं बोधमात्र हूँ । किन्तु मेरे द्वारा अज्ञान से उपाधि की कल्पना की गई है । इस प्रकार नित्य विचार करते हुए मैं निर्विकल्प में स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: I am pure awareness, but ignorance has created a false identity around me. Reflecting on this constantly, I remain established in the undifferentiated state.
essence: Your true self is pure awareness; all separation is imagined by confusion.
simple_meaning: Your true self is pure awareness. The sense of being separate is a false idea created by confusion. By seeing this clearly, you rest in a peaceful undivided state.
insight: It teaches you to recognize the false labels your mind creates and return to the direct experience of awareness.
modern_relevance: When your restless mind invents stories about who you are, you can pause and remember you are simply aware, untouched by those stories.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
न मे बन्धोऽस्ति मोक्षो वा भ्रान्तिः शान्तो निराश्रया ।
अहो मयि स्थितं विश्वं वस्तुतो न मयि स्थितम् ॥
translation: आश्चर्य है ! मुझमें स्थित हुआ विश्व वास्तव में मुझमें स्थित नहीं है । इसलिए न मेरा बन्ध है, न मोक्ष।
english_translation: Surprisingly, the universe appears to be within me, but in truth, it is not within me; thus, I have neither bondage nor freedom.
essence: The true self is untouched by the seeming presence of the universe within it.
simple_meaning: Though it seems the universe exists within you, in reality it does not; therefore, you are neither bound nor freed.
insight: It shifts your view from feeling trapped by appearances to recognizing your inner freedom beyond them.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by everything around you, remember that none of it truly confines your true self.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
सशरीरमिदं विश्वं न किञ्चिदिति निश्चितम् ।
शुद्धचिन्मात्र आत्मा च तत्कस्मिन् कल्पनाधुना ॥
translation: निश्चय ही शरीरयुक्त यह विश्व कुछ भी नहीं है । यह शुद्ध चैतन्यमात्र आत्मा है तो इसकी कल्पना ही किसमें है।
english_translation: This body-bound universe is certainly nothing; the pure conscious self alone exists, so what is there to imagine?
essence: The body and universe are imagined; only pure consciousness truly exists.
simple_meaning: The universe tied to the body is ultimately unreal; only the pure conscious self truly exists beyond all imagination.
insight: It shifts your perspective from identifying with the body and the world to recognizing the self as pure consciousness alone.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your surroundings, remember that what you experience as solid is just imagined by the mind over your pure awareness.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
शरीरं स्वर्गनरकौ बन्धमोक्षौ भयं तथा ।
कल्पनामात्रमेवैतत् किं मे कार्यं चिदात्मनः ॥
translation: यह शरीर, स्वर्ग, नरक, बन्ध, मोक्ष व भय कल्पना मात्र ही हैं । उससे मुझ चैतन्य आत्मा को क्या प्रयोजन ।
english_translation: The body, higher and lower realms, bondage, freedom, and fear are all mere imagination; what purpose do they serve for my conscious self?
essence: The true self is untouched by body, fear, or imagined states like bondage or freedom.
simple_meaning: The body, the ideas of higher and lower realms, bondage, freedom, and fear exist only as mental creations. The true self remains unaffected by these.
insight: It shifts your focus from identifying with physical and emotional fears to recognizing your unchanging conscious self.
modern_relevance: When stress or fear about your body or future overwhelms you, remembering these are just thoughts can bring calm.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अहो जनसमूहेऽपि न द्वैतं पश्यतो मम ।
अरण्यमिव संवृत्तं क्व रतिं करवाण्यहम् ॥
translation: आश्चर्य है कि जन समूह में भी मुझे द्वैत दिखाई नहीं देता है । यह अरण्यवत् हो गया है तो फिर मैं किससे प्रेम करूँ।
english_translation: I am amazed that even among the crowd, I see no duality; like being in a forest, whom then do I love?
essence: Being among many yet seeing no separation reveals love beyond boundaries.
simple_meaning: Even when surrounded by many people, you perceive no division in reality. Like being deep in a forest, you wonder to whom you should direct your love.
insight: It teaches you to recognize the oneness beneath apparent diversity, shifting from selective attachment to universal love.
modern_relevance: In a busy room full of faces, you suddenly sense that everyone is connected beyond appearances, making love and separation meaningless.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
नाहं देहो न मे देहो जीवो नाहमहं हि चित् ।
अयमेव हि मे बन्ध आसीद्या जीविते स्पृहा ॥
translation: न मैं शरीर हूँ, न मेरा शरीर है, मैं जीव नहीं हूँ, निश्चय ही मैं चैतन्यमात्र हूँ । मेरा यही बन्ध था कि मेरी जीने की इच्छा थी।
english_translation: I am not the body, nor do I possess a body; I am not the living being, indeed I am pure awareness. My only bondage was the desire to live.
essence: You are pure awareness, not the body or life, and desire alone created your bondage.
simple_meaning: You are not your body or your living self; you are pure awareness. The only thing that trapped you was the desire to keep living.
insight: Shift your identity from physical life and desires to the pure awareness that witnesses all experience.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your body’s needs or fears about survival, remember your true nature is awareness beyond all that.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अहो भुवनकल्लोलैर्विचित्रैर्द्राक् समुत्थितम् ।
मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ चित्तवाते समुद्यते ॥
translation: आश्चर्य की अनन्त समुद्ररूप मुझमें चित्तरूपी हवा के उठने पर शीघ्र ही विचित्र जगतरूपी तरंगें पैदा होती हैं ।
english_translation: In me, like an endless ocean, strange waves of the world swiftly arise with the rising of the mind-wind.
essence: Restless thoughts arise like waves, but your true self is the vast calm ocean.
simple_meaning: Your restless mind creates many strange waves of thoughts and emotions, but beneath them, you are like a vast, endless ocean.
insight: It teaches you to see your restless thoughts as temporary waves, not your true nature.
modern_relevance: When your mind races with worry or distraction, remember that your true self remains calm and vast beneath the noise.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ चित्तवाते प्रशाम्यति ।
अभाग्याज्जीववणिजो जगत्पोतो विनश्वरः ॥
translation: अनन्त महासागररूप मुझ में चित्तरूप वायु के शान्त होने पर जीवरूप व्यापारी के अभाग्य से जगत रूपी नौका नाश को प्राप्त होती है।
english_translation: In me, the infinite great ocean, the mind calms like the wind; yet, due to misfortune, the living merchant and the world-boat perish.
essence: The mind can be deeply calm and infinite even while the outer world suffers loss.
simple_meaning: Your mind can become as vast and peaceful as an endless ocean, even while life itself faces destruction and misfortune.
insight: It teaches you that inner calm is separate from outer events and can remain steady despite life's misfortunes.
modern_relevance: After a harsh failure or loss, your mind can still find a deep stillness that no external event can shake.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधावाश्चर्यं जीववीचयः ।
उद्यन्ति घ्नन्ति खेलन्ति प्रविशन्ति स्वभावतः ॥
translation: आश्चर्य है कि अनन्त महासागररूप मुझ में जीवरूप तरंगें उठती हैं, परस्पर संघर्ष करती हैं, खेलती हैं तथा स्वभाव से ही लय हो जाती हैं।
english_translation: It is astonishing that within me, the infinite great ocean, waves of life rise, clash, play, and naturally dissolve.
essence: Your inner being is an infinite ocean where life’s waves arise and dissolve naturally.
simple_meaning: Within you is an infinite ocean where waves of life appear, interact, and naturally disappear again.
insight: It teaches you to see your changing thoughts and feelings as natural waves within your vast inner being, not permanent or threatening.
modern_relevance: You notice your emotions and thoughts rising and falling like waves inside you, sometimes clashing, sometimes playing, always changing.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अविनाशिनमात्मानमेकं विज्ञाय तत्त्वतः ।
तवात्मज्ञानस्य धीरस्य कथमर्थार्जने रतिः ॥
translation: अष्टावक्र कहते हैं – आत्मा को तत्वतः एक और अविनाशी जानकर भी तुझ आत्मज्ञानी धीर को धन कमाने में आसक्ति क्यों है।
english_translation: Ashtavakra says: Knowing the self as truly one and indestructible, why does your wise and steady self still desire to earn wealth?
essence: Knowing your self is unchanging, attachment to wealth reveals a hidden inner conflict.
simple_meaning: You understand that your true self is one and indestructible, yet your steady self still craves earning money.
insight: It shifts the mind to notice the gap between knowing your true nature and habits of craving external rewards.
modern_relevance: You’ve grasped your core identity beyond change, yet find yourself anxiously chasing promotions or money that can’t truly satisfy.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
आत्माज्ञानादहो प्रीतिर्विषयभ्रमगोचरे ।
शुक्तेरज्ञानतो लोभो यथा रजतविभ्रमे ॥
translation: आश्चर्य कि आत्मा के अज्ञान से विषय का भ्रम होने पर वैसी ही प्रीति होती है जैसी सीपी के अज्ञान से चाँदी की भ्रान्ति में लोभ होता है।
english_translation: It is surprising that ignorance of the true self causes attachment to objects, just as a shell's ignorance causes greed for silver.
essence: Attachment arises from ignorance of your true self, like mistaking a shell for silver.
simple_meaning: Attachment to things happens because you don’t recognize your true self, just like a shell wrongly thinks it holds silver.
insight: It teaches you to see craving as a mistake born from not knowing your real nature, easing attachment’s hold.
modern_relevance: You might find yourself chasing things that seem valuable, only to realize later they aren’t what truly matters because you haven’t connected with your deeper self.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
विश्वं स्फुरति यत्रेदं तरङ्गा इव सागरे ।
सोऽहमस्मीति विज्ञाय किं दीन इव धावसि ॥
translation: जहाँ यह विश्व आत्मा में समुद्र में तरंग के समान स्फुरित होता है, ‘वही मैं हूँ’, ऐसा जानकर क्यों तू दीन की तरह दौड़ता है।
english_translation: Where the entire universe flickers like waves in the ocean of the self, knowing 'I am that,' why do you run like a helpless one?
essence: You are the unchanging ocean in which all waves of the universe appear.
simple_meaning: You are the vast self in which the whole universe appears like waves. Knowing this, you need not run helplessly.
insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with fleeting fears to resting as the unchanging self beneath all change.
modern_relevance: When anxiety makes you feel small and frantic, remember you are the vast foundation beneath all your worries, steady and unshaken.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
श्रुत्वापि शुद्धचैतन्य आत्मानमतिसुन्दरम् ।
उपस्थेऽत्यन्तसंसक्तो मालिन्यमधिगच्छति ॥
translation: आत्मा को शुद्ध चैतन्य व अति सुन्दर सुनकर भी कैसे कोई इन्द्रिय के विषय में अत्यन्त आसक्त होकर मलिनता को प्राप्त होता है।
english_translation: How can the true self, pure consciousness, and supremely beautiful, become tainted by extreme attachment to sense objects despite hearing this?
essence: Pure self remains untainted, but attachment to senses clouds awareness despite knowing this.
simple_meaning: Even when you understand that your true self is pure and beautiful, strong attachment to sensory things can still cloud your inner clarity.
insight: It reveals the gap between intellectual understanding of purity and the habitual emotional attachment that blocks inner clarity.
modern_relevance: You know your best self is clear and calm, yet you find yourself stuck in endless distractions and cravings that cloud your peace.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि ।
मुनेर्जानत आश्चर्यं ममत्वमनुवर्तते ॥
translation: सब भूतों में आत्मा को और आत्मा में सब भूतों को जानकर भी मुनि को ममता होती है । यही आश्चर्य है।
english_translation: The sage knows the true self in all beings and all beings in the true self, yet still feels attachment — that is the wonder.
essence: Knowing oneness doesn’t erase the experience of personal identity—it coexists as a mystery.
simple_meaning: Even when a wise person fully understands that their true self is in all beings and all beings are in their true self, they surprisingly still feel a sense of personal identity or attachment.
insight: It teaches you to hold the paradox of knowing unity while experiencing individuality without conflict or judgment.
modern_relevance: You might deeply understand your shared humanity and connection but still feel a strong personal identity or ego that surprises you.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
आस्थितः परमाद्वैतं मोक्षार्थेऽपि व्यवस्थितः ।
आश्चर्यं कामवशगो विकलः केलिशिक्षया ॥
translation: परम अद्वैत में स्थित हुआ और मोक्ष के लिए भी उद्यत हुआ पुरुष काम के वश होकर क्रीड़ा के अभ्यास से व्याकुल होता है । यही आश्चर्य है।
english_translation: One established in supreme non-duality and striving for freedom yet becomes disturbed by desires through playful habits; this is surprising.
essence: Knowing freedom doesn’t stop desire’s playful disturbances from affecting you.
simple_meaning: A person may be deeply established in the understanding of oneness and still seek freedom, yet old desires disturb them through habitual play.
insight: Recognize that intellectual understanding alone doesn't dissolve desire; habitual patterns can still disturb the mind.
modern_relevance: You might have clarity about your goals and values, yet find yourself distracted by old habits or cravings that disrupt your focus and peace.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
उद्भूतं ज्ञानदुर्मित्रमवधार्यातिदुर्बलः ।
आश्चर्यं काममाकाङ्क्षेत् कालमन्तमनुश्रितः ॥
translation: काम को उद्भूत ज्ञान का शत्रु जानकर भी अति दुर्बल और अन्तकाल को प्राप्त हुआ पुरुष काम भोग की इच्छा करता है । यही आश्चर्य है।
english_translation: Even knowing desire is the enemy of arising knowledge, the very weak man, nearing death, still longs to satisfy desire. This is truly astonishing.
essence: Knowing desire harms wisdom doesn’t stop the weak from craving it, even near death.
simple_meaning: Even when a person knows desire harms true understanding and is weak, they still want to satisfy desire near death. This is surprising.
insight: It teaches you to notice how strong desire’s hold can be, even against your best understanding, inviting honest self-awareness.
modern_relevance: You might recognize this in moments when you know a habit or craving hurts you deeply, yet you keep returning to it despite that awareness.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
इहामुत्र विरक्तस्य नित्यानित्यविवेकिनः ।
आश्चर्यं मोक्षकामस्य मोक्षाद् एव विभीषिका ॥
translation: जो इहलोक और परलोक के भोग से विरक्त है और जो नित्य और अनित्य का विवेक रखता है वह भी मोक्ष से भय करता है । यही आश्चर्य है।
english_translation: One who is detached from worldly and otherworldly enjoyments and discerns the eternal from the transient still fears freedom; this is surprising.
essence: Even clear detachment and desire for freedom can hide a subtle fear of freedom itself.
simple_meaning: Even when you let go of desires for this life and the next and see what is permanent and what is not, you can still be afraid of true freedom.
insight: It teaches you to recognize that fear can remain even after intellectual understanding and detachment, requiring deeper inner work.
modern_relevance: You’ve worked hard to detach from old habits and understand your true self, yet fear still lingers when facing real change.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
धीरस्तु भोज्यमानोऽपि पीड्यमानोऽपि सर्वदा ।
आत्मानं केवलं पश्यन् न तुष्यति न कुप्यति ॥
translation: धीर पुरुष तो भोगता हुआ भी और पीड़ित होता हुआ भी नित्य केवल आत्मा को देखता हुआ न प्रसन्न होता है, न क्रुद्ध होता है।
english_translation: A steady person, whether enjoying or suffering, always sees only the true self and is neither pleased nor angry.
essence: Steady awareness of the true self frees you from emotional swings of pleasure and pain.
simple_meaning: You remain steady and calm whether you enjoy or suffer, because you see only your true self and do not react with pleasure or anger.
insight: It teaches you to observe your experiences without letting pleasure or pain disturb your inner balance.
modern_relevance: You face constant ups and downs, yet when you focus on who you truly are, emotional storms cannot shake you.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
चेष्टमानं शरीरं स्वं पश्यत्यन्यशरीरवत् ।
संस्तवे चापि निन्दायां कथं क्षुभ्येत् महाशयः ॥
translation: जो अपने चेष्टारत शरीर को दूसरे के शरीर की भाँति देखता है, वह महाशय पुरुष स्तुति और निन्दा में भी कैसे क्षोभ को प्राप्त हो सकता है।
english_translation: One who sees their active body as someone else's body cannot be disturbed by praise or blame.
essence: Seeing your active body as not truly yours frees you from disturbance by praise or blame.
simple_meaning: If you view your active body as if it belonged to someone else, praise and blame cannot shake you.
insight: This verse shifts your perspective from identifying with bodily actions to observing them as separate, reducing emotional reactivity.
modern_relevance: You face criticism or compliments at work, yet when you don't identify completely with your actions, their impact on your mood lessens.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
मायामात्रमिदं विश्वं पश्यन् विगतकौतुकः ।
अपि सन्निहिते मृत्यौ कथं त्रस्यति धीरधीः ॥
translation: जो इस विश्व को मायामात्र देखता है, और जो आश्चर्य को पार कर गया है, वह धीर पुरुष मृत्यु के आने पर भी क्यों भयभीत होता है।
english_translation: One who sees this world as mere illusion and has surpassed all wonder, why would such a steady person fear death when it arrives?
essence: Seeing the world as illusion removes fear even of death itself.
simple_meaning: If you truly see the world as just an illusion and have moved beyond surprise, then even when death comes close, you remain unshaken and fearless.
insight: It teaches you to steady your mind by recognizing the temporary nature of all things, including death.
modern_relevance: When you face the uncertainty of loss or endings, remembering that appearances are not absolute can help you stay grounded and calm.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
निःस्पृहं मानसं यस्य नैराश्येऽपि महात्मनः ।
तस्यात्मज्ञानतृप्तस्य तुलना केन जायते ॥
translation: जिस महात्मा का मन नैराश्य में भी स्पृहा नहीं रखता, उस आत्मज्ञान से तृप्त पुरुष की तुलना किससे की जाए।
english_translation: Whose mind is desireless even in despair, who is fulfilled by self-knowledge—how can anyone be compared to such a great being?
essence: True greatness is being desireless and fulfilled within, even in despair.
simple_meaning: A truly great being has a mind free of desire even in despair and is completely satisfied by knowing their true self.
insight: It shifts your focus from chasing fleeting hopes to resting in unshakable self-awareness, even amid hardship.
modern_relevance: When everything feels lost and your mind craves relief, discovering fulfillment within yourself can steady you completely.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
स्वभावाद् एव जानानो दृश्यमेतन्न किञ्चन ।
इदं ग्राह्यमिदं त्याज्यं स किं पश्यति धीरधीः ॥
translation: जो जानता है कि यह दृश्य स्वभाव से ही कुछ नहीं है, वह धीर बुद्धि कैसे देख सकता है कि यह ग्रहण करने योग्य है और यह त्यागने योग्य।
english_translation: The wise know that this appearance is nothing by nature; how can they then see it as something to accept or reject?
essence: True wisdom sees that nothing appearing is truly graspable or avoidable.
simple_meaning: The wise understand that what appears to you is not truly real, so it cannot be properly accepted or rejected.
insight: It shifts your mind from reacting to appearances toward seeing them as empty and neutral phenomena.
modern_relevance: You scroll endlessly through fleeting images and opinions, realizing none fully define you or deserve your full embrace or rejection.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अन्तस्त्यक्तकषायस्य निर्द्वन्द्वस्य निराशिषः ।
यदृच्छयागतो भोगो न दुःखाय न तुष्टये ॥
translation: जिसने अन्तःकरण के कषाय को त्याग दिया है, और जो द्वन्द्वरहित और आशारहित है । ऐसे पुरुष को दैवयोग से प्राप्त भोगों में न दुःख है, न सुख।
english_translation: One who has abandoned inner attachments, is free from duality and desire; whatever pleasures come by chance bring neither pain nor joy.
essence: Without inner craving, chance pleasures bring neither suffering nor delight.
simple_meaning: If you release all inner attachments and desires, then random pleasures won't cause you happiness or suffering.
insight: It shifts your focus from craving experiences to steady inner freedom beyond ups and downs.
modern_relevance: You scroll social media and see moments of joy or envy arise suddenly, but your calm comes from not clinging to any feeling.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
हन्तात्मज्ञानस्य धीरस्य खेलतो भोगलीलया ।
न हि संसारवाहीकैर्मूढैः सह समानता ॥
translation: भोग-विलास के साथ खेलते हुए आत्मज्ञानी धीर पुरुष की बराबरी संसार को सिर पर ढोने वाले मूढ़ पुरुषों के साथ कैसे की जा सकती है।
english_translation: How can the steady knower of the self, who plays with enjoyment as a sport, be compared to the fools burdened by the world?
essence: True self-knowledge lets you play freely while others are trapped by their burdens.
simple_meaning: A person who knows their true self lives with calm joy, unlike those blindly burdened by worldly struggles.
insight: It shifts your view from being overwhelmed by life’s burdens to embracing a joyful steadiness rooted in self-knowledge.
modern_relevance: You watch others anxiously chase results while you find ease and joy in your steady inner knowing.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
यत् पदं प्रेप्सवो दीनाः शक्राद्याः सर्वदेवताः ।
अहो तत्र स्थितो योगी न हर्षमुपगच्छति ॥
translation: जिस पद की इच्छा करते हुए इन्द्रादि सम्पूर्ण देवता दीन हो रहे हैं, उस पर स्थित हुआ भी योगी हर्ष को प्राप्त नहीं होता । यही आश्चर्य है ।
english_translation: The place desired by even the great deities like Indra leaves the yogi there without joy; this is the wonder.
essence: You can be where others yearn to be and still find no joy inside.
simple_meaning: Even the highest beings long for certain places, but a yogi resting there may still feel no happiness.
insight: It shifts your focus from chasing desires to recognizing that joy is independent of external achievements.
modern_relevance: You might reach a milestone or a dream job everyone admires, but still feel empty or unsatisfied inside.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
तज्ज्ञस्य पुण्यपापाभ्यां स्पर्शो ह्यन्तर्न जायते ।
न ह्याकाशस्य धूमेन दृश्यमानापि सङ्गतिः ॥
translation: उस पद को जानने वाले के अन्तःकरण का स्पर्श वैसे ही पुण्य और पाप के साथ नहीं होता जैसे आकाश का सम्बन्ध भासता हुआ भी धुएँ के साथ नहीं होता।
english_translation: The one who knows that state does not have contact of virtue and sin in their inner being, just as space appears untouched by smoke.
essence: The true self is untouched by moral dualities, like space is untouched by smoke.
simple_meaning: Knowing your true self means your inner being is not affected by good or bad, just like space is not affected by smoke.
insight: It teaches you to recognize your inner being as inherently pure and unaffected by external moral labels.
modern_relevance: When harsh judgments or praise come your way, you can remember your inner self remains untouched, like clear space beyond passing clouds of smoke.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
आत्मैवेदं जगत्सर्वं ज्ञातं येन महात्मना ।
यदृच्छया वर्तमानं तं निषेद्धुं क्षमेत कः ॥
translation: जिस महात्मा ने इस सम्पूर्ण जगत को आत्मा की तरह जान लिया है, उस ज्ञानी को अपनी इच्छा के अनुसार व्यवहार करने से कौन रोक सकता है।
english_translation: Who can prevent the great soul who knows the entire world as the true self from acting according to their own will?
essence: Knowing the world as yourself grants unstoppable freedom to act by your own will.
simple_meaning: A person who truly understands that everything is their own true self cannot be stopped from acting as they wish.
insight: It shifts your mind from feeling restricted by external forces to embracing your intrinsic freedom to act.
modern_relevance: You feel the pressure of others trying to control your choices, but when you truly know yourself, that control loses its power.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्ते भूतग्रामे चतुर्विधे ।
विज्ञस्यैव हि सामर्थ्यमिच्छानिच्छाविवर्जने ॥
translation: ब्रह्मा से चींटी पर्यन्त चार प्रकार के जीवों के समूह में ज्ञानी को ही इच्छा और अनिच्छा को रोकने की सामर्थ्य है।
english_translation: Among all groups of beings from Brahma to ants, only the wise have the power to overcome desire and aversion.
essence: Only the wise possess true power to transcend desire and aversion among all beings.
simple_meaning: Among all living beings, only those with wisdom can control their wants and dislikes.
insight: It teaches you to recognize wisdom as the capacity that stops the mind’s swinging between wanting and rejecting.
modern_relevance: When emotions pull you between craving and rejection, remember that wisdom gives you the power to remain steady and free.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
आत्मानमद्वयं कश्चिज्जानाति जगदीश्वरम् ।
यद् वेत्ति तत्स कुरुते न भयं तस्य कुत्रचित् ॥
translation: कोई विरला ही आत्मा को अद्वय और जगदीश्वर रूप में जानता है। वह जिसे करने योग्य मानता है उसे करता है । उसे किसी प्रकार का भय नहीं।
english_translation: Very few truly know the true self as non-dual and as the supreme lord of the universe. Whoever knows this acts accordingly and fears nothing anywhere.
essence: Knowing your true self as undivided power removes all fear and doubt.
simple_meaning: Only a rare person truly knows the self as unified and supreme. Such a person acts rightly and feels no fear anywhere.
insight: This verse invites you to root your actions in the fearless certainty of your true self rather than in shifting appearances.
modern_relevance: When you deeply understand your true nature, you can face any challenge with calm courage and act without hesitation.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
न ते सङ्गोऽस्ति केनापि किं शुद्धस्त्यक्तुमिच्छसि ।
सङ्घातविलयं कुर्वन्नेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥
translation: तेरा किसी से भी संग नहीं है, इसलिए तू शुद्ध है, फिर किसको त्यागना चाहता है। इस प्रकार देहभमान के त्याग की इच्छा करके लय को प्राप्त हो।
english_translation: You have no attachment to anything, so you are already pure; whom do you wish to renounce? By abandoning the false sense of the body, you attain dissolution.
essence: Purity is your natural state because you have no real attachments to renounce.
simple_meaning: You have no real attachments, so you are already pure; wanting to renounce the body-mind is the way to dissolve false identity.
insight: It shifts your mindset from trying to discard attachments to recognizing your innate freedom beyond all clinging.
modern_relevance: You may feel pressure to give up habits or identities to be 'better,' but this reminds you that your essence was never polluted to begin with.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
उदेति भवतो विश्वं वारिधेरिव बुद्बुदः ।
इति ज्ञात्वैकमात्मानमेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥
translation: तुझसे संसार उत्पन्न होता है, जैसे समुद्र से बुलबुला। इस प्रकार आत्मा को एक जानकर मोक्ष को प्राप्त हो।
english_translation: The entire world arises from you like bubbles from the ocean; knowing this, the true self alone attains liberation.
essence: The true self is the source of all and alone attains freedom.
simple_meaning: Everything in the world comes from you like bubbles come from the ocean. Realizing this, the true self alone is free.
insight: It teaches you to see yourself as the source of all experience and recognize your freedom beyond appearances.
modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by chaos, imagine the world arising from your own being. Knowing your true self is untouched brings calm and freedom.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
प्रत्यक्षमप्यवस्तुत्वाद् विश्वं नास्त्यमले त्वयि ।
रज्जुसर्प इव व्यक्तमेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥
translation: दृश्यमान जगत प्रत्यक्ष होता हुआ भी रज्जु सर्प की भाँति तुझ शुद्ध के लिए नहीं है। इसलिए तू मोक्ष को प्राप्त हो।
english_translation: The visible world, though appearing real, is like a snake made of rope and is not real for your pure self; therefore, attain freedom.
essence: What appears real is illusion to your pure self; freedom lies beyond appearances.
simple_meaning: The world you see looks real but is like a rope mistaken for a snake; it is not real for your pure self.
insight: It teaches you to see appearances as illusions and not let imagined fears bind your true self.
modern_relevance: You panic over imagined threats in your day—like worrying all night over a problem that doesn’t truly exist.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
समदुःखसुखः पूर्ण आशानैराश्ययोः समः ।
समजीवितमृत्युः सन्नेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥
translation: दुःख और सुख जिसके लिए समान है, जो पूर्ण है, जो आशा और निराशा में समान है, जीवन और मृत्यु में समान है। ऐसा होकर तू मोक्ष को प्राप्त हो।
english_translation: One who is equal to pain and pleasure, complete, equal in hope and despair, equal in life and death, attains freedom.
essence: Freedom comes from treating all extremes as equal and staying steady within.
simple_meaning: Being equally steady in pain and pleasure, hope and despair, life and death leads to true freedom.
insight: It teaches you to hold your emotional balance regardless of external changes or outcomes.
modern_relevance: When a sudden failure or success hits you, your peace depends on staying steady, not getting swept away by emotion.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
आकाशवदनन्तोऽहं घटवत् प्राकृतं जगत् ।
इति ज्ञानं तथैतस्य न त्यागो न ग्रहो लयः ॥
translation: मैं आकाश की भाँति अनन्त हूँ । यह संसार घड़े की भाँति प्रकृतिजन्य है, ऐसा ज्ञान है । इसलिए न इसका त्याग है, न ग्रहण और न लय है।
english_translation: I am infinite like space; the world is natural like a pot. This knowledge means there is no renunciation, acceptance, or dissolution of it.
essence: You are infinite like space, untouched by the natural world's forms or changes.
simple_meaning: You are infinite like space and unchanged by the natural world, which is like a pot. This means you neither reject nor cling to it, nor do you merge with it.
insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with the world to recognizing your infinite nature beyond appearances.
modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by change, remember your true self is vast and unchanged, beyond the natural ups and downs.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
महोदधिरिवाहं स प्रपञ्चो वीचिसऽन्निभः ।
इति ज्ञानं तथैतस्य न त्यागो न ग्रहो लयः ॥
translation: मैं समुद्र के समान हूँ, यह संसार तरंगों के समान है, ऐसा ज्ञान है । इसलिए न इसका त्याग है, न ग्रहण और न इसका लय है।
english_translation: I am like the great ocean; this world is like its waves. Such knowledge means there is no rejection, acceptance, or dissolution of it.
essence: Your true self remains steady and untouched despite the world's constant changes.
simple_meaning: You are like the vast ocean and the world is like the waves on it. Knowing this means you neither reject nor cling to the world, and you don’t disappear into it.
insight: It teaches you to see yourself as stable and vast, not shaped by passing events or emotions.
modern_relevance: When life tosses you between ups and downs, you can stay grounded by remembering your deeper steady nature beneath the shifting events.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अहं स शुक्तिसङ्काशो रूप्यवद् विश्वकल्पना ।
इति ज्ञानं तथैतस्य न त्यागो न ग्रहो लयः ॥
translation: मैं सीपी के समान हूँ, विश्व की कल्पना चाँदी के समान है । ऐसा ज्ञान है । अतएव इसका न त्याग है, न ग्रहण है और न लय है।
english_translation: I am like a polished shell, the world's appearance is like silver; such knowledge neither accepts, rejects, nor dissolves.
essence: You remain unchanged while the world’s shining appearance neither binds nor alters you.
simple_meaning: You are like a polished shell, solid and unchanged; the world around you is like silver, a shining appearance. This knowledge neither accepts, rejects, nor dissolves the world.
insight: It teaches you to see yourself as unaffected by the world's changing appearances, neither grasping nor rejecting them.
modern_relevance: When everything around you gleams with attraction or distraction, you can hold your calm like a steady shell, not swept away by appearances.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अहं वा सर्वभूतेषु सर्वभूतान्यथो मयि ।
इति ज्ञानं तथैतस्य न त्यागो न ग्रहो लयः ॥
translation: मैं निश्चित ही सब भूतों में हूँ और ये सब भूत मुझमें हैं । ऐसा ज्ञान है । इसलिए इसका न त्याग है, न ग्रहण है और न लय है।
english_translation: I am indeed in all beings, and all beings are within me. This is true knowledge. Therefore, it has no abandonment, no acceptance, and no destruction.
essence: You and every being are inseparably present within each other beyond gain or loss.
simple_meaning: You are present in every being, and every being exists within you. This deep knowledge is beyond gaining, losing, or giving up.
insight: It shifts your view from separation to unity, removing attachment to identity as isolated and fixed.
modern_relevance: When you feel alone or isolated, remembering that you are connected deeply to everyone can bring calm and belonging.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्वपोत इतस्ततः ।
भ्रमति स्वान्तवातेन न ममास्त्यसहिष्णुता ॥
translation: मुझ अन्तहीन महासमुद्र में विश्वरूपी नाव अपनी ही प्रकृत वायु से इधर-उधर डोलती है । मुझे असहिष्णुता नहीं है।
english_translation: In me, the infinite great ocean, the universal boat drifts here and there by its own natural wind; I have no intolerance.
essence: Your true self is a vast ocean calmly carried by natural winds, free of resistance.
simple_meaning: Your true self is like an endless ocean where the universal boat floats gently, moved by natural winds, without resistance or intolerance.
insight: It teaches you to embrace life's natural rhythms without resistance, cultivating deep equanimity.
modern_relevance: You face unexpected changes and pressures, but inside, you can remain vast and calm like an ocean, letting life’s natural flow carry you.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ जगद्वीचिः स्वभावतः ।
उदेतु वास्तमायातु न मे वृद्धिर्न च क्षतिः ॥
translation: मुझ अन्तहीन महासमुद्र में जगतरूपी लहर स्वभाव से उदय हो । मेरी न वृद्धि है, न हानि।
english_translation: In me, the infinite great ocean, the waves of the world arise naturally; I have no increase nor loss.
essence: Your true self remains unchanged as the world’s waves rise and fall within you.
simple_meaning: You are like an infinite ocean where the world’s waves rise naturally, but you yourself don’t grow or shrink.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with passing events to recognizing your unchanging awareness as the base of all experience.
modern_relevance: When your emotions surge like waves, remember your inner core stays calm and unchanged beneath the surface.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्वं नाम विकल्पना ।
अतिशान्तो निराकार एतदेवाहमास्थितः ॥
translation: मुझ अन्तहीन महासमुद्र में निश्चय ही संसार कल्पनामात्र है । मैं अत्यन्त शान्त हूँ, निराकार हूँ और इसी अवस्था में स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: In my infinite great ocean, the entire world is just imagination. I am extremely peaceful, formless, and established in this state.
essence: You are an infinite, formless ocean in which the world appears as mere imagination.
simple_meaning: Everything you see as the world is merely imagination inside your infinite being. You are deeply peaceful and formless, resting in that true state.
insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with fleeting forms to resting as the infinite, peaceful ground behind all experience.
modern_relevance: When distractions flood your mind, remember your true nature is a vast, calm ocean beyond all thoughts and worries.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
नात्मा भावेषु नो भावस्तत्रानन्ते निरञ्जने ।
इत्यसक्तोऽस्पृहः शान्त एतदेवाहमास्तितः ॥
translation: आत्मा विषयों में नहीं है और विषय उस अनन्त निरञ्जन आत्मा में नहीं है । इस प्रकार मैं अनासक्त हूँ, स्पृहामुक्त हूँ, और इसी अवस्था में स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: The true self is not in objects, nor are objects in the infinite pure self; thus, I am unattached, desireless, and established in this state.
essence: You can be free and desireless because your true self is beyond objects.
simple_meaning: You are not part of objects, nor are objects part of your true self. Being free means no attachment or desire.
insight: It teaches you to see yourself as separate from external things and to release desire for them.
modern_relevance: You notice your mind chasing things around you, but your true being remains untouched, calm, and free from wanting.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अहो चिन्मात्रमेवाहमिन्द्रजालोपमं जगत् ।
इति मम कथं कुत्र हेयोपादेयकल्पना ॥
translation: अहो ! मैं चैतन्यमात्र हूँ । संसार इन्द्रजाल की भाँति है । तब मेरी हेय और उपादेय की कल्पना किसमें हो।
english_translation: Ah! I am pure consciousness alone. The world is like a magic illusion. How can I imagine anything to be worthy or unworthy?
essence: Your true self is pure awareness; the world’s values are illusions.
simple_meaning: You are nothing but pure awareness. The world is like a magical illusion, so ideas of good or bad don’t truly apply.
insight: It shifts your mind from valuing external things to resting in your nature as pure awareness beyond judgment.
modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed by judging situations or people as good or bad. This reminds you that those judgments come from appearances, not from your true self.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
तदा बन्धो यदा चित्तं किञ्चिद् वाञ्छति शोचति ।
किञ्चिन् मुञ्चति गृण्हाति किञ्चिद् दृष्यति कुप्यति ॥
translation: जब चित्त कुछ चाहता है, कुछ सोचता है, कुछ त्याग करता है, कुछ ग्रहण करता है, जब दुःखी और सुखी होता है – तब बन्ध है।
english_translation: When the mind wants something, thinks, lets go, takes, sees, and gets angry, bondage exists.
essence: Bondage exists wherever the mind desires or reacts emotionally.
simple_meaning: Bondage arises whenever your mind desires, feels sorrow, lets go, takes, sees, or gets angry.
insight: It teaches you to watch how your mind’s desires and reactions create your sense of being trapped.
modern_relevance: When you catch yourself craving, resenting, or reacting strongly to events, you’re experiencing this inner bondage.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
तदा मुक्तिर्यदा चित्तं न वाञ्छति न शोचति ।
न मुञ्चति न गृण्हाति न हृष्यति न कुप्यति ॥
translation: जब मन न चाह करता है, न सोचता है, न त्यागता है, न ग्रहण करता है, जब यह न सुखी होता है, न दुखी होता है – तभी मुक्त है।
english_translation: Freedom arises when the mind neither desires, grieves, lets go, nor clings, neither rejoices nor angers.
essence: Freedom is the mind completely free from desire and emotional disturbance.
simple_meaning: Freedom is the state when the mind stops wanting, grieving, letting go, holding on, rejoicing, or getting angry.
insight: It teaches you to observe your mind without reacting to cravings or emotions, revealing true freedom.
modern_relevance: In a heated argument, your mind can quickly flip between wanting to win and feeling hurt. Freedom is the quiet in between.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
तदा बन्धो यदा चित्तं सक्तं काश्वपि दृष्टिषु ।
तदा मोक्षो यदा चित्तमसक्तं सर्वदृष्टिषु ॥
translation: जब चित्त किसी दृष्टि अथवा विषय में लगा है तब बन्ध है और चित्त जब सब दृष्टियों से अनासक्त है तब मोक्ष है।
english_translation: When the mind is attached to any perception or object, there is bondage; when the mind is unattached to all perceptions, there is freedom.
essence: Freedom arises when the mind lets go of attachment to every perception.
simple_meaning: Being mentally attached to any idea or object causes bondage, but when you release attachment to all things, you find freedom.
insight: It teaches you to observe and release the mind's attachments to perceptions, opening the door to inner freedom.
modern_relevance: You notice how stress rises when you obsess over one problem, but peace arrives when you let your mind rest without clinging.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
यदा नाहं तदा मोक्षो यदाहं बन्धनं तदा ।
मत्वेति हेलया किञ्चिन्मा गृहाण विमुञ्च मा ॥
translation: जब तक ‘मैं’ है तब तक बन्ध है, जब ‘मैं’ नहीं है तब मोक्ष है । इस प्रकार का विचार कर, न इच्छा कर, न ग्रहण कर, न त्याग कर।
english_translation: As long as there is 'I', there is bondage; when 'I' is not, there is freedom. Consider this and neither desire, accept, nor reject anything.
essence: True freedom arises only when the sense of 'I' disappears completely.
simple_meaning: The feeling of 'I' creates bondage; when this sense disappears, true freedom arises. So do not cling to desire, acceptance, or rejection.
insight: It shifts attention from attachment to the separate self toward resting in pure awareness beyond 'I'.
modern_relevance: You feel trapped by your identity and desires, but true freedom comes when you stop identifying with 'me' and 'mine'.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
कृताकृते च द्वन्द्वानि कदा शान्तानि कस्य वा ।
एवं ज्ञात्वेह निर्वेदाद् भव त्यागपरोऽव्रती ॥
translation: कृत्य-अकृत्य और द्वन्द्व किसके कब शान्त हुए हैं । इस प्रकार निश्चिन्त जानकर इस संसार से निर्वेद होकर त्याग और अव्रती हो।
english_translation: When have opposites like action and inaction truly ceased? Knowing this, become free from desire and renunciation in this world.
essence: True freedom goes beyond the endless cycle of opposites like action and inaction.
simple_meaning: Opposites like action and inaction never fully end. When you truly understand this, you become free from craving and giving up.
insight: It shifts your view from trying to end opposites to realizing freedom lies beyond desire and renunciation.
modern_relevance: You feel stuck trying to balance doing versus not doing, wanting versus letting go. This teaches that real freedom comes beyond such struggles.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
कस्यापि तात धन्यस्य लोकचेष्टावलोकनात् ।
जीवितेच्छा बुभुक्षा च बुभुत्सोपशमः गताः ॥
translation: हे तात ! लोक की चेष्टा को देखकर किसी भाग्यशाली की ही जीने की कामना, भोगने की वासना और ज्ञान की इच्छा शान्त हुई है।
english_translation: O father, upon seeing the world's ways, even the fortunate lose desire to live, to enjoy, and to seek knowledge.
essence: Observing the world deeply can quiet even the strongest desires in the fortunate.
simple_meaning: Watching how the world acts causes even fortunate people to lose their desire to live, enjoy, or seek more knowledge.
insight: It shifts your mind from chasing desires to noticing their natural fading when fully witnessed.
modern_relevance: You scroll through endless social media, seeing others chase desires, and realize how tiring constant wanting really is.
speaker: Janaka

verse_text:
अनित्यं सर्वमेवेदं तापत्रितयदूषितम् ।
असारं निन्दितं हेयमिति निश्चित्य शाम्यति ॥
translation: यह सब अनित्य है, तीनों तापों से दूषित है, सारहीन है, निन्दित है, हेय है । ऐसा निश्चित होने पर शान्ति प्राप्त होती है ।
english_translation: Everything that exists is impermanent, tainted by the three sufferings, without essence, blameworthy, and to be rejected; realizing this brings peace.
essence: Peace arises by clearly seeing all things as impermanent and unworthy of attachment.
simple_meaning: Everything you see changes, causes suffering, lacks true essence, and is not worth holding onto. Understanding this brings calm.
insight: It shifts your attention from clinging to appearances toward embracing their impermanence and emptiness.
modern_relevance: You watch your favorite things fade or fail, feeling restless—this teaches you to find peace beyond them.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
कोऽसौ कालो वयः किं वा यत्र द्वन्द्वानि नो नृणाम् ।
तान्युपेक्ष्य यथाप्राप्तवर्ती सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
translation: वह कौन सा काल है व कौन सी अवस्था है जिसमें मनुष्य को द्वन्द्व न हों । उनकी उपेक्षा कर यथाप्राप्य वस्तुओं में संतोष करने वाला मनुष्य सिद्धि को प्राप्त होता है।
english_translation: What time or stage is there when humans have no conflicts? By ignoring them and being content with what comes, one attains accomplishment.
