essence: Conflicts are inevitable; mastery is accepting and being content with what arises.
simple_meaning: Humans always experience conflicts. True success comes when you accept this and find contentment in whatever life gives.
insight: It teaches you to shift focus from eliminating conflicts to accepting them and finding satisfaction in what you have.
modern_relevance: You face constant challenges at work or in relationships. Trying to avoid them only adds stress; accepting them lets you focus on what you can handle.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
नाना मतं महर्षीणां साधूनां योगिनां तथा ।
दृष्ट्वा निर्वेदमापन्नः को न शाम्यति मानवः ॥
translation: महर्षियों के, योगियों के एवं साधुओं के अनेक मत हैं । ऐसा देखकर उपेक्षा को प्राप्त हुआ कौन मनुष्य शान्ति को प्राप्त नहीं होता ।
english_translation: Among great sages, yogis, and saints, many opinions exist; seeing this, who does not grow weary? Yet who does not find peace?
essence: Conflicting views tire the mind, but peace remains accessible to every human.
simple_meaning: You encounter many differing opinions from sages and yogis, which can cause weariness, yet everyone can still find peace.
insight: Recognize that conflicting ideas don't prevent your peace; your calm can exist beyond opinions.
modern_relevance: You scroll through endless advice online, feeling overwhelmed by contradictions—yet a calm center inside you can still be found.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
कृत्वा मूर्तिपरिज्ञानं चैतन्यस्य न किं गुरुः ।
निर्वेदसमतायुक्त्या यस्तारयति संसृतेः ॥
translation: जो उपेक्षा, समता और युक्ति के द्वारा चैतन्य के सच्चे स्वरूप को जानकर संसार में अपने को तारता है, क्या वह गुरु नहीं है ।
english_translation: Who, having realized the true nature of pure awareness through detachment, equanimity, and reasoning, liberates themselves from the cycle of the natural world, is indeed a true teacher.
essence: Clear, calm understanding of pure awareness liberates you like a true teacher.
simple_meaning: When you understand your true awareness through letting go, balance, and clear thinking, you free yourself from life's endless cycle. Such a person is a real teacher.
insight: It teaches you to combine detachment, balance, and reasoning to recognize your pure awareness and break free from repetitive patterns.
modern_relevance: You feel stuck in repeating mistakes until you calmly see your true nature with clear reasoning and balanced emotions, freeing yourself from old cycles.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
पश्य भूतविकारांस्त्वं भूतमात्रान् यथार्थतः ।
तत्क्षणाद् बन्धनिर्मुक्तः स्वरूपस्थो भविष्यसि ॥
translation: जब भूत-विकारों को तू यथार्थतः भूतमात्र देखेगा – उसी क्षण बन्ध से मुक्त होकर अपने स्वरूप में स्थित हो जाएगा ।
english_translation: When you truly see all changes as nothing but appearances, you become free from bondage and remain established in your true nature.
essence: True freedom arises the moment you see all change as mere appearances.
simple_meaning: When you recognize that all changes you see are just appearances, you instantly become free and rest in your true self.
insight: It shifts your view from reacting to appearances to resting in your unchanging true self instantly.
modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by constant change and inner turmoil; realizing it’s all just surface helps you find calm and freedom now.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
वासना एव संसार इति सर्वा विमुञ्च ताः ।
तत्त्यागो वासनात्यागात्स्थितिरद्य यथा तथा ॥
translation: वासना ही संसार है इसलिये इन सबका त्याग कर । वासना के त्याग से ही संसार का त्याग है । अब जहाँ चाहे वहाँ रह।
english_translation: Desire alone is the cause of the cycle of reactivity; abandon all desires. By abandoning desires, you abandon the cycle. Now you can remain wherever you wish.
essence: Abandoning desire breaks the cycle that binds you, granting freedom anywhere.
simple_meaning: All suffering and repeated reactions come from desire. Letting go of desire ends that cycle, letting you exist freely anywhere.
insight: This verse shifts your focus from chasing desires to simply releasing them, breaking habitual patterns.
modern_relevance: You feel trapped in patterns driven by what you want but can't have. Letting go of these cravings frees you to find peace wherever you are.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
विहाय वैरिणं काममर्थं चानर्थसङ्कुलम् ।
धर्ममप्येतयोर्हेतुं सर्वत्रानादरं कुरु ॥
translation: वैर स्वरूप काम को और अनर्थ से भरे अर्थ को त्याग कर और दोनों के कारण-रूप धर्म को भी छोड़कर तू सबकी उपेक्षा कर।
english_translation: Give up enmity, desire, and goals filled with harm; even abandon the dharma born from these, and everywhere disregard all.
essence: Freedom arises by releasing harm, desire, and even the duties they create.
simple_meaning: Let go of hatred, desire, harmful goals, and even the duties that arise from them. Disregard all such attachments everywhere.
insight: This shifts your mind from clinging to any motivation born of harm or desire, freeing you from all binding attachments.
modern_relevance: You’ve been holding grudges and chasing goals that cause stress; letting go of both the feelings and the obligations tied to them opens space for peace.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
स्वप्नेन्द्रजालवत् पश्य दिनानि त्रीणि पञ्च वा ।
मित्रक्षेत्रधनागारदारदायादिसम्पदः ॥
translation: मित्र, खेत, धन, मकान, स्त्री, भाई आदि सम्पदा को तू स्वप्न और इन्द्रजाल के समान देख जो तीन या पाँच दिन ही टिकते हैं ।
english_translation: See friends, fields, wealth, houses, wives, brothers, and such possessions as like a dream or magical illusion that lasts only three or five days.
essence: All worldly attachments are fleeting illusions that cannot last.
simple_meaning: Everything you consider valuable—friends, land, wealth, and family—is temporary, like a brief dream or illusion.
insight: It shifts your mind to see attachments as temporary, reducing clinging and anxiety about loss.
modern_relevance: You watch a social media highlight fade or a prized possession break, realizing how quickly what you value can change or disappear.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
यत्र यत्र भवेत्तृष्णा संसारं विद्धि तत्र वै ।
प्रौढवैराग्यमाश्रित्य वीततृष्णः सुखी भव ॥
translation: जहाँ-जहाँ तृष्णा हो वहाँ-वहाँ ही संसार जान । प्रौढ़ वैराग्य को आश्रय करके वीततृष्णा होकर सुखी हो।
english_translation: Wherever craving arises, realize that there is the cycle of reactivity; relying on mature non-attachment, become free of craving and be happy.
essence: Craving reveals the cycle of reactivity; mature non-attachment dissolves craving and brings happiness.
simple_meaning: Whenever you notice craving, recognize that it causes continuous reactivity. By embracing mature non-attachment, you can become free of craving and find happiness.
insight: It teaches you to observe craving as the start of reactivity and shift towards mature non-attachment to break free.
modern_relevance: You scroll social media and feel a sudden urge for more likes or approval. Recognizing that craving fuels your unrest, you choose to let go and find calm instead.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
तृष्णामात्रात्मको बन्धस्तन्नाशो मोक्ष उच्यते ।
भवासंसक्तिमात्रेण प्राप्तितुष्टिर्मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
translation: तृष्णामात्र ही आत्मा का बन्ध है और उसका नाश मोक्ष कहा जाता है । संसार मात्र से अनासक्त होने से निरन्तर प्राप्ति और तुष्टि होती है।
english_translation: The only bond is craving; its destruction is freedom. Continuous detachment from the cycle of existence brings repeated fulfillment and contentment.
essence: Freedom arises not by gaining but by ending craving, the true bond.
simple_meaning: Craving is the only true bond that traps you. When this craving ends, you find freedom and ongoing satisfaction beyond worldly attachments.
insight: It teaches you to identify craving as your inner bond and to cultivate detachment for lasting contentment.
modern_relevance: You notice how wanting more or different things pulls you into stress and restlessness. Letting go of craving reveals a steady satisfaction beneath.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
त्वमेकश्चेतनः शुद्धो जडं विश्वमसत्तथा ।
अविद्यापि न किञ्चित्सा का बुभुत्सा तथापि ते ॥
translation: तू एक शुद्ध चैतन्य है, संसार जड़ और असत् है । यह अविद्या भी असत् है । इस पर भी तू क्या जानने की इच्छा रखता है।
english_translation: You are pure consciousness alone; the world is insentient and unreal. Ignorance itself is unreal. Why then do you seek to know it?
essence: Your true nature is pure consciousness; all else, including ignorance, is unreal.
simple_meaning: You are pure awareness alone. The world and ignorance are unreal and insentient. So why desire to know what does not truly exist?
insight: It shifts your focus from chasing illusions to recognizing your true, unchanging nature as pure awareness.
modern_relevance: You might catch yourself endlessly chasing worries or false identities, forgetting your true clear awareness beyond all that noise.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
राज्यं सुताः कलत्राणि शरीराणि सुखानि च ।
संसक्तस्यापि नष्टानि तव जन्मनि जन्मनि ॥
translation: तेरे राज्य, पुत्र, पुत्रियाँ, शरीर और सुख जन्म-जन्म से नष्ट हुए हैं, यद्यपि तू उनमें आसक्त था।
english_translation: Your kingdom, sons, wives, body, and pleasures have been lost again and again in your many births, even though you were attached to them.
essence: Clinging to impermanent things only leads to repeated loss over many lives.
simple_meaning: Everything you have clung to—your kingdom, family, body, and pleasures—has been lost repeatedly through many lifetimes.
insight: It encourages shifting your focus from clinging to impermanent things toward recognizing what truly endures beyond them.
modern_relevance: You might hold tightly to your career, relationships, or health, only to watch them change or disappear over time.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अलमर्थेन कामेन सुकृतेनापि कर्मणा ।
एभ्यः संसारकान्तारे न विश्रान्तमभून् मनः ॥
translation: अर्थ, काम और सुकृत कर्म बहुत हो चुके । इनमें भी संसाररूपी जंगल में मन विश्रान्ति को प्राप्त नहीं हुआ।
english_translation: Even after much wealth, desire, and good deeds, the mind found no rest in the forest of the cycle of reactivity.
essence: External gains and good actions alone cannot still a restless mind trapped in reactivity.
simple_meaning: Having wealth, fulfilling desires, and doing good deeds do not guarantee that your mind will be peaceful or free from restlessness.
insight: Recognize that external achievements and desires don’t quiet the mind; true rest requires inner transformation beyond action.
modern_relevance: After chasing promotions, buying things, and doing favors, you still lie awake with a busy mind that won’t settle.
speaker: Janaka

verse_text:
कृतं न कति जन्मानि कायेन मनसा गिरा ।
दुःखमायासदं कर्म तदद्याप्युपरम्यताम् ॥
translation: कितने जन्मों तक तूने क्या शरीर, मन और वाणी के दुखपूर्ण और श्रमपूर्ण कर्म नहीं किये हैं । अब तो आराम कर।
english_translation: How many lifetimes have you not performed painful actions with body, mind, and speech? Now, rest at last.
essence: After endless painful effort, the true self can finally rest free of action.
simple_meaning: You have performed many difficult actions over many lives with your body, mind, and speech. Now it is time to stop and rest.
insight: It shifts the mind from continuous struggle to allowing rest as a form of freedom.
modern_relevance: You’ve pushed yourself through endless tasks and worries, caught in constant effort. This moment invites you to pause and just rest.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
भावाभावविकारश्च स्वभावादिति निश्चयी ।
निर्विकारो गतक्लेशः सुखेनैवोपशाम्यति ॥
translation: और अभाव का विकार स्वभाव से होता है ऐसा जो निश्चयपूर्वक जानता है, वह निर्विकार और क्लेशरहित पुरुष सुखपूर्वक ही शान्ति को उपलब्ध होता है।
english_translation: One who firmly knows that existence and non-existence arise from nature is free from disturbance and pain, and attains peace with joy.
essence: True peace and joy come from knowing change and pain are natural and do not disturb you.
simple_meaning: Understanding that all changes and opposites come from nature helps you become free from disturbance and pain, reaching peaceful joy.
insight: It shifts your mind from reacting to change and pain towards embracing them as natural, bringing steady joy.
modern_relevance: After losing control or facing constant ups and downs, you realize peace comes when you stop resisting change and pain.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
ईश्वरः सर्वनिर्माता नेहान्य इति निश्चयी ।
अन्तर्गलितसर्वाशः शान्तः क्वापि न सज्जते ॥
translation: सबको बनाने वाले ईश्वर हैं अन्य कोई नहीं है, ऐसा जो निश्चयपूर्वक जानता है वह पुरुष शान्त है । उसकी सब आशाएँ जड़ से नष्ट हो गयी हैं । वह कहीं भी आसक्त नहीं होता।
english_translation: The one who firmly knows that the supreme being alone is the creator of all is peaceful; all their desires are completely dissolved, and they are attached nowhere.
essence: Peace arises when you fully know the supreme alone creates all and all desires vanish.
simple_meaning: Knowing with certainty that the supreme being alone creates everything brings deep peace and frees you from all desires and attachments.
insight: It shifts your focus from chasing desires to resting in the certainty of a single creative source, calming restless seeking.
modern_relevance: You feel calm when you stop chasing every desire and accept that the source of everything is beyond personal control.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
आपदः सम्पदः काले दैवादेवेति निश्चयी ।
तृप्तः स्वस्थेन्द्रियो नित्यं न वान्छति न शोचति ॥
translation: विपत्ति और सम्पत्ति दैवयोग से ही समय पर आती है, ऐसा निश्चय वाला पुरुष सदा सन्तुष्ट हुआ, न कोई कामना करता है, न शोक करता है।
english_translation: Calamity and prosperity come in their own time by the divine's will; a person resolved in this remains always content, desires nothing, and grieves not.
essence: Contentment arises by trusting life's timing, freeing you from desire and grief.
simple_meaning: Good or bad events happen according to their own time beyond your control; trusting this, you stay content without craving or sorrow.
insight: It teaches you to anchor your peace in trust of timing, not in external events.
modern_relevance: You face sudden news: a lost job or unexpected praise. Trusting that these come and go naturally keeps your mind calm.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
सुखदुःखे जन्ममृत्यू दैवादेवेति निश्चयी ।
साध्यादर्शी निरायासः कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते ॥
translation: सुख-दुःख, जन्म-मृत्यु दैवयोग से ही होती है, ऐसा निश्चय वाला व्यक्ति साध्य कर्मों को देखता हुआ और निरायास कर्मों को करता हुआ भी उनमें लिप्त नहीं होता।
english_translation: A person firmly certain that pleasure, pain, birth, and death happen by the divine order sees actions as unavoidable and performs effortless acts without attachment.
essence: You can act effortlessly without attachment, accepting life’s natural cycles.
simple_meaning: You understand that happiness, suffering, birth, and death happen naturally. Seeing this, you act without effort and without getting caught up in outcomes.
insight: It shifts your focus from resisting life’s ups and downs to embracing your actions without emotional entanglement.
modern_relevance: You face unexpected setbacks or successes at work but remain calm, knowing these events are part of life’s natural rhythm.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
चिन्तया जायते दुःखं नान्यथेहेति निश्चयी ।
तया हीनः सुखी शान्तः सर्वत्र गलितस्पृहः ॥
translation: चिन्ता से दुःख उत्पन्न होता है अन्यथा नहीं । ऐसा जो निश्चयपूर्वक जानता है, वह सुखी और शान्त है । सर्वत्र उसकी स्पृहा गलित है और चिन्ता से मुक्त है।
english_translation: Suffering arises only from worry; knowing this with certainty brings peace and joy, dissolving all desire everywhere.
essence: Suffering arises only from worry; knowing this brings lasting peace and ends craving.
simple_meaning: Suffering comes only from worry. When you know this firmly, you become peaceful and joyful, free from all craving.
insight: Shift focus from external troubles to your mental response; calming worry dissolves suffering.
modern_relevance: Your mind races with 'what ifs' and fears, making simple moments heavy. Seeing worry as the source frees you to relax.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
नाहं देहो न मे देहो बोधोऽहमिति निश्चयी ।
कैवल्यमिव सम्प्राप्तो न स्मरत्यकृतं कृतम् ॥
translation: मैं शरीर नहीं हूँ, देह मेरी नहीं है, मैं तो बोधस्वरूप हूँ, ऐसा जो निश्चयपूर्वक जानता है वह पुरुष कैवल्य को प्राप्त होकर किये और अनकिये कर्म का स्मरण नहीं करता।
english_translation: I am not the body, nor does the body belong to me; I am pure awareness. One who firmly knows this, having attained complete freedom, does not recall actions done or undone.
essence: Realizing you are pure awareness frees you from attachment to body and actions.
simple_meaning: You are not the body, nor does it belong to you. You are pure awareness. When you truly know this, you no longer remember your past actions or unfinished tasks.
insight: It shifts your identity from body and deeds to pure awareness, freeing you from attachment to results.
modern_relevance: You finish a task but still feel burdened by what’s done or left undone. Knowing you are beyond these actions lifts that weight.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्तमहमेवेति निश्चयी ।
निर्विकल्पः शुचिः शान्तः प्राप्ताप्राप्तविनिर्वृतः ॥
translation: ब्रह्म से लेकर तृणपर्यन्त ‘मैं ही हूँ’ ऐसा जो निश्चयपूर्वक जानता है, वह निर्विकार, शुद्ध, शान्त और प्राप्त-अप्राप्त से निवृत्त होता है।
english_translation: One who firmly knows 'I am the supreme reality' from Brahman to the blade of grass becomes free from all dualities, pure, peaceful, and beyond gain or loss.
essence: Knowing you are the unchanging reality beneath all things brings lasting peace and freedom.
simple_meaning: Knowing deeply that you are the one reality behind all things, big or small, brings purity, peace, and freedom from all ups and downs.
insight: It shifts focus from fleeting achievements to the constant, pure presence you already are, freeing you from emotional swings.
modern_relevance: You realize that beneath every success or failure, you remain untouched and steady, like the quiet truth beneath all your experiences.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
नाश्चर्यमिदं विश्वं न किञ्चिदिति निश्चयी ।
निर्वासनः स्फूर्तिमात्रो न किञ्चिदिव शाम्यति ॥
translation: अनेक आश्चर्यों वाला वह विश्व कुछ भी नहीं है अर्थात मिथ्या है ऐसा जो निश्चयपूर्वक जानता है, वह वासनारहित, बोधस्वरूप पुरुष इस प्रकार शान्ति को प्राप्त होता है, मानो कुछ भी नहीं है ।
english_translation: The world full of wonders is ultimately nothing; one who firmly knows this, free from desire, attains a peace as if nothing exists.
essence: True peace comes from fully knowing the world’s wonders are empty appearances.
simple_meaning: The world, though full of wonders, is ultimately empty. One who truly understands this and is free from desire finds deep peace as if nothing disturbs them.
insight: It shifts your mind from craving and confusion to steady calm by recognizing appearances as empty.
modern_relevance: You pause in a moment of chaos and realize your worries are shadows, not solid threats to your peace.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
कायकृत्यासहः पूर्वं ततो वाग्विस्तरासहः ।
अथ चिन्तासहस्तस्माद् एवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
translation: पहले मैं शारीरिक कर्मों का न सराहने वाला हुआ, फिर वाणी के विस्तृत कर्म का न सराहने वाला हुआ । इस प्रकार मैं स्थिर हूँ।
english_translation: First, I became indifferent to bodily actions, then to the extensive actions of speech; thus, I have remained steady.
essence: Steadiness arises when you release attachment to body, speech, and mental worries.
simple_meaning: You find steadiness by no longer clinging to your bodily actions, your words, or your thoughts.
insight: It teaches you to progressively detach from body, speech, and mind to become unshakable.
modern_relevance: You stop obsessing over what you say, what you do, and what you think, and suddenly your inner calm deepens.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
प्रीत्यभावेन शब्दादेरदृश्यत्वेन चात्मनः ।
विक्षेपैकाग्रहृदय एवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
translation: शब्द आदि ऐन्द्रिक विषयों के प्रति राग के अभाव से और आत्मा की अदृश्यता से प्राप्त विक्षेपों से जिसका मन मुक्त होकर एकाग्र हो गया – ऐसा ही मैं स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: I remain established with a heart free from attachment to sensory objects like sounds and free from distractions caused by the invisible nature of the self, fully concentrated on one point.
essence: You can remain fully focused and undistracted by sensory attachments or the invisible self.
simple_meaning: You can be free from attachment to sensory things and distractions, keeping your heart focused on one point.
insight: It teaches you to loosen attachment to sensory distractions and anchor your attention steadily.
modern_relevance: When your mind wanders amidst constant notifications and noise, knowing how to stay focused and unattached brings clarity and calm.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
समाध्यासादिविक्षिप्तौ व्यवहारः समाधये ।
एवं विलोक्य नियममेवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
translation: सम्यक् अध्यास आदि के कारण विक्षेप होने पर ही समाधि का व्यवहार होता है । ऐसे नियम को देखकर मैं स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: Disturbance arises in action due to attachment and other causes; seeing this rule, I remain steady.
essence: Seeing attachment's disturbance in action lets you remain steady and present.
simple_meaning: Attachment and similar distractions disturb your actions and presence; recognizing this helps you remain steady.
insight: Recognize attachment as the source of disturbance to maintain inner steadiness during action.
modern_relevance: You feel distracted when your mind clings to results or worries, but noticing this pattern helps you stay grounded.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
हेयोपादेयविरहाद् एवं हर्षविषादयोः ।
अभावादद्य हे ब्रह्मन्न् एवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
translation: हे ब्रह्मन् ! हेय और उपादेय के वियोग से जो हर्ष और विषाद होता है उसके अभाव में अब मैं जैसा हूँ वैसा ही स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: O Brahman! Without the separation of what is to be rejected and what is to be embraced, I remain as I am now.
essence: True steadiness arises when you stop separating your experience into accepted and rejected parts.
simple_meaning: When you stop dividing your experiences into what you want and what you reject, you remain peaceful and steady as you are.
insight: It shifts your mind from reacting to experiences as good or bad to resting in unshaken presence beyond those labels.
modern_relevance: You notice your mood swings when you label moments as good or bad; this teaches how to stay unshaken by releasing those judgments.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
आश्रमानाश्रमं ध्यानं चित्तस्वीकृतवर्जनम् ।
विकल्पं मम वीक्ष्यैतैरेवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
translation: आश्रम एवं अनाश्रम है, ध्यान है तथा चित्त का स्वीकार और वर्जन है । उन सबसे उत्पन्न हुए अपने विकल्प को देखकर मैं उन तीनों से मुक्त हुआ स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: The hermitage and non-hermitage, meditation, acceptance and rejection of the mind—seeing these choices arise, I remain free from all three.
essence: Freedom comes from watching mental choices without identifying with them.
simple_meaning: You can see all mental choices and states arise—like hermitage, meditation, acceptance, and rejection—and remain untouched by them, resting in freedom.
insight: It shifts your attention from identifying with mental preferences to witnessing them dispassionately, creating inner freedom.
modern_relevance: When your mind flips between decisions or moods, this teaching invites you to watch without getting caught or overwhelmed.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
कर्मानुष्ठानमज्ञानाद् यथैवोपरमस्तथा ।
बुध्वा सम्यगिदं तत्त्वमेवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
translation: जैसे कर्म का अनुष्ठान अज्ञान से है, वैसे ही उसके त्याग का अनुष्ठान भी अज्ञान से है । इस तत्व को भली भाँति जानकर मैं कर्म अकर्म से मुक्त हुआ अपने में स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: Just as performing actions arises from ignorance, so does renouncing actions; knowing this truth well, I remain established beyond action and inaction.
essence: Freedom lies beyond both action and renunciation, both born of ignorance.
simple_meaning: Both doing actions and giving them up come from not knowing. Understanding this, you stand free beyond action and inaction.
insight: It shifts your view from opposing action and renunciation to seeing both as rooted in the same confusion, freeing you to rest beyond them.
modern_relevance: You struggle between pushing forward and giving up, not seeing both come from the same confusion. Recognizing this frees your mind.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अचिन्त्यं चिन्त्यमानोऽपि चिन्तारूपं भजत्यसौ ।
त्यक्त्वा तद्भावनं तस्माद् एवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
translation: अचिन्त्य का चिन्तन करता हुआ भी वह पुरुष चिन्ता को ही भजता है । इसलिए उस भाव को त्यागकर मैं भावनामुक्त हुआ स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: Even when contemplating the inconceivable, that person worships only the form of thought. Therefore, having abandoned that contemplation, I remain established free from all mental formations.
essence: True freedom arises by abandoning even the deepest engagement with thought.
simple_meaning: Even focusing deeply on the unthinkable still ties you to thought. True freedom comes from letting go of even that.
insight: It teaches you to recognize when deep contemplation becomes another form of attachment and shift towards release.
modern_relevance: You might find yourself obsessing over a complex problem or idea, trying to figure it all out. This verse invites you to release that effort and find peace beyond thinking.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
एवमेव कृतं येन स कृतार्थो भवेदसौ ।
एवमेव स्वभावो यः स कृतार्थो भवेदसौ ॥
translation: जिसने साधनों से क्रियारहित स्वरूप अर्जित किया है – वह पुरुष कृतकृत्य है और जो ऐसा ही स्वभाव वाला है वह तो कृतकृत्य है ही, इसमें कहना ही क्या।
english_translation: One who has attained a natural state beyond action is truly fulfilled; and one whose nature is such is indeed fulfilled, needless to say.
essence: True fulfillment arises when your nature is free from all action.
simple_meaning: You become truly fulfilled when you reach a natural state beyond all actions and effort. When your nature itself is free from doing, you are complete.
insight: It shifts focus from actions performed to the natural state of being fulfilled without doing.
modern_relevance: You feel fulfilled not when checking off tasks, but when you rest as your true self beyond effort and striving.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अकिञ्चनभवं स्वास्थं कौपीनत्वेऽपि दुर्लभम् ।
त्यागादाने विहायास्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
translation: है कुछ भी – ऐसे भाव से पैदा हुआ जो स्वास्थ्य है वह कोपीन को धारण करने पर भी दुर्लभ है । इसलिए त्याग और ग्रहण दोनों को छोड़कर मैं सुखपूर्वक स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: Being without attachment, I remain happily established, even while wearing a loincloth, which is rare to find.
essence: You can be happily settled by giving up both craving and rejection.
simple_meaning: You can stay happily settled without grasping or pushing away anything, even with very little.
insight: It shifts your mindset from reacting to circumstances toward resting quietly in acceptance beyond desire and aversion.
modern_relevance: When your phone dies and you have no backup, yet you feel calm and okay without needing more.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
कुत्रापि खेदः कायस्य जिह्वा कुत्रापि खेद्यते ।
मनः कुत्रापि तत्त्यक्त्वा पुरुषार्थे स्थितः सुखम् ॥
translation: कहीं तो शरीर का दुःख है, कहीं वाणी दुःखी है, कहीं मन दुःखी होता है । इसलिए तीनों को त्यागकर मैं पुरुषार्थ में सुखपूर्वक स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: The body suffers in some place, the speech suffers elsewhere, and the mind suffers somewhere else; abandoning all three, I remain happily established in true purpose.
essence: You find true happiness by letting go of suffering in body, speech, and mind.
simple_meaning: The body, speech, and mind each experience suffering in different ways. By letting go of attachment to all three, you remain happily established in your true purpose.
insight: It teaches you to shift attention from transient pains of body, speech, and mind to abiding in your deeper purpose.
modern_relevance: You feel stress in your body, frustration in your words, and unrest in your mind. Letting go of identifying with all these brings calm and focus.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
कृतं किमपि नैव स्याद् इति सञ्चिन्त्य तत्त्वतः ।
यदा यत्कर्तुमायाति तत् कृत्वासे यथासुखम् ॥
translation: किया हुआ कर्म कुछ भी वास्तव में आत्मकृत नहीं होता । ऐसा यथार्थ विचारकर मैं जब जो कुछ कर्म करने को आ पड़ता है उसे करके सुखपूर्वक स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: No action done is truly your own; understanding this, do whatever must be done with ease and contentment.
essence: No action is truly yours; act calmly with that understanding.
simple_meaning: No action you do is truly owned by you; when you understand this, you can act with comfort and ease.
insight: This verse shifts focus from ownership of results to peaceful acceptance of necessary action.
modern_relevance: You face unexpected tasks today. Realizing none belong fully to you lets you meet them calmly and without stress.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
कर्मनैष्कर्म्यनिर्बन्धभावा देहस्थयोगिनः ।
संयोगायोगविरहादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
translation: कर्म और निष्कर्म के बन्धन से संयुक्त भाव वाले शरीर में आसक्त जो योगी है मैं इस देह के संयोग वियोग से सर्वदा पृथक होने के कारण सुखपूर्वक स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: I am free from attachment to action or inaction in this embodied state; unlike yogis attached to union or separation, I remain happily detached from both.
essence: True freedom comes from detaching equally from action and inaction.
simple_meaning: You can remain happily free by not being attached to doing or not doing, unlike those who cling to action or its opposite.
insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with action or inaction to abiding freely beyond both.
modern_relevance: You feel pressure to always be either productive or resting perfectly, but real ease comes when you release attachment to both states.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अर्थानर्थौ न मे स्थित्या गत्या न शयनेन वा ।
तिष्ठन् गच्छन् स्वपन् तस्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
translation: मुझको ठहरने से, चलने से या सोने से अर्थ या अनर्थ कुछ भी नहीं है । इस कारण ‘मैं’ ठहरता हुआ, जाता हुआ और सोता हुआ भी सुखपूर्वक स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: Staying, moving, or sleeping brings me no gain or loss; therefore, I remain happy whether still, moving, or sleeping.
essence: True happiness remains steady regardless of activity or rest.
simple_meaning: You don’t gain or lose anything by staying still, moving, or sleeping. That’s why you can remain happy in all these states.
insight: It shifts your focus from external activity to an inner steadiness that remains unshaken by changing states.
modern_relevance: You feel restless switching between busy work and rest, but this teaches peace can remain unchanged through all your daily shifts.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
स्वपतो नास्ति मे हानिः सिद्धिर्यत्नवतो न वा ।
नाशोल्लासौ विहायास्मदहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
translation: सोते हुए मुझे हानि नहीं है, न यत्न करते हुए मुझे सिद्धि है । इसलिए मैं हानि-लाभ दोनों को छोड़कर सुखपूर्वक स्थित हूँ ।
english_translation: Sleeping does not harm me; striving does not grant me success. So I have abandoned both loss and gain and remain happily as I am.
essence: True peace comes from releasing attachment to both effort and its results.
simple_meaning: Neither resting nor striving changes your true state. You can let go of both and be peacefully content.
insight: It teaches you to stop equating your value with achievements or setbacks and to rest in contentment.
modern_relevance: After a long day of pushing yourself, you realize neither rest nor frantic effort truly changes your inner peace.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
सुखादिरूपा नियमं भावेष्वालोक्य भूरिशः ।
शुभाशुभे विहायास्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
translation: इसलिए अनेक परिस्थितियों में सुखादि की अनित्यता को बारम्बार देखकर और शुभ और अशुभ दोनों को छोड़कर मैं सुखपूर्वक स्थित हूँ।
english_translation: Having repeatedly seen the impermanence of pleasure and pain in many states, I let go of good and bad and remain happily established.
essence: True peace comes from releasing attachment to both pleasure and pain.
simple_meaning: When you notice how pleasure and pain always change, you can stop chasing good or avoiding bad and simply be peaceful.
insight: It teaches you to stop judging your experiences as good or bad and to stay peacefully aware instead.
modern_relevance: You’ve felt excitement fade or discomfort pass, and finally stop reacting, just resting calmly without chasing highs or fearing lows.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
प्रकृत्या शून्यचित्तो यः प्रमादाद् भावभावनः ।
निद्रितो बोधित इव क्षीणसंस्मरणो हि सः ॥
translation: स्वभाव से ही शून्य चित्त है पर प्रमाद से विषयों की भावना करता है और सोता हुआ भी जागने के समान है – वह पुरुष संसार से मुक्त है।
english_translation: By nature, the mind is empty, but through carelessness, it creates feelings about objects; even in sleep, if one remains aware, they are free from the cycle of reactivity.
essence: The mind is naturally empty; carelessness fills it with restless feelings.
simple_meaning: Your natural mind is empty and calm. Carelessness causes it to create feelings and distractions, but even in sleep, awareness means freedom from reactivity.
insight: It teaches you to recognize carelessness as the cause of mental agitation and to nurture awareness even in passive states.
modern_relevance: When your mind drifts into worry or distraction, remember its true nature is empty and calm—staying aware is freedom.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व धनानि क्व मित्राणि क्व मे विषयदस्यवः ।
क्व शास्त्रं क्व च विज्ञानं यदा मे गलिता स्पृहा ॥
translation: जब मेरी स्पृहा नष्ट हो गयी तब मेरे लिए कहाँ धन, कहाँ मित्र, कहाँ विषयीरूप चोर, कहाँ शास्त्र और कहाँ ज्ञान है।
english_translation: When my desire was destroyed, then where were wealth, friends, sensual thieves, scriptures, and knowledge for me?
essence: Without desire, all attachments including wealth and knowledge lose their grip.
simple_meaning: When your craving or desire disappears, things like money, friends, sensual distractions, scriptures, and knowledge lose their importance to you.
insight: It teaches you to see desire as the root of attachment, so letting it go frees you from external dependencies.
modern_relevance: You finally stop chasing likes, money, or approval—suddenly, all those things feel empty and irrelevant.
speaker: Janaka

verse_text:
विज्ञाते साक्षिपुरुषे परमात्मनि चेश्वरे ।
नैराश्ये बन्धमोक्षे च न चिन्ता मुक्तये मम ॥
translation: साक्षी पुरुष, परमात्मा, ईश्वर, आशा-मुक्ति तथा बन्ध-मुक्ति के जान लेने पर मुझे मुक्ति के लिए चिन्ता नहीं है।
english_translation: Knowing the witness, the pure awareness, the supreme being, and the lord, I have no worry about liberation or bondage.
essence: Knowing your true self as witness ends all worry about bondage and freedom.
simple_meaning: When you understand your true self as the witness and the supreme being, you stop worrying about being bound or free.
insight: It shifts your focus from fearing entrapment or chasing freedom to simply knowing your true self beyond those states.
modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by endless worries about success or failure, but realizing your deeper awareness dissolves all that anxiety.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अन्तर्विकल्पशून्यस्य बहिः स्वच्छन्दचारिणः ।
भ्रान्तस्येव दशास्तास्तास्तादृशा एव जानते ॥
translation: जो भीतर विकल्प से शून्य है और बाहर भ्रान्त हुए पुरुष की भाँति स्वछन्दचारी है । ऐसे पुरुष की भिन्न-भिन्न दशाओं को वैसी ही दशा वाले पुरुष जानते हैं।
english_translation: The one who is free of inner doubt and moves freely outside is known by others who share the same state.
essence: Only those free inside can truly recognize freedom in others.
simple_meaning: A person whose mind is free of inner doubts moves freely in the world and is recognized by others who share that same freedom.
insight: It teaches you to see that authentic freedom is recognized only by those who have experienced it themselves.
modern_relevance: You feel completely calm inside and act without hesitation, and others who have found that same calm recognize you instantly.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
यथातथोपदेशेन कृतार्थः सत्त्वबुद्धिमान् ।
आजीवमपि जिज्ञासुः परस्तत्र विमुह्यति ॥
translation: सत्व बुद्धि वाला पुरुष थोड़े से उपदेश से ही कृतार्थ होता है । असत् बुद्धि वाला पुरुष आजीवन जिज्ञासा करके उसमें मोह को ही प्राप्त होता है।
english_translation: A person with pure wisdom is fulfilled by little teaching; one with impure wisdom remains confused, endlessly seeking elsewhere.
essence: Clear wisdom quickly fulfills; confusion endlessly chases more and more.
simple_meaning: Some people grasp wisdom quickly from few teachings, but others stay confused, searching endlessly for answers.
insight: It shifts your effort from gathering more information to trusting simple, clear insights that satisfy your mind.
modern_relevance: You’ve sat through many talks and read many books but still feel lost; sometimes clarity arrives simply, not from endless searching.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
मोक्षो विषयवैरस्यं बन्धो वैषयिको रसः ।
एतावदेव विज्ञानं यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
translation: विषयों में विरसता मोक्ष है, विषयों में रस बन्ध है । इतना ही विज्ञान है । तू जैसा चाहे वैसा कर।
english_translation: Freedom is finding disinterest in pleasures; attachment to them is bondage. This much is true knowledge. Do as you wish.
essence: Freedom is the disinterest in sensory pleasures; attachment creates bondage.
simple_meaning: True freedom comes when you stop craving pleasures; being attached to them keeps you bound. Understand this and act as you wish.
insight: It shifts your mindset from chasing pleasure to choosing freedom by releasing interest in outcomes.
modern_relevance: You scroll endlessly for likes or feel restless chasing pleasures, yet peace comes when these cravings lose their grip.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
वाग्मिप्राज्ञामहोद्योगं जनं मूकजडालसम् ।
करोति तत्त्वबोधोऽयमतस्त्यक्तो बुभुक्षभिः ॥
translation: यह तत्व बोध वाचाल, बुद्धिमान और महाउद्योगी पुरुष को गूँगा, जड़ और आलसी कर जाता है । इसलिए भोग की अभिलाषा रखने वालों के द्वारा तत्व-बोध त्यक्त है।
english_translation: This knowledge of truth makes the eloquent, wise, and diligent man mute, inert, and lazy; therefore, those craving sensory pleasures abandon this knowledge.
essence: Profound truth silences the restless mind and dims craving for sensory pleasures.
simple_meaning: Deep understanding of truth can make even the most active and clever person quiet and inactive because it lessens desire for pleasures.
insight: Shift your focus from constant doing and craving to deep knowing that naturally reduces restless activity.
modern_relevance: You push yourself hard chasing success and distractions, but true insight can make you pause, slowing your restless striving for fleeting rewards.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
न त्वं देहो न ते देहो भोक्ता कर्ता न वा भवान् ।
चिद्रूपोऽसि सदा साक्षी निरपेक्षः सुखं चर ॥
translation: तू शरीर नहीं है, न तेरा शरीर है, तू भोक्ता और कर्ता भी नहीं है । तू वो चैतन्यरूप है, नित्य है, साक्षी है, निरपेक्ष है । तू सुखपूर्वक विचर।
english_translation: You are not the body, nor is the body yours; you are neither the experiencer nor the doer. You are the consciousness itself, always the witness, impartial, and moving in bliss.
essence: You are pure awareness, never the body or its doer, always peacefully witnessing.
simple_meaning: You are not your body, nor the one who acts or experiences. You are pure consciousness, always watching calmly and enjoying peace.
insight: It shifts your focus from identifying with body and roles to recognizing yourself as the impartial observer beneath all experiences.
modern_relevance: When stress hits, notice how the restless mind is not really you but just passing. Your true self stays calm beyond all that.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
रागद्वेषौ मनोधर्मौ न मनस्ते कदाचन ।
निर्विकल्पोऽसि बोधात्मा निर्विकारः सुखं चर ॥
translation: राग और द्वेष मन के धर्म हैं । तू कभी मन नहीं है । तू निर्विकल्प, निर्विकार, बोध-स्वरूप आत्मा है । तू सुखपूर्वक विचर।
english_translation: Attachment and aversion are qualities of the mind. You are never the mind. You are the awareness beyond distinctions and changes, dwelling in peaceful bliss.
essence: You are unchanging awareness, not the ever-changing mind with its likes and dislikes.
simple_meaning: Attachment and aversion arise in the mind, but you are not the mind. You are the unchanging awareness that experiences peaceful happiness.
insight: It teaches you to separate your sense of self from the mind’s emotional ups and downs, resting as the witness instead.
modern_relevance: When your emotions swing between liking and disliking, remember you are the calm that notices these shifts, not the shifts themselves.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि ।
विज्ञाय निरहङ्कारो निर्ममस्त्वं सुखी भव ॥
translation: सब भूतों में आत्म को तथा सब भूतों में आत्मा को जानकर तू अहँकाररहित और ममता रहित है । तू सुखी हो।
english_translation: Knowing the true self in all beings and all beings in the true self, be free from ego and possessiveness; be happy.
essence: True happiness arises when you know yourself as one with all, free from ego and possessiveness.
simple_meaning: Recognize that your true self is present in all beings and all beings exist in your true self. This understanding frees you from ego and possessiveness and brings happiness.
insight: Shift from seeing yourself as isolated to recognizing your shared true self with all beings, dissolving ego and possessiveness.
modern_relevance: When you stop seeing others as separate and stop clinging to your identity, you find relief from jealousy, competition, and loneliness.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
विश्वं स्फुरति यत्रेदं तरङ्गा इव सागरे ।
तत्त्वमेव न सन्देहश्चिन्मूर्ते विज्वरो भव ॥
translation: जिसमें यह संसार तरंगों की भाँति स्फुरित होता है वह तू ही है, इसमें सन्देह नहीं है । हे चैतन्य स्वरूप ! तू सन्ताप रहित हो।
english_translation: You are the one in whom this entire world shines like waves in the ocean; there is no doubt about this. O embodiment of pure awareness, you are beyond suffering.
essence: You are the unchanging ocean in which the world’s waves rise and fall without disturbing you.
simple_meaning: The entire world appears like waves on the ocean, but you are the ocean itself—pure awareness without suffering.
insight: Shift your focus from fleeting experiences to your unchanging awareness, finding freedom from emotional turmoil.
modern_relevance: When stress and change feel overwhelming, remember you are the calm, vast presence beneath the shifting surface.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
श्रद्धस्व तात श्रद्धस्व नात्र मोऽहं कुरुष्व भोः ।
ज्ञानस्वरूपो भगवानात्मा त्वं प्रकृतेः परः ॥
translation: हे तात ! श्रद्धा कर, श्रद्धा कर । इसमें मोह मत कर । तू ज्ञानस्वरूप, भगवान्-स्वरूप आत्मा है तथा प्रकृति से परे है।
english_translation: Have faith, son, have faith; do not be confused. You are the true self, embodying wisdom and beyond the natural world.
essence: You are pure wisdom beyond nature; trust removes all confusion.
simple_meaning: You are urged to have faith without confusion because your true nature is wisdom itself and beyond the changing natural world.
insight: It teaches you to replace doubt with trust in the true self beyond appearances and distractions.
modern_relevance: When your mind is restless and confused, trust the deeper wisdom within you that is untouched by everyday worries.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
गुणैः संवेष्टितो देहस्तिष्ठत्यायाति याति च ।
आत्मा न गन्ता नागन्ता किमेनमनुशोचसि ॥
translation: गुणों से लिप्त यह शरीर रहता है, आता है और जाता है । किन्तु आत्मा न जाने वाला है, न आने वाला । इसके लिए क्यों सोच करता है।
english_translation: The body, covered by qualities, stays, comes, and goes; the true self neither comes nor goes. Why do you grieve over this?
essence: Your true self remains unchanged while the body moves and changes; grief is unnecessary.
simple_meaning: Your body changes and moves, but your true self remains unchanged and does not come or go. There is no need to grieve over what is always steady.
insight: Shift your focus from the changing body to the unchanging true self to reduce grief and attachment.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by life's ups and downs, remember your core self remains steady beyond all changes.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
देहस्तिष्ठतु कल्पान्तं गच्छत्वद्यैव वा पुनः ।
क्व वृद्धिः क्व च वा हानिस्तव चिन्मात्ररूपिणः ॥
translation: देह चाहे अन्त तक रहे, चाहे वह अभी चली जाए, तुम चैतन्य-रूप वालों की कहाँ वृद्धि है, कहाँ नाश है।
english_translation: Whether the body remains until the end of an age or leaves now, where is increase or decrease for you, the one who is pure consciousness?
essence: Pure consciousness remains unchanged regardless of the body's coming and going.
simple_meaning: Your true nature as pure consciousness does not grow or diminish, even if your body changes or disappears.
insight: It shifts your focus from physical identity to recognizing your unchanging inner being beyond appearances.
modern_relevance: You watch your body age or face illness, yet your inner awareness remains untouched and whole, beyond these shifts.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
त्वय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्ववीचिः स्वभावतः ।
उदेतु वास्तमायातु न ते वृद्धिर्न वा क्षतिः ॥
translation: तुझ अनन्त महासमुद्र में विश्वरूप तरंग अपने स्वभाव से उदय और अस्त को प्राप्त होती है, किन्तु न तेरी वृद्धि है, न नाश है।
english_translation: In your infinite great ocean, the universal wave naturally rises and sets, yet it is neither your growth nor your decay.
essence: Your true self remains unchanged amid all natural changes around it.
simple_meaning: You are like an endless ocean where waves rise and fall naturally, but these changes do not affect your true nature.
insight: It teaches you to see yourself as the unchanging presence beneath all fluctuations and experiences.
modern_relevance: When emotions or events surge and fade around you, your core remains steady beyond their ebb and flow.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
तात चिन्मात्ररूपोऽसि न ते भिन्नमिदं जगत् ।
अतः कस्य कथं कुत्र हेयोपादेयकल्पना ॥
translation: हे तात ! तू चैतन्यरूप है, तेरा यह जगत तुझसे भिन्न नहीं है । इसलिये हेय और उपादेय की कल्पना किसकी, क्योंकर और कहाँ हो सकती है।
english_translation: Dear one, you are pure consciousness; this world is not separate from you. So who can be despised or praised, and where or why could such ideas arise?
essence: You are pure awareness; ideas of blame or praise arise only from false separation.
simple_meaning: You are pure awareness, and the world around you is not truly separate from your true self. Therefore, ideas of someone being worthy of blame or praise do not truly apply.
insight: It teaches you to question the reality of separation and judgment, shifting your view to see unity beneath appearances.
modern_relevance: You might notice how quickly your mind judges others or situations as good or bad. This verse invites you to see that at the core, you and everything else share the same essence beyond those judgments.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
एकस्मिन्नव्यये शान्ते चिदाकाशेऽमले त्वयि ।
कुतो जन्म कुतो कर्म कुतोऽहङ्कार एव च ॥
translation: तुझ एक निर्मल, अविनाशी, शान्त और चैतन्यरूप आकाश में कहाँ जन्म है, कहाँ कर्म है और कहाँ अहंकार।
english_translation: In you, the pure, unchanging, peaceful, and conscious sky, where is birth, where is action, and where is ego?
essence: Your true self is pure and peaceful, beyond birth, action, and ego.
simple_meaning: You are like a pure, peaceful, unchanging sky beyond birth, action, and ego.
insight: Recognize that your true self is distinct from birth, actions, and ego, freeing you from identification with them.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your mistakes or identity, remember your deeper self is untouched and free like a clear sky.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
यत्त्वं पश्यसि तत्रैकस्त्वमेव प्रतिभाससे ।
किं पृथक् भासते स्वर्णात् कटकाङ्गदनूपुरम् ॥
translation: जिसको तू देखता है, उसमें एक तू ही भासता है । क्या कंगन, बाजूबन्द और नूपुर सोने से भिन्न भासते है।
english_translation: What you see is only you shining there; do the golden bracelet, armlet, and anklet shine differently from gold?
essence: The same light shines through you and all you perceive; there is no real difference.
simple_meaning: Everything you see shines with the same light—you and all objects share that one radiance.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing things as separate to recognizing a single light animating all appearances.
modern_relevance: When you look around, notice how the same awareness lights up your thoughts, feelings, and the world outside alike.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अयं सोऽहमयं नाहं विभागमिति सन्त्यज ।
सर्वमात्मेति निश्चित्य निःसङ्कल्पः सुखी भव ॥
translation: ‘यह मैं हूँ’, ‘यह मैं नहीं हूँ’ ऐसे विभाग को छोड़ दे । ‘सब आत्मा है’ ऐसा निश्चय करके तू संकल्परहित हो, सुखी हो।
english_translation: Let go of the division 'This is me' and 'This is not me.' Be certain that everything is the true self, be without doubt, and be happy.
essence: Happiness arises when you drop the division between self and other completely.
simple_meaning: You should stop dividing experience into 'this is me' and 'this is not me.' Instead, be sure that all is the true self and live without conflicting thoughts to be happy.
insight: It shifts your mind from clinging to separateness toward embracing wholeness without hesitation.
modern_relevance: When you stop labeling experiences as 'mine' or 'not mine,' you ease mental tension and find calm amid daily chaos.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
तवैवाज्ञानतो विश्वं त्वमेकः परमार्थतः ।
त्वत्तोऽन्यो नास्ति संसारी नासंसारी च कश्चन ॥
translation: तेरे ही अज्ञान से विश्व है । परमार्थतः तू एक है । तेरे अतिरिक्त कोई दूसरा नहीं है । न संसारी है, न असंसारी है।
english_translation: The entire universe exists due to your ignorance. In ultimate reality, you alone are one. There is no other besides you, neither bound nor free.
essence: You alone are the singular ultimate reality beyond all illusion and duality.
simple_meaning: All that seems to exist comes from your own ignorance. In truth, you alone are the singular reality, beyond being bound or free.
insight: It invites you to see beyond appearances and recognize that your true nature is the sole reality, free from all dualities.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by the chaos around you, remember that beneath it all, your true self remains untouched and singular.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
भ्रान्तिमात्रमिदं विश्वं न किञ्चिदिति निश्चयी ।
निर्वासनः स्फूर्तिमात्रो न किञ्चिदिव शाम्यति ॥
translation: यह विश्व भ्रान्तिमात्र है और कुछ नहीं है । ऐसा निश्चयपूर्वक जानने वाला वासनारहित और चैतन्यमात्र है । वह ऐसी शान्ति को प्राप्त है मानो कुछ नहीं है।
english_translation: This entire world is merely an illusion; one who is certain of this, free from desire and full of pure consciousness, attains a peace as if nothing exists.
essence: True peace arises from seeing the world as illusion and resting in pure awareness.
simple_meaning: The world you see is just an illusion. When you fully realize this without desire and rest in pure consciousness, you experience a deep peace as if nothing disturbs you.
insight: It shifts your mind from clinging to appearances toward resting in pure awareness without disturbance.
modern_relevance: When everything feels overwhelming or uncertain, realizing that much of what disturbs you is illusion can bring surprising calm and clarity.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
एक एव भवाम्भोधावासीदस्ति भविष्यति ।
न ते बन्धोऽस्ति मोक्षो वा कृत्यकृत्यः सुखं चर ॥
translation: संसाररूपी समुद्र में तू एक ही था और होगा । तेरा बन्ध और मोक्ष नहीं है । तू कृतकृत्य होकर सुखपूर्वक विचर।
english_translation: In the ocean of existence, you alone have always been and will always be. You have neither bondage nor freedom. Be fulfilled and move joyfully.
essence: You have always been complete beyond bondage or freedom.
simple_meaning: You have always existed as the one unchanging presence in the ocean of existence. You are not trapped or free because those ideas do not apply. Live fulfilled and joyful as you are.
insight: It shifts your view from striving for freedom to recognizing your already complete nature, freeing energy for joyful living.
modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by endless pressure to fix or improve yourself. This reminds you that you are already whole and free beneath it all.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
मा सङ्कल्पविकल्पाभ्यां चित्तं क्षोभय चिन्मय ।
उपशाम्य सुखं तिष्ठ स्वात्मन्यानन्दविग्रहे ॥
translation: हे चिन्मय ! तू चित्त को संकल्प और विकल्पों से क्षोभित मत कर । शान्त होकर आनन्दपूरित अपने स्वरूप में सुखपूर्वक स्थित हो ।
english_translation: O Conscious Being, do not disturb your mind with decisions and doubts. Calmly stay happily established in your blissful true nature.
essence: Calm your restless mind and rest happily in your true blissful nature.
simple_meaning: You should not disturb your mind with constant thinking and doubts. Instead, calmly remain happily rooted in your true self and its bliss.
insight: It shifts your attention from mental agitation to peaceful presence by calming your restless mind and resting in your true nature.
modern_relevance: Your mind races with endless questions and options. This verse invites you to pause, stop the noise, and rest in your natural happiness beneath the chaos.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
त्यजैव ध्यानं सर्वत्र मा किञ्चिद् हृदि धारय ।
आत्मा त्वं मुक्त एवासि किं विमृश्य करिष्यसि ॥
translation: सर्वत्र ध्यान को त्यागकर हृदय में कुछ भी धारण मत कर । तू आत्मा मुक्त ही है । तू विमर्श करके क्या करेगा।
english_translation: Abandon meditation everywhere; do not hold anything in your heart. You are the true self, already free. What will you gain by questioning?
essence: You are already free; holding on or questioning only blocks that truth.
simple_meaning: Let go of all meditation and mental holding; you are already free as the true self, so questioning is unnecessary.
insight: This shifts your focus from trying to attain freedom to simply resting in the freedom you already have.
modern_relevance: When you obsess over self-improvement or spiritual practices, this reminds you that your true freedom is already present beneath it all.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
आचक्ष्व श‍ृणु वा तात नानाशास्त्राण्यनेकशः ।
तथापि न तव स्वास्थ्यं सर्वविस्मरणाद् ऋते ॥
translation: तात ! अनेक शास्त्रों को अनेक प्रकार से तू कह अथवा सुन लेकिन सब के विस्मरण के बिना तुझे स्वास्थ्य नहीं मिलेगी।
english_translation: Listen well, son; you may speak or hear many scriptures in many ways, but without forgetting all of them, you will not find health.
essence: True well-being requires forgetting all teachings, not accumulating them.
simple_meaning: You can hear or speak many teachings, but true well-being comes only when you forget them all.
insight: It teaches you to release rigid attachment to knowledge, allowing natural peace to arise.
modern_relevance: You scroll endlessly through advice and ideas online but feel overwhelmed until you stop trying to retain every opinion.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
भोगं कर्म समाधिं वा कुरु विज्ञ तथापि ते ।
चित्तं निरस्तसर्वाशमत्यर्थं रोचयिष्यति ॥
translation: हे विज्ञ ! भोग, कर्म अथवा समाधि को तू चाहे साधे, तो भी तेरा चित्त स्वभाव से सभी आशयों से रहित होने पर भी अत्यधिक लोभायमान रहेगा।
english_translation: O wise one, whether you seek pleasure, action, or absorbed presence, your mind will still crave intensely even when free from all desires by nature.
essence: The mind craves intensely even when free from all desires by nature.
simple_meaning: Even if you pursue pleasure, action, or deep stillness, your mind naturally continues to crave strongly despite seeming free of all desires.
insight: It shifts your understanding from expecting craving to end with success or stillness, to seeing craving as a persistent nature of the mind itself.
modern_relevance: You finish a project, meditate deeply, or enjoy a moment of joy — but still your mind pulls you toward wanting more, restless as ever.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन ।
अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥
translation: प्रयास से सब लोग दुःखी हैं, इसको कोई नहीं जानता है । इसी उपदेश से भाग्यवान लोग निर्वाण को प्राप्त होते हैं।
english_translation: Effort causes all suffering; no one truly knows this. By this teaching alone, the fortunate attain freedom.
essence: Suffering comes from effort; true freedom arises from seeing this clearly.
simple_meaning: Trying too hard causes suffering, but understanding this leads to true freedom.
insight: It teaches you to notice how effort can create resistance and suffering, shifting your approach toward letting be.
modern_relevance: You push yourself relentlessly, chasing success or control, unaware that the very effort fuels your stress and exhaustion.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
व्यापारे खिद्यते यस्तु निमेषोन्मेषयोरपि ।
तस्यालस्य धुरीणस्य सुखं नन्यस्य कस्यचित् ॥
translation: जो आँख के खोलने और ढकने के व्यापार से दुःखी होता है, वह आलसी-शिरोमणि का ही सुख है । दूसरे किसी का नहीं।
english_translation: The one who suffers from the opening and closing of the eyes is the master of laziness's own pleasure, not anyone else's.
essence: Suffering from fleeting distractions is the product of your own restless habit.
simple_meaning: If you feel troubled by every little change or distraction, that restlessness is your own habit causing suffering.
insight: It teaches you to notice how clinging to every distraction creates your own suffering and to loosen that grip.
modern_relevance: When a tiny annoyance like a phone notification unsettles you, it's your restless habit causing your suffering, not the event itself.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
इदं कृतमिदं नेति द्वन्द्वैर्मुक्तं यदा मनः ।
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षेषु निरपेक्षं तदा भवेत् ॥
translation: यह किया गया है और यह नहीं किया गया, ऐसे द्वन्द्व से जब मन मुक्त हो तब वह धर्म, अर्थ, काम और मोक्ष के प्रति उदासीन हो जाता है।
english_translation: When the mind is free from the pairs of opposites 'this is done' and 'this is not done,' it becomes indifferent to dharma, wealth, desire, and freedom.
essence: True freedom arises when the mind transcends all judgments of action and inaction.
simple_meaning: The mind becomes free when it stops seeing actions as done or not done and no longer clings to duty, wealth, desire, or freedom.
insight: It teaches you to let go of judging actions as success or failure and to rest in impartial awareness.
modern_relevance: You finish a big task and stop obsessing over whether it was perfect or not; your mind rests beyond judgment.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
विरक्तो विषयद्वेष्टा रागी विषयलोलुपः ।
ग्रहमोक्षविहीनस्तु न विरक्तो न रागवान् ॥
translation: विषय का दोषी विरक्त है । विषयलोलुप रागी है । जो ग्रहण और त्याग दोनों से रहित है वह न विरक्त है, न रागवान है।
english_translation: The one free from attachment is averse to sense objects; the one attached is desirous of them. One who is neither taking nor renouncing is neither detached nor attached.
essence: You cannot be truly detached without rejecting desire, nor truly attached without embracing it.
simple_meaning: You are either attached to things or truly detached. Being stuck between wanting and rejecting means you are neither.
insight: This verse teaches you to recognize that hesitation between wanting and rejecting causes inner turmoil.
modern_relevance: You feel uneasy when you’re indecisive—neither fully embracing nor letting go of a situation or desire.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
हेयोपादेयता तावत्संसारविटपाङ्कुरः ।
स्पृहा जीवति यावद् वै निर्विचारदशास्पदम् ॥
translation: जब तक स्पृहा जीवित है – जो कि अविवेक की दशा है – तब तक हेय और उपादेय भी जीवित है – जो कि संसाररूपी वृक्ष का अंकुर है।
english_translation: As long as craving lives—the state of confusion—both what should be avoided and what should be attained continue to live, like sprouts on the tree of worldly existence.
essence: Craving sustains the endless cycle of desire and aversion in the restless mind.
simple_meaning: As long as you have craving, the cycle of wanting and avoiding continues like new sprouts on a tree of suffering.
insight: It shifts your view from chasing and avoiding to seeing craving itself as the root of unrest.
modern_relevance: When you feel caught between wanting something and fearing its opposite, that restless craving is what keeps your stress alive.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
प्रवृत्तौ जायते रागो निर्वृत्तौ द्वेष एव हि ।
निर्द्वन्द्वो बालवद् धीमान् एवमेव व्यवस्थितः ॥
translation: प्रवृत्ति से राग, व निवृत्ति से द्वेष पैदा होता है । इसलिए बुद्धिमान पुरुष द्वन्द्वमुक्त बालक के समान जैसा है, वैसा ही रहता है।
english_translation: Attachment arises in engagement, aversion arises in withdrawal; the wise remain free of duality like a child.
essence: Freedom arises by transcending attachment and aversion, staying peacefully beyond conflict.
simple_meaning: When you act, attachment to things arises; when you withdraw, aversion arises. The wise stay free from these opposites, like a peaceful child.
insight: You learn to observe your impulses without getting caught in attraction or rejection, stabilizing your mind like a child’s openness.
modern_relevance: You feel torn between chasing what you want and pushing away what you dislike. True calm comes when you stop reacting both ways.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
हातुमिच्छति संसारं रागी दुःखजिहासया ।
वीतरागो हि निर्दुःखस्तस्मिन्नपि न खिद्यति ॥
translation: रागी पुरुष दुःख से बचने के लिए संसार को त्यागना चाहता है लेकिन वीतरागी दुःखमुक्त होकर संसार के बीच भी खेद को प्राप्त नहीं होता।
english_translation: A person attached to desire wants to leave the world to avoid suffering, but one free from desire is without suffering and feels no regret even within the world.
essence: Freedom from desire ends suffering and regret even while engaged in the world.
simple_meaning: Desire makes you want to avoid suffering by leaving the world. Without desire, you no longer suffer or regret even when in the world.
insight: It shifts your view from avoiding pain by escape to embracing presence without regret.
modern_relevance: You may feel like quitting when problems arise, but real freedom lets you face life without pain or regret.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
यस्याभिमानो मोक्षेऽपि देहेऽपि ममता तथा ।
न च ज्ञानी न वा योगी केवलं दुःखभागसौ ॥
translation: जिसका मोक्ष के प्रति अहंकार है और वैसी ही शरीर के प्रति ममता है, वह न तो योगी है, न ज्ञानी है । वह केवल दुःख का भागी है।
english_translation: One who clings with ego to freedom and attachment to the body is neither yogi nor knower, only a partaker in suffering.
essence: Ego attachment to freedom or body keeps you trapped in suffering, not truly free.
simple_meaning: Holding pride about being free or attachment to your body means you aren’t truly wise or free but caught in suffering.
insight: It teaches to examine how ego clings even to positive states, and to release that grip for genuine peace.
modern_relevance: You may chase personal growth or health, but pride in these achievements can secretly keep you restless and unhappy.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
हरो यद्युपदेष्टा ते हरिः कमलजोऽपि वा ।
तथापि न तव स्वाथ्यं सर्वविस्मरणादृते ॥
translation: यदि तेरा उपदेशक शिव है, विष्णु है अथवा ब्रह्मा है तो भी सबके विस्मरण के बिना तुझे स्वास्थ्य नहीं होगी ।
english_translation: Even if your teacher is Shiva, Vishnu, or Brahma, you will not find health without forgetting all else.
essence: True well-being requires forgetting all else, regardless of who teaches you.
simple_meaning: No matter who teaches you—even the greatest teachers—true health or well-being comes only when you forget all distractions and attachments.
insight: It shifts focus from relying on external authorities to internal freedom through letting go of all attachments.
modern_relevance: You might admire many experts or mentors, but true growth happens only when you stop clinging to all distractions and fully commit.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
तेन ज्ञानफलं प्राप्तं योगाभ्यासफलं तथा ।
तृप्तः स्वच्छेन्द्रियो नित्यमेकाकी रमते तु यः ॥
translation: जो पुरुष तृप्त है, शुद्ध इन्द्रियों वाला है और सदा एकाकी रमण करता है उसी को ज्ञान और योगाभ्यास का फल प्राप्त होता है।
english_translation: The person who is content, pure in senses, and constantly delights in solitude attains the fruit of knowledge and yoga practice.
essence: Contentment, pure senses, and solitude unlock the real fruits of knowledge and yoga.
simple_meaning: You gain the full benefit of knowledge and yoga when you are satisfied, your senses are clear, and you enjoy solitude.
insight: It shifts your focus from external achievements to cultivating inner contentment and sensory clarity as the foundation for progress.
modern_relevance: When you stop chasing distractions, feel satisfied with yourself, and find calm in solitude, your efforts in growth and learning genuinely deepen.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
न कदाचिज्जगत्यस्मिन् तत्त्वज्ञो हन्त खिद्यति ।
यत एकेन तेनेदं पूर्णं ब्रह्माण्डमण्डलम् ॥
translation: हन्त ! तत्त्वज्ञानी इस जगत में कभी खेद को प्राप्त नहीं होता है क्योंकि उसी एक से यह ब्रह्माण्ड मण्डल पूर्ण है।
english_translation: The true knower of reality never experiences regret because the entire universe is complete in that one.
essence: Regret cannot arise when you recognize the universe is fully complete in oneness.
simple_meaning: Someone who truly understands reality never feels regret because they see the whole universe as complete in one.
insight: It shifts your mind from scarcity and loss to completeness and acceptance in all experience.
modern_relevance: You look back at a decision and realize everything unfolded as it should — no room for regret.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
न जातु विषयाः केऽपि स्वारामं हर्षयन्त्यमी ।
सल्लकीपल्लवप्रीतमिवेभं निम्बपल्लवाः ॥
translation: जैसे सल्लकी के पत्तों से प्रसन्न हुए हाथी को नीम के पत्ते हर्षित नहीं करते हैं, वैसे ही ये विषय आत्मा में रमण करने वाले को कभी नहीं हर्षित करते हैं।
english_translation: Just as a neem leaf never delights an elephant pleased by sal tree leaves, worldly objects never delight the self immersed in itself.
essence: True happiness arises only when the self is established, untouched by worldly things.
simple_meaning: If you are truly settled in your own self, external things cannot make you happy or disturb you.
insight: It teaches you to root your happiness inside yourself, so outer changes don’t disturb your peace.
modern_relevance: You get excited about some new gadget or trend but soon it loses charm—your deeper self stays calm amid such changes.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
यस्तु भोगेषु भुक्तेषु न भवत्यधिवासितः ।
अभुक्तेषु निराकाङ्क्षी तदृशो भवदुर्लभः ॥
translation: जो भोगे हुए भोगों में वासना नहीं रखता तथा भोगे हुए विषयों के प्रति आकांक्षा नहीं रखता, ऐसा मनुष्य संसार में दुर्लभ है।
english_translation: A person who does not cling to pleasures already enjoyed and does not desire those unexperienced is rare in this world.
essence: True rarity lies in neither clinging to past nor craving future pleasures.
simple_meaning: Someone who neither holds onto past pleasures nor desires new ones is very rare in the world.
insight: It shifts your mind from clinging to pleasures toward accepting experience without desire or attachment.
modern_relevance: You notice how most people replay past moments or chase new experiences, yet true ease comes when you stop holding on or wanting more.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
बुभुक्षुरिह संसारे मुमुक्षुरपि दृश्यते ।
भोगमोक्षनिराकाङ्क्षी विरलो हि महाशयः ॥
translation: इस संसार में भोग की इच्छा रखने वाले और मोक्ष की इच्छा रखने वाले दोनों देखे जाते हैं, लेकिन भोग और मोक्ष दोनों के प्रति निरकांक्षी विरल महाशय ही मिलेगा।
english_translation: In this world, both those who desire pleasure and those who seek freedom are seen, but rare indeed is the noble one who desires neither pleasure nor freedom.
essence: True nobility lies in freeing yourself from every desire, pleasure or freedom alike.
simple_meaning: In life, some chase pleasure, others seek freedom, but very few release all desires completely.
insight: It invites you to notice desire itself as a barrier and consider stepping beyond all wanting.
modern_relevance: You scroll social media, see people chasing happiness or escape, but feel drawn to simply rest beyond all craving.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षेषु जीविते मरणे तथा ।
कस्याप्युदारचित्तस्य हेयोपादेयता न हि ॥
translation: कोई उदारचित्त ही धर्म, अर्थ, काम, मोक्ष, जीवन और मृत्यु के प्रति हेय-उपादेय का भाव नहीं रखता।
english_translation: No generous-hearted person regards duty, wealth, desire, freedom, life, or death as contemptible or to be rejected.
essence: A generous heart accepts all experiences—duty, desire, life, and death—as worthy.
simple_meaning: A truly generous heart does not reject or look down on any aspect of life or death, nor on duty, desire, or freedom.
insight: It teaches you to embrace life's full spectrum without judgment, dissolving resistance and inner conflict.
modern_relevance: When faced with challenges like career pressure, personal desires, or fears about mortality, you can choose to hold all experiences without rejection or fear.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
वाञ्छा न विश्वविलये न द्वेषस्तस्य च स्थितौ ।
यथा जीविकया तस्माद् धन्य आस्ते यथा सुखम् ॥
translation: जिसमें विश्व के विलय की इच्छा नहीं है और न उसकी स्थिति के प्रति द्वेष है, इसलिए वह धन्य पुरुष यथाप्राप्य आजीविका से सुखपूर्वक जीता है।
english_translation: One who has neither desire for the world's destruction nor hatred toward its state lives blessed, content with what sustains life.
essence: Blessed living comes from neither craving the world’s end nor hating its state.
simple_meaning: You live a happy, blessed life when you neither desire the world to end nor hate how it is, accepting what supports your living.
insight: It teaches you to release both craving for radical change and aversion toward current conditions to find contentment.
modern_relevance: You’ve stopped wishing your situation was different and stopped resenting what you can’t control, feeling a quiet ease with life as it is.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
कृतार्थोऽनेन ज्ञानेनेत्येवं गलितधीः कृती ।
पश्यन् श‍ृण्वन् स्पृशन् जिघ्रन्न् अश्नन्नास्ते यथा सुखम् ॥
translation: इस ज्ञान से कृतार्थ अनुभव कर, गलित हो गयी बुद्धि जिसकी, ऐसा कृतकार्य पुरुष देखता हुआ, स्पर्श करता हुआ, सूँघता हुआ, खाता हुआ सुखपूर्वक रहता है।
english_translation: With this knowledge, the wise feel fulfilled; their confused mind dissolves. Such a fulfilled person experiences joy while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, and eating.
essence: Fulfillment comes when the confused mind dissolves and joy naturally arises in all experiences.
simple_meaning: When your confusion dissolves through true knowledge, you feel fulfilled and enjoy life fully through all your senses.
insight: It teaches you to recognize that true fulfillment comes from clarity that frees the mind, not from external pleasures alone.
modern_relevance: You notice how overwhelming thoughts vanish sometimes, letting you fully enjoy a meal or a walk without distraction.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
शून्या दृष्टिर्वृथा चेष्टा विकलानीन्द्रियाणि च ।
न स्पृहा न विरक्तिर्वा क्षीणसंसारसागरे ॥
translation: जिसका संसार सागर क्षीण हो गया है, ऐसे पुरुष में न तृष्णा है, न विरक्ति है । उसकी दृष्टि शून्य हो गयी है, चेष्टा व्यर्थ हो गयी है और इन्द्रियाँ विफल हो गयी हैं।
english_translation: A person whose ocean of worldly existence has been exhausted has no thirst, no detachment; their vision is empty, efforts are futile, and senses ineffective.
essence: When worldly craving ends, both desire and detachment disappear into emptiness.
simple_meaning: When a person’s engagement with the world is completely exhausted, they no longer crave or reject anything. Their vision feels empty, efforts seem pointless, and the senses lose their power.
insight: It teaches you to recognize when desire and aversion both lose their hold, revealing a deeper stillness beneath restless effort.
modern_relevance: You’ve worn yourself out trying to control outcomes, pushing and pulling, until nothing excites or repels you anymore—and in that quiet, a new kind of freedom begins.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
न जागर्ति न निद्राति नोन्मीलति न मीलति ।
अहो परदशा क्वापि वर्तते मुक्तचेतसः ॥
translation: वह न जागता है, न मरता है, न पलक खोलता है, न पलक बन्द करता है । अहो ! मुक्तचेतस् की कैसी परम दशा होती है।
english_translation: The liberated mind neither wakes nor sleeps, neither opens nor closes the eyelids; such is the supreme state of the free mind.
essence: Freedom is the unchanging state beyond waking, sleeping, and all dualities.
simple_meaning: The truly free mind is beyond waking, sleeping, or any change in awareness. It remains in an unchanging supreme state.
insight: It teaches you to recognize freedom as the unchanging awareness beyond all mental fluctuations.
modern_relevance: When your mind feels restless and distracted, imagine a state beyond all shifting moods and thoughts—pure, steady, and free.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
सर्वत्र दृश्यते स्वस्थः सर्वत्र विमलाशयः ।
समस्तवासना मुक्तो मुक्तः सर्वत्र राजते ॥
translation: मुक्त पुरुष सर्वत्र स्वस्थ, सर्वत्र विमल आशय वाला दिखाई देता है और सब वासनाओं से रहित सर्वत्र सुशोभित होता है।
english_translation: The liberated person appears established everywhere, with a pure heart everywhere, free from all desires, shining everywhere.
essence: Freedom shines as steady purity and desirelessness everywhere you go.
simple_meaning: A truly free person is steady and pure in every place, free from all desires, and naturally radiant.
insight: It teaches you to recognize your freedom and purity as constant, not tied to location or situations.
modern_relevance: You walk into any room and feel calm, clear, and unaffected by distractions or cravings around you.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
पश्यन् श‍ृण्वन् स्पृशन् जिघ्रन्न् अश्नन् गृण्हन् वदन् व्रजन् ।
ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो मुक्त एव महाशयः ॥
translation: देखता हुआ, सुनता हुआ, स्पर्श करता हुआ, सूँघता हुआ, खाता हुआ, ग्रहण करता हुआ, बोलता हुआ, चलता हुआ, हित और अहित से मुक्त महाशय निश्चय ही जीवन मुक्त है।
english_translation: Seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, taking, speaking, walking—free from benefit and harm, the great being is truly free in life.
essence: True freedom means engaging with life without being bound by gain or loss.
simple_meaning: You can experience the world through all senses and actions without becoming attached to benefits or harms, remaining free within life.
insight: It teaches you to remain centered and unattached while fully participating in life's sensory and social experiences.
modern_relevance: You attend a lively gathering, fully present and engaged, yet your peace stays unshaken by praise or criticism.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
न निन्दति न च स्तौति न हृष्यति न कुप्यति ।
न ददाति न गृण्हाति मुक्तः सर्वत्र नीरसः ॥
translation: मुक्तपुरुष सर्वत्र रसरहित है । वह न निन्दा करता है, न स्तुति करता है, न हर्षित होता है, न क्रुद्ध होता है, न लेता है, न देता है।
english_translation: The liberated person is free from all emotions everywhere; they neither blame nor praise, neither rejoice nor get angry, neither give nor take.
essence: True freedom is steady presence beyond all emotional reactions.
simple_meaning: A truly free person is emotionally steady everywhere, not moved by praise, blame, joy, anger, giving, or taking.
insight: It teaches you to observe emotions without getting pulled into them or reacting impulsively.
modern_relevance: In moments when social media praise or criticism flood your mind, you can stay calm and not get swept away.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
सानुरागां स्त्रियं दृष्ट्वा मृत्युं वा समुपस्थितम् ।
अविह्वलमनाः स्वस्थो मुक्त एव महाशयः ॥
translation: प्रीतियुक्त स्त्री और समीप में उपस्थित मृत्यु को देखकर जो महाशय अविचलमना और स्वस्थ रहता है, वह निश्चय ही मुक्त है।
english_translation: A great person who remains steady and healthy in mind upon seeing a beloved woman or the approaching death is surely free.
essence: True freedom is unshaken calm when facing both love and death.
simple_meaning: You are free when your mind remains calm and steady even when facing someone you love or death itself.
insight: It teaches you to steady your mind so external joys or fears no longer control your inner peace.
modern_relevance: You stay composed when a loved one leaves or when you confront your own limits, revealing your deepest freedom.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
सुखे दुःखे नरे नार्यां सम्पत्सु च विपत्सु च ।
विशेषो नैव धीरस्य सर्वत्र समदर्शिनः ॥
translation: समदर्शी धीर के लिए सुख और दुःख में, नर और नारी में, सम्पत्ति और विपत्ति में कहीं भेद नहीं है।
english_translation: For the steady-minded seer, there is no difference in pleasure or pain, man or woman, wealth or loss.
essence: A steady mind sees no difference in apparent opposites like pain and pleasure or wealth and loss.
simple_meaning: A person with steady wisdom sees no difference between pleasure and pain, men and women, or wealth and loss.
insight: It trains you to stop reacting to external labels and see events and people without bias or preference.
modern_relevance: You face the flood of news, social differences, and life’s ups and downs without losing your calm or judging.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
न हिंसा नैव कारुण्यं नौद्धत्यं न च दीनता ।
नाश्चर्यं नैव च क्षोभः क्षीणसंसरणे नरे ॥
translation: क्षीण हो गया है संसार जिसका, ऐसे मनुष्य में न हिंसा है, न करुणा है, न उद्दण्डता है, न दीनता, न आश्चर्य है, न क्षोभ।
english_translation: A person whose cycle of reactivity has ended shows no violence, no pity, no arrogance, no helplessness, no surprise, and no disturbance.
essence: True freedom means no emotional disturbance or reactive impulses remain.
simple_meaning: A person free from the cycle of reactive emotions no longer feels violence, pity, arrogance, helplessness, surprise, or inner disturbance.
insight: It teaches you to recognize and transcend emotional triggers, cultivating a steady and peaceful inner state.
modern_relevance: You notice how frustration or anger no longer grips you during a stressful conversation or unexpected event; your mind stays steady and undisturbed.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
न मुक्तो विषयद्वेष्टा न वा विषयलोलुपः ।
असंसक्तमना नित्यं प्राप्ताप्राप्तमुपाश्नुते ॥
translation: मुक्त पुरुष न विषयों से द्वेष करने वाला है, न विषयलोलुप है । सदा आसक्तिरहित मन वाला होकर प्राप्त और अप्राप्त वस्तु का उपभोग करता है।
english_translation: The liberated person neither hates nor craves objects; with a mind free from attachment, they constantly experience what comes and goes.
essence: Freedom means experiencing life without craving or aversion, with a mind untethered to outcomes.
simple_meaning: You don't need to hate or crave things. Staying free from attachment lets you accept whatever happens, good or bad.
insight: It teaches you to maintain inner balance by neither chasing after nor resisting experiences.
modern_relevance: You scroll through social media, sometimes thrilled, sometimes frustrated, yet your peace stays when you don’t cling or push away those feelings.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
समाधानसमाधानहिताहितविकल्पनाः ।
शून्यचित्तो न जानाति कैवल्यमिव संस्थितः ॥
translation: शून्यचित्त पुरुष समाधान और असमाधान के, हित और अहित के विकल्प को नहीं जानता है । वह तो कैवल्य जैसा स्थित है।
english_translation: The one whose mind is empty does not know alternatives of satisfaction or dissatisfaction, benefit or harm; they are established as if in perfect freedom.
essence: An empty mind no longer sees gain or loss and rests in perfect freedom.
