speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
निर्ममः शोभते धीरः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ।
सुभिन्नहृदयग्रन्थिर्विनिर्धूतरजस्तमः ॥
translation: जो ममता रहित है उसके लिए मिट्टी, पत्थर और सोना समान है । जिसके हृदय की ग्रन्थि टूट गयी है और जिसका रज-तम धुल गया है वह धीर पुरुष ही शोभता है।
english_translation: One who is free from attachment sees clay, stone, and gold as the same; whose heart’s knot is undone and whose impurities are removed is the truly steady person.
essence: Freedom from attachment makes all things appear equally radiant and steady.
simple_meaning: A person free from attachment sees all things the same, whether valuable or not, because their heart’s confusion is cleared.
insight: It teaches you to clear emotional confusion so external labels lose their power over your peace.
modern_relevance: You notice how you react differently to praise or criticism, success or failure—this verse invites you to find the calm beyond those swings.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
सर्वत्रानवधानस्य न किञ्चिद् वासना हृदि ।
मुक्तात्मनो वितृप्तस्य तुलना केन जायते ॥
translation: जो सर्वत्र व्यवधान से मुक्त उदासीन है और जिसके हृदय में कुछ भी वासना नहीं है । ऐसे तृप्त हुए मुक्तात्मा की किसके साथ तुलना हो सकती है।
english_translation: Someone who is free from all distraction and desire, whose heart holds no cravings, cannot be compared to anyone else.
essence: A heart free from desire and distraction is uniquely fulfilled and beyond comparison.
simple_meaning: A person who has no distractions or desires and whose heart is free from cravings is fully satisfied and incomparable.
insight: It teaches you to recognize that freedom from distraction and craving creates an incomparable inner satisfaction.
modern_relevance: When your mind is not pulled in every direction and your heart holds no craving, you experience a calm no one else can match.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
जानन्नपि न जानाति पश्यन्नपि न पश्यति ।
ब्रुवन्न् अपि न च ब्रूते कोऽन्यो निर्वासनादृते ॥
translation: वासनारहित पुरुष के अतिरिक्त दूसरा कौन है जो जानता हुआ भी नहीं जानता है, देखता हुआ भी नहीं देखता है, बोलता हुआ भी नहीं बोलता है।
english_translation: Who else exists without desire who neither knows, nor sees, nor speaks despite appearing to do so?
essence: The desireless self neither knows, sees, nor speaks, yet is the true witness.
simple_meaning: The true self is beyond desire and appears to know, see, and speak, yet actually does not act or perceive in the usual way.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with active knowing to recognizing silent, desireless presence.
modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed by endless thoughts and words, yet your true self remains untouched, watching silently beyond all noise.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
भिक्षुर्वा भूपतिर्वापि यो निष्कामः स शोभते ।
भावेषु गलिता यस्य शोभनाशोभना मतिः ॥
translation: जिसकी सब भावों में शोभन, अशोभन बुद्धि गलित हो गयी है और जो निष्काम है, वही शोभायमान है, चाहे वह भिखारी हो या भूपति।
english_translation: One whose mind is free of conflicting thoughts and who acts without craving shines brightly, whether a beggar or a king.
essence: You shine by dissolving mental conflict and acting without desire, regardless of status.
simple_meaning: You shine when your mind is free of confusing thoughts and you act without wanting anything in return.
insight: It teaches you to clear mental clutter and release craving to reveal your natural brightness.
modern_relevance: You feel calm and confident when your thoughts stop racing and you focus on doing your work without obsessing over rewards.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व स्वाच्छन्द्यं क्व सङ्कोचः क्व वा तत्त्वविनिश्चयः ।
निर्व्याजार्जवभूतस्य चरितार्थस्य योगिनः ॥
translation: निष्कपट, सरल और यथार्थ चरित्र वाले योगी को कहाँ स्वच्छन्दता है, कहाँ संकोच है और कहाँ तत्त्व का निश्चय है।
english_translation: Where is freedom, where hesitation, and where is certainty of truth for the sincere, simple, and genuine yogi?
essence: Sincere, genuine character leaves no room for hesitation or doubt about truth.
simple_meaning: A yogi whose character is sincere, simple, and genuine does not experience hesitation, doubt, or even the need for certainty about truth.
insight: It shifts your focus from needing external proof to trusting your sincere inner conduct as enough.
modern_relevance: When you act with honest intentions and integrity, you stop second-guessing yourself and find natural clarity in your choices.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
आत्मविश्रान्तितृप्तेन निराशेन गतार्तिना ।
अन्तर्यदनुभूयेत तत् कथं कस्य कथ्यते ॥
translation: आत्मा में विश्राम कर तृप्त हुए आशारहित और शोकरहित ज्ञानी के अन्तस् में जो अनुभव होता है उसे कैसे और किसको कहा जाए।
english_translation: When the wise one rests satisfied in the true self, without hope or sorrow, who and how can describe the inner experience?
essence: The deepest inner peace is beyond words and cannot be described.
simple_meaning: When you are fully at peace within yourself without expecting or grieving, the inner experience is beyond words or explanation.
insight: It teaches you to accept that some inner states transcend language and cannot be communicated fully.
modern_relevance: You have moments of quiet peace inside when nothing troubles or excites you, and you realize some experiences simply cannot be put into words.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
सुप्तोऽपि न सुषुप्तौ च स्वप्नेऽपि शयितो न च ।
जागरेऽपि न जागर्ति धीरस्तृप्तः पदे पदे ॥
translation: जो सोया हुआ भी सुषुप्त नहीं है, और न स्वप्न में भी सोया हुआ है, जाग्रत में भी नहीं जागा हुआ है, वही धीर पुरुष क्षण-क्षण तृप्त है।
english_translation: Even when asleep, one is not in deep sleep; even in dreams, not truly asleep; and even awake, one is not truly awake — the wise are satisfied moment to moment.
essence: Wisdom is steady satisfaction beyond waking, dreaming, or sleeping states.
simple_meaning: A truly wise person is never fully lost in sleep, dreams, or waking restlessness but remains satisfied and steady at every moment.
insight: It teaches you to remain inwardly centered and content regardless of external or mental conditions.
modern_relevance: When stress pulls you between restless worry and tired distraction, the wise presence is calm and content through it all.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
ज्ञः सचिन्तोऽपि निश्चिन्तः सेन्द्रियोऽपि निरिन्द्रियः ।
सुबुद्धिरपि निर्बुद्धिः साहङ्कारोऽनहङ्कृतिः ॥
translation: ज्ञानी चिन्तायुक्त भी चिन्तारहित है, इन्द्रियों सहित भी इन्द्रियों रहित है, बुद्धिसहित भी बुद्धिरहित है तथा अहंकारयुक्त भी अहंकाररहित है।
english_translation: The wise one, though engaged in thought, is without anxious thought; though with senses, is without being bound by them; though possessing intellect, is without intellect; though with ego, is without ego.
essence: You can fully engage with mind and senses yet remain untouched by them.
simple_meaning: You can think and sense without being controlled by thoughts, senses, intellect, or ego.
insight: It shifts your view from being captive to your mind and senses to being their calm observer.
modern_relevance: You sit through a busy day, your mind active but not overwhelmed, fully present without stress controlling you.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
न सुखी न च वा दुःखी न विरक्तो न सङ्गवान् ।
न मुमुक्षुर्न वा मुक्ता न किञ्चिन्न्न च किञ्चन ॥
translation: ज्ञानी न सुखी है, न दुःखी है, न विरक्त है, न संगयुक्त है, न मुमुक्षु है, न मुक्त है, न किञ्चन है, न अकिञ्चन।
english_translation: The knower is neither happy nor unhappy, neither detached nor attached, neither seeker nor liberated, neither anything nor nothing.
essence: True knowing is beyond all opposites and identities.
simple_meaning: You are not limited to feelings like joy or sadness, nor to desires or freedom. You simply are beyond all these states.
insight: It shifts your sense of self from identification with emotions or desires to awareness beyond all contrasts.
modern_relevance: When moods swing or identities feel confining, this reminds you that your true self is untouched by changing feelings or roles.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
विक्षेपेऽपि न विक्षिप्तः समाधौ न समाधिमान् ।
जाड्येऽपि न जडो धन्यः पाण्डित्येऽपि न पण्डितः ॥
translation: धन्य पुरुष विक्षेप में भी विक्षिप्त नहीं होता, समाधि में भी समाधि वाला नहीं है, जड़ता में भी जड़ नहीं है, पाण्डित्य में भी पण्डित नहीं है।
english_translation: A blessed person is not disturbed even when distractions arise, nor does one possess absorption; not dull in dullness, nor wise in wisdom.
essence: True steadiness lies beyond all mental states, whether distraction, absorption, dullness, or wisdom.
simple_meaning: A truly blessed person stays calm and unchanged whether distracted, absorbed, dull, or wise.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with fluctuating states to recognizing your unchanging steadiness beyond them.
modern_relevance: You face moments of distraction, deep focus, confusion, or clarity; yet your inner balance need not shift with them.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
मुक्तो यथास्थितिस्वस्थः कृतकर्तव्यनिर्वृतः ।
समः सर्वत्र वैतृष्ण्यान्न स्मरत्यकृतं कृतम् ॥
translation: मुक्त पुरुष सब स्थितियों में स्वस्थ है, किये हुए और करने योग्य कर्म में तृप्त है, सर्वत्र समान है, तृष्णा के अभाव में किये और अनकिये कर्म को स्मरण नहीं करता है।
english_translation: The liberated person remains steady and healthy in all conditions, content with done and to-do actions, equal everywhere, without craving, and does not recall what is done or undone.
essence: True freedom is steady contentment, free from craving and memory of actions.
simple_meaning: You can be steady and healthy in every situation, satisfied with what you have done and what remains, without craving or remembering past or future actions.
insight: It shifts your mind from regret or anticipation to steady acceptance and freedom in the present.
modern_relevance: When you stop obsessing over past mistakes or future plans, you find peace and steady well-being in any circumstance.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
न प्रीयते वन्द्यमानो निन्द्यमानो न कुप्यति ।
नैवोद्विजति मरणे जीवने नाभिनन्दति ॥
translation: मुक्तपुरुष न स्तुति किये जाने पर प्रसन्न होता है, न निन्दित होने पर क्रुद्ध होता है । न मृत्यु में उद्विग्न होता है, न जीवन में हर्षित होता।
english_translation: The liberated person neither feels pleased when praised, nor angry when blamed; neither disturbed by death nor joyful in life.
essence: True freedom means remaining steady and unaffected by praise, blame, life, or death.
simple_meaning: A truly free person does not get happy from praise or angry from blame; they stay calm through life and death.
insight: It teaches you to observe others' opinions without letting them sway your emotions or disturb your inner balance.
modern_relevance: You receive a compliment or criticism on social media but inside, your mood stays calm and steady, unaffected by others' opinions.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
न धावति जनाकीर्णं नारण्यमुपशान्तधीः ।
यथातथा यत्रतत्र सम एवावतिष्ठते ॥
translation: शान्त बुद्धि वाला पुरुष न लोगों से भरे नगर की ओर भागता है, न वन की ओर ही । वह सभी स्थिति और सभी स्थान में समभाव से ही स्थित रहता है।
english_translation: A calm mind does not flee crowded cities nor retreat to forests; it remains equally steady everywhere.
essence: Calmness means being equally steady everywhere, not escaping from what surrounds you.
simple_meaning: A peaceful mind does not run away from busy places or hide in solitude; it remains balanced everywhere.
insight: It teaches you to cultivate inner steadiness that does not depend on external surroundings.
modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed in a noisy café or restless in an empty room, but peace comes when your mind stays steady regardless of place.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
तत्त्वविज्ञानसन्दंशमादाय हृदयोदरात् ।
नाविधपरामर्शशल्योद्धारः कृतो मया ॥
translation: राजा जनक बोले – “मैंने आपके तत्त्वज्ञानरूपी संसी को लेकर हृदय और उदर से अनेक प्रकार के विचाररूपी बाणों को निकाल दिया है”।
english_translation: King Janaka said: "I have removed the arrows of many kinds of thoughts from my heart and belly, which were wounds caused by your teaching of the true nature."
essence: Deep teaching can remove the painful arrows of confusing thoughts lodged inside you.
simple_meaning: King Janaka says that Ashtavakra's teaching has helped him remove many painful, confusing thoughts from deep inside.
insight: It shows how deep understanding can release the mind from painful, stuck thinking.
modern_relevance: You feel the relief after a tough conversation that finally clears confusing doubts weighing on your mind.
speaker: Janaka

verse_text:
क्व धर्मः क्व च वा कामः क्व चार्थः क्व विवेकिता ।
क्व द्वैतं क्व च वाऽद्वैतं स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
translation: अपनी महिमा में स्थित मुझको कहाँ धर्म है, कहाँ काम है, कहाँ अर्थ है, कहाँ विवेकिता है, कहाँ द्वैत है और कहाँ अद्वैत है।
english_translation: In my own greatness, where is duty, where desire, where wealth, where discernment, where duality, and where non-duality?
essence: True greatness transcends all distinctions like duty, desire, and duality.
simple_meaning: When you realize your true greatness, concepts like duty, desire, wealth, discernment, and even duality or non-duality lose their meaning.
insight: It shifts your perspective from identifying with roles and concepts to resting in your unchanging essence.
modern_relevance: When you're deeply confident in who you are, societal labels and expectations around roles, wants, and beliefs lose their hold on you.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व भूतं क्व भविष्यद् वा वर्तमानमपि क्व वा ।
क्व देशः क्व च वा नित्यं स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
translation: नित्य अपनी महिमा में स्थित हुए मुझको कहाँ भूत है, कहाँ भविष्य है, कहाँ वर्तमान है अथवा देश भी कहाँ है।
english_translation: Where was I in the past, where will I be in the future, and where am I now? Where is the place for the one who abides eternally in my own majesty?
essence: Your true self is never confined to time or place but exists eternally.
simple_meaning: You who remain eternally within your own greatness are not limited by past, present, future, or any place.
insight: Shift your view from being a time-bound self to an eternal presence beyond change.
modern_relevance: When life feels overwhelmed by past regrets or future worries, this reminds you that your true self is beyond these moments.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व चात्मा क्व च वानात्मा क्व शुभं क्वाशुभं यथा ।
क्व चिन्ता क्व च वाचिन्ता स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
translation: अपनी महिमा में स्थित हुए मुझको कहाँ आत्मा है और कहाँ अनात्मा अथवा कहाँ शुभ है, कहाँ अशुभ है, कहाँ चिन्ता है अथवा कहाँ अचिन्ता है।
english_translation: Established in my own greatness, where is the self or non-self? Where is good or bad? Where is worry or its absence?
essence: Resting in your true greatness dissolves all distinctions and worries.
simple_meaning: When you rest in your true greatness, distinctions like self or non-self, good or bad, and worry disappear.
insight: It shifts your mind from reacting to dualities toward resting in undivided presence beyond judgments and worries.
modern_relevance: After a stressful day, you finally sit quietly and realize your anxieties and judgments lose their grip when you connect with your inner strength.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व स्वप्नः क्व सुषुप्तिर्वा क्व च जागरणं तथा ।
क्व तुरीयं भयं वापि स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
translation: अपनी महिमा में स्थित हुए मुझको कहाँ स्वप्न, कहाँ सुषुप्ति, कहाँ जाग्रत और कहाँ तुरीय अवस्था का भय है।
english_translation: Being established in my own greatness, where is the fear of dream, deep sleep, waking, or the fourth state for me?
essence: True self-awareness removes all fear of changing states or experiences.
simple_meaning: When you recognize your true self, you no longer fear dreams, deep sleep, waking, or the fourth state.
insight: It teaches you to root your awareness in your true self, beyond all changing mental states, dissolving fear.
modern_relevance: In moments of anxiety or uncertainty, remembering your inner strength makes fears about changing states of mind or life situations disappear.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व दूरं क्व समीपं वा बाह्यं क्वाभ्यन्तरं क्व वा ।
क्व स्थूलं क्व च वा सूक्ष्मं स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
translation: अपनी महिमा में स्थित मुझको कहाँ दूर है, कहाँ समीप है, कहाँ बाह्य है, कहाँ अभ्यन्तर है, स्थूल कहाँ है और सूक्ष्म कहाँ है।
english_translation: Where is the self established in its own greatness—far or near, outside or inside, gross or subtle?
essence: The true self transcends all notions of distance, location, and form.
simple_meaning: The true self is not limited by distance, location, or form; it is beyond near, far, inside, outside, gross, or subtle.
insight: It shifts your perspective from identifying with outer or inner limits to recognizing your boundless true self.
modern_relevance: When you feel confined by your circumstances or identity, remember your true nature is beyond all limits and labels.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व मृत्युर्जीवितं वा क्व लोकाः क्वास्य क्व लौकिकम् ।
क्व लयः क्व समाधिर्वा स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
translation: अपनी महिमा में स्थित हुए मुझको कहाँ मृत्यु है अथवा कहाँ जीवन है । कहाँ लोक है व कहाँ इसका लौकिक व्यवहार है । कहाँ लय है और कहाँ समाधि।
english_translation: Where is death or life for me who is established in my own greatness? Where are worlds or worldly affairs? Where is dissolution or absorbed presence?
essence: Your true self is untouched by life, death, worlds, or absorbed states.
simple_meaning: When you rest in your true greatness, life, death, and worldly states lose their hold on you.
insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as caught in change to realizing your stable, untouchable core.
modern_relevance: When stress makes you feel trapped by life’s ups and downs, remember your deepest self is beyond all that.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
अलं त्रिवर्गकथया योगस्य कथयाप्यलम् ।
अलं विज्ञानकथया विश्रान्तस्य ममात्मनि ॥
translation: अपनी आत्मा में विश्रान्त हुए मुझको त्रिवर्ग की कथा पर्याप्त है, योग की कथा भी पर्याप्त है, विज्ञान की कथा भी पर्याप्त है।
english_translation: For my soul at rest, the stories of the three worlds, of yoga, and of wisdom are all enough.
essence: When your soul rests deeply, all teachings become naturally sufficient and satisfying.
simple_meaning: When your soul is truly at peace, stories about the universe, yoga, or wisdom all feel fully sufficient.
insight: It shifts your mind from seeking external teachings to recognizing inner peace as the true fulfillment.
modern_relevance: After restless searching, you finally feel settled and realize you don’t need more advice or concepts to find peace.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व भूतानि क्व देहो वा क्वेन्द्रियाणि क्व वा मनः ।
क्व शून्यं क्व च नैराश्यं मत्स्वरूपे निरञ्जने ॥
translation: मेरे निरञ्जन स्वरूप में कहाँ पंचभूत हैं, कहाँ देह है, कहाँ इन्द्रियाँ हैं अथवा कहाँ मन है, कहाँ शून्य है और कहाँ नैराश्य है।
english_translation: In my pure, untouched nature, where are the five elements, the body, the senses, the mind, emptiness, or despair?
essence: Your true self is untouched by body, mind, or any limitation.
simple_meaning: Your true nature is pure and untouched by physical elements, senses, mind, emptiness, or despair.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing body and mind to recognizing the unchanging true self.
modern_relevance: When stress or despair overwhelm you, remember your true nature remains untouched beneath all mental and physical turmoil.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व शास्त्रं क्वात्मविज्ञानं क्व वा निर्विषयं मनः ।
क्व तृप्तिः क्व वितृष्णात्वं गतद्वन्द्वस्य मे सदा ॥
translation: सदा द्वन्द्वरहित मुझको कहाँ शास्त्र, कहाँ आत्मविज्ञान है, कहाँ विषयरहित मन है, कहाँ तृप्ति है, कहाँ तृष्णा का अभाव है।
english_translation: I am always free from duality; where is scripture, where is knowledge of the true self, where is a mind without desire, where is satisfaction, where is absence of craving?
essence: True self is beyond craving, conflict, and all distinctions.
simple_meaning: You have always been free from duality, craving, and desire; your true self knows no conflict or dissatisfaction.
insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with restless desires to recognizing the unchanging peace beyond all duality.
modern_relevance: In moments when your mind races with wants and restlessness, you can remember your essential freedom beyond those urges and conflicts.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व विद्या क्व च वाविद्या क्वाहं क्वेदं मम क्व वा ।
क्व बन्ध क्व च वा मोक्षः स्वरूपस्य क्व रूपिता ॥
translation: स्व स्वरूप की कहाँ रूपिता है, कहाँ विद्या है और कहाँ अविद्या है, कहाँ ‘मैं’ है अथवा कहाँ ‘यह’ है, कहाँ ‘मेरा’ है, कहाँ बन्ध है अथवा कहाँ मोक्ष है।
english_translation: Where is knowledge? Where is ignorance? Where am I? Where is this? Where is mine? Where is bondage? Where is freedom? Where is the form of the true self?
essence: The self and its qualities have no fixed location or form to be found or lost.
simple_meaning: Questions about where knowledge, ignorance, self, and freedom exist show that these ideas have no fixed place or form in reality.
insight: It shifts your thinking from searching for fixed states to recognizing the emptiness of such concepts as separate realities.
modern_relevance: You wonder where your true self or clarity lives amid swirling doubts and shifting identities, but the real you has no fixed address.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व प्रारब्धानि कर्माणि जीवन्मुक्तिरपि क्व वा ।
क्व तद् विदेहकैवल्यं निर्विशेषस्य सर्वदा ॥
translation: मुझ सदैव निर्विशेष को प्रारब्ध कर्म कहाँ अथवा कहाँ जीवन्मुक्ति है और कहाँ यह विदेह कैवल्य ही है।
english_translation: Where are the consequences of past actions, where is liberation, and where is the formless isolation that is always present?
essence: True freedom is always present and never limited by past actions.
simple_meaning: There is no real place where past actions limit you, no separate liberation needed because the formless freedom is always present.
insight: It shifts your view from being trapped by history to recognizing your constant freedom beyond it.
modern_relevance: When regrets or past mistakes weigh on you, this reminds you that your true self remains untouched and free now.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व कर्ता क्व च वा भोक्ता निष्क्रियं स्फुरणं क्व वा ।
क्वापरोक्षं फलं वा क्व निःस्वभावस्य मे सदा ॥
translation: सदा स्वभावरहित मुझको कहाँ कर्त्तापन है और कहाँ भोक्तापन । कहाँ निष्क्रियता है और कहाँ स्फुरण है । कहाँ अपरोक्ष ज्ञान है अथवा कहाँ फल है।
english_translation: I am always free of doer-ness and experiencer-ness; where is action or reaction? Where is direct result or effect for my true nature?
essence: Your true self is never the doer or experiencer and remains untouched by action or result.
simple_meaning: You are never truly the one who acts or the one who experiences results. Your true nature is untouched by action, reaction, or outcomes.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying as the actor or sufferer to seeing yourself as the unmoved witness beyond all action.
modern_relevance: When stress hits after a tough conversation, you can remember you are not the doer of all effects, freeing you from unnecessary guilt and anxiety.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व लोकं क्व मुमुक्षुर्वा क्व योगी ज्ञानवान् क्व वा ।
क्व बद्धः क्व च वा मुक्तः स्वस्वरूपेऽहमद्वये ॥
translation: मुझ अद्वय स्वरूप को कहाँ लोक है अथवा कहाँ मुमुक्षु है । कहाँ योगी है, कहाँ ज्ञानवान है अथवा कहाँ बद्ध है और कहाँ मुक्त।
english_translation: Where is the world, where the seeker, where the yogi, the wise one? Where is the bound, and where the free? I am my own non-dual nature.
essence: Your true self is beyond all divided identities and roles.
simple_meaning: You are not the world, the seeker, the yogi, or the bound and free states. You are your own undivided true nature.
insight: It shifts your understanding from identifying with roles to recognizing your unchanging true nature.
modern_relevance: When you feel torn by roles or expectations, remember your true self is beyond all these shifting identities.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व सृष्टिः क्व च संहारः क्व साध्यं क्व च साधनम् ।
क्व साधकः क्व सिद्धिर्वा स्वस्वरूपेऽहमद्वये ॥
translation: मुझ अद्वय स्वरूप को कहाँ सृष्टि और कहाँ संहार । कहाँ साध्य है और कहाँ साधन है । कहाँ साधक है अथवा कहाँ सिद्धि है।
english_translation: Where is creation, where destruction? Where is the to-be-achieved, where the means? Where is the doer, and where is the achievement? I am my nondual nature.
essence: Your true self is beyond doer, deed, and duality—it is pure nondual nature.
simple_meaning: Everything like creation, destruction, doer, and achievement does not apply to your true self, which is nondual and unchanged.
insight: It shifts your focus from identifying as a doer or a goal to recognizing your unchanging, nondual essence.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by roles or achievements, knowing your true self is beyond these brings deep relief and clarity.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व प्रमाता प्रमाणं वा क्व प्रमेयं क्व च प्रमा ।
क्व किञ्चित् क्व न किञ्चिद् वा सर्वदा विमलस्य मे ॥
translation: सर्वदा विमालरूप मुझको कहाँ प्रमाता, कहाँ प्रमाण, कहाँ प्रमेय और कहाँ प्रमा है । कहाँ किंचित् है और कहाँ अकिंचित् है।
english_translation: Where is the doer, the object of knowledge, the means of knowledge, or the knowledge itself? Where is anything or nothing for the ever-pure self?
essence: The true self transcends all roles of doer, known, and knowledge simultaneously.
simple_meaning: The true self is beyond being a doer, the known, the means of knowing, or knowledge itself; it is always pure and untouched by any object or concept.
insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with actions and perceptions to recognizing your nature as pure awareness beyond all distinctions.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by choices or roles, remember you are not defined by what you do or know but by your pure existence beyond it all.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व विक्षेपः क्व चैकाग्र्यं क्व निर्बोधः क्व मूढता ।
क्व हर्षः क्व विषादो वा सर्वदा निष्क्रियस्य मे ॥
translation: सर्वदा क्रियारहित मुझको कहाँ एकाग्रता, कहाँ ज्ञान, कहाँ मूढ़ता, कहाँ हर्ष और कहाँ विषाद है।
english_translation: Where is distraction, where is focus, where is knowledge, where is confusion? Where is joy, where is sorrow, for me who is always inactive?
essence: The true self remains unaffected and inactive beyond all emotions and mental activity.
simple_meaning: There is no distraction, focus, knowledge, confusion, joy, or sorrow in the self that remains always still and inactive.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with fluctuating emotions to resting in the steady awareness beyond them.
modern_relevance: When your mind feels overwhelmed with emotions or scattered thoughts, this reminds you that your true self remains calm and unaffected beneath it all.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व चैष व्यवहारो वा क्व च सा परमार्थता ।
क्व सुखं क्व च वा दुखं निर्विमर्शस्य मे सदा ॥
translation: सदा निर्विकाररूप मुझको कहाँ यह व्यवहार है और कहाँ वह परमार्थता है । कहाँ सुख है अथवा कहाँ दुःख है।
english_translation: I am always the changeless reality; where is this worldly life, or that supreme truth? Where is happiness or sorrow for one who sees clearly?
essence: The true self never changes and remains untouched by happiness or sorrow.
simple_meaning: You are always the unchanging reality; worldly life, supreme truth, happiness, and sorrow do not touch your true nature.
insight: It teaches you to shift focus from external ups and downs to the inner unchanging awareness.
modern_relevance: When stress and emotions overwhelm you, remembering your core remains steady brings relief and perspective.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व माया क्व च संसारः क्व प्रीतिर्विरतिः क्व वा ।
क्व जीवः क्व च तद्ब्रह्म सर्वदा विमलस्य मे ॥
translation: मुझ सदा विमलस्वरूप को कहाँ माया और कहाँ संसार है । कहाँ प्रीति है अथवा कहाँ विरति है । कहाँ जीव है और कहाँ ब्रह्म है।
english_translation: For my always pure self, where is illusion, where is the cycle of change? Where is attachment or detachment? Where is the individual self, and where is the supreme reality?
essence: Your true self is always pure and beyond all illusion and division.
simple_meaning: The pure true self is untouched by illusion, change, attachment, or any division between self and supreme reality.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with change and confusion to recognizing your unchanging pure nature.
modern_relevance: When your mind is restless with confusion or attachment, this reminds you that your true self remains untouched and pure beneath all that noise.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व प्रवृत्तिर्निर्वृत्तिर्वा क्व मुक्तिः क्व च बन्धनम् ।
कूटस्थनिर्विभागस्य स्वस्थस्य मम सर्वदा ॥
translation: सर्वदा कूटस्थ, अखण्डरूप और स्वस्थ मुझको कहाँ निवृत्ति है, कहाँ मुक्ति है और कहाँ बन्ध है।
english_translation: I am always steady, undivided, and healthy; where is activity, release, or bondage for me?
essence: Your true self is always steady and untouched by activity, freedom, or bondage.
simple_meaning: Your true self is always steady, whole, and healthy; it never truly experiences activity, freedom, or bondage.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as a changing doer to recognizing an ever-unchanging presence.
modern_relevance: When life feels chaotic or you feel trapped by circumstances, this reminds you that your core is untouched and steady beneath it all.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्वोपदेशः क्व वा शास्त्रं क्व शिष्यः क्व च वा गुरुः ।
क्व चास्ति पुरुषार्थो वा निरुपाधेः शिवस्य मे ॥
translation: उपाधिरहित शिवरूप मुझको कहाँ उपदेश है, कहाँ शास्त्र है, कहाँ शिष्य है, कहाँ गुरु है और कहाँ पुरुषार्थ है।
english_translation: To the limitless form of the auspicious, there is no teaching, no scripture, no student, no teacher, and no effort.
essence: The limitless true self transcends teaching, scripture, effort, and all dualities.
simple_meaning: The true self is unlimited and free of all conditions—there is no need for teachings, scriptures, students, teachers, or effort to reach it.
insight: It shifts your focus from external authorities and effort to recognizing your innate completeness beyond conditions.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by instructions or efforts to improve, remember that your true nature is beyond all those demands and already whole.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
क्व चास्ति क्व च वा नास्ति क्वास्ति चैकं क्व च द्वयम् ।
बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन किञ्चिन्नोत्तिष्ठते मम ॥
translation: कहाँ अस्ति है और कहाँ नास्ति । कहाँ एक है अथवा कहाँ दो है । इसमें बहुत कहने से क्या प्रयोजन, मुझको तो कुछ भी नहीं उठ रहा है।
english_translation: Where is existence, and where is non-existence? Where is the one, and where is the two? There is no point in saying much; nothing arises for me.
essence: Nothing truly arises or disappears; existence and non-existence are illusions to the true self.
simple_meaning: You cannot locate where things truly exist or don’t exist; for your true self, nothing really appears or disappears.
insight: It shifts your mind from searching for external truths to recognizing the unchanging nature within yourself.
modern_relevance: You stare at problems that seem real but suddenly realize they don’t truly affect who you are at your core.
speaker: Ashtavakra

verse_text:
ईश्वरानुग्रहादेव पुंसामद्वैतवासना ।
महद्भयपरित्राणाद्विप्राणामुपजायते ॥
translation: महान भय से रक्षा करने वाली अद्वैत की वासना मनुष्यों में, विप्रों में, ईश्वर के अनुग्रह (कृपा) से ही उत्पन्न होती है।
english_translation: The desire for non-duality that frees from great fear arises in humans, especially sages, only by the divine's grace.
essence: The desire to transcend fear and grasp non-duality emerges only by divine kindness.
simple_meaning: The wish to realize oneness and escape great fear arises in people only through the divine's kindness.
insight: It teaches you to recognize that your deepest spiritual yearnings are not just personal efforts but arise through grace.
modern_relevance: When fear grips you at night, the sudden hope or yearning to find peace often feels like a gift beyond your control.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
येनेदं पूरितं सर्वमात्मनैवात्मनात्मनि ।
निराकारं कथं वन्दे ह्यभिन्नं शिवमव्ययम् ॥
translation: यह दृश्यमान सम्पूर्ण जगत जिस आत्मा द्वारा आत्मा से आत्मा में ही पूर्ण हो रहा है उस निराकार (ब्रह्म) का मैं किस प्रकार वन्दन करूँ क्योंकि वह (जीव से) अभिन्न है, कल्याण स्वरूप है, (तथा) अव्यय है।
english_translation: I worship that formless, eternal supreme reality that fills all and is inseparable from the true self.
essence: The true self and the formless eternal whole are inseparable and already complete within you.
simple_meaning: Everything visible is completely filled by the true self, which is formless, eternal, and inseparable from you.
insight: It shifts your view from seeking outside to recognizing your own inseparable unity with the eternal presence.
modern_relevance: When you realize you are deeply connected to the unchanging presence around you, worship becomes a heartfelt recognition, not a distant ritual.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
पञ्चभूतात्मकं विश्वं मरीचिजलसन्निभम् ।
कस्याप्यहो नमस्कुर्यामहमेको निरञ्जनः ॥
translation: यह विश्व पाँच भूतों का समुदाय हैं जो मृगतृष्णा के जल के समान मिथ्या भी है। मैं एक ही निरन्जन (निर्दोष) हूँ। फिर मैं किसको नमस्कार करूँ।
english_translation: The world is made of five elements, like a mirage or water illusion. I alone am pure and spotless; to whom should I bow?
essence: You alone are pure; the world is a fleeting illusion of elements.
simple_meaning: The entire world is made of changing elements and illusions like a mirage. Only your true self is pure and untainted.
insight: This verse shifts your focus from outer appearances to recognizing your inner purity beyond all change.
modern_relevance: When everything around you feels uncertain and unstable, remember that your true essence remains pure and steady beneath all appearances.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
आत्मैव केवलं सर्वं भेदाभेदो न विद्यते ।
अस्ति नास्ति कथं ब्रूयां विस्मयः प्रतिभाति मे ॥
translation: यह आत्मा ही सर्वरूप है तथा केवल है जिसमें भेद और अभेद विद्यमान नहीं है- इसे मैं ‘है’ अथवा ‘नहीं है’ किस प्रकार कहूँ। मुझे यह आश्चर्य रूप प्रतीत होता है।
english_translation: The true self alone is everything; there is no difference or non-difference in it. How can I say it 'exists' or 'does not exist'? This amazes me.
essence: Your true self is the undivided whole beyond existence and non-existence.
simple_meaning: The true self is everything and cannot be split into parts or opposites. It cannot be described as simply existing or not existing.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as a limited thing to recognizing you are the indivisible whole beyond all distinctions.
modern_relevance: When you try to define yourself strictly by what you are or are not, you feel stuck—this verse points to a freedom beyond such limits.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
वेदान्तसारसर्वस्वं ज्ञानं विज्ञानमेव च ।
अहमात्मा निराकारः सर्वव्यापी स्वभावतः ॥
translation: वेदान्त का सार ही हमारा सर्वस्व है और वही ज्ञान एवं विज्ञान है। मैं आत्मा हूँ, निराकार हूँ तथा स्वभाव से ही सर्वव्यापी हूँ।
english_translation: The essence of Vedanta is our all; it is knowledge and wisdom. I am the true self, formless, and naturally all-pervading.
essence: You are the formless true self, knowledge, and presence naturally all around.
simple_meaning: You are the essence of the highest teaching, pure knowledge and wisdom, without form and present everywhere naturally.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with form-bound identity to recognizing your boundless, formless presence.
modern_relevance: In moments when you feel limited by your body or thoughts, recall that your true self is vast, formless, and everywhere beyond those limits.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
यो वै सर्वात्मको देवो निष्कलो गगनोपमः ।
स्वभावनिर्मलः शुद्धः स एवायं न संशयः ॥
translation: जो सर्वस्वरूप देव ( ब्रह्म) है वह अवयव रहित,आकाश के सदृश, स्वभाव से निर्मल एवं शुद्ध है। वही मैं हूँ, इसमें संशय नहीं है।
english_translation: The divine that is the essence of all is without parts, like the sky, pure by nature, and spotless; that is exactly who I am, without doubt.
essence: Your true self is pure, whole, and limitless like the sky, beyond all division.
simple_meaning: You are the pure and indivisible essence of everything, like the vast sky, without any flaw or division.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as broken or limited to recognizing your complete and flawless nature.
modern_relevance: When you feel fragmented or flawed, remember your true self is whole and pure, like the endless sky above.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
अहमेवाव्ययोऽनन्तः शुद्धविज्ञानविग्रहः ।
सुखं दुःखं न जानामि कथं कस्यापि वर्तते ॥
translation: मैं निश्चय ही नाश रहित, अनन्त एवं शुद्ध विज्ञान स्वरूप हूँ। मैं सुख-दु:ख को नहीं जानता हूँ कि ये किसको व किस प्रकार होते हैं।
english_translation: I am certainly imperishable, infinite, and pure consciousness itself. I do not know pleasure or pain, nor how they affect anyone.
essence: You are infinite pure awareness beyond all pleasure and pain.
simple_meaning: You are the eternal and infinite pure consciousness that does not experience pleasure or pain.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with fleeting feelings to recognizing your unchanging true nature.
modern_relevance: When stress or joy overwhelms you, remember your core self remains untouched and infinite beyond these feelings.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
न मानसं कर्म शुभाशुभं मे न कायिकं कर्म शुभाशुभं मे ।
न वाचिकं कर्म शुभाशुभं मे ज्ञानामृतं शुद्धमतीन्द्रियोऽहम् ॥
translation: मन के द्वारा किये गये शुभ व अशुभ कर्म मेरे नहीं हैं, न शरीर द्वारा किये गये शुभ अशुभ कर्म मेरे हैं, वाणी द्वारा किये गये शुभ अशुभ कर्म भी मेरे नहीं हैं। मैं शुद्ध, ज्ञानामृत एवं इन्द्रियों का अविषय हूँ।
english_translation: Neither the good nor the bad actions of the mind, body, or speech belong to me; I am pure, the nectar of knowledge, and beyond the senses.
essence: Your true self is pure and untouched by mind, body, or speech actions.
simple_meaning: You are not the good or bad actions done by your mind, body, or speech. Your true self is pure, full of knowledge, and beyond the senses.
insight: It shifts your identity from the doer of actions to the pure awareness beyond all activity and sensory involvement.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your thoughts, words, or deeds, remember your true self remains untouched and pure beneath it all.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
मनो वै गगनाकारं मनो वै सर्वतोमुखम् ।
मनोऽतीतं मनः सर्वं न मनः परमार्थतः ॥
translation: निश्चय ही यह मन गगन के आकार वाला है तथा इसके सभी ओर मुख हैं, मन से पार कुछ भी नहीं है, मन ही सब कुछ है किन्तु यह मन भी परमार्थ से सत्य नहीं है।
english_translation: The mind is like the sky in shape and faces all directions; beyond mind there is nothing, mind is everything, yet even mind is not the ultimate truth.
essence: The mind includes everything but is not the ultimate truth beyond it.
simple_meaning: The mind appears limitless and contains everything, but even it is not the highest reality or true self.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying fully with your thoughts to recognizing the true self beyond the mind’s reach.
modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by countless thoughts and emotions swirling around, you sense your mind is vast but still feel something deeper beyond it.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
अहमेकमिदं सर्वं व्योमातीतं निरन्तरम् ।
पश्यामि कथमात्मानं प्रत्यक्षं वा तिरोहितम् ॥
translation: मैं आत्मा को प्रत्यक्ष अथवा तिरोहित किस प्रकार देखूँ क्योंकि मैं आत्मा स्वरूप होने के कारण एक तथा सर्वरूप हूँ तथा आकाश से भी परे निरन्तर हूँ।
english_translation: I am the one and all, beyond space and endless; how can I see the true self as visible or hidden?
essence: The true self transcends all forms of visibility and invisibility as the one endless reality.
simple_meaning: You are the single reality beyond everything, endless like space. The true self cannot be simply seen or hidden because it is your own nature.
insight: It shifts your view from trying to observe the self as an object to recognizing it as the boundless presence you already are.
modern_relevance: You stare into the mirror of your mind, realizing your true nature cannot be captured by simple seeing or hiding.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
त्वमेवमेकं हि कथं न बुध्यसे 
समं हि सर्वेषु विमृष्टमव्ययम् ।
सदोदितोऽसि त्वमखण्डितः प्रभो
दिवा च नक्तं च कथं हि मन्यसे ॥
translation: ‘हे प्रभो ! तू क्यों नहीं जानता कि तू एक ही है, सभी में समान है, नाश रहित है’ ऐसा विचार किया गया है। तू सदा ही प्रकाशमान है तथा अखण्ड है (भेद रहित है) फिर तू दिन और रात्रि को किस प्रकार मानता है।
english_translation: You are indeed the one alone, unchanging and the same in all; always radiant and undivided, so how can you perceive day and night as real?
essence: Your true self is one, unchanging, and beyond all dualities like day and night.
simple_meaning: You are the same unchanging presence in everyone, always shining and whole. Day and night are just appearances you mistakenly believe in.
insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with fleeting appearances to recognizing your constant, undivided nature.
modern_relevance: When your mood shifts and you feel scattered, remember your true self remains steady beneath all change.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
आत्मानं सततं विद्धि सर्वत्रैकं निरन्तरम् ।
अहं ध्याता परं ध्येयमखण्डं खण्ड्यते कथम् ॥
translation: आत्मा को तुम सदा सर्वत्र, एक एवं अविचल जानो। फिर ‘मैं ध्याता ( ध्यान करने वाला) हूँ तथा आत्मा ध्येय’ (जिसका ध्यान किया जाता है) का भेद किस प्रकार करते हो। जो अखण्ड है उसका खण्डन कैसे करते हो।
english_translation: Always know the true self as one, unchanging everywhere. How do you separate the meditator 'I' from the meditation object, the self, which is indivisible?
essence: The true self is indivisible; the watcher and the watched are one.
simple_meaning: You are always the one true self everywhere, unchanging. The sense of separating the observer from the observed self is mistaken.
insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as split between watcher and what is watched, to recognizing a seamless unity.
modern_relevance: When you try to watch your thoughts or feelings as if they are separate, notice how that separation itself cannot hold; you are always the same unchanging self.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
न जातो न मृतोऽसि त्वं न ते देहः कदाचन ।
सर्वं ब्रह्मेति विख्यातं ब्रवीति बहुधा श्रुतिः ॥
translation: न तो तेरा कभी जन्म हुआ है न कभी मरता ही है, न कभी तेरा शरीर ही है। यह सब ब्रह्म ही है ऐसा प्रसिद्ध है तथा अनेक श्रुतियाँ ऐसा ही कहती हैं।
english_translation: You were never born, nor do you ever die; your body is never truly yours. Everything is known as Brahman, as many scriptures repeatedly declare.
essence: You are never born or dead; your true nature is beyond the body.
simple_meaning: You have never been born and will never die. Your body is not your true self. Everything is ultimately the supreme reality called Brahman.
insight: It shifts your identity from the physical and mortal to the timeless and unchanging reality.
modern_relevance: When you face fear of change or loss, remembering you are beyond your body and life’s cycles can bring deep peace.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
स बाह्याभ्यन्तरोऽसि त्वं शिवः सर्वत्र सर्वदा ।
इतस्ततः कथं भ्रान्तः प्रधावसि पिशाचवत् ॥
translation: जो आत्मा (ब्रह्म) बाहर और भीतर सर्वत्र एवं सदा से ही विद्यमान है तथा कल्याण रूप है, वह तू ही है। फिर तू भ्रान्त होकर इधर-उधर पिशाच की तरह क्यों दौड़ता फिरता है।
english_translation: You are the true self, the auspicious one, present everywhere always; why then do you wander confused like a ghost?
essence: You are always fully present and auspicious; confusion is your own making.
simple_meaning: You are the ever-present true self, complete and auspicious everywhere, so why are you confused and restless like a lost spirit?
insight: It teaches shifting from restless confusion to recognizing your constant, unchanging presence everywhere.
modern_relevance: You feel scattered, chasing distractions and doubts, forgetting that your essential self is always calm and complete.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
संयोगश्च वियोगश्च वर्तते न च ते न मे ।
न त्वं नाहं जगन्नेदं सर्वमात्मैव केवलम् ॥
translation: तुझमें और मुझमें कोई संयोग और विभाग नहीं है। न तू है, न मैं हूँ और न यह जगत ही है बल्कि यह सब केवल आत्मा ही है।
english_translation: There is no union or separation between you and me. Neither you, nor I, nor this world exists; all is only the true self.
essence: You, me, and the world are not separate; all is only the true self.
simple_meaning: There is no real difference or separation between you, me, or the world. Everything is only the true self.
insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as separate to recognizing unbroken oneness with all existence.
modern_relevance: You notice how often you feel divided from others or your environment, but this teaches that all separation is imagined.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
शब्दादिपञ्चकस्यास्य नैवासि त्वं न ते पुनः ।
त्वमेव परमं तत्त्वमतः किं परितप्यसे ॥
translation: फिर ये शब्दादि पंचक (शब्द, स्पर्श, रूप, रस, गंध) न तो तुम हो न ये तुम्हारे हैं। तुम एक ही परम तत्व ( ब्रह्म) हो इसलिए क्यों संतप्त होते हो।
english_translation: You are neither the five elements of sound and so on, nor are they yours; you alone are the supreme reality, so why do you suffer?
essence: You are the supreme reality, not the senses or their experiences; suffering is needless.
simple_meaning: You are not the five senses or their experiences. You alone are the supreme reality, so there is no reason to suffer.
insight: This verse shifts your view from identifying with fleeting sensations to recognizing your true, unchanging nature.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by what you see, hear, or touch, remember you are more than these passing sensations.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
जन्म मृत्युर्न ते चित्तं बन्धमोक्षौ शुभाशुभौ ।
कथं रोदिषि रे वत्स नामरूपं न ते न मे ॥
translation: जन्म और मृत्यु, बन्धन और मोक्ष तथा शुभ-अशुभ सब मन के धर्म हैं, तेरे नहीं हैं, ये नाम और रूप भी न तेरे हैं न मेरे। फिर हे वत्स! तू क्यों रूदन करता है।
english_translation: Birth and death, bondage and freedom, good and bad are all functions of the mind; they belong neither to you nor to me. So why do you cry, dear one?
essence: Your true self is untouched by birth, death, and mental distinctions; sorrow is needless.
simple_meaning: Birth, death, bondage, freedom, good, and bad exist only in the mind, not in your true self or mine. So there is no reason to cry.
insight: This verse shifts your perspective from identifying with changing experiences to recognizing your unchanging true self beyond them.
modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by worries and hopes that seem personal but are just mental patterns you don’t truly own.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
अहो चित्त कथं भ्रान्तः प्रधावसि पिशाचवत् ।
अभिन्नं पश्य चात्मानं रागत्यागात्सुखी भव ॥
translation: खेद है कि यह चित्त किस प्रकार भ्रान्त होकर पिशाच की भाँति दौड़ता-फिरता है। तू अपनी आत्मा को अभिन्न देख तथा राग का त्याग करके सुखी हो।
english_translation: Alas, how the restless mind wanders like a ghost. See your true self as one and be happy by abandoning craving.
essence: Your mind wanders in confusion, but your true self is always whole and free from craving.
simple_meaning: Your restless mind confuses you like a ghost chasing illusions. Recognize your true self as whole and let go of craving to find happiness.
insight: This verse shifts attention from chasing desires to recognizing your undivided self, calming mental restlessness.
modern_relevance: Your mind jumps anxiously from thought to thought, restless and never settled. Seeing yourself beyond this helps you relax and feel content.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
त्वमेव तत्त्वं हि विकारवर्जितं
निष्कम्पमेकं हि विमोक्षविग्रहम् ।
न ते च रागो ह्यथवा विरागः
कथं हि सन्तप्यसि कामकामतः ॥
translation: तू निश्चय ही आत्म तत्व है जो विकार रहित है, निष्काम है, एक ही है तथा मोक्ष स्वरूप है। ये राग और विराग भी तेरे नहीं हैं फिर कामों की कामना से क्यों संतप्त है।
english_translation: You are the true essence, free from change, desireless, one, and the form of freedom. Attachment and detachment are not yours; so why do you suffer from desires?
essence: Your true self is beyond desire and free from suffering caused by craving.
simple_meaning: You are the unchanging true essence, free from desires and attachments. Those feelings are not truly yours, so there is no reason to suffer from wanting.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with desire to recognizing your essence beyond craving and suffering.
modern_relevance: You feel restless chasing what you want, yet deep inside, you’re untouched by those cravings. Recognizing this can ease your inner struggle.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
वदन्ति श्रुतयः सर्वाः निर्गुणं शुद्धमव्ययम् ।
अशरीरं समं तत्त्वं तन्मां विद्धि न संशयः ॥
translation: सम्पूर्ण श्रुतियाँ आत्म तत्व को निर्गुण, शुद्ध, नाश रहित, शरीर से रहित, समरूप ही कहती हैं वही तुम मुझे जानो इसमें संशय नहीं है।
english_translation: All scriptures declare the true self as formless, pure, imperishable, bodiless, and equal; know that as me without doubt.
essence: Your true self is pure, formless, eternal, and beyond any doubt.
simple_meaning: The true self is described by all scriptures as pure, without form, never perishing, and beyond the body. You should recognize this without any doubt.
insight: It teaches you to identify beyond your body and mind as the unchanging, pure essence.
modern_relevance: When your body ages or your feelings shift, remember your true nature remains pure, unchanged, and beyond all forms.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
साकारमनृतं विद्धि निराकारं निरन्तरम् ।
एतत्तत्त्वोपदेशेन न पुनर्भवसम्भवः ॥
translation: साकार को मिथ्या जाने, निराकार को निरन्तर (नित्य) जाने। इस तत्व के उपदेश से संसार में पुन: उत्पत्ति नहीं होती।
english_translation: Know the form-based as false, the formless as eternal; this teaching ends rebirth.
essence: Form is false; the formless eternal truth frees from rebirth.
simple_meaning: The appearance of form is an illusion, but the formless reality is eternal. Understanding this ends the cycle of rebirth.
insight: It shifts your mind from attachment to appearances toward abiding in unchanging reality.
modern_relevance: When distractions and appearances overwhelm you, remembering that the unchanging truth lies beyond form can bring lasting peace.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
एकमेव समं तत्त्वं वदन्ति हि विपश्चितः ।
रागत्यागात्पुनश्चित्तमेकानेकं न विद्यते ॥
translation: विद्वान् जन कहते हैं कि एक ही तत्व समान रूप से व्याप्त है। राग के त्याग देने से यह चित्त फिर एक और अनेक को नहीं जानता।
english_translation: The wise say that the one truth pervades all equally; when attachment is renounced, the mind no longer perceives multiplicity.
essence: Letting go of attachment reveals the mind’s true vision of oneness.
simple_meaning: The one true reality is the same everywhere. When you give up attachment, your mind stops seeing many separate things.
insight: It teaches you to release attachment so your mind naturally perceives unity instead of division.
modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by choices and desires pulling you in every direction, but letting go of craving brings calm and clarity.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
अनात्मरूपं च कथं समाधि-
रात्मस्वरूपं च कथं समाधिः ।
अस्तीति नास्तीति कथं समाधि-
र्मोक्षस्वरूपं यदि सर्वमेकम् ॥
translation: अनात्म रूप को समाधि कैसे हो सकती है, तथा आत्म स्वरूप को समाधि कैसे हो सकती है। इसी प्रकार ‘है’ और ‘नहीं है’ को भी समाधि कैसे हो सकती है और जो मोक्ष स्वरूप एक ही ब्रह्म है तो भी समाधि कैसे हो सकती है।
english_translation: How can there be samadhi of what is not the true self, or samadhi of the true self's form? How can 'exists' and 'does not exist' be samadhi? If the supreme freedom is all one, how can samadhi be?
essence: True freedom transcends all forms, existence, and non-existence; samadhi is beyond definition.
simple_meaning: Samadhi cannot be about something that is not the true self or even the true self's form. It cannot depend on existence or non-existence. Since freedom is all one, samadhi transcends such distinctions.
insight: It shifts your understanding from trying to fix samadhi as an object to seeing it as the absence of all dual distinctions.
modern_relevance: When you search for peace, you may try to grasp or define it, but true freedom is beyond all labels and opposites you hold in your mind.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
विशुद्धोऽसि समं तत्त्वं विदेहस्त्वमजोऽव्ययः ।
जानामीह न जानामीत्यात्मानं मन्यसे कथम् ॥
translation: तू (आत्मा स्वरूप होने से) विशुद्ध, समरस, देह रहित, जन्म से रहित तथा नाश से रहित है। फिर तू यह कैसे मानता है कि मैं आत्मा को जानता हूँ मैं आत्मा को नहीं जानता।
english_translation: You are pure, equal to all, bodiless, unborn, and imperishable. How then do you think 'I know the self' or 'I do not know the self'?
essence: You are pure and unchanging; knowing or not knowing your true self is just a mental illusion.
simple_meaning: You are fundamentally pure, equal everywhere, without a body, unborn, and never destroyed. So how can you truly say you know or don't know your true self?
insight: It shifts you from identifying with mental labels of knowing or ignorance to recognizing your unchanging nature beyond thought.
modern_relevance: When you doubt your own nature or feel confused about who you truly are, remember that your essence is beyond all such thoughts.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्येन स्वात्मा हि प्रतिपादितः ।
नेति नेति श्रुतिर्ब्रूयादनृतं पाञ्चभौतिकम् ॥
translation: और ‘तत्वमसि’ (यह तू ही है) आदि वाक्यों से अपने आत्मा का ही प्रतिपादन किया गया है और श्रुति ‘नेति नेति’ कहती है। यह पंचभौतिक मिथ्या है।
english_translation: The true self is revealed by sayings like 'You are that'; the scriptures negate the false five-element world.
essence: The true self is revealed by negating the false five-element world through scripture.
simple_meaning: The true self is described by phrases like 'You are that'. The scriptures teach to reject the false physical world made of five elements.
insight: It shifts your attention from identifying with your physical body to recognizing your unchanging true self.
modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by your changing body and environment, remember these are not your true self but passing forms to see through.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
आत्मन्येवात्मना सर्वं त्वया पूर्णं निरन्तरम् ।
ध्याता ध्यानं न ते चित्तं निर्लज्जं ध्यायते कथम् ॥
translation: तेरी आत्मा ही सभी आत्म रूप से पूर्ण एवं निरन्तर है। इसलिए ध्याता और ध्यान तुम्हारे नहीं हैं फिर यह निर्लज्ज मन कैसे ध्यान करता है।
english_translation: Your inner being itself is complete and continuous; the meditator and meditation are not truly yours, so how can a shameless mind meditate?
essence: Your true self is always complete; restless mind cannot genuinely meditate.
simple_meaning: Your inner being is already complete and continuous. Since the meditator and meditation are not truly separate from you, how can a restless, shameless mind meditate?
insight: It shifts attention from trying to control the mind to recognizing your already complete true self beyond mental distractions.
modern_relevance: You try to quiet your mind during meditation, but it keeps wandering, reminding you that your true self is already complete beyond this restlessness.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
शिवं न जानामि कथं वदामि
शिवं न जानामि कथं भजामि ।
अहं शिवश्चेत्परमार्थतत्त्वं
समस्वरूपं गगनोपमं च ॥
translation: मैं शिव को नहीं जानता तो कैसे उसका वर्णन करूँ मैं शिव को नहीं जानता तो कैसे उसे भजूँ, मैं ही शिव स्वरूप एवं परमार्थ तत्व हूँ जो गगन के तुल्य और सम स्वरूप है।
english_translation: I do not know Shiva, so how can I describe or worship him? I am Shiva's form and the supreme reality, identical and like the sky.
essence: You cannot know or worship what you already are, the infinite supreme reality.
simple_meaning: You cannot truly know or describe the divine because you already are that supreme reality, vast and unchanging like the sky.
insight: It teaches you to stop searching outside and recognize your identity with the supreme reality right now.
modern_relevance: When you stop chasing ideals or descriptions of yourself, you realize you already embody what you sought—vast, unchanging, and whole.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
नाहं तत्त्वं समं तत्त्वं कल्पनाहेतुवर्जितम् ।
ग्राह्यग्राहकनिर्मुक्तं स्वसंवेद्यं कथं भवेत् ॥
translation: न मैं तत्व हूँ न किसी के समान तत्व हूँ, कल्पना तथा उसके हेतु से भी रहित हूँ, ग्राह्य तथा ग्राहक के व्यवहार से भी रहित हूँ, स्वयंवेद्य भी कैसे हो।
english_translation: I am neither a principle nor like any principle, beyond imagination and its cause, free from the relation of subject and object, and how can I be self-known?
essence: You are beyond all concepts, including knowing and being known.
simple_meaning: You are not a principle or like any principle. You are beyond imagination, beyond subject and object, and cannot be grasped or even known by yourself.
insight: It teaches you to release all mental categories of self and stop trying to grasp your identity as an object or subject.
modern_relevance: When you struggle to label or understand yourself, this reminds you that your true nature cannot be boxed by any idea or self-image.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
अनन्तरूपं न हि वस्तु किंचि-
त्तत्त्वस्वरूपं न हि वस्तु किंचित् ।
आत्मैकरूपं परमार्थतत्त्वं
न हिंसको वापि न चाप्यहिंसा ॥
translation: यह आत्मा (ब्रह्म) अनन्त रूप है ऐसी अन्य कोई वस्तु नहीं है। यह ब्रह्म ही तत्व स्वरूप है, ऐसी कोई अन्य वस्तु नहीं है। यह आत्मा एक रूप ही है तथा परमार्थ तत्व है इसलिए न तो कोई हिंसक है न अहिंसा ही है।
english_translation: The true self is infinite in form; no other object exists. It alone is the supreme reality, neither harmful nor harmless.
essence: Your true self is infinite and beyond all opposites like harm and harmlessness.
simple_meaning: Your true self has infinite form and is the supreme reality beyond harm or kindness.
insight: Recognize the true self as beyond dual qualities, freeing your mind from fear and attachment.
modern_relevance: In moments of judgment or fear, realize you are beyond simple labels like harm or safety, limitless in your true nature.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
विशुद्धोऽसि समं तत्त्वं विदेहमजमव्ययम् ।
विभ्रमं कथमात्मार्थे विभ्रान्तोऽहं कथं पुनः ॥
translation: तुम विशुद्ध हो, देह रहित, जन्म रहित, अव्यय तथा समरस तत्व हो। आत्मा के विषय में तुम्हे भ्रांति क्यों है ? तुम कैसे कह सकते हो कि मैं भ्रान्ति युक्त हूँ।
english_translation: You are pure, without body, unborn, imperishable, and the same essence. Why is there confusion about the true self? How can you claim to be deluded?
essence: Your true self is pure and unchanging; confusion about it is impossible.
simple_meaning: You are the pure, unchanging essence beyond body and birth. Confusion about your true self cannot be real.
insight: It teaches you to reject self-doubt and recognize your unchanging true nature beyond appearances.
modern_relevance: When self-doubt clouds your mind, remember you are the unchanged essence beyond any confusion.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
घटे भिन्ने घटाकाशं सुलीनं भेदवर्जितम् ।
शिवेन मनसा शुद्धो न भेदः प्रतिभाति मे ॥
translation: घट के नाश होने पर घटाकाश महाकाश में लीन होकर भेद रहित हो जाता है (इसी प्रकार) शुद्ध मन से शुद्ध ही प्रतीत होता है। मुझे आत्मा का भेद प्रतीत नहीं होता है।
english_translation: When the pot breaks, the space within it merges with the vast space, becoming undivided; likewise, a pure mind perceives no division in the true self.
essence: Pure awareness reveals that apparent divisions vanish like space freed from a broken pot.
simple_meaning: When the pot breaks, the space inside merges with the open sky without divisions. Similarly, a pure mind sees the true self as undivided and whole.
insight: It teaches you to recognize that divisions are mental constructs and your true self is seamless and whole.
modern_relevance: When you let go of mental barriers, your sense of separation fades and you feel connected with everything around you.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
न घटो न घटाकाशो न जीवो जीवविग्रहः ।
केवलं ब्रह्म संविद्धि वेद्यवेदकवर्जितम् ॥
translation: न घट है, न घटाकाश है, न जीव हैं न उसका कोई विग्रह है। केवल ब्रह्म को ही सम्यक् जान जो ज्ञान तथा ज्ञाता से रहित है।
english_translation: There is no pot, no pot-space, no living being, no form; only Brahman is truly known, free from knowledge and knower.
essence: You are not any form or identity; only the supreme reality truly exists.
simple_meaning: There are no separate things like pot, space, living being, or form ultimately; only the supreme reality exists, beyond any knowledge or knower.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing forms to recognizing yourself as the unchanging supreme reality.
modern_relevance: When you feel boxed in by your roles and identities, remember you are more than those labels—pure and unlimited at core.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
सर्वत्र सर्वदा सर्वमात्मानं सततं ध्रुवम् ।
सर्वं शून्यमशून्यं च तन्मां विद्धि न संशयः ॥
translation: तू आत्मा को सर्वत्र, सदा, सर्वरूप (सब कुछ), सतत एवं नित्य जान तथा इस समस्त जगत को शून्य जान और आत्मा को ही अशून्य जान। वह आत्मा मुझे ही जान इसमें संशय नहीं है।
english_translation: Know that the true self is everywhere, always, and is all that exists; the entire world is void, and the true self alone is real without doubt.
essence: You are the unchanging reality beyond all empty appearances everywhere and always.
simple_meaning: The true self is constant, everywhere present, and is all that truly exists; the world appears empty, but the true self alone is real without doubt.
insight: It shifts your understanding from seeing separations to recognizing your unchanging presence as the reality behind all change.
modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by endless distractions and shifting situations, you can remember that your true self remains constant and whole beneath it all.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
वेदा न लोका न सुरा न यज्ञा
वर्णाश्रमो नैव कुलं न जातिः ।
न धूममार्गो न च दीप्तिमार्गो
ब्रह्मैकरूपं परमार्थतत्त्वम् ॥
translation: वेद भी नहीं हैं, लोक भी नहीं है, देवता भी नहीं है, यज्ञ भी नहीं हैं, वर्ण और आश्रम भी नहीं है, न कुल है, न जाति हैं, धूतमार्ग भी नहीं है और न अग्निमार्ग ही है। केवल एकरूप ब्रह्म ही परमार्थ तत्व है।
english_translation: There are no Vedas, no worlds, no deities, no sacrifices, no social classes or lineages, no smoke path nor fire path; only the one-form supreme reality exists.
essence: All divisions vanish; only the one undivided supreme reality exists.
simple_meaning: All external divisions like scriptures, social groups, and rituals do not define reality; only the undivided supreme reality truly exists.
insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with social or religious categories to recognizing the undivided essence beneath all appearances.
modern_relevance: When you feel boxed in by labels or roles others impose, remember your true nature is beyond all divisions and identities.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
व्याप्यव्यापकनिर्मुक्तः त्वमेकः सफलं यदि ।
प्रत्यक्षं चापरोक्षं च ह्यात्मानं मन्यसे कथम् ॥
translation: यदि तू एक ही, फल के सहित है और व्याप्त-व्यापक भाव से रहित है तू प्रत्यक्ष और अपरोक्ष आत्मा को कैसे मानता है।
english_translation: If you are the one, complete and free from the pervader and the pervaded, how do you consider the self as both direct and indirect?
essence: True self is never partly hidden or divided; it is always fully present.
simple_meaning: You are whole and free from all divisions; it makes no sense to think of the self as sometimes seen and sometimes hidden.
insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as divided to recognizing your constant wholeness.
modern_relevance: When you feel fragmented or unsure of yourself, remember that your true nature is always whole and present, not partly hidden.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
अद्वैतं केचिदिच्छन्ति द्वैतमिच्छन्ति चापरे ।
समं तत्त्वं न विन्दन्ति द्वैताद्वैतविवर्जितम् ॥
translation: कुछ अद्वैत की इच्छा करते हैं और कुछ द्वैत की इच्छा करते हैं किन्तु वे समतत्व को नहीं जानते जो द्वैत और अद्वैत से रहित है।
english_translation: Some desire non-duality, others desire duality, but neither knows the same essence beyond both.
essence: The true essence is beyond wanting duality or non-duality; it transcends both.
simple_meaning: People either want unity without difference or separation between things, but neither understands the essence that goes beyond both ideas.
insight: It shifts your mind from choosing sides to recognizing a single reality beyond all distinctions.
modern_relevance: When you argue over extremes or labels, you miss the deeper reality that holds everything together beyond those differences.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
श्वेतादिवर्णरहितं शब्दादिगुणवर्जितम् ।
कथयन्ति कथं तत्त्वं मनोवाचामगोचरम् ॥
translation: जो सफेद आदि वर्गों से रहित है, शब्दादि गुणों से भी रहित है, जो मन और वाणी का विषय ही नहीं है उसे तत्व किस प्रकार कहा जा सकता है।
english_translation: How can that principle be described which is free from whiteness and other qualities, beyond words, and not subject to mind or speech?
essence: The true principle cannot be captured by words, qualities, or mental concepts.
simple_meaning: The true principle cannot be described by words, thoughts, or qualities because it is beyond all of these.
insight: It shifts your mind away from trying to define the true self and towards simply recognizing its indefinable presence.
modern_relevance: When you try to explain your deepest feelings or experiences, you find words fall short—this shows some truths are beyond description.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
यदाऽनृतमिदं सर्वं देहादिगगनोपमम् ।
तदा हि ब्रह्म संवेत्ति न ते द्वैतपरम्परा ॥
translation: जिस समय यह सम्पूर्ण दृश्य जगत मिथ्या ज्ञात होने लगे तथा ये शरीर आदि आकाश के समान शून्य जान पड़े तभी ब्रह्म को ठीक प्रकार से जाना जाता है। उस समय तुझे द्वैत परम्परा का भान नहीं होगा।
english_translation: When all this apparent world is known to be false and the body and such are understood as empty like space, then the supreme reality is truly realized, and you no longer perceive duality.
essence: Knowing the world as empty like space reveals the supreme reality beyond duality.
simple_meaning: You truly know the supreme reality when you see the world and body as empty like space, and duality disappears.
insight: It shifts your perception from seeing yourself as separate to recognizing oneness beyond appearances.
modern_relevance: In moments when you see your worries and identity as fleeting and empty, you glimpse beyond the usual divisions and fears.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
परेण सहजात्मापि ह्यभिन्नः प्रतिभाति मे ।
व्योमाकारं तथैवैकं ध्याता ध्यानं कथं भवेत् ॥
translation: मुझे यह भान हो रहा है कि यह अनादि आत्मा परब्रह्म से भिन्न नहीं है जो आकाश के समान व्यापक एवं एक ही है तो फिर ध्याता और ध्यान कैसे हो सकता है।
english_translation: I realize that my natural self is not different from the supreme reality, which is vast like the sky and one; so how can there be a meditator and meditation?
essence: The natural self and supreme reality are one; separation between observer and observed is impossible.
simple_meaning: You realize your natural self is not separate from the supreme reality, so there is no true division between meditator and meditation.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing itself as a separate doer to recognizing unity with all experience.
modern_relevance: You catch a quiet moment seeing that the 'you' trying to control things is actually part of everything, not apart from it.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
यत्करोमि यदश्नामि यज्जुहोमि ददामि यत् ।
एतत्सर्वं न मे किंचिद्विशुद्धोऽहमजोऽव्ययः ॥
translation: जो मैं करता हूँ, जो मैं भक्षण करता हूँ, जो मैं हवन करता हूँ, जो मैं देता हूँ वह सब किंचिद् भी मेरा नहीं है। मैं विशुद्ध, जन्म रहित एवं नाश रहित हूँ।
english_translation: Whatever I do, eat, offer, or give—all of this is not mine. I am pure, unborn, and indestructible.
essence: Your true self transcends all actions, possessions, and changes.
simple_meaning: Your actions, meals, offerings, and gifts don’t belong to you. Your true self is pure, eternal, and beyond birth or death.
insight: It shifts your focus from identifying with actions or possessions to recognizing your unchanging, pure nature.
modern_relevance: You may feel overwhelmed by roles and responsibilities, but your true self remains untouched by all you do or give.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
सर्वं जगद्विद्धि निराकृतीदं
सर्वं जगद्विद्धि विकारहीनम् ।
सर्वं जगद्विद्धि विशुद्धदेहं
सर्वं जगद्विद्धि शिवैकरूपम् ॥
translation: इस सम्पूर्ण जगत को तू आकार रहित जान, इस सम्पूर्ण जगत को तू विकार रहित जान, इस सम्पूर्ण जगत को तू विशुद्ध ब्रह्म का शरीर जान, इस सम्पूर्ण जगत को तू कल्याण स्वरूप जान।
english_translation: Know the entire world as formless, free from change, the pure body of the supreme reality, and the embodiment of auspiciousness.
essence: All appearances are the formless, pure, and auspicious true self at their core.
simple_meaning: The whole world is not made of shapes or changes but is the pure, unchanging true self and the source of all goodness.
insight: Shift your view from seeing only physical change to recognizing the underlying unchanging essence in all things.
modern_relevance: When everything around you feels unstable or confusing, remembering that the world’s true nature is pure and unchanging can bring peace amid chaos.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
तत्त्वं त्वं न हि सन्देहः किं जानाम्यथवा पुनः ।
असंवेद्यं स्वसंवेद्यमात्मानं मन्यसे कथम् ॥
translation: वह तू ही है तथा तू वही है इसमें कोई सन्देह नहीं है फिर और मैं क्या जानूँ। फिर आत्मा को असंवेद्य ‘किसी से भी जानने योग्य नहीं’ तथा स्वसंवेद्य ‘अपने से ही जानने योग्य’ कैसे माना जाए।
english_translation: You are the essence, there is no doubt in this; what else do I need to know? How can the true self be both unknowable by others and known only by itself?
essence: You are the undeniable essence; no contradiction or doubt can exist about this.
simple_meaning: You are the fundamental reality without any doubt. The true self cannot be both unknown to others and known only to itself.
insight: It shifts the mind from confusion to certainty about your inner identity and unity with reality.
modern_relevance: When you feel unsure about who you really are, remember that your true nature is clear and undeniable.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
मायाऽमाया कथं तात छायाऽछाया न विद्यते ।
तत्त्वमेकमिदं सर्वं व्योमाकारं निरञ्जनम् ॥
translation: हे तात! माया और अमाया कैसे है, छाया और अछाया भी विद्यमान नहीं है। यह तू एक ही है तथा यह सम्पूर्ण जगत आकाश के समान व्यापक एवं निर्दोष है।
english_translation: O father! How can there be illusion and non-illusion, shadow and no shadow? This is all one truth, vast like space and pure.
essence: Opposites like illusion and reality dissolve into one pure, limitless truth.
simple_meaning: Illusion and its opposite do not truly exist; everything is one pure, boundless reality like space.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing dualities to embracing undivided unity beyond appearances.
modern_relevance: When confusion about right and wrong, real and fake overwhelms you, remember that beyond these opposites lies a single pure reality.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
आदिमध्यान्तमुक्तोऽहं न बद्धोऽहं कदाचन ।
स्वभावनिर्मलः शुद्ध इति मे निश्चिता मतिः ॥
translation: मैं आदि, मध्य और अन्त से रहित हूँ, न मैं कभी बद्ध ही हूँ। मेरी यह निश्चित मति है कि मैं स्वभाव से ही निर्मल और शुद्ध हूँ।
english_translation: I am free from beginning, middle, and end; never bound. I am naturally pure and spotless, this is my firm conviction.
essence: Your true self is timeless, always free, and naturally pure.
simple_meaning: You are beyond time and never truly limited. Your true nature is pure and unchanging.
insight: Recognize your identity beyond all phases and limits, resting in innate purity and freedom.
modern_relevance: When life feels like a timeline of stress and obligations, this reminds you that your true self is beyond all that pressure and naturally clear.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
महदादि जगत्सर्वं न किंचित्प्रतिभाति मे ।
ब्रह्मैव केवलं सर्वं कथं वर्णाश्रमस्थितिः ॥
translation: महतत्व आदि से इस सम्पूर्ण जगत का मुझे थोड़ा सा भी ज्ञान नहीं होता। केवल ब्रह्म ही सब कुछ है फिर वर्णाश्रम की स्थिति किस प्रकार हो सकती है।
english_translation: I perceive nothing of the vast universe; only Brahman is all that exists. How then can the distinctions of caste and stages of life be true?
essence: Only the supreme reality truly exists; social distinctions are unreal.
simple_meaning: You recognize that the entire universe is just the supreme reality; social categories like caste and life stages are unreal.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with social roles to recognizing the unity underlying all distinctions.
modern_relevance: You notice how social roles and labels often limit you, but deep down, you are beyond all such divisions.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
जानामि सर्वथा सर्वमहमेको निरन्तरम् ।
निरालम्बमशून्यं च शून्यं व्योमादिपञ्चकम् ॥
translation: मैं जानता हूँ कि ये आकाशादि पंचक (पृथ्वी, जल, अग्नि, वायु और आकाश) शून्य है तथा मैं सब प्रकार से सर्वरूप एक ही निरन्तर, आलम्बन रहित एवं अशून्य हूँ।
english_translation: I know completely that the five elements—earth, water, fire, air, and space—are empty, and I alone am the continuous, independent, and unchanging reality, one in all forms.
essence: You alone are the continuous, unchanging reality beyond all empty forms.
simple_meaning: You are the single unchanging reality, independent and continuous, beyond the empty five elements of the world.
insight: It teaches you to see beyond appearances to the eternal continuity that you are.
modern_relevance: When everything around you feels unstable or empty, remember your true self remains steady and whole beneath it all.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
न षण्ढो न पुमान्न स्त्री न बोधो नैव कल्पना ।
सानन्दो वा निरानन्दमात्मानं मन्यसे कथम् ॥
translation: आत्मा न नपुन्सक है, न पुरुष है, न स्त्री है, न ज्ञान है, न कल्पना ही है। यह आनन्दमय एवं निरानन्द भी नहीं है। फिर तुम आत्मा को किस प्रकार का मानते हो।
english_translation: The true self is neither male nor female, neither knowledge nor imagination. It is neither joyful nor sorrowful. How then do you conceive of the true self?
essence: The true self cannot be defined by any identity, feeling, or thought.
simple_meaning: The true self transcends all identities like male, female, knowledge, or imagination. It is beyond joy and sorrow. It cannot be limited by any concept.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing traits to recognizing a limitless, unconditioned self.
modern_relevance: When you feel boxed in by roles or emotions—male, female, happy, sad—this verse reminds you that your true essence is beyond those limits.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
षडङ्गयोगान्न तु नैव शुद्धं
मनोविनाशान्न तु नैव शुद्धम् ।
गुरूपदेशान्न तु नैव शुद्धं
स्वयं च तत्त्वं स्वयमेव बुद्धम् ॥
translation: आत्मा षडंग योग से शुद्ध नहीं होता, मन के नाश होने से भी शुद्ध नहीं होता, गुरु के उपदेश से भी शुद्ध नहीं होता। वह स्वयं ही सार तत्व है और स्वयं ही शुद्ध है।
english_translation: The true self is not purified by the sixfold yoga, nor by the destruction of the mind, nor by the guru's teachings; it is itself the essence and inherently pure.
essence: The true self transcends all purification efforts because it is inherently pure essence.
simple_meaning: Your true self is never something to be purified by practices, mind changes, or teachings; it is already pure and is the essence itself.
insight: It shifts your view from trying to purify yourself to recognizing your innate purity as the true self.
modern_relevance: When you struggle to ‘fix’ or ‘improve’ yourself, this verse reminds you that your true nature is already pure and complete, beyond effort.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
न हि पञ्चात्मको देहो विदेहो वर्तते न हि ।
आत्मैव केवलं सर्वं तुरीयं च त्रयं कथम् ॥
translation: आत्मा पंचभौतिक शरीर भी नहीं है तथा देह से रहित भी नहीं वर्तता है। आत्मा ही केवल और सर्व रूप है फिर इसकी तुरीय और तीन अवस्थाएँ कैसे हैं।
english_translation: The true self is neither the five-element body nor without a body; it alone is everything. How then can it have the three states and the fourth beyond them?
essence: You are the whole reality beyond body and all states of consciousness.
simple_meaning: You are not simply your physical body nor completely without one. You alone are the complete reality beyond all states of being.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as limited to recognizing yourself as the unchanging whole beyond all conditions.
modern_relevance: You might feel stuck identifying only with your body or mind, but this invites you to sense yourself as unlimited—beyond all labels and states.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
न बद्धो नैव मुक्तोऽहं न चाहं ब्रह्मणः पृथक् ।
न कर्ता न च भोक्ताहं व्याप्यव्यापकवर्जितः ॥
translation: मैं बद्ध भी नहीं हूँ, न मुक्त ही हूँ मैं ब्रह्म से भिन्न भी नहीं हूँ, न मैं कर्ता हूँ और न भोक्ता हूँ। मैं व्याप्य और व्यापक भाव से भी रहित हूँ।
english_translation: I am neither bound nor free, nor separate from the supreme reality. I am neither the doer nor the experiencer. I am beyond both the pervading and the pervaded.
essence: You are beyond being bound, free, doer, or experiencer—beyond all dual roles.
simple_meaning: You are not truly bound or free, not separate from the supreme reality, and not the doer or experiencer of actions.
insight: It shifts your self-understanding from identifying as a separate agent or sufferer to recognizing your limitless essence beyond all dualities.
modern_relevance: When you feel trapped by your choices or outcomes, remember you are not the doer or the one who truly experiences limits—you are beyond those roles.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
यथा जलं जले न्यस्तं सलिलं भेदवर्जितम् ।
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं तद्वदभिन्नं प्रतिभाति मे ॥
translation: जिस प्रकार जल में फेंका हुआ जल जलरूप ही भेद रहित हो जाता है वैसे ही प्रकृति और पुरुष मुझे अभिन्न प्रतीत होते हैं।
english_translation: Just as water poured into water becomes indistinguishable from water, so too do nature and pure awareness appear to me as one without difference.
essence: Separation between nature and pure awareness is only an illusion, like water mixing with water.
simple_meaning: Nature and pure awareness are not two separate things but one, just like water poured into water becomes inseparable.
insight: It teaches you to see apparent separations as illusions and recognize underlying unity.
modern_relevance: When you feel divided or disconnected, remember how water loses all borders when it joins more water—your true self is never apart from the world.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
यदि नाम न मुक्तोऽसि न बद्धोऽसि कदाचन ।
साकारं च निराकारमात्मानं मन्यसे कथम् ॥
translation: यदि ऐसा प्रसिद्ध है कि तू मुक्त भी नहीं है और बद्ध भी नहीं है तो फिर आत्मा को साकार और निराकार किस प्रकार मानता है।
english_translation: If you are neither free nor bound at any time, then how do you consider the true self both with form and formless?
essence: The true self cannot be limited by opposing ideas of freedom and form.
simple_meaning: If you claim to be neither free nor bound, then how can you think of the true self as having form and also being formless?
insight: It shifts your view from accepting contradictory self-images to recognizing the limits of dualistic labels on the true self.
modern_relevance: You feel stuck between feeling restricted and free — and wonder how you can be both at once in your own identity.
