translation: यह आत्मा सर्वरूप, नित्य एवं सबके चित्तों में रहता है। इस संसार में यही केवल निश्चल भाव से सब चित्तों में रहता है। यह दो पाँव से रहित सबके चित्त में रहता है। हे मन! तू वही आत्मा होने से सर्व में सम है फिर किस कारण से रूदन करता है।
english_translation: This true self is all forms, always present in every mind. It is the only unchanging presence in all minds, beyond feet or limbs. O mind, since you are that true self present in all, why do you weep?
essence: You are the unchanging presence in every mind; sorrow is unnecessary.
simple_meaning: The true self is present in every mind, always unchanging and whole. Since you are this true self everywhere, there is no reason to suffer or weep.
insight: It shifts your perspective from seeing yourself as separate and vulnerable to recognizing your constant, unchanging nature everywhere.
modern_relevance: When you feel isolated or upset, remembering you are the same unchanging self in all can bring calm and lessen your pain.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
अतिसर्वनिरन्तरसर्वगतं अतिनिर्मलनिश्चलसर्वगतम् ।
दिनरात्रिविवर्जितसर्वगतं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
translation: यह आत्मा श्रेष्ठ, सर्वरूप, नित्य एवं सभी में व्याप्त है, यह अति निर्मल, निश्चल एवं सबमें व्याप्त है, फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम वही आत्मा है।
english_translation: The true self is supreme, present in all forms, eternally pure and unmoving everywhere. So, mind, why do you weep? The true self is the same in all.
essence: The pure, unchanging true self pervades all — there is no reason to grieve.
simple_meaning: Your true self is pure, steady, and present in everything at all times. The restless mind has no reason to grieve.
insight: It shifts your focus from transient emotions to the ever-present, unchanging true self within and around you.
modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by a difficult situation, but this reminds you that your core remains unchanged, steady, and present regardless of external troubles.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
न हि बन्धविबन्धसमागमनं न हि योगवियोगसमागमनम् ।
न हि तर्कवितर्कसमागमनं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
translation: आत्मा में बन्ध और विबन्ध का समागम नहीं है, न योग और वियोग का समागम है, न तर्क और वितर्क का समागम हैं। हे मन! फिर तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम है।
english_translation: The true self does not unite with bondage or liberation, nor with joining or separation, nor with reasoning or non-reasoning. O mind, why do you weep? You are equal in all.
essence: Your true self remains equal and untouched by all opposites the mind experiences.
simple_meaning: Your true self is untouched by bonds, freedom, joining, separation, or reasoning. It remains equally present in everything, so your mind’s sorrow is unfounded.
insight: It teaches you to stop identifying with mental conflicts and see yourself as steady and undivided.
modern_relevance: When your mind feels torn by conflict or confusion, remember your true self is untouched and equal in all situations.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
इह कालविकालनिराकरणं अणुमात्रकृशानुनिराकरणम् ।
न हि केवलसत्यनिराकरणं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
translation: आत्मा में काल एवं विकाल का निराकरण है, इसमें अणु मात्र भी अग्नि का निराकरण है, केवल सत्य का निराकरण इसमें नहीं है। क्योंकि यह स्वयं सत्य है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम है।
english_translation: In the true self, both time and its decay are negated, even the tiniest spark of fire is negated; only the truth itself is never negated. So, mind, why do you weep? You are equal in all.
essence: Your true self transcends time and decay; grief arises only in the restless mind.
simple_meaning: Your true self is beyond time and decay; nothing in you truly diminishes. So, your mind, there is no reason to grieve because you are equal in all things.
insight: This verse shifts your perspective from identifying with fleeting loss to recognizing your timeless, unchanging nature.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by loss or aging, remember your true self is untouched by time’s changes and remains whole.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
इह देहविदेहविहीन इति ननु स्वप्नसुषुप्तिविहीनपरम् ।
अभिधानविधानविहीनपरं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
translation: यह आत्मा देह और विदेह से रहित हैं, स्वप्न और सुषुप्ति से भी रहित हैं, विधि एवं निषेध से भी रहित है। फिर हे मन ! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू वही आत्मा है जो सर्व में सम है।
english_translation: This self is without body or disembodied, beyond dream and deep sleep, beyond rules and prohibitions. So why do you weep, mind? You are the same self present in all.
essence: You are the same limitless self beyond body, mind, and rules.
simple_meaning: You are not limited by body, mind, or any rules. You are the same self everywhere. So why does your mind grieve?
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with limited experiences to recognizing your boundless, unchanging nature.
modern_relevance: When your thoughts spiral in anxiety, remember you are not your body or mind. This awareness can calm your restless emotions.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
गगनोपमशुद्धविशालसमं अतिसर्वविवर्जितसर्वसमम् ।
गतसारविसारविकारसमं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
translation: यह आत्मा आकाश के समान व्यापक, शुद्ध, विशाल एवं सम हैं, यह सर्व से रहित नहीं है किन्तु सर्व में सम हैं, यह सार, विसार एवं विकार से रहित है तथा सम है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम है।
english_translation: The true self is like the sky—pure, vast, and equal; it is not separate but present in all. It is free from essence, change, and corruption. So mind, why do you grieve? You are present in everything.
essence: Your true self is vast, pure, unchanging, and present in everything — so grief is needless.
simple_meaning: Your true self is like the vast sky—pure, equal, and present in everything. It does not change or suffer loss. So your mind need not grieve.
insight: It teaches you to see beyond mental grief by recognising your true self as vast and unchanging within all experiences.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by loss or change, remember your true self remains vast, untouched, and present everywhere—beyond all turmoil.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
इह धर्मविधर्मविरागतरमिह वस्तुविवस्तुविरागतरम् ।
इह कामविकामविरागतरं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
translation: इस संसार में धर्म और विधर्म से वैराग्य ही श्रेष्ठ हैं, काम और विकाम से वैराग्य ही श्रेष्ठ है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम है।
english_translation: In this world, dispassion toward what is right and wrong is supreme; dispassion toward desire and aversion is supreme. So, mind, why do you weep? You are equal in everything.
essence: True peace arises when your mind becomes equally free from desire and judgment.
simple_meaning: True freedom comes from letting go of judgments about right and wrong and from releasing desire and dislike. When your mind is equal to all things, there is no need to suffer.
insight: It shifts your focus from reacting to opposites toward resting in your mind’s inherent balance and equality.
modern_relevance: When your thoughts swirl between what’s right or wrong, what you want or don’t want, you feel stuck. Recognizing your mind’s natural balance can stop that endless stress.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
सुखदुःखविवर्जितसर्वसममिह शोकविशोकविहीनपरम् ।
गुरुशिष्यविवर्जिततत्त्वपरं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
translation: यह आत्मा सुख और दुःख से रहित सर्व एवं सम है, यह शोक और विशोक से रहित परम है, यह गुरु एवं शिष्य से रहित परम सत्व है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम है।
english_translation: The true self is free from pleasure and pain, equal in all, beyond sorrow and distress, beyond teacher and student. So why does your mind weep? You are equal in everything.
essence: The true self is beyond all dualities, so your mind need not suffer.
simple_meaning: Your true self is untouched by pleasure or pain, sorrow or joy, teacher or student. So your mind need not cry, because you are equal in all.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with fluctuating feelings to resting in the unchanging true self beneath them.
modern_relevance: When your emotions overwhelm you, remember that your deeper being is untouched by highs and lows, beyond any role or relationship.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
न किलाङ्कुरसारविसार इति न चलाचलसाम्यविसाम्यमिति ।
अविचारविचारविहीनमिति किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
translation: आत्मा में निश्चय ही सार एवं विसार का अंकुर भी नहीं है, चल, अचल, साम्य एवं वैषाम्य भी इसमें नहीं है, यह विचार एवं अविचार से भी रहित है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम आत्मा है।
english_translation: The true self has no trace of arising or ceasing, no change or unchange, equality or difference; it is beyond thought and beyond non-thought. So why does your restless mind cry? The true self is the same in all.
essence: The true self is always unchanging and equal in all; the mind’s suffering is needless.
simple_meaning: Your true self does not change or move; it is beyond all thoughts and differences. So your restless mind has no reason to suffer.
insight: It teaches you to recognize the stable, changeless self beneath all mental fluctuations and to stop identifying with restless thoughts.
modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by shifting feelings and thoughts, yet your core remains steady and untouched beneath the noise.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
इह सारसमुच्चयसारमिति कथितं निजभावविभेद इति ।
विषये करणत्वमसत्यमिति किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
translation: यह आत्मा सार समुच्चय (सभी प्रकार के सारों का) का भी सार हैं। ऐसा कहा गया है। अपने भाव से भी इसका विभेद है (यह भाव रूप नहीं है), विषयों का करणत्व (कार्य) यही है ऐसा असत्य ही कहा गया है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम है।
english_translation: The self is said to be the essence of all essences. It is distinct from feelings and not the cause of objects. So why does your mind weep? You are equal in all.
essence: You are the universal essence, not the cause or the feelings you experience.
simple_meaning: You are the core essence behind all things, not the feelings you have or the cause of objects. So your mind’s sorrow is unnecessary because you are present equally everywhere.
insight: It teaches you to separate your true self from the mind’s emotional reactions and the mistaken belief that you cause everything.
modern_relevance: When your emotions overwhelm you, remember you are more than your feelings or the things happening around you. Your true self remains steady and equal in all situations.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
बहुधा श्रुतयः प्रवदन्ति यतो वियदादिरिदं मृगतोयसमम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वसमं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
translation: अनेक श्रुतियाँ कथन करती हैं कि जितना भी यह आकाशादि प्रपंच है वह मृगतृष्णा के जल के समान है। और यह एक चेतन ही नित्य एवं सर्व में सम है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू वही आत्म है जो सभी में समान रूप से है।
english_translation: Many scriptures say the cosmic play is like mirage water, but the one true self is constant and present in all; why then does your mind grieve?
essence: The true self is one and unchanging; the mind’s grief is needless illusion.
simple_meaning: The world is often compared to a mirage, but your true self is constant and present everywhere. Your mind should not suffer grief.
insight: It teaches you to recognize the mind’s grief as misunderstanding your constant, universal true self.
modern_relevance: You struggle with sadness over events that seem real but are like illusions; knowing your true self is steady can ease that pain.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
विन्दति विन्दति न हि न हि यत्र छन्दोलक्षणं न हि न हि तत्र ।
समरसमग्नो भावितपूतः प्रलपति तत्त्वं परमवधूतः ॥
translation: परम अवधूत ( श्रेष्ठ ज्ञानी) जिसका अन्त:करण पवित्र है उस एकरस आत्मा में ही मग्न रहता है तथा उस आत्मतत्व का ही कथन करता है। जिसमें छन्द और लक्षण नहीं हैं उसी आत्मा को प्राप्त होता है।
english_translation: The supreme Avadhuta, whose inner being is pure, remains absorbed in that unified true self and speaks only of that ultimate reality, which has no form or qualities.
essence: The supreme being is absorbed in the pure, formless true self and speaks only that truth.
simple_meaning: The highest wise one, pure inside, remains fully absorbed in the formless true self and speaks only of that ultimate reality.
insight: It teaches you to rest in the pure essence within, beyond all forms and mental qualities.
modern_relevance: In moments of quiet, you find yourself connected to something pure and beyond all labels or roles you play.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
बहुधा श्रुतयः प्रवदन्ति वयं वियदादिरिदं मृगतोयसमम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवमुपमेयमथोह्युपमा च कथम् ॥
translation: अनेक श्रुतियाँ हमें कहती हैं कि यह आकाश आदि प्रपंच मृगतृष्णा के जल के समान है। यदि यह एक ही चेतन नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव स्वरूप है तो यह उपमेय और उपमा किस प्रकार हो सकता है।
english_translation: Many scriptures say this world is like a mirage, yet if it is one eternal, all-pervading, auspicious consciousness, how can it be both the object and the comparison?
essence: One eternal reality cannot simultaneously be an illusory object and its own comparison.
simple_meaning: If the entire world is one eternal, all-good consciousness, it cannot also be an illusion or separate object.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing the world as fragmented to recognizing one unchanging reality beyond all appearances.
modern_relevance: You’ve heard people call life an illusion, but deep down you sense reality is more unified than that.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
अविभक्तिविभक्तिविहीनपरं ननु कार्यविकार्यविहीनपरम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं यजनं च कथं तपनं च कथम् ॥
translation: यह चेतन तत्व अविभक्ति एवं विभक्ति से रहित परम तत्व है, निश्चय ही यह कार्य विकार्य से भी रहित है। यदि यह एक ही नित्य, सर्व रूप एवं शिव है तो फिर यजन और तप कैसे हो सकता है।
english_translation: The conscious principle is without division or separation, beyond all change or effect; if it is one, eternal, and all-blissful, then how could worship or austerity apply to it?
essence: The true self is always whole and unaffected by any practice or change.
simple_meaning: The true self is beyond division, change, or action; since it is always whole and blissful, practices like worship and austerity do not apply to it.
insight: It shifts your mind from trying to change your essence to recognizing the unchanging nature beneath all effort.
modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed trying to fix yourself with constant effort or rituals, but your core being is already whole and unchanged beneath it all.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
मन एव निरन्तरसर्वगतं ह्यविशालविशालविहीनपरम् ।
मन एव निरन्तरसर्वशिवं मनसापि कथं वचसा च कथम् ॥
translation: मन ही निरन्तर एवं सर्वगत है, निश्चय ही यह अविशाल और विशाल से रहित है, मन ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिवरूप, है। इसलिये उस आत्मा को मन और वाणी से कैसे जाना जाये।
english_translation: The mind alone is continuously all-pervading, beyond vastness and limitation; it is eternal, all, and the embodiment of the supreme reality. Therefore, how can that true self be known by mind or speech?
essence: The mind is vast yet cannot know the true self beyond mind and words.
simple_meaning: The mind is always present everywhere but is not capable of fully knowing the true self, which is beyond mind and words.
insight: It teaches you to stop relying on mind or language to capture your true self and open to direct experience instead.
modern_relevance: You struggle to understand yourself through thoughts or words, but this shows why that effort can never fully succeed.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
दिनरात्रिविभेदनिराकरणमुदितानुदितस्य निराकरणम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं रविचन्द्रमसौ ज्वलनश्च कथम् ॥
translation: दिन और रात्रि का भेद भी उसमें नहीं है। उदय और अस्त का भेद भी उसमें नहीं है। यदि वह एक ही नित्य और सर्वरूप शिव है तो फिर सूर्य, चन्द्रमा और अग्नि उसमें कैसे हो सकती है।
english_translation: There is no distinction of day and night in that. No difference between rising and setting. If it is one eternal and all-pervading true self, then how can sun, moon, and fire exist within it?
essence: The true self is beyond all dualities and natural cycles of change.
simple_meaning: The true self is timeless and unchanging, beyond all dualities like day and night or rising and setting.
insight: It shifts your perspective from identifying with changing appearances to recognizing your timeless essence.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by constant change and cycles, remember your core remains untouched by time or events.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
गतकामविकामविभेद इति गतचेष्टविचेष्टविभेद इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं बहिरन्तरभिन्नमतिश्च कथम् ॥
translation: काम एवं विकाम का भेद उसमें नहीं है, चेष्टा और विचेष्टा का भेद भी उसमें नहीं है। यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्वरूप एवं शिव है तो फिर वह बाहर और भीतर भिन्न है ऐसी बुद्धि कैसे हो सकती है।
english_translation: There is no difference in desire or its absence, no difference in action or inaction; if the true self is one, eternal, and blissful, how can the mind perceive a difference between inside and outside?
essence: Your true self is beyond all differences like desire, action, inside, and outside.
simple_meaning: Desire and its absence, action and inaction, are not different for the true self, which is always whole and blissful; so the mind's idea of inside versus outside is mistaken.
insight: It teaches you to stop dividing experience into inner and outer; all is one in your true self.
modern_relevance: When you notice your thoughts and urges rise and fall, you sense how they don’t truly define who you are inside.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
यदि सारविसारविहीन इति यदि शून्यविशून्यविहीन इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं प्रथमं च कथं चरमं च कथम् ॥
translation: यदि वह ब्रह्म सार एवं असार से रहित है, यदि वह शून्य और अशून्य से भी रहित है ऐसा कहा जाता है। यदि वह नित्य, सर्वरूप एवं शिव है तो फिर उसे आदि व अन्त वाला कैसे कहा जा सकता है।
english_translation: If the supreme reality is beyond existence and non-existence, beyond emptiness and fullness, and is eternal, all-pervading, and auspicious, then how can it be called the beginning or the end?
essence: The true self beyond all dualities has no beginning and no end.
simple_meaning: The supreme reality is beyond all dualities like existence and non-existence, so it cannot be called having a beginning or an end.
insight: It shifts your mind from seeing things as limited by time to recognizing the boundless nature of the true self.
modern_relevance: When you think about your own nature beyond labels, you realize it doesn't fit into any timeline or category.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
यदिभेदविभेदनिराकरणं यदि वेदकवेद्यनिराकरणम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं तृतीयं च कथं तुरीयं च कथम् ॥
translation: यदि वह ब्रह्म भेद और विभेद से रहित है यदि उसमें ज्ञाता और ज्ञेय का भेद नहीं हैं, यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्वरूप एवं शिव है तो फिर उसमें तृतीय अवस्था (सुषुप्ति) एवं तुरीय अवस्था का भेद कैसे हो सकता है।
english_translation: If the supreme reality is free from difference and division, beyond knower and known, and is one eternal, all-pervading, and auspicious essence, then how can there be a distinction between the third (deep sleep) and the fourth (transcendent) states?
essence: True reality has no divisions; states of consciousness are illusions of separation.
simple_meaning: If the supreme reality is truly one and beyond all distinctions, then the usual separations between states of consciousness don't actually exist.
insight: It teaches you to stop seeing your experiences as fundamentally separate and instead recognize their underlying unity.
modern_relevance: When your mind tries to separate your experiences into strict categories, this reminds you that deeper reality is whole and indivisible.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
गदिताविदितं न हि सत्यमिति विदिताविदितं नहि सत्यमिति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं विषयेन्द्रियबुद्धिमनांसि कथम् ॥
translation: ब्रह्म के बारे में जो कहा गया है और जो नहीं कहा गया है दोनों सत्य नहीं हैं। जो विदित है और अविदित है दोनों सत्य नहीं है। यदि वह चेतन नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव रूप एक ही है तो ये विषय, इन्द्रियाँ, बुद्धि और मन कैसे हो सकते हैं।
english_translation: What is spoken and unspoken about the supreme reality are both not true; if the supreme is conscious, eternal, all, and benevolent, how can there be senses, intellect, and mind?
essence: Truth about the supreme is beyond everything said or unsaid and cannot coexist with separate faculties.
simple_meaning: Neither what is said nor what is unsaid about the supreme reality fully captures the truth. If the supreme is one, eternal, conscious, and benevolent, then how can separate senses, mind, and intellect exist?
insight: It shifts your mind from relying on conceptual knowledge to embracing the mystery beyond all categories.
modern_relevance: When you try to explain your deepest experience, words fall short and feel disconnected from what you truly know inside.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
गगनं पवनो न हि सत्यमिति धरणी दहनो न हि सत्यमिति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं जलदश्च कथं सलिलं च कथम् ॥
translation: आकाश और वायु सत्य नहीं है, पृथ्वी और अग्नि भी सत्य नहीं हैं। यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो यह बादल और जल किस प्रकार सत्य हो सकते हैं।
english_translation: The sky and wind are not the true self, nor are earth and fire; if the one eternal supreme reality is all, how can clouds and water be true?
essence: Only the one eternal reality is truly real; all else is impermanent.
simple_meaning: Everything that changes like sky, wind, earth, fire, clouds, and water is not the true self; only the one eternal supreme reality is real.
insight: This verse shifts your view from identifying with ever-changing things to recognizing the unchanging reality behind them.
modern_relevance: You watch the weather shift outside your window, realizing that nothing permanent appears in the changing sky or wind, just like your thoughts and feelings.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
यदि कल्पितलोकनिराकरणं यदि कल्पितदेवनिराकरणम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं गुणदोषविचारमतिश्च कथम् ॥
translation: शास्त्रों में इसका निराकरण किया गया है कि ये सभी लोक कल्पित हैं, ये सभी देवता कल्पित हैं। केवल एक ब्रह्म ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर गुण दोष विचार वाली बुद्धि कैसे सत्य हो सकती है।
english_translation: The scriptures reject the world and gods as imagined; only the supreme reality is eternal, universal, and auspicious—so how can the mind that judges qualities and faults be true?
essence: The ultimate reality is beyond all mental judgments of qualities and faults.
simple_meaning: Only the supreme reality is truly real and eternal; the world, gods, and the mind that judges qualities are all imagined and not ultimately true.
insight: Stop trusting your mind’s constant judgment as a reflection of true reality; it shifts your perspective beyond duality.
modern_relevance: When your mind categorizes people or situations as good or bad, remember this division is a mental construct, not the whole truth.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
मरणामरणं हि निराकरणं करणाकरणं हि निराकरणम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं गमनागमनं हि कथं वदति ॥
translation: वेद ग्रन्थों में जन्म एवं मृत्यु का निराकरण किया गया है, कर्तव्य एवं अकर्तव्य का भी निराकरण किया गया है। यदि वह ब्रह्म एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर गमन आगमन किस प्रकार कहा जा सकता है।
english_translation: The Vedas negate birth and death, action and inaction; if the supreme is one, eternal, and all-good, how can movement and change be spoken of?
essence: The supreme reality is beyond birth, death, and any change, so movement is an illusion.
simple_meaning: Birth, death, doing, and not doing are negated by the supreme reality, which is one and eternal. Movement and change cannot truly happen to it.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as caught in change to recognizing your unchanging essence beyond all movement.
modern_relevance: When life's ups and downs feel overwhelming, remember the deepest part of you is beyond all change and cycles of loss and gain.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
प्रकृतिः पुरुषो न हि भेद इति न हि कारणकार्यविभेद इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं पुरुषापुरुषं च कथं वदति ॥
translation: इसमें प्रकृति और पुरुष का भेद नहीं हैं, न ही कारण एवं कार्य का विभेद ही है। यदि सर्वत्र एक ही नित्य सर्वरूप एवं शिव आत्मा ही है तो फिर पुरुष और अपुरुष (प्रकृति) किस प्रकार कहा जाता हैं।
english_translation: There is no difference between the natural world and pure awareness, nor between cause and effect. If everything is eternally one and wholly auspicious, how can we speak of awareness and the non-awareness as separate?
essence: All appearances of duality between awareness and nature are ultimately false.
simple_meaning: There is no real difference between pure awareness and the natural world, or between cause and effect. Everything is eternally one and auspicious.
insight: It shifts your mind from seeing separate things to recognizing underlying unity in all experience.
modern_relevance: You catch yourself dividing experience into self and other, cause and result, only to see how everything flows as one seamless reality beneath.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
तृतीयं न हि दुःखसमागमनं न गुणाद्द्वितीयस्य समागमनम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं स्थविरश्च युवा च शिशुश्च कथम् ॥
translation: ब्रह्म में तीन प्रकार के दु:खों का समागम नहीं है, न ही दोनों गुणों का समागम है। यदि सर्वत्र एक ही नित्य शिव रूप ब्रह्म है तो फिर बुढ़ापा, युवावस्था एवं शिशु अवस्था किस प्रकार कही जा सकती है।
english_translation: In the supreme reality, there is no coming together of three types of suffering, nor the union of two qualities. If the supreme reality is eternally one and unchanging, then how can old age, youth, and childhood be said to exist?
essence: The true self is timeless and beyond all changes like age or suffering.
simple_meaning: The true self is one and unchanging, so suffering and different life stages like youth or old age do not truly belong to it.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing life stages to recognizing your unchanging true self.
modern_relevance: When you worry about growing older or facing hardship, this verse reminds you that your essence is untouched by time or pain.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
ननु आश्रमवर्णविहीनपरं ननु कारणकर्तृविहीनपरम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवमविनष्टविनष्टमतिश्च कथम् ॥
translation: निश्चय ही आत्मा आश्रम और वर्ण से रहित श्रेष्ठ हैं, निश्चय ही यह कारण एवं कार्य से रहित श्रेष्ठ है। यदि यह एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो इसमें नाश होने वाली एवं नाश रहित बुद्धि कैसे हो सकती है।
english_translation: The true self is indeed beyond ashramas and social classes, beyond cause and effect. If it is the one eternal, all-pervading, and auspicious reality, how can it have a nature that is both perishable and imperishable?
essence: Your true self transcends all social divisions, causes, and contradictory natures.
simple_meaning: Your true self is beyond social roles, causes, and effects. It is one eternal reality that cannot be both destructible and indestructible.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing roles and causes to recognizing your unchanging essence beyond opposites.
modern_relevance: You may feel trapped by roles, causes, or outcomes—this reminds you that your true self is beyond all these shifting conditions.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
ग्रसिताग्रसितं च वितथ्यमिति जनिताजनितं च वितथ्यमिति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवमविनाशि विनाशि कथं हि भवेत् ॥
translation: ग्रसने वाला और ग्रसित दोनों ही मिथ्या हैं। उत्पन्न करने वाला और उत्पन्न हुआ दोनों ही मिथ्या हैं। यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर वह अविनाशी एवं नाश होने वाला कैसे हो सकता है।
english_translation: The devourer and the devoured are both false. The creator and the created are both false. If the one is eternal, all, and auspicious, how can it be both destructible and indestructible?
essence: The eternal self transcends all dualities of creator and creation, devourer and devoured.
simple_meaning: Both the roles of eater and eaten, and creator and created, are illusions. The one true self is eternal and cannot be both destructible and indestructible.
insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with changing roles to recognizing the unchanging eternal self beyond all dualities.
modern_relevance: When you feel torn between roles—maker and made, winner and loser—remember your true nature is beyond these opposites.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
पुरुषापुरुषस्य विनष्टमिति वनितावनितस्य विनष्टमिति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवमविनोदविनोदमतिश्च कथम् ॥
translation: आत्मा में पुरुष एवं अपुरुष का भाव नहीं हैं, उस में स्त्री एवं अस्त्री का भाव भी नहीं हैं। यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर उसमें अविनोद और विनोद की बुद्धि किस प्रकार हो सकती है।
english_translation: The true self contains no sense of person or non-person, no sense of woman or non-woman; if it is the one eternal, all-pervading, and auspicious reality, how can the mind of pleasure and displeasure arise in it?
essence: Your true self is beyond all opposites, untouched by pleasure or pain.
simple_meaning: The true self is beyond all distinctions of person, gender, or emotions like pleasure and pain. It is one eternal reality without duality.
insight: It teaches you to see beyond shifting identities and emotions to the unchanging reality within.
modern_relevance: When your mood swings between joy and frustration, this reminds you that your core being remains steady beyond those changes.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
यदि मोहविषादविहीनपरो यदि संशयशोकविहीनपरः ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवमहमत्र ममेति कथं च पुनः ॥
translation: जब वह आत्मा मोह एवं विषाद से रहित इनसे परे है, यदि वह संशय और शोक से रहित और इनसे परे है, यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर ‘मैं’ और ‘मेरा’ इस प्रकार का कथन कैसे हो सकता है।
english_translation: If the true self is beyond attachment and despair, beyond doubt and sorrow, if it is one, eternal, all, and auspicious, then how can 'I' and 'mine' arise here again?
essence: 'I' and 'mine' cannot belong to the true self that is beyond all attachment and sorrow.
simple_meaning: Your true self is beyond attachment, sorrow, doubt, and separation; it is one and eternal, so ideas of 'I' and 'mine' cannot apply.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing emotions to recognizing your unchanging true self beyond personal claims.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by doubt or sorrow, remember your deepest self remains untouched and beyond such feelings.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
महमेति ननु धर्मविधर्मविनाश इति ननु बन्धविबन्धविनाश इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवंमिहदुःखविदुःखमतिश्च कथम् ॥
translation: निश्चय ही आत्मा धर्म एवं विधर्म से रहित है। निश्चय ही वह बन्ध और मुक्ति से भी रहित है। यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर उसमें सुख एवं दु:ख की बुद्धि किस प्रकार हो सकती है।
english_translation: The true self is certainly free from right and wrong, free from bondage and liberation; if it is one, eternal, all, and auspicious, how can it have the mind of pleasure and pain?
essence: The true self transcends all pairs of opposites including pleasure and pain.
simple_meaning: The true self is beyond concepts like right and wrong, bondage and freedom, pleasure and pain. It is unchanging, all-encompassing, and auspicious.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing feelings to recognizing your unchanging true self beyond them.
modern_relevance: When you face conflicting feelings or moral dilemmas, remember your deeper self remains untouched and peaceful beyond them.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
न हि याज्ञिकयज्ञविभाग इति न हुताशनवस्तुविभाग इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं वद कर्मफलानि भवन्ति कथम् ॥
translation: आत्मा में याज्ञिक और यज्ञ का विभाग नहीं है, न हवन सामग्री एवं अग्नि का विभाग ही है। यदि वह एक ही निरन्तर, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर कहो उसमें कर्मों का फल किस प्रकार होता है।
english_translation: The true self has no division of priest or ritual, no separate fire or offerings; if it is one, continuous, all-pervading, and auspicious, then how can actions bear fruit in it?
essence: The true self is one and undivided; it cannot be affected by action’s results.
simple_meaning: The true self is undivided and beyond ritual roles or objects. If it is always one and auspicious, then actions cannot produce results in it.
insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as fragmented by roles and actions to recognizing your unchanging unity beyond them.
modern_relevance: You might feel pressured to fit roles or outcomes at work, but your core self remains untouched by those divisions or results.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
ननु शोकविशोकविमुक्त इति ननु दर्पविदर्पविमुक्त इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं ननु रागविरागमतिश्च कथम् ॥
translation: निश्चय ही आत्मा शोक-विशोक से मुक्त है, निश्चय ही वह अहंकार एवं निरहंकार से भी मुक्त है। यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर उसमें राग एवं विराग की बुद्धि किस प्रकार हो सकती है।
english_translation: The true self is certainly free from sorrow and joy, and also free from pride and humility; if it is one, eternal, all-pervading, and auspicious, then how can it have the intellect of attachment and detachment?
essence: The true self is beyond all pairs of opposites like sorrow and joy or attachment and detachment.
simple_meaning: You are naturally free from sorrow, pride, attachment, and detachment because your true self is one, eternal, and complete.
insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as caught in emotional ups and downs to recognizing your constant, unchanging nature.
modern_relevance: When your mood swings between pride and shame or attachment and rejection, remember your true self remains untouched and whole beyond these feelings.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
न हि मोहविमोहविकार इति न हि लोभविलोभविकार इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं ह्यविवेकविवेकमतिश्च कथम् ॥
translation: आत्मा में मोह विमोह का विकार नहीं हैं, न ही लोभ और अलोभ का विकार ही है। यदि यह आत्मा एक ही, नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर उसमें अविवेक और विवेक बुद्धि किस प्रकार हो सकती है।
english_translation: The true self has no defects of attachment or detachment, no faults of greed or lack of greed; if the self is one, eternal, all-pervading, and benevolent, how can it possess ignorance or wisdom?
essence: The true self is beyond all dualities like attachment, greed, ignorance, and wisdom.
simple_meaning: The true self is free from any faults like attachment, greed, or their opposites. Being eternal and all-pervading, it cannot have ignorance or wisdom as qualities.
insight: This verse shifts your view from identifying with fluctuating desires and judgments to recognizing your unchanging, faultless essence.
modern_relevance: When emotions like craving or aversion arise, remember your true self remains untouched, offering a steady refuge in any turmoil.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
त्वमहं न हि हन्त कदाचिदपि कुलजातिविचारमसत्यमिति ।
अहमेव शिवः परमार्थ इति अभिवादनमत्र करोमि कथम् ॥
translation: खेद है कि आत्मा में तू और मैं का भेद कदापि नहीं है तथा उसमें कुल एवं जाति का विचार भी असत्य ही है। परमार्थ रूप में में ही कल्याणकारी आत्मा हूँ फिर में किस प्रकार यहाँ अभिवादन करूँ।
english_translation: I regret that in the true self there is never a distinction of you and me, nor of family or caste; in ultimate reality, I am the benevolent true self, so how can I offer respect here?
essence: All divisions vanish in the true self where only unity remains.
simple_meaning: There is never any real difference between you and me or among social groups in the true self; in ultimate reality, I am the benevolent true self, so offering respect here seems unnecessary.
insight: It shifts your mind from seeing others as separate to recognizing fundamental oneness beyond social labels.
modern_relevance: When you realize the divisions between people are mental, it frees you from judgment and separation in daily life.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
गुरुशिष्यविचारविशीर्ण इति उपदेशविचारविशीर्ण इति ।
अहमेव शिवः परमार्थ इति अभिवादनमत्र करोमि कथम् ॥
translation: आत्मा में गुरु शिष्य का विचार भी नहीं है जिससे उपदेश का विचार भी नहीं हैं। में ही परमार्थ में शिव रूप हूँ। फिर मैं यहाँ किस प्रकार अभिवादन करूँ।
english_translation: In the true self, there is no thought of teacher or student, nor of instruction. I alone am the supreme reality as Shiva. How then can I offer salutations here?
essence: The true self transcends all dualities including teacher and student; it alone is supreme.
simple_meaning: The true self has no separation of teacher and student or any instruction. It alone is the ultimate reality as Shiva, making formal salutations unnecessary.
insight: It shifts your perspective from relying on external roles to recognizing your own inherent completeness as the supreme reality.
modern_relevance: When you realize your true nature, the need for external authorities or roles fades, freeing you from dependency on others for guidance.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
न हि कल्पितदेहविभाग इति न हि कल्पितलोकविभाग इति ।
अहमेव शिवः परमार्थ इति अभिवादनमत्र करोमि कथम् ॥
translation: कल्पित देह से भी आत्मा का भेद सिद्ध नहीं होता, कल्पित लोकों से भी इसका भेद सिद्ध नहीं होता। मैं ही परमार्थ में शिव रूप आत्मा हूँ फिर मैं किस प्रकार अभिवादन करूं।
english_translation: The true self does not differ from the imagined body or the imagined worlds. I am the supreme being in reality; how then could I offer reverence?
essence: You are the supreme reality beyond all imagined division, so reverence to the self is needless.
simple_meaning: The true self is not different from the body or the worlds we imagine. The self is the supreme reality, so offering reverence to it is unnecessary.
insight: It shifts thinking from seeing yourself as a fragmented being to recognizing your oneness with all appearances.
modern_relevance: When you see yourself as separate from your body or surroundings, you might feel small or limited, but recognizing your true nature as whole frees you from that division.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
सरजो विरजो न कदाचिदपि ननु निर्मलनिश्चलशुद्ध इति ।
अहमेव शिवः परमार्थ इति अभिवादनमत्र करोमि कथम् ॥
translation: वह आत्मा कभी भी राग एवं विराग वाली नहीं है, निश्चय ही यह निर्मल, निश्चल एवं शुद्ध है। मैं परमार्थ रूप में वही शिवरूप आत्मा हूँ फिर में किस प्रकार अभिवादन करूँ।
english_translation: The true self is never attached or detached; it is pure, steady, and immaculate. I am that self as the supreme reality, so how could I offer salutations to myself?
essence: The true self is eternally pure and steady; it needs no salutation.
simple_meaning: The true self never experiences attachment or detachment. It is always pure, steady, and immaculate. Realizing this, there is no need to offer respect to something that you already are.
insight: It shifts your perspective from seeking approval to owning your unchanging true self as whole.
modern_relevance: When you struggle with self-doubt or feel the need to prove your worth, this reminds you that your true nature is already pure and complete.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
न हि देहविदेहविकल्प इति अनृतं चरितं न हि सत्यमिति ।
अहमेव शिवः परमार्थ इति अभिवादनमत्र करोमि कथम् ॥
translation: उस आत्मा में देह और विदेह का विकल्प भी नहीं है, उसमें मिथ्या चरित्र भी सत्य नहीं हैं। मैं ही परमार्थ रूप में वही शिव रूप आत्मा हूँ। फिर मैं किस प्रकार अभिवादन करूं।
english_translation: In that true self, there is no distinction of embodied or disembodied, no false or true character. I am the true self, the supreme reality, the auspicious being. How then should I offer respect?
essence: No duality exists in your true self, so honoring another separate self is unnecessary.
simple_meaning: There is no real difference between having a body or not, or between truth and falsehood in the true self. The true self is the supreme reality. So, there is no one else to honor.
insight: It shifts your understanding from seeing yourself as a separate entity to recognizing your unity with all existence, dissolving the need for external validation.
modern_relevance: You realize that all the roles and labels you juggle don't define your true self, so you stop feeling the pressure to perform or please others.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
विन्दति विन्दति न हि न हि यत्र छन्दोलक्षणं न हि न हि तत्र ।
समरसमग्नो भावितपूतः प्रलपति तत्त्वं परमवधूतः ॥
translation: परम अवधूत ( श्रेष्ठ ज्ञानी) जिसका अन्त:करण पवित्र है वह उस एकरस आत्मा में ही मग्न रहता है तथा उसी का कथन करता है जिसमें छन्द और लक्षण नहीं है उसी आत्मा को प्राप्त होता है।
english_translation: The supreme Avadhuta, whose inner being is pure, remains immersed in the one undifferentiated self beyond form and qualities, and speaks only that ultimate truth.
essence: The highest self is pure, undivided, and beyond all forms and qualities.
simple_meaning: A fully realized person stays absorbed in the pure self beyond all appearances and speaks only that ultimate reality.
insight: Shift your focus from external forms to the unchanging pure awareness within you.
modern_relevance: When distractions and labels overwhelm you, remember your true self is untouched and pure beneath all noise.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
रथ्याकर्पटविरचितकन्थः पुण्यापुण्यविवर्जितपन्थः ।
शून्यागारे तिष्ठति नग्नो शुद्धनिरञ्जनसमरसमग्नः ॥
translation: जीवन्मुक्त अवधूत गलियों में पड़े चिथड़ों की झोली बनाकर, पाप और पुण्य रहित मार्ग पर चलता हुआ नग्न होकर शून्य मन्दिर में स्थित होकर शुद्ध, निर्दोष एवं समरस आत्मा में ही लीन रहता है।
english_translation: The liberated Avadhuta walks the path free of good and bad, naked, dwelling in the empty temple, immersed in the pure, spotless, and undivided self.
essence: Freedom arises when you shed all dualities and rest naked in pure awareness.
simple_meaning: You live beyond good and bad, stripped of all pretenses, resting in pure and undivided being.
insight: It invites you to stop defining yourself by external values and rest in your pure, undivided nature instead.
modern_relevance: You let go of all judgments about yourself and others, standing vulnerable yet whole, beyond any moral labels or societal masks.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
लक्ष्यालक्ष्यविवर्जितलक्ष्यो युक्तायुक्तविवर्जितदक्षः ।
केवलतत्त्वनिरञ्जनपूतो वादविवादः कथमवधूतः ॥
translation: लक्ष्य और अलक्ष्य से रहित ही जिसका लक्ष्य है, युक्त और अयुक्त से रहित जो दक्ष है, केवल उस निरंजन आत्मतत्व में मग्न अवधूत वाद-विवाद कैसे करे।
english_translation: The Avadhuta, immersed in the pure essence beyond visible and invisible, capable beyond the attached and unattached, how could he engage in argument or dispute?
essence: True mastery is living beyond all dualities where argument no longer arises.
simple_meaning: When you are fully absorbed in the pure true self beyond all opposites, arguing or debating has no place.
insight: It teaches you to recognize when conflict is unnecessary because your awareness transcends all opposites.
modern_relevance: You’ve stopped fighting with yourself or others because you see beyond right or wrong, beyond winning or losing.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
आशापाशविबन्धनमुक्ताः शौचाचारविवर्जितयुक्ताः ।
एवं सर्वविवर्जितशान्तास्तत्त्वं शुद्धनिरञ्जनवन्तः ॥
translation: आशा रूपी पाश के बन्धन से मुक्त हैं, बाहर के शौच आचार से रहित आत्मा से युक्त सन्त सभी प्रकार के तत्वों से रहित शुद्ध एवं निर्दोष है।
english_translation: Those freed from the bonds of desire, untouched by external rites, are pure, spotless, and free from all elements.
essence: True purity arises when desire and external rituals no longer bind you.
simple_meaning: Freedom from desire and external rituals reveals your pure, peaceful true nature beyond all elements.
insight: It shifts your focus from outer forms and desires to the pure essence that is naturally free and peaceful.
modern_relevance: You feel peace when you stop chasing wants and relax your need to follow every rule or expectation around you.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
कथमिह देहविदेहविचारः कथमिह रागविरागविचारः ।
निर्मलनिश्चलगगनाकारं स्वयमिह तत्त्वं सहजाकारम् ॥
translation: जीवन्मुक्त ज्ञानी में देह और विदेह का विचार किस प्रकार हो सकता है, उसमें राग एवं विराग का विचार भी कैसे हो सकता है। वह स्वयं ही स्वभाव से ही आत्म तत्व हैं जो निर्मल, निश्चल एवं आकाश के समान व्यापक है।
english_translation: How can a liberated knower think of body and beyond-body, or feel attachment and detachment? They are naturally the pure, steady essence, vast like the sky.
essence: True freedom means being steady and pure beyond body and desire.
simple_meaning: A truly liberated person does not think in terms of body or outside body, attachment or detachment. Their true nature is pure, steady, and vast like the sky.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with fleeting states to recognizing your natural, unchanging essence.
modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by your body’s needs and emotional swings. Yet your true self remains calm and vast beneath those waves.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
कथमिह तत्त्वं विन्दति यत्र रूपमरूपं कथमिह तत्र ।
गगनाकारः परमो यत्र विषयीकरणं कथमिह तत्र ॥
translation: जीवन्मुक्त ज्ञानी जहाँ इस अवस्था में तत्व को किस प्रकार जान सकता है वहाँ रूप एवं अरूप को भी किस प्रकार जान सकता है क्योंकि वह जहाँ आकाश स्वरूप परमतत्व आत्मा ही है फिर वहाँ विषयों का व्यवहार भी नहीं हो सकता।
english_translation: How can the liberated knower find the essence where form and formlessness exist? How can there be distinctions where the supreme reality is like space, free of qualities?
essence: The supreme reality is beyond all form and distinctions, like infinite space.
simple_meaning: You cannot understand essence where form and formlessness both exist, because the supreme reality is like space without distinctions.
insight: It shifts your mind from looking for defined forms to recognizing the limitless, undifferentiated reality beneath appearances.
modern_relevance: When you try to define your true nature, you realize it cannot be pinned down by any shape or category—it's boundless and free.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
गगनाकारनिरन्तरहंसस्तत्त्वविशुद्धनिरञ्जनहंसः ।
एवं कथमिह भिन्नविभिन्नं बन्धविबन्धविकारविभिन्नम् ॥
translation: यह आत्मतत्व आकाश तुल्य व्यापक, नित्य, विशुद्ध, निर्दोष एवं हंस तुल्य है। यह एक ही है इसलिए इसमें भिन्नता एवं समानता का कथन कैसे हो सकता है। इसमें बन्धन, बन्धन रहित एवं विकार का भेद भी नहीं हो सकता।
english_translation: The true self is vast like the sky, eternal, pure, and spotless like a swan; therefore, how can it have differences, bonds, or faults?
essence: The true self is eternally pure and one without distinction or defect.
simple_meaning: The true self is vast and pure, like the sky and an untouched swan. It cannot have differences, bonds, or faults.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as limited and flawed to recognizing your essential boundless purity.
modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your flaws or mistakes, remember your true self is vast and pure, unaffected by those changes.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
केवलतत्त्वनिरन्तरसर्वंयोगवियोगौ कथमिह गर्वम् ।
एवं परमनिरन्तरसर्व मेवं कथमिह सारविसारम् ॥
translation: केवल आत्मतत्व ही नित्य एवं सर्व है, इसमें अहंकारवश योग और वियोग को कथन किस प्रकार हो सकता है। तथा यह आत्मा परम, नित्य एवं सर्व है तो इसमें सार एवं असार भी कैसे हो सकता है।
english_translation: The true self alone is eternal and all-pervading; how can pride arise from union and separation? Since the self is supreme, eternal, and all, how can there be essence and non-essence?
essence: The eternal true self cannot be divided by union, separation, or value judgments.
simple_meaning: The true self is always whole and eternal. It cannot be divided by ideas of coming together or falling apart, nor by what is important or not.
insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with fluctuating events to resting in the unchanging self.
modern_relevance: When relationships or situations shift, you might feel pride or loss. Recognizing your inner self is beyond these ups and downs steadies your sense of self.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
केवलतत्त्वनिरञ्जनसर्वं गगनाकारनिरन्तरशुद्धम् ।
एवं कथमिह सङ्गविसङ्गं सत्यं कथमिह रङ्गविरङ्गम् ॥
translation: केवल यह आत्मा ही निर्दोष, सवरूप, आकाश, तुल्य व्यापक, नित्य एवं शुद्ध है इसलिए इसमें संग और विसंग कैसे हो सकता है। इसमें सत्य, रंग और विरंग कैसे हो सकता है।
english_translation: The true self alone is pure, formless like space, endlessly pure and pervasive; how then can it have attachment or detachment, truth or falsehood?
essence: The true self is endlessly pure and cannot hold division or contradiction.
simple_meaning: The true self is like pure space—always spotless and unlimited. It cannot have attachments, separations, or contradictions like truth and falsehood.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as fragmented to recognizing your unbroken, pure essence.
modern_relevance: When you feel torn by conflicting desires or judgments, remember your true nature is beyond all these divisions and remains pure.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
योगवियोगै रहितो योगी भोगविभोगै रहितो भोगी ।
एवं चरति हि मन्दं मन्दं मनसा कल्पितसहजानन्दम् ॥
translation: आत्मज्ञानी योगी योग एवं वैराग्य से रहित हो जाता है, भोगी होकर भी भोग और त्याग से रहित हो जाता है। वह अपने मन द्वारा कल्पित स्वाभाविक आनन्द में मन्द-मन्द गति से ( अपनी ही मस्ती में) विचरण करता है।
english_translation: The true knower moves beyond yoga and renunciation, enjoying natural bliss in gentle ease.
essence: You can be free from effort and craving while gently living in imagined natural bliss.
simple_meaning: You become free from the need for spiritual striving and from craving or rejecting pleasures. You gently live in your mind’s natural joy.
insight: It shifts your focus from forcing spiritual effort to allowing natural joy to unfold quietly within.
modern_relevance: You stop wrestling with every urge or discipline and instead find calm joy simply by letting things be, moving gently through life.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
बोधविबोधैः सततं युक्तो द्वैताद्वैतैः कथमिह मुक्तः ।
सहजो विरजः कथमिह योगी शुद्धनिरञ्जनसमरसभोगी ॥
translation: जो व्यक्ति ज्ञान एवं अज्ञान से निरन्तर युक्त हैं, तथा जो द्वैत और अद्वैत से भी युक्त है वह कैसे मुक्त हो सकता है। इस संसार में योगी सहज ही राग रहित किस प्रकार हो सकता है। आत्मानन्द का भोक्ता ही शुद्ध, निर्दोष एवं समरस होता है।
english_translation: How can one be free who is constantly attached to both knowledge and ignorance, duality and non-duality? How can a yogi be naturally without desire? Only the one who enjoys the bliss of the true self is pure, spotless, and fully harmonious.
essence: True freedom arises only when you are naturally free from all attachments, including to knowledge and ignorance.
simple_meaning: You cannot be truly free if you remain attached to knowledge or ignorance, or to any duality. True purity and harmony come from being naturally free of desire and fully immersed in the bliss of your true self.
insight: It teaches you to drop all mental attachments, including to the concepts of knowledge and ignorance, to experience true freedom.
modern_relevance: You feel stuck toggling between what you think you know and what you doubt, unable to find peace or freedom in your mind.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
भग्नाभग्नविवर्जितभग्नो लग्नालग्नविवर्जितलग्नः ।
एवं कथमिह सारविसारः समरसतत्त्वं गगनाकारः ॥
translation: यह आत्मा समरस तत्व एवं आकाश तुल्य व्यापक हैं जो खण्ड-अखण्ड एवं खण्ड से रहित हैं, यह किसी में लगा हुआ, नहीं लगा हुआ एवं लगे हुए से रहित है। इसे सार एवं असार भी किस प्रकार कहा जा सकता है।
english_translation: The true self is like vast sky—both fragmented and unfragmented, attached and unattached simultaneously; how can it be called real or unreal?
essence: You are vast and free beyond all opposites, both attached and unattached at once.
simple_meaning: The true self is vast and all-pervading like the sky. It is beyond being fragmented or whole, attached or detached. It cannot be labeled as real or unreal.
insight: It shifts your view from defining yourself by conditions to recognizing your unbounded, paradox-embracing nature.
modern_relevance: When your mind tries to pin you down as this or that, remember you are vast and free, beyond any label or limitation.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
सततं सर्वविवर्जितयुक्तः सर्वं तत्त्वविवर्जितमुक्तः ।
एवं कथमिह जीवितमरणं ध्यानाध्यानैः कथमिह करणम् ॥
translation: योगी निरन्तर उस सर्व रहित आत्मा से मुक्त रहता है तथा सम्पूर्ण तत्वों से रहित होकर मुक्त रहता है। इस प्रकार उसका जीना और मरना किस प्रकार होता है। फिर उसका ध्यान करना और न करना कैसे हो सकता है।
english_translation: The yogi remains constantly free, detached from everything and all elements; thus, how can living and dying, or meditating and not meditating, happen to them?
essence: Complete freedom dissolves all distinctions of action, life, and death.
simple_meaning: A yogi who is fully free and detached from everything does not truly experience living or dying, nor the act of meditating or not meditating.
insight: It shifts your view from identifying with life’s changes to recognizing your unchanging freedom beyond them.
modern_relevance: You’ve felt overwhelmed by endless choices and worries about success or failure—this frees you from all that pressure entirely.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
इन्द्रजालमिदं सर्वं यथा मरुमरीचिका ।
अखण्डितमनाकारो वर्तते केवलः शिवः ॥
translation: यह सम्पूर्ण जगत इन्द्रजाल के समान हैं अथवा मरुस्थल की मरीचिका के समान है। इनमें केवल घनाकार के रूप में अखण्डित कल्याण स्वरूप आत्मा ही वर्तता है।
english_translation: This entire world is like a magic illusion or a mirage in the desert; only the undivided, radiant true self exists.
essence: Only the undivided, radiant true self truly exists beyond all illusions.
simple_meaning: The world you perceive is like a magic illusion or desert mirage. Only the whole, radiant true self truly exists.
insight: It shifts your mind from clinging to appearances toward recognizing the unchanging true self behind all change.
modern_relevance: When life feels confusing and unstable, like things are slipping away, remember that your true self remains unshaken, like a steady light behind all illusions.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
धर्मादौ मोक्षपर्यन्तं निरीहाः सर्वथा वयम् ।
कथं रागविरागैश्च कल्पयन्ति विपश्चितः ॥
translation: हम धर्म आदि को लेकर मोक्ष पर्यन्त इच्छा रहित हैं। फिर पण्डित लोग किस प्रकार हम में राग और विराग की कल्पना करते हैं।
english_translation: From duty to liberation, we remain without desire in every way; how then do the wise imagine attachment and detachment in us?
essence: You are untouched by desire or aversion through every stage of existence.
simple_meaning: You remain completely free of desire through all stages, from duty to liberation. Wise people mistakenly imagine you have attachment or detachment.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing desire and aversion as real states to understanding them as mental projections.
modern_relevance: When you feel pressured to want or reject things to grow, remember that your true self is already beyond these swings.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
विन्दति विन्दति न हि न हि यत्र छन्दोलक्षणं न हि न हि तत्र ।
समरसमग्नो भावितपूतः प्रलपति तत्त्वं परमवधूतः ॥
translation: परम अवधूत ( श्रेष्ठ ज्ञानी) जिसका अन्त:करण पवित्र है उस एकरस आत्मा में ही मग्न रहता है तथा उस आत्मतत्व का ही कथन करता है। जिसमें छन्द और लक्षण नहीं हैं उसी आत्मा को प्राप्त होता है।
english_translation: The supreme wise one, whose inner being is pure, remains absorbed in the unified true self and speaks only of that essence where there are no divisions or qualities.
essence: True wisdom is immersion in the pure self beyond all qualities and divisions.
simple_meaning: The highest wise one stays absorbed in the pure true self, which has no divisions or qualities, and speaks only of that essence.
insight: Recognize your identity beyond all mental categories and descriptions, resting in pure awareness itself.
modern_relevance: When all external labels and judgments fall away, you can find calm and deep connection to your true nature beneath the noise.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
त्वद्यात्रया व्यापकता हता ते
ध्यानेन चेतःपरता हता ते ।
स्तुत्या मया वाक्परता हता ते
क्षमस्व नित्यं त्रिविधापराधान् ॥
translation: तुम्हारी यात्रा से व्यापकता नष्ट हुई, तुम्हारे ध्यान से चित्त की विषयपरता नष्ट हुई, तुम्हारी स्तुति से मेरी वाणी की विषयपरता नष्ट हुई अब मैं नित्य तीन प्रकार के अपराधों से क्षमा माँगता हूँ।
english_translation: Your journey ended my expansion, your meditation ended my mind's restlessness, your praise ended my speech's distractions; now I eternally seek forgiveness for these three offenses.
essence: Focused presence dissolves restless distractions and opens the way to lasting forgiveness.
simple_meaning: Your journey stopped my restless expansion, your meditation calmed my distracted mind, and your praise quieted my distracted speech; now I ask forgiveness for these faults forever.
insight: It teaches you to recognize how presence and focused attention can dissolve mental chaos and open the heart to forgiveness.
modern_relevance: After a long day overwhelmed by scattered thoughts and restless speech, you finally find calm and feel ready to forgive yourself for the slip-ups.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
कामैरहतधीर्दान्तो मृदुः शुचिरकिञ्चनः ।
अनीहो मितभुक् शान्तः स्थिरो मच्छरणो मुनिः ॥
translation: जिसकी बुद्धि कामना रहित है (निष्काम है), जिसने बाह्य इन्द्रियों को वश में कर लिया है, जो कोमल स्वभाव वाला है, पवित्र रहता हो, थोड़े में गुजारा करता हो, इच्छा रहित हो, थोड़ा भोजन करता हो, शान्त हो, स्थिर बुद्धि वाला हो तथा आत्मा की शरण हो वही मुनि है।
english_translation: One whose mind is free of desire, who controls the senses, is gentle, pure, content with little, desireless, calm, steady-minded, and refuge of the self—that one is a sage.
essence: A sage is calm, desireless, gentle, and steady, offering refuge to the true self.
simple_meaning: A sage is someone who is free from craving, controls their senses, stays gentle and pure, lives simply, and remains calm and steady as a refuge for their true self.
insight: It teaches you to cultivate calmness and simplicity by releasing desire and mastering your senses to become steady and centered.
modern_relevance: You find peace when you stop chasing wants, control impulses, stay gentle with yourself, and live simply without needless desires.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
अप्रमत्तो गभीरात्मा धृतिमान् जितषड्गुणः ।
अमानी मानदः कल्पो मैत्रः कारुणिकः कविः ॥
translation: जो प्रमाद से रहित, गम्भीर स्वभाव वाला, धैर्य युक्त, छ: विकारों को जिसने जीत लिया है, अभिमान रहित, दूसरों को मान देने वाला, मित्रतापूर्वक व्यवहार करने वाला, करुणावान, दयाशील है वही आत्मज्ञानी है।
english_translation: The self-knower is vigilant, profound, steady, has conquered the six faults, is free of pride, honors others, is friendly and compassionate.
essence: True wisdom is shown by steady calmness and kindness after mastering inner faults.
simple_meaning: A person who is always alert, deeply calm, patient, free of six inner faults, humble, respectful, friendly, and compassionate is truly wise.
insight: This verse shifts your focus from external achievement to mastering inner qualities like humility and compassion.
modern_relevance: When you stay calm under pressure, avoid negative reactions, and treat others with kindness, you become a source of steady wisdom in any situation.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
कृपालुरकृतद्रोहस्तितिक्षुः सर्वदेहिनाम् ।
सत्यसारोऽनवद्यात्मा समः सर्वोपकारकः ॥
translation: जो सम्पूर्ण देहधारियों के प्रति कृपालु, द्रोह ने करने वाला, सहनशील, सत्य का सार, जन्म-मरण से रहित, सम तथा सबका उपकार करने वाला है वही आत्मज्ञानी है।
english_translation: The true knower of the self is compassionate to all beings, free from hostility, patient, the essence of truth, beyond birth and death, equal to all, and a benefactor to everyone.
essence: Your true self is patient, kind, equal, and beyond all conflict or change.
simple_meaning: Your true self is kind to all, patient, free from hostility, beyond birth and death, equal to everyone, and always helpful.
insight: It teaches you to embody patience and compassion beyond personal grievances, seeing all as equal and worthy of kindness.
modern_relevance: When tensions rise around you, remember your inner self can remain calm, kind, and unaffected by conflict.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
अवधूतलक्षणं वर्णैर्ज्ञातव्यं भगवत्तमैः ।
वेदवर्णार्थतत्त्वज्ञैर्वेदवेदान्तवादिभिः ॥
translation: अवधूत (जीवन्मुक्त ज्ञानी) के ये लक्षण सभी वर्ण वालों को, भक्तों को, वेद वर्ण के तत्वज्ञ पण्डितों को, वेद-वेदान्त के ज्ञाता को जानना चाहिए।
english_translation: The characteristics of the Avadhuta (one liberated in life) must be known by all classes, devotees, scholars of Vedic knowledge, and teachers of Vedanta.
essence: The Avadhuta's qualities are essential knowledge for all sincere seekers.
simple_meaning: The qualities of the Avadhuta should be understood by all social groups, devotees, and learned Vedic and Vedanta scholars.
insight: It invites you to see spiritual freedom as accessible and relevant beyond any social or intellectual category.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
आशापाशविनिर्मुक्त आदिमध्यान्तनिर्मलः ।
आनन्दे वर्तते नित्यमकारं तस्य लक्षणम् ॥
translation: अवधूत शब्द चार अक्षरों से मिलकर बना है। अ+व+ धू+त। इसमें दत्तात्रेय जी अकार (अ) का लक्षण बताते हुए कहते हैं कि जो ‘आशा’ रूपी पाश से मुक्त है, ‘आदि’ मध्य और अन्त से निर्मल है, ‘आनन्द’ में ही नित्य मग्न रहता है ये तीनों अकार (अ) की अवधूत के लक्षण हैं।
english_translation: The liberated one is free from the bond of desire, pure in beginning, middle, and end, and always immersed in bliss; this is the mark of the Avadhuta.
essence: True freedom is being desireless, pure at every moment, and naturally immersed in bliss.
simple_meaning: You are completely free from desire and remain pure throughout, always living in bliss; this defines the liberated state.
insight: It teaches you to recognize that freedom and bliss arise when you release all desires and remain pure in your being.
modern_relevance: You notice how craving or longing no longer weighs you down, and joy flows naturally without effort, freeing you from restless wants.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
वासना वर्जिता येन वक्तव्यं च निरामयम् ।
वर्तमानेषु वर्तेत वकारं तस्य लक्षणम् ॥
translation: इसमें अ+व+धू+त शब्द में ‘व’ अक्षर का लक्षण बताते हुए दत्तात्रेय जी कहते हैं कि ‘वासना’ का जिसने त्याग कर दिया है और ‘वक्तव्य’ जिसका राग-रहित है, जो ‘वर्तमान’ में ही रहता है। ‘व’ (वकार) ही अवधूत के लक्षण हैं।
english_translation: The sign of the Avadhuta is one who has renounced desire, speaks without attachment, and lives fully in the present.
essence: Freedom is living desire-free, speaking without attachment, fully present now.
simple_meaning: The Avadhuta lives without desire, speaks without attachment, and stays fully present in the moment.
insight: This verse shifts your focus from clinging desires to clear, present living, freeing your speech and actions.
modern_relevance: You notice how your mood shifts when you stop chasing wants and just say what is true now.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
धूलिधूसरगात्राणि धूतचित्तो निरामयः ।
धारणाध्याननिर्मुक्तो धूकारस्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥
translation: दत्तात्रेय जी इसमें अ+व+ धू+त शब्द में ‘धू’ अक्षर का लक्षण बताते हुए कहते हैं कि ‘धूलिधूसर’ जिसके अंग हैं, ‘धूत चित्त’ (पापों से धोया गया चित्त) जिसका है, रोग रहित है, ‘धारणा ध्यान’ से जो मुक्त हो गया है ये तीन ‘धूकार’ ही अवधूत के लक्षण हैं।
english_translation: The Avadhuta’s marks are a body cleansed of dust and dirt, a mind washed free of faults, and liberation from attachment to meditation and concentration.
essence: Freedom is shown by a clean body, pure mind, and release from mental grasping.
simple_meaning: You are marked by a body free of dirt, a mind cleansed of faults, and freedom from attachment to mental focus.
insight: It teaches you to recognize freedom as a state beyond physical cleanliness and mental fixation.
modern_relevance: You wipe away all distractions and judgments, carrying a clear mind and body that no longer cling to habits or thoughts.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
तत्त्वचिन्ता धृता येन चिन्ताचेष्टाविवर्जितः ।
तमोऽहंकारनिर्मुक्तस्तकारस्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥
translation: दत्तात्रेय जी इसमें अ+व+ धू+त शब्द में तकार (त) का अर्थ बताते हुए कहते हैं कि जिसने ‘तत्व चिन्ता’ को ही धारण किया है, जो ‘चिन्ता और चेष्टा’ से रहित है, ‘तम रूपी अहंकार’ से जो रहित है ये तीनों ‘तकार’ अवधूत के लक्षण हैं।
english_translation: The one who holds only true reality in mind, free from restless thought and action, and released from the ego of darkness, these three qualities define the free one.
essence: Freedom is holding only true reality, free from restless mind and ego darkness.
simple_meaning: You are defined by focusing only on true reality, without restless mental activity or ego’s darkness.
insight: It teaches you to rest your mind solely on what is real, dropping all restless efforts and egoic attachments.
modern_relevance: When your mind stops chasing endless worries and self-doubt, you experience true clarity and freedom.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text:
दत्तात्रेयावधूतेन निर्मितानन्दरूपिणा ।
ये पठन्ति च श‍ृण्वन्ति तेषां नैव पुनर्भवः ॥
translation: आनन्द मूर्ति दत्तात्रेय जी अवधूत ने इसका निर्माण किया है जो इसको पढ़ते हैं और सुनते हैं उनका पुनर्जन्म कभी नहीं होता।
english_translation: The blissful Avadhuta Dattatreya created this; those who read or hear it never take rebirth.
essence: Engaging with this teaching ends the cycle of rebirth.
simple_meaning: This text was created by the blissful Avadhuta Dattatreya. Those who read or listen to it will not be reborn again.
insight: It shifts the focus from endless seeking to the power of deep understanding through the text.
speaker: Dattatreya

verse_text: धृतराष्ट्र उवाचधर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः । मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥
translation: धृतराष्ट्र बोले   हे संजय  धर्मभूमि कुरुक्षेत्र में युद्ध की इच्छा से इकट्ठे हुए मेरेे और पाण्डु के पुत्रों ने भी क्या किया ॥
english_translation: Dhritarashtra said: O Sanjaya, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do, assembled on the holy field of Kurukshetra and eager for battle?
essence: The war begins in a question, not a sword strike.
simple_meaning: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what happened when both sides gathered on the battlefield, ready to fight.
insight: It frames the entire Gita as a witness account of a crisis already in motion.
modern_relevance: You sit outside a hospital room, waiting for news after a family conflict has finally exploded. Nothing has been said yet, but everything has already changed.
speaker: Dhritarashtra

verse_text: सञ्जय उवाचदृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा । आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
translation: संजय बोले  उस समय वज्रव्यूहसे खड़ी हुई पाण्डवसेना को देखकर राजा दुर्योधन द्रोणाचार्य के पास जाकर यह वचन बोला ॥
english_translation: Sanjaya said: Seeing the Pandava army arranged in battle formation, King Duryodhana went to Dronacharya and spoke these words.
essence: War becomes real the moment the enemy is seen clearly.
simple_meaning: Duryodhana sees the Pandava army in battle formation and goes to Drona to speak.
insight: It sets up the first crack in Duryodhana’s certainty and moves the scene into open confrontation.
modern_relevance: You spot the other side is ready, organized, and serious. Before you can hide behind confidence, you walk straight to the person who taught you and admit the pressure.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम् । व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता ॥
translation: हे आचार्य आपके बुद्धिमान् शिष्य द्रुपदपुत्र धृष्टद्युम्न के द्वारा व्यूहरचना से खड़ी की हुई पाण्डवों की इस बड़ी भारी सेना को देखिये ॥
english_translation: O teacher, look at this great army of the sons of Pandu, arranged in battle formation by your wise disciple, the son of Drupada.
essence: A battlefield can be won first by how it is described.
simple_meaning: Duryodhana points out the Pandava army to Drona and reminds him that the commander is Drona's own clever student.
insight: It shows how speech can frame a situation to influence another person's response before action begins.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting and someone names the room's strongest rival first. The point is not just information; it is pressure, meant to unsettle the person across the table.
speaker: Duryodhana

verse_text: अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि । युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः ॥
translation: यहाँ पाण्डवों की सेना में बड़ेबड़े शूरवीर हैं, जिनके बहुत बड़ेबड़े धनुष हैं तथा जो युद्ध में भीम और अर्जुनके समान हैं ।  उनमें युयुधान सात्यकि, राजा विराट और महारथी द्रुपद भी हैं ।  धृष्टकेतु और चेकितान तथा पराक्रमी काशिराज भी हैं ।  पुरुजित् और कुन्तिभोजये दोनों भाई तथा मनुष्योंमें श्रेष्ठ शैब्य भी हैं ।  पराक्रमी युधामन्यु और पराक्रमी उत्तमौजा भी हैं ।  सुभद्रापुत्र अभिमन्यु और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र भी हैं ।  ये सबकेसब महारथी हैं ॥
english_translation: Here in the Pandava army are mighty warriors, great archers, equal to Bhima and Arjuna in battle: Satyaki, Virata, and the great chariot-warrior Drupada.
essence: The other side is strong, and pretending otherwise changes nothing.
simple_meaning: Duryodhana points out the Pandava army's strongest warriors and praises their battle skill.
insight: It shifts attention from denial to clear-eyed assessment of what you are facing.
modern_relevance: You walk into a meeting already knowing the other team is stronger, sharper, and better prepared. Naming the challenge clearly is the first step before any real response.
speaker: Duryodhana

verse_text: धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् । पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः ॥
translation: यहाँ पाण्डवों की सेना में बड़ेबड़े शूरवीर हैं, जिनके बहुत बड़ेबड़े धनुष हैं तथा जो युद्ध में भीम और अर्जुनके समान हैं ।  उनमें युयुधान सात्यकि, राजा विराट और महारथी द्रुपद भी हैं ।  धृष्टकेतु और चेकितान तथा पराक्रमी काशिराज भी हैं ।  पुरुजित् और कुन्तिभोजये दोनों भाई तथा मनुष्योंमें श्रेष्ठ शैब्य भी हैं ।  पराक्रमी युधामन्यु और पराक्रमी उत्तमौजा भी हैं ।  सुभद्रापुत्र अभिमन्यु और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र भी हैं ।  ये सबकेसब महारथी हैं ॥
english_translation: Dhृष्टकेतु, Chekitana, and the valiant king of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the best among men.
essence: The battlefield is already full of power and named allies.
simple_meaning: Sanjaya continues listing the mighty warriors in the Pandava army.
insight: It frames the scene as overwhelming reality, not abstract debate.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room knowing the decision ahead will affect everyone there. The names, the faces, the stakes keep piling up before you can even speak.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् । सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः ॥
translation: यहाँ पाण्डवों की सेना में बड़ेबड़े शूरवीर हैं, जिनके बहुत बड़ेबड़े धनुष हैं तथा जो युद्ध में भीम और अर्जुनके समान हैं ।  उनमें युयुधान सात्यकि, राजा विराट और महारथी द्रुपद भी हैं ।  धृष्टकेतु और चेकितान तथा पराक्रमी काशिराज भी हैं ।  पुरुजित् और कुन्तिभोजये दोनों भाई तथा मनुष्योंमें श्रेष्ठ शैब्य भी हैं ।  पराक्रमी युधामन्यु और पराक्रमी उत्तमौजा भी हैं ।  सुभद्रापुत्र अभिमन्यु और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र भी हैं ।  ये सबकेसब महारथी हैं ॥
english_translation: Yudhamanyu, brave and powerful, Uttamaujas, brave and powerful, Subhadra's son, and the sons of Draupadi — all of them are great warriors.
essence: The enemy line is full of elite fighters.
simple_meaning: Duryodhana keeps listing the Pandava side's strongest fighters, showing how formidable Arjuna's army is.
insight: It sharpens the scene by showing the Pandavas are backed by many elite warriors, not just Arjuna.
modern_relevance: You enter a room knowing the other side is stronger than you expected. Before the first word is spoken, the tension already tells you this will be a real fight.
speaker: Duryodhana

verse_text: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम । नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते ॥
translation: हे द्विजोत्तम हमारे पक्ष में भी जो मुख्य हैं, उनपर भी आप ध्यान दीजिये ।  आपको याद दिलाने के लिये मेरी सेना के जो नायक हैं, उनको मैं कहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: O best of the twice-born, note also our own chief warriors. I name them to remind you of our army.
essence: Pride counts its own strength when fear is near.
simple_meaning: Duryodhana tells Drona to notice the main warriors on his own side too. He is naming them so they can be recognised before the battle.
insight: It shows how anxiety hides inside boasting and turns into a need to count allies.
modern_relevance: Before a tense meeting, someone starts reciting names, titles, and achievements to prove the team is strong. The real feeling underneath is fear of being outmatched.
speaker: Duryodhana

verse_text: भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः । अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च ॥
translation: आप द्रोणाचार्य और पितामह भीष्म तथा कर्ण और संग्रामविजयी कृपाचार्य तथा वैसे ही अश्वत्थामा, विकर्ण और सोमदत्त का पुत्र भूरिश्रवा ॥
english_translation: Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and the son of Somadatta are also there.
essence: Fear clings to strength by naming it aloud.
simple_meaning: Duryodhana keeps listing the strongest warriors on his side, naming more of the commanders gathered for battle.
insight: It shows how the mind tries to control uncertainty by assembling names, numbers, and status.
modern_relevance: Before a tense meeting, someone starts reciting credentials, titles, and backup plans just to feel less exposed. The list itself becomes a shield against fear.
speaker: Duryodhana

verse_text: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः । नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः ॥
translation: इनके अतिरिक्त बहुतसे शूरवीर हैं, जिन्होंने मेरे लिये अपने जीने की इच्छा का भी त्याग कर दिया है और जो अनेक प्रकार के शस्त्रअस्त्रों को चलानेवाले हैं तथा जो सबकेसब युद्धकला में अत्यन्त चतुर हैं ॥
english_translation: Besides these, many heroes have given up their lives for my sake. They wield many kinds of weapons and are all skilled in warfare.
essence: Confidence built on numbers still trembles before battle.
simple_meaning: More warriors stand on Duryodhana's side too. They are fearless, heavily armed, and experienced in battle.
insight: It shows how fear can be masked by tallying strength instead of facing reality.
modern_relevance: Before a high-stakes confrontation, someone rattles off every ally, every backup, every advantage, trying to silence doubt with a show of force.
speaker: Duryodhana

verse_text: अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम् । पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम् ॥
translation: वह हमारी सेना पाण्डवों पर विजय करने में अपर्याप्त है, असमर्थ है क्योंकि उसके संरक्षक उभयपक्षपाती भीष्म हैं ।  परन्तु इन पाण्डवों की सेना हमारे पर विजय करने में पर्याप्त है, समर्थ है क्योंकि इसके संरक्षक निजसेनापक्षपाती भीमसेन हैं ॥
english_translation: Our force, guarded by Bhishma, is insufficient; their force, guarded by Bhima, is sufficient.
essence: Fear can declare defeat before the battle starts.
simple_meaning: Duryodhana judges his own army as weaker and the Pandavas' army as stronger, based on who protects each side.
insight: It shows how fear distorts judgment before action begins.
modern_relevance: You walk into a meeting already expecting defeat, and every face seems to confirm it. Fear can make one side look larger before a single word is spoken.
speaker: Duryodhana

verse_text: अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः । भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि ॥
translation: आप सबकेसब लोग सभी मोर्चों पर अपनीअपनी जगह दृढ़ता से स्थित रहते हुए ही पितामह भीष्म की चारों ओर से रक्षा करें ॥
english_translation: Remain at your stations on every front and protect Bhishma from all sides.
essence: Victory begins with disciplined formation, not scattered strength.
simple_meaning: Duryodhana orders all his warriors to hold their positions and guard Bhishma from every side.
insight: It shifts attention from individual impulse to coordinated support around the most vulnerable point.
modern_relevance: Before a tense group presentation, everyone starts drifting into their own panic. One person has to call the room back into formation: stay in your place, cover the weak spot, don't let the center collapse.
speaker: Duryodhana

verse_text: तस्य संजनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः । सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् ॥
translation: दुर्योधन के हृदय में हर्ष उत्पन्न करते हुए कुरुवृद्ध प्रभावशाली पितामह भीष्म ने सिंह के समान गरज कर जोर से शंख बजाया ॥
english_translation: The elder of the Kuru clan, the powerful grandfather Bhishma, roared like a lion and blew his conch loudly, filling Duryodhana with joy.
essence: A single battle cry can turn fear into momentum.
simple_meaning: Bhishma blows his conch loudly, and Duryodhana feels encouraged. It is a battle signal, not a teaching verse.
insight: It sets the scene for war and shows how leadership can stir collective emotion before action begins.
modern_relevance: A room goes silent before the announcement everyone has been dreading. One decisive sound, one firm gesture, and the whole atmosphere changes.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः । सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत् ॥
translation: उसके बाद शंख, भेरी नगाड़े, ढोल, मृदङ्ग और नरसिंघे बाजे एक साथ बज उठे ।  उनका वह शब्द बड़ा भयंकर हुआ ॥
english_translation: Then conches, kettledrums, drums, and trumpets burst forth at once. Their sound became thunderous.
essence: The war announces itself before the first blow.
simple_meaning: Conches, drums, and trumpets all sounded together, and the noise became overwhelming.
insight: It turns the scene from preparation into full confrontation.
modern_relevance: A room goes silent before a hard meeting starts, then every phone buzzes at once. The moment of pressure arrives before a single word is spoken.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ । माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः ॥
translation: उसके बाद सफेद घोड़ों से युक्त महान् रथ पर बैठे हुए लक्ष्मीपति भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण और पाण्डुपुत्र अर्जुन ने दिव्य शंखों को बड़े जोर से बजाया ॥
english_translation: Then, seated on the great chariot yoked with white horses, Madhava and Pandava blew their divine conches.
essence: Resolve answers chaos before words begin.
simple_meaning: Krishna and Arjuna stand together on their great chariot and sound their conches. It marks their answer to the Kaurava war cries.
insight: It shifts attention from noise around you to the steadiness of your own response.
modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with bad news, and everyone around you is already panicking. You take one breath, steady yourself, and answer with clarity instead of fear.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनंजयः । पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ॥
translation: अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण ने पाञ्चजन्य नामक तथा धनञ्जय अर्जुन ने देवदत्त नामक शंख बजाया और भयानक कर्म करनेवाले वृकोदर भीम ने पौण्ड्र नामक महाशंख बजाया ॥
english_translation: Hrisikesha Krishna blew the Panchajanya, Dhananjaya Arjuna blew the Devadatta, and Bhima of mighty deeds blew the great conch Paundra.
essence: The war begins in sound before a single strike.
simple_meaning: Krishna, Arjuna, and Bhima each blew their own conches as the battle began.
insight: It shifts attention from the names and symbols to the irreversible step of commitment.
modern_relevance: The room goes quiet before the hard announcement. Then one clear voice speaks, and everyone knows the moment has crossed into action.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः । नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ॥
translation: कुन्तीपुत्र राजा युधिष्ठिर ने अनन्तविजय नामक शंख बजाया तथा नकुल और सहदेव ने सुघोष और मणिपुष्पक नामक शंख बजाये ॥
english_translation: King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughosha and Manipushpaka.
essence: The war begins to answer back in sound.
simple_meaning: Yudhishthira, Nakula, and Sahadeva blow their conches. The verse adds to the battle scene and names their sacred war horns.
insight: It shifts attention from individual heroes to the full force gathering on one side.
