modern_relevance: The room goes quiet before the announcement. One voice follows another, and everyone feels the pressure rise before a hard beginning.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः । धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ॥
translation: हे राजन् श्रेष्ठ धनुषवाले काशिराज और महारथी शिखण्डी तथा धृष्टद्युम्न एवं राजा विराट और अजेय सात्यकि, राजा द्रुपद और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र तथा लम्बीलम्बी भुजाओंवाले सुभद्रापुत्र अभिमन्यु  इन सभी ने सब ओर से अलगअलग अपनेअपने शंख बजाये ॥
english_translation: The great archer from Kashi, Shikhandi the great warrior, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and invincible Satyaki.
essence: Names and conches turn hesitation into commitment.
simple_meaning: This is a battlefield roll call. More warriors on the Pandava side blow their conches before the war begins.
insight: It shifts attention from strategy to resolve: the side has chosen itself, and action is about to begin.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet before the announcement. One by one, the people who will stand with you are named, and the moment stops being theoretical.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते । सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् ॥
translation: हे राजन् श्रेष्ठ धनुषवाले काशिराज और महारथी शिखण्डी तथा धृष्टद्युम्न एवं राजा विराट और अजेय सात्यकि, राजा द्रुपद और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र तथा लम्बीलम्बी भुजाओंवाले सुभद्रापुत्र अभिमन्यु  इन सभी ने सब ओर से अलगअलग अपनेअपने शंख बजाये ॥
english_translation: Drupada, Draupadi's sons, and mighty Abhimanyu each blew their conches separately, O lord of the earth.
essence: Allied resolve announces itself before the battle starts.
simple_meaning: Drupada, Draupadi's sons, and Abhimanyu each blew their conches. The Pandava side answers the Kaurava side with a full display of strength.
insight: It shifts attention from silent fear to visible resolve before action begins.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet before you speak up against something wrong. Your voice may tremble, but the moment you join in, everyone knows you are not backing down.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् । नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन् ॥
translation: पाण्डवसेना के शंखों के उस भयंकर शब्द ने आकाश और पृथ्वी को भी गुँजाते हुए अन्यायपूर्वक राज्य हड़पनेवाले दुर्योधन आदि के हृदय विदीर्ण कर दिये ॥
english_translation: That terrible sound split the hearts of Dhritarashtra's side, echoing through sky and earth.
essence: A single sound can break resolve before battle begins.
simple_meaning: The loud blast from the Pandava army shook the Kaurava side so deeply that it felt like the sky and earth were trembling too.
insight: It shifts attention from the action itself to its psychological impact on those who resist it.
modern_relevance: You hear the notification, read the message, and know everything has changed before you even reply. Some sounds announce a decision no one can undo.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः । प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसंपाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ॥
translation: हे महीपते धृतराष्ट्र अब शस्त्रों के चलने की तैयारी हो ही रही थी कि उस समय अन्यायपूर्वक राज्य को धारण करनेवाले राजाओं और उनके साथियों को व्यवस्थितरूप से सामने खड़े हुए देखकर कपिध्वज पाण्डुपुत्र अर्जुन ने अपना गाण्डीव धनुष उठा लिया और अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण से ये वचन बोले ॥
english_translation: Then, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra standing in battle order while the weapons were about to begin, Arjuna lifted his bow.
essence: The battle reaches its threshold, and action begins before words do.
simple_meaning: Arjuna sees the opposing army ready for battle and raises his bow.
insight: It shows the threshold before decisive speech or action, when seeing clearly forces a response.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that changes everything. Your hand is on the phone, your chest tight, and you know there is no taking it back.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचहृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे अच्युत दोनों सेनाओं के मध्य में मेरे रथ को आप तब तक खड़ा कीजिये, जब तक मैं युद्धक्षेत्र में खड़े हुए इन युद्ध की इच्छावालों को देख न लूँ कि इस युद्धरूप उद्योग में मुझे किनकिन के साथ युद्ध करना योग्य है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: O Hrishikesha, place my chariot between the two armies, O Achyuta, until I can look at these men who wish to fight and see with whom I must battle in this war.
essence: Clear sight comes before decisive action.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to stop his chariot between the two armies so he can see who he must fight.
insight: It teaches you to pause before irreversible action and face the human reality of what you are about to do.
modern_relevance: You are one step from sending the message, signing the form, or walking away. Before the point of no return, Arjuna’s pause asks for one honest look.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्धुकामानवस्थितान् । कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन्रणसमुद्यमे ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे अच्युत दोनों सेनाओं के मध्य में मेरे रथ को आप तब तक खड़ा कीजिये, जब तक मैं युद्धक्षेत्र में खड़े हुए इन युद्ध की इच्छावालों को देख न लूँ कि इस युद्धरूप उद्योग में मुझे किनकिनके साथ युद्ध करना योग्य है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: O Achyuta, keep my chariot between the two armies until I can inspect these men standing here, eager for battle, and see with whom I must fight in this great struggle.
essence: Clear seeing comes before irreversible action.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to hold the chariot still so he can look at the warriors and understand whom he must face.
insight: It shifts the mind from automatic action to deliberate seeing before commitment.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that will end a friendship, and your hand freezes over the button. Before acting, you need one clear look at what is really in front of you.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः । धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः ॥
translation: दुष्टबुद्धि दुर्योधन का युद्ध में प्रिय करने की इच्छावाले जो ये राजालोग इस सेना में आये हुए हैं, युद्ध करने को उतावले हुए इन सबको मैं देख लूँ ॥
english_translation: I want to see those who have gathered here, eager to fight and wishing to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra.
essence: Conflict becomes real when you look at the people involved.
simple_meaning: Arjuna wants to inspect the warriors gathered on the opposite side, especially those fighting for Duryodhana.
insight: It shifts the mind from abstract conflict to the real human faces inside it.
modern_relevance: You pause before sending the message that will end a friendship. First you read the names again, face the people involved, and feel the weight of what is about to happen.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: संजय उवाचएवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥
translation: संजय बोले  हे भरतवंशी राजन् निद्राविजयी अर्जुन के द्वारा इस तरह कहने पर अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण ने दोनों सेनाओं के मध्यभाग में पितामह भीष्म और आचार्य द्रोण के सामने तथा सम्पूर्ण राजाओं के सामने श्रेष्ठ रथ को खड़ा करके इस तरह कहा कि हे पार्थ इन इकट्ठे हुए कुरुवंशियोंको देख ॥
english_translation: Sanjaya said: Spoken to thus by Gudakesha, Hrishikesha stationed the finest chariot between the two armies, in front of Bhishma, Drona, and all the kings.
essence: The chariot is placed where choice becomes unavoidable.
simple_meaning: Krishna places Arjuna’s chariot between the two armies, right where the decision must happen.
insight: It shifts attention from the setup to the moment of direct confrontation.
modern_relevance: You walk into the meeting, sit between two sides, and everyone waits for your answer. The real pressure begins only when the conflict is no longer abstract.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम् । उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति ॥
translation: संजय बोले  हे भरतवंशी राजन् निद्राविजयी अर्जुन के द्वारा इस तरह कहने पर अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण ने दोनों सेनाओं के मध्यभाग में पितामह भीष्म और आचार्य द्रोण के सामने तथा सम्पूर्ण राजाओं के सामने श्रेष्ठ रथको खड़ा करके इस तरह कहा कि हे पार्थ इन इकट्ठे हुए कुरुवंशियोंको देख ॥
english_translation: Standing before Bhishma, Drona, and all the rulers, Krishna said, "O Partha, behold these assembled Kurus."
essence: Seeing the people involved makes denial impossible.
simple_meaning: Krishna positions Arjuna’s chariot between the armies and asks him to look at the gathered Kurus, including Bhishma, Drona, and the kings.
insight: It shifts the mind from abstract conflict to direct seeing of real people and real stakes.
modern_relevance: You stand at the edge of a hard message, and the people it will hurt are all in front of you. Before you speak or act, you have to look directly.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितृ़नथ पितामहान् । आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातृ़न्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा ॥
translation: उसके बाद पृथानन्दन अर्जुनने उन दोनों ही सेनाओंमें स्थित पिताओंको, पितामहोंको, आचार्योंको, मामाओंको, भाइयोंको, पुत्रोंको, पौत्रोंको तथा मित्रोंको, ससुरोंको और सुहृदोंको भी देखा ॥
english_translation: Then Arjuna, son of Pritha, saw fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, friends, fathers-in-law, and well-wishers standing there.
essence: Recognition turns battle into sorrow.
simple_meaning: Arjuna looks across the battlefield and recognizes his own relatives and teachers among the enemy ranks.
insight: It shifts the mind from strategy to human cost.
modern_relevance: You open a group chat before a painful family decision and see every name tied to memory. The choice is no longer theoretical; it cuts through your own relationships.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि । तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान् ॥
translation: अपनीअपनी जगह पर स्थित उन सम्पूर्ण बान्धवों को देखकर वे कुन्तीनन्दन अर्जुन अत्यन्त कायरता से युक्त होकर विषाद करते हुए ये वचन बोले ॥
english_translation: Seeing all his relatives standing there, Arjuna sank into grief and spoke in fear.
essence: The battle becomes unbearable when every side is family.
simple_meaning: Arjuna sees every kind of relative on both sides of the battlefield and is overwhelmed with grief.
insight: It turns a distant conflict into a personal wound, making action emotionally impossible.
modern_relevance: You open a family group chat and realize the conflict has names and faces. The issue is no longer abstract, and your stomach drops.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचकृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे कृष्ण युद्ध की इच्छावाले इस कुटुम्बसमुदाय को अपने सामने उपस्थित देखकर मेरे अङ्ग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुख सूख रहा है तथा मेरे शरीर में कँपकँपी आ रही है एवं रोंगटे खड़े हो रहे हैं ।  हाथ से गाण्डीव धनुष गिर रहा है और त्वचा भी जल रही है ।  मेरा मन भ्रमितसा हो रहा है और मैं खड़े रहने में भी असमर्थ हो रहा हूँ ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: Seeing my own people gathered here, eager for battle, I am overcome with pity and grief, O Krishna.
essence: Compassion can stop the warrior before the first arrow flies.
simple_meaning: Arjuna tells Krishna that seeing his own relatives gathered for battle has overwhelmed him with grief and pity.
insight: It shifts the reader from abstract conflict to the human cost hidden inside it.
modern_relevance: You open a message thread and realize the argument will wound people you love. Your body tightens before your mind can defend the choice.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे कृष्ण युद्ध की इच्छावाले इस कुटुम्बसमुदाय को अपने सामने उपस्थित देखकर मेरे अङ्ग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुख सूख रहा है तथा मेरे शरीर में कँपकँपी आ रही है एवं रोंगटे खड़े हो रहे हैं ।  हाथ से गाण्डीव धनुष गिर रहा है और त्वचा भी जल रही है ।  मेरा मन भ्रमितसा हो रहा है और मैं खड़े रहने में भी असमर्थ हो रहा हूँ ॥
english_translation: My limbs are failing, my mouth is drying up, my body trembles, and my hair stands on end.
essence: The body reveals fear before the mind can explain it.
simple_meaning: Arjuna's body is breaking under the pressure of what he sees. His strength, speech, and composure are all slipping away at once.
insight: It teaches you to notice distress as a physical signal, not just a mental opinion.
modern_relevance: You open the message you were dreading, and your hands go cold before you even reply. The body often knows the cost of a hard truth first.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे कृष्ण युद्ध की इच्छावाले इस कुटुम्बसमुदाय को अपने सामने उपस्थित देखकर मेरे अङ्ग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुख सूख रहा है तथा मेरे शरीर में कँपकँपी आ रही है एवं रोंगटे खड़े हो रहे हैं ।  हाथ से गाण्डीव धनुष गिर रहा है और त्वचा भी जल रही है ।  मेरा मन भ्रमितसा हो रहा है और मैं खड़े रहने में भी असमर्थ हो रहा हूँ ॥
english_translation: My bow slips from my hand. My skin burns. I cannot stand steady, and my mind reels.
essence: Fear strips away control before a single arrow is released.
simple_meaning: Arjuna is overwhelmed by fear and grief. His body shakes, his bow slips, and he cannot steady his mind or even stand.
insight: It shows how inner collapse first appears as bodily instability, not just thought.
modern_relevance: You are about to speak in a meeting, but your throat tightens and your hands shake. The body knows before the mind admits it: this is too much right now.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव । न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ॥
translation: हे केशव मैं लक्षणों  शकुनों को भी विपरीत देख रहा हूँ और युद्ध में स्वजनोंको मारकर श्रेय लाभ भी नहीं देख रहा हूँ ॥
english_translation: O Keshava, I see only inauspicious signs, and I see no good in killing my own people in battle.
essence: A victory that destroys your own people is not worth having.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says he sees bad signs and no real good in killing his own relatives in battle.
insight: It shifts attention from winning to the moral cost of winning.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that will end a friendship, and every detail feels wrong. The mind keeps warning: forcing this will not make life better.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च । किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ॥
translation: हे कृष्ण मैं न तो विजय चाहता हूँ, न राज्य चाहता हूँ और न सुखों को ही चाहता हूँ ।  हे गोविन्द हमलोगों को राज्य से क्या लाभ भोगों से क्या लाभ अथवा जीने से भी क्या लाभ ॥
english_translation: I do not desire victory, Krishna, nor kingdom, nor pleasures. What use is kingdom to us, Govinda? What use are pleasures or even life?
essence: Victory means nothing when the price is the destruction of what you love.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says he no longer wants victory, a kingdom, pleasure, or even life itself. The fight has lost its meaning for him.
insight: It exposes the moment when outer success can no longer justify inner collapse.
modern_relevance: You are staring at the email that could save your career, but it asks you to betray yourself. Suddenly the promotion, the applause, even the job feel empty.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च । त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ॥
translation: जिनके लिये हमारी राज्य, भोग और सुखकी इच्छा है, वे ही ये सब अपने प्राणों की और धन की आशा का त्याग करके युद्ध में खड़े हैं ॥
english_translation: Those for whom we wanted kingdom, pleasures, and comfort stand here in battle, ready to give up life and wealth.
essence: The prize is empty when the people attached to it stand in the line of fire.
simple_meaning: The people Arjuna hoped to protect and enjoy life with are standing on the battlefield, willing to risk everything. That makes his refusal to fight even heavier.
insight: It turns the battle from a political contest into a personal wound, making action feel unbearable.
modern_relevance: You open a family group chat and see the people you love lined up on opposite sides of a painful inheritance dispute. The choice is no longer abstract; every option cuts into someone familiar.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः । मातुलाः श्चशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा ॥
translation: आचार्य, पिता, पुत्र और उसी प्रकार पितामह, मामा, ससुर, पौत्र, साले तथा अन्य जितने भी सम्बन्धी हैं, मुझ पर प्रहार करने पर भी मैं इनको मारना नहीं चाहता, और हे मधुसूदन मुझे त्रिलोकी का राज्य मिलता हो, तो भी मैं इनको मारना नहीं चाहता, फिर पृथ्वी के लिये तो मैं इनको मारूँ ही क्या ॥
english_translation: Teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other relatives.
essence: Blood ties make victory feel like loss.
simple_meaning: Arjuna lists the family members and relatives on both sides of the battlefield. He is overwhelmed because the people he would have to fight are his own kin.
insight: It shifts the mind from winning a conflict to facing the human cost of victory.
modern_relevance: You open a message thread and realize the argument is no longer about the issue. It is about people you love, and hurting them now feels impossible.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन । अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ॥
translation: आचार्य, पिता, पुत्र और उसी प्रकार पितामह, मामा, ससुर, पौत्र, साले तथा अन्य जितने भी सम्बन्धी हैं, मुझपर प्रहार करने पर भी मैं इनको मारना नहीं चाहता, और हे मधुसूदन मुझे त्रिलोकी का राज्य मिलता हो, तो भी मैं इनको मारना नहीं चाहता, फिर पृथ्वीके लिये तो मैं इनको मारूँ ही क्या ॥
english_translation: I do not want to kill these people, even if they kill me, O Madhusudana. Not even for the rule of the three worlds, much less for the earth.
essence: No prize can justify killing what is sacred to you.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says he cannot bring himself to kill his own relatives, even for power over all three worlds, let alone for a kingdom on earth.
insight: It shifts the mind from winning at any cost to measuring the moral cost of victory.
modern_relevance: You are one signature away from harming a family member's future, and the reward is huge. Something in you knows the price is too high.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन । पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः ॥
translation: हे जनार्दन इन धृतराष्ट्रसम्बन्धियों को मारकर हमलोगों को क्या प्रसन्नता होगी इन आततायियों को मारने से तो हमें पाप ही लगेगा ॥
english_translation: O Janardana, what joy would come to us by killing these sons of Dhritarashtra? Killing these aggressors would only bring us sin.
essence: Violence against kin brings no joy; it only deepens the wound.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says that killing his own relatives will bring no happiness and will only stain the killers with wrongdoing.
insight: It shifts the mind from triumph to moral consequence before taking irreversible action.
modern_relevance: You are about to expose a lie that will break a family dinner open. The room goes silent, and you realize winning the argument would cost something deeper than being right.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान् । स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥
translation: इसलिये अपने बान्धव इन धृतराष्ट्रसम्बन्धियों को मारने के लिये हम योग्य नहीं हैं क्योंकि हे माधव अपने कुटुम्बियों को मारकर हम कैसे सुखी होंगे ॥
english_translation: Therefore, we are not fit to kill our own kinsmen, the sons of Dhritarashtra. How could we be happy after killing our relatives, O Madhava?
essence: Kinship makes violence feel unbearable.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says the Kaurava side are his own relatives, so killing them would not bring happiness.
insight: It shifts the mind from winning to seeing the human cost of action.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that will end a friendship. Before you hit send, you feel the weight of what cannot be undone.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः । कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् ॥
translation: यद्यपि लोभ के कारण जिनका विवेकविचार लुप्त हो गया है, ऐसे ये दुर्योधन आदि कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को और मित्रों के साथ द्वेष करने से होनेवाले पाप को नहीं देखते, तो भी हे जनार्दन कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को ठीकठीक जाननेवाले हमलोग इस पाप से निवृत्त होने का विचार क्यों न करें ॥
english_translation: Though greed has blinded them, they do not see the fault in destroying a family or the wrong in betraying friends.
essence: Greed blinds people to the damage they are causing.
simple_meaning: Greed has made these people blind. They cannot see the harm in destroying their own family or betraying friends.
insight: It shifts attention from winning the argument to seeing the moral cost of greed-driven action.
modern_relevance: You’re in a family meeting where money has turned relatives against each other. Everyone speaks loudly, but no one sees the damage being done until it is too late.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम् । कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन ॥
translation: यद्यपि लोभ के कारण जिनका विवेकविचार लुप्त हो गया है, ऐसे ये दुर्योधन आदि कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को और मित्रों के साथ द्वेष करने से होनेवाले पाप को नहीं देखते, तो भी हे जनार्दन कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को ठीकठीक जाननेवाले हमलोग इस पाप से निवृत्त होनेका विचार क्यों न करें ॥
english_translation: Why should we not turn away from this sin, when we clearly see the fault in destroying the family, O Janardana?
essence: Clear sight makes withdrawal from harm the only sane choice.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says that because he can see the harm caused by destroying the family, he and his side should turn away from this wrong action.
insight: It shifts the mind from winning to refusing harm once the cost is understood.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that will break a family apart. The facts are clear, and so is the damage. This verse is the moment you ask whether continuing is worth becoming the person who did it.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः । धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत ॥
translation: कुल का क्षय होने पर सदा से चलते आये कुलधर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं और धर्म का नाश होनेपर बचे हुए सम्पूर्ण कुल को अधर्म दबा लेता है ॥
english_translation: When a family falls apart, its ancient duties disappear. When duty is lost, wrongdoing overtakes the whole family.
essence: Destroy the family, and the moral order inside it collapses.
simple_meaning: When a family is broken, its long-standing duties disappear. Once duty is gone, wrongdoing spreads through the whole family.
insight: It shifts attention from immediate victory to the long-term moral cost of breaking inherited obligations.
modern_relevance: A household where promises keep getting broken does not stay stable for long. Soon the children learn the chaos as normal, and everyone starts living by damage control instead of responsibility.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः । स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः ॥
translation: हे कृष्ण अधर्म के अधिक बढ़ जाने से कुल की स्त्रियाँ दूषित हो जाती हैं और हे वार्ष्णेय स्त्रियों के दूषित होने पर वर्णसंकर पैदा हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: When lawlessness grows, the women of the family are corrupted. When women are corrupted, mixed social disorder is born.
essence: When order breaks, the damage spreads into future generations.
simple_meaning: Arjuna fears that when lawlessness takes over a family, women are harmed and social order breaks down further.
insight: It shifts attention from personal victory to the wider social cost of destructive action.
modern_relevance: A family argument turns ugly, and suddenly everyone is carrying the damage. One harsh decision can echo into children, trust, and the whole home.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च । पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः ॥
translation: वर्णसंकर कुलघातियों को और कुल को नरक में ले जानेवाला ही होता है ।  श्राद्ध और तर्पण न मिलने से इन कुलघातियों के पितर भी अपने स्थान से गिर जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Mixed lineage leads the destroyers of family to ruin, and their ancestors fall because offerings of food and water stop.
essence: Breaking family order is imagined as ruin that reaches even the dead.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says that destroying family order creates ruin for the family and even harms the ancestors, because the rites that support them stop.
insight: It shows how moral panic turns consequences into a chain of fear, making action feel spiritually catastrophic.
modern_relevance: You are about to cut off a relationship, and the mind races ahead to every harm it might cause. In that panic, one decision starts to feel like it will damage an entire family line.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः । उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः ॥
translation: इन वर्णसंकर पैदा करनेवाले दोषोंसे कुलघातियों के सदा से चलते आये कुलधर्म और जातिधर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Because of these faults that create mixed social order, the eternal duties of family and community are destroyed.
essence: When conduct breaks, the inherited order that protects everyone breaks too.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says that when family lines break down, long-standing duties within the family and society are destroyed.
insight: It shifts attention from one wrong act to the wider damage it can do to shared responsibility.
modern_relevance: A household that normalises cruelty or secrecy does not stay contained. The habits spread, and soon even the basic rules that kept everyone steady start disappearing.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन । नरकेऽनियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम ॥
translation: हे जनार्दन जिनके कुलधर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं, उन मनुष्यों का बहुत काल तक नरकों में वापस होता है, ऐसा हम सुनते आये हैं ॥
english_translation: O Janardana, we have always heard that those whose family duties are destroyed dwell long in a lower realm.
essence: Breaking family duty brings suffering that lasts beyond one lifetime.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says he has heard that people who destroy family duties end up suffering for a long time in a lower realm.
insight: It shifts the mind from immediate gain to the long shadow of broken obligations.
modern_relevance: You are about to sign something that will hurt your own family later. The short-term win looks smaller when you can already see the damage spreading.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम् । यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः ॥
translation: यह बड़े आश्चर्य और खेद की बात है कि हमलोग बड़ा भारी पाप करने का निश्चय कर बैठे हैं, जो कि राज्य और सुख के लोभ से अपने स्वजनों को मारने के लिये तैयार हो गये हैं ॥
english_translation: Alas, we have resolved to commit a grave wrong—driven by greed for kingdom and pleasure, we are ready to kill our own kin.
essence: Greed can make even victory feel like a crime.
simple_meaning: Arjuna sees the war as a terrible wrong. He feels they are driven by greed for power and pleasure, and ready to kill their own relatives.
insight: It shifts the mind from winning at any cost to noticing the moral price of winning.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that will break a family apart, and you can feel the wrongness before your finger moves. That hesitation is not weakness.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः । धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ॥
translation: अगर ये हाथों में शस्त्रअस्त्र लिये हुए धृतराष्ट्र के पक्षपाती लोग युद्धभूमि में सामना न करनेवाले तथा शस्त्ररहित मुझ को मार भी दें, तो वह मेरे लिये बड़ा ही हितकारक होगा ॥
english_translation: If the armed sons of Dhritarashtra were to kill me in battle while I stood unresisting and without weapons, that would be far better for me.
essence: Harming loved ones feels worse than losing your own life.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says that even dying unarmed in battle would be better than fighting his own relatives.
insight: It shifts the mind from winning at any cost to seeing the cost of violence itself.
modern_relevance: You are standing in a doorway, keys in hand, about to leave a relationship or job that once felt safe. Part of you would rather be hurt than become the one who causes harm.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् । विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥
translation: संजय बोले  ऐसा कहकर शोकाकुल मनवाले अर्जुन बाणसहित धनुष का त्याग करके युद्धभूमि में रथके मध्यभाग में बैठ गये ॥
english_translation: Sanjaya said: Saying this, Arjuna sat down on the chariot seat in the midst of the battlefield, casting aside his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief.
essence: Grief can make even a warrior lay down his weapons.
simple_meaning: Arjuna gives up his bow and sits down in the chariot, overwhelmed by grief.
insight: It shows the exact moment paralysis takes over, before Krishna begins to answer it.
modern_relevance: You open the message, stare at it, and set the phone down. The decision is still there, but your hands have gone still because the weight of it has landed.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: सञ्जय उवाचतं तथा कृपयाऽविष्टमश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम् । विषीदन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः ॥
translation: संजय बोले  वैसी कायरता से आविष्ट उन अर्जुन के प्रति, जो कि विषाद कर रहे हैं और आँसुओं के कारण जिनके नेत्रों की देखने की शक्ति अवरुद्ध हो रही है, भगवान् मधुसूदन ये आगे कहे जानेवाले वचन बोले ॥
english_translation: Sanjaya said: To Arjuna, overcome by pity, his eyes full of tears and clouded with grief, Madhusudana spoke these words.
essence: Grief opens the door for instruction.
simple_meaning: Sanjaya describes Arjuna in tears and grief as Krishna begins to speak to him.
insight: It frames the teaching as a response to collapse, not abstract theory.
modern_relevance: You sit in your car after a brutal phone call, unable to start the engine. Before any advice can help, the mind first has to be seen in its breaking point.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचकुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् । अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले   हे अर्जुन इस विषम अवसरपर तुम्हें यह कायरता कहाँसे प्राप्त हुई, जिसका कि श्रेष्ठ पुरुष सेवन नहीं करते, जो स्वर्गको देनेवाली नहीं है और कीर्ति करनेवाली भी नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Krishna said: Arjuna, where has this delusion come from in this crisis? Noble people do not follow it. It does not lead upward, and it brings disgrace.
essence: Delusion has no place in a decisive moment.
simple_meaning: Arjuna's collapse is called out as misplaced weakness. It is not the response of a noble person, and it only lowers him.
insight: It teaches you to interrupt panic before it becomes your identity.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that changes everything, and your hand freezes above the screen. The mind calls it caution; Krishna calls it collapse.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते । क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन अर्जुन  इस नपुंसकताको मत प्राप्त हो क्योंकि तुम्हारेमें यह उचित नहीं है ।  हे परंतप  हृदयकी इस तुच्छ दुर्बलताका त्याग करके युद्धके लिये खड़े हो जाओ ॥
english_translation: Do not yield to weakness, Partha. It does not suit you. Cast off this petty weakness of heart and rise, scorcher of foes.
essence: Weakness is optional; the call to act remains.
simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna not to sink into weakness. He must drop this small-hearted fear and stand up to fight.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-doubt to immediate responsibility.
modern_relevance: You are halfway through a hard conversation, your voice starts shaking, and you want to back out. This verse says the collapse is temporary — stand back up and finish what must be done.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचकथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन । इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे मधुसूदन मैं रणभूमिमें भीष्म और द्रोणके साथ बाणोंसे युद्ध कैसे करूँ क्योंकि हे अरिसूदन ये दोनों ही पूजाके योग्य हैं ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: How can I fight Bhishma and Drona with arrows in battle, O Madhusudana? They are worthy of worship, O destroyer of enemies.
essence: Respect can make necessary action feel unbearable.
simple_meaning: Arjuna cannot imagine fighting his own respected teachers and elders. His hesitation is not tactical; it is moral and emotional.
insight: It names the paralysis that comes when duty collides with reverence.
modern_relevance: You have to speak against a mentor who shaped you. Your hand freezes because the person in front of you is not just wrong — they are beloved.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान्श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके । हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैवभुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥
translation: महानुभाव गुरुजनोंको न मारकर इस लोकमें मैं भिक्षाका अन्न खाना भी श्रेष्ठ समझता हूँ ।  क्योंकि गुरुजनोंको मारकर यहाँ रक्तसे सने हुए तथा धनकी कामनाकी मुख्यतावाले भोगोंको ही तो भोगूँगा ॥
english_translation: It is better to live on alms in this world than to kill these great teachers. If I kill them, the pleasures I enjoy here will be stained with blood and bound to greed.
essence: A victory that destroys reverence is already a loss.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says it would be better to live on alms than kill his respected teachers. He sees any victory gained that way as tainted by blood and greed.
insight: It shifts the question from can I win to can I live with the cost.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that will end a friendship, or take the promotion that depends on someone else being pushed out. The win feels dirty before you even touch it.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयोयद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः । यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥
translation: हम यह भी नहीं जानते कि हमलोगोंके लिये युद्ध करना और न करना  इन दोनोंमेंसे कौनसा अत्यन्त श्रेष्ठ है और हमें इसका भी पता नहीं है कि हम उन्हें जीतेंगे अथवा वे हमें जीतेंगे ।  जिनको मारकर हम जीना भी नहीं चाहते, वे ही धृतराष्ट्रके सम्बन्धी हमारे सामने खड़े हैं ॥
english_translation: We do not know which is better for us: to fight or not to fight. We do not even know whether we will conquer them or they us. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us, and we do not wish to live after killing them.
essence: Honest uncertainty is the first crack in moral paralysis.
simple_meaning: Arjuna admits complete uncertainty. He cannot tell whether fighting or not fighting is the better choice, and he cannot bear the thought of killing relatives who stand before him.
insight: It shifts the mind from false certainty to honest doubt, making room for guidance instead of panic.
modern_relevance: You are holding your phone after a message that could end a relationship, and your thumb freezes. One choice may hurt either way, and you finally admit you cannot sort it alone.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्िचतं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥
translation: कायरतारूपदोषसे तिरस्कृत स्वभाववाला और धर्मके विषयमें मोहित अन्तःकरणवाला मैं आपसे पूछता हूँ कि जो निश्चित कल्याण करनेवाली हो, वह मेरे लिये कहिये ।  मैं आपका शिष्य हूँ ।  आपके शरण हुए मुझे शिक्षा दीजिये ॥
english_translation: My nature is overwhelmed by weakness, and my mind is confused about duty. I ask you: tell me with certainty what is best for me. I am your student; instruct me, for I have taken refuge in you.
essence: Clarity begins when you admit you cannot see the right action alone.
simple_meaning: Arjuna admits he is overwhelmed and confused about what is truly right. He asks Krishna to clearly tell him the best course, as a student seeking guidance.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliant confusion to disciplined seeking of guidance.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a message you do not want to send, knowing it will change everything. Instead of forcing confidence, you finally admit: I need the clearest counsel I can find.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
translation: पृथ्वीपर धनधान्यसमृद्ध और शत्रुरहितराज्य तथा स्वर्गमें देवताओंका आधिपत्य मिल जाय तो भी इन्द्रियोंको सुखानेवाला मेरा जो शोक है, वह दूर हो जाय  ऐसा मैं नहीं देखता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Even if I gained an unrivaled, prosperous kingdom on earth or lordship over the gods, I see nothing that could remove this grief that dries up my senses.
essence: No outer victory can cure an inner collapse.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says that even the greatest possible power and wealth would not remove his grief. His mind is so overwhelmed that nothing outside can fix it.
insight: It shifts attention from external gains to the inner wound that must be faced directly.
modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the apartment, the applause — and still feel hollow on the ride home. Some pain is too deep to be solved by winning more.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप । न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥
translation: संजय बोले  हे शत्रुतापन धृतराष्ट्र ऐसा कहकर निद्राको जीतनेवाले अर्जुन अन्तर्यामी भगवान् गोविन्दसे मैं युद्ध नहीं करूँगा ऐसा साफसाफ कहकर चुप हो गये ॥
english_translation: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha, Gudakesha, the scorcher of foes, said to Govinda, “I will not fight,” and fell silent.
essence: Refusal has stopped the war inside him.
simple_meaning: Arjuna tells Krishna he will not fight, then falls silent. The argument pauses in complete refusal.
insight: It marks the collapse of will before Krishna begins to answer it.
modern_relevance: You finally say the thing you’ve been avoiding: “I can’t do this.” Then the room goes quiet, and everyone feels the weight of your choice.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशोद्भव धृतराष्ट्र दोनों सेनाओंके मध्यभागमें विषाद करते हुए उस अर्जुनके प्रति हँसते हुएसे भगवान् हृषीकेश यह आगे कहे जानेवाले वचन बोले ॥
english_translation: Hṛṣīkeśa spoke to the grieving Arjuna, smiling slightly, in the midst of the two armies.
essence: Guidance begins when grief is met without rejection.
simple_meaning: Krishna begins speaking to Arjuna, who is overwhelmed with grief between the two armies.
insight: It shifts the mind from emotional paralysis to receiving guidance.
modern_relevance: You are frozen in the middle of a hard decision, and everything in you wants to shut down. The first real help often arrives not as pressure, but as a steady voice that can hold your fear.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचअशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे । गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  तुमने शोक न करनेयोग्यका शोक किया है और पण्डिताईकी बातें कह रहे हो परन्तु जिनके प्राण चले गये हैं, उनके लिये और जिनके प्राण नहीं गये हैं, उनके लिये पण्डितलोग शोक नहीं करते ॥
english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: You grieve for what should not be grieved for, yet speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the dead or the living.
essence: Clear seeing ends grief where the wise know none is needed.
simple_meaning: Arjuna is mourning people who should not be mourned, while speaking as if he understands wisdom. Krishna says the wise do not grieve for either the dead or the living.
insight: It shifts the mind from emotional confusion to clear discrimination about what truly deserves grief.
modern_relevance: You stand beside a hospital bed, rehearsing the perfect words while your chest tightens. The mind reaches for philosophy, but the heart is still caught in fear and loss.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः । न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥
translation: किसी कालमें मैं नहीं था और तू नहीं था तथा ये राजालोग नहीं थे, यह बात भी नहीं है और इसके बाद भविष्य में मैं, तू और राजलोग  हम सभी नहीं रहेंगे, यह बात भी नहीं है ॥
english_translation: I was never absent, nor were you, nor these kings. Nor will any of us cease to be in the future.
essence: What truly exists was never born and never lost.
simple_meaning: Krishna says that he, Arjuna, and the kings have always existed in some form, and none of them will simply vanish after death.
insight: It shifts attention from the body’s ending to the continuity of the true self.
modern_relevance: You are standing at a hospital bed, hearing that a loved one may not recover. Panic narrows everything to the body in front of you. This verse opens a larger horizon.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा । तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥
translation: देहधारीके इस मनुष्यशरीरमें जैसे बालकपन, जवानी और वृद्धावस्था होती है, ऐसे ही देहान्तरकी प्राप्ति होती है ।  उस विषयमें धीर मनुष्य मोहित नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: Just as the embodied one passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too it passes into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
essence: What changes form is not what you truly are.
simple_meaning: The body changes through stages, and the one living in it moves on to another body. A steady person does not get confused by this.
insight: It shifts attention from the body’s changing stages to the steady awareness that outlives them.
modern_relevance: You watch an old photo and barely recognise yourself. The face, voice, and fears have changed — yet something in you has kept witnessing all of it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः । आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥
translation: हे कुन्तीनन्दन इन्द्रियोंके जो विषय जड पदार्थ हैं, वो तो शीत अनुकूलता और उष्ण प्रतिकूलता  के द्वारा सुख और दुःख देनेवाले हैं तथा आनेजानेवाले और अनित्य हैं ।  हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन उनको तुम सहन करो ॥
english_translation: Contacts with the senses, O son of Kunti, bring heat and cold, pleasure and pain. They come and go; they are impermanent. Endure them, O Bharata.
essence: Passing sensations lose power when you stop treating them as permanent.
simple_meaning: Pleasure and pain from the senses are temporary. They come and go, so you should learn to bear them without being shaken.
insight: It trains you to notice discomfort without obeying it, so reaction does not become action.
modern_relevance: You get a sharp message, feel your stomach drop, and want to react instantly. The feeling is real, but it does not deserve the steering wheel.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ । समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
translation: कारण कि हे पुरुषोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन सुखदुःखमें सम रहनेवाले जिस धीर मनुष्यको ये मात्रास्पर्श पदार्थ व्यथित सुखीदुःखी नहीं कर पाते, वह अमर होनेमें समर्थ हो जाता है अर्थात् वह अमर हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: The wise person who is not shaken by these, and remains equal in pain and pleasure, becomes fit for freedom.
essence: Freedom begins where pain and pleasure stop controlling you.
simple_meaning: A steady person who stays even through pleasure and pain is not thrown off by changing experiences and becomes ready for inner freedom.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing comfort and avoiding pain to holding both with equal steadiness.
modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with bad news, then a compliment, then another crisis. The mind jerks in every direction. This verse asks for a steadier center that does not collapse with each swing.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः । उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
translation: टिप्पणी प0 55 असत् का तो भाव सत्ता विद्यमान नहीं है और सत् का अभाव विद्यमान नहीं है, तत्त्वदर्शी महापुरुषोंने इन दोनोंका ही अन्त अर्थात् तत्त्व देखा है ॥
english_translation: The unreal has no being; the real has no nonbeing. Seers have understood the boundary of both.
essence: What passes away was never ultimate; what is real cannot vanish.
simple_meaning: What is temporary does not truly exist, and what is real cannot be destroyed. Those who see clearly understand the difference between the two.
insight: It shifts attention from appearances to what remains unchanged beneath them.
modern_relevance: You reread a message that stung, then imagine the whole relationship collapsing. Krishna’s point cuts through that spiral: not every passing state deserves the weight you give it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित् कर्तुमर्हति ॥
translation: अविनाशी तो उसको जान, जिससे यह सम्पूर्ण संसार व्याप्त है ।  इस अविनाशीका विनाश कोई भी नहीं कर सकता ॥
english_translation: Know that to be imperishable by which this entire world is pervaded. No one can destroy this imperishable reality.
essence: What truly pervades everything cannot be destroyed.
simple_meaning: Know that the reality behind everything is imperishable. No force can destroy what pervades the whole world.
insight: It shifts attention from what changes to what remains untouched beneath change.
modern_relevance: A diagnosis, a breakup, a public failure — everything seems to collapse at once. This verse reminds you that the deepest reality in you is not fragile, even when your situation is.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः । अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत ॥
translation: अविनाशी, अप्रमेय और नित्य रहनेवाले इस शरीरी के ये देह अन्तवाले कहे गये हैं ।  इसलिये हे अर्जुन तुम युद्ध करो ॥
english_translation: These bodies are said to be finite, but the embodied being is eternal, indestructible, and immeasurable. Therefore, fight, Arjuna.
essence: What is truly you cannot be destroyed, so duty remains.
simple_meaning: Bodies are temporary, but the inner being is eternal and cannot be measured or destroyed. Arjuna is told to fight because of that truth.
insight: It shifts the mind from bodily loss to rightful action.
modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, about to make a hard decision for someone you love. The body can change, weaken, and end, but your duty does not vanish with your fear.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् । उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य इस अविनाशी शरीरीको मारनेवाला मानता है और जो मनुष्य इसको मरा मानता है, वे दोनों ही इसको नहीं जानते क्योंकि यह न मारता है और न मारा जाता है ॥
english_translation: Whoever thinks this imperishable being is the killer, and whoever thinks it is killed, both do not understand. It neither kills nor is killed.
essence: What you are cannot be reduced to killer or victim.
simple_meaning: The true self cannot be killed, and it does not kill. Seeing it as either one is ignorance.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal guilt and fear to clear seeing of what can and cannot be harmed.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that ends a friendship, or walk away from a role that once defined you. The mind says, 'I am ruining everything.' This verse says the deepest part of you is untouched by such labels.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः । अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणोन हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥
translation: यह शरीरी न कभी जन्मता है और न मरता है तथा यह उत्पन्न होकर फिर होनेवाला नहीं है ।  यह जन्मरहित, नित्यनिरन्तर रहनेवाला, शाश्वत और पुराण अनादि है ।  शरीरके मारे जानेपर भी यह नहीं मारा जाता ॥
english_translation: It is never born and never dies. It did not come into being, and it will not cease. Unborn, eternal, everlasting, ancient, it is not destroyed when the body is destroyed.
essence: What you are cannot be touched by birth or death.
simple_meaning: The true self is never born and never dies. It does not begin with the body, and it is not destroyed when the body ends.
insight: It shifts attention from bodily loss to the unbroken reality that witnesses change.
modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed or a graveside and feel everything collapsing. This verse asks you to see that the person you love, and the deepest part of yourself, are not limited to the body alone.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम् । कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम् ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन जो मनुष्य इस शरीरीको अविनाशी, नित्य, जन्मरहित और अव्यय जानता है, वह कैसे किसको मारे और कैसे किसको मरवाये ॥
english_translation: One who knows the imperishable, eternal, unborn, and unchanging cannot think of killing or causing death.
essence: Clear seeing makes violence look absurd.
simple_meaning: Anyone who truly sees the inner being as unborn and unchanging cannot think in terms of killing or being killed.
insight: It shifts the mind from physical appearance to what remains unchanged beneath change.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that ends a relationship, or stay silent and let harm continue. This verse asks you to see deeper than the body of the moment and act from clear seeing, not panic.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहायनवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि । तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥
translation: मनुष्य जैसे पुराने कपड़ोंको छोड़कर दूसरे नये कपड़े धारण कर लेता है, ऐसे ही देही पुराने शरीरोंको छोड़कर दूसरे नये शरीरोंमें चला जाता है ॥
english_translation: As a person discards worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the embodied being discards worn-out bodies and enters new ones.
essence: What you are does not end when one body is left behind.
simple_meaning: The true self passes from one body to another the way a person changes clothes.
insight: It shifts attention from identifying with the body to seeing the body as a temporary covering.
modern_relevance: Standing beside a hospital bed, you watch a loved one weaken and feel helpless. This image does not erase grief, but it reminds you that change touches the body, not the deepest reality.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः । न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥
translation: शस्त्र इस शरीरीको काट नहीं सकते, अग्नि इसको जला नहीं सकती, जल इसको गीला नहीं कर सकता और वायु इसको सुखा नहीं सकती ॥
english_translation: Weapons cannot cut it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, and wind cannot dry it.
essence: Your deepest reality is beyond every physical force.
simple_meaning: The true self cannot be harmed by weapons, fire, water, or wind. It is beyond physical destruction.
insight: It shifts attention from protecting the body to recognising the untouched witness within.
modern_relevance: You read the message that changes everything after a breakup, a diagnosis, or a dismissal. The body may be shaken, but the deepest part of you is not at the mercy of events.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च । नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥
translation: यह शरीरी काटा नहीं जा सकता, यह जलाया नहीं जा सकता, यह गीला नहीं किया जा सकता और यह सुखाया भी नहीं जा सकता ।  कारण कि यह नित्य रहनेवाला सबमें परिपूर्ण, अचल, स्थिर स्वभाववाला और अनादि है ॥
english_translation: This embodied self cannot be cut, burned, wetted, or dried. It is eternal, all-pervading, unmoving, fixed, and timeless.
essence: What you are cannot be harmed by anything that changes.
simple_meaning: The true self cannot be destroyed by any physical force. It is permanent, present everywhere, unmoving, and beyond time.
insight: It shifts attention from the body’s vulnerability to the true self’s permanence.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a medical report, a breakup message, or a sudden layoff notice. Everything feels fragile. This verse reminds you that the deepest part of you is not made of what can be broken.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते । तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि ॥
translation: यह देही प्रत्यक्ष नहीं दीखता, यह चिन्तनका विषय नहीं है और यह निर्विकार कहा जाता है ।  अतः इस देहीको ऐसा जानकर शोक नहीं करना चाहिये ॥
english_translation: It is unseen, beyond thought, and said to be unchanged. Therefore, knowing it this way, you should not grieve.
essence: What is deepest in you was never available for loss.
simple_meaning: The true self is not something you can see, think through, or alter. Knowing that, Arjuna should stop grieving.
insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with what changes to resting in what does not.
modern_relevance: You reread the message three times after the breakup, trying to make the loss feel logical. Some things cannot be held, explained, or broken in the first place.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् । तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
translation: हे महाबाहो  अगर तुम इस देहीको नित्य पैदा होनेवाला अथवा नित्य मरनेवाला भी मानो, तो भी तुम्हें इस प्रकार शोक नहीं करना चाहिये ॥
english_translation: O mighty-armed one, even if you think this embodied being is always born and always dies, you still should not grieve like this.
essence: Even the plain fact of change is no reason to drown in sorrow.
simple_meaning: Even if you see this embodied being as something that keeps being born and dying, grief is still not fitting. Krishna is pushing Arjuna beyond sorrow itself.
insight: It shifts the mind from emotional collapse to steady seeing, even before deeper understanding arrives.
modern_relevance: You are sitting beside a hospital bed, bracing for news you cannot control. Even if you think only in terms of birth and death, panic does not help you meet the moment.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च । तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
translation: क्योंकि पैदा हुएकी जरूर मृत्यु होगी और मरे हुएका जरूर जन्म होगा ।  इस जन्ममरणरूप परिवर्तन के प्रवाह का परिहार अर्थात् निवारण नहीं हो सकता ।  अतः इस विषयमें तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिये ॥
english_translation: For what is born, death is certain; for what dies, birth is certain. What cannot be avoided should not be grieved over.
essence: What must change is not a reason for grief.
simple_meaning: Anything that is born will die, and anything that dies will be born again. Since this cycle cannot be stopped, there is no reason to grieve over it.
insight: It shifts the mind from resisting inevitability to meeting it without panic.
modern_relevance: You are sitting beside a hospital bed, watching a monitor you cannot negotiate with. The fear is real, but the fact is plain: some changes cannot be prevented, only met with steadiness.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत । अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥
translation: हे भारत  सभी प्राणी जन्मसे पहले अप्रकट थे और मरनेके बाद अप्रकट हो जायँगे, केवल बीचमें ही प्रकट दीखते हैं ।  अतः इसमें शोक करनेकी बात ही क्या है ॥
english_translation: All beings are unmanifest before birth and unmanifest after death; they are manifest only in between. Why grieve over that?
essence: What appears briefly was never meant to be clung to.
simple_meaning: All beings are hidden before birth and hidden again after death. Since life is only a brief visible interval, there is no reason for grief.
insight: It shifts attention from the temporary display to the larger continuity beneath it.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a hospital monitor, waiting for news you cannot control. The shape of a life is changing in front of you. This verse steadies the heart by showing that appearance and disappearance are not the whole story.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेनमाश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः । आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः श्रृणोतिश्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित् ॥
translation: कोई इस शरीरीको आश्चर्यकी तरह देखता है और वैसे ही अन्य कोई इसका आश्चर्यकी तरह वर्णन करता है तथा अन्य कोई इसको आश्चर्यकी तरह सुनता है और इसको सुनकर भी कोई नहीं जानता ।  अर्थात यह शरीरी दुर्विज्ञेय है ॥
english_translation: Some behold the inner being as wondrous; some speak of it as wondrous; some hear of it as wondrous; and even after hearing, no one truly knows it.
essence: The true self remains mysterious even after endless hearing.
simple_meaning: The true self is astonishing to behold, describe, and hear about, yet almost no one truly understands it.
insight: It shifts the mind from collecting descriptions to seeking direct understanding.
modern_relevance: You can read three books, hear five opinions, and still miss what matters. Some truths stay hidden until your attention becomes quieter than your analysis.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत । तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन सबके देहमें यह देही नित्य ही अवध्य है ।  इसलिये सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके लिये अर्थात् किसी भी प्राणीके लिये तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिये ॥
english_translation: O descendant of Bharata, the embodied one in every body is eternal and cannot be slain. Therefore you should not grieve for any being.
essence: What is most real in a person cannot be killed, so grief loses its ground.
simple_meaning: The true self in every body cannot be destroyed, so there is no reason to grieve for anyone.
insight: It shifts the mind from mourning the body alone to seeing the enduring presence within it.
modern_relevance: You stand beside a hospital bed, hearing a diagnosis you cannot fix. Panic says everything is ending; this verse says what is deepest in a person is beyond harm.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि । धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाछ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते ॥
translation: अपने स्वधर्म क्षात्रधर्म को देखकर भी तुम्हें विकम्पित अर्थात् कर्तव्यकर्मसे विचलित नहीं होना चाहिये क्योंकि धर्ममय युद्धसे बढ़कर क्षत्रियके लिये दूसरा कोई कल्याणकारक कर्म नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Considering your own duty, you should not waver. For a warrior, no action is more beneficial than a righteous battle.
essence: Right action can feel hard and still be the best choice.
simple_meaning: Arjuna is told not to hesitate once he sees his own duty clearly. For a warrior, fighting for what is right is the best course.
insight: It shifts you from hesitation to committed action when your role and responsibility are already clear.
modern_relevance: You are standing at the door, phone in hand, about to send the message you have delayed for weeks. The discomfort is real, but the right action does not disappear because it feels hard.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम् । सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम् ॥
translation: अपनेआप प्राप्त हुआ युद्ध खुला हुआ स्वर्गका दरवाजा भी है ।  हे पृथानन्दन  वे क्षत्रिय बड़े सुखी भाग्यशाली हैं, जिनको ऐसा युद्ध प्राप्त होता है ॥
english_translation: An unbidden battle is an open gate to higher realms. O Partha, fortunate are the warriors who receive such a war.
essence: A righteous burden can become the highest opening.
simple_meaning: A warrior who is given a righteous battle has a rare chance to act with honor and courage. Krishna calls such an opportunity a doorway to a higher realm.
insight: It shifts the mind from avoiding difficulty to recognizing honorable obligation when it appears.
modern_relevance: You are handed the hard conversation you hoped would disappear: telling the truth, ending the false peace, or standing up when silence would be easier. The moment is costly, but it is also clean.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अथ चैत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि । ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
translation: अब अगर तू यह धर्ममय युद्ध नहीं करेगा, तो अपने धर्म और कीर्तिका त्याग करके पापको प्राप्त होगा ॥
english_translation: If you do not fight this righteous war, you will abandon your duty and honor and incur blame.
essence: Avoiding the right duty does not protect you; it stains you.
simple_meaning: Refusing a just battle would mean abandoning your duty and honor, and that choice would bring blame.
insight: It shifts the mind from fear-based avoidance to responsibility for the action that preserves integrity.
modern_relevance: You’re staring at a message you know you must send, because staying silent will hurt more. The fear of discomfort is real, but so is the cost of walking away from what you know is right.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम् । संभावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥
translation: और सब प्राणी भी तेरी सदा रहनेवाली अपकीर्तिका कथन अर्थात निंदा करेंगे ।  वह अपकीर्ति सम्मानित मनुष्यके लिये मृत्युसे भी बढ़कर दुःखदायी होती है ॥
english_translation: And all beings will speak of your everlasting disgrace. For an honored person, disgrace is worse than death.
essence: A honored life can be wounded more by shame than by death.
simple_meaning: People will keep speaking of your disgrace, and for someone who has been honored, that shame feels worse than death.
insight: It shifts the mind from fearing pain to fearing the loss of integrity.
modern_relevance: You walk out of a room knowing the hard truth but choosing silence. The image that follows you is not comfort — it is the version of yourself that backed away.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः । येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥
translation: महारथीलोग तुझे भयके कारण युद्धसे उपरत हटा हुआ मानेंगे ।  जिनकी धारणामें तू बहुमान्य हो चुका है, उनकी दृष्टिमें तू लघुताको प्राप्त हो जायगा ॥
english_translation: The great warriors will think you withdrew from battle out of fear. Those who once held you in high regard will see you as small.
essence: Retreat from duty, and respect turns to shrinkage.
simple_meaning: If Arjuna stops fighting, the great warriors will assume he fled from fear. People who respected him will now look down on him.
insight: It shifts the mind from protecting comfort to protecting integrity under pressure.
modern_relevance: You back out of the difficult conversation at the last minute, and everyone notices. The silence protects you for a moment, then quietly rewrites how people see you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून् वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः । निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥
translation: तेरे शत्रुलोग तेरी सार्मथ्यकी निन्दा करते हुए न कहनेयोग्य बहुतसे वचन भी कहेंगे ।  उससे बढ़कर और दुःखकी बात क्या होगी ॥
english_translation: Your enemies will speak many unworthy words, mocking your strength. What could be more painful than that?
essence: Public shame can hurt more than physical danger.
simple_meaning: Your enemies will mock your ability and say cruel things about you. For a respected person, that kind of public shame can feel worse than death.
insight: It exposes how fear of ridicule can paralyze action, and pushes the mind back toward duty.
modern_relevance: You back out of the hard conversation, and later people call you weak behind your back. The wound is not the criticism itself — it is watching your own courage get rewritten.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् । तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥
translation: अगर युद्धमें तू मारा जायगा तो तुझे स्वर्गकी प्राप्ति होगी और अगर युद्धमें तू जीत जायगा तो पृथ्वीका राज्य भोगेगा ।  अतः हे कुन्तीनन्दन तू युद्धके लिये निश्चय करके खड़ा हो जा ॥
english_translation: If you are killed, you will attain heaven; if you win, you will enjoy the kingdom. Therefore, rise, Kaunteya, and fight with resolve.
essence: Act now; the result does not cancel the duty.
simple_meaning: Arjuna is told to stand up and fight without wavering. Whether he wins or dies, he must do what stands before him now.
insight: It shifts the mind from outcome anxiety to firm action in the present.
modern_relevance: You are staring at the message that could end a relationship or save one. Either way, the longer you delay, the heavier it becomes. Krishna’s answer is simple: decide, then stand up.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ । ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
translation: जयपराजय, लाभहानि और सुखदुःखको समान करके फिर युद्धमें लग जा ।  इस प्रकार युद्ध करनेसे तू पापको प्राप्त नहीं होगा ॥
english_translation: Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike. Then enter the battle; you will not incur wrongdoing.
essence: Equanimity frees action from the stain of panic and craving.
simple_meaning: Stay steady through pleasure and pain, success and failure. Act from that balance, and your action will not bind you.
insight: It shifts attention from emotional reaction to even-minded action under pressure.
modern_relevance: You open the email that could end a friendship or save one. Your hands shake, but the decision still has to be made. This verse asks for balance before the next move.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां श्रृणु । बुद्ध्यायुक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि ॥
translation: हे पार्थ यह समबुद्धि तेरे लिए पहले सांख्ययोगमें कही गयी, अब तू इसको कर्मयोगके विषयमें सुन जिस समबुद्धिसे युक्त हुआ तू कर्मबन्धनका त्याग कर देगा ॥
english_translation: This wisdom has been taught to you in Sankhya. Now hear it in yoga. Equipped with this understanding, Arjuna, you will cast off the bondage of action.
essence: Clear understanding frees action from bondage.
simple_meaning: Krishna says the same wisdom has already been explained as knowledge, and now he will explain it as action. With this clear understanding, Arjuna can break free from the bondage created by action.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing knowledge and action as separate to seeing action as the expression of clear understanding.
modern_relevance: You understand the principle in a quiet room, then face the hard conversation. The real test is whether that clarity still holds when action begins.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
translation: मनुष्यलोकमें इस समबुद्धिरूप धर्मके आरम्भका नाश नहीं होता, इसके अनुष्ठानका उलटा फल भी नहीं होता और इसका थोड़ासा भी अनुष्ठान जन्ममरणरूप महान् भयसे रक्षा कर लेता है ॥
english_translation: In this human world, no effort toward this steady wisdom is ever lost. No harmful result comes from it. Even a little practice of this dharma protects one from great fear.
essence: Even a tiny start on the right path protects you from fear.
simple_meaning: Even a small beginning in this discipline is never wasted, never backfires, and can protect you from deep fear.
insight: It shifts the mind from all-or-nothing thinking to trusting small, sincere practice.
modern_relevance: You finally open the meditation app after weeks of avoidance, sit for three minutes, and wonder whether it matters. It matters more than you think.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन । बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥
translation: हे कुरुनन्दन इस समबुद्धिकी प्राप्तिके विषयमें व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धि एक ही होती है ।  अव्यवसायी मनुष्योंकी बुद्धियाँ अनन्त और बहुशाखाओंवाली ही होती हैं ॥
english_translation: O son of the Kurus, the resolute intellect is one-pointed here. The intellect of the irresolute is many-branched and endless.
essence: Resolute seeing unifies the mind; hesitation multiplies it.
simple_meaning: A focused mind has one clear direction, while an unfocused mind keeps branching into endless doubts and options.
insight: It shifts attention from scattered possibilities to a single settled intention.
modern_relevance: You have three tabs open, four messages unanswered, and one hard decision you keep postponing. The problem is not too little information — it is a mind that refuses one clear direction.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः । वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन  जो कामनाओंमें तन्मय हो रहे हैं, स्वर्गको ही श्रेष्ठ माननेवाले हैं, वेदोंमें कहे हुए सकाम कर्मोंमें प्रीति रखनेवाले हैं, भोगोंके सिवाय और कुछ है ही नहीं  ऐसा कहनेवाले हैं, वे अविवेकी मनुष्य इस प्रकारकी जिस पुष्पित दिखाऊ शोभायुक्त वाणीको कहा करते हैं, जो कि जन्मरूपी कर्मफलको देनेवाली है तथा भोग और ऐश्वर्यकी प्राप्तिके लिये बहुतसी क्रियाओंका वर्णन करनेवाली है ॥
english_translation: The unwise speak flowery words. They delight in the ritual sections of the Vedas and say nothing else exists.
essence: Beautiful words can hide a mind trapped by desire.
simple_meaning: Ignorant people speak in attractive, polished language that promises pleasure and reward. They get stuck in ritual talk and claim there is nothing beyond it.
insight: It teaches you to distrust language that flatters craving and narrows reality to immediate reward.
modern_relevance: A polished video ad tells you that one purchase will fix your emptiness. Krishna would call that flowered speech: attractive, persuasive, and built to keep desire spinning.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम् । क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन  जो कामनाओंमें तन्मय हो रहे हैं, स्वर्गको ही श्रेष्ठ माननेवाले हैं, वेदोंमें कहे हुए सकाम कर्मोंमें प्रीति रखनेवाले हैं, भोगोंके सिवाय और कुछ है ही नहीं  ऐसा कहनेवाले हैं, वे अविवेकी मनुष्य इस प्रकारकी जिस पुष्पित दिखाऊ शोभायुक्त वाणीको कहा करते हैं, जो कि जन्मरूपी कर्मफलको देनेवाली है तथा भोग और ऐश्वर्यकी प्राप्तिके लिये बहुतसी क्रियाओंका वर्णन करनेवाली है ॥
english_translation: Those without clear seeing speak flowery words that promise birth and action-fruit, and describe many rites for enjoyment and power.
essence: Flowery promises can keep desire alive while pretending to guide you.
simple_meaning: People driven by desire praise rituals that promise pleasure, status, and future rewards. Their words sound attractive, but they keep the mind chasing more rewards.
insight: It trains you to spot teachings that increase wanting instead of reducing it.
modern_relevance: A polished ad, a glossy seminar, a mentor promising status if you just follow the system — it all sounds convincing until you notice it is feeding craving, not clearing it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् । व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥
translation: उस पुष्पित वाणीसे जिसका अन्तःकरण हर लिया गया है अर्थात् भोगोंकी तरफ खिंच गया है और जो भोग तथा ऐश्वर्यमें अत्यन्त आसक्त हैं, उन मनुष्योंकी परमात्मामें निश्चयात्मिका बुद्धि नहीं होती ॥
english_translation: For those whose minds are carried away by pleasure and power, steadfast determination in meditation does not arise.
essence: Craving scatters the mind before wisdom can settle.
simple_meaning: People who are pulled toward pleasure and power lose clear judgment. Their mind cannot settle into steady focus on the supreme reality.
insight: It shifts attention from external reward to inner steadiness as the basis of right understanding.
modern_relevance: You open your phone for one quick check, and an hour disappears into wanting more. The mind that keeps chasing reward cannot hold a steady line.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन । निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥
translation: वेद तीनों गुणोंके कार्यका ही वर्णन करनेवाले हैं हे अर्जुन तू तीनों गुणोंसे रहित हो जा, निर्द्वन्द्व हो जा, निरन्तर नित्य वस्तु परमात्मा में स्थित हो जा, योगक्षेमकी चाहना भी मत रख और परमात्मपरायण हो जा ॥
english_translation: The Vedas deal with the three qualities. Arjuna, rise beyond the three qualities, beyond opposites, fixed in lasting reality, free from concern for gain and security, and established in the true self.
essence: Freedom begins when gain and loss stop defining you.
simple_meaning: The sacred texts describe the world of changing forces, but Krishna tells Arjuna to rise above them. He should stop chasing comfort and security, and stay rooted in what is unchanging.
insight: It shifts attention from managing outcomes to resting in what does not change.
modern_relevance: You are refreshing your bank app for the tenth time, waiting for reassurance. The verse says the deeper life begins when you stop living by gain, fear, and the next update.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः संप्लुतोदके । तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः ॥
translation: सब तरफसे परिपूर्ण महान् जलाशयके प्राप्त होनेपर छोटे गड्ढों में भरे जल में मनुष्यका जितना प्रयोजन रहता है अर्थात् कुछ भी प्रयोजन नहीं रहता, वेदों और शास्त्रोंको तत्त्वसे जाननेवाले ब्रह्मज्ञानीका सम्पूर्ण वेदोंमें उतना ही प्रयोजन रहता है अर्थात् कुछ भी प्रयोजन नहीं रहता ॥
english_translation: For one who understands, all the Vedas are as useful as a small puddle when a great reservoir of water is at hand.
essence: Complete understanding makes lesser sources unnecessary.
simple_meaning: A person who truly understands the supreme reality needs the Vedas no more than a person beside a full reservoir needs a tiny puddle.
insight: It shifts the mind from collecting information to recognizing the decisive truth that makes excess instruction unnecessary.
modern_relevance: You have read every article, saved every thread, and still feel unsure before making the hard call. At some point, more input stops helping; clear seeing does.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
translation: कर्तव्यकर्म करनेमें ही तेरा अधिकार है, फलोंमें कभी नहीं ।  अतः तू कर्मफलका हेतु भी मत बन और तेरी अकर्मण्यतामें भी आसक्ति न हो ॥
english_translation: You have a right to action alone, never to its fruits. Do not become the cause of the result, and do not cling to inaction.
essence: Action belongs to you; the result does not.
simple_meaning: You control your action, not what it produces. Do your duty without chasing the reward or getting attached to doing nothing.
insight: It shifts attention from controlling outcomes to carrying out the action cleanly.
modern_relevance: You send the apology text after midnight, then keep rereading it for the perfect reply. This verse cuts that loop: speak, act, and stop trying to control the response.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
translation: हे धनञ्जय  तू आसक्तिका त्याग करके सिद्धिअसिद्धिमें सम होकर योगमें स्थित हुआ कर्मोंको कर क्योंकि समत्व ही योग कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: O Dhananjaya, perform actions while established in yoga, abandoning attachment. Remain equal in success and failure, for equanimity is called yoga.
essence: Equanimity turns action into yoga.
simple_meaning: Keep doing your duty without clinging to results. Stay steady whether things work out or not; that steady balance is yoga.
insight: It shifts attention from outcome-chasing to steady action, so success and failure stop controlling the mind.
modern_relevance: You send the message, then stare at the screen waiting for a reply. The mind rises and falls with every notification; this verse teaches you to keep your centre anyway.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय । बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥
translation: बुद्धियोगसमता की अपेक्षा सकामकर्म दूरसे अत्यन्त ही निकृष्ट है ।  अतः हे धनञ्जय  तू बुद्धि समता का आश्रय ले क्योंकि फलके हेतु बननेवाले अत्यन्त दीन हैं ॥
english_translation: Action driven by craving is far below the steadiness of clear discernment. Seek refuge in clear discernment, for those who chase results are pitiable.
essence: Clear discernment is richer than reward-chasing.
simple_meaning: Action done for rewards is lower than action guided by clear discernment. Krishna tells Arjuna to rely on that steadiness instead of craving outcomes.
insight: It shifts attention from outcome-chasing to the stability of right seeing.
modern_relevance: You send the message, then keep checking for the reply every two minutes. The mind that needs a payoff has already lost its steadiness.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते । तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥
translation: बुद्धिसमता से युक्त मनुष्य यहाँ जीवित अवस्थामें ही पुण्य और पाप दोनोंका त्याग कर देता है ।  अतः तू योगसमता में लग जा, क्योंकि योग ही कर्मोंमें कुशलता है ॥
english_translation: One who is united with clear discernment casts off both good and bad deeds in this life. Therefore, devote yourself to yoga, for yoga is skill in action.
essence: Clear action frees you from the weight of both success and failure.
simple_meaning: Clear discernment lets a person rise above both merit and fault. Krishna tells Arjuna to take up yoga, because true yoga is skill in action.
insight: It shifts attention from moral self-judgment to disciplined action with clarity.
modern_relevance: You send the message, then keep rereading it for hours, trying to judge whether it was right or wrong. This verse says the steady mind stops living inside that loop and simply acts cleanly.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः । जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥
translation: समतायुक्त मनीषी साधक कर्मजन्य फलका त्याग करके जन्मरूप बन्धनसे मुक्त होकर निर्विकार पदको प्राप्त हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Wise people, united in clarity, abandon the fruit born of action and reach the flawless state, free from the bondage of birth.
essence: Freedom comes when action is done without clutching its reward.
simple_meaning: Wise people let go of the results of their actions. That freedom breaks the chain that keeps them bound to repeated birth and suffering.
insight: It shifts attention from owning outcomes to doing the work cleanly, so action no longer tightens the mind.
modern_relevance: You send the hard email, then keep checking for a reply every five minutes. The action is complete, but your mind keeps demanding ownership of the result. This verse cuts that cord.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति । तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥
translation: जिस समय तेरी बुद्धि मोहरूपी दलदलको तर जायगी, उसी समय तू सुने हुए और सुननेमें आनेवाले भोगोंसे वैराग्यको प्राप्त हो जायगा ॥
english_translation: When your intellect crosses the swamp of delusion, you will grow dispassionate toward what has been heard and what remains to be heard.
essence: Clear seeing ends the pull of future pleasures.
simple_meaning: When clear understanding rises above confusion, attachment to pleasures you have heard of or are still chasing naturally fades.
insight: It shifts you from chasing experiences to seeing through their lure.
modern_relevance: You finally read the message, and the fantasy collapses. The relationship, the job, the purchase, the applause — all of it looks smaller once the fog clears.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला । समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥
translation: जिस कालमें शास्त्रीय मतभेदोंसे विचलित हुई तेरी बुद्धि निश्चल हो जायगी और परमात्मामें अचल हो जायगी, उस कालमें तू योगको प्राप्त हो जायगा ॥
english_translation: When your intellect, unmoved by conflicting teachings, becomes steady in complete stillness, you will attain yoga.
essence: Yoga begins when the mind stops being pulled in every direction.
simple_meaning: When your mind is no longer shaken by conflicting ideas and becomes completely steady, you reach yoga.
insight: It shifts attention from intellectual churn to inner steadiness as the condition for clear action.
modern_relevance: You have three tabs open, ten opinions in your head, and one hard choice in front of you. The answer does not come by adding more noise — it comes when the mind settles enough to see.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचस्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव । स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे केशव  परमात्मामें स्थित स्थिर बुद्धिवाले मनुष्यके क्या लक्षण होते हैं वह स्थिर बुद्धिवाला मनुष्य कैसे बोलता है, कैसे बैठता है और कैसे चलता है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: O Kesava, what are the marks of one whose wisdom is steady and who is absorbed in stillness? How does a person of steady understanding speak, sit, and walk?
