essence: Steady wisdom must be recognizable in ordinary movement.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks how a person with steady wisdom behaves in daily life — how they speak, sit, and move.
insight: It shifts attention from abstract understanding to visible conduct under pressure.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who stays calm under pressure and wonder, what makes them different? Arjuna asks the same thing before the hardest decision of his life.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान् । आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे पृथानन्दन  जिस कालमें साधक मनोगत सम्पूर्ण कामनाओंका अच्छी तरह त्याग कर देता है और अपनेआपसे अपनेआपमें ही सन्तुष्ट रहता है, उस कालमें वह स्थितप्रज्ञ कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: The divine said: When a person gives up all desires that arise in the mind, and is satisfied in the true self by the true self alone, that person is called steady in wisdom.
essence: Steadiness begins when desire no longer defines your sense of enough.
simple_meaning: A person becomes steady in wisdom when all mental desires are released and contentment comes from within, not from outside things.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing satisfaction to recognising contentment as inward and already available.
modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the message, the praise — and still feel restless. This verse points to the deeper shift: stop waiting for outside approval to settle you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः । वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥
translation: दुःखोंकी प्राप्ति होनेपर जिसके मनमें उद्वेग नहीं होता और सुखोंकी प्राप्ति होनेपर जिसके मनमें स्पृहा नहीं होती तथा जो राग, भय और क्रोधसे सर्वथा रहित हो गया है, वह मननशील मनुष्य स्थिरबुद्धि कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: The steady-minded sage is unshaken by sorrow, free from craving in joy, and beyond attachment, fear, and anger.
essence: Steadiness remains when pleasure and pain lose their grip.
simple_meaning: A truly steady person stays calm in hardship, does not chase pleasure, and is free from attachment, fear, and anger.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing comfort to building inner steadiness that stays intact under praise, loss, and pressure.
modern_relevance: You get a painful message, then a flattering one, then another setback. Your mood whiplashes with each ping. This verse points to a steadier way: let events pass through without letting them seize the mind.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् । नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
translation: सब जगह आसक्तिरहित हुआ जो मनुष्य उसउस शुभअशुभको प्राप्त करके न तो अभिनन्दित होता है और न द्वेष करता है, उसकी बुद्धि प्रतिष्ठित है ॥
english_translation: One who feels no clinging anywhere, and neither rejoices nor hates when good or bad comes, has steady wisdom.
essence: Steady wisdom does not need life to feel favorable.
simple_meaning: A person with steady wisdom does not cling to anything. When good or bad events happen, they neither get thrilled nor upset.
insight: It shifts attention from reacting to events toward remaining inwardly even as events change.
modern_relevance: You get the message that changed the plan is bad news, then the next hour brings unexpected praise. Both can hit the same inbox. This verse teaches you not to build your identity from either one.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
translation: जिस तरह कछुआ अपने अङ्गोंको सब ओरसे समेट लेता है, ऐसे ही जिस कालमें यह कर्मयोगी इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंसे इन्द्रियोंको सब प्रकारसे समेट लेता हटा लेता है, तब उसकी बुद्धि प्रतिष्ठित हो जाती है ॥
english_translation: When this one draws the senses fully back from sense-objects, like a tortoise withdrawing its limbs, wisdom is steady.
essence: Steadiness begins when the senses stop running outward.
simple_meaning: Wisdom becomes stable when the senses are pulled back from the things they chase, just as a tortoise draws in its limbs.
insight: It shifts the mind from constant reaching to deliberate withdrawal from distraction.
modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message, then three more tabs, then a video you did not mean to watch. The day starts leaking away the moment your attention keeps reaching outward.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः । रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥
translation: निराहारी इन्द्रियोंको विषयोंसे हटानेवाले मनुष्यके भी विषय तो निवृत्त हो जाते हैं, पर रस निवृत्त नहीं होता ।  परन्तु इस स्थितप्रज्ञ मनुष्यका तो रस भी परमात्मतत्त्वका अनुभव होनेसे निवृत्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Objects fall away from the self-denying person, but the taste for them remains. For the one who has seen the supreme reality, even that taste falls away.
essence: Craving ends only when a higher reality becomes more compelling.
simple_meaning: Stopping the senses is not enough. The outer attraction may fade, but the inner taste remains until a higher reality is directly seen.
insight: It shifts the mind from suppression to transformation: remove the craving by changing what you truly value.
modern_relevance: You delete the app, mute the chat, and swear off the habit — yet the urge returns at midnight. The surface trigger is gone, but the deeper appetite still needs to be seen through.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः । इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥
translation: हे कुन्तीनन्दन रसबुद्धि रहनेसे यत्न करते हुए विद्वान् मनुष्यकी भी प्रमथनशील इन्द्रियाँ उसके मनको बलपूर्वक हर लेती हैं ॥
english_translation: Even for a wise person who strives, the turbulent senses can forcibly carry away the mind.
essence: Restraint fails without disciplined senses.
simple_meaning: Even a thoughtful person who is trying hard can lose control when the senses become restless and drag the mind away.
insight: It shifts the focus from occasional restraint to steady discipline of the senses and mind.
modern_relevance: You delete the app, silence the phone, and still reach for it. The urge returns from inside, and it can pull even a careful mind off course.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः । वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
translation: कर्मयोगी साधक उन सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियोंको वशमें करके मेरे परायण होकर बैठे क्योंकि जिसकी इन्द्रियाँ वशमें हैं, उसकी बुद्धि प्रतिष्ठित है ॥
english_translation: Having restrained all the senses, the disciplined one should sit devoted to Me. For one whose senses are under control, wisdom is firmly established.
essence: Wisdom becomes steady only when the senses are no longer in charge.
simple_meaning: Hold the senses in check and stay focused on the divine. When the senses are controlled, clear wisdom becomes steady.
insight: It shifts attention from reacting to every impulse toward holding the senses steady so judgment can stay clear.
modern_relevance: You open your phone to avoid one hard message and lose ten minutes. The real issue is not the screen — it is whether your senses are steering you or you are steering them.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते । सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥
translation: विषयोंका चिन्तन करनेवाले मनुष्यकी उन विषयोंमें आसक्ति पैदा हो जाती है ।  आसक्तिसे कामना पैदा होती है ।  कामनासे क्रोध पैदा होता है ।  क्रोध होनेपर सम्मोह मूढ़भाव हो जाता है ।  सम्मोहसे स्मृति भ्रष्ट हो जाती है ।  स्मृति भ्रष्ट होनेपर बुद्धिका नाश हो जाता है ।  बुद्धिका नाश होनेपर मनुष्यका पतन हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Thinking about sense objects creates attachment to them. Attachment gives rise to desire; desire gives rise to anger.
essence: What you dwell on becomes what you cling to, then what burns you.
simple_meaning: Fixating on pleasures or objects creates attachment. Attachment turns into wanting, and wanting turns into anger when blocked.
insight: It teaches you to interrupt the chain at the first attachment, not after the anger has already taken root.
modern_relevance: You keep checking a message thread, then the silence starts to sting, then irritation takes over. The verse names that slide from fixation to fury before it owns you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥
translation: विषयोंका चिन्तन करनेवाले मनुष्यकी उन विषयोंमें आसक्ति पैदा हो जाती है ।  आसक्तिसे कामना पैदा होती है ।  कामनासे क्रोध पैदा होता है ।  क्रोध होनेपर सम्मोह मूढ़भाव हो जाता है ।  सम्मोहसे स्मृति भ्रष्ट हो जाती है ।  स्मृति भ्रष्ट होनेपर बुद्धिका नाश हो जाता है ।  बुद्धिका नाश होनेपर मनुष्यका पतन हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, loss of discernment; from loss of discernment, ruin.
essence: Anger first distorts seeing, then destroys the mind that should guide action.
simple_meaning: Anger starts a chain reaction: confusion, broken memory, lost judgment, and finally self-destruction.
insight: It teaches you to interrupt anger early, before it hijacks memory and judgment.
modern_relevance: You read one hostile message and your chest tightens. Within minutes, you forget what mattered, misread everything, and say the thing you’ll regret later.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् । आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति ॥
translation: वशीभूत अन्तःकरणवाला कर्मयोगी साधक रागद्वेषसे रहित अपने वशमें की हुई इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा विषयोंका सेवन करता हुआ अन्तःकरणकी निर्मलता को प्राप्त हो जाता है ।  निर्मलता प्राप्त होनेपर साधकके सम्पूर्ण दुःखोंका नाश हो जाता है और ऐसे शुद्ध चित्तवाले साधककी बुद्धि निःसन्देह बहुत जल्दी परमात्मामें स्थिर हो जाती है ॥
english_translation: The disciplined person, moving among objects with senses under control and free from attraction and aversion, attains serenity.
essence: Freedom comes from meeting experience without attraction or aversion.
simple_meaning: A person with controlled senses can engage with the world without craving or rejecting it, and that steadiness brings inner clarity.
insight: It shifts the mind from reaction to regulated contact with experience.
modern_relevance: You open a message from someone you both miss and resent. The old reaction wants to pull you in or push you away. This verse points to a third way: stay steady, respond cleanly.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते । प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥
translation: वशीभूत अन्तःकरणवाला कर्मयोगी साधक रागद्वेषसे रहित अपने वशमें की हुई इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा विषयोंका सेवन करता हुआ अन्तःकरणकी निर्मलता को प्राप्त हो जाता है ।  निर्मलता प्राप्त होनेपर साधकके सम्पूर्ण दुःखोंका नाश हो जाता है और ऐसे शुद्ध चित्तवाले साधककी बुद्धि निःसन्देह बहुत जल्दी परमात्मामें स्थिर हो जाती है ॥
english_translation: In inner clarity, all suffering falls away. For one whose mind is clear, understanding settles quickly.
essence: Clear seeing ends suffering and lets understanding settle at once.
simple_meaning: When the mind becomes calm and clear, suffering drops away and understanding becomes steady very quickly.
insight: It shifts attention from emotional turbulence to the clarity that dissolves it.
modern_relevance: You finally stop arguing with a message you already know is true. The tightness in your chest loosens, and the next right thought arrives without force.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना । न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥
translation: जिसके मनइन्द्रियाँ संयमित नहीं हैं, ऐसे मनुष्यकी व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धि नहीं होती और व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धि न होनेसे उसमें कर्तव्यपरायणताकी भावना नहीं होती ।  ऐसी भावना न होनेसे उसको शान्ति नहीं मिलती ।  फिर शान्तिरहित मनुष्यको सुख कैसे मिल सकता है ॥
english_translation: A restless mind has no steady discernment, no steady purpose, no peace, and without peace, no happiness.
essence: Without inner discipline, even happiness has no place to stand.
simple_meaning: A person who cannot control the mind and senses lacks clear judgment, steady purpose, peace, and therefore real happiness.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing comfort to building inner steadiness first.
modern_relevance: You open your phone to calm down, then ten minutes later you are more scattered than before. Krishna points to the real problem: a mind that cannot hold itself together cannot produce peace on demand.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते । तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥
translation: अपनेअपने विषयोंमें विचरती हुई इन्द्रियोंमेंसे एक ही इन्द्रिय जिस मनको अपना अनुगामी बना लेती है, वह अकेला मन जलमें नौकाको वायुकी तरह इसकी बुद्धिको हर लेता है ॥
english_translation: As the winds carry a boat on water, even one roaming sense can sweep away the mind's discernment.
essence: One uncontrolled sense can carry the mind away.
simple_meaning: If even one sense runs after its objects, it can pull the mind along and destroy clear judgment, like wind pushing a boat off course.
insight: It teaches you to treat attention as fragile: one unchecked sense can derail judgment.
modern_relevance: You open one app “for a minute,” then your focus is gone. A single unchecked pull can scatter the whole mind before you notice.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
translation: इसलिये हे महाबाहो  जिस मनुष्यकी इन्द्रियाँ इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंसे सर्वथा निगृहीत वशमें की हुई हैं, उसकी बुद्धि स्थिर है ॥
english_translation: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, the wisdom of one whose senses are fully restrained from sense-objects is steady.
essence: Steady wisdom begins when the senses stop ruling your attention.
simple_meaning: A person who fully controls the senses and keeps them away from objects of desire develops steady understanding.
insight: It shifts attention from impulse control in the moment to a stable pattern of restraint.
modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message and lose twenty minutes. The problem is not the message — it's the senses running outward before your mind can choose.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी । यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥
translation: सम्पूर्ण प्राणियों की जो रात परमात्मासे विमुखता है, उसमें संयमी मनुष्य जागता है, और जिसमें सब प्राणी जागते हैं भोग और संग्रहमें लगे रहते हैं, वह तत्त्वको जाननेवाले मुनिकी दृष्टिमें रात है ॥
english_translation: What is night for all beings is wakefulness for the self-controlled one. What all beings wake toward is night for the seer who knows the real.
essence: What the many pursue in sleep, the wise leave behind awake.
simple_meaning: Ordinary people chase pleasure and possessions, but the disciplined seeker sees through that pull. What seems valuable to most becomes empty to the one who knows the real.
insight: It shifts attention from shared craving to clear seeing, so desire no longer defines what feels real.
modern_relevance: Everyone around you is refreshing, comparing, buying, and chasing the next hit of approval. You pause, and the whole game looks strangely dim. That pause is not weakness; it is seeing.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठंसमुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् । तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वेस शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥
translation: जैसे सम्पूर्ण नदियोंका जल चारों ओरसे जलद्वारा परिपूर्ण समुद्रमें आकर मिलता है, पर समुद्र अपनी मर्यादामें अचल प्रतिष्ठित रहता है ऐसे ही सम्पूर्ण भोगपदार्थ जिस संयमी मनुष्य को विकार उत्पन्न किये बिना ही उसको प्राप्त होते हैं, वही मनुष्य परमशान्तिको प्राप्त होता है, भोगोंकी कामनावाला नहीं ॥
english_translation: As rivers flow into the sea and the sea remains steady, so desires may enter a disciplined person without disturbing inner peace. The person who wants pleasures does not find peace.
essence: Peace belongs to the one who stays steady while desire moves.
simple_meaning: A person can meet desire without being shaken by it. Peace belongs to the one who stays steady, not to the one chasing pleasure.
insight: It trains the mind to receive experience without becoming dependent on it.
modern_relevance: You open your phone and a hundred wants rush in — one more message, one more purchase, one more distraction. You do not need to obey the wave. You can stay larger than it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः । निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कामनाओंका त्याग करके स्पृहारहित, ममतारहित और अहंकाररहित होकर आचरण करता है, वह शान्तिको प्राप्त होता है ॥
english_translation: One who gives up all desires, moves without craving, without possessiveness, and without ego, attains peace.
essence: Peace begins when wanting, owning, and self-importance fall away.
simple_meaning: A person who acts after releasing desire, possessiveness, and ego finds peace.
insight: It shifts the mind from needing validation to moving cleanly through action.
modern_relevance: You send the message, then keep checking for a reply. You finish the work, then want credit. This verse points to the calm that comes when action is no longer chained to grasping.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति । स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन  यह ब्राह्मी स्थिति है ।  इसको प्राप्त होकर कभी कोई मोहित नहीं होता ।  इस स्थितिमें यदि अन्तकालमें भी स्थित हो जाय, तो निर्वाण शान्त ब्रह्मकी प्राप्ति हो जाती है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, this is the Brahmic state. Having reached it, one is never deluded. Remaining established in it even at the end of life, one attains freedom in the supreme reality.
essence: Steadiness in the supreme reality ends confusion, even at life’s edge.
simple_meaning: A person who reaches this steady inner state is no longer confused. Even at life’s end, that steadiness leads to freedom in the supreme reality.
insight: It shifts the goal from temporary calm to an unbroken inner steadiness that survives the hardest moment.
modern_relevance: You are sitting in a hospital corridor after a hard diagnosis, and panic keeps trying to take over. This verse points to a steadiness that does not collapse, even there.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन । तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे जनार्दन अगर आप कर्मसे बुद्धि ज्ञान को श्रेष्ठ मानते हैं, तो फिर हे केशव  मुझे घोर कर्ममें क्यों लगाते हैं  आप अपने मिले हुएसे वचनोंसे मेरी बुद्धिको मोहितसी कर रहे हैं ।  अतः आप निश्चय करके उस एक बात को कहिये, जिससे मैं कल्याणको प्राप्त हो जाऊँ ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: O Janardana, if you consider understanding superior to action, then why do you urge me to this terrible action, O Keshava? Your mixed words confuse my mind; tell me one clear thing by which I may attain what is good.
essence: Mixed guidance deepens paralysis; clarity must come before action.
simple_meaning: Arjuna is confused. Krishna seems to praise understanding over action, yet still asks him to fight. He asks for one clear instruction that will lead him toward what is good.
insight: It teaches you to name confusion directly and ask for one decisive principle.
modern_relevance: You get two confident answers from two people you trust, and both cannot be followed at once. Instead of pretending to understand, you ask for the single clear step that matters.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे । तदेकं वद निश्िचत्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे जनार्दन अगर आप कर्मसे बुद्धि ज्ञान को श्रेष्ठ मानते हैं, तो फिर हे केशव मुझे घोर कर्ममें क्यों लगाते हैं  आप अपने मिले हुएसे वचनोंसे मेरी बुद्धिको मोहितसी कर रहे हैं ।  अतः आप निश्चय करके एक बात को कहिये, जिससे मैं कल्याणको प्राप्त हो जाऊँ ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: Your words seem mixed and confusing to me. Tell me one thing clearly, so I may find the highest good.
essence: Confusion ends when the mind asks for one clear direction.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says Krishna's advice feels mixed and confusing. He asks for one clear teaching that will lead him to the highest good.
insight: It shifts the mind from juggling options to demanding a single, workable truth.
modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, phone in hand, unable to decide whether to tell the hard truth. Half-answers only stretch the dread. This verse names the need for one clear direction.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचलोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ । ज्ञानयोगेन सांख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम् ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे निष्पाप अर्जुन इस मनुष्यलोकमें दो प्रकारसे होनेवाली निष्ठा मेरे द्वारा पहले कही गयी है ।  उनमें ज्ञानियोंकी निष्ठा ज्ञानयोगसे और योगियोंकी निष्ठा कर्मयोगसे होती है ॥
english_translation: The divine said: In this world, I have already taught two kinds of steadfast practice: the path of knowledge for the contemplative, and the path of action for the active.
essence: Different natures are steadied by different disciplines.
simple_meaning: There are two valid ways to live steadily: one through understanding, one through action. Different temperaments need different disciplines.
insight: It shifts the mind from searching for one universal method to recognizing the right path for one’s temperament.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a life decision and want one perfect rule to settle everything. Instead, the answer may be simpler: some people need study and reflection, others need disciplined action.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते । न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥
translation: मनुष्य न तो कर्मोंका आरम्भ किये बिना निष्कर्मताको प्राप्त होता है और न कर्मोंके त्यागमात्रसे सिद्धिको ही प्राप्त होता है ॥
english_translation: A person does not reach actionless freedom by avoiding action, nor by renouncing action alone does one reach perfection.
essence: Freedom is not found by escaping action, but by changing your relation to it.
simple_meaning: Freedom does not come from simply stopping action, and perfection does not come from merely giving things up. Real growth requires a deeper way of acting.
insight: It shifts the mind from escape to right engagement: freedom is found in how you act, not in avoiding action itself.
modern_relevance: You quit the project, mute every notification, and hope the pressure disappears. It doesn’t. Relief comes when your relationship to action changes, not when action vanishes.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न हि कश्िचत्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् । कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥
translation: कोई भी मनुष्य किसी भी अवस्थामें क्षणमात्र भी कर्म किये बिना नहीं रह सकता क्योंकि प्रकृतिके परवश हुए सब प्राणियोंसे प्रकृतिजन्य गुण कर्म कराते हैं ॥
english_translation: No one can remain without action even for a moment. Everyone is driven to act by the qualities born of nature.
essence: Inaction is an illusion; nature is already moving you.
simple_meaning: No one can stay inactive forever. The qualities of nature keep pushing every person into action.
insight: It shifts the mind from pretending neutrality to seeing what force is already moving you.
modern_relevance: You sit frozen with your phone in hand, avoiding the email that could change everything. Even that delay is a kind of action. The question is not whether you act, but what is steering you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् । इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥
translation: जो कर्मेन्द्रियों सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियों को हठपूर्वक रोककर मनसे इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंका चिन्तन करता रहता है, वह मूढ़ बुद्धिवाला मनुष्य मिथ्याचारी मिथ्या आचरण करनेवाला कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: One who restrains the organs of action but keeps thinking of sense objects in the mind is deluded and called a hypocrite.
essence: Outer restraint means nothing if the mind still feeds desire.
simple_meaning: Holding back your actions while the mind still chases desire is self-deception. Outer restraint means little without inner discipline.
insight: It shifts attention from outward control to inner honesty. The real task is to align thought and action together.
modern_relevance: You delete the app, but keep checking the craving in your head. You cancel the habit, yet rehearse it all day. The form changed; the attachment did not.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन । कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥
translation: हे अर्जुन जो मनुष्य मनसे इन्द्रियोंपर नियन्त्रण करके आसक्तिरहित होकर निष्काम भावसे समस्त इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा कर्मयोगका आचरण करता है, वही श्रेष्ठ है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, the one who restrains the senses with the mind and begins karma yoga without attachment is श्रेष्ठ.
essence: Self-mastery makes action noble, not the outer task alone.
simple_meaning: The best way to act is to keep the senses under the mind's control and do your work without attachment.
insight: It shifts action from impulse-led reaction to deliberate, disciplined doing.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, make the apology, or walk out of the room. The pull to react is strong, but the cleaner move is to steady the mind first and act without grabbing for the result.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
translation: तू शास्त्रविधिसे नियत किये हुए कर्तव्यकर्म कर क्योंकि कर्म न करनेकी अपेक्षा कर्म करना श्रेष्ठ है तथा कर्म न करनेसे तेरा शरीरनिर्वाह भी सिद्ध नहीं होगा ॥
english_translation: Do the duty prescribed for you. Action is better than inaction, and even your body cannot be sustained by inaction.
essence: Right action is unavoidable; even survival depends on it.
simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna to do the duty assigned to him. Action is better than sitting idle, and even basic life cannot continue through inaction.
insight: It shifts the mind from avoiding discomfort to fulfilling the task already in front of you.
modern_relevance: You are staring at the unanswered message, the apology, the hard resignation email. Waiting for perfect certainty only deepens the knot; action is what loosens it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः । तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसंगः समाचर ॥
translation: यज्ञ कर्तव्यपालन के लिये किये जानेवाले कर्मोंसे अन्यत्र अपने लिये किये जानेवाले कर्मोंमें लगा हुआ यह मनुष्यसमुदाय कर्मोंसे बँधता है, इसलिये हे कुन्तीनन्दन  तू आसक्तिरहित होकर उस यज्ञके लिये ही कर्तव्यकर्म कर ॥
english_translation: Actions done for sacrifice free a person; actions done for personal gain bind. Therefore, Arjuna, do your duty without attachment for that purpose alone.
essence: Work becomes bondage when it is done for yourself.
simple_meaning: Work done only for personal gain creates bondage. Work done as an offering, without attachment, should be done instead.
insight: It shifts effort from personal payoff to clean participation in duty.
modern_relevance: You send the email, then keep checking for praise. The knot tightens when the action is for your ego; it loosens when the action is for what needs doing.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः । अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक् ॥
translation: प्रजापति ब्रह्माजीने सृष्टिके आदिकालमें कर्तव्यकर्मोंके विधानसहित प्रजामनुष्य आदि की रचना करके उनसे प्रधानतया मनुष्योंसे कहा कि तुमलोग इस कर्तव्यके द्वारा सबकी वृद्धि करो और वह कर्तव्यकर्मरूप यज्ञ तुमलोगोंको कर्तव्यपालनकी आवश्यक सामग्री प्रदान करनेवाला हो ।  अपने कर्तव्यकर्मके द्वारा तुमलोग देवताओंको उन्नत करो और वे देवतालोग अपने कर्तव्यके द्वारा तुमलोगोंको उन्नत करें ।  इस प्रकार एकदूसरेको उन्नत करते हुए तुमलोग परम कल्याणको प्राप्त हो जाओगे ॥
english_translation: In the beginning, Prajapati created beings together with sacrifice and said: “By this, you shall prosper. May this sacrifice be the wish-fulfilling cow for you.”
essence: Life flourishes when duty becomes mutual support.
simple_meaning: At the start of creation, Prajapati set up a way of living where sacrifice and duty help all beings flourish. The message is to support life through shared responsibility.
insight: It shifts action from private gain to participation in a shared order.
modern_relevance: You are stocking shelves before dawn, or caring for a parent no one sees. The task feels small, but it belongs to a larger web that lets everyone else keep moving.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः । परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥
translation: प्रजापति ब्रह्माजीने सृष्टिके आदिकालमें कर्तव्यकर्मोंके विधानसहित प्रजामनुष्य आदि की रचना करके उनसे, प्रधानतया मनुष्योंसे कहा कि तुमलोग इस कर्तव्यके द्वारा सबकी वृद्धि करो और वह कर्तव्यकर्मरूप यज्ञ तुमलोगोंको कर्तव्यपालनकी आवश्यक सामग्री प्रदान करनेवाला हो ।  अपने कर्तव्यकर्मके द्वारा तुमलोग देवताओंको उन्नत करो और वे देवतालोग अपने कर्तव्यके द्वारा तुमलोगोंको उन्नत करें ।  इस प्रकार एकदूसरेको उन्नत करते हुए तुमलोग परम कल्याणको प्राप्त हो जाओगे ॥
english_translation: By nurturing the radiant beings through this duty, let them nurture you. Nurturing one another, you will attain the highest good.
essence: Your duty nourishes the whole, and the whole nourishes you back.
simple_meaning: Support the larger order through your actions, and that order will support you in return. Mutual support leads to the highest good.
insight: It shifts action from self-protection to participation in a mutual system of giving and receiving.
modern_relevance: You keep the neighborhood garden alive, and it keeps feeding everyone. The effort feels one-sided until you see how much your own life depends on what you sustain.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः । तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥
translation: यज्ञसे भावित पुष्ट हुए देवता भी तुमलोगोंको बिना माँगे ही कर्तव्यपालनकी आवश्यक सामग्री देते रहेंगे ।  इस प्रकार उन देवताओंसे प्राप्त हुई सामग्रीको दूसरोंकी सेवामें लगाये बिना जो मनुष्य स्वयं ही उसका उपभोग करता है, वह चोर ही है ॥
english_translation: The radiant beings, nourished by sacrifice, will give you the enjoyments you need. One who enjoys their gifts without offering back is a thief.
essence: What is received must be offered back, or it becomes theft.
simple_meaning: The world keeps giving when you participate in shared responsibility. Taking benefits without giving back is treated as theft.
insight: It shifts action from taking to participating in a cycle of return.
modern_relevance: You use the last of the office printer paper, ignore the shared supply closet, and walk away. The verse lands there: what you consume without replenishing was never truly yours.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः । भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥
translation: यज्ञशेष योग का अनुभव करनेवाले श्रेष्ठ मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण पापोंसे मुक्त हो जाते हैं ।  परन्तु जो केवल अपने लिये ही पकाते अर्थात् सब कर्म करते हैं, वे पापीलोग तो पापका ही भक्षण करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who eat the leftovers of sacrifice are freed from all faults. Those who cook only for themselves eat only wrongdoing.
essence: What is offered purifies; what is hoarded for the self corrupts.
simple_meaning: People who take only what remains after offering their work for the larger order are cleansed. People who act only for themselves end up consuming their own wrongdoing.
insight: It shifts action from self-collection to offering, so work becomes clean instead of contaminated by greed.
modern_relevance: You finish dinner and notice you grabbed the best piece before anyone else. That tiny reflex is the same one that makes larger acts feel hollow.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः । यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥
translation: सम्पूर्ण प्राणी अन्नसे उत्पन्न होते हैं ।  अन्न वर्षासे होती है ।  वर्षा यज्ञसे होती है ।  यज्ञ कर्मोंसे निष्पन्न होता है ।  कर्मोंको तू वेदसे उत्पन्न जान और वेदको अक्षरब्रह्मसे प्रकट हुआ जान ।  इसलिये वह सर्वव्यापी परमात्मा यज्ञ कर्तव्यकर्म में नित्य प्रतिष्ठित है ॥
english_translation: All beings arise from food. Food comes from rain. Rain comes from sacrifice. Sacrifice arises from action.
essence: Action sustains the cycle that makes life possible.
simple_meaning: Life depends on a chain: food comes from rain, rain comes from sacrifice, and sacrifice comes from action.
insight: It shifts attention from private consumption to the shared systems your actions sustain.
modern_relevance: You open the fridge after a long week and forget the path behind that meal: weather, work, trade, care. One careless act can still belong to a larger system.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् । तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
translation: सम्पूर्ण प्राणी अन्नसे उत्पन्न होते हैं ।  अन्न वर्षासे होती है ।  वर्षा यज्ञसे होती है ।  यज्ञ कर्मोंसे निष्पन्न होता है ।  कर्मोंको तू वेदसे उत्पन्न जान और वेदको अक्षरब्रह्मसे प्रकट हुआ जान ।  इसलिये वह सर्वव्यापी परमात्मा यज्ञ कर्तव्यकर्म में नित्य प्रतिष्ठित है ॥
english_translation: Know that action comes from the Vedas, and the Vedas come from the imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervading supreme reality is always established in sacrifice.
essence: Right action is not random; it rests in a deeper, sustaining order.
simple_meaning: Action arises from sacred order, that order arises from the imperishable, and the all-pervading supreme reality is rooted in selfless offering.
insight: It shifts action from private ambition to participation in a sacred pattern.
modern_relevance: You are about to make a hard call that affects other people, and the choice feels bigger than your mood. This verse reminds you that right action belongs to a larger order than personal preference.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः । अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ॥
translation: हे पार्थ जो मनुष्य इस लोकमें इस प्रकार परम्परासे प्रचलित सृष्टिचक्रके अनुसार नहीं चलता, वह इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा भोगोंमें रमण करनेवाला अघायु पापमय जीवन बितानेवाला मनुष्य संसारमें व्यर्थ ही जीता है ॥
english_translation: O Partha, the one who does not follow this cycle set in motion here lives in vain, delighting only in the senses and living a life of wrongdoing.
essence: A life detached from duty empties itself from within.
simple_meaning: A person who ignores the world’s proper cycle of action and only chases pleasure ends up living a wasted life.
insight: It shifts the mind from appetite as freedom to responsibility as the condition for a meaningful life.
modern_relevance: You keep scrolling, snacking, and numbing out after a hard day, but something inside feels dead. Krishna names that drift: a life cut off from responsibility begins to waste itself.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः । आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य अपनेआपमें ही रमण करनेवाला और अपनेआपमें ही तृप्त तथा अपनेआपमें ही संतुष्ट है, उसके लिये कोई कर्तव्य नहीं है ॥
english_translation: The person who delights in the true self, is satisfied in the true self, and is content in the true self has no duty left.
essence: Fulfillment in the true self ends the need for striving.
simple_meaning: A person who finds complete fulfillment in the true self does not act from inner lack. Nothing remains to be gained through duty or effort.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing completion through action to resting in inner fullness before acting.
modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the praise, the relationship milestone — and still feel restless. The verse points to a deeper fullness that does not depend on the next achievement.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन । न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्िचदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥
translation: उस कर्मयोगसे सिद्ध हुए महापुरुषका इस संसारमें न तो कर्म करनेसे कोई प्रयोजन रहता है, और न कर्म न करनेसे ही कोई प्रयोजन रहता है, तथा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें किसी भी प्राणीके साथ इसका किञ्चिन्मात्र भी स्वार्थका सम्बन्ध नहीं रहता ॥
english_translation: For the perfected person, no purpose remains in doing, and no purpose remains in not doing. No being in the world is a source of personal gain.
essence: Freedom ends the need to profit from action.
simple_meaning: A person who has reached inner completeness no longer acts for personal gain. Neither action nor inaction adds anything to that person.
insight: It shifts the mind from transaction to freedom: action is no longer a bargain with the world.
modern_relevance: You send the message, make the apology, or walk away from the deal without calculating how it will benefit you. The action stands on its own, even when nothing comes back.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
translation: इसलिये तू निरन्तर आसक्तिरहित होकर कर्तव्यकर्मका भलीभाँति आचरण कर क्योंकि आसक्तिरहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परमात्माको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment; by acting without attachment, a person reaches the supreme.
essence: Freedom comes when action is done without grasping at its reward.
simple_meaning: Keep doing what must be done, but do it without clinging to results. That kind of action leads you to the highest good.
insight: It shifts attention from owning the result to offering the action cleanly.
modern_relevance: You send the message, make the hard apology, or submit the work knowing it may not land how you hope. The act is complete even before the response arrives.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः । लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
translation: राजा जनकजैसे अनेक महापुरुष भी कर्मके द्वारा ही परमसिद्धिको प्राप्त हुए हैं ।  इसलिये लोकसंग्रहको देखते हुए भी तू निष्कामभावसे कर्म करनेके योग्य है ॥
english_translation: Janaka and others attained perfection through action itself. You should act too, while keeping the welfare of the world in view.
essence: Perfection comes through action that serves more than the self.
simple_meaning: Great people like Janaka reached perfection by acting, not by withdrawing. You should also act for the good of the world.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal withdrawal to responsible participation in shared life.
modern_relevance: You are tempted to step back because your decision affects others and you want to stay clean. Krishna says the cleaner move is to act well, because someone else is counting on your example.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः । स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥
translation: श्रेष्ठ मनुष्य जोजो आचरण करता है, दूसरे मनुष्य वैसावैसा ही आचरण करते हैं ।  वह जो कुछ प्रमाण देता है, दूसरे मनुष्य उसीके अनुसार आचरण करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Whatever the best person does, others follow. Whatever standard they set, the world copies.
essence: The highest standard is not spoken; it is copied.
simple_meaning: People copy the conduct of those they admire. A respected person's actions become the standard others imitate.
insight: It shifts attention from private morality to public influence: your conduct becomes a template for others.
modern_relevance: A parent answers a rude message with calm. A child sees it, and that response becomes normal. People learn more from what you repeatedly do than from what you say.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन । नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ॥
translation: हे पार्थ मुझे तीनों लोकोंमें न तो कुछ कर्तव्य है और न कोई प्राप्त करनेयोग्य वस्तु अप्राप्त है, फिर भी मैं कर्तव्यकर्ममें ही लगा रहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: O Partha, there is nothing in the three worlds that I must do, and nothing I have not yet gained that must be gained. Yet I remain engaged in action.
essence: Even the fulfilled keep working, because action need not come from lack.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he has no unfinished duty and nothing left to gain, yet he still stays active.
insight: It shifts action from personal gain to steady example and responsibility.
modern_relevance: You’ve already won the argument in your head, but you still show up for the hard conversation. You do it not to get something, but because the action itself matters.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः । मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥
translation: हे पार्थ अगर मैं किसी समय सावधान होकर कर्तव्यकर्म न करूँ तो बड़ी हानि हो जाय क्योंकि मनुष्य सब प्रकारसे मेरे ही मार्गका अनुसरण करते हैं ।  यदि मैं कर्म न करूँ, तो ये सब मनुष्य नष्टभ्रष्ट हो जायँ और मैं वर्णसंकरताको करनेवाला होऊँ तथा इस समस्त प्रजाको नष्ट करनेवाला बनूँ ॥
english_translation: For if I ever stopped acting with care, people would follow my path in every way, Arjuna.
essence: Careless withdrawal by the highest would unravel everyone below.
simple_meaning: Krishna says that if he stopped doing his duty carefully, people would copy that neglect and society would suffer.
insight: It shifts attention from private freedom to public responsibility: your conduct becomes a model others unconsciously follow.
modern_relevance: A parent says, “Do your homework,” while scrolling on a phone all evening. The child learns the real lesson from the behavior, not the lecture.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् । सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ॥
translation: हे पार्थ  अगर मैं किसी समय सावधान होकर कर्तव्यकर्म न करूँ तो बड़ी हानि हो जाय क्योंकि मनुष्य सब प्रकारसे मेरे ही मार्गका अनुसरण करते हैं ।  यदि मैं कर्म न करूँ, तो ये सब मनुष्य नष्टभ्रष्ट हो जायँ और मैं वर्णसंकरताको करनेवाला तथा इस समस्त प्रजाको नष्ट करनेवाला बनूँ ॥
english_translation: If I did not act, these worlds would fall into ruin. I would create disorder and destroy these people.
essence: Even the highest must act to prevent disorder.
simple_meaning: Krishna says that even he must keep acting, because if he stopped, society would fall into disorder and people would be harmed.
insight: It shifts duty from personal preference to responsibility for the wider order.
modern_relevance: You skip the hard conversation, hoping the problem will wait. It doesn't. Silence spreads confusion, and everyone around you ends up paying for your avoidance.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत । कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्िचकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम् ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन कर्ममें आसक्त हुए अज्ञानीजन जिस प्रकार कर्म करते हैं, आसक्तिरहित विद्वान भी लोकसंग्रह करना चाहता हुआ उसी प्रकार कर्म करे ।  तत्त्वज्ञ महापुरुष कर्मोंमें आसक्तिवाले अज्ञानी मनुष्योंकी बुद्धिमें भ्रम उत्पन्न न करे, प्रत्युत स्वयं समस्त कर्मोंको अच्छी तरहसे करता हुआ उनसे भी वैसे ही करवाये ॥
english_translation: As the ignorant act with attachment to action, so should the wise act without attachment, seeking the welfare of the world.
essence: Wisdom keeps acting, but never for personal gain.
simple_meaning: A wise person should keep acting, but without clinging to the results. The point is to support the world, not feed ego.
insight: It shifts action from self-serving ambition to responsible participation for the good of others.
modern_relevance: You’re the senior person in a room full of anxious newcomers, and everyone is watching how you handle the pressure. Stay active, stay steady, and let your example carry the room.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् । जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान् युक्तः समाचरन् ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन कर्ममें आसक्त हुए अज्ञानीजन जिस प्रकार कर्म करते हैं आसक्तिरहित विद्वान भी लोकसंग्रह करना चाहता हुआ उसी प्रकार कर्म करे ।  सावधान तत्त्वज्ञ महापुरुष कर्मोंमें आसक्तिवाले अज्ञानी मनुष्योंकी बुद्धिमें भ्रम उत्पन्न न करे, प्रत्युत स्वयं समस्त कर्मोंको अच्छी तरहसे करता हुआ उनसे भी वैसे ही करवाये ॥
english_translation: An awakened person should not unsettle the minds of those attached to action. Instead, acting skillfully, such a person should engage them in all work.
essence: Wisdom should steady people, not shake their footing.
simple_meaning: A wise person should not confuse people who are still attached to action. Instead, by acting well, they should guide others into right action.
insight: It shifts the aim from proving insight to preserving others’ ability to act well.
modern_relevance: You’ve finally learned a hard lesson, and someone around you is still clinging to the old pattern. Blasting them with your clarity may only make them resist harder.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः । अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते ॥
translation: सम्पूर्ण कर्म सब प्रकारसे प्रकृतिके गुणोंद्वारा किये जाते हैं परन्तु अहंकारसे मोहित अन्तःकरणवाला अज्ञानी मनुष्य मैं कर्ता हूँ  ऐसा मानता है ॥
english_translation: All actions are carried out in every way by the qualities of nature. Deluded by ego, a person thinks, 'I am the doer.'
essence: The doer is imagined; action belongs to nature's forces.
simple_meaning: Actions happen through the forces of nature, not through the false sense of 'I am the doer.' Ego creates the illusion of authorship.
insight: It shifts responsibility from ego-ownership to clear participation in what is already unfolding.
modern_relevance: You replay a painful conversation in your head and keep editing your part in it. Krishna cuts through that loop: the event unfolded through many causes, not one heroic or guilty self.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः । गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ॥
translation: हे महाबाहो गुणविभाग और कर्मविभागको तत्त्वसे जाननेवाला महापुरुष सम्पूर्ण गुण ही गुणोंमें बरत रहे हैं  ऐसा मानकर उनमें आसक्त नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: The one who truly understands the division of qualities and actions does not cling, seeing that qualities act upon qualities.
essence: Seeing action as nature's movement ends attachment.
simple_meaning: A person who understands how qualities and actions work sees that nature is doing the acting, not the separate ego. That understanding removes attachment.
insight: It shifts attention from personal ownership of action to clear observation of how nature operates.
modern_relevance: You watch yourself getting pulled into a family argument, then catch the pattern before speaking. The pause changes everything: you stop defending a self-image and start seeing the forces at work.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु । तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत् ॥
translation: प्रकृतिजन्य गुणोंसे अत्यन्त मोहित हुए अज्ञानी मनुष्य गुणों और कर्मोंमें आसक्त रहते हैं ।  उन पूर्णतया न समझनेवाले मन्दबुद्धि अज्ञानियोंको पूर्णतया जाननेवाला ज्ञानी मनुष्य विचलित न करे ॥
english_translation: The ignorant, deluded by the qualities of nature, cling to actions born of those qualities. The wise should not unsettle those who do not yet understand fully.
essence: Clarity should guide confusion, not crush it.
simple_meaning: People lost in the forces of nature become attached to action and its results. A person who understands more deeply should not shake them up unnecessarily.
insight: It teaches restraint in teaching: see confusion clearly, but do not weaponize your clarity.
modern_relevance: You finally understand a hard truth, but the person beside you is still reacting from fear. Pushing too fast can break trust before understanding has a chance to grow.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा । निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥
translation: तू विवेकवती बुद्धिके द्वारा सम्पूर्ण कर्तव्यकर्मोंको मेरे अर्पण करके कामना, ममता और संतापरहित होकर युद्धरूप कर्तव्यकर्मको कर ॥
english_translation: Surrender all actions to me with the disciplined mind. Free from desire, possessiveness, and sorrow, fight.
essence: Action becomes free when you stop claiming its results.
simple_meaning: Give every action inwardly to the divine, then do your duty without craving results, without clinging, and without inner distress.
insight: It shifts action from self-protection to offering, so duty can be done without mental strain.
modern_relevance: You send the message, make the hard call, or walk into the tense room knowing the outcome is not yours to own. What remains is clean action.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः । श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य दोषदृष्टिसे रहित होकर श्रद्धापूर्वक मेरे इस पूर्वश्लोकमें वर्णित मतका सदा अनुसरण करते हैं, वे भी कर्मोंके बन्धनसे मुक्त हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who always follow this teaching of Mine with trust and without fault-finding are freed from the bonds of action.
essence: Trusting the teaching frees action from its binding force.
simple_meaning: People who follow Krishna's teaching with trust and without resentment or criticism are freed from the binding effects of action.
insight: It shifts the mind from skeptical paralysis to trustful practice.
modern_relevance: You hear advice that could change your life, but your first reflex is to pick it apart. This verse says the door opens when you stop resisting long enough to try.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् । सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ॥
translation: परन्तु जो मनुष्य मेरे इस मतमें दोषदृष्टि करते हुए इसका अनुष्ठान नहीं करते, उन सम्पूर्ण ज्ञानोंमें मोहित और अविवेकी मनुष्योंको नष्ट हुए ही समझो ॥
english_translation: But those who, finding fault with this teaching, do not follow it—know them to be deluded in all knowledge and ruined in understanding.
essence: Rejecting clear guidance leaves the mind stranded.
simple_meaning: People who reject this teaching out of fault-finding lose clear understanding and become confused. The problem is not the teaching; it is the closed mind that refuses to practise it.
insight: It shifts the mind from cynical refusal to disciplined practice.
modern_relevance: You hear advice that could help, but your first reaction is, “That won’t work.” The real trap is not the advice itself — it is the reflex to dismiss what might free you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि । प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥
translation: सम्पूर्ण प्राणी प्रकृतिको प्राप्त होते हैं ।  ज्ञानी महापुरुष भी अपनी प्रकृतिके अनुसार चेष्टा करता है ।  फिर इसमें किसीका हठ क्या करेगा ॥
english_translation: Even the wise act according to their own nature. All beings follow nature; what can restraint do?
essence: Nature drives behavior; force alone cannot overrule it.
simple_meaning: Even a wise person acts according to their own nature. Every living being follows its nature, so force alone cannot change that.
insight: It shifts attention from moral self-blame to honest observation of ingrained tendencies.
modern_relevance: You promise yourself you will not check the phone again, then your hand reaches for it before you notice. Krishna points to the harder truth: habits run deep, and brute force alone rarely wins.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ । तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥
translation: इन्द्रियइन्द्रियके अर्थमें प्रत्येक इन्द्रियके प्रत्येक विषयमें मनुष्यके राग और द्वेष व्यवस्थासे अनुकूलता और प्रतिकूलताको लेकर स्थित हैं ।  मनुष्यको उन दोनोंके वशमें नहीं होना चाहिये क्योंकि वे दोनों ही इसके पारमार्थिक मार्गमें विघ्न डालनेवाले शत्रु हैं ॥
english_translation: Attachment and aversion sit in every sense-object. Do not come under their power, for they are your enemies on the path.
essence: Freedom begins when attraction and aversion stop steering action.
simple_meaning: Craving and dislike appear in every sense experience. Do not let either one control your choices, because both block the path forward.
insight: It shifts attention from impulse-driven reaction to conscious choice before action.
modern_relevance: You open a message and feel the instant urge to defend yourself, or to ignore it completely. That split-second pull is exactly what this verse warns against.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
translation: अच्छी तरह आचरणमें लाये हुए दूसरेके धर्मसे गुणोंकी कमीवाला अपना धर्म श्रेष्ठ है ।  अपने धर्ममें तो मरना भी कल्याणकारक है और दूसरेका धर्म भयको देनेवाला है ॥
english_translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than another's duty well performed. Better death in one's own duty; another's duty is dangerous.
essence: Imperfect right action is safer than perfect imitation.
simple_meaning: Your own responsibility matters more than copying someone else's path. Even if you do it imperfectly, it is better than doing another person's role well.
insight: It shifts attention from imitation to rightful action. The measure is not polish, but fidelity to one's own role.
modern_relevance: You are in a room full of people telling you what you should be: the calmer sibling, the louder leader, the easier partner. The verse cuts through the comparison and asks what is actually yours to do.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचअथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः । अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे वार्ष्णेय  फिर यह मनुष्य न चाहता हुआ भी जबर्दस्ती लगाये हुएकी तरह किससे प्रेरित होकर पापका आचरण करता है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: O descendant of the Vrishni clan, what drives a person to commit wrongdoing, even unwillingly, as if forced?
essence: Compulsion has a cause, and Arjuna wants to name it.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks what makes a person do wrong even when they do not want to, as if some force is pushing them.
insight: It shifts attention from self-blame to investigating the hidden force behind compulsive action.
modern_relevance: You promise yourself you will not send that text, open that tab, or say that cutting remark. Then you do it anyway. The question is no longer moral blame — it is: what is driving me?
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचकाम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः । महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  रजोगुणसे उत्पन्न हुआ यह काम ही क्रोध है ।  यह बहुत खानेवाला और महापापी है ।  इस विषयमें तू इसको ही वैरी जान ॥
english_translation: Krishna said: Desire, born of rajas, turns into anger. It is all-consuming and deeply destructive. Know it as your enemy here.
essence: Desire is not harmless; it mutates into the force that ruins judgment.
simple_meaning: Desire, born from restlessness, turns into anger and destroys clarity. Krishna says to recognize it as an enemy before it takes over.
insight: It shifts the mind from blaming others to spotting the inner impulse that distorts action.
modern_relevance: You open a message, feel ignored, and the irritation hardens into a cutting reply. The first spark looked harmless; the full fire changes everything.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च । यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥
translation: जैसे धुएँसे अग्नि और मैलसे दर्पण ढक जाता है तथा जैसे जेरसे गर्भ ढका रहता है, ऐसे ही उस कामके द्वारा यह ज्ञान  विवेक ढका हुआ है ॥
english_translation: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and a womb by a membrane, so clear seeing is covered by desire.
essence: Clear seeing is not destroyed; it is simply covered.
simple_meaning: Desire hides clear seeing just as smoke hides fire, dust hides a mirror, and a womb-covering hides an embryo.
insight: It shifts attention from searching for new answers to removing the obstruction already blocking clear judgment.
modern_relevance: You know the right thing to say, but the message sits unopened while anger blurs your judgment. The clarity is still there; something is clouding it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा । कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥
translation: और हे कुन्तीनन्दन  इस अग्निके समान कभी तृप्त न होनेवाले और विवेकियोंके नित्य वैरी इस कामके द्वारा मनुष्यका विवेक ढका हुआ है ॥
english_translation: O son of Kunti, wisdom is covered by this desire, the eternal enemy of the wise, as fire is never satisfied.
essence: Desire does not just tempt; it hides wisdom itself.
simple_meaning: Desire hides clear understanding. It never feels satisfied, and it keeps working against the wise like an unquenchable fire.
insight: It shifts attention from fighting symptoms to seeing desire as the force that clouds judgment.
modern_relevance: You open one more tab, then another, then another, hoping the urge will settle. It does not. It keeps your judgment fogged until you notice what is driving you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते । एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ॥
translation: इन्द्रियाँ, मन और बुद्धि इस कामके वासस्थान कहे गये हैं ।  यह काम इन इन्द्रियाँ, मन और बुद्धि के द्वारा ज्ञानको ढककर देहाभिमानी मनुष्यको मोहित करता है ॥
english_translation: The senses, the mind, and the discerning mind are said to be its seat. Through them, it deludes the embodied person by veiling understanding.
essence: Desire conquers by hijacking the mind's own instruments.
simple_meaning: Desire works through the senses, the restless mind, and the discerning mind. It clouds understanding and makes a person act blindly.
insight: It teaches you to watch where desire enters so you can interrupt the slide before judgment is lost.
modern_relevance: You open a message you knew would pull you off course, and suddenly the whole evening is gone. The pull did not begin in the app; it began in the chain of attention.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ । पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥
translation: इसलिये हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  तू सबसे पहले इन्द्रियोंको वशमें करके इस ज्ञान और विज्ञानका नाश करनेवाले महान् पापी कामको अवश्य ही बलपूर्वक मार डाल ॥
english_translation: Therefore, O best of the Bharatas, first control the senses, and then destroy this great sinner, the destroyer of knowledge and wisdom.
essence: Sense-control comes before clear action.
simple_meaning: Control the senses first, because unchecked craving destroys clear understanding. The real enemy is not outside you but the force that clouds judgment from within.
insight: It shifts action from reactive impulse to deliberate restraint, so judgment can return before choice.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that could end the relationship, or keep the promise that costs you comfort. Your hands shake over the phone. Krishna's advice is simple: stop the rush of impulse first, then choose.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः । मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥
translation: इन्द्रियोंको स्थूलशरीरसे पर श्रेष्ठ, सबल, प्रकाशक, व्यापक तथा सूक्ष्म कहते हैं ।  इन्द्रियोंसे पर मन है, मनसे भी पर बुद्धि है औऱ जो बुद्धिसे भी पर है, वह काम है ।  इस तरह बुद्धिसे पर  काम को जानकर अपने द्वारा अपनेआपको वशमें करके हे महाबाहो  तू इस कामरूप दुर्जय शत्रुको मार डाल ॥
english_translation: The senses are higher than the body; the mind is higher than the senses; the discerning mind is higher than the mind. What is beyond the discerning mind, however, is desire.
essence: Desire sits above reason, so mastery must begin earlier.
simple_meaning: The senses are above the body, the mind is above the senses, and the discerning mind is above the mind. Beyond even the discerning mind stands desire, which must be mastered.
insight: It teaches you to locate impulse before it becomes action, and to use discernment before desire takes over.
modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message and lose twenty minutes. The pull did not start in your hands; it rose from deeper layers. You can catch it earlier.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना । जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥
translation: इन्द्रियोंको स्थूलशरीरसे पर श्रेष्ठ, सबल, प्रकाशक, व्यापक तथा सूक्ष्म कहते हैं ।  इन्द्रियोंसे पर मन है, मनसे भी पर बुद्धि है औऱ जो बुद्धिसे भी पर है वह काम है ।  इस तरह बुद्धिसे पर  काम को जानकर अपने द्वारा अपनेआपको वशमें करके हे महाबाहो  तू इस कामरूप दुर्जय शत्रुको मार डाल ॥
english_translation: Thus, knowing the higher beyond the intellect, steady the lower self by the higher self, and destroy that enemy in the form of desire, which is hard to conquer.
essence: Desire loses power when the higher mind takes command.
simple_meaning: Recognize that desire is not the highest force in you. Use your deeper discernment to steady yourself and overcome it.
insight: It shifts the response from suppressing desire to leading with discernment.
modern_relevance: You open the app to check one message and end up scrolling for an hour. The urge feels automatic, but another part of you can still take the wheel.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचइमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम् । विवस्वान् मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत् ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  मैंने इस अविनाशी योगको सूर्यसे कहा था ।  फिर सूर्यने अपने पुत्र वैवस्वत मनुसे कहा और मनुने अपने पुत्र राजा इक्ष्वाकुसे कहा ॥
english_translation: The Lord said: I taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvan. Vivasvan taught it to Manu, and Manu taught it to Ikshvaku.
essence: Timeless wisdom survives by being passed on, not newly invented.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he taught this timeless yoga to the sun-god, who passed it to Manu, then to Ikshvaku. The teaching is ancient and preserved through a lineage.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating wisdom as personal invention to seeing it as a preserved lineage of understanding.
modern_relevance: You inherit a practice from a teacher who learned it from someone before them, and they from someone before them. What feels new to you may be older than your doubts.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः । स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप ॥
translation: हे परंतप  इस तरह परम्परासे प्राप्त इस कर्मयोग को राजर्षियोंने जाना ।  परन्तु बहुत समय बीत जानेके कारण वह योग इस मनुष्यलोकमें लुप्तप्राय हो गया ॥
english_translation: O scorcher of foes, this yoga was known by the royal sages through an unbroken lineage. In the course of great time, this yoga was lost in this world.
essence: Even timeless wisdom disappears when no one keeps receiving it.
simple_meaning: This ancient yoga was passed down from teacher to student and known by wise rulers, but over time it faded from the world.
insight: It shifts attention from private belief to living lineage, showing that wisdom survives only when it is carried forward.
modern_relevance: A skill your grandfather knew may survive only as a half-remembered family story. Without living transmission, even the most valuable wisdom can vanish between generations.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः । भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥
translation: तू मेरा भक्त और प्रिय सखा है, इसलिये वही यह पुरातन योग आज मैंने तुझसे कहा है क्योंकि यह बड़ा उत्तम रहस्य है ॥
english_translation: Because you are my devotee and my friend, I have taught you today this ancient yoga. It is a supreme secret.
essence: The deepest teaching opens only to devotion and trust.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is teaching Arjuna an ancient teaching because Arjuna is both devoted and close to him. This teaching is a rare and highest secret.
insight: It shifts the mind from demanding proof to recognising that deep understanding ripens through trust and relationship.
modern_relevance: A mentor finally tells you the hard truth after years of trust, not because you asked perfectly, but because you are ready to hear it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचअपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः । कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  आपका जन्म तो अभीका है और सूर्यका जन्म बहुत पुराना है अतः आपने ही सृष्टिके आदिमें सूर्यसे यह योग कहा था  यह बात मैं कैसे समझूँ ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: Your birth is recent, while the birth of the Sun is ancient. How am I to understand that you taught this yoga at the beginning of creation?
essence: Doubt becomes the doorway to deeper seeing.
simple_meaning: Arjuna doubts Krishna's claim. Krishna is younger than the Sun, so Arjuna cannot see how Krishna could have taught this yoga at the beginning of creation.
insight: It shifts the mind from passive acceptance to careful inquiry before belief.
modern_relevance: You hear a claim that sounds impossible from someone standing right in front of you. Instead of pretending you understand, you ask the hard question that exposes the gap.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचबहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन । तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे परन्तप अर्जुन  मेरे और तेरे बहुतसे जन्म हो चुके हैं ।  उन सबको मैं जानता हूँ, पर तू नहीं जानता ॥
english_translation: Krishna said: Many births of yours and mine have passed, Arjuna. I know them all, but you do not, enemy-burner.
essence: Your memory is partial; the divine awareness is not.
simple_meaning: Krishna says that both of them have passed through many births, but only Krishna remembers them all. Arjuna does not remember his own past births.
insight: It shifts the mind from assuming its own memory is complete to recognising a wider continuity of existence.
modern_relevance: You argue from memory, but the other person sees the whole pattern. In a family conflict, you remember only the last hurt; the deeper story stretches far beyond what you can hold.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन् । प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय संभवाम्यात्ममायया ॥
translation: मैं अजन्मा और अविनाशीस्वरूप होते हुए भी तथा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंका ईश्वर होते हुए भी अपनी प्रकृतिको अधीन करके अपनी योगमायासे प्रकट होता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Though unborn and imperishable, and though I am the lord of all beings, I manifest myself by controlling my own nature through my own power of appearance.
essence: The unborn can still appear without ceasing to be free.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is unborn and imperishable, yet still appears in the world by using his own power over nature.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Krishna as a historical figure to seeing incarnation as conscious manifestation.
modern_relevance: Someone you trust suddenly acts in a way you never expected, and you wonder what is real. This verse says appearance can hide power: not everything that shows up is bound the way it seems.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत । अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशी अर्जुन जबजब धर्मकी हानि और अधर्मकी वृद्धि होती है, तबतब ही मैं अपनेआपको साकाररूपसे प्रकट करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and a rise of adharma, I manifest myself.
essence: When dharma collapses, the divine steps into history.
simple_meaning: Whenever righteous order declines and wrongdoing rises, Krishna says he manifests in the world to restore balance.
insight: It shifts the mind from helplessness to confidence that disorder is not the final word.
modern_relevance: A family, company, or community starts normalizing what once felt unacceptable. The slide feels slow, then sudden. This verse says the turning point is not invisible — the force that restores order is already at work.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् । धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे ॥
translation: साधुओंभक्तों की रक्षा करनेके लिये, पापकर्म करनेवालोंका विनाश करनेके लिये और धर्मकी भलीभाँति स्थापना करनेके लिये मैं युगयुगमें प्रकट हुआ करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: For the protection of the righteous, for the destruction of wrongdoers, and for the establishment of dharma, I appear age after age.
essence: The divine returns whenever order must be restored.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he appears again and again to protect the good, stop wrongdoing, and restore dharma.
insight: It shifts the mind from passive despair to trust in restorative action.
modern_relevance: When a family system is poisoned by one cruel person, or a workplace has become toxic, you want to believe repair is still possible. This verse insists that protection and restoration are not fantasies.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः । त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन ॥
translation: हे अर्जुन  मेरे जन्म और कर्म दिव्य हैं ।  इस प्रकार मेरे जन्म और कर्मको जो मनुष्य तत्त्वसे जान लेता अर्थात् दृढ़तापूर्वक मान लेता है, वह शरीरका त्याग करके पुनर्जन्मको प्राप्त नहीं होता, प्रत्युत मुझे प्राप्त होता है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, my birth and action are divine. One who truly understands this does not take birth again after leaving the body, but comes to me.
essence: Seeing Krishna truly ends the cycle of return.
simple_meaning: Krishna says his birth and actions are not ordinary. Whoever understands their divine nature reaches him and is not born again.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Krishna as a person to recognising divine action in human form.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary, yet their presence changes everything. The mind that sees only the surface misses the deeper reality already shaping the moment.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः । बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥
translation: राग, भय और क्रोधसे सर्वथा रहित, मेरेमें ही तल्लीन, मेरे ही आश्रित तथा ज्ञानरूप तपसे पवित्र हुए बहुतसे भक्त मेरे भाव स्वरूप को प्राप्त हो चुके हैं ॥
english_translation: Many, purified by the austerity of knowledge, free from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in Me and taking refuge in Me, have attained My being.
essence: Purified minds reach what fear and craving cannot.
simple_meaning: People who shed attachment, fear, and anger, and stay centered in the divine, become purified through knowledge and reach that divine state.
insight: It shifts attention from outer achievement to inner purification as the condition for transformation.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, make the apology, or walk away from what is familiar. The shaking in your chest matters less than whether fear, anger, and clinging are still steering.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् । मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन  जो भक्त जिस प्रकार मेरी शरण लेते हैं, मैं उन्हें उसी प्रकार आश्रय देता हूँ क्योंकि सभी मनुष्य सब प्रकारसे मेरे मार्गका अनुकरण करते हैं ॥
english_translation: As people approach Me, so I respond to them. All people follow My path in every way, O Arjuna.
essence: The divine response matches the way you come forward.
simple_meaning: People meet the divine according to their own approach, and the divine responds accordingly. Everyone ultimately follows that same higher path, even if they do it unconsciously.
insight: It shifts the mind from demanding one correct approach to recognizing that sincerity itself shapes the encounter.
modern_relevance: You finally admit you need help, but you do it half-defensively, expecting rejection. The response you receive often mirrors the honesty, openness, or resistance you bring.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः । क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा ॥
translation: कर्मोंकी सिद्धि फल चाहनेवाले मनुष्य देवताओंकी उपासना किया करते हैं क्योंकि इस मनुष्यलोकमें कर्मोंसे उत्पन्न होनेवाली सिद्धि जल्दी मिल जाती है ॥
english_translation: People who want quick success worship radiant beings, because results from action come quickly in the human world.
essence: Desire for quick success makes people chase fast-acting powers.
simple_meaning: People who want immediate success often turn to lesser powers for help, because in the human world action can produce quick results.
insight: It shifts attention from craving immediate payoff to seeing why the mind reaches for shortcuts.
modern_relevance: You refresh the app after sending the message, hoping for an instant reply. That hunger for speed can push you toward shortcuts, hacks, and quick fixes that never last.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः । तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम् ॥
translation: मेरे द्वारा गुणों और कर्मोंके विभागपूर्वक चारों वर्णोंकी रचना की गयी है ।  उससृष्टिरचना आदि का कर्ता होनेपर भी मुझ अव्यय रमेश्वरको तू अकर्ता जान ।  कारण कि कर्मोंके फलमें मेरी स्पृहा नहीं है, इसलिये मुझे कर्म लिप्त नहीं करते ।  इस प्रकार जो मुझे तत्त्वसे जान लेता है, वह भी कर्मोंसे नहीं बँधता ॥
english_translation: The four social orders were created by Me according to qualities and actions. Though I am their maker, know Me as the unchanging non-doer.
essence: The source of order stands outside the order it creates.
simple_meaning: The four social orders arise from qualities and actions, but Krishna says he remains the unchanging one who is not bound by creation.
insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with social form to seeing the unchanging awareness behind all roles.
modern_relevance: You are handed a role, a label, a family pattern, a job title, and everyone acts as if that is all you are. This verse says the structure may shape action, but it does not imprison the one who sees clearly.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा । इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते ॥
translation: मेरे द्वारा गुणों और कर्मोंके विभागपूर्वक चारों वर्णोंकी रचना की गयी है ।  उससृष्टिरचना आदि का कर्ता होनेपर भी मुझ अव्यय परमेश्वरको तू अकर्ता जान ।  कारण कि कर्मोंके फलमें मेरी स्पृहा नहीं है, इसलिये मुझे कर्म लिप्त नहीं करते ।  इस प्रकार जो मुझे तत्त्वसे जान लेता है, वह भी कर्मोंसे नहीं बँधता ॥
english_translation: Actions do not stain me, and I do not crave their fruits. One who knows me this way is not bound by actions.
essence: Knowing the action is not yours to possess breaks its grip.
simple_meaning: Actions do not affect Krishna, because he has no desire for their results. Anyone who understands this deeply is also freed from being bound by action.
insight: It shifts the mind from ownership of results to freedom in action.
modern_relevance: You send the message, make the hard call, or finish the surgery, then wait for the reaction. The verse says your hands can stay clean even when the outcome is beyond you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः । कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम् ॥
translation: पूर्वकालके मुमुक्षुओंने भी इस प्रकार जानकर कर्म किये हैं, इसलिये तू भी पूर्वजोंके द्वारा सदासे किये जानेवाले कर्मोंको ही उन्हींकी तरह कर ॥
english_translation: Even seekers of freedom acted after knowing this. Therefore, do the work that your ancestors always did.
essence: Right action is the path even for those seeking freedom.
simple_meaning: People seeking freedom acted in this way before you. So you should do the same rightful work that has long been done.
insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to inherited responsibility: act because the work is right, not because it feels easy.
modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, phone in hand, about to tell the truth no one wants. The path is not to escape the hard duty, but to do it cleanly.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः । तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥
translation: कर्म क्या है और अकर्म क्या है  इस प्रकार इस विषयमें विद्वान् भी मोहित हो जाते हैं ।  अतः वह कर्मतत्त्व मैं तुम्हें भलीभाँति कहूँगा, जिसको जानकर तू अशुभ संसारबन्धन से मुक्त हो जायगा ॥
english_translation: What is action, and what is inaction? Even the wise are confused here. I will explain that action to you, knowing which you will be freed from what is harmful.
essence: Clear seeing about action is what breaks bondage.
simple_meaning: Even intelligent people get confused about what action and inaction really mean. Krishna says he will explain it clearly so Arjuna can be freed from harmful bondage.
insight: It shifts the mind from guessing about action to learning its true structure.
modern_relevance: You stand at the edge of a hard choice and realize you do not even know what the right kind of action looks like. Before moving, you need clarity, not more noise.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः । अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः ॥
translation: कर्मका तत्त्व भी जानना चाहिये और अकर्मका तत्त्व भी जानना चाहिये तथा विकर्मका तत्त्व भी जानना चाहिये क्योंकि कर्मकी गति गहन है ॥
english_translation: Action, forbidden action, and inaction must all be understood, because the movement of action is hard to grasp.
essence: Action cannot be judged quickly; its true pattern is subtle.
simple_meaning: You must understand action, wrong action, and inaction, because the way action works is subtle and difficult to see.
insight: It shifts the mind from automatic reaction to careful discrimination before acting.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, sign the form, or walk away — and every option feels morally tangled. This verse says the first task is to see clearly, not rush blindly.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः । स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य कर्ममें अकर्म देखता है और जो अकर्ममें कर्म देखता है, वह मनुष्योंमें बुद्धिमान् है, योगी है और सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंको करनेवाला है ॥
english_translation: One who sees action in inaction, and inaction in action, is wise among people; that person is disciplined and complete in action.
essence: Freedom can live inside action, and bondage can hide inside stillness.
simple_meaning: A truly wise person sees that outward action can be inwardly free, and apparent inaction can still hide attachment or effort.
insight: It shifts attention from outward motion to the inner state from which action arises.
modern_relevance: You sit in a silent room after sending the message that may end a relationship. Nothing looks dramatic from outside, yet everything has changed. This verse names that hidden kind of action.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः । ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः ॥
translation: जिसके सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंके आरम्भ संकल्प और कामनासे रहित हैं तथा जिसके सम्पूर्ण कर्म ज्ञानरूपी अग्निसे जल गये हैं, उसको ज्ञानिजन भी पण्डित बुद्धिमान् कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: The wise call that person learned whose actions begin without desire or personal planning, and whose deeds are burned by the fire of knowledge.
essence: Knowledge frees action from craving and leaves no binding trace.
simple_meaning: A truly wise person starts actions without craving or mental scheming, and knowledge has already burned up the binding force of those actions.
insight: It shifts action from desire-driven effort to intention-free clarity, where knowledge dissolves the binding residue of doing.
modern_relevance: You send the difficult message after checking your motives one last time. Not to win, not to be praised, not to control the result — only because it is the clean thing to do.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः । कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥
translation: जो कर्म और फलकी आसक्तिका त्याग करके आश्रयसे रहित और सदा तृप्त है, वह कर्मोंमें अच्छी तरह लगा हुआ भी वास्तवमें कुछ भी नहीं करता ॥
english_translation: One who has abandoned attachment to the fruits of action, remains ever content, and depends on nothing, does nothing at all even while fully engaged in action.
essence: Action loses its grip when nothing in you waits to possess its fruit.
simple_meaning: A person can stay fully active and still be inwardly free by dropping attachment to results and resting in inner contentment.
insight: It shifts attention from ownership of results to freedom within action.
modern_relevance: You send the message, make the call, or resign from the safe job — and then you stop chasing the reaction. The clean act is enough.
speaker: Krishna
