verse_text: निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः । शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
translation: जिसका शरीर और अन्तःकरण अच्छी तरहसे वशमें किया हुआ है, जिसने सब प्रकारके संग्रहका परित्याग कर दिया है, ऐसा आशारहित कर्मयोगी केवल शरीरसम्बन्धी कर्म करता हुआ भी पापको प्राप्त नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: One who has no hope, who has controlled the body and mind, and who has given up all possessions, does only bodily action and incurs no fault.
essence: Freedom from clinging keeps action untouched.
simple_meaning: A person who has no craving, controls the body and mind, and lets go of possessions can act without being stained by wrongdoing.
insight: It shifts action from possession and anxiety to clean, necessary doing.
modern_relevance: You sign the resignation letter, delete the backup plan, and still keep your hands steady. The fear is there, but it no longer owns the action.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥
translation: जो कर्मयोगी फल की इच्छा के बिना, अपनेआप जो कुछ मिल जाय, उसमें सन्तुष्ट रहता है और जो ईर्ष्यासे रहित, द्वन्द्वोंसे अतीत तथा सिद्धि और असिद्धिमें सम है, वह कर्म करते हुए भी उससे नहीं बँधता ॥
english_translation: Content with whatever comes by itself, beyond opposites, free from envy, equal in success and failure, such a person is not bound even while acting.
essence: Equal-minded action leaves no hook for bondage.
simple_meaning: A person who is satisfied with whatever comes naturally, stays calm through ups and downs, and does not envy others remains free even while working.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing results to staying even-minded while acting.
modern_relevance: You sent the message, waited, and saw the outcome go sideways. The old urge is to compare, resent, or replay everything. This verse says the work can stay yours without the emotional leash.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः । यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते ॥
translation: जिसकी आसक्ति सर्वथा मिट गयी है, जो मुक्त हो गया है, जिसकी बुद्धि स्वरूपके ज्ञानमें स्थित है, ऐसे केवल यज्ञके लिये कर्म करनेवाले मनुष्यके सम्पूर्ण कर्म विलीन हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: For one who has given up attachment, is freed, and whose mind rests in knowledge, all action melts away when done only for sacrifice.
essence: Action loses its grip when it becomes offering, not possession.
simple_meaning: When attachment is gone and the mind rests in clear understanding, work done as an offering no longer binds a person.
insight: It shifts action from self-protection to offering, so effort no longer leaves a chain of consequences in the mind.
modern_relevance: You send the message, make the apology, or sign the resignation with a steady hand. The act is finished; the mental grip on it does not have to continue.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् । ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥
translation: जिस यज्ञमें अर्पण भी ब्रह्म है, हवी भी ब्रह्म है और ब्रह्मरूप कर्ताके द्वारा ब्रह्मरूप अग्निमें आहुति देनारूप क्रिया भी ब्रह्म है, ऐसे यज्ञको करनेवाले जिस मनुष्यकी ब्रह्ममें ही कर्मसमाधि हो गयी है, उसके द्वारा प्राप्त करनेयोग्य फल भी ब्रह्म ही है ॥
english_translation: In such sacrifice, the offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, and the act of offering into the fire of Brahman is Brahman. One whose action is absorbed in Brahman reaches Brahman alone.
essence: When action is fully absorbed, even the result is not separate from Brahman.
simple_meaning: When action is fully understood, the giver, the offering, the fire, and the result all belong to the same ultimate reality.
insight: It shifts action from personal striving to complete alignment with the supreme reality.
modern_relevance: You are standing before a hard apology, a resignation, or a truth that will change everything. The verse says the whole act can be sacred when your attention is fully aligned.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते । ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति ॥
translation: अन्य योगीलोग भगवदर्पणरूप यज्ञका ही अनुष्ठान करते हैं और दूसरे योगीलोग ब्रह्मरूप अग्निमें विचाररूप यज्ञके द्वारा ही जीवात्मारूप यज्ञका हवन करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Some yogis offer sacrifice to the divine alone. Others offer the self into the fire of Brahman through sacrifice itself.
essence: Sacrifice changes shape, but its aim remains surrender into the absolute.
simple_meaning: Different yogis practice sacrifice in different ways. Some dedicate worship to the divine, while others make the act of sacrifice itself into an offering within Brahman.
insight: It shifts attention from the outer form of practice to the inward quality of offering.
modern_relevance: You sit in a quiet room before a hard decision, trying to get the wording right before you speak. The form may differ, but the real task is the same: let the act become an offering, not a performance.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति । शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति ॥
translation: अन्य योगीलोग श्रोत्रादि समस्त इन्द्रियोंका संयमरूप अग्नियोंमें हवन किया करते हैं और दूसरे योगीलोग शब्दादि विषयोंका इन्द्रियरूप अग्नियोंमें हवन किया करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Some yogis offer the senses into the fires of restraint. Others offer sound and the other sense-objects into the fires of the senses.
essence: Restraint can consume desire before desire consumes you.
simple_meaning: Some seekers restrain the senses like a fire sacrifice. Others use the senses themselves to consume sense-objects, turning experience into a disciplined offering.
insight: It shifts discipline from moral guilt to conscious redirection of sensory energy.
modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message and lose twenty minutes to noise. The real practice is not pretending desire is absent, but training attention before it carries you away.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे । आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते ॥
translation: अन्य योगीलोग सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियोंकी क्रियाओंको और प्राणोंकी क्रियाओंको ज्ञानसे प्रकाशित आत्मसंयमयोगरूप अग्निमें हवन किया करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Others offer all the activities of the senses and the life-force into the fire of self-control, lit by knowledge.
essence: Knowledge turns self-control into a fire that consumes every impulse.
simple_meaning: Some seekers train themselves so deeply that every sense activity and every life-force activity is offered into the fire of self-control, which is lit by knowledge.
insight: It shifts practice from suppressing behavior to governing the forces beneath behavior.
modern_relevance: Your hand reaches for the phone before you notice. Your breath shortens, your jaw tightens, your attention scatters. This verse points to a deeper training: not just stopping action, but mastering the energies that drive it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे । स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः ॥
translation: दूसरे कितने ही तीक्ष्ण व्रत करनेवाले प्रयत्नशील साधक द्रव्यसम्बन्धी यज्ञ करनेवाले हैं, और कितने ही तपोयज्ञ करनेवाले हैं, और दूसरे कितने ही योगयज्ञ करनेवाले हैं, तथा कितने ही स्वाध्यायरूप ज्ञानयज्ञ करनेवाले हैं ॥
english_translation: Others offer wealth, austerity, yoga, and the study of sacred texts as sacrifice, while disciplined seekers make these offerings with firm vows.
essence: Sacrifice can be wealth, effort, austerity, or study.
simple_meaning: Different seekers turn different things into an offering: wealth, austerity, yoga practice, and study. All of them are disciplined forms of sacrifice.
insight: It expands sacrifice beyond ritual into daily disciplines like study, restraint, and practice.
modern_relevance: You are up before dawn, opening a book instead of your phone, or skipping comfort to keep a vow. The sacrifice is not only dramatic; it can be quiet, disciplined, and mental.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अपाने जुह्वति प्राण प्राणेऽपानं तथाऽपरे । प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः ॥
translation: दूसरे कितने ही प्राणायामके परायण हुए योगीलोग अपानमें प्राणका पूरक करके, प्राण और अपानकी गति रोककर फिर प्राणमें अपानका हवन करते हैं तथा अन्य कितने ही नियमित आहार करनेवाले प्राणोंका प्राणोंमें हवन किया करते हैं ।  ये सभी साधक यज्ञोंद्वारा पापोंका नाश करनेवाले और यज्ञोंको जाननेवाले हैं ॥
english_translation: Some offer the outgoing breath into the incoming breath, and the incoming breath into the outgoing breath, restraining the movement of both through breath-control as their aim. Others, with regulated food, offer the breaths into the breaths. All of them know sacrifice and are cleansed by sacrifice.
essence: Breath itself can become disciplined offering.
simple_meaning: Some practitioners use breath-control as a kind of sacrifice. They regulate inhalation and exhalation, and others do the same with disciplined eating.
insight: It turns ordinary bodily regulation into a conscious practice that steadies the mind and weakens impulsive reactivity.
modern_relevance: You catch yourself holding your breath before sending the message. Instead of letting anxiety drive the body, you slow the breath and regain command of yourself.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति । सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः ॥
translation: दूसरे कितने ही प्राणायामके परायण हुए योगीलोग अपानमें प्राणका पूरक करके, प्राण और अपानकी गति रोककर फिर प्राणमें अपानका हवन करते हैं तथा अन्य कितने ही नियमित आहार करनेवाले प्राणोंका प्राणोंमें हवन किया करते हैं ।  ये सभी साधक यज्ञोंद्वारा पापोंका नाश करनेवाले और यज्ञोंको जाननेवाले हैं ॥
english_translation: Some offer the breath into the breath through regulated breathing; some, with regulated food, offer the life-forces into the life-forces. All of them know sacrifice, and sacrifice has washed away their impurities.
essence: Discipline itself becomes offering, and offering burns away inner stain.
simple_meaning: Some people discipline their breathing, and some control their eating and life-energy. All of them are sincere practitioners of sacrifice, and that practice cleanses them.
insight: It broadens sacrifice beyond ritual into disciplined self-regulation that steadily clears the mind.
modern_relevance: You skip the second coffee, keep your breathing steady, and stop feeding your nerves with more noise. Quiet discipline can be its own offering.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् । नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतो़ऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम ॥
translation: हे कुरुवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  यज्ञसे बचे हुए अमृतका अनुभव करनेवाले सनातन परब्रह्म परमात्माको प्राप्त होते हैं ।  यज्ञ न करनेवाले मनुष्यके लिये यह मनुष्यलोक भी सुखदायक नहीं है, फिर परलोक कैसे सुखदायक होगा ॥
english_translation: Those who partake of the nectar left over from sacrifice attain the eternal supreme reality. This world is not for the one who does not perform sacrifice; how then the next world?
essence: A life without offering cannot even support itself.
simple_meaning: People who live by sacrifice and accept its blessed remainder move toward the eternal supreme reality. Without sacrifice, even this life loses its value, so the next one cannot be better.
insight: It shifts the mind from passive consumption to reciprocal offering, showing that meaningful living depends on contribution.
modern_relevance: You keep taking from a relationship, a team, or a family without giving anything back. Eventually the whole thing feels lifeless. The verse says participation is what keeps life alive.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे । कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे ॥
translation: इस प्रकार और भी बहुत तरहके यज्ञ वेदकी वाणीमें विस्तारसे कहे गये हैं ।  उन सब यज्ञोंको तू कर्मजन्य जान ।  इस प्रकार जानकर यज्ञ करनेसे तू कर्मबन्धनसे मुक्त हो जायगा ॥
english_translation: In this way, many kinds of sacrifice are described in the sacred teaching. Know them all as born of action; knowing this, you will be freed from the bondage of action.
essence: Seeing every offering as action frees you from action’s binding force.
simple_meaning: Many kinds of sacrifice are laid out in the sacred teaching. Understand that all of them arise from action, and that understanding frees you from action’s binding force.
insight: It shifts the mind from scattered ritual thinking to seeing the common principle behind every act.
modern_relevance: You keep replaying a mistake, thinking one more ritual, apology, or correction will make you clean. Seeing the pattern clearly breaks the spell and lets you move on.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप । सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते ॥
translation: हे परन्तप अर्जुन  द्रव्यमय यज्ञसे ज्ञानयज्ञ श्रेष्ठ है ।  सम्पूर्ण कर्म और पदार्थ ज्ञानतत्त्वज्ञान में समाप्त हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Arjuna, knowledge-sacrifice is better than sacrifice made of material things. All action and all matter end in knowledge.
essence: Knowledge is the point where every action finally comes to rest.
simple_meaning: Inner understanding is higher than outer offerings. Every action and every material effort finally leads toward knowledge.
insight: It shifts attention from accumulating outer acts to seeking the understanding that completes them.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to fix a painful situation with more effort, more advice, more buying, more doing. Then one honest insight changes everything. Some problems end not in force, but in understanding.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
translation: उस तत्त्वज्ञान को तत्त्वदर्शी ज्ञानी महापुरुषोंके पास जाकर समझ ।  उनको साष्टाङ्ग दण्डवत् प्रणाम करनेसे, उनकी सेवा करनेसे और सरलतापूर्वक प्रश्न करनेसे वे तत्त्वदर्शी ज्ञानी महापुरुष तुझे उस तत्त्वज्ञानका उपदेश देंगे ॥
english_translation: Know that by prostration, by sincere questioning, and by service. The wise who see reality will teach you that knowledge.
essence: Humility opens the door to knowledge that pride cannot reach.
simple_meaning: Real understanding comes from approaching wise people with humility, honest questions, and service. Those who truly see reality can teach knowledge.
insight: It teaches you to seek truth through humility, not ego-driven certainty.
modern_relevance: You are stuck on a hard decision and keep re-reading articles, still confused. Then one honest conversation with someone wiser cuts through the noise because you finally ask cleanly and listen fully.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव । येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि ॥
translation: जिस तत्त्वज्ञान का अनुभव करनेके बाद तू फिर इस प्रकार मोहको नहीं प्राप्त होगा, और हे अर्जुन  जिस तत्त्वज्ञान से तू सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंको निःशेषभावसे पहले अपनेमें और उसके बाद मुझ सच्चिदानन्दघन परमात्मामें देखेगा ॥
english_translation: Knowing which, you will not fall into confusion again. Through which, you will see all beings without remainder first in yourself, and then in me.
essence: Knowing deeply ends confusion by revealing one reality in all beings.
simple_meaning: True understanding ends confusion. It lets you see every being as part of one reality, first within yourself and then in the supreme reality.
insight: It shifts perception from isolated pieces to a single connected reality, reducing confusion at the root.
modern_relevance: You stare at a message before sending it, knowing it will change everything. Clear seeing cuts through the fear of fragments and lets you act from wholeness instead of panic.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः । सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥
translation: अगर तू सब पापियोंसे भी अधिक पापी है, तो भी तू ज्ञानरूपी नौकाके द्वारा निःसन्देह सम्पूर्ण पापसमुद्रसे अच्छी तरह तर जायगा ॥
english_translation: Even if you are the worst of wrongdoers, you will cross all wrongdoing by the raft of knowledge alone.
essence: Clear understanding can carry even the heaviest past across.
simple_meaning: Even if someone has done terrible things, clear understanding can still carry them beyond the whole burden of wrongdoing.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to transformation through clear seeing.
modern_relevance: You replay the mistake in your head after the argument, the lie, the betrayal. Krishna says the mind can stop circling the wound: clear understanding can still carry you through.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन । ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥
translation: हे अर्जुन  जैसे प्रज्वलित अग्नि ईंधनोंको सर्वथा भस्म कर देती है, ऐसे ही ज्ञानरूपी अग्नि सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंको सर्वथा भस्म कर देती है ॥
english_translation: As a blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, so the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes, Arjuna.
essence: Real understanding burns the binding power of every action.
simple_meaning: Clear understanding destroys the binding force of past actions, just as fire destroys fuel.
insight: It shifts the mind from managing consequences to seeing through the mechanism that creates them.
modern_relevance: You replay a mistake at 2 a.m., convinced it has branded you forever. Then one honest insight breaks the spell and the story stops running you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते । तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥
translation: इस मनुष्यलोकमें ज्ञानके समान पवित्र करनेवाला निःसन्देह दूसरा कोई साधन नहीं है ।  जिसका योग भलीभाँति सिद्ध हो गया है, वह कर्मयोगी उस तत्त्वज्ञानको अवश्य ही स्वयं अपनेआपमें पा लेता है ॥
english_translation: No purifier compares to knowledge in this world. The one perfected in yoga finds that knowledge within the self in time.
essence: Nothing purifies like knowledge, and yoga ripens it from within.
simple_meaning: Clear understanding is the highest purifier. A person who has matured through yoga eventually discovers that truth within themselves.
insight: It shifts the seeker from collecting answers to becoming fit for direct realization.
modern_relevance: You’ve tried advice, self-help, and endless opinions, but the knot remains. Then one quiet realization changes everything — not because someone handed it to you, but because it finally became yours.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः । ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥
translation: जो जितेन्द्रिय तथा साधनपरायण है, ऐसा श्रद्धावान् मनुष्य ज्ञानको प्राप्त होता है और ज्ञानको प्राप्त होकर वह तत्काल परम शान्तिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: The person with trust, discipline, and controlled senses gains knowledge. Having gained knowledge, that person quickly reaches supreme peace.
essence: Trust, discipline, and restraint make room for peace.
simple_meaning: Trust, steady effort, and sense control bring knowledge. Once knowledge arrives, deep peace comes quickly.
insight: It shifts the mind from demanding certainty first to cultivating the conditions that let clarity arrive.
modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, phone in hand, about to hear bad news. Panic will not help. Trust, steadiness, and self-control create the inner space where clear understanding can land.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति । नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥
translation: विवेकहीन और श्रद्धारहित संशयात्मा मनुष्यका पतन हो जाता है ।  ऐसे संशयात्मा मनुष्यके लिये न यह लोक है न परलोक है और न सुख ही है ॥
english_translation: The ignorant and faithless person who doubts is ruined. For the doubter, there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.
essence: A divided mind loses both peace and direction.
simple_meaning: A person who lacks clear understanding and trust, and keeps doubting, falls apart. Such a divided mind finds no real happiness here or beyond.
insight: It pushes the mind toward commitment: clear seeing and trust are necessary before action can become steady.
modern_relevance: You keep reopening the same message before sending it, afraid of being wrong. The delay is not caution anymore — it is the split mind making you smaller.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम् । आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥
translation: हे धनञ्जय  योग समता के द्वारा जिसका सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंसे सम्बन्धविच्छेद हो गया है और ज्ञानके द्वारा जिसके सम्पूर्ण संशयोंका नाश हो गया है, ऐसे स्वरूपपरायण मनुष्यको कर्म नहीं बाँधते ॥
english_translation: O Dhananjaya, actions do not bind the one who has renounced action through yoga, whose doubts have been cut away by knowledge, and who abides in the true self.
essence: Freedom begins when action no longer leaves a hook.
simple_meaning: A person rooted in yoga, free of doubt, and established in the true self is not trapped by actions. Action still happens, but it no longer leaves a binding mark.
insight: It shifts attention from the action itself to the state of inner freedom in which action happens.
modern_relevance: You send the message, sign the papers, or walk away from the room knowing the choice is clean. The body acts, but the mind no longer clings to the residue.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तस्मादज्ञानसंभूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः । छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥
translation: इसलिये हे भरतवंशी अर्जुन  हृदयमें स्थित इस अज्ञानसे उत्पन्न अपने संशयका ज्ञानरूप तलवारसे छेदन करके योग समता में स्थित हो जा, और युद्धके लिये खड़ा हो जा ॥
english_translation: Therefore, O Bharata, cut away this doubt in your heart, born of ignorance, with the sword of knowledge. Stand in yoga and rise up for battle.
essence: Knowledge cuts doubt, and then action becomes possible again.
simple_meaning: Knowledge should cut through inner doubt, and then you should stand steady and act. Krishna is telling Arjuna to stop wavering and rise for battle.
insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to decisive action after understanding is clear.
modern_relevance: You have the message typed out, but your finger hovers over send because you fear the fallout. The mind wants another delay; clarity asks for one clean decision.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचसंन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि । यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्िचतम् ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे कृष्ण  आप कर्मोंका स्वरूपसे त्याग करनेकी और फिर कर्मयोगकी प्रशंसा करते हैं ।  अतः इन दोनों साधनोंमें जो एक निश्चितरूपसे कल्याणकारक हो, उसको मेरे लिये कहिये ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: Krishna, you praise both renunciation of action and yoga of action. Tell me clearly which one is definitely better for my welfare.
essence: Choose the path that truly serves your welfare.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to choose between renouncing action and acting with discipline, and wants the one path that is clearly best.
insight: It shifts the reader from vague spiritual confusion to a direct search for the more beneficial way to live.
modern_relevance: You are torn between quitting a draining commitment and staying to do it well. The mind wants a clean answer, not more philosophy.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचसंन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ । तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  संन्यास सांख्ययोग और कर्मयोग दोनों ही कल्याण करनेवाले हैं ।  परन्तु उन दोनोंमें भी कर्मसंन्यास सांख्ययोग से कर्मयोग श्रेष्ठ है ॥
english_translation: Renunciation and karma yoga both lead to the highest good, but karma yoga is better than renouncing action.
essence: Renunciation matures when action continues without grasping.
simple_meaning: Both renunciation and karma yoga lead to the highest good, but Krishna says karma yoga is better than simply giving up action.
insight: It shifts the mind from escape to engaged renunciation: keep acting, but drop possessiveness over the result.
modern_relevance: You are tempted to quit the conversation, the project, or the relationship just to avoid the mess. Krishna says the cleaner move is not always to withdraw; sometimes it is to stay and act without grasping.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति । निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ॥
translation: हे महाबाहो  जो मनुष्य न किसीसे द्वेष करता है और न किसीकी आकाङ्क्षा करता है वह कर्मयोगी सदा संन्यासी समझनेयोग्य है क्योंकि द्वन्द्वोंसे रहित मनुष्य सुखपूर्वक संसारबन्धनसे मुक्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: One who neither hates nor desires is always a renunciant. Free from opposites, such a person is easily released from bondage, O mighty-armed one.
essence: Freedom comes when craving and resistance no longer steer the mind.
simple_meaning: A true renunciant is not someone who abandons action, but someone who drops hatred and craving. Freedom comes when inner opposites no longer pull the mind.
insight: It shifts renunciation from outward withdrawal to inward non-reactivity.
modern_relevance: You open a message from someone you resent, then feel the old heat rise. Or you keep refreshing for praise that never arrives. The grip is not the event — it is the wanting and resisting.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सांख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः । एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम् ॥
translation: बेसमझ लोग सांख्ययोग और कर्मयोगको अलगअलग फलवाले कहते हैं, न कि पण्डितजन क्योंकि इन दोनोंमेंसे एक साधनमें भी अच्छी तरहसे स्थित मनुष्य दोनोंके फलरूप परमात्माको प्राप्त कर लेता है ॥
english_translation: The unwise say that renunciation and yoga lead to different results. The wise see that one who is firmly established in either reaches the same fruit.
essence: Different methods can reach the same fulfillment when practiced wholeheartedly.
simple_meaning: People who do not understand think renunciation and disciplined action give different results. A wise person sees that either one, practiced well, leads to the same highest fulfillment.
insight: It shifts the mind from comparing spiritual methods to committing fully to one practice.
modern_relevance: You’re torn between quitting everything for a quieter life or staying and doing the hard work where you are. The verse says the split is false — depth matters more than the label on the path.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यत्सांख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते । एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
translation: सांख्ययोगियोंके द्वारा जो तत्त्व प्राप्त किया जाता है, कर्मयोगियोंके द्वारा भी वही प्राप्त किया जाता है ।  अतः जो मनुष्य सांख्ययोग और कर्मयोगको फलरूपमें एक देखता है, वही ठीक देखता है ॥
english_translation: The state reached by the wise is also reached through yoga. One who sees wisdom and yoga as one sees rightly.
essence: Different paths can lead to the same freedom.
simple_meaning: The wise path of understanding and the path of disciplined action lead to the same realization. Seeing them as separate is the mistake.
insight: It shifts the mind from arguing over methods to recognizing the shared result beneath them.
modern_relevance: You are stuck between quitting and pushing harder, as if only one choice can be right. This verse cuts through that panic: different methods can lead to the same settled place.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः । योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म नचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥
translation: परन्तु हे महाबाहो  कर्मयोगके बिना संन्यास सिद्ध होना कठिन है ।  मननशील कर्मयोगी शीघ्र ही ब्रह्मको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: But, mighty-armed one, renunciation without yoga is hard to attain. The disciplined seeker in yoga quickly reaches the supreme reality.
essence: Real renunciation grows through practice, not withdrawal.
simple_meaning: Letting go is not achieved by avoiding action. A steady, disciplined path of yoga leads the thoughtful seeker to the supreme reality quickly.
insight: It shifts renunciation from escape to transformation: act rightly until inner freedom becomes natural.
modern_relevance: You quit the argument, delete the app, and still feel the same pull inside. The outer move did nothing because the habit was never uprooted.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः । सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते ॥
translation: जिसकी इन्द्रियाँ अपने वशमें हैं, जिसका अन्तःकरण निर्मल है, जिसका शरीर अपने वशमें है और सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंकी आत्मा ही जिसकी आत्मा है, ऐसा कर्मयोगी कर्म करते हुए भी लिप्त नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: A disciplined yogi, pure in mind, self-mastered, and senses conquered, sees the same self in all beings and is not tainted by action while acting.
essence: Inner freedom lets action happen without leaving a trace.
simple_meaning: A person grounded in yoga, with a pure mind and mastered senses, acts without being stained by action because they see the same self in all beings.
insight: It shifts action from self-protection to clear participation, so work happens without leaving a residue of clinging.
modern_relevance: You answer the message, attend the meeting, and still feel the pull to perform, impress, or defend yourself. This verse says the work can happen without the inner stain of grasping.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नैव किंचित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित् । पश्यन् श्रृणवन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपन् श्वसन् ॥
translation: तत्त्वको जाननेवाला सांख्ययोगी देखता, सुनता, छूता, सूँघता, खाता, चलता, ग्रहण करता, बोलता, मलमूत्र का त्याग करता, सोता, श्वास लेता तथा आँखें खोलता और मूँदता भी सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियाँ इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंमें बरत रही हैं  ऐसा समझकर मैं स्वयं कुछ भी नहीं करता हूँ  ऐसा माने ॥
english_translation: The knower of reality should think, "I do nothing at all," while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, taking, speaking, discarding, sleeping, breathing, and opening and closing the eyes.
essence: Seeing life happen is not the same as claiming it.
simple_meaning: A person who knows reality sees the senses doing all the work and no longer claims personal doership.
insight: It shifts attention from personal ownership to clear witnessing of bodily and mental activity.
modern_relevance: You replay every word after a tense conversation and think, "I ruined it." This verse interrupts that habit: actions happen through the senses, but the self does not need to clutch them as "mine."
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृह्णन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन् ॥
translation: तत्त्वको जाननेवाला सांख्ययोगी देखता, सुनता, छूता, सूँघता, खाता, चलता, ग्रहण करता, बोलता, मलमूत्र का त्याग करता, सोता हुआ, श्वास लेता तथा आँखें खोलता और मूँदता हुआ भी सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियाँ इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंमें बरत रही हैं  ऐसा समझकर मैं स्वयं कुछ भी नहीं करता हूँ  ऐसा माने ॥
english_translation: Even while speaking, releasing, taking, opening, and closing the eyes, the wise know: the senses move among their objects.
essence: Action happens; ownership is the illusion.
simple_meaning: A person who knows the truth understands that actions are happening through the senses, not through a separate doer.
insight: It shifts attention from personal ownership of action to clear witnessing of bodily processes.
modern_relevance: Your phone lights up, your mouth answers, your hand reaches for the message. This verse asks you to notice the movement before you call it 'me.'
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः । लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥
translation: जो भक्तियोगी सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंको भगवान् में अर्पण करके और आसक्तिका त्याग करके कर्म करता है, वह जलसे कमलके पत्तेकी तरह पापसे लिप्त नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: One who offers actions to Brahman, renounces attachment, and acts is not stained by wrongdoing, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
essence: Action without attachment leaves no stain.
simple_meaning: Do your actions without clinging to them, and they do not bind you. Like a lotus leaf in water, you remain untouched.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to clean action: do the work, release the grip, and let consequences unfold.
modern_relevance: You send the message, make the hard apology, or sign the document that changes everything. What matters is not whether the moment feels clean, but whether you acted without clinging to the result.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि । योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये ॥
translation: कर्मयोगी आसक्तिका त्याग करके केवल ममतारहित इन्द्रियाँशरीरमनबुद्धि के द्वारा केवल अन्तःकरणकी शुद्धिके लिये ही कर्म करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Yogis perform action with body, mind, intellect, and the senses, giving up attachment, only for inner purification.
essence: Action becomes cleansing when attachment is removed.
simple_meaning: A true practitioner acts with the body, mind, intellect, and senses, but without clinging to results. The purpose is inner cleansing, not possession.
insight: It shifts action from self-protection to purification, so effort becomes a practice instead of a grab for results.
modern_relevance: You send the difficult message, close the laptop, and still feel the knot in your stomach. The verse says the act can be clean even when the outcome is uncertain.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् । अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥
translation: कर्मयोगी कर्मफलका त्याग करके नैष्ठिकी शान्तिको प्राप्त होता है ।  परन्तु सकाम मनुष्य कामनाके कारण फलमें आसक्त होकर बँध जाता है ॥
english_translation: The disciplined one gives up the fruit of action and attains steady peace. The undisciplined one, clinging to results through desire, becomes bound.
essence: Peace comes when action is no longer chained to reward.
simple_meaning: Letting go of results brings steady peace. Wanting a specific reward keeps you trapped.
insight: Shift attention from getting to giving; that loosens the mind’s grip.
modern_relevance: You send the message, then keep checking for the reply. The knot in your chest is not from the action — it is from needing a certain outcome.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सर्वकर्माणि मनसा संन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी । नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन् ॥
translation: जिसकी इन्द्रियाँ और मन वशमें हैं, ऐसा देहधारी पुरुष नौ द्वारोंवाले शरीररूपी पुरमें सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंका विवेकपूर्वक मनसे त्याग करके निःसन्देह न करता हुआ और न करवाता हुआ सुखपूर्वक अपने स्वरूपमें स्थित रहता है ॥
english_translation: The embodied one, who has mastered the senses and mind, dwells happily in the city of nine gates, mentally renouncing all actions, neither doing nor causing action.
essence: Freedom begins when action no longer feels personally owned.
simple_meaning: A self-mastered person can live peacefully in the body while inwardly letting go of all action. Such a person does not feel like the doer or the one making others act.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal authorship to quiet participation in action.
modern_relevance: You sent the message, made the call, and still feel responsible for every reaction. This verse reminds you that peace comes when you stop claiming ownership over everything that follows.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः । न कर्मफलसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्तते ॥
translation: परमेश्वर मनुष्योंके न कर्तापनकी, न कर्मोंकी और न कर्मफलके साथ संयोगकी रचना करते हैं किन्तु स्वभाव ही बरत रहा है ॥
english_translation: The supreme being creates neither doership nor actions nor the link between action and result for people. Nature alone keeps moving.
essence: What looks like personal control is nature moving through form.
simple_meaning: The supreme being does not manufacture a separate doer, the actions, or the binding link between action and result. What actually operates is nature.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame to clear seeing of how action actually happens.
modern_relevance: You replay a painful conversation at 2 a.m. and blame yourself for everything. This verse cuts through that loop: the ego claims ownership, but many forces move through a person.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः । अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः ॥
translation: सर्वव्यापी परमात्मा न किसीके पापकर्मको और न शुभकर्मको ही ग्रहण करता है किन्तु अज्ञानसे ज्ञान ढका हुआ है, उसीसे सब जीव मोहित हो रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The all-pervading one takes neither anyone's wrongdoing nor anyone's good deed. Knowledge is covered by ignorance, and that is why living beings are deluded.
essence: Ignorance, not action, is what keeps beings confused.
simple_meaning: The divine does not collect anyone's good or bad actions. People get confused because ignorance covers their understanding.
insight: It shifts attention from moral bookkeeping to clear seeing. When ignorance lifts, the mind stops being ruled by confusion.
modern_relevance: You replay one mistake at 2 a.m. and treat it like your identity. This verse cuts deeper: the real problem is not the act alone, but the ignorance that keeps repeating it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः । तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम् ॥
translation: परन्तु जिन्होंने अपने जिस ज्ञानविवक के द्वारा उस अज्ञानका नाश कर दिया है, उनका वह ज्ञान सूर्यकी तरह परमतत्त्व परमात्माको प्रकाशित कर देता है ॥
english_translation: But for those whose ignorance has been destroyed by knowledge of the true self, that knowledge reveals the supreme reality like the sun.
essence: Clear seeing does not create reality; it uncovers what was always there.
simple_meaning: When ignorance is removed by true understanding, that understanding itself reveals the highest reality, just as the sun reveals everything in daylight.
insight: It shifts the mind from collecting more data to removing the confusion that hides what is already true.
modern_relevance: You reread the same message ten times, then suddenly understand the room was never the problem. The facts were there; confusion was filtering them. Clear seeing changes everything.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः । गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः ॥
translation: जिनकी बुद्धि तदाकार हो रही है, जिनका मन तदाकार हो रहा है, जिनकी स्थिति परमात्मतत्वमें है, ऐसे परमात्मपरायण साधक ज्ञानके द्वारा पापरहित होकर अपुनरावृत्ति परमगति को प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those whose intellect is fixed in That, whose mind is That, who are established in That, and who are devoted to That, go to the state of no return, their impurities washed away by knowledge.
essence: Complete alignment with the supreme reality ends the cycle of return.
simple_meaning: When a person's mind, intellect, and whole focus are fully aligned with the supreme reality, knowledge clears away impurity and they reach a state beyond coming back.
insight: It shifts the goal from partial improvement to complete inward alignment with what is real.
modern_relevance: You sit in the car after the hardest conversation of your life, hands still shaking. Something in you has already chosen, and the old version of you cannot drive home with you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि । शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥
translation: ज्ञानी महापुरुष विद्याविनययुक्त ब्राह्मणमें और चाण्डालमें तथा गाय, हाथी एवं कुत्तेमें भी समरूप परमात्माको देखनेवाले होते हैं ॥
english_translation: The wise see the same reality in a learned, humble brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and an outcaste.
essence: Real wisdom erases rank and reveals sameness.
simple_meaning: A truly wise person does not rank living beings by status, species, or social position. The same reality is seen in all of them.
insight: It shifts the mind from status-based judgment to equal vision across all forms of life.
modern_relevance: You walk past a hospital corridor, a luxury lobby, and a street corner in the same hour. The outer labels change fast; this verse asks whether your seeing changes at all.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः । निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः ॥
translation: जिनका अन्तःकरण समतामें स्थित है, उन्होंने इस जीवितअवस्थामें ही सम्पूर्ण संसारको जीत लिया है ब्रह्म निर्दोष और सम है, इसलिये वे ब्रह्ममें ही स्थित हैं ॥
english_translation: Those whose mind rests in sameness conquer rebirth here itself. The supreme reality is flawless and equal, so they are established in it.
essence: Sameness of mind is the real conquest; everything else is aftermath.
simple_meaning: A mind that stays even and unshaken has already overcome the cycle of reactivity. Because the supreme reality is free of flaw and division, such a person is established in it.
insight: It shifts the goal from winning events to stabilizing the mind that meets them.
modern_relevance: You read a painful message, feel the surge of anger, and want to fire back. The verse asks for a different victory: let the mind stay even first, and the situation stops owning you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् । स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥
translation: जो प्रियको प्राप्त होकर हर्षित न हो और अप्रियको प्राप्त होकर उद्विग्न न हो, वह स्थिर बुद्धिवाला, मूढ़तारहित तथा ब्रह्मको जाननेवाला मनुष्य ब्रह्ममें स्थित है ॥
english_translation: One who does not rejoice at the pleasant, and does not shrink from the unpleasant, is steady in understanding, free from delusion, and established in the supreme reality.
essence: Steadiness begins when pleasure and pain lose their power over you.
simple_meaning: A person who stays calm in both good and bad situations has clear understanding and lives in the supreme reality.
insight: It trains the mind to stop using external events as the measure of your stability.
modern_relevance: You open the message and see praise, then an hour later a harsh reply. If your mood rises and falls with every notification, this verse calls you back to center.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥
translation: बाह्यस्पर्शमें आसक्तिरहित अन्तःकरणवाला साधक आत्मामें जो सुख है, उसको प्राप्त होता है ।  फिर वह ब्रह्ममें अभिन्नभावसे स्थित मनुष्य अक्षय सुखका अनुभव करता है ॥
english_translation: One who is not attached to outer contacts finds the joy within the true self. Unified with the supreme reality, that person enjoys unending happiness.
essence: Freedom begins when outer contact stops controlling inner joy.
simple_meaning: Real happiness is found by turning away from outside pleasures and resting in the true self. That inner joy does not wear out.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing stimulation to recognising a deeper source of contentment already present.
modern_relevance: You close the app, the room goes quiet, and the buzz is still there in your chest. No amount of scrolling, praise, or distraction reaches the place that actually needs rest.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते । आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥
translation: क्योंकि हे कुन्तीनन्दन  जो इन्द्रियों और विषयोंके संयोगसे पैदा होनेवाले भोग सुख हैं, वे आदिअन्तवाले और दुःखके ही कारण हैं ।  अतः विवेकशील मनुष्य उनमें रमण नहीं करता ॥
english_translation: The pleasures born from contact with the senses are only sources of suffering. They have a beginning and an end, O Arjuna, and the wise do not delight in them.
essence: Passing pleasure loses its power when its ending is seen.
simple_meaning: Pleasures that come from the senses do not last and often lead to suffering. A clear-minded person does not get absorbed in them.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing stimulation to seeing its cost before you reach for it.
modern_relevance: You open your phone for one quick check and lose twenty minutes, then feel worse. The pull was brief; the aftertaste was not. Clear seeing breaks that loop.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥
translation: इस मनुष्यशरीरमें जो कोई मनुष्य शरीर छूटनेसे पहले ही कामक्रोधसे उत्पन्न होनेवाले वेगको सहन करनेमें समर्थ होता है, वह नर योगी है और वही सुखी है ॥
english_translation: Whoever can withstand the surge of desire and anger here before the body falls, is a disciplined person and is truly happy.
essence: Master the surge before it masters you.
simple_meaning: A person who can endure the rush of desire and anger before death is truly disciplined and truly happy.
insight: It trains you to notice the impulse, hold it, and act from steadiness instead of heat.
modern_relevance: A sharp message lands in your inbox, and your chest tightens before you reply. The verse asks for that one breath of restraint where reaction is still optional.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः । स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य केवल परमात्मामें सुखवाला है और केवल परमात्मामें रमण करनेवाला है तथा जो केवल परमात्मामें ज्ञानवाला है, वह ब्रह्ममें अपनी स्थितिका अनुभव करनेवाला सांख्ययोगी निर्वाण ब्रह्मको प्राप्त होता है ॥
english_translation: One who finds happiness within, delights within, and has inner light alone, becomes one with the supreme reality and reaches freedom in the supreme reality.
essence: Inner fulfillment makes freedom possible right now.
simple_meaning: Real freedom comes to the person who finds joy, delight, and clear awareness within, rather than depending on outside things.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing stimulation to resting in inner fullness.
modern_relevance: You close the app, silence the room, and still feel the pull to check one more message. This verse points to the rare relief of not needing the next hit of approval or distraction.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः । छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
translation: जिनका शरीर मनबुद्धिइन्द्रियोंसहित वशमें है, जो सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके हितमें रत हैं, जिनके सम्पूर्ण संशय मिट गये हैं, जिनके सम्पूर्ण कल्मष दोष नष्ट हो गये हैं, वे विवेकी साधक निर्वाण ब्रह्मको प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Sages who are free of impurity, free of doubt, self-controlled, and devoted to the welfare of all beings attain freedom in the supreme reality.
essence: Freedom arrives when doubt ends and life turns toward all beings.
simple_meaning: People who have cleansed themselves, ended doubt, controlled their minds and senses, and care for the good of all beings reach freedom in the supreme reality.
insight: It shifts the goal from private purity to a life that benefits every being.
modern_relevance: You’re standing outside a hospital room after a hard diagnosis, holding back panic so you can help your family. Clear action begins when doubt settles and concern widens beyond yourself.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कामक्रोधवियुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाम् । अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम् ॥
translation: कामक्रोधसे सर्वथा रहित, जीते हुए मनवाले और स्वरूपका साक्षात्कार किये हुए सांख्ययोगियोंके लिये दोनों ओरसेशरीरके रहते हुए अथवा शरीर छूटनेके बाद निर्वाण ब्रह्म परिपूर्ण है ॥
english_translation: For those free from desire and anger, with disciplined minds and self-knowledge, freedom in the supreme reality is near on both sides.
essence: Freedom comes when desire and anger no longer govern the mind.
simple_meaning: When desire and anger no longer control the mind, and a person knows the true self, inner freedom is close whether alive or after death.
insight: It shifts attention from managing events to mastering the reactions that bind them.
modern_relevance: You read the message that set you off, and the reply is already forming. This verse asks you to notice the heat before it becomes action, because freedom starts there.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यांश्चक्षुश्चैवान्तरे भ्रुवोः । प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ ॥
translation: बाह्य पदार्थोंको बाहर ही छोड़कर और नेत्रोंकी दृष्टिको भौंहोंके बीचमें स्थित करके तथा नासिकामें विचरनेवाले प्राण और अपान वायुको सम करके जिसकी इन्द्रियाँ, मन और बुद्धि अपने वशमें हैं, जो मोक्षपरायण है तथा जो इच्छा, भय और क्रोधसे सर्वथा रहित है, वह मुनि सदा मुक्त ही है ॥
english_translation: Leaving outer objects outside, fixing the gaze between the eyebrows, and balancing the inward and outward breaths moving through the nose.
essence: Outer restraint and balanced breath prepare the mind for freedom.
simple_meaning: Withdraw the senses from outer objects, steady the gaze, and balance the breath. This prepares the mind for deep inward focus.
insight: It shifts attention from outer stimulation to bodily regulation, creating the conditions for a steadier mind.
modern_relevance: You sit in the car before walking into a room where one conversation could change everything. Before the door opens, you breathe, settle your eyes, and stop feeding the noise.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः । विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः ॥
translation: बाह्य पदार्थोंको बाहर ही छोड़कर और नेत्रोंकी दृष्टिको भौंहोंके बीचमें स्थित करके तथा नासिकामें विचरनेवाले प्राण और अपान वायुको सम करके जिसकी इन्द्रियाँ, मन और बुद्धि अपने वशमें हैं, जो मोक्षपरायण है तथा जो इच्छा, भय और क्रोधसे सर्वथा रहित है, वह मुनि सदा मुक्त ही है ॥
english_translation: One who has controlled the senses, mind, and intellect, who seeks freedom as the highest aim, and who is free from desire, fear, and anger is forever free.
essence: Freedom begins where desire, fear, and anger lose authority.
simple_meaning: A person who has mastered the senses, mind, and intellect, and has let go of desire, fear, and anger, lives in freedom already.
insight: It shifts attention from outer circumstances to inner mastery as the sign of freedom.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that could end a relationship, and your chest is tight with fear. This verse points to the steadiness that lets you act without being ruled by panic.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् । सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति ॥
translation: भक्त मुझे सब यज्ञों और तपोंका भोक्ता, सम्पूर्ण लोकोंका महान् ईश्वर तथा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंका सुहृद् स्वार्थरहित दयालु और प्रेमी जानकर शान्तिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Knowing me as the enjoyer of all sacrifice and austerity, the great lord of all worlds, and the friend of all beings, one attains peace.
essence: Peace comes from knowing the divine receives all effort and cares for all beings.
simple_meaning: Peace comes from knowing Krishna as the true receiver of sacrifice and effort, the ruler of all worlds, and the friend of every being.
insight: It shifts effort from anxious self-ownership to trust in a benevolent order.
modern_relevance: You finish the hard conversation, heart racing, and still wonder whether it meant anything. This verse says peace comes when you trust that your effort was received by something larger and kinder.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचअनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः । स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  कर्मफलका आश्रय न लेकर जो कर्तव्यकर्म करता है, वही संन्यासी तथा योगी है और केवल अग्निका त्याग करनेवाला संन्यासी नहीं होता तथा केवल क्रियाओंका त्याग करनेवाला योगी नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: One who performs the required action without taking shelter in the fruit of action is a renunciate and a yogi. Not one who merely gives up fire, and not one who merely stops acting.
essence: Renunciation means acting without needing to own the result.
simple_meaning: Real renunciation is not escaping action. It is doing what must be done without clinging to the result.
insight: It shifts attention from outcome-hunting to clean, necessary action.
modern_relevance: You send the message, make the hard call, or finish the task late at night. The cleanest act is the one you can stand behind even if nobody rewards it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव । न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन ॥
translation: हे अर्जुन  लोग जिसको संन्यास कहते हैं, उसीको तुम योग समझो क्योंकि संकल्पोंका त्याग किये बिना मनुष्य कोईसा भी योगी नहीं हो सकता ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, what people call renunciation is yoga. No one becomes a yogi without giving up intentions.
essence: Yoga begins when the mind stops clutching its own agenda.
simple_meaning: Real renunciation is not outer withdrawal. It is letting go of inner plans and fixed desires so the mind can truly enter yoga.
insight: It shifts practice from external gestures to the inner release of wanting and planning.
modern_relevance: You close the laptop, but your mind keeps rehearsing the outcome of the conversation. The real letting go is not in your hands or schedule — it is in the plans you keep gripping.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते । योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते ॥
translation: जो योगसमता में आरूढ़ होना चाहता है, ऐसे मननशील योगीके लिये कर्तव्यकर्म करना कारण कहा गया है और उसी योगारूढ़ मनुष्यका शम शान्ति परमात्मप्राप्तिमें कारण कहा गया है ॥
english_translation: For the sage who seeks to rise into yoga, action is the means. For the one who has risen in yoga, stillness is the means.
essence: You reach steadiness through action, then preserve it through stillness.
simple_meaning: Action helps a seeker rise into yoga. Once that steadiness is reached, calm stillness becomes the support.
insight: It shifts the mind from forcing stillness to building the conditions for it.
modern_relevance: You are learning to meditate, but your mind keeps darting to messages, chores, and unfinished conversations. First you need disciplined practice; later, the deeper work is learning to stay quiet without effort.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते । सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते ॥
translation: जिस समय न इन्द्रियोंके भोगोंमें तथा न कर्मोंमें ही आसक्त होता है, उस समय वह सम्पूर्ण संकल्पोंका त्यागी मनुष्य योगारूढ़ कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: When one no longer clings to sense pleasures or to actions, that person is called established in yoga, having renounced all intentions.
essence: Yoga begins when neither pleasure nor action can hook you.
simple_meaning: A person is truly steady in yoga when neither pleasures nor actions hook the mind, and all intentions have been let go.
insight: It shifts attention from achievement and stimulation to non-clinging presence.
modern_relevance: You finish the presentation, then keep refreshing the email thread for praise. Or you stop chasing the praise and feel your shoulders drop. This verse names that release.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
translation: अपने द्वारा अपना उद्धार करे, अपना पतन न करे क्योंकि आप ही अपना मित्र है और आप ही अपना शत्रु है ॥
english_translation: Lift yourself by yourself; do not let yourself fall. The true self is its own friend, and the true self is its own enemy.
essence: Your own inner handling makes you rise or collapse.
simple_meaning: Your own effort can raise you or ruin you. The same mind that helps you grow can also drag you down.
insight: It shifts responsibility inward: stop waiting for rescue and start becoming the force that steadies you.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, quit the habit, or tell the truth—and the old voice says to delay again. In that moment, your own inner handling decides whether you rise or shrink.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः । अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥
translation: जिसने अपनेआपसे अपनेआपको जीत लिया है, उसके लिये आप ही अपना बन्धु है और जिसने अपनेआपको नहीं जीता है, ऐसे अनात्माका आत्मा ही शत्रुतामें शत्रुकी तरह बर्ताव करता है ॥
english_translation: For one who has conquered the lower self by the true self, the true self is a friend. For one who has not conquered the lower self, the true self behaves like an enemy.
essence: The same inner nature that frees you can also fight you.
simple_meaning: When you master your restless impulses, your deepest nature supports you. If you do not, your own mind and habits work against you.
insight: It shifts the struggle from controlling the world to mastering the impulses that distort your own judgment.
modern_relevance: You sit alone after sending the message you were afraid to send. If you acted from clarity, something in you steadies. If you acted from fear, the same mind turns harsh and restless.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥
translation: जिसने अपनेआपपर अपनी विजय कर ली है, उस शीतउष्ण अनुकूलताप्रतिकूलता सुखदुःख तथा मानअपमानमें निर्विकार मनुष्यको परमात्मा नित्यप्राप्त हैं ॥
english_translation: For one who has conquered the self and is serene, the supreme reality is ever present in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, honor and dishonor.
essence: Steadiness makes the highest reality feel near in every opposite.
simple_meaning: A person who has mastered the restless mind stays steady through comfort and discomfort, praise and insult. In that steadiness, the supreme reality is immediately present.
insight: It shifts attention from outer conditions to inner steadiness, showing that true presence is possible amid opposites.
modern_relevance: You get praised in the meeting, then criticized in the hallway, and your mood swings with both. This verse asks for a steadier center that no comment can shake.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः । युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ॥
translation: जिसका अन्तःकरण ज्ञानविज्ञानसे तृप्त है, जो कूटकी तरह निर्विकार है, जितेन्द्रिय है और मिट्टीके ढेले, पत्थर तथा स्वर्णमें समबुद्धिवाला है  ऐसा योगी युक्त योगारूढ़ कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: One whose mind is satisfied by knowledge and realization, who remains steady, who has conquered the senses, and who sees clay, stone, and gold alike is called a yogi in union.
essence: True mastery makes gold and dust feel identical.
simple_meaning: A person who is fulfilled by clear understanding, steady in mind, and in control of the senses sees wealth and ordinary matter with the same calmness.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing value to recognizing sameness beneath appearances.
modern_relevance: You open a message that could change your salary, your status, or your plans. The mind that has settled itself does not flinch at gain or loss; it stays even.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु । साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते ॥
translation: सुहृद्, मित्र, वैरी, उदासीन, मध्यस्थ, द्वेष्य और सम्बन्धियोंमें तथा साधुआचरण करनेवालोंमें और पापआचरण करनेवालोंमें भी समबुद्धिवाला मनुष्य श्रेष्ठ है ॥
english_translation: The one whose understanding is equal toward friend, enemy, neutral person, mediator, hateful person, relative, the virtuous, and the sinful is श्रेष्ठ.
essence: Equal vision toward all people marks the highest steadiness.
simple_meaning: A calm, even-minded person does not get pulled by labels like friend, enemy, good, or bad. That balanced understanding is considered best.
insight: It trains you to respond from clear seeing, not from liking and disliking.
modern_relevance: A group chat splits into camps and everyone wants your reaction. You feel the pull to defend one side and condemn the other. This verse asks for a steadier mind that does not get recruited by emotion.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः । एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः ॥
translation: भोगबुद्धिसे संग्रह न करनेवाला, इच्छारहित और अन्तःकरण तथा शरीरको वशमें रखनेवाला योगी अकेला एकान्तमें स्थित होकर मनको निरन्तर परमात्मामें लगाये ॥
english_translation: The disciplined yogi, dwelling alone in seclusion, should constantly unite the mind with the supreme being, free from desire and possessiveness, with body and mind under control.
essence: Steady inward practice begins when desire and possessiveness end.
simple_meaning: A yogi should sit alone, keep the mind steadily focused on the divine, and let go of desire and possessiveness.
insight: It shifts practice from chasing stimulation to steady inward attention.
modern_relevance: You close the bedroom door after a draining day, but your mind keeps reaching for messages, praise, and proof. This verse asks you to sit down, stop grasping, and return inward.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः । नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम् ॥
translation: शुद्ध भूमिपर, जिसपर क्रमशः कुश, मृगछाला और वस्त्र बिछे हैं, जो न अत्यन्त ऊँचा है और न अत्यन्त नीचा, ऐसे अपने आसनको स्थिरस्थापन करके ॥
english_translation: Having placed a firm seat for himself on a clean spot, neither too high nor too low, with cloth, deerskin, and kusha grass laid in layers.
essence: A steady mind begins with a steady seat.
simple_meaning: Choose a clean, steady seat that is neither too high nor too low, and prepare it with cloth, deerskin, and kusha grass.
insight: It shifts attention from abstract intention to physical preparation, showing that practice starts by setting conditions well.
modern_relevance: You sit on the edge of the bed after midnight, phone face down, trying to calm a racing mind. The first step is not insight — it is creating a steady place to begin.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः । उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये ॥
translation: उस आसनपर बैठकर चित्त और इन्द्रियोंकी क्रियाओंको वशमें रखते हुए मनको एकाग्र करके अन्तःकरणकी शुद्धिके लिये योगका अभ्यास करे ॥
english_translation: Sitting on that seat, with the mind made one-pointed and the movements of mind and senses restrained, one should practice yoga for inner purification.
essence: Meditation begins by gathering the mind and training the senses.
simple_meaning: Sit steadily, gather the mind, restrain the senses, and practice yoga to purify the inner state.
insight: It shifts meditation from a vague wish into a disciplined act of collecting attention.
modern_relevance: You sit down to meditate, but the phone buzzes, your body fidgets, and your thoughts scatter. The practice begins by gathering yourself before anything deeper can happen.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः । संप्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन् ॥
translation: काया, शिर और ग्रीवाको सीधे अचल धारण करके तथा दिशाओंको न देखकर केवल अपनी नासिकाके अग्रभागको देखते हुए स्थिर होकर बैठे ॥
english_translation: Holding the body, head, and neck straight and still, and gazing only at the tip of the nose without looking around.
essence: Steady posture is the first gate to a steady mind.
simple_meaning: Sit with your body straight and still. Keep your gaze fixed and do not let the eyes wander.
insight: It shifts meditation from a vague idea to a concrete bodily discipline.
modern_relevance: You sit down to breathe for five minutes, but your eyes keep jumping to the phone, the door, the clock. The practice starts when the body stops asking to escape.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः । मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः ॥
translation: जिसका अन्तःकरण शान्त है, जो भयरहित है और जो ब्रह्मचारिव्रतमें स्थित है, ऐसा सावधान योगी मनका संयम करके मेरेमें चित्त लगाता हुआ मेरे परायण होकर बैठे ॥
english_translation: The yogi, with a peaceful mind, free of fear, and firm in celibate discipline, restrains the mind, fixes awareness on Me, and sits devoted to Me as the supreme aim.
essence: A disciplined mind can rest in devotion without fear.
simple_meaning: A steady yogi keeps the mind under control, stays free from fear, and turns awareness toward Krishna while sitting in disciplined practice.
insight: It shifts practice from technique alone to the inner conditions that make practice hold.
modern_relevance: You sit alone before sending the message that could change a relationship. Your chest is tight, your thoughts are racing, and you choose calm restraint before you speak.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी नियतमानसः । शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति ॥
translation: नियत मनवाला योगी मनको इस तरहसे सदा परमात्मामें लगाता हुआ मेरेमें सम्यक् स्थितिवाली जो निर्वाणपरमा शान्ति है, उसको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: The disciplined yogi, always uniting the mind in this way, attains the supreme peace of freedom rooted in Me.
essence: A steady mind reaches the peace that restlessness can never touch.
simple_meaning: A steady yogi keeps the mind gathered and focused, and reaches the highest peace rooted in the divine presence.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing relief to building a mind that can actually hold peace.
modern_relevance: You close the laptop after an argument and your mind keeps replaying every line. The body is still, but the mind keeps running. This verse points to the deeper quiet that comes only when attention is trained.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः । न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥
translation: हे अर्जुन  यह योग न तो अधिक खानेवालेका और न बिलकुल न खानेवालेका तथा न अधिक सोनेवालेका और न बिलकुल न सोनेवालेका ही सिद्ध होता है ॥
english_translation: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who eats nothing at all. It is not for one who sleeps too much, nor for one who stays awake too long, Arjuna.
essence: Balance makes meditation possible; extremes break it.
simple_meaning: Meditation does not work with extremes. Too much food, no food, too much sleep, or no sleep all disturb the practice.
insight: It shifts discipline from heroic intensity to balanced repetition.
modern_relevance: You skip meals, then overeat at night. You sleep badly, then try to meditate anyway. The mind cannot settle when the body is being pushed into extremes.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु । युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥
translation: दुःखोंका नाश करनेवाला योग तो यथायोग्य आहार और विहार करनेवालेका, कर्मोंमें यथायोग्य चेष्टा करनेवालेका तथा यथायोग्य सोने और जागनेवालेका ही सिद्ध होता है ॥
english_translation: Yoga that destroys suffering comes from balanced eating, balanced activity, balanced work, and balanced sleep and waking.
essence: Balanced living makes inner practice possible.
simple_meaning: A steady practice works when daily life is balanced: eating, moving, working, sleeping, and waking all in proper measure.
insight: It shifts discipline from heroic intensity to sustainable rhythm.
modern_relevance: You skip meals, scroll past midnight, then wonder why your mind feels broken during the hard conversation at 9 a.m. Balance in the body gives the mind a place to stand.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते । निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा ॥
translation: वशमें किया हुआ चित्त जिस कालमें अपने स्वरूपमें ही स्थित हो जाता है और स्वयं सम्पूर्ण पदार्थोंसे निःस्पृह हो जाता है, उस कालमें वह योगी है  ऐसा कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: When the controlled mind rests in the true self alone and is free from craving for all pleasures, that person is called united in yoga.
essence: Yoga begins when craving loses its grip and the mind comes home.
simple_meaning: A person is truly steady in yoga when the mind settles into the true self and no longer chases every desire.
insight: It shifts attention from managing impulses to recognizing the mind’s settled state.
modern_relevance: You finally close the laptop after midnight, but your mind keeps reaching for one more reply, one more check, one more fix. Peace begins when the chasing stops.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता । योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥
translation: जैसे स्पन्दनरहित वायुके स्थानमें स्थित दीपककी लौ चेष्टारहित हो जाती है, योगका अभ्यास करते हुए वश में किए हुए चित्तवाले योगीके चित्तकी वैसी ही उपमा कही गयी है ॥
english_translation: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker, so the disciplined mind of a yogi does not waver while practicing yoga of the true self.
essence: A trained mind becomes steady enough to stop flickering.
simple_meaning: A trained mind becomes steady and unmoving, like a lamp that does not flicker when there is no wind.
insight: It shifts attention from managing thoughts to stabilizing the mind that holds them.
modern_relevance: You finally sit down after a fight, but your thoughts keep replaying every word. This verse points to a steadiness that no argument, memory, or fear can shake.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया । यत्र चैवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥
translation: योगका सेवन करनेसे जिस अवस्थामें निरुद्ध चित्त उपराम हो जाता है तथा जिस अवस्थामें स्वयं अपनेआप से अपनेआपको देखता हुआ अपनेआपमें ही सन्तुष्ट हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: When the restrained mind becomes still through yoga practice, and the person sees the true self by the true self, one is content in the true self alone.
essence: Stillness reveals a completeness that no outside thing can improve.
simple_meaning: Through steady yoga practice, the mind becomes quiet. In that quiet, a person directly sees the true self and feels complete within it.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing stimulation to resting in direct awareness.
modern_relevance: You finally put the phone down after an hour of scrolling and sit in silence. The noise thins, and the craving for one more distraction loses its grip.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद्बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् । वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥
translation: जो सुख आत्यन्तिक, अतीन्द्रिय और बुद्धिग्राह्य है, उस सुखका जिस अवस्थामें अनुभव करता है और जिस सुखमें स्थित हुआ यह ध्यानयोगी फिर कभी तत्त्वसे विचलित नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: One knows the boundless joy beyond the senses and grasped by the discerning mind; established in it, one never truly falls away.
essence: True joy is deeper than sensation and keeps you from wavering.
simple_meaning: Meditation reveals a deep joy that the senses cannot reach. Once someone is grounded in it, that person no longer wavers in truth.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing stimulation to recognising a joy that stabilises the mind.
modern_relevance: You sit alone after a hard decision, phone face down, heart still racing. Then something quieter arrives — not excitement, not escape, but a steadiness that does not need applause to remain.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः । यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते ॥
translation: जिस लाभकी प्राप्ति होनेपर उससे अधिक कोई दूसरा लाभ उसके माननेमें भी नहीं आता और जिसमें स्थित होनेपर वह बड़े भारी दुःखसे भी विचलित नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
english_translation: Having attained it, one thinks no greater gain exists. Established in it, one is not shaken even by great sorrow.
essence: True fulfillment leaves nothing more to chase and nothing strong enough to unsettle you.
simple_meaning: A person who reaches this state sees nothing greater to attain and cannot be shaken even by severe suffering.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing improvement to resting in unshakable steadiness.
modern_relevance: You get the message that would normally wreck your day, and your chest stays open anyway. Nothing inside you begs for a different reality.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् । स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥
translation: जिसमें दुःखोंके संयोगका ही वियोग है, उसीको योग नामसे जानना चाहिये ।  वह योग जिस ध्यानयोगका लक्ष्य है, उस ध्यानयोगका अभ्यास न उकताये हुए चित्तसे निश्चयपूर्वक करना चाहिये ॥
english_translation: Know that as yoga: the severance of union with suffering. Practice that yoga with certainty, with an undiscouraged mind.
essence: Yoga is the breaking of suffering’s grip, practiced steadily.
simple_meaning: True meditation is the ending of the mind’s bond with suffering. That practice should be continued steadily, without losing heart.
insight: It shifts meditation from a mood you wait for to a discipline you keep practicing until suffering loosens.
modern_relevance: You sit in a parked car after a hard conversation, replaying every word and wanting to avoid the next one. This verse says the way out is not escape, but steady practice without losing heart.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सङ्कल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः । मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः ॥
translation: संकल्पसे उत्पन्न होनेवाली सम्पूर्ण कामनाओंका सर्वथा त्याग करके और मनसे ही इन्द्रियसमूहको सभी ओरसे हटाकर ॥
english_translation: Abandon every desire born of resolve, and restrain the whole field of the senses on all sides with the mind alone.
essence: Desire loses power when the mind stops feeding it.
simple_meaning: Let go of every desire that rises from planning and craving. Use the mind to pull the senses back from every direction.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing impulses to actively gathering the senses under one steady mind.
modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one thing, and twenty minutes vanish. The mind has to pull the senses back before they pull you apart.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया । आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥
translation: धैर्ययुक्त बुद्धिके द्वारा संसारसे धीरेधीरे उपराम हो जाय और परमात्मस्वरूपमें मनबुद्धि को सम्यक् प्रकारसे स्थापन करके फिर कुछ भी चिन्तन न करे ॥
english_translation: Little by little, the mind should be quieted by steady discernment. Fix the mind in the true self and think of nothing else.
essence: Stillness comes by degrees when the mind stops feeding itself.
simple_meaning: The mind should be calmed gradually with firm understanding. Once it rests in the true self, it should stop chasing thoughts.
insight: It teaches you to calm thought through gradual restraint, not sudden suppression.
modern_relevance: You sit in a parked car after a hard conversation, replaying every sentence. The answer is not to wrestle the mind harder, but to bring it back, gently, until the loop loosens.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥
translation: यह अस्थिर और चञ्चल मन जहाँजहाँ विचरण करता है, वहाँवहाँसे हटाकर इसको एक परमात्मामें ही लगाये ॥
english_translation: Whenever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, bring it back under the control of the true self.
essence: The mind is mastered by repeated return, not by force.
simple_meaning: Each time the mind runs off, bring it back again and again to the true self.
insight: It trains the mind to recover quickly from distraction instead of obeying every impulse.
modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message and lose twenty minutes. The practice is not to shame the drift — it is to notice it, and return.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् । उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम् ॥
translation: जिसके सब पाप नष्ट हो गये हैं, जिसका रजोगुण तथा मन सर्वथा शान्तनिर्मल हो गया है, ऐसे इस ब्रह्मस्वरूप योगीको निश्चित ही उत्तम सात्त्विक सुख प्राप्त होता है ॥
english_translation: The yogi whose mind is peaceful, whose passion is stilled, and who is free from impurity attains the highest joy.
essence: Joy comes when the restless mind finally becomes still.
simple_meaning: A person who has calmed the mind, quieted passion, and become free of inner impurity reaches the highest kind of joy.
insight: It shifts the goal from chasing stimulation to cultivating inner quiet that can actually receive joy.
modern_relevance: After the argument ends and your phone stops buzzing, you finally sit in silence and notice how noisy your own mind has been. Relief begins there, not in the next distraction.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः । सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते ॥
translation: इस प्रकार अपनेआपको सदा परमात्मामें लगाता हुआ पापरहित योगी सुखपूर्वक ब्रह्मप्राप्तिरूप अत्यन्त सुखको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Thus, the disciplined yogi, free from impurity, always unites the self with the supreme reality and attains limitless joy through that contact.
essence: Repeated union with the supreme reality yields effortless, lasting joy.
simple_meaning: A purified yogi keeps the mind steadily joined to the supreme reality and experiences deep, lasting joy.
insight: It shifts meditation from effortful forcing to a settled intimacy with what is real.
modern_relevance: You sit in a silent room after a brutal week, and the mind finally stops bargaining. The relief is not dramatic; it is clean, steady, and strangely enough, enough.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥
translation: सब जगह अपने स्वरूपको देखनेवाला और ध्यानयोगसे युक्त अन्तःकरणवाला योगा अपने स्वरूपको सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें स्थित देखता है और सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंको अपने स्वरूपमें देखता है ॥
english_translation: The one united in yoga sees the true self in all beings and all beings in the true self, seeing everything with equal vision.
essence: Equal vision dissolves the illusion of separation.
simple_meaning: A person steady in meditation sees the same inner self present in every living being, and sees every living being within that same self.
insight: It trains the mind to move from separation to shared essence, changing how you look at people before you act toward them.
modern_relevance: You are in a tense room where everyone feels like an opponent. This verse shifts the room: the person across from you is no longer a threat to manage, but a life sharing the same ground.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति । तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥
translation: जो सबमें मुझे देखता है और सबको मुझमें देखता है, उसके लिये मैं अदृश्य नहीं होता और वह मेरे लिये अदृश्य नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: Who sees Me in all beings and sees all beings in Me, I am never lost to that person, and that person is never lost to Me.
essence: Seeing the divine everywhere ends separation.
simple_meaning: Seeing the divine in every being creates a living connection that cannot be broken. The one who sees this way is never separated from Krishna, and Krishna is never separated from that person.
insight: It shifts perception from separation to shared presence, making devotion feel immediate rather than abstract.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room and see the same fear in the patient, the nurse, and yourself. In that moment, the wall between 'me' and 'them' softens, and compassion becomes natural.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः । सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते ॥
translation: मेरेमें एकीभावसे स्थित हुआ जो योगी सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें स्थित मेरा भजन करता है, वह सब कुछ बर्ताव करता हुआ भी मेरेमें ही बर्ताव कर रहा है अर्थात् वह सर्वथा मेरेमें ही स्थित है ॥
english_translation: The yogi who abides in unity and worships Me in all beings lives in Me, even while acting in every way.
essence: Unity turns every action into abiding presence.
simple_meaning: A person who sees the divine in every being and lives in that oneness remains rooted in the divine, even while going through ordinary activity.
insight: It shifts devotion from a separate ritual into a continuous way of seeing and acting.
modern_relevance: You are in a crowded train, answering messages, half-distracted, and still something in you is steady. The verse points to that steadiness: outward motion does not have to break inward communion.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन । सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः ॥
translation: हे अर्जुन  जो ध्यानयुक्त ज्ञानी महापुरुष अपने शरीरकी उपमासे सब जगह अपनेको समान देखता है और सुख अथवा दुःखको भी समान देखता है, वह परम योगी माना गया है ॥
english_translation: O Arjuna, the yogi who sees all beings as equal through the measure of the true self, and sees pleasure and pain alike, is considered the highest yogi.
essence: Equal vision makes you unshaken by pleasure or pain.
