simple_meaning: A true meditator sees every being with equal regard and does not get thrown off by pleasure or pain.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal reaction to even-minded seeing.
modern_relevance: You get praised in the morning and criticized by evening. If your whole mood rises and falls with each message, this verse asks for a steadier center.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचयोऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे मधुसूदन  आपने समतापूर्वक जो यह योग कहा है, मनकी चञ्चलताके कारण मैं इस योगकी स्थिर स्थिति नहीं देखता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: Krishna, you have described this yoga as balanced, but I do not see its steady practice, because the mind is restless.
essence: Restlessness makes even clear teaching feel unreachable.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says the balanced state Krishna described sounds clear, but his restless mind cannot hold it steadily.
insight: It names mental restlessness as the first obstacle, so the response becomes steadiness rather than self-blame.
modern_relevance: You sit in the car before walking into a hard conversation, heart racing, rehearsing every possible outcome. Part of you knows the right thing; another part cannot settle long enough to do it.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
translation: क्योंकि हे कृष्ण  मन बड़ा ही चञ्चल, प्रमथनशील, दृढ़ जिद्दी और बलवान् है ।  उसका निग्रह करना मैं वायुकी तरह अत्यन्त कठिन मानता हूँ ॥
english_translation: The mind is restless, turbulent, stubborn, and strong. I think controlling it is as hard as controlling the wind.
essence: The mind resists control like wind resists the hand.
simple_meaning: Arjuna admits that the mind is wild, forceful, and hard to restrain, almost like trying to catch the wind.
insight: It names the first obstacle clearly: the mind is not naturally obedient, so practice must begin with that fact.
modern_relevance: You sit down to pray, meditate, or even make one clean decision, and your thoughts scatter in every direction. The struggle is real before the discipline even begins.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचअसंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे महाबाहो  यह मन बड़ा चञ्चल है और इसका निग्रह करना भी बड़ा कठिन है  यह तुम्हारा कहना बिलकुल ठीक है ।  परन्तु हे कुन्तीनन्दन  अभ्यास और वैराग्यके द्वारा इसका निग्रह किया जाता है ॥
english_translation: The mind is hard to control, but it is mastered through practice and detachment.
essence: A restless mind is not a verdict; it is a training ground.
simple_meaning: The mind really is restless and difficult to control, but steady practice and letting go of cravings can bring it under control.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-criticism to patient training: repetition and release are the method.
modern_relevance: You sit down to meditate, and the same ten thoughts return before the timer ends. Instead of treating that as failure, you keep returning — again and again — until the mind learns a new habit.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः । वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥
translation: जिसका मन पूरा वशमें नहीं है, उसके द्वारा योग प्राप्त होना कठिन है ।  परन्तु उपायपूर्वक यत्न करनेवाले वश्यात्माको योग प्राप्त हो सकता है, ऐसा मेरा मत है ॥
english_translation: Yoga is hard to attain for one whose mind is not fully controlled. But for one who controls the mind and strives with the right method, it can be reached.
essence: Yoga becomes reachable when the mind is trained, not merely hoped for.
simple_meaning: A person ruled by an uncontrolled mind struggles to reach yoga. With self-control, steady effort, and the right method, yoga becomes possible.
insight: It shifts the focus from wishing for calm to building the control and method that make calm possible.
modern_relevance: You sit at the edge of a hard conversation, rehearsing and retreating at once. The problem is not the conversation itself; it is the mind that keeps slipping away from your intention.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचअयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे कृष्ण  जिसकी साधनमें श्रद्धा है, पर जिसका प्रयत्न शिथिल है, वह अन्तसमयमें अगर योगसे विचलितमना हो जाय, तो वह योगसिद्धिको प्राप्त न करके किस गतिको चला जाता है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: What happens to a person who has faith but lacks steady effort, whose mind turns away from yoga before full success is reached, O Krishna?
essence: Faith without completion still deserves a clear answer.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who begins with faith but loses steadiness before reaching full yogic success.
insight: It shifts the mind from judging failure to asking what remains of sincere effort.
modern_relevance: You start therapy, prayer, or a hard habit change with real hope, then life knocks you sideways. The question is whether a falter erases the sincerity that began the effort.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति । अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥
translation: हे महाबाहो  संसारके आश्रयसे रहित और परमात्मप्राप्तिके मार्गमें मोहित अर्थात् विचलित  इस तरह दोनों ओरसे भ्रष्ट हुआ साधक क्या छिन्नभिन्न बादलकी तरह नष्ट तो नहीं हो जाता ॥
english_translation: O mighty-armed one, does a person who has fallen from both sides, like a torn cloud, perish without support, deluded on the path of the supreme reality?
essence: Half-finished striving can feel like total ruin.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks whether a person who fails in both worldly life and spiritual practice is lost completely, like a torn cloud blown apart.
insight: It names the terror of spiritual failure and prepares the mind to seek reassurance beyond success or loss.
modern_relevance: You quit the job, leave the relationship, or walk away from the old identity — and then fear hits: what if the new path fails and the old one is already gone?
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः । त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥
translation: हे कृष्ण मेरे इस सन्देहका सर्वथा छेदन करनेके लिये आप ही योग्य हैं क्योंकि इस संशयका छेदन करनेवाला आपके सिवाय दूसरा कोई हो नहीं सकता ॥
english_translation: O Krishna, only you can fully cut away this doubt. No one else is able to remove it.
essence: Only clear seeing can end confusion completely.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to remove his doubt completely, saying no one else can resolve it.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-argument to seeking clear guidance from someone who sees beyond confusion.
modern_relevance: You keep circling the same decision at 1 a.m., reading opinions, still unsure. At some point, you need someone who can see the whole pattern and name the real issue.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचपार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते । नहि कल्याणकृत्कश्िचद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे पृथानन्दन  उसका न तो इस लोकमें और न परलोकमें ही विनाश होता है क्योंकि हे प्यारे  कल्याणकारी काम करनेवाला कोई भी मनुष्य दुर्गतिको प्राप्त नहीं जाता ॥
english_translation: Krishna said: O Partha, there is no destruction for him either here or hereafter. No one who does good ever comes to a bad end, my dear.
essence: Sincere effort toward the good cannot end in ruin.
simple_meaning: A person who does good practice does not lose everything. Even if progress feels interrupted, that effort is never destroyed and never leads to a bad end.
insight: It shifts the mind from fear of failure to trust in continued effort.
modern_relevance: You finally start therapy, meditation, or a hard apology, then stumble and feel you ruined everything. This verse says the effort still counts; one setback does not erase sincere movement.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः । शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ॥
translation: वह योगभ्रष्ट पुण्यकर्म करनेवालोंके लोकोंको प्राप्त होकर और वहाँ बहुत वर्षोंतक रहकर फिर यहाँ शुद्ध श्रीमानोंके घरमें जन्म लेता है ॥
english_translation: The one who falls from yoga reaches the worlds earned by good deeds, dwells there for many long years, and is then born again in the house of the pure and prosperous.
essence: A fall from yoga still carries you forward.
simple_meaning: A person who slips from yoga does not lose everything. After enjoying the results of good deeds for a long time, that person is born again in a pure, prosperous family.
insight: It shifts the mind from shame about interruption to trust in the continuity of practice.
modern_relevance: You meditated for months, then life derailed you. The verse says the effort did not vanish; it can return as a better beginning, not a failure.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम् । एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम् ॥
translation: अथवा वैराग्यवान् योगभ्रष्ट ज्ञानवान् योगियोंके कुलमें ही जन्म लेता है ।  इस प्रकारका जो यह जन्म है, यह संसारमें बहुत ही दुर्लभ है ॥
english_translation: Or he is born into the family of wise yogis. Such a birth is very rare in this world.
essence: A fallen practitioner is not lost; the next birth can restart the work.
simple_meaning: A person who falls from yoga may be born into a family of wise practitioners. That kind of birth is very rare.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing failure as loss to seeing it as a delayed continuation of practice.
modern_relevance: You feel like you wasted years after a relapse, a failed attempt, or a broken routine. The path is not erased; the next good environment can carry you forward again.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम् । यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥
translation: हे कुरुनन्दन  वहाँपर उसको पूर्वजन्मकृत साधनसम्पत्ति अनायास ही प्राप्त हो जाती है ।  फिर उससे वह साधनकी सिद्धिके विषयमें पुनः विशेषतासे यत्न करता है ॥
english_translation: O son of Kuru, there he effortlessly regains the spiritual understanding from his previous life. Then he strives again, with greater force, toward complete success.
essence: Nothing gained in sincere practice is ever truly lost.
simple_meaning: A person who falls from yoga does not lose everything. He regains the insight and practice from a former life and continues striving toward full success.
insight: It shifts the mind from fear of wasted effort to trust in accumulated practice.
modern_relevance: You return to a practice after months away and expect to start from zero. Something in you remembers. The old discipline is not gone; it waits to be reawakened.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः । जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥
translation: वह श्रीमानोंके घरमें जन्म लेनेवाला योगभ्रष्ट मनुष्य भोगोंके परवश होता हुआ भी पूर्वजन्ममें किये हुए अभ्याससाधन के कारण ही परमात्माकी तरफ खिंच जाता है क्योंकि योगसमता का जिज्ञासु भी वेदोंमें कहे हुए सकाम कर्मोंका अतिक्रमण कर जाता है ॥
english_translation: Even against his will, he is drawn onward by that earlier practice. Even the seeker of yoga goes beyond the sound of ritual words.
essence: Earlier practice keeps pulling you forward, even against resistance.
simple_meaning: Past practice pulls a person toward yoga even when the person is not fully in control. A sincere seeker also rises beyond ritual words and outer religious forms.
insight: It reframes spiritual effort as cumulative: even broken practice keeps carrying you forward.
modern_relevance: You open your meditation app after weeks of skipping it, and something in you still remembers the way. That quiet pull is not random — practice leaves a trail.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः । अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
translation: परन्तु जो योगी प्रयत्नपूर्वक यत्न करता है और जिसके पाप नष्ट हो गये हैं तथा जो अनेक जन्मोंसे सिद्ध हुआ है, वह योगी फिर परमगतिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: But the yogi who keeps striving with effort, whose impurities have been cleared, and who has been perfected through many births, reaches the highest goal.
essence: Persistent striving eventually ripens into the highest fulfillment.
simple_meaning: Persistent effort clears inner impurities, and over many lives of practice, the yogi reaches the highest goal.
insight: It shifts the mind from judging practice by speed to trusting cumulative transformation.
modern_relevance: You return to the mat after months away, stiff and distracted, wondering whether any of it still counts. It does. The effort itself keeps shaping you, even when progress feels invisible.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः । कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन ॥
translation: सकामभाववाले तपस्वियोंसे भी योगी श्रेष्ठ है, ज्ञानियोंसे भी योगी श्रेष्ठ है और कर्मियोंसे भी योगी श्रेष्ठ है  ऐसा मेरा मत है ।  अतः हे अर्जुन  तू योगी हो जा ॥
english_translation: The yogi is greater than ascetics, greater than scholars, and greater than workers. Therefore, Arjuna, become a yogi.
essence: Inner mastery outranks every outer path.
simple_meaning: Meditation and inner mastery are higher than harsh austerity, intellectual learning, or mere action. Krishna urges Arjuna to become a true yogi.
insight: It shifts the goal from collecting spiritual methods to becoming inwardly integrated.
modern_relevance: You can meditate for years, read every book, and still feel split when the hard choice arrives at midnight. The real test is whether your mind can stay centered when action is unavoidable.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: योगिनामपि सर्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना । श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः ॥
translation: सम्पूर्ण योगियोंमें भी जो श्रद्धावान् भक्त मुझमें तल्लीन हुए मनसे मेरा भजन करता है, वह मेरे मतमें सर्वश्रेष्ठ योगी है ॥
english_translation: Among all yogis, the one who worships me with trust, with the inner self absorbed in me, is considered the most fully united.
essence: Trusting devotion is the highest integration of yoga.
simple_meaning: Among all kinds of yogis, the one whose inner being is fixed on Krishna and who worships him with trust is the highest.
insight: It shifts the goal from technical mastery to wholehearted devotion, where inner attention and worship become one.
modern_relevance: You can master breathing exercises, routines, and self-control, yet still feel divided. The deepest integration comes when attention, trust, and love all point in one direction.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः । असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे पृथानन्दन  मुझमें आसक्त मनवाला, मेरे आश्रित होकर योगका अभ्यास करता हुआ तू मेरे समग्ररूपको निःसन्देह जैसा जानेगा, उसको सुन ॥
english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: Arjuna, fix your mind on Me, take refuge in Me, and practice yoga. Hear how you will know Me fully, without doubt.
essence: Refuge and practice open the way to complete knowing.
simple_meaning: Keep your mind focused on Krishna, rely on him, and practice yoga. Then you will come to know him fully and without doubt.
insight: It shifts the mind from scattered doubt to devoted attention, making full understanding possible.
modern_relevance: You are about to make a choice that will change a relationship, a career, or a life direction. Before the noise of opinions takes over, you steady the mind, lean on what is higher, and listen for what is true.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः । यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते ॥
translation: तेरे लिये मैं विज्ञानसहित ज्ञान सम्पूर्णतासे कहूँगा, जिसको जाननेके बाद फिर यहाँ कुछ भी जानना बाकी नहीं रहेगा ॥
english_translation: I will reveal to you knowledge together with direct realization in full. Knowing that, nothing more remains to be known here.
essence: Real knowing leaves no unfinished hunger for more.
simple_meaning: Krishna promises to explain both understanding and direct realization completely, so that after grasping it, nothing else needs to be learned about the matter.
insight: It shifts the mind from endless partial answers to a truth that settles the whole search.
modern_relevance: You finally ask the question you have avoided for years: whether to stay in the safe job, leave the relationship, or tell the truth. A real answer ends the spinning.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्िचद्यतति सिद्धये । यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्िचन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ॥
translation: हजारों मनुष्योंमें कोई एक वास्तविक सिद्धिके लिये यत्न करता है और उन यत्न करनेवाले सिद्धोंमें कोई एक ही मुझे तत्त्वसे जानता है ॥
english_translation: Among thousands of people, one may strive for perfection; among those striving, one may know Me in truth.
essence: True knowing is rarer than striving, even among the successful.
simple_meaning: Many people try to reach perfection, but very few reach true understanding of Krishna. Effort is common; real realization is rare.
insight: It shifts the mind from collecting effort to seeking direct realization.
modern_relevance: You read a dozen books, follow every step, and still feel something missing. The gap is not more information — it is the rare shift into direct understanding.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च । अहङ्कार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा ॥
translation: पृथ्वी, जल, तेज, वायु, आकाश  ये पञ्चमहाभूत और मन, बुद्धि तथा अहंकार  यह आठ प्रकारके भेदोंवाली मेरी अपरा प्रकृति है ।  हे महाबाहो  इस अपरा प्रकृतिसे भिन्न जीवरूप बनी हुई मेरी परा प्रकृतिको जान, जिसके द्वारा यह जगत् धारण किया जाता है ॥
english_translation: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and ego: this is My eightfold lower nature.
essence: What changes is not the whole of what you are.
simple_meaning: Krishna names eight parts of his lower nature: the five elements, mind, intellect, and ego. This is the material side of existence, not the highest reality.
insight: It shifts attention from identifying with the changing mind-body complex to seeing it as only the lower field.
modern_relevance: You are overwhelmed by your own reactions, your thoughts, and the noise around you. This verse helps you see those layers as parts of life, not the deepest truth about you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम् । जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत् ॥
translation: पृथ्वी, जल, तेज, वायु, आकाश  ये पञ्चमहाभूत और मन, बुद्धि तथा अहंकार  यह आठ प्रकारके भेदोंवाली मेरी अपरा प्रकृति है ।  हे महाबाहो  इस अपरा प्रकृतिसे भिन्न मेरी जीवरूपा बनी हुुई मेरी परा प्रकृतिको जान, जिसके द्वारा यह जगत् धारण किया जाता है ॥
english_translation: Know My higher nature, which is different from this lower nature, O mighty-armed one. By that living nature, this world is sustained.
essence: What sustains the world is subtler than what the senses first show.
simple_meaning: There is a higher nature beyond matter and mind. That living power holds up the whole world.
insight: It shifts attention from surface appearances to the sustaining principle underneath them.
modern_relevance: You look at a room full of charts, deadlines, and noise, and still feel something essential is missing. Krishna points to the deeper force that makes the whole system hold together.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय । अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा ॥
translation: अपरा और परा  इन दोनों प्रकृतियोंके संयोगसे ही सम्पूर्ण प्राणी उत्पन्न होते हैं, ऐसा तुम समझो ।  मैं सम्पूर्ण जगत् का प्रभव तथा प्रलय हूँ ॥
english_translation: Know that all beings are born from these two natures. I am the source and the dissolution of the entire universe.
essence: Everything that appears rises from one source and returns there.
simple_meaning: All beings arise from these two natures. Krishna says he is the source and end of the whole universe.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing life as isolated events to seeing one source behind all change.
modern_relevance: You watch a child, a career, or a relationship begin and end, and it feels fragile. This verse asks you to see the larger ground beneath every rise and collapse.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय । मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥
translation: हे धनञ्जय  मेरे बढ़कर इस जगत् का दूसरा कोई किञ्चिन्मात्र भी कारण नहीं है ।  जैसे सूतकी मणियाँ सूतके धागेमें पिरोयी हुई होती हैं, ऐसे ही यह सम्पूर्ण जगत् मेरेमें ही ओतप्रोत है ॥
english_translation: O Dhananjaya, nothing exists higher than Me. All this world is strung on Me like pearls on a thread.
essence: Everything is held in one sustaining reality.
simple_meaning: Krishna says nothing is greater than him, and the whole world is held together within him like beads on a string.
insight: It shifts the mind from scattered fragments to a single sustaining presence beneath all experience.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a hospital corridor, waiting for news that could change everything. The room feels isolated, but this verse says nothing is truly separate from the ground that holds it all.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभास्मि शशिसूर्ययोः । प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु ॥
translation: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  जलोंमें रस मैं हूँ, चन्द्रमा और सूर्यमें प्रभा प्रकाश मैं हूँ, सम्पूर्ण वेदोंमें प्रणव ओंकार मैं हूँ, आकाशमें शब्द और मनुष्योंमें पुरुषार्थ मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: O son of Kunti, I am the taste in water, the light in the moon and sun, the syllable Om in all the Vedas, the sound in space, and the valor in human beings.
essence: The sacred is already inside ordinary experience.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the life and meaning present in ordinary things: taste in water, light in the sun and moon, Om in the Vedas, sound in space, and strength in people.
insight: It shifts attention from searching for the divine elsewhere to recognising it in lived experience.
modern_relevance: You sip water after a long, anxious day and suddenly notice how simple relief can feel sacred. The same presence shows up in sunlight, music, breath, and the courage to keep going.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ । जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु ॥
translation: पृथ्वीमें पवित्र गन्ध मैं हूँ, और अग्निमें तेज मैं हूँ, तथा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें जीवनीशक्ति मैं हूँ और तपस्वियोंमें तपस्या मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: I am the pure fragrance in the earth, the radiance in fire, the life in all beings, and the austerity in ascetics.
essence: The sacred is already inside nature, vitality, and discipline.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is present as the earth’s fragrance, fire’s brilliance, the life in every creature, and the discipline of seekers.
insight: It shifts attention from seeking the divine elsewhere to recognising it in ordinary life and disciplined effort.
modern_relevance: You catch the smell of rain on dry soil, feel heat from a stove, or notice someone’s steady self-control. The sacred is not separate from these moments; it is already there.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम् । बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन  सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंका अनादि बीज मुझे जान ।  बुद्धिमानोंमें बुद्धि और तेजस्वियोंमें तेज मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Know Me, O Partha, as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the intelligence of the intelligent and the brilliance of the brilliant.
essence: All brilliance is borrowed from the same source.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the original source of every living being, and that intelligence and brilliance in people come from him.
insight: It shifts attention from personal pride to the shared source behind intelligence, vitality, and presence.
modern_relevance: You watch someone speak with rare clarity in a tense room and feel small beside them. The verse says that clarity itself is not privately owned; it flows from a deeper source.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: बलं बलवतामस्मि कामरागविवर्जितम् । धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  बलवालोंमें काम और रागसे रहित बल मैं हूँ ।  मनुषयोंमें धर्मसे अविरुद्ध धर्मयुक्त काम मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among the strong, I am strength free from desire and attachment. In beings, I am desire that does not oppose dharma, O best of the Bharatas.
essence: Strength becomes clean when desire no longer fights dharma.
simple_meaning: True strength is free from craving, and desire is right only when it does not fight against dharma.
insight: It teaches you to separate raw impulse from rightful desire and to use energy without inner conflict.
modern_relevance: You feel a surge of anger before sending the text. The force is real, but it does not have to become harm. Some wanting can move you forward without breaking your values.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये । मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि नत्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥
translation: और तो क्या कहूँ जितने भी सात्त्विक, राजस और तामस भाव हैं, वे सब मुझ से ही होते हैं  ऐसा समझो ।  पर मैं उनमें और वे मेरेमें नहीं हैं ॥
english_translation: Know that all states of being—sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic—arise from Me. I am not in them; they are in Me.
essence: All qualities arise in the divine, yet the divine is not bound by any of them.
simple_meaning: Every mode of nature—clear, restless, or dull—comes from Krishna. But Krishna is beyond all of them and is not confined by any one quality.
insight: It shifts attention from identifying with changing states to recognising the source behind them.
modern_relevance: You feel calm in the morning, driven by noon, numb by night, and then call one of those states “me.” This verse reminds you that moods pass through you; they are not your deepest identity.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत् । मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम् ॥
translation: किन्तु  इन तीनों गुणरूप भावोंसे मोहित यह सब जगत् इन गुणोंसे अतीत अविनाशी मुझे नहीं जानता ॥
english_translation: Deluded by these three qualities, the whole world does not know me, who am beyond them and imperishable.
essence: Three qualities can hide the imperishable reality from plain sight.
simple_meaning: The whole world gets confused by the three qualities of nature and fails to recognize Krishna as the imperishable reality beyond them.
insight: It shifts the mind from reacting inside appearances to asking what lies beyond them.
modern_relevance: You are certain a person is being difficult, but your own anger is coloring every word they say. This verse points to the hidden filter that keeps reality from being seen clearly.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया । मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥
translation: क्योंकि मेरी यह गुणमयी दैवी माया बड़ी दुरत्यय है अर्थात् इससे पार पाना बड़ा कठिन है ।  जो केवल मेरे ही शरण होते हैं, वे इस मायाको तर जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: My divine illusion, made of the three qualities, is hard to cross. Only those who take refuge in Me go beyond it.
essence: The way beyond the veil is not force, but refuge.
simple_meaning: The forces that shape ordinary life are hard to overcome on your own. Surrendering to Krishna is what carries a person beyond them.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance against confusion to surrender as the way through confusion.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to think your way out of the same loop at 1:40 a.m., replaying the conversation, the mistake, the fear. The verse says the exit is not more strain, but a deeper refuge.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः । माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः ॥
translation: मायाके द्वारा अपहृत ज्ञानवाले, आसुर भावका आश्रय लेनेवाले और मनुष्योंमें महान् नीच तथा पापकर्म करनेवाले मूढ़ मनुष्य मेरे शरण नहीं होते । ९ ॥
english_translation: The deluded, the lowest among people, the wrongdoers, and those whose understanding has been stolen by the veil do not turn to me. They take refuge in a shadowed nature instead.
essence: A corrupted mind cannot recognise what would free it.
simple_meaning: People who are deeply confused, morally corrupt, and trapped by the veil do not turn toward the divine. They lean into a destructive nature instead.
insight: It shifts attention from asking why truth is absent to seeing how inner resistance blocks it.
modern_relevance: Someone hears the truth twice, then laughs it off a third time. The issue is no longer lack of information; the refusal has become a habit of character.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन । आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुनव  पवित्र कर्म करनेवाले अर्थार्थी, आर्त, जिज्ञासु और ज्ञानी अर्थात् प्रेमी  ये चार प्रकारके मनुष्य मेरा भजन करते हैं अर्थात् मेरे शरण होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Four kinds of virtuous people worship Me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise one, O best of the Bharatas.
essence: Different needs can still lead to one real turning toward the divine.
simple_meaning: People come to Krishna for different reasons: pain, curiosity, gain, or wisdom. All four are counted among the virtuous.
insight: It expands the idea of devotion beyond purity tests and shows that sincere seeking matters more than perfect motives.
modern_relevance: A person opens a prayer app after a panic attack, another after reading a hard question, another because life feels empty, another because they finally want what is true. The door is open to all of them.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्ितर्विशिष्यते । प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः ॥
translation: उन चार भक्तोंमें मेरेमें निरन्तर लगा हुआ, अनन्यभक्तिवाला ज्ञानी अर्थात् प्रेमी भक्त श्रेष्ठ है क्योंकि ज्ञानी भक्तको मैं अत्यन्त प्रिय हूँ और वह भी मेरेको अत्यन्त प्रिय है ॥
english_translation: Among those four, the wise devotee who is ever united and one-pointed is श्रेष्ठ. For I am exceedingly dear to the wise one, and the wise one is dear to me.
essence: Deep knowing and devoted love become a mutual bond.
simple_meaning: Among the four kinds of devotees, the wise one who is constantly devoted and single-minded stands highest. Krishna says this devotee is very dear to him, and he is very dear to that devotee.
insight: It shifts devotion from neediness to intimate understanding.
modern_relevance: You finally understand someone you once only admired from a distance. The relationship changes when attention, trust, and knowledge stop competing and start reinforcing each other.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् । आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥
translation: पहले कहे हुए सबकेसब भक्त बड़े उदार श्रेष्ठ भाववाले हैं ।  परन्तु ज्ञानी प्रेमी तो मेरा स्वरूप ही है  ऐसा मेरा मत है ।  कारण कि वह युक्तात्मा है और जिससे श्रेष्ठ दूसरी कोई गति नहीं है, ऐसे मेरेमें ही दृढ़ आस्थावाला है ॥
english_translation: All these are noble indeed, but the wise devotee is My very self. Established in yoga, that person is steadfast in Me as the unsurpassed goal.
essence: Deep knowing turns devotion into identity.
simple_meaning: All four kinds of devotees are good, but the wise devotee is the closest to Krishna. Such a person is firmly united with him and sees him as the highest goal.
insight: It shifts devotion from asking for help to recognising intimate union with the divine.
modern_relevance: You have read every argument, sat through every doubt, and still feel pulled toward the same calling. At that point, knowing stops being abstract and becomes a bond that changes who you are.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते । वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः ॥
translation: बहुत जन्मोंके अन्तमें अर्थात् मनुष्यजन्ममें सब कुछ परमात्मा ही है, ऐसा जो ज्ञानवान् मेरे शरण होता है, वह महात्मा अत्यन्त दुर्लभ है ॥
english_translation: After many births, the wise one surrenders to Me, knowing that Vasudeva is everything. Such a great soul is very rare.
essence: Deep seeing ends in surrender to the one reality in all things.
simple_meaning: Real understanding ripens over many lives. At its peak, a person sees that everything is the divine and naturally turns in surrender.
insight: It shifts the mind from fragmented seeking to whole-hearted surrender.
modern_relevance: You keep searching for one more fix, one more answer, one more sign. Then a quiet certainty lands: nothing is separate, and the need to grasp begins to loosen.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः । तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया ॥
translation: उनउन कामनाओंसे जिनका ज्ञान अपहृत हो गया है, ऐसे वे मनुष्य अपनीअपनी प्रकृतिसे नियन्त्रित होकर देवताओंके उनउन नियमोंको धारण करते हुए उनउन देवताओंके शरण हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Driven by desire, people whose understanding has been taken away turn to other radiant beings. They follow the rules of each, shaped by their own nature.
essence: Desire clouds judgment and sends the mind toward smaller refuges.
simple_meaning: When desire overwhelms clear thinking, people begin seeking help from other powers and follow whatever practices fit their own nature.
insight: It shifts attention from impulse-driven seeking to the need for clear seeing before commitment.
modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone, hoping one more answer will calm you. In that restless state, you start handing your attention to whatever promises relief, even if it never frees you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति । तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् ॥
translation: जोजो भक्त जिसजिस देवताका श्रद्धापूर्वक पूजन करना चाहता है, उसउस देवताके प्रति मैं उसकी श्रद्धाको दृढ़ कर देता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Whatever form a devotee wants to worship with faith, I make that faith firm in that very form.
essence: Faith becomes firm where the devotee turns.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he strengthens a devotee's faith in whatever form that devotee wishes to worship.
insight: It shifts attention from judging other forms of devotion to seeing faith itself as something nurtured and deepened.
modern_relevance: You keep returning to the same prayer, the same image, the same practice, even when your mind wanders. What feels like your own devotion is being quietly strengthened.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते । लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान् हि तान् ॥
translation: उस मेरे द्वारा दृढ़ की हुई श्रद्धासे युक्त होकर वह मनुष्य सकामभावपूर्वक उस देवताकी उपासना करता है और उसकी वह कामना पूरी भी होती है परन्तु वह कामनापूर्ति मेरे द्वारा विहित की हुई होती है ॥
english_translation: Endowed with that faith, that person seeks that worship, and receives those desires, granted by Me alone.
essence: Faith draws the result, but the deeper order grants it.
simple_meaning: A person with strong faith turns to that chosen deity and gets the desired result, but even that fulfillment is ultimately arranged by Krishna.
insight: It shifts attention from the visible object of worship to the deeper source that makes any result possible.
modern_relevance: You finally get the opportunity you prayed for, and it feels completely earned. This verse asks you to notice the hidden order behind the result, not just your effort.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम् । देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि ॥
translation: परन्तु उन अल्पबुद्धिवाले मनुष्योंको उन देवताओंकी आराधनाका फल अन्तवाला नाशवान् ही मिलता है ।  देवताओंका पूजन करनेवाले देवताओंको प्राप्त होते हैं और मेरे भक्त मेरे ही प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
english_translation: But the reward gained by those of limited understanding is finite. Those who worship the radiant beings go to the radiant beings; my devotees come to me.
essence: Finite worship brings finite results; devotion returns you to Krishna.
simple_meaning: Half-hearted understanding gives limited results. Those who worship lesser powers reach those powers, while Krishna's devotees reach Krishna.
insight: It shifts attention from short-term gains to the object of devotion itself.
modern_relevance: You keep checking three different opinions before sending the message that matters. The mind wants a safe outcome, but the heart follows the thing it truly serves.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अव्यक्तं व्यक्ितमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः । परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम् ॥
translation: बुद्धिहीन मनुष्य मेरे सर्वश्रेष्ठ अविनाशी परमभावको न जानते हुए अव्यक्त मनइन्द्रियोंसे पर मुझ सच्चिदानन्दघन परमात्माको मनुष्यकी तरह ही शरीर धारण करनेवाला मानते हैं ॥
english_translation: The unwise think I have taken a visible form from the unseen. They do not know my imperishable, supreme nature.
essence: Form can hide the imperishable reality beneath it.
simple_meaning: People without clear understanding think Krishna has taken on a limited human body. They do not recognize his imperishable, highest nature beyond what the senses can see.
insight: It shifts the mind from judging by appearance to recognising a deeper reality beyond form.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary, and you dismiss the depth behind their calm face. Later you realise you were only seeing the surface. This verse warns against shrinking what is vast into what is familiar.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः । मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम् ॥
translation: जो मूढ़ मनुष्य मेरेको अज और अविनाशी ठीक तरहसे नहीं जानते मानते, उन सबके सामने योगमायासे अच्छी तरहसे आवृत हुआ मैं प्रकट नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: Veiled by yoga-maya, I am not visible to everyone. Deluded people do not recognize me as unborn and imperishable.
essence: The hidden divine is missed by confused seeing, not by absence.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is hidden from people who are confused. They do not recognize his unborn, unchanging nature because their minds are covered by the veil of appearance.
insight: It shifts attention from demanding proof to clearing the mind that cannot recognize what is already present.
modern_relevance: You can sit beside someone who loves you and still miss what they are trying to say because your mind is already defending itself. The problem is often not absence, but distorted seeing.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन । भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन ॥
translation: हे अर्जुन  जो प्राणी भूतकालमें हो चुके हैं, तथा जो वर्तमानमें हैं और जो भविष्यमें होंगे, उन सब प्राणियोंको तो मैं जानता हूँ परन्तु मेरेको कोई मूढ़ मनुष्य नहीं जानता ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, I know all beings of the past, the present, and the future. No one knows me.
essence: Everything is visible to the divine; the divine remains unseen to ordinary minds.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he knows every being across past, present, and future, but no ordinary person truly knows him.
insight: It shifts the mind from collecting information to recognising the limits of ordinary perception.
modern_relevance: You can track every detail of a relationship, a project, or a crisis and still miss the one thing that matters most. Knowing facts is not the same as knowing what stands behind them.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत । सर्वभूतानि संमोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशमें उत्पन्न परंतप  इच्छा राग और द्वेषसे उत्पन्न होनेवाले द्वन्द्वमोहसे मोहित सम्पूर्ण प्राणी संसारमें मूढ़ताको अर्थात् जन्ममरणको प्राप्त हो रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: O descendant of Bharata, all beings fall into delusion at birth, from the confusion born of desire and aversion, O scorcher of foes.
essence: Desire and aversion turn clear seeing into confusion.
simple_meaning: Desire and aversion create confusion in living beings, and that confusion keeps them trapped in repeated cycles of ignorance and rebirth.
insight: It shifts the mind from blaming itself to noticing the forces of attraction and rejection that distort judgment.
modern_relevance: You know the moment you want one thing badly and hate the other option so much that you cannot think clearly. That tug-of-war is the very fog Krishna names.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम् । ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः ॥
translation: परन्तु जिन पुण्यकर्मा मनुष्योंके पाप नष्ट गये हैं, वे द्वन्द्वमोहसे रहित हुए मनुष्य दृढ़व्रती होकर मेरा भजन करते हैं ॥
english_translation: But those whose wrongdoing has been cleared away, and whose good deeds have matured, are freed from confusion and worship me with firm resolve.
essence: Clear hearts stop wavering and move toward the divine with resolve.
simple_meaning: People whose harmful impulses have been cleared and whose good actions have ripened are no longer torn by confusion. With steady commitment, they turn toward Krishna.
insight: It shifts the focus from divided impulse to steadiness of commitment.
modern_relevance: You sit in the car after a hard conversation, replaying every sentence and feeling split in two. The mind that has stopped feeding its own confusion can finally choose cleanly.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये । ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम् ॥
translation: जरा वृद्धावस्था और मरण मृत्यु से मोक्ष पानेके लिये जो मेरा आश्रय लेकर प्रयत्न करते हैं, वे उस ब्रह्मको, सम्पूर्ण अध्यात्मको और सम्पूर्ण कर्मको भी जान जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who, seeking release from old age and death, take refuge in me, come to know Brahman, the whole field of the inner life, and all action.
essence: Refuge in the divine opens total understanding of reality, inner life, and action.
simple_meaning: Those who take refuge in Krishna and strive for freedom from aging and death come to know the supreme reality, the whole inner life, and all action.
insight: It shifts the mind from fearing mortality to seeking the whole pattern behind existence and action.
modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed after hearing a diagnosis, and suddenly every theory about life feels thin. The deeper search for relief can open a wider understanding than comfort alone ever could.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः । प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य अधिभूत, अधिदैव और अधियज्ञके सहित मुझे जानते हैं, वे युक्तचेता मनुष्य अन्तकालमें भी मुझे ही जानते हैं अर्थात् प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who know me together with the physical realm, the radiant powers, and the inner sacrifice know me even at the time of death.
essence: Complete understanding remains steady even at the moment of departure.
simple_meaning: Those who understand Krishna as present in the physical world, the divine powers, and the ritual offering remember him even at death.
insight: It shifts the mind from partial religious ideas to a unified vision of reality.
modern_relevance: At a bedside when machines are beeping and everyone is silent, the mind does not reach for trivia. It reaches for what was truly known. This verse points to a clarity strong enough to stay present at the end.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचकिं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम । अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे पुरुषोत्तम  वह ब्रह्म क्या है अध्यात्म क्या है कर्म क्या है अधिभूत किसको कहा गया है और अधिदैव किसको कहा जाता है यहाँ अधियज्ञ कौन है और वह इस देहमें कैसे है हे मधूसूदन  नियतात्मा वशीभूत अंतःकरण वाले मनुष्यके द्वारा अन्तकालमें आप कैसे जाननेमें आते हैं ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: O Supreme Person, what is Brahman? What is the self? What is action? What is called the field of changing things, and what is called the divine principle? What is the sacred offering here in this body, and how are you known at the time of death by those with disciplined minds?
essence: Clear seeing starts by asking what each word truly means.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain the key terms of spiritual teaching: Brahman, the self, action, the changing world, and the divine principle.
insight: It shifts the mind from vague belief to precise inquiry about what is real.
modern_relevance: You are standing at a hospital door, a resignation letter in your hand, or a graveside with no easy answers. Before certainty comes, honest questions have to be named.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन । प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे पुरुषोत्तम  वह ब्रह्म क्या है अध्यात्म क्या है कर्म क्या है अधिभूत किसको कहा गया है और अधिदैव किसको कहा जाता है यहाँ अधियज्ञ कौन है और वह इस देहमें कैसे है हे मधूसूदन  नियतात्मा वशीभूत अन्तःकरणवाले मनुष्यके द्वारा अन्तकालमें आप कैसे जाननेमें आते हैं ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: O Madhusudana, who is the sacrifice here, and how does he dwell in this body? And at the time of death, how are you known by those with disciplined minds?
essence: Real understanding begins by asking what remains when life is ending.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks who the inner sacrificer is, how that presence lives in the body, and how a disciplined person can know Krishna at death.
insight: It shifts the mind from vague belief to precise questioning about the deepest reality.
modern_relevance: You are standing in a hospital corridor, waiting for news that could change everything. The mind wants one clear answer: what truly matters now, and how do I hold it when time is running out?
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचअक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते । भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  परम अक्षर ब्रह्म है और जीवका अपना जो होनापन है, उसको अध्यात्म कहते हैं ।  प्राणियों का उद्भव सत्ता को प्रकट करनेवाला जो त्याग है उसको कर्म कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: The imperishable is the supreme reality. One's own nature is called the inner self. The offering that brings beings into existence is called action.
essence: What lasts, what you are, and what you do are not the same.
simple_meaning: The imperishable is the highest reality. Inner nature is called the inner self, and the act that brings beings into existence is called action.
insight: It shifts the mind from vague spiritual language to precise categories: reality, nature, and action.
modern_relevance: You are trying to name what matters while everything is already moving toward a hard decision. Before you can act cleanly, you need to know what is lasting, what is your nature, and what is simply an act.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम् । अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर ॥
translation: हे देहधारियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  क्षरभाव अर्थात् नाशवान् पदार्थको अधिभूत कहते हैं, पुरुष अर्थात् हिरण्यगर्भ ब्रह्माजी अधिदैव हैं और इस देहमें अन्तर्यामीरूपसे मैं ही अधियज्ञ हूँ ॥
english_translation: The perishable world is the lower realm; the cosmic person is the radiant being. I am the inner witness of sacrifice in this body, Arjuna.
essence: The changing world, the cosmic order, and the inner witness are not separate.
simple_meaning: The changing world is called the lower realm. The cosmic person is called the radiant being. In this body, Krishna says he himself is the inner witness of sacrifice.
insight: It shifts attention from outer labels to the hidden presence that makes action meaningful.
modern_relevance: You are trying to understand what really matters before a hard goodbye, a hospital room, or a final decision. The mind wants labels; the teaching points to the deeper order behind them.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम् । यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य अन्तकालमें भी मेरा स्मरण करते हुए शरीर छोड़कर जाता है, वह मेरे स्वरुप को ही प्राप्त होता है, इसमें सन्देह नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Whoever remembers Me at the end and leaves the body attains My state; there is no doubt.
essence: The last remembered presence shapes the next state of being.
simple_meaning: A person who remembers Krishna at the moment of death and leaves the body reaches Krishna's state without doubt.
insight: It shifts attention from physical ending to the quality of final remembrance.
modern_relevance: You are sitting beside a hospital bed, trying to stay steady while everything is slipping away. What the mind holds in that last, fragile moment may matter more than the words anyone says.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् । तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥
translation: हे कुन्तीपुत्र अर्जुन  मनुष्य अन्तकाल में जिसजिस भी भावका स्मरण करते हुए शरीर छोड़ता है वह उस अन्तकालके भावसे सदा भावित होता हुआ उसउसको ही प्राप्त होता है अर्थात् उसउस योनिमें ही चला जाता है ॥
english_translation: Whatever state a person remembers at the end, that state is reached, because the mind has been shaped by it.
essence: The end follows the state you have trained.
simple_meaning: The final thought at death shapes where consciousness goes next. A person tends toward whatever state has been cultivated again and again.
insight: It shifts attention from the last moment alone to the whole pattern of what the mind has been fed.
modern_relevance: You lie awake after a hard conversation, replaying the same fear. That repeated inner loop does not just reflect you — it trains the direction your mind takes next.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम् ॥
translation: इसलिये तू सब समयमें मेरा स्मरण कर और युद्ध भी कर ।  मेरेमें मन और बुद्धि अर्पित करनेवाला तू निःसन्देह मेरेको ही प्राप्त होगा ॥
english_translation: Therefore, remember Me at all times and fight. With mind and intellect offered to Me, you will surely come to Me.
essence: Action and remembrance can happen together without conflict.
simple_meaning: Keep the divine in mind all the time, do your duty, and place your thoughts and understanding there. Then you will surely reach the divine.
insight: It joins outer duty with inward remembrance, so action no longer fragments the mind.
modern_relevance: You are in the middle of a hard conversation, heart racing, ready to back away. This verse says you can stay present, do what must be done, and keep your attention anchored.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना । परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन् ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन  अभ्यासयोगसे युक्त और अन्यका चिन्तन न करनेवाले चित्तसे परम दिव्य पुरुषका चिन्तन करता हुआ शरीर छोड़नेवाला मनुष्य उसीको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: One who departs while remembering the divine person with a mind trained by practice and fixed on nothing else reaches that supreme divine being, O Partha.
essence: What the mind has practiced most will claim you at the end.
simple_meaning: A mind trained by steady practice, and not wandering to other things, reaches the supreme divine being when life ends.
insight: It shifts attention from last-minute panic to lifelong mental training.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone in the hospital waiting room, trying to stay steady before the call comes. What your mind has practiced returning to will meet you in the hardest moment.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कविं पुराणमनुशासितारमणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्यः । सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूपमादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् ॥
translation: जो सर्वज्ञ, पुराण, शासन करनेवाला, सूक्ष्मसेसूक्ष्म, सबका धारणपोषण करनेवाला, अज्ञानसे अत्यन्त परे, सूर्यकी तरह प्रकाशस्वरूप  ऐसे अचिन्त्य स्वरूपका चिन्तन करता है ॥
english_translation: Whoever remembers the wise, ancient, ruler, subtler than the subtle, supporter of all, beyond thought, radiant like the sun, and beyond darkness...
essence: Hold the ungraspable source in mind, not the passing form.
simple_meaning: Remember the supreme reality as wise, ancient, subtle, sustaining everything, beyond thought, radiant, and beyond darkness.
insight: It shifts remembrance from a person or image to the ungraspable source behind all forms.
modern_relevance: At the bedside of someone you love, words stop working. What remains is the quiet turning of attention toward what is steady when everything else is slipping.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: प्रयाणकाले मनसाऽचलेनभक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव । भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक्स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥
translation: वह भक्तियुक्त मनुष्य अन्तसमयमें अचल मनसे और योगबलके द्वारा भृकुटीके मध्यमें प्राणोंको अच्छी तरहसे प्रविष्ट करके शरीर छोड़नेपर उस परम दिव्य पुरुषको ही प्राप्त होता है ॥
english_translation: At the time of departure, one who leaves the body with an unmoving mind, devotion, and the power of yoga, placing the life-force between the eyebrows, reaches the divine supreme person.
essence: Steady devotion carries awareness beyond the body's final threshold.
simple_meaning: At death, a devoted person who keeps the mind steady and directs the life-force with yogic focus reaches the divine supreme person.
insight: It shifts attention from the fear of leaving the body to the quality of awareness at the moment of leaving.
modern_relevance: A surgeon says, 'We need a decision now,' and your chest tightens. This verse points to the kind of inner steadiness that lets a person meet the last, hardest moment without panic.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्तिविशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः । यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्तितत्ते पदं संग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये ॥
translation: वेदवेत्ता लोग जिसको अक्षर कहते हैं, वीतराग यति जिसको प्राप्त करते हैं और साधक जिसकी प्राप्तिकी इच्छा करते हुए ब्रह्मचर्यका पालन करते हैं, वह पद मैं तेरे लिये संक्षेपसे कहूँगा ॥
english_translation: I will briefly tell you that imperishable state, which the knowers of the Vedas call imperishable, which the detached ascetics enter, and which seekers follow through celibate discipline.
essence: The imperishable is reached by giving up desire, not by feeding it.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he will briefly describe the imperishable state that Vedic knowers speak of, detached ascetics enter, and disciplined seekers approach through celibate practice.
insight: It shifts the mind from pursuit of experience to release of craving as the condition for deeper realization.
modern_relevance: You are staring at the message that could change your life, but you keep refreshing instead of answering. The thing that matters most often arrives only when craving stops driving the hand.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च । मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम् ॥
translation: इन्द्रियोंके सम्पूर्ण द्वारोंको रोककर मनका हृदयमें निरोध करके और अपने प्राणोंको मस्तकमें स्थापित करके योगधारणामें सम्यक् प्रकारसे स्थित हुआ जो ऊँ इस एक अक्षर ब्रह्मका उच्चारण और मेरा स्मरण करता हुआ शरीरको छोड़कर जाता है, वह परमगतिको प्राप्त होता है ॥
english_translation: Closing all the doors of the senses, holding the mind in the heart, and placing the life-force in the head, one remains fixed in yoga-discipline.
essence: Mastery of the senses and mind prepares one for the final passage.
simple_meaning: At the moment of death, the practitioner shuts the senses, steadies the mind in the heart, and places the life-force at the head through yoga practice.
insight: It shifts the mind from accidental reaction to deliberate inner control.
modern_relevance: A hospital room goes quiet after bad news. Instead of scattering into fear, you can gather yourself, steady your breath, and meet the moment with trained attention.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् । यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
translation: इन्द्रियोंके सम्पूर्ण द्वारोंको रोककर मनका हृदयमें निरोध करके और अपने प्राणोंको मस्तकमें स्थापित करके योगधारणामें सम्यक् प्रकारसे स्थित हुआ जो साधक ऊँ इस एक अक्षर ब्रह्मका उच्चारण और मेरा स्मरण करता हुआ शरीरको छोड़कर जाता है, वह परमगतिको प्राप्त होता है ॥
english_translation: Uttering Om, the one-syllable Brahman, and remembering Me, one who departs while leaving the body attains the supreme state.
essence: Final remembrance can carry consciousness beyond the body.
simple_meaning: A person who leaves the body while remembering Om and Krishna reaches the highest destination.
insight: It shifts attention from panic at death to the quality of awareness carried into the final release.
modern_relevance: At a bedside, a family member grips your hand and the room goes quiet. In that stripped-down moment, what the mind holds most deeply matters more than anything spoken before.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः । तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन  अनन्यचित्तवाला जो मनुष्य मेरा नित्यनिरन्तर स्मरण करता है, उस नित्ययुक्त योगीके लिये मैं सुलभ हूँ अर्थात् उसको सुलभतासे प्राप्त हो जाता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, for the one whose mind is wholly on me and who remembers me constantly, I am easy to reach.
essence: Constant remembrance makes the divine easy to reach.
simple_meaning: A mind that stays focused on Krishna and remembers him continually finds him easy to reach.
insight: It shifts devotion from occasional feeling to continuous remembrance.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone before a hard conversation, trying to steady yourself. The mind that keeps returning to what matters becomes less scattered and more able to meet the moment.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम् । नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः ॥
translation: महात्मालोग मुझे प्राप्त करके दुःखालय और अशाश्वत पुनर्जन्मको प्राप्त नहीं होते क्योंकि वे परमसिद्धिको प्राप्त हो गये हैं अर्थात् उनको परम प्रेमकी प्राप्ति हो गयी है ॥
english_translation: Great souls who reach me do not return to this painful, temporary cycle of birth.
essence: True arrival ends the need to come back.
simple_meaning: Those who reach Krishna do not come back into the painful cycle of birth and death. They have reached the highest fulfillment.
insight: It shifts the goal from temporary relief to final release from the cycle of return.
modern_relevance: You finally get what you thought would fix everything, and it still feels unfinished. This verse points to a deeper arrival, where the old hunger to keep chasing simply stops.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन । मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते ॥
translation: हे अर्जुन  ब्रह्मलोकतक सभी लोक पुनरावर्ती है परन्तु हे कौन्तेय  मुझे प्राप्त होनेपर पुनर्जन्म नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: All worlds up to Brahma's realm return again, Arjuna. But having reached me, O son of Kunti, there is no rebirth.
essence: Even the highest attainments return, but union with Krishna does not.
simple_meaning: Even the highest realms are temporary and lead back into rebirth. Only reaching Krishna ends that cycle completely.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing better conditions to seeking what ends the entire cycle of return.
modern_relevance: You finally get what you wanted, and the relief lasts a week. Then the old restlessness comes back. This verse points to a security that does not wear out.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः । रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य ब्रह्माके एक हज़ार चतुर्युगीवाले एक दिनको और सहस्त्र चतुर्युगीपर्यन्त एक रातको जानते हैं, वे मनुष्य ब्रह्माके दिन और रातको जाननेवाले हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who know that Brahma’s day lasts a thousand yugas, and his night lasts a thousand yugas, know day and night truly.
essence: Cosmic time reveals how small ordinary urgency is.
simple_meaning: Some people understand the vast scale of Brahma's day and night. They can see time on a cosmic scale, not just as ordinary human hours.
insight: It shifts attention from human-scale urgency to cosmic rhythm, making creation and dissolution feel natural rather than absolute.
modern_relevance: You watch a deadline panic swallow the whole week, then remember the project is one cycle inside a much larger life. The pressure loosens when time stops feeling like a cage.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे । रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके ॥
translation: ब्रह्माजीके दिनके आरम्भकालमें अव्यक्त ब्रह्माजीके सूक्ष्मशरीर से सम्पूर्ण प्राणी पैदा होते हैं और ब्रह्माजीकी रातके आरम्भकालमें उसी अव्यक्तमें सम्पूर्ण प्राणी लीन हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: At the start of Brahma's day, all beings arise from the unmanifest; at the start of Brahma's night, they dissolve back into that same unmanifest.
essence: Everything formed returns to the unmanifest in time.
simple_meaning: All beings emerge from the unmanifest at the beginning of Brahma's day and return to it at the beginning of Brahma's night.
insight: It shifts the mind from panic about endings to seeing change as part of a larger cycle.
modern_relevance: You watch a relationship, a job, or even your own plans fall apart and feel like everything is ending. This verse zooms out: forms come, forms go, and the deeper pattern continues.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते । रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे ॥
translation: हे पार्थ  वही यह प्राणिसमुदाय उत्पन्न होहोकर प्रकृतिके परवश हुआ ब्रह्माके दिनके समय उत्पन्न होता है और ब्रह्माकी रात्रिके समय लीन होता है ॥
english_translation: O Arjuna, this entire group of beings is born again and again, and is dissolved at the coming of night; at the coming of day, it rises again, helplessly.
essence: All formed things return and rise again under nature’s compulsion.
simple_meaning: All living beings keep arising and dissolving again and again. They do so under the pull of nature, not by choice.
insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to temporary forms toward seeing their repeated rising and falling as natural.
modern_relevance: You build a life, a role, a relationship, then watch it shift overnight. What felt fixed was always moving through a larger rhythm you do not control.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः । यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति ॥
translation: परन्तु उस अव्यक्त ब्रह्माजीके सूक्ष्मशरीर से अन्य अनादि सर्वश्रेष्ठ भावरूप जो अव्यक्त है, उसका सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके नष्ट होनेपर भी नाश नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: Beyond that unmanifest is another, eternal unmanifest. Even when all beings perish, it does not perish.
essence: What is deepest in reality cannot be destroyed by any ending.
simple_meaning: There is something beyond the visible world that is eternal and cannot be destroyed, even when all living things disappear.
insight: It shifts attention from what changes and disappears to what remains present through every change.
modern_relevance: You watch a relationship, a career, or a plan fall apart and feel the floor disappear. This verse says the deepest ground of reality is still there, untouched by the collapse.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम् । यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
translation: उसीको अव्यक्त और अक्षर कहा गया है और उसीको परमगति कहा गया है तथा जिसको प्राप्त होनेपर जीव फिर लौटकर नहीं आते, वह मेरा परमधाम है ॥
english_translation: That is called the unmanifest and the imperishable. It is the highest goal. Having reached it, one does not return. It is my supreme abode.
essence: The highest arrival is beyond return.
simple_meaning: The highest reality is beyond change and form. Whoever reaches it does not come back to the cycle of repeated return.
insight: It shifts the mind from temporary achievement to final release from return.
modern_relevance: You finally choose the harder right over the easier wrong, and something in you knows there is no going back. This verse speaks to that irreversible threshold.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया । यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन अर्जुन  सम्पूर्ण प्राणी जिसके अन्तर्गत हैं और जिससे यह सम्पूर्ण संसार व्याप्त है, वह परम पुरुष परमात्मा तो अनन्यभक्तिसे प्राप्त होनेयोग्य है ॥
english_translation: O Arjuna, the supreme person is reached through undivided devotion. All beings dwell within that being, and this entire world is pervaded by that being.
essence: Undivided devotion reaches the one presence that holds all beings.
simple_meaning: The supreme person is reached through single-pointed devotion. That presence holds all beings within it and fills the whole world.
insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to direct recognition of shared presence in all beings.
modern_relevance: You sit in your car after a painful phone call, knowing you must answer honestly. The courage comes easier when you remember the person you face is not separate from the whole web of life.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः । प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  जिस काल अर्थात् मार्गमें शरीर छोड़कर गये हुए योगी अनावृत्तिको प्राप्त होते हैं अर्थात् पीछे लौटकर नहीं आते और जिस मार्गमें गये हुए आवृत्तिको प्राप्त होते हैं अर्थात् पीछे लौटकर आते हैं, उस कालको अर्थात् दोनों मार्गोंको मैं कहूँगा ॥
english_translation: I will tell you of the time when yogis do not return, and the time when they do, O best of the Bharatas.
essence: Not every departure leads the same way; some paths return you, others do not.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he will explain which departing moments lead to no return and which lead back into return.
insight: It shifts attention from the act of leaving to the quality of the path being taken.
modern_relevance: You leave a relationship, a job, or a habit and feel the difference immediately: one choice frees you, another pulls you back into the same cycle. This verse points to that hidden direction.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् । तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥
translation: जिस मार्गमें प्रकाशस्वरूप अग्निका अधिपति देवता, दिनका अधिपति देवता, शुक्लपक्षका अधिपति देवता, और छः महीनोंवाले उत्तरायणका अधिपति देवता है, शरीर छोड़कर उस मार्गसे गये हुए ब्रह्मवेत्ता पुरुष पहले ब्रह्मलोकको प्राप्त होकर पीछे ब्रह्माजीके साथ ब्रह्मको प्राप्त हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Fire, daylight, the bright fortnight, and the six months of the northward course: those who depart then, knowing the supreme reality, go to the supreme reality.
essence: The final passage opens for those who know the supreme reality.
simple_meaning: Those who leave the body during an auspicious path of light and know the supreme reality reach that supreme reality.
insight: It shifts attention from fear of death to the clarity with which one meets the final moment.
modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed, signing a document you never wanted to sign. The mind wants certainty, but the teaching points to the quality of consciousness at the threshold, not the panic around it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् । तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते ॥
translation: जिस मार्गमें धूमका अधिपति देवता, रात्रिका अधिपति देवता, कृष्णपक्षका अधिपति देवता और छः महीनोंवाले दक्षिणायनका अधिपति देवता है, शरीर छोड़कर उस मार्गसे गया हुआ योगी सकाम मनुष्य चन्द्रमाकी ज्योतिको प्राप्त होकर लौट आता है अर्थात् जन्ममरणको प्राप्त होता है ॥
english_translation: In the path ruled by smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the six months of the southern course, the yogi who departs there returns after reaching the moon's light.
essence: Some routes only delay return; they do not end the cycle.
simple_meaning: A person who departs through this darker path reaches a lunar realm and returns again to mortal life.
insight: It shifts attention from vague spirituality to seeing the difference between a path that frees and a path that repeats.
modern_relevance: You choose what feels easier because it is familiar, then wonder why you are back in the same pattern again. Some choices carry you forward; others quietly send you in circles.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते । एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययाऽऽवर्तते पुनः ॥
translation: क्योंकि शुक्ल और कृष्ण  ये दोनों गतियाँ अनादिकालसे जगत्प्राणिमात्र के साथ सम्बन्ध रखनेवाली मानी गई हैं ।  इनमेंसे एक गतिमें जानेवालेको लौटना नहीं पड़ता और दूसरी गतिमें जानेवालेको लौटना पड़ता है ॥
english_translation: The bright and the dark are the two eternal paths of the world. One leads to non-return; the other brings return again.
essence: Some choices free you from the cycle; others send you back into it.
simple_meaning: Two eternal paths exist. One leads beyond repeated return, and the other brings a person back again.
insight: It shifts attention from surface success to the deeper direction a life is moving in.
modern_relevance: You are standing at a crossroads after a breakup, a resignation letter in hand. One choice ends the old cycle; the other sends you back into it with a new name.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन । तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन  इन दोनों मार्गोंको जाननेवाला कोई भी योगी मोहित नहीं होता ।  अतः हे अर्जुन  तू सब समयमें योगयुक्त हो जा ॥
english_translation: O Arjuna, the yogi who knows these two paths is never deluded. Therefore, remain steadfast in yoga at all times.
essence: Understanding the two paths keeps the mind unshaken.
simple_meaning: A person who understands these two routes after death is not confused. Krishna tells Arjuna to stay connected to yoga at all times.
insight: It shifts you from reactive confusion to steady awareness, even when the stakes feel absolute.
modern_relevance: You are standing in a hospital corridor after hearing two very different medical opinions. Panic wants to decide for you. Clear understanding, held calmly, keeps you from being dragged by fear.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैवदानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम् । अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वायोगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम् ॥
translation: योगी इसको शुक्ल और कृष्णमार्गके रहस्यको जानकर वेदोंमें, यज्ञोंमें, तपोंमें तथा दानमें जोजो पुण्यफल कहे गये हैं, उन सभी पुण्यफलोंका अतिक्रमण कर जाता है और आदिस्थान परमात्माको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Knowing the two paths, the yogi goes beyond all the merits declared in the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities, and gifts, and reaches the primal supreme abode.
essence: Knowing the way beyond rewards leads to the highest home.
simple_meaning: Knowing the two paths frees a yogi from chasing ritual rewards. That understanding leads beyond all promised merit and into the highest state.
insight: It shifts the mind from earning merit to seeing beyond all reward-based practice.
modern_relevance: You finish a long ritual, a donation, or a hard discipline and still feel hungry for approval. This verse cuts through that bargain: real understanding is not about collecting spiritual points.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचइदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे । ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  यह अत्यन्त गोपनीय विज्ञानसहित ज्ञान दोषदृष्टिरहित तेरे लिये तो मैं फिर अच्छी तरहसे कहूँगा, जिसको जानकर तू अशुभसे अर्थात् जन्ममरणरूप संसारसे मुक्त हो जायगा ॥
english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: I will now tell you this most secret knowledge, joined with direct realization, to you who are not envious. Knowing it, you will be freed from all that is harmful.
essence: The deepest truth frees only a heart that does not resist it.
simple_meaning: Krishna promises to share the deepest teaching with Arjuna because Arjuna is not hostile to it. Understanding this knowledge fully will free him from suffering and the cycle of rebirth.
insight: It shifts the mind from defensiveness to receptivity, making insight possible.
modern_relevance: You finally ask for honest feedback after months of avoiding it. The answer stings less than your resistance does, because openness lets truth actually reach you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् । प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम् ॥
translation: यह सम्पूर्ण विद्याओंका और सम्पूर्ण गोपनीयोंका राजा है ।  यह अति पवित्र तथा अतिश्रेष्ठ है और इसका फल भी प्रत्यक्ष है ।  यह धर्ममय है, अविनाशी है और करनेमें बहुत सुगम है अर्थात् इसको प्राप्त करना बहुत सुगम है ॥
english_translation: This is the king of all knowledge, the king of all secrets. It is supremely pure, directly knowable, aligned with dharma, easy to practice, and imperishable.
essence: The highest truth is both profound and simple to live.
simple_meaning: This teaching is called the highest knowledge because it is pure, direct, righteous, easy to practice, and never lost.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating spiritual understanding as abstract to seeing it as immediate and usable.
modern_relevance: You are standing at a hospital corridor, waiting for a hard diagnosis. The clearest truth is not always the most complicated one; sometimes it is the one you can actually live by.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप । अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि ॥
translation: हे परंतप इस धर्मकी महिमापर श्रद्धा न रखनेवाले मनुष्य मेरे प्राप्त न होकर मृत्युरूप संसारके मार्गमें लौटते रहते हैं अर्थात् बारबार जन्मतेमरते रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: O conqueror of foes, people without trust in this dharma do not reach Me and keep returning on the path of repeated death and rebirth.
essence: Without trust, the highest teaching cannot carry you beyond repetition.
simple_meaning: People who lack trust in this sacred teaching do not reach Krishna and remain trapped in repeated birth and death.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating trust as optional to seeing it as the condition for transformation.
modern_relevance: You stand at the edge of a hard choice and keep asking for one more guarantee, one more sign. Doubt can become a loop that sends you back to the same fear instead of forward into action.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना । मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः ॥
translation: यह सब संसार मेरे निराकार स्वरूपसे व्याप्त है ।  सम्पूर्ण प्राणी मेरेमें स्थित हैं परन्तु मैं उनमें स्थित नहीं हूँ तथा वे प्राणी भी मुझ में स्थित नहीं हैं  मेरे इस ईश्वरसम्बन्धी योगसामर्थ्य को देख  सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंको उत्पन्न करनेवाला और उनका धारण, भरणपोषण करनेवाला मेरा स्वरूप उन प्राणियोंमें स्थित नहीं है ॥
english_translation: All this universe is pervaded by my unmanifest form. All beings dwell in me, but I do not dwell in them.
essence: The supreme reality holds everything without being held by anything.
simple_meaning: Krishna says the whole universe is sustained by his unseen presence. Every being exists within him, yet he is not limited by any being.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing the divine as one object among many to seeing all objects as resting in the divine.
modern_relevance: You sit in a crowded room after a breakup, feeling swallowed by everyone else's opinions. This verse reminds you that presence can surround everything without being reduced by it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् । भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः ॥
translation: यह सब संसार मेरे निराकार स्वरूपसे व्याप्त है ।  सम्पूर्ण प्राणी मुझ में स्थित हैं परन्तु मैं उनमें स्थित नहीं हूँ तथा वे प्राणी भी मेरेमें स्थित नहीं हैं  मेरे इस ईश्वरसम्बन्धी योगसामर्थ्य को देख  सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंको उत्पन्न करनेवाला और उनका धारण, भरणपोषण करनेवाला मेरा स्वरूप उन प्राणियोंमें स्थित नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Behold My divine power: beings are not in Me, and yet I sustain all beings.
essence: The supreme reality sustains all beings without being contained by them.
simple_meaning: Krishna says that all beings are sustained by him, yet he is not contained within them. He asks Arjuna to see this divine power.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing presence as entanglement to seeing it as sustaining without being confined.
modern_relevance: You keep a family together, answer every message, and hold everything in place — yet no one sees how untouched you remain beneath it all.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यथाऽऽकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् । तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय ॥
translation: जैसे सब जगह विचरनेवाली महान् वायु नित्य ही आकाशमें स्थित रहती है, ऐसे ही सम्पूर्ण प्राणी मुझमें ही स्थित रहते हैं  ऐसा तुम मान लो ॥
english_translation: As the great wind, moving everywhere, always rests in space, so all beings rest in Me.
essence: What moves everywhere still rests in the divine.
simple_meaning: All living beings exist within Krishna just as wind moves within space. The verse asks Arjuna to hold this vision of divine presence everywhere.
insight: It shifts the mind from scattered separation to a felt sense of shared belonging.
modern_relevance: You sit alone after a hard conversation, replaying every word, feeling cut off from everyone. This verse reminds you that isolation is not the deepest reality; life is held inside something larger.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम् । कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम् ॥
translation: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  कल्पोंका क्षय होनेपर सम्पूर्ण प्राणी मेरी प्रकृतिको प्राप्त होते हैं और कल्पोंके आदिमें मैं फिर उनकी रचना करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: O son of Kunti, at the end of a cosmic cycle all beings enter my nature; at its beginning, I send them forth again.
essence: What seems like ending is only a return before another beginning.
simple_meaning: At the end of a vast cycle, every being dissolves back into Krishna's nature. When the next cycle begins, he brings them forth again.
insight: It shifts attention from personal control to the larger rhythm that carries all change.
modern_relevance: A project collapses, a relationship ends, a role disappears — and it feels final. This verse pulls the mind back from that panic and shows that endings belong to a larger cycle, not absolute loss.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः । भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात् ॥
translation: प्रकृतिके वशमें होनेसे परतन्त्र हुए इस सम्पूर्ण प्राणिसमुदायको मैं कल्पोंके आदिमें अपनी प्रकृतिको वशमें करके बारबार रचता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Taking hold of my own nature, I repeatedly create this entire multitude of beings, helpless under the sway of nature.
essence: Life unfolds through a power larger than individual will.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he keeps bringing forth the whole world again and again through his own nature, while beings remain bound by nature’s power.
insight: It shifts attention from personal control to the larger forces that shape repeated patterns.
modern_relevance: You watch the same family pattern repeat in a new generation and feel helpless to stop it. This verse points to a larger force shaping the cycle, even when you cannot yet see it clearly.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय । उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु ॥
translation: हे धनञ्जय  उन सृष्टिरचना आदि कर्मोंमें अनासक्त और उदासीनकी तरह रहते हुए मेरेको वे कर्म नहीं बाँधते ॥
english_translation: Those actions of creation do not bind me, Dhananjaya, because I remain detached and indifferent to them.
essence: Action can continue without leaving a chain behind.
simple_meaning: Creation and world-order do not bind Krishna, because he remains unattached and unconcerned while they happen.
insight: It shifts the mind from ownership of action to freedom within action.
modern_relevance: You send the message, make the hard call, and still do not let the role swallow you. The action happens; your identity does not have to cling to it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मयाऽध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम् । हेतुनाऽनेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते ॥
translation: प्रकृति मेरी अध्यक्षतामें सम्पूर्ण चराचर जगत् को रचती है ।  हे कुन्तीनन्दन  इसी हेतुसे जगत् का विविध प्रकारसे परिवर्तन होता है ॥
english_translation: Nature, under my supervision, brings forth all moving and unmoving beings. Because of this, the world keeps changing, O son of Kunti.
