essence: Change is not chaotic; it unfolds within a higher order.
simple_meaning: All changing life unfolds under Krishna's supervision. The world keeps transforming because nature works through his oversight.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing change as random to seeing it as governed by a deeper intelligence.
modern_relevance: A plan collapses, a relationship changes, or a job disappears overnight, and it feels like chaos. This verse says the turning of events is not outside the larger order you cannot yet see.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम् । परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम् ॥
translation: मूर्खलोग मेरे सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके महान् ईश्वररूप परमभावको न जानते हुए मुझे मनुष्यशरीरके आश्रित मानकर अर्थात् साधारण मनुष्य मानकर मेरी अवज्ञा करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Fools despise Me when I dwell in a human form, not knowing My higher nature as the great Lord of all beings.
essence: Ordinary appearance can hide the highest reality.
simple_meaning: People mock Krishna because they see only a human body and miss his higher nature as the lord of all beings.
insight: It shifts attention from outer appearance to the deeper reality behind a person.
modern_relevance: You meet someone in a plain shirt and underestimate them before they speak. Or you dismiss a quiet teacher, a grieving parent, or a soft-spoken leader because the surface seems ordinary.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः । राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः ॥
translation: जिनकी सब आशाएँ व्यर्थ होती हैं, सब शुभकर्म व्यर्थ होते हैं और सब ज्ञान व्यर्थ होते हैं अर्थात् जिनकी आशाएँ, कर्म और ज्ञान सत्फल देनेवाले नहीं होते, ऐसे अविवेकी मनुष्य आसुरी, राक्षसी और मोहिनी फकृतिका आश्रय लेते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those whose hopes, actions, and understanding are all wasted, confused minds take shelter in deluding, demonic, and shadowy nature.
essence: A confused mind turns even hope, effort, and learning into waste.
simple_meaning: Confused people end up leaning on forces that distort their judgment. Their hopes, actions, and understanding do not bear fruit because they are guided by delusion.
insight: It shifts attention from results alone to the inner quality of the mind guiding them.
modern_relevance: You keep checking the same toxic chat thread, hoping for clarity, and leave more tangled than before. Delusion feeds on attention and makes every effort misfire.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः । भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम् ॥
translation: परन्तु हे पृथानन्दन  दैवी प्रकृतिके आश्रित अनन्यमनवाले महात्मालोग मुझे सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंका आदि और अविनाशी समझकर मेरा भजन करते हैं ॥
english_translation: But, Arjuna, the great-minded ones, relying on the divine nature, worship Me with one-pointed minds, knowing Me as the unborn and imperishable source of all beings.
essence: True devotion begins when the mind recognises the imperishable source.
simple_meaning: Noble people rely on the divine nature, stay focused on Krishna alone, and worship him as the unborn, imperishable source of all beings.
insight: It shifts devotion from emotion alone to clear recognition and single-hearted attention.
modern_relevance: You are standing at the edge of a hard choice, and every noisy opinion is pulling you apart. This verse points to the mind that settles, sees what is lasting, and moves from that place.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सततं कीर्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः । नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ॥
translation: नित्य मेरेमें युक्त मनुष्य दृढ़व्रती होकर लगनपूर्वक साधनमें लगे हुए और भक्तिपूर्वक कीर्तन करते हुए तथा नमस्कार करते हुये निरन्तर मेरी उपासना करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Ever united with Me, steadfast in vows, they worship Me by chanting, striving, and bowing with devotion.
essence: Steady devotion becomes a life of continual remembrance.
simple_meaning: Devoted people keep chanting, bowing, and striving with steady commitment, always focused on Krishna.
insight: It shifts devotion from private emotion to repeated, embodied practice.
modern_relevance: You light a candle before dawn, repeat the same prayer, and keep showing up even when your mind is tired. Devotion lives in repetition.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ज्ञानयज्ञेन चाप्यन्ये यजन्तो मामुपासते । एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन बहुधा विश्वतोमुखम् ॥
translation: दूसरे साधक ज्ञानयज्ञके द्वारा एकीभावसे अभेदभावसे मेरा पूजन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं और दूसरे कई साधक अपनेको पृथक् मानकर चारों तरफ मुखवाले मेरे विराट्ररुपकी अर्थात् संसारको मेरा विराट्ररुप मानकर सेव्यसेवकभावसे मेरी अनेक प्रकारसे उपासना करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Others worship Me through the sacrifice of knowledge, seeing Me as one, as separate, or as the all-facing form.
essence: The same reality can be approached as one, many, or all-encompassing.
simple_meaning: Some people worship Krishna through understanding. They see him as one reality, as separate forms, or as the universal form facing everywhere.
insight: It expands devotion beyond one style of belief and shows that understanding can itself be an offering.
modern_relevance: You are trying to make sense of a loss, and every explanation feels partial. One person sees unity, another sees difference, another sees the whole pattern. The verse says all three can be forms of reverent seeing.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाऽहमहमौषधम् । मंत्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम् ॥
translation: क्रतु मैं हूँ, यज्ञ मैं हूँ, स्वधा मैं हूँ, औषध मैं हूँ, मन्त्र मैं हूँ, घृत मैं हूँ, अग्नि मैं हूँ और हवनरूप क्रिया भी मैं हूँ ।  जाननेयोग्य पवित्र, ओंकार, ऋग्वेद, सामवेद और यजुर्वेद भी मैं ही हूँ ।  इस सम्पूर्ण जगत्का पिता, धाता, माता, पितामह, गति, भर्ता, प्रभु, साक्षी, निवास, आश्रय, सुहृद्, उत्पत्ति, प्रलय, स्थान, निधान तथा अविनाशी बीज भी मैं ही हूँ ॥
english_translation: I am the sacrifice, I am the ritual, I am the offering, I am the herb, I am the mantra, I am the ghee, I am the fire, and I am the act of offering. I am the sacred syllable Om, the Vedas, the father, mother, supporter, grandfather, object of knowledge, purifier, and imperishable seed of this world.
essence: All sacred action is already filled with the divine presence.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is every part of sacred ritual: the offering, the chant, the fire, and the act itself. He is also the sacred sound, the Vedas, and the sustaining source of the world.
insight: It shifts devotion from isolated ceremony to seeing the divine presence in every sacred act and support.
modern_relevance: You light a lamp before a hard day, whisper a prayer, or sit in silence before a decision. The ritual feels small until you realize the whole act is already held by the divine.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: पिताऽहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः । वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च ॥
translation: क्रतु मैं हूँ, यज्ञ मैं हूँ, स्वधा मैं हूँ, औषध मैं हूँ, मन्त्र मैं हूँ, घृत मैं हूँ, अग्नि मैं हूँ और हवनरूप क्रिया भी मैं हूँ ।  जाननेयोग्य पवित्र, ओंकार, ऋग्वेद, सामवेद और यजुर्वेद भी मैं ही हूँ ।  इस सम्पूर्ण जगत् का पिता, धाता, माता, पितामह, गति, भर्ता, प्रभु, साक्षी, निवास, आश्रय, सुहृद्, उत्पत्ति, प्रलय, स्थान, निधान तथा अविनाशी बीज भी मैं ही हूँ ॥
english_translation: I am the father of this world, the mother, the supporter, and the grandfather. I am the object of knowledge, the purifier, the sacred syllable Om, and also the Rig, Sama, and Yajur Vedas.
essence: All sources of life and meaning are gathered in Krishna.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the world’s father, mother, supporter, and ancestor. He is also the sacred sound Om and the Vedas themselves.
insight: It shifts attention from asking where the sacred is to recognising that all sacred forms point back to Krishna.
modern_relevance: When everything familiar collapses — family expectations, labels, even your own certainty — this speaks to the ground beneath them all.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् । प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥
translation: क्रतु मैं हूँ, यज्ञ मैं हूँ, स्वधा मैं हूँ, औषध मैं हूँ, मन्त्र मैं हूँ, घृत मैं हूँ, अग्नि मैं हूँ और हवनरूप क्रिया भी मैं हूँ ।  जाननेयोग्य पवित्र, ओंकार, ऋग्वेद, सामवेद और यजुर्वेद भी मैं ही हूँ ।  इस सम्पूर्ण जगत्का पिता, धाता, माता, पितामह, गति, भर्ता, प्रभु, साक्षी, निवास, आश्रय, सुहृद्, उत्पत्ति, प्रलय, स्थान, निधान तथा अविनाशी बीज भी मैं ही हूँ ॥
english_translation: I am the goal, the supporter, the lord, the witness, the refuge, the friend, the source, the dissolution, the resting place, the treasure, and the imperishable seed.
essence: Everything rests in one imperishable source.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is everything that supports, witnesses, shelters, begins, ends, and sustains existence.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing the world as separate pieces to seeing one sustaining presence in all roles.
modern_relevance: You are sitting in a parked car after a hard call, afraid of what happens next. The verse reminds you that the same reality that receives the ending also holds the beginning.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च । अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन ॥
translation: हे अर्जुन  संसारके हितके लिये मैं ही सूर्यरूपसे तपता हूँ, जलको ग्रहण करता हूँ और फिर उस जलको वर्षारूपसे बरसा देता हूँ ।  और तो क्या कहूँ अमृत और मृत्यु तथा सत् और असत् भी मैं ही हूँ ॥
english_translation: I heat the world as the sun, I hold back the rain and send it forth. I am immortality and death, being and non-being, Arjuna.
essence: Opposites do not stand outside the divine; they flow from it.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the force behind sunlight, rain, immortality, death, existence, and non-existence. Everything that sustains and changes the world moves through him.
insight: It shifts the mind from dividing life into good and bad forces to seeing one reality working through both.
modern_relevance: You watch a storm flood the street, then clear the next morning, and realize the same sky held both. This verse trains you to see order inside forces that look opposite.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापायज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते । ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोकमश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान् ॥
translation: वेदत्रयीमें कहे हुए सकाम अनुष्ठानको करनेवाले और सोमरसको पीनेवाले जो पापरहित मनुष्य यज्ञोंके द्वारा इन्द्ररूपसे मेरा पूजन करके स्वर्गप्राप्तिकी प्रार्थना करते हैं, वे पुण्यके फलस्वरूप इन्द्रलोकको प्राप्त करके वहाँ स्वर्गमें देवताओंके दिव्य भोगोंको भोगते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who know the three Vedas, drink soma, and are purified by sacrifice pray for heaven. Having earned merit, they enjoy the divine pleasures of the realm of the radiant beings.
essence: Rewarded devotion still keeps you bound to return.
simple_meaning: People who perform Vedic sacrifices and seek reward pray for heaven. They gain merit, reach the heavenly realm, and enjoy its pleasures for a time.
insight: It shifts the mind from spiritual transaction to seeing the limits of reward-based worship.
modern_relevance: You finish a big religious event, post the photos, and wait for the praise to feel like enough. The verse reminds you that reward-seeking always keeps you reaching for the next high.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालंक्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति । एव त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्नागतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते ॥
translation: वे उस विशाल स्वर्गलोकके भोगोंको भोगकर पुण्य क्षीण होनेपर मृत्युलोकमें आ जाते हैं ।  इस प्रकार तीनों वेदोंमें कहे हुए सकाम धर्मका आश्रय लिये हुए भोगोंकी कामना करनेवाले मनुष्य आवागमनको प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
english_translation: After enjoying the vast heaven-world, they return to the mortal world when their merit is exhausted. Thus, those who follow the ritual path of the three Vedas and seek pleasures gain repeated coming and going.
essence: What is won by wanting is lost by time.
simple_meaning: People who seek heavenly rewards through ritual enjoy those rewards for a while, but when their merit is used up, they return to ordinary life and the cycle continues.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing temporary payoff to seeing the loop beneath it.
modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the applause, the bonus trip — and by Monday the hunger is back. Krishna points to the exhaustion behind every reward that depends on accumulation.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते । तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥
translation: जो अनन्य भक्त मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, मेरेमें निरन्तर लगे हुए उन भक्तोंका योगक्षेम अप्राप्तकी प्राप्ति और प्राप्तकी रक्षा मैं वहन करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Those who think of me alone and worship me with unwavering focus—I carry their welfare and security.
essence: Unwavering devotion is met by unwavering support.
simple_meaning: People who focus on Krishna alone and worship him steadily do not have to carry every burden by themselves. He takes responsibility for their well-being and security.
insight: It shifts devotion from asking for favors to trusting steady support. The mind stops clutching and begins relying.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a hospital bill, a breakup text, and a job notice all at once. This verse answers the panic that says, 'I have to hold everything myself.'
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: येऽप्यन्यदेवता भक्ता यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः । तेऽपि मामेव कौन्तेय यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम् ॥
translation: हे कुन्तीनन्दन जो भी भक्त मनुष्य श्रद्धापूर्वक अन्य देवताओंका पूजन करते हैं, वे भी करते हैं मेरा ही पूजन, पर करते है अविधिपूर्वक ॥
english_translation: Even those who, filled with trust, worship other radiant beings, worship Me alone, but in the wrong way, O son of Kunti.
essence: All sincere worship reaches the one reality, even when the form is confused.
simple_meaning: People who worship other radiant beings with trust are still, in a deeper sense, worshipping Krishna, but without the full understanding of how worship truly works.
insight: It shifts devotion from many separate targets to one underlying source.
modern_relevance: You light a lamp before one name, pray before another, and still feel the same ache for help. The heart reaches upward; the mind only names the doorway differently.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च । न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति ते ॥
translation: क्योंकि मैं ही सम्पूर्ण यज्ञोंका भोक्ता और स्वामी भी हूँ परन्तु वे मेरेको तत्त्वसे नहीं जानते, इसीसे उनका पतन होता है ॥
english_translation: For I am the enjoyer and lord of all sacrifices. But those people do not know me in truth, and so they fall away.
essence: Every offering matters only when you know who receives it.
simple_meaning: All sacrifices ultimately belong to Krishna, who receives them and rules over them. People fall when they do not know this truth clearly.
insight: It shifts devotion from ritual performance to clear recognition of the one who receives every offering.
modern_relevance: You give time, money, and attention to what matters most, but forget the deeper source behind it all. That forgetfulness quietly drains the meaning out of your effort.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यान्ति देवव्रता देवान् पितृ़न्यान्ति पितृव्रताः । भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम् ॥
translation: सकामभावसे देवताओंका पूजन करनेवाले शरीर छोड़नेपर देवताओंको प्राप्त होते हैं ।  पितरोंका पूजन करनेवाले पितरोंको प्राप्त होते हैं ।  भूतप्रेतोंका पूजन करनेवाले भूतप्रेतोंको प्राप्त होते हैं ।  परन्तु मेरा पूजन करनेवाले मुझे ही प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those devoted to the radiant beings reach the radiant beings. Those devoted to the ancestors reach the ancestors. Those devoted to spirits reach the spirits. But those devoted to me come to me.
essence: Devotion does not stay abstract; it carries you to its chosen end.
simple_meaning: People reach the object they devote themselves to. Worship directed toward Krishna leads to Krishna; other devotions lead elsewhere.
insight: It shifts devotion from a vague feeling to a directional force that determines what the heart reaches.
modern_relevance: You keep returning to the same feed, the same crowd, the same craving. Over time, you start arriving where your attention has been going all along.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
translation: जो भक्त पत्र, पुष्प, फल, जल आदि यथासाध्य प्राप्त वस्तु को भक्तिपूर्वक मेरे अर्पण करता है, उस मेरेमें तल्लीन हुए अन्तःकरणवाले भक्तके द्वारा भक्तिपूर्वक दिये हुए उपहारभेंट को मैं खा लेता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Whoever offers me a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water with devotion, I accept that devoted offering from the pure-hearted.
essence: A small offering becomes complete when devotion fills it.
simple_meaning: Even the smallest offering becomes meaningful when it is given with devotion and a sincere heart.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to sincerity, showing that wholehearted offering is what truly counts.
modern_relevance: You bring a small homemade meal to someone grieving, unsure it is enough. What matters is not the size of the gift, but the love carried into it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् । यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् ॥
translation: हे कुन्तीपुत्र  तू जो कुछ करता है, जो कुछ खाता है, जो कुछ यज्ञ करता है, जो कुछ दान देता है और जो कुछ तप करता है, वह सब मेरे अर्पण कर दे ॥
english_translation: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give, and whatever austerity you practice, offer it to me.
essence: Every action becomes complete when it is offered.
simple_meaning: Whatever you do in daily life can become an offering. Work, food, giving, sacrifice, and discipline all gain meaning when dedicated to the divine.
insight: It turns daily activity into devotion, so nothing is spiritually wasted.
modern_relevance: You finish a hard day, eat in silence, answer messages, and keep going. This verse says none of it is too small to be offered with care.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: शुभाशुभफलैरेवं मोक्ष्यसे कर्मबन्धनैः । संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा विमुक्तो मामुपैष्यसि ॥
translation: इस प्रकार मेरे अर्पण करनेसे जिनसे कर्मबन्धन होता है, ऐसे शुभ विहित और अशुभ निषिद्ध सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंके फलोंसे तू मुक्त हो जायगा ।  ऐसे अपनेसहित सब कुछ मेरे अर्पण करनेवाला और सबसे मुक्त हुआ तू मेरेको प्राप्त हो जायगा ॥
english_translation: In this way, you will be freed from the bonds of action and its results. Given over to renunciation-yoga, released, you will come to me.
essence: Freedom begins when even the result is no longer yours to carry.
simple_meaning: Offer every action and its results to the divine, and you become free from the bondage created by action.
insight: It shifts attention from owning results to offering the whole act.
modern_relevance: You send the message, then stare at the screen for hours, replaying every word. This verse says the work can be complete even when the response is not yours to own.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः । ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् ॥
translation: मैं सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें समान हूँ ।  उन प्राणियोंमें न तो कोई मेरा द्वेषी है और न कोई प्रिय है ।  परन्तु जो भक्तिपूर्वक मेरा भजन करते हैं, वे मेरेमें हैं और मैं उनमें हूँ ॥
english_translation: I am equal toward all beings. No one is hated by me, and no one is especially dear. But those who worship me with devotion dwell in me, and I dwell in them.
essence: Equality is universal; intimacy is born through devotion.
simple_meaning: The divine is not partial or biased. Everyone is met equally, but loving devotion creates a living closeness between the divine and the devotee.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to impress the divine to entering a relationship of mutual presence.
modern_relevance: You send the message, then wait for the reply that might never come. This verse says the deepest presence is not bought by approval; it grows where devotion is real.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक् । साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः ॥
translation: अगर कोई दुराचारीसेदुराचारी भी अनन्यभावसे मेरा भजन करता है, तो उसको साधु ही मानना चाहिये ।  कारण कि उसने निश्चय बहुत अच्छी तरह कर लिया है ॥
english_translation: Even if a person of very bad conduct worships Me with undivided devotion, that person must be regarded as righteous, for the resolve is rightly made.
essence: Undivided devotion can outweigh even a deeply flawed life.
simple_meaning: Even someone with a very bad past is still worthy if that person turns to the divine with one-pointed devotion.
insight: It shifts judgment from moral history to present direction: the decisive fact is where attention and devotion now go.
modern_relevance: Someone who has lied, failed, or hurt others may still choose one honest step tonight: a call, an apology, a return. The past is heavy, but a clean turning still matters.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति । कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति ॥
translation: वह तत्काल उसी क्षण धर्मात्मा हो जाता है और निरन्तर रहनेवाली शान्तिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ।  हे कुन्तीनन्दन  तुम प्रतिज्ञा करो कि मेरे भक्तका विनाश पतन नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: One who is devoted to Me quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace. O son of Kunti, declare it boldly: My devotee never perishes.
essence: Devotion quickly changes a person and protects them from ruin.
simple_meaning: A devoted person quickly becomes upright and finds lasting peace. Krishna says his devotee will not come to ruin.
insight: It shifts the mind from fear of collapse to trust in a sustaining presence.
modern_relevance: You are standing at the hospital corridor after bad news, unsure whether you can keep going. This verse says devotion does not leave you stranded; it steadies you when fear says collapse.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः । स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम् ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन  जो भी पापयोनिवाले हों तथा जो भी स्त्रियाँ, वैश्य और शूद्र हों, वे भी सर्वथा मेरे शरण होकर निःसन्देह परमगतिको प्राप्त हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Partha, even those born in difficult circumstances, and women, merchants, and workers, can reach the highest state by taking refuge in me.
essence: No birth or status can block one who takes refuge.
simple_meaning: Anyone, regardless of birth or social position, can reach the highest state by taking refuge in Krishna.
insight: It shifts the mind from social exclusion to spiritual access through refuge.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room already feeling disqualified because of where you came from, what you earn, or how people label you. This verse cuts through that shame: the door is not locked by your background.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा । अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम् ॥
translation: जो पवित्र आचरणवाले ब्राह्मण और ऋषिस्वरूप क्षत्रिय भगवान् के भक्त हों, वे परमगतिको प्राप्त हो जायँ, इसमें तो कहना ही क्या है ।  इसलिये इस अनित्य और सुखरहित शरीरको प्राप्त करके तू मेरा भजन कर ॥
english_translation: If even pure Brahmins and royal sages devoted to the divine reach the highest state, what to speak of you? So, having come into this impermanent and joyless world, worship Me.
essence: What does not last cannot finally satisfy; turn your life toward the divine.
simple_meaning: Even the most virtuous devotees and wise rulers can reach the highest state through devotion. Since this world is temporary and unsatisfying, turn toward Krishna.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing temporary comfort to orienting life around devotion.
modern_relevance: You finish something you thought would finally satisfy you, and the relief never comes. The verse points you away from chasing another temporary fix and toward what can actually hold you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु । मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः ॥
translation: तू मेरा भक्त हो जा, मेरेमें मनवाला हो जा, मेरा पूजन करनेवाला हो जा और मेरेको नमस्कार कर ।  इस प्रकार मेरे साथ अपनेआपको लगाकर, मेरे परायण हुआ तू मेरेको ही प्राप्त होगा । , ॥
english_translation: Fix your mind on me. Be devoted to me. Worship me. Bow to me. United with me in this way, and fully oriented toward me, you will come to me.
essence: Total orientation toward the divine becomes the way to reach the divine.
simple_meaning: Krishna asks Arjuna to place his mind, devotion, worship, and respect entirely on him. He promises that this full orientation will lead Arjuna to him.
insight: It shifts devotion from emotion alone to a full-life orientation that gathers thought, action, and surrender into one movement.
modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, deciding whether to tell the truth that will change everything. This verse asks for total alignment, not half-hearted loyalty: let the mind, intention, and action point in one direction.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचभूय एव महाबाहो श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे महाबाहो अर्जुन  मेरे परम वचनको तुम फिर भी सुनो, जिसे मैं तुम्हारे हितकी कामनासे कहूँगा क्योंकि तुम मेरेमें अत्यन्त प्रेम रखते हो ॥
english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: Listen again, O mighty-armed one, to my supreme word, which I will speak for your welfare because you are deeply dear to me.
essence: Deeper truth arrives as care for the one who is ready.
simple_meaning: Krishna asks Arjuna to listen again to a deeper teaching, spoken for Arjuna’s good because he is dear to him.
insight: It frames teaching as an act of loving concern, not distant instruction.
modern_relevance: A mentor leans in after your second failed attempt and says, “Listen carefully — I’m telling you this for your good.” The hardest truths often arrive wrapped in care.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः । अहमादिर्हि देवानां महर्षीणां च सर्वशः ॥
translation: मेरे प्रकट होनेको न देवता जानते हैं और न महर्षि क्योंकि मैं सब प्रकारसे देवताओं और महर्षियोंका आदि हूँ ॥
english_translation: The hosts of devas do not know my origin, nor do the great sages, for I am the beginning of the devas and the great sages in every way.
essence: Even the highest knowers stand inside the source they seek.
simple_meaning: Even the devas and great sages do not know Krishna’s full source, because he is their own beginning.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating the divine as an object of study to recognising it as the source of all knowers.
modern_relevance: You think you have understood someone because they are brilliant, spiritual, or widely respected. Then they reveal a depth that even the best minds cannot fully map.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यो मामजमनादिं च वेत्ति लोकमहेश्वरम् । असम्मूढः स मर्त्येषु सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य मुझे अजन्मा, अनादि और सम्पूर्ण लोकोंका महान् ईश्वर जानता है अर्थात् दृढ़तासे मानता है, वह मनुष्योंमें असम्मूढ़ जानकार है और वह सम्पूर्ण पापोंसे मुक्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: One who knows Me as unborn, beginningless, and the great lord of all worlds is undeluded among mortals and is freed from every wrong deed.
essence: Clear recognition of the divine ends confusion and frees action.
simple_meaning: Knowing Krishna as unborn, beginningless, and the ruler of all worlds removes confusion and frees a person from wrongdoing.
insight: It shifts devotion from vague admiration to clear recognition, and that recognition dissolves confusion at its root.
modern_relevance: You are standing at the edge of a choice that could change everything, and the noise in your head is louder than your judgment. Seeing what is higher than fear can steady the whole mind.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः । सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च ॥
translation: बुद्धि, ज्ञान, असम्मोह, क्षमा, सत्य, दम, शम, सुख, दुःख, भव, अभाव, भय, अभय, अहिंसा, समता, तुष्टि, तप, दान, यश और अपयश  प्राणियोंके ये अनेक प्रकारके और अलगअलग बीस भाव मेरेसे ही होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Understanding, wisdom, freedom from confusion, forgiveness, truth, self-restraint, calmness, pleasure, pain, coming into being, ceasing to be, fear, fearlessness, nonviolence, evenness, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and disgrace arise from me alone.
essence: All human qualities arise from the same source.
simple_meaning: Krishna says that every good and difficult human quality comes from him alone, including wisdom, restraint, joy, fear, courage, and even changes in existence itself.
insight: It shifts attention from self-blame or self-pride to seeing every state as part of a larger order.
modern_relevance: You watch your own mood swing before a hard conversation: courage, fear, calm, and shame all seem to arrive uninvited. This verse says those states are not random accidents; they come from one deeper source.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अहिंसा समता तुष्टिस्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः । भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः ॥
translation: बुद्धि, ज्ञान, असम्मोह, क्षमा, सत्य, दम, शम, सुख, दुःख, भव, अभाव, भय, अभय, अहिंसा, समता, तुष्टि, तप, दान, यश और अपयश  प्राणियोंके ये अनेक प्रकारके और अलगअलग बीस भाव मेरेसे ही होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Nonviolence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, honor, and dishonor—all these different states of beings arise from Me alone.
essence: All qualities are expressions of the same divine source.
simple_meaning: Nonviolence, balance, contentment, discipline, generosity, honor, and dishonor all arise from Krishna alone in different beings.
insight: It shifts attention from self-judgment to the source of qualities, so you can align with what nourishes them.
modern_relevance: You catch yourself being kind in one conversation and harsh in the next, then wonder which version is real. This verse says the deeper source is bigger than either mood.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: महर्षयः सप्त पूर्वे चत्वारो मनवस्तथा । मद्भावा मानसा जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः ॥
translation: सात महर्षि और उनसे भी पूर्वमें होनेवाले चार सनकादि तथा चौदह मनु  ये सबकेसब मेरे मनसे पैदा हुए हैं और मेरेमें भाव श्रद्धाभक्ति रखनेवाले हैं, जिनकी संसारमें यह सम्पूर्ण प्रजा है ॥
english_translation: The seven great sages, the four ancient sages, and the fourteen Manus were born from my mind. The people of these worlds descend from them.
essence: All lineages and worlds emerge from Krishna’s mind.
simple_meaning: Krishna says that the great sages, the ancient sages, and the Manus all arose from him, and all beings in these worlds descend through them.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated individuals to the sacred source behind all lineages and life.
modern_relevance: You look at a family tree, a lineage of teachers, or the chain behind a tradition and wonder where it all began. This verse says the deepest source is not random history but a living divine origin.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः । सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य मेरी इस विभूतिको और योगको तत्त्वसे जानता है अर्थात् दृढ़तापूर्वक मानता है, वह अविचल भक्तियोगसे युक्त हो जाता है इसमें कुछ भी संशय नहीं है ॥
english_translation: One who truly knows this glory and this yoga of mine becomes steadfast in yoga without doubt.
essence: True recognition of Krishna's presence makes devotion unshakable.
simple_meaning: Knowing Krishna's divine manifestations deeply makes devotion steady and unshakable. Real understanding removes doubt and draws the mind into firm union.
insight: It shifts devotion from vague feeling to clear recognition, making commitment firm instead of wavering.
modern_relevance: You suddenly recognise the person in front of you is not just a role or label. In that moment, hesitation drops and your whole response becomes steadier and more sincere.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते । इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः ॥
translation: मैं संसारमात्रका प्रभव मूलकारण हूँ, और मुझसे ही सारा संसार प्रवृत्त हो रहा है अर्थात् चेष्टा कर रहा है  ऐसा मेरेको मानकर मेरेमें ही श्रद्धाप्रेम रखते हुए बुद्धिमान् भक्त मेरा ही भजन करते हैं  सब प्रकारसे मेरे ही शरण होते हैं ॥
english_translation: I am the source of all; everything moves from me. Knowing this, the wise worship me with wholehearted devotion.
essence: Knowing the source turns understanding into devotion.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the source of everything, and wise people respond with devoted worship and full-hearted love.
insight: It shifts devotion from sentiment to recognition: when you see the source everywhere, worship becomes natural.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a decision that affects everyone around you, and the pressure to control every outcome is crushing. This verse says the deepest steadiness comes from knowing where life itself flows from.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् । कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ॥
translation: मेरेमें चित्तवाले, मेरेमें प्राणोंको अर्पण करनेवाले भक्तजन आपसमें मेरे गुण, प्रभाव आदिको जानते हुए और उनका कथन करते हुए ही नित्यनिरन्तर सन्तुष्ट रहते हैं और मेरेमें प्रेम करते हैं ॥
english_translation: With minds fixed on Me and lives offered to Me, My devotees speak of Me to one another, and find continual joy in that shared devotion.
essence: Shared remembrance keeps devotion alive.
simple_meaning: People devoted to Krishna keep their minds and lives focused on him. They talk about him together, and that shared remembrance brings them lasting joy.
insight: It shifts devotion from a private feeling into a living practice of shared remembrance and mutual encouragement.
modern_relevance: You leave a temple gathering or a retreat and the conversation keeps circling back to what moved you most. The feeling lasts because remembrance is being shared, not kept private.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम् । ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते ॥
translation: उन नित्यनिरन्तर मेरेमें लगे हुए और प्रेमपूर्वक मेरा भजन करनेवाले भक्तोंको मैं वह बुद्धियोग देता हूँ, जिससे उनको मेरी प्राप्ति हो जाती है ॥
english_translation: To those who are always devoted and worship Me with love, I give the discernment that leads them to Me.
essence: Steady devotion itself draws forth the understanding that reaches the divine.
simple_meaning: Those who keep turning toward Krishna with steady love receive the discernment that leads them to him.
insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to a disciplined openness that invites discernment.
modern_relevance: You keep returning to the same prayer, the same practice, the same honest question at 2 a.m. The answer does not always arrive as a sign; sometimes it arrives as clearer seeing.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तमः । नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता ॥
translation: उन भक्तोंपर कृपा करनेके लिये ही उनके स्वरूप होनेपन में रहनेवाला मैं उनके अज्ञानजन्य अन्धकारको देदीप्यमान ज्ञानरूप दीपकके द्वारा सर्वथा नष्ट कर देता हूँ ॥
english_translation: To show them compassion, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge, dwelling in their own being.
essence: Compassion becomes knowledge that burns away inner darkness.
simple_meaning: Out of compassion, Krishna removes the darkness of ignorance from devoted people by giving them the light of understanding from within.
insight: It shifts devotion from emotional closeness to inner transformation: real connection clears confusion at the root.
modern_relevance: You finally sit with the truth you have been avoiding, and something inside stops arguing. The fog lifts not by force, but by seeing clearly.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचपरं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् । पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम् ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  परम ब्रह्म, परम धाम और महान् पवित्र आप ही हैं ।  आप शाश्वत, दिव्य पुरुष, आदिदेव, अजन्मा और विभु व्यापक हैं  ऐसा सबकेसब ऋषि, देवर्षि नारद, असित, देवल तथा व्यास कहते हैं और स्वयं आप भी मेरे प्रति कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: You are the supreme reality, the highest refuge, the purest one, the eternal divine person, the first being, unborn, and all-pervading.
essence: Recognition turns into surrender when the highest reality stands revealed.
simple_meaning: Arjuna recognises Krishna as the highest reality, the purest refuge, eternal, unborn, and present everywhere.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Krishna as a teacher to seeing him as the source behind everything.
modern_relevance: You stand before someone’s brutal honesty and feel your defenses collapse. In that moment, respect becomes recognition: what is larger than your fear deserves your surrender.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा । असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  परम ब्रह्म, परम धाम और महान् पवित्र आप ही हैं ।  आप शाश्वत, दिव्य पुरुष, आदिदेव, अजन्मा और विभु व्यापक हैं  ऐसा सबकेसब ऋषि, देवर्षि नारद, असित, देवल तथा व्यास कहते हैं और स्वयं आप भी मेरे प्रति कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: All the sages speak of you this way: the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa. You yourself also say this to me.
essence: The deepest recognition is echoed by the wise and by Krishna himself.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says that all the great sages, including Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa, speak of Krishna this way, and Krishna himself says the same to him.
insight: It shifts faith from private doubt to confirmed recognition through respected testimony.
modern_relevance: You keep doubting a hard truth until the people you trust most all say the same thing. Then the resistance weakens, and you can finally listen.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव । न हि ते भगवन् व्यक्ितं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः ॥
translation: हे केशव  मेरेसे आप जो कुछ कह रहे हैं, यह सब मैं सत्य मानता हूँ ।  हे भगवन्  आपके प्रकट होनेको न तो देवता जानते हैं और न दानव ही जानते हैं ॥
english_translation: I accept as true all that you have said, O Keshava. O Bhagavan, neither the devas nor the asuras know your manifested form.
essence: True recognition begins where ordinary beings cannot see.
simple_meaning: Arjuna accepts Krishna's words as true and says that even radiant beings and shadow beings do not understand Krishna's revealed form.
insight: It shifts the mind from needing total proof to recognising a reality greater than ordinary perception.
modern_relevance: Someone explains something life-changing, and your first instinct is to argue. Arjuna does the opposite: he admits the truth before he fully understands it.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: स्वयमेवात्मनाऽत्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम । भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते ॥
translation: हे भूतभावन  हे भूतेश  हे देवदेव  हे जगत्पते  हे पुरुषोत्तम  आप स्वयं ही अपनेआपसे अपनेआपको जानते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Supreme Person, you alone know yourself by yourself, O source of all beings, lord of all beings, divine of the divine, ruler of the world.
essence: The supreme one is known fully only by the supreme one.
simple_meaning: Arjuna praises Krishna as the Supreme Person who alone fully knows his own nature and rules over all beings.
insight: It shifts reverence from asking for proof to recognising a reality that is self-luminous and complete.
modern_relevance: You sit across from someone whose motives you cannot read, yet they seem to hold the whole room together. This verse names that rare recognition: some presence is deeper than your questions.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः । याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि ॥
translation: जिन विभूतियोंसे आप इन सम्पूर्ण लोकोंको व्याप्त करके स्थित हैं, उन सभी अपनी दिव्य विभूतियोंका सम्पूर्णतासे वर्णन करनेमें आप ही समर्थ हैं ॥
english_translation: Only you can fully describe your own divine manifestations, by which you pervade and sustain all these worlds.
essence: Only the source can fully name its own presence in the world.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says only Krishna can fully explain his own divine manifestations, because Krishna pervades and supports all the worlds through them.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to define the whole to receiving the whole through its living expressions.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence seems to change the whole room, but you cannot explain why. Some realities are only understood by the one who embodies them.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन् । केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया ॥
translation: हे योगिन्  हरदम साङ्गोपाङ्ग चिन्तन करता हुआ मैं आपको कैसे जानूँ  और हे भगवन्  किनकिन भावोंमें आप मेरे द्वारा चिन्तन किये जा सकते हैं अर्थात् किनकिन भावोंमें मैं आपका चिन्तन करूँ ॥
english_translation: O Yogi, how shall I know You by constant contemplation? In what forms should You be contemplated, O Blessed One?
essence: Devotion needs a form the mind can return to again and again.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna how to keep remembering him and in what forms he should meditate on him.
insight: It shifts devotion from vague feeling to specific remembrance through form, image, and attention.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who changed your life, then realise you keep forgetting what made them matter. The mind wants a concrete way to stay oriented toward what it reveres.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन । भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि श्रृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम् ॥
translation: हे जनार्दन  आप अपने योग सामर्थ्य को और विभूतियोंको विस्तारसे फिर कहिये क्योंकि आपके अमृतमय वचन सुनतेसुनते मेरी तृप्ति नहीं हो रही है ॥
english_translation: O Janardana, tell me again in detail of Your yogic power and Your manifestations, for I am not satisfied hearing Your nectar-like words.
essence: True devotion never feels finished hearing the beloved.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to keep speaking about his divine powers and forms, because hearing about them never feels complete.
insight: It shifts attention from getting an answer to staying in living contact with what inspires reverence.
modern_relevance: You find one line in a talk that opens something in you, and you replay it again and again on the walk home. Real longing does not get bored; it wants deeper contact.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचहन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः । प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हाँ, ठीक है ।  मैं अपनी दिव्य विभूतियोंको तेरे लिये प्रधानतासे संक्षेपसे कहूँगा क्योंकि हे कुरुश्रेष्ठ  मेरी विभूतियोंके विस्तारका अन्त नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Krishna said: I will tell you briefly of my divine manifestations, chief of them, Arjuna, for there is no end to their विस्तार.
essence: The divine can be named briefly, never exhausted.
simple_meaning: Krishna agrees to describe his chief divine manifestations, but only in brief, because his full extent has no limit.
insight: It shifts attention from trying to catalogue the divine to recognising its limitless presence in what stands out most.
modern_relevance: You ask someone to explain what keeps them steady through chaos, and they give you a few examples — then admit the real answer is bigger than any summary.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः । अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥
translation: हे नींदको जीतनेवाले अर्जुन  सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके आदि, मध्य तथा अन्तमें भी मैं ही हूँ और प्राणियोंके अन्तःकरणमें आत्मरूपसे भी मैं ही स्थित हूँ ॥
english_translation: I am the Self, O Gudakesha, seated in the heart of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of all beings.
essence: Everything that exists is held within one enduring presence.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he lives within every being as the inner self and is present at every stage of existence: beginning, middle, and end.
insight: It shifts attention from scattered appearances to the single presence running through all change.
modern_relevance: You sit beside someone in a hospital corridor, watching a life change in silence. This verse says the deepest presence is already there, inside every beginning, middle, and ending.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान् । मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी ॥
translation: मैं अदितिके पुत्रोंमें विष्णु वामन और प्रकाशमान वस्तुओंमें किरणोंवाला सूर्य हूँ ।  मैं मरुतोंका तेज और नक्षत्रोंका अधिपति चन्द्रमा हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among the sons of Aditi, I am Vishnu; among radiant things, I am the sun with rays. I am the brilliance in the Maruts, and among stars, I am the moon.
essence: Every radiance is a sign of one presence.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he appears as Vishnu among the sons of Aditi, as the sun among bright things, as the Maruts' brilliance, and as the moon among stars.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated objects to the sacred source shining through them.
modern_relevance: You step outside after a sleepless night and the morning light hits your face. The warmth, the brightness, the quiet order in it all can feel like more than weather — like presence.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः । इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना ॥
translation: मैं वेदोंमें सामवेद हूँ, देवताओंमें इन्द्र हूँ, इन्द्रियोंमें मन हूँ और प्राणियोंकी चेतना हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among the Vedas, I am the Sama Veda; among the radiant beings, I am Indra. Among the senses, I am the mind; among living beings, I am consciousness.
essence: The divine is not elsewhere; it is the awareness within everything.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he appears as the highest sacred chant, as Indra among radiant beings, as the mind among the senses, and as awareness in all living things.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated objects to the living presence that animates them.
modern_relevance: You are sitting in a noisy train, trying to steady yourself before a painful conversation. The calm, the clarity, the awareness watching your fear — all of it can be seen as sacred presence, not random accident.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम् । वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम् ॥
translation: रुद्रोंमें शंकर और यक्षराक्षसोंमें कुबेर मैं हूँ । वसुओंमें पावक अग्नि और शिखरवाले पर्वतोंमें सुमेरु मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among the Rudras, I am Shankara; among the Yakshas and Rakshasas, I am Kubera. Among the Vasus, I am fire, and among mountain peaks, I am Mount Meru.
essence: Greatness in the world is a visible sign of Krishna's presence.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is present as the brightest or most powerful form within Rudras, Yakshas, Vasus, fire, and Mount Meru.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated objects to the sacred force shining through their greatest forms.
modern_relevance: You stand at a cliff edge at dawn and feel the wind, the heat, the vastness, the pull of awe. The world is not empty matter; its grandeur can wake reverence.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् । सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः ॥
translation: हे पार्थ  पुरोहितोंमें मुख्य बृहस्पतिको मेरा स्वरूप समझो ।  सेनापतियोंमें स्कन्द और जलाशयोंमें समुद्र मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among priests, know Me as Brihaspati; among commanders, I am Skanda; among waters, I am the ocean.
essence: Greatness in the world is a trace of Krishna everywhere.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the highest among priests, the commander Skanda, and the ocean among all waters.
insight: It trains the mind to recognise greatness, order, and depth as expressions of one source.
modern_relevance: You stand at the shore after a hard day and feel small before the dark water. The verse says that same vastness is not empty — it is a sign of the divine everywhere.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् । यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः ॥
translation: महर्षियोंमें भृगु और वाणियोंशब्दों में एक अक्षर अर्थात् प्रणव मैं हूँ ।  सम्पूर्ण यज्ञोंमें जपयज्ञ और स्थिर रहनेवालोंमें हिमालय मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among great sages I am Bhrigu; among words I am the one imperishable syllable. Among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetition; among the steadfast I am the Himalayas.
essence: The divine appears through the noblest forms of speech, ritual, and nature.
simple_meaning: Krishna names his presence in sacred sages, sacred sound, silent repetition, and the Himalayas. He is showing that the divine can be found in revered forms across the world.
insight: It trains the mind to recognise the divine through symbols, practices, and forms of greatness.
modern_relevance: You are standing before a shrine, a mountain, or a line of chant that suddenly quiets you. The moment feels bigger than the object itself, as if something unseen is shining through it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः । गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः ॥
translation: सम्पूर्ण वृक्षोंमें पीपल, देवर्षियोंमें नारद, गन्धर्वोंमें चित्ररथ और सिद्धोंमें कपिल मुनि मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among all trees I am the sacred fig tree. Among divine sages I am Narada; among celestial musicians, Chitraratha; among perfected sages, the sage Kapila.
essence: The finest forms in creation are windows into Krishna.
simple_meaning: Krishna names the most revered example in each group of trees, sages, musicians, and perfected beings, showing how his presence appears through the finest forms in creation.
insight: It trains the mind to notice excellence in the world as a pointer to the divine presence behind it.
modern_relevance: You are walking through a temple garden after a hard decision, and one tree, one song, one face suddenly steadies you. The world keeps offering small doorways back to what matters.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम् । ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम् ॥
translation: घोड़ोंमें अमृतके साथ समुद्रसे प्रकट होनेवाले उच्चैःश्रवा नामक घोड़ेको, श्रेष्ठ हाथियोंमें ऐरावत नामक हाथीको और मनुष्योंमें राजाको मेरी विभूति मानो ॥
english_translation: Among horses, know me as Ucchaihshravas, born from nectar. Among royal elephants, I am Airavata, and among humans, I am the king.
essence: Greatness in the world is a visible trace of Krishna.
simple_meaning: Krishna says to see his presence in the finest horse, the greatest elephant, and the human king.
insight: It trains the mind to recognise excellence as a manifestation of the divine, not as mere accident or status.
modern_relevance: You watch a leader command a room, a rescue dog save a child, a musician hold everyone silent. Something in you knows: greatness is not random.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक् । प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः ॥
translation: आयुधोंमें वज्र और धेनुओंमें कामधेनु मैं हूँ ।  सन्तानउत्पत्तिका हेतु कामदेव मैं हूँ और सर्पोंमें वासुकि मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among weapons, I am the thunderbolt; among cows, I am the wish-fulfilling cow. I am the cause of procreation, and among serpents, I am Vasuki.
essence: Power, fertility, and danger all reveal the same source.
simple_meaning: Krishna names more of the finest powers and beings in the world as his expressions: thunderbolt, wish-fulfilling cow, the force behind procreation, and Vasuki among serpents.
insight: It trains attention to recognise excellence, force, and generative power as signs of the divine everywhere.
modern_relevance: You notice a flash of lightning over an empty field, then the calm strength of a cow in the next lane. The world feels less like separate objects and more like one living presence.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम् । पितृ़णामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम् ॥
translation: नागोंमें अनन्त शेषनाग और जलजन्तुओंका अधिपति वरुण मैं हूँ ।  पितरोंमें अर्यमा और शासन करनेवालोंमें यमराज मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among serpents I am Ananta; among water beings I am Varuna. Among ancestors I am Aryaman; among those who govern, I am Yama.
essence: The divine is visible in every order of existence.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the highest presence among serpents, water beings, ancestors, and rulers. He is showing that his presence runs through every level of the world.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated things to the one presence expressed through many forms.
modern_relevance: You sit in a room full of titles, family history, and hidden hierarchies. This verse asks you to see the same sacred presence moving through all of it, not just in obvious holy moments.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम् । मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम् ॥
translation: दैत्योंमें प्रह्लाद और गणना करनेवालोंमें काल मैं हूँ  ।  पशुओंमें सिंह और पक्षियोंमें गरुड मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among the daityas I am Prahlada; among calculators I am Time. Among beasts I am the lion, and among birds I am Garuda.
essence: Power, devotion, and majesty are all windows into one presence.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is present as Prahlada among the daityas, as Time among those who count, as the lion among beasts, and as Garuda among birds.
insight: It trains the mind to recognise the divine in excellence, courage, and devoted steadfastness.
modern_relevance: You watch a child protect a smaller one, or see fierce courage in someone facing illness without flinching. The same force that makes greatness visible is not random — it carries a deeper presence.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम् । झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी ॥
translation: पवित्र करनेवालोंमें वायु और शास्त्रधारियोंमें राम मैं हूँ ।  जलजन्तुओंमें मगर मैं हूँ ।  बहनेवाले स्त्रोतोंमें गङ्गाजी मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among purifiers, I am the wind. Among wielders of weapons, I am Rama. Among aquatic beings, I am the crocodile. Among flowing rivers, I am the Ganga.
essence: One reality appears as every noble force.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the purifying wind, Rama among warriors, the crocodile among water beings, and the Ganga among rivers.
insight: It trains the mind to recognise one sacred presence shining through many forms.
modern_relevance: You are standing by a river at dawn, exhausted and unsure. Then a sudden gust, the current, and the sheer force of nature make your private crisis feel smaller and more bearable.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन । अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम् ॥
translation: हे अर्जुन  सम्पूर्ण सर्गोंके आदि, मध्य तथा अन्तमें मैं ही हूँ ।  विद्याओंमें अध्यात्मविद्या और परस्पर शास्त्रार्थ करनेवालोंकातत्त्वनिर्णयके लिये किया जानेवाला वाद मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of all creation, Arjuna. Among all forms of knowledge, I am the knowledge of the true self; among speakers, I am the reasoned debate that seeks truth.
essence: All creation and all truth-seeking speech point back to Krishna.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the beginning, middle, and end of all creation. He is also the deepest self-knowledge and the honest debate that seeks truth.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated facts to the presence that holds every beginning, process, and ending together.
modern_relevance: You are in a room where two people argue past each other, each trying to win. Krishna points to the kind of speech that actually searches for truth, not ego.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च । अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताऽहं विश्वतोमुखः ॥
translation: अक्षरोंमें अकार और समासोंमें द्वन्द्व समास मैं हूँ ।  अक्षयकाल अर्थात् कालका भी महाकाल तथा सब ओर मुखवाला धाता भी मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among letters I am the letter A. Among compounds I am the dual compound. I am endless time itself, and I am the all-facing sustainer.
essence: Even letters and time carry Krishna's presence.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is present in the first letter, in a basic kind of compound word, in endless time, and in the all-facing power that sustains the world.
insight: It trains the mind to notice the sacred pattern inside language, time, and structure instead of treating them as ordinary background.
modern_relevance: You open a book before a hard exam, and even the first letter feels heavy. Or you watch a clock after a loss and realize time itself has become the thing you cannot outrun.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् । कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा ॥
translation: सबका हरण करनेवाली मृत्यु और उत्पन्न होनेवालोंका उभ्दव मैं हूँ तथा स्त्रीजातिमें कीर्ति, श्री, वाक्, स्मृति, मेधा, धृति और क्षमा मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: I am death that takes everything, and the source of all future beings. Among women, I am fame, fortune, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness, and forgiveness.
essence: Even death and virtue are expressions of the same divine source.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is both the force that ends all lives and the source of all that is yet to come. He also shines as noble qualities in women: fame, beauty, speech, memory, intelligence, steadiness, and forgiveness.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated events and traits to the larger source that holds them all.
modern_relevance: At a hospital bedside, a family watches both an ending and a beginning at once. This verse helps you see that loss, birth, and every admirable human quality can all be held within one larger presence.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम् । मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः ॥
translation: गायी जानेवाली श्रुतियोंमें बृहत्साम और वैदिक छन्दोंमें गायत्री छन्द मैं हूँ ।  बारह महीनोंमें मार्गशीर्ष और छः ऋतुओंमें वसन्त मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among hymns I am the Brihat-Sama; among meters I am Gayatri. Among months I am Margashirsha; among seasons I am spring.
essence: Sacred sound, time, and spring all carry the same presence.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the finest sacred chant, the most revered meter, the best month, and the season of spring.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated beauty to the presence shining through it.
modern_relevance: You hear a hymn in a temple and feel your chest soften. You notice first rain after a dry stretch and something in you wakes up. Krishna says that recognition is not accidental.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् । जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम् ॥
translation: छल करनेवालोंमें जूआ और तेजस्वियोंमें तेज मैं हूँ ।  जीतनेवालोंकी विजय, निश्चय करनेवालोंका निश्चय और सात्त्विक मनुष्योंका सात्त्विक भाव मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among deceivers I am gambling, among the vigorous I am splendor. I am victory, I am resolve, and I am the goodness of the good.
essence: What shines through victory and resolve is not separate from the divine.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is present as the force behind victory, determination, and the goodness found in noble people.
insight: It shifts the mind from owning success to recognising the source of strength behind success.
modern_relevance: You finally make the hard call after weeks of fear, and the steadiness in that moment feels bigger than personal confidence. This verse names that strength.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनंजयः । मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः ॥
translation: वृष्णिवंशियोंमें वासुदेव और पाण्डवोंमें धनञ्जय मैं हूँ ।  मुनियोंमें वेदव्यास और कवियोंमें कवि शुक्राचार्य भी मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among the Vrishnis I am Vasudeva; among the Pandavas I am Dhananjaya. Among sages I am Vyasa, and among poets I am Ushana, the poet.
essence: Greatness in many forms is one presence showing itself.
simple_meaning: Krishna says that the finest examples in different groups of people are his expressions. Greatness in warriors, sages, and poets all points back to him.
insight: It shifts the mind from isolated admiration to seeing one source expressed in many gifts.
modern_relevance: You meet a mentor, a fighter, and a writer who all seem to carry the same rare force. Instead of worshipping separate idols, you begin to sense one current moving through them all.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम् । मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम् ॥
translation: दमन करनेवालोंमें दण्डनीति और विजय चाहनेवालोंमें नीति मैं हूँ ।  गोपनीय भावोंमें मौन और ज्ञानवानोंमें ज्ञान मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: Among enforcers, I am punishment; among those seeking victory, I am policy. Among secrets, I am silence; among the wise, I am knowledge.
essence: True power is measured by restraint, silence, and clear understanding.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he appears as rightful force, strategic conduct, silence, and true understanding wherever they are found.
insight: It shifts attention from raw force to disciplined, intelligent action shaped by silence.
modern_relevance: You are in a room where one harsh word could break everything. The strongest move is not volume — it may be restraint, timing, and the calm choice to say only what is true.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन । न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम् ॥
translation: हे अर्जुन सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंका जो बीज है, वह बीज मैं ही हूँ क्योंकि मेरे बिना कोई भी चरअचर प्राणी नहीं है अर्थात् चरअचर सब कुछ मैं ही हूँ ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, I am the seed of all beings. Without me, nothing moving or unmoving could exist.
essence: All existence grows from one hidden source.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the source of every being. Nothing that moves or stands still can exist without him.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing life as scattered events to seeing one living source behind all forms.
modern_relevance: Standing alone in a hospital corridor while waiting for news, it can feel like life has split into separate pieces. This verse says the same source runs through all of it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परंतप । एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया ॥
translation: हे परंतप अर्जुन  मेरी दिव्य विभूतियोंका अन्त नहीं है ।  मैंने तुम्हारे सामने अपनी विभूतियोंका जो विस्तार कहा है, यह तो केवल संक्षेपसे कहा है ॥
english_translation: O scorcher of foes, my divine manifestations have no end. What I have described to you is only a brief summary of my vast manifestations.
essence: No list can contain the divine's endless expressions.
simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that his divine manifestations are limitless, and the examples already given are only a brief outline.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to contain the divine in examples to recognising endless presence beyond them.
modern_relevance: You finally understand one person’s brilliance, then another side of them appears that you never expected. The lesson is humbling: reality always exceeds the list you made.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा । तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम् ॥
translation: जोजो ऐश्वर्ययुक्त, शोभायुक्त और बलयुक्त प्राणी तथा वस्तु है, उसउसको तुम मेरे ही तेजयोग के अंशसे उत्पन्न हुई समझो ॥
english_translation: Whatever being or thing is endowed with splendour, beauty, or power—know that to have arisen from a spark of my radiance.
essence: Every genuine greatness is only a spark of my radiance.
simple_meaning: Anything that shines with beauty, strength, or greatness comes from Krishna's radiance. He asks Arjuna to recognize that source in every impressive thing.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated excellence to the deeper source behind all excellence.
modern_relevance: You see a leader command a room, a musician fill a hall, or a child radiate unusual courage. The verse asks you not to worship the surface alone, but to notice the source of that brilliance.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन । विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत् ॥
translation: अथवा हे अर्जुन  तुम्हें इस प्रकार बहुतसी बातें जाननेकी क्या आवश्यकता है मैं अपने किसी एक अंशसे सम्पूर्ण जगत् को व्याप्त करके स्थित हूँ ॥
english_translation: Or, Arjuna, what is the need for all this detailed knowledge? I sustain this entire universe with a single fragment of myself.
essence: The whole universe rests in a single fragment of the divine.
simple_meaning: Krishna says there is no need for endless detail: even a single part of his presence supports the entire universe.
insight: It shifts attention from counting manifestations to recognising the single source behind them all.
modern_relevance: You keep asking for one more explanation before you can trust the decision. But sometimes the pattern is already clear, and the rest is just your mind delaying surrender.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचमदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम् । यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  केवल मेरेपर कृपा करनेके लिये ही आपने जो परम गोपनीय अध्यात्मतत्तव जाननेका वचन कहा, उससे मेरा यह मोह नष्ट हो गया है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: By the gracious words you spoke for my benefit alone, my delusion has been dispelled.
essence: Clarity arrives when the hidden teaching is finally heard as personal grace.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says Krishna’s hidden teaching has cleared away his confusion. He feels the words were spoken just for his own good.
insight: It shifts the mind from confusion to gratitude, recognizing clarity as a gift received.
modern_relevance: After a hard conversation, you suddenly see what you were avoiding all along. The relief is not in winning the argument, but in having the fog lift.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया । त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम् ॥
translation: हे कमलनयन  सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंकी उत्पत्ति और प्रलय मैंने विस्तारपूर्वक आपसे ही सुना है और आपका अविनाशी माहात्म्य भी सुना है ॥
english_translation: O lotus-eyed one, I have heard from You in detail about the arising and passing away of all beings, and also about Your imperishable majesty.
essence: All change is clear only beside what does not change.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says he has learned from Krishna about how all beings come and go, and about Krishna's imperishable greatness.
insight: It shifts attention from the changing world to the unchanging source that gives it meaning.
modern_relevance: You sit beside someone who has just told you the hard truth, and the room goes quiet. The facts land, but what stays with you is the sense of something larger that cannot be shaken.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर । द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम ॥
translation: हे पुरुषोत्तम  आप अपनेआपको जैसा कहते हैं, यह वास्तवमें ऐसा ही है ।  हे परमेश्वर  आपके ईश्वरसम्बन्धी रूपको मैं देखना चाहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: O Supreme Person, everything you have said about yourself is true. Yet I wish to see your divine form.
essence: Belief becomes complete only when it wants to see.
simple_meaning: Arjuna accepts Krishna’s words as true, but asks to see Krishna’s divine form directly.
insight: It shifts the seeker from verbal understanding to direct vision.
modern_relevance: A friend explains something painful and true, and you nod because you believe them. But part of you still needs to see the full reality for yourself before you can move forward.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो । योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयाऽत्मानमव्ययम् ॥
translation: हे प्रभो  मेरे द्वारा आपका वह परम ऐश्वर रूप देखा जा सकता है  ऐसा अगर आप मानते हैं, तो हे योगेश्वर  आप अपने उस अविनाशी स्वरूपको मुझे दिखा दीजिये ॥
english_translation: If you think I can see that form, Lord, then show me your imperishable self, Master of yoga.
essence: Real vision begins when control gives way to asking.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to reveal his imperishable form if it can be seen by human eyes.
insight: It shifts the mind from control to receptive seeing.
modern_relevance: You stand before a decision too large for your own certainty and finally say, “Show me what is real.” That pause can be wiser than forcing an answer.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचपश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः । नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे पृथानन्दन  अब मेरे अनेक तरहके, अनेक अनेक वर्णों और आकृतियोंवाले सैकड़ोंहजारों दिव्यरूपोंको तू देख ॥
english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: See, Partha, my forms in hundreds and thousands, diverse, divine, and of many colors and shapes.
essence: The divine cannot be contained in one shape.
simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna to look at his countless divine forms, each with different colors and shapes.
insight: It shifts the mind from fixed identity to vast, living presence.
modern_relevance: You think you know someone by one role, one mood, one label. Then a crisis opens and you see how many forms a single life can hold.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: पश्यादित्यान्वसून्रुद्रानश्िवनौ मरुतस्तथा । बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याऽश्चर्याणि भारत ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन तू बारह आदित्योंको, आठ वसुओंको, ग्यारह रुद्रोंको और दो अश्विनीकुमारोंको तथा उनचास मरुद्गणोंको देख ।  जिनको तूने पहले कभी देखा नहीं, ऐसे बहुतसे आश्चर्यजनक रूपोंको भी तू देख ॥
english_translation: See the twelve Adityas, the eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras, the two Ashvins, and the forty-nine Maruts. See many wonders never seen before, O Bharata.
essence: The familiar universe is only a small part of what Krishna reveals.
simple_meaning: Krishna invites Arjuna to see the cosmic form’s many divine beings and wonders, beyond anything he has seen before.
insight: It trains the mind to widen its frame before it judges what is in front of it.
modern_relevance: You think one conversation will define everything, then the room opens and you realize there are larger forces, larger patterns, and more than one way to understand what is happening.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम् । मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद्द्रष्टुमिच्छसि ॥
translation: हे नींदको जीतनेवाले अर्जुन मेरे इस शरीरके एक देशमें चराचरसहित सम्पूर्ण जगत् को अभी देख ले ।  इसके सिवाय तू और भी जो कुछ देखना चाहता है, वह भी देख ले ॥
english_translation: Behold the entire universe, with all that moves and does not move, gathered here in one place in My body. See whatever else you wish to see as well.
essence: Everything you seek is already gathered in the divine form.
simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that the whole universe, moving and still, is contained in his body. Arjuna can also look for anything else he wants to see.
insight: It shifts the mind from fragmented seeing to a sense of all-in-one presence.
modern_relevance: You stand before a decision that feels split into a hundred pieces. Then one clear view arrives: the whole mess belongs to a larger order than your fear.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा । दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ॥
translation: परन्तु तू अपनी इस आँखसे अर्थात् चर्मचक्षुसे मेरेको देख ही नहीं सकता, इसलिये मैं तुझे दिव्य चक्षु देता हूँ, जिससे तू मेरी ईश्वरसम्बन्धी सामर्थ्यको देख ॥
english_translation: You cannot see me with these ordinary eyes. I give you divine sight, so you may behold my supreme power.
essence: Ordinary sight cannot hold the infinite; grace must widen the eye.
simple_meaning: Ordinary sight is not enough to see Krishna's true form. He gives Arjuna a divine way of seeing so he can witness that supreme power.
insight: It shifts the mind from forced inspection to receptive seeing.
modern_relevance: You can stare at the same problem for hours and still miss what matters. Sometimes clarity does not come from looking harder, but from receiving a wider way of seeing.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरिः । दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम् ॥
translation: सञ्जय बोले  हे राजन्  ऐसा कहकर फिर महायोगेश्वर भगवान् श्रीकृष्णने अर्जुनको परम ऐश्वररूप दिखाया ॥
english_translation: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus, O King, the great lord of yoga, Hari, revealed to Arjuna the supreme divine form.
essence: The answer is not a theory; it arrives as a vision.
simple_meaning: Sanjaya tells the king that Krishna then showed Arjuna his supreme divine form.
insight: It shifts the mind from hearing about the divine to confronting it directly.
modern_relevance: A person finally asks to see the full truth, not the comforting version. The answer arrives all at once, and it changes everything they thought they could control.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: अनेकवक्त्रनयनमनेकाद्भुतदर्शनम् । अनेकदिव्याभरणं दिव्यानेकोद्यतायुधम् ॥
translation: जिसके अनेक मुख और नेत्र हैं, अनेक तहरके अद्भुत दर्शन हैं, अनेक दिव्य आभूषण हैं, हाथोंमें उठाये हुए अनेक दिव्य आयुध हैं तथा जिनके गलेमें दिव्य मालाएँ हैं, जो दिव्य वस्त्र पहने हुए हैं, जिनके ललाट तथा शरीरपर दिव्य चन्दन, कुंकुम आदि लगा हुआ है, ऐसे सम्पूर्ण आश्चर्यमय, अनन्तरूपवाले तथा चारों तरफ मुखवाले देवअपने दिव्य स्वरूप को भगवान् ने दिखाया ॥
english_translation: With many mouths and eyes, with countless wondrous forms, adorned with many divine ornaments and many uplifted divine weapons.
essence: The divine form cannot be held inside one human image.
simple_meaning: The cosmic form appears with countless faces, eyes, ornaments, and divine weapons. It is a vast, overwhelming vision rather than a single human shape.
insight: It trains the mind to accept that reality may exceed ordinary categories and familiar appearances.
modern_relevance: You finally see the full picture after weeks of narrow thinking, and it is bigger, stranger, and harder to contain than you expected.
speaker: Sanjaya

verse_text: दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनम् । सर्वाश्चर्यमयं देवमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम् ॥
translation: जिसके अनेक मुख और नेत्र हैं, अनेक तहरके अद्भुत दर्शन हैं, अनेक दिव्य आभूषण हैं, हाथोंमें उठाये हुए अनेक दिव्य आयुध हैं तथा जिनके गलेमें दिव्य मालाएँ हैं, जो दिव्य वस्त्र पहने हुए हैं, जिनके ललाट तथा शरीरपर दिव्य चन्दन, कुंकुम आदि लगा हुआ है, ऐसे सम्पूर्ण आश्चर्यमय, अनन्त रूपोंवाले तथा चारों तरफ मुखवाले देवअपने दिव्य स्वरूप को भगवान् ने दिखाया ॥
english_translation: Wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrances, wondrous in every way, endless, and facing everywhere.
essence: The divine presence is beautiful, boundless, and impossible to face from only one side.
simple_meaning: Krishna's cosmic form is covered in divine garlands, clothes, and fragrance. It is endless, wondrous, and faces in every direction.
insight: It shifts perception from a single bounded form to an all-facing presence beyond limits.
modern_relevance: You stand speechless in front of something too vast to fit your plans — a birth, a loss, a revelation. The mind stops arguing when reality becomes larger than your frame.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता । यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ॥
translation: अगर आकाशमें एक साथ हजारों सूर्य उदित हो जायँ, तो भी उन सबका प्रकाश मिलकर उस महात्माविराट् रूप परमात्मा के प्रकाशके समान शायद ही हो ॥
english_translation: If a thousand suns rose together in the sky, their light would still barely match that great being's radiance.
essence: Even the brightest familiar light cannot measure the cosmic form's radiance.
simple_meaning: Arjuna says that even a thousand suns rising at once would not match the radiance of Krishna's cosmic form.
insight: It shifts the mind from measuring the divine by familiar things to admitting that ordinary scales collapse before it.
modern_relevance: You stand in a dark room and suddenly the screen flashes open with a truth you cannot unsee. The mind reaches for comparison, but the experience already exceeds it.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा । अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा ॥
translation: उस समय अर्जुनने देवोंके देव भगवान् के उस शरीरमें एक जगह स्थित अनेक प्रकारके विभागोंमें विभक्त सम्पूर्ण जगत् को देखा ॥
english_translation: There Arjuna saw the entire universe gathered in one place, divided in countless ways within the body of the Lord of the gods.
essence: One form can contain the whole universe.
simple_meaning: Arjuna saw the whole universe inside Krishna's cosmic form, all held together in one body and yet appearing in countless forms.
insight: It shifts the mind from narrow, personal perception to a wider vision of interconnected reality.
modern_relevance: You open a message expecting one answer, and instead the situation reveals a whole web of hidden causes, loyalties, and consequences. The simple story you carried in your head suddenly looks too small.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जयः । प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत ॥
translation: भगवान् के विश्वरूपको देखकर अर्जुन बहुत चकित हुए और आश्चर्यके कारण उनका शरीर रोमाञ्चित हो गया ।  वे हाथ जोड़कर विश्वरूप देवको मस्तकसे प्रणाम करके बोले ॥
english_translation: Then, overwhelmed with wonder, Arjuna’s hair stood on end. He bowed his head to the divine and spoke with folded hands.
essence: A glimpse of the vast can turn shock into surrender.
simple_meaning: Arjuna is stunned by the cosmic form. He bows his head, joins his hands, and begins to speak.
insight: It shifts the response from analysis to reverent speech when reality exceeds control.
modern_relevance: You open a message and realize the truth is bigger than your plan. Before you can argue, your body goes quiet and humility takes over.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचपश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहेसर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसङ्घान् । ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थमृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान् ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे देव  मैं आपके शरीरमें सम्पूर्ण देवताओंको, प्राणियोंके विशेषविशेष समुदायोंको कमलासनपर बैठे हुए ब्रह्माजीको, शङ्करजीको, सम्पूर्ण ऋषियोंको और सम्पूर्ण दिव्य सर्पोंको देख रहा हूँ ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: O divine one, I see all the gods in your body, and all kinds of distinct beings, Brahma seated on the lotus, Shiva, all the sages, and all the radiant serpents.
essence: The many forms of existence appear within one vast body.
simple_meaning: Arjuna sees the entire divine order inside Krishna's cosmic body: gods, beings of every kind, Brahma, Shiva, sages, and radiant serpents.
insight: It shifts perception from isolated details to the whole living field contained in one reality.
modern_relevance: You stare at a decision that seems private, then suddenly see how many lives, histories, and forces are braided into it. The choice is bigger than your fear.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रंपश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम् । नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिंपश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप ॥
translation: हे विश्वरूप  हे विश्वेश्वरव  आपको मैं अनेक हाथों, पेटों, मुखों और नेत्रोंवाला तथा सब ओरसे अनन्त रूपोंवाला देख रहा हूँ ।  मैं आपके न आदिको, न मध्यको और न अन्तको ही देख रहा हूँ ॥
english_translation: I see You with many arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes, everywhere without end. I see no beginning, middle, or end of You, O Lord of all, O cosmic form.
essence: The largest reality has no edge the mind can grasp.
simple_meaning: Arjuna sees Krishna’s cosmic form as limitless, with countless arms, mouths, and eyes. He cannot find its beginning, middle, or end.
insight: It shifts the mind from measuring reality to bowing before what cannot be contained.
modern_relevance: You stand before a truth too large to fit your old categories. The urge to label it fades; reverence begins where control ends.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं चतेजोराशिं सर्वतोदीप्तिमन्तम् । पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ताद्दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम् ॥
translation: मैं आपको किरीट, गदा, चक्र तथा शङ्ख और पद्म धारण किये हुए देख रहा हूँ ।  आपको तेजकी राशि, सब ओर प्रकाश करनेवाले, देदीप्यमान अग्नि तथा सूर्यके समान कान्तिवाले, नेत्रोंके द्वारा कठिनतासे देखे जानेयोग्य और सब तरफसे अप्रमेयस्वरूप देख रहा हूँ ॥
