translation: प्रकृति और पुरुष  दोनोंको ही तुम अनादि समझो और विकारों तथा गुणोंको भी प्रकृतिसे ही उत्पन्न समझो ।  कार्य और करणके द्वारा होनेवाली क्रियाओंको उत्पन्न करनेमें प्रकृति हेतु कही जाती है और सुखदुःखोंके भोक्तापनमें पुरुष हेतु कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: Nature is said to be the cause of the body, the senses, and action. The inner being is said to be the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain.
essence: Action belongs to nature; experience belongs to the one who knows.
simple_meaning: The body, senses, and actions belong to nature. Pleasure and pain are experienced by the inner being. Krishna separates the changing process from the one who experiences it.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame to clear witnessing of action and experience.
modern_relevance: You watch your body tense before a hard conversation, then feel the sting afterward. This verse reminds you that the surge belongs to nature; the witness is not the storm.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान् । कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु ॥
translation: प्रकृतिमें स्थित पुरुष ही प्रकृतिजन्य गुणोंका भोक्ता बनता है और गुणोंका सङ्ग ही उसके ऊँचनीच योनियोंमें जन्म लेनेका कारण बनता है ॥
english_translation: The inner being, situated in nature, experiences the qualities born of nature. Attachment to those qualities causes birth in good and bad wombs.
essence: Attachment to changing qualities keeps the cycle of birth going.
simple_meaning: The inner being, while tied to nature, experiences its changing qualities. Clinging to those qualities is what leads to repeated births in favorable and unfavorable forms.
insight: It shifts attention from the event to the attachment that keeps the cycle going.
modern_relevance: You keep replaying the same argument in your head after the call ends. The event is over, but your attachment to its emotional charge keeps pulling you back.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: उपद्रष्टाऽनुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः । परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः ॥
translation: यह पुरुष प्रकृतिशरीर के साथ सम्बन्ध रखनेसे उपद्रष्टा, उसके साथ मिलकर सम्मति, अनुमति देनेसे अनुमन्ता, अपनेको उसका भरणपोषण करनेवाला माननेसे भर्ता, उसके सङ्गसे सुखदुःख भोगनेसे भोक्ता, और अपनेको उसका स्वामी माननेसे महेश्वर बन जाता है ।  परन्तु स्वरूपसे यह पुरुष परमात्मा कहा जाता है ।  यह देहमें रहता हुआ भी देहसे पर सम्बन्धरहित ही है ॥
english_translation: The inner self becomes the witness, consent-giver, supporter, enjoyer, and great lord through its relation with the body. Yet in its true nature, it is called the supreme self and remains beyond the body.
essence: Identity is borrowed from the body; the true self stands beyond it.
simple_meaning: The inner self seems to take on many roles because it is linked with the body, but in its true nature it remains beyond the body.
insight: It shifts the mind from role-based identity to direct seeing of what remains unchanged beneath experience.
modern_relevance: You replay one mistake after a hard conversation and start calling yourself the failure, the fixer, the victim, the judge. This verse cuts through that blur: roles arise from identification, not from your deepest nature.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैःसह । सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते ॥
translation: इस प्रकार पुरुषको और गुणोंके सहित प्रकृतिको जो मनुष्य अलगअलग जानता है, वह सब तरहका बर्ताव करता हुआ भी फिर जन्म नहीं लेता ॥
english_translation: Whoever thus knows the purusha and prakriti together with the qualities is not born again, even while living and acting in every way.
essence: Clear seeing frees you while life still continues.
simple_meaning: A person who clearly sees the true self, the body-nature, and the qualities that move them is no longer caught in rebirth, even while living normally.
insight: It shifts attention from being trapped inside experience to recognizing the one who can observe it.
modern_relevance: You are in the middle of a painful conversation, but part of you is watching the fear, the anger, and the urge to defend. That inner clarity changes everything about how much the moment owns you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना । अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे ॥
translation: कई मनुष्य ध्यानयोगके द्वारा, कई सांख्ययोगके द्वारा और कई कर्मयोगके द्वारा अपनेआपसे अपनेआपमें परमात्मतत्त्वका अनुभव करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Some realize the true self within through meditation on the self. Others through clear discernment and yoga, and still others through the yoga of action.
essence: The same realization opens through different disciplines.
simple_meaning: People realize the true self in different ways: through meditation, through clear discernment, or through the yoga of action.
insight: It shifts the mind from one-size-fits-all spirituality to a recognition that different practices can lead to the same realization.
modern_relevance: You sit in a quiet room, trying to force clarity before a hard decision, and nothing comes. This verse reminds you that insight may arrive through stillness, analysis, or steady action.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य उपासते । तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः ॥
translation: दूसरे मनुष्य इस प्रकार ध्यानयोग, सांख्ययोग, कर्मयोग, आदि साधनोंको नहीं जानते, केवल जीवन्मुक्त महापुरुषोंसे सुनकर उपासना करते हैं, ऐसे वे सुननेके परायण मनुष्य भी मृत्युको तर जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Others do not know these paths, but they worship by hearing from others. Even they cross beyond death if they listen with devotion.
essence: Devoted listening can carry a person beyond fear and mortality.
simple_meaning: Some people do not understand these practices directly, but they listen to wise teachers and worship with trust. Even they can go beyond death through devoted listening.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliant certainty to receptive trust in living guidance.
modern_relevance: You sit in a hospital corridor, not knowing what to do next, while one steady voice explains the next step. In that moment, trust in the right guidance matters more than having every answer.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यावत्सञ्जायते किञ्चित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम् । क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  स्थावर और जंगम जितने भी प्राणी पैदा होते हैं, उनको तुम क्षेत्र और क्षेत्रज्ञके संयोगसे उत्पन्न हुए समझो ॥
english_translation: O best among the Bharatas, know that whatever comes into being, moving or unmoving, arises from the union of the field and the knower of the field.
essence: All forms arise from the meeting of awareness and changing nature.
simple_meaning: All living forms, moving or still, arise from the meeting of the field and the knower of the field.
insight: It shifts attention from outer forms to the hidden principle that makes any form appear.
modern_relevance: You watch a child sleep, a crowd rush past, a body age in the mirror. Krishna points beneath all forms and says: look for the meeting of awareness and the changing field.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् । विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
translation: जो नष्ट होते हुए सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें परमात्माको नाशरहित और समरूपसे स्थित देखता है, वही वास्तवमें सही देखता है ॥
english_translation: One who sees the supreme being equally present in all beings, imperishable amid the perishing, truly sees.
essence: Real seeing notices one imperishable presence in every changing form.
simple_meaning: True seeing means recognizing one unchanging presence in every living being, even while bodies and forms keep changing and disappearing.
insight: It shifts perception from separation to shared presence, changing how you look at every person before you act.
modern_relevance: You’re in a hospital corridor, staring at a stranger’s exhausted face, then at your own family member in the next room. The verse asks you to see beyond labels and notice the same living presence in both.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् । न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
translation: क्योंकि सब जगह समरूपसे स्थित ईश्वरको समरूपसे देखनेवाला मनुष्य अपनेआपसे अपनी हिंसा नहीं करता, इसलिये वह परमगतिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Seeing the divine equally everywhere, a person does not wound the true self by the true self, and reaches the highest state.
essence: Seeing unity everywhere ends the violence that returns to yourself.
simple_meaning: Seeing the same divine presence everywhere ends inner self-harm and leads to the highest state.
insight: It shifts perception from divided beings to one shared presence, ending the reflex to injure yourself through hatred or fear.
modern_relevance: You replay a harsh conversation in your head and turn it into self-blame. The moment you stop dividing people into enemies and allies, the inner violence eases.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः । यः पश्यति तथाऽऽत्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति ॥
translation: जो सम्पूर्ण क्रियाओंको सब प्रकारसे प्रकृतिके द्वारा ही की जाती हुई देखता है और अपनेआपको अकर्ता देखता अनुभव करता है, वही यथार्थ देखता है ॥
english_translation: One who sees all actions as being done only by nature, and sees the true self as the non-doer, sees rightly.
essence: Freedom begins when you stop claiming every action as yours.
simple_meaning: All actions are carried out by nature, while the true self remains a non-doer. Clear seeing means noticing this distinction directly.
insight: It shifts attention from personal ownership of action to clear witnessing of how action actually occurs.
modern_relevance: You replay a painful conversation at 2 a.m., convinced you caused everything. This verse loosens that knot: action flows through conditions, and not every movement belongs to your deepest identity.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति । तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा ॥
translation: जिस कालमें साधक प्राणियोंके अलगअलग भावोंको एक प्रकृतिमें ही स्थित देखता है और उस प्रकृतिसे ही उन सबका विस्तार देखता है, उस कालमें वह ब्रह्मको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: When one sees all beings as rooted in one nature and all expansion arising from that source, one attains the supreme reality.
essence: Many beings are one reality seen through different forms.
simple_meaning: When a person sees the many forms of living beings as arising from one underlying reality, that person reaches that reality.
insight: It shifts perception from isolated forms to the single reality behind them.
modern_relevance: You watch a family argument and stop seeing only sides. Beneath the anger, fear, pride, and hurt, you begin to notice one shared human source moving through different forms.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः । शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते ॥
translation: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  यह पुरुष स्वयं अनादि और गुणोंसे रहित होनेसे अविनाशी परमात्मस्वरूप ही है ।  यह शरीरमें रहता हुआ भी न करता है और न लिप्त होता है ॥
english_translation: O son of Kunti, this supreme self is beginningless, beyond the gunas, and imperishable. Though abiding in the body, it does not act and is not stained.
essence: What you are remains unstained, even while life moves through you.
simple_meaning: The true self has no beginning, is beyond the three qualities of nature, and cannot be destroyed. Even while living in a body, it neither performs actions nor gets tainted by them.
insight: It shifts identity away from what the body and mind do toward the untouched awareness that remains.
modern_relevance: You said something sharp in anger, then spent the whole night replaying it. The mind wants to fuse you with the mistake; this verse separates the actor from the deeper witness.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते । सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥
translation: जैसे सब जगह व्याप्त आकाश अत्यन्त सूक्ष्म होनेसे कहीं भी लिप्त नहीं होता, ऐसे ही सब जगह परिपूर्ण आत्मा किसी भी देहमें लिप्त नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: As all-pervading space is not tainted because of its subtlety, so the self, present in every body, is not tainted.
essence: What is everywhere cannot be stained by what changes.
simple_meaning: The true self is present in every body, but it is never stained or affected by the body it inhabits.
insight: It shifts identity from the changing body to the untouched awareness that witnesses change.
modern_relevance: You hear a harsh comment and feel it sink into your chest. The verse reminds you that what is aware of the hurt is not the hurt itself.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः । क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन  जैसे एक ही सूर्य सम्पूर्ण संसारको प्रकाशित करता है, ऐसे ही क्षेत्री क्षेत्रज्ञ, आत्मा सम्पूर्ण क्षेत्रको प्रकाशित करता है ॥
english_translation: As one sun illuminates this whole world, so the knower of the field illuminates the whole field, O Bharata.
essence: Awareness illuminates everything without being touched by what it sees.
simple_meaning: The one who knows the field makes the whole field known, just as one sun lights up the entire world.
insight: It shifts attention from the contents of experience to the awareness that makes experience visible.
modern_relevance: You sit alone after a painful argument, replaying every sentence. The mind feels like the whole room — until you notice the quiet awareness in which the replay appears.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा । भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम् ॥
translation: इस प्रकार जो ज्ञानरूपी नेत्रसे क्षेत्र और क्षेत्रज्ञके अन्तरविभाग को तथा कार्यकारणसहित प्रकृतिसे स्वयंको अलग जानते हैं, वे परमात्माको प्राप्त हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: In this way, those who know the distinction between the field and the knower of the field with the eye of wisdom, and who know release from the source of nature, attain the supreme.
essence: Clear seeing separates you from what changes and opens the way beyond it.
simple_meaning: True seeing separates the changing field from the one who knows it. That clear discrimination frees a person from identification with nature and leads to the highest state.
insight: It shifts attention from identifying with the changing field to recognising the witness that stands apart.
modern_relevance: You catch yourself saying, "I am a failure," after one brutal conversation. This verse interrupts that collapse: the hurt, the thought, and the one who notices them are not the same.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचपरं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् । यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  सम्पूर्ण ज्ञानोंमें उत्तम और पर ज्ञानको मैं फिर कहूँगा, जिसको जानकर सबकेसब मुनिलोग इस संसारसे मुक्त होकर परमसिद्धिको प्राप्त हो गये हैं ॥
english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: I will speak again of the highest knowledge, the best of all knowledge. Knowing this, all sages have reached the supreme perfection from here.
essence: Some knowledge does not inform you; it completes you.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he will teach the highest kind of knowledge, the one that has taken wise seekers to the greatest fulfillment.
insight: It shifts the mind from collecting ideas to seeking the understanding that transforms being itself.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a message that could change a relationship, and your finger hovers over send. Some knowledge does not add more facts — it changes who can act without fear.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः । सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च ॥
translation: इस ज्ञानका आश्रय लेकर जो मनुष्य मेरी सधर्मताको प्राप्त हो गये हैं, वे महासर्गमें भी पैदा नहीं होते और महाप्रलयमें भी व्यथित नहीं होते ॥
english_translation: Having taken refuge in this knowledge, they attain my likeness. They are not born at creation, and they are not troubled at dissolution.
essence: True understanding makes beginning and ending stop ruling you.
simple_meaning: With this knowledge, a person becomes like Krishna in nature. Such a person is no longer shaken by cosmic creation or destruction.
insight: It shifts attention from temporary events to the unshaken ground beneath them.
modern_relevance: You are standing in a hospital corridor after hearing that life will never be the same. This verse speaks to the part of you that can remain steady even when everything around you begins or ends.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन् गर्भं दधाम्यहम् । संभवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन  मेरी मूल प्रकृति तो उत्पत्तिस्थान है और मैं उसमें जीवरूप गर्भका स्थापन करता हूँ ।  उससे सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंकी उत्पत्ति होती है ॥
english_translation: O Bharata, my primal nature is the womb; I place the seed in it. From that, all beings are born.
essence: All birth comes from a source beyond personal control.
simple_meaning: All living forms arise from the union of primal nature and the seed placed within it. Krishna is explaining how birth itself unfolds.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated individuality to the hidden process that generates every form.
modern_relevance: A child’s first heartbeat appears on a screen, and no one in the room can explain life in a single sentence. The verse reminds you that existence comes through forces larger than personal control.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः सम्भवन्ति याः । तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता ॥
translation: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  सम्पूर्ण योनियोंमें प्राणियोंके जितने शरीर पैदा होते हैं, उन सबकी मूल प्रकृति तो माता है और मैं बीजस्थापन करनेवाला पिता हूँ ॥
english_translation: O son of Kunti, in all forms of birth, the material nature is the womb, and I am the seed-giving father.
essence: All forms arise from one source, and the divine gives them life.
simple_meaning: All living forms come from the same source of nature, while Krishna says he is the seed-giving father behind their coming into being.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated individuals to the one source from which all forms arise.
modern_relevance: You look at a newborn’s face and then at an old family photo, and the same lineage runs through both. Behind every separate life, there is one shared source you rarely notice.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः । निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् ॥
translation: हे महाबाहो  प्रकृतिसे उत्पन्न होनेवाले सत्त्व, रज और तम  ये तीनों गुण अविनाशी देहीको देहमें बाँध देते हैं ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, the three qualities of nature—sattva, rajas, and tamas—bind the imperishable inner being to the body.
essence: Nature's three forces keep the changeless one identified with the body.
simple_meaning: The three qualities born from nature keep the imperishable inner being tied to the body.
insight: It shifts attention from moral blame to seeing the forces shaping behavior.
modern_relevance: You know that moment when you promise yourself you will react calmly, then irritation, craving, or fog takes over anyway? This verse points to the deeper machinery behind that takeover.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम् । सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ ॥
translation: हे पापरहित अर्जुन  उन गुणोंमें सत्त्वगुण निर्मल स्वच्छ होनेके कारण प्रकाशक और निर्विकार है ।  वह सुख और ज्ञानकी आसक्तिसे देहीको बाँधता है ॥
english_translation: Among those qualities, sattva—because it is pure and luminous and free from affliction—binds the embodied being through attachment to happiness and to knowledge, O sinless one.
essence: Even clarity becomes bondage when you cling to its pleasure.
simple_meaning: Even purity can become a chain when you cling to comfort or to being wise. Sattva brings light, but attachment to that light still binds.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing refined states to seeing how attachment operates even inside them.
modern_relevance: You finally feel calm after weeks of stress, then panic at the thought of losing that calm. You start guarding the feeling instead of living. The grip has simply changed shape.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् । तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् ॥
translation: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  तृष्णा और आसक्तिको पैदा करनेवाले रजोगुणको तुम रागस्वरूप समझो ।  वह कर्मोंकी आसक्तिसे शरीरधारीको बाँधता है ॥
english_translation: Know rajas as passion-born, born of craving and attachment. It binds the embodied being through attachment to action, O son of Kunti.
essence: Craving turns action into a chain.
simple_meaning: Restless desire and attachment create rajas. That force traps a person by making them cling to action and its rewards.
insight: It shifts attention from the task itself to the craving that clings to it.
modern_relevance: You refresh your inbox again, then check the message thread, then the notifications. The urge feels small, but it keeps pulling you back into the same loop.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् । प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशी अर्जुन  सम्पूर्ण देहधारियोंको मोहित करनेवाले तमोगुणको तुम अज्ञानसे उत्पन्न होनेवाला समझो ।  वह प्रमाद, आलस्य और निद्राके द्वारा देहधारियोंको बाँधता है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, know tamas to be born of ignorance and deluding all embodied beings. It binds them through heedlessness, laziness, and sleep.
essence: Confusion binds most through laziness, not force.
simple_meaning: Tamas is the force of confusion and inertia. It clouds judgment and traps people through carelessness, laziness, and sleepiness.
insight: It teaches you to identify inertia by its symptoms: delay, dullness, and mental fog.
modern_relevance: You open your phone “for a minute” and lose half an hour, then feel foggy and late. That drag is not harmless rest; it is tamas quietly taking the wheel.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत । ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन  सत्त्वगुण सुखमें और रजोगुण कर्ममें लगाकर मनुष्यपर विजय करता है तथा तमोगुण ज्ञानको ढककर एवं प्रमादमें भी लगाकर मनुष्यपर विजंय करता है ॥
english_translation: Sattva binds through pleasure, rajas through action, and tamas, covering knowledge, binds through negligence.
essence: Each force traps you in a different way: comfort, activity, or blindness.
simple_meaning: Three forces shape human behavior differently: one lures with pleasure, one drives constant activity, and one hides understanding while pulling a person into carelessness.
insight: It trains you to spot the hidden mode driving your choices so you can step back before it controls you.
modern_relevance: You open your phone for one quick check and lose twenty minutes, then another hour chasing tasks, then realize you never thought clearly at all. This verse names the three ways the mind gets hijacked.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत । रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन  रजोगुण और तमोगुणको दबाकर सत्त्वगुण सत्त्वगुण, और तमोगुणको दबाकर रजोगुण, वैसे ही सत्त्वगुण और रजोगुणको दबाकर तमोगुण बढ़ता है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, when rajas and tamas are subdued, sattva rises. When sattva and tamas are subdued, rajas rises. When sattva and rajas are subdued, tamas rises.
essence: What dominates the mind is temporary, not who you are.
simple_meaning: The three qualities keep replacing one another. When one becomes stronger, the others are pushed down.
insight: It teaches you to notice which quality is currently leading, instead of mistaking a passing state for your nature.
modern_relevance: You wake up sharp, then drift into fog by noon, then feel restless at night. The mind is not one fixed mood — it keeps changing hands.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते । ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत ॥
translation: जब इस मनुष्यशरीरमें सब द्वारोंइन्द्रियों और अन्तःकरण में प्रकाश स्वच्छता और ज्ञान विवेक प्रकट हो जाता है, तब जानना चाहिये कि सत्त्वगुण बढ़ा हुआ है ॥
english_translation: When light, clarity, and understanding arise in all the gates of this body, know that sattva has grown strong.
essence: Inner brightness is the sign that clarity is taking over.
simple_meaning: When the senses and mind become bright, clear, and wise, that is a sign that sattva is increasing.
insight: It shifts attention from judging yourself by mood to reading the quality of awareness itself.
modern_relevance: You wake up after a chaotic night and suddenly the room feels sharper, your thoughts less sticky, your reactions slower. That quiet brightness is a sign that your mind has cleared.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा । रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  रजोगुणके बढ़नेपर लोभ, प्रवृत्ति, कर्मोंका आरम्भ, अशान्ति और स्पृहा  ये वृत्तियाँ पैदा होती हैं ॥
english_translation: O best of the Bharatas, when rajas grows, greed, activity, the beginning of actions, restlessness, and desire arise.
essence: Restless wanting multiplies action, but never settles the mind.
simple_meaning: When rajas becomes strong, greed, restless activity, constant starting, and craving appear.
insight: It teaches you to notice the signature of rajas in your own mind: urgency, craving, and unfinished motion.
modern_relevance: You open five tabs, start three tasks, and still feel unsatisfied. That buzzing urge to keep doing more is not productivity — it is restlessness taking over.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च । तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन ॥
translation: हे कुरुनन्दन  तमोगुणके बढ़नेपर अप्रकाश, अप्रवृत्ति, प्रमाद और मोह  ये वृत्तियाँ भी पैदा होती हैं ॥
english_translation: O descendant of Kuru, when tamas grows strong, darkness, inertia, negligence, and delusion arise.
essence: Darkness does not stay still; it breeds neglect and confusion.
simple_meaning: When tamas becomes stronger, a person loses clarity, becomes inactive, starts neglecting things, and falls into confusion.
insight: It teaches you to recognize inertia as a pattern that breeds confusion, not as harmless rest.
modern_relevance: You keep scrolling at 1:13 a.m., telling yourself you will decide tomorrow. By morning, the problem feels heavier, and even simple action feels distant.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् । तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते ॥
translation: जिस समय सत्त्वगुण बढ़ा हो, उस समय यदि देहधारी मनुष्य मर जाता है, तो वह,उत्तमवेत्ताओंके निर्मल लोकोंमें जाता है ॥
english_translation: When sattva is predominant at death, the embodied being reaches the pure worlds of the wise.
essence: A clear state carries consciousness toward a clearer destination.
simple_meaning: If a person dies while sattva is strongest, that being reaches pure realms associated with the wise.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated actions to the quality of mind that dominates your life.
modern_relevance: You are exhausted after a long day, and your mind is either clear or clouded when the hardest conversation arrives. The state you live in most deeply leaves the strongest imprint.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते । तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते ॥
translation: रजोगुणके बढ़नेपर मरनेवाला प्राणी मनुष्ययोनिमें जन्म लेता है तथा तमोगुणके बढ़नेपर मरनेवाला मूढ़योनियोंमें जन्म लेता है ॥
english_translation: A being who dies in rajas is born among those attached to action. A being who dies in tamas is born among deluded forms.
essence: Your strongest tendency decides the shape of your next beginning.
simple_meaning: The state of mind at death shapes the kind of birth that follows. Restless desire leads to another life of attachment; dull confusion leads to a lower, more deluded condition.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated choices to the dominant force shaping a life over time.
modern_relevance: You keep choosing the same kind of relationship, the same kind of fight, the same kind of excuse. Krishna would say the pattern is already teaching you where it leads.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम् । रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम् ॥
translation: विवेकी पुरुषोंने शुभकर्मका तो सात्त्विक निर्मल फल कहा है, राजस कर्मका फल दुःख कहा है और तामस कर्मका फल अज्ञान मूढ़ता कहा है ॥
english_translation: The result of wholesome action is pure and clear; the result of rajasic action is suffering; the result of tamasic action is ignorance and delusion.
essence: Action carries its own flavor of result.
simple_meaning: Wholesome action leads to a clear, pure result. Restless action leads to suffering. Dark, confused action leads to ignorance and delusion.
insight: It shifts attention from the act alone to the quality of mind behind it.
modern_relevance: You send the message in anger, then stare at the screen all night. The words were yours; the fallout was too. This verse helps you see the cost before you act.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च । प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ॥
translation: सत्त्वगुणसे ज्ञान और रजोगुणसे लोभ आदि ही उत्पन्न होते हैं तमोगुणसे प्रमाद, मोह एवं अज्ञान भी उत्पन्न होता है ॥
english_translation: From sattva comes knowledge; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance.
essence: Your mental weather has causes: clarity, craving, and confusion each grow from different qualities.
simple_meaning: A clear, balanced nature gives rise to understanding. Restless nature produces greed. Heavy, dull nature produces carelessness, delusion, and ignorance.
insight: It shifts attention from moral self-blame to pattern recognition: notice which guna is driving the mind, then respond wisely.
modern_relevance: You open your phone at 1 a.m. and feel the pull to keep scrolling, buying, comparing, numbing. The verse helps you name the force behind the spiral instead of calling it 'just me.'
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः । जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः ॥
translation: सत्त्वगुणमें स्थित मनुष्य ऊर्ध्वलोकोंमें जाते हैं, रजोगुणमें स्थित मनुष्य मृत्युलोकमें जन्म लेते हैं और निन्दनीय तमोगुणकी वृत्तिमें स्थित मनुष्य अधोगतिमें जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those established in sattva go upward; those in rajas remain in the middle; those in the lowest movement of tamas go downward.
essence: Your inner quality decides the direction of your life.
simple_meaning: People shaped by clarity rise to higher states. People ruled by restlessness stay in the middle. People sunk in dullness fall into lower states.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated actions to the deeper quality that drives them.
modern_relevance: You keep repeating the same late-night spiral, the same reactive argument, the same drained morning. The state you live from quietly decides the life you keep rebuilding.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति । गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति ॥
translation: जब विवेकी विचारकुशल मनुष्य तीनों गुणोंके सिवाय अन्य किसीको कर्ता नहीं देखता और अपनेको गुणोंसे पर अनुभव करता है, तब वह मेरे स्वरूपको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: When the seer understands that no doer exists apart from the three qualities, and knows the divine nature beyond them, that seer reaches my being.
essence: Freedom begins when you stop mistaking qualities for a personal doer.
simple_meaning: Clear seeing reveals that action belongs to the three qualities, not to a separate personal doer. When a person sees beyond them, they come to Krishna's nature.
insight: It shifts responsibility from ego to clear seeing, so action can happen without false ownership.
modern_relevance: You replay a painful conversation for hours, blaming yourself for every word. Then it clicks: much of what happened came from moods, habits, and pressures larger than one isolated self.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान् । जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते ॥
translation: देहधारी विवेकी मनुष्य देहको उत्पन्न करनेवाले इन तीनों गुणोंका अतिक्रमण करके जन्म, मृत्यु और वृद्धावस्थारूप दुःखोंसे रहित हुआ अमरताका अनुभव करता है ॥
english_translation: The embodied one who rises beyond these three qualities, which arise from the body, is freed from birth, death, old age, and sorrow, and attains immortality.
essence: Freedom begins when the three qualities no longer define you.
simple_meaning: A person who rises above the three qualities that shape the body is no longer bound by birth, death, old age, or sorrow.
insight: It shifts attention from managing symptoms of change to seeing the self as untouched by them.
modern_relevance: You watch your body age in the mirror, then feel the panic rise with every ache, deadline, and loss. This verse says the deepest part of you is not trapped in that churn.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचकैर्लिंगैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो । किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे प्रभो  इन तीनों गुणोंसे अतीत हुआ मनुष्य किन लक्षणोंसे युक्त होता है उसके आचरण कैसे होते हैं और इन तीनों गुणोंका अतिक्रमण कैसे किया जा सकता है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: O Lord, by what signs is a person known who has gone beyond these three qualities? How does such a person behave, and how does one cross beyond the three qualities?
essence: Real freedom must be visible, livable, and learnable.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks how to recognize someone who has gone beyond the three qualities, how that person behaves, and how such freedom is reached.
insight: It turns abstract philosophy into a practical test: look for signs, conduct, and method.
modern_relevance: You hear a calm person speak after a painful breakup and wonder: what changed in them? This is the question behind the question — how does freedom actually show up in a human life?
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव । न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे पाण्डव  प्रकाश, प्रवृत्ति तथा मोह  ये सभी अच्छी तरहसे प्रवृत्त हो जायँ तो भी गुणातीत मनुष्य इनसे द्वेष नहीं करता, और ये सभी निवृत्त हो जायँ तो इनकी इच्छा नहीं करता ॥
english_translation: Krishna said: O Arjuna, the one who has gone beyond the three gunas does not hate light, activity, or confusion when they appear, and does not long for them when they disappear.
essence: Freedom begins when changing states stop controlling your response.
simple_meaning: A person beyond the three gunas stays even-minded. When clarity, energy, or confusion appear, there is no hatred. When they fade, there is no craving.
insight: It teaches you to observe changing inner states without resistance or craving.
modern_relevance: You wake up clear one day, restless the next, numb after that. Instead of treating each state like a verdict on your life, you let it move through without panic or pursuit.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते । गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते ॥
translation: जो उदासीनकी तरह स्थित है और जो गुणोंके द्वारा विचलित नहीं किया जा सकता तथा गुण ही गुणोंमें बरत रहे हैं  इस भावसे जो अपने स्वरूपमें ही स्थित रहता है और स्वयं कोई भी चेष्टा नहीं करता ॥
english_translation: One who remains like an indifferent witness, unmoved by the three qualities, stands firm and does not stir, knowing only that the qualities are acting among themselves.
essence: Freedom begins when movement happens, but identity does not.
simple_meaning: A wise person stays steady, not shaken by the three qualities, and sees that they are only moving among themselves.
insight: It shifts attention from being carried by mental states to remaining established while they change.
modern_relevance: A harsh email lands, your chest tightens, and the old urge to react flares up. This verse teaches you to notice the surge without becoming it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः । तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः ॥
translation: जो धीर मनुष्य सुखदुःखमें सम तथा अपने स्वरूपमें स्थित रहता है जो मिट्टीके ढेले, पत्थर और सोनेमें सम रहता है जो प्रियअप्रियमें तथा अपनी निन्दास्तुतिमें सम रहता है जो मानअपमानमें तथा मित्रशत्रुके पक्षमें सम रहता है जो सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंके आरम्भका त्यागी है, वह मनुष्य गुणातीत कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: The steady one remains equal in pleasure and pain, in a clod of earth, a stone, and gold; equal toward the liked and the disliked, toward praise and blame.
essence: Steadiness means nothing external gets to decide your center.
simple_meaning: A truly steady person does not get shaken by pleasure, pain, praise, blame, wealth, or ordinary objects. They stay centered in themselves.
insight: It trains you to stop measuring your worth by shifting conditions and opinions.
modern_relevance: You open your phone and see praise from one person, criticism from another, and your mood swings before breakfast. This verse reminds you that stability is not controlled by other people's reactions.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः । सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥
translation: जो धीर मनुष्य सुखदुःखमें सम तथा अपने स्वरूपमें स्थित रहता है जो मिट्टीके ढेले, पत्थर और सोनेमें सम रहता है जो प्रियअप्रियमें तथा अपनी निन्दास्तुतिमें सम रहता है जो मानअपमानमें तथा मित्रशत्रुके पक्षमें सम रहता है जो सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंके आरम्भका त्यागी है, वह मनुष्य गुणातीत कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: The steady one is equal in honor and dishonor, equal toward friend and foe, and has abandoned all undertakings. Such a person is called beyond the three gunas.
essence: Freedom begins when praise, blame, and personal impulse lose their power over you.
simple_meaning: A truly steady person stays the same in praise or insult, with friends or enemies, and no longer starts actions from personal craving. That person rises beyond the three gunas.
insight: It shifts the mind from social reaction to inner steadiness and non-reactive action.
modern_relevance: A harsh comment lands in a group chat, and your chest tightens. Before you reply, you can notice how quickly praise and insult try to steer you. This verse points to a steadier place.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्ितयोगेन सेवते । स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य अव्यभिचारी भक्तियोगके द्वारा मेरा सेवन करता है, वह इन गुणोंका अतिक्रमण करके ब्रह्मप्राप्तिका पात्र हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Whoever serves Me with unwavering devotion transcends these qualities and becomes fit for union with the supreme reality.
essence: Steady devotion can carry you beyond the forces that shape ordinary life.
simple_meaning: Steady devotion to Krishna lifts a person beyond the three qualities of nature and makes that person fit for union with the supreme reality.
insight: It shifts the goal from self-improvement alone to sustained devotion as the force that transforms nature.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to fix yourself through sheer will, but the deeper shift comes when your whole heart stays aligned. That steady devotion changes what you can become.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाऽहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च । शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च ॥
translation: क्योंकि ब्रह्म, अविनाशी अमृत, शाश्वत धर्म और ऐकान्तिक सुखका आश्रय मैं ही हूँ ॥
english_translation: For I am the foundation of Brahman, of immortality, of the imperishable, of eternal dharma, and of unending bliss.
essence: All ultimate freedom rests in Krishna, not apart from him.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the support behind Brahman, immortality, the imperishable, eternal dharma, and ultimate bliss.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing separate spiritual goals to recognising their source as one.
modern_relevance: You finally reach the edge of a decision you cannot undo: leave the safe life, tell the hard truth, or stop pretending. This verse says the deepest security is not in control, but in what supports all reality.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् । छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  ऊपरकी ओर मूलवाले तथा नीचेकी ओर शाखावाले जिस संसाररूप अश्वत्थवृक्षको अव्यय कहते हैं और वेद जिसके पत्ते हैं, उस संसारवृक्षको जो जानता है, वह सम्पूर्ण वेदोंको जाननेवाला है ॥
english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: They speak of the imperishable banyan-like tree of the world, with roots above and branches below. The Vedas are its leaves. One who knows this tree knows the Vedas.
essence: Understanding the world-tree is the beginning of true understanding.
simple_meaning: The world is like an upside-down tree: its roots are above, its branches below, and the Vedas are its leaves. Truly understanding this structure means understanding the deepest teaching.
insight: It shifts attention from scattered appearances to the underlying order that shapes them.
modern_relevance: You open your phone for one answer and get pulled into ten tabs, ten opinions, ten cravings. Krishna points to the deeper pattern underneath that mental branching: learn the structure, not just the surface noise.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा     गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः । अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि     कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके ॥
translation: उस संसारवृक्षकी गुणोंसत्त्व, रज और तम के द्वारा बढ़ी हुई तथा विषयरूप कोंपलोंवाली शाखाएँ नीचे, मध्यमें और ऊपर सब जगह फैली हुई हैं ।  मनुष्यलोकमें कर्मोंके अनुसार बाँधनेवाले मूल भी नीचे और ऊपर सभी लोकोंमें व्याप्त हो रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Its branches spread below, above, and across. They are nourished by the three qualities, with sense-pleasures as their shoots. In the human world, action-bound roots extend everywhere, tying beings to results.
essence: Craving and action keep the world-tree growing in every direction.
simple_meaning: The world-tree spreads everywhere, fed by the three qualities and by desire for sense-pleasures. Its roots reach through human life through action and its consequences.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated choices to the hidden system of craving and consequence that keeps experience looping.
modern_relevance: You keep checking one message, then another, then another. Each small craving feeds the whole pattern until it feels like the pattern is running you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते    नान्तो न चादिर्न च संप्रतिष्ठा । अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूल    मसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा ॥
translation: इस संसारवृक्षका जैसा रूप देखनेमें आता है, वैसा यहाँ विचार करनेपर मिलता नहीं क्योंकि इसका न तो आदि है, न अन्त है और न स्थिति ही है ।  इसलिये इस दृढ़ मूलोंवाले संसाररूप अश्वत्थवृक्षको दृढ़ असङ्गतारूप शस्त्रके द्वारा काटकर ॥
english_translation: Its form is not perceived here as it truly is: it has no beginning, no end, and no fixed base. Cut down this deeply rooted ashvattha tree with the strong sword of detachment.
essence: What traps you has no fixed form; detachment cuts it cleanly.
simple_meaning: The world-tree cannot be grasped as a normal thing, because it has no clear beginning, end, or stable base. Cut through it with firm detachment.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to map life perfectly to severing attachment to appearances.
modern_relevance: You keep replaying the breakup, the job offer, the family argument, trying to find the exact point where everything became real. The mind wants a fixed story; this verse says the story itself must be cut loose.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्य    यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः । तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये    यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी ॥
translation: उसके बाद उस परमपदपरमात्मा की खोज करनी चाहिये जिसको प्राप्त होनेपर मनुष्य फिर लौटकर संसारमें नहीं आते और जिससे अनादिकालसे चली आनेवाली यह सृष्टि विस्तारको प्राप्त हुई है, उस आदिपुरुष परमात्माके ही मैं शरण हूँ ॥
english_translation: Therefore one should seek that supreme state, reaching which one does not return again. I take refuge in that original Person from whom this ancient creation has spread forth.
essence: The final refuge is a state where return itself stops.
simple_meaning: Beyond the changing world lies a supreme state where return stops. Krishna says that state should be sought, and he himself takes refuge in the original Person from whom creation unfolds.
insight: It shifts the mind from managing the cycle to seeking what ends the cycle entirely.
modern_relevance: You keep reopening the same message thread, the same argument, the same regret. At some point you realize the answer is not another round of fixing, but a deeper place to stand.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा    अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः । द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै    र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥
translation: जो मान और मोहसे रहित हो गये हैं, जिन्होंने आसक्तिसे होनेवाले दोषोंको जीत लिया है, जो नित्यनिरन्तर परमात्मामें ही लगे हुए हैं, जो अपनी दृष्टिसे सम्पूर्ण कामनाओंसे रहित हो गये हैं, जो सुखदुःखरूप द्वन्द्वोंसे मुक्त हो गये हैं, ऐसे ऊँची स्थितिवाले मोहरहित साधक भक्त उस अविनाशी परमपदपरमात्मा को प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Free from pride and delusion, victorious over attachment, ever rooted in the true self, desireless, and beyond the opposites of pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach that imperishable state.
essence: Freedom begins when pride, craving, and inner division fall away.
simple_meaning: Those who lose pride, cut attachment, stay rooted in the true self, and rise above pleasure and pain reach the imperishable state.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing comfort to becoming fit for freedom.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that may end a relationship, or finally leave the safe path that has become false. This verse says clarity arrives when pride, craving, and emotional whiplash stop steering.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः । यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
translation: उसपरमपद को न सूर्य, न चन्द्र और न अग्नि ही प्रकाशित कर सकती है और जिसको प्राप्त होकर जीव लौटकर संसारमें नहीं आते, वही मेरा परमधाम है ॥
english_translation: The sun, moon, and fire do not illumine that place. Having reached it, one does not return. That supreme abode is Mine.
essence: The highest home is beyond every ordinary light and beyond return.
simple_meaning: Krishna says his highest abode cannot be illuminated by ordinary light, and anyone who reaches it does not come back to the cycle of return.
insight: It shifts attention from temporary sources of guidance to the unchanging goal that ends return.
modern_relevance: You leave a hospital room after a final goodbye, and the fluorescent lights feel weak against what just changed. Some thresholds are not about more effort — they are about crossing into a life that cannot be undone.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः । मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥
translation: इस संसारमें जीव बना हुआ आत्मा मेरा ही सनातन अंश है परन्तु वह प्रकृतिमें स्थित मन और पाँचों इन्द्रियोंको आकर्षित करता है अपना मान लेता है ॥
english_translation: The embodied being in this world is my eternal part, yet it draws the mind and the five senses, which rest in nature.
essence: What is eternal gets pulled around by what changes.
simple_meaning: The living being is Krishna's eternal part, but it gets pulled by the mind and senses that belong to nature and mistakes them for itself.
insight: It shifts attention from blaming the self to seeing how nature drags awareness into identification.
modern_relevance: You know the feeling: you meant to stay calm, then one comment, one craving, one memory drags you off center. The verse explains that pull as the mind and senses taking over.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः । गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात् ॥
translation: जैसे वायु गन्धके स्थानसे गन्धको ग्रहण करके ले जाती है, ऐसे ही शरीरादिका स्वामी बना हुआ जीवात्मा भी जिस शरीरको छोड़ता है, वहाँसे मनसहित इन्द्रियोंको ग्रहण करके फिर जिस शरीरको प्राप्त होता है, उसमें चला जाता है ॥
english_translation: Just as the wind carries fragrance from its source, the embodied being carries the mind and senses into a new body.
essence: The body changes, but the carried pattern moves on.
simple_meaning: The embodied being leaves one body and enters another, carrying the mind and senses along, just as wind carries scent.
insight: It shifts attention from the body as the whole self to the carried pattern of mind and senses.
modern_relevance: You leave a job, a city, or a relationship, and the same habits travel with you. The outer setting changes fast; the inner pattern arrives first.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च । अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते ॥
translation: यह जीवात्मा मनका आश्रय लेकर श्रोत्र, नेत्र, त्वचा, रसना और घ्राण  इन पाँचों इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा विषयोंका सेवन करता है ॥
english_translation: Taking hold of the mind, the inner being experiences objects through the ears, eyes, skin, tongue, and nose.
essence: Experience passes through mind and senses; it does not define the true self.
simple_meaning: The inner being uses the mind as a base and experiences the world through the five senses.
insight: It shifts attention from sensory experience to the awareness that witnesses it.
modern_relevance: You scroll, taste, touch, and react, then call it 'me.' But the reaction is moving through your senses and mind, not defining what you are.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् । विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः ॥
translation: शरीरको छोड़कर जाते हुए या दूसरे शरीरमें स्थित हुए अथवा विषयोंको भोगते हुए भी गुणोंसे युक्त जीवात्माके स्वरूपको मूढ़ मनुष्य नहीं जानते, ज्ञानरूपी नेत्रोंवाले ज्ञानी मनुष्य ही जानते हैं ॥
english_translation: The deluded do not see the inner being departing, staying, or enjoying the world through the qualities. Those with the eye of understanding do see.
essence: What changes is seen by the wise; the true self is not what moves.
simple_meaning: Ordinary sight cannot grasp the true self moving through bodies and experiences. Only clear understanding sees what is really happening.
insight: It shifts attention from the changing body and moods to the unchanging witness behind them.
modern_relevance: You watch yourself become a different person in every room: child, employee, partner, patient, critic. The verse says the deepest part of you is not any of those shifting masks.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् । यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः ॥
translation: यत्न करनेवाले योगीलोग अपनेआपमें स्थित इस परमात्मतत्त्वका अनुभव करते हैं ।  परन्तु जिन्होंने अपना अन्तःकरण शुद्ध नहीं किया है, ऐसे अविवेकी मनुष्य यत्न करनेपर भी इस तत्त्वका अनुभव नहीं करते ॥
english_translation: The striving yogis see this supreme reality abiding in themselves. The unrefined and thoughtless, even while striving, do not see it.
essence: Seeing the supreme reality depends on inner purification, not effort alone.
simple_meaning: People who have disciplined and purified themselves can realize the supreme reality within. Effort without inner refinement is not enough.
insight: It shifts the goal from trying harder to becoming inwardly clear enough to perceive what is already present.
modern_relevance: You sit in silence after a fight, trying to understand why the same pattern keeps repeating. More information does not help until your inner state changes enough to see what was hidden.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् । यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम् ॥
translation: सूर्यमें आया हुआ जो तेज सम्पूर्ण जगत् को प्रकाशित करता है और जो तेज चन्द्रमामें है तथा जो तेज अग्निमें है, उस तेजको मेरा ही जान ॥
english_translation: The radiance in the sun, the moon, and the fire is Mine alone.
essence: Every brightness in the world points back to one source.
simple_meaning: Krishna says that the light shining in the sun, the moon, and fire belongs to him. All visible brilliance is a sign of his presence.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated objects to the living presence shining through them.
modern_relevance: You step outside after a sleepless night and the morning sun still reaches you. The warmth, the glow on water, the flame on your stove — nothing ordinary is truly separate from the source behind it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा । पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः ॥
translation: मैं ही पृथ्वीमें प्रविष्ट होकर अपनी शक्तिसे समस्त प्राणियोंको धारण करता हूँ और मैं ही रसमय चन्द्रमाके रूपमें समस्त ओषधियोंवनस्पतियों को पुष्ट करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Entering the earth, I sustain all beings with my power. Becoming the moon of life-giving essence, I nourish all plants.
essence: Life is nourished from within by the same presence that holds it together.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he enters the earth to support all living beings, and he becomes the moon that nourishes all plants and herbs.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated objects to the sustaining presence running through them all.
modern_relevance: You water a dying plant on a kitchen sill and think it is a small act. This verse says even that life-giving moisture, firmness, and growth are already held by the divine presence.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः । प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम् ॥
translation: प्राणियोंके शरीरमें रहनेवाला मैं प्राणअपानसे युक्त वैश्वानर होकर चार प्रकारके अन्नको पचाता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I become the digestive fire within living beings, joined with the outgoing and incoming breaths, and digest the four kinds of food.
essence: The divine is already working inside your body as life itself.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he lives inside every body as the force that digests food, working through the breaths that sustain life.
insight: It shifts attention from a distant divinity to the living processes already sustaining you.
modern_relevance: You sit at a table after a hard day, too tired to think, and your body still quietly does its work. Even that hidden, ordinary functioning is not outside the sacred.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो    मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च । वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो    वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् ॥
translation: मैं सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके हृदयमें स्थित हूँ ।  मेरेसे ही स्मृति, ज्ञान और अपोहन संशय आदि दोषोंका नाश होता है ।  सम्पूर्ण वेदोंके द्वारा मैं ही जाननेयोग्य हूँ ।  वेदोंके तत्त्वका निर्णय करनेवाला और वेदोंको जाननेवाला भी मैं ही हूँ ॥
english_translation: I dwell in the hearts of all beings. Memory, knowledge, and removal of doubt come from Me. I am the one known through all the Vedas, the maker of Vedanta, and the knower of the Vedas.
essence: The deepest knowing comes from the one already dwelling within every heart.
simple_meaning: Krishna says He lives in every being’s heart. Memory, understanding, and the clearing of confusion come from Him. All the Vedas point to Him, and He is their final knower.
insight: It shifts attention from scattered mental effort to a deeper source of remembrance and discernment.
modern_relevance: You sit awake after a painful conversation, replaying every sentence and doubting your own judgment. This verse says the mind’s clarity is not manufactured by strain alone; it can be received from a deeper center.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च । क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते ॥
translation: इस संसारमें क्षर नाशवान् और अक्षर अविनाशी  ये दो प्रकारके पुरुष हैं ।  सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके शरीर नाशवान् और कूटस्थ जीवात्मा अविनाशी कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: In this world, there are two kinds of beings: the perishable and the imperishable. All embodied beings are perishable; the steadfast one is called imperishable.
essence: What changes is not the whole of you.
simple_meaning: There are two kinds of existence here: what changes and what does not. Bodies pass away, but the unchanging reality within remains.
insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with the changing body to recognising the unchanging witness.
modern_relevance: You watch a loved one age in a hospital room and feel time stripping everything away. This verse reminds you that what changes is not the deepest reality of a person.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः । यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः ॥
translation: उत्तम पुरुष तो अन्य ही है, जो परमात्मा नामसे कहा गया है ।  वही अविनाशी ईश्वर तीनों लोकोंमें प्रविष्ट होकर सबका भरणपोषण करता है ॥
english_translation: The Supreme Self is beyond both the perishable and the imperishable. The imperishable ruler enters the three worlds and sustains them all.
essence: Even the imperishable witness is not the final reality.
simple_meaning: Beyond the changing world and even beyond the unchanging witness stands the highest reality, which enters all three worlds and sustains them.
insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with the imperishable witness to recognising the supreme source that sustains all experience.
modern_relevance: You can understand your thoughts, your habits, even your calm — and still miss the deepest source holding your life together. The mind can map the landscape and never notice the ground beneath it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः । अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
translation: मैं क्षरसे अतीत हूँ और अक्षरसे भी उत्तम हूँ, इसलिये लोकमें और वेदमें पुरुषोत्तम नामसे प्रसिद्ध हूँ ॥
english_translation: I am beyond the perishable and even beyond the imperishable. Therefore, I am known in the world and in the Vedas as Purushottama, the Supreme Self.
essence: The highest reality lies beyond both change and permanence.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he is beyond both the changing world and the unchanging principle behind it. That is why he is called the Supreme Self.
insight: It shifts the mind from settling for any limited identity to recognising the highest reality beyond all categories.
modern_relevance: You finally reach the thing you thought would settle everything — the title, the relationship, the achievement — and it still feels incomplete. Krishna points beyond every stopping place.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् । स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशी अर्जुन  इस प्रकार जो मोहरहित मनुष्य मुझे पुरुषोत्तम जानता है, वह सर्वज्ञ सब प्रकारसे मेरा ही भजन करता है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, the one who is free from confusion and knows Me as the Supreme Self, worships Me with all his being.
essence: Clear seeing of the Supreme Self becomes total devotion.
simple_meaning: Knowing Krishna as the Supreme Self removes confusion and leads to wholehearted devotion. Clear understanding and complete worship become one movement.
insight: It shifts devotion from blind feeling to total response grounded in clear seeing.
modern_relevance: You finally understand someone’s character after a long conflict, and your resistance drops. What was once mixed with doubt becomes wholehearted respect and trust.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयाऽनघ । एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत ॥
translation: हे निष्पाप अर्जुन  इस प्रकार यह अत्यन्त गोपनीय शास्त्र मेरे द्वारा कहा गया है ।  हे भरतवंशी अर्जुन  इसको जानकर मनुष्य ज्ञानवान् तथा प्राप्तप्राप्तव्य और कृतकृत्य हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: O sinless Arjuna, thus this most secret teaching has been spoken by Me. Knowing this, a person becomes wise and has accomplished all that must be done, O descendant of Bharata.
essence: Secret knowledge makes a person complete.
simple_meaning: Krishna says he has shared the most hidden teaching. A person who truly understands it becomes wise and feels complete, with nothing essential left undone.
insight: It shifts the mind from collecting ideas to recognising the kind of understanding that completes action and ends doubt.
modern_relevance: You finish the hardest conversation of your life and sit in silence afterward, knowing the truth has finally been said. Some understandings do not add more to you; they make you whole.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचअभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः । दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  भयका सर्वथा अभाव अन्तःकरणकी शुद्धि ज्ञानके लिये योगमें दृढ़ स्थिति सात्त्विक दान इन्द्रियोंका दमन यज्ञ स्वाध्याय कर्तव्यपालनके लिये कष्ट सहना शरीरमनवाणीकी सरलता ॥
english_translation: Fearlessness, purity of mind, steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge, generosity, self-control, sacrifice, study of the sacred texts, austerity, and straightforwardness.
essence: Right action starts with disciplined character.
simple_meaning: A divine life begins with fearlessness, inner purity, self-control, generosity, sacrifice, study, disciplined effort, and honesty.
insight: It shifts attention from winning approval to building the qualities that make right action possible.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, walk into the meeting, or tell the truth that may change everything. Before the outcome, the verse asks for steadiness, honesty, and self-mastery.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् । दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥
translation: अहिंसा, सत्यभाषण क्रोध न करना संसारकी कामनाका त्याग अन्तःकरणमें रागद्वेषजनित हलचलका न होना चुगली न करना प्राणियोंपर दया करना सांसारिक विषयोंमें न ललचाना अन्तःकरणकी कोमलता अकर्तव्य करनेमें लज्जा चपलताका अभाव ॥
english_translation: Nonviolence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, inner calm, absence of slander, compassion for all beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, and absence of restlessness.
essence: A noble character is proven by how gently it reacts.
simple_meaning: A divine life is built from nonviolence, honesty, calm, compassion, restraint, and modest conduct.
insight: It trains the mind to replace impulse with restraint, and reaction with humane conduct.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the angry message, repeat the gossip, or take the easy shortcut. This verse asks for a different reflex: soften, tell the truth, and stop the spiral.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता । भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत ॥
translation: तेज प्रभाव, क्षमा, धैर्य, शरीरकी शुद्धि, वैरभावका न रहना और मानको न चाहना, हे भरतवंशी अर्जुन  ये सभी दैवी सम्पदाको प्राप्त हुए मनुष्यके लक्षण हैं ॥
english_translation: Splendor, forgiveness, steadiness, purity, absence of hostility, and lack of pride belong to the one born with divine qualities, O Bharata.
essence: True strength looks like forgiveness, steadiness, and no need to dominate.
simple_meaning: A person with noble qualities shows strength, forgiveness, steadiness, purity, no hostility, and no pride.
insight: It shifts attention from outer success to the inner traits that reveal a disciplined character.
modern_relevance: A tense family dinner turns sharp, and everyone is waiting for you to strike back. This verse says real strength can stay clean, calm, and uninflated under pressure.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च । अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम् ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन  दम्भ करना, घमण्ड करना, अभिमान करना, क्रोध करना, कठोरता रखना और अविवेकका होना भी  ये सभी आसुरीसम्पदाको प्राप्त हुए मनुष्यके लक्षण हैं ॥
english_translation: O son of Pritha, hypocrisy, arrogance, self-importance, anger, harshness, and ignorance are the marks of one born with demonic qualities.
essence: False pride and cruelty reveal a nature already turned away from wisdom.
simple_meaning: False display, pride, self-importance, anger, harsh speech, and ignorance are signs of a destructive nature.
insight: It teaches you to spot character by recurring reactions, not by polished appearances.
modern_relevance: In a tense family argument, someone smiles politely while cutting you down, then explodes when challenged. The verse names that mix of pride, cruelty, and blindness for what it is.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता । मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव ॥
translation: दैवीसम्पत्ति मुक्तिके लिये और आसुरीसम्पत्ति बन्धनके लिये है ।  हे पाण्डव तुम दैवीसम्पत्तिको प्राप्त हुए हो, इसलिये तुम्हें शोक चिन्ता नहीं करना चाहिये ॥
english_translation: The divine nature leads to freedom; the demonic nature leads to bondage. Do not grieve, Pandava. You are born with the divine nature.
essence: Freedom grows from one kind of character; bondage grows from another.
simple_meaning: Qualities that uplift a person lead to freedom, while qualities rooted in ego create bondage. Krishna tells Arjuna not to despair, because Arjuna already has the qualities that lead upward.
insight: It shifts attention from self-doubt to the qualities you are cultivating, so you can align with what frees rather than what binds.
modern_relevance: You catch yourself spiralling after a harsh conversation, wondering whether you are becoming the kind of person you fear. This verse says to stop and remember what you are already leaning toward.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन् दैव आसुर एव च । दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे श्रृणु ॥
translation: इस लोकमें दो तरहके प्राणियोंकी सृष्टि है  दैवी और आसुरी ।  दैवीका तो मैंने विस्तारसे वर्णन कर दिया, अब हे पार्थ  तुम मेरेसे आसुरीका विस्तार सुनो ॥
english_translation: In this world there are two kinds of beings: the divine and the shadowed. I have already described the divine in detail; now listen to the shadowed, Arjuna.
essence: Human life divides by inner orientation, not by appearance.
simple_meaning: Krishna says there are two broad kinds of human nature: one shaped by clarity and virtue, the other by ego and confusion. He has already explained the first and now turns to the second.
insight: It shifts attention from judging isolated actions to seeing the underlying nature behind them.
modern_relevance: You watch a group chat turn cruel in minutes, and one voice keeps escalating everything. This verse helps you name the pattern: not every reaction comes from the same kind of character.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः । न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते ॥
translation: आसुरी प्रकृतिवाले मनुष्य प्रवृत्ति और निवृत्तिको नहीं जानते और उनमें न बाह्यशुद्धि, न श्रेष्ठ आचरण तथा न सत्यपालन ही होता है ॥
english_translation: People of a shadowed nature do not know what should be pursued and what should be withdrawn from. In them, there is no purity, no noble conduct, and no truthfulness.
essence: Without discernment, conduct collapses and truth disappears.
simple_meaning: A shadowed nature cannot tell right action from wrong withdrawal. It also lacks purity, good conduct, and honesty.
insight: It trains you to measure character by discernment and basic self-restraint, not by charm or ambition.
modern_relevance: A group chat turns ugly, and someone keeps feeding it with half-truths, sloppy boundaries, and impulsive replies. The problem is not one mistake — it is a pattern of inner disorder.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम् । अपरस्परसम्भूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम् ॥
translation: वे कहा करते हैं कि संसार असत्य, अप्रतिष्ठित और बिना ईश्वरके अपनेआप केवल स्त्रीपुरुषके संयोगसे पैदा हुआ है ।  इसलिये काम ही इसका कारण है, और कोई कारण नहीं है ॥
english_translation: They say the world is unreal, without foundation, and without a ruling order, born only from the union of male and female. They say desire alone is its cause, and nothing else.
essence: Cynical explanations of life can become a permission slip for harmful action.
simple_meaning: Some people deny any higher order in the world. They reduce existence to chance, physical union, and desire alone.
insight: It shifts the mind from cynical reduction to seeing that beliefs about reality shape conduct.
modern_relevance: A friend shrugs at betrayal and says, “People are just wired this way.” That sentence can sound clever, but it can also erase responsibility and flatten the whole moral world.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः । प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः ॥
translation: उपर्युक्त नास्तिक दृष्टिका आश्रय लेनेवाले जो मनुष्य अपने नित्य स्वरूपको नहीं मानते, जिनकी बुद्धि तुच्छ है, जो उग्रकर्मा और संसारके शत्रु हैं, उन मनुष्योंकी सामर्थ्यका उपयोग जगत्का नाश करनेके लिये ही होता है ॥
english_translation: Holding this view, deluded people with ruined discernment and fierce actions arise only to destroy the world.
essence: False vision turns strength into destruction.
simple_meaning: People who deny their true nature and cling to a false view become small-minded and destructive. Their energy turns toward harming the world instead of serving it.
insight: It shifts attention from judging bad behavior alone to seeing the false belief that generates it.
modern_relevance: A person who keeps feeding cynicism, contempt, and denial of responsibility may start with words, then wreck a family, a team, or a community without noticing the damage.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः । मोहाद्गृहीत्वासद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः ॥
translation: कभी पूरी न होनेवाली कामनाओंका आश्रय लेकर दम्भ, अभिमान और मदमें चूर रहनेवाले तथा अपवित्र व्रत धारण करनेवाले मनुष्य मोहके कारण दुराग्रहोंको धारण करके संसारमें विचरते रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Taking refuge in desires that can never be filled, filled with hypocrisy, pride, and intoxication, they wander under delusion, holding onto impure vows and false beliefs.
essence: Endless wanting turns the mind into a home for delusion.
simple_meaning: People trapped by endless wanting become arrogant, deluded, and stubborn. Their lives keep moving, but they keep holding on to false ideas and impure aims.
insight: It shifts attention from external success to the hidden habits that deform judgment.
modern_relevance: You keep refreshing the message thread, hoping the next reply will settle you. Instead, the wanting grows, and with it the need to look right, feel superior, and cling harder.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः । कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्िचताः ॥
translation: वे मृत्युपर्यन्त रहनेवाली अपार चिन्ताओंका आश्रय लेनेवाले, पदार्थोंका संग्रह और उनका भोग करनेमें ही लगे रहनेवाले और जो कुछ है, वह इतना ही है  ऐसा निश्चय करनेवाले होते हैं ॥
english_translation: They take refuge in endless worries that last until death, live only for acquiring and enjoying things, and decide that this is all there is.
essence: Endless wanting turns life into a tunnel with no horizon.
simple_meaning: People trapped in desire live with endless worry, chase possessions and pleasure, and conclude that material life is all that exists.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing accumulation to noticing how desire manufactures anxiety.
modern_relevance: You scroll past midnight, checking prices, messages, and comparisons, convinced you still need one more thing. The mind keeps asking for more, and never feels full.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः । ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान् ॥
translation: वे आशाकी सैकड़ों फाँसियोंसे बँधे हुए मनुष्य कामक्रोधके परायण होकर पदार्थोंका भोग करनेके लिये अन्यायपूर्वक धनसंचय करनेकी चेष्टा करते रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Bound by hundreds of cords of hope, driven by desire and anger, they strive to gather wealth unjustly for the enjoyment of desires.
essence: Desire and anger turn ambition into injustice.
simple_meaning: Endless hopes trap people. Desire and anger drive them to gather wealth by unfair means just to feed more wanting.
insight: It shifts attention from outward success to the inner forces that corrupt it.
modern_relevance: A person cuts corners, hides numbers, and calls it ambition. The hunger for more has already turned into a cage.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् । इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम् ॥
translation: इतनी वस्तुएँ तो हमने आज प्राप्त कर लीं और अब इस मनोरथको प्राप्त पूरा कर लेंगे । ,इतना धन तो हमारे पास है ही, इतना धन फिर हो जायगा ॥
english_translation: This much I have gained today; I will get this desire fulfilled. This wealth is mine now, and more will be mine again.
essence: Possession feeds appetite when the mind mistakes gain for completion.
simple_meaning: A deluded person keeps thinking, “I have gained this, I will get more, and this wealth will keep increasing.”
insight: It reveals how greed multiplies itself by turning every gain into proof that more is owed.
modern_relevance: You check your account after a bonus and immediately start planning the next purchase, the next upgrade, the next win. The mind never says, enough.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि । ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी ॥
translation: वह शत्रु तो हमारे द्वारा मारा गया और उन दूसरे शत्रुओंको भी हम मार डालेंगे ।  हम सर्वसमर्थ हैं ।  हमारे पास भोगसामग्री बहुत है ।  हम सिद्ध हैं ।  हम बड़े बलवान् और सुखी हैं ॥
english_translation: That enemy has been slain by me, and I will slay the others too. I am the lord, I enjoy, I am accomplished, powerful, and happy.
essence: Ego turns achievement into delusion and mistakes possession for mastery.
simple_meaning: Pride speaks through the arrogant mind: it claims victory, power, pleasure, success, and happiness as its own.
insight: It teaches you to notice how success can harden into delusion and make a person confuse power with truth.
modern_relevance: After one successful deal, someone starts talking like nothing can stop them. The next decision gets made from a swollen ego, not clear seeing.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया । यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥
translation: हम धनवान् हैं, बहुतसे मनुष्य हमारे पास हैं, हमारे समान और कौन है हम खूब यज्ञ करेंगे, दान देंगे और मौज करेंगे  इस तरह वे अज्ञानसे मोहित रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: We are rich, surrounded by many people. Who is equal to us? We will sacrifice, give, and enjoy. Deluded by ignorance, they think this way.
essence: Pride turns abundance into delusion and makes more wanting feel justified.
simple_meaning: Arrogance makes a person feel rich, superior, and endlessly secure. That delusion then turns even sacrifice and giving into excuses for more enjoyment.
insight: It shifts attention from outward success to the hidden arrogance driving it.
modern_relevance: You scroll past your own wins, then start counting what still proves you matter. The urge to announce, compare, and consume can come dressed as confidence.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः । प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ ॥
translation: कामनाओंके कारण तरहतरहसे भ्रमित चित्तवाले, मोहजालमें अच्छी तरहसे फँसे हुए तथा पदार्थों और भोगोंमें अत्यन्त आसक्त रहनेवाले मनुष्य भयङ्कर नरकोंमें गिरते हैं ॥
english_translation: Deluded by many desires, trapped in the net of confusion, and deeply attached to pleasures, people fall into a lower realm of misery.
essence: Desire scatters the mind, and confusion turns that scattering into a fall.
simple_meaning: A mind pulled in many directions by desire gets caught in confusion and falls into misery through attachment to pleasure.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing pleasure to noticing how desire fragments judgment.
modern_relevance: You open your phone for one thing and end up half-lost in ten cravings, three tabs, and a bad mood. The mind does not stay neutral for long when it keeps feeding wanting.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः । यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥
translation: अपनेको सबसे अधिक पूज्य माननेवाले, अकड़ रखनेवाले तथा धन और मानके मदमें चूर रहनेवाले वे मनुष्य दम्भसे अविधिपूर्वक नाममात्रके यज्ञोंसे यजन करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Self-important, stubborn, drunk on wealth and praise, they perform ritual in name only, with pretence and without proper method.
essence: Pride can hollow out sacred action until only appearance remains.
simple_meaning: People swollen with pride, wealth, and status may still perform rituals, but only as show. The outer act remains, while the inner sincerity and right method are missing.
insight: It teaches you to examine motive, not just performance, and to let practice become honest rather than decorative.
modern_relevance: You post the apology, attend the ceremony, and say the right words — but your chest is tight with image-management. Krishna names the gap between appearance and sincerity.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः । मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः ॥
translation: वे अहङ्कार, हठ, घमण्ड, कामना और क्रोधका आश्रय लेनेवाले मनुष्य अपने और दूसरोंके शरीरमें रहनेवाले मुझ अन्तर्यामीके साथ द्वेष करते हैं तथा मेरे और दूसरोंके गुणोंमें दोषदृष्टि रखते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who take refuge in ego, force, arrogance, desire, and anger hate Me, who dwell in their own bodies and in the bodies of others, and they find fault with My qualities.
essence: Ego makes you fight the divine presence you carry yourself.
simple_meaning: People ruled by ego, force, arrogance, desire, and anger turn against the divine presence within themselves and others. They also habitually look for faults in what is good.
insight: It shifts attention from outer conflict to the inner attitudes that create contempt, envy, and fault-finding.
modern_relevance: A group chat turns cruel, and every message assumes bad intent. The same inner heat that makes you snap at yourself also makes you misread everyone else.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु नराधमान् । क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु ॥
translation: उन द्वेष करनेवाले, क्रूर स्वभाववाले और संसारमें महान् नीच, अपवित्र मनुष्योंको मैं बारबार आसुरी योनियोंमें गिराता ही रहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I cast those hateful, cruel, and vile people again and again into demonic births.
essence: Repeated hatred drives a person into worse and worse forms of existence.
simple_meaning: People who hate, act cruelly, and live in impurity fall into lower births again and again.
insight: It shifts the mind from blaming fate to seeing how repeated cruelty hardens into a downward pattern.
modern_relevance: A person keeps choosing contempt, manipulation, and violence, then wonders why life feels smaller each year. The habits do not stay private; they shape the kind of future being built.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: असुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि । मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम् ॥
translation: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  वे मूढ मनुष्य मेरेको प्राप्त न करके ही जन्मजन्मान्तरमें आसुरी योनिको प्राप्त होते हैं, फिर उससे भी अधिक अधम गतिमें अर्थात् भयङ्कर नरकोंमें चले जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those deluded beings, born again and again into shadowed births, never reach me and sink into a lower state.
essence: Repeated delusion keeps pulling a person farther from the divine.
simple_meaning: People trapped in delusion keep taking shadowed births again and again. Because they never turn toward the divine, they sink into still lower states.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating repeated bad choices as isolated mistakes to seeing them as a reinforcing descent.
modern_relevance: You keep making the same self-sabotaging choice after the breakup, after the apology, after the warning. The pattern does not feel dramatic — until you notice it has become your life.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः । कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
translation: काम, क्रोध और लोभ  ये तीन प्रकारके नरकके दरवाजे जीवात्माका पतन करनेवाले हैं, इसलिये इन तीनोंका त्याग कर देना चाहिये ॥
