english_translation: Desire, anger, and greed are the three gates of ruin. Abandon these three.
essence: Three inner forces open the way to ruin; dropping them protects the self.
simple_meaning: Desire, anger, and greed are the three forces that drag a person downward. Krishna says they must be given up.
insight: It shifts the mind from impulse-driven reaction to deliberate restraint.
modern_relevance: You open your phone to send one sharp message, then another, then another. The urge feels justified, but it is really pulling you into a smaller version of yourself. Stop there.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः । आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
translation: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  इन नरकके तीनों दरवाजोंसे रहित हुआ जो मनुष्य अपने कल्याणका आचरण करता है, वह परमगतिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Freed from these three gates of darkness, a person acts for their own good and reaches the highest state.
essence: Freedom from the three dark impulses opens the way to your highest good.
simple_meaning: When a person is free from desire, anger, and greed, they live in a way that supports their highest good and reach the highest state.
insight: It shifts attention from impulse to self-protective action, showing that restraint opens the way to better choices.
modern_relevance: You pause before sending the cruel text, buying the thing you do not need, or lashing out in pride. That pause can save your character.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः । न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम् ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य शास्त्रविधिको छोड़कर अपनी इच्छासे मनमाना आचरण करता है, वह न सिद्धिअन्तःकरणकी शुद्धि को, न सुखको और न परमगतिको ही प्राप्त होता है ॥
english_translation: Whoever sets aside scripture and acts on desire alone does not attain perfection, happiness, or the highest state.
essence: Impulse cannot deliver what it promises.
simple_meaning: Acting only on impulse, while ignoring wise guidance, blocks real fulfilment, lasting happiness, and the highest good.
insight: It shifts action from craving-led reaction to disciplined choice shaped by what is truly right.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the text, quit the job, or spend the money because the urge is loud. The verse says impulse can feel decisive while quietly cutting off what you actually want most.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ । ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि ॥
translation: अतः तेरे लिये कर्तव्यअकर्तव्यकी व्यवस्थामें शास्त्र ही प्रमाण है  ऐसा जानकर तू इस लोकमें शास्त्रविधिसे नियत कर्तव्य कर्म करनेयोग्य है ॥
english_translation: Therefore, scripture is your authority for deciding what should be done and what should not be done. Knowing the duties laid out in scripture, you should act here in the world.
essence: Impulse cannot judge action; a higher standard must.
simple_meaning: Right and wrong action should be judged by scripture, not impulse. Knowing that guidance, a person should do the duty set before them.
insight: It shifts decision-making from personal craving to a tested standard of right action.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that could end a relationship, and your feelings are shouting louder than your conscience. Krishna says: do not let impulse be the judge.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः । तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे कृष्ण  जो मनुष्य शास्त्रविधिका त्याग करके श्रद्धापूर्वक देवता आदिका पूजन करते हैं, उनकी निष्ठा फिर कौनसी है सात्त्विकी है अथवा राजसीतामसी ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, what is the standing of those who worship with faith while setting aside the rules of scripture? Is it sattvic, rajasic, or tamasic?
essence: Faith alone does not reveal its quality; the motive beneath it does.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks what kind of faith people have when they worship without following scripture. He wants to know whether their faith is pure, restless, or confused.
insight: It shifts attention from outward sincerity to the inner quality behind belief and practice.
modern_relevance: You watch someone follow a spiritual trend with total sincerity, but something feels off. The question is not whether they mean well — it is what kind of force is shaping their devotion.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचत्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा । सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां श्रृणु ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  मनुष्योंकी वह स्वभावसे उत्पन्न हुई श्रद्धा सात्त्विकी तथा राजसी और तामसी  ऐसे तीन तरहकी ही होती है, उसको तुम मेरेसे सुनो ॥
english_translation: The faith of embodied beings is born of their nature. It is of three kinds: sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic. Listen to this.
essence: Faith takes the shape of the nature beneath it.
simple_meaning: Faith is not all the same. It comes from a person's nature and appears in three forms: clear, restless, or dull.
insight: It shifts attention from judging beliefs alone to noticing the inner quality that produces them.
modern_relevance: You watch someone defend a choice they barely understand, then realise the energy behind it matters as much as the belief itself. The shape of faith reveals the state underneath.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत । श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥
translation: हे भारत  सभी मनुष्योंकी श्रद्धा अन्तःकरणके अनुरूप होती है ।  यह मनुष्य श्रद्धामय है ।  इसलिये जो जैसी श्रद्धावाला है, वही उसका स्वरूप है अर्थात् वही उसकी निष्ठा  स्थिति है ॥
english_translation: O Bharata, each person's trust matches their inner nature. A person is made of trust; whatever trust he holds, that is what he becomes.
essence: Trust is not just held; it becomes the person.
simple_meaning: A person's deepest trust reflects their inner makeup, and that trust shapes who they become.
insight: It shifts attention from surface belief to the deeper loyalties that form character and action.
modern_relevance: You keep returning to the same app, the same voice, the same habit, the same fear. What you trust most quietly starts to define you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः । प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः ॥
translation: सात्त्विक मनुष्य देवताओंका पूजन करते हैं, राजस मनुष्य यक्षों और राक्षसोंका और दूसरे जो तामस मनुष्य हैं, वे प्रेतों और भूतगणोंका पूजन करते हैं ॥
english_translation: The sattvic worship radiant beings; the rajasic worship yakshas and rakshasas; the tamasic worship spirits and hosts of the dead.
essence: Faith reveals itself in what each person chooses to revere.
simple_meaning: People worship different kinds of beings according to the quality that dominates their nature. Their faith shapes the form their devotion takes.
insight: It shifts attention from outer worship to the quality of mind behind worship.
modern_relevance: A person who chases charisma, power, or fear usually reveals something about their own inner state. What you keep admiring is often a mirror of what rules you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः । दम्भाहङ्कारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य शास्त्रविधिसे रहित घोर तप करते हैं जो दम्भ और अहङ्कारसे अच्छी तरह युक्त हैं जो भोगपदार्थ, आसक्ति और हठसे युक्त हैं जो शरीरमें स्थित पाँच भूतोंको अर्थात् पाञ्चभौतिक शरीरको तथा अन्तःकरणमें स्थित मुझ परमात्माको भी कृश करनेवाले हैं उन अज्ञानियोंको तू आसुर निश्चयवाले आसुरी सम्पदावाले समझ ॥
english_translation: People who perform harsh austerities without scriptural guidance, driven by vanity, ego, desire, attachment, and stubbornness, are not purified by them.
essence: Harsh effort without right guidance can deepen ego instead of cleansing it.
simple_meaning: Severe self-punishment without right guidance, mixed with pride and craving, does not make a person better.
insight: It warns you to examine motive before praising endurance. A hard practice can still strengthen the wrong parts of you.
modern_relevance: Someone bragging about a brutal detox, sleep deprivation, or punishing routine may look committed, but the hidden motive is still control and self-display.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कर्षयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः । मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान् ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य शास्त्रविधिसे रहित घोर तप करते हैं जो दम्भ और अहङ्कारसे अच्छी तरह युक्त हैं जो भोगपदार्थ, आसक्ति और हठसे युक्त हैं जो शरीरमें स्थित पाँच भूतोंको अर्थात् पाञ्चभौतिक शरीरको तथा अन्तःकरणमें स्थित मुझ परमात्माको भी कृश करनेवाले हैं उन अज्ञानियोंको तू आसुर निश्चयवाले आसुरी सम्पदावाले समझ ॥
english_translation: Those who are ignorant and perform terrible austerities without scriptural guidance, wasting away the body’s elements and Me dwelling within the body, should be known as having demonic resolve.
essence: Harshness is not holiness when it destroys the body and ignores what lives within.
simple_meaning: Blind, self-willed austerity can damage the body and ignore the divine presence within it. Such harsh practice is not purity; it comes from confused, destructive resolve.
insight: It shifts discipline from self-punishment to wise restraint that protects both body and intention.
modern_relevance: Someone brags about fasting through exhaustion, sleeping three hours, and calling it commitment. The body is breaking, the mind is proud, and the practice is feeding ego instead of clarity.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः । यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं श्रृणु ॥
translation: आहार भी सबको तीन प्रकारका प्रिय होता है और वैसे ही यज्ञ, दान और तप भी तीन प्रकारके होते हैं अर्थात् शास्त्रीय कर्मोंमें भी तीन प्रकारकी रुचि होती है, तू उनके इस भेदको सुन ॥
english_translation: Food, sacrifice, charity, and austerity are each of three kinds. Listen to these distinctions.
essence: Even sacred actions differ; their inner quality decides their worth.
simple_meaning: Food, sacrifice, charity, and austerity all come in three kinds. Krishna asks Arjuna to listen to the differences.
insight: It shifts attention from the outer form of an act to the quality of consciousness behind it.
modern_relevance: You choose a meal, make a donation, or push through a hard practice and assume the act itself is enough. Krishna says the inner quality behind it matters just as much.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः । रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥
translation: आयु, सत्त्वगुण, बल, आरोग्य, सुख और प्रसन्नता बढ़ानेवाले, स्थिर रहनेवाले, हृदयको शक्ति देनेवाले, रसयुक्त तथा चिकने  ऐसे आहार अर्थात् भोजन करनेके पदार्थ सात्त्विक मनुष्यको प्रिय होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Foods that increase life, purity, strength, health, happiness, and cheerfulness, and are tasty, smooth, firm, and pleasing, are dear to the sattvic person.
essence: Wholesome food quietly builds the conditions for a steadier life.
simple_meaning: Pure, nourishing food supports long life, strength, health, calmness, and happiness. A clear-minded person naturally prefers what is wholesome and steadying.
insight: It shifts attention from taste alone to the effect food has on energy, mood, and clarity.
modern_relevance: You grab whatever is quick after a draining day, then wonder why your body feels heavy and your mood frays. The choice on your plate quietly shapes your steadiness.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कट्वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः । आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः ॥
translation: अति कड़वे, अति खट्टे, अति नमकीन, अति गरम, अति तीखे, अति रूखे और अति दाहकारक आहार अर्थात् भोजनके पदार्थ राजस मनुष्यको प्रिय होते हैं, जो कि दुःख, शोक और रोगोंको देनेवाले हैं ॥
english_translation: Bitter, sour, salty, overly hot, pungent, dry, and burning foods are dear to the passionate person. They bring pain, grief, and illness.
essence: What excites the senses can quietly produce suffering.
simple_meaning: Foods that are too sharp, hot, dry, or harsh attract a restless, passionate nature, but they lead to pain, grief, and illness.
insight: It shifts attention from taste alone to the mental state that chooses the food and the result it creates.
modern_relevance: You reach for another extra-spicy, late-night meal because your nerves want a hit, not balance. The body feels it later — in sleep, mood, and energy.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत् । उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम् ॥
translation: जो भोजन अधपका, रसरहित, दुर्गन्धित, बासी और उच्छिष्ट है तथा जो महान् अपवित्र भी है, वह तामस मनुष्यको प्रिय होता है ॥
english_translation: Food that is half-cooked, tasteless, foul-smelling, stale, leftover, and impure is dear to people ruled by tamas.
essence: What you repeatedly choose to consume reveals the heaviness within.
simple_meaning: People dominated by tamas are drawn to food that is stale, tasteless, foul-smelling, leftover, or impure.
insight: It shifts attention from taste alone to the quality of what you repeatedly accept.
modern_relevance: You open the fridge late at night and reach for whatever is dead easiest, not what actually helps you. The body keeps a record of what the mind has been feeding it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते । यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः ॥
translation: यज्ञ करना कर्तव्य है  इस तरह मनको समाधान करके फलेच्छारहित मनुष्योंद्वारा जो शास्त्रविधिसे नियत यज्ञ किया जाता है, वह सात्त्विक है ॥
english_translation: A sacrifice performed according to scriptural rule by people without desire for reward, with the mind settled on “it must be done,” is sattvic.
essence: Right action becomes pure when reward stops being the reason.
simple_meaning: A sacrifice is pure when it is done because it should be done, not for reward.
insight: It shifts action from reward-seeking to duty-centered offering.
modern_relevance: You send the apology text even though no one may soften. You do it because it is the right thing, not because you can control the reply.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् । इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् ॥
translation: परन्तु हे भरतश्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  जो यज्ञ फलकी इच्छाको लेकर अथवा दम्भदिखावटीपन के लिये भी किया जाता है, उसको तुम राजस समझो ॥
english_translation: But, best of the Bharatas, know that sacrifice to be rajasic when it is performed for reward or for show.
essence: An offering for reward or applause loses its purity.
simple_meaning: A sacrifice done for personal gain or to look impressive is not pure. Its motive makes it rajasic, driven by restlessness and ego.
insight: It shifts attention from the outer act to the motive behind it.
modern_relevance: You post the donation receipt, the volunteer photo, the perfect caption. The act may help others, but part of you is still feeding on recognition.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् । श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते ॥
translation: शास्त्रविधिसे हीन, अन्नदानसे रहित, बिना मन्त्रोंके, बिना दक्षिणाके और बिना श्रद्धाके किये जानेवाले यज्ञको तामस यज्ञ कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: They call a sacrifice dark when it lacks scriptural rule, food offering, mantra, fee, and trust.
essence: Ritual without trust becomes empty and heavy.
simple_meaning: A sacrifice done without proper guidance, offering, mantra, giving, or trust is called dark and lifeless.
insight: It shifts the mind from outward performance to inward sincerity.
modern_relevance: You light a candle, say the words, and still feel nothing because your attention never arrived. A practice done on autopilot may look complete, yet it carries no real force.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् । ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते ॥
translation: देवता, ब्राह्मण, गुरुजन और जीवन्मुक्त महापुरुषका पूजन करना, शुद्धि रखना, सरलता, ब्रह्मचर्यका पालन करना और हिंसा न करना  यह शरीरसम्बन्धी तप कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: Worship of the radiant beings, the wise, the teacher, and the enlightened; purity, simplicity, celibacy, and non-violence — these are called bodily austerity.
essence: The body itself can become a disciplined offering.
simple_meaning: True bodily discipline includes honoring wise teachers, staying clean, living simply, practicing self-restraint, and avoiding harm.
insight: It shifts discipline from private intention to visible conduct: what you do with the body reveals the quality of your practice.
modern_relevance: You scroll past a cruel comment, then feel the urge to add one more. The verse asks for a different kind of strength: keep your body, habits, and actions clean enough to deserve your own respect.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
translation: उद्वेग न करनेवाला, सत्य, प्रिय, हितकारक भाषण तथा स्वाध्याय और अभ्यास करना  यह वाणीसम्बन्धी तप कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: Speech that does not agitate, is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial, together with study and practice, is called austerity of speech.
essence: Speech becomes discipline when it tells the truth without creating harm.
simple_meaning: Speech becomes a disciplined practice when it is calm, truthful, kind, helpful, and supported by study.
insight: It shifts speech from impulse to disciplined care, so words become a practice of restraint and usefulness.
modern_relevance: You are about to send a text that could inflame everything, or calm it. This verse asks whether your words reduce heat, carry truth, and actually help before you hit send.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः । भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते ॥
translation: मनकी प्रसन्नता, सौम्य भाव, मननशीलता, मनका निग्रह और भावोंकी शुद्धि  इस तरह यह मनसम्बन्धी तप कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-control, and purity of feeling are called mental austerity.
essence: A trained mind is its own austerity.
simple_meaning: Mental discipline means keeping the mind calm, gentle, quiet, controlled, and clean in its feelings.
insight: It shifts discipline from outward performance to inward regulation of thought and feeling.
modern_relevance: You close your laptop after a tense message and feel the urge to replay every line. The harder practice is not sending another reply — it is keeping the mind soft, quiet, and clean.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्ित्रविधं नरैः । अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते ॥
translation: परम श्रद्धासे युक्त फलेच्छारहित मनुष्योंके द्वारा तीन प्रकारशरीर, वाणी और मन का तप किया जाता है, उसको सात्त्विक कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: That threefold discipline of body, speech, and mind, performed with supreme trust and without craving results, is called sattvic.
essence: True discipline is clean only when reward is no longer the motive.
simple_meaning: Body, speech, and mind are called pure discipline when practiced with trust and without wanting any reward.
insight: It shifts discipline from performance for approval to steady practice rooted in trust.
modern_relevance: You keep the promise to train at dawn, then no one sees the effort and the applause never comes. The practice still counts when you were never negotiating for praise.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् । क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् ॥
translation: जो तप सत्कार, मान और पूजाके लिये तथा दिखानेके भावसे किया जाता है, वह इस लोकमें अनिश्चित और नाशवान् फल देनेवाला तप राजस कहा गया है ॥
english_translation: Austerity done for honor, praise, and worship, or with a show of display, is said to be rajasic here. It gives unstable, temporary results.
essence: Practice for applause collapses into instability.
simple_meaning: Practice done to impress others, gain respect, or look holy is unstable and short-lived. It may bring attention, but not lasting value.
insight: It shifts action away from image-making and back toward sincerity.
modern_relevance: You post the disciplined routine, the perfect meal, the early-morning run — and wait for the praise. The moment approval becomes the fuel, the practice starts to hollow out.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः । परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
translation: जो तप मूढ़तापूर्वक हठसे अपनेको पीड़ा देकर अथवा दूसरोंको कष्ट देनेके लिये किया जाता है, वह तप तामस कहा गया है ॥
english_translation: Austerity done with foolish stubbornness, by torturing oneself or harming others, is called tamasic.
essence: Pain imposed in ignorance only deepens confusion.
simple_meaning: Austerity becomes dark and mistaken when it is done through foolish self-torture or to hurt other people.
insight: It separates genuine discipline from self-punishment and aggression.
modern_relevance: You force yourself through a brutal routine because you think suffering proves commitment. Or you use harshness to control someone else. Krishna calls that confusion, not strength.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे । देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥
translation: दान देना कर्तव्य है  ऐसे भावसे जो दान देश, काल और पात्रके प्राप्त होनेपर अनुपकारीको दिया जाता है, वह दान सात्त्विक कहा गया है ॥
english_translation: A gift given with the feeling that giving is a duty, offered to a worthy person at the right place and time, is called sattvic.
essence: Giving becomes pure when nothing is being bought in return.
simple_meaning: A gift is pure when it is given as a duty, to the right person, at the right time and place, without expecting anything back.
insight: It shifts giving from exchange to offering, so the mind stops counting what comes back.
modern_relevance: You send money to a friend who will never repay you, or help quietly without posting it anywhere. The act feels clean because it was never a transaction.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः । दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
translation: किन्तु जो दान प्रत्युपकारके लिये अथवा फलप्राप्तिका उद्देश्य बनाकर फिर क्लेशपूर्वक दिया जाता है, वह दान राजस कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: But charity given in return, or for a desired result, and given grudgingly, is said to be rajasic.
essence: A gift becomes lesser the moment it starts asking for something back.
simple_meaning: A gift loses its purity when you give it to get something back or to force a result, especially if you give it unwillingly.
insight: It teaches you to notice hidden bargaining inside generosity and strip it out.
modern_relevance: You send the money, then keep checking whether they thanked you properly. The gift was real, but part of you was still negotiating.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते । असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
translation: जो दान बिना सत्कारके तथा अवज्ञापूर्वक अयोग्य देश और कालमें कुपात्रको दिया जाता है, वह दान तामस कहा गया है ॥
english_translation: Charity given at the wrong place and time, to an unworthy recipient, without respect and with contempt, is called tamasic.
essence: A gift can become degrading when respect is missing.
simple_meaning: A gift given at the wrong time and place, to the wrong person, without respect, is a low form of giving.
insight: It shifts attention from the outer act of giving to the quality of respect behind it.
modern_relevance: You hand someone cash while looking at your phone, hoping they go away. The act may look generous, but the attitude turns it cold.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः । ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा ॥
translation: ऊँ, तत् और सत्  इन तीनों नामोंसे जिस परमात्माका निर्देश किया गया है, उसी परमात्माने सृष्टिके आदिमें वेदों, ब्राह्मणों और यज्ञोंकी रचना की है ॥
english_translation: Om, Tat, and Sat are the three names by which the supreme reality is known. By that, the Vedas, the priests, and the sacrifices were established in the beginning.
essence: Sacred action matters because it points beyond itself to what is real.
simple_meaning: The sacred syllables Om, Tat, and Sat point to the supreme reality. They also mark the origin of the Vedas, priests, and sacrifices.
insight: It shifts practice from ritual as habit to ritual as alignment with the real.
modern_relevance: Before a memorial, a wedding, or a vow, people often reach for words that feel bigger than personal opinion. This verse reminds you that some words are meant to align action with what is most real, not just sound holy.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः । प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम् ॥
translation: इसलिये वैदिक सिद्धान्तोंको माननेवाले पुरुषोंकी शास्त्रविधिसे नियत यज्ञ, दान और तपरूप क्रियाएँ सदा ऊँ इस परमात्माके नामका उच्चारण करके ही आरम्भ होती हैं ॥
english_translation: Therefore, the ritual acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity prescribed by scripture are always begun by uttering Om, for those who speak of Brahman.
essence: Sacred action begins by naming the supreme reality first.
simple_meaning: People who follow scripture begin sacrifice, giving, and austerity by saying Om.
insight: It teaches you to begin action with awareness of the supreme reality, not mechanical routine.
modern_relevance: Before a difficult family conversation, you pause, breathe, and remember what you stand for. That small opening can turn a tense act into a sacred one.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः । दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षि ॥
translation: तत् नामसे कहे जानेवाले परमात्माके लिये ही सब कुछ है  ऐसा मानकर मुक्ति चाहनेवाले मनुष्योंद्वारा फलकी इच्छासे रहित होकर अनेक प्रकारकी यज्ञ और तपरूप क्रियाएँ तथा दानरूप क्रियाएँ की जाती हैं ॥
english_translation: Thinking “all this is for the supreme reality,” seekers of freedom perform many kinds of sacrifice, austerity, and giving without wanting the result.
essence: Freedom deepens when action stops demanding a private return.
simple_meaning: People seeking freedom do sacred actions, self-discipline, and giving without chasing personal reward. They treat the work itself as an offering.
insight: It shifts action from self-benefit to offering, so the mind stops bargaining with life.
modern_relevance: You send the apology, make the donation, or do the hard right thing — and no one thanks you. The act still stands complete without applause.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते । प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते ॥
translation: हे पार्थ  परमात्माके सत्इस नामका सत्तामात्रमें और श्रेष्ठ भावमें प्रयोग किया जाता है तथा प्रशंसनीय कर्मके साथ सत् शब्द जोड़ा जाता है ॥
english_translation: O Partha, the word sat is used for existence itself, for noble being, and for praiseworthy action.
essence: What is real and worthy carries the mark of sat.
simple_meaning: The word sat is used for what truly exists, for noble character, and for good action.
insight: It trains you to measure action by truth and worth, not by visible payoff.
modern_relevance: You sign a document you know is honest, even though no one is watching. The quiet relief comes from knowing the act itself is clean, whether or not it brings applause.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते । कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते ॥
translation: यज्ञ, तप और दानरूप क्रियामें जो स्थिति निष्ठा है, वह भी सत्  ऐसे कही जाती है और उस परमात्माके निमित्त किया जानेवाला कर्म भी सत्  ऐसा ही कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and giving is called sat. Action done for that purpose is also called sat.
essence: Steady offering makes ordinary action sacred.
simple_meaning: Steady dedication in sacrifice, disciplined effort, and giving is called sat. Any action done for that sacred purpose is also called sat.
insight: It shifts attention from the size of the act to the steadiness and intention behind it.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up for a hard promise no one can verify: caring for a parent, finishing a repair, telling the truth. The steadiness itself gives the act its worth.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् । असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह ॥
translation: हे पार्थ  अश्रद्धासे किया हुआ हवन, दिया हुआ दान और तपा हुआ तप तथा और भी जो,कुछ किया जाय, वह सब असत्  ऐसा कहा जाता है ।  उसका फल न यहाँ होता है, न मरनेके बाद ही होता है अर्थात् उसका कहीं भी सत् फल नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: O Partha, sacrifice, charity, austerity, and any deed done without trust are called unreal. Its fruit exists neither here nor after death.
essence: Trust is what makes action real; without it, effort becomes empty.
simple_meaning: Actions like sacrifice, charity, and austerity lose their value when done without trust. They produce no real result in this life or after death.
insight: It shifts action from performance to sincerity, showing that inner trust is what gives deeds weight.
modern_relevance: You donate money because it looks good, or apologize because others expect it, but your heart is absent. The act may happen, yet it leaves no real trace inside you or around you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अर्जुन उवाचसंन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् । त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन ॥
translation: अर्जुन बोले  हे महाबाहो  हे हृषीकेश  हे केशिनिषूदन  मैं संन्यास और त्यागका तत्त्व अलगअलग जानना चाहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Arjuna said: O mighty-armed one, O master of the senses, O slayer of Kesi, I wish to know the distinct truth of renunciation and relinquishment.
essence: Clear seeing begins with asking what must be separated.
simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain the difference between renunciation and relinquishment.
insight: It shifts the mind from vague spirituality to precise discernment before action.
modern_relevance: You are staring at two options that look similar but lead to very different lives. Before you quit, give up, or let go, you need to know what each one really means.
speaker: Arjuna

verse_text: श्री भगवानुवाचकाम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः । सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः ॥
english_translation: The wise call renunciation the giving up of desire-born actions. The discerning call renunciation the giving up of all results of action.
essence: Renunciation means releasing both craving and attachment to results.
simple_meaning: Wise people define renunciation in two ways: giving up actions driven by desire, and giving up attachment to all results of action.
insight: It shifts the mind from controlling outcomes to releasing attachment while still acting.
modern_relevance: You send the hard message, hit submit, and then keep checking for approval. This verse cuts that loop: do the work, then release the grip on what comes back.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः । यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे ॥
translation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  कई विद्वान् काम्यकर्मोंके त्यागको संन्यास कहते हैं और कई विद्वान् सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंके फलके त्यागको त्याग कहते हैं ।  कई विद्वान् कहते हैं कि कर्मोंको दोषकी तरह छोड़ देना चाहिये और कई विद्वान् कहते हैं कि यज्ञ, दान और तपरूप कर्मोंका त्याग नहीं करना चाहिये ॥
english_translation: Some wise people say all action should be abandoned as flawed. Others say sacrifice, giving, and disciplined effort should not be abandoned.
essence: Renunciation is not simple refusal; some actions must remain.
simple_meaning: Some teachers say action itself should be dropped because it seems flawed. Others say sacrifice, charity, and disciplined effort should never be dropped.
insight: It separates blind rejection from wise release, so you can keep what purifies action and drop what binds it.
modern_relevance: You’re about to quit a commitment because it feels messy and imperfect. Part of you wants to drop everything; part of you knows some responsibilities still matter.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: निश्चयं श्रृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम । त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः संप्रकीर्तितः ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  तू संन्यास और त्याग  इन दोनोंमेंसे पहले त्यागके विषयमें मेरा निश्चय सुन क्योंकि हे पुरुषश्रेष्ठ  त्याग तीन प्रकारका कहा गया है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, first hear my settled view on renunciation. Renunciation is said to be threefold.
essence: Renunciation is not one thing; it has distinct forms.
simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna to listen carefully to his clear view on renunciation. He says renunciation has three forms, so the subject needs to be understood with precision.
insight: It shifts the mind from vague renunciation to precise discrimination about what must be released.
modern_relevance: You are staring at an email that could end a partnership, and you keep rereading it. Before the decision, you need to know what kind of letting go is actually being asked of you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत् । यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम् ॥
translation: यज्ञ, दान और तपरूप कर्मोंका त्याग नहीं करना चाहिये, प्रत्युत उनको तो करना ही चाहिये क्योंकि यज्ञ, दान और तप  ये तीनों ही कर्म मनीषियोंको पवित्र करनेवाले हैं ॥
english_translation: Sacrifice, giving, and disciplined effort should not be abandoned; they must be done. These three actions purify thoughtful people.
essence: What purifies you should be done, not dropped.
simple_meaning: Sacrifice, giving, and disciplined effort should not be dropped. They are actions that purify a thoughtful person.
insight: It shifts renunciation from avoidance to purification through action.
modern_relevance: You want to skip the donation, the difficult conversation, the morning practice. Something in you calls it optional. Krishna says these are exactly the acts that clear the mind.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च । कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्िचतं मतमुत्तमम् ॥
translation: हे पार्थ  पूर्वोक्त यज्ञ, दान और तप   इन कर्मोंको तथा दूसरे भी कर्मोंको आसक्ति और फलोंका त्याग करके करना चाहिये  यह मेरा निश्चित किया हुआ उत्तम मत है ॥
english_translation: Even these actions, and all other actions, should be done without attachment and without wanting their results. This is my settled and best teaching, O Arjuna.
essence: Right action is complete only when desire for reward is dropped.
simple_meaning: Even sacred actions and all other duties should be done without clinging to results. Krishna says this is the best and settled teaching.
insight: It shifts action from outcome-hunger to clean participation in what must be done.
modern_relevance: You send the message, make the apology, or hand in the project, then sit with the uncertainty. The value was in doing it rightly, not in controlling how it lands.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते । मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः ॥
translation: नियत कर्मका तो त्याग करना उचित नहीं है ।  उसका मोहपूर्वक त्याग करना तामस कहा गया है ॥
english_translation: Abandoning prescribed action is not right. Giving it up in confusion is called tamasic.
essence: Right action should not be abandoned just because it feels difficult.
simple_meaning: You should not give up the work that is properly yours to do. If you drop it out of confusion, that is a dark and dull kind of renunciation.
insight: It shifts the mind from avoiding responsibility to testing whether the urge to quit is clear or merely fearful.
modern_relevance: You are about to quit a hard conversation because it feels uncomfortable, not because it is wrong. The urge to escape can look noble, but confusion is not wisdom.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् । स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥
translation: जो कुछ कर्म है, वह दुःखरूप ही है  ऐसा समझकर कोई शारीरिक क्लेशके भयसे उसका त्याग कर दे, तो वह राजस त्याग करके भी त्यागके फलको नहीं पाता ॥
english_translation: If someone gives up action thinking it is only suffering and fearing bodily strain, that renunciation is passionate, and it brings no fruit of renunciation.
essence: Fearful withdrawal is not freedom; it is avoidance wearing a noble name.
simple_meaning: Giving up your responsibilities because they feel hard is not true renunciation. It is a restless, fear-driven rejection of effort.
insight: It separates true renunciation from escape, so you stop dressing fear as virtue.
modern_relevance: You quit the hard conversation, then tell yourself you are “protecting your peace.” The body may feel safer, but the mind knows the move was avoidance, not freedom.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन । सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः ॥
translation: हे अर्जुन  केवल कर्तव्यमात्र करना है  ऐसा समझकर जो नियत कर्म आसक्ति और फलका त्याग करके किया जाता है, वही सात्त्विक त्याग माना गया है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, when fixed duty is done as only duty, without clinging to results, that renunciation is called sattvic.
essence: Renunciation means doing what must be done without gripping the result.
simple_meaning: Fixed duty becomes pure renunciation when it is done without attachment to personal gain or to the result.
insight: It shifts action from reward-chasing to clean responsibility.
modern_relevance: You send the message that could change everything, then stare at the screen for the reply. This verse says the honesty was the task; the response was never yours to hold.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते । त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः ॥
translation: जो अकुशल कर्मसे द्वेष नहीं करता और कुशल कर्ममें आसक्त नहीं होता, वह त्यागी, बुद्धिमान्, सन्देहरहित और अपने स्वरूपमें स्थित है ॥
english_translation: One who neither rejects unwholesome action nor clings to wholesome action is a wise renunciate, free of doubt and established in clear seeing.
essence: Freedom means neither resisting the hard nor craving the pleasant.
simple_meaning: A truly wise renunciate does not hate difficult actions and does not become attached to good ones. Such a person is steady, clear, and free of doubt.
insight: It shifts renunciation from avoidance to freedom from reaction, so action can stay clean under any condition.
modern_relevance: You take the job nobody wants because it matters, but you do not build your identity around being the hero. You do what must be done without craving praise or resenting the task.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः । यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते ॥
translation: कारण कि देहधारी मनुष्यके द्वारा सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंका त्याग करना सम्भव नहीं है ।  इसलिये जो कर्मफलका त्यागी है, वही त्यागी है  ऐसा कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: For embodied beings, total renunciation of action is impossible. Therefore, one who renounces the fruits of action is called a renunciant.
essence: Freedom begins when action continues and attachment stops.
simple_meaning: A person with a body cannot give up all action. Real renunciation means giving up attachment to the results, not abandoning work itself.
insight: It shifts the mind from escaping responsibility to releasing ownership of outcomes.
modern_relevance: You send the hard message, hit submit, and wait for the fallout. You cannot control every consequence, but you can stop clinging to what happens next.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम् । भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित् ॥
translation: कर्मफलका त्याग न करनेवाले मनुष्योंको कर्मोंका इष्ट, अनिष्ट और मिश्रित  ऐसे तीन प्रकारका फल मरनेके बाद भी होता है परन्तु कर्मफलका त्याग करनेवालोंको कहीं भी नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: For those who do not renounce the fruits of action, action produces three kinds of results—pleasant, unpleasant, and mixed—even after death; but for those who renounce the fruits, there is no such result anywhere.
essence: The chain of action ends when desire for its fruit ends.
simple_meaning: If you keep wanting the result of your actions, those actions keep producing effects for you. If you let go of results, that chain ends.
insight: It shifts attention from owning outcomes to releasing them after action.
modern_relevance: You send the message, then keep reopening the chat for a reply that decides your mood. The verse points to the hidden chain: craving the result keeps the action alive inside you.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे । सांख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम् ॥
translation: हे महाबाहो  कर्मोंका अन्त करनेवाले सांख्यसिद्धान्तमें सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंकी सिद्धिके लिये ये पाँच कारण बताये गये हैं, इनको तू मेरेसे समझ ॥
english_translation: O mighty-armed one, learn from Me these five causes, taught in the Sankhya system, for the accomplishment of all actions.
essence: Action has many causes; the ego is not the whole story.
simple_meaning: Krishna asks Arjuna to understand the five causes that make any action possible. Human action is not as simple as one person deciding and doing everything alone.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal monopoly over action to a clearer view of shared causes and conditions.
modern_relevance: You replay a mistake at 2 a.m. and ask, “How could I have done that?” Or you take full credit for a win. This verse widens the frame: one person is rarely the whole cause.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् । विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥
translation: इसमें कर्मोंकी सिद्धिमें अधिष्ठान तथा कर्ता और अनेक प्रकारके करण एवं विविध प्रकारकी अलगअलग चेष्टाएँ और वैसे ही पाँचवाँ कारण दैव संस्कार है ॥
english_translation: The field, the doer, the instruments, the many efforts, and the fifth factor, the unseen force, all shape every action.
essence: Action has many causes, and no one factor owns the result.
simple_meaning: Every action depends on several causes: the base, the doer, the tools, the different efforts, and a fifth factor beyond human control.
insight: It shifts the mind from absolute personal control to a clearer view of shared causation.
modern_relevance: You replay a difficult conversation for hours, asking who caused the damage. This verse reminds you that outcomes are rarely single-cause; many forces move together, including factors you could not control.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः । न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः ॥
translation: मनुष्य, शरीर वाणी और मनके द्वारा शास्त्रविहित अथवा शास्त्रविरुद्ध जो कुछ भी कर्म आरम्भ करता है, उसके ये पूर्वोक्त पाँचों हेतु होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Whatever action a person begins through body, speech, and mind—right or wrong—has these five causes.
essence: Every deed comes from five causes, not one isolated doer.
simple_meaning: Any action a person starts through body, speech, or mind is driven by five causes, whether the action is proper or improper.
insight: It shifts blame and pride away from a single ego and toward a clearer view of how action actually arises.
modern_relevance: You send the message in anger, then later say, “I just snapped.” Krishna points earlier: the body, words, mind, habits, and conditions were already moving.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
translation: परन्तु ऐसे पाँच हेतुओंके होनेपर भी जो उस कर्मोंके विषयमें केवल शुद्ध आत्माको कर्ता मानता है, वह दुर्मति ठीक नहीं समझता क्योंकि उसकी बुद्धि शुद्ध नहीं है ॥
english_translation: But one who sees only the pure self as the doer, even though these five causes are present, has not seen rightly; such a confused mind does not understand.
essence: Action has many causes; the pure self is not the lone doer.
simple_meaning: Action does not come from the pure self alone. A confused person wrongly thinks the self is the only doer and misses the real causes at work.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal overclaiming to clear seeing of shared causes.
modern_relevance: You replay a conversation at 1 a.m. and decide, "I caused everything." Krishna cuts through that mental trap: one person is rarely the whole cause.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते । हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते ॥
translation: जिसका अहंकृतभाव नहीं है और जिसकी बुद्धि लिप्त नहीं होती, वह इन सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंको मारकर भी न मारता है और न बँधता है ॥
english_translation: One who has no sense of separate self and whose understanding remains unstained does not kill, even by killing all these beings, and is not bound.
essence: Without egoic ownership, action leaves no stain.
simple_meaning: A person who has dropped ego and stays inwardly untouched is not truly the killer, and is not trapped by the act.
insight: It shifts responsibility from self-image to clear action, so the mind stops clinging to ownership.
modern_relevance: You make the call that ends a broken partnership. The words are heavy, but you do not have to carry them as personal guilt if you acted from clarity, not ego.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना । करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसंग्रहः ॥
translation: ज्ञान, ज्ञेय और परिज्ञाता  इन तीनोंसे कर्मप्रेरणा होती है तथा करण, कर्म और कर्ता  इन तीनोंसे कर्मसंग्रह होता है ॥
english_translation: Knowledge, the object known, and the knower—these three drive action. Instrument, act, and actor—these three make up the whole of action.
essence: Action is a system, not a single ego doing everything.
simple_meaning: Action is built from three parts: the knower, what is known, and the knowing itself; and also from the tool, the act, and the doer.
insight: It shifts the mind from blaming a single doer to seeing the structure behind any action.
modern_relevance: You replay a harsh conversation in your head and ask, “Who caused this?” The mind wants one culprit, but the event came from many parts moving together.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः । प्रोच्यते गुणसंख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि ॥
translation: गुणसंख्यान गुणोंके सम्बन्धसे प्रत्येक पदार्थके भिन्नभिन्न भेदोंकी गणना करनेवाले शास्त्रमें गुणोंके भेदसे ज्ञान और कर्म तथा कर्ता तीनतीन प्रकारसे ही कहे जाते हैं, उनको भी तुम यथार्थरूपसे सुनो ॥
english_translation: In the analysis of the three qualities, knowledge, action, and the doer are each said to be threefold. Listen now to these distinctions as they truly are.
essence: Every action, knower, and deed carries the mark of a quality.
simple_meaning: Knowledge, action, and the doer are each understood in three different ways according to the three qualities. Krishna asks Arjuna to listen carefully to this classification.
insight: It shifts attention from the outer event to the quality of consciousness behind it.
modern_relevance: You can do the same task with a clear mind, a restless mind, or a dull mind. The outer act looks identical, but the inner quality changes everything.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते । अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् ॥
translation: जिस ज्ञानके द्वारा साधक सम्पूर्ण विभक्त प्राणियोंमें विभागरहित एक अविनाशी भावसत्ता को देखता है, उस ज्ञानको तुम सात्त्विक समझो ॥
english_translation: Know that knowledge to be sattvic by which one sees the one imperishable reality in all beings, undivided among the divided.
essence: True understanding sees one undivided reality inside every divided form.
simple_meaning: Pure understanding sees one unchanging reality in all beings, even though they appear separate.
insight: It shifts perception from surface differences to the underlying unity that makes judgment softer.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after an argument and see only sides, labels, and distance. This verse asks you to look again and notice the shared humanity beneath the split.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान् । वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम् ॥
translation: परन्तु जो ज्ञान अर्थात् जिस ज्ञानके द्वारा मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें अलगअलग अनेक भावोंको अलगअलग रूपसे जानता है, उस ज्ञानको तुम राजस समझो ॥
english_translation: But know that knowledge as rajasic by which one sees many different beings as separate and distinct in all beings.
essence: Dividing everything into parts is not clarity; it is restless seeing.
simple_meaning: Knowledge that only notices differences and treats every being as separate is restless and driven by ego.
insight: It shifts the mind from categorising everything separately to asking whether the seeing itself is restless and partial.
modern_relevance: You meet someone new and instantly reduce them to labels, roles, and differences. The mind feels precise, but it is only chopping reality into pieces and calling that insight.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम् । अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
translation: किंतु जो ज्ञान एक कार्यरूप शरीरमें ही सम्पूर्णके तरह आसक्त है तथा जो युक्तिरहित, वास्तविक ज्ञानसे रहित और तुच्छ है, वह तामस कहा गया है ॥
english_translation: But knowledge that clings to one body as if it were the whole, without reason, without truth, and petty, is called dark.
essence: Small certainty can hide the least real understanding.
simple_meaning: A dark kind of understanding mistakes one limited thing for the whole, lacks clear reasoning, and stays small and confused.
insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to a partial picture toward testing whether a view actually fits reality.
modern_relevance: You’re certain your first angry reaction is the full story, and you build a whole argument on it. This verse warns that a tiny, rigid view can feel complete while missing reality.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् । अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते ॥
translation: जो कर्म शास्त्रविधिसे नियत किया हुआ और कर्तृत्वाभिमानसे रहित हो तथा फलेच्छारहित मनुष्यके द्वारा बिना रागद्वेषके किया हुआ हो, वह सात्त्विक कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: Action that is guided by duty, free from attachment, and done without craving results is called sattvic.
essence: The purest action asks for nothing back.
simple_meaning: Action is pure when it follows duty, is free from attachment, and is done without craving the result.
insight: It shifts attention from reward-seeking to duty-shaped action, so effort stays steady and uncorrupted.
modern_relevance: You send the message you’ve been avoiding, knowing it may change everything. What makes it right is not the reaction you get, but the clean intention behind it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः । क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् ॥
translation: परन्तु जो कर्म भोगोंको चाहनेवाले मनुष्यके द्वारा अहंकार अथवा परिश्रमपूर्वक किया जाता है, वह राजस कहा गया है ॥
english_translation: But action done with desire for pleasure, or with ego, or with great strain, is said to be rajasic.
essence: Desire and ego turn action restless, even when it looks productive.
simple_meaning: Action driven by craving, ego, or strain belongs to restlessness, not clarity. It is active, but it is not clean.
insight: It teaches you to notice when effort is powered by craving and self-importance, not purpose.
modern_relevance: You keep pushing because you want the praise, the win, the proof. The work gets done, but it leaves you tighter than before.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् । मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते ॥
translation: जो कर्म परिणाम, हानि, हिंसा और सामर्थ्यको न देखकर मोहपूर्वक आरम्भ किया जाता है, वह तामस कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: Action begun in delusion, ignoring its consequences, harm, and one’s own capacity, is called tamasic.
essence: Blind action begins where clear seeing is absent.
simple_meaning: Action driven by confusion, without considering consequences, damage, or your real ability, is dark and unwise.
insight: It teaches you to pause long enough to judge consequences before acting.
modern_relevance: You hit send on the angry message, then realize it will wound three people and solve nothing. This verse asks for one breath of clear seeing before the damage starts.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥
translation: जो कर्ता रागरहित, अनहंवादी, धैर्य और उत्साहयुक्त तथा सिद्धि और असिद्धिमें निर्विकार है, वह सात्त्विक कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: The doer who is free from attachment, free from ego, endowed with steadiness and enthusiasm, and unchanged by success or failure is called sattvic.
essence: Pure action leaves the ego out and stays calm in victory or defeat.
simple_meaning: A truly pure doer works without attachment, ego, or inner disturbance, and remains steady whether the result succeeds or fails.
insight: It shifts attention from ownership and outcome to steadiness of character in action.
modern_relevance: You sent the message, made the call, and waited for the reply that could change everything. Your chest tightens. This verse asks you to stay clear inside, no matter what answer comes back.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः । हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः ॥
translation: जो कर्ता रागी, कर्मफलकी इच्छावाला, लोभी, हिंसाके स्वभाववाला, अशुद्ध और हर्षशोकसे युक्त है, वह राजस कहा गया है ॥
english_translation: The doer ruled by craving, chasing results, greedy, violent in nature, impure, and tossed by joy and sorrow is called passionate.
essence: Craving turns action into a chase for reward and emotional swing.
simple_meaning: A person driven by craving, greed, and attachment to results acts in a restless, passionate way and stays pulled between pleasure and disappointment.
insight: It teaches you to notice when desire for payoff is contaminating your action.
modern_relevance: You hit refresh after sending the message, hoping for praise, then sink when it is ignored. That swing reveals a mind acting for reward, not from steadiness.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः । विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥
translation: जो कर्ता असावधान, अशिक्षित, ऐंठअकड़वाला, जिद्दी, उपकारीका अपकार करनेवाला, आलसी, विषादी और दीर्घसूत्री है, वह तामस कहा जाता है ॥
english_translation: A careless, crude, stubborn, deceitful, lazy, gloomy, and procrastinating doer is called tamasic.
essence: Dullness in the doer makes even action inert and harmful.
simple_meaning: A person who acts carelessly, lazily, stubbornly, and deceitfully is working from tamasic energy. That kind of action is dull, delayed, and harmful.
insight: It shifts attention from excuses to the quality of the doer behind the deed.
modern_relevance: You keep postponing the hard email, then tell yourself you will do it tomorrow. The task is still there, but your energy has gone heavy, vague, and self-protective.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं श्रृणु । प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय ॥
translation: हे धनञ्जय  अब तू गुणोंके अनुसार बुद्धि और धृतिके भी तीन प्रकारके भेद अलगअलगरूपसे सुन, जो कि मेरे द्वारा पूर्णरूपसे कहे जा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: O Dhananjaya, now hear the threefold distinctions of understanding and steadfastness according to the three qualities, fully and separately explained.
essence: Understanding and resolve differ by the quality that shapes them.
simple_meaning: Krishna asks Arjuna to listen to the three kinds of understanding and steadfastness, explained separately according to the three qualities.
insight: It shifts attention from the decision itself to the quality of mind making the decision.
modern_relevance: You are staring at two job offers, one safe and one honest, and your mind keeps changing its story. First notice what kind of understanding is speaking, then decide.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये । बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन  जो बुद्धि प्रवृत्ति और निवृत्तिको, कर्तव्य और अकर्तव्यको, भय और अभयको तथा बन्धन और मोक्षको जानती है, वह बुद्धि सात्त्विकी है ॥
english_translation: O Partha, the intellect that knows what leads forward and what withdraws, what should be done and not done, what is fear and fearlessness, what binds and what frees, is sattvic.
essence: True intelligence recognizes the difference between bondage and freedom.
simple_meaning: A clear mind can tell the difference between action and withdrawal, right and wrong action, fear and fearlessness, bondage and freedom.
insight: It trains discernment: not every option is equal, and clear seeing separates duty from confusion.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a message you know will change everything. The real question is not what feels safer, but whether your mind can see what binds and what frees.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च । अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥
translation: हे पार्थ  मनुष्य जिसके द्वारा धर्म और अधर्मको, कर्तव्य और अकर्तव्यको भी ठीक तरहसे नहीं जानता, वह बुद्धि राजसी है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, the intellect that does not truly know right action and wrong action, duty and what should not be done, is rajasic.
essence: Restless intelligence cannot tell duty from harm.
simple_meaning: A restless, rajasic mind misreads right action and wrong action. It cannot clearly tell what should be done and what should be avoided.
insight: It trains you to notice when agitation is distorting judgment and to pause until duty becomes clear.
modern_relevance: You are staring at two replies before sending one that could change a relationship. One part of you knows what is right; another part keeps spinning. That spinning is rajasic confusion.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसाऽऽवृता । सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन  तमोगुणसे घिरी हुई जो बुद्धि अधर्मको धर्म और सम्पूर्ण चीजोंको उलटा मान लेती है, वह तामसी है ॥
english_translation: The mind covered by darkness calls wrongdoing right and reverses everything.
essence: Darkness can make the wrong choice feel morally correct.
simple_meaning: A mind clouded by darkness mistakes wrongdoing for righteousness and gets its judgment completely reversed.
insight: It trains you to test your judgments before acting, especially when a bad choice feels emotionally comfortable.
modern_relevance: You defend a choice in your head at 1 a.m., and it starts sounding noble. This verse catches that moment when self-justification begins to wear the mask of conscience.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः । योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥
translation: हे पार्थ  समतासे युक्त जिस अव्यभिचारिणी धृतिके द्वारा मनुष्य मन, प्राण और इन्द्रियोंकी क्रियाओंको धारण करता है, वह धृति सात्त्विकी है ॥
english_translation: O Partha, that steadfastness by which one holds steady the functions of mind, life-force, and senses through unwavering yoga is sattvic steadfastness.
essence: Steadiness becomes pure when it keeps the whole being aligned.
simple_meaning: True steadfastness is the power to keep the mind, life-force, and senses steady through yoga, without wavering.
insight: It teaches you to regulate inner forces instead of being ruled by them.
modern_relevance: You're about to send the message, make the call, or walk into the room, and your body wants to bolt. This verse points to the kind of steadiness that keeps you aligned when nerves, impulses, and distractions all surge at once.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यया तु धर्मकामार्थान् धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन । प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥
translation: हे पृथानन्दन अर्जुन  फलकी इच्छावाला मनुष्य जिस धृतिके द्वारा धर्म, काम भोग और अर्थको अत्यन्त आसक्तिपूर्वक धारण करता है, वह धृति राजसी है ॥
english_translation: Arjuna, the steadiness that clings intensely to duty, pleasure, and wealth, while craving results, is passionate steadiness.
essence: Steadiness becomes restless when it is tied to reward.
simple_meaning: A person can appear steady and disciplined, yet still be driven by attachment to duty, pleasure, and wealth, along with desire for results. That kind of firmness is restless, not pure.
insight: It separates true discipline from ambition disguised as discipline, so you can see what is actually driving your effort.
modern_relevance: You keep a strict routine, but every habit is secretly aimed at applause, profit, or control. The outside looks disciplined; the inside is bargaining.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च । न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥
translation: हे पार्थ  दुष्ट बुद्धिवाला मनुष्य जिस धृतिके द्वारा निद्रा, भय, चिन्ता, दुःख और घमण्डको भी नहीं छोड़ता, वह धृति तामसी है ॥
english_translation: The dull-minded one does not let go of sleep, fear, grief, sorrow, and pride. That steadfastness is tamasic, Arjuna.
essence: Clinging to fear and sorrow is not strength; it is tamasic inertia.
simple_meaning: Some people hold on to sleepiness, fear, grief, despair, and pride instead of releasing them. That kind of stubbornness is dull and tamasic.
insight: It shifts you to notice whether your resolve is clarifying action or merely preserving mental fog.
modern_relevance: You keep replaying the same failure in bed at 2 a.m., feeding the fear instead of setting it down. Krishna calls that not strength, but heaviness.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ । अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  अब तीन प्रकारके सुखको भी तुम मेरेसे सुनो ।  जिसमें अभ्याससे रमण होता है और जिससे दुःखोंका अन्त हो जाता है, ऐसा वह परमात्मविषयक बुद्धिकी प्रसन्नतासे पैदा होनेवाला जो सुख सांसारिक आसक्तिके कारण आरम्भमें विषकी तरह और परिणाममें अमृतकी तरह होता है, वह सुख सात्त्विक कहा गया है ॥
english_translation: O best of the Bharatas, hear from me now about three kinds of happiness. The happiness that comes from practice, ends sorrow, and first feels like poison but later like nectar is called sattvic.
essence: True happiness begins as discipline and ends as relief.
simple_meaning: Krishna describes a higher kind of happiness: it grows through practice, brings lasting relief, and feels difficult at first but sweet in the end.
insight: It shifts the mind to value disciplined practice that matures into freedom from suffering.
modern_relevance: You keep returning to the meditation cushion even when it feels awkward and unrewarding. Weeks later, the mind settles, and the struggle that once felt heavy starts to feel like home.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् । तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥
translation: हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  अब तीन प्रकारके सुखको भी तुम मेरेसे सुनो ।  जिसमें अभ्याससे रमण होता है और जिससे दुःखोंका अन्त हो जाता है, ऐसा वह परमात्मविषयक बुद्धिकी प्रसन्नतासे पैदा होनेवाला जो सुख सांसारिक आसक्तिके कारण आरम्भमें विषकी तरह और परिणाममें अमृतकी तरह होता है, वह सुख सात्त्विक कहा गया है ॥
english_translation: That happiness is called sattvic, which seems like poison at first and like nectar in the end, born from clarity of the discerning mind and the peace of inner understanding.
essence: Lasting ease can begin as discomfort and end as release.
simple_meaning: A calm, clear happiness may feel difficult at first, but it ends in deep relief. It comes from a mind that sees clearly and settles inwardly.
insight: It shifts you to value what strengthens clear seeing over what merely feels pleasant at first.
modern_relevance: You start therapy, meditation, or a hard conversation and feel worse before you feel better. The discomfort is not a sign of failure; it may be the beginning of real ease.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् । परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
translation: जो सुख इन्द्रियों और विषयोंके संयोगसे आरम्भमें अमृतकी तरह और परिणाममें विषकी तरह होता है, वह सुख राजस कहा गया है ॥
english_translation: The pleasure that begins like nectar from contact between the senses and their objects, but ends like poison, is called rajasic pleasure.
essence: What feels sweetest first can become the harshest later.
simple_meaning: Pleasures that come from sensory contact can feel wonderful at first, but they often leave pain, restlessness, or disappointment afterward.
insight: It trains you to judge pleasure by its full arc, not its first taste.
modern_relevance: You open the app for one quick scroll after midnight, then another, then another. The rush feels harmless in the moment, but the next morning tells the truth.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः । निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
translation: निद्रा, आलस्य और प्रमादसे उत्पन्न होनेवाला जो सुख आरम्भमें और परिणाममें अपनेको मोहित करनेवाला है, वह सुख तामस कहा गया है ॥
english_translation: That pleasure, born of sleep, laziness, and negligence, deludes the self at the beginning and at the end; it is called tamasic.
essence: Pleasure that dulls you is not relief; it is confusion in disguise.
simple_meaning: Pleasure that comes from sleep, laziness, and carelessness feels good only briefly. It dulls the mind and leaves a person more confused.
insight: It teaches you to test pleasure by its aftereffect, not its first taste.
modern_relevance: You keep scrolling after midnight because stopping feels strangely pleasant. In the morning, the fog is heavier, not lighter. That comfort was never rest; it was drift.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः । सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्ित्रभिर्गुणैः ॥
translation: पृथ्वीमें या स्वर्गमें अथवा देवताओंमें तथा इनके सिवाय और कहीं भी वह ऐसी कोई वस्तु नहीं है, जो प्रकृतिसे उत्पन्न इन तीनों गुणोंसे रहित हो ॥
english_translation: There is nothing on earth, in heaven, or among the radiant beings that is free from the three qualities born of nature.
essence: No state is free from the three qualities of nature.
simple_meaning: Everything in the world is shaped by the three qualities of nature. Nothing in the material order is completely free from them.
insight: It shifts attention from judging appearances to seeing the forces that shape every response.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems effortlessly calm, then catch their irritation under pressure. The verse cuts through the fantasy that any person or status is beyond temperament, habit, and conditioning.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परंतप । कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः ॥
translation: हे परंतप  ब्राह्मण, क्षत्रिय, वैश्य और शूद्रोंके कर्म स्वभावसे उत्पन्न हुए तीनों गुणोंके द्वारा विभक्त किये गये हैं ॥
english_translation: O scorcher of foes, the duties of priests, warriors, merchants, and workers are divided according to the qualities born of their nature.
essence: Your rightful work comes from your nature, not imitation.
simple_meaning: Different kinds of work belong to different people according to their nature and qualities.
insight: It shifts attention from borrowed identity to the work that matches your actual nature.
modern_relevance: A student keeps forcing themselves into a career because everyone praises it, while their real strengths are elsewhere. The pressure eases when they stop copying and start listening to what fits.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च । ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
translation: मनका निग्रह करना इन्द्रियोंको वशमें करना धर्मपालनके लिये कष्ट सहना बाहरभीतरसे शुद्ध रहना दूसरोंके अपराधको क्षमा करना शरीर, मन आदिमें सरलता रखना वेद, शास्त्र आदिका ज्ञान होना यज्ञविधिको अनुभवमें लाना और परमात्मा, वेद आदिमें आस्तिक भाव रखना  ये सबकेसब ब्राह्मणके स्वाभाविक कर्म हैं ॥
english_translation: Self-restraint, control of the senses, austerity, purity, forgiveness, honesty, knowledge, realization, and faith in the supreme reality are the natural duties of a brahmin.
essence: True duty begins as disciplined character, not public role.
simple_meaning: A person's natural work can include self-control, purity, forgiveness, honesty, knowledge, and trust in the supreme reality. These qualities belong to a brahmin by nature.
insight: It shifts duty from outer status to inner formation: the right work grows from the qualities you cultivate.
modern_relevance: Before a difficult conversation, you can feel the urge to bluff, snap, or hide. This verse points to a different strength: stay clean in speech, steady in mind, and honest in intent.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् । दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
translation: शूरवीरता, तेज, धैर्य, प्रजाके संचालन आदिकी विशेष चतुरता, युद्धमें कभी पीठ न दिखाना, दान करना और शासन करनेका भाव  ये सबकेसब क्षत्रियके स्वाभाविक कर्म हैं ॥
english_translation: Valor, radiance, firmness, quick skill, never fleeing in battle, generosity, and leadership are the natural duties of a warrior.
essence: True strength serves, stands firm, and does not retreat.
simple_meaning: A warrior’s natural duties include courage, steadiness, skill, generosity, and refusing to run from battle.
insight: It shifts duty from self-protection to fearless responsibility.
modern_relevance: A parent walks into a tense school meeting and stays calm while everyone expects defensiveness. The verse points to that kind of steadiness: meet pressure with courage, not retreat.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् । परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम् ॥
translation: खेती करना, गायोंकी रक्षा करना और शुद्ध व्यापार करना  ये सबकेसब वैश्यके स्वाभाविक कर्म हैं, तथा चारों वर्णोंकी सेवा करना शूद्रका भी स्वाभाविक कर्म है ॥
english_translation: Farming, cattle-keeping, and trade are the natural work of the merchant class. Service to others is the natural work of the worker class.
essence: Every nature has its own rightful work.
simple_meaning: Different kinds of work suit different people. Farming, cattle care, trade, and service are described as natural duties for two social groups.
insight: It shifts attention from status-seeking to honest fit: the right work is the work aligned with your nature and role.
modern_relevance: You are forcing yourself into a career that looks impressive but drains you. Relief comes when you stop asking, “What should I be?” and start asking, “What fits my nature?”
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः । स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥
translation: अपनेअपने कर्ममें तत्परतापूर्वक लगा हुआ मनुष्य सम्यक् सिद्धिपरमात्माको प्राप्त कर लेता है ।  अपने कर्ममें लगा हुआ मनुष्य जिस प्रकार सिद्धिको प्राप्त होता है उस प्रकारको तू मेरेसे सुन ॥
english_translation: A person devoted to their own work attains perfection. Listen as I explain how a person devoted to their own work reaches that perfection.
essence: Fulfillment comes from living your own work, not someone else’s.
simple_meaning: A person reaches fulfillment by staying devoted to their own duty, rather than chasing someone else’s role.
insight: It redirects attention from imitation to rightful action, showing that steady devotion to one's role leads to completion.
modern_relevance: You are comparing your path to a friend’s promotion, a sibling’s marriage, a stranger’s confidence. The verse cuts through that ache: your fulfillment grows where your own responsibility is.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥
translation: जिस परमात्मासे सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंकी उत्पत्ति होती है और जिससे यह सम्पूर्ण संसार व्याप्त है, उस परमात्माका अपने कर्मके द्वारा पूजन करके मनुष्य सिद्धिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: By worshipping the one from whom all beings arise and by whom this whole world is pervaded, a person attains perfection through their own work.
essence: Offering your work to the source of life turns ordinary action into fulfillment.
simple_meaning: A person reaches fulfillment by offering their own work to the source of all beings and all existence.
insight: It shifts action from self-display to offering, so the mind stops measuring worth by applause.
modern_relevance: You are doing something difficult that no one will fully understand — caring for a parent, finishing a lonely project, keeping a promise. The verse says that the act itself becomes complete when offered beyond the ego.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
translation: अच्छी तरहसे अनुष्ठान किये हुए परधर्मसे गुणरहित अपना धर्म श्रेष्ठ है ।  कारण कि स्वभावसे नियत किये हुए स्वधर्मरूप कर्मको करता हुआ मनुष्य पापको प्राप्त नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: One's own duty, though imperfect, is better than another's duty well performed. Doing the work set by one's nature, a person does not incur wrongdoing.
essence: Your imperfect duty is cleaner than a borrowed perfection.
simple_meaning: It is better to do your own duty, even imperfectly, than to do someone else's duty well. Acting according to your nature does not lead you into wrongdoing.
insight: It shifts the mind from comparison to alignment: choose the work that matches your nature, not the work that flatters your ego.
modern_relevance: You are tempted to take the job that looks impressive, the role that earns praise, the life that belongs to someone else. This verse says the mismatch itself creates friction; your own work, even imperfectly done, keeps you clean.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
translation: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  दोषयुक्त होनेपर भी सहज कर्मका त्याग नहीं करना चाहिये क्योंकि सम्पूर्ण कर्म धुएँसे अग्निकी तरह किसीनकिसी दोषसे युक्त हैं ॥
english_translation: O son of Kunti, one should not abandon one's natural duty, even if it has flaws. All undertakings are clouded by some defect, just as fire is veiled by smoke.
essence: Your right work is still right, even when it is imperfect.
simple_meaning: Do not give up your natural duty just because it is imperfect. Every action has some flaw in it.
insight: It shifts the mind from perfectionism to faithful action despite flaws.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the apology, start the difficult conversation, or take the job that fits your values but feels messy. Imperfection is not a reason to freeze.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः । नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥
translation: जिसकी बुद्धि सब जगह आसक्तिरहित है, जिसने शरीरको वशमें कर रखा है, जो स्पृहारहित है, वह मनुष्य सांख्ययोगके द्वारा नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: One whose mind is detached everywhere, who has mastered the self, and who is free from craving attains the highest perfection of non-action through renunciation.
essence: Freedom arrives when the mind stops reaching outward.
simple_meaning: A person who is detached everywhere, self-controlled, and free from craving reaches the highest state of actionlessness through renunciation.
insight: It shifts attention from outward gain to inward freedom, showing that mastery begins when craving ends.
modern_relevance: You finish a hard conversation and keep replaying it for approval. The mind that stops reaching for praise finds a quieter kind of strength.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे । समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा ॥
translation: हे कौन्तेय  सिद्धिअन्तःकरणकी शुद्धि को प्राप्त हुआ साधक ब्रह्मको, जो कि ज्ञानकी परा निष्ठा है, जिस प्रकारसे प्राप्त होता है, उस प्रकारको तुम मुझसे संक्षेपमें ही समझो ॥
english_translation: Listen to me briefly, O Arjuna, as I explain how one who has reached perfection attains the supreme reality, the highest culmination of knowledge.
essence: Knowledge has a highest point: direct arrival, not endless thinking.
simple_meaning: Krishna asks Arjuna to listen briefly as he explains how a perfected seeker reaches the supreme reality, the highest point of knowledge.
insight: It shifts the mind from collecting ideas to seeking the final state those ideas point toward.
modern_relevance: You have read, reflected, and still feel stuck at the edge of a hard choice. At some point, understanding must become arrival — not more analysis.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्याऽऽत्मानं नियम्य च । शब्दादीन् विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च ॥
translation: जो विशुद्ध सात्त्विकी बुद्धिसे युक्त, वैराग्यके आश्रित, एकान्तका सेवन करनेवाला और नियमित भोजन करनेवाला साधक धैर्यपूर्वक इन्द्रियोंका नियमन करके, शरीरवाणीमनको वशमें करके, शब्दादि विषयोंका त्याग करके और रागद्वेषको छोड़कर निरन्तर ध्यानयोगके परायण हो जाता है, वह अहंकार, बल, दर्प, काम, क्रोध और परिग्रहका त्याग करके एवं निर्मम तथा शान्त होकर ब्रह्मप्राप्तिका पात्र हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Endowed with purified understanding, holding the self steady with firm resolve, giving up sense-objects, and casting away attraction and aversion...
essence: Purified resolve cuts the pull of craving and aversion.
simple_meaning: A person with clear understanding steadies the mind, restrains the senses, gives up sense pleasures, and drops attraction and aversion.
insight: It shifts attention from reacting to training the mind to stay steady under pressure.
modern_relevance: You open your phone to escape one uncomfortable message, then another craving follows. The mind keeps pulling until you deliberately stop feeding it.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः । ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः ॥
translation: जो विशुद्ध सात्त्विकी बुद्धिसे युक्त, वैराग्यके आश्रित, एकान्तका सेवन करनेवाला और नियमित भोजन करनेवाला साधक धैर्यपूर्वक इन्द्रियोंका नियमन करके, शरीरवाणीमनको वशमें करके, शब्दादि विषयोंका त्याग करके और रागद्वेषको छोड़कर निरन्तर ध्यानयोगके परायण हो जाता है, वह अहंकार, बल, दर्प, काम, क्रोध और परिग्रहका त्याग करके एवं निर्मम तथा शान्त होकर ब्रह्मप्राप्तिका पात्र हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Dwelling in solitude, eating lightly, and controlling speech, body, and mind, one stays absorbed in meditation, grounded in non-attachment.
essence: Freedom grows from deliberate simplicity and steady restraint.
simple_meaning: A serious seeker lives simply, keeps the senses under control, and stays devoted to meditation with non-attachment.
insight: It shifts the focus from heroic moments to the habits that make inner steadiness possible.
modern_relevance: You turn off your phone, skip the extra noise, and sit alone before dawn. The mind settles faster when the day stops feeding it distractions.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् । विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
translation: जो विशुद्ध सात्त्विकी बुद्धिसे युक्त, वैराग्यके आश्रित, एकान्तका सेवन करनेवाला और नियमित भोजन करनेवाला साधक धैर्यपूर्वक इन्द्रियोंका नियमन करके, शरीरवाणीमनको वशमें करके, शब्दादि विषयोंका त्याग करके और रागद्वेषको छोड़कर निरन्तर ध्यानयोगके परायण हो जाता है, वह अहंकार, बल, दर्प, काम, क्रोध और परिग्रहका त्याग करके एवं निर्मम तथा शान्त होकर ब्रह्मप्राप्तिका पात्र हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Free from ego, force, pride, desire, anger, and possession, one becomes peaceful, without “mine,” and fit for union with the supreme reality.
essence: Peace begins when the sense of ownership ends.
simple_meaning: Let go of ego, pride, craving, anger, and possessiveness. When the sense of “mine” falls away, the mind becomes peaceful and ready for the supreme reality.
insight: It shifts the goal from self-protection to inner freedom by dropping the habits that harden the mind.
modern_relevance: You type a reply full of defensiveness, then stop before sending. In that pause, you can feel the grip of “I must win” loosening. That release is the real turning point.
speaker: Krishna

verse_text: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥
translation: वह ब्रह्मभूतअवस्थाको प्राप्त प्रसन्न मनवाला साधक न तो किसीके लिये शोक करता है और न किसीकी इच्छा करता है ।  ऐसा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें समभाववाला साधक मेरी पराभक्तिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
