translation: संत सरल हृदय और जगत के हितकारी होते हैं, उनके ऐसे स्वभाव और स्नेह को जानकर मैं विनय करता हूँ, मेरी इस बाल-विनय को सुनकर कृपा करके श्री रामजी के चरणों में मुझे प्रीति दें ॥
english_translation: Saints are simple-hearted and seek the welfare of the world. Knowing their nature and affection, I humbly ask: hearing this childlike prayer, please grant me love for Ram's feet.
essence: Saintly simplicity awakens love for Ram.
simple_meaning: True saints are simple, loving, and concerned for everyone’s good. Seeing that, the poet asks for grace to feel devotion to Ram.
insight: It shifts admiration into practice: let noble company awaken devotion, not comparison.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who never gossips, never competes, and somehow leaves everyone calmer. Their quiet kindness makes you want to become better, not louder.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: बहुरि बंदि खल गन सतिभाएँ। जे बिनु काज दाहिनेहु बाएँ॥ पर हित हानि लाभ जिन्ह केरें। उजरें हरष बिषाद बसेरें ॥
translation: अब मैं सच्चे भाव से दुष्टों को प्रणाम करता हूँ, जो बिना ही प्रयोजन, अपना हित करने वाले के भी प्रतिकूल आचरण करते हैं। दूसरों के हित की हानि ही जिनकी दृष्टि में लाभ है, जिनको दूसरों के उजड़ने में हर्ष और बसने में विषाद होता है ॥
english_translation: Again, I bow with sincere feeling to the wicked, who, without cause, act against even those who do them good. They count others' loss as gain; they rejoice when others are ruined and grieve when others prosper.
essence: Even malice can be read clearly when you refuse to be swept away by it.
simple_meaning: Even harmful people are acknowledged here. They oppose goodness for no reason, and they treat other people’s suffering as their own gain.
insight: It trains you to recognize distorted motives without getting pulled into their mood.
modern_relevance: A colleague smiles while quietly blocking your work, then acts wounded when you succeed. The verse helps you see that some resistance is not about you — it is a mind addicted to comparison and harm.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: हरि हर जस राकेस राहु से। पर अकाज भट सहसबाहु से॥ जे पर दोष लखहिं सहसाखी। पर हित घृत जिन्ह के मन माखी ॥
translation: जो हरि और हर के यश रूपी पूर्णिमा के चन्द्रमा के लिए राहु के समान हैं (अर्थात जहाँ कहीं भगवान विष्णु या शंकर के यश का वर्णन होता है, उसी में वे बाधा देते हैं) और दूसरों की बुराई करने में सहस्रबाहु के समान वीर हैं। जो दूसरों के दोषों को हजार आँखों से देखते हैं और दूसरों के हित रूपी घी के लिए जिनका मन मक्खी के समान है (अर्थात् जिस प्रकार मक्खी घी में गिरकर उसे खराब कर देती है और स्वयं भी मर जाती है, उसी प्रकार दुष्ट लोग दूसरों के बने-बनाए काम को अपनी हानि करके भी बिगाड़ देते हैं) ॥
english_translation: Like Rahu to the moon of Hari and Hara's fame, they are like Sahasrabahu in doing harm to others' work. They spot others' faults with a thousand eyes, and their mind is like a fly drawn to another's good like ghee, ruining it even at their own loss.
essence: Some minds cannot bear goodness, so they spoil it and call it insight.
simple_meaning: Evil people block good work, obsess over others' faults, and ruin what helps others even when it harms themselves.
insight: It trains you to recognize destructive criticism as a pattern of inner corruption, not just bad manners.
modern_relevance: A group chat turns sour because one person keeps hunting for flaws in every plan. The project stalls, morale drops, and even their own reputation takes the hit.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तेज कृसानु रोष महिषेसा। अघ अवगुन धन धनी धनेसा॥ उदय केत सम हित सबही के। कुंभकरन सम सोवत नीके ॥
translation: जो तेज (दूसरों को जलाने वाले ताप) में अग्नि और क्रोध में यमराज के समान हैं, पाप और अवगुण रूपी धन में कुबेर के समान धनी हैं, जिनकी बढ़ती सभी के हित का नाश करने के लिए केतु (पुच्छल तारे) के समान है और जिनके कुम्भकर्ण की तरह सोते रहने में ही भलाई है ॥
english_translation: They blaze like fire, rage like Yama, hoard evil and faults like Kubera hoards treasure, rise like a comet to ruin everyone’s good, and sleep well only like Kumbhakarna.
essence: Destructive people poison even their rise, and peace comes only in their absence.
simple_meaning: Evil people burn others with their presence, rage destructively, collect faults like treasure, and even their rise harms everyone. They rest only when they are asleep.
insight: It shifts the mind from moral confusion to clear seeing of destructive tendencies.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose every comment leaves the room colder, whose success seems to create new damage, and whose silence is the only relief. The verse names that pattern without flinching.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: पर अकाजु लगि तनु परिहरहीं। जिमि हिम उपल कृषी दलि गरहीं॥ बंदउँ खल जस सेष सरोषा। सहस बदन बरनइ पर दोषा ॥
translation: जैसे ओले खेती का नाश करके आप भी गल जाते हैं, वैसे ही वे दूसरों का काम बिगाड़ने के लिए अपना शरीर तक छोड़ देते हैं। मैं दुष्टों को (हजार मुख वाले) शेषजी के समान समझकर प्रणाम करता हूँ, जो पराए दोषों का हजार मुखों से बड़े रोष के साथ वर्णन करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Like hailstones that ruin crops and then melt away, such people ruin others' work and waste away their own bodies. I bow to the wicked, like Shesha with a thousand mouths, who angrily describe the faults of others with a thousand tongues.
essence: Malice destroys others and consumes the one who carries it.
simple_meaning: People driven by malice ruin others even at the cost of their own well-being. They obsess over other people's faults and speak about them with anger.
insight: It shifts attention from blaming others to seeing how corrosive fault-finding becomes in the mind that repeats it.
modern_relevance: A group chat turns into a pile-on, and someone keeps adding more fuel just to feel righteous. The room gets darker, but the person feeding it is the first to be scorched.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: पुनि प्रनवउँ पृथुराज समाना। पर अघ सुनइ सहस दस काना॥ बहुरि सक्र सम बिनवउँ तेही। संतत सुरानीक हित जेही ॥
translation: पुनः उनको राजा पृथु (जिन्होंने भगवान का यश सुनने के लिए दस हजार कान माँगे थे) के समान जानकर प्रणाम करता हूँ, जो दस हजार कानों से दूसरों के पापों को सुनते हैं। फिर इन्द्र के समान मानकर उनकी विनय करता हूँ, जिनको सुरा (मदिरा) नीकी और हितकारी मालूम देती है (इन्द्र के लिए भी सुरानीक अर्थात् देवताओं की सेना हितकारी है) ॥
english_translation: I bow again to the one like King Prithu, who hears others' faults with ten thousand ears. I bow again to the one like Indra, to whom the hosts of the gods seem always beneficial.
essence: Corruption makes wrongdoing feel useful and other people's faults worth hearing.
simple_meaning: The poet is mocking a corrupt person: he listens eagerly to others' faults and treats harmful things as useful.
insight: It trains you to notice how craving can make bad things seem attractive and other people's flaws seem fascinating.
modern_relevance: A group chat fills with gossip, and one person leans in for every detail. What should have felt ugly starts feeling entertaining. This verse catches that slide before it hardens into habit.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: बचन बज्र जेहि सदा पिआरा। सहस नयन पर दोष निहारा ॥
translation: जिनको कठोर वचन रूपी वज्र सदा प्यारा लगता है और जो हजार आँखों से दूसरों के दोषों को देखते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who love harsh words like thunder and see others' faults with a thousand eyes.
essence: A cruel mind loves sharp speech and hunts for flaws.
simple_meaning: Evil people enjoy harsh speech and constantly scan others for flaws.
insight: It shifts attention from judging others to noticing the aggression behind judgment.
modern_relevance: A group chat turns sour, and one person keeps replying with sharp jabs and instant criticism. The habit is not just rude; it trains the mind to live on fault-finding.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: उदासीन अरि मीत हित सुनत जरहिं खल रीति। जानि पानि जुग जोरि जन बिनती करइ सप्रीति ॥
translation: दुष्टों की यह रीति है कि वे उदासीन, शत्रु अथवा मित्र, किसी का भी हित सुनकर जलते हैं। यह जानकर दोनों हाथ जोड़कर यह जन प्रेमपूर्वक उनसे विनय करता है ॥
english_translation: The wicked burn even at hearing good done to the indifferent, enemy, or friend. Knowing this, this person bows with both hands joined and speaks with love.
essence: Goodwill stays clean even when envy answers it.
simple_meaning: Wicked people resent good news no matter who receives it. Knowing that, the speaker still offers a loving, respectful plea.
insight: It teaches you to meet hostility with composure, not imitation, and to keep your own manners clean.
modern_relevance: You share good news in a family group chat, and one person immediately twists it into envy. You do not have to answer with the same heat; you can stay respectful and clear.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मैं अपनी दिसि कीन्ह निहोरा। तिन्ह निज ओर न लाउब भोरा॥ बायस पलिअहिं अति अनुरागा। होहिं निरामिष कबहुँ कि कागा ॥
translation: मैंने अपनी ओर से विनती की है, परन्तु वे अपनी ओर से कभी नहीं चूकेंगे। कौओं को बड़े प्रेम से पालिए, परन्तु वे क्या कभी मांस के त्यागी हो सकते हैं? ॥
english_translation: I have pleaded from my side, but they will never turn from theirs. Feed crows with great affection, but can crows ever become meatless?
essence: Kindness does not remake a fixed nature.
simple_meaning: A plea has been made, but stubborn people do not change. Affection cannot turn a crow into a meatless bird.
insight: It teaches you to stop expecting transformation where only habit and nature are ruling.
modern_relevance: You keep explaining yourself to someone who twists every word back into blame. At some point, clarity matters more than another attempt to be understood.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बंदउँ संत असज्जन चरना। दुःखप्रद उभय बीच कछु बरना॥ बिछुरत एक प्रान हरि लेहीं। मिलत एक दुख दारुन देहीं ॥
translation: अब मैं संत और असंत दोनों के चरणों की वन्दना करता हूँ, दोनों ही दुःख देने वाले हैं, परन्तु उनमें कुछ अन्तर कहा गया है। वह अंतर यह है कि एक (संत) तो बिछुड़ते समय प्राण हर लेते हैं और दूसरे (असंत) मिलते हैं, तब दारुण दुःख देते हैं। (अर्थात् संतों का बिछुड़ना मरने के समान दुःखदायी होता है और असंतों का मिलना।) ॥
english_translation: I bow to the feet of saints and the wicked alike. Both bring pain, yet in different ways: separation from a saint feels like losing one’s life, while meeting the wicked brings terrible suffering.
essence: The right company feels like life; the wrong company feels like injury.
simple_meaning: Saints and wicked people both affect you deeply, but in opposite ways. Losing the company of a saint feels unbearable, while meeting the wicked brings harsh suffering.
insight: It shifts attention toward the quality of association, not just the content of conversation.
modern_relevance: You leave a mentor’s house after an honest conversation and feel strangely hollow, then spend ten minutes with someone toxic and feel your chest tighten. Company changes the shape of the mind.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: उपजहिं एक संग जग माहीं। जलज जोंक जिमि गुन बिलगाहीं॥ सुधा सुरा सम साधु असाधू। जनक एक जग जलधि अगाधू ॥
translation: दोनों (संत और असंत) जगत में एक साथ पैदा होते हैं, पर (एक साथ पैदा होने वाले) कमल और जोंक की तरह उनके गुण अलग-अलग होते हैं। (कमल दर्शन और स्पर्श से सुख देता है, किन्तु जोंक शरीर का स्पर्श पाते ही रक्त चूसने लगती है।) साधु अमृत के समान (मृत्यु रूपी संसार से उबारने वाला) और असाधु मदिरा के समान (मोह, प्रमाद और जड़ता उत्पन्न करने वाला) है, दोनों को उत्पन्न करने वाला जगत रूपी अगाध समुद्र एक ही है। (शास्त्रों में समुद्रमन्थन से ही अमृत और मदिरा दोनों की उत्पत्ति बताई गई है।) ॥
english_translation: Saints and unholy people arise together in the world, yet their qualities differ like a lotus and a leech. The saint is like nectar and the unholy like liquor; both come from the same vast ocean of the world.
essence: Shared origin does not make shared character.
simple_meaning: Good and bad people can come from the same world, but their nature is completely different. One gives nourishment; the other drains and harms.
insight: It shifts attention from origin to nature, teaching you to judge by effect rather than by surface similarity.
modern_relevance: Two coworkers may come from the same office, the same training, even the same family culture. One leaves people steadier; the other leaves them depleted. Shared background never guarantees shared character.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भल अनभल निज निज करतूती। लहत सुजस अपलोक बिभूती॥ सुधा सुधाकर सुरसरि साधू। गरल अनल कलिमल सरि ब्याधू ॥ गुन अवगुन जानत सब कोई। जो जेहि भाव नीक तेहि सोई ॥
translation: भले और बुरे अपनी-अपनी करनी के अनुसार सुंदर यश और अपयश की सम्पत्ति पाते हैं। अमृत, चन्द्रमा, गंगाजी और साधु एवं विष, अग्नि, कलियुग के पापों की नदी अर्थात् कर्मनाशा और हिंसा करने वाला व्याध, इनके गुण-अवगुण सब कोई जानते हैं, किन्तु जिसे जो भाता है, उसे वही अच्छा लगता है॥4-5॥
english_translation: The good and the bad reap fame or disgrace according to their own deeds. Everyone knows the qualities and faults of nectar, the moon, the Ganges, the virtuous, poison, fire, the river of sins, and the hunter. Yet each person favors what pleases them.
essence: Knowing right from wrong does not stop desire from choosing.
simple_meaning: People receive praise or blame according to their own actions. Everyone knows what is good or harmful, yet they still prefer what suits their liking.
insight: It shifts attention from public opinion to the inner habit that keeps choosing what it already likes.
modern_relevance: You know the third late-night drink will wreck your sleep, yet you reach for it anyway. Clear seeing is not the same as clear choosing.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भलो भलाइहि पै लहइ लहइ निचाइहि नीचु। सुधा सराहिअ अमरताँ गरल सराहिअ मीचु ॥
translation: भला भलाई ही ग्रहण करता है और नीच नीचता को ही ग्रहण किए रहता है। अमृत की सराहना अमर करने में होती है और विष की मारने में ॥
english_translation: The good take in goodness; the lowly keep lowliness. Nectar is praised for making one immortal, poison for killing.
essence: Nature pulls in its own kind of result.
simple_meaning: A person tends to receive what matches their nature. Goodness leads to good results, while poison leads to harm.
insight: It shifts attention from blaming circumstances to examining the quality you are cultivating.
modern_relevance: You keep returning to the same kind of friends, the same habits, the same mess. What you nurture in yourself decides what your life keeps feeding back to you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: खल अघ अगुन साधु गुन गाहा। उभय अपार उदधि अवगाहा॥ तेहि तें कछु गुन दोष बखाने। संग्रह त्याग न बिनु पहिचाने ॥
translation: दुष्टों के पापों और अवगुणों की और साधुओं के गुणों की कथाएँ- दोनों ही अपार और अथाह समुद्र हैं। इसी से कुछ गुण और दोषों का वर्णन किया गया है, क्योंकि बिना पहचाने उनका ग्रहण या त्याग नहीं हो सकता ॥
english_translation: The tales of the wicked's faults and the saintly's virtues are both unfathomable oceans. So a few qualities and faults are described, because no one can accept or reject what is not recognized.
essence: Recognition must come before acceptance or rejection.
simple_meaning: Good and bad qualities are both vast and hard to fully measure. We name a few so people can know what to accept and what to avoid.
insight: It trains the mind to recognize patterns before making moral judgments or life choices.
modern_relevance: You meet someone polished in public and cruel in private, and your first impression wobbles. This verse says: don’t rush. Learn the signs before you trust, keep, or cut away.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भलेउ पोच सब बिधि उपजाए। गनि गुन दोष बेद बिलगाए॥ कहहिं बेद इतिहास पुराना। बिधि प्रपंचु गुन अवगुन साना ॥
translation: भले-बुरे सभी ब्रह्मा के पैदा किए हुए हैं, पर गुण और दोषों को विचार कर वेदों ने उनको अलग-अलग कर दिया है। वेद, इतिहास और पुराण कहते हैं कि ब्रह्मा की यह सृष्टि गुण-अवगुणों से सनी हुई है ॥
english_translation: The good and the bad are all created by Brahma, but the Vedas separate them by weighing their qualities and faults. The Vedas, Itihasa, and Puranas say that Brahma's creation is filled with qualities and faults.
essence: The world is mixed; clear seeing separates what is worth keeping from what is not.
simple_meaning: Creation contains both excellence and flaw. Sacred teaching does not deny that mix; it helps you see and sort it clearly.
insight: It trains the mind to distinguish mixed reality instead of reacting with simplistic praise or blame.
modern_relevance: You open a news app and feel everything is either heroic or corrupt. Then you remember: real life is mixed. Clear seeing means not flattening people, events, or yourself into one label.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: दुख सुख पाप पुन्य दिन राती। साधु असाधु सुजाति कुजाती॥ दानव देव ऊँच अरु नीचू। अमिअ सुजीवनु माहुरु मीचू ॥ माया ब्रह्म जीव जगदीसा। लच्छि अलच्छि रंक अवनीसा॥ कासी मग सुरसरि क्रमनासा। मरु मारव महिदेव गवासा ॥ सरग नरक अनुराग बिरागा। निगमागम गुन दोष बिभागा ॥
translation: दुःख-सुख, पाप-पुण्य, दिन-रात, साधु-असाधु, सुजाति-कुजाति, दानव-देवता, ऊँच-नीच, अमृत-विष, सुजीवन (सुंदर जीवन)-मृत्यु, माया-ब्रह्म, जीव-ईश्वर, सम्पत्ति-दरिद्रता, रंक-राजा, काशी-मगध, गंगा-कर्मनाशा, मारवाड़-मालवा, ब्राह्मण-कसाई, स्वर्ग-नरक, अनुराग-वैराग्य (ये सभी पदार्थ ब्रह्मा की सृष्टि में हैं।) वेद-शास्त्रों ने उनके गुण-दोषों का विभाग कर दिया है॥3-5॥
english_translation: Pain and pleasure, sin and merit, day and night, the good and the bad, noble birth and low birth, demons and radiant beings, high and low, nectar and poison, life-giving and deadly, illusion and the supreme reality, the individual and the lord of the world, wealth and poverty, beggar and king, Kashi and Magadh, the Ganga and the Karmanasha, Marwar and Malwa, priest and butcher, heaven and lower realm, attachment and detachment, all are part of creation. The Vedas and scriptures divide their qualities and faults.
essence: Opposites are built into creation; wisdom is learning their difference.
simple_meaning: The world contains every opposite: joy and sorrow, virtue and fault, wealth and poverty, attachment and detachment. Sacred teaching does not erase these pairs; it helps you recognize and distinguish them.
insight: It trains the mind to distinguish without denial: to see mixed reality clearly instead of demanding a world with only one side.
modern_relevance: You are scrolling through a feed where one post feels inspiring and the next feels cruel. Instead of collapsing into confusion, you can notice: both belong to the same world, but they are not the same thing.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जड़ चेतन गुन दोषमय बिस्व कीन्ह करतार। संत हंस गुन गहहिं पय परिहरि बारि बिकार ॥
translation: विधाता ने इस जड़-चेतन विश्व को गुण-दोषमय रचा है, किन्तु संत रूपी हंस दोष रूपी जल को छोड़कर गुण रूपी दूध को ही ग्रहण करते हैं ॥
english_translation: The creator made this world of inert and conscious beings, full of virtues and faults. Saints, like swans, take the milk and leave the water's impurities.
essence: Wisdom keeps the essence and leaves the impurity behind.
simple_meaning: The world contains both good and bad. Wise people notice the difference and hold on to what is valuable while letting the rest pass away.
insight: It trains the mind to separate value from noise instead of reacting to everything as equal.
modern_relevance: You open a comment thread full of praise, cruelty, half-truths, and one useful idea. You do not have to swallow all of it. Keep the useful part and let the rest sink.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अस बिबेक जब देइ बिधाता। तब तजि दोष गुनहिं मनु राता॥ काल सुभाउ करम बरिआईं। भलेउ प्रकृति बस चुकइ भलाईं ॥
translation: विधाता जब इस प्रकार का (हंस का सा) विवेक देते हैं, तब दोषों को छोड़कर मन गुणों में अनुरक्त होता है। काल स्वभाव और कर्म की प्रबलता से भले लोग (साधु) भी माया के वश में होकर कभी-कभी भलाई से चूक जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: When the creator grants this kind of clear seeing, the mind turns away from faults and rests in virtues. Yet time, nature, and the force of action are so strong that even good people sometimes miss the good and fall under appearance.
essence: Clear seeing helps, but even good people can still slip.
simple_meaning: Clear seeing lets the mind choose virtues over faults. But time, nature, and past action can still pull even good people off course.
insight: It teaches you to expect weakness without romanticising it, and to keep choosing what is good anyway.
modern_relevance: You meant well, but stress, habit, and old patterns still hijacked your best intentions. The verse names that failure without excuse, and without cruelty.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सो सुधारि हरिजन जिमि लेहीं। दलि दुख दोष बिमल जसु देहीं॥ खलउ करहिं भल पाइ सुसंगू। मिटइ न मलिन सुभाउ अभंगू ॥
translation: भगवान के भक्त जैसे उस चूक को सुधार लेते हैं और दुःख-दोषों को मिटाकर निर्मल यश देते हैं, वैसे ही दुष्ट भी कभी-कभी उत्तम संग पाकर भलाई करते हैं, परन्तु उनका कभी भंग न होने वाला मलिन स्वभाव नहीं मिटता ॥
english_translation: As devotees correct their faults and give pure fame by removing sorrow and defects, so even the wicked may do good in good company; yet their ingrained dark nature does not disappear.
essence: Good company can polish conduct, but it cannot instantly erase a hardened nature.
simple_meaning: Good company can help even bad people do some good, but a deeply rooted bad nature does not disappear quickly.
insight: It shifts attention from temporary improvement to the harder work of changing the underlying pattern.
modern_relevance: Someone can act decent at a retreat, in therapy, or around respected friends, then return home and fall back into the same pattern. Environment matters, but it does not erase the deeper habit overnight.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: लखि सुबेष जग बंचक जेऊ। बेष प्रताप पूजिअहिं तेऊ॥ उघरहिं अंत न होइ निबाहू। कालनेमि जिमि रावन राहू ॥
translation: जो (वेषधारी) ठग हैं, उन्हें भी अच्छा (साधु का सा) वेष बनाए देखकर वेष के प्रताप से जगत पूजता है, परन्तु एक न एक दिन वे चौड़े आ ही जाते हैं, अंत तक उनका कपट नहीं निभता, जैसे कालनेमि, रावण और राहु का हाल हुआ ॥
english_translation: People may honor a false appearance when they see a fine disguise, but deception cannot last. In the end, it is exposed, as with Kalanemi, Ravana, and Rahu.
essence: A pleasing disguise can win honor, but deception always breaks.
simple_meaning: A good-looking disguise can win respect for a while, but falsehood does not last. In time, deception is revealed.
insight: It trains you to look past appearances and judge by what remains when the mask slips.
modern_relevance: A charming speaker walks into the room in a crisp suit, says all the right things, and everyone relaxes. Weeks later, the pattern cracks. The image held for a while; the character did not.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: किएहुँ कुबेषु साधु सनमानू। जिमि जग जामवंत हनुमानू॥ हानि कुसंग सुसंगति लाहू। लोकहुँ बेद बिदित सब काहू ॥
translation: बुरा वेष बना लेने पर भी साधु का सम्मान ही होता है, जैसे जगत में जाम्बवान् और हनुमान् जी का हुआ। बुरे संग से हानि और अच्छे संग से लाभ होता है, यह बात लोक और वेद में है और सभी लोग इसको जानते हैं ॥
english_translation: Even a bad disguise still receives the honor due to a saint, as the world honored Jambavan and Hanuman. Loss comes from bad company, gain from good company. This is known in both worldly life and the Vedas.
essence: Company quietly shapes character more than appearance does.
simple_meaning: A person is shaped by the company they keep. Good company brings benefit; bad company brings harm.
insight: It shifts attention from judging appearances to noticing the moral force of relationships.
modern_relevance: You leave a room after two hours with one friend feeling lighter, and after two hours with another feeling strangely smaller. The verse names that difference: company is never neutral.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गगन चढ़इ रज पवन प्रसंगा। कीचहिं मिलइ नीच जल संगा॥ साधु असाधु सदन सुक सारीं। सुमिरहिं राम देहिं गनि गारीं ॥
translation: पवन के संग से धूल आकाश पर चढ़ जाती है और वही नीच (नीचे की ओर बहने वाले) जल के संग से कीचड़ में मिल जाती है। साधु के घर के तोता-मैना राम-राम सुमिरते हैं और असाधु के घर के तोता-मैना गिन-गिनकर गालियाँ देते हैं ॥
english_translation: Dust rises into the sky with the help of the wind, and mud forms when it joins low water. Parrots and mynas in the homes of the good keep repeating Ram's name, while parrots and mynas in the homes of the bad keep counting out insults.
essence: Association decides whether the same nature rises or sinks.
simple_meaning: The kind of company you keep changes how you speak, think, and live. Good company lifts you upward; bad company pulls you down.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated willpower to the quality of the environment you repeatedly enter.
modern_relevance: A child repeats the language heard at home. A group chat can make you kinder or crueler without you noticing. The verse warns that your surroundings are teaching you all the time.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: धूम कुसंगति कारिख होई। लिखिअ पुरान मंजु मसि सोई॥ सोइ जल अनल अनिल संघाता। होइ जलद जग जीवन दाता ॥
translation: कुसंग के कारण धुआँ कालिख कहलाता है, वही धुआँ (सुसंग से) सुंदर स्याही होकर पुराण लिखने के काम में आता है और वही धुआँ जल, अग्नि और पवन के संग से बादल होकर जगत को जीवन देने वाला बन जाता है ॥
english_translation: Through bad company, smoke becomes soot. In good use, that same soot becomes beautiful ink for writing the Puranas. The same smoke, joined with water, fire, and wind, becomes a cloud that gives life to the world.
essence: Association can stain, refine, or transform the same thing.
simple_meaning: Bad company turns a thing ugly and useless, but the same thing can become useful and life-giving in the right company.
insight: It shifts attention from judging things alone to seeing how company changes their effect.
modern_relevance: A friend group starts normalizing gossip, late-night chaos, and shortcuts. The same person who felt clear a month ago now feels dull and reactive. Environment is not background — it is formation.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: ग्रह भेजष जल पवन पट पाइ कुजोग सुजोग। होहिं कुबस्तु सुबस्तु जग लखहिं सुलच्छन लोग ॥
translation: ग्रह, औषधि, जल, वायु और वस्त्र- ये सब भी कुसंग और सुसंग पाकर संसार में बुरे और भले पदार्थ हो जाते हैं। चतुर एवं विचारशील पुरुष ही इस बात को जान पाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Planets, medicine, water, wind, and cloth become bad or good through bad company or good company. Wise people alone can see this.
essence: Association can turn even neutral things harmful or beneficial.
simple_meaning: Even neutral things can become harmful or helpful depending on the company they keep. Wise people understand how surroundings change character.
insight: It shifts attention from judging things in isolation to noticing the influence of surroundings and association.
modern_relevance: A calm habit breaks down after a few nights with people who mock it. A helpful routine suddenly feels toxic in a chaotic room. The verse reminds you that environment quietly edits character.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सम प्रकास तम पाख दुहुँ नाम भेद बिधि कीन्ह। ससि सोषक पोषक समुझि जग जस अपजस दीन्ह ॥
translation: महीने के दोनों पखवाड़ों में उजियाला और अँधेरा समान ही रहता है, परन्तु विधाता ने इनके नाम में भेद कर दिया है (एक का नाम शुक्ल और दूसरे का नाम कृष्ण रख दिया)। एक को चन्द्रमा का बढ़ाने वाला और दूसरे को उसका घटाने वाला समझकर जगत ने एक को सुयश और दूसरे को अपयश दे दिया ॥
english_translation: The bright half and the dark half are equal in light and darkness, yet the creator gave them different names. Seeing one as the moon’s nourisher and the other as its diminisher, the world gave one fame and the other blame.
essence: Names create praise and blame where nature is the same.
simple_meaning: Two halves of the month are equally light and dark, but people label one good and the other bad. The verse warns that reputation often comes from naming, not from real difference.
insight: It trains the mind to separate appearance from value and to question the stories society attaches to the same reality.
modern_relevance: A team meeting turns tense because one person is called a “leader” and another a “problem,” even though both are doing similar work. The verse asks you to look past the label before deciding what is actually true.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जड़ चेतन जग जीव जत सकल राममय जानि। बंदउँ सब के पद कमल सदा जोरि जुग पानि ॥
translation: जगत में जितने जड़ और चेतन जीव हैं, सबको राममय जानकर मैं उन सबके चरणकमलों की सदा दोनों हाथ जोड़कर वन्दना करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Knowing all inert and conscious beings in the world as filled with Ram, I always bow to the lotus feet of all with both hands joined.
essence: Seeing Ram everywhere turns every bow into worship.
simple_meaning: Everything in the world, living and non-living, is seen as filled with Ram, so the speaker bows to all beings with reverence.
insight: It shifts the mind from selective reverence to seeing the divine presence in everyone and everything.
modern_relevance: You are stuck in traffic, irritated by strangers, and then one small act of patience changes the whole mood. The person who cut you off is not outside the sacred field.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: देव दनुज नर नाग खग प्रेत पितर गंधर्ब। बंदउँ किंनर रजनिचर कृपा करहु अब सर्ब ॥
translation: देवता, दैत्य, मनुष्य, नाग, पक्षी, प्रेत, पितर, गंधर्व, किन्नर और निशाचर सबको मैं प्रणाम करता हूँ। अब सब मुझ पर कृपा कीजिए ॥
english_translation: I bow to the radiant beings, the shadow beings, humans, serpents, birds, spirits, ancestors, celestial singers, hidden beings, night-wanderers, and all others. May all now show me grace.
essence: Devotion becomes complete when no being is left outside respect.
simple_meaning: The speaker bows to every kind of being, from radiant beings to night-wanderers, and asks for their grace.
insight: It shifts the mind from selective respect to universal reverence for all forms of life.
modern_relevance: You walk through a crowded train station, irritated by strangers, workers, and noise. Then you remember that every face carries a life as real as yours. The hard edges soften.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: आकर चारि लाख चौरासी। जाति जीव जल थल नभ बासी॥ सीय राममय सब जग जानी। करउँ प्रनाम जोरि जुग पानी ॥
translation: चौरासी लाख योनियों में चार प्रकार के (स्वेदज, अण्डज, उद्भिज्ज, जरायुज) जीव जल, पृथ्वी और आकाश में रहते हैं, उन सबसे भरे हुए इस सारे जगत को श्री सीताराममय जानकर मैं दोनों हाथ जोड़कर प्रणाम करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: The world holds 8.4 million forms of life, dwelling in water, on land, and in the sky. Seeing all of creation filled with Sita and Ram, I bow with both hands joined.
essence: Everything alive becomes worthy of bowing when seen as filled with Ram and Sita.
simple_meaning: All forms of life across water, land, and sky are seen as filled with Sita and Ram, so the poet bows to all of creation.
insight: It shifts attention from classification to reverence, making every encounter feel sacred and equal.
modern_relevance: You step outside and notice pigeons, street dogs, ants, and people all sharing the same morning air. The mind softens when it stops ranking life and starts honouring it.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जानि कृपाकर किंकर मोहू। सब मिलि करहु छाड़ि छल छोहू॥ निज बुधि बल भरोस मोहि नाहीं। तातें बिनय करउँ सब पाहीं ॥
translation: मुझको अपना दास जानकर कृपा की खान आप सब लोग मिलकर छल छोड़कर कृपा कीजिए। मुझे अपने बुद्धि-बल का भरोसा नहीं है, इसीलिए मैं सबसे विनती करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Knowing me as your servant, O treasure of compassion, all of you together, leave aside deceit and pity me. I have no भरोसा in my own intelligence or strength, so I bow before everyone and ask for grace.
essence: Real devotion begins by dropping pride in your own power.
simple_meaning: The poet asks everyone to treat him as a humble servant and to show mercy. He admits he has no confidence in his own intelligence or strength, so he comes asking for help.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-confidence to humble receptivity before speaking or creating.
modern_relevance: You sit down to write, speak, or create, and the blank page feels bigger than your skill. The first honest move is not performance — it is admitting you need help.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: करन चहउँ रघुपति गुन गाहा। लघु मति मोरि चरित अवगाहा॥ सूझ न एकउ अंग उपाऊ। मन मति रंक मनोरथ राउ ॥
translation: मैं श्री रघुनाथजी के गुणों का वर्णन करना चाहता हूँ, परन्तु मेरी बुद्धि छोटी है और श्री रामजी का चरित्र अथाह है। इसके लिए मुझे उपाय का एक भी अंग अर्थात् कुछ (लेशमात्र) भी उपाय नहीं सूझता। मेरे मन और बुद्धि कंगाल हैं, किन्तु मनोरथ राजा है ॥
english_translation: I want to sing the qualities of Raghupati, but my intellect is small and Ram's character is unfathomable. No part of the method appears to me. My mind and understanding are poor, yet my aspiration is royal.
essence: Longing can be royal even when the mind feels poor.
simple_meaning: The poet wants to praise Ram, but he feels too limited to do it well. His desire is vast, yet he cannot see a clear way forward.
insight: It shifts the reader from self-confidence to humble inquiry before what is vast.
modern_relevance: You open a blank page before writing something that matters, then freeze because the subject feels larger than your skill. The reverence is real, and so is the fear of not measuring up.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मति अति नीच ऊँचि रुचि आछी। चहिअ अमिअ जग जुरइ न छाछी॥ छमिहहिं सज्जन मोरि ढिठाई। सुनिहहिं बालबचन मन लाई ॥
translation: मेरी बुद्धि तो अत्यन्त नीची है और चाह बड़ी ऊँची है, चाह तो अमृत पाने की है, पर जगत में जुड़ती छाछ भी नहीं। सज्जन मेरी ढिठाई को क्षमा करेंगे और मेरे बाल वचनों को मन लगाकर (प्रेमपूर्वक) सुनेंगे ॥
english_translation: My mind is very low, and my desire is very high. I seek nectar, but in this world even buttermilk does not mix. Good people will forgive my boldness and listen to my childish words with care.
essence: Humility can ask for nectar without pretending to deserve it.
simple_meaning: The speaker admits to having a humble mind but an elevated desire, and asks kind people to forgive the boldness and listen with affection.
insight: It teaches you to ask for grace before speaking, and to value longing over self-importance.
modern_relevance: You send the first draft anyway, even though you know it is rough. What matters is sincerity, not polish — and the right people can hear devotion beneath imperfect words.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जौं बालक कह तोतरि बाता। सुनहिं मुदित मन पितु अरु माता॥ हँसिहहिं कूर कुटिल कुबिचारी। जे पर दूषन भूषनधारी ॥
translation: जैसे बालक जब तोतले वचन बोलता है, तो उसके माता-पिता उन्हें प्रसन्न मन से सुनते हैं, किन्तु क्रूर, कुटिल और बुरे विचार वाले लोग जो दूसरों के दोषों को ही भूषण रूप से धारण किए रहते हैं (अर्थात् जिन्हें पराए दोष ही प्यारे लगते हैं), हँसेंगे ॥
english_translation: Like a child babbling with a lisp, parents listen with delight. Cruel, crooked, and ill-minded people laugh, feeding on others' faults.
essence: Love hears imperfection as sweetness; cruelty turns it into a joke.
simple_meaning: Good people listen to imperfect speech with affection, like parents hearing a child. Bad-minded people enjoy mocking and noticing faults in others.
insight: It trains you to read others with generosity and to notice when your own mind feeds on criticism.
modern_relevance: You send a half-finished message, then see the reply. One person understands what you meant; another circles the typo and misses your heart. This verse knows both kinds of readers.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: निज कबित्त केहि लाग न नीका। सरस होउ अथवा अति फीका॥ जे पर भनिति सुनत हरषाहीं। ते बर पुरुष बहुत जग नाहीं ॥
translation: रसीली हो या अत्यन्त फीकी, अपनी कविता किसे अच्छी नहीं लगती? किन्तु जो दूसरे की रचना को सुनकर हर्षित होते हैं, ऐसे उत्तम पुरुष जगत में बहुत नहीं हैं ॥
english_translation: What poem of one's own does not seem pleasing, whether sweet or extremely dull? But those who rejoice when hearing another's composition are rare indeed.
essence: True greatness can rejoice in another person's work.
simple_meaning: People naturally love their own work, no matter how good or bad it is. Truly noble people are the ones who can joyfully appreciate someone else's creation.
insight: It trains the mind to notice self-bias and replace comparison with sincere appreciation.
modern_relevance: You post something and keep checking for likes, secretly convinced it deserves more. Then a friend shares their work, and you can either compare or genuinely celebrate it. That response reveals the quality of your mind.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जग बहु नर सर सरि सम भाई। जे निज बाढ़ि बढ़हि जल पाई॥ सज्जन सकृत सिंधु सम कोई। देखि पूर बिधु बाढ़इ जोई ॥
translation: हे भाई! जगत में तालाबों और नदियों के समान मनुष्य ही अधिक हैं, जो जल पाकर अपनी ही बाढ़ से बढ़ते हैं (अर्थात् अपनी ही उन्नति से प्रसन्न होते हैं)। समुद्र सा तो कोई एक बिरला ही सज्जन होता है, जो चन्द्रमा को पूर्ण देखकर (दूसरों का उत्कर्ष देखकर) उमड़ पड़ता है ॥
english_translation: Most people are like ponds and rivers: they grow only when they receive water. Rare is the noble person like the ocean, who swells when the moon is full and others rise.
essence: Nobility is measured by joy in another's rise.
simple_meaning: Most people are pleased only when their own status grows. A rare noble person feels enlarged when someone else shines.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-comparison to spacious rejoicing in others' growth.
modern_relevance: Your colleague gets praised in the meeting, and your stomach tightens for a second. This verse asks whether their success can become your joy instead of your private defeat.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भाग छोट अभिलाषु बड़ करउँ एक बिस्वास। पैहहिं सुख सुनि सुजन सब खल करिहहिं उपहास ॥
translation: मेरा भाग्य छोटा है और इच्छा बहुत बड़ी है, परन्तु मुझे एक विश्वास है कि इसे सुनकर सज्जन सभी सुख पावेंगे और दुष्ट हँसी उड़ावेंगे ॥
english_translation: My means are small and my desire is great, but I have one confidence: hearing this, the good will feel joy, and the wicked will mock.
essence: Small means can still carry a great offering.
simple_meaning: The poet says his resources are limited, but he trusts that good people will find joy in hearing this work, while critics may laugh.
insight: It shifts attention from public approval to the response of the sincere reader.
modern_relevance: You post something sincere after weeks of work, then watch the comments split in two. Some people feel it deeply; others sneer. The verse says that is normal — keep going.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: खल परिहास होइ हित मोरा। काक कहहिं कलकंठ कठोरा॥ हंसहि बक दादुर चातकही। हँसहिं मलिन खल बिमल बतकही ॥
translation: किन्तु दुष्टों के हँसने से मेरा हित ही होगा। मधुर कण्ठ वाली कोयल को कौए तो कठोर ही कहा करते हैं। जैसे बगुले हंस को और मेंढक पपीहे को हँसते हैं, वैसे ही मलिन मन वाले दुष्ट निर्मल वाणी को हँसते हैं ॥
english_translation: The wicked's mockery becomes my benefit. The crow calls the cuckoo harsh, the heron mocks the swan, and the frog mocks the chatak. In the same way, impure minds laugh at pure speech.
essence: Mockery from the impure only confirms the purity of the words.
simple_meaning: Wicked people may mock pure speech, but their ridicule only proves their own limitation. The pure remain pure, just as birds with dull eyesight cannot judge beauty.
insight: It shifts attention from public approval to the quality of the listener and the purity of the message.
modern_relevance: You post something honest and a few cynical comments come in fast. Their sneers do not change the truth of what you said; they only show what kind of mind is reading it.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कबित रसिक न राम पद नेहू। तिन्ह कहँ सुखद हास रस एहू॥ भाषा भनिति भोरि मति मोरी। हँसिबे जो हँसें नहिं खोरी ॥
translation: जो न तो कविता के रसिक हैं और न जिनका श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में प्रेम है, उनके लिए भी यह कविता सुखद हास्यरस का काम देगी। प्रथम तो यह भाषा की रचना है, दूसरे मेरी बुद्धि भोली है, इससे यह हँसने के योग्य ही है, हँसने में उन्हें कोई दोष नहीं ॥
english_translation: Even those who do not delight in poetry or love Ram's feet may still find this verse pleasantly amusing. It is written in a simple tongue, and my mind is plain; laughing at it is no fault.
essence: Simple words can still carry devotion, and even laughter need not be a fault.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas says this verse may still amuse readers who do not care for poetry or love Ram. He calls his own language simple and says people may laugh without blame.
insight: It frames the coming story as accessible, lowering pride so the reader can receive it.
modern_relevance: You send a message to a group chat and worry it sounds too plain. Instead of defending it, you smile and let the words stand. Humility can open more doors than polish.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: प्रभु पद प्रीति न सामुझि नीकी। तिन्हहि कथा सुनि लागिहि फीकी॥ हरि हर पद रति मति न कुतर की। तिन्ह कहँ मधुर कथा रघुबर की ॥
translation: जिन्हें न तो प्रभु के चरणों में प्रेम है और न अच्छी समझ ही है, उनको यह कथा सुनने में फीकी लगेगी। जिनकी श्री हरि (भगवान विष्णु) और श्री हर (भगवान शिव) के चरणों में प्रीति है और जिनकी बुद्धि कुतर्क करने वाली नहीं है (जो श्री हरि-हर में भेद की या ऊँच-नीच की कल्पना नहीं करते), उन्हें श्री रघुनाथजी की यह कथा मीठी लगेगी ॥
english_translation: Those without love for the Lord's feet and without clear understanding find this story bland. Those whose hearts love Hari and Hara, and whose minds do not twist into clever arguments, find the story of Raghubar sweet.
essence: Devotion makes the same story taste sweet; argument makes it go flat.
simple_meaning: Ram's story feels dull to people without devotion or good understanding. But for those who love the divine and avoid twisted arguments, it becomes sweet.
insight: It shifts attention from judging the teaching to preparing the mind that hears it.
modern_relevance: You open a sacred talk with folded arms, ready to debate every line. Someone else listens with devotion and leaves quietly changed. The same words can taste flat or life-giving, depending on the mind that receives them.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: राम भगति भूषित जियँ जानी। सुनिहहिं सुजन सराहि सुबानी॥ कबि न होउँ नहिं बचन प्रबीनू। सकल कला सब बिद्या हीनू ॥
translation: सज्जनगण इस कथा को अपने जी में श्री रामजी की भक्ति से भूषित जानकर सुंदर वाणी से सराहना करते हुए सुनेंगे। मैं न तो कवि हूँ, न वाक्य रचना में ही कुशल हूँ, मैं तो सब कलाओं तथा सब विद्याओं से रहित हूँ ॥
english_translation: Knowing this tale to be adorned with devotion to Ram, the good will hear it and praise it in beautiful speech. I am no poet, nor skilled in wording; I am devoid of all arts and all learning.
essence: Devotion makes plain speech beautiful, even without poetic skill.
simple_meaning: Good people will hear this story as devotion to Ram, while the speaker humbly says he has no poetic skill or learning.
insight: It shifts attention from performance to sincerity, and from verbal skill to devotional intent.
modern_relevance: You post something heartfelt and worry it sounds clumsy. A friend reads it and feels the honesty immediately. That is the kind of beauty Tulsidas trusts here.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: आखर अरथ अलंकृति नाना। छंद प्रबंध अनेक बिधाना॥ भाव भेद रस भेद अपारा। कबित दोष गुन बिबिध प्रकारा ॥
translation: नाना प्रकार के अक्षर, अर्थ और अलंकार, अनेक प्रकार की छंद रचना, भावों और रसों के अपार भेद और कविता के भाँति-भाँति के गुण-दोष होते हैं ॥
english_translation: There are many kinds of letters, meanings, and ornaments; many kinds of meter and composition; countless shades of feeling and flavor; and many kinds of poetic faults and virtues.
essence: True devotion begins with admitting your limits.
simple_meaning: Poetry has many forms, styles, emotions, and qualities, both good and flawed. The speaker is admitting how vast and subtle the art of composition is.
insight: It shifts the mind from performance to honest self-assessment before speaking.
modern_relevance: You open a blank document and realise how much craft you do not yet own. Instead of pretending mastery, you name the gap honestly and begin anyway.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कबित बिबेक एक नहिं मोरें। सत्य कहउँ लिखि कागद कोरें ॥
translation: इनमें से काव्य सम्बन्धी एक भी बात का ज्ञान मुझमें नहीं है, यह मैं कोरे कागज पर लिखकर (शपथपूर्वक) सत्य-सत्य कहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I have no poetic discernment at all. I speak the truth, writing it on a blank sheet of paper.
essence: Truth matters more than poetic skill.
simple_meaning: The poet says he has no skill in poetry and is speaking honestly, with nothing hidden.
insight: It shifts the reader from performance to sincerity, valuing truth over display.
modern_relevance: Before a presentation, you admit you are not trying to impress anyone — only to be honest. That kind of plain speaking often lands deeper than polished performance.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भनिति मोरि सब गुन रहित बिस्व बिदित गुन एक। सो बिचारि सुनिहहिं सुमति जिन्ह कें बिमल बिबेक ॥
translation: मेरी रचना सब गुणों से रहित है, इसमें बस, जगत्प्रसिद्ध एक गुण है। उसे विचारकर अच्छी बुद्धिवाले पुरुष, जिनके निर्मल ज्ञान है, इसको सुनेंगे ॥
english_translation: My composition lacks every merit, yet it has one quality known throughout the world. Thinking of that, wise people with pure discernment will listen to it.
essence: Humility can hide the one quality that truly matters.
simple_meaning: The poet says his work has no literary merit, but it has one famous quality that wise readers will notice and hear it for that reason.
insight: It frames the text as modest in style but powerful in essence, inviting readers to look past surface flaws.
modern_relevance: You publish something you poured your heart into and still feel it is imperfect. A few careful readers may come for the polish, but stay for the one thing that feels true.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: एहि महँ रघुपति नाम उदारा। अति पावन पुरान श्रुति सारा॥ मंगल भवन अमंगल हारी। उमा सहित जेहि जपत पुरारी ॥
translation: इसमें श्री रघुनाथजी का उदार नाम है, जो अत्यन्त पवित्र है, वेद-पुराणों का सार है, कल्याण का भवन है और अमंगलों को हरने वाला है, जिसे पार्वतीजी सहित भगवान शिवजी सदा जपा करते हैं ॥
english_translation: In this, the noble name of Raghupati is supremely pure, the essence of the Puranas and the Vedas. It is a house of auspiciousness and the remover of inauspiciousness, and Lord Shiva, along with Uma, always chants it.
essence: Ram’s name itself carries purity, protection, and blessing.
simple_meaning: Ram’s name is pure, sacred, and powerful. It brings good and removes what is harmful, and even Shiva and Parvati repeat it.
insight: It shifts attention from outer rituals to the living power of remembrance.
modern_relevance: When the room feels heavy before a hard conversation, one steady phrase can change your whole center. Some names do that: they gather courage, clear fear, and remind you what is worth holding onto.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भनिति बिचित्र सुकबि कृत जोऊ। राम नाम बिनु सोह न सोउ॥ बिधुबदनी सब भाँति सँवारी। सोह न बसन बिना बर नारी ॥
translation: जो अच्छे कवि के द्वारा रची हुई बड़ी अनूठी कविता है, वह भी राम नाम के बिना शोभा नहीं पाती। जैसे चन्द्रमा के समान मुख वाली सुंदर स्त्री सब प्रकार से सुसज्जित होने पर भी वस्त्र के बिना शोभा नहीं देती ॥
english_translation: Even a beautifully crafted poem does not shine without Ram's name. A lovely woman, though adorned in every way, does not look complete without clothes.
essence: Ram's name is what makes beauty feel complete.
simple_meaning: Even the best poetry and the most beautiful appearance feel incomplete without Ram's name.
insight: It shifts attention from surface polish to the sacred center that gives form its meaning.
modern_relevance: You polish the slide, fix the lighting, and rehearse the speech one more time. Still, something feels missing until the purpose behind it is real.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सब गुन रहित कुकबि कृत बानी। राम नाम जस अंकित जानी॥ सादर कहहिं सुनहिं बुध ताही। मधुकर सरिस संत गुनग्राही ॥
translation: इसके विपरीत, कुकवि की रची हुई सब गुणों से रहित कविता को भी, राम के नाम एवं यश से अंकित जानकर, बुद्धिमान लोग आदरपूर्वक कहते और सुनते हैं, क्योंकि संतजन भौंरे की भाँति गुण ही को ग्रहण करने वाले होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Even a poem lacking all merit is honored when it bears Ram's name and praise. Wise people respectfully speak and listen to it, just as saints, like bees, gather only the sweetness of virtue.
essence: Ram's name can make even flawed words worthy of respect.
simple_meaning: Even weak poetry becomes worthy when it carries Ram's name and praise. Wise people focus on the good in it, not the defects.
insight: It shifts attention from surface flaws to the good hidden within speech, art, and people.
modern_relevance: You open a half-finished message someone sent at midnight and almost dismiss it because the writing is messy. Then one honest line lands and changes everything. Wisdom learns to catch that line.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जदपि कबित रस एकउ नाहीं। राम प्रताप प्रगट एहि माहीं॥ सोइ भरोस मोरें मन आवा। केहिं न सुसंग बड़प्पनु पावा ॥
translation: यद्यपि मेरी इस रचना में कविता का एक भी रस नहीं है, तथापि इसमें श्री रामजी का प्रताप प्रकट है। मेरे मन में यही एक भरोसा है। भले संग से भला, किसने बड़प्पन नहीं पाया? ॥
english_translation: Even if this poem has no poetic flavor at all, Ram's glory shines forth in it. That is the only confidence in my mind: who has not gained greatness through good company?
essence: Flawed words become radiant when Ram shines through them.
simple_meaning: The poet says his own writing may lack beauty, but Ram's greatness still shines through it. He trusts that good company lifts everything up.
insight: It shifts attention from technical perfection to the transforming force of noble company and divine presence.
modern_relevance: You send a rough draft, unsure it is good enough. Then one strong idea, one honest line, changes everything. The work is still yours, but its power comes from what it is near.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: धूमउ तजइ सहज करुआई। अगरु प्रसंग सुगंध बसाई॥ भनिति भदेस बस्तु भलि बरनी। राम कथा जग मंगल करनी ॥
translation: धुआँ भी अगर के संग से सुगंधित होकर अपने स्वाभाविक कड़ुवेपन को छोड़ देता है। मेरी कविता अवश्य भद्दी है, परन्तु इसमें जगत का कल्याण करने वाली रामकथा रूपी उत्तम वस्तु का वर्णन किया गया है। (इससे यह भी अच्छी ही समझी जाएगी।) ॥
english_translation: Smoke loses its natural bitterness beside incense and takes on fragrance. My verse may be crude, but it describes the noble story of Ram, which brings welfare to the world.
essence: Ram’s story makes even rough words fragrant.
simple_meaning: A rough poem becomes worthy because it carries Ram’s story. Just as smoke takes on fragrance near incense, this verse gains value from its holy subject.
insight: It shifts attention from polish to presence: the worth of expression comes from the devotion behind it.
modern_relevance: You send a clumsy message, then realize the apology mattered more than the wording. A sincere heart can make even rough speech feel clean.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मंगल करनि कलिमल हरनि तुलसी कथा रघुनाथ की। गति कूर कबिता सरित की ज्यों सरित पावन पाथ की॥ प्रभु सुजस संगति भनिति भलि होइहि सुजन मन भावनी भव अंग भूति मसान की सुमिरत सुहावनि पावनी॥
translation: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि श्री रघुनाथजी की कथा कल्याण करने वाली और कलियुग के पापों को हरने वाली है। मेरी इस भद्दी कविता रूपी नदी की चाल पवित्र जल वाली नदी (गंगाजी) की चाल की भाँति टेढ़ी है। प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी के सुंदर यश के संग से यह कविता सुंदर तथा सज्जनों के मन को भाने वाली हो जाएगी। श्मशान की अपवित्र राख भी श्री महादेवजी के अंग के संग से सुहावनी लगती है और स्मरण करते ही पवित्र करने वाली होती है।
english_translation: Tulsidas says: Rama's story brings auspiciousness and removes the impurities of this age. My crude poem moves like a crooked river, but the company of Rama's fame will make it pleasing to noble hearts. Even ashes from a cremation ground become lovely and purifying when remembered with Shiva.
essence: Rama's fame can make even rough words beautiful.
simple_meaning: Rama's story brings goodness and washes away the impurities of this age. Even a rough poem becomes beautiful when joined with his praise.
insight: It shifts attention from literary perfection to the transforming power of devotion.
modern_relevance: You send a clumsy message to someone you love, worried it sounds awkward. Then they reply warmly, because the feeling was real. That's the power Tulsidas trusts in Rama's name.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: दोहाः प्रिय लागिहि अति सबहि मम भनिति राम जस संग। दारु बिचारु कि करइ कोउ बंदिअ मलय प्रसंग ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के यश के संग से मेरी कविता सभी को अत्यन्त प्रिय लगेगी। जैसे मलय पर्वत के संग से काष्ठमात्र (चंदन बनकर) वंदनीय हो जाता है, फिर क्या कोई काठ (की तुच्छता) का विचार करता है? ॥
english_translation: My speech will become dear to everyone through the company of Ram's glory. Like ordinary wood honored by contact with the Malaya sandalwood mountain, who then thinks about its base nature?
essence: Ram's glory makes even plain speech worthy of love.
simple_meaning: A humble poem becomes beloved when it is joined to Ram's glory. Contact with greatness can make even something plain worthy of honor.
insight: It shifts attention from personal brilliance to the power of association with what is sacred and true.
modern_relevance: You send a rough draft late at night, worried it sounds ordinary. Then one sharp, honest line changes everything. The value was never just in polish; it was in what gave the words their life.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: स्याम सुरभि पय बिसद अति गुनद करहिं सब पान। गिरा ग्राम्य सिय राम जस गावहिं सुनहिं सुजान ॥
translation: श्यामा गो काली होने पर भी उसका दूध उज्ज्वल और बहुत गुणकारी होता है। यही समझकर सब लोग उसे पीते हैं। इसी तरह गँवारू भाषा में होने पर भी श्री सीतारामजी के यश को बुद्धिमान लोग बड़े चाव से गाते और सुनते हैं ॥
english_translation: Even a black cow's milk is pure and nourishing, so wise people drink it. In the same way, even though the language is simple, wise people gladly sing and hear the praise of Sita and Ram.
essence: Simple words become sacred when they carry loving praise.
simple_meaning: Even plain, rustic language becomes sweet and nourishing when it carries praise of Sita and Ram. Wise people do not reject the form; they receive the devotion within it.
insight: It shifts attention from literary elegance to the sincerity of what is being offered.
modern_relevance: You send a heartfelt message that is awkward, unedited, and maybe a little plain. The person who matters feels it anyway. Real care does not need perfect packaging to land.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मनि मानिक मुकुता छबि जैसी। अहि गिरि गज सिर सोह न तैसी॥ नृप किरीट तरुनी तनु पाई। लहहिं सकल सोभा अधिकाई ॥
translation: मणि, माणिक और मोती की जैसी सुंदर छबि है, वह साँप, पर्वत और हाथी के मस्तक पर वैसी शोभा नहीं पाती। राजा के मुकुट और नवयुवती स्त्री के शरीर को पाकर ही ये सब अधिक शोभा को प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Gems and pearls are not truly beautiful on a snake, a mountain, or an elephant's head. They gain greater splendour when placed on a king's crown or a young woman's body.
essence: Beauty appears fully only when placed where it belongs.
simple_meaning: A gem looks best when it belongs where it truly fits. Out of place, even something precious loses its beauty.
insight: It shifts attention from raw value to right placement and context.
modern_relevance: A talented person can look ordinary in the wrong role, then suddenly seem brilliant in the right team, room, or responsibility. Fit changes everything.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तैसेहिं सुकबि कबित बुध कहहीं। उपजहिं अनत अनत छबि लहहीं॥ भगति हेतु बिधि भवन बिहाई। सुमिरत सारद आवति धाई ॥
translation: इसी तरह, बुद्धिमान लोग कहते हैं कि सुकवि की कविता भी उत्पन्न और कहीं होती है और शोभा अन्यत्र कहीं पाती है (अर्थात कवि की वाणी से उत्पन्न हुई कविता वहाँ शोभा पाती है, जहाँ उसका विचार, प्रचार तथा उसमें कथित आदर्श का ग्रहण और अनुसरण होता है)। कवि के स्मरण करते ही उसकी भक्ति के कारण सरस्वतीजी ब्रह्मलोक को छोड़कर दौड़ी आती हैं ॥
english_translation: In the same way, wise poets say their poetry is born in one place and finds its beauty in another. Out of devotion, Saraswati leaves her abode and rushes down at the poet's remembrance.
essence: Devoted remembrance draws inspiration that the self cannot force.
simple_meaning: Good poetry takes shape in one place but shines in another. Because of devotion, Saraswati leaves her own abode and comes running when the poet remembers her.
insight: It shifts authorship from ego to devotion, showing that inspired speech comes when the mind remembers the divine.
modern_relevance: You stare at a blank page, then a line arrives that feels larger than you. The best work often feels borrowed from somewhere beyond effort, not forced from willpower.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: राम चरित सर बिनु अन्हवाएँ। सो श्रम जाइ न कोटि उपाएँ॥ कबि कोबिद अस हृदयँ बिचारी। गावहिं हरि जस कलि मल हारी ॥
translation: सरस्वतीजी की दौड़ी आने की वह थकावट रामचरित रूपी सरोवर में उन्हें नहलाए बिना दूसरे करोड़ों उपायों से भी दूर नहीं होती। कवि और पण्डित अपने हृदय में ऐसा विचारकर कलियुग के पापों को हरने वाले श्री हरि के यश का ही गान करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Only bathing in Ram's story can wash away this fatigue; no other effort of millions can remove it. Poets and scholars, reflecting this in their hearts, sing only the praises of Hari, who removes the stains of the age of conflict.
essence: Ram's story cleans what countless remedies cannot.
simple_meaning: Only Ram's story can wash away the weariness in the mind. Wise poets therefore sing Ram's praise, because it removes the stains of this difficult age.
insight: It shifts attention from external fixes to devotional listening and praise as real purification.
modern_relevance: You have tried podcasts, advice threads, and another self-help book, but the heaviness remains. Then a single hymn, prayer, or story settles something deeper than analysis ever could.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कीन्हें प्राकृत जन गुन गाना। सिर धुनि गिरा लगत पछिताना॥ हृदय सिंधु मति सीप समाना। स्वाति सारदा कहहिं सुजाना ॥
translation: संसारी मनुष्यों का गुणगान करने से सरस्वतीजी सिर धुनकर पछताने लगती हैं (कि मैं क्यों इसके बुलाने पर आई)। बुद्धिमान लोग हृदय को समुद्र, बुद्धि को सीप और सरस्वती को स्वाति नक्षत्र के समान कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: When ordinary people are praised, Saraswati shakes her head in regret. The wise say the heart is an ocean, the intellect is a shell, and Saraswati comes like the Swati star.
essence: True poetry appears when a receptive mind meets a vast heart.
simple_meaning: Praise of ordinary people is shallow. True poetry comes when the heart is vast, the mind is receptive, and inspiration arrives like rare rain.
insight: It shifts creativity from effortful performance to receptive depth.
modern_relevance: You stare at a blank page after ten half-finished drafts, trying to force brilliance. The line finally arrives only when your mind settles enough to receive it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जौं बरषइ बर बारि बिचारू। हो हिं कबित मुकुतामनि चारू ॥
translation: इसमें यदि श्रेष्ठ विचार रूपी जल बरसता है तो मुक्ता मणि के समान सुंदर कविता होती है ॥
english_translation: If rich thought rains down, poetry becomes a beautiful pearl necklace.
essence: Deep thought turns poetry into something precious.
simple_meaning: When deep thought flows into poetry, the result is something beautiful and precious, like pearls.
insight: It shifts attention from clever wording to the depth of thought beneath the wording.
modern_relevance: A speech full of polished lines can still feel empty. But when someone has truly thought through what they are saying, even a short message lands with weight and beauty.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जुगुति बेधि पुनि पोहिअहिं रामचरित बर ताग। पहिरहिं सज्जन बिमल उर सोभा अति अनुराग ॥
translation: उन कविता रूपी मुक्तामणियों को युक्ति से बेधकर फिर रामचरित्र रूपी सुंदर तागे में पिरोकर सज्जन लोग अपने निर्मल हृदय में धारण करते हैं, जिससे अत्यन्त अनुराग रूपी शोभा होती है (वे आत्यन्तिक प्रेम को प्राप्त होते हैं) ॥
english_translation: Wise readers thread those pearl-like verses onto the beautiful string of Ram's story and wear them in their pure hearts, where they blossom as deep love.
essence: Ram's story turns beautiful words into living devotion.
simple_meaning: Good people take beautiful verses, connect them with Ram's story, and keep them in a pure heart. That turns poetry into deep love.
insight: It shifts reading from collecting clever lines to letting sacred meaning reshape the heart.
modern_relevance: You save a line on your phone because it touched something real. Later, it matters only if it changes how you speak, choose, and love.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जे जनमे कलिकाल कराला। करतब बायस बेष मराला॥ चलत कुपंथ बेद मग छाँड़े। कपट कलेवर कलि मल भाँड़े ॥
translation: जो कराल कलियुग में जन्मे हैं, जिनकी करनी कौए के समान है और वेष हंस का सा है, जो वेदमार्ग को छोड़कर कुमार्ग पर चलते हैं, जो कपट की मूर्ति और कलियुग के पापों के भाँड़ें हैं ॥
english_translation: Those born in the terrible age of Kali act like crows but dress like swans. They walk the wrong path, abandon the Vedas, and become masks of deceit and vessels of the age's corruption.
essence: False holiness hides corruption, but conduct always reveals the mask.
simple_meaning: People can look noble while acting corrupt. They reject right conduct, follow the wrong path, and become full of deceit.
insight: It trains you to judge character by conduct, not costume.
modern_relevance: A polished speech, a clean profile picture, and the right vocabulary can still hide selfish motives. The real test is whether someone's conduct matches their appearance.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: बंचक भगत कहाइ राम के। किंकर कंचन कोह काम के॥ तिन्ह महँ प्रथम रेख जग मोरी। धींग धरम ध्वज धंधक धोरी ॥
translation: जो श्री रामजी के भक्त कहलाकर लोगों को ठगते हैं, जो धन (लोभ), क्रोध और काम के गुलाम हैं और जो धींगाधींगी करने वाले, धर्मध्वजी (धर्म की झूठी ध्वजा फहराने वाले दम्भी) और कपट के धन्धों का बोझ ढोने वाले हैं, संसार के ऐसे लोगों में सबसे पहले मेरी गिनती है ॥
english_translation: I count myself first among the world’s hypocrites: those who call themselves Ram’s devotees while deceiving others, those enslaved by greed, anger, and desire, and those who wear the banner of dharma while carrying the burden of deceit.
essence: Pretended devotion collapses under greed, anger, desire, and deceit.
simple_meaning: False devotion is exposed here. People may wear the name of Ram, but greed, anger, desire, pride, and deceit reveal what they really serve.
insight: It shifts attention from public appearance to private motive, asking the reader to examine whether devotion is real or only performed.
modern_relevance: You post a quote about values, then snap at your family five minutes later. The gap between image and impulse is exactly what this verse refuses to hide.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जौं अपने अवगुन सब कहऊँ। बाढ़इ कथा पार नहिं लहऊँ ॥ ताते मैं अति अलप बखाने। थोरे महुँ जानिहहिं सयाने ॥
translation: यदि मैं अपने सब अवगुणों को कहने लगूँ तो कथा बहुत बढ़ जाएगी और मैं पार नहीं पाऊँगा। इससे मैंने बहुत कम अवगुणों का वर्णन किया है। बुद्धिमान लोग थोड़े ही में समझ लेंगे ॥
english_translation: If I were to tell all my faults, the story would grow too long and I would never finish. So I have described only a few. Wise people will understand from so little.
essence: A few clear examples can carry a whole warning.
simple_meaning: The speaker says he has only mentioned a few faults because listing every fault would make the story endless. Wise readers will understand the point from the small amount said.
insight: It teaches the reader to state the essential point without drowning it in excess detail.
modern_relevance: You write a long message pointing out what went wrong, then delete half of it because the point is already clear. Sometimes restraint makes a criticism sharper, not weaker.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: समुझि बिबिधि बिधि बिनती मोरी। कोउ न कथा सुनि देइहि खोरी॥ एतेहु पर करिहहिं जे असंका। मोहि ते अधिक ते जड़ मति रंका ॥
translation: मेरी अनेकों प्रकार की विनती को समझकर, कोई भी इस कथा को सुनकर दोष नहीं देगा। इतने पर भी जो शंका करेंगे, वे तो मुझसे भी अधिक मूर्ख और बुद्धि के कंगाल हैं ॥
english_translation: Understanding my many kinds of humble request, no one will fault this story. Even so, whoever still doubts it is more foolish than I am, poor in understanding.
essence: Humble speech asks for trust before criticism.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he has already asked humbly, so no fair listener should criticize the story. Anyone who still doubts it is being foolish.
insight: It shifts the reader from suspicion to receptive listening before the story unfolds.
modern_relevance: You share something tender and personal, and before anyone has even finished reading, they start picking at it. This verse asks for a fair hearing before judgment.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कबि न होउँ नहिं चतुर कहावउँ। मति अनुरूप राम गुन गावउँ॥ कहँ रघुपति के चरित अपारा। कहँ मति मोरि निरत संसारा ॥
translation: मैं न तो कवि हूँ, न चतुर कहलाता हूँ, अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार श्री रामजी के गुण गाता हूँ। कहाँ तो श्री रघुनाथजी के अपार चरित्र, कहाँ संसार में आसक्त मेरी बुद्धि ! ॥।
english_translation: I am neither a poet nor one to be called clever; I sing Ram's virtues according to my own understanding. Where are the endless deeds of Raghupati, and where is my mind, still tied to the world?
essence: Great praise begins with admitting your own smallness.
simple_meaning: The poet says he is not a great scholar; he can only sing Ram's boundless virtues as best as he understands them, while knowing his own mind is still worldly and limited.
insight: It shifts expression from self-display to sincere offering, so the focus stays on Ram rather than the speaker.
modern_relevance: You sit down to write, present, or pray, and immediately feel unqualified. Instead of pretending expertise, you begin honestly from your actual understanding — and that honesty makes the work truer.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जेहिं मारुत गिरि मेरु उड़ाहीं। कहहु तूल केहि लेखे माहीं॥ समुझत अमित राम प्रभुताई। करत कथा मन अति कदराई ॥
translation: जिस हवा से सुमेरु जैसे पहाड़ उड़ जाते हैं, कहिए तो, उसके सामने रूई किस गिनती में है। श्री रामजी की असीम प्रभुता को समझकर कथा रचने में मेरा मन बहुत हिचकता है- ॥
english_translation: The wind that can lift Mount Meru can make cotton count for nothing. Understanding Ram's immeasurable greatness, my mind hesitates to tell this story.
essence: Ram's greatness makes even the storyteller fall silent.
simple_meaning: Ram's greatness is beyond measure, so the poet feels too small and hesitant to describe it fully.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to master the subject to approaching it with humility and awe.
modern_relevance: You sit down to write about someone who changed your life, and every sentence feels too small. The hesitation itself is respect; not everything sacred can be captured cleanly.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सारद सेस महेस बिधि आगम निगम पुरान। नेति नेति कहि जासु गुन करहिं निरंतर गान ॥
translation: सरस्वतीजी, शेषजी, शिवजी, ब्रह्माजी, शास्त्र, वेद और पुराण- ये सब 'नेति-नेति' कहकर (पार नहीं पाकर 'ऐसा नहीं', ऐसा नहीं कहते हुए) सदा जिनका गुणगान किया करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Saraswati, Shesha, Shiva, Brahma, the scriptures, the Vedas, and the Puranas all sing endlessly of the one whose qualities they describe only by saying, 'not this, not this.'
essence: The greatest praise is knowing words cannot contain him.
simple_meaning: Even the greatest beings and the sacred texts can only point to Ram indirectly. His qualities are so vast that they keep praising him without ever exhausting him.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to define the divine to staying in humble, endless praise.
modern_relevance: You try to explain someone you love, and every sentence feels too small. That frustration is not failure; it is a sign that the thing you are touching is larger than your words.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सब जानत प्रभु प्रभुता सोई। तदपि कहें बिनु रहा न कोई॥ तहाँ बेद अस कारन राखा। भजन प्रभाउ भाँति बहु भाषा ॥
translation: यद्यपि प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी की प्रभुता को सब ऐसी (अकथनीय) ही जानते हैं, तथापि कहे बिना कोई नहीं रहा। इसमें वेद ने ऐसा कारण बताया है कि भजन का प्रभाव बहुत तरह से कहा गया है। (अर्थात भगवान की महिमा का पूरा वर्णन तो कोई कर नहीं सकता, परन्तु जिससे जितना बन पड़े उतना भगवान का गुणगान करना चाहिए, क्योंकि भगवान के गुणगान रूपी भजन का प्रभाव बहुत ही अनोखा है, उसका नाना प्रकार से शास्त्रों में वर्णन है। थोड़ा सा भी भगवान का भजन मनुष्य को सहज ही भवसागर से तार देता है) ॥
english_translation: Everyone knows the Lord's greatness, yet no one can stop speaking of it. The Vedas give the reason: praise has many forms and great power.
essence: Ram's greatness overflows into praise, and praise itself changes the one who speaks.
simple_meaning: Everyone already knows Ram's greatness, yet people still keep speaking of it. The scriptures say praise itself has many forms and great power.
insight: It shifts devotion from a duty to a living force that keeps deepening through speech.
modern_relevance: You hear a song that reminds you of someone you miss, and you play it again. Not because the feeling is unfinished, but because love keeps finding new words. Ram's praise works the same way.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: एक अनीह अरूप अनामा। अज सच्चिदानंद पर धामा॥ ब्यापक बिस्वरूप भगवाना। तेहिं धरि देह चरित कृत नाना ॥
translation: जो परमेश्वर एक है, जिनके कोई इच्छा नहीं है, जिनका कोई रूप और नाम नहीं है, जो अजन्मा, सच्चिदानन्द और परमधाम है और जो सबमें व्यापक एवं विश्व रूप हैं, उन्हीं भगवान ने दिव्य शरीर धारण करके नाना प्रकार की लीला की है ॥
english_translation: The one supreme being has no desire, no form, and no name. Unborn, pure awareness and bliss, the supreme abode, all-pervading and universal in form, that divine one takes a body and performs many plays.
essence: The formless one enters form without losing anything.
simple_meaning: Ram is beyond form, name, and desire, yet he enters the world in a body and acts in many ways.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing divinity as remote to seeing it as present within lived action.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary at first, then realize their calm changes the whole room. Ram's greatness works like that: the limitless can still arrive in a visible, human way.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सो केवल भगतन हित लागी। परम कृपाल प्रनत अनुरागी॥ जेहि जन पर ममता अति छोहू। जेहिं करुना करि कीन्ह न कोहू ॥
translation: वह लीला केवल भक्तों के हित के लिए ही है, क्योंकि भगवान परम कृपालु हैं और शरणागत के बड़े प्रेमी हैं। जिनकी भक्तों पर बड़ी ममता और कृपा है, जिन्होंने एक बार जिस पर कृपा कर दी, उस पर फिर कभी क्रोध नहीं किया ॥
english_translation: That play exists only for the sake of devotees. The supreme compassionate one loves those who surrender. He holds deep affection for his people, and once he shows mercy, he never turns to anger again.
essence: Ram’s mercy is for the surrendered, and it does not turn back.
simple_meaning: Ram's divine play is meant for devotees. He is deeply loving toward those who surrender, and once he shows kindness, he does not turn hostile again.
insight: It shifts devotion from fear to trust by showing that grace, once given, is not revoked.
modern_relevance: After you finally admit you need help, the person who stays patient instead of shaming you changes everything. This verse points to a love that meets surrender with warmth, not punishment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गई बहोर गरीब नेवाजू। सरल सबल साहिब रघुराजू॥ बुध बरनहिं हरि जस अस जानी। करहिं पुनीत सुफल निज बानी ॥
translation: वे प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी गई हुई वस्तु को फिर प्राप्त कराने वाले, गरीब नवाज (दीनबन्धु), सरल स्वभाव, सर्वशक्तिमान और सबके स्वामी हैं। यही समझकर बुद्धिमान लोग उन श्री हरि का यश वर्णन करके अपनी वाणी को पवित्र और उत्तम फल (मोक्ष और दुर्लभ भगवत्प्रेम) देने वाली बनाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Lord Raghunath restores what is lost. Gentle, mighty, and sovereign, Hari is praised by the wise, and that praise purifies speech and bears great fruit.
essence: Praise of Ram purifies speech and turns words fruitful.
simple_meaning: Ram is gentle, powerful, and kind to the poor. Wise people praise his glory, and that praise purifies their speech and gives it lasting fruit.
insight: It shifts speech from noise to devotion, making words an offering instead of a habit.
modern_relevance: After a day of talking too much, you hear yourself repeat complaints, gossip, and half-truths. Then one honest prayer or remembrance of Ram changes the whole tone of your voice.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहिं बल मैं रघुपति गुन गाथा। कहिहउँ नाइ राम पद माथा॥ मुनिन्ह प्रथम हरि कीरति गाई। तेहिं मग चलत सुगम मोहि भाई ॥
translation: उसी बल से (महिमा का यथार्थ वर्णन नहीं, परन्तु महान फल देने वाला भजन समझकर भगवत्कृपा के बल पर ही) मैं श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर श्री रघुनाथजी के गुणों की कथा कहूँगा। इसी विचार से (वाल्मीकि, व्यास आदि) मुनियों ने पहले हरि की कीर्ति गाई है। भाई! उसी मार्ग पर चलना मेरे लिए सुगम होगा ॥
english_translation: By that power alone I will sing the praises of Raghupati, bowing my head at Ram's feet. The sages first sang Hari's glory; following that path makes it easy for me too.
essence: True praise begins with bowed head, not clever speech.
simple_meaning: The poet says he can speak of Ram only by Ram's grace. He bows first, then follows the path the sages used: praising the divine before trying to describe it.
insight: It shifts speech from self-confidence to reverent dependence, so the words feel received rather than manufactured.
modern_relevance: Before you explain something sacred, personal, or deeply important, you pause. You don't rush to sound clever; you begin with respect, because some words only come cleanly after humility.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अति अपार जे सरित बर जौं नृप सेतु कराहिं। चढ़ि पिपीलिकउ परम लघु बिनु श्रम पारहि जाहिं ॥
translation: जो अत्यन्त बड़ी श्रेष्ठ नदियाँ हैं, यदि राजा उन पर पुल बँधा देता है, तो अत्यन्त छोटी चींटियाँ भी उन पर चढ़कर बिना ही परिश्रम के पार चली जाती हैं। (इसी प्रकार मुनियों के वर्णन के सहारे मैं भी श्री रामचरित्र का वर्णन सहज ही कर सकूँगा) ॥
english_translation: If a king builds a bridge over vast rivers, even tiny ants cross them without effort.
essence: A great bridge lets even the smallest cross without strain.
simple_meaning: A great bridge makes crossing huge rivers easy, even for the smallest creature. In the same way, a wise helper can make a huge task feel possible.
insight: It shifts attention from personal strength to enabling conditions that make action possible.
modern_relevance: You open a document that once felt impossible, and the right template is already there. What looked overwhelming becomes manageable because someone built the bridge before you arrived.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: एहि प्रकार बल मनहि देखाई। करिहउँ रघुपति कथा सुहाई॥ ब्यास आदि कबि पुंगव नाना। जिन्ह सादर हरि सुजस बखाना ॥
translation: इस प्रकार मन को बल दिखलाकर मैं श्री रघुनाथजी की सुहावनी कथा की रचना करूँगा। व्यास आदि जो अनेकों श्रेष्ठ कवि हो गए हैं, जिन्होंने बड़े आदर से श्री हरि का सुयश वर्णन किया है ॥
english_translation: In this way, I steady my mind and will compose the lovely story of Raghupati. Vyasa and many other great poets have respectfully sung Hari's fame.
essence: Humility steadies the mind before sacred work begins.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he will steady his mind and then tell Ram's beautiful story, following the example of great poets who praised Hari with reverence.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to disciplined humility before creative work.
modern_relevance: Before starting a difficult project, you take a breath, collect yourself, and remember the people who did it well before you. That steadies your hand more than raw confidence ever could.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: चरन कमल बंदउँ तिन्ह केरे। पुरवहुँ सकल मनोरथ मेरे॥ कलि के कबिन्ह करउँ परनामा। जिन्ह बरने रघुपति गुन ग्रामा ॥
translation: मैं उन सब (श्रेष्ठ कवियों) के चरणकमलों में प्रणाम करता हूँ, वे मेरे सब मनोरथों को पूरा करें। कलियुग के भी उन कवियों को मैं प्रणाम करता हूँ, जिन्होंने श्री रघुनाथजी के गुण समूहों का वर्णन किया है ॥
english_translation: I bow to the feet of those poets; may they fulfill all my desires. I bow to the poets of Kali Yuga who have described the virtues and hosts of Raghupati.
essence: True devotion begins by honoring those who kept Ram's name alive.
simple_meaning: The poet bows to earlier poets who praised Ram, asking their blessings. He also honors the poets of the present age who have sung Ram's virtues.
insight: It shifts creation from self-display to reverent participation in a shared tradition.
modern_relevance: You open a book, an essay, or a song and remember it did not begin with you. Someone else cleared the path, and gratitude makes your own work cleaner.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जे प्राकृत कबि परम सयाने। भाषाँ जिन्ह हरि चरित बखाने॥ भए जे अहहिं जे होइहहिं आगें। प्रनवउँ सबहि कपट सब त्यागें ॥
translation: जो बड़े बुद्धिमान प्राकृत कवि हैं, जिन्होंने भाषा में हरि चरित्रों का वर्णन किया है, जो ऐसे कवि पहले हो चुके हैं, जो इस समय वर्तमान हैं और जो आगे होंगे, उन सबको मैं सारा कपट त्यागकर प्रणाम करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I bow to all poets without deceit: the wise earthly poets who have described Hari's deeds in language, those who have lived before, those who live now, and those who will come after.
essence: Humility honors every true voice before it speaks.
simple_meaning: The poet bows to every sincere poet who has ever described Ram's deeds, past, present, and future, and does so without any deceit or ego.
insight: It shifts authorship from self-display to gratitude and lineage.
modern_relevance: Before you publish the article, post the poem, or launch the project, you remember the people who taught you how to do it. The work feels cleaner when ego steps aside.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: होहु प्रसन्न देहु बरदानू। साधु समाज भनिति सनमानू॥ जो प्रबंध बुध नहिं आदरहीं। सो श्रम बादि बाल कबि करहीं ॥
translation: आप सब प्रसन्न होकर यह वरदान दीजिए कि साधु समाज में मेरी कविता का सम्मान हो, क्योंकि बुद्धिमान लोग जिस कविता का आदर नहीं करते, मूर्ख कवि ही उसकी रचना का व्यर्थ परिश्रम करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Be pleased and grant this boon: let the noble community honor this poem. Wise people do not respect a composition, so foolish poets labor in vain.
essence: A work matters when the wise can honor it.
simple_meaning: The poet asks for a blessing: may thoughtful people honor this poem, because writing that no wise person values is wasted effort.
insight: It shifts attention from applause to worthy reception, and from vanity to sincere offering.
modern_relevance: You finish something deeply personal and send it into the world, not knowing whether anyone will understand it. The verse carries that quiet hope: let the right people receive what you made.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कीरति भनिति भूति भलि सोई। सुरसरि सम सब कहँ हित होई॥ राम सुकीरति भनिति भदेसा। असमंजस अस मोहि अँदेसा ॥
translation: कीर्ति, कविता और सम्पत्ति वही उत्तम है, जो गंगाजी की तरह सबका हित करने वाली हो। श्री रामचन्द्रजी की कीर्ति तो बड़ी सुंदर (सबका अनन्त कल्याण करने वाली ही) है, परन्तु मेरी कविता भद्दी है। यह असामंजस्य है (अर्थात इन दोनों का मेल नहीं मिलता), इसी की मुझे चिन्ता है ॥
english_translation: Good fame, good speech, and good wealth are only those that benefit everyone like the Ganga. Ram's fame is truly beautiful, but my poetry is crude. That mismatch troubles me.
essence: True worth helps everyone; anything else is only decoration.
simple_meaning: Only fame, speech, and wealth that help everyone are truly good. Ram's glory is pure and beneficial, but the poet feels his own words fall short of that standard.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to usefulness: value is what blesses others, not what flatters the maker.
modern_relevance: You publish something heartfelt and then reread it at midnight, noticing every rough edge. The gap between what you meant and what you made can sting — but it can also keep you honest.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तुम्हरी कृपाँ सुलभ सोउ मोरे। सिअनि सुहावनि टाट पटोरे ॥
translation: परन्तु हे कवियों! आपकी कृपा से यह बात भी मेरे लिए सुलभ हो सकती है। रेशम की सिलाई टाट पर भी सुहावनी लगती है ॥
