english_translation: Lord Ram, who sees everything and knows every heart, understood Sati's deception. By remembering Him, ignorance is destroyed. He is the all-knowing, glorious Ram.
essence: Ram's clear seeing ends deception and ignorance at once.
simple_meaning: Ram sees through Sati's disguise because He knows every heart. Remembering Him removes ignorance, because He is fully aware of all things.
insight: It shifts attention from concealment to inner honesty, showing that remembrance of Ram dissolves confusion at its root.
modern_relevance: You rehearse a lie in your head before a difficult conversation, then feel exposed the moment the other person looks at you calmly. This verse says clear seeing can strip away the mask before words even begin.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सती कीन्ह चह तहँहुँ दुराऊ। देखहु नारि सुभाव प्रभाऊ॥ निज माया बलु हृदयँ बखानी। बोले बिहसि रामु मृदु बानी ॥
translation: स्त्री स्वभाव का असर तो देखो कि वहाँ (उन सर्वज्ञ भगवान् के सामने) भी सतीजी छिपाव करना चाहती हैं। अपनी माया के बल को हृदय में बखानकर, श्री रामचंद्रजी हँसकर कोमल वाणी से बोले ॥
english_translation: Sati still tried to hide it there too. See the power of a woman's nature. Ram smiled softly and spoke, saying in his heart that this was the strength of his own illusion.
essence: No disguise survives clear seeing.
simple_meaning: Sati still tried to conceal herself, and Ram gently recognized that this was the force of his own illusion at work.
insight: It shifts the mind from clever concealment to honest recognition of what is already visible.
modern_relevance: You rehearse a harmless excuse in your head before speaking, but the other person already senses the dodge. Ram's calm seeing cuts through the mask without cruelty.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जोरि पानि प्रभु कीन्ह प्रनामू। पिता समेत लीन्ह निज नामू॥ कहेउ बहोरि कहाँ बृषकेतू। बिपिन अकेलि फिरहु केहि हेतू ॥
translation: पहले प्रभु ने हाथ जोड़कर सती को प्रणाम किया और पिता सहित अपना नाम बताया। फिर कहा कि वृषकेतु शिवजी कहाँ हैं? आप यहाँ वन में अकेली किसलिए फिर रही हैं? ॥
english_translation: The Lord bowed with joined hands and gave his name along with his father’s. Then he asked, “Where is Shiva, the Bull-bannered one? Why do you wander alone in the forest?”
essence: Grace answers suspicion without losing composure.
simple_meaning: Ram respectfully greets Sati, identifies himself through his father, and asks where Shiva is and why she is alone in the forest.
insight: It teaches you to keep dignity and courtesy even when others are testing you.
modern_relevance: Someone questions you in a guarded tone, and you can feel the tension rise. You still answer with respect, stay composed, and ask the real question underneath the surface.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: राम बचन मृदु गूढ़ सुनि उपजा अति संकोचु। सती सभीत महेस पहिं चलीं हृदयँ बड़ सोचु ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के कोमल और रहस्य भरे वचन सुनकर सतीजी को बड़ा संकोच हुआ। वे डरती हुई (चुपचाप) शिवजी के पास चलीं, उनके हृदय में बड़ी चिन्ता हो गई ॥
english_translation: Hearing Ram's gentle, veiled words, Sati felt deep shame. Fearful, she went to Mahesh, her heart full of worry.
essence: Hidden doubt turns into shame when clear seeing meets it.
simple_meaning: Sati hears Ram's calm, subtle words and feels embarrassed and uneasy. She goes back to Shiva with fear and heavy worry in her heart.
insight: It shows how concealment collapses under clear seeing, pushing the mind into shame and self-correction.
modern_relevance: You send a message trying to hide your real doubt, and the reply lands too cleanly. Suddenly your own pretence feels loud. The heart knows when it has been seen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मैं संकर कर कहा न माना। निज अग्यानु राम पर आना॥ जाइ उतरु अब देहउँ काहा। उर उपजा अति दारुन दाहा ॥
translation: कि मैंने शंकरजी का कहना न माना और अपने अज्ञान का श्री रामचन्द्रजी पर आरोप किया। अब जाकर मैं शिवजी को क्या उत्तर दूँगी? (यों सोचते-सोचते) सतीजी के हृदय में अत्यन्त भयानक जलन पैदा हो गई ॥
english_translation: I did not obey Shankar’s words and placed my ignorance upon Ram. What answer will I give now? As she thought this, a fierce burning rose in Sati’s heart.
essence: The first pain of error is finally seeing it clearly.
simple_meaning: Sati realizes she ignored Shiva’s warning and wrongly blamed Ram. Shame and inner burning rise as she faces the consequence of her mistake.
insight: It shifts the mind from blaming outward to witnessing its own confusion.
modern_relevance: You reread the message after sending the accusation and feel your stomach drop. The ache is not punishment from outside — it is the cost of seeing your own mistake clearly.
speaker: Sati

verse_text: जाना राम सतीं दुखु पावा। निज प्रभाउ कछु प्रगटि जनावा॥ सतीं दीख कौतुकु मग जाता। आगें रामु सहित श्री भ्राता ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने जान लिया कि सतीजी को दुःख हुआ, तब उन्होंने अपना कुछ प्रभाव प्रकट करके उन्हें दिखलाया। सतीजी ने मार्ग में जाते हुए यह कौतुक देखा कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित आगे चले जा रहे हैं। (इस अवसर पर सीताजी को इसलिए दिखाया कि सतीजी श्री राम के सच्चिदानंदमय रूप को देखें, वियोग और दुःख की कल्पना जो उन्हें हुई थी, वह दूर हो जाए तथा वे प्रकृतिस्थ हों।) ॥
english_translation: Ram understood that Sati was distressed, so he revealed a little of his power to her. As Sati watched on the road, she saw the wonder of Ram walking ahead with Sita and Lakshman.
essence: A glimpse of Ram corrects confusion before it hardens.
simple_meaning: Ram sees Sati's distress and briefly reveals his divine power. Sati then sees Ram walking ahead with Sita and Lakshman.
insight: It shifts attention from Sati's inner confusion to the revealing of Ram's presence.
modern_relevance: You misread someone, then catch one small moment that changes everything. A single clear sight can dissolve a whole spiral of doubt.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: फिरि चितवा पाछें प्रभु देखा। सहित बंधु सिय सुंदर बेषा॥ जहँ चितवहिं तहँ प्रभु आसीना। सेवहिं सिद्ध मुनीस प्रबीना ॥
translation: (तब उन्होंने) पीछे की ओर फिरकर देखा, तो वहाँ भी भाई लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी के साथ श्री रामचन्द्रजी सुंदर वेष में दिखाई दिए। वे जिधर देखती हैं, उधर ही प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी विराजमान हैं और सुचतुर सिद्ध मुनीश्वर उनकी सेवा कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Turning back, she saw the Lord again there, together with his brother and Sita in a beautiful form. Wherever she looked, the Lord was seated there, and perfected sages and wise ascetics were serving him.
essence: Ram appears everywhere to the one who can truly see.
simple_meaning: Sati turns and sees Ram, Lakshman, and Sita again in a beautiful form. Wherever she looks, Ram is present, and sages are serving him.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing one fixed image to recognising presence as all-pervading.
modern_relevance: You keep searching one corner of the room for an answer, then notice it was never confined to one spot. The same truth keeps showing up from every angle once your attention changes.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखे सिव बिधि बिष्नु अनेका। अमित प्रभाउ एक तें एका॥ बंदत चरन करत प्रभु सेवा। बिबिध बेष देखे सब देवा ॥
translation: सतीजी ने अनेक शिव, ब्रह्मा और विष्णु देखे, जो एक से एक बढ़कर असीम प्रभाव वाले थे। (उन्होंने देखा कि) भाँति-भाँति के वेष धारण किए सभी देवता श्री रामचन्द्रजी की चरणवन्दना और सेवा कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Sati saw countless Shivas, Brahmas, and Vishnus, each more immeasurably radiant than the last. She saw all the radiant beings in many forms bowing at Ram's feet and serving him.
essence: The greatest beings are the ones who bow first.
simple_meaning: Sati sees endless divine forms, each radiant and powerful, all bowing to Ram and serving him in different disguises.
insight: It shifts the mind from ranking power by appearance to recognising reverence as the mark of true greatness.
modern_relevance: You meet someone quietly helping everyone in the room, while the loudest people keep seeking attention. Real stature often shows up as service, not display.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सती बिधात्री इंदिरा देखीं अमित अनूप। जेहिं जेहिं बेष अजादि सुर तेहि तेहि तन अनुरूप ॥
translation: उन्होंने अनगिनत अनुपम सती, ब्रह्माणी और लक्ष्मी देखीं। जिस-जिस रूप में ब्रह्मा आदि देवता थे, उसी के अनुकूल रूप में (उनकी) ये सब (शक्तियाँ) भी थीं ॥
english_translation: Sati saw countless incomparable forms of the divine feminine powers—Brahma's consort, Lakshmi, and others. In whatever form the ancient beings appeared, their forms matched that appearance.
essence: Each radiant being appears in the form that belongs to it.
simple_meaning: Sati sees endless divine forms, and each form matches the being it belongs to. The scene shows a universe where every power appears in a fitting shape.
insight: It prepares the mind to see form and essence as aligned, not accidental.
modern_relevance: You meet someone and instantly sense their role, their energy, their place in the room. Some presences fit themselves so completely that the outer form feels inevitable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखे जहँ जहँ रघुपति जेते। सक्तिन्ह सहित सकल सुर तेते॥ जीव चराचर जो संसारा। देखे सकल अनेक प्रकारा ॥
translation: सतीजी ने जहाँ-जहाँ जितने रघुनाथजी देखे, शक्तियों सहित वहाँ उतने ही सारे देवताओं को भी देखा। संसार में जो चराचर जीव हैं, वे भी अनेक प्रकार के सब देखे ॥
english_translation: Wherever Sati saw Raghu's lord, she saw all the radiant beings there with their powers. She also saw all moving and unmoving beings in the world, in many forms.
essence: One presence appears in endless forms.
simple_meaning: Sati sees Ram everywhere and, with him, all the radiant beings and all living forms in the world.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated figures to the shared presence behind all forms.
modern_relevance: You walk into a crowded station and suddenly notice how many lives are moving at once — each with its own burden, each part of one larger field of reality.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पूजहिं प्रभुहि देव बहु बेषा। राम रूप दूसर नहिं देखा॥ अवलोके रघुपति बहुतेरे। सीता सहित न बेष घनेरे ॥
translation: (उन्होंने देखा कि) अनेकों वेष धारण करके देवता प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी की पूजा कर रहे हैं, परन्तु श्री रामचन्द्रजी का दूसरा रूप कहीं नहीं देखा। सीता सहित श्री रघुनाथजी बहुत से देखे, परन्तु उनके वेष अनेक नहीं थे ॥
english_translation: Many deities worshiped the Lord in many forms, but no second form of Ram was seen. Raghunath was seen many times with Sita, but not in many disguises.
essence: Ram does not need many forms to be fully present.
simple_meaning: The deities appeared in many forms, but Ram did not appear as a second, separate form. Sita and Ram were seen many times, yet not in countless disguises.
insight: It shifts attention from changing appearances to the one reality beneath them.
modern_relevance: You keep scrolling through polished versions of the same person, same brand, same promise. Then one presence cuts through all the noise because it does not need costumes to be real.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सोइ रघुबर सोइ लछिमनु सीता। देखि सती अति भईं सभीता॥ हृदय कंप तन सुधि कछु नाहीं। नयन मूदि बैठीं मग माहीं ॥
translation: (सब जगह) वही रघुनाथजी, वही लक्ष्मण और वही सीताजी- सती ऐसा देखकर बहुत ही डर गईं। उनका हृदय काँपने लगा और देह की सारी सुध-बुध जाती रही। वे आँख मूँदकर मार्ग में बैठ गईं ॥
english_translation: Seeing the same Raghubar, the same Lakshman, and the same Sita, Sati became very frightened. Her heart trembled; she lost all bodily awareness and sat down on the path with her eyes closed.
essence: Overwhelm can silence the body before the mind understands.
simple_meaning: Sati sees Ram, Lakshman, and Sita in every form and becomes overwhelmed with fear. Her heart shakes, her senses fail, and she sits down with her eyes closed.
insight: It shows how shock can shut down perception before understanding catches up.
modern_relevance: You open a message and realize you have misunderstood the whole situation. Your chest tightens, your thoughts scatter, and you need a moment before you can even respond.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरि बिलोकेउ नयन उघारी। कछु न दीख तहँ दच्छकुमारी॥ पुनि पुनि नाइ राम पद सीसा। चलीं तहाँ जहँ रहे गिरीसा ॥
translation: फिर आँख खोलकर देखा, तो वहाँ दक्षकुमारी (सतीजी) को कुछ भी न दिख पड़ा। तब वे बार-बार श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर वहाँ चलीं, जहाँ श्री शिवजी थे ॥
english_translation: She opened her eyes again, but saw nothing there. Then, bowing again and again at Ram's feet, she went to where Shiva was.
essence: Sight can fail, but devotion keeps moving.
simple_meaning: Sati opens her eyes again but cannot see Ram's form. She keeps bowing to Ram and then goes to Shiva.
insight: It shows how reverence continues even after perception fails, and how the scene moves toward Shiva's questioning.
modern_relevance: You double-check the message, the email, the screen — and the clarity is gone. In that small panic, the only steady response is to bow to what is higher than your confusion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गईं समीप महेस तब हँसि पूछी कुसलात। लीन्हि परीछा कवन बिधि कहहु सत्य सब बात ॥
translation: जब पास पहुँचीं, तब श्री शिवजी ने हँसकर कुशल प्रश्न करके कहा कि तुमने रामजी की किस प्रकार परीक्षा ली, सारी बात सच-सच कहो ॥
english_translation: Then Mahesh came near, smilingly asked after her welfare, and said, "Tell me truly: in what way did you test Ram? Tell the whole truth."
essence: Shiva invites truth, not performance, after Sati's failed test.
simple_meaning: Shiva comes near Sati, asks kindly about her well-being, and asks her to tell the truth about how she tested Ram.
insight: It shifts the mind from concealment to confession, showing that clarity begins with telling the whole story.
modern_relevance: You come home after a conversation you wish you could take back. The other person is calm, not accusing, and that calm makes it harder to hide. Truth has a way of arriving softly.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सतीं समुझि रघुबीर प्रभाऊ। भय बस सिव सन कीन्ह दुराऊ॥ कछु न परीछा लीन्हि गोसाईं। कीन्ह प्रनामु तुम्हारिहि नाईं ॥
translation: सतीजी ने श्री रघुनाथजी के प्रभाव को समझकर डर के मारे शिवजी से छिपाव किया और कहा- हे स्वामिन् ! मैंने कुछ भी परीक्षा नहीं ली, (वहाँ जाकर) आपकी ही तरह प्रणाम किया ॥
english_translation: Sati understood the power of Ram and, out of fear, concealed the truth from Shiva. "I did not test him at all, lord; I bowed to you in the same way."
essence: Recognition of greatness can make concealment feel safer than honesty.
simple_meaning: Sati hides what she did because she has realized Ram's power and feels afraid to speak plainly to Shiva.
insight: It shows how ego protects itself once it meets something greater than it expected.
modern_relevance: You come home after saying something careless in a meeting, then soften the story when someone asks what happened. The real issue is not the event — it is the fear of being seen clearly.
speaker: Sati

verse_text: जो तुम्ह कहा सो मृषा न होई। मोरें मन प्रतीति अति सोई॥ तब संकर देखेउ धरि ध्याना। सतीं जो कीन्ह चरित सबु जाना ॥
translation: आपने जो कहा वह झूठ नहीं हो सकता, मेरे मन में यह बड़ा (पूरा) विश्वास है। तब शिवजी ने ध्यान करके देखा और सतीजी ने जो चरित्र किया था, सब जान लिया ॥
english_translation: What you said cannot be false; I trust it deeply in my mind. Then Shiva looked through meditation and understood everything Sati had done.
essence: Trust may begin with words, but truth appears in still seeing.
simple_meaning: Shiva tells Sati he trusts her words, then sees through meditation that she has hidden the truth about what happened.
insight: It shifts the mind from surface trust to deeper discernment through still attention.
modern_relevance: Someone gives you a neat explanation after a tense conversation, and you want to accept it. Later, when you sit quietly and replay the details, you realize something important was left out.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: बहुरि राममायहि सिरु नावा। प्रेरि सतिहि जेहिं झूँठ कहावा॥ हरि इच्छा भावी बलवाना। हृदयँ बिचारत संभु सुजाना ॥
translation: फिर श्री रामचन्द्रजी की माया को सिर नवाया, जिसने प्रेरणा करके सती के मुँह से भी झूठ कहला दिया। सुजान शिवजी ने मन में विचार किया कि हरि की इच्छा रूपी भावी प्रबल है ॥
english_translation: Again he bowed to the power of Ram's illusion, which had made even Sati speak falsely. Wise Shiva reflected in his heart that the will of Hari and the force of what is to come are mighty.
essence: Even falsehood can serve a power larger than human control.
simple_meaning: Shiva bows to Ram's mysterious power and realises that divine will and what must unfold are stronger than human certainty.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal control to humility before a larger unfolding.
modern_relevance: You replay a conversation and realise the mistake was already in motion before you understood it. The verse meets that helpless moment and says: some outcomes are bigger than your private certainty.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सतीं कीन्ह सीता कर बेषा। सिव उर भयउ बिषाद बिसेषा॥ जौं अब करउँ सती सन प्रीती। मिटइ भगति पथु होइ अनीती ॥
translation: सतीजी ने सीताजी का वेष धारण किया, यह जानकर शिवजी के हृदय में बड़ा विषाद हुआ। उन्होंने सोचा कि यदि मैं अब सती से प्रीति करता हूँ तो भक्तिमार्ग लुप्त हो जाता है और बड़ा अन्याय होता है ॥
english_translation: Sati took on Sita's form, and Shiva felt deep sorrow in his heart. He thought, 'If I now show affection to Sati, the path of devotion will be lost and great wrongdoing will follow.'
essence: Clear seeing can require refusing even sincere attachment.
simple_meaning: Sati appears as Sita, and Shiva feels sorrow. He sees that continuing personal affection would damage devotion and create wrongdoing.
insight: It shifts the mind from emotional impulse to clear moral seeing.
modern_relevance: You realise a relationship is becoming a trap, not a bond. Even though your heart wants to hold on, you step back because staying would blur what is right.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परम पुनीत न जाइ तजि किएँ प्रेम बड़ पापु। प्रगटि न कहत महेसु कछु हृदयँ अधिक संतापु ॥
translation: सती परम पवित्र हैं, इसलिए इन्हें छोड़ते भी नहीं बनता और प्रेम करने में बड़ा पाप है। प्रकट करके महादेवजी कुछ भी नहीं कहते, परन्तु उनके हृदय में बड़ा संताप है ॥
english_translation: Sati is supremely pure, so I cannot abandon her; yet loving her is a great wrong. Mahesh says nothing aloud, but his heart burns with deep distress.
essence: Purity and attachment can clash until the heart aches in silence.
simple_meaning: Shiva feels torn: Sati is pure, yet his attachment to her now feels wrong. He says nothing, but the pain inside him is intense.
insight: It shows the mind can recognize a painful truth before the tongue can speak it.
modern_relevance: You realize someone you care about is not who you thought they were. No dramatic speech comes out, only that tight, silent ache in the chest.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: तब संकर प्रभु पद सिरु नावा। सुमिरत रामु हृदयँ अस आवा॥ एहिं तन सतिहि भेंट मोहि नाहीं। सिव संकल्पु कीन्ह मन माहीं ॥
translation: तब शिवजी ने प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरण कमलों में सिर नवाया और श्री रामजी का स्मरण करते ही उनके मन में यह आया कि सती के इस शरीर से मेरी (पति-पत्नी रूप में) भेंट नहीं हो सकती और शिवजी ने अपने मन में यह संकल्प कर लिया ॥
english_translation: Then Shiva bowed his head at the Lord's feet. Remembering Ram, this thought arose in his heart: 'I cannot meet Sati in this body.' Shiva made that resolve in his mind.
essence: Reverence makes release possible.
simple_meaning: Shiva bows to Ram and realizes that his bond with Sati cannot continue in this body. He quietly resolves this in his mind.
insight: It teaches you to release a bond without bitterness when continuing would violate what is real.
modern_relevance: You realize a relationship, role, or season has ended while sitting alone after midnight. Instead of forcing what no longer fits, you bow inwardly and let the next step become clear.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: अस बिचारि संकरु मतिधीरा। चले भवन सुमिरत रघुबीरा॥ चलत गगन भै गिरा सुहाई। जय महेस भलि भगति दृढ़ाई ॥
translation: स्थिर बुद्धि शंकरजी ऐसा विचार कर श्री रघुनाथजी का स्मरण करते हुए अपने घर (कैलास) को चले। चलते समय सुंदर आकाशवाणी हुई कि हे महेश ! आपकी जय हो। आपने भक्ति की अच्छी दृढ़ता की ॥
english_translation: Thinking thus, the steadfast Shiva went home, remembering Raghubir. As he walked, a lovely voice from the sky said, “Victory to Mahesh! Your devotion is firm and true.”
essence: True devotion keeps walking even after the choice is made.
simple_meaning: Shiva leaves after remembering Ram, and a voice from the sky praises the firmness of his devotion.
insight: It shifts attention from proving yourself to remaining faithful under pressure.
modern_relevance: You walk away from a conflict without needing the last word. Later, the quiet in you says what applause never could: you stayed true.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस पन तुम्ह बिनु करइ को आना। रामभगत समरथ भगवाना॥ सुनि नभगिरा सती उर सोचा। पूछा सिवहि समेत सकोचा ॥
translation: आपको छोड़कर दूसरा कौन ऐसी प्रतिज्ञा कर सकता है। आप श्री रामचन्द्रजी के भक्त हैं, समर्थ हैं और भगवान् हैं। इस आकाशवाणी को सुनकर सतीजी के मन में चिन्ता हुई और उन्होंने सकुचाते हुए शिवजी से पूछा- ॥
english_translation: Who else can make such a vow except you? You are Ram's devotee, mighty, and divine. Hearing the voice from the sky, Sati felt troubled and shyly asked Shiva.
essence: Praise can awaken doubt before it becomes understanding.
simple_meaning: A voice from the sky praises Shiva's vow and calls him Ram's devotee. Sati becomes uneasy and, with hesitation, asks Shiva about it.
insight: It shifts attention from outward praise to the inner question that follows it.
modern_relevance: You hear someone praised for a choice you don't fully understand, and your mind tightens. That uneasy question can become the beginning of real seeing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कीन्ह कवन पन कहहु कृपाला। सत्यधाम प्रभु दीनदयाला॥ जदपि सतीं पूछा बहु भाँती। तदपि न कहेउ त्रिपुर आराती ॥
translation: हे कृपालु! कहिए, आपने कौन सी प्रतिज्ञा की है? हे प्रभो! आप सत्य के धाम और दीनदयालु हैं। यद्यपि सतीजी ने बहुत प्रकार से पूछा, परन्तु त्रिपुरारि शिवजी ने कुछ न कहा ॥
english_translation: "O compassionate one, tell me what vow you made. O Lord, you are the abode of truth and the friend of the humble." Though Sati asked in many ways, the destroyer of the three cities still said nothing.
essence: Silence can carry a truth that words are not yet fit to hold.
simple_meaning: Sati keeps asking Shiva what vow he made, but he stays silent even after she pleads in many ways.
insight: It shows that not every truth is spoken immediately; some are revealed only through patience and inner readiness.
modern_relevance: You keep asking the same question, but the other person only smiles and changes the subject. Silence can feel like a wall when you want certainty.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: सतीं हृदयँ अनुमान किय सबु जानेउ सर्बग्य। कीन्ह कपटु मैं संभु सन नारि सहज जड़ अग्य ॥
translation: सतीजी ने हृदय में अनुमान किया कि सर्वज्ञ शिवजी सब जान गए। मैंने शिवजी से कपट किया, स्त्री स्वभाव से ही मूर्ख और बेसमझ होती है ॥
english_translation: Sita understood in her heart that the all-knowing Shiva had seen everything. "I deceived Shiva; by nature, a woman is foolish and naive."
essence: Self-deception collapses the moment it is truly seen.
simple_meaning: Sati realizes Shiva already knows what happened, and she feels ashamed for having hidden the truth from him.
insight: It shifts attention from the outer act of deception to the inner moment of self-awareness.
modern_relevance: You rehearse a lie in your head, then realize the other person already understood. The heat in your face is not from being caught — it is from finally seeing yourself clearly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जलु पय सरिस बिकाइ देखहु प्रीति कि रीति भलि। बिलग होइ रसु जाइ कपट खटाई परत पुनि ॥
translation: प्रीति की सुंदर रीति देखिए कि जल भी (दूध के साथ मिलकर) दूध के समान भाव बिकता है, परन्तु फिर कपट रूपी खटाई पड़ते ही पानी अलग हो जाता है (दूध फट जाता है) और स्वाद (प्रेम) जाता रहता है ॥
english_translation: See the beautiful way of love: water mixed with milk seems to become milk, but a little sourness of deceit separates it and the taste is lost.
essence: Deceit separates what love has blended.
simple_meaning: Love looks pure when trust is present, but deceit quickly separates hearts and destroys the sweetness.
insight: It teaches you to see deceit as the force that breaks intimacy, not a small flaw to ignore.
modern_relevance: A friendship feels easy while everyone is honest. One hidden lie, one edited message, one half-truth in a group chat — and the warmth changes instantly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हृदयँ सोचु समुझत निज करनी। चिंता अमित जाइ नहिं बरनी॥ कृपासिंधु सिव परम अगाधा। प्रगट न कहेउ मोर अपराधा ॥
translation: अपनी करनी को याद करके सतीजी के हृदय में इतना सोच है और इतनी अपार चिन्ता है कि जिसका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। (उन्होंने समझ लिया कि) शिवजी कृपा के परम अथाह सागर हैं। इससे प्रकट में उन्होंने मेरा अपराध नहीं कहा ॥
english_translation: Remembering her own conduct, Sati's heart filled with endless remorse and unspoken anxiety. Shiva is an ocean of compassion, so he did not openly speak of my fault.
essence: Compassion can hide a fault, but it cannot hide it from the heart.
simple_meaning: Sati feels deep remorse over what she did. She also realizes that Shiva is so compassionate that he does not expose her fault openly.
insight: It shifts attention from blame to self-recognition, showing how compassion can make guilt feel sharper.
modern_relevance: You replay a conversation at midnight and realize the other person already chose kindness. That realization stings more than any argument could.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: संकर रुख अवलोकि भवानी। प्रभु मोहि तजेउ हृदयँ अकुलानी॥ निज अघ समुझि न कछु कहि जाई। तपइ अवाँ इव उर अधिकाई ॥
translation: शिवजी का रुख देखकर सतीजी ने जान लिया कि स्वामी ने मेरा त्याग कर दिया और वे हृदय में व्याकुल हो उठीं। अपना पाप समझकर कुछ कहते नहीं बनता, परन्तु हृदय (भीतर ही भीतर) कुम्हार के आँवे के समान अत्यन्त जलने लगा ॥
english_translation: Seeing Shiva's mood, Bhavani understood: "My lord has abandoned me." Her heart grew restless. Realizing her own fault, she could say nothing, yet inside she burned like a kiln.
essence: A guilty mind turns silence into fire.
simple_meaning: Sati sees Shiva's change in mood and feels abandoned. She knows her own fault, cannot speak, and burns with inner anguish.
insight: It shows how perception can become self-torment when the mind turns its own fault into a burning story.
modern_relevance: You notice the unread message, the shorter reply, the sudden distance in someone's voice. Before anyone says a word, your mind has already built the whole wound.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सतिहि ससोच जानि बृषकेतू। कहीं कथा सुंदर सुख हेतू॥ बरनत पंथ बिबिध इतिहासा। बिस्वनाथ पहुँचे कैलासा ॥
translation: वृषकेतु शिवजी ने सती को चिन्तायुक्त जानकर उन्हें सुख देने के लिए सुंदर कथाएँ कहीं। इस प्रकार मार्ग में विविध प्रकार के इतिहासों को कहते हुए विश्वनाथ कैलास जा पहुँचे ॥
english_translation: Seeing Sati troubled, Lord Shiva told beautiful stories to give her comfort. Speaking of many histories along the way, the Lord of the universe reached Kailash.
essence: Gentle words can carry someone through a hard moment.
simple_meaning: Shiva noticed Sati’s disturbed mind and spoke pleasant stories to soothe her as they traveled to Kailash.
insight: It teaches you to meet emotional pain with soothing speech instead of confrontation.
modern_relevance: A friend is spiraling after a tense conversation, and you do not answer with more logic. You shift the tone, tell a gentler story, and help them breathe again.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: तहँ पुनि संभु समुझि पन आपन। बैठे बट तर करि कमलासन॥ संकर सहज सरूपु सम्हारा। लागि समाधि अखंड अपारा ॥
translation: वहाँ फिर शिवजी अपनी प्रतिज्ञा को याद करके बड़ के पेड़ के नीचे पद्मासन लगाकर बैठ गए। शिवजी ने अपना स्वाभाविक रूप संभाला। उनकी अखण्ड और अपार समाधि लग गई ॥
english_translation: Then Shiva remembered his vow and sat beneath the banyan tree in lotus posture. Shiva gathered his natural form, and an unbroken, boundless absorption arose.
essence: Remembered restraint opens into boundless stillness.
simple_meaning: Shiva sits down, remembers his vow, settles into lotus posture, returns to his natural state, and enters deep, unbroken absorption.
insight: It shifts attention from reaction to inward steadiness, showing that deep calm begins with a deliberate pause.
modern_relevance: You step away from the argument, sit down, and stop feeding the spiral. The body becomes still first; then the mind remembers how to be quiet.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सती बसहिं कैलास तब अधिक सोचु मन माहिं। मरमु न कोऊ जान कछु जुग सम दिवस सिराहिं ॥
translation: तब सतीजी कैलास पर रहने लगीं। उनके मन में बड़ा दुःख था। इस रहस्य को कोई कुछ भी नहीं जानता था। उनका एक-एक दिन युग के समान बीत रहा था ॥
english_translation: Then Sati remained on Kailasa, and great sorrow filled her mind. No one understood this hidden cause, and each day passed like an age.
essence: Private sorrow can turn ordinary time into an age.
simple_meaning: Sati stays on Kailasa, but her mind is filled with deep sorrow. No one knows the reason, and time feels unbearably slow to her.
insight: It shifts attention from outward normalcy to the private burden underneath it.
modern_relevance: You sit through a family dinner smiling, while one sentence keeps replaying in your head. Everyone sees you there. No one sees the storm you are carrying.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नित नव सोचु सती उर भारा। कब जैहउँ दुख सागर पारा॥ मैं जो कीन्ह रघुपति अपमाना। पुनि पतिबचनु मृषा करि जाना ॥
translation: सतीजी के हृदय में नित्य नया और भारी सोच हो रहा था कि मैं इस दुःख समुद्र के पार कब जाऊँगी। मैंने जो श्री रघुनाथजी का अपमान किया और फिर पति के वचनों को झूठ जाना- ॥
english_translation: A fresh grief kept rising in Sati’s heart: when will I cross this ocean of sorrow? I insulted Raghupati, and then I treated my husband’s words as false.
essence: Regret grows when the heart remembers its own betrayal.
simple_meaning: Sati feels a new wave of grief and shame. She remembers insulting Ram and doubting Shiva’s words, and she longs to be free of that sorrow.
insight: It shows how regret deepens when the mind keeps revisiting a violated value.
modern_relevance: You lie awake after saying something cruel, and the memory returns sharper each time. The mind does not let you escape what the heart knows it must answer.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सो फलु मोहि बिधाताँ दीन्हा। जो कछु उचित रहा सोइ कीन्हा॥ अब बिधि अस बूझिअ नहिं तोही। संकर बिमुख जिआवसि मोही ॥
translation: उसका फल विधाता ने मुझको दिया, जो उचित था वही किया, परन्तु हे विधाता! अब तुझे यह उचित नहीं है, जो शंकर से विमुख होने पर भी मुझे जिला रहा है ॥
english_translation: That fate gave me the result. I did what was proper. But now, O fate, this is not proper: you keep me alive even after I turned away from Shiva.
essence: Regret deepens when the mind cannot escape its own verdict.
simple_meaning: Sati feels the consequence of her own choice. She says she received the result of what she did, but now she is troubled that fate is still keeping her alive after she turned away from Shiva.
insight: It exposes the mind’s split between owning consequences and resisting them, making regret impossible to hide.
modern_relevance: You replay the message you should never have sent, then stare at the screen wondering why the day still continues. The discomfort is not just pain — it is your own conscience speaking back.
speaker: Sati

verse_text: कहि न जाइ कछु हृदय गलानी। मन महुँ रामहि सुमिर सयानी॥ जौं प्रभु दीनदयालु कहावा। आरति हरन बेद जसु गावा ॥
translation: सतीजी के हृदय की ग्लानि कुछ कही नहीं जाती। बुद्धिमती सतीजी ने मन में श्री रामचन्द्रजी का स्मरण किया और कहा- हे प्रभो! यदि आप दीनदयालु कहलाते हैं और वेदों ने आपका यह यश गाया है कि आप दुःख को हरने वाले हैं, ॥
english_translation: The pain in Sati's heart cannot be spoken. Wise Sati remembered Ram in her mind: “If you are called the compassionate lord of the poor, and the Vedas sing your fame as the remover of sorrow...”
essence: Remorse becomes prayer when the mind remembers mercy.
simple_meaning: Sati feels deep remorse and turns her mind to Ram, recalling his reputation as the compassionate one who removes suffering.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to seeking compassionate refuge.
modern_relevance: You replay a painful conversation at 2 a.m., unable to sleep. In that raw moment, the mind reaches for the one presence it trusts to be merciful.
speaker: Sati

verse_text: तौ मैं बिनय करउँ कर जोरी। छूटउ बेगि देह यह मोरी॥ जौं मोरें सिव चरन सनेहू। मन क्रम बचन सत्य ब्रतु एहू ॥
translation: तो मैं हाथ जोड़कर विनती करती हूँ कि मेरी यह देह जल्दी छूट जाए। यदि मेरा शिवजी के चरणों में प्रेम है और मेरा यह (प्रेम का) व्रत मन, वचन और कर्म (आचरण) से सत्य है, ॥
english_translation: Then I fold my hands and pray: let this body be released quickly. If I truly love Shiva's feet, and if my vow is true in mind, speech, and action,
essence: True love asks for a life that matches its vow.
simple_meaning: Sati prays for her body to end quickly, saying that if her love for Shiva is true, her vow should be proven true in mind, speech, and action.
insight: It shifts devotion from sentiment to embodied commitment.
modern_relevance: You say you stand by someone, but the real test comes when loyalty costs you comfort, image, or certainty. Sati wants her whole life to match her vow.
speaker: Sati

verse_text: तौ सबदरसी सुनिअ प्रभु करउ सो बेगि उपाइ। होइ मरनु जेहिं बिनहिं श्रम दुसह बिपत्ति बिहाइ ॥
translation: तो हे सर्वदर्शी प्रभो! सुनिए और शीघ्र वह उपाय कीजिए, जिससे मेरा मरण हो और बिना ही परिश्रम यह (पति-परित्याग रूपी) असह्य विपत्ति दूर हो जाए ॥
english_translation: O all-seeing Lord, hear me and quickly make a way by which I may die, and this unbearable hardship of leaving my husband may end without effort.
essence: When suffering becomes unbearable, the heart asks only for release.
simple_meaning: Sati begs for an easy end to the unbearable pain of being separated from Shiva.
insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to surrender when pain has become too heavy to carry.
modern_relevance: You reach the point where every phone call, every room, every memory hurts. You stop asking for answers and just want the weight to lift.
speaker: Sati

verse_text: एहि बिधि दुखित प्रजेसकुमारी। अकथनीय दारुन दुखु भारी॥ बीतें संबत सहस सतासी। तजी समाधि संभु अबिनासी ॥
translation: दक्षसुता सतीजी इस प्रकार बहुत दुःखित थीं, उनको इतना दारुण दुःख था कि जिसका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। सत्तासी हजार वर्ष बीत जाने पर अविनाशी शिवजी ने समाधि खोली ॥
english_translation: In this way, the daughter of the king of the mountains was filled with sorrow, a grief too terrible to describe. After eighty-seven thousand years had passed, the imperishable Shiva came out of meditation.
essence: Great grief can pass through vast silence before the next awakening.
simple_meaning: Sati suffers unbearable grief while Shiva remains in deep meditation for a very long time. The verse simply marks the passage of time before the next turning point.
insight: It slows the reader down before the next revelation, showing that transformation often follows a long stillness.
modern_relevance: You sit with a heartbreak that feels frozen in time, while the rest of the world keeps moving. Then, without warning, something in you finally stirs again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम नाम सिव सुमिरन लागे। जानेउ सतीं जगतपति जागे॥ जाइ संभु पद बंदनु कीन्हा। सनमुख संकर आसनु दीन्हा ॥
translation: शिवजी रामनाम का स्मरण करने लगे, तब सतीजी ने जाना कि अब जगत के स्वामी (शिवजी) जागे। उन्होंने जाकर शिवजी के चरणों में प्रणाम किया। शिवजी ने उनको बैठने के लिए सामने आसन दिया ॥
english_translation: Shiva began remembering Ram's name, and Sati understood that the Lord of the world had awakened. She went and bowed at Shiva's feet. Shiva gave her a seat facing him.
essence: Reverence restores closeness before words can.
simple_meaning: Shiva turns to Ram's name, and Sati recognizes his awakened state. She bows to him, and he seats her with honor.
insight: It teaches you to let reverence lead the next move. Respect can reopen a relationship faster than explanation.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a tense silence, and one person softens first. A respectful gesture breaks the chill before any argument can continue.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लगे कहन हरि कथा रसाला। दच्छ प्रजेस भए तेहि काला॥ देखा बिधि बिचारि सब लायक। दच्छहि कीन्ह प्रजापति नायक ॥
translation: शिवजी भगवान हरि की रसमयी कथाएँ कहने लगे। उसी समय दक्ष प्रजापति हुए। ब्रह्माजी ने सब प्रकार से योग्य देख-समझकर दक्ष को प्रजापतियों का नायक बना दिया ॥
english_translation: Shiva began speaking the sweet stories of Hari. At that time, Daksha the lord of creatures arose. Seeing and considering all things, Brahma made Daksha the leader of the prajapatis.
essence: Authority can arrive while devotion quietly continues.
simple_meaning: Shiva was speaking about Hari when Daksha rose to power. Brahma, after considering who was fit, appointed Daksha as leader of the prajapatis.
insight: It sets up the contrast between outer authority and the inner state that follows it.
modern_relevance: A meeting continues in one room while, elsewhere, someone gets promoted and starts believing the title defines them. The change in status matters less than what it does to the heart.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: बड़ अधिकार दच्छ जब पावा। अति अभिनामु हृदयँ तब आवा॥ नहिं कोउ अस जनमा जग माहीं। प्रभुता पाइ जाहि मद नाहीं ॥
translation: जब दक्ष ने इतना बड़ा अधिकार पाया, तब उनके हृदय में अत्यन्त अभिमान आ गया। जगत में ऐसा कोई नहीं पैदा हुआ, जिसको प्रभुता पाकर मद न हो ॥
english_translation: When Daksha gained such great authority, pride arose in his heart. No one is born in this world who does not become intoxicated after gaining power.
essence: Power easily turns into pride unless the heart stays watchful.
simple_meaning: Daksha gained great authority, and that success made him arrogant. The verse warns that power often feeds pride in anyone who receives it.
insight: It shifts attention from external status to the ego reaction status can trigger.
modern_relevance: You get promoted, your name is suddenly on every email, and people start treating you differently. Before long, the role can feel like proof that you matter more than others.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दच्छ लिए मुनि बोलि सब करन लगे बड़ जाग। नेवते सादर सकल सुर जे पावत मख भाग ॥
translation: दक्ष ने सब मुनियों को बुला लिया और वे बड़ा यज्ञ करने लगे। जो देवता यज्ञ का भाग पाते हैं, दक्ष ने उन सबको आदर सहित निमन्त्रित किया ॥
english_translation: Daksha gathered all the sages and began a great sacrifice. He invited with respect all the radiant beings who receive a share in the sacrifice.
essence: Pride often enters first as a perfectly arranged invitation.
simple_meaning: Daksha gathers the sages and begins a large sacrifice, inviting all the radiant beings who receive offerings there.
insight: It trains attention on the social gesture before the rupture, where pride first becomes visible.
modern_relevance: A meeting invite goes out to everyone except the one person who matters most. The exclusion is polite on the surface, but it already contains the wound.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: किंनर नाग सिद्ध गंधर्बा। बधुन्ह समेत चले सुर सर्बा॥ बिष्नु बिरंचि महेसु बिहाई। चले सकल सुर जान बनाई ॥
translation: (दक्ष का निमन्त्रण पाकर) किन्नर, नाग, सिद्ध, गन्धर्व और सब देवता अपनी-अपनी स्त्रियों सहित चले। विष्णु, ब्रह्मा और महादेवजी को छोड़कर सभी देवता अपना-अपना विमान सजाकर चले ॥
english_translation: (On receiving Daksha's invitation) the Kinnaras, Nagas, Siddhas, Gandharvas, and all the radiant beings went along with their wives. Leaving Vishnu, Brahma, and Mahesh aside, all the radiant beings set out in their own celestial vehicles.
essence: Not every grand gathering deserves your presence.
simple_meaning: All kinds of celestial beings went to Daksha's ceremony with their wives. Vishnu, Brahma, and Shiva did not go.
insight: It shifts attention from social inclusion to discernment about where not to go.
modern_relevance: Everyone is RSVPing yes to the big event, and your phone keeps lighting up. But three names stay out of the room. Sometimes wisdom is knowing which crowd does not deserve your presence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सतीं बिलोके ब्योम बिमाना। जात चले सुंदर बिधि नाना॥ सुर सुंदरी करहिं कल गाना। सुनत श्रवन छूटहिं मुनि ध्याना ॥
translation: सतीजी ने देखा, अनेकों प्रकार के सुंदर विमान आकाश में चले जा रहे हैं, देव-सुन्दरियाँ मधुर गान कर रही हैं, जिन्हें सुनकर मुनियों का ध्यान छूट जाता है ॥
english_translation: Sati saw many beautiful celestial vehicles moving through the sky. The divine maidens sang sweetly, and hearing them, the sages lost their meditation.
essence: Beauty can scatter even a disciplined mind.
simple_meaning: Sati notices the gods passing overhead in beautiful flying vehicles, while the celestial women sing so sweetly that even sages lose concentration.
insight: It shows how quickly the senses can interrupt inward absorption, even in the presence of spiritual discipline.
modern_relevance: You are trying to stay focused, but a flood of notifications, music, and movement keeps pulling your attention away. The mind can be broken by beauty before it is broken by pain.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पूछेउ तब सिवँ कहेउ बखानी। पिता जग्य सुनि कछु हरषानी॥ जौं महेसु मोहि आयसु देहीं। कछु िदन जाइ रहौं मिस एहीं ॥
translation: सतीजी ने (विमानों में देवताओं के जाने का कारण) पूछा, तब शिवजी ने सब बातें बतलाईं। पिता के यज्ञ की बात सुनकर सती कुछ प्रसन्न हुईं और सोचने लगीं कि यदि महादेवजी मुझे आज्ञा दें, तो इसी बहाने कुछ दिन पिता के घर जाकर रहूँ ॥
english_translation: Then Sati asked Shiva, and he explained everything. Hearing that her father was performing a sacrifice, Sati felt some joy and thought, "If Mahesh gives me permission, I will go stay at my father's house for a few days under that pretext."
essence: A simple family invitation can awaken buried longing and pain.
simple_meaning: Sati asks Shiva about the gathering and becomes glad when she hears her father is holding a sacrifice. She hopes Shiva will let her visit her father's home for a few days.
insight: It sets up the hidden tension between outward politeness and inner hurt.
modern_relevance: You hear one family message and suddenly old feelings wake up. A simple invitation can carry hope, longing, and the fear of what will happen next.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: पति परित्याग हृदयँ दुखु भारी। कहइ न निज अपराध बिचारी॥ बोली सती मनोहर बानी। भय संकोच प्रेम रस सानी ॥
translation: क्योंकि उनके हृदय में पति द्वारा त्यागी जाने का बड़ा भारी दुःख था, पर अपना अपराध समझकर वे कुछ कहती न थीं। आखिर सतीजी भय, संकोच और प्रेमरस में सनी हुई मनोहर वाणी से बोलीं- ॥
english_translation: With a heart heavy with grief at being set aside by her husband, she said nothing, seeing her own fault. Then Sati spoke in a gentle voice, sweetened by fear, modesty, and love.
essence: Love speaks softly even when it is wounded.
simple_meaning: Sati feels deep hurt and shame, so she speaks carefully and gently. Her words come from fear, hesitation, and love.
insight: It shows how self-doubt, love, and restraint can shape speech before a difficult request.
modern_relevance: You reread a message three times before sending it, knowing one careless sentence could wound someone you love. The heart is full, but the voice must stay gentle.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पिता भवन उत्सव परम जौं प्रभु आयसु होइ। तौ मैं जाउँ कृपायतन सादर देखन सोइ ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! मेरे पिता के घर बहुत बड़ा उत्सव है। यदि आपकी आज्ञा हो तो हे कृपाधाम! मैं आदर सहित उसे देखने जाऊँ ॥
english_translation: O Lord, there is a great celebration at my father's house. If you permit, O abode of grace, I shall go respectfully to see it.
essence: Respectful desire asks before it moves.
simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva for permission to visit her father's grand celebration and see it with respect.
insight: It teaches you to seek permission and move without entitlement, even when the pull of family is strong.
modern_relevance: You hear your family is gathering for a major event, but your partner is uneasy about it. The question is not just whether you can go — it is whether you can go with respect and care.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: कहेहु नीक मोरेहूँ मन भावा। यह अनुचित नहिं नेवत पठावा॥ दच्छ सकल निज सुता बोलाईं। हमरें बयर तुम्हउ बिसराईं ॥
translation: शिवजी ने कहा- तुमने बात तो अच्छी कही, यह मेरे मन को भी पसंद आई पर उन्होंने न्योता नहीं भेजा, यह अनुचित है। दक्ष ने अपनी सब लड़कियों को बुलाया है, किन्तु हमारे बैर के कारण उन्होंने तुमको भी भुला दिया ॥
english_translation: You spoke well; I also like it. Yet it is improper that no invitation was sent. Daksha has called all his daughters, but because of our old enmity, you were forgotten too.
essence: Old enmity can turn even an invitation into exclusion.
simple_meaning: Shiva agrees that Parvati's wish is reasonable, but says the lack of invitation is disrespectful. Daksha invited his daughters, yet left Parvati out because of old hostility.
insight: It shows how unresolved hostility turns even a simple invitation into a social wound.
modern_relevance: You hear about a family gathering everyone was invited to except one person. The exclusion is polite on the surface, but everyone feels the old wound underneath.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: ब्रह्मसभाँ हम सन दुखु माना। तेहि तें अजहुँ करहिं अपमाना॥ जौं बिनु बोलें जाहु भवानी। रहइ न सीलु सनेहु न कानी ॥
translation: एक बार ब्रह्मा की सभा में हम से अप्रसन्न हो गए थे, उसी से वे अब भी हमारा अपमान करते हैं। हे भवानी! जो तुम बिना बुलाए जाओगी तो न शील-स्नेह ही रहेगा और न मान-मर्यादा ही रहेगी ॥
english_translation: In Brahma's assembly, I was once slighted. Because of that, they still insult us. O Bhavani, if you go without being invited, neither decorum nor affection nor honor will remain.
essence: Uninvited presence can turn affection into insult.
simple_meaning: Shiva says that being excluded once still matters, so going uninvited would break decorum, affection, and respect.
insight: It teaches you to honor social boundaries instead of treating closeness as entitlement.
modern_relevance: You know that moment when a family gathering is tense and one person says, “Just show up anyway”? Sometimes forcing access only deepens the wound.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: जदपि मित्र प्रभु पितु गुर गेहा। जाइअ बिनु बोलेहुँ न सँदेहा॥ तदपि बिरोध मान जहँ कोई। तहाँ गएँ कल्यानु न होई ॥
translation: यद्यपि इसमें संदेह नहीं कि मित्र, स्वामी, पिता और गुरु के घर बिना बुलाए भी जाना चाहिए तो भी जहाँ कोई विरोध मानता हो, उसके घर जाने से कल्याण नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: Even though there is no doubt that one may go without invitation to the home of a friend, lord, father, or teacher, if someone feels hostility there, going there brings no good.
essence: Closeness without welcome turns even rightful presence into harm.
simple_meaning: You may visit a friend, parent, teacher, or lord without invitation, but not where your presence is unwelcome. Forced closeness brings no good.
insight: It teaches restraint: do not force entry where resentment is active. Respect the emotional reality of the space before you step in.
modern_relevance: You know that message you want to send after the argument, just to prove you still can? Sometimes the mature move is to wait until the room is willing again.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: भाँति अनेक संभु समुझावा। भावी बस न ग्यानु उर आवा॥ कह प्रभु जाहु जो बिनहिं बोलाएँ। नहिं भलि बात हमारे भाएँ ॥
translation: शिवजी ने बहुत प्रकार से समझाया, पर होनहारवश सती के हृदय में बोध नहीं हुआ। फिर शिवजी ने कहा कि यदि बिना बुलाए जाओगी, तो हमारी समझ में अच्छी बात न होगी ॥
english_translation: Shiva explained in many ways, but by fate no understanding arose in Sati's heart. Then Shiva said, 'If you go without being invited, it is not a good thing in our view.'
essence: Forcing entry where you are unwelcome brings harm.
simple_meaning: Shiva tries to reason with Sati, but she still cannot see clearly. He warns her that going uninvited is not wise.
insight: It shifts the mind from impulse to restraint, especially when pride wants to override warning.
modern_relevance: You already know the room is tense, but you still want to walk in and prove a point. The wiser move is to pause before turning hurt into a scene.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: कहि देखा हर जतन बहु रहइ न दच्छकुमारि। दिए मुख्य गन संग तब बिदा कीन्ह त्रिपुरारि ॥
translation: शिवजी ने बहुत प्रकार से कहकर देख लिया, किन्तु जब सती किसी प्रकार भी नहीं रुकीं, तब त्रिपुरारि महादेवजी ने अपने मुख्य गणों को साथ देकर उनको बिदा कर दिया ॥
english_translation: Shiva tried many ways to stop her, but when Sati would not stay, Tripurari sent her off with his chief attendants.
essence: Love cannot force a heart to stay.
simple_meaning: Shiva tried to persuade Sati not to go, but she would not listen. So he finally sent her off with his attendants.
insight: It shows the limit of persuasion and the dignity of releasing control when another person insists on their own course.
modern_relevance: You warn someone you love, but they still walk into the conversation you know will hurt them. At some point, care becomes letting them go.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पिता भवन जब गईं भवानी। दच्छ त्रास काहुँ न सनमानी॥ सादर भलेहिं मिली एक माता। भगिनीं मिलीं बहुत मुसुकाता ॥
translation: भवानी जब पिता (दक्ष) के घर पहुँची, तब दक्ष के डर के मारे किसी ने उनकी आवभगत नहीं की, केवल एक माता भले ही आदर से मिली। बहिनें बहुत मुस्कुराती हुई मिलीं ॥
english_translation: When Bhavani reached her father's house, no one honored her out of fear of Daksha. Only one mother welcomed her respectfully, and the sisters greeted her with forced smiles.
essence: Fear can make even family feel like strangers.
simple_meaning: Bhavani returned to her father's house, but fear of Daksha made everyone cold. Only one mother showed respect, while her sisters smiled without warmth.
insight: It shows how social fear can erase warmth and make courtesy feel empty.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering and feel the room tighten. People smile, but no one really meets your eyes. The verse captures how fear turns even home into a place of distance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दच्छ न कछु पूछी कुसलाता। सतिहि बिलोकी जरे सब गाता॥ सतीं जाइ देखेउ तब जागा। कतहूँ न दीख संभु कर भागा ॥
translation: दक्ष ने तो उनकी कुछ कुशल तक नहीं पूछी, सतीजी को देखकर उलटे उनके सारे अंग जल उठे। तब सती ने जाकर यज्ञ देखा तो वहाँ कहीं शिवजी का भाग दिखाई नहीं दिया ॥
english_translation: Daksha did not even ask after her well-being. Seeing Sati, all his body burned with anger. Then Sati went and saw the sacrifice, but nowhere could she see any share of Shiva.
essence: Exclusion makes disrespect unmistakable.
simple_meaning: Daksha ignores Sati completely, and his anger flares at her presence. Sati then looks for Shiva's share in the sacrifice and finds none.
insight: It shows how insult and exclusion can become immediately visible, before anyone says a word.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering and no one asks how you are. The silence itself tells you where you stand, and one missing seat says everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब चित चढ़ेउ जो संकर कहेऊ। प्रभु अपमानु समुझि उर दहेऊ॥ पाछिल दुखु न हृदयँ अस ब्यापा। जस यह भयउ महा परितापा ॥
translation: तब शिवजी ने जो कहा था, वह उनकी समझ में आया। स्वामी का अपमान समझकर सती का हृदय जल उठा। पिछला (पति परित्याग का) दुःख उनके हृदय में उतना नहीं व्यापा था, जितना महान् दुःख इस समय (पति अपमान के कारण) हुआ ॥
english_translation: Then Sati understood what Shiva had said. Seeing her lord insulted, her heart burned. The earlier grief had not weighed on her heart as much as this great pain did.
essence: Insult to the one you love can burn deeper than your own sorrow.
simple_meaning: Sati finally understood Shiva’s warning, and the insult to her husband hurt her more than her earlier grief had.
insight: It shifts attention from private hurt to the sharper pain of public dishonour.
modern_relevance: You hear a cruel joke made about someone you love in front of everyone. The embarrassment lands harder than the original problem, because disrespect cuts deeper than pain.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जद्यपि जग दारुन दुख नाना। सब तें कठिन जाति अवमाना॥ समुझि सो सतिहि भयउ अति क्रोधा। बहु बिधि जननीं कीन्ह प्रबोधा ॥
translation: यद्यपि जगत में अनेक प्रकार के दारुण दुःख हैं, तथापि, जाति अपमान सबसे बढ़कर कठिन है। यह समझकर सतीजी को बड़ा क्रोध हो आया। माता ने उन्हें बहुत प्रकार से समझाया-बुझाया ॥
english_translation: Although the world holds many terrible sorrows, insult to one’s own kind is the hardest to bear. Realizing this, Sati became intensely angry, and her mother tried in many ways to calm her.
essence: Humiliation of one’s own people can burn hotter than any ordinary pain.
simple_meaning: Many kinds of suffering exist, but humiliation of one’s own family or group cuts the deepest. Sati felt that sting, and her mother kept trying to calm her.
insight: It shows how insult can trigger protective anger before reason has a chance to intervene.
modern_relevance: A relative is mocked at a family gathering, and your chest tightens before you can think. The hurt is not just for them — it touches your sense of belonging and dignity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिव अपमानु न जाइ सहि हृदयँ न होइ प्रबोध। सकल सभहि हठि हटकि तब बोलीं बचन सक्रोध ॥
translation: परन्तु उनसे शिवजी का अपमान सहा नहीं गया, इससे उनके हृदय में कुछ भी प्रबोध नहीं हुआ। तब वे सारी सभा को हठपूर्वक डाँटकर क्रोधभरे वचन बोलीं- ॥
english_translation: But she could not bear Shiva's insult, and no counsel could reach her heart. Then, pushing aside the whole assembly, she spoke angry words.
essence: Insult to what you love can silence all reason.
simple_meaning: Sati cannot bear the insult to Shiva, and no advice can calm her. She turns away from the assembly and speaks in anger.
insight: It shows how wounded loyalty can override reason and turn the mind against counsel.
modern_relevance: Someone mocks the person you love in a room full of people, and your chest tightens before you can think. The mind shuts the door on advice when hurt feels like honor.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: सुनहु सभासद सकल मुनिंदा। कही सुनी जिन्ह संकर निंदा॥ सो फलु तुरत लहब सब काहूँ। भली भाँति पछिताब पिताहूँ ॥
translation: हे सभासदों और सब मुनीश्वरो! सुनो। जिन लोगों ने यहाँ शिवजी की निंदा की या सुनी है, उन सबको उसका फल तुरंत ही मिलेगा और मेरे पिता दक्ष भी भलीभाँति पछताएँगे ॥
english_translation: Listen, all members of the assembly and all sages. Everyone who has spoken or heard Shiva's slander will quickly bear its result, and my father Daksha will surely repent deeply.
essence: Insult carries its own punishment, and the speaker is not spared.
simple_meaning: Sati warns the assembly that anyone involved in insulting Shiva will face the consequence at once, including her father.
insight: It shifts the mind from casual criticism to awareness of the cost of disrespect.
modern_relevance: A family dinner turns sharp when someone mocks a person who is absent. The room feels lighter for a second, then heavier for days. Public contempt always leaves a mark.
speaker: Sati

verse_text: संत संभु श्रीपति अपबादा। सुनिअ जहाँ तहँ असि मरजादा॥ काटिअ तासु जीभ जो बसाई। श्रवन मूदि न त चलिअ पराई ॥
translation: जहाँ संत, शिवजी और लक्ष्मीपति श्री विष्णु भगवान की निंदा सुनी जाए, वहाँ ऐसी मर्यादा है कि यदि अपना वश चले तो उस (निंदा करने वाले) की जीभ काट लें और नहीं तो कान मूँदकर वहाँ से भाग जाएँ ॥
english_translation: Where saints, Shiva, and Lord Vishnu are insulted, such conduct is never proper. If one has the power, cut out the slanderer's tongue; otherwise, cover your ears and leave at once.
essence: Respect demands distance from contempt.
simple_meaning: A person should not tolerate insults against saints, Shiva, or Vishnu. The proper response is to stop listening and leave.
insight: It trains the reader to protect reverence by refusing to participate in contempt.
modern_relevance: You open a group chat and see mockery aimed at someone you respect. You do not need to argue with every cruel voice. Sometimes dignity means closing the thread and walking away.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जगदातमा महेसु पुरारी। जगत जनक सब के हितकारी॥ पिता मंदमति निंदत तेही। दच्छ सुक्र संभव यह देही ॥
translation: त्रिपुर दैत्य को मारने वाले भगवान महेश्वर सम्पूर्ण जगत की आत्मा हैं, वे जगत्पिता और सबका हित करने वाले हैं। मेरा मंदबुद्धि पिता उनकी निंदा करता है और मेरा यह शरीर दक्ष ही के वीर्य से उत्पन्न है ॥
english_translation: Shiva, destroyer of Tripura, is the self of the world, the father of the universe, and the benefactor of all. My foolish father reviles him, and this body was born from Daksha's own seed.
essence: A heart that sees Shiva clearly cannot remain in insult.
simple_meaning: Sati praises Shiva as the universal benefactor and condemns her father's insult of him. She feels torn because her body itself came from Daksha's lineage.
insight: It shows how devotion can become moral clarity: once reverence is violated, compromise feels like self-betrayal.
modern_relevance: You sit at a family dinner while someone casually mocks the person you love most. The room goes silent, and suddenly staying polite feels impossible.
speaker: Sati

verse_text: तजिहउँ तुरत देह तेहि हेतू। उर धरि चंद्रमौलि बृषकेतू॥ अस कहि जोग अगिनि तनु जारा। भयउ सकल मख हाहाकारा ॥
translation: इसलिए चन्द्रमा को ललाट पर धारण करने वाले वृषकेतु शिवजी को हृदय में धारण करके मैं इस शरीर को तुरंत ही त्याग दूँगी। ऐसा कहकर सतीजी ने योगाग्नि में अपना शरीर भस्म कर डाला। सारी यज्ञशाला में हाहाकार मच गया ॥
english_translation: Therefore, I will immediately leave this body for his sake, keeping Lord Shiva, the one with the moon on his brow and the bull-banner, in my heart. Saying this, Sati burned her body in the fire of yoga. The whole sacrificial arena erupted in uproar.
essence: Devotion can become so absolute that the body is no longer bearable.
simple_meaning: Sati decides to give up her body for Shiva and burns herself in the fire of yogic power, causing chaos in the sacrificial arena.
insight: It shows how inner loyalty can be stronger than social pressure, even when the cost is total.
modern_relevance: You sit at a family table where someone you love is being mocked. The room keeps eating, but you cannot. Something in you breaks before the conversation does.
speaker: Sati

verse_text: सती मरनु सुनि संभु गन लगे करन मख खीस। जग्य बिधंस बिलोकि भृगु रच्छा कीन्हि मुनीस ॥ ॥
translation: सती का मरण सुनकर शिवजी के गण यज्ञ विध्वंस करने लगे। यज्ञ विध्वंस होते देखकर मुनीश्वर भृगुजी ने उसकी रक्षा की ॥
english_translation: Hearing of Sati's death, Shiva's attendants began to disrupt the sacrifice. Seeing the sacrifice being ruined, the sage Bhrigu protected it.
essence: Anger spreads fast; steadiness protects what rage would destroy.
simple_meaning: When Sati's death reached Shiva's attendants, they moved to wreck the sacrifice. Bhrigu saw the danger and protected the ritual.
insight: It shifts attention from revenge to containment when emotions begin to spread.
modern_relevance: A family chat turns explosive after one painful message, and everyone starts taking sides. Before the whole situation burns down, someone steady has to protect what still matters.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समाचार सब संकर पाए। बीरभद्रु करि कोप पठाए॥ जग्य बिधंस जाइ तिन्ह कीन्हा। सकल सुरन्ह बिधिवत फलु दीन्हा ॥
translation: ये सब समाचार शिवजी को मिले, तब उन्होंने क्रोध करके वीरभद्र को भेजा। उन्होंने वहाँ जाकर यज्ञ विध्वंस कर डाला और सब देवताओं को यथोचित फल (दंड) दिया ॥
english_translation: When Shiva received the news, he sent Virabhadra in anger. Virabhadra went there and destroyed the sacrifice, giving all the radiant beings their due punishment.
essence: Violating reverence brings a forceful reckoning.
simple_meaning: Shiva hears what happened and sends Virabhadra to destroy Daksha's sacrifice. The heavenly beings involved receive the consequences of their actions.
insight: It shows that disrespect and cruelty trigger consequences that cannot be contained by ceremony or status.
modern_relevance: A room full of people thinks a cruel joke will pass unnoticed. It doesn't. The damage comes back fast, and everyone has to face what they helped create.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भै जगबिदित दच्छ गति सोई। जसि कछु संभु बिमुख कै होई॥ यह इतिहास सकल जग जानी। ताते मैं संछेप बखानी ॥
translation: दक्ष की जगत्प्रसिद्ध वही गति हुई, जो शिवद्रोही की हुआ करती है। यह इतिहास सारा संसार जानता है, इसलिए मैंने संक्षेप में वर्णन किया ॥
english_translation: Daksha met the well-known fate that befalls one who turns away from Shiva. The whole world knows this story, so I have told it briefly.
essence: Turning away from Shiva brings a fate everyone remembers.
simple_meaning: Daksha suffered the fate that comes to one who turns away from Shiva. Everyone already knows this story, so the poet tells it briefly.
insight: It frames the episode as a remembered warning, not just a private feud.
modern_relevance: A family argument has already gone too far, and everyone can feel the damage. Some choices become public lessons because the consequences are so clear that no one needs the full retelling.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सतीं मरत हरि सन बरु मागा। जनम जनम सिव पद अनुरागा॥ तेहि कारन हिमगिरि गृह जाई। जनमीं पारबती तनु पाई ॥
translation: सती ने मरते समय भगवान हरि से यह वर माँगा कि मेरा जन्म-जन्म में शिवजी के चरणों में अनुराग रहे। इसी कारण उन्होंने हिमाचल के घर जाकर पार्वती के शरीर से जन्म लिया ॥
english_translation: Sati asked Hari for one boon at the time of death: may love for Shiva's feet remain through every birth. For that reason, she went to the home of Himavan and was born as Parvati in a new body.
essence: Love that clings to the divine returns in every life.
simple_meaning: Sati asks for one blessing before death: unwavering love for Shiva in every life. That prayer becomes the reason she is born again as Parvati.
insight: It shifts devotion from a passing feeling to a lasting orientation of the heart.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who changed your life, and even after years, your heart still returns to them. This verse says the deepest love does not fade with time; it shapes who you become next.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जब तें उमा सैल गृह जाईं। सकल सिद्धि संपति तहँ छाईं॥ जहँ तहँ मुनिन्ह सुआश्रम कीन्हे। उचित बास हिम भूधर दीन्हे ॥
translation: जब से उमाजी हिमाचल के घर जन्मीं, तबसे वहाँ सारी सिद्धियाँ और सम्पत्तियाँ छा गईं। मुनियों ने जहाँ-तहाँ सुंदर आश्रम बना लिए और हिमाचल ने उनको उचित स्थान दिए ॥
english_translation: From the time Uma came to the mountain-house, all blessings and abundance spread there. Sages built lovely hermitages everywhere, and Himachal gave them proper places to live.
essence: Sacred presence turns a place into a refuge.
simple_meaning: Uma's arrival made the mountain land blessed and prosperous. Sages settled there in beautiful hermitages, and Himachal welcomed them with suitable places to live.
insight: It shifts attention from decoration to presence: blessing is shown through the life a place begins to hold.
modern_relevance: A home feels different the moment a kind, steady person enters it. Calm spreads, guests feel welcome, and even the atmosphere seems to settle into order.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सदा सुमन फल सहित सब द्रुम नव नाना जाति। प्रगटीं सुंदर सैल पर मनि आकर बहु भाँति ॥
translation: उस सुंदर पर्वत पर बहुत प्रकार के सब नए-नए वृक्ष सदा पुष्प-फलयुक्त हो गए और वहाँ बहुत तरह की मणियों की खानें प्रकट हो गईं ॥
english_translation: All kinds of new trees, always full of flowers and fruit, appeared on the beautiful mountain. Mines of gems of many kinds also emerged there.
essence: Blessing turns barren ground into abundance.
simple_meaning: The mountain becomes abundantly fertile and rich, with flowering trees, fruit, and many kinds of gems.
insight: It shifts attention from scarcity to the way presence can make a place flourish.
modern_relevance: A neglected home suddenly feels alive after one loving person arrives and begins caring for it. The same rooms, the same walls — yet everything seems to bloom.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सरिता सब पुनीत जलु बहहीं। खग मृग मधुप सुखी सब रहहीं॥ सहज बयरु सब जीवन्ह त्यागा। गिरि पर सकल करहिं अनुरागा ॥
translation: सारी नदियों में पवित्र जल बहता है और पक्षी, पशु, भ्रमर सभी सुखी रहते हैं। सब जीवों ने अपना स्वाभाविक बैर छोड़ दिया और पर्वत पर सभी परस्पर प्रेम करते हैं ॥
english_translation: All rivers flow with pure water there, and birds, animals, and bees all live happily. All creatures have given up their natural hostility, and on the mountain everyone loves one another.
essence: Holiness turns hostility into harmony.
simple_meaning: The mountain has become so blessed that nature itself feels peaceful there. Even creatures that usually live by fear or hostility now live in harmony.
insight: It shifts attention from decoration to atmosphere: real sanctity makes conflict lose its grip.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home where everyone is tense, and somehow one calm person changes the whole room. No one is forced to soften, yet the atmosphere does it for them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सोह सैल गिरिजा गृह आएँ। जिमि जनु रामभगति के पाएँ॥ नित नूतन मंगल गृह तासू। ब्रह्मादिक गावहिं जसु जासू ॥
translation: पार्वतीजी के घर आ जाने से पर्वत ऐसा शोभायमान हो रहा है जैसा रामभक्ति को पाकर भक्त शोभायमान होता है। उस (पर्वतराज) के घर नित्य नए-नए मंगलोत्सव होते हैं, जिसका ब्रह्मादि यश गाते हैं ॥
english_translation: The mountain shines with Girija’s arrival, just as a devotee shines upon gaining Ram-bhakti. His home holds ever-new celebrations, and Brahma and the other radiant beings sing his praise.
essence: Love turns an ordinary home into a place of continual auspiciousness.
simple_meaning: Parvati’s arrival makes the mountain-home radiant and full of celebration. Tulsidas compares that joy to the glow of a devotee who has gained loving devotion to Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from outer beauty to the joy created by loving presence and devotion.
modern_relevance: A house feels different the day someone you love walks back in after a long absence. The rooms are the same, but everything seems alive again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नारद समाचार सब पाए। कोतुकहीं गिरि गेह सिधाए॥ सैलराज बड़ आदर कीन्हा। पद पखारि बर आसनु दीन्हा ॥
translation: जब नारदजी ने ये सब समाचार सुने तो वे कौतुक ही से हिमाचल के घर पधारे। पर्वतराज ने उनका बड़ा आदर किया और चरण धोकर उनको उत्तम आसन दिया ॥
english_translation: When Narad heard all the news, he went to the mountain home out of curiosity. The mountain king showed him great respect, washed his feet, and offered him a fine seat.
essence: Honor opens the door before words do.
simple_meaning: Narad hears the news and visits the mountain palace. Himachal welcomes him with honor, washes his feet, and seats him respectfully.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the etiquette of reverence and welcome.
modern_relevance: A respected elder walks into your home, and you stop everything to greet them properly. The way you receive a guest reveals the culture of your heart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नारि सहित मुनि पद सिरु नावा। चरन सलिल सबु भवनु सिंचावा॥ निज सौभाग्य बहुत गिरि बरना। सुता बोलि मेली मुनि चरना ॥
translation: फिर अपनी स्त्री सहित मुनि के चरणों में सिर नवाया और उनके चरणोदक को सारे घर में छिड़काया। हिमाचल ने अपने सौभाग्य का बहुत बखान किया और पुत्री को बुलाकर मुनि के चरणों पर डाल दिया ॥
english_translation: Then, along with his wife, he bowed his head at the sage's feet and sprinkled the water from the sage's feet all over the house. Himachal praised his own great good fortune and called his daughter forward, placing her at the sage's feet.
essence: True honor is offering yourself, not just respect.
simple_meaning: Himachal honors the sage with full humility, uses the sacred foot-water to bless the home, and offers his daughter to the sage's feet.
insight: It shows how reverence moves from ceremony into surrender, preparing the heart to receive guidance.
modern_relevance: You welcome a revered teacher into your home and suddenly every gesture matters — the bow, the water, the words, the trust behind them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: त्रिकालग्य सर्बग्य तुम्ह गति सर्बत्र तुम्हारि। कहहु सुता के दोष गुन मुनिबर हृदयँ बिचारि ॥
translation: (और कहा-) हे मुनिवर! आप त्रिकालज्ञ और सर्वज्ञ हैं, आपकी सर्वत्र पहुँच है। अतः आप हृदय में विचार कर कन्या के दोष-गुण कहिए ॥
english_translation: O best of sages, you know the three times and are all-knowing; your reach is everywhere. So, reflect in your heart and speak of your daughter’s faults and virtues.
essence: True judgment sees both fault and virtue before speaking.
simple_meaning: Parvati asks Narada to judge her daughter fairly, because he is wise and can see everywhere. She wants him to think carefully and speak honestly about the girl's faults and virtues.
insight: It shifts the mind toward balanced evaluation: see both strengths and flaws before forming a judgment.
modern_relevance: You’re asking a trusted mentor for honest feedback before a big decision. You don’t want flattery — you want someone to look closely and tell the truth kindly.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: कह मुनि बिहसि गूढ़ मृदु बानी। सुता तुम्हारि सकल गुन खानी॥ सुंदर सहज सुसील सयानी। नाम उमा अंबिका भवानी ॥
translation: नारद मुनि ने हँसकर रहस्ययुक्त कोमल वाणी से कहा- तुम्हारी कन्या सब गुणों की खान है। यह स्वभाव से ही सुंदर, सुशील और समझदार है। उमा, अम्बिका और भवानी इसके नाम हैं ॥
english_translation: The sage smiled and spoke in soft, hidden words: “Your daughter is a mine of every virtue. She is beautiful, naturally gentle, well-mannered, and wise. Her names are Uma, Ambika, and Bhavani.”
essence: Gentle speech can bless more than it judges.
simple_meaning: Narada gently praises Parvati as naturally beautiful, virtuous, and wise, using her sacred names to honor her character.
insight: It teaches you to answer sensitive questions with kindness, precision, and respect.
modern_relevance: You’re introducing someone to parents who are anxious and watching every word. A thoughtful response can calm the room without lying or flattering too much.
speaker: Narada

verse_text: सब लच्छन संपन्न कुमारी। होइहि संतत पियहि पिआरी॥ सदा अचल एहि कर अहिवाता। एहि तें जसु पैहहिं पितु माता ॥
translation: कन्या सब सुलक्षणों से सम्पन्न है, यह अपने पति को सदा प्यारी होगी। इसका सुहाग सदा अचल रहेगा और इससे इसके माता-पिता यश पावेंगे ॥
english_translation: The maiden has every auspicious mark. She will always be dear to her husband. Her married life will remain unbroken, and her parents will gain honor through her.
essence: A woman’s virtue can bless her marriage and uplift her whole family.
simple_meaning: The girl is blessed with every good sign. She will remain dear to her husband, her married life will stay secure, and her parents will be honored through her.
insight: It shifts attention from display to lasting character, showing that true honor comes from the quality of one’s life and bonds.
modern_relevance: A family watches their daughter step into a new life, and everyone quietly hopes she will be cherished, respected, and safe. That wish for her well-being carries the whole room.
speaker: Narada

verse_text: होइहि पूज्य सकल जग माहीं। एहि सेवत कछु दुर्लभ नाहीं॥ एहि कर नामु सुमिरि संसारा। त्रिय चढ़िहहिं पतिब्रत असिधारा ॥
translation: यह सारे जगत में पूज्य होगी और इसकी सेवा करने से कुछ भी दुर्लभ न होगा। संसार में स्त्रियाँ इसका नाम स्मरण करके पतिव्रता रूपी तलवार की धार पर चढ़ जाएँगी ॥
english_translation: She will be revered throughout the world. Serving her brings nothing unattainable. By remembering her name, women will walk the razor’s edge of wifely fidelity.
essence: Her name becomes a support for steadfast fidelity.
simple_meaning: Nārada says Sita will be honored everywhere, and even remembering her name will help women uphold steadfast fidelity.
insight: It shifts admiration into imitation: remembering a noble example strengthens conduct.
modern_relevance: A young woman hears a story about someone who stayed loyal under pressure and feels steadier in her own choices. An ideal can become a support beam when life asks for integrity.
speaker: Nārada

verse_text: सैल सुलच्छन सुता तुम्हारी। सुनहु जे अब अवगुन दुइ चारी॥ अगुन अमान मातु पितु हीना। उदासीन सब संसय छीना ॥
translation: हे पर्वतराज! तुम्हारी कन्या सुलच्छनी है। अब इसमें जो दो-चार अवगुण हैं, उन्हें भी सुन लो। गुणहीन, मानहीन, माता-पिताविहीन, उदासीन, संशयहीन (लापरवाह) ॥
english_translation: O king of the mountain, your daughter is full of good marks. Listen now to the two or four faults in her. She is without qualities, without pride, without mother and father, and unconcerned, with all doubts cut away.
essence: Her greatest 'faults' are the marks of freedom.
simple_meaning: The speaker praises the princess, then lists playful 'faults': she has no pride, no worldly attachment, no parents to cling to, and no doubts or hesitation.
insight: It flips the meaning of weakness and shows that humility, detachment, and certainty can be the highest strengths.
modern_relevance: Someone calls you 'too simple' because you do not chase status, drama, or constant approval. What they call a lack may be the exact steadiness that makes you whole.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जोगी जटिल अकाम मन नगन अमंगल बेष। अस स्वामी एहि कहँ मिलिहि परी हस्त असि रेख ॥
translation: योगी, जटाधारी, निष्काम हृदय, नंगा और अमंगल वेष वाला, ऐसा पति इसको मिलेगा। इसके हाथ में ऐसी ही रेखा पड़ी है ॥
english_translation: A yogi, matted-haired, desireless, naked, and in an inauspicious garb—such a husband will she get. Such is the mark drawn on her hand.
essence: Outer appearance can hide the life that truly belongs.
simple_meaning: The child’s future husband is described as a renunciant with an inauspicious appearance, because that is what her hand-mark shows.
insight: It shifts attention from social image to the deeper truth of what a life is meant to hold.
modern_relevance: You hear a forecast that sounds nothing like the life you wanted. The first reaction is disappointment; the deeper question is whether appearances are hiding a greater fit.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुनि मुनि गिरा सत्य जियँ जानी। दुख दंपतिहि उमा हरषानी॥ नारदहूँ यह भेदु न जाना। दसा एक समुझब बिलगाना ॥
translation: नारद मुनि की वाणी सुनकर और उसको हृदय में सत्य जानकर पति-पत्नी (हिमवान् और मैना) को दुःख हुआ और पार्वतीजी प्रसन्न हुईं। नारदजी ने भी इस रहस्य को नहीं जाना, क्योंकि सबकी बाहरी दशा एक सी होने पर भी भीतरी समझ भिन्न-भिन्न थी ॥
english_translation: Hearing the sage's words, they knew them true in their hearts. The parents felt sorrow, and Uma felt joy. Even Narada did not know this hidden difference: though the outer state seemed the same, the inner understanding was different.
essence: The same words can become grief or joy, depending on the heart that receives them.
simple_meaning: The same words can land differently in different hearts. Himavan and Maina feel grief, while Uma feels joy, because each understands the same message in a different way.
insight: It trains you to notice that understanding depends on readiness, not just on hearing the same facts.
modern_relevance: A family hears the same diagnosis in the hospital corridor. One person hears disaster, another hears a path forward, and a third hears only noise. The words are identical; the inner state is not.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकल सखीं गिरिजा गिरि मैना। पुलक सरीर भरे जल नैना॥ होइ न मृषा देवरिषि भाषा। उमा सो बचनु हृदयँ धरि राखा ॥
translation: सारी सखियाँ, पार्वती, पर्वतराज हिमवान् और मैना सभी के शरीर पुलकित थे और सभी के नेत्रों में जल भरा था। देवर्षि के वचन असत्य नहीं हो सकते, (यह विचारकर) पार्वती ने उन वचनों को हृदय में धारण कर लिया ॥
english_translation: All the companions, Parvati, Himalaya, and Maina were thrilled, their eyes filled with tears. Thinking, “The words of the divine sage cannot be false,” Uma held those words in her heart.
essence: Trust lets a hard truth enter before it is fully understood.
simple_meaning: Parvati and her family are moved to tears and accept Narada's words as true. Parvati keeps that promise in her heart.
insight: It teaches you to receive a difficult truth without immediate resistance.
modern_relevance: A friend tells you something difficult to hear, and you feel the sting before you understand it. You do not dismiss it; you let it settle and watch what it changes in you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उपजेउ सिव पद कमल सनेहू। मिलन कठिन मन भा संदेहू॥ जानि कुअवसरु प्रीति दुराई। सखी उछँग बैठी पुनि जाई ॥
translation: उन्हें शिवजी के चरण कमलों में स्नेह उत्पन्न हो आया, परन्तु मन में यह संदेह हुआ कि उनका मिलना कठिन है। अवसर ठीक न जानकर उमा ने अपने प्रेम को छिपा लिया और फिर वे सखी की गोद में जाकर बैठ गईं ॥
english_translation: Love for Shiva's lotus feet arose in her heart, but she doubted whether meeting him would be difficult. Seeing the wrong moment, Uma hid her love and went back to sit in her companion's lap.
essence: True feeling can stay hidden until the right moment arrives.
simple_meaning: Uma feels devotion for Shiva, but she also feels doubt and hides that feeling for the moment.
insight: It shows how devotion can be inwardly alive even when outwardly restrained.
modern_relevance: You feel something deeply in a room where saying it would only make things awkward. So you smile, stay quiet, and wait for a better moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: झूठि न होइ देवरिषि बानी। सोचहिं दंपति सखीं सयानी॥ उर धरि धीर कहइ गिरिराऊ। कहहु नाथ का करिअ उपाऊ ॥
translation: देवर्षि की वाणी झूठी न होगी, यह विचार कर हिमवान् , मैना और सारी चतुर सखियाँ चिन्ता करने लगीं। फिर हृदय में धीरज धरकर पर्वतराज ने कहा- हे नाथ! कहिए, अब क्या उपाय किया जाए? ॥
english_translation: The sage's word cannot be false. The husband, wife, and wise attendants grew anxious. Keeping courage in his heart, the mountain king said, “Lord, tell me what should be done now.”
essence: Truth is accepted first; the next step is asked for second.
simple_meaning: They trust the sage's words, but that trust brings worry. Himavan stays steady and asks what remedy is possible now.
insight: It shifts the mind from fear to practical surrender: stop resisting the truth and ask for the next right step.
modern_relevance: You get a message that a difficult truth is probably real, and your first impulse is to spiral. Then you breathe, steady yourself, and ask the one useful question: what now?
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह मुनीस हिमवंत सुनु जो बिधि लिखा लिलार। देव दनुज नर नाग मुनि कोउ न मेटनिहार ॥
translation: मुनीश्वर ने कहा- हे हिमवान् ! सुनो, विधाता ने ललाट पर जो कुछ लिख दिया है, उसको देवता, दानव, मनुष्य, नाग और मुनि कोई भी नहीं मिटा सकते ॥
english_translation: The sage said, “Listen, Himavan: whatever fate has written on the forehead, no being can erase.”
essence: No force can erase what has already been written.
simple_meaning: Whatever has been written on the forehead cannot be erased by anyone, no matter how powerful or wise.
insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to acceptance of what cannot be changed.
modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone, hoping the verdict will change. The email is already sent, the result already fixed. Sometimes the only honest move is to stop wrestling what cannot be rewritten.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तदपि एक मैं कहउँ उपाई। होइ करै जौं दैउ सहाई॥ जस बरु मैं बरनेउँ तुम्ह पाहीं। मिलिहि उमहि तस संसय नाहीं ॥
translation: तो भी एक उपाय मैं बताता हूँ। यदि दैव सहायता करें तो वह सिद्ध हो सकता है। उमा को वर तो निःसंदेह वैसा ही मिलेगा, जैसा मैंने तुम्हारे सामने वर्णन किया है ॥
english_translation: Still, I will suggest one way. If the divine helps, it can succeed. The bride Uma will surely get the same groom I described to you.
essence: A workable path exists, but success still rests on grace.
simple_meaning: Shiva offers one possible solution, but only if divine help makes it work. He assures that Uma will get the same groom he has already described.
insight: It shifts the mind from rigid control to humble action supported by grace.
modern_relevance: You have a careful plan, but the room is still full of uncertainty. You can do your part clearly and still admit that some outcomes need help beyond you.
