speaker: Shiva

verse_text: जे जे बर के दोष बखाने। ते सब सिव पहिं मैं अनुमाने॥ जौं बिबाहु संकर सन होई। दोषउ गुन सम कह सबु कोई ॥
translation: परन्तु मैंने वर के जो-जो दोष बतलाए हैं, मेरे अनुमान से वे सभी शिवजी में हैं। यदि शिवजी के साथ विवाह हो जाए तो दोषों को भी सब लोग गुणों के समान ही कहेंगे ॥
english_translation: The faults I listed in a bridegroom all belong to Shiva in my view. If marriage happens with Shiva, everyone will call those faults virtues.
essence: Devotion rewrites defects as virtues.
simple_meaning: Parvati says that the flaws she mentioned in a bridegroom are not real flaws in Shiva. If Shiva becomes the husband, people will see those same traits as virtues.
insight: It shifts attention from social judgment to the lens of devotion, where character is seen as sacred rather than defective.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you care about through a thousand small habits that outsiders would call flaws. The same quiet, the same roughness, the same strangeness feels precious because love has already changed the verdict.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: जौं अहि सेज सयन हरि करहीं। बुध कछु तिन्ह कर दोषु न धरहीं॥ भानु कृसानु सर्ब रस खाहीं। तिन्ह कहँ मंद कहत कोउ नाहीं ॥
translation: जैसे विष्णु भगवान शेषनाग की शय्या पर सोते हैं, तो भी पण्डित लोग उनको कोई दोष नहीं लगाते। सूर्य और अग्निदेव अच्छे-बुरे सभी रसों का भक्षण करते हैं, परन्तु उनको कोई बुरा नहीं कहता ॥
english_translation: As Vishnu rests on Sheshnag, wise people do not blame him. The sun and fire consume every kind of essence, yet no one calls them bad.
essence: Great beings are measured by their nature, not by ordinary standards.
simple_meaning: Great beings are not judged by ordinary rules. What seems like a fault in them is part of their nature and power.
insight: It shifts judgment from surface appearance to the nature and role of what is being seen.
modern_relevance: You see a leader, teacher, or parent do something that would look wrong in anyone else. The mind rushes to judge. This verse asks you to pause and ask whether the same rule even applies.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुभ अरु असुभ सलिल सब बहई। सुरसरि कोउ अपुनीत न कहई॥ समरथ कहुँ नहिं दोषु गोसाईं। रबि पावक सुरसरि की नाईं ॥
translation: गंगाजी में शुभ और अशुभ सभी जल बहता है, पर कोई उन्हें अपवित्र नहीं कहता। सूर्य, अग्नि और गंगाजी की भाँति समर्थ को कुछ दोष नहीं लगता ॥
english_translation: Good and bad waters both flow in the river, yet no one calls the river impure. In the same way, no fault clings to the capable, just as it does not cling to the sun, fire, or the river.
essence: Real strength stays pure even in mixed surroundings.
simple_meaning: Pure and impure things can flow together, yet the river stays pure. In the same way, great beings are not diminished by the faults around them.
insight: It shifts judgment from surface contamination to inner capacity and steadiness.
modern_relevance: You work in a room full of gossip, shortcuts, and mixed motives, yet you keep your standards intact. That is what this verse defends: character strong enough to stay clean in contaminated surroundings.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जौं अस हिसिषा करहिं नर जड़ बिबेक अभिमान। परहिं कलप भरि नरक महुँ जीव कि ईस समान ॥
translation: यदि मूर्ख मनुष्य ज्ञान के अभिमान से इस प्रकार होड़ करते हैं, तो वे कल्पभर के लिए नरक में पड़ते हैं। भला कहीं जीव भी ईश्वर के समान (सर्वथा स्वतंत्र) हो सकता है? ॥
english_translation: If foolish people, out of pride in their understanding, compete like this, they fall into lower realms for ages. Can a living being ever be equal to the supreme being?
essence: Pride in insight collapses the very clarity it claims.
simple_meaning: Pride in one's own intelligence becomes a trap. A human being cannot claim the same freedom or power as the supreme reality.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to clear limits, so discernment can stay clean.
modern_relevance: You win an argument, then keep replaying it in your head because being right felt too good. The verse cuts that loop: intelligence without humility becomes self-destruction.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सुरसरि जल कृत बारुनि जाना। कबहुँ न संत करहिं तेहि पाना॥ सुरसरि मिलें सो पावन जैसें। ईस अनीसहि अंतरु तैसें ॥
translation: गंगा जल से भी बनाई हुई मदिरा को जानकर संत लोग कभी उसका पान नहीं करते। पर वही गंगाजी में मिल जाने पर जैसे पवित्र हो जाती है, ईश्वर और जीव में भी वैसा ही भेद है ॥
english_translation: Saints never drink liquor, even if it is made from Ganga water. When it mixes with the Ganga, it becomes pure; in the same way, there is a difference between the divine and the individual self.
essence: Contact can purify, but it never makes the finite infinite.
simple_meaning: Saints avoid impurity even in disguised form. The verse then says the divine and the individual self are not the same, just as polluted water becomes pure only by joining the Ganga.
insight: It shifts the mind from surface resemblance to essential distinction.
modern_relevance: A person may sit in the same room, wear the same clothes, and speak the same language as a mentor, but still not become that mentor. Proximity can refine you, but it does not erase the difference between source and reflection.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: संभु सहज समरथ भगवाना। एहि बिबाहँ सब बिधि कल्याना॥ दुराराध्य पै अहहिं महेसू। आसुतोष पुनि किएँ कलेसू ॥
translation: शिवजी सहज ही समर्थ हैं, क्योंकि वे भगवान हैं, इसलिए इस विवाह में सब प्रकार कल्याण है, परन्तु महादेवजी की आराधना बड़ी कठिन है, फिर भी क्लेश (तप) करने से वे बहुत जल्द संतुष्ट हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Shiva is naturally capable, for he is the divine. This marriage is blessed in every way. Yet Mahadeva is hard to win, and through hardship he becomes quickly pleased.
essence: What is hard to win yields to sincere hardship.
simple_meaning: Shiva is powerful and naturally auspicious, but he is not easy to please. He responds to sincere effort and austerity.
insight: It shifts devotion from casual wishing to serious, sustained practice that can actually transform a situation.
modern_relevance: You show up with a half-hearted apology, hoping the tension will vanish. It does not. Some things respond only when your effort becomes real and sustained.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जौं तपु करै कुमारि तुम्हारी। भाविउ मेटि सकहिं त्रिपुरारी॥ जद्यपि बर अनेक जग माहीं। एहि कहँ सिव तजि दूसर नाहीं ॥
translation: यदि तुम्हारी कन्या तप करे, तो त्रिपुरारि महादेवजी होनहार को मिटा सकते हैं। यद्यपि संसार में वर अनेक हैं, पर इसके लिए शिवजी को छोड़कर दूसरा वर नहीं है ॥
english_translation: If your daughter performs austerity, Tripurari can alter what is fated. Though many bridegrooms exist in the world, none but Shiva is fit for her.
essence: Some unions are so fitting they seem to rewrite fate.
simple_meaning: Shiva alone is the right match for this daughter, and his grace can overcome what seems fixed by fate.
insight: It shifts attention from social options to the deeper rightness of a bond.
modern_relevance: You meet someone and everyone has opinions, but one choice keeps feeling unmistakably right. This verse speaks to that quiet certainty that some bonds are not just convenient — they are fitting.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बर दायक प्रनतारति भंजन। कृपासिंधु सेवक मन रंजन॥ इच्छित फल बिनु सिव अवराधें। लहिअ न कोटि जोग जप साधें ॥
translation: शिवजी वर देने वाले, शरणागतों के दुःखों का नाश करने वाले, कृपा के समुद्र और सेवकों के मन को प्रसन्न करने वाले हैं। शिवजी की आराधना किए बिना करोड़ों योग और जप करने पर भी वांछित फल नहीं मिलता ॥
english_translation: Shiva is the giver of boons, the remover of the suffering of those who seek refuge, an ocean of grace, and delight to his servants. Without worshipping Shiva, even millions of yogic practices and chants cannot bring the desired result.
essence: Devotion opens what technique cannot reach.
simple_meaning: Shiva is praised as the one who grants boons, removes suffering, and delights his devotees. The verse says that even endless spiritual practice cannot replace worship of him.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to control outcomes through method alone to seeking the deeper source of blessing.
modern_relevance: You have done every technique, every checklist, every self-improvement hack, and still feel blocked. The verse says some doors open only through reverent relationship, not sheer technique.
speaker: Narada

verse_text: अस कहि नारद सुमिरि हरि गिरिजहि दीन्हि असीस। होइहि यह कल्यान अब संसय तजहु गिरीस ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर भगवान का स्मरण करके नारदजी ने पार्वती को आशीर्वाद दिया। (और कहा कि-) हे पर्वतराज! तुम संदेह का त्याग कर दो, अब यह कल्याण ही होगा ॥
english_translation: Having said this, Narada remembered Hari and blessed Girija. “This will bring welfare; O lord of the mountains, give up your doubt.”
essence: Blessing begins when doubt is released.
simple_meaning: Narada blesses Parvati after remembering Hari and tells Shiva to let go of doubt. He assures them that what follows will be auspicious.
insight: It shifts the mind from suspicion to trust in what is unfolding.
modern_relevance: A friend texts, “I think this will work out,” right after the interview that felt shaky. You do not have proof yet, but the reassurance steadies your chest.
speaker: Narada

verse_text: कहि अस ब्रह्मभवन मुनि गयऊ। आगिल चरित सुनहु जस भयऊ॥ पतिहि एकांत पाइ कह मैना। नाथ न मैं समुझे मुनि बैना ॥
translation: यों कहकर नारद मुनि ब्रह्मलोक को चले गए। अब आगे जो चरित्र हुआ उसे सुनो। पति को एकान्त में पाकर मैना ने कहा- हे नाथ! मैंने मुनि के वचनों का अर्थ नहीं समझा ॥
english_translation: Saying this, the sage Narada went to Brahmaloka. Hear now how the rest of the story unfolded. Finding her husband alone, Maina said, "Lord, I did not understand the sage's words."
essence: Uncertainty after a sacred message becomes the doorway to the next teaching.
simple_meaning: Narada leaves after speaking, and Maina tells her husband she did not understand the sage's words.
insight: It shifts attention from the speaker's departure to the listener's unresolved doubt, which drives the story forward.
modern_relevance: A conversation ends, and you replay the last sentence in your head while the room goes quiet. You know something important was said, but the meaning has not settled yet.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जौं घरु बरु कुलु होइ अनूपा। करिअ बिबाहु सुता अनुरूपा॥ न त कन्या बरु रहउ कुआरी। कंत उमा मम प्रानपिआरी ॥
translation: जो हमारी कन्या के अनुकूल घर, वर और कुल उत्तम हो तो विवाह कीजिए। नहीं तो लड़की चाहे कुमारी ही रहे (मैं अयोग्य वर के साथ उसका विवाह नहीं करना चाहती), क्योंकि हे स्वामिन् ! पार्वती मुझको प्राणों के समान प्यारी है ॥
english_translation: If the house, groom, and family are excellent, arrange the marriage to a fitting daughter. Otherwise, let the daughter remain unmarried; Parvati is dear to me as my own life.
essence: Love refuses a match that would wound the beloved.
simple_meaning: Maina says a daughter should marry only a truly suitable match. If no such match exists, it is better for her to remain unmarried than be joined badly.
insight: It teaches you to value fit over haste, and to protect dignity even under social pressure.
modern_relevance: A parent reviews a proposal and feels the pressure to say yes quickly. Maina's stance is different: affection must still have standards, or it stops protecting the one you love.
speaker: Maina

verse_text: जौं न मिलिहि बरु गिरिजहि जोगू। गिरि जड़ सहज कहिहि सबु लोगू॥ सोइ बिचारि पति करेहु बिबाहू। जेहिं न बहोरि होइ उर दाहू ॥
translation: यदि पार्वती के योग्य वर न मिला तो सब लोग कहेंगे कि पर्वत स्वभाव से ही जड़ (मूर्ख) होते हैं। हे स्वामी! इस बात को विचारकर ही विवाह कीजिएगा, जिसमें फिर पीछे हृदय में सन्ताप न हो ॥
english_translation: If no suitable groom is found for Girija, everyone will call the mountains foolish by nature. Thinking of that, O lord, arrange the marriage only in a way that leaves no later sorrow in the heart.
essence: Choose so the heart has no reason to burn later.
simple_meaning: Maina asks Shiva to arrange Parvati's marriage wisely, so no one can later mock the mountains and no regret will burn in the heart.
insight: It shifts the mind from immediate convenience to consequences that will return later.
modern_relevance: A parent signs the papers, then lies awake replaying every clause and compromise. One rushed choice can echo for years; this verse asks for foresight before commitment.
speaker: Maina

verse_text: अस कहि परी चरन धरि सीसा। बोले सहित सनेह गिरीसा॥ बरु पावक प्रगटै ससि माहीं। नारद बचनु अन्यथा नाहीं ॥
translation: इस प्रकार कहकर मैना पति के चरणों पर मस्तक रखकर गिर पड़ीं। तब हिमवान् ने प्रेम से कहा- चाहे चन्द्रमा में अग्नि प्रकट हो जाए, पर नारदजी के वचन झूठे नहीं हो सकते ॥
english_translation: Saying this, Maina fell at her husband's feet and bowed her head. Then Himavan said with love, "Even if fire appears in the moon, Narad's words cannot be false."
essence: Faith holds firm when the mind cannot verify the outcome.
simple_meaning: Maina bows in humility, and Himavan affirms that Narad's words are certain, even if they seem impossible.
insight: It shifts the mind from demanding proof to resting in trustworthy guidance.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a message from someone wiser than you, but the plan still looks impossible. This verse says: some guidance is worth trusting before it makes sense.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रिया सोचु परिहरहु सबु सुमिरहु श्रीभगवान। पारबतिहि निरमयउ जेहिं सोइ करिहि कल्यान ॥
translation: हे प्रिये! सब सोच छोड़कर श्री भगवान का स्मरण करो, जिन्होंने पार्वती को रचा है, वे ही कल्याण करेंगे ॥
english_translation: Beloved, let go of all worry and remember the Supreme Lord. The one who created Parvati will bring welfare.
essence: Trust the one who made her to protect her future.
simple_meaning: Worry is unnecessary when the divine power that created Parvati is being remembered. Trust that same power to bring a good result.
insight: It shifts attention from anxious prediction to trust in a greater order.
modern_relevance: You are refreshing your phone for news about your child, your interview, your test. The mind keeps spinning. This verse asks for one clean move: stop feeding fear and place the outcome in higher hands.
speaker: Himavan

verse_text: अब जौं तुम्हहि सुता पर नेहू। तौ अस जाइ सिखावनु देहू॥ करै सो तपु जेहिं मिलहिं महेसू। आन उपायँ न मिटिहि कलेसू ॥
translation: अब यदि तुम्हें कन्या पर प्रेम है, तो जाकर उसे यह शिक्षा दो कि वह ऐसा तप करे, जिससे शिवजी मिल जाएँ। दूसरे उपाय से यह क्लेश नहीं मिटेगा ॥
english_translation: If you truly love your daughter, then teach her this: let her perform such tapas that she attains Shiva. No other means will end this sorrow.
essence: True love guides longing toward its rightful fulfillment.
simple_meaning: Himavan says that if he truly loves his daughter, he should guide her toward the tapas that leads to Shiva. No other remedy can remove her sorrow.
insight: It shifts support from soothing feelings to guiding someone toward the discipline that matches their deepest longing.
modern_relevance: Your friend is heartbroken over someone they cannot forget. You can offer distractions, or you can help them choose the one practice that actually changes their life.
speaker: Himavan

verse_text: नारद बचन सगर्भ सहेतू। सुंदर सब गुन निधि बृषकेतू॥ अस बिचारि तुम्ह तजहु असंका। सबहि भाँति संकरु अकलंका ॥
translation: नारदजी के वचन रहस्य से युक्त और सकारण हैं और शिवजी समस्त सुंदर गुणों के भण्डार हैं। यह विचारकर तुम (मिथ्या) संदेह को छोड़ दो। शिवजी सभी तरह से निष्कलंक हैं ॥
english_translation: Narad's words are meaningful and well-grounded. Shiva, the Bull-bannered one, is a treasure-house of all beautiful qualities. Thinking this way, you should abandon doubt. Shiva is flawless in every respect.
essence: Doubt falls when character is seen clearly.
simple_meaning: Narad's words are sincere and justified, and Shiva is full of noble qualities. So abandon doubt and trust Shiva's purity.
insight: It shifts the mind from suspicion to settled trust by recalling character, not gossip.
modern_relevance: A friend warns you not to trust someone, but you know the person’s character from years of steady conduct. You stop feeding suspicion and look at the evidence of who they have always been.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सुनि पति बचन हरषि मन माहीं। गई तुरत उठि गिरिजा पाहीं॥ उमहि बिलोकि नयन भरे बारी। सहित सनेह गोद बैठारी ॥
translation: पति के वचन सुन मन में प्रसन्न होकर मैना उठकर तुरंत पार्वती के पास गईं। पार्वती को देखकर उनकी आँखों में आँसू भर आए। उसे स्नेह के साथ गोद में बैठा लिया ॥
english_translation: Hearing her husband's words, Maina felt joy in her heart. She rose at once and went to Girija. Seeing Uma, tears filled her eyes. With affection, she seated her in her lap.
essence: Trust turns hesitation into tears and tenderness.
simple_meaning: Maina hears her husband's words, feels glad, and goes at once to see Parvati. When she sees her daughter, tears come to her eyes and she holds her lovingly in her lap.
insight: It shifts attention from suspicion to affectionate reconnection, showing how trust restores warmth fast.
modern_relevance: You get a call that changes the mood of the whole house. One sentence from someone you trust, and the fear loosens before you even realize it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बारहिं बार लेति उर लाई। गदगद कंठ न कछु कहि जाई॥ जगत मातु सर्बग्य भवानी। मातु सुखद बोलीं मृदु बानी ॥ सुनहि मातु मैं दीख अस सपन सुनावउँ तोहि। सुंदर गौर सुबिप्रबर अस उपदेसेउ मोहि ॥
translation: फिर बार-बार उसे हृदय से लगाने लगीं। प्रेम से मैना का गला भर आया, कुछ कहा नहीं जाता। जगज्जननी भवानीजी तो सर्वज्ञ ठहरीं। (माता के मन की दशा को जानकर) वे माता को सुख देने वाली कोमल वाणी से बोलीं- ॥ माँ! सुन, मैं तुझे सुनाती हूँ, मैंने ऐसा स्वप्न देखा है कि मुझे एक सुंदर गौरवर्ण श्रेष्ठ ब्राह्मण ने ऐसा उपदेश दिया है- ॥
english_translation: Again and again she held her close to her heart. Her throat choked with love, and she could say nothing. Bhavani, the all-knowing mother of the world, then spoke gently to comfort her mother: “Listen, Mother. I will tell you a dream. A beautiful, fair Brahmin gave me this teaching.”
essence: Gentle reassurance prepares the heart for truth.
simple_meaning: Parvati comforts her mother with gentle words and begins to explain a dream in which a noble Brahmin gave her a teaching.
insight: It shows that reassurance opens the way for guidance; tenderness comes before instruction.
modern_relevance: You sit beside a parent who is upset, holding their hand while your own voice shakes. Before advice can help, care has to soften the room.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: करहि जाइ तपु सैलकुमारी। नारद कहा सो सत्य बिचारी॥ मातु पितहि पुनि यह मत भावा। तपु सुखप्रद दुख दोष नसावा ॥
translation: हे पार्वती! नारदजी ने जो कहा है, उसे सत्य समझकर तू जाकर तप कर। फिर यह बात तेरे माता-पिता को भी अच्छी लगी है। तप सुख देने वाला और दुःख-दोष का नाश करने वाला है ॥
english_translation: O daughter of the mountain, go and perform austerity, taking Narada's words as true. Your parents also approve this counsel. Austerity brings ease and destroys suffering and flaws.
essence: Austerity clears suffering and strengthens the life within.
simple_meaning: Parvati is told to accept Narada's advice and go do austerity. Her parents agree, and the verse praises austerity as something that brings ease and removes suffering and flaws.
insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to sustained practice, treating discipline as cleansing rather than punishment.
modern_relevance: You know that moment when a mentor's hard advice finally lands, and even your family quietly agrees? This is that turning point: stop circling the decision and begin the practice.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तपबल रचइ प्रपंचु बिधाता। तपबल बिष्नु सकल जग त्राता॥ तपबल संभु करहिं संघारा। तपबल सेषु धरइ महिभारा ॥
translation: तप के बल से ही ब्रह्मा संसार को रचते हैं और तप के बल से ही बिष्णु सारे जगत का पालन करते हैं। तप के बल से ही शम्भु (रुद्र रूप से) जगत का संहार करते हैं और तप के बल से ही शेषजी पृथ्वी का भार धारण करते हैं ॥
english_translation: By the power of tapas, the Creator creates the world. By the power of tapas, Vishnu protects the whole world. By the power of tapas, Shiva destroys. By the power of tapas, Shesha bears the weight of the earth.
essence: Tapas is the hidden power behind every great act.
simple_meaning: Disciplined effort is shown as the force behind all cosmic functions: creation, protection, destruction, and support. The verse praises tapas as the energy that makes everything possible.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing discipline as sacrifice to seeing it as the hidden force that sustains everything.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up before dawn while everyone else sleeps, training for a race or caring for a sick parent. What looks ordinary is what holds the whole day together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तप अधार सब सृष्टि भवानी। करहि जाइ तपु अस जियँ जानी॥ सुनत बचन बिसमित महतारी। सपन सुनायउ गिरिहि हँकारी ॥
translation: हे भवानी! सारी सृष्टि तप के ही आधार पर है। ऐसा जी में जानकर तू जाकर तप कर। यह बात सुनकर माता को बड़ा अचरज हुआ और उसने हिमवान् को बुलाकर वह स्वप्न सुनाया ॥
english_translation: O Bhavani, all creation rests on tapas. Knowing this in your heart, go and perform tapas. Hearing these words, the mother was astonished and called Himalaya, then told him the dream.
essence: Creation itself depends on disciplined effort.
simple_meaning: Tapas is presented as the basis of creation, and Parvati is urged to undertake it. Her mother is amazed by the message and tells Himalaya about the dream.
insight: It frames discipline as the hidden support of all becoming, not a punishment or side task.
modern_relevance: A parent hears their child say, with total certainty, that a hard path is calling them. The room goes still. What looks like delay is actually the preparation for a life-changing calling.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मातु पितहि बहुबिधि समुझाई। चलीं उमा तप हित हरषाई॥ प्रिय परिवार पिता अरु माता। भए बिकल मुख आव न बाता ॥ बेदसिरा मुनि आइ तब सबहि कहा समुझाइ। पारबती महिमा सुनत रहे प्रबोधहि पाइ ॥
translation: माता-पिता को बहुत तरह से समझाकर बड़े हर्ष के साथ पार्वतीजी तप करने के लिए चलीं। प्यारे कुटुम्बी, पिता और माता सब व्याकुल हो गए। किसी के मुँह से बात नहीं निकलती ॥ तब वेदशिरा मुनि ने आकर सबको समझाकर कहा। पार्वतीजी की महिमा सुनकर सबको समाधान हो गया ॥
english_translation: After reassuring her parents in many ways, Uma joyfully set out to do tapas. Her dear family, father, and mother were all distraught; no one could speak. Then the sage Vedashira came and explained everything to them, and hearing of Parvati's greatness, they were comforted.
essence: A worthy discipline can wound the family that loves you.
simple_meaning: Parvati leaves for austerity after reassuring her parents, while her family grieves until a sage consoles them by explaining her greatness.
insight: It shows that discipline can require leaving comfort behind, and that others may need time to understand the sacrifice.
modern_relevance: You accept a fellowship overseas, and your parents go silent at the dinner table. You know the choice is right, but you also feel the cost. This verse understands both sides.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उर धरि उमा प्रानपति चरना। जाइ बिपिन लागीं तपु करना॥ अति सुकुमार न तनु तप जोगू। पति पद सुमिरि तजेउ सबु भोगू ॥
translation: प्राणपति (शिवजी) के चरणों को हृदय में धारण करके पार्वतीजी वन में जाकर तप करने लगीं। पार्वतीजी का अत्यन्त सुकुमार शरीर तप के योग्य नहीं था, तो भी पति के चरणों का स्मरण करके उन्होंने सब भोगों को तज दिया ॥
english_translation: Holding the feet of her lord in her heart, Uma went into the forest to practice austerity. Her body was very delicate and unsuited for austerity, yet remembering her husband's feet, she gave up all pleasures.
essence: Remembrance of the beloved makes hardship bearable.
simple_meaning: Uma leaves comfort behind and goes into the forest to practice austerity, keeping Shiva in her heart. Though her body is delicate, her devotion makes her give up every pleasure.
insight: It shifts the mind from comfort-seeking to disciplined remembrance of what you value most.
modern_relevance: You cancel the soft weekend plans, turn off the phone, and sit with the hard thing you keep avoiding. What carries you is not toughness, but love for what matters.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नित नव चरन उपज अनुरागा। बिसरी देह तपहिं मनु लागा॥ संबत सहस मूल फल खाए। सागु खाइ सत बरष गवाँए ॥
translation: स्वामी के चरणों में नित्य नया अनुराग उत्पन्न होने लगा और तप में ऐसा मन लगा कि शरीर की सारी सुध बिसर गई। एक हजार वर्ष तक उन्होंने मूल और फल खाए, फिर सौ वर्ष साग खाकर बिताए ॥
english_translation: A fresh love for the lotus feet kept rising every day, and the mind became absorbed in austerity until the body was forgotten. For a thousand years they lived on roots and fruits, then spent a hundred years eating only greens.
essence: Devotion makes endurance feel natural.
simple_meaning: Parvati's devotion keeps deepening. She becomes so absorbed in penance that she forgets her body and lives for years on very simple food.
insight: It shifts the mind from measuring discomfort to sustaining devotion through repetition.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up for a hard practice long after the novelty is gone — the run, the study session, the caregiving shift — because something deeper than comfort now drives you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कछु दिन भोजनु बारि बतासा। किए कठिन कछु दिन उपबासा॥ बेल पाती महि परइ सुखाई। तीनि सहस संबत सोइ खाई ॥
translation: कुछ दिन जल और वायु का भोजन किया और फिर कुछ दिन कठोर उपवास किए, जो बेल पत्र सूखकर पृथ्वी पर गिरते थे, तीन हजार वर्ष तक उन्हीं को खाया ॥
english_translation: For some days she lived on water and air; for some days she kept a hard fast. When bel leaves dried and fell to the ground, she ate only those for three thousand years.
essence: Steady restraint can become a force stronger than appetite.
simple_meaning: Parvati kept intensifying her austerity: first water and air, then hard fasting, then only dried bel leaves for three thousand years.
insight: It shifts attention from dramatic effort to sustained restraint over time.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up before sunrise while everyone else sleeps, repeating the same practice until it changes you. Progress often looks like this: quiet, severe, and invisible.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि परिहरे सुखानेउ परना। उमहि नामु तब भयउ अपरना॥ देखि उमहि तप खीन सरीरा। ब्रह्मगिरा भै गगन गभीरा ॥
translation: फिर सूखे पर्ण (पत्ते) भी छोड़ दिए, तभी पार्वती का नाम 'अपर्णा' हुआ। तप से उमा का शरीर क्षीण देखकर आकाश से गंभीर ब्रह्मवाणी हुई- ॥
english_translation: She even gave up dry leaves. Then Uma became Aparna. Seeing Uma's body weakened by austerity, a grave voice from the sky spoke.
essence: Total devotion can become a new identity.
simple_meaning: Uma gives up even dry leaves as food. Because of this extreme austerity, she becomes known as Aparna, and a deep heavenly voice speaks when her body grows frail.
insight: It shows that devotion can become so total that even self-denial turns into identity.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up for something that matters, even when comfort is gone and your energy is low. The name changes when the commitment becomes complete.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भयउ मनोरथ सुफल तव सुनु गिरिराजकुमारि। परिहरु दुसह कलेस सब अब मिलिहहिं त्रिपुरारि ॥
translation: हे पर्वतराज की कुमारी! सुन, तेरा मनोरथ सफल हुआ। तू अब सारे असह्य क्लेशों को (कठिन तप को) त्याग दे। अब तुझे शिवजी मिलेंगे ॥
english_translation: O daughter of the mountain king, listen: your wish has borne fruit. Give up all unbearable hardship now. Shiva will meet you.
essence: Your longing has ripened; now release the strain.
simple_meaning: Parvati is told that her long penance has succeeded, and she can stop the severe hardship because Shiva will now come to her.
insight: It teaches that sincere effort can reach a point where the outcome arrives on its own.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up before dawn, training for months, and nothing seems to move. Then the moment comes when the work quietly opens its own door.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: अस तपु काहुँ न कीन्ह भवानी। भए अनेक धीर मुनि ग्यानी॥ अब उर धरहु ब्रह्म बर बानी। सत्य सदा संतत सुचि जानी ॥
translation: हे भवानी! धीर, मुनि और ज्ञानी बहुत हुए हैं, पर ऐसा (कठोर) तप किसी ने नहीं किया। अब तू इस श्रेष्ठ ब्रह्मा की वाणी को सदा सत्य और निरंतर पवित्र जानकर अपने हृदय में धारण कर ॥
english_translation: Bhavani, no one has performed austerity like this. Many steadfast sages and knowers have existed. Keep this supreme word of Brahma in your heart, knowing it always true and pure.
essence: Rare effort must be met with steady trust.
simple_meaning: No one has done austerity like this before. Brahma's word should be held in the heart as always true and pure.
insight: It shifts attention from proving your effort to receiving confirmation with trust.
modern_relevance: You have pushed through months of practice, waiting, and uncertainty, and then the guidance finally arrives. The harder part now is not effort — it's trusting the answer enough to let it land.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आवै पिता बोलावन जबहीं। हठ परिहरि घर जाएहु तबहीं॥ मिलहिं तुम्हहि जब सप्त रिषीसा। जानेहु तब प्रमान बागीसा ॥
translation: जब तेरे पिता बुलाने को आवें, तब हठ छोड़कर घर चली जाना और जब तुम्हें सप्तर्षि मिलें तब इस वाणी को ठीक समझना ॥
english_translation: When your father calls you, then leave your stubbornness and go home. When you meet the seven great sages, then know this speech to be true.
essence: Truth ripens in stages; stubbornness must yield before confirmation arrives.
simple_meaning: Parvati is told to stop resisting, return home when her father calls, and trust the message when the seven sages confirm it.
insight: It shifts the mind from forcing certainty to recognizing the right timing of confirmation.
modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone, waiting for someone to finally confirm what you already feel. This verse says: stop forcing it, go home, and let reality answer in its own time.
speaker: Brahma

verse_text: सुनत गिरा बिधि गगन बखानी। पुलक गात गिरिजा हरषानी॥ उमा चरित सुंदर मैं गावा। सुनहु संभु कर चरित सुहावा ॥
translation: (इस प्रकार) आकाश से कही हुई ब्रह्मा की वाणी को सुनते ही पार्वतीजी प्रसन्न हो गईं और (हर्ष के मारे) उनका शरीर पुलकित हो गया। (याज्ञवल्क्यजी भरद्वाजजी से बोले कि-) मैंने पार्वती का सुंदर चरित्र सुनाया, अब शिवजी का सुहावना चरित्र सुनो ॥
english_translation: Hearing the voice spoken from the sky, Parvati rejoiced, and her body thrilled with joy. "I have sung the lovely story of Uma; now listen to the graceful story of Shiva."
essence: Joy at confirmation opens the way to the next teaching.
simple_meaning: Parvati is delighted when she hears Brahma's message from the sky. Yajnavalkya then shifts from Uma's story to Shiva's story.
insight: It marks a transition from Parvati's testing to Shiva's deeper story.
modern_relevance: You finally hear the answer you were waiting for after a long stretch of uncertainty. Relief arrives first; only then does the next part of the story become possible.
speaker: Yajnavalkya

verse_text: जब तें सतीं जाइ तनु त्यागा। तब तें सिव मन भयउ बिरागा॥ जपहिं सदा रघुनायक नामा। जहँ तहँ सुनहिं राम गुन ग्रामा ॥
translation: जब से सती ने जाकर शरीर त्याग किया, तब से शिवजी के मन में वैराग्य हो गया। वे सदा श्री रघुनाथजी का नाम जपने लगे और जहाँ-तहाँ श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुणों की कथाएँ सुनने लगे ॥
english_translation: Since Sati abandoned her body, Shiva's mind turned away from worldly attachment. He always chanted the name of Raghunath and listened everywhere to the stories of Ram's virtues.
essence: Loss can strip attachment and deepen remembrance.
simple_meaning: After Sati left her body, Shiva became detached from worldly attachment. He kept repeating Ram's name and listening to Ram's stories everywhere.
insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to remembrance and devotional listening.
modern_relevance: A relationship ends, and instead of spiraling into replaying the hurt, you begin walking, breathing, and returning to what steadies you. Grief can either trap you or redirect you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चिदानंद सुखधाम सिव बिगत मोह मद काम। बिचरहिं महि धरि हृदयँ हरि सकल लोक अभिराम ॥
translation: चिदानन्द, सुख के धाम, मोह, मद और काम से रहित शिवजी सम्पूर्ण लोकों को आनंद देने वाले भगवान श्री हरि (श्री रामचन्द्रजी) को हृदय में धारण कर (भगवान के ध्यान में मस्त हुए) पृथ्वी पर विचरने लगे ॥
english_translation: Shiva, the abode of bliss and consciousness, free from delusion, pride, and desire, wandered the earth with Ram in his heart, delighting all the worlds.
essence: A heart filled with Ram turns presence itself into blessing.
simple_meaning: Shiva, free from delusion, pride, and desire, walked the earth with Ram held in his heart, bringing joy to all beings.
insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to a lived presence that quietly benefits everyone nearby.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who has stopped needing attention, status, or validation. They still move through the world, but their calm changes the atmosphere around them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कतहुँ मुनिन्ह उपदेसहिं ग्याना। कतहुँ राम गुन करहिं बखाना॥ जदपि अकाम तदपि भगवाना। भगत बिरह दुख दुखित सुजाना ॥
translation: वे कहीं मुनियों को ज्ञान का उपदेश करते और कहीं श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुणों का वर्णन करते थे। यद्यपि सुजान शिवजी निष्काम हैं, तो भी वे भगवान अपने भक्त (सती) के वियोग के दुःख से दुःखी हैं ॥
english_translation: He taught wisdom to the sages here and praised Ram's virtues there. Though Shiva is desireless, he still feels the sorrow of separation from his devotee.
essence: True detachment still feels the wound of loving separation.
simple_meaning: Shiva spends his time teaching sages and praising Ram, yet he still feels pain when separated from his devotee.
insight: It shifts devotion from a ritual act to a living bond that can feel absence.
modern_relevance: You can be composed in public, giving guidance to others, while still carrying a private ache for someone you love. Strength does not erase tenderness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि बिधि गयउ कालु बहु बीती। नित नै होइ राम पद प्रीती॥ नेमु प्रेमु संकर कर देखा। अबिचल हृदयँ भगति कै रेखा ॥
translation: इस प्रकार बहुत समय बीत गया। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में नित नई प्रीति हो रही है। शिवजी के (कठोर) नियम, (अनन्य) प्रेम और उनके हृदय में भक्ति की अटल टेक को (जब श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने) देखा ॥
english_translation: In this way, much time passed, and Shiva's love for Ram's feet grew ever new. When Ram saw Shiva's vow, love, and the unbroken line of devotion in his heart...
essence: Time tests devotion and makes it more alive.
simple_meaning: Time passes, but Shiva's love for Ram only deepens. Ram sees Shiva's steady vow, loving heart, and unbroken devotion.
insight: It shifts attention from intensity to constancy, showing that devotion matures through repetition.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone or something long after the first excitement is gone. The feeling is no longer new, but the bond has become deeper, steadier, and harder to break.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रगटे रामु कृतग्य कृपाला। रूप सील निधि तेज बिसाला॥ बहु प्रकार संकरहि सराहा। तुम्ह बिनु अस ब्रतु को निरबाहा ॥
translation: तब कृतज्ञ (उपकार मानने वाले), कृपालु, रूप और शील के भण्डार, महान् तेजपुंज भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी प्रकट हुए। उन्होंने बहुत तरह से शिवजी की सराहना की और कहा कि आपके बिना ऐसा (कठिन) व्रत कौन निबाह सकता है ॥
english_translation: Then Ram appeared—grateful, compassionate, a treasure of beauty and virtue, vast in radiance. In many ways he praised Shiva and said, “Without you, who could carry out such a vow?”
essence: Even the divine honors sincere devotion with gratitude.
simple_meaning: Ram appears in radiant form and praises Shiva, saying that such a vow could not be fulfilled without him.
insight: It shifts devotion from one-sided worship to mutual recognition and gratitude.
modern_relevance: You finally finish a hard promise with help from someone who stayed behind the scenes. The relief is not just success — it is being seen and thanked by the person you served.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुबिधि राम सिवहि समुझावा। पारबती कर जन्मु सुनावा॥ अति पुनीत गिरिजा कै करनी। बिस्तर सहित कृपानिधि बरनी ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने बहुत प्रकार से शिवजी को समझाया और पार्वतीजी का जन्म सुनाया। कृपानिधान श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने विस्तारपूर्वक पार्वतीजी की अत्यन्त पवित्र करनी का वर्णन किया ॥
english_translation: Ram explained many things to Shiva and told him of Parvati's birth. The treasure of compassion, Ram, described Girija's supremely pure conduct in detail.
essence: Respect opens the way before any request is made.
simple_meaning: Ram explains Parvati's birth to Shiva and praises her pure conduct in detail.
insight: It teaches you to begin with reverence, not demand.
modern_relevance: You are trying to ask for something important, but first you show respect for the other person's values. That careful recognition can open the door more than pressure ever will.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अब बिनती मम सुनहु सिव जौं मो पर निज नेहु। जाइ बिबाहहु सैलजहि यह मोहि मागें देहु ॥
translation: (फिर उन्होंने शिवजी से कहा-) हे शिवजी! यदि मुझ पर आपका स्नेह है, तो अब आप मेरी विनती सुनिए। मुझे यह माँगें दीजिए कि आप जाकर पार्वती के साथ विवाह कर लें ॥
english_translation: Then Ram said to Shiva: "If you love me, listen to my request. Grant me this: go and marry Parvati."
essence: Love asks without demanding, and reverence answers it.
simple_meaning: Ram asks Shiva to accept his loving request and marry Parvati. The line shows Ram speaking with affection and honor toward Shiva.
insight: It shifts attention from command to loving invitation, where relationship matters more than force.
modern_relevance: A child asks a parent for something not as a demand, but as a sign of trust. The request itself carries love: "If you care for me, hear me."
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कह सिव जदपि उचित अस नाहीं। नाथ बचन पुनि मेटि न जाहीं॥ सिर धरि आयसु करिअ तुम्हारा। परम धरमु यह नाथ हमारा ॥
translation: शिवजी ने कहा- यद्यपि ऐसा उचित नहीं है, परन्तु स्वामी की बात भी मेटी नहीं जा सकती। हे नाथ! मेरा यही परम धर्म है कि मैं आपकी आज्ञा को सिर पर रखकर उसका पालन करूँ ॥
english_translation: Shiva said, “Even if this is not proper, a lord’s command cannot be undone. I bear your order on my head; this is my highest duty, my lord.”
essence: Duty begins where personal opinion ends.
simple_meaning: Shiva says that even if something feels improper, a lord's command cannot be ignored. He treats obedience to that command as his highest duty.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal preference to rightful responsibility.
modern_relevance: Your manager asks you to fix a messy mistake you did not create. You know it is awkward, but you do it cleanly because the responsibility is now yours.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: मातु पिता गुर प्रभु कै बानी। बिनहिं बिचार करिअ सुभ जानी॥ तुम्ह सब भाँति परम हितकारी। अग्या सिर पर नाथ तुम्हारी ॥
translation: माता, पिता, गुरु और स्वामी की बात को बिना ही विचारे शुभ समझकर करना (मानना) चाहिए। फिर आप तो सब प्रकार से मेरे परम हितकारी हैं। हे नाथ! आपकी आज्ञा मेरे सिर पर है ॥
english_translation: The words of mother, father, teacher, and master should be accepted as good without hesitation. You are my greatest well-wisher in every way, O Lord. Your command rests on my head.
essence: Right guidance is obeyed before the mind starts arguing.
simple_meaning: A child should accept the words of parents, teacher, and master as right without arguing. Shiva says Ram is his greatest well-wisher, so Ram's command is above his own will.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to obedient trust in rightful guidance.
modern_relevance: Your mentor gives you hard feedback after a messy mistake, and your first urge is to defend yourself. This verse asks for a different move: hear the correction first, ego second.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: प्रभु तोषेउ सुनि संकर बचना। भक्ति बिबेक धर्म जुत रचना॥ कह प्रभु हर तुम्हार पन रहेऊ। अब उर राखेहु जो हम कहेऊ ॥
translation: शिवजी की भक्ति, ज्ञान और धर्म से युक्त वचन रचना सुनकर प्रभु रामचन्द्रजी संतुष्ट हो गए। प्रभु ने कहा- हे हर! आपकी प्रतिज्ञा पूरी हो गई। अब हमने जो कहा है, उसे हृदय में रखना ॥
english_translation: Rama was pleased to hear Shiva's words, full of devotion, discernment, and dharma. Rama said, “O Hari, your vow is fulfilled. Now keep in your heart what I have said.”
essence: Devotion is complete only when the heart keeps what it hears.
simple_meaning: Ram is pleased by Shiva's devotional words and confirms that Shiva's vow has been fulfilled. He then asks Shiva to keep Ram's instruction in his heart.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to relationship: reverence is completed by remembrance.
modern_relevance: You finally hear the apology, the gratitude, or the recognition you hoped for. The moment is not just relief — it becomes a shared bond when the other person asks you to carry the exchange forward.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: अंतरधान भए अस भाषी। संकर सोइ मूरति उर राखी॥ तबहिं सप्तरिषि सिव पहिं आए। बोले प्रभु अति बचन सुहाए ॥
translation: इस प्रकार कहकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी अन्तर्धान हो गए। शिवजी ने उनकी वह मूर्ति अपने हृदय में रख ली। उसी समय सप्तर्षि शिवजी के पास आए। प्रभु महादेवजी ने उनसे अत्यन्त सुहावने वचन कहे- ॥
english_translation: After speaking thus, Shri Ramchandra disappeared. Shiva kept that very image in his heart. Then the seven sages came to Shiva, and the Lord spoke to them with very pleasing words.
essence: What devotion receives, the heart keeps.
simple_meaning: Ram disappears after speaking. Shiva holds Ram's image in his heart. Then the seven sages arrive, and Shiva speaks kindly to them.
insight: It shifts attention from what disappears outwardly to what devotion preserves inwardly.
modern_relevance: Someone leaves the room after a brief, life-changing conversation. The words are over, but the presence stays with you, and you carry it into the next meeting.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पारबती पहिं जाइ तुम्ह प्रेम परिच्छा लेहु। गिरिहि प्रेरि पठएहु भवन दूरि करेहु संदेहु ॥
translation: आप लोग पार्वती के पास जाकर उनके प्रेम की परीक्षा लीजिए और हिमाचल को कहकर (उन्हें पार्वती को लिवा लाने के लिए भेजिए तथा) पार्वती को घर भिजवाइए और उनके संदेह को दूर कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Go to Parvati and test her love. Ask Himachal to send her home and remove her doubt.
essence: Love proves itself when doubt is cleared.
simple_meaning: Go to Parvati, test her love, and remove the doubt that still surrounds her choice.
insight: It shifts attention from outward display to the steadiness of love under scrutiny.
modern_relevance: A family is waiting for a decision that will change everything, but one person still hesitates. Before the next step, the doubt has to be cleared honestly.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: रिषिन्ह गौरि देखी तहँ कैसी। मूरतिमंत तपस्या जैसी॥ बोले मुनि सुनु सैलकुमारी। करहु कवन कारन तपु भारी ॥
translation: ऋषियों ने (वहाँ जाकर) पार्वती को कैसी देखा, मानो मूर्तिमान् तपस्या ही हो। मुनि बोले- हे शैलकुमारी! सुनो, तुम किसलिए इतना कठोर तप कर रही हो? ॥
english_translation: The sages saw Parvati there, like living austerity itself. The sage said, “Listen, daughter of the mountain: why are you performing such severe penance?”
essence: Austerity without its reason still invites a question.
simple_meaning: The sages see Parvati as the living form of austerity and ask why she is doing such severe penance.
insight: It shifts attention from the outward display of discipline to the motive beneath it.
modern_relevance: A friend notices you skipping meals, sleeping less, and pushing yourself hard for something no one else can see. The first question is not praise — it is: what are you doing this for?
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: केहि अवराधहु का तुम्ह चहहू। हम सन सत्य मरमु किन कहहू॥ कहत बचन मनु अति सकुचाई। हँसिहहु सुनि हमारि जड़ताई ॥
translation: तुम किसकी आराधना करती हो और क्या चाहती हो? हमसे अपना सच्चा भेद क्यों नहीं कहतीं? (पार्वती ने कहा-) बात कहते मन बहुत सकुचाता है। आप लोग मेरी मूर्खता सुनकर हँसेंगे ॥
english_translation: Who do you worship, and what do you want? Why not tell us your true secret? Parvati said, "My mind feels very shy to speak. You will laugh when you hear my foolishness."
essence: True longing is shy before it becomes speech.
simple_meaning: Parvati asks who she should worship and what she truly wants, but she feels shy to reveal her heart because she fears being laughed at.
insight: It shows how devotion begins with trust enough to speak what the mind wants to hide.
modern_relevance: You start to answer a question in a group chat, then delete it three times because it feels too honest. The heart often knows first; the voice arrives later.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: मनु हठ परा न सुनइ सिखावा। चहत बारि पर भीति उठावा॥ नारद कहा सत्य सोइ जाना। बिनु पंखन्ह हम चहहिं उड़ाना ॥
translation: मन ने हठ पकड़ लिया है, वह उपदेश नहीं सुनता और जल पर दीवाल उठाना चाहता है। नारदजी ने जो कह दिया उसे सत्य जानकर मैं बिना ही पाँख के उड़ना चाहती हूँ ॥
english_translation: The mind has grown stubborn; it will not listen to instruction and wants to raise a wall on water. Narada spoke the truth, and I know it: without wings, I still want to fly.
essence: Desire can make the mind deny what it already knows.
simple_meaning: Parvati admits that her mind has become stubborn. She knows Narada spoke the truth, yet she still wants the impossible: to fly without wings.
insight: It exposes the mind's refusal to learn when desire has taken over, and invites honest self-observation.
modern_relevance: You know the advice is right, but you keep checking the same message, chasing the same person, making the same impossible plan. Wanting can make the mind ignore reality.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: देखहु मुनि अबिबेकु हमारा। चाहिअ सदा सिवहि भरतारा ॥
translation: हे मुनियों! आप मेरा अज्ञान तो देखिए कि मैं सदा शिवजी को ही पति बनाना चाहती हूँ ॥
english_translation: O sages, look at my lack of discernment: I always wish for Shiva as my husband.
essence: True devotion chooses one beloved without hesitation.
simple_meaning: Parvati humbly admits to the sages that she wants Shiva alone as her husband.
insight: It shifts attention from social approval to wholehearted devotion.
modern_relevance: You know that moment when everyone expects you to be practical, but your heart has already chosen? You stop explaining and simply name what you want.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: सुनत बचन बिहसे रिषय गिरिसंभव तव देह। नारद कर उपदेसु सुनि कहहु बसेउ किसु गेह ॥
translation: पार्वतीजी की बात सुनते ही ऋषि लोग हँस पड़े और बोले- तुम्हारा शरीर पर्वत से ही तो उत्पन्न हुआ है! भला, कहो तो नारद का उपदेश सुनकर आज तक किसका घर बसा है? ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, the sages laughed and said: 'O daughter of the mountain, your body arose from the mountain itself! Tell us, after hearing Narada's counsel, whose household has ever truly settled?'
essence: True counsel can unsettle the household before it reveals a higher calling.
simple_meaning: The sages laugh at Parvati's statement and point out that Narada's advice has a strange effect: it unsettles household life instead of settling it.
insight: It shifts attention from social comfort to the disruptive power of true counsel.
modern_relevance: A friend gives you advice that sounds wise, but it leaves your plans wobbling instead of secure. Sometimes the right teaching does not make life tidier first — it makes false certainty collapse.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दच्छसुतन्ह उपदेसेन्हि जाई। तिन्ह फिरि भवनु न देखा आई॥ चित्रकेतु कर घरु उन घाला। कनककसिपु कर पुनि अस हाला ॥
translation: उन्होंने जाकर दक्ष के पुत्रों को उपदेश दिया था, जिससे उन्होंने फिर लौटकर घर का मुँह भी नहीं देखा। चित्रकेतु के घर को नारद ने ही चौपट किया। फिर यही हाल हिरण्यकशिपु का हुआ ॥
english_translation: He went and instructed the sons of Daksha, and they never returned home again. Narada ruined the house of Citraketu, and the same happened with Hiranyakashipu.
essence: True teaching can sever old attachments in a single stroke.
simple_meaning: Narada's teaching turned those who heard him away from ordinary household life. The verse lists famous examples to show how strongly his words changed people.
insight: It shifts attention from social normalcy to the force of transformative instruction.
modern_relevance: You hear one honest conversation and suddenly your old routine feels thin. A mentor, book, or warning can do that — it can break a comfortable life open.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नारद सिख जे सुनहिं नर नारी। अवसि होहिं तजि भवनु भिखारी॥ मन कपटी तन सज्जन चीन्हा। आपु सरिस सबही चह कीन्हा ॥
translation: जो स्त्री-पुरुष नारद की सीख सुनते हैं, वे घर-बार छोड़कर अवश्य ही भिखारी हो जाते हैं। उनका मन तो कपटी है, शरीर पर सज्जनों के चिह्न हैं। वे सभी को अपने समान बनाना चाहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who listen to Narad's teaching, men or women, certainly become beggars after leaving home. Their mind is deceitful, while their body wears the marks of a saint. They want to make everyone like themselves.
essence: Outer sainthood means nothing if the mind stays crooked.
simple_meaning: People who blindly follow Narad's advice leave ordinary life behind, but their outer appearance can hide a crooked mind. They often try to reshape others in their own image.
insight: It shifts attention from outward holiness to inner honesty and exposes the danger of moral imitation without transformation.
modern_relevance: Someone quotes a spiritual line on social media, dresses the part, and sounds elevated at dinner—but still manipulates everyone around them. The warning is about mismatch between appearance and mind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहि कें बचन मानि बिस्वासा। तुम्ह चाहहु पति सहज उदासा॥ निर्गुन निलज कुबेष कपाली। अकुल अगेह दिगंबर ब्याली ॥
translation: उनके वचनों पर विश्वास मानकर तुम ऐसा पति चाहती हो जो स्वभाव से ही उदासीन, गुणहीन, निर्लज्ज, बुरे वेषवाला, नर-कपालों की माला पहनने वाला, कुलहीन, बिना घर-बार का, नंगा और शरीर पर साँपों को लपेटे रखने वाला है ॥
english_translation: Believing his words, you want a husband who is naturally detached, without qualities, shameless, oddly dressed, wearing a garland of skulls, without lineage, without a home, naked, and wrapped in serpents.
essence: Borrowed praise can turn sacred choice into confusion.
simple_meaning: The speaker mocks Sati for wanting a husband who is detached, unconventional, and frightening in appearance.
insight: It shifts the mind from accepting reputation at face value to examining what the words are really claiming.
modern_relevance: A friend forwards a polished message about someone you barely know, and suddenly everyone sounds convincing. This verse warns how easily borrowed opinions can distort judgment.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: कहहु कवन सुखु अस बरु पाएँ। भल भूलिहु ठग के बौराएँ॥ पंच कहें सिवँ सती बिबाही। पुनि अवडेरि मराएन्हि ताही ॥
translation: ऐसे वर के मिलने से कहो, तुम्हें क्या सुख होगा? तुम उस ठग (नारद) के बहकावे में आकर खूब भूलीं। पहले पंचों के कहने से शिव ने सती से विवाह किया था, परन्तु फिर उसे त्यागकर मरवा डाला॥
english_translation: What happiness would you gain from finding such a husband? You have been badly misled by that trickster. At first, on the advice of the council, Shiva married Sati, but later he abandoned her and caused her death.
essence: Blind trust in bad advice turns choice into regret.
simple_meaning: A false guide can make a choice look wise when it is not. The verse warns that blind trust in bad advice brings pain and regret.
insight: It shifts the mind from obedience to scrutiny, asking you to test advice before surrendering to it.
modern_relevance: A friend forwards a confident voice note, and you almost act on it before checking the facts. The damage from one bad recommendation can take years to undo.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अब सुख सोवत सोचु नहिं भीख मागि भव खाहिं। सहज एकाकिन्ह के भवन कबहुँ कि नारि खटाहिं ॥
translation: अब शिव को कोई चिन्ता नहीं रही, भीख माँगकर खा लेते हैं और सुख से सोते हैं। ऐसे स्वभाव से ही अकेले रहने वालों के घर भी भला क्या कभी स्त्रियाँ टिक सकती हैं? ॥
english_translation: Now Shiva has no worry. He begs for food and sleeps in comfort. Can a woman ever stay in the home of one who is naturally alone?
essence: A life built for solitude cannot easily hold domestic life.
simple_meaning: Shiva is described as carefree and naturally solitary. The verse argues that a woman would not stay long in the home of someone who lives like that.
insight: It frames compatibility as a matter of lived nature, not just affection or clever argument.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who loves silence, freedom, and living out of a backpack. You love homes, routines, and shared meals. The gap is not small — it shapes the whole future.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अजहूँ मानहु कहा हमारा। हम तुम्ह कहुँ बरु नीक बिचारा॥ अति सुंदर सुचि सुखद सुसीला। गावहिं बेद जासु जस लीला ॥
translation: अब भी हमारा कहा मानो, हमने तुम्हारे लिए अच्छा वर विचारा है। वह बहुत ही सुंदर, पवित्र, सुखदायक और सुशील है, जिसका यश और लीला वेद गाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Still accept what I say. I have chosen a good bridegroom for you. He is very beautiful, pure, delightful, and well-mannered; the Vedas sing of his fame and play.
essence: Trust the one who sees the worth you cannot yet see.
simple_meaning: Shiva tells Parvati to trust his choice. The bridegroom he has in mind is beautiful, pure, gracious, and praised by the Vedas.
insight: It shifts attention from doubt to reverent trust in a wiser judgment.
modern_relevance: A parent reassures a worried family that the person they chose is truly worthy. The details matter, but the deeper message is simpler: let wisdom speak before suspicion takes over.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: दूषन रहित सकल गुन रासी। श्रीपति पुर बैकुंठ निवासी॥ अस बरु तुम्हहि मिलाउब आनी। सुनत बिहसि कह बचन भवानी ॥
translation: वह दोषों से रहित, सारे सद् गुणों की राशि, लक्ष्मी का स्वामी और वैकुण्ठपुरी का रहने वाला है। हम ऐसे वर को लाकर तुमसे मिला देंगे। यह सुनते ही पार्वतीजी हँसकर बोलीं- ॥
english_translation: He is free of faults, a treasury of every virtue, the lord of Lakshmi, and a resident of Vaikuntha. "I will bring you such a bridegroom," she said. Hearing this, Parvati smiled and replied:
essence: Ram is praised as the faultless source of every virtue.
simple_meaning: Shiva describes Ram as flawless, full of virtues, and fit to be the ideal bridegroom. Parvati hears this and smiles, about to answer.
insight: It shifts attention from outward description to inward recognition of Ram's worth.
modern_relevance: You hear someone speak about a person they truly admire, and their voice changes. The praise is not performance — it reveals recognition, affection, and certainty all at once.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सत्य कहेहु गिरिभव तनु एहा। हठ न छूट छूटै बरु देहा॥ कनकउ पुनि पषान तें होई। जारेहुँ सहजु न परिहर सोई ॥
translation: आपने यह सत्य ही कहा कि मेरा यह शरीर पर्वत से उत्पन्न हुआ है, इसलिए हठ नहीं छूटेगा, शरीर भले ही छूट जाए। सोना भी पत्थर से ही उत्पन्न होता है, सो वह जलाए जाने पर भी अपने स्वभाव (सुवर्णत्व) को नहीं छोड़ता ॥
english_translation: You have spoken truthfully: my body is born of the mountain, so stubbornness will not leave it even if the body falls away. Gold comes from stone; even when burned, it does not give up its nature.
essence: Deep nature survives pressure; force cannot easily remake it.
simple_meaning: Parvati admits her stubborn resolve: even death will not change her nature. She compares herself to gold that keeps its essential quality even under fire.
insight: It shifts attention from surface promises to the enduring shape of character under pressure.
modern_relevance: You keep saying you'll soften, compromise, and let it go. Then the same old reaction returns in the first hard conversation. Parvati names that deep pattern without pretending it is easy to erase.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: नारद बचन न मैं परिहरऊँ। बसउ भवनु उजरउ नहिं डरउँ॥ गुर कें बचन प्रतीति न जेही। सपनेहुँ सुगम न सुख सिधि तेही ॥
translation: अतः मैं नारदजी के वचनों को नहीं छोड़ूँगी, चाहे घर बसे या उजड़े, इससे मैं नहीं डरती। जिसको गुरु के वचनों में विश्वास नहीं है, उसको सुख और सिद्धि स्वप्न में भी सुगम नहीं होती ॥
english_translation: I will not abandon Narad's words. I do not fear whether the home stands or falls. One who does not trust the guru's words cannot easily find happiness or success, even in dreams.
essence: Trust in guidance opens the door that effort alone cannot.
simple_meaning: Parvati says she will not abandon Narad's counsel, even if her home is ruined. Trust in the guru's words is what makes happiness and success possible.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to receptivity, making guidance more important than comfort.
modern_relevance: Your mentor gives you hard advice that doesn't flatter you. You can keep defending your old plan, or you can let the guidance land and change course before the damage grows.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: महादेव अवगुन भवन बिष्नु सकल गुन धाम। जेहि कर मनु रम जाहि सन तेहि तेही सन काम ॥
translation: माना कि महादेवजी अवगुणों के भवन हैं और विष्णु समस्त सद् गुणों के धाम हैं, पर जिसका मन जिसमें रम गया, उसको तो उसी से काम है ॥
english_translation: Mahadev is the abode of faults and Vishnu the home of all virtues; yet the mind seeks whatever it is attached to.
essence: Love decides the mind’s allegiance more than praise or blame.
simple_meaning: People are drawn to what their mind already loves. Labels about virtue or fault matter less than where the heart is actually settled.
insight: It shifts the reader from judging objects by reputation to examining where the mind repeatedly returns.
modern_relevance: You keep saying you want one thing, but your browser history, late-night scrolling, and secret habits keep pulling you elsewhere. Your attention reveals your real devotion.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: जौं तुम्ह मिलतेहु प्रथम मुनीसा। सुनतिउँ सिख तुम्हारि धरि सीसा॥ अब मैं जन्मु संभु हित हारा। को गुन दूषन करै बिचारा ॥
translation: हे मुनीश्वरों! यदि आप पहले मिलते, तो मैं आपका उपदेश सिर-माथे रखकर सुनती, परन्तु अब तो मैं अपना जन्म शिवजी के लिए हार चुकी! फिर गुण-दोषों का विचार कौन करे? ॥
english_translation: O sages, if you had come first, I would have held your teaching to my head. But now I have given my life to Shiva. Who would still weigh virtues and faults?
essence: Once the heart has chosen, fault-finding loses its power.
simple_meaning: Parvati says she would have listened to the sages earlier, but now she has given herself to Shiva, so judging by merits and faults no longer matters to her.
insight: It shifts attention from weighing options to honoring the commitment already made.
modern_relevance: You already chose your person, your path, your promise. At that point, endless comparison stops feeling wise and starts feeling disloyal.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: जौं तुम्हरे हठ हृदयँ बिसेषी। रहि न जाइ बिनु किएँ बरेषी॥ तौ कौतुकिअन्ह आलसु नाहीं। बर कन्या अनेक जग माहीं ॥
translation: यदि आपके हृदय में बहुत ही हठ है और विवाह की बातचीत (बरेखी) किए बिना आपसे रहा ही नहीं जाता, तो संसार में वर-कन्या बहुत हैं। खिलवाड़ करने वालों को आलस्य तो होता नहीं (और कहीं जाकर कीजिए) ॥
english_translation: If your heart is so stubborn that you cannot stop without a formal proposal, then there are many brides and grooms in the world. Let the playful ones take no rest.
essence: Dignity can answer pressure with a smile.
simple_meaning: Sita says that if someone insists on a formal marriage proposal, there are plenty of other brides and grooms in the world. She answers with sharp wit, not submission.
insight: It teaches you to hold your ground without anger, using wit to protect your dignity.
modern_relevance: A relative keeps pushing, “So when are you settling down?” You smile, but you do not bend. Sita’s reply is the voice of self-respect under pressure.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: जन्म कोटि लगि रगर हमारी। बरउँ संभु न त रहउँ कुआरी॥ तजउँ न नारद कर उपदेसू। आपु कहहिं सत बार महेसू ॥
translation: मेरा तो करोड़ जन्मों तक यही हठ रहेगा कि या तो शिवजी को वरूँगी, नहीं तो कुमारी ही रहूँगी। स्वयं शिवजी सौ बार कहें, तो भी नारदजी के उपदेश को न छोड़ूँगी ॥
english_translation: My resolve will last for countless births: I will marry Shiva, or remain unmarried. I will not abandon Narada's counsel, even if Shiva himself speaks a hundred times.
essence: True devotion does not bend just because the pressure repeats.
simple_meaning: Parvati says her vow is fixed: she will marry Shiva or stay unmarried forever. She will not give up Narada's advice, even if Shiva says otherwise many times.
insight: It shifts the mind from external persuasion to inner commitment.
modern_relevance: A family keeps pushing you toward the “practical” choice, but you already know what your heart has chosen. Parvati’s steadiness is the courage to stay with a vow under pressure.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: मैं पा परउँ कहइ जगदंबा। तुम्ह गृह गवनहु भयउ बिलंबा॥ देखि प्रेमु बोले मुनि ग्यानी। जय जय जगदंबिके भवानी ॥
translation: जगज्जननी पार्वतीजी ने फिर कहा कि मैं आपके पैरों पड़ती हूँ। आप अपने घर जाइए, बहुत देर हो गई। (शिवजी में पार्वतीजी का ऐसा) प्रेम देखकर ज्ञानी मुनि बोले- हे जगज्जननी! हे भवानी! आपकी जय हो! जय हो!! ॥
english_translation: The Mother of the universe said, “I bow at your feet. Please go home; it has grown late.” Seeing such love, the wise sage exclaimed, “Victory, victory to the Mother of the universe, Bhavani!”
essence: True love bows, even while asking someone to leave.
simple_meaning: Parvati lovingly asks Shiva to go home, and the sage responds with praise at her devotion.
insight: It shows that reverence and intimacy can exist together without conflict.
modern_relevance: You keep one eye on the clock while someone you love lingers at the door, unwilling to end the moment. Real affection can be soft, patient, and still direct.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: तुम्ह माया भगवान सिव सकल गजत पितु मातु। नाइ चरन सिर मुनि चले पुनि पुनि हरषत गातु ॥
translation: आप माया हैं और शिवजी भगवान हैं। आप दोनों समस्त जगत के माता-पिता हैं। (यह कहकर) मुनि पार्वतीजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर चल दिए। उनके शरीर बार-बार पुलकित हो रहे थे ॥
english_translation: You are the divine veil, and Shiva and the entire world are your father and mother. After bowing to Parvati's feet, the sages departed, their bodies trembling with repeated joy.
essence: Humility ends the exchange; joy remains.
simple_meaning: The sages honor Parvati respectfully and leave, filled with joy. The scene closes the exchange between Parvati and Shiva's framing narration.
insight: It shifts the reader from argument to reverence, showing how humility ends tension.
modern_relevance: You finish a heartfelt conversation, lower your head in gratitude, and walk away lighter than before. Some moments do not need more explanation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जाइ मुनिन्ह हिमवंतु पठाए। करि बिनती गिरजहिं गृह ल्याए॥ बहुरि सप्तरिषि सिव पहिं जाई। कथा उमा कै सकल सुनाई ॥
translation: मुनियों ने जाकर हिमवान् को पार्वतीजी के पास भेजा और वे विनती करके उनको घर ले आए, फिर सप्तर्षियों ने शिवजी के पास जाकर उनको पार्वतीजी की सारी कथा सुनाई ॥
english_translation: The sages went and sent Himavan to Parvati. They persuaded her and brought her home. Then the seven sages went to Shiva and told him all of Uma's story.
essence: Reconciliation often begins when one wise messenger carries the whole story.
simple_meaning: The sages first bring Himavan to Parvati, then go to Shiva and explain everything that happened with Uma.
insight: It shows the value of mediation: separate hearts are reached one by one before harmony returns.
modern_relevance: A family argument cools only after one trusted person talks to each side separately. Before resolution comes, someone has to carry the story carefully.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भए मगन सिव सुनत सनेहा। हरषि सप्तरिषि गवने गेहा॥ मनु थिर करि तब संभु सुजाना। लगे करन रघुनायक ध्याना ॥
translation: पार्वतीजी का प्रेम सुनते ही शिवजी आनन्दमग्न हो गए। सप्तर्षि प्रसन्न होकर अपने घर (ब्रह्मलोक) को चले गए। तब सुजान शिवजी मन को स्थिर करके श्री रघुनाथजी का ध्यान करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Shiva became absorbed with joy on hearing of Parvati's love. The Saptarishis, pleased, returned to their home. Then wise Shiva steadied his mind and began meditating on Raghunath.
essence: Joy in love naturally settles into meditation on Ram.
simple_meaning: Shiva feels joy on hearing about Parvati's love, and then turns his steady mind toward meditating on Ram.
insight: It shifts devotion from emotion alone into settled remembrance.
modern_relevance: You hear someone speak warmly about the person you revere, and your whole mood softens. After the room empties, you sit quietly and return to the one presence that steadies you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तारकु असुर भयउ तेहि काला। भुज प्रताप बल तेज बिसाला॥ तेहिं सब लोक लोकपति जीते। भए देव सुख संपति रीते ॥
translation: उसी समय तारक नाम का असुर हुआ, जिसकी भुजाओं का बल, प्रताप और तेज बहुत बड़ा था। उसने सब लोक और लोकपालों को जीत लिया, सब देवता सुख और सम्पत्ति से रहित हो गए ॥
english_translation: At that time, the demon Taraka arose, immense in arm-strength, power, and radiance. He conquered all worlds and their rulers, and the radiant beings were stripped of joy and prosperity.
essence: Unchecked power empties the world around it.
simple_meaning: Taraka, a powerful demon, rose at that time and conquered all the worlds, leaving the radiant beings deprived of joy and prosperity.
insight: It frames oppression as the natural result of power severed from restraint.
modern_relevance: A person or system grows unchecked, dominates every room, and leaves everyone else drained. The danger is not just strength — it is strength without limits.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अजर अमर सो जीति न जाई। हारे सुर करि बिबिध लराई॥ तब बिरंचि सन जाइ पुकारे। देखे बिधि सब देव दुखारे ॥
translation: वह अजर-अमर था, इसलिए किसी से जीता नहीं जाता था। देवता उसके साथ बहुत तरह की लड़ाइयाँ लड़कर हार गए। तब उन्होंने ब्रह्माजी के पास जाकर पुकार मचाई। ब्रह्माजी ने सब देवताओं को दुःखी देखा ॥
english_translation: He was deathless, so no one could defeat him. The radiant beings fought him in many ways and lost. Then they went to Brahma and cried out for help. Brahma saw all the radiant beings in sorrow.
essence: Force fails against what cannot yet be ended.
simple_meaning: That demon could not be defeated because he had no death. The radiant beings tried many battles and still lost, so they went to Brahma for help.
insight: It shifts attention from repeated struggle to the need for a deeper remedy.
modern_relevance: You keep trying the same fix on the same problem, and nothing changes. At some point, the answer is not more force — it is a wiser question.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब सन कहा बुझाइ बिधि दनुज निधन तब होइ। संभु सुक्र संभूत सुत एहि जीतइ रन सोइ ॥
translation: ब्रह्माजी ने सबको समझाकर कहा- इस दैत्य की मृत्यु तब होगी जब शिवजी के वीर्य से पुत्र उत्पन्न हो, इसको युद्ध में वही जीतेगा ॥
english_translation: Brahma explained to everyone: this demon will die only when a son is born from Shiva's seed; only he will defeat him in battle.
essence: The enemy falls only when the right cause is born.
simple_meaning: Brahma tells the gods that the demon can only be killed by a son born from Shiva's power.
insight: It shifts attention from repeated effort to the deeper cause that must be created first.
modern_relevance: A team keeps trying the same fixes and nothing changes. Then someone finally names the real condition that must exist before the problem can end.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मोर कहा सुनि करहु उपाई। होइहि ईस्वर करिहि सहाई॥ सतीं जो तजी दच्छ मख देहा। जनमी जाइ हिमाचल गेहा ॥
translation: मेरी बात सुनकर उपाय करो। ईश्वर सहायता करेंगे और काम हो जाएगा। सतीजी ने जो दक्ष के यज्ञ में देह का त्याग किया था, उन्होंने अब हिमाचल के घर जाकर जन्म लिया है ॥
english_translation: Listen to my words and take a remedy. The divine will help, and the task will be done. Sati, who gave up her body in Daksha's sacrifice, has now been born in Himachal's house.
essence: Help arrives when the larger order is trusted.
simple_meaning: Shiva tells Parvati to trust the divine help and explains that Sati has now taken birth in Himachal's home after leaving her previous body.
insight: It shifts the mind from panic to trust in a larger order already at work.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a problem that feels sealed shut. Someone wiser says: stop forcing the whole answer, take the next right step, and let help arrive in its own time.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: तेहिं तपु कीन्ह संभु पति लागी। सिव समाधि बैठे सबु त्यागी॥ जदपि अहइ असमंजस भारी। तदपि बात एक सुनहु हमारी ॥
translation: उन्होंने शिवजी को पति बनाने के लिए तप किया है, इधर शिवजी सब छोड़-छाड़कर समाधि लगा बैठे हैं। यद्यपि है तो बड़े असमंजस की बात, तथापि मेरी एक बात सुनो ॥
english_translation: She performed austerity to win Shiva as husband. Shiva sat in meditation, abandoning everything. Though the situation is highly puzzling, still listen to my one suggestion.
essence: A blocked situation needs a clear next move, not panic.
simple_meaning: Parvati is describing a strange situation: she has done austerity for Shiva, but Shiva remains absorbed in meditation and detached from everything. She is about to propose a way forward.
insight: It shifts attention from the impossible-looking situation to the first practical step that can change it.
modern_relevance: Two people want the same future, but one is withdrawn and unreachable. Before forcing a solution, someone has to name the problem clearly and listen for the next right move.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: पठवहु कामु जाइ सिव पाहीं। करै छोभु संकर मन माहीं॥ तब हम जाइ सिवहि सिर नाई। करवाउब बिबाहु बरिआई ॥
translation: तुम जाकर कामदेव को शिवजी के पास भेजो, वह शिवजी के मन में क्षोभ उत्पन्न करे (उनकी समाधि भंग करे)। तब हम जाकर शिवजी के चरणों में सिर रख देंगे और जबरदस्ती (उन्हें राजी करके) विवाह करा देंगे ॥
english_translation: Send Kama to Shiva. Let him stir Shiva's mind. Then we will go bow to Shiva and arrange the marriage by force.
essence: Great aims often need both strategy and reverence.
simple_meaning: The gods decide to send Kama to disturb Shiva's deep meditation, then bow to Shiva and press for the marriage.
insight: It shows that wise action can combine strategy, humility, and timing.
modern_relevance: A team knows the main decision-maker is deeply set in a position. Instead of forcing the issue, they first prepare the ground, then approach with respect and a clear plan.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि बिधि भलेहिं देवहित होई। मत अति नीक कहइ सबु कोई॥ अस्तुति सुरन्ह कीन्हि अति हेतू। प्रगटेउ बिषमबान झषकेतू ॥
translation: इस प्रकार से भले ही देवताओं का हित हो (और तो कोई उपाय नहीं है) सबने कहा- यह सम्मति बहुत अच्छी है। फिर देवताओं ने बड़े प्रेम से स्तुति की। तब विषम (पाँच) बाण धारण करने वाला और मछली के चिह्नयुक्त ध्वजा वाला कामदेव प्रकट हुआ ॥
english_translation: In this way, everyone agreed that this was the best course for the gods' welfare. Then the gods praised him with deep affection, and Kamadeva appeared, bearing five arrows and the banner marked with a fish.
essence: A risky plan becomes clear when everyone agrees to the cost.
simple_meaning: The gods agree that this plan is best for them, and they praise Kamadeva so he will appear and help.
insight: It frames the mission as a collective choice and prepares for decisive action.
modern_relevance: A group chat settles on the one uncomfortable plan nobody loves but everyone knows is necessary. Then someone steps up to do the hard part, and the whole room exhales.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुरन्ह कही निज बिपति सब सुनि मन कीन्ह बिचार। संभु बिरोध न कुसल मोहि बिहसि कहेउ अस मार ॥
translation: देवताओं ने कामदेव से अपनी सारी विपत्ति कही। सुनकर कामदेव ने मन में विचार किया और हँसकर देवताओं से यों कहा कि शिवजी के साथ विरोध करने में मेरी कुशल नहीं है ॥
english_translation: The gods told Kamadeva their whole plight. Hearing it, Kamadeva thought it over and laughed, saying, "I have no success in opposing Shiva."
essence: Clear seeing begins with admitting a force you cannot casually oppose.
simple_meaning: The gods explain their problem to Kamadeva. He thinks it over and admits that opposing Shiva will not end well for him.
insight: It shifts the mind from impulsive action to clear-eyed assessment of risk and consequence.
modern_relevance: Your friends want you to push a risky idea in a meeting, but you can already feel the room's resistance. Before speaking, you quietly assess whether the fight is worth it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तदपि करब मैं काजु तुम्हारा। श्रुति कह परम धरम उपकारा॥ पर हित लागि तजइ जो देही। संतत संत प्रसंसहिं तेही ॥
translation: तथापि मैं तुम्हारा काम तो करूँगा, क्योंकि वेद दूसरे के उपकार को परम धर्म कहते हैं। जो दूसरे के हित के लिए अपना शरीर त्याग देता है, संत सदा उसकी बड़ाई करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Still, I will do your work, because the Vedas call helping others the highest dharma. Those who give up their own body for another's good are always praised by the wise.
essence: Helping another is the highest law of action.
simple_meaning: Helping others is the highest duty. A person who gives up even his own body for someone else's good is praised by good people.
insight: It shifts action from self-protection to service, treating sacrifice for others as the mark of a noble life.
modern_relevance: You stay late to finish a task that protects your team, even though no one can repay you. The quiet respect you feel afterward is exactly what this verse honors.
speaker: Kamadeva

verse_text: अस कहि चलेउ सबहि सिरु नाई। सुमन धनुष कर सहित सहाई॥ चलत मार अस हृदयँ बिचारा। सिव बिरोध ध्रुब मरनु हमारा ॥
translation: यों कह और सबको सिर नवाकर कामदेव अपने पुष्प के धनुष को हाथ में लेकर (वसन्तादि) सहायकों के साथ चला। चलते समय कामदेव ने हृदय में ऐसा विचार किया कि शिवजी के साथ विरोध करने से मेरा मरण निश्चित है ॥
english_translation: Saying this, he bowed to everyone and departed with his flower-bow and helpers. As he walked, Kama thought in his heart, "Opposing Shiva means certain death for me."
essence: He goes forward knowing the cost may be his life.
simple_meaning: Kama leaves respectfully with his helpers, but he knows opposing Shiva will surely destroy him.
insight: It shows that commitment can continue even when the mind foresees danger.
modern_relevance: You say yes to a hard task, then feel the knot in your stomach as you walk into the meeting. Courage and fear can travel together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब आपन प्रभाउ बिस्तारा। निज बस कीन्ह सकल संसारा॥ कोपेउ जबहिं बारिचरकेतू। छन महुँ मिटे सकल श्रुति सेतू ॥
translation: तब उसने अपना प्रभाव फैलाया और समस्त संसार को अपने वश में कर लिया। जिस समय उस मछली के चिह्न की ध्वजा वाले कामदेव ने कोप किया, उस समय क्षणभर में ही वेदों की सारी मर्यादा मिट गई ॥
english_translation: Then he spread his influence and brought the whole world under his control. When Kamadeva, whose flag bears the fish emblem, grew angry, the boundary set by the Vedas vanished in an instant.
essence: Desire can erase discipline in a moment.
simple_meaning: Kamadeva spreads his power over the world, and when he becomes angry, even the limits set by the Vedas collapse at once.
insight: It shifts attention from outer order to the power of desire to dissolve inner discipline.
modern_relevance: A single notification, one glance, one craving, and the whole careful plan you built at night can start unraveling before breakfast.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ब्रह्मचर्ज ब्रत संजम नाना। धीरज धरम ग्यान बिग्याना॥ सदाचार जप जोग बिरागा। सभय बिबेक कटकु सबु भागा ॥
translation: ब्रह्मचर्य, नियम, नाना प्रकार के संयम, धीरज, धर्म, ज्ञान, विज्ञान, सदाचार, जप, योग, वैराग्य आदि विवेक की सारी सेना डरकर भाग गई ॥
english_translation: Many forms of self-restraint, patience, dharma, knowledge, discernment, right conduct, chanting, yoga, and detachment all fled in fear; the whole army of clear seeing ran away.
essence: Craving can rout every discipline the mind has built.
simple_meaning: Desire can overwhelm even the best habits and insights. When the mind is seized by craving, restraint, discernment, and discipline all collapse at once.
insight: It shifts attention from moral ideals to the power that can suddenly sweep them aside.
modern_relevance: You open one app “just for a minute,” and an hour disappears. The habits you trusted most feel weak in front of a single craving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भागेउ बिबेकु सहाय सहित सो सुभट संजुग महि मुरे। सदग्रंथ पर्बत कंदरन्हि महुँ जाइ तेहि अवसर दुरे॥ होनिहार का करतार को रखवार जग खरभरु परा। दुइ माथ केहि रतिनाथ जेहि कहुँ कोपि कर धनु सरु धरा॥
translation: विवेक अपने सहायकों सहित भाग गया, उसके योद्धा रणभूमि से पीठ दिखा गए। उस समय वे सब सद्ग्रन्थ रूपी पर्वत की कन्दराओं में जा छिपे (अर्थात ज्ञान, वैराग्य, संयम, नियम, सदाचारादि ग्रंथों में ही लिखे रह गए, उनका आचरण छूट गया)। सारे जगत् में खलबली मच गई (और सब कहने लगे) हे विधाता! अब क्या होने वाला है? हमारी रक्षा कौन करेगा? ऐसा दो सिर वाला कौन है, जिसके लिए रति के पति कामदेव ने कोप करके हाथ में धनुष-बाण उठाया है?
english_translation: Wisdom fled with its helpers; its warriors turned back in battle. They hid in the caves of the sacred texts. The world fell into turmoil: “Who will protect us now? What two-headed being is this, for whom the lord of desire has raised bow and arrows in anger?”
essence: Clear seeing retreats when desire rules the mind.
simple_meaning: Clear seeing and its allies retreat when desire takes over. What remains is confusion, fear, and a world that no longer knows how to protect itself.
insight: It shifts attention from cleverness to the need for steady self-rule before desire spreads.
modern_relevance: A room full of smart people can still make a terrible choice when attraction, ego, or impulse takes the wheel. Later, everyone wonders how no one stopped it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जे सजीव जग अचर चर नारि पुरुष अस नाम। ते निज निज मरजाद तजि भए सकल बस काम ॥
translation: जगत में स्त्री-पुरुष संज्ञा वाले जितने चर-अचर प्राणी थे, वे सब अपनी-अपनी मर्यादा छोड़कर काम के वश में हो गए ॥
english_translation: All living beings in the world—moving and unmoving, men and women—left their proper bounds and fell under desire.
essence: Desire makes beings abandon the limits that protect them.
simple_meaning: Desire overwhelmed every kind of being and made them abandon the limits that normally guide their conduct.
insight: It shifts attention from blaming others to noticing how desire first weakens your own boundaries.
modern_relevance: A group chat starts with one flirtatious message, and suddenly everyone is joking, posturing, and crossing lines they would normally keep. Desire spreads fast and makes people betray their own standards.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सब के हृदयँ मदन अभिलाषा। लता निहारि नवहिं तरु साखा॥ नदीं उमगि अंबुधि कहुँ धाईं। संगम करहिं तलाव तलाईं ॥
translation: सबके हृदय में काम की इच्छा हो गई। लताओं (बेलों) को देखकर वृक्षों की डालियाँ झुकने लगीं। नदियाँ उमड़-उमड़कर समुद्र की ओर दौड़ीं और ताल-तलैयाँ भी आपस में संगम करने (मिलने-जुलने) लगीं ॥
english_translation: Desire for pleasure rose in every heart. Seeing the vines, tree branches bowed. Rivers surged toward the ocean, and ponds and pools rushed to mingle together.
essence: Desire bends even the natural world toward itself.
simple_meaning: Desire spreads through all living things and even through nature itself. The verse says the whole world seems to move toward union under its force.
insight: It shifts attention from the object of craving to the way craving spreads and captures perception.
modern_relevance: You open your phone for one quick check, and suddenly everything feels urgent, attractive, and unfinished. Desire spreads fast, and soon the whole day bends around it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ असि दसा जड़न्ह कै बरनी। को कहि सकइ सचेतन करनी॥ पसु पच्छी नभ जल थल चारी। भए काम बस समय बिसारी ॥
translation: जब जड़ (वृक्ष, नदी आदि) की यह दशा कही गई, तब चेतन जीवों की करनी कौन कह सकता है? आकाश, जल और पृथ्वी पर विचरने वाले सारे पशु-पक्षी (अपने संयोग का) समय भुलाकर काम के वश में हो गए ॥
english_translation: When even inert things were described like this, who can describe what conscious beings did? Animals and birds in sky, water, and land all forgot time and fell under desire.
essence: Desire spreads so widely that even time is forgotten.
