simple_meaning: Even trees and rivers seemed stirred by desire, so conscious beings were even more overwhelmed. Animals and birds everywhere forgot time and fell under desire.
insight: It shifts attention from private impulse to contagious social drift, showing how desire can overtake judgment.
modern_relevance: A group chat turns flirty, then the whole office starts acting strange. One mood spreads fast, and suddenly everyone has forgotten what mattered an hour ago.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मदन अंध ब्याकुल सब लोका। निसि दिनु नहिं अवलोकहिं कोका॥ देव दनुज नर किंनर ब्याला। प्रेत पिसाच भूत बेताला ॥
translation: सब लोक कामान्ध होकर व्याकुल हो गए। चकवा-चकवी रात-दिन नहीं देखते। देव, दैत्य, मनुष्य, किन्नर, सर्प, प्रेत, पिशाच, भूत, बेताल- ॥
english_translation: The whole world was blinded by desire and became restless. Night and day, the chakravaka birds did not meet. Devas, asuras, humans, kinnars, serpents, pretas, pisachas, bhutas, and vetalas—
essence: Desire blinds every kind of being and leaves no world untouched.
simple_meaning: Desire has made every kind of being restless and blind. The poet begins listing how universal this disturbance is.
insight: It shifts attention from one person's craving to desire as a universal force that disturbs all beings.
modern_relevance: A room full of people keeps refreshing their phones, each pretending to be calm. The unease is shared, not personal — and that is exactly the point.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: इन्ह कै दसा न कहेउँ बखानी। सदा काम के चेरे जानी॥ सिद्ध बिरक्त महामुनि जोगी। तेपि कामबस भए बियोगी ॥
translation: ये तो सदा ही काम के गुलाम हैं, यह समझकर मैंने इनकी दशा का वर्णन नहीं किया। सिद्ध, विरक्त, महामुनि और महान् योगी भी काम के वश होकर योगरहित या स्त्री के विरही हो गए ॥
english_translation: I will not describe their condition in detail, knowing that they are always slaves of desire. Even perfected sages, detached renunciates, great seers, and yogis fell under desire and became separated.
essence: Even the disciplined can fall when desire takes control.
simple_meaning: Desire can overpower even the most disciplined people. Tulsidas says he will not dwell on their downfall, because they were already enslaved by it.
insight: It shifts attention from spiritual status to the hidden force that can still capture the mind.
modern_relevance: A person who has meditated for years can still be undone by a single craving, a single message, a single pull. Skill does not cancel vulnerability.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भए कामबस जोगीस तापस पावँरन्हि की को कहै। देखहिं चराचर नारिमय जे ब्रह्ममय देखत रहे॥ अबला बिलोकहिं पुरुषमय जगु पुरुष सब अबलामयं। दुइ दंड भरि ब्रह्मांड भीतर कामकृत कौतुक अयं॥
translation: जब योगीश्वर और तपस्वी भी काम के वश हो गए, तब पामर मनुष्यों की कौन कहे? जो समस्त चराचर जगत को ब्रह्ममय देखते थे, वे अब उसे स्त्रीमय देखने लगे। स्त्रियाँ सारे संसार को पुरुषमय देखने लगीं और पुरुष उसे स्त्रीमय देखने लगे। दो घड़ी तक सारे ब्राह्मण्ड के अंदर कामदेव का रचा हुआ यह कौतुक (तमाशा) रहा।
english_translation: When even yogis and ascetics fell under desire, what can be said of ordinary people? Those who once saw all moving and unmoving beings as filled with the supreme reality now saw them as woman-filled; women saw the world as man-filled; men saw the world as woman-filled. For two moments, the entire cosmos became a play made by desire.
essence: Desire does not just tempt; it rewrites how the world appears.
simple_meaning: Even the disciplined can lose clear seeing when desire takes over. The world is no longer seen as it is, but through craving and projection.
insight: It shifts attention from outer objects to the mind that distorts them.
modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message, and suddenly every face, every post, every silence seems loaded with attraction or rejection. Desire has quietly rewritten the whole room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धरी न काहूँ धीर सब के मन मनसिज हरे। जे राखे रघुबीर ते उबरे तेहि काल महुँ ॥
translation: किसी ने भी हृदय में धैर्य नहीं धारण किया, कामदेव ने सबके मन हर लिए। श्री रघुनाथजी ने जिनकी रक्षा की, केवल वे ही उस समय बचे रहे ॥
english_translation: No one kept composure; Kamadeva seized every mind. Only those protected by Raghubir survived that moment.
essence: Desire topples everyone; only Ram's protection holds.
simple_meaning: No one stayed steady; desire overwhelmed every mind. Only those protected by Ram were saved in that crisis.
insight: It shifts attention from personal control alone to the need for divine protection when the mind is overrun.
modern_relevance: A room full of people can look composed until attraction, envy, or panic hits. Then the careful mask slips. This verse names that collapse and the need for a steadier refuge.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उभय घरी अस कौतुक भयऊ। जौ लगि कामु संभु पहिं गयऊ॥ सिवहि बिलोकि ससंकेउ मारू। भयउ जथाथिति सबु संसारू ॥
translation: दो घड़ी तक ऐसा तमाशा हुआ, जब तक कामदेव शिवजी के पास पहुँच गया। शिवजी को देखकर कामदेव डर गया, तब सारा संसार फिर जैसा-का तैसा स्थिर हो गया।
english_translation: For two moments this strange spectacle lasted, until Kama reached Shiva. Seeing Shiva, Kama grew afraid, and the whole world returned to its natural order.
essence: Fearless presence restores the world to order.
simple_meaning: For a brief time, desire disturbed even the highest beings, but Shiva's presence restored order. The world settled back into its proper state.
insight: It shows that true steadiness can dissolve disorder without force.
modern_relevance: A room full of tension can feel unbearable until one calm person walks in and everyone straightens up. Presence can restore order faster than argument.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भए तुरत सब जीव सुखारे। जिमि मद उतरि गएँ मतवारे॥ रुद्रहि देखि मदन भय माना। दुराधरष दुर्गम भगवाना ॥
translation: तुरंत ही सब जीव वैसे ही सुखी हो गए, जैसे मतवाले (नशा पिए हुए) लोग मद (नशा) उतर जाने पर सुखी होते हैं। दुराधर्ष (जिनको पराजित करना अत्यन्त ही कठिन है) और दुर्गम (जिनका पार पाना कठिन है) भगवान (सम्पूर्ण ऐश्वर्य, धर्म, यश, श्री, ज्ञान और वैराग्य रूप छह ईश्वरीय गुणों से युक्त) रुद्र (महाभयंकर) शिवजी को देखकर कामदेव भयभीत हो गया ॥
english_translation: At once all living beings became happy, like drunken men after the intoxication wears off. Seeing Rudra, Kama felt fear. The Lord was hard to approach and impossible to overcome.
essence: True steadiness makes desire itself lose courage.
simple_meaning: When Shiva appears, the disturbing force of desire loses its grip, and everyone feels relief again.
insight: It shifts attention from emotional chaos to the stabilising presence that ends it.
modern_relevance: A tense room after a heated argument can change the moment one steady person walks in. The mood drops, the panic fades, and everyone breathes again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: फिरत लाज कछु करि नहिं जाई। मरनु ठानि मन रचेसि उपाई॥ प्रगटेसि तुरत रुचिर रितुराजा। कुसुमित नव तरु राजि बिराजा ॥
translation: लौट जाने में लज्जा मालूम होती है और करते कुछ बनता नहीं। आखिर मन में मरने का निश्चय करके उसने उपाय रचा। तुरंत ही सुंदर ऋतुराज वसन्त को प्रकट किया। फूले हुए नए-नए वृक्षों की कतारें सुशोभित हो गईं ॥
english_translation: Unable to turn back in shame, he resolved in his mind to die and devised a plan. At once he manifested the lovely king of seasons, and rows of blooming young trees shone forth.
essence: Even shame can become the threshold for a new beginning.
simple_meaning: He could not turn back in shame, so he resolved to die and set about a plan. Then spring appeared at once, and fresh flowering trees filled the scene.
insight: It shifts attention from inner embarrassment to the fact that action can still transform the moment.
modern_relevance: You miss your exit, sit in the car for a moment, and feel the sting of having no easy way back. Then you take the next turn and keep going.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बन उपबन बापिका तड़ागा। परम सुभग सब दिसा बिभागा॥ जहँ तहँ जनु उमगत अनुरागा। देखि मुएहुँ मन मनसिज जागा ॥
translation: वन-उपवन, बावली-तालाब और सब दिशाओं के विभाग परम सुंदर हो गए। जहाँ-तहाँ मानो प्रेम उम़ड़ रहा है, जिसे देखकर मरे मनों में भी कामदेव जाग उठा ॥
english_translation: The forests, groves, pools, and tanks became beautiful in every direction. Love seemed to rise everywhere, and even dead hearts were stirred by desire at the sight.
essence: Beauty can awaken longing even in a numb heart.
simple_meaning: The whole landscape becomes so beautiful that it seems to awaken love even in hearts that were lifeless.
insight: It shifts attention from inner heaviness to how surroundings can quietly reshape feeling.
modern_relevance: You walk into a courtyard after rain, and the smell of wet earth, flowers, and quiet light suddenly softens your mood before you can explain why.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जागइ मनोभव मुएहुँ मन बन सुभगता न परै कही। सीतल सुगंध सुमंद मारुत मदन अनल सखा सही॥ बिकसे सरन्हि बहु कंज गुंजत पुंज मंजुल मधुकरा। कलहंस पिक सुक सरस रव करि गान नाचहिं अपछरा
translation: मरे हुए मन में भी कामदेव जागने लगा, वन की सुंदरता कही नहीं जा सकती। कामरूपी अग्नि का सच्चा मित्र शीतल-मन्द-सुगंधित पवन चलने लगा। सरोवरों में अनेकों कमल खिल गए, जिन पर सुंदर भौंरों के समूह गुंजार करने लगे। राजहंस, कोयल और तोते रसीली बोली बोलने लगे और अप्सराएँ गा-गाकर नाचने लगीं॥
english_translation: Desire awakens even in a dead mind; the forest's beauty cannot be described. A cool, gentle, fragrant breeze becomes the true friend of the fire of desire. Many lotuses bloom in the lakes, clusters of bees hum sweetly, and swans, cuckoos, and parrots sing while heavenly dancers dance and sing.
essence: Beauty itself can awaken desire in a heart that seemed finished.
simple_meaning: The forest becomes so beautiful that it stirs desire even in a dead heart. Breezes, flowers, birds, and bees all seem to join that awakening.
insight: It frames attraction as something awakened by atmosphere, not forced by will.
modern_relevance: You walk into a garden after a hard breakup, expecting nothing, and one scent, one birdcall, one breeze brings everything back. The world can reopen a closed heart without asking permission.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकल कला करि कोटि बिधि हारेउ सेन समेत। चली न अचल समाधि सिव कोपेउ हृदयनिकेत ॥
translation: कामदेव अपनी सेना समेत करोड़ों प्रकार की सब कलाएँ (उपाए) करके हार गया, पर शिवजी की अचल समाधि न डिगी। तब कामदेव क्रोधित हो उठा ॥
english_translation: Kama, with his countless arts and his army, was defeated. Shiva's unshaken meditation did not move, and then Kama grew furious.
essence: Desire fails before unshaken stillness, then turns to rage.
simple_meaning: Kama tried every possible tactic, but Shiva's deep meditation stayed unmoved. Failing to break that stillness, Kama became angry.
insight: It shows that unshaken attention can outlast even the strongest pull of desire.
modern_relevance: You are halfway through a late-night scroll, trying to pull yourself out of focus, and every distraction has already tried its turn. The mind that stays steady does not need to fight back.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि रसाल बिटप बर साखा। तेहि पर चढ़ेउ मदनु मन माखा॥ सुमन चाप निज सर संधाने। अति रिस ताकि श्रवन लगि ताने ॥
translation: आम के वृक्ष की एक सुंदर डाली देखकर मन में क्रोध से भरा हुआ कामदेव उस पर चढ़ गया। उसने पुष्प धनुष पर अपने (पाँचों) बाण चढ़ाए और अत्यन्त क्रोध से (लक्ष्य की ओर) ताककर उन्हें कान तक तान लिया ॥
english_translation: Seeing a beautiful mango branch, Madana climbed it, his mind inflamed with anger. He strung his flower-bow and, glaring fiercely, drew the bowstring to his ear.
essence: Desire arms itself the moment it sees an opening.
simple_meaning: Madana, angered and eager, climbs a beautiful branch and prepares his flower arrows to attack Shiva’s meditation.
insight: It shows how desire becomes aggressive when it senses an opening.
modern_relevance: You feel calm until one tempting image hooks your attention and the whole mind rushes forward. The reaction is sudden, almost automatic, and hard to stop once it starts.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: छाड़े बिषम बिसिख उर लागे। छूटि समाधि संभु तब जागे॥ भयउ ईस मन छोभु बिसेषी। नयन उघारि सकल दिसि देखी ॥
translation: कामदेव ने तीक्ष्ण पाँच बाण छोड़े, जो शिवजी के हृदय में लगे। तब उनकी समाधि टूट गई और वे जाग गए। ईश्वर (शिवजी) के मन में बहुत क्षोभ हुआ। उन्होंने आँखें खोलकर सब ओर देखा ॥
english_translation: Kamadeva shot his sharp arrows, and they struck Shiva's heart. Then Shiva's meditation broke, and he awoke. The Lord felt deep disturbance in his mind. Opening his eyes, he looked all around.
essence: Desire breaks stillness in a single strike.
simple_meaning: Kamadeva's arrows break Shiva's meditation and stir his mind. He wakes, opens his eyes, and looks around in anger.
insight: It shows how desire can interrupt stillness and trigger an immediate, reactive awakening.
modern_relevance: You were finally focused, then one notification, one comment, one memory shattered the calm. The mind wakes instantly, and not always gently.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सौरभ पल्लव मदनु बिलोका। भयउ कोपु कंपेउ त्रैलोका॥ तब सिवँ तीसर नयन उघारा। चितवन कामु भयउ जरि छारा ॥
translation: जब आम के पत्तों में (छिपे हुए) कामदेव को देखा तो उन्हें बड़ा क्रोध हुआ, जिससे तीनों लोक काँप उठे। तब शिवजी ने तीसरा नेत्र खोला, उनको देखते ही कामदेव जलकर भस्म हो गया ॥
english_translation: When Shiva saw Kama hidden among the mango leaves, great anger arose and the three worlds trembled. Then Shiva opened his third eye; at one glance, Kama burned to ashes.
essence: Clear seeing can burn desire to ashes.
simple_meaning: Shiva notices Kama hiding in the leaves, becomes furious, and opens his third eye. Kama is instantly reduced to ashes.
insight: It shifts the mind from being seduced by desire to seeing desire as something that can be ended by clear awareness.
modern_relevance: You finally notice the craving hiding inside a harmless-looking habit. The moment you see it clearly, it loses its power to run your day.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हाहाकार भयउ जग भारी। डरपे सुर भए असुर सुखारी॥ समुझि कामसुख सोचहिं भोगी। भए अकंटक साधक जोगी ॥
translation: जगत में बड़ा हाहाकर मच गया। देवता डर गए, दैत्य सुखी हुए। भोगी लोग कामसुख को याद करके चिन्ता करने लगे और साधक योगी निष्कंटक हो गए ॥
english_translation: There was a great uproar in the world. The radiant beings were afraid, and the beings of shadow were pleased. Those who chase pleasure worried about desire; seekers of yoga became free of disturbance.
essence: What ruins craving frees the one who seeks discipline.
simple_meaning: The world reacts in opposite ways: some are shaken by the fall of desire, while seekers feel relief and freedom.
insight: It contrasts two responses to the same event: craving panics, discipline relaxes.
modern_relevance: A breakup, a temptation, or a habit finally losing its grip can feel like disaster to one circle of people and relief to another. What weakens craving can unsettle the restless mind and steady the one who is serious.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जोगी अकंटक भए पति गति सुनत रति मुरुछित भई। रोदति बदति बहु भाँति करुना करति संकर पहिं गई॥ अति प्रेम करि बिनती बिबिध बिधि जोरि कर सन्मुख रही। प्रभु आसुतोष कृपाल सिव अबला निरखि बोले सही॥
translation: योगी निष्कंटक हो गए, कामदेव की स्त्री रति अपने पति की यह दशा सुनते ही मूर्च्छित हो गई। रोती-चिल्लाती और भाँति-भाँति से करुणा करती हुई वह शिवजी के पास गई। अत्यन्त प्रेम के साथ अनेकों प्रकार से विनती करके हाथ जोड़कर सामने खड़ी हो गई। शीघ्र प्रसन्न होने वाले कृपालु शिवजी अबला (असहाय स्त्री) को देखकर सुंदर (उसको सान्त्वना देने वाले) वचन बोले।
english_translation: The yogis became free of disturbance. Hearing of her husband's condition, Rati fainted. Weeping and grieving in many ways, she went to Shiva. With deep love she stood before him, hands joined, and Shiva, the compassionate one, spoke gentle words to the helpless woman.
essence: Relief for one side can be devastation for another.
simple_meaning: The yogis are now free from disturbance. Rati, hearing what happened to her husband, faints in grief and goes to Shiva, pleading with him in tears.
insight: It shifts attention from cosmic event to human cost, showing that even victory carries sorrow for someone.
modern_relevance: A person gets the worst possible call in the middle of the day, drops everything, and walks into the only room where help might still exist. Grief does that: it strips away pride and asks for mercy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अब तें रति तव नाथ कर होइहि नामु अनंगु। बिनु बपु ब्यापिहि सबहि पुनि सुनु निज मिलन प्रसंगु ॥
translation: हे रति! अब से तेरे स्वामी का नाम अनंग होगा। वह बिना ही शरीर के सबको व्यापेगा। अब तू अपने पति से मिलने की बात सुन ॥
english_translation: O Rati, from now on your husband will be named Ananga. Without a body, he will pervade everyone. Now listen to the story of your reunion.
essence: What loses form can still continue to move through the world.
simple_meaning: Rati is told that Kama will lose his body and live on as Ananga, moving through everyone invisibly. The verse points toward the story of how they will meet again.
insight: It shifts attention from physical form to the continuing force of longing.
modern_relevance: A breakup leaves someone saying, 'I can't even think straight.' The feeling still moves through the body, even after the old form of love is gone.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: जब जदुबंस कृष्न अवतारा। होइहि हरन महा महिभारा॥ कृष्न तनय होइहि पति तोरा। बचनु अन्यथा होइ न मोरा ॥
translation: जब पृथ्वी के बड़े भारी भार को उतारने के लिए यदुवंश में श्री कृष्ण का अवतार होगा, तब तेरा पति उनके पुत्र (प्रद्युम्न) के रूप में उत्पन्न होगा। मेरा यह वचन अन्यथा नहीं होगा ॥
english_translation: When Krishna descends in the Yadu line to lift the great burden of the earth, your husband will be born as his son. My word never fails.
essence: A divine promise can outlast even death and return as form.
simple_meaning: Shiva tells Rati that her husband will return in a future birth as Krishna's son, and his promise will come true.
insight: It shifts grief from finality to continuity, showing that a broken moment may belong to a larger arc.
modern_relevance: You are standing beside someone whose life has split into before and after. The comfort that helps most is not explanation, but a promise you can trust when nothing else makes sense.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: रति गवनी सुनि संकर बानी। कथा अपर अब कहउँ बखानी॥ देवन्ह समाचार सब पाए। ब्रह्मादिक बैकुंठ सिधाए ॥
translation: शिवजी के वचन सुनकर रति चली गई। अब दूसरी कथा बखानकर (विस्तार से) कहता हूँ। ब्रह्मादि देवताओं ने ये सब समाचार सुने तो वे वैकुण्ठ को चले ॥
english_translation: Hearing Shiva's words, Rati departed. Now I tell another story in detail. After hearing all this news, the gods, including Brahma, went to Vaikuntha.
essence: The story turns from one divine scene to the next.
simple_meaning: Rati leaves after hearing Shiva's words, and the narrator shifts to another story. The gods hear the news and go to Vaikuntha.
insight: It marks a narrative turn, reminding the reader that sacred stories move through connected scenes.
modern_relevance: A conversation ends, and everyone in the room instantly shifts to the next task. The emotional moment has passed, but the story keeps moving.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सब सुर बिष्नु बिरंचि समेता। गए जहाँ सिव कृपानिकेता॥ पृथक-पृथक तिन्ह कीन्हि प्रसंसा। भए प्रसन्न चंद्र अवतंसा ॥
translation: फिर वहाँ से विष्णु और ब्रह्मा सहित सब देवता वहाँ गए, जहाँ कृपा के धाम शिवजी थे। उन सबने शिवजी की अलग-अलग स्तुति की, तब शशिभूषण शिवजी प्रसन्न हो गए ॥
english_translation: Then all the gods, along with Vishnu and Brahma, went to where Shiva, the abode of grace, dwelt. Each one praised Shiva in his own way, and Shashibhushan became pleased.
essence: Sincere praise opens the way for grace.
simple_meaning: All the gods went to Shiva and praised him individually. Shiva was pleased by their devotion.
insight: It frames reverence as the opening move before asking for help or guidance.
modern_relevance: A room full of powerful people can still feel tense until someone speaks with genuine respect. Real admiration softens pride faster than status ever can.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बोले कृपासिंधु बृषकेतू। कहहु अमर आए केहि हेतू॥ कह बिधि तुम्ह प्रभु अंतरजामी। तदपि भगति बस बिनवउँ स्वामी ॥
translation: कृपा के समुद्र शिवजी बोले- हे देवताओं! कहिए, आप किसलिए आए हैं? ब्रह्माजी ने कहा- हे प्रभो! आप अन्तर्यामी हैं, तथापि हे स्वामी! भक्तिवश मैं आपसे विनती करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Shiva, the ocean of compassion, said: "Tell me, immortals, what brings you here?" Brahma said: "Lord, you are the indweller of all hearts. Still, out of devotion, I bow to you, master."
essence: Knowing everything does not cancel devotion; it deepens it.
simple_meaning: Shiva asks the gods why they have come. Brahma answers that even though Shiva knows every heart, he still bows to him in devotion.
insight: It shifts the mind from performing respect to offering it sincerely, even when no explanation is needed.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone already knows the answer, but you still speak with humility. Respect is not reduced by insight; it becomes deeper because of it.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सकल सुरन्ह के हृदयँ अस संकर परम उछाहु। निज नयनन्हि देखा चहहिं नाथ तुम्हार बिबाहु ॥
translation: हे शंकर! सब देवताओं के मन में ऐसा परम उत्साह है कि हे नाथ! वे अपनी आँखों से आपका विवाह देखना चाहते हैं ॥
english_translation: All the gods feel such great joy in their hearts, O Shankar, that they want to see your wedding with their own eyes, O Lord.
essence: Joy in Shiva’s wedding draws every heart toward direct seeing.
simple_meaning: The gods are so delighted that they want to witness Shiva’s wedding themselves.
insight: It shifts attention from hearing about holiness to wanting direct presence with it.
modern_relevance: A family gathers before a wedding, and everyone keeps leaning toward the doorway for the first glimpse. Some moments are so sacred and joyful that people do not want a summary — they want to witness them live.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: यह उत्सव देखिअ भरि लोचन। सोइ कछु करहु मदन मद मोचन॥ कामु जारि रति कहुँ बरु दीन्हा। कृपासिन्धु यह अति भल कीन्हा ॥
translation: हे कामदेव के मद को चूर करने वाले! आप ऐसा कुछ कीजिए, जिससे सब लोग इस उत्सव को नेत्र भरकर देखें। हे कृपा के सागर! कामदेव को भस्म करके आपने रति को जो वरदान दिया, सो बहुत ही अच्छा किया ॥
english_translation: O destroyer of Cupid's pride, let everyone behold this festival with full eyes. O ocean of grace, you did very well to burn Cupid and grant Rati a boon.
essence: True grace destroys craving and still leaves room for blessing.
simple_meaning: Shiva asks Ram to make the wedding festival fully visible to everyone, and praises Ram for destroying desire's arrogance while still blessing Rati.
insight: It trains attention to see sacred joy without getting lost in desire or spectacle.
modern_relevance: At a wedding where everyone is trying to capture the perfect moment, one person quietly notices the deeper grace behind the celebration. Beauty feels fuller when pride and longing no longer distort it.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सासति करि पुनि करहिं पसाऊ। नाथ प्रभुन्ह कर सहज सुभाऊ॥ पारबतीं तपु कीन्ह अपारा। करहु तासु अब अंगीकारा ॥
translation: हे नाथ! श्रेष्ठ स्वामियों का यह सहज स्वभाव ही है कि वे पहले दण्ड देकर फिर कृपा किया करते हैं। पार्वती ने अपार तप किया है, अब उन्हें अंगीकार कीजिए ॥
english_translation: O Lord, it is the natural conduct of noble masters to punish first and then show grace. Parvati has performed immense austerity; now accept her.
essence: Grace arrives after endurance is fully seen.
simple_meaning: A noble master may first test or discipline someone, then show mercy. Parvati has already done immense austerity, so she should now be accepted.
insight: It shifts the mind from proving worth forever to recognising when effort has already been answered.
modern_relevance: You kept showing up for months, proving yourself in silence, while everyone else moved on. Then the door finally opens. This verse holds that long-awaited moment of being received.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि बिधि बिनय समुझि प्रभु बानी। ऐसेइ होउ कहा सुखु मानी॥ तब देवन्ह दुंदुभीं बजाईं। बरषि सुमन जय जय सुर साईं ॥
translation: ब्रह्माजी की प्रार्थना सुनकर और प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के वचनों को याद करके शिवजी ने प्रसन्नतापूर्वक कहा- 'ऐसा ही हो।' तब देवताओं ने नगाड़े बजाए और फूलों की वर्षा करके 'जय हो! देवताओं के स्वामी जय हो' ऐसा कहने लगे ॥
english_translation: Hearing Brahma's prayer and remembering the Lord's words, Shiva gladly said, 'So be it.' Then the devas rang their drums, showered flowers, and cried, 'Victory, victory to the Lord of the devas!'
essence: Right consent turns tension into celebration.
simple_meaning: Shiva agrees with Brahma's prayer and Ram's words, then the devas celebrate with drums, flowers, and praise.
insight: It shifts attention from hesitation to wholehearted assent, showing how right action can be recognised and celebrated immediately.
modern_relevance: You finally hear the confirmation you were waiting for, and the room shifts. Relief spreads, people smile, and what was uncertain now feels blessed.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: अवसरु जानि सप्तरिषि आए। तुरतहिं बिधि गिरिभवन पठाए॥ प्रथम गए जहँ रहीं भवानी। बोले मधुर बचन छल सानी ॥
translation: उचित अवसर जानकर सप्तर्षि आए और ब्रह्माजी ने तुरंत ही उन्हें हिमाचल के घर भेज दिया। वे पहले वहाँ गए जहाँ पार्वतीजी थीं और उनसे छल से भरे मीठे (विनोदयुक्त, आनंद पहुँचाने वाले) वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: Knowing the right moment, the seven sages arrived, and Brahma immediately sent them to Himavan's home. They first went where Parvati was and spoke sweet, playful words filled with a hidden purpose.
essence: Sweet words can carry a hidden agenda.
simple_meaning: The seven sages arrive at the right moment and first go to Parvati. They speak in sweet words, but their words carry a hidden intention.
insight: It trains you to notice both tone and intention, not just pleasant speech.
modern_relevance: A friendly message lands in your inbox just after a tense conversation. The tone feels warm, but something underneath it is steering the exchange. You sense the hidden agenda before the words finish.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहा हमार न सुनेहु तब नारद कें उपदेस॥ अब भा झूठ तुम्हार पन जारेउ कामु महेस ॥
translation: नारदजी के उपदेश से तुमने उस समय हमारी बात नहीं सुनी। अब तो तुम्हारा प्रण झूठा हो गया, क्योंकि महादेवजी ने काम को ही भस्म कर डाला ॥
english_translation: You did not listen to our words then, despite Narada's counsel. Now your vow has become false, because Mahadeva has burned Kama to ashes.
essence: A vow loses force when action contradicts it.
simple_meaning: Parvati reminds Shiva that he ignored Narada's warning before, so his vow now seems broken because he has burned Kama.
insight: It exposes the gap between a stated vow and a later action that breaks it.
modern_relevance: You promised you were fine with something, then reacted sharply when it actually happened. The contradiction stings because everyone can see it now.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: सुनि बोलीं मुसुकाइ भवानी। उचित कहेहु मुनिबर बिग्यानी॥ तुम्हरें जान कामु अब जारा। अब लगि संभु रहे सबिकारा ॥
translation: यह सुनकर पार्वतीजी मुस्कुराकर बोलीं- हे विज्ञानी मुनिवरों! आपने उचित ही कहा। आपकी समझ में शिवजी ने कामदेव को अब जलाया है, अब तक तो वे विकारयुक्त (कामी) ही रहे! ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Bhavani smiled and said, "You have spoken rightly, O wise sages. In your view, Shiva burned desire only now; until now, he was still ruled by passion."
essence: A smile can agree with words while quietly correcting them.
simple_meaning: Parvati answers the sages with a smile, agreeing with their words in a teasing way. She says that, by their view, Shiva only just burned desire, and before that he was still full of passion.
insight: It shows how a listener can accept praise while quietly exposing its limits.
modern_relevance: Someone compliments a person for being "so calm now," and the room laughs because everyone knows the change took time. A smile can carry both agreement and a sharper truth than the words alone.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: हमरें जान सदासिव जोगी। अज अनवद्य अकाम अभोगी॥ जौं मैं सिव सेये अस जानी। प्रीति समेत कर्म मन बानी ॥
translation: किन्तु हमारी समझ से तो शिवजी सदा से ही योगी, अजन्मे, अनिन्द्य, कामरहित और भोगहीन हैं और यदि मैंने शिवजी को ऐसा समझकर ही मन, वचन और कर्म से प्रेम सहित उनकी सेवा की है ॥
english_translation: But in my understanding, Shiva is always a yogi: unborn, blameless, free from desire, and beyond enjoyment. If I have served Shiva with love in thought, speech, and action, knowing him thus...
essence: True devotion serves without trying to possess.
simple_meaning: Parvati says she has always understood Shiva as a pure renunciant, and that her loving service was offered to him with that understanding in mind, speech, and action.
insight: It shifts devotion from emotional impulse to informed reverence, where service follows clear seeing.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone because you know their character, not because you need constant proof. That kind of devotion stays clean when understanding comes before expectation.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: तौ हमार पन सुनहु मुनीसा। करिहहिं सत्य कृपानिधि ईसा॥ तुम्ह जो कहा हर जारेउ मारा। सोइ अति बड़ अबिबेकु तुम्हारा ॥
translation: तो हे मुनीश्वरो! सुनिए, वे कृपानिधान भगवान मेरी प्रतिज्ञा को सत्य करेंगे। आपने जो यह कहा कि शिवजी ने कामदेव को भस्म कर दिया, यही आपका बड़ा भारी अविवेक है ॥
english_translation: O great sages, listen. The merciful Lord will make my vow true. What you said—that Shiva burned Kama to ashes—is your great mistake.
essence: True understanding corrects even confident misunderstanding.
simple_meaning: Parvati says Shiva will prove her vow true, and she corrects the sages: their idea that Shiva burned Kama is a serious mistake.
insight: It shifts the mind from accepting inherited claims to seeing clearly and correcting them.
modern_relevance: In a room full of people confidently repeating the wrong story, you do not need to shout. A steady correction can be stronger than argument.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: तात अनल कर सहज सुभाऊ। हिम तेहि निकट जाइ नहिं काऊ॥ गएँ समीप सो अवसि नसाई। असि मन्मथ महेस की नाई ॥
translation: हे तात! अग्नि का तो यह सहज स्वभाव ही है कि पाला उसके समीप कभी जा ही नहीं सकता और जाने पर वह अवश्य नष्ट हो जाएगा। महादेवजी और कामदेव के संबंध में भी यही न्याय (बात) समझना चाहिए ॥
english_translation: O dear one, fire is naturally such that snow cannot come near it. If snow goes close, it is surely destroyed. The same rule applies to the union of Shambhu and Kamadeva.
essence: Some opposites destroy each other on contact.
simple_meaning: Fire and snow cannot coexist. In the same way, Shiva and Kamadeva cannot meet without destruction.
insight: It teaches you to recognize incompatible states before forcing them together.
modern_relevance: You try to keep a clear boundary with something that always pulls you off center. The more you let it in, the more it dissolves your focus.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: हियँ हरषे मुनि बचन सुनि देखि प्रीति बिस्वास। चले भवानिहि नाइ सिर गए हिमाचल पास ॥
translation: पार्वती के वचन सुनकर और उनका प्रेम तथा विश्वास देखकर मुनि हृदय में बड़े प्रसन्न हुए। वे भवानी को सिर नवाकर चल दिए और हिमाचल के पास पहुँचे ॥
english_translation: Hearing Parvati's words and seeing her love and trust, the sages were delighted in their hearts. Bowing to Bhavani, they set out and reached near Mount Himachal.
essence: Trust and reverence make the next teaching possible.
simple_meaning: The sages felt joy at Parvati's loving trust. They bowed to her and went on to Mount Himachal.
insight: It shows that sincere listening earns a deeper response and carries a conversation forward.
modern_relevance: A teacher notices the student is listening with real trust, not just waiting to interrupt. The conversation changes immediately; respect makes the next truth possible.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सबु प्रसंगु गिरिपतिहि सुनावा। मदन दहन सुनि अति दुखु पावा॥ बहुरि कहेउ रति कर बरदाना। सुनि हिमवंत बहुत सुखु माना ॥
translation: उन्होंने पर्वतराज हिमाचल को सब हाल सुनाया। कामदेव का भस्म होना सुनकर हिमाचल बहुत दुःखी हुए। फिर मुनियों ने रति के वरदान की बात कही, उसे सुनकर हिमवान् ने बहुत सुख माना ॥
english_translation: They told Himavan the whole story. Hearing that Kama had been burned, he felt deep sorrow. Then they spoke of Rati’s boon, and hearing that, Himavan felt great relief.
essence: Partial news wounds; the fuller story restores ease.
simple_meaning: The sages explain the events to Himavan. He grieves at Kama’s destruction, then feels relief when he hears of Rati’s boon.
insight: It shifts the mind from partial hearing to fuller understanding, where sorrow can soften.
modern_relevance: You hear only the worst part of a story and your chest tightens. Then one more detail arrives, and the whole picture changes. Relief often comes from context, not control.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हृदयँ बिचारि संभु प्रभुताई। सादर मुनिबर लिए बोलाई। सुदिनु सुनखतु सुघरी सोचाई। बेगि बेदबिधि लगन धराई ॥
translation: शिवजी के प्रभाव को मन में विचार कर हिमाचल ने श्रेष्ठ मुनियों को आदरपूर्वक बुला लिया और उनसे शुभ दिन, शुभ नक्षत्र और शुभ घड़ी शोधवाकर वेद की विधि के अनुसार शीघ्र ही लग्न निश्चय कराकर लिखवा लिया ॥
english_translation: Considering Shiva's power in his heart, Himachal respectfully summoned the best sages. He chose an auspicious day, a lucky star, and a favorable hour, and quickly fixed the wedding time according to Vedic procedure.
essence: Reverence turns even planning into a sacred act.
simple_meaning: Himachal, thinking of Shiva's greatness, called the sages and fixed the wedding time by choosing an auspicious day, star, and hour.
insight: It shifts attention from impulse to proper preparation, showing that important acts deserve thoughtful timing and respect.
modern_relevance: Before a family wedding, everyone is checking dates, calling elders, and making sure the timing feels right. Beneath the logistics is reverence: some moments deserve care, not haste.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पत्री सप्तरिषिन्ह सोइ दीन्ही। गहि पद बिनय हिमाचल कीन्ही॥ जाइ बिधिहि तिन्ह दीन्हि सो पाती। बाचत प्रीति न हृदयँ समाती ॥
translation: फिर हिमाचल ने वह लग्नपत्रिका सप्तर्षियों को दे दी और चरण पकड़कर उनकी विनती की। उन्होंने जाकर वह लग्न पत्रिका ब्रह्माजी को दी। उसको पढ़ते समय उनके हृदय में प्रेम समाता न था ॥
english_translation: Then Himachal gave that wedding proposal to the seven sages and, bowing at their feet, made his request. They went and gave that proposal to Brahma. As he read it, his heart could not contain its joy.
essence: A sacred announcement can make even the messenger’s heart overflow.
simple_meaning: Himachal sends the wedding proposal through the seven sages and bows to ask for help. Brahma receives it with such joy that his heart overflows.
insight: It shifts attention from the request itself to the shared joy it awakens.
modern_relevance: You send the final message that makes everything real: the date, the plan, the commitment. The room is quiet, but your chest is full because the waiting is over.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लगन बाचि अज सबहि सुनाई। हरषे मुनि सब सुर समुदाई॥ सुमन बृष्टि नभ बाजन बाजे। मंगल कलस दसहुँ दिसि साजे ॥
translation: ब्रह्माजी ने लग्न पढ़कर सबको सुनाया, उसे सुनकर सब मुनि और देवताओं का सारा समाज हर्षित हो गया। आकाश से फूलों की वर्षा होने लगी, बाजे बजने लगे और दसों दिशाओं में मंगल कलश सजा दिए गए ॥
english_translation: Brahma read out the auspicious wedding time, and all the sages and the assembly of the radiant beings rejoiced. Flowers rained from the sky, drums sounded, and auspicious pots were set in all ten directions.
essence: A blessed moment draws the whole world into celebration.
simple_meaning: Brahma announces the auspicious wedding time, and everyone rejoices. Flowers fall from the sky, music begins, and auspicious pots are arranged everywhere.
insight: It turns a private arrangement into a shared celebration, where even the sky seems to participate.
modern_relevance: A family hears the final confirmation that the ceremony can begin. The room changes at once — relief, joy, and movement replace all the waiting.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लगे सँवारन सकल सुर बाहन बिबिध बिमान। होहिं सगुन मंगल सुभद करहिं अपछरा गान ॥
translation: सब देवता अपने भाँति-भाँति के वाहन और विमान सजाने लगे, कल्याणप्रद मंगल शकुन होने लगे और अप्सराएँ गाने लगीं ॥
english_translation: All the radiant beings began arranging their various mounts and celestial vehicles. Auspicious signs appeared, and the celestial dancers began to sing.
essence: The world itself joins in when the sacred moment arrives.
simple_meaning: The heavens are getting ready for a sacred wedding. Everything around the event turns auspicious, and the celestial singers begin their song.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the sacred mood surrounding it.
modern_relevance: A room fills with flowers, music starts before the guests arrive, and everyone can feel something important is about to happen. The atmosphere itself announces the moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिवहि संभु गन करहिं सिंगारा। जटा मुकुट अहि मौरु सँवारा॥ कुंडल कंकन पहिरे ब्याला। तन बिभूति पट केहरि छाला ॥
translation: शिवजी के गण शिवजी का श्रृंगार करने लगे। जटाओं का मुकुट बनाकर उस पर साँपों का मौर सजाया गया। शिवजी ने साँपों के ही कुंडल और कंकण पहने, शरीर पर विभूति रमायी और वस्त्र की जगह बाघम्बर लपेट लिया ॥
english_translation: Shiva's attendants began adorning Shiva. They made a crown from his matted hair and decorated it with serpents. He wore serpent earrings and bracelets, smeared sacred ash on his body, and wrapped tiger skin instead of cloth.
essence: True grandeur can wear the marks of renunciation.
simple_meaning: Shiva is being ceremonially dressed by his attendants, with serpents, ash, and tiger skin as his adornment.
insight: It shifts attention from outer luxury to the dignity of renunciation.
modern_relevance: A room full of people may prize polished clothes and status symbols, yet the person who has nothing to prove can wear simplicity like a crown.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ससि ललाट सुंदर सिर गंगा। नयन तीनि उपबीत भुजंगा॥ गरल कंठ उर नर सिर माला। असिव बेष सिवधाम कृपाला ॥
translation: शिवजी के सुंदर मस्तक पर चन्द्रमा, सिर पर गंगाजी, तीन नेत्र, साँपों का जनेऊ, गले में विष और छाती पर नरमुण्डों की माला थी। इस प्रकार उनका वेष अशुभ होने पर भी वे कल्याण के धाम और कृपालु हैं ॥
english_translation: The moon adorns his forehead, the Ganga crowns his head, and three eyes shine. Snakes form his sacred thread; poison rests in his throat; a garland of human skulls hangs on his chest. Though his appearance is fearsome, Shiva is the abode of grace and compassion.
essence: Fearsome appearance can hide the gentlest heart.
simple_meaning: Shiva’s form looks fierce and inauspicious, yet it is filled with beauty, holiness, and compassion.
insight: It shifts attention from outward appearance to the deeper character beneath it.
modern_relevance: A person walks into a room with tattoos, scars, and a hard face, and everyone assumes the worst. Then they speak gently, help quietly, and carry more tenderness than anyone expected.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कर त्रिसूल अरु डमरु बिराजा। चले बसहँ चढ़ि बाजहिं बाजा॥ देखि सिवहि सुरत्रिय मुसुकाहीं। बर लायक दुलहिनि जग नाहीं ॥
translation: एक हाथ में त्रिशूल और दूसरे में डमरू सुशोभित है। शिवजी बैल पर चढ़कर चले। बाजे बज रहे हैं। शिवजी को देखकर देवांगनाएँ मुस्कुरा रही हैं (और कहती हैं कि) इस वर के योग्य दुलहिन संसार में नहीं मिलेगी ॥
english_translation: The trident and drum shine in Shiva's hands. Shiva rides forward on the bull while music plays. Seeing Shiva, the celestial women smile and say, 'No bride in the world is worthy of this groom.'
essence: Shiva's wedding procession draws delighted admiration from the heavens.
simple_meaning: Shiva arrives in splendid wedding procession, and the celestial women admire him as an unmatched groom.
insight: It frames divine presence as something so striking that even onlookers respond with delight.
modern_relevance: At a wedding procession, everyone turns to look at the groom and smiles at the beauty of the moment. Some arrivals carry a presence so complete that admiration comes before words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिष्नु बिरंचि आदि सुरब्राता। चढ़ि चढ़ि बाहन चले बराता॥ सुर समाज सब भाँति अनूपा। नहिं बरात दूल्हे अनुरूपा ॥
translation: विष्णु और ब्रह्मा आदि देवताओं के समूह अपने-अपने वाहनों (सवारियों) पर चढ़कर बारात में चले। देवताओं का समाज सब प्रकार से अनुपम (परम सुंदर) था, पर दूल्हे के योग्य बारात न थी ॥
english_translation: Vishnu, Brahma, and the host of other radiant beings rode on their own mounts and went in the wedding procession. The company of radiant beings was splendid in every way, yet it was not a procession fit for the groom.
essence: Splendor can still be mismatched when it lacks true fit.
simple_meaning: Vishnu, Brahma, and the other radiant beings joined the wedding procession on their own mounts. The procession was beautiful, but it still did not match the groom's greatness.
insight: It shifts attention from outward grandeur to whether the whole scene truly matches its center.
modern_relevance: A grand event can be full of expensive details, perfect lighting, and famous guests — and still feel oddly wrong. The real measure is not spectacle, but fit.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिष्नु कहा अस बिहसि तब बोलि सकल दिसिराज। बिलग बिलग होइ चलहु सब निज निज सहित समाज ॥
translation: तब विष्णु भगवान ने सब दिक्पालों को बुलाकर हँसकर ऐसा कहा- सब लोग अपने-अपने दल समेत अलग-अलग होकर चलो ॥
english_translation: Then Vishnu smiled and said to all the guardians of the directions: "All of you, with your own retinues, go separately."
essence: Order protects joy from turning into spectacle.
simple_meaning: Vishnu tells the direction-guardians to go separately with their own groups. The wedding procession should not move as one huge crowd.
insight: It teaches coordination without ego: even celebration works best when each person knows their place.
modern_relevance: A group chat explodes before a big event, everyone talking at once and nobody hearing the plan. One calm voice says, 'Split up, handle your parts, and move cleanly.'
speaker: Vishnu

verse_text: बर अनुहारि बरात न भाई। हँसी करैहहु पर पुर जाई॥ बिष्नु बचन सुनि सुर मुसुकाने। निज निज सेन सहित बिलगाने ॥
translation: हे भाई! हम लोगों की यह बारात वर के योग्य नहीं है। क्या पराए नगर में जाकर हँसी कराओगे? विष्णु भगवान की बात सुनकर देवता मुस्कुराए और वे अपनी-अपनी सेना सहित अलग हो गए ॥
english_translation: Brother, this procession is not fit for the groom. Will you go to a foreign city and invite ridicule? Hearing Vishnu's words, the devas smiled and separated into their own armies.
essence: A playful remark can bring a grand procession back into harmony.
simple_meaning: Vishnu jokes that the divine wedding procession is not suited to the groom's dignity, so the devas separate into their own groups.
insight: It shows how wit can restore order in a grand gathering without losing dignity.
modern_relevance: At a formal event, one person cracks a dry joke and the whole room relaxes. Tension drops, everyone finds their place, and the occasion feels alive instead of stiff.
speaker: Vishnu

verse_text: मनहीं मन महेसु मुसुकाहीं। हरि के बिंग्य बचन नहिं जाहीं॥ अति प्रिय बचन सुनत प्रिय केरे। भृंगिहि प्रेरि सकल गन टेरे ॥
translation: महादेवजी (यह देखकर) मन-ही-मन मुस्कुराते हैं कि विष्णु भगवान के व्यंग्य-वचन (दिल्लगी) नहीं छूटते! अपने प्यारे (विष्णु भगवान) के इन अति प्रिय वचनों को सुनकर शिवजी ने भी भृंगी को भेजकर अपने सब गणों को बुलवा लिया ॥
english_translation: Shiva smiles inwardly: Hari’s playful words never fail to amuse. Hearing those beloved words from his beloved, Shiva sends Bhṛngi to summon all his attendants.
essence: Even divine reverence can answer with a smile.
simple_meaning: Shiva smiles at Hari’s teasing words and quickly calls his attendants together through Bhṛngi.
insight: It shows devotion as a living relationship, where reverence includes delight and play.
modern_relevance: A friend teases you in a group chat, and instead of taking offense, you laugh because you know the affection behind it. That ease is the mood here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिव अनुसासन सुनि सब आए। प्रभु पद जलज सीस तिन्ह नाए॥ नाना बाहन नाना बेषा। बिहसे सिव समाज निज देखा ॥
translation: शिवजी की आज्ञा सुनते ही सब चले आए और उन्होंने स्वामी के चरण कमलों में सिर नवाया। तरह-तरह की सवारियों और तरह-तरह के वेष वाले अपने समाज को देखकर शिवजी हँसे ॥
english_translation: Hearing Shiva's command, everyone came and bowed their heads at the lord's lotus feet. Seeing his own company with many different mounts and many different disguises, Shiva laughed.
essence: True majesty can smile at its own strange variety.
simple_meaning: Shiva's followers arrive, bow to the lord, and Shiva laughs at the varied forms in his own company.
insight: It frames sacred gathering as alive, varied, and lightly self-aware rather than formal and rigid.
modern_relevance: A wedding convoy rolls in with scooters, cars, and borrowed outfits, and everyone is trying a little too hard. The moment still works because the joy is real, not polished.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोउ मुख हीन बिपुल मुख काहू। बिनु पद कर कोउ बहु पद बाहू॥ बिपुल नयन कोउ नयन बिहीना। रिष्टपुष्ट कोउ अति तनखीना ॥
translation: कोई बिना मुख का है, किसी के बहुत से मुख हैं, कोई बिना हाथ-पैर का है तो किसी के कई हाथ-पैर हैं। किसी के बहुत आँखें हैं तो किसी के एक भी आँख नहीं है। कोई बहुत मोटा-ताजा है, तो कोई बहुत ही दुबला-पतला है ॥
english_translation: Some have no mouth, some have many mouths. Some have no hands or feet, some have many hands and feet. Some have many eyes, some have no eyes. Some are very fat, and some are very thin.
essence: Life appears in countless forms, each with its own shape.
simple_meaning: Different beings appear with very different bodies: some lack mouths or limbs, some have many, some have many eyes, and some are thin or stout.
insight: It shifts attention from sameness to the sheer range of living forms.
modern_relevance: You walk into a crowded train and see every kind of body, face, and posture at once. The mind wants to sort and judge; the verse simply notices how varied life already is.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तन कीन कोउ अति पीन पावन कोउ अपावन गति धरें। भूषन कराल कपाल कर सब सद्य सोनित तन भरें॥ खर स्वान सुअर सृकाल मुख गन बेष अगनित को गनै। बहु जिनस प्रेत पिसाच जोगि जमात बरनत नहिं बनै॥
translation: कोई बहुत दुबला, कोई बहुत मोटा, कोई पवित्र और कोई अपवित्र वेष धारण किए हुए है। भयंकर गहने पहने हाथ में कपाल लिए हैं और सब के सब शरीर में ताजा खून लपेटे हुए हैं। गधे, कुत्ते, सूअर और सियार के से उनके मुख हैं। गणों के अनगिनत वेषों को कौन गिने? बहुत प्रकार के प्रेत, पिशाच और योगिनियों की जमाते हैं। उनका वर्णन करते नहीं बनता।
english_translation: Some are extremely thin, some extremely stout; some bear auspicious forms, some in inauspicious forms. They wear terrible ornaments and skulls in their hands, and their bodies are smeared with fresh blood. Their faces are like donkeys, dogs, pigs, and jackals. Who can count the countless forms of the attendants? Many kinds of ghosts, spirits, and yoginis are there; their company cannot be described.
essence: Countless forms gather around Shiva, too strange to fully name.
simple_meaning: Shiva's attendants appear in countless strange forms, some beautiful and some terrifying, with wild ornaments and fierce faces. The verse is describing their bizarre crowd, not teaching a doctrine.
insight: It trains attention to receive vivid scene-setting without forcing a moral onto every detail.
modern_relevance: A festival crowd spills out of a side street at midnight: painted faces, strange costumes, drums, laughter, and masks that are half playful and half unsettling. The point is the atmosphere, not a lesson.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाचहिं गावहिं गीत परम तरंगी भूत सब। देखत अति बिपरीत बोलहिं बचन बिचित्र बिधि ॥
translation: भूत-प्रेत नाचते और गाते हैं, वे सब बड़े मौजी हैं। देखने में बहुत ही बेढंगे जान पड़ते हैं और बड़े ही विचित्र ढंग से बोलते हैं ॥
english_translation: The spirits dance and sing, all full of wild delight. They look utterly strange and speak in wonderfully odd ways.
essence: The divine wedding turns even the strange into celebration.
simple_meaning: The spirits are dancing, singing, and speaking in strange, playful ways. The verse simply describes their odd, lively behavior.
insight: It trains attention to notice vivid scene-setting without forcing a moral lesson onto every detail.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall and everything feels slightly unreal — loud music, strange costumes, people laughing too hard. Some moments are meant to overwhelm you with color and motion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जस दूलहु तसि बनी बराता। कौतुक बिबिध होहिं मग जाता॥ इहाँ हिमाचल रचेउ बिताना। अति बिचित्र नहिं जाइ बखाना ॥
translation: जैसा दूल्हा है, अब वैसी ही बारात बन गई है। मार्ग में चलते हुए भाँति-भाँति के कौतुक (तमाशे) होते जाते हैं। इधर हिमाचल ने ऐसा विचित्र मण्डप बनाया कि जिसका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता ॥
english_translation: As the bridegroom is, so has the wedding party become. On the way, all kinds of marvels arise. Here, Himachal has built a wondrous pavilion beyond description.
essence: A great union makes the whole world seem newly arranged.
simple_meaning: The wedding procession matches the bridegroom’s grandeur, and the journey is full of wonders. Himachal has prepared an indescribably beautiful pavilion for the ceremony.
insight: It shifts attention from plot to atmosphere, showing how devotion makes even the setting feel sacred.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall and everything feels transformed — the lights, the music, even the air. A sacred or joyful moment changes the whole world around it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सैल सकल जहँ लगि जग माहीं। लघु बिसाल नहिं बरनि सिराहीं॥ बन सागर सब नदी तलावा। हिमगिरि सब कहुँ नेवत पठावा ॥
translation: जगत में जितने छोटे-बड़े पर्वत थे, जिनका वर्णन करके पार नहीं मिलता तथा जितने वन, समुद्र, नदियाँ और तालाब थे, हिमाचल ने सबको नेवता भेजा ॥
english_translation: Himachal sent invitations to all mountains, forests, seas, rivers, and lakes in the world.
essence: A sacred celebration becomes large enough to include the whole world.
simple_meaning: Himachal sent invitations to every mountain, forest, sea, river, and lake in the world.
insight: It frames the event as a celebration that includes the entire world, not just the immediate family.
modern_relevance: You plan a wedding, and suddenly every cousin, neighbor, and old family friend gets included. The joy feels bigger than the guest list — as if the whole world should be there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कामरूप सुंदर तन धारी। सहित समाज सहित बर नारी॥ गए सकल तुहिमाचल गेहा। गावहिं मंगल सहित सनेहा ॥
translation: वे सब अपनी इच्छानुसार रूप धारण करने वाले सुंदर शरीर धारण कर सुंदरी स्त्रियों और समाजों के साथ हिमाचल के घर गए। सभी स्नेह सहित मंगल गीत गाते हैं ॥
english_translation: All those who could take whatever form they wished, with beautiful bodies, along with their companions and women, went to Himachal's home. Everyone sang auspicious songs with affection.
essence: A sacred gathering becomes joyful when everyone arrives in love.
simple_meaning: The guests arrive in splendid forms, bringing their companions and women, and they enter Himachal's home singing auspicious songs with love.
insight: It shifts attention from doctrine to atmosphere: the sacred event is unfolding through collective celebration.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall fills before the ceremony begins: relatives in bright clothes, music starting up, everyone arriving with smiles and excitement. The moment is about shared joy, not a single speech.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रथमहिं गिरि बहु गृह सँवराए। जथाजोगु तहँ तहँ सब छाए॥ पुर सोभा अवलोकि सुहाई। लागइ लघु बिरंचि निपुनाई ॥
translation: हिमाचल ने पहले ही से बहुत से घर सजवा रखे थे। यथायोग्य उन-उन स्थानों में सब लोग उतर गए। नगर की सुंदर शोभा देखकर ब्रह्मा की रचना चातुरी भी तुच्छ लगती थी ॥
english_translation: Himachal had already prepared many houses. Everyone settled in the right place. Seeing the city’s beauty, even Brahma’s skill seemed small.
essence: Prepared welcome can make greatness feel ordinary.
simple_meaning: Himachal has already arranged homes for everyone, and the city is so beautiful that even Brahma’s craftsmanship seems small beside it.
insight: It shifts attention from mere arrangement to the feeling of being fully received.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where every flower, light, and seat has been arranged with care. Before anyone speaks, the whole place tells you: you were expected, and you were welcomed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लघु लाग बिधि की निपुनता अवलोकि पुर सोभा सही। बन बाग कूप तड़ाग सरिता सुभग सब सक को कही॥ मंगल बिपुल तोरन पताका केतु गृह गृह सोहहीं। बनिता पुरुष सुंदर चतुर छबि देखि मुनि मन मोहहीं॥
translation: नगर की शोभा देखकर ब्रह्मा की निपुणता सचमुच तुच्छ लगती है। वन, बाग, कुएँ, तालाब, नदियाँ सभी सुंदर हैं, उनका वर्णन कौन कर सकता है? घर-घर बहुत से मंगल सूचक तोरण और ध्वजा-पताकाएँ सुशोभित हो रही हैं। वहाँ के सुंदर और चतुर स्त्री-पुरुषों की छबि देखकर मुनियों के भी मन मोहित हो जाते हैं॥
english_translation: Seeing the beauty of the city, Brahma's skill seems small. Forests, gardens, wells, ponds, and rivers are all lovely; who can describe them all? Great auspicious banners and flags adorn every house. The beautiful and clever women and men there enchant even the sages' minds.
essence: Beauty can be so complete it makes even creation seem modest.
simple_meaning: The city is so beautiful that even Brahma's craftsmanship seems small by comparison. Every part of it, from gardens to rivers to houses, is adorned and enchanting.
insight: It shifts attention from utility to sacred beauty, showing how an environment can elevate the mind before any event begins.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding venue where every lamp, flower, and doorway has been arranged with care. Before anyone speaks, the whole place already tells you that something sacred is about to happen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जगदंबा जहँ अवतरी सो पुरु बरनि कि जाइ। रिद्धि सिद्धि संपत्ति सुख नित नूतन अधिकाइ ॥
translation: जिस नगर में स्वयं जगदम्बा ने अवतार लिया, क्या उसका वर्णन हो सकता है? वहाँ ऋद्धि, सिद्धि, सम्पत्ति और सुख नित-नए बढ़ते जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Can the city where Jagadamba herself incarnated ever be described? There, prosperity, accomplishment, wealth, and joy keep increasing anew every day.
essence: A place touched by the divine keeps becoming more abundant.
simple_meaning: The city where the world-mother was born cannot be fully described. Its prosperity, success, wealth, and joy keep growing every day.
insight: It shifts attention from material beauty alone to the sacred presence that makes abundance deepen.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home where the air feels different — calmer, warmer, somehow more generous. No one can list why it feels blessed, but everyone can feel it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नगर निकट बरात सुनि आई। पुर खरभरु सोभा अधिकाई॥ करि बनाव सजि बाहन नाना। चले लेन सादर अगवाना ॥
translation: बारात को नगर के निकट आई सुनकर नगर में चहल-पहल मच गई, जिससे उसकी शोभा बढ़ गई। अगवानी करने वाले लोग बनाव-श्रृंगार करके तथा नाना प्रकार की सवारियों को सजाकर आदर सहित बारात को लेने चले ॥
english_translation: Hearing that the marriage procession had reached near the city, the city became lively and even more beautiful. People dressed up, decorated many kinds of vehicles, and went out respectfully to welcome it.
essence: Arrival itself can beautify an entire city.
simple_meaning: The city became lively when the wedding procession came close. People prepared themselves, decorated their rides, and went out respectfully to welcome it.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the shared excitement it creates.
modern_relevance: A neighborhood wakes up because the guests everyone has waited for are finally turning into the lane. People sweep the steps, straighten their clothes, and step out smiling before the first knock.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हियँ हरषे सुर सेन निहारी। हरिहि देखि अति भए सुखारी॥ सिव समाज जब देखन लागे। बिडरि चले बाहन सब भागे ॥
translation: देवताओं के समाज को देखकर सब मन में प्रसन्न हुए और विष्णु भगवान को देखकर तो बहुत ही सुखी हुए, किन्तु जब शिवजी के दल को देखने लगे तब तो उनके सब वाहन (सवारियों के हाथी, घोड़े, रथ के बैल आदि) डरकर भाग चले ॥
english_translation: The gods were delighted to see their host. Seeing Hari made them deeply happy. But when they looked at Shiva's company, all their mounts fled in fear.
essence: Divine presence can delight the heart and unsettle the body at once.
simple_meaning: The gods felt joy at the sight of the divine company, but their mounts panicked when they saw Shiva's group.
insight: It shows how sacred presence can be felt before it is understood, and how fear can arise from awe.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where one person instantly relaxes everyone, while another's intensity makes people go silent. Presence itself changes the atmosphere before a word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धरि धीरजु तहँ रहे सयाने। बालक सब लै जीव पराने॥ गएँ भवन पूछहिं पितु माता। कहहिं बचन भय कंपित गाता ॥
translation: कुछ बड़ी उम्र के समझदार लोग धीरज धरकर वहाँ डटे रहे। लड़के तो सब अपने प्राण लेकर भागे। घर पहुँचने पर जब माता-पिता पूछते हैं, तब वे भय से काँपते हुए शरीर से ऐसा वचन कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: The wise stayed there with patience. The boys fled with their lives. When they returned home, their mothers and fathers asked them, and they answered with trembling bodies.
essence: Fear sends some running while steadiness holds its ground.
simple_meaning: The elders stayed calm, but the younger people ran away in fear. Later, they went home shaking and had to explain what happened to their parents.
insight: It contrasts steady composure with panic, showing how the same situation exposes different levels of inner steadiness.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and instantly feel you are the least prepared person there. Some people stay composed, but others rush out and rehearse excuses before they even reach home.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहिअ काह कहि जाइ न बाता। जम कर धार किधौं बरिआता॥ बरु बौराह बसहँ असवारा। ब्याल कपाल बिभूषन छारा ॥
translation: क्या कहें, कोई बात कही नहीं जाती। यह बारात है या यमराज की सेना? दूल्हा पागल है और बैल पर सवार है। साँप, कपाल और राख ही उसके गहने हैं ॥
english_translation: What can be said? No words can describe it. Is this a wedding procession or Yama's army? The groom is wild, riding a bull, with snakes, skulls, and ash as ornaments.
essence: Shiva's procession shatters every ordinary expectation of beauty.
simple_meaning: The crowd is stunned by Shiva's appearance. His wedding procession looks terrifying, unlike any ordinary marriage.
insight: It shifts attention from polished appearance to the startling reality beneath it.
modern_relevance: You open the door expecting a neat, normal scene and find complete chaos instead. The first reaction is disbelief before understanding catches up.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तन छार ब्याल कपाल भूषन नगन जटिल भयंकरा। सँग भूत प्रेत पिसाच जोगिनि बिकट मुख रजनीचरा॥ जो जिअत रहिहि बरात देखत पुन्य बड़ तेहि कर सही। देखिहि सो उमा बिबाहु घर घर बात असि लरिकन्ह कही॥
translation: दूल्हे के शरीर पर राख लगी है, साँप और कपाल के गहने हैं, वह नंगा, जटाधारी और भयंकर है। उसके साथ भयानक मुखवाले भूत, प्रेत, पिशाच, योगिनियाँ और राक्षस हैं, जो बारात को देखकर जीता बचेगा, सचमुच उसके बड़े ही पुण्य हैं और वही पार्वती का विवाह देखेगा। लड़कों ने घर-घर यही बात कही।
english_translation: His body was smeared with ash, adorned with snakes and skulls, naked, matted-haired, and terrifying. With him were fearsome ghosts, spirits, ghouls, yoginis, and wild-eyed night-walkers. The boys said, 'Whoever lives to see this wedding procession is truly blessed; that person will see Uma's marriage.' They carried this story from house to house.
essence: The most terrifying sight can also be a blessed one.
simple_meaning: The boys describe Shiva's strange wedding procession and joke that anyone who survives seeing it is blessed enough to witness Uma's wedding.
insight: It turns shock into awe and prepares the reader for Shiva's marriage as a sacred, otherworldly event.
modern_relevance: A group chat fills with screenshots after someone shows up in the most unexpected way at a formal event. People panic, then joke, then realize they have witnessed something unforgettable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समुझि महेस समाज सब जननि जनक मुसुकाहिं। बाल बुझाए बिबिध बिधि निडर होहु डरु नाहिं ॥
translation: महेश्वर (शिवजी) का समाज समझकर सब लड़कों के माता-पिता मुस्कुराते हैं। उन्होंने बहुत तरह से लड़कों को समझाया कि निडर हो जाओ, डर की कोई बात नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Seeing that it is Lord Shiva’s company, all the parents smile. They reassure the boys in many ways: “Be fearless; there is nothing to fear.”
essence: Clear seeing turns fear into a smile.
simple_meaning: The parents realize this is Shiva’s wedding party, so they smile and calm the boys, telling them not to be afraid.
insight: It shifts panic into calm by naming the situation clearly.
modern_relevance: A child sees a masked performer at a festival and starts to cry. The parent leans down, names what is happening, and the fear melts. Understanding changes the whole feeling of the moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लै अगवान बरातहि आए। दिए सबहि जनवास सुहाए॥ मैनाँ सुभ आरती सँवारी। संग सुमंगल गावहिं नारी ॥
translation: अगवान लोग बारात को लिवा लाए, उन्होंने सबको सुंदर जनवासे ठहरने को दिए। मैना (पार्वतीजी की माता) ने शुभ आरती सजाई और उनके साथ की स्त्रियाँ उत्तम मंगलगीत गाने लगीं ॥
english_translation: The attendants brought the wedding party in and gave everyone pleasant lodging. Maina prepared a blessed aarti, and the women with her sang auspicious songs.
essence: True welcome is shown in the care prepared before anyone asks.
simple_meaning: The wedding party is welcomed properly, with lodging, aarti, and songs of blessing.
insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle of arrival to the care that makes welcome complete.
modern_relevance: The guests are arriving before dawn, shoes piled at the door, tea already warming on the stove. Someone has thought of everything, and the whole house feels ready to receive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कंचन थार सोह बर पानी। परिछन चली हरहि हरषानी॥ बिकट बेष रुद्रहि जब देखा। अबलन्ह उर भय भयउ बिसेषा ॥
translation: सुंदर हाथों में सोने का थाल शोभित है, इस प्रकार मैना हर्ष के साथ शिवजी का परछन करने चलीं। जब महादेवजी को भयानक वेष में देखा तब तो स्त्रियों के मन में बड़ा भारी भय उत्पन्न हो गया ॥
english_translation: Mina, delighted, went to perform Shiva's ceremonial welcome with a golden tray. But when she saw Rudra in a fierce form, a great fear rose in the hearts of the women.
essence: A joyful welcome can collapse into fear before the unexpected.
simple_meaning: Mina goes joyfully to welcome Shiva, but his fierce appearance frightens the women.
insight: It shows how quickly the mind can shift from welcome to alarm when appearances unsettle it.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room expecting a warm introduction, and the person you came to meet feels intimidating instead. The body reacts before the mind can catch up.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भागि भवन पैठीं अति त्रासा। गए महेसु जहाँ जनवासा॥ मैना हृदयँ भयउ दुखु भारी। लीन्ही बोली गिरीसकुमारी ॥
translation: बहुत ही डर के मारे भागकर वे घर में घुस गईं और शिवजी जहाँ जनवासा था, वहाँ चले गए। मैना के हृदय में बड़ा दुःख हुआ, उन्होंने पार्वतीजी को अपने पास बुला लिया ॥
english_translation: Overcome with fear, she ran inside the house. Mahesh went to the guest quarters. Deep sorrow filled Maina’s heart, and she called Parvati to her side.
essence: Fear can break the welcome of a sacred moment.
simple_meaning: Maina is frightened by Shiva’s fierce appearance, runs inside, and then calls Parvati to comfort her and explain the situation.
insight: It shows how fear interrupts hospitality and pushes a person back into protective instinct.
modern_relevance: You open the door expecting a normal visit, then freeze because the person standing there feels overwhelming. Fear changes the whole room before anyone speaks.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अधिक सनेहँ गोद बैठारी। स्याम सरोज नयन भरे बारी॥ जेहिं बिधि तुम्हहि रूपु अस दीन्हा। तेहिं जड़ बरु बाउर कस कीन्हा ॥
translation: और अत्यन्त स्नेह से गोद में बैठाकर अपने नीलकमल के समान नेत्रों में आँसू भरकर कहा- जिस विधाता ने तुमको ऐसा सुंदर रूप दिया, उस मूर्ख ने तुम्हारे दूल्हे को बावला कैसे बनाया? ॥
english_translation: With deep affection she lifted her into her lap, tears filling her blue-lotus eyes. "The one who gave you such beauty—how did that fool make your bridegroom so bewildered?"
essence: Beauty here is so overwhelming it leaves the bridegroom dazed.
simple_meaning: Parvati lovingly takes Sita into her lap, tears in her eyes, and marvels that the same maker who gave Sita such beauty has made her bridegroom so bewildered.
insight: It shifts the scene from fear to affectionate wonder, showing how warmth can soften tension instantly.
modern_relevance: At a wedding, an elder pulls the bride close, tears shining, and says with a smile, "How did fate make such a beautiful match so lopsided?"
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: कस कीन्ह बरु बौराह बिधि जेहिं तुम्हहि सुंदरता दई। जो फलु चहिअ सुरतरुहिं सो बरबस बबूरहिं लागई॥ तुम्ह सहित गिरि तें गिरौं पावक जरौं जलनिधि महुँ परौं। घरु जाउ अपजसु होउ जग जीवत बिबाहु न हौं करौं॥
translation: जिस विधाता ने तुमको सुंदरता दी, उसने तुम्हारे लिए वर बावला कैसे बनाया? जो फल कल्पवृक्ष में लगना चाहिए, वह जबर्दस्ती बबूल में लग रहा है। मैं तुम्हें लेकर पहाड़ से गिर पड़ूँगी, आग में जल जाऊँगी या समुद्र में कूद पड़ूँगी। चाहे घर उजड़ जाए और संसार भर में अपकीर्ति फैल जाए, पर जीते जी मैं इस बावले वर से तुम्हारा विवाह न करूँगी।
english_translation: How did the one who gave you beauty give you this mad husband? The fruit meant for a wish-fulfilling tree is being forced onto a thorny bush. I would rather fall from a mountain with you, burn in fire, or plunge into the sea than let this marriage happen while I live, even if the house is ruined and the world speaks ill of me.
essence: Protective love can refuse the whole world to defend a child.
simple_meaning: Maina is overwhelmed by grief and refuses to accept this marriage. She says the girl deserves a worthy match, not this foolish one, and she would rather face ruin than consent.
insight: It shows how deep care can override fear of gossip, loss, or social approval.
modern_relevance: A parent sits through a marriage discussion, hearing polite praise for a match that feels wrong in the gut. The room wants agreement; the heart wants protection. Maina's refusal is that raw, protective instinct.
speaker: Maina

verse_text: भईं बिकल अबला सकल दुखित देखि गिरिनारि। करि बिलापु रोदति बदति सुता सनेहु सँभारि ॥।
translation: हिमाचल की स्त्री (मैना) को दुःखी देखकर सारी स्त्रियाँ व्याकुल हो गईं। मैना अपनी कन्या के स्नेह को याद करके विलाप करती, रोती और कहती थीं- ॥
english_translation: All the women were distressed to see the mountain lady in sorrow. Mena wept, lamented, and spoke, remembering her daughter's love.
essence: A mother’s grief pulls everyone into the same wound.
simple_meaning: All the women around Mena are shaken by her grief. Mena herself weeps and speaks while remembering her daughter's love.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the emotional contagion of loss.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and instantly feel the tension in a mother’s face, the silence in the women around her, the grief no one has named yet. Some pain enters everyone at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नारद कर मैं काह बिगारा। भवनु मोर जिन्ह बसत उजारा॥ अस उपदेसु उमहि जिन्ह दीन्हा। बौरे बरहि लागि तपु कीन्हा ॥
translation: मैंने नारद का क्या बिगाड़ा था, जिन्होंने मेरा बसता हुआ घर उजाड़ दिया और जिन्होंने पार्वती को ऐसा उपदेश दिया कि जिससे उसने बावले वर के लिए तप किया ॥
english_translation: What harm did I do to Narada, who ruined my settled home? He gave Uma such counsel that she performed austerity for a foolish bridegroom.
essence: A careless counsel can reorder an entire life.
simple_meaning: Parvati complains that Narada disturbed her peaceful home by advising Uma to do austerity for an unusual bridegroom.
insight: It warns you to measure advice by its consequences, not by how clever it sounds.
modern_relevance: A friend sends one message, meant as a clever suggestion, and suddenly a relationship, a plan, or a family mood changes shape overnight.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: साचेहुँ उन्ह कें मोह न माया। उदासीन धनु धामु न जाया॥ पर घर घालक लाज न भीरा। बाँझ कि जान प्रसव कै पीरा ॥
translation: सचमुच उनके न किसी का मोह है, न माया, न उनके धन है, न घर है और न स्त्री ही है, वे सबसे उदासीन हैं। इसी से वे दूसरे का घर उजाड़ने वाले हैं। उन्हें न किसी की लाज है, न डर है। भला, बाँझ स्त्री प्रसव की पीड़ा को क्या जाने ॥
english_translation: Truly, they have no attachment, no illusion, no wealth, no home, and no wife; they are utterly indifferent. That is why they are destroyers of another's home. They have no shame and no fear. How can a barren woman know the pain of childbirth?
essence: Grief turns private pain into a fierce accusation.
simple_meaning: Parvati is blaming the beings who ruined her home, saying they are detached, shameless, and unable to understand a mother's suffering.
insight: It shows how wounded love can judge others through the lens of its own loss.
modern_relevance: A parent watches a family fracture after one careless remark and says, 'You don't know what this cost.' Grief turns into sharp moral language before calm returns.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जननिहि बिकल बिलोकि भवानी। बोली जुत बिबेक मृदु बानी॥ अस बिचारि सोचहि मति माता। सो न टरइ जो रचइ बिधाता ॥
translation: माता को विकल देखकर पार्वतीजी विवेकयुक्त कोमल वाणी बोलीं- हे माता! जो विधाता रच देते हैं, वह टलता नहीं, ऐसा विचार कर तुम सोच मत करो! ॥
english_translation: Seeing her mother distressed, Bhavani spoke with gentle, discerning words: "Mother, do not grieve. What the Creator has written does not turn aside."
essence: Peace begins when you stop resisting what cannot be changed.
simple_meaning: Parvati gently tells her mother not to grieve, because what is ordained cannot be avoided.
insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to calm acceptance of what cannot be altered.
modern_relevance: You stare at a message you cannot take back, then pace the room replaying every line. Parvati’s answer is the pause that ends the spiral: some things cannot be rewritten by panic.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: करम लिखा जौं बाउर नाहू। तौ कत दोसु लगाइअ काहू॥ तुम्ह सन मिटहिं कि बिधि के अंका। मातु ब्यर्थ जनि लेहु कलंका ॥
translation: जो मेरे भाग्य में बावला ही पति लिखा है, तो किसी को क्यों दोष लगाया जाए? हे माता! क्या विधाता के अंक तुमसे मिट सकते हैं? वृथा कलंक का टीका मत लो ॥
english_translation: If a foolish husband was written into my fate, why blame anyone? Mother, can the marks of the creator be erased? Do not take this useless stain upon yourself.
essence: What cannot be changed should not be blamed.
simple_meaning: Parvati tells her mother not to blame anyone for her marriage, because what has been written by fate cannot be changed.
insight: It shifts the mind from blame to acceptance, so energy stops leaking into regret and shame.
modern_relevance: You replay the breakup, the job loss, the diagnosis, hunting for the one person to blame. Then someone wiser says: stop. Some things are already written into the shape of your life.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: जनि लेहु मातु कलंकु करुना परिहरहु अवसर नहीं। दुखु सुखु जो लिखा लिलार हमरें जाब जहँ पाउब तहीं॥ सुनि उमा बचन बिनीत कोमल सकल अबला सोचहीं। बहु भाँति बिधिहि लगाइ दूषन नयन बारि बिमोचहीं॥
translation: हे माता! कलंक मत लो, रोना छोड़ो, यह अवसर विषाद करने का नहीं है। मेरे भाग्य में जो दुःख-सुख लिखा है, उसे मैं जहाँ जाऊँगी, वहीं पाऊँगी! पार्वतीजी के ऐसे विनय भरे कोमल वचन सुनकर सारी स्त्रियाँ सोच करने लगीं और भाँति-भाँति से विधाता को दोष देकर आँखों से आँसू बहाने लगीं।
english_translation: Do not take this as disgrace, Mother. Let go of grief; this is no time for sorrow. The joy and sorrow written on my brow will meet me wherever I go. Hearing Uma's gentle, humble words, all the women reflected, blamed fate in many ways, and shed tears.
essence: Some grief must be faced, not fought.
simple_meaning: Parvati tells her mother not to feel ashamed or keep grieving. She says whatever joy or sorrow is written for her will find her wherever she goes, and the women around her begin to weep and blame fate.
insight: It shifts the mind from protest to acceptance, so pain is met without extra shame or resistance.
modern_relevance: A family group chat has just turned into a flood of blame after bad news. One person stops the spiral and says, with quiet steadiness, that some things cannot be undone and must be faced as they are.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: तेहि अवसर नारद सहित अरु रिषि सप्त समेत। समाचार सुनि तुहिनगिरि गवने तुरत निकेत ॥
translation: इस समाचार को सुनते ही हिमाचल उसी समय नारदजी और सप्त ऋषियों को साथ लेकर अपने घर गए ॥
english_translation: At that moment, Narada and the seven sages came along, and after hearing the news, Himavan immediately returned home.
essence: News arrives, and the whole household turns toward what it means.
simple_meaning: Narada and the seven sages arrived, and Himavan hurried home after hearing the news.
insight: It keeps the narrative moving from private grief to public revelation.
modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent, then one message lands and everyone starts moving at once. Some news changes the whole room before anyone has time to think.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब नारद सबही समुझावा। पूरुब कथा प्रसंगु सुनावा॥ मयना सत्य सुनहु मम बानी। जगदंबा तव सुता भवानी ॥
translation: तब नारदजी ने पूर्वजन्म की कथा सुनाकर सबको समझाया (और कहा) कि हे मैना! तुम मेरी सच्ची बात सुनो, तुम्हारी यह लड़की साक्षात जगज्जनी भवानी है ॥
english_translation: Then Narad explained everything to all. He told the story of the past birth. "Mena, hear my true words: your daughter is the world-mother, Bhavani."
essence: A wise voice reveals the divine identity hidden inside an ordinary birth.
simple_meaning: Narad explains the hidden identity of Mena's daughter by recounting her past birth and calling her the world-mother Bhavani.
insight: It shifts attention from surface appearance to hidden identity and meaning.
modern_relevance: A family hears difficult news about a daughter’s future, and one wise voice reframes the whole moment: what seems fragile is actually sacred and immense.
speaker: Narad

verse_text: अजा अनादि सक्ति अबिनासिनि। सदा संभु अरधंग निवासिनि॥ जग संभव पालन लय कारिनि। निज इच्छा लीला बपु धारिनि ॥
translation: ये अजन्मा, अनादि और अविनाशिनी शक्ति हैं। सदा शिवजी के अर्द्धांग में रहती हैं। ये जगत की उत्पत्ति, पालन और संहार करने वाली हैं और अपनी इच्छा से ही लीला शरीर धारण करती हैं ॥
english_translation: She is birthless, beginningless, and imperishable power. She always dwells as Shiva's half. She brings forth, sustains, and dissolves the world, and takes a form of her own will for divine play.
essence: She is eternal power, not a passing figure in the tale.
simple_meaning: Parvati is described as the eternal power behind creation, preservation, and dissolution. She is not born or destroyed, and she takes form by her own will.
insight: It shifts attention from Parvati's story to her cosmic nature as the power behind all change.
modern_relevance: A person may look like only a role, a body, or a name on paper. But some presences in life feel larger than biography — steady, formative, and impossible to reduce to one incident.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जनमीं प्रथम दच्छ गृह जाई। नामु सती सुंदर तनु पाई॥ तहँहुँ सती संकरहि बिबाहीं। कथा प्रसिद्ध सकल जग माहीं ॥
translation: पहले ये दक्ष के घर जाकर जन्मी थीं, तब इनका सती नाम था, बहुत सुंदर शरीर पाया था। वहाँ भी सती शंकरजी से ही ब्याही गई थीं। यह कथा सारे जगत में प्रसिद्ध है ॥
english_translation: She was first born in Daksha's house, where she received the name Sati and a beautiful body. There too, Sati was married to Shiva. This story is famous throughout the world.
essence: Sati's former life is recalled to prepare for a deeper revelation.
simple_meaning: Sati was first born in Daksha's house, married Shiva, and became well known across the world.
insight: It sets up the identity of the speaker's former life before the deeper divine recognition begins.
modern_relevance: A family keeps repeating a story everyone already knows, because the real point is not the facts — it is what those facts are about to reveal.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक बार आवत सिव संगा। देखेउ रघुकुल कमल पतंगा॥ भयउ मोहु सिव कहा न कीन्हा। भ्रम बस बेषु सीय कर लीन्हा ॥
translation: एक बार इन्होंने शिवजी के साथ आते हुए (राह में) रघुकुल रूपी कमल के सूर्य श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखा, तब इन्हें मोह हो गया और इन्होंने शिवजी का कहना न मानकर भ्रमवश सीताजी का वेष धारण कर लिया ॥
english_translation: Once, while coming with Shiva, she saw Ram, the sun of the Raghu line, and became deluded. Ignoring Shiva's words, she took on Sita's form under the spell of confusion.
essence: Delusion makes imitation feel like devotion.
simple_meaning: Sati saw Ram and became confused. She ignored Shiva's warning and took Sita's form.
insight: It shows how attraction without clear seeing leads to imitation instead of understanding.
modern_relevance: You see someone admired by everyone and instantly want to become like them. In that rush, you copy the surface and miss the deeper truth.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिय बेषु सतीं जो कीन्ह तेहिं अपराध संकर परिहरीं। हर बिरहँ जाइ बहोरि पितु कें जग्य जोगानल जरीं॥ अब जनमि तुम्हरे भवन निज पति लागि दारुन तपु किया। अस जानि संसय तजहु गिरिजा सर्बदा संकरप्रिया॥
translation: सतीजी ने जो सीता का वेष धारण किया, उसी अपराध के कारण शंकरजी ने उनको त्याग दिया। फिर शिवजी के वियोग में ये अपने पिता के यज्ञ में जाकर वहीं योगाग्नि से भस्म हो गईं। अब इन्होंने तुम्हारे घर जन्म लेकर अपने पति के लिए कठिन तप किया है ऐसा जानकर संदेह छोड़ दो, पार्वतीजी तो सदा ही शिवजी की प्रिया (अर्द्धांगिनी) हैं।
english_translation: Because Sati once took on Sita's form, Shiva left her for that offense. In separation from Shiva, she later went to her father's sacrifice and burned herself in the fire of yoga. Now she has been born in your house and has done severe austerity for her husband. Knowing this, cast away doubt, Girija is always dear to Shiva.
essence: Trust the bond that has already endured loss and return.
simple_meaning: Parvati should not doubt Shiva's love. Sati's past, her suffering, and her present birth as Parvati all prove that she is always dear to Shiva.
insight: It shifts the mind from suspicion to confidence in a bond that has already been tested.
modern_relevance: You replay an old misunderstanding in your mind while the other person keeps showing up with care. The mind wants proof; the heart needs trust. This verse asks you to stop feeding suspicion.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सुनि नारद के बचन तब सब कर मिटा बिषाद। छन महुँ ब्यापेउ सकल पुर घर घर यह संबाद ॥
translation: तब नारद के वचन सुनकर सबका विषाद मिट गया और क्षणभर में यह समाचार सारे नगर में घर-घर फैल गया ॥
english_translation: Hearing Narad's words, everyone's sorrow vanished. In a moment, the news spread through the whole city, house to house.
essence: One true message can dissolve collective sorrow.
simple_meaning: Narad's words remove everyone's sadness, and the good news quickly spreads through the whole city.
insight: It shows how truthful reassurance can calm a whole community at once.
modern_relevance: A tense family group chat suddenly goes quiet after one reassuring message. One clear sentence can dissolve hours of dread and spread relief instantly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब मयना हिमवंतु अनंदे। पुनि पुनि पारबती पद बंदे॥ नारि पुरुष सिसु जुबा सयाने। नगर लोग सब अति हरषाने ॥
translation: तब मैना और हिमवान आनंद में मग्न हो गए और उन्होंने बार-बार पार्वती के चरणों की वंदना की। स्त्री, पुरुष, बालक, युवा और वृद्ध नगर के सभी लोग बहुत प्रसन्न हुए ॥
