english_translation: Then Maina and Himavan overflowed with joy and repeatedly bowed at Parvati's feet. Men, women, children, youths, and elders—all the people of the city were deeply delighted.
essence: Joy becomes complete when an entire community shares it.
simple_meaning: Maina, Himavan, and everyone in the city felt great joy and honored Parvati with repeated bows.
insight: It shifts attention from private relief to communal gratitude and celebration.
modern_relevance: The message lands when a family gets good news after days of tension, and relief turns into shared celebration. One person's blessing can lift an entire home.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लगे होन पुर मंगल गाना। सजे सबहिं हाटक घट नाना॥ भाँति अनेक भई जेवनारा। सूपसास्त्र जस कछु ब्यवहारा ॥
translation: नगर में मंगल गीत गाए जाने लगे और सबने भाँति-भाँति के सुवर्ण के कलश सजाए। पाक शास्त्र में जैसी रीति है, उसके अनुसार अनेक भाँति की ज्योनार हुई (रसोई बनी) ॥
english_translation: The city began singing auspicious songs, and many golden vessels were arranged. In many different ways, the feast was prepared according to the rules of cooking.
essence: A sacred arrival turns the whole city into celebration.
simple_meaning: The whole city celebrates with songs, gold vessels, and a grand feast prepared in proper order.
insight: It shifts attention from private emotion to shared preparation and collective joy.
modern_relevance: The kitchen is crowded, the lights are up, and relatives keep arriving with trays and flowers. Everyone is busy because something precious is about to be welcomed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सो जेवनार कि जाइ बखानी। बसहिं भवन जेहिं मातु भवानी॥ सादर बोले सकल बराती। बिष्नु बिरंचि देव सब जाती ॥
translation: जिस घर में स्वयं माता भवानी रहती हों, वहाँ की ज्योनार (भोजन सामग्री) का वर्णन कैसे किया जा सकता है? हिमाचल ने आदरपूर्वक सब बारातियों, विष्णु, ब्रह्मा और सब जाति के देवताओं को बुलवाया ॥
english_translation: How can the feast be described, where Mother Bhavani herself dwells? With reverence, Himachal invited all the wedding guests, Vishnu, Brahma, and all classes of deities.
essence: Presence makes ordinary hospitality feel beyond description.
simple_meaning: The wedding feast is beyond description because Bhavani herself lives there. Himachal respectfully invites all the guests, including Vishnu, Brahma, and every class of divine beings.
insight: It shifts attention from the meal itself to the sanctity of the gathering and the honor shown to each guest.
modern_relevance: A home fills with guests, the kitchen runs hot, and everyone keeps smiling because one beloved person has arrived. The whole gathering feels larger than the food on the table.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिबिधि पाँति बैठी जेवनारा। लागे परुसन निपुन सुआरा॥ नारिबृंद सुर जेवँत जानी। लगीं देन गारीं मृदु बानी ॥
translation: भोजन (करने वालों) की बहुत सी पंगतें बैठीं। चतुर रसोइए परोसने लगे। स्त्रियों की मंडलियाँ देवताओं को भोजन करते जानकर कोमल वाणी से गालियाँ देने लगीं ॥
english_translation: Many rows of diners were seated. Skilled cooks began serving them. The women, seeing the gods eating, began offering playful teasing in gentle words.
essence: Celebration turns even teasing into sweetness.
simple_meaning: Guests sat in many rows while expert cooks served the food. The women, seeing the divine guests eating, began teasing them with gentle, playful words.
insight: It shifts attention from the meal itself to the social warmth surrounding it.
modern_relevance: At a wedding buffet, the aunties see the groom's side eating too slowly and start smiling, teasing, and laughing across the hall. The food is good, but the shared delight is what fills the room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गारीं मधुर स्वर देहिं सुंदरि बिंग्य बचन सुनावहीं। भोजनु करहिं सुर अति बिलंबु बिनोदु सुनि सचु पावहीं॥ जेवँत जो बढ्यो अनंदु सो मुख कोटिहूँ न परै कह्यो। अचवाँइ दीन्हें पान गवने बास जहँ जाको रह्यो॥
translation: सब सुंदरी स्त्रियाँ मीठे स्वर में गालियाँ देने लगीं और व्यंग्य भरे वचन सुनाने लगीं। देवगण विनोद सुनकर बहुत सुख अनुभव करते हैं, इसलिए भोजन करने में बड़ी देर लगा रहे हैं। भोजन के समय जो आनंद बढ़ा वह करोड़ों मुँह से भी नहीं कहा जा सकता। (भोजन कर चुकने पर) सबके हाथ-मुँह धुलवाकर पान दिए गए। फिर सब लोग, जो जहाँ ठहरे थे, वहाँ चले गए।
english_translation: The beautiful women spoke sweetly, offering teasing jests. The gods ate with delight and took their time, because the feast was so enjoyable. The joy of the meal cannot be told even with millions of mouths. After water for washing and betel leaves were given, everyone returned to their own lodging.
essence: True hospitality makes even delay feel like delight.
simple_meaning: The feast is so joyful and playful that even the guests linger over it. After the meal, everyone is properly attended to and sent back to their places.
insight: It turns attention from the food itself to the atmosphere of generous celebration and care.
modern_relevance: At a wedding table where everyone keeps talking long after the food is finished, the room itself becomes the memory. No one wants to leave because the welcome felt complete.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरि मुनिन्ह हिमवंत कहुँ लगन सुनाई आइ। समय बिलोकि बिबाह कर पठए देव बोलाइ ॥
translation: फिर मुनियों ने लौटकर हिमवान् को लगन (लग्न पत्रिका) सुनाई और विवाह का समय देखकर देवताओं को बुला भेजा ॥
english_translation: Then the sages returned and informed Himavan about the wedding date. Seeing the proper time, they sent for the deities.
essence: The wedding is now formally set in motion.
simple_meaning: The sages returned to Himavan, told him the wedding date, and arranged for the deities to be invited at the right time.
insight: It shifts attention from meaning to sequence: the sacred event now moves into formal preparation.
modern_relevance: The guest list is finally set, the hall is booked, and the ceremony can begin. Some verses matter because they move the moment into place.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बोलि सकल सुर सादर लीन्हे। सबहि जथोचित आसन दीन्हे॥ बेदी बेद बिधान सँवारी। सुभग सुमंगल गावहिं नारी ॥
translation: सब देवताओं को आदर सहित बुलवा लिया और सबको यथायोग्य आसन दिए। वेद की रीति से वेदी सजाई गई और स्त्रियाँ सुंदर श्रेष्ठ मंगल गीत गाने लगीं ॥
english_translation: All the radiant beings were invited respectfully and given seats according to custom. The altar was arranged according to Vedic rule, and women sang beautiful, auspicious songs.
essence: Reverence is shown first in the way a space is prepared.
simple_meaning: The gods are welcomed properly, the wedding altar is prepared, and the women sing auspicious songs.
insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to reverent preparation. The sacred begins in how carefully people make room for it.
modern_relevance: A family gathers before a wedding, checking every seat, every offering, every detail. No one is rushing; everyone is making space for what matters.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिंघासनु अति दिब्य सुहावा। जाइ न बरनि बिरंचि बनावा॥ बैठे सिव बिप्रन्ह सिरु नाई। हृदयँ सुमिरि निज प्रभु रघुराई ॥
translation: वेदिका पर एक अत्यन्त सुंदर दिव्य सिंहासन था, जिस (की सुंदरता) का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता, क्योंकि वह स्वयं ब्रह्माजी का बनाया हुआ था। ब्राह्मणों को सिर नवाकर और हृदय में अपने स्वामी श्री रघुनाथजी का स्मरण करके शिवजी उस सिंहासन पर बैठ गए ॥
english_translation: The throne on the altar was so wonderfully divine that even Brahma could not describe its beauty. Shiva bowed to the Brahmins, remembered his own lord Raghunath in his heart, and sat on that throne.
essence: Greatness is complete only when it bows before the divine.
simple_meaning: A magnificently divine throne was prepared. Shiva honored the Brahmins, remembered Ram in his heart, and took his seat.
insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing that true dignity begins with humility and remembrance.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is watching, and the spotlight could easily become yours. Instead, you greet the elders first, steady yourself, and remember what matters before taking your seat.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरि मुनीसन्ह उमा बोलाईं। करि सिंगारु सखीं लै आईं॥ देखत रूपु सकल सुर मोहे। बरनै छबि अस जग कबि को है ॥
translation: फिर मुनीश्वरों ने पार्वतीजी को बुलाया। सखियाँ श्रृंगार करके उन्हें ले आईं। पार्वतीजी के रूप को देखते ही सब देवता मोहित हो गए। संसार में ऐसा कवि कौन है, जो उस सुंदरता का वर्णन कर सके? ॥
english_translation: Then the sages called Uma. Her companions brought her, fully adorned. Seeing her form, all the radiant beings were enchanted. Who in this world could describe such beauty?
essence: Beauty can overwhelm speech before it can be named.
simple_meaning: Parvati is brought in beautifully dressed, and her beauty leaves the radiant beings spellbound. The verse ends by saying no poet could fully describe her grace.
insight: It shifts attention from explanation to awe, showing that some realities are meant to be witnessed, not reduced.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when someone enters and everyone feels it at once. No caption, no review, no analysis can fully hold that kind of presence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जगदंबिका जानि भव भामा। सुरन्ह मनहिं मन कीन्ह प्रनामा॥ सुंदरता मरजाद भवानी। जाइ न कोटिहुँ बदन बखानी ॥
translation: पार्वतीजी को जगदम्बा और शिवजी की पत्नी समझकर देवताओं ने मन ही मन प्रणाम किया। भवानीजी सुंदरता की सीमा हैं। करोड़ों मुखों से भी उनकी शोभा नहीं कही जा सकती ॥
english_translation: Knowing her as the Mother of the universe and the wife of Shiva, the devas bowed to her inwardly. Bhavani is the limit of beauty; even millions of mouths cannot describe her radiance.
essence: True greatness makes even praise fall silent.
simple_meaning: The devas silently honor Parvati as the Mother of the universe and praise her beauty as beyond description.
insight: It shifts attention from spoken praise to inward reverence when words cannot match what is seen.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm, dignity, and warmth make the whole room soften. Nobody says it out loud, but everyone feels they are in the presence of something rare.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोटिहुँ बदन नहिं बनै बरनत जग जननि सोभा महा। सकुचहिं कहत श्रुति सेष सारद मंदमति तुलसीकहा॥ छबिखानि मातु भवानि गवनीं मध्य मंडप सिव जहाँ। अवलोकि सकहिं न सकुच पति पद कमल मनु मधुकरु तहाँ॥
translation: जगज्जननी पार्वतीजी की महान शोभा का वर्णन करोड़ों मुखों से भी करते नहीं बनता। वेद, शेषजी और सरस्वतीजी तक उसे कहते हुए सकुचा जाते हैं, तब मंदबुद्धि तुलसी किस गिनती में है? सुंदरता और शोभा की खान माता भवानी मंडप के बीच में, जहाँ शिवजी थे, वहाँ गईं। वे संकोच के मारे पति (शिवजी) के चरणकमलों को देख नहीं सकतीं, परन्तु उनका मन रूपी भौंरा तो वहीं (रसपान कर रहा) था।
english_translation: Millions of mouths cannot describe the great splendor of the mother of the world. Even the Vedas, Shesha, and Saraswati hesitate to speak of it; then what count has Tulsidas, with his dull mind? The fountain of beauty, Mother Bhavani, went into the center of the pavilion where Shiva stood. She could not bring herself to look at her husband's lotus feet, yet her mind, like a bee, remained there drinking the nectar.
essence: True reverence can be too deep for words and too shy for direct gaze.
simple_meaning: Parvati's beauty is beyond description, and even sacred authorities hesitate to speak of it. She enters the pavilion where Shiva sits, and although she cannot openly look at his feet, her mind remains drawn to them.
insight: It shifts attention from outward composure to inward devotion and restraint.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and cannot meet someone's eyes, yet your whole attention is already with them. The body hesitates; the heart has arrived.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मुनि अनुसासन गनपतिहि पूजेउ संभु भवानि। कोउ सुनि संसय करै जनि सुर अनादि जियँ जानि ॥
translation: मुनियों की आज्ञा से शिवजी और पार्वतीजी ने गणेशजी का पूजन किया। मन में देवताओं को अनादि समझकर कोई इस बात को सुनकर शंका न करे (कि गणेशजी तो शिव-पार्वती की संतान हैं, अभी विवाह से पूर्व ही वे कहाँ से आ गए?) ॥
english_translation: By the sages' instruction, Shiva and Parvati worshipped Ganapati. Knowing the gods are beginningless, no one should doubt this on hearing it.
essence: Beginningless beings do not fit ordinary chronology.
simple_meaning: Shiva and Parvati first worship Ganesh as the sages direct. The poet adds that no one should be troubled by doubt, because the divine beings are beyond ordinary time.
insight: It shifts the mind from literal suspicion to reverent understanding of sacred time.
modern_relevance: You hear a story that seems to break the timeline, and your first instinct is to argue. The verse asks you to stop and trust the larger sacred frame before forcing it into neat logic.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जसि बिबाह कै बिधि श्रुति गाई। महामुनिन्ह सो सब करवाई॥ गहि गिरीस कुस कन्या पानी। भवहि समरपीं जानि भवानी ॥
translation: वेदों में विवाह की जैसी रीति कही गई है, महामुनियों ने वह सभी रीति करवाई। पर्वतराज हिमाचल ने हाथ में कुश लेकर तथा कन्या का हाथ पकड़कर उन्हें भवानी (शिवपत्नी) जानकर शिवजी को समर्पण किया ॥
english_translation: The Vedas describe the rite of marriage, and the great sages carried it out in full. Himachal took sacred grass in hand, joined the bride's hand, and offered Bhavani to Shiva, knowing her as the divine consort.
essence: Marriage becomes complete when it is offered through sacred rite.
simple_meaning: The marriage is performed according to sacred custom, and Himachal formally gives Parvati's hand to Shiva.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the sacred order that frames it.
modern_relevance: A family gathers for a wedding and every small ritual matters more than it seems. The ceremony is not decoration; it is the shape that gives the union dignity and meaning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पानिग्रहन जब कीन्ह महेसा। हियँ हरषे तब सकल सुरेसा॥ बेदमन्त्र मुनिबर उच्चरहीं। जय जय जय संकर सुर करहीं ॥
translation: जब महेश्वर (शिवजी) ने पार्वती का पाणिग्रहण किया, तब (इन्द्रादि) सब देवता हृदय में बड़े ही हर्षित हुए। श्रेष्ठ मुनिगण वेदमंत्रों का उच्चारण करने लगे और देवगण शिवजी का जय-जयकार करने लगे ॥
english_translation: When Mahesha took Parvati's hand in marriage, all the lords of the devas rejoiced in their hearts. The best sages recited Vedic मंत्रas, and the devas cried victory to Shankara.
essence: A rightful union makes the whole world rejoice.
simple_meaning: Shiva and Parvati's marriage filled the heavenly beings with joy. The sages chanted sacred words, and the divine hosts celebrated Shiva.
insight: It shifts attention from private ceremony to shared cosmic celebration.
modern_relevance: A wedding crowd goes quiet for a second, then breaks into smiles and applause as the couple takes the final vow. Everyone feels it: something fitting has just been made complete.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बाजहिं बाजन बिबिध बिधाना। सुमनबृष्टि नभ भै बिधि नाना॥ हर गिरिजा कर भयउ बिबाहू। सकल भुवन भरि रहा उछाहू ॥
translation: अनेकों प्रकार के बाजे बजने लगे। आकाश से नाना प्रकार के फूलों की वर्षा हुई। शिव-पार्वती का विवाह हो गया। सारे ब्राह्माण्ड में आनंद भर गया ॥
english_translation: Many kinds of instruments began to play. Flowers rained down from the sky in many forms. Shiva and Girija were married. Joy filled all the worlds.
essence: Their union turns one marriage into a joy shared by all worlds.
simple_meaning: The wedding of Shiva and Parvati is celebrated with music, flowers, and joy spreading through every world.
insight: It shifts attention from private celebration to a moment that restores harmony everywhere.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall goes quiet for a second, then erupts in cheers as the couple walks in. The happiness is bigger than the room — everyone feels carried by it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दासीं दास तुरग रथ नागा। धेनु बसन मनि बस्तु बिभागा॥ अन्न कनकभाजन भरि जाना। दाइज दीन्ह न जाइ बखाना ॥
translation: दासी, दास, रथ, घोड़े, हाथी, गायें, वस्त्र और मणि आदि अनेक प्रकार की चीजें, अन्न तथा सोने के बर्तन गाड़ियों में लदवाकर दहेज में दिए, जिनका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता ॥
english_translation: Servants, male servants, horses, chariots, elephants, cows, clothes, jewels, goods, food, and gold vessels were all given as dowry, beyond description.
essence: Love can overflow into gifts too many to count.
simple_meaning: Himachal gave a vast dowry for the wedding, loading carts with servants, animals, clothes, jewels, food, and gold vessels. The gifts were so many they could not be fully described.
insight: It shifts attention from the items themselves to the abundance and honor behind them.
modern_relevance: A wedding warehouse is packed with boxes, furniture, and gifts from both families, and no one can keep track anymore. The scene is about overflow, not calculation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दाइज दियो बहु भाँति पुनि कर जोरि हिमभूधर कह्यो। का देउँ पूरनकाम संकर चरन पंकज गहि रह्यो॥ सिवँ कृपासागर ससुर कर संतोषु सब भाँतिहिं कियो। पुनि गहे पद पाथोज मयनाँ प्रेम परिपूरन हियो॥
translation: बहुत प्रकार का दहेज देकर, फिर हाथ जोड़कर हिमाचल ने कहा- हे शंकर! आप पूर्णकाम हैं, मैं आपको क्या दे सकता हूँ? (इतना कहकर) वे शिवजी के चरणकमल पकड़कर रह गए। तब कृपा के सागर शिवजी ने अपने ससुर का सभी प्रकार से समाधान किया। फिर प्रेम से परिपूर्ण हृदय मैनाजी ने शिवजी के चरण कमल पकड़े (और कहा-)।
english_translation: Having given many gifts, Himachal folded his hands and said, “What can I give you, O Shankar, who are already complete?” Then he held Shiva’s lotus feet. The ocean of grace Shiva satisfied his father-in-law in every way. Then Parvati, her heart full of love, held Shiva’s lotus feet.
essence: Completeness receives nothing and still gives everything.
simple_meaning: Himalaya gives gifts to Shiva but says Shiva needs nothing. Shiva responds with grace, and Maina then bows to his feet in love.
insight: It shifts attention from giving things to offering reverence, gratitude, and surrender.
modern_relevance: At a wedding where the gifts are extravagant, the real moment is the bowed head, the softened pride, the heart that knows it cannot repay love. Some bonds are answered by humility, not by exchange.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ उमा मम प्रान सम गृहकिंकरी करेहु। छमेहु सकल अपराध अब होइ प्रसन्न बरु देहु ॥
translation: हे नाथ! यह उमा मुझे मेरे प्राणों के समान (प्यारी) है। आप इसे अपने घर की टहलनी बनाइएगा और इसके सब अपराधों को क्षमा करते रहिएगा। अब प्रसन्न होकर मुझे यही वर दीजिए ॥
english_translation: O Lord, Uma is dear to me as my own life. Please make her a servant in your household, forgive all her faults, and now be pleased to grant this boon.
essence: True affection asks for mercy, not status.
simple_meaning: Himalaya asks Shiva to accept Uma as part of his household, forgive her mistakes, and bless her with kindness.
insight: It teaches you to ask for acceptance with humility, not entitlement.
modern_relevance: You introduce your daughter to someone you deeply respect and quietly ask for kindness toward her imperfections. That mix of pride, love, and humility is all in this line.
speaker: Himalaya

verse_text: बहु बिधि संभु सासु समुझाई। गवनी भवन चरन सिरु नाई॥ जननीं उमा बोलि तब लीन्ही। लै उछंग सुंदर सिख दीन्ही ॥
translation: शिवजी ने बहुत तरह से अपनी सास को समझाया। तब वे शिवजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर घर गईं। फिर माता ने पार्वती को बुला लिया और गोद में बिठाकर यह सुंदर सीख दी- ॥
english_translation: Shiva explained in many ways to his mother-in-law. Then she bowed her head at Shiva's feet and returned home. After that, the mother called Parvati and, seating her in her lap, gave her this beautiful instruction.
essence: A private lesson follows the public bow.
simple_meaning: Shiva persuades Parvati's mother-in-law, who then goes home. Parvati's mother calls her aside and prepares to give her an important lesson.
insight: It shifts attention from the public moment to the intimate instruction that follows.
modern_relevance: A mother pulls her daughter aside after a family gathering and says, quietly, what really matters. The advice lands because it comes from love, not performance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करेहु सदा संकर पद पूजा। नारिधरमु पति देउ न दूजा॥ बचन कहत भरे लोचन बारी। बहुरि लाइ उर लीन्हि कुमारी ॥
translation: हे पार्वती! तू सदाशिवजी के चरणों की पूजा करना, नारियों का यही धर्म है। उनके लिए पति ही देवता है और कोई देवता नहीं है। इस प्रकार की बातें कहते-कहते उनकी आँखों में आँसू भर आए और उन्होंने कन्या को छाती से चिपटा लिया ॥
english_translation: O Parvati, always worship the feet of Shankar. For women, the husband is the only deity, and no other. Saying these words, her eyes filled with tears, and she drew the girl close to her chest.
essence: A mother's blessing carries both duty and tears.
simple_meaning: Parvati is told to worship Shiva and to regard her husband as her highest devotion. The mother speaks with tears and holds her daughter close.
insight: It links family guidance with social duty, showing how a private blessing becomes a rule for conduct.
modern_relevance: A mother adjusts her daughter's dupatta before a wedding and gives one last serious warning about marriage. The advice may sound old-fashioned, but the emotion is familiar: protect, prepare, and let go.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: कत बिधि सृजीं नारि जग माहीं। पराधीन सपनेहूँ सुखु नाहीं॥ भै अति प्रेम बिकल महतारी। धीरजु कीन्ह कुसमय बिचारी ॥
translation: (फिर बोलीं कि) विधाता ने जगत में स्त्री जाति को क्यों पैदा किया? पराधीन को सपने में भी सुख नहीं मिलता। यों कहती हुई माता प्रेम में अत्यन्त विकल हो गईं, परन्तु कुसमय जानकर (दुःख करने का अवसर न जानकर) उन्होंने धीरज धरा ॥
english_translation: Why was woman created in this world? Even in dreams, one who is dependent finds no happiness. Speaking this way, the mother was overwhelmed with love, but seeing the untimely moment, she steadied herself.
essence: Love may overwhelm, but restraint keeps it from breaking the moment.
simple_meaning: Maina, overwhelmed by love for Parvati, asks why dependence brings no happiness and then restrains herself, seeing that this is not the right moment for grief.
insight: It shows the difference between emotional surge and wise self-control.
modern_relevance: You get a text that stings, and your first impulse is to pour everything out. Then you remember: not every feeling needs immediate release. Some moments ask for restraint.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि पुनि मिलति परति गहि चरना। परम प्रेमु कछु जाइ न बरना॥ सब नारिन्ह मिलि भेंटि भवानी। जाइ जननि उर पुनि लपटानी ॥
translation: मैना बार-बार मिलती हैं और (पार्वती के) चरणों को पकड़कर गिर पड़ती हैं। बड़ा ही प्रेम है, कुछ वर्णन नहीं किया जाता। भवानी सब स्त्रियों से मिल-भेंटकर फिर अपनी माता के हृदय से जा लिपटीं ॥
english_translation: Maina again and again met her, grasped her feet, and fell before her. Such immense love cannot be described. Bhavani met all the women, then went and clung again to her mother's heart.
essence: Love that deep needs no explanation.
simple_meaning: Maina repeatedly bows to Parvati with overwhelming love. Parvati greets the women, then returns to her mother's embrace.
insight: It shifts attention from explanation to embodied affection, showing that some feelings are expressed through repeated gestures, not arguments.
modern_relevance: You finally see your daughter after months away. You keep touching her shoulder, then stepping back, then hugging her again because the heart has more to say than speech can carry.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जननिहि बहुरि मिलि चली उचित असीस सब काहूँ दईं। फिरि फिरि बिलोकति मातु तन तब सखीं लै सिव पहिं गईं॥ जाचक सकल संतोषि संकरु उमा सहित भवन चले। सब अमर हरषे सुमन बरषि निसान नभ बाजे भले॥
translation: पार्वतीजी माता से फिर मिलकर चलीं, सब किसी ने उन्हें योग्य आशीर्वाद दिए। पार्वतीजी फिर-फिरकर माता की ओर देखती जाती थीं। तब सखियाँ उन्हें शिवजी के पास ले गईं। महादेवजी सब याचकों को संतुष्ट कर पार्वती के साथ घर (कैलास) को चले। सब देवता प्रसन्न होकर फूलों की वर्षा करने लगे और आकाश में सुंदर नगाड़े बजाने लगे।
english_translation: Parvati returned after meeting her mother; everyone gave her fitting blessings. She kept looking back at her mother again and again. Then her companions led her to Shiva. Mahadeva satisfied all the petitioners and left for Kailasa with Uma. All the radiant beings rejoiced, showered flowers, and the skies resounded with drums.
essence: A loving farewell can carry the whole family forward.
simple_meaning: Parvati leaves her mother after receiving blessings, keeps looking back, and then goes to Shiva. Shiva returns to Kailasa with her, while the heavenly beings rejoice and shower flowers.
insight: It turns a departure into a blessed transition, not a loss.
modern_relevance: You leave your childhood home after a wedding or a move, then keep looking back through the car window. The goodbye is real, but so is the blessing that carries you forward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चले संग हिमवंतु तब पहुँचावन अति हेतु। बिबिध भाँति परितोषु करि बिदा कीन्ह बृषकेतु ॥
translation: तब हिमवान् अत्यन्त प्रेम से शिवजी को पहुँचाने के लिए साथ चले। वृषकेतु (शिवजी) ने बहुत तरह से उन्हें संतोष कराकर विदा किया ॥
english_translation: Then Himavan, with great affection, accompanied Shiva to see him off. Bṛṣaketu soothed him in many ways and bade him farewell.
essence: True affection can make parting feel complete and peaceful.
simple_meaning: Himavan lovingly goes with Shiva to see him off, and Shiva sends him back after comforting him in many ways.
insight: It shows how affection can honor departure without clinging to it.
modern_relevance: You walk a friend to the cab at midnight, still talking because neither of you wants the moment to end. Some goodbyes become tender because both people know the bond is secure.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तुरत भवन आए गिरिराई। सकल सैल सर लिए बोलाई॥ आदर दान बिनय बहुमाना। सब कर बिदा कीन्ह हिमवाना ॥
translation: पर्वतराज हिमाचल तुरंत घर आए और उन्होंने सब पर्वतों और सरोवरों को बुलाया। हिमवान ने आदर, दान, विनय और बहुत सम्मानपूर्वक सबकी विदाई की ॥
english_translation: Himalaya returned home at once. He summoned all the mountains and lakes. With honor, gifts, humility, and great respect, Himalaya bade them farewell.
essence: True grandeur includes knowing how to let everyone go well.
simple_meaning: Himalaya returns home, gathers the mountains and lakes, and sends everyone away with honor and generosity.
insight: It shifts attention from holding on to an event to completing it with dignity.
modern_relevance: The guests have left after a wedding, and the house still smells of flowers and food. You thank everyone, pack the gifts, and close the door with grace instead of emptiness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जबहिं संभु कैलासहिं आए। सुर सब निज निज लोक सिधाए॥ जगत मातु पितु संभु भवानी। तेहिं सिंगारु न कहउँ बखानी ॥
translation: जब शिवजी कैलास पर्वत पर पहुँचे, तब सब देवता अपने-अपने लोकों को चले गए। (तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि) पार्वतीजी और शिवजी जगत के माता-पिता हैं, इसलिए मैं उनके श्रृंगार का वर्णन नहीं करता ॥
english_translation: When Shiva reached Kailash, all the devas returned to their own realms. The world’s mother and father are Shiva and Parvati, so I do not describe their adornment.
essence: Some presence is too vast for description; reverence begins where speech ends.
simple_meaning: Shiva returns to Kailash, the other beings leave, and Tulsidas pauses to say he will not try to describe Shiva and Parvati’s beauty.
insight: It shifts the reader from trying to capture everything with words to recognising when reverence is better than explanation.
modern_relevance: You enter a temple after the crowd has thinned and the air still feels charged. Some moments do not need commentary; they ask for reverent attention instead.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करहिं बिबिध बिधि भोग बिलासा। गनन्ह समेत बसहिं कैलासा॥ हर गिरिजा बिहार नित नयऊ। एहि बिधि बिपुल काल चलि गयऊ ॥
translation: शिव-पार्वती विविध प्रकार के भोग-विलास करते हुए अपने गणों सहित कैलास पर रहने लगे। वे नित्य नए विहार करते थे। इस प्रकार बहुत समय बीत गया ॥
english_translation: Shiva and Parvati enjoyed many kinds of pleasures and lived with their attendants on Kailash. They spent each day in fresh delight. In this way, a great deal of time passed.
essence: Joy shared in the right company makes time pass unnoticed.
simple_meaning: Shiva and Parvati live on Kailash with their attendants, enjoying fresh pastimes each day. Time passes quietly in their company.
insight: It turns attention from dramatic action to the quiet fullness of sacred companionship.
modern_relevance: A long evening with people you love can feel like no time has passed. The clock moves, but shared joy makes the hours light.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जब जनमेउ षटबदन कुमारा। तारकु असुरु समर जेहिं मारा॥ आगम निगम प्रसिद्ध पुराना। षन्मुख जन्मु सकल जग जाना ॥
translation: तब छ: मुखवाले पुत्र (स्वामिकार्तिक) का जन्म हुआ, जिन्होंने (बड़े होने पर) युद्ध में तारकासुर को मारा। वेद, शास्त्र और पुराणों में स्वामिकार्तिक के जन्म की कथा प्रसिद्ध है और सारा जगत उसे जानता है ॥
english_translation: Then the six-faced son was born, who later slew the demon Taraka in battle. His birth is famed in the Vedas, scriptures, and Puranas, and the whole world knows of the six-faced one.
essence: A famous birth is introduced before its full story unfolds.
simple_meaning: Kartikeya is born, and his later victory over Taraka is already part of his fame. The verse simply marks his celebrated arrival.
insight: It frames a celebrated figure through public memory, not personal instruction.
modern_relevance: A family announcement goes out and everyone already knows the name before the child has even grown. The moment is about fame and recognition, not a lesson you can apply directly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जगु जान षन्मुख जन्मु कर्मु प्रतापु पुरुषारथु महा। तेहि हेतु मैं बृषकेतु सुत कर चरित संछेपहिं कहा॥ यह उमा संभु बिबाहु जे नर नारि कहहिं जे गावहीं। कल्यान काज बिबाह मंगल सर्बदा सुखु पावहीं॥
translation: षडानन (स्वामिकार्तिक) के जन्म, कर्म, प्रताप और महान पुरुषार्थ को सारा जगत जानता है, इसलिए मैंने वृषकेतु (शिवजी) के पुत्र का चरित्र संक्षेप में ही कहा है। शिव-पार्वती के विवाह की इस कथा को जो स्त्री-पुरुष कहेंगे और गाएँगे, वे कल्याण के कार्यों और विवाहादि मंगलों में सदा सुख पाएँगे।
english_translation: The world knows the birth, deeds, glory, and great effort of Shanmukha, so I have told the story of Shiva's son only in brief. Whoever men and women speak or sing of the marriage of Uma and Shambhu will find lasting joy in auspicious works and wedding rites.
essence: Holy stories bless the lives that keep repeating them.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he has only briefly told Shanmukha's story, because the world already knows it. He adds that singing or speaking of Shiva and Uma's marriage brings lasting joy and blessings to good works and weddings.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the power of spoken remembrance in making the event sacred.
modern_relevance: At a wedding where relatives keep reciting the couple's story and blessings, the room changes. The words are not decoration; they shape the mood, calm the mind, and make the celebration feel held by something larger.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: चरित सिंधु गिरिजा रमन बेद न पावहिं पारु। बरनै तुलसीदासु किमि अति मतिमंद गवाँरु ॥
translation: गिरिजापति महादेवजी का चरित्र समुद्र के समान (अपार) है, उसका पार वेद भी नहीं पाते। तब अत्यन्त मन्दबुद्धि और गँवार तुलसीदास उसका वर्णन कैसे कर सकता है? ॥
english_translation: Shiva's story is an ocean; even the Vedas cannot reach its far shore. How can dull-minded Tulsidas describe it?
essence: True devotion begins where description fails.
simple_meaning: Shiva's character is so vast that even the Vedas cannot fully describe it, and Tulsidas humbly says he cannot do it justice.
insight: It shifts the mind from performance to reverence, teaching that some realities are best approached with humility.
modern_relevance: You try to explain someone you deeply admire, and every sentence feels too small. The more you love what you are describing, the more honest it becomes to admit its depth.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: संभु चरित सुनि सरस सुहावा। भरद्वाज मुनि अति सुखु पावा॥ बहु लालसा कथा पर बाढ़ी। नयनन्हि नीरु रोमावलि ठाढ़ी ॥
translation: शिवजी के रसीले और सुहावने चरित्र को सुनकर मुनि भरद्वाजजी ने बहुत ही सुख पाया। कथा सुनने की उनकी लालसा बहुत बढ़ गई। नेत्रों में जल भर आया तथा रोमावली खड़ी हो गई ॥
english_translation: Hearing Shiva's charming, delightful story, sage Bharadvaja felt great joy. His longing to hear more grew strong. Tears filled his eyes, and the hair on his body stood on end.
essence: Love for the divine makes the body answer before words do.
simple_meaning: Bharadvaja feels deep joy listening to Shiva's story. His longing grows, and his body shows signs of devotion: tears and goosebumps.
insight: It shifts attention from understanding devotion intellectually to recognising devotion as a full-bodied response of love and longing.
modern_relevance: You hear a song from childhood in a crowded train, and suddenly your eyes sting. Some truths are felt before they are explained — and the body knows first.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रेम बिबस मुख आव न बानी। दसा देखि हरषे मुनि ग्यानी॥ अहो धन्य तब जन्मु मुनीसा। तुम्हहि प्रान सम प्रिय गौरीसा ॥
translation: वे प्रेम में मुग्ध हो गए, मुख से वाणी नहीं निकलती। उनकी यह दशा देखकर ज्ञानी मुनि याज्ञवल्क्य बहुत प्रसन्न हुए (और बोले-) हे मुनीश! अहा हा! तुम्हारा जन्म धन्य है, तुमको गौरीपति शिवजी प्राणों के समान प्रिय हैं ॥
english_translation: Overwhelmed by love, he could not speak. Seeing his state, the wise sage Yajnavalkya rejoiced. "Ah, blessed is your birth, O great sage. Shiva is dear to you as life itself."
essence: Real devotion can make speech unnecessary.
simple_meaning: Love leaves Bharadvaj speechless, and Yajnavalkya blesses him for loving Shiva as dearly as life itself.
insight: It shifts the reader from speaking about devotion to recognising devotion as a living state.
modern_relevance: You sit quietly after hearing a song, a prayer, or a story that hits something deep. You do not need a commentary. The silence itself proves the heart has been touched.
speaker: Yajnavalkya

verse_text: सिव पद कमल जिन्हहि रति नाहीं। रामहि ते सपनेहुँ न सोहाहीं॥ बिनु छल बिस्वनाथ पद नेहू। राम भगत कर लच्छन एहू ॥
translation: शिवजी के चरण कमलों में जिनकी प्रीति नहीं है, वे श्री रामचन्द्रजी को स्वप्न में भी अच्छे नहीं लगते। विश्वनाथ श्री शिवजी के चरणों में निष्कपट (विशुद्ध) प्रेम होना यही रामभक्त का लक्षण है ॥
english_translation: Those who have no love for Shiva's lotus feet are not pleasing to Ram even in a dream. Pure love for Shiva's feet is the mark of Ram's devotee.
essence: Pure love for Shiva is one sign of a heart devoted to Ram.
simple_meaning: A true devotee of Ram has sincere love for Shiva as well. Without that pure devotion to Shiva, Ram does not fully accept a person.
insight: It shifts devotion from personal preference to a wider, cleaner loyalty that honors both Ram and Shiva.
modern_relevance: You admire one teacher online, but mock the other tradition that shaped them. The verse cuts through that split: real devotion is not selective respect; it is clean, consistent reverence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिव सम को रघुपति ब्रतधारी। बिनु अघ तजी सती असि नारी॥ पनु करि रघुपति भगति देखाई। को सिव सम रामहि प्रिय भाई ॥
translation: शिवजी के समान रघुनाथजी (की भक्ति) का व्रत धारण करने वाला कौन है? जिन्होंने बिना ही पाप के सती जैसी स्त्री को त्याग दिया और प्रतिज्ञा करके श्री रघुनाथजी की भक्ति को दिखा दिया। हे भाई! श्री रामचन्द्रजी को शिवजी के समान और कौन प्यारा है? ॥
english_translation: Who keeps the vow of Raghupati like Shiva does? Who, without any fault, abandoned Sati in that way and proved devotion to Raghupati by his vow? Brother, who is as dear to Ram as Shiva?
essence: Shiva’s vow-bound devotion makes him uniquely dear to Ram.
simple_meaning: Shiva is held up as the greatest devotee of Ram. His vow and devotion make him uniquely dear to Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from public devotion to steadfast loyalty that proves itself through action.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone even when no one notices, and even when it costs you status. That quiet loyalty is what makes a bond unbreakable.
speaker: Yajnavalkya

verse_text: प्रथमहिं मैं कहि सिव चरित बूझा मरमु तुम्हार। सुचि सेवक तुम्ह राम के रहित समस्त बिकार ॥
translation: मैंने पहले ही शिवजी का चरित्र कहकर तुम्हारा भेद समझ लिया। तुम श्री रामचन्द्रजी के पवित्र सेवक हो और समस्त दोषों से रहित हो ॥
english_translation: I have already told Shiva's story and understood your inner nature. You are a pure servant of Ram, free from all faults.
essence: Pure service to Ram leaves no room for corruption.
simple_meaning: Shiva says he already understands the listener's nature: the listener is a pure servant of Ram, free from faults.
insight: It shifts attention from status to devotion: what you serve reveals who you are.
modern_relevance: A mentor sees through your polished words and names the real thing: your character shows in what you serve. Quiet loyalty leaves a clearer mark than self-promotion ever can.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: मैं जाना तुम्हार गुन सीला। कहउँ सुनहु अब रघुपति लीला॥ सुनु मुनि आजु समागम तोरें। कहि न जाइ जस सुखु मन मोरें ॥
translation: मैंने तुम्हारा गुण और शील जान लिया। अब मैं श्री रघुनाथजी की लीला कहता हूँ, सुनो। हे मुनि! सुनो, आज तुम्हारे मिलने से मेरे मन में जो आनंद हुआ है, वह कहा नहीं जा सकता ॥
english_translation: I have understood your virtues and character. Now I will tell the play of Raghupati; listen. O sage, the joy in my mind from meeting you today cannot be spoken.
essence: True meeting creates joy before any words are spoken.
simple_meaning: The speaker recognizes the sage's character and then turns to Ram's story, saying the joy of this meeting is beyond words.
insight: It teaches you to begin sacred or important speech by acknowledging the quality of the relationship first.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence immediately feels clean and steady. Before the agenda begins, you just want to say: being with you has already changed the room.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: राम चरित अति अमित मुनीसा। कहि न सकहिं सत कोटि अहीसा॥ तदपि जथाश्रुत कहउँ बखानी। सुमिरि गिरापति प्रभु धनुपानी ॥
translation: हे मुनीश्वर! रामचरित्र अत्यन्त अपार है। सौ करोड़ शेषजी भी उसे नहीं कह सकते। तथापि जैसा मैंने सुना है, वैसा वाणी के स्वामी (प्रेरक) और हाथ में धनुष लिए हुए प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी का स्मरण करके कहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: O sage, Ram’s story is immeasurable. Even a hundred million Sheshas cannot tell it fully. Still, I speak as I have heard it, remembering the Lord of speech and the Lord who holds the bow.
essence: Ram’s story can be spoken only through humble remembrance.
simple_meaning: Ram’s story is so vast that no one can fully describe it. The speaker can only tell it as he has heard it, with reverence and memory of Ram.
insight: It shifts the reader from trying to master sacred meaning to approaching it with humility and remembrance.
modern_relevance: You try to explain a moment that changed your life, but the words keep falling short. That failure is not weakness. Some things deserve reverent telling, not tidy explanation.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सारद दारुनारि सम स्वामी। रामु सूत्रधर अंतरजामी॥ जेहि पर कृपा करहिं जनु जानी। कबि उर अजिर नचावहिं बानी ॥
translation: सरस्वतीजी कठपुतली के समान हैं और अन्तर्यामी स्वामी श्री रामचन्द्रजी (सूत पकड़कर कठपुतली को नचाने वाले) सूत्रधार हैं। अपना भक्त जानकर जिस कवि पर वे कृपा करते हैं, उसके हृदय रूपी आँगन में सरस्वती को वे नचाया करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Saraswati is like a puppet; Ram is the inner controller who holds the strings. When he shows grace to a poet as his own, he makes her words dance in the poet's heart-courtyard.
essence: Grace makes words move where willpower cannot.
simple_meaning: Ram is the inner controller of speech and inspiration. A poet can speak beautifully only when Ram's grace makes words arise within the heart.
insight: It shifts authorship from personal control to received grace, so speech becomes an offering rather than a performance.
modern_relevance: You sit staring at a blank page, waiting for the right sentence to arrive. Then, suddenly, it does. This verse reminds you that the best words often come when ego stops gripping the wheel.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: प्रनवउँ सोइ कृपाल रघुनाथा। बरनउँ बिसद तासु गुन गाथा॥ परम रम्य गिरिबरु कैलासू। सदा जहाँ सिव उमा निवासू ॥
translation: उन्हीं कृपालु श्री रघुनाथजी को मैं प्रणाम करता हूँ और उन्हीं के निर्मल गुणों की कथा कहता हूँ। कैलास पर्वतों में श्रेष्ठ और बहुत ही रमणीय है, जहाँ शिव-पार्वतीजी सदा निवास करते हैं ॥
english_translation: I bow to that compassionate Lord of the Raghu line and sing the spotless story of His virtues. Mount Kailash is the most beautiful of mountains, where Shiva and Uma always dwell.
essence: Reverence comes first; only then can the story of Ram be told.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas bows to Ram and begins praising His pure qualities. He then describes Kailash as the beautiful home of Shiva and Uma.
insight: It teaches you to begin with humility and devotion, not self-importance.
modern_relevance: Before speaking about something sacred or important, you pause, bow inwardly, and choose reverence over haste. That changes the whole tone of what follows.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सिद्ध तपोधन जोगिजन सुर किंनर मुनिबृंद। बसहिं तहाँ सुकृती सकल सेवहिं सिव सुखकंद ॥
translation: सिद्ध, तपस्वी, योगीगण, देवता, किन्नर और मुनियों के समूह उस पर्वत पर रहते हैं। वे सब बड़े पुण्यात्मा हैं और आनंदकन्द श्री महादेवजी की सेवा करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Siddhas, ascetics, yogis, devas, kinnaras, and hosts of sages dwell there. All of them are virtuous and serve Shiva, the source of joy.
essence: Holy places are recognized by the devotion they attract.
simple_meaning: That holy mountain is home to many exalted beings, and they all serve Shiva there.
insight: It shifts attention from the place alone to the character of those who are drawn to it.
modern_relevance: A quiet place filled with sincere people feels different the moment you enter. The room itself is not the miracle; the devotion, discipline, and humility of the people there make it feel alive.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: हरि हर बिमुख धर्म रति नाहीं। ते नर तहँ सपनेहुँ नहिं जाहीं॥ तेहि गिरि पर बट बिटप बिसाला। नित नूतन सुंदर सब काला ॥
translation: जो भगवान विष्णु और महादेवजी से विमुख हैं और जिनकी धर्म में प्रीति नहीं है, वे लोग स्वप्न में भी वहाँ नहीं जा सकते। उस पर्वत पर एक विशाल बरगद का पेड़ है, जो नित्य नवीन और सब काल (छहों ऋतुओं) में सुंदर रहता है ॥
english_translation: Those who turn away from Hari and Shiva and feel no love for dharma cannot even reach that mountain in a dream. On that mountain stands a vast banyan tree, ever fresh and beautiful in every season.
essence: Only a dharmic heart can enter the sacred place.
simple_meaning: Only those who love the divine and live by dharma can reach that sacred mountain. A huge banyan tree there stays fresh and beautiful in every season.
insight: It shifts attention from physical access to inner fit: reverence and dharma make a person belong where they stand.
modern_relevance: You can walk into a temple, a retreat, or a quiet room and still remain elsewhere inside. The verse says some places are reached by the heart long before the feet arrive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: त्रिबिध समीर सुसीतलि छाया। सिव बिश्राम बिटप श्रुति गाया॥ एक बार तेहि तर प्रभु गयऊ। तरु बिलोकि उर अति सुखु भयऊ ॥
translation: वहाँ तीनों प्रकार की (शीतल, मंद और सुगंध) वायु बहती रहती है और उसकी छाया बड़ी ठंडी रहती है। वह शिवजी के विश्राम करने का वृक्ष है, जिसे वेदों ने गाया है। एक बार प्रभु श्री शिवजी उस वृक्ष के नीचे गए और उसे देखकर उनके हृदय में बहुत आनंद हुआ ॥
english_translation: Three kinds of cool, gentle, fragrant winds blow there, and its shade is very soothing. The Vedas sing of it as Shiva's resting tree. Once, the Lord went beneath it and felt great joy at the sight of the tree.
essence: Even Shiva delights in a place that naturally brings rest.
simple_meaning: The tree’s shade and breeze are so soothing that even Shiva rests there, and he feels joy just seeing it.
insight: It shifts attention from dramatic events to the power of a pure, calming environment.
modern_relevance: You step into a quiet courtyard after a noisy commute, and your whole body loosens before anyone speaks. Some places restore you before they explain anything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निज कर डासि नागरिपु छाला। बैठे सहजहिं संभु कृपाला॥ कुंद इंदु दर गौर सरीरा। भुज प्रलंब परिधन मुनिचीरा ॥
translation: अपने हाथ से बाघम्बर बिछाकर कृपालु शिवजी स्वभाव से ही (बिना किसी खास प्रयोजन के) वहाँ बैठ गए। कुंद के पुष्प, चन्द्रमा और शंख के समान उनका गौर शरीर था। बड़ी लंबी भुजाएँ थीं और वे मुनियों के से (वल्कल) वस्त्र धारण किए हुए थे ॥
english_translation: Having spread the tiger-skin with his own hands, compassionate Shiva sat there naturally. His fair body shone like a jasmine flower, the moon, and a conch. His arms were long, and he wore the bark cloth of a sage.
essence: Majesty can appear as complete simplicity.
simple_meaning: Shiva sits calmly on a tiger skin, with a bright fair body, long arms, and simple sage clothing.
insight: It shifts attention from status to composure, showing that dignity can be simple and unforced.
modern_relevance: A person walks into a room wearing no badge of importance, yet everyone feels the steadiness. No performance, no self-importance — just quiet presence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तरुन अरुन अंबुज सम चरना। नख दुति भगत हृदय तम हरना॥ भुजग भूति भूषन त्रिपुरारी। आननु सरद चंद छबि हारी ॥
translation: उनके चरण नए (पूर्ण रूप से खिले हुए) लाल कमल के समान थे, नखों की ज्योति भक्तों के हृदय का अंधकार हरने वाली थी। साँप और भस्म ही उनके भूषण थे और उन त्रिपुरासुर के शत्रु शिवजी का मुख शरद (पूर्णिमा) के चन्द्रमा की शोभा को भी हरने वाला (फीकी करने वाला) था ॥
english_translation: His feet were like fresh red lotuses, and the shine of his nails removed the darkness from devotees' hearts. Serpents and ash were his ornaments, and the face of Tripurari outshone even the beauty of the autumn moon.
essence: Shiva's beauty is measured by how it clears devotion's darkness.
simple_meaning: Shiva is described as radiantly beautiful: his feet are like red lotuses, his nails dispel devotees' inner darkness, and his face surpasses the autumn moon.
insight: It shifts attention from outward ornament to a presence that transforms the heart.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm changes the whole room. Nothing flashy about them — yet their presence makes your own mind feel less crowded.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जटा मुकुट सुरसरित सिर लोचन नलिन बिसाल। नीलकंठ लावन्यनिधि सोह बालबिधु भाल ॥
translation: उनके सिर पर जटाओं का मुकुट और गंगाजी (शोभायमान) थीं। कमल के समान बड़े-बड़े नेत्र थे। उनका नील कंठ था और वे सुंदरता के भंडार थे। उनके मस्तक पर द्वितीया का चन्द्रमा शोभित था ॥
english_translation: His head bore a matted-crown, the Ganga rested there, and his eyes were vast lotuses. Blue-throated, a treasure of beauty, he shone with the crescent moon on his brow.
essence: Beauty and stillness meet in Shiva's form.
simple_meaning: Shiva is described as radiant and beautiful, with matted hair, the Ganga on his head, lotus-like eyes, a blue throat, and the crescent moon on his forehead.
insight: It shifts attention from Shiva's role in the story to his presence as a living image of calm, grace, and majesty.
modern_relevance: You enter a quiet temple after a long, noisy day and suddenly notice stillness has a face. Beauty feels less like decoration and more like peace made visible.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बैठे सोह कामरिपु कैसें। धरें सरीरु सांतरसु जैसें॥ पारबती भल अवसरु जानी। गईं संभु पहिं मातु भवानी ॥
translation: कामदेव के शत्रु शिवजी वहाँ बैठे हुए ऐसे शोभित हो रहे थे, मानो शांतरस ही शरीर धारण किए बैठा हो। अच्छा मौका जानकर शिवपत्नी माता पार्वतीजी उनके पास गईं।
english_translation: Shiva, enemy of desire, sat there like peace itself taking form. Seeing the right moment, Parvati, Mother Bhavani, went to Shiva.
essence: Calm presence creates the opening for wisdom to begin.
simple_meaning: Shiva sat in perfect calm, and Parvati approached him at the right moment.
insight: It shifts attention from forcing speech to waiting for the right opening.
modern_relevance: You finally catch someone after their phone is off and the room is quiet. The hard conversation lands because the moment is open, not forced.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जानि प्रिया आदरु अति कीन्हा। बाम भाग आसनु हर दीन्हा॥ बैठीं सिव समीप हरषाई। पूरुब जन्म कथा चित आई ॥
translation: अपनी प्यारी पत्नी जानकार शिवजी ने उनका बहुत आदर-सत्कार किया और अपनी बायीं ओर बैठने के लिए आसन दिया। पार्वतीजी प्रसन्न होकर शिवजी के पास बैठ गईं। उन्हें पिछले जन्म की कथा स्मरण हो आई ॥
english_translation: Knowing her as his beloved, Shiva showed her great respect and gave her a seat on his left side. Parvati sat near Shiva, delighted, and the memory of her previous birth came to her mind.
essence: Respect creates the opening where remembrance returns.
simple_meaning: Shiva welcomes Parvati with great honor and gives her a seat beside him. As she sits happily near him, she remembers the story of her earlier birth.
insight: It shows how reverent welcome can open the mind to deeper remembrance and inquiry.
modern_relevance: Someone makes space for you in a crowded room without being asked. That small gesture softens you, and an old memory or feeling suddenly rises to the surface.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पति हियँ हेतु अधिक अनुमानी। बिहसि उमा बोलीं प्रिय बानी॥ कथा जो सकल लोक हितकारी। सोइ पूछन चह सैल कुमारी ॥
translation: स्वामी के हृदय में (अपने ऊपर पहले की अपेक्षा) अधिक प्रेम समझकर पार्वतीजी हँसकर प्रिय वचन बोलीं। (याज्ञवल्क्यजी कहते हैं कि) जो कथा सब लोगों का हित करने वाली है, उसे ही पार्वतीजी पूछना चाहती हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing that her husband held her in even greater affection, Uma smiled and spoke sweetly. "I wish to ask about the story that brings benefit to all beings, daughter of the mountain."
essence: A loving question can open the door to a teaching that benefits all.
simple_meaning: Parvati smiles and asks to hear the story that benefits everyone. Her question opens the deeper teaching that follows.
insight: It shifts attention from casual chatter to the question that can help everyone.
modern_relevance: At a family dinner, someone asks the one question that matters instead of filling the room with small talk. That single honest question changes the whole conversation.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: बिस्वनाथ मम नाथ पुरारी। त्रिभुवन महिमा बिदित तुम्हारी॥ चर अरु अचर नाग नर देवा। सकल करहिं पद पंकज सेवा ॥
translation: (पार्वतीजी ने कहा-) हे संसार के स्वामी! हे मेरे नाथ! हे त्रिपुरासुर का वध करने वाले! आपकी महिमा तीनों लोकों में विख्यात है। चर, अचर, नाग, मनुष्य और देवता सभी आपके चरण कमलों की सेवा करते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Lord of the universe, my Lord, destroyer of Tripura, your glory is known in all three worlds. Moving and unmoving beings, serpents, humans, and radiant beings all serve your lotus feet.
essence: True greatness draws every being into service.
simple_meaning: Parvati praises Shiva as the lord of all worlds and says every kind of being serves his feet.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to reverent recognition of what is greater.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who carries quiet authority, and the room changes without anyone speaking. Respect rises on its own because the person’s presence makes ego feel small.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: प्रभु समरथ सर्बग्य सिव सकल कला गुन धाम। जोग ग्यान बैराग्य निधि प्रनत कलपतरु नाम ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! आप समर्थ, सर्वज्ञ और कल्याणस्वरूप हैं। सब कलाओं और गुणों के निधान हैं और योग, ज्ञान तथा वैराग्य के भंडार हैं। आपका नाम शरणागतों के लिए कल्पवृक्ष है ॥
english_translation: O Lord, you are mighty, all-knowing, the source of every art and virtue. You are the treasury of yoga, wisdom, and detachment, and your name is a wish-fulfilling tree for those who seek refuge.
essence: Ram contains every virtue, and his name shelters the surrendered.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as all-powerful, all-knowing, and full of every virtue. His name itself grants refuge to anyone who turns to him.
insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to refuge: not just praising Ram, but relying on his name as shelter.
modern_relevance: You are exhausted, and the phone is full of advice, fixes, and noise. One steady name, one trusted presence, can feel like the first place your mind finally rests.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: जौं मो पर प्रसन्न सुखरासी। जानिअ सत्य मोहि निज दासी॥ तौ प्रभु हरहु मोर अग्याना। कहि रघुनाथ कथा बिधि नाना ॥
translation: हे सुख की राशि ! यदि आप मुझ पर प्रसन्न हैं और सचमुच मुझे अपनी दासी (या अपनी सच्ची दासी) जानते हैं, तो हे प्रभो! आप श्री रघुनाथजी की नाना प्रकार की कथा कहकर मेरा अज्ञान दूर कीजिए ॥
english_translation: If you are pleased with me and truly know me as your own servant, then, Lord, remove my ignorance by telling me the many stories of Raghunath.
essence: Humility opens the door to wisdom.
simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to treat her as his own devoted servant and remove her ignorance by speaking the many stories of Ram.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to sincere asking, making room for understanding to enter.
modern_relevance: You sit with someone who knows more than you and stop pretending. Instead of performing understanding, you ask the real question that clears the fog.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: जासु भवनु सुरतरु तर होई। सहि कि दरिद्र जनित दुखु सोई॥ ससिभूषन अस हृदयँ बिचारी। हरहु नाथ मम मति भ्रम भारी ॥
translation: जिसका घर कल्पवृक्ष के नीचे हो, वह भला दरिद्रता से उत्पन्न दुःख को क्यों सहेगा? हे शशिभूषण! हे नाथ! हृदय में ऐसा विचार कर मेरी बुद्धि के भारी भ्रम को दूर कीजिए ॥
english_translation: How can one whose home is beneath the wish-fulfilling tree endure the suffering born of poverty? O Shashibhushan, O Lord, consider this in your heart and remove the great confusion of my mind.
essence: Abundance makes poverty's fear look absurd.
simple_meaning: A person sheltered by abundance should not suffer the pain of poverty. The speaker asks the Lord to think this way and remove the heavy confusion from his mind.
insight: It shifts attention from external lack to the mind's habit of magnifying fear.
modern_relevance: You have food in the fridge, rent paid, and still panic when the savings dip. The mind keeps inventing scarcity even in the middle of enough.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: प्रभु जे मुनि परमारथबादी। कहहिं राम कहुँ ब्रह्म अनादी॥ सेस सारदा बेद पुराना। सकल करहिं रघुपति गुन गाना ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! जो परमार्थतत्व (ब्रह्म) के ज्ञाता और वक्ता मुनि हैं, वे श्री रामचन्द्रजी को अनादि ब्रह्म कहते हैं और शेष, सरस्वती, वेद और पुराण सभी श्री रघुनाथजी का गुण गाते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Lord, the sages who speak of the highest reality call Ram the beginningless supreme reality. Shesha, Saraswati, the Vedas, and the Puranas all sing the praises of Raghupati.
essence: Ram stands as the beginningless reality all sacred voices praise.
simple_meaning: Wise sages call Ram the beginningless supreme reality, and every sacred source keeps praising him.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating Ram as a local deity to recognising him as the ground of all sacred speech.
modern_relevance: You hear a chant in a temple, a verse in a book, and a line from a teacher — all pointing the same way. The mind relaxes when it sees that the deepest truth is being echoed everywhere.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तुम्ह पुनि राम राम दिन राती। सादर जपहु अनँग आराती॥ रामु सो अवध नृपति सुत सोई। की अज अगुन अलखगति कोई ॥
translation: और हे कामदेव के शत्रु! आप भी दिन-रात आदरपूर्वक राम-राम जपा करते हैं- ये राम वही अयोध्या के राजा के पुत्र हैं? या अजन्मे, निर्गुण और अगोचर कोई और राम हैं? ॥
english_translation: And you, enemy of desire, also chant Ram's name day and night with reverence. Is Ram the prince of Ayodhya, or some unborn, attribute-free, ungraspable reality?
essence: Ram is both the prince and the unborn reality.
simple_meaning: Shiva says that even the destroyer of desire chants Ram's name constantly, then asks whether Ram is only Dasharath's son or the unborn, attribute-free reality itself.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as only a historical figure to recognising his divine reality.
modern_relevance: You hear a name repeated so often in a prayer hall that it stops sounding like a name and starts feeling like a presence. Then one question arrives: are you remembering a person, or touching something far larger?
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: जौं नृप तनय त ब्रह्म किमि नारि बिरहँ मति भोरि। देखि चरित महिमा सुनत भ्रमति बुद्धि अति मोरि ॥
translation: यदि वे राजपुत्र हैं तो ब्रह्म कैसे? (और यदि ब्रह्म हैं तो) स्त्री के विरह में उनकी मति बावली कैसे हो गई? इधर उनके ऐसे चरित्र देखकर और उधर उनकी महिमा सुनकर मेरी बुद्धि अत्यन्त चकरा रही है ॥
english_translation: If they are a prince, how can they be Brahman? And if they are Brahman, how can their mind be so bewildered by separation from a woman? Seeing their conduct and hearing their glory, my understanding is utterly confused.
essence: Greatness can look human, and human feeling can hide greatness.
simple_meaning: Parvati is confused by Ram's human-like actions and divine glory. She cannot reconcile his royal life, his grief in separation, and his supreme nature.
insight: It shifts the mind from quick labels to patient questioning, so deeper meaning can emerge.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary in one moment and astonishingly wise in another. Their contradictions unsettle you, but that discomfort can become the beginning of real understanding.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: जौं अनीह ब्यापक बिभु कोऊ। कहहु बुझाइ नाथ मोहि सोऊ॥ अग्य जानि रिस उर जनि धरहू। जेहि बिधि मोह मिटै सोइ करहू ॥
translation: यदि इच्छारहित, व्यापक, समर्थ ब्रह्म कोई और हैं, तो हे नाथ! मुझे उसे समझाकर कहिए। मुझे नादान समझकर मन में क्रोध न लाइए। जिस तरह मेरा मोह दूर हो, वही कीजिए ॥
english_translation: If some other desireless, all-pervading, mighty supreme reality exists, then, Lord, explain that to me. Do not grow angry, thinking me ignorant. Do whatever removes my delusion.
essence: Honest questioning is the doorway through which delusion leaves.
simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to explain the idea of a desireless, all-pervading supreme reality. She asks him not to be offended by her confusion and to answer in whatever way removes her delusion.
insight: It shifts the mind from passive listening to fearless inquiry for the sake of clear seeing.
modern_relevance: You are in a late-night conversation with someone wiser than you, and your questions feel clumsy. Instead of nodding along, you finally ask the thing that actually matters: explain it so the confusion can leave.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: मैं बन दीखि राम प्रभुताई। अति भय बिकल न तुम्हहि सुनाई॥ तदपि मलिन मन बोधु न आवा। सो फलु भली भाँति हम पावा ॥
translation: मैंने (पिछले जन्म में) वन में श्री रामचन्द्रजी की प्रभुता देखी थी, परन्तु अत्यन्त भयभीत होने के कारण मैंने वह बात आपको सुनाई नहीं। तो भी मेरे मलिन मन को बोध न हुआ। उसका फल भी मैंने अच्छी तरह पा लिया ॥
english_translation: I saw Ram's majesty in the forest before, but fear kept me from telling you. Even so, my impure mind did not awaken. I received the full fruit of that.
essence: Fear can silence truth, but confusion still bears its own fruit.
simple_meaning: Parvati says she once saw Ram's greatness in the forest, but fear stopped her from speaking. Because her mind remained unclear, she suffered the result of that confusion.
insight: It shifts the mind from passive seeing to honest recognition. Fear may block insight, but unspoken truth still shapes the result.
modern_relevance: You notice the right answer in a tense meeting, but fear of looking foolish keeps you silent. Later, the missed moment weighs on you more than speaking ever would have.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: अजहूँ कछु संसउ मन मोरें। करहु कृपा बिनवउँ कर जोरें॥ प्रभु तब मोहि बहु भाँति प्रबोधा। नाथ सो समुझि करहु जनि क्रोधा ॥
translation: अब भी मेरे मन में कुछ संदेह है। आप कृपा कीजिए, मैं हाथ जोड़कर विनती करती हूँ। हे प्रभो! आपने उस समय मुझे बहुत तरह से समझाया था (फिर भी मेरा संदेह नहीं गया), हे नाथ! यह सोचकर मुझ पर क्रोध न कीजिए ॥
english_translation: I still have some doubt in my mind. Please show me kindness; I bow with folded hands. Lord, you explained it to me in many ways before, but do not be angry with me for still not understanding.
essence: Doubt can be sacred when it is asked with humility.
simple_meaning: Parvati still has a doubt and asks Shiva to explain again without anger. She is humble, honest, and still searching for understanding.
insight: It normalizes honest questioning and shows that clarity can require patient, respectful repetition.
modern_relevance: You replay the conversation after everyone leaves the room, still unsure what was really meant. Instead of pretending you understood, you ask again with humility.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: तब कर अस बिमोह अब नाहीं। रामकथा पर रुचि मन माहीं॥ कहहु पुनीत राम गुन गाथा। भुजगराज भूषन सुरनाथा ॥
translation: मुझे अब पहले जैसा मोह नहीं है, अब तो मेरे मन में रामकथा सुनने की रुचि है। हे शेषनाग को अलंकार रूप में धारण करने वाले देवताओं के नाथ! आप श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुणों की पवित्र कथा कहिए ॥
english_translation: I am no longer deluded as before. My mind now longs to hear Ram's story. Please tell the pure tale of Ram's virtues, O ornament of Shesha and lord of the radiant beings.
essence: Clear seeing turns the mind toward Ram's story.
simple_meaning: Parvati says her confusion has cleared, and now she wants to hear Ram's story and virtues with a pure mind.
insight: It shifts attention from confusion to receptive listening, showing that devotion begins when the mind is ready to hear.
modern_relevance: After a long argument, you finally stop defending yourself and ask for the real story. The noise has dropped away. What you want now is something true enough to settle the mind.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: बंदउँ पद धरि धरनि सिरु बिनय करउँ कर जोरि। बरनहु रघुबर बिसद जसु श्रुति सिद्धांत निचोरि ॥
translation: मैं पृथ्वी पर सिर टेककर आपके चरणों की वंदना करती हूँ और हाथ जोड़कर विनती करती हूँ। आप वेदों के सिद्धांत को निचोड़कर श्री रघुनाथजी का निर्मल यश वर्णन कीजिए ॥
english_translation: I bow with my head to the earth and join my hands in prayer. Please describe the pure glory of Raghubar, distilled from the essence of the Vedas.
essence: Humility opens the way to hearing Ram clearly.
simple_meaning: Parvati bows respectfully and asks Shiva to describe Ram's pure glory, distilled from the essence of the Vedas.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to receptive listening before sacred truth.
modern_relevance: You finally ask the teacher the question you were afraid to ask. Pride drops, and real learning begins the moment you stop performing certainty.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: जदपि जोषिता नहिं अधिकारी। दासी मन क्रम बचन तुम्हारी॥ गूढ़उ तत्त्व न साधु दुरावहिं। आरत अधिकारी जहँ पावहिं ॥
translation: यद्यपि स्त्री होने के कारण मैं उसे सुनने की अधिकारिणी नहीं हूँ, तथापि मैं मन, वचन और कर्म से आपकी दासी हूँ। संत लोग जहाँ आर्त अधिकारी पाते हैं, वहाँ गूढ़ तत्त्व भी उससे नहीं छिपाते ॥
english_translation: Although I am not formally qualified to hear it as a woman, I am your servant in mind, deed, and speech. Wise people do not hide even the deepest truth from one who is truly distressed.
essence: Sincere need can qualify a person for hidden truth.
simple_meaning: Parvati says she may not be formally qualified, but her devotion makes her worthy. She asks that even the deepest truth be shared with someone who is sincerely distressed.
insight: It shifts the mind from entitlement to receptivity, showing that humility invites deeper teaching.
modern_relevance: You sit in a quiet room after a breakup, finally admitting you do not understand what happened. The bravado is gone. This verse says honest need can unlock the answer.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: अति आरति पूछउँ सुरराया। रघुपति कथा कहहु करि दाया॥ प्रथम सो कारन कहहु बिचारी। निर्गुन ब्रह्म सगुन बपु धारी ॥
translation: हे देवताओं के स्वामी! मैं बहुत ही आर्तभाव (दीनता) से पूछती हूँ, आप मुझ पर दया करके श्री रघुनाथजी की कथा कहिए। पहले तो वह कारण विचारकर बतलाइए, जिससे निर्गुण ब्रह्म सगुण रूप धारण करता है ॥
english_translation: O lord of the devas, I ask with deep humility: please, out of compassion, tell the story of Raghupati. First, reflect and explain the reason why the formless supreme reality takes a manifest form.
essence: The deepest question is why the formless becomes visible.
simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to tell Ram's story and explain why the formless supreme reality appears in a visible form.
insight: It shifts the mind from surface story to the deeper question of why the divine becomes approachable.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence feels larger than their body, and you want to know what makes them so real. This verse names that hunger: not just to admire, but to understand the mystery behind the appearance.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: पुनि प्रभु कहहु राम अवतारा। बालचरित पुनि कहहु उदारा॥ कहहु जथा जानकी बिबाहीं। राज तजा सो दूषन काहीं ॥
translation: फिर हे प्रभु! श्री रामचन्द्रजी के अवतार (जन्म) की कथा कहिए तथा उनका उदार बाल चरित्र कहिए। फिर जिस प्रकार उन्होंने श्री जानकीजी से विवाह किया, वह कथा कहिए और फिर यह बतलाइए कि उन्होंने जो राज्य छोड़ा, सो किस दोष से ॥
english_translation: Then, Lord, tell of Ram’s descent, and then his noble childhood. Tell how Janaki was married, and then explain by what fault he gave up the kingdom.
essence: A true story is understood by its whole arc, not one event.
simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to continue the story: Ram’s birth, his childhood, Sita’s marriage, and why he left the kingdom.
insight: It invites the listener to follow Ram’s life as a complete arc, not isolated events.
modern_relevance: A child asks, “Tell me everything from the beginning.” You realize the hardest moments in a life only make sense when you see the full chain, not one painful scene cut loose from the rest.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: बन बसि कीन्हे चरित अपारा। कहहु नाथ जिमि रावन मारा॥ राज बैठि कीन्हीं बहु लीला। सकल कहहु संकर सुखसीला ॥
translation: हे नाथ! फिर उन्होंने वन में रहकर जो अपार चरित्र किए तथा जिस तरह रावण को मारा, वह कहिए। हे सुखस्वरूप शंकर! फिर आप उन सारी लीलाओं को कहिए जो उन्होंने राज्य (सिंहासन) पर बैठकर की थीं ॥
english_translation: O Lord, tell how He lived in the forest and how Ravana was slain. O blissful Shiva, tell all the deeds He performed while seated on the throne.
essence: Ram’s greatness must be told through exile, victory, and rule together.
simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to describe Ram’s forest life, Ravana’s defeat, and the many deeds Ram did as king.
insight: It shifts attention from a single event to the full pattern of a life.
modern_relevance: Someone asks you to tell the full story, not the highlight reel: the hard years, the victory, and the quiet years after success. Real understanding comes from the whole arc.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: बहुरि कहहु करुनायतन कीन्ह जो अचरज राम। प्रजा सहित रघुबंसमनि किमि गवने निज धाम ॥
translation: हे कृपाधाम! फिर वह अद्भुत चरित्र कहिए जो श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने किया- वे रघुकुल शिरोमणि प्रजा सहित किस प्रकार अपने धाम को गए? ॥
english_translation: O abode of compassion, tell again the wondrous act that Ram performed: how did the jewel of the Raghu line go to his own home with the people?
essence: Ram's greatest wonder is returning home with everyone who belongs with him.
simple_meaning: The speaker asks to hear again how Ram, along with his people, returned to his own home after his wondrous deeds.
insight: It shifts attention from heroic events to the sacred completion of return.
modern_relevance: After a long year of sacrifice, the family finally unlocks the old house, carries in the last box, and stands in the doorway together. The real victory is not the struggle — it is coming home whole.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: पुनि प्रभु कहहु सो तत्त्व बखानी। जेहिं बिग्यान मगन मुनि ग्यानी॥ भगति ग्यान बिग्यान बिरागा। पुनि सब बरनहु सहित बिभागा ॥
translation: हे प्रभु! फिर आप उस तत्त्व को समझाकर कहिए, जिसकी अनुभूति में ज्ञानी मुनिगण सदा मग्न रहते हैं और फिर भक्ति, ज्ञान, विज्ञान और वैराग्य का विभाग सहित वर्णन कीजिए ॥
english_translation: O Lord, speak again of that truth, in which wise sages remain absorbed. Also describe devotion, knowledge, discernment, and non-attachment, with their distinctions.
essence: Real understanding begins by asking for the distinctions.
simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to explain the deepest truth again, along with the differences between devotion, knowledge, discernment, and non-attachment.
insight: It shifts the mind from passive listening to precise inquiry about how these paths differ.
modern_relevance: You hear a spiritual idea once in a lecture, then sit with it all week because it still feels unfinished. That second question is not failure; it is real learning.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: और राम रहस्य अनेका। कहहु नाथ अति बिमल बिबेका॥ जो प्रभु मैं पूछा नहिं होई। सोउ दयाल राखहु जनि गोई ॥
translation: (इसके सिवा) श्री रामचन्द्रजी के और भी जो अनेक रहस्य (छिपे हुए भाव अथवा चरित्र) हैं, उनको कहिए। हे नाथ! आपका ज्ञान अत्यन्त निर्मल है। हे प्रभो! जो बात मैंने न भी पूछी हो, हे दयालु! उसे भी आप छिपा न रखिएगा ॥
english_translation: (Besides this) tell also the many other hidden mysteries of Ram. O Lord, your understanding is utterly pure. O merciful one, do not keep hidden even what I did not ask.
essence: True inquiry asks for what has not yet been asked.
simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to explain Ram’s many hidden mysteries and to share even the things she has not thought to ask. She trusts his pure understanding and wants nothing left concealed.
insight: It shifts inquiry from selective questions to full receptivity, asking for what lies beyond your own awareness.
modern_relevance: You finally sit with someone wise enough to tell you the hard part, not just the polished version. You want the whole answer, including the part you didn’t know to ask about.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: तुम्ह त्रिभुवन गुर बेद बखाना। आन जीव पाँवर का जाना॥ प्रस्न उमा कै सहज सुहाई। छल बिहीन सुनि सिव मन भाई ॥
translation: वेदों ने आपको तीनों लोकों का गुरु कहा है। दूसरे पामर जीव इस रहस्य को क्या जानें! पार्वतीजी के सहज सुंदर और छलरहित (सरल) प्रश्न सुनकर शिवजी के मन को बहुत अच्छे लगे ॥
english_translation: The Vedas call you the teacher of the three worlds. What can ordinary beings know of this mystery? Shiva's mind was delighted by Parvati's simple, sincere question.
essence: Humility makes room for revelation.
simple_meaning: The Vedas praise Ram as the teacher of all three worlds, while ordinary people cannot fully grasp that mystery. Shiva is pleased by Parvati's simple, honest question.
insight: It shifts attention from intellectual pride to humble receptivity.
modern_relevance: You sit with someone wiser than you and finally ask the plain question you were embarrassed to voice. That honesty changes the whole conversation.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: हर हियँ रामचरित सब आए। प्रेम पुलक लोचन जल छाए॥ श्रीरघुनाथ रूप उर आवा। परमानंद अमित सुख पावा ॥
translation: श्री महादेवजी के हृदय में सारे रामचरित्र आ गए। प्रेम के मारे उनका शरीर पुलकित हो गया और नेत्रों में जल भर आया। श्री रघुनाथजी का रूप उनके हृदय में आ गया, जिससे स्वयं परमानन्दस्वरूप शिवजी ने भी अपार सुख पाया ॥
english_translation: All the stories of Ram entered Shiva's heart. Love made his body tremble, and tears filled his eyes. Ram's form arose within his heart, and Shiva, whose nature is supreme bliss, tasted boundless joy.
essence: Ram's remembrance turns devotion into visible joy.
simple_meaning: Shiva becomes so filled with love for Ram that his body trembles, his eyes fill with tears, and Ram's form brings him immense joy.
insight: It shows that remembrance can become embodied devotion, where feeling and vision deepen each other.
modern_relevance: You hear a song that takes you straight back to someone you love, and your throat tightens before you can explain why. Some truths are felt first in the body.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: मगन ध्यान रस दंड जुग पुनि मन बाहेर कीन्ह। रघुपति चरित महेस तब हरषित बरनै लीन्ह॥111।
translation: शिवजी दो घड़ी तक ध्यान के रस (आनंद) में डूबे रहे, फिर उन्होंने मन को बाहर खींचा और तब वे प्रसन्न होकर श्री रघुनाथजी का चरित्र वर्णन करने लगे ॥
english_translation: For two watches Shiva remained immersed in the taste of meditation, then drew his mind outward and, delighted, began to narrate the deeds of Raghupati.
essence: Meditation ripens into joy when Ram's story is spoken.
simple_meaning: Shiva sat absorbed in meditation, then turned back with joy to speak Ram's story.
insight: It shifts attention from private absorption to expressive remembrance.
modern_relevance: You sit quietly after a long day, phone face down, and the mind finally settles. Then one memory of someone you love brings warmth back into the room. Devotion does that: it turns silence into praise.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: झूठेउ सत्य जाहि बिनु जानें। जिमि भुजंग बिनु रजु पहिचानें॥ जेहि जानें जग जाइ हेराई। जागें जथा सपन भ्रम जाई ॥
translation: जिसके बिना जाने झूठ भी सत्य मालूम होता है, जैसे बिना पहचाने रस्सी में साँप का भ्रम हो जाता है और जिसके जान लेने पर जगत का उसी तरह लोप हो जाता है, जैसे जागने पर स्वप्न का भ्रम जाता रहता है ॥
english_translation: Without knowing it, falsehood appears true, like mistaking a rope for a snake. Knowing it, the world vanishes like a dream after waking.
essence: Clear seeing dissolves the world of error like waking from a dream.
simple_meaning: Ignorance makes false things seem real. Clear understanding removes the illusion, just as waking ends a dream.
insight: It shifts the mind from reacting to appearances to checking what is actually real.
modern_relevance: You read one harsh text at midnight and suddenly your whole friendship feels broken. By morning, the panic looks smaller. Clear seeing can undo a whole world built by fear.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: बंदउँ बालरूप सोइ रामू। सब सिधि सुलभ जपत जिसु नामू॥ मंगल भवन अमंगल हारी। द्रवउ सो दसरथ अजिर बिहारी ॥
translation: मैं उन्हीं श्री रामचन्द्रजी के बाल रूप की वंदना करता हूँ, जिनका नाम जपने से सब सिद्धियाँ सहज ही प्राप्त हो जाती हैं। मंगल के धाम, अमंगल के हरने वाले और श्री दशरथजी के आँगन में खेलने वाले (बालरूप) श्री रामचन्द्रजी मुझ पर कृपा करें ॥
english_translation: I bow to that child-form of Ram. All powers come easily by repeating his name. He is the home of auspiciousness, the remover of inauspiciousness. May that Ram, who played in Dasharath's courtyard, soften my heart.
essence: Ram’s name gives what striving cannot.
simple_meaning: Ram’s child form is worthy of reverence, and repeating his name brings every attainment easily. He is the source of auspiciousness and the remover of what harms.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing scattered remedies to resting in a single sacred refuge.
modern_relevance: You are exhausted, scrolling for the next fix, and nothing sticks. Then one simple practice steadies you again: return to what is worthy, repeat it, and let the noise fall away.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: करि प्रनाम रामहि त्रिपुरारी। हरषि सुधा सम गिरा उचारी॥ धन्य धन्य गिरिराजकुमारी। तुम्ह समान नहिं कोउ उपकारी ॥
translation: त्रिपुरासुर का वध करने वाले शिवजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी को प्रणाम करके आनंद में भरकर अमृत के समान वाणी बोले- हे गिरिराजकुमारी पार्वती! तुम धन्य हो! धन्य हो!! तुम्हारे समान कोई उपकारी नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Shiva bowed to Ram and, overjoyed, spoke words like nectar: "Blessed, blessed is Giriraj's daughter. No one serves like you."
essence: Humility that asks for Ram is itself a great service.
simple_meaning: Shiva first bows to Ram, then praises Parvati for asking about Ram's story. He calls her blessed and says no one serves like she does.
insight: It shifts attention from the answer alone to the devotion and receptivity that make the answer possible.
modern_relevance: Someone asks a sincere question in a quiet room, and the whole mood changes. The person answering does not just give information — he honors the humility that made the question possible.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: पूँछेहु रघुपति कथा प्रसंगा। सकल लोक जग पावनि गंगा॥ तुम्ह रघुबीर चरन अनुरागी। कीन्हिहु प्रस्न जगत हित लागी ॥
translation: जो तुमने श्री रघुनाथजी की कथा का प्रसंग पूछा है, जो कथा समस्त लोकों के लिए जगत को पवित्र करने वाली गंगाजी के समान है। तुमने जगत के कल्याण के लिए ही प्रश्न पूछे हैं। तुम श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों में प्रेम रखने वाली हो ॥
english_translation: You have asked about the story of Raghupati, a tale that purifies all worlds like the Ganga. You asked for the welfare of the world, for you love the feet of the Lord of the Raghu clan.
essence: A question asked in love can purify everyone who hears it.
simple_meaning: Parvati’s question is praised as sincere and beneficial because it comes from love for Ram and seeks the good of the world.
insight: It reframes inquiry as service: asking well can be an act of devotion, not just curiosity.
modern_relevance: You ask a question in a meeting not to sound clever, but because people are confused and the room needs clarity. That kind of question changes the whole atmosphere.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: राम कृपा तें पारबति सपनेहुँ तव मन माहिं। सोक मोह संदेह भ्रम मम बिचार कछु नाहिं ॥
translation: हे पार्वती! मेरे विचार में तो श्री रामजी की कृपा से तुम्हारे मन में स्वप्न में भी शोक, मोह, संदेह और भ्रम कुछ भी नहीं है ॥
english_translation: O Parvati, by Ram's grace there is not even in a dream any sorrow, delusion, doubt, or confusion in your mind.
essence: Ram's grace leaves no space for sorrow or confusion.
simple_meaning: Ram's grace can make the mind so clear that sorrow, confusion, doubt, and delusion do not enter it.
insight: It shifts attention from mental noise to the quiet confidence that comes from grace.
modern_relevance: You replay a painful conversation at 2 a.m., trying to untangle every meaning. Then something settles, and the mind stops spinning. This verse points to that kind of inward clarity.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: तदपि असंका कीन्हिहु सोई। कहत सुनत सब कर हित होई॥ जिन्ह हरिकथा सुनी नहिं काना। श्रवन रंध्र अहिभवन समाना ॥
translation: फिर भी तुमने इसीलिए वही (पुरानी) शंका की है कि इस प्रसंग के कहने-सुनने से सबका कल्याण होगा। जिन्होंने अपने कानों से भगवान की कथा नहीं सुनी, उनके कानों के छिद्र साँप के बिल के समान हैं ॥
english_translation: Still, you asked that very question so that hearing and speaking this story may do good to everyone. The ears of those who have never heard the divine story are like snake holes.
essence: Ram's story itself is a blessing to anyone who hears it.
simple_meaning: Hearing and speaking Ram's story brings benefit to everyone. People who never listen to it remain spiritually empty, like snake holes with no life in them.
insight: It shifts attention from clever analysis to receptive listening as a form of care.
modern_relevance: You put on a podcast in the car because your mind felt scattered, and halfway through you notice your breathing has softened. Some words do that: they quietly change the room inside you.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: नयनन्हि संत दरस नहिं देखा। लोचन मोरपंख कर लेखा॥ तेसिर कटु तुंबरि समतूला। जे न नमत हरि गुर पद मूला ॥
translation: जिन्होंने अपने नेत्रों से संतों के दर्शन नहीं किए, उनके वे नेत्र मोर के पंखों पर दिखने वाली नकली आँखों की गिनती में हैं। वे सिर कड़वी तूँबी के समान हैं, जो श्री हरि और गुरु के चरणतल पर नहीं झुकते ॥
english_translation: Those who have never seen saints with their eyes have eyes like the false eyes painted on peacock feathers. Their heads are like bitter gourds, unbowed at the feet of Hari and the guru.
essence: Sight without reverence is almost useless.
simple_meaning: Without meeting holy people, even eyes and a head lose their worth. Real sight is shown by humility before the divine and the teacher.
insight: It shifts attention from display and information to reverence, humility, and the company you keep.
modern_relevance: You can scroll through a hundred spiritual posts and still miss what matters. One quiet meeting with someone rooted in humility can change how you see everything.
speaker: Tulsidas
