verse_text: जिन्ह हरिभगति हृदयँ नहिं आनी। जीवत सव समान तेइ प्रानी॥ जो नहिं करइ राम गुन गाना। जीह सो दादुर जीह समाना ॥
translation: जिन्होंने भगवान की भक्ति को अपने हृदय में स्थान नहीं दिया, वे प्राणी जीते हुए ही मुर्दे के समान हैं, जो जीभ श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुणों का गान नहीं करती, वह मेंढक की जीभ के समान है ॥
english_translation: Those who have not brought devotion to Ram into their hearts are like the dead while still alive. A tongue that does not sing Ram's virtues is like a frog's tongue.
essence: Life without devotion is only motion; speech without praise is empty noise.
simple_meaning: A person who keeps no devotion for Ram is spiritually lifeless. A tongue that never praises Ram is as useless as a frog's croak.
insight: It shifts the reader from merely existing and speaking to living with devotion and using speech for praise.
modern_relevance: You scroll through a hundred voices before breakfast, but nothing stays with you. Then one name, one song, one truth keeps returning. This verse asks whether your heart has actually been moved by anything real.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कुलिस कठोर निठुर सोइ छाती। सुनि हरिचरित न जो हरषाती॥ गिरिजा सुनहु राम कै लीला। सुर हित दनुज बिमोहनसीला ॥
translation: वह हृदय वज्र के समान कड़ा और निष्ठुर है, जो भगवान के चरित्र सुनकर हर्षित नहीं होता। हे पार्वती! श्री रामचन्द्रजी की लीला सुनो, यह देवताओं का कल्याण करने वाली और दैत्यों को विशेष रूप से मोहित करने वाली है ॥
english_translation: That heart is as hard as a thunderbolt and cruel, which does not rejoice on hearing the deeds of the divine. O Parvati, listen to Ram's play: it brings benefit to the radiant beings and bewilders the forces of ego and shadow.
essence: A heart that cannot rejoice at Ram's story has already hardened.
simple_meaning: A heart that feels no joy at hearing Ram's story has become hard. Tulsidas then invites Parvati to hear Ram's play, which blesses the good and confounds the forces of ego and shadow.
insight: It shifts the reader from emotional numbness to receptive devotion, treating delight in Ram's story as a spiritual test.
modern_relevance: You keep scrolling past stories of kindness, sacrifice, and grace without feeling anything. That numbness is not neutrality; it is a heart that has gone hard. Hearing what is noble should still move you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: रामकथा सुरधेनु सम सेवत सब सुख दानि। सतसमाज सुरलोक सब को न सुनै अस जानि ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की कथा कामधेनु के समान सेवा करने से सब सुखों को देने वाली है और सत्पुरुषों के समाज ही सब देवताओं के लोक हैं, ऐसा जानकर इसे कौन न सुनेगा! ॥
english_translation: Ram's story is like a wish-fulfilling cow: serving it gives every joy. The company of the good is itself a higher realm; knowing this, who would not listen?
essence: Ram's story nourishes completely, and good company is its own reward.
simple_meaning: Ram's story brings every kind of joy, like a wish-fulfilling cow. Good company itself feels like a higher realm, so listening to this story is natural.
insight: It shifts attention from entertainment to nourishment, and from casual company to people who deepen devotion.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where every conversation is cynical, then into another where people speak with honesty and care. One drains you; the other restores you. This verse points you toward the second room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामकथा सुंदर कर तारी। संसय बिहग उड़ावनिहारी॥ रामकथा कलि बिटप कुठारी। सादर सुनु गिरिराजकुमारी ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की कथा हाथ की सुंदर ताली है, जो संदेह रूपी पक्षियों को उड़ा देती है। फिर रामकथा कलियुग रूपी वृक्ष को काटने के लिए कुल्हाड़ी है। हे गिरिराजकुमारी! तुम इसे आदरपूर्वक सुनो ॥
english_translation: Ram's story is a beautiful clap of the hands that drives away the birds of doubt. Ram's story is an axe for cutting down the tree of Kali Yuga. Listen to it with reverence, Giriraj's daughter.
essence: Ram's story clears doubt and cuts through confusion.
simple_meaning: Ram's story removes doubt and destroys the habits of confusion. It is powerful enough to clear the mind and cut through what weakens spiritual life.
insight: It shifts the mind from skeptical scattering to receptive listening.
modern_relevance: You are half-listening to a podcast while ten tabs stay open in your head. Then one clear line lands and the noise drops. That is the kind of force this verse gives Ram's story.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: राम नाम गुन चरित सुहाए। जनम करम अगनित श्रुति गाए॥ जथा अनंत राम भगवाना। तथा कथा कीरति गुन नाना ॥
translation: वेदों ने श्री रामचन्द्रजी के सुंदर नाम, गुण, चरित्र, जन्म और कर्म सभी अनगिनत कहे हैं। जिस प्रकार भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी अनन्त हैं, उसी तरह उनकी कथा, कीर्ति और गुण भी अनंत हैं ॥
english_translation: The Vedas sing of Ram's beautiful name, virtues, deeds, birth, and actions as endless. Just as Lord Ram is infinite, so too are his stories, fame, and qualities without end.
essence: Ram cannot be fully described because his glory has no limit.
simple_meaning: Ram's name, qualities, life, and deeds are beyond counting. His greatness cannot be exhausted, so every telling of him remains incomplete and alive.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to contain Ram in one definition to receiving him as inexhaustible.
modern_relevance: You reread a letter from someone you love and notice a detail you missed before. Some presences are like that: the more closely you look, the more they reveal.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: तदपि जथा श्रुत जसि मति मोरी। कहिहउँ देखि प्रीति अति तोरी॥ उमा प्रस्न तव सहज सुहाई। सुखद संतसंमत मोहि भाई ॥
translation: तो भी तुम्हारी अत्यन्त प्रीति देखकर, जैसा कुछ मैंने सुना है और जैसी मेरी बुद्धि है, उसी के अनुसार मैं कहूँगा। हे पार्वती! तुम्हारा प्रश्न स्वाभाविक ही सुंदर, सुखदायक और संतसम्मत है और मुझे तो बहुत ही अच्छा लगा है ॥
english_translation: Still, according to what I have heard and as my understanding allows, I will speak, moved by your great affection. O Uma, your question is naturally beautiful, pleasing, and approved by the wise, and I am very glad of it.
essence: Honest teaching begins with a worthy question.
simple_meaning: Shiva says he will answer as best he can, guided by what he has heard and understood, because Parvati's question is sincere, beautiful, and worthy of the wise.
insight: It teaches you to meet sincere inquiry with humility and care, not with display.
modern_relevance: Someone asks a careful question in a quiet room, not to win an argument but to understand. The best answer begins there — with respect, not performance.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: एक बात नहिं मोहि सोहानी। जदपि मोह बस कहेहु भवानी॥ तुम्ह जो कहा राम कोउ आना। जेहि श्रुति गाव धरहिं मुनि ध्याना ॥
translation: परंतु हे पार्वती! एक बात मुझे अच्छी नहीं लगी, यद्यपि वह तुमने मोह के वश होकर ही कही है। तुमने जो यह कहा कि वे राम कोई और हैं, जिन्हें वेद गाते और मुनिजन जिनका ध्यान धरते हैं- ॥
english_translation: One thing does not please me, though you said it under the spell of delusion, O Bhavani. You said that Ram is someone else, the one whom the Vedas sing and the sages meditate on.
essence: Ram is not another being; he is the one the Vedas already praise.
simple_meaning: Shiva gently corrects Parvati: Ram is not someone separate from the one praised in the Vedas and meditated on by sages.
insight: It shifts attention from labels and separateness to the unity behind all reverence.
modern_relevance: You hear someone reduce what you love most into a name or a role. The correction matters: the deepest reality is not a distant concept, but the one already being praised and sought.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: कहहिं सुनहिं अस अधम नर ग्रसे जे मोह पिसाच। पाषंडी हरि पद बिमुख जानहिं झूठ न साच ॥
translation: जो मोह रूपी पिशाच के द्वारा ग्रस्त हैं, पाखण्डी हैं, भगवान के चरणों से विमुख हैं और जो झूठ-सच कुछ भी नहीं जानते, ऐसे अधम मनुष्य ही इस तरह कहते-सुनते हैं ॥
english_translation: Such vile people speak and listen this way—people seized by the demon of delusion, hypocrites, turned away from Hari's feet, and unable to tell false from true.
essence: Delusion destroys the ability to recognize truth.
simple_meaning: People caught in delusion, hypocrisy, and rejection of the divine lose the ability to tell truth from falsehood.
insight: It shifts the reader from arguing over appearances to checking whether the mind itself is clouded.
modern_relevance: You are scrolling through a comment thread where everyone is certain, angry, and wrong. The loudest voices often sound convincing precisely because they have lost contact with what is real.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: अग्य अकोबिद अंध अभागी। काई बिषय मुकुर मन लागी॥ लंपट कपटी कुटिल बिसेषी। सपनेहुँ संतसभा नहिं देखी ॥
translation: जो अज्ञानी, मूर्ख, अंधे और भाग्यहीन हैं और जिनके मन रूपी दर्पण पर विषय रूपी काई जमी हुई है, जो व्यभिचारी, छली और बड़े कुटिल हैं और जिन्होंने कभी स्वप्न में भी संत समाज के दर्शन नहीं किए ॥
english_translation: Ignorant, foolish, blind, and unfortunate, their minds are coated with the moss of worldly cravings. Lustful, deceitful, and deeply crooked, they have never even seen the company of the good in a dream.
essence: A stained mind cannot recognise what is pure.
simple_meaning: People trapped in desire cannot see clearly. Their minds are stained, their character is twisted, and they have never truly come near the company of the wise.
insight: It shifts attention from debating ideas to noticing the state of the mind that judges them.
modern_relevance: You keep arguing with a message, but the real issue is the fog in your own head. When craving, ego, or resentment takes over, even good advice sounds wrong.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: कहहिं ते बेद असंमत बानी। जिन्ह कें सूझ लाभु नहिं हानी॥ मुकुर मलिन अरु नयन बिहीना। राम रूप देखहिं किमि दीना ॥
translation: और जिन्हें अपने लाभ-हानि नहीं सूझती, वे ही ऐसी वेदविरुद्ध बातें कहा करते हैं, जिनका हृदय रूपी दर्पण मैला है और जो नेत्रों से हीन हैं, वे बेचारे श्री रामचन्द्रजी का रूप कैसे देखें! ॥
english_translation: Those who cannot see gain or loss speak such contrary words. With a stained mirror and no eyes, how can the poor see Ram's form?
essence: Clouded seeing turns even Ram invisible.
simple_meaning: People who cannot tell gain from loss end up speaking against what the Vedas teach. Their mind is dirty and their vision is gone, so they cannot recognize Ram's form.
insight: It shifts attention from arguing with sacred truth to cleaning the mind that cannot receive it.
modern_relevance: You dismiss a relationship, a teacher, or a hard truth because it threatens your comfort. Later, you realize the problem was never the thing itself — your own clouded seeing was blocking it.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जिन्ह कें अगुन न सगुन बिबेका। जल्पहिं कल्पित बचन अनेका॥ हरिमाया बस जगत भ्रमाहीं। तिन्हहि कहत कछु अघटित नाहीं ॥
translation: जिनको निर्गुण-सगुण का कुछ भी विवेक नहीं है, जो अनेक मनगढ़ंत बातें बका करते हैं, जो श्री हरि की माया के वश में होकर जगत में (जन्म-मृत्यु के चक्र में) भ्रमते फिरते हैं, उनके लिए कुछ भी कह डालना असंभव नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Those who lack discernment between the formless and the formed, who utter countless imagined words, wander the world under Hari's veil of illusion; for them, nothing impossible can be said.
essence: Without discernment, imagination starts sounding like fact.
simple_meaning: People who cannot tell the difference between the formless and the formed get lost in imagination and confusion. Under the veil of illusion, even absurd claims can seem normal to them.
insight: It shifts attention from loud speculation to discernment between what is real and what is imagined.
modern_relevance: A group chat fills with confident opinions, half-remembered facts, and dramatic certainty. You can feel the room tilt away from reality. This verse names that drift before it takes over.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: बातुल भूत बिबस मतवारे। ते नहिं बोलहिं बचन बिचारे॥ जिन्ह कृत महामोह मद पाना। तिन्ह कर कहा करिअ नहिं काना ॥
translation: जिन्हें वायु का रोग (सन्निपात, उन्माद आदि) हो गया हो, जो भूत के वश हो गए हैं और जो नशे में चूर हैं, ऐसे लोग विचारकर वचन नहीं बोलते। जिन्होंने महामोह रूपी मदिरा पी रखी है, उनके कहने पर कान नहीं देना चाहिए ॥
english_translation: People afflicted by madness, possessed by spirits, or drunk with intoxication do not speak thoughtfully. Do not listen to those who have drunk the wine of delusion.
essence: Delusion speaks loudly, but its words deserve no authority.
simple_meaning: People lost to madness, possession, or intoxication do not speak wisely. The same is true of those drunk on deep delusion: their words should not guide you.
insight: It teaches you to separate volume from wisdom and refuse guidance from a clouded mind.
modern_relevance: A group chat fills with hot takes at midnight, each one louder than the last. You do not have to treat every confident voice as clear sight.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अस निज हृदयँ बिचारि तजु संसय भजु राम पद। सुनु गिरिराज कुमारि भ्रम तम रबि कर बचन मम ॥
translation: अपने हृदय में ऐसा विचार कर संदेह छोड़ दो और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों को भजो। हे पार्वती! भ्रम रूपी अंधकार के नाश करने के लिए सूर्य की किरणों के समान मेरे वचनों को सुनो! ॥
english_translation: Reflect thus in your own heart, give up doubt, and worship Ram's feet. Listen, O daughter of the mountain king: my words are like the sun's rays that destroy the darkness of confusion.
essence: Clear seeing begins when doubt is surrendered to devotion.
simple_meaning: Think carefully, drop your doubt, and turn to Ram with devotion. Shiva tells Parvati that his words can cut through confusion like sunlight.
insight: It shifts the mind from scattered speculation to inward reflection and devotional trust.
modern_relevance: You are spiraling at 1:13 a.m., rereading the same message thread and making it mean everything. Stop, look inward, and let one clear principle cut the noise.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सगुनहि अगुनहि नहिं कछु भेदा। गावहिं मुनि पुरान बुध बेदा॥ अगुन अरूप अलख अज जोई। भगत प्रेम बस सगुन सो होई ॥
translation: सगुण और निर्गुण में कुछ भी भेद नहीं है- मुनि, पुराण, पण्डित और वेद सभी ऐसा कहते हैं। जो निर्गुण, अरूप (निराकार), अलख (अव्यक्त) और अजन्मा है, वही भक्तों के प्रेमवश सगुण हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: There is no difference at all between the manifest and the unmanifest. The sages, the Puranas, the wise, and the Vedas all sing this. The one who is unmanifest, formless, unseen, and unborn becomes manifest through the love of devotees.
essence: Love turns the unseen into presence.
simple_meaning: There is no real split between the formless divine and the visible form. The sages say the formless one appears in form through the love of devotees.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating form and formlessness as opposites to seeing devotion as the bridge between them.
modern_relevance: You feel something holy in a song, a face, or a small ritual at your kitchen counter. What seems invisible is not absent; love gives it shape you can meet.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जो गुन रहित सगुन सोइ कैसें। जलु हिम उपल बिलग नहिं जैसें॥ जासु नाम भ्रम तिमिर पतंगा। तेहि किमि कहिअ बिमोह प्रसंगा ॥
translation: जो निर्गुण है वही सगुण कैसे है? जैसे जल और ओले में भेद नहीं। (दोनों जल ही हैं, ऐसे ही निर्गुण और सगुण एक ही हैं।) जिसका नाम भ्रम रूपी अंधकार के मिटाने के लिए सूर्य है, उसके लिए मोह का प्रसंग भी कैसे कहा जा सकता है? ॥
english_translation: How can the formless be different from the formed? Water and hail are not separate. How can delusion be spoken of for one whose name is the sun that destroys the darkness of confusion?
essence: Ram's form and formlessness are not two different truths.
simple_meaning: The divine can appear with form and still remain beyond form. Ram's name itself removes confusion, so there is no real basis for doubt about his nature.
insight: It shifts the mind from dividing form and essence to seeing them as one reality.
modern_relevance: You are trying to make sense of someone you deeply admire, but your mind keeps splitting them into contradictions. This verse says the split is in your seeing, not in the reality before you.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: राम सच्चिदानंद दिनेसा। नहिं तहँ मोह निसा लवलेसा॥ सहज प्रकासरूप भगवाना। नहिं तहँ पुनि बिग्यान बिहाना ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी सच्चिदानन्दस्वरूप सूर्य हैं। वहाँ मोह रूपी रात्रि का लवलेश भी नहीं है। वे स्वभाव से ही प्रकाश रूप और (षडैश्वर्ययुक्त) भगवान है, वहाँ तो विज्ञान रूपी प्रातःकाल भी नहीं होता (अज्ञान रूपी रात्रि हो तब तो विज्ञान रूपी प्रातःकाल हो, भगवान तो नित्य ज्ञान स्वरूप हैं।) ॥
english_translation: Ram is consciousness, being, and bliss, like the sun. There is not even the slightest darkness of delusion there. He is naturally radiant and the Lord himself; there is no need for dawn of understanding there.
essence: Ram is pure radiance, where confusion cannot even begin.
simple_meaning: Ram is pure awareness and bliss itself. In his presence, delusion has no place, and even the idea of a dawn after darkness does not apply.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating understanding as gradual repair to seeing clarity as a full illumination.
modern_relevance: You sit in the car after a hard conversation, replaying every line, trying to figure out what was real. This verse points to a clarity so complete that confusion cannot survive in it.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: हरष बिषाद ग्यान अग्याना। जीव धर्म अहमिति अभिमाना॥ राम ब्रह्म ब्यापक जग जाना। परमानंद परेस पुराना ॥
translation: हर्ष, शोक, ज्ञान, अज्ञान, अहंता और अभिमान- ये सब जीव के धर्म हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी तो व्यापक ब्रह्म, परमानन्दस्वरूप, परात्पर प्रभु और पुराण पुरुष हैं। इस बात को सारा जगत जानता है ॥
english_translation: Joy and sorrow, knowledge and ignorance, the sense of separate self and pride — these belong to the embodied being. Ram is the all-pervading supreme reality, the bliss beyond all, the ancient supreme lord. Everyone in the world knows this.
essence: Your moods and ego belong to change; Ram belongs to the vast.
simple_meaning: Joy, sorrow, knowledge, ignorance, self-importance, and pride belong to the individual being. Ram is the all-pervading supreme reality, pure bliss, and the ancient supreme lord.
insight: It trains the mind to separate passing mental states from the unchanging ground beneath them.
modern_relevance: You check your phone after a harsh email and feel yourself swing from confidence to shame. The verse says those swings belong to the changing mind, not to the vast reality you rest in.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुरुष प्रसिद्ध प्रकाश निधि प्रगट परावर नाथ। रघुकुलमनि मम स्वामि सोइ कहि सिवँ नायउ माथ ॥
translation: जो (पुराण) पुरुष प्रसिद्ध हैं, प्रकाश के भंडार हैं, सब रूपों में प्रकट हैं, जीव, माया और जगत सबके स्वामी हैं, वे ही रघुकुल मणि श्री रामचन्द्रजी मेरे स्वामी हैं- ऐसा कहकर शिवजी ने उनको मस्तक नवाया ॥
english_translation: Saying, "He is the famed Person, the storehouse of light, manifest in all forms, the lord of all beyond and within. He, the jewel of Raghu's line, is my master," Shiva bowed his head.
essence: True seeing ends in bowing.
simple_meaning: Shiva identifies Ram as the supreme master, the source of light, and bows in reverence.
insight: It shifts the mind from intellectual description to lived reverence.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm changes the whole room, and your ego softens without argument. Recognition turns into respect before you even plan it.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: निज भ्रम नहिं समुझहिं अग्यानी। प्रभु पर मोह धरहिं जड़ प्रानी॥ जथा गगन घन पटल निहारी। झाँपेउ भानु कहहिं कुबिचारी ॥
translation: अज्ञानी मनुष्य अपने भ्रम को तो समझते नहीं और वे मूर्ख प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी पर उसका आरोप करते हैं, जैसे आकाश में बादलों का परदा देखकर कुविचारी (अज्ञानी) लोग कहते हैं कि बादलों ने सूर्य को ढँक लिया ॥
english_translation: Ignorant people do not understand their own confusion. Deluded beings blame the divine, just as foolish people see clouds in the sky and say the sun has been covered.
essence: Confusion blames the divine for what it cannot see.
simple_meaning: People who are confused do not see their own confusion. Instead, they blame Ram, like someone who mistakes clouds for the sun being gone.
insight: It shifts blame inward first: check your perception before judging what you see.
modern_relevance: You read a message in a bad mood and decide the other person is cold. Later you realise your own fear was doing the talking. The verse points to that mistake before it hardens into blame.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: चितव जो लोचन अंगुलि लाएँ। प्रगट जुगल ससि तेहि के भाएँ॥ उमा राम बिषइक अस मोहा। नभ तम धूम धूरि जिमि सोहा ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य आँख में अँगुली लगाकर देखता है, उसके लिए तो दो चन्द्रमा प्रकट (प्रत्यक्ष) हैं। हे पार्वती! श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विषय में इस प्रकार मोह की कल्पना करना वैसा ही है, जैसा आकाश में अंधकार, धुएँ और धूल का सोहना (दिखना)। (आकाश जैसे निर्मल और निर्लेप है, उसको कोई मलिन या स्पर्श नहीं कर सकता, इसी प्रकार भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी नित्य निर्मल और निर्लेप हैं।) ॥
english_translation: If a person looks with a finger in the eye, two moons seem visible. O Uma, imagining such delusion about Ram is like seeing darkness, smoke, and dust in the sky.
essence: Confusion distorts vision; Ram's purity is never the problem.
simple_meaning: A confused mind can project impurity onto Ram, just as an eye pressed by a finger can see two moons. Ram is never actually stained.
insight: It shifts attention from judging the object to examining the lens that is judging it.
modern_relevance: You read one harsh comment and suddenly the whole person looks corrupt. The distortion may be in your own hurt, not in what they truly are.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: बिषय करन सुर जीव समेता। सकल एक तें एक सचेता॥ सब कर परम प्रकासक जोई। राम अनादि अवधपति सोई ॥
translation: विषय, इन्द्रियाँ, इन्द्रियों के देवता और जीवात्मा- ये सब एक की सहायता से एक चेतन होते हैं। (अर्थात विषयों का प्रकाश इन्द्रियों से, इन्द्रियों का इन्द्रियों के देवताओं से और इन्द्रिय देवताओं का चेतन जीवात्मा से प्रकाश होता है।) इन सबका जो परम प्रकाशक है (अर्थात जिससे इन सबका प्रकाश होता है), वही अनादि ब्रह्म अयोध्या नरेश श्री रामचन्द्रजी हैं ॥
english_translation: The objects of sense, the senses, the presiding beings of the senses, and the individual being all become conscious through one source. The supreme illuminator of all is that same beginningless Ram, lord of Ayodhya.
essence: All awareness shines because Ram is already shining through it.
simple_meaning: Everything in experience depends on one supreme source for its awareness and existence. Ram is that beginningless source of all light.
insight: It shifts attention from fragmented experience to the single reality that makes experience possible.
modern_relevance: You are staring at three screens, a buzzing phone, and a mind split in ten directions. The verse cuts through the noise: every bit of awareness you have is borrowed from a deeper source.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जगत प्रकास्य प्रकासक रामू। मायाधीस ग्यान गुन धामू॥ जासु सत्यता तें जड़ माया। भास सत्य इव मोह सहाया ॥
translation: यह जगत प्रकाश्य है और श्री रामचन्द्रजी इसके प्रकाशक हैं। वे माया के स्वामी और ज्ञान तथा गुणों के धाम हैं। जिनकी सत्ता से, मोह की सहायता पाकर जड़ माया भी सत्य सी भासित होती है ॥
english_translation: Ram is the light that reveals the world. He is the master of maya and the source of knowledge and qualities. By his reality, inert maya appears real through the help of delusion.
essence: Ram is the light that makes even illusion seem real.
simple_meaning: Ram is the light that makes the world visible. He rules maya and is the source of knowledge and good qualities. Even illusion seems real only because of his reality.
insight: It shifts attention from appearances to the source that makes appearances possible.
modern_relevance: You stare at a message thread and build a whole story from three words. Later, you realize you were reacting to your own projection. This verse points to the light behind the projection.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: रजत सीप महुँ भास जिमि जथा भानु कर बारि। जदपि मृषा तिहुँ काल सोइ भ्रम न सकइ कोउ टारि ॥
translation: जैसे सीप में चाँदी की और सूर्य की किरणों में पानी की (बिना हुए भी) प्रतीति होती है। यद्यपि यह प्रतीति तीनों कालों में झूठ है, तथापि इस भ्रम को कोई हटा नहीं सकता ॥
english_translation: As silver appears in mother-of-pearl and water appears in sunbeams, so the unreal appears real. Though false in all three times, no one can remove that illusion.
essence: False appearance can feel real even after it is disproved.
simple_meaning: What seems real can be only an illusion, like silver seen in shell or water seen in sunlight. Even knowing it is false, the mind may still not let go of the mistake.
insight: It trains the reader to question appearances and notice how perception can mistake one thing for another.
modern_relevance: You double-check the message, know the rumor is baseless, and still feel your stomach tighten. The mind can keep projecting what is not there.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: एहि बिधि जग हरि आश्रित रहई। जदपि असत्य देत दुख अहई॥ जौं सपनें सिर काटै कोई। बिनु जागें न दूरि दुख होई ॥
translation: इसी तरह यह संसार भगवान के आश्रित रहता है। यद्यपि यह असत्य है, तो भी दुःख तो देता ही है, जिस तरह स्वप्न में कोई सिर काट ले तो बिना जागे वह दुःख दूर नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: In this way, the world remains dependent on Hari. Though unreal, it still causes suffering, just as if someone cuts off a head in a dream, the pain does not end until waking.
essence: Illusion can hurt until awareness wakes up.
simple_meaning: The world may not be ultimately real, but it still produces suffering. Like a dream injury, its pain lasts until awareness changes.
insight: It shifts attention from arguing with appearances to seeing how the mind manufactures suffering from them.
modern_relevance: You replay a humiliating message in bed at 2 a.m., and your chest still tightens even though the moment is over. The event passed, but the mind kept it alive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जासु कृपाँ अस भ्रम मिटि जाई। गिरिजा सोइ कृपाल रघुराई॥ आदि अंत कोउ जासु न पावा। मति अनुमानि निगम अस गावा ॥
translation: हे पार्वती! जिनकी कृपा से इस प्रकार का भ्रम मिट जाता है, वही कृपालु श्री रघुनाथजी हैं। जिनका आदि और अंत किसी ने नहीं (जान) पाया। वेदों ने अपनी बुद्धि से अनुमान करके इस प्रकार (नीचे लिखे अनुसार) गाया है- ॥
english_translation: O Girija, the compassionate Raghunath alone is the one whose grace removes such confusion. No one has found his beginning or end. The Vedas sing of him by reasoning and inference.
essence: Grace clears confusion; the supreme reality remains beyond full measure.
simple_meaning: Ram's grace clears confusion. His beginning and end cannot be found, and even the Vedas describe him only through reasoned hints.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to master the ultimate with logic alone to receiving understanding through a clearer state of mind.
modern_relevance: You keep rereading the same paragraph, sure the answer should finally click. Then a calmer mind sees what effort missed: some things are understood only when confusion falls away.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: बिनु पद चलइ सुनइ बिनु काना। कर बिनु करम करइ बिधि नाना॥ आनन रहित सकल रस भोगी। बिनु बानी बकता बड़ जोगी ॥
translation: वह (ब्रह्म) बिना ही पैर के चलता है, बिना ही कान के सुनता है, बिना ही हाथ के नाना प्रकार के काम करता है, बिना मुँह (जिव्हा) के ही सारे (छहों) रसों का आनंद लेता है और बिना ही वाणी के बहुत योग्य वक्ता है ॥
english_translation: Without feet, it walks; without ears, it hears. Without hands, it performs countless acts. Without a mouth, it enjoys every flavor. Without speech, it is a great speaker.
essence: The supreme reality acts freely without needing a body.
simple_meaning: The supreme reality is beyond physical limits. It acts, hears, sees, enjoys, and speaks without needing a body like ours.
insight: It shifts the mind from physical limitation to divine freedom.
modern_relevance: A child asks how you can know someone who is far away. You answer with presence, not hardware. The deepest reality does not need a body to be fully active.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तन बिनु परस नयन बिनु देखा। ग्रहइ घ्रान बिनु बास असेषा॥ असि सब भाँति अलौकिक करनी। महिमा जासु जाइ नहिं बरनी ॥
translation: वह बिना ही शरीर (त्वचा) के स्पर्श करता है, बिना ही आँखों के देखता है और बिना ही नाक के सब गंधों को ग्रहण करता है (सूँघता है)। उस ब्रह्म की करनी सभी प्रकार से ऐसी अलौकिक है कि जिसकी महिमा कही नहीं जा सकती ॥
english_translation: He touches without a body, sees without eyes, and perceives every scent without a nose. In every way, that supreme reality acts in a way beyond the ordinary, and its greatness cannot be described.
essence: The supreme reality works beyond every human limit.
simple_meaning: The supreme reality is not limited by a body or senses. It can perceive and act in ways ordinary beings cannot understand or describe.
insight: It shifts the mind from literal expectation to reverent recognition of what exceeds ordinary form.
modern_relevance: You try to explain a person you love, but words keep falling short. Some realities cannot be boxed into ordinary categories — they are known by their effect, not by measurement.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: जेहि इमि गावहिं बेद बुध जाहि धरहिं मुनि ध्यान। सोइ दसरथ सुत भगत हित कोसलपति भगवान ॥
translation: जिसका वेद और पंडित इस प्रकार वर्णन करते हैं और मुनि जिसका ध्यान धरते हैं, वही दशरथनंदन, भक्तों के हितकारी, अयोध्या के स्वामी भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी हैं ॥
english_translation: The one whom the Vedas and the wise describe, and whom sages meditate upon, is the same Ram, son of Dasharath, friend of devotees, and Lord of Kosala.
essence: The highest reality is the same Ram who protects devotees.
simple_meaning: The Vedas and wise teachers speak of Ram, and sages meditate on him. He is Dasharath's son, the protector of devotees, and the lord of Kosala.
insight: It shifts the mind from abstract divinity to a personal, approachable presence that can be loved and trusted.
modern_relevance: You hear a hymn in a temple, then see a father carrying his sleeping child home through the rain. The same greatness can be intimate, near, and protective.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कासीं मरत जंतु अवलोकी। जासु नाम बल करउँ बिसोकी॥ सोइ प्रभु मोर चराचर स्वामी। रघुबर सब उर अंतरजामी ॥
translation: (हे पार्वती !) जिनके नाम के बल से काशी में मरते हुए प्राणी को देखकर मैं उसे (राम मंत्र देकर) शोकरहित कर देता हूँ (मुक्त कर देता हूँ), वही मेरे प्रभु रघुश्रेष्ठ श्री रामचन्द्रजी जड़-चेतन के स्वामी और सबके हृदय के भीतर की जानने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: O Parvati, seeing a being dying in Kashi, I free it from sorrow by the power of whose name. That same Lord is my master of all moving and unmoving beings, Raghu's श्रेष्ठ, the indweller in every heart.
essence: Ram's name reaches where fear and death cannot.
simple_meaning: Shiva says Ram's name has such power that it can free a dying being from sorrow. He calls Ram the master of all beings and the indweller of every heart.
insight: It shifts devotion from ritual performance to inward reliance on Ram's name and presence.
modern_relevance: At a hospital bedside, words fail and everyone grows quiet. In that moment, this verse says the deepest help is not control but a name, a presence, and trust that reaches beyond fear.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: बिबसहुँ जासु नाम नर कहहीं। जनम अनेक रचित अघ दहहीं॥ सादर सुमिरन जे नर करहीं। भव बारिधि गोपद इव तरहीं ॥
translation: विवश होकर (बिना इच्छा के) भी जिनका नाम लेने से मनुष्यों के अनेक जन्मों में किए हुए पाप जल जाते हैं। फिर जो मनुष्य आदरपूर्वक उनका स्मरण करते हैं, वे तो संसार रूपी (दुस्तर) समुद्र को गाय के खुर से बने हुए गड्ढे के समान (अर्थात बिना किसी परिश्रम के) पार कर जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Even without intention, people speak that name, and sins from many births burn away. Those who remember that name with reverence cross the ocean of becoming as easily as a cow's hoofprint.
essence: Ram's name turns burden into passage.
simple_meaning: Even saying Ram's name can burn away the burden of past wrongs. Remembering Him with reverence carries a person across the cycle of suffering with ease.
insight: It shifts attention from self-improvement alone to the transforming power of devoted remembrance.
modern_relevance: You are half-distracted, whispering a prayer before a hard phone call. Nothing around you has changed, yet your chest loosens. That is the power this verse points to: remembrance can move you before circumstances do.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम सो परमातमा भवानी। तहँ भ्रम अति अबिहित तव बानी॥ अस संसय आनत उर माहीं। ग्यान बिराग सकल गुन जाहीं ॥
translation: हे पार्वती! वही परमात्मा श्री रामचन्द्रजी हैं। उनमें भ्रम (देखने में आता) है, तुम्हारा ऐसा कहना अत्यन्त ही अनुचित है। इस प्रकार का संदेह मन में लाते ही मनुष्य के ज्ञान, वैराग्य आदि सारे सद्गुण नष्ट हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Bhavani, Ram is the supreme reality. To see confusion in him is utterly improper. Once doubt enters the heart, wisdom, detachment, and every noble quality are destroyed.
essence: Doubt about Ram destroys the very qualities needed to know him.
simple_meaning: Ram is the supreme reality, and doubting him is a serious mistake. Doubt does not stay small; it weakens wisdom, detachment, and every good quality.
insight: It shifts the mind from entertaining suspicion to protecting clear understanding.
modern_relevance: You hear one cynical comment about someone you trust, and suddenly your whole mind starts rearranging the story. This verse warns how quickly doubt can poison clarity, restraint, and steadiness.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सुनि सिव के भ्रम भंजन बचना। मिटि गै सब कुतरक कै रचना॥ भइ रघुपति पद प्रीति प्रतीती। दारुन असंभावना बीती ॥
translation: शिवजी के भ्रमनाशक वचनों को सुनकर पार्वतीजी के सब कुतर्कों की रचना मिट गई। श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों में उनका प्रेम और विश्वास हो गया और कठिन असम्भावना (जिसका होना- सम्भव नहीं, ऐसी मिथ्या कल्पना) जाती रही! ॥
english_translation: Hearing Shiva’s words that shattered doubt, all of Parvati’s twisted arguments vanished. Her love and trust in the feet of Raghupati arose, and the impossible doubt was gone.
essence: Doubt falls away when trust in Ram takes root.
simple_meaning: Parvati hears Shiva’s clear words and her doubts disappear. Love and trust in Ram replace confusion.
insight: It shifts the mind from suspicion to trust by showing that clarity can dissolve overthinking.
modern_relevance: You’ve argued yourself into a corner at 1:13 a.m., rereading the same message and making the worst-case story bigger. Then one honest sentence from someone you trust cuts through it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि पुनि प्रभु पद कमल गहि जोरि पंकरुह पानि। बोलीं गिरिजा बचन बर मनहुँ प्रेम रस सानि ॥
translation: बार- बार स्वामी (शिवजी) के चरणकमलों को पकड़कर और अपने कमल के समान हाथों को जोड़कर पार्वतीजी मानो प्रेमरस में सानकर सुंदर वचन बोलीं ॥
english_translation: Again and again, holding the Lord's lotus feet and folding her lotus-like hands, Girija spoke beautiful words, as if mixed with the nectar of love.
essence: Love turns surrender into beautiful speech.
simple_meaning: Parvati, moved by love, bows again and again to Shiva and speaks with a heart softened by devotion.
insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to reverent listening.
modern_relevance: After a hard conversation, you finally realize the other person was right. Your shoulders drop, your hands unclench, and gratitude replaces the urge to argue.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: ससि कर सम सुनि गिरा तुम्हारी। मिटा मोह सरदातप भारी॥ तुम्ह कृपाल सबु संसउ हरेऊ। राम स्वरूप जानि मोहि परेऊ ॥
translation: आपकी चन्द्रमा की किरणों के समान शीतल वाणी सुनकर मेरा अज्ञान रूपी शरद-ऋतु (क्वार) की धूप का भारी ताप मिट गया। हे कृपालु! आपने मेरा सब संदेह हर लिया, अब श्री रामचन्द्रजी का यथार्थ स्वरूप मेरी समझ में आ गया ॥
english_translation: Hearing your speech, clear as moonbeams, the heavy heat of autumn confusion has vanished. O compassionate one, you have removed all doubt; now I understand the true form of Ram.
essence: Compassionate words can dissolve confusion and reveal Ram clearly.
simple_meaning: Parvati says Shiva's gentle words have removed her confusion and doubts. She now understands Ram more clearly.
insight: It shifts the mind from suspicion to clear seeing, where doubt no longer rules the heart.
modern_relevance: You finally talk to someone who explains the thing you've been circling for weeks. The tension drops, and what felt tangled suddenly looks simple.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: नाथ कृपाँ अब गयउ बिषादा। सुखी भयउँ प्रभु चरन प्रसादा॥ अब मोहि आपनि किंकरि जानी। जदपि सहज जड़ नारि अयानी ॥
translation: हे नाथ! आपकी कृपा से अब मेरा विषाद जाता रहा और आपके चरणों के अनुग्रह से मैं सुखी हो गई। यद्यपि मैं स्त्री होने के कारण स्वभाव से ही मूर्ख और ज्ञानहीन हूँ, तो भी अब आप मुझे अपनी दासी जानकर- ॥
english_translation: By your grace, O Lord, my sorrow is gone, and by the favor of your feet I have become joyful. Though I am naturally dull and ignorant, still know me as your servant.
essence: True relief begins when the heart stops defending itself.
simple_meaning: Parvati says her sorrow has ended through Shiva's grace, and she asks to be accepted as his servant despite her own limitations.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to humble belonging.
modern_relevance: After a long argument, you finally stop defending yourself and say, 'I hear you. I want to come back.' That softening is the real turning point.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: प्रथम जो मैं पूछा सोइ कहहू। जौं मो पर प्रसन्न प्रभु अहहू॥ राम ब्रह्म चिनमय अबिनासी। सर्ब रहित सब उर पुर बासी ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! यदि आप मुझ पर प्रसन्न हैं, तो जो बात मैंने पहले आपसे पूछी थी, वही कहिए। (यह सत्य है कि) श्री रामचन्द्रजी ब्रह्म हैं, चिन्मय (ज्ञानस्वरूप) हैं, अविनाशी हैं, सबसे रहित और सबके हृदय रूपी नगरी में निवास करने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: O Lord, if you are pleased with me, then tell me again the question I asked before. Ram is Brahman, consciousness itself, imperishable, beyond all, and dwelling in every heart-city.
essence: Ram is the imperishable presence dwelling in every heart.
simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to repeat her earlier question, then states that Ram is the supreme reality: conscious, imperishable, beyond all limits, and present in every heart.
insight: It shifts the mind from asking about events to recognising Ram’s all-pervading nature.
modern_relevance: You finally feel calm after a long talk, then realise the real question is still waiting underneath. What is this presence you keep turning toward, and why does it feel so intimate?
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: नाथ धरेउ नरतनु केहि हेतू। मोहि समुझाइ कहहु बृषकेतू॥ उमा बचन सुनि परम बिनीता। रामकथा पर प्रीति पुनीता ॥
translation: फिर हे नाथ! उन्होंने मनुष्य का शरीर किस कारण से धारण किया? हे धर्म की ध्वजा धारण करने वाले प्रभो! यह मुझे समझाकर कहिए। पार्वती के अत्यन्त नम्र वचन सुनकर और श्री रामचन्द्रजी की कथा में उनका विशुद्ध प्रेम देखकर- ॥
english_translation: Then, O Lord, why did you take a human body? O bearer of the bull-banner, explain this to me. Hearing Parvati's very humble words and seeing her pure love for Ram's story—
essence: Sincere wonder opens the door to deeper understanding.
simple_meaning: Parvati asks why the divine took a human form and asks Shiva to explain it clearly. Her humility and pure love for Ram's story deepen the question.
insight: It shifts the mind from accepting the surface story to asking for the purpose beneath it.
modern_relevance: You hear a story about someone extraordinary, and one question keeps returning: why would greatness choose limitation? That honest curiosity is where understanding starts.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: हियँ हरषे कामारि तब संकर सहज सुजान। बहु बिधि उमहि प्रसंसि पुनि बोले कृपानिधान ॥
translation: तब कामदेव के शत्रु, स्वाभाविक ही सुजान, कृपा निधान शिवजी मन में बहुत ही हर्षित हुए और बहुत प्रकार से पार्वती की बड़ाई करके फिर बोले- ॥
english_translation: Then Shiva, enemy of desire and naturally wise, was filled with joy in his heart. Praising Parvati in many ways, the treasure of compassion spoke again.
essence: Devoted questioning draws out a fuller teaching.
simple_meaning: Shiva feels delighted, praises Parvati, and then continues speaking.
insight: It shows that reverent listening itself prepares the mind for truth.
modern_relevance: A mentor sees you are finally ready to hear the hard answer. Before the lesson comes, there is a moment of recognition: yes, you are asking the right question.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सुनु सुभ कथा भवानि रामचरितमानस बिमल। कहा भुसुंडि बखानि सुना बिहग नायक गरुड़ ॥
translation: हे पार्वती! निर्मल रामचरितमानस की वह मंगलमयी कथा सुनो जिसे काकभुशुण्डि ने विस्तार से कहा और पक्षियों के राजा गरुड़जी ने सुना था ॥
english_translation: O Parvati, listen to the pure Ramcharitmanas, the auspicious story that Bhushundi narrated and Garuda heard, lord of birds.
essence: A pure story is itself a blessing before its meaning arrives.
simple_meaning: Shiva invites Parvati to hear the pure and auspicious Ram story, told by Bhushundi and heard by Garuda.
insight: It shifts the reader from casual listening to reverent reception.
modern_relevance: Someone lowers their voice and says, 'Listen to this one carefully.' Before the details even begin, you feel that what follows is meant to cleanse attention, not just entertain it.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सो संबाद उदार जेहि बिधि भा आगें कहब। सुनहु राम अवतार चरति परम सुंदर अनघ ॥
translation: वह श्रेष्ठ संवाद जिस प्रकार हुआ, वह मैं आगे कहूँगा। अभी तुम श्री रामचन्द्रजी के अवतार का परम सुंदर और पवित्र (पापनाशक) चरित्र सुनो ॥
english_translation: I will tell that noble dialogue later, as it happened. First, listen to the most beautiful and pure story of Ram's incarnation.
essence: The main story must be heard before the explanation arrives.
simple_meaning: Shiva pauses the story and tells Parvati that he will explain the earlier dialogue later. For now, he asks her to listen to the beautiful, pure account of Ram's incarnation.
insight: It teaches you to receive the central truth first, before getting lost in side details.
modern_relevance: A friend starts telling you a story, then stops and says, “Wait — first hear the main event.” That pause matters: it tells you what deserves your full attention before the details arrive.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: हरि गुन नाम अपार कथा रूप अगनित अमित। मैं निज मति अनुसार कहउँ उमा सादर सुनहु ॥
translation: श्री हरि के गुण, मान, कथा और रूप सभी अपार, अगणित और असीम हैं। फिर भी हे पार्वती! मैं अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार कहता हूँ, तुम आदरपूर्वक सुनो ॥
english_translation: The divine's qualities, names, stories, and forms are endless and immeasurable. Still, O Parvati, I speak according to my own understanding; listen with reverence.
essence: The divine is too vast for complete speech; humility is the right beginning.
simple_meaning: Ram's qualities, names, stories, and forms cannot be fully counted. The speaker can only offer a humble account and asks Parvati to listen respectfully.
insight: It shifts the reader from mastering the divine with words to approaching it with humility and reverence.
modern_relevance: You try to explain someone you love deeply, and every sentence feels too small. The heart knows more than language can hold, so you speak carefully and with respect.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सुनु गिरिजा हरिचरित सुहाए। बिपुल बिसद निगमागम गाए॥ हरि अवतार हेतु जेहि होई। इदमित्थं कहि जाइ न सोई ॥
translation: हे पार्वती! सुनो, वेद-शास्त्रों ने श्री हरि के सुंदर, विस्तृत और निर्मल चरित्रों का गान किया है। हरि का अवतार जिस कारण से होता है, वह कारण 'बस यही है' ऐसा नहीं कहा जा सकता (अनेकों कारण हो सकते हैं और ऐसे भी हो सकते हैं, जिन्हें कोई जान ही नहीं सकता) ॥
english_translation: O Girija, listen to the lovely deeds of Hari. The Vedas and scriptures sing them in many clear ways. The cause for Hari's incarnation cannot be stated as only this and nothing else.
essence: Ram's coming cannot be trapped in one explanation.
simple_meaning: The sacred texts praise Ram's beautiful deeds in many ways, and no single explanation can fully capture why he comes into the world.
insight: It trains the mind to stop forcing sacred or complex events into a single explanation.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to reduce a life-changing choice to one clean reason — a job move, a breakup, a sudden return to prayer. Some things are bigger than the story you can tell about them.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: राम अतर्क्य बुद्धि मन बानी। मत हमार अस सुनहि सयानी॥ तदपि संत मुनि बेद पुराना। जस कछु कहहिं स्वमति अनुमाना ॥
translation: हे सयानी! सुनो, हमारा मत तो यह है कि बुद्धि, मन और वाणी से श्री रामचन्द्रजी की तर्कना नहीं की जा सकती। तथापि संत, मुनि, वेद और पुराण अपनी-अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार जैसा कुछ कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: O wise one, know this: Ram cannot be grasped by intellect, mind, or speech. Yet saints, sages, the Vedas, and the Puranas speak as best they can, each from its own understanding.
essence: Ram stands beyond thought, while every description remains partial.
simple_meaning: Ram cannot be fully captured by thinking, feeling, or speaking. Even the saints and scriptures can only describe him from their own limited understanding.
insight: It shifts the mind from total explanation to reverent humility before what cannot be reduced.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to explain a loss, a love, or a calling in perfect words, and every sentence falls short. Some realities are bigger than the language you bring to them.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: तस मैं सुमुखि सुनावउँ तोही। समुझि परइ जस कारन मोही॥ जब जब होई धरम कै हानी। बाढ़हिं असुर अधम अभिमानी ॥
translation: और जैसा कुछ मेरी समझ में आता है, हे सुमुखि! वही कारण मैं तुमको सुनाता हूँ। जब-जब धर्म का ह्रास होता है और नीच अभिमानी राक्षस बढ़ जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: And as far as I understand, O gentle one, I will tell you that reason. Whenever dharma declines and low, arrogant beings grow strong...
essence: The divine appears when dharma breaks down.
simple_meaning: Shiva begins explaining why Ram appears in the world: whenever righteousness declines and arrogant forces rise, the divine comes to restore balance.
insight: It shifts attention from despair over decline to confidence that renewal answers moral collapse.
modern_relevance: When a workplace turns toxic and cruelty starts looking normal, it can feel like decency has lost. This verse says that collapse is often the very moment restoration begins.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: करहिं अनीति जाइ नहिं बरनी। सीदहिं बिप्र धेनु सुर धरनी॥ तब तब प्रभु धरि बिबिध सरीरा। हरहिं कृपानिधि सज्जन पीरा ॥
translation: और वे ऐसा अन्याय करते हैं कि जिसका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता तथा ब्राह्मण, गो, देवता और पृथ्वी कष्ट पाते हैं, तब-तब वे कृपानिधान प्रभु भाँति-भाँति के (दिव्य) शरीर धारण कर सज्जनों की पीड़ा हरते हैं ॥
english_translation: They commit injustice beyond description, and priests, cows, the radiant beings, and the earth suffer. Then and again, the Lord takes many forms and removes the suffering of the good.
essence: Ram appears wherever injustice makes the good suffer.
simple_meaning: When injustice becomes unbearable and the good suffer, Ram takes different forms to remove their pain.
insight: It shifts the mind from helplessness to trust that right action can reappear when needed most.
modern_relevance: When cruelty spreads and decent people feel cornered, it can seem like no help is coming. This verse answers that despair with a larger trust: protection may arrive in unexpected forms.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: असुर मारि थापहिं सुरन्ह राखहिं निज श्रुति सेतु। जग बिस्तारहिं बिसद जस राम जन्म कर हेतु ॥
translation: वे असुरों को मारकर देवताओं को स्थापित करते हैं, अपने (श्वास रूप) वेदों की मर्यादा की रक्षा करते हैं और जगत में अपना निर्मल यश फैलाते हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के अवतार का यह कारण है ॥
english_translation: They destroy the asuras, establish the radiant beings, protect the order of the Vedas, and spread their pure fame through the world. This is the reason for Ram's birth.
essence: Ram comes to restore order, protect dharma, and remove what distorts the world.
simple_meaning: Ram appears to remove destructive forces, restore righteous order, protect sacred teaching, and spread his pure fame across the world.
insight: It shifts attention from Ram's birth as a miracle to Ram's birth as purposeful restoration.
modern_relevance: When a family system is breaking down and one person finally steps in to protect what is right, the goal is not applause. The real work is restoring order, defending the vulnerable, and setting a standard others can trust.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सोइ जस गाइ भगत भव तरहीं। कृपासिंधु जन हित तनु धरहीं॥ राम जनम के हेतु अनेका। परम बिचित्र एक तें एका ॥
translation: उसी यश को गा-गाकर भक्तजन भवसागर से तर जाते हैं। कृपासागर भगवान भक्तों के हित के लिए शरीर धारण करते हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के जन्म लेने के अनेक कारण हैं, जो एक से एक बढ़कर विचित्र हैं ॥
english_translation: By singing that glory, devotees cross beyond the cycle of reactivity. The ocean of mercy takes form for the good of his people. Ram's birth has many causes, each stranger than the last.
essence: Ram's glory carries devotees across suffering, and his birth serves mercy.
simple_meaning: Devotees cross beyond suffering by singing Ram's glory. Ram takes form out of mercy for the good of his people, and his birth has many wondrous reasons.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating devotion as ornament to seeing it as a way across suffering.
modern_relevance: You are exhausted, but you still hum the name of what steadies you on the train home. The act is small; the shift is not. Recalling the beloved can carry you through what raw effort cannot.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जनम एक दुइ कहउँ बखानी। सावधान सुनु सुमति भवानी॥ द्वारपाल हरि के प्रिय दोऊ। जय अरु बिजय जान सब कोऊ ॥
translation: हे सुंदर बुद्धि वाली भवानी! मैं उनके दो-एक जन्मों का विस्तार से वर्णन करता हूँ, तुम सावधान होकर सुनो। श्री हरि के जय और विजय दो प्यारे द्वारपाल हैं, जिनको सब कोई जानते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Bhavani, beautiful in wisdom, I will describe one or two of their births in detail; listen carefully. Jay and Vijay are the two beloved gatekeepers of Hari, and everyone knows them.
essence: Even a brief beginning can hide a much larger sacred story.
simple_meaning: Shiva tells Parvati to listen carefully as he begins the story of Hari's two beloved gatekeepers, Jay and Vijay, whose births he will explain.
insight: It shifts attention from the surface event to the hidden backstory that gives it meaning.
modern_relevance: Someone starts a long family story with, “Listen carefully, this matters.” You lean in, because the smallest detail may explain a wound, a pattern, or a destiny-shaped turn.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: बिप्र श्राप तें दूनउ भाई। तामस असुर देह तिन्ह पाई॥ कनककसिपु अरु हाटकलोचन। जगत बिदित सुरपति मद मोचन ॥
translation: उन दोनों भाइयों ने ब्राह्मण (सनकादि) के शाप से असुरों का तामसी शरीर पाया। एक का नाम था हिरण्यकशिपु और दूसरे का हिरण्याक्ष। ये देवराज इन्द्र के गर्व को छुड़ाने वाले सारे जगत में प्रसिद्ध हुए ॥
english_translation: By the curse of the brahmins, the two brothers received bodies of darkness as asuras. One was Hiranyakashipu and the other Hiranyaksha, known throughout the world as the removers of Indra's pride.
essence: Pride can make someone famous, but it also prepares the fall.
simple_meaning: The two brothers were born with dark asura bodies because of a brahmin's curse. They became famous across the world for humbling Indra's pride.
insight: It shifts attention from surface greatness to the karmic force that eventually corrects inflated ego.
modern_relevance: A person who has built their whole identity on status can feel untouchable for years. Then one blunt failure exposes the arrogance underneath and changes the whole story.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिजई समर बीर बिख्याता। धरि बराह बपु एक निपाता॥ होइ नरहरि दूसर पुनि मारा। जन प्रहलाद सुजस बिस्तारा ॥
translation: वे युद्ध में विजय पाने वाले विख्यात वीर थे। इनमें से एक (हिरण्याक्ष) को भगवान ने वराह (सूअर) का शरीर धारण करके मारा, फिर दूसरे (हिरण्यकशिपु) का नरसिंह रूप धारण करके वध किया और अपने भक्त प्रह्लाद का सुंदर यश फैलाया ॥
english_translation: They were famous warriors, victorious in battle. One was slain when the divine took the form of Varaha; then the other was killed when the divine appeared as Narasimha, and the glory of Prahlad spread beautifully.
essence: Pride falls, while devotion keeps its name alive.
simple_meaning: Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakashipu were powerful enemies, but the divine destroyed them in two different forms and made Prahlad's devotion famous.
insight: It shifts attention from brute strength to the moral law that outlives it.
modern_relevance: A person can dominate a room, a company, even a whole family, and still be undone by arrogance. What remains remembered is not force, but the goodness that survives it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भए निसाचर जाइ तेइ महाबीर बलवान। कुंभकरन रावन सुभट सुर बिजई जग जान ॥
translation: वे ही (दोनों) जाकर देवताओं को जीतने वाले तथा बड़े योद्धा, रावण और कुम्भकर्ण नामक बड़े बलवान और महावीर राक्षस हुए, जिन्हें सारा जगत जानता है ॥
english_translation: They became the mighty, powerful demons who conquered the radiant beings: Kumbhakarna and Ravana, the world knows them as great warriors.
essence: Great power can still belong to a mind ruled by pride.
simple_meaning: Those same two brothers were born again as the powerful demon kings Kumbhakarna and Ravana, known everywhere for their strength and victories.
insight: It shifts attention from outward success to the deeper character that drives it.
modern_relevance: A person can become famous for strength, wins, and dominance, yet still be trapped by the same pride underneath. Public victory does not mean inner freedom.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुकुत न भए हते भगवाना। तीनि जनम द्विज बचन प्रवाना॥ एक बार तिन्ह के हित लागी। धरेउ सरीर भगत अनुरागी ॥
translation: भगवान के द्वारा मारे जाने पर भी वे (हिरण्याक्ष और हिरण्यकशिपु) इसीलिए मुक्त नहीं हुए कि ब्राह्मण के वचन (शाप) का प्रमाण तीन जन्म के लिए था। अतः एक बार उनके कल्याण के लिए भक्तप्रेमी भगवान ने फिर अवतार लिया ॥
english_translation: Even when slain by the divine, they were not freed, because the Brahmin's words bound them to three births. For their welfare, the devotee-loving divine took form again.
essence: Mercy keeps returning until even the bound are reached.
simple_meaning: Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakashipu were not freed just because the divine killed them. A Brahmin's curse kept them bound to three births, so the divine returned for their welfare.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing divine action as punishment to seeing it as patient rescue.
modern_relevance: You think one harsh consequence will finally end a pattern, but it doesn't. Some people need repeated chances, and the deepest care keeps returning even after failure.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कस्यप अदिति तहाँ पितु माता। दसरथ कौसल्या बिख्याता॥ एक कलप एहि बिधि अवतारा। चरित पवित्र किए संसारा ॥
translation: वहाँ (उस अवतार में) कश्यप और अदिति उनके माता-पिता हुए, जो दशरथ और कौसल्या के नाम से प्रसिद्ध थे। एक कल्प में इस प्रकार अवतार लेकर उन्होंने संसार में पवित्र लीलाएँ कीं ॥
english_translation: There, Kashyapa and Aditi were the father and mother, known as Dasharatha and Kaushalya. In one cosmic age, he descended in this way and made the world pure through his sacred deeds.
essence: Divinity takes birth in a human family and sanctifies the world.
simple_meaning: Ram's divine birth is described as a descent of Kashyapa and Aditi as Dasharatha and Kaushalya. His life purified the world through sacred deeds.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary biography to sacred presence entering human history.
modern_relevance: A child is born in a quiet hospital room, yet the whole family feels changed. Some arrivals do not just join a home — they cleanse it, reorder it, and make everyone around them more upright.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक कलप सुर देखि दुखारे। समर जलंधर सन सब हारे॥ संभु कीन्ह संग्राम अपारा। दनुज महाबल मरइ न मारा ॥
translation: एक कल्प में सब देवताओं को जलन्धर दैत्य से युद्ध में हार जाने के कारण दुःखी देखकर शिवजी ने उसके साथ बड़ा घोर युद्ध किया, पर वह महाबली दैत्य मारे नहीं मरता था ॥
english_translation: In one age, seeing the radiant beings distressed because all had been defeated by Jalandhar in battle, Shiva fought a fierce war with him. But the powerful demon could not be slain.
essence: Raw power still fails against what cannot yet be ended.
simple_meaning: The radiant beings were defeated by Jalandhar, so Shiva fought him in a terrible battle, but Jalandhar could not be killed.
insight: It shifts attention from heroic effort to the limits of force when ego is deeply entrenched.
modern_relevance: You’ve done everything you can, but the problem still stands there, unchanged. Some conflicts cannot be solved by force alone; they need a deeper opening.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परम सती असुराधिप नारी। तेहिं बल ताहि न जितहिं पुरारी ॥
translation: उस दैत्यराज की स्त्री परम सती (बड़ी ही पतिव्रता) थी। उसी के प्रताप से त्रिपुरासुर (जैसे अजेय शत्रु) का विनाश करने वाले शिवजी भी उस दैत्य को नहीं जीत सके ॥
english_translation: The wife of the lord of the demons was utterly devoted. Because of her power, even Tripurari could not defeat him.
essence: Steadfast devotion can shield even the seemingly invincible.
simple_meaning: The demon king's wife was so devoted that even Shiva could not defeat him because of her power.
insight: It shifts attention from visible strength to the hidden power of faithfulness and vows.
modern_relevance: A person may look untouchable from the outside, but one quiet bond of loyalty can hold far more power than force or status.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: छल करि टारेउ तासु ब्रत प्रभु सुर कारज कीन्ह। जब तेहिं जानेउ मरम तब श्राप कोप करि दीन्ह ॥
translation: प्रभु ने छल से उस स्त्री का व्रत भंग कर देवताओं का काम किया। जब उस स्त्री ने यह भेद जाना, तब उसने क्रोध करके भगवान को शाप दिया ॥
english_translation: The Lord used deceit to break her vow and complete the gods' task. When she understood the deception, she cursed him in anger.
essence: Deception may finish the task, but it also plants a curse.
simple_meaning: The Lord completed the gods' task by breaking the woman's vow through deceit. Once she understood what had happened, she cursed him in anger.
insight: It shows that a short-term victory gained through deceit can still trigger a deeper consequence.
modern_relevance: A hidden trick gets the result you wanted, but the person who was deceived will not stay silent. Winning by manipulation always leaves a wound behind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तासु श्राप हरि दीन्ह प्रमाना। कौतुकनिधि कृपाल भगवाना॥ तहाँ जलंधर रावन भयऊ। रन हति राम परम पद दयऊ ॥
translation: लीलाओं के भंडार कृपालु हरि ने उस स्त्री के शाप को प्रामाण्य दिया (स्वीकार किया)। वही जलन्धर उस कल्प में रावण हुआ, जिसे श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने युद्ध में मारकर परमपद दिया ॥
english_translation: The compassionate Lord of play accepted that curse. That Jalandhara became Ravana, whom Ram killed in battle and granted the highest state.
essence: What looks like a curse becomes part of Ram's larger design.
simple_meaning: Ram accepted the curse and later appeared as Ravana's slayer. The verse explains that Jalandhara was born again as Ravana and was freed by Ram in battle.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing events as random punishment to seeing them as part of a wider arc.
modern_relevance: A mistake, setback, or harsh consequence can feel final in the moment. Later, you may see it was one thread in a much larger pattern you could not yet read.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक जनम कर कारन एहा। जेहि लगि राम धरी नरदेहा॥ प्रति अवतार कथा प्रभु केरी। सुनु मुनि बरनी कबिन्ह घनेरी ॥
translation: एक जन्म का कारण यह था, जिससे श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने मनुष्य देह धारण किया। हे भरद्वाज मुनि! सुनो, प्रभु के प्रत्येक अवतार की कथा का कवियों ने नाना प्रकार से वर्णन किया है ॥
english_translation: The reason for this birth was that Ram took a human body. Listen, best of sages: poets have described the Lord's many incarnations in many ways.
essence: Ram's human birth is never accidental; it serves a larger purpose.
simple_meaning: Ram took a human body for a reason. Poets have told the stories of his many forms in many ways.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated events to the deeper reason behind repeated divine descent.
modern_relevance: You look back at a hard season and ask why it happened at all. This verse points to a larger pattern: some arrivals in human life are not random, but purposeful.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नारद श्राप दीन्ह एक बारा। कलप एक तेहि लगि अवतारा॥ गिरिजा चकित भईं सुनि बानी। नारद बिष्नुभगत पुनि ग्यानी ॥
translation: एक बार नारदजी ने शाप दिया, अतः एक कल्प में उसके लिए अवतार हुआ। यह बात सुनकर पार्वतीजी बड़ी चकित हुईं (और बोलीं कि) नारदजी तो विष्णु भक्त और ज्ञानी हैं ॥
english_translation: Once Narad gave a curse, and for one kalpa that became the cause of an incarnation. Hearing this, Parvati was astonished and said, 'Narad is a devotee of Vishnu and also a sage of wisdom.'
essence: A wise devotee can still become the cause of a cosmic turn.
simple_meaning: Narad's curse led to an incarnation for one cosmic age. Parvati is surprised because Narad is known as both a devotee and a wise sage.
insight: It shifts attention from simple labels to the deeper causes behind a person's actions.
modern_relevance: You hear a respected elder say something sharp at a family gathering, and everyone freezes. The person you trusted as calm and wise has a hidden side, and the whole room wants the backstory.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कारन कवन श्राप मुनि दीन्हा। का अपराध रमापति कीन्हा॥ यह प्रसंग मोहि कहहु पुरारी। मुनि मन मोह आचरज भारी ॥
translation: मुनि ने भगवान को शाप किस कारण से दिया। लक्ष्मीपति भगवान ने उनका क्या अपराध किया था? हे पुरारि (शंकरजी)! यह कथा मुझसे कहिए। मुनि नारद के मन में मोह होना बड़े आश्चर्य की बात है ॥
english_translation: What was the reason the sage was cursed? What offense did the Lord of Lakshmi commit? O Purari, tell me this episode. It is deeply astonishing that the sage Narada's mind became deluded.
essence: Even the wise can be shaken; the real task is to ask why.
simple_meaning: Parvati asks why Narada was cursed, what offense Ram committed, and why Narada's mind became confused. She wants Shiva to explain the strange episode.
insight: It shifts the mind from quick judgment to patient questioning.
modern_relevance: You hear a respected person make a disastrous choice, and your first reaction is disbelief. Instead of judging fast, you ask what pressure, pride, or blind spot led there.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: बोले बिहसि महेस तब ग्यानी मूढ़ न कोइ। जेहि जस रघुपति करहिं जब सो तस तेहि छन होइ ॥
translation: तब महादेवजी ने हँसकर कहा- न कोई ज्ञानी है न मूर्ख। श्री रघुनाथजी जब जिसको जैसा करते हैं, वह उसी क्षण वैसा ही हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Then Mahadev smiled and said: no one is truly wise or foolish. When Raghunath makes someone what they are, they become that in an instant.
essence: Ram can remake any person in a single moment.
simple_meaning: Shiva says no one is fixed as wise or foolish. Ram can shape any person instantly into whatever form he wills.
insight: It shifts attention from self-judgment to surrender to transformation. Identity becomes something received, not defended.
modern_relevance: You were certain you were the same person who walked into the meeting yesterday. Then one hard conversation, one honest apology, one unexpected grace later — your whole self feels rearranged.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: कहउँ राम गुन गाथ भरद्वाज सादर सुनहु। भव भंजन रघुनाथ भजु तुलसी तजि मान मद ॥
translation: (याज्ञवल्क्यजी कहते हैं-) हे भरद्वाज! मैं श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुणों की कथा कहता हूँ, तुम आदर से सुनो। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- मान और मद को छोड़कर आवागमन का नाश करने वाले रघुनाथजी को भजो ॥
english_translation: I sing the story of Ram's virtues. Listen with respect, Bharadvaj. Tulsidas says: give up pride and arrogance, and worship Raghunath, the destroyer of the cycle of rebirth.
essence: Humility opens the door that pride keeps shut.
simple_meaning: A sacred teacher invites respectful listening and says the real path is to drop pride and worship Ram, who ends repeated rebirth.
insight: It shifts attention from self-display to receptive listening and humble devotion.
modern_relevance: You enter a room already needing to look impressive, and the whole conversation hardens. This verse cuts that reflex before it starts: drop the performance, listen well, and let devotion begin where ego ends.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: हिमगिरि गुहा एक अति पावनि। बह समीप सुरसरी सुहावनि॥ आश्रम परम पुनीत सुहावा। देखि देवरिषि मन अति भावा ॥
translation: हिमालय पर्वत में एक बड़ी पवित्र गुफा थी। उसके समीप ही सुंदर गंगाजी बहती थीं। वह परम पवित्र सुंदर आश्रम देखने पर नारदजी के मन को बहुत ही सुहावना लगा ॥
english_translation: In the Himalayas there was a very sacred cave. Nearby flowed the beautiful Ganga. The supremely pure, lovely hermitage delighted the mind of the divine seer Narada.
essence: Sacred places can settle the mind before any teaching begins.
simple_meaning: A sacred cave, the Ganga nearby, and a pure hermitage make Narada feel deeply pleased.
insight: It shifts attention from inner chatter to the power of sacred surroundings to calm and prepare the mind.
modern_relevance: You step into a temple courtyard after a noisy commute. The bells, the water, the stillness — before you pray, something in you has already softened.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निरखि सैल सरि बिपिन बिभागा। भयउ रमापति पद अनुरागा॥ सुमिरत हरिहि श्राप गति बाधी। सहज बिमल मन लागि समाधी ॥
translation: पर्वत, नदी और वन के (सुंदर) विभागों को देखकर नादरजी का लक्ष्मीकांत भगवान के चरणों में प्रेम हो गया। भगवान का स्मरण करते ही उन (नारद मुनि) के शाप की (जो शाप उन्हें दक्ष प्रजापति ने दिया था और जिसके कारण वे एक स्थान पर नहीं ठहर सकते थे) गति रुक गई और मन के स्वाभाविक ही निर्मल होने से उनकी समाधि लग गई ॥
english_translation: Seeing the mountains, river, and forest, Narada developed love for the feet of Lakshmipati. Remembering Hari, the movement of his curse was halted, and with a naturally pure mind, he entered samadhi.
essence: Remembering Ram can still even a cursed, restless mind.
simple_meaning: Narada sees the beauty of the place and falls into loving remembrance of Ram. That remembrance quiets his curse and naturally settles his mind into deep stillness.
insight: It shifts attention from outer restlessness to inner stillness through remembrance.
modern_relevance: You step out of a noisy train station into a quiet riverside path, and your breathing changes before you even notice it. Sometimes the right place, seen rightly, can settle a scattered mind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि गति देखि सुरेस डेराना। कामहि बोलि कीन्ह सनमाना॥ सहित सहाय जाहु मम हेतू। चलेउ हरषि हियँ जलचरकेतू ॥
translation: नारद मुनि की (यह तपोमयी) स्थिति देखकर देवराज इंद्र डर गया। उसने कामदेव को बुलाकर उसका आदर-सत्कार किया (और कहा कि) मेरे (हित के) लिए तुम अपने सहायकों सहित (नारद की समाधि भंग करने को) जाओ। (यह सुनकर) मीनध्वज कामदेव मन में प्रसन्न होकर चला ॥
english_translation: Seeing Narada's absorbed state, Indra grew afraid. He summoned Kama and honored him, saying, 'Go with your helpers for my sake.' Delighted in his heart, Kama went forth.
essence: Fear makes power protect itself by breaking another's stillness.
simple_meaning: Indra fears Narada's deep meditation and sends Kama to break it. Kama leaves happily with his helpers.
insight: It exposes how insecurity can turn admiration into sabotage.
modern_relevance: You see someone stay calm under pressure while everyone else spirals. Instead of learning from them, a jealous mind tries to unsettle them. That reaction reveals fear more than strength.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनासीर मन महुँ असि त्रासा। चहत देवरिषि मम पुर बासा॥ जे कामी लोलुप जग माहीं। कुटिल काक इव सबहि डेराहीं ॥
translation: इन्द्र के मन में यह डर हुआ कि देवर्षि नारद मेरी पुरी (अमरावती) का निवास (राज्य) चाहते हैं। जगत में जो कामी और लोभी होते हैं, वे कुटिल कौए की तरह सबसे डरते हैं ॥
english_translation: Indra feared that the divine sage Narada wanted to dwell in his city. In the world, the lustful and greedy fear everyone, like crooked crows do.
essence: Desire turns the mind suspicious and afraid of everyone.
simple_meaning: Greed and desire make the mind suspicious. A person ruled by craving starts fearing everyone, even harmless people.
insight: It shifts the mind from projecting threat onto others to noticing how craving distorts perception.
modern_relevance: You see a coworker glance at your project and instantly assume they want to take credit. That reflex often reveals your own insecurity more than their intent.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सूख हाड़ लै भाग सठ स्वान निरखि मृगराज। छीनि लेइ जनि जान जड़ तिमि सुरपतिहि न लाज ॥
translation: जैसे मूर्ख कुत्ता सिंह को देखकर सूखी हड्डी लेकर भागे और वह मूर्ख यह समझे कि कहीं उस हड्डी को सिंह छीन न ले, वैसे ही इन्द्र को (नारदजी मेरा राज्य छीन लेंगे, ऐसा सोचते) लाज नहीं आई ॥
english_translation: Like a foolish dog running with a dry bone at the sight of a lion, Indra thought Narad would steal his kingdom.
essence: Fear makes a ruler defend a loss that never existed.
simple_meaning: A foolish mind imagines a threat where none exists and panics over what it cannot truly protect.
insight: It trains the mind to spot projection, not reality, before reacting.
modern_relevance: You see a senior's unread message and instantly assume you're in trouble. The mind grabs a tiny fear, then builds a whole disaster around it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहि आश्रमहिं मदन जब गयऊ। निज मायाँ बसंत निरमयऊ॥ कुसुमित बिबिध बिटप बहुरंगा। कूजहिं कोकिल गुंजहिं भृंगा ॥
translation: जब कामदेव उस आश्रम में गया, तब उसने अपनी माया से वहाँ वसन्त ऋतु को उत्पन्न किया। तरह-तरह के वृक्षों पर रंग-बिरंगे फूल खिल गए, उन पर कोयलें कूकने लगीं और भौंरे गुंजार करने लगे ॥
english_translation: When Kama entered that hermitage, he used his illusion to create spring there. Trees of many kinds blossomed in many colors, cuckoos sang, and bees hummed.
essence: Desire can dress itself as spring and still unsettle the heart.
simple_meaning: Kama enters the hermitage and makes spring appear. Flowers bloom, cuckoos call, and bees hum all around.
insight: It shows how desire often enters through beauty, then reshapes the whole mindscape.
modern_relevance: You open your phone for one quick check, and suddenly the whole evening has changed. One small spark can turn calm attention into restless wanting.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चली सुहावनि त्रिबिध बयारी। काम कृसानु बढ़ावनिहारी॥ रंभादिक सुर नारि नबीना। सकल असमसर कला प्रबीना ॥
translation: कामाग्नि को भड़काने वाली तीन प्रकार की (शीतल, मंद और सुगंध) सुहावनी हवा चलने लगी। रम्भा आदि नवयुवती देवांगनाएँ, जो सब की सब कामकला में निपुण थीं, ॥
english_translation: A pleasant threefold breeze began to blow, fanning the fire of desire. Rambha and other youthful celestial women, all skilled in every art of seduction, appeared.
essence: Desire spreads when the surroundings begin to feed it.
simple_meaning: A soft, pleasant wind rises, and beautiful celestial women appear, adding to the atmosphere of desire.
insight: It shows how temptation builds through sensory stimulation and social imagery before any overt action begins.
modern_relevance: A playlist, a perfume, a late-night scroll — small cues can stir cravings before you notice them. The mind is often led by atmosphere long before it feels led by choice.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करहिं गान बहु तान तरंगा। बहुबिधि क्रीड़हिं पानि पतंगा॥ देखि सहाय मदन हरषाना। कीन्हेसि पुनि प्रपंच बिधि नाना ॥
translation: वे बहुत प्रकार की तानों की तरंग के साथ गाने लगीं और हाथ में गेंद लेकर नाना प्रकार के खेल खेलने लगीं। कामदेव अपने इन सहायकों को देखकर बहुत प्रसन्न हुआ और फिर उसने नाना प्रकार के मायाजाल किए ॥
english_translation: They sang with many flowing melodies and played many kinds of ball games. Seeing these helpers, Kama was delighted and created yet more forms of illusion.
essence: Desire never rests; it keeps inventing new temptations.
simple_meaning: The nymphs sing and play to stir desire, and Kama responds by creating even more seductive illusions.
insight: It shows how craving escalates by multiplying distractions around itself.
modern_relevance: You open one harmless video, and the feed keeps changing shape to hold your attention. The pull does not stop at enough; it learns your weakness and keeps decorating it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: काम कला कछु मुनिहि न ब्यापी। निज भयँ डरेउ मनोभव पापी॥ सीम कि चाँपि सकइ कोउ तासू। बड़ रखवार रमापति जासू ॥
translation: परन्तु कामदेव की कोई भी कला मुनि पर असर न कर सकी। तब तो पापी कामदेव अपने ही (नाश के) भय से डर गया। लक्ष्मीपति भगवान जिसके बड़े रक्षक हों, भला, उसकी सीमा (मर्यादा) को कोई दबा सकता है? ॥
english_translation: No art of desire could touch the sage. The sinful god of desire grew afraid of his own ruin. Who can crush the boundary of one protected by the Lord of Lakshmi?
essence: Desire fails where the protected mind cannot be breached.
simple_meaning: Desire could not disturb the sage, and desire itself became afraid. No one can overrun the limits of someone guarded by the Lord of Lakshmi.
insight: It shifts attention from resisting temptation to standing in a protection stronger than temptation.
modern_relevance: A group chat fills with flirtation, pressure, and subtle bait, but one person simply does not bite. The noise loses force when the mind is already guarded.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सहित सहाय सभीत अति मानि हारि मन मैन। गहेसि जाइ मुनि चरन तब कहि सुठि आरत बैन ॥
translation: तब अपने सहायकों समेत कामदेव ने बहुत डरकर और अपने मन में हार मानकर बहुत ही आर्त (दीन) वचन कहते हुए मुनि के चरणों को जा पकड़ा ॥
english_translation: Then Kama, with all his helpers, grew very afraid, admitted defeat in his mind, and went to clasp the sage's feet, speaking very humble and distressed words.
essence: Fear makes pride bow before humility.
simple_meaning: Kama loses his courage, gives up his pride, and humbly approaches the sage's feet with distressed words.
insight: It shows that defeat becomes bearable only when pride is set down.
modern_relevance: You send the apology text after a harsh argument, then stare at the screen before hitting send. The hard part is not the words — it's dropping the ego first.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भयउ न नारद मन कछु रोषा। कहि प्रिय बचन काम परितोषा॥ नाइ चरन सिरु आयसु पाई। गयउ मदन तब सहित सहाई ॥
translation: नारदजी के मन में कुछ भी क्रोध न आया। उन्होंने प्रिय वचन कहकर कामदेव का समाधान किया। तब मुनि के चरणों में सिर नवाकर और उनकी आज्ञा पाकर कामदेव अपने सहायकों सहित लौट गया ॥
english_translation: Narad felt no anger at all. He spoke kindly and satisfied Kama. Then, bowing his head at the sage's feet and receiving the sage's permission, Kama returned with his helpers.
essence: Gentleness ends conflict more surely than force.
simple_meaning: Narad stays calm, speaks kindly, and sends Kama away peacefully after Kama bows and receives permission.
insight: It teaches you to answer pressure with composure instead of reflexive retaliation.
modern_relevance: Someone snaps at you in a meeting, expecting a fight. You lower your voice, answer cleanly, and the whole room softens. Not every provocation deserves your heat.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि सुसीलता आपनि करनी। सुरपति सभाँ जाइ सब बरनी॥ सुनि सब कें मन अचरजु आवा। मुनिहि प्रसंसि हरिहि सिरु नावा ॥
translation: देवराज इन्द्र की सभा में जाकर उसने मुनि की सुशीलता और अपनी करतूत सब कही, जिसे सुनकर सबके मन में आश्चर्य हुआ और उन्होंने मुनि की बड़ाई करके श्री हरि को सिर नवाया ॥
english_translation: He went to Indra's court and told everyone of the sage's gentleness and of his own conduct. Hearing this, everyone was amazed. They praised the sage and bowed their heads to Hari.
essence: Humility and virtue win respect even in a divine court.
simple_meaning: He reported the sage's goodness and his own actions in Indra's court. Everyone was astonished, praised the sage, and bowed to Hari.
insight: It shifts attention from self-importance to the power of truthful, humble conduct.
modern_relevance: You explain a tense incident to a room full of people, expecting judgment. Instead, your honesty makes the whole room quiet, and respect rises where defensiveness could have been.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब नारद गवने सिव पाहीं। जिता काम अहमिति मन माहीं॥ मार चरति संकरहि सुनाए। अतिप्रिय जानि महेस सिखाए ॥
translation: तब नारदजी शिवजी के पास गए। उनके मन में इस बात का अहंकार हो गया कि हमने कामदेव को जीत लिया। उन्होंने कामदेव के चरित्र शिवजी को सुनाए और महादेवजी ने उन (नारदजी) को अत्यन्त प्रिय जानकर (इस प्रकार) शिक्षा दी- ॥
english_translation: Then Narad went to Shiva, proud in his mind that he had conquered desire. He told Shiva of desire's defeat, and Shiva, knowing him to be dear, gave him this teaching.
essence: A conquered desire can return as pride.
simple_meaning: Narad becomes proud after defeating desire and goes to Shiva to boast. Shiva, seeing him as dear, teaches him a lesson.
insight: It shifts attention from outer victory to the mind's hidden self-congratulation.
modern_relevance: You finally handled a temptation, a deadline, or a hard conversation well — and immediately started narrating your victory to yourself. That second story can be the trap.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बार बार बिनवउँ मुनि तोही। जिमि यह कथा सुनायहु मोही॥ तिमि जनि हरिहि सुनावहु कबहूँ। चलेहुँ प्रसंग दुराएहु तबहूँ ॥
translation: हे मुनि! मैं तुमसे बार-बार विनती करता हूँ कि जिस तरह यह कथा तुमने मुझे सुनाई है, उस तरह भगवान श्री हरि को कभी मत सुनाना। चर्चा भी चले तब भी इसको छिपा जाना ॥
english_translation: O sage, I beg you again and again: never tell Hari this story as you told it to me. Even if the topic comes up, keep it hidden.
essence: Humility sometimes begins by asking for silence.
simple_meaning: Narad asks the sage not to repeat the story to Hari, even casually. He wants the matter kept hidden.
insight: It shifts the mind from publicizing every experience to guarding what humility requires be kept private.
modern_relevance: You tell a friend something embarrassing in confidence, then spend the next day praying it never comes back around. That instinct to protect what is tender is in Narad's plea.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: संभु दीन्ह उपदेस हित नहिं नारदहि सोहान। भरद्वाज कौतुक सुनहु हरि इच्छा बलवान ॥
translation: यद्यपि शिवजी ने यह हित की शिक्षा दी, पर नारदजी को वह अच्छी न लगी। हे भरद्वाज! अब कौतुक (तमाशा) सुनो। हरि की इच्छा बड़ी बलवान है ॥
english_translation: Although Shiva gave this beneficial counsel, Narada did not like it. Listen, Bharadvaja, to the marvel: the will of Hari is mighty indeed.
essence: Hari's will outruns every human plan.
simple_meaning: Shiva gave Narada good advice, but Narada did not accept it. The real wonder is that Hari's will is stronger than anyone's plan.
insight: It shifts attention from personal control to trust in a greater unfolding.
modern_relevance: You can carefully plan a conversation, a move, even a whole future — and still watch it go sideways. This verse steadies the mind: the larger order is not yours to control.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: राम कीन्ह चाहहिं सोइ होई। करै अन्यथा अस नहिं कोई॥ संभु बचन मुनि मन नहिं भाए। तब बिरंचि के लोक सिधाए ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी जो करना चाहते हैं, वही होता है, ऐसा कोई नहीं जो उसके विरुद्ध कर सके। श्री शिवजी के वचन नारदजी के मन को अच्छे नहीं लगे, तब वे वहाँ से ब्रह्मलोक को चल दिए ॥
english_translation: Whatever Ram desires comes to be. No one can do otherwise. The sage did not like Shiva's words, so he went to Brahmaloka.
essence: Ram's will overrides every other plan.
simple_meaning: Everything happens according to Ram's will, and no one can overturn it. Narad did not accept Shiva's words and left for Brahmaloka.
insight: It shifts the mind from control to trust in a larger order.
modern_relevance: You plan every detail of a family event, and then one small change ruins the schedule. This verse reminds you that life does not obey your control — and that peace begins when you stop demanding that it should.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक बार करतल बर बीना। गावत हरि गुन गान प्रबीना॥ छीरसिंधु गवने मुनिनाथा। जहँ बस श्रीनिवास श्रुतिमाथा ॥
