translation: एक बार गानविद्या में निपुण मुनिनाथ नारदजी हाथ में सुंदर वीणा लिए, हरिगुण गाते हुए क्षीरसागर को गए, जहाँ वेदों के मस्तकस्वरूप (मूर्तिमान वेदांतत्व) लक्ष्मी निवास भगवान नारायण रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Once, Narada, master of song, took his beautiful veena and went singing the praises of Hari to the Ocean of Milk, where Lord Narayana, the dwelling of Lakshmi and the crown of the Vedas, resides.
essence: Devotion moves the seeker straight toward the beloved.
simple_meaning: Narada, skilled in music and devotion, goes to Vishnu’s abode in the Ocean of Milk while singing his praises.
insight: It frames devotion as an approach, not just a feeling.
modern_relevance: You’re walking into a room already humming the words you want to say. The verse captures that charged moment before an important encounter begins.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरषि मिले उठि रमानिकेता। बैठे आसन रिषिहि समेता॥ बोले बिहसि चराचर राया। बहुते दिनन कीन्हि मुनि दाया ॥
translation: रमानिवास भगवान उठकर बड़े आनंद से उनसे मिले और ऋषि (नारदजी) के साथ आसन पर बैठ गए। चराचर के स्वामी भगवान हँसकर बोले- हे मुनि! आज आपने बहुत दिनों पर दया की ॥
english_translation: The Lord of all beings rose joyfully to meet the sage and sat with him. Smiling, the Lord of the moving and unmoving said, "Sage, you have shown great kindness after so many days."
essence: Real greatness rises to greet the seeker.
simple_meaning: Ram welcomes Narad with joy, sits with him, and speaks kindly. The scene shows warm divine hospitality before Narad tells the story of desire.
insight: It shifts attention from status to welcome: true greatness makes room for others first.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room carrying embarrassment, and the other person stands up to meet you with a smile. The tension drops before a single explanation is needed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: काम चरित नारद सब भाषे। जद्यपि प्रथम बरजि सिवँ राखे॥ अति प्रचंड रघुपति कै माया। जेहि न मोह अस को जग जाया ॥
translation: यद्यपि श्री शिवजी ने उन्हें पहले से ही बरज रखा था, तो भी नारदजी ने कामदेव का सारा चरित्र भगवान को कह सुनाया। श्री रघुनाथजी की माया बड़ी ही प्रबल है। जगत में ऐसा कौन जन्मा है, जिसे वे मोहित न कर दें ॥
english_translation: Although Shiva had warned him earlier, Narada still recounted the full story of desire to the Lord. Raghupati's power of illusion is immense; who in the world is not deluded by it?
essence: Pride invites delusion; clear seeing begins with humility.
simple_meaning: Narada tells Ram the story of desire even after Shiva warned him not to. The verse says Ram's power of illusion is so strong that no one in the world is beyond being affected by it.
insight: It shifts attention from intellectual confidence to self-observation, showing how pride can blind even a careful mind.
modern_relevance: You think you’re above a mistake because you’ve read the warning signs. Then one flattering comment or one ego boost and your judgment bends. Pride is often the first crack.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रूख बदन करि बचन मृदु बोले श्रीभगवान। तुम्हरे सुमिरन तें मिटहिं मोह मार मद मान ॥
translation: भगवान रूखा मुँह करके कोमल वचन बोले- हे मुनिराज! आपका स्मरण करने से दूसरों के मोह, काम, मद और अभिमान मिट जाते हैं (फिर आपके लिए तो कहना ही क्या है!) ॥
english_translation: With a stern face, the Lord spoke gently: "By remembering you, delusion, desire, pride, and ego vanish."
essence: Pure remembrance dissolves the very distortions it never carries.
simple_meaning: Remembering the divine removes delusion, desire, pride, and ego. Even the Lord praises the power of a devotee's remembrance.
insight: It shifts the focus from self-importance to the cleansing power of steady remembrance.
modern_relevance: Someone you respect quietly thanks you for helping them stay steady. Their words land harder than praise because they reveal what your presence has been doing all along.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनु मुनि मोह होइ मन ताकें। ग्यान बिराग हृदय नहिं जाकें॥ ब्रह्मचरज ब्रत रत मतिधीरा। तुम्हहि कि करइ मनोभव पीरा ॥
translation: हे मुनि! सुनिए, मोह तो उसके मन में होता है, जिसके हृदय में ज्ञान-वैराग्य नहीं है। आप तो ब्रह्मचर्यव्रत में तत्पर और बड़े धीर बुद्धि हैं। भला, कहीं आपको भी कामदेव सता सकता है? ॥
english_translation: Listen, sage: delusion arises in a mind that lacks wisdom and non-attachment. You are devoted to celibate discipline and steady understanding—how could desire trouble you?
essence: Desire cannot disturb a mind rooted in wisdom and non-attachment.
simple_meaning: Delusion belongs to a mind without wisdom or detachment. Ram tells Narad that his disciplined, steady mind is beyond desire's disturbance.
insight: It shifts attention from fighting desire to strengthening the mind that receives it.
modern_relevance: You are scrolling at midnight, half-restless, half-curious, and the urge grows stronger. Ram points to the real issue: craving enters only where the mind is already unguarded.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: नारद कहेउ सहित अभिमाना। कृपा तुम्हारि सकल भगवाना॥ करुनानिधि मन दीख बिचारी। उर अंकुरेउ गरब तरु भारी ॥
translation: नारदजी ने अभिमान के साथ कहा- भगवन! यह सब आपकी कृपा है। करुणानिधान भगवान ने मन में विचारकर देखा कि इनके मन में गर्व के भारी वृक्ष का अंकुर पैदा हो गया है ॥
english_translation: Narada spoke with pride, "All this is your grace, O Lord." The compassionate Lord considered in his mind and saw that a very heavy tree of pride had sprouted in Narada's heart.
essence: Ram sees pride the moment it begins to grow.
simple_meaning: Narada praises Ram, but pride has quietly begun growing inside him. Ram sees the hidden flaw at once.
insight: It teaches you to watch the hidden motive beneath even noble speech and spiritual pride.
modern_relevance: You get thanked in public for doing the right thing, and a small part of you starts enjoying the spotlight. The warning is simple: even holy-sounding words can hide self-importance.
speaker: Narada

verse_text: बेगि सो मैं डारिहउँ उखारी। पन हमार सेवक हितकारी॥ मुनि कर हित मम कौतुक होई। अवसि उपाय करबि मैं सोई ॥
translation: मैं उसे तुरंत ही उखाड़ फेंकूँगा, क्योंकि सेवकों का हित करना हमारा प्रण है। मैं अवश्य ही वह उपाय करूँगा, जिससे मुनि का कल्याण और मेरा खेल हो ॥
english_translation: I will uproot it at once. Serving the welfare of my servants is my vow. I will surely do whatever brings the sage good and makes my play complete.
essence: Ram makes his servant's welfare his own vow.
simple_meaning: Ram says he will remove the obstacle at once, because protecting his devotee is his promise. He will arrange whatever is needed for the sage's good.
insight: It shifts attention from self-importance to protective care for those who rely on you.
modern_relevance: You send a message late at night because someone you care about is struggling. You don't calculate whether it is convenient. You act because their well-being matters to you.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तब नारद हरि पद सिर नाई। चले हृदयँ अहमिति अधिकाई॥ श्रीपति निज माया तब प्रेरी। सुनहु कठिन करनी तेहि केरी ॥
translation: तब नारदजी भगवान के चरणों में सिर नवाकर चले। उनके हृदय में अभिमान और भी बढ़ गया। तब लक्ष्मीपति भगवान ने अपनी माया को प्रेरित किया। अब उसकी कठिन करनी सुनो ॥
english_translation: Then Narada bowed his head at Hari's feet and departed. Pride grew even stronger in his heart. Then the Lord of Lakshmi stirred his own illusion. Listen now to the difficult deed it performed.
essence: Even devotion can feed ego if the heart is not watched.
simple_meaning: Narada bows to Hari, but pride grows in him. Seeing this, the divine power of illusion is set in motion, and the next verse begins the trouble it causes.
insight: It shifts attention from outward devotion to the ego that can hide inside it.
modern_relevance: You finish a beautiful prayer, a helpful post, or a sincere apology — and still secretly want applause. That hidden craving is where the next mistake begins.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिरचेउ मग महुँ नगर तेहिं सत जोजन बिस्तार। श्रीनिवासपुर तें अधिक रचना बिबिध प्रकार ॥
translation: उस (हरिमाया) ने रास्ते में सौ योजन (चार सौ कोस) का एक नगर रचा। उस नगर की भाँति-भाँति की रचनाएँ लक्ष्मीनिवास भगवान विष्णु के नगर (वैकुण्ठ) से भी अधिक सुंदर थीं ॥
english_translation: She built a city on the road, stretching one hundred yojanas wide. Its many kinds of structures were even more splendid than the city of Vishnu's abode.
essence: Appearance can outshine reality and still be only illusion.
simple_meaning: The divine illusion created a vast, beautiful city on the road, more splendid than Vishnu's own abode.
insight: It trains attention to question appearances before trusting them.
modern_relevance: You walk into a perfectly staged showroom and almost believe the story it tells. The lights, the layout, the polish — all of it can be designed to shape your mind before you notice.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बसहिं नगर सुंदर नर नारी। जनु बहु मनसिज रति तनुधारी॥ तेहिं पुर बसइ सीलनिधि राजा। अगनित हय गय सेन समाजा ॥
translation: उस नगर में ऐसे सुंदर नर-नारी बसते थे, मानो बहुत से कामदेव और (उसकी स्त्री) रति ही मनुष्य शरीर धारण किए हुए हों। उस नगर में शीलनिधि नाम का राजा रहता था, जिसके यहाँ असंख्य घोड़े, हाथी और सेना के समूह (टुकड़ियाँ) थे ॥
english_translation: In that city lived beautiful men and women, as if many Cupids and Rati had taken human bodies. In that city lived King Sīl-nidhi, with countless horses, elephants, and armies.
essence: Splendor can dazzle the eye and still remain only a display.
simple_meaning: The verse describes a splendid city full of beautiful people and a powerful king with vast armies.
insight: It trains the mind to notice appearance without mistaking it for reality.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where everything gleams — lights, flowers, polished smiles, perfect order. It feels complete at first glance, yet you still do not know what holds it together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सत सुरेस सम बिभव बिलासा। रूप तेज बल नीति निवासा॥ बिस्वमोहनी तासु कुमारी। श्री बिमोह जिसु रूपु निहारी ॥
translation: उसका वैभव और विलास सौ इन्द्रों के समान था। वह रूप, तेज, बल और नीति का घर था। उसके विश्वमोहिनी नाम की एक (ऐसी रूपवती) कन्या थी, जिसके रूप को देखकर लक्ष्मीजी भी मोहित हो जाएँ ॥
english_translation: His wealth and splendor were like those of a hundred Indras. He was a dwelling of beauty, radiance, strength, and noble conduct. He had a daughter named Vishvamohini, whose form could even enchant Lakshmi herself.
essence: Splendor here is a prelude, not the point.
simple_meaning: The king's court was unimaginably splendid, and his daughter was so beautiful that even Lakshmi would be enchanted by her.
insight: It shifts attention from plot to atmosphere, showing how grandeur can foreshadow a decisive turning point.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall before the guests arrive, and everything already feels charged — lights, flowers, silence, expectation. The setting itself tells you that an important meeting is coming.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सोइ हरिमाया सब गुन खानी। सोभा तासु कि जाइ बखानी॥ करइ स्वयंबर सो नृपबाला। आए तहँ अगनित महिपाला ॥
translation: वह सब गुणों की खान भगवान की माया ही थी। उसकी शोभा का वर्णन कैसे किया जा सकता है। वह राजकुमारी स्वयंवर करना चाहती थी, इससे वहाँ अगणित राजा आए हुए थे ॥
english_translation: She was the divine veil of appearance, a storehouse of every virtue. Her beauty cannot be described. She chose a swayamvara, and countless kings gathered there.
essence: True splendor needs no praise; it gathers kings by itself.
simple_meaning: She was a princess of extraordinary beauty and virtues. Her swayamvara drew countless kings, and her splendor was beyond description.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary admiration to the force of character that naturally draws the world in.
modern_relevance: A room falls quiet when someone with real presence walks in. No exaggeration is needed; people simply turn their heads. Some qualities announce themselves before a single word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि कौतुकी नगर तेहि गयऊ। पुरबासिन्ह सब पूछत भयऊ॥ सुनि सब चरित भूपगृहँ आए। करि पूजा नृप मुनि बैठाए ॥
translation: खिलवाड़ी मुनि नारदजी उस नगर में गए और नगरवासियों से उन्होंने सब हाल पूछा। सब समाचार सुनकर वे राजा के महल में आए। राजा ने पूजा करके मुनि को (आसन पर) बैठाया ॥
english_translation: The curious sage went to the city and asked the townspeople about everything. Hearing the whole story, he came to the king's palace. The king worshipped the sage and seated him with honor.
essence: Curiosity enters politely, and the truth starts to reveal itself.
simple_meaning: Narada visits the city, asks the people what is happening, then goes to the king's palace, where the king honors him and gives him a seat.
insight: It shifts attention from gossip to careful inquiry and respectful listening before any judgment is made.
modern_relevance: You hear a strange rumor about a family wedding and ask around before judging. Then you show up respectfully, listen first, and the real story begins to unfold.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आनि देखाई नारदहि भूपति राजकुमारि। कहहु नाथ गुन दोष सब एहि के हृदयँ बिचारि ॥
translation: (फिर) राजा ने राजकुमारी को लाकर नारदजी को दिखलाया (और पूछा कि-) हे नाथ! आप अपने हृदय में विचार कर इसके सब गुण-दोष कहिए ॥
english_translation: The king brought the princess and showed her to Narada, asking, “O Lord, think in your heart and tell me all her virtues and faults.”
essence: Wise choice begins with clear judgment, not excitement.
simple_meaning: The king presents the princess to Narada and asks him to judge her qualities and flaws from the heart.
insight: It shifts attention from attraction to discernment, asking for an honest reading before commitment.
modern_relevance: Before a major commitment, you want someone wise to look past the excitement and tell you what is actually there. The heart can rush; clear seeing takes longer.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि रूप मुनि बिरति बिसारी। बड़ी बार लगि रहे निहारी॥ लच्छन तासु बिलोकि भुलाने। हृदयँ हरष नहिं प्रगट बखाने ॥
translation: उसके रूप को देखकर मुनि वैराग्य भूल गए और बड़ी देर तक उसकी ओर देखते ही रह गए। उसके लक्षण देखकर मुनि अपने आपको भी भूल गए और हृदय में हर्षित हुए, पर प्रकट रूप में उन लक्षणों को नहीं कहा ॥
english_translation: Seeing her beauty, the sage forgot detachment and kept looking for a long time. Seeing her marks, he was delighted inwardly, but did not speak them aloud.
essence: Beauty can silence even detachment.
simple_meaning: Narad sees Sita's beauty and becomes absorbed. He feels joy inside, but keeps his thoughts to himself.
insight: It shows how beauty can unsettle even a disciplined observer and how strong feeling can remain unspoken.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a wedding and lose your practiced composure for a moment. The face is calm, but inside everything has shifted before a single word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जो एहि बरइ अमर सोइ होई। समरभूमि तेहि जीत न कोई॥ सेवहिं सकल चराचर ताही। बरइ सीलनिधि कन्या जाही ॥
translation: (लक्षणों को सोचकर वे मन में कहने लगे कि) जो इसे ब्याहेगा, वह अमर हो जाएगा और रणभूमि में कोई उसे जीत न सकेगा। यह शीलनिधि की कन्या जिसको वरेगी, सब चर-अचर जीव उसकी सेवा करेंगे ॥
english_translation: Whoever marries her becomes immortal; no one can defeat him on the battlefield. Whomsoever this daughter of the treasury of virtue chooses, all moving and unmoving beings will serve.
essence: Virtue makes a person unconquerable and universally honoured.
simple_meaning: Narad sees Sita's qualities and thinks the man who marries her will be invincible, and all beings will serve the one she chooses.
insight: It shifts attention from outward power to the quiet force of virtue and worth.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose character changes the room before they speak. Their steadiness, grace, and integrity make force look small.
speaker: Narad

verse_text: लच्छन सब बिचारि उर राखे। कछुक बनाइ भूप सन भाषे॥ सुता सुलच्छन कहि नृप पाहीं। नारद चले सोच मन माहीं ॥
translation: सब लक्षणों को विचारकर मुनि ने अपने हृदय में रख लिया और राजा से कुछ अपनी ओर से बनाकर कह दिए। राजा से लड़की के सुलक्षण कहकर नारदजी चल दिए। पर उनके मन में यह चिन्ता थी कि- ॥
english_translation: After considering all the signs, the sage kept them in his heart and spoke to the king in a slightly altered way. He praised the princess's excellent marks and then departed, but worry remained in Narad's mind.
essence: Careful words can hide a mind already in conflict.
simple_meaning: Narad notices the signs, holds his thoughts back, and speaks to the king in a careful way. He leaves, but his mind stays troubled.
insight: It shows how a person can speak calmly while carrying a private storm inside.
modern_relevance: You leave a family gathering after saying something polite, but your mind keeps replaying the conversation in the car. The real story is happening under the surface.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करौं जाइ सोइ जतन बिचारी। जेहि प्रकार मोहि बरै कुमारी॥ जप तप कछु न होइ तेहि काला। हे बिधि मिलइ कवन बिधि बाला ॥
translation: मैं जाकर सोच-विचारकर अब वही उपाय करूँ, जिससे यह कन्या मुझे ही वरे। इस समय जप-तप से तो कुछ हो नहीं सकता। हे विधाता! मुझे यह कन्या किस तरह मिलेगी? ॥
english_translation: I will go and think of the right plan, the one by which the princess will choose me. At this time, no chanting or austerity can help. O Fate, by what means can I win this girl?
essence: Winning requires the right method, not just desire.
simple_meaning: The speaker decides to think carefully and find a way to win the princess. Prayer and austerity feel useless in that moment.
insight: It shifts the mind from vague striving to practical, situation-specific action.
modern_relevance: You’ve tried being sincere, patient, and well-prepared, but the moment still needs a smarter move. Sometimes the answer is not more intensity — it’s better direction.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: एहि अवसर चाहिअ परम सोभा रूप बिसाल। जो बिलोकि रीझै कुअँरि तब मेलै जयमाल ॥
translation: इस समय तो बड़ी भारी शोभा और विशाल (सुंदर) रूप चाहिए, जिसे देखकर राजकुमारी मुझ पर रीझ जाए और तब जयमाल (मेरे गले में) डाल दे ॥
english_translation: At this moment, only great splendor and a vast, beautiful form are needed—one that the princess will see, delight in, and then place the garland around my neck.
essence: Pride hunts for approval through appearance.
simple_meaning: The sage is thinking that the only thing needed now is a stunning appearance that will win the princess's heart and bring the garland to him.
insight: It exposes the ego's belief that outer charm can control another person's choice.
modern_relevance: You are getting ready for a wedding, interview, or stage entrance and start believing everything depends on how you look. The mind narrows to one thought: will they be impressed?
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरि सन मागौं सुंदरताई। होइहि जात गहरु अति भाई॥ मोरें हित हरि सम नहिं कोऊ। एहि अवसर सहाय सोइ होऊ ॥
translation: (एक काम करूँ कि) भगवान से सुंदरता माँगूँ, पर भाई! उनके पास जाने में तो बहुत देर हो जाएगी, किन्तु श्री हरि के समान मेरा हितू भी कोई नहीं है, इसलिए इस समय वे ही मेरे सहायक हों ॥
english_translation: I should ask Hari for beauty, but getting to Him takes too long, brother. No one is as helpful to me as Hari, so let Him be my aid now.
essence: Hari alone can help when every other plan feels too slow.
simple_meaning: Narada wants beauty, but he knows only Hari can truly help him right now. He turns to Hari because no one else can do what is needed.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance to direct appeal for grace.
modern_relevance: You are preparing for a meeting that could change everything, and your own confidence feels thin. The mind stops bargaining and simply turns to the one source of help it trusts.
speaker: Narada

verse_text: बहुबिधि बिनय कीन्हि तेहि काला। प्रगटेउ प्रभु कौतुकी कृपाला॥ प्रभु बिलोकि मुनि नयन जुड़ाने। होइहि काजु हिएँ हरषाने ॥
translation: उस समय नारदजी ने भगवान की बहुत प्रकार से विनती की। तब लीलामय कृपालु प्रभु (वहीं) प्रकट हो गए। स्वामी को देखकर नारदजी के नेत्र शीतल हो गए और वे मन में बड़े ही हर्षित हुए कि अब तो काम बन ही जाएगा ॥
english_translation: At that moment, Narada offered many kinds of prayers. Then the playful, compassionate Lord appeared. Seeing the Lord, Narada's eyes cooled, and his heart filled with joy: now the task would surely be done.
essence: Sincere prayer meets a compassionate response.
simple_meaning: Narada prays in many ways, and Ram appears in response. Seeing him, Narada feels relief and joy because his request now has a chance to succeed.
insight: It shifts the mind from anxious pleading to confident expectation once help has truly arrived.
modern_relevance: You send the final message after days of hesitation, then see the reply appear. The tightness in your chest loosens instantly. Relief can feel like grace arriving on time.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अति आरति कहि कथा सुनाई। करहु कृपा करि होहु सहाई॥ आपन रूप देहु प्रभु मोहीं। आन भाँति नहिं पावौं ओही ॥
translation: नारदजी ने बहुत आर्त (दीन) होकर सब कथा कह सुनाई (और प्रार्थना की कि) कृपा कीजिए और कृपा करके मेरे सहायक बनिए। हे प्रभो! आप अपना रूप मुझको दीजिए और किसी प्रकार मैं उस (राजकन्या) को नहीं पा सकता ॥
english_translation: Narad, deeply distressed, told the whole story and prayed, "Please be merciful and help me. Lord, give me your own form; otherwise I cannot obtain her in any other way."
essence: True help begins when pride gives way to honest need.
simple_meaning: Narad asks for mercy and help. He says he wants the Lord's own form, because no other way can win the princess.
insight: It shifts the mind from clever strategy to direct surrender and need.
modern_relevance: You stand outside a doorway, rehearsing confidence, but the real request is simpler: help me become what is needed. Honest need changes everything.
speaker: Narad

verse_text: जेहि बिधि नाथ होइ हित मोरा। करहु सो बेगि दास मैं तोरा॥ निज माया बल देखि बिसाला। हियँ हँसि बोले दीनदयाला ॥
translation: हे नाथ! जिस तरह मेरा हित हो, आप वही शीघ्र कीजिए। मैं आपका दास हूँ। अपनी माया का विशाल बल देख दीनदयालु भगवान मन ही मन हँसकर बोले- ॥
english_translation: O Lord, do whatever is best for me, and do it quickly. I am Your servant. Seeing the vast power of My own illusion, the compassionate Lord smiled inwardly and spoke.
essence: True surrender asks for the highest good, not personal preference.
simple_meaning: Narada asks the Lord to do whatever will truly help him, quickly, and calls himself the Lord's servant. The Lord, seeing the vast power of illusion, smiles and answers.
insight: It shifts the mind from demanding a preferred outcome to asking for the best outcome.
modern_relevance: You finally admit you do not know what will help most. In that honest moment, you stop bargaining and ask for what is truly good.
speaker: Narada

verse_text: जेहि बिधि होइहि परम हित नारद सुनहु तुम्हार। सोइ हम करब न आन कछु बचन न मृषा हमार ॥
translation: हे नारदजी! सुनो, जिस प्रकार आपका परम हित होगा, हम वही करेंगे, दूसरा कुछ नहीं। हमारा वचन असत्य नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: O Narada, listen: whatever will be for your highest good, that alone I will do. I will do nothing else. My word is never false.
essence: True care tells the truth and chooses what helps, not what flatters.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Narada that he will do only what truly benefits him, and that his promise is always true.
insight: It shifts trust from getting what you ask for to receiving what truly helps.
modern_relevance: You finally tell someone the real problem, and they don't rush to please you. They say, 'I won't give you what you want if it harms you.' That kind of honesty feels rare.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कुपथ माग रुज ब्याकुल रोगी। बैद न देइ सुनहु मुनि जोगी॥ एहि बिधि हित तुम्हार मैं ठयऊ। कहि अस अंतरहित प्रभु भयऊ ॥
translation: हे योगी मुनि! सुनिए, रोग से व्याकुल रोगी कुपथ्य माँगे तो वैद्य उसे नहीं देता। इसी प्रकार मैंने भी तुम्हारा हित करने की ठान ली है। ऐसा कहकर भगवान अन्तर्धान हो गए ॥
english_translation: O yogi sage, listen: when a sick patient asks for harmful food, the physician does not give it. In the same way, I have decided what is truly good for you. Saying this, the Lord disappeared.
essence: True care sometimes refuses the thing most loudly asked for.
simple_meaning: Ram refuses Narada's request because it would not be good for him, just as a doctor refuses harmful food to a sick patient. He vanishes after making the point.
insight: It shifts the mind from pleasing requests to protecting real welfare.
modern_relevance: A friend begs you to cover for them again, and you know it will only deepen the mess. Saying no can be the most caring response.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: माया बिबस भए मुनि मूढ़ा। समुझी नहिं हरि गिरा निगूढ़ा॥ गवने तुरत तहाँ रिषिराई। जहाँ स्वयंबर भूमि बनाई ॥
translation: (भगवान की) माया के वशीभूत हुए मुनि ऐसे मूढ़ हो गए कि वे भगवान की अगूढ़ (स्पष्ट) वाणी को भी न समझ सके। ऋषिराज नारदजी तुरंत वहाँ गए जहाँ स्वयंवर की भूमि बनाई गई थी ॥
english_translation: Deluded by maya, the sage became foolish and could not understand the hidden words of Hari. Then the king of sages hurried to the place where the swayamvar ground had been prepared.
essence: Pride makes a wise mind miss what is plainly before it.
simple_meaning: Maya clouds Narad's judgment, so he cannot grasp Ram's subtle warning. Still caught in that confusion, he rushes to the swayamvar ground.
insight: It shows how self-importance can block clear seeing, even when the truth is already being spoken.
modern_relevance: You reread a message three times and still miss the obvious tone because you are already sure you are right. Narad's mistake is that kind of blindness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निज निज आसन बैठे राजा। बहु बनाव करि सहित समाजा॥ मुनि मन हरष रूप अति मोरें। मोहि तजि आनहि बरिहि न भोरें ॥
translation: राजा लोग खूब सज-धजकर समाज सहित अपने-अपने आसन पर बैठे थे। मुनि (नारद) मन ही मन प्रसन्न हो रहे थे कि मेरा रूप बड़ा सुंदर है, मुझे छोड़ कन्या भूलकर भी दूसरे को न वरेगी ॥
english_translation: The kings sat on their own seats, all decorated and assembled. The sage felt delighted in his mind: “My form is so beautiful that the maiden will surely choose me and no one else, not even by mistake.”
essence: Pride makes a person certain of being chosen before the test begins.
simple_meaning: The kings are seated in splendor for the swayamvar, and Narada privately becomes proud of his own appearance, thinking Sita will choose no one but him.
insight: It exposes how self-admiration quietly distorts judgment before reality has even spoken.
modern_relevance: You check your reflection before entering the room and decide, almost automatically, that you’ll be the one chosen, noticed, preferred. That small inner boast is where trouble begins.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि हित कारन कृपानिधाना। दीन्ह कुरूप न जाइ बखाना॥ सो चरित्र लखि काहुँ न पावा। नारद जानि सबहिं सिर नावा ॥
translation: कृपानिधान भगवान ने मुनि के कल्याण के लिए उन्हें ऐसा कुरूप बना दिया कि जिसका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता, पर यह चरित कोई भी न जान सका। सबने उन्हें नारद ही जानकर प्रणाम किया ॥
english_translation: For the welfare of the sage, the gracious Lord made him so ugly that it cannot be described. No one could understand that whole episode, and everyone bowed, knowing him to be Narada.
essence: Grace can disguise itself as humiliation to save you from pride.
simple_meaning: Narada was transformed into an ugly form for his own good, and no one could fully understand the divine play behind it. Everyone still bowed to him as Narada.
insight: It shifts the mind from pride in appearance to humility before unseen correction.
modern_relevance: You get corrected in public, and your first instinct is embarrassment. Later you realise the sting saved you from a bigger fall. Not every loss is a punishment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रहे तहाँ दुइ रुद्र गन ते जानहिं सब भेउ। बिप्रबेष देखत फिरहिं परम कौतुकी तेउ ॥
translation: वहाँ शिवजी के दो गण भी थे। वे सब भेद जानते थे और ब्राह्मण का वेष बनाकर सारी लीला देखते-फिरते थे। वे भी बड़े मौजी थे ॥
english_translation: There, two of Shiva's attendants were present. They knew all the secrets and wandered about watching the divine play in the guise of Brahmins, full of delight.
essence: True sight keeps its joy even behind a disguise.
simple_meaning: Two attendants of Shiva were there too. They understood the whole hidden play and moved about in Brahmin disguise, watching everything with delight.
insight: It shifts attention from outward roles to the hidden awareness that sees through every costume.
modern_relevance: At a crowded wedding, you notice two quiet elders who seem ordinary but miss nothing. They are not there to impress anyone; they are simply watching the whole drama with calm amusement.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जेहिं समाज बैठे मुनि जाई। हृदयँ रूप अहमिति अधिकाई॥ तहँ बैठे महेस गन दोऊ। बिप्रबेष गति लखइ न कोऊ ॥
translation: नारदजी अपने हृदय में रूप का बड़ा अभिमान लेकर जिस समाज (पंक्ति) में जाकर बैठे थे, ये शिवजी के दोनों गण भी वहीं बैठ गए। ब्राह्मण के वेष में होने के कारण उनकी इस चाल को कोई न जान सका ॥
english_translation: Narada sat in the assembly with pride in his heart. Shiva's two attendants sat there too, unseen in the disguise of brahmins.
essence: Pride walks in blind; the hidden world watches back.
simple_meaning: Narada sits among the assembly, proud of his beauty, while Shiva's two attendants also sit there in disguise, unnoticed by anyone.
insight: It shows how self-regard blinds a person to what is actually happening around them.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room convinced everyone is noticing you. Meanwhile, the real story is already unfolding in the corners you are too busy admiring yourself to see.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करहिं कूटि नारदहि सुनाई। नीकि दीन्हि हरि सुंदरताई॥ रीझिहि राजकुअँरि छबि देखी। इन्हहि बरिहि हरि जानि बिसेषी ॥
translation: वे नारदजी को सुना-सुनाकर, व्यंग्य वचन कहते थे- भगवान ने इनको अच्छी 'सुंदरता' दी है। इनकी शोभा देखकर राजकुमारी रीझ ही जाएगी और 'हरि' (वानर) जानकर इन्हीं को खास तौर से वरेगी ॥
english_translation: They mock Narad, saying, "What fine beauty Hari has given him! Seeing his charm, the princess will be delighted and, knowing him to be a monkey, will choose him specially."
essence: Mock praise feeds pride before pride can defend itself.
simple_meaning: Shiva's attendants tease Narad with sharp, mocking praise. Their joke sets up Narad's growing vanity and the coming confusion.
insight: It shows how praise can distort judgment before a person even notices the shift.
modern_relevance: A group chat fills with half-joking compliments about your new profile photo. You laugh, but the praise lands deeper than you admit. That tiny swell of pride is the trap.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनिहि मोह मन हाथ पराएँ। हँसहिं संभु गन अति सचु पाएँ॥ जदपि सुनहिं मुनि अटपटि बानी। समुझि न परइ बुद्धि भ्रम सानी ॥
translation: नारद मुनि को मोह हो रहा था, क्योंकि उनका मन दूसरे के हाथ (माया के वश) में था। शिवजी के गण बहुत प्रसन्न होकर हँस रहे थे। यद्यपि मुनि उनकी अटपटी बातें सुन रहे थे, पर बुद्धि भ्रम में सनी हुई होने के कारण वे बातें उनकी समझ में नहीं आती थीं (उनकी बातों को वे अपनी प्रशंसा समझ रहे थे) ॥
english_translation: Narada was deluded, for his mind was in the grip of illusion. Shiva's attendants laughed with great delight. Though the sage heard their strange words, his mind was clouded, so he could not understand them.
essence: Pride turns even ridicule into self-praise.
simple_meaning: Narad is caught in delusion and cannot understand the teasing around him. Shiva's attendants laugh because they know he has misunderstood everything.
insight: It shows how vanity filters perception, making the mind hear what it wants instead of what is there.
modern_relevance: You reread a message three times, sure it means praise, while everyone else can see the sarcasm. When self-image takes over, even clear signals get distorted.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: काहुँ न लखा सो चरित बिसेषा। सो सरूप नृपकन्याँ देखा॥ मर्कट बदन भयंकर देही। देखत हृदयँ क्रोध भा तेही ॥
translation: इस विशेष चरित को और किसी ने नहीं जाना, केवल राजकन्या ने (नारदजी का) वह रूप देखा। उनका बंदर का सा मुँह और भयंकर शरीर देखते ही कन्या के हृदय में क्रोध उत्पन्न हो गया ॥
english_translation: No one understood this strange event. The princess saw that form. Seeing his monkey face and fearsome body, anger rose in her heart.
essence: A strange appearance can turn curiosity into anger in one breath.
simple_meaning: No one understood the strange incident except the princess, and when she saw the ugly, fearsome form, anger rose in her heart.
insight: It shows how appearance can trigger instant emotional judgment before understanding arrives.
modern_relevance: You open a profile photo and decide everything in two seconds. The mind has already judged the person before the story is even known.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सखीं संग लै कुअँरि तब चलि जनु राजमराल। देखत फिरइ महीप सब कर सरोज जयमाल ॥
translation: तब राजकुमारी सखियों को साथ लेकर इस तरह चली मानो राजहंसिनी चल रही है। वह अपने कमल जैसे हाथों में जयमाला लिए सब राजाओं को देखती हुई घूमने लगी ॥
english_translation: Then the princess, taking her companions with her, moved like a royal swan. Holding the garland in her lotus-like hands, she looked around at all the kings.
essence: Grace moves through the crowd before it chooses.
simple_meaning: The princess walks into the assembly with her companions, graceful and composed, carrying the garland as she looks at the gathered kings.
insight: It shifts attention to deliberate choice under public pressure.
modern_relevance: You enter a room full of people judging, waiting, and hoping. You keep your composure, look steadily, and choose with your own eyes.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जेहि दिसि बैठे नारद फूली। सो दिसि तेहिं न बिलोकी भूली॥ पुनि-पुनि मुनि उकसहिं अकुलाहीं। देखि दसा हर गन मुसुकाहीं ॥
translation: जिस ओर नारदजी (रूप के गर्व में) फूले बैठे थे, उस ओर उसने भूलकर भी नहीं ताका। नारद मुनि बार-बार उचकते और छटपटाते हैं। उनकी दशा देखकर शिवजी के गण मुसकराते हैं ॥
english_translation: Narad sat puffed up in one direction, and she did not look that way even by mistake. Again and again the sage leapt and fidgeted, and Shiva's attendants smiled at his condition.
essence: Pride suffers most when nobody looks back.
simple_meaning: The princess refuses to look at the proud sage, and his embarrassment grows. Even Shiva's attendants smile at the scene.
insight: It exposes how vanity depends on being noticed, and how quickly dignity collapses when attention is withheld.
modern_relevance: You send the message, then watch the screen. No reply. No view. No sign that your performance landed. The silence itself becomes the mirror.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धरि नृपतनु तहँ गयउ कृपाला। कुअँरि हरषि मेलेउ जयमाला॥ दुलहिनि लै गे लच्छिनिवासा। नृपसमाज सब भयउ निरासा ॥
translation: कृपालु भगवान भी राजा का शरीर धारण कर वहाँ जा पहुँचे। राजकुमारी ने हर्षित होकर उनके गले में जयमाला डाल दी। लक्ष्मीनिवास भगवान दुलहिन को ले गए। सारी राजमंडली निराश हो गई ॥
english_translation: The compassionate Lord took a king's form and went there. The princess joyfully placed the victory garland around his neck. The Lord who dwells with Lakshmi took the bride away. The whole gathering of kings was left in despair.
essence: Grace chooses the one pride could not win.
simple_meaning: Ram appears in human form at the swayamvar, Sita chooses him, and every other king loses hope.
insight: It shifts attention from rivalry and display to grace and rightful recognition.
modern_relevance: You can spend months competing for something, only to realize the deepest choice was never about status at all. One quiet decision can end all the noise.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि अति बिकल मोहँ मति नाठी। मनि गिरि गई छूटि जनु गाँठी॥ तब हर गन बोले मुसुकाई। निज मुख मुकुर बिलोकहु जाई ॥
translation: मोह के कारण मुनि की बुद्धि नष्ट हो गई थी, इससे वे (राजकुमारी को गई देख) बहुत ही विकल हो गए। मानो गाँठ से छूटकर मणि गिर गई हो। तब शिवजी के गणों ने मुसकराकर कहा- जाकर दर्पण में अपना मुँह तो देखिए! ॥
english_translation: The sage's mind was overwhelmed by delusion and became unsteady, like a jewel slipping loose from a knot. Then Shiva's attendants smiled and said, "Go look at your own face in a mirror."
essence: Delusion breaks self-command; seeing yourself can break the spell.
simple_meaning: Nārada loses self-control because of pride and desire. Shiva's attendants point him back to himself by telling him to look at his own face.
insight: It shifts attention from outer excitement to self-observation, showing how delusion can be exposed by direct seeing.
modern_relevance: You reread your own message five times after sending it, suddenly certain everyone noticed your mistake. One honest look at your reaction can expose the story your ego is telling.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस कहि दोउ भागे भयँ भारी। बदन दीख मुनि बारि निहारी॥ बेषु बिलोकि क्रोध अति बाढ़ा। तिन्हहि सराप दीन्ह अति गाढ़ा ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर वे दोनों बहुत भयभीत होकर भागे। मुनि ने जल में झाँककर अपना मुँह देखा। अपना रूप देखकर उनका क्रोध बहुत बढ़ गया। उन्होंने शिवजी के उन गणों को अत्यन्त कठोर शाप दिया- ॥
english_translation: Saying this, both fled in great fear. The sage looked into the water and saw his own face. Seeing his appearance, his anger rose sharply, and he gave those attendants a severe curse.
essence: Wounded pride turns a small slight into a harsh curse.
simple_meaning: The two attendants ran away in fear. The sage saw his own reflection, became furious, and cursed them harshly.
insight: It shows how wounded self-image can harden into retaliation almost instantly.
modern_relevance: You catch your reflection after a careless comment and feel the sting rise all over again. One embarrassed moment can become a long chain of anger.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: होहु निसाचर जाइ तुम्ह कपटी पापी दोउ। हँसेहु हमहि सो लेहु फल बहुरि हँसेहु मुनि कोउ॥।135॥
translation: तुम दोनों कपटी और पापी जाकर राक्षस हो जाओ। तुमने हमारी हँसी की, उसका फल चखो। अब फिर किसी मुनि की हँसी करना।135॥
english_translation: You two are deceitful and sinful. Go and be born as demons. You mocked me; now take the fruit. Mock another sage again, if you dare.
essence: Mocking a sage ripens into your own downfall.
simple_meaning: The sage curses the two mockers, telling them to become demons and suffer the result of their insult.
insight: It turns ridicule into consequence, warning that contempt shapes the future of the one who speaks it.
modern_relevance: You laugh at someone’s humiliation in a group chat, and the joke lands harder than you expected. Mockery does not vanish; it changes hands and comes back as damage.
speaker: Muni

verse_text: पुनि जल दीख रूप निज पावा। तदपि हृदयँ संतोष न आवा॥ फरकत अधर कोप मन माहीं। सपदि चले कमलापति पाहीं ॥
translation: मुनि ने फिर जल में देखा, तो उन्हें अपना (असली) रूप प्राप्त हो गया, तब भी उन्हें संतोष नहीं हुआ। उनके होठ फड़क रहे थे और मन में क्रोध (भरा) था। तुरंत ही वे भगवान कमलापति के पास चले ॥
english_translation: Seeing his own form again in the water, the sage still found no peace in his heart. His lips trembled with anger, and he immediately went to Kamalapati.
essence: A restored appearance can still leave anger untouched.
simple_meaning: The sage sees his own form restored, but anger still burns. Instead of calming down, he goes straight to Ram.
insight: It shows that outer correction does not automatically heal wounded pride.
modern_relevance: You finally get the apology you wanted, but your chest is still tight. The issue was never just the words — the wound has already gone deeper.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: देहउँ श्राप कि मरिहउँ जाई। जगत मोरि उपहास कराई॥ बीचहिं पंथ मिले दनुजारी। संग रमा सोइ राजकुमारी ॥
translation: (मन में सोचते जाते थे-) जाकर या तो शाप दूँगा या प्राण दे दूँगा। उन्होंने जगत में मेरी हँसी कराई। दैत्यों के शत्रु भगवान हरि उन्हें बीच रास्ते में ही मिल गए। साथ में लक्ष्मीजी और वही राजकुमारी थीं ॥
english_translation: I will curse them, or I will die. They made me a laughingstock in the world. The enemy of demons met them on the road, along with Lakshmi and that princess.
essence: Wounded pride looks for revenge until grace interrupts it.
simple_meaning: Narada burns with shame and anger after being mocked. He thinks of cursing the offenders or dying, and then sees Ram with Sita on the road.
insight: It shows how injured ego immediately seeks retaliation, even before understanding what is happening.
modern_relevance: You leave a room after being laughed at in front of everyone. Your chest is hot, your mind is already drafting revenge, and then one unexpected sight interrupts the spiral.
speaker: Narada

verse_text: बोले मधुर बचन सुरसाईं। मुनि कहँ चले बिकल की नाईं॥ सुनत बचन उपजा अति क्रोधा। माया बस न रहा मन बोधा ॥
translation: देवताओं के स्वामी भगवान ने मीठी वाणी में कहा- हे मुनि! व्याकुल की तरह कहाँ चले? ये शब्द सुनते ही नारद को बड़ा क्रोध आया, माया के वशीभूत होने के कारण मन में चेत नहीं रहा ॥
english_translation: The Lord of the gods spoke gently: “O sage, why are you leaving in such distress?” Hearing those words, Narada became very angry; under the veil of appearance, his mind lost its clarity.
essence: Pride hears insult where gentleness was offered.
simple_meaning: The divine speaks gently, but Narada takes offense and loses his composure. The veil of appearance clouds his judgment.
insight: It shows how pride distorts perception, turning a kind response into a personal slight.
modern_relevance: Someone texts you a calm correction, and you instantly read disrespect into it. The words were mild; the wound was already waiting. That is how the mind gets trapped.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पर संपदा सकहु नहिं देखी। तुम्हरें इरिषा कपट बिसेषी॥ मथत सिंधु रुद्रहि बौरायहु। सुरन्ह प्रेरि बिष पान करायहु ॥
translation: (मुनि ने कहा-) तुम दूसरों की सम्पदा नहीं देख सकते, तुम्हारे ईर्ष्या और कपट बहुत है। समुद्र मथते समय तुमने शिवजी को बावला बना दिया और देवताओं को प्रेरित करके उन्हें विषपान कराया ॥
english_translation: You cannot bear to see another’s wealth. Your envy and deceit are extreme. You churned the ocean and bewildered Shiva, and you urged the radiant beings to make him drink poison.
essence: Accusation reveals the accuser’s own agitation more than the one being blamed.
simple_meaning: Narad rebukes Ram for jealousy and deceit, accusing him of causing Shiva to drink poison during the churning of the ocean.
insight: It shows how anger can become accusation, turning one person’s hurt into a sweeping moral attack.
modern_relevance: A friend calls out your hidden resentment after you downplay someone else’s success. The sting is real, but so is the mirror it holds up.
speaker: Narad

verse_text: असुर सुरा बिष संकरहि आपु रमा मनि चारु। स्वारथ साधक कुटिल तुम्ह सदा कपट ब्यवहारु ॥
translation: असुरों को मदिरा और शिवजी को विष देकर तुमने स्वयं लक्ष्मी और सुंदर (कौस्तुभ) मणि ले ली। तुम बड़े धोखेबाज और मतलबी हो। सदा कपट का व्यवहार करते हो ॥
english_translation: You gave poison to the demons and to Shiva, and took Lakshmi and the beautiful gem for yourself. You are cunning, selfish, and always act with deceit.
essence: Pride sees unfairness everywhere and calls it truth.
simple_meaning: Narad accuses the divine of acting unfairly and selfishly, giving poison to some and taking the best for himself.
insight: It reveals how wounded pride turns every event into proof of bias.
modern_relevance: A colleague gets praised for work you did, and the pattern feels obvious. The hurt is not just about the loss — it's about seeing the same unfairness repeated again and again.
speaker: Narad

verse_text: परम स्वतंत्र न सिर पर कोई। भावइ मनहि करहु तुम्ह सोई॥ भलेहि मंद मंदेहि भल करहू। बिसमय हरष न हियँ कछु धरहू ॥
translation: तुम परम स्वतंत्र हो, सिर पर तो कोई है नहीं, इससे जब जो मन को भाता है, (स्वच्छन्दता से) वही करते हो। भले को बुरा और बुरे को भला कर देते हो। हृदय में हर्ष-विषाद कुछ भी नहीं लाते ॥
english_translation: You are utterly independent; no one stands above your head. You do whatever pleases your mind. You turn good into bad and bad into good, and your heart holds neither joy nor sorrow.
essence: Freedom without restraint becomes moral blindness.
simple_meaning: You act without restraint, answer to no one, and feel no remorse or delight. The verse condemns a mind so unchecked that it inverts moral judgment.
insight: It shifts attention from external freedom to moral accountability: power without restraint becomes blindness.
modern_relevance: A manager rewrites the story after every mistake, always making themselves the hero. After a while, even their own conscience stops protesting. That numbness is what this verse warns against.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: डहकि डहकि परिचेहु सब काहू। अति असंक मन सदा उछाहू॥ करम सुभासुभ तुम्हहि न बाधा। अब लगि तुम्हहि न काहूँ साधा ॥
translation: सबको ठग-ठगकर परक गए हो और अत्यन्त निडर हो गए हो, इसी से (ठगने के काम में) मन में सदा उत्साह रहता है। शुभ-अशुभ कर्म तुम्हें बाधा नहीं देते। अब तक तुम को किसी ने ठीक नहीं किया था ॥
english_translation: You have deceived everyone and grown fearless. Your mind is always eager for trickery. Good and bad actions do not restrain you. Until now, no one has set you right.
essence: Repeated deceit makes fearlessness look like strength until reality corrects it.
simple_meaning: Ravana is being called out for repeated deceit and reckless fearlessness. He has ignored moral limits so long that no one has corrected him.
insight: It exposes how repeated deception dulls conscience and invites correction before damage deepens.
modern_relevance: A person keeps bending the truth in meetings, then starts believing the lie is just strategy. Eventually the pattern hardens into character, and someone finally has to name it.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: भले भवन अब बायन दीन्हा। पावहुगे फल आपन कीन्हा॥ बंचेहु मोहि जवनि धरि देहा। सोइ तनु धरहु श्राप मम एहा ॥
translation: अबकी तुमने अच्छे घर बैना दिया है (मेरे जैसे जबर्दस्त आदमी से छेड़खानी की है।) अतः अपने किए का फल अवश्य पाओगे। जिस शरीर को धारण करके तुमने मुझे ठगा है, तुम भी वही शरीर धारण करो, यह मेरा शाप है ॥
english_translation: You have made a good bargain now. You will surely reap the fruit of your deed. The body with which you deceived me, take that same body now—this is my curse.
essence: Deceit returns in the same form it used to harm.
simple_meaning: Ravana curses the deceiver, saying the person will suffer the result of their own actions and keep the same body they used for the trick.
insight: It shifts attention from the immediate insult to the moral consequence built into the act itself.
modern_relevance: You find out the person who promised honesty edited the numbers behind your back. The anger is real, but so is the pattern: every hidden act leaves a mark that returns.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: कपि आकृति तुम्ह कीन्हि हमारी। करिहहिं कीस सहाय तुम्हारी॥ मम अपकार कीन्ह तुम्ह भारी। नारि बिरहँ तुम्ह होब दुखारी ॥
translation: तुमने हमारा रूप बंदर का सा बना दिया था, इससे बंदर ही तुम्हारी सहायता करेंगे। (मैं जिस स्त्री को चाहता था, उससे मेरा वियोग कराकर) तुमने मेरा बड़ा अहित किया है, इससे तुम भी स्त्री के वियोग में दुःखी होंगे ॥
english_translation: You gave me a monkey's form; monkeys will help you. You harmed me greatly; you too will suffer separation from a woman.
essence: Humiliated pride answers injury with a curse.
simple_meaning: Ravana curses Narada: because Narada made him look like a monkey, monkeys will aid his enemy. Because Narada caused his grief, Narada will also know the pain of separation.
insight: It exposes how insult hardens into retaliation, and how retaliation often recreates the original harm.
modern_relevance: Someone humiliates you in a group chat, and your first impulse is to strike back with a sharper message. Ravana shows how quickly wounded ego turns pain into a curse.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: श्राप सीस धरि हरषि हियँ प्रभु बहु बिनती कीन्हि॥ निज माया कै प्रबलता करषि कृपानिधि लीन्हि ॥
translation: शाप को सिर पर चढ़ाकर, हृदय में हर्षित होते हुए प्रभु ने नारदजी से बहुत विनती की और कृपानिधान भगवान ने अपनी माया की प्रबलता खींच ली ॥
english_translation: Placing the curse on his head, the Lord gladly made many humble requests. The compassionate Lord then drew back the force of his own illusion.
essence: Real greatness can accept blame and remain joyful.
simple_meaning: The Lord accepts the curse without bitterness, speaks politely, and then withdraws the power of his illusion.
insight: It teaches you to absorb offense without retaliation and respond from steadiness, not wounded pride.
modern_relevance: Someone criticizes you harshly in front of others, and your first impulse is to defend yourself. Instead, you listen, stay steady, and answer without ego.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जब हरि माया दूरि निवारी। नहिं तहँ रमा न राजकुमारी॥ तब मुनि अति सभीत हरि चरना। गहे पाहि प्रनतारति हरना ॥
translation: जब भगवान ने अपनी माया को हटा लिया, तब वहाँ न लक्ष्मी ही रह गईं, न राजकुमारी ही। तब मुनि ने अत्यन्त भयभीत होकर श्री हरि के चरण पकड़ लिए और कहा- हे शरणागत के दुःखों को हरने वाले! मेरी रक्षा कीजिए ॥
english_translation: When Hari removed the veil of illusion, neither Lakshmi nor the princess remained there. Then the sage, greatly frightened, held Hari's feet and cried, "Protect me, remover of the suffering of those who seek refuge."
essence: When illusion falls, surrender begins.
simple_meaning: When the illusion lifts, the sage sees only Hari and falls at his feet for protection.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance and pride to refuge and surrender.
modern_relevance: You finally get the message after a humiliation, a breakup, or a mistake strips away your story about yourself. What remains is the need to ask for help honestly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मृषा होउ मम श्राप कृपाला। मम इच्छा कह दीनदयाला॥ मैं दुर्बचन कहे बहुतेरे। कह मुनि पाप मिटिहिं किमि मेरे ॥
translation: हे कृपालु! मेरा शाप मिथ्या हो जाए। तब दीनों पर दया करने वाले भगवान ने कहा कि यह सब मेरी ही इच्छा (से हुआ) है। मुनि ने कहा- मैंने आप को अनेक खोटे वचन कहे हैं। मेरे पाप कैसे मिटेंगे? ॥
english_translation: O compassionate one, may my curse become false. O giver of mercy, this was your own will. I have spoken many harsh words, O sage. How can my wrongdoing be erased?
essence: Humility begins when the speaker asks mercy for his own wrong words.
simple_meaning: Narada admits his harsh words and asks Ram to make the curse ineffective. He also wonders how his own wrongdoing can ever be cleared.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-justification to humble admission, making repentance the doorway to relief.
modern_relevance: You snap in anger, then replay the words later in silence. The embarrassment is real, but so is the opening to own it cleanly instead of defending yourself.
speaker: Narada

verse_text: जपहु जाइ संकर सत नामा। होइहि हृदयँ तुरत बिश्रामा॥ कोउ नहिं सिव समान प्रिय मोरें। असि परतीति तजहु जनि भोरें ॥
translation: (भगवान ने कहा-) जाकर शंकरजी के शतनाम का जप करो, इससे हृदय में तुरंत शांति होगी। शिवजी के समान मुझे कोई प्रिय नहीं है, इस विश्वास को भूलकर भी न छोड़ना ॥
english_translation: Go and recite the hundred names of Shankar. Your heart will find peace at once. No one is dear to me like Shiva. Never let this conviction fade, even in a dream.
essence: Shiva's remembrance calms the heart because Ram treasures Shiva above all.
simple_meaning: Ram tells the sage to recite Shiva's hundred names, because that will bring immediate calm. He also says that no one is dear to him like Shiva.
insight: It shifts devotion from abstract belief to a concrete practice that restores steadiness through remembrance.
modern_relevance: You are spiraling after a harsh conversation, and one trusted practice brings you back to center. The mind calms faster when it leans toward what it reveres most.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जेहि पर कृपा न करहिं पुरारी। सो न पाव मुनि भगति हमारी॥ अस उर धरि महि बिचरहु जाई। अब न तुम्हहि माया निअराई ॥
translation: हे मुनि ! पुरारि (शिवजी) जिस पर कृपा नहीं करते, वह मेरी भक्ति नहीं पाता। हृदय में ऐसा निश्चय करके जाकर पृथ्वी पर विचरो। अब मेरी माया तुम्हारे निकट नहीं आएगी ॥
english_translation: O sage, one on whom Purari does not show grace does not attain my devotion. Hold this certainty in your heart and roam the earth. Now my veil of appearance will not come near you.
essence: Grace from Shiva makes Ram’s devotion possible.
simple_meaning: Ram tells the sage that Shiva’s grace is necessary to receive his devotion. With that certainty in heart, the sage can now live freely, and illusion will no longer trouble him.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance alone to trust in grace as the opening to devotion.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to force clarity through effort alone, but some doors open only when trust arrives first. Once that settles in, the noise loses its grip.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: बहुबिधि मुनिहि प्रबोधि प्रभु तब भए अंतरधान। सत्यलोक नारद चले करत राम गुन गान ॥
translation: बहुत प्रकार से मुनि को समझा-बुझाकर (ढाँढस देकर) तब प्रभु अंतर्द्धान हो गए और नारदजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुणों का गान करते हुए सत्य लोक (ब्रह्मलोक) को चले ॥
english_translation: After comforting the sage in many ways, the Lord then disappeared. Narada went on to Satyaloka singing the praises of Ram.
essence: True devotion keeps singing after the teacher is gone.
simple_meaning: The Lord reassures the sage, then vanishes. Narada leaves singing Ram's praises.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the after-effect devotion leaves behind.
modern_relevance: A hard conversation ends, and the room goes quiet. One person leaves calmer than before, still repeating the words that steadied him. The meeting is over, but the inner effect keeps moving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हर गन मुनिहि जात पथ देखी। बिगत मोह मन हरष बिसेषी॥ अति सभीत नारद पहिं आए। गहि पद आरत बचन सुहाए ॥
translation: शिवजी के गणों ने जब मुनि को मोहरहित और मन में बहुत प्रसन्न होकर मार्ग में जाते हुए देखा तब वे अत्यन्त भयभीत होकर नारदजी के पास आए और उनके चरण पकड़कर दीन वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: Seeing the sage walking on the path, the attendants of Shiva felt their delusion gone and their joy rise. Terrified, they came to Narada, held his feet, and spoke humble words.
essence: A clear mind unsettles fear and invites humility.
simple_meaning: Shiva's attendants saw Narada walking free of confusion and felt both joy and fear. They rushed to him, bowed at his feet, and spoke with humility.
insight: It shifts attention from outer conflict to the power of inner composure and humility.
modern_relevance: You leave a tense meeting calmer than everyone else, and the room notices. Even people who resisted you can feel the force of a steady mind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हर गन हम न बिप्र मुनिराया। बड़ अपराध कीन्ह फल पाया॥ श्राप अनुग्रह करहु कृपाला। बोले नारद दीनदयाला ॥
translation: हे मुनिराज! हम ब्राह्मण नहीं हैं, शिवजी के गण हैं। हमने बड़ा अपराध किया, जिसका फल हमने पा लिया। हे कृपालु! अब शाप दूर करने की कृपा कीजिए। दीनों पर दया करने वाले नारदजी ने कहा- ॥
english_translation: We are not priests or sages, O great seer. We committed a great offense and have received its fruit. O compassionate one, please grant a release from this curse," said Narad, the friend of the humble.
essence: Pride softens when fault is openly owned.
simple_meaning: Narad admits the attendants were wrong and asks the sage to soften the curse they have earned.
insight: It teaches you to own the harm first, then ask for repair.
modern_relevance: You realize you’ve crossed a line in a conversation and stop defending yourself. The first healing move is not explanation — it is honest admission and a request for mercy.
speaker: Narad

verse_text: निसिचर जाइ होहु तुम्ह दोऊ। बैभव बिपुल तेज बल होऊ॥ भुज बल बिस्व जितब तुम्ह जहिआ। धरिहहिं बिष्नु मनुज तनु तहिआ ॥
translation: तुम दोनों जाकर राक्षस होओ, तुम्हें महान ऐश्वर्य, तेज और बल की प्राप्ति हो। तुम अपनी भुजाओं के बल से जब सारे विश्व को जीत लोगे, तब भगवान विष्णु मनुष्य का शरीर धारण करेंगे ॥
english_translation: Go and be born as demons. You will gain vast splendor, brilliance, and strength. When you conquer the world with your arms, Vishnu will take a human body.
essence: Even exile from grace can become the doorway to return.
simple_meaning: The two cursed beings are told to take demon birth, grow powerful, and force the divine incarnation to appear in human form.
insight: It reframes suffering as part of a larger divine pattern, not a dead end.
modern_relevance: A setback can look cruel at first, yet later you see it pushed everything into motion. What felt like ruin may have been the pressure that changed the whole story.
speaker: Narada

verse_text: समर मरन हरि हाथ तुम्हारा। होइहहु मुकुत न पुनि संसारा॥ चले जुगल मुनि पद सिर नाई। भए निसाचर कालहि पाई ॥
translation: युद्ध में श्री हरि के हाथ से तुम्हारी मृत्यु होगी, जिससे तुम मुक्त हो जाओगे और फिर संसार में जन्म नहीं लोगे। वे दोनों मुनि के चरणों में सिर नवाकर चले और समय पाकर राक्षस हुए ॥
english_translation: Your death will come by the hand of Hari in battle, and you will be freed from rebirth. The two bowed their heads to the sage's feet and departed; in due time, they became demons.
essence: What looks like ruin can also be the door out.
simple_meaning: The sage's curse is also a hidden blessing: they will die at Hari's hands in battle and be freed from rebirth. Then they bow and leave, later taking demon birth.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing only punishment to seeing hidden release inside consequence.
modern_relevance: A harsh consequence at work can feel like pure punishment at first. Later, you realize it forced a hard reset that broke a pattern you could not break yourself.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक कलप एहि हेतु प्रभु लीन्ह मनुज अवतार। सुर रंजन सज्जन सुखद हरि भंजन भुमि भार ॥
translation: देवताओं को प्रसन्न करने वाले, सज्जनों को सुख देने वाले और पृथ्वी का भार हरण करने वाले भगवान ने एक कल्प में इसी कारण मनुष्य का अवतार लिया था ॥
english_translation: For this very reason, the Lord took a human incarnation in one age: to delight the radiant beings, give joy to the good, and lift the burden of the earth.
essence: Ram enters the world to relieve suffering and restore harmony.
simple_meaning: Ram took birth as a human to please the radiant beings, bless good people, and remove the earth’s burden.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to world-relief: real greatness reduces burden.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is tense, and you lower the temperature without asking for credit. Some people enter a situation to add weight; others enter to remove it.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: एहि बिधि जनम करम हरि केरे। सुंदर सुखद बिचित्र घनेरे॥ कलप कलप प्रति प्रभु अवतरहीं। चारु चरित नानाबिधि करहीं ॥
translation: इस प्रकार भगवान के अनेक सुंदर, सुखदायक और अलौकिक जन्म और कर्म हैं। प्रत्येक कल्प में जब-जब भगवान अवतार लेते हैं और नाना प्रकार की सुंदर लीलाएँ करते हैं, ॥
english_translation: In this way, the divine births and actions are many, beautiful, delightful, and wondrous. In every age, the divine descends again and again and performs many kinds of lovely deeds.
essence: Ram returns again and again, and each return is fresh wonder.
simple_meaning: Ram's births and deeds are many, beautiful, and wondrous. Again and again, he appears in each age and performs many kinds of lovely acts.
insight: It shifts attention from one fixed event to a recurring divine pattern that keeps revealing fresh meaning.
modern_relevance: A child asks why the same bedtime story never gets old, and you realize the answer: what truly matters returns in new forms. Love, courage, and grace are not exhausted by one appearance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब-तब कथा मुनीसन्ह गाई। परम पुनीत प्रबंध बनाई॥ बिबिध प्रसंग अनूप बखाने। करहिं न सुनि आचरजु सयाने ॥
translation: तब-तब मुनीश्वरों ने परम पवित्र काव्य रचना करके उनकी कथाओं का गान किया है और भाँति-भाँति के अनुपम प्रसंगों का वर्णन किया है, जिनको सुनकर समझदार (विवेकी) लोग आश्चर्य नहीं करते ॥
english_translation: Again and again, the sages sang this story. They composed a supremely pure work. They described many unmatched episodes, and wise people do not find them surprising.
essence: Ram's story is too vast for one telling.
simple_meaning: Sages have long sung Ram's story in many pure, beautiful forms. Wise people hear these varied episodes and are not astonished, because they know the divine story is limitless.
insight: It shifts you from expecting a single complete telling to recognizing that profound meaning comes through many forms.
modern_relevance: You hear the same lesson from a mentor, a podcast, and an old friend, and it still lands differently each time. A real truth keeps revealing new angles without losing itself.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरि अनंत हरि कथा अनंता। कहहिं सुनहिं बहुबिधि सब संता॥ रामचंद्र के चरित सुहाए। कलप कोटि लगि जाहिं न गाए ॥
translation: श्री हरि अनंत हैं (उनका कोई पार नहीं पा सकता) और उनकी कथा भी अनंत है। सब संत लोग उसे बहुत प्रकार से कहते-सुनते हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के सुंदर चरित्र करोड़ों कल्पों में भी गाए नहीं जा सकते ॥
english_translation: Hari is endless, and Hari's story is endless. All saints speak and hear it in many ways. The beautiful deeds of Ramchandra cannot be sung even in countless ages.
essence: Ram's story is inexhaustible; devotion deepens because it never runs out.
simple_meaning: The divine and Ram's story have no limit. Saints keep speaking and listening to them, yet they can never be fully exhausted.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to finish Ram's story to entering it with humility and wonder.
modern_relevance: You reread a letter from someone you love and still find new meaning in it. Some things do not get smaller with repetition; they keep revealing more.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: यह प्रसंग मैं कहा भवानी। हरिमायाँ मोहहिं मुनि ग्यानी॥ प्रभु कौतुकी प्रनत हितकारी। सेवत सुलभ सकल दुखहारी ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं कि) हे पार्वती! मैंने यह बताने के लिए इस प्रसंग को कहा कि ज्ञानी मुनि भी भगवान की माया से मोहित हो जाते हैं। प्रभु कौतुकी (लीलामय) हैं और शरणागत का हित करने वाले हैं। वे सेवा करने में बहुत सुलभ और सब दुःखों के हरने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: I told this story, O Bhavani, to show that even wise sages are deluded by the divine veil of appearance. The Lord is playful, kind to the surrendered, easy to serve, and the remover of all suffering.
essence: Even the wise are fooled; surrender makes Ram near.
simple_meaning: Even learned sages can be confused by divine illusion. Ram is playful, kind to those who surrender, easy to approach through service, and able to remove suffering.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-confidence in understanding to humble dependence on Ram's grace.
modern_relevance: You can spend years studying a problem and still miss the obvious because your own assumptions are in the way. Humility opens the door faster than cleverness.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सुर नर मुनि कोउ नाहिं जेहि न मोह माया प्रबल। अस बिचारि मन माहिं भजिअ महामाया पतिहि ॥
translation: देवता, मनुष्य और मुनियों में ऐसा कोई नहीं है, जिसे भगवान की महान बलवती माया मोहित न कर दे। मन में ऐसा विचारकर उस महामाया के स्वामी (प्रेरक) श्री भगवान का भजन करना चाहिए ॥
english_translation: No one among gods, humans, or sages escapes the great force of maya. Knowing this in the mind, worship the Lord of that great maya.
essence: Even the wise are shaken by illusion; devotion begins with that humility.
simple_meaning: Even the wise can be confused by the force of illusion. Knowing that, the heart should turn to Ram, who stands above that power.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-confidence in perception to humble reliance on the divine.
modern_relevance: You reread the same message three times and still misread the tone. Pride in your own certainty only makes the mistake worse; humility steadies you.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: अपर हेतु सुनु सैलकुमारी। कहउँ बिचित्र कथा बिस्तारी॥ जेहि कारन अज अगुन अरूपा। ब्रह्म भयउ कोसलपुर भूपा ॥
translation: हे गिरिराजकुमारी! अब भगवान के अवतार का वह दूसरा कारण सुनो- मैं उसकी विचित्र कथा विस्तार करके कहता हूँ- जिस कारण से जन्मरहित, निर्गुण और रूपरहित (अव्यक्त सच्चिदानंदघन) ब्रह्म अयोध्यापुरी के राजा हुए ॥
english_translation: O daughter of the mountain king, hear now the other reason. I will विस्तार this wondrous story: for that cause, the unborn, formless, attribute-less supreme reality became the king of Kosala.
essence: The formless supreme reality entered history as Kosala's king.
simple_meaning: Shiva tells Parvati there is another reason for Ram's birth: the unborn, formless supreme reality took human form and became king of Kosala.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram's birth as event to seeing it as deliberate descent.
modern_relevance: A child asks why a great leader would leave comfort and live among ordinary people. The answer is not ambition but intention: sometimes the highest presence enters the smallest room for a reason.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: जो प्रभु बिपिन फिरत तुम्ह देखा। बंधु समेत धरें मुनिबेषा॥ जासु चरित अवलोकि भवानी। सती सरीर रहिहु बौरानी ॥
translation: जिन प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को तुमने भाई लक्ष्मणजी के साथ मुनियों का सा वेष धारण किए वन में फिरते देखा था और हे भवानी! जिनके चरित्र देखकर सती के शरीर में तुम ऐसी बावली हो गई थीं कि- ॥
english_translation: You saw that Lord Ram wandering in the forest with Lakshman, dressed like a sage. Seeing his deeds, O Bhavani, Sati became so bewildered that she lost her composure.
essence: Ram's conduct can bewilder even the wise.
simple_meaning: Ram was seen in the forest with Lakshman, dressed like a sage. His conduct was so extraordinary that Sati lost her composure when she saw it.
insight: It shifts attention from appearances to the moral force of conduct.
modern_relevance: You meet someone quietly helping others while carrying their own burden, and their steadiness throws your assumptions off. Some lives do not announce their greatness; they expose your blindness.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: अजहुँ न छाया मिटति तुम्हारी। तासु चरित सुनु भ्रम रुज हारी॥ लीला कीन्हि जो तेहिं अवतारा। सो सब कहिहउँ मति अनुसारा ॥
translation: अब भी तुम्हारे उस बावलेपन की छाया नहीं मिटती, उन्हीं के भ्रम रूपी रोग के हरण करने वाले चरित्र सुनो। उस अवतार में भगवान ने जो-जो लीला की, वह सब मैं अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार तुम्हें कहूँगा ॥
english_translation: Even now the shadow of your bewilderment has not faded. Listen to the deeds that destroy confusion and illness. I will tell, as far as my understanding allows, all the play the divine performed in that incarnation.
essence: Ram’s deeds heal confusion by being truly heard.
simple_meaning: Parvati still carries confusion, so Shiva says he will describe Ram’s deeds, which remove that confusion and heal the mind.
insight: It shifts the reader from muddled reaction to patient listening for understanding.
modern_relevance: You replay the same conversation in your head after midnight, trying to make sense of what happened. A clear account can calm what rumination keeps inflaming.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: भरद्वाज सुनि संकर बानी। सकुचि सप्रेम उमा मुसुकानी॥ लगे बहुरि बरनै बृषकेतू। सो अवतार भयउ जेहि हेतू ॥
translation: (याज्ञवल्क्यजी ने कहा-) हे भरद्वाज! शंकरजी के वचन सुनकर पार्वतीजी सकुचाकर प्रेमसहित मुस्कुराईं। फिर वृषकेतु शिवजी जिस कारण से भगवान का वह अवतार हुआ था, उसका वर्णन करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Bharadwaj, hearing Shiva's words, Uma smiled shyly with love. Then the Bull-bannered Lord began describing the reason for that incarnation.
essence: Love opens the way to understanding why the divine comes into form.
simple_meaning: Parvati reacts lovingly to Shiva's words, and Shiva then starts explaining why Ram took that incarnation.
insight: It shifts the reader from receiving a story to listening for its reason.
modern_relevance: You hear one sentence that changes everything, and you go quiet before asking the next question. Real understanding often begins with that pause.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सो मैं तुम्ह सन कहउँ सबु सुनु मुनीस मन लाइ। रामकथा कलि मल हरनि मंगल करनि सुहाइ ॥
translation: हे मुनीश्वर भरद्वाज! मैं वह सब तुमसे कहता हूँ, मन लगाकर सुनो। श्री रामचन्द्रजी की कथा कलियुग के पापों को हरने वाली, कल्याण करने वाली और बड़ी सुंदर है ॥
english_translation: O best of sages, I tell you all this. Listen with attention: Ram's story removes the impurities of the age, brings auspiciousness, and is beautiful.
essence: Ram's story purifies the listener and makes life auspicious.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas tells Bharadvaj to listen carefully because Ram's story removes the impurities of this age and brings goodness and beauty.
insight: It shifts the reader from passive hearing to attentive listening, treating Ram's story as a cleansing practice.
modern_relevance: You open a story while your mind is crowded with noise, guilt, and half-finished thoughts. Then one clear, beautiful truth lands and everything feels less contaminated.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: स्वायंभू मनु अरु सतरूपा। जिन्ह तें भै नरसृष्टि अनूपा॥ दंपति धरम आचरन नीका। अजहुँ गाव श्रुति जिन्ह कै लीका ॥
translation: स्वायम्भुव मनु और (उनकी पत्नी) शतरूपा, जिनसे मनुष्यों की यह अनुपम सृष्टि हुई, इन दोनों पति-पत्नी के धर्म और आचरण बहुत अच्छे थे। आज भी वेद जिनकी मर्यादा का गान करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Svayambhu Manu and Shatarupa gave rise to the unmatched human race. Their conduct as husband and wife was excellent, and even today the Vedas praise their standard of conduct.
essence: Exemplary conduct turns a family line into a lasting standard.
simple_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa were the original human couple, and their married life was exemplary. Their conduct became a model that the Vedas still praise.
insight: It shifts attention from ancestry alone to the moral quality that makes a lineage worthy of remembrance.
modern_relevance: A couple quietly keeps promises, raises children with care, and never makes a show of it. Years later, their children still measure love by that example.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नृप उत्तानपाद सुत तासू। ध्रुव हरिभगत भयउ सुत जासू॥ लघु सुत नाम प्रियब्रत ताही। बेद पुरान प्रसंसहिं जाही ॥
translation: राजा उत्तानपाद उनके पुत्र थे, जिनके पुत्र (प्रसिद्ध) हरिभक्त ध्रुवजी हुए। उन (मनुजी) के छोटे लड़के का नाम प्रियव्रत था, जिनकी प्रशंसा वेद और पुराण करते हैं ॥
english_translation: King Uttanapada was their son; from him was born Dhruva, the devotee of Hari. His younger son was named Priyavrata, whom the Vedas and Puranas praise.
essence: Famous sons are being named to carry the lineage forward.
simple_meaning: Uttanapada had two famous sons: Dhruva, known for devotion, and Priyavrata, praised in sacred tradition. The verse is naming ancestral figures, not teaching a direct lesson.
insight: It shifts attention from individual drama to the larger sacred lineage that frames the story.
modern_relevance: A family tree is being read aloud at a ceremony, and one name after another carries a whole history of character, duty, and memory. Some verses simply place you inside that inherited world.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देवहूति पुनि तासु कुमारी। जो मुनि कर्दम कै प्रिय नारी॥ आदि देव प्रभु दीनदयाला। जठर धरेउ जेहिं कपिल कृपाला ॥
translation: पुनः देवहूति उनकी कन्या थी, जो कर्दम मुनि की प्यारी पत्नी हुई और जिन्होंने आदि देव, दीनों पर दया करने वाले समर्थ एवं कृपालु भगवान कपिल को गर्भ में धारण किया ॥
english_translation: Devahuti was also his daughter, who became the beloved wife of the sage Kardama. She bore in her womb the primal Lord, the compassionate and powerful Kapila.
essence: A quiet family line becomes the birthplace of profound teaching.
simple_meaning: Devahuti, daughter of Manu, became Kardama’s wife and gave birth to Kapila, the compassionate teacher of deep wisdom.
insight: It shifts attention from names and lineage to the moment a teacher appears in a family line.
modern_relevance: A family photo can look ordinary, yet it may hide the person who changes everything for others. What seems like a genealogy is really the arrival of a teacher.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सांख्य सास्त्र जिन्ह प्रगट बखाना। तत्व बिचार निपुन भगवाना॥ तेहिं मनु राज कीन्ह बहु काला। प्रभु आयसु सब बिधि प्रतिपाला ॥
translation: तत्वों का विचार करने में अत्यन्त निपुण जिन (कपिल) भगवान ने सांख्य शास्त्र का प्रकट रूप में वर्णन किया, उन (स्वायम्भुव) मनुजी ने बहुत समय तक राज्य किया और सब प्रकार से भगवान की आज्ञा (रूप शास्त्रों की मर्यादा) का पालन किया ॥
english_translation: Kapila, the divine one, clearly expounded the science of Samkhya and was skilled in discerning truth. Manu ruled for a long time, and in every way he followed the Lord's command.
essence: Truth means little unless life actually follows it.
simple_meaning: Kapila taught the Samkhya system with clarity, and Manu spent a long time ruling while following the Lord's command in every way.
insight: It links understanding with disciplined conduct, showing that knowledge must be lived, not just admired.
modern_relevance: You can know the right principles, hold a responsible role for years, and still feel the ache of something missing. Mere order is not the same as inner fulfillment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: होइ न बिषय बिराग भवन बसत भा चौथपन॥ हृदयँ बहुत दुख लाग जनम गयउ हरिभगति बिनु ॥
translation: घर में रहते बुढ़ापा आ गया, परन्तु विषयों से वैराग्य नहीं होता (इस बात को सोचकर) उनके मन में बड़ा दुःख हुआ कि श्री हरि की भक्ति बिना जन्म यों ही चला गया ॥
english_translation: Even after living in the house until old age, worldly attachment did not fade. Their heart felt deep sorrow that life had passed without devotion to Hari.
essence: A life can be long and still remain unfinished inside.
simple_meaning: Living long is not the same as becoming free from craving. The pain here is realizing that a whole life can pass without devotion.
insight: It shifts the mind from postponing detachment to seeing urgency in the present moment.
modern_relevance: You look up from years of routine, a mortgage, school runs, and deadlines, and suddenly realize the same cravings still run the show. That sting can become the start of real turning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बरबस राज सुतहि तब दीन्हा। नारि समेत गवन बन कीन्हा॥ तीरथ बर नैमिष बिख्याता। अति पुनीत साधक सिधि दाता ॥
translation: तब मनुजी ने अपने पुत्र को जबर्दस्ती राज्य देकर स्वयं स्त्री सहित वन को गमन किया। अत्यन्त पवित्र और साधकों को सिद्धि देने वाला तीर्थों में श्रेष्ठ नैमिषारण्य प्रसिद्ध है ॥
english_translation: Then Manu forcibly gave the kingdom to his son and went to the forest with his wife. Naimisharanya, famous among holy places, is extremely pure and grants accomplishment to seekers.
essence: True renunciation is giving away power before it owns you.
simple_meaning: Manu hands the kingdom to his son and leaves for the forest with his wife. Naimisharanya is described as a deeply pure place that helps seekers succeed.
insight: It shifts the mind from holding power to releasing it cleanly.
modern_relevance: You finally sign the business over to your child, close the office door, and book the train to a quiet ashram town. What you built can now live without you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बसहिं तहाँ मुनि सिद्ध समाजा। तहँ हियँ हरषि चलेउ मनु राजा॥ पंथ जात सोहहिं मतिधीरा। ग्यान भगति जनु धरें सरीरा ॥
translation: वहाँ मुनियों और सिद्धों के समूह बसते हैं। राजा मनु हृदय में हर्षित होकर वहीं चले। वे धीर बुद्धि वाले राजा-रानी मार्ग में जाते हुए ऐसे सुशोभित हो रहे थे मानों ज्ञान और भक्ति ही शरीर धारण किए जा रहे हों ॥
english_translation: There the company of sages and perfected beings dwelt. King Manu, filled with joy, went there. The wise king and queen shone on the path, as if wisdom and devotion had taken bodily form.
essence: Inner wisdom and devotion make even a simple walk radiant.
simple_meaning: Manu and his queen travel joyfully to a sacred place where sages and perfected beings live. Their calm, wise bearing makes them seem like wisdom and devotion themselves.
insight: It shifts attention from outer status to the visible grace of a life aligned with higher values.
modern_relevance: You see an older couple quietly entering a temple town after leaving behind power and family control. They do not look defeated. They look transformed by what they have chosen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पहुँचे जाइ धेनुमति तीरा। हरषि नहाने निरमल नीरा॥ आए मिलन सिद्ध मुनि ग्यानी। धरम धुरंधर नृपरिषि जानी ॥
translation: (चलते-चलते) वे गोमती के किनारे जा पहुँचे। हर्षित होकर उन्होंने निर्मल जल में स्नान किया। उनको धर्मधुरंधर राजर्षि जानकर सिद्ध और ज्ञानी मुनि उनसे मिलने आए ॥
english_translation: They reached the bank of the Gomati River and bathed joyfully in its pure water. Knowing them as a king-sage steadfast in dharma, perfected sages and wise ascetics came to meet them.
essence: Steady conduct draws reverence before any words are spoken.
simple_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa reach the Gomati river, bathe happily, and are honored by sages who come to meet them.
insight: It shows how visible character becomes: dharma attracts recognition naturally, without self-promotion.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a quiet river after a long drive, tired but clear-headed. People who know your conduct don't need an introduction; they feel your steadiness the moment you arrive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ जहँ तीरथ रहे सुहाए। मुनिन्ह सकल सादर करवाए॥ कृस सरीर मुनिपट परिधाना। सत समाज नित सुनहिं पुराना ॥
translation: जहाँ-जहाँ सुंदर तीर्थ थे, मुनियों ने आदरपूर्वक सभी तीर्थ उनको करा दिए। उनका शरीर दुर्बल हो गया था। वे मुनियों के से (वल्कल) वस्त्र धारण करते थे और संतों के समाज में नित्य पुराण सुनते थे ॥
english_translation: Wherever there were lovely pilgrimage places, the sages respectfully had them perform the rites there. Their bodies grew lean, they wore the bark garments of ascetics, and they constantly listened to the Puranas in gatherings of holy people.
essence: Sacred living reshapes the body, habits, and mind together.
simple_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa lived like ascetics on their pilgrimage. They stayed lean, wore simple bark clothes, and spent their days listening to sacred stories among holy people.
insight: It shifts attention from comfort and display to steady practice, simplicity, and nourishing company.
modern_relevance: You step away from noise for a while, eat simply, keep your phone away, and sit with people who remind you what matters. That quiet discipline changes you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: द्वादस अच्छर मंत्र पुनि जपहिं सहित अनुराग। बासुदेव पद पंकरुह दंपति मन अति लाग ॥
translation: और द्वादशाक्षर मन्त्र (ऊँ नमो भगवते वासुदेवाय) का प्रेम सहित जप करते थे। भगवान वासुदेव के चरणकमलों में उन राजा-रानी का मन बहुत ही लग गया ॥
english_translation: They then chanted the twelve-syllable mantra with love, and the king and queen’s minds became deeply fixed at the lotus feet of Vasudeva.
essence: Love turns repetition into fixed devotion.
simple_meaning: The king and queen repeated a sacred twelve-syllable mantra with love, and their hearts settled completely on Ram’s lotus feet.
insight: It shows how loving repetition gathers the mind and turns practice into surrender.
modern_relevance: You keep repeating a prayer, name, or line while walking alone before dawn. At first it feels like habit; then one day your mind is no longer scattered.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करहिं अहार साक फल कंदा। सुमिरहिं ब्रह्म सच्चिदानंदा॥ पुनि हरि हेतु करन तप लागे। बारि अधार मूल फल त्यागे ॥
translation: वे साग, फल और कन्द का आहार करते थे और सच्चिदानंद ब्रह्म का स्मरण करते थे। फिर वे श्री हरि के लिए तप करने लगे और मूल-फल को त्यागकर केवल जल के आधार पर रहने लगे ॥
english_translation: They ate leaves, fruits, and roots, and remembered the supreme reality, full of being, consciousness, and bliss. Then, for the sake of Hari, they began austerity, giving up roots and fruits and living only on water.
essence: Devotion becomes real when comfort is willingly reduced.
simple_meaning: They lived on simple food, kept remembering the supreme reality, and then took up harder austerity for Ram by giving up even roots and fruits.
insight: It shifts attention from comfort to disciplined remembrance, showing that devotion can reshape daily habits.
modern_relevance: You clear the pantry after a hard month and decide to live simply for a while. The point is not punishment. It is making room for what matters most.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उर अभिलाष निरंतर होई। देखिअ नयन परम प्रभु सोई॥ अगुन अखंड अनंत अनादी। जेहि चिंतहिं परमारथबादी ॥
