translation: हृदय में निरंतर यही अभिलाषा हुआ करती कि हम (कैसे) उन परम प्रभु को आँखों से देखें, जो निर्गुण, अखंड, अनंत और अनादि हैं और परमार्थवादी (ब्रह्मज्ञानी, तत्त्ववेत्ता) लोग जिनका चिन्तन किया करते हैं ॥
english_translation: A constant longing lived in the heart: may we see that supreme Lord with our own eyes. He is without qualities, unbroken, endless, and beginningless, the one contemplative sages keep in mind.
essence: True devotion wants direct sight, not just distant reverence.
simple_meaning: The heart keeps wanting direct vision of the supreme Lord, who is beyond qualities, endless, and beyond beginning.
insight: It shifts devotion from ritual effort to a hunger for direct presence.
modern_relevance: You finish meditation and still feel restless, not because you failed, but because the heart wants more than calm. It wants contact, not just technique.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नेति नेति जेहि बेद निरूपा। निजानंद निरुपाधि अनूपा॥ संभु बिरंचि बिष्नु भगवाना। उपजहिं जासु अंस तें नाना ॥
translation: जिन्हें वेद 'नेति-नेति' (यह भी नहीं, यह भी नहीं) कहकर निरूपण करते हैं। जो आनंदस्वरूप, उपाधिरहित और अनुपम हैं एवं जिनके अंश से अनेक शिव, ब्रह्मा और विष्णु भगवान प्रकट होते हैं ॥
english_translation: The Vedas describe the supreme reality as "not this, not this." It is self-blissful, beyond all attributes, unmatched. From its partial expression arise the many forms of Shiva, Brahma, and Vishnu.
essence: The source of all forms cannot be captured by any form.
simple_meaning: The highest reality cannot be fully described by any name or concept. It is pure, attribute-free bliss, and even the great forms of Shiva, Brahma, and Vishnu come from a partial expression of it.
insight: It shifts the mind from defining the absolute to revering what cannot be contained.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to explain your deepest experience in a text thread, and every sentence feels too small. Some things are real precisely because they exceed your words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ऐसेउ प्रभु सेवक बस अहई। भगत हेतु लीलातनु गहई॥ जौं यह बचन सत्य श्रुति भाषा। तौ हमार पूजिहि अभिलाषा ॥
translation: ऐसे (महान) प्रभु भी सेवक के वश में हैं और भक्तों के लिए (दिव्य) लीला विग्रह धारण करते हैं। यदि वेदों में यह वचन सत्य कहा है, तो हमारी अभिलाषा भी अवश्य पूरी होगी ॥
english_translation: Even such a Lord comes under the control of his devotee and takes a visible form for devotion. If this word of the Vedas is true, then our longing must also be fulfilled.
essence: The Lord answers devotion by becoming reachable.
simple_meaning: The supreme Lord is said to answer devotion by taking form for devotees. That promise gives the speaker confidence that a long-held longing will be fulfilled.
insight: It shifts the mind from private longing to trusting that devotion can draw a real response.
modern_relevance: You have waited through another night of prayer, grief, or uncertainty, wondering whether anything hears you. This verse answers with quiet confidence: devotion is not wasted; longing can meet response.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि विधि बीते बरष षट सहस बारि आहार। संबत सप्त सहस्र पुनि रहे समीर अधार ॥
translation: इस प्रकार जल का आहार (करके तप) करते छह हजार वर्ष बीत गए। फिर सात हजार वर्ष वे वायु के आधार पर रहे ॥
english_translation: In this way, six thousand years passed on a diet of water. Then for seven thousand years more, they lived sustained by air.
essence: Enduring restraint changes a person more than short intensity ever can.
simple_meaning: They kept up severe austerity for thousands of years, first living on water, then on air.
insight: It shifts attention from quick effort to sustained self-mastery over time.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone, then finally place it face down for ten minutes. Real discipline is not dramatic — it is repeated refusal, long enough to reshape you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बरष सहस दस त्यागेउ सोऊ। ठाढ़े रहे एक पद दोऊ ॥ बिधि हरि हर तप देखि अपारा। मनु समीप आए बहु बारा ॥
translation: दस हजार वर्ष तक उन्होंने वायु का आधार भी छोड़ दिया। दोनों एक पैर से खड़े रहे। उनका अपार तप देखकर ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और शिवजी कई बार मनुजी के पास आए ॥
english_translation: For ten thousand years they gave up even support from the air. Both stood on one foot. Seeing their immense austerity, Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva came many times to Manu.
essence: Enduring discipline can draw the highest attention.
simple_meaning: They kept up extreme austerity for ten thousand years, standing on one foot. Their discipline was so great that Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva came to Manu again and again.
insight: It shifts attention from short effort to sustained self-mastery that commands respect.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up before sunrise, long after the excitement is gone. No one claps. Still, the work changes you so completely that even your own standards feel different.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मागहु बर बहु भाँति लोभाए। परम धीर नहिं चलहिं चलाए॥ अस्थिमात्र होइ रहे सरीरा। तदपि मनाग मनहिं नहिं पीरा ॥
translation: उन्होंने इन्हें अनेक प्रकार से ललचाया और कहा कि कुछ वर माँगो। पर ये परम धैर्यवान (राजा-रानी अपने तप से किसी के) डिगाए नहीं डिगे। यद्यपि उनका शरीर हड्डियों का ढाँचा मात्र रह गया था, फिर भी उनके मन में जरा भी पीड़ा नहीं थी ॥
english_translation: They tried many ways to tempt them and said, "Ask for a boon." But the steadfast pair could not be shaken. Though their bodies were reduced to little more than bones, their minds still felt no pain.
essence: Temptation cannot move a mind rooted in tapas.
simple_meaning: The divine beings tried to tempt the king and queen with boons, but they could not be shaken. Even when their bodies were nearly reduced to bones, they felt no pain in their minds.
insight: It shifts attention from reward-seeking to unshaken endurance under pressure.
modern_relevance: You are worn down after months of caring for a sick parent, yet a shortcut would betray what you stand for. Their steadiness shows what it means not to bend.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु सर्बग्य दास निज जानी। गति अनन्य तापस नृप रानी॥ मागु मागु बरु भै नभ बानी। परम गभीर कृपामृत सानी ॥
translation: सर्वज्ञ प्रभु ने अनन्य गति (आश्रय) वाले तपस्वी राजा-रानी को 'निज दास' जाना। तब परम गंभीर और कृपा रूपी अमृत से सनी हुई यह आकाशवाणी हुई कि 'वर माँगो' ॥
english_translation: The all-knowing Lord recognized the ascetic king and queen as his own servants, devoted to a single refuge. Then a deep, nectar-like voice from the sky said, “Ask for a boon.”
essence: Single-minded devotion is recognized before it is rewarded.
simple_meaning: Ram recognizes the king and queen as devoted servants who have no refuge but him. Then a voice from the sky invites them to ask for a boon.
insight: It shifts the mind from striving for approval to trusting that sincere devotion is already seen.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up for years with no guarantee anyone notices. Then, in one quiet moment, someone finally names your devotion and asks what you need.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मृतक जिआवनि गिरा सुहाई। श्रवन रंध्र होइ उर जब आई॥ हृष्ट पुष्ट तन भए सुहाए। मानहुँ अबहिं भवन ते आए ॥
translation: मुर्दे को भी जिला देने वाली यह सुंदर वाणी कानों के छेदों से होकर जब हृदय में आई, तब राजा-रानी के शरीर ऐसे सुंदर और हृष्ट-पुष्ट हो गए, मानो अभी घर से आए हैं ॥
english_translation: The beautiful speech that could revive the dead entered through the ears and reached the heart. Then the king and queen’s bodies became radiant and full of life, as if they had just come home.
essence: Grace can revive a heart before it can explain itself.
simple_meaning: The king and queen hear words so sweet they feel life return to them. Their grief lifts, and their bodies seem renewed.
insight: It shifts attention from harshness to the healing power of sound and trust.
modern_relevance: After a night of bad news, one calm voice on the phone changes everything. Your shoulders drop, your breathing returns, and the body remembers hope before the mind does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: श्रवन सुधा सम बचन सुनि पुलक प्रफुल्लित गात। बोले मनु करि दंडवत प्रेम न हृदयँ समात ॥
translation: कानों में अमृत के समान लगने वाले वचन सुनते ही उनका शरीर पुलकित और प्रफुल्लित हो गया। तब मनुजी दण्डवत करके बोले- प्रेम हृदय में समाता न था- ॥
english_translation: Hearing words as sweet as nectar, their bodies thrilled with joy. Then Manu bowed and spoke, his heart too full of love to contain.
essence: Love overflows when grace is finally heard.
simple_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa hear Ram's gracious words and are overwhelmed with joy and reverence. Their love is so full that ordinary speech cannot hold it.
insight: It shifts the reader from analysis to reverent response: first receive, then bow.
modern_relevance: You finally hear the apology you never expected from someone you love. Your chest loosens, tears come, and you can only bow your head because gratitude is bigger than language.
speaker: Manu

verse_text: सुनु सेवक सुरतरु सुरधेनू। बिधि हरि हर बंदित पद रेनू॥ सेवत सुलभ सकल सुखदायक। प्रनतपाल सचराचर नायक ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! सुनिए, आप सेवकों के लिए कल्पवृक्ष और कामधेनु हैं। आपके चरण रज की ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और शिवजी भी वंदना करते हैं। आप सेवा करने में सुलभ हैं तथा सब सुखों के देने वाले हैं। आप शरणागत के रक्षक और जड़-चेतन के स्वामी हैं ॥
english_translation: Listen: for servants, you are the wish-fulfilling tree and the wish-fulfilling cow. Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva bow to the dust of your feet. You are easy to reach through service, giver of all happiness, protector of those who take refuge, and lord of all moving and unmoving beings.
essence: Service makes the highest presence feel near.
simple_meaning: Ram is the easiest refuge for a devoted servant. He gives joy, protects those who surrender, and is honored even by Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.
insight: It shifts the mind from bargaining with the divine to serving with trust, knowing refuge itself is the reward.
modern_relevance: You keep helping someone who never seems to notice, and then one day they stand by you when it matters most. This verse says that real service is never wasted.
speaker: Manu

verse_text: जौं अनाथ हित हम पर नेहू। तौ प्रसन्न होई यह बर देहू॥ जोसरूप बस सिव मन माहीं। जेहिं कारन मुनि जतन कराहीं ॥
translation: हे अनाथों का कल्याण करने वाले! यदि हम लोगों पर आपका स्नेह है, तो प्रसन्न होकर यह वर दीजिए कि आपका जो स्वरूप शिवजी के मन में बसता है और जिस (की प्राप्ति) के लिए मुनि लोग यत्न करते हैं ॥
english_translation: If you truly love us, O protector of the helpless, then be pleased and grant this boon: let us behold the form that dwells in Shiva's heart and that sages strive to attain.
essence: True devotion asks for vision, not advantage.
simple_meaning: Manu asks Ram to show the form that even Shiva holds in his heart and that sages seek through effort.
insight: It shifts prayer from asking for benefits to asking for direct vision of the divine form.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you deeply admire, and you do not ask for favors or shortcuts. You ask for the one thing that matters most: to truly see who they are.
speaker: Manu

verse_text: जो भुसुंडि मन मानस हंसा। सगुन अगुन जेहि निगम प्रसंसा॥ देखहिं हम सो रूप भरि लोचन। कृपा करहु प्रनतारति मोचन ॥
translation: जो काकभुशुण्डि के मन रूपी मान सरोवर में विहार करने वाला हंस है, सगुण और निर्गुण कहकर वेद जिसकी प्रशंसा करते हैं, हे शरणागत के दुःख मिटाने वाले प्रभो! ऐसी कृपा कीजिए कि हम उसी रूप को नेत्र भरकर देखें ॥
english_translation: O Lord, who dwells in the swan-like mind of Kakabhushundi, whom the Vedas praise as both with form and without form, grant us your grace so that we may behold that form with our eyes full of longing.
essence: Trust seeks a face, not an idea.
simple_meaning: The speaker asks to see Ram’s divine form directly, with eyes full of longing, and praises him as beyond ordinary categories of form and formlessness.
insight: It shifts devotion from abstract belief to direct longing for presence.
modern_relevance: You scroll past a thousand images, but one face still matters more than all of them. This verse names that ache: not information, but a clear, loving glimpse of what you trust.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: दंपति बचन परम प्रिय लागे। मृदुल बिनीत प्रेम रस पागे॥ भगत बछल प्रभु कृपानिधाना। बिस्वबास प्रगटे भगवाना ॥
translation: राजा-रानी के कोमल, विनययुक्त और प्रेमरस में पगे हुए वचन भगवान को बहुत ही प्रिय लगे। भक्तवत्सल, कृपानिधान, सम्पूर्ण विश्व के निवास स्थान (या समस्त विश्व में व्यापक), सर्वसमर्थ भगवान प्रकट हो गए ॥
english_translation: The king and queen’s gentle, humble, love-filled words were dear to the Lord. Compassionate to devotees, a treasure of grace, the all-pervading Lord appeared.
essence: Humility and love draw the divine into view.
simple_meaning: Gentle, humble words filled with love please the divine, and the beloved Lord appears to those who speak with devotion.
insight: It shifts attention from performance to sincerity: devotion opens the way for revelation.
modern_relevance: You finally say what matters without posturing or pressure. The other person softens, because honest warmth reaches places argument never touches.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नील सरोरुह नील मनि नील नीरधर स्याम। लाजहिं तन सोभा निरखि कोटि कोटि सत काम ॥
translation: भगवान के नीले कमल, नीलमणि और नीले (जलयुक्त) मेघ के समान (कोमल, प्रकाशमय और सरस) श्यामवर्ण (चिन्मय) शरीर की शोभा देखकर करोड़ों कामदेव भी लजा जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing the beauty of the divine blue body, even millions of love-gods feel ashamed.
essence: True beauty makes desire bow in silence.
simple_meaning: Ram's blue form is so beautiful that even countless love-gods lose their pride before it.
insight: It shifts attention from attraction as craving to beauty as reverence.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone so calm and radiant that your restless wanting suddenly feels small. The mind falls quiet because it has met something greater than appetite.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सरद मयंक बदन छबि सींवा। चारु कपोल चिबुक दर ग्रीवा॥ अधर अरुन रद सुंदर नासा। बिधु कर निकर बिनिंदक हासा ॥
translation: उनका मुख शरद (पूर्णिमा) के चन्द्रमा के समान छबि की सीमास्वरूप था। गाल और ठोड़ी बहुत सुंदर थे, गला शंख के समान (त्रिरेखायुक्त, चढ़ाव-उतार वाला) था। लाल होठ, दाँत और नाक अत्यन्त सुंदर थे। हँसी चन्द्रमा की किरणावली को नीचा दिखाने वाली थी ॥
english_translation: His face shone like the autumn moon. His cheeks, chin, neck, lips, teeth, nose, and smile were all exquisitely beautiful.
essence: His beauty exceeds every image used to describe it.
simple_meaning: His face is described as moonlike and every feature as beautifully formed, with a smile brighter than moonbeams.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary description to reverent seeing, where every feature becomes a sign of grace.
modern_relevance: You catch someone’s face in soft evening light and forget your next sentence. Some presence needs no introduction; it rearranges the room by simply being seen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नव अंबुज अंबक छबि नीकी। चितवनि ललित भावँतीजी की॥ भृकुटि मनोज चाप छबि हारी। तिलक ललाट पटल दुतिकारी ॥
translation: नेत्रों की छवि नए (खिले हुए) कमल के समान बड़ी सुंदर थी। मनोहर चितवन जी को बहुत प्यारी लगती थी। टेढ़ी भौंहें कामदेव के धनुष की शोभा को हरने वाली थीं। ललाट पटल पर प्रकाशमय तिलक था ॥
english_translation: His eyes were beautifully like new lotus blossoms. His graceful glance delighted everyone. His arched brows outshone Cupid's bow. A radiant tilak glowed on his forehead.
essence: Ram's presence is so beautiful that even a glance feels like grace.
simple_meaning: His face is described in beautiful detail: lotus-like eyes, a charming glance, arched brows, and a glowing tilak on the forehead.
insight: It shifts attention from plot to presence, letting beauty itself carry the moment.
modern_relevance: You catch sight of someone across a crowded room and everything in you goes quiet. Before they speak, their presence already changes the atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कुंडल मकर मुकुट सिर भ्राजा। कुटिल केस जनु मधुप समाजा॥ उर श्रीबत्स रुचिर बनमाला। पदिक हार भूषन मनिजाला ॥
translation: कानों में मकराकृत (मछली के आकार के) कुंडल और सिर पर मुकुट सुशोभित था। टेढ़े (घुँघराले) काले बाल ऐसे सघन थे, मानो भौंरों के झुंड हों। हृदय पर श्रीवत्स, सुंदर वनमाला, रत्नजड़ित हार और मणियों के आभूषण सुशोभित थे ॥
english_translation: Earrings shaped like makara shone on the ears, and a crown on the head. The dark, curling hair clustered like a swarm of bees. On the chest shone the Srivatsa mark, a lovely forest garland, jeweled necklaces, and ornaments set with gems.
essence: Ram’s beauty turns every ornament into a sign of presence.
simple_meaning: The verse describes Ram’s divine beauty and ornaments: earrings, crown, curly hair, the Srivatsa mark, garland, necklace, and jeweled adornments.
insight: It trains attention to see radiance as character made visible, not mere appearance.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone entering a room, and the whole atmosphere changes. Not because of display, but because presence can make ornament feel secondary.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: केहरि कंधर चारु जनेऊ। बाहु बिभूषन सुंदर तेऊ॥ मकरि कर सरिस सुभग भुजदंडा। कटि निषंग कर सर कोदंडा ॥
translation: सिंह की सी गर्दन थी, सुंदर जनेऊ था। भुजाओं में जो गहने थे, वे भी सुंदर थे। हाथी की सूँड के समान (उतार-चढ़ाव वाले) सुंदर भुजदंड थे। कमर में तरकस और हाथ में बाण और धनुष (शोभा पा रहे) थे ॥
english_translation: The neck was like a lion's, and the sacred thread was beautiful. The ornaments on the arms were lovely. The upper arms were graceful like an elephant's trunk. A quiver hung at the waist, and bow and arrows shone in the hand.
essence: Grace and power can live in the same body.
simple_meaning: The verse describes Ram's graceful body and the weapons and ornaments that adorned him.
insight: It trains attention to see dignity as harmony of appearance, bearing, and readiness.
modern_relevance: You notice someone enter the room and everything about them feels composed: posture, clothes, and readiness all match. Nothing is wasted, nothing is exaggerated.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तड़ित बिनिंदक पीत पट उदर रेख बर तीनि। नाभि मनोहर लेति जनु जमुन भँवर छबि छीनि ॥
translation: (स्वर्ण-वर्ण का प्रकाशमय) पीताम्बर बिजली को लजाने वाला था। पेट पर सुंदर तीन रेखाएँ (त्रिवली) थीं। नाभि ऐसी मनोहर थी, मानो यमुनाजी के भँवरों की छबि को छीने लेती हो ॥
english_translation: The shining yellow cloth outshone lightning. Three graceful lines marked the belly. The navel was so lovely it seemed to steal the beauty of Yamuna's whirlpools.
essence: Even Ram's smallest features are radiant enough to eclipse nature's beauty.
simple_meaning: Ram's body is described as radiant and beautiful: his yellow garment shines like lightning, his belly has three graceful lines, and his navel is so lovely it seems to surpass the beauty of the Yamuna's whirlpools.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary appearance to form as a carrier of devotion.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone walking into a room and everything else fades for a second. The verse names that rare presence that doesn't ask for attention but quietly takes it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पद राजीव बरनि नहिं जाहीं। मुनि मन मधुप बसहिं जेन्ह माहीं॥ बाम भाग सोभति अनुकूला। आदिसक्ति छबिनिधि जगमूला ॥
translation: जिनमें मुनियों के मन रूपी भौंरे बसते हैं, भगवान के उन चरणकमलों का तो वर्णन ही नहीं किया जा सकता। भगवान के बाएँ भाग में सदा अनुकूल रहने वाली, शोभा की राशि जगत की मूलकारण रूपा आदि शक्ति श्री जानकीजी सुशोभित हैं ॥
english_translation: The lotus feet cannot be described. Munis live in the honey of their minds there. On his left side shines the ever-auspicious one, the original power, the source of the universe, Sita.
essence: Ram’s presence draws the mind home, and Sita completes his divine radiance.
simple_meaning: Ram's feet are beyond description, and sages rest their minds on them. Beside him shines Sita, the original power and source of the world.
insight: It shifts attention from outward description to inward devotion, showing that reverence is where the mind belongs.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence calms a crowded room, and everyone around them naturally settles. The mind stops chasing and simply rests. That is the kind of still beauty this verse points to.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जासु अंस उपजहिं गुनखानी। अगनित लच्छि उमा ब्रह्मानी॥ भृकुटि बिलास जासु जग होई। राम बाम दिसि सीता सोई ॥
translation: जिनके अंश से गुणों की खान अगणित लक्ष्मी, पार्वती और ब्रह्माणी (त्रिदेवों की शक्तियाँ) उत्पन्न होती हैं तथा जिनकी भौंह के इशारे से ही जगत की रचना हो जाती है, वही (भगवान की स्वरूपा शक्ति) श्री सीताजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी की बाईं ओर स्थित हैं ॥
english_translation: From whose power arise countless Lakshmis, Parvati, and Brahmani, and by whose brow's play the world comes into being, that very divine power, Sita, stands on Ram's left.
essence: The power behind creation stands beside Ram as Sita.
simple_meaning: Sita is shown as the divine power of Ram. She is not just beside him; she is the force from which greatness, creation, and beauty emerge.
insight: It shifts attention from visible status to the hidden power that supports and completes it.
modern_relevance: At a wedding, everyone admires the groom's entrance, but the room changes when the bride arrives. This verse reminds you that quiet presence can carry the deepest power.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: छबिसमुद्र हरि रूप बिलोकी। एकटक रहे नयन पट रोकी॥ चितवहिं सादर रूप अनूपा। तृप्ति न मानहिं मनु सतरूपा ॥
translation: शोभा के समुद्र श्री हरि के रूप को देखकर मनु-शतरूपा नेत्रों के पट (पलकें) रोके हुए एकटक (स्तब्ध) रह गए। उस अनुपम रूप को वे आदर सहित देख रहे थे और देखते-देखते अघाते ही न थे ॥
english_translation: Seeing Hari’s radiant form, Manu and Shatarupa stood fixed, their eyes unblinking. With reverence, they kept gazing at the incomparable form and never felt satisfied.
essence: True beauty stills the eyes and leaves desire satisfied by seeing.
simple_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa see Ram’s beautiful form and cannot look away. Their reverent gaze never feels complete.
insight: It shifts attention from consuming an image to reverently receiving presence.
modern_relevance: You open a photo and keep staring longer than you meant to. Not because it flatters you, but because something in it feels larger than ordinary seeing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरष बिबस तन दसा भुलानी। परे दंड इव गहि पद पानी॥ सिर परसे प्रभु निज कर कंजा। तुरत उठाए करुनापुंजा ॥
translation: आनंद के अधिक वश में हो जाने के कारण उन्हें अपने देह की सुधि भूल गई। वे हाथों से भगवान के चरण पकड़कर दण्ड की तरह (सीधे) भूमि पर गिर पड़े। कृपा की राशि प्रभु ने अपने करकमलों से उनके मस्तकों का स्पर्श किया और उन्हें तुरंत ही उठा लिया ॥
english_translation: Overwhelmed with joy, they forgot their bodies. Grasping the Lord's feet, they fell like sticks. The Lord touched their heads with his lotus hands and lifted them up at once.
essence: Joy before Ram dissolves the self and draws forth instant compassion.
simple_meaning: Overjoyed, they lost awareness of their bodies, fell at Ram's feet, and were gently lifted up by his compassionate touch.
insight: It shows how surrender is answered by immediate grace, not delay or judgment.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you have admired for years, and your voice catches. In that moment, real warmth doesn't keep its distance — it reaches down and steadies you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बोले कृपानिधान पुनि अति प्रसन्न मोहि जानि। मागहु बर जोइ भाव मन महादानि अनुमानि ॥
translation: फिर कृपानिधान भगवान बोले- मुझे अत्यन्त प्रसन्न जानकर और बड़ा भारी दानी मानकर, जो मन को भाए वही वर माँग लो ॥
english_translation: Then the Lord of compassion, knowing me to be greatly pleased, said: ask for whatever boon your heart desires, thinking me a great giver.
essence: Compassion invites desire without fear.
simple_meaning: Ram, pleased by the sight of his devotees, invites them to ask for any boon their hearts want.
insight: It shifts devotion from silent awe to open asking, showing that grace welcomes honest desire.
modern_relevance: You finally hear praise from someone you deeply respect, and they ask what would make you happiest. The moment feels bigger than the request — it feels like being seen.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनि प्रभु बचन जोरि जुग पानी। धरि धीरजु बोली मृदु बानी॥ नाथ देखि पद कमल तुम्हारे। अब पूरे सब काम हमारे ॥
translation: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर, दोनों हाथ जोड़कर और धीरज धरकर राजा ने कोमल वाणी कही- हे नाथ! आपके चरणकमलों को देखकर अब हमारी सारी मनःकामनाएँ पूरी हो गईं ॥
english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, he folded both hands, gathered his courage, and spoke softly: "Lord, seeing your lotus feet, all our wishes are now fulfilled."
essence: Seeing Ram is enough; every other wish falls away.
simple_meaning: Janaka hears Ram's words, bows with folded hands, and says that simply seeing Ram's feet has fulfilled every desire.
insight: It shifts desire from getting something from the divine to being satisfied by presence alone.
modern_relevance: You finally meet the person you have admired from afar. The meeting itself feels complete — no extra reward, no bigger moment needed.
speaker: King Janaka

verse_text: एक लालसा बड़ि उर माहीं। सुगम अगम कहि जाति सो नाहीं॥ तुम्हहि देत अति सुगम गोसाईं। अगम लाग मोहि निज कृपनाईं ॥
translation: फिर भी मन में एक बड़ी लालसा है। उसका पूरा होना सहज भी है और अत्यन्त कठिन भी, इसी से उसे कहते नहीं बनता। हे स्वामी! आपके लिए तो उसका पूरा करना बहुत सहज है, पर मुझे अपनी कृपणता (दीनता) के कारण वह अत्यन्त कठिन मालूम होता है ॥
english_translation: Still, one great longing lives in my heart. It is called both easy and hard, so it cannot be spoken plainly. O Lord, for you it is very easy to grant, but my own meanness makes it seem very hard.
essence: Humility can make the easiest gift feel impossible to ask for.
simple_meaning: The speaker has one deep wish, but feels too small to ask for it clearly. Ram could grant it easily; the obstacle is the speaker's own humility and hesitation.
insight: It shifts the mind from entitlement to humble asking, while still trusting that the giver is able.
modern_relevance: You finally get a chance to ask for help from someone generous, but your throat tightens. The request feels simple, and your pride makes it impossible. This verse knows that hesitation.
speaker: King Janaka

verse_text: जथा दरिद्र बिबुधतरु पाई। बहु संपति मागत सकुचाई॥ तासु प्रभाउ जान नहिं सोई। तथा हृदयँ मम संसय होई ॥
translation: जैसे कोई दरिद्र कल्पवृक्ष को पाकर भी अधिक द्रव्य माँगने में संकोच करता है, क्योंकि वह उसके प्रभाव को नहीं जानता, वैसे ही मेरे हृदय में संशय हो रहा है ॥
english_translation: Like a poor man who finds a wish-fulfilling tree but still hesitates to ask for more, not knowing its power, so doubt has arisen in my heart.
essence: Doubt makes even abundance feel inaccessible.
simple_meaning: A person may stand before a source of limitless blessing and still hesitate, simply because the source is not fully understood. That hesitation is what is happening in the speaker’s heart.
insight: It shifts the mind from timid asking to trusting reception.
modern_relevance: You sit across from someone who can help, but you keep shrinking your request because you do not want to seem greedy. The real barrier is not lack — it is doubt about generosity.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सो तुम्ह जानहु अंतरजामी। पुरवहु मोर मनोरथ स्वामी॥ सकुच बिहाइ मागु नृप मोही। मोरें नहिं अदेय कछु तोही ॥
translation: हे स्वामी! आप अन्तरयामी हैं, इसलिए उसे जानते ही हैं। मेरा वह मनोरथ पूरा कीजिए। (भगवान ने कहा-) हे राजन् ! संकोच छोड़कर मुझसे माँगो। तुम्हें न दे सकूँ ऐसा मेरे पास कुछ भी नहीं है ॥
english_translation: You know the heart within all hearts, Lord. Fulfil my desire. Cast off hesitation and ask freely, king. Nothing I have is beyond your reach.
essence: Trust makes honest asking possible.
simple_meaning: The speaker trusts Ram to know the heart and fulfil the wish. Ram answers by asking for direct, fearless asking, promising that nothing is beyond his giving.
insight: It shifts the mind from guarded wanting to open, trusting request.
modern_relevance: You rehearse the request in your head, then delete the message before sending it. The real barrier is not lack — it is hesitation. This verse asks for directness.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: दानि सिरोमनि कृपानिधि नाथ कहउँ सतिभाउ। चाहउँ तुम्हहि समान सुत प्रभु सन कवन दुराउ ॥
translation: (राजा ने कहा-) हे दानियों के शिरोमणि! हे कृपानिधान! हे नाथ! मैं अपने मन का सच्चा भाव कहता हूँ कि मैं आपके समान पुत्र चाहता हूँ। प्रभु से भला क्या छिपाना! ॥
english_translation: The king said, "O crown jewel among givers, ocean of compassion, my lord, I speak my true heart: I want a son like you. What can be hidden from the lord?"
essence: Trust makes the deepest wish speakable.
simple_meaning: Dasharath speaks with complete honesty. He asks for a son like Ram and admits that nothing can be hidden from the lord.
insight: It shifts the mind from guarded asking to wholehearted truth-telling.
modern_relevance: You sit across from someone who truly cares about you, and the words you have rehearsed finally feel unnecessary. The real request comes out plain, because trust has made honesty possible.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: देखि प्रीति सुनि बचन अमोले। एवमस्तु करुनानिधि बोले॥ आपु सरिस खोजौं कहँ जाई। नृप तव तनय होब मैं आई ॥
translation: राजा की प्रीति देखकर और उनके अमूल्य वचन सुनकर करुणानिधान भगवान बोले- ऐसा ही हो। हे राजन् ! मैं अपने समान (दूसरा) कहाँ जाकर खोजूँ! अतः स्वयं ही आकर तुम्हारा पुत्र बनूँगा ॥
english_translation: Seeing his devotion and hearing those priceless words, the compassionate one said, "So be it. O king, where shall I go to find another like myself? I will come and be born as your son."
essence: Sincere longing can bring the divine into your home.
simple_meaning: Ram accepts the king's heartfelt wish and promises to be born as his son.
insight: It shifts the mind from asking for control to trusting that sincere devotion can be answered.
modern_relevance: You speak honestly to someone you trust, without polishing your words. They hear the truth beneath the request and meet you there — not with distance, but with presence.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सतरूपहिं बिलोकि कर जोरें। देबि मागु बरु जो रुचि तोरें॥ जो बरु नाथ चतुर नृप मागा। सोइ कृपाल मोहि अति प्रिय लागा ॥
translation: शतरूपाजी को हाथ जोड़े देखकर भगवान ने कहा- हे देवी! तुम्हारी जो इच्छा हो, सो वर माँग लो। (शतरूपा ने कहा-) हे नाथ! चतुर राजा ने जो वर माँगा, हे कृपालु! वह मुझे बहुत ही प्रिय लगा, ॥
english_translation: Seeing Satarupa with folded hands, the Lord said, “O देवी, ask for whatever boon you wish.” Satarupa replied, “O Lord, the boon the wise king asked for is very dear to me, O merciful one.”
essence: A wise wish feels dear because it matches what is already true.
simple_meaning: Ram offers Satarupa any boon she wants. She says the boon asked by the wise king pleases her deeply.
insight: It shifts desire from personal preference to shared alignment with what is already right.
modern_relevance: You hear a request that already feels right in your chest, even before you say yes. The relief is not in getting your own way, but in recognizing a wise desire and blessing it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु परंतु सुठि होति ढिठाई। जदपि भगत हित तुम्हहि सोहाई॥ तुम्ह ब्रह्मादि जनक जग स्वामी। ब्रह्म सकल उर अंतरजामी ॥
translation: परंतु हे प्रभु! बहुत ढिठाई हो रही है, यद्यपि हे भक्तों का हित करने वाले! वह ढिठाई भी आपको अच्छी ही लगती है। आप ब्रह्मा आदि के भी पिता (उत्पन्न करने वाले), जगत के स्वामी और सबके हृदय के भीतर की जानने वाले ब्रह्म हैं ॥
english_translation: Lord, this is certainly bold. Yet that boldness pleases You, since You are the benefactor of devotees. You are Brahma's source, the master of the world, and the all-knowing supreme reality within every heart.
essence: Bold devotion is welcome before the one who knows every heart.
simple_meaning: Shatarupa praises Ram as the source of all beings, the ruler of the world, and the one who knows every heart. She admits her request is bold, but says such boldness pleases him because he cares for devotees.
insight: It shifts prayer from timid formality to sincere, trusting speech.
modern_relevance: You hesitate before asking for help from someone you deeply respect. Then you remember that real care makes honest asking possible, not shameful.
speaker: Shatarupa

verse_text: अस समुझत मन संसय होई। कहा जो प्रभु प्रवान पुनि सोई॥ जे निज भगत नाथ तव अहहीं। जो सुख पावहिं जो गति लहहीं ॥
translation: ऐसा समझने पर मन में संदेह होता है, फिर भी प्रभु ने जो कहा वही प्रमाण (सत्य) है। (मैं तो यह माँगती हूँ कि) हे नाथ! आपके जो निज जन हैं, वे जो (अलौकिक, अखंड) सुख पाते हैं और जिस परम गति को प्राप्त होते हैं- ॥
english_translation: Even so, my mind feels doubt. Still, what the Lord has said is true. I ask for the same bliss, the same state, and the same fate that belong to your own devotees.
essence: Doubt can remain, but trust still asks for the Lord's own gift.
simple_meaning: Parvati admits a lingering doubt, but accepts Ram's word as true. She asks to receive the same bliss and final state that Ram's own devotees receive.
insight: It shifts the mind from proof-seeking to receptive trust in the Lord's promise.
modern_relevance: You are unsure whether this path will really change anything, yet you keep listening because something in it feels true. That quiet willingness to trust is where devotion begins.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: सोइ सुख सोइ गति सोइ भगति सोइ निज चरन सनेहु। सोइ बिबेक सोइ रहनि प्रभु हमहि कृपा करि देहु ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! वही सुख, वही गति, वही भक्ति, वही अपने चरणों में प्रेम, वही ज्ञान और वही रहन-सहन कृपा करके हमें दीजिए ॥
english_translation: O Lord, grant us only that: the same joy, the same state, the same devotion, the same love for your feet, the same discernment, and the same way of living.
essence: True devotion asks for Ram himself, not separate rewards.
simple_meaning: Parvati asks Ram for the same joy, devotion, love for his feet, discernment, and way of living that belong to true devotees.
insight: It shifts desire from scattered ambitions to a single request for inner alignment with Ram.
modern_relevance: You scroll through ten different goals at midnight, but none of them quiet the ache. Then one honest sentence appears in you: let my life be shaped by what is worth loving.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: सुनि मृदु गूढ़ रुचिर बर रचना। कृपासिंधु बोले मृदु बचना॥ जो कछु रुचि तुम्हरे मन माहीं। मैं सो दीन्ह सब संसय नाहीं ॥
translation: (रानी की) कोमल, गूढ़ और मनोहर श्रेष्ठ वाक्य रचना सुनकर कृपा के समुद्र भगवान कोमल वचन बोले- तुम्हारे मन में जो कुछ इच्छा है, वह सब मैंने तुमको दिया, इसमें कोई संदेह न समझना ॥
english_translation: Hearing the queen's soft, subtle, and lovely words, the Ocean of Compassion spoke gently: "Whatever your mind desires, I have already given. Doubt it not."
essence: Grace answers before doubt can finish speaking.
simple_meaning: Ram hears the queen's humble words and gently assures her that her wish has already been granted. He removes all doubt.
insight: It teaches the mind to stop demanding extra proof once grace has already answered.
modern_relevance: You finally send the message you've been rehearsing for an hour, then stare at the screen waiting for reassurance. The answer you needed may already be there — if you can trust it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मातु बिबेक अलौकिक तोरें। कबहुँ न मिटिहि अनुग्रह मोरें॥ बंदि चरन मनु कहेउ बहोरी। अवर एक बिनती प्रभु मोरी ॥
translation: हे माता! मेरी कृपा से तुम्हारा अलौकिक ज्ञान कभी नष्ट न होगा। तब मनु ने भगवान के चरणों की वंदना करके फिर कहा- हे प्रभु! मेरी एक विनती और है- ॥
english_translation: O Mother, my grace will never let your extraordinary understanding fade. Bowing to his feet, Manu said again, "Lord, I have one more request."
essence: Grace can preserve the insight it awakens.
simple_meaning: Manu is assured that divine grace will preserve his special understanding, and he humbly asks for one more boon.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating understanding as fragile to trusting grace as sustaining.
modern_relevance: You finally understand something important after a hard season, and then you fear losing that clarity. This verse feels like the reassurance that insight can be held, not just visited.
speaker: Manu

verse_text: सुत बिषइक तव पद रति होऊ। मोहि बड़ मूढ़ कहे किन कोऊ॥ मनि बिनु फनि जिमि जल बिनु मीना। मम जीवन तिमि तुम्हहि अधीना ॥
translation: आपके चरणों में मेरी वैसी ही प्रीति हो जैसी पुत्र के लिए पिता की होती है, चाहे मुझे कोई बड़ा भारी मूर्ख ही क्यों न कहे। जैसे मणि के बिना साँप और जल के बिना मछली (नहीं रह सकती), वैसे ही मेरा जीवन आपके अधीन रहे (आपके बिना न रह सके) ॥
english_translation: May my love for your feet be like a father's love for his son. Let anyone call me a great fool. Like a serpent without its jewel and a fish without water, let my life remain dependent on you.
essence: True devotion is wanting only closeness, even at the cost of being misunderstood.
simple_meaning: Manu asks for love of Ram's feet so deep that his life depends on Ram alone, even if others think him foolish.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to dependence, making love for the divine the center of life.
modern_relevance: You choose the harder, quieter loyalty and others call it naive. Still, you keep showing up for what you love because approval is not the point.
speaker: Manu

verse_text: अस बरु मागि चरन गहि रहेऊ। एवमस्तु करुनानिधि कहेऊ॥ अब तुम्ह मम अनुसासन मानी। बसहु जाइ सुरपति रजधानी ॥
translation: ऐसा वर माँगकर राजा भगवान के चरण पकड़े रह गए। तब दया के निधान भगवान ने कहा- ऐसा ही हो। अब तुम मेरी आज्ञा मानकर देवराज इन्द्र की राजधानी (अमरावती) में जाकर वास करो ॥
english_translation: Having asked for this boon, Manu held on to the Lord's feet. Then the ocean of compassion said, “So be it. Now, obey my instruction: go and dwell in the city of Indra, the king of the gods.”
essence: True devotion accepts the boon and the command together.
simple_meaning: Manu asks for a blessing and stays at Ram's feet. Ram grants it and tells him to obey and live in Indra's city.
insight: It shifts devotion from asking for what you want to accepting the divine instruction that follows.
modern_relevance: You finally get the chance you prayed for, but it comes with a strange condition. The harder part is not receiving the gift — it's trusting the guidance that comes with it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तहँ करि भोग बिसाल तात गएँ कछु काल पुनि। होइहहु अवध भुआल तब मैं होब तुम्हार सुत ॥
translation: हे तात! वहाँ (स्वर्ग के) बहुत से भोग भोगकर, कुछ काल बीत जाने पर, तुम अवध के राजा होंगे। तब मैं तुम्हारा पुत्र होऊँगा ॥
english_translation: Father, after enjoying abundant pleasures there for some time, you will become the king of Ayodhya. Then I will become your son.
essence: Delay is not denial; the promised return is already unfolding.
simple_meaning: Dasharath will spend some time enjoying heavenly pleasures, then return to rule Ayodhya, and only after that will Ram be born as his son.
insight: It shifts attention from immediate desire to the timing of dharma and divine grace.
modern_relevance: You keep thinking the delay means nothing is happening, but life is already arranging the next turn. What feels like waiting may be the path itself.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: इच्छामय नरबेष सँवारें। होइहउँ प्रगट निकेत तुम्हारें॥ अंसन्ह सहित देह धरि ताता। करिहउँ चरित भगत सुखदाता ॥
translation: इच्छानिर्मित मनुष्य रूप सजकर मैं तुम्हारे घर प्रकट होऊँगा। हे तात! मैं अपने अंशों सहित देह धारण करके भक्तों को सुख देने वाले चरित्र करूँगा ॥
english_translation: Taking on a human form by my own will, I will appear in your house. Father, I will assume a body with my aspects and perform deeds that bring joy to devotees.
essence: The divine comes in human form to bless those who love.
simple_meaning: Ram says he will appear in human form in Dasharath's house and live out divine deeds that delight devotees.
insight: It shifts devotion from distant worship to welcoming the divine in human life and action.
modern_relevance: A child is born into a family, and only later do people see how that arrival changed everything. Some presences do not announce themselves with thunder; they enter quietly and transform a home from within.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जे सुनि सादर नर बड़भागी। भव तरिहहिं ममता मद त्यागी॥ आदिसक्ति जेहिं जग उपजाया। सोउ अवतरिहि मोरि यह माया ॥
translation: जिन (चरित्रों) को बड़े भाग्यशाली मनुष्य आदरसहित सुनकर, ममता और मद त्यागकर, भवसागर से तर जाएँगे। आदिशक्ति यह मेरी (स्वरूपभूता) माया भी, जिसने जगत को उत्पन्न किया है, अवतार लेगी ॥
english_translation: Those fortunate people who listen to these stories with reverence, giving up attachment and pride, will cross the cycle of reactivity. The primal power that created the world will also descend in my form through this veil of appearance.
essence: Reverent hearing can carry a person beyond ego.
simple_meaning: Reverent listening can free a person from attachment and pride. The same primal power that brought forth the world will also appear here in a human form.
insight: It shifts the reader from consuming sacred story as information to receiving it as a force that dissolves ego.
modern_relevance: You hear a story that strips away your ego instead of feeding it. Something in you loosens, and for a moment you stop needing to be the center.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: पुरउब मैं अभिलाष तुम्हारा। सत्य सत्य पन सत्य हमारा॥ पुनि पुनि अस कहि कृपानिधाना। अंतरधान भए भगवाना ॥
translation: इस प्रकार मैं तुम्हारी अभिलाषा पूरी करूँगा। मेरा प्रण सत्य है, सत्य है, सत्य है। कृपानिधान भगवान बार-बार ऐसा कहकर अन्तरधान हो गए ॥
english_translation: I will fulfill your wish. My vow is true, true, true. Saying this again and again, the compassionate Lord disappeared.
essence: Ram's promise is enough; his repeated vow makes doubt fall away.
simple_meaning: Ram promises to fulfill the request and repeats that his vow is absolutely true. After speaking, he disappears.
insight: It teaches trust in a promise that is complete before the proof arrives.
modern_relevance: Someone finally says, “I’ll be there,” and means it. The relief is not in the speech, but in the certainty behind it.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: दंपति उर धरि भगत कृपाला। तेहिं आश्रम निवसे कछु काला॥ समय पाइ तनु तजि अनयासा। जाइ कीन्ह अमरावति बासा ॥
translation: वे स्त्री-पुरुष (राजा-रानी) भक्तों पर कृपा करने वाले भगवान को हृदय में धारण करके कुछ काल तक उस आश्रम में रहे। फिर उन्होंने समय पाकर, सहज ही (बिना किसी कष्ट के) शरीर छोड़कर, अमरावती (इन्द्र की पुरी) में जाकर वास किया ॥
english_translation: The devoted royal couple kept the compassionate Lord in their hearts and lived in that hermitage for some time. Then, when the time came, they left the body effortlessly and took residence in Amaravati.
essence: Devotion makes even leaving the body effortless.
simple_meaning: The king and queen stayed in the hermitage while keeping the compassionate Lord in their hearts. When their time ended, they left the body without struggle and went to Amaravati.
insight: It shifts attention from clinging to the body toward a peaceful release when the time is ripe.
modern_relevance: An elderly parent slips away in sleep after years of steady prayer and quiet trust. There is no battle in the leaving, only completion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: यह इतिहास पुनीत अति उमहि कही बृषकेतु। भरद्वाज सुनु अपर पुनि राम जनम कर हेतु ॥
translation: (याज्ञवल्क्यजी कहते हैं-) हे भरद्वाज! इस अत्यन्त पवित्र इतिहास को शिवजी ने पार्वती से कहा था। अब श्रीराम के अवतार लेने का दूसरा कारण सुनो ॥
english_translation: O Bharadvaja, this most sacred history was told by Shiva to Parvati. Now hear the second reason for Ram's birth.
essence: A sacred story has more than one reason hidden inside it.
simple_meaning: Yajnavalkya tells Bharadvaja that Shiva once narrated this holy story to Parvati, and now he should hear the second reason for Ram's birth.
insight: It prepares the listener to receive a deeper cause, shifting attention from the surface event to the larger divine purpose behind it.
modern_relevance: Someone starts a family story with, 'There is more behind this than you know.' You lean in because the first explanation was only the beginning.
speaker: Yajnavalkya

verse_text: सुनु मुनि कथा पुनीत पुरानी। जो गिरिजा प्रति संभु बखानी॥ बिस्व बिदित एक कैकय देसू। सत्यकेतु तहँ बसइ नरेसू ॥
translation: हे मुनि! वह पवित्र और प्राचीन कथा सुनो, जो शिवजी ने पार्वती से कही थी। संसार में प्रसिद्ध एक कैकय देश है। वहाँ सत्यकेतु नाम का राजा रहता (राज्य करता) था ॥
english_translation: Listen, sage, to the ancient sacred story that Shiva told Parvati. In the world-famous land of Kekaya, a king named Satyaketu ruled.
essence: An old story begins with the king who will set it in motion.
simple_meaning: Shiva is introducing an old sacred story about a king from the land of Kekaya.
insight: It shifts attention from the headline event to the hidden family history beneath it.
modern_relevance: A conversation begins with a name, a place, and a memory that seem small at first. Later, you realise that this was the doorway to everything that followed.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: धरम धुरंधर नीति निधाना। तेज प्रताप सील बलवाना॥ तेहि कें भए जुगल सुत बीरा। सब गुन धाम महा रनधीरा ॥
translation: वह धर्म की धुरी को धारण करने वाला, नीति की खान, तेजस्वी, प्रतापी, सुशील और बलवान था, उसके दो वीर पुत्र हुए, जो सब गुणों के भंडार और बड़े ही रणधीर थे ॥
english_translation: He upheld righteousness, was a treasury of wise conduct, radiant, majestic, virtuous, and strong. He had two brave sons, both abodes of every good quality and great warriors.
essence: A righteous ruler naturally gives rise to heroic sons.
simple_meaning: The king is described as righteous, wise, radiant, virtuous, and strong. He has two heroic sons who possess every good quality.
insight: It sets up the family line by showing that noble rule and noble children belong together.
modern_relevance: A child hears people speak about a parent before ever meeting them. The qualities that shape a home do not stay hidden for long; they show up in the next generation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राज धनी जो जेठ सुत आही। नाम प्रतापभानु अस ताही॥ अपर सुतहि अरिमर्दन नामा। भुजबल अतुल अचल संग्रामा ॥
translation: राज्य का उत्तराधिकारी जो बड़ा लड़का था, उसका नाम प्रतापभानु था। दूसरे पुत्र का नाम अरिमर्दन था, जिसकी भुजाओं में अपार बल था और जो युद्ध में (पर्वत के समान) अटल रहता था ॥
english_translation: The elder son, heir to the throne, was named Pratapbhanu. The other son was named Arimardan, whose arms held immense strength and who stood firm in battle.
essence: Names can quietly prepare the ground for a whole life story.
simple_meaning: The king’s elder son was Pratapbhanu, and his younger son was Arimardan, a warrior of great strength and steadiness.
insight: It frames character through naming, preparing the reader for the family drama that follows.
modern_relevance: A family group chat is full of introductions before a wedding, and one name quietly carries the weight of a future role. Not every line announces a turning point; some just set the stage.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भाइहि भाइहि परम समीती। सकल दोष छल बरजित प्रीती॥ जेठे सुतहि राज नृप दीन्हा। हरि हित आपु गवन बन कीन्हा ॥
translation: भाई-भाई में बड़ा मेल और सब प्रकार के दोषों और छलों से रहित (सच्ची) प्रीति थी। राजा ने जेठे पुत्र को राज्य दे दिया और आप भगवान (के भजन) के लिए वन को चल दिए ॥
english_translation: There was deep harmony between the brothers, and their love was free of faults and deceit. The king gave the throne to his eldest son and went to the forest for the divine.
essence: True affection gives up power without resentment.
simple_meaning: The brothers lived in genuine harmony, and the king gave the kingdom to his eldest son before leaving for the forest in devotion.
insight: It shifts attention from possession to rightful handoff: love proves itself by letting the next person lead.
modern_relevance: A parent signs over the family business to the child best suited for it, then steps back instead of controlling everything. Love becomes visible when power is released cleanly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जब प्रतापरबि भयउ नृप फिरी दोहाई देस। प्रजा पाल अति बेदबिधि कतहुँ नहीं अघ लेस ॥
translation: जब प्रतापभानु राजा हुआ, देश में उसकी दुहाई फिर गई। वह वेद में बताई हुई विधि के अनुसार उत्तम रीति से प्रजा का पालन करने लगा। उसके राज्य में पाप का कहीं लेश भी नहीं रह गया ॥
english_translation: When Pratapabhanu became king, his fame spread through the land. He ruled the people according to the Vedas, and not even a trace of wrongdoing remained anywhere.
essence: Power becomes worthy only when it protects people cleanly.
simple_meaning: Pratapabhanu became king, and his rule was so just that the whole kingdom prospered and wrongdoing disappeared.
insight: It shifts attention from royal status to the moral quality of rule.
modern_relevance: A neighborhood feels different when the landlord is fair, the rules are clear, and no one has to fear being cheated. People relax because power is being used to protect, not exploit.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नृप हितकारक सचिव सयाना। नाम धरमरुचि सुक्र समाना॥ सचिव सयान बंधु बलबीरा। आपु प्रतापपुंज रनधीरा ॥
translation: राजा का हित करने वाला और शुक्राचार्य के समान बुद्धिमान धर्मरुचि नामक उसका मंत्री था। इस प्रकार बुद्धिमान मंत्री और बलवान तथा वीर भाई के साथ ही स्वयं राजा भी बड़ा प्रतापी और रणधीर था ॥
english_translation: The king had a wise minister who cared for his welfare, named Dharmaruchi, like Shukracharya. The wise minister and the strong, brave brother stood with him, and the king himself was full of splendor and fearless in battle.
essence: Power holds when wisdom, loyalty, and courage stand together.
simple_meaning: The king is supported by a wise minister, a strong brother, and his own courage. The verse is building the picture of his power and readiness for rule.
insight: It shifts attention from lone heroism to the network of wisdom, loyalty, and courage that makes leadership possible.
modern_relevance: Before a big launch, one person has strategy, another handles the pressure, and a third keeps morale steady. Success rarely comes from one strong figure alone.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सेन संग चतुरंग अपारा। अमित सुभट सब समर जुझारा॥ सेन बिलोकि राउ हरषाना। अरु बाजे गहगहे निसाना ॥
translation: साथ में अपार चतुरंगिणी सेना थी, जिसमें असंख्य योद्धा थे, जो सब के सब रण में जूझ मरने वाले थे। अपनी सेना को देखकर राजा बहुत प्रसन्न हुआ और घमाघम नगाड़े बजने लगे ॥
english_translation: He had an immense fourfold army, with countless warriors ready for battle. Seeing his forces, the king rejoiced, and loud drums rang out.
essence: An army can inspire confidence before a single battle is fought.
simple_meaning: The king's army was huge and battle-ready. He felt pleased when he saw its strength, and war drums sounded loudly.
insight: It shifts attention from inner preparation to the outward display of force.
modern_relevance: You open the campaign dashboard and see the numbers spike. The room feels electric, the team cheers, and the plan finally looks real.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिजय हेतु कटकई बनाई। सुदिन साधि नृप चलेउ बजाई॥ जहँ तहँ परीं अनेक लराईं। जीते सकल भूप बरिआईं ॥
translation: दिग्विजय के लिए सेना सजाकर वह राजा शुभ दिन (मुहूर्त) साधकर और डंका बजाकर चला। जहाँ-तहाँ बहुतसी लड़ाइयाँ हुईं। उसने सब राजाओं को बलपूर्वक जीत लिया ॥
english_translation: He assembled an army for victory, chose an auspicious day, and marched with drums sounding. Battles broke out everywhere, and he conquered all kings by sheer force.
essence: Victory by force still arrives through many battles.
simple_meaning: The king set out with a prepared army, picked an auspicious time, and won battles everywhere by force.
insight: It keeps attention on outward conquest, showing how quickly ambition turns into conflict.
modern_relevance: A campaign launches with banners, planning, and confidence. Then the real world hits back in fragments, and every win still depends on force.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सप्त दीप भुजबल बस कीन्हे। लै लै दंड छाड़ि नृप दीन्हे॥ सकल अवनि मंडल तेहि काला। एक प्रतापभानु महिपाला ॥
translation: अपनी भुजाओं के बल से उसने सातों द्वीपों (भूमिखण्डों) को वश में कर लिया और राजाओं से दंड (कर) ले-लेकर उन्हें छोड़ दिया। सम्पूर्ण पृथ्वी मंडल का उस समय प्रतापभानु ही एकमात्र (चक्रवर्ती) राजा था ॥
english_translation: By the strength of his arms, he brought the seven islands under control and made kings pay tribute before releasing them. In that time, only Pratapbhanu was the sole sovereign of the whole earth.
essence: Worldly rule can stretch across everything and still last only for a moment.
simple_meaning: Pratapbhanu conquered a vast realm, collected tribute from other kings, and ruled as the only emperor of the earth.
insight: It frames success as expansion that can be recorded, admired, and still remain only a passing condition.
modern_relevance: A leader wins one contract after another, the office celebrates, and every chart points upward. For a moment it feels like the whole field belongs to one name.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: स्वबस बिस्व करि बाहुबल निज पुर कीन्ह प्रबेसु। अरथ धरम कामादि सुख सेवइ समयँ नरेसु ॥
translation: संसारभर को अपनी भुजाओं के बल से वश में करके राजा ने अपने नगर में प्रवेश किया। राजा अर्थ, धर्म और काम आदि के सुखों का समयानुसार सेवन करता था ॥
english_translation: Having brought the whole world under his control by his own arm-strength, the king entered his city. The king enjoyed wealth, duty, desire, and other pleasures at the proper time.
essence: True strength includes knowing when to enjoy and when to hold back.
simple_meaning: A powerful king conquered the world and returned to rule his city well, enjoying life’s aims in their proper place and time.
insight: It shifts attention from winning alone to governing power with timing, balance, and restraint.
modern_relevance: You finally finish the big project, win the argument, or get the promotion. The real test comes after: can you return home and live wisely, without letting victory turn into excess?
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूप प्रतापभानु बल पाई। कामधेनु भै भूमि सुहाई॥ सब दुख बरजित प्रजा सुखारी। धरमसील सुंदर नर नारी ॥
translation: राजा प्रतापभानु का बल पाकर भूमि सुंदर कामधेनु (मनचाही वस्तु देने वाली) हो गई। (उनके राज्य में) प्रजा सब (प्रकार के) दुःखों से रहित और सुखी थी और सभी स्त्री-पुरुष सुंदर और धर्मात्मा थे ॥
english_translation: By the strength of King Pratapbhanu, the land became like a wish-fulfilling cow. All the people were free from suffering and lived in happiness; men and women were beautiful and righteous.
essence: True power shows up as a whole society becoming easier to live in.
simple_meaning: King Pratapbhanu's rule made the land prosperous and pleasant. People lived without suffering, and society was orderly, happy, and righteous.
insight: It shifts attention from personal glory to the social conditions a ruler creates.
modern_relevance: A neighborhood feels different when the local leader is fair, calm, and dependable. People stop bracing for trouble and start living normally, because the atmosphere itself has changed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सचिव धरमरुचि हरि पद प्रीती। नृप हित हेतु सिखव नित नीती॥ गुर सुर संत पितर महिदेवा। करइ सदा नृप सब कै सेवा ॥
translation: धर्मरुचि मंत्री का श्री हरि के चरणों में प्रेम था। वह राजा के हित के लिए सदा उसको नीति सिखाया करता था। राजा गुरु, देवता, संत, पितर और ब्राह्मण- इन सबकी सदा सेवा करता रहता था ॥
english_translation: The minister Dharmaruchi loved the feet of Hari. For the king's welfare, he always taught policy and right conduct. The king always served the teacher, the radiant beings, saints, ancestors, and holy men.
essence: Power stays clean when counsel is given in love and received in humility.
simple_meaning: A wise minister loved Ram and kept advising the king for his welfare. The king, in turn, respected and served teachers, saints, ancestors, and holy men.
insight: It shifts authority from pride to service, showing that real power listens, learns, and honors what is worthy.
modern_relevance: A manager who tells the truth even when it is inconvenient, and a leader who listens instead of defending ego — that combination keeps a team healthy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूप धरम जे बेद बखाने। सकल करइ सादर सुख माने॥ दिन प्रति देइ बिबिध बिधि दाना। सुनइ सास्त्र बर बेद पुराना ॥
translation: वेदों में राजाओं के जो धर्म बताए गए हैं, राजा सदा आदरपूर्वक और सुख मानकर उन सबका पालन करता था। प्रतिदिन अनेक प्रकार के दान देता और उत्तम शास्त्र, वेद और पुराण सुनता था ॥
english_translation: The duties of kings described in the Vedas were all performed with respect and joy. Each day he gave many kinds of charity and listened to excellent scriptures, the Vedas, and the Puranas.
essence: Righteous rule is daily discipline, generosity, and learning.
simple_meaning: The king followed the duties laid out for rulers, gave charity every day, and regularly listened to sacred teachings.
insight: It shifts leadership from status to steady self-education and generous action.
modern_relevance: A manager who reads the same hard feedback every morning, gives credit freely, and keeps learning instead of coasting is doing this verse in modern form.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाना बापीं कूप तड़ागा। सुमन बाटिका सुंदर बागा॥ बिप्रभवन सुरभवन सुहाए। सब तीरथन्ह विचित्र बनाए ॥
translation: उसने बहुत सी बावलियाँ, कुएँ, तालाब, फुलवाड़ियाँ सुंदर बगीचे, ब्राह्मणों के लिए घर और देवताओं के सुंदर विचित्र मंदिर सब तीर्थों में बनवाए ॥
english_translation: He built many wells, ponds, tanks, flower-gardens, beautiful parks, houses for priests, pleasing temples for the radiant beings, and all kinds of sacred places.
essence: Real rule shows itself in what it builds for others.
simple_meaning: The king built wells, ponds, gardens, priestly homes, temples, and sacred sites everywhere.
insight: It shifts leadership from display to service: build what sustains daily life and sacred life together.
modern_relevance: A city block with no shade, no water, no quiet place to sit feels harsh. This verse imagines leadership that makes life easier, greener, and more livable for everyone.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ लजि कहे पुरान श्रुति एक एक सब जाग। बार सहस्र सहस्र नृप किए सहित अनुराग ॥
translation: वेद और पुराणों में जितने प्रकार के यज्ञ कहे गए हैं, राजा ने एक-एक करके उन सब यज्ञों को प्रेम सहित हजार-हजार बार किया ॥
english_translation: The king performed every sacrifice described in the Vedas and Puranas, again and again, with love.
essence: Love makes repeated sacred action feel natural, not heavy.
simple_meaning: The king carried out every prescribed sacrifice many times, and he did it with devotion, not reluctance.
insight: It shifts attention from ritual performance to the spirit of loving consistency behind it.
modern_relevance: A person quietly keeps showing up for the same responsibility year after year — the school fundraiser, the family ritual, the community duty — not for praise, but because the heart is in it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हृदयँ न कछु फल अनुसंधाना। भूप बिबेकी परम सुजाना॥ करइ जे धरम करम मन बानी। बासुदेव अर्पित नृप ग्यानी ॥
translation: (राजा के) हृदय में किसी फल की टोह (कामना) न थी। राजा बड़ा ही बुद्धिमान और ज्ञानी था। वह ज्ञानी राजा कर्म, मन और वाणी से जो कुछ भी धर्म करता था, सब भगवान वासुदेव को अर्पित करते रहता था ॥
english_translation: The king sought no reward in his heart. He was wise, discerning, and supremely intelligent. Whatever he did in duty, thought, and speech, that king offered to Vasudeva.
essence: True action is rewardless offering.
simple_meaning: A wise king did his duties with no desire for reward. He offered every action, thought, and word to the divine.
insight: It shifts action from self-benefit to offering, so work stays pure even when results are uncertain.
modern_relevance: You finish a hard task, send it out, and refuse to keep checking for praise. The cleanest work comes from giving fully without bargaining with the result.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चढ़ि बर बाजि बार एक राजा। मृगया कर सब साजि समाजा॥ बिंध्याचल गभीर बन गयऊ। मृग पुनीत बहु मारत भयऊ ॥
translation: एक बार वह राजा एक अच्छे घोड़े पर सवार होकर, शिकार का सब सामान सजाकर विंध्याचल के घने जंगल में गया और वहाँ उसने बहुत से उत्तम-उत्तम हिरन मारे ॥
english_translation: Once the king rode out on a fine horse with all his hunting gear and entered the deep forest of Vindhyachal, where he killed many noble deer.
essence: Power without restraint quickly turns into harm.
simple_meaning: The king went into the deep forest with hunting gear and killed many deer.
insight: It shifts attention from royal display to the moral weight of casual violence.
modern_relevance: You start the day treating something as harmless entertainment, and by noon you have hurt people or things you meant to overlook.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: फिरत बिपिन नृप दीख बराहू। जनु बन दुरेउ ससिहि ग्रसि राहू॥ बड़ बिधु नहिं समात मुख माहीं। मनहुँ क्रोध बस उगिलत नाहीं ॥
translation: राजा ने वन में फिरते हुए एक सूअर को देखा। (दाँतों के कारण वह ऐसा दिख पड़ता था) मानो चन्द्रमा को ग्रसकर (मुँह में पकड़कर) राहु वन में आ छिपा हो। चन्द्रमा बड़ा होने से उसके मुँह में समाता नहीं है और मानो क्रोधवश वह भी उसे उगलता नहीं है ॥
english_translation: While roaming the forest, the king saw a boar, as if Rahu had swallowed the moon and hidden in the woods. The moon was too large for its mouth, and in anger it seemed not to spit it out.
essence: A forest sight is made vast through cosmic imagery.
simple_meaning: The king sees a huge boar in the forest, described with a vivid comparison to Rahu swallowing the moon. It is a visual description, not a teaching verse.
insight: It slows the reader down to see the scene before the hunt continues.
modern_relevance: You catch sight of something enormous moving through the trees on an early morning drive, and for a second the whole world narrows to that one shape. The verse does the same with the boar.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोल कराल दसन छबि गाई। तनु बिसाल पीवर अधिकाई॥ घुरुघुरात हय आरौ पाएँ। चकित बिलोकत कान उठाएँ ॥
translation: यह तो सूअर के भयानक दाँतों की शोभा कही गई। (इधर) उसका शरीर भी बहुत विशाल और मोटा था। घोड़े की आहट पाकर वह घुरघुराता हुआ कान उठाए चौकन्ना होकर देख रहा था ॥
english_translation: Its fearsome tusks were praised, and its body was huge and very stout. Hearing the horse’s sound, it grunted, lifted its ears, and stared in alert surprise.
essence: The boar’s size and vigilance heighten the chase.
simple_meaning: The boar is described as huge, fierce, and alert. It hears the horse and reacts at once.
insight: It slows the action to sharpen the threat before the pursuit begins.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नील महीधर सिखर सम देखि बिसाल बराहु। चपरि चलेउ हय सुटुकि नृप हाँकि न होइ निबाहु ॥
translation: नील पर्वत के शिखर के समान विशाल (शरीर वाले) उस सूअर को देखकर राजा घोड़े को चाबुक लगाकर तेजी से चला और उसने सूअर को ललकारा कि अब तेरा बचाव नहीं हो सकता ॥
english_translation: Seeing the huge boar, as large as a mountain peak, the king urged his horse forward at once and challenged it, as if saying there would be no escape now.
essence: The chase begins the instant fear is answered with speed.
simple_meaning: The king sees the huge boar and rushes after it on horseback, challenging it to flee if it can.
insight: It shifts attention from observation to immediate pursuit.
modern_relevance: You spot the problem before everyone else does. Instead of circling it for an hour, you move straight toward it and deal with it now.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आवत देखि अधिक रव बाजी। चलेउ बराह मरुत गति भाजी॥ तुरत कीन्ह नृप सर संधाना। महि मिलि गयउ बिलोकत बाना ॥
translation: अधिक शब्द करते हुए घोड़े को (अपनी तरफ) आता देखकर सूअर पवन वेग से भाग चला। राजा ने तुरंत ही बाण को धनुष पर चढ़ाया। सूअर बाण को देखते ही धरती में दुबक गया ॥
english_translation: Seeing the horse coming closer, the boar ran away at the speed of the wind. The king quickly fitted an arrow to his bow, and the boar, seeing the arrow, sank into the earth.
essence: The chase begins, and the boar slips from sight.
simple_meaning: The boar flees when the horse nears. The king readies his arrow at once, and the boar hides itself in the ground.
insight: It keeps the action moving by showing the boar’s evasive fear and the king’s immediate response.
modern_relevance: A tense conversation starts to turn serious, and the other person suddenly dodges the issue. You feel the chase begin before either side says the real thing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तकि तकि तीर महीस चलावा। करि छल सुअर सरीर बचावा॥ प्रगटत दुरत जाइ मृग भागा। रिस बस भूप चलेउ सँग लागा ॥
translation: राजा तक-तककर तीर चलाता है, परन्तु सूअर छल करके शरीर को बचाता जाता है। वह पशु कभी प्रकट होता और कभी छिपता हुआ भाग जाता था और राजा भी क्रोध के वश उसके साथ (पीछे) लगा चला जाता था ॥
english_translation: The king shot arrows again and again, but the boar kept saving its body through trickery. Appearing and disappearing, it ran off like a deer, and the king, driven by anger, kept chasing after it.
essence: Anger makes pursuit feel like purpose.
simple_meaning: The king keeps shooting, but the boar dodges and runs off. Anger drives the king to keep chasing it deeper into the forest.
insight: It shows how anger can trap a person in reactive pursuit instead of clear judgment.
modern_relevance: You keep refreshing the message thread, trying to get the last word. The more they slip away, the more your temper pulls you forward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गयउ दूरि घन गहन बराहू। जहँ नाहिन गज बाजि निबाहू॥ अति अकेल बन बिपुल कलेसू। तदपि न मृग मग तजइ नरेसू ॥
translation: सूअर बहुत दूर ऐसे घने जंगल में चला गया, जहाँ हाथी-घोड़े का निबाह (गमन) नहीं था। राजा बिलकुल अकेला था और वन में क्लेश भी बहुत था, फिर भी राजा ने उस पशु का पीछा नहीं छोड़ा ॥
english_translation: The boar went far into a dense forest where elephants and horses could not follow. The king was utterly alone, the forest was full of hardship, yet he did not abandon the chase.
essence: Difficulty does not cancel resolve.
simple_meaning: The king keeps chasing the boar even when the path becomes lonely and difficult. He does not give up just because the terrain is harsh.
insight: It teaches you to stay with a worthy task even when support disappears and conditions turn difficult.
modern_relevance: You are the last one still troubleshooting at midnight after the team has gone home. The problem is messy, the path is ugly, and quitting would be easier — but you keep going.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोल बिलोकि भूप बड़ धीरा। भागि पैठ गिरिगुहाँ गभीरा॥ अगम देखि नृप अति पछिताई। फिरेउ महाबन परेउ भुलाई ॥
translation: राजा को बड़ा धैर्यवान देखकर, सूअर भागकर पहाड़ की एक गहरी गुफा में जा घुसा। उसमें जाना कठिन देखकर राजा को बहुत पछताकर लौटना पड़ा, पर उस घोर वन में वह रास्ता भूल गया ॥
english_translation: Seeing the king’s great patience, the boar ran into a deep mountain cave. Finding it impossible to enter, the king turned back in deep regret, but in that vast forest he lost his way.
essence: A hard chase can leave the pursuer more lost than the quarry.
simple_meaning: The boar escapes into a deep cave, and the king cannot follow. Frustrated and lost, he turns back and loses his way in the forest.
insight: It shifts attention from pursuit to the cost of stubborn chasing when the situation has already slipped beyond control.
modern_relevance: You keep chasing a problem through endless tabs, calls, and dead ends. Then the trail goes cold, and suddenly you are the one who feels lost.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: खेद खिन्न छुद्धित तृषित राजा बाजि समेत। खोजत ब्याकुल सरित सर जल बिनु भयउ अचेत ॥
translation: बहुत परिश्रम करने से थका हुआ और घोड़े समेत भूख-प्यास से व्याकुल राजा नदी-तालाब खोजता-खोजता पानी बिना बेहाल हो गया ॥
english_translation: The king, exhausted, hungry, and thirsty, wandered with his horse, searching for lakes and rivers. Finding no water, he fell senseless.
essence: Pursuit without rest ends in collapse.
simple_meaning: The king grows exhausted and desperate as he searches for water with his horse. With no water to be found, he collapses.
insight: It shifts attention from heroic striving to bodily limits and vulnerability.
modern_relevance: You keep circling the city after a long day, phone dying, throat dry, and every café is closed. At some point, effort alone cannot carry you further.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: फिरत बिपिन आश्रम एक देखा। तहँ बस नृपति कपट मुनिबेषा॥ जासु देस नृप लीन्ह छड़ाई। समर सेन तजि गयउ पराई ॥
translation: वन में फिरते-फिरते उसने एक आश्रम देखा, वहाँ कपट से मुनि का वेष बनाए एक राजा रहता था, जिसका देश राजा प्रतापभानु ने छीन लिया था और जो सेना को छोड़कर युद्ध से भाग गया था ॥
english_translation: Roaming through the forest, he saw one hermitage. There lived a king disguised as a mendicant. He had lost his kingdom to King Pratapbhanu and had abandoned his army, fleeing the battle.
essence: A false renunciate can still carry the wound of flight.
simple_meaning: While wandering in the forest, the king saw a hermitage where a deposed ruler lived in disguise, having lost his kingdom and fled the battle.
insight: It prepares the reader for a hidden identity and shows how defeat can drive a person into disguise.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a retreat who speaks softly, dresses simply, and seems transformed. Then you learn they are hiding from the very life they abandoned. The costume cannot erase the escape.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समय प्रतापभानु कर जानी। आपन अति असमय अनुमानी॥ गयउ न गृह मन बहुत गलानी। मिला न राजहि नृप अभिमानी ॥
translation: प्रतापभानु का समय (अच्छे दिन) जानकर और अपना कुसमय (बुरे दिन) अनुमानकर उसके मन में बड़ी ग्लानि हुई। इससे वह न तो घर गया और न अभिमानी होने के कारण राजा प्रतापभानु से ही मिला (मेल किया) ॥
english_translation: Knowing the time was favorable for King Pratapbhanu and sensing his own time was unfavorable, he felt deep shame. So he did not return home, and pride kept him from meeting the king.
essence: Shame and pride can both keep a fallen person from seeking help.
simple_meaning: He sees that the king’s fortune is rising while his own has fallen, and shame keeps him from going home or facing the king.
insight: It shows how status loss can turn into withdrawal instead of repair.
modern_relevance: You get the message that someone else is moving ahead while you feel left behind. Shame says disappear; pride says don’t reach out. Both can keep you isolated.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रिस उर मारि रंक जिमि राजा। बिपिन बसइ तापस कें साजा॥ तासु समीप गवन नृप कीन्हा। यह प्रतापरबि तेहिं तब चीन्हा ॥
translation: दरिद्र की भाँति मन ही में क्रोध को मारकर वह राजा तपस्वी के वेष में वन में रहता था। राजा (प्रतापभानु) उसी के पास गया। उसने तुरंत पहचान लिया कि यह प्रतापभानु है ॥
english_translation: Having crushed anger within, the king lived in the forest like a beggar, dressed as a hermit. When Pratapbhanu approached him, he immediately recognized him.
essence: Disguise can hide rank, not recognition.
simple_meaning: A king hid his anger, lived in the forest as an ascetic, and recognized another king who came near him.
insight: It shows that outer roles can hide inner states, but careful awareness still reads the truth.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room thinking no one knows what you are carrying. Someone with sharper attention notices the strain in your face before you speak.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राउ तृषित नहिं सो पहिचाना। देखि सुबेष महामुनि जाना॥ उतरि तुरग तें कीन्ह प्रनामा। परम चतुर न कहेउ निज नामा ॥
translation: राजा प्यासा होने के कारण (व्याकुलता में) उसे पहचान न सका। सुंदर वेष देखकर राजा ने उसे महामुनि समझा और घोड़े से उतरकर उसे प्रणाम किया, परन्तु बड़ा चतुर होने के कारण राजा ने उसे अपना नाम नहीं बताया ॥
english_translation: The king, thirsty and distracted, did not recognize him. Seeing his fine disguise, the king took him for a great sage. He got down from the horse and bowed, but the clever king did not reveal his own name.
essence: Need makes pride pause, and courtesy remains.
simple_meaning: The thirsty king mistakes the disguised man for a sage, bows to him, and keeps his own identity hidden.
insight: It shifts attention from status to conduct: even confusion can be met with respectful restraint.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a difficult moment and cannot tell who they really are. You still choose courtesy, because humility matters more than control.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूपति तृषित बिलोकि तेहिं सरबरू दीन्ह देखाइ। मज्जन पान समेत हय कीन्ह नृपति हरषाइ ॥
translation: राजा को प्यासा देखकर उसने सरोवर दिखला दिया। हर्षित होकर राजा ने घोड़े सहित उसमें स्नान और जलपान किया ॥
english_translation: Seeing the king thirsty, he showed him a lake. Delighted, the king bathed and drank there with his horse.
essence: Kindness begins with noticing another’s need.
simple_meaning: Seeing the king’s thirst, the ascetic showed him a lake. The king happily bathed and drank there with his horse.
insight: It highlights simple hospitality before the story turns to deeper instruction.
modern_relevance: You hand someone a glass of water after a long, hot commute. It seems small, but that one gesture can change the whole mood of the day.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गै श्रम सकल सुखी नृप भयऊ। निज आश्रम तापस लै गयऊ॥ आसन दीन्ह अस्त रबि जानी। पुनि तापस बोलेउ मृदु बानी ॥
translation: सारी थकावट मिट गई, राजा सुखी हो गया। तब तपस्वी उसे अपने आश्रम में ले गया और सूर्यास्त का समय जानकर उसने (राजा को बैठने के लिए) आसन दिया। फिर वह तपस्वी कोमल वाणी से बोला- ॥
english_translation: The king’s fatigue vanished. The ascetic took him to his own hermitage, gave him a seat when he saw the sun had set, and then spoke in a gentle voice.
essence: Gentle hospitality opens the way for honest speech.
simple_meaning: The king rests at the ascetic’s hermitage, and the ascetic treats him kindly before asking anything.
insight: It shifts attention from the event to the atmosphere of trust being created.
modern_relevance: After a long train ride, a stranger offers you a chair, water, and a quiet minute before asking who you are. That small care lowers the guard before any real conversation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: को तुम्ह कस बन फिरहु अकेलें। सुंदर जुबा जीव परहेलें॥ चक्रबर्ति के लच्छन तोरें। देखत दया लागि अति मोरें ॥
translation: तुम कौन हो? सुंदर युवक होकर, जीवन की परवाह न करके वन में अकेले क्यों फिर रहे हो? तुम्हारे चक्रवर्ती राजा के से लक्षण देखकर मुझे बड़ी दया आती है ॥
english_translation: Who are you, and why do you wander alone in the forest, handsome youth? Seeing the marks of a universal ruler in you, I feel great pity.
essence: Royal bearing can still look like loneliness in the forest.
simple_meaning: The speaker asks an unknown young man who he is, why he is alone in the forest, and says his royal bearing inspires pity.
insight: It shifts attention from the surface encounter to the hidden story behind a person’s condition.
modern_relevance: You meet someone on a late train platform, dressed well but looking stranded. Before you know their story, you can still sense they have fallen far from where they belong.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: नाम प्रतापभानु अवनीसा। तासु सचिव मैं सुनहु मुनीसा॥ फिरत अहेरें परेउँ भुलाई। बड़ें भाग देखेउँ पद आई ॥
translation: (राजा ने कहा-) हे मुनीश्वर! सुनिए, प्रतापभानु नाम का एक राजा है, मैं उसका मंत्री हूँ। शिकार के लिए फिरते हुए राह भूल गया हूँ। बड़े भाग्य से यहाँ आकर मैंने आपके चरणों के दर्शन पाए हैं ॥
english_translation: I am a minister of King Pratapbhanu, lord of this land. While hunting, I lost my way. By great good fortune, I have come to your feet.
essence: What looks like getting lost can be the start of grace.
simple_meaning: The speaker introduces himself as King Pratapbhanu’s minister and says he lost his way while hunting. He feels fortunate to have reached the sage’s feet.
insight: It frames an accidental meeting as fortunate, preparing the listener for a hidden turning point.
modern_relevance: You take the wrong exit after a long drive and end up at a quiet house you never meant to visit. What felt like a mistake becomes the meeting that changes the day.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: हम कहँ दुर्लभ दरस तुम्हारा। जानत हौं कछु भल होनिहारा॥ कह मुनि तात भयउ अँधिआरा। जोजन सत्तरि नगरु तुम्हारा ॥
translation: हमें आपका दर्शन दुर्लभ था, इससे जान पड़ता है कुछ भला होने वाला है। मुनि ने कहा- हे तात! अँधेरा हो गया। तुम्हारा नगर यहाँ से सत्तर योजन पर है ॥
english_translation: “Your sight is hard to obtain. I know that some good fortune is near.” The sage said, “Dear one, darkness has fallen. Your city is seventy leagues away.”
essence: A fortunate meeting can arrive just as night makes action impossible.
simple_meaning: The sage tells the traveler that meeting him is a good sign, then warns that night has fallen and the city is far away.
insight: It teaches you to hold both intuition and reality at once: a hopeful sign does not cancel practical limits.
modern_relevance: You finally meet the right person after a long day, and the conversation feels meaningful. Still, the train is gone, the roads are dark, and you need to stay put tonight.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निसा घोर गंभीर बन पंथ न सुनहु सुजान। बसहु आजु अस जानि तुम्ह जाएहु होत बिहान ॥
translation: हे सुजान! सुनो, घोर अँधेरी रात है, घना जंगल है, रास्ता नहीं है, ऐसा समझकर तुम आज यहीं ठहर जाओ, सबेरा होते ही चले जाना ॥
english_translation: O wise one, the night is deep and the forest path is dark. Stay here today, and go at dawn.
essence: Wait for daylight before you move.
simple_meaning: The night is too dark and the forest road is unsafe. Stay where you are and travel after sunrise.
insight: It teaches you to delay action until conditions become clear and safe.
modern_relevance: You are driving on an unfamiliar road after midnight, GPS drifting and fatigue rising. The smartest move is not courage; it is stopping and waiting for daylight.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तुलसी जसि भवतब्यता तैसी मिलइ सहाइ। आपुनु आवइ ताहि पहिं ताहि तहाँ लै जाइ ॥
translation: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- जैसी भवितव्यता (होनहार) होती है, वैसी ही सहायता मिल जाती है। या तो वह आप ही उसके पास आती है या उसको वहाँ ले जाती है ॥
english_translation: Tulsidas says: Whatever is meant to happen finds its own helper. Either it comes by itself, or it brings the person there.
essence: What is meant to happen brings its own help.
simple_meaning: Whatever is truly meant to happen will find support. Sometimes help comes to you; sometimes life carries you to the right place.
insight: It shifts the mind from anxious control to trust in the unfolding of events.
modern_relevance: You missed the last train, then a friend called with a spare room. The plan looked broken, but life quietly rearranged itself around what needed to happen.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भलेहिं नाथ आयसु धरि सीसा। बाँधि तुरग तरु बैठ महीसा॥ नृप बहु भाँति प्रसंसेउ ताही। चरन बंदि निज भाग्य सराही ॥
translation: हे नाथ! बहुत अच्छा, ऐसा कहकर और उसकी आज्ञा सिर चढ़ाकर, घोड़े को वृक्ष से बाँधकर राजा बैठ गया। राजा ने उसकी बहुत प्रकार से प्रशंसा की और उसके चरणों की वंदना करके अपने भाग्य की सराहना की ॥
english_translation: “Very well, Lord,” he said, taking the command on his head. He tied the horse to a tree and sat down. The king praised him in many ways, bowed at his feet, and blessed his own fortune.
essence: True nobility bows before wise guidance.
simple_meaning: The king accepts the order, secures the horse, and praises the one who guided him. He bows in gratitude and feels blessed by the encounter.
insight: It trains the mind to accept guidance quickly and respond with gratitude, not ego.
modern_relevance: Your plan gets interrupted on a dark road, and the person with more experience says, “Stop here.” You could bristle — or you could recognize protection in the delay.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि बोलेउ मृदु गिरा सुहाई। जानि पिता प्रभु करउँ ढिठाई॥ मोहि मुनीस सुत सेवक जानी। नाथ नाम निज कहहु बखानी ॥
translation: फिर सुंदर कोमल वाणी से कहा- हे प्रभो! आपको पिता जानकर मैं ढिठाई करता हूँ। हे मुनीश्वर! मुझे अपना पुत्र और सेवक जानकर अपना नाम (धाम) विस्तार से बतलाइए ॥
english_translation: Then he spoke again in a soft, pleasant voice: "Knowing you as my father, I am being bold. O sage, knowing me as your son and servant, please tell me your name and lineage in full."
essence: Respectful humility makes the right question possible.
