simple_meaning: A respectful stranger speaks gently to the sage, calling him father and asking him to identify himself and explain his name and lineage.
insight: It teaches you to approach wisdom with humility before asking for answers.
modern_relevance: You meet someone generous at a retreat and, instead of rushing in, you ask who they are and how they came to be there. Respect first. Curiosity second. That order changes everything.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तेहि न जान नृप नृपहि सो जाना। भूप सुहृद सो कपट सयाना॥ बैरी पुनि छत्री पुनि राजा। छल बल कीन्ह चहइ निज काजा ॥
translation: राजा ने उसको नहीं पहचाना, पर वह राजा को पहचान गया था। राजा तो शुद्ध हृदय था और वह कपट करने में चतुर था। एक तो वैरी, फिर जाति का क्षत्रिय, फिर राजा। वह छल-बल से अपना काम बनाना चाहता था ॥
english_translation: The king did not recognize him, but he recognized the king. The king had a pure heart, while he was clever in deceit. An enemy, yet a Kshatriya, yet a king, he wanted to get his way through trickery and force.
essence: Pure hearts can be outmatched by cunning motives.
simple_meaning: The king does not see the man’s true nature, but the man sees the king clearly. One is sincere; the other is skilled in deceit and wants to use trickery and force.
insight: It teaches you to notice hidden intent beneath polite words, and to value sincerity over clever manipulation.
modern_relevance: A smooth-talking person shows up in a meeting with a friendly smile and a hidden agenda. You feel the shift before anyone else does. This verse names that uneasy clarity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समुझि राजसुख दुखित अराती। अवाँ अनल इव सुलगइ छाती॥ ससरल बचन नृप के सुनि काना। बयर सँभारि हृदयँ हरषाना ॥
translation: वह शत्रु अपने राज्य सुख को समझ करके (स्मरण करके) दुःखी था। उसकी छाती (कुम्हार के) आँवे की आग की तरह (भीतर ही भीतर) सुलग रही थी। राजा के सरल वचन कान से सुनकर, अपने वैर को यादकर वह हृदय में हर्षित हुआ ॥
english_translation: Remembering his royal comfort, the enemy burned with hidden anger. Hearing the king's plain words, he rejoiced inwardly at his old hatred.
essence: Old hatred can smolder beneath polite words.
simple_meaning: The enemy is still carrying old hatred. The king speaks simply, and that only makes the enemy's hidden anger flare up.
insight: It shows how unresolved resentment distorts hearing, so even plain speech gets filtered through old injury.
modern_relevance: Someone smiles at your apology, but their jaw stays tight. They say the right words, yet the old injury is still burning underneath, waiting for a chance to come back out.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कपट बोरि बानी मृदल बोलेउ जुगुति समेत। नाम हमार भिखारि अब निर्धन रहित निकेत ॥
translation: वह कपट में डुबोकर बड़ी युक्ति के साथ कोमल वाणी बोला- अब हमारा नाम भिखारी है, क्योंकि हम निर्धन और अनिकेत (घर-द्वारहीन) हैं ॥
english_translation: He spoke sweetly, masking deceit with cleverness: “Now my name is beggar, for I am poor and homeless.”
essence: Deceit often arrives wearing gentleness.
simple_meaning: He speaks softly and cleverly, hiding his deceit. He pretends to be a poor, homeless beggar.
insight: It teaches you to look past soft language and notice the intent underneath.
modern_relevance: Someone messages with perfect politeness, but every line is designed to get something from you. The tone feels kind; the motive is not.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह नृप जे बिग्यान निधाना। तुम्ह सारिखे गलित अभिमाना॥ सदा रहहिं अपनपौ दुराएँ। सब बिधि कुसल कुबेष बनाएँ ॥
translation: राजा ने कहा- जो आपके सदृश विज्ञान के निधान और सर्वथा अभिमानरहित होते हैं, वे अपने स्वरूप को सदा छिपाए रहते हैं, क्योंकि कुवेष बनाकर रहने में ही सब तरह का कल्याण है (प्रकट संत वेश में मान होने की सम्भावना है और मान से पतन की) ॥
english_translation: The king said, 'Those who are like you are treasures of wisdom and free from pride. They always hide their true nature, because wearing a disguise brings safety in every way.'
essence: Real wisdom hides itself and stays untouched by pride.
simple_meaning: Truly wise people do not advertise themselves. They stay humble and often keep a low profile, because pride and display can lead to trouble.
insight: It shifts attention from self-display to quiet protection of character.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a train platform in plain clothes who turns out to be far more accomplished than they look. The point is not image — it is the safety of staying unadvertised.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहि तें कहहिं संत श्रुति टेरें। परम अकिंचन प्रिय हरि केरें॥ तुम्ह सम अधन भिखारि अगेहा। होत बिरंचि सिवहि संदेहा ॥
translation: इसी से तो संत और वेद पुकारकर कहते हैं कि परम अकिंचन (सर्वथा अहंकार, ममता और मानरहित) ही भगवान को प्रिय होते हैं। आप सरीखे निर्धन, भिखारी और गृहहीनों को देखकर ब्रह्मा और शिवजी को भी संदेह हो जाता है (कि वे वास्तविक संत हैं या भिखारी) ॥
english_translation: Because of this, the saints and the Vedas cry out that the one who is utterly without possessions is dear to Hari. Seeing someone like you, so poor, a beggar, and without a home, even Brahma and Shiva would wonder whether he is a true saint or a beggar.
essence: Complete humility makes a person dear to Ram.
simple_meaning: Saints and scripture praise the one who has no pride, no possessions, and no home of attachment. Such emptiness makes a person dear to Ram.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to self-emptying, treating humility as spiritual strength rather than weakness.
modern_relevance: You show up to a gathering with nothing to impress anyone: no status story, no polished performance, no need to be seen. That quiet simplicity can feel strangely powerful.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जोसि सोसि तव चरन नमामी। मो पर कृपा करिअ अब स्वामी॥ सहज प्रीति भूपति कै देखी। आपु बिषय बिस्वास बिसेषी ॥
translation: आप जो हों सो हों (अर्थात् जो कोई भी हों), मैं आपके चरणों में नमस्कार करता हूँ। हे स्वामी! अब मुझ पर कृपा कीजिए। अपने ऊपर राजा की स्वाभाविक प्रीति और अपने विषय में उसका अधिक विश्वास देखकर ॥
english_translation: Whatever you are, I bow at your feet. Lord, now show me grace. Seeing the king's natural affection and his special trust in his own matter,
essence: Humility opens the way before words do.
simple_meaning: The speaker bows respectfully and asks for mercy, noticing that the king feels especially trusting and affectionate.
insight: It shows how humility and careful reading of another person can shape the next step in a conversation.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where someone has already softened. A respectful opening lands differently when the other person’s guard is down.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सब प्रकार राजहि अपनाई। बोलेउ अधिक सनेह जनाई॥ सुनु सतिभाउ कहउँ महिपाला। इहाँ बसत बीते बहु काला ॥
translation: सब प्रकार से राजा को अपने वश में करके, अधिक स्नेह दिखाता हुआ वह (कपट-तपस्वी) बोला- हे राजन् ! सुनो, मैं तुमसे सत्य कहता हूँ, मुझे यहाँ रहते बहुत समय बीत गया ॥
english_translation: Having won the king over in every way, he spoke, showing great affection: “Listen, O king, I speak truthfully. I have lived here for a long time.”
essence: Warm words can be a tool of control.
simple_meaning: The disguised ascetic flatters the king and speaks gently, claiming he has lived there for a long time and is speaking honestly.
insight: It trains you to notice charm as a tactic, not just a feeling.
modern_relevance: A stranger praises your judgment, lowers his voice, and says he only wants to be honest. The friendliness feels safe, but the real test is whether the words are meant to inform or to manipulate.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: अब लगि मोहि न मिलेउ कोउ मैं न जनावउँ काहु। लोकमान्यता अनल सम कर तप कानन दाहु ॥
translation: अब तक न तो कोई मुझसे मिला और न मैं अपने को किसी पर प्रकट करता हूँ, क्योंकि लोक में प्रतिष्ठा अग्नि के समान है, जो तप रूपी वन को भस्म कर डालती है ॥
english_translation: So far, no one has met me, and I do not reveal myself to anyone. Public reputation is like fire; it burns the forest of penance.
essence: Public admiration can destroy the very discipline it seems to honor.
simple_meaning: A person says he stays hidden because public recognition can destroy inner discipline the way fire destroys a forest.
insight: It shifts attention from being seen to preserving the conditions that let character deepen.
modern_relevance: You post something vulnerable, and the applause starts coming in. Part of you wants more of it, but another part feels the practice slipping. This verse protects that second part.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तुलसी देखि सुबेषु भूलहिं मूढ़ न चतुर नर। सुंदर केकिहि पेखु बचन सुधा सम असन अहि ॥
translation: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- सुंदर वेष देखकर मूढ़ नहीं (मूढ़ तो मूढ़ ही हैं), चतुर मनुष्य भी धोखा खा जाते हैं। सुंदर मोर को देखो, उसका वचन तो अमृत के समान है और आहार साँप का है ॥
english_translation: Tulsidas says: Foolish people are deceived by a fine disguise, and even clever people can be fooled. Look at the peacock: its voice is sweet like nectar, but its food is a snake.
essence: Beauty can hide danger; clear seeing must go deeper than appearances.
simple_meaning: A pleasing appearance can fool anyone, even intelligent people. The peacock looks beautiful and sounds sweet, but its food is a snake.
insight: It trains discernment: do not confuse attractive form with trustworthy nature.
modern_relevance: A polished profile, perfect smile, and calm voice can still hide selfish intent. The warning lands the moment you feel yourself trusting the packaging before the person.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तातें गुपुत रहउँ जग माहीं। हरि तजि किमपि प्रयोजन नाहीं॥ प्रभु जानत सब बिनहिं जनाए। कहहु कवनि सिधि लोक रिझाएँ ॥
translation: (कपट-तपस्वी ने कहा-) इसी से मैं जगत में छिपकर रहता हूँ। श्री हरि को छोड़कर किसी से कुछ भी प्रयोजन नहीं रखता। प्रभु तो बिना जनाए ही सब जानते हैं। फिर कहो संसार को रिझाने से क्या सिद्धि मिलेगी ॥
english_translation: That is why I remain hidden in the world. I seek nothing apart from Hari. The Lord knows everything without being told. So what gain comes from pleasing the crowd?
essence: When Hari is enough, public approval loses its power.
simple_meaning: The speaker says he stays hidden because only Ram matters to him. Since the Lord already knows everything, there is no need to impress people.
insight: It shifts attention from reputation management to sincere intention.
modern_relevance: You draft the message ten times, wondering how it will sound to everyone else. Then you remember the one person who matters already sees your intent. That changes the whole tone.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तुम्ह सुचि सुमति परम प्रिय मोरें। प्रीति प्रतीति मोहि पर तोरें॥ अब जौं तात दुरावउँ तोही। दारुन दोष घटइ अति मोही ॥
translation: तुम पवित्र और सुंदर बुद्धि वाले हो, इससे मुझे बहुत ही प्यारे हो और तुम्हारी भी मुझ पर प्रीति और विश्वास है। हे तात! अब यदि मैं तुमसे कुछ छिपाता हूँ, तो मुझे बहुत ही भयानक दोष लगेगा ॥
english_translation: You are pure-minded and dear to me. You trust me, and I trust you. If I hide anything from you now, I will commit a grave fault.
essence: Real trust makes hiding the truth feel like a moral wound.
simple_meaning: The speaker says the listener is pure-minded, dear, and trusted. Hiding the truth now would be a serious wrong.
insight: It shifts the mind from strategic concealment to truthful disclosure.
modern_relevance: A friend asks you a question you’ve been avoiding for weeks. You can feel the moment where politeness ends and honesty begins — and the relationship depends on crossing it cleanly.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जिमि जिमि तापसु कथइ उदासा। तिमि तिमि नृपहि उपज बिस्वासा॥ देखा स्वबस कर्म मन बानी। तब बोला तापस बगध्यानी ॥
translation: ज्यों-ज्यों वह तपस्वी उदासीनता की बातें कहता था, त्यों ही त्यों राजा को विश्वास उत्पन्न होता जाता था। जब उस बगुले की तरह ध्यान लगाने वाले (कपटी) मुनि ने राजा को कर्म, मन और वचन से अपने वश में जाना, तब वह बोला- ॥
english_translation: As the ascetic spoke more and more of detachment, the king's trust kept growing. When the deceitful, crane-like meditator saw the king under his control in body, mind, and speech, he began to speak.
essence: Polished detachment can be a mask for control.
simple_meaning: The king grows more trusting as the ascetic speaks of detachment. Seeing the king fully under control, the deceitful holy man begins his next move.
insight: It teaches you to watch whether words of virtue are matched by honest intent and steady conduct.
modern_relevance: A smooth-talking person keeps lowering your guard with just the right phrases about humility and good intentions. By the time you notice the pattern, you are already leaning toward their agenda.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाम हमार एकतनु भाई। सुनि नृप बोलेउ पुनि सिरु नाई॥ कहहु नाम कर अरथ बखानी। मोहि सेवक अति आपन जानी ॥
translation: हे भाई! हमारा नाम एकतनु है। यह सुनकर राजा ने फिर सिर नवाकर कहा- मुझे अपना अत्यन्त (अनुरागी) सेवक जानकर अपने नाम का अर्थ समझाकर कहिए ॥
english_translation: “My name is Ekatanu, brother.” Hearing this, the king bowed his head again and said, “Please tell me the meaning of your name and explain it. Regard me as your devoted servant.”
essence: Humility opens the door to real inquiry.
simple_meaning: The king humbly asks the sage to explain the meaning of his name, treating himself as the sage’s servant.
insight: It shifts the mind from display to inquiry, making humility the doorway to understanding.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm feels deeper than your own. Instead of performing knowledge, you lower your head and ask the one question that can actually change you.
speaker: Ekatanu

verse_text: आदिसृष्टि उपजी जबहिं तब उतपति भै मोरि। नाम एकतनु हेतु तेहि देह न धरी बहोरि ॥
translation: (कपटी मुनि ने कहा-) जब सबसे पहले सृष्टि उत्पन्न हुई थी, तभी मेरी उत्पत्ति हुई थी। तबसे मैंने फिर दूसरी देह नहीं धारण की, इसी से मेरा नाम एकतनु है ॥
english_translation: When the first creation arose, I arose then too. Since then I have not taken another body, so my name is Ekatanu.
essence: Confidence can hide deception.
simple_meaning: The speaker claims to have existed since the beginning of creation and says he has never taken another body, which is why he is called Ekatanu.
insight: It trains the reader to question polished claims and look for consistency before believing them.
modern_relevance: Someone in a meeting speaks with calm certainty, uses sacred-sounding language, and wins trust fast. The danger is not only lies — it is how easily confidence can masquerade as wisdom.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जनि आचरजु करहु मन माहीं। सुत तप तें दुर्लभ कछु नाहीं॥ तप बल तें जग सृजइ बिधाता। तप बल बिष्नु भए परित्राता ॥
translation: हे पुत्र! मन में आश्चर्य मत करो, तप से कुछ भी दुर्लभ नहीं है, तप के बल से ब्रह्मा जगत को रचते हैं। तप के ही बल से विष्णु संसार का पालन करने वाले बने हैं ॥
english_translation: O son, do not be surprised in your mind. Nothing is unattainable through tapas. By the power of tapas, Brahma creates the world, and by the power of tapas, Vishnu becomes its protector.
essence: Tapas makes the impossible ordinary.
simple_meaning: Serious discipline can accomplish what seems impossible. The verse says even the powers that create and protect the world arise from tapas.
insight: It shifts attention from what looks impossible to what consistent practice can build over time.
modern_relevance: You keep restarting the same habit on Monday morning, then quitting by Thursday. This verse says the missing ingredient is not talent — it is sustained inner discipline.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तपबल संभु करहिं संघारा। तप तें अगम न कछु संसारा॥ भयउ नृपहि सुनि अति अनुरागा। कथा पुरातन कहै सो लागा ॥
translation: तप ही के बल से रुद्र संहार करते हैं। संसार में कोई ऐसी वस्तु नहीं जो तप से न मिल सके। यह सुनकर राजा को बड़ा अनुराग हुआ। तब वह (तपस्वी) पुरानी कथाएँ कहने लगा ॥
english_translation: By the power of tapas, Rudra brings destruction. Nothing in the world is beyond the reach of tapas. Hearing this, the king felt deep eagerness, and the ascetic began to tell the ancient story.
essence: Tapas can reach what ordinary effort cannot.
simple_meaning: Tapsya is presented as so powerful that even Shiva's work of destruction happens through it. Hearing this, the king becomes eager to listen, and the old story continues.
insight: It shifts attention from quick results to the long power of disciplined effort.
modern_relevance: You keep practicing while everyone else calls it pointless. Months later, the habit has changed what used to feel impossible.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करम धरम इतिहास अनेका। करइ निरूपन बिरति बिबेका॥ उदभव पालन प्रलय कहानी। कहेसि अमित आचरज बखानी ॥
translation: कर्म, धर्म और अनेकों प्रकार के इतिहास कहकर वह वैराग्य और ज्ञान का निरूपण करने लगा। सृष्टि की उत्पत्ति, पालन (स्थिति) और संहार (प्रलय) की अपार आश्चर्यभरी कथाएँ उसने विस्तार से कही ॥
english_translation: He explained many stories of action, duty, and history, and then taught renunciation and clear seeing. He told the wondrous tale of creation, preservation, and dissolution in great detail.
essence: Stories of duty open into renunciation and the great cycle of change.
simple_meaning: He taught many stories about action and duty, then explained renunciation and clear seeing. He also told the vast, wondrous story of how the world arises, lasts, and ends.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated events to the larger pattern behind action, duty, and change.
modern_relevance: A teacher finally stops giving rules and starts connecting the dots: why people act, why they cling, and how larger patterns shape a life. The room goes quiet because the story has become a mirror.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि महीप तापस बस भयऊ। आपन नाम कहन तब लयउ॥ कह तापस नृप जानउँ तोही। कीन्हेहु कपट लाग भल मोही ॥
translation: राजा सुनकर उस तपस्वी के वश में हो गया और तब वह उसे अपना नाम बताने लगा। तपस्वी ने कहा- राजन ! मैं तुमको जानता हूँ। तुमने कपट किया, वह मुझे अच्छा लगा ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, the king came under the ascetic's influence and then began to reveal his name. The ascetic said, 'King, I know you. You used a clever ruse, and that pleased me.'
essence: True recognition makes disguise unnecessary.
simple_meaning: The king is so impressed that he reveals his name. The ascetic already knows who he is and praises the king's cleverness.
insight: It shifts the mind from guarded self-presentation to honest recognition.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a retreat who seems to read you instantly. Instead of performing, you relax and speak honestly. Being understood can be more disarming than being praised.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनु महीस असि नीति जहँ तहँ नाम न कहहिं नृप। मोहि तोहि पर अति प्रीति सोइ चतुरता बिचारि तव ॥
translation: हे राजन् ! सुनो, ऐसी नीति है कि राजा लोग जहाँ-तहाँ अपना नाम नहीं कहते। तुम्हारी वही चतुराई समझकर तुम पर मेरा बड़ा प्रेम हो गया है ॥
english_translation: Listen, O king: there is a rule that kings do not reveal their names everywhere. Seeing that cleverness in you, I grew very fond of you.
essence: Measured speech can create trust before full disclosure.
simple_meaning: The speaker says kings do not casually reveal their names, and that your cleverness made me like you even more.
insight: It shifts attention from oversharing to measured speech, showing that tact can deepen respect.
modern_relevance: At a first meeting, someone answers with just enough, not too much. That restraint feels confident, and it makes the other person lean in.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: नाम तुम्हार प्रताप दिनेसा। सत्यकेतु तव पिता नरेसा॥ गुर प्रसाद सब जानिअ राजा। कहिअ न आपन जानि अकाजा ॥
translation: तुम्हारा नाम प्रतापभानु है, महाराज सत्यकेतु तुम्हारे पिता थे। हे राजन् ! गुरु की कृपा से मैं सब जानता हूँ, पर अपनी हानि समझकर कहता नहीं ॥
english_translation: Your name is Pratapbhanu, and your father was the king Satyaketu. By the guru's grace, I know everything, but I do not say it, knowing it would harm me.
essence: Wisdom knows both what to say and what to hold back.
simple_meaning: The teacher knows the king's identity and family, but speaks carefully because saying everything would bring harm.
insight: It teaches restraint in speech: speak only when truth will help, not when it will wound.
modern_relevance: A colleague starts revealing private details in a meeting, then stops because the room has turned unsafe. Knowing something is not the same as saying it. Timing is part of wisdom.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: देखि तात तव सहज सुधाई। प्रीति प्रतीति नीति निपुनाई॥ उपजि परी ममता मन मोरें। कहउँ कथा निज पूछे तोरें ॥
translation: हे तात! तुम्हारा स्वाभाविक सीधापन (सरलता), प्रेम, विश्वास और नीति में निपुणता देखकर मेरे मन में तुम्हारे ऊपर बड़ी ममता उत्पन्न हो गई है, इसीलिए मैं तुम्हारे पूछने पर अपनी कथा कहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Seeing your natural simplicity, affection, trust, and skill in conduct, affection arose in my heart. So I tell my own story because you asked.
essence: Sincerity invites closeness, and closeness invites revelation.
simple_meaning: Recognizing the king’s sincerity and good conduct, the speaker feels affection and answers his request by sharing his own story.
insight: It shifts communication from formal exchange to earned intimacy and truthful sharing.
modern_relevance: A mentor listens to you differently when your questions come with humility and sincerity. Real trust changes the whole conversation before a single answer is given.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: अब प्रसन्न मैं संसय नाहीं। मागु जो भूप भाव मन माहीं॥ सुनि सुबचन भूपति हरषाना। गहि पद बिनय कीन्हि बिधि नाना ॥
translation: अब मैं प्रसन्न हूँ, इसमें संदेह न करना। हे राजन् ! जो मन को भावे वही माँग लो। सुंदर (प्रिय) वचन सुनकर राजा हर्षित हो गया और (मुनि के) पैर पकड़कर उसने बहुत प्रकार से विनती की ॥
english_translation: I am pleased now; have no doubt. Ask for whatever your heart desires, O king. Hearing those gracious words, the king rejoiced and bowed at the sage's feet in many ways.
essence: True generosity removes doubt and invites the real request.
simple_meaning: The sage tells the king he is pleased and should ask for any boon he wants. The king is overjoyed and falls at the sage's feet in gratitude.
insight: It shifts the moment from uncertainty to permission, showing how generosity makes honest asking possible.
modern_relevance: A mentor finally says, “Tell me what you really need.” The tension breaks, and gratitude rushes in before the request even comes out.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: कृपासिंधु मुनि दरसन तोरें। चारि पदारथ करतल मोरें॥ प्रभुहि तथापि प्रसन्न बिलोकी। मागि अगम बर होउँ असोकी ॥
translation: हे दयासागर मुनि! आपके दर्शन से ही चारों पदार्थ (अर्थ, धर्म, काम और मोक्ष) मेरी मुट्ठी में आ गए। तो भी स्वामी को प्रसन्न देखकर मैं यह दुर्लभ वर माँगकर (क्यों न) शोकरहित हो जाऊँ ॥
english_translation: O ocean of compassion, merely seeing the sage has placed the four aims of life in my hand. Yet, seeing the Lord pleased, I ask for this rare boon: let me become free of sorrow.
essence: The highest boon is a heart that wants the Lord's pleasure, not its own prize.
simple_meaning: Janaka says that even though meeting the sage has given him all four aims of life, he still asks for one rare blessing: to remain free from sorrow because the Lord is pleased.
insight: It shifts desire from personal gain to the beloved's satisfaction.
modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the praise, the money — and still notice what matters most is whether the person you love is at peace. Some victories feel small beside that quiet relief.
speaker: King Janaka

verse_text: जरा मरन दुख रहित तनु समर जितै जनि कोउ। एकछत्र रिपुहीन महि राज कलप सत होउ ॥
translation: मेरा शरीर वृद्धावस्था, मृत्यु और दुःख से रहित हो जाए, मुझे युद्ध में कोई जीत न सके और पृथ्वी पर मेरा सौ कल्पतक एकछत्र अकण्टक राज्य हो ॥
english_translation: May my body be free from old age, death, and sorrow; may no enemy defeat me in battle; may I rule the earth, unchallenged, for a hundred kalpas.
essence: Worldly perfection still depends on what time and conflict can take away.
simple_meaning: The king asks for a body free from aging, death, and suffering, invincibility in war, and a long, undisturbed reign over the earth.
insight: It exposes the limits of worldly power and sets up the higher teaching that follows.
modern_relevance: Someone wants the perfect job, perfect health, no rivals, and total control over the future. The wish sounds strong until you hear how fragile every part of it is.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: कह तापस नृप ऐसेइ होऊ। कारन एक कठिन सुनु सोऊ॥ कालउ तुअ पद नाइहि सीसा। एक बिप्रकुल छाड़ि महीसा ॥
translation: तपस्वी ने कहा- हे राजन् ! ऐसा ही हो, पर एक बात कठिन है, उसे भी सुन लो। हे पृथ्वी के स्वामी! केवल ब्राह्मण कुल को छोड़ काल भी तुम्हारे चरणों पर सिर नवाएगा ॥
english_translation: The ascetic said, “So be it, O king. But hear one hard condition: even Time will bow his head at your feet, yet not one priestly lineage will be left out.”
essence: Even granted power meets a law it cannot erase.
simple_meaning: The ascetic grants the king’s wish, but adds one hard rule: even Time will bow to him, yet the priestly line will remain beyond his control.
insight: It shifts the mind from total control to respectful limits: desire can be answered, but not without boundaries.
modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the raise, the title you wanted — and still one person can say no. This verse reminds you that no amount of ambition makes you master of everything.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तपबल बिप्र सदा बरिआरा। तिन्ह के कोप न कोउ रखवारा॥ जौं बिप्रन्ह बस करहु नरेसा। तौ तुअ बस बिधि बिष्नु महेसा ॥
translation: तप के बल से ब्राह्मण सदा बलवान रहते हैं। उनके क्रोध से रक्षा करने वाला कोई नहीं है। हे नरपति! यदि तुम ब्राह्मणों को वश में कर लो, तो ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और महेश भी तुम्हारे अधीन हो जाएँगे ॥
english_translation: By the power of austerity, brahmins are always strong. No one can protect against their anger. O king, if you bring brahmins under your control, then Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh will also be under your control.
essence: A ruler who tries to control the righteous invites forces beyond control.
simple_meaning: Austerity gives brahmins their strength, and no one can safely oppose them. If a king controls brahmins, even the highest powers would be forced under his influence.
insight: It shifts the mind from domination to respect for moral and spiritual authority.
modern_relevance: A manager bullies the only person in the room who knows the system inside out. The shortcut looks strong for a day, then the whole structure starts to wobble.
speaker: Tapsi

verse_text: चल न ब्रह्मकुल सन बरिआई। सत्य कहउँ दोउ भुजा उठाई॥ बिप्र श्राप बिनु सुनु महिपाला। तोर नास नहिं कवनेहुँ काला ॥
translation: ब्राह्मण कुल से जोर जबर्दस्ती नहीं चल सकती, मैं दोनों भुजा उठाकर सत्य कहता हूँ। हे राजन् ! सुनो, ब्राह्मणों के शाप बिना तुम्हारा नाश किसी काल में नहीं होगा ॥
english_translation: Force cannot prevail against the Brahmin lineage. I speak the truth with both arms raised: O ruler, without a Brahmin's curse, your destruction will not come at any time.
essence: Force fails where moral authority stands.
simple_meaning: Power cannot override the moral force of the Brahmin order. The speaker warns the king that his downfall will not come unless a Brahmin curses him.
insight: It shifts the mind from brute confidence to respect for limits that power cannot erase.
modern_relevance: You push your way through a dispute, sure that influence will protect you. Then one small act of disrespect turns the room against you. Some boundaries are not physical; they are moral.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: हरषेउ राउ बचन सुनि तासू। नाथ न होइ मोर अब नासू॥ तव प्रसाद प्रभु कृपानिधाना। मो कहुँ सर्बकाल कल्याना ॥
translation: राजा उसके वचन सुनकर बड़ा प्रसन्न हुआ और कहने लगा- हे स्वामी! मेरा नाश अब नहीं होगा। हे कृपानिधान प्रभु! आपकी कृपा से मेरा सब समय कल्याण होगा ॥
english_translation: The king was delighted to hear those words and said, “Lord, now my ruin will not come. By your grace, merciful one, may I always be blessed.”
essence: Relief arrives when fear gives way to trust in grace.
simple_meaning: The king feels relieved and grateful after hearing the sage’s words. He believes divine grace will keep him safe and благословed.
insight: It shifts the mind from panic to trust when danger feels near.
modern_relevance: After a tense call from someone who can change your plans, you finally hear a calm voice that steadies the room. The body unclenches before the mind can explain why.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: एवमस्तु कहि कपट मुनि बोला कुटिल बहोरि। मिलब हमार भुलाब निज कहहु त हमहि न खोरि ॥
translation: 'एवमस्तु' (ऐसा ही हो) कहकर वह कुटिल कपटी मुनि फिर बोला- (किन्तु) तुम मेरे मिलने तथा अपने राह भूल जाने की बात किसी से (कहना नहीं, यदि) कह दोगे, तो हमारा दोष नहीं ॥
english_translation: “So be it,” said the crooked sage, and then spoke again: “If you mention our meeting or your losing the way, then the blame is not ours.”
essence: Agreement can still conceal fear of blame.
simple_meaning: The deceitful sage agrees, but immediately warns the king not to reveal the meeting or the lost path. He wants to keep himself safe from blame.
insight: It trains the reader to notice manipulation wrapped in agreement and to watch for hidden self-interest.
modern_relevance: Someone says, “Sure, do it my way,” then quietly adds, “And don’t tell anyone I advised this.” The smile is still there, but the self-protection is now obvious.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तातें मैं तोहि बरजउँ राजा। कहें कथा तव परम अकाजा॥ छठें श्रवन यह परत कहानी। नास तुम्हार सत्य मम बानी ॥
translation: हे राजन् ! मैं तुमको इसलिए मना करता हूँ कि इस प्रसंग को कहने से तुम्हारी बड़ी हानि होगी। छठे कान में यह बात पड़ते ही तुम्हारा नाश हो जाएगा, मेरा यह वचन सत्य जानना ॥
english_translation: O king, I warn you for this reason: telling this story will bring you great harm. The moment it reaches a sixth ear, your ruin will be certain; believe my words as true.
essence: Some truths destroy the listener who hears them too soon.
simple_meaning: The sage warns the king not to repeat the story, because hearing it by the wrong person will destroy him.
insight: It teaches restraint in speech: not every truth should be repeated, and timing can matter as much as content.
modern_relevance: You almost repeat a private conversation in a group chat, then stop. Not every true thing belongs everywhere; some words become harmful the moment they leave the wrong room.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: यह प्रगटें अथवा द्विजश्रापा। नास तोर सुनु भानुप्रतापा॥ आन उपायँ निधन तव नाहीं। जौं हरि हर कोपहिं मन माहीं ॥
translation: हे प्रतापभानु! सुनो, इस बात के प्रकट करने से अथवा ब्राह्मणों के शाप से तुम्हारा नाश होगा और किसी उपाय से, चाहे ब्रह्मा और शंकर भी मन में क्रोध करें, तुम्हारी मृत्यु नहीं होगी ॥
english_translation: O glorious king, know this: if it becomes known, or if the brahmins curse you, your ruin will come. No other remedy exists, even if Brahma and Shiva become angry in their minds.
essence: Fear can make a false warning feel unavoidable.
simple_meaning: The disguised sage warns King Pratāpa Bhānu that revealing the secret or earning the brahmins’ curse will bring ruin, and no other escape exists.
insight: It exposes how fear is used to control judgment by making every alternative seem fatal.
modern_relevance: A stranger in a polished office lowers their voice and says, “Don’t tell anyone this.” The threat is vague, but it grips you. Fear can make a lie feel like the only safe path.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सत्य नाथ पद गहि नृप भाषा। द्विज गुर कोप कहहु को राखा॥ राखइ गुर जौं कोप बिधाता। गुर बिरोध नहिं कोउ जग त्राता ॥
translation: राजा ने मुनि के चरण पकड़कर कहा- हे स्वामी! सत्य ही है। ब्राह्मण और गुरु के क्रोध से, कहिए, कौन रक्षा कर सकता है? यदि ब्रह्मा भी क्रोध करें, तो गुरु बचा लेते हैं, पर गुरु से विरोध करने पर जगत में कोई भी बचाने वाला नहीं है ॥
english_translation: The king clasped the sage's feet and said, "Master, what you say is true. Who can protect anyone from the anger of a brahmin and a teacher? Even if Brahma grows angry, a teacher can still save one; but no one in the world can save against a teacher's opposition."
essence: Teacherly opposition is treated as beyond ordinary protection.
simple_meaning: The king admits the sage is right: a teacher's anger is dangerous, and no one can protect a person who opposes a teacher.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-assertion to reverence for guidance and consequences.
modern_relevance: You argue with someone who has guided you for years, then realize the damage is already in the room. Some relationships carry a weight that pride cannot afford to ignore.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जौं न चलब हम कहे तुम्हारें। होउ नास नहिं सोच हमारें॥ एकहिं डर डरपत मन मोरा। प्रभु महिदेव श्राप अति घोरा ॥
translation: यदि मैं आपके कथन के अनुसार नहीं चलूँगा, तो (भले ही) मेरा नाश हो जाए। मुझे इसकी चिन्ता नहीं है। मेरा मन तो हे प्रभो! (केवल) एक ही डर से डर रहा है कि ब्राह्मणों का शाप बड़ा भयानक होता है ॥
english_translation: If I do not follow your command, let me perish. I do not worry about that. My mind fears only one thing: the terrible curse of the Brahmins, O Lord.
essence: Death is bearable; breaking sacred order is not.
simple_meaning: The king says he is willing to die rather than disobey, but he is terrified of the Brahmins' curse.
insight: It shifts attention from physical loss to moral consequence and reverence for higher authority.
modern_relevance: You can face losing your reputation, your comfort, even your position. What shakes you more is the feeling that you have crossed a line you should never have crossed.
speaker: Pratapbhanu

verse_text: होहिं बिप्र बस कवन बिधि कहहु कृपा करि सोउ। तुम्ह तजि दीनदयाल निज हितू न देखउँ कोउ ॥
translation: वे ब्राह्मण किस प्रकार से वश में हो सकते हैं, कृपा करके वह भी बताइए। हे दीनदयालु! आपको छोड़कर और किसी को मैं अपना हितू नहीं देखता ॥
english_translation: Please tell me, by what means can the Brahmins be brought under control? O compassionate one, apart from you I see no helper who can truly protect me.
essence: True help begins when pride stops looking elsewhere.
simple_meaning: The king asks how the Brahmins can be brought under control, and says he sees no protector except the compassionate one he is addressing.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance under pressure to humble dependence on a wiser guide.
modern_relevance: You have exhausted every workaround, every apology, every clever plan. At last you admit, 'I need someone wiser than me to show the next step.'
speaker: King

verse_text: सुनु नृप बिबिध जतन जग माहीं। कष्टसाध्य पुनि होहिं कि नाहीं॥ अहइ एक अति सुगम उपाई। तहाँ परन्तु एक कठिनाई ॥
translation: (तपस्वी ने कहा-) हे राजन् !सुनो, संसार में उपाय तो बहुत हैं, पर वे कष्ट साध्य हैं (बड़ी कठिनता से बनने में आते हैं) और इस पर भी सिद्ध हों या न हों (उनकी सफलता निश्चित नहीं है) हाँ, एक उपाय बहुत सहज है, परन्तु उसमें भी एक कठिनता है ॥
english_translation: Hear, O king: there are many methods in the world, but they are hard to accomplish. Even then, success is uncertain. There is one very easy method, but it has one difficulty.
essence: The easiest solution is often blocked by one hard condition.
simple_meaning: Many methods exist, but most are hard and uncertain. One method is easy, yet it has a single obstacle.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing complexity to asking what simple obstacle remains.
modern_relevance: You’ve tried five complicated fixes, and none of them held. Then someone suggests a simpler route — and you resist it because it feels too easy to be real.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: मम आधीन जुगुति नृप सोई। मोर जाब तव नगर न होई॥ आजु लगें अरु जब तें भयऊँ। काहू के गृह ग्राम न गयऊँ ॥
translation: हे राजन् ! वह युक्ति तो मेरे हाथ है, पर मेरा जाना तुम्हारे नगर में हो नहीं सकता। जब से पैदा हुआ हूँ, तब से आज तक मैं किसी के घर अथवा गाँव नहीं गया ॥
english_translation: O king, that method is in my hands, but I cannot go to your city. Since I was born until today, I have never gone to anyone's house or village.
essence: Power stays clean when it refuses convenience.
simple_meaning: The speaker says he knows the solution, but he will not enter the king's city or visit anyone's home. He has kept that rule his whole life.
insight: It shows that real authority can include strict self-limitation. The method is offered without compromising the speaker's way of life.
modern_relevance: A respected elder refuses a flattering dinner invitation because he will not trade his integrity for access. The answer is available, but not on borrowed terms.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जौं न जाउँ तव होइ अकाजू। बना आइ असमंजस आजू॥ सुनि महीस बोलेउ मृदु बानी। नाथ निगम असि नीति बखानी ॥
translation: परन्तु यदि नहीं जाता हूँ, तो तुम्हारा काम बिगड़ता है। आज यह बड़ा असमंजस आ पड़ा है। यह सुनकर राजा कोमल वाणी से बोला, हे नाथ! वेदों में ऐसी नीति कही है कि- ॥
english_translation: But if I do not go, your work will fail. A difficult dilemma has arisen today. Hearing this, the king spoke gently: "Master, the Vedas teach this policy..."
essence: Refusing the task would harm others, so duty must answer the dilemma.
simple_meaning: The speaker says that refusing to go would ruin the other person's task, so a painful dilemma has arisen. The king then replies gently, appealing to the moral guidance of the Vedas.
insight: It frames obligation as immediate and unavoidable, shifting attention from comfort to responsibility.
modern_relevance: You’re on the phone at midnight, hearing that backing out will leave someone stranded. There’s no elegant option left — only the weight of showing up anyway.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बड़े सनेह लघुन्ह पर करहीं। गिरि निज सिरनि सदा तृन धरहीं॥ जलधि अगाध मौलि बह फेनू। संतत धरनि धरत सिर रेनू ॥
translation: बड़े लोग छोटों पर स्नेह करते ही हैं। पर्वत अपने सिरों पर सदा तृण (घास) को धारण किए रहते हैं। अगाध समुद्र अपने मस्तक पर फेन को धारण करता है और धरती अपने सिर पर सदा धूलि को धारण किए रहती है ॥
english_translation: Great beings show affection to those below them. Mountains hold grass on their heads, the deep ocean holds foam on its crown, and the earth always bears dust upon its head.
essence: Greatness proves itself by carrying what is smaller.
simple_meaning: Truly great people naturally treat those beneath them with care and humility. The mountain, ocean, and earth are used as examples of bearing what is small without pride.
insight: It shifts status from dominance to responsibility: the higher one stands, the more gently one should hold others.
modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, and the new intern is terrified to ask questions. The way you answer them shows whether you rose in rank or in character.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस कहि गहे नरेस पद स्वामी होहु कृपाल। मोहि लागि दुख सहिअ प्रभु सज्जन दीनदयाल ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर राजा ने मुनि के चरण पकड़ लिए। (और कहा-) हे स्वामी! कृपा कीजिए। आप संत हैं। दीनदयालु हैं। (अतः) हे प्रभो! मेरे लिए इतना कष्ट (अवश्य) सहिए ॥
english_translation: Saying this, the king grasped the sage's feet: “Be gracious, my lord. You are kind to the lowly and distressed. Please bear this hardship for my sake.”
essence: True need bows first and asks with humility.
simple_meaning: The king bows to the sage's feet and asks him to be kind, noble, and willing to bear hardship for his sake.
insight: It teaches you to ask for help without ego and to honour the one who can carry the burden with you.
modern_relevance: You are asking a senior colleague to cover for your mistake, and your voice softens before you finish the sentence. Real need sounds like this: respectful, direct, and unguarded.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जानि नृपहि आपन आधीना। बोला तापस कपट प्रबीना॥ सत्य कहउँ भूपति सुनु तोही। जग नाहिन दुर्लभ कछु मोही ॥
translation: राजा को अपने अधीन जानकर कपट में प्रवीण तपस्वी बोला- हे राजन् ! सुनो, मैं तुमसे सत्य कहता हूँ, जगत में मुझे कुछ भी दुर्लभ नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Seeing the king under his control, the skilled deceiver spoke: "Listen, king, I speak truthfully to you. In this world, nothing is beyond my reach."
essence: Control makes deception sound like certainty.
simple_meaning: The ascetic, skilled in deception, sees the king is now under his control and speaks confidently, claiming nothing in the world is beyond his reach.
insight: It warns you to notice when persuasion is being used to create dependence before a request is made.
modern_relevance: A smooth speaker notices you are already leaning in and turns that opening into leverage. The danger is not loud force; it is a calm voice that knows exactly how to steer you.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: अवसि काज मैं करिहउँ तोरा। मन तन बचन भगत तैं मोरा॥ जोग जुगुति तप मंत्र प्रभाऊ। फलइ तबहिं जब करिअ दुराऊ ॥
translation: मैं तुम्हारा काम अवश्य करूँगा, (क्योंकि) तुम, मन, वाणी और शरीर (तीनों) से मेरे भक्त हो। पर योग, युक्ति, तप और मंत्रों का प्रभाव तभी फलीभूत होता है जब वे छिपाकर किए जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: I will certainly do your work, because you are my devotee in mind, speech, and body. But the power of yoga, skill, austerity, and mantra bears fruit only when done in secret.
essence: Wholehearted devotion moves the divine; display is what weakens practice.
simple_meaning: Ram says he will do the king's work because the king loves him with mind, speech, and body. He adds that spiritual practices work best when kept private.
insight: It shifts the mind from performance to inward sincerity, showing that real practice matures away from applause.
modern_relevance: You help someone late at night, then resist posting about it. The act itself carries the weight. What is done quietly often has the deepest force.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जौं नरेस मैं करौं रसोई। तुम्ह परुसहु मोहि जान न कोई॥ अन्न सो जोइ जोइ भोजन करई। सोइ सोइ तव आयसु अनुसरई ॥
translation: हे नरपति! मैं यदि रसोई बनाऊँ और तुम उसे परोसो और मुझे कोई जानने न पावे, तो उस अन्न को जो-जो खाएगा, सो-सो तुम्हारा आज्ञाकारी बन जाएगा ॥
english_translation: O king, if I cook the meal and you serve it, and no one knows me, then whoever eats that food will become obedient to you.
essence: Quiet support can shape an entire crowd.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas says that if the king serves food made by him without revealing him, everyone who eats it will come under the king's influence.
insight: It shifts attention from visible control to the hidden causes that shape obedience and loyalty.
modern_relevance: A team meeting ends, and one person quietly backs the decision so well that everyone leaves aligned. Influence often comes from invisible support, not public credit.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: पुनि तिन्ह के गृह जेवँइ जोऊ। तव बस होइ भूप सुनु सोऊ॥ जाइ उपाय रचहु नृप एहू। संबत भरि संकलप करेहू ॥
translation: यही नहीं, उन (भोजन करने वालों) के घर भी जो कोई भोजन करेगा, हे राजन् ! सुनो, वह भी तुम्हारे अधीन हो जाएगा। हे राजन् ! जाकर यही उपाय करो और वर्षभर (भोजन कराने) का संकल्प कर लेना ॥
english_translation: Not only that, whoever eats in the homes of those diners will also come under your control, O king. Go and arrange this remedy, and make the vow for a full year.
essence: A single vow can shape lives beyond the people you directly serve.
simple_meaning: The promise is widened: not only the guests, but even the people they feed will be influenced by the king's vow.
insight: It shifts attention from one visible result to the wider ripple of a sincere act.
modern_relevance: You help one person, and they go home kinder to everyone they meet. A single generous act can keep moving long after you stop watching.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: नित नूतन द्विज सहस सत बरेहु सहित परिवार। मैं तुम्हरे संकलप लगि दिनहिं करबि जेवनार ॥
translation: नित्य नए एक लाख ब्राह्मणों को कुटुम्ब सहित निमंत्रित करना। मैं तुम्हारे सकंल्प (के काल अर्थात एक वर्ष) तक प्रतिदिन भोजन बना दिया करूँगा ॥
english_translation: Invite one hundred thousand Brahmins each day, with their families. I will prepare meals daily for the full year of your vow.
essence: Sustained service can gather what force cannot.
simple_meaning: The plan is to invite huge numbers of Brahmins every day, and the speaker will cook for them throughout the vow period.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to sustained service as the real power behind influence.
modern_relevance: A family gathering is spinning out of control, and one person quietly says, “I’ll handle the food every day.” That steady help changes everything.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: एहि बिधि भूप कष्ट अति थोरें। होइहहिं सकल बिप्र बस तोरें॥ करिहहिं बिप्र होममख सेवा। तेहिं प्रसंग सहजेहिं बस देवा ॥
translation: हे राजन् ! इस प्रकार बहुत ही थोड़े परिश्रम से सब ब्राह्मण तुम्हारे वश में हो जाएँगे। ब्राह्मण हवन, यज्ञ और सेवा-पूजा करेंगे, तो उस प्रसंग (संबंध) से देवता भी सहज ही वश में हो जाएँगे ॥
english_translation: In this way, O king, with very little effort all the priests will come under your control. The priests will perform homa, yajna, and service-worship, and through that connection the radiant beings will also naturally come under your control.
essence: Gentle support can achieve what force cannot.
simple_meaning: With little effort, the king will gain influence over the priests, and through their rituals even the radiant beings will be reached.
insight: It shifts the mind from brute control to indirect influence through support and ritual order.
modern_relevance: You help organize a community event, and suddenly people who never noticed your work start trusting your judgment. Influence often comes through service and alignment, not force.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: और एक तोहि कहउँ लखाऊ। मैं एहिं बेष न आउब काऊ॥ तुम्हरे उपरोहित कहुँ राया। हरि आनब मैं करि निज माया ॥
translation: मैं एक और पहचान तुमको बताए देता हूँ कि मैं इस रूप में कभी न आऊँगा। हे राजन् ! मैं अपनी माया से तुम्हारे पुरोहित को हर लाऊँगा ॥\
english_translation: I will tell you one more thing: I will never come in this form. O king, I will use my power to take your priest away.
essence: The disguise is temporary; the real change is already underway.
simple_meaning: The speaker says he will not appear in this disguise again and will use his power to remove the king’s priest.
insight: It prepares the reader for a strategic shift: what looks like a simple request is actually part of a larger divine intervention.
modern_relevance: A person smiles politely in a meeting, then quietly rewrites the entire plan behind the scenes. The real move is not always the one announced first.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तपबल तेहि करि आपु समाना। रखिहउँ इहाँ बरष परवाना॥ मैं धरि तासु बेषु सुनु राजा। सब बिधि तोर सँवारब काजा ॥
translation: तप के बल से उसे अपने समान बनाकर एक वर्ष यहाँ रखूँगा और हे राजन् ! सुनो, मैं उसका रूप बनाकर सब प्रकार से तुम्हारा काम सिद्ध करूँगा ॥
english_translation: By the power of austerity, I will make him like myself and keep him here for a year. Listen, O king, I will take his form and accomplish all your work in every way.
essence: Spiritual power can reshape events without public display.
simple_meaning: The sage says he will use his spiritual power to keep a man in place for a year and take that man's form to handle the king's work.
insight: It shifts attention from visible effort to hidden power working behind events.
modern_relevance: A skilled fixer steps into a broken process, takes on someone else's role, and quietly makes the whole thing work while everyone else sleeps.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: गै निसि बहुत सयन अब कीजे। मोहि तोहि भूप भेंट दिन तीजे॥ मैं तपबल तोहि तुरग समेता। पहुँचैहउँ सोवतहि निकेता ॥
translation: हे राजन् ! रात बहुत बीत गई, अब सो जाओ। आज से तीसरे दिन मुझसे तुम्हारी भेंट होगी। तप के बल से मैं घोड़े सहित तुमको सोते ही में घर पहुँचा दूँगा ॥
english_translation: O king, the night has passed. Now go to sleep. On the third day from today, you and I will meet. By the power of my austerity, I will carry you home along with your horse while you sleep.
essence: True power can protect without being seen.
simple_meaning: The speaker tells the king to sleep, promises a meeting in three days, and says he will carry the king and horse home while the king sleeps.
insight: It shifts attention from personal control to confident reliance on a capable guide.
modern_relevance: You fall asleep after a long, exhausting day, trusting someone else has already handled the problem. Relief comes when control is no longer yours to carry.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: मैं आउब सोइ बेषु धरि पहिचानेहु तब मोहि। जब एकांत बोलाइ सब कथा सुनावौं तोहि ॥
translation: मैं वही (पुरोहित का) वेश धरकर आऊँगा। जब एकांत में तुमको बुलाकर सब कथा सुनाऊँगा, तब तुम मुझे पहचान लेना ॥
english_translation: I will come in that same disguise. When I call you aside in private and tell you the whole story, then you will recognize me.
essence: Truth can wear a disguise until the right moment.
simple_meaning: The speaker says he will return in disguise and reveal the full story only in private, so the king will know who he is.
insight: It teaches you to respect timing and context, not force revelation before trust is ready.
modern_relevance: Someone texts, 'Can we talk in private?' and suddenly the whole tone changes. Some conversations need the right setting before the truth can land.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सयन कीन्ह नृप आयसु मानी। आसन जाइ बैठ छलग्यानी॥ श्रमित भूप निद्रा अति आई। सो किमि सोव सोच अधिकाई ॥
translation: राजा ने आज्ञा मानकर शयन किया और वह कपट-ज्ञानी आसन पर जा बैठा। राजा थका था, (उसे) खूब (गहरी) नींद आ गई। पर वह कपटी कैसे सोता। उसे तो बहुत चिन्ता हो रही थी ॥
english_translation: The king obeyed and lay down to sleep. The deceiver sat on the seat. The weary king fell into deep sleep, but how could the deceiver sleep? His mind was full of worry.
essence: A tired body can sleep; a scheming mind cannot.
simple_meaning: The king goes to sleep, but the deceitful man cannot rest because he is full of worry and scheming.
insight: It shows how inner agitation outlasts physical fatigue when the mind is caught in deceit.
modern_relevance: You finally turn off the lights after a draining day, but your mind keeps replaying the conversation, the plan, the lie, the risk. The body wants rest; the restless mind refuses it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कालकेतु निसिचर तहँ आवा। जेहिं सूकर होइ नृपहि भुलावा॥ परम मित्र तापस नृप केरा। जानइ सो अति कपट घनेरा ॥
translation: (उसी समय) वहाँ कालकेतु राक्षस आया, जिसने सूअर बनकर राजा को भटकाया था। वह तपस्वी राजा का बड़ा मित्र था और खूब छल-प्रपंच जानता था ॥
english_translation: At that very time, the demon Kalaketu arrived, the same one who had once misled the king in the form of a boar. He was the ascetic king's close friend and knew many tricks of deceit.
essence: Deceit is most dangerous when it returns as a friend.
simple_meaning: Kalaketu, a deceitful demon and close friend of the king, arrives. The verse reminds us that he is skilled in trickery and has already misled the king before.
insight: It trains you to notice repeated manipulation, especially when it comes disguised as friendship.
modern_relevance: A smooth-talking colleague shows up again right after you lowered your guard. The danger is not loud; it arrives wearing trust and old familiarity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहि के सत सुत अरु दस भाई। खल अति अजय देव दुखदाई॥ प्रथमहिं भूप समर सब मारे। बिप्र संत सुर देखि दुखारे ॥
translation: उसके सौ पुत्र और दस भाई थे, जो बड़े ही दुष्ट, किसी से न जीते जाने वाले और देवताओं को दुःख देने वाले थे। ब्राह्मणों, संतों और देवताओं को दुःखी देखकर राजा ने उन सबको पहले ही युद्ध में मार डाला था ॥
english_translation: He had a hundred sons and ten brothers, all extremely wicked, unconquerable, and harmful to the radiant beings. Seeing the suffering of the learned, the holy, and the radiant beings, the king had already killed them in battle.
essence: Protecting the vulnerable can create enemies among the cruel.
simple_meaning: The verse describes the king's enemies: a huge family of wicked, powerful beings. It also says the king had already slain them because they caused suffering to the learned, holy, and radiant beings.
insight: It frames conflict as a response to prior harm, not random hostility.
modern_relevance: A person who quietly protects a vulnerable community may later become the target of resentment from those who benefited from the harm. The earlier act of defense is what the next conflict is really about.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहिं खल पाछिल बयरु सँभारा। तापस नृप मिलि मंत्र बिचारा॥ जेहिं रिपु छय सोइ रचेन्हि उपाऊ। भावी बस न जान कछु राऊ ॥
translation: उस दुष्ट ने पिछला बैर याद करके तपस्वी राजा से मिलकर सलाह विचारी (षड्यंत्र किया) और जिस प्रकार शत्रु का नाश हो, वही उपाय रचा। भावीवश राजा (प्रतापभानु) कुछ भी न समझ सका ॥
english_translation: That wicked one revived his old enmity. He met the ascetic king and plotted a strategy. He devised a way to destroy his enemy, but fate kept King Pratapbhanu unaware.
essence: Old enmity quietly becomes a trap.
simple_meaning: The enemy remembered an old grudge, planned in secret with the king, and set a trap. The king did not realize what was happening.
insight: It trains the reader to notice how resentment and strategy can work together before harm becomes obvious.
modern_relevance: A colleague smiles in the meeting, then quietly turns others against you after it ends. By the time the damage is visible, the plan was already in motion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रिपु तेजसी अकेल अपि लघु करि गनिअ न ताहु। अजहुँ देत दुख रबि ससिहि सिर अवसेषित राहु ॥
translation: तेजस्वी शत्रु अकेला भी हो तो भी उसे छोटा नहीं समझना चाहिए। जिसका सिर मात्र बचा था, वह राहु आज तक सूर्य-चन्द्रमा को दुःख देता है ॥
english_translation: A powerful enemy should not be underestimated, even when alone. Rahu, with only his head left, still troubles the sun and moon.
essence: A weakened enemy can still strike hard.
simple_meaning: A strong enemy must never be dismissed just because he stands alone. Even a defeated force can still cause harm.
insight: It teaches you not to mistake partial defeat for complete safety.
modern_relevance: You think the conflict is over because one loud critic is gone. Then one message, one rumor, one stubborn person keeps the whole situation burning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तापस नृप निज सखहि निहारी। हरषि मिलेउ उठि भयउ सुखारी॥ मित्रहि कहि सब कथा सुनाई। जातुधान बोला सुख पाई ॥
translation: तपस्वी राजा अपने मित्र को देख प्रसन्न हो उठकर मिला और सुखी हुआ। उसने मित्र को सब कथा कह सुनाई, तब राक्षस आनंदित होकर बोला ॥
english_translation: The ascetic king saw his friend, rose joyfully, and embraced him. He told his friend the whole story, and the demon rejoiced.
essence: Joy can blind a person to danger standing right beside him.
simple_meaning: The king greets his friend happily and shares everything with him. The demon listens and feels pleased.
insight: It warns you to test trust before disclosure, especially when someone is already aligned with harm.
modern_relevance: You call an old friend to vent, relieved to be understood. But the person smiling at your pain may be the one feeding it forward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अब साधेउँ रिपु सुनहु नरेसा। जौं तुम्ह कीन्ह मोर उपदेसा॥ परिहरि सोच रहहु तुम्ह सोई। बिनु औषध बिआधि बिधि खोई ॥
translation: हे राजन् ! सुनो, जब तुमने मेरे कहने के अनुसार (इतना) काम कर लिया, तो अब मैंने शत्रु को काबू में कर ही लिया (समझो)। तुम अब चिन्ता त्याग सो रहो। विधाता ने बिना ही दवा के रोग दूर कर दिया ॥
english_translation: O king, listen. Since you have followed my instruction, the enemy has now been subdued. Let go of your worry and rest. Fate has removed the illness without medicine.
essence: False reassurance can be the final step of a trap.
simple_meaning: The speaker tells the king that following the advice has already defeated the enemy, so there is no need to worry anymore.
insight: It warns you not to mistake soothing words for real safety.
modern_relevance: Someone says, “It’s all fine now,” right after you’ve been pushed into relaxing your guard. The calm tone itself is part of the trick.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: कुल समेत रिपु मूल बहाई। चौथें दिवस मिलब मैं आई॥ तापस नृपहि बहुत परितोषी। चला महाकपटी अतिरोषी ॥
translation: कुल सहित शत्रु को जड़-मूल से उखाड़-बहाकर, (आज से) चौथे दिन मैं तुमसे आ मिलूँगा। (इस प्रकार) तपस्वी राजा को खूब दिलासा देकर वह महामायावी और अत्यन्त क्रोधी राक्षस चला ॥
english_translation: After uprooting the enemy from the root along with his whole line, I will meet you on the fourth day. Giving the ascetic-king great comfort in this way, that great deceiver and furious demon went away.
essence: A lie can soothe before it strikes.
simple_meaning: The deceiver promises to destroy the enemy and return in four days. He uses this promise to comfort the king, then leaves in anger.
insight: It trains you to notice reassurance that serves manipulation rather than truth.
modern_relevance: A smooth-talking person says, “Leave it to me, I’ll fix everything by Thursday,” and you feel relieved for a second. The danger is in how comfort can be manufactured.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: भानुप्रतापहि बाजि समेता। पहुँचाएसि छन माझ निकेता॥ नृपहि नारि पहिं सयन कराई। हयगृहँ बाँधेसि बाजि बनाई ॥
translation: उसने प्रतापभानु राजा को घोड़े सहित क्षणभर में घर पहुँचा दिया। राजा को रानी के पास सुलाकर घोड़े को अच्छी तरह से घुड़साल में बाँध दिया ॥
english_translation: He carried King Bhanupratap home with his horse in an instant. He laid the king beside his queen and tied the horse securely in the stable.
essence: Deception can arrive dressed as help and leave no alarm behind.
simple_meaning: The disguised figure quickly brings the king home, settles him beside his wife, and secures the horse in the stable.
insight: It shows how illusion can move fast enough to feel like rescue.
modern_relevance: A problem seems solved in one smooth sweep, and everyone relaxes before noticing the trap was part of the solution. Quick relief can hide deeper manipulation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राजा के उपरोहितहि हरि लै गयउ बहोरि। लै राखेसि गिरि खोह महुँ मायाँ करि मति भोरि ॥
translation: फिर वह राजा के पुरोहित को उठा ले गया और माया से उसकी बुद्धि को भ्रम में डालकर उसे उसने पहाड़ की खोह में ला रखा ॥
english_translation: Then he carried off the king's priest again, and by illusion clouded his mind and left him in a mountain cave.
essence: Illusion first clouds the mind, then moves the person.
simple_meaning: The king's priest is taken away again and left confused in a mountain cave through illusion.
insight: It shows how manipulation works by isolating helpers and weakening clear thinking.
modern_relevance: Someone in a group chat keeps steering everyone off course, and by the time people notice, the damage is already done. Confusion spreads fastest when judgment is blurred.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आपु बिरचि उपरोहित रूपा। परेउ जाइ तेहि सेज अनूपा॥ जागेउ नृप अनभएँ बिहाना। देखि भवन अति अचरजु माना ॥
translation: वह आप पुरोहित का रूप बनाकर उसकी सुंदर सेज पर जा लेटा। राजा सबेरा होने से पहले ही जागा और अपना घर देखकर उसने बड़ा ही आश्चर्य माना ॥
english_translation: He fashioned himself as the priest and lay down on the priest's beautiful bed. The king woke before dawn and, seeing his own palace, was filled with wonder.
essence: A disguise can reorder reality for a moment.
simple_meaning: He took the priest's form and lay on the priest's bed. At daybreak, the king woke up in his own palace and was astonished.
insight: It shows a story moving through disguise and disorientation, setting up the next step.
modern_relevance: You wake up in a hotel room after a long night and need a second to remember where you are. That brief confusion is all this verse holds.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि महिमा मन महुँ अनुमानी। उठेउ गवँहिं जेहिं जान न रानी॥ कानन गयउ बाजि चढ़ि तेहीं। पुर नर नारि न जानेउ केहीं ॥
translation: मन में मुनि की महिमा का अनुमान करके वह धीरे से उठा, जिसमें रानी न जान पावे। फिर उसी घोड़े पर चढ़कर वन को चला गया। नगर के किसी भी स्त्री-पुरुष ने नहीं जाना ॥
english_translation: Thinking of the sage's greatness in his heart, he rose quietly so the queen would not know. Then he mounted that same horse and rode into the forest. No man or woman in the city knew.
essence: Quiet action can carry the heaviest turning point.
simple_meaning: He leaves quietly, without letting the queen or the city know, and rides into the forest.
insight: It shows action without display: move decisively, but without stirring the whole house.
modern_relevance: You slip out before dawn for a difficult conversation, hoping no one notices the weight you’re carrying. Some responsibilities are borne in silence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गएँ जाम जुग भूपति आवा। घर घर उत्सव बाज बधावा॥ उपरोहितहि देख जब राजा। चकित बिलोक सुमिरि सोइ काजा ॥
translation: दो पहर बीत जाने पर राजा आया। घर-घर उत्सव होने लगे और बधावा बजने लगा। जब राजा ने पुरोहित को देखा, तब वह (अपने) उसी कार्य का स्मरणकर उसे आश्चर्य से देखने लगा ॥
english_translation: After half the day passed, the king returned. Every house filled with celebration and drums of welcome. When the king saw the priest, he stared in amazement, remembering that very deed.
essence: Joy outside cannot erase the memory of a hidden deed.
simple_meaning: The king comes home to a city full of celebration, then sees the priest and remembers the strange deed with surprise.
insight: It shows how a buried action can resurface the moment its witness appears.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering after a private mistake, and someone’s face reminds you instantly. The room is cheerful, but your own memory is not.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जुग सम नृपहि गए दिन तीनी। कपटी मुनि पद रह मति लीनी॥ समय जान उपरोहित आवा। नृपहि मते सब कहि समुझावा ॥
translation: राजा को तीन दिन युग के समान बीते। उसकी बुद्धि कपटी मुनि के चरणों में लगी रही। निश्चित समय जानकर पुरोहित (बना हुआ राक्षस) आया और राजा के साथ की हुई गुप्त सलाह के अनुसार (उसने अपने) सब विचार उसे समझाकर कह दिए ॥
english_translation: Three days passed for the king like ages. His mind stayed fixed at the feet of the deceitful ascetic. At the right time, the priest arrived and explained everything according to the secret plan agreed upon with the king.
essence: Uncertainty makes even a few days feel endless.
simple_meaning: The king waited three days in anxious expectation, still trusting the disguised ascetic. Then the priest arrived at the appointed time and explained the agreed plan.
insight: It shows how expectation can distort time and hold the mind captive until the next instruction arrives.
modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone after sending a message that matters. Every minute feels longer than it should, because your mind has already gone ahead of the answer.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नृप हरषेउ पहिचानि गुरु भ्रम बस रहा न चेत। बरे तुरत सत सहस बर बिप्र कुटुंब समेत ॥
translation: (संकेत के अनुसार) गुरु को (उस रूप में) पहचानकर राजा प्रसन्न हुआ। भ्रमवश उसे चेत न रहा (कि यह तापस मुनि है या कालकेतु राक्षस)। उसने तुरंत एक लाख उत्तम ब्राह्मणों को कुटुम्ब सहित निमंत्रण दे दिया ॥
english_translation: The king rejoiced after recognizing the guru. Deluded by illusion, he did not realize what was happening, and at once invited one hundred thousand excellent Brahmins with their families.
essence: Recognition without clear seeing still leaves a person easy to mislead.
simple_meaning: The king thinks he has recognized his teacher and feels happy, but illusion still clouds his mind. He quickly invites a huge number of Brahmins with their families.
insight: It shows how relief can deepen error when the mind stops questioning too soon.
modern_relevance: You finally get a reply from someone you trust, and relief makes you stop checking the details. One warm feeling can make you overlook the whole setup.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उपरोहित जेवनार बनाई। छरस चारि बिधि जसि श्रुति गाई॥ मायामय तेहिं कीन्हि रसोई। बिंजन बहु गनि सकइ न कोई ॥
translation: पुरोहित ने छह रस और चार प्रकार के भोजन, जैसा कि वेदों में वर्णन है, बनाए। उसने मायामयी रसोई तैयार की और इतने व्यंजन बनाए, जिन्हें कोई गिन नहीं सकता ॥
english_translation: The priest prepared a feast with six tastes and four kinds of food, as the Vedas describe. He set up an illusion-made kitchen and cooked countless dishes no one could number.
essence: Illusion can dress itself as abundance and still carry harm.
simple_meaning: The false priest prepares a lavish, magical feast with many kinds of food. It is part of his trick to deceive the king and the court.
insight: It trains attention to look past spectacle and ask what intention is being served.
modern_relevance: A polished presentation, a glossy deck, a perfect menu, a smooth voice — all of it can still be a setup. The danger often arrives dressed as refinement.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिबिध मृगन्ह कर आमिष राँधा। तेहि महुँ बिप्र माँसु खल साँधा॥ भोजन कहुँ सब बिप्र बोलाए। पद पखारि सादर बैठाए ॥
translation: अनेक प्रकार के पशुओं का मांस पकाया और उसमें उस दुष्ट ने ब्राह्मणों का मांस मिला दिया। सब ब्राह्मणों को भोजन के लिए बुलाया और चरण धोकर आदर सहित बैठाया ॥
english_translation: He cooked various kinds of animal meat and mixed in the flesh of the Brahmins. He invited all the Brahmins for food, washed their feet, and seated them with respect.
essence: Respect without sincerity becomes another form of harm.
simple_meaning: The wicked man prepared meat, mixed in human flesh, and invited the Brahmins to eat after honoring them.
insight: It trains you to judge conduct by motive, not ceremony.
modern_relevance: Someone smiles warmly in a meeting, offers tea, and signs off with perfect manners — while quietly setting a trap behind the scenes. This verse exposes that split between appearance and intent.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परुसन जबहिं लाग महिपाला। भै अकासबानी तेहि काला॥ बिप्रबृंद उठि उठि गृह जाहू। है बड़ि हानि अन्न जनि खाहू ॥
translation: ज्यों ही राजा परोसने लगा, उसी काल (कालकेतुकृत) आकाशवाणी हुई- हे ब्राह्मणों! उठ-उठकर अपने घर जाओ, यह अन्न मत खाओ। इस (के खाने) में बड़ी हानि है ॥
english_translation: As soon as the king began serving the food, a voice from the sky rang out: "Priests, rise and go home. Do not eat this food. It brings great harm."
essence: A clear warning can interrupt hidden harm before it is swallowed.
simple_meaning: Just as the king starts serving the meal, a voice from the sky warns the priests to leave at once and not eat, because the food is dangerous.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremonial appearance to hidden danger, reminding you to pause before accepting what looks generous.
modern_relevance: You’re about to accept food at a gathering, but something feels off: the smell, the timing, the person insisting too hard. Sometimes caution arrives as a sudden inner alarm.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भयउ रसोईं भूसुर माँसू। सब द्विज उठे मानि बिस्वासू॥ भूप बिकल मति मोहँ भुलानी। भावी बस न आव मुख बानी ॥
translation: रसोई में ब्राह्मणों का मांस बना है। (आकाशवाणी का) विश्वास मानकर सब ब्राह्मण उठ खड़े हुए। राजा व्याकुल हो गया (परन्तु), उसकी बुद्धि मोह में भूली हुई थी। होनहारवश उसके मुँह से (एक) बात (भी) न निकली ॥
english_translation: The kitchen had become a place of brahmin flesh. Trusting the warning, all the brahmins stood up. The king was distressed, his mind lost in delusion, and fate left him speechless.
essence: Delusion silences the wrongdoer; clear trust lets others walk away.
simple_meaning: The brahmins realize the food is defiled and leave at once. The king is stunned, trapped in confusion, and cannot speak.
insight: It shows how confusion silences wrongdoing and how timely awareness lets others withdraw before harm deepens.
modern_relevance: You open a group chat and see the warning you ignored ten minutes ago. Everyone else has already stepped back, but you are still staring at the screen, frozen by the mess you made.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बोले बिप्र सकोप तब नहिं कछु कीन्ह बिचार। जाइ निसाचर होहु नृप मूढ़ सहित परिवार ॥
translation: तब ब्राह्मण क्रोध सहित बोल उठे- उन्होंने कुछ भी विचार नहीं किया- अरे मूर्ख राजा! तू जाकर परिवार सहित राक्षस हो ॥
english_translation: Then the angry Brahmins spoke: without thinking at all, "Go, O foolish king, and become a demon along with your family."
essence: Anger without reflection turns correction into destruction.
simple_meaning: The Brahmins, angered by the king’s mistake, curse him and his family to become demons.
insight: It shows how unchecked anger hardens judgment and escalates conflict instead of resolving it.
modern_relevance: A group chat explodes after one careless mistake, and the first angry reply makes everything worse. The damage is no longer the mistake itself, but the words thrown in heat.
speaker: Brahmins

verse_text: छत्रबंधु तैं बिप्र बोलाई। घालै लिए सहित समुदाई॥ ईश्वर राखा धरम हमारा। जैहसि तैं समेत परिवारा ॥
translation: रे नीच क्षत्रिय! तूने तो परिवार सहित ब्राह्मणों को बुलाकर उन्हें नष्ट करना चाहा था, ईश्वर ने हमारे धर्म की रक्षा की। अब तू परिवार सहित नष्ट होगा ॥
english_translation: You low-born warrior, you called the brahmins here with your family and tried to destroy them. The divine protected our way of life. Now you will perish with your family.
essence: Harm aimed at others returns to the one who planned it.
simple_meaning: The brahmins accuse the king of trying to destroy them. They say the divine protected them, and now the king and his family will be destroyed.
insight: It shows how violent intention rebounds, and how protection of the innocent becomes the basis for judgment.
modern_relevance: You set a trap in a group chat, expecting the other side to be cornered. Instead, the message thread exposes your intent, and the damage lands back on your own name.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: संबत मध्य नास तव होऊ। जलदाता न रहिहि कुल कोऊ॥ नृप सुनि श्राप बिकल अति त्रासा। भै बहोरि बर गिरा अकासा ॥
translation: एक वर्ष के भीतर तेरा नाश हो जाए, तेरे कुल में कोई पानी देने वाला तक न रहेगा। शाप सुनकर राजा भय के मारे अत्यन्त व्याकुल हो गया। फिर सुंदर आकाशवाणी हुई- ॥
english_translation: May your line be destroyed within a year, and no one in your family remain to offer water. Hearing the curse, the king became extremely fearful and distressed. Then a beautiful voice came from the sky.
essence: Fear arrives before the sky has finished speaking.
simple_meaning: The brahmin curses the king’s line to end within a year. The king is terrified, and then a voice from the sky speaks.
insight: It shifts attention from the curse itself to the king’s immediate collapse under fear.
modern_relevance: A message lands in your phone inbox and your stomach drops before you even finish reading it. One sentence can turn a whole day into fear.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिप्रहु श्राप बिचारि न दीन्हा। नहिं अपराध भूप कछु कीन्हा॥ चकित बिप्र सब सुनि नभबानी। भूप गयउ जहँ भोजन खानी ॥
translation: हे ब्राह्मणों! तुमने विचार कर शाप नहीं दिया। राजा ने कुछ भी अपराध नहीं किया। आकाशवाणी सुनकर सब ब्राह्मण चकित हो गए। तब राजा वहाँ गया, जहाँ भोजन बना था ॥
english_translation: O Brahmins, you did not think before cursing him. The king had done no wrong. Hearing the voice from the sky, all the Brahmins were stunned. Then the king went to the place where the food had been prepared.
essence: Judgment softens when innocence becomes clear.
simple_meaning: The Brahmins realize the curse was not justified, because the king had done nothing wrong. Shocked by the heavenly voice, they watch him go to the place where the meal was being prepared.
insight: It shifts the mind from emotional certainty to factual checking before judgment.
modern_relevance: You fire off a furious message, then realize you misunderstood the whole situation. By the time the facts land, the damage is already moving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तहँ न असन नहिं बिप्र सुआरा। फिरेउ राउ मन सोच अपारा॥ सब प्रसंग महिसुरन्ह सुनाई। त्रसित परेउ अवनीं अकुलाई ॥
translation: (देखा तो) वहाँ न भोजन था, न रसोइया ब्राह्मण ही था। तब राजा मन में अपार चिन्ता करता हुआ लौटा। उसने ब्राह्मणों को सब वृत्तान्त सुनाया और (बड़ा ही) भयभीत और व्याकुल होकर वह पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा ॥
english_translation: There was no food there, and no Brahmin cook. The king returned with great worry in his mind. He told the Brahmins everything, then fell to the ground in fear and distress.
essence: Fear can break a person before events do.
simple_meaning: The king finds no meal and no Brahmin cook, so he returns in deep worry, explains the situation, and collapses in fear.
insight: It shows how anxiety magnifies a problem and makes a person collapse before the outcome is known.
modern_relevance: You open the kitchen after a long day and realize nothing is ready, the deadline is still real, and your mind starts spiraling before anything has actually gone wrong.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूपति भावी मिटइ नहिं जदपि न दूषन तोर। किएँ अन्यथा दोइ नहिं बिप्रश्राप अति घोर ॥
translation: हे राजन! यद्यपि तुम्हारा दोष नहीं है, तो भी होनहार नहीं मिटता। ब्राह्मणों का शाप बहुत ही भयानक होता है, यह किसी तरह भी टाले टल नहीं सकता ॥
english_translation: O king, what is destined does not change, even though you are not at fault. A brahmin's curse is very terrible; it cannot be turned aside in any other way.
essence: Faultlessness does not always prevent suffering.
simple_meaning: Even without fault, the king must face what has already come. The curse is said to be unavoidable.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame and resistance toward sober acceptance of what cannot be reversed.
modern_relevance: You did everything right, and the project still collapsed. The apology is real, but so is the fact that some losses cannot be negotiated away.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस कहि सब महिदेव सिधाए। समाचार पुरलोगन्ह पाए॥ सोचहिं दूषन दैवहि देहीं। बिरचत हंस काग किए जेहीं ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर सब ब्राह्मण चले गए। नगरवासियों ने (जब) यह समाचार पाया, तो वे चिन्ता करने और विधाता को दोष देने लगे, जिसने हंस बनाते-बनाते कौआ कर दिया (ऐसे पुण्यात्मा राजा को देवता बनाना चाहिए था, सो राक्षस बना दिया) ॥
english_translation: After saying this, all the Brahmins departed. When the townspeople heard the news, they began to worry and blame fate, saying that the one who forms swans has made crows.
essence: Grief turns into blame when people cannot undo what happened.
simple_meaning: The Brahmins leave, and the town falls into grief and complaint. People blame fate for turning a noble ruler into a ruined one.
insight: It shows how grief quickly becomes projection when people feel powerless.
modern_relevance: A family group chat blows up after bad news, and everyone starts asking who ruined everything. The first response is often blame, not clarity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उपरोहितहि भवन पहुँचाई। असुर तापसहि खबरि जनाई॥ तेहिं खल जहँ तहँ पत्र पठाए। सजि सजि सेन भूप सब धाए ॥
translation: पुरोहित को उसके घर पहुँचाकर असुर (कालकेतु) ने (कपटी) तपस्वी को खबर दी। उस दुष्ट ने जहाँ-तहाँ पत्र भेजे, जिससे सब (बैरी) राजा सेना सजा-सजाकर (चढ़) दौड़े ॥
english_translation: After escorting the priest to his home, the demon informed the deceitful ascetic. That wicked one sent letters everywhere, and all the hostile kings hurried forth, arraying their armies.
essence: False news can summon armies before anyone sees the truth.
simple_meaning: The demon passes the message on, the deceitful ascetic spreads the word, and enemy kings rush out with their armies.
insight: It shows how deception spreads conflict quickly by recruiting others before clarity can arrive.
modern_relevance: A group chat turns one rumor into three meetings, then a full-blown crisis. One careless message can mobilize people faster than truth can catch up.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: घेरेन्हि नगर निसान बजाई। बिबिध भाँति नित होइ लराई॥ जूझे सकल सुभट करि करनी। बंधु समेत परेउ नृप धरनी ॥
translation: और उन्होंने डंका बजाकर नगर को घेर लिया। नित्य प्रति अनेक प्रकार से लड़ाई होने लगी। (प्रताप भानु के) सब योद्धा (शूरवीरों की) करनी करके रण में जूझ मरे। राजा भी भाई सहित खेत रहा ॥
english_translation: They surrounded the city and sounded the war drums. Battles raged there in many forms every day. All the warriors fought bravely and fell on the battlefield, and the king fell there with his brothers.
essence: War closes in, and even kings fall.
simple_meaning: The city is surrounded, fighting breaks out daily, and the king and his brothers die in battle.
insight: It shifts attention from heroic display to the cost of conflict.
modern_relevance: A neighborhood goes tense after days of threats, sirens keep sounding, and everyone is bracing for the next blow. In that atmosphere, even the strongest people can be swept into collapse.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सत्यकेतु कुल कोउ नहिं बाँचा। बिप्रश्राप किमि होइ असाँचा॥ रिपु जिति सब नृप नगर बसाई। निज पुर गवने जय जसु पाई ॥
translation: सत्यकेतु के कुल में कोई नहीं बचा। ब्राह्मणों का शाप झूठा कैसे हो सकता था। शत्रु को जीतकर नगर को (फिर से) बसाकर सब राजा विजय और यश पाकर अपने-अपने नगर को चले गए ॥
english_translation: No one in Satyaketu's line survived. How could the Brahmins' curse prove false? Defeating the enemy, the kings rebuilt the city, gained victory and fame, and returned to their own kingdoms.
essence: Victory in the city cannot undo a curse already fulfilled.
simple_meaning: Satyaketu's family was wiped out because the curse had to come true. After defeating the enemy, the kings restored the city and went back home with victory.
insight: It shifts attention from surface victory to the deeper consequences already unfolding beneath it.
modern_relevance: A group finishes cleaning up the office after a scandal, and everyone wants to move on. But the damage that was set in motion earlier has already done its work.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरद्वाज सुनु जाहि जब होई बिधाता बाम। धूरि मेरुसम जनक जम ताहि ब्यालसम दाम ॥
translation: (याज्ञवल्क्यजी कहते हैं-) हे भरद्वाज! सुनो, विधाता जब जिसके विपरीत होते हैं, तब उसके लिए धूल सुमेरु पर्वत के समान (भारी और कुचल डालने वाली), पिता यम के समान (कालरूप) और रस्सी साँप के समान (काट खाने वाली) हो जाती है ॥
english_translation: Bharadwaj, listen: when the creator turns against someone, dust becomes like Mount Meru, a father becomes like Yama, and a rope becomes like a snake.
essence: When life turns hostile, perception itself becomes heavy and dangerous.
simple_meaning: When life turns against someone, even ordinary things feel unbearable: dust feels huge, a father feels like death, and a rope feels like a snake.
insight: It trains the mind to recognize fear's exaggeration instead of accepting every impression as reality.
modern_relevance: You get one bad email, and suddenly every message feels hostile. The room, the tone, the silence — all of it seems heavier than it is. This verse names that warped seeing.
speaker: Yajnavalkya

verse_text: काल पाइ मुनि सुनु सोइ राजा। भयउ निसाचर सहित समाजा॥ दस सिर ताहि बीस भुजदंडा। रावन नाम बीर बरिबंडा ॥
translation: हे मुनि! सुनो, समय पाकर वही राजा परिवार सहित रावण नामक राक्षस हुआ। उसके दस सिर और बीस भुजाएँ थीं और वह बड़ा ही प्रचण्ड शूरवीर था ॥
english_translation: O sage, listen: in time, that very king became a demon along with his household. He was called Ravana, with ten heads, twenty arms, and immense heroic might.
essence: Great power, cut off from restraint, becomes a force of ruin.
simple_meaning: That king and his household later became Ravana and his demon clan. He is described as a mighty warrior with ten heads and twenty arms.
insight: It frames Ravana as a warning: greatness twisted by ego becomes destruction.
modern_relevance: A person who keeps feeding pride, control, and resentment can slowly become unrecognizable to everyone around them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूप अनुज अरिमर्दन नामा। भयउ सो कुंभकरन बलधामा॥ सचिव जो रहा धरमरुचि जासू। भयउ बिमात्र बंधु लघु तासू ॥
translation: अरिमर्दन नामक जो राजा का छोटा भाई था, वह बल का धाम कुम्भकर्ण हुआ। उसका जो मंत्री था, जिसका नाम धर्मरुचि था, वह रावण का सौतेला छोटा भाई हुआ ॥
english_translation: The king's younger brother, Arimardan, became Kumbhakarna, the strong one. The minister named Dharamaruchi became Ravana's younger half-brother.
essence: Old relations return in new forms around Ravana.
simple_meaning: Ravana's former allies and relatives are being identified by their later births in his family. The verse simply lists who became whom.
insight: It keeps the reader oriented in the genealogy, not the philosophy.
modern_relevance: A family photo can hide a whole history of loyalty, resentment, and change. Later, the same people may return in roles no one expected.
speaker: Narrator
