insight: It connects public duty with private study: serve people, keep learning, and teach what you learn to those near you.
modern_relevance: You finish a long day, then still sit with a younger sibling or teammate and explain what you learned instead of showing off. Real care includes helping others understand.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रातकाल उठि कै रघुनाथा। मातु पिता गुरु नावहिं माथा॥ आयसु मागि करहिं पुर काजा। देखि चरित हरषइ मन राजा ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी प्रातःकाल उठकर माता-पिता और गुरु को मस्तक नवाते हैं और आज्ञा लेकर नगर का काम करते हैं। उनके चरित्र देख-देखकर राजा मन में बड़े हर्षित होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Raghunath rises at dawn, bows to his mother, father, and teacher, and asks permission before handling the city's affairs. Seeing his conduct, the king's heart fills with joy.
essence: True greatness bows before it acts.
simple_meaning: Ram begins the day with respect, asks permission before acting, and handles his duties well. His conduct delights the king.
insight: It teaches you to begin action with humility and permission, not ego and impulse.
modern_relevance: You wake before everyone else, check your phone, and still choose to greet the people who shaped you before touching the day's tasks. That small order changes everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ब्यापक अकल अनीह अज निर्गुन नाम न रूप। भगत हेतु नाना बिधि करत चरित्र अनूप ॥
translation: जो व्यापक, अकल (निरवयव), इच्छारहित, अजन्मा और निर्गुण है तथा जिनका न नाम है न रूप, वही भगवान भक्तों के लिए नाना प्रकार के अनुपम (अलौकिक) चरित्र करते हैं ॥
english_translation: The all-pervading, uncreated, desireless, birthless, formless one performs many wondrous acts for devotees.
essence: The formless one becomes personally present for those who love him.
simple_meaning: Ram is beyond form, name, and desire, yet he still appears in countless beautiful ways for devotees.
insight: It shifts devotion from abstract belief to lived encounter: the infinite becomes relatable through loving action.
modern_relevance: You can feel utterly unseen, then one small act of care changes everything. This verse says the deepest presence often arrives quietly, in a form you can actually meet.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: यह सब चरित कहा मैं गाई। आगिलि कथा सुनहु मन लाई॥ बिस्वामित्र महामुनि ग्यानी। बसहिं बिपिन सुभ आश्रम जानी ॥
translation: यह सब चरित्र मैंने गाकर (बखानकर) कहा। अब आगे की कथा मन लगाकर सुनो। ज्ञानी महामुनि विश्वामित्रजी वन में शुभ आश्रम (पवित्र स्थान) जानकर बसते थे, ॥
english_translation: I have sung and told all these deeds. Now listen closely to the next part of the story. The wise great sage Vishwamitra lived in a beautiful hermitage in the forest.
essence: A new chapter begins when attention turns fully toward it.
simple_meaning: The narrator closes one section and asks the listener to pay attention to the next. Vishwamitra, a wise sage, lives in a holy forest hermitage.
insight: It teaches you to treat transitions as sacred attention points, not empty gaps.
modern_relevance: You finish one chapter of your life and sense the next one arriving. Before the next demand hits, the mind needs a pause so it can actually receive what comes.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ जप जग्य जोग मुनि करहीं। अति मारीच सुबाहुहि डरहीं॥ देखत जग्य निसाचर धावहिं। करहिं उपद्रव मुनि दुख पावहिं ॥
translation: जहाँ वे मुनि जप, यज्ञ और योग करते थे, परन्तु मारीच और सुबाहु से बहुत डरते थे। यज्ञ देखते ही राक्षस दौड़ पड़ते थे और उपद्रव मचाते थे, जिससे मुनि (बहुत) दुःख पाते थे ॥
english_translation: Where the sages performed chanting, sacrifice, and yoga, Maricha and Subahu feared them greatly. At the sight of a sacrifice, the demons would rush in and create trouble, and the sages suffered distress.
essence: Sacred work collapses when disturbance is allowed to rule.
simple_meaning: The sages were trying to live in peace through chanting, sacrifice, and meditation, but demons kept attacking and disturbing their rites.
insight: It shifts attention from the ritual itself to the conditions needed to protect it.
modern_relevance: You finally sit down to focus, and the phone keeps buzzing, the door keeps opening, and your attention keeps getting stolen. Some work cannot survive without protection.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गाधितनय मन चिंता ब्यापी। हरि बिनु मरहिं न निसिचर पापी॥ तब मुनिबर मन कीन्ह बिचारा। प्रभु अवतरेउ हरन महि भारा ॥
translation: गाधि के पुत्र विश्वामित्रजी के मन में चिन्ता छा गई कि ये पापी राक्षस भगवान के (मारे) बिना न मरेंगे। तब श्रेष्ठ मुनि ने मन में विचार किया कि प्रभु ने पृथ्वी का भार हरने के लिए अवतार लिया है ॥
english_translation: A worry filled the mind of Gadhi's son: these sinful demons will not die without the divine. Then the great sage reflected: the Lord has incarnated to remove the burden of the earth.
essence: Some problems yield only to the force already sent to end them.
simple_meaning: विश्वामित्र को चिंता हुई कि ये राक्षस भगवान के बिना नहीं मरेंगे। तब उन्होंने सोचा कि प्रभु पृथ्वी का बोझ हरने के लिए अवतार ले चुके हैं।
insight: It shifts the mind from helpless struggle to seeking the right support at the right level.
modern_relevance: You have tried every practical fix, and the problem keeps returning. Then a quieter thought arrives: this is bigger than your control, and the right help already exists.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहूँ मिस देखौं पद जाई। करि बिनती आनौं दोउ भाई॥ ग्यान बिराग सकल गुन अयना। सो प्रभु मैं देखब भरि नयना ॥
translation: इसी बहाने जाकर मैं उनके चरणों का दर्शन करूँ और विनती करके दोनों भाइयों को ले आऊँ। (अहा!) जो ज्ञान, वैराग्य और सब गुणों के धाम हैं, उन प्रभु को मैं नेत्र भरकर देखूँगा ॥
english_translation: Using this excuse, I will go and see his feet. After praying, I will bring both brothers back. The Lord who is the home of wisdom, non-attachment, and every virtue—I will behold him with these eyes full.
essence: Even a mission can become a longing to behold the highest.
simple_meaning: Vishwamitra plans to visit Ram, bow before him, and bring the two brothers back. He longs to see Ram, who embodies wisdom, detachment, and every virtue.
insight: It shifts action from mere strategy to pilgrimage, where even a task becomes a way to meet what is highest.
modern_relevance: You make a practical visit for help, but your deeper reason is reverence. Beneath the errand, you are longing to be near what you admire most.
speaker: Vishwamitra

verse_text: बहुबिधि करत मनोरथ जात लागि नहिं बार। करि मज्जन सरऊ जल गए भूप दरबार ॥
translation: बहुत प्रकार से मनोरथ करते हुए जाने में देर नहीं लगी। सरयूजी के जल में स्नान करके वे राजा के दरवाजे पर पहुँचे ॥
english_translation: Thinking many thoughts along the way, he wasted no time. After bathing in the Saryu, he reached the king's court.
essence: Thought becomes real only when it reaches the door.
simple_meaning: Visvamitra makes his way to the palace quickly, after bathing in the Saryu. The verse simply moves the story forward.
insight: It shifts the mind from planning to arrival, showing that intention must become action.
modern_relevance: You finally stop rehearsing the conversation in your head, wash your face, and walk into the room. The real change begins when thought becomes movement.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि आगमन सुना जब राजा। मिलन गयउ लै बिप्र समाजा॥ करि दंडवत मुनिहि सनमानी। निज आसन बैठारेन्हि आनी ॥
translation: राजा ने जब मुनि का आना सुना, तब वे ब्राह्मणों के समाज को साथ लेकर मिलने गए और दण्डवत् करके मुनि का सम्मान करते हुए उन्हें लाकर अपने आसन पर बैठाया ॥
english_translation: When the king heard of the sage's arrival, he went to meet him with the company of brahmins. He bowed down, honored the sage, brought him in, and seated him on his own seat.
essence: Greatness bows first.
simple_meaning: The king hears that a sage has arrived, goes out with the brahmins, bows to him, honors him, and seats him on his own throne.
insight: It teaches you to meet wisdom with humility and visible respect.
modern_relevance: You hear that a respected elder has come to visit. You stop what you are doing, walk out to greet them, and make room for them first. Honor is shown in how you receive people.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चरन पखारि कीन्हि अति पूजा। मो सम आजु धन्य नहिं दूजा॥ बिबिध भाँति भोजन करवावा। मुनिबर हृदयँ हरष अति पावा ॥
translation: चरणों को धोकर बहुत पूजा की और कहा- मेरे समान धन्य आज दूसरा कोई नहीं है। फिर अनेक प्रकार के भोजन करवाए, जिससे श्रेष्ठ मुनि ने अपने हृदय में बहुत ही हर्ष प्राप्त किया ॥
english_translation: He washed the sage’s feet and offered great worship, saying, "No one is more blessed than I today." Then he served many kinds of food, and the best of sages felt great joy in his heart.
essence: True honor is shown through humble service.
simple_meaning: The king honors the sage with foot-washing, worship, and a generous meal. The sage feels deep joy at the king’s respect.
insight: It teaches that reverence must be embodied through concrete care and hospitality.
modern_relevance: A guest arrives after a long journey, and you stop everything to care for them properly. No performance, no hurry — just real honor shown through service.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि चरननि मेले सुत चारी। राम देखि मुनि देह बिसारी॥ भए मगन देखत मुख सोभा। जनु चकोर पूरन ससि लोभा ॥
translation: फिर राजा ने चारों पुत्रों को मुनि के चरणों पर डाल दिया (उनसे प्रणाम कराया)। श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर मुनि अपनी देह की सुधि भूल गए। वे श्री रामजी के मुख की शोभा देखते ही ऐसे मग्न हो गए, मानो चकोर पूर्ण चन्द्रमा को देखकर लुभा गया हो ॥
english_translation: Then the king had his four sons placed at the sage's feet. Seeing Ram, the sage forgot his body. He became so absorbed in Ram's beautiful face, like a chakor longing for the full moon.
essence: Ram's beauty makes the seeker forget himself.
simple_meaning: The king brings his four sons before the sage. The sage sees Ram and becomes so absorbed in his beauty that he forgets his own body.
insight: It shows how true beauty and reverence can pull the mind out of self-consciousness.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence instantly quiets the room. Your phone stays in your pocket, your thoughts stop racing, and for a moment attention becomes pure admiration.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब मन हरषि बचन कह राऊ। मुनि अस कृपा न कीन्हिहु काऊ॥ केहि कारन आगमन तुम्हारा। कहहु सो करत न लावउँ बारा ॥
translation: तब राजा ने मन में हर्षित होकर ये वचन कहे- हे मुनि! इस प्रकार कृपा तो आपने कभी नहीं की। आज किस कारण से आपका शुभागमन हुआ? कहिए, मैं उसे पूरा करने में देर नहीं लगाऊँगा ॥
english_translation: Then the king, delighted in his heart, said: "O sage, you have never shown such kindness to anyone. For what reason have you come? Tell me, and I will not delay doing it."
essence: True welcome offers help before the request is even spoken.
simple_meaning: King Dasharath welcomes the sage with joy and promises to do whatever he asks without delay.
insight: It teaches readiness to serve before knowing the full demand.
modern_relevance: Someone you deeply respect asks for help, and your first response is not calculation. You listen fully, because trust moves faster than suspicion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: असुर समूह सतावहिं मोही। मैं जाचन आयउँ नृप तोही॥ अनुज समेत देहु रघुनाथा। निसिचर बध मैं होब सनाथा ॥
translation: (मुनि ने कहा-) हे राजन् ! राक्षसों के समूह मुझे बहुत सताते हैं, इसीलिए मैं तुमसे कुछ माँगने आया हूँ। छोटे भाई सहित श्री रघुनाथजी को मुझे दो। राक्षसों के मारे जाने पर मैं सनाथ (सुरक्षित) हो जाऊँगा ॥
english_translation: O king, the hosts of demons torment me. I have come asking you for a gift: give me Raghunath together with his younger brother. When the demons are slain, I will be safe.
essence: True refuge may require giving up what you most want to keep.
simple_meaning: The sage says the demons trouble him and asks King Dasharath to give him Ram and Lakshman. He says their death will leave him safe.
insight: It shifts attention from possession to protection: what matters is not keeping the beloved close, but letting dharma move through them.
modern_relevance: A parent is asked to let a gifted child leave home for something hard and dangerous. The instinct is to hold on, but the larger duty is to release them for the work only they can do.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: देहु भूप मन हरषित तजहु मोह अग्यान। धर्म सुजस प्रभु तुम्ह कौं इन्ह कहँ अति कल्यान ॥
translation: हे राजन् ! प्रसन्न मन से इनको दो, मोह और अज्ञान को छोड़ दो। हे स्वामी! इससे तुमको धर्म और सुयश की प्राप्ति होगी और इनका परम कल्याण होगा ॥
english_translation: O king, give them with a joyful mind; abandon delusion and ignorance. O lord, this will bring you dharma and good fame, and bring great welfare to them.
essence: Right giving requires dropping attachment first.
simple_meaning: The request is simple: give the boys willingly, drop confusion, and choose what is right. That choice will honour the king and help everyone involved.
insight: It shifts the mind from possessiveness to righteous release.
modern_relevance: You are asked to let go of something you love because it is the right thing to do. Every instinct resists, but a clear mind knows that clinging can become its own kind of blindness.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुनि राजा अति अप्रिय बानी। हृदय कंप मुख दुति कुमुलानी॥ चौथेंपन पायउँ सुत चारी। बिप्र बचन नहिं कहेहु बिचारी ॥
translation: इस अत्यन्त अप्रिय वाणी को सुनकर राजा का हृदय काँप उठा और उनके मुख की कांति फीकी पड़ गई। (उन्होंने कहा-) हे ब्राह्मण! मैंने चौथेपन में चार पुत्र पाए हैं, आपने विचार कर बात नहीं कही ॥
english_translation: Hearing this very unpleasant speech, the king's heart trembled and the color left his face. He said, "O Brahmin, I have gained four sons only in old age; you have spoken without thinking."
essence: Grief makes the heart protest before it can understand.
simple_meaning: Dasharath is shaken by the sage's demand. He says the request is cruel because he has only just received four sons in old age.
insight: It shows how attachment makes even a generous person feel wounded before understanding the larger demand.
modern_relevance: You finally hear the words you were dreading after years of hoping for good news. Your chest tightens, and all you can say is, "Please think again."
speaker: King Dasharath

verse_text: मागहु भूमि धेनु धन कोसा। सर्बस देउँ आजु सहरोसा॥ देह प्रान तें प्रिय कछु नाहीं। सोउ मुनि देउँ निमिष एक माहीं ॥
translation: हे मुनि! आप पृथ्वी, गो, धन और खजाना माँग लीजिए, मैं आज बड़े हर्ष के साथ अपना सर्वस्व दे दूँगा। देह और प्राण से अधिक प्यारा कुछ भी नहीं होता, मैं उसे भी एक पल में दे दूँगा ॥
english_translation: Ask for land, cows, wealth, and treasure. Today I will give everything gladly. Nothing is dearer than body and life; I would give even that in a moment.
essence: Generosity fails when attachment reaches the heart.
simple_meaning: Dasharath offers everything he owns, even his own life, to honor the sage's request.
insight: It reveals the first crack in Dasharath’s resolve: he can offer possessions, but not what his heart clings to.
modern_relevance: You say, “Take whatever I have, just don’t ask for the one thing I cannot bear to lose.” That is the sound of love meeting a limit.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: सब सुत प्रिय मोहि प्रान की नाईं। राम देत नहिं बनइ गोसाईं॥ कहँ निसिचर अति घोर कठोरा। कहँ सुंदर सुत परम किसोरा ॥
translation: सभी पुत्र मुझे प्राणों के समान प्यारे हैं, उनमें भी हे प्रभो! राम को तो (किसी प्रकार भी) देते नहीं बनता। कहाँ अत्यन्त डरावने और क्रूर राक्षस और कहाँ परम किशोर अवस्था के (बिलकुल सुकुमार) मेरे सुंदर पुत्र! ॥
english_translation: All my sons are dear to me like my very life, but I cannot give Ram away, O Lord. How can I compare fierce, dreadful demons with my beautiful, tender young son?
essence: A father’s love trembles when duty asks for his child.
simple_meaning: Dasharath says all his sons are precious, but he cannot bear to give Ram away. Ram is gentle and beautiful, while the demons sound terrifying and cruel.
insight: It reveals the clash between parental attachment and the demands of dharma.
modern_relevance: A parent watches a child pack for a risky move, a harsh job, or a dangerous city. The mind knows courage matters; the heart still resists letting go.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: सुनि नृप गिरा प्रेम रस सानी। हृदयँ हरष माना मुनि ग्यानी॥ तब बसिष्ट बहुबिधि समुझावा। नृप संदेह नास कहँ पावा ॥
translation: प्रेम रस में सनी हुई राजा की वाणी सुनकर ज्ञानी मुनि विश्वामित्रजी ने हृदय में बड़ा हर्ष माना। तब वशिष्ठजी ने राजा को बहुत प्रकार से समझाया, जिससे राजा का संदेह नाश को प्राप्त हुआ ॥
english_translation: Hearing the king's words soaked in the nectar of love, the wise sage felt great joy in his heart. Then Vasishtha explained many things to the king, and the king's doubt was removed.
essence: Love-filled speech opens the heart to understanding.
simple_meaning: The king speaks with loving sincerity, and the sage feels joy. Then Vasishtha explains things clearly, and the king's doubt disappears.
insight: It shows that heartfelt honesty can make guidance effective and dissolve confusion.
modern_relevance: You finally tell the truth in a voice that shakes a little. The other person stops arguing and starts listening. Honest feeling opens the door that force never could.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अति आदर दोउ तनय बोलाए। हृदयँ लाइ बहु भाँति सिखाए॥ मेरे प्रान नाथ सुत दोऊ। तुम्ह मुनि पिता आन नहिं कोऊ ॥
translation: राजा ने बड़े ही आदर से दोनों पुत्रों को बुलाया और हृदय से लगाकर बहुत प्रकार से उन्हें शिक्षा दी। (फिर कहा-) हे नाथ! ये दोनों पुत्र मेरे प्राण हैं। हे मुनि! (अब) आप ही इनके पिता हैं, दूसरा कोई नहीं ॥
english_translation: With great respect, the king called both sons and embraced them, instructing them in many ways. He said, "These two sons are my very life, O sage; now you are their father, and no one else."
essence: True care can mean handing your most beloved over with trust.
simple_meaning: Dasharath lovingly brings both sons close, teaches them carefully, and entrusts them to Vishvamitra as their true guide and father for the journey ahead.
insight: It teaches you to bless the next step even when it hurts to let go.
modern_relevance: A parent walks a child to the first day at a new school, smiling through the ache. Love is not always holding on; sometimes it is handing over with trust.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सौंपे भूप रिषिहि सुत बहुबिधि देइ असीस। जननी भवन गए प्रभु चले नाइ पद सीस॥208 क ॥
translation: राजा ने बहुत प्रकार से आशीर्वाद देकर पुत्रों को ऋषि के हवाले कर दिया। फिर प्रभु माता के महल में गए और उनके चरणों में सिर नवाकर चले ॥
english_translation: The king handed the sons over to the sage with many blessings. Then the Lord went to his mother's chamber, bowed his head at her feet, and departed.
essence: Duty can be tender, not cold.
simple_meaning: Dasharath gives Ram and Lakshman to Vishwamitra with blessings. Ram then bows to Kaushalya and leaves.
insight: It teaches you to honour duty without bitterness, even when it separates you from what you love.
modern_relevance: You pack your child’s bag for the first day away from home, then watch them walk out the door. Love does not stop the leaving; it blesses it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुरुष सिंह दोउ बीर हरषि चले मुनि भय हरन। कृपासिंधु मतिधीर अखिल बिस्व कारन करन ॥
translation: पुरुषों में सिंह रूप दोनों भाई (राम-लक्ष्मण) मुनि का भय हरने के लिए प्रसन्न होकर चले। वे कृपा के समुद्र, धीर बुद्धि और सम्पूर्ण विश्व के कारण के भी कारण हैं ॥
english_translation: The two lion-like brothers went happily to remove the sage's fear. They are oceans of grace, steady in mind, and the cause behind the cause of the entire universe.
essence: Real greatness walks in gladly to remove another's fear.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman go joyfully to protect the sage and remove his fear. The verse also praises Ram as compassionate, steady, and the source behind all existence.
insight: It links courage with protection and reminds the reader that true power steadies others, not intimidates them.
modern_relevance: You walk into a difficult room with someone who feels unsafe. Your calm changes the atmosphere before a single word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अरुन नयन उर बाहु बिसाला। नील जलज तनु स्याम तमाला॥ कटि पट पीत कसें बर भाथा। रुचिर चाप सायक दुहुँ हाथा ॥
translation: भगवान के लाल नेत्र हैं, चौड़ी छाती और विशाल भुजाएँ हैं, नील कमल और तमाल के वृक्ष की तरह श्याम शरीर है, कमर में पीताम्बर (पहने) और सुंदर तरकस कसे हुए हैं। दोनों हाथों में (क्रमशः) सुंदर धनुष और बाण हैं ॥
english_translation: His eyes are red, his chest broad, his arms vast. His body is dark like a blue lotus and tamal tree. A yellow garment is tied at his waist, a beautiful quiver is strapped on, and a lovely bow and arrows are in both hands.
essence: Beauty and strength meet in one armed presence.
simple_meaning: Ram is described as beautifully radiant, dark-complexioned, and fully armed, with a bow and arrows in his hands.
insight: It shifts attention from abstract reverence to embodied presence: the divine is seen as beautiful, strong, and ready to act.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone entering a room and everything changes — calm, strength, and readiness all arrive together. That kind of presence needs no introduction.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: स्याम गौर सुंदर दोउ भाई। बिस्वामित्र महानिधि पाई॥ प्रभु ब्रह्मन्यदेव मैं जाना। मोहि निति पिता तजेउ भगवाना ॥
translation: श्याम और गौर वर्ण के दोनों भाई परम सुंदर हैं। विश्वामित्रजी को महान निधि प्राप्त हो गई। (वे सोचने लगे-) मैं जान गया कि प्रभु ब्रह्मण्यदेव (ब्राह्मणों के भक्त) हैं। मेरे लिए भगवान ने अपने पिता को भी छोड़ दिया ॥
english_translation: Both brothers, dark and fair, are beautifully radiant. Vishwamitra has found a great treasure. He thought, "I know the Lord is devoted to the righteous and the learned; for my sake, the Blessed One even left his father."
essence: True greatness shows itself in the willingness to leave comfort for duty.
simple_meaning: Vishvamitra sees Ram and Lakshman as a priceless blessing. He realises Ram protects those devoted to dharma and has already chosen to leave his father for this higher calling.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance to the moral courage behind a person's choices.
modern_relevance: You watch someone step away from family expectations to do what they know is right. The choice looks costly from outside, but it reveals a steadier kind of greatness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चले जात मुनि दीन्हि देखाई। सुनि ताड़का क्रोध करि धाई॥ एकहिं बान प्रान हरि लीन्हा। दीन जानि तेहि निज पद दीन्हा ॥
translation: मार्ग में चले जाते हुए मुनि ने ताड़का को दिखलाया। शब्द सुनते ही वह क्रोध करके दौड़ी। श्री रामजी ने एक ही बाण से उसके प्राण हर लिए और दीन जानकर उसको निजपद (अपना दिव्य स्वरूप) दिया ॥
english_translation: Walking along, the sage showed her. Hearing this, Tadka rushed in anger. Ram took her life with a single arrow and, seeing her as helpless, granted her his own divine state.
essence: Power becomes righteous when it protects the helpless.
simple_meaning: Ram ends Tadka's threat with one arrow, then shows mercy by giving her release.
insight: It teaches you to meet threat decisively, without losing compassion once the threat is ended.
modern_relevance: A bully corners the weakest person in the room, and everyone waits. Someone steps in firmly, stops the harm, and does not keep hatred after the danger ends.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब रिषि निज नाथहि जियँ चीन्ही। बिद्यानिधि कहुँ बिद्या दीन्ही॥ जाते लाग न छुधा पिपासा। अतुलित बल तनु तेज प्रकासा ॥
translation: तब ऋषि विश्वामित्र ने प्रभु को मन में विद्या का भंडार समझते हुए भी (लीला को पूर्ण करने के लिए) ऐसी विद्या दी, जिससे भूख-प्यास न लगे और शरीर में अतुलित बल और तेज का प्रकाश हो ॥
english_translation: Then the sage recognized his Lord in his heart and gave the treasure of knowledge the knowledge that prevents hunger and thirst and reveals incomparable strength and radiance in the body.
essence: True recognition gives the right knowledge at the right moment.
simple_meaning: विश्वामित्र ने मन में राम को अपना प्रभु पहचानकर उन्हें ऐसी विद्या दी, जिससे भूख-प्यास न लगे और शरीर में असाधारण बल और तेज प्रकट हो।
insight: It shifts the reader from thinking of knowledge as information to seeing it as support that sustains action.
modern_relevance: A mentor sees your potential before you do and gives you exactly what you need to keep going through the hard stretch.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आयुध सर्ब समर्पि कै प्रभु निज आश्रम आनि। कंद मूल फल भोजन दीन्ह भगति हित जानि ॥
translation: सब अस्त्र-शस्त्र समर्पण करके मुनि प्रभु श्री रामजी को अपने आश्रम में ले आए और उन्हें परम हितू जानकर भक्तिपूर्वक कंद, मूल और फल का भोजन कराया ॥
english_translation: After surrendering all weapons, the Lord brought him to his own hermitage and, knowing him to be devoted, gave him roots, fruits, and forest food.
essence: Devotion turns simple hospitality into an offering.
simple_meaning: The sage brings Ram to his hermitage, offers food, and receives him with devotion, seeing him as supremely worthy.
insight: It shifts attention from the food itself to the spirit in which service is given.
modern_relevance: A host clears the table, sets aside the phone, and serves a tired guest without making a show of it. Care becomes sacred in that small, unforced gesture.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रात कहा मुनि सन रघुराई। निर्भय जग्य करहु तुम्ह जाई॥ होम करन लागे मुनि झारी। आपु रहे मख कीं रखवारी ॥
translation: सबेरे श्री रघुनाथजी ने मुनि से कहा- आप जाकर निडर होकर यज्ञ कीजिए। यह सुनकर सब मुनि हवन करने लगे। आप (श्री रामजी) यज्ञ की रखवाली पर रहे ॥
english_translation: In the morning, Raghurai said to the sage, “Go and perform the sacrifice without fear.” The sage began the rite, while Ram himself stood guard over the sacrifice.
essence: Protection becomes real when Ram stands beside the work.
simple_meaning: Ram tells the sage to perform the sacrifice without fear, then stands guard while the ritual begins.
insight: It teaches that duty is not only promise but presence: protect the task by standing with it.
modern_relevance: You finally start the presentation after weeks of tension, and the one person you trusted stays beside you while you speak. Fear drops when support becomes visible.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनि मारीच निसाचर क्रोही। लै सहाय धावा मुनिद्रोही॥ बिनु फर बान राम तेहि मारा। सत जोजन गा सागर पारा ॥
translation: यह समाचार सुनकर मुनियों का शत्रु कोरथी राक्षस मारीच अपने सहायकों को लेकर दौड़ा। श्री रामजी ने बिना फल वाला बाण उसको मारा, जिससे वह सौ योजन के विस्तार वाले समुद्र के पार जा गिरा ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Maricha, the enemy of sages, rushed forward with his allies. Ram struck him with an arrow that bore no fruit, and he was hurled across the ocean of a hundred yojanas.
essence: One clear strike can silence a whole assault.
simple_meaning: Maricha, angry and backed by helpers, attacked the sages. Ram answered with one arrow and sent him flying far across the ocean.
insight: It shows force used without hesitation, so protection comes before drama.
modern_relevance: A chaotic message thread explodes with blame and panic, but one calm reply cuts through the noise. Not every attack deserves a long reaction.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पावक सर सुबाहु पुनि मारा। अनुज निसाचर कटकु सँघारा॥ मारि असुर द्विज निर्भयकारी। अस्तुति करहिं देव मुनि झारी ॥
translation: फिर सुबाहु को अग्निबाण मारा। इधर छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी ने राक्षसों की सेना का संहार कर डाला। इस प्रकार श्री रामजी ने राक्षसों को मारकर ब्राह्मणों को निर्भय कर दिया। तब सारे देवता और मुनि स्तुति करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Then Ram struck Subahu with a fire-arrow. Lakshman destroyed the army of demons. By killing the demons, Ram made the priests fearless, and the gods and sages began to praise him.
essence: True protection ends fear, and fearless people naturally praise what saved them.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman defeat the demons, and the priests are left safe. The gods and sages respond with praise.
insight: It shifts attention from heroic force to the peace that force makes possible.
modern_relevance: A room finally goes quiet after one person stands up and stops the chaos. Everyone else can breathe again, and the relief itself feels like praise.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तहँ पुनि कछुक दिवस रघुराया। रहे कीन्हि बिप्रन्ह पर दाया॥ भगति हेतु बहुत कथा पुराना। कहे बिप्र जद्यपि प्रभु जाना ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी ने वहाँ कुछ दिन और रहकर ब्राह्मणों पर दया की। भक्ति के कारण ब्राह्मणों ने उन्हें पुराणों की बहुत सी कथाएँ कहीं, यद्यपि प्रभु सब जानते थे ॥
english_translation: Raghunath stayed there for some more days and showed kindness to the Brahmins. Out of devotion, the Brahmins told many ancient stories, even though the Lord already knew them.
essence: Love turns familiar stories into sacred listening.
simple_meaning: Ram stayed a little longer, treated the Brahmins kindly, and listened as they shared old stories out of devotion, even though he already knew them.
insight: It shifts attention from information to reverent presence, where hearing itself becomes an act of devotion.
modern_relevance: A guest sits in your kitchen and listens to your parents repeat stories you have heard a hundred times. No one is bored. That is what love does to ordinary conversation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब मुनि सादर कहा बुझाई। चरित एक प्रभु देखिअ जाई॥ धनुषजग्य सुनि रघुकुल नाथा। हरषि चले मुनिबर के साथा ॥
translation: तदन्तर मुनि ने आदरपूर्वक समझाकर कहा- हे प्रभो! चलकर एक चरित्र देखिए। रघुकुल के स्वामी श्री रामचन्द्रजी धनुषयज्ञ (की बात) सुनकर मुनिश्रेष्ठ विश्वामित्रजी के साथ प्रसन्न होकर चले ॥
english_translation: Then the sage respectfully explained and said, "Come and see a wondrous event." Hearing of the bow sacrifice, the Lord of Raghu joyfully went with the great sage.
essence: The worthy invitation is answered with joyful readiness.
simple_meaning: Viswamitra invites Ram to witness the bow sacrifice. Ram hears the news and goes joyfully with him.
insight: It shifts the mind from passive listening to willing participation in dharma's unfolding.
modern_relevance: A mentor says, "Come with me, you need to see this," and you go without hesitation. Some moments are not chores; they are doorways into a larger life.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आश्रम एक दीख मग माहीं। खग मृग जीव जंतु तहँ नाहीं॥ पूछा मुनिहि सिला प्रभु देखी। सकल कथा मुनि कहा बिसेषी ॥
translation: मार्ग में एक आश्रम दिखाई पड़ा। वहाँ पशु-पक्षी, को भी जीव-जन्तु नहीं था। पत्थर की एक शिला को देखकर प्रभु ने पूछा, तब मुनि ने विस्तारपूर्वक सब कथा कही ॥
english_translation: On the road, they saw an ashram. There were no birds, beasts, or living creatures there. The Lord saw a stone slab and asked the sage about it. The sage then told the whole story in detail.
essence: One question can uncover a forgotten past.
simple_meaning: They come to a deserted hermitage where no creatures live. Ram notices a stone slab and asks about it, prompting the sage to tell its story.
insight: It shifts attention from the surface of a place to the story buried inside it.
modern_relevance: You walk into an old house and notice one cracked wall everyone else ignores. You ask about it, and suddenly a family story, a wound, or a truth comes back into view.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गौतम नारि श्राप बस उपल देह धरि धीर। चरन कमल रज चाहति कृपा करहु रघुबीर ॥
translation: गौतम मुनि की स्त्री अहल्या शापवश पत्थर की देह धारण किए बड़े धीरज से आपके चरणकमलों की धूलि चाहती है। हे रघुवीर! इस पर कृपा कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Gautama's wife, bound by a curse, has taken a stone body. With patient longing, she seeks the dust of your lotus feet. O Raghuvir, show her grace.
essence: Patient longing can still draw grace.
simple_meaning: Ahalya has been turned to stone by a curse, yet she still waits with patience for Ram's grace and the dust of his feet.
insight: It shifts attention from helplessness to receptive trust: grace can meet patient longing.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone who cannot yet respond — a parent in recovery, a friend in silence, a relationship under strain. This verse honors the dignity of waiting without losing hope.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परसत पद पावन सोकनसावन प्रगट भई तपपुंज सही। देखत रघुनायक जन सुखदायक सनमुख होइ कर जोरि रही॥ अति प्रेम अधीरा पुलक शरीरा मुख नहिं आवइ बचन कही। अतिसय बड़भागी चरनन्हि लागी जुगल नयन जलधार बही ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के पवित्र और शोक को नाश करने वाले चरणों का स्पर्श पाते ही सचमुच वह तपोमूर्ति अहल्या प्रकट हो गई। भक्तों को सुख देने वाले श्री रघुनाथजी को देखकर वह हाथ जोड़कर सामने खड़ी रह गई। अत्यन्त प्रेम के कारण वह अधीर हो गई। उसका शरीर पुलकित हो उठा, मुख से वचन कहने में नहीं आते थे। वह अत्यन्त बड़भागिनी अहल्या प्रभु के चरणों से लिपट गई और उसके दोनों नेत्रों से जल (प्रेम और आनंद के आँसुओं) की धारा बहने लगी ॥
english_translation: Touching Ram's holy feet, Ahalya rose from her long penance. Seeing Raghunath, the giver of joy to all beings, she stood before him with folded hands. Overcome by love, her body thrilled, words failed her, and she clung to his feet as tears flowed from both eyes.
essence: Ram's touch restores what suffering had frozen.
simple_meaning: Ahalya is restored by Ram's touch. Overwhelmed with love, she stands before him, cannot speak, and weeps at his feet.
insight: It shifts attention from the miracle itself to the surrender and gratitude it awakens.
modern_relevance: After months of feeling numb, you finally meet the person who helped you heal. You cannot explain it cleanly. You just stand there, overwhelmed and grateful.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धीरजु मन कीन्हा प्रभु कहुँ चीन्हा रघुपति कृपाँ भगति पाई। अति निर्मल बानी अस्तुति ठानी ग्यानगम्य जय रघुराई॥ मैं नारि अपावन प्रभु जग पावन रावन रिपु जन सुखदाई। राजीव बिलोचन भव भय मोचन पाहि पाहि सरनहिं आई ॥
translation: फिर उसने मन में धीरज धरकर प्रभु को पहचाना और श्री रघुनाथजी की कृपा से भक्ति प्राप्त की। तब अत्यन्त निर्मल वाणी से उसने (इस प्रकार) स्तुति प्रारंभ की- हे ज्ञान से जानने योग्य श्री रघुनाथजी! आपकी जय हो! मैं (सहज ही) अपवित्र स्त्री हूँ, और हे प्रभो! आप जगत को पवित्र करने वाले, भक्तों को सुख देने वाले और रावण के शत्रु हैं। हे कमलनयन! हे संसार (जन्म-मृत्यु) के भय से छुड़ाने वाले! मैं आपकी शरण आई हूँ, (मेरी) रक्षा कीजिए, रक्षा कीजिए ॥
english_translation: She steadied her mind, recognized the Lord, and by Raghu's grace received devotion. Then, in utterly pure words, she began to praise: "Victory to you, Raghu's lord, known only through wisdom! I am an impure woman, and you are the purifier of the world, the delight of your devotees, the foe of Ravana. Lotus-eyed one, remover of the fear of worldly existence, I have come to your refuge. Protect me, protect me."
essence: Recognition becomes devotion, and devotion becomes shelter.
simple_meaning: Ahalya regains composure, recognizes Ram, and praises him with pure devotion. She admits her own impurity and asks the lotus-eyed Lord to protect her from fear.
insight: It turns self-condemnation into refuge-seeking, showing that humility can become prayer.
modern_relevance: After a mistake you thought would define you, you finally meet someone who sees past it. Your voice shakes at first, then steadies. What comes out is not explanation, but gratitude and a plea for mercy.
speaker: Ahalya

verse_text: मुनि श्राप जो दीन्हा अति भल कीन्हा परम अनुग्रह मैं माना। देखेउँ भरि लोचन हरि भव मोचन इहइ लाभ संकर जाना॥ बिनती प्रभु मोरी मैं मति भोरी नाथ न मागउँ बर आना। पद कमल परागा रस अनुरागा मम मन मधुप करै पाना ॥
translation: मुनि ने जो मुझे शाप दिया, सो बहुत ही अच्छा किया। मैं उसे अत्यन्त अनुग्रह (करके) मानती हूँ कि जिसके कारण मैंने संसार से छुड़ाने वाले श्री हरि (आप) को नेत्र भरकर देखा। इसी (आपके दर्शन) को शंकरजी सबसे बड़ा लाभ समझते हैं। हे प्रभो! मैं बुद्धि की बड़ी भोली हूँ, मेरी एक विनती है। हे नाथ ! मैं और कोई वर नहीं माँगती, केवल यही चाहती हूँ कि मेरा मन रूपी भौंरा आपके चरण-कमल की रज के प्रेमरूपी रस का सदा पान करता रहे ॥
english_translation: The sage's curse did me great good; I count it as supreme grace, for it let me behold Hari, the liberator from worldly bondage, with my own eyes. Even Shankar knows that this is the highest gain. Lord, I am foolish in mind and ask for no other boon: let my bee-like mind drink forever the love-rasa of the dust of your lotus feet.
essence: Even suffering can become grace when it leads to Ram.
simple_meaning: Ahalya says the curse was a blessing because it gave her Ram's darshan. She asks for nothing else except a mind forever devoted to his feet.
insight: It shifts the mind from resenting hardship to seeing how hardship can deepen longing and surrender.
modern_relevance: A setback that once felt humiliating can later reveal the one meeting that changed everything. You look back and realize the detour was the doorway.
speaker: Ahalya

verse_text: जेहिं पद सुरसरिता परम पुनीता प्रगट भई सिव सीस धरी। सोई पद पंकज जेहि पूजत अज मम सिर धरेउ कृपाल हरी॥ एहि भाँति सिधारी गौतम नारी बार बार हरि चरन परी। जो अति मन भावा सो बरु पावा गै पति लोक अनंद भरी ॥
translation: जिन चरणों से परमपवित्र देवनदी गंगाजी प्रकट हुईं, जिन्हें शिवजी ने सिर पर धारण किया और जिन चरणकमलों को ब्रह्माजी पूजते हैं, कृपालु हरि (आप) ने उन्हीं को मेरे सिर पर रखा। इस प्रकार (स्तुति करती हुई) बार-बार भगवान के चरणों में गिरकर, जो मन को बहुत ही अच्छा लगा, उस वर को पाकर गौतम की स्त्री अहल्या आनंद में भरी हुई पतिलोक को चली गई ॥
english_translation: The feet from which the sacred Ganga emerged, which Shiva bears on his head, and which Brahma worships, those same lotus feet compassionate Hari placed on my head. In this way, Gautama's wife Ahalya, again and again falling at Hari's feet, received the boon that pleased her mind and went, filled with joy, to her husband's realm.
essence: The feet worshipped by the highest beings redeem the one who bows.
simple_meaning: Ram places his sacred feet on Ahalya's head, and the same feet are honored by Shiva and Brahma. Ahalya keeps bowing again and again, receives the blessing she longs for, and leaves in joy.
insight: It shifts the reader from self-justification to reverent surrender, showing that grace meets the one who yields.
modern_relevance: You finally apologize after carrying guilt for years. The other person doesn't need a perfect speech — they need sincerity, humility, and the courage to bow without defending yourself.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस प्रभु दीनबंधु हरि कारन रहित दयाल। तुलसिदास सठ तेहि भजु छाड़ि कपट जंजाल ॥
translation: प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ऐसे दीनबंधु और बिना ही कारण दया करने वाले हैं। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं, हे शठ (मन)! तू कपट-जंजाल छोड़कर उन्हीं का भजन कर ॥
english_translation: Ram is the friend of the humble and merciful without cause. Tulsidas says: O foolish mind, abandon deceit and worship him.
essence: Ram meets humility with mercy, not with conditions.
simple_meaning: Ram is merciful to the humble without needing a reason. Tulsidas tells the mind to stop pretending and turn toward him sincerely.
insight: It shifts devotion from appearance to sincerity, and from self-protection to direct turning toward Ram.
modern_relevance: You catch yourself performing sincerity in a prayer room, a meeting, or even a private apology. The verse cuts through the performance and asks for one clean thing: stop pretending and come honestly.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: चले राम लछिमन मुनि संगा। गए जहाँ जग पावनि गंगा॥ गाधिसूनु सब कथा सुनाई। जेहि प्रकार सुरसरि महि आई ॥
translation: श्री रामजी और लक्ष्मणजी मुनि के साथ चले। वे वहाँ गए, जहाँ जगत को पवित्र करने वाली गंगाजी थीं। महाराज गाधि के पुत्र विश्वामित्रजी ने वह सब कथा कह सुनाई जिस प्रकार देवनदी गंगाजी पृथ्वी पर आई थीं ॥
english_translation: Ram and Lakshman walked with the sage to the Ganga, the purifier of the world. Gadhi's son then told the whole story of how the river Ganga came to earth.
essence: A journey becomes sacred when the teacher begins the story.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman go with Vishwamitra to the Ganga, and Vishwamitra explains how the river came down to earth.
insight: It frames movement and place as part of spiritual instruction, not just travel.
modern_relevance: You are walking somewhere ordinary with someone who knows the whole backstory. A simple stop becomes a lesson, and the conversation changes the mood of the entire day.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब प्रभु रिषिन्ह समेत नहाए। बिबिध दान महिदेवन्हि पाए॥ हरषि चले मुनि बृंद सहाया। बेगि बिदेह नगर निअराया ॥
translation: तब प्रभु ने ऋषियों सहित (गंगाजी में) स्नान किया। ब्राह्मणों ने भाँति-भाँति के दान पाए। फिर मुनिवृन्द के साथ वे प्रसन्न होकर चले और शीघ्र ही जनकपुर के निकट पहुँच गए ॥
english_translation: Then the Lord bathed with the sages, and the holy men received many gifts. Joyfully, He went on with the band of ascetics and quickly reached near the city of Videha.
essence: Sacred action does not stop the journey; it makes the next step joyful.
simple_meaning: Ram bathes with the sages, gives gifts, and then travels on cheerfully toward Janakpur.
insight: It keeps the focus on graceful transition: receive, give, and move on without delay.
modern_relevance: You finish a meaningful ritual, thank the people who helped, and keep moving without fuss. The day stays clean because gratitude and progress travel together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुर रम्यता राम जब देखी। हरषे अनुज समेत बिसेषी॥ बापीं कूप सरित सर नाना। सलिल सुधासम मनि सोपाना ॥
translation: श्री रामजी ने जब जनकपुर की शोभा देखी, तब वे छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण सहित अत्यन्त हर्षित हुए। वहाँ अनेकों बावलियाँ, कुएँ, नदी और तालाब हैं, जिनमें अमृत के समान जल है और मणियों की सीढ़ियाँ (बनी हुई) हैं ॥
english_translation: When Ram saw the beauty of Janakpur, he and Lakshman were greatly delighted. There were many wells, ponds, rivers, and lakes, with water sweet as nectar and stairways made of gems.
essence: Wonder begins when the heart actually sees beauty.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman admire the beauty of Janakpur, with its many wells, rivers, ponds, and gem-studded steps filled with sweet water.
insight: It slows the reader into attention, teaching that reverence begins by truly seeing what is before you.
modern_relevance: You step into a city after a long train ride, exhausted and dusty, and suddenly the streets open into trees, water, and light. The body relaxes before the mind even knows why.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गुंजत मंजु मत्त रस भृंगा। कूजत कल बहुबरन बिहंगा॥ बरन बरन बिकसे बनजाता। त्रिबिध समीर सदा सुखदाता ॥
translation: मकरंद रस से मतवाले होकर भौंरे सुंदर गुंजार कर रहे हैं। रंग-बिरंगे (बहुत से) पक्षी मधुर शब्द कर रहे हैं। रंग-रंग के कमल खिले हैं। सदा (सब ऋतुओं में) सुख देने वाला शीतल, मंद, सुगंध पवन बह रहा है ॥
english_translation: Bees hum softly drunk on nectar. Birds sing in many sweet colors. Lotuses bloom in many hues. A cool, gentle breeze gives steady delight in every season.
essence: A blessed setting announces the sacred moment before it arrives.
simple_meaning: The garden around Janakpur is full of life, color, flowers, birds, and a pleasant breeze.
insight: It shifts attention from event to atmosphere, showing how place can carry meaning before action begins.
modern_relevance: You walk into a courtyard before a family wedding: flowers arranged, music drifting, everyone suddenly softer. The setting itself tells you something sacred is about to happen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुमन बाटिका बाग बन बिपुल बिहंग निवास। फूलत फलत सुपल्लवत सोहत पुर चहुँ पास॥212।
translation: पुष्प वाटिका (फुलवारी), बाग और वन, जिनमें बहुत से पक्षियों का निवास है, फूलते, फलते और सुंदर पत्तों से लदे हुए नगर के चारों ओर सुशोभित हैं ॥
english_translation: Flower gardens, groves, and forests with many birds dwell around the city, blooming and fruiting, beautiful with tender leaves on all four sides.
essence: The city’s beauty surrounds you before anyone even enters it.
simple_meaning: Gardens, groves, forests, and birds make the city beautiful on every side.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated details to the living harmony of a place.
modern_relevance: You step into a neighborhood at dusk and notice jasmine on a wall, trees overhanging the lane, birds settling in the branches. The place feels alive before anyone speaks.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बनइ न बरनत नगर निकाई। जहाँ जाइ मन तहँइँ लोभाई॥ चारु बजारु बिचित्र अँबारी। मनिमय बिधि जनु स्वकर सँवारी ॥
translation: नगर की सुंदरता का वर्णन करते नहीं बनता। मन जहाँ जाता है, वहीं लुभा जाता (रम जाता) है। सुंदर बाजार है, मणियों से बने हुए विचित्र छज्जे हैं, मानो ब्रह्मा ने उन्हें अपने हाथों से बनाया है ॥
english_translation: The city's beauty cannot be described. Wherever the mind goes, it is drawn in. Beautiful markets and wondrous balconies stand there, as if the creator shaped them by hand.
essence: Ayodhya is so beautiful that the mind cannot keep its distance.
simple_meaning: The city is so beautiful that words fail to capture it. Every part of it attracts the mind, from the markets to the jeweled balconies.
insight: It shifts attention from analysis to wonder, letting the mind receive beauty without needing to control it.
modern_relevance: You walk into a festival street at dusk, with lights strung above stalls and music drifting from every corner. For a moment, you stop scrolling, stop planning, and simply look.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धनिक बनिक बर धनद समाना। बैठे सकल बस्तु लै नाना। चौहट सुंदर गलीं सुहाई। संतत रहहिं सुगंध सिंचाई ॥
translation: कुबेर के समान श्रेष्ठ धनी व्यापारी सब प्रकार की अनेक वस्तुएँ लेकर (दुकानों में) बैठे हैं। सुंदर चौराहे और सुहावनी गलियाँ सदा सुगंध से सिंची रहती हैं ॥
english_translation: Wealthy merchants, like Kubera, sat with many kinds of goods. Beautiful crossroads and pleasant lanes were always sprinkled with fragrance.
essence: A blessed city makes abundance visible in every street.
simple_meaning: Wealthy merchants fill the city with many goods, while its crossroads and lanes stay fragrant and beautiful.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated riches to a whole culture of beauty, order, and plenty.
modern_relevance: You walk into a market where every stall is full, the alleys are clean, and the air smells of flowers and spice. The place itself feels cared for.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंगलमय मंदिर सब केरें। चित्रित जनु रतिनाथ चितेरें॥ पुर नर नारि सुभग सुचि संता। धरमसील ग्यानी गुनवंता ॥
translation: सबके घर मंगलमय हैं और उन पर चित्र कढ़े हुए हैं, जिन्हें मानो कामदेव रूपी चित्रकार ने अंकित किया है। नगर के (सभी) स्त्री-पुरुष सुंदर, पवित्र, साधु स्वभाव वाले, धर्मात्मा, ज्ञानी और गुणवान हैं ॥
english_translation: All the houses are filled with auspicious beauty, as if painted by Cupid himself. The men and women of the city are handsome, pure, gentle, righteous, wise, and virtuous.
essence: A truly beautiful city is made by both its homes and its people.
simple_meaning: The city is so beautiful that every house seems blessed and artist-made. Its people are also pure, righteous, wise, and full of good qualities.
insight: It trains the eye to notice that true grandeur includes moral beauty, not just decoration.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home where everything is clean, calm, and thoughtfully placed, and then the people greet you with the same warmth. The whole place feels blessed because character matches beauty.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अति अनूप जहँ जनक निवासू। बिथकहिं बिबुध बिलोकि बिलासू॥ होत चकित चित कोट बिलोकी। सकल भुवन सोभा जनु रोकी ॥
translation: जहाँ जनकजी का अत्यन्त अनुपम (सुंदर) निवास स्थान (महल) है, वहाँ के विलास (ऐश्वर्य) को देखकर देवता भी थकित (स्तम्भित) हो जाते हैं (मनुष्यों की तो बात ही क्या!)। कोट (राजमहल के परकोटे) को देखकर चित्त चकित हो जाता है, (ऐसा मालूम होता है) मानो उसने समस्त लोकों की शोभा को रोक (घेर) रखा है ॥
english_translation: Janak's residence is uniquely beautiful. Even the radiant beings are stunned by its splendor. Seeing the fort walls, the mind is amazed, as if all the world's beauty were gathered there.
essence: Beauty here is so complete it seems to contain the whole world.
simple_meaning: Janak's palace is so beautiful that even the radiant beings are amazed by it. Its walls seem to hold all beauty inside them.
insight: It slows the reader into wonder before the meeting of Ram and Sita.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home so carefully kept that conversation stops for a second. The light, the order, the elegance — everything feels gathered into one place.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धवल धाम मनि पुरट पट सुघटित नाना भाँति। सिय निवास सुंदर सदन सोभा किमि कहि जाति ॥
translation: उज्ज्वल महलों में अनेक प्रकार के सुंदर रीति से बने हुए मणि जटित सोने की जरी के परदे लगे हैं। सीताजी के रहने के सुंदर महल की शोभा का वर्णन किया ही कैसे जा सकता है ॥
english_translation: The bright palace has many kinds of finely fitted curtains of gems and gold. How can the beauty of Sita’s lovely dwelling even be described?
essence: Beauty beyond measure leaves language behind.
simple_meaning: Sita’s palace is so beautiful and richly decorated that words cannot fully describe it.
insight: It shifts attention from naming beauty to receiving it fully without trying to contain it in words.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room prepared with such care that you stop speaking for a moment. The attention in the space says more than any explanation could.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुभग द्वार सब कुलिस कपाटा। भूप भीर नट मागध भाटा॥ बनी बिसाल बाजि गज साला। हय गय रख संकुल सब काला ॥
translation: राजमहल के सब दरवाजे (फाटक) सुंदर हैं, जिनमें वज्र के (मजबूत अथवा हीरों के चमकते हुए) किवाड़ लगे हैं। वहाँ (मातहत) राजाओं, नटों, मागधों और भाटों की भीड़ लगी रहती है। घोड़ों और हाथियों के लिए बहुत बड़ी-बड़ी घुड़सालें और गजशालाएँ (फीलखाने) बनी हुई हैं, जो सब समय घोड़े, हाथी और रथों से भरी रहती हैं ॥
english_translation: All the gates are beautiful, with iron-clad doors. Kings, dancers, heralds, and bards crowd the court. Great stables and elephant houses stand ready, always packed with horses and elephants.
essence: Grandeur is revealed by the order it can sustain.
simple_meaning: Janak's palace is described as richly built, with strong doors, many visitors, and huge stables full of horses and elephants.
insight: It shifts attention from decorative beauty to the social and material order that supports it.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding venue where security, guests, staff, and vehicles all move at once. The building matters, but the real impression is the scale of life it can hold.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सूर सचिव सेनप बहुतेरे। नृपगृह सरिस सदन सब केरे॥ पुर बाहेर सर सरित समीपा। उतरे जहँ तहँ बिपुल महीपा ॥
translation: बहुत से शूरवीर, मंत्री और सेनापति हैं। उन सबके घर भी राजमहल सरीखे ही हैं। नगर के बाहर तालाब और नदी के निकट जहाँ-तहाँ बहुत से राजा लोग उतरे हुए (डेरा डाले हुए) हैं ॥
english_translation: There are many brave warriors, ministers, and commanders. Their homes are like royal palaces. Outside the city, near ponds and rivers, many kings have camped here and there.
essence: Power surrounds the moment, but the real turning point has not arrived.
simple_meaning: The city is full of powerful people and their grand homes. Many kings have set up camp around it near water.
insight: It trains attention to notice scene-setting without mistaking it for the message.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding venue and see VIP cars, security, and grand decorations everywhere. The room is impressive, but it is still only the backdrop before the real moment begins.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि अनूप एक अँवराई। सब सुपास सब भाँति सुहाई। कौसिक कहेउ मोर मनु माना। इहाँ रहिअ रघुबीर सुजाना ॥
translation: (वहीं) आमों का एक अनुपम बाग देखकर, जहाँ सब प्रकार के सुभीते थे और जो सब तरह से सुहावना था, विश्वामित्रजी ने कहा- हे सुजान रघुवीर! मेरा मन कहता है कि यहीं रहा जाए ॥
english_translation: Seeing a unique mango grove there, pleasant in every way and full of conveniences, Vishwamitra said, “O wise Raghubir, my mind says we should stay here.”
essence: A wise traveler knows when a place is fit to stop.
simple_meaning: Vishwamitra sees a beautiful mango grove and decides it is a good place to stop and stay.
insight: It shifts attention from pushing onward to recognizing the right place to pause and rest.
modern_relevance: After hours on the road, you finally spot a quiet grove, a water tap, and shade. The body knows before the mind does: this is where you stop.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भलेहिं नाथ कहि कृपानिकेता। उतरे तहँ मुनि बृंद समेता॥ बिस्वामित्र महामुनि आए। समाचार मिथिलापति पाए ॥
translation: कृपा के धाम श्री रामचन्द्रजी 'बहुत अच्छा स्वामिन् !' कहकर वहीं मुनियों के समूह के साथ ठहर गए। मिथिलापति जनकजी ने जब यह समाचार पाया कि महामुनि विश्वामित्र आए हैं, ॥
english_translation: Saying, “Very well, Lord,” the shelter of grace settled there with the sages. When the great sage Vishvamitra arrived, King Janaka learned the news.
essence: The meeting begins before the people meet.
simple_meaning: Ram agrees to stay there with the sages. Then Vishvamitra arrives, and King Janaka hears the news.
insight: It shifts attention from action to arrival: the verse prepares the meeting by showing both parties in motion.
modern_relevance: A host points you to a quiet room, you settle in, and then the message comes that the person you were waiting for has arrived. The whole atmosphere changes in an instant.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: संग सचिव सुचि भूरि भट भूसुर बर गुर ग्याति। चले मिलन मुनिनायकहि मुदित राउ एहि भाँति ॥
translation: तब उन्होंने पवित्र हृदय के (ईमानदार, स्वामिभक्त) मंत्री बहुत से योद्धा, श्रेष्ठ ब्राह्मण, गुरु (शतानंदजी) और अपनी जाति के श्रेष्ठ लोगों को साथ लिया और इस प्रकार प्रसन्नता के साथ राजा मुनियों के स्वामी विश्वामित्रजी से मिलने चले ॥
english_translation: Then the king, with pure ministers, many warriors, excellent brahmins, the teacher, and noble kinsmen, went joyfully to meet the sage chief.
essence: Joyful respect makes room for a worthy arrival.
simple_meaning: King Janak goes out joyfully with his trusted court and respected elders to greet Vishwamitra.
insight: It shifts attention to the dignity of welcome and the social harmony behind it.
modern_relevance: A senior leader walks into a room with the people who hold the organization together, not for show, but to greet an important guest properly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कीन्ह प्रनामु चरन धरि माथा। दीन्हि असीस मुदित मुनिनाथा॥ बिप्रबृंद सब सादर बंदे। जानि भाग्य बड़ राउ अनंदे ॥
translation: राजा ने मुनि के चरणों पर मस्तक रखकर प्रणाम किया। मुनियों के स्वामी विश्वामित्रजी ने प्रसन्न होकर आशीर्वाद दिया। फिर सारी ब्राह्मणमंडली को आदर सहित प्रणाम किया और अपना बड़ा भाग्य जानकर राजा आनंदित हुए ॥
english_translation: The king bowed with his head at the sage's feet. The lord of the sages, pleased, gave his blessing. He then honored all the learned Brahmins with respect, and the king rejoiced, knowing his great good fortune.
essence: True greatness begins with humility before wisdom.
simple_meaning: King Janaka bows to Vishwamitra, receives his blessing, honors the Brahmins, and feels joy at the good fortune of this visit.
insight: It shows how humility and honor create a dignified meeting before any discussion begins.
modern_relevance: You enter a room where everyone is waiting for your answer, and you choose respect first. That small bow changes the whole atmosphere before a single word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कुसल प्रस्न कहि बारहिं बारा। बिस्वामित्र नृपहि बैठारा॥ तेहि अवसर आए दोउ भाई। गए रहे देखन फुलवाई ॥
translation: बार-बार कुशल प्रश्न करके विश्वामित्रजी ने राजा को बैठाया। उसी समय दोनों भाई आ पहुँचे, जो फुलवाड़ी देखने गए थे ॥
english_translation: विश्वामित्र repeatedly asked after the king's welfare and seated him. At that moment the two brothers arrived; they had gone to see the flower garden.
essence: A calm welcome makes room for the arrival that matters.
simple_meaning: Vishwamitra warmly seated King Janak and kept asking after his well-being. At that moment Rama and Lakshman arrived from the flower garden.
insight: It sets the scene for a decisive meeting by showing how ordinary courtesy can frame a moment of destiny.
modern_relevance: You are deep in small talk at a family gathering when the one person everyone has been waiting for walks in. The room shifts before anyone says a word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: स्याम गौर मृदु बयस किसोरा। लोचन सुखद बिस्व चित चोरा॥ उठे सकल जब रघुपति आए। बिस्वामित्र निकट बैठाए ॥
translation: सुकुमार किशोर अवस्था वाले श्याम और गौर वर्ण के दोनों कुमार नेत्रों को सुख देने वाले और सारे विश्व के चित्त को चुराने वाले हैं। जब रघुनाथजी आए तब सभी (उनके रूप एवं तेज से प्रभावित होकर) उठकर खड़े हो गए। विश्वामित्रजी ने उनको अपने पास बैठा लिया ॥
english_translation: The dark and fair youths were tender in age, pleasing to the eyes, and stealing the hearts of the world. When Raghunath arrived, everyone stood up, and Vishwamitra seated them near himself.
essence: Their presence alone makes the whole assembly rise.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman arrive as beautiful young boys. Their presence delights everyone, and Vishvamitra makes them sit beside him.
insight: It shows how Ram’s presence naturally draws respect and tenderness without force.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the conversation stops for a second. Not because you demanded attention, but because your presence carried something unmistakable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भए सब सुखी देखि दोउ भ्राता। बारि बिलोचन पुलकित गाता॥ मूरति मधुर मनोहर देखी भयउ बिदेहु बिदेहु बिसेषी ॥
translation: दोनों भाइयों को देखकर सभी सुखी हुए। सबके नेत्रों में जल भर आया (आनंद और प्रेम के आँसू उमड़ पड़े) और शरीर रोमांचित हो उठे। रामजी की मधुर मनोहर मूर्ति को देखकर विदेह (जनक) विशेष रूप से विदेह (देह की सुध-बुध से रहित) हो गए ॥
english_translation: Seeing the two brothers, everyone became happy. Their eyes filled with tears and their bodies thrilled with joy. Seeing Ram's sweet, beautiful form, Janak became especially lost beyond bodily awareness.
essence: Ram's presence turns sight into joy and self-forgetting.
simple_meaning: Everyone feels joy on seeing Ram and Lakshman. Janak is especially overwhelmed by Ram's beautiful form and forgets his body.
insight: It shifts attention from explanation to direct experience: the sight of the beloved can transform the whole body at once.
modern_relevance: You catch sight of someone you have waited weeks to meet, and your chest loosens before you can speak. Some presences arrive before language does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रेम मगन मनु जानि नृपु करि बिबेकु धरि धीर। बोलेउ मुनि पद नाइ सिरु गदगद गिरा गभीर ॥
translation: मन को प्रेम में मग्न जान राजा जनक ने विवेक का आश्रय लेकर धीरज धारण किया और मुनि के चरणों में सिर नवाकर गद् गद् (प्रेमभरी) गंभीर वाणी से कहा- ॥
english_translation: Knowing his mind was overwhelmed by love, the king gathered himself with discernment and calm. Bowing his head at the sage's feet, he spoke in a choked, deep voice.
essence: Love can overwhelm the heart without overthrowing composure.
simple_meaning: Janak is overwhelmed by love, but he steadies himself, bows to the sage, and speaks calmly through tears.
insight: It teaches you to let feeling be real without letting it seize control of your speech or conduct.
modern_relevance: You see someone you love walk into the room and your chest tightens. You still lower your voice, breathe, and speak with care instead of spilling everything at once.
speaker: Janak

verse_text: कहहु नाथ सुंदर दोउ बालक। मुनिकुल तिलक कि नृपकुल पालक॥ ब्रह्म जो निगम नेति कहि गावा। उभय बेष धरि की सोइ आवा ॥
translation: हे नाथ! कहिए, ये दोनों सुंदर बालक मुनिकुल के आभूषण हैं या किसी राजवंश के पालक? अथवा जिसका वेदों ने 'नेति' कहकर गान किया है कहीं वह ब्रह्म तो युगल रूप धरकर नहीं आया है? ॥
english_translation: O Lord, tell me: are these two beautiful boys ornaments of the sage's line, or protectors of the king's line? Or has the same supreme reality, praised in the Vedas as beyond all description, come here wearing two forms?
essence: Beauty can reveal the supreme reality before words can explain it.
simple_meaning: Janaka is overwhelmed by Rama and Lakshmana's beauty and wonders who they really are. He suspects they may be the supreme reality itself appearing in human form.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance to sacred presence, teaching the mind to recognize greatness before analysis.
modern_relevance: You meet someone and their calm, dignity, and grace stop your mind cold. Before you can categorize them, something in you recognizes depth and bows.
speaker: Janaka

verse_text: सहज बिरागरूप मनु मोरा। थकित होत जिमि चंद चकोरा॥ ताते प्रभु पूछउँ सतिभाऊ। कहहु नाथ जनि करहु दुराऊ ॥
translation: मेरा मन जो स्वभाव से ही वैराग्य रूप (बना हुआ) है, (इन्हें देखकर) इस तरह मुग्ध हो रहा है, जैसे चन्द्रमा को देखकर चकोर। हे प्रभो! इसलिए मैं आपसे सत्य (निश्छल) भाव से पूछता हूँ। हे नाथ! बताइए, छिपाव न कीजिए ॥
english_translation: My mind is naturally turned toward detachment, yet it becomes captivated like a chakora before the moon. Therefore, Lord, I ask you with complete sincerity. O Master, do not hide the truth.
essence: Detachment can still bow before what is truly radiant.
simple_meaning: Janaka says his mind is usually detached, yet the sight of the two boys has overwhelmed him. He asks the teacher to answer honestly and without hiding anything.
insight: It shifts the mind from polished certainty to sincere inquiry when experience breaks the old frame.
modern_relevance: You thought you had a situation figured out, then one unexpected encounter unsettles everything. Instead of pretending certainty, you ask the hard question directly.
speaker: Janaka

verse_text: इन्हहि बिलोकत अति अनुरागा। बरबस ब्रह्मसुखहि मन त्यागा॥ कह मुनि बिहसि कहेहु नृप नीका। बचन तुम्हार न होइ अलीका ॥
translation: इनको देखते ही अत्यन्त प्रेम के वश होकर मेरे मन ने जबर्दस्ती ब्रह्मसुख को त्याग दिया है। मुनि ने हँसकर कहा- हे राजन् ! आपने ठीक (यथार्थ ही) कहा। आपका वचन मिथ्या नहीं हो सकता ॥
english_translation: Looking at them, my heart was overwhelmed with love and forcibly gave up the bliss of Brahman. The sage laughed and said, "You speak rightly, O king. Your words cannot be false."
essence: Love for Ram can outweigh even the bliss of Brahman.
simple_meaning: Seeing the two boys, the sage becomes so moved by love that even the highest spiritual bliss feels secondary. He confirms that the king has spoken truly.
insight: It shifts devotion from an idea into an experience that can outshine even spiritual achievement.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence makes the room feel different, and all your polished detachment suddenly looks thin. Some recognitions are stronger than theory.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: ए प्रिय सबहि जहाँ लगि प्रानी। मन मुसुकाहिं रामु सुनि बानी॥ रघुकुल मनि दसरथ के जाए। मम हित लागि नरेस पठाए ॥
translation: जगत में जहाँ तक (जितने भी) प्राणी हैं, ये सभी को प्रिय हैं। मुनि की (रहस्य भरी) वाणी सुनकर श्री रामजी मन ही मन मुस्कुराते हैं (हँसकर मानो संकेत करते हैं कि रहस्य खोलिए नहीं)। (तब मुनि ने कहा-) ये रघुकुल मणि महाराज दशरथ के पुत्र हैं। मेरे हित के लिए राजा ने इन्हें मेरे साथ भेजा है ॥
english_translation: All beings in the world are dear to him. Hearing the sage's veiled words, Ram smiles inwardly. Then the sage says, "He is the jewel of Raghu's line, the son of King Dasharath. The king has sent him with me for my welfare."
essence: Recognition turns an ordinary meeting into a sacred unveiling.
simple_meaning: Ram is dear to every living being. The sage then identifies him as Dasharath's son, sent for the sage's welfare.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance to recognition, showing how a name can uncover hidden stature.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a gathering who seems ordinary, then a shared friend quietly reveals who they are. The room changes, but the person has not.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामु लखनु दोउ बंधुबर रूप सील बल धाम। मख राखेउ सबु साखि जगु जिते असुर संग्राम ॥
translation: ये राम और लक्ष्मण दोनों श्रेष्ठ भाई रूप, शील और बल के धाम हैं। सारा जगत (इस बात का) साक्षी है कि इन्होंने युद्ध में असुरों को जीतकर मेरे यज्ञ की रक्षा की है ॥
english_translation: Ram and Lakshman, the two noble brothers, are abodes of beauty, character, and strength. The whole world is witness that they protected my sacrifice and defeated the demons in battle.
essence: Their beauty matters because it is backed by courage and protection.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are praised as noble, beautiful, strong brothers who protected the sage's sacrifice and defeated hostile forces.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance alone to the proof of character found in action.
modern_relevance: A parent watches two siblings quietly step in when a family crisis hits. No speech is needed — everyone sees who protected the home when it mattered.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: मुनि तव चरन देखि कह राऊ। कहि न सकउँ निज पुन्य प्रभाऊ॥ सुंदर स्याम गौर दोउ भ्राता। आनँदहू के आनँद दाता ॥
translation: राजा ने कहा- हे मुनि! आपके चरणों के दर्शन कर मैं अपना पुण्य प्रभाव कह नहीं सकता। ये सुंदर श्याम और गौर वर्ण के दोनों भाई आनंद को भी आनंद देने वाले हैं।
english_translation: The king said, “O sage, seeing your feet, I cannot describe the power of my own merit. These beautiful dark and fair brothers are givers of joy even to joy itself.”
essence: Their presence makes joy feel larger than joy.
simple_meaning: Janak bows before the sage and praises Ram and Lakshman as brothers whose presence deepens joy itself.
insight: It shifts attention from self-importance to reverent recognition of true greatness.
modern_relevance: You meet someone so steady and gracious that your own pride drops away. Around them, even a happy room feels more alive.
speaker: Janak

verse_text: इन्ह कै प्रीति परसपर पावनि। कहि न जाइ मन भाव सुहावनि॥ सुनहु नाथ कह मुदित बिदेहू। ब्रह्म जीव इव सहज सनेहू ॥
translation: इनकी आपस की प्रीति बड़ी पवित्र और सुहावनी है, वह मन को बहुत भाती है, पर (वाणी से) कही नहीं जा सकती। विदेह (जनकजी) आनंदित होकर कहते हैं- हे नाथ! सुनिए, ब्रह्म और जीव की तरह इनमें स्वाभाविक प्रेम है ॥
english_translation: Their mutual love is pure and delightful. It cannot be spoken; it pleases the mind deeply. Listen, lord, says Janaka joyfully: their natural affection is like Brahman and the individual being.
essence: True affection needs no explanation; it reveals a deeper unity already there.
simple_meaning: Janaka says Ram and Lakshman share a love that is pure, beautiful, and beyond words. He compares their natural bond to the relation between the supreme reality and the individual being.
insight: It shifts attention from spoken sentiment to the quiet evidence of a bond that needs no performance.
modern_relevance: You watch two siblings protect each other at a family wedding, without a single dramatic speech. Everyone feels it. Some loyalties are so natural they make explanation unnecessary.
speaker: Janaka

verse_text: पुनि पुनि प्रभुहि चितव नरनाहू। पुलक गात उर अधिक उछाहू॥ मुनिहि प्रसंसि नाइ पद सीसू। चलेउ लवाइ नगर अवनीसू ॥
translation: राजा बार-बार प्रभु को देखते हैं (दृष्टि वहाँ से हटना ही नहीं चाहती)। (प्रेम से) शरीर पुलकित हो रहा है और हृदय में बड़ा उत्साह है। (फिर) मुनि की प्रशंसा करके और उनके चरणों में सिर नवाकर राजा उन्हें नगर में लिवा चले ॥
english_translation: The king kept looking at the Lord again and again. His body thrilled with joy, and his heart overflowed with eagerness. Then he praised the sage, bowed his head at the sage's feet, and led him toward the city.
essence: True admiration keeps returning to its source.
simple_meaning: The king cannot stop looking at Ram. Joy rises in his body and heart, and after honoring the sage, he leads him toward the city.
insight: It shifts attention from formal duty to heartfelt welcome and visible reverence.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence changes the room, and you keep glancing back even after the conversation ends. Respect turns into hospitality before you even plan it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुंदर सदनु सुखद सब काला। तहाँ बासु लै दीन्ह भुआला॥ करि पूजा सब बिधि सेवकाई। गयउ राउ गृह बिदा कराई ॥
translation: एक सुंदर महल जो सब समय (सभी ऋतुओं में) सुखदायक था, वहाँ राजा ने उन्हें ले जाकर ठहराया। तदनन्तर सब प्रकार से पूजा और सेवा करके राजा विदा माँगकर अपने घर गए ॥
english_translation: A beautiful hall, pleasant in every season, was arranged for them there. The king offered every kind of worship and service, then took leave and returned home.
essence: True honor serves completely and then withdraws gracefully.
simple_meaning: The king arranged comfortable lodging for Ram and Lakshman, honored them properly, and then left after asking permission.
insight: It models dignified hospitality: provide fully, honor properly, and do not cling to attention.
modern_relevance: A host sets out clean sheets, water, and food before guests arrive, then steps back without making a scene. Real respect knows when to serve and when to leave space.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रिषय संग रघुबंस मनि करि भोजनु बिश्रामु। बैठे प्रभु भ्राता सहित दिवसु रहा भरि जामु ॥
translation: रघुकुल के शिरोमणि प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ऋषियों के साथ भोजन और विश्राम करके भाई लक्ष्मण समेत बैठे। उस समय पहरभर दिन रह गया था ॥
english_translation: Rama, jewel of the Raghu line, ate and rested with the sages. He sat with Lakshmana, and then a quarter of the day remained.
essence: Peace can live inside the simplest shared meal.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshmana eat, rest, and sit with the sages. The day is already passing, so the scene pauses before the next event.
insight: It teaches you to notice the holiness of ordinary rest and companionship before the next demand arrives.
modern_relevance: After a long drive, you finally sit down at a friend's house, eat something simple, and let the noise of the day fall away. Not every sacred moment is dramatic.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लखन हृदयँ लालसा बिसेषी। जाइ जनकपुर आइअ देखी॥ प्रभु भय बहुरि मुनिहि सकुचाहीं। प्रगट न कहहिं मनहिं मुसुकाहीं ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी के हृदय में विशेष लालसा है कि जाकर जनकपुर देख आवें, परन्तु प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी का डर है और फिर मुनि से भी सकुचाते हैं, इसलिए प्रकट में कुछ नहीं कहते, मन ही मन मुस्कुरा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Lakshman has a strong desire in his heart to go see Janakpur, but he feels shy before Lord Ram and even before the sage, so he says nothing openly and smiles to himself.
essence: Desire can remain alive even when respect keeps it silent.
simple_meaning: Lakshman wants to see Janakpur, but he is too shy to ask openly. He keeps the wish in his heart and smiles quietly.
insight: It shows a feeling being contained by reverence, not erased by it.
modern_relevance: You want to ask for the extra day off, but your manager is already overloaded and you hold back. The wish is real; the restraint is real too.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम अनुज मन की गति जानी। भगत बछलता हियँ हुलसानी॥ परम बिनीत सकुचि मुसुकाई। बोले गुर अनुसासन पाई ॥
translation: (अन्तर्यामी) श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने छोटे भाई के मन की दशा जान ली, (तब) उनके हृदय में भक्तवत्सलता उमड़ आई। वे गुरु की आज्ञा पाकर बहुत ही विनय के साथ सकुचाते हुए मुस्कुराकर बोले ॥
english_translation: Ram knew his younger brother's wish. His heart overflowed with love for a devotee. With deep humility, he smiled shyly and spoke after receiving the teacher's permission.
essence: True love notices desire before it becomes speech.
simple_meaning: Ram understands Lakshman's unspoken wish and responds with affectionate humility. He smiles gently and speaks only after receiving his teacher's permission.
insight: It teaches you to notice unspoken needs and answer with humility instead of self-importance.
modern_relevance: A younger sibling keeps hinting they want something but won't ask directly. You notice, soften first, and respond without making them feel small.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ लखनु पुरु देखन चहहीं। प्रभु सकोच डर प्रगट न कहहीं॥ जौं राउर आयसु मैं पावौं। नगर देखाइ तुरत लै आवौं ॥
translation: हे नाथ! लक्ष्मण नगर देखना चाहते हैं, किन्तु प्रभु (आप) के डर और संकोच के कारण स्पष्ट नहीं कहते। यदि आपकी आज्ञा पाऊँ, तो मैं इनको नगर दिखलाकर तुरंत ही (वापस) ले आऊँ ॥
english_translation: Lord, Lakshman wants to see the city, but out of respect and fear of you, he does not say it openly. If I receive your order, I will show him the city and bring him back at once.
essence: True service notices the wish before it is spoken.
simple_meaning: Lakshman wants to see the city, but he is too respectful to ask directly. The speaker offers to take him there only if ordered to do so.
insight: It shows how service listens for unspoken needs and waits for permission before acting.
modern_relevance: You want to ask for something simple, but you hesitate because the room feels too formal. A respectful person notices the need and makes space for it without forcing the issue.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुनि मुनीसु कह बचन सप्रीती। कस न राम तुम्ह राखहु नीती॥ धरम सेतु पालक तुम्ह ताता। प्रेम बिबस सेवक सुखदाता ॥
translation: यह सुनकर मुनीश्वर विश्वामित्रजी ने प्रेम सहित वचन कहे- हे राम! तुम नीति की रक्षा कैसे न करोगे, हे तात! तुम धर्म की मर्यादा का पालन करने वाले और प्रेम के वशीभूत होकर सेवकों को सुख देने वाले हो ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, the sage Vishvamitra spoke with affection: “Why would you not uphold righteous conduct, Ram? You are the guardian of dharma, dear one, and you are bound by love to give joy to your servants.”
essence: True righteousness protects others and still remains tender.
simple_meaning: Vishvamitra praises Ram as someone who naturally protects righteousness and brings happiness to those who serve him.
insight: It shifts respect toward people whose kindness does not weaken their standards.
modern_relevance: A younger colleague quietly covers for everyone, refuses shortcuts, and still treats the team kindly. You notice that real strength is not coldness — it is the steadiness to do right while staying warm.
speaker: Vishvamitra

verse_text: जाइ देखि आवहु नगरु सुख निधान दोउ भाइ। करहु सुफल सब के नयन सुंदर बदन देखाइ ॥
translation: सुख के निधान दोनों भाई जाकर नगर देख आओ। अपने सुंदर मुख दिखलाकर सब (नगर निवासियों) के नेत्रों को सफल करो ॥
english_translation: Go and see the city, both brothers, treasure of joy. Show your beautiful faces and make everyone's eyes fruitful.
essence: Their beauty blesses every pair of eyes that sees them.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman should go into the city, let people see them, and feel their eyes fulfilled by the sight of their beauty.
insight: It shifts attention from performing to appearing fully, letting goodness be received rather than announced.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after months away, and the whole place turns to look. Sometimes the kindest thing you can do is simply arrive fully and let people feel your presence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि पद कमल बंदि दोउ भ्राता। चले लोक लोचन सुख दाता॥ बालक बृंद देखि अति सोभा। लगे संग लोचन मनु लोभा ॥
translation: सब लोकों के नेत्रों को सुख देने वाले दोनों भाई मुनि के चरणकमलों की वंदना करके चले। बालकों के झुंड इन (के सौंदर्य) की अत्यन्त शोभा देखकर साथ लग गए। उनके नेत्र और मन (इनकी माधुरी पर) लुभा गए ॥
english_translation: After bowing to the sage’s lotus feet, the two brothers set out. Seeing the beauty of the children, the boys gathered around, and eyes and minds were drawn to them.
essence: Beauty grounded in humility quietly gathers every eye.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman bow to the sage and walk on. Their beauty is so striking that children gather around them, unable to look away.
insight: It keeps attention on the brothers’ visible grace, not on any teaching. The verse functions as a bridge into the next scene.
modern_relevance: You walk into a crowded station, and the noise shifts for a second because someone calm and kind has entered. No speech, no performance — just a presence people trust.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पीत बसन परिकर कटि भाथा। चारु चाप सर सोहत हाथा॥ तन अनुहरत सुचंदन खोरी। स्यामल गौर मनोहर जोरी ॥
translation: (दोनों भाइयों के) पीले रंग के वस्त्र हैं, कमर के (पीले) दुपट्टों में तरकस बँधे हैं। हाथों में सुंदर धनुष-बाण सुशोभित हैं। (श्याम और गौर वर्ण के) शरीरों के अनुकूल (अर्थात् जिस पर जिस रंग का चंदन अधिक फबे उस पर उसी रंग के) सुंदर चंदन की खौर लगी है। साँवरे और गोरे (रंग) की मनोहर जोड़ी है ॥
english_translation: They wear yellow garments, with quivers tied at their waists. Beautiful bows and arrows shine in their hands. Their bodies are adorned with sandal paste suited to their complexions. Dark and fair, they form a lovely pair.
essence: Their beauty is inseparable from their readiness.
simple_meaning: The two brothers are dressed beautifully, armed with bows and arrows, and marked with sandal paste that suits their dark and fair complexions.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary appearance to embodied readiness — grace that is already armed for action.
modern_relevance: You see two siblings step out together before a ceremony, one in deep blue, one in light cream, both composed and ready. The room notices their presence before a word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: केहरि कंधर बाहु बिसाला। उर अति रुचिर नागमनि माला॥ सुभग सोन सरसीरुह लोचन। बदन मयंक तापत्रय मोचन ॥
translation: सिंह के समान (पुष्ट) गर्दन (गले का पिछला भाग) है, विशाल भुजाएँ हैं। (चौड़ी) छाती पर अत्यन्त सुंदर गजमुक्ता की माला है। सुंदर लाल कमल के समान नेत्र हैं। तीनों तापों से छुड़ाने वाला चन्द्रमा के समान मुख है ॥
english_translation: His neck is strong like a lion's, and his arms are broad. A splendid pearl necklace rests on his chest. His eyes are beautiful like red lotuses, and his face is like the moon that removes the threefold suffering.
essence: Ram's beauty is strength that soothes suffering.
simple_meaning: Ram's body is described as noble and radiant, with a strong neck, broad arms, lotus-like eyes, and a moonlike face that brings relief from suffering.
insight: It shifts attention from mere appearance to presence that heals and steadies others.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm presence changes the whole room before they even speak. Their steadiness feels like relief, not performance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कानन्हि कनक फूल छबि देहीं। चितवत चितहि चोरि जनु लेहीं॥ चितवनि चारु भृकुटि बर बाँकी। तिलक रेख सोभा जनु चाँकी ॥
translation: कानों में सोने के कर्णफूल (अत्यन्त) शोभा दे रहे हैं और देखते ही (देखने वाले के) चित्त को मानो चुरा लेते हैं। उनकी चितवन (दृष्टि) बड़ी मनोहर है और भौंहें तिरछी एवं सुंदर हैं। (माथे पर) तिलक की रेखाएँ ऐसी सुंदर हैं, मानो (मूर्तिमती) शोभा पर मुहर लगा दी गई है ॥
english_translation: Gold earrings brighten their beauty and seem to steal the viewer’s mind. Their gaze is lovely, their brows are gracefully curved, and the tilak on their foreheads seems to seal their beauty.
essence: Beauty can seize the mind before the mind knows what happened.
simple_meaning: The brothers are described as breathtakingly beautiful. Their ornaments, gaze, brows, and forehead mark all heighten their charm.
insight: It slows the mind down to notice how form, posture, and expression carry meaning before speech begins.
modern_relevance: You notice someone walk into a room and the whole atmosphere shifts before a word is spoken. The details are small, but the presence is unmistakable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रुचिर चौतनीं सुभग सिर मेचक कुंचित केस। नख सिख सुंदर बंधु दोउ सोभा सकल सुदेस ॥
translation: सिर पर सुंदर चौकोनी टोपियाँ (दिए) हैं, काले और घुँघराले बाल हैं। दोनों भाई नख से लेकर शिखा तक (एड़ी से चोटी तक) सुंदर हैं और सारी शोभा जहाँ जैसी चाहिए वैसी ही है ॥
english_translation: Both brothers are beautiful from head to toe, with dark curly hair and lovely square caps on their heads. Their beauty fits every place perfectly.
essence: Complete beauty needs no extra ornament.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are described as beautiful from head to toe. Their appearance is graceful, complete, and fitting in every way.
insight: It shifts attention from action to presence, showing how wholeness can command attention without effort.
modern_relevance: You notice someone walk into a room and the whole atmosphere changes before they speak. Their calm, complete presence makes everyone look up.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखन नगरु भूपसुत आए। समाचार पुरबासिन्ह पाए॥ धाए धाम काम सब त्यागी। मनहुँ रंक निधि लूटन लागी ॥
translation: जब पुरवासियों ने यह समाचार पाया कि दोनों राजकुमार नगर देखने के लिए आए हैं, तब वे सब घर-बार और सब काम-काज छोड़कर ऐसे दौड़े मानो दरिद्री (धन का) खजाना लूटने दौड़े हों ॥
