english_translation: When the townspeople heard that the two princes had come to see the city, they left home and work and rushed out like poor people running to seize a treasure.
essence: True beauty makes ordinary life stop and run toward it.
simple_meaning: The whole city drops its work and rushes out just to see the two princes. Their arrival creates a wave of joy and excitement.
insight: It shows how genuine radiance interrupts habit and draws people toward it before they even decide.
modern_relevance: A street vendor leaves his stall half-open because word spreads that someone extraordinary has arrived nearby. People stop ordinary life for a moment when presence feels rare and precious.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निरखि सहज सुंदर दोउ भाई। होहिं सुखी लोचन फल पाई॥ जुबतीं भवन झरोखन्हि लागीं। निरखहिं राम रूप अनुरागीं ॥
translation: स्वभाव ही से सुंदर दोनों भाइयों को देखकर वे लोग नेत्रों का फल पाकर सुखी हो रहे हैं। युवती स्त्रियाँ घर के झरोखों से लगी हुई प्रेम सहित श्री रामचन्द्रजी के रूप को देख रही हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing the two brothers, beautiful by nature, they became joyful as if their eyes had found their reward. Young women leaned from the windows of their houses, gazing lovingly at Ram's form.
essence: Ram's presence makes seeing itself feel fulfilled.
simple_meaning: People feel complete just by seeing Ram and Lakshman. Young women lean from their windows, lovingly watching Ram's beauty.
insight: It shifts attention from what is said to the effect a noble presence has on others.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone walking into a room and the whole atmosphere changes. No announcement, no performance — just a presence that makes people look up and feel glad to be there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहहिं परसपर बचन सप्रीती। सखि इन्ह कोटि काम छबि जीती॥ सुर नर असुर नाग मुनि माहीं। सोभा असि कहुँ सुनिअति नाहीं ॥
translation: वे आपस में बड़े प्रेम से बातें कर रही हैं- हे सखी! इन्होंने करोड़ों कामदेवों की छबि को जीत लिया है। देवता, मनुष्य, असुर, नाग और मुनियों में ऐसी शोभा तो कहीं सुनने में भी नहीं आती ॥
english_translation: They speak to one another with deep affection: “Sakhi, these two have conquered the beauty of millions of Cupids. Among gods, humans, demons, serpents, and sages, no such splendor has ever been heard of.”
essence: Their beauty silences comparison and turns strangers into witnesses.
simple_meaning: The women speak lovingly among themselves, saying that the two brothers are more beautiful than millions of love-gods and unlike anyone else in all worlds.
insight: It turns admiration into a collective act, showing how beauty creates instant reverence and shared speech.
modern_relevance: You catch sight of someone walking into a room and the whole atmosphere changes. People stop talking, lean closer, and share the same stunned thought before they even know why.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिष्नु चारि भुज बिधि मुख चारी। बिकट बेष मुख पंच पुरारी॥ अपर देउ अस कोउ ना आही। यह छबि सखी पटतरिअ जाही ॥
translation: भगवान विष्णु के चार भुजाएँ हैं, ब्रह्माजी के चार मुख हैं, शिवजी का विकट (भयानक) वेष है और उनके पाँच मुँह हैं। हे सखी! दूसरा देवता भी कोई ऐसा नहीं है, जिसके साथ इस छबि की उपमा दी जाए ॥
english_translation: Vishnu has four arms, Brahma has four faces, and Shiva has a fierce form with five mouths. O friend, no other deity exists whose beauty can be compared to this one.
essence: Their beauty outruns every comparison.
simple_meaning: The women say that even the great deities of the world cannot match Ram and Lakshman's beauty.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary description to reverent astonishment.
modern_relevance: You see someone enter a room and every other conversation quietly stops. People reach for comparisons, but nothing fits. The moment feels larger than language.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बय किसोर सुषमा सदन स्याम गौर सुख धाम। अंग अंग पर वारिअहिं कोटि कोटि सत काम ॥
translation: इनकी किशोर अवस्था है, ये सुंदरता के घर, साँवले और गोरे रंग के तथा सुख के धाम हैं। इनके अंग-अंग पर करोड़ों-अरबों कामदेवों को निछावर कर देना चाहिए ॥
english_translation: Their youth is a home of beauty, dark and fair, a dwelling of bliss. On every limb, millions and billions of Kamas should be offered up.
essence: Their beauty makes even desire look small.
simple_meaning: Ram and Sita are being praised as radiantly beautiful in their youth. Their beauty is so overwhelming that even countless Kamas seem small beside it.
insight: It shifts the mind from ordinary attraction to reverent wonder before beauty.
modern_relevance: You catch yourself staring at someone across a crowded room, then realize the feeling is not desire alone. It is awe — the mind quietly admitting it has met something greater than its usual standards.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहहु सखी अस को तनु धारी। जो न मोह यह रूप निहारी॥ कोउ सप्रेम बोली मृदु बानी। जो मैं सुना सो सुनहु सयानी ॥
translation: हे सखी! (भला) कहो तो ऐसा कौन शरीरधारी होगा, जो इस रूप को देखकर मोहित न हो जाए (अर्थात यह रूप जड़-चेतन सबको मोहित करने वाला है)। (तब) कोई दूसरी सखी प्रेम सहित कोमल वाणी से बोली- हे सयानी! मैंने जो सुना है उसे सुनो- ॥
english_translation: Tell me, dear friend, who could wear a body and not be charmed by this form? Then another friend spoke lovingly and softly: "Listen, wise one, to what I have heard."
essence: Ram's beauty first disarms the mind, then opens the door to devotion.
simple_meaning: The women are marveling at Ram and asking who could see such beauty without being moved. One of them then begins to answer gently.
insight: It prepares the reader for a revelation by showing how Ram's form naturally draws devotion.
modern_relevance: You catch sight of someone entering a room and the whole conversation changes. Before anyone names what happened, everyone already feels it: presence can silence the mind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ए दोऊ दसरथ के ढोटा। बाल मरालन्हि के कल जोटा॥ मुनि कौसिक मख के रखवारे। जिन्ह रन अजिर निसाचर मारे ॥
translation: ये दोनों (राजकुमार) महाराज दशरथजी के पुत्र हैं! बाल राजहंसों का सा सुंदर जोड़ा है। ये मुनि विश्वामित्र के यज्ञ की रक्षा करने वाले हैं, इन्होंने युद्ध के मैदान में राक्षसों को मारा है ॥
english_translation: These two are King Dasharath's sons, a beautiful pair like young swans. They protect Sage Vishwamitra's sacrifice and have killed demons on the battlefield.
essence: True beauty shows itself in protection and courage.
simple_meaning: The verse praises Ram and Lakshman as Dasharath's handsome sons. It also recalls how they protected Vishvamitra's sacrifice and defeated demons in battle.
insight: It frames identity through service and courage, not appearance alone.
modern_relevance: At a family gathering, someone introduces two siblings with pride: not just how they look, but what they have already done for others. The introduction itself carries their character.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: स्याम गात कल कंज बिलोचन। जो मारीच सुभुज मदु मोचन॥ कौसल्या सुत सो सुख खानी। नामु रामु धनु सायक पानी ॥
translation: जिनका श्याम शरीर और सुंदर कमल जैसे नेत्र हैं, जो मारीच और सुबाहु के मद को चूर करने वाले और सुख की खान हैं और जो हाथ में धनुष-बाण लिए हुए हैं, वे कौसल्याजी के पुत्र हैं, इनका नाम राम है ॥
english_translation: They have a dark complexion and lovely lotus-like eyes. They humbled Maricha and Subahu. They are a source of joy. The one with bow and arrows in hand is Kaushalya's son, Ram.
essence: Ram's beauty is inseparable from his strength.
simple_meaning: Ram is described as dark-complexioned, lotus-eyed, joyful to behold, and armed with bow and arrows. He is identified as Kaushalya's son.
insight: It shifts attention from mere appearance to the combination of grace, power, and proven courage.
modern_relevance: You spot someone in a crowded room and know, before words, that they carry calm strength. Their presence feels steady, not flashy — and everyone notices.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गौर किसोर बेषु बर काछें। कर सर चाप राम के पाछें॥ लछिमनु नामु राम लघु भ्राता। सुनु सखि तासु सुमित्रा माता ॥
translation: जिनका रंग गोरा और किशोर अवस्था है और जो सुंदर वेष बनाए और हाथ में धनुष-बाण लिए श्री रामजी के पीछे-पीछे चल रहे हैं, वे इनके छोटे भाई हैं, उनका नाम लक्ष्मण है। हे सखी! सुनो, उनकी माता सुमित्रा हैं ॥
english_translation: Fair and youthful in appearance, handsome in dress, with bow and arrows in hand, Lakshman walks behind Ram. Listen, friend: his name is Lakshman, and his mother is Sumitra.
essence: True support stays close and never competes for the front.
simple_meaning: Lakshman is introduced as Ram's younger brother, walking behind Ram with bow and arrows in hand.
insight: It trains attention toward faithful presence and self-effacing service.
modern_relevance: You notice the friend who never steps in front, only beside or behind, ready before anyone asks. That quiet loyalty changes the whole room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिप्रकाजु करि बंधु दोउ मग मुनिबधू उधारि। आए देखन चापमख सुनि हरषीं सब नारि ॥
translation: दोनों भाई ब्राह्मण विश्वामित्र का काम करके और रास्ते में मुनि गौतम की स्त्री अहल्या का उद्धार करके यहाँ धनुषयज्ञ देखने आए हैं। यह सुनकर सब स्त्रियाँ प्रसन्न हुईं ॥
english_translation: After serving the priest's purpose and redeeming Ahalya on the way, both brothers have come to see the bow sacrifice. Hearing this, all the women rejoiced.
essence: Good action announces itself before the person does.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have arrived after helping Vishwamitra and rescuing Ahalya. The women hear this and feel joy at the sight of them coming to the bow sacrifice.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance to reputation earned through action.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after helping someone quietly on the way there. Before you say a word, the atmosphere changes — people already feel your character.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि राम छबि कोउ एक कहई। जोगु जानकिहि यह बरु अहई॥ जौं सखि इन्हहि देख नरनाहू। पन परिहरि हठि करइ बिबाहू ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की छबि देखकर कोई एक (दूसरी सखी) कहने लगी- यह वर जानकी के योग्य है। हे सखी! यदि कहीं राजा इन्हें देख ले, तो प्रतिज्ञा छोड़कर हठपूर्वक इन्हीं से विवाह कर देगा ॥
english_translation: Seeing Rama's radiance, one lady said, “He is fit for Janaki. O friend, if the king sees him, he will abandon his vow and insist on this marriage.”
essence: True fit can make even a vow feel small.
simple_meaning: A woman sees Rama and says he is the right bridegroom for Janaki. She adds that even the king would forget his vow if he saw Rama.
insight: It shows how true suitability can feel self-evident, stronger than rules or formal plans.
modern_relevance: At a wedding venue, the room goes quiet when one person walks in and everyone feels the match before any words are spoken. Some recognitions are instant and undeniable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोउ कह ए भूपति पहिचाने। मुनि समेत सादर सनमाने॥ सखि परंतु पनु राउ न तजई। बिधि बस हठि अबिबेकहि भजई ॥
translation: किसी ने कहा- राजा ने इन्हें पहचान लिया है और मुनि के सहित इनका आदरपूर्वक सम्मान किया है, परंतु हे सखी! राजा अपना प्रण नहीं छोड़ता। वह होनहार के वशीभूत होकर हठपूर्वक अविवेक का ही आश्रय लिए हुए हैं (प्रण पर अड़े रहने की मूर्खता नहीं छोड़ता) ॥
english_translation: Someone said, "The king has recognized them and honored them respectfully along with the sage. Yet, O friend, the king will not let go of his vow. Driven by fate, he clings stubbornly to foolishness."
essence: Seeing clearly changes nothing if pride keeps the vow.
simple_meaning: The women see that the king understands who Rama is, yet he still refuses to release his vow and act wisely.
insight: It shifts attention from what is understood to what stubbornness still refuses to release.
modern_relevance: You know your partner is right in the middle of an argument, but you keep defending your position anyway. Clear seeing means nothing if pride keeps steering.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोउ कह जौं भल अहइ बिधाता। सब कहँ सुनिअ उचित फल दाता॥ तौ जानकिहि मिलिहि बरु एहू। नाहिन आलि इहाँ संदेहू ॥
translation: कोई कहती है- यदि विधाता भले हैं और सुना जाता है कि वे सबको उचित फल देते हैं, तो जानकीजी को यही वर मिलेगा। हे सखी! इसमें संदेह नहीं है ॥
english_translation: If the creator is kind and gives each person the right result, then Janaki will surely get this groom. O friend, there is no doubt.
essence: What fits rightly will find its place.
simple_meaning: If the creator truly gives each person the fitting result, then Janaki will surely receive this groom. The women watching the swayamvar feel certain about Ram.
insight: It shifts the mind from anxious wishing to trusting what aligns naturally.
modern_relevance: You watch two people in a room and know, without forcing it, that the right match is already obvious. The heart stops bargaining and simply recognises what fits.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जौं बिधि बस अस बनै सँजोगू। तौ कृतकृत्य होइ सब लोगू॥ सखि हमरें आरति अति तातें। कबहुँक ए आवहिं एहि नातें ॥
translation: जो दैवयोग से ऐसा संयोग बन जाए, तो हम सब लोग कृतार्थ हो जाएँ। हे सखी! मेरे तो इसी से इतनी अधिक आतुरता हो रही है कि इसी नाते कभी ये यहाँ आवेंगे ॥
english_translation: If fate arranges such a meeting, everyone will be fulfilled. O friend, my longing is so intense that perhaps they will come here through this bond.
essence: Hope turns a possible meeting into a whole world.
simple_meaning: If destiny brings this meeting about, everyone will feel fulfilled. The speaker longs so deeply that even a small bond feels like a possible path to that meeting.
insight: It shifts the mind from certainty to hopeful waiting, where desire reads meaning into every possible sign.
modern_relevance: You keep replaying a message, a meeting, a chance encounter, because one small opening feels like it could change everything. Hope makes even uncertainty feel alive.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: नाहिं त हम कहुँ सुनहु सखि इन्ह कर दरसनु दूरि। यह संघटु तब होइ जब पुन्य पुराकृत भूरि ॥
translation: नहीं तो (विवाह न हुआ तो) हे सखी! सुनो, हमको इनके दर्शन दुर्लभ हैं। यह संयोग तभी हो सकता है, जब हमारे पूर्वजन्मों के बहुत पुण्य हों ॥
english_translation: Otherwise, listen, dear friend: seeing them is hard for us. This union can happen only if our past lives hold great merit.
essence: Rare meetings feel like the fruit of deep merit.
simple_meaning: The women say that meeting Ram is rare and can happen only through great past merit.
insight: It shifts desire from entitlement to reverence, making the reader see precious meetings as earned, not owed.
modern_relevance: You meet someone and feel, almost instantly, that this connection is not ordinary. The mind calls it chance, but the heart feels the weight of everything that led here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बोली अपर कहेहु सखि नीका। एहिं बिआह अति हित सबही का। कोउ कह संकर चाप कठोरा। ए स्यामल मृदु गात किसोरा ॥
translation: दूसरी ने कहा- हे सखी! तुमने बहुत अच्छा कहा। इस विवाह से सभी का परम हित है। किसी ने कहा- शंकरजी का धनुष कठोर है और ये साँवले राजकुमार कोमल शरीर के बालक हैं ॥
english_translation: Another said, “Sakhi, you spoke well. This marriage is for everyone’s highest good. Someone said, “Shankar’s bow is hard, and these dark, tender-bodied youths are boys.”
essence: Hope and doubt can stand side by side before the same impossible task.
simple_meaning: One woman agrees that this marriage would bless everyone. Another points out the obstacle: Shiva’s bow is hard to bend, while the princes look young and delicate.
insight: It shows how a hopeful vision can coexist with clear-eyed recognition of difficulty.
modern_relevance: A family chat fills with excitement about a wedding, then someone quietly names the practical problem no one wants to say aloud. Hope and doubt are both speaking at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सबु असमंजस अहइ सयानी। यह सुनि अपर कहइ मृदु बानी॥ सखि इन्ह कहँ कोउ कोउ अस कहहीं। बड़ प्रभाउ देखत लघु अहहीं ॥
translation: हे सयानी! सब असमंजस ही है। यह सुनकर दूसरी सखी कोमल वाणी से कहने लगी- हे सखी! इनके संबंध में कोई-कोई ऐसा कहते हैं कि ये देखने में तो छोटे हैं, पर इनका प्रभाव बहुत बड़ा है ॥
english_translation: O wise one, everything is bewildering. Hearing this, another spoke gently: "Sister, some say this about them: they look small, yet their power is great."
essence: True power can hide behind a modest appearance.
simple_meaning: The women are unsure about the match, but one of them says the prince may look young while still carrying great power.
insight: It shifts attention from outward size to hidden capacity.
modern_relevance: At a job interview, the quiet candidate speaks softly and looks unassuming. Then one answer changes the room. People often mistake calm presence for weakness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परसि जासु पद पंकज धूरी। तरी अहल्या कृत अघ भूरी॥ सो कि रहिहि बिनु सिव धनु तोरें। यह प्रतीति परिहरिअ न भोरें ॥
translation: जिनके चरणकमलों की धूलि का स्पर्श पाकर अहल्या तर गई, जिसने बड़ा भारी पाप किया था, वे क्या शिवजी का धनुष बिना तोड़े रहेंगे। इस विश्वास को भूलकर भी नहीं छोड़ना चाहिए ॥
english_translation: The dust from whose lotus feet redeemed Ahalya, burdened with grave wrongdoing, can such a one fail to break Shiva's bow? Never let go of this faith, even for a moment.
essence: Past grace is reason enough for trust.
simple_meaning: Ram's feet have already shown their power by redeeming Ahalya. That same power makes it unthinkable that he will fail to break Shiva's bow.
insight: It shifts the mind from present doubt to remembered proof.
modern_relevance: You are doubting whether a hard conversation will work, then remember every time this person has already shown up for you. Past grace becomes present confidence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जेहिं बिरंचि रचि सीय सँवारी। तेहिं स्यामल बरु रचेउ बिचारी॥ तासु बचन सुनि सब हरषानीं। ऐसेइ होउ कहहिं मृदु बानीं ॥
translation: जिस ब्रह्मा ने सीता को सँवारकर (बड़ी चतुराई से) रचा है, उसी ने विचार कर साँवला वर भी रच रखा है। उसके ये वचन सुनकर सब हर्षित हुईं और कोमल वाणी से कहने लगीं- ऐसा ही हो ॥
english_translation: The one who fashioned Sita with care also fashioned the dark-hued groom with thought. Hearing this, everyone rejoiced and softly said, "So be it."
essence: What is truly matched needs no argument.
simple_meaning: The women agree that Sita and Ram are perfectly matched, as if both were fashioned with the same care. Their doubt turns into joy and acceptance.
insight: It turns hesitation into assent by framing the union as already rightly made.
modern_relevance: At a wedding when everyone is still measuring the match, one quiet comment can dissolve the tension. Suddenly the choice feels not forced, but beautifully obvious.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हियँ हरषहिं बरषहिं सुमन सुमुखि सुलोचनि बृंद। जाहिं जहाँ जहँ बंधु दोउ तहँ तहँ परमानंद ॥
translation: सुंदर मुख और सुंदर नेत्रों वाली स्त्रियाँ समूह की समूह हृदय में हर्षित होकर फूल बरसा रही हैं। जहाँ-जहाँ दोनों भाई जाते हैं, वहाँ-वहाँ परम आनंद छा जाता है ॥
english_translation: Women with lovely faces and beautiful eyes felt joy in their hearts and showered flowers. Wherever the two brothers went, there was supreme delight.
essence: Their presence turns an ordinary path into celebration.
simple_meaning: As Ram and Lakshman walk through the crowd, the women around them feel joy and shower flowers. Their presence fills every place with delight.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the living presence that makes the event feel blessed.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the mood changes before you speak. Some people carry that kind of quiet grace, and everyone around them feels it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुर पूरब दिसि गे दोउ भाई। जहँ धनुमख हित भूमि बनाई॥ अति बिस्तार चारु गच ढारी। बिमल बेदिका रुचिर सँवारी ॥
translation: दोनों भाई नगर के पूरब ओर गए, जहाँ धनुषयज्ञ के लिए (रंग) भूमि बनाई गई थी। बहुत लंबा-चौड़ा सुंदर ढाला हुआ पक्का आँगन था, जिस पर सुंदर और निर्मल वेदी सजाई गई थी ॥
english_translation: The two brothers went to the eastern side of the city, where the ground had been prepared for the bow sacrifice. It was a broad, beautifully arranged courtyard, with a pure and lovely altar set in place.
essence: A sacred event begins with a carefully prepared space.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman walk to the prepared site for the bow sacrifice. The verse simply describes the sacred space set up for the event.
insight: It shifts attention from the drama to the sacred preparation that makes the drama possible.
modern_relevance: Before a wedding, the hall is being decorated, chairs aligned, flowers placed, and the altar set. The verse captures that charged stillness just before everything begins.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चहुँ दिसि कंचन मंच बिसाला। रचे जहाँ बैठहिं महिपाला॥ तेहि पाछें समीप चहुँ पासा। अपर मंच मंडली बिलासा ॥
translation: चारों ओर सोने के बड़े-बड़े मंच बने थे, जिन पर राजा लोग बैठेंगे। उनके पीछे समीप ही चारों ओर दूसरे मचानों का मंडलाकार घेरा सुशोभित था ॥
english_translation: All around stood broad golden platforms where the kings would sit. Behind them, close on every side, another circular array of elegant platforms was set.
essence: Royal splendor is carefully arranged before the moment begins.
simple_meaning: Golden platforms were arranged for the kings, with another ring of platforms set just behind them. The verse is describing the ceremonial seating area.
insight: It shifts attention from the event to the order and dignity built around it.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall is set before the guests arrive: chairs aligned, lights tested, stage polished. The verse lingers on the arrangement itself, because the event’s importance is already visible in the space.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कछुक ऊँचि सब भाँति सुहाई। बैठहिं नगर लोग जहँ जाई॥ तिन्ह के निकट बिसाल सुहाए। धवल धाम बहुबरन बनाए ॥
translation: वह कुछ ऊँचा था और सब प्रकार से सुंदर था, जहाँ जाकर नगर के लोग बैठेंगे। उन्हीं के पास विशाल एवं सुंदर सफेद मकान अनेक रंगों के बनाए गए हैं ॥
english_translation: It was somewhat raised and beautiful in every way, where the city people would sit and watch. Beside it stood large, lovely white buildings made in many colors.
essence: The ceremony’s beauty begins with the space built around it.
simple_meaning: The viewing area was built higher and made beautiful, with large white buildings nearby for the people of the city.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the careful creation of a worthy setting for it.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall is being decorated before guests arrive, and every chair, curtain, and walkway is placed with care. The beauty of the space already signals the importance of what is about to happen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ बैठें देखहिं सब नारी। जथाजोगु निज कुल अनुहारी॥ पुर बालक कहि कहि मृदु बचना। सादर प्रभुहि देखावहिं रचना ॥
translation: जहाँ अपने-अपने कुल के अनुसार सब स्त्रियाँ यथायोग्य (जिसको जहाँ बैठना उचित है) बैठकर देखेंगी। नगर के बालक कोमल वचन कह-कहकर आदरपूर्वक प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को (यज्ञशाला की) रचना दिखला रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Where all the women will sit and watch according to their family rank. The boys of the city, speaking gently, respectfully show Lord Ram the arrangement.
essence: Order and tenderness can make even a public gathering feel sacred.
simple_meaning: The verse describes the arranged seating at the ceremony and the city boys politely showing Ram around. It is a scene of order, respect, and joyful attention.
insight: It highlights how devotion and respect can appear as simple, courteous conduct in public spaces.
modern_relevance: At a wedding venue, volunteers quietly guide guests to their seats while children point out the decorations with pride. The atmosphere feels orderly because everyone is being treated with care.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब सिसु एहि मिस प्रेमबस परसि मनोहर गात। तन पुलकहिं अति हरषु हियँ देखि देखि दोउ भ्रात ॥
translation: सब बालक इसी बहाने प्रेम के वश में होकर श्री रामजी के मनोहर अंगों को छूकर शरीर से पुलकित हो रहे हैं और दोनों भाइयों को देख-देखकर उनके हृदय में अत्यन्त हर्ष हो रहा है ॥
english_translation: All the children, under the pretext of this, touched the lovely limbs of Ram in love. Their bodies thrilled with joy as they kept looking at the two brothers.
essence: Love makes even touch feel like blessing.
simple_meaning: The children use the moment to touch Ram and Lakshman lovingly, and seeing them fills everyone with joy.
insight: It shows how genuine beauty and goodness draw spontaneous affection, not forced respect.
modern_relevance: A child reaches for a beloved teacher at a school event, then beams just from standing nearby. Some presence makes people soften without effort.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिसु सब राम प्रेमबस जाने। प्रीति समेत निकेत बखाने॥ निज निज रुचि सब लेहिं बोलाई। सहित सनेह जाहिं दोउ भाई ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सब बालकों को प्रेम के वश जानकर (यज्ञभूमि के) स्थानों की प्रेमपूर्वक प्रशंसा की। (इससे बालकों का उत्साह, आनंद और प्रेम और भी बढ़ गया, जिससे) वे सब अपनी-अपनी रुचि के अनुसार उन्हें बुला लेते हैं और (प्रत्येक के बुलाने पर) दोनों भाई प्रेम सहित उनके पास चले जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram knew all the children were moved by love. He described the sacred place with affection. Each one called them over as they wished, and the two brothers went along lovingly.
essence: Love turns public gathering into personal welcome.
simple_meaning: Ram understood that the children were acting out of loving excitement. They admired the place, called the brothers over, and the brothers went with affection.
insight: It shows how presence can create warmth without effort; the brothers move through the crowd as beloved guests, not distant figures.
modern_relevance: At a wedding hall before the ceremony, cousins keep pulling the groom aside just to admire his clothes, tease him, and bring him to different groups. The room feels warm because everyone is moved by affection, not formality.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम देखावहिं अनुजहि रचना। कहि मृदु मधुर मनोहर बचना॥ लव निमेष महुँ भुवन निकाया। रचइ जासु अनुसासन माया ॥
translation: कोमल, मधुर और मनोहर वचन कहकर श्री रामजी अपने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण को (यज्ञभूमि की) रचना दिखलाते हैं। जिनकी आज्ञा पाकर माया लव निमेष (पलक गिरने के चौथाई समय) में ब्रह्माण्डों के समूह रच डालती है, ॥
english_translation: Ram shows the arrangement to Lakshman, speaking soft, sweet, and lovely words. By whose command Maya creates countless worlds in a moment of a blink,
essence: True greatness can speak in the softest voice.
simple_meaning: Ram gently shows Lakshman the sacred arrangement and speaks to him with tender words. The verse also points to Ram's command over the power that creates worlds in an instant.
insight: It teaches you to hold strength without hardness, letting power remain warm and approachable.
modern_relevance: You are explaining something ordinary to a younger sibling, calm and patient, while carrying a depth they cannot yet see. The verse holds both the gentle human moment and the vast power behind it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भगति हेतु सोइ दीनदयाला। चितवत चकित धनुष मखसाला॥ कौतुक देखि चले गुरु पाहीं। जानि बिलंबु त्रास मन माहीं ॥
translation: वही दीनों पर दया करने वाले श्री रामजी भक्ति के कारण धनुष यज्ञ शाला को चकित होकर (आश्चर्य के साथ) देख रहे हैं। इस प्रकार सब कौतुक (विचित्र रचना) देखकर वे गुरु के पास चले। देर हुई जानकर उनके मन में डर है ॥
english_translation: The Lord of the humble, moved by devotion, gazed in wonder at the sacrificial hall. Seeing all the marvels, he went to the teacher, fearing delay in his mind.
essence: True greatness can look like wonder and hurry to serve.
simple_meaning: Ram looks with childlike wonder at the sacrificial hall, then quickly goes to his teacher, afraid of being late.
insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing that dignity can include childlike curiosity.
modern_relevance: You enter a grand hall for an interview, a wedding, or a formal meeting and still feel small enough to look around with wonder. Respect and humility can coexist with confidence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जासु त्रास डर कहुँ डर होई। भजन प्रभाउ देखावत सोई॥ कहि बातें मृदु मधुर सुहाईं। किए बिदा बालक बरिआईं ॥
translation: जिनके भय से डर को भी डर लगता है, वही प्रभु भजन का प्रभाव (जिसके कारण ऐसे महान प्रभु भी भय का नाट्य करते हैं) दिखला रहे हैं। उन्होंने कोमल, मधुर और सुंदर बातें कहकर बालकों को जबर्दस्ती विदा किया ॥
english_translation: By whose fear even fear itself becomes afraid, he now displays the power of devotion. Speaking gently, sweetly, and beautifully, he sent the boys away by force.
essence: True greatness can choose gentleness without losing power.
simple_meaning: Ram, who makes fear itself tremble, is showing the power of devotion by gently sending the boys away.
insight: It shifts attention from outward authority to the quiet force of loving conduct.
modern_relevance: You have every reason to dominate the room, but you choose a gentle tone instead. That restraint often carries more strength than pressure ever could.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सभय सप्रेम बिनीत अति सकुच सहित दोउ भाइ। गुर पद पंकज नाइ सिर बैठे आयसु पाइ ॥
translation: फिर भय, प्रेम, विनय और बड़े संकोच के साथ दोनों भाई गुरु के चरण कमलों में सिर नवाकर आज्ञा पाकर बैठे ॥
english_translation: Then, with fear, love, humility, and deep modesty, both brothers bowed their heads at the guru's lotus feet and sat down after receiving permission.
essence: Even victory bows before guidance.
simple_meaning: Both brothers bow to their teacher with love and humility, then sit only after receiving permission.
insight: It teaches you to pause, bow, and receive direction before acting further.
modern_relevance: You finish presenting your work and still wait for your mentor's nod before speaking again. Confidence without humility feels loud; confidence with restraint feels complete.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निसि प्रबेस मुनि आयसु दीन्हा। सबहीं संध्याबंदनु कीन्हा॥ कहत कथा इतिहास पुरानी। रुचिर रजनि जुग जाम सिरानी ॥
translation: रात्रि का प्रवेश होते ही (संध्या के समय) मुनि ने आज्ञा दी, तब सबने संध्यावंदन किया। फिर प्राचीन कथाएँ तथा इतिहास कहते-कहते सुंदर रात्रि दो पहर बीत गई ॥
english_translation: As night fell, the sage gave the order, and everyone performed the evening worship. Then they spent two watches of the beautiful night telling old stories and histories.
essence: Evening worship and shared stories make the night sacred.
simple_meaning: Night falls, the sage gives the order, and everyone does evening worship. After that, they spend the night listening to old stories until two watches pass.
insight: It shifts attention from action to shared rhythm, showing how discipline and story can steady a night.
modern_relevance: The house goes quiet after dinner, phones are set aside, and an elder begins telling family stories no one wants to end. The evening becomes a small sanctuary.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनिबर सयन कीन्हि तब जाई। लगे चरन चापन दोउ भाई॥ जिन्ह के चरन सरोरुह लागी। करत बिबिध जप जोग बिरागी ॥
translation: तब श्रेष्ठ मुनि ने जाकर शयन किया। दोनों भाई उनके चरण दबाने लगे, जिनके चरण कमलों के (दर्शन एवं स्पर्श के) लिए वैराग्यवान् पुरुष भी भाँति-भाँति के जप और योग करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Then the great sage went to sleep. The two brothers began massaging his feet. Even renunciates perform many chants and disciplines to reach the lotus feet that bear his touch.
essence: Love kneels where pride would hesitate.
simple_meaning: The sage goes to sleep, and both brothers massage his feet. The verse praises those feet so highly that even renunciates seek them through chant and yoga.
insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing that real devotion is expressed through humble service.
modern_relevance: You stay up beside an exhausted mentor after a long day, quietly helping however you can. No applause, no spotlight — just the dignity of serving well.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेइ दोउ बंधु प्रेम जनु जीते। गुर पद कमल पलोटत प्रीते॥ बार बार मुनि अग्या दीन्ही। रघुबर जाइ सयन तब कीन्ही ॥
translation: वे ही दोनों भाई मानो प्रेम से जीते हुए प्रेमपूर्वक गुरुजी के चरण कमलों को दबा रहे हैं। मुनि ने बार-बार आज्ञा दी, तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने जाकर शयन किया ॥
english_translation: Those two brothers were as if conquered by love, tenderly massaging the guru's lotus feet. Again and again the sage gave the command, and then Raghubar went to sleep.
essence: Love obeys through service and rests only when asked.
simple_meaning: The two brothers lovingly serve their teacher by massaging his feet. Only after the sage insists does Ram go to sleep.
insight: It shifts attention from claiming closeness to expressing it through humble care.
modern_relevance: You keep helping a mentor pack up after the workshop ends, even when they tell you to stop. Respect can look like quiet service, not grand speech.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चापत चरन लखनु उर लाएँ। सभय सप्रेम परम सचु पाएँ॥ पुनि पुनि प्रभु कह सोवहु ताता। पौढ़े धरि उर पद जलजाता ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के चरणों को हृदय से लगाकर भय और प्रेम सहित परम सुख का अनुभव करते हुए लक्ष्मणजी उनको दबा रहे हैं। प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने बार-बार कहा- हे तात! (अब) सो जाओ। तब वे उन चरण कमलों को हृदय में धरकर लेटे रहे ॥
english_translation: Laxman pressed Ram's feet, holding them to his heart, and felt fearless, loving, and utterly fulfilled. Again and again, the Lord said, 'Sleep now, dear one.' Then he lay down with those lotus feet kept in his heart.
essence: Closeness to Ram makes even exhaustion feel sacred.
simple_meaning: Laxman holds Ram's feet to his heart and feels complete. Ram keeps telling him to rest, but Laxman stays lying with those feet in his chest.
insight: It shifts attention from self-care alone to the joy of devoted service.
modern_relevance: You stay awake beside a loved one in the hospital, ignoring your own fatigue because caring for them feels more real than sleep. That is Laxman's tenderness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उठे लखनु निसि बिगत सुनि अरुनसिखा धुनि कान। गुर तें पहिलेहिं जगतपति जागे रामु सुजान ॥
translation: रात बीतने पर, मुर्गे का शब्द कानों से सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी उठे। जगत के स्वामी सुजान श्री रामचन्द्रजी भी गुरु से पहले ही जाग गए ॥
english_translation: When night had passed and the rooster's cry was heard, Lakshman rose. Lord of the world, wise Ram awoke even before the teacher.
essence: True greatness wakes before everyone else.
simple_meaning: Lakshman rises at dawn, and Ram is already awake before the teacher. The verse shows their disciplined, attentive routine.
insight: It shifts attention from sleep and comfort to alertness, readiness, and respect for order.
modern_relevance: The alarm goes off before sunrise, and you get up before the second snooze. No one is watching, but the day already belongs to your discipline.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकल सौच करि जाइ नहाए। नित्य निबाहि मुनिहि सिर नाए॥ समय जानि गुर आयसु पाई। लेन प्रसून चले दोउ भाई ॥
translation: सब शौचक्रिया करके वे जाकर नहाए। फिर (संध्या-अग्निहोत्रादि) नित्यकर्म समाप्त करके उन्होंने मुनि को मस्तक नवाया। (पूजा का) समय जानकर, गुरु की आज्ञा पाकर दोनों भाई फूल लेने चले ॥
english_translation: After completing all cleansing rites, they bathed. After finishing their daily duties, they bowed to the sage. Knowing the proper time and receiving the teacher’s permission, both brothers went to gather flowers.
essence: Right action begins with cleansing, respect, and proper timing.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman finish their morning cleansing, bow to the sage, wait for the proper time, receive permission from their teacher, and then go to gather flowers.
insight: It shifts action from impulse to disciplined timing and deference to guidance.
modern_relevance: You finish your shower, silence your phone, and check in with the person guiding the project before starting. Even a small task goes better when you enter it with respect.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूप बागु बर देखेउ जाई। जहँ बसंत रितु रही लोभाई॥ लागे बिटप मनोहर नाना। बरन बरन बर बेलि बिताना ॥
translation: उन्होंने जाकर राजा का सुंदर बाग देखा, जहाँ वसंत ऋतु लुभाकर रह गई है। मन को लुभाने वाले अनेक वृक्ष लगे हैं। रंग-बिरंगी उत्तम लताओं के मंडप छाए हुए हैं ॥
english_translation: They went and saw the king's beautiful garden, where spring itself seemed to linger in delight. Many charming trees stood there, and trellises of many-colored, excellent vines spread everywhere.
essence: Beauty fills the world before anyone speaks.
simple_meaning: They entered a royal garden full of beautiful trees and colorful vines, so lovely that spring itself seemed to stay there.
insight: It slows the mind enough to notice sacred beauty before the next action begins.
modern_relevance: You step into a public garden at dawn, and everything looks almost unreal — the trees, the vines, the light. Before any task begins, the world itself seems to breathe.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नव पल्लव फल सुमन सुहाए। निज संपति सुर रूख लजाए॥ चातक कोकिल कीर चकोरा। कूजत बिहग नटत कल मोरा ॥
translation: नए, पत्तों, फलों और फूलों से युक्त सुंदर वृक्ष अपनी सम्पत्ति से कल्पवृक्ष को भी लजा रहे हैं। पपीहे, कोयल, तोते, चकोर आदि पक्षी मीठी बोली बोल रहे हैं और मोर सुंदर नृत्य कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Fresh leaves, fruits, and flowers made the trees beautiful. Their abundance put even the wish-fulfilling tree to shame. Cuckoos, parrots, chakoras, and other birds sang sweetly, while peacocks danced gracefully.
essence: Nature’s abundance fills the garden with song and dance.
simple_meaning: The garden is overflowing with fresh beauty, sweet birdsong, and peacocks dancing. It is a rich, festive scene.
insight: It invites attention to abundance and sensory wonder before the story moves on.
modern_relevance: You step into a quiet park after rain and notice everything seems to be showing off — the leaves, the flowers, the birds, even the air. The world can feel like that for a moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मध्य बाग सरु सोह सुहावा। मनि सोपान बिचित्र बनावा॥ बिमल सलिलु सरसिज बहुरंगा। जलखग कूजत गुंजत भृंगा ॥
translation: बाग के बीचोंबीच सुहावना सरोवर सुशोभित है, जिसमें मणियों की सीढ़ियाँ विचित्र ढंग से बनी हैं। उसका जल निर्मल है, जिसमें अनेक रंगों के कमल खिले हुए हैं, जल के पक्षी कलरव कर रहे हैं और भ्रमर गुंजार कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: In the middle of the garden stands a lovely lake, with wondrous stairways made of gems. Its water is clear, with many-colored lotuses blooming; water birds call, and bees hum.
essence: The setting itself becomes part of the wonder.
simple_meaning: A beautiful lake sits in the center of the garden, with gem-like steps, clear water, colorful lotuses, birds, and bees all adding to its charm.
insight: It trains attention to notice atmosphere, not just objects.
modern_relevance: You step into a quiet public garden after a noisy commute and suddenly notice the pond, the lilies, the birds, the hum. The mind softens before it even tries.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बागु तड़ागु बिलोकि प्रभु हरषे बंधु समेत। परम रम्य आरामु यहु जो रामहि सुख देत ॥
translation: बाग और सरोवर को देखकर प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी भाई लक्ष्मण सहित हर्षित हुए। यह बाग (वास्तव में) परम रमणीय है, जो (जगत को सुख देने वाले) श्री रामचन्द्रजी को सुख दे रहा है ॥
english_translation: Seeing the garden and lake, Lord Ram rejoiced with Lakshman. This garden is truly beautiful, bringing delight even to Ram, who gives delight to the world.
essence: Even Ram is delighted by beauty.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman feel happy seeing the beautiful garden and lake. The place is so lovely that it seems to give joy even to Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from plot to atmosphere, showing how setting can prepare the mind for the next encounter.
modern_relevance: You walk into a quiet public garden after a long week and feel your shoulders drop. Before any conversation begins, the place itself has already changed your mood.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चहुँ दिसि चितइ पूँछि मालीगन। लगे लेन दल फूल मुदित मन॥ तेहि अवसर सीता तहँ आई। गिरिजा पूजन जननि पठाई ॥
translation: चारों ओर दृष्टि डालकर और मालियों से पूछकर वे प्रसन्न मन से पत्र-पुष्प लेने लगे। उसी समय सीताजी वहाँ आईं। माता ने उन्हें गिरिजाजी (पार्वती) की पूजा करने के लिए भेजा था ॥
english_translation: Looking all around and asking the gardeners, they happily began gathering leaves and flowers. At that moment Sita arrived there, sent by her mother to worship Girija.
essence: A simple errand opens the door to a sacred meeting.
simple_meaning: The people gather flowers and leaves for worship, and Sita arrives at the same time, sent by her mother to honor Girija.
insight: It shifts attention from the task itself to the timing and grace woven through it.
modern_relevance: You are hurrying to collect flowers before a family ritual begins, and someone you love walks in at the exact right moment. Ordinary errands can suddenly feel charged with meaning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: संग सखीं सब सुभग सयानीं। गावहिं गीत मनोहर बानीं॥ सर समीप गिरिजा गृह सोहा। बरनि न जाइ देखि मनु मोहा ॥
translation: साथ में सब सुंदरी और सयानी सखियाँ हैं, जो मनोहर वाणी से गीत गा रही हैं। सरोवर के पास गिरिजाजी का मंदिर सुशोभित है, जिसका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता, देखकर मन मोहित हो जाता है॥।2॥
english_translation: All her beautiful, wise companions sang sweet songs. Near the lake, Girija's shrine shone; its beauty cannot be described, and the mind was enchanted at the sight.
essence: A holy place can enchant the mind before any prayer begins.
simple_meaning: Sita arrives with her companions singing sweet songs. Near the lake, Girija's shrine is so beautiful that it leaves the mind spellbound.
insight: It shifts attention from action to atmosphere, showing how sacred space shapes the mind before prayer.
modern_relevance: You walk into a temple courtyard at dusk, and the lamps, flowers, and singing change your mood before you speak a word. The place itself prepares the heart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मज्जनु करि सर सखिन्ह समेता। गई मुदित मन गौरि निकेता॥ पूजा कीन्हि अधिक अनुरागा। निज अनुरूप सुभग बरु मागा ॥
translation: सखियों सहित सरोवर में स्नान करके सीताजी प्रसन्न मन से गिरिजाजी के मंदिर में गईं। उन्होंने बड़े प्रेम से पूजा की और अपने योग्य सुंदर वर माँगा ॥
english_translation: After bathing in the lake with her companions, Sita went joyfully to the shrine of Gauri. With deep love, she worshipped and asked for a beautiful bridegroom suited to her own nature.
essence: Pure prayer asks for what matches one’s nature.
simple_meaning: Sita bathes with her friends, goes happily to Gauri's shrine, worships with great love, and asks for a husband suited to her nature.
insight: It frames desire through reverence, not grasping, and teaches the mind to ask cleanly for what aligns with dharma.
modern_relevance: You light a candle before a big decision, not to control the future, but to ask for the right path with a steady heart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक सखी सिय संगु बिहाई। गई रही देखन फुलवाई॥ तेहिं दोउ बंधु बिलोके जाई। प्रेम बिबस सीता पहिं आई ॥
translation: एक सखी सीताजी का साथ छोड़कर फुलवाड़ी देखने चली गई थी। उसने जाकर दोनों भाइयों को देखा और प्रेम में विह्वल होकर वह सीताजी के पास आई ॥
english_translation: One companion left Sita's side and went to see the flower garden. There she saw the two brothers, and overwhelmed by love, she returned to Sita.
essence: A glimpse of Ram's grace can overwhelm the heart at once.
simple_meaning: A companion briefly leaves Sita, sees the two brothers, and returns overwhelmed with love.
insight: It shows how presence can move the heart before thought has a chance to speak.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room planning to stay detached, then one unexpected presence changes your whole mood. Some encounters do that instantly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तासु दसा देखी सखिन्ह पुलक गात जलु नैन। कहु कारनु निज हरष कर पूछहिं सब मृदु बैन ॥
translation: सखियों ने उसकी दशा देखी कि उसका शरीर पुलकित है और नेत्रों में जल भरा है। सब कोमल वाणी से पूछने लगीं कि अपनी प्रसन्नता का कारण बता ॥
english_translation: Seeing her condition, the friends saw her body thrill and tears fill her eyes. In soft words they asked, "Tell us the cause of your joy."
essence: Love reveals itself before speech can catch up.
simple_meaning: Her friends notice her body trembling and her eyes filling with tears, and they gently ask what has made her so joyful.
insight: It shows emotion becoming visible before explanation, preparing the scene for Sita's confession of love.
modern_relevance: Your friend notices the sudden shine in your eyes after one glance across the room. Before you can hide it, they already know something has changed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखन बागु कुअँर दुइ आए। बय किसोर सब भाँति सुहाए॥ स्याम गौर किमि कहौं बखानी। गिरा अनयन नयन बिनु बानी ॥
translation: (उसने कहा-) दो राजकुमार बाग देखने आए हैं। किशोर अवस्था के हैं और सब प्रकार से सुंदर हैं। वे साँवले और गोरे (रंग के) हैं, उनके सौंदर्य को मैं कैसे बखानकर कहूँ। वाणी बिना नेत्र की है और नेत्रों के वाणी नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Two princes have come to see the garden. They are young and beautiful in every way. How can I describe their beauty? Speech has no eyes, and eyes have no speech.
essence: Beauty beyond words leaves only wonder.
simple_meaning: Two young princes have entered the garden, and their beauty is beyond description. The speaker can only say that words cannot fully capture what the eyes have seen.
insight: It shifts attention from explanation to direct seeing, letting wonder come before analysis.
modern_relevance: You spot someone across a crowded station and forget your sentence halfway through. The mind goes quiet because the sight itself says more than language can hold.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि हरषीं सब सखीं सयानी। सिय हियँ अति उतकंठा जानी॥ एक कहइ नृपसुत तेइ आली। सुने जे मुनि सँग आए काली ॥
translation: यह सुनकर और सीताजी के हृदय में बड़ी उत्कंठा जानकर सब सयानी सखियाँ प्रसन्न हुईं। तब एक सखी कहने लगी- हे सखी! ये वही राजकुमार हैं, जो सुना है कि कल विश्वामित्र मुनि के साथ आए हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, all the wise companions were delighted and sensed Sita's intense eagerness. Then one companion said, 'O friend, these are the same princes said to have come yesterday with the sage Vishvamitra.'
essence: Longing becomes visible to those who know how to look.
simple_meaning: The companions realize Sita is longing deeply, and one of them identifies the princes as the same boys who arrived yesterday with Vishvamitra.
insight: It shows how devotion often begins as recognition: the heart knows before the mouth speaks.
modern_relevance: You glance at a friend across the room and instantly know something has changed in them. A close companion notices before words arrive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जिन्ह निज रूप मोहनी डारी। कीन्हे स्वबस नगर नर नारी॥ बरनत छबि जहँ तहँ सब लोगू। अवसि देखिअहिं देखन जोगू ॥
translation: और जिन्होंने अपने रूप की मोहिनी डालकर नगर के स्त्री-पुरुषों को अपने वश में कर लिया है। जहाँ-तहाँ सब लोग उन्हीं की छबि का वर्णन कर रहे हैं। अवश्य (चलकर) उन्हें देखना चाहिए, वे देखने ही योग्य हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who have cast the spell of their own beauty over the city have brought the men and women under their sway. Everyone everywhere is speaking of their radiance; surely they are worth seeing.
essence: True radiance draws people in before a single word is spoken.
simple_meaning: Their beauty has captivated the whole city. Everyone is talking about them, and all agree they must be seen.
insight: It heightens anticipation by showing that true presence announces itself before words do.
modern_relevance: You hear a room go quiet when someone rare walks in. No one needs to explain why they matter; the atmosphere already knows.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तासु बचन अति सियहि सोहाने। दरस लागि लोचन अकुलाने॥ चली अग्र करि प्रिय सखि सोई। प्रीति पुरातन लखइ न कोई ॥
translation: उसके वचन सीताजी को अत्यन्त ही प्रिय लगे और दर्शन के लिए उनके नेत्र अकुला उठे। उसी प्यारी सखी को आगे करके सीताजी चलीं। पुरानी प्रीति को कोई लख नहीं पाता ॥
english_translation: Her words delighted Sita deeply, and her eyes grew restless to see him. She moved forward with that dear friend leading the way. No one can fully trace an old, hidden love.
essence: Love moves first in the heart, long before anyone else can name it.
simple_meaning: Sita feels deep joy at those words and becomes eager to see Ram. She walks forward with her dear friend leading, moved by an old love that no one else can fully understand.
insight: It shifts attention from public explanation to the private pull of devotion.
modern_relevance: You hear a name, a song, or a voice message and something in you instantly leans forward. No one else sees why, but your heart already knows.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुमिरि सीय नारद बचन उपजी प्रीति पुनीत। चकित बिलोकति सकल दिसि जनु सिसु मृगी सभीत ॥
translation: नारदजी के वचनों का स्मरण करके सीताजी के मन में पवित्र प्रीति उत्पन्न हुई। वे चकित होकर सब ओर इस तरह देख रही हैं, मानो डरी हुई मृगछौनी इधर-उधर देख रही हो ॥
english_translation: Remembering Narad's words, Sita's heart filled with pure love. She looked in every direction in astonishment, like a frightened fawn glancing around.
essence: Pure love makes the heart both fearless and shy.
simple_meaning: Sita remembers Narad's words, and pure love rises in her heart. She looks around in startled wonder, like a frightened young deer.
insight: It shows how devotion begins as a startled, tender attentiveness rather than a settled certainty.
modern_relevance: You reread a message that changed everything, then stare out the window before answering. The heart knows before the mind does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कंकन किंकिनि नूपुर धुनि सुनि। कहत लखन सन रामु हृदयँ गुनि॥ मानहुँ मदन दुंदुभी दीन्ही। मनसा बिस्व बिजय कहँ कीन्ही ॥
translation: कंकण (हाथों के कड़े), करधनी और पायजेब के शब्द सुनकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी हृदय में विचार कर लक्ष्मण से कहते हैं- (यह ध्वनि ऐसी आ रही है) मानो कामदेव ने विश्व को जीतने का संकल्प करके डंके पर चोट मारी है ॥
english_translation: Hearing the sound of bracelets, anklets, and waist-bells, Ram thought in his heart and said to Lakshman: it is as if Cupid has sounded his drum, declaring a vow to conquer the world.
essence: Desire announces itself before the eyes ever meet it.
simple_meaning: Ram hears the ornaments before he sees anyone, and he recognizes the approach of beauty. He compares the sound to Cupid announcing his aim to conquer the world.
insight: It sharpens attention to the mind's quick response to attraction before full sight or judgment arrives.
modern_relevance: You hear someone laughing in the next room before you walk in, and your attention shifts instantly. The mind knows desire and beauty by sound before reason catches up.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: अस कहि फिरि चितए तेहि ओरा। सिय मुख ससि भए नयन चकोरा॥ भए बिलोचन चारु अचंचल। मनहुँ सकुचि निमि तजे दिगंचल ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर श्री रामजी ने फिर कर उस ओर देखा। श्री सीताजी के मुख रूपी चन्द्रमा (को निहारने) के लिए उनके नेत्र चकोर बन गए। सुंदर नेत्र स्थिर हो गए (टकटकी लग गई)। मानो निमि (जनकजी के पूर्वज) ने (जिनका सबकी पलकों में निवास माना गया है, लड़की-दामाद के मिलन-प्रसंग को देखना उचित नहीं, इस भाव से) सकुचाकर पलकें छोड़ दीं, (पलकों में रहना छोड़ दिया, जिससे पलकों का गिरना रुक गया) ॥
english_translation: After saying this, Ram looked back toward her. Sita's face became a moon, and his eyes became chakoras for that moon. His lovely eyes stayed still, as if Nimi, ashamed, had left the eyelids.
essence: True seeing holds still when love is present.
simple_meaning: Ram turns to look at Sita again, and both are lost in each other’s beauty. His eyes do not move, as if even blinking has stopped out of reverence.
insight: It shifts attention from outer activity to inward absorption, where seeing itself becomes an act of reverence.
modern_relevance: You catch someone across a crowded room and forget the noise around you. For one suspended second, attention itself becomes devotion.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: देखि सीय शोभा सुखु पावा। हृदयँ सराहत बचनु न आवा॥ जनु बिरंचि सब निज निपुनाई। बिरचि बिस्व कहँ प्रगटि देखाई ॥
translation: सीताजी की शोभा देखकर श्री रामजी ने बड़ा सुख पाया। हृदय में वे उसकी सराहना करते हैं, किन्तु मुख से वचन नहीं निकलते। (वह शोभा ऐसी अनुपम है) मानो ब्रह्मा ने अपनी सारी निपुणता को मूर्तिमान कर संसार को प्रकट करके दिखा दिया हो ॥
english_translation: Seeing Sita's beauty, Ram felt deep joy. He praised her inwardly, but no words came to his lips. Her beauty seemed like Brahma had displayed all his skill by revealing the world itself.
essence: True beauty leaves even praise speechless.
simple_meaning: Ram is overwhelmed by Sita's beauty and can only admire her inwardly. Her grace is compared to the creator's finest work made visible in the world.
insight: It shifts attention from speaking about beauty to feeling its power directly.
modern_relevance: You catch sight of someone across a crowded room and forget your sentence mid-thought. Some moments do that: they leave admiration too full for language.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुंदरता कहुँ सुंदर करई। छबिगृहँ दीपसिखा जनु बरई॥ सब उपमा कबि रहे जुठारी। केहिं पटतरौं बिदेहकुमारी ॥
translation: वह (सीताजी की शोभा) सुंदरता को भी सुंदर करने वाली है। (वह ऐसी मालूम होती है) मानो सुंदरता रूपी घर में दीपक की लौ जल रही हो। (अब तक सुंदरता रूपी भवन में अँधेरा था, वह भवन मानो सीताजी की सुंदरता रूपी दीपशिखा को पाकर जगमगा उठा है, पहले से भी अधिक सुंदर हो गया है)। सारी उपमाओं को तो कवियों ने जूँठा कर रखा है। मैं जनकनन्दिनी श्री सीताजी की किससे उपमा दूँ ॥
english_translation: Beauty itself becomes more beautiful. Like a lamp flame burning in a house of beauty. Poets have exhausted every comparison. What can compare with Janak's daughter?
essence: Sita's presence makes every comparison collapse.
simple_meaning: Sita's beauty outshines every comparison. It makes beauty itself seem more beautiful, and language runs out trying to describe her.
insight: It shifts attention from naming beauty to feeling its power directly.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence makes the whole room feel different. Your usual words feel thin, and for once the right response is silence, not explanation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिय शोभा हियँ बरनि प्रभु आपनि दसा बिचारि॥ बोले सुचि मन अनुज सन बचन समय अनुहारि ॥
translation: (इस प्रकार) हृदय में सीताजी की शोभा का वर्णन करके और अपनी दशा को विचारकर प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी पवित्र मन से अपने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण से समयानुकूल वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: After praising Sita's beauty in his heart and considering his own situation, the Lord spoke to his younger brother Lakshman with a pure mind, in words suited to the moment.
essence: Feeling deeply and speaking rightly can happen in the same breath.
simple_meaning: Ram quietly reflects on Sita and on his own position, then speaks to Lakshman with a calm, fitting response.
insight: It teaches you to let feeling settle before responding, so your words match the moment instead of your impulse.
modern_relevance: You notice something beautiful, feel the pull of it, and still choose your words carefully. That pause before speaking can keep a moment from becoming chaos.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तात जनकतनया यह सोई। धनुषजग्य जेहि कारन होई॥ पूजन गौरि सखीं लै आईं। करत प्रकासु फिरइ फुलवाईं ॥
translation: हे तात! यह वही जनकजी की कन्या है, जिसके लिए धनुषयज्ञ हो रहा है। सखियाँ इसे गौरी पूजन के लिए ले आई हैं। यह फुलवाड़ी में प्रकाश करती हुई फिर रही है ॥
english_translation: O father, this is the same daughter of Janaka for whom the bow sacrifice is being held. The maidens brought her for the worship of Gauri, and she moves through the flower-grove like light itself.
essence: Beauty becomes clear when it is seen with reverence.
simple_meaning: Ram recognizes Sita as Janaka’s daughter and explains why she is there: the bow ceremony and the Gauri worship. He sees her moving through the flower-grove like radiant light.
insight: It shifts attention from surface attraction to sacred recognition.
modern_relevance: You spot someone across a crowded temple courtyard and everything else blurs. The mind does not just notice beauty; it searches for meaning, reverence, and the story behind the face.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जासु बिलोकि अलौकिक सोभा। सहज पुनीत मोर मनु छोभा॥ सो सबु कारन जान बिधाता। फरकहिं सुभद अंग सुनु भ्राता ॥
translation: जिसकी अलौकिक सुंदरता देखकर स्वभाव से ही पवित्र मेरा मन क्षुब्ध हो गया है। वह सब कारण (अथवा उसका सब कारण) तो विधाता जानें, किन्तु हे भाई! सुनो, मेरे मंगलदायक (दाहिने) अंग फड़क रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing her wondrous beauty, my naturally pure mind was stirred. The cause of it all only the Creator knows, brother; listen, my auspicious right limbs are twitching.
essence: Pure seeing can still shake the heart.
simple_meaning: Ram sees Sita’s extraordinary beauty and feels his pure mind stirred. He says the cause is known only to the Creator and notices auspicious signs in his body.
insight: It shifts attention from control to reverent recognition: some encounters move you before you can explain them.
modern_relevance: You meet someone and feel your composure break for a moment. The feeling is real, but it does not have to make you careless or confused.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: रघुबंसिन्ह कर सहज सुभाऊ। मनु कुपंथ पगु धरइ न काऊ॥ मोहि अतिसय प्रतीति मन केरी। जेहिं सपनेहुँ परनारि न हेरी ॥
translation: रघुवंशियों का यह सहज (जन्मगत) स्वभाव है कि उनका मन कभी कुमार्ग पर पैर नहीं रखता। मुझे तो अपने मन का अत्यन्त ही विश्वास है कि जिसने (जाग्रत की कौन कहे) स्वप्न में भी पराई स्त्री पर दृष्टि नहीं डाली है ॥
english_translation: The natural nature of Raghu's line is this: the mind never steps onto the wrong path. I trust my own mind completely, for it has never looked at another man's wife even in a dream.
essence: Pride mistakes self-assurance for purity.
simple_meaning: Ravana says that the people of Raghu's line naturally avoid wrongdoing, and he trusts his own mind because it has never even glanced at another man's wife in a dream.
insight: It shifts attention from declared self-control to the deeper question of whether the mind is actually clear.
modern_relevance: Someone says, "I know myself too well to fall for that," right before making the exact mistake they swore they would avoid. Confidence can hide the blind spot.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: जिन्ह कै लहहिं न रिपु रन पीठी। नहिं पावहिं परतिय मनु डीठी॥ मंगन लहहिं न जिन्ह कै नाहीं। ते नरबर थोरे जग माहीं ॥
translation: रण में शत्रु जिनकी पीठ नहीं देख पाते (अर्थात् जो लड़ाई के मैदान से भागते नहीं), पराई स्त्रियाँ जिनके मन और दृष्टि को नहीं खींच पातीं और भिखारी जिनके यहाँ से 'नाहीं' नहीं पाते (खाली हाथ नहीं लौटते), ऐसे श्रेष्ठ पुरुष संसार में थोड़े हैं ॥
english_translation: Rare in the world are noble men whom enemies cannot see fleeing from battle, whose minds and eyes are not drawn to another man's wife, and whose doors never send a beggar away empty-handed.
essence: Nobility shows itself in courage, purity, and generosity.
simple_meaning: Truly noble people do not run from battle, do not chase another man's wife, and do not send beggars away empty-handed.
insight: It trains the mind to judge character by conduct under pressure, not by status or talk.
modern_relevance: You see someone panic under pressure, flirt where they shouldn't, and ignore the person asking for help at the door. This verse cuts through that mess and names real character: steadiness, self-control, and generosity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करत बतकही अनुज सन मन सिय रूप लोभान। मुख सरोज मकरंद छबि करइ मधुप इव पान ॥
translation: यों श्री रामजी छोटे भाई से बातें कर रहे हैं, पर मन सीताजी के रूप में लुभाया हुआ उनके मुखरूपी कमल के छबि रूप मकरंद रस को भौंरे की तरह पी रहा है ॥
english_translation: While talking with his younger brother, Ram's mind is captivated by Sita's beauty. Like a bee, he drinks the nectar of his lotus-like face.
essence: The heart drinks beauty even while the mouth speaks elsewhere.
simple_meaning: Ram is speaking with Lakshman, but his attention keeps drifting to Sita's beauty. The image compares his gaze to a bee drawn to nectar.
insight: It shows how attraction can shape attention before any words are spoken.
modern_relevance: You are answering someone politely, but your eyes keep drifting to the person across the room. The body stays in the moment; the mind has already fallen elsewhere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चितवति चकित चहूँ दिसि सीता। कहँ गए नृप किसोर मनु चिंता॥ जहँ बिलोक मृग सावक नैनी। जनु तहँ बरिस कमल सित श्रेनी ॥
translation: सीताजी चकित होकर चारों ओर देख रही हैं। मन इस बात की चिन्ता कर रहा है कि राजकुमार कहाँ चले गए। बाल मृगनयनी (मृग के छौने की सी आँख वाली) सीताजी जहाँ दृष्टि डालती हैं, वहाँ मानो श्वेत कमलों की कतार बरस जाती है ॥
english_translation: Sita, startled, looks in all directions. Her mind wonders where the prince has gone. Wherever the doe-eyed maiden looks, it is as if rows of white lotuses rain down there.
essence: Longing sharpens sight, and absence becomes the strongest presence.
simple_meaning: Sita looks around in surprise and worries about where Ram has gone. Her beauty is so gentle that wherever she looks, it seems to bloom with white lotuses.
insight: It shifts attention from the crowd to the ache of separation, making longing the center of the scene.
modern_relevance: You scan a crowded wedding hall for one face and feel the room tighten when you do not find it. The mind goes to the missing person first; everything else fades.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लता ओट तब सखिन्ह लखाए। स्यामल गौर किसोर सुहाए॥ देखि रूप लोचन ललचाने। हरषे जनु निज निधि पहिचाने ॥
translation: तब सखियों ने लता की ओट में सुंदर श्याम और गौर कुमारों को दिखलाया। उनके रूप को देखकर नेत्र ललचा उठे, वे ऐसे प्रसन्न हुए मानो उन्होंने अपना खजाना पहचान लिया ॥
english_translation: Then the maidens showed them from behind the vines: the handsome dark-complexioned and fair-complexioned princes. Seeing their beauty, their eyes were captivated; they rejoiced as if they had recognized their own treasure.
essence: True beauty feels like finding what was already yours.
simple_meaning: The maidens point out Ram and Lakshman hiding behind the vines. Sita sees their beauty and feels instant joy, as if she has found something precious she already knew.
insight: It shifts attention from looking to recognizing, showing how love can feel like recovery rather than discovery.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone across a crowded room and feel an instant certainty before you can explain it. The heart sometimes recognizes what the mind has not yet named.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: थके नयन रघुपति छबि देखें। पलकन्हिहूँ परिहरीं निमेषें॥ अधिक सनेहँ देह भै भोरी। सरद ससिहि जनु चितव चकोरी ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी की छबि देखकर नेत्र थकित (निश्चल) हो गए। पलकों ने भी गिरना छोड़ दिया। अधिक स्नेह के कारण शरीर विह्वल (बेकाबू) हो गया। मानो शरद ऋतु के चन्द्रमा को चकोरी (बेसुध हुई) देख रही हो ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ram's beauty, the eyes grew tired and the eyelids stopped blinking. Love overwhelmed the body, like a chakori gazing at the autumn moon.
essence: Ram's beauty stops the body before the mind can move.
simple_meaning: Ram's beauty is so overwhelming that the eyes stop blinking and the body goes weak with love. The sight leaves the viewer absorbed and spellbound.
insight: It shifts attention from looking at beauty to being overtaken by it, showing devotion as physical absorption.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone you love across a crowded station, and for a second everything else disappears. The body knows before the mind can explain.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लोचन मग रामहि उर आनी। दीन्हे पलक कपाट सयानी॥ जब सिय सखिन्ह प्रेमबस जानी। कहि न सकहिं कछु मन सकुचानी ॥
translation: नेत्रों के रास्ते श्री रामजी को हृदय में लाकर चतुरशिरोमणि जानकीजी ने पलकों के किवाड़ लगा दिए (अर्थात नेत्र मूँदकर उनका ध्यान करने लगीं)। जब सखियों ने सीताजी को प्रेम के वश जाना, तब वे मन में सकुचा गईं, कुछ कह नहीं सकती थीं ॥
english_translation: With the eyes, Sita brought Ram into her heart and shut the eyelids as gates. When the companions saw Sita overwhelmed by love, they fell silent, shy and unable to speak.
essence: Love closes the eyes and keeps Ram within.
simple_meaning: Sita drew Ram into her heart through her gaze and closed her eyes in loving meditation. Her companions saw that love and became too shy to speak.
insight: It shifts attention from outward seeing to inward holding, where love becomes steady and private.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone who matters and everything else goes quiet. Even the people beside you can tell: your attention has already gone somewhere deeper.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लताभवन तें प्रगट भे तेहि अवसर दोउ भाइ। तकिसे जनु जुग बिमल बिधु जलद पटल बिलगाई ॥
translation: उसी समय दोनों भाई लता मंडप (कुंज) में से प्रकट हुए। मानो दो निर्मल चन्द्रमा बादलों के परदे को हटाकर निकले हों ॥
english_translation: At that moment, the two brothers emerged from the bower. It was as if two pure moons had come out, parting a screen of clouds.
essence: Their appearance turns the whole scene luminous.
simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshman stepped out of the bower together, shining like two full moons emerging from behind clouds.
insight: It shifts attention from event to radiance, asking the reader to notice presence itself.
modern_relevance: You look up from a crowded room and see two people enter with such calm presence that the noise seems to fall away. Some arrivals change the atmosphere before a single word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सोभा सीवँ सुभग दोउ बीरा। नील पीत जलजाभ सरीरा॥ मोरपंख सिर सोहत नीके। गुच्छ बीच बिच कुसुम कली के ॥
translation: दोनों सुंदर भाई शोभा की सीमा हैं। उनके शरीर की आभा नीले और पीले कमल की सी है। सिर पर सुंदर मोरपंख सुशोभित हैं। उनके बीच-बीच में फूलों की कलियों के गुच्छे लगे हैं ॥
english_translation: Both brothers were the height of beauty. Their bodies shone like blue and yellow lotuses. Fine peacock feathers adorned their heads, with clusters of flowers and buds placed between them.
essence: Their beauty is revealed as part of their divine presence.
simple_meaning: Both brothers are described as stunningly beautiful, with lotus-like bodies and peacock feathers and flowers adorning them.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary appearance to the charged beauty of presence.
modern_relevance: You catch someone in a rare, unguarded moment and realize the room has changed. The details — a tilt of the head, a simple ornament, a calm face — suddenly feel unforgettable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भाल तिलक श्रम बिन्दु सुहाए। श्रवन सुभग भूषन छबि छाए॥ बिकट भृकुटि कच घूघरवारे। नव सरोज लोचन रतनारे ॥
translation: माथे पर तिलक और पसीने की बूँदें शोभायमान हैं। कानों में सुंदर भूषणों की छबि छाई है। टेढ़ी भौंहें और घुँघराले बाल हैं। नए लाल कमल के समान रतनारे (लाल) नेत्र हैं ॥
english_translation: A tilak and beads of sweat adorn the forehead. Lovely ornaments shine on the ears. Strong brows, curly hair, and fresh red lotus eyes complete the beauty.
essence: Even exertion becomes ornament in Ram's presence.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are described in detail: their foreheads, ornaments, brows, curls, and red lotus-like eyes all add to their beauty.
insight: It turns strain into grace, showing that effort can heighten presence instead of diminishing it.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone after a long, intense effort — hair slightly undone, face marked by strain — and the whole presence becomes more compelling, not less.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चारु चिबुक नासिका कपोला। हास बिलास लेत मनु मोला॥ मुखछबि कहि न जाइ मोहि पाहीं। जो बिलोकि बहु काम लजाहीं ॥
translation: ठोड़ी नाक और गाल बड़े सुंदर हैं और हँसी की शोभा मन को मोल लिए लेती है। मुख की छबि तो मुझसे कही ही नहीं जाती, जिसे देखकर बहुत से कामदेव लजा जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: The chin, nose, and cheeks are beautiful, and the charm of the smile steals the mind. I cannot describe the beauty of the face, before which many Cupids grow ashamed.
essence: Ram's beauty defeats description and humbles desire itself.
simple_meaning: Ram's face is so beautiful that words cannot capture it. Even the god of desire would feel humbled before it.
insight: It shifts attention from analysis to wonder, letting beauty be received instead of reduced.
modern_relevance: You catch someone smiling across a crowded room, and the whole noise of the day drops away. Some presence does not ask to be explained; it simply rearranges your attention.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उर मनि माल कंबु कल गीवा। काम कलभ कर भुज बलसींवा॥ सुमन समेत बाम कर दोना। सावँर कुअँर सखी सुठि लोना ॥
translation: वक्षःस्थल पर मणियों की माला है। शंख के सदृश सुंदर गला है। कामदेव के हाथी के बच्चे की सूँड के समान (उतार-चढ़ाव वाली एवं कोमल) भुजाएँ हैं, जो बल की सीमा हैं। जिसके बाएँ हाथ में फूलों सहित दोना है, हे सखि! वह साँवला कुँअर तो बहुत ही सलोना है ॥
english_translation: His chest wears a jewel garland. His neck is beautiful like a conch. His arms, soft and powerful like a baby elephant’s trunk, hold strength itself. In his left hand he carries a flower-filled bowl. O friend, that dark prince is truly lovely.
essence: Ram’s beauty overwhelms thought and leaves only admiration.
simple_meaning: The verse keeps describing Ram’s beauty: jeweled chest, graceful neck, strong arms, flowers in his left hand, and a dark, lovely form.
insight: It teaches attention to move from analysis to reverent seeing.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone across a crowded room and forget your train of thought. The mind goes quiet before beauty that feels larger than language.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: केहरि कटि पट पीत धर सुषमा सील निधान। देखि भानुकुलभूषनहि बिसरा सखिन्ह अपान ॥
translation: सिंह की सी (पतली, लचीली) कमर वाले, पीताम्बर धारण किए हुए, शोभा और शील के भंडार, सूर्यकुल के भूषण श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर सखियाँ अपने आपको भूल गईं ॥
english_translation: Seeing the ornament of the solar line, the companions forgot themselves.
essence: Ram's presence makes even the observer disappear.
simple_meaning: Ram's beauty and grace are so striking that the women around him lose awareness of themselves while looking at him.
insight: It shifts attention from self-display to pure, wordless admiration.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone in a crowded wedding hall and stop mid-step, forgetting the message in your hand. Some presence is so complete it erases self-consciousness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धरि धीरजु एक आलि सयानी। सीता सन बोली गहि पानी॥ बहुरि गौरि कर ध्यान करेहू। भूपकिसोर देखि किन लेहू ॥
translation: एक चतुर सखी धीरज धरकर, हाथ पकड़कर सीताजी से बोली- गिरिजाजी का ध्यान फिर कर लेना, इस समय राजकुमार को क्यों नहीं देख लेतीं ॥
english_translation: A clever companion, steadying herself, took Sita's hand and said, "Remember Gauri later; why not look at the prince now?"
essence: A gentle nudge can open the heart to what it already seeks.
simple_meaning: A wise companion gently urges Sita to look at Ram now and remember Gauri later.
insight: It shows how one careful companion can help someone cross from hesitation into direct seeing.
modern_relevance: At a crowded engagement ceremony, your friend squeezes your hand and points toward the person you came to see. One gentle cue can open the heart faster than a thousand thoughts.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकुचि सीयँ तब नयन उघारे। सनमुख दोउ रघुसिंघ निहारे॥ नख सिख देखि राम कै सोभा। सुमिरि पिता पनु मनु अति छोभा ॥
translation: तब सीताजी ने सकुचाकर नेत्र खोले और रघुकुल के दोनों सिंहों को अपने सामने (खड़े) देखा। नख से शिखा तक श्री रामजी की शोभा देखकर और फिर पिता का प्रण याद करके उनका मन बहुत क्षुब्ध हो गया ॥
english_translation: Then Sita, shyly, opened her eyes and saw the two lions of the Raghu line before her. Seeing Ram's beauty from head to toe, and remembering her father's vow, her mind became deeply agitated.
essence: Beauty can stir the heart and disturb it at once.
simple_meaning: Sita finally looks at Ram, sees his full beauty, and remembers the vow her father made. That mixture of joy and duty shakes her heart.
insight: It shows how attraction, memory, and duty can all seize the mind together.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who feels unmistakably right, then remember the promise, the family expectation, the consequences. One look can carry delight and pressure at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परबस सखिन्ह लखी जब सीता। भयउ गहरु सब कहहिं सभीता॥ पुनि आउब एहि बेरिआँ काली। अस कहि मन बिहसी एक आली ॥
translation: जब सखियों ने सीताजी को परवश (प्रेम के वश) देखा, तब सब भयभीत होकर कहने लगीं- बड़ी देर हो गई। (अब चलना चाहिए)। कल इसी समय फिर आएँगी, ऐसा कहकर एक सखी मन में हँसी ॥
english_translation: When the friends saw Sita overcome by love, they all grew uneasy and said, "It is already very late. We should go now." Then one friend laughed inwardly and said, "We will come again at this same time tomorrow."
essence: Love makes even restraint look obvious.
simple_meaning: Sita’s love is so visible that her friends become flustered and quickly try to end the meeting, though one friend secretly smiles at the situation.
insight: It shifts attention from public composure to the quiet power of love to expose the heart.
modern_relevance: You notice the room change when someone’s feelings become impossible to hide. A friend clears her throat, checks the time, and suddenly everyone knows something real has happened.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गूढ़ गिरा सुनि सिय सकुचानी। भयउ बिलंबु मातु भय मानी॥ धरि बड़ि धीर रामु उर आने। फिरी अपनपउ पितुबस जाने ॥
translation: सखी की यह रहस्यभरी वाणी सुनकर सीताजी सकुचा गईं। देर हो गई जान उन्हें माता का भय लगा। बहुत धीरज धरकर वे श्री रामचन्द्रजी को हृदय में ले आईं और (उनका ध्यान करती हुई) अपने को पिता के अधीन जानकर लौट चलीं ॥
english_translation: Hearing the mysterious words, Sita became shy. Thinking of her mother’s warning, she felt the delay. Gathering great courage, she brought Ram into her heart and, feeling herself under her father’s command, turned back.
essence: Deep feeling can bow to restraint without losing its force.
simple_meaning: Sita feels shy and delays, then gathers herself, holds Ram in her heart, and returns with a sense of duty and restraint.
insight: It shows how devotion can coexist with self-control, turning longing into disciplined restraint.
modern_relevance: You almost send the message, then stop and breathe. The feeling is real, but so is the boundary. Not every strong pull should be followed immediately.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखन मिस मृग बिहग तरु फिरइ बहोरि बहोरि। निरखि निरखि रघुबीर छबि बाढ़इ प्रीति न थोरि ॥
translation: मृग, पक्षी और वृक्षों को देखने के बहाने सीताजी बार-बार घूम जाती हैं और श्री रामजी की छबि देख-देखकर उनका प्रेम कम नहीं बढ़ रहा है। (अर्थात् बहुत ही बढ़ता जाता है) ॥
english_translation: Again and again, under the pretext of looking at deer, birds, and trees, Sita keeps circling back; each sight of Ram's radiance only deepens her love.
essence: True love keeps returning and grows stronger each time it looks.
simple_meaning: Sita keeps finding excuses to look around so she can keep seeing Ram. The more she sees him, the more her love grows.
insight: It reveals how devotion redirects attention toward the beloved, even through ordinary gestures.
modern_relevance: You pretend to check your phone, then glance up just to see one person across the room again. The excuse changes; the pull does not.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जानि कठिन सिवचाप बिसूरति। चली राखि उर स्यामल मूरति॥ प्रभु जब जात जानकी जानी। सुख सनेह सोभा गुन खानी ॥
translation: शिवजी के धनुष को कठोर जानकर वे विसूरती (मन में विलाप करती) हुई हृदय में श्री रामजी की साँवली मूर्ति को रखकर चलीं। (शिवजी के धनुष की कठोरता का स्मरण आने से उन्हें चिंता होती थी कि ये सुकुमार रघुनाथजी उसे कैसे तोड़ेंगे, पिता के प्रण की स्मृति से उनके हृदय में क्षोभ था ही, इसलिए मन में विलाप करने लगीं। प्रेमवश ऐश्वर्य की विस्मृति हो जाने से ही ऐसा हुआ, फिर भगवान के बल का स्मरण आते ही वे हर्षित हो गईं और साँवली छबि को हृदय में धारण करके चलीं।) प्रभु श्री रामजी ने जब सुख, स्नेह, शोभा और गुणों की खान श्री जानकीजी को जाती हुई जाना, ॥
english_translation: Knowing Shiva's bow to be hard, she walked on, keeping Ram's dark image in her heart. When the Lord saw Janaki depart, he knew her as a treasure-house of joy, love, beauty, and virtue.
essence: Fear yields when the heart stays fixed on Ram.
simple_meaning: Sita worries that Shiva's bow is too hard, but she keeps Ram in her heart and continues forward. Ram sees her leave and knows her as full of joy, love, beauty, and virtue.
insight: It shifts attention from the obstacle to the beloved presence held within the heart.
modern_relevance: You are about to walk into a room where one obstacle looks impossible. Your chest tightens, then you remember who you are doing it for and keep going.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परम प्रेममय मृदु मसि कीन्ही। चारु चित्त भीतीं लिखि लीन्ही॥ गई भवानी भवन बहोरी। बंदि चरन बोली कर जोरी ॥
translation: तब परमप्रेम की कोमल स्याही बनाकर उनके स्वरूप को अपने सुंदर चित्त रूपी भित्ति पर चित्रित कर लिया। सीताजी पुनः भवानीजी के मंदिर में गईं और उनके चरणों की वंदना करके हाथ जोड़कर बोलीं- ॥
english_translation: Then she made her form into a soft ink of pure love and wrote it on the beautiful wall of her heart. She returned to Parvati's shrine, bowed at her feet, and spoke with joined palms.
essence: True love writes the beloved into the heart forever.
simple_meaning: Sita holds Ram's form in her heart with the deepest love, then returns to Parvati and bows before speaking.
insight: It shifts devotion from a passing feeling into an inner imprint that guides speech and action.
modern_relevance: You leave a room after meeting someone who changed you, and their presence stays with you all day. The mind keeps replaying the moment because the heart has already made its choice.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जय जय गिरिबरराज किसोरी। जय महेस मुख चंद चकोरी॥ जय गजबदन षडानन माता। जगत जननि दामिनि दुति गाता ॥
translation: हे श्रेष्ठ पर्वतों के राजा हिमाचल की पुत्री पार्वती! आपकी जय हो, जय हो, हे महादेवजी के मुख रूपी चन्द्रमा की (ओर टकटकी लगाकर देखने वाली) चकोरी! आपकी जय हो, हे हाथी के मुख वाले गणेशजी और छह मुख वाले स्वामिकार्तिकजी की माता! हे जगज्जननी! हे बिजली की सी कान्तियुक्त शरीर वाली! आपकी जय हो! ॥
english_translation: Victory, victory to the daughter of the king of mountains. Victory to the moon-like face of Mahesh. Victory to the mother of Ganesha and Kartikeya. Victory to the world-mother, whose body shines like lightning.
essence: Praise reveals Parvati as beloved, mother, and radiant source at once.
simple_meaning: Parvati is praised as the daughter of the mountain king, Shiva’s beloved, the mother of Ganesha and Kartikeya, and the radiant mother of the world.
insight: It trains the mind to see a person’s fullness instead of reducing them to one role.
modern_relevance: At a family ceremony, one person is seen only as a mother, another only as a spouse, another only as a daughter. This verse widens the frame and says a person can hold all those identities at once, with sacred dignity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नहिं तव आदि मध्य अवसाना। अमित प्रभाउ बेदु नहिं जाना॥ भव भव बिभव पराभव कारिनि। बिस्व बिमोहनि स्वबस बिहारिनि ॥
translation: आपका न आदि है, न मध्य है और न अंत है। आपके असीम प्रभाव को वेद भी नहीं जानते। आप संसार को उत्पन्न, पालन और नाश करने वाली हैं। विश्व को मोहित करने वाली और स्वतंत्र रूप से विहार करने वाली हैं ॥
english_translation: You have no beginning, middle, or end. Even the Vedas do not know your limitless power. You create, sustain, and dissolve the world. You enchant the universe and move freely by your own will.
essence: What has no beginning or end cannot be fully known by words.
simple_meaning: Parvati is praised as beyond beginning, middle, and end. Her power is beyond even the Vedas, and she is described as the force behind creation, preservation, dissolution, and the world's enchantment.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to fully define greatness to revering what exceeds language.
modern_relevance: A person can spend years trying to explain a mother, a teacher, or a beloved mentor — and still fail. Some forms of power are known only by their effects, not by definition.
speaker: Parvati

verse_text: पतिदेवता सुतीय महुँ मातु प्रथम तव रेख। महिमा अमित न सकहिं कहि सहस सारदा सेष ॥
translation: पति को इष्टदेव मानने वाली श्रेष्ठ नारियों में हे माता! आपकी प्रथम गणना है। आपकी अपार महिमा को हजारों सरस्वती और शेषजी भी नहीं कह सकते ॥
