verse_text: बैनतेय बलि जिमि चह कागू। जिमि ससु चहै नाग अरि भागू॥ जिमि चह कुसल अकारन कोही। सब संपदा चहै सिवद्रोही ॥
translation: जैसे गरुड़ का भाग कौआ चाहे, सिंह का भाग खरगोश चाहे, बिना कारण ही क्रोध करने वाला अपनी कुशल चाहे, शिवजी से विरोध करने वाला सब प्रकार की सम्पत्ति चाहे, ॥
english_translation: Like a crow wanting Garuda's strength, like a rabbit wanting a lion's place, like an angry man wanting welfare for himself, like one opposed to Shiva wanting every kind of wealth.
essence: Unfit desires cannot deliver the good you claim to want.
simple_meaning: A person cannot sincerely want good fortune while living in anger, hostility, or the wrong nature. Desire must match character.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing outcomes to correcting the character that is asking for them.
modern_relevance: You want a calm relationship, but your messages are sharp and defensive. You want respect, but you keep poisoning the room. The verse says the mismatch is the problem.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लोभी लोलुप कल कीरति चहई। अकलंकता कि कामी लहई॥ हरि पद बिमुख परम गति चाहा। तस तुम्हार लालचु नरनाहा ॥
translation: लोभी-लालची सुंदर कीर्ति चाहे, कामी मनुष्य निष्कलंकता (चाहे तो) क्या पा सकता है? और जैसे श्री हरि के चरणों से विमुख मनुष्य परमगति (मोक्ष) चाहे, हे राजाओं! सीता के लिए तुम्हारा लालच भी वैसा ही व्यर्थ है ॥
english_translation: A greedy person may desire fame; can a lustful person gain spotless purity? And can one turned away from Hari's feet attain the highest state? O kings, your greed for Sita is just as futile.
essence: Greed disqualifies the very thing it chases.
simple_meaning: A greedy or lustful mind cannot gain what requires purity. Likewise, someone turned away from Hari cannot reach the highest state. The kings' desire for Sita is therefore pointless.
insight: It shifts the mind from craving outcomes to seeing whether the craving itself has already spoiled the aim.
modern_relevance: You want recognition, but the need to be praised is exactly what makes your work feel hollow. The more you chase validation, the less clean your effort becomes.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कोलाहलु सुनि सीय सकानी। सखीं लवाइ गईं जहँ रानी॥ रामु सुभायँ चले गुरु पाहीं। सिय सनेहु बरनत मन माहीं ॥
translation: कोलाहल सुनकर सीताजी शंकित हो गईं। तब सखियाँ उन्हें वहाँ ले गईं, जहाँ रानी (सीताजी की माता) थीं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी मन में सीताजी के प्रेम का बखान करते हुए स्वाभाविक चाल से गुरुजी के पास चले ॥
english_translation: Hearing the uproar, Sita became alarmed. Her companions took her to where the queen was. Ram then naturally went to the teacher, while thinking of Sita's love in his heart.
essence: Outward calm can hold deep feeling without losing direction.
simple_meaning: Sita is startled by the commotion and taken to the queen. Ram quietly goes to his teacher, carrying Sita's love in his heart.
insight: It separates outward action from inward feeling: Ram stays composed while love remains alive within him.
modern_relevance: In a crowded wedding hall, everyone is whispering about what just happened. One person panics, another steadies the room, and the one at the center keeps moving with quiet grace.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रानिन्ह सहित सोच बस सीया। अब धौं बिधिहि काह करनीया॥ भूप बचन सुनि इत उत तकहीं। लखनु राम डर बोलि न सकहीं ॥
translation: रानियों सहित सीताजी (दुष्ट राजाओं के दुर्वचन सुनकर) सोच के वश हैं कि न जाने विधाता अब क्या करने वाले हैं। राजाओं के वचन सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी इधर-उधर ताकते हैं, किन्तु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के डर से कुछ बोल नहीं सकते ॥
english_translation: Sita, along with the queens, is overcome with worry: what will fate do now? Hearing the kings' words, Lakshman looks here and there, but out of fear of Ram he cannot speak.
essence: Anxious hearts and restrained speech sharpen the moment before action.
simple_meaning: Sita and the queens are anxious about what will happen next. Lakshman, hearing the kings, keeps looking around but stays silent because he fears Ram's presence.
insight: It shows how social pressure and reverence can silence reaction, even when anger is rising.
modern_relevance: You sit in a room where someone says something insulting, and everyone feels the air tighten. You want to speak, but the presence of one respected person keeps you controlled.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अरुन नयन भृकुटी कुटिल चितवत नृपन्ह सकोप। मनहुँ मत्त गजगन निरखि सिंघकिसोरहि चोप ॥
translation: उनके नेत्र लाल और भौंहें टेढ़ी हो गईं और वे क्रोध से राजाओं की ओर देखने लगे, मानो मतवाले हाथियों का झुंड देखकर सिंह के बच्चे को जोश आ गया हो ॥
english_translation: Their eyes turned red, their brows twisted in anger, and they stared fiercely at the kings, like a lion cub facing a herd of drunk elephants.
essence: Fierce anger rises when pride meets a real challenge.
simple_meaning: The kings' fierce challenge fills the scene with anger and tension. Their look is compared to a lion cub bristling at a herd of elephants.
insight: It frames conflict as a visible surge of force, not just a private feeling.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where someone has just spoken too boldly. The air changes instantly; everyone feels the challenge before a single reply is made.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: खरभरु देखि बिकल पुर नारीं। सब मिलि देहिं महीपन्ह गारीं॥ तेहिं अवसर सुनि सिवधनु भंगा। आयउ भृगुकुल कमल पतंगा ॥
translation: खलबली देखकर जनकपुरी की स्त्रियाँ व्याकुल हो गईं और सब मिलकर राजाओं को गालियाँ देने लगीं। उसी मौके पर शिवजी के धनुष का टूटना सुनकर भृगुकुल रूपी कमल के सूर्य परशुरामजी आए ॥
english_translation: Seeing the uproar, the women of Janakpur became agitated and all together began to curse the kings. At that moment, hearing that Shiva's bow had been broken, Parashuram came like the sun to the lotus of Bhrigu's line.
essence: One broken bow brings a new storm into the court.
simple_meaning: The crowd in Janakpur is shaken, the women curse the kings, and Parashuram arrives after hearing that Shiva's bow has been broken.
insight: It shifts attention from the wedding's success to the immediate threat the broken bow now creates.
modern_relevance: A room that was cheering a minute ago goes silent after one bad headline. Joy can flip into tension before anyone has time to breathe.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि महीप सकल सकुचाने। बाज झपट जनु लवा लुकाने॥ गौरि सरीर भूति भल भ्राजा। भाल बिसाल त्रिपुंड बिराजा ॥
translation: इन्हें देखकर सब राजा सकुचा गए, मानो बाज के झपटने पर बटेर लुक (छिप) गए हों। गोरे शरीर पर विभूति (भस्म) बड़ी फब रही है और विशाल ललाट पर त्रिपुण्ड्र विशेष शोभा दे रहा है ॥
english_translation: Seeing him, all the kings grew uneasy, like quails hiding when a hawk swoops down. Sacred ash shone beautifully on his fair body, and the triple mark on his broad forehead stood out with special grace.
essence: True presence makes pride shrink before a single word is spoken.
simple_meaning: The kings felt shaken at his sight. His ash-covered body and sacred forehead markings stood out with striking grace.
insight: It shows how embodied presence can unsettle pride and command attention without argument.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the mood shifts before you speak. Everyone senses steadiness, or fear, or power — and reacts instantly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीस जटा ससिबदनु सुहावा। रिस बस कछुक अरुन होइ आवा॥ भृकुटी कुटिल नयन रिस राते। सहजहुँ चितवत मनहुँ रिसाते ॥
translation: सिर पर जटा है, सुंदर मुखचन्द्र क्रोध के कारण कुछ लाल हो आया है। भौंहें टेढ़ी और आँखें क्रोध से लाल हैं। सहज ही देखते हैं, तो भी ऐसा जान पड़ता है मानो क्रोध कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: His hair is matted, his face is moon-like and lovely, but anger has made it slightly red. His brows are crooked, his eyes are red with fury, and even his calm glance seems full of anger.
essence: Beauty and anger can live in the same face.
simple_meaning: The man is described as outwardly beautiful but visibly angered, with red eyes and a tense face.
insight: It teaches you to read the emotional charge beneath a composed exterior.
modern_relevance: You see someone quiet at a family gathering, but their jaw is tight and their eyes are fixed. The silence is not emptiness; it is pressure before speech.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: बृषभ कंध उर बाहु बिसाला। चारु जनेउ माल मृगछाला॥ कटि मुनिबसन तून दुइ बाँधें। धनु सर कर कुठारु कल काँधें ॥
translation: बैल के समान (ऊँचे और पुष्ट) कंधे हैं, छाती और भुजाएँ विशाल हैं। सुंदर यज्ञोपवीत धारण किए, माला पहने और मृगचर्म लिए हैं। कमर में मुनियों का वस्त्र (वल्कल) और दो तरकस बाँधे हैं। हाथ में धनुष-बाण और सुंदर कंधे पर फरसा धारण किए हैं ॥
english_translation: His shoulders are like a bull's, with broad chest and arms. He wears the sacred thread, a garland, and deer skin. Around his waist are tied a hermit's cloth and two quivers; in his hands are a bow, arrows, and an axe on his graceful shoulder.
essence: True strength can wear the clothes of simplicity.
simple_meaning: The figure is dressed like a hermit but armed like a warrior. His body, clothes, and weapons all show a strange mix of restraint and power.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance alone to the disciplined power hidden beneath restraint.
modern_relevance: Someone walks into the room in plain clothes, carrying no ego, yet everyone feels the weight of their presence. The strongest person is not always the loudest one.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सांत बेषु करनी कठिन बरनि न जाइ सरूप। धरि मुनितनु जनु बीर रसु आयउ जहँ सब भूप ॥
translation: शांत वेष है, परन्तु करनी बहुत कठोर हैं, स्वरूप का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। मानो वीर रस ही मुनि का शरीर धारण करके, जहाँ सब राजा लोग हैं, वहाँ आ गया हो ॥
english_translation: His dress is calm, but his deeds are severe; his form cannot be described. It is as if heroic energy itself has taken a sage’s body and come among all the kings.
essence: A peaceful appearance can hide overwhelming force.
simple_meaning: He looks like a calm sage, but his actions are fierce and powerful. He seems like heroic force itself has taken a saint’s body and entered the royal gathering.
insight: It trains you to read character beyond appearance and respect power that does not advertise itself.
modern_relevance: A soft-spoken person walks into the room wearing simple clothes, and the whole atmosphere changes. You realize calmness is not weakness, and restraint can carry real force.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखत भृगुपति बेषु कराला। उठे सकल भय बिकल भुआला॥ पितु समेत कहि कहि निज नामा। लगे करन सब दंड प्रनामा ॥
translation: परशुरामजी का भयानक वेष देखकर सब राजा भय से व्याकुल हो उठ खड़े हुए और पिता सहित अपना नाम कह-कहकर सब दंडवत प्रणाम करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Seeing Parashurama's terrible form, all the kings rose in fear and became agitated. Naming themselves and their fathers again and again, they all bowed down flat in reverence.
essence: Pride dissolves when fear enters the room.
simple_meaning: The kings see Parashurama's fierce appearance and are shaken. They stand up, state their names and fathers, and bow fully in fear.
insight: It shows how power can collapse self-importance and force immediate humility.
modern_relevance: A room goes silent when the senior judge walks in and everyone straightens their papers. Status vanishes in a second; the body tells the truth before the mouth does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जेहि सुभायँ चितवहिं हितु जानी। सो जानइ जनु आइ खुटानी॥ जनक बहोरि आइ सिरु नावा। सीय बोलाइ प्रनामु करावा ॥
translation: परशुरामजी हित समझकर भी सहज ही जिसकी ओर देख लेते हैं, वह समझता है मानो मेरी आयु पूरी हो गई। फिर जनकजी ने आकर सिर नवाया और सीताजी को बुलाकर प्रणाम कराया ॥
english_translation: Whoever Parashurama looks at with goodwill feels as if his life has reached its end. Then King Janaka came and bowed his head, and he called Sita forward to offer salutations.
essence: Humility is the only safe response to overwhelming force.
simple_meaning: Parashurama's gaze is so fierce that even a kind look from him feels like death. Janaka returns, bows again, and brings Sita forward to salute him.
insight: It shows how to respond to overwhelming authority with humility instead of resistance.
modern_relevance: A room goes silent when the senior partner walks in after the failed presentation. Everyone straightens up, rereads the mood, and lowers their voice before speaking again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आसिष दीन्हि सखीं हरषानीं। निज समाज लै गईं सयानीं॥ बिस्वामित्रु मिले पुनि आई। पद सरोज मेले दोउ भाई ॥
translation: परशुरामजी ने सीताजी को आशीर्वाद दिया। सखियाँ हर्षित हुईं और (वहाँ अब अधिक देर ठहरना ठीक न समझकर) वे सयानी सखियाँ उनको अपनी मंडली में ले गईं। फिर विश्वामित्रजी आकर मिले और उन्होंने दोनों भाइयों को उनके चरण कमलों पर गिराया ॥
english_translation: The wise companions, delighted, gave blessings and took Sita back into their group. Then Vishvamitra came again and made both brothers bow at his lotus feet.
essence: Blessing and bowing keep sacred moments in motion.
simple_meaning: Sita receives blessings, and her companions take her back with them. Then Vishvamitra arrives and both brothers bow at his feet.
insight: It keeps the scene moving from celebration to reverence, showing social grace and order.
modern_relevance: At a wedding, the elders finish their blessings, the bride is led away, and the next greeting begins. Not every beautiful moment is meant to be held onto.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामु लखनु दसरथ के ढोटा। दीन्हि असीस देखि भल जोटा॥ रामहि चितइ रहे थकि लोचन। रूप अपार मार मद मोचन ॥
translation: (विश्वामित्रजी ने कहा-) ये राम और लक्ष्मण राजा दशरथ के पुत्र हैं। उनकी सुंदर जोड़ी देखकर परशुरामजी ने आशीर्वाद दिया। कामदेव के भी मद को छुड़ाने वाले श्री रामचन्द्रजी के अपार रूप को देखकर उनके नेत्र थकित (स्तम्भित) हो रहे ॥
english_translation: These are Ram and Lakshman, the sons of King Dasharath. Seeing the beautiful pair, Parashurama gave his blessing. His eyes grew fixed, gazing at Ram's boundless form, the one who removes even Cupid's pride.
essence: Ram's presence stops pride before it can speak.
simple_meaning: Parashurama sees Ram and Lakshman together, blesses them, and becomes absorbed in Ram's extraordinary beauty and power.
insight: It shifts attention from conflict to the quiet authority that can hold conflict without flinching.
modern_relevance: You enter a room already charged with tension, and one person's calm presence changes the whole atmosphere. Before anyone speaks, the mood has already shifted.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: बहुरि बिलोकि बिदेह सन कहहु काह अति भीर। पूँछत जानि अजान जिमि ब्यापेउ कोपु सरीर ॥
translation: फिर सब देखकर, जानते हुए भी अनजान की तरह जनकजी से पूछते हैं कि कहो, यह बड़ी भारी भीड़ कैसी है? उनके शरीर में क्रोध छा गया ॥
english_translation: Then, looking around, he asked Janaka, “Why is there such a great crowd here?” Though he knew, he asked as if unaware, and anger filled his body.
essence: Knowing the answer, he still asks — and anger is already in control.
simple_meaning: Parashurama asks Janaka about the crowd, though he already knows the answer. His anger is already rising.
insight: It shows how pride can turn a simple question into a warning sign of conflict.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room already tense, then ask a question you know will expose the problem. Everyone can feel the heat before anyone speaks plainly.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: समाचार कहि जनक सुनाए। जेहि कारन महीप सब आए॥ सुनत बचन फिरि अनत निहारे। देखे चापखंड महि डारे ॥
translation: जिस कारण सब राजा आए थे, राजा जनक ने वे सब समाचार कह सुनाए। जनक के वचन सुनकर परशुरामजी ने फिरकर दूसरी ओर देखा तो धनुष के टुकड़े पृथ्वी पर पड़े हुए दिखाई दिए ॥
english_translation: Janaka explained the situation and told why all the kings had come. Hearing him, Parashurama looked elsewhere and saw the broken pieces of the bow lying on the ground.
essence: The broken bow is seen before the anger is spoken.
simple_meaning: Janaka explains why the kings have gathered. Parashurama turns and sees the shattered bow on the ground.
insight: It shifts attention from the explanation to the visible evidence that will trigger the next conflict.
modern_relevance: You finally look up from the argument and see the broken object on the floor, the silence in the room, the damage already done. The facts are there before the shouting starts.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अति रिस बोले बचन कठोरा। कहु जड़ जनक धनुष कै तोरा॥ बेगि देखाउ मूढ़ न त आजू। उलटउँ महि जहँ लहि तव राजू ॥
translation: अत्यन्त क्रोध में भरकर वे कठोर वचन बोले- रे मूर्ख जनक! बता, धनुष किसने तोड़ा? उसे शीघ्र दिखा, नहीं तो अरे मूढ़! आज मैं जहाँ तक तेरा राज्य है, वहाँ तक की पृथ्वी उलट दूँगा ॥
english_translation: In great rage, he spoke harsh words: "Tell me, foolish Janak, who broke the bow? Show me quickly, fool, or today I will overturn the earth as far as your kingdom extends."
essence: Anger makes even power speak like a threat.
simple_meaning: Parashurama, furious, insults Janak and demands to know who broke the bow. He threatens to destroy the kingdom if he is not shown immediately.
insight: It shows how anger seeks domination first and truth second.
modern_relevance: A senior manager slams a report on the table and asks who ruined it, not really listening for an answer. The room freezes because anger has already taken over the conversation.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: अति डरु उतरु देत नृपु नाहीं। कुटिल भूप हरषे मन माहीं॥ सुर मुनि नाग नगर नर नारी। सोचहिं सकल त्रास उर भारी ॥
translation: राजा को अत्यन्त डर लगा, जिसके कारण वे उत्तर नहीं देते। यह देखकर कुटिल राजा मन में बड़े प्रसन्न हुए। देवता, मुनि, नाग और नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष सभी सोच करने लगे, सबके हृदय में बड़ा भय है ॥
english_translation: The king was so afraid that he could not answer. The crooked king was pleased in his heart. Devas, sages, serpents, and all men and women in the city were filled with fear.
essence: Fear can silence a king and spread through an entire city.
simple_meaning: King Janak cannot answer because he is terrified. Parashurama feels pleased, while everyone in the city is shaken with fear.
insight: It shows how intimidation silences action and how fear becomes collective in a charged atmosphere.
modern_relevance: You are in a meeting when one senior voice turns sharp and nobody dares respond. The whole room tightens, and even the confident people start thinking twice.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मन पछिताति सीय महतारी। बिधि अब सँवरी बात बिगारी॥ भृगुपति कर सुभाउ सुनि सीता। अरध निमेष कलप सम बीता ॥
translation: सीताजी की माता मन में पछता रही हैं कि हाय! विधाता ने अब बनी-बनाई बात बिगाड़ दी। परशुरामजी का स्वभाव सुनकर सीताजी को आधा क्षण भी कल्प के समान बीतते लगा ॥
english_translation: Sita's mother regretted in her heart: "Alas, fate has spoiled what was already settled." Hearing Parashurama's fierce nature, Sita felt even half a moment stretch like a cosmic age.
essence: Fear can make a single moment feel like an age.
simple_meaning: Sita's mother feels regret as the marriage situation turns tense, and Sita becomes so afraid of Parashurama that even a moment feels endless.
insight: It captures how anxiety distorts time and makes calm situations feel unstable.
modern_relevance: You are waiting outside a room while a hard conversation unfolds inside. Every second feels longer than it should, and one wrong word could change everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सभय बिलोके लोग सब जानि जानकी भीरु। हृदयँ न हरषु बिषादु कछु बोले श्रीरघुबीरु ॥
translation: तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी सब लोगों को भयभीत देखकर और सीताजी को डरी हुई जानकर बोले- उनके हृदय में न कुछ हर्ष था न विषाद- ॥
english_translation: Then Shri Ramchandra saw everyone frightened and Sita afraid, yet his own heart held neither joy nor sorrow.
essence: True composure stays untouched by fear or excitement.
simple_meaning: Ram sees the crowd frightened and Sita afraid, but he stays beyond both excitement and distress before speaking.
insight: It teaches you to answer pressure without being pulled into its mood.
modern_relevance: A room goes silent after a harsh email lands on the screen. Everyone is bracing for the worst, but one person reads it, breathes, and answers without panic. That steadiness changes everything.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: नाथ संभुधनु भंजनिहारा। होइहि केउ एक दास तुम्हारा॥ आयसु काह कहिअ किन मोही। सुनि रिसाइ बोले मुनि कोही ॥
translation: हे नाथ! शिवजी के धनुष को तोड़ने वाला आपका कोई एक दास ही होगा। क्या आज्ञा है, मुझसे क्यों नहीं कहते? यह सुनकर क्रोधी मुनि रिसाकर बोले- ॥
english_translation: O Lord, the one who broke Shiva's bow will be your servant. Why not tell me your command? Hearing this, the angry sage spoke in fury.
essence: Pride hears service as insult and answers with anger.
simple_meaning: Parashurama says the bow-breaker must be Ram's servant, and asks why Ram has not given him orders. Hearing this, he grows angry.
insight: It exposes how quickly wounded pride turns a conversation into conflict.
modern_relevance: Someone corrects you in public and you feel your face heat up before you even think. The ego wants status, not truth.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: सेवकु सो जो करै सेवकाई। अरि करनी करि करिअ लराई॥ सुनहु राम जेहिं सिवधनु तोरा। सहसबाहु सम सो रिपु मोरा ॥
translation: सेवक वह है जो सेवा का काम करे। शत्रु का काम करके तो लड़ाई ही करनी चाहिए। हे राम! सुनो, जिसने शिवजी के धनुष को तोड़ा है, वह सहस्रबाहु के समान मेरा शत्रु है ॥
english_translation: A servant is one who does a servant’s work. If someone does an enemy’s deed, then only battle remains. Listen, Ram: the one who broke Shiva’s bow is my enemy, equal to Sahasrabahu.
essence: A servant cannot act like an enemy and still claim service.
simple_meaning: A true servant acts in service, not in opposition. Parashurama sees the bow-breaker as an enemy and prepares for conflict.
insight: It separates loyal action from hostile action, making the conflict explicit instead of hidden.
modern_relevance: A team member says they will help, then quietly blocks the project in meetings. Everyone feels the split immediately. This verse names that fracture: service cannot wear the mask of sabotage.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: सो बिलगाउ बिहाइ समाजा। न त मारे जैहहिं सब राजा॥ सुनि मुनि बचन लखन मुसुकाने। बोले परसुधरहि अपमाने ॥
translation: वह इस समाज को छोड़कर अलग हो जाए, नहीं तो सभी राजा मारे जाएँगे। मुनि के वचन सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी मुस्कुराए और परशुरामजी का अपमान करते हुए बोले- ॥
english_translation: Let him step away from this assembly; otherwise all the kings will be slain. Hearing the sage's words, Lakshman smiled and spoke in insult to Parashurama.
essence: Mockery turns a warning into a clash.
simple_meaning: Parashurama demands that the challenger step aside or all the kings will die. Lakshman hears this and smiles, answering with sharp disrespect.
insight: It shows how a single mocking response can turn warning into open confrontation.
modern_relevance: A tense room goes quiet after one person makes a threat. Another person smirks instead of softening the moment, and suddenly everyone can feel the conflict sharpen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहु धनुहीं तोरीं लरिकाईं। कबहुँ न असि रिस कीन्हि गोसाईं॥ एहि धनु पर ममता केहि हेतू। सुनि रिसाइ कह भृगुकुलकेतू ॥
translation: हे गोसाईं! लड़कपन में हमने बहुत सी धनुहियाँ तोड़ डालीं, किन्तु आपने ऐसा क्रोध कभी नहीं किया। इसी धनुष पर इतनी ममता किस कारण से है? यह सुनकर भृगुवंश की ध्वजा स्वरूप परशुरामजी कुपित होकर कहने लगे ॥
english_translation: O noble one, in childhood I broke many bows, yet you never became angry. Why do you cherish this bow so much? Hearing this, the banner of Bhrigu's line grew furious and spoke.
essence: Attachment flares when calm truth touches it.
simple_meaning: Ram reminds Parashurama that he broke many bows as a child and asks why this one bow is so precious. The question triggers Parashurama’s anger.
insight: It shows how calm truth can expose hidden attachment and inflate wounded ego.
modern_relevance: You ask one honest question in a tense room, and the real issue surfaces at once. The volume rises because the attachment was never really about the object.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: रे नृप बालक काल बस बोलत तोहि न सँभार। धनुही सम तिपुरारि धनु बिदित सकल संसार ॥
translation: अरे राजपुत्र! काल के वश होने से तुझे बोलने में कुछ भी होश नहीं है। सारे संसार में विख्यात शिवजी का यह धनुष क्या धनुही के समान है? ॥
english_translation: O prince, under time's power you speak without restraint. Is Shiva's bow merely like a toy bow? The whole world knows that bow.
essence: Pride talks first and sees last.
simple_meaning: Parashurama scolds the prince for speaking carelessly and mocks the sacred bow by comparing it to a child's toy bow.
insight: It exposes how insult and ego can distort judgment, turning a sacred object into something to belittle.
modern_relevance: In a tense room, someone snaps before checking the facts. The harshest words often come from wounded pride, not clear seeing.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: लखन कहा हँसि हमरें जाना। सुनहु देव सब धनुष समाना॥ का छति लाभु जून धनु तोरें। देखा राम नयन के भोरें ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी ने हँसकर कहा- हे देव! सुनिए, हमारे जान में तो सभी धनुष एक से ही हैं। पुराने धनुष के तोड़ने में क्या हानि-लाभ! श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने तो इसे नवीन के धोखे से देखा था ॥
english_translation: Lakshman laughed and said, “O noble one, hear me: in our view, all bows are the same. What loss or gain is there in breaking an old bow? Ram saw it as a new one in the morning light.”
essence: Sacred objects lose power when pride inflates them.
simple_meaning: Lakshman says the bow is just an old bow, so breaking it brings no real loss. Ram had seen it as ordinary, not special.
insight: It shifts attention from symbolic pride to plain reality, making inflated anger look unnecessary.
modern_relevance: Someone gets furious because a family heirloom cracked at a wedding, while everyone else sees only wood and metal. Lakshman's tone cuts through the drama and asks what, exactly, is being protected.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: छुअत टूट रघुपतिहु न दोसू। मुनि बिनु काज करिअ कत रोसू॥ बोले चितइ परसु की ओरा। रे सठ सुनेहि सुभाउ न मोरा ॥
translation: फिर यह तो छूते ही टूट गया, इसमें रघुनाथजी का भी कोई दोष नहीं है। मुनि! आप बिना ही कारण किसलिए क्रोध करते हैं? परशुरामजी अपने फरसे की ओर देखकर बोले- अरे दुष्ट! तूने मेरा स्वभाव नहीं सुना ॥
english_translation: The bow broke on mere touch, and Raghunath bears no fault. Why do you rage without cause, sage? Parashuram looked toward his axe and said, "Wretch, you have not heard my nature."
essence: Pride can survive even when blame disappears.
simple_meaning: Parashuram says the bow broke by itself and Ram is not at fault, but he still turns angry and warns that his true nature is fierce.
insight: It shows how wounded ego can keep fighting even after the facts are clear.
modern_relevance: You get a calm explanation in the group chat, but someone still snaps back as if being right matters more than being fair.
speaker: Parashuram

verse_text: बालकु बोलि बधउँ नहिं तोही। केवल मुनि जड़ जानहि मोही॥ बाल ब्रह्मचारी अति कोही। बिस्व बिदित छत्रियकुल द्रोही ॥
translation: मैं तुझे बालक जानकर नहीं मारता हूँ। अरे मूर्ख! क्या तू मुझे निरा मुनि ही जानता है। मैं बालब्रह्मचारी और अत्यन्त क्रोधी हूँ। क्षत्रियकुल का शत्रु तो विश्वभर में विख्यात हूँ ॥
english_translation: I do not kill you because you are a child. Fool, do you think I am merely a hermit? I am a lifelong celibate and fiercely angry. I am known everywhere as the enemy of the warrior clan.
essence: Do not mistake a calm face for harmlessness.
simple_meaning: Parashurama says he is not harmless just because he looks like a sage. He warns that he is fierce, celibate, and famous for opposing the warrior clan.
insight: It warns against confusing gentleness with powerlessness and teaches respect for hidden strength.
modern_relevance: Someone smiles calmly in a tense room, and the whole atmosphere shifts because the calm is not weakness. A quiet person can still carry force, boundaries, and memory.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: भुजबल भूमि भूप बिनु कीन्ही। बिपुल बार महिदेवन्ह दीन्ही॥ सहसबाहु भुज छेदनिहारा। परसु बिलोकु महीपकुमारा ॥
translation: अपनी भुजाओं के बल से मैंने पृथ्वी को राजाओं से रहित कर दिया और बहुत बार उसे ब्राह्मणों को दे डाला। हे राजकुमार! सहस्रबाहु की भुजाओं को काटने वाले मेरे इस फरसे को देख! ॥
english_translation: By the strength of my arms, I emptied the earth of kings and gave it away many times to the priests. O prince, behold my axe, the one that cut off Sahasrabahu's arms!
essence: Old victories become threats when pride takes over.
simple_meaning: Parashurama boasts that he cleared the earth of kings and gave it to priests, then points to the axe that cut Sahasrabahu's arms.
insight: It shows how ego uses past strength as a weapon in the present.
modern_relevance: Someone in an argument starts listing old wins, old fights, old favors, as if history alone should end the discussion. The room gets smaller when pride begins to speak in trophies.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: मातु पितहि जनि सोचबस करसि महीसकिसोर। गर्भन्ह के अर्भक दलन परसु मोर अति घोर ॥
translation: अरे राजा के बालक! तू अपने माता-पिता को सोच के वश न कर। मेरा फरसा बड़ा भयानक है, यह गर्भों के बच्चों का भी नाश करने वाला है ॥
english_translation: Do not make your parents suffer, prince. My axe is terrible; it can destroy even the children in the womb.
essence: Pride in anger turns warning into a weapon.
simple_meaning: Parashurama warns the prince not to cause his parents grief and boasts that his axe is so fierce it can even destroy unborn children.
insight: It shows how threatened ego speaks in extremes, trying to dominate instead of resolve.
modern_relevance: A furious senior keeps escalating a family argument until the words become more dangerous than the problem. The threat sounds strong, but it only exposes how quickly anger loses proportion.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: बिहसि लखनु बोले मृदु बानी। अहो मुनीसु महा भटमानी॥ पुनि पुनि मोहि देखाव कुठारू। चहत उड़ावन फूँकि पहारू ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी हँसकर कोमल वाणी से बोले- अहो, मुनीश्वर तो अपने को बड़ा भारी योद्धा समझते हैं। बार-बार मुझे कुल्हाड़ी दिखाते हैं। फूँक से पहाड़ उड़ाना चाहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Lakshman smiled and spoke gently: "Ah, great ascetic, you think yourself a mighty warrior. Again and again you show me your axe, as if you could blow away a mountain with a puff."
essence: Bluster loses power when met by steady calm.
simple_meaning: Lakshman answers the sage’s threat with calm mockery. He says the axe is no match for him, and the boast sounds empty.
insight: It teaches you to stay unshaken under intimidation and answer from composure, not panic.
modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in a meeting and starts talking like they own the room. You can feel the heat rise, or you can answer with steady wit and not hand them your fear.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: इहाँ कुम्हड़बतिया कोउ नाहीं। जे तरजनी देखि मरि जाहीं॥ देखि कुठारु सरासन बाना। मैं कछु कहा सहित अभिमाना ॥
translation: यहाँ कोई कुम्हड़े की बतिया (छोटा कच्चा फल) नहीं है, जो तर्जनी (सबसे आगे की) अँगुली को देखते ही मर जाती हैं। कुठार और धनुष-बाण देखकर ही मैंने कुछ अभिमान सहित कहा था ॥
english_translation: There is no weak pumpkin here, one that dies at the sight of a raised finger. I spoke with some pride only after seeing the axe, bow, and arrows.
essence: True courage does not wilt before threats.
simple_meaning: Lakshman says he is not fragile or easily frightened. He only spoke boldly because he saw the weapons and felt confident enough to answer back.
insight: It teaches you to recognize intimidation and answer it without collapsing into fear.
modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a meeting, trying to make you fold with a sharp tone and a glare. You do not need to become small just because they sound large.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: भृगुसुत समुझि जनेउ बिलोकी। जो कछु कहहु सहउँ रिस रोकी॥ सुर महिसुर हरिजन अरु गाई। हमरें कुल इन्ह पर न सुराई ॥
translation: भृगुवंशी समझकर और यज्ञोपवीत देखकर तो जो कुछ आप कहते हैं, उसे मैं क्रोध को रोककर सह लेता हूँ। देवता, ब्राह्मण, भगवान के भक्त और गो- इन पर हमारे कुल में वीरता नहीं दिखाई जाती ॥
english_translation: Recognizing you as a descendant of Bhrigu and seeing the sacred thread, I can bear whatever you say by restraining my anger. Gods, priests, devotees of the Lord, and cows are not met with valor in our line.
essence: Restraint can coexist with a warrior's pride.
simple_meaning: Parashurama says he can tolerate Lakshman's words because he sees his lineage and sacred thread. He also says his family does not show aggression toward the divine, priests, devotees, or cows.
insight: It shows how social respect can delay anger without dissolving ego.
modern_relevance: Someone cuts you down in front of everyone, and you answer with a smile that still carries a warning. You are trying to stay restrained, but the old pride is still standing guard.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: बधें पापु अपकीरति हारें। मारतहूँ पा परिअ तुम्हारें॥ कोटि कुलिस सम बचनु तुम्हारा। ब्यर्थ धरहु धनु बान कुठारा ॥
translation: क्योंकि इन्हें मारने से पाप लगता है और इनसे हार जाने पर अपकीर्ति होती है, इसलिए आप मारें तो भी आपके पैर ही पड़ना चाहिए। आपका एक-एक वचन ही करोड़ों वज्रों के समान है। धनुष-बाण और कुठार तो आप व्यर्थ ही धारण करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Because killing them brings sin and being defeated by them brings disgrace, even if you strike, I should fall at your feet. Your words alone are worth millions of thunderbolts; you wear bow, arrows, and axe in vain.
essence: True strength makes violence and humiliation equally impossible.
simple_meaning: Parashurama says that fighting this opponent brings shame either way, so the only proper response is reverence. He also says the other man's words are as powerful as thunderbolts and that weapons are unnecessary.
insight: It shifts the mind from confrontation to recognition of higher strength.
modern_relevance: You are ready to snap back in a meeting, then the other person speaks with such calm authority that your anger collapses. The fight was never equal.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: जो बिलोकि अनुचित कहेउँ छमहु महामुनि धीर। सुनि सरोष भृगुबंसमनि बोले गिरा गभीर ॥
translation: इन्हें (धनुष-बाण और कुठार को) देखकर मैंने कुछ अनुचित कहा हो, तो उसे हे धीर महामुनि! क्षमा कीजिए। यह सुनकर भृगुवंशमणि परशुरामजी क्रोध के साथ गंभीर वाणी बोले- ॥
english_translation: If I spoke improperly after seeing these, forgive me, O patient great sage. Hearing this, the jewel of Bhrigu's line spoke in a grave, angry voice.
essence: A polite apology can stand right before a storm of anger.
simple_meaning: Parashuram apologizes for any disrespect in his words, then the narration says he answered in an angry, serious tone.
insight: It shows the instant before conflict hardens, when courtesy still exists but barely holds.
modern_relevance: You realize you overstepped in the middle of a heated argument and try to soften it — but the room is already charged, and the next words can still cut.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कौसिक सुनहु मंद यहु बालकु। कुटिल कालबस निज कुल घालकु॥ भानु बंस राकेस कलंकू। निपट निरंकुस अबुध असंकू ॥
translation: हे विश्वामित्र! सुनो, यह बालक बड़ा कुबुद्धि और कुटिल है, काल के वश होकर यह अपने कुल का घातक बन रहा है। यह सूर्यवंश रूपी पूर्ण चन्द्र का कलंक है। यह बिल्कुल उद्दण्ड, मूर्ख और निडर है ॥
english_translation: O Kaushik, listen: this boy is foolish and crooked. Under the grip of fate, he is destroying his own lineage. He is a stain on the Sun dynasty, utterly unruly, ignorant, and fearless.
essence: Anger sees a child as a threat and mistakes contempt for insight.
simple_meaning: Parashurama insults the boy in front of Vishwamitra, calling him foolish, crooked, and a disgrace to his lineage.
insight: It shows how anger reduces a person to insults instead of seeing character or context.
modern_relevance: A heated group chat makes someone the villain before anyone asks what actually happened. The loudest voice can sound certain and still be blind.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: काल कवलु होइहि छन माहीं। कहउँ पुकारि खोरि मोहि नाहीं॥ तुम्ह हटकहु जौं चहहु उबारा। कहि प्रतापु बलु रोषु हमारा ॥
translation: अभी क्षण भर में यह काल का ग्रास हो जाएगा। मैं पुकारकर कहे देता हूँ, फिर मुझे दोष नहीं है। यदि तुम इसे बचाना चाहते हो, तो हमारा प्रताप, बल और क्रोध बतलाकर इसे मना कर दो ॥
english_translation: It will be swallowed by death in a moment. I warn you openly; blame me not later. If you want to save it, stop it by speaking of my power, strength, and anger.
essence: Arrogance mistakes loudness for power and walks straight into ruin.
simple_meaning: Ravana warns that the bow will be destroyed immediately and says no one can blame him. If anyone wants to save it, they must stop him by showing his power and fury.
insight: It shows how ego turns a simple challenge into a public display of force.
modern_relevance: A person in a meeting laughs too loudly, daring anyone to challenge them. Everyone can hear the insecurity under the volume. Ravana's voice is what unchecked ego sounds like.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: लखन कहेउ मुनि सुजसु तुम्हारा। तुम्हहि अछत को बरनै पारा॥ अपने मुँह तुम्ह आपनि करनी। बार अनेक भाँति बहु बरनी ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी ने कहा- हे मुनि! आपका सुयश आपके रहते दूसरा कौन वर्णन कर सकता है? आपने अपने ही मुँह से अपनी करनी अनेकों बार बहुत प्रकार से वर्णन की है ॥
english_translation: Lakshman said, "O sage, who else can describe your fame while you are still alive? You have often spoken of your own deeds in many ways."
essence: Self-praise loses force when it is named aloud.
simple_meaning: Lakshman answers the sage sharply, saying that the sage has already praised his own deeds many times, so no one else needs to describe his fame.
insight: It shows how to answer arrogance without losing composure: name the self-praise plainly and move the exchange forward.
modern_relevance: Someone keeps listing their achievements in a meeting, waiting for applause. One calm sentence can cut through the performance and bring the room back to reality.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: नहिं संतोषु त पुनि कछु कहहू। जनि रिस रोकि दुसह दुख सहहू॥ बीरब्रती तुम्ह धीर अछोभा। गारी देत न पावहु सोभा ॥
translation: इतने पर भी संतोष न हुआ हो तो फिर कुछ कह डालिए। क्रोध रोककर असह्य दुःख मत सहिए। आप वीरता का व्रत धारण करने वाले, धैर्यवान और क्षोभरहित हैं। गाली देते शोभा नहीं पाते ॥
english_translation: If that still does not satisfy you, say more. Do not swallow unbearable pain by holding back anger. You are vowed to heroic conduct, steady and unshaken. Insults do not suit you.
essence: Heroic steadiness does not need insults to prove itself.
simple_meaning: Lakshman tells the sage to speak plainly if he is still unhappy, but not to endure terrible pain by suppressing anger. A heroic person should stay steady, not answer with abuse.
insight: It teaches you to hold firm without collapsing into either silence or abuse.
modern_relevance: Someone keeps provoking you in a group chat, and you feel the heat rising in your chest. The verse points to a harder choice: stay composed, but do not confuse dignity with self-erasure.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: सूर समर करनी करहिं कहि न जनावहिं आपु। बिद्यमान रन पाइ रिपु कायर कथहिं प्रतापु ॥
translation: शूरवीर तो युद्ध में करनी (शूरवीरता का कार्य) करते हैं, कहकर अपने को नहीं जनाते। शत्रु को युद्ध में उपस्थित पाकर कायर ही अपने प्रताप की डींग मारा करते हैं ॥
english_translation: The brave do their work in battle and do not advertise themselves. The cowardly, when they meet an enemy face to face, boast of their own valor.
essence: Bravery proves itself in action, not in claims.
simple_meaning: Real courage shows itself through action, not self-praise. Only cowards talk about their greatness when an enemy is right there.
insight: It shifts attention from self-promotion to visible action under pressure.
modern_relevance: A colleague keeps talking about how indispensable they are, right when the actual crisis is in front of everyone. The people who matter are already fixing the problem.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तुम्ह तौ कालु हाँक जनु लावा। बार बार मोहि लागि बोलावा॥ सुनत लखन के बचन कठोरा। परसु सुधारि धरेउ कर घोरा ॥
translation: आप तो मानो काल को हाँक लगाकर बार-बार उसे मेरे लिए बुलाते हैं। लक्ष्मणजी के कठोर वचन सुनते ही परशुरामजी ने अपने भयानक फरसे को सुधारकर हाथ में ले लिया ॥
english_translation: You seem to be summoning Death itself again and again for me. Hearing Lakshman's harsh words, Parashurama adjusted his terrible axe and took it in hand.
essence: Pride hears insult and reaches for force.
simple_meaning: Parashurama feels Lakshman's words are so sharp they are like calling death itself. He immediately grips his axe, ready to respond.
insight: It shows how quickly pride can convert words into confrontation.
modern_relevance: One cutting sentence in a family argument can change the whole room. A voice rises, hands clench, and suddenly everyone can feel the danger in the air.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: अब जनि देइ दोसु मोहि लोगू। कटुबादी बालकु बधजोगू॥ बाल बिलोकि बहुत मैं बाँचा। अब यहु मरनिहार भा साँचा ॥
translation: (और बोले-) अब लोग मुझे दोष न दें। यह कडुआ बोलने वाला बालक मारे जाने के ही योग्य है। इसे बालक देखकर मैंने बहुत बचाया, पर अब यह सचमुच मरने को ही आ गया है ॥
english_translation: “Do not let people blame me now. This sharp-tongued boy deserves death. I spared him because he was only a child, but now he has truly become fit to die.”
essence: Anger always finds a reason once pride feels insulted.
simple_meaning: Parashurama says he should not be blamed for wanting to kill Lakshman, because Lakshman has spoken harshly and now seems truly deserving of death.
insight: It shows how wounded pride turns into moral justification, making anger feel righteous.
modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in a meeting, then smirks like nothing happened. You feel the heat rise and start building a case in your head for why they deserve a harsh reply.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: कौसिक कहा छमिअ अपराधू। बाल दोष गुन गनहिं न साधू॥ खर कुठार मैं अकरुन कोही। आगें अपराधी गुरुद्रोही ॥
translation: विश्वामित्रजी ने कहा- अपराध क्षमा कीजिए। बालकों के दोष और गुण को साधु लोग नहीं गिनते। (परशुरामजी बोले-) तीखी धार का कुठार, मैं दयारहित और क्रोधी और यह गुरुद्रोही और अपराधी मेरे सामने- ॥
english_translation: Kausika said, “Forgive the offense. Noble people do not count the faults and merits of a child.” Parashurama said, “My sharp axe, I am merciless and angry; before me stands a culprit and a betrayer of his teacher.”
essence: Anger turns a child into a criminal.
simple_meaning: Visvamitra asks for forgiveness and says noble people do not judge a child by faults. Parashurama answers with anger, calling himself fierce and the boy guilty.
insight: It shows how perception changes with temper: the same person can be seen as a child or as a threat.
modern_relevance: A teenager snaps back in a family argument, and the room instantly shrinks into blame. One person sees a child; another sees an offense. The verse captures how anger turns a moment into a verdict.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: उतर देत छोड़उँ बिनु मारें। केवल कौसिक सील तुम्हारें॥ न त एहि काटि कुठार कठोरें। गुरहि उरिन होतेउँ श्रम थोरें ॥
translation: उत्तर दे रहा है। इतने पर भी मैं इसे बिना मारे छोड़ रहा हूँ, सो हे विश्वामित्र! केवल तुम्हारे शील (प्रेम) से। नहीं तो इसे इस कठोर कुठार से काटकर थोड़े ही परिश्रम से गुरु से उऋण हो जाता ॥
english_translation: I am answering. Even so, I am leaving him alive without killing him, only because of your gentleness, O Vishvamitra. Otherwise, I would have cut him down with this hard axe and repaid my teacher with little effort.
essence: Strength proves itself by not striking.
simple_meaning: Parashurama says he is sparing the boy only out of respect for Vishvamitra. He claims he could have killed him easily and still settled his debt to his teacher.
insight: It teaches restraint under anger: even justified power can be held back by reverence.
modern_relevance: You’re furious in a meeting and ready to humiliate someone back. Then a senior person’s presence or a deeper respect stops you. The strongest response is sometimes the one you do not use.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: गाधिसूनु कह हृदयँ हँसि मुनिहि हरिअरइ सूझ। अयमय खाँड़ न ऊखमय अजहुँ न बूझ अबूझ ॥
translation: विश्वामित्रजी ने हृदय में हँसकर कहा- मुनि को हरा ही हरा सूझ रहा है (अर्थात सर्वत्र विजयी होने के कारण ये श्री राम-लक्ष्मण को भी साधारण क्षत्रिय ही समझ रहे हैं), किन्तु यह लोहमयी (केवल फौलाद की बनी हुई) खाँड़ (खाँड़ा-खड्ग) है, ऊख की (रस की) खाँड़ नहीं है (जो मुँह में लेते ही गल जाए। खेद है,) मुनि अब भी बेसमझ बने हुए हैं, इनके प्रभाव को नहीं समझ रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Gadhi's son smiled inwardly: the sage sees only green everywhere. This is an iron blade, not a sugar blade; even now he does not understand.
essence: What looks harmless may be far harder than it seems.
simple_meaning: विश्वामित्र मन ही मन सोचते हैं कि परशुराम राम-लक्ष्मण की असली शक्ति नहीं समझ रहे। वे उन्हें साधारण मान रहे हैं, जबकि सामने लोहे जैसी कठोर शक्ति है, कोई मीठी चीज़ नहीं।
insight: It shifts the mind from surface appearance to hidden force.
modern_relevance: You dismiss the quiet person in the room, assuming they will fold. Then they speak once, cleanly, and the whole atmosphere changes.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहेउ लखन मुनि सीलु तुम्हारा। को नहिं जान बिदित संसारा॥ माता पितहि उरिन भए नीकें। गुर रिनु रहा सोचु बड़ जीकें ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी ने कहा- हे मुनि! आपके शील को कौन नहीं जानता? वह संसार भर में प्रसिद्ध है। आप माता-पिता से तो अच्छी तरह उऋण हो ही गए, अब गुरु का ऋण रहा, जिसका जी में बड़ा सोच लगा है ॥
english_translation: Lakshman said, "O sage, everyone in the world knows your noble conduct. You have already repaid your debt to mother and father. Only the guru's debt remains, and that weighs heavily on my heart."
essence: Honor is incomplete until the remaining debt is repaid.
simple_meaning: Lakshman praises the sage's character and says the sage has already settled his debts to his parents. Only the teacher's debt remains, and that still troubles him.
insight: It shifts attention from public praise to the unfinished obligation that still needs care.
modern_relevance: You’ve cleared your parents’ calls, your deadlines, your obligations — but one promise still sits in the back of your mind. Until that’s handled, you feel it.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: सो जनु हमरेहि माथे काढ़ा। दिन चलि गए ब्याज बड़ बाढ़ा॥ अब आनिअ ब्यवहरिआ बोली। तुरत देउँ मैं थैली खोली ॥
translation: वह मानो हमारे ही मत्थे काढ़ा था। बहुत दिन बीत गए, इससे ब्याज भी बहुत बढ़ गया होगा। अब किसी हिसाब करने वाले को बुला लाइए, तो मैं तुरंत थैली खोलकर दे दूँ ॥
english_translation: It was as if he had been set on our own head. So much time has passed that the interest has grown greatly. Now call a moneylender, and I will open my bag at once.
essence: Bold wit can puncture pride before force is needed.
simple_meaning: Lakshman says the burden has sat on their heads for a long time, so the debt has grown huge. He asks for someone to settle accounts and says he will pay immediately.
insight: It shows how fearless speech can cut through intimidation and shift the balance of power.
modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a group chat, acting as if you owe them obedience. You answer calmly, with enough edge to expose the bluff without losing your footing.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: सुनि कटु बचन कुठार सुधारा। हाय हाय सब सभा पुकारा॥ भृगुबर परसु देखावहु मोही। बिप्र बिचारि बचउँ नृपदोही ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी के कडुए वचन सुनकर परशुरामजी ने कुठार सम्हाला। सारी सभा हाय-हाय! करके पुकार उठी। (लक्ष्मणजी ने कहा-) हे भृगुश्रेष्ठ! आप मुझे फरसा दिखा रहे हैं? पर हे राजाओं के शत्रु! मैं ब्राह्मण समझकर बचा रहा हूँ (तरह दे रहा हूँ) ॥
english_translation: Hearing the bitter words, Parashurama raised his axe. The whole assembly cried out, “Alas, alas!” “O best of the Bhargavas, you show me your axe? But I spare you only because you are a Brahmin, O enemy of kings.”
essence: One sharp word can turn a public gathering into a crisis.
simple_meaning: Parashurama lifts his axe after Lakshman’s sharp words, and the crowd panics. Lakshman answers with a taunt, saying he is being spared only because he is a Brahmin.
insight: It shows how a single insult can escalate a whole room, and how status can become a weapon.
modern_relevance: A tense group chat turns into a live wire after one cutting reply. Everyone can feel the room tighten before anyone even types again.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: मिले न कबहुँ सुभट रन गाढ़े। द्विज देवता घरहि के बा़ढ़े॥ अनुचित कहि सब लोग पुकारे। रघुपति सयनहिं लखनु नेवारे ॥
translation: आपको कभी रणधीर बलवान् वीर नहीं मिले हैं। हे ब्राह्मण देवता ! आप घर ही में बड़े हैं। यह सुनकर 'अनुचित है, अनुचित है' कहकर सब लोग पुकार उठे। तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने इशारे से लक्ष्मणजी को रोक दिया ॥
english_translation: You have never met a true warrior in battle. You have grown up only at home, Brahmin deity. Hearing this, everyone cried out, "This is improper!" Then Lord Raghunath signaled Lakshman to stop.
essence: A heated exchange ends when Ram restrains Lakshman before pride can spread.
simple_meaning: Lakshman taunts Parashurama, saying he has only grown strong at home, not in battle. The assembly protests, and Ram quietly stops Lakshman from continuing.
insight: It teaches restraint in the middle of provocation, especially when pride could escalate conflict.
modern_relevance: A group chat is heating up, and one reply could humiliate everyone. You type it anyway, then catch yourself. The wiser move is the one that prevents the room from breaking.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: लखन उतर आहुति सरिस भृगुबर कोपु कृसानु। बढ़त देखि जल सम बचन बोले रघुकुलभानु ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी के उत्तर से, जो आहुति के समान थे, परशुरामजी के क्रोध रूपी अग्नि को बढ़ते देखकर रघुकुल के सूर्य श्री रामचंद्रजी जल के समान (शांत करने वाले) वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: Seeing Parashurama's anger rise, Ram of the Raghu line spoke words that were cooling like water.
essence: Cooling words can stop a blaze of anger.
simple_meaning: Ram responds to rising anger with calming words. He does not meet fire with fire.
insight: It teaches you to interrupt escalation with restraint and soothing speech.
modern_relevance: A group chat is spiraling after one rude message, and everyone is ready to strike back. One calm reply can stop the whole fire before it spreads.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ करहु बालक पर छोहु। सूध दूधमुख करिअ न कोहू॥ जौं पै प्रभु प्रभाउ कछु जाना। तौ कि बराबरि करत अयाना ॥
translation: हे नाथ ! बालक पर कृपा कीजिए। इस सीधे और दूधमुँहे बच्चे पर क्रोध न कीजिए। यदि यह प्रभु का (आपका) कुछ भी प्रभाव जानता, तो क्या यह बेसमझ आपकी बराबरी करता ? ॥
english_translation: O Lord, show kindness to the child. Do not be angry with this simple, milk-mouthed boy. If he knew even a little of your power, would this fool dare compare himself with you?
essence: Power should answer childish provocation with mercy, not force.
simple_meaning: Lakshman asks Parashurama to spare the boy and not stay angry. He says the child is innocent and foolish enough not to understand Parashurama's greatness.
insight: It shifts the response from punishment to proportion, reminding you to read immaturity before reacting to insult.
modern_relevance: A teenager snaps in a family argument, and the room heats up fast. Someone older steps in and says, 'He doesn't know what he's doing.' That pause can save the whole relationship.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: जौं लरिका कछु अचगरि करहीं। गुर पितु मातु मोद मन भरहीं॥ करिअ कृपा सिसु सेवक जानी। तुम्ह सम सील धीर मुनि ग्यानी ॥
translation: बालक यदि कुछ चपलता भी करते हैं, तो गुरु, पिता और माता मन में आनंद से भर जाते हैं। अतः इसे छोटा बच्चा और सेवक जानकर कृपा कीजिए। आप तो समदर्शी, सुशील, धीर और ज्ञानी मुनि हैं ॥
english_translation: If children show a little mischief, teachers, fathers, and mothers are filled with joy. So please show mercy, knowing him as a child and servant. You are a sage—equal-minded, virtuous, patient, and wise.
essence: Mercy grows when strength sees innocence.
simple_meaning: Children’s small mischief can delight the adults who care for them. Ram asks Parashurama to show mercy, seeing the boy as a child and servant, while honoring Parashurama’s calm wisdom.
insight: It shifts the response from punishment to compassionate understanding, especially when someone is immature or reactive.
modern_relevance: A teenager snaps back in a family argument, and the room tightens. The most powerful response is not to escalate, but to remember the person in front of you is still learning.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: राम बचन सुनि कछुक जुड़ाने। कहि कछु लखनु बहुरि मुसुकाने॥ हँसत देखि नख सिख रिस ब्यापी। राम तोर भ्राता बड़ पापी ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी के वचन सुनकर वे कुछ ठंडे पड़े। इतने में लक्ष्मणजी कुछ कहकर फिर मुस्कुरा दिए। उनको हँसते देखकर परशुरामजी के नख से शिखा तक (सारे शरीर में) क्रोध छा गया। उन्होंने कहा- हे राम! तेरा भाई बड़ा पापी है ॥
english_translation: Hearing Ram's words, he calmed somewhat. Then Lakshman said something and smiled again. Seeing him laugh, anger spread through Parashuram from head to toe. He said, “Ram, your brother is very sinful.”
essence: A single smile can bring anger roaring back.
simple_meaning: Ram speaks, Lakshman smiles, and Parashuram's anger flares again. The scene turns from brief calm to open insult.
insight: It shows how fragile peace is when pride is still active. One mocking response can reignite the whole conflict.
modern_relevance: You finally calm a tense room, then one sarcastic grin undoes everything. A tiny reaction can revive an argument everyone thought was settling.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गौर सरीर स्याम मन माहीं। कालकूट मुख पयमुख नाहीं॥ सहज टेढ़ अनुहरइ न तोही। नीचु मीचु सम देख न मोही ॥
translation: यह शरीर से गोरा, पर हृदय का बड़ा काला है। यह विषमुख है, दूधमुँहा नहीं। स्वभाव ही टेढ़ा है, तेरा अनुसरण नहीं करता (तेरे जैसा शीलवान नहीं है)। यह नीच मुझे काल के समान नहीं देखता ॥
english_translation: This body is fair, but the mind is dark. It has a poison mouth, not a milk mouth. Its nature is crooked, and it does not follow you. It does not see me, lowly and mortal, as death itself.
essence: Anger makes the mind crooked and the other person look monstrous.
simple_meaning: Parashurama is insulting Lakshman, saying his appearance is fair but his mind is harsh and crooked. He sees Lakshman as disrespectful and dangerous.
insight: It shows how anger projects darkness onto others and blinds the speaker to reality.
modern_relevance: You read a sharp text at midnight and decide the other person is cruel. The mind fills in poison before it checks the facts.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: लखन कहेउ हँसि सुनहु मुनि क्रोधु पाप कर मूल। जेहि बस जन अनुचित करहिं चरहिं बिस्व प्रतिकूल ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी ने हँसकर कहा- हे मुनि! सुनिए, क्रोध पाप का मूल है, जिसके वश में होकर मनुष्य अनुचित कर्म कर बैठते हैं और विश्वभर के प्रतिकूल चलते (सबका अहित करते) हैं ॥
english_translation: Lakshman said with a smile, "Listen, sage: anger is the root of wrongdoing. Under its control, people do what is improper and act against the whole world."
essence: Anger is the first wrong move; everything else follows it.
simple_meaning: Anger is the source of bad actions. Once anger takes control, people do things that hurt others and go against what is right.
insight: It shifts attention from the outer conflict to the inner trigger, so restraint begins earlier.
modern_relevance: You are one sharp reply away from ruining a family dinner, a team chat, or a friendship. Lakshman names the moment before damage becomes irreversible.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: मैं तुम्हार अनुचर मुनिराया। परिहरि कोपु करिअ अब दाया॥ टूट चाप नहिं जुरिहि रिसाने। बैठिअ होइहिं पाय पिराने ॥
translation: हे मुनिराज! मैं आपका दास हूँ। अब क्रोध त्यागकर दया कीजिए। टूटा हुआ धनुष क्रोध करने से जुड़ नहीं जाएगा। खड़े-खड़े पैर दुःखने लगे होंगे, बैठ जाइए ॥
english_translation: O great sage, I am your servant. Now leave anger and show mercy. A broken bow will not be mended by rage. Sit down; your feet must be aching from standing.
essence: Anger cannot repair what only skill and calm can mend.
simple_meaning: Lakshman speaks respectfully to the sage and asks him to stop being angry. He says anger will not fix the broken bow, and the sage should sit down if standing is tiring.
insight: It shifts the mind from reacting with force to responding with calm usefulness.
modern_relevance: A meeting is going sideways, and one person keeps escalating the room. Lakshman’s words cut through the heat: anger does not repair what already broke.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: जौं अति प्रिय तौ करिअ उपाई। जोरिअ कोउ बड़ गुनी बोलाई॥ बोलत लखनहिं जनकु डेराहीं। मष्ट करहु अनुचित भल नाहीं ॥
translation: यदि धनुष अत्यन्त ही प्रिय हो, तो कोई उपाय किया जाए और किसी बड़े गुणी (कारीगर) को बुलाकर जुड़वा दिया जाए। लक्ष्मणजी के बोलने से जनकजी डर जाते हैं और कहते हैं- बस, चुप रहिए, अनुचित बोलना अच्छा नहीं ॥
english_translation: If the bow is very dear, then have it repaired. Call a skilled craftsman to join it again. Janaka grows afraid at Lakshmana's words and says, "Enough—do not speak improperly."
essence: A wise response can calm anger before it becomes damage.
simple_meaning: Janaka tries to defuse Lakshmana's sharp words by suggesting the bow could simply be repaired. He then asks him to stop speaking in a way that feels improper.
insight: It teaches you to interrupt escalation and return the exchange to a workable level.
modern_relevance: Someone makes a cutting remark in a family meeting, and the room tightens instantly. You can feel the urge to answer harder, but the wiser move is to slow the spiral before it becomes a fight.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: थर थर काँपहिं पुर नर नारी। छोट कुमार खोट बड़ भारी॥ भृगुपति सुनि सुनि निरभय बानी। रिस तन जरइ होई बल हानी ॥
translation: जनकपुर के स्त्री-पुरुष थर-थर काँप रहे हैं (और मन ही मन कह रहे हैं कि) छोटा कुमार बड़ा ही खोटा है। लक्ष्मणजी की निर्भय वाणी सुन-सुनकर परशुरामजी का शरीर क्रोध से जला जा रहा है और उनके बल की हानि हो रही है (उनका बल घट रहा है) ॥
english_translation: The people of Janakpur trembled. They called the young prince deeply rude. Hearing Lakshman's fearless words again and again, Parashurama burned with rage and his strength began to fail.
essence: Rage looks powerful, but it burns away its own strength.
simple_meaning: The people of Janakpur are frightened by Lakshman's bold words. Parashurama's anger keeps rising, and that anger weakens him.
insight: It shifts attention from the force of angry speech to the self-damage anger creates.
modern_relevance: A family dinner turns silent after one cutting remark. Everyone feels the temperature drop, and the angriest person in the room is also the one losing control fastest.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बोले रामहि देइ निहोरा। बचउँ बिचारि बंधु लघु तोरा॥ मनु मलीन तनु सुंदर कैसें। बिष रस भरा कनक घटु जैसें ॥
translation: तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी पर एहसान जनाकर परशुरामजी बोले- तेरा छोटा भाई समझकर मैं इसे बचा रहा हूँ। यह मन का मैला और शरीर का कैसा सुंदर है, जैसे विष के रस से भरा हुआ सोने का घड़ा! ॥
english_translation: Parashurama said, "I grant this favor to Ram: I spare you because you are your younger brother. How can a mind be impure and a body beautiful? It is like a golden pot filled with poison."
essence: A beautiful exterior means nothing when the mind is poisoned.
simple_meaning: Parashurama says he is sparing Lakshman because Ram is his elder brother. Then he insults Lakshman, saying a beautiful body means nothing if the mind is corrupt.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance to character, warning that beauty without inner purity is fragile and misleading.
modern_relevance: Someone looks polished in a meeting, speaks smoothly, and still leaves a sour feeling behind. The verse cuts through appearances: a refined exterior cannot cover a bitter, reckless mind.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: सुनि लछिमन बिहसे बहुरि नयन तरेरे राम। गुर समीप गवने सकुचि परिहरि बानी बाम ॥
translation: यह सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी फिर हँसे। तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने तिरछी नजर से उनकी ओर देखा, जिससे लक्ष्मणजी सकुचाकर, विपरीत बोलना छोड़कर, गुरुजी के पास चले गए ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Lakshman laughed again. Then Ram gave him a sidelong look, and Lakshman, embarrassed, stopped speaking harshly and went near the teacher.
essence: Ram's glance is enough to turn pride into restraint.
simple_meaning: Lakshman laughs again, Ram silences him with a look, and Lakshman stops his sharp words and returns to the teacher.
insight: It shows how restraint can restore order faster than argument.
modern_relevance: You make a cutting joke in a tense room, and one calm look from someone you respect tells you to stop. No speech is needed; the correction lands instantly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अति बिनीत मृदु सीतल बानी। बोले रामु जोरि जुग पानी॥ सुनहु नाथ तुम्ह सहज सुजाना। बालक बचनु करिअ नहिं काना ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी दोनों हाथ जोड़कर अत्यन्त विनय के साथ कोमल और शीतल वाणी बोले- हे नाथ! सुनिए, आप तो स्वभाव से ही सुजान हैं। आप बालक के वचन पर कान न दीजिए (उसे सुना-अनसुना कर दीजिए) ॥
english_translation: With extreme humility, soft and cooling words, Rama spoke with both hands joined: "Listen, lord, you are naturally wise. Do not heed a child's words."
essence: Gentleness can disarm anger before it grows teeth.
simple_meaning: Rama speaks with humility and asks the elder to ignore a child's harsh words.
insight: It teaches restraint before reaction, using humility to defuse conflict.
modern_relevance: Someone snaps at you in a group chat, and every instinct says to clap back. Instead, you answer softly, lower the temperature, and refuse to let one sharp remark become a bigger fire.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: बररै बालकु एकु सुभाऊ। इन्हहि न संत बिदूषहिं काऊ ॥ तेहिं नाहीं कछु काज बिगारा। अपराधी मैं नाथ तुम्हारा ॥
translation: बर्रै और बालक का एक स्वभाव है। संतजन इन्हें कभी दोष नहीं लगाते। फिर उसने (लक्ष्मण ने) तो कुछ काम भी नहीं बिगाड़ा है, हे नाथ! आपका अपराधी तो मैं हूँ ॥
english_translation: A child and a wild horse share one nature. The wise never blame them. He has ruined nothing, O Lord. I alone am at fault.
essence: Real strength takes responsibility before it takes offense.
simple_meaning: Ram says Lakshman is only acting like a child and has done no real harm. The fault is his alone.
insight: It shifts you from defending ego to absorbing blame for the sake of harmony.
modern_relevance: A younger sibling snaps at dinner, and the room tightens. Instead of escalating it, someone wiser lowers the heat, protects the vulnerable one, and takes responsibility for peace.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कृपा कोपु बधु बँधब गोसाईं। मो पर करिअ दास की नाईं॥ कहिअ बेगि जेहि बिधि रिस जाई। मुनिनायक सोइ करौं उपाई ॥
translation: अतः हे स्वामी! कृपा, क्रोध, वध और बंधन, जो कुछ करना हो, दास की तरह (अर्थात दास समझकर) मुझ पर कीजिए। जिस प्रकार से शीघ्र आपका क्रोध दूर हो। हे मुनिराज! बताइए, मैं वही उपाय करूँ ॥
english_translation: O master, do whatever you wish—grace, anger, punishment, or bondage. Treat me like a servant. Tell me quickly how your anger may be removed, and I will do that remedy, O sage.
essence: Humility asks for correction before asking for pardon.
simple_meaning: Ram offers himself completely to the sage, even accepting punishment, and asks for the quickest way to remove the sage's anger.
insight: It teaches you to prioritize repair over self-protection when conflict has already begun.
modern_relevance: A meeting goes sideways, and you know your tone made it worse. Before defending yourself, you ask what would repair the damage.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कह मुनि राम जाइ रिस कैसें। अजहुँ अनुज तव चितव अनैसें॥ एहि कें कंठ कुठारु न दीन्हा। तौ मैं कहा कोपु करि कीन्हा ॥
translation: मुनि ने कहा- हे राम! क्रोध कैसे जाए, अब भी तेरा छोटा भाई टेढ़ा ही ताक रहा है। इसकी गर्दन पर मैंने कुठार न चलाया, तो क्रोध करके किया ही क्या? ॥
english_translation: The sage said, "How can anger leave when your younger brother still looks at me so crookedly? If I did not strike off his head, what did I accomplish by being angry?"
essence: Anger survives as long as pride still wants a wound repaid.
simple_meaning: The sage says his anger cannot calm down because Lakshman is still glaring at him. He feels that if he did not retaliate, his anger had no real force behind it.
insight: It exposes how pride feeds anger, and how retaliation becomes the ego’s proof of power.
modern_relevance: You replay a rude reply in your head long after the conversation ends. The body wants payback, not peace. Until the insult loses its grip, anger keeps finding reasons to stay.
speaker: Muni

verse_text: गर्भ स्रवहिं अवनिप रवनि सुनि कुठार गति घोर। परसु अछत देखउँ जिअत बैरी भूपकिसोर ॥
translation: मेरे जिस कुठार की घोर करनी सुनकर राजाओं की स्त्रियों के गर्भ गिर पड़ते हैं, उसी फरसे के रहते मैं इस शत्रु राजपुत्र को जीवित देख रहा हूँ ॥
english_translation: The cruel force of my axe is such that, hearing of it, queens miscarry. Yet with that axe in hand, I still see this enemy prince alive.
essence: Raw power becomes humiliation when it cannot control the moment.
simple_meaning: The speaker says his axe is so feared that even hearing of it makes queens miscarry, yet this enemy prince still lives in front of him.
insight: It shows how wounded ego reacts when its force meets resistance it cannot instantly break.
modern_relevance: You bring every argument, every fact, every sharp line you have prepared — and still the other person stands there unchanged. That helplessness can turn power into rage.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: बहइ न हाथु दहइ रिस छाती। भा कुठारु कुंठित नृपघाती॥ भयउ बाम बिधि फिरेउ सुभाऊ। मोरे हृदयँ कृपा कसि काऊ ॥
translation: हाथ चलता नहीं, क्रोध से छाती जली जाती है। (हाय!) राजाओं का घातक यह कुठार भी कुण्ठित हो गया। विधाता विपरीत हो गया, इससे मेरा स्वभाव बदल गया, नहीं तो भला, मेरे हृदय में किसी समय भी कृपा कैसी? ॥
english_translation: My hand will not strike, and anger burns my chest. This king-slayer's axe has become dull. Fate has turned against me, and my nature has changed; otherwise, how could compassion ever live in my heart?
essence: Violence weakens when compassion unexpectedly enters the heart.
simple_meaning: Parashurama admits his hand cannot strike, his anger is burning, and even his axe has lost its force. He blames adverse fate for changing his nature and making compassion arise in him.
insight: It shows how anger can be exposed as unstable the moment it meets a stronger presence.
modern_relevance: You are ready to lash out in a group chat, then notice your fingers hovering over the screen. The heat is still there, but the impulse to strike has lost its power.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: आजु दया दुखु दुसह सहावा। सुनि सौमित्रि बिहसि सिरु नावा॥ बाउ कृपा मूरति अनुकूला। बोलत बचन झरत जनु फूला ॥
translation: आज दया मुझे यह दुःसह दुःख सहा रही है। यह सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी ने मुस्कुराकर सिर नवाया (और कहा-) आपकी कृपा रूपी वायु भी आपकी मूर्ति के अनुकूल ही है, वचन बोलते हैं, मानो फूल झड़ रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Today, compassion has made me bear unbearable pain. Hearing this, Lakshman smiled and bowed his head. Your grace, like the wind, is always in harmony with your form. Your words fall like flowers.
essence: Grace can meet anger without losing its softness.
simple_meaning: Parashurama says that compassion has made him suffer unbearable pain. Lakshman responds with calm respect, praising the gentleness in his words.
insight: It teaches you to answer hostility with composed respect instead of reflexive anger.
modern_relevance: Someone snaps at you in a meeting, and you answer without matching their heat. The room changes before anyone notices — not because you won, but because you stayed gentle.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: जौं पै कृपाँ जरिहिं मुनि गाता। क्रोध भएँ तनु राख बिधाता॥ देखु जनक हठि बालकु एहू। कीन्ह चहत जड़ जमपुर गेहू ॥
translation: हे मुनि ! यदि कृपा करने से आपका शरीर जला जाता है, तो क्रोध होने पर तो शरीर की रक्षा विधाता ही करेंगे। (परशुरामजी ने कहा-) हे जनक! देख, यह मूर्ख बालक हठ करके यमपुरी में घर (निवास) करना चाहता है ॥
english_translation: O sage, if kindness can burn your body, then anger can surely protect it by the Creator's will. Look, Janak, this stubborn boy wants to make his home in the city of death.
essence: Anger sees defiance as disaster.
simple_meaning: Parashurama mocks the boy's stubbornness and warns Janak that this child is inviting death by his arrogance.
insight: It shows how anger quickly turns into contempt and how contempt inflates a small conflict into a life-or-death challenge.
modern_relevance: A senior in the room dismisses a younger person's confidence as arrogance. The atmosphere tightens before anyone even speaks back.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: बेगि करहु किन आँखिन्ह ओटा। देखत छोट खोट नृपु ढोटा॥ बिहसे लखनु कहा मन माहीं। मूदें आँखि कतहुँ कोउ नाहीं ॥
translation: इसको शीघ्र ही आँखों की ओट क्यों नहीं करते? यह राजपुत्र देखने में छोटा है, पर है बड़ा खोटा। लक्ष्मणजी ने हँसकर मन ही मन कहा- आँख मूँद लेने पर कहीं कोई नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Why not quickly move him out of sight? He looks small, but he is very wicked. Lakshman smiled and thought to himself, "If eyes are closed, nowhere is anyone seen."
essence: A closed mind sees no one; Lakshman answers insult with inward ease.
simple_meaning: Parashuram wants the boy removed from sight, calling him small but deceitful. Lakshman quietly thinks that if the eyes are shut, nothing is seen anywhere.
insight: It shows how to keep inner ease when another person tries to provoke shame or fear.
modern_relevance: Someone snaps at a teenager in front of a crowd, expecting fear. Instead, the teenager stays inwardly amused, untouched by the glare. That calm humor can be stronger than a fight.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परसुरामु तब राम प्रति बोले उर अति क्रोधु। संभु सरासनु तोरि सठ करसि हमार प्रबोधु ॥
translation: तब परशुरामजी हृदय में अत्यन्त क्रोध भरकर श्री रामजी से बोले- अरे शठ! तू शिवजी का धनुष तोड़कर उलटा हमीं को ज्ञान सिखाता है ॥
english_translation: Then Parashurama, filled with intense anger in his heart, said to Ram: "You fool, you broke Shiva's bow and now you are trying to instruct me!"
essence: Pride hears insult where wisdom is being offered.
simple_meaning: Parashurama, furious, accuses Ram of breaking Shiva's bow and then lecturing him.
insight: It shows how ego turns guidance into offense and blocks clear seeing.
modern_relevance: Someone corrects you in front of others, and your chest tightens before you even hear the words. In that second, pride turns a simple moment into a fight.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: बंधु कहइ कटु संमत तोरें। तू छल बिनय करसि कर जोरें॥ करु परितोषु मोर संग्रामा। नाहिं त छाड़ कहाउब रामा ॥
translation: तेरा यह भाई तेरी ही सम्मति से कटु वचन बोलता है और तू छल से हाथ जोड़कर विनय करता है। या तो युद्ध में मेरा संतोष कर, नहीं तो राम कहलाना छोड़ दे ॥
english_translation: Your brother speaks harsh words with your approval. You fold your hands and speak with deceit. Satisfy me in battle, or stop calling yourself Ram.
essence: Pride sees deceit where humility stands.
simple_meaning: Parashurama accuses Ram of hidden disrespect. He demands either a real fight or that Ram stop claiming his name.
insight: It shows how wounded pride turns every gesture into suspicion and demands a public test of worth.
modern_relevance: A senior keeps pressing you after you apologize politely, convinced your calm tone is fake. The room tightens because the issue is no longer the mistake — it is whether your sincerity will be believed.
speaker: Parashurama

verse_text: छलु तजि करहि समरु सिवद्रोही। बंधु सहित न त मारउँ तोही॥ भृगुपति बकहिं कुठार उठाएँ। मन मुसुकाहिं रामु सिर नाएँ ॥
translation: अरे शिवद्रोही! छल त्यागकर मुझसे युद्ध कर। नहीं तो भाई सहित तुझे मार डालूँगा। इस प्रकार परशुरामजी कुठार उठाए बक रहे हैं और श्री रामचन्द्रजी सिर झुकाए मन ही मन मुस्कुरा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: “O enemy of Shiva, give up deceit and fight me in battle. Otherwise I will kill you along with your brother.” Thus Parashurama raised his axe and spoke harshly, while Ram Chandr bowed his head and smiled inwardly.
essence: True strength stays calm while pride rages.
simple_meaning: Parashurama, still furious, demands honest combat and threatens to kill Ram and Lakshman. Ram stays calm, bows respectfully, and smiles inwardly.
insight: It teaches you to hold your center when anger demands a reaction.
modern_relevance: Someone is shouting in the meeting, trying to provoke you into matching their heat. You stay quiet, respectful, and untouched. That restraint changes the whole room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गुनह लखन कर हम पर रोषू। कतहुँ सुधाइहु ते बड़ दोषू॥ टेढ़ जानि सब बंदइ काहू। बक्र चंद्रमहि ग्रसइ न राहू ॥
translation: (श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने मन ही मन कहा-) गुनाह (दोष) तो लक्ष्मण का और क्रोध मुझ पर करते हैं। कहीं-कहीं सीधेपन में भी बड़ा दोष होता है। टेढ़ा जानकर सब लोग किसी की भी वंदना करते हैं, टेढ़े चन्द्रमा को राहु भी नहीं ग्रसता ॥
english_translation: Laxmana is at fault, yet people blame me. Straightness itself can become a great flaw. Everyone bows to what is bent; even Rahu does not swallow the curved moon.
essence: Even truth needs flexibility to be received.
simple_meaning: Ram says that people often blame him for Laxmana's fault. He adds that being too straight can itself be a weakness, while the world often bows to what is bent or flexible.
insight: It shifts the mind from rigid self-assertion to strategic humility and social intelligence.
modern_relevance: You keep insisting on being perfectly direct in a tense family argument, and the room only hardens. Sometimes the person who bends slightly keeps the whole relationship from breaking.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: राम कहेउ रिस तजिअ मुनीसा। कर कुठारु आगें यह सीसा॥ जेहिं रिस जाइ करिअ सोइ स्वामी। मोहि जानिअ आपन अनुगामी ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने (प्रकट) कहा- हे मुनीश्वर! क्रोध छोड़िए। आपके हाथ में कुठार है और मेरा यह सिर आगे है, जिस प्रकार आपका क्रोध जाए, हे स्वामी! वही कीजिए। मुझे अपना अनुचर (दास) जानिए ॥
english_translation: Rama said, 'O sage, give up anger. My head is before your axe. Let your anger go as it will, lord. Know me as your servant.'
essence: True authority can offer itself before force.
simple_meaning: Rama asks the sage to drop his anger and do what he must, while placing himself completely in the sage's hands as a servant.
insight: It teaches you to absorb hostility without mirroring it, turning confrontation into restraint.
modern_relevance: Someone is ready to explode in a family argument, and you choose the harder move: lowering your voice, taking responsibility, and refusing to escalate the room.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: प्रभुहि सेवकहि समरु कस तजहु बिप्रबर रोसु। बेषु बिलोकें कहेसि कछु बालकहू नहिं दोसु ॥
translation: स्वामी और सेवक में युद्ध कैसा? हे ब्राह्मण श्रेष्ठ! क्रोध का त्याग कीजिए। आपका (वीरों का सा) वेष देखकर ही बालक ने कुछ कह डाला था, वास्तव में उसका भी कोई दोष नहीं है ॥
english_translation: What war can there be between a master and a servant? O best of brahmins, give up anger. Seeing your warrior-like appearance, the boy said something; he too is not at fault.
essence: Real authority does not need to turn anger into punishment.
simple_meaning: A master and servant should not treat each other as enemies. The boy reacted to the priest’s warrior-like appearance, so the priest should let go of anger.
insight: It shifts the mind from punishment to understanding the cause of reaction.
modern_relevance: A teacher snaps at a student for speaking too quickly, but the student was only reacting to the teacher’s harsh tone. This verse asks you to lower the temperature before you assign blame.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि कुठार बान धनु धारी। भै लरिकहि रिस बीरु बिचारी॥ नामु जान पै तुम्हहि न चीन्हा। बंस सुभायँ उतरु तेहिं दीन्हा ॥
translation: आपको कुठार, बाण और धनुष धारण किए देखकर और वीर समझकर बालक को क्रोध आ गया। वह आपका नाम तो जानता था, पर उसने आपको पहचाना नहीं। अपने वंश (रघुवंश) के स्वभाव के अनुसार उसने उत्तर दिया ॥
english_translation: Seeing the axe, arrows, and bow in his hands, the boy grew angry, thinking him a warrior. He knew your name, but did not recognize you. According to the nature of his lineage, he gave that reply.
essence: Anger begins when appearance is mistaken for identity.
simple_meaning: The boy mistook the sage for a warrior because of his weapons and answered in anger. He knew the man's name, but not his identity.
insight: It shows how appearance can distort response, and how pride reacts before recognition.
modern_relevance: You read a harsh text message and answer in the same tone. Later you learn the person was tired, not hostile. One wrong reading can turn a small moment into a fight.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जौं तुम्ह औतेहु मुनि की नाईं। पद रज सिर सिसु धरत गोसाईं॥ छमहु चूक अनजानत केरी। चहिअ बिप्र उर कृपा घनेरी ॥
translation: यदि आप मुनि की तरह आते, तो हे स्वामी! बालक आपके चरणों की धूलि सिर पर रखता। अनजाने की भूल को क्षमा कर दीजिए। ब्राह्मणों के हृदय में बहुत अधिक दया होनी चाहिए ॥
english_translation: If you had come like a sage, the child would have placed the dust of your feet on his head. Forgive the mistake made in ignorance. A Brahmin’s heart should hold abundant compassion.
essence: Humility invites reverence; ignorance calls for mercy.
simple_meaning: The child says he would have shown respect if the visitor had come humbly. Since the mistake was made in ignorance, he asks for forgiveness and says a Brahmin should have great compassion.
insight: It shifts the response from retaliation to dignified forgiveness, while still asking for respect.
modern_relevance: Someone snaps at you in a meeting because they misunderstood your tone. The real test is whether you answer with pride or with mercy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हमहि तुम्हहि सरिबरि कसि नाथा। कहहु न कहाँ चरन कहँ माथा॥ राम मात्र लघुनाम हमारा। परसु सहित बड़ नाम तोहारा ॥
translation: हे नाथ! हमारी और आपकी बराबरी कैसी? कहिए न, कहाँ चरण और कहाँ मस्तक! कहाँ मेरा राम मात्र छोटा सा नाम और कहाँ आपका परशुसहित बड़ा नाम ॥
english_translation: O Lord, how can we compare ourselves? Tell me, where are your feet and where is my head? My Ram is only a small name; your name is great, with the axe.
essence: Real greatness makes comparison feel foolish.
simple_meaning: Parasurama admits that he and Ram are not equal. He bows to Ram's feet and says his own name is only a small one beside Ram's greater name.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to reverence before strength and grace.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room ready to prove yourself, then meet someone whose presence makes boasting feel childish. The wiser move is to bow internally and speak cleanly.
speaker: Parasurama

verse_text: देव एकु गुनु धनुष हमारें। नव गुन परम पुनीत तुम्हारें॥ सब प्रकार हम तुम्ह सन हारे। छमहु बिप्र अपराध हमारे ॥
translation: हे देव! हमारे तो एक ही गुण धनुष है और आपके परम पवित्र (शम, दम, तप, शौच, क्षमा, सरलता, ज्ञान, विज्ञान और आस्तिकता ये) नौ गुण हैं। हम तो सब प्रकार से आपसे हारे हैं। हे विप्र! हमारे अपराधों को क्षमा कीजिए ॥
english_translation: O divine one, we have only one quality: the bow. Your qualities are nine and supremely pure. In every way, we have been defeated by you. O learned one, forgive our offense.
essence: True strength can begin by admitting defeat.
simple_meaning: Ram admits defeat before Parashurama and asks forgiveness for any offense. He contrasts his single strength with the sage's many pure qualities.
insight: It teaches you to defuse conflict with humility rather than ego-driven defense.
modern_relevance: A tense argument is about to explode in a family group chat. Instead of defending every word, you say, 'I may have missed something. Please forgive me.' The temperature drops instantly.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: बार बार मुनि बिप्रबर कहा राम सन राम। बोले भृगुपति सरुष हसि तहूँ बंधू सम बाम ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने परशुरामजी को बार-बार 'मुनि' और 'विप्रवर' कहा। तब भृगुपति (परशुरामजी) कुपित होकर (अथवा क्रोध की हँसी हँसकर) बोले- तू भी अपने भाई के समान ही टेढ़ा है ॥
english_translation: Ram kept calling Parashurama “sage” and “best of the learned.” Bhargupati then laughed in anger and said, “You are crooked like your brother.”
essence: Courtesy can meet anger and still not stop it.
simple_meaning: Ram keeps addressing Parashurama respectfully, but Parashurama answers with angry mockery, accusing Ram of being crooked like his brother.
