translation: शूरता का बाना धारण किए हुए रणधीर वीर सब निकलकर नगर के बाहर आ खड़े हुए। वे चतुर अपने घोड़ों को तरह-तरह की चालों से फेर रहे हैं और भेरी तथा नगाड़े की आवाज सुन-सुनकर प्रसन्न हो रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Clad in the garb of valor, the brave warriors stood outside the city. They twirled their fine horses in many ways and rejoiced at the sound of drums and kettledrums.
essence: Battle spirit rises before the first blow is struck.
simple_meaning: The warriors ride out of the city, full of battle spirit, showing off their horses and enjoying the war drums.
insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle to the charged mood before action begins.
modern_relevance: At a stadium tunnel before the final match, players bounce on their toes, adjusting gloves, grinning at the roar outside. The noise itself lifts their courage.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रथ सारथिन्ह बिचित्र बनाए। ध्वज पताक मनि भूषन लाए॥ चवँर चारु किंकिनि धुनि करहीं। भानु जान सोभा अपहरहीं ॥
translation: सारथियों ने ध्वजा, पताका, मणि और आभूषणों को लगाकर रथों को बहुत विलक्षण बना दिया है। उनमें सुंदर चँवर लगे हैं और घंटियाँ सुंदर शब्द कर रही हैं। वे रथ इतने सुंदर हैं, मानो सूर्य के रथ की शोभा को छीने लेते हैं ॥
english_translation: The charioteers made the chariots wondrous, adorning them with flags, pennants, jewels, and ornaments. Beautiful fly-whisks and tinkling bells made them shine so brightly they seemed to rival the sun’s splendor.
essence: Splendour itself becomes part of the procession.
simple_meaning: The chariots are richly decorated with flags, jewels, fly-whisks, and bells. They shine so brightly that they seem to outshine the sun.
insight: It shifts attention from the riders to the atmosphere they create: form, ceremony, and collective awe.
modern_relevance: A wedding convoy rolls out with lights, ribbons, and music, and everyone pauses to look. The moment feels larger than the people inside it — a whole world announcing itself.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सावँकरन अगनित हय होते। ते तिन्ह रथन्ह सारथिन्ह जोते॥ सुंदर सकल अलंकृत सोहे। जिन्हहि बिलोकत मुनि मन मोहे ॥
translation: अगणित श्यामवर्ण घोड़े थे। उनको सारथियों ने उन रथों में जोत दिया है, जो सभी देखने में सुंदर और गहनों से सजाए हुए सुशोभित हैं और जिन्हें देखकर मुनियों के मन भी मोहित हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: There were countless dark horses. The charioteers yoked them to the chariots, all beautifully adorned, so lovely that even sages were enchanted at the sight.
essence: Splendour itself can announce a turning point.
simple_meaning: Countless dark horses are yoked to beautifully decorated chariots. The sight is so splendid that even sages are captivated.
insight: It shifts attention from the fighters to the charged atmosphere of preparation and grandeur.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall fills with polished cars, bright fabric, and restless guests before the ceremony begins. The atmosphere itself signals that something important is about to unfold.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जे जल चलहिं थलहि की नाईं। टाप न बूड़ बेग अधिकाईं॥ अस्त्र सस्त्र सबु साजु बनाई। रथी सारथिन्ह लिए बोलाई ॥
translation: जो जल पर भी जमीन की तरह ही चलते हैं। वेग की अधिकता से उनकी टाप पानी में नहीं डूबती। अस्त्र-शस्त्र और सब साज सजाकर सारथियों ने रथियों को बुला लिया ॥
english_translation: Those who move on water as if on land. Their hoofprints do not sink in the water because of their great speed. After preparing all weapons and gear, the charioteers called the warriors to the chariots.
essence: Speed and splendor signal that the procession has fully begun.
simple_meaning: The army’s horses are so swift that they seem to run on water like they run on land. The chariots are fully armed and the warriors are being called to mount them.
insight: It shifts attention from meaning to motion, showing how a scene can build force through detail alone.
modern_relevance: You hear the elevator ding, grab your bag, and step into the hallway already moving. Everything has been arranged; now the day is about to carry you forward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चढ़ि चढ़ि रथ बाहेर नगर लागी जुरन बरात। होत सगुन सुंदर सबहि जो जेहि कारज जात ॥
translation: रथों पर चढ़-चढ़कर बारात नगर के बाहर जुटने लगी, जो जिस काम के लिए जाता है, सभी को सुंदर शकुन होते हैं ॥
english_translation: The wedding party climbed onto the chariots and gathered outside the city. For every person going to a worthy task, good omens appear.
essence: A sacred journey begins with auspicious signs.
simple_meaning: The wedding procession gathers outside the city on decorated chariots, and the scene is marked by good omens.
insight: It keeps the mind on the unfolding scene rather than forcing a lesson from it.
modern_relevance: You step out of the house before dawn for a day that matters. The air feels charged, and even small signs seem to bless the road ahead.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कलित करिबरन्हि परीं अँबारीं। कहि न जाहिं जेहि भाँति सँवारीं॥ चले मत्त गज घंट बिराजी। मनहुँ सुभग सावन घन राजी॥1।
translation: श्रेष्ठ हाथियों पर सुंदर अंबारियाँ पड़ी हैं। वे जिस प्रकार सजाई गई थीं, सो कहा नहीं जा सकता। मतवाले हाथी घंटों से सुशोभित होकर (घंटे बजाते हुए) चले, मानो सावन के सुंदर बादलों के समूह (गरते हुए) जा रहे हों॥
english_translation: Beautiful palanquins were placed upon noble elephants, so finely adorned that their arrangement cannot be described. The intoxicated elephants, bright with bells, moved like lovely monsoon clouds drifting across the sky.
essence: Splendor turns a procession into a moving festival.
simple_meaning: The wedding procession is richly decorated, with elephants carrying beautiful palanquins and moving like monsoon clouds.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the atmosphere it creates around everyone present.
modern_relevance: A wedding convoy rolls past your window at dusk, lights strung across every vehicle, drums echoing down the street. The whole city seems to breathe in rhythm with the celebration.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बाहन अपर अनेक बिधाना। सिबिका सुभग सुखासन जाना॥ तिन्ह चढ़ि चले बिप्रबर बृंदा। जनु तनु धरें सकल श्रुति छंदा ॥
translation: सुंदर पालकियाँ, सुख से बैठने योग्य तामजान (जो कुर्सीनुमा होते हैं) और रथ आदि और भी अनेकों प्रकार की सवारियाँ हैं। उन पर श्रेष्ठ ब्राह्मणों के समूह चढ़कर चले, मानो सब वेदों के छन्द ही शरीर धारण किए हुए हों ॥
english_translation: There were many kinds of beautiful rides: palanquins, comfortable seats, and chariots. The finest Brahmins rode on them, as if all the Vedic hymns had taken bodily form.
essence: The procession carries not just people, but living sacred order.
simple_meaning: Many kinds of decorated vehicles carried the Brahmin groups in the procession, and they looked like the Vedic hymns themselves taking form.
insight: It turns a festive procession into a sacred public event, where learning and ritual travel together.
modern_relevance: A wedding convoy rolls past with music, flowers, and elders in every car. The scene feels bigger than transport alone — it feels like tradition itself has entered the street.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मागध सूत बंधि गुनगायक। चले जान चढ़ि जो जेहि लायक॥ बेसर ऊँट बृषभ बहु जाती। चले बस्तु भरि अगनित भाँती ॥
translation: मागध, सूत, भाट और गुण गाने वाले सब, जो जिस योग्य थे, वैसी सवारी पर चढ़कर चले। बहुत जातियों के खच्चर, ऊँट और बैल असंख्यों प्रकार की वस्तुएँ लाद-लादकर चले ॥
english_translation: The bards, singers, and praise-singers set out on whatever mounts suited them. Countless mules, camels, and bullocks went along, laden with goods of every kind.
essence: A grand journey depends on every kind of helper, rider, and load-bearer.
simple_meaning: The procession includes singers, praise-singers, and many kinds of animals carrying goods and supplies.
insight: It shifts attention from a single hero to the many supporting roles that make a celebration possible.
modern_relevance: A wedding convoy, moving trucks, and family helpers all arrive at once. The event feels grand only because many unseen hands and vehicles make it possible.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोटिन्ह काँवरि चले कहारा। बिबिध बस्तु को बरनै पारा॥ चले सकल सेवक समुदाई। निज निज साजु समाजु बनाई ॥
translation: कहार करोड़ों काँवरें लेकर चले। उनमें अनेकों प्रकार की इतनी वस्तुएँ थीं कि जिनका वर्णन कौन कर सकता है। सब सेवकों के समूह अपना-अपना साज-समाज बनाकर चले ॥
english_translation: Porters walked carrying millions of canopies and loads. Who can describe the countless kinds of goods they bore? All the servants marched together, arranging their own gear and procession.
essence: A royal celebration moves on the shoulders of unseen workers.
simple_meaning: The people traveling with the wedding procession carried huge amounts of goods and supplies, each group arranging its own transport.
insight: It shifts attention from the grand event to the collective labor that makes it possible.
modern_relevance: At a wedding, the back room is crowded with boxes, folded chairs, flowers, and people hurrying with lists in hand. The celebration only exists because many unseen helpers keep moving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब कें उर निर्भर हरषु पूरित पुलक सरीर। कबहिं देखिबे नयन भरि रामु लखनु दोउ बीर ॥
translation: सबके हृदय में अपार हर्ष है और शरीर पुलक से भरे हैं। (सबको एक ही लालसा लगी है कि) हम श्री राम-लक्ष्मण दोनों भाइयों को नेत्र भरकर कब देखेंगे ॥
english_translation: Everyone's heart overflows with joy, and their bodies are covered in goosebumps: When will we behold Ram and Lakshman with our own eyes?
essence: Joy swells when the beloved is about to appear.
simple_meaning: Everyone is thrilled and physically moved with joy, eagerly waiting to see Ram and Lakshman with their own eyes.
insight: It captures shared anticipation before a moment everyone has been waiting for.
modern_relevance: You wait at the edge of a crowded platform, craning for one person who matters more than the rest. The whole room feels charged with the same hope.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गरजहिं गज घंटा धुनि घोरा। रथ रव बाजि हिंस चहु ओरा॥ निदरि घनहि घुर्म्मरहिं निसाना। निज पराइ कछु सुनिअ न काना ॥
translation: हाथी गरज रहे हैं, उनके घंटों की भीषण ध्वनि हो रही है। चारों ओर रथों की घरघराहट और घोड़ों की हिनहिनाहट हो रही है। बादलों का निरादर करते हुए नगाड़े घोर शब्द कर रहे हैं। किसी को अपनी-पराई कोई बात कानों से सुनाई नहीं देती ॥
english_translation: Elephants roar, their bells thunder loudly. All around, the rumble of chariots and the neighing of horses rise. Drums beat so fiercely they seem to defy the clouds. No ear can tell one side from another.
essence: The arrival is so grand that sound itself becomes the announcement.
simple_meaning: The whole scene is filled with loud celebration and movement. The noise is so overwhelming that nothing else can be heard clearly.
insight: It turns the moment into pure atmosphere, preparing the reader for the royal gathering that follows.
modern_relevance: A wedding procession turns the street into thunder: horns, drums, engines, shouting, all at once. You cannot hear your own thoughts, only the fact that something important is arriving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: महा भीर भूपति के द्वारें। रज होइ जाइ पषान पबारें॥ चढ़ी अटारिन्ह देखहिं नारीं। लिएँ आरती मंगल थारीं ॥
translation: राजा दशरथ के दरवाजे पर इतनी भारी भीड़ हो रही है कि वहाँ पत्थर फेंका जाए तो वह भी पिसकर धूल हो जाए। अटारियों पर चढ़ी स्त्रियाँ मंगल थालों में आरती लिए देख रही हैं ॥
english_translation: At the king's gate, the crowd was so immense that even a thrown stone would be ground to dust. Women climbed the terraces, holding lamps and auspicious plates for the aarti.
essence: The king's gate overflows with joy before the brothers appear.
simple_meaning: The king's palace is packed with people, and women on the terraces watch the scene with lamps and auspicious offerings.
insight: It turns a private arrival into a shared festival, showing how devotion can fill an entire place.
modern_relevance: You stand outside a wedding hall while relatives crowd the steps, phones in hand, waiting for the bride and groom. The building itself seems to vibrate with expectation before the doors open.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गावहिं गीत मनोहर नाना। अति आनंदु न जाइ बखाना॥ तब सुमंत्र दुइ स्यंदन साजी। जोते रबि हय निंदक बाजी ॥
translation: और नाना प्रकार के मनोहर गीत गा रही हैं। उनके अत्यन्त आनंद का बखान नहीं हो सकता। तब सुमन्त्रजी ने दो रथ सजाकर उनमें सूर्य के घोड़ों को भी मात करने वाले घोड़े जोते ॥
english_translation: And they sang many lovely songs. Their joy was beyond description. Then Sumantra prepared two chariots and yoked horses that could outmatch the sun’s own steeds.
essence: Joy rises, and the journey is set in motion.
simple_meaning: The people sing with great joy while Sumantra gets two chariots ready and harnesses excellent horses.
insight: It keeps attention on atmosphere and preparation, not on private feeling or inner debate.
modern_relevance: A house is buzzing before dawn, phones are ringing, clothes are being packed, and everyone is half-excited, half-nervous. The day has already begun moving before anyone is ready.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दोउ रथ रुचिर भूप पहिं आने। नहिं सारद पहिं जाहिं बखाने॥ राज समाजु एक रथ साजा। दूसर तेज पुंज अति भ्राजा ॥
translation: दोनों सुंदर रथ वे राजा दशरथ के पास ले आए, जिनकी सुंदरता का वर्णन सरस्वती से भी नहीं हो सकता। एक रथ पर राजसी सामान सजाया गया और दूसरा जो तेज का पुंज और अत्यन्त ही शोभायमान था, ॥
english_translation: They brought two beautiful chariots to the king, beyond even Sarada's power to describe. One chariot was decked for royal use; the other shone like a blazing mass of light.
essence: Preparation itself can carry the dignity of the moment.
simple_meaning: Two splendid chariots are brought for King Dasharath. One is prepared for royal display, and the other shines with extraordinary brilliance.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the care that makes the event worthy.
modern_relevance: Before a wedding procession, someone is still fastening the flowers on the car while everyone waits in bright, nervous excitement. The visible preparation matters because a sacred moment is about to begin.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहिं रथ रुचिर बसिष्ठ कहुँ हरषि चढ़ाई नरेसु। आपु चढ़ेउ स्यंदन सुमिरि हर गुर गौरि गनेसु ॥
translation: उस सुंदर रथ पर राजा वशिष्ठजी को हर्ष पूर्वक चढ़ाकर फिर स्वयं शिव, गुरु, गौरी (पार्वती) और गणेशजी का स्मरण करके (दूसरे) रथ पर चढ़े ॥
english_translation: He joyfully seated Vashishtha on the beautiful chariot. Then he himself boarded the chariot, remembering Shiva, the guru, Gauri, and Ganesha.
essence: True action begins with remembrance, not self-assertion.
simple_meaning: King Dasharath seats Vashishtha on one chariot and then gets on another after remembering Shiva, the teacher, Parvati, and Ganesha.
insight: It teaches you to begin important action with reverence, not ego.
modern_relevance: Before a big presentation, you pause, breathe, and silently remember the people and values that steadied you. The move is not empty ritual; it keeps pride from taking over.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सहित बसिष्ठ सोह नृप कैसें। सुर गुर संग पुरंदर जैसें॥ करि कुल रीति बेद बिधि राऊ। देखि सबहि सब भाँति बनाऊ ॥
translation: वशिष्ठजी के साथ (जाते हुए) राजा दशरथजी कैसे शोभित हो रहे हैं, जैसे देव गुरु बृहस्पतिजी के साथ इन्द्र हों। वेद की विधि से और कुल की रीति के अनुसार सब कार्य करके तथा सबको सब प्रकार से सजे देखकर, ॥
english_translation: How splendid King Dasharath looked with Vashishtha, like Indra with Brihaspati. He completed every act by Vedic rule and family custom, and saw that everything was fully arranged.
essence: True dignity comes from doing every detail in the right order.
simple_meaning: Dasharath appears radiant beside Vashishtha, like Indra with his teacher. He follows sacred rules and family custom carefully, making sure everything is properly prepared.
insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to disciplined preparation and respectful order.
modern_relevance: Before a wedding procession, a family checks every garland, seat, and timing detail. The calm dignity comes from care done properly, not from rushing or improvising.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुमिरि रामु गुर आयसु पाई। चले महीपति संख बजाई॥ हरषे बिबुध बिलोकि बराता। बरषहिं सुमन सुमंगल दाता ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का स्मरण करके, गुरु की आज्ञा पाकर पृथ्वी पति दशरथजी शंख बजाकर चले। बारात देखकर देवता हर्षित हुए और सुंदर मंगलदायक फूलों की वर्षा करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Remembering Ram and receiving the guru's command, the king set out with a conch blast. The radiant beings rejoiced at the wedding procession and showered auspicious flowers.
essence: Guided action becomes sacred the moment it leaves the heart.
simple_meaning: King Dasharath remembers Ram, follows his guru's instruction, and sets out with the wedding procession. The radiant beings celebrate and shower flowers.
insight: It shows how obedience to right guidance turns an ordinary departure into an auspicious beginning.
modern_relevance: You finally get the message that changes everything, and you move. The room may still be ordinary, but the step you take has already been blessed by clarity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भयउ कोलाहल हय गय गाजे। ब्योम बरात बाजने बाजे॥ सुर नर नारि सुमंगल गाईं। सरस राग बाजहिं सहनाईं ॥
translation: बड़ा शोर मच गया, घोड़े और हाथी गरजने लगे। आकाश में और बारात में (दोनों जगह) बाजे बजने लगे। देवांगनाएँ और मनुष्यों की स्त्रियाँ सुंदर मंगलगान करने लगीं और रसीले राग से शहनाइयाँ बजने लगीं ॥
english_translation: A great uproar arose. Horses and elephants roared; drums and trumpets sounded in the sky and in the wedding procession. Celestial beings, men, and women sang auspicious songs, and sweet shawms played melodious tunes.
essence: Joy spills outward until the whole world seems to join it.
simple_meaning: The wedding procession becomes loud and festive, with animals, instruments, and singing filling the air.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the atmosphere it creates around everyone.
modern_relevance: A neighborhood lane fills with music, laughter, and the clatter of guests arriving for a wedding. For a moment, the whole street feels lifted by one shared joy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: घंट घंटि धुनि बरनि न जाहीं। सरव करहिं पाइक फहराहीं॥ करहिं बिदूषक कौतुक नाना। हास कुसल कल गान सुजाना ॥
translation: घंटे-घंटियों की ध्वनि का वर्णन नहीं हो सकता। पैदल चलने वाले सेवकगण अथवा पट्टेबाज कसरत के खेल कर रहे हैं और फहरा रहे हैं (आकाश में ऊँचे उछलते हुए जा रहे हैं।) हँसी करने में निपुण और सुंदर गाने में चतुर विदूषक (मसखरे) तरह-तरह के तमाशे कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The sound of bells cannot be described. Foot soldiers and attendants leap and wave flags. Jokers perform many amusements, skilled in laughter and sweet song.
essence: The procession is so alive that words fall short.
simple_meaning: The wedding procession is overflowing with noise, movement, jokes, and music. It is a lively scene, not a teaching verse.
insight: It sets the scene with sensory abundance, preparing the reader for the procession’s grandeur.
modern_relevance: You reach a wedding baraat and the whole street is alive with drums, shouting, dancing, and people making each other laugh. The moment is bigger than description.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तुरग नचावहिं कुअँर बर अकनि मृदंग निसान। नागर नट चितवहिं चकित डगहिं न ताल बँधान ॥
translation: सुंदर राजकुमार मृदंग और नगाड़े के शब्द सुनकर घोड़ों को उन्हीं के अनुसार इस प्रकार नचा रहे हैं कि वे ताल के बंधान से जरा भी डिगते नहीं हैं। चतुर नट चकित होकर यह देख रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The handsome princes make the horses dance to the beat of the drum and kettledrum. Even skilled acrobats watch in wonder, unable to keep time without faltering.
essence: True skill stays steady even under a roaring rhythm.
simple_meaning: The princes ride so skillfully to the beat of the drums that even expert performers are amazed by their control.
insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to mastery under pressure.
modern_relevance: At a crowded arena, someone handles pressure so smoothly that the experts in the stands go quiet. Skill like that doesn't announce itself; it simply holds the room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बनइ न बरनत बनी बराता। होहिं सगुन सुंदर सुभदाता॥ चारा चाषु बाम दिसि लेई। मनहुँ सकल मंगल कहि देई ॥
translation: बारात ऐसी बनी है कि उसका वर्णन करते नहीं बनता। सुंदर शुभदायक शकुन हो रहे हैं। नीलकंठ पक्षी बाईं ओर चारा ले रहा है, मानो सम्पूर्ण मंगलों की सूचना दे रहा हो॥।1॥
english_translation: The wedding procession was so splendid it could not be described. Auspicious signs appeared everywhere, and the blue-necked bird on the left seemed to announce good fortune.
essence: A blessed moment makes even nature seem to speak.
simple_meaning: The wedding procession is overflowing with beauty and good omens. Even the birds and signs around it seem to announce blessing.
insight: It trains attention to notice harmony and blessing in the atmosphere around an event.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall and feel the air change before anyone speaks. The lights, the music, the smiles, even the smallest details seem to say: something sacred is beginning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दाहिन काग सुखेत सुहावा। नकुल दरसु सब काहूँ पावा॥ सानुकूल बह त्रिबिध बयारी। सघट सबाल आव बर नारी ॥
translation: दाहिनी ओर कौआ सुंदर खेत में शोभा पा रहा है। नेवले का दर्शन भी सब किसी ने पाया। तीनों प्रकार की (शीतल, मंद, सुगंधित) हवा अनुकूल दिशा में चल रही है। श्रेष्ठ (सुहागिनी) स्त्रियाँ भरे हुए घड़े और गोद में बालक लिए आ रही हैं ॥
english_translation: A crow appears auspiciously on the right. A mongoose is seen by everyone. Three kinds of favorable breeze blow. Married women come carrying full pots and infants in their laps.
essence: The world itself seems to bless the marriage before it begins.
simple_meaning: A series of auspicious signs appears around the wedding procession: crows, mongooses, gentle winds, and married women carrying pots and children.
insight: It trains attention to read the atmosphere of a moment, not just its facts.
modern_relevance: You step outside on a day that suddenly feels unusually gentle: the air is soft, people smile without reason, and everything seems to line up. Some days seem to welcome what is about to happen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लोवा फिरि फिरि दरसु देखावा। सुरभी सनमुख सिसुहि पिआवा॥ मृगमाला फिरि दाहिनि आई। मंगल गन जनु दीन्हि देखाई ॥
translation: लोमड़ी फिर-फिरकर (बार-बार) दिखाई दे जाती है। गायें सामने खड़ी बछड़ों को दूध पिलाती हैं। हरिनों की टोली (बाईं ओर से) घूमकर दाहिनी ओर को आई, मानो सभी मंगलों का समूह दिखाई दिया ॥
english_translation: The fox kept appearing again and again. Cows stood facing their calves and fed them milk. A herd of deer came around to the right, as if a whole cluster of auspicious signs had appeared.
essence: The world itself seems to bless the procession.
simple_meaning: More auspicious signs appear as the wedding procession moves forward: animals and birds behave in fortunate ways, suggesting everything is going well.
insight: It trains attention to read the moment as favorable and aligned, not random.
modern_relevance: You leave home for a big family ceremony, and every small detail feels meaningful — the traffic clears, a child smiles, the day seems to open. This verse lives in that feeling of being gently blessed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: छेमकरी कह छेम बिसेषी। स्यामा बाम सुतरु पर देखी॥ सनमुख आयउ दधि अरु मीना। कर पुस्तक दुइ बिप्र प्रबीना ॥
translation: क्षेमकरी (सफेद सिरवाली चील) विशेष रूप से क्षेम (कल्याण) कह रही है। श्यामा बाईं ओर सुंदर पेड़ पर दिखाई पड़ी। दही, मछली और दो विद्वान ब्राह्मण हाथ में पुस्तक लिए हुए सामने आए ॥
english_translation: The auspicious bird called Khemkari gave a special sign of well-being. The dark one appeared on the left in a beautiful tree. Curds, fish, and two learned Brahmins with books came into view ahead.
essence: A blessed moment seems to announce itself from every direction.
simple_meaning: A series of auspicious signs appears together, pointing toward success and blessing.
insight: It trains attention to notice a pattern of blessing rather than random fragments.
modern_relevance: Before a big interview, you notice every small thing seems to go right — the train is on time, your notes are ready, the room feels calm. The mind starts reading the day as favorable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंगलमय कल्यानमय अभिमत फल दातार। जनु सब साचे होन हित भए सगुन एक बार ॥
translation: सभी मंगलमय, कल्याणमय और मनोवांछित फल देने वाले शकुन मानो सच्चे होने के लिए एक ही साथ हो गए ॥
english_translation: All auspicious, all beneficial, and all desired omens seemed to become true at once.
essence: A blessed moment makes even signs seem to speak in one voice.
simple_meaning: Every good sign appeared together, as if the whole world was confirming that this moment would bring blessing and the desired result.
insight: It shifts attention from uncertainty to the felt sense that a moment is being quietly affirmed.
modern_relevance: You are already nervous before a big decision, then everything seems to line up at once: the call comes through, the timing works, the signs feel unmistakable. This verse captures that rare feeling of life opening its hand.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंगल सगुन सुगम सब ताकें। सगुन ब्रह्म सुंदर सुत जाकें॥ राम सरिस बरु दुलहिनि सीता। समधी दसरथु जनकु पुनीता ॥
translation: स्वयं सगुण ब्रह्म जिसके सुंदर पुत्र हैं, उसके लिए सब मंगल शकुन सुलभ हैं। जहाँ श्री रामचन्द्रजी सरीखे दूल्हा और सीताजी जैसी दुलहिन हैं तथा दशरथजी और जनकजी जैसे पवित्र समधी हैं, ॥
english_translation: For that one, all auspicious signs come easily. The supreme reality has a beautiful son. Ram is the bridegroom, Sita the bride, and pure Dasharath and Janak are the noble fathers-in-law.
essence: Purity at the center makes every sign turn auspicious.
simple_meaning: A house blessed by Ram and Sita needs no effort for good signs. The wedding is holy because the bridegroom, bride, and both fathers are all pure and noble.
insight: It shifts attention from lucky signs to the moral purity that makes a moment truly auspicious.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall fills with noise, relatives, and last-minute chaos, yet one simple thing changes everything: the people at the center are good, steady, and sincere. Then even the disorder feels blessed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि अस ब्याहु सगुन सब नाचे। अब कीन्हे बिरंचि हम साँचे॥ एहि बिधि कीन्ह बरात पयाना। हय गय गाजहिं हने निसाना ॥
translation: ऐसा ब्याह सुनकर मानो सभी शकुन नाच उठे (और कहने लगे-) अब ब्रह्माजी ने हमको सच्चा कर दिया। इस तरह बारात ने प्रस्थान किया। घोड़े, हाथी गरज रहे हैं और नगाड़ों पर चोट लग रही है ॥
english_translation: Hearing of such a wedding, all the auspicious signs seemed to dance. "Now Brahma himself has made us true." In this way the wedding procession set out; horses and elephants roared, and the drums were struck.
essence: A blessed beginning moves like the whole world agrees.
simple_meaning: The wedding procession begins amid joy and celebration. Horses, elephants, and drums announce the start of Ram and Sita's marriage journey.
insight: It shifts attention from the ceremony itself to the living momentum that follows a fulfilled blessing.
modern_relevance: The car pulls away from the house after the ceremony, and everyone on the street turns to look. The noise, the movement, the relief — a long-awaited beginning is finally underway.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आवत जानि भानुकुल केतू। सरितन्हि जनक बँधाए सेतू॥ बीच-बीच बर बास बनाए। सुरपुर सरिस संपदा छाए ॥
translation: सूर्यवंश के पताका स्वरूप दशरथजी को आते हुए जानकर जनकजी ने नदियों पर पुल बँधवा दिए। बीच-बीच में ठहरने के लिए सुंदर घर (पड़ाव) बनवा दिए, जिनमें देवलोक के समान सम्पदा छाई है, ॥
english_translation: Knowing that the Sun-line prince was coming, King Janak had bridges built over the rivers. At intervals he had beautiful rest houses made, filled with wealth like the realm of the radiant beings.
essence: True welcome builds the road before the guest arrives.
simple_meaning: Janak prepares the route for Dasharath's arrival by building bridges and rest houses along the way.
insight: It shifts respect from words and ceremony to concrete preparation that eases another person's journey.
modern_relevance: A guest is arriving after a long drive, and you clear the path, set up water, and make the rooms ready before they knock. Real welcome is built in advance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: असन सयन बर बसन सुहाए। पावहिं सब निज निज मन भाए॥ नित नूतन सुख लखि अनुकूले। सकल बरातिन्ह मंदिर भूले ॥
translation: और जहाँ बारात के सब लोग अपने-अपने मन की पसंद के अनुसार सुहावने उत्तम भोजन, बिस्तर और वस्त्र पाते हैं। मन के अनुकूल नित्य नए सुखों को देखकर सभी बारातियों को अपने घर भूल गए ॥
english_translation: And there, all the wedding guests received pleasing food, beds, and clothes suited to their own taste. Seeing new delights each day in perfect comfort, all the guests forgot their homes.
essence: True hospitality makes people forget the road home.
simple_meaning: The wedding guests are treated so well that they get exactly what they like, and the comfort makes them forget their homes.
insight: It shifts attention from grand display to precise hospitality: real care means meeting each person's actual need.
modern_relevance: You arrive tired at a host's house after a long train ride, and they notice everything — the tea you like, the blanket you need, the silence you need. That kind of welcome makes a stranger feel instantly held.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आवत जानि बरात बर सुनि गहगहे निसान। सजि गज रथ पदचर तुरग लेन चले अगवान ॥
translation: बड़े जोर से बजते हुए नगाड़ों की आवाज सुनकर श्रेष्ठ बारात को आती हुई जानकर अगवानी करने वाले हाथी, रथ, पैदल और घोड़े सजाकर बारात लेने चले ॥
english_translation: Hearing the splendid wedding procession approach, the welcoming party set out with decorated elephants, chariots, foot soldiers, and horses to receive it.
essence: Joy is revealed by how carefully it receives what it loves.
simple_meaning: The wedding party is arriving, and the welcoming group goes out with elephants, chariots, foot soldiers, and horses to receive it.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the honour shown in receiving it well.
modern_relevance: A long-awaited guest is finally near, and the whole house changes at once — shoes lined up, lights switched on, everyone moving faster because something precious is about to arrive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कनक कलस भरि कोपर थारा। भाजन ललित अनेक प्रकारा॥ भरे सुधा सम सब पकवाने। नाना भाँति न जाहिं बखाने ॥
translation: (दूध, शर्बत, ठंडाई, जल आदि से) भरकर सोने के कलश तथा जिनका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता ऐसे अमृत के समान भाँति-भाँति के सब पकवानों से भरे हुए परात, थाल आदि अनेक प्रकार के सुंदर बर्तन, ॥
english_translation: Golden pitchers, trays, and many beautiful vessels were filled; the dishes were like nectar, beyond counting in variety.
essence: Honor becomes visible in the way people are fed and received.
simple_meaning: The wedding welcome is lavish: golden vessels, beautiful trays, and many kinds of food and drink are prepared in abundance.
insight: It shifts attention from abstract celebration to concrete hospitality and generosity.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home where every dish is set out before you speak. The welcome is already doing the talking.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: फल अनेक बर बस्तु सुहाईं। हरषि भेंट हित भूप पठाईं॥ भूषन बसन महामनि नाना। खग मृग हय गय बहुबिधि जाना ॥
translation: उत्तम फल तथा और भी अनेकों सुंदर वस्तुएँ राजा ने हर्षित होकर भेंट के लिए भेजीं। गहने, कपड़े, नाना प्रकार की मूल्यवान मणियाँ (रत्न), पक्षी, पशु, घोड़े, हाथी और बहुत तरह की सवारियाँ, ॥
english_translation: The king joyfully sent gifts of fine fruits and many beautiful things. He also sent ornaments, clothes, priceless jewels, birds, animals, horses, elephants, and many kinds of mounts.
essence: Welcome becomes real through generous preparation.
simple_meaning: The king sends many fine gifts, including fruit, clothes, jewels, animals, horses, and elephants, to welcome the arriving wedding party.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to the lived act of welcoming with abundance.
modern_relevance: A home fills with boxes, flowers, sweets, and last-minute gifts before guests arrive for a wedding. The care is in the details, and everyone can feel it before a word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंगल सगुन सुगंध सुहाए। बहुत भाँति महिपाल पठाए॥ दधि चिउरा उपहार अपारा। भरि भरि काँवरि चले कहारा ॥
translation: तथा बहुत प्रकार के सुगंधित एवं सुहावने मंगल द्रव्य और शगुन के पदार्थ राजा ने भेजे। दही, चिउड़ा और अगणित उपहार की चीजें काँवरों में भर-भरकर कहार चले ॥
english_translation: The king sent many auspicious gifts and fragrant offerings. Bearers loaded baskets with curd, flattened rice, and countless presents.
essence: Generous giving turns preparation into celebration.
simple_meaning: The king sends many auspicious gifts, and the bearers carry them in baskets.
insight: It shifts attention from the objects themselves to the intention and joy behind the offering.
modern_relevance: You’re packing gifts before a wedding and checking every box twice. The point is not the size of the present, but the warmth carried in its careful sending.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अगवानन्ह जब दीखि बराता। उर आनंदु पुलक भर गाता॥ देखि बनाव सहित अगवाना। मुदित बरातिन्ह हने निसाना ॥
translation: अगवानी करने वालों को जब बारात दिखाई दी, तब उनके हृदय में आनंद छा गया और शरीर रोमांच से भर गया। अगवानों को सज-धज के साथ देखकर बारातियों ने प्रसन्न होकर नगाड़े बजाए ॥
english_translation: When the welcoming party saw the wedding procession, joy rose in their hearts and their bodies thrilled. Seeing the greeters dressed in splendor, the wedding guests happily beat the drums.
essence: Joy leaps first; celebration follows.
simple_meaning: The greeters and the wedding guests are overjoyed when they see each other. Their happiness shows in tears, thrills, and drumbeats.
insight: It simply shows joy spreading between two groups at first sight.
modern_relevance: You spot your family at the airport after months apart, and before anyone speaks, everyone is already smiling, waving, and rushing forward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरषि परसपर मिलन हित कछुक चले बगमेल। जनु आनंद समुद्र दुइ मिलत बिहाइ सुबेल ॥
translation: (बाराती तथा अगवानों में से) कुछ लोग परस्पर मिलने के लिए हर्ष के मारे बाग छोड़कर (सरपट) दौड़ चले और ऐसे मिले मानो आनंद के दो समुद्र मर्यादा छोड़कर मिलते हों ॥
english_translation: Some people, overjoyed to meet each other, ran out of the garden. It was like two oceans of joy meeting and overflowing their banks.
essence: True joy cannot stay contained; it rushes toward meeting.
simple_meaning: People were so happy to meet that they rushed out to greet one another. Their joy felt vast, like two oceans overflowing together.
insight: It turns emotion into vivid movement, showing joy as something that naturally seeks connection.
modern_relevance: You spot someone you have not seen in years at a train platform, and before you even think, you are already walking fast. Some happiness is too large to sit still.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बरषि सुमन सुर सुंदरि गावहिं। मुदित देव दुंदुभीं बजावहिं॥ बस्तु सकल राखीं नृप आगें। बिनय कीन्हि तिन्ह अति अनुरागें ॥
translation: देवसुंदरियाँ फूल बरसाकर गीत गा रही हैं और देवता आनंदित होकर नगाड़े बजा रहे हैं। (अगवानी में आए हुए) उन लोगों ने सब चीजें दशरथजी के आगे रख दीं और अत्यन्त प्रेम से विनती की ॥
english_translation: The divine maidens shower flowers and sing, while the radiant beings joyfully beat drums. They placed all gifts before King Dasharatha and bowed with deep affection.
essence: True festivity bows before what it honors.
simple_meaning: Heavenly beings celebrate the wedding procession, place gifts before Dasharatha, and greet him with loving respect.
insight: It turns celebration into reverence, showing that joy deepens when pride steps aside.
modern_relevance: A bride’s family opens the door, the guests step in, and the room fills with music, gifts, and bowed heads. The moment becomes sacred because everyone enters with respect.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रेम समेत रायँ सबु लीन्हा। भै बकसीस जाचकन्हि दीन्हा॥ करि पूजा मान्यता बड़ाई। जनवासे कहुँ चले लवाई ॥
translation: राजा दशरथजी ने प्रेम सहित सब वस्तुएँ ले लीं, फिर उनकी बख्शीशें होने लगीं और वे याचकों को दे दी गईं। तदनन्तर पूजा, आदर-सत्कार और बड़ाई करके अगवान लोग उनको जनवासे की ओर लिवा ले चले ॥
english_translation: With affection, the king received everything. Gifts were then handed to the petitioners. After worship, honor, and praise, the escorts led them toward the guest quarters.
essence: Honor is complete only when it flows onward.
simple_meaning: King Dasharath receives the offerings with affection, gives gifts to those who ask, and is then escorted with honor to the guest quarters.
insight: It shifts attention from receiving honor to returning honor through generosity.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a ceremony where every gesture matters: the welcome, the gifts, the walk to the room. The point is not status, but graciousness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बसन बिचित्र पाँवड़े परहीं। देखि धनदु धन मदु परिहरहीं॥ अति सुंदर दीन्हेउ जनवासा। जहँ सब कहुँ सब भाँति सुपासा ॥
translation: विलक्षण वस्त्रों के पाँवड़े पड़ रहे हैं, जिन्हें देखकर कुबेर भी अपने धन का अभिमान छोड़ देते हैं। बड़ा सुंदर जनवासा दिया गया, जहाँ सबको सब प्रकार का सुभीता था ॥
english_translation: There were exquisite carpets underfoot; even Kubera would give up pride in wealth at the sight. A beautiful guest-house was provided, where everyone had every comfort.
essence: Wealth becomes humble when it serves everyone well.
simple_meaning: The wedding arrangements were lavish and welcoming. The carpets, lodging, and comfort were so fine that even the lord of wealth would lose his pride.
insight: It shifts attention from display to hospitality: the measure of prosperity is how completely others are at ease.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where every detail has been thought through — the seating, the food, the shade, the welcome. Nobody feels like a burden. That kind of care is its own wealth.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जानी सियँ बरात पुर आई। कछु निज महिमा प्रगटि जनाई॥ हृदयँ सुमिरि सब सिद्धि बोलाईं। भूप पहुनई करन पठाईं ॥
translation: सीताजी ने बारात जनकपुर में आई जानकर अपनी कुछ महिमा प्रकट करके दिखलाई। हृदय में स्मरणकर सब सिद्धियों को बुलाया और उन्हें राजा दशरथजी की मेहमानी करने के लिए भेजा ॥
english_translation: Knowing that the wedding procession had arrived in Janakpur, Sita revealed a little of her own splendor. Remembering it in her heart, she called all powers and sent them to honor King Dasharath.
essence: Greatness becomes real when it serves without announcing itself.
simple_meaning: Sita notices the wedding procession has arrived and, with quiet power, arranges a grand welcome for Dasharath. Her inner greatness appears through service and hospitality.
insight: It shifts attention from status to gracious action: power becomes visible through service, not display.
modern_relevance: You hear guests are coming, and suddenly the whole house comes alive — cleaning, cooking, arranging, welcoming. The best host does not make a speech; the care is visible in every detail.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिधि सब सिय आयसु अकनि गईं जहाँ जनवास। लिएँ संपदा सकल सुख सुरपुर भोग बिलास ॥
translation: सीताजी की आज्ञा सुनकर सब सिद्धियाँ जहाँ जनवासा था, वहाँ सारी सम्पदा, सुख और इंद्रपुरी के भोग-विलास को लिए हुए गईं ॥
english_translation: When Sita gave the order, all the siddhis went to the guest quarters carrying wealth, comfort, and the pleasures of the gods' city.
essence: Sita's command turns hospitality into abundance.
simple_meaning: Sita's command sends all divine powers to the guest quarters with every kind of wealth and delight.
insight: It shifts attention from showing wealth to creating welcome.
modern_relevance: A home opens for guests, and everything feels quietly ready: extra bedding, food, warmth, care. Real hospitality does not brag; it makes people feel richly received.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निज निज बास बिलोकि बराती। सुर सुख सकल सुलभ सब भाँती॥ बिभव भेद कछु कोउ न जाना। सकल जनक कर करहिं बखाना ॥
translation: बारातियों ने अपने-अपने ठहरने के स्थान देखे तो वहाँ देवताओं के सब सुखों को सब प्रकार से सुलभ पाया। इस ऐश्वर्य का कुछ भी भेद कोई जान न सका। सब जनकजी की बड़ाई कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The wedding guests saw their own places and found every pleasure of the higher realm available in every way. No one could understand the details of this splendor. Everyone praised King Janaka.
essence: Real magnificence makes everyone feel at home.
simple_meaning: The wedding guests found their lodging filled with heavenly comfort and unmatched splendour, beyond anyone's full understanding. Everyone praised Janaka for it.
insight: It shifts attention from display to hospitality: true greatness makes others comfortable, not impressed.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home where every detail has been thought through before you arrived. The room is ready, the water is poured, the welcome is already there — and you feel cared for before saying a word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिय महिमा रघुनायक जानी। हरषे हृदयँ हेतु पहिचानी॥ पितु आगमनु सुनत दोउ भाई। हृदयँ न अति आनंदु अमाई ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी यह सब सीताजी की महिमा जानकर और उनका प्रेम पहचानकर हृदय में हर्षित हुए। पिता दशरथजी के आने का समाचार सुनकर दोनों भाइयों के हृदय में महान आनंद समाता न था ॥
english_translation: Raghunath understood Sita's greatness and rejoiced, recognizing her love. Hearing of Father Dasharath's arrival, both brothers felt such joy that their hearts could not contain it.
essence: True joy comes from recognizing love and longing for what is coming.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are filled with joy. Ram sees Sita's worth and love clearly, and both brothers overflow with happiness at hearing their father is coming.
insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to recognition: real joy comes from seeing love clearly and welcoming family.
modern_relevance: You spot someone’s care in the smallest gesture and feel your own heart open. Then you hear a parent is on the way, and the whole room suddenly feels brighter.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकुचन्ह कहि न सकत गुरु पाहीं। पितु दरसन लालचु मन माहीं॥ बिस्वामित्र बिनय बड़ि देखी। उपजा उर संतोषु बिसेषी ॥
translation: संकोचवश वे गुरु विश्वामित्रजी से कह नहीं सकते थे, परन्तु मन में पिताजी के दर्शनों की लालसा थी। विश्वामित्रजी ने उनकी बड़ी नम्रता देखी, तो उनके हृदय में बहुत संतोष उत्पन्न हुआ ॥
english_translation: Out of shyness, they could not speak to the guru, yet their minds longed to see their father. Seeing Vishvamitra's great humility, a deep satisfaction arose in his heart.
essence: Shyness can still reveal the heart clearly.
simple_meaning: They feel shy before the teacher, but their hearts long to see their father. Vishvamitra notices their humility and feels pleased.
insight: It shows that humility can communicate more than direct speech.
modern_relevance: You sit across from a mentor, wanting to ask about family news but holding back out of respect. The silence itself reveals your heart, and the elder understands anyway.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरषि बंधु दोउ हृदयँ लगाए। पुलक अंग अंबक जल छाए॥ चले जहाँ दसरथु जनवासे। मनहुँ सरोबर तकेउ पिआसे ॥
translation: प्रसन्न होकर उन्होंने दोनों भाइयों को हृदय से लगा लिया। उनका शरीर पुलकित हो गया और नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया। वे उस जनवासे को चले, जहाँ दशरथजी थे। मानो सरोवर प्यासे की ओर लक्ष्य करके चला हो ॥
english_translation: Delighted, he embraced both brothers to his heart. His body thrilled, and his eyes filled with tears. He went to the camp where Dasharath was, like a thirsty one moving toward a lake.
essence: Longing turns the heart toward its beloved like thirst toward water.
simple_meaning: Dasharath joyfully hugs both sons, his body trembles with emotion, and he rushes to meet them, longing for their sight.
insight: It turns reunion into a bodily event, showing how longing becomes immediate action.
modern_relevance: You spot your child across a crowded station after days away. Your body moves before your thoughts do. This is what love looks like when it finally reaches what it has been missing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूप बिलोके जबहिं मुनि आवत सुतन्ह समेत। उठे हरषि सुखसिंधु महुँ चले थाह सी लेत ॥
translation: जब राजा दशरथजी ने पुत्रों सहित मुनि को आते देखा, तब वे हर्षित होकर उठे और सुख के समुद्र में थाह सी लेते हुए चले ॥
english_translation: When King Dasharath saw the sage arrive with his sons, he rose joyfully and walked as if measuring the depths of a sea of bliss.
essence: Long-awaited presence turns joy into motion.
simple_meaning: Dasharath sees Vishwamitra arrive with the princes and rises with great joy.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to emotion: the heart moves first, and the body follows.
modern_relevance: You spot someone you’ve been waiting for at the station, and your whole body lifts before your mind catches up. Some arrivals speak before any words do.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनिहि दंडवत कीन्ह महीसा। बार बार पद रज धरि सीसा॥ कौसिक राउ लिए उर लाई। कहि असीस पूछी कुसलाई ॥
translation: पृथ्वीपति दशरथजी ने मुनि की चरणधूलि को बारंबार सिर पर चढ़ाकर उनको दण्डवत् प्रणाम किया। विश्वामित्रजी ने राजा को उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया और आशीर्वाद देकर कुशल पूछी ॥
english_translation: King Dasharath bowed to the sage again and again, pressing the sage's dust to his head. Kaushik raised him into his arms, gave blessings, and asked after his welfare.
essence: Humility opens the door before any request is made.
simple_meaning: King Dasharath bows fully to the sage, touching the sage's feet dust to his head. The sage lifts him up, blesses him, and asks how he is.
insight: It teaches you to begin important relationships with humility, not status.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where someone older, wiser, or more experienced is waiting. Instead of performing confidence, you lower your guard first — and the whole conversation changes.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि दंडवत करत दोउ भाई। देखि नृपति उर सुखु न समाई॥ सुत हियँ लाइ दुसह दुख मेटे। मृतक सरीर प्रान जनु भेंटे ॥
translation: फिर दोनों भाइयों को दण्डवत् प्रणाम करते देखकर राजा के हृदय में सुख समाया नहीं। पुत्रों को (उठाकर) हृदय से लगाकर उन्होंने अपने (वियोगजनित) दुःसह दुःख को मिटाया। मानो मृतक शरीर को प्राण मिल गए हों ॥
english_translation: Seeing both brothers bow again, the king could not contain his joy. He drew his sons to his heart and the unbearable pain of separation vanished, as if life had returned to a dead body.
essence: Separation ends, and the heart feels life return.
simple_meaning: Dasharath sees both sons bow again, overflows with joy, and hugs them close. The pain of separation briefly disappears, like life returning to a lifeless body.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to reunion: the body remembers love before words do.
modern_relevance: You spot your child across the platform after days apart, and your chest loosens before you even speak. Some joy is so physical it feels like breath returning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि बसिष्ठ पद सिर तिन्ह नाए। प्रेम मुदित मुनिबर उर लाए॥ बिप्र बृंद बंदे दुहुँ भाईं। मनभावती असीसें पाईं ॥
translation: फिर उन्होंने वशिष्ठजी के चरणों में सिर नवाया। मुनि श्रेष्ठ ने प्रेम के आनंद में उन्हें हृदय से लगा लिया। दोनों भाइयों ने सब ब्राह्मणों की वंदना की और मनभाए आशीर्वाद पाए ॥
english_translation: Then they bowed their heads at Vashishtha's feet. The great sage, filled with love, embraced them. Both brothers bowed to the Brahmins and received blessings that pleased their hearts.
essence: Humility turns victory into blessing.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman bow to Vashishtha and the Brahmins. The sage embraces them with affection, and they receive blessings that delight the heart.
insight: It teaches you to meet honour with humility, and to let respect create connection instead of pride.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a big win and choose humility over display. The people around you feel the difference immediately, and the atmosphere turns warm.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत सहानुज कीन्ह प्रनामा। लिए उठाइ लाइ उर रामा॥ हरषे लखन देखि दोउ भ्राता। मिले प्रेम परिपूरित गाता ॥
translation: भरतजी ने छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न सहित श्री रामचन्द्रजी को प्रणाम किया। श्री रामजी ने उन्हें उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया। लक्ष्मणजी दोनों भाइयों को देखकर हर्षित हुए और प्रेम से परिपूर्ण हुए शरीर से उनसे मिले ॥
english_translation: Bharat, with Shatrughna beside him, bowed to Ram. Ram lifted him up and embraced him. Lakshman rejoiced at seeing both brothers and met them with a body full of love.
essence: Respect and love erase the distance between brothers.
simple_meaning: Bharat and Shatrughna bow to Ram. Ram lifts Bharat up and embraces him. Lakshman is overjoyed to see the brothers and welcomes them with love.
insight: It shifts attention from formal greeting to the healing power of affectionate recognition.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after months apart, unsure whether anyone still feels the same. Then someone stands, pulls you close, and all the distance disappears in one embrace.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुरजन परिजन जातिजन जाचक मंत्री मीत। मिले जथाबिधि सबहि प्रभु परम कृपाल बिनीत ॥
translation: तदन्तर परम कृपालु और विनयी श्री रामचन्द्रजी अयोध्यावासियों, कुटुम्बियों, जाति के लोगों, याचकों, मंत्रियों और मित्रों सभी से यथा योग्य मिले ॥
english_translation: Then the supremely compassionate and humble Lord met all properly: the townspeople, relatives, people of his caste, petitioners, ministers, and friends.
essence: Greatness is proved by equal warmth toward everyone.
simple_meaning: Ram meets everyone in the right way, from relatives and citizens to petitioners, ministers, and friends. He does it with humility and kindness.
insight: It shifts attention from status to respect, showing that dignity must be distributed, not reserved.
modern_relevance: At a family gathering, you notice the person everyone admires also remembers the server, the driver, and the shy cousin. That small equality reveals the character more than any speech.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामहि देखि बरात जुड़ानी। प्रीति कि रीति न जाति बखानी॥ नृप समीप सोहहिं सुत चारी। जनु धन धरमादिक तनुधारी ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर बारात शीतल हुई (राम के वियोग में सबके हृदय में जो आग जल रही थी, वह शांत हो गई)। प्रीति की रीति का बखान नहीं हो सकता। राजा के पास चारों पुत्र ऐसी शोभा पा रहे हैं, मानो अर्थ, धर्म, काम और मोक्ष शरीर धारण किए हुए हों ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ram, the wedding party became calm. Love's way cannot be described. The king's four sons shone beside him, like embodied wealth, duty, desire, and freedom.
essence: Ram's presence soothes, and love itself becomes impossible to explain.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram calmed the whole wedding party. His presence creates a love that words cannot fully explain. The four princes beside Dasharath shine like wealth, duty, desire, and freedom made visible.
insight: It shifts attention from explanation to presence: some qualities are felt before they are understood.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a tense family argument, and one person’s calm changes everything. No speech fixes it. Their presence does the work first.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुतन्ह समेत दसरथहि देखी। मुदित नगर नर नारि बिसेषी॥ सुमन बरिसि सुर हनहिं निसाना। नाकनटीं नाचहिं करि गाना ॥
translation: पुत्रों सहित दशरथजी को देखकर नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष बहुत ही प्रसन्न हो रहे हैं। (आकाश में) देवता फूलों की वर्षा करके नगाड़े बजा रहे हैं और अप्सराएँ गा-गाकर नाच रही हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing Dasharatha together with his sons, the people of the city—men and women—were especially delighted. The deities showered flowers, beat drums, and celestial singers danced and sang.
essence: Arrival itself can make a city feel sacred.
simple_meaning: The city rejoices at Dasharatha’s arrival with his sons, while the heavenly beings celebrate above with flowers, music, and dance.
insight: It frames reunion as something larger than one family, turning private happiness into shared celebration.
modern_relevance: A father walks in after a long trip, and the whole house changes at once. The relief is not private anymore—faces soften, voices rise, and the room feels blessed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सतानंद अरु बिप्र सचिव गन। मागध सूत बिदुष बंदीजन॥ सहित बरात राउ सनमाना। आयसु मागि फिरे अगवाना ॥
translation: अगवानी में आए हुए शतानंदजी, अन्य ब्राह्मण, मंत्रीगण, मागध, सूत, विद्वान और भाटों ने बारात सहित राजा दशरथजी का आदर-सत्कार किया। फिर आज्ञा लेकर वे वापस लौटे ॥
english_translation: Shatananda, the other brahmins, ministers, bards, singers, scholars, and praise-speakers honoured King Dasharatha along with the wedding party. Taking permission, they returned to lead the procession onward.
essence: True welcome respects, then steps aside.
simple_meaning: The welcoming party honours Dasharatha and the wedding procession, then asks permission to go back and continue leading them.
insight: It shows that grace includes both honouring others and knowing when to withdraw.
modern_relevance: A host greets arriving guests, handles the introductions, and then steps back so the event can continue smoothly. Good hospitality knows when to lead and when to let the moment move on.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रथम बरात लगन तें आई। तातें पुर प्रमोदु अधिकाई॥ ब्रह्मानंदु लोग सब लहहीं। बढ़हुँ दिवस निसि बिधि सन कहहीं ॥
translation: बारात लग्न के दिन से पहले आ गई है, इससे जनकपुर में अधिक आनंद छा रहा है। सब लोग ब्रह्मानंद प्राप्त कर रहे हैं और विधाता से मनाकर कहते हैं कि दिन-रात बढ़ जाएँ (बड़े हो जाएँ) ॥
english_translation: The wedding procession arrived before the auspicious day, so the city’s joy grew even greater. Everyone felt overwhelming delight and begged time itself to stretch longer.
essence: Joy makes people ask time to slow down.
simple_meaning: The wedding party arrives early, and the whole city becomes even happier. People feel such joy that they wish time would move more slowly.
insight: It captures how joy can make time feel too small for what the heart is receiving.
modern_relevance: You get the message that the guests have arrived early, and suddenly the whole house feels brighter. No one wants the evening to end because something beloved is already here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामु सीय सोभा अवधि सुकृत अवधि दोउ राज। जहँ तहँ पुरजन कहहिं अस मिलि नर नारि समाज ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी और सीताजी सुंदरता की सीमा हैं और दोनों राजा पुण्य की सीमा हैं, जहाँ-तहाँ जनकपुरवासी स्त्री-पुरुषों के समूह इकट्ठे हो-होकर यही कह रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram and Sita are the limit of beauty, and both are the limit of merit. Wherever people gather, men and women of the city say this.
essence: Beauty and virtue seem complete when Ram and Sita arrive.
simple_meaning: The people of Janakpur see Ram and Sita as the highest expression of beauty and virtue, and they keep saying so to one another.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary admiration to recognising a presence that feels complete and unsurpassable.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and everyone goes quiet for a second because something rare has arrived. Some presences do not need an introduction; they change the atmosphere by being there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जनक सुकृत मूरति बैदेही। दसरथ सुकृत रामु धरें देही॥ इन्ह सम काहुँ न सिव अवराधे। काहुँ न इन्ह समान फल लाधे ॥
translation: जनकजी के सुकृत (पुण्य) की मूर्ति जानकीजी हैं और दशरथजी के सुकृत देह धारण किए हुए श्री रामजी हैं। इन (दोनों राजाओं) के समान किसी ने शिवजी की आराधना नहीं की और न इनके समान किसी ने फल ही पाए ॥
english_translation: Janak's accumulated merit has become Vaidehi, and Dasharath's accumulated merit has taken bodily form as Ram. No one has worshipped Shiva like these two, and no one has received such fruits.
essence: True devotion returns as living blessing.
simple_meaning: Janak and Dasharath’s good deeds have taken form as Sita and Ram. Their devotion to Shiva brought incomparable results.
insight: It shifts attention from effort as expense to effort as seed, showing that devotion can mature into visible grace.
modern_relevance: You spend years doing quiet, unglamorous good while no one notices. Then one day you see the shape it made: trust, character, and a life that blesses others.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: इन्ह सम कोउ न भयउ जग माहीं। है नहिं कतहूँ होनेउ नाहीं॥ हम सब सकल सुकृत कै रासी। भए जग जनमि जनकपुर बासी ॥
translation: इनके समान जगत में न कोई हुआ, न कहीं है, न होने का ही है। हम सब भी सम्पूर्ण पुण्यों की राशि हैं, जो जगत में जन्म लेकर जनकपुर के निवासी हुए, ॥
english_translation: No one in the world was like them, is like them, or will ever be like them. We too are a heap of good deeds, born into the world and living in Janakpur.
essence: Some presences are so rare they make comparison fail.
simple_meaning: No one compares to Ram and Sita. The people of Janakpur feel blessed just to have been born there and to witness them.
insight: It shifts attention from comparison to reverent recognition of extraordinary grace.
modern_relevance: You stand in a crowded temple courtyard, and for a moment everyone falls silent at the sight of a bride and groom who seem made for each other. The room knows it has witnessed something rare.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जिन्ह जानकी राम छबि देखी। को सुकृती हम सरिस बिसेषी॥ पुनि देखब रघुबीर बिआहू। लेब भली बिधि लोचन लाहू ॥
translation: और जिन्होंने जानकीजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी की छबि देखी है। हमारे सरीखा विशेष पुण्यात्मा कौन होगा! और अब हम श्री रघुनाथजी का विवाह देखेंगे और भलीभाँति नेत्रों का लाभ लेंगे ॥
english_translation: Those who have seen the beauty of Janaki and Ram are the most fortunate. Now we will see Raghubir's wedding and gain the true reward of our eyes.
essence: Seeing Ram and Janaki is itself the reward.
simple_meaning: The speaker says that anyone who has seen Ram and Janaki is truly blessed, and that watching their wedding will be the eyes' greatest reward.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary seeing to reverent witnessing of what is precious.
modern_relevance: You finally reach the temple festival after months of waiting, and the first glimpse of the procession makes the whole journey feel worthwhile.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहहिं परसपर कोकिलबयनीं। एहि बिआहँ बड़ लाभु सुनयनीं॥ बड़ें भाग बिधि बात बनाई। नयन अतिथि होइहहिं दोउ भाई ॥
translation: कोयल के समान मधुर बोलने वाली स्त्रियाँ आपस में कहती हैं कि हे सुंदर नेत्रों वाली! इस विवाह में बड़ा लाभ है। बड़े भाग्य से विधाता ने सब बात बना दी है, ये दोनों भाई हमारे नेत्रों के अतिथि हुआ करेंगे ॥
english_translation: Women with cuckoo-like sweet voices speak among themselves: “O beautiful-eyed one, this wedding brings great fortune. By great luck, the creator has arranged everything; these two brothers will become guests for our eyes.”
essence: A blessed meeting turns everyone into a witness of joy.
simple_meaning: The women praise the wedding as a great blessing. They feel fortunate that the two beautiful brothers will be present before their eyes.
insight: It frames a sacred celebration as a communal delight, not a private event.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a wedding hall where everyone keeps turning to look at the groom’s entrance. The room feels lighter because beauty, joy, and blessing are being shared by all.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बारहिं बार सनेह बस जनक बोलाउब सीय। लेन आइहहिं बंधु दोउ कोटि काम कमनीय ॥
translation: जनकजी स्नेहवश बार-बार सीताजी को बुलावेंगे और करोड़ों कामदेवों के समान सुंदर दोनों भाई सीताजी को लेने (विदा कराने) आया करेंगे ॥
english_translation: Again and again, out of affection, Janak will call Sita; the two brothers, beautiful like millions of Cupids, will come to escort her.
essence: Affection turns farewell into a blessing.
simple_meaning: Janak will keep calling Sita with affection, and Ram and Lakshman will come to take her away in beauty and honour.
insight: It frames separation as an act of affection, not abandonment.
modern_relevance: You keep walking your daughter to the car, then calling her back for one more hug. The parting hurts, but love keeps turning it into blessing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिबिध भाँति होइहि पहुनाई। प्रिय न काहि अस सासुर माई॥ तब तब राम लखनहि निहारी। होइहहिं सब पुर लोग सुखारी ॥
translation: तब उनकी अनेकों प्रकार से पहुनाई होगी। सखी! ऐसी ससुराल किसे प्यारी न होगी! तब-तब हम सब नगर निवासी श्री राम-लक्ष्मण को देख-देखकर सुखी होंगे ॥
english_translation: She will be welcomed in many ways. Who would not love such a home? Then all the people of the city will feel happy just seeing Ram and Lakshman again and again.
essence: A noble union makes an entire city rejoice.
simple_meaning: Sita’s new home will welcome her warmly, and the city will rejoice whenever Ram and Lakshman are seen.
insight: It turns a private marriage into a public blessing and a shared delight.
modern_relevance: At a wedding hall, relatives keep stepping aside just to catch another glimpse of the couple. The happiness is bigger than the ceremony itself; everyone feels it in the room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सखि जस राम लखन कर जोटा। तैसेइ भूप संग हुइ ढोटा॥ स्याम गौर सब अंग सुहाए। ते सब कहहिं देखि जे आए ॥
translation: हे सखी! जैसा श्री राम-लक्ष्मण का जोड़ा है, वैसे ही दो कुमार राजा के साथ और भी हैं। वे भी एक श्याम और दूसरे गौर वर्ण के हैं, उनके भी सब अंग बहुत सुंदर हैं। जो लोग उन्हें देख आए हैं, वे सब यही कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: O friend, just as Ram and Lakshman are a pair, so are the two princes with the king. One is dark, the other fair, and all their limbs are lovely. Everyone who has seen them says the same.
essence: Beauty becomes unforgettable when two forms belong together.
simple_meaning: The two princes are described as a beautiful pair, one dark and one fair, and everyone who sees them praises their beauty.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated beauty to the power of a matching pair.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the whole mood changes before anyone speaks. People notice not just appearance, but the rare harmony between two people standing together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहा एक मैं आजु निहारे। जनु बिरंचि निज हाथ सँवारे॥ भरतु राम ही की अनुहारी। सहसा लखि न सकहिं नर नारी ॥
translation: एक ने कहा- मैंने आज ही उन्हें देखा है, इतने सुंदर हैं, मानो ब्रह्माजी ने उन्हें अपने हाथों सँवारा है। भरत तो श्री रामचन्द्रजी की ही शकल-सूरत के हैं। स्त्री-पुरुष उन्हें सहसा पहचान नहीं सकते ॥
english_translation: One person said, “I saw them today. They are so beautiful, as if Brahma shaped them with his own hands.” Bharat resembles Ram so closely that men and women cannot recognize him at once.
essence: Bharat’s face carries Ram’s likeness so fully that recognition lags behind wonder.
simple_meaning: Someone says Bharat looks so much like Ram that people cannot recognize him immediately. His beauty seems divinely crafted.
insight: It trains attention toward likeness, beauty, and the quiet wonder of seeing kinship in another face.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a family gathering and stop mid-sentence because they carry the same face as someone you deeply miss. Recognition arrives late, but the resemblance lands instantly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लखनु सत्रुसूदनु एकरूपा। नख सिख ते सब अंग अनूपा॥ मन भावहिं मुख बरनि न जाहीं। उपमा कहुँ त्रिभुवन कोउ नाहीं ॥
translation: लक्ष्मण और शत्रुघ्न दोनों का एक रूप है। दोनों के नख से शिखा तक सभी अंग अनुपम हैं। मन को बड़े अच्छे लगते हैं, पर मुख से उनका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता। उनकी उपमा के योग्य तीनों लोकों में कोई नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Lakshman and Shatrughna are one in form. From head to toe, every limb is incomparable. The mind delights in them, but the mouth cannot describe them. In the three worlds, no one is their equal.
essence: Some forms of grace can only be witnessed, never fully said.
simple_meaning: Lakshman and Shatrughna are perfectly beautiful and beyond comparison. Their charm is so great that words fail to describe it.
insight: It shifts attention from analysis to direct appreciation of rare excellence.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm, grace, and presence stop the room. Everyone tries to explain it, but the real experience is simpler: some people are beyond description.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उपमा न कोउ कह दास तुलसी कतहुँ कबि कोबिद कहैं। बल बिनय बिद्या सील सोभा सिंधु इन्ह से एइ अहैं॥ पुर नारि सकल पसारि अंचल बिधिहि बचन सुनावहीं॥ ब्याहिअहुँ चारिउ भाइ एहिं पुर हम सुमंगल गावहीं॥
translation: दास तुलसी कहता है कवि और कोविद (विद्वान) कहते हैं, इनकी उपमा कहीं कोई नहीं है। बल, विनय, विद्या, शील और शोभा के समुद्र इनके समान ये ही हैं। जनकपुर की सब स्त्रियाँ आँचल फैलाकर विधाता को यह वचन (विनती) सुनाती हैं कि चारों भाइयों का विवाह इसी नगर में हो और हम सब सुंदर मंगल गावें।
english_translation: I, Tulsidas the servant, say that no comparison exists anywhere; even poets and scholars cannot find one. Their strength, humility, learning, virtue, and beauty are like oceans, and the women of the city spread their veils before the Creator, praying that all four brothers be married here so this town may sing auspicious songs.
essence: True greatness draws praise, humility, and shared celebration at once.
simple_meaning: No one can compare these four brothers to anything else. Their strength, humility, learning, virtue, and beauty seem unmatched, and the women of Janakpur pray that the wedding happen there.
insight: It shifts attention from judging greatness to reverently receiving it and helping it unfold.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone quietly feels the same thing: this moment is special. No one is trying to own it; they just want to bless it before it passes.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कहहिं परस्पर नारि बारि बिलोचन पुलक तन। सखि सबु करब पुरारि पुन्य पयोनिधि भूप दोउ ॥
translation: नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भरकर पुलकित शरीर से स्त्रियाँ आपस में कह रही हैं कि हे सखी! दोनों राजा पुण्य के समुद्र हैं, त्रिपुरारी शिवजी सब मनोरथ पूर्ण करेंगे ॥
english_translation: With eyes full of tears and bodies thrilled with joy, the women say to one another, "Sakhi, both kings are oceans of merit; Tripurari Shiva will fulfill every wish."
essence: Wonder makes the heart trust before the outcome arrives.
simple_meaning: The women at Sita's swayamvar are so moved that they weep and thrill with joy. They praise both kings as highly virtuous and trust Shiva to fulfill their hopes.
insight: It turns attention from dry observation to shared wonder and hopeful reverence.
modern_relevance: You sit in a crowded hall watching two people step forward for a life-changing choice, and the whole room leans in. Everyone can feel that something sacred is about to happen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि बिधि सकल मनोरथ करहीं। आनँद उमगि उमगि उर भरहीं॥ जे नृप सीय स्वयंबर आए। देखि बंधु सब तिन्ह सुख पाए ॥
translation: इस प्रकार सब मनोरथ कर रही हैं और हृदय को उमंग-उमंगकर (उत्साहपूर्वक) आनंद से भर रही हैं। सीताजी के स्वयंवर में जो राजा आए थे, उन्होंने भी चारों भाइयों को देखकर सुख पाया ॥
english_translation: In this way, everyone was making their hearts' wishes come true, their hearts overflowing with joy. The kings who had come to Sita's swayamvar also felt delight on seeing the four brothers.
essence: Noble presence can quiet rivalry before it starts.
simple_meaning: Everyone at the swayamvar feels joy. The kings are pleased just seeing Ram and his brothers.
insight: It shifts attention from rivalry to shared delight in noble presence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where even strangers soften for a moment. Before anyone competes, the room itself seems to bless certain people with presence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहत राम जसु बिसद बिसाला। निज निज भवन गए महिपाला॥ गए बीति कछु दिन एहि भाँती। प्रमुदित पुरजन सकल बराती ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का निर्मल और महान यश कहते हुए राजा लोग अपने-अपने घर गए। इस प्रकार कुछ दिन बीत गए। जनकपुर निवासी और बाराती सभी बड़े आनंदित हैं ॥
english_translation: The kings returned to their own homes while speaking of Ram's pure, vast glory. In this way, some days passed. The people of Janakpur and all the wedding guests remained delighted.
essence: Ram's glory leaves people joyful even after they go home.
simple_meaning: The kings went home praising Ram, and the wedding party stayed joyful as days passed.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the atmosphere devotion creates around it.
modern_relevance: You leave a ceremony still talking about one person’s grace, and the whole group feels brighter for it. Some moments keep their glow long after the crowd disperses.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंगल मूल लगन दिनु आवा। हिम रितु अगहनु मासु सुहावा॥ ग्रह तिथि नखतु जोगु बर बारू। लगन सोधि बिधि कीन्ह बिचारू ॥
translation: मंगलों का मूल लग्न का दिन आ गया। हेमंत ऋतु और सुहावना अगहन का महीना था। ग्रह, तिथि, नक्षत्र, योग और वार श्रेष्ठ थे। लग्न (मुहूर्त) शोधकर ब्रह्माजी ने उस पर विचार किया, ॥
english_translation: The auspicious wedding day arrived. It was the pleasant winter month of Magha. The planets, date, star, yoga, and weekday were all favorable. After checking the auspicious time, Brahma considered the match.
essence: A sacred moment arrives when every sign is in harmony.
simple_meaning: The wedding day arrives at the right season and under the right stars. Everything is arranged for the ceremony to begin.
insight: It shifts attention from human planning to the feeling of perfect timing before an important event.
modern_relevance: The room is finally ready, the guests are seated, and the one person you were waiting for has arrived. Before the ceremony begins, you feel that rare sense that everything has come together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पठै दीन्हि नारद सन सोई। गनी जनक के गनकन्ह जोई॥ सुनी सकल लोगन्ह यह बाता। कहहिं जोतिषी आहिं बिधाता ॥
translation: और उस (लग्न पत्रिका) को नारदजी के हाथ (जनकजी के यहाँ) भेज दिया। जनकजी के ज्योतिषियों ने भी वही गणना कर रखी थी। जब सब लोगों ने यह बात सुनी तब वे कहने लगे- यहाँ के ज्योतिषी भी ब्रह्मा ही हैं ॥
english_translation: He sent that horoscope through Narada. Janaka's astrologers had made the same calculation. When everyone heard this, they said, "The astrologers here are like Brahma himself."
essence: Perfect timing is confirmed when careful minds arrive at the same answer.
simple_meaning: Janak sent the horoscope through Narada, and his own astrologers reached the same conclusion. Everyone was amazed by their accuracy.
insight: It highlights verified timing and shared confidence, not personal opinion.
modern_relevance: You double-check the numbers before a major launch, and your team arrives at the same answer from different angles. That quiet agreement builds confidence before the big moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धेनुधूरि बेला बिमल सकल सुमंगल मूल। बिप्रन्ह कहेउ बिदेह सन जानि सगुन अनुकूल ॥
translation: निर्मल और सभी सुंदर मंगलों की मूल गोधूलि की पवित्र बेला आ गई और अनुकूल शकुन होने लगे, यह जानकर ब्राह्मणों ने जनकजी से कहा ॥
english_translation: The pure dusk hour arrived, the source of all auspiciousness. Seeing favorable omens, the Brahmins told King Janaka.
essence: Favorable timing announces what should happen next.
simple_meaning: The auspicious dusk hour arrived, and the Brahmins saw that the signs were favorable, so they informed Janaka.
insight: It shifts attention from forcing events to recognizing when conditions are ready.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet before the ceremony begins. The planner checks the sky, the clock, the faces in the crowd — and knows the moment has come to proceed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उपरोहितहि कहेउ नरनाहा। अब बिलंब कर कारनु काहा॥ सतानंद तब सचिव बोलाए। मंगल सकल साजि सब ल्याए ॥
translation: तब राजा जनक ने पुरोहित शतानंदजी से कहा कि अब देरी का क्या कारण है। तब शतानंदजी ने मंत्रियों को बुलाया। वे सब मंगल का सामान सजाकर ले आए ॥
english_translation: Then King Janak said to the priest, “Why is there still delay?” Shatanand then called the ministers, and they brought all the auspicious preparations.
essence: A sacred event still depends on practical readiness.
simple_meaning: Janak asks why the ceremony is delayed, and Shatanand calls the ministers to bring the auspicious items.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the discipline of making readiness happen.
modern_relevance: The guests are waiting, the room is set, and one missing detail keeps the whole event on hold. Someone has to notice, speak up, and get the preparations moving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: संख निसान पनव बहु बाजे। मंगल कलस सगुन सुभ साजे॥ सुभग सुआसिनि गावहिं गीता। करहिं बेद धुनि बिप्र पुनीता ॥
translation: शंख, नगाड़े, ढोल और बहुत से बाजे बजने लगे तथा मंगल कलश और शुभ शकुन की वस्तुएँ (दधि, दूर्वा आदि) सजाई गईं। सुंदर सुहागिन स्त्रियाँ गीत गा रही हैं और पवित्र ब्राह्मण वेद की ध्वनि कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Conches, drums, and many other instruments began to sound. Auspicious pots and other good omens were arranged. Beautiful married women sang songs, and pure Brahmins chanted the Vedas.
essence: A sacred occasion is announced by music, ritual, and shared joy.
simple_meaning: The wedding preparations are in full swing: music, auspicious symbols, women singing, and Brahmins chanting sacred sounds.
insight: It frames a sacred occasion as something carried by community, ritual, and shared anticipation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लेन चले सादर एहि भाँती। गए जहाँ जनवास बराती॥ कोसलपति कर देखि समाजू। अति लघु लाग तिन्हहि सुरराजू ॥
translation: सब लोग इस प्रकार आदरपूर्वक बारात को लेने चले और जहाँ बारातियों का जनवासा था, वहाँ गए। अवधपति दशरथजी का समाज (वैभव) देखकर उनको देवराज इन्द्र भी बहुत ही तुच्छ लगने लगे ॥
english_translation: They went forth respectfully to receive the wedding party and reached the place where the guests were staying. Seeing the assembly of King of Kosala, even Indra seemed very small to them.
essence: True dignity can make even heaven's king seem small.
simple_meaning: The wedding party is formally received and brought to the guest area. Janak's court is so grand that even Indra seems insignificant beside it.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary comparison to the felt grandeur of a properly honoured gathering.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hall dressed for a family wedding and stop for a second — the lights, the flowers, the order, the dignity. Some spaces announce respect before anyone speaks.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भयउ समउ अब धारिअ पाऊ। यह सुनि परा निसानहिं घाऊ ॥ गुरहि पूछि करि कुल बिधि राजा। चले संग मुनि साधु समाजा ॥
translation: (उन्होंने जाकर विनती की-) समय हो गया, अब पधारिए। यह सुनते ही नगाड़ों पर चोट पड़ी। गुरु वशिष्ठजी से पूछकर और कुल की सब रीतियों को करके राजा दशरथजी मुनियों और साधुओं के समाज को साथ लेकर चले ॥
english_translation: “The time has come; please come now.” Hearing this, the drums were struck. After consulting Guru Vashistha and following the family rites, King Dasharath set out with the sages and holy men.
essence: Right action moves with guidance and timing.
simple_meaning: The wedding procession is set in motion. Dasharath follows the proper rites, consults his teacher, and goes forward with sages and holy men.
insight: It teaches that important action should be guided by counsel and custom, not haste.
modern_relevance: A family gathering is ready, the elders are waiting, and you do not rush ahead on impulse. You pause, ask the right person, and move in the right order.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भाग्य बिभव अवधेस कर देखि देव ब्रह्मादि। लगे सराहन सहस मुख जानि जनम निज बादि ॥
translation: अवध नरेश दशरथजी का भाग्य और वैभव देखकर और अपना जन्म व्यर्थ समझकर, ब्रह्माजी आदि देवता हजारों मुखों से उसकी सराहना करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Seeing the fortune and splendor of the king of Ayodhya, Brahma and the other radiant beings praised him with a thousand mouths, considering their own births wasted.
essence: Great fortune can make even the radiant beings feel small.
simple_meaning: The heavenly beings see Dasharath's good fortune and greatness and praise him intensely, feeling their own births were less fruitful by comparison.
insight: It shifts attention from status alone to the virtue and fortune that make a life worthy of praise.
modern_relevance: You walk into a celebration where everything is effortless, warm, and full of grace. The room itself seems to honor someone’s character, not just their status.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुरन्ह सुमंगल अवसरु जाना। बरषहिं सुमन बजाइ निसाना॥ सिव ब्रह्मादिक बिबुध बरूथा। चढ़े बिमानन्हि नाना जूथा ॥
translation: देवगण सुंदर मंगल का अवसर जानकर, नगाड़े बजा-बजाकर फूल बरसाते हैं। शिवजी, ब्रह्माजी आदि देववृन्द यूथ (टोलियाँ) बना-बनाकर विमानों पर जा चढ़े ॥
english_translation: The radiant beings knew the moment was auspicious. They showered flowers and beat their drums. Shiva, Brahma, and other exalted hosts rose in many groups aboard their celestial vehicles.
essence: A truly blessed moment draws even the heavens into celebration.
simple_meaning: The heavenly beings recognize the wedding time as deeply auspicious, so they celebrate with flowers, drums, and celestial processions.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary ceremony to the sense that some events reveal a larger order.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall falls quiet for a second, then erupts in cheers as the couple enters. Everyone can feel it: this is one of those rare moments that carries its own blessing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रेम पुलक तन हृदयँ उछाहू। चले बिलोकन राम बिआहू॥ देखि जनकपुरु सुर अनुरागे। निज निज लोक सबहिं लघु लागे ॥
translation: और प्रेम से पुलकित शरीर हो तथा हृदय में उत्साह भरकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी का विवाह देखने चले। जनकपुर को देखकर देवता इतने अनुरक्त हो गए कि उन सबको अपने-अपने लोक बहुत तुच्छ लगने लगे ॥
english_translation: Filled with love, their bodies thrilled and hearts joyful, they went to behold Ram's wedding. Seeing Janakpur, the radiant beings became so enamored that all their own realms seemed small.
essence: Beauty so complete makes even paradise feel small.
simple_meaning: The radiant beings go joyfully to see Ram's wedding. Janakpur's beauty makes even their own heavenly realms feel small.
insight: It shifts attention from possession to wonder, showing how beauty can dissolve pride in status.
modern_relevance: You step into a wedding hall glowing with flowers, music, and faces lit by joy. For a moment, every other place you know feels dull beside it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चितवहिं चकित बिचित्र बिताना। रचना सकल अलौकिक नाना। नगर नारि नर रूप निधाना। सुघर सुधरम सुसील सुजाना ॥
translation: विचित्र मंडप को तथा नाना प्रकार की सब अलौकिक रचनाओं को वे चकित होकर देख रहे हैं। नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष रूप के भंडार, सुघड़, श्रेष्ठ धर्मात्मा, सुशील और सुजान हैं ॥
english_translation: They gaze in wonder at the wondrous pavilion and all its many otherworldly designs. The men and women of the city are treasures of beauty, well-formed, virtuous, gentle, and wise.
essence: A sacred scene can make even the divine pause in wonder.
simple_meaning: The heavenly visitors are amazed by the wedding pavilion, the many strange decorations, and the beauty and goodness of the city’s people.
insight: It slows the reader into attentive wonder before the celebration’s meaning is revealed.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall lit like a dream, and for a second everyone falls quiet. Beauty, order, and kindness can still stop the mind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तिन्हहि देखि सब सुर सुरनारीं। भए नखत जनु बिधु उजिआरीं॥ बिधिहि भयउ आचरजु बिसेषी। निज करनी कछु कतहुँ न देखी ॥
translation: उन्हें देखकर सब देवता और देवांगनाएँ ऐसे प्रभाहीन हो गए जैसे चन्द्रमा के उजियाले में तारागण फीके पड़ जाते हैं। ब्रह्माजी को विशेष आश्चर्य हुआ, क्योंकि वहाँ उन्होंने अपनी कोई करनी (रचना) तो कहीं देखी ही नहीं ॥
english_translation: Seeing them, all the devas and celestial women shone like stars in moonlight. Brahma felt a special wonder, for he could not see his own handiwork there.
essence: Creation falls silent before a beauty it cannot explain.
simple_meaning: The divine beings are overwhelmed by what they see, and even Brahma is astonished because his own creation cannot account for it.
insight: It shifts attention from human design to a reality that can surpass design itself.
