The lovely brides and handsome grooms stand together in one pavilion, like the four states of consciousness with their lords enthroned in the heart.
essence: Perfect pairing makes the whole scene feel like inner harmony made visible.
simple_meaning: The wedding pavilion is full of matched couples, quiet joy, praise, and celebration. The poet compares that harmony to the four states of consciousness shining together in the heart.
insight: It turns a wedding scene into a vision of inner order and completeness.
modern_relevance: At a wedding where everyone keeps pausing to look at the couples, the room itself feels arranged by grace. The verse notices that rare moment when outer harmony and inner delight seem to mirror each other.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुदित अवधपति सकल सुत बधुन्ह समेत निहारि। जनु पाए महिपाल मनि क्रियन्ह सहित फल चारि ॥
translation: सब पुत्रों को बहुओं सहित देखकर अवध नरेश दशरथजी ऐसे आनंदित हैं, मानो वे राजाओं के शिरोमणि क्रियाओं (यज्ञक्रिया, श्रद्धाक्रिया, योगक्रिया और ज्ञानक्रिया) सहित चारों फल (अर्थ, धर्म, काम और मोक्ष) पा गए हों ॥
english_translation: Seeing all his sons and daughters-in-law together, the king of Ayodhya was delighted, as if a ruler of kings had obtained the four aims of life along with the four kinds of sacred acts.
essence: True fulfillment can look like everyone you love gathered in one place.
simple_meaning: Dasharath feels deep joy seeing all his sons and daughters-in-law together. It feels to him like a king has gained the four aims of life and the four sacred acts.
insight: It turns achievement into gratitude, showing that wholeness can be felt in family togetherness.
modern_relevance: You stand at the wedding reception watching both families laugh across one long table. For one quiet minute, the years of worry, planning, and longing feel worth it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जसि रघुबीर ब्याह बिधि बरनी। सकल कुअँर ब्याहे तेहिं करनी॥ कहि न जा कछु दाइज भूरी। रहा कनक मनि मंडपु पूरी ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विवाह की जैसी विधि वर्णन की गई, उसी रीति से सब राजकुमार विवाहे गए। दहेज की अधिकता कुछ कही नहीं जाती, सारा मंडप सोने और मणियों से भर गया ॥
english_translation: The wedding of Ram was arranged in that same manner, and all the princes were married likewise. The gifts were beyond counting; the marriage pavilion was filled with gold and jewels.
essence: Blessing becomes visible when joy fills every detail.
simple_meaning: The princes were all married in the same grand way as Ram, with an enormous amount of gifts and a pavilion full of gold and jewels.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony as cost to ceremony as overflowing blessing.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall glows under chandeliers, gifts stacked to the ceiling, relatives smiling through tears. The event feels bigger than expense — it feels like shared joy made tangible.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कंबल बसन बिचित्र पटोरे। भाँति भाँति बहु मोल न थोरे॥ गज रथ तुरगदास अरु दासी। धेनु अलंकृत कामदुहा सी ॥
translation: बहुत से कम्बल, वस्त्र और भाँति-भाँति के विचित्र रेशमी कपड़े, जो थोड़ी कीमत के न थे (अर्थात बहुमूल्य थे) तथा हाथी, रथ, घोड़े, दास-दासियाँ और गहनों से सजी हुई कामधेनु सरीखी गायें- ॥
english_translation: Blankets, garments, and many kinds of rich silk cloths; elephants, chariots, horses, servants, maidservants, and a cow adorned like wish-fulfilling Kamadhenu.
essence: Abundance becomes visible through the list itself.
simple_meaning: The wedding gifts were lavish: fine cloth, animals, servants, and richly adorned cows. The list is part of a scene showing overwhelming abundance.
insight: It shifts attention from the single object to the sheer scale of giving.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall filled with stacked gift boxes, silk bags, and flower-covered trays tells its own story before anyone speaks. Some moments are so full that listing the details becomes the point.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बस्तु अनेक करिअ किमि लेखा। कहि न जाइ जानहिं जिन्ह देखा॥ लोकपाल अवलोकि सिहाने। लीन्ह अवधपति सबु सुखु माने ॥
translation: (आदि) अनेकों वस्तुएँ हैं, जिनकी गिनती कैसे की जाए। उनका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता, जिन्होंने देखा है, वही जानते हैं। उन्हें देखकर लोकपाल भी सिहा गए। अवधराज दशरथजी ने सुख मानकर प्रसन्नचित्त से सब कुछ ग्रहण किया ॥
english_translation: Countless gifts cannot be numbered or fully described. Even the guardians of the worlds were astonished, and King Dasharatha accepted everything with delight.
essence: Overflowing joy makes counting impossible.
simple_meaning: The wedding gifts were so many they could not be counted or fully described. Even the guardians of the worlds were amazed, and Dasharatha gladly accepted everything.
insight: It shifts attention from tallying possessions to recognizing the fullness of a blessed moment.
modern_relevance: You open the wedding hall door and see gifts stacked to the ceiling, relatives buzzing, and nothing left to explain. Some joy is too full for accounting.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दीन्ह जाचकन्हि जो जेहि भावा। उबरा सो जनवासेहिं आवा॥ तब कर जोरि जनकु मृदु बानी। बोले सब बरात सनमानी ॥
translation: उन्होंने वह दहेज का सामान याचकों को, जो जिसे अच्छा लगा, दे दिया। जो बच रहा, वह जनवासे में चला आया। तब जनकजी हाथ जोड़कर सारी बारात का सम्मान करते हुए कोमल वाणी से बोले ॥
english_translation: They gave away whatever each beggar desired, and what remained went to the bridal lodging. Then Janak folded his hands and, honoring the whole wedding party, spoke gently.
essence: Generosity and courtesy turn abundance into grace.
simple_meaning: Janak gives away the wedding gifts freely, then welcomes the whole wedding party with respectful, gentle words.
insight: It shifts attention from possession to hospitality, showing that wealth becomes meaningful only when shared and offered with respect.
modern_relevance: After a big family celebration, you notice the leftovers, the gifts, the extra plates, the last details. Someone still makes sure every guest leaves feeling honored. That quiet dignity is the point here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सनमानि सकल बरात आदर दान बिनय बड़ाइ कै। प्रमुदित महामुनि बृंद बंदे पूजि प्रेम लड़ाइ कै॥ सिरु नाइ देव मनाइ सब सन कहत कर संपुट किएँ। सुर साधु चाहत भाउ सिंधु कि तोष जल अंजलि दिएँ ॥
translation: आदर, दान, विनय और बड़ाई के द्वारा सारी बारात का सम्मान कर राजा जनक ने महान आनंद के साथ प्रेमपूर्वक लड़ाकर (लाड़ करके) मुनियों के समूह की पूजा एवं वंदना की। सिर नवाकर, देवताओं को मनाकर, राजा हाथ जोड़कर सबसे कहने लगे कि देवता और साधु तो भाव ही चाहते हैं, (वे प्रेम से ही प्रसन्न हो जाते हैं, उन पूर्णकाम महानुभावों को कोई कुछ देकर कैसे संतुष्ट कर सकता है), क्या एक अंजलि जल देने से कहीं समुद्र संतुष्ट हो सकता है ॥
english_translation: King Janaka honored the entire wedding party with respect, gifts, humility, and praise. The delighted sages were bowed to and worshiped with loving affection. Bowing his head, pleasing the devas, and joining his palms, he said to all that devas and saints desire only devotion; how could a handful of water satisfy the ocean?
essence: Devotion, not display, reaches what offerings cannot.
simple_meaning: Janaka honors the whole wedding party and says that saints and radiant beings want loving devotion, not material offerings.
insight: It shifts attention from external generosity to the quality of feeling behind it.
modern_relevance: You bring expensive flowers to a teacher’s farewell, but what they remember is your honest gratitude and steady care. Janaka’s insight cuts through performance: heartfelt reverence matters more than impressive giving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कर जोरि जनकु बहोरि बंधु समेत कोसलराय सों। बोले मनोहर बयन सानि सनेह सील सुभाय सों॥ संबंध राजन रावरें हम बड़े अब सब बिधि भए। एहि राज साज समेत सेवक जानिबे बिनु गथ लए ॥
translation: फिर जनकजी भाई सहित हाथ जोड़कर कोसलाधीश दशरथजी से स्नेह, शील और सुंदर प्रेम में सानकर मनोहर वचन बोले- हे राजन् ! आपके साथ संबंध हो जाने से अब हम सब प्रकार से बड़े हो गए। इस राज-पाट सहित हम दोनों को आप बिना दाम के लिए हुए सेवक ही समझिएगा ॥
english_translation: Then Janak, with his brothers, joined his hands and spoke charming words to the king of Kosala, sweetened by affection, gentleness, and grace: “Our relation with you has made us great in every way. Regard us, along with this royal wealth, as your servants taken without payment.”
essence: True dignity bows and calls itself a servant.
simple_meaning: Janak greets Dasharath with humility and says their new bond has made them greater, not lesser. He asks to be treated as servants, not as owners of the royal gifts.
insight: It teaches you to meet honor with humility, and to treat relationship as a gift rather than a bargain.
modern_relevance: At a wedding, one family tries to outdo the other with status and expense. Janak does the opposite: he lowers himself, honors the bond, and makes generosity feel sacred instead of transactional.
speaker: Janak

verse_text: ए दारिका परिचारिका करि पालिबीं करुना नई। अपराधु छमिबो बोलि पठए बहुत हौं ढीट्यो कई॥ पुनि भानुकुलभूषन सकल सनमान निधि समधी किए। कहि जाति नहिं बिनती परस्पर प्रेम परिपूरन हिए ॥
translation: इन लड़कियों को टहलनी मानकर, नई-नई दया करके पालन कीजिएगा। मैंने बड़ी ढिठाई की कि आपको यहाँ बुला भेजा, अपराध क्षमा कीजिएगा। फिर सूर्यकुल के भूषण दशरथजी ने समधी जनकजी को सम्पूर्ण सम्मान का निधि कर दिया (इतना सम्मान किया कि वे सम्मान के भंडार ही हो गए)। उनकी परस्पर की विनय कही नहीं जाती, दोनों के हृदय प्रेम से परिपूर्ण हैं ॥
english_translation: Please treat these girls as attendants and raise them with fresh compassion. Forgive my boldness in having sent for you. Then the jewel of the solar line, Dasharatha, made King Janaka a treasury of honor. Their mutual humility cannot be described; both hearts were filled with love.
essence: Humility turns ceremony into love.
simple_meaning: Janaka humbly asks Dasharatha to care for the girls with kindness and forgive his boldness. Dasharatha responds with such honor that both families overflow with mutual love.
insight: It shifts attention from social formality to the quality of humility that creates genuine closeness.
modern_relevance: At a wedding dinner, two families keep apologizing for small inconveniences and thanking each other for everything. The real gift is not the event itself — it is the tenderness that makes strangers feel like kin.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बृंदारका गन सुमन बरिसहिं राउ जनवासेहि चले। दुंदुभी जय धुनि बेद धुनि नभ नगर कौतूहल भले॥ तब सखीं मंगल गान करत मुनीस आयसु पाइ कै। दूल्हे दुलहिनिन्ह सहित सुंदरि चलीं कोहबर ल्याइ कै ॥
translation: देवतागण फूल बरसा रहे हैं, राजा जनवासे को चले। नगाड़े की ध्वनि, जयध्वनि और वेद की ध्वनि हो रही है, आकाश और नगर दोनों में खूब कौतूहल हो रहा है (आनंद छा रहा है), तब मुनीश्वर की आज्ञा पाकर सुंदरी सखियाँ मंगलगान करती हुई दुलहिनों सहित दूल्हों को लिवाकर कोहबर को चलीं ॥
english_translation: The divine beings shower flowers. The king goes to the wedding pavilion. Drumbeats, victory cries, and Vedic chants fill the sky and the city with joy. Then, after receiving the sage's command, the beautiful bridesmaids sing auspicious songs and lead the brides and grooms to the wedding chamber.
essence: Joy spills outward when a holy union begins.
simple_meaning: The wedding procession moves forward in celebration. Flowers fall from above, drums and chants fill the air, and the bridesmaids lead the couples toward the wedding chamber.
insight: It shifts attention from the couple alone to the shared joy that surrounds a sacred union.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a wedding hall before the ceremony, and every corridor hums with music, perfume, and anticipation. Even strangers smile. Some moments make an entire place feel blessed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि पुनि रामहि चितव सिय सकुचति मनु सकुचै न। हरत मनोहर मीन छबि प्रेम पिआसे नैन ॥
translation: सीताजी बार-बार रामजी को देखती हैं और सकुचा जाती हैं, पर उनका मन नहीं सकुचाता। प्रेम के प्यासे उनके नेत्र सुंदर मछलियों की छबि को हर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Sita looks at Ram again and again and grows shy; her mind does not grow shy. Her eyes, thirsty for love, keep drinking in his beautiful fish-like eyes.
essence: Shyness can hide a heart already surrendered.
simple_meaning: Sita keeps looking at Ram and feels shy, but her mind is fully drawn to him. Her eyes cannot stop drinking in his beauty.
insight: It shows how devotion can be hidden in restraint: outward modesty, inward absorption.
modern_relevance: You catch yourself glancing at someone across a crowded room, then looking away too quickly. The face goes shy; the attention does not. That split is human.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: स्याम सरीरु सुभायँ सुहावन। सोभा कोटि मनोज लजावन॥ जावक जुत पद कमल सुहाए। मुनि मन मधुप रहत जिन्ह छाए ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का साँवला शरीर स्वभाव से ही सुंदर है। उसकी शोभा करोड़ों कामदेवों को लजाने वाली है। महावर से युक्त चरण कमल बड़े सुहावने लगते हैं, जिन पर मुनियों के मन रूपी भौंरे सदा छाए रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram's dark body is naturally beautiful. Its splendor shames millions of Cupids. His lovely lotus feet, adorned with red dye, are where the minds of sages stay like bees.
essence: Ram's beauty silences every lesser charm and holds the heart still.
simple_meaning: Ram's dark form is naturally beautiful, and even the most enchanting beauty seems small beside it. His feet draw the minds of sages the way bees gather around flowers.
insight: It shifts attention from surface glamour to the kind of beauty that naturally draws devotion.
modern_relevance: You scroll past polished faces, curated profiles, and perfect lighting, then meet someone whose calm presence stops you cold. Real beauty doesn't need performance; it quietly commands attention.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: पीत पुनीत मनोहर धोती। हरति बाल रबि दामिनि जोती॥ कल किंकिनि कटि सूत्र मनोहर। बाहु बिसाल बिभूषन सुंदर ॥
translation: पवित्र और मनोहर पीली धोती प्रातःकाल के सूर्य और बिजली की ज्योति को हरे लेती है। कमर में सुंदर किंकिणी और कटिसूत्र हैं। विशाल भुजाओं में सुंदर आभूषण सुशोभित हैं ॥
english_translation: The pure yellow cloth is beautiful and radiant, outshining the morning sun and lightning. Lovely bells and a waist cord adorn the waist. Beautiful ornaments shine on the broad arms.
essence: Radiant adornment turns a moment into a sacred event.
simple_meaning: Ram's wedding attire is described in vivid detail: a bright yellow cloth, ornaments, bells, and a beautiful waist cord all add to his splendor.
insight: It trains the eye to notice how outer form can express inner significance.
modern_relevance: You see someone dressed for a once-in-a-lifetime ceremony, and every detail feels charged. The clothes are not just clothing anymore; they carry the weight of the moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पीत जनेउ महाछबि देई। कर मुद्रिका चोरि चितु लेई॥ सोहत ब्याह साज सब साजे। उर आयत उरभूषन राजे ॥
translation: पीला जनेऊ महान शोभा दे रहा है। हाथ की अँगूठी चित्त को चुरा लेती है। ब्याह के सब साज सजे हुए वे शोभा पा रहे हैं। चौड़ी छाती पर हृदय पर पहनने के सुंदर आभूषण सुशोभित हैं ॥
english_translation: The yellow sacred thread adds great beauty. The ring steals the mind. Every wedding ornament shines on the broad chest.
essence: Every ornament on Ram deepens the spell of his presence.
simple_meaning: Ram's wedding ornaments make him look even more radiant: the sacred thread, ring, and chest ornaments all add to his beauty.
insight: It trains attention on the harmony of small details that create an unforgettable whole.
modern_relevance: You see someone walk into a wedding hall, and the room shifts before they even speak. The right details do that: a thread, a ring, a necklace, all quietly announcing presence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पिअर उपरना काखासोती। दुहुँ आँचरन्हि लगे मनि मोती॥ नयन कमल कल कुंडल काना। बदनु सकल सौंदर्ज निदाना ॥
translation: पीला दुपट्टा काँखासोती (जनेऊ की तरह) शोभित है, जिसके दोनों छोरों पर मणि और मोती लगे हैं। कमल के समान सुंदर नेत्र हैं, कानों में सुंदर कुंडल हैं और मुख तो सारी सुंदरता का खजाना ही है ॥
english_translation: A yellow shawl shines on the shoulder, its two ends set with gems and pearls. Eyes are like lotuses, ears wear lovely earrings, and the face is the treasure-house of all beauty.
essence: Ram's beauty is calm, complete, and impossible to overlook.
simple_meaning: Ram is described as beautifully dressed and adorned, with a radiant face, lotus eyes, and earrings. The verse is pure praise of his appearance.
insight: It trains attention toward grace, poise, and inner composure expressed through form.
modern_relevance: You notice someone enter a room and the whole atmosphere changes. Nothing flashy, nothing forced — just a quiet radiance that makes everyone look twice.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुंदर भृकुटि मनोहर नासा। भाल तिलकु रुचिरता निवासा॥ सोहत मौरु मनोहर माथे। मंगलमय मुकुता मनि गाथे ॥
translation: सुंदर भौंहें और मनोहर नासिका है। ललाट पर तिलक तो सुंदरता का घर ही है, जिसमें मंगलमय मोती और मणि गुँथे हुए हैं, ऐसा मनोहर मौर माथे पर सोह रहा है ॥
english_translation: Beautiful eyebrows and a lovely nose. The tilak on the forehead seems like a home of beauty, with auspicious pearls and gems woven into the graceful crown on the head.
essence: Beauty here is not decoration; it announces sacred presence.
simple_meaning: The groom is described as dazzlingly beautiful, with lovely features, a bright tilak, and an ornamented crown.
insight: It slows the reader down to notice how form itself can carry reverence.
modern_relevance: You catch someone across a crowded room and every detail feels radiant at once. The mind stops arguing and simply sees beauty.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गाथे महामनि मौर मंजुल अंग सब चित चोरहीं। पुर नारि सुर सुंदरीं बरहि बिलोकि सब तिन तोरहीं॥ मनि बसन भूषन वारि आरति करहिं मंगल गावहीं। सुर सुमन बरिसहिं सूत मागध बंदि सुजसु सुनावहीं ॥
translation: सुंदर मौर में बहुमूल्य मणियाँ गुँथी हुई हैं, सभी अंग चित्त को चुराए लेते हैं। सब नगर की स्त्रियाँ और देवसुंदरियाँ दूल्हे को देखकर तिनका तोड़ रही हैं (उनकी बलैयाँ ले रही हैं) और मणि, वस्त्र तथा आभूषण निछावर करके आरती उतार रही और मंगलगान कर रही हैं। देवता फूल बरसा रहे हैं और सूत, मागध तथा भाट सुयश सुना रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The groom’s jeweled crest and graceful limbs steal every heart. Townswomen and celestial beauties gaze at him, offer worship, sing blessings, shower gifts, and proclaim his fame.
essence: Ram’s presence draws worship before anyone speaks.
simple_meaning: Ram appears so beautiful at the wedding that everyone is captivated. Women, celestial beings, and singers all honor him with gifts, songs, flowers, and praise.
insight: It shifts attention from performance to presence: when character is radiant, recognition follows naturally.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the mood changes before you say a word. Not because you demanded attention, but because your presence carried something worth honoring.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोहबरहिं आने कुअँर कुअँरि सुआसिनिन्ह सुख पाइ कै। अति प्रीति लौकिक रीति लागीं करन मंगल गाइ कै॥ लहकौरि गौरि सिखाव रामहि सीय सन सारद कहैं। रनिवासु हास बिलास रस बस जन्म को फलु सब लहैं ॥
translation: सुहागिनी स्त्रियाँ सुख पाकर कुँअर और कुमारियों को कोहबर (कुलदेवता के स्थान) में लाईं और अत्यन्त प्रेम से मंगल गीत गा-गाकर लौकिक रीति करने लगीं। पार्वतीजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी को लहकौर (वर-वधू का परस्पर ग्रास देना) सिखाती हैं और सरस्वतीजी सीताजी को सिखाती हैं। रनिवास हास-विलास के आनंद में मग्न है, (श्री रामजी और सीताजी को देख-देखकर) सभी जन्म का परम फल प्राप्त कर रही हैं ॥
english_translation: The married women brought the prince and princess into the wedding chamber, singing auspicious songs with deep affection and following the customary rites. Parvati teaches Ram the bride-groom’s first morsel, Saraswati teaches Sita, and the palace women, lost in laughter and delight, feel they have gained the fruit of all their births by seeing Ram and Sita.
essence: Seeing Ram and Sita makes life feel complete.
simple_meaning: The wedding chamber fills with joy, songs, and ritual. Everyone feels that seeing Ram and Sita is the highest blessing of life.
insight: It shifts attention from ritual as form to ritual as shared wonder and fulfillment.
modern_relevance: At a wedding where the room goes quiet the moment the couple enters, everyone feels it: this is more than ceremony. The joy in the room becomes its own blessing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निज पानि मनि महुँ देखिअति मूरति सुरूपनिधान की। चालति न भुजबल्ली बिलोकनि बिरह भय बस जानकी॥ कौतुक बिनोद प्रमोदु प्रेमु न जाइ कहि जानहिं अलीं। बर कुअँरि सुंदर सकल सखीं लवाइ जनवासेहि चलीं ॥
translation: 'अपने हाथ की मणियों में सुंदर रूप के भण्डार श्री रामचन्द्रजी की परछाहीं दिख रही है। यह देखकर जानकीजी दर्शन में वियोग होने के भय से बाहु रूपी लता को और दृष्टि को हिलाती-डुलाती नहीं हैं। उस समय के हँसी-खेल और विनोद का आनंद और प्रेम कहा नहीं जा सकता, उसे सखियाँ ही जानती हैं। तदनन्तर वर-कन्याओं को सब सुंदर सखियाँ जनवासे को लिवा चलीं ॥
english_translation: In the jewels in her hand, Janaki sees the beautiful form of Ram. Fearful of separation, she does not move her arms or her gaze. The laughter, play, delight, and love of that moment cannot be described; only the companions know it. Then the beautiful attendants led the bride and groom to the marriage pavilion.
essence: A single glimpse of Ram makes the heart afraid to blink.
simple_meaning: Janaki sees Ram’s image reflected in her jewels and becomes afraid of losing that sight. She stays still, while the wedding party moves the bride and groom toward the marriage pavilion.
insight: It shifts attention from the ceremony itself to the intensity of seeing Ram, where devotion freezes motion.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone you love across a crowded room and suddenly everything else fades. You do not want the moment to end; you want to keep looking.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहि समय सुनिअ असीस जहँ तहँ नगर नभ आनँदु महा। चिरु जिअहुँ जोरीं चारु चार् यो मुदित मन सबहीं कहा॥ जोगींद्र सिद्ध मुनीस देव बिलोकि प्रभु दुंदुभि हनी। चले हरषि बरषि प्रसून निज निज लोक जय जय जय भनी ॥
translation: उस समय नगर और आकाश में जहाँ सुनिए, वहीं आशीर्वाद की ध्वनि सुनाई दे रही है और महान आनंद छाया है। सभी ने प्रसन्न मन से कहा कि सुंदर चारों जोड़ियाँ चिरंजीवी हों। योगीराज, सिद्ध, मुनीश्वर और देवताओं ने प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर दुन्दुभी बजाई और हर्षित होकर फूलों की वर्षा करते हुए तथा 'जय हो, जय हो, जय हो' कहते हुए वे अपने-अपने लोक को चले ॥
english_translation: At that time, blessings were heard everywhere in the city and the sky was filled with great joy. Everyone, delighted, said, "May the four beautiful couples live long." The lords of yoga, the perfected sages, the great seers, and the radiant beings saw Lord Ram, beat their drums, showered flowers, and returned to their own realms crying, "Victory, victory, victory."
essence: Ram's presence makes even the heavens rejoice.
simple_meaning: The whole city and sky overflow with blessings and joy. Sages and radiant beings rejoice at Ram's sight, shower flowers, and return praising him.
insight: It turns the wedding into a cosmic celebration, showing Ram's presence as something the whole world recognizes.
modern_relevance: At a wedding when the room suddenly goes quiet and then erupts into blessings, you feel it: some joy is bigger than the people in the room. This verse lives in that overflowing moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सहित बधूटिन्ह कुअँर सब तब आए पितु पास। सोभा मंगल मोद भरि उमगेउ जनु जनवास ॥
translation: तब सब (चारों) कुमार बहुओं सहित पिताजी के पास आए। ऐसा मालूम होता था मानो शोभा, मंगल और आनंद से भरकर जनवासा उमड़ पड़ा हो ॥
english_translation: Then all the princes, along with their brides, came to their father. It seemed as if the bridal pavilion itself overflowed with beauty, auspiciousness, and joy.
essence: Joy becomes visible when a family comes together in harmony.
simple_meaning: The princes return with their brides to their father, and the whole wedding pavilion feels full of beauty and joy.
insight: It turns a family reunion into a picture of collective blessing and celebration.
modern_relevance: After a wedding, the whole house is still buzzing — relatives moving through rooms, laughter spilling into the hallway, everyone carrying the glow of something just completed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि जेवनार भई बहु भाँती। पठए जनक बोलाइ बराती॥ परत पाँवड़े बसन अनूपा। सुतन्ह समेत गवन कियो भूपा ॥
translation: फिर बहुत प्रकार की रसोई बनी। जनकजी ने बारातियों को बुला भेजा। राजा दशरथजी ने पुत्रों सहित गमन किया। अनुपम वस्त्रों के पाँवड़े पड़ते जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Then many kinds of food were prepared. Janak sent word to invite the wedding guests. King Dasharath set out with his sons, while splendid cloths were laid beneath their feet.
essence: Honor turns celebration into something larger than celebration.
simple_meaning: A grand feast was prepared, the wedding guests were invited, and Dasharath departed with his sons on beautifully laid cloths.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the reverence shown through preparation and welcome.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall fills with fragrance, relatives bustle through the rooms, and every detail is arranged to honor the moment. Some occasions become sacred simply because everyone present chooses care.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सादर सब के पाय पखारे। जथाजोगु पीढ़न्ह बैठारे॥ धोए जनक अवधपति चरना। सीलु सनेहु जाइ नहिं बरना ॥
translation: आदर के साथ सबके चरण धोए और सबको यथायोग्य पीढ़ों पर बैठाया। तब जनकजी ने अवधपति दशरथजी के चरण धोए। उनका शील और स्नेह वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
english_translation: With respect, everyone’s feet were washed and everyone was seated according to rank. Then Janaka washed the feet of the king of Ayodhya. His nobility and affection cannot be described.
essence: Honor becomes real when pride kneels before service.
simple_meaning: Janaka honors every guest properly, then personally washes Dasharath’s feet. The verse highlights his noble manners and heartfelt affection.
insight: It teaches that status is not lost by humility; it is revealed through it.
modern_relevance: You welcome guests into your home, then notice the oldest person at the table and quietly bring water yourself. No speech can match that kind of respect.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरि राम पद पंकज धोए। जे हर हृदय कमल महुँ गोए॥ तीनिउ भाइ राम सम जानी। धोए चरन जनक निज पानी ॥
translation: फिर श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणकमलों को धोया, जो श्री शिवजी के हृदय कमल में छिपे रहते हैं। तीनों भाइयों को श्री रामचन्द्रजी के समान जानकर जनकजी ने उनके भी चरण अपने हाथों से धोए ॥
english_translation: Then Janaka washed Ram's lotus feet, the feet that dwell in Shiva's lotus heart. Seeing all three brothers as equal to Ram, Janaka washed their feet with his own hands.
essence: Reverence becomes complete when it honors Ram in every brother.
simple_meaning: Janaka honors Ram by washing his feet, then does the same for Ram's brothers, seeing all three as equal in dignity.
insight: It shifts reverence from status to recognition: honor the divine presence, not just the most visible one.
modern_relevance: You meet someone famous at a family gathering, but you still make tea for their quieter sibling and ask their opinion too. Respect is real when it is not selective.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आसन उचित सबहि नृप दीन्हे। बोलि सूपकारी सब लीन्हे॥ सादर लगे परन पनवारे। कनक कील मनि पान सँवारे ॥
translation: राजा जनकजी ने सभी को उचित आसन दिए और सब परसने वालों को बुला लिया। आदर के साथ पत्तलें पड़ने लगीं, जो मणियों के पत्तों से सोने की कील लगाकर बनाई गई थीं ॥
english_translation: King Janaka gave everyone fitting seats and called the servers. Respectfully, leaf-plates were set out, adorned with jewels and fastened with golden pegs.
essence: Respect becomes visible in the smallest arrangements.
simple_meaning: Janaka arranges the feast with care and respect. Everyone is seated properly, and the serving plates are beautifully prepared.
insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to care: dignity is shown through how people are seated and served.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where the hosts have already noticed who needs a chair, who needs water, and who should be seated together. That quiet attention makes people feel seen before a word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सूपोदन सुरभी सरपि सुंदर स्वादु पुनीत। छन महुँ सब कें परुसि गे चतुर सुआर बिनीत ॥
translation: चतुर और विनीत रसोइए सुंदर, स्वादिष्ट और पवित्र दाल-भात और गाय का (सुगंधित) घी क्षण भर में सबके सामने परस गए ॥
english_translation: The wise and courteous cooks quickly served everyone with fragrant rice, lentils, ghee, and pure, delicious food.
essence: True honour is served as quickly as it is felt.
simple_meaning: The cooks served the meal quickly and respectfully, with fine food and ghee for everyone.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to care: real respect is making others comfortable without delay.
modern_relevance: A host notices the plates are still empty while guests keep glancing around the room. The meal arrives fast, warm, and thoughtful — and everyone feels seen before a word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पंच कवल करि जेवन लागे। गारि गान सुनि अति अनुरागे। भाँति अनेक परे पकवाने। सुधा सरिस नहिं जाहिं बखाने ॥
translation: सब लोग पंचकौर करके (अर्थात 'प्राणाय स्वाहा, अपानाय स्वाहा, व्यानाय स्वाहा, उदानाय स्वाहा और समानाय स्वाहा' इन मंत्रों का उच्चारण करते हुए पहले पाँच ग्रास लेकर) भोजन करने लगे। गाली का गाना सुनकर वे अत्यन्त प्रेममग्न हो गए। अनेकों तरह के अमृत के समान (स्वादिष्ट) पकवान परसे गए, जिनका बखान नहीं हो सकता ॥
english_translation: They began eating after taking the five mouthfuls. Hearing songs of abuse, they became deeply delighted. Many kinds of dishes were served; they were like nectar and beyond description.
essence: Abundance becomes memorable when it is offered with delight.
simple_meaning: Everyone started eating, delighted by the festive singing and the many dishes served. The food was so varied and exquisite that it could not be fully described.
insight: It shifts attention from the meal itself to the atmosphere of generous hospitality that surrounds it.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where the air is full of laughter, music, and the smell of fresh food. The details blur because the feeling is larger than the menu.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परुसन लगे सुआर सुजाना। बिंजन बिबिध नाम को जाना॥ चारि भाँति भोजन बिधि गाई। एक एक बिधि बरनि न जाई ॥
translation: चतुर रसोइए नाना प्रकार के व्यंजन परसने लगे, उनका नाम कौन जानता है। चार प्रकार के (चर्व्य, चोष्य, लेह्य, पेय अर्थात चबाकर, चूसकर, चाटकर और पीना-खाने योग्य) भोजन की विधि कही गई है, उनमें से एक-एक विधि के इतने पदार्थ बने थे कि जिनका वर्ण नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
english_translation: Skilled cooks began serving the dishes. Who could even name the many kinds of food? Four kinds of food were prepared, and each kind had so many varieties that they could not be fully described.
essence: Some abundance is too rich to be fully named.
simple_meaning: The cooks served many kinds of food, and the variety was beyond counting or description.
insight: It shifts attention from counting details to feeling the fullness of the offering.
modern_relevance: You open a festival menu and freeze for a second, smiling at how much care went into every dish. Some moments are so full that listing them feels smaller than simply receiving them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: छरस रुचिर बिंजन बहु जाती। एक एक रस अगनित भाँती॥ जेवँत देहिं मधुर धुनि गारी। लै लै नाम पुरुष अरु नारी ॥
translation: छहों रसों के बहुत तरह के सुंदर (स्वादिष्ट) व्यंजन हैं। एक-एक रस के अनगिनत प्रकार के बने हैं। भोजन के समय पुरुष और स्त्रियों के नाम ले-लेकर स्त्रियाँ मधुर ध्वनि से गाली दे रही हैं (गाली गा रही हैं) ॥
english_translation: There are many kinds of beautiful dishes, each taste in countless forms. As they eat, women sing playful scoldings in sweet voices, calling out the names of men and women.
essence: Delight multiplies when abundance is joined by playful song.
simple_meaning: The feast is overflowing with many kinds of delicious food, and the women add playful singing and teasing as everyone eats.
insight: It keeps the focus on atmosphere, showing how celebration is made complete by shared sound and social ease.
modern_relevance: A family gathering comes alive when the table is full, someone starts joking, and the room loosens into laughter. The memory is not just the food — it is the warmth around it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समय सुहावनि गारि बिराजा। हँसत राउ सुनि सहित समाजा॥ एहि बिधि सबहीं भोजनु कीन्हा। आदर सहित आचमनु दीन्हा ॥
translation: समय की सुहावनी गाली शोभित हो रही है। उसे सुनकर समाज सहित राजा दशरथजी हँस रहे हैं। इस रीति से सभी ने भोजन किया और तब सबको आदर सहित आचमन (हाथ-मुँह धोने के लिए जल) दिया गया ॥
english_translation: A pleasant jest adorned the moment. King Dasharath laughed with the assembled company upon hearing it. In this way everyone ate, and then water was respectfully given for rinsing the mouth.
essence: A joyful meal becomes memorable through laughter and respect.
simple_meaning: The feast was cheerful and respectful. Dasharath laughed with the gathered people, everyone ate, and water was served afterward.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony alone to the human warmth that makes ceremony alive.
modern_relevance: At a family wedding table, someone cracks a harmless joke and the whole room loosens at once. The best gatherings are remembered not just for food, but for ease, laughter, and respect.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देइ पान पूजे जनक दसरथु सहित समाज। जनवासेहि गवने मुदित सकल भूप सिरताज ॥
translation: फिर पान देकर जनकजी ने समाज सहित दशरथजी का पूजन किया। सब राजाओं के सिरमौर (चक्रवर्ती) श्री दशरथजी प्रसन्न होकर जनवासे को चले ॥
english_translation: Then Janaka offered betel leaf and honored Dasharatha with the assembled kings. Delighted, the crowned king Dasharatha went to the guest quarters.
essence: Honor turns a visit into blessing.
simple_meaning: Janaka honors Dasharatha and the gathered kings, then Dasharatha happily goes to the guest quarters.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the dignity created by respectful welcome.
modern_relevance: After a long wedding function, the host walks over with a respectful gesture, and the whole room softens. Small acts of honour can change the atmosphere instantly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नित नूतन मंगल पुर माहीं। निमिष सरिस दिन जामिनि जाहीं॥ बड़े भोर भूपतिमनि जागे। जाचक गुन गन गावन लागे ॥
translation: जनकपुर में नित्य नए मंगल हो रहे हैं। दिन और रात पल के समान बीत जाते हैं। बड़े सबेरे राजाओं के मुकुटमणि दशरथजी जागे। याचक उनके गुण समूह का गान करने लगे ॥
english_translation: In Janakpur, new auspiciousness arose each day. Day and night passed like a moment. At dawn, king Dasharath awoke, and the supplicants began singing his many virtues.
essence: Joy makes a whole day feel like a moment.
simple_meaning: Janakpur is full of festive joy, time seems to fly, and Dasharath wakes at dawn while people praise him.
insight: It frames the scene as festive atmosphere, not teaching, and carries the story forward into the next morning.
modern_relevance: After a wedding feast that runs past midnight, the house is still glowing at dawn. Nobody wants the night to end, and even the early hours feel too brief.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि कुअँर बर बधुन्ह समेता। किमि कहि जात मोदु मन जेता॥ प्रातक्रिया करि गे गुरु पाहीं। महाप्रमोदु प्रेमु मन माहीं ॥
translation: चारों कुमारों को सुंदर वधुओं सहित देखकर उनके मन में जितना आनंद है, वह किस प्रकार कहा जा सकता है? वे प्रातः क्रिया करके गुरु वशिष्ठजी के पास गए। उनके मन में महान आनंद और प्रेम भरा है ॥
english_translation: Seeing the four princes together with their beautiful brides, their joy cannot be described. After their morning rites, they went to Guru Vashistha, filled with great delight and love.
essence: Joy becomes speechless when life finally feels complete.
simple_meaning: The fathers see all four princes with their brides and feel overwhelming joy. After their morning duties, the princes go to their teacher, full of love and happiness.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to the emotional fullness that ceremony reveals.
modern_relevance: You look across the room at your children standing beside the people they chose, and something in you softens. The day feels complete before anyone says a word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि प्रनामु पूजा कर जोरी। बोले गिरा अमिअँ जनु बोरी॥ तुम्हरी कृपाँ सुनहु मुनिराजा। भयउँ आजु मैं पूरन काजा ॥
translation: राजा प्रणाम और पूजन करके, फिर हाथ जोड़कर मानो अमृत में डुबोई हुई वाणी बोले- हे मुनिराज! सुनिए, आपकी कृपा से आज मैं पूर्णकाम हो गया ॥
english_translation: After bowing and worshipping with joined hands, the king spoke in words like nectar: “By your grace, O great sage, today I have accomplished my purpose.”
essence: Completion becomes sweeter when it is offered back as gratitude.
simple_meaning: Janaka bows to the sage and says he has completed his task through the sage's grace.
insight: It shifts success from self-ownership to humble acknowledgment of help received.
modern_relevance: You finish a project, but the mentor who shaped you is the first person you call. The achievement feels real only when pride gives way to gratitude.
speaker: Janaka

verse_text: अब सब बिप्र बोलाइ गोसाईं। देहु धेनु सब भाँति बनाईं॥ सुनि गुर करि महिपाल बड़ाई। पुनि पठए मुनिबृंद बोलाई ॥
translation: हे स्वामिन् ! अब सब ब्राह्मणों को बुलाकर उनको सब तरह (गहनों-कपड़ों) से सजी हुई गायें दीजिए। यह सुनकर गुरुजी ने राजा की बड़ाई करके फिर मुनिगणों को बुलवा भेजा ॥
english_translation: O Lord, now call all the brahmins and give away cows, fully adorned in every way. Hearing this, the guru praised the king and then sent word to summon the host of sages.
essence: Joy becomes complete when it is given away.
simple_meaning: The king is told to honor the brahmins with decorated cows, and the guru responds by praising him and calling the sages.
insight: It shifts celebration from display to offering, making joy communal instead of private.
modern_relevance: A family finishes a wedding and everyone wants photos, applause, and speeches. One elder quietly says: feed people first, honor them properly, and let gratitude lead the day.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: बामदेउ अरु देवरिषि बालमीकि जाबालि। आए मुनिबर निकर तब कौसिकादि तपसालि ॥
translation: तब वामदेव, देवर्षि नारद, वाल्मीकि, जाबालि और विश्वामित्र आदि तपस्वी श्रेष्ठ मुनियों के समूह के समूह आए ॥
english_translation: Then Vamadeva, the divine sage Narada, Valmiki, Jabali, and the great ascetics led by Vishvamitra came in a group of sages.
essence: A sacred gathering grows as revered sages arrive.
simple_meaning: Many respected sages arrived together, including Vamadeva, Narada, Valmiki, Jabali, and Vishvamitra.
insight: It shifts attention from the ritual itself to the sacred company gathered around it.
modern_relevance: A formal ceremony is underway, and the room suddenly fills with elders, teachers, and respected guests. Their arrival signals that something important is about to be witnessed, honored, and remembered.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दंड प्रनाम सबहि नृप कीन्हे। पूजि सप्रेम बरासन दीन्हे॥ चारि लच्छ बर धेनु मगाईं। काम सुरभि सम सील सुहाईं ॥
translation: राजा ने सबको दण्डवत् प्रणाम किया और प्रेम सहित पूजन करके उन्हें उत्तम आसन दिए। चार लाख उत्तम गायें मँगवाईं, जो कामधेनु के समान अच्छे स्वभाव वाली और सुहावनी थीं ॥
english_translation: The king bowed to everyone with full prostration, honored them with loving hospitality, and brought four hundred thousand excellent cows—gentle and beautiful like Kamadhenu.
essence: Honor becomes real when it is given as service.
simple_meaning: The king shows complete respect to the gathered sages, welcomes them warmly, and gives away huge numbers of fine cows.
insight: It shifts respect from performance to concrete hospitality.
modern_relevance: You greet the elder who came to your home with a quick nod, then stop and bring a chair, water, and real attention. Respect becomes visible the moment you make room for someone.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब बिधि सकल अलंकृत कीन्हीं। मुदित महिप महिदेवन्ह दीन्हीं॥ करत बिनय बहु बिधि नरनाहू। लहेउँ आजु जग जीवन लाहू ॥
translation: उन सबको सब प्रकार से (गहनों-कपड़ों से) सजाकर राजा ने प्रसन्न होकर भूदेव ब्राह्मणों को दिया। राजा बहुत तरह से विनती कर रहे हैं कि जगत में मैंने आज ही जीने का लाभ पाया ॥
english_translation: He had them adorned in every way and gave them away joyfully to the Brahmins. The king kept bowing in many ways and said, "Today I have found the true benefit of living in the world."
essence: True gain comes from giving without holding back.
simple_meaning: The king honors the Brahmins with gifts, ornaments, and repeated bows, and feels that serving them is the true value of his life.
insight: It shifts the mind from keeping score to finding fulfillment in service itself.
modern_relevance: You stay after the ceremony to thank the people who made it possible, even though no one is watching. Something in you knows that recognition is small compared with sincere giving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पाइ असीस महीसु अनंदा। लिए बोलि पुनि जाचक बृंदा॥ कनक बसन मनि हय गय स्यंदन। दिए बूझि रुचि रबिकुलनंदन ॥
translation: (ब्राह्मणों से) आशीर्वाद पाकर राजा आनंदित हुए। फिर याचकों के समूहों को बुलवा लिया और सबको उनकी रुचि पूछकर सोना, वस्त्र, मणि, घोड़ा, हाथी और रथ (जिसने जो चाहा सो) सूर्यकुल को आनंदित करने वाले दशरथजी ने दिए ॥
english_translation: After receiving blessings, the king was filled with joy. He then called the groups of petitioners and, asking each what they desired, gave gold, clothes, jewels, horses, elephants, and chariots to the delight of the Solar dynasty's lord.
essence: True giving asks what each person needs.
simple_meaning: King Dasharath, happy after receiving blessings, called the beggars and gave each person what they wanted: wealth, clothes, jewels, horses, elephants, and chariots.
insight: It shifts giving from display to responsiveness.
modern_relevance: At a wedding feast, the host notices what each guest actually needs instead of handing out the same gift to everyone. Real generosity pays attention before it gives.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चले पढ़त गावत गुन गाथा। जय जय जय दिनकर कुल नाथा॥ एहि बिधि राम बिआह उछाहू। सकइ न बरनि सहस मुख जाहू ॥
translation: वे सब गुणानुवाद गाते और 'सूर्यकुल के स्वामी की जय हो, जय हो, जय हो' कहते हुए चले। इस प्रकार श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विवाह का उत्सव हुआ, जिन्हें सहस्र मुख हैं, वे शेषजी भी उसका वर्णन नहीं कर सकते ॥
english_translation: They walked along singing praises of his virtues, crying, 'Victory, victory, victory to the lord of the solar race!' In this way the joy of Ram's wedding unfolded, a joy that even a thousand-mouthed being cannot describe.
essence: Joy around Ram exceeds every attempt to describe it.
simple_meaning: The wedding celebration fills everyone with praise and joy, and its greatness feels beyond description.
insight: It turns attention from explanation to celebration, showing that some truths are best carried in praise.
modern_relevance: A wedding crowd spills out into the street, still humming the same name, still smiling at nothing and everything. Some happiness is too large to fit into a sentence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बार बार कौसिक चरन सीसु नाइ कह राउ। यह सबु सुखु मुनिराज तव कृपा कटाच्छ पसाउ ॥
translation: बार-बार विश्वामित्रजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर राजा कहते हैं- हे मुनिराज! यह सब सुख आपके ही कृपाकटाक्ष का प्रसाद है ॥
english_translation: Again and again, the king bowed his head to Kaushika’s feet and said, "All this joy is the gift of your grace, O great sage."
essence: True joy remembers the hands that made it possible.
simple_meaning: King Dasharath bows repeatedly to Vishwamitra and credits him for all the joy of the wedding, calling it the result of the sage’s gracious glance.
insight: It teaches you to name the people whose grace made your success possible.
modern_relevance: After a long ceremony ends perfectly, you thank the person who quietly made it possible. The spotlight may land elsewhere, but your heart knows who held the whole thing together.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: जनक सनेहु सीलु करतूती। नृपु सब भाँति सराह बिभूती॥ दिन उठि बिदा अवधपति मागा। राखहिं जनकु सहित अनुरागा ॥
translation: राजा दशरथजी जनकजी के स्नेह, शील, करनी और ऐश्वर्य की सब प्रकार से सराहना करते हैं। प्रतिदिन (सबेरे) उठकर अयोध्या नरेश विदा माँगते हैं। पर जनकजी उन्हें प्रेम से रख लेते हैं ॥
english_translation: King Dasharath praises Janak's affection, gentleness, conduct, and splendour in every way. Each morning the lord of Ayodhya asks to depart, but Janak keeps him there with loving warmth.
essence: Respect deepens into affection, and departure keeps getting delayed.
simple_meaning: Dasharath admires Janak's character and wealth, and keeps asking to leave, but Janak lovingly continues to host him.
insight: It shifts attention from formal farewell to the human bond that makes parting difficult.
modern_relevance: You stand at the door after a wedding weekend, still being fed tea and stories while everyone delays goodbye. The leaving matters, but the warmth matters more.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नित नूतन आदरु अधिकाई। दिन प्रति सहस भाँति पहुनाई॥ नित नव नगर अनंद उछाहू। दसरथ गवनु सोहाइ न काहू ॥
translation: आदर नित्य नया बढ़ता जाता है। प्रतिदिन हजारों प्रकार से मेहमानी होती है। नगर में नित्य नया आनंद और उत्साह रहता है, दशरथजी का जाना किसी को नहीं सुहाता ॥
english_translation: Respect grew anew each day. Every day brought a thousand kinds of hospitality. New joy and excitement filled the city each day, and no one liked Dasharath's departure.
essence: True welcome makes even leaving feel like loss.
simple_meaning: King Dasharath is honored more and more each day in Mithila. The city keeps celebrating him with endless hospitality, and no one wants him to leave.
insight: It shows how genuine hospitality can deepen attachment and make departure feel wrong even when it is necessary.
modern_relevance: You stay a few extra days at a house where every meal feels like love and every goodbye keeps getting delayed. Leaving starts to feel like breaking a shared heartbeat.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुत दिवस बीते एहि भाँती। जनु सनेह रजु बँधे बराती॥ कौसिक सतानंद तब जाई। कहा बिदेह नृपहि समुझाई ॥
translation: इस प्रकार बहुत दिन बीत गए, मानो बाराती स्नेह की रस्सी से बँध गए हैं। तब विश्वामित्रजी और शतानंदजी ने जाकर राजा जनक को समझाकर कहा- ॥
english_translation: Many days passed in this way, as if the wedding guests were bound by the rope of affection. Then Vishvamitra and Shatananda went and spoke to King Janaka, explaining the matter.
essence: Affection can hold people together longer than ceremony itself.
simple_meaning: The wedding guests stayed on for many days, held there by mutual affection. Then Vishvamitra and Shatananda went to Janaka and explained the situation.
insight: It frames delay as a sign of shared affection, not inconvenience.
modern_relevance: A house full of relatives stays lively long after the ceremony ends. Nobody wants to be the first to leave, because the connection itself has become the celebration.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अब दसरथ कहँ आयसु देहू। जद्यपि छाड़ि न सकहु सनेहू॥ भलेहिं नाथ कहि सचिव बोलाए। कहि जय जीव सीस तिन्ह नाए ॥
translation: यद्यपि आप स्नेह (वश उन्हें) नहीं छोड़ सकते, तो भी अब दशरथजी को आज्ञा दीजिए। 'हे नाथ! बहुत अच्छा' कहकर जनकजी ने मंत्रियों को बुलवाया। वे आए और 'जय जीव' कहकर उन्होंने मस्तक नवाया ॥
english_translation: Though you cannot bear to part from them, now give King Dasharatha his leave. Janaka said, "Very well, my lord," and called his ministers. They came and bowed their heads, saying, "Victory and long life."
essence: Affection need not erase proper farewell.
simple_meaning: Janaka asks that Dasharatha be formally given permission to depart, even though affection makes parting hard. He then calls his ministers, who come and bow respectfully.
insight: It shows how tenderness and formality can coexist, so separation is handled with dignity instead of clinging.
modern_relevance: You know the moment when a long, warm visit is ending and nobody wants to say goodbye. Still, someone has to make the departure graceful, not awkward.
speaker: Janaka

verse_text: अवधनाथु चाहत चलन भीतर करहु जनाउ। भए प्रेमबस सचिव सुनि बिप्र सभासद राउ ॥
translation: (जनकजी ने कहा-) अयोध्यानाथ चलना चाहते हैं, भीतर (रनिवास में) खबर कर दो। यह सुनकर मंत्री, ब्राह्मण, सभासद और राजा जनक भी प्रेम के वश हो गए ॥
english_translation: Janak said, "The lord of Ayodhya wants to depart; go and inform the inner quarters." Hearing this, the ministers, priests, courtiers, and King Janak himself were overcome by love.
essence: Love remains present even as departure begins.
simple_meaning: Janak asks that Rama's departure be announced inside the palace. The news moves everyone so deeply that even Janak and his court are overcome with love.
insight: It shows how devotion deepens even ordinary parting, turning a departure into a shared ache.
modern_relevance: The guest is already at the door with his bag in hand, and no one wants the evening to end. Everyone smiles, but the room has gone quiet because goodbye has already begun.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुरबासी सुनि चलिहि बराता। बूझत बिकल परस्पर बाता॥ सत्य गवनु सुनि सब बिलखाने। मनहुँ साँझ सरसिज सकुचाने ॥
translation: जनकपुरवासियों ने सुना कि बारात जाएगी, तब वे व्याकुल होकर एक-दूसरे से बात पूछने लगे। जाना सत्य है, यह सुनकर सब ऐसे उदास हो गए मानो संध्या के समय कमल सकुचा गए हों ॥
english_translation: Hearing that the wedding procession would leave, the people of Janakpur grew restless and asked each other what was happening. When they heard the departure was certain, everyone became sorrowful, like lotuses shrinking at dusk.
essence: Even happy news can sting when separation is certain.
simple_meaning: The people of Janakpur hear that the wedding procession is leaving, and they become anxious and sad. The certainty of departure makes them feel the loss before it happens.
insight: It shows how attachment turns anticipation into sorrow before the event even arrives.
modern_relevance: You hear the flight is booked, and the house goes quiet. The visit is still happening, but everyone already feels the ending.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ जहँ आवत बसे बराती। तहँ तहँ सिद्ध चला बहु भाँती॥ बिबिध भाँति मेवा पकवाना। भोजन साजु न जाइ बखाना ॥
translation: आते समय जहाँ-जहाँ बाराती ठहरे थे, वहाँ-वहाँ बहुत प्रकार का सीधा (रसोई का सामान) भेजा गया। अनेकों प्रकार के मेवे, पकवान और भोजन की सामग्री जो बखानी नहीं जा सकती- ॥
english_translation: Wherever the wedding party had stayed, food and supplies were sent there in many ways. Countless kinds of sweets, cooked dishes, and feast items cannot be described.
essence: True welcome overflows into abundance.
simple_meaning: Every place the wedding guests stopped received food and supplies. The arrangements were so abundant that no one could fully describe them.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the sacredness of generous preparation.
modern_relevance: A house fills with relatives before a wedding, and someone keeps bringing more trays, more mats, more water, more care. The joy is not in show — it is in making every guest feel held.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरि भरि बसहँ अपार कहारा। पठईं जनक अनेक सुसारा॥ तुरग लाख रथ सहस पचीसा। सकल सँवारे नख अरु सीसा ॥
translation: अनगिनत बैलों और कहारों पर भर-भरकर (लाद-लादकर) भेजी गई। साथ ही जनकजी ने अनेकों सुंदर शय्याएँ (पलंग) भेजीं। एक लाख घोड़े और पचीस हजार रथ सब नख से शिखा तक (ऊपर से नीचे तक) सजाए हुए, ॥
english_translation: Countless bearers and carriers were loaded to the brim and sent by Janak. One hundred thousand horses and twenty-five thousand chariots were all made ready, polished from hoof to head.
essence: Grandeur is only the visible edge of careful preparation.
simple_meaning: Janak sends out huge quantities of transport, beds, horses, and chariots, all fully prepared for the wedding procession.
insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle to the disciplined preparation that makes the spectacle possible.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall looks effortless only because dozens of people have worked all night. The beauty you see is the result of meticulous, invisible care.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मत्त सहस दस सिंधुर साजे। जिन्हहि देखि दिसिकुंजर लाजे॥ कनक बसन मनि भरि भरि जाना। महिषीं धेनु बस्तु बिधि नाना ॥ दाइज अमित न सकिअ कहि दीन्ह बिदेहँ बहोरि। जो अवलोकत लोकपति लोक संपदा थोरि ॥
translation: दस हजार सजे हुए मतवाले हाथी, जिन्हें देखकर दिशाओं के हाथी भी लजा जाते हैं, गाड़ियों में भर-भरकर सोना, वस्त्र और रत्न (जवाहरात) और भैंस, गाय तथा और भी नाना प्रकार की चीजें दीं ॥ (इस प्रकार) जनकजी ने फिर से अपरिमित दहेज दिया, जो कहा नहीं जा सकता और जिसे देखकर लोकपालों के लोकों की सम्पदा भी थोड़ी जान पड़ती थी ॥
english_translation: Ten thousand decorated elephants were prepared; even elephants of the directions felt ashamed to see them. Carts were filled again and again with gold, cloth, and jewels, and with buffaloes, cows, and many other things. Janak gave limitless gifts beyond speech; the wealth of the world seemed small beside what he sent.
essence: True giving feels infinite because it is unstinting.
simple_meaning: Janak sends an enormous bridal gift with the wedding procession: elephants, gold, cloth, jewels, cattle, and countless other riches. The gift is so vast that even heavenly wealth seems small beside it.
insight: It shifts attention from the objects given to the abundance of the giver's heart.
modern_relevance: You pack a moving truck for someone you love and keep adding more than seems necessary. The point is not display. It is the fullness of a heart that gives without measuring.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सबु समाजु एहि भाँति बनाई। जनक अवधपुर दीन्ह पठाई॥ चलिहि बरात सुनत सब रानीं। बिकल मीनगन जनु लघु पानीं ॥
translation: इस प्रकार सब सामान सजाकर राजा जनक ने अयोध्यापुरी को भेज दिया। बारात चलेगी, यह सुनते ही सब रानियाँ ऐसी विकल हो गईं, मानो थोड़े जल में मछलियाँ छटपटा रही हों ॥
english_translation: In this way, the entire wedding procession was prepared and sent to Ayodhya by King Janak. Hearing that the procession would set out, all the queens became agitated like fish in shallow water.
essence: Even a joyful departure can make the heart tremble.
simple_meaning: Janak sends the wedding procession to Ayodhya, and the queens are overwhelmed with emotion when they hear it is about to leave.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to the emotional cost of transition.
modern_relevance: You watch your daughter leave after the wedding, and the house suddenly feels too quiet. Joy is there, but it hurts too.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि पुनि सीय गोद करि लेहीं। देह असीस सिखावनु देहीं॥ होएहु संतत पियहि पिआरी। चिरु अहिबात असीस हमारी ॥
translation: वे बार-बार सीताजी को गोद कर लेती हैं और आशीर्वाद देकर सिखावन देती हैं- तुम सदा अपने पति की प्यारी होओ, तुम्हारा सोहाग अचल हो, हमारी यही आशीष है ॥
english_translation: They repeatedly take Sita into their laps, blessing and instructing her: “May you always be dear to your husband. May your married bond remain unbroken. This is our blessing.”
essence: Affection can teach the shape of a life.
simple_meaning: The women lovingly bless Sita and teach her the ideals expected of a married woman in their world.
insight: It shows how elders pass on values through tenderness, not just instruction.
modern_relevance: At a family gathering before a wedding, older relatives pull the bride close, adjust her veil, and whisper advice she may remember for years. Care and guidance arrive together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सासु ससुर गुर सेवा करेहू। पति रुख लखि आयसु अनुसरेहू॥ अति सनेह बस सखीं सयानी। नारि धरम सिखवहिं मृदु बानी ॥
translation: सास, ससुर और गुरु की सेवा करना। पति का रुख देखकर उनकी आज्ञा का पालन करना। सयानी सखियाँ अत्यन्त स्नेह के वश कोमल वाणी से स्त्रियों के धर्म सिखलाती हैं ॥
english_translation: Serve your mother-in-law, father-in-law, and teacher. Read your husband's mood and follow his wishes. Wise friends, moved by affection, gently teach women their duty in soft words.
essence: Family duty begins with service, attentiveness, and gentle speech.
simple_meaning: Women are advised to serve elders, notice their husband's wishes, and learn their role through gentle guidance from wise friends.
insight: It shifts attention from personal preference to respectful participation in family life.
modern_relevance: Before a wedding, an older aunt pulls you aside and says, 'Learn the family, watch the room, speak softly.' The verse carries that same lived advice about entering a new home with care.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सादर सकल कुअँरि समुझाईं। रानिन्ह बार बार उर लाईं॥ बहुरि बहुरि भेटहिं महतारीं। कहहिं बिरंचि रचीं कत नारीं ॥
translation: आदर के साथ सब पुत्रियों को (स्त्रियों के धर्म) समझाकर रानियों ने बार-बार उन्हें हृदय से लगाया। माताएँ फिर-फिर भेंटती और कहती हैं कि ब्रह्मा ने स्त्री जाति को क्यों रचा ॥
english_translation: With respect, the queens explained everything to the brides and embraced them again and again. The mothers came again and again to meet them, saying, "Why did Brahma create women at all?"
essence: Parting is softened by love, but love cannot stop the ache.
simple_meaning: The queens lovingly instruct the brides and keep embracing them, while the mothers keep returning to see them and speak in sorrowful wonder about the lot of women.
insight: It shows how farewell becomes a ritual of repeated embrace and repeated release.
modern_relevance: A mother keeps smoothing her daughter's hair before the wedding procession leaves. She smiles, gives advice, then turns away and comes back again because letting go hurts more than she can say.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहि अवसर भाइन्ह सहित रामु भानु कुल केतु। चले जनक मंदिर मुदित बिदा करावन हेतु ॥
translation: उसी समय सूर्यवंश के पताका स्वरूप श्री रामचन्द्रजी भाइयों सहित प्रसन्न होकर विदा कराने के लिए जनकजी के महल को चले ॥
english_translation: At that moment, Ram, the banner of the solar dynasty, went with his brothers to Janak's palace, pleased to take leave.
essence: Leave with joy, even at the moment of departure.
simple_meaning: Ram goes with his brothers to Janak's palace to take leave, and he does so gladly.
insight: It keeps attention on the dignity of transition, not on drama.
modern_relevance: The event is over, the guests are still chatting, and you walk back in to say goodbye properly. Small departures still matter when they are done with grace.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चारिउ भाइ सुभायँ सुहाए। नगर नारि नर देखन धाए॥ कोउ कह चलन चहत हहिं आजू। कीन्ह बिदेह बिदा कर साजू ॥
translation: स्वभाव से ही सुंदर चारों भाइयों को देखने के लिए नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष दौड़े। कोई कहता है- आज ये जाना चाहते हैं। विदेह ने विदाई का सब सामान तैयार कर लिया है ॥
english_translation: The four brothers were naturally beautiful. Men and women in the city rushed out to see them. Some said, “Today they are leaving.” “King Janaka has arranged the farewell.”
essence: Their beauty makes the whole city stop and look.
simple_meaning: The four brothers are so beautiful that the whole city rushes out to see them and talk about their departure.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the living presence that makes the event unforgettable.
modern_relevance: You catch sight of a family stepping out of a car at a wedding, and everyone on the street turns to look. Some presences need no announcement; they draw attention by their very nature.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लेहु नयन भरि रूप निहारी। प्रिय पाहुने भूप सुत चारी॥ को जानै केहिं सुकृत सयानी। नयन अतिथि कीन्हे बिधि आनी ॥
translation: राजा के चारों पुत्र, इन प्यारे मेहमानों के (मनोहर) रूप को नेत्र भरकर देख लो। हे सयानी! कौन जाने, किस पुण्य से विधाता ने इन्हें यहाँ लाकर हमारे नेत्रों का अतिथि किया है ॥
english_translation: Look at the beauty with full eyes, dear guests, the four sons of the king. Wise lady, who knows by what merit Fate has brought them here and made them the guests of our eyes?
essence: Beauty has arrived as a guest, and the eyes are blessed.
simple_meaning: The women of Mithila are told to look fully at Ram and his brothers, and to wonder what merit brought such beauty to their sight.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary seeing to reverent noticing.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone entering a room and the whole mood changes. Before anyone speaks, you already know something precious has arrived.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मरनसीलु जिमि पाव पिऊषा। सुरतरु लहै जनम कर भूखा॥ पाव नार की हरिपदु जैसें। इन्ह कर दरसनु हम कहँ तैसें ॥
translation: मरने वाला जिस तरह अमृत पा जाए, जन्म का भूखा कल्पवृक्ष पा जाए और नरक में रहने वाला (या नरक के योग्य) जीव जैसे भगवान के परमपद को प्राप्त हो जाए, हमारे लिए इनके दर्शन वैसे ही हैं ॥
english_translation: For the dying, it is like nectar; for the hungry, like the wish-fulfilling tree; for one fit for the lower realm, like reaching the supreme abode. For us, seeing them is exactly like that.
essence: Ram's presence feels like rescue to every kind of longing.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram and his brothers feels like receiving nectar, a wish-fulfilling tree, and the highest refuge all at once.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary admiration to the sense that true presence can restore a person completely.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone who changes the whole room — and suddenly your tiredness, hunger, and worry all loosen at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निरखि राम सोभा उर धरहू। निज मन फनि मूरति मनि करहू॥ एहि बिधि सबहि नयन फलु देता। गए कुअँर सब राज निकेता ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की शोभा को निरखकर हृदय में धर लो। अपने मन को साँप और इनकी मूर्ति को मणि बना लो। इस प्रकार सबको नेत्रों का फल देते हुए सब राजकुमार राजमहल में गए ॥
english_translation: Keep Ram's beauty in your heart. Make your mind the serpent and his image the jewel. In this way, giving everyone's eyes their reward, the princes went to the royal palace.
essence: Beauty should be held inwardly, not just glanced at and forgotten.
simple_meaning: Hold Ram's beauty in your heart and let your mind become a fitting vessel for it. The princes then go to the palace after blessing everyone with their sight.
insight: It trains attention to receive beauty with reverence before moving on.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone who changes the mood of the whole room, and everyone stops talking for a second. Some moments are meant to be taken in, not merely passed through.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रूप सिंधु सब बंधु लखि हरषि उठा रनिवासु। करहिं निछावरि आरती महा मुदित मन सासु ॥
translation: रूप के समुद्र सब भाइयों को देखकर सारा रनिवास हर्षित हो उठा। सासुएँ महान प्रसन्न मन से निछावर और आरती करती हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing the ocean of beauty in all the brothers, the whole women’s quarters burst into joy. The mothers, delighted, offered lamps and waved blessings with glad hearts.
essence: Beauty becomes sacred when it is met with devotion.
simple_meaning: The royal household is overjoyed when it sees Ram and his brothers. The mothers respond with loving worship and blessings.
insight: It shifts attention from passive seeing to active welcome and blessing.
modern_relevance: A family gathers at the doorway after a long separation. Before anyone speaks, someone lights a lamp, someone smiles through tears, and the whole room softens into gratitude.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि राम छबि अति अनुरागीं। प्रेमबिबस पुनि पुनि पद लागीं॥ रही न लाज प्रीति उर छाई। सहज सनेहु बरनि किमि जाई ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की छबि देखकर वे प्रेम में अत्यन्त मग्न हो गईं और प्रेम के विशेष वश होकर बार-बार चरणों लगीं। हृदय में प्रीति छा गई, इससे लज्जा नहीं रह गई। उनके स्वाभाविक स्नेह का वर्णन किस तरह किया जा सकता है ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ram's beauty, they became utterly absorbed in love. Overcome by love, they fell at his feet again and again. Shame disappeared as affection filled the heart. How can such natural tenderness be described?
essence: True affection makes self-consciousness disappear.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram's beauty, the women are swept into loving devotion. Their affection becomes so natural and complete that self-consciousness disappears.
insight: It shifts attention from social restraint to spontaneous reverence when the heart is fully moved.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence makes you forget to perform. The careful mask drops, and what remains is simple, unguarded warmth.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भाइन्ह सहित उबटि अन्हवाए। छरस असन अति हेतु जेवाँए॥ बोले रामु सुअवसरु जानी। सील सनेह सकुचमय बानी ॥
translation: उन्होंने भाइयों सहित श्री रामजी को उबटन करके स्नान कराया और बड़े प्रेम से षट्रस भोजन कराया। सुअवसर जानकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी शील, स्नेह और संकोचभरी वाणी बोले- ॥
english_translation: They anointed and bathed Ram and his brothers, then lovingly served a six-flavoured meal. Ram, seeing the right moment, spoke with gentle, affectionate modesty.
essence: Grace is proven by humility, not display.
simple_meaning: The household welcomes Ram and his brothers with bathing, food, and loving care. Ram then speaks at the proper moment with gentle humility.
insight: It teaches you to receive honor without losing humility, and to speak only when the moment is right.
modern_relevance: A family has gone all out for a guest, and the most impressive person in the room still speaks softly, thanks everyone, and never acts entitled.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राउ अवधपुर चहत सिधाए। बिदा होन हम इहाँ पठाए॥ मातु मुदित मन आयसु देहू। बालक जानि करब नित नेहू ॥
translation: महाराज अयोध्यापुरी को चलाना चाहते हैं, उन्होंने हमें विदा होने के लिए यहाँ भेजा है। हे माता! प्रसन्न मन से आज्ञा दीजिए और हमें अपने बालक जानकर सदा स्नेह बनाए रखिएगा ॥
english_translation: The king of Ayodhya wants to depart. He has sent us here to take leave. Mother, grant your blessing with a glad heart and keep loving us as your children.
essence: Even departure can ask for blessing and keep affection alive.
simple_meaning: The king’s party is preparing to leave, and they ask the mothers to bless them and keep loving them like children.
insight: It shifts farewell from a cold exit into a sacred exchange of respect, blessing, and ongoing care.
modern_relevance: You stand at the door after a family visit, shoes on, bags in hand, not wanting the moment to end. The hardest goodbye is the one that still asks for blessing.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुनत बचन बिलखेउ रनिवासू। बोलि न सकहिं प्रेमबस सासू॥ हृदयँ लगाई कुअँरि सब लीन्ही। पतिन्ह सौंपि बिनती अति कीन्ही ॥
translation: इन वचनों को सुनते ही रनिवास उदास हो गया। सासुएँ प्रेमवश बोल नहीं सकतीं। उन्होंने सब कुमारियों को हृदय से लगा लिया और उनके पतियों को सौंपकर बहुत विनती की ॥
english_translation: On hearing these words, the women of the palace grew distressed. The mothers-in-law could not speak, overwhelmed by love. They embraced all the princesses and, entrusting them to their husbands, offered many prayers.
essence: Love lets go by blessing, not by speaking.
simple_meaning: The palace women are overcome with emotion. They embrace the princesses, hand them to their husbands, and pray deeply.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to surrender, showing how love expresses itself through blessing, not possession.
modern_relevance: At a wedding farewell, the room goes quiet. The aunt who joked all evening suddenly cannot speak, and the hug says everything her voice cannot.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि बिनय सिय रामहि समरपी जोरि कर पुनि पुनि कहै। बलि जाउँ तात सुजान तुम्ह कहुँ बिदित गति सब की अहै॥ परिवार पुरजन मोहि राजहि प्रानप्रिय सिय जानिबी। तुलसीस सीलु सनेहु लखि निज किंकरी करि मानिबी॥
translation: विनती करके उन्होंने सीताजी को श्री रामचन्द्रजी को समर्पित किया और हाथ जोड़कर बार-बार कहा- हे तात! हे सुजान! मैं बलि जाती हूँ, तुमको सबकी गति (हाल) मालूम है। परिवार को, पुरवासियों को, मुझको और राजा को सीता प्राणों के समान प्रिय है, ऐसा जानिएगा। हे तुलसी के स्वामी! इसके शील और स्नेह को देखकर इसे अपनी दासी करके मानिएगा।
english_translation: After making a humble request, she surrendered Sita to Ram and, joining her hands, said again and again: "I sacrifice myself to you, wise one; you know the condition of everyone. Family, citizens, myself, and the king all hold Sita dear as life. O lord of Tulsidas, seeing her character and affection, please accept her as your own servant."
essence: True love offers what it cherishes without trying to keep it.
simple_meaning: Sita is formally offered to Ram with deep humility. The speaker asks Ram to see her character, her affection, and the love everyone already has for her.
insight: It shifts the mind from possession to reverent offering, asking that worth be recognized rather than claimed.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you love step into a new life, and your only honest response is blessing, not control. You want their goodness to be seen, not owned.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तुम्ह परिपूरन काम जान सिरोमनि भावप्रिय। जन गुन गाहक राम दोष दलन करुनायतन ॥
translation: तुम पूर्ण काम हो, सुजान शिरोमणि हो और भावप्रिय हो (तुम्हें प्रेम प्यारा है)। हे राम! तुम भक्तों के गुणों को ग्रहण करने वाले, दोषों को नाश करने वाले और दया के धाम हो ॥
english_translation: You are complete in every way, the wisest among the wise, and beloved of loving hearts. O Ram, you accept your devotees' virtues, destroy their faults, and are the home of compassion.
essence: Ram receives loving hearts and remakes them from within.
simple_meaning: Ram is perfect, wise, and dear to loving hearts. He welcomes a devotee's good qualities, removes faults, and rests as compassion itself.
insight: It shifts devotion from earning approval to offering a heart that can be transformed.
modern_relevance: You sit beside someone who has disappointed you, yet you still see the good in them. This verse names that rare kind of love: one that notices faults without being ruled by them.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: अस कहि रही चरन गहि रानी। प्रेम पंक जनु गिरा समानी॥ सुनि सनेहसानी बर बानी। बहुबिधि राम सासु सनमानी ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर रानी चरणों को पकड़कर (चुप) रह गईं। मानो उनकी वाणी प्रेम रूपी दलदल में समा गई हो। स्नेह से सनी हुई श्रेष्ठ वाणी सुनकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सास का बहुत प्रकार से सम्मान किया ॥
english_translation: Having said this, the queen remained holding his feet. Her speech seemed to sink into the mud of love. Hearing the noble words soaked in affection, Ram honored his mother-in-law in many ways.
essence: Love can silence speech and still be fully answered.
simple_meaning: The queen falls silent in devotion and holds Ram's feet. Ram responds by honoring his mother-in-law with great respect.
insight: It shows that devotion need not be loud; it can be met with humble honor.
modern_relevance: A parent watches their child leave home after the wedding and cannot quite speak. The goodbye is too full for words, and the most loving response is simple respect.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम बिदा मागत कर जोरी। कीन्ह प्रनामु बहोरि बहोरी॥ पाइ असीस बहुरि सिरु नाई। भाइन्ह सहित चले रघुराई ॥
translation: तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने हाथ जोड़कर विदा माँगते हुए बार-बार प्रणाम किया। आशीर्वाद पाकर और फिर सिर नवाकर भाइयों सहित श्री रघुनाथजी चले ॥
english_translation: Then Shri Ramchandra, with joined hands, asked for leave and bowed again and again. After receiving blessings and bowing his head once more, Raghurai departed with his brothers.
essence: True greatness leaves with humility, not entitlement.
simple_meaning: Ram respectfully asks permission to leave, bows for blessings, and departs with his brothers.
insight: It teaches graceful exit: honour others fully before moving on.
modern_relevance: You finish a difficult family visit, stand at the doorway, and still make time for one more thank-you, one more bow of respect. Leaving well can be its own form of love.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: मंजु मधुर मूरति उर आनी। भईं सनेह सिथिल सब रानी॥ पुनि धीरजु धरि कुअँरि हँकारीं। बार बार भेटहि महतारीं ॥
translation: श्री रामजी की सुंदर मधुर मूर्ति को हृदय में लाकर सब रानियाँ स्नेह से शिथिल हो गईं। फिर धीरज धारण करके कुमारियों को बुलाकर माताएँ बारंबार उन्हें (गले लगाकर) भेंटने लगीं ॥
english_translation: Bringing Ram's sweet, beautiful form into their hearts, all the queens were overcome with affection. Then they steadied themselves, called the young women, and the mothers embraced them again and again.
essence: Love makes farewell linger in the body.
simple_meaning: The queens think of Ram with love and become overwhelmed. After calming themselves, they call the young women and keep embracing them.
insight: It shows how love can make parting gentle instead of abrupt, and how people prolong closeness through repeated embrace.
modern_relevance: You watch someone leave after a family visit, and nobody wants to be the first to let go. The goodbye keeps turning into one more hug, one more look, one more second together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पहुँचावहिं फिरि मिलहिं बहोरी। बढ़ी परस्पर प्रीति न थोरी॥ पुनि पुनि मिलत सखिन्ह बिलगाई। बाल बच्छ जिमि धेनु लवाई ॥
translation: पुत्रियों को पहुँचाती हैं, फिर लौटकर मिलती हैं। परस्पर में कुछ थोड़ी प्रीति नहीं बढ़ी (अर्थात बहुत प्रीति बढ़ी)। बार-बार मिलती हुई माताओं को सखियों ने अलग कर दिया। जैसे हाल की ब्यायी हुई गाय को कोई उसके बालक बछड़े (या बछिया) से अलग कर दे ॥
english_translation: They escort them and then come back to meet again. Their mutual love only grows. Again and again the mothers meet, and the companions separate them, like a cow newly calved being pulled away from her calf.
essence: Parting hurts most when love is deepest.
simple_meaning: The mothers keep returning to see the daughters they love, and the friends keep separating them. Their affection grows so strong it feels like a mother cow being torn from her calf.
insight: It turns a departure into a shared act of tenderness, not a clean farewell.
modern_relevance: At a train platform, your mother keeps stepping forward for one more hug while friends gently pull her back. Nobody is dramatic; everyone is simply unable to let go.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रेमबिबस नर नारि सब सखिन्ह सहित रनिवासु। मानहुँ कीन्ह बिदेहपुर करुनाँ बिरहँ निवासु ॥
translation: सब स्त्री-पुरुष और सखियों सहित सारा रनिवास प्रेम के विशेष वश हो रहा है। (ऐसा लगता है) मानो जनकपुर में करुणा और विरह ने डेरा डाल दिया है ॥
english_translation: All the men and women, along with the maids, were overcome by love. It seemed as if Janakpur itself had become the home of compassion and separation.
essence: Love turns an entire place into longing.
simple_meaning: Everyone in the palace is so overwhelmed by love and longing that the whole city feels filled with compassion and separation.
insight: It shifts attention from individual feeling to the way love and loss shape an entire community.
modern_relevance: A house after a farewell can feel strangely silent, as if the rooms themselves are grieving. One person's departure can change the emotional weather for everyone left behind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुक सारिका जानकी ज्याए। कनक पिंजरन्हि राखि पढ़ाए॥ ब्याकुल कहहिं कहाँ बैदेही। सुनि धीरजु परिहरइ न केही ॥
translation: जानकी ने जिन तोता और मैना को पाल-पोसकर बड़ा किया था और सोने के पिंजड़ों में रखकर पढ़ाया था, वे व्याकुल होकर कह रहे हैं- वैदेही कहाँ हैं। उनके ऐसे वचनों को सुनकर धीरज किसको नहीं त्याग देगा (अर्थात सबका धैर्य जाता रहा) ॥
english_translation: Sita had raised the parrots and mynas, keeping them in golden cages and teaching them. They cry out in distress, “Where is Vaidehi?” Hearing such words, who could keep composure?
essence: Absence is so strong it reaches the birds Sita raised.
simple_meaning: Sita's trained birds cry out for her, and their grief shakes everyone nearby.
insight: It turns grief into a shared atmosphere, not a private feeling.
modern_relevance: You open a voice note from a pet sitter, and your cat keeps waiting by the door. Even the animals notice the absence before the people do.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भए बिकल खग मृग एहि भाँती। मनुज दसा कैसें कहि जाती॥ बंधु समेत जनकु तब आए। प्रेम उमगि लोचन जल छाए ॥
translation: जब पक्षी और पशु तक इस तरह विकल हो गए, तब मनुष्यों की दशा कैसे कही जा सकती है! तब भाई सहित जनकजी वहाँ आए। प्रेम से उमड़कर उनके नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया ॥
english_translation: Even birds and animals were distraught like this; how can the condition of human beings be described? Then King Janaka came with his brothers, and love welled up so strongly that tears filled his eyes.
essence: Love can make even the whole world seem distressed.
simple_meaning: Even the birds and animals are shaken by this separation. Janaka arrives with his brothers, overwhelmed with love and tears.
insight: It shifts attention from public ceremony to private grief, showing how deeply love can unsettle composure.
modern_relevance: You walk into a quiet house after everyone has left, and the silence feels alive. Some losses are so large that even the room seems to know them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीय बिलोकि धीरता भागी। रहे कहावत परम बिरागी॥ लीन्हि रायँ उर लाइ जानकी। मिटी महामरजाद ग्यान की ॥
translation: वे परम वैराग्यवान कहलाते थे, पर सीताजी को देखकर उनका भी धीरज भाग गया। राजा ने जानकीजी को हृदय से लगा लिया। (प्रेम के प्रभाव से) ज्ञान की महान मर्यादा मिट गई (ज्ञान का बाँध टूट गया) ॥
english_translation: Seeing Sita, his composure fled. The one called utterly detached lost all restraint. The king embraced Janaki to his heart, and the great boundary of knowledge dissolved.
essence: True love can break the rules of restraint without becoming weakness.
simple_meaning: The sight of Sita overwhelms even the most detached mind. Love breaks through restraint, and the usual limits of reason fall away.
insight: It shifts attention from polished control to the force of genuine feeling.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room planning to stay cool, but one look at someone you love changes everything. The body knows what the mind tries to manage.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समुझावत सब सचिव सयाने। कीन्ह बिचारु न अवसर जाने॥ बारहिं बार सुता उर लाईं। सजि सुंदर पालकीं मगाईं ॥
translation: सब बुद्धिमान मंत्री उन्हें समझाते हैं। तब राजा ने विषाद करने का समय न जानकर विचार किया। बारंबार पुत्रियों को हृदय से लगाकर सुंदर सजी हुई पालकियाँ मँगवाई ॥
english_translation: The wise ministers tried to console him. Then the king, seeing no time for grief, made a decision. He kept embracing his daughters again and again and ordered beautiful palanquins to be brought.
essence: Grief can coexist with clear action.
simple_meaning: The king is overwhelmed, but the ministers steady him. He gathers himself, hugs his daughters again and again, and arranges for the palanquins.
insight: It shifts the mind from being swallowed by feeling to acting with care despite feeling.
modern_relevance: You are wiping your eyes in the hallway before your daughter's wedding, then checking the guest list one more time. Love and responsibility do not cancel each other.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रेमबिबस परिवारु सबु जानि सुलगन नरेस। कुअँरि चढ़ाईं पालकिन्ह सुमिरे सिद्धि गनेस ॥
translation: सारा परिवार प्रेम में विवश है। राजा ने सुंदर मुहूर्त जानकर सिद्धि सहित गणेशजी का स्मरण करके कन्याओं को पालकियों पर चढ़ाया ॥
english_translation: The whole family was overcome by love. The king, choosing an auspicious moment and remembering Ganesh for success, placed the princesses in palanquins.
essence: Love moves the family, but order still carries the moment.
simple_meaning: Everyone is swept up in love, and the king arranges the princesses’ departure at an auspicious time after remembering Ganesh.
insight: It shows how devotion, custom, and tenderness can coexist even in a painful farewell.
modern_relevance: A family gathers at a train platform, trying not to cry as the youngest leaves home. Someone still checks the clock, adjusts the bags, and makes sure the goodbye is done properly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुबिधि भूप सुता समुझाईं। नारिधरमु कुलरीति सिखाईं॥ दासीं दास दिए बहुतेरे। सुचि सेवक जे प्रिय सिय केरे ॥
translation: राजा ने पुत्रियों को बहुत प्रकार से समझाया और उन्हें स्त्रियों का धर्म और कुल की रीति सिखाई। बहुत से दासी-दास दिए, जो सीताजी के प्रिय और विश्वास पात्र सेवक थे ॥
english_translation: The king instructed his daughters in many ways, teaching them the duties of women and the customs of the family line. He gave them many maidservants and servants, all pure and trusted attendants dear to Sita.
essence: Love prepares others before letting them go.
