simple_meaning: King Janak prepares his daughters for marriage by teaching them proper conduct and sending trusted servants with them.
insight: It shifts love from emotion alone to preparation, guidance, and dependable support.
modern_relevance: A parent packing a child for a new city does more than say goodbye. They teach, prepare, and quietly place support in the child's hands before the door closes.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीय चलत ब्याकुल पुरबासी। होहिं सगुन सुभ मंगल रासी॥ भूसुर सचिव समेत समाजा। संग चले पहुँचावन राजा ॥
translation: सीताजी के चलते समय जनकपुरवासी व्याकुल हो गए। मंगल की राशि शुभ शकुन हो रहे हैं। ब्राह्मण और मंत्रियों के समाज सहित राजा जनकजी उन्हें पहुँचाने के लिए साथ चले ॥
english_translation: As Sita set out, the people of Janakpur grew restless. Auspicious signs and blessings appeared. King Janak, with brahmins, ministers, and the whole assembly, went along to escort her.
essence: A blessed farewell can carry an entire city’s love.
simple_meaning: The people of Janakpur feel emotional as Sita leaves, and everyone sees this moment as blessed. King Janak escorts her with his court.
insight: It turns departure into a shared act of honor, not a private loss.
modern_relevance: At a train platform, everyone goes quiet when the bride steps forward and her family walks beside her. The goodbye hurts, but the escort itself becomes love made visible.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समय बिलोकि बाजने बाजे। रथ गज बाजि बरातिन्ह साजे॥ दसरथ बिप्र बोलि सब लीन्हे। दान मान परिपूरन कीन्हे ॥
translation: समय देखकर बाजे बजने लगे। बारातियों ने रथ, हाथी और घोड़े सजाए। दशरथजी ने सब ब्राह्मणों को बुला लिया और उन्हें दान और सम्मान से परिपूर्ण कर दिया ॥
english_translation: At the right time, the drums began to sound. The wedding party readied chariots, elephants, and horses. Dasharath called all the brahmins and fulfilled them with gifts and honour.
essence: Sacred occasions begin with order, timing, and honour.
simple_meaning: The wedding procession is getting ready. Drums sound, vehicles and animals are prepared, and Dasharath honours the brahmins with gifts.
insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle to the care that prepares it.
modern_relevance: The hall is buzzing before the ceremony begins. Someone checks the guest list, someone else adjusts the decorations, and the host quietly makes sure every elder is welcomed properly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चरन सरोज धूरि धरि सीसा। मुदित महीपति पाइ असीसा॥ सुमिरि गजाननु कीन्ह पयाना। मंगल मूल सगुन भए नाना ॥
translation: उनके चरण कमलों की धूलि सिर पर धरकर और आशीष पाकर राजा आनंदित हुए और गणेशजी का स्मरण करके उन्होंने प्रस्थान किया। मंगलों के मूल अनेकों शकुन हुए ॥
english_translation: Placing the dust of the lotus feet on his head, the king departed delighted after receiving blessings. Remembering Ganesha, many auspicious signs appeared.
essence: Blessed beginnings turn movement into auspicious momentum.
simple_meaning: The king leaves joyfully after bowing to holy feet and receiving blessings. He remembers Ganesha, and many good omens appear.
insight: It frames a major departure as an act of reverence, not mere travel.
modern_relevance: Before a big family event, someone touches the feet of elders, gets their blessing, and finally steps out with a lighter heart. The day feels protected before it even begins.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुर प्रसून बरषहिं हरषि करहिं अपछरा गान। चले अवधपति अवधपुर मुदित बजाइ निसान ॥
translation: देवता हर्षित होकर फूल बरसा रहे हैं और अप्सराएँ गान कर रही हैं। अवधपति दशरथजी नगाड़े बजाकर आनंदपूर्वक अयोध्यापुरी चले ॥
english_translation: The radiant beings shower flowers in delight, and the celestial dancers sing. The lord of Ayodhya returned to Ayodhya with drums sounding in joy.
essence: A blessed return makes the whole world seem to rejoice.
simple_meaning: The city welcomes Dasharath's return with joy from the heavens and music all around. This is a celebratory scene, not a teaching verse.
insight: It frames a joyful turning point as a public celebration, not a private feeling.
modern_relevance: You finally leave the hospital after hearing good news, and the whole ride home feels lighter. Even the traffic seems less harsh because your chest is full of relief.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नृप करि बिनय महाजन फेरे। सादर सकल मागने टेरे॥ भूषन बसन बाजि गज दीन्हे। प्रेम पोषि ठाढ़े सब कीन्हे ॥
translation: राजा दशरथजी ने विनती करके प्रतिष्ठित जनों को लौटाया और आदर के साथ सब मँगनों को बुलवाया। उनको गहने-कपड़े, घोड़े-हाथी दिए और प्रेम से पुष्ट करके सबको सम्पन्न अर्थात बलयुक्त कर दिया ॥।
english_translation: King Dasharath respectfully sent the honored guests away, then called all the beggars and gave them ornaments, clothes, horses, and elephants. He filled them with love and made them prosperous.
essence: Joy becomes complete only when it feeds everyone nearby.
simple_meaning: Dasharath honors the guests, then gives gifts generously to everyone who asks. He sends them away satisfied and strengthened.
insight: It shifts the mind from ceremonial celebration to practical generosity toward those who need support.
modern_relevance: After a family celebration, you notice the leftovers, the extra chairs, the unopened gifts, and the people waiting quietly near the gate. The real test is whether joy stays private or becomes sharing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बार बार बिरिदावलि भाषी। फिरे सकल रामहि उर राखी॥ बहुरि बहुरि कोसलपति कहहीं। जनकु प्रेमबस फिरै न चहहीं ॥
translation: वे सब बारंबार विरुदावली (कुलकीर्ति) बखानकर और श्री रामचन्द्रजी को हृदय में रखकर लौटे। कोसलाधीश दशरथजी बार-बार लौटने को कहते हैं, परन्तु जनकजी प्रेमवश लौटना नहीं चाहते ॥
english_translation: They praised the family glory again and again, keeping Ram in their hearts as they returned. The king of Kosala kept asking them to return, but Janaka, moved by love, did not want to turn back.
essence: Love lingers longer than the journey home.
simple_meaning: Everyone kept praising Ram and returned with him in their hearts. King Dasharath kept asking Janaka to turn back, but Janaka, full of love, did not want to leave.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the emotional cost of parting from what the heart has held dear.
modern_relevance: You leave a wedding hall after midnight, still looking back at the people you love. The car starts, but your heart stays behind in the light and music.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि कह भूपत बचन सुहाए। फिरिअ महीस दूरि बड़ि आए॥ राउ बहोरि उतरि भए ठाढ़े। प्रेम प्रबाह बिलोचन बाढ़े ॥
translation: दशरथजी ने फिर सुहावने वचन कहे- हे राजन् ! बहुत दूर आ गए, अब लौटिए। फिर राजा दशरथजी रथ से उतरकर खड़े हो गए। उनके नेत्रों में प्रेम का प्रवाह बढ़ आया (प्रेमाश्रुओं की धारा बह चली) ॥
english_translation: King Dasharatha spoke gently again: "Turn back, O king. You have come very far." Then the king stepped down from the chariot and stood there, while tears of love rose in his eyes.
essence: Love makes farewell feel impossible.
simple_meaning: Dasharatha gently asks the king to turn back. He gets down from the chariot and stands there, overwhelmed with love and tears.
insight: It shows how deep affection softens pride and turns etiquette into tenderness.
modern_relevance: You walk your guest to the door, then keep talking because neither of you wants the moment to end. Sometimes affection makes simple goodbyes impossible.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब बिदेह बोले कर जोरी। बचन सनेह सुधाँ जनु बोरी॥ करौं कवन बिधि बिनय बनाई। महाराज मोहि दीन्हि बड़ाई ॥
translation: तब जनकजी हाथ जोड़कर मानो स्नेह रूपी अमृत में डुबोकर वचन बोले- मैं किस तरह बनाकर (किन शब्दों में) विनती करूँ। हे महाराज! आपने मुझे बड़ी बड़ाई दी है ॥
english_translation: Then the King of Videha folded his hands and spoke, as if pouring his words into nectar of affection: “How should I frame my thanks? O great king, you have shown me great honor.”
essence: Honor is best received with folded hands and a smaller ego.
simple_meaning: Janak greets Dasharath with folded hands and speaks humbly, saying he cannot even find the right words to thank him for the honor shown.
insight: It shifts the reader from self-importance to gracious receiving, showing how honor is answered with modesty.
modern_relevance: You receive a call from someone you deeply respect, and they speak to you with warmth you did not expect. Your first response is not performance, but humility and gratitude.
speaker: Janak

verse_text: कोसलपति समधी सजन सनमाने सब भाँति। मिलनि परसपर बिनय अति प्रीति न हृदयँ समाति ॥
translation: अयोध्यानाथ दशरथजी ने अपने स्वजन समधी का सब प्रकार से सम्मान किया। उनके आपस के मिलने में अत्यन्त विनय थी और इतनी प्रीति थी जो हृदय में समाती न थी ॥
english_translation: The lord of Kosala honored his in-laws in every way. Their meeting was full of humility and such love that it could not fit in the heart.
essence: Honor can carry more love than words can hold.
simple_meaning: Dasharath welcomed Janak and his family with full respect. Their meeting overflowed with humility and affection.
insight: It shifts attention from status to gracious conduct in relationships.
modern_relevance: You meet your child’s in-laws for the first time, and every gesture matters: the seat you offer, the tone you use, the respect you show. This verse remembers that dignity can feel like love.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि मंडलिहि जनक सिरु नावा। आसिरबादु सबहि सन पावा॥ सादर पुनि भेंटे जामाता। रूप सील गुन निधि सब भ्राता ॥
translation: जनकजी ने मुनि मंडली को सिर नवाया और सभी से आशीर्वाद पाया। फिर आदर के साथ वे रूप, शील और गुणों के निधान सब भाइयों से, अपने दामादों से मिले, ॥
english_translation: Janak bowed his head to the assembly of sages and received blessings from all. Then, with respect, he greeted his sons-in-law, treasures of beauty, character, and virtue, along with all the brothers.
essence: Humility opens the door to blessing and affectionate welcome.
simple_meaning: Janak first bows to the sages and receives their blessings. Then he respectfully greets his sons-in-law and the brothers gathered there.
insight: It teaches that reverence is not separate from family warmth; proper respect creates harmony in public and private life.
modern_relevance: You enter a room where elders, in-laws, and guests are all watching. The way you bow, greet, and honor each person quietly sets the tone for everything that follows.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जोरि पंकरुह पानि सुहाए। बोले बचन प्रेम जनु जाए॥ राम करौं केहि भाँति प्रसंसा। मुनि महेस मन मानस हंसा ॥
translation: और सुंदर कमल के समान हाथों को जोड़कर ऐसे वचन बोले जो मानो प्रेम से ही जन्मे हों। हे रामजी! मैं किस प्रकार आपकी प्रशंसा करूँ! आप मुनियों और महादेवजी के मन रूपी मानसरोवर के हंस हैं ॥
english_translation: Joining his beautiful lotus-like hands, he spoke words born from love: "How can I praise Ram? He is the swan in the mind-lake of sages and Mahadev."
essence: True praise ends in humility before Ram.
simple_meaning: Janak bows with love and says Ram cannot be praised enough. Even sages and Shiva hold Ram in the deepest place of their minds.
insight: It teaches reverence without performance: let praise become surrender when language runs out.
modern_relevance: You try to thank someone who changed your life, and every sentence feels too small. Janak's response is that feeling made sacred: words bow before what the heart already knows.
speaker: Janak

verse_text: करहिं जोग जोगी जेहि लागी। कोहु मोहु ममता मदु त्यागी॥ ब्यापकु ब्रह्मु अलखु अबिनासी। चिदानंदु निरगुन गुनरासी ॥
translation: योगी लोग जिनके लिए क्रोध, मोह, ममता और मद को त्यागकर योग साधन करते हैं, जो सर्वव्यापक, ब्रह्म, अव्यक्त, अविनाशी, चिदानंद, निर्गुण और गुणों की राशि हैं, ॥
english_translation: Yogis practice yoga for the one who is free of anger, delusion, attachment, and pride: the all-pervading Brahman, unseen, imperishable, consciousness-bliss, without qualities, yet the storehouse of all qualities.
essence: What yogis seek is beyond anger, form, and decay.
simple_meaning: The yogis seek the supreme reality by dropping anger, delusion, possessiveness, and pride. That reality fills everything, cannot be seen directly, never perishes, and is beyond ordinary qualities.
insight: It shifts attention from emotional clutter to the unchanging reality that underlies it.
modern_relevance: You sit in a silent room after a fight, replaying every sharp word. Beneath the noise, something in you knows that anger and possessiveness are not the whole of you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मन समेत जेहि जान न बानी। तरकि न सकहिं सकल अनुमानी॥ महिमा निगमु नेति कहि कहई। जो तिहुँ काल एकरस रहई ॥
translation: जिनको मन सहित वाणी नहीं जानती और सब जिनका अनुमान ही करते हैं, कोई तर्कना नहीं कर सकते, जिनकी महिमा को वेद 'नेति' कहकर वर्णन करता है और जो (सच्चिदानंद) तीनों कालों में एकरस (सर्वदा और सर्वथा निर्विकार) रहते हैं, ॥
english_translation: The mind and speech cannot know him. All reasoning falls short. The Vedas describe his greatness by saying, “not this, not this.” He remains unchanged through all three times.
essence: The highest reality cannot be captured, only recognised.
simple_meaning: Ram's true nature cannot be fully grasped by mind, speech, or logic. Even the Vedas point to him by saying he is beyond all descriptions and remains unchanged through past, present, and future.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to define the highest reality to bowing before what cannot be reduced.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to explain a loss, a love, or a calling to yourself late at night, and the words keep failing. Some realities are too vast for analysis; they ask for humility instead.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: नयन बिषय मो कहुँ भयउ सो समस्त सुख मूल। सबइ लाभु जग जीव कहँ भएँ ईसु अनुकूल ॥
translation: वे ही समस्त सुखों के मूल (आप) मेरे नेत्रों के विषय हुए। ईश्वर के अनुकूल होने पर जगत में जीव को सब लाभ ही लाभ है ॥
english_translation: Your form, which my eyes behold, has become the root of all happiness. When the divine is favorable, every gain comes to the living being in the world.
essence: Seeing Ram turns ordinary life into abundance.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram has become the source of all joy. When life is aligned with the divine, nothing is truly lacking.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing gains to recognising that alignment with the divine is the real gain.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone who steadied your whole life, and suddenly the room feels different. What once felt ordinary now feels like grace showing up in front of you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सबहि भाँति मोहि दीन्हि बड़ाई। निज जन जानि लीन्ह अपनाई॥ होहिं सहस दस सारद सेषा। करहिं कलप कोटिक भरि लेखा ॥
translation: आपने मुझे सभी प्रकार से बड़ाई दी और अपना जन जानकर अपना लिया। यदि दस हजार सरस्वती और शेष हों और करोड़ों कल्पों तक गणना करते रहें ॥
english_translation: You have honored me in every way and accepted me as your own. Even ten thousand Saraswatis and Shesha, counting for countless ages, could not finish the account.
essence: Ram's grace is so complete that praise itself runs out.
simple_meaning: Ram has shown full grace by honoring the speaker and taking him as his own. That kindness is too vast for endless counting to describe.
insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to belonging: the devotee is not outside Ram's care, but counted as one of his own.
modern_relevance: You finally get a message from someone you admire: not a polite reply, but real warmth, real welcome. The relief is bigger than the words themselves.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मोर भाग्य राउर गुन गाथा। कहि न सिराहिं सुनहु रघुनाथा॥ मैं कछु कहउँ एक बल मोरें। तुम्ह रीझहु सनेह सुठि थोरें ॥
translation: तो भी हे रघुनाजी! सुनिए, मेरे सौभाग्य और आपके गुणों की कथा कहकर समाप्त नहीं की जा सकती। मैं जो कुछ कह रहा हूँ, वह अपने इस एक ही बल पर कि आप अत्यन्त थोड़े प्रेम से प्रसन्न हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Even so, O Raghunath, the story of my good fortune and your virtues cannot be finished. I speak only on the strength that you are pleased by even a little affection.
essence: A little true love is enough to please Ram.
simple_meaning: Janak says he can never finish praising Ram's virtues, but he dares to speak because Ram is pleased even by a little love.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to sincerity: the smallest true offering can be enough.
modern_relevance: You rehearse what to say before sending the message, afraid it won't be enough. Then you remember that real closeness is not built on polished words, but on honest affection.
speaker: Janak

verse_text: बार बार मागउँ कर जोरें। मनु परिहरै चरन जनि भोरें॥ सुनि बर बचन प्रेम जनु पोषे। पूरनकाम रामु परितोषे ॥
translation: मैं बार-बार हाथ जोड़कर यह माँगता हूँ कि मेरा मन भूलकर भी आपके चरणों को न छोड़े। जनकजी के श्रेष्ठ वचनों को सुनकर, जो मानो प्रेम से पुष्ट किए हुए थे, पूर्ण काम श्री रामचन्द्रजी संतुष्ट हुए ॥
english_translation: Again and again, with hands joined, I ask that my mind never turn away from your feet. Hearing Janak's noble words, lovingly nourished, Ram was delighted, the fulfilled one pleased completely.
essence: True devotion asks only to remain at Ram's feet.
simple_meaning: Janak humbly asks Ram not to let his mind ever stray from Ram's feet. Ram hears these loving words and feels fully pleased.
insight: It shifts devotion from ceremony to inner loyalty, showing that love is proven by remembrance.
modern_relevance: At a wedding, someone speaks not about gifts or status, but about never letting love become casual. That kind of devotion still lands with force.
speaker: Janak

verse_text: करि बर बिनय ससुर सनमाने। पितु कौसिक बसिष्ठ सम जाने॥ बिनती बहुरि भरत सन कीन्ही। मिलि सप्रेमु पुनि आसिष दीन्ही ॥
translation: उन्होंने सुंदर विनती करके पिता दशरथजी, गुरु विश्वामित्रजी और कुलगुरु वशिष्ठजी के समान जानकर ससुर जनकजी का सम्मान किया। फिर जनकजी ने भरतजी से विनती की और प्रेम के साथ मिलकर फिर उन्हें आशीर्वाद दिया ॥
english_translation: After offering respectful greetings, he honored his father-in-law as he would his father, Kaushika, and Vasistha. Then he again made a request to Bharat, met him with affection, and gave blessings.
essence: Honor creates family before blood does.
simple_meaning: Janak honors his in-laws and treats them like his own family. He then meets Bharat with affection, asks again, and gives blessings.
insight: It shifts attention from formal relations to shared regard, showing how affection can turn ceremony into kinship.
modern_relevance: At a wedding dinner, two families who barely knew each other start speaking with real warmth. No one is performing. Everyone feels the bridge being built in real time.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मिले लखन रिपुसूदनहि दीन्हि असीस महीस। भए परसपर प्रेमबस फिरि फिरि नावहिं सीस ॥
translation: फिर राजा ने लक्ष्मणजी और शत्रुघ्नजी से मिलकर उन्हें आशीर्वाद दिया। वे परस्पर प्रेम के वश होकर बार-बार आपस में सिर नवाने लगे ॥
english_translation: Then the king met Lakshman and Shatrughna and gave them blessings. Overcome by mutual love, they bowed again and again to one another.
essence: Love makes even formal bows feel endless.
simple_meaning: The king blesses Lakshman and Shatrughna, and everyone keeps bowing to one another out of affection.
insight: It shows how respect deepens when affection is real, not forced by status.
modern_relevance: After a wedding dinner, two families stand at the doorway refusing to leave, each one bowing, blessing, and smiling through the goodbye. No one wants the moment to end.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बार बार करि बिनय बड़ाई। रघुपति चले संग सब भाई॥ जनक गहे कौसिक पद जाई। चरन रेनु सिर नयनन्ह लाई ॥
translation: जनकजी की बार-बार विनती और बड़ाई करके श्री रघुनाथजी सब भाइयों के साथ चले। जनकजी ने जाकर विश्वामित्रजी के चरण पकड़ लिए और उनके चरणों की रज को सिर और नेत्रों में लगाया ॥
english_translation: After repeatedly offering praise and respect, Lord Raghunath set out with all his brothers. Janak went and clasped Vishwamitra's feet, then placed the dust of those feet on his head and eyes.
essence: True honour is shown by bowing, not by words alone.
simple_meaning: Ram leaves with his brothers after honoring Janak. Janak bows to Vishwamitra and places the dust of the guru's feet on his head and eyes.
insight: It shifts respect from polite feeling to embodied humility and gratitude.
modern_relevance: At the end of a wedding, everyone is smiling for photos, but one elder still bends fully to touch a teacher's feet. The gesture says what the celebration cannot: gratitude is real when it becomes action.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनु मुनीस बर दरसन तोरें। अगमु न कछु प्रतीति मन मोरें॥ जो सुखु सुजसु लोकपति चहहीं। करत मनोरथ सकुचत अहहीं ॥
translation: (उन्होंने कहा-) हे मुनीश्वर! सुनिए, आपके सुंदर दर्शन से कुछ भी दुर्लभ नहीं है, मेरे मन में ऐसा विश्वास है, जो सुख और सुयश लोकपाल चाहते हैं, परन्तु (असंभव समझकर) जिसका मनोरथ करते हुए सकुचाते हैं, ॥
english_translation: Listen, sage lord: by your sight, nothing is impossible to me. My mind believes that the joy and fame even the rulers of the world desire, yet hesitate to seek, are within reach.
essence: True presence makes the impossible feel ordinary.
simple_meaning: Janaka says that seeing the sage has removed all doubt from his mind. Even the highest joys and honors now seem attainable.
insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to confidence through the power of sacred presence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room expecting rejection, but one person’s calm welcome changes everything. Suddenly the conversation you were afraid to start feels easy.
speaker: Janaka

verse_text: सो सुखु सुजसु सुलभ मोहि स्वामी। सब सिधि तव दरसन अनुगामी॥ कीन्हि बिनय पुनि पुनि सिरु नाई। फिरे महीसु आसिषा पाई ॥
translation: हे स्वामी! वही सुख और सुयश मुझे सुलभ हो गया, सारी सिद्धियाँ आपके दर्शनों की अनुगामिनी अर्थात पीछे-पीछे चलने वाली हैं। इस प्रकार बार-बार विनती की और सिर नवाकर तथा उनसे आशीर्वाद पाकर राजा जनक लौटे ॥
english_translation: O Lord, that very happiness and fame have become easy for me to attain. All powers follow after your sight. Thus the king bowed his head again and again, offered repeated prayers, and returned after receiving blessings.
essence: Humility makes even honor and success feel effortless.
simple_meaning: Janaka tells Vishwamitra that true happiness and honour come easily through his sight. He bows again and again, asks for blessings, and then leaves.
insight: It shifts the response from status-protection to humble receptivity, where blessing becomes possible.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence quietly changes the room. Instead of performing, you soften, listen, and let respect replace self-importance.
speaker: Janaka

verse_text: चली बरात निसान बजाई। मुदित छोट बड़ सब समुदाई॥ रामहि निरखि ग्राम नर नारी। पाइ नयन फलु होहिं सुखारी ॥
translation: डंका बजाकर बारात चली। छोटे-बड़े सभी समुदाय प्रसन्न हैं। (रास्ते के) गाँव के स्त्री-पुरुष श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर नेत्रों का फल पाकर सुखी होते हैं ॥
english_translation: The wedding procession set out with drums beating. Small and large alike in the whole assembly were delighted. Seeing Ram, the men and women of the villages felt their eyes had found their true reward and became joyful.
essence: Seeing Ram is itself the fulfillment of the eyes.
simple_meaning: Ram's wedding procession begins, and everyone who sees him feels fulfilled and joyful.
insight: It frames Ram's presence as the reward itself, shifting attention from ceremony to blessing.
modern_relevance: You catch sight of someone entering a room and the whole atmosphere changes. People straighten up, smile, and feel lighter without knowing why. Some presences do that.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बीच बीच बर बास करि मग लोगन्ह सुख देत। अवध समीप पुनीत दिन पहुँची आइ जनेत ॥
translation: बीच-बीच में सुंदर मुकाम करती हुई तथा मार्ग के लोगों को सुख देती हुई वह बारात पवित्र दिन में अयोध्यापुरी के समीप आ पहुँची ॥
english_translation: Stopping at beautiful resting places along the way, giving joy to the people on the road, the wedding party arrived near Ayodhya on the sacred day.
essence: A noble journey blesses everyone it passes.
simple_meaning: The wedding procession paused at pleasant places along the way, bringing happiness to the people it passed, and reached near Ayodhya on an auspicious day.
insight: It shifts attention from the destination to the way one moves through other people’s lives.
modern_relevance: A convoy pulls off at a roadside dhaba after hours on the highway, and the whole group lightens the mood for the staff and travelers around them. Even arrival can carry grace.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हने निसान पनव बर बाजे। भेरि संख धुनि हय गय गाजे॥ झाँझि बिरव डिंडिमीं सुहाई। सरस राग बाजहिं सहनाई ॥
translation: नगाड़ों पर चोटें पड़ने लगीं, सुंदर ढोल बजने लगे। भेरी और शंख की बड़ी आवाज हो रही है, हाथी-घोड़े गरज रहे हैं। विशेष शब्द करने वाली झाँझें, सुहावनी डफलियाँ तथा रसीले राग से शहनाइयाँ बज रही हैं ॥
english_translation: Drums were struck and fine drums played. The great sounds of kettle-drum and conch rose; horses and elephants thundered. Bright cymbals, lovely hand-drums, and sweet shehnai melodies sounded.
essence: The procession announces itself through sound before sight.
simple_meaning: The wedding procession moves forward in a flood of music and celebration. Drums, conches, horses, elephants, cymbals, and shehnais all fill the air.
insight: It slows the scene into pure atmosphere, letting the reader feel the procession's grandeur before the city sees it.
modern_relevance: You hear music from the street before the wedding car turns the corner. Even before anyone arrives, the whole lane knows something joyful is coming.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुर जन आवत अकनि बराता। मुदित सकल पुलकावलि गाता॥ निज निज सुंदर सदन सँवारे। हाट बाट चौहटपुर द्वारे ॥
translation: बारात को आती हुई सुनकर नगर निवासी प्रसन्न हो गए। सबके शरीरों पर पुलकावली छा गई। सबने अपने-अपने सुंदर घरों, बाजारों, गलियों, चौराहों और नगर के द्वारों को सजाया ॥
english_translation: Hearing that the wedding procession was coming, the city people became joyful and their bodies bristled with delight. They decorated their own beautiful homes, markets, lanes, crossroads, and city gates.
essence: Joy spreads fast when a cherished arrival is near.
simple_meaning: The whole city lights up with joy at the arrival of the wedding procession, and everyone decorates their homes and streets.
insight: It shows how a shared moment of welcome can transform an entire community into one coordinated act of joy.
modern_relevance: You hear the message that the guests are five minutes away, and suddenly the whole house moves at once. Beds are straightened, lights are fixed, and even the hallway feels festive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गलीं सकल अरगजाँ सिंचाईं। जहँ तहँ चौकें चारु पुराईं॥ बना बजारु न जाइ बखाना। तोरन केतु पताक बिताना ॥
translation: सारी गलियाँ अरगजे से सिंचाई गईं, जहाँ-तहाँ सुंदर चौक पुराए गए। तोरणों ध्वजा-पताकाओं और मंडपों से बाजार ऐसा सजा कि जिसका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
english_translation: All the lanes were sprinkled with fragrant water. Beautiful squares were filled in here and there. The marketplace was decorated beyond description with arches, flags, banners, and canopies.
essence: Beauty prepares the world for what is sacred.
simple_meaning: The whole town is being prepared for the wedding with scented water, filled squares, and rich decorations everywhere.
insight: It shifts attention from the event alone to the shared devotion shown in preparation.
modern_relevance: Before a wedding, neighbors are out early sweeping the lane, hanging strings of lights, and setting up tents. The effort feels bigger than decoration — it says, "Something precious is coming."
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सफल पूगफल कदलि रसाला। रोपे बकुल कदंब तमाला॥ लगे सुभग तरु परसत धरनी। मनिमय आलबाल कल करनी ॥
translation: फल सहित सुपारी, केला, आम, मौलसिरी, कदम्ब और तमाल के वृक्ष लगाए गए। वे लगे हुए सुंदर वृक्ष (फलों के भार से) पृथ्वी को छू रहे हैं। उनके मणियों के थाले बड़ी सुंदर कारीगरी से बनाए गए हैं ॥
english_translation: Fruit-bearing areca, banana, mango, bakula, kadamba, and tamala trees were planted. The lovely trees seemed to touch the earth with their heavy fruit. Jewelled flower-beds were made with exquisite craft.
essence: Celebration turns the whole city into an offering.
simple_meaning: The city is being decorated with fruit trees and jewel-like flower-beds for the wedding celebration.
insight: It shifts attention from bare description to sacred preparation: ordinary space is being transformed for joy.
modern_relevance: You help decorate a hall before a wedding, adjusting flowers and lights until everything feels alive. The work itself becomes part of the celebration.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिबिध भाँति मंगल कलस गृह गृह रचे सँवारि। सुर ब्रह्मादि सिहाहिं सब रघुबर पुरी निहारि ॥
translation: अनेक प्रकार के मंगल-कलश घर-घर सजाकर बनाए गए हैं। श्री रघुनाथजी की पुरी (अयोध्या) को देखकर ब्रह्मा आदि सब देवता सिहाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Many kinds of auspicious pots were arranged and decorated in every home. Seeing Raghubar's city, Brahma and the other radiant beings all stood amazed.
essence: The city itself becomes an offering before the celebration begins.
simple_meaning: Every house is decorated with auspicious pots, and the whole city shines so beautifully that even the radiant beings are amazed.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary space to sacred celebration and shared wonder.
modern_relevance: A neighborhood is lit up for a wedding, every doorway cleaned, every wall brightened, and even the guests pause at the care in it. Some moments are made to be admired.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूप भवनु तेहि अवसर सोहा। रचना देखि मदन मनु मोहा॥ मंगल सगुन मनोहरताई। रिधि सिधि सुख संपदा सुहाई ॥
translation: उस समय राजमहल (अत्यन्त) शोभित हो रहा था। उसकी रचना देखकर कामदेव भी मन मोहित हो जाता था। मंगल शकुन, मनोहरता, ऋद्धि-सिद्धि, सुख, सुहावनी सम्पत्ति ॥
english_translation: At that time the royal palace shone brilliantly. Even Kama would be enchanted by its beauty. Auspicious signs, charm, prosperity, delight, and all forms of grace adorned it.
essence: Beauty and auspiciousness filled the palace before the celebration began.
simple_meaning: The palace was dazzling with beauty and auspiciousness. Everything there looked fortunate, graceful, and full of prosperity.
insight: It builds anticipation by showing that outer beauty can mirror inner joy and readiness.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home before a wedding and feel the air change — flowers, lights, careful arranging, and a quiet sense that something blessed is about to happen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जनु उछाह सब सहज सुहाए। तनु धरि धरि दसरथ गृहँ छाए॥ देखन हेतु राम बैदेही। कहहु लालसा होहि न केही ॥
translation: और सब प्रकार के उत्साह (आनंद) मानो सहज सुंदर शरीर धर-धरकर दशरथजी के घर में छा गए हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी और सीताजी के दर्शनों के लिए भला कहिए, किसे लालसा न होगी ॥
english_translation: And all delight seemed to take on natural, lovely bodies and fill Dasharath's house. Who would not long to see Ram and Sita?
essence: Longing for Ram and Sita makes joy itself seem alive.
simple_meaning: Joy itself seems to fill Dasharath's palace as Ram and Sita are about to be seen. The whole city is alive with eager longing.
insight: It turns anticipation into a shared, visible mood rather than a private feeling.
modern_relevance: You wait outside a hospital room or at a stage door, and the whole crowd changes. No one is casual anymore. Everyone is held by the same hope of seeing someone beloved.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जूथ जूथ मिलि चलीं सुआसिनि। निज छबि निदरहिं मदन बिलासिनि॥ सकल सुमंगल सजें आरती। गावहिं जनु बहु बेष भारती ॥
translation: सुहागिनी स्त्रियाँ झुंड की झुंड मिलकर चलीं, जो अपनी छबि से कामदेव की स्त्री रति का भी निरादर कर रही हैं। सभी सुंदर मंगलद्रव्य एवं आरती सजाए हुए गा रही हैं, मानो सरस्वतीजी ही बहुत से वेष धारण किए गा रही हों ॥
english_translation: The married women came in groups, their beauty surpassing even Cupid’s beloved. They carried all auspicious offerings and sang as if Saraswati herself had taken many forms.
essence: Shared joy can make a place feel holy before anything begins.
simple_meaning: Married women arrive in joyful groups, carrying auspicious offerings and singing with beauty and celebration.
insight: It shifts attention from the central event to the sacred energy created by collective participation.
modern_relevance: A home fills with noise before a wedding, women carrying trays, singing, laughing, adjusting veils, and blessing the moment. The atmosphere itself becomes part of the ceremony.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूपति भवन कोलाहलु होई। जाइ न बरनि समउ सुखु सोई॥ कौसल्यादि राम महतारीं। प्रेमबिबस तन दसा बिसारीं ॥
translation: राजमहल में (आनंद के मारे) शोर मच रहा है। उस समय का और सुख का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। कौसल्याजी आदि श्री रामचन्द्रजी की सब माताएँ प्रेम के विशेष वश होने से शरीर की सुध भूल गईं ॥
english_translation: There was a joyful uproar in the royal palace. No one can describe that time or that happiness. Kaushalya and the other mothers of Ram were so overcome with love that they forgot their bodies.
essence: Love can be so full that the body disappears from awareness.
simple_meaning: The palace was full of joy, beyond description. Ram's mothers were so overwhelmed by love that they forgot their bodies.
insight: It shifts attention from outward celebration to the inward effect of love: self-forgetfulness.
modern_relevance: A family room erupts when a long-awaited child finally comes home. Nobody is checking their phone or watching the clock. Joy has taken over the whole house.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दिए दान बिप्रन्ह बिपुल पूजि गनेस पुरारि। प्रमुदित परम दरिद्र जनु पाइ पदारथ चारि ॥
translation: गणेशजी और त्रिपुरारि शिवजी का पूजन करके उन्होंने ब्राह्मणों को बहुत सा दान दिया। वे ऐसी परम प्रसन्न हुईं, मानो अत्यन्त दरिद्री चारों पदार्थ पा गया हो ॥
english_translation: After worshiping Ganesha and Shiva, they gave abundant gifts to the Brahmins. They became utterly delighted, as if a poor person had obtained all four aims of life.
essence: Reverence and giving turn joy into fullness.
simple_meaning: They honored Ganesha and Shiva, gave generous gifts to the Brahmins, and felt complete joy, like a poor person suddenly receiving everything desired.
insight: It shifts celebration from self-enjoyment to reverent generosity.
modern_relevance: You finish a big family ritual, then quietly hand envelopes to the people who helped make it happen. The real joy is not just in the ceremony — it is in giving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मोद प्रमोद बिबस सब माता। चलहिं न चरन सिथिल भए गाता॥ राम दरस हित अति अनुरागीं। परिछनि साजु सजन सब लागीं ॥
translation: सुख और महान आनंद से विवश होने के कारण सब माताओं के शरीर शिथिल हो गए हैं, उनके चरण चलते नहीं हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शनों के लिए वे अत्यन्त अनुराग में भरकर परछन का सब सामान सजाने लगीं ॥
english_translation: Overwhelmed by joy and delight, all the mothers' bodies grew weak; their feet could hardly move. Burning with love for Ram's sight, they began arranging the welcoming ceremony.
essence: Joy for Ram weakens the body and wakes up service.
simple_meaning: The mothers are so filled with joy that they can barely walk. Their love for seeing Ram makes them prepare the welcome ceremony.
insight: It shows how devotion turns emotional overwhelm into careful preparation.
modern_relevance: You wait outside a hospital room with flowers in your hand, too anxious to sit still. The worry and the hope live in the same body.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिबिध बिधान बाजने बाजे। मंगल मुदित सुमित्राँ साजे॥ हरद दूब दधि पल्लव फूला। पान पूगफल मंगल मूला ॥
translation: अनेकों प्रकार के बाजे बजते थे। सुमित्राजी ने आनंदपूर्वक मंगल साज सजाए। हल्दी, दूब, दही, पत्ते, फूल, पान और सुपारी आदि मंगल की मूल वस्तुएँ, ॥
english_translation: Various kinds of instruments were played. Sumitra arranged the auspicious decorations with delight. Turmeric, sacred grass, curd, leaves, flowers, betel leaf, and areca nut—the basic signs of good fortune—were all set out.
essence: A joyful welcome begins with careful preparation.
simple_meaning: The house is being prepared for an auspicious celebration. Music, decorations, and ritual items are all arranged with joy.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the loving care that makes the event sacred.
modern_relevance: You set out extra plates, flowers, and lights before family arrives after a long absence. The preparation itself carries the love before anyone even walks in.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अच्छत अंकुर लोचन लाजा। मंजुल मंजरि तुलसि बिराजा॥ छुहे पुरट घट सहज सुहाए। मदन सकुन जनु नीड़ बनाए ॥
translation: तथा अक्षत (चावल), अँखुए, गोरोचन, लावा और तुलसी की सुंदर मंजरियाँ सुशोभित हैं। नाना रंगों से चित्रित किए हुए सहज सुहावने सुवर्ण के कलश ऐसे मालूम होते हैं, मानो कामदेव के पक्षियों ने घोंसले बनाए हों ॥
english_translation: Rice, sprouts, turmeric, and tulsi blossoms adorn the scene. The painted golden vessels look so lovely they seem like nests built by Cupid's birds.
essence: A prepared space can itself feel sacred.
simple_meaning: The wedding preparations are filled with auspicious items, flowers, and beautifully painted golden vessels that look like nests made by lovebirds.
insight: It trains the eye to notice how careful preparation can carry reverence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room before a wedding and notice the flowers, the lamps, the careful placement of every bowl. The feeling is bigger than decoration — attention itself has become devotion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सगुन सुगंध न जाहिं बखानी। मंगल सकल सजहिं सब रानी॥ रचीं आरतीं बहतु बिधाना। मुदित करहिं कल मंगल गाना ॥
translation: शकुन की सुगन्धित वस्तुएँ बखानी नहीं जा सकतीं। सब रानियाँ सम्पूर्ण मंगल साज सज रही हैं। बहुत प्रकार की आरती बनाकर वे आनंदित हुईं सुंदर मंगलगान कर रही हैं ॥
english_translation: The fragrance of auspicious signs cannot be described. All the queens prepare every kind of blessing. They make many lamps for the aarti and sing joyful songs of good fortune.
essence: A true welcome begins before the beloved arrives.
simple_meaning: The queens are joyfully preparing auspicious offerings, lamps, and songs for a ceremonial welcome.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the loving preparation that makes welcome sacred.
modern_relevance: A home fills with quiet excitement before a long-awaited arrival — flowers on the table, lamps ready, voices soft with happiness. Love often looks like careful preparation before anyone even appears.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कनक थार भरि मंगलन्हि कमल करन्हि लिएँ मात। चलीं मुदित परिछनि करन पुलक पल्लवित गात ॥
translation: सोने के थालों को मांगलिक वस्तुओं से भरकर अपने कमल के समान (कोमल) हाथों में लिए हुए माताएँ आनंदित होकर परछन करने चलीं। उनके शरीर पुलकावली से छा गए हैं ॥
english_translation: The mothers, carrying golden trays filled with auspicious items in their lotus-like hands, went joyfully to perform the welcoming rite. Their bodies trembled with delight.
essence: Preparation itself can become celebration.
simple_meaning: The women of the house go out joyfully with trays of auspicious items to welcome the event. Their excitement shows in their bodies.
insight: It shifts attention to the sacredness of preparation, not just the event itself.
modern_relevance: You are setting out cups, flowers, and sweets before guests arrive, and the whole room feels charged. Anticipation itself becomes part of the welcome.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धूप धूम नभु मेचक भयऊ। सावन घन घमंडु जनु ठयऊ॥ सुरतरु सुमन माल सुर बरषहिं। मनहुँ बलाक अवलि मनु करषहिं ॥
translation: धूप के धुएँ से आकाश ऐसा काला हो गया है मानो सावन के बादल घुमड़-घुमड़कर छा गए हों। देवता कल्पवृक्ष के फूलों की मालाएँ बरसा रहे हैं। वे ऐसी लगती हैं, मानो बगुलों की पाँति मन को (अपनी ओर) खींच रही हो ॥
english_translation: The smoke of the incense darkened the sky like monsoon clouds. The gods showered garlands of celestial flowers, as if a line of cranes were drawing the mind toward them.
essence: Celebration can make the whole world feel enchanted.
simple_meaning: Incense smoke darkens the sky, and flowers rain down from the heavens. The whole scene feels like nature itself has joined the celebration.
insight: It turns a ceremonial scene into a living, sensory celebration.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall fills with incense, lights, music, and petals. For one brief moment, the room feels larger than life, as if the world itself has entered the celebration.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंजुल मनिमय बंदनिवारे। मनहुँ पाकरिपु चाप सँवारे॥ प्रगटहिं दुरहिं अटन्ह पर भामिनि। चारु चपल जनु दमकहिं दामिनि ॥
translation: सुंदर मणियों से बने बंदनवार ऐसे मालूम होते हैं, मानो इन्द्रधनुष सजाए हों। अटारियों पर सुंदर और चपल स्त्रियाँ प्रकट होती और छिप जाती हैं (आती-जाती हैं), वे ऐसी जान पड़ती हैं, मानो बिजलियाँ चमक रही हों ॥
english_translation: Beautiful jeweled festoons seem like rainbows stretched across the gates. On the palace terraces, lovely and lively women appear and disappear, flashing like lightning.
essence: Celebration makes the whole city shimmer.
simple_meaning: The palace is richly decorated for the celebration. Jewels, colors, women on the terraces, and flashes of movement make the whole scene feel alive and radiant.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the sacred mood a community creates around it.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home before a wedding and notice the strings of lights, the bright fabrics, the hurried movement on balconies. The atmosphere itself announces that something precious is about to happen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दुंदुभि धुनि घन गरजनि घोरा। जाचक चातक दादुर मोरा॥ सुर सुगंध सुचि बरषहिं बारी। सुखी सकल ससि पुर नर नारी ॥
translation: नगाड़ों की ध्वनि मानो बादलों की घोर गर्जना है। याचकगण पपीहे, मेंढक और मोर हैं। देवता पवित्र सुगंध रूपी जल बरसा रहे हैं, जिससे खेती के समान नगर के सब स्त्री-पुरुष सुखी हो रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The drums sound like the roar of dark clouds. Beggars, cuckoos, frogs, and peacocks call out. The divine shower fragrant, pure water, and every man and woman in the city feels joy.
essence: A blessed arrival makes the whole city feel alive.
simple_meaning: Drums boom like thunder, birds and frogs call, and the divine rain fragrant water over the city so everyone feels happy.
insight: It shifts attention from private expectation to a whole world lit by arrival.
modern_relevance: A neighborhood starts buzzing when the long-awaited guest finally arrives. Doors open, voices rise, and even strangers feel caught in the same relief.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समउ जानि गुर आयसु दीन्हा। पुर प्रबेसु रघुकुलमनि कीन्हा॥ सुमिरि संभु गिरिजा गनराजा। मुदित महीपति सहित समाजा ॥
translation: (प्रवेश का) समय जानकर गुरु वशिष्ठजी ने आज्ञा दी। तब रघुकुलमणि महाराज दशरथजी ने शिवजी, पार्वतीजी और गणेशजी का स्मरण करके समाज सहित आनंदित होकर नगर में प्रवेश किया ॥
english_translation: Knowing the right moment, Guru Vashistha gave the order. Then Raghu's jewel, King Dasharatha, remembered Shiva, Parvati, and Ganesha, and entered the city joyfully with his retinue.
essence: Right timing and reverence turn an arrival into an auspicious beginning.
simple_meaning: At the right moment, Vashistha gives the signal. Dasharatha enters the city with his entourage, remembering Shiva, Parvati, and Ganesha, and feeling joyful.
insight: It frames a major public moment as something entered with timing, reverence, and collective joy.
modern_relevance: A family steps out of the car before a wedding, everyone adjusting clothes, checking the time, and pausing for a quick prayer before walking in together. The moment matters because the mood matters.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: होहिं सगुन बरषहिं सुमन सुर दुंदभीं बजाइ। बिबुध बधू नाचहिं मुदित मंजुल मंगल गाइ ॥
translation: शकुन हो रहे हैं, देवता दुन्दुभी बजा-बजाकर फूल बरसा रहे हैं। देवताओं की स्त्रियाँ आनंदित होकर सुंदर मंगल गीत गा-गाकर नाच रही हैं ॥
english_translation: Auspicious signs appear. The radiant beings shower flowers and beat the drums. Their delighted women dance, singing graceful songs of blessing.
essence: A blessed moment makes the whole world rejoice.
simple_meaning: The scene is filled with auspicious signs: flowers fall, drums sound, and joyful celestial women dance and sing blessings.
insight: It frames a sacred arrival as something the whole world can celebrate.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall falls quiet for a second, then erupts in music as the couple enters. Everyone feels it: this moment matters. The verse captures that shared sense of blessing before words are spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मागध सूत बंदि नट नागर। गावहिं जसु तिहु लोक उजागर॥ जय धुनि बिमल बेद बर बानी। दस दिसि सुनिअ सुमंगल सानी ॥
translation: मागध, सूत, भाट और चतुर नट तीनों लोकों के उजागर (सबको प्रकाश देने वाले परम प्रकाश स्वरूप) श्री रामचन्द्रजी का यश गा रहे हैं। जय ध्वनि तथा वेद की निर्मल श्रेष्ठ वाणी सुंदर मंगल से सनी हुई दसों दिशाओं में सुनाई पड़ रही है ॥
english_translation: Minstrels, bards, and performers sing the glory of Ram, whose radiance fills the three worlds. The cry of victory and the pure words of the Vedas, rich with auspiciousness, are heard in all ten directions.
essence: Ram's glory makes the whole world ring with auspiciousness.
simple_meaning: All around, singers and praise-makers celebrate Ram. Victory cries and sacred words fill every direction with joy and blessing.
insight: It turns attention from private excitement to a shared atmosphere of celebration.
modern_relevance: At a wedding hall before the bride enters, the musicians tune up, relatives clap, and the whole room starts humming with anticipation. The feeling spreads before anyone speaks.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिपुल बाज ने बाजन लागे। नभ सुर नगर लोग अनुरागे॥ बने बराती बरनि न जाहीं। महा मुदित मन सुख न समाहीं ॥
translation: बहुत से बाजे बजने लगे। आकाश में देवता और नगर में लोग सब प्रेम में मग्न हैं। बाराती ऐसे बने-ठने हैं कि उनका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता। परम आनंदित हैं, सुख उनके मन में समाता नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Many instruments began to play. In the sky, the radiant beings and in the city, the people were filled with love. The wedding guests were so splendid they could not be described. Great joy overflowed; no room remained in the mind for anything else.
essence: Joy spills past description when the moment is truly blessed.
simple_meaning: The wedding celebration bursts into music and joy. Everyone, from the sky to the city, is caught up in delight, and the wedding guests are too splendid to describe.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the shared joy that surrounds it.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall erupts when the bride appears, and even the most reserved uncle is smiling through tears. Some moments are too full for neat explanation; they simply overflow.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुरबासिन्ह तब राय जोहारे। देखत रामहि भए सुखारे॥ करहिं निछावरि मनिगन चीरा। बारि बिलोचन पुलक सरीरा ॥
translation: तब अयोध्यावसियों ने राजा को जोहार (वंदना) की। श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखते ही वे सुखी हो गए। सब मणियाँ और वस्त्र निछावर कर रहे हैं। नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भरा है और शरीर पुलकित हैं ॥।
english_translation: Then the people of Ayodhya bowed to their king. Seeing Ram, they became filled with joy. They offered gems and clothes in tribute. Their eyes filled with tears, and their bodies thrilled with love.
essence: True welcome overflows into gifts, tears, and trembling joy.
simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya greet their king with gifts and reverence. Just seeing Ram fills them with joy, tears, and trembling devotion.
insight: It shifts attention from formal welcome to the physical signs of genuine devotion and relief.
modern_relevance: You spot someone you have missed for years at the airport gate. Before any words, your face changes, your hands move, and gratitude spills out without effort.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आरति करहिं मुदित पुर नारी। हरषहिं निरखि कुअँर बर चारी॥ सिबिका सुभग ओहार उघारी। देखि दुलहिनिन्ह होहिं सुखारी ॥
translation: नगर की स्त्रियाँ आनंदित होकर आरती कर रही हैं और सुंदर चारों कुमारों को देखकर हर्षित हो रही हैं। पालकियों के सुंदर परदे हटा-हटाकर वे दुलहिनों को देखकर सुखी होती हैं ॥
english_translation: The women of the city, joyful and delighted, perform ārati. Seeing the four handsome princes, they rejoice. Lifting the beautiful curtains of the palanquins, they look at the brides and feel happy.
essence: Joy deepens when everyone welcomes the sacred moment together.
simple_meaning: The women of Ayodhya celebrate the wedding procession, wave lamps, and feel joy seeing the princes and brides.
insight: It turns attention from individual spectatorship to communal celebration.
modern_relevance: You step into a family wedding hall and see strangers smiling like relatives. The music, lamps, and lifted curtains turn a private union into a shared blessing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि बिधि सबही देत सुखु आए राजदुआर। मुदित मातु परिछनि करहिं बधुन्ह समेत कुमार ॥
translation: इस प्रकार सबको सुख देते हुए राजद्वार पर आए। माताएँ आनंदित होकर बहुओं सहित कुमारों का परछन कर रही हैं ॥
english_translation: In this way, bringing joy to everyone, they came to the royal gate. The mothers, delighted, along with the daughters-in-law, performed the auspicious welcoming ritual for the princes.
essence: Their arrival blesses everyone before a word is spoken.
simple_meaning: The princes arrive at the palace gate, bringing joy to everyone. The mothers and daughters-in-law welcome them with an auspicious ritual.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the warmth it creates in a community.
modern_relevance: You come home after a long trip and the whole house changes mood the moment you walk in. Someone lights a lamp, someone smiles through tears, and welcome becomes its own ceremony.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करहिं आरती बारहिं बारा। प्रेमु प्रमोदु कहै को पारा॥ भूषन मनि पट नाना जाती। करहिं निछावरि अगनित भाँती ॥
translation: वे बार-बार आरती कर रही हैं। उस प्रेम और महान आनंद को कौन कह सकता है! अनेकों प्रकार के आभूषण, रत्न और वस्त्र तथा अगणित प्रकार की अन्य वस्तुएँ निछावर कर रही हैं ॥
english_translation: They perform the aarti again and again. Who can describe that love and joy? They offer countless kinds of ornaments, jewels, garments, and other gifts.
essence: Overflowing love turns reverence into generous giving.
simple_meaning: The women keep performing aarti for the four princes and shower them with gifts. Their love and joy are so great that no one can fully describe them.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the abundance of feeling behind it.
modern_relevance: A family reunion ends with everyone piling food, gifts, and blessings into one room. Nobody is keeping score. The joy is too full for restraint.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बधुन्ह समेत देखि सुत चारी। परमानंद मगन महतारी॥ पुनि पुनि सीय राम छबि देखी। मुदित सफल जग जीवन लेखी ॥
translation: बहुओं सहित चारों पुत्रों को देखकर माताएँ परमानंद में मग्न हो गईं। सीताजी और श्री रामजी की छबि को बार-बार देखकर वे जगत में अपने जीवन को सफल मानकर आनंदित हो रही हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing the four sons with their brides, the mothers fell into supreme bliss. Again and again they gazed at the beauty of Sita and Ram, feeling their lives in the world had become fruitful.
essence: Love can make a lifetime feel fulfilled in one glance.
simple_meaning: The mothers see their sons with their brides and are overwhelmed with joy. Seeing Sita and Ram again and again, they feel their lives have been fulfilled.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary celebration to the rare instant when love makes life feel complete.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of your child walking in with someone they love, and something in you settles. No applause, no achievement, just a sudden sense that the years meant something.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सखीं सीय मुख पुनि पुनि चाही। गान करहिं निज सुकृत सराही॥ बरषहिं सुमन छनहिं छन देवा। नाचहिं गावहिं लावहिं सेवा ॥
translation: सखियाँ सीताजी के मुख को बार-बार देखकर अपने पुण्यों की सराहना करती हुई गान कर रही हैं। देवता क्षण-क्षण में फूल बरसाते, नाचते, गाते तथा अपनी-अपनी सेवा समर्पण करते हैं ॥
english_translation: The companions keep looking again and again at Sita's face and sing, praising their own good fortune. The radiant beings shower flowers each moment; they dance, sing, and offer their service.
essence: Beauty so complete turns spectators into worshippers.
simple_meaning: Sita's companions keep gazing at her with joy, while radiant beings shower flowers and celebrate with song and service.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary celebration to reverent witnessing, where beauty naturally becomes offering.
modern_relevance: At a wedding, everyone falls quiet for a second when the bride enters and the room feels larger than itself. Some moments don't need explanation; they call out gratitude on their own.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि मनोहर चारिउ जोरीं। सारद उपमा सकल ढँढोरीं॥ देत न बनहिं निपट लघु लागीं। एकटक रहीं रूप अनुरागीं ॥
translation: चारों मनोहर जोड़ियों को देखकर सरस्वती ने सारी उपमाओं को खोज डाला, पर कोई उपमा देते नहीं बनी, क्योंकि उन्हें सभी बिलकुल तुच्छ जान पड़ीं। तब हारकर वे भी श्री रामजी के रूप में अनुरक्त होकर एकटक देखती रह गईं ॥
english_translation: Seeing the four beautiful pairs, Saraswati searched through every comparison. None would do, for all seemed utterly small. So she too, captivated by their beauty, stood gazing without blinking.
essence: Beauty beyond comparison leaves even speech silent.
simple_meaning: Saraswati tries to find words for the beauty before her, but every comparison falls short. Even she can only stare in admiration.
insight: It teaches that some experiences should be received before they are explained.
modern_relevance: You open a photo from a wedding or family gathering, and for a second you just stop. Nothing clever comes to mind. The moment is too full for commentary.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निगम नीति कुल रीति करि अरघ पाँवड़े देत। बधुन्ह सहित सुत परिछि सब चलीं लवाइ निकेत ॥
translation: वेद की विधि और कुल की रीति करके अर्घ्य-पाँवड़े देती हुई बहुओं समेत सब पुत्रों को परछन करके माताएँ महल में लिवा चलीं ॥
english_translation: Following the Vedic rule and family custom, the mothers, along with their daughters-in-law, welcomed the sons with offerings and led them into the palace.
essence: Joy becomes complete when love follows proper form.
simple_meaning: The palace women formally welcome the returning princes and escort them inside, following sacred and family customs.
insight: It turns celebration into a form of respect, showing that joy can still follow right conduct.
modern_relevance: A family reunion finally happens after years apart. Before the hugs and laughter, someone still sets out water, greets the elders properly, and makes sure everyone is received with care.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चारि सिंघासन सहज सुहाए। जनु मनोज निज हाथ बनाए॥ तिन्ह पर कुअँरि कुअँर बैठारे। सादर पाय पुनीत पखारे ॥
translation: स्वाभाविक ही सुंदर चार सिंहासन थे, जो मानो कामदेव ने ही अपने हाथ से बनाए थे। उन पर माताओं ने राजकुमारियों और राजकुमारों को बैठाया और आदर के साथ उनके पवित्र चरण धोए ॥
english_translation: Four beautiful thrones stood there, as if Love himself had made them by hand. The mothers seated the princes and princesses upon them and reverently washed their sacred feet.
essence: Honor makes joy feel sacred.
simple_meaning: Four beautiful thrones were prepared, and the mothers seated the royal couples on them and washed their feet with reverence.
insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to reverent welcome.
modern_relevance: At a wedding, an elder gently washes the couple’s feet before the ceremony begins. The room goes quiet. Honor is not spoken here; it is performed with care.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धूप दीप नैबेद बेद बिधि। पूजे बर दुलहिनि मंगल निधि॥ बारहिं बार आरती करहीं। ब्यजन चारु चामर सिर ढरहीं ॥
translation: फिर वेद की विधि के अनुसार मंगल के निधान दूल्हे की दुलहिनों की धूप, दीप और नैवेद्य आदि के द्वारा पूजा की। माताएँ बारम्बार आरती कर रही हैं और वर-वधुओं के सिरों पर सुंदर पंखे तथा चँवर ढल रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Then, according to Vedic ritual, they worshiped the auspicious bridegroom with incense, lamps, and offerings. The mothers repeatedly waved lamps, and beautiful fans and whisk whisks were lowered over the heads of the bride and groom.
essence: Joy bows before union and turns itself into worship.
simple_meaning: The mothers perform wedding worship with lamps, offerings, aarti, fans, and whisk whisks for the bride and groom.
insight: It turns celebration into embodied reverence, showing love through repeated acts of honor.
modern_relevance: A family kitchen fills with steam, noise, and laughter as everyone rushes to serve the newly married couple. The affection is too full to stay silent; it becomes gesture, ritual, and movement.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बस्तु अनेक निछावरि होहीं। भरीं प्रमोद मातु सब सोहीं॥ पावा परम तत्व जनु जोगीं। अमृतु लहेउ जनु संतत रोगीं ॥
translation: अनेकों वस्तुएँ निछावर हो रही हैं, सभी माताएँ आनंद से भरी हुई ऐसी सुशोभित हो रही हैं मानो योगी ने परम तत्व को प्राप्त कर लिया। सदा के रोगी ने मानो अमृत पा लिया ॥
english_translation: Many gifts are being offered. All the mothers glow with joy, as if a yogi has found the highest reality, as if a lifelong sufferer has received nectar.
essence: Joy can feel like healing when longing finally ends.
simple_meaning: The wedding gifts overflow, and the mothers are radiant with joy. Their happiness is compared to a yogi reaching the highest truth and a sick person finally receiving nectar.
insight: It turns ordinary happiness into a sign of deep fulfillment and release.
modern_relevance: You watch a family finally come together after months of tension. The room is full of gifts, smiles, and tears that feel bigger than the occasion itself. Some moments feel like healing, not just celebration.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जनम रंक जनु पारस पावा। अंधहि लोचन लाभु सुहावा॥ मूक बदन जनु सारद छाई। मानहुँ समर सूर जय पाई ॥
translation: जन्म का दरिद्री मानो पारस पा गया। अंधे को सुंदर नेत्रों का लाभ हुआ। गूँगे के मुख में मानो सरस्वती आ विराजीं और शूरवीर ने मानो युद्ध में विजय पा ली ॥
english_translation: A poor person has found the philosopher's stone. A blind person has gained beautiful eyes. A mute person has found speech through Saraswati. A warrior has won victory in battle.
essence: Joy can make every lack feel healed at once.
simple_meaning: The wedding joy feels like impossible blessings: the poor become rich, the blind see, the mute speak, and the defeated win.
insight: It turns celebration into a vision of total restoration, not just happiness.
modern_relevance: You watch your child walk onstage after months of fear, and suddenly every sleepless night feels redeemed. Some moments make life seem to give back more than it took.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि सुख ते सत कोटि गुन पावहिं मातु अनंदु। भाइन्ह सहित बिआहि घर आए रघुकुलचंदु ॥
translation: इन सुखों से भी सौ करोड़ गुना बढ़कर आनंद माताएँ पा रही हैं, क्योंकि रघुकुल के चंद्रमा श्री रामजी विवाह कर के भाइयों सहित घर आए हैं ॥
english_translation: The mothers’ joy is greater than hundreds of millions of pleasures, because the moon of the Raghu clan, Ram, has returned home after the wedding with his brothers.
essence: Homecoming with Ram makes ordinary joy look tiny.
simple_meaning: The mothers feel joy beyond measure because Ram has come home after his wedding, together with his brothers.
insight: It shifts attention from private pleasure to shared homecoming as the deepest happiness.
modern_relevance: You wait at the airport with flowers, then see your child step out after a long separation. The relief is not just happiness — it feels like the house itself has started breathing again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लोक रीति जननीं करहिं बर दुलहिनि सकुचाहिं। मोदु बिनोदु बिलोकि बड़ रामु मनहिं मुसुकाहिं ॥
translation: माताएँ लोकरीति करती हैं और दूल्हे-दुलहिनें सकुचाते हैं। इस महान आनंद और विनोद को देखकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी मन ही मन मुस्कुरा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The mothers observe social custom, and the bride and groom feel shy. Seeing this great joy and playfulness, Ram smiles to himself.
essence: Joy becomes complete when it is seen with a calm heart.
simple_meaning: The wedding is filled with joy and playful shyness. The mothers follow custom, and Ram quietly smiles at the scene.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony alone to the quiet awareness that blesses the ceremony.
modern_relevance: At a family wedding, everyone is busy with rituals, teasing, and shy glances across the room. In the middle of all that noise, one calm smile can hold the whole memory together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देव पितर पूजे बिधि नीकी। पूजीं सकल बासना जी की॥ सबहि बंदि माँगहिं बरदाना। भाइन्ह सहित राम कल्याना ॥
translation: मन की सभी वासनाएँ पूरी हुई जानकर देवता और पितरों का भलीभाँति पूजन किया। सबकी वंदना करके माताएँ यही वरदान माँगती हैं कि भाइयों सहित श्री रामजी का कल्याण हो ॥
english_translation: After honoring the deities and ancestors properly, the mothers' every longing was fulfilled. Bowing to all, they asked for one blessing: may Ram be blessed with his brothers.
essence: Real joy asks for another's well-being first.
simple_meaning: The mothers complete the wedding rites, honor the deities and ancestors, and ask only for Ram's well-being with his brothers.
insight: It shifts the heart from receiving blessing to offering it for another's welfare.
modern_relevance: You finally get the news you waited for, and the first thing you do is call someone else to share it. Joy deepens when it turns outward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अंतरहित सुर आसिष देहीं। मुदित मातु अंचल भरि लेहीं॥ भूपति बोलि बराती लीन्हे। जान बसन मनि भूषन दीन्हे ॥
translation: देवता छिपे हुए (अन्तरिक्ष से) आशीर्वाद दे रहे हैं और माताएँ आनन्दित हो आँचल भरकर ले रही हैं। तदनन्तर राजा ने बारातियों को बुलवा लिया और उन्हें सवारियाँ, वस्त्र, मणि (रत्न) और आभूषणादि दिए ॥
english_translation: The hidden deities gave blessings. The mothers joyfully filled their laps. Then the king called the wedding guests and gave them vehicles, clothes, jewels, and ornaments.
essence: True celebration includes blessing others and giving freely.
simple_meaning: The unseen deities bless the wedding, the mothers receive the joy, and King Janaka honors the guests with gifts.
insight: It shows how celebration becomes complete through blessing, gratitude, and generous hospitality.
modern_relevance: A family wedding finally comes together: the room is glowing, elders are smiling, and the host keeps making sure every guest leaves honored and cared for.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आयसु पाइ राखि उर रामहि। मुदित गए सब निज निज धामहि॥ पुर नर नारि सकल पहिराए। घर घर बाजन लगे बधाए ॥
translation: आज्ञा पाकर, श्री रामजी को हृदय में रखकर वे सब आनंदित होकर अपने-अपने घर गए। नगर के समस्त स्त्री-पुरुषों को राजा ने कपड़े और गहने पहनाए। घर-घर बधावे बजने लगे ॥
english_translation: After receiving the command, keeping Ram in their hearts, they all returned happily to their own homes. The king dressed all the men and women of the city in clothes and ornaments, and celebration drums sounded in every house.
essence: Ram's presence turns the city into one shared celebration.
simple_meaning: Everyone goes home joyful after the king's order, and the whole city is dressed up for celebration.
insight: It shifts attention from private excitement to a whole community sharing one celebration.
modern_relevance: A neighborhood feels different after one good piece of news: doors open, people dress up, and even the smallest homes sound brighter.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जाचक जन जाचहिं जोइ जोई। प्रमुदित राउ देहिं सोइ सोई॥ सेवक सकल बजनिआ नाना। पूरन किए दान सनमाना ॥
translation: याचक लोग जो-जो माँगते हैं, विशेष प्रसन्न होकर राजा उन्हें वही-वही देते हैं। सम्पूर्ण सेवकों और बाजे वालों को राजा ने नाना प्रकार के दान और सम्मान से सन्तुष्ट किया ॥
english_translation: The king cheerfully gave each beggar whatever each one asked for. He satisfied all the servants and musicians with many gifts and honors.
essence: Joy becomes real when it turns into generous giving.
simple_meaning: Beggars received exactly what they asked for, and the king also rewarded the servants and musicians generously.
insight: It shifts attention from celebrating the event to honoring everyone who made it possible.
modern_relevance: At the end of a wedding, someone quietly makes sure the caterers, drivers, and helpers leave with extra envelopes and full stomachs. Real gratitude shows up as generous, specific giving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देहिं असीस जोहारि सब गावहिं गुन गन गाथ। तब गुर भूसुर सहित गृहँ गवनु कीन्ह नरनाथ ॥
translation: सब जोहार (वंदन) करके आशीष देते हैं और गुण समूहों की कथा गाते हैं। तब गुरु और ब्राह्मणों सहित राजा दशरथजी ने महल में गमन किया ॥
english_translation: Everyone bowed, gave blessings, and sang praises of his virtues. Then the king entered the palace with the guru and the brahmins.
essence: Public joy fades into a dignified return home.
simple_meaning: People bowed, blessed the king, and sang his praises. Then Dasharath returned to the palace with the guru and the brahmins.
insight: It closes the scene with honor and transition, not a new teaching.
modern_relevance: After a long ceremony, the guests linger by the gate, smiling, offering blessings, and slowly drifting home. The big moment is over; what remains is quiet respect.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जो बसिष्ट अनुसासन दीन्ही। लोक बेद बिधि सादर कीन्ही॥ भूसुर भीर देखि सब रानी। सादर उठीं भाग्य बड़ जानी ॥
translation: वशिष्ठजी ने जो आज्ञा दी, उसे लोक और वेद की विधि के अनुसार राजा ने आदरपूर्वक किया। ब्राह्मणों की भीड़ देखकर अपना बड़ा भाग्य जानकर सब रानियाँ आदर के साथ उठीं ॥
english_translation: Vashishtha's instructions were carried out with reverence according to worldly custom and Vedic rule. Seeing the crowd of brahmins, all the queens rose respectfully, knowing their great good fortune.
essence: Respect is proved by how you rise for others.
simple_meaning: Vashishtha's instructions are followed with respect, and the queens rise when they see the gathered brahmins, feeling blessed by the honor.
insight: It teaches deference through action: honor is not felt privately, but enacted in public conduct.
modern_relevance: A respected elder enters the room, and everyone quietly stands. No speech is needed — the room itself shows who is being honored.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पाय पखारि सकल अन्हवाए। पूजि भली बिधि भूप जेवाँए॥ आदर दान प्रेम परिपोषे। देत असीस चले मन तोषे ॥
translation: चरण धोकर उन्होंने सबको स्नान कराया और राजा ने भली-भाँति पूजन करके उन्हें भोजन कराया! आदर, दान और प्रेम से पुष्ट हुए वे संतुष्ट मन से आशीर्वाद देते हुए चले ॥
english_translation: He washed their feet, bathed them all, worshipped them properly, and fed them. Honored with gifts and loved deeply, they left content, giving blessings.
essence: Honor becomes complete when care is made visible.
simple_meaning: King Dasharath honors the guests with foot-washing, bathing, worship, food, gifts, and loving respect. The guests leave pleased and blessing him.
insight: It shifts attention from status to service, showing that respect becomes real only when it is enacted.
modern_relevance: Someone comes to your home tired from travel, and you stop everything to make them comfortable. No performance, no display — just wholehearted hospitality that leaves both people lighter.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहु बिधि कीन्हि गाधिसुत पूजा। नाथ मोहि सम धन्य न दूजा॥ कीन्हि प्रसंसा भूपति भूरी। रानिन्ह सहित लीन्हि पग धूरी ॥
translation: राजा ने गाधि पुत्र विश्वामित्रजी की बहुत तरह से पूजा की और कहा- हे नाथ! मेरे समान धन्य दूसरा कोई नहीं है। राजा ने उनकी बहुत प्रशंसा की और रानियों सहित उनकी चरणधूलि को ग्रहण किया ॥
english_translation: The king honored Vishwamitra, son of Gadhi, in many ways and said, “O Lord, no one is as blessed as I am.” He praised him greatly and, with the queens, took the dust of his feet.
essence: True honor begins when pride is willing to bow.
simple_meaning: King Dasharath honors Vishwamitra with gifts, praise, and humility. He even takes the dust from Vishwamitra’s feet along with the queens.
insight: It teaches the reader to honor genuine greatness without self-importance.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose experience dwarfs your own, and you stop performing. You listen, thank them properly, and let your pride kneel first.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भीतर भवन दीन्ह बर बासू। मन जोगवत रह नृपु रनिवासू॥ पूजे गुर पद कमल बहोरी। कीन्हि बिनय उर प्रीति न थोरी ॥
translation: उन्हें महल के भीतर ठहरने को उत्तम स्थान दिया, जिसमें राजा और सब रनिवास उनका मन जोहता रहे (अर्थात जिसमें राजा और महल की सारी रानियाँ स्वयं उनकी इच्छानुसार उनके आराम की ओर दृष्टि रख सकें) फिर राजा ने गुरु वशिष्ठजी के चरणकमलों की पूजा और विनती की। उनके हृदय में कम प्रीति न थी (अर्थात बहुत प्रीति थी) ॥
english_translation: A fine residence was given inside the palace. The king and the queens kept watch over their comfort. Then the king worshiped the guru's lotus feet and bowed with deep love in his heart.
essence: True honor is shown through care and humility, not rank.
simple_meaning: The king gave the visitors a good place to stay, made sure they were cared for, and bowed to his guru with deep respect and love.
insight: It shifts attention from status to service: first care for others, then bow to the source of guidance.
modern_relevance: A guest arrives after a long journey, and you make sure the room is ready before you ask anything of them. Then you thank the mentor who made the meeting possible. Care and humility together change the whole atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बधुन्ह समेत कुमार सब रानिन्ह सहित महीसु। पुनि पुनि बंदत गुर चरन देत असीस मुनीसु ॥
translation: बहुओं सहित सब राजकुमार और सब रानियों समेत राजा बार-बार गुरुजी के चरणों की वंदना करते हैं और मुनीश्वर आशीर्वाद देते हैं ॥
english_translation: With the princes, their wives, and the queens together, the king repeatedly bowed at the guru's feet, and the sage gave his blessings.
essence: Humility becomes complete when an entire household bows together.
simple_meaning: The king, his sons, their wives, and the queens all bow again and again to the guru, and the sage blesses them.
insight: It highlights reverence as a shared family act, not a private gesture.
modern_relevance: A family gathers before an elder who has shaped their lives. No one performs for show; everyone simply bows, listens, and receives blessing with humility.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिनय कीन्हि उर अति अनुरागें। सुत संपदा राखि सब आगें॥ नेगु मागि मुनिनायक लीन्हा। आसिरबादु बहुत बिधि दीन्हा ॥
translation: राजा ने अत्यन्त प्रेमपूर्ण हृदय से पुत्रों को और सारी सम्पत्ति को सामने रखकर (उन्हें स्वीकार करने के लिए) विनती की, परन्तु मुनिराज ने (पुरोहित के नाते) केवल अपना नेग माँग लिया और बहुत तरह से आशीर्वाद दिया ॥
english_translation: With great affection in his heart, the king placed his sons and all his wealth before the sage and made his request. The sage accepted only the customary honor-gift and gave blessings in many ways.
essence: Honor matters more than wealth when reverence is real.
simple_meaning: Dasharath respectfully offers his sons and wealth to the sage, but the sage asks only for the customary honor-gift and blesses them generously.
insight: It shifts attention from material display to proper respect and simple generosity.
modern_relevance: You meet someone important and start offering favors, gifts, and leverage. They do not want your display of abundance — only sincerity and the right gesture.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उर धरि रामहि सीय समेता। हरषि कीन्ह गुर गवनु निकेता॥ बिप्रबधू सब भूप बोलाईं। चैल चारु भूषन पहिराईं ॥
translation: फिर सीताजी सहित श्री रामचन्द्रजी को हृदय में रखकर गुरु वशिष्ठजी हर्षित होकर अपने स्थान को गए। राजा ने सब ब्राह्मणों की स्त्रियों को बुलवाया और उन्हें सुंदर वस्त्र तथा आभूषण पहनाए ॥
english_translation: Holding Ram and Sita in his heart, the teacher returned home with joy. The king called all the wives of the Brahmins and dressed them in fine clothes and ornaments.
essence: Joy becomes complete when it turns into honoring others.
simple_meaning: Vashishtha leaves happily with Ram and Sita in his heart. King Janaka then calls the Brahmin women and honors them with beautiful clothes and ornaments.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the grace shown in how people are treated afterward.
modern_relevance: After a long family ceremony ends, the host does not rush to collapse. He thanks the guests, honors the elders, and sends everyone home with care. That is the dignity of a generous heart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरि बोलाइ सुआसिनि लीन्हीं। रुचि बिचारि पहिरावनि दीन्हीं॥ नेगी नेग जोग जब लेहीं। रुचि अनुरूप भूपमनि देहीं ॥
translation: फिर अब सुआसिनियों को (नगर की सौभाग्यवती बहिन, बेटी, भानजी आदि को) बुलवा लिया और उनकी रुचि समझकर (उसी के अनुसार) उन्हें पहिरावनी दी। नेगी लोग सब अपना-अपना नेग-जोग लेते और राजाओं के शिरोमणि दशरथजी उनकी इच्छा के अनुसार देते हैं ॥
english_translation: Then he called the married women and, understanding what each liked, gave them gifts and garments accordingly. The recipients took their customary gifts, and King Dasharath gave each one according to her wish.
essence: True generosity meets each person where their heart already is.
simple_meaning: Dasharath honors the women at the wedding by giving each one gifts suited to her liking.
insight: It shifts giving from routine charity to attentive, person-shaped care.
modern_relevance: At a family wedding, one aunt loves silver bangles, another prefers a shawl, and a child only wants sweets. Real generosity notices the person, not just the price tag.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रिय पाहुने पूज्य जे जाने। भूपति भली भाँति सनमाने॥ देव देखि रघुबीर बिबाहू। बरषि प्रसून प्रसंसि उछाहू ॥
translation: जिन मेहमानों को प्रिय और पूजनीय जाना, उनका राजा ने भलीभाँति सम्मान किया। देवगण श्री रघुनाथजी का विवाह देखकर, उत्सव की प्रशंसा करके फूल बरसाते हुए- ॥
english_translation: The king honored the guests he regarded as dear and worthy of reverence. Seeing Raghubir's wedding, the divine beings praised the celebration and showered flowers.
essence: Honor the guests; the sacred joy answers with flowers.
simple_meaning: The king treated honored guests with respect. The divine beings rejoiced at Ram's wedding and showered flowers.
insight: It turns ceremony into reverence, showing that celebration and hospitality belong together.
modern_relevance: At a wedding reception, the host notices the elderly aunt, the quiet teacher, the distant cousin, and makes each one feel seen. That kind of grace turns a gathering into blessing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चले निसान बजाइ सुर निज निज पुर सुख पाइ। कहत परसपर राम जसु प्रेम न हृदयँ समाइ ॥
translation: नगाड़े बजाकर और (परम) सुख प्राप्त कर अपने-अपने लोकों को चले। वे एक-दूसरे से श्री रामजी का यश कहते जाते हैं। हृदय में प्रेम समाता नहीं है ॥
english_translation: The gods departed to their own abodes, beating drums in joy. They spoke among themselves of Ram's glory, and love would not fit within their hearts.
essence: True joy keeps turning into praise.
simple_meaning: The radiant beings left joyfully after the wedding, praising Ram among themselves. Their hearts were so full of love that it could not be contained.
insight: It shows how devotion expresses itself as shared remembrance, not private feeling.
modern_relevance: You leave a wedding, still buzzing, and keep replaying the best moments with the friend beside you. The joy is so full it keeps turning into praise.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब बिधि सबहि समदि नरनाहू। रहा हृदयँ भरि पूरि उछाहू॥ जहँ रनिवासु तहाँ पगु धारे। सहित बहूटिन्ह कुअँर निहारे ॥
translation: सब प्रकार से सबका प्रेमपूर्वक भली-भाँति आदर-सत्कार कर लेने पर राजा दशरथजी के हृदय में पूर्ण उत्साह (आनंद) भर गया। जहाँ रनिवास था, वे वहाँ पधारे और बहुओं समेत उन्होंने कुमारों को देखा ॥
english_translation: After honoring everyone properly, the king’s heart filled with joy. He then went to the queens’ residence and looked upon the princes with his daughters-in-law.
essence: Honor everyone first; joy naturally fills the heart.
simple_meaning: King Dasharath, full of joy after honoring his guests, goes to the queens’ quarters and looks at the princes with their wives.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to the human warmth that remains after ceremony ends.
modern_relevance: After hosting a wedding, you finally walk into the quiet house and see your family gathered, laughing in the kitchen. The relief is not in the event itself, but in everyone being safely together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लिए गोद करि मोद समेता। को कहि सकइ भयउ सुखु जेता॥ बधू सप्रेम गोद बैठारीं। बार बार हियँ हरषि दुलारीं ॥
translation: राजा ने आनंद सहित पुत्रों को गोद में ले लिया। उस समय राजा को जितना सुख हुआ उसे कौन कह सकता है? फिर पुत्रवधुओं को प्रेम सहित गोदी में बैठाकर, बार-बार हृदय में हर्षित होकर उन्होंने उनका दुलार (लाड़-चाव) किया ॥
english_translation: The king joyfully took the sons into his lap. Who can describe the happiness he felt? Then he lovingly seated the daughters-in-law on his lap and, again and again delighted in his heart, caressed them tenderly.
essence: Joy becomes complete when it is shared through loving touch.
simple_meaning: Dasharath overflows with joy as he embraces his sons and lovingly welcomes the daughters-in-law.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to tenderness, showing that affection is the real celebration.
modern_relevance: You finally get everyone under one roof after a long wedding weekend. The noise is exhausting, the room is crowded, and yet one embrace makes the whole house feel blessed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि समाजु मुदित रनिवासू। सब कें उर अनंद कियो बासू॥ कहेउ भूप जिमि भयउ बिबाहू। सुनि सुनि हरषु होत सब काहू ॥
translation: यह समाज (समारोह) देखकर रनिवास प्रसन्न हो गया। सबके हृदय में आनंद ने निवास कर लिया। तब राजा ने जिस तरह विवाह हुआ था, वह सब कहा। उसे सुन-सुनकर सब किसी को हर्ष होता है ॥
english_translation: Seeing the gathering, the women in the inner chambers were delighted. Joy settled in every heart. Then the king told how the marriage had happened, and hearing it again and again, everyone felt happiness.
essence: Joy multiplies when a beloved story is retold.
simple_meaning: The whole household feels joy as the king recounts the wedding, and everyone keeps listening with happiness.
insight: It shows how joyful memory can renew a whole room, turning narration itself into celebration.
modern_relevance: A family sits around the dinner table after a wedding, retelling the same beautiful moment from different angles. Nobody is bored; everyone keeps smiling because love becomes richer when it is remembered together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जनक राज गुन सीलु बड़ाई। प्रीति रीति संपदा सुहाई॥ बहुबिधि भूप भाट जिमि बरनी। रानीं सब प्रमुदित सुनि करनी ॥
translation: राजा जनक के गुण, शील, महत्व, प्रीति की रीति और सुहावनी सम्पत्ति का वर्णन राजा ने भाट की तरह बहुत प्रकार से किया। जनकजी की करनी सुनकर सब रानियाँ बहुत प्रसन्न हुईं ॥
english_translation: The king described Janak's virtues, noble character, loving conduct, and splendid wealth in many ways, like a bard. Hearing of Janak's deeds, all the queens were greatly pleased.
essence: True greatness is the kind that delights others when spoken aloud.
simple_meaning: Janak's virtues, conduct, love, and prosperity are praised at length, and the queens feel delighted hearing about him.
insight: It shifts attention from status to character, showing how conduct creates trust and joy.
modern_relevance: At a wedding dinner, someone tells stories about the bride's father — how steady, generous, and respected he is. The table softens. People who never met him feel warmth just hearing his name.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुतन्ह समेत नहाइ नृप बोलि बिप्र गुर ग्याति। भोजन कीन्ह अनेक बिधि घरी पंच गइ राति॥।354॥
translation: पुत्रों सहित स्नान करके राजा ने ब्राह्मण, गुरु और कुटुम्बियों को बुलाकर अनेक प्रकार के भोजन किए। (यह सब करते-करते) पाँच घड़ी रात बीत गई ॥
english_translation: After bathing with his sons, the king called the priests, the teacher, and his relatives, and they ate many kinds of food. Five watches of the night passed in this way.
essence: Joy ripens when the whole household is gathered.
