simple_meaning: The king, his sons, priests, teacher, and relatives shared a festive meal after bathing. Time passed into the night as the celebration continued.
insight: It keeps the focus on communal celebration, not private emotion, showing how joy is shared through ritual and hospitality.
modern_relevance: A family reunion runs late after a wedding, with elders, cousins, and teachers all still gathered around the table. No one wants the evening to end.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंगलगान करहिं बर भामिनि। भै सुखमूल मनोहर जामिनि॥ अँचइ पान सब काहूँ पाए। स्रग सुगंध भूषित छबि छाए ॥
translation: सुंदर स्त्रियाँ मंगलगान कर रही हैं। वह रात्रि सुख की मूल और मनोहारिणी हो गई। सबने आचमन करके पान खाए और फूलों की माला, सुगंधित द्रव्य आदि से विभूषित होकर सब शोभा से छा गए ॥
english_translation: Beautiful women sang auspicious songs. The night became the very source of delight, lovely and sweet. Everyone received betel leaf and wereca nut, and they shone with garlands, fragrance, and adornment.
essence: Joy can turn even night into ornament.
simple_meaning: The celebration is in full swing. Women sing auspicious songs, everyone is adorned, and the whole night feels joyful and beautiful.
insight: It shifts attention from event to atmosphere, letting the reader feel the fullness of the moment.
modern_relevance: At a wedding reception, the music keeps rising, trays keep moving, and every face looks softened by celebration. Nothing is being argued here — only joy filling the room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामहि देखि रजायसु पाई। निज निज भवन चले सिर नाई॥ प्रेम प्रमोदु बिनोदु बड़ाई। समउ समाजु मनोहरताई ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर और आज्ञा पाकर सब सिर नवाकर अपने-अपने घर को चले। वहाँ के प्रेम, आनंद, विनोद, महत्व, समय, समाज और मनोहरता को- ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ram and receiving his leave, everyone bowed their heads and returned to their own homes. The love, joy, delight, greatness, occasion, gathering, and beauty of that moment were beyond measure.
essence: Ram's presence turns an ordinary departure into a scene of grace.
simple_meaning: After seeing Ram and receiving permission, everyone bowed and went home. The scene was full of love, joy, and beauty.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the atmosphere of love it creates.
modern_relevance: The wedding ends, the last guest steps into the night, and no one wants the evening to break. You leave carrying the warmth of a room where everyone felt held.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहि न सकहिं सतसारद सेसू। बेद बिरंचि महेस गनेसू॥ सो मैं कहौं कवन बिधि बरनी। भूमिनागु सिर धरइ कि धरनी ॥
translation: सैकड़ों सरस्वती, शेष, वेद, ब्रह्मा, महादेवजी और गणेशजी भी नहीं कह सकते। फिर भला मैं उसे किस प्रकार से बखानकर कहूँ? कहीं केंचुआ भी धरती को सिर पर ले सकता है? ॥
english_translation: Even a hundred Saraswatis, Shesha, the Vedas, Brahma, Mahesh, and Ganesha cannot describe it. How can I, then, tell it fully? Can an earthworm carry the earth on its head?
essence: Greatness outruns speech; humility is the only faithful response.
simple_meaning: No one can fully describe what happened, not even the greatest beings and sages. The poet says he cannot carry the whole weight of it in words.
insight: It teaches the reader to honor what exceeds description instead of forcing a neat summary.
modern_relevance: You try to explain a moment that changed your life, and every sentence feels flat. Some things deserve reverence more than explanation.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: नृप सब भाँति सबहि सनमानी। कहि मृदु बचन बोलाईं रानी॥ बधू लरिकनीं पर घर आईं। राखेहु नयन पलक की नाई ॥
translation: राजा ने सबका सब प्रकार से सम्मान करके, कोमल वचन कहकर रानियों को बुलाया और कहा- बहुएँ अभी बच्ची हैं, पराए घर आई हैं। इनको इस तरह से रखना जैसे नेत्रों को पलकें रखती हैं (जैसे पलकें नेत्रों की सब प्रकार से रक्षा करती हैं और उन्हें सुख पहुँचाती हैं, वैसे ही इनको सुख पहुँचाना) ॥
english_translation: The king honored everyone in every way, spoke gently, and called the queens, saying: "The daughters-in-law are still children and have come to another home. Care for them as the eyelids care for the eyes."
essence: Care for newcomers like eyes are guarded by eyelids.
simple_meaning: The king tells the queens to treat the young daughters-in-law with gentle care, like eyelids protect eyes.
insight: It shifts attention from judging newcomers to protecting their dignity and ease.
modern_relevance: A new daughter-in-law arrives with awkward silence, folded hands, and a heart trying not to show fear. The right response is not scrutiny, but care that makes her feel safe.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लरिका श्रमित उनीद बस सयन करावहु जाइ। अस कहि गे बिश्रामगृहँ राम चरन चितु लाइ ॥
translation: लड़के थके हुए नींद के वश हो रहे हैं, इन्हें ले जाकर शयन कराओ। ऐसा कहकर राजा श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में मन लगाकर विश्राम भवन में चले गए ॥
english_translation: The children are tired and falling asleep. Take them and put them to bed. Saying this, he went to the rest house, fixing his mind on Ram's feet.
essence: Tender duty and inward devotion move together.
simple_meaning: The king tells the women to put the sleepy children to bed, then leaves for the rest house with his mind fixed on Ram.
insight: It models calm responsibility: attend to practical needs first, then return the mind to what is sacred.
modern_relevance: A parent notices the kids nodding off after a long family gathering, quietly gets them settled, and then slips away without fuss. Care can be tender and inwardly devoted at the same time.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूप बचन सुनि सहज सुहाए। जरित कनक मनि पलँग डसाए॥ सुभग सुरभि पय फेन समाना। कोमल कलित सुपेतीं नाना ॥
translation: राजा के स्वाभव से ही सुंदर वचन सुनकर (रानियों ने) मणियों से जड़े सुवर्ण के पलँग बिछवाए। (गद्दों पर) गो के फेन के समान सुंदर एवं कोमल अनेकों सफेद चादरें बिछाईं ॥
english_translation: Hearing the king's gentle words, they spread jewel-studded golden beds. On them they laid many soft white coverings, beautiful like foaming milk.
essence: Kind authority creates care without force.
simple_meaning: The royal women prepare luxurious beds and soft white coverings for the children after hearing the king's kind instructions.
insight: It shifts attention from grand gestures to the quiet, immediate acts that make others feel protected.
modern_relevance: A parent comes home exhausted after a hard day, and the family quietly sets out food, water, and a clean bed before a single complaint is spoken. Care begins with how you respond.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उपबरहन बर बरनि न जाहीं। स्रग सुगंध मनिमंदिर माहीं॥ रतनदीप सुठि चारु चँदोवा। कहत न बनइ जान जेहिं जोवा ॥
translation: सुंदर तकियों का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। मणियों के मंदिर में फूलों की मालाएँ और सुगंध द्रव्य सजे हैं। सुंदर रत्नों के दीपकों और सुंदर चँदोवे की शोभा कहते नहीं बनती। जिसने उन्हें देखा हो, वही जान सकता है ॥
english_translation: The cushions cannot be described. In the jeweled palace, garlands and fragrant offerings were arranged. The glow of jeweled lamps and the beauty of the canopy cannot be told; only one who has seen it knows.
essence: Some forms of care can only be felt, not fully described.
simple_meaning: The palace room is so beautifully arranged with cushions, flowers, fragrance, lamps, and a canopy that words cannot fully capture it.
insight: It shifts attention from the objects themselves to the love that arranged them.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after someone quietly prepared it for you: clean sheets, soft light, flowers, and everything in place. The care is obvious before a single word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सेज रुचिर रचि रामु उठाए। प्रेम समेत पलँग पौढ़ाए॥ अग्या पुनि पुनि भाइन्ह दीन्ही। निज निज सेज सयन तिन्ह कीन्ही ॥
translation: इस प्रकार सुंदर शय्या सजाकर (माताओं ने) श्री रामचन्द्रजी को उठाया और प्रेम सहित पलँग पर पौढ़ाया। श्री रामजी ने बार-बार भाइयों को आज्ञा दी। तब वे भी अपनी-अपनी शय्याओं पर सो गए ॥
english_translation: After arranging a lovely bed, they laid Ram down on the couch with love. Again and again, he instructed his brothers, and then they all lay down in their own beds.
essence: Ram's care reaches his brothers before his own rest.
simple_meaning: Ram is lovingly put to rest, and he makes sure his brothers also sleep in their own beds.
insight: It shifts attention from private comfort to shared responsibility, even in small domestic moments.
modern_relevance: After a long family gathering, everyone is tired and drifting toward bed. One person still checks that the younger siblings are settled, lights are off, and everyone is comfortable before resting.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि स्याम मृदु मंजुल गाता। कहहिं सप्रेम बचन सब माता॥ मारग जात भयावनि भारी। केहि बिधि तात ताड़का मारी ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के साँवले सुंदर कोमल अँगों को देखकर सब माताएँ प्रेम सहित वचन कह रही हैं- हे तात! मार्ग में जाते हुए तुमने बड़ी भयावनी ताड़का राक्षसी को किस प्रकार से मारा? ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ram's soft, beautiful dark form, all the mothers speak with love: "Dear son, while traveling on the road, how did you kill the dreadful Tadka?"
essence: His gentleness and strength are seen as one.
simple_meaning: The mothers look at young Ram's gentle, beautiful form and lovingly ask how he killed the terrible Tadka on the road.
insight: It shifts attention from the violence of the act to the tenderness of the one who acted.
modern_relevance: A child comes home with scraped knees after handling a bully at school, and the family keeps asking the same thing: how did you do that? The question is really admiration.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: घोर निसाचर बिकट भट समर गनहिं नहिं काहु। मारे सहित सहाय किमि खल मारीच सुबाहु ॥
translation: बड़े भयानक राक्षस, जो विकट योद्धा थे और जो युद्ध में किसी को कुछ नहीं गिनते थे, उन दुष्ट मारीच और सुबाहु को सहायकों सहित तुमने कैसे मारा? ॥
english_translation: How did you kill the terrible night-rangers, fierce warriors who counted no one in battle, Maricha and Subahu, along with their helpers?
essence: Gentleness can conceal overwhelming strength.
simple_meaning: The mothers ask how Ram managed to defeat the fierce demons Maricha and Subahu, along with their allies.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance to hidden capacity.
modern_relevance: A parent watches a quiet teenager and remembers the day that same child stood up to a bully everyone else avoided. The memory makes ordinary strength look almost miraculous.
speaker: Mothers

verse_text: मुनि प्रसाद बलि तात तुम्हारी। ईस अनेक करवरें टारी॥ मख रखवारी करि दुहुँ भाईं। गुरु प्रसाद सब बिद्या पाईं ॥
translation: हे तात! मैं बलैया लेती हूँ, मुनि की कृपा से ही ईश्वर ने तुम्हारी बहुत सी बलाओं को टाल दिया। दोनों भाइयों ने यज्ञ की रखवाली करके गुरुजी के प्रसाद से सब विद्याएँ पाईं ॥
english_translation: By the sage's grace, dear son, your many dangers were averted. Both brothers guarded the sacrifice, and by the teacher's grace they received all knowledge.
essence: Grace protects, service teaches, and learning arrives through the teacher.
simple_meaning: The mothers bless Ram and Lakshman, saying their dangers were removed by the sage's grace. They also praise how both brothers guarded the sacrifice and gained all learning through their teacher's blessing.
insight: It shifts attention from raw talent to the quiet forces that shape a life: blessing, guidance, and faithful duty.
modern_relevance: A parent watches a child leave for a hard school, a first job, or a risky city, and can only bless them inwardly. Some protection comes from unseen help, and some learning comes from serving a larger purpose.
speaker: Mothers

verse_text: मुनितिय तरी लगत पग धूरी। कीरति रही भुवन भरि पूरी॥ कमठ पीठि पबि कूट कठोरा। नृप समाज महुँ सिव धनु तोरा ॥
translation: चरणों की धूलि लगते ही मुनि पत्नी अहल्या तर गई। विश्वभर में यह कीर्ति पूर्ण रीति से व्याप्त हो गई। कच्छप की पीठ, वज्र और पर्वत से भी कठोर शिवजी के धनुष को राजाओं के समाज में तुमने तोड़ दिया! ॥
english_translation: The moment the dust of your feet touched her, Ahalya was redeemed. That fame spread fully across the worlds. You broke Shiva’s bow in the assembly of kings, though it was harder than a tortoise’s back, thunderbolt, and mountain.
essence: His touch restores, and his power shatters what none else could.
simple_meaning: Ahalya is freed by the touch of Ram’s feet, and his fame spreads everywhere. In the kings’ assembly, he breaks Shiva’s bow, proving his unmatched strength.
insight: It links mercy and strength, showing that true greatness heals first and proves itself without boasting.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room carrying shame, and one person treats you with dignity instead of suspicion. That can change a life. Then comes the harder test: can you still act with strength?
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिस्व बिजय जसु जानकि पाई। आए भवन ब्याहि सब भाई॥ सकल अमानुष करम तुम्हारे। केवल कौसिक कृपाँ सुधारे ॥
translation: विश्वविजय के यश और जानकी को पाया और सब भाइयों को ब्याहकर घर आए। तुम्हारे सभी कर्म अमानुषी हैं (मनुष्य की शक्ति के बाहर हैं), जिन्हें केवल विश्वामित्रजी की कृपा ने सुधारा है (सम्पन्न किया है) ॥
english_translation: You won the world and won Janaki, then returned home with all your brothers married. All your deeds are beyond ordinary human power; only Vishwamitra's grace brought them to completion.
essence: Even victory becomes humble when grace is remembered.
simple_meaning: The brothers return home with Janaki after winning her hand. Their achievements are described as beyond ordinary human power and made complete by Vishvamitra's grace.
insight: It shifts credit away from personal mastery and toward the grace that made success possible.
modern_relevance: You finally close the deal, get the offer, and come home to celebrate. But one honest glance back tells you how many hands, chances, and blessings carried you there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आजु सुफल जग जनमु हमारा। देखि तात बिधुबदन तुम्हारा॥ जे दिन गए तुम्हहि बिनु देखें। ते बिरंचि जनि पारहिं लेखें ॥
translation: हे तात! तुम्हारा चन्द्रमुख देखकर आज हमारा जगत में जन्म लेना सफल हुआ। तुमको बिना देखे जो दिन बीते हैं, उनको ब्रह्मा गिनती में न लावें (हमारी आयु में शामिल न करें) ॥
english_translation: O dear one, seeing your moon-like face, our life feels fulfilled today. The days spent without seeing you should not even be counted by Brahma.
essence: Presence with Ram makes every other day feel incomplete.
simple_meaning: The speaker says that seeing Ram's face makes life feel fulfilled, and the days spent without his sight feel unworthy of counting.
insight: It shifts attention from counting days to valuing presence. What matters is not duration, but contact with what you love most.
modern_relevance: You finally see someone you have waited months to meet, and the whole room changes. The long wait vanishes the moment they arrive, because presence matters more than the calendar.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: राम प्रतोषीं मातु सब कहि बिनीत बर बैन। सुमिरि संभु गुरु बिप्र पद किए नीदबस नैन ॥
translation: विनय भरे उत्तम वचन कहकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सब माताओं को संतुष्ट किया। फिर शिवजी, गुरु और ब्राह्मणों के चरणों का स्मरण कर नेत्रों को नींद के वश किया। (अर्थात वे सो रहे) ॥
english_translation: Ram satisfied all the mothers with humble and gracious words. Then, remembering Shiva, the teacher, and the Brahmins, he let sleep take his eyes.
essence: Greatness stays gentle when it remembers whom to honor.
simple_meaning: Ram speaks gently to the mothers, then remembers Shiva, his teacher, and the learned Brahmins before falling asleep.
insight: It shifts attention from achievement to reverence, showing that success should end in gratitude, not self-importance.
modern_relevance: You finally finish the big event everyone praised, then still thank the people who made it possible. The real mark of maturity is not the applause — it is the humility that follows it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नीदउँ बदन सोह सुठि लोना। मनहुँ साँझ सरसीरुह सोना॥ घर घर करहिं जागरन नारीं। देहिं परसपर मंगल गारीं ॥
translation: नींद में भी उनका अत्यन्त सलोना मुखड़ा ऐसा सोह रहा था, मानो संध्या के समय का लाल कमल सोह रहा हो। स्त्रियाँ घर-घर जागरण कर रही हैं और आपस में (एक-दूसरी को) मंगलमयी गालियाँ दे रही हैं ॥
english_translation: Even in sleep, his lovely face shone so beautifully, like a red lotus at dusk. Women held wakeful celebrations from house to house and exchanged blessings in the form of playful scolding.
essence: Presence makes even sleep radiant, and celebration becomes blessing.
simple_meaning: Ram's face was so beautiful even in sleep that it looked like a glowing lotus. In Ayodhya, women stayed awake in celebration and greeted each other with affectionate teasing.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the atmosphere devotion creates around it.
modern_relevance: A home after a long-awaited reunion feels different: people stay up late, talk over each other, and laugh at small things because the person they missed is finally there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुरी बिराजति राजति रजनी। रानीं कहहिं बिलोकहु सजनी॥ सुंदर बधुन्ह सासु लै सोईं। फनिकन्ह जनु सिरमनि उर गोईं ॥
translation: रानियाँ कहती हैं- हे सजनी! देखो, (आज) रात्रि की कैसी शोभा है, जिससे अयोध्यापुरी विशेष शोभित हो रही है! (यों कहती हुई) सासुएँ सुंदर बहुओं को लेकर सो गईं, मानो सर्पों ने अपने सिर की मणियों को हृदय में छिपा लिया है ॥
english_translation: The city shone in the night. The queens said, “Look, dear friend, how beautiful the night is.” The graceful daughters-in-law took their mothers-in-law to sleep, like snakes hiding their jewels in their hearts.
essence: Peaceful order makes a city glow from within.
simple_meaning: Ayodhya is so peaceful and beautiful at night that even the queens admire it. The household settles into sleep, with the younger women gently attending to the older women.
insight: It shifts attention from action to atmosphere, showing how harmony itself becomes a sign of grace.
modern_relevance: A house finally goes quiet after a long family gathering. The dishes are done, the elders are settled, and the whole place feels held. That soft order is its own kind of blessing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रात पुनीत काल प्रभु जागे। अरुनचूड़ बर बोलन लागे॥ बंदि मागधन्हि गुनगन गाए। पुरजन द्वार जोहारन आए ॥
translation: प्रातःकाल पवित्र ब्रह्म मुहूर्त में प्रभु जागे। मुर्गे सुंदर बोलने लगे। भाट और मागधों ने गुणों का गान किया तथा नगर के लोग द्वार पर जोहार करने को आए ॥
english_translation: At the sacred dawn, the Lord awoke. The red-crested roosters began to crow. Bards and minstrels sang his praises, and the townspeople came to the door to pay respects.
essence: Dawn itself seems to rise in reverence around Ram.
simple_meaning: Ram wakes at dawn, the birds crow, singers praise him, and the townspeople gather to honor him.
insight: It frames ordinary morning activity as an atmosphere of honor and blessing, not just routine.
modern_relevance: You wake before sunrise and the house is still quiet, but the day already feels charged. Before anyone asks anything of you, the morning itself seems to bow.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बंदि बिप्र सुर गुर पितु माता। पाइ असीस मुदित सब भ्राता॥ जननिन्ह सादर बदन निहारे। भूपति संग द्वार पगु धारे ॥
translation: ब्राह्मणों, देवताओं, गुरु, पिता और माताओं की वंदना करके आशीर्वाद पाकर सब भाई प्रसन्न हुए। माताओं ने आदर के साथ उनके मुखों को देखा। फिर वे राजा के साथ दरवाजे (बाहर) पधारे ॥
english_translation: Having bowed to the brahmins, the radiant beings, the teacher, father, and mother, all the brothers rejoiced after receiving blessings. The mothers looked upon their faces with reverence. Then they went out through the doorway with the king.
essence: Blessing comes before movement.
simple_meaning: The brothers bow to elders and receive blessings before leaving with the king. Their mothers watch them with loving respect.
insight: It places humility before action and shows that strength begins with honoring those who raised and guided you.
modern_relevance: Before a child leaves for an exam, a parent quietly touches their forehead and blesses them. Before the day begins, respect and blessing come first.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कीन्हि सौच सब सहज सुचि सरित पुनीत नहाइ। प्रातक्रिया करि तात पहिं आए चारिउ भाइ ॥
translation: स्वभाव से ही पवित्र चारों भाइयों ने सब शौचादि से निवृत्त होकर पवित्र सरयू नदी में स्नान किया और प्रातःक्रिया (संध्या वंदनादि) करके वे पिता के पास आए ॥
english_translation: The four brothers, naturally pure, completed their cleansing, bathed in the sacred Sarayu, performed their morning rites, and then came to their father.
essence: Purity and routine come before action.
simple_meaning: The four brothers bathe, complete their morning duties, and go to their father. It is a calm, orderly morning scene.
insight: It shifts attention from rushing into the day to beginning with order and care.
modern_relevance: You finish your morning shower, prayers, and a quiet walk before the house wakes up. The day feels steadier because you began it clean and composed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूप बिलोकि लिए उर लाई। बैठे हरषि रजायसु पाई॥ देखि रामु सब सभा जुड़ानी। लोचन लाभ अवधि अनुमानी ॥
translation: राजा ने देखते ही उन्हें हृदय से लगा लिया। तदनन्तर वे आज्ञा पाकर हर्षित होकर बैठ गए। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन कर और नेत्रों के लाभ की बस यही सीमा है, ऐसा अनुमान कर सारी सभा शीतल हो गई। (अर्थात सबके तीनों प्रकार के ताप सदा के लिए मिट गए) ॥
english_translation: The king embraced them at once and seated them with joy. Seeing Ram, the whole assembly felt cooled, as if the eyes had reached their limit.
essence: Ram’s presence cools what the world has heated.
simple_meaning: The king hugs the brothers and seats them happily. Seeing Ram makes everyone feel complete and deeply soothed.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to presence: Ram’s arrival itself restores the whole gathering.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after weeks away, and one familiar face changes everything. The tension drops, shoulders loosen, and everyone knows they are safe again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि बसिष्टु मुनि कौसिकु आए। सुभग आसनन्हि मुनि बैठाए॥ सुतन्ह समेत पूजि पद लागे। निरखि रामु दोउ गुर अनुरागे ॥
translation: फिर मुनि वशिष्ठजी और विश्वामित्रजी आए। राजा ने उनको सुंदर आसनों पर बैठाया और पुत्रों समेत उनकी पूजा करके उनके चरणों लगे। दोनों गुरु श्री रामजी को देखकर प्रेम में मुग्ध हो गए ॥
english_translation: Then the sage Vashishtha and sage Kaushika arrived. The king seated the sages on fine seats, worshipped them with his sons, and bowed at their feet. Seeing Ram, both teachers were filled with love.
essence: True honor turns arrival into devotion.
simple_meaning: King Janak honors Vashishtha and Vishwamitra, seats them well, bows with his sons, and both teachers are moved with love on seeing Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from status and ceremony to reverence that softens everyone present.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when someone greets elders with real humility, not performance. The atmosphere changes before a word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहहिं बसिष्टु धरम इतिहासा। सुनहिं महीसु सहित रनिवासा॥ मुनि मन अगम गाधिसुत करनी। मुदित बसिष्ठ बिपुल बिधि बरनी ॥
translation: वशिष्ठजी धर्म के इतिहास कह रहे हैं और राजा रनिवास सहित सुन रहे हैं, जो मुनियों के मन को भी अगम्य है, ऐसी विश्वामित्रजी की करनी को वशिष्ठजी ने आनंदित होकर बहुत प्रकार से वर्णन किया ॥
english_translation: Vashishtha speaks of the histories of dharma, and the king with the royal women listens. The deeds of Vishvamitra are beyond even a sage's mind, and Vashishtha joyfully describes them in many ways.
essence: A saint's life becomes living instruction when told with reverence.
simple_meaning: Vashishtha recounts the sacred history of Vishvamitra's life while the king and the palace women listen with attention.
insight: It shifts attention from the present scene to the moral power of remembered example.
modern_relevance: At a family gathering, an elder tells the story of someone who changed completely through discipline and courage. Everyone falls quiet, not for entertainment, but because the story itself carries authority.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बोले बामदेउ सब साँची। कीरति कलित लोक तिहुँ माची॥ सुनि आनंदु भयउ सब काहू। राम लखन उर अधिक उछाहू ॥
translation: वामदेवजी बोले- ये सब बातें सत्य हैं। विश्वामित्रजी की सुंदर कीर्ति तीनों लोकों में छाई हुई है। यह सुनकर सब किसी को आनंद हुआ। श्री राम-लक्ष्मण के हृदय में अधिक उत्साह (आनंद) हुआ ॥
english_translation: Vamadeva said, “All of this is true. Vishvamitra's splendid fame has spread through all three worlds.” Hearing this, everyone felt joy, and Ram and Lakshman felt even greater delight in their hearts.
essence: True greatness needs no defence; it is already known.
simple_meaning: Vamadeva confirms that Vishvamitra's fame is truly widespread. Everyone feels happy hearing it, and Ram and Lakshman feel especially glad.
insight: It shifts attention from private opinion to public recognition of earned greatness.
modern_relevance: A respected mentor walks into the room and someone finally names what everyone already felt: this person has earned it. The mood changes instantly, and the people who listen with humility feel it most.
speaker: Vamadeva

verse_text: मंगल मोद उछाह नित जाहिं दिवस एहि भाँति। उमगी अवध अनंद भरि अधिक अधिक अधिकाति ॥
translation: नित्य ही मंगल, आनंद और उत्सव होते हैं, इस तरह आनंद में दिन बीतते जाते हैं। अयोध्या आनंद से भरकर उमड़ पड़ी, आनंद की अधिकता अधिक-अधिक बढ़ती ही जा रही है ॥
english_translation: Auspiciousness, delight, and festivity pass every day in this way. Ayodhya swells with joy, and its joy keeps growing and growing.
essence: Joy multiplies until the whole city overflows.
simple_meaning: Ayodhya is overflowing with joy, and each day brings more celebration and delight.
insight: It shifts attention from a single happy event to the way joy can saturate an entire atmosphere.
modern_relevance: A house after good news feels different: people move lighter, speak softer, and keep smiling at nothing in particular. Happiness spreads through shared space before anyone names it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुदिन सोधि कल कंकन छोरे। मंगल मोद बिनोद न थोरे॥ नित नव सुखु सुर देखि सिहाहीं। अवध जन्म जाचहिं बिधि पाहीं ॥
translation: अच्छा दिन (शुभ मुहूर्त) शोधकर सुंदर कंकण खोले गए। मंगल, आनंद और विनोद कुछ कम नहीं हुए (अर्थात बहुत हुए)। इस प्रकार नित्य नए सुख को देखकर देवता सिहाते हैं और अयोध्या में जन्म पाने के लिए ब्रह्माजी से याचना करते हैं ॥
english_translation: After choosing an auspicious day, the ceremonial bracelets were removed. Joy, delight, and festivity did not lessen. Seeing the ever-new happiness, the radiant beings long to take birth in Ayodhya and beg Brahma for that fate.
essence: Ram's arrival makes even the radiant beings long for Ayodhya.
simple_meaning: The auspicious birth rituals begin, and the joy in Ayodhya keeps growing. Even the radiant beings envy that happiness and long to be born there.
insight: It frames Ram's birth as a joy so complete that it draws longing even from the radiant beings.
modern_relevance: A home fills with laughter before a newborn arrives. The room feels larger than itself, and everyone present knows they are standing inside a blessing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिस्वामित्रु चलन नित चहहीं। राम सप्रेम बिनय बस रहहीं॥ दिन दिन सयगुन भूपति भाऊ। देखि सराह महामुनिराऊ ॥
translation: विश्वामित्रजी नित्य ही चलना (अपने आश्रम जाना) चाहते हैं, पर रामचन्द्रजी के स्नेह और विनयवश रह जाते हैं। दिनोंदिन राजा का सौ गुना भाव (प्रेम) देखकर महामुनिराज विश्वामित्रजी उनकी सराहना करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Vishvamitra kept wanting to leave, but Ram's affection and humility kept him there. Day by day, the great sage praised the king more and more for his hundredfold love.
essence: Affection and humility can keep a blessing from leaving.
simple_meaning: Vishvamitra keeps trying to depart, but Ram's loving humility makes him stay. Watching the king's love grow stronger each day, the great sage keeps praising him.
insight: It shifts attention from formal duty to the living force of affectionate respect.
modern_relevance: A mentor packs up after the work is done, but the family keeps insisting he stay for dinner. What holds him there is not duty, but the warmth of being genuinely valued.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मागत बिदा राउ अनुरागे। सुतन्ह समेत ठाढ़ भे आगे॥ नाथ सकल संपदा तुम्हारी। मैं सेवकु समेत सुत नारी ॥
translation: अंत में जब विश्वामित्रजी ने विदा माँगी, तब राजा प्रेममग्न हो गए और पुत्रों सहित आगे खड़े हो गए। (वे बोले-) हे नाथ! यह सारी सम्पदा आपकी है। मैं तो स्त्री-पुत्रों सहित आपका सेवक हूँ ॥
english_translation: When Vishvamitra asked to leave, King Dasharath stood forward in love with his sons. He said, “O lord, all this wealth is yours. I am your servant, with my sons and wife.”
essence: Love turns possession into service.
simple_meaning: Dasharath responds to Vishvamitra with loving humility. He offers his wealth, family, and himself in service.
insight: It shifts the mind from ownership to offering, turning possession into service.
modern_relevance: A respected guest is about to leave after helping your family, and you find yourself offering more than thanks. You offer food, time, help, and your full respect without calculating what it costs.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करब सदा लरिकन्ह पर छोहू। दरसनु देत रहब मुनि मोहू॥ अस कहि राउ सहित सुत रानी। परेउ चरन मुख आव न बानी ॥
translation: हे मुनि! लड़कों पर सदा स्नेह करते रहिएगा और मुझे भी दर्शन देते रहिएगा। ऐसा कहकर पुत्रों और रानियों सहित राजा दशरथजी विश्वामित्रजी के चरणों पर गिर पड़े, (प्रेमविह्वल हो जाने के कारण) उनके मुँह से बात नहीं निकलती ॥
english_translation: “Always show affection to the boys and keep giving me your darshan, O sage.” Saying this, King Dasharath fell at the sage's feet with his sons and queens, too moved to speak.
essence: Devotion can make speech unnecessary.
simple_meaning: Dasharath, overwhelmed with love, asks Vishwamitra to keep blessing his sons and to keep visiting him. Then he falls at the sage's feet, unable to speak.
insight: It shifts attention from speaking well to expressing love directly, even when language fails.
modern_relevance: You try to thank someone who changed your life, but the words vanish. Your chest tightens, your eyes fill, and all you can do is bow your head.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: दीन्हि असीस बिप्र बहु भाँति। चले न प्रीति रीति कहि जाती॥ रामु सप्रेम संग सब भाई। आयसु पाइ फिरे पहुँचाई ॥
translation: ब्राह्मण विश्वमित्रजी ने बहुत प्रकार से आशीर्वाद दिए और वे चल पड़े। प्रीति की रीति कही नहीं जीती। सब भाइयों को साथ लेकर श्री रामजी प्रेम के साथ उन्हें पहुँचाकर और आज्ञा पाकर लौटे ॥
english_translation: The Brahmin gave many blessings and departed, but affection could not be expressed in the proper way. Ram went with loving care, took leave, and returned after escorting him with all his brothers.
essence: Love is proven by how you part, not by how you greet.
simple_meaning: विश्वामित्रजी ने आशीर्वाद देकर विदा ली। राम अपने भाइयों के साथ प्रेम से उन्हें छोड़ने गए और अनुमति लेकर लौट आए।
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to care: real courtesy follows someone all the way out.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम रूपु भूपति भगति ब्याहु उछाहु अनंदु। जात सराहत मनहिं मन मुदित गाधिकुलचंदु ॥
translation: गाधिकुल के चन्द्रमा विश्वामित्रजी बड़े हर्ष के साथ श्री रामचन्द्रजी के रूप, राजा दशरथजी की भक्ति, (चारों भाइयों के) विवाह और (सबके) उत्साह और आनंद को मन ही मन सराहते जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: The sage from the Gadhi line kept admiring Ram's beauty, King Dasharath's devotion, the wedding, and everyone's joy as he went along.
essence: True joy keeps itself alive by remembering what is beautiful.
simple_meaning: Worldly and spiritual joy meet here: Vishwamitra walks on, quietly admiring Ram's beauty, Dasharath's devotion, and the wedding festivities.
insight: It shifts attention from outer ceremony to the quiet joy that devotion and harmony create.
modern_relevance: You leave a family gathering and keep replaying one small moment of grace — a parent’s pride, a child’s smile, a room suddenly softened by love.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बामदेव रघुकुल गुर ग्यानी। बहुरि गाधिसुत कथा बखानी॥ सुनि मुनि सुजसु मनहिं मन राऊ। बरनत आपन पुन्य प्रभाऊ ॥
translation: वामदेवजी और रघुकुल के गुरु ज्ञानी वशिष्ठजी ने फिर विश्वामित्रजी की कथा बखानकर कही। मुनि का सुंदर यश सुनकर राजा मन ही मन अपने पुण्यों के प्रभाव का बखान करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Vamadeva and Vashistha, the wise teachers of the Raghu line, again recounted the story of Vishvamitra. Hearing the sage's fame, the king quietly began praising his own past merit.
essence: Sacred praise can still awaken the king's hidden pride.
simple_meaning: The sages retell Vishvamitra's story, and King Dasharath privately feels proud of the merit that brought this blessing to him.
insight: It reveals how admiration can turn inward into self-congratulation, even when the heart is meant to be humble.
modern_relevance: At a family gathering, everyone praises the guest of honour, and you quietly think, 'I must have done something right.' The moment is grateful, but the ego slips in unnoticed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरे लोग रजायसु भयऊ। सुतन्ह समेत नृपति गृहँ गयऊ॥ जहँ तहँ राम ब्याहु सबु गावा। सुजसु पुनीत लोक तिहुँ छावा ॥
translation: आज्ञा हुई तब सब लोग (अपने-अपने घरों को) लौटे। राजा दशरथजी भी पुत्रों सहित महल में गए। जहाँ-तहाँ सब श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विवाह की गाथाएँ गा रहे हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी का पवित्र सुयश तीनों लोकों में छा गया ॥
english_translation: Then everyone received permission and returned home. King Dasharath went to the palace with his sons. Everywhere people sang of Ram's wedding, and Ram's pure fame spread through the three worlds.
essence: Ram's wedding leaves no one unchanged; even the air carries its joy.
simple_meaning: The wedding is over, and everyone goes home. Ram's marriage becomes the talk of the land, and his holy fame spreads everywhere.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the way joy travels through a community.
modern_relevance: After a family wedding, relatives are still replaying the best moments in group chats, voice notes, and dinner tables. Some events don't end when the ceremony ends; they keep spreading joy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आए ब्याहि रामु घर जब तें। बसइ अनंद अवध सब तब तें॥ प्रभु बिबाहँ जस भयउ उछाहू। सकहिं न बरनि गिरा अहिनाहू ॥
translation: जब से श्री रामचन्द्रजी विवाह करके घर आए, तब से सब प्रकार का आनंद अयोध्या में आकर बसने लगा। प्रभु के विवाह में आनंद-उत्साह हुआ, उसे सरस्वती और सर्पों के राजा शेषजी भी नहीं कह सकते ॥
english_translation: From the moment Ram came home after the wedding, all joy came to dwell in Ayodhya. The delight and excitement of the Lord's marriage cannot be described even by Saraswati or Shesha.
essence: Ram's presence turns a city into joy.
simple_meaning: Ram's return home after marriage fills Ayodhya with joy. The celebration is so great that even divine speech cannot fully describe it.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the transforming presence that makes a whole place feel alive.
modern_relevance: The house feels different the moment someone you love walks back in after a long absence. The tension drops, voices soften, and the whole room seems to breathe again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कबिकुल जीवनु पावन जानी। राम सीय जसु मंगल खानी॥ तेहि ते मैं कछु कहा बखानी। करन पुनीत हेतु निज बानी ॥
translation: श्री सीतारामजी के यश को कविकुल के जीवन को पवित्र करने वाला और मंगलों की खान जानकर, इससे मैंने अपनी वाणी को पवित्र करने के लिए कुछ (थोड़ा सा) बखानकर कहा है ॥
english_translation: Knowing the glory of Ram and Sita as the life of poets and a source of blessings, I have spoken a little to purify my own speech.
essence: Praise of Ram and Sita purifies the one who speaks it.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he speaks about Ram and Sita to make his own speech pure, because their glory brings blessings and ennobles poets.
insight: It shifts expression from self-display to self-purification.
modern_relevance: You open a notebook after a messy day and write about the one person or moment that still feels clean. The act of speaking about what is noble steadies your own mind.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: निज गिरा पावनि करन कारन राम जसु तुलसीं कह्यो। रघुबीर चरित अपार बारिधि पारु कबि कौनें लह्यो॥ उपबीत ब्याह उछाह मंगल सुनि जे सादर गावहीं। बैदेहि राम प्रसाद ते जन सर्बदा सुखु पावहीं॥
translation: अपनी वाणी को पवित्र करने के लिए तुलसी ने राम का यश कहा है। (नहीं तो) श्री रघुनाथजी का चरित्र अपार समुद्र है, किस कवि ने उसका पार पाया है? जो लोग यज्ञोपवीत और विवाह के मंगलमय उत्सव का वर्णन आदर के साथ सुनकर गावेंगे, वे लोग श्री जानकीजी और श्री रामजी की कृपा से सदा सुख पावेंगे।
english_translation: Tulsidas has spoken Ram's glory to purify his own speech. Raghubir's life is an endless ocean; which poet has ever crossed its far shore? Those who listen with reverence and sing the auspicious celebration of the sacred thread and the wedding will always receive happiness by the grace of Sita and Ram.
essence: Ram's glory is too vast to finish, yet singing it purifies the singer.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he sings Ram's glory to purify his own speech, because Ram's life is too vast for any poet to fully describe. Anyone who reverently sings of Ram and Sita's wedding receives lasting happiness.
insight: It shifts expression from cleverness to worship, and from description to blessing.
modern_relevance: You open a notebook before writing about someone you love and realize no sentence will be enough. Still, the act of speaking with reverence changes you first.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सिय रघुबीर बिबाहु जे सप्रेम गावहिं सुनहिं। तिन्ह कहुँ सदा उछाहु मंगलायतन राम जसु ॥
translation: श्री सीताजी और श्री रघुनाथजी के विवाह प्रसंग को जो लोग प्रेमपूर्वक गाएँ-सुनेंगे, उनके लिए सदा उत्साह (आनंद) ही उत्साह है, क्योंकि श्री रामचन्द्रजी का यश मंगल का धाम है ॥
english_translation: Those who lovingly sing and hear the wedding of Sita and Raghubir will always know joy upon joy, for Ram’s glory is the home of auspiciousness.
essence: Love-filled hearing of Ram’s story turns life into celebration.
simple_meaning: People who lovingly sing or hear Ram and Sita’s wedding story will always feel joy, because Ram’s fame itself is a source of blessing.
insight: It teaches you to treat sacred stories as living nourishment, not information.
modern_relevance: You put on a song that reminds you of someone you love, and the whole room softens. Some stories do that too — they don’t just entertain, they change the atmosphere.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: यस्यांके च विभाति भूधरसुता देवापगा मस्तके भाले बालविधुर्गले च गरलं यस्योरसि व्यालराट्। सोऽयं भूतिविभूषणः सुरवरः सर्वाधिपः सर्वदा शर्वः सर्वगतः शिवः शशिनिभः श्री शंकरः पातु माम् ॥
translation: जिनकी गोद में हिमाचलसुता पार्वतीजी, मस्तक पर गंगाजी, ललाट पर द्वितीया का चन्द्रमा, कंठ में हलाहल विष और वक्षःस्थल पर सर्पराज शेषजी सुशोभित हैं, वे भस्म से विभूषित, देवताओं में श्रेष्ठ, सर्वेश्वर, संहारकर्ता (या भक्तों के पापनाशक), सर्वव्यापक, कल्याण रूप, चन्द्रमा के समान शुभ्रवर्ण श्री शंकरजी सदा मेरी रक्षा करें ॥
english_translation: May Shri Shankar, adorned with ash, the best among the radiant beings, lord of all, ever-present, all-pervading, auspicious, moon-like, protect me forever. On his lap shines Parvati, on his head the Ganga, on his forehead the crescent moon, around his neck the poison, and on his chest the king of serpents.
essence: Shiva’s vast presence is invoked as shelter before the sorrow begins.
simple_meaning: A prayer to Shiva describes his cosmic form and asks for his protection.
insight: It shifts attention from personal anxiety to a larger, stabilizing presence.
modern_relevance: Before a hard conversation, you pause and steady yourself. A few words of reverence can turn fear into composure before the day begins.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: प्रसन्नतां या न गताभिषेकतस्तथा न मम्ले वनवासदुःखतः। मुखाम्बुजश्री रघुनन्दनस्य मे सदास्तु सा मंजुलमंगलप्रदा ॥
translation: रघुकुल को आनंद देने वाले श्री रामचन्द्रजी के मुखारविंद की जो शोभा राज्याभिषेक से (राज्याभिषेक की बात सुनकर) न तो प्रसन्नता को प्राप्त हुई और न वनवास के दुःख से मलिन ही हुई, वह (मुखकमल की छबि) मेरे लिए सदा सुंदर मंगलों की देने वाली हो ॥
english_translation: May the beauty of Ram's lotus face, which did not swell with joy at coronation nor fade in the sorrow of exile, always bring me auspiciousness.
essence: Joy and exile cannot disturb the one who is inwardly whole.
simple_meaning: Ram's face remained beautiful and unchanged whether he was about to be crowned king or sent into exile. Tulsidas asks that this sight always bless him.
insight: It shifts attention from external outcomes to inner steadiness under changing circumstances.
modern_relevance: You get the promotion email, then the project is cancelled two days later. Your mood swings with both. This verse points to a steadier way to live: let success and setback pass without changing your face.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: नीलाम्बुजश्यामलकोमलांग सीतासमारोपितवामभागम् । पाणौ महासायकचारुचापं नमामि रामं रघुवंशनाथम् ॥
translation: नीले कमल के समान श्याम और कोमल जिनके अंग हैं, श्री सीताजी जिनके वाम भाग में विराजमान हैं और जिनके हाथों में (क्रमशः) अमोघ बाण और सुंदर धनुष है, उन रघुवंश के स्वामी श्री रामचन्द्रजी को मैं नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I bow to Rama, lord of the Raghu line, whose body is dark as a blue lotus, tender-limbed, with Sita on his left side, and with a mighty arrow and beautiful bow in his hands.
essence: Beauty, tenderness, and strength meet in Rama.
simple_meaning: Rama is praised as beautiful, tender, and royal, with Sita beside him and bow and arrow in his hands.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary description to worshipful seeing.
modern_relevance: Before a speech, a meeting, or a hard conversation, you pause and remember who you are answering to: not ego, but what is worthy. That changes your posture.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: श्री गुरु चरन सरोज रज निज मनु मुकुरु सुधारि। बरनउँ रघुबर बिमल जसु जो दायकु फल चारि॥
translation: श्री गुरुजी के चरण कमलों की रज से अपने मन रूपी दर्पण को साफ करके मैं श्री रघुनाथजी के उस निर्मल यश का वर्णन करता हूँ, जो चारों फलों को (धर्म, अर्थ, काम, मोक्ष को) देने वाला है।
english_translation: By cleansing my mind-mirror with the dust of my guru's lotus feet, I sing the spotless glory of Raghubar, who grants the four aims of life.
essence: Purify the mind first; only then does Ram's glory become visible.
simple_meaning: The poet says he first purifies his own mind by honoring the guru, and only then can he speak about Ram's pure glory, which gives the four goals of human life.
insight: It shifts attention from raw information to the condition of the mind receiving it.
modern_relevance: You open a book after a chaotic morning, and nothing lands until you sit still for a minute. The same words feel different once the mind stops smudging everything.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जब तें रामु ब्याहि घर आए। नित नव मंगल मोद बधाए॥ भुवन चारिदस भूधर भारी। सुकृत मेघ बरषहिं सुख बारी ॥
translation: जब से श्री रामचन्द्रजी विवाह करके घर आए, तब से (अयोध्या में) नित्य नए मंगल हो रहे हैं और आनंद के बधावे बज रहे हैं। चौदहों लोक रूपी बड़े भारी पर्वतों पर पुण्य रूपी मेघ सुख रूपी जल बरसा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Since Ram came home after marriage, every day in Ayodhya brought new auspiciousness and joy. Across the fourteen worlds, heavy mountains of merit rained down waters of happiness.
essence: Ram's arrival turns the whole world festive.
simple_meaning: Ram's return after marriage fills Ayodhya with constant celebration, as if merit itself is raining happiness across the world.
insight: It shifts attention from private happiness to the way one noble event can lift an entire community.
modern_relevance: A house feels different the day someone beloved returns. The air is lighter, the routines soften, and even ordinary tasks seem blessed with meaning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रिधि सिधि संपति नदीं सुहाई। उमगि अवध अंबुधि कहुँ आई॥ मनिगन पुर नर नारि सुजाती। सुचि अमोल सुंदर सब भाँती ॥
translation: ऋद्धि-सिद्धि और सम्पत्ति रूपी सुहावनी नदियाँ उमड़-उमड़कर अयोध्या रूपी समुद्र में आ मिलीं। नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष अच्छी जाति के मणियों के समूह हैं, जो सब प्रकार से पवित्र, अमूल्य और सुंदर हैं ॥
english_translation: Rivers of prosperity and accomplishment flowed into Ayodhya like lovely streams. The men and women of the city were like fine jewels—pure, priceless, and beautiful in every way.
essence: Ram's presence turns a city into a field of abundance and purity.
simple_meaning: Ayodhya is overflowing with prosperity, and its people are pure, precious, and beautiful.
insight: It shifts attention from material abundance to the moral beauty of a whole community.
modern_relevance: A neighborhood feels different after one family brings warmth, generosity, and steadiness to it. The change is not only in money or comfort, but in the quality of everyone who lives there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहि न जाइ कछु नगर बिभूती। जनु एतनिअ बिरंचि करतूती॥ सब बिधि सब पुर लोग सुखारी। रामचंद मुख चंदु निहारी ॥
translation: नगर का ऐश्वर्य कुछ कहा नहीं जाता। ऐसा जान पड़ता है, मानो ब्रह्माजी की कारीगरी बस इतनी ही है। सब नगर निवासी श्री रामचन्द्रजी के मुखचन्द्र को देखकर सब प्रकार से सुखी हैं ॥
english_translation: The city's splendor cannot be described. It seems as if Brahma's craftsmanship has reached its limit. Everyone in the city is happy in every way, gazing upon Ramchandra's moonlike face.
essence: Ram's presence turns a city into joy.
simple_meaning: Ayodhya's beauty is beyond description, and everyone there is joyful because they keep looking at Ram's radiant face.
insight: It shifts attention from external splendor to the presence that makes a place feel blessed.
modern_relevance: A home after a wedding feels different when everyone keeps stealing glances at the person who returned with love intact. The room itself is full, but the real brightness is in the faces around it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुदित मातु सब सखीं सहेली। फलित बिलोकि मनोरथ बेली॥ राम रूपु गुन सीलु सुभाऊ। प्रमुदित होइ देखि सुनि राऊ ॥
translation: सब माताएँ और सखी-सहेलियाँ अपनी मनोरथ रूपी बेल को फली हुई देखकर आनंदित हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के रूप, गुण, शील और स्वभाव को देख-सुनकर राजा दशरथजी बहुत ही आनंदित होते हैं ॥
english_translation: All the mothers and their female companions are delighted, seeing the vine of their wish bear fruit. Seeing and hearing Ram's form, virtues, conduct, and nature, King Dasharath is filled with joy.
essence: A noble life makes everyone else's hope bloom.
simple_meaning: The women of Ayodhya are overjoyed because their wish is coming true. Dasharath is equally delighted as he sees Ram's noble qualities.
insight: It shifts attention from private wishing to the visible ripening of a worthy life.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you've raised finally step into the role they were meant for. Pride, relief, and hope all arrive at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब कें उर अभिलाषु अस कहहिं मनाइ महेसु। आप अछत जुबराज पद रामहि देउ नरेसु ॥
translation: सबके हृदय में ऐसी अभिलाषा है और सब महादेवजी को मनाकर (प्रार्थना करके) कहते हैं कि राजा अपने जीते जी श्री रामचन्द्रजी को युवराज पद दे दें ॥
english_translation: Everyone in their hearts wished that the king, after consulting Mahesh, would give the crown prince's seat to Ram while he was still alive.
essence: Ram's worth is so clear that even the city hopes for it.
simple_meaning: Everyone hopes the king will give Ram the crown prince's seat while he is still alive.
insight: It shifts attention from private ambition to communal recognition of worth.
modern_relevance: A room full of people senses who is ready for the promotion before the email is sent. The decision is still pending, but the recognition has already spread.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक समय सब सहित समाजा। राजसभाँ रघुराजु बिराजा॥ सकल सुकृत मूरति नरनाहू। राम सुजसु सुनि अतिहि उछाहू ॥
translation: एक समय रघुकुल के राजा दशरथजी अपने सारे समाज सहित राजसभा में विराजमान थे। महाराज समस्त पुण्यों की मूर्ति हैं, उन्हें श्री रामचन्द्रजी का सुंदर यश सुनकर अत्यन्त आनंद हो रहा है ॥
english_translation: At one time, King Dasharath sat in the royal assembly with all his attendants. The lord of the people, a treasury of all good deeds, felt great delight hearing Ram's beautiful fame.
essence: Love rejoices when the beloved is praised.
simple_meaning: King Dasharath sits in his court with his attendants and feels deep joy hearing Ram's praise.
insight: It shifts attention from status to love: a king's delight comes from Ram's reputation, not his own power.
modern_relevance: You hear your child praised at a school event, and your chest loosens before you even speak. Some joy arrives just from seeing someone you love reflected well.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नृप सब रहहिं कृपा अभिलाषें। लोकप करहिं प्रीति रुख राखें॥ वन तीनि काल जग माहीं। भूरिभाग दसरथ सम नाहीं ॥
translation: सब राजा उनकी कृपा चाहते हैं और लोकपालगण उनके रुख को रखते हुए (अनुकूल होकर) प्रीति करते हैं। (पृथ्वी, आकाश, पाताल) तीनों भुवनों में और (भूत, भविष्य, वर्तमान) तीनों कालों में दशरथजी के समान बड़भागी (और) कोई नहीं है ॥
english_translation: All kings seek his grace, and the guardians of the worlds stay aligned with his will. In the three worlds and the three times, no one is more fortunate than Dasharath.
essence: Even the most fortunate ruler still stands inside time.
simple_meaning: Dasharath is so fortunate that every king wants his favor, and even the guardians of the worlds stay in harmony with him.
insight: It frames success as visible alignment from others, not just private achievement.
modern_relevance: A person walks into a room and every senior voice bends toward them. The praise feels absolute — until the story reminds you that status can vanish in a single breath.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंगलमूल रामु सुत जासू। जो कछु कहिअ थोर सबु तासू॥ रायँ सुभायँ मुकुरु कर लीन्हा। बदनु बिलोकि मुकुटु सम कीन्हा ॥
translation: मंगलों के मूल श्री रामचन्द्रजी जिनके पुत्र हैं, उनके लिए जो कुछ कहा जाए सब थोड़ा है। राजा ने स्वाभाविक ही हाथ में दर्पण ले लिया और उसमें अपना मुँह देखकर मुकुट को सीधा किया ॥
english_translation: Ram, the source of all auspiciousness, is his son; whatever can be said about him is only a little. The king naturally took a mirror in hand, looked at his face, and straightened his crown.
essence: Even a king becomes small before Ram.
simple_meaning: Ram is beyond full praise, and King Dasharath adjusts his crown after seeing his reflection.
insight: It shifts attention from self-display to honouring the higher presence in one's life.
modern_relevance: You catch your reflection before a big family gathering and fix your collar, then remember the child who makes your name matter more than your title. Pride softens into reverence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: श्रवन समीप भए सित केसा। मनहुँ जरठपनु अस उपदेसा॥ नृप जुबराजु राम कहुँ देहू। जीवन जनम लाहु किन लेहू ॥
translation: (देखा कि) कानों के पास बाल सफेद हो गए हैं, मानो बुढ़ापा ऐसा उपदेश कर रहा है कि हे राजन् ! श्री रामचन्द्रजी को युवराज पद देकर अपने जीवन और जन्म का लाभ क्यों नहीं लेते ॥
english_translation: His hair near the ears had turned white, as if old age itself were advising him: "O king, give Rama the crown prince's seat. Why not take the true benefit of your life and birth?"
essence: Time itself urges the right decision before it slips away.
simple_meaning: Old age seems to advise Dasharath to give Rama the crown prince's seat and make his life truly worthwhile.
insight: It shifts attention from delay to decisive obligation: do the rightful act while the moment is still open.
modern_relevance: You catch your reflection in the bathroom mirror and notice the first silver hairs. The question changes: will you keep postponing the hard, right decision, or finally make the call that matters?
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: यह बिचारु उर आनि नृप सुदिनु सुअवसरु पाइ। प्रेम पुलकि तन मुदित मन गुरहि सुनायउ जाइ ॥
translation: हृदय में यह विचार लाकर (युवराज पद देने का निश्चय कर) राजा दशरथजी ने शुभ दिन और सुंदर समय पाकर, प्रेम से पुलकित शरीर हो आनंदमग्न मन से उसे गुरु वशिष्ठजी को जा सुनाया ॥
english_translation: Having brought this thought into his heart, the king found an auspicious day and fitting moment. His body thrilled with love, his mind filled with joy, and he went to tell Guru Vashishtha.
essence: A loving decision ripens before it is spoken.
simple_meaning: King Dasharath held the decision in his heart, waited for the right moment, and then joyfully told Guru Vashishtha.
insight: It teaches you to honor important decisions by timing and sharing them well, not blurting them out in haste.
modern_relevance: You finally know the hard thing you need to say. Before sending the message, you wait for the right time, steady yourself, and speak with care.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहइ भुआलु सुनिअ मुनिनायक। भए राम सब बिधि सब लायक॥ सेवक सचिव सकल पुरबासी। जे हमार अरि मित्र उदासी ॥
translation: राजा ने कहा- हे मुनिराज! (कृपया यह निवेदन) सुनिए। श्री रामचन्द्रजी अब सब प्रकार से सब योग्य हो गए हैं। सेवक, मंत्री, सब नगर निवासी और जो हमारे शत्रु, मित्र या उदासीन हैं- ॥
english_translation: The king said, "Listen, sage leader. Ram is now fit in every way, for every role. Servants, ministers, all the people of the city, and even those who are our enemies, friends, or indifferent."
essence: Ram is ready because his whole life has already trained him for the throne.
simple_meaning: Dasharath tells the sage that Ram is fully ready for kingship, and that everyone in the kingdom sees it too.
insight: It shifts attention from ambition to earned readiness, showing that true calling is confirmed by character and community.
modern_relevance: You watch someone step into a role after years of quiet responsibility — and everyone who has worked with them knows it before the title arrives.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: सबहि रामु प्रिय जेहि बिधि मोही। प्रभु असीस जनु तनु धरि सोही॥ बिप्र सहित परिवार गोसाईं। करहिं छोहु सब रौरिहि नाईं ॥
translation: सभी को श्री रामचन्द्र वैसे ही प्रिय हैं, जैसे वे मुझको हैं। (उनके रूप में) आपका आशीर्वाद ही मानो शरीर धारण करके शोभित हो रहा है। हे स्वामी! सारे ब्राह्मण, परिवार सहित आपके ही समान उन पर स्नेह करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram is dear to everyone just as he is dear to me. Your blessing seems to have taken form in him. O lord, all the Brahmins and the whole family love him as you do.
essence: True worth wins the same love from everyone.
simple_meaning: Dasharath says Ram is loved by everyone, just as he loves Ram. He sees Ram as a living blessing, and says even the Brahmins and family feel affection for him.
insight: It frames Ram’s worth as publicly visible, not merely a father’s bias.
modern_relevance: You introduce someone at a family gathering and every room softens at once. Their kindness is obvious before anyone explains it.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: जे गुर चरन रेनु सिर धरहीं। ते जनु सकल बिभव बस करहीं॥ मोहि सम यहु अनुभयउ न दूजें। सबु पायउँ रज पावनि पूजें ॥
translation: जो लोग गुरु के चरणों की रज को मस्तक पर धारण करते हैं, वे मानो समस्त ऐश्वर्य को अपने वश में कर लेते हैं। इसका अनुभव मेरे समान दूसरे किसी ने नहीं किया। आपकी पवित्र चरण रज की पूजा करके मैंने सब कुछ पा लिया ॥
english_translation: Those who place the dust of the teacher's feet on their heads seem to bring all prosperity under their control. No one has had this experience like I have. By worshipping your sacred foot-dust, I have attained everything.
essence: Humility before the teacher opens what pride cannot reach.
simple_meaning: Honouring the teacher with complete humility brings real abundance. The speaker says that worshipping the teacher's sacred foot-dust gave him everything he needed.
insight: It shifts reverence from ceremony to a practical source of transformation.
modern_relevance: You sit across from a mentor who has seen your excuses before. You stop performing, listen properly, and something in you opens. Respect becomes the doorway, not the price.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अब अभिलाषु एकु मन मोरें। पूजिहि नाथ अनुग्रह तोरें॥ मुनि प्रसन्न लखि सहज सनेहू। कहेउ नरेस रजायसु देहू ॥
translation: अब मेरे मन में एक ही अभिलाषा है। हे नाथ! वह भी आप ही के अनुग्रह से पूरी होगी। राजा का सहज प्रेम देखकर मुनि ने प्रसन्न होकर कहा- नरेश! आज्ञा दीजिए (कहिए, क्या अभिलाषा है?) ॥
english_translation: Now my mind has only one desire. O Lord, it will be fulfilled by your grace. Seeing the king's natural affection, the sage grew pleased and said, 'O king, speak your wish.'
essence: One true wish becomes enough when it rests on grace.
simple_meaning: The king has one sincere wish, and he trusts it will be fulfilled only through grace. The sage, seeing this natural affection, invites him to speak freely.
insight: It shifts the mind from grasping for outcomes to offering one honest request with trust.
modern_relevance: You finally sit across from someone who can help, but you stop performing and speak plainly. The pressure drops the moment you trust that sincerity matters more than control.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राजन राउर नामु जसु सब अभिमत दातार। फल अनुगामी महिप मनि मन अभिलाषु तुम्हार ॥
translation: हे राजन! आपका नाम और यश ही सम्पूर्ण मनचाही वस्तुओं को देने वाला है। हे राजाओं के मुकुटमणि! आपके मन की अभिलाषा फल का अनुगमन करती है (अर्थात आपके इच्छा करने के पहले ही फल उत्पन्न हो जाता है) ॥
english_translation: O king, your very name and fame grant everything desired. Jewel among rulers, your wish is followed by its fruit.
essence: True greatness makes good things arrive before they are asked for.
simple_meaning: The king’s name is praised as one that fulfills every wish, and his desire is said to bear fruit even before it is spoken.
insight: It shifts attention from power as control to power as blessing others effortlessly.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence changes the room before they speak. Their calm, integrity, and goodwill make everything feel possible, as if good things gather around them naturally.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब बिधि गुरु प्रसन्न जियँ जानी। बोलेउ राउ रहँसि मृदु बानी॥ नाथ रामु करिअहिं जुबराजू। कहिअ कृपा करि करिअ समाजू ॥
translation: अपने जी में गुरुजी को सब प्रकार से प्रसन्न जानकर, हर्षित होकर राजा कोमल वाणी से बोले- हे नाथ! श्री रामचन्द्र को युवराज कीजिए। कृपा करके कहिए (आज्ञा दीजिए) तो तैयारी की जाए ॥
english_translation: Having seen the teacher fully pleased in his heart, the king spoke with a smile in gentle words: “O lord, let Ram be crowned prince. Kindly give the order, and preparations will be made.”
essence: The king asks for Ram's rightful place with humility, not force.
simple_meaning: Dasharath, seeing his teacher pleased, gently asks that Ram be made crown prince and the preparations begin.
insight: It teaches you to ask directly, but with humility and good timing.
modern_relevance: You finally get a chance to ask for what matters after sensing the other person is open. The right timing makes even a big request feel simple and respectful.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: मोहि अछत यहु होइ उछाहू। लहहिं लोग सब लोचन लाहू॥ प्रभु प्रसाद सिव सबइ निबाहीं। यह लालसा एक मन माहीं ॥
translation: मेरे जीते जी यह आनंद उत्सव हो जाए, (जिससे) सब लोग अपने नेत्रों का लाभ प्राप्त करें। प्रभु (आप) के प्रसाद से शिवजी ने सब कुछ निबाह दिया (सब इच्छाएँ पूर्ण कर दीं), केवल यही एक लालसा मन में रह गई है ॥
english_translation: May this celebration happen while I am still alive, so everyone can behold it with their own eyes. By the divine grace, Shiva has fulfilled everything; only this one longing remains in my mind.
essence: A fulfilled life can still ache for one last sight.
simple_meaning: Dasharath wants to live long enough to see Ram's joyful coronation. He says everything else has been fulfilled; only this one wish remains.
insight: It shifts attention from private satisfaction to witnessing a loved one's fulfillment.
modern_relevance: You keep one photo on your phone because it holds the moment you most want to see happen. Dasharath's heart is like that: everything else can wait, but not this.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: पुनि न सोच तनु रहउ कि जाऊ। जेहिं न होइ पाछें पछिताऊ॥ सुनि मुनि दसरथ बचन सुहाए। मंगल मोद मूल मन भाए ॥
translation: (इस लालसा के पूर्ण हो जाने पर) फिर सोच नहीं, शरीर रहे या चला जाए, जिससे मुझे पीछे पछतावा न हो। दशरथजी के मंगल और आनंद के मूल सुंदर वचन सुनकर मुनि मन में बहुत प्रसन्न हुए ॥
english_translation: Then I will have no more worry, whether this body remains or departs, so that I do not regret it later. Hearing King Dasharath's lovely words, rooted in auspiciousness and joy, the sage was delighted in his mind.
essence: Choose so completely that regret has nowhere to enter.
simple_meaning: Dasharath says he wants the blessing fulfilled so completely that he will have no regret, even if his body must go. The sage listening is filled with joy.
insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to clean commitment: act in a way that leaves no later remorse.
modern_relevance: You sign the form, send the message, and know there is no clean way back. What matters now is choosing so clearly that you can live with it tomorrow.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: सुनु नृप जासु बिमुख पछिताहीं। जासु भजन बिनु जरनि न जाहीं॥ भयउ तुम्हार तनय सोइ स्वामी। रामु पुनीत प्रेम अनुगामी ॥
translation: (वशिष्ठजी ने कहा-) हे राजन् ! सुनिए, जिनसे विमुख होकर लोग पछताते हैं और जिनके भजन बिना जी की जलन नहीं जाती, वही स्वामी (सर्वलोक महेश्वर) श्री रामजी आपके पुत्र हुए हैं, जो पवित्र प्रेम के अनुगामी हैं। (श्री रामजी पवित्र प्रेम के पीछे-पीछे चलने वाले हैं, इसी से तो प्रेमवश आपके पुत्र हुए हैं।) ॥
english_translation: Listen, king: people regret turning away from the one whose worship ends the burning in the heart. That same Lord has become your son, Ram, who follows pure love.
essence: Ram is the one whose nearness ends regret and inner burning.
simple_meaning: Turning away from Ram brings regret, and devotion to him ends the inner burning. Vashishtha says this same Ram has been born as Dasharath's son and follows pure love.
insight: It shifts attention from temporary relief to the one presence that truly ends restlessness.
modern_relevance: You finally meet the person who makes your mind quiet after months of chasing noise. The relief is not that they changed your life, but that your heart recognized its own home.
speaker: Vashishtha

verse_text: बेगि बिलंबु न करिअ नृप साजिअ सबुइ समाजु। सुदिन सुमंगलु तबहिं जब रामु होहिं जुबराजु ॥
translation: हे राजन् ! अब देर न कीजिए, शीघ्र सब सामान सजाइए। शुभ दिन और सुंदर मंगल तभी है, जब श्री रामचन्द्रजी युवराज हो जाएँ (अर्थात उनके अभिषेक के लिए सभी दिन शुभ और मंगलमय हैं) ॥
english_translation: O king, do not delay. Prepare everything at once. The day is truly auspicious only when Ram becomes crown prince.
essence: The right day is the one that places Ram first.
simple_meaning: Vasistha urges King Dasharath to stop delaying and arrange the coronation immediately. The real blessing of the day is Ram becoming crown prince.
insight: It shifts attention from procedural delay to immediate alignment with dharma.
modern_relevance: You finally have everyone's agreement, but the room still drags its feet. This verse cuts through the hesitation: stop polishing the plan and do the thing that matters.
speaker: Vasistha

verse_text: मुदित महीपति मंदिर आए। सेवक सचिव सुमंत्रु बोलाए॥ कहि जयजीव सीस तिन्ह नाए। भूप सुमंगल बचन सुनाए ॥
translation: राजा आनंदित होकर महल में आए और उन्होंने सेवकों को तथा मंत्री सुमंत्र को बुलवाया। उन लोगों ने 'जय-जीव' कहकर सिर नवाए। तब राजा ने सुंदर मंगलमय वचन (श्री रामजी को युवराज पद देने का प्रस्ताव) सुनाए ॥
english_translation: The king returned to the palace in joy, summoned his servants and the minister Sumantra, and they bowed their heads saying, 'Victory and long life.' Then the king spoke auspicious words.
essence: Joy gathers in the palace before the decisive words are spoken.
simple_meaning: King Dasharath returns happily to the palace, calls his attendants and Sumantra, and speaks in a joyful, formal way.
insight: It sets the scene for the announcement, showing how public joy can hide a coming fracture.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family room smiling, and everyone straightens up because they sense news is coming. The mood is warm, but the real change is still just about to be spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जौं पाँचहि मत लागै नीका। करहु हरषि हियँ रामहि टीका ॥
translation: (और कहा-) यदि पंचों को (आप सबको) यह मत अच्छा लगे, तो हृदय में हर्षित होकर आप लोग श्री रामचन्द्र का राजतिलक कीजिए ॥
english_translation: If the council approves, then gladly crown Ram in your hearts.
essence: A good act should be welcomed openly, not imposed in haste.
simple_meaning: If the ministers agree, then Ram should be crowned with joy.
insight: It models leadership that seeks consent before action, not ego before approval.
modern_relevance: You have the plan ready, but the room still needs to be brought with you. A leader speaks plainly, checks alignment, and then moves forward without forcing the moment.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: मंत्री मुदित सुनत प्रिय बानी। अभिमत बिरवँ परेउ जनु पानी॥ बिनती सचिव करहिं कर जोरी। जिअहु जगतपति बरिस करोरी ॥
translation: इस प्रिय वाणी को सुनते ही मंत्री ऐसे आनंदित हुए मानो उनके मनोरथ रूपी पौधे पर पानी पड़ गया हो। मंत्री हाथ जोड़कर विनती करते हैं कि हे जगत्पति! आप करोड़ों वर्ष जिएँ ॥
english_translation: The ministers were delighted to hear the beloved words, as if water had fallen on a wished-for plant. With folded hands, the ministers prayed: "May you live for millions of years, lord of the world."
essence: Delighted support rises when words match hidden hopes.
simple_meaning: The ministers are overjoyed by the king’s words and respectfully pray for his long life.
insight: It shows how shared joy can quickly transform a group from passive listeners into active supporters.
modern_relevance: A team hears the plan they had secretly hoped for, and the whole room changes at once. Relief makes people generous, respectful, and eager to support what was just announced.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जग मंगल भल काजु बिचारा। बेगिअ नाथ न लाइअ बारा॥ नृपहि मोदु सुनि सचिव सुभाषा। बढ़त बौंड़ जनु लही सुसाखा ॥
translation: आपने जगतभर का मंगल करने वाला भला काम सोचा है। हे नाथ! शीघ्रता कीजिए, देर न लगाइए। मंत्रियों की सुंदर वाणी सुनकर राजा को ऐसा आनंद हुआ मानो बढ़ती हुई बेल सुंदर डाली का सहारा पा गई हो ॥
english_translation: You have planned a deed that will bring auspiciousness to the whole world. Lord, do not delay. Hearing the ministers' gracious words, the king felt such joy, like a growing vine finding a lovely support.
essence: A right deed gains force when everyone helps it move quickly.
simple_meaning: The ministers praise the plan to crown Ram and urge the king to act quickly. The king is so pleased that his joy is compared to a vine finding a strong branch.
insight: It shifts attention from private hesitation to timely support for the right action.
modern_relevance: A team finally agrees on the right decision in a tense meeting, and relief floods the room. The hardest part is over: everyone can feel the work moving forward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहेउ भूप मुनिराज कर जोइ जोइ आयसु होइ। राम राज अभिषेक हित बेगि करहु सोइ सोइ ॥
translation: राजा ने कहा- श्री रामचन्द्र के राज्याभिषेक के लिए मुनिराज वशिष्ठजी की जो-जो आज्ञा हो, आप लोग वही सब तुरंत करें ॥
english_translation: The king said, "Whatever command the sage-king gives, do it all at once for Rama's coronation."
essence: True readiness obeys the right command without delay.
simple_meaning: Dasharath tells his ministers to carry out every order of Vashishtha quickly for Rama's coronation.
insight: It shifts attention from wishing for a good outcome to carrying out the needed steps without delay.
modern_relevance: Your team finally agrees on the plan, and the room fills with relief. The next step is not debate but clean execution.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: हरषि मुनीस कहेउ मृदु बानी। आनहु सकल सुतीरथ पानी॥ औषध मूल फूल फल पाना। कहे नाम गनि मंगल नाना ॥
translation: मुनिराज ने हर्षित होकर कोमल वाणी से कहा कि सम्पूर्ण श्रेष्ठ तीर्थों का जल ले आओ। फिर उन्होंने औषधि, मूल, फूल, फल और पत्र आदि अनेकों मांगलिक वस्तुओं के नाम गिनकर बताए ॥
english_translation: The sage spoke joyfully in a gentle voice: "Bring water from all sacred places. Gather medicines, roots, flowers, fruits, leaves, and many other auspicious items."
essence: Joy turns into exact preparation.
simple_meaning: Vashistha calmly gives practical instructions for the coronation ritual: bring sacred water and gather auspicious plants and offerings.
insight: It shifts attention from grand intention to the disciplined gathering that makes a holy event possible.
modern_relevance: Before a wedding, a memorial, or a major family ceremony, someone has to make the lists, gather the items, and keep the atmosphere steady. Reverence is often hidden inside those small exact tasks.
speaker: Vashistha

verse_text: चामर चरम बसन बहु भाँती। रोम पाट पट अगनित जाती॥ मनिगन मंगल बस्तु अनेका। जो जग जोगु भूप अभिषेका ॥
translation: चँवर, मृगचर्म, बहुत प्रकार के वस्त्र, असंख्यों जातियों के ऊनी और रेशमी कपड़े, (नाना प्रकार की) मणियाँ (रत्न) तथा और भी बहुत सी मंगल वस्तुएँ, जो जगत में राज्याभिषेक के योग्य होती हैं, (सबको मँगाने की उन्होंने आज्ञा दी) ॥
english_translation: Many kinds of fans, deer skins, many kinds of garments, countless kinds of wool and silk cloth, many jewels, and many auspicious items fit for a king's consecration in the world.
essence: Great occasions are honored through careful gathering, not haste.
simple_meaning: The preparations for Ram's coronation include many fine cloths, jewels, and auspicious items suitable for a royal consecration.
insight: It shifts attention from grand intention to exact preparation. Sacred or important work is completed through disciplined attention to detail.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall is being set before dawn: flowers, lights, fabrics, and utensils arrive in careful piles. The moment matters, so every detail is gathered with reverence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बेद बिदित कहि सकल बिधाना। कहेउ रचहु पुर बिबिध बिताना॥ सफल रसाल पूगफल केरा। रोपहु बीथिन्ह पुर चहुँ फेरा ॥
translation: मुनि ने वेदों में कहा हुआ सब विधान बताकर कहा- नगर में बहुत से मंडप (चँदोवे) सजाओ। फलों समेत आम, सुपारी और केले के वृक्ष नगर की गलियों में चारों ओर रोप दो ॥
english_translation: Having explained all the rites known in the Vedas, he said, "Set up many canopies throughout the city. Plant fruitful mango, areca, and banana trees along the streets on all four sides."
essence: A sacred event begins with careful order.
simple_meaning: The sage instructs the city to be decorated for the coming ceremony with canopies and rows of fruit trees along the streets.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony as spectacle to ceremony as disciplined preparation.
modern_relevance: You are setting up chairs before dawn, hanging lights, and placing flowers where people will walk in silence. The work is ordinary, but the care makes it feel holy.
speaker: Muni

verse_text: रचहु मंजु मनि चौकें चारू। कहहु बनावन बेगि बजारू॥ पूजहु गनपति गुर कुलदेवा। सब बिधि करहु भूमिसुर सेवा ॥
translation: सुंदर मणियों के मनोहर चौक पुरवाओ और बाजार को तुरंत सजाने के लिए कह दो। श्री गणेशजी, गुरु और कुलदेवता की पूजा करो और भूदेव ब्राह्मणों की सब प्रकार से सेवा करो ॥
english_translation: Have beautiful jewel-studded courtyards laid out and quickly prepare the market. Worship Ganesha, the teacher, and the family deities, and serve the learned brahmins in every way.
essence: A worthy welcome begins with reverence, service, and careful preparation.
simple_meaning: The city is being prepared for a great welcome. Beautiful decorations are put up, sacred worship is performed, and respected brahmins are served with care.
insight: It shifts attention from celebration alone to the discipline of preparing well and honoring what is sacred in the moment.
modern_relevance: Before a wedding, a housewarming, or a family reunion, someone is still sweeping the floor, arranging flowers, and making sure elders are welcomed first. Great joy is built through careful, respectful preparation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ध्वज पताक तोरन कलस सजहु तुरग रथ नाग। सिर धरि मुनिबर बचन सबु निज निज काजहिं लाग ॥
translation: ध्वजा, पताका, तोरण, कलश, घोड़े, रथ और हाथी सबको सजाओ! मुनि श्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी के वचनों को शिरोधार्य करके सब लोग अपने-अपने काम में लग गए ॥
english_translation: Decorate the banners, flags, arches, pots, horses, chariots, and elephants. Holding the sage's words on their heads, everyone set to their own tasks.
essence: Order appears when everyone takes up their own task.
simple_meaning: The city is being prepared for a great celebration. Everyone follows Vashistha's instructions and gets to work at once.
insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to coordinated action under wise direction.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall is half-finished, guests are arriving, and everyone suddenly knows their role. The whole scene works because people stop debating and start doing exactly what needs doing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जो मुनीस जेहि आयसु दीन्हा। सो तेहिं काजु प्रथम जनु कीन्हा॥ बिप्र साधु सुर पूजत राजा। करत राम हित मंगल काजा ॥
translation: मुनीश्वर ने जिसको जिस काम के लिए आज्ञा दी, उसने वह काम (इतनी शीघ्रता से कर डाला कि) मानो पहले से ही कर रखा था। राजा ब्राह्मण, साधु और देवताओं को पूज रहे हैं और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के लिए सब मंगल कार्य कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Whatever task the sage assigned to each person, each completed it as if it had already been done first. The king honored Brahmins, saints, and radiant beings, and carried out every auspicious act for Ram.
essence: Shared devotion makes many hands move as one.
simple_meaning: Everyone obeyed the sage's instructions at once. The king was busy honoring holy people and arranging auspicious rites for Ram.
insight: It shows how shared purpose turns many separate actions into one coordinated act.
modern_relevance: A wedding venue before sunrise: florists, cooks, relatives, and priests all move without confusion because one clear purpose holds them together. When everyone knows what matters, effort stops scattering.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनत राम अभिषेक सुहावा। बाज गहागह अवध बधावा॥ राम सीय तन सगुन जनाए। फरकहिं मंगल अंग सुहाए ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के राज्याभिषेक की सुहावनी खबर सुनते ही अवधभर में बड़ी धूम से बधावे बजने लगे। श्री रामचन्द्रजी और सीताजी के शरीर में भी शुभ शकुन सूचित हुए। उनके सुंदर मंगल अंग फड़कने लगे ॥
english_translation: As soon as the happy news of Ram's coronation was heard, Ayodhya rang with loud celebrations. Auspicious signs appeared in Ram and Sita's bodies, and their beautiful limbs trembled with joy.
essence: Joy in the city and joy in the body rise together.
simple_meaning: Ayodhya erupts in celebration at the news of Ram's coronation, and Ram and Sita themselves show joyful auspicious signs.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the visible signs of shared joy.
modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with the message you were waiting for, and before you even speak, your body changes—shoulders loosen, breath deepens, a smile comes. Some happiness arrives before language.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुलकि सप्रेम परसपर कहहीं। भरत आगमनु सूचक अहहीं॥ भए बहुत दिन अति अवसेरी। सगुन प्रतीति भेंट प्रिय केरी ॥
translation: पुलकित होकर वे दोनों प्रेम सहित एक-दूसरे से कहते हैं कि ये सब शकुन भरत के आने की सूचना देने वाले हैं। (उनको मामा के घर गए) बहुत दिन हो गए, बहुत ही अवसेर आ रही है (बार-बार उनसे मिलने की मन में आती है) शकुनों से प्रिय (भरत) के मिलने का विश्वास होता है ॥
english_translation: With joy and love, they tell one another that these omens point to Bharat's arrival. He has been away for many days, and every sign now feels like the beloved's meeting is near.
essence: Love turns even omens into messages of return.
simple_meaning: The people around Ram read the omens as signs that Bharat is coming. Their hearts have waited so long that every sign now feels like hope fulfilled.
insight: It trains the mind to notice hope in small signs instead of collapsing into doubt.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after a long silence from someone you love. A tiny message, a typing bubble, even a delayed reply starts to feel like a blessing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत सरिस प्रिय को जग माहीं। इहइ सगुन फलु दूसर नाहीं॥ रामहि बंधु सोच दिन राती। अंडन्हि कमठ हृदय जेहि भाँती ॥
translation: और भरत के समान जगत में (हमें) कौन प्यारा है! शकुन का बस, यही फल है, दूसरा नहीं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी को (अपने) भाई भरत का दिन-रात ऐसा सोच रहता है जैसा कछुए का हृदय अंडों में रहता है ॥
english_translation: Who in the world is dear like Bharat? This is the only fruit of the omen, nothing else. Ram thinks of his brother Bharat day and night, like a turtle guarding its eggs in its heart.
essence: True love keeps the absent beloved alive in the heart.
simple_meaning: Bharat is described as the dearest person in the world, and Ram keeps thinking of him constantly, with deep protective concern.
insight: It shifts attention from public celebration to the private bond that gives the celebration its heart.
modern_relevance: You are halfway through a crowded family wedding when one person keeps scanning the entrance, not for attention but for someone they love. That quiet loyalty is what this verse honors.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि अवसर मंगलु परम सुनि रहँसेउ रनिवासु। सोभत लखि बिधु बढ़त जनु बारिधि बीचि बिलासु ॥
translation: इसी समय यह परम मंगल समाचार सुनकर सारा रनिवास हर्षित हो उठा। जैसे चन्द्रमा को बढ़ते देखकर समुद्र में लहरों का विलास (आनंद) सुशोभित होता है ॥
english_translation: At this moment, hearing this most auspicious news, the whole inner palace rejoiced. Like waves dancing in the sea when the moon grows brighter, it became beautiful.
essence: Hope arriving at last makes even waiting feel beautiful.
simple_meaning: The royal women hear the news and become joyful at once. Their delight is compared to sea waves brightening under the rising moon.
insight: It turns waiting into visible joy and shows how hope animates an entire household.
modern_relevance: You see a message from someone you've been waiting for all week, and your whole body loosens before you even open it. Relief can feel like light returning to a room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रथम जाइ जिन्ह बचन सुनाए। भूषन बसन भूरि तिन्ह पाए॥ प्रेम पुलकि तन मन अनुरागीं। मंगल कलस सजन सब लागीं ॥
translation: सबसे पहले (रनिवास में) जाकर जिन्होंने ये वचन (समाचार) सुनाए, उन्होंने बहुत से आभूषण और वस्त्र पाए। रानियों का शरीर प्रेम से पुलकित हो उठा और मन प्रेम में मग्न हो गया। वे सब मंगल कलश सजाने लगीं ॥
english_translation: Those who first went and told the news received many ornaments and garments. The queens' bodies thrilled with love, and their minds were absorbed in affection. They all began arranging the auspicious pots.
essence: Good news turns sorrow into celebration before anything else changes.
simple_meaning: The messengers who brought the good news were rewarded. The queens overflowed with joy and began preparing for celebration.
insight: It shows how hope instantly reorganizes behavior, turning waiting into preparation.
modern_relevance: A text message finally arrives after hours of silence, and the whole room changes. Relief turns into motion: calls, plans, food, clothes, everything suddenly has purpose again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चौकें चारु सुमित्राँ पूरी। मनिमय बिबिध भाँति अति रूरी॥ आनँद मगन राम महतारी। दिए दान बहु बिप्र हँकारी ॥
translation: सुमित्राजी ने मणियों (रत्नों) के बहुत प्रकार के अत्यन्त सुंदर और मनोहर चौक पूरे। आनंद में मग्न हुई श्री रामचन्द्रजी की माता कौसल्याजी ने ब्राह्मणों को बुलाकर बहुत दान दिए ॥
english_translation: Sumitra filled the courtyards with many kinds of beautiful jeweled designs. In joy, Ram's mother Kaushalya, absorbed in bliss, called the Brahmins and gave many gifts.
essence: Joy does not stay still; it becomes giving.
simple_meaning: The palace is being decorated for a joyful celebration, and Kaushalya gives gifts to Brahmins in her happiness.
insight: It shifts emotion into offering: delight becomes visible through generosity and care.
modern_relevance: You get the message that someone you love is safe, and suddenly you start tidying the house, buying sweets, calling relatives. Happiness wants to become action, not stay private.
