modern_relevance: Your oldest friend finally gets the promotion everyone expected. You still speak to them like the person who knew your worst days, not the title on their door.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: फिरहिं भवन प्रिय आयसु पाई। करत परसपर राम बड़ाई॥ को रघुबीर सरिस संसारा। सीलु सनेहु निबाहनिहारा ॥
translation: अपने प्रिय सखा श्री रामचन्द्रजी की आज्ञा पाकर वे आपस में एक-दूसरे से श्री रामचन्द्रजी की बड़ाई करते हुए घर लौटते हैं और कहते हैं- संसार में श्री रघुनाथजी के समान शील और स्नेह को निबाहने वाला कौन है? ॥
english_translation: They return to their homes after receiving Ram's kind permission, praising Ram to one another. "Who in the world is like the Lord of the Raghu clan, who keeps both character and affection?"
essence: Character and affection make Ram unforgettable.
simple_meaning: Ram's friends go home after his permission, praising him among themselves. They see him as unmatched in keeping both character and affection.
insight: It shifts admiration from status to character, showing that true authority is measured by how faithfully someone treats others.
modern_relevance: You leave a reunion still talking about the one person who treated everyone with rare steadiness. No performance, no sharp edges — just the kind of respect that makes people remember you on the drive home.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जेहिं-जेहिं जोनि करम बस भ्रमहीं। तहँ तहँ ईसु देउ यह हमहीं॥ सेवक हम स्वामी सियनाहू। होउ नात यह ओर निबाहू ॥
translation: भगवान हमें यही दें कि हम अपने कर्मवश भ्रमते हुए जिस-जिस योनि में जन्में, वहाँ-वहाँ (उस-उस योनि में) हम तो सेवक हों और सीतापति श्री रामचन्द्रजी हमारे स्वामी हों और यह नाता अन्त तक निभ जाए॥
english_translation: May the divine grant that, wherever we are driven by the force of our actions in any birth, we remain servants there, and Ram, Lord of Sita, remains our master. May this bond endure to the end.
essence: True freedom is to belong to Ram in every life.
simple_meaning: No matter where karma sends us in future births, let us remain servants and let Ram remain our master forever.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing status to preserving devotion through every change.
modern_relevance: After a long career change, a family move, or a season of uncertainty, you may not know what role life will give you next. This prayer says identity can stay steady even when circumstances do not.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अस अभिलाषु नगर सब काहू। कैकयसुता हृदयँ अति दाहू॥ को न कुसंगति पाइ नसाई। रहइ न नीच मतें चतुराई ॥
translation: नगर में सबकी ऐसी ही अभिलाषा है, परन्तु कैकेयी के हृदय में बड़ी जलन हो रही है। कुसंगति पाकर कौन नष्ट नहीं होता। नीच के मत के अनुसार चलने से चतुराई नहीं रह जाती ॥
english_translation: Everyone in the city has the same wish, but Kaikeyi's heart burns with intense jealousy. Who does not get ruined by bad company? Wisdom does not remain when one follows the counsel of the base.
essence: Bad company burns away clear judgment before a person notices.
simple_meaning: The whole city wants one thing, but Kaikeyi is burning inside. Bad company ruins people, and following base advice destroys good judgment.
insight: It shifts attention from the outward event to the hidden influence shaping the mind.
modern_relevance: You leave a conversation feeling oddly smaller, then realise someone has been feeding your worst suspicion for weeks. This verse names that slow corruption before it becomes your own voice.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: साँझ समय सानंद नृपु गयउ कैकई गेहँ। गवनु निठुरता निकट किय जनु धरि देह सनेहँ ॥
translation: संध्या के समय राजा दशरथ आनंद के साथ कैकेयी के महल में गए। मानो साक्षात स्नेह ही शरीर धारण कर निष्ठुरता के पास गया हो! ॥
english_translation: At dusk, King Dasharath went joyfully to Kaikeyi's palace. It was as if affection itself had taken a body and walked toward cruelty.
essence: Affection can walk straight into cruelty without noticing the trap.
simple_meaning: Dasharath walks happily into Kaikeyi's palace, unaware that affection is entering the place where cruelty waits.
insight: It prepares the mind for betrayal by showing how trust can be blind to its own vulnerability.
modern_relevance: You walk into a familiar house smiling, carrying good news, and the room changes before you understand why. Sometimes the heart arrives before the danger does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोपभवन सुनि सकुचेउ राऊ। भय बस अगहुड़ परइ न पाऊ॥ सुरपति बसइ बाहँबल जाकें। नरपति सकल रहहिं रुख ताकें ॥
translation: कोप भवन का नाम सुनकर राजा सहम गए। डर के मारे उनका पाँव आगे को नहीं पड़ता। स्वयं देवराज इन्द्र जिनकी भुजाओं के बल पर (राक्षसों से निर्भय होकर) बसता है और सम्पूर्ण राजा लोग जिनका रुख देखते रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing of the anger chamber, the king grew timid. In fear, his feet would not move forward. Even Indra lives by the strength of his arms, and all kings keep watching his face.
essence: Fear can stop even the powerful before they speak.
simple_meaning: Dasharath hears of the anger chamber and loses his courage. Fear stops him, even though he is a powerful king.
insight: It shows how fear can shrink even the strongest person before any words are spoken.
modern_relevance: You stand outside a room where a hard conversation is waiting. Your body knows before your mind admits it: one sentence inside could change everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सो सुनि तिय रिस गयउ सुखाई। देखहु काम प्रताप बड़ाई॥ सूल कुलिस असि अँगवनिहारे। ते रतिनाथ सुमन सर मारे ॥
translation: वही राजा दशरथ स्त्री का क्रोध सुनकर सूख गए। कामदेव का प्रताप और महिमा तो देखिए। जो त्रिशूल, वज्र और तलवार आदि की चोट अपने अंगों पर सहने वाले हैं, वे रतिनाथ कामदेव के पुष्पबाण से मारे गए ॥
english_translation: Hearing her anger, King Dasharath withered away. See the greatness of Kamadeva's power. Those who bear tridents, thunderbolts, and swords on their bodies are struck by the flower-arrows of the lord of passion.
essence: Even the strongest body falls before an unsettled mind.
simple_meaning: Dasharath weakens at the sound of Kaikeyi's anger. The verse marvels that even the strongest beings can be pierced by desire's softest arrows.
insight: It shifts attention from physical strength to the mind's hidden weakness before desire and fear.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense conversation already tired, already hoping to keep the peace. One sharp tone from the other person and your resolve collapses before the real argument even begins.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सभय नरेसु प्रिया पहिं गयऊ। देखि दसा दुखु दारुन भयऊ॥ भूमि सयन पटु मोट पुराना। दिए डारि तन भूषन नाना ॥
translation: राजा डरते-डरते अपनी प्यारी कैकेयी के पास गए। उसकी दशा देखकर उन्हें बड़ा ही दुःख हुआ। कैकेयी जमीन पर पड़ी है। पुराना मोटा कपड़ा पहने हुए है। शरीर के नाना आभूषणों को उतारकर फेंक दिया है।
english_translation: The frightened king went to his beloved Kaikeyi. Seeing her condition, he was deeply grieved. Kaikeyi lay on the ground, wearing an old coarse cloth, having cast off all her ornaments.
essence: Fear and love meet in a single wounded glance.
simple_meaning: Dasharath goes anxiously to Kaikeyi and is pained by her miserable appearance. She lies on the floor in plain clothes, having removed her ornaments.
insight: It shifts attention from accusation to the raw human cost of conflict.
modern_relevance: You walk into a bedroom after an argument and find the other person curled on the floor, silent and wrecked. Your anger drops before the sight of their pain.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कुमतिहि कसि कुबेषता फाबी। अनअहिवातु सूच जनु भाबी॥ जाइ निकट नृपु कह मृदु बानी। प्रानप्रिया केहि हेतु रिसानी ॥
translation: उस दुर्बुद्धि कैकेयी को यह कुवेषता (बुरा वेष) कैसी फब रही है, मानो भावी विधवापन की सूचना दे रही हो। राजा उसके पास जाकर कोमल वाणी से बोले- हे प्राणप्रिये! किसलिए रिसाई (रूठी) हो? ॥
english_translation: Why does this ugly disguise suit the foolish-minded Kaikeyi so well, as if it were a sign of coming widowhood? The king went near her and spoke gently: "Beloved, why are you angry?"
essence: Gentle speech can enter even a poisoned room.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi’s harsh appearance seems like a bad omen, and Dasharath approaches her softly, asking why she is angry.
insight: It teaches you to meet conflict with calm speech before the damage deepens.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and instantly feel something is wrong. Instead of snapping back, you soften your voice and ask what hurt them. That is the king’s instinct here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: केहि हेतु रानि रिसानि परसत पानि पतिहि नेवारई। मानहुँ सरोष भुअंग भामिनि बिषम भाँति निहारई॥ दोउ बासना रसना दसन बर मरम ठाहरु देखई। तुलसी नृपति भवतब्यता बस काम कौतुक लेखई॥
translation: 'हे रानी! किसलिए रूठी हो?' यह कहकर राजा उसे हाथ से स्पर्श करते हैं, तो वह उनके हाथ को (झटककर) हटा देती है और ऐसे देखती है मानो क्रोध में भरी हुई नागिन क्रूर दृष्टि से देख रही हो। दोनों (वरदानों की) वासनाएँ उस नागिन की दो जीभें हैं और दोनों वरदान दाँत हैं, वह काटने के लिए मर्मस्थान देख रही है। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि राजा दशरथ होनहार के वश में होकर इसे (इस प्रकार हाथ झटकने और नागिन की भाँति देखने को) कामदेव की क्रीड़ा ही समझ रहे हैं।
english_translation: “Why are you angry, queen?” When the king touches her hand, she pushes his hand away and looks at him like an enraged serpent. Her two desires are like that serpent’s two tongues, its two boons like its fangs, searching for a vital spot to strike. Tulsidas says the king, trapped by fate, mistakes this as a play of desire.
essence: Blind trust turns a warning into a joke.
simple_meaning: Dasharath thinks Kaikeyi is merely angry, but her mind is already set on the two boons that will wound him. He cannot see the danger because desire has clouded his judgment.
insight: It teaches you to notice when emotion is masking a deeper agenda, instead of assuming goodwill will explain everything.
modern_relevance: You keep reassuring yourself that a tense conversation is only moodiness, while the other person has already decided the outcome. The cost of misreading intention is often paid too late.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बार बार कह राउ सुमुखि सुलोचनि पिकबचनि। कारन मोहि सुनाउ गजगामिनि निज कोप कर ॥
translation: राजा बार-बार कह रहे हैं- हे सुमुखी! हे सुलोचनी! हे कोकिलबयनी! हे गजगामिनी! मुझे अपने क्रोध का कारण तो बताओ ॥
english_translation: Again and again the king said, 'O fair-faced one, lovely-eyed one, voice like a cuckoo, graceful one, tell me the reason for your anger.'
essence: Tender words cannot reach a heart already closed.
simple_meaning: Dasharath keeps gently asking Kaikeyi why she is angry and wants her to explain herself.
insight: It shows a helpless attempt to restore intimacy by appealing to tenderness instead of force.
modern_relevance: You keep asking, softly, what went wrong in the conversation, while the other person stays cold and silent. The heartbreak is not the shouting; it is the refusal to explain.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: अनहित तोर प्रिया केइँ कीन्हा। केहि दुइ सिर केहि जमु चह लीन्हा॥ कहु केहि रंकहि करौं नरेसू। कहु केहि नृपहि निकासौं देसू ॥
translation: हे प्रिये! किसने तेरा अनिष्ट किया? किसके दो सिर हैं? यमराज किसको लेना (अपने लोक को ले जाना) चाहते हैं? कह, किस कंगाल को राजा कर दूँ या किस राजा को देश से निकाल दूँ? ॥
english_translation: Beloved, who has wronged you? Who has two heads? Which Yama wants to take away? Tell me, which beggar should I make king, or which king should I drive from the land?
essence: Love, once shaken, can make a king beg like a child.
simple_meaning: Dasharath begs Kaikeyi to explain her anger and offers impossible rewards to whoever she names. He is trying to calm her, not teaching a principle by itself.
insight: It shows how attachment can make power look helpless and turn speech into pleading.
modern_relevance: Someone you love goes cold for reasons you cannot understand. You start bargaining, apologising, promising anything — because the silence feels unbearable.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: सकउँ तोर अरि अमरउ मारी। काह कीट बपुरे नर नारी॥ जानसि मोर सुभाउ बरोरू। मनु तव आनन चंद चकोरू ॥
translation: तेरा शत्रु अमर (देवता) भी हो, तो मैं उसे भी मार सकता हूँ। बेचारे कीड़े-मकोड़े सरीखे नर-नारी तो चीज ही क्या हैं। हे सुंदरी! तू तो मेरा स्वभाव जानती ही है कि मेरा मन सदा तेरे मुख रूपी चन्द्रमा का चकोर है ॥
english_translation: I could even kill your enemy if he were immortal. What are mere human beings? You know my nature well, fair one: my mind is always a chakora bird to your moonlike face.
essence: Pride turns cruelty into self-display.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he could kill even an immortal enemy, dismisses ordinary people as insignificant, and says his mind is fixed on Mandodari’s face like a bird on the moon.
insight: It exposes how desire and arrogance can dress themselves up as confidence.
modern_relevance: A person in a heated argument starts talking like no one else matters and every problem is beneath them. The louder the boasting gets, the more fragile the ego underneath it looks.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: प्रिया प्रान सुत सरबसु मोरें। परिजन प्रजा सकल बस तोरें॥ जौं कछु कहौं कपटु करि तोही। भामिनि राम सपथ सत मोही ॥
translation: हे प्रिये! मेरी प्रजा, कुटम्बी, सर्वस्व (सम्पत्ति), पुत्र, यहाँ तक कि मेरे प्राण भी, ये सब तेरे वश में (अधीन) हैं। यदि मैं तुझसे कुछ कपट करके कहता होऊँ तो हे भामिनी! मुझे सौ बार राम की सौगंध है ॥
english_translation: My beloved, my life, my son, my everything, my family, my people, and all my wealth are under your control. If I speak deceitfully to you, then, O beautiful one, may I be struck a hundred times by Ram's oath.
essence: Flattery can wear the mask of devotion while hiding coercion.
simple_meaning: Ravana claims that everything he values is under Sita's control, and he swears by Ram that he is not lying.
insight: It exposes how language can be used to disarm judgment before a harmful demand.
modern_relevance: Someone floods your inbox with praise, then asks for a favor that crosses a line. The warmth is real in the words, but the pressure underneath is the point.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: बिहसि मागु मनभावति बाता। भूषन सजहि मनोहर गाता॥। घरी कुघरी समुझि जियँ देखू। बेगि प्रिया परिहरहि कुबेषू ॥
translation: तू हँसकर (प्रसन्नतापूर्वक) अपनी मनचाही बात माँग ले और अपने मनोहर अंगों को आभूषणों से सजा। मौका-बेमौका तो मन में विचार कर देख। हे प्रिये! जल्दी इस बुरे वेष को त्याग दे ॥
english_translation: Smilingly ask for whatever pleases your mind, and adorn your beautiful body with ornaments. Consider the right and wrong time in your heart. Dear one, quickly give up this ugly disguise.
essence: Love can make a person bless the very harm that will destroy him.
simple_meaning: Dasharath, still under Kaikeyi's influence, speaks gently and tells her to ask for what she wants, dress well, and quickly drop the harsh disguise she has worn.
insight: It shows how affection and blindness can coexist, making a person unable to see danger even while naming it.
modern_relevance: You smile at someone you trust, trying to keep the mood light, while missing the damage already taking shape in the room.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: यह सुनि मन गुनि सपथ बड़ि बिहसि उठी मतिमंद। भूषन सजति बिलोकिमृगु मनहुँ किरातिनि फंद ॥
translation: यह सुनकर और मन में रामजी की बड़ी सौंगंध को विचारकर मंदबुद्धि कैकेयी हँसती हुई उठी और गहने पहनने लगी, मानो कोई भीलनी मृग को देखकर फंदा तैयार कर रही हो! ॥
english_translation: Hearing this and reflecting on Ram's great oath in her mind, the foolish Kaikeyi rose laughing and began putting on ornaments, like a hunter-woman setting a snare after seeing a deer.
essence: A trapped mind can hear honesty and still prepare betrayal.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi hears Ram's oath, thinks about it, and laughs as she puts on ornaments. The verse compares her to a hunter preparing a trap.
insight: It exposes how cunning works: hearing truth without being changed by it.
modern_relevance: Someone hears a sincere apology, nods, and quietly plans the next move anyway. The face is calm, but the mind is already loading the trap.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि कह राउ सुहृद जियँ जानी। प्रेम पुलकि मृदु मंजुल बानी॥ भामिनि भयउ तोर मनभावा। घर घर नगर अनंद बधावा ॥
translation: अपने जी में कैकेयी को सुहृद् जानकर राजा दशरथजी प्रेम से पुलकित होकर कोमल और सुंदर वाणी से फिर बोले- हे भामिनि! तेरे मन का ही होगा। नगर में घर-घर आनंद के बधावे बज रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: King Dasharath, seeing Kaikeyi as a friend in his heart, spoke again with love, his body thrilled, in soft and lovely words: “O beautiful one, whatever is in your heart will happen. In every house of the city, songs of joy are being sung.”
essence: Warm trust can make a king blind to danger.
simple_meaning: Dasharath speaks gently to Kaikeyi, trusting her as a friend and saying he will grant what she wants. He believes the city is already celebrating.
insight: It shows how affection without discernment can leave a person exposed to manipulation.
modern_relevance: You’re speaking warmly to someone you trust, unaware they are about to ask for something that will split your life open. The heartbreak is not in the shouting; it begins in the softness.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: रामहि देउँ कालि जुबराजू। सजहि सुलोचनि मंगल साजू॥ दलकि उठेउ सुनि हृदउ कठोरू। जनु छुइ गयउ पाक बरतोरू ॥
translation: मैं कल ही राम को युवराज पद दे रहा हूँ, इसलिए हे सुनयनी! तू मंगल साज सज। यह सुनते ही उसका कठोर हृदय दलक उठा (फटने लगा)। मानो पका हुआ बालतोड़ (फोड़ा) छू गया हो ॥
english_translation: I will give Ram the crown prince’s seat tomorrow. O beautiful-eyed one, prepare the auspicious ornaments. Hearing this, her hard heart split open, like a ripe boil touched by a hand.
essence: Desire turns celebration into pain.
simple_meaning: Dasharath announces that Ram will be crowned tomorrow. Kaikeyi’s heart, hardened by desire, breaks open in pain and shock.
insight: It exposes how a heart hardened by craving can react violently to joy it does not want.
modern_relevance: You hear a promotion, a wedding plan, or a family decision and realize someone in the room is not celebrating. Their silence suddenly feels dangerous.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: ऐसिउ पीर बिहसि तेहिं गोई। चोर नारि जिमि प्रगटि न रोई॥ लखहिं न भूप कपट चतुराई। कोटि कुटिल मनि गुरू पढ़ाई ॥
translation: ऐसी भारी पीड़ा को भी उसने हँसकर छिपा लिया, जैसे चोर की स्त्री प्रकट होकर नहीं रोती (जिसमें उसका भेद न खुल जाए)। राजा उसकी कपट-चतुराई को नहीं लख रहे हैं, क्योंकि वह करोड़ों कुटिलों की शिरोमणि गुरु मंथरा की पढ़ाई हुई है ॥
english_translation: She hid even that intense pain with a smile, like a thief's wife who does not cry in public so her secret is not exposed. The king does not see her deceitful cunning, because she was taught by Manthara, the teacher of millions of crooked minds.
essence: A smiling face can conceal a mind already captured by deceit.
simple_meaning: She hides her pain behind a smile so her deceit is not exposed. The king still cannot see her cunning.
insight: It trains attention on hidden motive, not visible politeness. The mind learns to look beneath performance.
modern_relevance: Someone laughs at the dinner table after a harsh text just arrived, then keeps the conversation moving. Everyone sees calm; no one sees the plan forming underneath.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जद्यपि नीति निपुन नरनाहू। नारिचरित जलनिधि अवगाहू॥ कपट सनेहु बढ़ाई बहोरी। बोली बिहसि नयन मुहु मोरी ॥
translation: यद्यपि राजा नीति में निपुण हैं, परन्तु त्रियाचरित्र अथाह समुद्र है। फिर वह कपटयुक्त प्रेम बढ़ाकर (ऊपर से प्रेम दिखाकर) नेत्र और मुँह मोड़कर हँसती हुई बोली- ॥
english_translation: Although the king is skilled in policy, a woman's conduct is an unfathomable sea. She then increased her pretended affection and, turning her eyes and face away, spoke with a smile.
essence: Charm can conceal intention better than force.
simple_meaning: Even a wise king can be fooled when deceit is wrapped in a smile. The verse shows a hidden intention behind outward affection.
insight: It trains the mind to look past performance and notice the motive underneath.
modern_relevance: Someone says, “Of course I’m happy for you,” while their jaw is tight and their eyes won’t meet yours. The words sound gentle, but the room has already changed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मागु मागु पै कहहु पिय कबहुँ न देहु न लेहु। देन कहेहु बरदान दुइ तेउ पावत संदेहु ॥
translation: हे प्रियतम! आप माँग-माँग तो कहा करते हैं, पर देते-लेते कभी कुछ भी नहीं। आपने दो वरदान देने को कहा था, उनके भी मिलने में संदेह है ॥
english_translation: Beloved, you keep saying, “Ask, ask,” yet you never truly give or take. You spoke of granting two boons, but even that seems uncertain.
essence: Empty offers breed suspicion, not peace.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi speaks bitterly to Dasharath, saying he keeps urging her to ask, yet never truly gives anything. Even the promised two boons now feel doubtful to her.
insight: It exposes a mind that can no longer trust words, only motives.
modern_relevance: A partner says, “Tell me what you need,” but every time you do, they change the subject. After a while, even their promises start to sound empty.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: जानेउँ मरमु राउ हँसि कहई। तुम्हहि कोहाब परम प्रिय अहई॥ थाती राखि न मागिहु काऊ। बिसरि गयउ मोहि भोर सुभाऊ ॥
translation: राजा ने हँसकर कहा कि अब मैं तुम्हारा मर्म (मतलब) समझा। मान करना तुम्हें परम प्रिय है। तुमने उन वरों को थाती (धरोहर) रखकर फिर कभी माँगा ही नहीं और मेरा भूलने का स्वभाव होने से मुझे भी वह प्रसंग याद नहीं रहा ॥
english_translation: The king laughed and said, 'Now I understand your meaning. Pride is what you love most. You kept those boons as a stored treasure and never asked for them again, and because I forget easily, I also forgot that matter.'
essence: Silence can hide pride until it becomes a wound.
simple_meaning: The king says he now sees the other person’s real intention: they value pride most, kept the boons unused, and never brought them up again. He also says he forgot about them because of his own forgetful nature.
insight: It shifts attention from the spoken demand to the motive beneath it, showing how unspoken pride can harden into conflict.
modern_relevance: A family argument suddenly turns cold: one person says, 'So that’s what this was really about.' The hurt is not just the request — it is the years of silence that made the request feel like a trap.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: झूठेहुँ हमहि दोषु जनि देहू। दुइ कै चारि मागि मकु लेहू॥ रघुकुल रीति सदा चलि आई। प्रान जाहुँ परु बचनु न जाई ॥
translation: मुझे झूठ-मूठ दोष मत दो। चाहे दो के बदले चार माँग लो। रघुकुल में सदा से यह रीति चली आई है कि प्राण भले ही चले जाएँ, पर वचन नहीं जाता ॥
english_translation: Do not wrongly blame me. Ask for four instead of two if you wish. The Raghus have always kept this rule: life may go, but a promise does not.
essence: A true promise is kept even when it costs everything.
simple_meaning: A promise matters more than life itself. The royal line of Raghu is defined by keeping one’s word, even at the highest cost.
insight: It shifts the mind from convenience to covenant: what you promised becomes more important than what is easiest now.
modern_relevance: You told your child you'd show up, then the meeting ran late and the excuse came easily. This verse remembers the cost of saying yes and the dignity of still arriving.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: नहिं असत्य सम पातक पुंजा। गिरि सम होहिं कि कोटिक गुंजा॥ सत्यमूल सब सुकृत सुहाए। बेद पुरान बिदित मनु गाए ॥
translation: असत्य के समान पापों का समूह भी नहीं है। क्या करोड़ों घुँघचियाँ मिलकर भी कहीं पहाड़ के समान हो सकती हैं। 'सत्य' ही समस्त उत्तम सुकृतों (पुण्यों) की जड़ है। यह बात वेद-पुराणों में प्रसिद्ध है और मनुजी ने भी यही कहा है ॥
english_translation: No heap of sins is equal to falsehood. Can millions of tiny shells ever become a mountain? Truth is the root of all noble deeds. The Vedas, Puranas, and Manu declare this.
essence: Falsehood corrupts everything; truth gives every good act its root.
simple_meaning: Falsehood is the worst corruption, and truth is the source of every good action. The verse says this is a timeless principle taught by tradition.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating honesty as optional to seeing it as the base of all right action.
modern_relevance: You are about to send a message that hides the real reason, hoping it will make things easier. The verse cuts through that impulse: once truth is bent, the whole act is weakened from the root.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहि पर राम सपथ करि आई। सुकृत सनेह अवधि रघुराई॥ बाद दृढ़ाइ कुमति हँसि बोली। कुमत कुबिहग कुलह जनु खोली ॥
translation: उस पर मेरे द्वारा श्री रामजी की शपथ करने में आ गई (मुँह से निकल पड़ी)। श्री रघुनाथजी मेरे सुकृत (पुण्य) और स्नेह की सीमा हैं। इस प्रकार बात पक्की कराके दुर्बुद्धि कैकेयी हँसकर बोली, मानो उसने कुमत (बुरे विचार) रूपी दुष्ट पक्षी (बाज) (को छोड़ने के लिए उस) की कुलही (आँखों पर की टोपी) खोल दी ॥
english_translation: Then, by invoking Ram's name, she spoke. Raghunath is the limit of my merit and affection. Having firmly fixed the matter, the foolish woman laughed, as if she had opened the hood to release a cruel hawk of evil intent.
essence: A corrupted mind can use sacred words to fasten its own harm.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi brings Ram's name into her oath, then laughs after securing her demand. Her hardened mind is shown as if it has opened a hood and released a dangerous bird of bad intent.
insight: It exposes how self-deception can dress itself in noble language and still push a harmful decision forward.
modern_relevance: You say a promise is for the best, but some hidden part of you is already smiling at the damage it will do. The harm begins the moment you stop questioning your own motive.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: भूप मनोरथ सुभग बनु सुख सुबिहंग समाजु। भिल्लिनि जिमि छाड़न चहति बचनु भयंकरु बाजु ॥
translation: राजा का मनोरथ सुंदर वन है, सुख सुंदर पक्षियों का समुदाय है। उस पर भीलनी की तरह कैकेयी अपना वचन रूपी भयंकर बाज छोड़ना चाहती है ॥
english_translation: The king's wish is a beautiful forest, and the company of joy is like lovely birds. Yet Kaikeyi, like a huntress, wants to release the terrible arrow of her vow.
essence: A beautiful order can be broken by one spoken vow.
simple_meaning: Dasharath's hopes are pictured as a peaceful forest full of beauty and joy, but Kaikeyi is about to unleash a cruel promise like a deadly arrow.
insight: It shows how hidden intention can sit inside calm appearances until one decisive word releases it.
modern_relevance: A quiet dinner can change in one sentence. Someone says the thing they've been holding back, and the room goes cold. You can feel the moment before the damage lands.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनहु प्रानप्रिय भावत जी का। देहु एक बर भरतहि टीका॥ मागउँ दूसर बर कर जोरी। पुरवहु नाथ मनोरथ मोरी ॥
translation: (वह बोली-) हे प्राण प्यारे! सुनिए, मेरे मन को भाने वाला एक वर तो दीजिए, भरत को राजतिलक और हे नाथ! दूसरा वर भी मैं हाथ जोड़कर माँगती हूँ, मेरा मनोरथ पूरा कीजिए- ॥
english_translation: “Listen, my dear life, grant one boon that pleases me: give the coronation to Bharata. And, my lord, I ask for a second boon with folded hands: fulfill my wish.”
essence: A gentle request can conceal a devastating demand.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi asks Dasharath to give Bharata the coronation and to fulfill a second wish she is about to name.
insight: It shows how desire can wear a soft face while setting tragedy in motion.
modern_relevance: A message sounds polite, almost tender, but the real demand is hidden beneath it. The calm tone makes the blow harder when it lands.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: तापस बेष बिसेषि उदासी। चौदह बरिस रामु बनबासी॥ सुनि मृदु बचन भूप हियँ सोकू। ससि कर छुअत बिकल जिमि कोकू ॥
translation: तपस्वियों के वेष में विशेष उदासीन भाव से (राज्य और कुटुम्ब आदि की ओर से भलीभाँति उदासीन होकर विरक्त मुनियों की भाँति) राम चौदह वर्ष तक वन में निवास करें। कैकेयी के कोमल (विनययुक्त) वचन सुनकर राजा के हृदय में ऐसा शोक हुआ जैसे चन्द्रमा की किरणों के स्पर्श से चकवा विकल हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Ram will live in the forest for fourteen years, dressed like an ascetic and turned away from home and kingdom. Hearing Kaikeyi's gentle words, the king's heart filled with sorrow, like a chakravak bird struck by moonlight.
essence: A spoken boon becomes a king's deepest grief.
simple_meaning: Ram is to live in the forest for fourteen years, dressed like an ascetic and detached from royal life. Hearing this, Dasharath is overwhelmed with grief.
insight: It shifts attention from the words spoken to the life-altering duty those words impose.
modern_relevance: You read a message that changes a family forever. One sentence redirects a whole life, and the person who must honor it feels the blow first.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गयउ सहमि नहिं कछु कहि आवा। जनु सचान बन झपटेउ लावा॥ बिबरन भयउ निपट नरपालू। दामिनि हनेउ मनहुँ तरु तालू ॥
translation: राजा सहम गए, उनसे कुछ कहते न बना मानो बाज वन में बटेर पर झपटा हो। राजा का रंग बिलकुल उड़ गया, मानो ताड़ के पेड़ को बिजली ने मारा हो (जैसे ताड़ के पेड़ पर बिजली गिरने से वह झुलसकर बदरंगा हो जाता है, वही हाल राजा का हुआ) ॥
english_translation: The king was stunned and could say nothing, as if a hawk had pounced on a quail in the forest. His face turned completely pale, like a palm tree struck by lightning.
essence: Grief can strike faster than thought and leave no words behind.
simple_meaning: The king is so shocked by the news that he cannot speak. His face loses all color, and he looks stricken and helpless.
insight: It shows how overwhelming grief can silence speech and drain the body at once.
modern_relevance: You read a message that changes everything, and your hands go cold before you can reply. The mind has not caught up, but the body already knows.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: माथें हाथ मूदि दोउ लोचन। तनु धरि सोचु लाग जनु सोचन॥ मोर मनोरथु सुरतरु फूला। फरत करिनि जिमि हतेउ समूला ॥
translation: माथे पर हाथ रखकर, दोनों नेत्र बंद करके राजा ऐसे सोच करने लगे, मानो साक्षात् सोच ही शरीर धारण कर सोच कर रहा हो। (वे सोचते हैं- हाय!) मेरा मनोरथ रूपी कल्पवृक्ष फूल चुका था, परन्तु फलते समय कैकेयी ने हथिनी की तरह उसे जड़ समेत उखाड़कर नष्ट कर डाला ॥
english_translation: Placing his hand on his head and closing both eyes, the king sank into grief, as if grief itself had taken bodily form. 'My wish was a flowering wish-tree; just as it was bearing fruit, Kaikeyi uprooted it completely like an elephant uprooting a tree.'
essence: Hope can flower fully and still be torn out at the root.
simple_meaning: Dasharath collapses into grief and says his long-cherished wish was ruined just as it was about to bear fruit.
insight: It shows how quickly hope can turn into collapse when the thing you built your life around is cut off at the root.
modern_relevance: You finally see the future you worked for — the offer, the wedding, the home, the breakthrough — and then one call changes everything. The grief is not just loss; it's the timing.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: अवध उजारि कीन्हि कैकेईं। दीन्हिसि अचल बिपति कै नेईं ॥
translation: कैकेयी ने अयोध्या को उजाड़ कर दिया और विपत्ति की अचल (सुदृढ़) नींव डाल दी ॥
english_translation: Kaikeyi laid waste to Ayodhya and set the firm foundation of calamity.
essence: A selfish demand can turn a home into ruin.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi's action brought ruin to Ayodhya and made disaster feel permanent.
insight: It shifts attention from private desire to the wider damage a choice can leave behind.
modern_relevance: A single text message sent in anger can change a family group forever. One demand, one lie, one reckless choice can become the thing everyone has to live around.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कवनें अवसर का भयउ गयउँ नारि बिस्वास। जोग सिद्धि फल समय जिमि जतिहि अबिद्या नास ॥
translation: किस अवसर पर क्या हो गया! स्त्री का विश्वास करके मैं वैसे ही मारा गया, जैसे योग की सिद्धि रूपी फल मिलने के समय योगी को अविद्या नष्ट कर देती है ॥
english_translation: At what moment did this happen? Trusting a woman, I was ruined, just as ignorance vanishes for a yogi when the fruit of yoga is reached.
essence: Trust can become the very thing that undoes you.
simple_meaning: Dasharath laments that trusting Kaikeyi has destroyed him, comparing his ruin to the moment a yogi's ignorance disappears at the end of practice.
insight: It shows how misplaced trust can turn a decisive moment into a catastrophe.
modern_relevance: You open a message and realise the person you trusted has already made the decision without you. The shock is not just betrayal — it's the sudden collapse of the world you thought was secure.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: एहि बिधि राउ मनहिं मन झाँखा। देखि कुभाँति कुमति मन माखा॥ भरतु कि राउर पूत न होंही। आनेहु मोल बेसाहि कि मोही ॥
translation: इस प्रकार राजा मन ही मन झींख रहे हैं। राजा का ऐसा बुरा हाल देखकर दुर्बुद्धि कैकेयी मन में बुरी तरह से क्रोधित हुई। (और बोली-) क्या भरत आपके पुत्र नहीं हैं? क्या मुझे आप दाम देकर खरीद लाए हैं? (क्या मैं आपकी विवाहिता पत्नी नहीं हूँ?) ॥
english_translation: In this way, the king kept churning his mind in silence. Seeing his cruel state, wicked Kaikeyi grew furious in her mind and said, “Is Bharata not your son? Did you buy me with money? Am I not your lawful wife?”
essence: Pain without clarity becomes accusation.
simple_meaning: Dasharath is inwardly tormented, and Kaikeyi reacts with anger, challenging his claim to Bharata and to her place as his wife.
insight: It shows how a mind caught in hurt stops seeing clearly and starts striking back.
modern_relevance: A tense conversation at midnight can turn one wounded silence into three new accusations. Nobody is listening anymore; each person is defending a wound.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जो सुनि सरु अस लाग तुम्हारें। काहे न बोलहु बचनु सँभारें॥ देहु उतरु अनु करहु कि नाहीं। सत्यसंध तुम्ह रघुकुल माहीं ॥
translation: जो मेरा वचन सुनते ही आपको बाण सा लगा तो आप सोच-समझकर बात क्यों नहीं कहते? उत्तर दीजिए- हाँ कीजिए, नहीं तो नाहीं कर दीजिए। आप रघुवंश में सत्य प्रतिज्ञा वाले (प्रसिद्ध) हैं! ॥
english_translation: If my words struck you like an arrow, why not speak carefully? Give a clear answer: yes or no. You are famed in the Raghu line for keeping truth.
essence: Truthfulness means answering clearly, even when the answer hurts.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi urges the king to answer clearly instead of reacting in pain. She reminds him that truthfulness is his family’s honor.
insight: It shifts the mind from emotional recoil to direct accountability in speech.
modern_relevance: A tense family conversation goes sideways because one person feels hurt and stops answering directly. The other person demands a clear yes or no, because half-spoken words only deepen the damage.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: देन कहेहु अब जनि बरु देहू। तजहु सत्य जग अपजसु लेहू॥ सत्य सराहि कहेहु बरु देना। जानेहु लेइहि मागि चबेना ॥
translation: आपने ही वर देने को कहा था, अब भले ही न दीजिए। सत्य को छोड़ दीजिए और जगत में अपयश लीजिए। सत्य की बड़ी सराहना करके वर देने को कहा था। समझा था कि यह चबेना ही माँग लेगी! ॥
english_translation: You asked for a boon, so now do not give it. Abandon truth and accept disgrace in the world. You praised truth and said to grant the boon. You thought I was only asking for a small snack.
essence: A promise becomes a weapon when desire speaks through it.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi taunts Dasharath: he promised a boon, so he should either give it or lose his good name. She says he praised truth, yet now acts as if her request was harmless.
insight: It reveals how self-justifying speech can weaponize another person's vow.
modern_relevance: Someone says, “You agreed to this,” after hiding the real cost until the last second. The room goes quiet, and you see how a promise can be used like a knife.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: सिबि दधीचि बलि जो कछु भाषा। तनु धनु तजेउ बचन पनु राखा॥ अति कटु बचन कहति कैकेई। मानहुँ लोन जरे पर देई ॥
translation: राजा शिबि, दधीचि और बलि ने जो कुछ कहा, शरीर और धन त्यागकर भी उन्होंने अपने वचन की प्रतिज्ञा को निबाहा। कैकेयी बहुत ही कड़ुवे वचन कह रही है, मानो जले पर नमक छिड़क रही हो ॥
english_translation: Shibi, Dadhichi, and Bali gave up body and wealth, yet kept their word. Kaikeyi speaks with such bitter words, it is like salt on a wound.
essence: Keeping a vow can cost everything; bitter speech can cut like fire on a wound.
simple_meaning: Great figures like Shibi, Dadhichi, and Bali gave up everything to keep their word. Kaikeyi’s harsh speech feels like salt poured on a burn.
insight: It shifts attention from the heat of the insult to the moral weight of keeping one’s word.
modern_relevance: A family argument turns vicious, and one sentence lands like acid on an old bruise. In that moment, you remember that some people would lose everything before they would break a promise.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धरम धुरंधर धीर धरि नयन उघारे रायँ। सिरु धुनि लीन्हि उसास असि मारेसि मोहि कुठायँ ॥
translation: धर्म की धुरी को धारण करने वाले राजा दशरथ ने धीरज धरकर नेत्र खोले और सिर धुनकर तथा लंबी साँस लेकर इस प्रकार कहा कि इसने मुझे बड़े कुठौर मारा (ऐसी कठिन परिस्थिति उत्पन्न कर दी, जिससे बच निकलना कठिन हो गया) ॥
english_translation: King Dasharath, bearer of dharma, opened his eyes with composure, shook his head, and sighed, saying, 'This has struck me in a terrible place.'
essence: Composure can remain even when a promise turns into pain.
simple_meaning: Dasharath opens his eyes, stays composed, and admits that the situation has struck him painfully and left him trapped.
insight: It shifts attention from outward control to the inward fact of being cornered by one’s own promise.
modern_relevance: You read the message that changes everything, then sit still for a long second before replying. The body knows before the mind can argue: this has landed badly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आगें दीखि जरत सिर भारी। मनहुँ रोष तरवारि उघारी॥ मूठि कुबुद्धि धार निठुराई। धरी कूबरीं सान बनाई ॥
translation: प्रचंड क्रोध से जलती हुई कैकेयी सामने इस प्रकार दिखाई पड़ी, मानो क्रोध रूपी तलवार नंगी (म्यान से बाहर) खड़ी हो। कुबुद्धि उस तलवार की मूठ है, निष्ठुरता धार है और वह कुबरी (मंथरा) रूपी सान पर धरकर तेज की हुई है ॥
english_translation: Kaikeyi appeared before him like a blazing sword of rage, unsheathed. Wrong understanding was its hilt, cruelty its blade, and Manthara's counsel had sharpened it on the whetstone.
essence: Anger becomes deadly when wrong counsel sharpens it.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi appears to Dasharath as a weapon of rage, sharpened by bad counsel and cruelty.
insight: It shifts attention from the person alone to the chain of influence that armed the anger.
modern_relevance: A family conversation turns cold in seconds. One harsh voice, one toxic influence, and suddenly the room feels armed. This verse names how manipulation sharpens anger.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लखी महीप कराल कठोरा। सत्य कि जीवनु लेइहि मोरा॥ बोले राउ कठिन करि छाती। बानी सबिनय तासु सोहाती ॥
translation: राजा ने देखा कि यह (तलवार) बड़ी ही भयानक और कठोर है (और सोचा-) क्या सत्य ही यह मेरा जीवन लेगी? राजा अपनी छाती कड़ी करके, बहुत ही नम्रता के साथ उसे (कैकेयी को) प्रिय लगने वाली वाणी बोले- ॥
english_translation: The king saw the cruel, hard blade and wondered, "Will truth itself take my life?" Then the king hardened his chest and spoke gently, in words pleasing to her.
essence: Pain can be met with gentleness, even at the edge of collapse.
simple_meaning: Dasharath sees the harshness of the moment and speaks with outward gentleness, even while his heart is breaking.
insight: It teaches emotional control under extreme hurt: respond with measured speech instead of immediate retaliation.
modern_relevance: Your throat tightens when someone you love says something unforgivable. You still choose not to throw the wound back at them. That restraint is its own courage.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: प्रिया बचन कस कहसि कुभाँती। भीर प्रतीति प्रीति करि हाँती॥ मोरें भरतु रामु दुइ आँखी। सत्य कहउँ करि संकरु साखी ॥
translation: हे प्रिये! हे भीरु! विश्वास और प्रेम को नष्ट करके ऐसे बुरी तरह के वचन कैसे कह रही हो। मेरे तो भरत और रामचन्द्र दो आँखें (अर्थात एक से) हैं, यह मैं शंकरजी की साक्षी देकर सत्य कहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: My dear, why do you speak such harsh words? You are ruining trust and love. For me, Bharata and Rama are like two eyes. I speak truth, with Shiva as witness.
essence: True love refuses to choose between two beloveds.
simple_meaning: Dasharath gently rebukes Kaikeyi for speaking harshly and says Bharata and Rama are equally dear to him, like two eyes. He swears this truth before Shiva.
insight: It shifts conflict from accusation to tenderness, reminding you to defend love before you defend yourself.
modern_relevance: A spouse says something cruel in the middle of a fight, and you feel the room split open. In that moment, the deepest response is not winning — it is protecting the trust that still remains.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: अवसि दूतु मैं पठइब प्राता। ऐहहिं बेगि सुनत दोउ भ्राता॥ सुदिन सोधि सबु साजु सजाई। देउँ भरत कहुँ राजु बजाई ॥
translation: मैं अवश्य सबेरे ही दूत भेजूँगा। दोनों भाई (भरत-शत्रुघ्न) सुनते ही तुरंत आ जाएँगे। अच्छा दिन (शुभ मुहूर्त) शोधवाकर, सब तैयारी करके डंका बजाकर मैं भरत को राज्य दे दूँगा ॥
english_translation: I will surely send a messenger at dawn. Both brothers will come at once when they hear it. After choosing an auspicious day and arranging everything, I will publicly give the kingdom to Bharat.
essence: Private resolve becomes public duty.
simple_meaning: Dasharath decides to send a messenger at dawn, call his sons quickly, and formally hand the kingdom to Bharat on an auspicious day.
insight: It turns private intention into public responsibility, showing that important choices must be made clearly and openly.
modern_relevance: You finally decide to make the call you have avoided for days: to tell your family, your team, or your partner the hard decision. The relief is real, but the consequences are still waiting.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: लोभु न रामहि राजु कर बहुत भरत पर प्रीति। मैं बड़ छोट बिचारि जियँ करत रहेउँ नृपनीति ॥
translation: राम को राज्य का लोभ नहीं है और भरत पर उनका बड़ा ही प्रेम है। मैं ही अपने मन में बड़े-छोटे का विचार करके राजनीति का पालन कर रहा था (बड़े को राजतिलक देने जा रहा था) ॥
english_translation: Ram has no desire for the throne, and he loves Bharat deeply. I was only following royal custom, thinking in terms of senior and junior.
essence: Rank disappears when love is seen clearly.
simple_meaning: Dasharath admits that Ram does not want the kingdom and loves Bharat deeply. The mistake was his own, thinking in terms of rank and royal custom.
insight: It shifts the mind from measuring people by position to seeing what they actually value and love.
modern_relevance: You assume the promotion matters most, then discover the person you admire never cared about the title. The real error was reading a relationship like a hierarchy.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: राम सपथ सत कहउँ सुभाऊ। राममातु कछु कहेउ न काऊ॥ मैं सबु कीन्ह तोहि बिनु पूँछें। तेहि तें परेउ मनोरथु छूछें ॥
translation: राम की सौ बार सौगंध खाकर मैं स्वभाव से ही कहता हूँ कि राम की माता (कौसल्या) ने (इस विषय में) मुझसे कभी कुछ नहीं कहा। अवश्य ही मैंने तुमसे बिना पूछे यह सब किया। इसी से मेरा मनोरथ खाली गया ॥
english_translation: I swear by Ram a hundred times: by nature I say that Ram's mother never said anything to me about this. I did everything without asking you. Because of that, my wish has become empty.
essence: A decision made without asking can hollow out the heart that made it.
simple_meaning: Dasharath insists he acted without consulting Bharata and that no one else pushed him into it. He admits the result has left his wish empty.
insight: It shows how acting without consultation can turn intention into regret.
modern_relevance: You send the message, make the decision, and only later realize you never checked with the person most affected. The damage is done before the explanation begins.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: रिस परिहरु अब मंगल साजू। कछु दिन गएँ भरत जुबराजू॥ एकहि बात मोहि दुखु लागा। बर दूसर असमंजस मागा ॥
translation: अब क्रोध छोड़ दे और मंगल साज सज। कुछ ही दिनों बाद भरत युवराज हो जाएँगे। एक ही बात का मुझे दुःख लगा कि तूने दूसरा वरदान बड़ी अड़चन का माँगा ॥
english_translation: Leave anger now and prepare for auspiciousness. In a few days, Bharata will be crowned crown prince. Only one thing caused me sorrow: you asked for the second boon in a way that created such trouble.
essence: A single strained request can poison an entire household.
simple_meaning: Dasharath tells Kaikeyi to drop her anger and get ready for the celebration, saying Bharata will soon become crown prince. He also says her second boon caused him pain because it created this crisis.
insight: It shifts attention from the demand to the emotional fallout that follows it.
modern_relevance: A parent hears one more impossible demand in the middle of a family argument, and knows the damage is already done. The real pain is not the request itself, but the confusion it creates.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: अजहूँ हृदय जरत तेहि आँचा। रिस परिहास कि साँचेहुँ साँचा॥ कहु तजि रोषु राम अपराधू। सबु कोउ कहइ रामु सुठि साधू ॥
translation: उसकी आँच से अब भी मेरा हृदय जल रहा है। यह दिल्लगी में, क्रोध में अथवा सचमुच ही (वास्तव में) सच्चा है? क्रोध को त्यागकर राम का अपराध तो बता। सब कोई तो कहते हैं कि राम बड़े ही साधु हैं ॥
english_translation: My heart still burns from that sting. Was it a joke, anger, or truly real? Set aside your rage and tell me Ram’s fault. Everyone says Ram is very noble.
essence: Hurt mind makes suspicion feel like proof.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is still hurt and asks whether the earlier words were a joke or truly meant. She tells Manthara to drop the anger and explain what fault Ram has, since everyone praises him as noble.
insight: It shows how wounded attention turns into doubt and searches for fault even where none is clear.
modern_relevance: You replay a text message for the tenth time, trying to decide whether it was careless or cruel. The hurt becomes its own evidence, and suspicion starts writing the story for you.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: तुहूँ सराहसि करसि सनेहू। अब सुनि मोहि भयउ संदेहू॥ जासु सुभाउ अरिहि अनूकूला। सो किमि करिहि मातु प्रतिकूला ॥
translation: तू स्वयं भी राम की सराहना करती और उन पर स्नेह किया करती थी। अब यह सुनकर मुझे संदेह हो गया है (कि तुम्हारी प्रशंसा और स्नेह कहीं झूठे तो न थे?) जिसका स्वभाव शत्रु को भी अनूकल है, वह माता के प्रतिकूल आचरण क्यों कर करेगा? ॥
english_translation: You yourself used to praise Ram and love him. Hearing this now, I have begun to doubt you. How could one whose nature is kind even to an enemy act against his mother?
essence: Kindness to all makes betrayal harder to believe.
simple_meaning: Dasharath remembers Kaikeyi's earlier love for Ram and cannot reconcile it with her present demand. He reasons that someone naturally kind, even to enemies, would not act against her own family.
insight: It shifts judgment from the latest outburst to the deeper pattern of a person’s conduct.
modern_relevance: Someone who once stood by you now speaks coldly in a family group chat. You replay every kind moment and wonder which version was real. The verse catches that painful disbelief.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: प्रिया हास रिस परिहरहि मागु बिचारि बिबेकु। जेहिं देखौं अब नयन भरि भरत राज अभिषेकु ॥
translation: हे प्रिये! हँसी और क्रोध छोड़ दे और विवेक (उचित-अनुचित) विचारकर वर माँग, जिससे अब मैं नेत्र भरकर भरत का राज्याभिषेक देख सकूँ ॥
english_translation: Beloved, set aside laughter and anger. Think with discernment and ask for a boon so that I may see Bharata's coronation with my own eyes.
essence: Discernment should guide desire before desire becomes damage.
simple_meaning: Dasharath asks Kaikeyi to stop joking or getting angry and to think carefully before asking for a boon. He wants to witness Bharata's coronation with joy.
insight: It teaches you to choose discernment over emotional heat before making a life-altering request.
modern_relevance: You can feel a conversation turning wrong before the words land. One person asks for calm and clarity, not knowing the request itself will change everything.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: जिऐ मीन बरु बारि बिहीना। मनि बिनु फनिकु जिऐ दुख दीना॥ कहउँ सुभाउ न छलु मन माहीं। जीवनु मोर राम बिनु नाहीं ॥
translation: मछली चाहे बिना पानी के जीती रहे और साँप भी चाहे बिना मणि के दीन-दुःखी होकर जीता रहे, परन्तु मैं स्वभाव से ही कहता हूँ, मन में (जरा भी) छल रखकर नहीं कि मेरा जीवन राम के बिना नहीं है ॥
english_translation: A fish may live without water, and a serpent may live miserably without its jewel; I speak my nature without any deceit in my mind: my life cannot exist without Ram.
essence: Ram is not an ornament to life; he is the life that remains.
simple_meaning: Dasharath says that just as some beings cannot live without what sustains them, he cannot live without Ram. He speaks plainly, without deceit, from his true feeling.
insight: It shifts devotion from idea to dependence: Ram is not praised from a distance, but felt as necessary for life.
modern_relevance: You watch someone leave the house after a fight, and the room feels hollow. Some bonds are not optional comforts; they are the shape of your whole day.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: समुझि देखु जियँ प्रिया प्रबीना। जीवनु राम दरस आधीना॥ सुनि मृदु बचन कुमति अति जरई। मनहुँ अनल आहुति घृत परई ॥
translation: हे चतुर प्रिये! जी में समझ देख, मेरा जीवन श्री राम के दर्शन के अधीन है। राजा के कोमल वचन सुनकर दुर्बुद्धि कैकेयी अत्यन्त जल रही है। मानो अग्नि में घी की आहुतियाँ पड़ रही हैं ॥
english_translation: “Understand this, wise one, in your heart: my life depends on seeing Ram. Hearing the king’s gentle words, Kaikeyi’s bad sense burned fiercely, as if ghee were poured into a fire.”
essence: A heart ruled by craving burns brighter when touched by tenderness.
simple_meaning: Dasharath tells Kaikeyi that his life depends on seeing Ram. Her hearing his gentle words only makes her selfish thinking burn hotter.
insight: It shows how a mind ruled by craving turns even kindness into fuel for harm.
modern_relevance: A parent speaks gently, hoping to calm a tense home. Instead, the wrong desire in one person flares up harder. Not every soft word soothes; some only expose what is already burning.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: कहइ करहु किन कोटि उपाया। इहाँ न लागिहि राउरि माया॥ देहु कि लेहु अजसु करि नाहीं। मोहि न बहुत प्रपंच सोहाहीं ॥
translation: (कैकेयी कहती है-) आप करोड़ों उपाय क्यों न करें, यहाँ आपकी माया (चालबाजी) नहीं लगेगी। या तो मैंने जो माँगा है सो दीजिए, नहीं तो 'नाहीं' करके अपयश लीजिए। मुझे बहुत प्रपंच (बखेड़े) नहीं सुहाते ॥
english_translation: (Kaikeyi said:) You may try millions of tricks, but your magic will not work here. Give me what I asked for, or take the shame of refusal. I do not like endless scheming.
essence: Demand without reflection turns into hard refusal.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi refuses delay and manipulation. She wants the demand fulfilled now, or she wants the shame of refusal openly accepted.
insight: It exposes how desire becomes rigid when it refuses reflection and only wants immediate satisfaction.
modern_relevance: You are in a tense family argument and someone keeps changing the subject, hoping the storm will pass. Kaikeyi’s voice is the opposite of that drift: name the demand, face the cost, stop hiding behind words.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: रामु साधु तुम्ह साधु सयाने। राममातु भलि सब पहिचाने॥ जस कौसिलाँ मोर भल ताका। तस फलु उन्हहि देउँ करि साका ॥
translation: राम साधु हैं, आप सयाने साधु हैं और राम की माता भी भली है, मैंने सबको पहचान लिया है। कौसल्या ने मेरा जैसा भला चाहा है, मैं भी साका करके (याद रखने योग्य) उन्हें वैसा ही फल दूँगी ॥
english_translation: Ram is noble; you are a wise noble woman. Ram's mother is also good, and I have understood all of you. Kaushalya wished me well, so I will repay her with the same kindness, in a memorable way.
essence: Kind words can conceal a binding demand.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi flatters Ram, Sita? No—she speaks of Ram, the wise listener, and Kaushalya, saying she has understood everyone and will answer good with good.
insight: It teaches you to notice when courtesy is being used to mask leverage and emotional pressure.
modern_relevance: Someone smiles warmly in a family meeting while quietly keeping score. The room feels civil, but every sentence is carrying a hidden invoice.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: होत प्रात मुनिबेष धरि जौं न रामु बन जाहिं। मोर मरनु राउर अजस नृप समुझिअ मन माहिं ॥
translation: (सबेरा होते ही मुनि का वेष धारण कर यदि राम वन को नहीं जाते, तो हे राजन् ! मन में (निश्चय) समझ लीजिए कि मेरा मरना होगा और आपका अपयश! ॥
english_translation: If, by dawn, Rama does not leave for the forest in the guise of a sage, then understand in your heart that I will die and you will be disgraced.
essence: Urgency turns a demand into a trap.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi sets a deadline: if Rama does not go to the forest by dawn, she says she will die and the king will be shamed.
insight: It shows how coercion works: urgency, shame, and emotional blackmail narrow another person's choices.
modern_relevance: A tense conversation turns into a deadline at midnight: either the decision happens now, or consequences follow by morning. Pressure can make a request feel like a threat.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: अस कहि कुटिल भई उठि ठाढ़ी। मानहुँ रोष तरंगिनि बाढ़ी॥ पाप पहार प्रगट भइ सोई। भरी क्रोध जल जाइ न जोई ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर कुटिल कैकेयी उठ खड़ी हुई, मानो क्रोध की नदी उमड़ी हो। वह नदी पाप रूपी पहाड़ से प्रकट हुई है और क्रोध रूपी जल से भरी है, (ऐसी भयानक है कि) देखी नहीं जाती! ॥
english_translation: After saying this, crooked Kaikeyi stood up, as if a river of anger had swelled. It seemed to rise from a mountain of sin, full of the water of rage, too dreadful to look at.
essence: Anger can rise so fully that it takes a person over.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi rises in a surge of anger, and the poet compares her fury to a terrifying river born from a mountain of wrongdoing.
insight: It teaches you to notice rage before it becomes action and starts reshaping everything around it.
modern_relevance: You hit send on the message while your chest is still hot. Ten minutes later, you can already see the damage. Anger feels powerful right before it becomes irreversible.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दोउ बर कूल कठिन हठ धारा। भवँर कूबरी बचन प्रचारा॥ ढाहत भूपरूप तरु मूला। चली बिपति बारिधि अनूकूला ॥
translation: दोनों वरदान उस नदी के दो किनारे हैं, कैकेयी का कठिन हठ ही उसकी (तीव्र) धारा है और कुबरी (मंथरा) के वचनों की प्रेरणा ही भँवर है। (वह क्रोध रूपी नदी) राजा दशरथ रूपी वृक्ष को जड़-मूल से ढहाती हुई विपत्ति रूपी समुद्र की ओर (सीधी) चली है ॥
english_translation: The two boons are the river's two banks; Kaikeyi's hard stubbornness is its current, and Manthara's words are its whirlpool. That river of disaster rushes straight on, uprooting King Dasharath like a tree and flowing toward the sea of calamity.
essence: Stubborn desire plus bad counsel can uproot even a king.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi's stubbornness and Manthara's urging are pictured as a river of disaster. Together they are pulling Dasharath toward ruin.
insight: It teaches you to see how obsession and outside prompting can combine into irreversible harm.
modern_relevance: A friend keeps feeding your worst suspicion, and suddenly a simple disagreement becomes a family rupture. This verse shows how repeated pressure can carry a person straight into disaster.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लखी नरेस बात फुरि साँची। तिय मिस मीचु सीस पर नाची॥ गहि पद बिनय कीन्ह बैठारी। जनि दिनकर कुल होसि कुठारी ॥
translation: राजा ने समझ लिया कि बात सचमुच (वास्तव में) सच्ची है, स्त्री के बहाने मेरी मृत्यु ही सिर पर नाच रही है। (तदनन्तर राजा ने कैकेयी के) चरण पकड़कर उसे बिठाकर विनती की कि तू सूर्यकुल (रूपी वृक्ष) के लिए कुल्हाड़ी मत बन ॥
english_translation: The king understood the truth was real: death itself was dancing over his head because of a woman. He held her feet, made her sit down, and pleaded, "Do not become the axe for the solar dynasty."
essence: Denial breaks, and the full cost becomes visible.
simple_meaning: Dasharath realizes Kaikeyi's demand is truly deadly for his family. He begs her not to become the instrument that cuts down the solar dynasty.
insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to clear-eyed recognition of loss.
modern_relevance: You read the text message twice, then a third time. The meaning finally lands, and your stomach drops because the damage is no longer hypothetical.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मागु माथ अबहीं देउँ तोही। राम बिरहँ जनि मारसि मोही॥ राखु राम कहुँ जेहि तेहि भाँती। नाहिं त जरिहि जनम भरि छाती ॥
translation: तू मेरा मस्तक माँग ले, मैं तुझे अभी दे दूँ। पर राम के विरह में मुझे मत मार। जिस किसी प्रकार से हो तू राम को रख ले। नहीं तो जन्मभर तेरी छाती जलेगी ॥
english_translation: Take my head right now, and I will give it to you. But do not kill me with separation from Ram. Keep Ram somehow, any way you can. Otherwise your chest will burn for this whole birth.
essence: Separation from Ram burns more than death itself.
simple_meaning: Dasharath offers his head, but begs not to be destroyed by separation from Ram. He wants Ram preserved by any means, or the pain will last his whole life.
insight: It shifts attention from bargaining with pain to seeing how completely love has anchored the heart.
modern_relevance: You stare at a hospital corridor, ready to trade anything for one more hour with someone you love. Some losses cannot be negotiated with; they only expose the depth of attachment.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: देखी ब्याधि असाध नृपु परेउ धरनि धुनि माथ। कहत परम आरत बचन राम राम रघुनाथ ॥
translation: राजा ने देखा कि रोग असाध्य है, तब वे अत्यन्त आर्तवाणी से 'हा राम! हा राम! हा रघुनाथ!' कहते हुए सिर पीटकर जमीन पर गिर पड़े ॥
english_translation: Seeing the incurable illness, the king fell to the ground, striking his head, and cried out in utter distress, 'Ram, Ram, Raghunath!'
essence: Grief strips away power and leaves only the name the heart can hold.
simple_meaning: The king sees that the illness cannot be cured and collapses in grief, crying out Ram's name again and again.
insight: It shifts attention from control to refuge when suffering becomes unbearable.
modern_relevance: You get a call from the hospital and suddenly the room goes silent. In that instant, the mind drops its arguments and reaches for the one presence it trusts.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ब्याकुल राउ सिथिल सब गाता। करिनि कलपतरु मनहुँ निपाता॥ कंठु सूख मुख आव न बानी। जनु पाठीनु दीन बिनु पानी ॥
translation: राजा व्याकुल हो गए, उनका सारा शरीर शिथिल पड़ गया, मानो हथिनी ने कल्पवृक्ष को उखाड़ फेंका हो। कंठ सूख गया, मुख से बात नहीं निकलती, मानो पानी के बिना पहिना नामक मछली तड़प रही हो ॥
english_translation: King Dasharath became distressed; his whole body went limp, as if a female elephant had uprooted a wish-fulfilling tree. His throat dried up and no words came from his mouth, like a fish gasping without water.
essence: Grief can leave even a king wordless and weak.
simple_meaning: Dasharath is overcome with grief. His body weakens, his throat dries, and he cannot speak.
insight: It shifts attention from dramatic reaction to the bodily reality of sorrow.
modern_relevance: You get the message late at night and just sit on the edge of the bed, unable to answer anyone. Grief can make the body fail before the words arrive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि कह कटु कठोर कैकेई। मनहुँ घाय महुँ माहुर देई॥ जौं अंतहुँ अस करतबु रहेऊ। मागु मागु तुम्ह केहिं बल कहेऊ ॥
translation: कैकेयी फिर कड़वे और कठोर वचन बोली, मानो घाव में जहर भर रही हो। (कहती है-) जो अंत में ऐसा ही करना था, तो आपने 'माँग, माँग' किस बल पर कहा था? ॥
english_translation: Kaikeyi spoke again with bitter, harsh words, as if pouring poison into a wound. She said, "If you meant to do this in the end, on what strength did you say, 'Ask, ask'?"
essence: Cruel speech can make a wound deeper than the wound itself.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi speaks cruelly to Dasharath, accusing him of weakness and hypocrisy after his promise to grant her boons.
insight: It shifts attention from the content of blame to the damage caused by a hardened mind.
modern_relevance: A family argument reaches the point where one person is already hurting and the other keeps pressing harder. At that moment, the issue is no longer the problem itself — it is the cruelty of how it is spoken.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: दुइ कि होइ एक समय भुआला। हँसब ठठाइ फुलाउब गाला॥ दानि कहाउब अरु कृपनाई। होइ कि खेम कुसल रौताई ॥
translation: हे राजा! ठहाका मारकर हँसना और गाल फुलाना- क्या ये दोनों एक साथ हो सकते हैं? दानी भी कहाना और कंजूसी भी करना। क्या रजपूती में क्षेम-कुशल भी रह सकती है?(लड़ाई में बहादुरी भी दिखावें और कहीं चोट भी न लगे!) ॥
english_translation: Can two opposite things happen at the same time? Can one laugh loudly and still puff out the cheeks? Can one claim generosity and still be stingy? Can royal courage remain intact while fear and harm are both avoided?
essence: Contradictory claims collapse when conduct reveals the truth.
simple_meaning: A person cannot claim opposite qualities at the same time. The verse warns that courage, generosity, and dignity must be real, not just spoken about.
insight: It pushes the mind toward consistency: say what you mean, and let conduct match the claim.
modern_relevance: A manager says she values honesty, then hides the real reason for a layoff. The room feels the split instantly. This verse cuts through that kind of double speech and demands one clean position.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: छाड़हु बचनु कि धीरजु धरहू। जनि अबला जिमि करुना करहू॥ तनु तिय तनय धामु धनु धरनी। सत्यसंध कहुँ तृन सम बरनी ॥
translation: या तो वचन (प्रतिज्ञा) ही छोड़ दीजिए या धैर्य धारण कीजिए। यों असहाय स्त्री की भाँति रोइए-पीटिए नहीं। सत्यव्रती के लिए तो शरीर, स्त्री, पुत्र, घर, धन और पृथ्वी- सब तिनके के बराबर कहे गए हैं ॥
english_translation: Either give up your promise or hold your composure. Do not cry and lament like a helpless woman. For one who keeps truth, body, wife, son, home, wealth, and land are all as small as blades of grass.
essence: Truth demands steadiness, not sentimental collapse.
simple_meaning: Keep your promise or keep your composure. A person bound to truth must treat body, family, wealth, and land as small as grass.
insight: It shifts the mind from emotional collapse to moral consistency under pressure.
modern_relevance: You promised something in a meeting, then panic hit the moment it became costly. This verse cuts through the drama: either own the promise or admit you will not keep it.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: मरम बचन सुनि राउ कह कहु कछु दोषु न तोर। लागेउ तोहि पिसाच जिमि कालु कहावत मोर ॥
translation: कैकेयी के मर्मभेदी वचन सुनकर राजा ने कहा कि तू जो चाहे कह, तेरा कुछ भी दोष नहीं है। मेरा काल तुझे मानो पिशाच होकर लग गया है, वही तुझसे यह सब कहला रहा है ॥
english_translation: Hearing Kaikeyi's piercing words, the king said, “Say what you wish; no fault is yours. My death itself has come upon you like a demon, making you speak like this.”
essence: Grief can silence blame and make death feel present.
simple_meaning: Dasharath hears Kaikeyi's cruel demand and refuses to blame her. He says his own death has overtaken him, as if a dark force has possessed the moment.
insight: It shifts the mind from blame to helpless recognition of a loss already in motion.
modern_relevance: You get the message that changes everything, and your first reaction is not anger but stunned surrender. The argument is over before it begins.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: चहत न भरत भूपतहि भोरें। बिधि बस कुमति बसी जिय तोरें॥ सो सबु मोर पाप परिनामू। भयउ कुठाहर जेहिं बिधि बामू॥
translation: भरत तो भूलकर भी राजपद नहीं चाहते। होनहारवश तेरे ही जी में कुमति आ बसी। यह सब मेरे पापों का परिणाम है, जिससे कुसमय (बेमौके) में विधाता विपरीत हो गया ॥
english_translation: Bharat does not want kingship, not even in his sleep. Fate placed crooked thinking in your heart. All this is the result of my own sins, by which the times turned against me.
essence: Bharat never wanted power; the disaster came from crooked desire.
simple_meaning: Bharat does not want the throne at all. The queen sees the disaster as the result of her own wrongdoing and says fate has turned against her.
insight: It shifts blame inward and exposes how desire can distort judgment and invite regret.
modern_relevance: After the argument is over, you replay every sentence and realise the damage came from one selfish decision. The shame is not abstract anymore; it has a name and a face.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुबस बसिहि फिरि अवध सुहाई। सब गुन धाम राम प्रभुताई॥ करिहहिं भाइ सकल सेवकाई। होइहि तिहुँ पुर राम बड़ाई ॥
translation: (तेरी उजाड़ी हुई) यह सुंदर अयोध्या फिर भलीभाँति बसेगी और समस्त गुणों के धाम श्री राम की प्रभुता भी होगी। सब भाई उनकी सेवा करेंगे और तीनों लोकों में श्री राम की बड़ाई होगी ॥
english_translation: Beautiful Ayodhya will be restored again, and Ram, the abode of all virtues, will reign there. All the brothers will serve him, and Ram's glory will spread through the three worlds.
essence: Ram's rightful presence restores the home and gives every brother a place in service.
simple_meaning: Ayodhya will be restored under Ram's rule. His brothers will serve him, and his greatness will be known everywhere.
insight: It shifts attention from personal gain to restored harmony around a worthy center.
modern_relevance: A family home after a bitter fight can feel ruined. Then one person starts cleaning, another starts cooking, and slowly the place feels livable again. Order returns when everyone gives themselves to the right center.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: तोर कलंकु मोर पछिताऊ। मुएहुँ न मिटिहि न जाइहि काऊ॥ अब तोहि नीक लाग करु सोई। लोचन ओट बैठु मुहु गोई ॥
translation: केवल तेरा कलंक और मेरा पछतावा मरने पर भी नहीं मिटेगा, यह किसी तरह नहीं जाएगा। अब तुझे जो अच्छा लगे वही कर। मुँह छिपाकर मेरी आँखों की ओट जा बैठ (अर्थात मेरे सामने से हट जा, मुझे मुँह न दिखा) ॥
english_translation: Your disgrace and my regret will not disappear, even in death. Do what you think best now. Hide your face and sit out of my sight.
essence: Some pain cannot be repaired; it can only be faced and endured.
simple_meaning: The speaker says this shame and regret can never be undone. So the other person should do whatever seems best and leave the speaker's sight.
insight: It shifts the mind from arguing for repair to acknowledging irreversible hurt and creating distance.
modern_relevance: After a family argument, one person sits in the kitchen long after midnight, unable to fix what was said. The only honest thing left is to ask for space before more damage is done.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जब लगि जिऔं कहउँ कर जोरी। तब लगि जनि कछु कहसि बहोरी॥ फिरि पछितैहसि अंत अभागी। मारसि गाइ नहारू लागी ॥
translation: मैं हाथ जोड़कर कहता हूँ कि जब तक मैं जीता रहूँ, तब तक फिर कुछ न कहना (अर्थात मुझसे न बोलना)। अरी अभागिनी! फिर तू अन्त में पछताएगी जो तू नहारू (ताँत) के लिए गाय को मार रही है ॥
english_translation: As long as I live, I beg you with folded hands, do not say another word. You wretched woman will regret it in the end, killing a cow for the sake of a thread.
essence: Small gain, ignored warning, lasting regret.
simple_meaning: Ravana begs the other person to stop speaking and warns that this harmful choice will bring regret later.
insight: It shows how ego refuses correction and turns a small desire into a destructive choice.
modern_relevance: You are one message away from saying something irreversible, but your anger is louder than your judgment. Later, the cost will feel much bigger than the victory.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: परेउ राउ कहि कोटि बिधि काहे करसि निदानु। कपट सयानि न कहति कछु जागति मनहुँ मसानु ॥
translation: राजा करोड़ों प्रकार से (बहुत तरह से) समझाकर (और यह कहकर) कि तू क्यों सर्वनाश कर रही है, पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े। पर कपट करने में चतुर कैकेयी कुछ बोलती नहीं, मानो (मौन होकर) मसान जगा रही हो (श्मशान में बैठकर प्रेतमंत्र सिद्ध कर रही हो) ॥
english_translation: King Dasharath fell to the ground, saying, “Why are you bringing ruin?” Cunning Kaikeyi said nothing, as if she sat in a cremation ground, awakening dark rites.
essence: Some silences confirm ruin more clearly than words.
simple_meaning: Dasharath collapses, pleading with Kaikeyi to stop the destruction, but she stays silent and unmoved.
insight: It shows how to recognize a moment when persuasion has ended and damage has begun.
modern_relevance: You are pleading in a kitchen at midnight, asking someone not to say the thing that will break everyone. They go quiet, and that silence says the decision is already made.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम राम रट बिकल भुआलू। जनु बिनु पंख बिहंग बेहालू॥ हृदयँ मनाव भोरु जनि होई। रामहि जाइ कहै जनि कोई ॥
translation: राजा 'राम-राम' रट रहे हैं और ऐसे व्याकुल हैं, जैसे कोई पक्षी पंख के बिना बेहाल हो। वे अपने हृदय में मनाते हैं कि सबेरा न हो और कोई जाकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी से यह बात न कहे ॥
english_translation: King Dasharath cries, "Ram, Ram," and is as helpless as a bird without wings. In his heart he begs that dawn not come, so no one goes to tell Ram.
essence: Grief clings to the beloved's name and fears the coming day.
simple_meaning: Dasharath is overwhelmed with grief. He keeps repeating Ram's name and fears the morning, because dawn would bring the news to Ram.
insight: It shows grief as helplessness, not drama, and reveals how love can make even morning feel threatening.
modern_relevance: You stare at your phone before sunrise, dreading the message that will change everything. Part of you wants the morning to stay away a little longer.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उदउ करहु जनि रबि रघुकुल गुर। अवध बिलोकि सूल होइहि उर॥ भूप प्रीति कैकइ कठिनाई। उभय अवधि बिधि रची बनाई ॥
translation: हे रघुकुल के गुरु (बड़ेरे, मूलपुरुष) सूर्य भगवान् ! आप अपना उदय न करें। अयोध्या को (बेहाल) देखकर आपके हृदय में बड़ी पीड़ा होगी। राजा की प्रीति और कैकेयी की निष्ठुरता दोनों को ब्रह्मा ने सीमा तक रचकर बनाया है (अर्थात राजा प्रेम की सीमा है और कैकेयी निष्ठुरता की) ॥
english_translation: O sun, guru of the Raghu clan, do not rise. If you look upon Ayodhya, grief will fill your heart. The king's love and Kaikeyi's harshness were both fashioned by fate to their limit.
essence: Even sunrise feels painful when grief has taken over the heart.
simple_meaning: The poet begs the sun not to rise, because dawn will only deepen the king's grief over Ayodhya, love, and Kaikeyi's cruelty.
insight: It turns dawn into a measure of grief, showing how the world can feel cruel when the heart is broken.
modern_relevance: You wake before sunrise after a night of bad news, staring at the ceiling because morning means facing the same wound again. The day arrives, but your heart is not ready.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिलपत नृपहि भयउ भिनुसारा। बीना बेनु संख धुनि द्वारा॥ पढ़हिं भाट गुन गावहिं गायक। सुनत नृपहि जनु लागहिं सायक ॥
translation: विलाप करते-करते ही राजा को सबेरा हो गया! राज द्वार पर वीणा, बाँसुरी और शंख की ध्वनि होने लगी। भाट लोग विरुदावली पढ़ रहे हैं और गवैये गुणों का गान कर रहे हैं। सुनने पर राजा को वे बाण जैसे लगते हैं ॥
english_translation: Wailing, the king was overtaken by dawn. At the gate, the sounds of veena, flute, and conch arose. Bards recited praises and singers sang his virtues. Hearing them, the king felt as if arrows struck him.
essence: Joy becomes an arrow when the heart is already wounded.
simple_meaning: The king keeps grieving until morning arrives. Festive sounds and praise at the palace gate only deepen his pain, because everything reminds him of Ram's exile.
insight: It shows how sorrow can make ordinary joy feel painful and intrusive.
modern_relevance: You hear wedding drums from the next street while sitting in a silent room after bad news. The world keeps celebrating, but your chest cannot join it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंगल सकल सोहाहिं न कैसें। सहगामिनिहि बिभूषन जैसें॥ तेहि निसि नीद परी नहिं काहू। राम दरस लालसा उछाहू ॥
translation: राजा को ये सब मंगल साज कैसे नहीं सुहा रहे हैं, जैसे पति के साथ सती होने वाली स्त्री को आभूषण! श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन की लालसा और उत्साह के कारण उस रात्रि में किसी को भी नींद नहीं आई ॥
english_translation: How can all these auspicious decorations please the king, like ornaments on a woman going with her husband onto the funeral pyre? That night no one slept, because longing to see Ram and excitement kept everyone awake.
essence: Longing for Ram turns celebration into wakeful waiting.
simple_meaning: The usual signs of celebration do not feel festive here. Everyone stays awake through the night, held by longing and excitement for Ram's sight.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the emotional charge of anticipation.
modern_relevance: You refresh your phone all night before someone you love arrives at the airport. The room is ready, the bags are packed, but sleep won't come because the waiting itself has become alive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: द्वार भीर सेवक सचिव कहहिं उदित रबि देखि। जागेउ अजहुँ न अवधपति कारनु कवनु बिसेषि ॥
translation: राजद्वार पर मंत्रियों और सेवकों की भीड़ लगी है। वे सब सूर्य को उदय हुआ देखकर कहते हैं कि ऐसा कौन सा विशेष कारण है कि अवधपति दशरथजी अभी तक नहीं जागे? ॥
english_translation: The ministers and servants crowd the palace gate, and seeing the sun rise, they wonder what special reason keeps the king of Ayodhya from waking.
essence: A broken routine can announce hidden grief.
simple_meaning: The ministers and servants gather at the palace gate and notice that Dasharath has not woken up, which is unusual for him.
insight: It trains attention on small disruptions that reveal larger emotional or physical crisis.
modern_relevance: You check your phone at sunrise and see no reply from the person who always answers by dawn. The silence itself becomes the warning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पछिले पहर भूपु नित जागा। आजु हमहि बड़ अचरजु लागा॥ जाहु सुमंत्र जगावहु जाई। कीजिअ काजु रजायसु पाई ॥
translation: राजा नित्य ही रात के पिछले पहर जाग जाया करते हैं, किन्तु आज हमें बड़ा आश्चर्य हो रहा है। हे सुमंत्र! जाओ, जाकर राजा को जगाओ। उनकी आज्ञा पाकर हम सब काम करें ॥
english_translation: The king always woke in the last watch of the night, but today we are greatly surprised. Go, Sumantra, wake him and return. We will do the work after receiving his command.
essence: A ruler’s missing morning breaks the rhythm of the whole kingdom.
simple_meaning: The king usually woke before dawn, so everyone is shocked that he has not risen. They ask Sumantra to wake him so they can begin their work only after his command.
insight: It turns ordinary routine into a signal that the household’s order has begun to break.
modern_relevance: You open the office chat and see the one person who always replies first has gone silent. The whole team feels it at once: something is off before anyone says a word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गए सुमंत्रु तब राउर माहीं। देखि भयावन जात डेराहीं॥ धाइ खाई जनु जाइ न हेरा। मानहुँ बिपति बिषाद बसेरा ॥
translation: तब सुमंत्र रावले (राजमहल) में गए, पर महल को भयानक देखकर वे जाते हुए डर रहे हैं। (ऐसा लगता है) मानो दौड़कर काट खाएगा, उसकी ओर देखा भी नहीं जाता। मानो विपत्ति और विषाद ने वहाँ डेरा डाल रखा हो ॥
english_translation: Then Sumantra entered the royal palace, but the sight of it was so fearsome that he went in trembling. It was as if something would bite him if he rushed forward; no one could even bear to look at it. It seemed as though disaster and sorrow had made their home there.
essence: Grief can make a home feel uninhabitable.
simple_meaning: Sumantra enters the palace and feels fear and heaviness everywhere. The place itself seems filled with disaster and grief.
insight: It turns emotional atmosphere into something visible, showing how grief can change a place before any conversation begins.
modern_relevance: You walk into a house after a family argument and feel the silence before anyone says a word. The room itself seems to hold the hurt.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पूछें कोउ न ऊतरु देई। गए जेहिं भवन भूप कैकेई॥ कहि जयजीव बैठ सिरु नाई। देखि भूप गति गयउ सुखाई ॥
translation: पूछने पर कोई जवाब नहीं देता। वे उस महल में गए, जहाँ राजा और कैकेयी थे 'जय जीव' कहकर सिर नवाकर (वंदना करके) बैठे और राजा की दशा देखकर तो वे सूख ही गए ॥
english_translation: No one answers when asked. He entered the chamber where King Dasharath and Kaikeyi sat. Saying "Victory and long life," he bowed his head, and seeing the king's condition, he was dried up with shock.
essence: Silence and a broken face reveal the truth before speech does.
simple_meaning: No one gives Sumantra an answer. He enters the royal chamber, bows respectfully, and is stunned by the king's condition.
insight: It shifts attention from words to visible suffering, teaching the reader to read a room with compassion.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room and the air tells you everything before the family speaks. The face on the bed explains what no one is ready to say.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सोच बिकल बिबरन महि परेऊ। मानहु कमल मूलु परिहरेऊ॥ सचिउ सभीत सकइ नहिं पूँछी। बोली असुभ भरी सुभ छूँछी ॥
translation: (देखा कि-) राजा सोच से व्याकुल हैं, चेहरे का रंग उड़ गया है। जमीन पर ऐसे पड़े हैं, मानो कमल जड़ छोड़कर (जड़ से उखड़कर) (मुर्झाया) पड़ा हो। मंत्री मारे डर के कुछ पूछ नहीं सकते। तब अशुभ से भरी हुई और शुभ से विहीन कैकेयी बोली- ॥
english_translation: The king lay on the ground, pale and bewildered, like a lotus torn from its root. The ministers, afraid, could not ask anything. Then Kaikeyi, full of ill omen and empty of goodness, spoke.
essence: Grief can strip a king down to helplessness.
simple_meaning: Dasharath lies collapsed in grief, drained of life. His ministers are too frightened to speak, and Kaikeyi begins to talk with a dark, joyless heart.
insight: It shifts attention from outward authority to the inner collapse that fear and grief can cause.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room and see the strongest person in your family suddenly collapsed, unable to answer simple questions. Everyone lowers their voice because the room itself feels broken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परी न राजहि नीद निसि हेतु जान जगदीसु। रामु रामु रटि भोरु किय कहइ ना मरमु महीसु ॥
translation: राजा को रातभर नींद नहीं आई, इसका कारण जगदीश्वर ही जानें। इन्होंने 'राम राम' रटकर सबेरा कर दिया, परन्तु इसका भेद राजा कुछ भी नहीं बतलाते ॥
english_translation: The king did not sleep through the night; only the lord of the world knows why. He kept chanting "Ram, Ram" until dawn, yet the king revealed no secret.
essence: Grief can wake the whole night and still hide its cause.
simple_meaning: The king stayed awake all night, chanting Ram's name, but he would not reveal what was wrong.
insight: It captures grief before confession: the body shows the wound before words do.
modern_relevance: You lie awake after a message that changed everything, staring at the ceiling and repeating one name in your head. The truth is there, but you cannot say it yet.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आनहु रामहि बेगि बोलाई। समाचार तब पूँछेहु आई॥ चलेउ सुमंत्रु राय रुख जानी। लखी कुचालि कीन्हि कछु रानी ॥
translation: तुम जल्दी राम को बुला लाओ। तब आकर समाचार पूछना। राजा का रुख जानकर सुमंत्रजी चले, समझ गए कि रानी ने कुछ कुचाल की है ॥
english_translation: Bring Ram quickly. Then come back and ask about the news. Sumantra went, reading the king's mood, and realized the queen had done some mischief.
essence: Trouble is often visible before the truth is spoken.
simple_meaning: The king orders Ram to be called at once, and Sumantra notices that the queen has caused trouble.
insight: It trains attention to read tension and recognize hidden conflict early.
modern_relevance: A manager says, “Bring her in now, ask questions later,” and the room goes quiet. Everyone can feel something is wrong before the explanation arrives.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सोच बिकल मग परइ न पाऊ। रामहि बोलि कहिहि का राऊ॥ उर धरि धीरजु गयउ दुआरें। पूँछहिं सकल देखि मनु मारें ॥
translation: सुमंत्र सोच से व्याकुल हैं, रास्ते पर पैर नहीं पड़ता (आगे बढ़ा नहीं जाता), (सोचते हैं-) रामजी को बुलाकर राजा क्या कहेंगे? किसी तरह हृदय में धीरज धरकर वे द्वार पर गए। सब लोग उनको मन मारे (उदास) देखकर पूछने लगे ॥
english_translation: Sumantra was overwhelmed with worry and could not step forward. He thought, "What will the king say after calling Ram?" Holding his courage in his heart, he went to the door. Seeing him downcast, everyone began to ask him questions.
