modern_relevance: You prepare for a promotion, the date is set, the family is relieved — and then one sudden decision tears everything apart. The mind asks the same question: how did this happen?
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: निरखि राम रुख सचिवसुत कारनु कहेउ बुझाइ। सुनि प्रसंगु रहि मूक जिमि दसा बरनि नहिं जाइ ॥
translation: तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी का रुख देखकर मन्त्री के पुत्र ने सब कारण समझाकर कहा। उस प्रसंग को सुनकर वे गूँगी जैसी (चुप) रह गईं, उनकी दशा का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
english_translation: Then, seeing Ram's expression, the minister's son explained the reason. Hearing the whole matter, she became silent as if mute; her condition cannot be described.
essence: Some grief leaves no room for words.
simple_meaning: Hearing the explanation, she fell silent and was overwhelmed. Her pain was so deep that words could not capture it.
insight: It shifts attention from argument to emotional reality: some truths are understood only as pain, not as debate.
modern_relevance: You finally hear the full reason behind a decision that changes everything — a move, a breakup, a family choice. The explanation helps, but it does not soften the ache.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राखि न सकइ न कहि सक जाहू। दुहूँ भाँति उर दारुन दाहू॥ लिखत सुधाकर गा लिखि राहू। बिधि गति बाम सदा सब काहू ॥
translation: न रख ही सकती हैं, न यह कह सकती हैं कि वन चले जाओ। दोनों ही प्रकार से हृदय में बड़ा भारी संताप हो रहा है। (मन में सोचती हैं कि देखो-) विधाता की चाल सदा सबके लिए टेढ़ी होती है। लिखने लगे चन्द्रमा और लिखा गया राहु ॥
english_translation: She cannot keep him, and she cannot tell him to go to the forest. Both ways, her heart burns with terrible pain. Fate is always crooked for everyone: the moon was written, and Rahu came out.
essence: Love and duty can burn the heart from opposite sides.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is trapped between two impossible choices. She cannot hold on to Ram, and she cannot bear to send him away. Her heart burns with grief and confusion.
insight: It names the paralysis that comes when every option carries loss, and no choice feels clean.
modern_relevance: You are holding a phone after sending a message you cannot take back. One reply will wound someone, the other will wound you. The body knows what the mind cannot resolve.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: धरम सनेह उभयँ मति घेरी। भइ गति साँप छुछुंदरि केरी॥ राखउँ सुतहि करउँ अनुरोधू। धरमु जाइ अरु बंधु बिरोधू ॥
translation: धर्म और स्नेह दोनों ने कौसल्याजी की बुद्धि को घेर लिया। उनकी दशा साँप-छछूँदर की सी हो गई। वे सोचने लगीं कि यदि मैं अनुरोध (हठ) करके पुत्र को रख लेती हूँ तो धर्म जाता है और भाइयों में विरोध होता है, ॥
english_translation: Dharma and affection both surrounded Kaushalya's mind. She was in the state of a snake and a mongoose. If I insist and keep my son, duty is lost and there will be conflict among brothers.
essence: Love and duty can pull so hard that the mind freezes.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya feels torn between duty and love. Keeping her son would break dharma and create conflict among the brothers.
insight: It shifts the mind from choosing by emotion alone to weighing the deeper cost of each choice.
modern_relevance: You hold your phone after reading a message that could change everything. Replying honestly may hurt someone you love, but avoiding it would also be wrong. That split feeling is Kaushalya's moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहउँ जान बन तौ बड़ि हानी। संकट सोच बिबस भइ रानी॥ बहुरि समुझि तिय धरमु सयानी। रामु भरतु दोउ सुत सम जानी ॥
translation: और यदि वन जाने को कहती हूँ तो बड़ी हानि होती है। इस प्रकार के धर्मसंकट में पड़कर रानी विशेष रूप से सोच के वश हो गईं। फिर बुद्धिमती कौसल्याजी स्त्री धर्म (पातिव्रत धर्म) को समझकर और राम तथा भरत दोनों पुत्रों को समान जानकर- ॥
english_translation: If I tell him to go to the forest, it will be a great loss. Caught in this crisis of duty, the queen became helpless with thought. Then wise Kausalya reflected on a wife's duty and saw Ram and Bharat as equal sons.
essence: Wisdom begins when you stop demanding a choice without loss.
simple_meaning: Kausalya is torn between two harms: sending Ram away or keeping him back. She pauses, remembers her duty as a wife, and sees both Ram and Bharat as equally her sons.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeking a perfect outcome to facing a painful duty clearly.
modern_relevance: You’re on a call where either answer wounds someone you love. One option protects one relationship, the other protects another. The mind freezes until it can hold both losses without panic.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सरल सुभाउ राम महतारी। बोली बचन धीर धरि भारी॥ तात जाउँ बलि कीन्हेहु नीका। पितु आयसु सब धरमक टीका ॥
translation: सरल स्वभाव वाली श्री रामचन्द्रजी की माता बड़ा धीरज धरकर वचन बोलीं- हे तात! मैं बलिहारी जाती हूँ, तुमने अच्छा किया। पिता की आज्ञा का पालन करना ही सब धर्मों का शिरोमणि धर्म है ॥
english_translation: With a simple nature, Ram's mother spoke with great composure: "Dear son, I bless you. You have done well. Obeying a father's command is the crown of all righteousness."
essence: True duty can cost everything and still remain right.
simple_meaning: Kausalya praises Ram for obeying his father's command and says that keeping a parent's word is the highest duty.
insight: It shifts duty from burden to sacred priority, showing that obedience can be a conscious moral choice.
modern_relevance: Your parent asks for something that costs you dearly, and every part of you wants to refuse. Kausalya's answer is the opposite of convenience: some promises matter more than comfort, and keeping them can be an act of love.
speaker: Kausalya

verse_text: राजु देन कहिदीन्ह बनु मोहि न सो दुख लेसु। तुम्ह बिनु भरतहि भूपतिहि प्रजहि प्रचंड कलेसु ॥
translation: राज्य देने को कहकर वन दे दिया, उसका मुझे लेशमात्र भी दुःख नहीं है। (दुःख तो इस बात का है कि) तुम्हारे बिना भरत को, महाराज को और प्रजा को बड़ा भारी क्लेश होगा ॥
english_translation: I gave up the kingdom and sent myself to the forest; I feel no grief at all. The real pain is that, without you, Bharata, the king, and the people will suffer terribly.
essence: The loss is not the throne; it is the suffering left behind.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi says she does not grieve losing the kingdom. Her deeper sorrow is that Bharata, the king, and the people will suffer without Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from personal gain to the wider damage a decision can cause.
modern_relevance: You make a decision in a tense family meeting and feel certain at first. Later you realize the real cost was not your own comfort, but the strain it placed on everyone else.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: जौं केवल पितु आयसु ताता। तौ जनि जाहु जानि बड़ि माता॥ जौं पितु मातु कहेउ बन जाना। तौ कानन सत अवध समाना ॥
translation: हे तात! यदि केवल पिताजी की ही आज्ञा, हो तो माता को (पिता से) बड़ी जानकर वन को मत जाओ, किन्तु यदि पिता-माता दोनों ने वन जाने को कहा हो, तो वन तुम्हारे लिए सैकड़ों अयोध्या के समान है ॥
english_translation: O dear son, if only your father has commanded it, then do not go, regarding your mother as greater. But if both father and mother have told you to go to the forest, then the forest is as good as hundreds of Ayodhyas for you.
essence: A rightful command can turn exile into home.
simple_meaning: Kausalya tells Ram that if only his father ordered exile, he should stay for his mother’s sake. But if both parents agreed, the forest becomes as welcome as Ayodhya itself.
insight: It teaches you to weigh obligation by the full moral context, not by a single voice. Duty becomes steadier when it is confirmed from all sides.
modern_relevance: Your parent says one thing, your other parent another, and you stand frozen between loyalty and obligation. This verse knows that ache: the right choice becomes easier when the whole family’s truth is clear.
speaker: Kausalya

verse_text: पितु बनदेव मातु बनदेवी। खग मृग चरन सरोरुह सेवी॥ अंतहुँ उचित नृपहि बनबासू। बय बिलोकि हियँ होइ हराँसू ॥
translation: वन के देवता तुम्हारे पिता होंगे और वनदेवियाँ माता होंगी। वहाँ के पशु-पक्षी तुम्हारे चरणकमलों के सेवक होंगे। राजा के लिए अंत में तो वनवास करना उचित ही है। केवल तुम्हारी (सुकुमार) अवस्था देखकर हृदय में दुःख होता है ॥
english_translation: The forest would have your father as its deity and your mother as its goddess. The birds and animals there would serve your lotus feet. For a king, living in the forest is fitting in the end. Only your tender age makes my heart ache.
essence: The right path can still break the heart that loves you.
simple_meaning: The forest would welcome Ram like a royal home, and even its creatures would serve him. Yet Dasharath still grieves because Ram is so young.
insight: It separates what is fitting from what is emotionally bearable, showing that duty and tenderness can coexist.
modern_relevance: You tell yourself, "This will be good for me," while packing a child’s bag for a hard move. The decision may be right, and the ache may still be real.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बड़भागी बनु अवध अभागी। जो रघुबंसतिलक तुम्ह त्यागी॥ जौं सुत कहौं संग मोहि लेहू। तुम्हरे हृदयँ होइ संदेहू ॥
translation: हे रघुवंश के तिलक! वन बड़ा भाग्यवान है और यह अवध अभागा है, जिसे तुमने त्याग दिया। हे पुत्र! यदि मैं कहूँ कि मुझे भी साथ ले चलो तो तुम्हारे हृदय में संदेह होगा (कि माता इसी बहाने मुझे रोकना चाहती हैं) ॥
english_translation: O jewel of the Raghu line, the forest is fortunate and Ayodhya is unfortunate, for you have left it. If I say, 'Son, take me with you,' your heart will doubt me.
essence: Even a mother's plea can sound like a trap after trust breaks.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi says the forest is blessed because Ram will live there, while Ayodhya is unfortunate because it will lose him. She also says Ram may doubt her if she asks to go with him.
insight: It reveals how broken trust makes even loving words sound suspicious.
modern_relevance: You want to say, 'Let me come too,' but you already know the request will sound like control. Sometimes care arrives too late, after trust has cracked.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: पूत परम प्रिय तुम्ह सबही के। प्रान प्रान के जीवन जी के॥ ते तुम्ह कहहु मातु बन जाऊँ। मैं सुनि बचन बैठि पछिताऊँ ॥
translation: हे पुत्र! तुम सभी के परम प्रिय हो। प्राणों के प्राण और हृदय के जीवन हो। वही (प्राणाधार) तुम कहते हो कि माता! मैं वन को जाऊँ और मैं तुम्हारे वचनों को सुनकर बैठी पछताती हूँ! ॥
english_translation: O son, you are the dearest of all. You are the life of life, the very breath of our breath. And yet you say, “Mother, I must go to the forest,” and I sit here grieving after hearing your words.
essence: The dearest person can still be the hardest to let go.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi calls Ram the dearest life of everyone, then laments that he is still choosing exile. Her words carry both love and pain.
insight: It shows how affection can coexist with helpless grief, without turning into resistance or cruelty.
modern_relevance: You watch your child pack a bag for a long move, and every blessing feels like a small tear. Love does not always soften pain; sometimes it makes goodbye sharper.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: यह बिचारि नहिं करउँ हठ झूठ सनेहु बढ़ाइ। मानि मातु कर नात बलि सुरति बिसरि जनि जाइ ॥
translation: यह सोचकर झूठा स्नेह बढ़ाकर मैं हठ नहीं करती! बेटा! मैं बलैया लेती हूँ, माता का नाता मानकर मेरी सुध भूल न जाना ॥
english_translation: Thinking thus, I will not fake affection by stubbornness. Son, I bow to you; remembering your mother's bond, do not forget me.
essence: False affection cannot heal what truth must face.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi says she will not pretend affection or cling stubbornly. She accepts the bond of a mother and asks Ram not to forget her.
insight: It shifts the reader from possessive attachment to honest acceptance of what has already been set in motion.
modern_relevance: You realize a relationship is damaged, and the urge is to over-explain, over-text, and force warmth back into place. Sometimes the truest thing is a plain admission, without pretending everything is fine.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: देव पितर सब तुम्हहि गोसाईं। राखहुँ पलक नयन की नाईं॥ अवधि अंबु प्रिय परिजन मीना। तुम्ह करुनाकर धरम धुरीना ॥
translation: हे गोसाईं! सब देव और पितर तुम्हारी वैसी ही रक्षा करें, जैसे पलकें आँखों की रक्षा करती हैं। तुम्हारे वनवास की अवधि (चौदह वर्ष) जल है, प्रियजन और कुटुम्बी मछली हैं। तुम दया की खान और धर्म की धुरी को धारण करने वाले हो ॥
english_translation: May all the devas and ancestors protect you, O lord, as eyelids protect the eyes. Your exile is water; your loved ones and kin are fish in it. You are a mine of compassion and the bearer of dharma.
essence: Love blesses even the exile it cannot stop.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi blesses Ram and says his exile is like water, with his loved ones as fish in it. She calls him compassionate and steadfast in dharma.
insight: It shifts attention from the loss itself to the care that still surrounds it.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you love pack a bag for a long separation, and the room feels too small to hold it. What you offer is not logic, but blessing.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: अस बिचारि सोइ करहु उपाई। सबहि जिअत जेहिं भेंटहु आई॥ जाहु सुखेन बनहि बलि जाऊँ। करि अनाथ जन परिजन गाऊँ ॥
translation: ऐसा विचारकर वही उपाय करना, जिसमें सबके जीते जी तुम आ मिलो। मैं बलिहारी जाती हूँ, तुम सेवकों, परिवार वालों और नगर भर को अनाथ करके सुखपूर्वक वन को जाओ ॥
english_translation: Think of the way that lets everyone meet while still alive. I bless you: go peacefully to the forest, leaving your servants, family, and city orphaned.
essence: Love can release what it cannot keep.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi asks Ram to choose the path where everyone can meet while still alive, then sends him to the forest with painful resignation.
insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to closeness toward allowing the harder path that must unfold.
modern_relevance: You finally tell someone to take the job abroad, even though the house will feel empty without them. Love can bless the departure and still feel the loss.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: सब कर आजु सुकृत फल बीता। भयउ कराल कालु बिपरीता॥ बहुबिधि बिलपि चरन लपटानी। परम अभागिनि आपुहि जानी ॥
translation: आज सबके पुण्यों का फल पूरा हो गया। कठिन काल हमारे विपरीत हो गया। (इस प्रकार) बहुत विलाप करके और अपने को परम अभागिनी जानकर माता श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में लिपट गईं ॥
english_translation: Today the fruit of everyone's merit has been exhausted. Hard time has turned against us. After crying in many ways and seeing herself as most unfortunate, she clung to Ram's feet.
essence: Regret strips away excuses and leaves only remorse.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi feels that all good fortune has ended and disaster has turned against the family. In grief and self-blame, she clings to Ram's feet.
insight: It turns regret into self-recognition: the mind stops defending itself and sees the cost of its own choices.
modern_relevance: A message arrives and you instantly know your words, not the event, helped cause the damage. The stomach drops. Before any explanation, there is only regret and the need to face it.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: दारुन दुसह दाहु उर ब्यापा। बरनि न जाहिं बिलाप कलापा॥ राम उठाइ मातु उर लाई। कहि मृदु बचन बहुरि समुझाई ॥
translation: हृदय में भयानक दुःसह संताप छा गया। उस समय के बहुविध विलाप का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने माता को उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया और फिर कोमल वचन कहकर उन्हें समझाया ॥
english_translation: A terrible, unbearable grief seized the heart. No one could describe the many cries of mourning. Ram lifted his mother into his arms and gently comforted her with tender words.
essence: Grief needs embrace before explanation.
simple_meaning: Grief fills the heart so completely that words fail. Ram responds by holding his mother close and soothing her with gentle speech.
insight: It teaches you to meet grief with physical closeness and calm words instead of distance or analysis.
modern_relevance: When a family member breaks down in the kitchen after bad news, you do not need a perfect speech. Sometimes the healing starts when you hold them, stay near, and speak softly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समाचार तेहि समय सुनि सीय उठी अकुलाइ। जाइ सासु पद कमल जुग बंदि बैठि सिरु नाइ ॥
translation: उसी समय यह समाचार सुनकर सीताजी अकुला उठीं और सास के पास जाकर उनके दोनों चरणकमलों की वंदना कर सिर नीचा करके बैठ गईं ॥
english_translation: Hearing the news at that moment, Sita was overcome with anxiety. She went to her mother-in-law, bowed to her lotus feet, and sat with her head lowered.
essence: Distress need not erase humility.
simple_meaning: Hearing the news, Sita became distressed and immediately went to her mother-in-law, bowed respectfully, and sat down with her head lowered.
insight: It teaches grace under distress: respond first with respect, not impulse.
modern_relevance: You get a message that shakes you, but you still walk into the room, greet the elder properly, and hold yourself together before speaking.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दीन्हि असीस सासु मृदु बानी। अति सुकुमारि देखि अकुलानी॥ बैठि नमित मुख सोचति सीता। रूप रासि पति प्रेम पुनीता ॥
translation: सास ने कोमल वाणी से आशीर्वाद दिया। वे सीताजी को अत्यन्त सुकुमारी देखकर व्याकुल हो उठीं। रूप की राशि और पति के साथ पवित्र प्रेम करने वाली सीताजी नीचा मुख किए बैठी सोच रही हैं ॥
english_translation: Sita's mother-in-law gave her a gentle blessing. Seeing the very delicate Sita, she became distressed. Sita sat with her face lowered, thinking, a treasure of beauty and pure love for her husband.
essence: Love can sit quietly even when the world is breaking.
simple_meaning: Sita's mother-in-law blesses her gently, but worries when she sees how delicate Sita is. Sita sits quietly, bowed down, thinking of her pure love for her husband.
insight: It shifts attention from dramatic action to the quiet emotional weight carried in a family.
modern_relevance: You sit beside someone you love after bad news, trying to stay composed while your concern shows in every glance. Care and fear often speak at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चलन चहत बन जीवननाथू। केहि सुकृती सन होइहि साथू॥ की तनु प्रान कि केवल प्राना। बिधि करतबु कछु जाइ न जाना ॥
translation: जीवननाथ (प्राणनाथ) वन को चलना चाहते हैं। देखें किस पुण्यवान से उनका साथ होगा- शरीर और प्राण दोनों साथ जाएँगे या केवल प्राण ही से इनका साथ होगा? विधाता की करनी कुछ जानी नहीं जाती ॥
english_translation: The lord of my life wants to go to the forest. Who will be fortunate enough to go with him? Will both body and breath go together, or only breath? No one can know the workings of fate.
essence: Separation turns even breath into a question.
simple_meaning: Sita wonders who will accompany Ram into exile and whether she will go with both body and breath, or only her breath if she cannot follow.
insight: It shifts attention from logistics to the ache of devotion under uncertainty.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you love pack for a move you did not choose. Your mind races ahead of the goodbye, trying to measure how much of you can go with them.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: चारु चरन नख लेखति धरनी। नूपुर मुखर मधुर कबि बरनी॥ मनहुँ प्रेम बस बिनती करहीं। हमहि सीय पद जनि परिहरहीं ॥
translation: सीताजी अपने सुंदर चरणों के नखों से धरती कुरेद रही हैं। ऐसा करते समय नूपुरों का जो मधुर शब्द हो रहा है, कवि उसका इस प्रकार वर्णन करते हैं कि मानो प्रेम के वश होकर नूपुर यह विनती कर रहे हैं कि सीताजी के चरण कभी हमारा त्याग न करें ॥
english_translation: Sita scratches the earth with her lovely toenails. The poet says the anklets sound sweet, as if moved by love they are pleading, “Do not leave Sita’s feet.”
essence: Love makes even footsteps feel unwilling to part.
simple_meaning: Sita stands so delicately that even her anklets seem to beg not to be left behind by her feet.
insight: It teaches the mind to notice how love charges even ordinary movement with grief and devotion.
modern_relevance: You pack a bag before a hard goodbye and notice the smallest things: a shoe by the door, a bracelet on the table. Ordinary objects suddenly feel like they are asking not to be left behind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंजु बिलोचन मोचति बारी। बोली देखि राम महतारी॥ तात सुनहु सिय अति सुकुमारी। सास ससुर परिजनहि पिआरी ॥
translation: सीताजी सुंदर नेत्रों से जल बहा रही हैं। उनकी यह दशा देखकर श्री रामजी की माता कौसल्याजी बोलीं- हे तात! सुनो, सीता अत्यन्त ही सुकुमारी हैं तथा सास, ससुर और कुटुम्बी सभी को प्यारी हैं ॥
english_translation: Sita's beautiful eyes spill tears. Seeing this, Rama's mother Kaushalya said, “Listen, dear child: Sita is extremely delicate and beloved by her parents-in-law and family.”
essence: Gentleness deserves recognition, not correction.
simple_meaning: Sita is weeping softly, and Kaushalya comforts her by praising her gentle nature and her place in the family.
insight: It shifts attention from the tears themselves to the care that meets them.
modern_relevance: You see someone trying not to cry at a family gathering, and the room goes quiet. One gentle sentence can hold them together better than advice ever could.
speaker: Kaushalya

verse_text: पिता जनक भूपाल मनि ससुर भानुकुल भानु। पति रबिकुल कैरव बिपिन बिधु गुन रूप निधानु ॥
translation: इनके पिता जनकजी राजाओं के शिरोमणि हैं, ससुर सूर्यकुल के सूर्य हैं और पति सूर्यकुल रूपी कुमुदवन को खिलाने वाले चन्द्रमा तथा गुण और रूप के भंडार हैं ॥
english_translation: Janaka, the father, is the jewel among kings; the father-in-law is the sun of the solar line; the husband is the moon that makes the lotus grove of the solar line bloom, a storehouse of virtues and beauty.
essence: Honor surrounds the one who marries into a noble home.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya praises Janak, his lineage, and Ram as the perfect husband, full of virtues and beauty.
insight: It shifts attention from loss to the dignity already surrounding the relationship.
modern_relevance: You meet your partner’s parents for the first time and feel the quiet pressure to belong. A kind elder names the family with respect, and the room softens. Recognition can be its own blessing.
speaker: Kaushalya

verse_text: मैं पुनि पुत्रबधू प्रिय पाई। रूप रासि गुन सील सुहाई॥ नयन पुतरि करि प्रीति बढ़ाई। राखेउँ प्रान जानकिहिं लाई ॥
translation: फिर मैंने रूप की राशि, सुंदर गुण और शीलवाली प्यारी पुत्रवधू पाई है। मैंने इन (जानकी) को आँखों की पुतली बनाकर इनसे प्रेम बढ़ाया है और अपने प्राण इनमें लगा रखे हैं ॥
english_translation: I have also gained a beloved daughter-in-law, full of beauty, virtues, and gentle character. I have cherished Janaki like the pupil of my eye and placed my life in her.
essence: Love makes a daughter-in-law feel like the heart’s own child.
simple_meaning: Kausalya says she has gained a beloved daughter-in-law, and she has loved Janaki like the pupil of her eye, placing her whole heart in her.
insight: It shifts attention from formal family roles to the felt reality of belonging and care.
modern_relevance: You meet your partner’s mother and she instantly treats you like one of her own. That kind of welcome can soften even the hardest family rupture.
speaker: Kausalya

verse_text: कलपबेलि जिमि बहुबिधि लाली। सींचि सनेह सलिल प्रतिपाली॥ फूलत फलत भयउ बिधि बामा। जानि न जाइ काह परिनामा ॥
translation: इन्हें कल्पलता के समान मैंने बहुत तरह से बड़े लाड़-चाव के साथ स्नेह रूपी जल से सींचकर पाला है। अब इस लता के फूलने-फलने के समय विधाता वाम हो गए। कुछ जाना नहीं जाता कि इसका क्या परिणाम होगा ॥
english_translation: I have nurtured her like a wish-fulfilling vine with many kinds of affection and care. Now, just as she is flowering and fruiting, fate has turned against me. I cannot know what will happen next.
essence: Deep love makes uncertainty unbearable.
simple_meaning: Dasharath says he has raised Sita with great love, like a precious vine. Now that her life is reaching fullness, he fears something has gone wrong and cannot see what comes next.
insight: It shifts attention from possession to vulnerability: what is deeply loved is never fully controllable.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you’ve protected for years step into a new phase of life, and your chest tightens. Pride and fear arrive together, because love always includes the risk of not knowing.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: पलँग पीठ तजि गोद हिंडोरा। सियँ न दीन्ह पगु अवनि कठोरा॥ जिअनमूरि जिमि जोगवत रहउँ। दीप बाति नहिं टारन कहऊँ ॥
translation: सीता ने पर्यंकपृष्ठ (पलंग के ऊपर), गोद और हिंडोले को छोड़कर कठोर पृथ्वी पर कभी पैर नहीं रखा। मैं सदा संजीवनी जड़ी के समान (सावधानी से) इनकी रखवाली करती रही हूँ। कभी दीपक की बत्ती हटाने को भी नहीं कहती ॥
english_translation: Sita never set her foot on the hard earth, even leaving the bed, seat, lap, and swing. I cared for her like a life-saving herb, never even asking that the lamp’s wick be moved.
essence: Tender care makes exile feel even harsher.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi says Sita was raised in great comfort and care, never even touching the hard ground, and was watched over with extreme tenderness.
insight: It highlights the contrast between royal comfort and the harsh exile that follows.
modern_relevance: You tuck a child into bed, adjust the blanket, and quietly check the lamp before leaving the room. That instinct to protect without being asked is what this verse remembers.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: सोइ सिय चलन चहति बन साथा। आयसु काह होइ रघुनाथा॥ चंद किरन रस रसिक चकोरी। रबि रुखनयन सकइ किमि जोरी ॥
translation: वही सीता अब तुम्हारे साथ वन चलना चाहती है। हे रघुनाथ! उसे क्या आज्ञा होती है? चन्द्रमा की किरणों का रस (अमृत) चाहने वाली चकोरी सूर्य की ओर आँख किस तरह मिला सकती है ॥
english_translation: Sita now wants to go to the forest with you. O Raghunath, what command would she need? How can a chakor, longing for moonlight, turn its eyes toward the sun?
essence: Devotion needs no command; it follows love naturally.
simple_meaning: Sita wants to go to the forest with Ram, and no command is needed for her. Her love naturally turns toward him, just as a chakor turns toward the moon, not the sun.
insight: It shifts the mind from obligation to natural devotion: true love follows without being ordered.
modern_relevance: Someone you love is moving through a hard season, and you do not ask, “Should I come?” You already know where your heart belongs.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: करि केहरि निसिचर चरहिं दुष्ट जंतु बन भूरि। बिष बाटिकाँ कि सोह सुत सुभग सजीवनि मूरि ॥
translation: हाथी, सिंह, राक्षस आदि अनेक दुष्ट जीव-जन्तु वन में विचरते रहते हैं। हे पुत्र! क्या विष की वाटिका में सुंदर संजीवनी बूटी शोभा पा सकती है? ॥
english_translation: Elephants, lions, and wicked forest beings roam there in great numbers. Son, can a beautiful healing herb flourish in a garden of poison?
essence: A tender life cannot bloom in a poisonous place.
simple_meaning: A harsh forest full of dangerous creatures is no place for something delicate and life-giving. The setting itself makes the point: this environment cannot support tender beauty.
insight: It shifts attention from blaming the fragile thing to recognizing the toxicity of the setting.
modern_relevance: You try to keep a calm heart in a room where sarcasm, gossip, and cruelty are normal. The problem is not your effort — it is the climate around you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बन हित कोल किरात किसोरी। रचीं बिरंचि बिषय सुख भोरी॥ पाहन कृमि जिमि कठिन सुभाऊ। तिन्हहि कलेसु न कानन काऊ ॥
translation: वन के लिए तो ब्रह्माजी ने विषय सुख को न जानने वाली कोल और भीलों की लड़कियों को रचा है, जिनका पत्थर के कीड़े जैसा कठोर स्वभाव है। उन्हें वन में कभी क्लेश नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: For the forest, Brahma created the girls of the Kol and Kirat tribes, who know nothing of worldly pleasures. Their nature is hard like stone or a worm in stone, so the forest gives them no distress.
essence: Hard places do not trouble the one shaped for them.
simple_meaning: Some people are naturally fit for forest life because they are not attached to comfort. Their hardiness means the forest does not trouble them.
insight: It shifts judgment away from universal assumptions and toward the actual nature and capacity of each person.
modern_relevance: A friend who grew up hiking rough trails moves through a monsoon trek with ease while you struggle for every step. The same place can be home to one person and hardship to another.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कै तापस तिय कानन जोगू। जिन्ह तप हेतु तजा सब भोगू॥ सिय बन बसिहि तात केहि भाँती। चित्रलिखित कपि देखि डेराती ॥
translation: अथवा तपस्वियों की स्त्रियाँ वन में रहने योग्य हैं, जिन्होंने तपस्या के लिए सब भोग तज दिए हैं। हे पुत्र! जो तसवीर के बंदर को देखकर डर जाती हैं, वे सीता वन में किस तरह रह सकेंगी? ॥
english_translation: Or are the wives of ascetics fit for the forest, having given up all pleasures for penance? O son, how could Sita live in the forest when she trembles at seeing a painted monkey?
essence: Hardship fits only where the heart and habits can bear it.
simple_meaning: A forest is easier for people already used to austerity. Sita, who is delicate and frightened even by a painted monkey, would find forest life extremely hard.
insight: It shifts the mind from romanticizing hardship to seeing the actual human cost of forcing it on someone unprepared.
modern_relevance: You ask someone raised in comfort to sleep on a bare floor, eat little, and face constant uncertainty. The body may comply for a day, but the shock is real.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुरसर सुभग बनज बन चारी। डाबर जोगु कि हंसकुमारी॥ अस बिचारि जस आयसु होई। मैं सिख देउँ जानकिहि सोई ॥
translation: देवसरोवर के कमल वन में विचरण करने वाली हंसिनी क्या गड़ैयों (तलैयों) में रहने के योग्य है? ऐसा विचार कर जैसी तुम्हारी आज्ञा हो, मैं जानकी को वैसी ही शिक्षा दूँ ॥
english_translation: A swan belongs among lotus-filled lakes, not in a muddy pond. Thinking this over, I will teach Janaki according to your wish.
essence: What is fitting preserves dignity; what is harsh must not be mistaken for care.
simple_meaning: A noble woman belongs in a fitting, beautiful place, not in a harsh one. So the speaker says he will teach Sita according to what is appropriate.
insight: It shifts attention from bare survival to fitting care and appropriate conditions.
modern_relevance: Someone asks you to adapt to a cramped, stressful situation that clearly does not suit you. You realize kindness is not forcing endurance; it is choosing what preserves dignity and well-being.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जौं सिय भवन रहै कह अंबा। मोहि कहँ होइ बहुत अवलंबा॥ सुनि रघुबीर मातु प्रिय बानी। सील सनेह सुधाँ जनु सानी ॥
translation: माता कहती हैं- यदि सीता घर में रहें तो मुझको बहुत सहारा हो जाए। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने माता की प्रिय वाणी सुनकर, जो मानो शील और स्नेह रूपी अमृत से सनी हुई थी, ॥
english_translation: Mother said, "If Sita stays in the house, she will be a great support to me." Hearing his mother's dear words, Raghubir, as if soaked in the nectar of character and affection, ...
essence: Tender words can carry a hidden turning point.
simple_meaning: Mother says Sita would be a great comfort if she stayed at home. Ram hears this loving, gentle request, which feels soaked in kindness and affection.
insight: It shifts attention from the literal request to the emotional weight behind it.
modern_relevance: A parent asks for help in a voice too gentle to refuse. You hear the need beneath the words, even when the request will cost you something.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहि प्रिय बचन बिबेकमय कीन्हि मातु परितोष। लगे प्रबोधन जानकिहि प्रगटि बिपिन गुन दोष ॥
translation: विवेकमय प्रिय वचन कहकर माता को संतुष्ट किया। फिर वन के गुण-दोष प्रकट करके वे जानकीजी को समझाने लगे ॥
english_translation: He spoke loving, wise words and satisfied his mother. Then he began instructing Janaki, openly describing the merits and faults of forest life.
essence: Kind words can carry hard truth without losing tenderness.
simple_meaning: Ram reassures his mother with thoughtful words, then gently explains to Sita what forest life will be like.
insight: It teaches you to speak with kindness and clarity when others need both reassurance and reality.
modern_relevance: You are trying to calm a parent while also telling your partner the move will be hard. Ram shows how to be tender without being vague.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: मातु समीप कहत सकुचाहीं। बोले समउ समुझि मन माहीं॥ राजकुमारि सिखावनु सुनहू। आन भाँति जियँ जनि कछु गुनहू ॥
translation: माता के सामने सीताजी से कुछ कहने में सकुचाते हैं। पर मन में यह समझकर कि यह समय ऐसा ही है, वे बोले- हे राजकुमारी! मेरी सिखावन सुनो। मन में कुछ दूसरी तरह न समझ लेना ॥
english_translation: Near his mother, he hesitated to speak. Then, understanding the moment in his heart, he said, “Princess, listen to my counsel. Do not take my words in any other way.”
essence: Hard truth can be delivered without hardening the heart.
simple_meaning: Ram gently prepares Sita for the hard truth he must give her. He speaks carefully, so she does not misunderstand his counsel.
insight: It teaches you to speak difficult truth with tact, not bluntness.
modern_relevance: You know the conversation will hurt, but silence would hurt more. So you choose your words carefully, with respect, before the room hardens.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: आपन मोर नीक जौं चहहू। बचनु हमार मानि गृह रहहू॥ आयसु मोर सासु सेवकाई। सब बिधि भामिनि भवन भलाई ॥
translation: जो अपना और मेरा भला चाहती हो, तो मेरा वचन मानकर घर रहो। हे भामिनी! मेरी आज्ञा का पालन होगा, सास की सेवा बन पड़ेगी। घर रहने में सभी प्रकार से भलाई है ॥
english_translation: If you want what is best for both of us, obey my word and stay in the house. O gentle one, following my command will make service to the mother-in-law possible in every way, and staying at home is best in all respects.
essence: True welfare can begin with obeying what preserves harmony.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Sita that staying in the house and obeying him will bring the best outcome for everyone, including service to her elders.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal impulse to responsible restraint and care for family order.
modern_relevance: You want to leave the argument, send the text, and prove your point. But sometimes the wiser move is to stay, listen, and do the unglamorous work of keeping the home steady.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: एहि ते अधिक धरमु नहिं दूजा। सादर सासु ससुर पद पूजा॥ जब जब मातु करिहि सुधि मोरी। होइहि प्रेम बिकल मति भोरी ॥
translation: आदरपूर्वक सास-ससुर के चरणों की पूजा (सेवा) करने से बढ़कर दूसरा कोई धर्म नहीं है। जब-जब माता मुझे याद करेंगी और प्रेम से व्याकुल होने के कारण उनकी बुद्धि भोली हो जाएगी (वे अपने-आपको भूल जाएँगी) ॥
english_translation: No duty is greater than this: reverently serve the feet of your parents-in-law. Whenever your mother remembers me, she will be overwhelmed with love and lose herself in tenderness.
essence: Reverent service to elders is the highest duty.
simple_meaning: Respectful service to one's parents-in-law is presented as the highest duty. Sita also says that when her mother thinks of her, love will overwhelm her.
insight: It shifts duty from self-expression to reverent care for family roles.
modern_relevance: You move into a new home and quietly learn the rhythms of an older generation: tea at the right time, the right tone, the right respect. Love shows up as careful service, not big speeches.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: तब तब तुम्ह कहि कथा पुरानी। सुंदरि समुझाएहु मृदु बानी॥ कहउँ सुभायँ सपथ सत मोही। सुमुखि मातु हित राखउँ तोही ॥
translation: हे सुंदरी! तब-तब तुम कोमल वाणी से पुरानी कथाएँ कह-कहकर इन्हें समझाना। हे सुमुखि! मुझे सैकड़ों सौगंध हैं, मैं यह स्वभाव से ही कहता हूँ कि मैं तुम्हें केवल माता के लिए ही घर पर रखता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Then, gently remind them with old stories, dear one. I speak this from my own nature and with many vows: fair-faced one, I keep you at home only for my mother’s sake.
essence: Firm duty can still be spoken with tenderness.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Sita to use gentle words and old stories to explain why she must stay home. He says he keeps her there only because of his mother’s welfare.
insight: It teaches you to hold duty and tenderness together, so hard choices do not become harsh speech.
modern_relevance: You have to tell someone a painful family decision and you choose your words carefully, not to hide the truth but to keep the relationship intact.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: गुर श्रुति संमत धरम फलु पाइअ बिनहिं कलेस। हठ बस सब संकट सहे गालव नहुष नरेस ॥
translation: (मेरी आज्ञा मानकर घर पर रहने से) गुरु और वेद के द्वारा सम्मत धर्म (के आचरण) का फल तुम्हें बिना ही क्लेश के मिल जाता है, किन्तु हठ के वश होकर गालव मुनि और राजा नहुष आदि सब ने संकट ही सहे ॥
english_translation: By following the Dharma approved by the teacher and the Vedas, one receives its fruit without hardship; but under stubbornness, Gālava, Nahuṣa, and other kings suffered only trouble.
essence: Right conduct yields its fruit cleanly; stubbornness turns duty into suffering.
simple_meaning: Follow the guidance of the teacher and the Vedas, and dharma bears fruit without suffering. Stubbornness only brings trouble, as Gālava and Nahuṣa learned.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-willed pushing to disciplined obedience to right guidance.
modern_relevance: You keep arguing with the experienced person in the room, then spend three weeks cleaning up the mess. The verse says the hard lesson was avoidable: listen, align, and spare yourself the extra suffering.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मैं पुनि करि प्रवान पितु बानी। बेगि फिरब सुनु सुमुखि सयानी॥ दिवस जात नहिं लागिहि बारा। सुंदरि सिखवनु सुनहु हमारा ॥
translation: हे सुमुखि! हे सयानी! सुनो, मैं भी पिता के वचन को सत्य करके शीघ्र ही लौटूँगा। दिन जाते देर नहीं लगेगी। हे सुंदरी! हमारी यह सीख सुनो! ॥
english_translation: I will also fulfill my father's word and return soon, O wise and gentle one. Days will pass quickly; listen to my counsel, dear lady.
essence: A promise kept is more important than a promise that comforts.
simple_meaning: Ram promises to fulfill his father's word and return soon. He tries to reassure Sita that the time apart will feel short.
insight: It shifts attention from comforting delay to honoring a binding promise.
modern_relevance: You leave for a long trip and promise you'll be back soon, even though both of you know the house will feel empty. A real promise steadies the heart before distance does.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जौं हठ करहु प्रेम बस बामा। तौ तुम्ह दुखु पाउब परिनामा॥ काननु कठिन भयंकरु भारी। घोर घामु हिम बारि बयारी ॥
translation: हे वामा! यदि प्रेमवश हठ करोगी, तो तुम परिणाम में दुःख पाओगी। वन बड़ा कठिन (क्लेशदायक) और भयानक है। वहाँ की धूप, जाड़ा, वर्षा और हवा सभी बड़े भयानक हैं ॥
english_translation: O lovely one, if you insist out of love, you will suffer in the end. The forest is very harsh and frightening. Its heat, cold, rain, and wind are all terrible.
essence: Love can be sincere and still need to say no.
simple_meaning: Sita is warned that insisting on going will only bring suffering, because the forest is dangerous and full of harsh weather.
insight: It teaches you to separate affection from denial and speak plainly about risk.
modern_relevance: Someone you love wants to join you on a hard road, and you can already see the toll it will take. Honest care sometimes sounds like refusal, not encouragement.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: कुस कंटक मग काँकर नाना। चलब पयादेहिं बिनु पदत्राना॥ चरन कमल मृदु मंजु तुम्हारे। मारग अगम भूमिधर भारे ॥
translation: रास्ते में कुश, काँटे और बहुत से कंकड़ हैं। उन पर बिना जूते के पैदल ही चलना होगा। तुम्हारे चरणकमल कोमल और सुंदर हैं और रास्ते में बड़े-बड़े दुर्गम पर्वत हैं ॥
english_translation: The path is strewn with kusha grass, thorns, and stones. You will have to walk barefoot. Your lotus feet are soft and beautiful, and the road is full of high, impassable mountains.
essence: Devotion must walk through pain, not around it.
simple_meaning: The road is rough, sharp, and full of obstacles. Walking it means going barefoot over painful ground and through hard mountain terrain.
insight: It shifts the mind from romantic longing to the physical cost of commitment.
modern_relevance: You agree to a trip, then realise it means broken roads, no comfort, and a body that will feel every mile. Love sometimes asks for that kind of honesty.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कंदर खोह नदीं नद नारे। अगम अगाध न जाहिं निहारे॥ भालु बाघ बृक केहरि नागा। करहिं नाद सुनि धीरजु भागा ॥
translation: पर्वतों की गुफाएँ, खोह (दर्रे), नदियाँ, नद और नाले ऐसे अगम्य और गहरे हैं कि उनकी ओर देखा तक नहीं जाता। रीछ, बाघ, भेड़िये, सिंह और हाथी ऐसे (भयानक) शब्द करते हैं कि उन्हें सुनकर धीरज भाग जाता है ॥
english_translation: Caves, ravines, rivers, and streams are so impassable and deep that no one even dares look at them. Bears, tigers, wolves, lions, and elephants roar there, and the sound drives courage away.
essence: The forest is so severe that even courage starts to run.
simple_meaning: The forest route is terrifying and nearly impossible. Caves, ravines, deep waters, and wild animals make even brave people lose courage.
insight: It shifts attention from romance to reality: the exile is not symbolic; it is physically dangerous.
modern_relevance: You open the map for a night drive and see a route through empty hills, no signal, no shops, no comfort. The mind tightens before the road even begins.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूमि सयन बलकल बसन असनु कंद फल मूल। ते कि सदा सब दिन मिलहिं सबुइ समय अनुकूल ॥
translation: जमीन पर सोना, पेड़ों की छाल के वस्त्र पहनना और कंद, मूल, फल का भोजन करना होगा। और वे भी क्या सदा सब दिन मिलेंगे? सब कुछ अपने-अपने समय के अनुकूल ही मिल सकेगा ॥
english_translation: You will sleep on the ground, wear bark clothes, and live on roots, fruits, and tubers. Even those will not come every day; everything comes only in its proper season.
essence: Comfort is seasonal; endurance must be steady.
simple_meaning: Forest life will be hard. Even basic food and comfort will come only when nature allows.
insight: It trains the mind to expect irregularity without complaint and to prepare for hardship without panic.
modern_relevance: You pack for a long trek and realize the weather, the path, and even the meal stop are out of your control. The trip still happens, but on nature's terms, not yours.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नर अहार रजनीचर चरहीं। कपट बेष बिधि कोटिक करहीं॥ लागइ अति पहार कर पानी। बिपिन बिपति नहिं जाइ बखानी ॥
translation: मनुष्यों को खाने वाले निशाचर (राक्षस) फिरते रहते हैं। वे करोड़ों प्रकार के कपट रूप धारण कर लेते हैं। पहाड़ का पानी बहुत ही लगता है। वन की विपत्ति बखानी नहीं जा सकती ॥
english_translation: Man-eating night-wanderers roam there. They assume countless disguises of deceit. Even mountain water is hard to find. The dangers of the forest cannot be fully told.
essence: The forest is dangerous in ways words cannot hold.
simple_meaning: The forest is full of danger: man-eating beings, disguises, scarce water, and hardships that cannot be fully described.
insight: It trains the mind to see the real cost of exile, not romanticize hardship.
modern_relevance: You enter a new city at night with no contacts, no clear map, and every alley feels uncertain. The verse understands that feeling of being small inside a place that does not welcome you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ब्याल कराल बिहग बन घोरा। निसिचर निकर नारि नर चोरा॥ डरपहिं धीर गहन सुधि आएँ। मृगलोचनि तुम्ह भीरु सुभाएँ ॥
translation: वन में भीषण सर्प, भयानक पक्षी और स्त्री-पुरुषों को चुराने वाले राक्षसों के झुंड के झुंड रहते हैं। वन की (भयंकरता) याद आने मात्र से धीर पुरुष भी डर जाते हैं। फिर हे मृगलोचनि! तुम तो स्वभाव से ही डरपोक हो! ॥
english_translation: The forest holds terrible serpents, fierce birds, and bands of kidnappers. Even brave men tremble when they remember the forest. O lotus-eyed one, you are timid by nature.
essence: Fear makes the forest larger than it is.
simple_meaning: The forest is described as full of danger, and the speaker says even brave people fear it. The final line is a teasing warning that the listener is naturally timid.
insight: It shows how fear persuades through vivid images, not facts, and how warning can become pressure.
modern_relevance: You imagine the worst before a difficult move, and the whole situation starts feeling impossible. A single fearful picture can make a normal challenge seem like a threat.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: हंसगवनि तुम्ह नहिं बन जोगू। सुनि अपजसु मोहि देइहि लोगू॥ मानस सलिल सुधाँ प्रतिपाली। जिअइ कि लवन पयोधि मराली ॥
translation: हे हंसगमनी! तुम वन के योग्य नहीं हो। तुम्हारे वन जाने की बात सुनकर लोग मुझे अपयश देंगे (बुरा कहेंगे)। मानसरोवर के अमृत के समान जल से पाली हुई हंसिनी कहीं खारे समुद्र में जी सकती है ॥
english_translation: O swan-gaited one, you are not fit for the forest. Hearing of your going there, people will blame me. Can the swan, raised on the nectar-like waters of Manasarovar, live in the salty ocean?
essence: Real care knows when tenderness should not be tested by hardship.
simple_meaning: Sita is too delicate and refined for forest life, and Ram says her going there would bring him blame. The image compares her to a swan raised on sweet lake water, unable to live in the salty ocean.
insight: It frames care as discernment: not every hardship should be shared, and not every beloved person should be dragged into danger.
modern_relevance: You see someone you love packing for a situation that will grind them down, and your first instinct is to shield them, not prove a point.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: नव रसाल बन बिहरनसीला। सोह कि कोकिल बिपिन करीला॥ रहहु भवन अस हृदयँ बिचारी। चंदबदनि दुखु कानन भारी ॥
translation: नवीन आम के वन में विहार करने वाली कोयल क्या करील के जंगल में शोभा पाती है? हे चन्द्रमुखी! हृदय में ऐसा विचारकर तुम घर ही पर रहो। वन में बड़ा कष्ट है ॥
english_translation: Does a cuckoo that belongs in fresh mango groves belong in a forest of karil thorns? O moon-faced one, think this through in your heart and stay at home. The forest is full of hardship.
essence: Tenderness does not belong in every place.
simple_meaning: A tender, beautiful bird does not fit a harsh thorn forest. The speaker urges the listener to stay home because the forest is full of suffering.
insight: It shifts the mind from romantic impulse to honest discernment about what a person can endure.
modern_relevance: You want to follow someone into a situation you know will break you — a move, a crisis, a rough season. Love can be real and still admit: this place is not built for your tenderness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सहज सुहृद गुर स्वामि सिख जो न करइ सिर मानि। सो पछिताइ अघाइ उर अवसि होइ हित हानि ॥
translation: स्वाभाविक ही हित चाहने वाले गुरु और स्वामी की सीख को जो सिर चढ़ाकर नहीं मानता, वह हृदय में भरपेट पछताता है और उसके हित की हानि अवश्य होती है ॥
english_translation: One who does not hold in the head the advice of a natural friend, guru, and master will later regret it deeply, and his own good will surely be harmed.
essence: Pride turns good counsel into future regret.
simple_meaning: A true well-wisher's advice should be taken seriously. Ignoring it leads to regret and damages your own good.
insight: It teaches you to treat wise counsel as protection, not interference.
modern_relevance: Your friend, mentor, or parent sees the pattern before you do. You brush them off because you want your own way, then spend weeks cleaning up the mess they warned about.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुनि मृदु बचन मनोहर पिय के। लोचन ललित भरे जल सिय के॥ सीतल सिख दाहक भइ कैसें। चकइहि सरद चंद निसि जैसें ॥
translation: प्रियतम के कोमल तथा मनोहर वचन सुनकर सीताजी के सुंदर नेत्र जल से भर गए। श्री रामजी की यह शीतल सीख उनको कैसी जलाने वाली हुई, जैसे चकवी को शरद ऋतु की चाँदनी रात होती है ॥
english_translation: Hearing her beloved's gentle, beautiful words, Sita's lovely eyes filled with tears. How could this cooling advice burn her like a night of autumn moonlight burns a chakravaki bird?
essence: Tender words can still wound a heart that senses separation.
simple_meaning: Sita hears Ram's gentle words and cries. His soft advice feels painful to her, like a cold autumn moonlit night that hurts a chakravaki bird.
insight: It shows how attachment changes perception, making even kindness feel like sorrow.
modern_relevance: You get a calm, careful message from someone you love, but your chest tightens anyway because you know it means distance. The words are soft; the grief underneath is not.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उतरु न आव बिकल बैदेही। तजन चहत सुचि स्वामि सनेही॥ बरबस रोकि बिलोचन बारी। धरि धीरजु उर अवनिकुमारी ॥
translation: जानकीजी से कुछ उत्तर देते नहीं बनता, वे यह सोचकर व्याकुल हो उठीं कि मेरे पवित्र और प्रेमी स्वामी मुझे छोड़ जाना चाहते हैं। नेत्रों के जल (आँसुओं) को जबर्दस्ती रोककर वे पृथ्वी की कन्या सीताजी हृदय में धीरज धरकर, ॥
english_translation: Janaki could not answer. She grew restless, thinking, “My pure and loving husband wants to leave me.” Forcing back her tears, Sita, daughter of the earth, held courage in her heart.
essence: Love can tremble and still remain steady.
simple_meaning: Sita cannot speak at first. She feels distressed that her loving husband wants to leave her, so she holds back her tears and steadies herself.
insight: It shows how devotion can hold grief without collapsing into it.
modern_relevance: You hear a message from someone you love that changes everything, and your throat tightens before you can reply. The body feels the loss before the mind finds words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लागि सासु पग कह कर जोरी। छमबि देबि बड़ि अबिनय मोरी। दीन्हि प्रानपति मोहि सिख सोई। जेहि बिधि मोर परम हित होई ॥
translation: सास के पैर लगकर, हाथ जोड़कर कहने लगीं- हे देवि! मेरी इस बड़ी भारी ढिठाई को क्षमा कीजिए। मुझे प्राणपति ने वही शिक्षा दी है, जिससे मेरा परम हित हो ॥
english_translation: Sita bowed at her mother-in-law's feet and said, "Forgive my great boldness. My lord has taught me only what is for my highest good."
essence: True care can arrive as a painful instruction.
simple_meaning: Sita apologizes respectfully to her mother-in-law and says that Ram's teaching is meant for her highest good, even though it is painful.
insight: It shifts the mind from defending comfort to trusting a painful correction.
modern_relevance: You get a message that changes everything, and your first instinct is to argue. Then you remember the person who loves you most may be asking for your deeper good, not your immediate comfort.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: मैं पुनि समुझि दीखि मन माहीं। पिय बियोग सम दुखु जग नाहीं ॥
translation: परन्तु मैंने मन में समझकर देख लिया कि पति के वियोग के समान जगत में कोई दुःख नहीं है ॥
english_translation: But I have understood in my heart that no sorrow in the world equals separation from a husband.
essence: Separation from the beloved becomes the heaviest sorrow.
simple_meaning: Sita realises that no pain in the world is as great as being separated from her husband.
insight: It names emotional separation as a real wound, not a minor inconvenience.
modern_relevance: You can lose sleep over a message left unread, a call not returned, or a partner leaving the room after a fight. Some absences hurt more than any argument.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: प्राननाथ करुनायतन सुंदर सुखद सुजान। तुम्ह बिनु रघुकुल कुमुद बिधु सुरपुर नरक समान ॥
translation: हे प्राणनाथ! हे दया के धाम! हे सुंदर! हे सुखों के देने वाले! हे सुजान! हे रघुकुल रूपी कुमुद के खिलाने वाले चन्द्रमा! आपके बिना स्वर्ग भी मेरे लिए नरक के समान है ॥
english_translation: O lord of life, ocean of compassion, beautiful, giver of joy, all-knowing! Without you, O moon of the Raghu clan, even heaven feels like hell.
essence: Without Ram, even paradise becomes unbearable.
simple_meaning: The speaker says Ram is the source of life, compassion, beauty, joy, and wisdom. Without Ram, even the highest place feels unbearable.
insight: It shifts attention from external comfort to the presence that makes life feel alive.
modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the nicer apartment, the trip everyone envied — and still feel hollow because the one presence that mattered is missing. This verse names that ache exactly.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: मातु पिता भगिनी प्रिय भाई। प्रिय परिवारु सुहृदय समुदाई॥ सासु ससुर गुर सजन सहाई। सुत सुंदर सुसील सुखदाई ॥
translation: माता, पिता, बहिन, प्यारा भाई, प्यारा परिवार, मित्रों का समुदाय, सास, ससुर, गुरु, स्वजन (बन्धु-बांधव), सहायक और सुंदर, सुशील और सुख देने वाला पुत्र- ॥
english_translation: Mother, father, sister, dear brother, beloved family, a circle of friends, mother-in-law, father-in-law, teacher, kin, helpers, and a handsome, well-mannered, joy-giving son.
essence: Separation turns every loving bond into pain.
simple_meaning: Every close relationship and every source of support becomes painful in separation from the husband.
insight: It shifts attention from one missing person to the way their absence unsettles an entire life.
modern_relevance: You get one message after another while someone you love is gone, and even the kindest voices start to hurt. Loss does not stay in one corner; it spreads through every relationship.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जहँ लगिनाथ नेह अरु नाते। पिय बिनु तियहि तरनिहु ते ताते॥ तनु धनु धामु धरनि पुर राजू। पति बिहीन सबु सोक समाजू ॥
translation: हे नाथ! जहाँ तक स्नेह और नाते हैं, पति के बिना स्त्री को सूर्य से भी बढ़कर तपाने वाले हैं। शरीर, धन, घर, पृथ्वी, नगर और राज्य, पति के बिना स्त्री के लिए यह सब शोक का समाज है ॥
english_translation: As long as love and relationships exist, a husbandless woman is scorched even more than by the sun. Body, wealth, home, land, city, and kingdom—all become a gathering of sorrow without a husband.
essence: Without the beloved, even abundance becomes sorrow.
simple_meaning: A wife without her husband feels every part of life as pain. Even the things that should support her—home, wealth, and status—turn into sorrow.
insight: It shifts attention from outward comfort to the emotional center that gives life meaning.
modern_relevance: You walk into an empty apartment after a breakup and see the same chair, the same cup, the same walls. Nothing changed, yet everything feels wounded.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भोग रोगसम भूषन भारू। जम जातना सरिस संसारू॥ प्राननाथ तुम्ह बिनु जग माहीं। मो कहुँ सुखद कतहुँ कछु नाहीं ॥
translation: भोग रोग के समान हैं, गहने भार रूप हैं और संसार यम यातना (नरक की पीड़ा) के समान है। हे प्राणनाथ! आपके बिना जगत में मुझे कहीं कुछ भी सुखदायी नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Pleasures are like illness, ornaments are a burden, and the world is like Yama's torment. O Lord of my life, without you in this world I find nothing pleasant anywhere.
essence: Without Ram, even pleasure becomes pain.
simple_meaning: Worldly pleasures feel like illness, ornaments feel heavy, and life without Ram feels unbearable. Nothing in the world can comfort the one who is separated from him.
insight: It shifts attention away from outer comfort and toward the one presence that makes life feel whole.
modern_relevance: You get dressed for the party, check the mirror, and still feel strangely empty. The things meant to make life feel rich can feel heavy when the one thing you love is missing.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: जिय बिनु देह नदी बिनु बारी। तैसिअ नाथ पुरुष बिनु नारी॥ नाथ सकल सुख साथ तुम्हारें। सरद बिमल बिधु बदनु निहारें ॥
translation: जैसे बिना जीव के देह और बिना जल के नदी, वैसे ही हे नाथ! बिना पुरुष के स्त्री है। हे नाथ! आपके साथ रहकर आपका शरद्-(पूर्णिमा) के निर्मल चन्द्रमा के समान मुख देखने से मुझे समस्त सुख प्राप्त होंगे ॥
english_translation: As a body is nothing without life and a river is nothing without water, so a woman is nothing without her husband. O Lord, all happiness is with you; seeing your face, pure as the autumn full moon, brings every joy.
essence: Presence with Ram makes every hardship feel like home.
simple_meaning: Life gives the body meaning, water gives the river life, and the husband gives the wife her place in the world. Being with Ram brings complete joy, like seeing the bright moon.
insight: It shifts attention from comfort and setting to presence and companionship.
modern_relevance: You pack a suitcase for a move and realize the apartment, the city, even the future feel secondary. What matters is who you are carrying your life toward.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: खग मृग परिजन नगरु बनु बलकल बिमल दुकूल। नाथ साथ सुरसदन सम परनसाल सुख मूल ॥
translation: हे नाथ! आपके साथ पक्षी और पशु ही मेरे कुटुम्बी होंगे, वन ही नगर और वृक्षों की छाल ही निर्मल वस्त्र होंगे और पर्णकुटी (पत्तों की बनी झोपड़ी) ही स्वर्ग के समान सुखों की मूल होगी ॥
english_translation: Birds and deer will be my kin, the forest my city, bark my clean clothing, and a leaf-hut the root of heavenly comfort, if I am with you, Lord.
essence: Presence with Ram makes exile feel like home.
simple_meaning: With Ram beside her, Sita says the forest feels like home. Even simple things become enough when love is present.
insight: It shifts attention from external luxury to the quality of companionship.
modern_relevance: You move into a small rented room after leaving a bigger life behind. The walls are bare, the furniture is cheap, but the place feels livable because the person you love is there.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: बनदेबीं बनदेव उदारा। करिहहिं सासु ससुर सम सारा॥ कुस किसलय साथरी सुहाई। प्रभु सँग मंजु मनोज तुराई ॥
translation: उदार हृदय के वनदेवी और वनदेवता ही सास-ससुर के समान मेरी सार-संभार करेंगे और कुशा और पत्तों की सुंदर साथरी (बिछौना) ही प्रभु के साथ कामदेव की मनोहर तोशक के समान होगी ॥
english_translation: The benevolent forest deities will care for me like parents and in-laws. A bed of kusa grass and tender leaves will be a lovely couch beside my lord, as charming as Cupid's own bed.
essence: Presence transforms poverty into abundance.
simple_meaning: Sita says the forest itself will become her family and home. Even a bed of grass and leaves will feel beautiful because Ram will be beside her.
insight: It shifts attention from what is missing to who is present.
modern_relevance: You move into a tiny rented room with a thin mat, no furniture, and boxes for tables. Still, the place feels bearable because the person you love is there with you.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: कंद मूल फल अमिअ अहारू। अवध सौध सत सरिस पहारू॥ छिनु-छिनु प्रभु पद कमल बिलोकी। रहिहउँ मुदित दिवस जिमि कोकी ॥
translation: कन्द, मूल और फल ही अमृत के समान आहार होंगे और (वन के) पहाड़ ही अयोध्या के सैकड़ों राजमहलों के समान होंगे। क्षण-क्षण में प्रभु के चरण कमलों को देख-देखकर मैं ऐसी आनंदित रहूँगी जैसे दिन में चकवी रहती है ॥
english_translation: Roots, bulbs, and fruits will be like nectar for food, and the hills of the forest will be like hundreds of palaces in Ayodhya. Moment by moment, I will keep looking at the lotus feet of the Lord and remain joyful like a chakravaki in daylight.
essence: Presence can turn exile into a palace.
simple_meaning: Life in the forest will feel sweet and beautiful because Ram is there. Seeing his feet again and again will keep Sita joyful even in exile.
insight: It shifts the mind from measuring comfort by objects to measuring it by presence.
modern_relevance: You move into a tiny rented room after losing the apartment you loved. The walls are thin, the furniture is borrowed, but the person you love is beside you — and suddenly the place feels livable.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: बन दुख नाथ कहे बहुतेरे। भय बिषाद परिताप घनेरे॥ प्रभु बियोग लवलेस समाना। सब मिलि होहिं न कृपानिधाना ॥
translation: हे नाथ! आपने वन के बहुत से दुःख और बहुत से भय, विषाद और सन्ताप कहे, परन्तु हे कृपानिधान! वे सब मिलकर भी प्रभु (आप) के वियोग (से होने वाले दुःख) के लवलेश के समान भी नहीं हो सकते ॥
english_translation: O Lord, you have spoken of many forest hardships—fear, grief, and deep suffering. Yet all of them together are not even a tiny fraction of the pain of being separated from the Lord.
essence: Separation from Ram outweighs every other suffering.
simple_meaning: Forest hardships can be endured, but separation from Ram feels far worse than all of them combined.
insight: It shifts attention from external discomfort to the deeper pain of separation and longing.
modern_relevance: You can survive a hard move, a messy job, even loneliness in a new city. What hurts most is not the inconvenience — it is being cut off from the person or presence that gives life meaning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस जियँ जानि सुजान सिरोमनि। लेइअ संग मोहि छाड़िअ जनि॥ बिनती बहुत करौं का स्वामी। करुनामय उर अंतरजामी ॥
translation: ऐसा जी में जानकर, हे सुजान शिरोमणि! आप मुझे साथ ले लीजिए, यहाँ न छोड़िए। हे स्वामी! मैं अधिक क्या विनती करूँ? आप करुणामय हैं और सबके हृदय के अंदर की जानने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: Knowing this in my heart, O most wise one, take me along and do not leave me here. What more pleading can I make, my lord? You are full of compassion and know the heart within every heart.
essence: Love asks to be taken along, not merely understood.
simple_meaning: Bharat begs Ram to take him along and not leave him behind. He trusts Ram's compassion and inner knowledge, so he does not need to argue further.
insight: It shifts the mind from bargaining to surrender, trusting that love already sees what words cannot prove.
modern_relevance: You send one last message after a painful goodbye, not to persuade, but to be known. The deepest plea is simple: don't leave me outside your care.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: राखिअ अवध जो अवधि लगि रहत न जनिअहिं प्रान। दीनबंधु सुंदर सुखद सील सनेह निधान ॥
translation: हे दीनबन्धु! हे सुंदर! हे सुख देने वाले! हे शील और प्रेम के भंडार! यदि अवधि (चौदह वर्ष) तक मुझे अयोध्या में रखते हैं, तो जान लीजिए कि मेरे प्राण नहीं रहेंगे ॥
english_translation: O friend of the poor, O beautiful one, O giver of joy, O treasure of character and love! If you keep me in Ayodhya for fourteen years, know that my life will not remain.
essence: Separation from Ram is unbearable for the one who truly belongs to him.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he cannot live if Ram is kept in Ayodhya for the full exile period. He pleads with Ram as the source of kindness, beauty, joy, character, and love.
insight: It shifts loyalty from convenience to life-or-death belonging.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after the one person you trust leaves the room. Work and noise continue, but your attention stays with the absence. Bharat knows that kind of devotion.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: मोहि मग चलत न होइहि हारी। छिनु छिनु चरन सरोज निहारी॥ सबहि भाँति पिय सेवा करिहौं। मारग जनित सकल श्रम हरिहौं ॥
translation: क्षण-क्षण में आपके चरण कमलों को देखते रहने से मुझे मार्ग चलने में थकावट न होगी। हे प्रियतम! मैं सभी प्रकार से आपकी सेवा करूँगी और मार्ग चलने से होने वाली सारी थकावट को दूर कर दूँगी ॥
english_translation: Looking at your lotus feet every moment, I will not tire on the road. Beloved, I will serve you in every way and remove all weariness from the journey.
essence: Love makes the hard road lighter through service.
simple_meaning: Sita says she will keep looking at Ram’s feet as they travel, serve him in every way, and ease the fatigue of the journey.
insight: It shifts devotion into concrete help: attention, service, and relief of burden.
modern_relevance: You’re on a long train ride with someone carrying more than they admit. You stop talking about yourself, notice their tired shoulders, and quietly make the trip easier. That is the kind of care Sita models.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: पाय पखारि बैठि तरु छाहीं। करिहउँ बाउ मुदित मन माहीं॥ श्रम कन सहित स्याम तनु देखें। कहँ दुख समउ प्रानपति पेखें ॥
translation: आपके पैर धोकर, पेड़ों की छाया में बैठकर, मन में प्रसन्न होकर हवा करूँगी (पंखा झलूँगी)। पसीने की बूँदों सहित श्याम शरीर को देखकर प्राणपति के दर्शन करते हुए दुःख के लिए मुझे अवकाश ही कहाँ रहेगा ॥
english_translation: After washing your feet, I will sit in the shade of a tree and gladly fan you. Seeing your dark body covered with beads of sweat, where will sorrow find room when I behold my beloved lord?
essence: Love makes service feel like rest.
simple_meaning: Sita says she will serve Ram lovingly by washing his feet, fanning him in the shade, and finding joy in caring for him. Seeing his tired body brings her no sorrow, only devotion.
insight: It shifts service from obligation to delight, showing that devotion can erase the sense of burden.
modern_relevance: You wipe the sweat from someone’s forehead after a long hospital visit, and the fatigue disappears from your own body. Care stops feeling like sacrifice when love is real.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सम महि तृन तरुपल्लव डासी। पाय पलोटिहि सब निसि दासी॥ बार बार मृदु मूरति जोही। लागिहि तात बयारि न मोही ॥
translation: समतल भूमि पर घास और पेड़ों के पत्ते बिछाकर यह दासी रातभर आपके चरण दबावेगी। बार-बार आपकी कोमल मूर्ति को देखकर मुझको गरम हवा भी न लगेगी ॥
english_translation: I will spread grass, leaves, and tender shoots on the ground. This servant will massage your feet all night. Looking again and again at your gentle form, even hot wind will not touch me.
essence: Devotion turns hardship into service and nearness into comfort.
simple_meaning: Sita offers to make the ground soft, massage Ram's feet all night, and stay comforted just by seeing his gentle form.
insight: It shifts devotion from feeling to action: closeness is proven by care, not sentiment.
modern_relevance: You sit beside someone in a hospital corridor, folding a jacket into a pillow and forgetting your own discomfort. Love stops asking for ease and starts asking, 'What do you need right now?'
speaker: Sita

verse_text: को प्रभु सँग मोहि चितवनिहारा। सिंघबधुहि जिमि ससक सिआरा॥ मैं सुकुमारि नाथ बन जोगू। तुम्हहि उचित तप मो कहुँ भोगू ॥
translation: प्रभु के साथ (रहते) मेरी ओर (आँख उठाकर) देखने वाला कौन है (अर्थात कोई नहीं देख सकता)! जैसे सिंह की स्त्री (सिंहनी) को खरगोश और सियार नहीं देख सकते। मैं सुकुमारी हूँ और नाथ वन के योग्य हैं? आपको तो तपस्या उचित है और मुझको विषय भोग? ॥
english_translation: Who can look at me with the Lord present? A hare and a jackal cannot face a lioness. I am delicate, my lord belongs in the forest. You are fit for austerity; I am fit for comfort.
essence: Love makes itself small so the beloved can bear the harder road.
simple_meaning: Sita says she is too delicate for forest hardship and that Ram belongs in the forest life, while she belongs to comfort.
insight: It shifts the mind from claiming closeness to offering support without self-importance.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you love pack for a hard move, a risky job, or a long sacrifice, and your first instinct is to downplay yourself so they can go lighter.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: ऐसेउ बचन कठोर सुनि जौं न हृदउ बिलगान। तौ प्रभु बिषम बियोग दुख सहिहहिं पावँर प्रान ॥
translation: ऐसे कठोर वचन सुनकर भी जब मेरा हृदय न फटा तो, हे प्रभु! (मालूम होता है) ये पामर प्राण आपके वियोग का भीषण दुःख सहेंगे ॥
english_translation: Even after hearing such harsh words, if my heart did not break, then, O Lord, these worthless breaths will surely endure the terrible pain of separation from you.
essence: If the smaller wound holds, the greater sorrow can also be borne.
simple_meaning: Sita says that if harsh words did not break her heart, then she can endure the far greater pain of being separated from Ram.
insight: It shifts the mind from fearing discomfort to trusting endurance born of love.
modern_relevance: You were misunderstood in the meeting, and it stung. But the deeper test is whether you can still stay loyal to what matters when the cost gets heavier.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: अस कहि सीय बिकल भइ भारी। बचन बियोगु न सकी सँभारी॥ देखि दसा रघुपति जियँ जाना। हठि राखें नहिं राखिहि प्राना ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर सीताजी बहुत ही व्याकुल हो गईं। वे वचन के वियोग को भी न सम्हाल सकीं। (अर्थात शरीर से वियोग की बात तो अलग रही, वचन से भी वियोग की बात सुनकर वे अत्यन्त विकल हो गईं।) उनकी यह दशा देखकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने अपने जी में जान लिया कि हठपूर्वक इन्हें यहाँ रखने से ये प्राणों को न रखेंगी ॥
english_translation: Sita became deeply distressed after speaking. She could not bear even the thought of separation. Seeing her condition, Raghupati understood in his heart that if he kept her there by force, she would not keep her life.
essence: Forcing love destroys the one you mean to keep.
simple_meaning: Sita is overwhelmed by the pain of separation. Ram sees that forcing her to stay would cost her life.
insight: It shifts attention from obedience to compassion: Ram reads Sita’s state and responds to what preserves life.
modern_relevance: You watch someone go quiet after bad news, and you know the argument is over. Some bonds are so deep that force only breaks what love is trying to protect.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहेउ कृपाल भानुकुलनाथा। परिहरि सोचु चलहु बन साथा॥ नहिं बिषाद कर अवसरु आजू। बेगि करहु बन गवन समाजू ॥
translation: तब कृपालु, सूर्यकुल के स्वामी श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने कहा कि सोच छोड़कर मेरे साथ वन को चलो। आज विषाद करने का अवसर नहीं है। तुरंत वनगमन की तैयारी करो ॥
english_translation: Then the compassionate Lord of the Sun dynasty said, "Set aside sorrow and come with me to the forest. Today is no time for grief. Quickly make ready for the journey into the forest."
essence: Grief must wait when dharma calls you forward.
simple_meaning: Ram asks everyone to drop sorrow, come with him to the forest, and prepare quickly. The moment calls for action, not grief.
insight: It shifts attention from emotional paralysis to the next necessary act.
modern_relevance: The house is quiet after bad news, and everyone is frozen in shock. One person still has to pack the bag, call the driver, and keep the next step moving.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कहि प्रिय बचन प्रिया समुझाई। लगे मातु पद आसिष पाई॥ बेगि प्रजा दुख मेटब आई। जननी निठुर बिसरि जनि जाई ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने प्रिय वचन कहकर प्रियतमा सीताजी को समझाया। फिर माता के पैरों लगकर आशीर्वाद प्राप्त किया। (माता ने कहा-) बेटा! जल्दी लौटकर प्रजा के दुःख को मिटाना और यह निठुर माता तुम्हें भूल न जाए! ॥
english_translation: Speaking tender words, Ram comforted Sita. Then he bowed at his mother's feet and received her blessing. "Return quickly and remove the people's sorrow, and may this harsh mother not be forgotten by you."
essence: Love speaks softly, but duty still sends him back.
simple_meaning: Ram comforts Sita, bows to his mother, and receives a blessing to return quickly and relieve the people's suffering.
insight: It teaches you to honor love and obligation at the same time, without letting emotion erase action.
modern_relevance: You leave the hospital after saying goodbye to your mother, then still have to show up for the work that cannot wait. Grief does not cancel responsibility.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: फिरिहि दसा बिधि बहुरि कि मोरी। देखिहउँ नयन मनोहर जोरी। सुदिन सुघरी तात कब होइहि। जननी जिअत बदन बिधु जोइहि ॥
translation: हे विधाता! क्या मेरी दशा भी फिर पलटेगी? क्या अपने नेत्रों से मैं इस मनोहर जोड़ी को फिर देख पाऊँगी? हे पुत्र! वह सुंदर दिन और शुभ घड़ी कब होगी जब तुम्हारी जननी जीते जी तुम्हारा चाँद सा मुखड़ा फिर देखेगी! ॥
english_translation: O Fate, will my condition ever change again? Will I see that lovely pair again with my own eyes? O son, when will that beautiful day and fortunate hour come when your mother, while still alive, sees your moonlike face again?
essence: Separation turns even hope into a prayer for one more sight.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya longs to see Ram and Sita together again. She wonders if her own fate will ever turn, and if she will live to see Ram's face again.
insight: It shifts attention from political loss to the intimate cost of separation.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you love pack a bag for a long absence, and the room suddenly feels too quiet. Kaushalya's words carry that ache of not knowing when, or whether, the reunion will come.
speaker: Kaushalya

verse_text: बहुरि बच्छ कहि लालु कहि रघुपति रघुबर तात। कबहिं बोलाइ लगाइ हियँ हरषि निरखिहउँ गात ॥
translation: हे तात! 'वत्स' कहकर, 'लाल' कहकर, 'रघुपति' कहकर, 'रघुवर' कहकर, मैं फिर कब तुम्हें बुलाकर हृदय से लगाऊँगी और हर्षित होकर तुम्हारे अंगों को देखूँगी! ॥
english_translation: Mother says, 'Beloved son, when will I again call you by these names, hold you to my heart, and joyfully behold your body?'
essence: Separation turns ordinary affection into aching devotion.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya longs to call Ram by affectionate names, hold him close, and see him again. Her love is so deep that separation feels unbearable.
insight: It shifts the mind from taking closeness for granted to feeling its preciousness before it is gone.
modern_relevance: You stand at the airport watching someone you love walk toward security, and suddenly the ordinary words you used every day feel sacred. Distance makes affection audible.
speaker: Kaushalya

verse_text: लखि सनेह कातरि महतारी। बचनु न आव बिकल भइ भारी॥ राम प्रबोधु कीन्ह बिधि नाना। समउ सनेहु न जाइ बखाना ॥
translation: यह देखकर कि माता स्नेह के मारे अधीर हो गई हैं और इतनी अधिक व्याकुल हैं कि मुँह से वचन नहीं निकलता। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने अनेक प्रकार से उन्हें समझाया। वह समय और स्नेह वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
english_translation: Seeing his mother overcome with love and unable to speak, Ram comforted her in many ways. That moment and that affection cannot be described.
essence: Love can leave even comfort speechless.
simple_meaning: Ram sees his mother so overwhelmed with love that she cannot speak, and he comforts her in many ways. The depth of that moment is beyond words.
insight: It teaches you to meet overwhelming emotion with calm reassurance instead of forcing words.
modern_relevance: You stand at a train platform watching a parent try not to cry, and no perfect sentence appears. In some moments, the kindest thing is not explanation but steady presence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब जानकी सासु पग लागी। सुनिअ माय मैं परम अभागी॥ सेवा समय दैअँ बनु दीन्हा। मोर मनोरथु सफल न कीन्हा ॥
translation: तब जानकीजी सास के पाँव लगीं और बोलीं- हे माता! सुनिए, मैं बड़ी ही अभागिनी हूँ। आपकी सेवा करने के समय दैव ने मुझे वनवास दे दिया। मेरा मनोरथ सफल न किया ॥
english_translation: Then Janaki touched her mother-in-law's feet and said, "Listen, Mother, I am utterly unfortunate. Fate gave me exile just when I could serve you. It did not fulfill my wish."
essence: Blocked service becomes its own grief.
simple_meaning: Sita bows to her mother-in-law and says she feels unlucky because exile stopped her from serving properly.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-pity to service: the pain is not about status, but about blocked duty.
modern_relevance: You finally get the chance to care for an elder, a parent-in-law, or a mentor — then distance, illness, or family conflict blocks it. The grief is not only loss; it is the frustration of unspent love.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: तजब छोभु जनि छाड़िअ छोहू। करमु कठिन कछु दोसु न मोहू॥ सुनिसिय बचन सासु अकुलानी। दसा कवनि बिधि कहौं बखानी ॥
translation: आप क्षोभ का त्याग कर दें, परन्तु कृपा न छोड़िएगा। कर्म की गति कठिन है, मुझे भी कुछ दोष नहीं है। सीताजी के वचन सुनकर सास व्याकुल हो गईं। उनकी दशा को मैं किस प्रकार बखान कर कहूँ! ॥
english_translation: Please do not let distress drive you away from affection. Fate is hard; I bear no blame. Hearing Sita’s words, her mother-in-law became distraught. How can I even describe her condition?
essence: Pain need not end tenderness.
simple_meaning: Sita asks her mother-in-law not to let pain destroy affection. She accepts that fate is difficult and says she is not at fault. The mother-in-law is overwhelmed by emotion.
insight: It teaches you to separate suffering from blame, so affection can survive hardship.
modern_relevance: You are packing a bag in silence after a family argument, trying not to turn hurt into hatred. Sita shows how to keep tenderness alive even when life feels unfair.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: बारहिं बार लाइ उर लीन्ही। धरि धीरजु सिख आसिष दीन्ही॥ अचल होउ अहिवातु तुम्हारा। जब लगि गंग जमुन जल धारा ॥
translation: उन्होंने सीताजी को बार-बार हृदय से लगाया और धीरज धरकर शिक्षा दी और आशीर्वाद दिया कि जब तक गंगाजी और यमुनाजी में जल की धारा बहे, तब तक तुम्हारा सुहाग अचल रहे ॥
english_translation: She drew Sita into her heart again and again, gave her counsel with patience, and blessed her: may your married bond remain unbroken as long as the Ganga and Yamuna keep flowing.
essence: Tender blessing can hold a person steady when separation begins.
simple_meaning: Sita's mother-in-law embraced her repeatedly, steadied her with kind words, and blessed her long married life.
insight: It shifts attention from loss to blessing, showing how care can strengthen someone before separation.
modern_relevance: At an airport gate, your mother keeps pulling you into one last hug before you leave for a hard move. She cannot remove the pain, but she can steady you for the road.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीतहि सासु आसीस सिख दीन्हि अनेक प्रकार। चली नाइ पद पदुम सिरु अति हित बारहिं बार ॥
translation: सीताजी को सास ने अनेकों प्रकार से आशीर्वाद और शिक्षाएँ दीं और वे (सीताजी) बड़े ही प्रेम से बार-बार चरणकमलों में सिर नवाकर चलीं ॥
english_translation: Sita's mother-in-law gave her many blessings and teachings. Sita bowed her head again and again to the lotus feet and departed with deep affection.
essence: Deep affection bows before it walks away.
simple_meaning: Sita receives blessings and guidance from her mother-in-law, then leaves with repeated bows and deep affection.
insight: It teaches you to leave with humility, carrying love in your conduct rather than in words alone.
modern_relevance: You leave your childhood home after one last meal, and every goodbye feels heavier than the last. Quiet respect and repeated gratitude can hold a painful departure together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समाचार जब लछिमन पाए। ब्याकुल बिलख बदन उठि धाए॥ कंप पुलक तन नयन सनीरा। गहे चरन अति प्रेम अधीरा ॥
translation: जब लक्ष्मणजी ने समाचार पाए, तब वे व्याकुल होकर उदास मुँह उठ दौड़े। शरीर काँप रहा है, रोमांच हो रहा है, नेत्र आँसुओं से भरे हैं। प्रेम से अत्यन्त अधीर होकर उन्होंने श्री रामजी के चरण पकड़ लिए ॥
english_translation: When Lakshman heard the news, he rushed up in anguish, face clouded with grief. His body trembled, his hair stood on end, his eyes filled with tears. Overcome by love, he seized Ram's feet.
essence: Love for Ram makes Lakshman rush forward in helpless grief.
simple_meaning: Lakshman hears the news and runs to Ram in grief and love, unable to stay still. His body shows his emotion before he can speak.
insight: It shows devotion as an immediate bodily response, not a polished emotion. Grief and loyalty arrive together and drive action.
modern_relevance: You read a message that changes everything, and your hands start shaking before you even understand it. Some bonds hit the body first, then the mind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहि न सकत कछु चितवत ठाढ़े। मीनु दीन जनु जल तें काढ़े॥ सोचु हृदयँ बिधि का होनिहारा। सबु सुखु सुकृतु सिरान हमारा ॥
translation: वे कुछ कह नहीं सकते, खड़े-खड़े देख रहे हैं। (ऐसे दीन हो रहे हैं) मानो जल से निकाले जाने पर मछली दीन हो रही हो। हृदय में यह सोच है कि हे विधाता! क्या होने वाला है? क्या हमारा सब सुख और पुण्य पूरा हो गया? ॥
english_translation: They cannot say anything; they stand there staring. They are helpless like a fish taken out of water. Their hearts worry: what will fate bring now? Has all our happiness and merit been spent?
essence: Sudden grief leaves people speechless and afraid of what comes next.
simple_meaning: They stand frozen, unable to speak, overwhelmed by dread. Their hearts fear that everything good has run out and something painful is about to happen.
insight: It captures the freeze that follows sudden loss and the mind’s rush to fear the worst.
modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after one message changes everything. Nobody knows what to say, but everyone feels the same knot in the chest: something has broken, and the next moment may hurt.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मो कहुँ काह कहब रघुनाथा। रखिहहिं भवन कि लेहहिं साथा॥ राम बिलोकि बंधु कर जोरें। देह गेहसब सन तृनु तोरें ॥
translation: मुझको श्री रघुनाथजी क्या कहेंगे? घर पर रखेंगे या साथ ले चलेंगे? श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने भाई लक्ष्मण को हाथ जोड़े और शरीर तथा घर सभी से नाता तोड़े हुए खड़े देखा ॥
english_translation: What will Ragunath say to me? Will he keep me at home or take me along? Ram saw his brother with folded hands, standing free of body, home, and all possessions.
essence: True loyalty drops body and home without hesitation.
simple_meaning: Lakshman wonders whether Ram will keep him at home or take him along. He stands ready to give up body, house, and everything else for Ram.
insight: It shifts loyalty from comfort and possession to complete readiness for service.
