modern_relevance: You are packing a bag for someone you love and realize you would go wherever they need you. No bargaining, no conditions — just readiness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बोले बचनु राम नय नागर। सील सनेह सरल सुख सागर॥ तात प्रेम बस जनि कदराहू। समुझि हृदयँ परिनाम उछाहू ॥
translation: तब नीति में निपुण और शील, स्नेह, सरलता और सुख के समुद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी वचन बोले- हे तात! परिणाम में होने वाले आनंद को हृदय में समझकर तुम प्रेमवश अधीर मत होओ ॥
english_translation: Then Ram, skilled in wise conduct, spoke. He was an ocean of character, affection, simplicity, and joy: “Father, do not be distressed by love. Understand in your heart the joy that will come at the end, and do not lose heart.”
essence: Affection stays clear when it remembers the good ahead.
simple_meaning: Ram tells his father not to panic in love-driven distress. He asks him to remember the good that will come in the end and stay steady.
insight: It teaches you to hold emotion without letting it overturn judgment.
modern_relevance: You get the message that your family group chat has gone silent after bad news. Before replying in fear, you breathe and remember that love can stay steady without collapsing.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: मातु पिता गुरु स्वामि सिख सिर धरि करहिं सुभायँ। लहेउ लाभु तिन्ह जनम कर नतरु जनमु जग जायँ ॥
translation: जो लोग माता, पिता, गुरु और स्वामी की शिक्षा को स्वाभाविक ही सिर चढ़ाकर उसका पालन करते हैं, उन्होंने ही जन्म लेने का लाभ पाया है, नहीं तो जगत में जन्म व्यर्थ ही है ॥
english_translation: Those who naturally place the teachings of their mother, father, teacher, and master above their own head truly gain the value of birth; otherwise, life in the world is wasted.
essence: Life becomes worthwhile when guidance is placed above pride.
simple_meaning: A person gains real value from life by naturally honoring the guidance of mother, father, teacher, and master. Without that, simply being born achieves nothing.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-will to disciplined receptivity toward rightful guidance.
modern_relevance: Your mother repeats the same warning, your mentor gives one hard truth, and your first impulse is to dismiss both. This verse asks you to pause and treat guidance as a gift, not an interruption.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: अस जियँ जानि सुनहु सिख भाई। करहु मातु पितु पद सेवकाई॥ भवन भरतु रिपुसूदनु नाहीं। राउ बृद्ध मम दुखु मन माहीं ॥
translation: हे भाई! हृदय में ऐसा जानकर मेरी सीख सुनो और माता-पिता के चरणों की सेवा करो। भरत और शत्रुघ्न घर पर नहीं हैं, महाराज वृद्ध हैं और उनके मन में मेरा दुःख है ॥
english_translation: Knowing this in your heart, listen to my counsel, brother: serve your mother and father. Bharat and Shatrughna are not at home, and the old king grieves for my absence in his heart.
essence: Service to parents becomes urgent when they are left carrying grief alone.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Lakshman to serve their parents and stay with them, because the old king is suffering from Ram's exile and the brothers are not at home.
insight: It shifts action from self-directed desire to immediate responsibility toward family.
modern_relevance: Your father is unwell, your sibling is away, and everyone expects you to chase your own plans. Ram's words cut through that pressure: some moments ask for presence, not ambition.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: मैं बन जाउँ तुम्हहि लेइ साथा। होइ सबहि बिधि अवध अनाथा॥ गुरु पितु मातु प्रजा परिवारू। सब कहुँ परइ दुसह दुख भारू ॥
translation: इस अवस्था में मैं तुमको साथ लेकर वन जाऊँ तो अयोध्या सभी प्रकार से अनाथ हो जाएगी। गुरु, पिता, माता, प्रजा और परिवार सभी पर दुःख का दुःसह भार आ पड़ेगा ॥
english_translation: If I take you with me to the forest, Ayodhya will be left orphaned in every way. Guru, father, mother, subjects, and family would all bear unbearable sorrow.
essence: True love sometimes stays behind to carry everyone else.
simple_meaning: Ram says he cannot take Bharat into exile, because Ayodhya would then be left helpless and grieving. He sees the duty of king, family, and people all at once.
insight: It shifts loyalty from private feeling to public responsibility, showing that care must include the people who rely on you.
modern_relevance: You want to drop everything and follow the person you love, but your home is already depending on you. Sometimes devotion means staying put so others do not collapse.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: रहहु करहु सब कर परितोषू। नतरु तात होइहि बड़ दोषू॥ जासु राज प्रिय प्रजा दुखारी। सो नृपु अवसि नरक अधिकारी ॥
translation: अतः तुम यहीं रहो और सबका संतोष करते रहो। नहीं तो हे तात! बड़ा दोष होगा। जिसके राज्य में प्यारी प्रजा दुःखी रहती है, वह राजा अवश्य ही नरक का अधिकारी होता है ॥
english_translation: So remain here and keep everyone satisfied. Otherwise, dear one, a great fault will follow. A king whose people suffer in his reign is surely fit for lower realms.
essence: A ruler who lets people suffer has already failed.
simple_meaning: Bharat says a ruler must stay and care for everyone’s wellbeing. If the people suffer, that ruler has failed badly.
insight: It shifts attention from authority to responsibility: a leader is judged by the people’s lived experience.
modern_relevance: You run a team meeting while one quiet person has stopped speaking entirely. The project may look fine, but the room is not. Bharat would call that a leadership failure.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: रहहु तात असि नीति बिचारी। सुनत लखनु भए ब्याकुल भारी॥ सिअरें बचन सूखि गए कैसें। परसत तुहिन तामरसु जैसें ॥
translation: हे तात! ऐसी नीति विचारकर तुम घर रह जाओ। यह सुनते ही लक्ष्मणजी बहुत ही व्याकुल हो गए! इन शीतल वचनों से वे कैसे सूख गए, जैसे पाले के स्पर्श से कमल सूख जाता है! ॥
english_translation: “Considering such policy, stay here, dear brother.” Hearing this, Lakshman became deeply agitated. Those cooling words dried him out, like frost withering a lotus.
essence: Tender counsel can feel like a wound to loyal love.
simple_meaning: Ram asks Lakshman to stay home after weighing what is right. Lakshman's heart breaks at hearing it, as if a lotus were shriveled by frost.
insight: It shows how devotion can turn restraint into pain, and how careful words still carry emotional force.
modern_relevance: You tell someone you care about to stay back for their own good, and they go quiet in a way that hurts. Sometimes protection feels like abandonment to a loyal heart.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: उतरु न आवत प्रेम बस गहे चरन अकुलाइ। नाथ दासु मैं स्वामि तुम्ह तजहु त काह बसाइ ॥
translation: प्रेमवश लक्ष्मणजी से कुछ उत्तर देते नहीं बनता। उन्होंने व्याकुल होकर श्री रामजी के चरण पकड़ लिए और कहा- हे नाथ! मैं दास हूँ और आप स्वामी हैं, अतः आप मुझे छोड़ ही दें तो मेरा क्या वश है? ॥
english_translation: Overcome by love, he could not answer. He clutched Rama's feet in distress and said, "Lord, I am your servant and you are my master. If you abandon me, what power is left to me?"
essence: Surrender is not weakness; it is freedom from false control.
simple_meaning: Lakshman, overwhelmed with love, cannot argue back. He holds Ram's feet and admits complete dependence: Ram is the master, and without Ram he has no control.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance to willing dependence on what is greater and steadier.
modern_relevance: You finally admit to the friend, mentor, or partner that you cannot carry this alone. The relief is immediate: the burden gets lighter the moment control stops pretending to be strength.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: दीन्हि मोहि सिख नीकि गोसाईं। लागि अगम अपनी कदराईं॥ नरबर धीर धरम धुर धारी। निगम नीति कहुँ ते अधिकारी ॥
translation: हे स्वामी! आपने मुझे सीख तो बड़ी अच्छी दी है, पर मुझे अपनी कायरता से वह मेरे लिए अगम (पहुँच के बाहर) लगी। शास्त्र और नीति के तो वे ही श्रेष्ठ पुरुष अधिकारी हैं, जो धीर हैं और धर्म की धुरी को धारण करने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: O lord, you have given me a good teaching, but my own weakness made it hard for me to grasp. Only noble, steady people who bear the weight of dharma are fit for the scriptures and moral law.
essence: Good teaching still feels far away to the unsteady.
simple_meaning: Lakshman admits the teaching is good, but says his own weakness makes it hard to hold. He says only steady, noble people who carry dharma well are fit for scripture and moral discipline.
insight: It shifts the mind from defensiveness to self-honesty, so learning begins with admitting where you are not yet steady.
modern_relevance: You hear solid advice from someone you trust, then realise you are too reactive to follow it cleanly. The first honest move is admitting that gap instead of pretending mastery.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: मैं सिसु प्रभु सनेहँ प्रतिपाला। मंदरु मेरु कि लेहिं मराला॥ गुर पितु मातु न जानउँ काहू। कहउँ सुभाउ नाथ पतिआहू ॥
translation: मैं तो प्रभु (आप) के स्नेह में पला हुआ छोटा बच्चा हूँ! कहीं हंस भी मंदराचल या सुमेरु पर्वत को उठा सकते हैं! हे नाथ! स्वभाव से ही कहता हूँ, आप विश्वास करें, मैं आपको छोड़कर गुरु, पिता, माता किसी को भी नहीं जानता ॥
english_translation: I have been raised in your affection like a child. Can a swan lift Mount Mandara or Mount Meru? I know no guru, father, or mother. I speak from my nature, Lord; trust me.
essence: Belonging to Ram makes every other tie secondary.
simple_meaning: Lakshman says he has been raised in Ram's affection and speaks from his true nature, asking Ram to trust him. He knows no other master, parent, or guide.
insight: It shifts loyalty from formal duty to lived belonging, where trust matters more than proof.
modern_relevance: A younger sibling stands in the kitchen after a harsh family argument, voice shaking, saying, 'I was raised by you. You know me.' The verse carries that raw plea to be seen through love, not suspicion.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: जहँ लगि जगत सनेह सगाई। प्रीति प्रतीति निगम निजु गाई॥ मोरें सबइ एक तुम्ह स्वामी। दीनबंधु उर अंतरजामी ॥
translation: जगत में जहाँ तक स्नेह का संबंध, प्रेम और विश्वास है, जिनको स्वयं वेद ने गाया है- हे स्वामी! हे दीनबन्धु! हे सबके हृदय के अंदर की जानने वाले! मेरे तो वे सब कुछ केवल आप ही हैं ॥
english_translation: Wherever there is affection, love, and trust in the world, the Vedas themselves sing of them. For me, all of that is only you, my Lord, friend of the helpless, knower within every heart.
essence: Every true bond finds its completion in Ram.
simple_meaning: All affection, trust, and true connection in the world are gathered in Ram alone. For the speaker, Ram is the one source and meaning of every bond.
insight: It redirects attachment from scattered human bonds to a single, wholehearted devotion.
modern_relevance: You keep looking for one person, one group, or one approval that will finally make you feel held. Then you realise the ache was never about possession — it was about where you place your deepest loyalty.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: धरम नीति उपदेसिअ ताही। कीरति भूति सुगति प्रिय जाही॥ मन क्रम बचन चरन रत होई। कृपासिंधु परिहरिअ कि सोई ॥
translation: धर्म और नीति का उपदेश तो उसको करना चाहिए, जिसे कीर्ति, विभूति (ऐश्वर्य) या सद्गति प्यारी हो, किन्तु जो मन, वचन और कर्म से चरणों में ही प्रेम रखता हो, हे कृपासिन्धु! क्या वह भी त्यागने के योग्य है? ॥
english_translation: Teach duty and discipline to the one who wants fame, wealth, or a good afterlife. But should the compassionate one abandon the person who loves the feet with mind, speech, and body?
essence: Complete devotion is not a candidate for rejection.
simple_meaning: Rules and moral discipline suit people who still want worldly gain or a better future. But someone who loves Ram with complete devotion should not be pushed away.
insight: It shifts the mind from judging devotion by usefulness to honoring it as its own completion.
modern_relevance: Someone finally opens up in therapy, not asking for advice, just wanting to be held without judgment. You can correct a performance; you should not dismiss a heart that is already surrendered.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: करुनासिंधु सुबंधु के सुनि मृदु बचन बिनीत। समुझाए उर लाइ प्रभु जानि सनेहँ सभीत ॥
translation: दया के समुद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने भले भाई के कोमल और नम्रतायुक्त वचन सुनकर और उन्हें स्नेह के कारण डरे हुए जानकर, हृदय से लगाकर समझाया ॥
english_translation: The ocean of compassion, the noble brother, heard his gentle and humble words, and, knowing his love and fear, the Lord took him to his heart and reassured him.
essence: Gentle love can calm fear without dismissing it.
simple_meaning: Ram hears Lakshman’s gentle, respectful words and, seeing his loving fear, pulls him close and comforts him.
insight: It teaches you to meet another person’s hesitation with warmth, not pressure.
modern_relevance: A younger sibling finally says what they’re afraid to say: “I don’t want to lose you.” Instead of brushing it off, you soften, listen, and make room for the fear beneath the words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मागहु बिदा मातु सन जाई। आवहु बेगि चलहु बन भाई॥ मुदित भए सुनि रघुबर बानी। भयउ लाभ बड़ गइ बड़ि हानी ॥
translation: (और कहा-) हे भाई! जाकर माता से विदा माँग आओ और जल्दी वन को चलो! रघुकुल में श्रेष्ठ श्री रामजी की वाणी सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी आनंदित हो गए। बड़ी हानि दूर हो गई और बड़ा लाभ हुआ!॥1।
english_translation: “Go ask Mother for permission. Come quickly, brother; let us go to the forest.” Hearing the noble words of Raghubar, Lakshman rejoiced. A great loss was removed, and a great gain had come.
essence: Clear duty turns hardship into relief.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Lakshman to ask their mother for permission and come quickly to the forest. Lakshman feels joy, because the painful delay has finally ended.
insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to immediate, rightful action.
modern_relevance: You finally make the call you've been avoiding: leave the job, start the move, tell your family. The fear doesn't vanish, but the next step becomes clean.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: हरषित हृदयँ मातु पहिं आए। मनहुँ अंध फिरि लोचन पाए॥ जाइ जननि पग नायउ माथा। मनु रघुनंदन जानकि साथा ॥
translation: वे हर्षित हृदय से माता सुमित्राजी के पास आए, मानो अंधा फिर से नेत्र पा गया हो। उन्होंने जाकर माता के चरणों में मस्तक नवाया, किन्तु उनका मन रघुकुल को आनंद देने वाले श्री रामजी और जानकीजी के साथ था ॥
english_translation: Laxman returned to his mother with a joyful heart, as if a blind man had regained sight. He bowed his head at her feet, yet his mind stayed with Ram and Sita.
essence: True devotion keeps the heart with Ram even while honoring the mother.
simple_meaning: Laxman returns to his mother with joy and bows to her feet, but his heart remains with Ram and Sita.
insight: It shows how duty to family and devotion to Ram can coexist without conflict.
modern_relevance: You call your mother after making a hard choice, and she hears respect in your voice even when your life is pulling elsewhere. That split loyalty feels familiar.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पूँछे मातु मलिन मन देखी। लखन कही सब कथा बिसेषी। गई सहमि सुनि बचन कठोरा। मृगी देखि दव जनु चहुँ ओरा ॥
translation: माता ने उदास मन देखकर उनसे (कारण) पूछा। लक्ष्मणजी ने सब कथा विस्तार से कह सुनाई। सुमित्राजी कठोर वचनों को सुनकर ऐसी सहम गईं जैसे हिरनी चारों ओर वन में आग लगी देखकर सहम जाती है ॥
english_translation: Seeing her sad face, the mother asked the reason. Lakshman told her the whole story in full. Hearing the harsh words, Sumitra trembled like a deer that sees fire all around the forest.
essence: Pain becomes real the moment it is spoken aloud.
simple_meaning: Sumitra sees Lakshman’s sadness, asks why, and hears the whole terrible news. The harsh words shake her like a deer surrounded by fire.
insight: It shows how grief lands first in the body, then in speech, before understanding can catch up.
modern_relevance: You notice your mother’s face change the moment she reads your message. Before she says a word, she already knows something is wrong.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लखन लखेउ भा अनरथ आजू। एहिं सनेह सब करब अकाजू॥ मागत बिदा सभय सकुचाहीं। जाइ संग बिधि कहिहि कि नाहीं ॥
translation: लक्ष्मण ने देखा कि आज (अब) अनर्थ हुआ। ये स्नेह वश काम बिगाड़ देंगी! इसलिए वे विदा माँगते हुए डर के मारे सकुचाते हैं (और मन ही मन सोचते हैं) कि हे विधाता! माता साथ जाने को कहेंगी या नहीं ॥
english_translation: Lakshman saw that disaster had come today. This affection will ruin everything. So, asking for leave, he hesitated in fear, wondering, "Will Mother let me go with them, or not?"
essence: Affection can become harmful when it ignores duty.
simple_meaning: Lakshman sees that affection can create a mess, so he becomes shy and fearful about asking permission to go with Ram and Sita.
insight: It teaches you to notice when affection is about to override sound action.
modern_relevance: You want to say yes to a friend’s request, but you can already see it will complicate a fragile family situation. Caring deeply does not remove the need for clear judgment.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: समुझि सुमित्राँ राम सिय रूपु सुसीलु सुभाउ। नृप सनेहु लखि धुनेउ सिरु पापिनि दीन्ह कुदाउ ॥
translation: सुमित्राजी ने श्री रामजी और श्री सीताजी के रूप, सुंदर शील और स्वभाव को समझकर और उन पर राजा का प्रेम देखकर अपना सिर धुना (पीटा) और कहा कि पापिनी कैकेयी ने बुरी तरह घात लगाया ॥
english_translation: Understanding the beauty, virtue, and nature of Ram and Sita, and seeing the king's love, Sumitra shook her head and said, "Wicked Kaikeyi has struck a cruel blow."
essence: Seeing love clearly makes betrayal unbearable.
simple_meaning: Sumitra sees Ram, Sita, and Dasharath's love clearly, and realizes Kaikeyi has caused terrible harm.
insight: It shifts the mind from confusion to moral clarity about who has caused harm.
modern_relevance: You hear the whole story after the argument is already over. Then the pattern becomes obvious, and the person who caused it can no longer hide behind excuses.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धीरजु धरेउ कुअवसर जानी। सहज सुहृद बोली मृदु बानी॥ तात तुम्हारि मातु बैदेही। पिता रामु सब भाँति सनेही ॥
translation: परन्तु कुसमय जानकर धैर्य धारण किया और स्वभाव से ही हित चाहने वाली सुमित्राजी कोमल वाणी से बोलीं- हे तात! जानकीजी तुम्हारी माता हैं और सब प्रकार से स्नेह करने वाले श्री रामचन्द्रजी तुम्हारे पिता हैं! ॥
english_translation: But knowing the moment was inauspicious, she held her composure and spoke with gentle words, true to her kind nature: "Child, Janaki is your mother, and Ram is your father in every way."
essence: Composure and gentle speech can hold a family together in crisis.
simple_meaning: Sumitra stays calm in a tense moment and speaks gently to Lakshman. She reminds him that Sita is like his mother and Ram like his father.
insight: It teaches you to answer crisis with composure and relational clarity, not emotional heat.
modern_relevance: Your sibling is spiraling before a hard conversation, and you can feel the room tighten. One calm sentence from someone steady can stop the whole situation from breaking apart.
speaker: Sumitra

verse_text: अवध तहाँ जहँ राम निवासू। तहँइँ दिवसु जहँ भानु प्रकासू॥ जौं पै सीय रामु बन जाहीं। अवध तुम्हार काजु कछु नाहीं ॥
translation: जहाँ श्री रामजी का निवास हो वहीं अयोध्या है। जहाँ सूर्य का प्रकाश हो वहीं दिन है। यदि निश्चय ही सीता-राम वन को जाते हैं, तो अयोध्या में तुम्हारा कुछ भी काम नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Ayodhya is wherever Ram lives. Day is wherever the sun shines. If Sita and Ram truly go to the forest, then Ayodhya has no work left for you.
essence: Ram's presence makes a place complete; without him, even Ayodhya is empty.
simple_meaning: A city only feels complete when Ram is there. Without him, even Ayodhya loses its purpose.
insight: It shifts attention from geography and status to what truly makes a place whole: the presence of what you love and serve.
modern_relevance: You move into the perfect apartment, but the room still feels wrong without the person you love. This verse reminds you that meaning comes from presence, not address.
speaker: Sumitra

verse_text: गुर पितु मातु बंधु सुर साईं। सेइअहिं सकल प्रान की नाईं॥ रामु प्रानप्रिय जीवन जी के। स्वारथ रहित सखा सबही के ॥
translation: गुरु, पिता, माता, भाई, देवता और स्वामी, इन सबकी सेवा प्राण के समान करनी चाहिए। फिर श्री रामचन्द्रजी तो प्राणों के भी प्रिय हैं, हृदय के भी जीवन हैं और सभी के स्वार्थरहित सखा हैं ॥
english_translation: Guru, father, mother, brother, radiant beings, and master should all be served like life itself. Shri Ram is even more dear than life, the very life of the heart, and the selfless friend of everyone.
essence: Serve the worthy deeply; Ram is dearer still and asks for nothing in return.
simple_meaning: Serve teachers, parents, siblings, radiant beings, and masters as dearly as your own life. Ram is even more precious: the life of the heart and the friend of all without selfishness.
insight: It shifts devotion from social respect to wholehearted inward belonging.
modern_relevance: You keep helping the mentor who shaped you, the parent who worries for you, the friend who never asks for credit. Then one relationship rises above them all: the one that asks for no payment, only love.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पूजनीय प्रिय परम जहाँ तें। सब मानिअहिं राम के नातें॥ अस जियँ जानि संग बन जाहू। लेहु तात जग जीवन लाहू ॥
translation: जगत में जहाँ तक पूजनीय और परम प्रिय लोग हैं, वे सब रामजी के नाते से ही (पूजनीय और परम प्रिय) मानने योग्य हैं। हृदय में ऐसा जानकर, हे तात! उनके साथ वन जाओ और जगत में जीने का लाभ उठाओ! ॥
english_translation: Whatever is revered and dearly loved in the world should be regarded as belonging to Ram. Knowing this in your heart, dear son, go into the forest with them and gain the true benefit of life.
essence: Honor every bond by placing Ram first.
simple_meaning: All people and things that seem most worthy of love are to be seen through Ram. With that understanding, the son should go to the forest and live rightly.
insight: It shifts attachment from social approval and comfort toward faithful companionship in hardship.
modern_relevance: You are torn between staying home for comfort and leaving to support someone you love through a hard season. This verse says loyalty is not loss when it is rooted in what matters most.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूरि भाग भाजनु भयहु मोहि समेत बलि जाउँ। जौं तुम्हरें मन छाड़ि छलु कीन्ह राम पद ठाउँ ॥
translation: मैं बलिहारी जाती हूँ, (हे पुत्र!) मेरे समेत तुम बड़े ही सौभाग्य के पात्र हुए, जो तुम्हारे चित्त ने छल छोड़कर श्री राम के चरणों में स्थान प्राप्त किया है ॥
english_translation: I am blessed beyond measure, and I offer myself to you, my son. You and I are truly fortunate, because your mind has abandoned deceit and found a place at Ram's feet.
essence: True fortune is a mind that leaves deceit and rests in Ram.
simple_meaning: Real blessing is when the mind gives up deceit and settles at Ram's feet. The speaker celebrates a son who has found that place.
insight: It shifts attention from outward achievement to inward honesty and devotion.
modern_relevance: A parent watches a grown child stop pretending, stop performing, and finally choose what is true. The relief is not success or status — it is sincerity.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: पुत्रवती जुबती जग सोई। रघुपति भगतु जासु सुतु होई॥ नतरु बाँझ भलि बादि बिआनी। राम बिमुख सुत तें हित जानी ॥
translation: संसार में वही युवती स्त्री पुत्रवती है, जिसका पुत्र श्री रघुनाथजी का भक्त हो। नहीं तो जो राम से विमुख पुत्र से अपना हित जानती है, वह तो बाँझ ही अच्छी। पशु की भाँति उसका ब्याना (पुत्र प्रसव करना) व्यर्थ ही है ॥
english_translation: The only truly blessed woman in the world is the one whose son is devoted to Raghupati. Otherwise, a barren woman is better than one who has given birth in vain, thinking a son who turns away from Ram is a source of benefit.
essence: Birth means little unless it turns toward Ram.
simple_meaning: A son only truly blesses a mother if he loves Ram. A child who turns away from Ram brings no real benefit.
insight: It shifts the focus from producing success to nurturing devotion and character.
modern_relevance: A parent watches a child win trophies, but the real question is whether character is forming. Achievement without devotion to what is right feels hollow.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: तुम्हरेहिं भाग रामु बन जाहीं। दूसर हेतु तात कछु नाहीं॥ सकल सुकृत कर बड़ फलु एहू। राम सीय पद सहज सनेहू ॥
translation: तुम्हारे ही भाग्य से श्री रामजी वन को जा रहे हैं। हे तात! दूसरा कोई कारण नहीं है। सम्पूर्ण पुण्यों का सबसे बड़ा फल यही है कि श्री सीतारामजी के चरणों में स्वाभाविक प्रेम हो ॥
english_translation: By your own good fortune, Ram is going to the forest. Son, there is no other reason. The greatest fruit of all merit is a natural love for the feet of Ram and Sita.
essence: Grace looks like exile; the highest reward is natural love for Ram and Sita.
simple_meaning: Ram’s exile is not random; it comes by fate and blessing. The highest reward of good deeds is an effortless love for Ram and Sita.
insight: It shifts attention from outer success to inward devotion, teaching that the best outcome is spontaneous love for Ram and Sita.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you love lose a job, a home, or a plan they counted on. Later, you realise the break opened a deeper loyalty and a softer heart than success ever did.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रागु रोषु इरिषा मदु मोहू। जनि सपनेहुँ इन्ह के बस होहू॥ सकल प्रकार बिकार बिहाई। मन क्रम बचन करेहु सेवकाई ॥
translation: राग, रोष, ईर्षा, मद और मोह- इनके वश स्वप्न में भी मत होना। सब प्रकार के विकारों का त्याग कर मन, वचन और कर्म से श्री सीतारामजी की सेवा करना ॥
english_translation: Do not ever fall under the sway of desire, anger, jealousy, pride, or delusion, even in a dream. Give up all forms of corruption and serve Sita and Ram with mind, speech, and action.
essence: Clean service begins where ego's noise ends.
simple_meaning: Do not let desire, anger, jealousy, pride, or delusion control you. Leave all inner corruption behind and serve Sita and Ram with your whole being.
insight: It shifts action from ego-driven reaction to clean, disciplined service.
modern_relevance: You are about to send a message while angry, jealous, or trying to prove yourself. Stop. The next move matters less than the state of mind behind it.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तुम्ह कहुँ बन सब भाँति सुपासू। सँग पितु मातु रामु सिय जासू॥ जेहिं न रामु बन लहहिं कलेसू। सुत सोइ करेहु इहइ उपदेसू ॥
translation: तुमको वन में सब प्रकार से आराम है, जिसके साथ श्री रामजी और सीताजी रूप पिता-माता हैं। हे पुत्र! तुम वही करना जिससे श्री रामचन्द्रजी वन में क्लेश न पावें, मेरा यही उपदेश है ॥
english_translation: For you, the forest is comfortable in every way, with Ram and Sita as father and mother. Son, do only what keeps Ram free from hardship in the forest; this is my instruction.
essence: Real care asks what eases Ram's path, not your own.
simple_meaning: Bharat tells his son that the forest will be easy for him if Ram and Sita are with him like parents. He should act in whatever way keeps Ram from suffering there.
insight: It shifts duty from self-protection to service: measure choices by the other person's ease, not your own.
modern_relevance: You are packing for a difficult trip to help someone you love. Your own inconvenience stops mattering the moment you ask, 'What will make their day easier?'
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: उपदेसु यहु जेहिं तात तुम्हरे राम सिय सुख पावहीं। पितु मातु प्रिय परिवार पुर सुख सुरति बन बिसरावहीं॥ तुलसी प्रभुहि सिख देइ आयसु दीन्ह पुनि आसिष दई। रति होउ अबिरल अमल सिय रघुबीर पद नित-नित नई॥
translation: हे तात! मेरा यही उपदेश है (अर्थात तुम वही करना), जिससे वन में तुम्हारे कारण श्री रामजी और सीताजी सुख पावें और पिता, माता, प्रिय परिवार तथा नगर के सुखों की याद भूल जाएँ। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि सुमित्राजी ने इस प्रकार हमारे प्रभु (श्री लक्ष्मणजी) को शिक्षा देकर (वन जाने की) आज्ञा दी और फिर यह आशीर्वाद दिया कि श्री सीताजी और श्री रघुवीरजी के चरणों में तुम्हारा निर्मल (निष्काम और अनन्य) एवं प्रगाढ़ प्रेम नित-नित नया हो!
english_translation: Mother Sumitra said: "My counsel is this—go so that Rama and Sita may find comfort in the forest, and so that you forget the comforts of father, mother, loved ones, family, and city. May your pure, unwavering love for the feet of Sita and Raghubir grow ever fresh, day by day."
essence: True love sends you where service is needed, not where comfort remains.
simple_meaning: Sumitra tells Lakshman to go in a way that brings comfort to Ram and Sita, forgets home comforts, and deepens his pure love for their feet.
insight: It shifts loyalty from personal comfort to wholehearted support for dharma and beloved companions.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you love leave for a hard season, and you do not ask them to stay safe and small. You bless them to serve well and love without fading.
speaker: Sumitra

verse_text: मातु चरन सिरु नाइ चले तुरत संकित हृदयँ। बागुर बिषम तोराइ मनहुँ भाग मृगु भाग बस ॥
translation: माता के चरणों में सिर नवाकर, हृदय में डरते हुए (कि अब भी कोई विघ्न न आ जाए) लक्ष्मणजी तुरंत इस तरह चल दिए जैसे सौभाग्यवश कोई हिरन कठिन फंदे को तुड़ाकर भाग निकला हो ॥
english_translation: Bowing his head to his mother’s feet, he set out at once, his heart still trembling. Like a deer that has broken a deadly snare and fled, he moved on by good fortune.
essence: Respect first, then move without delay.
simple_meaning: He bows to his mother and leaves at once, still uneasy, like a deer escaping a trap.
insight: It teaches you to move forward quickly after honoring the relationship that matters.
modern_relevance: You finally hang up after a hard family call, still shaken, but you get up and do the next right thing anyway.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: गए लखनु जहँ जानकिनाथू। भे मन मुदित पाइ प्रिय साथू॥ बंदि राम सिय चरन सुहाए। चले संग नृपमंदिर आए ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी वहाँ गए जहाँ श्री जानकीनाथजी थे और प्रिय का साथ पाकर मन में बड़े ही प्रसन्न हुए। श्री रामजी और सीताजी के सुंदर चरणों की वंदना करके वे उनके साथ चले और राजभवन में आए ॥
english_translation: Lakshman went to where Janakinath was. Finding the company of the beloved, his mind became joyful. Bowing to the beautiful feet of Ram and Sita, he walked with them and came to the royal palace.
essence: True devotion shows itself in humble companionship.
simple_meaning: Lakshman reaches Ram and Sita, feels joy at being with them, bows to their feet, and goes with them to the palace.
insight: It shifts attention from dramatic declaration to quiet loyalty: show up, bow down, stay close.
modern_relevance: You finally get to the hospital room after the long drive, and the first thing you do is hold the hand of the person you came for. Relief arrives before words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहहिं परसपर पुर नर नारी। भलि बनाइ बिधि बात बिगारी॥ तन कृस मन दुखु बदन मलीने। बिकल मनहुँ माखी मधु छीने ॥
translation: नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष आपस में कह रहे हैं कि विधाता ने खूब बनाकर बात बिगाड़ी! उनके शरीर दुबले, मन दुःखी और मुख उदास हो रहे हैं। वे ऐसे व्याकुल हैं, जैसे शहद छीन लिए जाने पर शहद की मक्खियाँ व्याकुल हों ॥
english_translation: People in the city, men and women alike, say to one another, “The Creator has spoiled what was well made.” Their bodies grow thin, their minds are sorrowful, and their faces pale. They are restless like bees whose honey has been taken away.
essence: A broken departure can leave an entire city grieving.
simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya are grieving so deeply that they say fate has ruined what was once good. Their bodies weaken, their minds ache, and they feel restless with loss.
insight: It shows how loss spreads through a whole community, turning private pain into shared sorrow.
modern_relevance: At a family dinner after a sudden breakup, nobody knows what to say. Everyone feels the absence in the room, and even the strongest voice sounds tired.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कर मीजहिं सिरु धुनि पछिताहीं। जनु बिनु पंख बिहग अकुलाहीं॥ भइ बड़ि भीर भूप दरबारा। बरनि न जाइ बिषादु अपारा ॥
translation: सब हाथ मल रहे हैं और सिर धुनकर (पीटकर) पछता रहे हैं। मानो बिना पंख के पक्षी व्याकुल हो रहे हों। राजद्वार पर बड़ी भीड़ हो रही है। अपार विषाद का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
english_translation: They wring their hands and beat their heads in regret, like birds fluttering without wings. A great crowd gathers at the palace gate, and the depth of grief cannot be described.
essence: Grief overwhelms speech and leaves only helpless motion.
simple_meaning: The people are overwhelmed with grief and regret. They gather at the palace, but the sorrow is too deep to describe.
insight: It shows grief as a collective collapse: the body laments when speech can no longer hold the loss.
modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after one message changes everything. People keep typing, deleting, and typing again, but no one can find words that fit the shock.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सचिवँ उठाइ राउ बैठारे। कहि प्रिय बचन रामु पगु धारे॥ सिय समेत दोउ तनय निहारी। ब्याकुल भयउ भूमिपति भारी ॥
translation: 'श्री रामजी पधारे हैं', ये प्रिय वचन कहकर मंत्री ने राजा को उठाकर बैठाया। सीता सहित दोनों पुत्रों को (वन के लिए तैयार) देखकर राजा बहुत व्याकुल हुए ॥
english_translation: The minister helped the king sit up and spoke gentle words: "Ram has arrived." Seeing Sita with both sons, the king was deeply shaken.
essence: Hope briefly lifts the king; love makes the loss hurt again.
simple_meaning: The minister comforts Dasharath with hopeful news, but the sight of Ram, Sita, and the sons makes the king collapse into grief and agitation.
insight: It shows how grief can be triggered by the very presence that was hoped for, making emotion stronger than explanation.
modern_relevance: You finally hear the person you miss is at the door, and your body reacts before your mind can. Relief and heartbreak can arrive together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीय सहित सुत सुभग दोउ देखि देखि अकुलाइ। बारहिं बार सनेह बस राउ लेइ उर लाइ ॥
translation: सीता सहित दोनों सुंदर पुत्रों को देख-देखकर राजा अकुलाते हैं और स्नेह वश बारंबार उन्हें हृदय से लगा लेते हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing Sita and his two beautiful sons, the king grows restless and, overcome by love, repeatedly draws them to his chest.
essence: Love makes separation unbearable before it even begins.
simple_meaning: Dasharath cannot bear the sight of Sita and his sons. Love overwhelms him, and he keeps pulling them into his arms.
insight: It shows how grief and love can break composure before a loss has even fully arrived.
modern_relevance: You keep hugging your child before a long trip, even though you already said goodbye twice. Your body knows what your words cannot fix: this is the last moment together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकइ न बोलि बिकल नरनाहू। सोक जनित उर दारुन दाहू॥ नाइ सीसु पद अति अनुरागा। उठि रघुबीर बिदा तब मागा ॥
translation: राजा व्याकुल हैं, बोल नहीं सकते। हृदय में शोक से उत्पन्न हुआ भयानक सन्ताप है। तब रघुकुल के वीर श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने अत्यन्त प्रेम से चरणों में सिर नवाकर उठकर विदा माँगी- ॥
english_translation: The king could not speak. Grief burned fiercely in his heart. Then Ram, the hero of the Raghu line, bowed his head at his father's feet with deep affection and asked to leave.
essence: Duty can be carried on a bowed head.
simple_meaning: Dasharath is too overwhelmed to speak. Ram bows to his feet with great love and asks permission to leave.
insight: It teaches you to meet painful duty with humility, not force.
modern_relevance: Your parent is too upset to talk, but the flight is booked and the taxi is waiting. You lower your voice, touch their feet or hand, and ask for permission before you go.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पितु असीस आयसु मोहि दीजै। हरष समय बिसमउ कत कीजै॥ तात किएँ प्रिय प्रेम प्रमादू। जसु जग जाइ होइ अपबादू ॥
translation: हे पिताजी! मुझे आशीर्वाद और आज्ञा दीजिए। हर्ष के समय आप शोक क्यों कर रहे हैं? हे तात! प्रिय के प्रेमवश प्रमाद (कर्तव्यकर्म में त्रुटि) करने से जगत में यश जाता रहेगा और निंदा होगी ॥
english_translation: Father, give me your blessing and your command. Why do you grieve at a time of joy? Dear father, if affection makes us forget our duty, our fame will be lost and the world will blame us.
essence: Affection cannot be allowed to erase duty.
simple_meaning: Ram asks Dasharath for blessing and permission to go ahead with what must be done. He says love should not make a person forget duty, because that brings blame and loss of honour.
insight: It teaches you to honour affection without letting it override what must be done.
modern_relevance: Your parent begs you to stay, but you still have to make the hard call that keeps your promise. The ache is real; the responsibility is still yours.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनि सनेह बस उठि नरनाहाँ। बैठारे रघुपति गहि बाहाँ॥ सुनहु तात तुम्ह कहुँ मुनि कहहीं। रामु चराचर नायक अहहीं ॥
translation: यह सुनकर स्नेहवश राजा ने उठकर श्री रघुनाथजी की बाँह पकड़कर उन्हें बैठा लिया और कहा- हे तात! सुनो, तुम्हारे लिए मुनि लोग कहते हैं कि श्री राम चराचर के स्वामी हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, the king rose in affection, took Raghupati by the arm, and seated him. Then he said, “Listen, father. The sages say that Ram is the lord of all moving and unmoving beings.”
essence: Love naturally bows before Ram’s greatness.
simple_meaning: Moved by love, the king seats Ram beside him and says that the sages call Ram the lord of all beings and all that exists.
insight: It shifts devotion from abstract praise to embodied reverence, where affection itself becomes worship.
modern_relevance: A father pulls his son close after a hard conversation and, for a moment, pride disappears. What remains is the simple recognition that love bows before what it cherishes most.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुभ अरु असुभ करम अनुहारी। ईसु देइ फलु हृदयँ बिचारी॥ करइ जो करम पाव फल सोई। निगम नीति असि कह सबु कोई ॥
translation: शुभ और अशुभ कर्मों के अनुसार ईश्वर हृदय में विचारकर फल देता है, जो कर्म करता है, वही फल पाता है। ऐसी वेद की नीति है, यह सब कोई कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: The divine gives fruits in accordance with good and bad deeds, considering them in the heart. One who acts receives that very result; this is the rule of the Vedas, as everyone says.
essence: Every deed carries its own result back to the doer.
simple_meaning: Actions bring matching results. Nothing is random or handed out blindly; the moral quality of what you do returns to you.
insight: It shifts attention from blaming circumstances to owning the causes you create.
modern_relevance: You send the message in anger, then wait for the reply that stings. The delay feels personal, but the pattern was set by your own hand.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: औरु करै अपराधु कोउ और पाव फल भोगु। अति बिचित्र भगवंत गति को जग जानै जोगु ॥
translation: (किन्तु इस अवसर पर तो इसके विपरीत हो रहा है,) अपराध तो कोई और ही करे और उसके फल का भोग कोई और ही पावे। भगवान की लीला बड़ी ही विचित्र है, उसे जानने योग्य जगत में कौन है? ॥
english_translation: Another commits the offense, and another bears the suffering. Who in the world can understand the divine order, which is wonderfully strange?
essence: The consequences of wrongdoing often fall on someone else.
simple_meaning: Wrongdoing and suffering do not always fall on the same person. The world’s order is strange and hard to understand.
insight: It shifts the mind from rigid moral bookkeeping to humility before events that exceed simple cause and effect.
modern_relevance: You watch a family argument start over one sharp sentence, yet the quietest person at the table ends up carrying the hurt for days. Life does not distribute consequences neatly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रायँ राम राखन हित लागी। बहुत उपाय किए छलु त्यागी॥ लखी राम रुख रहत न जाने। धरम धुरंधर धीर सयाने ॥
translation: राजा ने इस प्रकार श्री रामचन्द्रजी को रखने के लिए छल छोड़कर बहुत से उपाय किए, पर जब उन्होंने धर्मधुरंधर, धीर और बुद्धिमान श्री रामजी का रुख देख लिया और वे रहते हुए न जान पड़े, ॥
english_translation: The king tried many ways, abandoning deceit, to keep Ram there. But when he saw Ram's resolve, steady wisdom, and nobility, he knew Ram would not stay.
essence: A firm dharmic resolve ends all argument.
simple_meaning: The king tried every honest and dishonest way to keep Ram from leaving, but Ram's firm, wise resolve made it clear he would not stay.
insight: It teaches you to recognise when duty has already settled the matter, and to stop resisting what must be done.
modern_relevance: You keep rewriting the message, hoping they will stay, but their mind is already made up. At some point, dignity means seeing the decision clearly instead of forcing another round of persuasion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब नृप सीय लाइ उर लीन्ही। अति हित बहुत भाँति सिख दीन्ही॥ कहि बन के दुख दुसह सुनाए। सासु ससुर पितु सुख समुझाए ॥
translation: तब राजा ने सीताजी को हृदय से लगा लिया और बड़े प्रेम से बहुत प्रकार की शिक्षा दी। वन के दुःसह दुःख कहकर सुनाए। फिर सास, ससुर तथा पिता के (पास रहने के) सुखों को समझाया ॥
english_translation: Then the king drew Sita close to his heart and lovingly instructed her in many ways. He described the unbearable hardships of the forest and explained the comfort of living with her mother-in-law, father-in-law, and father.
essence: Love can plead, but it cannot change a chosen path.
simple_meaning: Dasharath embraces Sita and gently tries to persuade her by describing the forest's hardships and the comforts of staying with her elders.
insight: It shows how attachment speaks through care, trying to protect by reminding someone of comfort and danger.
modern_relevance: A parent stands in a doorway, voice soft but urgent, trying to keep a child from a hard choice. The words are loving, but the fear underneath is unmistakable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिय मनु राम चरन अनुरागा। घरुन सुगमु बनु बिषमु न लागा॥ औरउ सबहिं सीय समुझाई। कहि कहि बिपिन बिपति अधिकाई ॥
translation: परन्तु सीताजी का मन श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में अनुरक्त था, इसलिए उन्हें घर अच्छा नहीं लगा और न वन भयानक लगा। फिर और सब लोगों ने भी वन में विपत्तियों की अधिकता बता-बताकर सीताजी को समझाया ॥
english_translation: But Sita's mind was attached to Ram's feet, so home felt unwelcome and the forest did not seem terrible. Then everyone else also tried to persuade Sita, repeating how full the forest was of hardships.
essence: Love for Ram makes comfort and hardship feel the same.
simple_meaning: Sita's heart is already with Ram, so neither palace life nor forest hardship changes her mind. The others keep warning her about the dangers ahead.
insight: It shifts attention from fear of discomfort to the pull of devotion.
modern_relevance: Your family keeps listing every reason not to leave a safe job, move cities, or follow someone you love. You hear them, but your heart has already chosen what matters most.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सचिव नारि गुर नारि सयानी। सहित सनेह कहहिं मृदु बानी॥ तुम्ह कहुँ तौ न दीन्ह बनबासू। करहु जो कहहिं ससुर गुर सासू ॥
translation: मंत्री सुमंत्रजी की पत्नी और गुरु वशिष्ठजी की स्त्री अरुंधतीजी तथा और भी चतुर स्त्रियाँ स्नेह के साथ कोमल वाणी से कहती हैं कि तुमको तो (राजा ने) वनवास दिया नहीं है, इसलिए जो ससुर, गुरु और सास कहें, तुम तो वही करो ॥
english_translation: The wives of ministers, the teacher's wife, and other wise women speak gently and with affection: 'You were not given exile. Do what your father-in-law, teacher, and mother-in-law tell you.'
essence: Gentle advice can still pull against the heart.
simple_meaning: Wise women gently tell Sita that she has not been sent into exile, so she should do what her elders ask.
insight: It reveals how social duty can arrive wrapped in affection, making refusal emotionally harder.
modern_relevance: A group chat fills with caring advice from relatives after a family crisis. Everyone sounds loving, but the message is the same: stay, comply, adjust. The pressure feels gentle and heavy at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिख सीतलि हित मधुर मृदु सुनि सीतहि न सोहानि। सरद चंद चंदिनि लगत जनु चकई अकुलानि ॥
translation: यह शीतल, हितकारी, मधुर और कोमल सीख सुनने पर सीताजी को अच्छी नहीं लगी। (वे इस प्रकार व्याकुल हो गईं) मानो शरद ऋतु के चन्द्रमा की चाँदनी लगते ही चकई व्याकुल हो उठी हो ॥
english_translation: Hearing this cool, helpful, sweet, and gentle counsel did not please Sita. She grew restless like a chakor bird at the sight of autumn moonlight.
essence: Gentle advice cannot calm a heart already flying toward love.
simple_meaning: Sita does not welcome the gentle advice meant for her comfort. She feels restless and pained, like a bird disturbed by moonlight.
insight: It shows that emotional truth can overpower polite counsel, especially when devotion is already set on one path.
modern_relevance: A friend says, “It’ll be fine, just stay back.” But your chest tightens because the thing you want most is to go with the person you love. Reasonable advice can still feel wrong when the heart has already chosen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीय सकुच बस उतरु न देई। सो सुनि तमकि उठी कैकेई॥ मुनि पट भूषन भाजन आनी। आगें धरि बोली मृदु बानी ॥
translation: सीताजी संकोचवश उत्तर नहीं देतीं। इन बातों को सुनकर कैकेयी तमककर उठी। उसने मुनियों के वस्त्र, आभूषण (माला, मेखला आदि) और बर्तन (कमण्डलु आदि) लाकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी के आगे रख दिए और कोमल वाणी से कहा- ॥
english_translation: Sita, out of modesty, gave no reply. Hearing this, Kaikeyi sprang up in anger. She brought garments of ascetics, ornaments, and utensils, placed them before Ram, and spoke gently.
essence: Gentle words can carry a decisive blow.
simple_meaning: Sita stays silent from modesty. Kaikeyi reacts sharply, then places ascetic items before Ram and speaks politely.
insight: It teaches you to watch the force behind polite speech, not just its tone.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone avoids answering the question everyone is circling. Then a person smiles, slides a paper across the table, and changes everything without raising their voice.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नृपहि प्रानप्रिय तुम्ह रघुबीरा। सील सनेह न छाड़िहि भीरा॥ सुकृतु सुजसु परलोकु नसाऊ। तुम्हहि जान बन कहिहि न काऊ ॥
translation: हे रघुवीर! राजा को तुम प्राणों के समान प्रिय हो। भीरु (प्रेमवश दुर्बल हृदय के) राजा शील और स्नेह नहीं छोड़ेंगे! पुण्य, सुंदर यश और परलोक चाहे नष्ट हे जाए, पर तुम्हें वन जाने को वे कभी न कहेंगे ॥
english_translation: O Raghuvira, you are dearer to the king than his own life. In fear and love, he will not abandon virtue and affection. Even if merit, good name, and the next world are lost, he will never ask you to go to the forest.
essence: Tender love can make the hardest duty impossible to speak.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi says King Dasharath loves Ram more than his own life and would never send him to the forest, even if it ruined his virtue, reputation, and future.
insight: It shows how affection can delay duty, even when the cost will be enormous.
modern_relevance: A parent says, “I could never ask you to leave,” while knowing a hard decision is coming. The tenderness is real — and that is what makes the later break unbearable.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: अस बिचारि सोइ करहु जो भावा। राम जननि सिख सुनि सुखु पावा॥ भूपहि बचन बानसम लागे। करहिं न प्रान पयान अभागे ॥
translation: ऐसा विचारकर जो तुम्हें अच्छा लगे वही करो। माता की सीख सुनकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने (बड़ा) सुख पाया, परन्तु राजा को ये वचन बाण के समान लगे। (वे सोचने लगे) अब भी अभागे प्राण (क्यों) नहीं निकलते! ॥
english_translation: Thinking thus, do whatever you like. Hearing the mother’s counsel, Ram found joy. The king’s words struck like arrows; the unlucky man still did not die.
essence: Gentle words can carry the sharpest wound.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi speaks as if she is giving gentle advice, but her words wound Dasharath deeply. The same words that bring Ram joy feel like arrows to the king.
insight: It teaches you to notice how tone and intention can hide harm behind polite language.
modern_relevance: A message meant to sound reasonable lands like a slap in a family group chat. One person hears calm advice; another hears betrayal. The same sentence can carry two completely different worlds.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लोग बिकल मुरुछित नरनाहू। काह करिअ कछु सूझ न काहू॥ रामु तुरत मुनि बेषु बनाई। चले जनक जननिहि सिरु नाई ॥
translation: राजा मूर्छित हो गए, लोग व्याकुल हैं। किसी को कुछ सूझ नहीं पड़ता कि क्या करें। श्री रामचन्द्रजी तुरंत मुनि का वेष बनाकर और माता-पिता को सिर नवाकर चल दिए ॥
english_translation: The king fell unconscious, and everyone was distraught. No one knew what to do. Ram at once dressed as a sage and left, bowing to his parents.
essence: Duty moves first, even when everyone else is overwhelmed.
simple_meaning: The king collapses, everyone panics, and Ram immediately prepares to leave in the garb of a sage after bowing to his parents.
insight: It shifts attention from emotional chaos to the one necessary action that must be done now.
modern_relevance: A family crisis has everyone speaking at once, but one person still packs the bag, makes the call, and steps forward. Clear duty cuts through panic.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सजि बन साजु समाजु सबु बनिता बंधु समेत। बंदि बिप्र गुर चरन प्रभु चले करि सबहि अचेत ॥
translation: वन का सब साज-सामान सजकर (वन के लिए आवश्यक वस्तुओं को साथ लेकर) श्री रामचन्द्रजी स्त्री (श्री सीताजी) और भाई (लक्ष्मणजी) सहित, ब्राह्मण और गुरु के चरणों की वंदना करके सबको अचेत करके चले ॥
english_translation: Having prepared all the forest provisions, the Lord departed with Sita and Lakshman. Bowing to the Brahmins and the guru's feet, he left everyone stunned.
essence: Prepare fully, bow properly, and step into exile without complaint.
simple_meaning: Ram leaves for the forest fully prepared, with Sita and Lakshman beside him, after bowing to the guru and the Brahmins.
insight: It teaches you to meet forced change with readiness and reverence, not panic.
modern_relevance: You close the apartment door after packing the last box, then pause to thank the neighbor who helped. The move hurts, but the leaving can still be graceful.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निकसि बसिष्ठ द्वार भए ठाढ़े। देखे लोग बिरह दव दाढ़े॥ कहि प्रिय बचन सकल समुझाए। बिप्र बृंद रघुबीर बोलाए ॥
translation: राजमहल से निकलकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी वशिष्ठजी के दरवाजे पर जा खड़े हुए और देखा कि सब लोग विरह की अग्नि में जल रहे हैं। उन्होंने प्रिय वचन कहकर सबको समझाया, फिर श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने ब्राह्मणों की मंडली को बुलाया ॥
english_translation: Leaving the palace, Ram stood at Vashishtha's door and saw everyone burning in the fire of separation. He spoke kind words, comforted them all, and then called the assembly of brahmins.
essence: Calm words can hold a room on fire.
simple_meaning: Ram steps out, sees everyone suffering from separation, comforts them with gentle words, and gathers the brahmins.
insight: It teaches emotional steadiness in crisis: soothe others first, then move to action.
modern_relevance: You walk into a house after bad news, and everyone is frozen, crying, or angry. Instead of feeding the panic, you lower your voice, steady the room, and handle what must be handled.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गुर सन कहि बरषासन दीन्हे। आदर दान बिनय बस कीन्हे॥ जाचक दान मान संतोषे। मीत पुनीत प्रेम परितोषे ॥
translation: गुरुजी से कहकर उन सबको वर्षाशन (वर्षभर का भोजन) दिए और आदर, दान तथा विनय से उन्हें वश में कर लिया। फिर याचकों को दान और मान देकर संतुष्ट किया तथा मित्रों को पवित्र प्रेम से प्रसन्न किया ॥
english_translation: He gave the guru a year’s provisions, and used respect, gifts, and humility to win them over. He satisfied the beggars with charity and honor, and delighted his friends with pure love.
essence: True duty includes honoring the teacher, the needy, and the beloved.
simple_meaning: Ram honors the guru, supports the needy, and cares for friends with loving generosity.
insight: It shifts duty from bare obedience to generous, relationship-centered action.
modern_relevance: Before a long move, you pack a box for your teacher, send food to the neighbor who helps everyone, and thank the friend who showed up. Small acts of care steady the whole day.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दासीं दास बोलाइ बहोरी। गुरहि सौंपि बोले कर जोरी॥ सब कै सार सँभार गोसाईं। करबि जनक जननी की नाईं ॥
translation: फिर दास-दासियों को बुलाकर उन्हें गुरुजी को सौंपकर, हाथ जोड़कर बोले- हे गुसाईं! इन सबकी माता-पिता के समान सार-संभार (देख-रेख) करते रहिएगा ॥
english_translation: Then he called the servants and maidservants again, entrusted them to the guru, and said with folded hands: "Lord, care for all of them as a mother and father would."
essence: True duty protects even the smallest people around you.
simple_meaning: Ram hands the servants over to the guru and asks him to care for everyone like a parent would.
insight: It shifts duty from self-protection to protective care for everyone dependent on you.
modern_relevance: You move out of a house and still worry about the cleaner, the driver, the cook — whether they’ll be looked after. That quiet concern is the standard here.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: बारहिं बार जोरि जुग पानी। कहत रामु सब सन मृदु बानी॥ सोइ सब भाँति मोर हितकारी। जेहि तें रहै भुआल सुखारी ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी बार-बार दोनों हाथ जोड़कर सबसे कोमल वाणी कहते हैं कि मेरा सब प्रकार से हितकारी मित्र वही होगा, जिसकी चेष्टा से महाराज सुखी रहें ॥
english_translation: Rama repeatedly folded his hands and spoke gently to everyone: "My true well-wisher is the one whose efforts keep the king happy."
essence: Real help is whatever truly steadies the one who must be protected.
simple_meaning: Rama speaks politely to everyone and says that the real helper is the one who keeps the king content and at ease.
insight: It shifts attention from self-expression to practical care for the person at the center of the situation.
modern_relevance: You are trying to help a family member through a hard day, and the loudest advice is not the best one. Real support is the choice that actually eases their burden, not the one that makes you feel useful.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: मातु सकल मोरे बिरहँ जेहिं न होहिं दुख दीन। सोइ उपाउ तुम्ह करेहु सब पुर जन परम प्रबीन ॥
translation: हे परम चतुर पुरवासी सज्जनों! आप लोग सब वही उपाए कीजिएगा, जिससे मेरी सब माताएँ मेरे विरह के दुःख से दुःखी न हों ॥
english_translation: O most skilful people of the city, please do whatever ensures that all my mothers do not suffer grief from my separation.
essence: True care measures separation by the pain it leaves behind.
simple_meaning: Ram asks the city’s wise people to find a way that keeps his mothers from suffering because of his separation.
insight: It shifts attention from personal departure to the burden that departure places on others.
modern_relevance: You are packing for a move and keep thinking about the parent who will sit in the quiet after you leave. Real care means planning for their hurt, not just your departure.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: एहि बिधि राम सबहि समुझावा। गुर पद पदुम हरषि सिरु नावा॥ गनपति गौरि गिरीसु मनाई। चले असीस पाइ रघुराई ॥
translation: इस प्रकार श्री रामजी ने सबको समझाया और हर्षित होकर गुरुजी के चरणकमलों में सिर नवाया। फिर गणेशजी, पार्वतीजी और कैलासपति महादेवजी को मनाकर तथा आशीर्वाद पाकर श्री रघुनाथजी चले ॥
english_translation: In this way, Ram explained everything to everyone, then joyfully bowed his head to the lotus feet of his teacher. After pleasing Ganesh, Parvati, and Lord Shiva, and receiving their blessings, Raghunath departed.
essence: True dignity bows before it moves on.
simple_meaning: Ram settles everyone’s concerns, bows to his teacher, honors Ganesh, Parvati, and Shiva, and leaves with their blessings.
insight: It teaches graceful departure: resolve what must be said, honor your teachers, and move on without self-importance.
modern_relevance: You finish a hard conversation, thank the people who guided you, and leave without ego. The moment stays clean because you did not make it about yourself.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम चलत अति भयउ बिषादू। सुनि न जाइ पुर आरत नादू॥ कुसगुन लंक अवध अति सोकू। हरष बिषाद बिबस सुरलोकू ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के चलते ही बड़ा भारी विषाद हो गया। नगर का आर्तनाद (हाहाकर) सुना नहीं जाता। लंका में बुरे शकुन होने लगे, अयोध्या में अत्यन्त शोक छा गया और देवलोक में सब हर्ष और विषाद दोनों के वश में गए। (हर्ष इस बात का था कि अब राक्षसों का नाश होगा और विषाद अयोध्यावासियों के शोक के कारण था) ॥
english_translation: As Rama departed, deep grief arose. The city's cries could not be borne. Ominous signs appeared in Lanka, great sorrow fell on Ayodhya, and even the heavenly worlds were caught between joy and grief.
essence: Rama's departure sends grief and omens through every realm.
simple_meaning: Rama's departure shakes every world: Ayodhya grieves, Lanka shows bad omens, and even the higher worlds feel mixed joy and sorrow.
insight: It shifts attention from one event to the many layers of grief and consequence it creates.
modern_relevance: A train pulls away after a goodbye no one wanted. One person leaves, but the whole house feels altered — and everyone reacts differently to the same loss.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गइ मुरुछा तब भूपति जागे। बोलि सुमंत्रु कहन अस लागे॥ रामु चले बन प्रान न जाहीं। केहि सुख लागि रहत तन माहीं ॥
translation: मूर्छा दूर हुई, तब राजा जागे और सुमंत्र को बुलाकर ऐसा कहने लगे- श्री राम वन को चले गए, पर मेरे प्राण नहीं जा रहे हैं। न जाने ये किस सुख के लिए शरीर में टिक रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: When his fainting passed, the king woke and called Sumantra, saying: "Rama has gone to the forest, yet my life does not leave. For what happiness does this body still remain?"
essence: Life can remain in the body after joy has already left.
simple_meaning: Dasharath wakes from fainting and realizes Rama has gone to the forest. He feels his own life should leave too, because the body has no joy left without Rama.
insight: It shifts attention from outward survival to the inner fact of grief: the body can remain while the person feels already gone.
modern_relevance: You open your phone and see the message that changes everything. The room is the same, your body is the same, but the person who made life feel alive is suddenly gone.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: एहि तें कवन ब्यथा बलवाना। जो दुखु पाइ तजहिं तनु प्राना॥ पुनि धरि धीर कहइ नरनाहू। लै रथु संग सखा तुम्ह जाहू ॥
translation: इससे अधिक बलवती और कौन सी व्यथा होगी, जिस दुःख को पाकर प्राण शरीर को छोड़ेंगे। फिर धीरज धरकर राजा ने कहा- हे सखा! तुम रथ लेकर श्री राम के साथ जाओ ॥
english_translation: What pain could be greater than this, when grief makes life leave the body? Then, gathering himself, the king said, “Friend, take the chariot and go with Ram.”
essence: Grief can break the body and still leave duty intact.
simple_meaning: Dasharath says no pain is greater than this grief, because it is killing him. After steadying himself, he asks Sumantra to take the chariot and go with Ram.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-consuming pain to one last responsible action.
modern_relevance: You get the worst news of your life, sit in silence for a long minute, and still manage one careful text to help someone else. Grief does not erase duty.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: सुठि सुकुमार कुमार दोउ जनकसुता सुकुमारि। रथ चढ़ाइ देखराइ बनु फिरेहु गएँ दिन चारि ॥
translation: अत्यन्त सुकुमार दोनों कुमारों को और सुकुमारी जानकी को रथ में चढ़ाकर, वन दिखलाकर चार दिन के बाद लौट आना ॥
english_translation: Take the very tender princes and the tender daughter of Janaka in the chariot, show them the forest, and return after four days.
essence: Grief turns exile into a brief errand to survive the pain.
simple_meaning: Dasharath asks that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita be taken by chariot to see the forest and brought back after four days.
insight: It shows how grief clings to a temporary story when it cannot bear permanent loss.
modern_relevance: You keep saying, “Just a few days,” while helping someone pack for a move that changes everything. The mind reaches for any small promise that makes loss feel manageable.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: जौं नहिं फिरहिं धीर दोउ भाई। सत्यसंध दृढ़ब्रत रघुराई॥ तौ तुम्ह बिनय करेहु कर जोरी। फेरिअ प्रभु मिथिलेसकिसोरी ॥॥
translation: यदि धैर्यवान दोनों भाई न लौटें- क्योंकि श्री रघुनाथजी प्रण के सच्चे और दृढ़ता से नियम का पालन करने वाले हैं- तो तुम हाथ जोड़कर विनती करना कि हे प्रभो! जनककुमारी सीताजी को तो लौटा दीजिए ॥
english_translation: If the two brothers do not return, for Raghunath is steadfast in truth and fixed vows, then you should pray with folded hands: "Lord, please send back the princess of Mithila."
essence: Steadfast vows can make one request more important than everything else.
simple_meaning: If the brothers do not come back, ask only for Sita to be returned. Dasharath trusts Ram's vow and focuses on protecting the daughter-in-law.
insight: It shifts attention from broad loss to the one responsibility that cannot be neglected.
modern_relevance: A parent watches a child leave for a hard move across the country and cannot fix everything. In the middle of helplessness, the heart narrows to one urgent prayer: keep the one who is most vulnerable safe.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: जब सिय कानन देखि डेराई। कहेहु मोरि सिख अवसरु पाई॥ सासु ससुर अस कहेउ सँदेसू। पुत्रि फिरिअ बन बहुत कलेसू ॥
translation: जब सीता वन को देखकर डरें, तब मौका पाकर मेरी यह सीख उनसे कहना कि तुम्हारे सास और ससुर ने ऐसा संदेश कहा है कि हे पुत्री! तुम लौट चलो, वन में बहुत क्लेश हैं ॥
english_translation: When Sita sees the forest and grows afraid, then, at a fitting moment, say this to her: 'Your mother-in-law and father-in-law have sent this message: Daughter, return home. The forest holds much hardship.'
essence: Borrowed concern can hide a controlling intent.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi tells the messenger to speak gently to Sita if the forest frightens her, and to urge her to return because forest life is full of hardship.
insight: It shows how persuasion often works through borrowed authority and emotional vulnerability.
modern_relevance: Someone waits until you look uncertain, then calls it concern and presses you toward the safer choice. The timing is gentle; the intention is not.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पितुगृह कबहुँ कबहुँ ससुरारी। रहेहु जहाँ रुचि होइ तुम्हारी॥ एहि बिधि करेहु उपाय कदंबा। फिरइ त होइ प्रान अवलंबा ॥
translation: कभी पिता के घर, कभी ससुराल, जहाँ तुम्हारी इच्छा हो, वहीं रहना। इस प्रकार तुम बहुत से उपाय करना। यदि सीताजी लौट आईं तो मेरे प्राणों को सहारा हो जाएगा ॥
english_translation: Stay sometimes in your father’s house, sometimes in your in-laws’ house, wherever you wish. In this way, use any means. If Sita returns, it will become the support of my life.
essence: Desperation will offer any bargain to keep love from leaving.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is still trying to bring Sita back by offering her any arrangement she wants, hoping that Sita’s return will save Dasharath’s life.
insight: It shows how fear can make a person grasp at any compromise to undo loss.
modern_relevance: You keep texting, calling, and making promises you never planned to make because someone you love is slipping away. Panic makes the mind negotiate with reality.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: नाहिं त मोर मरनु परिनामा। कछु न बसाइ भएँ बिधि बामा॥ अस कहि मुरुछि परा महि राऊ। रामु लखनु सिय आनि देखाऊ ॥
translation: (नहीं तो अंत में मेरा मरण ही होगा। विधाता के विपरीत होने पर कुछ वश नहीं चलता। हा! राम, लक्ष्मण और सीता को लाकर दिखाओ। ऐसा कहकर राजा मूर्छित होकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े ॥
english_translation: “Otherwise, my death will be the result. Nothing can be done when fate turns hostile.” Saying this, the king fainted and fell to the earth. “Bring Ram, Lakshman, and Sita before me.”
essence: When helplessness deepens, even a king collapses.
simple_meaning: Dasharath collapses under grief and helplessness. He feels that if Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are not brought back, death is all that remains.
insight: It shows grief at the edge of surrender, where speech breaks and the body registers loss first.
modern_relevance: You stare at an empty chair after the argument, the phone still silent, and your chest tightens because nothing you can say will undo what has happened.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: पाइ रजायसु नाइ सिरु रथु अति बेग बनाइ। गयउ जहाँ बाहेर नगर सीय सहित दोउ भाइ ॥
translation: सुमंत्रजी राजा की आज्ञा पाकर, सिर नवाकर और बहुत जल्दी रथ जुड़वाकर वहाँ गए, जहाँ नगर के बाहर सीताजी सहित दोनों भाई थे ॥
english_translation: Receiving the king's command, Sumantra bowed his head, quickly prepared the chariot, and went to where the two brothers were outside the city with Sita.
essence: Obedience moves faster than hesitation.
simple_meaning: Sumantra obeys the king at once, prepares the chariot quickly, and goes to Rama, Lakshman, and Sita outside the city.
insight: It shifts attention from hesitation to prompt, respectful action when a rightful command arrives.
modern_relevance: Your manager calls with a last-minute change, and you stop arguing and just move. The moment is not for drama; it is for clean, immediate response.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब सुमंत्र नृप बचन सुनाए। करि बिनती रथ रामु चढ़ाए॥ चढ़ि रथ सीय सहित दोउ भाई। चले हृदयँ अवधहि सिरु नाई ॥
translation: तब (वहाँ पहुँचकर) सुमंत्र ने राजा के वचन श्री रामचन्द्रजी को सुनाए और विनती करके उनको रथ पर चढ़ाया। सीताजी सहित दोनों भाई रथ पर चढ़कर हृदय में अयोध्या को सिर नवाकर चले ॥
english_translation: Then Sumantra conveyed the king's command, and with humble request helped Ram onto the chariot. The two brothers rode with Sita and departed, bowing their hearts to Ayodhya.
essence: A painful departure can still be carried with reverence.
simple_meaning: Sumantra brings the king's order, places Ram on the chariot, and the three depart after bowing inwardly to Ayodhya.
insight: It shifts attention from the mechanics of departure to the dignity of leaving with inward respect.
modern_relevance: You pack the car after a family argument, everyone quiet, nobody wanting the moment to be real. The departure itself carries the grief.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चलत रामु लखि अवध अनाथा। बिकल लोग सब लागे साथा॥ कृपासिंधु बहुबिधि समुझावहिं। फिरहिं प्रेम बस पुनि फिरि आवहिं ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी को जाते हुए और अयोध्या को अनाथ (होते हुए) देखकर सब लोग व्याकुल होकर उनके साथ हो लिए। कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामजी उन्हें बहुत तरह से समझाते हैं, तो वे (अयोध्या की ओर) लौट जाते हैं, परन्तु प्रेमवश फिर लौट आते हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ram depart, Ayodhya felt orphaned. The people became distraught and followed him. The ocean of compassion tried many ways to comfort them, but they returned only to come back again out of love.
essence: Love overrules farewell and keeps calling people back.
simple_meaning: As Ram leaves, Ayodhya feels abandoned and everyone runs after him. Ram gently tries to calm them, but love keeps drawing them back to him.
insight: It shifts attention from formal departure to the pull of attachment that keeps reversing separation.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you depend on walk out of the room, and the whole place feels hollow. You try to act normal, then find yourself following them just to stay near a little longer.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लागति अवध भयावनि भारी। मानहुँ कालराति अँधिआरी॥ घोर जंतु सम पुर नर नारी। डरपहिं एकहि एक निहारी ॥
translation: अयोध्यापुरी बड़ी डरावनी लग रही है, मानो अंधकारमयी कालरात्रि ही हो। नगर के नर-नारी भयानक जन्तुओं के समान एक-दूसरे को देखकर डर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Ayodhya felt terribly fearsome, as if dark Night herself had come. The city's men and women feared one another like savage creatures.
essence: Loss can make a familiar city feel like a dark wilderness.
simple_meaning: Ayodhya feels so dark and shaken that everyone fears everyone else.
insight: It turns grief into atmosphere: a broken bond can distort how an entire community sees itself.
modern_relevance: A house goes silent after one devastating argument. Nobody says it, but everyone moves carefully, afraid of the next glance or word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: घर मसान परिजन जनु भूता। सुत हित मीत मनहुँ जमदूता॥ बागन्ह बिटप बेलि कुम्हिलाहीं। सरित सरोवर देखि न जाहीं ॥
translation: घर श्मशान, कुटुम्बी भूत-प्रेत और पुत्र, हितैषी और मित्र मानो यमराज के दूत हैं। बगीचों में वृक्ष और बेलें कुम्हला रही हैं। नदी और तालाब ऐसे भयानक लगते हैं कि उनकी ओर देखा भी नहीं जाता ॥
english_translation: The house feels like a cremation ground; relatives seem like ghosts; sons, friends, and well-wishers seem like messengers of death. The garden trees and vines wither, and rivers and ponds are too dreadful even to look at.
essence: Grief can turn home itself into a place of fear.
simple_meaning: Ayodhya feels so grief-stricken that home, family, friends, gardens, rivers, and ponds all seem frightening and lifeless.
insight: It shows how sorrow distorts perception, turning ordinary life into something unbearable.
modern_relevance: You walk into a house after bad news and everything feels wrong — the chairs, the plants, even the silence. Loss can change the whole shape of a place.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हय गय कोटिन्ह केलिमृग पुरपसु चातक मोर। पिक रथांग सुक सारिका सारस हंस चकोर ॥
translation: करोड़ों घोड़े, हाथी, खेलने के लिए पाले हुए हिरन, नगर के (गाय, बैल, बकरी आदि) पशु, पपीहे, मोर, कोयल, चकवे, तोते, मैना, सारस, हंस और चकोर- ॥
english_translation: Millions of horses and elephants, tame deer, city animals, and birds like chataka, peacock, cuckoo, chakravaka, parrot, myna, saras, swan, and chakor.
essence: The city’s sorrow spreads until even its creatures seem changed.
simple_meaning: Ayodhya is filled with countless animals and birds, all listed as part of the scene. The verse deepens the sense that the whole city is shaken by Ram's absence.
insight: It shifts attention from human grief alone to a whole environment marked by absence.
modern_relevance: A house goes strangely quiet after someone leaves for good. The pets, the rooms, the familiar sounds — everything still exists, but the whole place feels altered.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम बियोग बिकल सब ठाढ़े। जहँ तहँ मनहुँ चित्र लिखि काढ़े॥ नगरु सफल बनु गहबर भारी। खग मृग बिपुल सकल नर नारी ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के वियोग में सभी व्याकुल हुए जहाँ-तहाँ (ऐसे चुपचाप स्थिर होकर) खड़े हैं, मानो तसवीरों में लिखकर बनाए हुए हैं। नगर मानो फलों से परिपूर्ण बड़ा भारी सघन वन था। नगर निवासी सब स्त्री-पुरुष बहुत से पशु-पक्षी थे। (अर्थात अवधपुरी अर्थ, धर्म, काम, मोक्ष चारों फलों को देने वाली नगरी थी और सब स्त्री-पुरुष सुख से उन फलों को प्राप्त करते थे।) ॥
english_translation: All stood stunned in Rama's separation, as if painted and fixed in place. The city was like a great, fruitful forest, full of birds, beasts, men, and women.
essence: Rama's absence turns a living city into stillness.
simple_meaning: Rama's absence left everyone stunned and motionless. Ayodhya felt like a dense, fruitful forest full of life, yet emptied by grief.
insight: It shifts attention from outward activity to the paralysis grief creates in an entire community.
modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after the bad news lands. Everyone is still online, still awake, but no one knows what to say. Grief can make a living home feel unmoving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिधि कैकई किरातिनि कीन्ही। जेहिं दव दुसह दसहुँ दिसि दीन्ही॥ सहि न सके रघुबर बिरहागी। चले लोग सब ब्याकुल भागी ॥
translation: विधाता ने कैकेयी को भीलनी बनाया, जिसने दसों दिशाओं में दुःसह दावाग्नि (भयानक आग) लगा दी। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विरह की इस अग्नि को लोग सह न सके। सब लोग व्याकुल होकर भाग चले ॥
english_translation: Providence made Kaikeyi a huntress, and she set a terrible fire in all ten directions. People could not bear the burning grief of separation from Raghubar. Everyone, overwhelmed, ran away in distress.
essence: One cruel turn can set the whole world burning.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi's action is compared to a fire spreading everywhere, and Ram's separation hurts so deeply that no one can bear it.
insight: It frames harmful action as a spreading fire and shows how grief can overwhelm an entire community.
modern_relevance: A single decision in a family group chat can scorch every relationship in the room. What starts as one person's demand can leave everyone else stunned, silent, and emotionally burned.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सबहिं बिचारु कीन्ह मन माहीं। राम लखन सिय बिनु सुखु नाहीं॥ जहाँ रामु तहँ सबुइ समाजू। बिनु रघुबीर अवध नहिं काजू ॥
translation: सबने मन में विचार कर लिया कि श्री रामजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी के बिना सुख नहीं है। जहाँ श्री रामजी रहेंगे, वहीं सारा समाज रहेगा। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के बिना अयोध्या में हम लोगों का कुछ काम नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Everyone thought in their hearts: there is no happiness without Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Wherever Ram stays, that alone is the true assembly. Without Raghubir, Ayodhya has no purpose.
essence: Without Ram, even Ayodhya has no real purpose.
simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya realize that life without Ram, Lakshman, and Sita feels empty. Their city only feels complete when Ram is present.
insight: It shifts attention from outer order to the presence that gives a place meaning.
modern_relevance: You enter a house after someone essential has left, and the rooms still look the same. Nothing feels alive until the person who makes the place feel like home returns.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चले साथ अस मंत्रु दृढ़ाई। सुर दुर्लभ सुख सदन बिहाई॥ राम चरन पंकज प्रिय जिन्हही। बिषय भोग बस करहिं कि तिन्हही ॥
translation: ऐसा विचार दृढ़ करके देवताओं को भी दुर्लभ सुखों से पूर्ण घरों को छोड़कर सब श्री रामचन्द्रजी के साथ चले पड़े। जिनको श्री रामजी के चरणकमल प्यारे हैं, उन्हें क्या कभी विषय भोग वश में कर सकते हैं ॥
english_translation: Having firmly resolved, they left homes filled with pleasures hard even for the gods to obtain, and went with Ram. Those who love Ram's lotus feet can never be ruled by worldly pleasures.
essence: Love for Ram breaks the spell of comfort.
simple_meaning: The people made a firm decision, left comfortable homes behind, and followed Ram. Anyone who truly loves Ram's feet cannot be ruled by worldly pleasures.
insight: It shifts loyalty from comfort to devotion, showing that attachment weakens when love becomes firm.
modern_relevance: You have a stable life, good food, and a safe home, but your heart says something deeper matters. When that call becomes clear, comfort stops being the master.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बालक बृद्ध बिहाइ गृहँ लगे लोग सब साथ। तमसा तीर निवासु किय प्रथम दिवस रघुनाथ ॥
translation: बच्चों और बूढ़ों को घरों में छोड़कर सब लोग साथ हो लिए। पहले दिन श्री रघुनाथजी ने तमसा नदी के तीर पर निवास किया ॥
english_translation: Leaving children and elders at home, everyone went along together. On the first day, Raghunath stayed on the bank of the Tamasa River.
essence: Even exile begins as a collective act of love.
simple_meaning: Everyone left home and followed Ram. On the first day, Ram camped by the Tamasa River.
insight: It turns a departure into a shared act of loyalty, not just a journey.
modern_relevance: A family leaves the house before dawn for a move nobody wanted, carrying boxes in silence. The first stop feels small, but it marks the moment life has already changed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रघुपति प्रजा प्रेमबस देखी। सदय हृदयँ दुखु भयउ बिसेषी॥ करुनामय रघुनाथ गोसाँई। बेगि पाइअहिं पीर पराई ॥
translation: प्रजा को प्रेमवश देखकर श्री रघुनाथजी के दयालु हृदय में बड़ा दुःख हुआ। प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी करुणामय हैं। पराई पीड़ा को वे तुरंत पा जाते हैं (अर्थात दूसरे का दुःख देखकर वे तुरंत स्वयं दुःखित हो जाते हैं) ॥
english_translation: Seeing the people moved by love, Raghupati's compassionate heart felt deep sorrow. The merciful Lord quickly feels another's pain as his own.
essence: Compassion means another person's pain lands in you at once.
simple_meaning: Ram sees the people acting from love, and his compassionate heart aches for their suffering. He feels other people's pain immediately as his own.
insight: It trains attention toward another person's suffering, not just their behavior, and turns sympathy into quick, caring response.
modern_relevance: You watch a friend smile through exhaustion after helping everyone else at the wedding. The room is loud, but you notice the strain behind their face. Real compassion catches that hidden hurt immediately.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहि सप्रेम मृदु बचन सुहाए। बहुबिधि राम लोग समुझाए॥ किए धरम उपदेस घनेरे। लोग प्रेम बस फिरहिं न फेरे ॥
translation: प्रेमयुक्त कोमल और सुंदर वचन कहकर श्री रामजी ने बहुत प्रकार से लोगों को समझाया और बहुतेरे धर्म संबंधी उपदेश दिए, परन्तु प्रेमवश लोग लौटाए लौटते नहीं ॥
english_translation: Speaking sweet, gentle, loving words, Ram explained many things to the people in many ways and gave them many teachings about dharma, but out of love the people would not turn back.
essence: Love can hold people so tightly that even dharma cannot send them back.
simple_meaning: Ram gently and lovingly tried to explain dharma to the people, but their love for him kept them from turning back.
insight: It shows that affection can override even the clearest practical advice.
modern_relevance: You tell a friend to go home, rest, and stop worrying about you. They keep standing there, unable to walk away because caring has become stronger than instruction.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीलु सनेहु छाड़ि नहिं जाई। असमंजस बस भे रघुराई॥ लोग सोग श्रम बस गए सोई। कछुक देवमायाँ मति मोई ॥
translation: शील और स्नेह छोड़ा नहीं जाता। श्री रघुनाथजी असमंजस के अधीन हो गए (दुविधा में पड़ गए)। शोक और परिश्रम (थकावट) के मारे लोग सो गए और कुछ देवताओं की माया से भी उनकी बुद्धि मोहित हो गई ॥
english_translation: Character and affection cannot be abandoned. Raghunath was overcome by bewilderment. People fell asleep from grief and exhaustion, and some were deluded by the divine illusion.
essence: Love and virtue do not vanish, even when confusion clouds action.
simple_meaning: Ram cannot simply cast off his gentleness and love, even when the situation has become confusing. Meanwhile, the people are overwhelmed by grief and exhaustion, and some lose their clarity.
insight: It shows that compassion does not erase human strain; it reveals how hard righteous action can be under pressure.
modern_relevance: You are trying to stay kind in a family crisis, but every conversation seems to pull you in two directions. Even steadiness can wobble when love, duty, and exhaustion collide.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जबहिं जाम जुग जामिनि बीती। राम सचिव सन कहेउ सप्रीती॥ खोज मारि रथु हाँकहु ताता। आन उपायँ बनिहि नहिं बाता ॥
translation: जब दो पहर बीत गई, तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने प्रेमपूर्वक मंत्री सुमंत्र से कहा- हे तात! रथ के खोज मारकर (अर्थात पहियों के चिह्नों से दिशा का पता न चले इस प्रकार) रथ को हाँकिए। और किसी उपाय से बात नहीं बनेगी ॥
english_translation: When two watches of the night had passed, Ram said lovingly to Sumantra, "Drive the chariot so its tracks cannot be traced, father. No other way will work."
essence: The right move can be tender and tactical at once.
simple_meaning: Ram gently asks Sumantra to drive the chariot in a way that leaves no tracks, because no other method will do.
insight: It shifts attention from emotion to precise action: do what the moment requires, cleanly and without delay.
modern_relevance: You slip out before dawn after a hard goodbye, trying not to wake the whole house. Some exits need care, not drama.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: राम लखन सिय जान चढ़ि संभु चरन सिरु नाइ। सचिवँ चलायउ तुरत रथु इत उत खोज दुराइ ॥
translation: शंकरजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर श्री रामजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी रथ पर सवार हुए। मंत्री ने तुरंत ही रथ को इधर-उधर खोज छिपाकर चला दिया ॥
english_translation: After bowing their heads at Shiva's feet, Ram, Lakshman, and Sita mounted the chariot. The minister quickly drove it away, hiding the tracks in every direction.
essence: Leave with reverence, then go without looking back.
simple_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita bow to Shiva before leaving in the chariot. Sumantra quickly drives them away and hides the tracks.
insight: It shifts attention from drama to disciplined departure: honor what matters, then move without delay.
modern_relevance: You leave before dawn with one bag, hoping no one sees the exit. A quiet goodbye, a final bow, and then the road takes over.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जागे सकल लोग भएँ भोरू। गे रघुनाथ भयउ अति सोरू॥ रथ कर खोज कतहुँ नहिं पावहिं। राम राम कहि चहुँ दिसि धावहिं ॥
translation: सबेरा होते ही सब लोग जागे, तो बड़ा शोर मचा कि रघुनाथजी चले गए। कहीं रथ का खोज नहीं पाते, सब 'हा राम! हा राम!' पुकारते हुए चारों ओर दौड़ रहे हैं ॥
