english_translation: At dawn, everyone woke up and there was a great uproar: Raghunath had gone. They could not find the chariot anywhere, and all ran in every direction crying, “Ram, Ram!”
essence: Absence turns a quiet morning into collective panic.
simple_meaning: At dawn, the whole camp wakes to panic. Ram is gone, the chariot cannot be found, and everyone runs around crying out his name.
insight: It shows how quickly uncertainty spreads when support disappears and no one knows what happened.
modern_relevance: You wake up and the person who was supposed to lead the meeting has vanished, leaving only unanswered messages. The room turns restless in seconds.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मनहुँ बारिनिधि बूड़ जहाजू। भयउ बिकल बड़ बनिक समाजू॥ एकहि एक देहिं उपदेसू। तजे राम हम जानि कलेसू ॥
translation: मानो समुद्र में जहाज डूब गया हो, जिससे व्यापारियों का समुदाय बहुत ही व्याकुल हो उठा हो। वे एक-दूसरे को उपदेश देते हैं कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने, हम लोगों को क्लेश होगा, यह जानकर छोड़ दिया है ॥
english_translation: It was as if a ship had sunk in the ocean, and the whole merchant crowd was thrown into deep distress. They kept advising one another, saying, "Ram has left us, knowing that we will suffer."
essence: Ram's absence hits like a shipwreck.
simple_meaning: Ram's departure shocks everyone so deeply that they feel like a ship has sunk in the sea. The whole crowd is stunned and keeps telling itself that Ram left to spare them pain.
insight: It turns grief into a shared shock, showing how deeply one beloved presence can hold a whole community together.
modern_relevance: You wake up to a message that changes everything, and suddenly the day feels unmoored. The mind keeps circling the same sentence, trying to make sense of the loss.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निंदहिं आपु सराहहिं मीना। धिग जीवनु रघुबीर बिहीना॥ जौं पै प्रिय बियोगु बिधि कीन्हा। तौ कस मरनु न मागें दीन्हा ॥
translation: वे लोग अपनी निंदा करते हैं और मछलियों की सराहना करते हैं। (कहते हैं-) श्री रामचन्द्रजी के बिना हमारे जीने को धिक्कार है। विधाता ने यदि प्यारे का वियोग ही रचा, तो फिर उसने माँगने पर मृत्यु क्यों नहीं दी! ॥
english_translation: They blame themselves and praise the fish: 'Life without Raghubir is cursed. If fate has already made us lose the beloved, why was death not given when we asked for it?'
essence: Love can make life feel cursed when the beloved is gone.
simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya feel life has no value without Ram. They are so overwhelmed by separation that they even wish death had come instead.
insight: It names grief honestly: when someone central is missing, even survival can feel like a burden.
modern_relevance: You open your phone and see the message that changes everything: they are gone, and the day still expects you to continue. This verse knows that unbearable gap.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि बिधि करत प्रलाप कलापा। आए अवध भरे परितापा॥ बिषम बियोगु न जाइ बखाना। अवधि आस सब राखहिं प्राना ॥
translation: इस प्रकार बहुत से प्रलाप करते हुए वे संताप से भरे हुए अयोध्याजी में आए। उन लोगों के विषम वियोग की दशा का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। (चौदह साल की) अवधि की आशा से ही वे प्राणों को रख रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: In this way, grieving and lamenting, they came to Ayodhya filled with sorrow. Their unbearable separation cannot be described. They kept their lives only by holding on to the hope that fourteen years would pass.
essence: A fixed hope can keep you alive inside deep separation.
simple_meaning: The people return to Ayodhya in deep sorrow, unable to bear the separation from Ram. They stay alive by clinging to the hope that the exile will end.
insight: It shifts attention from total despair to the one time-bound hope that makes endurance possible.
modern_relevance: You came home after the hospital visit and sat in the car for ten minutes, unable to speak. What kept you from falling apart was the date circled on the calendar.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम दरस हित नेम ब्रत लगे करन नर नारि। मनहुँ कोक कोकी कमल दीन बिहीन तमारि ॥
translation: (सब) स्त्री-पुरुष श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन के लिए नियम और व्रत करने लगे और ऐसे दुःखी हो गए जैसे चकवा, चकवी और कमल सूर्य के बिना दीन हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: For the sight of Ram, men and women began to observe vows and fasts. They became miserable like a chakwa, chakwi, and lotus without the sun.
essence: Separation makes people turn their whole lives toward one glimpse.
simple_meaning: People in Ayodhya began fasting and taking vows just to see Ram. Without him, they felt as helpless as birds and flowers without the sun.
insight: It shifts longing from private feeling into disciplined waiting and devotion.
modern_relevance: You keep checking the train platform, hoping one more delay will still end in the face you miss. The waiting changes your habits, your appetite, even your days.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीता सचिव सहित दोउ भाई। सृंगबेरपुर पहुँचे जाई॥ उतरे राम देवसरि देखी। कीन्ह दंडवत हरषु बिसेषी ॥
translation: सीताजी और मंत्री सहित दोनों भाई श्रृंगवेरपुर जा पहुँचे। वहाँ गंगाजी को देखकर श्री रामजी रथ से उतर पड़े और बड़े हर्ष के साथ उन्होंने दण्डवत की ॥
english_translation: Sita and the two brothers, along with the minister, reached Sringaverpur. Seeing the Ganga there, Ram got down and bowed with great joy.
essence: Respect can arrive before words do.
simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, Lakshman, and the minister reached Sringaverpur. Seeing the Ganga, Ram got down and bowed with great joy.
insight: It models instant humility before what deserves reverence, even in motion.
modern_relevance: You step out of the car before entering a temple, a riverbank, or your grandmother’s home, and your body softens before your mind does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लखन सचिवँ सियँ किए प्रनामा। सबहि सहित सुखु पायउ रामा॥ गंग सकल मुद मंगल मूला। सब सुख करनि हरनि सब सूला ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी, सुमंत्र और सीताजी ने भी प्रणाम किया। सबके साथ श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सुख पाया। गंगाजी समस्त आनंद-मंगलों की मूल हैं। वे सब सुखों को करने वाली और सब पीड़ाओं को हरने वाली हैं ॥
english_translation: Lakshmana, the minister, and Sita also bowed. Ram found joy together with everyone. The Ganga is the root of all delight and auspiciousness. She gives every happiness and removes every pain.
essence: Even a river crossing becomes blessed when you meet it with reverence.
simple_meaning: Lakshmana, Sumantra, and Sita bow to the Ganga, and Ram feels joy with them. The river is praised as the source of joy, blessing, happiness, and relief from pain.
insight: It shifts attention from mere travel to the sacredness of what carries and comforts you.
modern_relevance: You finally arrive somewhere after a hard drive, and the first thing you do is pause, breathe, and feel grateful. Even the crossing matters when your heart is open.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहि कहि कोटिक कथा प्रसंगा। रामु बिलोकहिं गंग तरंगा॥ सचिवहि अनुजहि प्रियहि सुनाई। बिबुध नदी महिमा अधिकाई ॥
translation: अनेक कथा प्रसंग कहते हुए श्री रामजी गंगाजी की तरंगों को देख रहे हैं। उन्होंने मंत्री को, छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी को और प्रिया सीताजी को देवनदी गंगाजी की बड़ी महिमा सुनाई ॥
english_translation: While recounting countless stories, Ram kept watching the waves of the Ganga. He then told his minister, his younger brother Lakshman, and Sita about the great glory of the divine river.
essence: Sacred attention turns an ordinary stop into a living blessing.
simple_meaning: Ram watches the Ganga while sharing stories with those close to him. He speaks of the river's greatness with affection and reverence.
insight: It turns travel into reverence by teaching you to pause, notice, and speak with gratitude.
modern_relevance: You stop beside a river on a long drive, and the whole group falls quiet for a moment. Someone begins naming what the place means, and the journey feels blessed instead of rushed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मज्जनु कीन्ह पंथ श्रम गयऊ। सुचि जलु पिअत मुदित मन भयऊ॥ सुमिरत जाहि मिटइ श्रम भारू। तेहि श्रम यह लौकिक ब्यवहारू ॥
translation: इसके बाद सबने स्नान किया, जिससे मार्ग का सारा श्रम (थकावट) दूर हो गया और पवित्र जल पीते ही मन प्रसन्न हो गया। जिनके स्मरण मात्र से (बार-बार जन्म ने और मरने का) महान श्रम मिट जाता है, उनको 'श्रम' होना- यह केवल लौकिक व्यवहार (नरलीला) है ॥
english_translation: After bathing, the fatigue of the road was gone, and drinking the pure water made the mind joyful. For the one whose remembrance removes the great burden of wandering through birth and death, ordinary fatigue is only a human appearance.
essence: Remembrance of Ram makes even suffering feel small.
simple_meaning: A simple bath and drink remove travel fatigue, but remembering Ram removes the deeper fatigue of repeated wandering through life. Compared to that, ordinary tiredness is small.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating exhaustion as only physical to seeing remembrance as a deeper form of release.
modern_relevance: You get home after a long train ride, drop your bag, wash your face, and feel human again. But some exhaustion is deeper than the body — and this verse points to a rest that reaches that layer too.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुद्ध सच्चिदानंदमय कंद भानुकुल केतु। चरितकरत नर अनुहरत संसृति सागर सेतु ॥
translation: शुद्ध (प्रकृतिजन्य त्रिगुणों से रहित, मायातीत दिव्य मंगलविग्रह) सच्चिदानंद-कन्द स्वरूप सूर्य कुल के ध्वजा रूप भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी मनुष्यों के सदृश ऐसे चरित्र करते हैं, जो संसार रूपी समुद्र के पार उतरने के लिए पुल के समान हैं ॥
english_translation: The pure, blissful, consciousness-filled Lord of the Sun dynasty acts like a human, and his deeds become a bridge across the ocean of worldly existence.
essence: His human life becomes the bridge that carries you beyond the world.
simple_meaning: Ram is pure and beyond change, yet he acts like a human so his life can carry people across suffering and confusion.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as distant majesty to seeing his life as a usable path.
modern_relevance: You watch someone stay gentle under pressure, keep their word, and carry others without needing credit. Their steadiness does more than inspire you — it shows you how to get across your own turbulent stretch.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: यह सुधि गुहँ निषाद जब पाई। मुदित लिए प्रिय बंधु बोलाई॥ लिए फल मूल भेंट भरि भारा। मिलन चलेउ हियँ हरषु अपारा ॥
translation: जब निषादराज गुह ने यह खबर पाई, तब आनंदित होकर उसने अपने प्रियजनों और भाई-बंधुओं को बुला लिया और भेंट देने के लिए फल, मूल (कन्द) लेकर और उन्हें भारों (बहँगियों) में भरकर मिलने के लिए चला। उसके हृदय में हर्ष का पार नहीं था ॥
english_translation: When Guha the Nishada heard this news, he became delighted, called his dear companions and brothers, took fruits and roots as gifts, filled loads with them, and went to meet them with immense joy in his heart.
essence: Love that is real moves your hands before your words.
simple_meaning: Guha hears that Ram is coming and is overjoyed. He gathers his people, loads up fruits and roots, and hurries out to welcome them.
insight: It shows how devotion turns greeting into service, not just feeling.
modern_relevance: You hear that someone you love is finally arriving after a long delay. Instantly, you start gathering food, calling people, and making space for them before they even walk in.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि दंडवत भेंट धरि आगें। प्रभुहि बिलोकत अति अनुरागें॥ सहज सनेह बिबस रघुराई। पूँछी कुसल निकट बैठाई ॥
translation: दण्डवत करके भेंट सामने रखकर वह अत्यन्त प्रेम से प्रभु को देखने लगा। श्री रघुनाथजी ने स्वाभाविक स्नेह के वश होकर उसे अपने पास बैठाकर कुशल पूछी ॥
english_translation: After bowing down and offering his gift, he looked at the Lord with deep love. Raghunath, moved by natural affection, seated him close and asked after his welfare.
essence: Love makes reverence feel like home.
simple_meaning: Guh bows before Ram with love, and Ram responds by drawing him close and asking after his well-being.
insight: It shows that true respect includes closeness, not formality.
modern_relevance: You meet someone after years apart, and they don’t keep you at a polite distance. They pull you close, ask how you really are, and make you feel seen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ कुसल पद पंकज देखें। भयउँ भागभाजन जन लेखें॥ देव धरनि धनु धामु तुम्हारा। मैं जनु नीचु सहित परिवारा ॥
translation: निषादराज ने उत्तर दिया- हे नाथ! आपके चरणकमल के दर्शन से ही कुशल है (आपके चरणारविन्दों के दर्शन कर) आज मैं भाग्यवान पुरुषों की गिनती में आ गया। हे देव! यह पृथ्वी, धन और घर सब आपका है। मैं तो परिवार सहित आपका नीच सेवक हूँ ॥
english_translation: Nishadraj said: "O Lord, seeing your lotus feet is enough for my welfare. By that sight alone, I count myself among the fortunate. O divine one, this earth, wealth, and home are all yours. I am only your lowly servant, along with my family."
essence: Seeing Ram makes possession feel borrowed and service feel natural.
simple_meaning: Guha says that simply seeing Ram's feet has made him feel blessed. He offers everything he has as belonging to Ram and calls himself a humble servant with his family.
insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to open-handed surrender of everything you call yours.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence steadies you after months of noise, and suddenly your status games feel small. What you own matters less than what you are willing to offer.
speaker: Nishadraj Guha

verse_text: कृपा करिअ पुर धारिअ पाऊ। थापिय जनु सबु लोगु सिहाऊ॥ कहेहु सत्य सबु सखा सुजाना। मोहि दीन्ह पितु आयसु आना ॥
translation: अब कृपा करके पुर (श्रृंगवेरपुर) में पधारिए और इस दास की प्रतिष्ठा बढ़ाइए, जिससे सब लोग मेरे भाग्य की बड़ाई करें। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने कहा- हे सुजान सखा! तुमने जो कुछ कहा सब सत्य है, परन्तु पिताजी ने मुझको और ही आज्ञा दी है ॥
english_translation: Please be gracious and enter the city, and raise this servant’s honor so that everyone may praise my good fortune. Shri Ram said, “O wise friend, what you have said is true, but my father has given me a different command.”
essence: Applause can wait; a father’s command cannot.
simple_meaning: Ram gently refuses the invitation to enter the city because his father’s command is greater than public praise.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeking recognition to protecting a binding commitment.
modern_relevance: A manager offers you a flattering shortcut that would make everyone applaud, but it would break the promise you already made. The verse reminds you that integrity matters more than approval.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: बरष चारिदस बासु बन मुनि ब्रत बेषु अहारु। ग्राम बासु नहिं उचित सुनि गुहहि भयउ दुखु भारु ॥
translation: (उनकी आज्ञानुसार) मुझे चौदह वर्ष तक मुनियों का व्रत और वेष धारण कर और मुनियों के योग्य आहार करते हुए वन में ही बसना है, गाँव के भीतर निवास करना उचित नहीं है। यह सुनकर गुह को बड़ा दुःख हुआ ॥
english_translation: I must live in the forest for fourteen years, wearing the dress and discipline of a sage and eating only what is fit for hermits. Hearing that, Guha was overwhelmed with sorrow.
essence: Duty stays binding even when it demands painful renunciation.
simple_meaning: Ram says he must spend fourteen years in the forest, living like a sage and following the rules of exile. Guha hears this and feels deep sorrow.
insight: It shifts attention from personal comfort to the duty you have already accepted.
modern_relevance: You accept a posting far from home because you made a promise, even though it changes everything. The cost is real, but the promise still stands.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: राम लखन सिय रूप निहारी। कहहिं सप्रेम ग्राम नर नारी॥ ते पितु मातु कहहु सखि कैसे। जिन्ह पठए बन बालक ऐसे ॥
translation: श्री रामजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी के रूप को देखकर गाँव के स्त्री-पुरुष प्रेम के साथ चर्चा करते हैं। (कोई कहती है-) हे सखी! कहो तो, वे माता-पिता कैसे हैं, जिन्होंने ऐसे (सुंदर सुकुमार) बालकों को वन में भेज दिया है ॥
english_translation: Seeing the forms of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, the village men and women speak with love. "Tell me, friend, what must their parents be like, who sent such tender children into the forest?"
essence: Their beauty makes the pain of exile impossible to ignore.
simple_meaning: The villagers see Ram, Lakshman, and Sita and are moved by their beauty and innocence. They wonder what kind of parents could send such gentle children into the forest.
insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle of exile to the human cost felt by ordinary people around it.
modern_relevance: You watch a young family leave a station with one suitcase and tired faces, and suddenly the whole room feels the ache of separation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक कहहिं भल भूपति कीन्हा। लोयन लाहु हमहि बिधि दीन्हा॥ तब निषादपति उर अनुमाना। तरु सिंसुपा मनोहर जाना ॥
translation: कोई एक कहते हैं- राजा ने अच्छा ही किया, इसी बहाने हमें भी ब्रह्मा ने नेत्रों का लाभ दिया। तब निषाद राज ने हृदय में अनुमान किया, तो अशोक के पेड़ को (उनके ठहरने के लिए) मनोहर समझा ॥
english_translation: Some say, “The king has done well; by this, Brahma has granted us the blessing of seeing them.” Then Nishad-raja thought in his heart that the tamarind tree looked lovely for their stay.
essence: Gratitude for a holy sight becomes care for their comfort.
simple_meaning: The villagers feel grateful to see Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Nishad-raja quietly notices a suitable tree nearby for their stay.
insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to service: first wonder, then practical care for the guests.
modern_relevance: You spot someone you deeply respect at a roadside stop, and the whole place feels different. Gratitude makes even a simple tree seem like a gift.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लै रघुनाथहिं ठाउँ देखावा। कहेउ राम सब भाँति सुहावा॥ पुरजन करि जोहारु घर आए। रघुबर संध्या करन सिधाए ॥
translation: उसने श्री रघुनाथजी को ले जाकर वह स्थान दिखाया। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने (देखकर) कहा कि यह सब प्रकार से सुंदर है। पुरवासी लोग जोहार (वंदना) करके अपने-अपने घर लौटे और श्री रामचन्द्रजी संध्या करने पधारे ॥
english_translation: He led Raghunath there and showed him the place. Ram said it was beautiful in every way. The townspeople bowed and returned home, and Raghubar went to perform his evening prayers.
essence: A humble welcome can turn exile into home.
simple_meaning: Guh shows Ram a place to stay. Ram finds it pleasing, the townspeople bow and leave, and Ram goes to do his evening prayer.
insight: It shifts attention from dramatic events to the dignity of simple hospitality and calm acceptance of the moment.
modern_relevance: You arrive tired at a friend's home after a hard day, and they quietly make space for you. No speech is needed; respect, welcome, and routine hold the moment together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गुहँ सँवारि साँथरी डसाई। कुस किसलयमय मृदुल सुहाई॥ सुचि फल मूल मधुर मृदु जानी। दोना भरि भरि राखेसि पानी ॥
translation: गुह ने (इसी बीच) कुश और कोमल पत्तों की कोमल और सुंदर साथरी सजाकर बिछा दी और पवित्र, मीठे और कोमल देख-देखकर दोनों में भर-भरकर फल-मूल और पानी रख दिया (अथवा अपने हाथ से फल-मूल दोनों में भर-भरकर रख दिए) ॥
english_translation: Guha arranged a soft bed of kusa grass and tender leaves, beautiful and comfortable. Knowing the fruits, roots, and water to be pure, sweet, and gentle, he filled two leaf-bowls with them and placed them there.
essence: True welcome is shown through simple, careful service.
simple_meaning: Guha prepares a soft resting place and offers clean fruit, roots, and water to Ram and the others.
insight: It shifts attention from grand devotion to practical care: comfort, cleanliness, and readiness for others.
modern_relevance: You set out extra blankets for a guest who arrived tired and unannounced. No speech, no display — just the quiet dignity of making someone feel safe.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिय सुमंत्र भ्राता सहित कंद मूल फल खाइ। सयन कीन्ह रघुबंसमनि पाय पलोटत भाइ ॥
translation: सीताजी, सुमंत्रजी और भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित कन्द-मूल-फल खाकर रघुकुल मणि श्री रामचन्द्रजी लेट गए। भाई लक्ष्मणजी उनके पैर दबाने लगे ॥
english_translation: Ram, Sita, Lakshman, and Sumantra ate roots, fruits, and bulbs, then the jewel of Raghu's line lay down while Lakshman massaged his feet.
essence: Service becomes sacred when it asks for nothing back.
simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, Lakshman, and Sumantra ate simple forest food. Then Ram lay down, and Lakshman lovingly massaged his feet.
insight: It shifts attention from status to service, showing that love is proved through practical care.
modern_relevance: After a long day away from home, someone shares the last simple meal with you, then stays awake to make sure you rest. That kind of care says everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उठे लखनु प्रभु सोवत जानी। कहि सचिवहि सोवन मृदु बानी॥ कछुक दूरि सजि बान सरासन। जागन लगे बैठि बीरासन ॥
translation: फिर प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को सोते जानकर लक्ष्मणजी उठे और कोमल वाणी से मंत्री सुमंत्रजी को सोने के लिए कहकर वहाँ से कुछ दूर पर धनुष-बाण से सजकर, वीरासन से बैठकर जागने (पहरा देने) लगे ॥
english_translation: Then Lakshman, seeing that the Lord was asleep, gently told the minister Sumantra to sleep. He moved a little away, armed himself with bow and arrows, and sat in a warrior's posture to keep watch.
essence: Love stays awake so someone else can rest.
simple_meaning: Lakshman quietly tells Sumantra to rest, then arms himself and stays awake guarding Ram.
insight: It shifts service from words into protective presence: you guard what you love even while others sleep.
modern_relevance: You finally get your child to sleep after a hard day, but you keep one eye open, listening for every sound. Love sometimes means being the one who does not rest.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गुहँ बोलाइ पाहरू प्रतीती। ठावँ ठावँ राखे अति प्रीती॥ आपु लखन पहिं बैठेउ जाई। कटि भाथी सर चाप चढ़ाई ॥
translation: गुह ने विश्वासपात्र पहरेदारों को बुलाकर अत्यन्त प्रेम से जगह-जगह नियुक्त कर दिया और आप कमर में तरकस बाँधकर तथा धनुष पर बाण चढ़ाकर लक्ष्मणजी के पास जा बैठा ॥
english_translation: Guha called trusted guards and placed them everywhere with great affection. Then he himself sat near Lakshman, fastening his quiver at his waist and lifting his bow and arrows.
essence: Love proves itself by standing guard.
simple_meaning: Guha carefully posts trusted guards everywhere, then sits beside Lakshman armed and ready.
insight: It shows devotion as practical protection, not sentiment. Love becomes watchfulness when someone vulnerable must be kept safe.
modern_relevance: You stay awake beside a friend in crisis, checking the door, the phone, the room, because love sometimes looks like staying alert.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सोवत प्रभुहि निहारि निषादू। भयउ प्रेम बस हृदयँ बिषादू॥ तनु पुलकित जलु लोचन बहई। बचन सप्रेम लखन सन कहई ॥
translation: प्रभु को जमीन पर सोते देखकर प्रेम वश निषाद राज के हृदय में विषाद हो आया। उसका शरीर पुलकित हो गया और नेत्रों से (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल बहने लगा। वह प्रेम सहित लक्ष्मणजी से वचन कहने लगा- ॥
english_translation: Seeing the Lord sleeping on the ground, Nishad's heart filled with sorrow born of love. His body thrilled, tears flowed from his eyes, and he spoke lovingly to Lakshman.
essence: Love deepens into sorrow when greatness chooses humility.
simple_meaning: Nishad sees Ram sleeping on the ground and feels such loving sorrow that his body trembles and tears flow.
insight: It shows how devotion can become visible as tears, trembling, and gentle speech.
modern_relevance: You see someone you respect sleeping on a hard floor after helping everyone else, and something in you breaks open. Gratitude and tenderness arrive together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूपति भवन सुभायँ सुहावा। सुरपति सदनु न पटतर पावा॥ मनिमय रचित चारु चौबारे। जनु रतिपति निज हाथ सँवारे ॥
translation: महाराज दशरथजी का महल तो स्वभाव से ही सुंदर है, इन्द्रभवन भी जिसकी समानता नहीं पा सकता। उसमें सुंदर मणियों के रचे चौबारे (छत के ऊपर बँगले) हैं, जिन्हें मानो रति के पति कामदेव ने अपने ही हाथों सजाकर बनाया है ॥
english_translation: King Dasharath's palace is naturally beautiful. Even Indra's own mansion could not match it. Its lovely upper chambers are built of gems, as if Cupid himself had decorated them with his own hands.
essence: Splendor can surround a house long before sorrow enters it.
simple_meaning: Dasharath's palace is described as extraordinarily beautiful, richer than even Indra's abode, with gem-built upper chambers.
insight: It frames the palace as a world of luxury, making the coming emotional collapse feel sharper.
modern_relevance: You walk through a house that once felt full of life, noticing the polished floor, the lights, the careful order. Beauty can stay in a place even after joy begins to leave it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुचि सुबिचित्र सुभोगमय सुमन सुगंध सुबास। पलँग मंजु मनि दीप जहँ सब बिधि सकल सुपास ॥
translation: जो पवित्र, बड़े ही विलक्षण, सुंदर भोग पदार्थों से पूर्ण और फूलों की सुगंध से सुवासित हैं, जहाँ सुंदर पलँग और मणियों के दीपक हैं तथा सब प्रकार का पूरा आराम है, ॥
english_translation: There are pure, wondrous, delightful offerings; flowers scent the air; a lovely bed, jeweled lamps, and every comfort are there.
essence: Luxury here is not vanity; it is care made visible.
simple_meaning: The place is richly prepared with fragrant flowers, a beautiful bed, jeweled lamps, and every kind of comfort.
insight: It shifts attention from mere luxury to the tenderness hidden inside hospitality.
modern_relevance: You walk into a guest room someone prepared for you with fresh sheets, soft light, and flowers on the table. The detail itself says: you were expected, and you were cared for.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिबिध बसन उपधान तुराईं। छीर फेन मृदु बिसद सुहाईं॥ तहँ सिय रामु सयन निसि करहीं। निज छबि रति मनोज मदु हरहीं ॥
translation: जहाँ (ओढ़ने-बिछाने के) अनेकों वस्त्र, तकिए और गद्दे हैं, जो दूध के फेन के समान कोमल, निर्मल (उज्ज्वल) और सुंदर हैं, वहाँ (उन चौबारों में) श्री सीताजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी रात को सोया करते थे और अपनी शोभा से रति और कामदेव के गर्व को हरण करते थे ॥
english_translation: There, with many garments, pillows, and mattresses soft as milk foam, Sita and Ram used to sleep at night, and their beauty humbled the pride of Rati and Kamadeva.
essence: Royal comfort means little beside the radiance of Ram and Sita.
simple_meaning: Sita and Ram once slept in royal comfort, surrounded by soft, beautiful bedding. Their radiance was so great it outshone even the pride of desire itself.
insight: It sets up a sharp contrast between former comfort and the exile that follows.
modern_relevance: You remember the house before the breakup: warm sheets, quiet rooms, everything in place. The details matter because they make the loss feel real.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ते सिय रामु साथरीं सोए। श्रमित बसन बिनु जाहिं न जोए॥ मातु पिता परिजन पुरबासी। सखा सुसील दास अरु दासी ॥
translation: वही श्री सीता और श्री रामजी आज घास-फूस की साथरी पर थके हुए बिना वस्त्र के ही सोए हैं। ऐसी दशा में वे देखे नहीं जाते। माता, पिता, कुटुम्बी, पुरवासी (प्रजा), मित्र, अच्छे शील-स्वभाव के दास और दासियाँ- ॥
english_translation: There, Sita and Ram slept on a grass bed, exhausted and unclothed, unseen in that state by mother, father, family, city people, friends, noble servants, and maidservants.
essence: Comfort can vanish, and still the beloved remains.
simple_meaning: Ram and Sita are sleeping on a simple grass bed, worn out and stripped of royal comfort. The people who once surrounded them with care can no longer even see them there.
insight: It shifts attention from royal dignity to the human cost of exile and separation.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you love sleep on a hospital chair after a brutal day, too tired to speak. The room is quiet, and all the status that once surrounded them feels far away.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जोगवहिं जिन्हहि प्रान की नाईं। महि सोवत तेइ राम गोसाईं॥ पिता जनक जग बिदित प्रभाऊ। ससुर सुरेस सखा रघुराऊ ॥
translation: सब जिनकी अपने प्राणों की तरह सार-संभार करते थे, वही प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी आज पृथ्वी पर सो रहे हैं। जिनके पिता जनकजी हैं, जिनका प्रभाव जगत में प्रसिद्ध है, जिनके ससुर इन्द्र के मित्र रघुराज दशरथजी हैं, ॥
english_translation: The one everyone cared for like their own life is now sleeping on the ground, Lord Ram. His father is Janak, whose fame is known throughout the world, and his father-in-law is Dasharath, friend of Indra and lord of Raghu.
essence: Honor and hardship can belong to the same person at once.
simple_meaning: Ram, who was once cared for like a precious life, now lies asleep on the bare ground. The verse also reminds us of his noble family and standing.
insight: It trains the mind to notice how quickly worldly comfort can fall away without touching a person's worth.
modern_relevance: You watch someone who once had every advantage sit on a hard floor after everything changes overnight. Status can vanish; character is what stays visible.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामचंदु पति सो बैदेही। सोवत महि बिधि बाम न केही॥ सिय रघुबीर कि कानन जोगू। करम प्रधान सत्य कह लोगू ॥
translation: और पति श्री रामचन्द्रजी हैं, वही जानकीजी आज जमीन पर सो रही हैं। विधाता किसको प्रतिकूल नहीं होता! सीताजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी क्या वन के योग्य हैं? लोग सच कहते हैं कि कर्म (भाग्य) ही प्रधान है ॥
english_translation: And Janaki's husband, Ramchandra, is lying on the ground. Who has not felt the world turn against them? Are Sita and Ram fit for the forest? People truly say that karma is supreme.
essence: Even the noblest lives must sometimes bow to hard reality.
simple_meaning: Even Ram and Sita are sleeping on the ground in exile. The verse accepts that life can turn harsh for anyone, and people call this the rule of karma.
insight: It shifts the mind from protest to sober acceptance of what cannot be controlled.
modern_relevance: You did everything right, and still the plan collapsed. The apartment fell through, the parent got sick, the promotion vanished. This verse meets you there and asks you to stop pretending life owes fairness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कैकयनंदिनि मंदमति कठिन कुटिलपन कीन्ह। जेहिं रघुनंदन जानकिहि सुख अवसर दुखु दीन्ह ॥
translation: कैकयराज की लड़की नीच बुद्धि कैकेयी ने बड़ी ही कुटिलता की, जिसने रघुनंदन श्री रामजी और जानकीजी को सुख के समय दुःख दिया ॥
english_translation: The daughter of Kaikeyi acted with cruel, crooked intent. She brought sorrow to Raghunandan and Janaki at the very moment of their joy.
essence: Crooked choices turn joy into grief for everyone nearby.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi acted with cruel deceit and turned Ram and Sita's happiness into sorrow.
insight: It exposes how desire and cunning can damage not just one life, but an entire household.
modern_relevance: A parent’s harsh decision at the wrong moment can shatter a home’s peace. One act of manipulation can turn a celebration into a wound that everyone carries.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भइ दिनकर कुल बिटप कुठारी। कुमति कीन्ह सब बिस्व दुखारी॥ भयउ बिषादु निषादहि भारी। राम सीय महि सयन निहारी ॥
translation: वह सूर्यकुल रूपी वृक्ष के लिए कुल्हाड़ी हो गई। उस कुबुद्धि ने सम्पूर्ण विश्व को दुःखी कर दिया। श्री राम-सीता को जमीन पर सोते हुए देखकर निषाद को बड़ा दुःख हुआ ॥
english_translation: She became an axe for the solar dynasty's tree. That foolish mind brought sorrow to the whole world. Nishad felt deep grief seeing Ram and Sita sleeping on the ground.
essence: A crooked choice can wound an entire world.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi's bad choice cut down the royal family's peace and hurt the whole world. Seeing Ram and Sita sleeping on the ground filled Nishad with grief.
insight: It shifts attention from private impulse to public consequence: your choices ripple through everyone around you.
modern_relevance: You watch one harsh message shatter a family dinner, and everyone goes quiet. The damage is bigger than the argument itself.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बोले लखन मधुर मृदु बानी। ग्यान बिराग भगति रस सानी॥ काहु न कोउ सुख दुख कर दाता। निज कृत करम भोग सबु भ्राता ॥
translation: तब लक्ष्मणजी ज्ञान, वैराग्य और भक्ति के रस से सनी हुई मीठी और कोमल वाणी बोले- हे भाई! कोई किसी को सुख-दुःख का देने वाला नहीं है। सब अपने ही किए हुए कर्मों का फल भोगते हैं ॥
english_translation: Then Lakshman spoke in sweet, gentle words, filled with the flavor of wisdom, non-attachment, and devotion. No one gives anyone else happiness or sorrow, brother. Everyone experiences the fruit of their own actions.
essence: Your experience comes from your own actions, not from other people.
simple_meaning: Lakshman says that nobody else is the true giver of your happiness or sorrow. What you experience comes from your own actions.
insight: It shifts blame into responsibility, so you stop seeing yourself as a victim of other people's hands.
modern_relevance: You replay a harsh email for hours, convinced one person ruined your day. Lakshman's words ask you to look deeper: what you feel now is also shaped by your own habits, reactions, and past choices.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: जोग बियोग भोग भल मंदा। हित अनहित मध्यम भ्रम फंदा॥ जनमु मरनु जहँ लगि जग जालू। संपति बिपति करमु अरु कालू ॥
translation: संयोग (मिलना), वियोग (बिछुड़ना), भले-बुरे भोग, शत्रु, मित्र और उदासीन- ये सभी भ्रम के फंदे हैं। जन्म-मृत्यु, सम्पत्ति-विपत्ति, कर्म और काल- जहाँ तक जगत के जंजाल हैं, ॥
english_translation: Union and separation, pleasure and pain, good and bad, friend and enemy, are all traps of confusion. Birth and death, gain and loss, action and time — all belong to the net of the world.
essence: Opposites are part of the trap, not the final reality.
simple_meaning: Opposites like pleasure and pain, friend and enemy, birth and death all belong to the world’s confusion. They are not the final reality.
insight: It shifts you from chasing and resisting opposites to seeing them as passing conditions, not your identity.
modern_relevance: You get a promotion and feel lifted, then one email ruins your day. This verse reminds you that both highs and lows are part of the same passing pattern.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: दरनि धामु धनु पुर परिवारू। सरगु नरकु जहँ लगि ब्यवहारू॥ देखिअ सुनिअ गुनिअ मन माहीं। मोह मूल परमारथु नाहीं ॥
translation: धरती, घर, धन, नगर, परिवार, स्वर्ग और नरक आदि जहाँ तक व्यवहार हैं, जो देखने, सुनने और मन के अंदर विचारने में आते हैं, इन सबका मूल मोह (अज्ञान) ही है। परमार्थतः ये नहीं हैं ॥
english_translation: Earth, home, wealth, city, and family; even heaven and hell belong only to worldly dealings. Whatever is seen, heard, or thought in the mind has ignorance at its root. In ultimate reality, none of this is what it seems.
essence: What the mind clings to is not the final truth.
simple_meaning: What looks real in ordinary life—possessions, places, family, even ideas of reward and punishment—can all be shaped by delusion. Ultimate reality is different from what the mind usually takes in.
insight: It shifts you from trusting appearances to questioning the mind that labels them.
modern_relevance: You refresh the same bank app, the same family chat, the same status update, hoping it will settle your mind. This verse asks you to notice that the craving itself is what keeps the whole scene spinning.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सपनें होइ भिखारि नृपु रंकु नाकपति होइ। जागें लाभु न हानि कछु तिमि प्रपंच जियँ जोइ ॥
translation: जैसे स्वप्न में राजा भिखारी हो जाए या कंगाल स्वर्ग का स्वामी इन्द्र हो जाए, तो जागने पर लाभ या हानि कुछ भी नहीं है, वैसे ही इस दृश्य-प्रपंच को हृदय से देखना चाहिए ॥
english_translation: As in a dream a king becomes a beggar and a beggar becomes the lord of the heavens, yet on waking there is neither gain nor loss, so you should regard this seen world in the heart.
essence: What shakes you in appearance may leave no trace in awakening.
simple_meaning: Worldly highs and lows are like dream changes: dramatic while they last, but empty after awakening. See the world with that distance, and it loses its grip.
insight: It trains you to step back from emotional overreaction by seeing success, loss, and status as temporary appearances.
modern_relevance: You wake up to a message that your promotion was cancelled, and by lunch another email says it was restored. The panic felt absolute for an hour, but the event itself was never the whole of you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अस बिचारि नहिं कीजिअ रोसू। काहुहि बादि न देइअ दोसू॥ मोह निसाँ सबु सोवनिहारा। देखिअ सपन अनेक प्रकारा ॥
translation: ऐसा विचारकर क्रोध नहीं करना चाहिए और न किसी को व्यर्थ दोष ही देना चाहिए। सब लोग मोह रूपी रात्रि में सोने वाले हैं और सोते हुए उन्हें अनेकों प्रकार के स्वप्न दिखाई देते हैं ॥
english_translation: Thinking this way, you should not get angry, and you should not blame anyone in vain. Everyone sleeps in the night of delusion and sees many kinds of dreams.
essence: Anger fades when you see people as dreamers in delusion.
simple_meaning: Do not get angry or assign blame carelessly. People act from confusion, like sleepers having different dreams in the dark.
insight: It trains you to observe confusion without immediately converting it into blame.
modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in traffic, then you see the same person later with tears in their eyes after a phone call. The verse asks you to pause before turning one moment into a verdict about their whole character.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: एहिं जग जामिनि जागहिं जोगी। परमारथी प्रपंच बियोगी॥ जानिअ तबहिं जीव जग जागा। जब सब बिषय बिलास बिरागा ॥
translation: इस जगत रूपी रात्रि में योगी लोग जागते हैं, जो परमार्थी हैं और प्रपंच (मायिक जगत) से छूटे हुए हैं। जगत में जीव को जागा हुआ तभी जानना चाहिए, जब सम्पूर्ण भोग-विलासों से वैराग्य हो जाए ॥
english_translation: In this world-night, yogis stay awake. Those devoted to the highest aim and free from worldly illusion are awake. A living being is truly awake only when all desire for pleasures has fallen away.
essence: Wakefulness begins when desire for pleasure no longer controls you.
simple_meaning: True wakefulness is not just being physically alert. A person is truly awake when attachment to pleasures has dropped away.
insight: It shifts attention from external alertness to inner freedom from craving.
modern_relevance: You close one tab, open another, and still feel restless. The phone is silent, but your mind keeps reaching for the next hit of distraction. This verse calls that restlessness sleep, not wakefulness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: होइ बिबेकु मोह भ्रम भागा। तब रघुनाथ चरन अनुरागा॥ सखा परम परमारथु एहू। मन क्रम बचन राम पद नेहू ॥
translation: विवेक होने पर मोह रूपी भ्रम भाग जाता है, तब (अज्ञान का नाश होने पर) श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों में प्रेम होता है। हे सखा! मन, वचन और कर्म से श्री रामजी के चरणों में प्रेम होना, यही सर्वश्रेष्ठ परमार्थ (पुरुषार्थ) है ॥
english_translation: When clear seeing arises, confusion and delusion fall away. Then love for Raghunath's feet awakens. Friend, the highest purpose is this: loving Ram's feet with mind, speech, and action.
essence: Clear seeing ends confusion, and devotion becomes your highest purpose.
simple_meaning: When confusion clears, love for Ram naturally rises. Loving Ram with mind, speech, and action is the highest human purpose.
insight: It shifts the mind from vague emotion to whole-life devotion: thought, speech, and action aligned toward Ram.
modern_relevance: After a long night of overthinking, you finally see the situation clearly and feel your heart soften toward what matters most. Clarity does not distance you from love; it deepens it.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: राम ब्रह्म परमारथ रूपा। अबिगत अलख अनादि अनूपा॥ सकल बिकार रहित गतभेदा। कहि नित नेति निरूपहिं बेदा ॥
translation: श्री रामजी परमार्थस्वरूप (परमवस्तु) परब्रह्म हैं। वे अविगत (जानने में न आने वाले) अलख (स्थूल दृष्टि से देखने में न आने वाले), अनादि (आदिरहित), अनुपम (उपमारहित) सब विकारों से रहति और भेद शून्य हैं, वेद जिनका नित्य 'नेति-नेति' कहकर निरूपण करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram is Brahman, the supreme reality, beyond change, unseen, without beginning, incomparable. Free of all alteration and beyond division, the Vedas describe him only by saying, 'not this, not this.'
essence: Ram cannot be captured by form, change, or language.
simple_meaning: Ram is the supreme reality: changeless, beginningless, unseen, and beyond all divisions. The Vedas can only point to him by negating every limited description.
insight: It shifts the mind from grasping at descriptions to resting in what cannot be boxed in.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to define yourself by job title, mood, or role, and it never fully fits. Some part of you knows you are larger than every label you wear.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भगत भूमि भूसुर सुरभि सुर हित लागि कृपाल। करत चरित धरि मनुज तनु सुनत मिटहिं जग जाल ॥
translation: वही कृपालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी भक्त, भूमि, ब्राह्मण, गो और देवताओं के हित के लिए मनुष्य शरीर धारण करके लीलाएँ करते हैं, जिनके सुनने से जगत के जंजाल मिट जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: That compassionate Ram takes a human body and performs his divine play for the good of devotees, the earth, the wise, cows, and the radiant beings; hearing of it loosens the knots of the world.
essence: Ram enters human life to untie the knots that burden you.
simple_meaning: Ram takes a human form and acts for the good of devotees and all who depend on him. Simply hearing about his life helps free the mind from worldly entanglement.
insight: It shifts attention from tangled self-management to receptive remembrance of Ram’s saving presence.
modern_relevance: You are exhausted after weeks of carrying family drama, deadlines, and guilt. Then one story, one prayer, one reminder of grace makes your chest unclench. That is the kind of relief this verse promises.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सखा समुझि अस परिहरि मोहू। सिय रघुबीर चरन रत होहू॥ कहत राम गुन भा भिनुसारा। जागे जग मंगल सुखदारा ॥
translation: हे सखा! ऐसा समझ, मोह को त्यागकर श्री सीतारामजी के चरणों में प्रेम करो। इस प्रकार श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुण कहते-कहते सबेरा हो गया! तब जगत का मंगल करने वाले और उसे सुख देने वाले श्री रामजी जागे ॥
english_translation: Friend, understand this and leave delusion behind. Be devoted to the feet of Sita and Raghubir. While speaking of Ram's qualities, dawn arrived; then Ram, who brings auspiciousness and joy to the world, awoke.
essence: Devotion can carry the night until dawn arrives.
simple_meaning: Let go of delusion and stay devoted to Ram and Sita. The praise of Ram continued until dawn, and then Ram awoke.
insight: It shifts attention from restless thinking to steady remembrance and devotion.
modern_relevance: You sit beside a friend through a long, sleepless night, talking only about what keeps you steady. By sunrise, the conversation itself has become a kind of prayer.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकल सौच करि राम नहावा। सुचि सुजान बट छीर मगावा॥ अनुज सहित सिर जटा बनाए। देखि सुमंत्र नयन जल छाए॥
translation: शौच के सब कार्य करके (नित्य) पवित्र और सुजान श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने स्नान किया। फिर बड़ का दूध मँगाया और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित उस दूध से सिर पर जटाएँ बनाईं। यह देखकर सुमंत्रजी के नेत्रों में जल छा गया ॥
english_translation: After completing all cleansing rites, Rama bathed. The wise one then had bark-cloth and milk brought, and with Lakshmana he made matted hair on his head. Seeing this, Sumantra's eyes filled with tears.
essence: Duty can be carried with complete calm, even when the heart is breaking.
simple_meaning: Rama prepares for exile with complete calm: he bathes, puts on matted hair, and makes Lakshmana do the same. Sumantra is moved to tears by the sight.
insight: It turns a painful departure into an act of composed obedience to dharma.
modern_relevance: You pack your bag for a move you never wanted, then still make the bed and lock the door properly. Some departures ask for dignity, not drama.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हृदयँ दाहु अति बदन मलीना। कह कर जोर बचन अति दीना॥ नाथ कहेउ अस कोसलनाथा। लै रथु जाहु राम कें साथा ॥
translation: उनका हृदय अत्यंत जलने लगा, मुँह मलिन (उदास) हो गया। वे हाथ जोड़कर अत्यंत दीन वचन बोले- हे नाथ! मुझे कौसलनाथ दशरथजी ने ऐसी आज्ञा दी थी कि तुम रथ लेकर श्री रामजी के साथ जाओ, ॥
english_translation: His heart burned with grief and his face grew pale. With folded hands he spoke in utter humility: "My lord, King of Kosala gave me this command: take the chariot and go with Ram."
essence: Grief and obedience can live in the same breath.
simple_meaning: Sumantra is overwhelmed with grief as he repeats Dasharath’s order to take the chariot and go with Ram.
insight: It shows how duty can be carried with humility even when the heart is breaking.
modern_relevance: You have to deliver news that will hurt someone you care about. Your face gives you away before your words are finished.
speaker: Sumantra

verse_text: बनु देखाइ सुरसरि अन्हवाई। आनेहु फेरि बेगि दोउ भाई॥ लखनु रामु सिय आनेहु फेरी। संसय सकल सँकोच निबेरी ॥
translation: वन दिखाकर, गंगा स्नान कराकर दोनों भाइयों को तुरंत लौटा लाना। सब संशय और संकोच को दूर करके लक्ष्मण, राम, सीता को फिरा लाना ॥
english_translation: Show them the forest, bathe them in the Ganga, and quickly bring both brothers back. Remove every doubt and hesitation, and bring Lakshman, Ram, and Sita back again.
essence: Hesitation cannot stop what duty has already set in motion.
simple_meaning: Sumantra asks that the brothers be shown the forest, bathed in the Ganga, and brought back quickly, with all hesitation removed.
insight: It shows a mind trying to manage grief by removing uncertainty before the painful step happens.
modern_relevance: You know that moment when you’re trying to delay bad news, hoping one more explanation will soften the blow? This verse carries that helpless urgency.
speaker: Sumantra

verse_text: नृप अस कहेउ गोसाइँ जस कहइ करौं बलि सोइ। करि बिनती पायन्ह परेउ दीन्ह बाल जिमि रोइ ॥
translation: महाराज ने ऐसा कहा था, अब प्रभु जैसा कहें, मैं वही करूँ, मैं आपकी बलिहारी हूँ। इस प्रकार से विनती करके वे श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में गिर पड़े और बालक की तरह रो दिए ॥
english_translation: The king had said this: now, Lord, whatever you say, I will do. I am yours. After making this plea, he fell at Ram's feet and wept like a child.
essence: Real surrender stops arguing and places everything at Ram's feet.
simple_meaning: The minister surrenders his own will and asks Ram to decide everything. His grief is so deep that he falls at Ram's feet and cries like a child.
insight: It shifts the mind from control to humble dependence on what is right.
modern_relevance: You finally admit you cannot fix the family crisis alone. After days of trying, you ask the one steady person left to decide what comes next.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तात कृपा करि कीजिअ सोई। जातें अवध अनाथ न होई॥ मंत्रिहि राम उठाइ प्रबोधा। तात धरम मतु तुम्ह सबु सोधा ॥
translation: (और कहा -) हे तात ! कृपा करके वही कीजिए जिससे अयोध्या अनाथ न हो श्री रामजी ने मंत्री को उठाकर धैर्य बँधाते हुए समझाया कि हे तात ! आपने तो धर्म के सभी सिद्धांतों को छान डाला है ॥
english_translation: “Dear father, please do only what keeps Ayodhya from becoming orphaned.” Ram lifted the minister up and reassured him, saying, “Father, you have examined the whole matter of dharma.”
essence: Duty means choosing what prevents others from being left helpless.
simple_meaning: Ram asks that the decision made should keep Ayodhya from feeling leaderless. He then comforts the minister, saying the minister has already understood dharma well.
insight: It shifts attention from personal loss to the responsibility of preserving order for others.
modern_relevance: You are about to leave a team, and everyone is silently wondering who will hold things together. The most mature move is not defending yourself — it is protecting the people who remain.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सिबि दधीच हरिचंद नरेसा। सहे धरम हित कोटि कलेसा॥ रंतिदेव बलि भूप सुजाना। धरमु धरेउ सहि संकट नाना ॥
translation: शिबि, दधीचि और राजा हरिश्चन्द्र ने धर्म के लिए करोड़ों (अनेकों) कष्ट सहे थे। बुद्धिमान राजा रन्तिदेव और बलि बहुत से संकट सहकर भी धर्म को पकड़े रहे (उन्होंने धर्म का परित्याग नहीं किया) ॥
english_translation: Shibi, Dadhichi, and King Harishchandra endured countless hardships for dharma. Wise King Rantideva and Bali held to dharma through many dangers and did not abandon it.
essence: Dharma is proven when hardship arrives.
simple_meaning: Great kings and sages endured huge suffering to stay loyal to dharma. The point is not comfort, but steadfastness.
insight: It shifts the mind from comfort-seeking to principled endurance.
modern_relevance: You keep a promise that ruins your weekend, your budget, and your mood. No one applauds, but you still do it because backing out would cost more than effort.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: धरमु न दूसर सत्य समाना। आगम निगम पुरान बखाना॥ मैं सोइ धरमु सुलभ करि पावा। तजें तिहूँ पुर अपजसु छावा ॥
translation: वेद, शास्त्र और पुराणों में कहा गया है कि सत्य के समान दूसरा धर्म नहीं है। मैंने उस धर्म को सहज ही पा लिया है। इस (सत्य रूपी धर्म) का त्याग करने से तीनों लोकों में अपयश छा जाएगा ॥
english_translation: The scriptures say there is no dharma higher than truth. I have attained that dharma easily, and abandoning it would spread disgrace through all three worlds.
essence: Truth is the one duty you cannot abandon without losing honour.
simple_meaning: Truth is the highest form of right action. Ram says he has already held to it, and giving it up would bring shame everywhere.
insight: It shifts you from protecting appearances to protecting integrity, even when honesty is uncomfortable.
modern_relevance: You’re asked to cover up a mistake in a meeting because it would look better for everyone. The easier option protects your image, but the lie would follow you long after the room empties.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: संभावित कहुँ अपजस लाहू। मरन कोटि सम दारुन दाहू॥ तुम्ह सन तात बहुत का कहउँ। दिएँ उतरु फिरि पातकु लहऊँ ॥
translation: प्रतिष्ठित पुरुष के लिए अपयश की प्राप्ति करोड़ों मृत्यु के समान भीषण संताप देने वाली है। हे तात! मैं आप से अधिक क्या कहूँ! लौटकर उत्तर देने में भी पाप का भागी होता हूँ ॥
english_translation: For an honorable person, disgrace is as dreadful as millions of deaths. Father, what more can I say to you? Even answering you again would make me share in wrongdoing.
essence: Honor can be wounded so deeply that even replying becomes costly.
simple_meaning: A respected person feels disgrace as a terrible suffering, even worse than death. Bharat says he cannot add more and that even replying again would be wrong.
insight: It teaches restraint in conflict: not every accusation deserves another round of speech.
modern_relevance: You read a message that twists your words in public, and your first urge is to defend yourself. Bharat’s response is the harder one: know when more explanation only deepens the wound.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: पितु पद गहि कहि कोटि नति बिनय करब कर जोरि। चिंता कवनिहु बात कै तात करिअ जनि मोरि ॥
translation: आप जाकर पिताजी के चरण पकड़कर करोड़ों नमस्कार के साथ ही हाथ जोड़कर बिनती करिएगा कि हे तात! आप मेरी किसी बात की चिन्ता न करें ॥
english_translation: Go and hold my father's feet, offer countless bows, and pray with folded hands: “Father, do not worry about me.”
essence: Humility can carry love farther than argument.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks that his father be reassured through humble respect: bow deeply, plead with folded hands, and tell him not to worry about Bharat.
insight: It teaches you to use humility as a way to reduce another person's suffering.
modern_relevance: You know a family conversation is breaking when every sentence could wound. In that moment, you lower your voice, bow your pride, and speak only to ease the other person's heart.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: तुम्ह पुनि पितु सम अति हित मोरें। बिनती करउँ तात कर जोरें॥ सब बिधि सोइ करतब्य तुम्हारें। दुख न पाव पितु सोच हमारें ॥
translation: आप भी पिता के समान ही मेरे बड़े हितैषी हैं। हे तात! मैं हाथ जोड़कर आप से विनती करता हूँ कि आपका भी सब प्रकार से वही कर्तव्य है, जिसमें पिताजी हम लोगों के सोच में दुःख न पावें ॥
english_translation: You are also as dear to me as a father. I beg you with folded hands: your duty, in every way, is to keep Father from suffering grief over us.
essence: Duty becomes love when it shields others from grief.
simple_meaning: Bharat speaks with deep respect and asks the other person to act in a way that keeps his father from suffering over their situation.
insight: It shifts duty from self-protection to protecting the emotional well-being of those who depend on you.
modern_relevance: You call your older sibling late at night because your parents are already overwhelmed. You are not asking for perfection — only for one choice that spares them another round of pain.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: सुनि रघुनाथ सचिव संबादू। भयउ सपरिजन बिकल निषादू॥ पुनि कछु लखन कही कटु बानी। प्रभु बरजे बड़ अनुचित जानी ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी और सुमंत्र का यह संवाद सुनकर निषादराज कुटुम्बियों सहित व्याकुल हो गया। फिर लक्ष्मणजी ने कुछ कड़वी बात कही। प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने उसे बहुत ही अनुचित जानकर उनको मना किया ॥
english_translation: Hearing the exchange between Raghunath and Sumantra, Nishadraj grew agitated with his family. Then Lakshman spoke some sharp words, and the Lord stopped him, seeing them as very improper.
essence: Care without restraint can still wound; Ram corrects that instantly.
simple_meaning: Nishadraj is shaken by the conversation, and Lakshman says something harsh. Ram immediately stops him because the words are out of place.
insight: It teaches you to interrupt harsh speech before it hardens into harm.
modern_relevance: In a tense family argument, someone says the cutting thing everyone was thinking. The room goes cold. Then the person who cares most steps in and stops the damage before it spreads.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकुचि राम निज सपथ देवाई। लखन सँदेसु कहिअ जनि जाई॥ कह सुमंत्रु पुनि भूप सँदेसू। सहि न सकिहि सिय बिपिन कलेसू ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सकुचाकर, अपनी सौगंध दिलाकर सुमंत्रजी से कहा कि आप जाकर लक्ष्मण का यह संदेश न कहिएगा। सुमंत्र ने फिर राजा का संदेश कहा कि सीता वन के क्लेश न सह सकेंगी ॥
english_translation: Ram, feeling shy, made Sumantra swear and said, "Do not go and tell Lakshman this message." Then Sumantra repeated the king's message: "Sita cannot bear the hardships of the forest."
essence: Mercy sometimes means holding back a message.
simple_meaning: Ram quietly stops Sumantra from repeating a message to Lakshman. The message is that Sita would not be able to bear forest life.
insight: It teaches restraint in speech when words would deepen another person's pain.
modern_relevance: You draft a message, read it twice, and realize it would only wound someone already struggling. Not every truth needs to be delivered in full force.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जेहि बिधि अवध आव फिरि सीया। होइ रघुबरहि तुम्हहि करनीया॥ नतरु निपट अवलंब बिहीना। मैं न जिअब जिमि जल बिनु मीना ॥
translation: अतएव जिस तरह सीता अयोध्या को लौट आवें, तुमको और श्री रामचन्द्र को वही उपाय करना चाहिए। नहीं तो मैं बिल्कुल ही बिना सहारे का होकर वैसे ही नहीं जीऊँगा जैसे बिना जल के मछली नहीं जीती ॥
english_translation: So arrange it that Sita returns to Ayodhya. You and Ram must find a way to do this. Otherwise, I will be utterly without support and will not live, just as a fish cannot live without water.
essence: Separation from Ram and Sita feels like losing the ground beneath you.
simple_meaning: Bharat says Sita must be brought back to Ayodhya somehow, or he cannot go on living without her and Ram's support.
insight: It reveals how devotion can turn absence into a felt loss of support, not just sadness.
modern_relevance: You wait in an empty house after someone leaves, and every room feels wrong. Bharat names that ache: when the heart loses its center, even breathing feels borrowed.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: मइकें ससुरें सकल सुख जबहिं जहाँ मनु मान। तहँ तब रहिहि सुखेन सिय जब लगि बिपति बिहान ॥
translation: सीता के मायके (पिता के घर) और ससुराल में सब सुख हैं। जब तक यह विपत्ति दूर नहीं होती, तब तक वे जब जहाँ जी चाहें, वहीं सुख से रहेंगी ॥
english_translation: Sita has happiness in both her parents' home and her in-laws' home. Until this trouble passes, let her stay happily wherever she wishes.
essence: Love sometimes means leaving someone where they can feel safe.
simple_meaning: Sita can stay wherever she feels comfortable, because both homes are places of happiness. Until this crisis ends, there is no need to force her elsewhere.
insight: It shifts you from forcing a solution to protecting emotional safety first.
modern_relevance: A family argument has left someone exhausted, and nobody wants to decide anything tonight. The kindest move is not pressure, but giving them room to breathe until the storm passes.
speaker: Sumantra

verse_text: बिनती भूप कीन्ह जेहि भाँती। आरति प्रीति न सो कहि जाती॥ पितु सँदेसु सुनि कृपानिधाना। सियहि दीन्ह सिख कोटि बिधाना ॥
translation: राजा ने जिस तरह (जिस दीनता और प्रेम से) विनती की है, वह दीनता और प्रेम कहा नहीं जा सकता। कृपानिधान श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने पिता का संदेश सुनकर सीताजी को करोड़ों (अनेकों) प्रकार से सीख दी ॥
english_translation: In whatever way the king pleaded, his humility and love cannot be fully described. After hearing his father's message, the compassionate Ram gave Sita countless kinds of counsel.
essence: True care can sound like firm guidance in a painful moment.
simple_meaning: The king's plea was full of humility and love. After hearing his father's message, Ram gave Sita many kinds of advice.
insight: It shows that duty can include tenderness: even in separation, Ram answers with patient, protective counsel.
modern_relevance: You call someone you love to explain a painful family decision, and every sentence lands with care. Sometimes the most loving response is clear guidance, not easy reassurance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सासु ससुर गुर प्रिय परिवारू। फिरहु त सब कर मिटै खभारू॥ सुनि पति बचन कहति बैदेही। सुनहु प्रानपति परम सनेही ॥
translation: (उन्होंने कहा-) जो तुम घर लौट जाओ, तो सास, ससुर, गुरु, प्रियजन एवं कुटुम्बी सबकी चिन्ता मिट जाए। पति के वचन सुनकर जानकीजी कहती हैं- हे प्राणपति! हे परम स्नेही! सुनिए ॥
english_translation: If you return home, your mother-in-law, father-in-law, teacher, beloved ones, and family will all be relieved. Hearing her husband's words, Vaidehi says, "Listen, my lord of life, my most beloved one."
essence: True love thinks of everyone’s burden before its own comfort.
simple_meaning: Sita gently points out that returning home would ease the worries of everyone who loves them. She then turns to Rama with deep tenderness and asks him to listen.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal desire to the wider circle of care around a decision.
modern_relevance: You are about to make a choice that affects your whole family, and everyone is quietly carrying it. The most loving voice in the room thinks beyond itself.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: प्रभु करुनामय परम बिबेकी। तनु तजि रहति छाँह किमि छेंकी॥ प्रभा जाइ कहँ भानु बिहाई। कहँ चंद्रिका चंदु तजि जाई ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! आप करुणामय और परम ज्ञानी हैं। (कृपा करके विचार तो कीजिए) शरीर को छोड़कर छाया अलग कैसे रोकी रह सकती है? सूर्य की प्रभा सूर्य को छोड़कर कहाँ जा सकती है? और चाँदनी चन्द्रमा को त्यागकर कहाँ जा सकती है? ॥
english_translation: O Lord, you are full of compassion and supremely discerning. How can a shadow be kept apart after the body is gone? Where can sunlight go after leaving the sun, and where can moonlight go after leaving the moon?
essence: True belonging cannot be forced apart.
simple_meaning: Sita says she cannot be kept apart from Ram any more than a shadow can be separated from a body, or sunlight from the sun.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating devotion as a choice to seeing it as a natural belonging.
modern_relevance: You are asked to leave the person who gives your life meaning, and your chest tightens. Some attachments are not stubbornness; they are identity itself.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: पतिहि प्रेममय बिनय सुनाई। कहति सचिव सन गिरा सुहाई॥ तुम्ह पितु ससुर सरिस हितकारी। उतरु देउँ फिरि अनुचित भारी ॥
translation: इस प्रकार पति को प्रेममयी विनती सुनाकर सीताजी मंत्री से सुहावनी वाणी कहने लगीं- आप मेरे पिताजी और ससुरजी के समान मेरा हित करने वाले हैं। आपको मैं बदले में उत्तर देती हूँ, यह बहुत ही अनुचित है ॥
english_translation: Having spoken her loving plea to her husband, Sita then addressed the minister in gentle words: "You are like my father and father-in-law, a benefactor to me. It would be very improper for me to answer you in return."
essence: Gentle speech preserves dignity under pressure.
simple_meaning: Sita speaks politely to the minister, saying he is like a father and father-in-law to her, so replying sharply would be wrong.
insight: It teaches you to protect relationships with measured speech, even when you disagree.
modern_relevance: A family member raises a difficult issue at dinner, and you feel the urge to snap back. Sita shows another way: keep your dignity, answer gently, and do not let hurt become disrespect.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: आरति बस सनमुख भइउँ बिलगु न मानब तात। आरजसुत पद कमल बिनु बादि जहाँ लगि नात ॥
translation: किन्तु हे तात! मैं आर्त्त होकर ही आपके सम्मुख हुई हूँ, आप बुरा न मानिएगा। आर्यपुत्र (स्वामी) के चरणकमलों के बिना जगत में जहाँ तक नाते हैं, सभी मेरे लिए व्यर्थ हैं ॥
english_translation: But, O father, I have come before you only in distress. Do not take offense. Without the lotus feet of the noble prince, all ties in this world are empty to me.
essence: Without Ram, every other bond becomes hollow.
simple_meaning: Sita tells the messenger she has come out of distress and asks him not to be offended. Without Ram, every relationship in the world feels meaningless to her.
insight: It shifts attachment away from social ties and toward the one relationship that gives all others meaning.
modern_relevance: You keep answering calls from people who only want a version of you that can function. But the part of you that matters most is still asking for the one bond that makes everything else bearable.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: पितु बैभव बिलास मैं डीठा। नृप मनि मुकुट मिलित पद पीठा॥ सुखनिधान अस पितु गृह मोरें। पिय बिहीन मन भाव न भोरें ॥
translation: मैंने पिताजी के ऐश्वर्य की छटा देखी है, जिनके चरण रखने की चौकी से सर्वशिरोमणि राजाओं के मुकुट मिलते हैं (अर्थात बड़े-बड़े राजा जिनके चरणों में प्रणाम करते हैं) ऐसे पिता का घर भी, जो सब प्रकार के सुखों का भंडार है, पति के बिना मेरे मन को भूलकर भी नहीं भाता ॥
english_translation: I have seen my father's royal splendor; kings bow where his feet rest. Yet even my father's house, a treasury of delight, does not please my mind without my husband.
essence: Wealth means little when the heart is separated from its beloved.
simple_meaning: Sita says she has seen her father's great royal life, but even that rich and honored home cannot satisfy her without her husband.
insight: It shifts value from luxury and rank to the presence of the beloved.
modern_relevance: You can sit in a beautiful family home, surrounded by care and status, and still feel a sharp emptiness after separation. Comfort does not always touch the heart.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: ससुर चक्कवइ कोसल राऊ। भुवन चारिदस प्रगट प्रभाऊ॥ आगें होइ जेहि सुरपति लेई। अरध सिंघासन आसनु देई ॥
translation: मेरे ससुर कोसलराज चक्रवर्ती सम्राट हैं, जिनका प्रभाव चौदहों लोकों में प्रकट है, इन्द्र भी आगे होकर जिनका स्वागत करता है और अपने आधे सिंहासन पर बैठने के लिए स्थान देता है, ॥
english_translation: My father-in-law is the emperor of Kosala, whose glory is manifest across the fourteen worlds. Even Indra comes forward to receive him and offers him a seat on half his throne.
essence: Even the greatest honor feels hollow without Ram.
simple_meaning: Sita is praising her father-in-law Dasharath as a mighty emperor whose fame reaches all worlds, so great that even Indra honors him.
insight: It shifts attention from outward prestige to the deeper condition of the heart.
modern_relevance: You walk into a house with polished floors, honored relatives, and every sign of success. It should feel like arrival, but without the person you love, it still feels incomplete.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: ससुरु एतादृस अवध निवासू। प्रिय परिवारु मातु सम सासू॥ बिनु रघुपति पद पदुम परागा। मोहि केउ सपनेहुँ सुखद न लागा ॥
translation: ऐसे (ऐश्वर्य और प्रभावशाली) ससुर, (उनकी राजधानी) अयोध्या का निवास, प्रिय कुटुम्बी और माता के समान सासुएँ- ये कोई भी श्री रघुनाथजी के चरण कमलों की रज के बिना मुझे स्वप्न में भी सुखदायक नहीं लगते ॥
english_translation: Such a father-in-law, such a home in Ayodhya, dear relatives, and mothers-like mothers-in-law — none of these feel pleasant to me, even in a dream, without the dust of Raghunath's feet.
essence: Without Ram, even abundance feels like exile.
simple_meaning: Bharat says that even a blessed family and a royal home mean nothing to him without Ram's presence and grace.
insight: It shifts the mind from measuring comfort by possessions to measuring it by presence and love.
modern_relevance: You move into the apartment you worked so hard to get, but the room still feels cold because the one person you miss is not there. Bharat knows that ache.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: अगम पंथ बनभूमि पहारा। करि केहरि सर सरित अपारा॥ कोल किरात कुरंग बिहंगा। मोहि सब सुखद प्रानपति संगा ॥
translation: दुर्गम रास्ते, जंगली धरती, पहाड़, हाथी, सिंह, अथाह तालाब एवं नदियाँ, कोल, भील, हिरन और पक्षी- प्राणपति (श्री रघुनाथजी) के साथ रहते ये सभी मुझे सुख देने वाले होंगे ॥
english_translation: The impassable forest path, wild land, mountains, elephants, lions, endless lakes and rivers, the Kol and Kirat people, deer and birds — all of them will be pleasing to me when I am with my lord of life.
essence: Ram's presence turns danger into comfort.
simple_meaning: Sita says that even forests, mountains, animals, and rough people will feel pleasant if she is with Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from external comfort to the presence that makes any setting livable.
modern_relevance: You move to a new city, sleep on a bare mattress, and miss everything familiar. Then the person you trust most walks in, and the place stops feeling hostile.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सासु ससुर सन मोरि हुँति बिनय करबि परि पायँ। मोर सोचु जनि करिअ कछु मैं बन सुखी सुभायँ ॥
translation: अतः सास और ससुर के पाँव पड़कर, मेरी ओर से विनती कीजिएगा कि वे मेरा कुछ भी सोच न करें, मैं वन में स्वभाव से ही सुखी हूँ ॥
english_translation: So please fall at my mother-in-law's and father-in-law's feet and tell them not to worry about me. I am naturally happy in the forest.
essence: Exile loses its sting when your heart is already at rest.
simple_meaning: Sita asks someone to reassure her in-laws that they need not worry. She says the forest life is naturally comfortable for her.
insight: It shifts the mind from needing comfort in surroundings to carrying comfort within.
modern_relevance: You move into a new city with almost nothing familiar, and everyone keeps asking whether you're managing. Quietly, you are. This verse understands the strange calm of being uprooted but not undone.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: प्राननाथ प्रिय देवर साथा। बीर धुरीन धरें धनु भाथा॥ नहिं मग श्रमु भ्रमु दुख मन मोरें। मोहि लगि सोचु करिअ जनि भोरें ॥
translation: वीरों में अग्रगण्य तथा धनुष और (बाणों से भरे) तरकश धारण किए मेरे प्राणनाथ और प्यारे देवर साथ हैं। इससे मुझे न रास्ते की थकावट है, न भ्रम है और न मेरे मन में कोई दुःख ही है। आप मेरे लिए भूलकर भी सोच न करें ॥
english_translation: My dear lord and younger brother are with me, warriors skilled with bow and quiver in hand. So I feel no weariness, no confusion, and no sorrow on the road. Do not worry about me, not even by morning.
essence: Presence transforms hardship into something you can carry.
simple_meaning: Sita tells Sumantra not to worry about her because Ram and Lakshman are with her. Their presence removes her fear, fatigue, and sorrow.
insight: It shifts attention from hardship itself to the stabilising power of loyal presence.
modern_relevance: You are leaving a hospital with someone you love, and the drive home feels impossible. Then a trusted friend sits beside you, takes the bag, and the whole night becomes bearable.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सुनि सुमंत्रु सिय सीतलि बानी। भयउ बिकल जनु फनि मनि हानी॥ नयन सूझ नहिं सुनइ न काना। कहि न सकइ कछु अति अकुलाना ॥
translation: सुमंत्र सीताजी की शीतल वाणी सुनकर ऐसे व्याकुल हो गए जैसे साँप मणि खो जाने पर। नेत्रों से कुछ सूझता नहीं, कानों से सुनाई नहीं देता। वे बहुत व्याकुल हो गए, कुछ कह नहीं सकते ॥
english_translation: Listening to Sita's calm words, Sumantra became distraught, like a serpent deprived of its jewel. He could neither see nor hear properly, and in his overwhelming anguish he could say nothing.
essence: Grief can make the mind go dark in a single moment.
simple_meaning: Sumantra is so overwhelmed by Sita's calm words that he loses his composure, his senses fail him, and he cannot speak.
insight: It shows how emotional shock can shut down perception, speech, and clear thought all at once.
modern_relevance: You hear someone stay calm while their life is breaking apart, and your own chest tightens. Sometimes another person's steadiness makes your grief louder.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम प्रबोधु कीन्ह बहु भाँती। तदपि होति नहिं सीतलि छाती॥ जतन अनेक साथ हित कीन्हे। उचित उतर रघुनंदन दीन्हे ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने उनका बहुत प्रकार से समाधान किया। तो भी उनकी छाती ठंडी न हुई। साथ चलने के लिए मंत्री ने अनेकों यत्न किए (युक्तियाँ पेश कीं), पर रघुनंदन श्री रामजी (उन सब युक्तियों का) यथोचित उत्तर देते गए ॥
english_translation: Ram tried to comfort him in many ways, but his chest did not grow calm. The minister made many efforts and appeals, and Raghunandan answered each one fittingly.
essence: Kind words cannot always reach a heart in shock.
simple_meaning: Ram speaks kindly and tries many ways to calm Sumantra, but Sumantra's grief does not ease. Even well-meant efforts cannot always soften a heart in shock.
insight: It teaches you to respect the pace of grief instead of forcing immediate relief.
modern_relevance: You sit beside someone after bad news and say everything right, but their face stays frozen. Not every wound opens to explanation; some hearts need time before they can receive comfort.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मेटि जाइ नहिं राम रजाई। कठिन करम गति कछु न बसाई॥ राम लखन सिय पद सिरु नाई। फिरेउ बनिक जिमि मूर गवाँई ॥
translation: श्री रामजी की आज्ञा मेटी नहीं जा सकती। कर्म की गति कठिन है, उस पर कुछ भी वश नहीं चलता। श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीताजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर सुमंत्र इस तरह लौटे जैसे कोई व्यापारी अपना मूलधन (पूँजी) गँवाकर लौटे ॥
english_translation: Ram's command cannot be undone. The movement of karma is hard to resist; nothing can control it. Bowing his head at the feet of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, Sumantra returned like a merchant who has lost his capital.
essence: Some commands and consequences cannot be reversed.
simple_meaning: Ram's command cannot be undone, and karma moves beyond human control. Sumantra bows to Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, then returns in grief like a merchant who has lost everything.
insight: It shifts the mind from control to humility when effort has reached its limit.
modern_relevance: You leave the hospital after hearing there is nothing more to do. You replay every choice, but the outcome has already moved beyond your hands.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रथु हाँकेउ हय राम तन हेरि हेरि हिहिनाहिं। देखि निषाद बिषाद बस धुनहिं सीस पछिताहिं ॥
translation: सुमंत्र ने रथ को हाँका, घोड़े श्री रामचन्द्रजी की ओर देख-देखकर हिनहिनाते हैं। यह देखकर निषाद लोग विषाद के वश होकर सिर धुन-धुनकर (पीट-पीटकर) पछताते हैं ॥
english_translation: The chariot moved on. The horses kept looking toward Ram and whinnying. Seeing this, the Nishads were overcome with grief, beating their heads in regret.
essence: Even the horses cannot bear Ram's departure.
simple_meaning: As Ram leaves, even the horses keep turning toward him, and the Nishads grieve deeply at the sight.
insight: It deepens the scene of separation, showing grief spreading through everyone who witnesses it.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you love leave, and even the dog keeps running to the door. The room itself seems to know something precious has gone.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जासु बियोग बिकल पसु ऐसें। प्रजा मातु पितु जिइहहिं कैसें॥ बरबस राम सुमंत्रु पठाए। सुरसरि तीर आपु तब आए ॥
translation: जिनके वियोग में पशु इस प्रकार व्याकुल हैं, उनके वियोग में प्रजा, माता और पिता कैसे जीते रहेंगे? श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने जबर्दस्ती सुमंत्र को लौटाया। तब आप गंगाजी के तीर पर आए ॥
english_translation: How will the people, mother, and father live without the one whose separation leaves even animals distressed? Ram sent Sumantra back by force, and then came to the bank of the Ganga.
essence: Ram's absence is so deep that even the world around him feels it.
simple_meaning: Even the animals are grief-stricken at Ram's departure, so how can the people, mother, and father bear it? Ram sends Sumantra back and continues on to the Ganga bank.
insight: It turns private grief into a shared human fracture, showing how deeply one person's presence can hold a whole community together.
modern_relevance: You leave a hospital room after saying goodbye, and the silence in the car feels heavier than the news itself. Some separations change the air around everyone who loves.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मागी नाव न केवटु आना। कहइ तुम्हार मरमु मैं जाना॥ चरन कमल रज कहुँ सबु कहई। मानुष करनि मूरि कछु अहई ॥
translation: श्री राम ने केवट से नाव माँगी, पर वह लाता नहीं। वह कहने लगा- मैंने तुम्हारा मर्म (भेद) जान लिया। तुम्हारे चरण कमलों की धूल के लिए सब लोग कहते हैं कि वह मनुष्य बना देने वाली कोई जड़ी है, ॥
english_translation: Kevat did not bring the boat. He said, "I know your secret. Everyone says the dust of your lotus feet is a herb that turns humans into something else."
essence: A heart in awe cannot treat the sacred as ordinary.
simple_meaning: The boatman refuses at first because he believes Ram's feet are so holy that even their dust can transform a person.
insight: It shows how devotion can turn ordinary service into a moment of trembling care.
modern_relevance: You hesitate before letting someone in because their presence feels too important to handle casually. Respect can make even a simple task feel sacred.
speaker: Kevat

verse_text: छुअत सिला भइ नारि सुहाई। पाहन तें न काठ कठिनाई॥ तरनिउ मुनि घरिनी होइ जाई। बाट परइ मोरि नाव उड़ाई ॥
translation: जिसके छूते ही पत्थर की शिला सुंदरी स्त्री हो गई (मेरी नाव तो काठ की है)। काठ पत्थर से कठोर तो होता नहीं। मेरी नाव भी मुनि की स्त्री हो जाएगी और इस प्रकार मेरी नाव उड़ जाएगी, मैं लुट जाऊँगा (अथवा रास्ता रुक जाएगा, जिससे आप पार न हो सकेंगे और मेरी रोजी मारी जाएगी) (मेरी कमाने-खाने की राह ही मारी जाएगी) ॥
english_translation: The stone became a beautiful woman at your touch. Wood is not harder than stone. If my boat turns into a sage's wife, it will be ruined on the road.
essence: Reverence can sound like bargaining when the heart is afraid to lose its livelihood.
simple_meaning: Kevat jokes that if Ram's touch turned stone into a woman, his wooden boat might also be transformed and lost.
insight: It shows how devotion can wear the mask of practical concern while still keeping the heart turned toward Ram.
modern_relevance: You stall for time with a joke when someone you admire asks for help and you know the moment matters.
speaker: Kevat

verse_text: एहिं प्रतिपालउँ सबु परिवारू। नहिं जानउँ कछु अउर कबारू॥ जौं प्रभु पार अवसि गा चहहू। मोहि पद पदुम पखारन कहहू ॥
translation: मैं तो इसी नाव से सारे परिवार का पालन-पोषण करता हूँ। दूसरा कोई धंधा नहीं जानता। हे प्रभु! यदि तुम अवश्य ही पार जाना चाहते हो तो मुझे पहले अपने चरणकमल पखारने (धो लेने) के लिए कह दो ॥
english_translation: I support my whole family with this boat alone. I know no other trade. Lord, if you truly want to cross over, tell me to wash your lotus feet first.
essence: True service can be both practical and deeply reverent.
simple_meaning: Kevat says his boat is his family’s only livelihood, and he asks Ram to let him wash the divine feet before crossing.
insight: It shows how livelihood and reverence can meet in one humble act of service.
modern_relevance: A taxi driver pauses before helping a passenger with muddy shoes. The gesture is small, but the respect behind it changes the whole exchange.
speaker: Kevat

verse_text: पद कमल धोइ चढ़ाइ नाव न नाथ उतराई चहौं। मोहि राम राउरि आन दसरथसपथ सब साची कहौं॥ बरु तीर मारहुँ लखनु पै जब लगि न पाय पखारिहौं। तब लगि न तुलसीदास नाथ कृपाल पारु उतारिहौं॥
translation: हे नाथ! मैं चरण कमल धोकर आप लोगों को नाव पर चढ़ा लूँगा, मैं आपसे कुछ उतराई नहीं चाहता। हे राम! मुझे आपकी दुहाई और दशरथजी की सौगंध है, मैं सब सच-सच कहता हूँ। लक्ष्मण भले ही मुझे तीर मारें, पर जब तक मैं पैरों को पखार न लूँगा, तब तक हे तुलसीदास के नाथ! हे कृपालु! मैं पार नहीं उतारूँगा।
english_translation: O Lord, I will wash your lotus feet, place you in the boat, and take no fee. By Ram, by your own word, and by Dasharath's oath, I speak only the truth. Even if Lakshman were to strike me with an arrow, I will not ferry you until I have washed your feet.
essence: True devotion refuses payment and asks only to serve first.
simple_meaning: The boatman refuses payment and insists on washing Ram's feet before taking Him across. His devotion is so strong that he values that service above even his own safety.
insight: It shifts service from commerce to reverence, showing that the deepest help is given freely.
modern_relevance: You help someone move apartments, and they offer money, but you smile and refuse. What you really wanted was the chance to serve well, not to be paid for it.
speaker: Kevat

verse_text: सुनि केवट के बैन प्रेम लपेटे अटपटे। बिहसे करुनाऐन चितइ जानकी लखन तन ॥
translation: केवट के प्रेम में लपेटे हुए अटपटे वचन सुनकर करुणाधाम श्री रामचन्द्रजी जानकीजी और लक्ष्मणजी की ओर देखकर हँसे ॥
english_translation: Hearing the boatman’s strange, love-filled words, the compassionate Lord smiled and looked at Janaki and Lakshman.
essence: Sincere love matters more than polished speech.
simple_meaning: Ram smiles at the boatman’s awkward but loving words and looks at Sita and Lakshman.
insight: It trains you to notice sincerity before polish, and respond with warmth rather than criticism.
modern_relevance: Someone fumbles through a heartfelt apology, and you can hear the love underneath the awkwardness. You smile instead of correcting every word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कृपासिंधु बोले मुसुकाई। सोइ करु जेहिं तव नाव न जाई॥ बेगि आनु जलपाय पखारू। होत बिलंबु उतारहि पारू ॥
translation: कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी केवट से मुस्कुराकर बोले भाई! तू वही कर जिससे तेरी नाव न जाए। जल्दी पानी ला और पैर धो ले। देर हो रही है, पार उतार दे ॥
english_translation: The ocean of compassion smiled and said, “Do what keeps your boat from going away. Quickly bring water and wash my feet. There is no time to waste; take us across.”
essence: Ram receives humble service with delight and removes every obstacle himself.
simple_meaning: Ram responds warmly to the boatman’s humility and asks him to hurry so the crossing can begin.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-consciousness to simple, loving service.
modern_relevance: You’re trying to help someone you deeply respect, and they meet your awkward sincerity with a smile instead of judgment. That kind response can dissolve your fear in an instant.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जासु नाम सुमिरत एक बारा। उतरहिं नर भवसिंधु अपारा॥ सोइ कृपालु केवटहि निहोरा। जेहिं जगु किय तिहु पगहु ते थोरा ॥
translation: एक बार जिनका नाम स्मरण करते ही मनुष्य अपार भवसागर के पार उतर जाते हैं और जिन्होंने (वामनावतार में) जगत को तीन पग से भी छोटा कर दिया था (दो ही पग में त्रिलोकी को नाप लिया था), वही कृपालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी (गंगाजी से पार उतारने के लिए) केवट का निहोरा कर रहे हैं! ॥
english_translation: The one whose name, remembered even once, carries people across the endless sea of becoming is now humbly asking the boatman for help. The same gracious Ram who once measured the world in three steps has made himself smaller than the world.
essence: The greatest one proves greatness by becoming humble.
simple_meaning: Ram's name is so powerful that it can carry people across life's endless struggles, yet Ram himself humbly asks a boatman for help.
insight: It shifts pride into reverence, showing that true power can choose gentleness and dependence.
modern_relevance: You know the feeling of being the most capable person in the room, yet still asking for help to get through one stubborn problem. Humility does not reduce strength; it reveals it.
speaker: Narrator
