verse_text: पद नख निरखि देवसरि हरषी। सुनि प्रभु बचन मोहँ मति करषी॥ केवट राम रजायसु पावा। पानि कठवता भरि लेइ आवा ॥
translation: प्रभु के इन वचनों को सुनकर गंगाजी की बुद्धि मोह से खिंच गई थी (कि ये साक्षात भगवान होकर भी पार उतारने के लिए केवट का निहोरा कैसे कर रहे हैं), परन्तु (समीप आने पर अपनी उत्पत्ति के स्थान) पदनखों को देखते ही (उन्हें पहचानकर) देवनदी गंगाजी हर्षित हो गईं। (वे समझ गईं कि भगवान नरलीला कर रहे हैं, इससे उनका मोह नष्ट हो गया और इन चरणों का स्पर्श प्राप्त करके मैं धन्य होऊँगी, यह विचारकर वे हर्षित हो गईं।) केवट श्री रामचन्द्रजी की आज्ञा पाकर कठौते में भरकर जल ले आया ॥
english_translation: Seeing the Lord's feet and toenails, the river goddess was delighted. Hearing the Lord's words, her mind was pulled by wonder. Then Kevat received Ram's command and brought water in a wooden vessel.
essence: Seeing the sacred removes doubt and invites service.
simple_meaning: Ganga is first puzzled by Ram's humble request, then delighted when she sees his feet. Kevat obeys and brings water in a wooden vessel.
insight: It shows how reverence clears confusion and turns the next action into service.
modern_relevance: You hear someone ask for help in a way that seems almost too humble to be real. Then you see their sincerity, and the resistance in you melts into willingness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अति आनंद उमगि अनुरागा। चरन सरोज पखारन लागा॥ बरषि सुमन सुर सकल सिहाहीं। एहि सम पुन्यपुंज कोउ नाहीं ॥
translation: अत्यन्त आनंद और प्रेम में उमंगकर वह भगवान के चरणकमल धोने लगा। सब देवता फूल बरसाकर सिहाने लगे कि इसके समान पुण्य की राशि कोई नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Overwhelmed with great joy and love, he began washing the Lord's lotus feet. All the radiant beings showered flowers and said, 'No one has a store of merit equal to this.'
essence: Love-filled service becomes greater than any ritual reward.
simple_meaning: He is so filled with love and joy that he washes Ram's feet, and the radiant beings praise this as unmatched merit.
insight: It shifts service from transaction to offering, where the value lies in the love behind the act.
modern_relevance: You help someone after a long day, not because it looks impressive, but because your heart is full. That quiet willingness is what makes ordinary care feel luminous.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पद पखारि जलु पान करि आपु सहित परिवार। पितर पारु करि प्रभुहि पुनि मुदित गयउ लेइ पार ॥
translation: चरणों को धोकर और सारे परिवार सहित स्वयं उस जल (चरणोदक) को पीकर पहले (उस महान पुण्य के द्वारा) अपने पितरों को भवसागर से पार कर फिर आनंदपूर्वक प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को गंगाजी के पार ले गया ॥
english_translation: After washing the feet, he drank that water with his whole family, brought his ancestors across, and then joyfully took the Lord across the river.
essence: Serving Ram becomes a blessing that reaches the whole family.
simple_meaning: The boatman washed Ram's feet, drank the water with his family, felt his ancestors freed, and then joyfully ferried Ram across the river.
insight: It turns service into reverence and shows how devotion can overflow into family and lineage.
modern_relevance: You help someone move house, and the whole family ends up eating dinner from the same exhausted kitchen. A small act of service quietly blesses everyone involved.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उतरि ठाढ़ भए सुरसरि रेता। सीय रामुगुह लखन समेता॥ केवट उतरि दंडवत कीन्हा। प्रभुहि सकुच एहि नहिं कछु दीन्हा ॥
translation: निषादराज और लक्ष्मणजी सहित श्री सीताजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी (नाव से) उतरकर गंगाजी की रेत (बालू) में खड़े हो गए। तब केवट ने उतरकर दण्डवत की। (उसको दण्डवत करते देखकर) प्रभु को संकोच हुआ कि इसको कुछ दिया नहीं ॥
english_translation: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman stepped ashore and stood on the sand by the Ganga. The boatman came down and bowed fully. Seeing that, the Lord felt embarrassed that he had given him nothing.
essence: Pure devotion can leave even the great feeling they owe more.
simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman step onto the riverbank, and the boatman bows down completely. Ram feels shy because he has nothing to offer in return.
insight: It shows how sincere service can reverse the usual power dynamic and awaken deep humility.
modern_relevance: You accept help from someone who expects nothing back, and their kindness leaves you strangely humbled. The moment reminds you that real devotion can make gratitude feel larger than payment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पिय हिय की सिय जाननिहारी। मनि मुदरी मन मुदित उतारी॥ कहेउ कृपाल लेहि उतराई। केवट चरन गहे अकुलाई ॥
translation: पति के हृदय की जानने वाली सीताजी ने आनंद भरे मन से अपनी रत्न जडि़त अँगूठी (अँगुली से) उतारी। कृपालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने केवट से कहा, नाव की उतराई लो। केवट ने व्याकुल होकर चरण पकड़ लिए ॥
english_translation: Sita, who knows what is in her husband's heart, happily removed her jeweled ring. The gracious Ram said, "Take the fare for the boat." The boatman, overwhelmed, fell at his feet.
essence: Love sees need and answers it without hesitation.
simple_meaning: Sita understands Ram without needing words, and Ram pays the boatman fairly. The boatman is so moved that he falls at Ram's feet.
insight: It shows how quiet understanding and respectful generosity can melt pride and create instant trust.
modern_relevance: You notice a friend is struggling before they ask for help, and you respond without making it a performance. That kind of care changes everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ आजु मैं काह न पावा। मिटे दोष दुख दारिद दावा॥ बहुत काल मैं कीन्हि मजूरी। आजु दीन्ह बिधि बनि भलि भूरी ॥
translation: (उसने कहा-) हे नाथ! आज मैंने क्या नहीं पाया! मेरे दोष, दुःख और दरिद्रता की आग आज बुझ गई है। मैंने बहुत समय तक मजदूरी की। विधाता ने आज बहुत अच्छी भरपूर मजदूरी दे दी ॥
english_translation: “Lord, what have I not gained today? My faults, sorrow, and poverty’s fire have all been put out. I have laboured for a long time; today fate has given me a rich and fitting reward.”
essence: Serving Ram turns even labour into abundance.
simple_meaning: The boatman feels that serving Ram has given him everything he lacked: relief from guilt, suffering, and poverty. What he receives is not just payment, but grace.
insight: It shifts you from measuring life by wages to recognising grace as the truest reward.
modern_relevance: You help someone move house, expecting only a thank-you, and they quietly cover your rent for the month. The deeper gift is not the money — it is the feeling of being seen and lifted.
speaker: Kevat

verse_text: अब कछु नाथ न चाहिअ मोरें। दीन दयाल अनुग्रह तोरें॥ फिरती बार मोहि जो देबा। सो प्रसादु मैं सिर धरि लेबा ॥
translation: हे नाथ! हे दीनदयाल! आपकी कृपा से अब मुझे कुछ नहीं चाहिए। लौटती बार आप मुझे जो कुछ देंगे, वह प्रसाद मैं सिर चढ़ाकर लूँगा ॥
english_translation: O Lord, I need nothing more. By your grace, I am content. Whatever you give me on your return, I will receive as sacred blessing on my head.
essence: Grace ends need; whatever comes next becomes an offering.
simple_meaning: Kevat says he needs nothing else from Ram. Whatever Ram gives later, he will accept it as a blessing.
insight: It shifts gratitude from transaction to blessing, and teaches you to receive without grasping.
modern_relevance: You help someone move house, and they keep thanking you even after the work is done. You realize the real gift was not money or credit, but the feeling of being touched by kindness.
speaker: Kevat

verse_text: बहुत कीन्ह प्रभु लखन सियँ नहिं कछु केवटु लेइ। बिदा कीन्ह करुनायतन भगति बिमल बरु देइ ॥
translation: प्रभु श्री रामजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी ने बहुत आग्रह (या यत्न) किया, पर केवट कुछ नहीं लेता। तब करुणा के धाम भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने निर्मल भक्ति का वरदान देकर उसे विदा किया ॥
english_translation: The Lord, Lakshman, and Sita offered much, but the boatman took nothing. Then the abode of compassion sent him away, giving him the pure boon of devotion.
essence: Refusing payment becomes the doorway to a greater gift.
simple_meaning: Kevat refuses payment, and Ram blesses him with devotion instead of money. The exchange becomes a lesson that love and grace are worth more than any gift.
insight: It shifts the mind from transaction to offering, showing that the highest return is inward.
modern_relevance: You help a stranger move house, and they keep trying to hand you cash. What stays with you is not the money refused, but the quiet dignity of giving without keeping score.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब मज्जनु करि रघुकुलनाथा। पूजि पारथिव नायउ माथा॥ सियँ सुरसरिहि कहेउ कर जोरी। मातु मनोरथ पुरउबि मोरी ॥
translation: फिर रघुकुल के स्वामी श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने स्नान करके पार्थिव पूजा की और शिवजी को सिर नवाया। सीताजी ने हाथ जोड़कर गंगाजी से कहा- हे माता! मेरा मनोरथ पूरा कीजिएगा ॥
english_translation: After bathing, the Lord of the Raghu clan worshiped the sacred image and bowed his head to Shiva. Sita joined her palms and said to the Ganga, "Mother, may you fulfill my wish."
essence: Reverence begins with the body before it becomes a prayer.
simple_meaning: Ram bathes, worships Shiva, and bows his head. Sita folds her hands before the Ganga and asks the river-mother to fulfil her wish.
insight: It shows devotion as a lived act: bow, pray, and move forward with humility.
modern_relevance: Before a long trip, you pause at a roadside shrine, touch your forehead, and ask quietly for safe passage. The gesture matters because it holds your whole hope.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पति देवर सँग कुसल बहोरी। आइ करौं जेहिं पूजा तोरी॥ सुनि सिय बिनय प्रेम रस सानी। भइ तब बिमल बारि बर बानी ॥
translation: जिससे मैं पति और देवर के साथ कुशलतापूर्वक लौट आकर तुम्हारी पूजा करूँ। सीताजी की प्रेम रस में सनी हुई विनती सुनकर तब गंगाजी के निर्मल जल में से श्रेष्ठ वाणी हुई- ॥
english_translation: "So that I may return safely with my husband and brother-in-law, and come back to worship you." Hearing Sita's plea, soaked in the nectar of love, the pure waters then spoke in a noble voice.
essence: Trust asks for help first and honors it afterward.
simple_meaning: Sita asks the river for safe passage back with Ram and Lakshman, promising to return and worship it afterward. Her request is full of love and trust.
insight: It teaches you to ask with humility and to treat help as something sacred, not automatic.
modern_relevance: You ask a friend, teacher, or elder for help before a hard trip, promising to thank them properly when you return. Real gratitude begins with trust.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सुनु रघुबीर प्रिया बैदेही। तब प्रभाउ जग बिदित न केही॥ लोकप होहिं बिलोकत तोरें। तोहि सेवहिं सब सिधि कर जोरें ॥
translation: हे रघुवीर की प्रियतमा जानकी! सुनो, तुम्हारा प्रभाव जगत में किसे नहीं मालूम है? तुम्हारे (कृपा दृष्टि से) देखते ही लोग लोकपाल हो जाते हैं। सब सिद्धियाँ हाथ जोड़े तुम्हारी सेवा करती हैं ॥
english_translation: Listen, beloved Vaidehi of Raghubir: who in the world does not know your power? Merely by seeing you, rulers become guardians of the world. All powers stand with folded hands and serve you.
essence: True greatness needs no display; everything bows to it naturally.
simple_meaning: Sita's presence is so powerful that even rulers and spiritual powers bow to her and serve her.
insight: It shifts attention from self-promotion to the quiet authority that comes from inner grace.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after years of being underestimated, and the mood changes before you speak. Some people don't need to announce their worth; their steadiness does it for them.
speaker: Ganga

verse_text: तुम्ह जो हमहि बड़ि बिनय सुनाई। कृपा कीन्हि मोहि दीन्हि बड़ाई॥ तदपि देबि मैं देबि असीसा। सफल होन हित निज बागीसा ॥
translation: तुमने जो मुझको बड़ी विनती सुनाई, यह तो मुझ पर कृपा की और मुझे बड़ाई दी है। तो भी हे देवी! मैं अपनी वाणी सफल होने के लिए तुम्हें आशीर्वाद दूँगी ॥
english_translation: You have shown me great humility and given me honour. Still, O Devi, I will bless you so that my words bear fruit.
essence: Humility invites blessing and turns speech into grace.
simple_meaning: Sita says the other woman’s respectful request has honoured her, and she responds by giving a blessing so her words may prove fruitful.
insight: It teaches you to meet respect with generosity, not superiority.
modern_relevance: You thank someone for their kindness, and they answer by blessing your path. A humble request can turn a conversation into mutual grace.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: प्राननाथ देवर सहित कुसल कोसला आइ। पूजिहि सब मनकामना सुजसु रहिहि जग छाइ ॥
translation: तुम अपने प्राणनाथ और देवर सहित कुशलपूर्वक अयोध्या लौटोगी। तुम्हारी सारी मनःकामनाएँ पूरी होंगी और तुम्हारा सुंदर यश जगतभर में छा जाएगा ॥
english_translation: You will return to Kosala safely with your lord and your brother. All your wishes will be fulfilled, and your beautiful fame will spread through the world.
essence: Safe return, fulfilled longing, and lasting honor are all promised together.
simple_meaning: Sita is assured that she will return safely to Kosala with Ram and Lakshman, that her wishes will be fulfilled, and that her good name will spread everywhere.
insight: It shifts the mind from dread to received assurance.
modern_relevance: After weeks of uncertainty, someone finally texts: the interview went well, the family is safe, and you can exhale. This verse carries that relief — the fear is not the final word.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: गंग बचन सुनि मंगल मूला। मुदित सीय सुरसरि अनुकूला॥ तब प्रभु गुहहि कहेउ घर जाहू। सुनत सूख मुखु भा उर दाहू ॥
translation: मंगल के मूल गंगाजी के वचन सुनकर और देवनदी को अनुकूल देखकर सीताजी आनंदित हुईं। तब प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने निषादराज गुह से कहा कि भैया! अब तुम घर जाओ! यह सुनते ही उसका मुँह सूख गया और हृदय में दाह उत्पन्न हो गया ॥
english_translation: Hearing Gangaji's words, the source of auspiciousness, and seeing the river goddess favorable, Sita felt joy. Then Lord Ram said to Guha, "Go home now." Hearing this, Guha's mouth went dry and his heart burned.
essence: A welcome sign can steady you, but parting still burns.
simple_meaning: Sita feels reassured by Gangaji's favorable sign. Ram then tells Guha to return home, and Guha is pained by the sudden separation.
insight: It shows how quickly joy and grief can turn when attachment meets separation.
modern_relevance: You finally get a warm reply after days of uncertainty, and your chest loosens. Then the other person says they have to leave, and the ache returns at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दीन बचन गुह कह कर जोरी। बिनय सुनहु रघुकुलमनि मोरी॥ नाथ साथ रहि पंथु देखाई। करि दिन चारि चरन सेवकाई ॥
translation: गुह हाथ जोड़कर दीन वचन बोला- हे रघुकुल शिरोमणि! मेरी विनती सुनिए। मैं नाथ (आप) के साथ रहकर, रास्ता दिखाकर, चार (कुछ) दिन चरणों की सेवा करके- ॥
english_translation: Guha, with folded hands, spoke humbly: "Listen to my request, jewel of Raghu's line. Let me stay with you, show you the path, and serve your feet for four days."
essence: Humility turns into service when love wants to help, not impress.
simple_meaning: Guha asks Ram to let him stay nearby, guide the route, and serve Him humbly for a few days.
insight: It shifts service from sentiment to action: be present, make the path easier, and ask for nothing back.
modern_relevance: Someone is leaving town with a broken heart, and you do not offer speeches. You pack water, print the route, and stay until the last bag is lifted. That is Guha's kind of love.
speaker: Guha

verse_text: जेहिं बन जाइ रहब रघुराई। परनकुटी मैं करबि सुहाई॥ तब मोहि कहँ जसि देब रजाई। सोइ करिहउँ रघुबीर दोहाई ॥
translation: हे रघुराज! जिस वन में आप जाकर रहेंगे, वहाँ मैं सुंदर पर्णकुटी (पत्तों की कुटिया) बना दूँगा। तब मुझे आप जैसी आज्ञा देंगे, मुझे रघुवीर (आप) की दुहाई है, मैं वैसा ही करूँगा ॥
english_translation: O Lord of Raghu, whichever forest you go to live in, I will make a beautiful leaf-hut there. Then, whatever command you give me, I swear by Raghubir I will do it.
essence: Service means making your hands available before your pride speaks.
simple_meaning: Guh offers to build Ram a hut wherever He stays in the forest and promises to do exactly as Ram commands.
insight: It teaches you to turn affection into concrete help, and to obey what truly matters without hesitation.
modern_relevance: A friend moves into a new place and you show up with tools, boxes, and a plan. You do not ask what you’ll get back. You just make their burden lighter.
speaker: Guh

verse_text: सहज सनेह राम लखि तासू। संग लीन्ह गुह हृदयँ हुलासू॥ पुनि गुहँ ग्याति बोलि सब लीन्हे। करि परितोषु बिदा तब कीन्हे ॥
translation: उसके स्वाभाविक प्रेम को देखकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने उसको साथ ले लिया, इससे गुह के हृदय में बड़ा आनंद हुआ। फिर गुह (निषादराज) ने अपनी जाति के लोगों को बुला लिया और उनका संतोष कराके तब उनको विदा किया ॥
english_translation: Seeing his natural affection, Ram took Guha along, and Guha’s heart filled with joy. Then Guha called his people, satisfied them, and only after that did he bid them farewell.
essence: Affection becomes joy when it is recognised and returned.
simple_meaning: Ram notices Guha’s natural affection and lets him stay close, which fills Guha with joy. Guha then gathers his people, settles them, and sends them back with contentment.
insight: It shifts the mind from hierarchy to mutual affection, showing that genuine welcome creates belonging.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a difficult family gathering, and they treat your care as something precious instead of awkward. That simple welcome changes the whole room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब गनपति सिव सुमिरि प्रभु नाइ सुरसरिहि माथ। सखा अनुज सिय सहित बन गवनु कीन्ह रघुनाथ ॥
translation: तब प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी गणेशजी और शिवजी का स्मरण करके तथा गंगाजी को मस्तक नवाकर सखा निषादराज, छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सहित वन को चले ॥
english_translation: Then Lord Raghunath, remembering Ganapati and Shiva and bowing his head to the Ganga, went to the forest with his friend Guha, his younger brother Lakshman, and Sita.
essence: A hard leaving becomes graceful when you begin with reverence.
simple_meaning: Ram begins the journey to the forest with Lakshman, Sita, and Guha after honoring Ganesh, Shiva, and the Ganga.
insight: It turns departure into a sacred transition, not a collapse.
modern_relevance: You pack the car after a life-changing goodbye, stop once to bow your head, and then keep driving. The next chapter starts with respect, not noise.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहि दिन भयउ बिटप तर बासू। लखन सखाँ सब कीन्ह सुपासू॥ प्रात प्रातकृत करि रघुराई। तीरथराजु दीख प्रभु जाई ॥
translation: उस दिन पेड़ के नीचे निवास हुआ। लक्ष्मणजी और सखा गुह ने (विश्राम की) सब सुव्यवस्था कर दी। प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सबेरे प्रातःकाल की सब क्रियाएँ करके जाकर तीर्थों के राजा प्रयाग के दर्शन किए ॥
english_translation: That day they stayed beneath a tree. Lakshman and their friend Guha arranged everything for their rest. At dawn, after completing his morning rites, Lord Ram went to see Prayag, the king of holy places.
essence: Resting in exile, Ram keeps reverence and routine intact.
simple_meaning: Ram spends the night under a tree, while Lakshman and Guha arrange the rest. In the morning, Ram completes his rituals and goes to see Prayag.
insight: It shows how dignity can remain intact even in hardship, through simple order and respectful care.
modern_relevance: You sleep on a borrowed floor after a hard day of travel, and someone quietly makes the space decent for you. The kindness matters more than the place.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सचिव सत्य श्रद्धा प्रिय नारी। माधव सरिस मीतु हितकारी॥ चारि पदारथ भरा भँडारू। पुन्य प्रदेस देस अति चारू ॥
translation: उस राजा का सत्य मंत्री है, श्रद्धा प्यारी स्त्री है और श्री वेणीमाधवजी सरीखे हितकारी मित्र हैं। चार पदार्थों (धर्म, अर्थ, काम और मोक्ष) से भंडार भरा है और वह पुण्यमय प्रांत ही उस राजा का सुंदर देश है ॥
english_translation: A king's minister is truth, his beloved queen is trust, and his helpful friend is like Madhav. His treasury is full of the four aims of life, and his beautiful country is a land of merit.
essence: A life ruled by truth and trust already contains its own wealth.
simple_meaning: A good life is built on truth, trust, and helpful friendship. When those are present, even your surroundings feel rich, orderly, and blessed.
insight: It shifts attention from outer wealth to the relationships and values that make a life truly prosperous.
modern_relevance: A home where people tell the truth, keep faith with each other, and show up when needed feels different the moment you walk in. The air is lighter, the arguments soften, and even ordinary life starts to feel abundant.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: छेत्रु अगम गढ़ु गाढ़ सुहावा। सपनेहुँ नहिं प्रतिपच्छिन्ह पावा॥ सेन सकल तीरथ बर बीरा। कलुष अनीक दलन रनधीरा ॥
translation: प्रयाग क्षेत्र ही दुर्गम, मजबूत और सुंदर गढ़ (किला) है, जिसको स्वप्न में भी (पाप रूपी) शत्रु नहीं पा सके हैं। संपूर्ण तीर्थ ही उसके श्रेष्ठ वीर सैनिक हैं, जो पाप की सेना को कुचल डालने वाले और बड़े रणधीर हैं ॥
english_translation: The sacred field is an inaccessible, fortified, beautiful stronghold that evil cannot reach even in dreams. All the great holy places are its finest warriors, brave in battle and destroyers of impurity.
essence: Holiness becomes a fortress that impurity cannot breach.
simple_meaning: Prayag is described as a sacred fortress so protected by holy power that impurity cannot enter it. Its many holy places are like brave warriors destroying inner corruption.
insight: It turns a place into a living force that repels corruption and strengthens the mind.
modern_relevance: You walk into a temple courtyard after a chaotic day and your shoulders drop before anyone speaks. Some spaces don't just host devotion — they seem to defend it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: संगमु सिंहासनु सुठि सोहा। छत्रु अखयबटु मुनि मनु मोहा॥ चवँर जमुन अरु गंग तरंगा। देखि होहिं दुख दारिद भंगा ॥
translation: (गंगा, यमुना और सरस्वती का) संगम ही उसका अत्यन्त सुशोभित सिंहासन है। अक्षयवट छत्र है, जो मुनियों के भी मन को मोहित कर लेता है। यमुनाजी और गंगाजी की तरंगें उसके (श्याम और श्वेत) चँवर हैं, जिनको देखकर ही दुःख और दरिद्रता नष्ट हो जाती है ॥
english_translation: The confluence itself is his splendid throne. The Akshayvat tree is his canopy, captivating even the minds of sages. The waves of the Yamuna and Ganga are his two fly-whisks; just seeing them destroys sorrow and poverty.
essence: Sacred presence can turn landscape into a throne of relief.
simple_meaning: The sacred meeting place of rivers is described like a royal seat, with the tree as a canopy and the river waves as ceremonial fans. Just seeing it is said to wash away sorrow and lack.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary scenery to sacred presence, where place itself becomes a support for the mind.
modern_relevance: You step into a riverbank temple at dawn, and the sound of water, bells, and wind seems to untie something tight in your chest before you say a word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सेवहिं सुकृती साधु सुचि पावहिं सब मनकाम। बंदी बेद पुरान गन कहहिं बिमल गुन ग्राम ॥
translation: पुण्यात्मा, पवित्र साधु उसकी सेवा करते हैं और सब मनोरथ पाते हैं। वेद और पुराणों के समूह भाट हैं, जो उसके निर्मल गुणगणों का बखान करते हैं ॥
english_translation: The virtuous and pure serve him, and all their wishes are fulfilled. The Vedas and Puranas sing the spotless array of his virtues.
essence: Serving Ram fulfills the heart more deeply than getting what it wants.
simple_meaning: Good and pure people serve Ram, and their deepest wishes are fulfilled. Even the Vedas and Puranas praise his flawless virtues.
insight: It shifts attention from getting blessings to becoming the kind of person who serves what is truly worthy.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up for the person who never asks for applause, and somehow that loyalty starts changing you. This verse knows that service can become its own reward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: को कहि सकइ प्रयाग प्रभाऊ। कलुष पुंज कुंजर मृगराऊ॥ अस तीरथपति देखि सुहावा। सुख सागर रघुबर सुखु पावा ॥
translation: पापों के समूह रूपी हाथी के मारने के लिए सिंह रूप प्रयागराज का प्रभाव (महत्व-माहात्म्य) कौन कह सकता है। ऐसे सुहावने तीर्थराज का दर्शन कर सुख के समुद्र रघुकुल श्रेष्ठ श्री रामजी ने भी सुख पाया ॥
english_translation: Who can describe the glory of Prayag? It is a lion that destroys the elephant of heaps of sin. Seeing that lovely king of pilgrimages, Ram, the ocean of joy, also felt joy.
essence: Some sacred places cleanse you before you even ask.
simple_meaning: Prayag is praised as a powerful sacred place that destroys heavy impurities. Even Ram felt joy at seeing it.
insight: It shifts attention from travel as movement to travel as purification and reverence.
modern_relevance: You step into a riverside town after months of noise, and your chest loosens before anyone speaks. Some places quiet the mind simply by being what they are.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहि सिय लखनहि सखहि सुनाई। श्री मुख तीरथराज बड़ाई॥ करि प्रनामु देखत बन बागा। कहत महातम अति अनुरागा ॥
translation: उन्होंने अपने श्रीमुख से सीताजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सखा गुह को तीर्थराज की महिमा कहकर सुनाई। तदनन्तर प्रणाम करके, वन और बगीचों को देखते हुए और बड़े प्रेम से माहात्म्य कहते हुए- ॥
english_translation: He spoke to Sita, Lakshman, and his friend, praising the glory of Prayagraj with his own holy lips. Then he bowed, looked at the forests and gardens, and spoke of its greatness with deep love.
essence: Reverence deepens even a simple arrival.
simple_meaning: Ram lovingly explains the greatness of Prayagraj to Sita, Lakshman, and Guha, then bows and keeps praising the place as he looks around.
insight: It teaches you to meet sacred or meaningful places with reverence, not speed.
modern_relevance: You arrive somewhere meaningful and do not rush past it. You pause, bow inwardly, and let gratitude shape how you look at the place.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: एहि बिधि आइ बिलोकी बेनी। सुमिरत सकल सुमंगल देनी॥ मुदित नहाइ कीन्हि सिव सेवा। पूजि जथाबिधि तीरथ देवा ॥
translation: इस प्रकार श्री राम ने आकर त्रिवेणी का दर्शन किया, जो स्मरण करने से ही सब सुंदर मंगलों को देने वाली है। फिर आनंदपूर्वक (त्रिवेणी में) स्नान करके शिवजी की सेवा (पूजा) की और विधिपूर्वक तीर्थ देवताओं का पूजन किया ॥
english_translation: In this way, Ram came and beheld the confluence, which gives all auspiciousness simply by being remembered. Then, rejoicing, he bathed, served Shiva, and worshipped the deities of the sacred place in proper order.
essence: Reverence becomes real through careful action.
simple_meaning: Ram reaches the sacred confluence, bathes happily, honors Shiva, and worships the local deities in the proper way.
insight: It teaches you that devotion is expressed through orderly, humble conduct, not just feeling.
modern_relevance: You enter a temple or shrine after a long journey, wash your hands, lower your voice, and naturally slow down. Reverence shows up first as careful, respectful action.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब प्रभु भारद्वाज पहिं आए। करत दंडवत मुनि उर लाए॥ मुनि मन मोद न कछु कहि जाई। ब्रह्मानंद रासि जनु पाई ॥
translation: (स्नान, पूजन आदि सब करके) तब प्रभु श्री रामजी भारद्वाजजी के पास आए। उन्हें दण्डवत करते हुए ही मुनि ने हृदय से लगा लिया। मुनि के मन का आनंद कुछ कहा नहीं जाता। मानो उन्हें ब्रह्मानन्द की राशि मिल गई हो ॥
english_translation: Then the Lord came to Bharadwaj. The sage embraced him to his heart as he bowed down. The sage's joy cannot be described. It was as if he had received a treasury of supreme bliss.
essence: Humility draws down the joy of being fully received.
simple_meaning: Ram arrives before Bharadwaj, bows to him, and the sage hugs him with overwhelming joy. The meeting feels like receiving a treasure of supreme bliss.
insight: It shifts devotion from distance to intimate meeting: reverence becomes warmth, and humility becomes connection.
modern_relevance: You finally meet the mentor who shaped your life, and they greet you like family. The relief is not in being praised, but in being truly held.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दीन्हि असीस मुनीस उर अति अनंदु अस जानि। लोचन गोचर सुकृत फल मनहुँ किए बिधि आनि ॥
translation: मुनीश्वर भारद्वाजजी ने आशीर्वाद दिया। उनके हृदय में ऐसा जानकर अत्यन्त आनंद हुआ कि आज विधाता ने (श्री सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन राकर) मानो हमारे सम्पूर्ण पुण्यों के फल को लाकर आँखों के सामने कर दिया ॥
english_translation: Bharadvaja, the sage-king, gave his blessing and felt immense joy, as if the fruit of all past merit had been brought before his eyes by fate.
essence: True reward is seeing the beloved before you.
simple_meaning: Bharadvaja blesses Ram and feels overwhelming joy, as though the result of all his good deeds has arrived in visible form.
insight: It shifts attention from achievement to presence: the highest reward is not possession, but sacred nearness.
modern_relevance: You open the door to someone you have long admired, and the room changes. The relief is not in being noticed — it is in finally being near what you have loved from afar.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कुसल प्रस्न करि आसन दीन्हे। पूजि प्रेम परिपूरन कीन्हे॥ कंद मूल फल अंकुर नीके। दिए आनि मुनि मनहुँ अमी के ॥
translation: कुशल पूछकर मुनिराज ने उनको आसन दिए और प्रेम सहित पूजन करके उन्हें संतुष्ट कर दिया। फिर मानो अमृत के ही बने हों, ऐसे अच्छे-अच्छे कन्द, मूल, फल और अंकुर लाकर दिए ॥
english_translation: After asking after their well-being, the sage gave them seats and welcomed them with loving devotion. Then he brought and offered excellent roots, fruits, and sprouts, as if they were nectar itself.
essence: Love proves itself by how it welcomes and nourishes.
simple_meaning: Bharadwaj welcomes Ram warmly, gives him a seat, and offers simple forest food with great love.
insight: It teaches you to turn reverence into practical care: seating, feeding, and honoring the person before you.
modern_relevance: A guest arrives tired at your door after a long train ride, and you stop everything to sit them down, pour water, and bring what you have. Love becomes visible in the welcome.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीय लखन जन सहित सुहाए। अति रुचि राम मूल फल खाए॥ भए बिगतश्रम रामु सुखारे। भारद्वाज मृदु बचन उचारे ॥
translation: सीताजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सेवक गुह सहित श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने उन सुंदर मूल-फलों को बड़ी रुचि के साथ खाया। थकावट दूर होने से श्री रामचन्द्रजी सुखी हो गए। तब भारद्वाजजी ने उनसे कोमल वचन कहे- ॥
english_translation: Sita, Lakshman, and the devoted companion Guha gladly ate the roots and fruits. When Ram was free from fatigue and refreshed, Bharadwaj spoke gentle words.
essence: Simple food and kind company restore the weary traveler.
simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, Lakshman, and Guha eat simple forest food after travel. Once Ram is rested, Bharadwaj speaks kindly to him.
insight: It slows the scene and shows that care begins with rest, nourishment, and gentle speech.
modern_relevance: After a long walk in the heat, you finally sit under a tree and share simple food with people who care for you. The relief itself becomes a blessing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आजु सफल तपु तीरथ त्यागू। आजु सुफल जप जोग बिरागू॥ सफल सकल सुभ साधन साजू। राम तुम्हहि अवलोकत आजू ॥
translation: हे राम! आपका दर्शन करते ही आज मेरा तप, तीर्थ सेवन और त्याग सफल हो गया। आज मेरा जप, योग और वैराग्य सफल हो गया और आज मेरे सम्पूर्ण शुभ साधनों का समुदाय भी सफल हो गया ॥
english_translation: O Ram, seeing you today has made my austerity, pilgrimages, and renunciation fruitful. Today my chanting, yoga, and detachment have become fruitful, and all my auspicious practices have succeeded.
essence: Ram's presence is the completion every practice was reaching for.
simple_meaning: Meeting Ram makes every spiritual practice complete. Austerity, pilgrimage, chanting, yoga, and detachment all find their fulfillment in his presence.
insight: It shifts devotion from technique to fulfillment: practice matters, but presence is the real completion.
modern_relevance: You finish the retreat, the long prayers, the disciplined habits — and then one quiet moment with the person you love makes everything feel complete.
speaker: Bharadvaja

verse_text: लाभ अवधि सुख अवधि न दूजी। तुम्हरें दरस आस सब पूजी॥ अब करि कृपा देहु बर एहू। निज पद सरसिज सहज सनेहू ॥
translation: लाभ की सीमा और सुख की सीमा (प्रभु के दर्शन को छोड़कर) दूसरी कुछ भी नहीं है। आपके दर्शन से मेरी सब आशाएँ पूर्ण हो गईं। अब कृपा करके यह वरदान दीजिए कि आपके चरण कमलों में मेरा स्वाभाविक प्रेम हो ॥
english_translation: There is no greater gain and no greater happiness than your sight. Seeing you has fulfilled all my hopes. Now, please grant this blessing: natural love for your lotus feet.
essence: Ram's sight is the highest gain; everything else becomes secondary.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram is the highest gain and joy. Bharadvaja says all his hopes are fulfilled, and he asks for one blessing: natural love for Ram's feet.
insight: It shifts desire from external reward to steady devotion, and from admiration to intimate love.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you have admired for years, and the room goes quiet. No achievement on your list feels as complete as that moment. What you ask for next is not more success, but a heart that can love without strain.
speaker: Bharadvaja

verse_text: करम बचन मन छाड़ि छलु जब लगि जनु न तुम्हार। तब लगि सुखु सपनेहुँ नहीं किएँ कोटि उपचार ॥
translation: जब तक कर्म, वचन और मन से छल छोड़कर मनुष्य आपका दास नहीं हो जाता, तब तक करोड़ों उपाय करने से भी, स्वप्न में भी वह सुख नहीं पाता ॥
english_translation: Until a person lets go of deceit in action, speech, and mind and becomes your servant, even millions of efforts bring no peace, not even in a dream.
essence: No remedy works until your whole being turns toward Ram.
simple_meaning: Real peace comes only when you stop being divided between what you do, say, and think, and fully belong to Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from external remedies to inner integrity and wholehearted surrender.
modern_relevance: You keep apologizing, explaining, and trying new fixes after hurting someone you love. But until your actions, words, and intentions line up, the relationship still feels broken.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सुनि मुनि बचन रामु सकुचाने। भाव भगति आनंद अघाने॥ तब रघुबर मुनि सुजसु सुहावा। कोटि भाँति कहि सबहि सुनावा ॥
translation: मुनि के वचन सुनकर, उनकी भाव-भक्ति के कारण आनंद से तृप्त हुए भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी (लीला की दृष्टि से) सकुचा गए। तब (अपने ऐश्वर्य को छिपाते हुए) श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने भारद्वाज मुनि का सुंदर सुयश करोड़ों (अनेकों) प्रकार से कहकर सबको सुनाया ॥
english_translation: Hearing the sage's words, Ram was bashful, yet full of devotion and joy. Then Raghubar lovingly praised the sage's noble fame in countless ways and told everyone.
essence: Love bows even when the world tries to lift it up.
simple_meaning: Ram hears the sage with loving joy, then humbly praises the sage's good name before everyone.
insight: It shifts attention from receiving praise to honoring the one who offered it.
modern_relevance: Someone compliments you in a room full of people, and you feel the urge to deflect instead of absorb it. Humility isn't shrinking — it's letting love move through you without self-importance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सो बड़ सो सब गुन गन गेहू। जेहि मुनीस तुम्ह आदर देहू॥ मुनि रघुबीर परसपर नवहीं। बचन अगोचर सुखु अनुभवहीं ॥
translation: (उन्होंने कहा-) हे मुनीश्वर! जिसको आप आदर दें, वही बड़ा है और वही सब गुण समूहों का घर है। इस प्रकार श्री रामजी और मुनि भारद्वाजजी दोनों परस्पर विनम्र हो रहे हैं और अनिर्वचनीय सुख का अनुभव कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The one you honor is truly great and the home of every virtue. In that way, Rama and the sage Bharadvaja bow to each other and taste wordless joy.
essence: True greatness bows, and that humility itself becomes joy.
simple_meaning: True greatness lies in humility. Rama and the sage honor each other, and that mutual respect creates a joy beyond words.
insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing that respect can be the source of joy.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is trying to seem important. Then one person quietly gives credit away, and the whole room softens. That is the kind of dignity this verse honors.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: यह सुधि पाइ प्रयाग निवासी। बटु तापस मुनि सिद्ध उदासी॥ भारद्वाज आश्रम सब आए। देखन दसरथ सुअन सुहाए ॥
translation: यह (श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीताजी के आने की) खबर पाकर प्रयाग निवासी ब्रह्मचारी, तपस्वी, मुनि, सिद्ध और उदासी सब श्री दशरथजी के सुंदर पुत्रों को देखने के लिए भारद्वाजजी के आश्रम पर आए ॥
english_translation: Hearing this news, the people of Prayag—celibates, ascetics, sages, perfected ones, and renunciates—came to Bharadvaja's hermitage to see the beautiful sons of Dasharath.
essence: Their arrival alone is enough to gather saints from everywhere.
simple_meaning: News of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita's arrival spreads quickly, and holy people rush to Bharadvaja's hermitage to see them.
insight: It shifts attention from the crowd's reaction to the quiet magnetism of Ram's presence.
modern_relevance: A rumor lands in a group chat before sunrise, and by noon everyone is rearranging plans just to catch a glimpse. Some people create their own gravity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम प्रनाम कीन्ह सब काहू। मुदित भए लहि लोयन लाहू॥ देहिं असीस परम सुखु पाई। फिरे सराहत सुंदरताई ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सब किसी को प्रणाम किया। नेत्रों का लाभ पाकर सब आनंदित हो गए और परम सुख पाकर आशीर्वाद देने लगे। श्री रामजी के सौंदर्य की सराहना करते हुए वे लौटे ॥
english_translation: Ram bowed to everyone. They were delighted to behold him, received the greatest joy, gave blessings, and returned praising his beauty.
essence: Real greatness makes everyone else feel honoured.
simple_meaning: Ram greets everyone humbly, and everyone feels deeply blessed just by seeing him. They leave praising his beauty.
insight: It shows how true greatness bows first and lifts others by simple presence.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm humility changes the whole room. Nobody feels smaller around them; everyone leaves lighter, kinder, and strangely grateful.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम कीन्ह बिश्राम निसि प्रात प्रयाग नहाइ। चले सहितसिय लखन जन मुदित मुनिहि सिरु नाइ ॥
translation: श्री रामजी ने रात को वहीं विश्राम किया और प्रातःकाल प्रयागराज का स्नान करके और प्रसन्नता के साथ मुनि को सिर नवाकर श्री सीताजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सेवक गुह के साथ वे चले ॥
english_translation: Ram rested there through the night, bathed at Prayag at dawn, and then departed happily with Sita, Lakshman, and the servant Guha after bowing to the sage.
essence: The journey continues with grace, not hurry.
simple_meaning: Ram spends the night at Prayag, bathes in the morning, bows to the sage, and leaves with Sita, Lakshman, and Guha.
insight: It keeps attention on the movement of the story, not on a separate teaching.
modern_relevance: You leave a guesthouse at dawn after a long trip, pack quietly, thank the host, and step back into the road without drama.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम सप्रेम कहेउ मुनि पाहीं। नाथ कहिअ हम केहि मग जाहीं॥ मुनि मन बिहसि राम सन कहहीं। सुगम सकल मग तुम्ह कहुँ अहहीं ॥
translation: (चलते समय) बड़े प्रेम से श्री रामजी ने मुनि से कहा- हे नाथ! बताइए हम किस मार्ग से जाएँ। मुनि मन में हँसकर श्री रामजी से कहते हैं कि आपके लिए सभी मार्ग सुगम हैं ॥
english_translation: With deep affection, Ram asked the sage, “Lord, which road should we take?” The sage smiled inwardly and said to Ram, “For you, every road is easy.”
essence: Right guidance makes every path workable.
simple_meaning: Ram asks the sage which path to take, and the sage replies that every path is easy for Ram.
insight: It shifts you from obsessing over the route to trusting the one who walks it with you.
modern_relevance: You stand at a train platform with three routes on the board, afraid of choosing wrong. This verse says the right presence makes even uncertain roads manageable.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: साथ लागि मुनि सिष्य बोलाए। सुनि मन मुदित पचासक आए॥ सबन्हि राम पर प्रेम अपारा। सकल कहहिं मगु दीख हमारा ॥
translation: फिर उनके साथ के लिए मुनि ने शिष्यों को बुलाया। (साथ जाने की बात) सुनते ही चित्त में हर्षित हो कोई पचास शिष्य आ गए। सभी का श्री रामजी पर अपार प्रेम है। सभी कहते हैं कि मार्ग हमारा देखा हुआ है ॥
english_translation: Then the sage called his disciples to go along. Hearing this, about fifty disciples came joyfully in their minds. All of them had immense love for Ram. All said, "We know the path well."
essence: Love for Ram makes even guidance feel like service.
simple_meaning: The sage gathers his disciples, and many come gladly. They all love Ram deeply and say they know the route.
insight: It shows how devotion turns ordinary help into willing participation.
modern_relevance: A friend says, “I need help moving this weekend,” and suddenly people you barely expected show up without complaint. Love makes guidance and service feel easy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि बटु चारि संग तब दीन्हे। जिन्ह बहु जनम सुकृत सब कीन्हे॥ करि प्रनामु रिषि आयसु पाई। प्रमुदित हृदयँ चले रघुराई ॥
translation: तब मुनि ने (चुनकर) चार ब्रह्मचारियों को साथ कर दिया, जिन्होंने बहुत जन्मों तक सब सुकृत (पुण्य) किए थे। श्री रघुनाथजी प्रणाम कर और ऋषि की आज्ञा पाकर हृदय में बड़े ही आनंदित होकर चले ॥
english_translation: Then the sage assigned four young brahmacharis to accompany them, men who had earned merit through many births. After bowing and receiving the sage's permission, Raghunath set out with great joy in his heart.
essence: Joy deepens when you accept guidance with humility.
simple_meaning: The sage sends four devoted students to accompany Ram. Ram bows, receives the sage's permission, and leaves happily.
insight: It teaches you to begin with respect, then move forward without resistance.
modern_relevance: You finally get the green light from someone you respect, and the whole task feels lighter. The work hasn't changed — but your heart has.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ग्राम निकट जब निकसहिं जाई। देखहिं दरसु नारि नर धाई॥ होहिं सनाथ जनम फलु पाई। फिरहिं दुखित मनु संग पठाई ॥
translation: जब वे किसी गाँव के पास होकर निकलते हैं, तब स्त्री-पुरुष दौड़कर उनके रूप को देखने लगते हैं। जन्म का फल पाकर वे (सदा के अनाथ) सनाथ हो जाते हैं और मन को नाथ के साथ भेजकर (शरीर से साथ न रहने के कारण) दुःखी होकर लौट आते हैं ॥
english_translation: When they pass near a village, men and women run to behold their sight. Having gained the fruit of human birth, they feel sheltered, and then return sorrowful, sending their minds away with the Lord.
essence: Ram's sight gives shelter, and separation turns that blessing into longing.
simple_meaning: Just seeing Ram fills people with a sense of being protected and fulfilled, but because they cannot stay with him, they return with sad hearts.
insight: It shifts devotion from idea to experience: even a moment of true presence can transform how you carry absence.
modern_relevance: You leave a room after meeting someone whose presence felt unmistakably safe. The conversation was brief, but the ache of returning to ordinary life tells you it mattered.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिदा किए बटु बिनय करि फिरे पाइ मन काम। उतरि नहाए जमुन जल जो सरीर सम स्याम ॥
translation: तदनन्तर श्री रामजी ने विनती करके चारों ब्रह्मचारियों को विदा किया, वे मनचाही वस्तु (अनन्य भक्ति) पाकर लौटे। यमुनाजी के पार उतरकर सबने यमुनाजी के जल में स्नान किया, जो श्री रामचन्द्रजी के शरीर के समान ही श्याम रंग का था ॥
english_translation: Then Ram bade farewell to the four brahmacharis with blessings. Crossing over, they bathed in the Yamuna, whose dark water matched Ram's own dark form.
essence: Meeting Ram leaves the heart already full.
simple_meaning: Ram sends the four students away with kindness, and they feel fulfilled. They then cross the Yamuna and bathe in its dark water, which resembles Ram's dark complexion.
insight: It shows how contact with Ram's presence satisfies longing and turns even ordinary places into reminders of him.
modern_relevance: You leave a brief visit with someone you deeply admire, and the whole day feels changed. The meeting was short, but it gave you exactly what you needed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनत तीरबासी नर नारी। धाए निज निज काज बिसारी॥ लखन राम सिय सुंदरताई। देखि करहिं निज भाग्य बड़ाई ॥
translation: यमुनाजी के किनारे पर रहने वाले स्त्री-पुरुष (यह सुनकर कि निषाद के साथ दो परम सुंदर सुकुमार नवयुवक और एक परम सुंदरी स्त्री आ रही है) सब अपना-अपना काम भूलकर दौड़े और लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामजी और सीताजी का सौंदर्य देखकर अपने भाग्य की बड़ाई करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, the men and women living by the Yamuna ran, forgetting their own tasks. Seeing the beauty of Lakshman, Ram, and Sita, they praised their own good fortune.
essence: Their beauty makes people forget everything else.
simple_meaning: People by the river forget their work and rush to see Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Their beauty makes them feel blessed just to have seen them.
insight: It shows how awe can interrupt routine and turn attention toward what feels sacred or rare.
modern_relevance: You hear a beloved teacher, artist, or elder has arrived nearby, and you leave your half-finished work to catch one glimpse. Some meetings feel like a gift before a single word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अति लालसा बसहिं मन माहीं। नाउँ गाउँ बूझत सकुचाहीं॥ जे तिन्ह महुँ बयबिरिध सयाने। तिन्ह करि जुगुति रामु पहिचाने ॥
translation: उनके मन में (परिचय जानने की) बहुत सी लालसाएँ भरी हैं। पर वे नाम-गाँव पूछते सकुचाते हैं। उन लोगों में जो वयोवृद्ध और चतुर थे, उन्होंने युक्ति से श्री रामचन्द्रजी को पहचान लिया ॥
english_translation: Their minds were full of eager curiosity, yet they felt shy to ask the names and village. Among them, the older and wiser ones recognized Ram through clever discernment.
essence: The wise recognize what shy curiosity cannot ask aloud.
simple_meaning: People are curious about the strangers, but they hesitate to ask directly. The older and wiser ones figure out that they are Ram and his companions.
insight: It shifts attention from open curiosity to careful reading of signs and context.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence feels important, but you hesitate to ask the obvious question. Someone older in the room notices the clues first and names what everyone else only senses.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकल कथा तिन्ह सबहि सुनाई। बनहि चले पितु आयसु पाई॥ सुनि सबिषाद सकल पछिताहीं। रानी रायँ कीन्ह भल नाहीं ॥
translation: उन्होंने सब कथा सब लोगों को सुनाई कि पिता की आज्ञा पाकर ये वन को चले हैं। यह सुनकर सब लोग दुःखित हो पछता रहे हैं कि रानी और राजा ने अच्छा नहीं किया ॥
english_translation: They told everyone the whole story: the sons had gone to the forest after receiving their father's command. Hearing this, everyone was distressed and regretted that the queen and king had done wrong.
essence: Public grief follows private failure.
simple_meaning: The news spreads that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita have gone to the forest because of their father's command. Everyone feels sorrow and realises the royal decision was wrong.
insight: It shows how a hidden decision becomes a shared wound once everyone understands it.
modern_relevance: A family decision made behind closed doors can hit the wider circle later — relatives, neighbours, and friends all feel the cost when the truth finally comes out.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहि अवसर एक तापसु आवा। तेजपुंज लघुबयस सुहावा॥ कबि अलखित गति बेषु बिरागी। मन क्रम बचन राम अनुरागी ॥
translation: उसी अवसर पर वहाँ एक तपस्वी आया, जो तेज का पुंज, छोटी अवस्था का और सुंदर था। उसकी गति कवि नहीं जानते (अथवा वह कवि था जो अपना परिचय नहीं देना चाहता)। वह वैरागी के वेष में था और मन, वचन तथा कर्म से श्री रामचन्द्रजी का प्रेमी था ॥
english_translation: At that moment, a renunciate arrived — radiant, youthful, and lovely. His movement was poetically indescribable; he wore the garb of a seeker, and in mind, speech, and action he loved Ram.
essence: Renunciation means little without love for Ram.
simple_meaning: A young ascetic arrives, glowing with radiance and beauty. He looks like a renunciate, but his mind, words, and actions are all devoted to Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance to inner alignment: the real measure is whether mind, speech, and action point the same way.
modern_relevance: A quiet person in simple clothes walks into a room where everyone is hurting. No announcement, no performance — but their calm, steady love changes the whole atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सजल नयन तन पुलकि निज इष्टदेउ पहिचानि। परेउ दंड जिमि धरनितल दसा न जाइ बखानि ॥
translation: अपने इष्टदेव को पहचानकर उसके नेत्रों में जल भर आया और शरीर पुलकित हो गया। वह दण्ड की भाँति पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा, उसकी (प्रेम विह्वल) दशा का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
english_translation: His eyes filled with tears, his body thrilled as he recognised his chosen Lord. He fell to the ground like a staff, beyond words to describe.
essence: Recognition of Ram makes the body fall silent.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram, he is overwhelmed with love: tears come, his body shivers, and he falls flat to the ground.
insight: It shows devotion as a full-body response that collapses ego and control.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you have long prayed to see, and your whole body reacts before your mind catches up.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: राम सप्रेम पुलकि उर लावा। परम रंक जनु पारसु पावा॥ मनहुँ प्रेमु परमारथु दोऊ। मिलत धरें तन कह सबु कोऊ ॥
translation: श्री रामजी ने प्रेमपूर्वक पुलकित होकर उसको हृदय से लगा लिया। (उसे इतना आनंद हुआ) मानो कोई महादरिद्री मनुष्य पारस पा गया हो। सब कोई (देखने वाले) कहने लगे कि मानो प्रेम और परमार्थ (परम तत्व) दोनों शरीर धारण करके मिल रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram lovingly and with delight embraced him to his chest. It was as if a poor man had found a touchstone. Everyone watching said it was as though love and the highest reality had taken form and met in one body.
essence: True devotion makes meeting the divine feel like finding a priceless treasure.
simple_meaning: Ram embraces the devotee with joy, and the moment feels like meeting the greatest treasure. Love and ultimate truth seem to become visible together.
insight: It shifts devotion from idea to lived encounter: love becomes something you can receive in the body.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone who has carried you in their heart for years, and the room changes. The relief is not just being recognized — it is being loved without hesitation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरि लखन पायन्ह सोइ लागा। लीन्ह उठाइ उमगि अनुरागा॥ पुनि सिय चरन धूरि धरि सीसा। जननि जानि सिसु दीन्हि असीसा ॥
translation: फिर वह लक्ष्मणजी के चरणों लगा। उन्होंने प्रेम से उमंगकर उसको उठा लिया। फिर उसने सीताजी की चरण धूलि को अपने सिर पर धारण किया। माता सीताजी ने भी उसको अपना बच्चा जानकर आशीर्वाद दिया ॥
english_translation: Then he fell at Lakshman's feet. Lakshman lifted him up with overflowing affection. Then he placed Sita's dust on his head, and Sita blessed him as a mother blesses her child.
essence: Love received in humility becomes blessing, not hierarchy.
simple_meaning: He bows to Lakshman, is lifted up with love, then receives Sita's blessing like a child receiving a mother's care.
insight: It shifts attention from status to belonging, showing that devotion is answered through human warmth and acceptance.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a hard week, expecting judgment. Instead, someone helps you up, and someone else treats you like family.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कीन्ह निषाद दंडवत तेही। मिलेउ मुदित लखि राम सनेही॥ पिअत नयन पुट रूपु पियुषा। मुदित सुअसनु पाइ जिमि भूखा ॥
translation: फिर निषादराज ने उसको दण्डवत की। श्री रामचन्द्रजी का प्रेमी जानकर वह उस (निषाद) से आनंदित होकर मिला। वह तपस्वी अपने नेत्र रूपी दोनों से श्री रामजी की सौंदर्य सुधा का पान करने लगा और ऐसा आनंदित हुआ जैसे कोई भूखा आदमी सुंदर भोजन पाकर आनंदित होता है ॥
english_translation: Nishad bowed down before him. Seeing Ram's beloved devotee, he met him with delight. He drank in Ram's beauty through the twin cups of his eyes, like a hungry man tasting fine food.
essence: Ram's presence nourishes the one who loves him.
simple_meaning: Nishad bows down, and Ram welcomes him warmly. Everyone drinks in Ram's beauty with joy, like a hungry person receiving food.
insight: It shifts attention from status to devotion, showing that true welcome is recognition of love.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you admire after months of distance, and the room changes. Their warmth feels like food after a long fast.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ते पितु मातु कहहु सखि कैसे। जिन्ह पठए बन बालक ऐसे॥ राम लखन सिय रूपु निहारी। होहिं सनेह बिकल नर नारी ॥
translation: (इधर गाँव की स्त्रियाँ कह रही हैं) हे सखी! कहो तो, वे माता-पिता कैसे हैं, जिन्होंने ऐसे (सुंदर सुकुमार) बालकों को वन में भेज दिया है। श्री रामजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी के रूप को देखकर सब स्त्री-पुरुष स्नेह से व्याकुल हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: O friend, tell me what kind of father and mother sent such tender boys into the forest. Seeing the forms of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, men and women are overcome with affection.
essence: Tenderness can make even strangers feel like family.
simple_meaning: The village women are amazed that such tender children were sent into the forest. Just seeing Ram, Lakshman, and Sita makes everyone feel deep affection and distress.
insight: It shows how beauty and innocence can disarm judgment and pull the mind into compassion.
modern_relevance: You see a young family at a train station, one child asleep on a shoulder, and something in you softens. Some sights make the heart ache before the mind can explain why.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब रघुबीर अनेक बिधि सखहि सिखावनु दीन्ह॥ राम रजायसु सीस धरि भवन गवनु तेइँ कीन्ह ॥
translation: तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सखा गुह को अनेकों तरह से (घर लौट जाने के लिए) समझाया। श्री रामचन्द्रजी की आज्ञा को सिर चढ़ाकर उसने अपने घर को गमन किया ॥
english_translation: Then Raghubir counseled his friend in many ways. Keeping Ram's command on his head, he went home.
essence: Love makes obedience feel natural, not forced.
simple_meaning: Ram gently tells Guha to go back home, and Guha obeys immediately, treating Ram's order as something sacred and final.
insight: It shifts obedience from pressure to love, showing that right action can be immediate and wholehearted.
modern_relevance: Your friend keeps trying to stay and help, but the visit is over and the house is already quiet. The loving thing is not to prolong the moment — it is to let them leave in peace.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि सियँ राम लखन कर जोरी। जमुनहि कीन्ह प्रनामु बहोरी॥ चले ससीय मुदित दोउ भाई। रबितनुजा कइ करत बड़ाई ॥
translation: फिर सीताजी, श्री रामजी और लक्ष्मणजी ने हाथ जोड़कर यमुनाजी को पुनः प्रणाम किया और सूर्यकन्या यमुनाजी की बड़ाई करते हुए सीताजी सहित दोनों भाई प्रसन्नतापूर्वक आगे चले ॥
english_translation: Then Sita, Ram, and Lakshman folded their hands and bowed again to the Yamuna. Praising the daughter of the Sun, they moved on joyfully with Sita, the two brothers continuing ahead.
essence: Gratitude and forward motion can move together.
simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman bow to the Yamuna again, praise her, and continue their journey happily.
insight: It teaches respectful movement: honor what supports you, then continue without delay.
modern_relevance: You leave a place after a hard goodbye, glance back once more, and quietly thank what carried you through. Then you keep walking.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पथिक अनेक मिलहिं मग जाता। कहहिं सप्रेम देखि दोउ भ्राता॥ राज लखन सब अंग तुम्हारें। देखि सोचु अति हृदय हमारें ॥
translation: रास्ते में जाते हुए उन्हें अनेकों यात्री मिलते हैं। वे दोनों भाइयों को देखकर उनसे प्रेमपूर्वक कहते हैं कि तुम्हारे सब अंगों में राज चिह्न देखकर हमारे हृदय में बड़ा सोच होता है ॥
english_translation: Along the road, many travelers meet them. Seeing the two brothers, they speak with love: “The marks of royalty are on all your limbs, and our hearts are filled with deep wonder.”
essence: Your outer signs can reveal a life out of place.
simple_meaning: Travelers meet Ram and Lakshman on the road and lovingly notice their royal signs. Their hearts fill with wonder at why such noble brothers are walking like this.
insight: It highlights how visible dignity can be, even when circumstances force humility.
modern_relevance: You show up in plain clothes to a formal event, and everyone can tell something is off. Their puzzled looks catch the gap between who you are and how you’re being made to live.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मारग चलहु पयादेहि पाएँ। ज्योतिषु झूठ हमारें भाएँ॥ अगमु पंथु गिरि कानन भारी। तेहि महँ साथ नारि सुकुमारी ॥
translation: (ऐसे राजचिह्नों के होते हुए भी) तुम लोग रास्ते में पैदल ही चल रहे हो, इससे हमारी समझ में आता है कि ज्योतिष शास्त्र झूठा ही है। भारी जंगल और बड़े-बड़े पहाड़ों का दुर्गम रास्ता है। तिस पर तुम्हारे साथ सुकुमारी स्त्री है ॥
english_translation: “You are walking on foot, so we think astrology must be false. The path is hard, with mountains and forests, and you have a delicate woman with you.”
essence: Outer hardship can look like error to shallow eyes.
simple_meaning: The travelers see Ram, Sita, and Lakshman walking through a harsh forest path and wrongly assume the stars have lied.
insight: It shifts the mind from judging by appearances to respecting choices that serve dharma.
modern_relevance: You see someone choosing the harder road, and you assume they must be confused. But some lives look impractical precisely because they are being lived with integrity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि केहरि बन जाइ न जोई। हम सँग चलहिं जो आयसु होई॥ जाब जहाँ लगि तहँ पहुँचाई। फिरब बहोरि तुम्हहि सिरु नाई ॥
translation: हाथी और सिंहों से भरा यह भयानक वन देखा तक नहीं जाता। यदि आज्ञा हो तो हम साथ चलें। आप जहाँ तक जाएँगे, वहाँ तक पहुँचाकर, फिर आपको प्रणाम करके हम लौट आवेंगे ॥
english_translation: We have not even seen this terrible forest full of elephants and lions. If you permit, we will travel with you. We will take you as far as you go, then bow and return.
essence: True help walks beside you, then lets you continue alone.
simple_meaning: The travelers say the forest is dangerous, but they offer to escort the brothers as far as needed and then return respectfully.
insight: It teaches you to offer support with humility, not possession.
modern_relevance: You see someone heading into a rough neighborhood alone after dark, and you offer to walk with them to the next corner. You help without taking over.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: एहि बिधि पूँछहिं प्रेम बस पुलक गात जलु नैन। कृपासिंधु फेरहिं तिन्हहि कहि बिनीत मृदु बैन ॥
translation: इस प्रकार वे यात्री प्रेमवश पुलकित शरीर हो और नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भरकर पूछते हैं, किन्तु कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी कोमल विनययुक्त वचन कहकर उन्हें लौटा देते हैं ॥
english_translation: In this way, the travelers ask with love, their bodies thrilled and their eyes full of tears. The ocean of compassion, Ram, sends them back with gentle, humble words.
essence: Kindness can be complete even when it is brief.
simple_meaning: The travelers, moved by love, ask their questions with tears in their eyes, and Ram gently sends them on their way.
insight: It highlights Ram’s gentle presence: even brief encounters become acts of grace.
modern_relevance: A stranger asks for directions while you are rushing to catch a train. You still slow down, answer kindly, and move on without making it about yourself.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जे पुर गाँव बसहिं मग माहीं। तिन्हहि नाग सुर नगर सिहाहीं॥ केहि सुकृतीं केहि घरीं बसाए। धन्य पुन्यमय परम सुहाए ॥
translation: जो गाँव और पुरवे रास्ते में बसे हैं, नागों और देवताओं के नगर उनको देखकर प्रशंसा पूर्वक ईर्षा करते और ललचाते हुए कहते हैं कि किस पुण्यवान् ने किस शुभ घड़ी में इनको बसाया था, जो आज ये इतने धन्य और पुण्यमय तथा परम सुंदर हो रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The villages and towns along the road are so blessed that even the cities of the gods envy them, asking, "What righteous person settled them, and in what lucky hour, that they have become so beautiful and full of merit?"
essence: Where Ram passes, ordinary places become enviable.
simple_meaning: Any place where Ram's journey passes becomes so blessed that even heavenly cities envy it.
insight: It shifts attention from external beauty to the blessing created by holy presence.
modern_relevance: A train platform where someone you love finally steps off can feel more alive than a palace. Presence changes the meaning of a place more than architecture ever can.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ जहँ राम चरन चलि जाहीं। तिन्ह समान अमरावति नाहीं॥ पुन्यपुंज मग निकट निवासी। तिन्हहि सराहहिं सुरपुरबासी ॥
translation: जहाँ-जहाँ श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरण चले जाते हैं, उनके समान इन्द्र की पुरी अमरावती भी नहीं है। रास्ते के समीप बसने वाले भी बड़े पुण्यात्मा हैं- स्वर्ग में रहने वाले देवता भी उनकी सराहना करते हैं- ॥
english_translation: Wherever Ram's feet have walked, even Amaravati cannot match that place. Those who live near that road are highly blessed, and the beings of heaven praise them.
essence: Ram's presence makes ordinary ground more precious than heaven.
simple_meaning: Any place touched by Ram's feet becomes greater than heaven. Even people living near that path are considered deeply blessed.
insight: It shifts attention from status to presence: holiness is measured by contact with Ram, not by location.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after someone kind, steady, and deeply loved has passed through it. The air feels different. Some presence doesn't need a throne to change everything around it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जे भरि नयन बिलोकहिं रामहि। सीता लखन सहित घनस्यामहि॥ जे सर सरित राम अवगाहहिं। तिन्हहि देव सर सरित सराहहिं ॥
translation: जो नेत्र भरकर सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित घनश्याम श्री रामजी के दर्शन करते हैं, जिन तालाबों और नदियों में श्री रामजी स्नान कर लेते हैं, देवसरोवर और देवनदियाँ भी उनकी बड़ाई करती हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who behold Ram with full eyes, along with Sita and Lakshman, and those lakes and rivers in which Ram bathes — even the divine lakes and rivers praise them.
essence: Ram's presence turns ordinary places into places of honor.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram with Sita and Lakshman makes a place sacred. Even lakes and rivers become worthy of praise when Ram bathes in them.
insight: It shifts attention from objects themselves to the sanctifying power of presence and devotion.
modern_relevance: You walk into a quiet temple courtyard after a hard week, and the whole place feels different because of one calm presence. Some people don't just enter a space — they change it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जेहि तरु तर प्रभु बैठहिं जाई। करहिं कलपतरु तासु बड़ाई॥ परसि राम पद पदुम परागा। मानति भूमि भूरि निज भागा ॥
translation: जिस वृक्ष के नीचे प्रभु जा बैठते हैं, कल्पवृक्ष भी उसकी बड़ाई करते हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणकमलों की रज का स्पर्श करके पृथ्वी अपना बड़ा सौभाग्य मानती है ॥
english_translation: The tree beneath which the Lord sits is praised even by the wish-fulfilling tree. Touching the pollen of Ram's lotus feet, the earth counts itself greatly blessed.
essence: Ram's presence makes even nature feel blessed.
simple_meaning: Even ordinary places become sacred when Ram is there. The tree under him is praised, and the earth feels fortunate just to touch his feet.
insight: It shifts attention from objects to presence: holiness comes from contact with the worthy, not from status alone.
modern_relevance: A room where someone kind and steady enters can feel different at once. The space did not change — but your whole nervous system did.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: छाँह करहिं घन बिबुधगन बरषहिं सुमन सिहाहिं। देखत गिरि बन बिहग मृग रामु चले मग जाहिं ॥
translation: रास्ते में बादल छाया करते हैं और देवता फूल बरसाते और सिहाते हैं। पर्वत, वन और पशु-पक्षियों को देखते हुए श्री रामजी रास्ते में चले जा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Clouds shade the path, radiant beings shower flowers and rejoice. Seeing the hills, forests, birds, and animals, Ram walks onward.
essence: Ram's presence turns the whole world into welcome.
simple_meaning: As Ram walks, nature itself seems to welcome him: clouds give shade, radiant beings shower flowers, and the hills, forests, birds, and animals are all part of the scene.
insight: It shifts attention from action to aura: the verse makes Ram's presence itself the event.
modern_relevance: You walk into a place after a hard day, and the room feels different before anyone speaks. Sometimes presence changes the atmosphere more than words ever could.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीता लखन सहित रघुराई। गाँव निकट जब निकसहिं जाई॥ सुनि सब बाल बृद्ध नर नारी। चलहिं तुरत गृह काजु बिसारी ॥
translation: सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित श्री रघुनाथजी जब किसी गाँव के पास जा निकलते हैं, तब उनका आना सुनते ही बालक-बूढ़े, स्त्री-पुरुष सब अपने घर और काम-काज को भूलकर तुरंत उन्हें देखने के लिए चल देते हैं ॥
english_translation: When Raghunath, along with Sita and Lakshman, comes near a village, hearing of their arrival all the old and young, men and women, leave their homes and work at once to go see them.
essence: Ram’s nearness makes ordinary life irrelevant for a moment.
simple_meaning: When Ram, Sita, and Lakshman come near a village, everyone leaves home and work to see them.
insight: It shows how devotion can interrupt ordinary life and make presence matter more than productivity.
modern_relevance: You hear a beloved teacher is coming to your neighborhood, and suddenly errands, chores, and schedules lose their grip. Something deeper than routine has already taken hold of you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम लखन सिय रूप निहारी। पाइ नयन फलु होहिं सुखारी॥ सजल बिलोचन पुलक सरीरा। सब भए मगन देखि दोउ बीरा ॥
translation: श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीताजी का रूप देखकर, नेत्रों का (परम) फल पाकर वे सुखी होते हैं। दोनों भाइयों को देखकर सब प्रेमानन्द में मग्न हो गए। उनके नेत्रों में जल भर आया और शरीर पुलकित हो गए ॥
english_translation: Seeing the forms of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, they became joyful as if their eyes had found their true reward. Seeing the two brothers, everyone was lost in love and delight. Their eyes filled with tears and their bodies thrilled with goosebumps.
essence: Their presence alone turns seeing into fulfillment.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram, Lakshman, and Sita fills everyone with joy, tears, and goosebumps. Their presence alone makes the crowd feel fulfilled.
insight: It shows how sacred presence can move people beyond thought into immediate love and reverence.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone you deeply respect across a crowded station, and your whole chest softens. Some presences speak before any words do.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बरनि न जाइ दसा तिन्ह केरी। लहि जनु रंकन्ह सुरमनि ढेरी॥ एकन्ह एक बोलि सिख देहीं। लोचन लाहु लेहु छन एहीं ॥
translation: उनकी दशा वर्णन नहीं की जाती। मानो दरिद्रों ने चिन्तामणि की ढेरी पा ली हो। वे एक-एक को पुकारकर सीख देते हैं कि इसी क्षण नेत्रों का लाभ ले लो ॥
english_translation: Their state cannot be described. It was as if the poor had found heaps of wish-fulfilling jewels. Each one called to another and said, “Take in the sight now, in this very moment.”
essence: Presence so precious makes every second feel like treasure.
simple_meaning: The people are overwhelmed by Ram, Lakshman, and Sita’s presence. Their joy is beyond description, like the poor suddenly finding priceless treasure.
insight: It turns attention into urgency: when something precious appears, the right response is immediate presence.
modern_relevance: You catch a brief glimpse of someone you love across a crowded station platform, and your whole body says, don’t look away.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामहि देखि एक अनुरागे। चितवत चले जाहिं सँग लागे॥ एक नयन मग छबि उर आनी। होहिं सिथिल तन मन बर बानी ॥
translation: कोई श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर ऐसे अनुराग में भर गए हैं कि वे उन्हें देखते हुए उनके साथ लगे चले जा रहे हैं। कोई नेत्र मार्ग से उनकी छबि को हृदय में लाकर शरीर, मन और श्रेष्ठ वाणी से शिथिल हो जाते हैं (अर्थात् उनके शरीर, मन और वाणी का व्यवहार बंद हो जाता है) ॥
english_translation: Some, filled with love just by seeing Ram, keep walking along with him while still gazing at him. Others bring his beauty into their hearts through a glance and then become quiet in body, mind, and speech.
essence: Love for Ram can quiet the whole person at once.
simple_meaning: Just seeing Ram overwhelms people in different ways: some follow him while staring, and some become so absorbed that body, mind, and speech fall quiet.
insight: It shows how genuine devotion shifts the whole person, not just the thoughts.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone you deeply admire across a crowded station, and for a moment everything else drops away. Attention, speech, and even your posture change before you notice.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक देखि बट छाँह भलि डासि मृदुल तृन पात। कहहिं गवाँइअ छिनुकु श्रमु गवनब अबहिंकि प्रात ॥
translation: कोई बड़ की सुंदर छाया देखकर, वहाँ नरम घास और पत्ते बिछाकर कहते हैं कि क्षण भर यहाँ बैठकर थकावट मिटा लीजिए। फिर चाहे अभी चले जाइएगा, चाहे सबेरे ॥
english_translation: Seeing a good banyan-tree shade, they spread soft grass and leaves and say, "Rest here a moment and ease your fatigue. You may leave now or in the morning."
essence: Devotion becomes real when it makes room for someone to rest.
simple_meaning: People see Ram and lovingly prepare a shady resting place for him, telling him to sit a moment and rest before continuing his journey.
insight: It shifts attention from admiration to practical care.
modern_relevance: You notice someone dragging after a long day and quietly pull out a chair, a bottle of water, and a place to breathe. Care often begins there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक कलस भरि आनहिं पानी। अँचइअ नाथ कहहिं मृदु बानी॥ सुनि प्रिय बचन प्रीति अति देखी। राम कृपाल सुसील बिसेषी ॥
translation: कोई घड़ा भरकर पानी ले आते हैं और कोमल वाणी से कहते हैं- नाथ! आचमन तो कर लीजिए। उनके प्यारे वचन सुनकर और उनका अत्यन्त प्रेम देखकर दयालु और परम सुशील श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने- ॥
english_translation: Some bring a pot full of water and softly say, “Lord, please take a sip.” Hearing their loving words and seeing their deep affection, compassionate and ever-gentle Ram...
essence: Affection becomes real when it turns into care.
simple_meaning: People lovingly bring water and invite Ram to rest and refresh himself. Their affection moves him, and his gentle nature responds to their care.
insight: It shifts attention from admiration to service: love is proven by what you do for someone in front of you.
modern_relevance: You hand someone a glass of water after a hard day, and the whole room changes. Small care, offered with love, can carry more power than grand speeches.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जानी श्रमित सीय मन माहीं। घरिक बिलंबु कीन्ह बट छाहीं॥ मुदित नारि नर देखहिं सोभा। रूप अनूप नयन मनु लोभा ॥
translation: मन में सीताजी को थकी हुई जानकर घड़ी भर बड़ की छाया में विश्राम किया। स्त्री-पुरुष आनंदित होकर शोभा देखते हैं। अनुपम रूप ने उनके नेत्र और मनों को लुभा लिया है ॥
english_translation: Knowing Sita was tired, they paused for a while in the shade of a banyan tree. Men and women looked on with delight; his unmatched beauty captivated their eyes and minds.
essence: Care for the tired person first; beauty follows naturally.
simple_meaning: Seeing Sita was tired, they rested briefly in the shade. Everyone around them felt joy, and Ram's unmatched beauty drew the eyes and hearts of all.
insight: It teaches you to respond to another person's fatigue with immediate care, not efficiency.
modern_relevance: You notice someone beside you is exhausted, so you slow down, find shade, and let the moment breathe. That small kindness changes the whole atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एकटक सब सोहहिं चहुँ ओरा। रामचन्द्र मुख चंद चकोरा॥ तरुन तमाल बरन तनु सोहा। देखत कोटि मदन मनु मोहा ॥
translation: सब लोग टकटकी लगाए श्री रामचन्द्रजी के मुख चन्द्र को चकोर की तरह (तन्मय होकर) देखते हुए चारों ओर सुशोभित हो रहे हैं। श्री रामजी का नवीन तमाल वृक्ष के रंग का (श्याम) शरीर अत्यन्त शोभा दे रहा है, जिसे देखते ही करोड़ों कामदेवों के मन मोहित हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Everyone stands all around, gazing without blinking, like chakors around the moon-face of Ramchandra. His body, dark as a young tamal tree, shines so beautifully that it enchants the minds of millions of Cupids.
essence: Ram's presence makes everyone forget everything else.
simple_meaning: Everyone is spellbound by Ram's beauty. His face is like the moon to loving eyes, and his dark, graceful form overwhelms every heart.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary appearance to the power of presence itself.
modern_relevance: You enter a room and the whole mood changes before anyone speaks. Some people carry a calm beauty that draws every eye and softens every heart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दामिनि बरन लखन सुठि नीके। नख सिख सुभग भावते जी के॥ मुनि पट कटिन्ह कसें तूनीरा। सोहहिं कर कमलनि धनु तीरा ॥
translation: बिजली के से रंग के लक्ष्मणजी बहुत ही भले मालूम होते हैं। वे नख से शिखा तक सुंदर हैं और मन को बहुत भाते हैं। दोनों मुनियों के (वल्कल आदि) वस्त्र पहने हैं और कमर में तरकस कसे हुए हैं। कमल के समान हाथों में धनुष-बाण शोभित हो रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Lakshman, the one with lightning-like color, looks truly splendid. Beautiful from head to toe, he delights the heart. Wearing the bark cloth of a forest ascetic and a quiver at his waist, his lotus-like hands carry bow and arrows.
essence: True beauty is strength placed in loving service.
simple_meaning: Lakshman is described as strikingly beautiful, dressed like a forest ascetic, with a bow and arrows ready at his side.
insight: It shifts attention from mere appearance to the dignity of devoted protection.
modern_relevance: You show up to protect someone you love, wearing no badge and asking for no credit. Even then, your steadiness changes the whole room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जटा मुकुट सीसनि सुभग उर भुज नयन बिसाल। सरद परब बिधु बदन बर लसत स्वेद कन जाल ॥
translation: उनके सिरों पर सुंदर जटाओं के मुकुट हैं, वक्षः स्थल, भुजा और नेत्र विशाल हैं और शरद पूर्णिमा के चन्द्रमा के समान सुंदर मुखों पर पसीने की बूँदों का समूह शोभित हो रहा है ॥
english_translation: Their heads wear lovely matted-crown locks, their chests, arms, and eyes are broad, and drops of sweat shine on their moonlike faces.
essence: Hardship does not dim their radiance.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are described as radiant and beautiful, with matted hair, broad bodies, and sweat shining on their faces.
insight: It shifts attention from polished appearance to the beauty of steadfast presence.
modern_relevance: After a long walk in the heat, your shirt is damp and your face is tired — yet someone still looks at you with admiration. Effort does not cancel dignity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बरनि न जाइ मनोहर जोरी। सोभा बहुत थोरि मति मोरी॥ राम लखन सिय सुंदरताई। सब चितवहिं चित मन मति लाई ॥
translation: उस मनोहर जोड़ी का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता, क्योंकि शोभा बहुत अधिक है और मेरी बुद्धि थोड़ी है। श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीताजी की सुंदरता को सब लोग मन, चित्त और बुद्धि तीनों को लगाकर देख रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: That lovely pair cannot be described; my understanding is too small for their great beauty. Everyone is looking at the beauty of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita with full attention of mind, heart, and intellect.
essence: True beauty leaves words behind and holds the whole mind still.
simple_meaning: Their beauty is beyond description, and everyone is looking at Ram, Lakshman, and Sita with complete attention.
insight: It shifts attention from explanation to direct seeing, where beauty is recognized before it is analyzed.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and everyone falls silent for a second, not from awkwardness but from presence. Some people carry a beauty that makes language feel too small.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: थके नारि नर प्रेम पिआसे। मनहुँ मृगी मृग देखि दिआ से॥ सीय समीप ग्रामतिय जाहीं। पूँछत अति सनेहँ सकुचाहीं ॥
translation: प्रेम के प्यासे (वे गाँवों के) स्त्री-पुरुष (इनके सौंदर्य-माधुर्य की छटा देखकर) ऐसे थकित रह गए जैसे दीपक को देखकर हिरनी और हिरन (निस्तब्ध रह जाते हैं)! गाँवों की स्त्रियाँ सीताजी के पास जाती हैं, परन्तु अत्यन्त स्नेह के कारण पूछते सकुचाती हैं ॥
english_translation: The men and women, thirsty for love, grew still as if deer had seen a lamp. The village women went near Sita, but their great affection made them shy to ask anything.
essence: A loving presence can leave people speechless.
simple_meaning: The people are so captivated by Ram, Lakshman, and Sita that they stand still in wonder. The village women approach Sita, but their affection makes them too shy to speak freely.
insight: It captures how reverence can quiet the mind before a beloved presence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and suddenly forget what you were going to say. The person in front of you feels so graceful, so kind, that your own words come out timid and small.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बार बार सब लागहिं पाएँ। कहहिं बचन मृदु सरल सुभाएँ॥ राजकुमारि बिनय हम करहीं। तिय सुभायँ कछु पूँछत डरहीं ॥
translation: बार-बार सब उनके पाँव लगतीं और सहज ही सीधे-सादे कोमल वचन कहती हैं- हे राजकुमारी! हम विनती करती (कुछ निवेदन करना चाहती) हैं, परन्तु स्त्री स्वभाव के कारण कुछ पूछते हुए डरती हैं ॥
english_translation: Again and again they touched her feet and spoke in gentle, simple words: 'Princess, we wish to make a request, but in a woman's nature there is some fear in asking.'
essence: Humility can make even fear speak beautifully.
simple_meaning: The women repeatedly bow to Sita and speak with soft respect, asking permission to speak while admitting they feel shy and hesitant.
insight: It shows how reverence turns hesitation into courteous speech.
modern_relevance: You rehearse the message three times before knocking on her door, then soften your voice the moment she opens it. Respect can make even fear speak gently.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: स्वामिनि अबिनय छमबि हमारी। बिलगु न मानब जानि गवाँरी॥ राजकुअँर दोउ सहज सलोने। इन्ह तें लही दुति मरकत सोने ॥
translation: हे स्वामिनी! हमारी ढिठाई क्षमा कीजिएगा और हमको गँवारी जानकर बुरा न मानिएगा। ये दोनों राजकुमार स्वभाव से ही लावण्यमय (परम सुंदर) हैं। मरकतमणि (पन्ने) और सुवर्ण ने कांति इन्हीं से पाई है (अर्थात मरकतमणि में और स्वर्ण में जो हरित और स्वर्ण वर्ण की आभा है, वह इनकी हरिताभ नील और स्वर्ण कान्ति के एक कण के बराबर भी नहीं है।) ॥
english_translation: O mistress, forgive our rudeness and do not take us for simple village women. These two princes are naturally beautiful; emerald and gold get their glow from them.
essence: Natural beauty makes hesitation turn into reverence.
simple_meaning: The village women politely ask Sita to forgive their boldness and say the two princes are naturally radiant and beautiful.
insight: It shifts attention from social hesitation to spontaneous reverence before genuine beauty.
modern_relevance: You meet someone so composed and radiant that your own awkwardness suddenly feels small. Instead of pretending confidence, you speak more gently and honestly.
speaker: Village women

verse_text: स्यामल गौर किसोर बर सुंदर सुषमा ऐन। सरद सर्बरीनाथ मुखु सरद सरोरुह नैन ॥
translation: श्याम और गौर वर्ण है, सुंदर किशोर अवस्था है, दोनों ही परम सुंदर और शोभा के धाम हैं। शरद पूर्णिमा के चन्द्रमा के समान इनके मुख और शरद ऋतु के कमल के समान इनके नेत्र हैं ॥
english_translation: Dark and fair, both are beautiful youths, full of loveliness. Their faces are like the autumn moon, and their eyes like autumn lotuses.
essence: Their beauty is so complete it makes even language wait.
simple_meaning: Both princes are strikingly beautiful, with moonlike faces and lotus-like eyes.
insight: It pauses the scene on pure appearance, letting wonder build before identity is revealed.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone across a crowded room and forget your own sentence. Some moments begin with beauty before they begin with words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोटि मनोज लजावनिहारे। सुमुखि कहहु को आहिं तुम्हारे॥ सुनि सनेहमय मंजुल बानी। सकुची सिय मन महुँ मुसुकानी ॥
translation: हे सुमुखि! कहो तो अपनी सुंदरता से करोड़ों कामदेवों को लजाने वाले ये तुम्हारे कौन हैं? उनकी ऐसी प्रेममयी सुंदर वाणी सुनकर सीताजी सकुचा गईं और मन ही मन मुस्कुराईं ॥
english_translation: O beautiful one, tell me who these are that shame millions of Cupids. Hearing that tender, lovely speech, Sita grew shy and smiled inwardly.
essence: Gentle speech can make beauty feel even more overwhelming.
