simple_meaning: The two princes are so beautiful that they seem to outshine even countless Cupids. Their gentle words make Sita shy and quietly happy.
insight: It shows how grace, not display, creates the deepest first impression.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose kindness is as striking as their appearance, and suddenly you cannot hide your smile. The heart notices before the mind can speak.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तिन्हहि बिलोकि बिलोकति धरनी। दुहुँ सकोच सकुचति बरबरनी॥ सकुचि सप्रेम बाल मृग नयनी। बोली मधुर बचन पिकबयनी ॥
translation: उत्तम (गौर) वर्णवाली सीताजी उनको देखकर (संकोचवश) पृथ्वी की ओर देखती हैं। वे दोनों ओर के संकोच से सकुचा रही हैं (अर्थात न बताने में ग्राम की स्त्रियों को दुःख होने का संकोच है और बताने में लज्जा रूप संकोच)। हिरन के बच्चे के सदृश नेत्र वाली और कोकिल की सी वाणी वाली सीताजी सकुचाकर प्रेम सहित मधुर वचन बोलीं- ॥
english_translation: Seeing them, fair Sita looks down at the ground. Shy from both sides, the fair lady grows bashful. Blushing with love, the doe-eyed one speaks sweetly, like a cuckoo.
essence: Shy love speaks softly before it speaks clearly.
simple_meaning: Sita feels shy when she sees them and lowers her gaze. Blushing with love and modesty, she finally speaks in a soft, sweet voice.
insight: It shows how reverence and affection can shape the very way you speak.
modern_relevance: You meet someone important and suddenly forget your rehearsed words. The pause, the lowered eyes, the careful first sentence — that is human warmth before confidence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सहज सुभाय सुभग तन गोरे। नामु लखनु लघु देवर मोरे॥ बहुरि बदनु बिधु अंचल ढाँकी। पिय तन चितइ भौंह करि बाँकी ॥
translation: ये जो सहज स्वभाव, सुंदर और गोरे शरीर के हैं, उनका नाम लक्ष्मण है, ये मेरे छोटे देवर हैं। फिर सीताजी ने (लज्जावश) अपने चन्द्रमुख को आँचल से ढँककर और प्रियतम (श्री रामजी) की ओर निहारकर भौंहें टेढ़ी करके, ॥
english_translation: By natural disposition, handsome and fair-bodied, his name is Lakshman, my younger brother-in-law. Then Sita covered her moonlike face with the edge of her veil and, looking at her beloved's body, arched her brows.
essence: Shyness becomes its own language when love is already understood.
simple_meaning: Sita shyly identifies Lakshman as her younger brother-in-law, then hides her face and glances toward Ram with a playful, loving gesture.
insight: It shows how affection often reveals itself through gesture, not explanation.
modern_relevance: At a family gathering, you introduce the person you love with a smile, then look down because everyone already understands more than your words say.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: खंजन मंजु तिरीछे नयननि। निज पति कहेउ तिन्हहि सियँ सयननि॥ भईं मुदित सब ग्रामबधूटीं। रंकन्ह राय रासि जनु लूटीं ॥
translation: खंजन पक्षी के से सुंदर नेत्रों को तिरछा करके सीताजी ने इशारे से उन्हें कहा कि ये (श्री रामचन्द्रजी) मेरे पति हैं। यह जानकर गाँव की सब युवती स्त्रियाँ इस प्रकार आनंदित हुईं, मानो कंगालों ने धन की राशियाँ लूट ली हों ॥
english_translation: Sita glanced sideways with her beautiful eyes and signaled, “He is my husband.” Hearing this, all the village women rejoiced, as if beggars had found heaps of treasure.
essence: Love needs no loud announcement; the heart understands at once.
simple_meaning: Sita quietly points out Ram as her husband, and the village women feel overjoyed at the sight of such a blessed union.
insight: It shows how recognition can transform a quiet moment into shared celebration.
modern_relevance: You catch the look between two people who finally belong together, and everyone nearby feels it. Some joy is so pure it spreads without explanation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अति सप्रेम सिय पाँय परि बहुबिधि देहिं असीस। सदा सोहागिनि होहु तुम्ह जब लगि महि अहि सीस॥117
translation: वे अत्यन्त प्रेम से सीताजी के पैरों पड़कर बहुत प्रकार से आशीष देती हैं (शुभ कामना करती हैं), कि जब तक शेषजी के सिर पर पृथ्वी रहे, तब तक तुम सदा सुहागिनी बनी रहो, ॥
english_translation: With deep love, they bowed at Sita's feet and blessed her in many ways: 'May you always remain a blessed wife as long as the earth rests on Shesha's head.'
essence: Love becomes blessing when it wishes another person lasting wholeness.
simple_meaning: The women lovingly honor Sita and pray that she always remain happily united with her husband.
insight: It turns admiration into blessing, showing how love naturally wants another person's life to remain whole.
modern_relevance: At a wedding, an elder quietly blesses the bride after the ceremony, not with grand words but with a wish that her home stay full of warmth and steadiness. That simple blessing carries real love.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पारबती सम पतिप्रिय होहू। देबि न हम पर छाड़ब छोहू॥ पुनि पुनि बिनय करिअ कर जोरी। जौं एहि मारग फिरिअ बहोरी ॥
translation: और पार्वतीजी के समान अपने पति की प्यारी होओ। हे देवी! हम पर कृपा न छोड़ना (बनाए रखना)। हम बार-बार हाथ जोड़कर विनती करती हैं, जिसमें आप फिर इसी रास्ते लौटें, ॥
english_translation: Be as devoted to your husband as Parvati is. O goddess, do not withdraw your grace from us. Again and again, with folded hands, we beg you to return by this path.
essence: True devotion asks for grace without claiming control.
simple_meaning: The women ask Sita to be as devoted to her husband as Parvati is, and to keep showing them kindness so she will return this way again.
insight: It teaches you to honor devotion in others without trying to own it.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose steadiness softens a whole room, and you find yourself wanting to ask, almost shyly, that they stay the same. This is the language of reverence, not possession.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दरसनु देब जानि निज दासी। लखीं सीयँ सब प्रेम पिआसी॥ मधुर बचन कहि कहि परितोषीं। जनु कुमुदिनीं कौमुदीं पोषीं ॥
translation: और हमें अपनी दासी जानकर दर्शन दें। सीताजी ने उन सबको प्रेम की प्यासी देखा और मधुर वचन कह-कहकर उनका भलीभाँति संतोष किया। मानो चाँदनी ने कुमुदिनियों को खिलाकर पुष्ट कर दिया हो ॥
english_translation: Knowing them as her own servants, Sita gave them darshan. Seeing them all thirsty for love, she soothed them with sweet words, like moonlight nourishing night-blooming lilies.
essence: Tenderness satisfies longing more deeply than status ever could.
simple_meaning: Sita welcomes the women kindly, sees their longing, and comforts them with gentle words.
insight: It teaches you to notice emotional hunger and answer it with kindness, not distance.
modern_relevance: A room full of people is waiting for your attention, and you can feel their need before they say a word. A few gentle words can change the whole atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तबहिं लखन रघुबर रुख जानी। पूँछेउ मगु लोगन्हि मृदु बानी॥ सुनत नारि नर भए दुखारी। पुलकित गात बिलोचन बारी ॥
translation: उसी समय श्री रामचन्द्रजी का रुख जानकर लक्ष्मणजी ने कोमल वाणी से लोगों से रास्ता पूछा। यह सुनते ही स्त्री-पुरुष दुःखी हो गए। उनके शरीर पुलकित हो गए और नेत्रों में (वियोग की सम्भावना से प्रेम का) जल भर आया ॥
english_translation: At that moment, seeing Ram's mood, Lakshman politely asked the people for the way. Hearing this, the men and women became sorrowful; their bodies trembled with emotion and tears filled their eyes.
essence: A gentle question can reveal a whole village's grief.
simple_meaning: Lakshman asks local people for the way in a gentle voice. They feel sudden sorrow at the thought of Ram leaving, and tears come to their eyes.
insight: It shows how deeply people feel Ram's presence, and how quickly the fear of separation spreads.
modern_relevance: You ask a stranger for directions, and their face changes because they know you are leaving for good. Sometimes the smallest question carries the weight of goodbye.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मिटा मोदु मन भए मलीने। बिधि निधि दीन्ह लेत जनु छीने॥ समुझि करम गति धीरजु कीन्हा। सोधि सुगम मगु तिन्ह कहि दीन्हा ॥
translation: उनका आनंद मिट गया और मन ऐसे उदास हो गए मानो विधाता दी हुई सम्पत्ति छीने लेता हो। कर्म की गति समझकर उन्होंने धैर्य धारण किया और अच्छी तरह निर्णय करके सुगम मार्ग बतला दिया ॥
english_translation: Their joy faded and their minds turned gloomy, as if fate were snatching away a gift it had given. Understanding the workings of karma, they held their patience and, after careful thought, showed the easy road.
essence: Patience lets you stay useful even when your heart is heavy.
simple_meaning: The people feel sad when Ram leaves, but they stay calm, understand the situation, and point out the easiest route.
insight: It teaches you to pause your reaction, understand the situation, and respond with practical calm.
modern_relevance: You just got difficult news, but someone still needs directions, a decision, or a calm answer. This verse shows how grief and usefulness can coexist.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लखन जानकी सहित तब गवनु कीन्ह रघुनाथ। फेरे सब प्रिय बचन कहि लिए लाइ मन साथ ॥
translation: तब लक्ष्मणजी और जानकीजी सहित श्री रघुनाथजी ने गमन किया और सब लोगों को प्रिय वचन कहकर लौटाया, किन्तु उनके मनों को अपने साथ ही लगा लिया ॥
english_translation: Then Raghunath departed with Lakshman and Janaki. He sent everyone back with kind words, yet carried their hearts away with him.
essence: Kind words can soothe departure, but not erase longing.
simple_meaning: Ram leaves with Lakshman and Sita, speaking kindly to the people, but their hearts remain with him.
insight: It shows how love can remain even after departure, and how a gentle farewell does not erase loss.
modern_relevance: You say a warm goodbye at the train station, but the room still feels empty after they leave. Their kindness helps, yet the ache stays.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: फिरत नारि नर अति पछिताहीं। दैअहि दोषु देहिं मन माहीं॥ सहित बिषाद परसपर कहहीं। बिधि करतब उलटे सब अहहीं ॥
translation: लौटते हुए वे स्त्री-पुरुष बहुत ही पछताते हैं और मन ही मन दैव को दोष देते हैं। परस्पर (बड़े ही) विषाद के साथ कहते हैं कि विधाता के सभी काम उलटे हैं ॥
english_translation: Men and women returning home feel deep regret. They blame fate in their hearts and, in sorrow, tell one another that the workings of fate are all reversed.
essence: Grief makes the heart call the world upside down.
simple_meaning: The people leaving feel regret and blame fate. In their sorrow, they say everything has gone backward.
insight: It shows how grief turns the mind toward blame and backward-looking regret instead of clear seeing.
modern_relevance: You leave a hospital room after bad news and keep replaying the last ten minutes. The mind wants an explanation before it can bear the hurt.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निपट निरंकुस निठुर निसंकू। जेहिं ससि कीन्ह सरुज सकलंकू॥ रूख कलपतरु सागरु खारा। तेहिं पठए बन राजकुमारा ॥
translation: वह विधाता बिल्कुल निरंकुश (स्वतंत्र), निर्दय और निडर है, जिसने चन्द्रमा को रोगी (घटने-बढ़ने वाला) और कलंकी बनाया, कल्पवृक्ष को पेड़ और समुद्र को खारा बनाया। उसी ने इन राजकुमारों को वन में भेजा है ॥
english_translation: That utterly unchecked, cruel, and fearless creator made the moon wan and blemished, made the wish-fulfilling tree a mere tree, and made the sea salty. That same power has sent these princes into the forest.
essence: Grief sees even the world’s beauty as wounded.
simple_meaning: The speaker blames the creator for making even beautiful things imperfect and for sending the princes into exile.
insight: It shows how sorrow turns perception harsh and makes suffering look like cruelty.
modern_relevance: You watch someone kind lose everything in one afternoon, and your mind reaches for someone to blame. Grief often speaks first in accusation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जौं पै इन्हहिं दीन्ह बनबासू। कीन्ह बादि बिधि भोग बिलासू॥ ए बिचरहिं मग बिनु पदत्राना। रचे बादि बिधि बाहन नाना ॥
translation: जब विधाता ने इनको वनवास दिया है, तब उसने भोग-विलास व्यर्थ ही बनाए। जब ये बिना जूते के (नंगे ही पैरों) रास्ते में चल रहे हैं, तब विधाता ने अनेकों वाहन (सवारियाँ) व्यर्थ ही रचे ॥
english_translation: If these princes must live in the forest, then luxury was created in vain. If they must walk barefoot on the road, then countless vehicles were created in vain.
essence: Exile makes luxury look pointless.
simple_meaning: The verse laments that luxury and vehicles seem pointless when these princes have been sent into forest exile and must travel on foot.
insight: It shifts the mind from status and comfort to what remains usable in hardship.
modern_relevance: You pack for a trip, then the flight is canceled and you end up walking through rain with one bag and sore feet. Suddenly, all the polished plans feel absurd beside what is actually needed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ए महि परहिं डासि कुस पाता। सुभग सेज कत सृजत बिधाता॥ तरुबर बास इन्हहि बिधि दीन्हा। धवल धाम रचि रचि श्रमु कीन्हा ॥
translation: जब ये कुश और पत्ते बिछाकर जमीन पर ही पड़े रहते हैं, तब विधाता सुंदर सेज (पलंग और बिछौने) किसलिए बनाता है? विधाता ने जब इनको बड़े-बड़े पेड़ों (के नीचे) का निवास दिया, तब उज्ज्वल महलों को बना-बनाकर उसने व्यर्थ ही परिश्रम किया ॥
english_translation: When they lie on the ground on kusa grass and leaves, why would the Creator make a beautiful bed? When they have been given life under great trees, the bright palaces built again and again were wasted effort.
essence: When simplicity is enough, luxury becomes unnecessary.
simple_meaning: The princes have been sent to live simply in the forest, so grand comforts and palaces no longer matter. Their present life makes luxury feel unnecessary.
insight: It shifts desire away from display and toward what can actually sustain you.
modern_relevance: You unpack into a tiny rented room after losing the apartment you thought was permanent. The bare floor, the thin mattress, the quiet air — suddenly, the expensive things you chased feel less important.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जौं ए मुनि पट धर जटिल सुंदर सुठि सुकुमार। बिबिध भाँति भूषन बसन बादि किए करतार ॥
translation: जो ये सुंदर और अत्यन्त सुकुमार होकर मुनियों के (वल्कल) वस्त्र पहनते और जटा धारण करते हैं, तो फिर करतार (विधाता) ने भाँति-भाँति के गहने और कपड़े वृथा ही बनाए ॥
english_translation: If these handsome, delicate ones wear the dress of sages and matted hair, then the Creator made ornaments and fine clothes in vain.
essence: Real beauty makes ornament feel unnecessary.
simple_meaning: Their natural beauty is so complete that even rough sage-clothes and matted hair suit them; compared with that, ornaments and fine clothes seem unnecessary.
insight: It shifts attention from decoration to intrinsic worth, showing that true beauty does not depend on display.
modern_relevance: You watch someone leave for a long, hard season with only a backpack and one plain shirt, yet they somehow look more complete than anyone dressed for display. Some people make excess feel unnecessary.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जौं ए कंदमूल फल खाहीं। बादि सुधादि असन जग माहीं॥ एक कहहिं ए सहज सुहाए। आपु प्रगट भए बिधि न बनाए ॥
translation: जो ये कन्द, मूल, फल खाते हैं, तो जगत में अमृत आदि भोजन व्यर्थ ही हैं। कोई एक कहते हैं- ये स्वभाव से ही सुंदर हैं (इनका सौंदर्य-माधुर्य नित्य और स्वाभाविक है)। ये अपने-आप प्रकट हुए हैं, ब्रह्मा के बनाए नहीं हैं ॥
english_translation: If they eat roots, bulbs, and fruits, then nectar-like foods in the world are pointless. Some say they are naturally lovely: their beauty and sweetness are self-evident, not made by Brahma.
essence: Simple living can make the finest things seem unnecessary.
simple_meaning: Forest life makes simple food feel enough, and these people seem so naturally lovely that their beauty feels self-made, not manufactured.
insight: It shifts attention from luxury to sufficiency, and from manufactured beauty to what is naturally complete.
modern_relevance: You open a lunchbox after a long day and a simple banana tastes better than a luxury meal. When life is stripped down, what is natural and enough starts to shine.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ लगिबेद कही बिधि करनी। श्रवन नयन मन गोचर बरनी॥ देखहु खोजि भुअन दस चारी। कहँ अस पुरुष कहाँ असि नारी ॥
translation: हमारे कानों, नेत्रों और मन के द्वारा अनुभव में आने वाली विधाता की करनी को जहाँ तक वेदों ने वर्णन करके कहा है, वहाँ तक चौदहों लोकों में ढूँढ देखो, ऐसे पुरुष और ऐसी स्त्रियाँ कहाँ हैं? (कहीं भी नहीं हैं, इसी से सिद्ध है कि ये विधाता के चौदहों लोकों से अलग हैं और अपनी महिमा से ही आप निर्मित हुए हैं) ॥
english_translation: As far as the Vedas describe the workings of the Creator that can be known by hearing, seeing, and mind, search through all fourteen worlds: where are such a man and such a woman? They are nowhere.
essence: True greatness outgrows every comparison.
simple_meaning: Even the Vedas can only partly describe them. If you search all fourteen worlds, you will not find a man or woman like them.
insight: It shifts the mind from comparison to reverence, letting excellence be seen without reducing it.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm, dignity, and goodness make every comparison feel small. You stop trying to rank them and simply recognise: this person stands apart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: इन्हहि देखि बिधि मनु अनुरागा। पटतर जोग बनावै लागा॥ कीन्ह बहुत श्रम ऐक न आए। तेहिं इरिषा बन आनि दुराए ॥
translation: इन्हें देखकर विधाता का मन अनुरक्त (मुग्ध) हो गया, तब वह भी इन्हीं की उपमा के योग्य दूसरे स्त्री-पुरुष बनाने लगा। उसने बहुत परिश्रम किया, परन्तु कोई उसकी अटकल में ही नहीं आए (पूरे नहीं उतरे)। इसी ईर्षा के मारे उसने इनको जंगल में लाकर छिपा दिया है ॥
english_translation: Seeing them, the creator's mind became enchanted. He began making others worthy of comparison, but after much effort, none matched them. Out of envy, he brought them into the forest and hid them there.
essence: True beauty defeats imitation and exposes the limits of making.
simple_meaning: Their beauty was so complete that even the creator was captivated. He tried to make others like them, but failed, and then hid them in the forest out of envy.
insight: It shifts attention from manufactured perfection to the rare presence that cannot be manufactured.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence makes every polished imitation feel flat. No filter, no upgrade, no careful branding can reproduce what is naturally whole.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक कहहिं हम बहुत न जानहिं। आपुहि परम धन्य करि मानहिं॥ ते पुनि पुन्यपुंज हम लेखे। जे देखहिं देखिहहिं जिन्ह देखे ॥
translation: कोई एक कहते हैं- हम बहुत नहीं जानते। हाँ, अपने को परम धन्य अवश्य मानते हैं (जो इनके दर्शन कर रहे हैं) और हमारी समझ में वे भी बड़े पुण्यवान हैं, जिन्होंने इनको देखा है, जो देख रहे हैं और जो देखेंगे ॥
english_translation: Some say, “We know very little, but we count ourselves supremely blessed.” They also call blessed those who have seen them, who are seeing them, and who will see them.
essence: Seeing what is precious makes even simple presence feel blessed.
simple_meaning: The people are overwhelmed by the sight of these figures. They say they do not know much, but feel deeply blessed just to be there, and they praise anyone who has seen them.
insight: It shifts attention from analysis to reverent presence, letting wonder become the response.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and feel words fail because something precious is happening there. You do not need to explain it to know you are fortunate to witness it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि बिधि कहि कहि बचन प्रिय लेहिं नयन भरि नीर। किमि चलिहहिं मारग अगम सुठि सुकुमार सरीर ॥
translation: इस प्रकार प्रिय वचन कह-कहकर सब नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर लेते हैं और कहते हैं कि ये अत्यन्त सुकुमार शरीर वाले दुर्गम (कठिन) मार्ग में कैसे चलेंगे ॥
english_translation: Saying such loving words, they all fill their eyes with tears and ask, "How will these very delicate bodies walk the difficult road?"
essence: Love sees the road, then worries about the body that must walk it.
simple_meaning: Everyone speaks with love and tears, worried that such delicate bodies cannot bear the hard journey ahead.
insight: It turns parting into tenderness, showing how love notices fragility first.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you love leave with a small bag and tired eyes. The blessing rises in your throat, but what you really feel is fear for their strength.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नारि सनेह बिकल बस होहीं। चकईं साँझ समय जनु सोहीं॥ मृदु पद कमल कठिन मगु जानी। गहबरि हृदयँ कहहिं बर बानी ॥
translation: स्त्रियाँ स्नेहवश विकल हो जाती हैं। मानो संध्या के समय चकवी (भावी वियोग की पीड़ा से) सोह रही हो। (दुःखी हो रही हो)। इनके चरणकमलों को कोमल तथा मार्ग को कठोर जानकर वे व्यथित हृदय से उत्तम वाणी कहती हैं- ॥
english_translation: Women, overcome by love, become helpless. Like a chakavi at dusk, they seem to sink into sorrow. Knowing the lotus-soft feet are tender and the road is hard, they speak beautiful words from troubled hearts.
essence: Love makes hardship feel unbearable, so the heart speaks gently.
simple_meaning: Love makes them weak with grief. Seeing the feet as tender and the path as hard, they speak gently from troubled hearts.
insight: It shows how love can soften speech, even when the heart is breaking.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you love zip up a bag for a move you cannot stop. Your throat tightens because you know the road will be harder than they admit.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परसत मृदुल चरन अरुनारे। सकुचति महि जिमि हृदय हमारे॥ जौं जगदीस इन्हहि बनु दीन्हा। कस न सुमनमय मारगु कीन्हा ॥
translation: इनके कोमल और लाल-लाल चरणों (तलवों) को छूते ही पृथ्वी वैसे ही सकुचा जाती है, जैसे हमारे हृदय सकुचा रहे हैं। जगदीश्वर ने यदि इन्हें वनवास ही दिया, तो सारे रास्ते को पुष्पमय क्यों नहीं बना दिया? ॥
english_translation: Touching their soft, red feet, the earth shrinks back just as our hearts are shrinking. If the lord of the world has sent them to the forest, why was the whole road not made of flowers?
essence: Even the road feels wrong when love is being sent away.
simple_meaning: The people are so heartbroken that even the ground seems to recoil under Rama and Sita's tender feet. They wish the exile road itself had been softened for them.
insight: It turns grief into tenderness, making the reader feel how deeply the heart resists separation.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you love leave with a small bag and no complaint, and the whole street feels too hard, too ordinary, too cruel for that moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जौं मागा पाइअ बिधि पाहीं। ए रखिअहिं सखि आँखिन्ह माहीं॥ जे नर नारि न अवसर आए। तिन्ह सिय रामु न देखन पाए ॥
translation: यदि ब्रह्मा से माँगे मिले तो हे सखी! (हम तो उनसे माँगकर) इन्हें अपनी आँखों में ही रखें! जो स्त्री-पुरुष इस अवसर पर नहीं आए, वे श्री सीतारामजी को नहीं देख सके ॥
english_translation: If such a sight could be obtained by asking Brahma, friend, we would keep it in our eyes. Men and women who did not come at this moment did not get to see Siya-Ram.
essence: Some sights are so precious you want to keep them in your eyes forever.
simple_meaning: The speaker says this sight is so precious that, if it could be asked from Brahma, it should be kept in the eyes forever. Anyone who missed this moment missed seeing Sita and Ram.
insight: It teaches you to recognise rare, life-defining moments before they pass.
modern_relevance: You scroll past the invitation, assume there will be another chance, and later hear everyone talk about the one evening you skipped. Some moments do not repeat.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि सुरूपु बूझहिं अकुलाई। अब लगि गए कहाँ लगि भाई॥ समरथ धाइ बिलोकहिं जाई। प्रमुदित फिरहिं जनमफलु पाई ॥
translation: उनके सौंदर्य को सुनकर वे व्याकुल होकर पूछते हैं कि भाई! अब तक वे कहाँ तक गए होंगे? और जो समर्थ हैं, वे दौड़ते हुए जाकर उनके दर्शन कर लेते हैं और जन्म का परम फल पाकर, विशेष आनंदित होकर लौटते हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing of his beauty, they anxiously ask, “Brother, how far has he gone now?” The capable run to see him and return delighted, having found the fruit of life.
essence: Ram’s beauty makes people restless until they reach him.
simple_meaning: People are so moved by Ram’s beauty that they ask where he has gone. The able rush to see him and feel they have gained life’s highest reward.
insight: It shifts attention from passive admiration to active seeking, showing that closeness transforms longing into joy.
modern_relevance: You hear someone mention a person who changed the whole room, and suddenly you need to see for yourself. The ones who make the effort come back lighter, as if they found something they had been missing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अबला बालक बृद्ध जन कर मीजहिं पछिताहिं। होहिं प्रेमबस लोग इमि रामु जहाँ जहँ जाहिं ॥
translation: (गर्भवती, प्रसूता आदि) अबला स्त्रियाँ, बच्चे और बूढ़े (दर्शन न पाने से) हाथ मलते और पछताते हैं। इस प्रकार जहाँ-जहाँ श्री रामचन्द्रजी जाते हैं, वहाँ-वहाँ लोग प्रेम के वश में हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Women, children, and the elderly rub their hands in regret when they miss seeing Ram. Wherever Ram goes, people are overcome by love.
essence: Ram's presence turns regret into love.
simple_meaning: Ram's presence moves everyone, especially the vulnerable. People feel regret if they miss him, because his arrival awakens love in them.
insight: It shifts attention from Ram's actions to the magnetic effect of his presence on ordinary people.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone who changes a room, and suddenly everyone leans in. No speech, no performance — just a presence that makes people feel more alive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गाँव गाँव अस होइ अनंदू। देखि भानुकुल कैरव चंदू॥ जे कछु समाचार सुनि पावहिं। ते नृप रानिहि दोसु लगावहिं ॥
translation: सूर्यकुल रूपी कुमुदिनी को प्रफुल्लित करने वाले चन्द्रमा स्वरूप श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन कर गाँव-गाँव में ऐसा ही आनंद हो रहा है, जो लोग (वनवास दिए जाने का) कुछ भी समाचार सुन पाते हैं, वे राजा-रानी (दशरथ-कैकेयी) को दोष लगाते हैं ॥
english_translation: In village after village there is such joy at seeing Ram, the moon of the solar dynasty. But when people hear even a little of the exile, they blame the king and queen.
essence: Ram's joy is public; his exile becomes everyone's grief.
simple_meaning: Ram's presence brings joy everywhere. But news of his exile makes people blame Dasharath and Kaikeyi.
insight: It shifts attention from celebration to collective grief, showing how public feeling can turn into moral judgment.
modern_relevance: You hear one painful detail about a friend's breakup, and suddenly the whole story feels unfair. People don't stay neutral when someone beloved has been hurt.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहहिं एक अति भल नरनाहू। दीन्ह हमहि जोइ लोचन लाहू॥ कहहिं परसपर लोग लोगाईं। बातें सरल सनेह सुहाईं ॥
translation: कोई एक कहते हैं कि राजा बहुत ही अच्छे हैं, जिन्होंने हमें अपने नेत्रों का लाभ दिया। स्त्री-पुरुष सभी आपस में सीधी, स्नेहभरी सुंदर बातें कह रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Some say, “The king is very noble; he has given us the gift of seeing him.” Men and women speak to one another in simple, loving, delightful words.
essence: Ram’s presence turns strangers into gentle, grateful people.
simple_meaning: People are so happy to see Ram that they praise the king and speak lovingly to one another.
insight: It shows how a steady, respectful presence can transform the tone of everyone around you.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a hard week, and the mood changes before you say a word. People relax, smile, and speak more gently because your presence feels safe.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ते पितु मातु धन्य जिन्ह जाए। धन्य सो नगरु जहाँ तें आए॥ धन्य सो देसु सैलु बन गाऊँ। जहँ-जहँ जाहिं धन्य सोइ ठाऊँ ॥
translation: (कहते हैं-) वे माता-पिता धन्य हैं, जिन्होंने इन्हें जन्म दिया। वह नगर धन्य है, जहाँ से ये आए हैं। वह देश, पर्वत, वन और गाँव धन्य है और वही स्थान धन्य है, जहाँ-जहाँ ये जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Blessed are the parents who gave them birth. Blessed is the city they came from. Blessed is the land, hill, forest, and village. Blessed is every place they visit.
essence: Ram makes every place and every family feel blessed.
simple_meaning: People feel that Ram makes every place and every family blessed just by being there.
insight: It shifts attention from physical location to the moral and emotional quality a person brings into it.
modern_relevance: A friend walks into a tense family gathering and the whole room softens. You realize some people don't just enter a place — they change its atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुखु पायउ बिरंचि रचि तेही। ए जेहि के सब भाँति सनेही॥ राम लखन पथि कथा सुहाई। रही सकल मग कानन छाई ॥
translation: ब्रह्मा ने उसी को रचकर सुख पाया है, जिसके ये (श्री रामचन्द्रजी) सब प्रकार से स्नेही हैं। पथिक रूप श्री राम-लक्ष्मण की सुंदर कथा सारे रास्ते और जंगल में छा गई है ॥
english_translation: Brahma found fulfillment in creating the one whom Ram loves in every way. The sweet story of Ram and Lakshman as travelers spread through the roads and forests.
essence: Ram’s presence turns even exile into something sweet.
simple_meaning: Brahma feels fulfilled only in creating the one whom Ram loves completely. Then Ram and Lakshman’s journey becomes such a beloved story that it spreads everywhere they pass.
insight: It shifts attention from the travelers themselves to the blessing their presence brings to others.
modern_relevance: A quiet walk to a new city, carrying your bag and your worries, can still change the whole mood of the street. Some people leave behind a trail of calm just by being present.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि बिधि रघुकुल कमल रबि मग लोगन्ह सुख देत। जाहिं चले देखत बिपिन सिय सौमित्रि समेत ॥
translation: रघुकुल रूपी कमल को खिलाने वाले सूर्य श्री रामचन्द्रजी इस प्रकार मार्ग के लोगों को सुख देते हुए सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित वन को देखते हुए चले जा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: In this way, Ram, the sun of the Raghu line, gave joy to the people on the road as he walked through the forest with Sita and Saumitra, looking around.
essence: Their presence itself turns hardship into blessing.
simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman move through the forest, and everyone who sees them feels blessed and happy.
insight: It shows how steady conduct can bless others without a speech or display.
modern_relevance: You pass through a hard season, but your calm presence still changes the room. Even while carrying your own burden, you can leave others feeling lighter.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आगें रामु लखनु बने पाछें। तापस बेष बिराजत काछें॥ उभय बीच सिय सोहति कैसें। ब्रह्म जीव बिच माया जैसें ॥
translation: आगे श्री रामजी हैं, पीछे लक्ष्मणजी सुशोभित हैं। तपस्वियों के वेष बनाए दोनों बड़ी ही शोभा पा रहे हैं। दोनों के बीच में सीताजी कैसी सुशोभित हो रही हैं, जैसे ब्रह्म और जीव के बीच में माया! ॥
english_translation: Ram and Lakshman stand ahead, dressed as ascetics behind. How beautifully Sita shines between them, like Maya between Brahman and the individual self.
essence: A forest image turns into a map of reality itself.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman walk in front and behind in ascetic dress, with Sita shining between them like Maya between the supreme reality and the individual self.
insight: It trains the mind to read visible scenes as symbols of deeper reality.
modern_relevance: You see a family walking through an airport after a life-changing move, dressed simply, carrying everything they own. The scene looks ordinary, but it already holds a whole story of loss, role, and hidden meaning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरि कहउँ छबि जसि मन बसई। जनु मधु मदन मध्य रति लसई॥ उपमा बहुरि कहउँ जियँ जोही। जनु बुध बिधु बिच रोहिनि सोही ॥
translation: फिर जैसी छबि मेरे मन में बस रही है, उसको कहता हूँ- मानो वसंत ऋतु और कामदेव के बीच में रति (कामेदव की स्त्री) शोभित हो। फिर अपने हृदय में खोजकर उपमा कहता हूँ कि मानो बुध (चंद्रमा के पुत्र) और चन्द्रमा के बीच में रोहिणी (चन्द्रमा की स्त्री) सोह रही हो ॥
english_translation: Again I describe the beauty as it lives in my mind: like Rati shining between Madhu and Madan. Again I search my heart for a fitting comparison: like Rohini shining between Budh and the moon.
essence: True beauty makes even poetry feel inadequate.
simple_meaning: The speaker keeps searching for the best comparison to describe Sita's beauty, using celestial and poetic images.
insight: It shifts attention from literal description to the limits of language before beauty.
modern_relevance: You try to explain someone you love, and every sentence feels too small. The feeling is real, but language keeps falling short.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु पद रेख बीच बिच सीता। धरति चरन मग चलति सभीता॥ सीय राम पद अंक बराएँ। लखन चलहिं मगु दाहिन लाएँ ॥
translation: प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के (जमीन पर अंकित होने वाले दोनों) चरण चिह्नों के बीच-बीच में पैर रखती हुई सीताजी (कहीं भगवान के चरण चिह्नों पर पैर न टिक जाए इस बात से) डरती हुईं मार्ग में चल रही हैं और लक्ष्मणजी (मर्यादा की रक्षा के लिए) सीताजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी दोनों के चरण चिह्नों को बचाते हुए दाहिने रखकर रास्ता चल रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Sita walks carefully, placing her feet between Rama's footprints, afraid of stepping on his sacred marks. Lakshman walks on the right, guarding the footprints of both Sita and Rama.
essence: Reverence and service can shape even the way you walk.
simple_meaning: Sita walks so carefully that she avoids stepping on Rama's footprints, and Lakshman walks beside them to protect both of them.
insight: It teaches you that devotion and service are shown through careful conduct, not loud declarations.
modern_relevance: You notice someone lowering their voice in a hospital corridor so a sleeping child won't wake. That quiet restraint, that protection of another's peace, is what this scene feels like.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम लखन सिय प्रीति सुहाई। बचन अगोचर किमि कहि जाई॥ खग मृग मगन देखि छबि होहीं। लिए चोरि चित राम बटोहीं ॥
translation: श्री रामजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी की सुंदर प्रीति वाणी का विषय नहीं है (अर्थात अनिर्वचनीय है), अतः वह कैसे कही जा सकती है? पक्षी और पशु भी उस छबि को देखकर (प्रेमानंद में) मग्न हो जाते हैं। पथिक रूप श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने उनके भी चित्त चुरा लिए हैं ॥
english_translation: The lovely affection of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita cannot be put into words. Birds and animals, too, are captivated by their beauty. Ram, the traveler on the road, has stolen even their hearts.
essence: Their love is so radiant that even the world around them is transformed.
simple_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita share a beauty and affection so deep that words cannot capture it. Even birds and animals are moved by seeing them.
insight: It shifts attention from what is said to the power of lived presence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a hard day, and the tension shifts before anyone speaks. Some people carry a quiet beauty that calms everything around them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जिन्ह जिन्ह देखे पथिक प्रिय सिय समेत दोउ भाइ। भव मगु अगमु अनंदु तेइ बिनु श्रम रहे सिराइ ॥
translation: प्यारे पथिक सीताजी सहित दोनों भाइयों को जिन-जिन लोगों ने देखा, उन्होंने भव का अगम मार्ग (जन्म-मृत्यु रूपी संसार में भटकने का भयानक मार्ग) बिना ही परिश्रम आनंद के साथ तय कर लिया (अर्थात वे आवागमन के चक्र से सहज ही छूटकर मुक्त हो गए) ॥
english_translation: Whoever sees Sita and both brothers, the hard road of worldly wandering becomes effortless and joyful for them; they are freed without strain.
essence: Their presence makes even the hardest journey feel effortless.
simple_meaning: Anyone who sees Sita and the two brothers finds the difficult path through worldly life becoming easy and joyful.
insight: It shifts attention from the difficulty of the path to the transforming power of holy company.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a brutal week, and one calm, loving presence steadies you at once. Some people do not solve your life; they make the road bearable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अजहुँ जासु उर सपनेहुँ काऊ। बसहुँ लखनु सिय रामु बटाऊ॥ राम धाम पथ पाइहि सोई। जो पथ पाव कबहु मुनि कोई ॥
translation: आज भी जिसके हृदय में स्वप्न में भी कभी लक्ष्मण, सीता, राम तीनों बटोही आ बसें, तो वह भी श्री रामजी के परमधाम के उस मार्ग को पा जाएगा, जिस मार्ग को कभी कोई बिरले ही मुनि पाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Even now, the one whose heart holds Lakshman, Sita, and Ram, even in a dream, will find Ram's abode — a path that only rare sages ever reach.
essence: Keeping Ram in your heart makes the impossible path reachable.
simple_meaning: Anyone who keeps Ram, Sita, and Lakshman in the heart, even in dreams, can reach Ram's divine abode. Devotion opens a path that even sages rarely find.
insight: It shifts devotion from ritual to remembrance: what lives in the heart becomes the path under your feet.
modern_relevance: You fall asleep replaying the face of someone you love, or the loss you fear, and wake changed. This verse says the heart you keep through the night shapes the road you walk by day.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब रघुबीर श्रमित सिय जानी। देखि निकट बटु सीतल पानी॥ तहँ बसि कंद मूल फल खाई। प्रात नहाइ चले रघुराई ॥
translation: तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी सीताजी को थकी हुई जानकर और समीप ही एक बड़ का वृक्ष और ठंडा पानी देखकर उस दिन वहीं ठहर गए। कन्द, मूल, फल खाकर (रात भर वहाँ रहकर) प्रातःकाल स्नान करके श्री रघुनाथजी आगे चले ॥
english_translation: Then Lord Raghubir, seeing Sita tired and finding a banyan tree and cool water nearby, stayed there. They ate roots, bulbs, and fruit, and at dawn bathed and set out again.
essence: Love notices fatigue and turns it into rest.
simple_meaning: Ram notices Sita is tired, so he stops where there is shade and cool water. They rest, eat simple forest food, bathe in the morning, and continue on their way.
insight: It teaches you to respond to another person's fatigue with immediate, practical care.
modern_relevance: You notice your partner is worn out after a long day, so you skip the plan, find water, sit down, and let the evening become gentler.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखत बन सर सैल सुहाए। बालमीकि आश्रम प्रभु आए॥ राम दीख मुनि बासु सुहावन। सुंदर गिरि काननु जलु पावन ॥
translation: सुंदर वन, तालाब और पर्वत देखते हुए प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी वाल्मीकिजी के आश्रम में आए। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने देखा कि मुनि का निवास स्थान बहुत सुंदर है, जहाँ सुंदर पर्वत, वन और पवित्र जल है ॥
english_translation: Seeing the lovely forests, lakes, and hills, Lord Ram came to Valmiki's hermitage. Ram saw the sage's dwelling as beautiful, with lovely mountains, forests, and pure water.
essence: Beauty itself can prepare the heart for holy company.
simple_meaning: Ram arrives at Valmiki's hermitage and sees its natural beauty — hills, forests, and pure water.
insight: It shifts attention from plot to atmosphere, letting the setting prepare the heart for what follows.
modern_relevance: You step off a noisy road into a quiet garden and your shoulders drop before anyone speaks. Some places steady you just by receiving you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सरनि सरोज बिटप बन फूले। गुंजत मंजु मधुप रस भूले॥ खग मृग बिपुल कोलाहल करहीं। बिरहित बैर मुदित मन चरहीं ॥
translation: सरोवरों में कमल और वनों में वृक्ष फूल रहे हैं और मकरन्द रस में मस्त हुए भौंरे सुंदर गुंजार कर रहे हैं। बहुत से पक्षी और पशु कोलाहल कर रहे हैं और वैर से रहित होकर प्रसन्न मन से विचर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Lotuses bloom in the lakes and trees bloom in the forest. Bees hum sweetly, drunk on nectar. Birds and animals make a lively sound and roam happily, free from hostility.
essence: Peace changes even the forest into a gentle home.
simple_meaning: The forest around Valmiki's hermitage is in full bloom, full of bees, birds, and animals living peacefully together.
insight: It shifts attention from action to atmosphere, showing how harmony is felt in the world around you.
modern_relevance: You step into a quiet park after a long, tense day and notice how even your breathing softens. Some places seem to lower the temperature of the heart before anyone says a word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुचि सुंदर आश्रमु निरखि हरषे राजिवनेन। सुनि रघुबर आगमनु मुनि आगें आयउ लेन ॥
translation: पवित्र और सुंदर आश्रम को देखकर कमल नयन श्री रामचन्द्रजी हर्षित हुए। रघु श्रेष्ठ श्री रामजी का आगमन सुनकर मुनि वाल्मीकिजी उन्हें लेने के लिए आगे आए ॥
english_translation: Seeing the pure, beautiful hermitage, lotus-eyed Ram felt joy. Hearing of Raghubar's arrival, the sage came forward to receive him.
essence: A pure place and a welcoming heart meet Ram with joy.
simple_meaning: Ram reaches Valmiki's hermitage, feels pleased by its purity and beauty, and the sage comes forward to welcome him.
insight: It shifts attention from grand events to the sacred power of hospitality and place.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home that feels calm before anyone says hello. The room itself tells you: you are welcome here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि कहुँ राम दंडवत कीन्हा। आसिरबादु बिप्रबर दीन्हा॥ देखि राम छबि नयन जुड़ाने। करि सनमानु आश्रमहिं आने ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने मुनि को दण्डवत किया। विप्र श्रेष्ठ मुनि ने उन्हें आशीर्वाद दिया। श्री रामचन्द्रजी की छबि देखकर मुनि के नेत्र शीतल हो गए। सम्मानपूर्वक मुनि उन्हें आश्रम में ले आए ॥
english_translation: Ram bowed to the sage. The best of the learned gave him blessings. Seeing Ram's beauty, the sage's eyes softened, and he respectfully led him into the hermitage.
essence: Humility and honour make a holy meeting possible.
simple_meaning: Ram bows to the sage, receives blessings, and is welcomed into the hermitage with honour.
insight: It shows how humility and welcome create sacred relationship before any conversation begins.
modern_relevance: You enter a home carrying grief, and the first thing you do is bow with humility. That simple respect changes the whole room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनिबर अतिथि प्रानप्रिय पाए। कंद मूल फल मधुर मँगाए॥ सिय सौमित्रि राम फल खाए। तब मुनि आश्रम दिए सुहाए ॥
translation: श्रेष्ठ मुनि वाल्मीकिजी ने प्राणप्रिय अतिथियों को पाकर उनके लिए मधुर कंद, मूल और फल मँगवाए। श्री सीताजी, लक्ष्मणजी और रामचन्द्रजी ने फलों को खाया। तब मुनि ने उनको (विश्राम करने के लिए) सुंदर स्थान बतला दिए ॥
english_translation: The great sage welcomed his life-dearest guests, had sweet roots, tubers, and fruits brought, and then showed Ram, Sita, and Lakshman a pleasant place to rest.
essence: Kindness first feeds and shelters before it speaks.
simple_meaning: Valmiki welcomes Ram, Sita, and Lakshman with simple forest food and a place to rest.
insight: It shifts attention from grand gestures to the first practical act of welcome.
modern_relevance: A tired friend shows up at your door after a hard day, and you stop everything to feed them and clear a place to sit. Care often begins with ordinary kindness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बालमीकि मन आनँदु भारी। मंगल मूरति नयन निहारी॥ तब कर कमल जोरि रघुराई। बोले बचन श्रवन सुखदाई ॥
translation: (मुनि श्री रामजी के पास बैठे हैं और उनकी) मंगल मूर्ति को नेत्रों से देखकर वाल्मीकिजी के मन में बड़ा भारी आनंद हो रहा है। तब श्री रघुनाथजी कमलसदृश हाथों को जोड़कर, कानों को सुख देने वाले मधुर वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: Valmiki's heart swelled with joy, seeing the auspicious form before his eyes. Then Raghuvir joined his lotus hands and spoke words that delighted the ear.
essence: Real greatness makes room for humility.
simple_meaning: Valmiki feels deep joy seeing Ram's auspicious presence, and Ram responds with respectful, pleasing words.
insight: It shifts attention from rank to reverence, showing that dignity and humility can meet without conflict.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm presence changes the room, and even the most respected person becomes humble. The exchange feels less like status and more like grace.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तुम्ह त्रिकाल दरसी मुनिनाथा। बिस्व बदर जिमि तुम्हरें हाथा ॥ अस कहि प्रभु सब कथा बखानी। जेहि जेहि भाँति दीन्ह बनु रानी ॥
translation: हे मुनिनाथ! आप त्रिकालदर्शी हैं। सम्पूर्ण विश्व आपके लिए हथेली पर रखे हुए बेर के समान है। प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने ऐसा कहकर फिर जिस-जिस प्रकार से रानी कैकेयी ने वनवास दिया, वह सब कथा विस्तार से सुनाई ॥
english_translation: O lord of sages, you see all three times. The whole world is like a berry held in your hand. Having said this, the Lord then told the whole story of how Queen Kaikeyi gave the exile, in every detail.
essence: True understanding makes even painful history feel fully held.
simple_meaning: Ram praises Valmiki as one who sees all of time, then explains the whole story of Kaikeyi's role in sending him into exile.
insight: It shows that truthful speech lands best in the presence of real understanding.
modern_relevance: You finally tell the full story to someone who already sees past the surface. The relief is not in hiding less, but in being understood without explanation.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तात बचन पुनि मातु हित भाइ भरत अस राउ। मो कहुँ दरस तुम्हार प्रभु सबु मम पुन्य प्रभाउ ॥
translation: (और कहा-) हे प्रभो! पिता की आज्ञा (का पालन), माता का हित और भरत जैसे (स्नेही एवं धर्मात्मा) भाई का राजा होना और फिर मुझे आपके दर्शन होना, यह सब मेरे पुण्यों का प्रभाव है ॥
english_translation: And he said: O Lord, the keeping of my father's word, my mother's welfare, my brother Bharat's rule, and then my having your darshan — all of this is the result of my past merit.
essence: What seems like burden can reveal itself as blessing.
simple_meaning: Ram says that his father's command, his mother's welfare, Bharat's rule, and this meeting with the sages are all signs of his past merit.
insight: It shifts the mind from resentment about interruption to recognition of hidden grace in obligation.
modern_relevance: You miss a promotion, move cities, and end up caring for family in a way you never planned. Later, you realise the detour gave you something cleaner than success: a life that actually fits.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: देखि पाय मुनिराय तुम्हारे। भए सुकृत सब सुफल हमारे॥॥ अब जहँ राउर आयसु होई। मुनि उदबेगु न पावै कोई ॥
translation: हे मुनिराज! आपके चरणों का दर्शन करने से आज हमारे सब पुण्य सफल हो गए (हमें सारे पुण्यों का फल मिल गया)। अब जहाँ आपकी आज्ञा हो और जहाँ कोई भी मुनि उद्वेग को प्राप्त न हो- ॥
english_translation: O sage king, seeing your feet has made all our good deeds fruitful. Now, wherever you command, let no sage feel distress.
essence: Honor becomes complete when power protects peace.
simple_meaning: Seeing the sage's feet brings full blessing, and Ram asks to be commanded in a way that never troubles any sage.
insight: It teaches you to treat authority as responsibility and to measure success by whether others remain untroubled.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who has quietly guided you for years, and the first thing you do is listen instead of perform. Real respect is not loud; it protects the other person's peace.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: मुनि तापस जिन्ह तें दुखु लहहीं। ते नरेस बिनु पावक दहहीं॥ मंगल मूल बिप्र परितोषू। दहइ कोटि कुल भूसुर रोषू ॥
translation: क्योंकि जिनसे मुनि और तपस्वी दुःख पाते हैं, वे राजा बिना अग्नि के ही (अपने दुष्ट कर्मों से ही) जलकर भस्म हो जाते हैं। ब्राह्मणों का संतोष सब मंगलों की जड़ है और भूदेव ब्राह्मणों का क्रोध करोड़ों कुलों को भस्म कर देता है ॥
english_translation: Kings who cause suffering to sages and ascetics burn themselves up without fire. The satisfaction of good Brahmins is the root of all auspiciousness, and the anger of Brahmins can burn millions of families to ash.
essence: Disrespecting the wise turns your own power against you.
simple_meaning: A ruler who harms sages destroys himself. Peace with wise people brings blessing, while provoking them can ruin whole families.
insight: It shifts you from dominance to reverence, showing that how you treat the wise shapes your own safety.
modern_relevance: You snap at the person who has quietly guided you for years, then wonder why support dries up. This verse says power without reverence burns its own house down.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस जियँ जानि कहिअ सोइ ठाऊँ। सिय सौमित्रि सहित जहँ जाऊँ॥ तहँ रचि रुचिर परन तृन साला। बासु करौं कछु काल कृपाला ॥
translation: ऐसा हृदय में समझकर- वह स्थान बतलाइए जहाँ मैं लक्ष्मण और सीता सहित जाऊँ और वहाँ सुंदर पत्तों और घास की कुटी बनाकर, हे दयालु! कुछ समय निवास करूँ ॥
english_translation: Knowing this in my heart, please tell me the place where I may go with Sita and Lakshman. There I will build a lovely hut of leaves and grass and stay there for some time, O compassionate one.
essence: Simplicity can be the highest form of royal dignity.
simple_meaning: Ram asks for a place where he can live with Sita and Lakshman in a simple hut made of leaves and grass.
insight: It shifts you from chasing comfort to choosing the setting that supports your true duties.
modern_relevance: You finally move out of the apartment with the marble lobby and choose the small room near the trees. Less status, less noise, more room to live the life you actually mean.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सहज सरल सुनि रघुबर बानी। साधु साधु बोले मुनि ग्यानी॥ कस न कहहु अस रघुकुलकेतू। तुम्ह पालक संतत श्रुति सेतू ॥
translation: श्री रामजी की सहज ही सरल वाणी सुनकर ज्ञानी मुनि वाल्मीकि बोले- धन्य! धन्य! हे रघुकुल के ध्वजास्वरूप! आप ऐसा क्यों न कहेंगे? आप सदैव वेद की मर्यादा का पालन (रक्षण) करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing Raghubar's simple, सहज words, the wise sage said, 'Well said! Well said! Why would you not say this, O banner of the Raghu line? You always uphold the boundary of the sacred tradition.'
essence: True greatness speaks simply and protects dharma without strain.
simple_meaning: Valmiki praises Ram's humble, straightforward speech and recognizes that Ram always protects the sacred order of conduct.
insight: It shifts respect away from display and toward steady conduct that preserves order.
modern_relevance: A leader answers a difficult question without posturing, and everyone in the room feels the difference. Real authority does not need to sound impressive; it protects what matters by speaking simply and acting rightly.
speaker: Valmiki

verse_text: श्रुति सेतु पालक राम तुम्ह जगदीस माया जानकी। जो सृजति जगु पालति हरति रुख पाइ कृपानिधान की॥ जो सहससीसु अहीसु महिधरु लखनु सचराचर धनी। सुर काज धरि नरराज तनु चले दलन खल निसिचर अनी॥
translation: हे राम! आप वेद की मर्यादा के रक्षक जगदीश्वर हैं और जानकीजी (आपकी स्वरूप भूता) माया हैं, जो कृपा के भंडार आपका रुख पाकर जगत का सृजन, पालन और संहार करती हैं। जो हजार मस्तक वाले सर्पों के स्वामी और पृथ्वी को अपने सिर पर धारण करने वाले हैं, वही चराचर के स्वामी शेषजी लक्ष्मण हैं। देवताओं के कार्य के लिए आप राजा का शरीर धारण करके दुष्ट राक्षसों की सेना का नाश करने के लिए चले हैं।
english_translation: O Ram, protector of the bridge of the Vedas and lord of the world, Janaki is your own power. By your grace, she creates, sustains, and withdraws the world. The thousand-headed serpent lord, bearer of the earth, is Lakshman, lord of all moving and unmoving beings. For the gods' work, you have taken a king's body and gone to destroy the armies of evil beings.
essence: The highest power can move through a human form without losing its sovereignty.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the lord of the world, with Janaki as his power and Lakshman as the great serpent-bearing supporter. He has taken human form to protect dharma and destroy evil forces.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as only a prince to seeing his human life as divine action in the world.
modern_relevance: You look ordinary to everyone at work, but your quiet role may be carrying a much larger purpose than anyone sees.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: राम सरूप तुम्हार बचन अगोचर बुद्धिपर। अबिगत अकथ अपार नेति नेति नित निगम कह।126॥
translation: हे राम! आपका स्वरूप वाणी के अगोचर, बुद्धि से परे, अव्यक्त, अकथनीय और अपार है। वेद निरंतर उसका 'नेति-नेति' कहकर वर्णन करते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Ram, your true form is beyond speech and beyond the discerning mind. It is unmanifest, indescribable, boundless; the Vedas continually point to it by saying, 'not this, not this.'
essence: The deepest reality is known by what words cannot hold.
simple_meaning: Ram's true nature cannot be fully described by words or grasped by the mind. The Vedas approach it only by saying what it is not.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to define the highest reality to recognising its limits and bowing in humility.
modern_relevance: You try to explain someone you love to a friend, and every sentence feels too small. Some things are not reduced by being unnamed; they are honoured.
speaker: Valmiki

verse_text: जगु पेखन तुम्ह देखनिहारे। बिधि हरि संभु नचावनिहारे॥ तेउ न जानहिं मरमु तुम्हारा। औरु तुम्हहि को जाननिहारा ॥
translation: हे राम! जगत दृश्य है, आप उसके देखने वाले हैं। आप ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और शंकर को भी नचाने वाले हैं। जब वे भी आपके मर्म को नहीं जानते, तब और कौन आपको जानने वाला है? ॥
english_translation: O Ram, the world is what is seen, and you are the Seer. You make Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva dance. Even they do not know your mystery, so who else could know you?
essence: The deepest reality is the Seer, not the seen.
simple_meaning: Ram is beyond the world of appearances. He is the one who sees everything, while even the highest beings cannot fully understand him.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to master the whole picture to bowing before what exceeds understanding.
modern_relevance: You can spend years trying to explain everything, then watch a crisis expose how little you control. This verse reminds you that the deepest reality is larger than your explanations.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सोइ जानइ जेहि देहु जनाई। जानत तुम्हहि तुम्हइ होइ जाई॥ तुम्हरिहि कृपाँ तुम्हहि रघुनंदन। जानहिं भगत भगत उर चंदन ॥
translation: वही आपको जानता है, जिसे आप जना देते हैं और जानते ही वह आपका ही स्वरूप बन जाता है। हे रघुनंदन! हे भक्तों के हृदय को शीतल करने वाले चंदन! आपकी ही कृपा से भक्त आपको जान पाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Only the one whom you reveal can know you; and in knowing you, that one becomes like you. By your grace alone, O Raghu's delight, devotees know you, sandalwood cooling the hearts of devotees.
essence: Knowing Ram is itself a gift from Ram.
simple_meaning: No one can know Ram by personal effort alone. Only the grace that reveals him makes real understanding possible, and that understanding changes the devotee from within.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-made understanding to received revelation.
modern_relevance: You can read every book, sit in every retreat, and still feel shut out. Then one quiet moment lands, and something opens that effort never could. That is how grace feels.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: चिदानंदमय देह तुम्हारी। बिगत बिकार जान अधिकारी॥ नर तनु धरेहु संत सुर काजा। कहहु करहु जस प्राकृत राजा ॥
translation: आपकी देह चिदानन्दमय है (यह प्रकृतिजन्य पंच महाभूतों की बनी हुई कर्म बंधनयुक्त, त्रिदेह विशिष्ट मायिक नहीं है) और (उत्पत्ति-नाश, वृद्धि-क्षय आदि) सब विकारों से रहित है, इस रहस्य को अधिकारी पुरुष ही जानते हैं। आपने देवता और संतों के कार्य के लिए (दिव्य) नर शरीर धारण किया है और प्राकृत (प्रकृति के तत्वों से निर्मित देह वाले, साधारण) राजाओं की तरह से कहते और करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Your body is made of consciousness and bliss, free from all change. Only the qualified know this mystery. You have taken a human form for the work of saints and radiant beings, yet you speak and act like an ordinary king.
essence: Ram's human form hides a nature untouched by change.
simple_meaning: Ram's true nature is beyond ordinary physical change, and only those fit to understand can see it. He has taken a human form to serve saints and radiant beings, while outwardly living like a king.
insight: It shifts attention from outward form to inward essence, and from surface judgment to deeper recognition.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems quiet, even plain, and only later realise their presence has been holding everything together. This verse reminds you that the deepest reality is often hidden behind the most ordinary surface.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: राम देखि सुनि चरित तुम्हारे। जड़ मोहहिं बुध होहिं सुखारे॥ तुम्ह जो कहहु करहु सबु साँचा। जस काछिअ तस चाहिअ नाचा ॥
translation: हे राम! आपके चरित्रों को देख और सुनकर मूर्ख लोग तो मोह को प्राप्त होते हैं और ज्ञानीजन सुखी होते हैं। आप जो कुछ कहते, करते हैं, वह सब सत्य (उचित) ही है, क्योंकि जैसा स्वाँग भरे वैसा ही नाचना भी तो चाहिए (इस समय आप मनुष्य रूप में हैं, अतः मनुष्योचित व्यवहार करना ठीक ही है।) ॥
english_translation: O Ram, seeing and hearing your deeds, the foolish fall into delusion, while the wise become joyful. Whatever you say and do is true and right, because when you have taken a human form, you should behave like a human being.
essence: True greatness can look ordinary when it wears a human form.
simple_meaning: Ram's actions can bewilder shallow minds, but they bring joy to the wise. Whatever he does is right, because he is choosing to live as a human being.
insight: It shifts you from judging by appearances to trusting conduct that fits the role and the moment.
modern_relevance: A parent looks ordinary while making a hard decision that children won't understand yet. A wise friend doesn't need the choice to look dramatic to know it is right.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: पूँछेहु मोहि कि रहौं कहँ मैं पूँछत सकुचाउँ। जहँ न होहु तहँ देहु कहि तुम्हहि देखावौं ठाउँ ॥
translation: आपने मुझसे पूछा कि मैं कहाँ रहूँ? परन्तु मैं यह पूछते सकुचाता हूँ कि जहाँ आप न हों, वह स्थान बता दीजिए। तब मैं आपके रहने के लिए स्थान दिखाऊँ ॥
english_translation: You asked me where I should stay. But I hesitate to ask where you are not. Tell me that place, and I will show you where to stay.
essence: Separation from the beloved is the only place that feels unfit.
simple_meaning: Ram answers with humility and devotion: he does not want a place that is separate from the one he loves. Home is wherever that presence is found.
insight: It shifts belonging from geography to relationship, teaching you to see presence as the real shelter.
modern_relevance: You move into a new city, but the room feels empty until someone you love walks in. Suddenly the address matters less than the presence inside it.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनि मुनि बचन प्रेम रस साने। सकुचि राम मन महुँ मुसुकाने॥ बालमीकि हँसि कहहिं बहोरी। बानी मधुर अमिअ रस बोरी ॥
translation: मुनि के प्रेमरस से सने हुए वचन सुनकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी रहस्य खुल जाने के डर से सकुचाकर मन में मुस्कुराए। वाल्मीकिजी हँसकर फिर अमृत रस में डुबोई हुई मीठी वाणी बोले- ॥
english_translation: Hearing the sage's words, steeped in the nectar of love, Ram smiled inwardly, shy and amused. Then Valmiki laughed and spoke again in sweet words soaked with nectar.
essence: True affection can make reverence feel shy and sweet.
simple_meaning: Ram hears Valmiki's loving words and smiles shyly. Valmiki then speaks again with even sweeter, nectar-like speech.
insight: It highlights the tenderness that appears when reverence and affection meet.
modern_relevance: Someone praises you too warmly after you help them, and you look down with that small embarrassed smile. You know the kindness is real, and it lands deeper than flattery.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनहु राम अब कहउँ निकेता। जहाँ बसहु सिय लखन समेता॥ जिन्ह के श्रवन समुद्र समाना। कथा तुम्हारि सुभग सरि नाना ॥
translation: हे रामजी! सुनिए, अब मैं वे स्थान बताता हूँ, जहाँ आप, सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी समेत निवास कीजिए। जिनके कान समुद्र की भाँति आपकी सुंदर कथा रूपी अनेक सुंदर नदियों से- ॥
english_translation: Listen, Ram, I now tell you the dwelling place where you, Sita, and Lakshman may live. Those whose ears are like the ocean receive many lovely streams of your beautiful story.
essence: A heart that loves your story becomes your true home.
simple_meaning: Valmiki says Ram, Sita, and Lakshman should live in hearts that eagerly receive Ram's beautiful story.
insight: It shifts devotion from external space to inner receptivity.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose eyes light up when you speak, and the whole room softens. That kind of welcome is rarer than a guest room — and far more real.
speaker: Valmiki

verse_text: भरहिं निरंतर होहिं न पूरे। तिन्ह के हिय तुम्ह कहुँ गुह रूरे॥ लोचन चातक जिन्ह करि राखे। रहहिं दरस जलधर अभिलाषे ॥
translation: निरंतर भरते रहते हैं, परन्तु कभी पूरे (तृप्त) नहीं होते, उनके हृदय आपके लिए सुंदर घर हैं और जिन्होंने अपने नेत्रों को चातक बना रखा है, जो आपके दर्शन रूपी मेघ के लिए सदा लालायित रहते हैं, ॥
english_translation: They are never full; their hearts are the lovely home where you dwell. They have made their eyes like the chatak bird, always longing for the rain-cloud of your sight.
essence: A heart that never feels full becomes Ram's true home.
simple_meaning: Real devotion never feels complete without Ram. The heart becomes his home, and the eyes keep waiting for his sight.
insight: It shifts devotion from possession to longing, showing that desire for the divine can itself purify the heart.
modern_relevance: You scroll past another beautiful thing, but nothing quite lands. That restless ache may be telling you your heart is still made for something deeper than passing satisfaction.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: निदरहिं सरित सिंधु सर भारी। रूप बिंदु जल होहिं सुखारी॥ तिन्ह कें हृदय सदन सुखदायक। बसहु बंधु सिय सह रघुनायक ॥
translation: तथा जो भारी-भारी नदियों, समुद्रों और झीलों का निरादर करते हैं और आपके सौंदर्य (रूपी मेघ) की एक बूँद जल से सुखी हो जाते हैं (अर्थात आपके दिव्य सच्चिदानन्दमय स्वरूप के किसी एक अंग की जरा सी भी झाँकी के सामने स्थूल, सूक्ष्म और कारण तीनों जगत के अर्थात पृथ्वी, स्वर्ग और ब्रह्मलोक तक के सौंदर्य का तिरस्कार करते हैं), हे रघुनाथजी! उन लोगों के हृदय रूपी सुखदायी भवनों में आप भाई लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सहित निवास कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Those who turn away from great rivers, oceans, and lakes and are satisfied by a single drop of your beauty—Lord of Raghu, dwell in their heart-homes of joy with Lakshman and Sita.
essence: A single glimpse of Ram makes all lesser beauty fade.
simple_meaning: Worldly beauty loses its power beside even a tiny glimpse of Ram's divine form. Such a heart becomes fit for Ram, Sita, and Lakshman to dwell in.
insight: It shifts desire from collecting more experiences to recognizing what is truly nourishing.
modern_relevance: You scroll past a hundred polished images, then one face, one song, one moment of grace stops you cold. After that, everything else feels thinner. This verse names that reversal of taste.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जसु तुम्हार मानस बिमल हंसिनि जीहा जासु। मुकताहल गुन गन चुनइ राम बसहु हियँ तासु ॥
translation: आपके यश रूपी निर्मल मानसरोवर में जिसकी जीभ हंसिनी बनी हुई आपके गुण समूह रूपी मोतियों को चुगती रहती है, हे रामजी! आप उसके हृदय में बसिए ॥
english_translation: In your pure lake of fame, let the tongue become a swan that keeps picking up the pearls of your qualities. O Ram, dwell in that heart.
essence: A heart that praises Ram becomes His dwelling place.
simple_meaning: A heart filled with loving praise for Ram becomes a home for Ram himself. The tongue should keep gathering his qualities like a swan picking pearls.
insight: It shifts attention from criticism to devoted remembrance, training the mind to dwell on what it loves.
modern_relevance: You keep replaying someone's flaws in your head after the argument. This verse turns the habit around: what you repeatedly honor and speak of begins to shape the home inside you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: प्रभु प्रसाद सुचि सुभग सुबासा। सादर जासु लहइ नित नासा॥ तुम्हहि निबेदित भोजन करहीं। प्रभु प्रसाद पट भूषन धरहीं ॥
translation: जिसकी नासिका प्रभु (आप) के पवित्र और सुगंधित (पुष्पादि) सुंदर प्रसाद को नित्य आदर के साथ ग्रहण करती (सूँघती) है और जो आपको अर्पण करके भोजन करते हैं और आपके प्रसाद रूप ही वस्त्राभूषण धारण करते हैं, ॥
english_translation: Those who respectfully inhale the sacred, fragrant offerings of the Lord, eat only food offered to You, and wear garments and ornaments received as Your grace.
essence: Devotion turns ordinary receiving into worship.
simple_meaning: A devoted person treats even food, fragrance, clothes, and ornaments as offerings received with reverence, not as possessions to boast about.
insight: It shifts you from possession to reverence, so daily habits become acts of remembrance.
modern_relevance: You sit down to dinner after a long day and pause before the first bite. The meal, the clothes you wear, even the small comforts around you can become reminders that life is received, not owned.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सीस नवहिं सुर गुरु द्विज देखी। प्रीति सहित करि बिनय बिसेषी॥ कर नित करहिं राम पद पूजा। राम भरोस हृदयँ नहिं दूजा ॥
translation: जिनके मस्तक देवता, गुरु और ब्राह्मणों को देखकर बड़ी नम्रता के साथ प्रेम सहित झुक जाते हैं, जिनके हाथ नित्य श्री रामचन्द्रजी (आप) के चरणों की पूजा करते हैं और जिनके हृदय में श्री रामचन्द्रजी (आप) का ही भरोसा है, दूसरा नहीं, ॥
english_translation: Those whose heads bow in loving reverence when they see the radiant beings, the teacher, and the learned; whose hands daily worship Ram's feet; and whose hearts hold no support except Ram.
essence: Real devotion bows, serves, and trusts without a second refuge.
simple_meaning: True devotion shows itself in humility, daily worship, and a heart that relies on Ram alone.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to dependence: respect outwardly, worship consistently, and let Ram become your only inner support.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is measuring status, and you quietly respect the people who deserve it, do your practice, and stop chasing approval. That steady center is what this verse honors.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: चरन राम तीरथ चलि जाहीं। राम बसहु तिन्ह के मन माहीं॥ मंत्रराजु नित जपहिं तुम्हारा। पूजहिं तुम्हहि सहित परिवारा ॥
translation: तथा जिनके चरण श्री रामचन्द्रजी (आप) के तीर्थों में चलकर जाते हैं, हे रामजी! आप उनके मन में निवास कीजिए। जो नित्य आपके (राम नाम रूप) मंत्रराज को जपते हैं और परिवार (परिकर) सहित आपकी पूजा करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Their feet go on pilgrimage to Ram's holy places. Ram lives in their hearts. They chant your king of mantras daily and worship you with their whole family.
essence: Repeated devotion invites Ram to stay in the heart.
simple_meaning: People who go to Ram's holy places, repeat his name, and worship him with their families are asking Ram to live in their hearts.
insight: It shifts worship from outward performance to inward companionship with Ram.
modern_relevance: You light a lamp before leaving for work, then whisper a name under your breath on the train. The ritual is small, but it changes the room inside you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तरपन होम करहिं बिधि नाना। बिप्र जेवाँइ देहिं बहु दाना॥ तुम्ह तें अधिक गुरहि जियँ जानी। सकल भायँ सेवहिं सनमानी ॥
translation: जो अनेक प्रकार से तर्पण और हवन करते हैं तथा ब्राह्मणों को भोजन कराकर बहुत दान देते हैं तथा जो गुरु को हृदय में आपसे भी अधिक (बड़ा) जानकर सर्वभाव से सम्मान करके उनकी सेवा करते हैं, ॥
english_translation: They perform many kinds of offerings and fire rituals, feed learned guests, give much charity, and serve the teacher with full respect, holding the teacher in their heart as greater even than you.
essence: Ritual matters less than the humility that makes service sincere.
simple_meaning: They honor the sacred through ritual, charity, and service, but the deepest devotion is their reverence for the teacher and for Ram.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to lived reverence, with service as the proof.
modern_relevance: You donate, volunteer, and keep every tradition carefully, but the real test is whether humility shows up in how you treat the person who teaches you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सबु करि मागहिं एक फलु राम चरन रति होउ। तिन्ह कें मन मंदिर बसहु सिय रघुनंदन दोउ ॥
translation: और ये सब कर्म करके सबका एक मात्र यही फल माँगते हैं कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में हमारी प्रीति हो, उन लोगों के मन रूपी मंदिरों में सीताजी और रघुकुल को आनंदित करने वाले आप दोनों बसिए ॥
english_translation: After doing all this, they ask for only one fruit: love for Ram's feet. May both Sita and Ram live in the temple of their minds.
essence: All practice is fulfilled by love for Ram alone.
simple_meaning: After every ritual and act of devotion, the only true request is love for Ram. When that love comes, Ram and Sita live in the heart.
insight: It shifts devotion from performing acts to asking for inner nearness and lasting love.
modern_relevance: You finish a long prayer, a charity drive, or a family ritual and still feel empty unless love has actually deepened. This verse says the real result is not applause, but closeness.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: काम कोह मद मान न मोहा। लोभ न छोभ न राग न द्रोहा॥ जिन्ह कें कपट दंभ नहिं माया। तिन्ह कें हृदय बसहु रघुराया ॥
translation: जिनके न तो काम, क्रोध, मद, अभिमान और मोह हैं, न लोभ है, न क्षोभ है, न राग है, न द्वेष है और न कपट, दम्भ और माया ही है- हे रघुराज! आप उनके हृदय में निवास कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Free from desire, anger, pride, delusion, greed, agitation, attachment, hatred, deceit, hypocrisy, and illusion—O Lord of Raghu, dwell in such hearts.
essence: A heart without ego becomes Ram's home.
simple_meaning: A heart emptied of craving, anger, pride, greed, attachment, hatred, deceit, and illusion becomes fit for Ram to live in.
insight: It shifts devotion from outer performance to inner readiness.
modern_relevance: You can do all the right rituals, post the right words, and still feel crowded inside. The real preparation is simpler and harder: clear out the noise that keeps love from staying.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सब के प्रिय सब के हितकारी। दुख सुख सरिस प्रसंसा गारी॥ कहहिं सत्य प्रिय बचन बिचारी। जागत सोवत सरन तुम्हारी ॥
translation: जो सबके प्रिय और सबका हित करने वाले हैं, जिन्हें दुःख और सुख तथा प्रशंसा (बड़ाई) और गाली (निंदा) समान है, जो विचारकर सत्य और प्रिय वचन बोलते हैं तथा जो जागते-सोते आपकी ही शरण हैं, ॥
english_translation: They are dear to everyone and helpful to everyone. Pleasure and pain, praise and blame are the same to them. They speak truth after reflection, with words that are pleasing. Awake or asleep, they remain in your refuge.
essence: Devotion makes you steady, kind, and free from the crowd's verdict.
simple_meaning: Ram stays with those who are kind to everyone, steady in praise or blame, truthful in speech, and always surrendered to him.
insight: It trains you to become consistent: kind, truthful, and unshaken by public approval or rejection.
modern_relevance: You get praised in the meeting, then mocked in the group chat. The verse asks whether your character changes with either one, or stays steady anyway.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तुम्हहि छाड़ि गति दूसरि नाहीं। राम बसहु तिन्ह के मन माहीं॥ जननी सम जानहिं परनारी। धनु पराव बिष तें बिष भारी ॥
translation: और आपको छोड़कर जिनके दूसरे कोई गति (आश्रय) नहीं है, हे रामजी! आप उनके मन में बसिए। जो पराई स्त्री को जन्म देने वाली माता के समान जानते हैं और पराया धन जिन्हें विष से भी भारी विष है, ॥
english_translation: Besides you, they have no other refuge. O Ram, dwell in the hearts of those who see another man's wife as their mother and another man's wealth as poison heavier than poison.
essence: Ram enters the heart that has stopped chasing poison.
simple_meaning: People who have no refuge except Ram, and who treat another man's wife like a mother and another man's wealth like poison, become fit for Ram's presence.
insight: It shifts the focus from spiritual display to inner restraint, showing that Ram dwells where desire and greed have been refused.
modern_relevance: You scroll past what you know will stir desire, then close the app before it drags you further. That small refusal is the kind of inner cleanliness this verse honors.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जे हरषहिं पर संपति देखी। दुखित होहिं पर बिपति बिसेषी॥ जिन्हहि राम तुम्ह प्रान पिआरे। तिन्ह के मन सुभ सदन तुम्हारे ॥
translation: जो दूसरे की सम्पत्ति देखकर हर्षित होते हैं और दूसरे की विपत्ति देखकर विशेष रूप से दुःखी होते हैं और हे रामजी! जिन्हें आप प्राणों के समान प्यारे हैं, उनके मन आपके रहने योग्य शुभ भवन हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who rejoice at another's good fortune and feel deep sorrow at another's hardship, and those for whom you are dear as life itself, their hearts are a blessed home for you, O Ram.
essence: Empathy makes the heart fit for Ram.
simple_meaning: A heart that rejoices in others' happiness and grieves in others' pain becomes fit for Ram to dwell in.
insight: It shifts attention from self-centered feeling to shared emotional life, where devotion becomes possible.
modern_relevance: You hear good news about a colleague who got the promotion you wanted, and instead of bitterness, something in you softens. That quiet generosity is the kind of space this verse points to.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: स्वामि सखा पितु मातु गुर जिन्ह के सब तुम्ह तात। मन मंदिर तिन्ह कें बसहु सीय सहित दोउ भ्रात ॥
translation: हे तात! जिनके स्वामी, सखा, पिता, माता और गुरु सब कुछ आप ही हैं, उनके मन रूपी मंदिर में सीता सहित आप दोनों भाई निवास कीजिए ॥
english_translation: O dear one, for those whose only lord, friend, father, mother, and teacher are you, dwell in their mind-temple, along with Sita and your two brothers.
essence: Whoever makes Ram their everything is already home.
simple_meaning: People who already hold Ram as their father, mother, teacher, friend, and lord are asked to keep him and Sita in their hearts.
insight: It shifts devotion from occasional prayer to making the heart a living home for Ram.
modern_relevance: After a hard day, you call the one person who steadies you, then realize you want more than comfort — you want your whole life to have that same center.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अवगुन तजि सब के गुन गहहीं। बिप्र धेनु हित संकट सहहीं॥ नीति निपुन जिन्ह कइ जग लीका। घर तुम्हार तिन्ह कर मनु नीका ॥
translation: जो अवगुणों को छोड़कर सबके गुणों को ग्रहण करते हैं, ब्राह्मण और गो के लिए संकट सहते हैं, नीति-निपुणता में जिनकी जगत में मर्यादा है, उनका सुंदर मन आपका घर है ॥
english_translation: Those who drop faults and gather everyone's good qualities, who endure hardship for the sake of priests and cows, and whose conduct is known everywhere for wise justice—your home is a beautiful mind.
essence: A heart that protects others becomes Ram's true home.
simple_meaning: Ram's home belongs to people who notice goodness in others, endure hardship for the vulnerable, and live with wise fairness.
insight: It shifts devotion from ritual to character: become the kind of person whose mind can shelter the divine.
modern_relevance: You stay late to defend a coworker who was treated unfairly, even though it costs you. That kind of heart is not just decent — it is spacious enough to hold Ram.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: गुन तुम्हार समुझइ निज दोसा। जेहि सब भाँति तुम्हार भरोसा॥ राम भगत प्रिय लागहिं जेही। तेहि उर बसहु सहित बैदेही ॥
translation: जो गुणों को आपका और दोषों को अपना समझता है, जिसे सब प्रकार से आपका ही भरोसा है और राम भक्त जिसे प्यारे लगते हैं, उसके हृदय में आप सीता सहित निवास कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Those who see your virtues as yours and their faults as their own, who trust you in every way, and who find Ram's devotees dear—may you dwell in their heart with Sita.
essence: Humility, trust, and love for devotees make the heart fit for Ram.
simple_meaning: The heart that stays humble, trusts Ram completely, and loves Ram's devotees becomes a fitting home for Ram and Sita.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to receptivity: humility, trust, and love for fellow devotees prepare the heart to receive grace.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose kindness feels effortless, and you wonder why their presence feels so safe. It is because they do not keep score, trust deeply, and welcome the people you love.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जाति पाँति धनु धरमु बड़ाई। प्रिय परिवार सदन सुखदाई॥ सब तजि तुम्हहि रहइ उर लाई। तेहि के हृदयँ रहहु रघुराई ॥
translation: जाति, पाँति, धन, धर्म, बड़ाई, प्यारा परिवार और सुख देने वाला घर, सबको छोड़कर जो केवल आपको ही हृदय में धारण किए रहता है, हे रघुनाथजी! आप उसके हृदय में रहिए ॥
english_translation: Leaving caste, status, wealth, duty, honor, dear family, and a comfortable home, the one who keeps only you in the heart — O Raghunath, stay in that person's heart.
essence: When Ram is all you keep, your heart becomes his home.
simple_meaning: Real devotion means letting go of status, wealth, family comfort, and social pride, and keeping Ram alone in the heart.
insight: It shifts attention from social identity and possessions toward single-pointed devotion.
modern_relevance: You step out of a family dinner where everyone is measuring success, reputation, and who has done better. Somewhere beneath all that noise, you know what you actually want to keep.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सरगु नरकु अपबरगु समाना। जहँ तहँ देख धरें धनु बाना॥ करम बचन मन राउर चेरा। राम करहु तेहि कें उर डेरा ॥
translation: स्वर्ग, नरक और मोक्ष जिसकी दृष्टि में समान हैं, क्योंकि वह जहाँ-तहाँ (सब जगह) केवल धनुष-बाण धारण किए आपको ही देखता है और जो कर्म से, वचन से और मन से आपका दास है, हे रामजी! आप उसके हृदय में डेरा कीजिए ॥
english_translation: He sees heaven, hell, and liberation as the same, because everywhere he looks he sees you holding bow and arrows. One who serves you in deed, word, and mind — Ram, please make that heart your home.
essence: A heart fully given to Ram no longer chases reward.
simple_meaning: A devoted heart sees Ram everywhere and no longer treats heaven, hell, and liberation as separate rewards. Such a person serves Ram through action, speech, and thought.
insight: It shifts devotion from ritual to total alignment: your actions, words, and thoughts all become one offering.
modern_relevance: You’re walking through a crowded station after a hard day, but one call from someone you love changes everything. The world is still noisy, yet your attention has found its true home.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जाहि न चाहिअ कबहुँ कछु तुम्ह सन सहज सनेहु। बसहु निरंतर तासु मन सो राउर निज गेहु ॥
translation: जिसको कभी कुछ भी नहीं चाहिए और जिसका आपसे स्वाभाविक प्रेम है, आप उसके मन में निरंतर निवास कीजिए, वह आपका अपना घर है ॥
english_translation: Let the one who never wants anything from you and loves you naturally live forever in your mind; that heart is your true home.
essence: The heart that asks for nothing becomes the divine's home.
simple_meaning: A person who asks nothing from Ram and loves Him naturally becomes Ram's own home. Pure love, not demand, makes the heart fit for Him.
insight: It shifts devotion from transaction to belonging, showing that asking less makes room for presence.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after helping someone, hoping for a thank-you that never comes. This verse turns that ache around: the deepest bond is the one that needs nothing back.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: एहि बिधि मुनिबर भवन देखाए। बचन सप्रेम राम मन भाए॥ कह मुनि सुनहु भानुकुलनायक। आश्रम कहउँ समय सुखदायक ॥
translation: इस प्रकार मुनि श्रेष्ठ वाल्मीकिजी ने श्री रामचन्द्रजी को घर दिखाए। उनके प्रेमपूर्ण वचन श्री रामजी के मन को अच्छे लगे। फिर मुनि ने कहा- हे सूर्यकुल के स्वामी! सुनिए, अब मैं इस समय के लिए सुखदायक आश्रम कहता हूँ (निवास स्थान बतलाता हूँ) ॥
english_translation: In this way the sage showed Ram the dwelling. His loving words pleased Ram's mind. Then the sage said, “Listen, O lord of the solar race. I will now tell you of a resting place that is pleasant for this time.”
essence: A loving guide turns even a simple shelter into comfort.
simple_meaning: The sage shows Ram a place to stay, and Ram is pleased by the loving way he speaks. Then the sage offers to point out a suitable hermitage nearby.
insight: It shifts attention from a destination to the kindness that makes refuge possible.
modern_relevance: A friend walks you through a new neighborhood after a hard move, pointing out where you could settle. Before the address matters, the care in the guidance already eases your heart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चित्रकूट गिरि करहु निवासू। तहँ तुम्हार सब भाँति सुपासू॥ सैलु सुहावन कानन चारू। करि केहरि मृग बिहग बिहारू ॥
translation: आप चित्रकूट पर्वत पर निवास कीजिए, वहाँ आपके लिए सब प्रकार की सुविधा है। सुहावना पर्वत है और सुंदर वन है। वह हाथी, सिंह, हिरन और पक्षियों का विहार स्थल है ॥
english_translation: Stay on Mount Chitrakoot. There, everything will be comfortable for you. It is a lovely mountain and a beautiful forest, where elephants, lions, deer, and birds roam.
essence: A place of exile can still become a place of rest.
simple_meaning: The sage is inviting Ram to live in Chitrakoot, describing it as a beautiful, comfortable place filled with wildlife.
insight: It shifts attention from loss to the possibility of dignified living in exile.
