modern_relevance: A friend points you toward a quiet hill town after your life has become too loud. They are not offering luxury — only a place where your mind can finally unclench.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नदी पुनीत पुरान बखानी। अत्रिप्रिया निज तप बल आनी॥ सुरसरि धार नाउँ मंदाकिनि। जो सब पातक पोतक डाकिनि ॥
translation: वहाँ पवित्र नदी है, जिसकी पुराणों ने प्रशंसा की है और जिसको अत्रि ऋषि की पत्नी अनसुयाजी अपने तपोबल से लाई थीं। वह गंगाजी की धारा है, उसका मंदाकिनी नाम है। वह सब पाप रूपी बालकों को खा डालने के लिए डाकिनी (डायन) रूप है ॥
english_translation: There is a pure river praised in the ancient texts, brought here by Anusuya through the power of her austerity. It is the stream of the celestial river, called Mandakini, and it devours all sins like a witch devours children.
essence: A sacred place holds the power of the discipline that sanctified it.
simple_meaning: The place has a holy river called Mandakini, brought by Anusuya's austerity. It is described as so pure that it destroys all sins.
insight: It shifts attention from scenery alone to the spiritual charge a place can carry through devotion and discipline.
modern_relevance: You step into a quiet riverside after a long, ugly week, and something in you loosens. Some places feel charged with calm because people have lived their discipline there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अत्रि आदि मुनिबर बहु बसहीं। करहिं जोग जप तप तन कसहीं॥ चलहु सफल श्रम सब कर करहू। राम देहु गौरव गिरिबरहू ॥
translation: अत्रि आदि बहुत से श्रेष्ठ मुनि वहाँ निवास करते हैं, जो योग, जप और तप करते हुए शरीर को कसते हैं। हे रामजी! चलिए, सबके परिश्रम को सफल कीजिए और पर्वत श्रेष्ठ चित्रकूट को भी गौरव दीजिए ॥
english_translation: Many great sages, beginning with Atri, live there, practicing yoga, chanting, and austerity, and strengthening their bodies. O Ram, come and make all this effort fruitful; bring honor to the best of mountains, Chitrakoot.
essence: Effort becomes complete only when Ram arrives.
simple_meaning: Chitrakoot is a sacred place where many sages live in discipline. The verse asks Ram to come there so their efforts become fruitful and the mountain receives honor.
insight: It shifts attention from scenery and effort to the presence that gives them meaning.
modern_relevance: You clean the room, prepare the meal, and wait for someone who matters deeply. Their arrival makes all the effort feel complete.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चित्रकूट महिमा अमित कही महामुनि गाइ। आइ नहाए सरित बर सिय समेत दोउ भाइ ॥
translation: महामुनि वाल्मीकिजी ने चित्रकूट की अपरिमित महिमा बखान कर कही। तब सीताजी सहित दोनों भाइयों ने आकर श्रेष्ठ नदी मंदाकिनी में स्नान किया ॥
english_translation: The great sage has sung the limitless glory of Chitrakoot. Then Sita and both brothers came and bathed in the best river, Mandakini.
essence: A holy place becomes real when Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana enter it.
simple_meaning: Valmiki praises Chitrakoot, and then Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana bathe in the Mandakini river.
insight: It shifts attention from the praise of a place to the lived arrival that makes the praise real.
modern_relevance: You finally reach the place everyone described so beautifully — a hill town, a riverside, a quiet retreat — and the first thing you do is wash the journey off you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रघुबर कहेउ लखन भल घाटू। करहु कतहुँ अब ठाहर ठाटू॥ लखन दीख पय उतर करारा। चहुँ दिसि फिरेउ धनुष जिमि नारा ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने कहा- लक्ष्मण! बड़ा अच्छा घाट है। अब यहीं कहीं ठहरने की व्यवस्था करो। तब लक्ष्मणजी ने पयस्विनी नदी के उत्तर के ऊँचे किनारे को देखा (और कहा कि-) इसके चारों ओर धनुष के जैसा एक नाला फिरा हुआ है॥।1॥
english_translation: Raghubar said, "Lakshman, this is a good landing place. Arrange our stay here." Lakshman saw the high northern bank of the Payaswini river and said, "A channel has curved around it like a bow."
essence: A wise pause begins with noticing where to rest.
simple_meaning: Ram chooses a good place to stop, and Lakshman notices the riverbank curves around it like a bow.
insight: It trains attention toward placement and surroundings, not just movement.
modern_relevance: You arrive tired at a new place and start scanning for the safest corner, the best light, the quietest seat. This is that same practical attention.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: नदी पनच सर सम दम दाना। सकल कलुष कलि साउज नाना॥ चित्रकूट जनु अचल अहेरी। चुकइ न घात मार मुठभेरी ॥
translation: नदी (मंदाकिनी) उस धनुष की प्रत्यंचा (डोरी) है और शम, दम, दान बाण हैं। कलियुग के समस्त पाप उसके अनेक हिंसक पशु (रूप निशाने) हैं। चित्रकूट ही मानो अचल शिकारी है, जिसका निशाना कभी चूकता नहीं और जो सामने से मारता है ॥
english_translation: The river is the bowstring, self-restraint, control of the senses, and giving are the arrows. All the many sins of Kali are the wild beasts it shoots down. Chitrakoot is like an unmoving hunter whose aim never fails and who strikes straight on.
essence: Chitrakoot becomes a force that hunts down corruption.
simple_meaning: The verse compares Chitrakoot and the river there to a hunter and his bow, saying that self-control and giving destroy the many harms of the age.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing holiness as decoration to seeing it as active protection against decay.
modern_relevance: You sit by a quiet river after a brutal week, and somehow the noise inside you starts to thin. A place, a practice, and a calmer rhythm can feel like they are hunting your worst habits down.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस कहि लखन ठाउँ देखरावा। थलु बिलोकि रघुबर सुखु पावा॥ रमेउ राम मनु देवन्ह जाना। चले सहित सुर थपति प्रधाना ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर लक्ष्मणजी ने स्थान दिखाया। स्थान को देखकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सुख पाया। जब देवताओं ने जाना कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी का मन यहाँ रम गया, तब वे देवताओं के प्रधान थवई (मकान बनाने वाले) विश्वकर्मा को साथ लेकर चले ॥
english_translation: Laxman showed the place. Seeing the spot, Ram felt content. When the devas knew that Ram's mind had settled there, they came with Vishwakarma, the chief craftsman.
essence: Ram’s contentment turns an ordinary place into a sacred home.
simple_meaning: Laxman shows Ram a place to stay, and Ram feels pleased with it. Seeing that Ram likes the spot, the devas arrange for help to build a dwelling.
insight: It shifts attention from building a shelter to recognising the place where the heart naturally settles.
modern_relevance: You step into a friend’s empty room, and something in you says, ‘Yes, this will do.’ Before the furniture arrives, the feeling of belonging is already there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोल किरात बेष सब आए। रचे परन तृन सदन सुहाए॥ बरनि न जाहिं मंजु दुइ साला। एक ललित लघु एक बिसाला ॥
translation: सब देवता कोल-भीलों के वेष में आए और उन्होंने (दिव्य) पत्तों और घासों के सुंदर घर बना दिए। दो ऐसी सुंदर कुटिया बनाईं जिनका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता। उनमें एक बड़ी सुंदर छोटी सी थी और दूसरी बड़ी थी ॥
english_translation: All the Kol and Kirat people came in disguise and built lovely homes of leaves and grass. Two beautiful huts were made that cannot be described. One was charmingly small, and the other was large.
essence: Love becomes shelter when it turns into service.
simple_meaning: The forest people came together and built two lovely leaf-and-grass huts for Ram, Sita, and Lakshman.
insight: It shifts attention from admiration to service, showing that devotion becomes shelter, work, and welcome.
modern_relevance: A neighbour drops by with groceries after your move, then stays to help assemble the bed. No applause, no ceremony — just care made visible.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लखन जानकी सहित प्रभु राजत रुचिर निकेत। सोह मदनु मुनि बेष जनु रति रितुराज समेत ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी और जानकीजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी सुंदर घास-पत्तों के घर में शोभायमान हैं। मानो कामदेव मुनि का वेष धारण करके पत्नी रति और वसंत ऋतु के साथ सुशोभित हो ॥
english_translation: Lord Ram, with Lakshman and Sita, shines in a lovely hut. It is as if Cupid has taken a sage's form, joined by Rati and spring.
essence: A humble home becomes radiant when Ram and Sita are there.
simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman shine in a beautiful forest hut. Their simple dwelling looks so lovely that it feels like spring itself has arrived there.
insight: It shifts attention from luxury to the quality of presence that makes a place feel complete.
modern_relevance: A bare room, a borrowed mattress, and two people you love can feel richer than any polished home when the heart is settled.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अमर नाग किंनर दिसिपाला। चित्रकूट आए तेहि काला॥ राम प्रनामु कीन्ह सब काहू। मुदित देव लहि लोचन लाहू ॥
translation: उस समय देवता, नाग, किन्नर और दिक्पाल चित्रकूट में आए और श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सब किसी को प्रणाम किया। देवता नेत्रों का लाभ पाकर आनंदित हुए ॥
english_translation: At that time the immortals, serpents, celestial singers, and guardians of the directions came to Chitrakoot. Ram bowed to them all, and the immortals rejoiced, blessed with the sight of his eyes.
essence: Real greatness bows first.
simple_meaning: The divine beings came to see Ram in Chitrakoot, and Ram honored them all. They left joyful after seeing him.
insight: It shows that true greatness includes humility, not distance.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence is calm and generous, and they greet the room with respect instead of pride. That small bow changes everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बरषि सुमन कह देव समाजू। नाथ सनाथ भए हम आजू॥ करि बिनती दुख दुसह सुनाए। हरषित निज निज सदन सिधाए ॥
translation: फूलों की वर्षा करके देव समाज ने कहा- हे नाथ! आज (आपका दर्शन पाकर) हम सनाथ हो गए। फिर विनती करके उन्होंने अपने दुःसह दुःख सुनाए और (दुःखों के नाश का आश्वासन पाकर) हर्षित होकर अपने-अपने स्थानों को चले गए ॥
english_translation: The divine assembly showered flowers and said, “O Lord, today we are blessed by your presence.” They offered their prayers, told of their unbearable sorrows, and then returned happily to their own abodes.
essence: True refuge makes even sorrow feel bearable.
simple_meaning: The heavenly beings rejoice at Ram's presence, pray to him about their suffering, and leave comforted.
insight: It shifts attention from solving alone to seeking the presence that steadies suffering.
modern_relevance: A room full of people can feel heavy until the one person who truly listens walks in. Suddenly everyone breathes easier, speaks honestly, and leaves lighter than they arrived.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चित्रकूट रघुनंदनु छाए। समाचार सुनि सुनि मुनि आए॥ आवत देखि मुदित मुनिबृंदा। कीन्ह दंडवत रघुकुल चंदा ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी चित्रकूट में आ बसे हैं, यह समाचार सुन-सुनकर बहुत से मुनि आए। रघुकुल के चन्द्रमा श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने मुदित हुई मुनि मंडली को आते देखकर दंडवत प्रणाम किया ॥
english_translation: Raghunandan has settled in Chitrakoot. Hearing the news again and again, many sages came. Seeing the joyful assembly of sages arrive, the moon of Raghu bowed down to them.
essence: Greatness reveals itself by bowing to wisdom.
simple_meaning: The sages hear that Ram is staying in Chitrakoot, so they come to see him. Ram greets them with full respect.
insight: It shows that real stature expresses itself through respect, not self-display.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after everyone has heard good news about you, and you still choose humility first. That quiet respect changes the whole atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि रघुबरहि लाइ उर लेहीं। सुफल होन हित आसिष देहीं॥ सिय सौमित्रि राम छबि देखहिं। साधन सकल सफल करि लेखहिं ॥
translation: मुनिगण श्री रामजी को हृदय से लगा लेते हैं और सफल होने के लिए आशीर्वाद देते हैं। वे सीताजी, लक्ष्मणजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी की छबि देखते हैं और अपने सारे साधनों को सफल हुआ समझते हैं ॥
english_translation: The sages embrace Raghubar to their hearts and bless him for his success. Seeing the beauty of Sita, Saumitra, and Ram, they feel all their spiritual practice has borne fruit.
essence: A single glimpse of Ram makes years of practice feel fulfilled.
simple_meaning: The sages are overwhelmed by Ram's presence. They embrace him, bless him, and feel that all their discipline has finally borne fruit.
insight: It shifts attention from private striving to the grace of being seen by what you revere.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after months of hard work, and one person you deeply respect nods with recognition. Suddenly the long effort feels worth it; that is the feeling here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जथाजोग सनमानि प्रभु बिदा किए मुनिबृंद। करहिं जोग जप जाग तप निज आश्रमन्हि सुछंद ॥
translation: प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने यथायोग्य सम्मान करके मुनि मंडली को विदा किया। (श्री रामचन्द्रजी के आ जाने से) वे सब अपने-अपने आश्रमों में अब स्वतंत्रता के साथ योग, जप, यज्ञ और तप करने लगे ॥
english_translation: The Lord respectfully sent the sages away, and they returned to their own hermitages, free to perform yoga, chanting, sacrifice, and austerity.
essence: Respect should leave others freer, not more dependent.
simple_meaning: Ram honors the sages and sends them back to their hermitages, where they can resume their spiritual practices freely.
insight: It shows that real honor restores other people's independence instead of creating dependence.
modern_relevance: You leave a mentor's home after a long, nourishing visit, and the best gift they gave you is not advice — it's the strength to return to your own work.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: यह सुधि कोल किरातन्ह पाई। हरषे जनु नव निधि घर आई॥ कंद मूल फल भरि भरि दोना। चले रंक जनु लूटन सोना ॥
translation: यह (श्री रामजी के आगमन का) समाचार जब कोल-भीलों ने पाया, तो वे ऐसे हर्षित हुए मानो नवों निधियाँ उनके घर ही पर आ गई हों। वे दोनों में कंद, मूल, फल भर-भरकर चले, मानो दरिद्र सोना लूटने चले हों ॥
english_translation: When the Kol and Kirat people heard this news, they rejoiced as if the nine treasures had come to their home. They filled two bowls with roots, tubers, and fruits and set out like the poor rushing to seize gold.
essence: A small offering becomes priceless when it is given with love.
simple_meaning: The forest tribes are so delighted by Ram's arrival that they bring him the best food they have, as if they have received a great fortune.
insight: It shifts attention from wealth to wholehearted offering, showing that devotion makes even simple food feel precious.
modern_relevance: Your friend shows up after a hard week, and you bring the only warm food in the house. The gift is small; the welcome is everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तिन्ह महँ जिन्ह देखे दोउ भ्राता। अपर तिन्हहि पूँछहिं मगु जाता॥ कहत सुनत रघुबीर निकाई। आइ सबन्हि देखे रघुराई ॥
translation: उनमें से जो दोनों भाइयों को (पहले) देख चुके थे, उनसे दूसरे लोग रास्ते में जाते हुए पूछते हैं। इस प्रकार श्री रामचन्द्रजी की सुंदरता कहते-सुनते सबने आकर श्री रघुनाथजी के दर्शन किए ॥
english_translation: Among them, those who had already seen the two brothers were asked the way by the others. Hearing and speaking of Raghuvir's beauty, everyone came and saw Raghuraj.
essence: Ram’s beauty makes people come looking for him.
simple_meaning: People who had already seen Ram and Lakshman were asked for directions by others. As word spread about Ram's beauty, everyone came to see him.
insight: It shows how beauty and goodness create their own path: hearing about Ram becomes the reason to seek him out.
modern_relevance: Someone mentions a friend’s kindness in a crowded train station, and strangers start asking, “Where is she?” Goodness travels faster than explanation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करहिं जोहारु भेंट धरि आगे। प्रभुहि बिलोकहिं अति अनुरागे॥ चित्र लिखे जनु जहँ तहँ ठाढ़े। पुलक सरीर नयन जल बाढ़े ॥
translation: भेंट आगे रखकर वे लोग जोहार करते हैं और अत्यन्त अनुराग के साथ प्रभु को देखते हैं। वे मुग्ध हुए जहाँ के तहाँ मानो चित्र लिखे से खड़े हैं। उनके शरीर पुलकित हैं और नेत्रों में प्रेमाश्रुओं के जल की बाढ़ आ रही है ॥
english_translation: Holding out offerings in front of them, they bow to the Lord and gaze at him with deep love. They stand there like painted figures, their bodies thrilled with goosebumps and their eyes overflowing with tears of love.
essence: True love can leave you wordless, still, and overflowing at once.
simple_meaning: The people greet Ram with offerings and look at him with overwhelming love. They stand still, moved to tears and trembling with devotion.
insight: It shows devotion as a bodily response: bow, behold, tremble, and weep before what you love.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone whose presence you had only imagined, and your rehearsed words disappear. Your body says what your mouth cannot: you are moved beyond speech.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम सनेह मगन सब जाने। कहि प्रिय बचन सकल सनमाने॥ प्रभुहि जोहारि बहोरि बहोरी। बचन बिनीत कहहिंकर जोरी ॥
translation: श्री रामजी ने उन सबको प्रेम में मग्न जाना और प्रिय वचन कहकर सबका सम्मान किया। वे बार-बार प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को जोहार करते हुए हाथ जोड़कर विनीत वचन कहते हैं- ॥
english_translation: Ram saw that everyone was lost in love, and he honored them all with loving words. Again and again they bowed to the Lord, speaking humbly with folded hands.
essence: Love is answered with honor, and humility becomes natural.
simple_meaning: Ram notices the love in the crowd and responds with kind words. Everyone keeps bowing to him with folded hands and humble speech.
insight: It shows how gracious recognition can meet devotion without ego or distance.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is nervous to meet you, and you lower the tension with a kind sentence. That small warmth changes the whole atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अब हम नाथ सनाथ सब भए देखि प्रभु पाय। भाग हमारें आगमनु राउर कोसलराय ॥
translation: हे नाथ! प्रभु (आप) के चरणों का दर्शन पाकर अब हम सब सनाथ हो गए। हे कोसलराज! हमारे ही भाग्य से आपका यहाँ शुभागमन हुआ है ॥
english_translation: O Lord, seeing your feet, we are all now blessed. O King of Kosala, your auspicious arrival has come by our own good fortune.
essence: Being near Ram turns strangers into the protected.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram makes everyone feel protected and fortunate. His presence itself is a blessing, and his arrival is treated as the greatest good fortune.
insight: It shifts attention from what Ram can give to what his presence already does: it restores belonging.
modern_relevance: When a weary family member finally walks into the room after a long separation, the tension drops at once. Their presence alone makes everyone breathe easier.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धन्य भूमि बन पंथ पहारा। जहँ जहँ नाथ पाउ तुम्ह धारा॥ धन्य बिहग मृग काननचारी। सफल जनम भए तुम्हहि निहारी ॥
translation: हे नाथ! जहाँ-जहाँ आपने अपने चरण रखे हैं, वे पृथ्वी, वन, मार्ग और पहाड़ धन्य हैं, वे वन में विचरने वाले पक्षी और पशु धन्य हैं, जो आपको देखकर सफल जन्म हो गए ॥
english_translation: Blessed are the earth, forest, path, and mountains where you have placed your feet. Blessed are the birds and animals of the forest; seeing you, they have found their lives fulfilled.
essence: Your presence can sanctify everything around you.
simple_meaning: Every place you touch becomes blessed, and every creature that sees you finds its life fulfilled.
insight: It shifts attention from what Ram receives to what his presence transforms around him.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a hard week, and the mood changes before you say a word. Some people carry that kind of blessing with them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हम सब धन्य सहित परिवारा। दीख दरसु भरि नयन तुम्हारा॥ कीन्ह बासु भल ठाउँ बिचारी। इहाँ सकल रितु रहब सुखारी ॥
translation: हम सब भी अपने परिवार सहित धन्य हैं, जिन्होंने नेत्र भरकर आपका दर्शन किया। आपने बड़ी अच्छी जगह विचारकर निवास किया है। यहाँ सभी ऋतुओं में आप सुखी रहिएगा ॥
english_translation: We and our families are blessed to have seen you with our own eyes. You have chosen a truly good place to stay; may you live here happily in every season.
essence: Being near the beloved makes ordinary land feel blessed.
simple_meaning: The villagers feel blessed just to see Ram. They praise the place he has chosen to stay and wish him comfort in every season.
insight: It shifts attention from what is lacking to the grace of welcomed presence.
modern_relevance: A guest arrives after a long drive, and the whole house feels brighter. No speech is needed — everyone knows that being near the right person changes the atmosphere.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: हम सब भाँति करब सेवकाई। करि केहरि अहि बाघ बराई॥ बन बेहड़ गिरि कंदर खोहा। सब हमार प्रभु पग पग जोहा ॥
translation: हम लोग सब प्रकार से हाथी, सिंह, सर्प और बाघों से बचाकर आपकी सेवा करेंगे। हे प्रभो! यहाँ के बीहड़ वन, पहाड़, गुफाएँ और खोह (दर्रे) सब पग-पग हमारे देखे हुए हैं ॥
english_translation: We will serve you in every way, protecting you from elephants, lions, snakes, and tigers. Lord, these rough forests, mountains, caves, and ravines are all familiar ground to us step by step.
essence: Service becomes real when your knowledge keeps others safe.
simple_meaning: The forest people promise to serve Ram by guiding and protecting him through dangerous terrain they know well.
insight: It shifts service from words to usable protection and lived familiarity.
modern_relevance: A local guide leads you through a mountain trail after dark, pointing out every loose stone and hidden turn. He is not showing off; he is offering himself as shelter.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तहँ तहँ तुम्हहि अहेर खेलाउब। सर निरझर जलठाउँ देखाउब॥ हम सेवक परिवार समेता। नाथ न सकुचब आयसु देता ॥
translation: हम वहाँ-वहाँ (उन-उन स्थानों में) आपको शिकार खिलाएँगे और तालाब, झरने आदि जलाशयों को दिखाएँगे। हम कुटुम्ब समेत आपके सेवक हैं। हे नाथ! इसलिए हमें आज्ञा देने में संकोच न कीजिए ॥
english_translation: We will take you hunting there and there, and show you ponds, springs, and waters. We are your servants, along with our families. O Lord, do not hesitate to give us your commands.
essence: True service makes the other person feel completely at home.
simple_meaning: The forest people offer Ram food, guidance, and service. They want him to feel welcome and ask for anything without hesitation.
insight: It shifts service from words to practical care: guide, provide, and remove hesitation.
modern_relevance: You have guests in a place they do not know, and you keep pointing out where to eat, rest, and find water. That kind of quiet hospitality is what this verse honors.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: बेद बचन मुनि मन अगम ते प्रभु करुना ऐन। बचन किरातन्ह के सुनत जिमि पितु बालक बैन ॥
translation: जो वेदों के वचन और मुनियों के मन को भी अगम हैं, वे करुणा के धाम प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी भीलों के वचन इस तरह सुन रहे हैं, जैसे पिता बालकों के वचन सुनता है ॥
english_translation: The Lord, who is beyond the words of the Vedas and the minds of sages, listens to the forest people’s words like a father listening to his children.
essence: Ram is beyond understanding, yet utterly open to your voice.
simple_meaning: Ram is beyond ordinary understanding, yet he listens to the forest people with the tenderness of a father hearing his children.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to relationship, showing that humble speech can still meet divine attention.
modern_relevance: You try to explain yourself to someone important and your words come out clumsy, half-formed, embarrassed. This verse says tenderness can understand what polished speech cannot.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामहि केवल प्रेमु पिआरा। जानि लेउ जो जान निहारा॥ राम सकल बनचर तब तोषे। कहि मृदु बचन प्रेम परिपोषे ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी को केवल प्रेम प्यारा है, जो जानने वाला हो (जानना चाहता हो), वह जान ले। तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने प्रेम से परिपुष्ट हुए (प्रेमपूर्ण) कोमल वचन कहकर उन सब वन में विचरण करने वाले लोगों को संतुष्ट किया ॥
english_translation: Ram is beloved only by love; let the one who wants to know, know this. Then Ram satisfied all the forest dwellers by speaking soft, loving words.
essence: Ram is reached through love, and love changes the whole room.
simple_meaning: Ram responds to love, not display or force. When he speaks gently, even the forest people feel satisfied and cared for.
insight: It shifts the mind from proving yourself to meeting others with genuine warmth.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense family gathering and stop trying to win the room. You listen, soften your voice, and the atmosphere changes before anyone notices why.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिदा किए सिर नाइ सिधाए। प्रभु गुन कहत सुनत घर आए॥ एहि बिधि सिय समेत दोउ भाई। बसहिं बिपिन सुर मुनि सुखदाई ॥
translation: फिर उनको विदा किया। वे सिर नवाकर चले और प्रभु के गुण कहते-सुनते घर आए। इस प्रकार देवता और मुनियों को सुख देने वाले दोनों भाई सीताजी समेत वन में निवास करने लगे ॥
english_translation: After bowing their heads, they departed. Speaking and listening to the Lord's virtues, they returned home. In this way, the two brothers, together with Sita, lived in the forest, which became a joy to the gods and sages.
essence: Even leaving can become devotion when your mind stays on Ram.
simple_meaning: They took leave, went home while speaking of Ram's virtues, and then Rama, Sita, and Lakshman lived in the forest, bringing joy to sages and radiant beings.
insight: It turns departure into remembrance and shows how sacred company changes the atmosphere around it.
modern_relevance: You leave a difficult visit quietly, still talking about what was good and true. By the time you reach home, the heaviness has eased because the conversation itself carried you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जब तें आइ रहे रघुनायकु। तब तें भयउ बनु मंगलदायकु॥ फूलहिं फलहिं बिटप बिधि नाना। मंजु बलित बर बेलि बिताना ॥
translation: जब से श्री रघुनाथजी वन में आकर रहे तब से वन मंगलदायक हो गया। अनेक प्रकार के वृक्ष फूलते और फलते हैं और उन पर लिपटी हुई सुंदर बेलों के मंडप तने हैं ॥
english_translation: Since Raghunath came here, the forest has become auspicious. Many kinds of trees bloom and bear fruit, and lovely vines spread their canopies over them.
essence: Ram's presence turns even the forest into blessing.
simple_meaning: Ram's presence makes the forest feel blessed and alive. Trees bloom, bear fruit, and vines spread beautifully everywhere.
insight: It shifts attention from the setting itself to the transformative effect of noble presence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room, and the mood shifts before anyone speaks. Some presences make life feel more alive, more generous, more whole.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुरतरु सरिस सुभायँ सुहाए। मनहुँ बिबुध बन परिहरि आए॥ गुंज मंजुतर मधुकर श्रेनी। त्रिबिध बयारि बहइ सुख देनी ॥
translation: वे कल्पवृक्ष के समान स्वाभाविक ही सुंदर हैं। मानो वे देवताओं के वन (नंदन वन) को छोड़कर आए हों। भौंरों की पंक्तियाँ बहुत ही सुंदर गुंजार करती हैं और सुख देने वाली शीतल, मंद, सुगंधित हवा चलती रहती है ॥
english_translation: They were naturally beautiful like wish-fulfilling trees, as if they had left the gods' own grove behind. Beautiful rows of bees hummed, and a gentle, cool, fragrant breeze gave delight.
essence: Ram's presence makes the forest feel like a divine grove.
simple_meaning: The forest around Ram is so lovely that it feels like a divine grove. Bees hum softly, and a cool breeze makes everything pleasant.
insight: It shifts attention from the scene itself to the sanctifying effect of Ram's presence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home where someone kind has been living alone for weeks. The room feels calmer, the air lighter, even the silence gentler. Some presences change the whole atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नीलकंठ कलकंठ सुक चातक चक्क चकोर। भाँति भाँति बोलहिं बिहग श्रवन सुखद चित चोर ॥
translation: नीलकंठ, कोयल, तोते, पपीहे, चकवे और चकोर आदि पक्षी कानों को सुख देने वाली और चित्त को चुराने वाली तरह-तरह की बोलियाँ बोलते हैं ॥
english_translation: Blue-throated birds, cuckoos, parrots, chataks, chakravaks, and chakors all sing in many ways, delighting the ear and stealing the heart.
essence: Ram's presence makes even the forest sing.
simple_meaning: The forest is so beautiful that even the birds' songs delight the ear and captivate the mind.
insight: It shifts attention from bare scenery to the way presence changes an entire environment.
modern_relevance: You walk into a quiet park after a hard week, and the first birdsong loosens something in your chest. Some places feel different because of the presence they hold.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि केहरि कपि कोल कुरंगा। बिगतबैर बिचरहिं सब संगा॥ फिरत अहेर राम छबि देखी। होहिं मुदित मृग बृंद बिसेषी ॥
translation: हाथी, सिंह, बंदर, सूअर और हिरन, ये सब वैर छोड़कर साथ-साथ विचरते हैं। शिकार के लिए फिरते हुए श्री रामचन्द्रजी की छबि को देखकर पशुओं के समूह विशेष आनंदित होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Elephants, lions, monkeys, boars, and deer all roam together, free of enmity. While roaming for the hunt, they see Ram's radiant form, and the herds of deer become especially joyful.
essence: Ram's presence turns fear into harmony.
simple_meaning: Even natural enemies live together in peace here, and Ram's presence makes the animals especially happy.
insight: It shifts attention from danger and division to the peace created by a noble presence.
modern_relevance: A room full of people who normally compete starts to relax the moment the person everyone trusts walks in. The atmosphere changes before anyone says a word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिबुध बिपिन जहँ लगि जग माहीं। देखि रामबनु सकल सिहाहीं॥ सुरसरि सरसइ दिनकर कन्या। मेकलसुता गोदावरि धन्या ॥
translation: जगत में जहाँ तक (जितने) देवताओं के वन हैं, सब श्री रामजी के वन को देखकर सिहाते हैं, गंगा, सरस्वती, सूर्यकुमारी यमुना, नर्मदा, गोदावरी आदि धन्य (पुण्यमयी) नदियाँ, ॥
english_translation: Wherever the divine groves exist in the world, they all envy Ram's forest. The sacred rivers — Ganga, Saraswati, Yamuna, Narmada, and Godavari — are blessed.
essence: Ram's presence makes even holy places feel small.
simple_meaning: Ram's forest is so beautiful that even the divine groves seem to envy it. Sacred rivers like Ganga, Saraswati, Yamuna, Narmada, and Godavari are praised as blessed.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary scenery to sacred atmosphere created by association.
modern_relevance: You walk into a quiet riverside grove at dawn and feel, for a moment, that the whole place has been sanctified by presence alone.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब सर सिंधु नदीं नद नाना। मंदाकिनि कर करहिं बखाना॥ उदय अस्त गिरि अरु कैलासू। मंदर मेरु सकल सुरबासू ॥
translation: सारे तालाब, समुद्र, नदी और अनेकों नद सब मंदाकिनी की बड़ाई करते हैं। उदयाचल, अस्ताचल, कैलास, मंदराचल और सुमेरु आदि सब, जो देवताओं के रहने के स्थान हैं, ॥
english_translation: All ponds, oceans, rivers, and countless streams praise the Mandakini. The eastern and western mountains, Kailash, Mandar, and Meru, all the homes of the radiant beings, too.
essence: Sacred greatness draws every other greatness into praise.
simple_meaning: Every river, sea, and mountain is described as praising the Mandakini and the holy places around it.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated greatness to the way holiness makes its surroundings testify.
modern_relevance: You walk into a place and feel its quiet authority before anyone speaks. The room, the people, even the silence seem to recognize what matters there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सैल हिमाचल आदिक जेते। चित्रकूट जसु गावहिं तेते॥ बिंधि मुदित मन सुखु न समाई। श्रम बिनु बिपुल बड़ाई पाई ॥
translation: और हिमालय आदि जितने पर्वत हैं, सभी चित्रकूट का यश गाते हैं। विन्ध्याचल बड़ा आनंदित है, उसके मन में सुख समाता नहीं, क्योंकि उसने बिना परिश्रम ही बहुत बड़ी बड़ाई पा ली है ॥
english_translation: All the mountains, including the Himalayas, sing the glory of Chitrakoot. Vindhyachal is filled with joy; his heart cannot contain the delight, because he received such great praise without any effort.
essence: Grace can make even the proud rejoice without effort.
simple_meaning: Even the great mountains praise Chitrakoot. Vindhyachal feels overjoyed because he has received great honor without any effort.
insight: It shifts attention from achievement to grace, showing that worth can be received, not only earned.
modern_relevance: You get unexpectedly praised in a room where you said almost nothing. The surprise is not the attention itself, but the feeling that something larger than effort is moving through your life.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चित्रकूट के बिहग मृग बेलि बिटप तृन जाति। पुन्य पुंज सब धन्य अस कहहिं देव दिन राति ॥
translation: चित्रकूट के पक्षी, पशु, बेल, वृक्ष, तृण-अंकुरादि की सभी जातियाँ पुण्य की राशि हैं और धन्य हैं- देवता दिन-रात ऐसा कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: The birds, animals, vines, trees, and blades of grass of Chitrakoot are all said to be a heap of merit and blessed; the devas say this day and night.
essence: Ram's presence makes even grass and birds feel blessed.
simple_meaning: Even the birds, animals, plants, and grass of Chitrakoot are considered blessed. The verse says this sacredness is so complete that even the devas keep praising it.
insight: It shifts attention from scenery alone to the sacred quality a presence can give to an entire place.
modern_relevance: You walk into a place where someone deeply loved has lived, and even the ordinary chair, cup, and doorway feel charged with meaning. Presence changes everything around it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नयनवंत रघुबरहि बिलोकी। पाइ जनम फल होहिं बिसोकी॥ परसि चरन रज अचर सुखारी। भए परम पद के अधिकारी ॥
translation: आँखों वाले जीव श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर जन्म का फल पाकर शोकरहित हो जाते हैं और अचर (पर्वत, वृक्ष, भूमि, नदी आदि) भगवान की चरण रज का स्पर्श पाकर सुखी होते हैं। यों सभी परम पद (मोक्ष) के अधिकारी हो गए ॥
english_translation: All who have eyes and behold Raghubar become free of sorrow, having found the fruit of birth. Even beings without movement become blessed by touching the dust of his feet, and all become worthy of the highest state.
essence: Ram's presence alone turns sorrow into blessing.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram brings the true reward of life. Even trees, rocks, and rivers are blessed by the dust of his feet.
insight: It shifts attention from what Ram gives to what his presence itself does.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the whole mood changes because one person arrived with real presence. That is the feeling here: being near Ram is not just comforting, it is transforming.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सो बनु सैलु सुभायँ सुहावन। मंगलमय अति पावन पावन॥ महिमा कहिअ कवनि बिधि तासू। सुखसागर जहँ कीन्ह निवासू ॥
translation: वह वन और पर्वत स्वाभाविक ही सुंदर, मंगलमय और अत्यन्त पवित्रों को भी पवित्र करने वाला है। उसकी महिमा किस प्रकार कही जाए, जहाँ सुख के समुद्र श्री रामजी ने निवास किया है ॥
english_translation: That forest and mountain are naturally beautiful, filled with auspiciousness, and purer than the pure. How can their glory be described, where the ocean of joy made his home?
essence: Ram's presence turns even wild places into sanctuaries.
simple_meaning: The forest and mountain became beautiful and deeply pure because Ram lived there. Their holiness is beyond words.
insight: It shifts attention from scenery to presence: what matters most is not the place, but who dwells there.
modern_relevance: You walk into a plain, cramped room after someone steady and kind has lived there for months. The room still looks ordinary, but it feels different because their presence changed its atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पय पयोधि तजि अवध बिहाई। जहँ सिय लखनु रामु रहे आई॥ कहि न सकहिं सुषमा जसि कानन। जौं सत सहस होहिं सहसानन ॥
translation: क्षीर सागर को त्यागकर और अयोध्या को छोड़कर जहाँ सीताजी, लक्ष्मणजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी आकर रहे, उस वन की जैसी परम शोभा है, उसको हजार मुख वाले जो लाख शेषजी हों तो वे भी नहीं कह सकते ॥
english_translation: Leaving the ocean of milk and abandoning Ayodhya, the forest where Sita, Lakshman, and Ram came to live is so beautiful that even a thousand-hooded serpent could not describe it.
essence: Love makes even exile feel radiant.
simple_meaning: The forest becomes unimaginably beautiful because Ram, Sita, and Lakshman live there. Even the greatest speaker could not fully describe it.
insight: It shifts attention from scenery to sanctifying presence.
modern_relevance: A cramped rented room can feel like home the moment the people you love sit on the floor and laugh there. Presence changes the whole atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सो मैं बरनि कहौं बिधि केहीं। डाबर कमठ कि मंदर लेहीं॥ सेवहिं लखनु करम मन बानी। जाइ न सीलु सनेहु बखानी ॥
translation: उसे भला, मैं किस प्रकार से वर्णन करके कह सकता हूँ। कहीं पोखरे का (क्षुद्र) कछुआ भी मंदराचल उठा सकता है? लक्ष्मणजी मन, वचन और कर्म से श्री रामचन्द्रजी की सेवा करते हैं। उनके शील और स्नेह का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
english_translation: How can I possibly describe it? Could even a tiny pond turtle lift Mount Mandara? Lakshman serves Ram with mind, speech, and action. His character and affection cannot be described.
essence: True service is so complete that description falls short.
simple_meaning: Lakshman serves Ram with complete devotion in thought, speech, and action, and his character and affection are beyond description.
insight: It shifts attention from performance to wholehearted service that is carried through mind, speech, and action.
modern_relevance: You try to explain why one friend stayed up all night helping you move, then still refused credit. The explanation always feels smaller than the loyalty itself.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: छिनु छिनु लखि सिय राम पद जानि आपु पर नेहु। करत न सपनेहुँ लखनु चितु बंधु मातु पितु गेहु ॥
translation: क्षण-क्षण पर श्री सीता-रामजी के चरणों को देखकर और अपने ऊपर उनका स्नेह जानकर लक्ष्मणजी स्वप्न में भी भाइयों, माता-पिता और घर की याद नहीं करते ॥
english_translation: Moment by moment, seeing Sita and Ram's feet and knowing their love for him, Lakshman never even dreams of brother, mother, father, or home.
essence: True devotion makes every lesser attachment fade.
simple_meaning: Lakshman is so absorbed in Ram and Sita's presence and love that he forgets his own family and home completely.
insight: It shifts attention from what you have left behind to what you are serving now.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your old group chat, your family thread, your childhood photos, looking for a feeling that has already been replaced by something deeper. Real belonging can make the old ache go quiet.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम संग सिय रहति सुखारी। पुर परिजन गृह सुरति बिसारी॥ छिनु छिनु पिय बिधु बदनु निहारी। प्रमुदित मनहुँ चकोर कुमारी ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के साथ सीताजी अयोध्यापुरी, कुटुम्ब के लोग और घर की याद भूलकर बहुत ही सुखी रहती हैं। क्षण-क्षण पर पति श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चन्द्रमा के समान मुख को देखकर वे वैसे ही परम प्रसन्न रहती हैं, जैसे चकोर कुमारी (चकोरी) चन्द्रमा को देखकर ! ॥
english_translation: Sita lives happily with Ram, forgetting the city, family, and home. Again and again she looks at her beloved Ram's moonlike face, delighted like a chakor bird seeing the moon.
essence: Presence with the beloved makes the whole world recede.
simple_meaning: Sita feels complete with Ram beside her. She forgets palace life and family ties, and finds joy simply in looking at his face.
insight: It shifts attention from external comfort to the steady joy of shared presence.
modern_relevance: You come home exhausted, drop your phone, and sit beside the one person who makes the day feel lighter. The noise of work, family demands, and unfinished tasks suddenly loosens its grip.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाह नेहु नित बढ़त बिलोकी। हरषित रहति दिवस जिमि कोकी॥ सिय मनु राम चरन अनुरागा। अवध सहस सम बनु प्रिय लागा ॥
translation: स्वामी का प्रेम अपने प्रति नित्य बढ़ता हुआ देखकर सीताजी ऐसी हर्षित रहती हैं, जैसे दिन में चकवी! सीताजी का मन श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में अनुरक्त है, इससे उनको वन हजारों अवध के समान प्रिय लगता है ॥
english_translation: Seeing her lord's love grow every day, Sita remains delighted like a chakori in daylight. Her mind is attached to Ram's feet, so the forest feels as dear to her as thousands of Ayodhyas.
essence: Devotion can make exile feel like home.
simple_meaning: Sita is so devoted to Ram that his growing love fills her with joy, and the forest itself feels dear to her.
insight: It shifts attachment from place and comfort to presence and love.
modern_relevance: You move to a new city and the apartment is bare, the streets unfamiliar, the days long. Then one steady relationship makes the whole place feel livable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परनकुटी प्रिय प्रियतम संगा। प्रिय परिवारु कुरंग बिहंगा॥ सासु ससुर सम मुनितिय मुनिबर। असनु अमिअ सम कंद मूल फर ॥
translation: प्रियतम (श्री रामचन्द्रजी) के साथ पर्णकुटी प्यारी लगती है। मृग और पक्षी प्यारे कुटुम्बियों के समान लगते हैं। मुनियों की स्त्रियाँ सास के समान, श्रेष्ठ मुनि ससुर के समान और कंद-मूल-फलों का आहार उनको अमृत के समान लगता है ॥
english_translation: The forest hut feels dear when you are with your beloved. Deer and birds feel like family. The women of the forest feel like mothers-in-law, the great sages feel like fathers-in-law, and roots, fruits, and tubers taste like nectar.
essence: Love can turn exile into belonging.
simple_meaning: When you are with the one you love, even a forest hut feels dear. Everything around you starts to feel like family, and simple forest food feels delicious.
insight: It shifts attention from outer comfort to the transforming power of loving presence.
modern_relevance: You move to a new city and the room is bare, the streets are strange, and the food is plain. Then one person you love walks in, and the whole place stops feeling foreign.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ साथ साँथरी सुहाई। मयन सयन सय सम सुखदाई॥ लोकप होहिं बिलोकत जासू। तेहि कि मोहि सक बिषय बिलासू ॥
translation: स्वामी के साथ सुंदर साथरी (कुश और पत्तों की सेज) सैकड़ों कामदेव की सेजों के समान सुख देने वाली है। जिनके (कृपापूर्वक) देखने मात्र से जीव लोकपाल हो जाते हैं, उनको कहीं भोग-विलास मोहित कर सकते हैं! ॥
english_translation: Being with my Lord, this simple bed of grass and leaves feels as सुखदायक as a hundred beds of desire. Those whom even the celestial guardians long to behold—how could worldly pleasures ever tempt me?
essence: Ram's presence turns hardship into ease and luxury into irrelevance.
simple_meaning: Sita says that being with Ram makes a simple grass bed feel better than luxurious comfort. When even great beings long to see him, worldly pleasures lose all appeal.
insight: It shifts attention from external comfort to the quality of companionship.
modern_relevance: You sit on a hard floor in a crowded train station, waiting beside someone you love, and the discomfort barely matters. Presence changes the whole experience.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सुमिरत रामहि तजहिं जन तृन सम बिषय बिलासु। रामप्रिया जग जननि सिय कछु न आचरजु तासु ॥
translation: जिन श्री रामचन्द्रजी का स्मरण करने से ही भक्तजन तमाम भोग-विलास को तिनके के समान त्याग देते हैं, उन श्री रामचन्द्रजी की प्रिय पत्नी और जगत की माता सीताजी के लिए यह (भोग-विलास का त्याग) कुछ भी आश्चर्य नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Those who remember Ram let go of worldly pleasures as if they were blades of grass. For Sita, beloved of Ram and mother of the world, that is no surprise.
essence: Love for Ram makes pleasure lose its power.
simple_meaning: Remembering Ram makes worldly pleasures lose their grip. For Sita, who belongs to Ram completely, giving them up is natural, not remarkable.
insight: It shifts desire from chasing pleasure to resting in what truly matters.
modern_relevance: You finally leave a party early, not from boredom but because your child's fever is rising and your mind is already elsewhere. What used to feel irresistible now feels small beside what you love most.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सीय लखन जेहि बिधि सुखु लहहीं। सोइ रघुनाथ करहिं सोइ कहहीं॥ कहहिं पुरातन कथा कहानी। सुनहिं लखनु सिय अति सुखु मानी ॥
translation: सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी को जिस प्रकार सुख मिले, श्री रघुनाथजी वही करते और वही कहते हैं। भगवान प्राचीन कथाएँ और कहानियाँ कहते हैं और लक्ष्मणजी तथा सीताजी अत्यन्त सुख मानकर सुनते हैं ॥
english_translation: In whatever way Sita and Lakshman find happiness, Raghunath does and says the same. He tells ancient stories and tales, and Lakshman and Sita listen with great delight.
essence: True closeness means shaping yourself around another's joy.
simple_meaning: Ram naturally does and says whatever brings Sita and Lakshman happiness. He spends time telling old stories, and they listen with deep joy.
insight: It shifts love from self-expression to responsive companionship.
modern_relevance: You come home exhausted, and instead of scrolling away in silence, you tell the story they needed to hear. The real intimacy is not grand speech — it is learning what brings the other person peace.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जब जब रामु अवध सुधि करहीं। तब तब बारि बिलोचन भरहीं॥ सुमिरि मातु पितु परिजन भाई। भरत सनेहु सीलु सेवकाई ॥
translation: जब-जब श्री रामचन्द्रजी अयोध्या की याद करते हैं, तब-तब उनके नेत्रों में जल भर आता है। माता-पिता, कुटुम्बियों और भाइयों तथा भरत के प्रेम, शील और सेवाभाव को याद करके- ॥
english_translation: Whenever Ram remembers Ayodhya, tears fill his eyes. He remembers his mother, father, family, brothers, and Bharat's love, character, and service.
essence: Remembrance can bring even Ram to tears.
simple_meaning: Ram thinks of Ayodhya and weeps, remembering his family and Bharat's loving service.
insight: It shows that remembrance is not passive; it can reopen love, grief, and gratitude all at once.
modern_relevance: You pass the old neighborhood on the train and suddenly your chest tightens. A name, a street, a face you miss — memory can still bring tears.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कृपासिंधु प्रभु होहिं दुखारी। धीरजु धरहिं कुसमउ बिचारी॥ लखि सिय लखनु बिकल होइ जाहीं। जिमि पुरुषहि अनुसर परिछाहीं ॥
translation: कृपा के समुद्र प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी दुःखी हो जाते हैं, किन्तु फिर कुसमय समझकर धीरज धारण कर लेते हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी को दुःखी देखकर सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी भी व्याकुल हो जाते हैं, जैसे किसी मनुष्य की परछाहीं उस मनुष्य के समान ही चेष्टा करती है ॥
english_translation: The ocean of compassion, the Lord, feels sorrow; then, seeing the wrong time, he steadies himself. Seeing Ram distressed, Sita and Lakshman become restless too, just as a shadow follows the body.
essence: Your inner weather quietly becomes everyone else's.
simple_meaning: Ram feels the pain of the moment, but he holds himself steady. When he is distressed, Sita and Lakshman are disturbed too, just as a shadow follows the body.
insight: It shows how emotional states ripple through close relationships and how self-restraint protects others from being swept along.
modern_relevance: You walk into the house after a brutal phone call, and everyone feels the shift before you say a word. Your silence, tension, or steadiness spreads faster than explanations.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रिया बंधु गति लखि रघुनंदनु। धीर कृपाल भगत उर चंदनु॥ लगे कहन कछु कथा पुनीता। सुनि सुखु लहहिं लखनु अरु सीता ॥
translation: तब धीर, कृपालु और भक्तों के हृदयों को शीतल करने के लिए चंदन रूप रघुकुल को आनंदित करने वाले श्री रामचन्द्रजी प्यारी पत्नी और भाई लक्ष्मण की दशा देखकर कुछ पवित्र कथाएँ कहने लगते हैं, जिन्हें सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सुख प्राप्त करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing the condition of his dear wife and brother, the gentle, compassionate Raghunandan, the sandalwood for devotees' hearts, began to speak some holy stories. Hearing them, Lakshman and Sita found peace.
essence: Ram heals distress by speaking what steadies the heart.
simple_meaning: Seeing Lakshman and Sita distressed, Ram begins speaking holy stories to soothe them. His words bring them peace.
insight: It shifts care from fixing problems to offering calming presence.
modern_relevance: Your partner is overwhelmed, your sibling is quiet, and you can feel the tension in the room. Instead of forcing solutions, you speak calmly and give them something steady to hold.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामु लखन सीता सहित सोहत परन निकेत। जिमि बासव बस अमरपुर सची जयंत समेत ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सहित श्री रामचन्द्रजी पर्णकुटी में ऐसे सुशोभित हैं, जैसे अमरावती में इन्द्र अपनी पत्नी शची और पुत्र जयंत सहित बसता है ॥
english_translation: Ram, with Lakshman and Sita, looks splendid in the forest hut, like Indra in Amaravati with Shachi and Jayant.
essence: True splendor can live inside a simple shelter.
simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman living in a forest hut are described as shining with the dignity of a royal household.
insight: It shifts attention from outward comfort to the grace created by how people live together.
modern_relevance: A family sharing a tiny rented room after a hard move can still feel rich if there is love, steadiness, and mutual care. Circumstance does not decide dignity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जोगवहिं प्रभुसिय लखनहि कैसें। पलक बिलोचन गोलक जैसें॥ सेवहिं लखनु सीय रघुबीरहि। जिमि अबिबेकी पुरुष सरीरहि ॥
translation: प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी की कैसी सँभाल रखते हैं, जैसे पलकें नेत्रों के गोलकों की। इधर लक्ष्मणजी श्री सीताजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी की (अथवा लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी की) ऐसी सेवा करते हैं, जैसे अज्ञानी मनुष्य शरीर की करते हैं ॥
english_translation: How does Lord Ram care for Sita and Lakshman? Like eyelids guard the eyes. Lakshman serves Sita and Raghuvir just as a careless person serves the body.
essence: True devotion protects gently and serves completely.
simple_meaning: Ram protects Sita and Lakshman with constant care, and Lakshman serves Ram and Sita with complete devotion.
insight: It teaches you to measure love by care given and service offered, not by words alone.
modern_relevance: You check on a tired sibling before you sleep, then stay up helping them anyway. Real love is both protection and service, given without complaint.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि बिधि प्रभु बन बसहिं सुखारी। खग मृग सुर तापस हितकारी॥ कहेउँ राम बन गवनु सुहावा। सुनहु सुमंत्र अवध जिमि आवा ॥
translation: पक्षी, पशु, देवता और तपस्वियों के हितकारी प्रभु इस प्रकार सुखपूर्वक वन में निवास कर रहे हैं। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- मैंने श्री रामचन्द्रजी का सुंदर वनगमन कहा। अब जिस तरह सुमन्त्र अयोध्या में आए वह (कथा) सुनो ॥
english_translation: In this way, the Lord lived happily in the forest, bringing benefit to birds, animals, devas, and sages. Tulsidas says: I have told the lovely departure of Ram to the forest. Now listen to how Sumantra returned to Ayodhya.
essence: Ram's exile still blesses every being around him.
simple_meaning: Ram lives in the forest in peace, and his presence benefits every kind of being there. The poet then turns the story toward Sumantra's return to Ayodhya.
insight: It shifts attention from loss to the quiet blessing a righteous presence brings.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room and people soften without knowing why. Some presence quiets the whole space, even when nothing outward has improved.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: फिरेउ निषादु प्रभुहि पहुँचाई। सचिव सहित रथ देखेसि आई॥ मंत्री बिकल बिलोकि निषादू। कहि न जाइ जस भयउ बिषादू ॥
translation: प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को पहुँचाकर जब निषादराज लौटा, तब आकर उसने रथ को मंत्री (सुमंत्र) सहित देखा। मंत्री को व्याकुल देखकर निषाद को जैसा दुःख हुआ, वह कहा नहीं जाता ॥
english_translation: After escorting Lord Ram away, Nishad returned and saw the chariot with the minister. Seeing the minister distressed, the grief Nishad felt cannot be told.
essence: Grief moves from one heart to another without a single word.
simple_meaning: Nishad returns after seeing Ram off and finds Sumantra in deep distress. That sight fills him with grief too, and the verse lingers on shared sorrow rather than teaching.
insight: It shows how sorrow is often recognized first through another person’s body and silence, not through speech.
modern_relevance: You walk back into a room after dropping someone at the airport, and one face tells you everything went wrong. Grief passes silently before anyone explains it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम राम सिय लखन पुकारी। परेउ धरनितल ब्याकुल भारी॥ देखि दखिन दिसि हय हिहिनाहीं। जनु बिनु पंख बिहग अकुलाहीं ॥
translation: (निषाद को अकेले आया देखकर) सुमंत्र हा राम! हा राम! हा सीते! हा लक्ष्मण! पुकारते हुए, बहुत व्याकुल होकर धरती पर गिर पड़े। (रथ के) घोड़े दक्षिण दिशा की ओर (जिधर श्री रामचन्द्रजी गए थे) देख-देखकर हिनहिनाते हैं। मानो बिना पंख के पक्षी व्याकुल हो रहे हों ॥
english_translation: Sumantra cried out, "Ram! Ram! Sita! Lakshman!" and fell to the ground in great distress. Seeing toward the south, the horses neighed again and again, as if birds without wings were in anguish.
essence: Absence can make the whole world ache.
simple_meaning: Sumantra breaks down in grief after Ram, Sita, and Lakshman leave. Even the horses seem to mourn their absence.
insight: It turns grief into a shared scene, showing how absence can echo through people and even animals.
modern_relevance: You come home after dropping someone at the airport, and the silence in the car feels physical. Even the smallest details keep turning toward the one who left.
speaker: Sumantra

verse_text: नहिं तृन चरहिं न पिअहिं जलु मोचहिं लोचन बारि। ब्याकुल भए निषाद सब रघुबर बाजि निहारि ॥
translation: वे न तो घास चरते हैं, न पानी पीते हैं। केवल आँखों से जल बहा रहे हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के घोड़ों को इस दशा में देखकर सब निषाद व्याकुल हो गए ॥
english_translation: The horses neither graze nor drink water. They only pour tears from their eyes. Seeing Ram's horses in this state, all the Nishads were overcome with grief.
essence: Even the horses are grieving Ram's absence.
simple_meaning: Ram's horses are so distressed by separation that they won't eat or drink. Even the Nishads feel that grief deeply when they see them.
insight: It turns separation into a shared atmosphere, showing how loss affects everyone present, not only the most obvious mourner.
modern_relevance: You come home and your dog won't touch its food because the house feels wrong without someone it loved. Grief can live in the whole room, not just in you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धरि धीरजु तब कहइ निषादू। अब सुमंत्र परिहरहु बिषादू॥ तुम्ह पंडित परमारथ ग्याता। धरहु धीर लखि बिमुख बिधाता ॥
translation: तब धीरज धरकर निषादराज कहने लगा- हे सुमंत्रजी! अब विषाद को छोड़िए। आप पंडित और परमार्थ के जानने वाले हैं। विधाता को प्रतिकूल जानकर धैर्य धारण कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Then, gathering courage, Nishad said to Sumantra: "Now let go of grief. You are learned and know the higher purpose. Hold steady, seeing that fate has turned against you."
essence: Steadiness begins when you stop arguing with what has already turned.
simple_meaning: Nishad asks Sumantra to stop grieving and remain steady, since he understands higher purpose and can see that events have turned against them.
insight: It shifts the mind from panic to composure, teaching you to meet reversal without losing dignity.
modern_relevance: Your friend sits in the parked car after a family argument, staring at the steering wheel, unable to speak. You don't solve everything — you help them breathe, name what happened, and keep their footing.
speaker: Nishad

verse_text: बिबिधि कथा कहि कहि मृदु बानी। रथ बैठारेउ बरबस आनी॥ सोक सिथिल रथु सकइ न हाँकी। रघुबर बिरह पीर उर बाँकी ॥
translation: कोमल वाणी से भाँति-भाँति की कथाएँ कहकर निषाद ने जबर्दस्ती लाकर सुमंत्र को रथ पर बैठाया, परन्तु शोक के मारे वे इतने शिथिल हो गए कि रथ को हाँक नहीं सकते। उनके हृदय में श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विरह की बड़ी तीव्र वेदना है ॥
english_translation: Nishad spoke gently and told many kinds of stories, then forced Sumantra onto the chariot. But Sumantra had become so weakened by grief that he could not drive the chariot; in his heart burned the sharp pain of separation from Ram.
essence: Grief can leave you unable to move, even when you must.
simple_meaning: Nishad gently speaks to Sumantra and seats him on the chariot, but grief has left him too weak to drive. His heart is pierced by separation from Ram.
insight: It shows how separation can drain the body, not just the mind.
modern_relevance: You sit in the car after dropping someone at the airport, hands still on the wheel, unable to start the engine. The silence is heavier than the road ahead.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चरफराहिं मग चलहिं न घोरे। बन मृग मनहुँ आनि रथ जोरे॥ अढ़ुकि परहिं फिरि हेरहिं पीछें। राम बियोगि बिकल दुख तीछें ॥
translation: घोड़े तड़फड़ाते हैं और (ठीक) रास्ते पर नहीं चलते। मानो जंगली पशु लाकर रथ में जोत दिए गए हों। वे श्री रामचन्द्रजी के वियोगी घोड़े कभी ठोकर खाकर गिर पड़ते हैं, कभी घूमकर पीछे की ओर देखने लगते हैं। वे तीक्ष्ण दुःख से व्याकुल हैं ॥
english_translation: The horses stumble off the road and do not go straight. It is as if wild animals were yoked to the chariot. They trip, fall, turn back to look behind, and burn with sharp pain at Ram’s separation.
essence: Separation makes even the steady lose their way.
simple_meaning: The horses are so grief-stricken by Ram’s absence that they cannot even walk properly. They stumble, fall, and keep looking back.
insight: It turns grief into a physical force, showing how separation can disrupt even ordinary movement.
modern_relevance: You start driving home after a goodbye that has cracked something open inside you. Your hands stay on the wheel, but your mind keeps turning back to the person you left behind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जो कह रामु लखनु बैदेही। हिंकरि हिंकरि हित हेरहिं तेही॥ बाजि बिरह गति कहि किमि जाती। बिनु मनि फनिक बिकल जेहिं भाँती ॥
translation: जो कोई राम, लक्ष्मण या जानकी का नाम ले लेता है, घोड़े हिकर-हिकरकर उसकी ओर प्यार से देखने लगते हैं। घोड़ों की विरह दशा कैसे कही जा सकती है? वे ऐसे व्याकुल हैं, जैसे मणि के बिना साँप व्याकुल होता है ॥
english_translation: Anyone who says Ram, Lakshman, or Sita's name makes the horses whinny and look lovingly that way. How can the horses' longing be described? They are as distressed as a snake without its jewel.
essence: Longing can make even the body answer a beloved name.
simple_meaning: The horses are so overcome by separation from Ram, Lakshman, and Sita that even hearing their names makes them turn and whinny with longing.
insight: It turns a passing scene into proof that separation is felt physically, not just mentally.
modern_relevance: You hear a song tied to someone you lost, and your chest tightens before you can think. Memory can pull the body toward what the heart still misses.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भयउ निषादु बिषादबस देखत सचिव तुरंग। बोलि सुसेवक चारि तब दिए सारथी संग ॥
translation: मंत्री और घोड़ों की यह दशा देखकर निषादराज विषाद के वश हो गया। तब उसने अपने चार उत्तम सेवक बुलाकर सारथी के साथ कर दिए ॥
english_translation: Seeing his minister and the horses in such a state, Nishadraj was overcome with sorrow. Then he called four of his best servants and sent them along with the charioteer.
essence: Compassion becomes real when grief turns into help.
simple_meaning: Seeing the grief around him, Nishadraj is moved to sorrow and sends four trusted servants with the charioteer.
insight: It shifts attention from feeling sympathy to offering practical support immediately.
modern_relevance: You see a friend leaving in tears, and without asking for thanks you quietly arrange the ride, the bag, the help they need. Grief often reveals who will act first.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गुह सारथिहि फिरेउ पहुँचाई। बिरहु बिषादु बरनि नहिं जाई॥ चले अवध लेइ रथहि निषादा। होहिं छनहिं छन मगन बिषादा ॥
translation: निषादराज गुह सारथी (सुमंत्रजी) को पहुँचाकर (विदा करके) लौटा। उसके विरह और दुःख का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। वे चारों निषाद रथ लेकर अवध को चले। (सुमंत्र और घोड़ों को देख-देखकर) वे भी क्षण-क्षणभर विषाद में डूबे जाते थे ॥
english_translation: Guh returned after seeing Sumantra off. His grief and sorrow cannot be described. The four Nishadas took the chariot toward Ayodhya, and every moment they sank again into sadness.
essence: Separation changes the ones who help carry it.
simple_meaning: Guh sends Sumantra on his way and returns in grief. The Nishadas take the chariot toward Ayodhya, but their hearts keep sinking into sorrow.
insight: It shows how separation can linger in the body long after the farewell is over.
modern_relevance: You walk back from the station after dropping off someone you cared for deeply. The road home is the same, but every step feels heavier because the leaving has changed you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सोच सुमंत्र बिकल दुख दीना। धिग जीवन रघुबीर बिहीना॥ रहिहि न अंतहुँ अधम सरीरू। जसु न लहेउ बिछुरत रघुबीरू ॥
translation: व्याकुल और दुःख से दीन हुए सुमंत्रजी सोचते हैं कि श्री रघुवीर के बिना जीना धिक्कार है। आखिर यह अधम शरीर रहेगा तो है ही नहीं। अभी श्री रामचन्द्रजी के बिछुड़ते ही छूटकर इसने यश (क्यों) नहीं ले लिया ॥
english_translation: Sumantra, overwhelmed by sorrow, thinks life without Raghuvir is unbearable. This worthless body will not even last to the end; why did it not lose its fame the moment it was separated from Ram?
essence: Without Ram, even life feels like a burden.
simple_meaning: Sumantra is crushed by grief after Ram leaves. He feels life without Ram is unbearable and even this body feels worthless without that closeness.
insight: It names grief as a total loss of meaning, not just sadness. The mind begins to question whether life itself still has purpose.
modern_relevance: You drop someone at the airport and drive home in silence, replaying the last goodbye. The house is still yours, but it feels strangely uninhabited.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भए अजस अघ भाजन प्राना। कवन हेतु नहिं करत पयाना॥ अहह मंद मनु अवसर चूका। अजहुँ न हृदय होत दुइ टूका ॥
translation: ये प्राण अपयश और पाप के भाँडे हो गए। अब ये किस कारण कूच नहीं करते (निकलते नहीं)? हाय! नीच मन (बड़ा अच्छा) मौका चूक गया। अब भी तो हृदय के दो टुकड़े नहीं हो जाते! ॥
english_translation: These breaths have become vessels of disgrace and wrongdoing. Why do they not depart now? Alas, the foolish mind has missed the moment. Why is the heart not split in two even now?
essence: Missing the right moment can make life feel stained beyond repair.
simple_meaning: Sumantra is overwhelmed with regret. He feels his life has become stained by shame, and he laments that he missed the chance to act at the right moment.
insight: It captures the grief of failed timing and the self-blame that follows a missed duty.
modern_relevance: You replay the moment after the text was sent, the meeting ended, the chance passed. What hurts most is not the loss itself, but knowing you were there and still missed it.
speaker: Sumantra

verse_text: मीजि हाथ सिरु धुनि पछिताई। मनहुँ कृपन धन रासि गवाँई॥ बिरिद बाँधि बर बीरु कहाई। चलेउ समर जनु सुभट पराई ॥
translation: सुमंत्र हाथ मल-मलकर और सिर पीट-पीटकर पछताते हैं। मानो कोई कंजूस धन का खजाना खो बैठा हो। वे इस प्रकार चले मानो कोई बड़ा योद्धा वीर का बाना पहनकर और उत्तम शूरवीर कहलाकर युद्ध से भाग चला हो! ॥
english_translation: Sumantra wrings his hands and beats his head in regret, as if a miser had lost a treasure of wealth. Bound by duty and called a brave man, he went on like a great warrior who flees the battle.
essence: Missed duty turns courage into bitter shame.
simple_meaning: Sumantra is overwhelmed with regret. He feels as if he has lost something precious and has failed the honour of a great warrior.
insight: It captures the pain of recognising missed responsibility after the decisive moment has passed.
modern_relevance: You replay the conversation on the drive home and realise the chance is gone. The apology, the warning, the brave sentence you should have said — all of it arrives too late.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिप्र बिबेकी बेदबिद संमत साधु सुजाति। जिमि धोखें मदपान कर सचिव सोच तेहि भाँति ॥
translation: जैसे कोई विवेकशील, वेद का ज्ञाता, साधुसम्मत आचरणों वाला और उत्तम जाति का (कुलीन) ब्राह्मण धोखे से मदिरा पी ले और पीछे पछतावे, उसी प्रकार मंत्री सुमंत्र सोच कर रहे (पछता रहे) हैं ॥
english_translation: Like a discerning Brahmin, learned in the Vedas, praised by the good, and of noble conduct, who is tricked into drinking liquor and then regrets it, so Sumantra is filled with sorrow.
essence: Deep regret can feel like moral contamination after a helpless mistake.
simple_meaning: Sumantra’s grief is compared to the shame of a good, wise man who has been tricked into drinking alcohol and then feels deep regret.
insight: It frames grief as shame mixed with helplessness, not just sadness.
modern_relevance: You replay the conversation after the damage is done, wondering how you missed the warning signs. The pain is not only loss — it is the humiliation of realizing you were powerless to prevent it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जिमि कुलीन तिय साधु सयानी। पतिदेवता करम मन बानी॥ रहै करम बस परिहरि नाहू। सचिव हृदयँ तिमि दारुन दाहू ॥
translation: जैसे किसी उत्तम कुलवाली, साधु स्वाभाव की, समझदार और मन, वचन, कर्म से पति को ही देवता मानने वाली पतिव्रता स्त्री को भाग्यवश पति को छोड़कर (पति से अलग) रहना पड़े, उस समय उसके हृदय में जैसे भयानक संताप होता है, वैसे ही मंत्री के हृदय में हो रहा है ॥
english_translation: Like a noble, virtuous, wise wife who holds her husband as her only deity, yet must live apart from him by fate, the minister's heart burns with the same terrible pain.
essence: Separation from what you love can burn like fire inside the heart.
simple_meaning: The minister's grief is compared to a devoted wife forced to live away from her husband. It is a pain of separation, not just sadness.
insight: It turns separation into a bodily grief, making emotional loss feel real and unavoidable.
modern_relevance: You drop someone at the airport after a life-changing goodbye, then sit in the car unable to start it. The distance is physical, but the ache feels lodged in your chest.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लोचन सजल डीठि भइ थोरी। सुनइ न श्रवन बिकल मति भोरी॥ सूखहिं अधर लागि मुहँ लाटी। जिउ न जाइ उर अवधि कपाटी ॥
translation: नेत्रों में जल भरा है, दृष्टि मंद हो गई है। कानों से सुनाई नहीं पड़ता, व्याकुल हुई बुद्धि बेठिकाने हो रही है। होठ सूख रहे हैं, मुँह में लाटी लग गई है, किन्तु (ये सब मृत्यु के लक्षण हो जाने पर भी) प्राण नहीं निकलते, क्योंकि हृदय में अवधि रूपी किवाड़ लगे हैं (अर्थात चौदह वर्ष बीत जाने पर भगवान फिर मिलेंगे, यही आशा रुकावट डाल रही है) ॥
english_translation: Tears fill the eyes and the gaze grows dim. Hearing fails, the mind grows unsteady and confused. The lips dry up and the mouth goes slack, yet life does not leave the body, because the doors of the heart are held shut by the hope that fourteen years will pass and Ram will return.
essence: Hope can keep the heart closed against surrender.
simple_meaning: Sumantra is so overwhelmed by grief that his body shows signs of death, yet he cannot die because he still hopes to see Ram after the exile ends.
insight: It shows how longing can suspend collapse, keeping a person alive through sheer expectation.
modern_relevance: You sit in a hospital corridor at 3 a.m., staring at a phone that still hasn’t rung. Your body feels spent, but one small hope keeps you from collapsing completely.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिबरन भयउ न जाइ निहारी। मारेसि मनहुँ पिता महतारी॥ हानि गलानि बिपुल मन ब्यापी। जमपुर पंथ सोच जिमि पापी ॥
translation: सुमंत्रजी के मुख का रंग बदल गया है, जो देखा नहीं जाता। ऐसा मालूम होता है मानो इन्होंने माता-पिता को मार डाला हो। उनके मन में रामवियोग रूपी हानि की महान ग्लानि (पीड़ा) छा रही है, जैसे कोई पापी मनुष्य नरक को जाता हुआ रास्ते में सोच कर रहा हो ॥
english_translation: Sumantra's face changed so much it could not be looked at. It was as if he had killed his own parents. A deep sense of loss and shame filled his mind, like a sinner walking toward the lower realm and thinking of his fate.
essence: Loyalty can hurt so deeply it feels like guilt.
simple_meaning: Sumantra is overwhelmed with grief and shame after leaving Ram behind. His face looks unrecognisable, as if he has committed the worst possible act.
insight: It shows how love can turn into self-reproach when duty forces separation.
modern_relevance: You come home after dropping someone at the airport and sit in the car for ten minutes, unable to start the engine. The silence feels like you failed them, even though you did everything you could.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बचनु न आव हृदयँ पछिताई। अवध काह मैं देखब जाई॥ राम रहित रथ देखिहि जोई। सकुचिहि मोहि बिलोकत सोई ॥
translation: मुँह से वचन नहीं निकलते। हृदय में पछताते हैं कि मैं अयोध्या में जाकर क्या देखूँगा? श्री रामचन्द्रजी से शून्य रथ को जो भी देखेगा, वही मुझे देखने में संकोच करेगा (अर्थात मेरा मुँह नहीं देखना चाहेगा) ॥
english_translation: No words come to his mouth; his heart is full of regret: what will I see if I go to Ayodhya? Whoever sees the chariot without Ram will shrink back from looking at me.
essence: Grief can make you feel unworthy to face the people you love.
simple_meaning: Sumantra is overwhelmed with shame and grief. He feels he cannot return to Ayodhya or face anyone there after bringing back a chariot without Ram.
insight: It shows how grief can make you fear the very people who care about you most.
modern_relevance: You come home after failing to protect someone who trusted you, and the silence in the car feels heavier than any explanation. That is Sumantra's pain.
speaker: Sumantra

verse_text: धाइ पूँछिहहिं मोहि जब बिकल नगर नर नारि। उतरु देब मैं सबहि तब हृदयँ बज्रु बैठारि ॥
translation: नगर के सब व्याकुल स्त्री-पुरुष जब दौड़कर मुझसे पूछेंगे, तब मैं हृदय पर वज्र रखकर सबको उत्तर दूँगा ॥
english_translation: When the anxious men and women of the city rush to ask me, I will answer them with a heart like steel.
essence: A heavy heart still has to speak clearly.
simple_meaning: Sumantra knows the people of Ayodhya will ask him what happened. He steels himself to answer their painful questions.
insight: It teaches you to face painful responsibility directly instead of avoiding the people who need the truth.
modern_relevance: You walk into a house after bad news has spread, and everyone turns to you first. You know the questions are coming, and you brace yourself to answer with care.
speaker: Sumantra

verse_text: पुछिहहिं दीन दुखित सब माता। कहब काह मैं तिन्हहि बिधाता। पूछिहि जबहिं लखन महतारी। कहिहउँ कवन सँदेस सुखारी ॥
translation: जब दीन-दुःखी सब माताएँ पूछेंगी, तब हे विधाता! मैं उन्हें क्या कहूँगा? जब लक्ष्मणजी की माता मुझसे पूछेंगी, तब मैं उन्हें कौन सा सुखदायी सँदेसा कहूँगा? ॥
english_translation: When all the grieving mothers ask me, what can I tell them, O Creator? When Lakshman's mother asks me, what comforting message can I give her?
essence: Some news is so painful that silence feels kinder than speech.
simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed by grief. He imagines the mothers in Ayodhya asking about Ram and Lakshman, and he cannot think of any answer that would not break their hearts.
insight: It shows how love makes you measure every word against another person's pain.
modern_relevance: You rehearse the conversation in the car before walking into the house, knowing a mother is waiting for news you cannot make gentle.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: राम जननि जब आइहि धाई। सुमिरि बच्छु जिमि धेनु लवाई॥ पूँछत उतरु देब मैं तेही। गे बनु राम लखनु बैदेही ॥
translation: श्री रामजी की माता जब इस प्रकार दौड़ी आवेंगी जैसे नई ब्यायी हुई गौ बछड़े को याद करके दौड़ी आती है, तब उनके पूछने पर मैं उन्हें यह उत्तर दूँगा कि श्री राम, लक्ष्मण, सीता वन को चले गए! ॥
english_translation: When Ram's mother comes running, remembering her calf like a cow that has just given birth, I will answer her: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita have gone to the forest.
essence: Honesty can demand the courage to wound someone you love.
simple_meaning: Bharat knows Ram's mother will rush to ask where her sons have gone. He prepares himself to answer honestly, even though the truth will be unbearable.
insight: It trains you to face painful conversation without hiding behind delay, excuses, or half-truths.
modern_relevance: You rehearse the phone call before you make it, knowing the other person will ask where they are. The truth is simple, but saying it cleanly takes everything you have.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जोई पूँछिहि तेहि ऊतरु देबा। जाइ अवध अब यहु सुखु लेबा॥ पूँछिहि जबहिं राउ दुख दीना। जिवनु जासु रघुनाथ अधीना ॥
translation: जो भी पूछेगा उसे यही उत्तर देना पड़ेगा! हाय! अयोध्या जाकर अब मुझे यही सुख लेना है! जब दुःख से दीन महाराज, जिनका जीवन श्री रघुनाथजी के (दर्शन के) ही अधीन है, मुझसे पूछेंगे, ॥
english_translation: Whoever asks, I will have to give the same answer. Alas, after reaching Ayodhya, I must take this sorrow as my only comfort. When grief-stricken King Dasharath asks me, whose life depends on Raghunath, ...
essence: Some answers are unavoidable, even when they reopen grief.
simple_meaning: He knows he will have to answer everyone in Ayodhya, especially Dasharath, and that the answer will bring only pain.
insight: It frames the return not as relief, but as the burden of reporting unbearable news.
modern_relevance: You rehearse the conversation on the drive home, knowing someone will ask the question you cannot soften. The answer is true, but it will hurt the one who hears it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देहउँ उतरु कौनु मुहु लाई। आयउँ कुसल कुअँर पहुँचाई॥ सुनत लखन सिय राम सँदेसू। तृन जिमि तनु परिहरिहि नरेसू ॥
translation: तब मैं कौन सा मुँह लेकर उन्हें उत्तर दूँगा कि मैं राजकुमारों को कुशल पूर्वक पहुँचा आया हूँ! लक्ष्मण, सीता और श्रीराम का समाचार सुनते ही महाराज तिनके की तरह शरीर को त्याग देंगे ॥
english_translation: Then what face would I have to answer with, saying I have safely brought the princes here? Hearing news of Lakshman, Sita, and Ram, the king will leave his body like a blade of grass.
essence: Grief can be so deep that even good news becomes unbearable.
simple_meaning: The speaker fears that reporting the safe return of Ram, Sita, and Lakshman will overwhelm the king with grief and make him give up his body.
insight: It shows how grief can make even joy feel dangerous, and how love can exhaust the body before the mind can recover.
modern_relevance: You finally call with the update everyone prayed for, but the person on the other end has already been shattered by waiting. Even relief can land like a blow.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: हृदउ न बिदरेउ पंक जिमि बिछुरत प्रीतमु नीरु। जानत हौं मोहि दीन्ह बिधि यहु जातना सरीरु ॥
translation: प्रियतम (श्री रामजी) रूपी जल के बिछुड़ते ही मेरा हृदय कीचड़ की तरह फट नहीं गया, इससे मैं जानता हूँ कि विधाता ने मुझे यह 'यातना शरीर' ही दिया है (जो पापी जीवों को नरक भोगने के लिए मिलता है) ॥
english_translation: My heart did not split like mud when my beloved was taken away. I know the creator gave me this torment-body.
essence: Enduring separation reveals how much pain the body can hold.
simple_meaning: Sumantra says his heart did not shatter when Ram left, so he knows he has been given a body made for suffering.
insight: It shifts grief from private failure to a burden the body is simply carrying.
modern_relevance: You watched a train pull away after saying goodbye to someone who changed your life. Your chest stayed intact, but only just. This verse names that strange survival.
speaker: Sumantra

verse_text: एहि बिधि करत पंथ पछितावा। तमसा तीर तुरत रथु आवा॥ बिदा किए करि बिनय निषादा। फिरे पायँ परि बिकल बिषादा ॥
translation: सुमंत्र इस प्रकार मार्ग में पछतावा कर रहे थे, इतने में ही रथ तुरंत तमसा नदी के तट पर आ पहुँचा। मंत्री ने विनय करके चारों निषादों को विदा किया। वे विषाद से व्याकुल होते हुए सुमंत्र के पैरों पड़कर लौटे ॥
english_translation: In this way, Sumantra kept regretting along the road. Soon the chariot reached the bank of the Tamasa river. The minister politely bade farewell to the Nishadas, and they returned, overcome with sorrow, falling at his feet.
essence: Departure can be polite and still break the heart.
simple_meaning: Sumantra travels in regret, reaches the Tamasa bank, gently dismisses the Nishadas, and they return in deep sorrow.
insight: It keeps the focus on the emotional cost of separation, not the logistics of travel.
modern_relevance: You wave goodbye after dropping someone at the station, but the car feels unbearably quiet on the drive home. Everyone has said enough, yet nobody feels finished.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पैठत नगर सचिव सकुचाई। जनु मारेसि गुर बाँभन गाई॥ बैठि बिटप तर दिवसु गवाँवा। साँझ समय तब अवसरु पावा ॥
translation: नगर में प्रवेश करते मंत्री (ग्लानि के कारण) ऐसे सकुचाते हैं, मानो गुरु, ब्राह्मण या गौ को मारकर आए हों। सारा दिन एक पेड़ के नीचे बैठकर बिताया। जब संध्या हुई तब मौका मिला ॥
english_translation: The minister entered the city in shame, as if he had killed his teacher, a Brahmin, or a cow. He spent the whole day under a tree. Only at dusk did he find the chance.
essence: Shame can make even coming home feel impossible.
simple_meaning: The minister feels deep shame on returning to Ayodhya. He stays hidden under a tree all day and waits until evening to enter the city.
insight: It shows how guilt can make a person delay even the simplest action.
modern_relevance: You come home after delivering news that changed everything, and you sit in your car for an hour before walking inside. Some truths make even ordinary entrances feel unbearable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अवध प्रबेसु कीन्ह अँधिआरें। पैठ भवन रथु राखि दुआरें॥ जिन्ह जिन्ह समाचार सुनि पाए। भूप द्वार रथु देखन आए ॥
translation: अँधेरा होने पर उन्होंने अयोध्या में प्रवेश किया और रथ को दरवाजे पर खड़ा करके वे (चुपके से) महल में घुसे। जिन-जिन लोगों ने यह समाचार सुना पाया, वे सभी रथ देखने को राजद्वार पर आए ॥
english_translation: At dusk they entered Ayodhya, left the chariot at the gate, and slipped into the palace. Whoever heard the news came to the royal gate to see the chariot.
essence: A hidden arrival can announce a wound before any words are spoken.
simple_meaning: They reached Ayodhya at night, left the chariot at the gate, and went inside quietly. Hearing the news, people came to see the chariot at the royal door.
insight: It shifts attention from action to atmosphere: even ordinary objects can carry grief, shock, and unspoken news.
modern_relevance: You pull into the driveway after a hard night and switch off the engine before anyone sees you. The silence itself tells the house that something has changed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रथु पहिचानि बिकल लखि घोरे। गरहिं गात जिमि आतप ओरे॥ नगर नारि नर ब्याकुल कैसें। निघटत नीर मीनगन जैसें ॥
translation: रथ को पहचानकर और घोड़ों को व्याकुल देखकर उनके शरीर ऐसे गले जा रहे हैं (क्षीण हो रहे हैं) जैसे घाम में ओले! नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष कैसे व्याकुल हैं, जैसे जल के घटने पर मछलियाँ (व्याकुल होती हैं) ॥
english_translation: Recognizing the chariot and seeing the horses agitated, their bodies seemed to melt like hail in the sun. How distraught the men and women of the city were, like fish when the water level drops.
essence: A whole city can feel grief before it is told.
simple_meaning: The city instantly senses that something terrible has happened. People grow pale with fear and confusion, like fish trapped as water dries up.
insight: It shows how atmosphere can carry truth faster than speech, turning a city into one trembling body.
modern_relevance: You hear the ambulance outside before anyone explains. The room changes at once, because everyone feels what is coming before the words arrive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सचिव आगमनु सुनत सबु बिकल भयउ रनिवासु। भवनु भयंकरु लाग तेहि मानहुँ प्रेत निवासु ॥
translation: मंत्री का (अकेले ही) आना सुनकर सारा रनिवास व्याकुल हो गया। राजमहल उनको ऐसा भयानक लगा मानो प्रेतों का निवास स्थान (श्मशान) हो ॥
english_translation: Hearing that the minister had come alone, the entire women’s quarters was thrown into distress. The palace seemed so dreadful to them, as if it were a dwelling of ghosts.
essence: Fear can turn home into a place of haunting.
simple_meaning: When the minister arrived alone, everyone in the women’s quarters panicked. The palace itself felt like a place of death and dread.
insight: It shows how dread spreads through a place before any facts are spoken.
modern_relevance: You hear one knock at the door late at night, and your stomach drops before anyone speaks. Sometimes the room changes before the news does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अति आरति सब पूँछहिं रानी। उतरु न आव बिकल भइ बानी॥ सुनइ न श्रवन नयन नहिं सूझा। कहहु कहाँ नृपु तेहि तेहि बूझा ॥
translation: अत्यन्त आर्त होकर सब रानियाँ पूछती हैं, पर सुमंत्र को कुछ उत्तर नहीं आता, उनकी वाणी विकल हो गई (रुक गई) है। न कानों से सुनाई पड़ता है और न आँखों से कुछ सूझता है। वे जो भी सामने आता है उस-उससे पूछते हैं कहो, राजा कहाँ हैं ? ॥
