english_translation: In deep anguish, all the queens keep asking, but Sumantra cannot answer; his speech fails him. He cannot hear, cannot see clearly, and asks everyone he meets, 'Where is the king?'
essence: Shock steals speech and leaves only one question.
simple_meaning: The queens are desperate for news, but Sumantra is too shaken to answer. He keeps asking everyone where King Dasharath is.
insight: It shows how shock breaks communication and turns the mind into repeated searching.
modern_relevance: You get the call no one wanted to make, and suddenly your words vanish. You know something terrible has happened, but your mind keeps circling the same question.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दासिन्ह दीख सचिव बिकलाई। कौसल्या गृहँ गईं लवाई॥ जाइ सुमंत्र दीख कस राजा। अमिअ रहित जनु चंदु बिराजा ॥
translation: दासियाँ मंत्री को व्याकुल देखकर उन्हें कौसल्याजी के महल में लिवा गईं। सुमंत्र ने जाकर वहाँ राजा को कैसा (बैठे) देखा मानो बिना अमृत का चन्द्रमा हो ॥
english_translation: The servants saw the minister in distress and took him to Kaushalya's chamber. Sumantra went and saw the king there, like the moon shining without nectar.
essence: Grief can strip even a king of all radiance.
simple_meaning: The servants noticed Sumantra's distress and brought him to Kaushalya. There he saw the king looking drained and sorrowful, like the moon stripped of its nectar.
insight: It prepares the mind to see grief not as weakness, but as visible depletion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आसन सयन बिभूषन हीना। परेउ भूमितल निपट मलीना॥ लेइ उसासु सोच एहि भाँती। सुरपुर तें जनु खँसेउ जजाती ॥
translation: राजा आसन, शय्या और आभूषणों से रहित बिलकुल मलिन (उदास) पृथ्वी पर पड़े हुए हैं। वे लंबी साँसें लेकर इस प्रकार सोच करते हैं, मानो राजा ययाति स्वर्ग से गिरकर सोच कर रहे हों ॥
english_translation: Deprived of seat, bed, and ornaments, the king lay on the bare ground, utterly dull. Drawing long breaths, he brooded like Yayati fallen from heaven.
essence: Sorrow can bring a king down to the ground.
simple_meaning: The king is lying on the ground in grief, stripped of comfort and dignity. He keeps sighing and sinking into sorrow as if he has fallen from a heavenly height.
insight: It shifts attention from royal status to the physical truth of grief: the body itself can collapse under sorrow.
modern_relevance: You sit on the bedroom floor after the worst phone call of your life, unable to reach the bed. Even dignity feels too heavy to carry.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लेत सोच भरि छिनु छिनु छाती। जनु जरि पंख परेउ संपाती॥ राम राम कह राम सनेही। पुनि कह राम लखन बैदेही ॥
translation: राजा क्षण-क्षण में सोच से छाती भर लेते हैं। ऐसी विकल दशा है मानो (गीध राज जटायु का भाई) सम्पाती पंखों के जल जाने पर गिर पड़ा हो। राजा (बार-बार) 'राम, राम' 'हा स्नेही (प्यारे) राम!' कहते हैं, फिर 'हा राम, हा लक्ष्मण, हा जानकी' ऐसा कहने लगते हैं॥4
english_translation: Moment by moment, grief fills the king's chest. He is like Sampati fallen after his wings were burned. He keeps crying, 'Ram, Ram, my beloved Ram,' and then, 'Ram, Lakshman, Sita.'
essence: Grief keeps calling the names it cannot bear to lose.
simple_meaning: Dasharath is overwhelmed with grief and keeps calling out the names of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita.
insight: It shows how loss narrows attention to repeated, aching remembrance.
modern_relevance: You stare at your phone after a message you can't undo, and your chest keeps tightening. The mind keeps returning to the names it misses.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि सचिवँ जय जीव कहि कीन्हेउ दंड प्रनामु। सुनत उठेउ ब्याकुल नृपति कहु सुमंत्र कहँ रामु ॥
translation: मंत्री ने देखकर 'जयजीव' कहकर दण्डवत् प्रणाम किया। सुनते ही राजा व्याकुल होकर उठे और बोले- सुमंत्र! कहो, राम कहाँ हैं ? ॥
english_translation: The minister saw him, bowed fully, and said, "Victory to the living." Hearing this, the king rose in distress and asked Sumantra, "Where is Ram?"
essence: Separation turns every moment into a search.
simple_meaning: Sumantra bows to Dasharath, and the king immediately rises in anguish, asking where Ram is.
insight: It shows how grief makes the mind circle back to the one it has lost.
modern_relevance: You hear a name in a crowded room and your chest tightens before you can stop it. Some absences stay so alive that every small reminder opens them again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूप सुमंत्रु लीन्ह उर लाई। बूड़त कछु अधार जनु पाई॥ सहित सनेह निकट बैठारी। पूँछत राउ नयन भरि बारी ॥
translation: राजा ने सुमंत्र को हृदय से लगा लिया। मानो डूबते हुए आदमी को कुछ सहारा मिल गया हो। मंत्री को स्नेह के साथ पास बैठाकर नेत्रों में जल भरकर राजा पूछने लगे- ॥
english_translation: The king clasped Sumantra to his heart, as if a drowning man had found a little support. Seating the minister nearby with affection, the king asked with tears in his eyes.
essence: Grief reaches for closeness before it can ask for news.
simple_meaning: Dasharath pulls Sumantra close like a drowning man grabbing support. He seats him beside him with love and, through tears, asks about Ram.
insight: It shows how sorrow seeks immediate human support before it can even ask its question.
modern_relevance: You get the call that changes everything, and your first instinct is to hold on to the nearest trusted person. Before answers, you need a witness to your pain.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम कुसल कहु सखा सनेही। कहँ रघुनाथु लखनु बैदेही॥ आने फेरि कि बनहि सिधाए। सुनत सचिव लोचन जल छाए ॥
translation: हे मेरे प्रेमी सखा! श्री राम की कुशल कहो। बताओ, श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और जानकी कहाँ हैं? उन्हें लौटा लाए हो कि वे वन को चले गए? यह सुनते ही मंत्री के नेत्रों में जल भर आया ॥
english_translation: Tell me, my dear friend, how is Ram? Where are Raghunath, Lakshman, and Sita? Have you brought them back, or have they gone to the forest again? Hearing this, the minister's eyes filled with tears.
essence: Love makes a king ask like a frightened child.
simple_meaning: Dasharath anxiously asks Sumantra whether Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are safe and whether they have returned or gone back to the forest. The question overwhelms Sumantra with tears.
insight: It shifts attention from royal authority to raw attachment, showing how grief strips away status.
modern_relevance: You refresh your phone after a long silence, hoping for one name to appear. The question is simple, but your whole chest is already answering it.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: सोक बिकल पुनि पूँछ नरेसू। कहु सिय राम लखन संदेसू॥ राम रूप गुन सील सुभाऊ। सुमिरि सुमिरि उर सोचत राऊ ॥
translation: शोक से व्याकुल होकर राजा फिर पूछने लगे- सीता, राम और लक्ष्मण का संदेशा तो कहो। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के रूप, गुण, शील और स्वभाव को याद कर-करके राजा हृदय में सोच करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Overcome with grief, the king asks again, "Tell me the message from Sita, Ram, and Lakshman." Remembering Ram's beauty, virtues, character, and nature again and again, the king keeps grieving in his heart.
essence: Love remembered in grief only deepens the wound.
simple_meaning: The king is overwhelmed with grief and keeps asking for news of Ram, Sita, and Lakshman. As he remembers Ram's beauty and virtues, his sorrow deepens.
insight: It shows how love and loss can keep the mind returning to the same ache.
modern_relevance: You keep reopening the chat thread, hoping for one more message from someone you miss. The memory itself is both comfort and wound.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राउ सुनाइ दीन्ह बनबासू। सुनि मन भयउ न हरषु हराँसू॥ सो सुत बिछुरत गए न प्राना। को पापी बड़ मोहि समाना ॥
translation: (और कहते हैं-) मैंने राजा होने की बात सुनाकर वनवास दे दिया, यह सुनकर भी जिस (राम) के मन में हर्ष और विषाद नहीं हुआ, ऐसे पुत्र के बिछुड़ने पर भी मेरे प्राण नहीं गए, तब मेरे समान बड़ा पापी कौन होगा ? ॥
english_translation: I told him he was exiled to the forest. Even then, his mind held neither joy nor sorrow. But when my son was separated from me, my life did not leave me. Who is more sinful than I?
essence: Ram stayed steady; Dasharath's suffering reveals his own brokenness.
simple_meaning: Dasharath admits that Ram accepted exile without emotional disturbance, while Dasharath himself cannot bear separation from his son and calls himself deeply blameworthy.
insight: It turns grief into moral self-recognition instead of self-pity.
modern_relevance: You sign the transfer letter that sends your child away, then sit in the quiet house and feel the cost in your chest. Sometimes the deepest pain is not punishment — it is seeing what your own choices have done.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: सखा रामु सिय लखनु जहँ तहाँ मोहि पहुँचाउ। नाहिं त चाहत चलन अब प्रान कहउँ सतिभाउ ॥
translation: हे सखा! श्री राम, जानकी और लक्ष्मण जहाँ हैं, मुझे भी वहीं पहुँचा दो। नहीं तो मैं सत्य भाव से कहता हूँ कि मेरे प्राण अब चलना ही चाहते हैं ॥
english_translation: O friend, take me to wherever Rama, Sita, and Lakshman are. Otherwise, I tell you in all sincerity, my life no longer wishes to continue.
essence: Separation from what you love can make life itself feel unwanted.
simple_meaning: Dasharath says he wants to be taken to Rama, Sita, and Lakshman immediately. If that cannot happen, he feels ready to let his life end.
insight: It shows how longing can overtake the will to continue and how attachment reshapes the body’s own energy.
modern_relevance: You stare at a phone that never lights up with the message you need. After enough silence, even ordinary hours can feel too heavy to carry.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: पुनि पुनि पूँछत मंत्रिहि राऊ। प्रियतम सुअन सँदेस सुनाऊ॥ करहि सखा सोइ बेगि उपाऊ। रामु लखनु सिय नयन देखाऊ ॥
translation: राजा बार-बार मंत्री से पूछते हैं- मेरे प्रियतम पुत्रों का संदेशा सुनाओ। हे सखा! तुम तुरंत वही उपाय करो जिससे श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीता को मुझे आँखों दिखा दो ॥
english_translation: The king kept asking the minister again and again, “Tell me news of my beloved sons. My friend, quickly find some way to let me see Ram, Lakshman, and Sita with my own eyes.”
essence: Separation makes even a king plead like a child.
simple_meaning: Dasharath keeps asking for news of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, and begs for a way to see them with his own eyes.
insight: It shows how grief narrows the mind to one impossible wish: just let me see them again.
modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone for one message from someone you miss. You don't want advice — you want their face, their voice, their presence.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: सचिव धीर धरि कह मृदु बानी। महाराज तुम्ह पंडित ग्यानी॥ बीर सुधीर धुरंधर देवा। साधु समाजु सदा तुम्ह सेवा ॥
translation: मंत्री धीरज धरकर कोमल वाणी बोले- महाराज! आप पंडित और ज्ञानी हैं। हे देव! आप शूरवीर तथा उत्तम धैर्यवान पुरुषों में श्रेष्ठ हैं। आपने सदा साधुओं के समाज की सेवा की है ॥
english_translation: The minister, steadying himself, spoke gently: "Maharaj, you are learned and wise. O noble one, you are a hero, steadfast and foremost among the brave. You have always served the company of saints."
essence: Gentle words can steady a heart already breaking.
simple_meaning: The minister speaks gently and praises the king as wise, brave, steady, and devoted to serving holy people.
insight: It teaches you to meet someone’s suffering with calm respect and affirming speech.
modern_relevance: A parent in tears still needs someone to speak with care, not panic. The right words do not erase pain, but they can hold it without making it worse.
speaker: Minister

verse_text: जनम मरन सब दुख सुख भोगा। हानि लाभु प्रिय मिलन बियोगा॥ काल करम बस होहिं गोसाईं। बरबस राति दिवस की नाईं ॥
translation: जन्म-मरण, सुख-दुःख के भोग, हानि-लाभ, प्यारों का मिलना-बिछुड़ना, ये सब हे स्वामी! काल और कर्म के अधीन रात और दिन की तरह बरबस होते रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Birth and death, the experience of pleasure and pain, loss and gain, meeting and parting from loved ones — all of this, O Lord, happens helplessly under time and action, like night and day.
essence: Everything you gain and lose is carried by time, not by your control.
simple_meaning: Life brings birth, death, joy, sorrow, gain, loss, meeting, and separation. All of it happens under the force of time and action, not personal control.
insight: It shifts the mind from resisting change to seeing it as part of the natural order, which makes steadiness possible.
modern_relevance: You get the call that a job offer vanished, the relationship changed, or a loved one moved away. The mind wants someone to blame, but this verse points to a larger pattern: change is built into life itself.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुख हरषहिं जड़ दुख बिलखाहीं। दोउ सम धीर धरहिं मन माहीं॥ धीरज धरहु बिबेकु बिचारी। छाड़िअ सोच सकल हितकारी ॥
translation: मूर्ख लोग सुख में हर्षित होते और दुःख में रोते हैं, पर धीर पुरुष अपने मन में दोनों को समान समझते हैं। हे सबके हितकारी (रक्षक)! आप विवेक विचारकर धीरज धरिए और शोक का परित्याग कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Fools rejoice in pleasure and weep in sorrow. The steadfast keep both equal in their minds. O protector of all, think wisely, hold firm, and abandon all grief.
essence: Steady minds are not shaken by pleasure or pain.
simple_meaning: Most people get carried away by happiness and sadness. A wise person stays steady through both and lets go of grief after thinking clearly.
insight: It shifts attention from emotional reaction to steady discernment.
modern_relevance: You get a praise email in the morning and a harsh message by noon. The mind wants to soar, then crash. This verse teaches you to stay even through both.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: प्रथम बासु तमसा भयउ दूसर सुरसरि तीर। न्हाइ रहे जलपानु करि सिय समेत दोउ बीर ॥
translation: श्री रामजी का पहला निवास (मुकाम) तमसा के तट पर हुआ, दूसरा गंगातीर पर। सीताजी सहित दोनों भाई उस दिन स्नान करके जल पीकर ही रहे ॥
english_translation: Their first stop was on the bank of the Tamsa River; their second was on the bank of the Ganga. Ram, Sita, and both brothers bathed and drank water before resting there.
essence: Even exile begins with ordinary stops and a little water.
simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and the two brothers paused at two riverbanks on their journey, bathing and resting there.
insight: It reminds you that major transitions unfold through simple, bodily moments of rest and movement.
modern_relevance: You leave home with a heavy heart, stop by a roadside river, wash your face, drink water, and keep going. Even sacred journeys still need ordinary pauses.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: केवट कीन्हि बहुत सेवकाई। सो जामिनि सिंगरौर गवाँई॥ होत प्रात बट छीरु मगावा। जटा मुकुट निज सीस बनावा ॥
translation: केवट (निषादराज) ने बहुत सेवा की। वह रात सिंगरौर (श्रृंगवेरपुर) में ही बिताई। दूसरे दिन सबेरा होते ही बड़ का दूध मँगवाया और उससे श्री राम-लक्ष्मण ने अपने सिरों पर जटाओं के मुकुट बनाए ॥
english_translation: Kevat rendered much service. He spent that night in Singraur. At dawn he brought banyan milk, and Ram and Lakshman made crowns of matted hair for their heads.
essence: Service turns an ordinary night into devotion.
simple_meaning: Kevat serves Ram and Lakshman with care, stays with them through the night, and helps them prepare simple crowns of matted hair at dawn.
insight: It shows how humble service supports sacred duty without asking for recognition.
modern_relevance: You stay up late helping a guest settle in, then wake early to make breakfast before they leave. No applause, no ceremony — just care offered cleanly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम सखाँ तब नाव मगाई। प्रिया चढ़ाई चढ़े रघुराई॥ लखन बान धनु धरे बनाई। आपु चढ़े प्रभु आयसु पाई ॥
translation: तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी के सखा निषादराज ने नाव मँगवाई। पहले प्रिया सीताजी को उस पर चढ़ाकर फिर श्री रघुनाथजी चढ़े। फिर लक्ष्मणजी ने धनुष-बाण सजाकर रखे और प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी की आज्ञा पाकर स्वयं चढ़े ॥
english_translation: Then Ram's friend had the boat brought. First he helped Sita board it, and then Raghunath climbed aboard. Lakshman, with bow and arrows ready, boarded only after receiving the Lord's command.
essence: True service knows who goes first and who waits.
simple_meaning: Nishadraj brings a boat, Sita boards first, then Ram, and Lakshman follows only after the Lord's command, with weapons ready.
insight: It teaches you to serve with precision, protect without drama, and wait for the right command before acting.
modern_relevance: You're helping someone move in the rain, carrying the heavier box, making sure the most vulnerable person goes first. Real care is practical, ordered, and attentive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिकल बिलोकि मोहि रघुबीरा। बोले मधुर बचन धरि धीरा॥ तात प्रनामु तात सन कहेहू। बार बार पद पंकज गहेहू ॥
translation: मुझे व्याकुल देखकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी धीरज धरकर मधुर वचन बोले- हे तात! पिताजी से मेरा प्रणाम कहना और मेरी ओर से बार-बार उनके चरण कमल पकड़ना ॥
english_translation: Seeing me distraught, Raghuvira spoke gentle words with composure: “Father, offer my salutations to our father, and again and again hold his lotus feet for me.”
essence: Composure can carry love even through painful departure.
simple_meaning: Ram sees the pain around him and still speaks gently. Even at the edge of exile, he asks Lakshman to carry his reverence to their father.
insight: It teaches you to keep respect alive even in separation and distress.
modern_relevance: You are leaving home after a fight, and your voice could easily turn sharp. Instead, you choose the calm sentence that protects the relationship.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: करबि पायँ परि बिनय बहोरी। तात करिअ जनि चिंता मोरी॥ बन मग मंगल कुसल हमारें। कृपा अनुग्रह पुन्य तुम्हारें ॥
translation: फिर पाँव पकड़कर विनती करना कि हे पिताजी! आप मेरी चिंता न कीजिए। आपकी कृपा, अनुग्रह और पुण्य से वन में और मार्ग में हमारा कुशल-मंगल होगा ॥
english_translation: Then bow at his feet again and say, 'Father, do not worry about me. By your grace, favor, and merit, we will be safe in the forest and on the road.'
essence: True care sends others forward without burdening them with fear.
simple_meaning: Ram asks Dasharath not to worry. He says the forest journey will be safe through his father's grace and merit.
insight: It shifts concern into blessing: instead of clinging anxiously, you send the person forward with trust.
modern_relevance: You’re dropping someone at the airport after a hard goodbye, trying not to show how scared you are for them. Their calm voice steadies you more than your own worry ever could.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तुम्हरें अनुग्रह तात कानन जात सब सुखु पाइहौं। प्रतिपालि आयसु कुसल देखन पाय पुनि फिरि आइहौं॥ जननीं सकल परितोषि परि परि पायँ करि बिनती घनी। तुलसी करहु सोइ जतनु जेहिं कुसली रहहिं कोसलधनी॥
translation: हे पिताजी! आपके अनुग्रह से मैं वन जाते हुए सब प्रकार का सुख पाऊँगा। आज्ञा का भलीभाँति पालन करके चरणों का दर्शन करने कुशल पूर्वक फिर लौट आऊँगा। सब माताओं के पैरों पड़-पड़कर उनका समाधान करके और उनसे बहुत विनती करके तुलसीदास कहते हैं- तुम वही प्रयत्न करना, जिसमें कोसलपति पिताजी कुशल रहें।
english_translation: By your grace, father, I will find all happiness in the forest. By faithfully obeying your command, I will return safely to see you again. After comforting all the mothers and bowing again and again at their feet, Tulsidas says: do whatever ensures that the lord of Kosala remains well.
essence: True obedience protects the one who gave the command.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Dasharath that, by his blessing, exile will still be bearable and he will return safely after obeying his command. He also asks that every effort be made to keep Dasharath well.
insight: It teaches you to carry out a painful duty without adding fear to someone else's heart.
modern_relevance: You leave the hospital after a hard conversation, then text your family that you are okay so they can breathe. Sometimes the kindest obedience is not dramatic — it is steady, reassuring, and focused on the other person's well-being.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: गुर सन कहब सँदेसु बार बार पद पदुम गहि। करब सोइ उपदेसु जेहिं न सोच मोहि अवधपति ॥
translation: बार-बार चरण कमलों को पकड़कर गुरु वशिष्ठजी से मेरा संदेशा कहना कि वे वही उपदेश दें, जिससे अवधपति पिताजी मेरा सोच न करें ॥
english_translation: Again and again, bow at the guru's lotus feet and tell him my message: let him give only such counsel that the king of Ayodhya does not grieve over me.
essence: Care with your words can protect the heart that receives them.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks that his message be delivered respectfully to Guru Vashistha, and that the advice given should keep Dasharath from worrying about him.
insight: It teaches you to filter speech through compassion, so your message reduces suffering instead of multiplying it.
modern_relevance: You draft a text to your father after a painful argument, deleting the sharp line before sending it. You want the truth to land softly, because the relationship matters more than winning.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: पुरजन परिजन सकल निहोरी। तात सुनाएहु बिनती मोरी॥ सोइ सब भाँति मोर हितकारी। जातें रह नरनाहु सुखारी ॥
translation: हे तात! सब पुरवासियों और कुटुम्बियों से निहोरा (अनुरोध) करके मेरी विनती सुनाना कि वही मनुष्य मेरा सब प्रकार से हितकारी है, जिसकी चेष्टा से महाराज सुखी रहें ॥
english_translation: Father, request all the townspeople and relatives for me. Tell them my plea: that person is truly helpful to me who keeps King Dasharath content and at ease.
essence: Serving Ram begins with easing the burden of his father.
simple_meaning: Ram asks his father to tell everyone that the person who truly helps him is the one who keeps King Dasharath happy and peaceful.
insight: It shifts care from self-interest to protecting the well-being of those who hold the family together.
modern_relevance: You are leaving for a new city, and the last thing you ask your family is simple: please look after the parent who is staying behind. Love becomes practical right there.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कहब सँदेसु भरत के आएँ। नीति न तजिअ राजपदु पाएँ॥ पालेहु प्रजहि करम मन बानी। सेएहु मातु सकल सम जानी ॥
translation: भरत के आने पर उनको मेरा संदेशा कहना कि राजा का पद पा जाने पर नीति न छोड़ देना, कर्म, वचन और मन से प्रजा का पालन करना और सब माताओं को समान जानकर उनकी सेवा करना ॥
english_translation: Tell Bharat when he arrives: do not abandon righteous conduct after gaining the throne. Protect the people with your actions, words, and mind, and serve all the mothers as equal.
essence: True authority is measured by conduct, not by the throne.
simple_meaning: Power should never make you careless. If you rise to a higher role, keep your conduct pure and serve everyone fairly.
insight: It shifts leadership from entitlement to responsibility, with equal care in thought, speech, and action.
modern_relevance: You get promoted, and suddenly people start watching how you speak, decide, and treat the team. This verse reminds you that a higher seat demands cleaner conduct, not a bigger ego.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: ओर निबाहेहु भायप भाई। करि पितु मातु सुजन सेवकाई॥ तात भाँति तेहि राखब राऊ। सोच मोर जेहिं करै न काऊ ॥
translation: और हे भाई! पिता, माता और स्वजनों की सेवा करके भाईपन को अंत तक निबाहना। हे तात! राजा (पिताजी) को उसी प्रकार से रखना जिससे वे कभी (किसी तरह भी) मेरा सोच न करें ॥
english_translation: Brother, keep brotherhood alive to the end by serving your father, mother, and good people. Dear one, keep Father in such a way that he never has any worry because of me.
essence: Brotherhood survives through service, not sentiment.
simple_meaning: Ram asks Bharat to keep family duty alive by serving parents and good people, and to care for Dasharath so he feels no worry on Ram's account.
insight: It shifts duty from a formal role into a lived act of care that protects others from worry.
modern_relevance: You call your parents after a hard day and hear the strain in their voice. Instead of making them carry your burden, you steady them with your presence. That is the kind of love Ram asks for.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: लखन कहे कछु बचन कठोरा। बरजि राम पुनि मोहि निहोरा॥ बार बार निज सपथ देवाई। कहबि न तात लखन लारिकाई ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी ने कुछ कठोर वचन कहे, किन्तु श्री रामजी ने उन्हें डांट कर फिर मुझसे अनुरोध किया और बार-बार अपनी सौगंध दिलाई (और कहा) हे तात! लक्ष्मण का लड़कपन वहाँ न कहना ॥
english_translation: Lakshman spoke some harsh words, but Ram stopped him and again urged me. He made me swear again and again: 'Father, do not call Lakshman childish there.'
essence: True care refuses to shame the one you love.
simple_meaning: Ram insists that Lakshman not be dismissed as childish, even while Lakshman has spoken harshly. He protects his brother’s dignity in front of others.
insight: It shifts you from reacting to the offense toward guarding the relationship and the other person’s honor.
modern_relevance: A family argument is still ringing in the kitchen, and someone starts mocking the younger brother for being immature. The wisest person in the room stops it immediately. Protecting dignity matters more than winning the moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहि प्रनामु कछु कहन लिय सिय भइ सिथिल सनेह। थकित बचन लोचन सजल पुलक पल्लवित देह ॥
translation: प्रणाम कर सीताजी भी कुछ कहने लगी थीं, परन्तु स्नेहवश वे शिथिल हो गईं। उनकी वाणी रुक गई, नेत्रों में जल भर आया और शरीर रोमांच से व्याप्त हो गया ॥
english_translation: After offering her प्रणाम, Sita tried to say a few words, but love made her weak. Her speech faltered, her eyes filled with tears, and her body trembled with goosebumps.
essence: Love can make even a farewell wordless.
simple_meaning: Sita begins to speak after bowing, but emotion overwhelms her. Her voice fails, tears come, and her body shivers with love.
insight: It shows how love can silence speech and reveal itself through tears, trembling, and stillness.
modern_relevance: You start to say goodbye at the train platform, but your throat closes. The words are there, yet love and grief arrive first.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहि अवसर रघुबर रुख पाई। केवट पारहि नाव चलाई॥ रघुकुलतिलक चले एहि भाँती। देखउँ ठाढ़ कुलिस धरि छाती ॥
translation: उसी समय श्री रामचन्द्रजी का रुख पाकर केवट ने पार जाने के लिए नाव चला दी। इस प्रकार रघुवंश तिलक श्री रामचन्द्रजी चल दिए और मैं छाती पर वज्र रखकर खड़ा-खड़ा देखता रहा ॥
english_translation: At that moment, seeing Ram's readiness, the boatman set the boat across the river. Then the jewel of Raghu's line moved on, and I stood there with a chest like thunder, watching.
essence: Love can leave you standing still while the beloved moves on.
simple_meaning: The boatman sends Ram across the river, and the speaker watches Ram depart with a heart as hard as a thunderbolt.
insight: It shows how devotion can deepen into helpless longing without turning bitter.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you love walk through an airport gate, unable to call them back. The body stays still, but the chest feels sealed shut.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मैं आपन किमि कहौं कलेसू। जिअत फिरेउँ लेइ राम सँदेसू॥ अस कहि सचिव बचन रहि गयऊ। हानि गलानि सोच बस भयऊ ॥
translation: मैं अपने क्लेश को कैसे कहूँ, जो श्री रामजी का यह संदेशा लेकर जीता ही लौट आया! ऐसा कहकर मंत्री की वाणी रुक गई (वे चुप हो गए) और वे हानि की ग्लानि और सोच के वश हो गए ॥
english_translation: How can I speak of my suffering? I returned alive carrying Ram's message. Saying this, the minister's voice stopped, and he was overcome by grief, shame, and anxious thought.
essence: Some pain returns with you and refuses to become words.
simple_meaning: Sumantra cannot even finish speaking. He has returned alive with Ram's message, but the pain of what happened has left him speechless.
insight: It shows how deep loss can silence speech before the mind can organize it.
modern_relevance: You come home after dropping someone at the airport, and the house feels wrong in a way you can't explain. The words stay stuck because the absence is still fresh.
speaker: Sumantra

verse_text: सूत बचन सुनतहिं नरनाहू। परेउ धरनि उर दारुन दाहू॥ तलफत बिषम मोह मन मापा। माजा मनहुँ मीन कहुँ ब्यापा ॥
translation: सारथी सुमंत्र के वचन सुनते ही राजा पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े, उनके हृदय में भयानक जलन होने लगी। वे तड़पने लगे, उनका मन भीषण मोह से व्याकुल हो गया। मानो मछली को माँजा व्याप गया हो (पहली वर्षा का जल लग गया हो) ॥
english_translation: As soon as the charioteer's words reached King Dasharath, he fell to the ground, and a fierce burning seized his chest. He thrashed in unbearable delusion, his mind overwhelmed—like a fish struck by the first rain.
essence: Grief can strike so hard that the body surrenders first.
simple_meaning: Dasharath collapses when he hears the news. Grief and confusion seize him so completely that he cannot hold himself together.
insight: It shows how overwhelming grief can overwhelm reason and pull the body into collapse.
modern_relevance: You read one message and feel your chest drop before you can even think. Some news arrives so suddenly that your body understands it first.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि बिलाप सब रोवहिं रानी। महा बिपति किमि जाइ बखानी॥ सुनि बिलाप दुखहू दुखु लागा। धीरजहू कर धीरजु भागा ॥
translation: सब रानियाँ विलाप करके रो रही हैं। उस महान विपत्ति का कैसे वर्णन किया जाए? उस समय के विलाप को सुनकर दुःख को भी दुःख लगा और धीरज का भी धीरज भाग गया! ॥
english_translation: All the queens weep in grief. How can such a great calamity be described? Hearing their lament, even sorrow felt sorrow, and even courage fled from courage.
essence: Grief can become so vast that even courage cannot stand upright.
simple_meaning: The queens are crying over a disaster so terrible that words cannot capture it. The grief is so deep it shakes even sorrow and courage itself.
insight: It shows how communal grief can overwhelm language, steadiness, and self-control all at once.
modern_relevance: You walk into a house after bad news has already spread. No one is speaking clearly, only crying. In that kind of room, even the strongest person feels the floor give way.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भयउ कोलाहलु अवध अति सुनि नृप राउर सोरु। बिपुल बिहग बन परेउ निसि मानहुँ कुलिस कठोरु ॥
translation: राजा के रावले (रनिवास) में (रोने का) शोर सुनकर अयोध्या भर में बड़ा भारी कुहराम मच गया! (ऐसा जान पड़ता था) मानो पक्षियों के विशाल वन में रात के समय कठोर वज्र गिरा हो ॥
english_translation: A great uproar spread through Ayodhya when the king's palace heard the lament; it was as if a hard thunderbolt had struck a forest full of birds in the night.
essence: Grief can strike a whole city like lightning.
simple_meaning: Ayodhya is thrown into panic and grief after hearing the king's palace filled with lament. The scene is compared to a thunderbolt striking a forest of birds at night.
insight: It turns grief into a shared shock, not a private feeling. The mind is made to register the weight of loss instantly.
modern_relevance: You hear crying from the next room and your whole body tightens before you even know why. Some news lands like a blow before your mind can name it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रान कंठगत भयउ भुआलू। मनि बिहीन जनु ब्याकुल ब्यालू॥ इंद्रीं सकल बिकल भइँ भारी। जनु सर सरसिज बनु बिनु बारी ॥
translation: राजा के प्राण कंठ में आ गए। मानो मणि के बिना साँप व्याकुल (मरणासन्न) हो गया हो। इन्द्रियाँ सब बहुत ही विकल हो गईं, मानो बिना जल के तालाब में कमलों का वन मुरझा गया हो ॥
english_translation: The king's breath rose to his throat. Like a snake made frantic without its jewel, he was shaken to the core. All his senses grew unsteady, like a lotus grove in a pond left without water.
essence: Grief can unmake the body before the mind finds words.
simple_meaning: Dasharath is so overwhelmed by grief that his breath seems stuck in his throat. His body and senses lose their steadiness, like a pond of lotuses left without water.
insight: It shifts attention from explaining pain to noticing how deeply the body carries it.
modern_relevance: You get the message that breaks you, and suddenly your chest tightens, your hands go numb, and the room feels far away. Grief can arrive as a bodily event before it becomes a thought.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कौसल्याँ नृपु दीख मलाना। रबिकुल रबि अँथयउ जियँ जाना॥ उर धरि धीर राम महतारी। बोली बचन समय अनुसारी ॥
translation: कौसल्याजी ने राजा को बहुत दुःखी देखकर अपने हृदय में जान लिया कि अब सूर्यकुल का सूर्य अस्त हो चला! तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी की माता कौसल्या हृदय में धीरज धरकर समय के अनुकूल वचन बोलीं- ॥
english_translation: Kaushalya saw the king in deep sorrow and knew in her heart that the sun of the सूर्यवंश had set. Then, holding courage in her heart, Ram's mother spoke words suited to the moment.
essence: Grief is met first with steadiness, then with the right words.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya sees Dasharath's grief and realizes the line of the सूर्यवंश is ending. She steadies herself and speaks with care.
insight: It teaches you to notice emotional collapse quickly and answer it with measured speech, not panic.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room and see a parent’s face change before anyone speaks. In that instant, you know the room has crossed into grief, and your next words must be chosen carefully.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ समुझि मन करिअ बिचारू। राम बियोग पयोधि अपारू॥ करनधार तुम्ह अवध जहाजू। चढ़ेउ सकल प्रिय पथिक समाजू ॥
translation: हे नाथ! आप मन में समझ कर विचार कीजिए कि श्री रामचन्द्र का वियोग अपार समुद्र है। अयोध्या जहाज है और आप उसके कर्णधार (खेने वाले) हैं। सब प्रियजन (कुटुम्बी और प्रजा) ही यात्रियों का समाज है, जो इस जहाज पर चढ़ा हुआ है ॥
english_translation: O lord, think it through in your mind: separation from Ram is an endless ocean. You are the boat’s helmsman, and Ayodhya is the ship. All your loved ones and subjects have boarded it together.
essence: Your sorrow may be vast, but others are still in your care.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya asks Dasharath to think clearly: losing Ram feels like an endless sea, and he must guide the whole family through it safely.
insight: It shifts you from private overwhelm to responsible steadiness for others.
modern_relevance: Your family is in the car after bad news, and everyone is looking at you to stay calm. You may be hurting too, but your steadiness becomes the bridge for everyone else.
speaker: Kaushalya

verse_text: धीरजु धरिअ त पाइअ पारू। नाहिं त बूड़िहि सबु परिवारू॥ जौं जियँ धरिअ बिनय पिय मोरी। रामु लखनु सिय मिलहिं बहोरी ॥
translation: आप धीरज धरिएगा, तो सब पार पहुँच जाएँगे। नहीं तो सारा परिवार डूब जाएगा। हे प्रिय स्वामी! यदि मेरी विनती हृदय में धारण कीजिएगा तो श्री राम, लक्ष्मण, सीता फिर आ मिलेंगे ॥
english_translation: Keep patience, and you will reach the other shore. Otherwise, the whole family will drown. Dear husband, if you hold my plea in your heart, Ram, Lakshman, and Sita will come back together.
essence: Patience is the raft that carries love across grief.
simple_meaning: Kausalya asks Dasharath to stay patient and listen. She says his calm will save the family, and her plea is that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita may be reunited.
insight: It teaches you to treat patience as active support, not weakness, when emotions threaten to overwhelm everyone.
modern_relevance: You're in the middle of a family crisis, and every sharp word makes it worse. One person choosing calm can keep the whole house from breaking apart.
speaker: Kausalya

verse_text: प्रिया बचन मृदु सुनत नृपु चितयउ आँखि उघारि। तलफत मीन मलीन जनु सींचत सीतल बारि ॥
translation: प्रिय पत्नी कौसल्या के कोमल वचन सुनते हुए राजा ने आँखें खोलकर देखा! मानो तड़पती हुई दीन मछली पर कोई शीतल जल छिड़क रहा हो ॥
english_translation: Hearing his beloved wife's gentle words, the king opened his eyes. He was like a dying fish revived by cool water.
essence: Tender words can briefly revive a heart already sinking.
simple_meaning: The king, overwhelmed by grief, stirs slightly when he hears his wife's tender words. Her voice is like cool water reaching someone gasping for relief.
insight: It shifts attention from dramatic action to the healing force of tenderness in a moment of collapse.
modern_relevance: You sit beside someone shattered by bad news, and your calm voice is the only thing they can still receive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धरि धीरजु उठि बैठ भुआलू। कहु सुमंत्र कहँ राम कृपालू॥ कहाँ लखनु कहँ रामु सनेही। कहँ प्रिय पुत्रबधू बैदेही ॥
translation: धीरज धरकर राजा उठ बैठे और बोले- सुमंत्र! कहो, कृपालु श्री राम कहाँ हैं? लक्ष्मण कहाँ हैं? स्नेही राम कहाँ हैं? और मेरी प्यारी बहू जानकी कहाँ है? ॥
english_translation: Steadying himself, the king sat up and said to Sumantra, “Where is kind Ram? Where is Lakshman? Where is loving Ram? Where is my dear daughter-in-law, Vaidehi?”
essence: Grief still reaches for the ones it cannot bear to lose.
simple_meaning: Dasharath gathers himself enough to ask where Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are. His grief has made him weak, but his love is still searching for them.
insight: It shows how love and loss can pull attention away from the body and toward the absent beloved.
modern_relevance: You wake from a fevered sleep and ask for the person who matters most before you ask anything else. Grief does that: it makes the heart search first.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: बिलपत राउ बिकल बहु भाँती। भइ जुग सरिस सिराति न राती॥ तापस अंध साप सुधि आई। कौसल्यहि सब कथा सुनाई ॥
translation: राजा व्याकुल होकर बहुत प्रकार से विलाप कर रहे हैं। वह रात युग के समान बड़ी हो गई, बीतती ही नहीं। राजा को अंधे तपस्वी (श्रवणकुमार के पिता) के शाप की याद आ गई। उन्होंने सब कथा कौसल्या को कह सुनाई ॥
english_translation: The king lamented in many ways, beside himself. The night passed like an age and would not end. Then the blind sage's curse came back to mind, and he told the whole story to Kausalya.
essence: Grief turns one night into an age and makes hidden guilt return.
simple_meaning: Dasharath is overwhelmed with grief. Time feels unbearable. In his pain, he remembers the curse linked to his past and tells Kausalya everything.
insight: It shows how unresolved pain stretches time and brings buried guilt to the surface.
modern_relevance: You lie awake after a fight, and one hour feels like five. Then an old mistake you thought was buried comes back with full force, and you finally say the whole truth aloud.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भयउ बिकल बरनत इतिहासा। राम रहित धिग जीवन आसा॥ सो तनु राखि करब मैं काहा। जेहिं न प्रेम पनु मोर निबाहा ॥
translation: उस इतिहास का वर्णन करते-करते राजा व्याकुल हो गए और कहने लगे कि श्री राम के बिना जीने की आशा को धिक्कार है। मैं उस शरीर को रखकर क्या करूँगा, जिसने मेरा प्रेम का प्रण नहीं निबाहा? ॥
english_translation: While recounting the old story, the king became distraught and said, "A life without Ram is cursed. What use is keeping this body, if it has not fulfilled my vow of love?"
essence: A body without fulfilled love feels like a burden.
simple_meaning: Dasharath sees that life without Ram has lost its value. He feels his body is useless if he cannot keep the promise of love he made.
insight: It shifts attention from physical survival to the deeper question of whether your life is still aligned with what you love.
modern_relevance: You keep scrolling old photos after a breakup, realizing the apartment, the routines, even your own body feel strangely hollow. When the bond is gone, the life built around it can feel uninhabited.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: हा रघुनंदन प्रान पिरीते। तुम्ह बिनु जिअत बहुत दिन बीते॥ हा जानकी लखन हा रघुबर। हा पितु हित चित चातक जलधर ॥
translation: हा रघुकुल को आनंद देने वाले मेरे प्राण प्यारे राम! तुम्हारे बिना जीते हुए मुझे बहुत दिन बीत गए। हा जानकी, लक्ष्मण! हा रघुवीर! हा पिता के चित्त रूपी चातक के हित करने वाले मेघ! ॥
english_translation: O delight of Raghu's line, beloved of my life! I have lived many days without you. O Janaki, Lakshman, O Raghubar! O cloud that brings relief to my father's thirsty heart!
essence: Separation makes even living feel like endurance.
simple_meaning: Dasharath cries out in grief, saying Ram is the beloved of his life and that living without him has gone on too long. He also calls to Sita, Lakshman, and Ram as the one who relieved his father’s heart.
insight: It names grief honestly instead of dressing it up, and shows how absence can hollow out ordinary time.
modern_relevance: You keep going through the motions after someone leaves, answering emails, making tea, sleeping badly. From the outside it looks normal; inside, you know you are only enduring the days.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: राम राम कहि राम कहि राम राम कहि राम। तनु परिहरि रघुबर बिरहँ राउ गयउ सुरधाम ॥
translation: राम-राम कहकर, फिर राम कहकर, फिर राम-राम कहकर और फिर राम कहकर राजा श्री राम के विरह में शरीर त्याग कर सुरलोक को सिधार गए ॥
english_translation: Saying Ram, Ram, Ram, Ram, the king left his body in separation from Raghubar and went to the higher realm.
essence: Separation from Ram becomes the king's final passage.
simple_meaning: Dasharath died with Ram's name on his lips, overwhelmed by separation from Ram.
insight: It shows how longing can shape even the final moment, turning loss into remembrance.
modern_relevance: Someone keeps whispering a loved one's name after a hospital call, unable to stop the ache. This verse understands that grief can become the last prayer.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जिअन मरन फलु दसरथ पावा। अंड अनेक अमल जसु छावा॥ जिअत राम बिधु बदनु निहारा। राम बिरह करि मरनु सँवारा ॥
translation: जीने और मरने का फल तो दशरथजी ने ही पाया, जिनका निर्मल यश अनेकों ब्रह्मांडों में छा गया। जीते जी तो श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चन्द्रमा के समान मुख को देखा और श्री राम के विरह को निमित्त बनाकर अपना मरण सुधार लिया ॥
english_translation: Dasharath received the fruit of both living and dying; his spotless fame spread across countless worlds. While alive, he beheld Ram's moon-like face, and through separation from Ram, he made his death complete.
essence: A life touched by Ram is complete, even in grief.
simple_meaning: Dasharath found fulfillment in both living and dying. He saw Ram's beautiful face while alive, and even Ram's separation became part of a blessed end.
insight: It shifts the mind from measuring life by comfort to measuring it by love and completion.
modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed after a long goodbye, knowing nothing can be fixed now. Yet the love was real, and the life shared was not empty.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सोक बिकल सब रोवहिं रानी। रूपु सीलु बलु तेजु बखानी॥ करहिं बिलाप अनेक प्रकारा। परहिं भूमितल बारहिं बारा ॥
translation: सब रानियाँ शोक के मारे व्याकुल होकर रो रही हैं। वे राजा के रूप, शील, बल और तेज का बखान कर-करके अनेकों प्रकार से विलाप कर रही हैं और बार-बार धरती पर गिर-गिर पड़ती हैं ॥
english_translation: The queens, overcome with grief, weep. They keep praising the king’s beauty, character, strength, and radiance, and lament in many ways, falling to the ground again and again.
essence: Grief makes even praise collapse into tears.
simple_meaning: The queens are shattered by grief. They keep remembering the king’s virtues and collapse in mourning again and again.
insight: It shows how bereavement moves through remembrance, not argument: the heart keeps returning to what it has lost.
modern_relevance: You stand beside a hospital bed after the last goodbye, and your mind keeps circling the same memories. Grief turns praise, memory, and collapse into one motion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिलपहिं बिकल दास अरु दासी। घर घर रुदनु करहिं पुरबासी॥ अँथयउ आजु भानुकुल भानू। धरम अवधि गुन रूप निधानू ॥
translation: दास-दासीगण व्याकुल होकर विलाप कर रहे हैं और नगर निवासी घर-घर रो रहे हैं। कहते हैं कि आज धर्म की सीमा, गुण और रूप के भंडार सूर्यकुल के सूर्य अस्त हो गए? ॥
english_translation: The servants and maidservants weep in anguish, and the townspeople cry in every home. They say, "Today the sun of the सूर्यवंश has set—the treasure of duty, virtue, and beauty."
essence: A righteous life can become the light a whole city depends on.
simple_meaning: Everyone in Ayodhya is grieving. They feel that the light of their kingdom has gone out with Dasharath's death.
insight: It shows how deeply a just leader shapes the emotional life of an entire community.
modern_relevance: A neighborhood goes quiet after the respected elder who held everyone together is gone. People don't just miss one person; they miss the moral center that made the place feel whole.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गारीं सकल कैकइहि देहीं। नयन बिहीन कीन्ह जग जेहीं॥ एहि बिधि बिलपत रैनि बिहानी। आए सकल महामुनि ग्यानी ॥
translation: सब कैकेयी को गालियाँ देते हैं, जिसने संसार भर को बिना नेत्रों का (अंधा) कर दिया! इस प्रकार विलाप करते रात बीत गई। प्रातःकाल सब बड़े-बड़े ज्ञानी मुनि आए ॥
english_translation: Everyone curses Kaikeyi, saying she has made the world blind. In this way they keep lamenting through the night, and at dawn all the great sages and wise men arrive.
essence: Blame floods the mind before wisdom can return.
simple_meaning: People blame Kaikeyi for the disaster and say she has blinded the world. Their grief lasts through the night until the sages arrive at dawn.
insight: It shows how shock turns into accusation, and how wisdom enters only after the first wave of pain.
modern_relevance: After a family rupture, everyone keeps replaying who ruined everything, and the blame keeps the house awake until morning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब बसिष्ठ मुनि समय सम कहि अनेक इतिहास। सोक नेवारेउ सबहि कर निज बिग्यान प्रकास ॥
translation: तब वशिष्ठ मुनि ने समय के अनुकूल अनेक इतिहास कहकर अपने विज्ञान के प्रकाश से सबका शोक दूर किया ॥
english_translation: Then sage Vashishtha, speaking in the right time with fitting stories, dispelled everyone's grief with the light of his own wisdom.
essence: The right wisdom at the right time can carry people through grief.
simple_meaning: Vashishtha spoke fitting stories at the right moment, and his clear understanding helped everyone move through their grief.
insight: It teaches you to meet pain with measured speech instead of forceful correction.
modern_relevance: A family sits in silence after bad news, and no one knows what to say. One calm person tells the right story, at the right pace, and the room slowly breathes again.
speaker: Vashishtha

verse_text: तेल नावँ भरि नृप तनु राखा। दूत बोलाइ बहुरि अस भाषा॥ धावहु बेगि भरत पहिं जाहू। नृप सुधि कतहुँ कहहु जनि काहू ॥
translation: वशिष्ठजी ने नाव में तेल भरवाकर राजा के शरीर को उसमें रखवा दिया। फिर दूतों को बुलवाकर उनसे ऐसा कहा- तुम लोग जल्दी दौड़कर भरत के पास जाओ। राजा की मृत्यु का समाचार कहीं किसी से न कहना ॥
english_translation: Vashishtha had the king's body placed in an oil-filled vessel, then called the messengers and said, "Hurry to Bharat at once. Do not tell anyone of the king's death."
essence: Grief first demands protection, not explanation.
simple_meaning: Vashishtha preserves Dasharath's body and sends messengers to bring Bharat quickly, while hiding the news of the king's death.
insight: It shifts attention from emotional collapse to immediate, careful action.
modern_relevance: A hospital corridor goes quiet after the doctor gives you the news. Before the relatives arrive, someone has to steady the room, make the calls, and keep panic from spreading.
speaker: Vashishtha

verse_text: एतनेइ कहेहु भरत सन जाई। गुर बोलाइ पठयउ दोउ भाई॥ सुनि मुनि आयसु धावन धाए। चले बेग बर बाजि लजाए ॥
translation: जाकर भरत से इतना ही कहना कि दोनों भाइयों को गुरुजी ने बुलवा भेजा है। मुनि की आज्ञा सुनकर धावन (दूत) दौड़े। वे अपने वेग से उत्तम घोड़ों को भी लजाते हुए चले ॥
english_translation: Tell Bharata only this: the guru has summoned both brothers. Hearing the sage's order, the messengers rushed off, moving so fast they shamed the finest horses.
essence: Some messages are so urgent they outrun hesitation.
simple_meaning: Vashishtha tells the messengers to inform Bharata that both brothers have been summoned. They hurry off at once, running so fast they outpace even the best horses.
insight: It captures the speed of action under pressure, before thought can catch up.
modern_relevance: The phone rings at midnight, and you already know the news is serious. You grab your keys before the message is even finished.
speaker: Vashishtha

verse_text: अनरथु अवध अरंभेउ जब तें। कुसगुन होहिं भरत कहुँ तब तें॥ देखहिं राति भयानक सपना। जागि करहिं कटु कोटि कलपना ॥
translation: जब से अयोध्या में अनर्थ प्रारंभ हुआ, तभी से भरतजी को अपशकुन होने लगे। वे रात को भयंकर स्वप्न देखते थे और जागने पर (उन स्वप्नों के कारण) करोड़ों (अनेकों) तरह की बुरी-बुरी कल्पनाएँ किया करते थे ॥
english_translation: Since the moment calamity began in Ayodhya, ominous signs appeared for Bharat. He would see frightening dreams at night and, upon waking, fall into countless dark imaginings.
essence: Trouble first appears as fear in the mind.
simple_meaning: From the moment trouble began in Ayodhya, Bharat was surrounded by bad signs, frightening dreams, and anxious thoughts.
insight: It shows how inner anxiety can mirror a family crisis before the crisis is spoken aloud.
modern_relevance: You wake at 3 a.m. after a bad dream, then spend the next hour turning it into ten worse stories. Bharat knows that spiraling feeling before the phone even rings.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिप्र जेवाँइ देहिं दिन दाना। सिव अभिषेक करहिं बिधि नाना॥ मागहिं हृदयँ महेस मनाई। कुसल मातु पितु परिजन भाई ॥
translation: (अनिष्टशान्ति के लिए) वे प्रतिदिन ब्राह्मणों को भोजन कराकर दान देते थे। अनेकों विधियों से रुद्राभिषेक करते थे। महादेवजी को हृदय में मनाकर उनसे माता-पिता, कुटुम्बी और भाइयों का कुशल-क्षेम माँगते थे ॥
english_translation: They fed Brahmins and gave daily charity, performed Shiva worship in many ways, and in their hearts prayed to Mahesh for the well-being of their mother, father, family, and brothers.
essence: Fear makes love reach for rituals and protection.
simple_meaning: Bharat and the people around him keep doing rituals, charity, and prayers for the safety of their loved ones.
insight: It shows how anxious love looks for every possible way to protect the people it cannot control.
modern_relevance: You start lighting incense, calling relatives, and checking on everyone after a family crisis. The rituals do not fix the pain, but they show how love reaches for protection.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि बिधि सोचत भरत मन धावन पहुँचे आइ। गुर अनुसासन श्रवन सुनि चले गनेसु मनाई ॥
translation: भरतजी इस प्रकार मन में चिंता कर रहे थे कि दूत आ पहुँचे। गुरुजी की आज्ञा कानों से सुनते ही वे गणेशजी को मनाकर चल पड़े।157॥
english_translation: While Bharat was thinking like this in his mind, the messenger arrived. Hearing the guru's instruction, he at once invoked Ganesh and set out.
essence: True readiness is moving before anxiety can finish its story.
simple_meaning: Bharat is lost in worry when the messenger arrives. As soon as he hears the guru's order, he invokes Ganesh and leaves at once.
insight: It shifts attention from anxious thinking to immediate response to rightful guidance.
modern_relevance: You are spiraling over bad news when your phone rings with the one message that matters. The noise in your head doesn't vanish first; you move first, and clarity follows.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चले समीर बेग हय हाँके। नाघत सरित सैल बन बाँके॥ हृदयँ सोचु बड़ कछु न सोहाई। अस जानहिं जियँ जाउँ उड़ाई ॥
translation: हवा के समान वेग वाले घोड़ों को हाँकते हुए वे विकट नदी, पहाड़ तथा जंगलों को लाँघते हुए चले। उनके हृदय में बड़ा सोच था, कुछ सुहाता न था। मन में ऐसा सोचते थे कि उड़कर पहुँच जाऊँ ॥
english_translation: Driving horses as fast as the wind, they crossed rough rivers, hills, and forests. Their heart was heavy with worry; nothing felt pleasant. In their mind, they wished they could fly there.
essence: An anxious heart turns every road into a delay.
simple_meaning: The travelers rushed forward as fast as they could, crossing difficult terrain. Their mind was full of worry, and they wanted to reach the city even faster.
insight: It captures the way grief and urgency make the body move faster than the world allows.
modern_relevance: You keep checking the map while the taxi crawls through traffic, because your mind is already at the hospital door.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक निमेष बरष सम जाई। एहि बिधि भरत नगर निअराई॥ असगुन होहिं नगर पैठारा। रटहिं कुभाँति कुखेत करारा ॥
translation: एक-एक निमेष वर्ष के समान बीत रहा था। इस प्रकार भरतजी नगर के निकट पहुँचे। नगर में प्रवेश करते समय अपशकुन होने लगे। कौए बुरी जगह बैठकर बुरी तरह से काँव-काँव कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: A single moment passed like a year. In this way Bharat drew near the city. Ominous signs appeared as he entered the city. Crows sat in bad places and cawed harshly.
essence: Grief makes a single moment feel like a year.
simple_meaning: Bharat is nearing Ayodhya, but every moment feels painfully long and the city is filled with bad omens.
insight: It shows how fear can distort time and make the world feel hostile before anything has even happened.
modern_relevance: You are ten minutes from home after a hard phone call, and every red light feels cruel. When your mind is braced for loss, even ordinary signs start to feel heavy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: खर सिआर बोलहिं प्रतिकूला। सुनि सुनि होइ भरत मन सूला॥ श्रीहत सर सरिता बन बागा। नगरु बिसेषि भयावनु लागा ॥
translation: गदहे और सियार विपरीत बोल रहे हैं। यह सुन-सुनकर भरत के मन में बड़ी पीड़ा हो रही है। तालाब, नदी, वन, बगीचे सब शोभाहीन हो रहे हैं। नगर बहुत ही भयानक लग रहा है ॥
english_translation: Donkeys and jackals are speaking in inauspicious ways. Hearing them again and again, Bharat feels deep pain. Lakes, rivers, forests, and gardens all seem stripped of beauty; the city itself feels terrifying.
essence: Pain makes even familiar places feel hostile.
simple_meaning: Bharat reaches the city, but every sign around him feels wrong and frightening. The bad omens deepen his pain and make the whole place seem stripped of joy.
insight: It shows how inner pain colors outer perception, turning beauty into threat.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital waiting room and every fluorescent light feels harsher than before. When your heart is already braced for loss, even ordinary places can feel ominous.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: खग मृग हय गय जाहिं न जोए। राम बियोग कुरोग बिगोए॥ नगर नारि नर निपट दुखारी। मनहुँ सबन्हि सब संपति हारी ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के वियोग रूपी बुरे रोग से सताए हुए पक्षी-पशु, घोड़े-हाथी (ऐसे दुःखी हो रहे हैं कि) देखे नहीं जाते। नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष अत्यन्त दुःखी हो रहे हैं। मानो सब अपनी सारी सम्पत्ति हार बैठे हों ॥
english_translation: Birds, animals, horses, and elephants look as if they can no longer bear the pain of Ram's separation. The men and women of the city are utterly sorrowful, as if they have lost all their wealth.
essence: Ram's absence makes even the city seem sick with loss.
simple_meaning: Ram's absence weighs so heavily on the city that even the animals seem afflicted, and everyone feels as if they have lost everything.
insight: It turns private grief into a shared atmosphere, so the reader feels how absence reshapes an entire world.
modern_relevance: You return to a house after a devastating breakup, and even the quiet feels bruised. The room, the street, the familiar faces — everything seems touched by absence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुरजन मिलहिं न कहहिं कछु गवँहि जोहारहिं जाहिं। भरत कुसल पूँछि न सकहिं भय बिषाद मन माहिं ॥
translation: नगर के लोग मिलते हैं, पर कुछ कहते नहीं, गौं से (चुपके से) जोहार (वंदना) करके चले जाते हैं। भरतजी भी किसी से कुशल नहीं पूछ सकते, क्योंकि उनके मन में भय और विषाद छा रहा है ॥
english_translation: The townspeople meet him but say nothing, bowing in silence as they pass. Bharat cannot ask anyone how they are, because fear and sorrow fill his mind.
essence: Grief can make even greeting feel like too much.
simple_meaning: The city is so heavy with grief that people only bow to Bharat in silence. Even Bharat cannot bring himself to ask after anyone's well-being.
insight: It shows how grief can freeze ordinary human contact, turning even kindness into silence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a house after bad news has spread. Everyone lowers their eyes, offers a quiet nod, and keeps moving. No one has the energy for small talk.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हाट बाट नहिं जाइ निहारी। जनु पुर दहँ दिसि लागि दवारी॥ आवत सुत सुनि कैकयनंदिनि। हरषी रबिकुल जलरुह चंदिनि ॥
translation: बाजार और रास्ते देखे नहीं जाते। मानो नगर में दसों दिशाओं में दावाग्नि लगी है! पुत्र को आते सुनकर सूर्यकुल रूपी कमल के लिए चाँदनी रूपी कैकेयी (बड़ी) हर्षित हुई ॥
english_translation: The market and roads could not be seen, as if a fire had spread in all ten directions through the city. Hearing that her son was coming, Kaikeyi—moonlight for the lotus of the solar dynasty—was overjoyed.
essence: Personal joy can feel cruel inside a shared wound.
simple_meaning: The city feels scorched with grief, and Kaikeyi feels joy at hearing her son is coming home.
insight: It shows how private relief can become morally jarring when everyone around you is grieving.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering after a painful breakup, and one person is smiling too brightly because their own news is good. The room can hold both relief and hurt at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सजि आरती मुदित उठि धाई। द्वारेहिं भेंटि भवन लेइ आई॥ भरत दुखित परिवारु निहारा॥ मानहुँ तुहिन बनज बनु मारा ॥
translation: वह आरती सजाकर आनंद में भरकर उठ दौड़ी और दरवाजे पर ही मिलकर भरत-शत्रुघ्न को महल में ले आई। भरत ने सारे परिवार को दुःखी देखा। मानो कमलों के वन को पाला मार गया हो ॥
english_translation: She quickly arranged an aarti, rose in delight, met him at the door, and brought him into the house. Bharat saw the whole family in sorrow, as if a frost had struck a forest of lotuses.
essence: Joy at the door cannot hide grief inside.
simple_meaning: A joyful welcome turns suddenly into grief when Bharat sees the whole family sunk in sorrow.
insight: It shifts attention from the welcoming gesture to the deeper emotional wound already filling the home.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering and feel the room go quiet. Someone has tried to welcome you, but the sadness in everyone’s faces is louder than the greeting.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कैकेई हरषित एहि भाँती। मनहुँ मुदित दव लाइ किराती॥ सुतिह ससोच देखि मनु मारें। पूँछति नैहर कुसल हमारें ॥
translation: एक कैकेयी ही इस तरह हर्षित दिखती है मानो भीलनी जंगल में आग लगाकर आनंद में भर रही हो। पुत्र को सोच वश और मन मारे (बहुत उदास) देखकर वह पूछने लगी- हमारे नैहर में कुशल तो है? ॥
english_translation: Kaikeyi alone looked delighted, like a forest woman rejoicing after setting the woods ablaze. Seeing her son sorrowful and downcast, she asked, "Is everyone well at my parental home?"
essence: Self-centered joy can bloom right beside someone else's grief.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is the only one who seems pleased. Seeing her son deeply troubled, she asks whether her parental home is doing well.
insight: It exposes the blindness of desire: a mind fixed on itself can mistake harm for happiness.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering and feel the tension instantly. One person seems oddly pleased while everyone else is hurting, and their concern sounds more like self-protection than care.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकल कुसल कहि भरत सुनाई। पूँछी निज कुल कुसल भलाई॥ कहु कहँ तात कहाँ सब माता। कहँ सिय राम लखन प्रिय भ्राता ॥
translation: भरतजी ने सब कुशल कह सुनाई। फिर अपने कुल की कुशल-क्षेम पूछी। (भरतजी ने कहा-) कहो, पिताजी कहाँ हैं? मेरी सब माताएँ कहाँ हैं? सीताजी और मेरे प्यारे भाई राम-लक्ष्मण कहाँ हैं? ॥
english_translation: Bharat first asked after everyone's well-being, then asked about his own family: "Where is my father? Where are all my mothers? Where are Sita, Ram, and my dear brother Lakshman?"
essence: Love asks after everyone else before it asks for itself.
simple_meaning: Bharat speaks with care and respect, asking first about everyone's welfare and then about his father, mothers, Sita, Ram, and Lakshman.
insight: It shifts attention from personal urgency to relational care and respectful inquiry.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital waiting room and ask about everyone else before mentioning your own pain. That instinct — to care first, to inquire gently — is Bharat's.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि सुत बचन सनेहमय कपट नीर भरि नैन। भरत श्रवन मन सूल सम पापिनि बोली बैन ॥
translation: पुत्र के स्नेहमय वचन सुनकर नेत्रों में कपट का जल भरकर पापिनी कैकेयी भरत के कानों में और मन में शूल के समान चुभने वाले वचन बोली- ॥
english_translation: Hearing her son's affectionate words, Kaikeyi filled her eyes with deceptive tears and spoke words to Bharata that pierced his ears and heart like a thorn.
essence: Deceptive tenderness can wound more sharply than open anger.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi hears Bharata's loving words, but answers with false tears and painful words that wound him deeply.
insight: It reveals how false emotion can disguise harmful intent and hurt trust at the very moment affection is expected.
modern_relevance: You finally speak gently to someone you love, and they answer with polished concern that feels strangely cold. The smile is there, but something in the words lands like a blade.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: तात बात मैं सकल सँवारी। भै मंथरा सहाय बिचारी॥ कछुक काज बिधि बीच बिगारेउ। भूपति सुरपति पुर पगु धारेउ ॥
translation: हे तात! मैंने सारी बात बना ली थी। बेचारी मंथरा सहायक हुई। पर विधाता ने बीच में जरा सा काम बिगाड़ दिया। वह यह कि राजा देवलोक को पधार गए ॥
english_translation: Father, I had arranged everything. Poor Manthara helped me. But fate spoiled a small part of it in between: the king has gone to the higher realm.
essence: A single disruption can undo a carefully arranged plan.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi says she had everything arranged, but fate interrupted and Dasharath has died. The verse is part of her explanation, not a complete teaching on its own.
insight: It shows how quickly control slips away, turning a planned outcome into loss.
modern_relevance: You think the plan is settled, the messages are sent, and the meeting is confirmed — then one call changes everything. This verse sits inside that sudden collapse.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: सुनत भरतु भए बिबस बिषादा। जनु सहमेउ करि केहरि नादा॥ तात तात हा तात पुकारी। परे भूमितल ब्याकुल भारी ॥
translation: भरत यह सुनते ही विषाद के मारे विवश (बेहाल) हो गए। मानो सिंह की गर्जना सुनकर हाथी सहम गया हो। वे 'तात! तात! हा तात!' पुकारते हुए अत्यन्त व्याकुल होकर जमीन पर गिर पड़े ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Bharat was overcome by grief, as if a lion’s roar had startled an elephant. Crying, “Father! Father! Ah, father!” he fell to the ground in deep anguish.
essence: Grief can strike so hard that the body falls before the mind understands.
simple_meaning: Bharat is shattered by the news and collapses in grief, calling out for his father in helpless anguish.
insight: It shows grief as a full-body reaction, not a polished emotion.
modern_relevance: You open a message and your body goes cold before your mind can catch up. Some news doesn't arrive as information — it arrives as collapse.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चलत न देखन पायउँ तोही। तात न रामहि सौंपेहु मोही॥ बहुरि धीर धरि उठे सँभारी। कहु पितु मरन हेतु महतारी ॥
translation: (और विलाप करने लगे कि) हे तात! मैं आपको (स्वर्ग के लिए) चलते समय देख भी न सका। (हाय!) आप मुझे श्री रामजी को सौंप भी नहीं गए! फिर धीरज धरकर वे सम्हलकर उठे और बोले- माता! पिता के मरने का कारण तो बताओ ॥
english_translation: “I never got to see you leave, dear father. You never handed me over to Ram. Then, gathering himself, he rose and said, ‘Mother, tell me the reason for my father’s death.’”
essence: Loss first breaks the heart; then it demands an explanation.
simple_meaning: Bharat grieves that he could not see his father’s final departure and that Dasharath did not entrust him to Ram. After steadying himself, he asks Kaikeyi why his father died.
insight: It shows grief moving from raw lament to a search for cause and responsibility.
modern_relevance: You miss the last call, the last message, the last chance to say goodbye. Later, after the shock settles, you finally ask the question you were avoiding: what happened?
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: सुनि सुत बचन कहति कैकेई। मरमु पाँछि जनु माहुर देई॥ आदिहु तें सब आपनि करनी। कुटिल कठोर मुदित मन बरनी ॥
translation: पुत्र का वचन सुनकर कैकेयी कहने लगी। मानो मर्म स्थान को पाछकर (चाकू से चीरकर) उसमें जहर भर रही हो। कुटिल और कठोर कैकेयी ने अपनी सब करनी शुरू से (आखिर तक बड़े) प्रसन्न मन से सुना दी ॥
english_translation: Hearing her son’s words, Kaikeyi began to speak. It was as if she were stabbing the wound and pouring poison into it. Crooked, harsh Kaikeyi recounted all her deeds from the very beginning with a pleased mind.
essence: Pride can make you poison your own wound.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi calmly repeats the very actions that caused the disaster, as if she has no tenderness left in her heart.
insight: It shows how the unexamined mind can keep justifying harm instead of seeing it clearly.
modern_relevance: Someone in a family argument keeps replaying old choices with a strange pride, making the hurt deeper each time. The verse captures that chilling lack of self-awareness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरतहि बिसरेउ पितु मरन सुनत राम बन गौनु। हेतु अपनपउ जानि जियँ थकित रहे धरि मौनु ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का वन जाना सुनकर भरतजी को पिता का मरण भूल गया और हृदय में इस सारे अनर्थ का कारण अपने को ही जानकर वे मौन होकर स्तम्भित रह गए (अर्थात उनकी बोली बंद हो गई और वे सन्न रह गए) ॥
english_translation: Hearing that Ram had gone to the forest, Bharat forgot his father's death and stood silent, realizing in his heart that he himself was the cause of this disaster.
essence: Guilt can make even grief disappear.
simple_meaning: Bharat is so shocked by Ram's exile that even his father's death fades from his mind. He blames himself and falls silent.
insight: It shifts attention from outward loss to inward responsibility, showing how guilt can eclipse every other feeling.
modern_relevance: You read the message that changed everything, and your first thought is, 'This is my fault.' The room goes quiet, and even your own pain feels secondary.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिकल बिलोकि सुतहि समुझावति। मनहुँ जरे पर लोनु लगावति॥ तात राउ नहिं सोचै जोगू। बिढ़इ सुकृत जसु कीन्हेउ भोगू ॥
translation: पुत्र को व्याकुल देखकर कैकेयी समझाने लगी। मानो जले पर नमक लगा रही हो। (वह बोली-) हे तात! राजा सोच करने योग्य नहीं हैं। उन्होंने पुण्य और यश कमाकर उसका पर्याप्त भोग किया ॥
english_translation: Seeing her son agitated, Kaikeyi tried to console him, as if rubbing salt into a burn. She said, “Dear child, a king is not meant for sorrow. He has already enjoyed the full fruit of his merit and fame.”
essence: Words meant to soothe can cut deeper than silence.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi comforts her son by saying that a king should not grieve and has already received the reward of his good deeds and fame.
insight: It shows how misplaced consolation can feel cruel when someone is grieving.
modern_relevance: Someone tells you to “move on” five minutes after your world has cracked. The words may be neat, but they can land like salt on an open wound.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जीवत सकल जनम फल पाए। अंत अमरपति सदन सिधाए॥ अस अनुमानि सोच परिहरहू। सहित समाज राज पुर करहू ॥
translation: जीवनकाल में ही उन्होंने जन्म लेने के सम्पूर्ण फल पा लिए और अंत में वे इन्द्रलोक को चले गए। ऐसा विचारकर सोच छोड़ दो और समाज सहित नगर का राज्य करो ॥
english_translation: They had already reaped the full fruit of life, and in the end they went to the abode of Indra. Thinking this way, let go of sorrow and, with the assembly, govern the city and kingdom.
essence: Loss can be honored without letting it stop your duty.
simple_meaning: The speaker says the dead king and queen had already lived a fulfilled life, so grief should be set aside and the kingdom should be managed with the people.
insight: It shifts the mind from being swallowed by grief to meeting the next duty with steadiness.
modern_relevance: After the funeral, someone still has to answer the phone, feed the children, and sign the papers. This verse speaks to the hard dignity of carrying on without pretending the loss did not happen.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: सुनि सुठि सहमेउ राजकुमारू। पाकें छत जनु लाग अँगारू॥ धीरज धरि भरि लेहिं उसासा। पापिनि सबहि भाँति कुल नासा ॥
translation: राजकुमार भरतजी यह सुनकर बहुत ही सहम गए। मानो पके घाव पर अँगार छू गया हो। उन्होंने धीरज धरकर बड़ी लम्बी साँस लेते हुए कहा- पापिनी! तूने सभी तरह से कुल का नाश कर दिया ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, the prince was deeply shaken, as if a spark had touched a healed wound. Gathering himself, he let out a long breath and said, 'Wicked woman, you have ruined the whole family in every way.'
essence: A hidden betrayal can strike like fire on old pain.
simple_meaning: Bharat is stunned by Kaikeyi’s words and struggles to steady himself before accusing her of destroying the family.
insight: It shows how sudden betrayal can overwhelm composure and force the truth into speech.
modern_relevance: You open a message and feel your stomach drop. Before you even speak, you know something precious has been broken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जौं पै कुरुचि रही अति तोही। जनमत काहे न मारे मोही॥ पेड़ काटि तैं पालउ सींचा। मीन जिअन निति बारि उलीचा ॥
translation: हाय! यदि तेरी ऐसी ही अत्यन्त बुरी रुचि (दुष्ट इच्छा) थी, तो तूने जन्मते ही मुझे मार क्यों नहीं डाला? तूने पेड़ को काटकर पत्ते को सींचा है और मछली के जीने के लिए पानी को उलीच डाला! (अर्थात मेरा हित करने जाकर उलटा तूने मेरा अहित कर डाला) ॥
english_translation: If your heart was so cruel, why didn't you kill me at birth? You cut the tree and watered the leaves, and you spilled water for a fish to live!
essence: Good intentions become cruelty when they destroy what they meant to protect.
simple_meaning: Bharat, overwhelmed by grief, says his mother’s actions were meant to help but only harmed him. He feels her care has brought the opposite of what she intended.
insight: It exposes how misplaced care can become harm, and how grief speaks in bitter images.
modern_relevance: You hear a parent say, 'I did this for your future,' but the result is wreckage. In that moment, intention means nothing beside the wound left behind.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: हंसबंसु दसरथु जनकु राम लखन से भाइ। जननी तूँ जननी भई बिधि सन कछु न बसाइ ॥
translation: मुझे सूर्यवंश (सा वंश), दशरथजी (सरीखे) पिता और राम-लक्ष्मण से भाई मिले। पर हे जननी! मुझे जन्म देने वाली माता तू हुई! (क्या किया जाए!) विधाता से कुछ भी वश नहीं चलता ॥
english_translation: I was born into the solar lineage, with Dasharath as father and Ram and Lakshman as brothers. But, mother, you were the one who gave me birth. What can be done when fate itself does not obey anyone?
essence: Even a blessed life can be shattered by one painful choice.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he was blessed with the best family, but his real pain is that his mother caused the exile. He ends by saying no one can control what fate allows.
insight: It captures the ache of betrayal inside a loving family and the helplessness of watching events move beyond your control.
modern_relevance: You find out, after the family argument, that the person you trusted most helped trigger the damage. In that moment, gratitude and betrayal can exist side by side.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जब मैं कुमति कुमत जियँ ठयऊ। खंड खंड होइ हृदउ न गयऊ॥ बर मागत मन भइ नहिं पीरा। गरि न जीह मुँह परेउ न कीरा ॥
translation: अरी कुमति! जब तूने हृदय में यह बुरा विचार (निश्चय) ठाना, उसी समय तेरे हृदय के टुकड़े-टुकड़े (क्यों) न हो गए? वरदान माँगते समय तेरे मन में कुछ भी पीड़ा नहीं हुई? तेरी जीभ गल नहीं गई? तेरे मुँह में कीड़े नहीं पड़ गए? ॥
english_translation: When I formed such evil intent in my heart, why did my heart not split apart? When I asked for the boon, why did my mind feel no pain? Why did my tongue not rot, and why did worms not fall into my mouth?
essence: A wrong intention can feel so vile that the heart itself should reject it.
simple_meaning: The speaker curses a cruel thought and says it should have destroyed the heart, mind, tongue, and mouth the moment it arose.
insight: It exposes how a single poisoned intention can feel unbearable once its consequences begin.
modern_relevance: You send the text, then stare at the screen wishing you could pull it back. The regret hits after the damage is done, not before.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: भूपँ प्रतीति तोरि किमि कीन्ही। मरन काल बिधि मति हरि लीन्ही॥ बिधिहुँ न नारि हृदय गति जानी। सकल कपट अघ अवगुन खानी ॥
translation: राजा ने तेरा विश्वास कैसे कर लिया? (जान पड़ता है,) विधाता ने मरने के समय उनकी बुद्धि हर ली थी। स्त्रियों के हृदय की गति (चाल) विधाता भी नहीं जान सके। वह सम्पूर्ण कपट, पाप और अवगुणों की खान है ॥
english_translation: How did the king come to trust you? At the time of death, fate took away his judgment. Even fate could not understand a woman's heart. It is a mine of deceit, fault, and flaws.
essence: Fear and blame can disguise themselves as certainty.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi blames the king’s trust and questions the nature of women’s hearts, calling them full of deceit and flaws.
insight: It shifts attention from the claim itself to the mind that is trying to protect itself through blame.
modern_relevance: After a family argument, someone starts rewriting the whole story to make themselves look right. Old hurt turns into harsh generalisations, and the real issue gets buried.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: सरल सुसील धरम रत राऊ। सो किमि जानै तीय सुभाऊ॥ अस को जीव जंतु जग माहीं। जेहि रघुनाथ प्रानप्रिय नाहीं ॥
translation: फिर राजा तो सीधे, सुशील और धर्मपरायण थे। वे भला, स्त्री स्वभाव को कैसे जानते? अरे, जगत के जीव-जन्तुओं में ऐसा कौन है, जिसे श्री रघुनाथजी प्राणों के समान प्यारे नहीं हैं ॥
english_translation: The king was simple, virtuous, and devoted to dharma. How could he understand a woman's nature? And who in the world is not dear to Raghunath as life itself?
essence: A virtuous heart can still miss deception, while Ram is universally beloved.
simple_meaning: Dasharath was gentle, virtuous, and devoted to dharma, so he could not understand Kaikeyi's mind. At the same time, Ram is dear to every living being.
insight: It shifts you from judging only character to noticing how innocence can miss what is hiding in plain sight.
modern_relevance: You trusted someone because they always seemed decent, and only later saw how little they understood the person beside them. At the same time, some people are simply loved by everyone who meets them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भे अति अहित रामु तेउ तोहीं। को तू अहसि सत्य कहु मोही॥ जो हसि सो हसि मुँह मसि लाई। आँखि ओट उठि बैठहि जाई ॥
translation: वे श्री रामजी भी तुझे अहित हो गए (वैरी लगे)! तू कौन है? मुझे सच-सच कह! तू जो है, सो है, अब मुँह में स्याही पोतकर (मुँह काला करके) उठकर मेरी आँखों की ओट में जा बैठ ॥
english_translation: Even Ram has become your enemy. Who are you? Tell me the truth. You are what you are—go blacken your face and sit out of sight.
essence: Mockery erupts when truth is too painful to face.
simple_meaning: The speaker is mocking someone as a liar and enemy of Ram, demanding the person admit the truth and disappear from sight.
insight: It shows how anger tries to punish dishonesty by shaming the person instead of resolving the wound.
modern_relevance: A heated argument spills into insults, and suddenly the real issue is buried under mockery. The verse captures how quickly wounded pride turns truth into attack.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: राम बिरोधी हृदय तें प्रगट कीन्ह बिधि मोहि। मो समान को पातकी बादि कहउँ कछु तोहि ॥
translation: विधाता ने मुझे श्री रामजी से विरोध करने वाले (तेरे) हृदय से उत्पन्न किया (अथवा विधाता ने मुझे हृदय से राम का विरोधी जाहिर कर दिया।) मेरे बराबर पापी दूसरा कौन है? मैं व्यर्थ ही तुझे कुछ कहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: The creator made me from a heart opposed to Ram. Who is as sinful as I am? I speak to you in vain.
essence: Self-condemnation is the first honest response to betraying Ram.
simple_meaning: The speaker says he was brought forth from a heart that opposes Ram, and that no one is as blameworthy as he is.
insight: It shifts blame outward into self-recognition, where remorse becomes more important than argument.
modern_relevance: You realize, mid-argument, that your own resistance caused the mess. The urge to defend yourself drops, and all that remains is honest regret.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सुनि सत्रुघुन मातु कुटिलाई। जरहिं गात रिस कछु न बसाई॥ तेहि अवसर कुबरी तहँ आई। बसन बिभूषन बिबिध बनाई ॥
translation: माता की कुटिलता सुनकर शत्रुघ्नजी के सब अंग क्रोध से जल रहे हैं, पर कुछ वश नहीं चलता। उसी समय भाँति-भाँति के कपड़ों और गहनों से सजकर कुबरी (मंथरा) वहाँ आई ॥
english_translation: Hearing of the queen's crookedness, Shatrughna's body burned with anger, but he could not control it. At that moment, Kubri came there dressed in many kinds of clothes and ornaments.
essence: Anger rises first; action comes only when the next spark arrives.
simple_meaning: Shatrughna hears of the queen's deceit and burns with anger. Before he can act, Manthara arrives dressed up in ornaments.
insight: It shows the instant when outrage gathers force, but the scene is still waiting to explode.
modern_relevance: You hear a betrayal in the middle of the day, and your whole body tightens before you even speak. The next person walking in can either calm the room or ignite it further.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लखि रिस भरेउ लखन लघु भाई। बरत अनल घृत आहुति पाई॥ हुमगि लात तकि कूबर मारा। परि मुँह भर महि करत पुकारा ॥
translation: उसे (सजी) देखकर लक्ष्मण के छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्नजी क्रोध में भर गए। मानो जलती हुई आग को घी की आहुति मिल गई हो। उन्होंने जोर से तककर कूबड़ पर एक लात जमा दी। वह चिल्लाती हुई मुँह के बल जमीन पर गिर पड़ी ॥
english_translation: Seeing her, Lakshman’s younger brother was filled with rage, like fire meeting a fresh offering of ghee. He sprang up, aimed a kick at her hump, and she fell face-first, crying out.
essence: Rage, once fed, moves faster than thought.
simple_meaning: Shatrughna’s anger flares at the sight of the hunchback woman, and he kicks her down in a burst of rage.
insight: It shows how quickly resentment becomes action when anger is left unchecked.
modern_relevance: You read one cruel message and your body is already hot, your fingers already moving. In that split second, damage can happen before thought returns.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कूबर टूटेउ फूट कपारू। दलित दसन मुख रुधिर प्रचारू॥ आह दइअ मैं काह नसावा। करत नीक फलु अनइस पावा ॥
translation: उसका कूबड़ टूट गया, कपाल फूट गया, दाँत टूट गए और मुँह से खून बहने लगा। (वह कराहती हुई बोली-) हाय दैव! मैंने क्या बिगाड़ा? जो भला करते बुरा फल पाया ॥
english_translation: Her hump was broken, her skull split, her teeth smashed, and blood streamed from her mouth. Crying out, she said, “Alas, what wrong have I done? I did good and got a cruel result.”
essence: Harm done to others can return and wound you first.
simple_meaning: She is badly injured and cries that she did good but received a bad result.
insight: It shows how harmful schemes can rebound on the one who set them in motion.
modern_relevance: You spend weeks stirring trouble in a group chat, then the blowback lands on you first. The damage feels sudden, but it was already set in motion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि रिपुहन लखि नख सिख खोटी। लगे घसीटन धरि धरि झोंटी॥ भरत दयानिधि दीन्हि छुड़ाई। कौसल्या पहिं गे दोउ भाई ॥
translation: उसकी यह बात सुनकर और उसे नख से शिखा तक दुष्ट जानकर शत्रुघ्नजी झोंटा पकड़-पकड़कर उसे घसीटने लगे। तब दयानिधि भरतजी ने उसको छुड़ा दिया और दोनों भाई (तुरंत) कौसल्याजी के पास गए ॥
english_translation: Hearing her words and seeing her wickedness from head to toe, Shatrughna began dragging her by the hair. Then merciful Bharat freed her, and both brothers went to Kaushalya.
essence: Mercy can stop anger before it becomes harm.
simple_meaning: Shatrughna sees the woman as evil and drags her by the hair, but Bharat stops him and sends both brothers to Kaushalya.
insight: It shifts you from retaliating at once to letting mercy interrupt escalation.
modern_relevance: You catch someone in the middle of a cruel outburst and feel your own anger rising. Then one calmer person steps in, breaks the chain, and keeps the moment from becoming worse.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मलिन बसन बिबरन बिकल कृस शरीर दुख भार। कनक कलप बर बेलि बन मानहुँ हनी तुसार ॥
translation: कौसल्याजी मैले वस्त्र पहने हैं, चेहरे का रंग बदला हुआ है, व्याकुल हो रही हैं, दुःख के बोझ से शरीर सूख गया है। ऐसी दिख रही हैं मानो सोने की सुंदर कल्पलता को वन में पाला मार गया हो ॥
english_translation: Kaushalya wears soiled clothes, her face has lost its color, she is restless, and grief has dried her body. She looks like a golden wish-fulfilling vine struck by frost in the forest.
