essence: Grief can make living beauty look frostbitten.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya is so worn down by grief that she looks physically faded and weakened, like a beautiful vine damaged by frost.
insight: It turns sorrow into a visible, bodily reality rather than an abstract feeling.
modern_relevance: You spot someone at the hospital waiting room after a sleepless night: wrinkled clothes, hollow eyes, a body that looks older than yesterday. Loss does that before words can.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरतहि देखि मातु उठि धाई। मुरुचित अवनि परी झइँ आई॥ देखत भरतु बिकल भए भारी। परे चरन तन दसा बिसारी ॥
translation: भरत को देखते ही माता कौसल्याजी उठ दौड़ीं। पर चक्कर आ जाने से मूर्च्छित होकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ीं। यह देखते ही भरतजी बड़े व्याकुल हो गए और शरीर की सुध भुलाकर चरणों में गिर पड़े ॥
english_translation: Seeing Bharata, Mother Kausalya rushed to him. She fainted and fell to the ground. Seeing this, Bharata was overwhelmed with grief and, forgetting himself, fell at her feet.
essence: Grief can bring both the mother and son to their knees.
simple_meaning: Kausalya runs to Bharata and faints from emotion. Bharata is so shaken by her grief that he falls at her feet, forgetting his own body.
insight: It shifts attention from action to emotional presence, showing that grief is sometimes met by silent surrender.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room and see your mother break down at the sight of you. In that instant, all your plans disappear; only love and helplessness remain.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मातु तात कहँ देहि देखाई। कहँ सिय रामु लखनु दोउ भाई॥ कैकइ कत जनमी जग माझा। जौं जनमि त भइ काहे न बाँझा ॥
translation: (फिर बोले-) माता! पिताजी कहाँ हैं? उन्हें दिखा दें। सीताजी तथा मेरे दोनों भाई श्री राम-लक्ष्मण कहाँ हैं? (उन्हें दिखा दें।) कैकेयी जगत में क्यों जनमी! और यदि जनमी ही तो फिर बाँझ क्यों न हुई?- ॥
english_translation: “Mother, Father, please show me where they are. Where are Sita and my two brothers, Ram and Lakshman? Why was Kaikeyi born into this world at all? If she was born, why was she not born barren?”
essence: Separation makes even a noble heart cry out in bitterness.
simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed with grief and asks to be shown his parents, Sita, Ram, and Lakshman. In his pain, he blames Kaikeyi for the ruin of the family.
insight: It reveals how sorrow narrows attention to absence and turns pain into blame.
modern_relevance: You walk into a house after a funeral and ask for the people who should still be there. The question is simple; the loss behind it is not.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: कुल कलंकु जेहिं जनमेउ मोही। अपजस भाजन प्रियजन द्रोही॥ को तिभुवन मोहि सरिस अभागी। गति असि तोरि मातुजेहि लागी ॥
translation: जिसने कुल के कलंक, अपयश के भाँडे और प्रियजनों के द्रोही मुझ जैसे पुत्र को उत्पन्न किया। तीनों लोकों में मेरे समान अभागा कौन है? जिसके कारण हे माता! तेरी यह दशा हुई! ॥
english_translation: The one who gave birth to me is a stain on the family, a source of disgrace, and a traitor to loved ones. Who in the three worlds is as unlucky as I am? Mother, because of me you have come to this state.
essence: Grief makes Bharat see himself as the cause of all suffering.
simple_meaning: Bharat blames himself completely for the suffering around him. He sees himself as the cause of his mother's condition and the family’s disgrace.
insight: It reveals how grief and guilt collapse into self-condemnation, making a person take responsibility for everything.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a family argument and feel everyone’s pain land on you at once. Even the parts you didn’t cause start to feel like your fault.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: पितु सुरपुर बन रघुबर केतू। मैं केवल सब अनरथ हेतू॥ धिग मोहि भयउँ बेनु बन आगी। दुसह दाह दुख दूषन भागी ॥
translation: पिताजी स्वर्ग में हैं और श्री रामजी वन में हैं। केतु के समान केवल मैं ही इन सब अनर्थों का कारण हूँ। मुझे धिक्कार है! मैं बाँस के वन में आग उत्पन्न हुआ और कठिन दाह, दुःख और दोषों का भागी बना ॥
english_translation: My father is in heaven and Raghubar is in the forest. I alone am the cause of all these calamities. Shame on me! I was born like fire in a bamboo grove, bringing unbearable burning, sorrow, and ruin.
essence: Grief can make you mistake yourself for the cause of everything.
simple_meaning: Bharat blames himself completely for the exile and family ruin. He sees himself as the source of all suffering and feels deep shame.
insight: It reveals how grief can distort judgment, turning sorrow into self-blame and collapsing the whole world into one wounded self.
modern_relevance: You replay one bad decision at 2 a.m. and suddenly every problem feels like your fault. Bharat’s grief shows how pain can turn into total self-condemnation.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: मातु भरत के बचन मृदु सुनि पुनि उठी सँभारि। लिए उठाइ लगाइ उर लोचन मोचति बारि ॥
translation: भरतजी के कोमल वचन सुनकर माता कौसल्याजी फिर सँभलकर उठीं। उन्होंने भरत को उठाकर छाती से लगा लिया और नेत्रों से आँसू बहाने लगीं ॥
english_translation: Hearing Bharata's gentle words, Mother Kaushalya gathered herself and rose again. She lifted Bharata into her arms, held him to her chest, and tears flowed from her eyes.
essence: Tender words can melt grief into embrace.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya hears Bharata's soft words, regains herself, hugs him close, and cries. Her grief and love overflow together.
insight: It shifts you from blame to tenderness, showing how grief can open into care.
modern_relevance: You hear your child finally say the honest thing they've been carrying. Your anger softens, and the hug comes before the explanation does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सरल सुभाय मायँ हियँ लाए। अति हित मनहुँ राम फिरि आए॥ भेंटेउ बहुरि लखन लघु भाई। सोकु सनेहु न हृदयँ समाई ॥
translation: सरल स्वभाव वाली माता ने बड़े प्रेम से भरतजी को छाती से लगा लिया, मानो श्री रामजी ही लौटकर आ गए हों। फिर लक्ष्मणजी के छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न को हृदय से लगाया। शोक और स्नेह हृदय में समाता नहीं है ॥
english_translation: With a gentle nature, the mother embraced Bharata to her heart, as if Ram himself had returned. Then she embraced Shatrughna, Lakshmana's younger brother. Grief and affection could not fit together in her heart.
essence: A grieving heart still reaches for the people it loves.
simple_meaning: Kausalya embraces Bharata like returning Ram, then holds Shatrughna close. Her heart is too full to hold both grief and love at once.
insight: It shows how grief can live beside affection without either one disappearing.
modern_relevance: You see a child after a long absence and hug them too hard, half-relieved and half-breaking inside. Some reunions carry both comfort and grief in the same breath.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि सुभाउ कहत सबु कोई। राम मातु अस काहे न होई॥ माताँ भरतु गोद बैठारे। आँसु पोछिं मृदु बचन उचारे ॥
translation: कौसल्याजी का स्वभाव देखकर सब कोई कह रहे हैं- श्री राम की माता का ऐसा स्वभाव क्यों न हो। माता ने भरतजी को गोद में बैठा लिया और उनके आँसू पोंछकर कोमल वचन बोलीं- ॥
english_translation: Seeing her nature, everyone said, “Why should Ram’s mother not be like this?” The mother seated Bharat in her lap, wiped away his tears, and spoke gently.
essence: A mother's tenderness can turn grief into belonging.
simple_meaning: Kausalya’s tenderness is so complete that everyone sees why Ram came from her. She comforts Bharat like her own child, wiping his tears and speaking softly.
insight: It shifts the response from judgment to shelter, showing how care can steady a shaken heart.
modern_relevance: Your younger brother shows up after a family fight, eyes red, trying to act fine. You pull him close, hand him water, and let your softness do what arguments cannot.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अजहुँ बच्छ बलि धीरज धरहू। कुसमउ समुझि सोक परिहरहू॥ जनि मानहु हियँ हानि गलानी। काल करम गति अघटित जानी ॥
translation: हे वत्स! मैं बलैया लेती हूँ। तुम अब भी धीरज धरो। बुरा समय जानकर शोक त्याग दो। काल और कर्म की गति अमिट जानकर हृदय में हानि और ग्लानि मत मानो ॥
english_translation: O child, I bless you. Still, keep your courage. Seeing the wrong season, let go of grief. Knowing the movement of time and action as unfathomable, do not carry loss or shame in your heart.
essence: Not every loss is yours to carry as guilt.
simple_meaning: Kausalya comforts Bharata by telling him to stay brave, release grief, and not blame himself for what time and action have brought.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame to calm endurance when life turns harsh.
modern_relevance: You sit on the edge of your bed after a family argument, replaying every sentence and wondering what you ruined. This verse says not every wound is proof of your failure.
speaker: Kausalya

verse_text: काहुहि दोसु देहु जनि ताता। भा मोहि सब बिधि बाम बिधाता॥ जो एतेहुँ दुख मोहि जिआवा। अजहुँ को जानइ का तेहि भावा ॥
translation: हे तात! किसी को दोष मत दो। विधाता मेरे िलए सब प्रकार से उलटा हो गया है, जो इतने दुःख पर भी मुझे जिला रहा है। अब भी कौन जानता है, उसे क्या भा रहा है? ॥
english_translation: Father, do not blame anyone. Fate has turned against me in every way, yet it still keeps me alive through this suffering. Who can know what it truly intends?
essence: Blame falls away when you admit life is moving beyond your control.
simple_meaning: She asks Bharat not to blame anyone and says her life feels turned upside down, yet she is still being kept alive. She admits no one can know what the hidden order truly wants.
insight: It shifts the mind from blaming people to facing the mystery of what life is doing.
modern_relevance: You get the call at midnight and everything changes, but no one can explain why it happened. Before the blame starts flying, this verse asks you to pause and face the confusion honestly.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: पितु आयस भूषन बसन तात तजे रघुबीर। बिसमउ हरषु न हृदयँ कछु पहिरे बलकल चीर ॥
translation: हे तात! पिता की आज्ञा से श्री रघुवीर ने भूषण-वस्त्र त्याग दिए और वल्कल वस्त्र पहन लिए। उनके हृदय में न कुछ विषाद था, न हर्ष! ॥
english_translation: O father, by his father's command, Raghubir gave up ornaments and fine clothes and put on bark garments. His heart held neither sorrow nor joy.
essence: Duty stays intact even when all outward honor is stripped away.
simple_meaning: Ram obeys his father's command, gives up royal clothes, and puts on bark garments. He does it without inner excitement or grief.
insight: It shifts attention from outer status to inner steadiness under obligation.
modern_relevance: You pack away the suit, the title, the polished image, and walk into the harder role anyway. What matters is not the outfit, but the steadiness you bring with it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुख प्रसन्न मन रंग न रोषू। सब कर सब बिधि करि परितोषू॥ चले बिपिन सुनि सिय सँग लागी। रहइ न राम चरन अनुरागी ॥
translation: उनका मुख प्रसन्न था, मन में न आसक्ति थी, न रोष (द्वेष)। सबका सब तरह से संतोष कराकर वे वन को चले। यह सुनकर सीता भी उनके साथ लग गईं। श्रीराम के चरणों की अनुरागिणी वे किसी तरह न रहीं ॥
english_translation: His face was cheerful, his mind free of attachment and anger. After pleasing everyone in every way, he went to the forest. Hearing this, Sita too followed him, and she could no longer stay apart from Ram’s feet.
essence: Calm dignity can carry love through exile.
simple_meaning: Ram leaves for the forest with a calm face and an untroubled mind, having satisfied everyone as much as possible. Sita hears this and follows him, unable to stay away from his feet.
insight: It shifts the reader from reactive hurt to composed acceptance, showing that love can move without complaint.
modern_relevance: You get the news you dreaded, and your face still has to meet the room. This verse shows how calm dignity can carry you through a painful turn without turning cruel.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनतहिं लखनु चले उठि साथा। रहहिं न जतन किए रघुनाथा॥ तब रघुपति सबही सिरु नाई। चले संग सिय अरु लघु भाई ॥
translation: सुनते ही लक्ष्मण भी साथ ही उठ चले। श्री रघुनाथ ने उन्हें रोकने के बहुत यत्न किए, पर वे न रहे। तब श्री रघुनाथजी सबको सिर नवाकर सीता और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण को साथ लेकर चले गए ॥
english_translation: As soon as he heard, Lakshman rose and went along. Raghunath tried many ways to stop him, but he would not stay. Then Raghupati bowed to everyone and left with Sita and his younger brother.
essence: Loyalty moves Lakshman faster than hesitation can speak.
simple_meaning: Lakshman immediately follows Ram, and Ram, after trying to stop him, leaves with Sita and Lakshman, bowing to everyone first.
insight: It shows how true loyalty answers before hesitation and chooses presence over convenience.
modern_relevance: Your best friend says, “Don’t come, I can manage.” You still grab your bag and go anyway. Some loyalties move before thought does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामु लखनु सिय बनहि सिधाए। गइउँ न संग न प्रान पठाए॥ यहु सबु भा इन्ह आँखिन्ह आगें। तउ न तजा तनु जीव अभागें ॥
translation: श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीता वन को चले गए। मैं न तो साथ ही गई और न मैंने अपने प्राण ही उनके साथ भेजे। यह सब इन्हीं आँखों के सामने हुआ, तो भी अभागे जीव ने शरीर नहीं छोड़ा ॥
english_translation: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita went to the forest. I did not go with them, nor did I send my life with them. All this happened before my eyes, yet this unlucky body did not leave.
essence: Some losses are witnessed too late to prevent, and still impossible to bear.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is overwhelmed by regret. She says Ram, Lakshman, and Sita left for the forest before her eyes, yet she still could not let her body die.
insight: It shows how guilt can outlive the moment of action and harden into bodily grief.
modern_relevance: You watch the person you pushed away walk out the door, and the silence after feels heavier than the argument. The mind keeps replaying what cannot be undone.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: मोहि न लाज निज नेहु निहारी। राम सरिस सुत मैं महतारी॥ जिऐ मरै भल भूपति जाना। मोर हृदय सत कुलिस समाना ॥
translation: अपने स्नेह की ओर देखकर मुझे लाज नहीं आती; राम सरीखे पुत्र की मैं माता! जीना और मरना तो राजा ने खूब जाना। मेरा हृदय तो सैकड़ों वज्रों के समान कठोर है ॥
english_translation: Looking at my own love, I feel no shame: I am the mother of a son like Ram. The king knows how to live and die; my heart is as hard as hundreds of thunderbolts.
essence: A mother’s pride in Ram survives even the crushing blow of separation.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya says she feels no shame in her love for Ram. She is proud to be the mother of a son like him, while her heart has become unbearably hard from grief.
insight: It shows how devotion can coexist with unbearable grief without becoming self-pity.
modern_relevance: You watch your child leave for a life you cannot protect, and pride and pain arrive together. You don't apologize for loving deeply, even when that love hurts.
speaker: Kaushalya

verse_text: कौसल्या के बचन सुनि भरत सहित रनिवासु। ब्याकुल बिलपत राजगृह मानहुँ सोक नेवासु ॥
translation: कौसल्याजी के वचनों को सुनकर भरत सहित सारा रनिवास व्याकुल होकर विलाप करने लगा। राजमहल मानो शोक का निवास बन गया ॥
english_translation: Hearing Kausalya's words, Bharata and the whole royal household were overwhelmed and began to lament. The royal palace became like a dwelling of grief.
essence: Grief, once spoken aloud, fills every corner of the home.
simple_meaning: Kausalya's words shake Bharata and everyone in the palace. Their grief fills the whole royal house.
insight: It shows how one truthful sorrow can spread through an entire household and make denial impossible.
modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after one honest message about loss. No one needs to explain it — the whole room has already changed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिलपहिं बिकल भरत दोउ भाई। कौसल्याँ लिए हृदयँ लगाई॥ भाँति अनेक भरतु समुझाए। कहि बिबेकमय बचन सुनाए ॥
translation: भरत, शत्रुघ्न दोनों भाई विकल होकर विलाप करने लगे। तब कौसल्याजी ने उनको हृदय से लगा लिया। अनेकों प्रकार से भरतजी को समझाया और बहुत सी विवेकभरी बातें उन्हें कहकर सुनाईं ॥
english_translation: Bharat and Shatrughna, both distraught brothers, wept. Kausalya drew them close to her heart and, in many ways, consoled Bharat with wise words.
essence: Comfort begins with closeness, not correction.
simple_meaning: Bharat and Shatrughna are overwhelmed with grief. Kausalya holds them close and comforts Bharat with wise, calming words.
insight: It shows that pain often needs embrace first, explanation second.
modern_relevance: Your younger brother is crying in the kitchen after bad news, and you stop everything just to hold him. Before advice, before fixing, presence itself becomes the first mercy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरतहुँ मातु सकल समुझाईं। कहि पुरान श्रुति कथा सुहाईं॥ छल बिहीन सुचि सरल सुबानी। बोले भरत जोरि जुग पानी ॥
translation: भरतजी ने भी सब माताओं को पुराण और वेदों की सुंदर कथाएँ कहकर समझाया। दोनों हाथ जोड़कर भरतजी छलरहित, पवित्र और सीधी सुंदर वाणी बोले- ॥
english_translation: Bharat also comforted all the mothers by telling them beautiful stories from the Puranas and the Vedas. With both hands joined, Bharat spoke in pure, simple, deceit-free, and beautiful words.
essence: Gentle truth can steady even a house in grief.
simple_meaning: Bharat comforts the grieving women with sacred stories and speaks to them with honest, gentle words.
insight: It shows that calm, truthful speech can hold a room that is breaking apart.
modern_relevance: You sit beside a crying parent after bad news, and you do not try to fix everything. You speak simply, honestly, and let your steadiness do the comforting.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जे अघ मातु पिता सुत मारें। गाइ गोठ महिसुर पुर जारें॥ जे अघ तिय बालक बध कीन्हें। मीत महीपति माहुर दीन्हें ॥
translation: जो पाप माता-पिता और पुत्र के मारने से होते हैं और जो गोशाला और ब्राह्मणों के नगर जलाने से होते हैं, जो पाप स्त्री और बालक की हत्या करने से होते हैं और जो मित्र और राजा को जहर देने से होते हैं- ॥
english_translation: The sins of killing mother, father, or child; burning a cowshed or a city of the learned; killing women and children; and poisoning a friend or king—
essence: Some harms are so grave they need no embellishment.
simple_meaning: It lists terrible acts of violence and betrayal: killing family members, burning sacred places, harming women and children, and poisoning trusted people.
insight: It sharpens moral speech by naming the darkest forms of harm without softening them.
modern_relevance: A family feud turns vicious, and someone says the unforgivable out loud: not every wound is accidental. Some betrayals are so grave they leave no room for excuses.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जे पातक उपपातक अहहीं। करम बचन मन भव कबि कहहीं॥ ते पातक मोहि होहुँ बिधाता। जौं यहु होइ मोर मत माता ॥
translation: कर्म, वचन और मन से होने वाले जितने पातक एवं उपपातक (बड़े-छोटे पाप) हैं, जिनको कवि लोग कहते हैं, हे विधाता! यदि इस काम में मेरा मत हो, तो हे माता! वे सब पाप मुझे लगें ॥
english_translation: Whatever major and minor sins arise through action, speech, and mind, as poets describe, may all of those sins fall on me, O Creator, if this is my mother's wish.
essence: Bharat would rather carry blame than let family loyalty break.
simple_meaning: Bharat is so devoted to his mother’s wishes that he is willing to take responsibility for any wrongdoing tied to this decision.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to sacrificial responsibility.
modern_relevance: You sit at the dinner table after a family decision has gone badly, and everyone is blaming each other. Instead of defending your pride, you choose to carry the discomfort and keep the bond intact.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जे परिहरि हरि हर चरन भजहिं भूतगन घोर। तेहि कइ गति मोहि देउ बिधि जौं जननी मत मोर ॥
translation: जो लोग श्री हरि और श्री शंकरजी के चरणों को छोड़कर भयानक भूत-प्रेतों को भजते हैं, हे माता! यदि इसमें मेरा मत हो तो विधाता मुझे उनकी गति दे ॥
english_translation: Those who abandon Hari and Hara's feet and worship terrifying spirits—if this is my own view, O Mother, may the Creator give me their fate.
essence: Fearful worship cannot replace true refuge.
simple_meaning: People who turn away from Hari and Shiva and instead worship frightening spirits are choosing the wrong refuge. Tulsidas says he would accept their fate if that were his own view.
insight: It shifts devotion from fear-based seeking to clear refuge in what is worthy of trust.
modern_relevance: You are anxious at midnight and reach for whatever promises quick relief, even if it deepens the fear. This verse asks whether you are turning toward what truly shelters you, or toward what only feeds panic.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: बेचहिं बेदु धरमु दुहि लेहीं। पिसुन पराय पाप कहि देहीं॥ कपटी कुटिल कलहप्रिय क्रोधी। बेद बिदूषक बिस्व बिरोधी ॥
translation: जो लोग वेदों को बेचते हैं, धर्म को दुह लेते हैं, चुगलखोर हैं, दूसरों के पापों को कह देते हैं, जो कपटी, कुटिल, कलहप्रिय और क्रोधी हैं तथा जो वेदों की निंदा करने वाले और विश्वभर के विरोधी हैं, ॥
english_translation: Those who sell the Vedas, milk dharma dry, gossip about others' faults, and are deceitful, crooked, quarrelsome, angry, critics of the Vedas, and enemies of the world...
essence: Corruption shows itself first in how you speak and what you attack.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas is listing the kinds of people who would fall into terrible ruin: those who misuse sacred learning, exploit righteousness, spread gossip, and live in deceit, conflict, and anger.
insight: It trains you to recognise moral corruption by its speech, habits, and hostility before it spreads further.
modern_relevance: A group chat turns poisonous the moment someone starts trading in gossip, mockery, and outrage. The verse points to the kind of mind that feeds on conflict and slowly poisons every room it enters.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: लोभी लंपट लोलुपचारा। जे ताकहिं परधनु परदारा॥ पावौं मैं तिन्ह कै गति घोरा। जौं जननी यहु संमत मोरा ॥
translation: जो लोभी, लम्पट और लालचियों का आचरण करने वाले हैं, जो पराए धन और पराई स्त्री की ताक में रहते हैं, हे जननी! यदि इस काम में मेरी सम्मति हो तो मैं उनकी भयानक गति को पाऊँ ॥
english_translation: I would meet the terrible fate of those who are greedy, licentious, and always eyeing other people's wealth and women, if my mother agrees.
essence: Desire for what is not yours leads straight to ruin.
simple_meaning: Greed and desire for what belongs to others lead to a terrible downfall. Tulsidas says he would accept that fate if his mother approved.
insight: It shifts attention from tempting possession to the cost of desire itself.
modern_relevance: You open a private tab, then another, chasing what someone else has. The verse cuts through that restless hunger before it hardens into character.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जे नहिं साधुसंग अनुरागे। परमारथ पथ बिमुख अभागे॥ जे न भजहिं हरि नर तनु पाई। जिन्हहि न हरि हर सुजसु सोहाई ॥
translation: जिनका सत्संग में प्रेम नहीं है, जो अभागे परमार्थ के मार्ग से विमुख हैं, जो मनुष्य शरीर पाकर श्री हरि का भजन नहीं करते, जिनको हरि-हर (भगवान विष्णु और शंकरजी) का सुयश नहीं सुहाता, ॥
english_translation: Those who have no love for the company of the good, who are unfortunate and turn away from the path of the highest good; those who do not worship Hari even after receiving a human body, and whom the fame of Hari and Hara does not delight.
essence: Human life is wasted when Ram no longer draws your heart.
simple_meaning: A human life becomes empty when it avoids good company, turns away from what truly matters, and never turns toward Hari.
insight: It shifts attention from random desire to the habits that either nourish or waste a human life.
modern_relevance: You keep scrolling past the one friend who actually steadies you, then wonder why your mind feels scattered. This verse points straight at that drift: the people you keep close and what you praise shape your whole life.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तजि श्रुतिपंथु बाम पथ चलहीं। बंचक बिरचि बेष जगु छलहीं॥ तिन्ह कै गति मोहि संकर देऊ। जननी जौं यहु जानौं भेऊ ॥
translation: जो वेद मार्ग को छोड़कर वाम (वेद प्रतिकूल) मार्ग पर चलते हैं, जो ठग हैं और वेष बनाकर जगत को छलते हैं, हे माता! यदि मैं इस भेद को जानता भी होऊँ तो शंकरजी मुझे उन लोगों की गति दें ॥
english_translation: Those who leave the straight path of the Vedas and walk a crooked road, who are deceitful and disguise themselves to cheat the world—Mother, if I know such people, may Shiva give me their fate.
essence: False appearance corrupts the one who chooses it.
simple_meaning: Bharat rejects deceit, hypocrisy, and crooked conduct so strongly that he says he would rather be punished than understand such people.
insight: It trains you to see false appearance as a moral danger, not a clever survival skill.
modern_relevance: You sit through a meeting where everyone smiles, but half the room is performing. Bharat's words hit that moment hard: you can refuse the mask, even if it costs you approval.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: मातु भरत के बचन सुनि साँचे सरल सुभायँ। कहति राम प्रिय तात तुम्ह सदा बचन मन कायँ ॥
translation: माता कौसल्याजी भरतजी के स्वाभाविक ही सच्चे और सरल वचनों को सुनकर कहने लगीं- हे तात! तुम तो मन, वचन और शरीर से सदा ही श्री रामचन्द्र के प्यारे हो ॥
english_translation: Hearing Bharata's sincere, simple words, Mother Kaushalya said, “Dear son, you are always beloved to Ram in mind, speech, and body.”
essence: True love shows itself when mind, speech, and action all agree.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya tells Bharata that his honest, simple nature makes him always dear to Ram in thought, speech, and action.
insight: It shifts devotion from display to alignment: what matters is whether your whole being points the same way.
modern_relevance: You speak plainly to someone you love, with no hidden agenda. They feel it immediately — because your words, intentions, and actions all match.
speaker: Kaushalya

verse_text: राम प्रानहु तें प्रान तुम्हारे। तुम्ह रघुपतिहि प्रानहु तें प्यारे॥ बिधु बिष चवै स्रवै हिमु आगी। होइ बारिचर बारि बिरागी ॥
translation: श्री राम तुम्हारे प्राणों से भी बढ़कर प्राण (प्रिय) हैं और तुम भी श्री रघुनाथ को प्राणों से भी अधिक प्यारे हो। चन्द्रमा चाहे विष चुआने लगे और पाला आग बरसाने लगे, जलचर जीव जल से विरक्त हो जाए, ॥
english_translation: Ram is dearer to you than life itself, and you are dearer to Raghupati than life itself. If the moon dripped poison, if frost rained fire, if a water-dwelling creature grew indifferent to water, ...
essence: A true bond survives even when the world turns impossible.
simple_meaning: Kausalya tells Bharat that Ram is more precious to him than life, and Bharat is equally dear to Ram. Even impossible reversals in nature would be easier than changing that bond.
insight: It shifts attention from fragile social ties to a bond rooted in mutual devotion and steadfastness.
modern_relevance: You have a friend who would cross town at midnight just to sit with you after bad news. No one is keeping score, but both of you know the bond is real.
speaker: Kausalya

verse_text: भएँ ग्यानु बरु मिटै न मोहू। तुम्ह रामहि प्रतिकूल न होहू॥ मत तुम्हार यहु जो जग कहहीं। सो सपनेहुँ सुख सुगति न लहहीं ॥
translation: और ज्ञान हो जाने पर भी चाहे मोह न मिटे, पर तुम श्री रामचन्द्र के प्रतिकूल कभी नहीं हो सकते। इसमें तुम्हारी सम्मति है, जगत में जो कोई ऐसा कहते हैं, वे स्वप्न में भी सुख और शुभ गति नहीं पावेंगे ॥
english_translation: Even if knowledge arises and delusion does not fully fade, you can never stand against Ram. What the world says is your approval—those who say such a thing will not find happiness or a good end, even in a dream.
essence: Loyalty to Ram cannot be overturned by confusion or gossip.
simple_meaning: Even if confusion remains, you can still stay loyal to Ram. The world may speak wrongly about you, but that does not make it true.
insight: It shifts you from defending your image to trusting the integrity of your own loyalty.
modern_relevance: A family group chat starts spinning your choice into something ugly, and suddenly everyone has an opinion about your motives. This verse says their story does not define your heart.
speaker: Kausalya

verse_text: अस कहि मातु भरतु हिएँ लाए। थन पय स्रवहिं नयन जल छाए॥ करत बिलाप बहुत एहि भाँती। बैठेहिं बीति गई सब राती ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर माता कौसल्या ने भरतजी को हृदय से लगा लिया। उनके स्तनों से दूध बहने लगा और नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल छा गया। इस प्रकार बहुत विलाप करते हुए सारी रात बैठे ही बैठे बीत गई ॥
english_translation: Saying this, Mother Kaushalya drew Bharat into her heart. Milk flowed from her breasts and tears covered her eyes. In this way, they kept lamenting, and the whole night passed sitting there.
essence: Love can hold grief without fixing it.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya hugs Bharat and weeps with him all night. Their grief is so deep that even her body responds like a mother’s at the sight of her child.
insight: It shifts attention from solving grief to witnessing it with tenderness.
modern_relevance: You hold your brother after a funeral and neither of you knows what to say. Grief does not need polished language; sometimes it only needs an embrace that lasts through the night.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बामदेउ बसिष्ठ तब आए। सचिव महाजन सकल बोलाए॥ मुनि बहु भाँति भरत उपदेसे। कहि परमारथ बचन सुदेसे ॥
translation: तब वामदेवजी और वशिष्ठजी आए। उन्होंने सब मंत्रियों तथा महाजनों को बुलाया। फिर मुनि वशिष्ठजी ने परमार्थ के सुंदर समयानुकूल वचन कहकर बहुत प्रकार से भरतजी को उपदेश दिया ॥
english_translation: Then Vamadeva and Vashistha came. They called all the ministers and leading elders. The sage gave Bharat many kinds of instruction, speaking timely words of highest truth.
essence: Steady counsel gathers people when grief has made them unsteady.
simple_meaning: Vashistha and Vamadeva arrive, gather the ministers and elders, and begin guiding Bharat with timely, serious counsel.
insight: It shifts attention from emotional collapse to the responsibility of guiding the moment wisely.
modern_relevance: After a family crisis, everyone is exhausted, and the room is full of tears and unfinished decisions. Then the one steady elder speaks, gathers everyone, and names the next right step.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तात हृदयँ धीरजु धरहु करहु जो अवसर आजु। उठे भरत गुर बचन सुनि करन कहेउ सबु साजु ॥
translation: (वशिष्ठजी ने कहा-) हे तात! हृदय में धीरज धरो और आज जिस कार्य के करने का अवसर है, उसे करो। गुरुजी के वचन सुनकर भरतजी उठे और उन्होंने सब तैयारी करने के लिए कहा ॥
english_translation: O dear one, keep courage in your heart and do today what must be done. Hearing the guru's words, Bharata rose and said to make all the arrangements.
essence: Courage is holding steady long enough to do what the moment requires.
simple_meaning: Keep your heart steady and do the task in front of you. Bharata hears the guidance, rises at once, and begins the necessary arrangements.
insight: It shifts attention from emotional overwhelm to the one action the moment demands.
modern_relevance: Your phone rings with bad news, the house is full of crying, and someone still has to make the next call. This verse gives you one clean instruction: steady yourself and do the needed thing.
speaker: Vasishtha

verse_text: नृपतनु बेद बिदित अन्हवावा। परम बिचित्र बिमानु बनावा॥ गाहि पदभरत मातु सब राखी। रहीं रानि दरसन अभिलाषी ॥
translation: वेदों में बताई हुई विधि से राजा की देह को स्नान कराया गया और परम विचित्र विमान बनाया गया। भरतजी ने सब माताओं को चरण पकड़कर रखा (अर्थात प्रार्थना करके उनको सती होने से रोक लिया)। वे रानियाँ भी (श्री राम के) दर्शन की अभिलाषा से रह गईं ॥
english_translation: The king's body was bathed according to the Vedas, and a wondrous bier was prepared. Bharat held back all the queens by clasping their feet. The queens remained longing for Ram's darshan.
essence: Love sometimes protects by holding others back.
simple_meaning: Dasharath's body is prepared for the last rites, while Bharat stops the queens from joining him in death. Their hearts stay fixed on seeing Ram.
insight: It shifts grief from impulsive action to protective steadiness.
modern_relevance: A family gathers after a death, and someone has to stop the room from collapsing into panic. This verse holds that painful moment where love means restraint.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चंदन अगर भार बहु आए। अमित अनेक सुगंध सुहाए॥ सरजु तीर रचि चिता बनाई। जनु सुरपुर सोपान सुहाई ॥
translation: चंदन और अगर के तथा और भी अनेकों प्रकार के अपार (कपूर, गुग्गुल, केसर आदि) सुगंध द्रव्यों के बहुत से बोझ आए। सरयूजी के तट पर सुंदर चिता रचकर बनाई गई, (जो ऐसी मालूम होती थी) मानो स्वर्ग की सुंदर सीढ़ी हो ॥
english_translation: Loads of sandalwood, agarwood, and many fragrant materials arrived. On the bank of the Sarayu, a beautiful funeral pyre was built, like a lovely stairway to the higher realm.
essence: Even the last farewell can be made beautiful with reverence.
simple_meaning: Many fragrant materials are brought, and a beautiful funeral pyre is built by the Sarayu River like a stairway to the higher realm.
insight: It shifts attention from raw loss to the dignity with which a final rite is carried out.
modern_relevance: You watch relatives carry flowers, wood, and cloth to a cremation ground, each detail handled with quiet respect. Even in farewell, love tries to make the last act beautiful.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि बिधि दाह क्रिया सब कीन्ही। बिधिवत न्हाइ तिलांजुलि दीन्ही॥ सोधि सुमृति सब बेद पुराना। कीन्ह भरत दसगात बिधाना ॥
translation: इस प्रकार सब दाह क्रिया की गई और सबने विधिपूर्वक स्नान करके तिलांजलि दी। फिर वेद, स्मृति और पुराण सबका मत निश्चय करके उसके अनुसार भरतजी ने पिता का दशगात्र विधान (दस दिनों के कृत्य) किया ॥
english_translation: In this way, all the funeral rites were completed. Everyone bathed properly and offered water mixed with sesame. After consulting the Vedas, Smritis, and Puranas, Bharat carried out the ten-day rites for his father.
essence: Even in grief, Bharat does what duty requires.
simple_meaning: The funeral was performed exactly as prescribed, and Bharat completed the required rites for his father after consulting sacred tradition.
insight: It shifts grief into dutiful action, showing that sorrow does not excuse neglect.
modern_relevance: You are arranging every detail after a parent’s death, even while your hands shake. Love can still show up as careful responsibility.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ जस मुनिबर आयसु दीन्हा। तहँ तस सहस भाँति सबु कीन्हा॥ भए बिसुद्ध दिए सब दाना। धेनु बाजि गज बाहन नाना ॥
translation: मुनि श्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी ने जहाँ जैसी आज्ञा दी, वहाँ भरतजी ने सब वैसा ही हजारों प्रकार से किया। शुद्ध हो जाने पर (विधिपूर्वक) सब दान दिए। गायें तथा घोड़े, हाथी आदि अनेक प्रकार की सवारियाँ, ॥
english_translation: Wherever the sage Vashishtha gave an order, Bharat carried it out in a thousand ways. After becoming purified, he gave all the gifts in proper form: cows, horses, elephants, and many other vehicles.
essence: Obedience becomes grace when it is carried out completely.
simple_meaning: Bharat obeyed Vashishtha’s instructions completely and gave away everything properly, including cows, horses, elephants, and other gifts.
insight: It teaches you to act with exactness and generosity when duty is already heavy.
modern_relevance: You’re in the middle of a family ritual, tired and grieving, but you still do every step properly because it matters. Bharat’s steadiness is that kind of respect.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिंघासन भूषन बसन अन्न धरनि धन धाम। दिए भरत लहि भूमिसुर भे परिपूरन काम ॥
translation: सिंहासन, गहने, कपड़े, अन्न, पृथ्वी, धन और मकान भरतजी ने दिए, भूदेव ब्राह्मण दान पाकर परिपूर्णकाम हो गए (अर्थात उनकी सारी मनोकामनाएँ अच्छी तरह से पूरी हो गईं) ॥
english_translation: Bharat gave away thrones, ornaments, clothes, food, land, wealth, and houses. The Brahmins received full gifts and their wishes were completely fulfilled.
essence: Real renunciation gives away even what looks most precious.
simple_meaning: Bharat gave away royal goods, wealth, and property as gifts to the Brahmins, leaving them fully satisfied.
insight: It shifts the mind from keeping and controlling to releasing and serving.
modern_relevance: After a family loss, someone quietly sorts through the house and gives away what can help others — clothes, furniture, valuables. Grief turns into generosity, and the giving itself becomes a way of honoring love.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पितु हित भरत कीन्हि जसि करनी। सो मुख लाख जाइ नहिं बरनी॥ सुदिनु सोधि मुनिबर तब आए। सचिव महाजन सकल बोलाए ॥
translation: पिताजी के लिए भरतजी ने जैसी करनी की वह लाखों मुखों से भी वर्णन नहीं की जा सकती। तब शुभ दिन शोधकर श्रेष्ठ मुनि वशिष्ठजी आए और उन्होंने मंत्रियों तथा सब महाजनों को बुलवाया ॥
english_translation: The way Bharat served his father cannot be described by millions of mouths. Then, after choosing an auspicious day, the great sage Vashishtha came and summoned the ministers and all the elders.
essence: Some acts of filial service are too vast for words.
simple_meaning: Bharat's service to his father was beyond description. After that, Vashishtha arrived on an auspicious day and called together the ministers and elders.
insight: It highlights service so complete that recognition becomes irrelevant, then moves the story toward the next public gathering.
modern_relevance: You quietly handled your father's hospital paperwork, calls, and bills for weeks. Nobody posted about it. Nobody needed to. Some acts are too full for praise.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बैठे राजसभाँ सब जाई। पठए बोलि भरत दोउ भाई॥ भरतु बसिष्ठ निकट बैठारे। नीति धरममय बचन उचारे ॥
translation: सब लोग राजसभा में जाकर बैठ गए। तब मुनि ने भरतजी तथा शत्रुघ्नजी दोनों भाइयों को बुलवा भेजा। भरतजी को वशिष्ठजी ने अपने पास बैठा लिया और नीति तथा धर्म से भरे हुए वचन कहे ॥
english_translation: Everyone went and sat in the royal assembly. Then the sage sent for both brothers, Bharat and Shatrughna. Vashishtha seated Bharat near him and spoke words full of policy and dharma.
essence: Wise counsel begins when the right person is seated close enough to listen.
simple_meaning: The court gathers, Bharat and Shatrughna are called in, and Vashishtha places Bharat close to him to speak wise, righteous words.
insight: It shifts the moment from public confusion to intimate instruction, where dharma can be heard without noise.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense family meeting and someone who knows the whole story asks you to sit beside them before speaking. That small gesture changes everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रथम कथा सब मुनिबर बरनी। कैकइ कुटिल कीन्हि जसि करनी॥ भूप धरमुब्रतु सत्य सराहा। जेहिं तनु परिहरि प्रेमु निबाहा ॥
translation: पहले तो कैकेयी ने जैसी कुटिल करनी की थी, श्रेष्ठ मुनि ने वह सारी कथा कही। फिर राजा के धर्मव्रत और सत्य की सराहना की, जिन्होंने शरीर त्याग कर प्रेम को निबाहा ॥
english_translation: First, the sage recounted Kaikeyi's crooked deed in full. Then he praised the king's vow of truth and duty, for he gave up his body yet kept faith with love.
essence: True love is proved by truth kept at the cost of everything.
simple_meaning: The sage first tells how Kaikeyi acted wrongly, then praises the king for keeping truth and love even as he gave up his body.
insight: It shifts attention from blame alone to the harder praise of integrity under suffering.
modern_relevance: At a family meeting after a painful inheritance dispute, someone finally names the betrayal, then remembers the parent who stayed honest even while breaking apart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहत राम गुन सील सुभाऊ। सजल नयन पुलकेउ मुनिराऊ॥ बहुरि लखन सिय प्रीति बखानी। सोक सनेह मगन मुनि ग्यानी ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुण, शील और स्वभाव का वर्णन करते-करते तो मुनिराज के नेत्रों में जल भर आया और वे शरीर से पुलकित हो गए। फिर लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी के प्रेम की बड़ाई करते हुए ज्ञानी मुनि शोक और स्नेह में मग्न हो गए ॥
english_translation: As he spoke of Ram's virtues, character, and nature, the sage's eyes filled with tears and his body thrilled. Then, praising Lakshman and Sita's love, the wise sage became lost in sorrow and affection.
essence: Praise of Ram becomes tears, and tears become devotion.
simple_meaning: The sage is overwhelmed with emotion while praising Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Their virtues move him so deeply that tears, joy, sorrow, and love all rise together.
insight: It shows that true praise can become a form of surrender, where emotion itself confirms what the mind knows.
modern_relevance: You hear someone describe a person who kept every promise, and suddenly your own eyes sting. Some lives are so steady, so loving, they break through your defenses.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनहु भरत भावी प्रबल बिलखि कहेउ मुनिनाथ। हानि लाभु जीवनु मरनु जसु अपजसु बिधि हाथ ॥
translation: मुनिनाथ ने बिलखकर (दुःखी होकर) कहा- हे भरत! सुनो, भावी (होनहार) बड़ी बलवान है। हानि-लाभ, जीवन-मरण और यश-अपयश, ये सब विधाता के हाथ हैं ॥
english_translation: Listen, Bharat. Fate is strong, the sage said in grief. Loss and gain, life and death, fame and disgrace are all in the hands of the divine order.
essence: What happens to you is not fully yours to command.
simple_meaning: The sage tells Bharat that outcomes are not fully in human control. Gain, loss, life, death, praise, and blame all unfold under a larger order.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal control to humble acceptance of what unfolds.
modern_relevance: You refresh your inbox and see the decision went the other way. The sting is real, but this verse reminds you that not every outcome was ever yours to hold.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस बिचारि केहि देइअ दोसू। ब्यरथ काहि पर कीजिअ रोसू॥ तात बिचारु करहु मन माहीं। सोच जोगु दसरथु नृपु नाहीं ॥
translation: ऐसा विचार कर किसे दोष दिया जाए? और व्यर्थ किस पर क्रोध किया जाए? हे तात! मन में विचार करो। राजा दशरथ सोच करने के योग्य नहीं हैं ॥
english_translation: With this in mind, whom should you blame? Why waste anger on anyone? O dear one, think carefully in your heart. King Dasharath is not someone to grieve over.
essence: Grief becomes clearer when you stop searching for someone to punish.
simple_meaning: There is no useful person to blame here, and anger will not help. The wiser response is to think calmly and accept that Dasharath's sorrow is not something to dwell on.
insight: It shifts the mind from accusation to clear seeing, so sorrow can be held without adding more harm.
modern_relevance: You replay the argument after the funeral, looking for who ruined everything. But some losses have no villain you can punish. The first mercy is to stop turning grief into blame.
speaker: Muni

verse_text: सोचिअ बिप्र जो बेद बिहीना। तजि निज धरमु बिषय लयलीना॥ सोचिअ नृपति जो नीति न जाना। जेहि न प्रजा प्रिय प्रान समाना ॥
translation: सोच उस ब्राह्मण का करना चाहिए, जो वेद नहीं जानता और जो अपना धर्म छोड़कर विषय भोग में ही लीन रहता है। उस राजा का सोच करना चाहिए, जो नीति नहीं जानता और जिसको प्रजा प्राणों के समान प्यारी नहीं है ॥
english_translation: You should worry about a Brahmin who does not know the Vedas and is absorbed in sensual pleasure after abandoning his own duty. You should worry about a king who does not know right conduct and does not love his people as dearly as life itself.
essence: A role becomes shameful when it loses its duty.
simple_meaning: A person in a role should be judged by whether they live that role well. A priest without learning and a ruler without care for the people are both cause for concern.
insight: It shifts attention from status to responsibility, and from public role to real care.
modern_relevance: A manager with a fancy title ignores the team’s burnout and calls it leadership. A parent says they care, but never notices the child’s fear. This verse asks whether your role is actually being lived.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सोचिअ बयसु कृपन धनवानू। जो न अतिथि सिव भगति सुजानू॥ सोचिअ सूद्रु बिप्र अवमानी। मुखर मानप्रिय ग्यान गुमानी ॥
translation: उस वैश्य का सोच करना चाहिए, जो धनवान होकर भी कंजूस है और जो अतिथि सत्कार तथा शिवजी की भक्ति करने में कुशल नहीं है। उस शूद्र का सोच करना चाहिए, जो ब्राह्मणों का अपमान करने वाला, बहुत बोलने वाला, मान-बड़ाई चाहने वाला और ज्ञान का घमंड रखने वाला है ॥
english_translation: One should feel concern for a wealthy merchant who is miserly and poor in hospitality, and for a shudra who insults brahmins, talks too much, craves honor, and is proud of his knowledge.
essence: Status without humility is still spiritual poverty.
simple_meaning: Wealth, learning, or social standing are not enough on their own. A person should be judged by humility, hospitality, respect for others, and freedom from pride.
insight: It shifts attention from rank and display to conduct, humility, and how you treat the people around you.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who talks endlessly about expertise but never listens, never gives, and never shows respect. The discomfort you feel is the same warning this verse gives: status can hide poverty of character.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सोचिअ पुनि पति बंचक नारी। कुटिल कलहप्रिय इच्छाचारी॥ सोचिअ बटु निज ब्रतु परिहरई। जो नहिं गुर आयसु अनुसरई ॥
translation: पुनः उस स्त्री का सोच करना चाहिए जो पति को छलने वाली, कुटिल, कलहप्रिय और स्वेच्छा चारिणी है। उस ब्रह्मचारी का सोच करना चाहिए, जो अपने ब्रह्मचर्य व्रत को छोड़ देता है और गुरु की आज्ञा के अनुसार नहीं चलता ॥
english_translation: Again, you should feel concern for a wife who deceives her husband, is crooked, loves quarrels, and follows only her own wishes. You should feel concern for a student who abandons his vow of celibacy and does not follow the teacher's command.
essence: Character weakens when trust, restraint, and guidance are abandoned.
simple_meaning: A person loses honour when they betray trust, stir conflict, or abandon the discipline they promised to keep.
insight: It shifts the mind from excuse-making to responsibility for the vows and guidance that shape character.
modern_relevance: You promised yourself one small rule and broke it by noon. The real loss is not the rule itself — it is the slow erosion of trust in your own word.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सोचिअ गृही जो मोह बस करइ करम पथ त्याग। सोचिअ जती प्रपंच रत बिगत बिबेक बिराग ॥
translation: उस गृहस्थ का सोच करना चाहिए, जो मोहवश कर्म मार्ग का त्याग कर देता है, उस संन्यासी का सोच करना चाहिए, जो दुनिया के प्रपंच में फँसा हुआ और ज्ञान-वैराग्य से हीन है ॥
english_translation: You should grieve for a householder who abandons the path of action out of delusion, and for a renunciant who clings to worldly entanglement, lacking discernment and detachment.
essence: Running from duty and clinging to renunciation are both forms of confusion.
simple_meaning: A person can go wrong in two opposite ways: a householder may abandon action out of confusion, and a renunciant may still be trapped in worldly attachment.
insight: It shifts attention from labels and roles to the state of mind doing them.
modern_relevance: You quit a responsibility because it feels heavy, then later chase approval in a simpler life that still feels noisy. The problem was never the role — it was the mind carrying it.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: बैखानस सोइ सोचै जोगू। तपु बिहाइ जेहि भावइ भोगू॥ सोचिअ पिसुन अकारन क्रोधी। जननि जनक गुर बंधु बिरोधी ॥
translation: वानप्रस्थ वही सोच करने योग्य है, जिसको तपस्या छोड़कर भोग अच्छे लगते हैं। सोच उसका करना चाहिए जो चुगलखोर है, बिना ही कारण क्रोध करने वाला है तथा माता, पिता, गुरु एवं भाई-बंधुओं के साथ विरोध रखने वाला है ॥
english_translation: The forest-dweller who abandons austerity for pleasure is worth grieving over. Grieve the one who slanders, grows angry for no reason, and opposes mother, father, teacher, and brothers.
essence: When self-restraint is abandoned, character starts to unravel.
simple_meaning: A person deserves concern when they abandon self-restraint for comfort, gossip, anger, and opposition to the people who raised and guided them.
insight: It shifts attention from judging manners to seeing the breakdown of restraint underneath them.
modern_relevance: You watch someone slowly become impossible to live with: quick to snap, eager to gossip, dismissive of the people who care for them. The verse says the real loss is not just bad behaviour — it is the collapse of discipline.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सब बिधि सोचिअ पर अपकारी। निज तनु पोषक निरदय भारी॥ सोचनीय सबहीं बिधि सोई। जो न छाड़ि छलु हरि जन होई ॥
translation: सब प्रकार से उसका सोच करना चाहिए, जो दूसरों का अनिष्ट करता है, अपने ही शरीर का पोषण करता है और बड़ा भारी निर्दयी है और वह तो सभी प्रकार से सोच करने योग्य है, जो छल छोड़कर हरि का भक्त नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: One should grieve for the person who harms others, feeds only their own body, and is deeply cruel. In every way, the one who is truly blameworthy is the person who, without giving up deceit, does not become a devotee of Hari.
essence: Cruelty and deceit are the real signs of a fallen heart.
simple_meaning: A cruel person who hurts others and lives only for themselves deserves concern. The deepest fault is staying deceitful while refusing sincere devotion to Ram.
insight: It shifts judgment from outward respectability to the inner pattern of harm, self-absorption, and dishonesty.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who smiles in public, undermines people in private, and still wants to be seen as decent. This verse cuts through that split: harm, deceit, and hollow piety cannot be separated.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सोचनीय नहिं कोसलराऊ। भुवन चारिदस प्रगट प्रभाऊ॥ भयउ न अहइ न अब होनिहारा। भूप भरत जस पिता तुम्हारा ॥
translation: कोसलराज दशरथजी सोच करने योग्य नहीं हैं, जिनका प्रभाव चौदहों लोकों में प्रकट है। हे भरत! तुम्हारे पिता जैसा राजा तो न हुआ, न है और न अब होने का ही है ॥
english_translation: King Dasharath of Kosala is not fit for sorrow. His fame is manifest across the fourteen worlds. O Bharat, no king like your father has ever been, is now, or will ever be.
essence: Greatness does not disappear when grief narrows your view.
simple_meaning: Dasharath is being praised as a king whose greatness is known everywhere. Bharat is told that his father is beyond ordinary sorrow and beyond comparison.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal mourning to a wider recognition of a person's public and moral stature.
modern_relevance: You stand at a funeral and hear stories that make you realize the person was larger than your private grief. Their life touched more people than you ever knew.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिधि हरि हरु सुरपति दिसिनाथा। बरनहिं सब दसरथ गुन गाथा ॥
translation: हब्रह्मा, विष्णु, शिव, इन्द्र और दिक्पाल सभी दशरथजी के गुणों की कथाएँ कहा करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, Indra, and the guardians of the directions all sing the praises of Dasharath's virtues.
essence: A truly noble life is praised even beyond human voices.
simple_meaning: Even the highest beings speak of Dasharath's virtues. His greatness is so wide that it reaches beyond ordinary praise.
insight: It shifts attention from one person's loss to the scale of the life that was lived.
modern_relevance: At a memorial, people keep saying the same thing: he was the kind of person everyone respected. The grief is real, but so is the rare dignity of a life that leaves that kind of echo.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहहु तात केहि भाँति कोउ करिहि बड़ाई तासु। राम लखन तुम्ह सत्रुहन सरिस सुअन सुचि जासु ॥
translation: हे तात! कहो, उनकी बड़ाई कोई किस प्रकार करेगा, जिनके श्री राम, लक्ष्मण, तुम और शत्रुघ्न-सरीखे पवित्र पुत्र हैं? ॥
english_translation: Father, who could possibly praise one whose pure sons are Ram, Lakshman, you, and Shatrughna?
essence: A worthy life is praised by the children it raises.
simple_meaning: A father's greatness is beyond ordinary praise when his sons themselves are noble and pure.
insight: It redirects attention from eulogy to legacy: a life is measured by the character it leaves behind.
modern_relevance: You’re standing at a memorial, trying to speak about a parent who shaped four good children. The tribute feels too small, because the real proof of their life is already standing beside you.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सब प्रकार भूपति बड़भागी। बादि बिषादु करिअ तेहि लागी॥ यह सुनि समुझि सोचु परिहरहू। सिर धरि राज रजायसु करहू ॥
translation: राजा सब प्रकार से बड़भागी थे। उनके लिए विषाद करना व्यर्थ है। यह सुन और समझकर सोच त्याग दो और राजा की आज्ञा सिर चढ़ाकर तदनुसार करो ॥
english_translation: The king was blessed in every way. Grieving for him is pointless. Hearing this and understanding it, let go of sorrow and obey the king's command with reverence.
essence: Grief must give way to reverent action.
simple_meaning: There is no need to grieve for the king. He was fortunate in every way, and the proper response is to drop sorrow and follow his command.
insight: It shifts you from emotional collapse to clear obedience to what remains to be done.
modern_relevance: After a funeral, relatives sit in a quiet room arguing over what the deceased would have wanted. This verse asks you to stop feeding sorrow and honor the responsibility left behind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रायँ राजपदु तुम्ह कहुँ दीन्हा। पिता बचनु फुर चाहिअ कीन्हा॥ तजे रामु जेहिं बचनहि लागी। तनु परिहरेउ राम बिरहागी ॥
translation: राजा ने राज पद तुमको दिया है। पिता का वचन तुम्हें सत्य करना चाहिए, जिन्होंने वचन के लिए ही श्री रामचन्द्रजी को त्याग दिया और रामविरह की अग्नि में अपने शरीर की आहुति दे दी ॥
english_translation: The king gave the throne to you. You should make your father's word come true. He gave up Ram for the sake of his promise and gave his body up in the fire of separation from Ram.
essence: The real inheritance is not power, but the duty to keep a promise alive.
simple_meaning: The throne was given to Bharata, but the real duty is to prove his father's words true. Dasharatha himself gave up Ram and even his body for the sake of truth.
insight: It shifts the mind from entitlement to responsibility, and from receiving a role to fulfilling the promise inside it.
modern_relevance: You were handed a family responsibility you never asked for: a hospital bill, a sibling's promise, a parent’s unfinished task. What matters now is not the title you received, but whether you carry the word faithfully.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नृपहि बचन प्रिय नहिं प्रिय प्राना। करहु तात पितु बचन प्रवाना॥ करहु सीस धरि भूप रजाई। हइ तुम्ह कहँ सब भाँति भलाई ॥
translation: राजा को वचन प्रिय थे, प्राण प्रिय नहीं थे, इसलिए हे तात! पिता के वचनों को प्रमाण (सत्य) करो! राजा की आज्ञा सिर चढ़ाकर पालन करो, इसमें तुम्हारी सब तरह भलाई है ॥
english_translation: The king loved his word more than his life. O dear one, prove your father's command true. Bow your head to the king's order; in every way, that is your good.
essence: A son's greatness begins with making his father's word come true.
simple_meaning: A king values his word more than his own life. So the son should treat the father's command as sacred and obey it fully.
insight: It shifts you from personal preference to responsibility grounded in your word.
modern_relevance: You promised your mother you'd handle the family matter, even though it means canceling your plans and swallowing your pride. This verse asks you to treat that promise as binding, not optional.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: परसुराम पितु अग्या राखी। मारी मातु लोक सब साखी॥ तनय जजातिहि जौबनु दयऊ। पितु अग्याँ अघ अजसु न भयऊ ॥
translation: परशुरामजी ने पिता की आज्ञा रखी और माता को मार डाला, सब लोक इस बात के साक्षी हैं। राजा ययाति के पुत्र ने पिता को अपनी जवानी दे दी। पिता की आज्ञा पालन करने से उन्हें पाप और अपयश नहीं हुआ ॥
english_translation: Parashuram kept his father's command and killed his mother; all the world is witness. The son of King Yayati gave his youth to his father. By obeying a father's command, they incurred no sin or disgrace.
essence: Some duties cost dearly and still leave your honor intact.
simple_meaning: The verse praises people who obey a father's command, even at great personal cost, and says such obedience can still be honorable.
insight: It shifts you from judging duty by comfort to judging it by fidelity.
modern_relevance: You agree to help a parent move, even though it ruins your weekend and drains you. The cost is real, but so is the dignity of keeping your word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अनुचित उचित बिचारु तजि ते पालहिं पितु बैन। ते भाजन सुख सुजस के बसहिं अमरपति ऐन ॥
translation: जो अनुचित और उचित का विचार छोड़कर पिता के वचनों का पालन करते हैं, वे (यहाँ) सुख और सुयश के पात्र होकर अंत में इन्द्रपुरी (स्वर्ग) में निवास करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who set aside judgments of right and wrong and keep their father's word become fit for happiness and good fame here, and dwell in Indra's city in the end.
essence: Keeping a father's word can matter more than personal comfort.
simple_meaning: A child who follows a father's command without overthinking right and wrong earns honor and lasting good.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to faithful obedience in a binding relationship.
modern_relevance: You know the moment: your parent asks for something awkward, inconvenient, and clearly not to your advantage. The verse says real character shows up when you honor the word anyway.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अवसि नरेस बचन फुर करहू। पालहु प्रजा सोकु परिहरहू॥ सुरपुर नृपु पाइहि परितोषू। तुम्ह कहुँ सुकृतु सुजसु नहिं दोषू ॥
translation: राजा का वचन अवश्य सत्य करो। शोक त्याग दो और प्रजा का पालन करो। ऐसा करने से स्वर्ग में राजा संतोष पावेंगे और तुम को पुण्य और सुंदर यश मिलेगा, दोष नहीं लगेगा ॥
english_translation: Surely keep the king's word true. Set aside grief and protect the people. Then the king will find contentment in the higher realm, and you will gain merit and good fame, not blame.
essence: Keep the promise, even when grief asks you to stop.
simple_meaning: A ruler must keep his father's promise, stop grieving, and continue protecting the people. Doing that brings honor, not blame.
insight: It shifts the mind from private sorrow to public responsibility, showing that duty can continue even in grief.
modern_relevance: You are still expected at the family meeting after the loss, even when your chest feels tight. The work of care does not pause just because your heart is breaking.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बेद बिदित संमत सबही का। जेहि पितु देइ सो पावइ टीका॥ करहु राजु परिहरहु गलानी। मानहु मोर बचन हित जानी ॥
translation: यह वेद में प्रसिद्ध है और (स्मृति-पुराणादि) सभी शास्त्रों के द्वारा सम्मत है कि पिता जिसको दे वही राजतिलक पाता है, इसलिए तुम राज्य करो, ग्लानि का त्याग कर दो। मेरे वचन को हित समझकर मानो ॥
english_translation: It is well known in the Vedas and accepted by all scriptures that the one whom the father gives the coronation belongs on the throne. So take the kingdom, let go of your grief, and accept my words as beneficial.
essence: Duty can arrive wearing grief, and still need your yes.
simple_meaning: The rightful coronation belongs to the son chosen by the father. Dasharath asks Bharat to accept the throne, drop his sorrow, and trust that this is for everyone's good.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal reluctance to accepting the binding duty in front of you.
modern_relevance: Your family hands you a responsibility you never asked for, and everyone is waiting while you hesitate. The room is heavy with emotion, but the task still belongs to you.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: सुनि सुखु लहब राम बैदेहीं। अनुचित कहब न पंडित केहीं॥ कौसल्यादि सकल महतारीं। तेउ प्रजा सुख होहिं सुखारीं ॥
translation: इस बात को सुनकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी और जानकीजी सुख पावेंगे और कोई पंडित इसे अनुचित नहीं कहेगा। कौसल्याजी आदि तुम्हारी सब माताएँ भी प्रजा के सुख से सुखी होंगी॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Ram and Sita will be happy, and no wise person will call it improper. Kaushalya and all the other mothers will also rejoice in the people's happiness.
essence: A righteous choice pleases the whole household, not just the ruler.
simple_meaning: A right decision will please Ram and Sita, and no wise person will object. It will also make the royal mothers happy because the people will be happy too.
insight: It shifts decision-making from personal gain to the wider well-being your choice creates.
modern_relevance: You’re deciding whether to take the promotion that looks good on paper but hurts your team. The verse points you toward the option that leaves everyone steadier, not just you.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: परम तुम्हार राम कर जानिहि। सो सब बिधि तुम्ह सन भल मानिहि॥ सौंपेहु राजु राम के आएँ। सेवा करेहु सनेह सुहाएँ ॥
translation: जो तुम्हारे और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के श्रेष्ठ संबंध को जान लेगा, वह सभी प्रकार से तुमसे भला मानेगा। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के लौट आने पर राज्य उन्हें सौंप देना और सुंदर स्नेह से उनकी सेवा करना ॥
english_translation: Anyone who understands the noble bond between you and Ram will regard you as good in every way. When Ram returns, hand the kingdom over to him and serve him with loving devotion.
essence: Power becomes noble when you can return it with love.
simple_meaning: Bharat says everyone will see the bond between him and Ram as noble. He should return the kingdom to Ram and serve him lovingly when Ram comes back.
insight: It shifts you from possession to stewardship: hold only what truly belongs to you, and return the rest without bitterness.
modern_relevance: You’ve been covering for a sibling, colleague, or friend and everyone now treats the role as yours. The harder move is to hand it back cleanly, without resentment, and let love stay intact.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: कीजिअ गुर आयसु अवसि कहहिं सचिव कर जोरि। रघुपति आएँ उचित जस तस तब करब बहोरि ॥
translation: मंत्री हाथ जोड़कर कह रहे हैं- गुरुजी की आज्ञा का अवश्य ही पालन कीजिए। श्री रघुनाथजी के लौट आने पर जैसा उचित हो, तब फिर वैसा ही कीजिएगा ॥
english_translation: The ministers fold their hands and say, "You must obey the teacher's command. When Raghunath returns, then do what is fitting."
essence: Honor the present duty; leave the larger decision for later.
simple_meaning: The ministers ask Bharata to obey the teacher's order first and leave the final decision for after Ram returns.
insight: It trains you to separate immediate duty from later judgment, so action stays steady under pressure.
modern_relevance: Your family is arguing in the kitchen and everyone wants an answer tonight. But the wisest move may be to honor the immediate responsibility first and postpone the final call until tempers cool.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कौसल्या धरि धीरजु कहई। पूत पथ्य गुर आयसु अहई॥ सो आदरिअ करिअ हित मानी। तजिअ बिषादु काल गति जानी ॥
translation: कौसल्याजी भी धीरज धरकर कह रही हैं- हे पुत्र! गुरुजी की आज्ञा पथ्य रूप है। उसका आदर करना चाहिए और हित मानकर उसका पालन करना चाहिए। काल की गति को जानकर विषाद का त्याग कर देना चाहिए ॥
english_translation: Kaushalya, steadying herself, said: 'Son, the guru's command is like medicine. Honour it and follow it as good for you. Knowing time's course, let go of grief.'
essence: What is truly good may arrive wearing the face of pain.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya tells her son to treat the guru's instruction as something beneficial, follow it with respect, and drop grief by understanding that time moves on.
insight: It shifts the mind from emotional resistance to respectful acceptance of guidance.
modern_relevance: You get a message that changes everything, and your first instinct is to spiral. Then someone steadier reminds you that not every painful instruction is harmful; some are the medicine you needed.
speaker: Kaushalya

verse_text: बन रघुपति सुरपति नरनाहू। तुम्ह एहि भाँति तात कदराहू॥ परिजन प्रजा सचिव सब अंबा। तुम्हहीं सुत सब कहँ अवलंबा ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी वन में हैं, महाराज स्वर्ग का राज्य करने चले गए और हे तात! तुम इस प्रकार कातर हो रहे हो। हे पुत्र! कुटुम्ब, प्रजा, मंत्री और सब माताओं के, सबके एक तुम ही सहारे हो ॥
english_translation: Ram has gone to the forest and the king of the gods has gone to his realm, yet you are grieving like this, dear one. Son, for your family, your people, your ministers, and all the mothers, you alone are the support for everyone.
essence: When everyone else is shaken, you become the support.
simple_meaning: Kausalya reminds Bharat that Ram is in the forest, Dasharath has gone to the higher realm, and the whole family and kingdom now depend on him.
insight: It shifts the mind from private grief to the responsibility of steadying others.
modern_relevance: You are sitting in a hospital corridor while your family keeps calling your phone. You can cry later, but right now everyone is looking to you to decide what happens next.
speaker: Kausalya

verse_text: लखि बिधि बाम कालु कठिनाई। धीरजु धरहु मातु बलि जाई॥ सिर धरि गुर आयसु अनुसरहू। प्रजा पालि परिजन दुखु हरहू ॥
translation: विधाता को प्रतिकूल और काल को कठोर देखकर धीरज धरो, माता तुम्हारी बलिहारी जाती है। गुरु की आज्ञा को सिर चढ़ाकर उसी के अनुसार कार्य करो और प्रजा का पालन कर कुटुम्बियों का दुःख हरो ॥
english_translation: Seeing fate as adverse and time as harsh, keep your courage, mother. Place the teacher's command on your head, rule the people, and remove the grief of your family.
essence: Steadiness lets you carry duty even in harsh times.
simple_meaning: Stay steady even when fate feels harsh. Honor your teacher's instruction, do your duty, care for the people, and ease your family's suffering.
insight: It shifts you from emotional collapse to responsible action under pressure.
modern_relevance: Your phone keeps buzzing after bad news, but the team still needs a calm decision and your family still needs you. This verse reminds you that steadiness is part of love.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: गुरु के बचन सचिव अभिनंदनु। सुने भरत हिय हित जनु चंदनु॥ सुनी बहोरि मातु मृदु बानी। सील सनेह सरल रस सानी ॥
translation: भरतजी ने गुरु के वचनों और मंत्रियों के अभिनंदन (अनुमोदन) को सुना, जो उनके हृदय के लिए मानो चंदन के समान (शीतल) थे। फिर उन्होंने शील, स्नेह और सरलता के रस में सनी हुई माता कौसल्या की कोमल वाणी सुनी ॥
english_translation: Bharat heard the ministers' approving words and the guru's blessing, and they felt cool to his heart like sandalwood. Then he heard Mother Kausalya's gentle voice, soaked in virtue, affection, and simplicity.
essence: Kind words can soothe a heart before it breaks.
simple_meaning: Bharat is comforted by the elders’ support and by his mother’s gentle, loving words.
insight: It shows how gentle, trustworthy words can steady a heart before deeper grief surfaces.
modern_relevance: You are overwhelmed after a family argument, and then one calm voice cuts through the noise. Not because it solves everything, but because it sounds like care instead of pressure.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सानी सरल रस मातु बानी सुनि भरतु ब्याकुल भए। लोचन सरोरुह स्रवत सींचत बिरह उर अंकुर नए॥ सो दसा देखत समय तेहि बिसरी सबहि सुधि देह की। तुलसी सराहत सकल सादर सीवँ सहज सनेह की॥
translation: सरलता के रस में सनी हुई माता की वाणी सुनकर भरतजी व्याकुल हो गए। उनके नेत्र कमल जल (आँसू) बहाकर हृदय के विरह रूपी नवीन अंकुर को सींचने लगे। (नेत्रों के आँसुओं ने उनके वियोग-दुःख को बहुत ही बढ़ाकर उन्हें अत्यन्त व्याकुल कर दिया।) उनकी वह दशा देखकर उस समय सबको अपने शरीर की सुध भूल गई। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- स्वाभाविक प्रेम की सीमा श्री भरतजी की सब लोग आदरपूर्वक सराहना करने लगे।
english_translation: Hearing his mother’s words steeped in simplicity, Bharat became overwhelmed. His lotus eyes poured tears, watering the new sprouts of separation in his heart. Seeing him like that, everyone forgot their own bodies. Tulsidas praises the natural love that makes such devotion worthy of respect.
essence: Natural love can make grief visible to everyone.
simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed by his mother’s gentle words. His tears deepen his grief, and everyone around him forgets themselves seeing his pain.
insight: It shifts attention from control to the raw force of love and loss.
modern_relevance: You hear a mother’s voice on the phone after a family rupture, and the whole room goes quiet. Some grief is so human that everyone nearby feels it too.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरतु कमल कर जोरि धीर धुरंधर धीर धरि। बचन अमिअँ जनु बोरि देत उचित उत्तर सबहि ॥
translation: धैर्य की धुरी को धारण करने वाले भरतजी धीरज धरकर, कमल के समान हाथों को जोड़कर, वचनों को मानो अमृत में डुबाकर सबको उचित उत्तर देने लगे- ॥
english_translation: Holding onto patience, Bharat joined his lotus-like hands and began giving everyone a fitting reply, as if dipping his words in nectar.
essence: Steady hands and gentle words can hold grief without spilling it.
simple_meaning: Bharat steadies himself, joins his hands, and answers everyone gently and appropriately.
insight: It teaches you to slow the mind before speaking, so your words carry steadiness instead of raw emotion.
modern_relevance: You are shaken, but the family group chat is waiting for a reply. Instead of firing back, you pause, breathe, and answer with care. That restraint changes the whole room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मोहि उपदेसु दीन्ह गुरु नीका। प्रजा सचिव संमत सबही का॥ मातु उचित धरि आयसु दीन्हा। अवसि सीस धरि चाहउँ कीन्हा ॥
translation: गुरुजी ने मुझे सुंदर उपदेश दिया। (फिर) प्रजा, मंत्री आदि सभी को यही सम्मत है। माता ने भी उचित समझकर ही आज्ञा दी है और मैं भी अवश्य उसको सिर चढ़ाकर वैसा ही करना चाहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: My guru gave me noble instruction. All the people and ministers agree with it. My mother has given her command as proper, and I too will certainly place it on my head and do it.
essence: Right action becomes easy when every rightful guide points the same way.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he has received good guidance from his teacher, and the approval of his family and leaders. He will accept his mother's command and carry it out fully.
insight: It teaches you to act on clear duty once wise guidance has aligned.
modern_relevance: You get three texts from family, your mentor, and your team, and they all point the same way. The relief is not in overthinking it — it is in finally doing what you already know is right.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: गुर पितु मातु स्वामि हित बानी। सुनि मन मुदित करिअ भलि जानी॥ उचित कि अनुचित किएँ बिचारू। धरमु जाइ सिर पातक भारू ॥
translation: (क्योंकि) गुरु, पिता, माता, स्वामी और सुहृद् (मित्र) की वाणी सुनकर प्रसन्न मन से उसे अच्छी समझकर करना (मानना) चाहिए। उचित-अनुचित का विचार करने से धर्म जाता है और सिर पर पाप का भार चढ़ता है ॥
english_translation: Listen to the words of your guru, father, mother, master, and well-wisher with a glad mind, and accept them as good. If you start judging what is proper and improper, dharma slips away and the burden of wrongdoing rises on your head.
essence: Good counsel works only when you receive it without inner resistance.
simple_meaning: When trusted people guide you, receive it with a willing heart. Endless weighing of right and wrong can make you lose your sense of duty.
insight: It shifts you from suspicious self-justification to humble acceptance of guidance.
modern_relevance: Your mother, mentor, or manager gives you clear advice before a hard decision, and you keep reopening it in your head until the moment passes. This verse says the heart should receive good counsel before the mind turns it into noise.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तुम्ह तौ देहु सरल सिख सोई। जो आचरत मोर भल होई॥ जद्यपि यह समुझत हउँ नीकें। तदपि होत परितोष न जी कें ॥
translation: आप तो मुझे वही सरल शिक्षा दे रहे हैं, जिसके आचरण करने में मेरा भला हो। यद्यपि मैं इस बात को भलीभाँति समझता हूँ, तथापि मेरे हृदय को संतोष नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: You are giving me the simple teaching that would do me good if I followed it. Even though I understand it well, my heart still finds no peace.
essence: You can understand the right thing and still not feel at ease.
simple_meaning: A person can understand the right guidance clearly and still not feel settled inside. Knowing what is good is not always enough to bring peace.
insight: It separates intellectual agreement from emotional resolution, showing that clarity alone may not yet transform the heart.
modern_relevance: You nod through the conversation, say the sensible thing, and still feel tight in your chest after everyone leaves. Knowing the answer and living the answer are not the same.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: अब तुम्ह बिनय मोरि सुनि लेहू। मोहि अनुहरत सिखावनु देहू॥ ऊतरु देउँ छमब अपराधू। दुखित दोष गुन गनहिं न साधू ॥
translation: अब आप लोग मेरी विनती सुन लीजिए और मेरी योग्यता के अनुसार मुझे शिक्षा दीजिए। मैं उत्तर दे रहा हूँ, यह अपराध क्षमा कीजिए। साधु पुरुष दुःखी मनुष्य के दोष-गुणों को नहीं गिनते।
english_translation: Now please hear my request and teach me according to my capacity. Please forgive me for replying. Good people do not keep counting the faults and virtues of someone who is distressed.
essence: A hurting person needs mercy before correction.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks for guidance suited to him and asks forgiveness for speaking back. He says kind people do not judge someone who is already in pain.
insight: It shifts you from evaluating a wounded person to responding with restraint and care.
modern_relevance: A family argument after bad news can turn every sentence into a weapon. This verse reminds you that when someone is hurting, the first response should be mercy, not analysis.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: पितु सुरपुर सिय रामु बन करन कहहु मोहि राजु। एहि तें जानहु मोर हित कै आपन बड़ काजु ॥
translation: पिताजी स्वर्ग में हैं, श्री सीतारामजी वन में हैं और मुझे आप राज्य करने के लिए कह रहे हैं। इसमें आप मेरा कल्याण समझते हैं या अपना कोई बड़ा काम (होने की आशा रखते हैं)? ॥
english_translation: My father is in heaven, Sita and Ram are in the forest, and you ask me to rule. Do you mean my welfare, or your own great gain?
essence: What looks like power can be a burden disguised as help.
simple_meaning: Bharat rejects the idea that ruling the kingdom could be good for him. With Ram in exile and his father gone, he sees the offer as serving someone else's gain, not his own welfare.
insight: It teaches you to test every opportunity by whether it serves your true good, not just others' convenience.
modern_relevance: A family asks you to take over a business after a painful loss, but the role feels like a trap dressed as responsibility. Bharat's clarity helps you name when an offer is not truly for your good.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: हित हमार सियपति सेवकाईं। सो हरि लीन्ह मातु कुटिलाईं॥ मैं अनुमानि दीख मन माहीं। आन उपायँ मोर हित नाहीं ॥
translation: मेरा कल्याण तो सीतापति श्री रामजी की चाकरी में है, सो उसे माता की कुटिलता ने छीन लिया। मैंने अपने मन में अनुमान करके देख लिया है कि दूसरे किसी उपाय से मेरा कल्याण नहीं है ॥
english_translation: My true good is serving Sita's lord, but my mother’s crookedness has taken that away. I have seen it clearly in my own mind: no other remedy will bring me good.
essence: What you truly need is not status but the chance to serve what you love.
simple_meaning: Bharat sees that his true welfare lies in serving Ram, and he accepts that his mother's actions have blocked that path. He concludes that no other option can make him whole.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing status to recognising where your real fulfilment lies.
modern_relevance: You get the promotion everyone wanted, but it feels empty because it pulls you away from what you truly care about. Bharat’s clarity is that some gains are losses in disguise.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: सोक समाजु राजु केहि लेखें। लखन राम सिय बिनु पद देखें॥ बादि बसन बिनु भूषन भारू। बादि बिरति बिनु ब्रह्मबिचारू ॥
translation: यह शोक का समुदाय राज्य लक्ष्मण, श्री रामचंद्रजी और सीताजी के चरणों को देखे बिना किस गिनती में है (इसका क्या मूल्य है)? जैसे कपड़ों के बिना गहनों का बोझ व्यर्थ है। वैराग्य के बिना ब्रह्मविचार व्यर्थ है ॥
english_translation: What is a kingdom worth when Lakshman, Ram, and Sita cannot be seen? Ornaments are useless without clothes, and thought of Brahman is useless without detachment.
essence: Without detachment, even wisdom becomes a burden.
simple_meaning: A kingdom has no value to Bharat without seeing Ram, Sita, and Lakshman. Outer possessions and even spiritual thought become empty without detachment.
insight: It shifts value from status and display to presence and inner release.
modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the title, the bigger office — and still feel sick because the one person you wanted to share it with is gone. Bharat knows that emptiness.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: सरुज सरीर बादि बहु भोगा। बिनु हरिभगति जायँ जप जोगा॥ जायँ जीव बिनु देह सुहाई। बादि मोर सबु बिनु रघुराई ॥
translation: रोगी शरीर के लिए नाना प्रकार के भोग व्यर्थ हैं। श्री हरि की भक्ति के बिना जप और योग व्यर्थ हैं। जीव के बिना सुंदर देह व्यर्थ है, वैसे ही श्री रघुनाथजी के बिना मेरा सब कुछ व्यर्थ है ॥
english_translation: A diseased body gains nothing from pleasures. Without devotion to Hari, chanting and yoga are useless. A beautiful body is useless without the living being within it, and everything of mine is useless without Raghunath.
essence: Everything loses meaning when Ram is missing.
simple_meaning: Pleasure, practice, beauty, and possessions all lose their value when Ram is absent. Real worth comes from devotion, not from outward success.
insight: It shifts value away from outer gain and toward devotion as the measure of a full life.
modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the new phone, the perfect apartment — and the room still feels strangely bare. Bharat names that ache: without what you love most, everything else can feel hollow.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जाउँ राम पहिं आयसु देहू। एकाहिं आँक मोर हित एहू॥ मोहि नृप करि भल आपन चहहू। सोउ सनेह जड़ता बस कहहू ॥
translation: मुझे आज्ञा दीजिए, मैं श्री रामजी के पास जाऊँ! एक ही आँक (निश्चयपूर्वक) मेरा हित इसी में है। और मुझे राजा बनाकर आप अपना भला चाहते हैं, यह भी आप स्नेह की जड़ता (मोह) के वश होकर ही कह रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Please let me go to Ram. My true good lies in that one aim. You want to make me king for my own benefit, but you say it only because love has clouded your mind.
essence: True benefit may be refusing the crown and walking toward what you love.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks for permission to go to Ram and says that is his only real good. He rejects the offer of kingship as a confused act of misplaced affection.
insight: It shifts you from accepting status to asking what actually serves your deepest duty.
modern_relevance: Your family insists the promotion is the safe choice, but your chest tightens because it would pull you away from what matters most. Bharat knows that not every good offer is your good.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: कैकेई सुअ कुटिलमति राम बिमुख गतलाज। तुम्ह चाहत सुखु मोहबस मोहि से अधम कें राज ॥
translation: कैकेयी के पुत्र, कुटिलबुद्धि, रामविमुख और निर्लज्ज मुझ से अधम के राज्य से आप मोह के वश होकर ही सुख चाहते हैं ॥
english_translation: O son of Kaikeyi, you are crooked-minded, turned away from Ram, and shameless. You desire happiness only because of delusion, and you want the kingdom for me, the most fallen of men.
essence: Power gained through delusion cannot satisfy a clear heart.
simple_meaning: Bharat rejects the idea that kingdom can bring real happiness when it comes from greed and turning away from Ram.
insight: It trains you to question rewards that separate you from what is right.
modern_relevance: You get offered the promotion everyone else envies, but your stomach knots because it would cost your integrity. Bharat names that feeling: some victories are just delusion wearing a crown.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: कहउँ साँचु सब सुनि पतिआहू। चाहिअ धरमसील नरनाहू॥ मोहि राजु हठि देइहहु जबहीं। रसा रसातल जाइहि तबहीं ॥
translation: मैं सत्य कहता हूँ, आप सब सुनकर विश्वास करें, धर्मशील को ही राजा होना चाहिए। आप मुझे हठ करके ज्यों ही राज्य देंगे, त्यों ही पृथ्वी पाताल में धँस जाएगी ॥
english_translation: I speak the truth; listen and believe me all of you: only a righteous king should rule. The moment you force the kingdom on me, the earth will sink into the underworld.
essence: Power given by force cannot hold a world together.
simple_meaning: Bharat says a kingdom should go only to a righteous ruler, and he warns that forcing him to accept it would be disastrous.
insight: It shifts the mind from grabbing authority to honoring moral fitness for responsibility.
modern_relevance: A family business gets handed to the one person who never wanted it, while the capable one is ignored. Bharat would say: don’t confuse pressure with rightful leadership.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: मोहि समान को पाप निवासू। जेहि लगि सीय राम बनबासू॥ रायँ राम कहुँ काननु दीन्हा। बिछुरत गमनु अमरपुर कीन्हा ॥
