translation: मेरे समान पापों का घर कौन होगा, जिसके कारण सीताजी और श्री रामजी का वनवास हुआ? राजा ने श्री रामजी को वन दिया और उनके बिछुड़ते ही स्वयं स्वर्ग को गमन किया ॥
english_translation: Who is a storehouse of sin like me, because of whom Sita and Ram were sent to the forest? The king gave Ram the forest, and the moment they parted, he departed for the higher realm.
essence: Grief turns inward and names itself as the wound's cause.
simple_meaning: The speaker blames himself for Ram and Sita's exile and says Dasharath died the moment they were separated.
insight: It shifts the mind from explanation to accountability, letting grief name the cost without hiding behind excuses.
modern_relevance: You replay one conversation for days after it breaks a family apart. Even if you didn't mean harm, your heart keeps asking what you set in motion.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: मैं सठु सब अनरथ कर हेतू। बैठ बात सब सुनउँ सचेतू॥ बिन रघुबीर बिलोकि अबासू। रहे प्रान सहि जग उपहासू ॥
translation: और मैं दुष्ट, जो अनर्थों का कारण हूँ, होश-हवास में बैठा सब बातें सुन रहा हूँ। श्री रघुनाथजी से रहित घर को देखकर और जगत् का उपहास सहकर भी ये प्राण बने हुए हैं ॥
english_translation: I am a fool, the cause of every disaster. I sit here awake, hearing everything. Seeing the home without Raghubir, and bearing the world's ridicule, these breaths still remain.
essence: Self-blame keeps breathing when love has been broken.
simple_meaning: Bharat calls himself the cause of disaster. He says he sits awake, sees the house without Ram, and still endures the world's mockery while life remains.
insight: It shifts the reader from self-justifying denial to honest remorse and the weight of consequences.
modern_relevance: You replay the family argument at 2 a.m., convinced you caused everything. The room is quiet, but your mind keeps calling you the reason the house broke.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: राम पुनीत बिषय रस रूखे। लोलुप भूमि भोग के भूखे॥ कहँ लगि कहौं हृदय कठिनाई। निदरि कुलिसु जेहिं लही बड़ाई ॥
translation: (इसका यही कारण है कि ये प्राण) श्री राम रूपी पवित्र विषय रस में आसक्त नहीं हैं। ये लालची भूमि और भोगों के ही भूखे हैं। मैं अपने हृदय की कठोरता कहाँ तक कहूँ? जिसने वज्र का भी तिरस्कार करके बड़ाई पाई है ॥
english_translation: Ram is pure and untouched by worldly taste, but these people are greedy and hungry for land and pleasure. How far can I speak of my own hard-heartedness? The one who has even surpassed a thunderbolt has won praise.
essence: Greed makes the heart harder than a thunderbolt.
simple_meaning: Ram remains untouched by worldly pleasure, while others crave land and enjoyment. The speaker blames his own hard heart, saying even a thunderbolt could be outdone by such hardness.
insight: It frames greed as a hardening of the heart that blocks repentance and clear seeing.
modern_relevance: You watch someone cling to property, status, or comfort long after it has begun hurting everyone around them. The tragedy is not only what they want, but how wanting has made them unreachable.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कारन तें कारजु कठिन होइ दोसु नहिं मोर। कुलिस अस्थि तें उपल तें लोह कराल कठोर ॥
translation: कारण से कार्य कठिन होता ही है, इसमें मेरा दोष नहीं। हड्डी से वज्र और पत्थर से लोहा भयानक और कठोर होता है ॥
english_translation: The task becomes hard because of its cause; the fault is not mine. From bone comes the thunderbolt, and from stone comes iron — both are fiercely hard.
essence: Hardness often comes from causes, not from your moral failure.
simple_meaning: A difficult outcome can come from the conditions that created it. Not everything hard is a personal failure.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal blame to causal understanding, so you can respond more clearly instead of collapsing into guilt.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family meeting already tense from weeks of silence, and the first sharp word makes everything worse. Later, you realise the conflict did not begin with that one moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कैकेई भव तनु अनुरागे। पावँर प्रान अघाइ अभागे॥ जौं प्रिय बिरहँ प्रान प्रिय लागे। देखब सुनब बहुत अब आगे ॥
translation: कैकेयी से उत्पन्न देह में प्रेम करने वाले ये पामर प्राण भरपेट (पूरी तरह से) अभागे हैं। जब प्रिय के वियोग में भी मुझे प्राण प्रिय लग रहे हैं, तब अभी आगे मैं और भी बहुत कुछ देखूँ-सुनूँगा ॥
english_translation: The lowly, unlucky life that loves Kaikeyi's body is already full. If life still feels dear even in separation from the beloved, then much more is still to come.
essence: Even life feels heavy when separation has already begun.
simple_meaning: These words describe how the speaker feels trapped by attachment and bad fortune, yet still expects even more suffering ahead.
insight: It shifts the reader into bracing awareness: pain is not over, and the heart is already carrying too much.
modern_relevance: You get the call after midnight, and one bad choice has already split the family in two. You can feel the next wave coming before it arrives.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लखन राम सिय कहुँ बनु दीन्हा। पठइ अमरपुर पति हित कीन्हा॥ लीन्ह बिधवपन अपजसु आपू। दीन्हेउ प्रजहि सोकु संतापू ॥
translation: लक्ष्मण, श्री रामजी और सीताजी को तो वन दिया, स्वर्ग भेजकर पति का कल्याण किया, स्वयं विधवापन और अपयश लिया, प्रजा को शोक और संताप दिया, ॥
english_translation: Lakshman, Ram, and Sita were sent to the forest; the king was made to serve their good. I took widowhood and disgrace upon myself, and gave the people sorrow and anguish.
essence: A defended wrong can still leave everyone wounded.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi justifies her demand by claiming it helped the king, but it brought exile, disgrace, and suffering to everyone else.
insight: It exposes how self-justification can hide the real cost of your choices.
modern_relevance: You explain a decision in the meeting as 'necessary,' but your team is silent and hurt. The story you tell yourself can sound noble while the damage spreads anyway.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: मोहि दीन्ह सुखु सुजसु सुराजू। कीन्ह कैकईं सब कर काजू॥ ऐहि तें मोर काह अब नीका। तेहि पर देन कहहु तुम्ह टीका ॥
translation: और मुझे सुख, सुंदर यश और उत्तम राज्य दिया! कैकेयी ने सभी का काम बना दिया! इससे अच्छा अब मेरे लिए और क्या होगा? उस पर भी आप लोग मुझे राजतिलक देने को कहते हैं! ॥
english_translation: You gave me happiness, fine fame, and a splendid kingdom! Kaikeyi has done everything well! What more could be right for me now? And yet you still speak of giving me the coronation!
essence: Real contentment makes even a crown feel unnecessary.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he already has happiness, fame, and a kingdom, so he sees no need for more. He questions why anyone would even offer him coronation.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing status to seeing how little status can satisfy.
modern_relevance: You get the promotion email after a week of chaos, but your chest feels empty instead of excited. Bharat knows that some prizes stop mattering once you see what they cost.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: कैकइ जठर जनमि जग माहीं। यह मोहि कहँ कछु अनुचित नाहीं॥ मोरि बात सब बिधिहिं बनाई। प्रजा पाँच कत करहु सहाई ॥
translation: कैकयी के पेट से जगत् में जन्म लेकर यह मेरे लिए कुछ भी अनुचित नहीं है। मेरी सब बात तो विधाता ने ही बना दी है। (फिर) उसमें प्रजा और पंच (आप लोग) क्यों सहायता कर रहे हैं? ॥
english_translation: Having been born into the world from Kaikeyi's womb, nothing in this is improper for me. My entire situation has been arranged by fate. Then why are you all, the subjects and the council, helping in this matter?
essence: What has already unfolded cannot be made wrong by your resistance.
simple_meaning: Bharat says that being born from Kaikeyi does not make his situation improper. He sees the whole event as already arranged, and asks why anyone is still trying to fix it.
insight: It shifts the mind from resisting the past to meeting reality without self-torment.
modern_relevance: You replay a family argument at 1am, trying to rewrite every line. At some point, the harder truth arrives: the event is done, and your peace depends on how you receive it.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: ग्रह ग्रहीत पुनि बात बस तेहि पुनि बीछी मार। तेहि पिआइअ बारुनी कहहु काह उपचार ॥
translation: जिसे कुग्रह लगे हों (अथवा जो पिशाचग्रस्त हो), फिर जो वायुरोग से पीड़ित हो और उसी को फिर बिच्छू डंक मार दे, उसको यदि मदिरा पिलाई जाए, तो कहिए यह कैसा इलाज है! ॥
english_translation: What kind of cure is it to give liquor to someone already seized by an evil influence, troubled by wind disorder, and then stung by a scorpion?
essence: A wrong remedy can intensify the wound it claims to fix.
simple_meaning: A bad remedy can make a bad situation worse. Tulsidas uses a sharp image to say that the wrong response only deepens suffering.
insight: It shifts you to question quick fixes that numb rather than heal.
modern_relevance: You are already overwhelmed, and someone tells you to just drink, scroll, or shut down. The verse names that false relief: not every soothing thing is a cure.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कैकइ सुअन जोगु जग जोई। चतुर बिरंचि दीन्ह मोहि सोई॥ दसरथ तनय राम लघु भाई। दीन्हि मोहि बिधि बादि बड़ाई ॥
translation: कैकेयी के लड़के के लिए संसार में जो कुछ योग्य था, चतुर विधाता ने मुझे वही दिया। पर 'दशरथजी का पुत्र' और 'राम का छोटा भाई' होने की बड़ाई मुझे विधाता ने व्यर्थ ही दी ॥
english_translation: Whatever was fit for Kaikeyi's son in this world, the wise creator gave me that alone. The glory of being Dasharath's son and Ram's younger brother was given to me by fate in vain.
essence: Real dignity comes from accepting the place that truly fits you.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he received only what suited him, and the honour of being Ram's brother was never truly his to claim.
insight: It shifts you from comparison to rightful place, so you stop measuring yourself by someone else's status.
modern_relevance: You watch someone else get the title, the praise, the family approval you wanted. Bharat's clarity says the role that fits you is enough, and borrowed honour cannot feed your heart.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: तुम्ह सब कहहु कढ़ावन टीका। राय रजायसु सब कहँ नीका॥ उतरु देउँ केहि बिधि केहि केही। कहहु सुखेन जथा रुचि जेही ॥
translation: आप सब लोग भी मुझे राज तिलक कराने को कह रहे हैं! राजा की आज्ञा सभी के लिए अच्छी है। मैं किस-किस को किस-किस प्रकार से उत्तर दूँ? जिसकी जैसी रुचि हो, आप लोग सुखपूर्वक वही कहें ॥
english_translation: You all are telling me to arrange the coronation! The king's command is good for everyone. How am I to answer each person in each way? Speak freely as you like, in whichever way suits you.
essence: You do not need to satisfy every demand at once.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he cannot answer everyone’s expectations about his coronation. He asks them to speak as they wish and says the king’s order must be respected.
insight: It teaches you to stay composed under competing demands and not let public pressure distort your duty.
modern_relevance: Your family group chat is full of opinions about what you should do next, and every message wants a different answer. Bharat’s calm shows you can refuse the noise without becoming harsh.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: मोहि कुमातु समेत बिहाई। कहहु कहिहि के कीन्ह भलाई॥ मो बिनु को सचराचर माहीं। जेहि सिय रामु प्रानप्रिय नाहीं ॥
translation: मेरी कुमाता कैकेयी समेत मुझे छोड़कर, कहिए और कौन कहेगा कि यह काम अच्छा किया गया? जड़-चेतन जगत् में मेरे सिवा और कौन है, जिसको श्री सीता-रामजी प्राणों के समान प्यारे न हों ॥
english_translation: Leaving aside my evil-minded mother, who will say that this was well done? In all the moving and unmoving world, who besides me does not hold Sita and Ram dearer than life?
essence: What looks like a gain to others can still be a deep loss to you.
simple_meaning: Bharat says no one can call this choice good, because he has been left behind. For him, nothing in the world is dearer than Sita and Ram.
insight: It teaches you to trust your own clear seeing when others mistake sacrifice for success.
modern_relevance: You smiled through the family dinner after being blamed for a decision you never made. Everyone called it fine. You knew exactly what it cost.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: परम हानि सब कहँ बड़ लाहू। अदिनु मोर नहिं दूषन काहू॥ संसय सील प्रेम बस अहहू। सबुइ उचित सब जो कछु कहहू ॥
translation: जो परम हानि है, उसी में सबको बड़ा लाभ दिख रहा है। मेरा बुरा दिन है किसी का दोष नहीं। आप सब जो कुछ कहते हैं सो सब उचित ही है, क्योंकि आप लोग संशय, शील और प्रेम के वश हैं ॥
english_translation: What is my greatest loss looks like the greatest gain to everyone else. My own bad day is no one else's fault. Everything you say is proper, because you are all moved by doubt, virtue, and love.
essence: Loss can be borne without blame when the heart stays clear.
simple_meaning: Bharat says his exile feels like a huge loss to him, but others may see benefit in it. He refuses blame and accepts that everyone is speaking from care, doubt, and love.
insight: It shifts you from accusation to mature acceptance, letting you name pain without making enemies of everyone around you.
modern_relevance: You got passed over for a promotion, and the team says it was 'for the best.' It still hurts. This verse teaches you to hold the pain without immediately turning it into resentment.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: राम मातु सुठि सरलचित मो पर प्रेमु बिसेषि। कहइ सुभाय सनेह बस मोरि दीनता देखि ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी की माता बहुत ही सरल हृदय हैं और मुझ पर उनका विशेष प्रेम है, इसलिए मेरी दीनता देखकर वे स्वाभाविक स्नेहवश ही ऐसा कह रही हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram's mother is very simple-hearted and has special affection for me, so seeing my helplessness, she speaks this way out of natural love.
essence: Bharat sees affection beneath Kaikeyi's harshness.
simple_meaning: Bharat says Kaikeyi is naturally tender toward him and speaks out of affection after seeing his helplessness.
insight: It shifts the mind from judging only the surface words to seeing the emotion underneath them.
modern_relevance: A parent says something cutting while watching you break down, and later you realize the words came from worry, not cruelty. Hurt can distort even love.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: गुर बिबेक सागर जगु जाना। जिन्हहि बिस्व कर बदर समाना॥ मो कहँ तिलक साज सज सोऊ। भएँ बिधि बिमुख बिमुख सबु कोऊ ॥
translation: गुरुजी ज्ञान के समुद्र हैं, इस बात को सारा जगत् जानता है, जिसके लिए विश्व हथेली पर रखे हुए बेर के समान है, वे भी मेरे लिए राजतिलक का साज सज रहे हैं। सत्य है, विधाता के विपरीत होने पर सब कोई विपरीत हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: The guru is an ocean of discernment, and the whole world knows it. To him, the world is like a berry held in the palm. Yet even he is arranging my coronation. When fate turns against you, everyone turns against you too.
essence: Even wisdom cannot stop the world from turning harsh when fortune turns.
simple_meaning: Bharat says that even the greatest teacher sees the world as small, yet he is preparing a coronation for him. But when fate turns against someone, everyone seems to turn away too.
insight: It shifts the mind from expecting fairness in the moment to seeing how quickly support can change under pressure.
modern_relevance: You watch a promotion vanish, and suddenly even your allies go quiet. This verse names that strange loneliness: when life shifts against you, people often shift with it.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: परिहरि रामु सीय जग माहीं। कोउ न कहिहि मोर मत नाहीं॥ सो मैं सुनब सहब सुखु मानी। अंतहुँ कीच तहाँ जहँ पानी ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी और सीताजी को छोड़कर जगत् में कोई यह नहीं कहेगा कि इस अनर्थ में मेरी सम्मति नहीं है। मैं उसे सुखपूर्वक सुनूँगा और सहूँगा, क्योंकि जहाँ पानी होता है, वहाँ अन्त में कीचड़ होता ही है ॥
english_translation: No one in the world, except Ram and Sita, will say I had no part in this. I will hear it gladly and bear it, because where there is water, mud will eventually appear.
essence: A clean heart can endure blame without needing to defend itself.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he will accept blame without protest. Even if people accuse him, he will endure it calmly, because any situation with good intentions can still end in some stain.
insight: It shifts you from image-protection to inner steadiness, so you can endure blame without losing your centre.
modern_relevance: You helped organize the plan, and now the group chat is blaming you for the mess. You could scramble to clear your name, or you could stay steady and let the noise pass.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: डरु न मोहि जग कहिहि कि पोचू। परलोकहु कर नाहिन सोचू॥ एकइ उर बस दुसह दवारी। मोहि लगि भे सिय रामु दुखारी ॥
translation: मुझे इसका डर नहीं है कि जगत् मुझे बुरा कहेगा और न मुझे परलोक का ही सोच है। मेरे हृदय में तो बस, एक ही दुःसह दावानल धधक रहा है कि मेरे कारण श्री सीता-रामजी दुःखी हुए ॥
english_translation: I do not fear that the world will call me base, nor do I worry about the next world. Only one unbearable fire burns in my heart: because of me, Sita and Ram are suffering.
essence: Love hurts most when it sees itself as the cause of another's pain.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he does not care about public shame or even the afterlife. What torments him is that Ram and Sita are suffering because of him.
insight: It shifts remorse from self-image to relationship: the measure is not how you look, but whom you have wounded.
modern_relevance: You replay a conversation all night, not because people might judge you, but because someone you love is hurting and you helped cause it.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जीवन लाहु लखन भल पावा। सबु तजि राम चरन मनु लावा॥ मोर जनम रघुबर बन लागी। झूठ काह पछिताउँ अभागी ॥
translation: जीवन का उत्तम लाभ तो लक्ष्मण ने पाया, जिन्होंने सब कुछ तजकर श्री रामजी के चरणों में मन लगाया। मेरा जन्म तो श्री रामजी के वनवास के लिए ही हुआ था। मैं अभागा झूठ-मूठ क्या पछताता हूँ? ॥
english_translation: Lakshman has gained the best reward of life: leaving everything, he set his mind on Ram's feet. My birth was meant for Raghubar's exile; why should I, the unfortunate one, pretend to regret it?
essence: What looks like sacrifice can be the truest gain.
simple_meaning: Lakshman’s life is praised as successful because he gave up everything and fixed his mind on Ram. The speaker also accepts that her own life was meant to support Ram’s exile.
insight: It shifts the mind from measuring success by gain to measuring it by fidelity.
modern_relevance: You walk past a promotion because taking it would betray someone you love. Later, you realise the real loss would have been becoming the kind of person who could not do that.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: आपनि दारुन दीनता कहउँ सबहि सिरु नाइ। देखें बिनु रघुनाथ पद जिय कै जरनि न जाइ ॥
translation: सबको सिर झुकाकर मैं अपनी दारुण दीनता कहता हूँ। श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों के दर्शन किए बिना मेरे जी की जलन न जाएगी ॥
english_translation: Bowing to everyone, I speak of my deep helplessness. Without seeing Raghunath's feet, the burning in my heart will not go.
essence: Humble surrender names the wound that only Ram can heal.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he is deeply helpless and humbly admits it to everyone. Only seeing Ram again can ease the burning in his heart.
insight: It shifts you from self-protective pride to humble longing for what truly restores you.
modern_relevance: You’ve replayed the same conversation all night, and nothing in you settles. The apology, the reunion, the answer you’re waiting for — you know exactly where your heart is headed.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: आन उपाउ मोहि नहिं सूझा। को जिय कै रघुबर बिनु बूझा॥ एकहिं आँक इहइ मन माहीं। प्रातकाल चलिहउँ प्रभु पाहीं ॥
translation: मुझे दूसरा कोई उपाय नहीं सूझता। श्री राम के बिना मेरे हृदय की बात कौन जान सकता है? मन में एक ही आँक (निश्चयपूर्वक) यही है कि प्रातः काल श्री रामजी के पास चल दूँगा ॥
english_translation: I can see no other way. Who can understand the heart without Ram? My mind has made one firm resolve: at dawn, I will go to my Lord.
essence: When the heart is clear, only return remains.
simple_meaning: Bharat feels there is no other solution except to go to Ram at dawn. Only Ram can truly understand what is in his heart.
insight: It shifts you from mental circling to direct return. The right response is not more analysis, but movement toward what is sacred and true.
modern_relevance: You lie awake after a family argument, rehearsing explanations that never feel enough. Then the mind settles on one honest move: go face the person who matters, not the story in your head.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जद्यपि मैं अनभल अपराधी। भै मोहि कारन सकल उपाधी॥ तदपि सरन सनमुख मोहि देखी। छमि सब करिहहिं कृपा बिसेषी ॥
translation: यद्यपि मैं बुरा हूँ और अपराधी हूँ और मेरे ही कारण यह सब उपद्रव हुआ है, तथापि श्री रामजी मुझे शरण में सम्मुख आया हुआ देखकर सब अपराध क्षमा करके मुझ पर विशेष कृपा करेंगे ॥
english_translation: Though I am unworthy and guilty, and all this trouble came because of me, still, if Ram sees me come before him in surrender, he will forgive every fault and show me special grace.
essence: Surrender does what guilt cannot: it makes forgiveness possible.
simple_meaning: Even when you know you caused the pain, surrendering sincerely can meet forgiveness and special grace.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to humble return, trusting grace to meet honesty.
modern_relevance: You rehearse an apology in the car before walking into the room where you hurt someone. The fear says hide. This verse says come honestly anyway.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: सील सकुच सुठि सरल सुभाऊ। कृपा सनेह सदन रघुराऊ॥ अरिहुक अनभल कीन्ह न रामा। मैं सिसु सेवक जद्यपि बामा ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी शील, संकोच, अत्यन्त सरल स्वभाव, कृपा और स्नेह के घर हैं। श्री रामजी ने कभी शत्रु का भी अनिष्ट नहीं किया। मैं यद्यपि टेढ़ा हूँ, पर हूँ तो उनका बच्चा और सेवक ही ॥
english_translation: Raghunath is the home of virtue, modesty, simplicity, compassion, and love. Ram has never harmed even an enemy. Though I am crooked, I am still his child and servant.
essence: Ram's love is large enough to hold your crookedness.
simple_meaning: Ram is naturally kind, gentle, and loving. He never harms even an enemy. The speaker calls himself crooked, yet still claims the place of a child and servant.
insight: It shifts you from self-rejection to humble return: speak honestly, serve sincerely, and trust that devotion still reaches home.
modern_relevance: You rehearse an apology in the car before walking back into a room where you know you messed up. This verse says your mistake is real, but your place in love is not gone.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तुम्ह पै पाँच मोर भल मानी। आयसु आसिष देहु सुबानी॥ जेहिं सुनि बिनय मोहि जनु जानी। आवहिं बहुरि रामु रजधानी ॥
translation: आप पंच (सब) लोग भी इसी में मेरा कल्याण मानकर सुंदर वाणी से आज्ञा और आशीर्वाद दीजिए, जिसमें मेरी विनती सुनकर और मुझे अपना दास जानकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी राजधानी को लौट आवें ॥
english_translation: Please, all of you, see this as my good. Give me your blessing and kind words so that, hearing my plea and knowing me as your servant, Ram may return to the capital.
essence: Humility asks for blessing so the beloved may return.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks everyone to bless him and speak kindly so Ram will return to the capital. He treats this as the highest good, not his own gain.
insight: It shifts you from self-protection to humble service of a larger good.
modern_relevance: You call three relatives before making a hard family decision, not to defend yourself, but to ask for their blessing. You want the choice to serve what is right, not what flatters you.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जद्यपि जनमु कुमातु तें मैं सठु सदा सदोस। आपन जानि न त्यागिहहिं मोहि रघुबीर भरोस ॥
translation: यद्यपि मेरा जन्म कुमाता से हुआ है और मैं दुष्ट तथा सदा दोषयुक्त भी हूँ, तो भी मुझे श्री रामजी का भरोसा है कि वे मुझे अपना जानकर त्यागेंगे नहीं ॥
english_translation: Although I was born from a bad mother and am wicked and always full of faults, I still trust Raghubir will not abandon me, knowing me as his own.
essence: Your flaws do not end Ram's claim on you.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he is full of flaws, yet he trusts that Ram will not reject him because Ram recognizes him as his own.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-rejection to trust in being accepted despite imperfection.
modern_relevance: You replay your mistakes before sleep and assume they have made you unlovable. This verse answers that fear with a quieter truth: being flawed does not erase belonging.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: भरत बचन सब कहँ प्रिय लागे। राम सनेह सुधाँ जनु पागे॥ लोग बियोग बिषम बिष दागे। मंत्र सबीज सुनत जनु जागे ॥
translation: भरतजी के वचन सबको प्यारे लगे। मानो वे श्री रामजी के प्रेमरूपी अमृत में पगे हुए थे। श्री रामवियोग रूपी भीषण विष से सब लोग जले हुए थे। वे मानो बीज सहित मंत्र को सुनते ही जाग उठे ॥
english_translation: Bharat's words were dear to everyone. They seemed soaked in the nectar of Ram's love. Everyone was scorched by the terrible poison of separation from Ram. Hearing those seed-filled words, they woke as if from sleep.
essence: Love-filled words can wake people from grief.
simple_meaning: Bharat's words comfort everyone because they are full of love for Ram. His speech reaches people who are already hurting from separation and helps them wake up from grief.
insight: It shows how compassionate speech can interrupt collective despair and restore attention.
modern_relevance: A family meeting after a painful loss can feel locked in silence until one person speaks with real tenderness. That kind of speech doesn't erase grief, but it lets everyone breathe again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मातु सचिव गुर पुर नर नारी। सकल सनेहँ बिकल भए भारी॥ भरतहि कहहिं सराहि सराही। राम प्रेम मूरति तनु आही ॥
translation: माता, मंत्री, गुरु, नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष सभी स्नेह के कारण बहुत ही व्याकुल हो गए। सब भरतजी को सराह-सराहकर कहते हैं कि आपका शरीर श्री रामप्रेम की साक्षात मूर्ति ही है ॥
english_translation: The mother, ministers, teacher, and all the men and women of the city were overwhelmed with love. Everyone kept praising Bharata, saying, 'Your body is nothing but a living form of love for Rama.'
essence: Love for Ram becomes so complete that it shows on the body itself.
simple_meaning: Everyone in Ayodhya is overwhelmed by love and grief, and they praise Bharata as a living embodiment of love for Rama.
insight: It shifts attention from outward role to inward devotion, showing that love can become a person’s visible identity.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone refuses an unfair advantage and still speaks gently. People don’t call that weakness — they feel the depth of a heart that loves without bargaining.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तात भरत अस काहे न कहहू। प्रान समान राम प्रिय अहहू॥ जो पावँरु अपनी जड़ताईं। तुम्हहि सुगाइ मातु कुटिलाईं ॥
translation: हे तात भरत! आप ऐसा क्यों न कहें। श्री रामजी को आप प्राणों के समान प्यारे हैं। जो नीच अपनी मूर्खता से आपकी माता कैकेयी की कुटिलता को लेकर आप पर सन्देह करेगा, ॥
english_translation: O dear Bharat, why would you not say this? Ram is dear to you as life itself. Anyone who, in their foolishness, doubts you because of your mother Kaikeyi's crookedness is vile.
essence: True love for Ram cannot be hidden by public suspicion.
simple_meaning: Bharat's love for Ram is so obvious that no wise person should doubt him because of Kaikeyi's actions.
insight: It separates your character from the actions of those around you, and asks others to judge you fairly.
modern_relevance: After a family scandal, people start whispering that you must be complicit too. This verse reminds you that your own love and integrity are not erased by someone else's choice.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सो सठु कोटिक पुरुष समेता। बसिहि कलप सत नरक निकेता॥ अहि अघ अवगुन नहिं मनि गहई। हरइ गरल दुख दारिद दहई ॥
translation: वह दुष्ट करोड़ों पुरखों सहित सौ कल्पों तक नरक के घर में निवास करेगा। साँप के पाप और अवगुण को मणि नहीं ग्रहण करती, बल्कि वह विष को हर लेती है और दुःख तथा दरिद्रता को भस्म कर देती है ॥
english_translation: That wicked one, along with millions of others, will dwell for hundreds of kalpas in the house of hell. A snake's poison and faults are not taken by a jewel; instead, it removes the poison and burns away suffering and poverty.
essence: A pure person removes poison instead of carrying it.
simple_meaning: A truly wicked person falls into deep suffering, while a true jewel does the opposite of poison: it removes harm and destroys misery.
insight: It shifts attention from outer status to inner effect: does your presence spread harm, or remove it?
modern_relevance: A room full of gossip can make one person meaner, but another person calmly changes the whole atmosphere. Some people absorb poison; others quietly clear it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अवसि चलिअ बन रामु जहँ भरत मंत्रु भल कीन्ह। सोक सिंधु बूड़त सबहि तुम्ह अवलंबनु दीन्ह ॥
translation: हे भरतजी! वन को अवश्य चलिए, जहाँ श्री रामजी हैं, आपने बहुत अच्छी सलाह विचारी। शोक समुद्र में डूबते हुए सब लोगों को आपने (बड़ा) सहारा दे दिया ॥
english_translation: O Bharat, you should surely go to the forest where Ram is. You have made a wise decision, and you have given everyone a great support while they were sinking in an ocean of sorrow.
essence: Wise support can keep others afloat in grief.
simple_meaning: Bharat is praised for wisely choosing to go to Ram in the forest, and for giving grieving people real support.
insight: It shifts the mind from private grief to responsible steadiness, showing how your judgment can become shelter for others.
modern_relevance: You are the one everyone texts when a family crisis hits, even though you are barely holding it together. Your calm choice can become the hand that keeps others from going under.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भा सब कें मन मोदु न थोरा। जनु घन धुनि सुनि चातक मोरा॥ चलत प्रात लखि निरनउ नीके। भरतु प्रानप्रिय भे सबही के ॥
translation: सबके मन में कम आनंद नहीं हुआ (अर्थात बहुत ही आनंद हुआ)! मानो मेघों की गर्जना सुनकर चातक और मोर आनंदित हो रहे हों। (दूसरे दिन) प्रातःकाल चलने का सुंदर निर्णय देखकर भरतजी सभी को प्राणप्रिय हो गए ॥
english_translation: Everyone’s heart filled with joy, like a chatak and a peacock hearing thunder. At dawn, seeing his noble decision to depart, Bharat became dear as life to everyone.
essence: Selfless resolve makes you beloved without asking for praise.
simple_meaning: Everyone felt great joy when Bharat decided to leave at dawn. His choice made him beloved to all.
insight: It shows how decisive, humble action restores trust and softens collective sorrow.
modern_relevance: A tense family meeting ends, and someone finally says, “I’ll handle it.” The room changes at once. Clear, unselfish action can calm everyone faster than long explanations.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनिहि बंदि भरतहि सिरु नाई। चले सकल घर बिदा कराई॥ धन्य भरत जीवनु जग माहीं। सीलु सनेहु सराहत जाहीं ॥
translation: मुनि वशिष्ठजी की वंदना करके और भरतजी को सिर नवाकर, सब लोग विदा लेकर अपने-अपने घर को चले। जगत में भरतजी का जीवन धन्य है, इस प्रकार कहते हुए वे उनके शील और स्नेह की सराहना करते जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: After bowing to the sage and to Bharat, everyone took leave and returned home. In the world, Bharat's life is blessed, they said, praising his character and affection.
essence: Bharat's nobility makes departure feel like a blessing.
simple_meaning: Everyone bows to the sage and to Bharat, then leaves. Bharat is praised as blessed in this world for his noble conduct and loving heart.
insight: It shows that real authority can inspire reverence without force, and that character can make even a farewell feel sacred.
modern_relevance: After a difficult family meeting, people stand up quietly, touch an elder's feet, and leave with less anger than they arrived. Some people change a room simply by how they carry themselves.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहहिं परसपर भा बड़ काजू। सकल चलै कर साजहिं साजू॥ जेहि राखहिं रहु घर रखवारी। सो जानइ जनु गरदनि मारी ॥
translation: आपस में कहते हैं, बड़ा काम हुआ। सभी चलने की तैयारी करने लगे। जिसको भी घर की रखवाली के लिए रहो, ऐसा कहकर रखते हैं, वही समझता है मानो मेरी गर्दन मारी गई ॥
english_translation: They said to one another, "A great task has been done." Everyone began making preparations to leave. Whoever is told to stay and guard the house feels as if his throat has been cut.
essence: The unseen duty feels like a wound to the one who must carry it.
simple_meaning: Everyone is eager to go, and nobody wants to be left behind to guard the house. Being assigned the staying role feels like a punishment.
insight: It shifts attention from the glamorous task to the necessary one that keeps everything safe.
modern_relevance: The group chat is full of excitement about the trip, but someone has to stay back and lock up. The volunteer role is invisible, yet the whole plan depends on it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोउ कह रहन कहिअ नहिं काहू। को न चहइ जग जीवन लाहू ॥
translation: कोई-कोई कहते हैं- रहने के लिए किसी को भी मत कहो, जगत में जीवन का लाभ कौन नहीं चाहता? ॥
english_translation: Some say, 'Do not ask anyone to stay.' Who in the world does not want the gain of life?
essence: Everyone clings to life’s benefit, even while speaking of letting go.
simple_meaning: People may say no one should be asked to stay, because everyone wants the benefit of life. The line points to a shared human urge to keep living and keep what life offers.
insight: It shifts attention from blame to shared human desire, making the scene feel less personal and more universal.
modern_relevance: At a family meeting where everyone is quietly trying to protect their own corner, the same motive is everywhere: nobody wants loss, and everyone wants to keep the good of their life intact.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जरउ सो संपति सदन सुखु सुहृद मातु पितु भाइ। सनमुख होत जो राम पद करै न सहस सहाइ ॥
translation: वह सम्पत्ति, घर, सुख, मित्र, माता, पिता, भाई जल जाए जो श्री रामजी के चरणों के सम्मुख होने में हँसते हुए (प्रसन्नतापूर्वक) सहायता न करे ॥
english_translation: May that wealth, home, comfort, friend, mother, father, and brother burn away that does not gladly help when the feet of Ram are in sight.
essence: Anything that cannot help you face Ram is not worth keeping.
simple_meaning: Wealth, home, comfort, and even family are worthless if they do not joyfully support your movement toward Ram.
insight: It shifts loyalty from possession and comfort to what helps you face the divine.
modern_relevance: You are packing for a move and suddenly see which friendships, habits, and comforts truly support your deepest commitments. Anything that quietly pulls you away may not deserve a place.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: घर घर साजहिं बाहन नाना। हरषु हृदयँ परभात पयाना॥ भरत जाइ घर कीन्ह बिचारू। नगरु बाजि गज भवन भँडारू ॥
translation: घर-घर लोग अनेकों प्रकार की सवारियाँ सजा रहे हैं। हृदय में (बड़ा) हर्ष है कि सबेरे चलना है। भरतजी ने घर जाकर विचार किया कि नगर घोड़े, हाथी, महल-खजाना आदि- ॥
english_translation: People in every house were preparing many kinds of vehicles. Their hearts were full of joy, because they would leave at dawn. Bharat went home and thought it over: the city, its horses, elephants, palaces, and stores of wealth...
essence: Before leaving, Bharat first measures what he must not neglect.
simple_meaning: The city is getting ready to leave at dawn, and Bharat is taking stock of everything the kingdom contains.
insight: It shifts attention from excitement about departure to responsibility for what remains behind.
modern_relevance: You stand in a half-packed house before moving day, checking what must stay safe, what must be carried, and what cannot be abandoned carelessly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: संपति सब रघुपति कै आही। जौं बिनु जतन चलौं तजि ताही॥ तौ परिनाम न मोरि भलाई। पाप सिरोमनि साइँ दोहाई ॥
translation: सारी सम्पत्ति श्री रघुनाथजी की है। यदि उसकी (रक्षा की) व्यवस्था किए बिना उसे ऐसे ही छोड़कर चल दूँ, तो परिणाम में मेरी भलाई नहीं है, क्योंकि स्वामी का द्रोह सब पापों में शिरोमणि (श्रेष्ठ) है ॥
english_translation: All wealth belongs to Raghupati. If I leave it behind without arranging for its care, there will be no good outcome for me, for betraying a master is the chief of all sins.
essence: Trust turns possession into responsibility.
simple_meaning: Bharat sees Ram's property as Ram's alone, and he refuses to leave it unattended. For him, neglecting a master's trust is a serious moral failure.
insight: It shifts loyalty from sentiment to responsibility: if something has been entrusted to you, you must preserve it carefully.
modern_relevance: You hand over your apartment keys before a long trip and keep wondering whether the plants, bills, and mail were left in good hands. Bharat feels that same weight: trust is something you must actively protect.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: करइ स्वामि हित सेवकु सोई। दूषन कोटि देइ किन कोई॥ अस बिचारि सुचि सेवक बोले। जे सपनेहुँ निज धरम न डोले ॥
translation: सेवक वही है, जो स्वामी का हित करे, चाहे कोई करोड़ों दोष क्यों न दे। भरतजी ने ऐसा विचारकर ऐसे विश्वासपात्र सेवकों को बुलाया, जो कभी स्वप्न में भी अपने धर्म से नहीं डिगे थे ॥
english_translation: The true servant acts for the master's good, even if millions of faults are laid upon him. Thinking this, Bharat called trustworthy servants who never wavered from their duty, even in a dream.
essence: Real service puts another's good above your own reputation.
simple_meaning: A real servant protects the master's good, no matter how much criticism comes. Bharat then chose only those helpers who would never drift from their duty.
insight: It shifts attention from protecting your image to protecting the task and the people depending on you.
modern_relevance: You take the heat for a family decision, then still do the next right thing. The comments may sting, but the work still needs loyal hands.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहि सबु मरमु धरमु भल भाषा। जो जेहि लायक सो तेहिं राखा॥ करि सबु जतनु राखि रखवारे। राम मातु पहिं भरतु सिधारे ॥
translation: भरतजी ने उनको सब भेद समझाकर फिर उत्तम धर्म बतलाया और जो जिस योग्य था, उसे उसी काम पर नियुक्त कर दिया। सब व्यवस्था करके, रक्षकों को रखकर भरतजी राम माता कौसल्याजी के पास गए ॥
english_translation: Having explained everything clearly and spoken of righteous conduct in gentle words, he assigned each person to the task suited to them. After making all arrangements and posting guards, Bharata went to Queen Kausalya, Ram's mother.
essence: Care becomes real when it organizes people and protects what matters.
simple_meaning: Bharata explains the situation, gives everyone the right responsibility, sets guards in place, and then goes to Kausalya.
insight: It teaches you to turn concern into structure: clear communication, proper roles, and steady protection before emotional reassurance.
modern_relevance: A family crisis hits, and everyone is panicking in different directions. You stop, explain the situation clearly, give each person a role, and only then go to comfort the one who is grieving most.
speaker: Bharata

verse_text: आरत जननी जानि सब भरत सनेह सुजान। कहेउ बनावन पालकीं सजन सुखासन जान ॥
translation: स्नेह के सुजान (प्रेम के तत्व को जानने वाले) भरतजी ने सब माताओं को आर्त (दुःखी) जानकर उनके लिए पालकियाँ तैयार करने तथा सुखासन यान (सुखपाल) सजाने के लिए कहा ॥
english_translation: Knowing all the mothers were distressed, wise Bharata said, "Prepare palanquins and comfortable seats for them."
essence: Love shows itself by making suffering easier to carry.
simple_meaning: Bharat sees that the mothers are in pain and immediately arranges a comfortable way for them to travel.
insight: It shifts care from feeling sympathy to removing someone’s burden in concrete ways.
modern_relevance: Your mother is exhausted after bad news, and you stop everything to arrange the ride, the chair, the water, the plan. Love becomes logistics.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: चक्क चक्कि जिमि पुर नर नारी। चहत प्रात उर आरत भारी॥ जागत सब निसि भयउ बिहाना। भरत बोलाए सचिव सुजाना ॥
translation: नगर के नर-नारी चकवे-चकवी की भाँति हृदय में अत्यन्त आर्त होकर प्रातःकाल का होना चाहते हैं। सारी रात जागते-जागते सबेरा हो गया। तब भरतजी ने चतुर मंत्रियों को बुलवाया ॥
english_translation: Like chakwa and chakwi, the people of the city longed for morning with aching hearts. The whole night passed awake, and then Bharat called his wise ministers.
essence: Restless hearts make even dawn feel like rescue.
simple_meaning: The city is filled with restless longing, and the night feels endless. When dawn finally comes, Bharat gathers his wise ministers.
insight: It frames collective grief as a tense pause before the next act of duty.
modern_relevance: You keep checking the clock at 4:17 a.m., unable to sleep before a hard conversation. The room is quiet, but your chest isn't. This verse knows that kind of night.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहेउ लेहु सबु तिलक समाजू। बनहिं देब मुनि रामहि राजू॥ बेगि चलहु सुनि सचिव जोहारे। तुरत तुरग रथ नाग सँवारे ॥
translation: और कहा- तिलक का सब सामान ले चलो। वन में ही मुनि वशिष्ठजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी को राज्य देंगे, जल्दी चलो। यह सुनकर मंत्रियों ने वंदना की और तुरंत घोड़े, रथ और हाथी सजवा दिए ॥
english_translation: Take all the tilak arrangements with you. In the forest, the sage Vasishtha will give Ram the kingdom. Hearing this, the ministers bowed, and at once had horses, chariots, and elephants prepared.
essence: Real loyalty prepares another person's honor before your own comfort.
simple_meaning: Bharat tells everyone to bring the coronation items and prepare to go quickly, because he believes Ram will be crowned in the forest. The ministers bow and ready the horses, chariots, and elephants.
insight: It shifts attention from personal gain to rightful service, even when the setting is painful.
modern_relevance: You are packing for a ceremony that should have happened in your own home, but you still arrange everything for someone else. That is the strange dignity Bharat lives with.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: अरुंधती अरु अगिनि समाऊ। रथ चढ़ि चले प्रथम मुनिराऊ॥ बिप्र बृंद चढ़ि बाहन नाना। चले सकल तप तेज निधाना ॥
translation: सबसे पहले मुनिराज वशिष्ठजी अरुंधती और अग्निहोत्र की सब सामग्री सहित रथ पर सवार होकर चले। फिर ब्राह्मणों के समूह, जो सब के सब तपस्या और तेज के भंडार थे, अनेकों सवारियों पर चढ़कर चले ॥
english_translation: First, the sage Vashistha rode out in a chariot with Arundhati and the fire offerings. Then the Brahmins, all treasure-houses of austerity and radiance, set out on many mounts.
essence: The procession begins with reverence, not haste.
simple_meaning: Vashistha leads the procession, followed by Brahmins riding out in splendour. It is a ceremonial departure, not a teaching verse.
insight: It shifts attention from inner teaching to the communal movement of a sacred occasion.
modern_relevance: A wedding convoy pulls out before dawn, cars packed with flowers, elders, and ritual items. Everyone is in motion because something sacred is about to happen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नगर लोग सब सजि सजि जाना। चित्रकूट कहँ कीन्ह पयाना॥ सिबिका सुभग न जाहिं बखानी। चढ़ि चढ़ि चलत भईं सब रानी ॥
translation: नगर के सब लोग रथों को सजा-सजाकर चित्रकूट को चल पड़े। जिनका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता, ऐसी सुंदर पालकियों पर चढ़-चढ़कर सब रानियाँ चलीं ॥
english_translation: All the people of the city, dressed and ready, set out for Chitrakoot. The queens climbed into beautiful palanquins beyond description and went along too.
essence: Ayodhya itself turns toward Chitrakoot in shared grief.
simple_meaning: The whole city sets out for Chitrakoot, with the queens traveling in beautiful palanquins.
insight: It shows the scale of the farewell and the public weight of Ram's exile.
modern_relevance: A family loads the car before dawn, not for a holiday but for a goodbye no one wants. Everyone moves together because the moment matters more than comfort.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सौंपि नगर सुचि सेवकनि सादर सकल चलाइ। सुमिरि राम सिय चरन तब चले भरत दोउ भाइ ॥
translation: विश्वासपात्र सेवकों को नगर सौंपकर और सबको आदरपूर्वक रवाना करके, तब श्री सीता-रामजी के चरणों को स्मरण करके भरत-शत्रुघ्न दोनों भाई चले ॥
english_translation: Entrusting the city to trustworthy servants and sending everyone off with respect, Bharat and Shatrughna then left, remembering the feet of Ram and Sita.
essence: You serve best when you release ownership.
simple_meaning: Bharat leaves after handing the city over to trusted servants and respectfully sending everyone away, while keeping Ram and Sita in his heart.
insight: It shifts duty from control to trust, showing how to leave something in good hands.
modern_relevance: You lock the office, brief the team, and leave the keys with someone reliable before stepping into the night. Real responsibility is calm, respectful, and complete.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम दरस बस सब नर नारी। जनु करि करिनि चले तकि बारी॥ बन सिय रामु समुझि मन माहीं। सानुज भरत पयादेहिं जाहीं ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन के वश में हुए (दर्शन की अनन्य लालसा से) सब नर-नारी ऐसे चले मानो प्यासे हाथी-हथिनी जल को तककर (बड़ी तेजी से बावले से हुए) जा रहे हों। श्री सीताजी-रामजी (सब सुखों को छोड़कर) वन में हैं, मन में ऐसा विचार करके छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्नजी सहित भरतजी पैदल ही चले जा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: All men and women were seized by the sight of Ram, rushing forward like thirsty elephants and cows toward water. Thinking in their minds, “Sita and Ram are in the forest,” Bharat and Shatrughna walked on foot.
essence: Longing for Ram makes comfort feel irrelevant.
simple_meaning: Everyone is drawn toward Ram with intense longing, and Bharat walks on foot, keeping Sita and Ram in mind.
insight: It shifts attention from status and comfort to the force of sincere longing.
modern_relevance: You see a loved one after months apart, and the whole room starts moving faster without anyone saying why. That pull is what this verse captures.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि सनेहु लोग अनुरागे। उतरि चले हय गय रथ त्यागे॥ जाइ समीप राखि निज डोली। राम मातु मृदु बानी बोली ॥
translation: उनका स्नेह देखकर लोग प्रेम में मग्न हो गए और सब घोड़े, हाथी, रथों को छोड़कर उनसे उतरकर पैदल चलने लगे। तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी की माता कौसल्याजी भरत के पास जाकर और अपनी पालकी उनके समीप खड़ी करके कोमल वाणी से बोलीं- ॥
english_translation: Seeing their affection, the people were filled with love and got down from horses, elephants, and chariots to walk on foot. Then Kaushalya, Ram's mother, came near Bharat, placed her palanquin beside him, and spoke softly.
essence: True affection makes even a crowd move gently.
simple_meaning: Bharat's presence moves everyone to tenderness. People abandon their vehicles and walk beside him, and Kaushalya approaches him gently to speak.
insight: It shows how sincere love can soften an entire crowd and shift the social mood without force.
modern_relevance: You enter a room after a painful family decision, and the whole atmosphere changes. People lower their voices, stand up, and move more carefully because your presence has made tenderness necessary.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तात चढ़हु रथ बलि महतारी। होइहि प्रिय परिवारु दुखारी॥ तुम्हरें चलत चलिहि सबु लोगू। सकल सोक कृस नहिं मग जोगू ॥
translation: हे बेटा! माता बलैया लेती है, तुम रथ पर चढ़ जाओ। नहीं तो सारा परिवार दुःखी हो जाएगा। तुम्हारे पैदल चलने से सभी लोग पैदल चलेंगे। शोक के मारे सब दुबले हो रहे हैं, पैदल रास्ते के (पैदल चलने के) योग्य नहीं हैं ॥
english_translation: “My dear, mount the chariot. Your mother blesses you. Otherwise, the whole family will remain sorrowful. If you walk, everyone will walk with you. Everyone is already worn thin with grief and not fit for the road on foot.”
essence: Love sometimes means choosing the easier road for everyone else.
simple_meaning: The speaker asks the brothers to ride in the chariot so the grieving family does not have to follow on foot and suffer more.
insight: It shifts attention from personal preference to the strain your choice places on others.
modern_relevance: You see a loved one already exhausted, yet you keep asking them to keep pace with you. This verse reminds you to notice when your own choice is making everyone else suffer more.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सिर धरि बचन चरन सिरु नाई। रथ चढ़ि चलत भए दोउ भाई॥ तमसा प्रथम दिवस करि बासू। दूसर गोमति तीर निवासू ॥
translation: माता की आज्ञा को सिर चढ़ाकर और उनके चरणों में सिर नवाकर दोनों भाई रथ पर चढ़कर चलने लगे। पहले दिन तमसा पर वास (मुकाम) करके दूसरा मुकाम गोमती के तीर पर किया ॥
english_translation: Bowing their heads to their mother's command and touching their heads to her feet, the two brothers set out in a chariot. They spent the first day at the Tamasa River and the second on the bank of the Gomati.
essence: Respect is proven by the way you move after you bow.
simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana obey their mother, bow to her feet, and begin their journey, stopping first at Tamasa and then at the Gomati bank.
insight: It shifts attention from emotional talk to embodied obedience and respectful follow-through.
modern_relevance: You finally make the hard call your family asked for, even though it costs you. The respect is not in the speech you gave, but in the steps you took.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पय अहार फल असन एक निसि भोजन एक लोग। करत राम हित नेम ब्रत परिहरि भूषन भोग ॥
translation: कोई दूध ही पीते, कोई फलाहार करते और कुछ लोग रात को एक ही बार भोजन करते हैं। भूषण और भोग-विलास को छोड़कर सब लोग श्री रामचन्द्रजी के लिए नियम और व्रत करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Some live on milk, some on fruit, some eat only once at night. Giving up ornaments and pleasures, they all keep vows and disciplines for Ram.
essence: Love for Ram shows itself as disciplined simplicity.
simple_meaning: People are changing their eating habits, clothes, and comforts to keep vows for Ram.
insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone into concrete habits, restraint, and self-discipline.
modern_relevance: You skip the dessert, turn off the music, and keep your promise anyway because someone you love is counting on you. That quiet discipline is a form of devotion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सई तीर बसि चले बिहाने। सृंगबेरपुर सब निअराने॥ समाचार सब सुने निषादा। हृदयँ बिचार करइ सबिषादा ॥
translation: रात भर सई नदी के तीर पर निवास करके सबेरे वहाँ से चल दिए और सब श्रृंगवेरपुर के समीप जा पहुँचे। निषादराज ने सब समाचार सुने, तो वह दुःखी होकर हृदय में विचार करने लगा- ॥
english_translation: After staying by the Sayi river through the night, they set out at dawn and came near Shrngverpur. Nishadraj heard all the news and, sorrowful, began to think deeply in his heart.
essence: News arrives first; the heart reacts before the mind knows why.
simple_meaning: After spending the night by the river, the party moved on at dawn and reached near Shrngverpur. Nishadraj heard the news and began worrying in sorrow.
insight: It shows how uncertainty can trigger sorrowful speculation before understanding arrives.
modern_relevance: You hear a rumor before sunrise that someone important is coming to your town, and your stomach tightens before you know why. That is Nishadraj's moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कारन कवन भरतु बन जाहीं। है कछु कपट भाउ मन माहीं॥ जौं पै जियँ न होति कुटिलाई। तौ कत लीन्ह संग कटकाई ॥
translation: क्या कारण है जो भरत वन को जा रहे हैं, मन में कुछ कपट भाव अवश्य है। यदि मन में कुटिलता न होती, तो साथ में सेना क्यों ले चले हैं ॥
english_translation: What reason could Bharat have for going to the forest? There must be some deceit in his heart. If there were no crookedness in him, why would he have brought an army along?
essence: A suspicious mind sees deceit even in ordinary movement.
simple_meaning: The speaker suspects Bharat's intentions because he is traveling to the forest with an army. A pure-hearted person would not need such a display.
insight: It shifts you from reacting to appearances toward examining the assumptions behind your judgment.
modern_relevance: You see someone arrive with two lawyers and a folder of printouts, and your mind fills in the worst. The verse shows how quickly suspicion turns gesture into proof.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जानहिं सानुज रामहि मारी। करउँ अकंटक राजु सुखारी॥ भरत न राजनीति उर आनी। तब कलंकु अब जीवन हानी ॥
translation: समझते हैं कि छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण सहित श्री राम को मारकर सुख से निष्कण्टक राज्य करूँगा। भरत ने हृदय में राजनीति को स्थान नहीं दिया (राजनीति का विचार नहीं किया)। तब (पहले) तो कलंक ही लगा था, अब तो जीवन से ही हाथ धोना पड़ेगा ॥
english_translation: They think Bharat wants to kill Ram and Lakshman to rule an unchallenged kingdom in comfort. Bharat never let such politics enter his heart; first that was a stain, and now it would cost him his life.
essence: Pure motives can still be crushed by suspicion.
simple_meaning: People suspect Bharat of wanting to kill Ram and Lakshman so he can rule without opposition. But Bharat never had such a thought; even the suspicion itself is a stain, and now it could ruin his life.
insight: It shifts the mind from judging by appearances to seeing how easily noble action gets misread.
modern_relevance: You volunteer to help, and someone still assumes you have an angle. The hurt is not just the accusation — it's that your good motive never even got a hearing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकल सुरासुर जुरहिं जुझारा। रामहि समर न जीतनिहारा॥ का आचरजु भरतु अस करहीं। नहिं बिष बेलि अमिअ फल फरहीं ॥
translation: सम्पूर्ण देवता और दैत्य वीर जुट जाएँ, तो भी श्री रामजी को रण में जीतने वाला कोई नहीं है। भरत जो ऐसा कर रहे हैं, इसमें आश्चर्य ही क्या है? विष की बेलें अमृतफल कभी नहीं फलतीं! ॥
english_translation: Even if all radiant beings and shadow beings came together as warriors, none could defeat Ram in battle. Why be surprised that Bharat acts this way? A vine of poison never bears the fruit of nectar.
essence: What you are rooted in will eventually show itself.
simple_meaning: No army can defeat Ram, so Bharat's noble conduct should not surprise anyone. Poisonous roots do not produce sweet fruit.
insight: It shifts attention from surface appearances to the moral source underneath them.
modern_relevance: When a family member keeps doubting your intentions, you can feel the sting of being misread. This verse reminds you that actions grow from character, not performance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस बिचारि गुहँ ग्याति सन कहेउ सजग सब होहु। हथवाँसहु बोरहु तरनि कीजिअ घाटारोहु ॥
translation: ऐसा विचारकर गुह (निषादराज) ने अपनी जाति वालों से कहा कि सब लोग सावधान हो जाओ। नावों को हाथ में (कब्जे में) कर लो और फिर उन्हें डुबा दो तथा सब घाटों को रोक दो ॥
english_translation: Thinking this, Guha told his companions to stay alert: seize the boats, sink them, and block every crossing place.
essence: Care can look like caution before trust is proven.
simple_meaning: Guha orders his people to stay alert, take control of the boats, sink them, and block the river crossings.
insight: It shows how vigilance works before certainty arrives: protect the vulnerable first, then sort out intentions.
modern_relevance: A security guard notices a crowd gathering near a closed gate and quietly locks the side entrances before anyone can rush in.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: होहु सँजोइल रोकहु घाटा। ठाटहु सकल मरै के ठाटा॥ सनमुख लोह भरत सन लेऊँ। जिअत न सुरसरि उतरन देऊँ ॥
translation: सुसज्जित होकर घाटों को रोक लो और सब लोग मरने के साज सजा लो (अर्थात भरत से युद्ध में लड़कर मरने के लिए तैयार हो जाओ)। मैं भरत से सामने (मैदान में) लोहा लूँगा (मुठभेड़ करूँगा) और जीते जी उन्हें गंगा पार न उतरने दूँगा ॥
english_translation: Get ready, block the crossings, and prepare yourselves for death. I will face Bharat head-on and never let him cross the Ganga alive.
essence: Protecting what you love can make you ready for battle before you know the truth.
simple_meaning: Guha orders his people to block the river crossings and be ready to fight Bharat if needed. He is determined not to let Bharat cross alive.
insight: It shows how fear and loyalty can push a person into defensive action before understanding the full situation.
modern_relevance: You see a rival team arrive with cameras and lawyers, and your whole crew stiffens. In one second, caution becomes a wall.
speaker: Guha

verse_text: समर मरनु पुनि सुरसरि तीरा। राम काजु छनभंगु सरीरा॥ भरत भाइ नृपु मैं जन नीचू। बड़ें भाग असि पाइअ मीचू ॥
translation: युद्ध में मरण, फिर गंगाजी का तट, श्री रामजी का काम और क्षणभंगुर शरीर (जो चाहे जब नाश हो जाए), भरत श्री रामजी के भाई और राजा (उनके हाथ से मरना) और मैं नीच सेवक- बड़े भाग्य से ऐसी मृत्यु मिलती है ॥
english_translation: Death in battle, then the bank of the Ganga, and Ram's work—this body is gone in a moment. Bharat is the king, and I am only a low servant; how blessed to receive such a death.
essence: A brief life becomes blessed when it is spent for Ram.
simple_meaning: Guh says he would gladly die fighting for Ram's work, especially with Bharat nearby. He sees the body as temporary and feels honored to die in such a cause.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to wholehearted loyalty in action.
modern_relevance: You step in to protect a friend at midnight, knowing you may get blamed. Something in you still says yes. That is the spirit here: service matters more than comfort or self-preservation.
speaker: Guh

verse_text: स्वामि काज करिहउँ रन रारी। जस धवलिहउँ भुवन दस चारी॥ तजउँ प्रान रघुनाथ निहोरें। दुहूँ हाथ मुद मोदक मोरें ॥
translation: मैं स्वामी के काम के लिए रण में लड़ाई करूँगा और चौदहों लोकों को अपने यश से उज्ज्वल कर दूँगा। श्री रघुनाथजी के निमित्त प्राण त्याग दूँगा। मेरे तो दोनों ही हाथों में आनंद के लड्डू हैं (अर्थात जीत गया तो राम सेवक का यश प्राप्त करूँगा और मारा गया तो श्री रामजी की नित्य सेवा प्राप्त करूँगा) ॥
english_translation: I will fight in battle for my master’s work and brighten the fourteen worlds with my fame. I will give up my life for Raghunath’s sake. For me, both hands already hold sweet reward.
essence: When your work is for Ram, both victory and death become gain.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he will fight for Ram's work, even if it costs his life. Whether he wins or dies, he sees only gain in serving Ram.
insight: It shifts effort from self-protection to wholehearted service, so success and sacrifice both feel meaningful.
modern_relevance: You take the harder shift, fix the mess, and no one may notice. Still, you know the work mattered because it was for something you love.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: साधु समाज न जाकर लेखा। राम भगत महुँ जासु न रेखा॥ जायँ जिअत जग सो महि भारू। जननी जौबन बिटप कुठारू ॥
translation: साधुओं के समाज में जिसकी गिनती नहीं और श्री रामजी के भक्तों में जिसका स्थान नहीं, वह जगत में पृथ्वी का भार होकर व्यर्थ ही जीता है। वह माता के यौवन रूपी वृक्ष के काटने के लिए कुल्हाड़ा मात्र है ॥
english_translation: One who has no place among the company of saints and no place among Ram's devotees lives in the world as a burden on the earth. Such a person is only an axe for cutting down the mother's tree of youth.
essence: A life outside devotion becomes a burden, not a blessing.
simple_meaning: A life that never joins the company of saints or Ram's devotees is called wasted. It does not uplift anyone; it only consumes what it was given.
insight: It shifts the mind from social success to spiritual belonging and service.
modern_relevance: You scroll through another week of being busy, but nothing in you feels aligned. This verse cuts through that drift: if your life never touches what is holy and loving, it starts to feel like mere occupancy.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: बिगत बिषाद निषादपति सबहि बढ़ाइ उछाहु। सुमिरि राम मागेउ तुरत तरकस धनुष सनाहु ॥
translation: (इस प्रकार श्री रामजी के लिए प्राण समर्पण का निश्चय करके) निषादराज विषाद से रहित हो गया और सबका उत्साह बढ़ाकर तथा श्री रामचन्द्रजी का स्मरण करके उसने तुरंत ही तरकस, धनुष और कवच माँगा ॥
english_translation: Freed from grief, the king of the Nishads lifted everyone's spirits. Remembering Ram, he immediately asked for his quiver, bow, and armor.
essence: Devotion clears grief and turns it into readiness.
simple_meaning: Nishadraj shakes off grief, encourages everyone around him, remembers Ram, and quickly asks for his bow, quiver, and armor.
insight: It shifts the mind from emotional collapse to prepared action.
modern_relevance: You get the message that changes everything, and suddenly the room stops feeling heavy. Before anyone else moves, you’re already gathering what you need.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बेगहु भाइहु सजहु सँजोऊ। सुनि रजाइ कदराइ न कोऊ॥ भलेहिं नाथ सब कहहिं सहरषा। एकहिं एक बढ़ावइ करषा ॥
translation: (उसने कहा-) हे भाइयों! जल्दी करो और सब सामान सजाओ। मेरी आज्ञा सुनकर कोई मन में कायरता न लावे। सब हर्ष के साथ बोल उठे- हे नाथ! बहुत अच्छा और आपस में एक-दूसरे का जोश बढ़ाने लगे ॥
english_translation: He said, “Brothers, hurry and get everything ready. Hearing my command, no one should feel fear. They all replied joyfully, “Very well, lord!” and kept lifting one another’s spirits.
essence: Courage spreads fastest when people begin moving together.
simple_meaning: Nishadraj urges his people to prepare quickly and not lose courage. They answer with joy and encourage each other.
insight: It shows how clear leadership and mutual encouragement keep a group from collapsing into hesitation.
modern_relevance: A team gets bad news before dawn, but someone starts assigning tasks calmly. The mood changes not because the problem vanished, but because one steady voice gave everyone a way forward.
speaker: Nishadraj

verse_text: चले निषाद जोहारि जोहारी। सूर सकल रन रूचइ रारी॥ सुमिरि राम पद पंकज पनहीं। भाथीं बाँधि चढ़ाइन्हि धनहीं ॥
translation: निषादराज को जोहार कर-करके सब निषाद चले। सभी बड़े शूरवीर हैं और संग्राम में लड़ना उन्हें बहुत अच्छा लगता है। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणकमलों की जूतियों का स्मरण करके उन्होंने भाथियाँ (छोटे-छोटे तरकस) बाँधकर धनुहियों (छोटे-छोटे धनुषों) पर प्रत्यंचा चढ़ाई ॥
english_translation: The Nishadas bowed to their leader and departed. They were all brave warriors who loved battle. Remembering the lotus feet of Shri Ramchandra, they fastened their quivers and fitted their bows.
essence: Bravery becomes noble when it is armed by remembrance.
simple_meaning: The Nishadas set out with respect, full of courage, remembering Ram as they prepared their weapons.
insight: It links action with remembrance, so courage stays clean instead of turning restless or proud.
modern_relevance: You gear up before a hard conversation, but first you steady yourself with what you respect most.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अँगरी पहिरि कूँड़ि सिर धरहीं। फरसा बाँस सेल सम करहीं॥ एक कुसल अति ओड़न खाँड़े। कूदहिं गगन मनहुँ छिति छाँड़े ॥
translation: कवच पहनकर सिर पर लोहे का टोप रखते हैं और फरसे, भाले तथा बरछों को सीधा कर रहे हैं (सुधार रहे हैं)। कोई तलवार के वार रोकने में अत्यन्त ही कुशल है। वे ऐसे उमंग में भरे हैं, मानो धरती छोड़कर आकाश में कूद (उछल) रहे हों ॥
english_translation: They put on armor and helmets, and set their axes, spears, and lances in order. Some are so skilled at blocking sword blows that they seem to leap into the sky, as if leaving the earth behind.
essence: Readiness itself can feel like flight.
simple_meaning: The warriors arm themselves, ready their weapons, and move with such energy that they seem to leap off the ground.
insight: It shifts attention from inner hesitation to outward readiness and decisive motion.
modern_relevance: You zip up your jacket, check your bag, and head out before dawn for a long day. The real shift has already happened: you’re no longer hesitating.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निज निज साजु समाजु बनाई। गुह राउतहि जोहारे जाई॥ देखि सुभट सब लायक जाने। लै लै नाम सकल सनमाने ॥
translation: अपना-अपना साज-समाज (लड़ाई का सामान और दल) बनाकर उन्होंने जाकर निषादराज गुह को जोहार की। निषादराज ने सुंदर योद्धाओं को देखकर, सबको सुयोग्य जाना और नाम ले-लेकर सबका सम्मान किया ॥
english_translation: They formed their own battle ranks and went to salute Guha the boatman. Seeing the noble warriors, Guha judged them worthy and honoured each one by name.
essence: True honour begins by seeing each person clearly.
simple_meaning: The warriors prepare themselves, greet Guha respectfully, and Guha welcomes them by recognizing each one’s worth.
insight: It teaches you to meet strength with recognition, not distance.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a new workplace, and the senior team member remembers everyone’s name before the meeting starts. That small respect changes the whole room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भाइहु लावहु धोख जनि आजु काज बड़ मोहि। सुनि सरोष बोले सुभट बीर अधीर न होहि ॥
translation: (उसने कहा-) हे भाइयों! धोखा न लाना (अर्थात मरने से न घबड़ाना), आज मेरा बड़ा भारी काम है। यह सुनकर सब योद्धा बड़े जोश के साथ बोल उठे- हे वीर! अधीर मत हो ॥
english_translation: He said, “Brothers, do not flinch today; I have a great task ahead.” Hearing this, the warriors replied with fierce enthusiasm, “Brave one, do not be impatient.”
essence: Clear resolve turns fear into readiness.
simple_meaning: A leader asks his companions not to hesitate or fear, because an important task must be done. The warriors answer with eager courage.
insight: It shows how confident speech can rally a group before a difficult task.
modern_relevance: Right before the presentation starts, one person says, “Don’t freeze now, we need this done.” The room straightens instantly. Clear urgency can steady everyone.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम प्रताप नाथ बल तोरे। करहिं कटकु बिनु भट बिनु घोरे॥ जीवन पाउ न पाछें धरहीं। रुंड मुंडमय मेदिनि करहीं ॥
translation: हे नाथ! श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्रताप से और आपके बल से हम लोग भरत की सेना को बिना वीर और बिना घोड़े की कर देंगे (एक-एक वीर और एक-एक घोड़े को मार डालेंगे)। जीते जी पीछे पाँव न रखेंगे। पृथ्वी को रुण्ड-मुण्डमयी कर देंगे (सिरों और धड़ों से छा देंगे) ॥
english_translation: By Ram's power and by your strength, we will destroy Bharata's army without warriors and without horses. We will not turn back while alive. We will turn the earth into a field of severed heads and bodies.
essence: Pride can turn devotion into a vow of destruction.
simple_meaning: The warriors boast that they will destroy the enemy army completely and never retreat alive.
insight: It captures the psychology of battle fever: loyalty, fear, and aggression fused into one loud promise.
modern_relevance: A group chat fills with chest-thumping bravado before a confrontation, and everyone sounds unstoppable until the real moment arrives.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: दीख निषादनाथ भल टोलू। कहेउ बजाउ जुझाऊ ढोलू॥ एतना कहत छींक भइ बाँए। कहेउ सगुनिअन्ह खेत सुहाए ॥
translation: निषादराज ने वीरों का बढ़िया दल देखकर कहा- जुझारू (लड़ाई का) ढोल बजाओ। इतना कहते ही बाईं ओर छींक हुई। शकुन विचारने वालों ने कहा कि खेत सुंदर हैं (जीत होगी) ॥
english_translation: Nishadraj saw the fine troop and said, "Beat the war drums." As he spoke, a sneeze came from the left. The omen-readers said, "The field is auspicious; victory is near."
essence: People under pressure turn small signs into certainty.
simple_meaning: Nishadraj sees his warriors and orders the war drums to be beaten. An omen appears, and the omen-readers take it as a sign of victory.
insight: It shows how fear and hope quickly turn random events into guidance.
modern_relevance: You are about to send a tense group message, and someone suddenly says, "That timing feels lucky." In moments like that, people cling to any sign that makes courage easier.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बूढ़ु एकु कह सगुन बिचारी। भरतहि मिलिअ न होइहि रारी॥ रामहि भरतु मनावन जाहीं। सगुन कहइ अस बिग्रहु नाहीं ॥
translation: एक बूढ़े ने शकुन विचारकर कहा- भरत से मिल लीजिए, उनसे लड़ाई नहीं होगी। भरत श्री रामचन्द्रजी को मनाने जा रहे हैं। शकुन ऐसा कह रहा है कि विरोध नहीं है ॥
english_translation: An old man, reading the signs, said, 'Meet Bharat; there will be no fight. Bharat is going to persuade Ram. The signs show no conflict.'
essence: Clear signs can reveal peace before fear does.
simple_meaning: An elder reads the signs and says there will be no conflict. Bharat is going to persuade Ram, not fight him.
insight: It teaches you to pause before assuming hostility and to read intentions more carefully.
modern_relevance: You see a tense family chat starting to spiral, but one calm voice reads the room correctly. What looked like a fight is really an attempt to make peace.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि गुह कहइ नीक कह बूढ़ा। सहसा करि पछिताहिं बिमूढ़ा॥ भरत सुभाउ सीलु बिनु बूझें। बड़ि हित हानि जानि बिनु जूझें ॥
translation: यह सुनकर निषादराज गुहने कहा- बूढ़ा ठीक कह रहा है। जल्दी में (बिना विचारे) कोई काम करके मूर्ख लोग पछताते हैं। भरतजी का शील स्वभाव बिना समझे और बिना जाने युद्ध करने में हित की बहुत बड़ी हानि है ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Guha said, “The old man speaks well. Rash actions make fools regret later. Without understanding Bharata’s nature and character, fighting him would bring great loss.”
essence: Rash action fades into regret when you ignore a person’s true character.
simple_meaning: Guha warns that acting in haste leads to regret. He says Bharata must be understood first, because attacking him without knowing his true nature would be a serious mistake.
insight: It shifts you from reactive suspicion to careful reading of another person’s character before acting.
modern_relevance: You read one angry message and almost fire back immediately. Then you pause, ask what the other person actually meant, and avoid making a small misunderstanding into a lasting rupture.
speaker: Guha

verse_text: गहहु घाट भट समिटि सब लेउँ मरम मिलि जाइ। बूझि मित्र अरि मध्य गति तस तब करिहउँ आइ ॥
translation: अतएव हे वीरों! तुम लोग इकट्ठे होकर सब घाटों को रोक लो, मैं जाकर भरतजी से मिलकर उनका भेद लेता हूँ। उनका भाव मित्र का है या शत्रु का या उदासीन का, यह जानकर तब आकर वैसा (उसी के अनुसार) प्रबंध करूँगा ॥
english_translation: Therefore, warriors, gather and block all the crossings. I will go meet Bharata and learn his true intent. Whether his heart is that of a friend, an enemy, or someone neutral, I will return and act accordingly.
essence: First understand another person's intent; then decide how to respond.
simple_meaning: The speaker tells his men to guard the crossings while he goes to meet Bharata and understand his true intention before deciding what to do.
insight: It shifts you from reactive defense to careful assessment before action.
modern_relevance: Before you answer a tense message or walk into a family argument, you pause, read the room, and find out what the other person actually means.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: लखब सनेहु सुभायँ सुहाएँ। बैरु प्रीति नहिं दुरइँ दुराएँ॥ अस कहि भेंट सँजोवन लागे। कंद मूल फल खग मृग मागे ॥
translation: उनके सुंदर स्वभाव से मैं उनके स्नेह को पहचान लूँगा। वैर और प्रेम छिपाने से नहीं छिपते। ऐसा कहकर वह भेंट का सामान सजाने लगा। उसने कंद, मूल, फल, पक्षी और हिरन मँगवाए ॥
english_translation: I will recognize his affection from his lovely nature. Enmity and love cannot stay hidden. Saying this, he began arranging gifts, asking for roots, fruits, birds, and deer.
essence: Love and hostility reveal themselves; your true nature cannot stay hidden.
simple_meaning: True feelings show themselves. Love and hostility cannot stay concealed for long. So he prepares gifts and gathers simple forest offerings for the meeting.
insight: It shifts attention from spoken claims to the deeper pattern a person's nature keeps showing.
modern_relevance: You meet someone after months of tension, and within two minutes you know whether the warmth is real. The face, the tone, the small gestures reveal what words try to hide.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: मीन पीन पाठीन पुराने। भरि भरि भार कहारन्ह आने॥ मिलन साजु सजि मिलन सिधाए। मंगल मूल सगुन सुभ पाए ॥
translation: कहार लोग पुरानी और मोटी पहिना नामक मछलियों के भार भर-भरकर लाए। भेंट का सामान सजाकर मिलने के लिए चले तो मंगलदायक शुभ-शकुन मिले ॥
english_translation: Porters brought loads of fish and other gifts. When they set out, arranging the meeting gifts, they found auspicious signs everywhere.
essence: Goodwill can turn a difficult meeting into an auspicious one.
simple_meaning: People bring gifts and set out to meet, and the journey is marked by good omens.
insight: It shifts attention from conflict to the goodwill carried into the meeting.
modern_relevance: You pack a small gift before visiting someone after a long misunderstanding. The awkwardness is still there, but the effort itself begins to soften the air.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि दूरि तें कहि निज नामू। कीन्ह मुनीसहि दंड प्रनामू॥ जानि रामप्रिय दीन्हि असीसा। भरतहि कहेउ बुझाइ मुनीसा ॥
translation: निषादराज ने मुनिराज वशिष्ठजी को देखकर अपना नाम बतलाकर दूर ही से दण्डवत प्रणाम किया। मुनीश्वर वशिष्ठजी ने उसको राम का प्यारा जानकर आशीर्वाद दिया और भरतजी को समझाकर कहा (कि यह श्री रामजी का मित्र है) ॥
english_translation: Seeing him from afar, he gave his own name and bowed with full prostration to the sage. Knowing him to be dear to Ram, the sage blessed him and explained to Bharat.
essence: Respect opens the door before familiarity does.
simple_meaning: Guha respectfully introduces himself to Vashishtha from a distance, bows fully, and receives a blessing once he is recognized as dear to Ram.
insight: It shows how recognition begins with respect, not status.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a family gathering and feel unsure how to approach. A respectful greeting and a little humility can dissolve distance faster than perfect words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम सखा सुनि संदनु त्यागा। चले उचरि उमगत अनुरागा॥ गाउँ जाति गुहँ नाउँ सुनाई। कीन्ह जोहारु माथ महि लाई ॥
translation: यह श्री राम का मित्र है, इतना सुनते ही भरतजी ने रथ त्याग दिया। वे रथ से उतरकर प्रेम में उमँगते हुए चले। निषादराज गुह ने अपना गाँव, जाति और नाम सुनाकर पृथ्वी पर माथा टेककर जोहार की ॥
english_translation: Hearing that this was Ram's friend, Bharat left the chariot. He climbed down and walked forward, overflowing with love. Guha announced his village, caste, and name, and bowed with his forehead to the ground.
essence: Love erases rank and makes reverence immediate.
simple_meaning: Bharat hears that Guha is Ram's friend and immediately steps out of his chariot. Guha responds with deep humility, naming himself and bowing fully to the ground.
insight: It shifts you from social rank to shared devotion, where recognition matters more than status.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a wedding, and the moment they mention your dearest friend's name, your whole posture changes. Formality drops. Warmth arrives first.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करत दंडवत देखि तेहि भरत लीन्ह उर लाइ। मनहुँ लखन सन भेंट भइ प्रेमु न हृदयँ समाइ ॥
translation: दण्डवत करते देखकर भरतजी ने उठाकर उसको छाती से लगा लिया। हृदय में प्रेम समाता नहीं है, मानो स्वयं लक्ष्मणजी से भेंट हो गई हो ॥
english_translation: Seeing him bow down, Bharat took him into his arms. Love would not fit in his heart, as if he had met Lakshman himself.
essence: Love recognises kinship before the world assigns roles.
simple_meaning: Bharat embraces Guha with such love that it feels like meeting Lakshman. The verse shows instant kinship, not social distance.
insight: It shifts the mind from rank and formality to shared humanity and immediate warmth.
modern_relevance: You meet someone in a tense family gathering and, instead of keeping distance, you pull them close. In that instant, respect becomes belonging.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भेंटत भरतु ताहि अति प्रीती। लोग सिहाहिं प्रेम कै रीती॥ धन्य धन्य धुनि मंगल मूला। सुर सराहि तेहि बरिसहिं फूला ॥
translation: भरतजी गुह को अत्यन्त प्रेम से गले लगा रहे हैं। प्रेम की रीति को सब लोग सिहा रहे हैं (ईर्षापूर्वक प्रशंसा कर रहे हैं)। मंगल की मूल 'धन्य-धन्य' की ध्वनि करके देवता उसकी सराहना करते हुए फूल बरसा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Bharat embraced Guha with deep love. Everyone praised the way of love. With cries of "Blessed, blessed," the heavens rejoiced and showered flowers.
essence: Love becomes visible when you greet without reserve.
simple_meaning: Bharat's embrace of Guha is so full of love that everyone sees it as a beautiful example of how love should look.
insight: It shifts the mind from social distance to wholehearted welcome.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who once stood outside your circle, and you greet them without coolness or calculation. That warmth changes the whole room before anyone says a word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लोक बेद सब भाँतिहिं नीचा। जासु छाँह छुइ लेइअ सींचा॥ तेहि भरि अंक राम लघु भ्राता। मिलत पुलक परिपूरित गाता ॥
translation: (वे कहते हैं-) जो लोक और वेद दोनों में सब प्रकार से नीचा माना जाता है, जिसकी छाया के छू जाने से भी स्नान करना होता है, उसी निषाद से अँकवार भरकर (हृदय से चिपटाकर) श्री रामचन्द्रजी के छोटे भाई भरतजी (आनंद और प्रेमवश) शरीर में पुलकावली से परिपूर्ण हो मिल रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: They say the Nishad is low in every way, by worldly custom and by the Vedas. Yet Bharat, the younger brother of Ram, fills him in his arms and meets him with his whole body thrilled.
essence: Real devotion does not see status; it sees whom to embrace.
simple_meaning: Bharat shows deep love by embracing the Nishad, even though society and scripture rank him low.
insight: It shifts you from social ranking to wholehearted recognition of another person.
modern_relevance: At a family gathering, everyone quietly skips over the cleaner who has been helping all evening. You walk straight up, thank him, and shake his hand like an equal.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम राम कहि जे जमुहाहीं। तिन्हहि न पाप पुंज समुहाहीं॥ यह तौ राम लाइ उर लीन्हा। कुल समेत जगु पावन कीन्हा ॥
translation: जो लोग राम-राम कहकर जँभाई लेते हैं (अर्थात आलस्य से भी जिनके मुँह से राम-नाम का उच्चारण हो जाता है), पापों के समूह (कोई भी पाप) उनके सामने नहीं आते। फिर इस गुह को तो स्वयं श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने हृदय से लगा लिया और कुल समेत इसे जगत्पावन (जगत को पवित्र करने वाला) बना दिया ॥
english_translation: Those who even say "Ram, Ram" while yawning are not met by a crowd of sins. And when Shri Ramchandra himself took Guha into his heart, he made him pure, along with his whole family and clan.
essence: Ram's name works even before your devotion feels complete.
simple_meaning: Even a casual utterance of Ram's name has power. Guha is not just welcomed; Ram embraces him and makes his whole family pure.
insight: It shifts the mind from measuring devotion by intensity to trusting the power of even a small remembrance.
modern_relevance: You mutter a prayer under your breath while rushing out the door, distracted and half-awake. Even that small turning toward Ram matters more than your self-criticism.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करमनास जलु सुरसरि परई। तेहि को कहहु सीस नहिं धरेई॥ उलटा नामु जपत जगु जाना। बालमीकि भए ब्रह्म समाना ॥
translation: कर्मनाशा नदी का जल गंगाजी में पड़ जाता है (मिल जाता है), तब कहिए, उसे कौन सिर पर धारण नहीं करता? जगत जानता है कि उलटा नाम (मरा-मरा) जपते-जपते वाल्मीकिजी ब्रह्म के समान हो गए ॥
english_translation: When the Karnali River water merges into the Ganga, who would not place it on their head? The world knows that by chanting the reversed name, 'mara-mara,' Valmiki became like Brahma.
essence: Even imperfect remembrance can turn you into something greater.
simple_meaning: A sacred name can transform even a reversed, imperfect chant into something holy. Valmiki became महान by repeating the name in reverse.
insight: It shifts attention from flawless practice to the transforming force of repeated remembrance.
modern_relevance: You mumble a prayer while driving, distracted and tired, and wonder if it counts. The verse says the power is not in your perfection; it is in the contact you make.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: स्वपच सबर खस जमन जड़ पावँर कोल किरात। रामु कहत पावन परम होत भुवन बिख्यात ॥
translation: मूर्ख और पामर चाण्डाल, शबर, खस, यवन, कोल और किरात भी राम-नाम कहते ही परम पवित्र और त्रिभुवन में विख्यात हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Even the lowest outcasts, hunters, forest-dwellers, and others become supremely pure and famed throughout the three worlds when they utter Ram’s name.
essence: Ram’s name makes the lowly radiant.
simple_meaning: No one is beyond Ram’s grace. Even people seen as low or impure become pure and honored when they speak his name.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to the cleansing power of remembrance.
modern_relevance: You catch yourself feeling ashamed after a mistake, then whisper Ram’s name in the car before walking back inside. The verse says your lowest hour is not your final identity.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: नहिं अचिरिजु जुग जुग चलि आई। केहि न दीन्हि रघुबीर बड़ाई॥ राम नाम महिमा सुर कहहीं। सुनि सुनि अवध लोग सुखु लहहीं ॥
