translation: इसमें कोई आश्चर्य नहीं है, युग-युगान्तर से यही रीति चली आ रही है। श्री रघुनाथजी ने किसको बड़ाई नहीं दी? इस प्रकार देवता राम नाम की महिमा कह रहे हैं और उसे सुन-सुनकर अयोध्या के लोग सुख पा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: There is nothing surprising in this; this has gone on age after age. Who has not been uplifted by Raghubir? The gods speak of Ram's greatness, and the people of Ayodhya keep finding comfort in hearing it again and again.
essence: Ram's name comforts because his greatness never stops being true.
simple_meaning: Ram's greatness is not new or rare; it has always been praised, and hearing his name brings comfort to people.
insight: It shifts attention from what is missing to the steady comfort of remembering Ram's name.
modern_relevance: You are exhausted after a hard week, and one voice you trust says, "You are not alone." The relief is immediate. Some words restore you before anything else changes.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामसखहि मिलि भरत सप्रेमा। पूँछी कुसल सुमंगल खेमा॥ देखि भरत कर सीलु सनेहू। भा निषाद तेहि समय बिदेहू ॥
translation: राम सखा निषादराज से प्रेम के साथ मिलकर भरतजी ने कुशल, मंगल और क्षेम पूछी। भरतजी का शील और प्रेम देखकर निषाद उस समय विदेह हो गया (प्रेममुग्ध होकर देह की सुध भूल गया) ॥
english_translation: Bharat met Nishadraj with love and asked after his well-being, welfare, and peace. Seeing Bharat's character and affection, Nishad was carried beyond body-consciousness in that moment.
essence: Love without pride makes another person forget themselves.
simple_meaning: Bharat greets Nishadraj with warmth and asks about his welfare. Nishad is so moved by Bharat's gentleness and affection that he forgets himself.
insight: It shifts attention from status to sincere regard, showing how respectful presence creates immediate trust.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who has helped your family, and instead of acting important, you ask about their life first. That simple respect can disarm years of distance in a moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकुच सनेहु मोदु मन बाढ़ा। भरतहि चितवत एकटक ठाढ़ा॥ धरि धीरजु पद बंदि बहोरी। बिनय सप्रेम करत कर जोरी ॥
translation: उसके मन में संकोच, प्रेम और आनंद इतना बढ़ गया कि वह खड़ा-खड़ा टकटकी लगाए भरतजी को देखता रहा। फिर धीरज धरकर भरतजी के चरणों की वंदना करके प्रेम के साथ हाथ जोड़कर विनती करने लगा- ॥
english_translation: Shyness, love, and joy rose so much in his mind that he stood there staring at Bharat without blinking. Then, gathering courage, he bowed at Bharat's feet and, with loving hands joined, began to speak humbly.
essence: Love and respect can leave you speechless before they make you bow.
simple_meaning: His heart overflows with shy love and joy at seeing Bharat. He steadies himself, bows to Bharat's feet, and speaks with folded hands.
insight: It shows how genuine reverence naturally becomes humility in action.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you deeply admire, and for a second you forget your words. Respect, gratitude, and affection all arrive at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कुसल मूल पद पंकज पेखी। मैं तिहुँ काल कुसल निज लेखी॥ अब प्रभु परम अनुग्रह तोरें। सहित कोटि कुल मंगल मोरें ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! कुशल के मूल आपके चरण कमलों के दर्शन कर मैंने तीनों कालों में अपना कुशल जान लिया। अब आपके परम अनुग्रह से करोड़ों कुलों (पीढ़ियों) सहित मेरा मंगल (कल्याण) हो गया ॥
english_translation: O Lord, seeing your lotus feet, the root of all good, I know myself blessed in all three times. Now, by your supreme grace, my welfare has spread to millions of generations.
essence: Ram's presence alone turns personal blessing into family-wide grace.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram's feet, Nishadraj feels that all his past, present, and future are blessed. He believes Ram's grace has turned his life and lineage toward good.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing security to receiving grace as the source of well-being.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence immediately settles your chest. No speech, no proof — just the quiet certainty that this moment is good and your life is larger now.
speaker: Nishadraj

verse_text: समुझि मोरि करतूति कुलु प्रभु महिमा जियँ जोइ। जो न भजइ रघुबीर पद जग बिधि बंचित सोइ ॥
translation: मेरी करतूत और कुल को समझकर और प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी की महिमा को मन में देख (विचार) कर (अर्थात कहाँ तो मैं नीच जाति और नीच कर्म करने वाला जीव, और कहाँ अनन्तकोटि ब्रह्माण्डों के स्वामी भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी! पर उन्होंने मुझ जैसे नीच को भी अपनी अहैतुकी कृपा वश अपना लिया- यह समझकर) जो रघुवीर श्री रामजी के चरणों का भजन नहीं करता, वह जगत में विधाता के द्वारा ठगा गया है ॥
english_translation: Considering my conduct and my lineage, and reflecting in your heart on the glory of Lord Ram, whoever does not worship Raghubir's feet is cheated in this world by fate.
essence: Ignoring Ram is the real loss, not your own smallness.
simple_meaning: Bharat says that when he remembers his own lowliness and Ram's greatness, anyone who does not worship Ram is truly cheated in life.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-judgment to grateful devotion.
modern_relevance: You compare your messy life to someone else's steadiness and feel small. Then you remember who has carried you, forgiven you, and stayed close anyway — and gratitude becomes the only honest response.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कपटी कायर कुमति कुजाती। लोक बेद बाहेर सब भाँती॥ राम कीन्ह आपन जबही तें। भयउँ भुवन भूषन तबही तें ॥
translation: मैं कपटी, कायर, कुबुद्धि और कुजाति हूँ और लोक-वेद दोनों से सब प्रकार से बाहर हूँ। पर जब से श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने मुझे अपनाया है, तभी से मैं विश्व का भूषण हो गया ॥
english_translation: I am deceitful, cowardly, of confused judgment, and of low birth, outside both social order and scripture in every way. But from the moment Lord Ram accepted me as his own, I became an ornament of the world.
essence: Ram's acceptance turns an outcast into an ornament of the world.
simple_meaning: Nishad calls himself unworthy by every worldly standard, then says Ram's acceptance alone made him honored.
insight: It shifts identity from self-judgment to received belonging.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room feeling like the least polished person there, already rehearsing your apology. Then someone you respect treats you like you belong, and your whole posture changes.
speaker: Nishad

verse_text: देखि प्रीति सुनि बिनय सुहाई। मिलेउ बहोरि भरत लघु भाई॥ कहि निषाद निज नाम सुबानीं। सादर सकल जोहारीं रानीं ॥
translation: निषाद राज की प्रीति को देखकर और सुंदर विनय सुनकर फिर भरतजी के छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्नजी उससे मिले। फिर निषाद ने अपना नाम ले-लेकर सुंदर (नम्र और मधुर) वाणी से सब रानियों को आदरपूर्वक जोहार की ॥
english_translation: Seeing his affection and hearing his lovely humility, Bharat's younger brother met him again. Then Nishad spoke his own name in gentle words and respectfully greeted all the queens.
essence: Respect makes strangers feel like family.
simple_meaning: Nishad's warm respect moves Bharat's brother to meet him again, and Nishad greets the queens politely by name.
insight: It shows how sincere humility creates immediate trust and dissolves social distance.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a family gathering who could easily ignore you, but they look you in the eye, remember your name, and make you feel included.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जानि लखन सम देहिं असीसा। जिअहु सुखी सय लाख बरीसा॥ निरखि निषादु नगर नर नारी। भए सुखी जनु लखनु निहारी ॥
translation: रानियाँ उसे लक्ष्मणजी के समान समझकर आशीर्वाद देती हैं कि तुम सौ लाख वर्षों तक सुख पूर्वक जिओ। नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष निषाद को देखकर ऐसे सुखी हुए, मानो लक्ष्मणजी को देख रहे हों ॥
english_translation: Thinking him to be like Lakshman, the queens bless him: "May you live happily for a hundred million years." Seeing Nishad, the men and women of the city became happy, as if they were seeing Lakshman himself.
essence: True goodness is recognized as kin before words are spoken.
simple_meaning: The queens bless Nishad as if he were Lakshman, and the city’s people feel joy on seeing him. His presence is received like a beloved friend’s.
insight: It shows how devotion and goodwill can make social distance disappear instantly.
modern_relevance: You walk into a house where everyone is tense, and one person greets you with such warmth that the whole room softens. That is the kind of welcome this verse holds.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहहिं लहेउ एहिं जीवन लाहू। भेंटेउ रामभद्र भरि बाहू॥ सुनि निषादु निज भाग बड़ाई। प्रमुदित मन लइ चलेउ लेवाई ॥
translation: सब कहते हैं कि जीवन का लाभ तो इसी ने पाया है, जिसे कल्याण स्वरूप श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने भुजाओं में बाँधकर गले लगाया है। निषाद अपने भाग्य की बड़ाई सुनकर मन में परम आनंदित हो सबको अपने साथ लिवा ले चला ॥
english_translation: Everyone says he has gained the true benefit of life, the one whom the благest Ramchandra has embraced in his arms. Hearing his own good fortune praised, Nishad became deeply joyful and led everyone along with him.
essence: Being embraced by Ram is the greatest gain of all.
simple_meaning: People see Nishad as blessed because Ram has embraced him. Hearing this, Nishad feels joyful and goes to bring the others along.
insight: It shifts value from status or achievement to being received with love.
modern_relevance: Someone introduces you at a gathering by the one moment that made your year — the person you admire remembered your name. That recognition can feel like a whole life being affirmed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सनकारे सेवक सकल चले स्वामि रुख पाइ। घर तरु तर सर बाग बन बास बनाएन्हि जाइ ॥
translation: उसने अपने सब सेवकों को इशारे से कह दिया। वे स्वामी का रुख पाकर चले और उन्होंने घरों में, वृक्षों के नीचे, तालाबों पर तथा बगीचों और जंगलों में ठहरने के लिए स्थान बना दिए ॥
english_translation: He signaled all his servants. Understanding their master's intention, they went and arranged places to stay in houses, under trees, by ponds, and in gardens and forests.
essence: Shared purpose turns many hands into one movement.
simple_meaning: The servants understood their leader’s intention and quickly arranged rest places everywhere along the route.
insight: It shows how clear intention can organize a whole group into calm, practical action.
modern_relevance: You’re coordinating a late-night arrival for someone important, and everyone just knows what to do. No speeches, no chaos — only shared purpose and quiet readiness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सृंगबेरपुर भरत दीख जब। भे सनेहँ सब अंग सिथिल तब॥ सोहत दिएँ निषादहि लागू। जनु तनु धरें बिनय अनुरागू ॥
translation: भरतजी ने जब श्रृंगवेरपुर को देखा, तब उनके सब अंग प्रेम के कारण शिथिल हो गए। वे निषाद को लाग दिए (अर्थात उसके कंधे पर हाथ रखे चलते हुए) ऐसे शोभा दे रहे हैं, मानो विनय और प्रेम शरीर धारण किए हुए हों ॥
english_translation: When Bharat saw Srngverpur, all his limbs grew soft with love. Leaning on Nishad’s shoulder, he shone like humility and affection taking bodily form.
essence: Love can make humility visible in the body.
simple_meaning: Bharat becomes physically softened by love when he sees Srngverpur, and his closeness to Nishad makes him look like humility and affection embodied.
insight: It shifts devotion from an idea into a bodily change: love becomes visible in posture, touch, and ease.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a place that reminds you of someone you love, and your whole body loosens. The guard drops, your voice softens, and even your posture begins to show what your heart feels.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि बिधि भरत सेनु सबु संगा। दीखि जाइ जग पावनि गंगा॥ रामघाट कहँ कीन्ह प्रनामू। भा मनु मगनु मिले जनु रामू ॥
translation: इस प्रकार भरतजी ने सब सेना को साथ में लिए हुए जगत को पवित्र करने वाली गंगाजी के दर्शन किए। श्री रामघाट को (जहाँ श्री रामजी ने स्नान संध्या की थी) प्रणाम किया। उनका मन इतना आनंदमग्न हो गया, मानो उन्हें स्वयं श्री रामजी मिल गए हों ॥
english_translation: In this way Bharat, traveling with the whole army, saw the purifying Ganga. He bowed to Ramghat, and his mind became so absorbed in joy that it was as if he had met Ram himself.
essence: Love can make a place feel like meeting Ram again.
simple_meaning: Bharat reaches the holy Ganga, bows at Ramghat, and feels such joy that it seems like meeting Ram himself.
insight: It shifts reverence from ritual gesture to living remembrance.
modern_relevance: You step off a train at a river town after years away, and one familiar ghat, one old prayer place, brings back someone you miss completely. The place feels like meeting them again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करहिं प्रनाम नगर नर नारी। मुदित ब्रह्ममय बारि निहारी॥ करि मज्जनु मागहिं कर जोरी। रामचन्द्र पद प्रीति न थोरी ॥
translation: नगर के नर-नारी प्रणाम कर रहे हैं और गंगाजी के ब्रह्म रूप जल को देख-देखकर आनंदित हो रहे हैं। गंगाजी में स्नान कर हाथ जोड़कर सब यही वर माँगते हैं कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में हमारा प्रेम कम न हो (अर्थात बहुत अधिक हो) ॥
english_translation: The men and women of the city bowed with joy at the sight of the Brahman-like waters. After bathing, they joined their hands and asked for one boon: that their love for Ramchandra's feet never grow less.
essence: Seeing holiness makes you ask for more love, not more things.
simple_meaning: The people of the city bow with joy at the holy water, bathe, and ask for one thing: more love for Ram's feet.
insight: It shifts desire from worldly gain to deeper devotion.
modern_relevance: You step into a temple after a long, messy week and suddenly your requests feel smaller. What you want most is not a better deal — just a softer, steadier love for what is sacred.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत कहेउ सुरसरि तव रेनू। सकल सुखद सेवक सुरधेनू॥ जोरि पानि बर मागउँ एहू। सीय राम पद सहज सनेहू ॥
translation: भरतजी ने कहा- हे गंगे! आपकी रज सबको सुख देने वाली तथा सेवक के लिए तो कामधेनु ही है। मैं हाथ जोड़कर यही वरदान माँगता हूँ कि श्री सीता-रामजी के चरणों में मेरा स्वाभाविक प्रेम हो ॥
english_translation: Bharat said, “O sacred river, your dust gives every kind of joy and is like the wish-fulfilling cow for a servant. With folded hands, I ask only this boon: natural love for the feet of Sita and Ram.”
essence: The highest boon is effortless love for Ram.
simple_meaning: Bharat treats the sacred river as a source of blessing and asks for one thing only: a natural, effortless love for Sita and Ram.
insight: It shifts desire away from outcomes and toward a relationship that can be lived with sincerity.
modern_relevance: You stand in a temple, a hospital corridor, or beside a parent you cannot fix. Instead of asking for control, you ask for a heart that can love cleanly and without strain.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: एहि बिधि मज्जनु भरतु करि गुर अनुसासन पाइ। मातु नहानीं जानि सब डेरा चले लवाइ ॥
translation: इस प्रकार भरतजी स्नान कर और गुरुजी की आज्ञा पाकर तथा यह जानकर कि सब माताएँ स्नान कर चुकी हैं, डेरा उठा ले चले ॥
english_translation: In this way, Bharata bathed, received the guru's instruction, and knowing that all the mothers had bathed, he had the camp moved on.
essence: True devotion also remembers the people around you.
simple_meaning: Bharata completes his bath, follows his teacher's guidance, checks on the mothers, and then moves the camp forward.
insight: It shows a leader whose devotion expresses itself as careful, practical attention to others.
modern_relevance: You finish your morning duties, check that everyone in the house is ready, and only then leave. Small care, done quietly, keeps a difficult day from fraying.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ तहँ लोगन्ह डेरा कीन्हा। भरत सोधु सबही कर लीन्हा॥ सुर सेवा करि आयसु पाई। राम मातु पहिं गे दोउ भाई ॥
translation: लोगों ने जहाँ-तहाँ डेरा डाल दिया। भरतजी ने सभी का पता लगाया (कि सब लोग आकर आराम से टिक गए हैं या नहीं)। फिर देव पूजन करके आज्ञा पाकर दोनों भाई श्री रामचन्द्रजी की माता कौसल्याजी के पास गए ॥
english_translation: People pitched their tents here and there. Bharat checked on everyone. After worshiping the radiant beings and receiving permission, the two brothers went to Ram's mother.
essence: Devotion here looks like careful, humble order.
simple_meaning: The group settles in camp, Bharat makes sure everyone is accounted for, and then he and his brother go to Ram's mother after worship and permission.
insight: It shifts attention from grand emotion to quiet responsibility and respectful sequence.
modern_relevance: After a long family trip, you count heads before leaving the parking lot, make sure no one is left behind, and only then walk inside together. Care looks like that.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चरन चाँपि कहि कहि मृदु बानी। जननीं सकल भरत सनमानी॥ भाइहि सौंपि मातु सेवकाई। आपु निषादहि लीन्ह बोलाई ॥
translation: चरण दबाकर और कोमल वचन कह-कहकर भरतजी ने सब माताओं का सत्कार किया। फिर भाई शत्रुघ्न को माताओं की सेवा सौंपकर आपने निषाद को बुला लिया ॥
english_translation: Touching their feet and speaking softly again and again, Bharat honoured all the mothers. Then he entrusted the mothers' service to his brother Shatrughna and called the Nishad chief to him.
essence: True respect is shown by quietly taking care of everyone present.
simple_meaning: Bharat shows respect to the mothers, assigns Shatrughna to care for them, and calls the Nishad chief to him.
insight: It shifts attention from status to service, showing that dignity is proved by how you care for others.
modern_relevance: At a family gathering after a funeral, you notice the elders sitting alone and quietly make sure someone stays with them. That small act reveals character more than any speech.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चले सखा कर सों कर जोरें। सिथिल सरीरु सनेह न थोरें॥ पूँछत सखहि सो ठाउँ देखाऊ। नेकु नयन मन जरनि जुड़ाऊ ॥
translation: सखा निषाद राज के हाथ से हाथ मिलाए हुए भरतजी चले। प्रेम कुछ थोड़ा नहीं है (अर्थात बहुत अधिक प्रेम है), जिससे उनका शरीर शिथिल हो रहा है। भरतजी सखा से पूछते हैं कि मुझे वह स्थान दिखलाओ और नेत्र और मन की जलन कुछ ठंडी करो- ॥
english_translation: Holding Nishad Raja's hand, Bharat walked on. His body was weak from love, and his love was boundless. He asked his friend to show him that place and cool the burning in his eyes and mind.
essence: Longing for Ram makes even the body tremble.
simple_meaning: Bharat walks with Nishad Raja, overwhelmed by love. He asks to be shown the place where Ram rested so his burning heart can be soothed.
insight: It shows how devotion can become physical longing, turning memory and place into a way of staying connected.
modern_relevance: You finally arrive at the hospital room after the emergency call. The bed is empty now, but you still want to stand where they stood, just to feel close again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ सिय रामु लखनु निसि सोए। कहत भरे जल लोचन कोए॥ भरत बचन सुनि भयउ बिषादू। तुरत तहाँ लइ गयउ निषादू ॥
translation: जहाँ सीताजी, श्री रामजी और लक्ष्मण रात को सोए थे। ऐसा कहते ही उनके नेत्रों के कोयों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया। भरतजी के वचन सुनकर निषाद को बड़ा विषाद हुआ। वह तुरंत ही उन्हें वहाँ ले गया ॥
english_translation: Where Sita, Ram, and Lakshman had slept through the night, his eyes filled with tears. Hearing Bharat's words, Nishad felt deep sorrow and quickly took him there.
essence: A loved place can still bring tears after everyone has gone.
simple_meaning: Bharat is shown the place where Ram, Sita, and Lakshman slept. The memory moves everyone there into tears and sorrow.
insight: It shifts attention from the scene itself to the devotion memory leaves behind.
modern_relevance: You return to an empty room after someone you love has left it. The bed is made, but the ache remains. Even silence can carry a presence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ सिंसुपा पुनीत तर रघुबर किय बिश्रामु। अति सनेहँ सादर भरत कीन्हेउ दंड प्रनामु ॥
translation: जहाँ पवित्र अशोक के वृक्ष के नीचे श्री रामजी ने विश्राम किया था। भरतजी ने वहाँ अत्यन्त प्रेम से आदरपूर्वक दण्डवत प्रणाम किया ॥
english_translation: At the sacred tree where Raghubar rested, Bharat bowed down in full prostration with deep love and respect.
essence: Love bows even before a place touched by the beloved.
simple_meaning: Bharat bowed fully at the place where Ram had rested, showing deep love and reverence.
insight: It shows how devotion turns ordinary places into reminders of love and absence.
modern_relevance: You stand in an empty room after someone you love has left, and the silence itself feels charged. Even their chair, their cup, their trace on the floor becomes something you want to honor.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कुस साँथरी निहारि सुहाई। कीन्ह प्रनामु प्रदच्छिन जाई॥ चरन देख रज आँखिन्ह लाई। बनइ न कहत प्रीति अधिकाई ॥
translation: कुशों की सुंदर साथरी देखकर उसकी प्रदक्षिणा करके प्रणाम किया। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरण चिह्नों की रज आँखों में लगाई। (उस समय के) प्रेम की अधिकता कहते नहीं बनती ॥
english_translation: Seeing the lovely grass bed, he bowed and circled it in reverence. He placed the dust of Ram's feet on his eyes. The depth of that love could not be spoken.
essence: Deep love turns even a patch of ground into a shrine.
simple_meaning: Bharat bows to the place where Ram rested and honors even the grass there as precious. His love is so deep that words cannot contain it.
insight: It trains the mind to honor signs, places, and reminders as carriers of relationship, not as ordinary objects.
modern_relevance: You find a crumpled note, a worn scarf, or an empty chair that still feels alive with someone's presence. Love can make the smallest trace unbearable and holy at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कनक बिंदु दुइ चारिक देखे। राखे सीस सीय सम लेखे॥ सजल बिलोचन हृदयँ गलानी। कहत सखा सन बचन सुबानी ॥
translation: भरतजी ने दो-चार स्वर्णबिन्दु (सोने के कण या तारे आदि जो सीताजी के गहने-कपड़ों से गिर पड़े थे) देखे तो उनको सीताजी के समान समझकर सिर पर रख लिया। उनके नेत्र (प्रेमाश्रु के) जल से भरे हैं और हृदय में ग्लानि भरी है। वे सखा से सुंदर वाणी में ये वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: Seeing two or four golden specks, Bharata placed them on his head, taking them as if they were Sita herself. His eyes were wet with tears, his heart full of remorse, and he spoke to his companion with beautiful words.
essence: Even a trace of the beloved can fill you with longing.
simple_meaning: Bharata finds a few golden specks and reveres them as if they were Sita herself. He is weeping, ashamed, and speaking gently to his companion.
insight: It trains attention to treat traces of the beloved with reverence, not possession.
modern_relevance: You find a scarf, a note, or a broken bracelet that belonged to someone you miss. Your hands go still before your heart does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: श्रीहत सीय बिरहँ दुतिहीना। जथा अवध नर नारि बिलीना॥ पिता जनक देउँ पटतर केही। करतल भोगु जोगु जग जेही ॥
translation: ये स्वर्ण के कण या तारे भी सीताजी के विरह से ऐसे श्रीहत (शोभाहीन) एवं कान्तिहीन हो रहे हैं, जैसे (राम वियोग में) अयोध्या के नर-नारी विलीन (शोक के कारण क्षीण) हो रहे हैं। जिन सीताजी के पिता राजा जनक हैं, इस जगत में भोग और योग दोनों ही जिनकी मुट्ठी में हैं, उन जनकजी को मैं किसकी उपमा दूँ? ॥
english_translation: These golden specks, dimmed by separation from Sita, look like Ayodhya's men and women, drained by grief for Ram. What comparison can I make for King Janaka, whose hands hold both enjoyment and yoga, and whose worth is beyond measure?
essence: Separation makes even the brightest things feel dim.
simple_meaning: Bharat says that even these golden specks have lost their shine in Sita's absence, just as Ayodhya has been dimmed by grief for Ram. He then says Janak is beyond comparison.
insight: It teaches you how love and loss reshape perception, making even neutral objects carry emotional charge.
modern_relevance: You open a drawer and find a small thing they once touched. It should feel ordinary, but it suddenly carries the weight of absence and makes the whole room feel different.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: ससुर भानुकुल भानु भुआलू। जेहि सिहात अमरावतिपालू॥ प्राननाथु रघुनाथ गोसाईं। जो बड़ होत सो राम बड़ाईं ॥
translation: सूर्यकुल के सूर्य राजा दशरथजी जिनके ससुर हैं, जिनको अमरावती के स्वामी इन्द्र भी सिहाते थे। (ईर्षापूर्वक उनके जैसा ऐश्वर्य और प्रताप पाना चाहते थे) और प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी जिनके प्राणनाथ हैं, जो इतने बड़े हैं कि जो कोई भी बड़ा होता है, वह श्री रामचन्द्रजी की (दी हुई) बड़ाई से ही होता है ॥
english_translation: King Dasharath, the sun of the solar dynasty, was so glorious that even Indra envied him. Yet Ram, his lord of life, is the one whose greatness makes all greatness shine.
essence: Every crown still rests beneath Ram's greater glory.
simple_meaning: Dasharath was so great that even Indra envied him, but Ram is greater still. Any greatness a person has comes through Ram's blessing.
insight: It shifts attention from personal achievement to the source that makes achievement possible.
modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the applause, the title — and then one quiet moment reminds you it all came through forces beyond your control. This verse keeps the ego from hardening.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पति देवता सुतीय मनि सीय साँथरी देखि। बिहरत हृदउ न हहरि हर पबि तें कठिन बिसेषि ॥
translation: उन श्रेष्ठ पतिव्रता स्त्रियों में शिरोमणि सीताजी की साथरी (कुश शय्या) देखकर मेरा हृदय हहराकर (दहलकर) फट नहीं जाता, हे शंकर! यह वज्र से भी अधिक कठोर है! ॥
english_translation: Seeing Sita's grass bed, the jewel among devoted wives, my heart does not burst. Shiva, this is harder than a thunderbolt.
essence: Tender suffering can feel harder than any blow.
simple_meaning: Seeing Sita lying on a bed of grass, the speaker is overwhelmed by how unbearably harsh her suffering is.
insight: It trains the mind to notice suffering directly instead of looking away or numbing it.
modern_relevance: You walk past a child sleeping on a thin mat in a crowded station and feel your chest tighten. Some scenes do not ask for explanation; they ask you to feel the weight of them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लालन जोगु लखन लघु लोने। भे न भाइ अस अहहिं न होने॥ पुरजन प्रिय पितु मातु दुलारे। सिय रघुबीरहि प्रानपिआरे ॥
translation: मेरे छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण बहुत ही सुंदर और प्यार करने योग्य हैं। ऐसे भाई न तो किसी के हुए, न हैं, न होने के ही हैं। जो लक्ष्मण अवध के लोगों को प्यारे, माता-पिता के दुलारे और श्री सीता-रामजी के प्राण प्यारे हैं, ॥
english_translation: My dear younger brother Lakshman is so lovely and worthy of love. No brother like him has ever been, is now, or will ever be. He is beloved by the people of Ayodhya, cherished by his parents, and dear as life to Sita and Ram.
essence: True loveliness is being dear to everyone without needing to announce yourself.
simple_meaning: Lakshman is described as the kind of brother everyone loves — by the people, by his parents, and by Sita and Ram themselves.
insight: It shifts attention from status to character: being cherished comes from how you live, not from what you claim.
modern_relevance: At a family gathering, one person quietly helps with the food, checks on the elders, and makes the children laugh. Nobody has to ask. That is the kind of presence this verse honors.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मृदु मूरति सुकुमार सुभाऊ। तात बाउ तन लाग न काउ॥ ते बन सहहिं बिपति सब भाँती। निदरे कोटि कुलिस एहिं छाती ॥
translation: जिनकी कोमल मूर्ति और सुकुमार स्वभाव है, जिनके शरीर में कभी गरम हवा भी नहीं लगी, वे वन में सब प्रकार की विपत्तियाँ सह रहे हैं। (हाय!) इस मेरी छाती ने (कठोरता में) करोड़ों वज्रों का भी निरादर कर दिया (नहीं तो यह कभी की फट गई होती) ॥
english_translation: Those who are tender in form and gentle by nature are enduring every hardship in the forest. My heart has become so hard that it has not shattered even under millions of thunderbolts.
essence: Tenderness and hardship should never have met like this.
simple_meaning: Beautiful, delicate people are bearing the forest's pain, while the speaker feels his own heart has turned harder than thunderbolts.
insight: It captures the ache of witnessing innocent suffering and the numbness grief can create.
modern_relevance: You watch someone kind and unprotected keep carrying a burden they never deserved. Your chest tightens because their softness makes the hardship feel unbearable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम जनमि जगु कीन्ह उजागर। रूप सील सुख सब गुन सागर॥ पुरजन परिजन गुरु पितु माता। राम सुभाउ सबहि सुखदाता ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी ने जन्म (अवतार) लेकर जगत् को प्रकाशित (परम सुशोभित) कर दिया। वे रूप, शील, सुख और समस्त गुणों के समुद्र हैं। पुरवासी, कुटुम्बी, गुरु, पिता-माता सभी को श्री रामजी का स्वभाव सुख देने वाला है ॥
english_translation: By being born, Ram made the world radiant. He is an ocean of beauty, character, joy, and every virtue. For the people of the city, his relatives, the teacher, father, and mother, Ram's nature gives delight to all.
essence: Ram's presence itself is a gift to everyone around him.
simple_meaning: Ram's birth makes the world shine. His beauty, character, joy, and virtues delight everyone around him.
insight: It shifts attention from achievement to character: the highest presence is the one that quietly blesses others.
modern_relevance: A quiet person walks into a tense family gathering, and the room softens before anyone speaks. Some people don't need to announce their goodness — their presence itself changes the atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बैरिउ राम बड़ाई करहीं। बोलनि मिलनि बिनय मन हरहीं॥ सारद कोटि कोटि सत सेषा। करि न सकहिं प्रभु गुन गन लेखा ॥
translation: शत्रु भी श्री रामजी की बड़ाई करते हैं। बोल-चाल, मिलने के ढंग और विनय से वे मन को हर लेते हैं। करोड़ों सरस्वती और अरबों शेषजी भी प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी के गुण समूहों की गिनती नहीं कर सकते ॥
english_translation: Even enemies praise Ram. His speech, meeting, and humility captivate the heart. Crores of Saraswati and Shesh cannot count the host of Lord Ram's virtues.
essence: Ram’s humility is so complete that even enemies are moved by it.
simple_meaning: Ram's character is so graceful that even enemies admire him. His speech, manners, and humility win hearts, and no one can fully count his virtues.
insight: It shifts attention from proving yourself to embodying qualities that naturally earn trust and admiration.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense family gathering, and the person everyone expected to argue simply listens well, speaks gently, and lowers the temperature in the room. That kind of presence changes people before any explanation does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुखस्वरूप रघुबंसमनि मंगल मोद निधान। ते सोवत कुस डासि महि बिधि गति अति बलवान ॥
translation: जो सुख स्वरूप रघुवंश शिरोमणि श्री रामचंद्रजी मंगल और आनंद के भंडार हैं, वे पृथ्वी पर कुशा बिछाकर सोते हैं। विधाता की गति बड़ी ही बलवान है ॥
english_translation: The joy-filled jewel of Raghu's line, the source of auspiciousness and delight, lies on kusa grass on the ground. Such is the mighty course of fate.
essence: Even the beloved can be made to sleep on the ground.
simple_meaning: Ram, the source of joy and blessing, is sleeping on kusa grass on the ground. The poet points to how powerful fate can be.
insight: It trains the mind to see how quickly status, comfort, and security can be stripped away.
modern_relevance: You watch someone who should have been protected sleeping on a hard floor after everything has fallen apart. The image lands because it feels unfair, and because life can change that fast.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: राम सुना दुखु कान न काऊ। जीवनतरु जिमि जोगवइ राउ॥ पलक नयन फनि मनि जेहि भाँती। जोगवहिं जननि सकल दिन राती ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी ने कानों से भी कभी दुःख का नाम नहीं सुना। महाराज स्वयं जीवन वृक्ष की तरह उनकी सार-सँभाल किया करते थे। सब माताएँ भी रात-दिन उनकी ऐसी सार-सँभाल करती थीं, जैसे पलक नेत्रों और साँप अपनी मणि की करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram had never even heard the word sorrow. The king cared for him like a tree of life. All the mothers protected him day and night like an eyelid guards the eye and a snake guards its jewel.
essence: Leaving home means losing the world that held you without effort.
simple_meaning: Ram grew up so protected and cherished that sorrow had never touched him. Dasharath and the queens guarded him constantly, with the same instinctive care as an eyelid protects an eye.
insight: It frames exile as a rupture from total protection, not just a change of place.
modern_relevance: You remember the house where every small need was anticipated before you asked. Leaving that kind of care behind is not just travel — it is heartbreak.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ते अब फिरत बिपिन पदचारी। कंद मूल फल फूल अहारी॥ धिग कैकई अमंगल मूला। भइसि प्रान प्रियतम प्रतिकूला ॥
translation: वही श्री रामचंद्रजी अब जंगलों में पैदल फिरते हैं और कंद-मूल तथा फल-फूलों का भोजन करते हैं। अमंगल की मूल कैकेयी धिक्कार है, जो अपने प्राणप्रियतम पति से भी प्रतिकूल हो गई ॥
english_translation: Now Ram wanders on foot through the forest, living on roots, fruits, and flowers. Shame on Kaikeyi, the root of all inauspiciousness, who turned against her own beloved husband.
essence: Exile begins when loyalty turns against love.
simple_meaning: Ram is now walking through the forest and eating simple forest food because Kaikeyi's actions turned him away from home and into exile.
insight: It shifts attention from the journey itself to the human cost of broken loyalty.
modern_relevance: You pack a small bag and leave the house after one argument that changes everything. The room is still standing, but the life you knew is not. This verse carries that ache of irreversible fracture.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मैं धिग धिग अघ उदधि अभागी। सबु उतपातु भयउ जेहि लागी॥ कुल कलंकु करि सृजेउ बिधाताँ। साइँदोह मोहि कीन्ह कुमाताँ ॥
translation: मुझे पापों के समुद्र और अभागे को धिक्कार है, धिक्कार है, जिसके कारण ये सब उत्पात हुए। विधाता ने मुझे कुल का कलंक बनाकर पैदा किया और कुमाता ने मुझे स्वामी द्रोही बना दिया ॥
english_translation: Wretched am I, a sea of sin—wretched, wretched! All this upheaval has come because of me. The creator made me a stain on my family line, and my wicked mind made me betray my own lord.
essence: Remorse can make one mistake feel like your whole identity.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is overwhelmed by guilt. She sees herself as the cause of the disaster, a stain on her family, and a traitor to her own lord.
insight: It shows how remorse can spiral into self-condemnation instead of repair.
modern_relevance: You replay one terrible choice at 2 a.m. and start calling yourself the mistake. The mind turns one action into your whole identity.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: सुनि सप्रेम समुझाव निषादू। नाथ करिअ कत बादि बिषादू॥ राम तुम्हहि प्रिय तुम्ह प्रिय रामहि। यह निरजोसु दोसु बिधि बामहि ॥
translation: यह सुनकर निषादराज प्रेमपूर्वक समझाने लगा- हे नाथ! आप व्यर्थ विषाद किसलिए करते हैं? श्री रामचंद्रजी आपको प्यारे हैं और आप श्री रामचंद्रजी को प्यारे हैं। यही निचोड़ (निश्चित सिद्धांत) है, दोष तो प्रतिकूल विधाता को है ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Nishad spoke with love: “Lord, why grieve needlessly? Ram loves you, and you love Ram. That is the clear truth; the fault lies with adverse fate.”
essence: Love can survive even when circumstances turn harsh.
simple_meaning: Nishad tells the grieving person not to waste time in sorrow. Ram and this person love each other, so the real problem is the harsh turn of events, not their bond.
insight: It shifts attention from self-blame and despair to the underlying relationship that still remains intact.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a phone after a fight, replaying the worst part and ignoring what has not changed. Someone who truly knows you would say: the bond is still there; the hurt came from the turn, not the love.
speaker: Nishad

verse_text: बिधि बाम की करनी कठिन जेहिं मातु कीन्ही बावरी। तेहि राति पुनि पुनि करहिं प्रभु सादर सरहना रावरी॥ तुलसी न तुम्ह सो राम प्रीतमु कहतु हौं सौंहे किएँ। परिनाम मंगल जानि अपने आनिए धीरजु हिएँ॥
translation: प्रतिकूल विधाता की करनी बड़ी कठोर है, जिसने माता कैकेयी को बावली बना दिया (उसकी मति फेर दी)। उस रात को प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी बार-बार आदरपूर्वक आपकी बड़ी सराहना करते थे। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- (निषादराज कहता है कि-) श्री रामचंद्रजी को आपके समान अतिशय प्रिय और कोई नहीं है, मैं सौगंध खाकर कहता हूँ। परिणाम में मंगल होगा, यह जानकर आप अपने हृदय में धैर्य धारण कीजिए।
english_translation: The harsh working of fate turned Kaikeyi’s mind. That night, Lord Ram again and again praised you with respect. Tulsidas says: I swear there is no one dearer to Ram than you. Knowing the end will be auspicious, keep courage in your heart.
essence: What looks cruel now can still end in blessing.
simple_meaning: Even though Kaikeyi’s actions caused great pain, this verse says Ram still spoke of her with respect, and the result of all this will ultimately be good. So Bharat is urged to stay steady.
insight: It shifts you from reacting to the wound toward holding steady until the larger result becomes clear.
modern_relevance: You’re sitting in a hospital corridor after a family decision has gone badly, and everyone is blaming someone. This verse asks you to breathe, remember that love can survive damage, and not collapse before the outcome is known.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अंतरजामी रामु सकुच सप्रेम कृपायतन। चलिअ करिअ बिश्रामु यह बिचारि दृढ़ आनि मन ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी अंतर्यामी तथा संकोच, प्रेम और कृपा के धाम हैं, यह विचार कर और मन में दृढ़ता लाकर चलिए और विश्राम कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Knowing that Ram is all-knowing, gentle, and a home of grace, go on and rest, holding this firmly in your mind.
essence: Knowing Ram’s gentle awareness lets you finally rest.
simple_meaning: Put your mind at ease and rest, because Ram is inwardly aware, gentle, loving, and full of grace.
insight: It shifts the mind from anxious striving to settled trust in Ram’s awareness and care.
modern_relevance: After a long night of replaying a conversation, you finally notice your phone is still in your hand and your shoulders are locked. The verse says you can unclench — the one you love is not absent from your heart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सखा बचन सुनि उर धरि धीरा। बास चले सुमिरत रघुबीरा॥ यह सुधि पाइ नगर नर नारी। चले बिलोकन आरत भारी ॥
translation: सखा के वचन सुनकर, हृदय में धीरज धरकर श्री रामचंद्रजी का स्मरण करते हुए भरतजी डेरे को चले। नगर के सारे स्त्री-पुरुष यह (श्री रामजी के ठहरने के स्थान का) समाचार पाकर बड़े आतुर होकर उस स्थान को देखने चले ॥
english_translation: Hearing his friend’s words, Bharat steadied his heart and walked to Rama’s resting place, remembering the Lord of Raghu. When the people of the city heard the news, men and women hurried out in great distress to see that place.
essence: Love turns a resting place into a destination for grieving hearts.
simple_meaning: Bharat hears his friend, gathers himself, and goes to Rama’s resting place while remembering Rama. News spreads through the city, and everyone rushes out in deep distress to see the place.
insight: It shows how love makes a place sacred and pulls an entire community toward shared feeling.
modern_relevance: You hear the address of the hospital room where someone you love is waiting, and your chest tightens before you even arrive. Grief turns a location into a magnet.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परदखिना करि करहिं प्रनामा। देहिं कैकइहि खोरि निकामा। भरि भरि बारि बिलोचन लेंहीं। बाम बिधातहि दूषन देहीं ॥
translation: वे उस स्थान की परिक्रमा करके प्रणाम करते हैं और कैकेयी को बहुत दोष देते हैं। नेत्रों में जल भर-भर लेते हैं और प्रतिकूल विधाता को दूषण देते हैं ॥
english_translation: They circle the place and bow down, while blaming Kaikeyi bitterly. Tears fill their eyes again and again, and they curse fate itself.
essence: Grief makes people bow to what they cannot repair.
simple_meaning: People circle the spot where Bharat passed, bow to it, cry over Kaikeyi's role, and blame the cruel hand of fate.
insight: It shows how collective sorrow fixes on symbols, turning memory into ritual and pain into accusation.
modern_relevance: You stand outside a house after a family split, staring at the steps where everything changed. People keep retelling the same wound, trying to make sense of what no one can reverse.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक सराहहिं भरत सनेहू। कोउ कह नृपति निबाहेउ नेहू॥ निंदहिं आपु सराहि निषादहि। को कहि सकइ बिमोह बिषादहि ॥
translation: कोई भरतजी के स्नेह की सराहना करते हैं और कोई कहते हैं कि राजा ने अपना प्रेम खूब निबाहा। सब अपनी निंदा करके निषाद की प्रशंसा करते हैं। उस समय के विमोह और विषाद को कौन कह सकता है? ॥
english_translation: Some praised Bharata's love, and some said the king had kept his love well. All blamed themselves and praised Nishada. Who can describe the confusion and grief then?
essence: Grief makes everyone speak from the wound, not from clarity.
simple_meaning: People are overwhelmed by grief and confusion. They praise Bharata, praise the king's love, blame themselves, and praise Nishada, but no one can fully explain the sorrow.
insight: It shows how sorrow scatters judgment, turning even praise and blame into signs of the same wound.
modern_relevance: A family group chat after a funeral starts filling with apologies, praise, blame, and memories. Everyone means well, but the room is full of grief no one can organize.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ऐहि बिधि राति लोगु सबु जागा। भा भिनुसार गुदारा लागा॥ गुरहि सुनावँ चढ़ाइ सुहाईं। नईं नाव सब मातु चढ़ाईं ॥
translation: इस प्रकार रातभर सब लोग जागते रहे। सबेरा होते ही खेवा लगा। सुंदर नाव पर गुरुजी को चढ़ाकर फिर नई नाव पर सब माताओं को चढ़ाया ॥
english_translation: In this way, everyone stayed awake through the night. At dawn, the crossing began. The teacher was put onto the fine boat, and all the mothers were placed onto a new boat.
essence: Care is shown by how carefully you get everyone across.
simple_meaning: Everyone stayed awake all night, and at dawn the river crossing began. The teacher was placed on one boat, and the mothers were placed on another.
insight: It shifts attention from emotion to orderly action, showing how care becomes practical.
modern_relevance: You pack the car before sunrise, checking seats, bags, and who needs help getting in. The day is not about meaning yet — just careful movement, one person safely at a time.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दंड चारि महँ भा सबु पारा। उतरि भरत तब सबहि सँभारा ॥
translation: चार घड़ी में सब गंगाजी के पार उतर गए। तब भरतजी ने उतरकर सबको सँभाला ॥
english_translation: In four watches, everyone crossed over. Then Bharat got down and gathered everyone together.
essence: Crossing is only half the work; Bharat’s care completes the journey.
simple_meaning: Everyone crossed the river in a short time, and Bharat stepped in to gather and support the group.
insight: It shifts attention from the feat itself to the quiet responsibility that follows it.
modern_relevance: You finally get everyone through the airport at midnight, bags scattered and children half-asleep. The real work begins after arrival, when someone has to steady the group.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रातक्रिया करि मातु पद बंदि गुरहि सिरु नाइ। आगें किए निषाद गन दीन्हेउ कटकु चलाइ ॥
translation: प्रातःकाल की क्रियाओं को करके माता के चरणों की वंदना कर और गुरुजी को सिर नवाकर भरतजी ने विषाद गणों को (रास्ता दिखलाने के लिए) आगे कर लिया और सेना चला दी ॥141॥
english_translation: After completing his morning duties, Bharata bowed at his mother's feet and to the teacher, then placed the Nishadas in front and set the retinue in motion.
essence: Humility leads the march before authority does.
simple_meaning: Bharata finishes his morning rites, honors his mother and teacher, places the Nishadas ahead, and moves the group onward.
insight: It shows leadership as ordered humility: honor what is above you, then guide those who follow.
modern_relevance: You step out of a temple after prayer, then quietly make sure everyone in your family gets home safely. Respect comes first; then responsibility.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कियउ निषादनाथु अगुआईं। मातु पालकीं सकल चलाईं॥ साथ बोलाइ भाइ लघु दीन्हा। बिप्रन्ह सहित गवनु गुर कीन्हा ॥
translation: निषादराज को आगे करके पीछे सब माताओं की पालकियाँ चलाईं। छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्नजी को बुलाकर उनके साथ कर दिया। फिर ब्राह्मणों सहित गुरुजी ने गमन किया ॥
english_translation: Bharat placed Nishadraj in front, sent the mothers' palanquins onward, called his younger brother Shatrughna to go with him, and set out with the Brahmins and the guru.
essence: Leadership begins by placing others where they can move safely.
simple_meaning: Bharat organizes the journey carefully: he puts Nishadraj in front, sends the mothers along, brings Shatrughna with him, and leaves with the priests and teacher.
insight: It shifts attention from personal movement to responsible care for the whole group.
modern_relevance: You’re coordinating a family trip after a hard morning, making sure the elders are settled, the younger sibling stays close, and no one is left behind. That quiet care is Bharat’s way.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आपु सुरसरिहि कीन्ह प्रनामू। सुमिरे लखन सहित सिय रामू॥ गवने भरत पयादेहिं पाए। कोतल संग जाहिं डोरिआए ॥
translation: तदनन्तर आप (भरतजी) ने गंगाजी को प्रणाम किया और लक्ष्मण सहित श्री सीता-रामजी का स्मरण किया। भरतजी पैदल ही चले। उनके साथ कोतल (बिना सवार के) घोड़े बागडोर से बँधे हुए चले जा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Then Bharata bowed to the Ganga and remembered Sita-Rama along with Lakshmana. Bharata walked on foot, while the tethered horses followed behind without riders.
essence: Humility walks where power would rather ride.
simple_meaning: Bharata bows to the Ganga, remembers Ram, Sita, and Lakshmana, and continues on foot while the horses follow untended.
insight: It shifts status into service: the body follows humility, not entitlement.
modern_relevance: You step out of a luxury car to walk the last stretch to a funeral, a temple, or a friend’s small apartment. The gesture says more than the ride ever could.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहहिं सुसेवक बारहिं बारा। होइअ नाथ अस्व असवारा॥ रामु पयादेहि पायँ सिधाए। हम कहँ रथ गज बाजि बनाए ॥
translation: उत्तम सेवक बार-बार कहते हैं कि हे नाथ! आप घोड़े पर सवार हो लीजिए। (भरतजी जवाब देते हैं कि) श्री रामचंद्रजी तो पैदल ही गए और हमारे लिए रथ, हाथी और घोड़े बनाए गए हैं ॥
english_translation: The devoted servants keep urging him, again and again, to ride a horse. Bharat replies, "Ram walked on foot, and for us he prepared chariots, elephants, and horses."
essence: True service copies the beloved’s hardship, not your own comfort.
simple_meaning: Bharat refuses comfort because Ram accepted hardship first. He sees service as following Ram's example, not choosing ease for himself.
insight: It shifts service from self-protection to imitation of sacrifice.
modern_relevance: You’re offered the front seat after someone else has already done the hard walking. Bharat’s answer is the quiet sting of true loyalty: take less, because the one you follow took more.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: सिर भर जाउँ उचित अस मोरा। सब तें सेवक धरमु कठोरा॥ देखि भरत गति सुनि मृदु बानी। सब सेवक गन गरहिं गलानी ॥
translation: मुझे उचित तो ऐसा है कि मैं सिर के बल चलकर जाऊँ। सेवक का धर्म सबसे कठिन होता है। भरतजी की दशा देखकर और कोमल वाणी सुनकर सब सेवकगण ग्लानि के मारे गले जा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: What is proper for me is to go with my head down. The duty of a servant is the hardest of all. Seeing Bharat's state and hearing his gentle words, all the servants hang their heads in shame.
essence: True service lowers the ego before it lowers the body.
simple_meaning: Bharat feels that a true servant should be deeply humble, even to the point of bowing low. His example makes everyone serving with him feel ashamed of their own pride.
insight: It shifts service from performance to self-erasure, where the standard is not comfort but humility.
modern_relevance: You show up to help, but the person you came to support is already carrying the burden better than you are. Their quiet dignity makes your own shortcuts feel small.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत तीसरे पहर कहँ कीन्ह प्रबेसु प्रयाग। कहत राम सिय राम सिय उमगि उमगि अनुराग ॥
translation: प्रेम में उमँग-उमँगकर सीताराम-सीताराम कहते हुए भरतजी ने तीसरे पहर प्रयाग में प्रवेश किया ॥
english_translation: In the third watch, Bharat entered Prayag, overflowing with love, calling out, "Ram, Sita, Ram, Sita."
essence: Repeated remembrance reveals where your heart truly lives.
simple_meaning: Bharat reached Prayag in the afternoon, repeating Ram and Sita’s names with overflowing love.
insight: It shifts attention from the destination to the living presence carried in the heart.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital corridor after hearing bad news, and your mind keeps repeating one name. Love does that: it makes even movement become remembrance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: झलका झलकत पायन्ह कैसें। पंकज कोस ओस कन जैसें॥ भरत पयादेहिं आए आजू। भयउ दुखित सुनि सकल समाजू ॥
translation: उनके चरणों में छाले कैसे चमकते हैं, जैसे कमल की कली पर ओस की बूँदें चमकती हों। भरतजी आज पैदल ही चलकर आए हैं, यह समाचार सुनकर सारा समाज दुःखी हो गया ॥
english_translation: How beautifully the blisters on his feet shine, like dew drops on a lotus bud. Bharata has come here on foot, and hearing this, the whole assembly grew sorrowful.
essence: Bharata's devotion is so costly that even his feet tell the story.
simple_meaning: Bharata has walked barefoot, and the sight of his blistered feet moves everyone to sorrow.
insight: It turns attention to visible sacrifice and the quiet grief it awakens in others.
modern_relevance: You notice the blisters after a long day of caring for someone who never asked you to stay. The pain on your feet says what your words never needed to.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: खबरि लीन्ह सब लोग नहाए। कीन्ह प्रनामु त्रिबेनिहिं आए॥ सबिधि सितासित नीर नहाने। दिए दान महिसुर सनमाने ॥
translation: जब भरतजी ने यह पता पा लिया कि सब लोग स्नान कर चुके, तब त्रिवेणी पर आकर उन्हें प्रणाम किया। फिर विधिपूर्वक (गंगा-यमुना के) श्वेत और श्याम जल में स्नान किया और दान देकर ब्राह्मणों का सम्मान किया ॥
english_translation: After learning that everyone had finished bathing, Bharat came to the Triveni and bowed there. Then he bathed properly in the mixed white and dark waters, gave gifts, and honoured the learned priests.
essence: Painful journeys still call for disciplined, respectful action.
simple_meaning: Bharat arrives at the sacred confluence, bows first, bathes properly, gives charity, and shows respect to the priests.
insight: It shifts attention from emotional overwhelm to respectful conduct, showing that inner pain need not disrupt outer order.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a funeral or family gathering carrying private pain, but you still greet elders properly, sit quietly, and do what respect requires. Bharat shows grief can remain disciplined.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखत स्यामल धवल हलोरे। पुलकि सरीर भरत कर जोरे॥ सकल काम प्रद तीरथराऊ। बेद बिदित जग प्रगट प्रभाऊ ॥
translation: श्याम और सफेद (यमुनाजी और गंगाजी की) लहरों को देखकर भरतजी का शरीर पुलकित हो उठा और उन्होंने हाथ जोड़कर कहा- हे तीर्थराज! आप समस्त कामनाओं को पूर्ण करने वाले हैं। आपका प्रभाव वेदों में प्रसिद्ध और संसार में प्रकट है ॥
english_translation: Seeing the dark and bright waves, Bharata's body shivered with joy, and he folded his hands. "O king of sacred places, you grant every wish. Your glory is known in the Vedas and shines openly in the world."
essence: True reverence rises when the heart meets a source larger than its own wants.
simple_meaning: Bharat sees the sacred river waves, feels joy rise in his body, and joins his hands in reverence. He praises the holy place as a giver of all wishes and widely renowned.
insight: It shifts attention from personal desire to reverent recognition of what feels sacred and fulfilling.
modern_relevance: You stand at the edge of the ocean after a hard year, and the sight makes you quiet. Some places don't just look beautiful — they make you remember how to bow.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मागउँ भीख त्यागि निज धरमू। आरत काह न करइ कुकरमू॥ अस जियँ जानि सुजान सुदानी। सफल करहिं जग जाचक बानी ॥
translation: मैं अपना धर्म (न माँगने का क्षत्रिय धर्म) त्यागकर आप से भीख माँगता हूँ। आर्त्त मनुष्य कौन सा कुकर्म नहीं करता? ऐसा हृदय में जानकर सुजान उत्तम दानी जगत् में माँगने वाले की वाणी को सफल किया करते हैं (अर्थात् वह जो माँगता है, सो दे देते हैं) ॥
english_translation: I set aside my own duty and beg from you. In distress, what wrong will a person not do? Knowing this in the heart, wise and generous people make a beggar's words come true.
essence: Need can override pride, and wise generosity makes room for it.
simple_meaning: A person in deep distress may set aside pride and ask for help. Good, generous people recognize that suffering can drive anyone to beg, and they respond kindly.
insight: It shifts the mind from protecting pride to asking plainly for what is needed.
modern_relevance: You finally text the friend you’ve avoided because the rent is due tomorrow. The honest ask feels humiliating for a second, but it opens the door to real help.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: अरथ न धरम न काम रुचि गति न चहउँ निरबान। जनम-जनम रति राम पद यह बरदानु न आन ॥
translation: मुझे न अर्थ की रुचि (इच्छा) है, न धर्म की, न काम की और न मैं मोक्ष ही चाहता हूँ। जन्म-जन्म में मेरा श्री रामजी के चरणों में प्रेम हो, बस, यही वरदान माँगता हूँ, दूसरा कुछ नहीं ॥
english_translation: I want no wealth, no righteousness, no desire, and not even liberation. My only boon is love for Ram's feet, birth after birth.
essence: Nothing else satisfies when your heart wants Ram alone.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he wants no wealth, pleasure, or even liberation. His only wish is lifelong love for Ram's feet.
insight: It shifts desire away from achievement and toward wholehearted belonging.
modern_relevance: You finally get the thing you thought would fix everything, and it still feels thin. Bharat shows a different hunger: not for status, comfort, or even escape, but for a bond that never wears out.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जानहुँ रामु कुटिल करि मोही। लोग कहउ गुर साहिब द्रोही॥ सीता राम चरन रति मोरें। अनुदिन बढ़उ अनुग्रह तोरें ॥
translation: स्वयं श्री रामचंद्रजी भी भले ही मुझे कुटिल समझें और लोग मुझे गुरुद्रोही तथा स्वामी द्रोही भले ही कहें, पर श्री सीता-रामजी के चरणों में मेरा प्रेम आपकी कृपा से दिन-दिन बढ़ता ही रहे ॥
english_translation: Even if Ram himself thinks of me as crooked, and people call me disloyal to my teacher and master, may my love for the feet of Sita and Ram grow day by day by your grace.
essence: Being misunderstood is bearable when love keeps growing.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he does not mind being seen as dishonest or disloyal, as long as his love for Sita and Ram keeps increasing by grace.
insight: It shifts attention from protecting your image to protecting your devotion.
modern_relevance: You do the right thing, and someone still calls you manipulative. The sting is real, but you keep showing up with a cleaner heart than before.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जलदु जनम भरि सुरति बिसारउ। जाचत जलु पबि पाहन डारउ॥ चातकु रटिन घटें घटि जाई। बढ़ें प्रेमु सब भाँति भलाई ॥
translation: मेघ चाहे जन्मभर चातक की सुध भुला दे और जल माँगने पर वह चाहे वज्र और पत्थर (ओले) ही गिरावे, पर चातक की रटन घटने से तो उसकी बात ही घट जाएगी (प्रतिष्ठा ही नष्ट हो जाएगी)। उसकी तो प्रेम बढ़ने में ही सब तरह से भलाई है ॥
english_translation: Let the cloud forget the chataka for a whole lifetime; let it even rain thunderbolts and stones when water is begged for. If the chataka's cry weakens, its very standing falls. Its good lies in love growing in every way.
essence: Love deepens when you keep calling without guarantee of reply.
simple_meaning: The chataka bird should keep crying for rain no matter what the cloud does. In devotion, longing itself is part of the blessing.
insight: It shifts you from judging love by outcomes to valuing the steadiness of your own longing.
modern_relevance: You keep texting someone who barely replies, yet you still care. This verse says your devotion is not measured by the response you get.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कनकहिं बान चढ़इ जिमि दाहें। तिमि प्रियतम पद नेम निबाहें॥ भरत बचन सुनि माझ त्रिबेनी। भइ मृदु बानि सुमंगल देनी ॥
translation: जैसे तपाने से सोने पर आब (चमक) आ जाती है, वैसे ही प्रियतम के चरणों में प्रेम का नियम निबाहने से प्रेमी सेवक का गौरव बढ़ जाता है। भरतजी के वचन सुनकर बीच त्रिवेणी में से सुंदर मंगल देने वाली कोमल वाणी हुई ॥
english_translation: As gold is refined by fire, so a devoted servant's glory is polished by keeping faith with the beloved's feet. Hearing Bharat's words, a gentle, auspicious voice arose from the middle of the Triveni.
essence: Faithful service does not diminish you; it makes your devotion shine.
simple_meaning: Keeping faith with the beloved's feet refines your worth, just as fire refines gold. Bharat's words move the sacred river crossing to answer with a gentle blessing.
insight: It shifts attention from personal gain to the refining power of faithful service.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone who never promised you anything back. The work feels costly, but over time it makes your devotion unmistakable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तात भरत तुम्ह सब बिधि साधू। राम चरन अनुराग अगाधू॥ बादि गलानि करहु मन माहीं। तुम्ह सम रामहि कोउ प्रिय नाहीं ॥
translation: हे तात भरत! तुम सब प्रकार से साधु हो। श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणों में तुम्हारा अथाह प्रेम है। तुम व्यर्थ ही मन में ग्लानि कर रहे हो। श्री रामचंद्रजी को तुम्हारे समान प्रिय कोई नहीं है ॥
english_translation: O Bharat, you are noble in every way. Your love for Ram's feet is boundless. Do not keep blaming yourself in your mind. No one is dearer to Ram than you.
essence: Your deepest love can be greater than your loudest guilt.
simple_meaning: Bharat is praised as noble and deeply devoted to Ram. He should stop blaming himself, because Ram loves him more than anyone else.
insight: It shifts self-judgment into trust in the sincerity of your devotion and character.
modern_relevance: You replay one conversation for hours, convinced you ruined everything. But the person you disappointed may still value your heart more than your mistake.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तनु पुलकेउ हियँ हरषु सुनि बेनि बचन अनुकूल। भरत धन्य कहि धन्य सुर हरषित बरषहिं फूल ॥
translation: त्रिवेणीजी के अनुकूल वचन सुनकर भरतजी का शरीर पुलकित हो गया, हृदय में हर्ष छा गया। भरतजी धन्य हैं, कहकर देवता हर्षित होकर फूल बरसाने लगे ॥
english_translation: Hearing Triveni's favorable words, Bharat's body thrilled and joy rose in his heart. 'Bharat is blessed,' the radiant beings said, and flowers rained down in joy.
essence: True humility is seen, and the world answers with joy.
simple_meaning: Triveni's kind words fill Bharat with joy, and the heavenly beings celebrate him with flowers.
insight: It shows how sincere virtue can create a ripple of joy, turning private goodness into public blessing.
modern_relevance: You hear someone finally say what they mean about you after months of quiet effort. The relief is instant, and even the room seems lighter.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रमुदित तीरथराज निवासी। बैखानस बटु गृही उदासी॥ कहहिं परसपर मिलि दस पाँचा। भरत सनेहु सीलु सुचि साँचा ॥
translation: तीर्थराज प्रयाग में रहने वाले वनप्रस्थ, ब्रह्मचारी, गृहस्थ और उदासीन (संन्यासी) सब बहुत ही आनंदित हैं और दस-पाँच मिलकर आपस में कहते हैं कि भरतजी का प्रेम और शील पवित्र और सच्चा है ॥
english_translation: The residents of Prayag, whether forest-dwellers, celibates, householders, or renunciates, are delighted. Gathering in small groups, they say to one another that Bharat's love and character are pure and true.
essence: Pure devotion speaks for itself.
simple_meaning: Everyone in Prayag is happy and speaking well of Bharat. They see his love and character as pure and genuine.
insight: It shows how sincere conduct earns trust across every social group.
modern_relevance: At a train station, a group of strangers notices the person quietly helping everyone without asking for credit. Soon they are all saying the same thing: that person's heart is unmistakably clean.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनत राम गुन ग्राम सुहाए। भारद्वाज मुनिबर पहिं आए॥ दंड प्रनामु करत मुनि देखे। मूरतिमंत भाग्य निज लेखे ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के सुंदर गुण समूहों को सुनते हुए वे मुनिश्रेष्ठ भारद्वाजजी के पास आए। मुनि ने भरतजी को दण्डवत प्रणाम करते देखा और उन्हें अपना मूर्तिमान सौभाग्य समझा ॥
english_translation: Hearing the lovely stories of Ram's virtues, they came to the great sage Bharadwaj. The sage saw Bharat bowing down in prostration and felt he was looking at his own embodied good fortune.
essence: Humility can look like living good fortune.
simple_meaning: Hearing praise of Ram, Bharat goes to Bharadwaj and bows deeply. The sage sees his humility and feels blessed just to witness it.
insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing that humility itself can be the highest richness.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who arrives without any ego, only respect. Their humility changes the whole room before a single word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धाइ उठाइ लाइ उर लीन्हे। दीन्हि असीस कृतारथ कीन्हे॥ आसनु दीन्ह नाइ सिरु बैठे। चहत सकुच गृहँ जनु भजि पैठे ॥
translation: उन्होंने दौड़कर भरतजी को उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया और आशीर्वाद देकर कृतार्थ किया। मुनि ने उन्हें आसन दिया। वे सिर नवाकर इस तरह बैठे मानो भागकर संकोच के घर में घुस जाना चाहते हैं ॥
english_translation: They ran forward, lifted Bharata into their embrace, blessed him, and made him feel fulfilled. The sage offered a seat, and Bharata sat after bowing his head, as if shyly entering the house of modesty itself.
essence: Humility can be so deep it makes honour feel almost embarrassing.
simple_meaning: The sage welcomes Bharata with warmth, blessing, and respect. Bharata responds with deep humility and such modesty that he seems almost to shrink away from attention.
insight: It shifts attention from status and performance to humility as a lived strength.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone expects you to speak first, but you bow your head and listen. That quiet modesty can change the whole atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि पूँछब कछु यह बड़ सोचू। बोले रिषि लखि सीलु सँकोचू॥ सुनहु भरत हम सब सुधि पाई। बिधि करतब पर किछु न बसाई ॥
translation: उनके मन में यह बड़ा सोच है कि मुनि कुछ पूछेंगे (तो मैं क्या उत्तर दूँगा)। भरतजी के शील और संकोच को देखकर ऋषि बोले- भरत! सुनो, हम सब खबर पा चुके हैं। विधाता के कर्तव्य पर कुछ वश नहीं चलता ॥
english_translation: Seeing Bharata's restraint and hesitation, the sage said, "Bharata, listen. We already know everything. No one can control what fate has set in motion."
essence: Some events cannot be stopped, only met with steadiness.
simple_meaning: Bharadwaj sees Bharata's humility and gently tells him that no one can control everything that happens. Some things are already in motion beyond human power.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame to clear acceptance of limits.
modern_relevance: You replay the message you sent, wondering if you could have prevented the fallout. Then you realize the chain had already started before you touched it. Some outcomes were never in your hands.
speaker: Bharadwaj

verse_text: तुम्ह गलानि जियँ जनि करहु समुझि मातु करतूति। तात कैकइहि दोसु नहिं गई गिरा मति धूति ॥
translation: माता की करतूत को समझकर (याद करके) तुम हृदय में ग्लानि मत करो। हे तात! कैकेयी का कोई दोष नहीं है, उसकी बुद्धि तो सरस्वती बिगाड़ गई थी ॥
english_translation: Do not feel remorse in your heart, remembering your mother's actions. O dear one, Kaikeyi is not at fault; the goddess of speech clouded her understanding.
essence: Not every painful act deserves your lifelong guilt.
simple_meaning: Bharat is told not to feel guilty about his mother’s actions. Kaikeyi is not being blamed fully, because her judgment was clouded.
insight: It shifts the mind from inherited shame to compassionate understanding of impaired judgment.
modern_relevance: You replay your parent’s worst decision for years, as if it lives inside your own name. This verse says not every family wound belongs to you to carry as guilt.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: यहउ कहत भल कहिहि न कोऊ। लोकु बेदु बुध संमत दोऊ॥ तात तुम्हार बिमल जसु गाई। पाइहि लोकउ बेदु बड़ाई ॥
translation: यह कहते भी कोई भला न कहेगा, क्योंकि लोक और वेद दोनों ही विद्वानों को मान्य है, किन्तु हे तात! तुम्हारा निर्मल यश गाकर तो लोक और वेद दोनों बड़ाई पावेंगे ॥
english_translation: No one would call this good either, for both society and the Vedas approve it. Yet, my dear son, singing your spotless fame will win praise from both society and the Vedas.
essence: A pure life makes praise feel true, not flattering.
simple_meaning: A wise person says that speaking well of Bharat is not wrong, because both society and sacred tradition respect it. His pure reputation will bring him honor everywhere.
insight: It shifts attention from awkward self-justification to the quiet power of a clean reputation.
modern_relevance: You hesitate before recommending someone who never self-promotes, yet everyone who worked with them already knows the truth. Their integrity carries farther than your praise.
speaker: Rishi

verse_text: लोक बेद संमत सबु कहई। जेहि पितु देइ राजु सो लहई॥ राउ सत्यब्रत तुम्हहि बोलाई। देत राजु सुखु धरमु बड़ाई ॥
translation: यह लोक और वेद दोनों को मान्य है और सब यही कहते हैं कि पिता जिसको राज्य दे वही पाता है। राजा सत्यव्रती थे, तुमको बुलाकर राज्य देते, तो सुख मिलता, धर्म रहता और बड़ाई होती ॥
english_translation: It is accepted by both worldly custom and the Vedas that whoever the father gives the kingdom to receives it. King Dasharath was true to his vow; if he had called you and given you the throne, you would have gained happiness, dharma, and honor.
essence: A vow can matter more than power, even when power is within reach.
simple_meaning: The rightful heir should receive the throne, and Dasharath’s vow-bound nature made that possible. If he had given Bharat the kingdom, Bharat would have gained comfort, duty, and respect.
insight: It shifts attention from personal gain to the moral weight of keeping a promise.
modern_relevance: You promised two people different things, and now both cannot be satisfied. The clean answer is not the easiest one — it is the one that keeps your word intact, even when it hurts.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम गवनु बन अनरथ मूला। जो सुनि सकल बिस्व भइ सूला॥ सो भावी बस रानि अयानी। करि कुचालि अंतहुँ पछितानी ॥
translation: सारे अनर्थ की जड़ तो श्री रामचन्द्रजी का वनगमन है, जिसे सुनकर समस्त संसार को पीड़ा हुई। वह श्री राम का वनगमन भी भावीवश हुआ। बेसमझ रानी तो भावीवश कुचाल करके अंत में पछताई ॥
english_translation: The exile of Ram was the root of all calamity, and hearing of it brought pain to the whole world. That exile happened by the force of fate. The foolish queen acted wrongly and later regretted it.
essence: One wrong turn can become the root of lasting pain.
simple_meaning: Ram's exile became the source of all suffering, and the whole world felt that pain. The queen's wrong choice was driven by fate, and she later regretted it.
insight: It shifts attention from immediate blame to the wider consequences of one wrong turn.
modern_relevance: A family argument that seemed manageable at midnight can still echo through years of silence, regret, and distance the next morning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तहँउँ तुम्हार अलप अपराधू। कहै सो अधम अयान असाधू॥ करतेहु राजु त तुम्हहि ना दोषू। रामहि होत सुनत संतोषू ॥
translation: उसमें भी तुम्हारा कोई तनिक सा भी अपराध कहे, तो वह अधम, अज्ञानी और असाधु है। यदि तुम राज्य करते तो भी तुम्हें दोष न होता। सुनकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी को भी संतोष ही होता ॥
english_translation: Even there, anyone who calls your conduct a small fault is base, ignorant, and unrighteous. Even if you had ruled the kingdom, you would still not be at fault. Hearing it, Ram would feel only gladness.
essence: Right action can look like wrongdoing to people who cannot see the heart.
simple_meaning: Bharat is told that even the smallest blame placed on him is unfair. He would not have been wrong even if he had taken the throne, and Ram would have accepted it peacefully.
insight: It shifts judgment away from appearances and back to intention, duty, and Ram's approval.
modern_relevance: A family meeting turns tense because someone implies you should have stepped in sooner. You know you acted from loyalty, not ambition, and the accusation does not fit the truth.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अब अति कीन्हेहु भरत भल तुम्हहि उचित मत एहु। सकल सुमंगल मूल जग रघुबर चरन सनेहु ॥
translation: हे भरत! अब तो तुमने बहुत ही अच्छा किया, यही मत तुम्हारे लिए उचित था। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में प्रेम होना ही संसार में समस्त सुंदर मंगलों का मूल है ॥
english_translation: O Bharat, you have done very well. This is the right way for you. Love for Raghubar's feet is the root of all auspiciousness in the world.
essence: Loving Ram is the source of every real blessing.
simple_meaning: Bharat has chosen the right path: loving Ram is the source of all true blessing.
insight: It shifts value from status and gain to devotion as the foundation of a rightly ordered life.
modern_relevance: You turn down the promotion because it would cost your integrity, and people call it foolish. This verse says the deeper choice is the one that keeps your heart aligned with what is highest.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सो तुम्हार धनु जीवनु प्राना। भूरिभाग को तुम्हहि समाना॥ यह तुम्हार आचरजु न ताता। दसरथ सुअन राम प्रिय भ्राता ॥
translation: सो वह (श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों का प्रेम) तो तुम्हारा धन, जीवन और प्राण ही है, तुम्हारे समान बड़भागी कौन है? हे तात! तुम्हारे लिए यह आश्चर्य की बात नहीं है, क्योंकि तुम दशरथजी के पुत्र और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्यारे भाई हो ॥
english_translation: That love for Ram's feet is your wealth, your life, and your breath. Who is as fortunate as you? Father, this is no surprise, because you are Dasharath's son and Ram's beloved brother.
essence: Love for Ram makes Bharat richer than kings.
simple_meaning: Bharat's greatest wealth is his love for Ram. That love is what gives his life meaning, and no one is more fortunate than he is.
insight: It shifts value away from ownership and toward loving relationship.
modern_relevance: When everyone around you measures success by salary, status, or control, you quietly choose loyalty to what matters most. That choice can look strange from outside and completely natural from within.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुनहु भरत रघुबर मन माहीं। पेम पात्रु तुम्ह सम कोउ नाहीं॥ लखन राम सीतहि अति प्रीती। निसि सब तुम्हहि सराहत बीती ॥
translation: हे भरत! सुनो, श्री रामचन्द्र के मन में तुम्हारे समान प्रेम पात्र दूसरा कोई नहीं है। लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामजी और सीताजी तीनों की सारी रात उस दिन अत्यन्त प्रेम के साथ तुम्हारी सराहना करते ही बीती ॥
english_translation: Bharat, listen: in Raghubar's heart, no one is as dear as you. Lakshman, Ram, and Sita spent the whole night praising you with love.
essence: True devotion makes you dear without asking to be seen.
simple_meaning: Bharat is told that Ram loves him more than anyone else, and Lakshman, Ram, and Sita spent the night praising him with affection.
insight: It shifts attention from self-doubt to the reality of being held in genuine affection.
modern_relevance: You leave a family gathering unsure whether anyone noticed your effort. Later, someone tells you the person you admire most was speaking warmly about you all evening.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जाना मरमु नहात प्रयागा। मगन होहिं तुम्हरें अनुरागा॥ तुम्ह पर अस सनेहु रघुबर कें। सुख जीवन जग जस जड़ नर कें ॥
translation: प्रयागराज में जब वे स्नान कर रहे थे, उस समय मैंने उनका यह मर्म जाना। वे तुम्हारे प्रेम में मग्न हो रहे थे। तुम पर श्री रामचन्द्रजी का ऐसा ही (अगाध) स्नेह है, जैसा मूर्ख (विषयासक्त) मनुष्य का संसार में सुखमय जीवन पर होता है ॥
english_translation: I came to know the secret while bathing at Prayag. They became absorbed in your affection. Lord Raghubar's love for you is like a foolish person's attachment to worldly comfort and praise.
essence: Ram's love for you can be as consuming as obsession.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he understood the depth of Ram's affection for Bharat at Prayag. Ram's love for Bharat is so strong that it resembles a person's attachment to comfort and praise.
insight: It shifts attention from your own effort to the depth of Ram's affection for the devotee.
modern_relevance: You notice someone checking their phone again and again, not for work, but for one message from a person they love. That quiet pull is the closest image to this verse's tenderness.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: यह न अधिक रघुबीर बड़ाई। प्रनत कुटुंब पाल रघुराई॥ तुम्ह तौ भरत मोर मत एहू। धरें देह जनु राम सनेहू ॥
translation: यह श्री रघुनाथजी की बहुत बड़ाई नहीं है, क्योंकि श्री रघुनाथजी तो शरणागत के कुटुम्ब भर को पालने वाले हैं। हे भरत! मेरा यह मत है कि तुम तो मानो शरीरधारी श्री रामजी के प्रेम ही हो ॥
english_translation: This is not great praise of Raghubir, for Raghurai sustains the whole family of those who take refuge. Bharata, my view is that you are as if embodied love for Ram.
essence: Ram's refuge includes everyone you love.
simple_meaning: Ram's greatness is that he protects everyone who takes refuge in him. Bharata is so filled with love for Ram that he seems like love itself in human form.
insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to a whole way of being that protects others too.
modern_relevance: You watch someone stay up all night caring for a sick parent, then still worry about everyone else in the house. This verse sees that kind of love and says: devotion changes who you are.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तुम्ह कहँ भरत कलंक यह हम सब कहँ उपदेसु। राम भगति रस सिद्धि हित भा यह समउ गनेसु ॥
translation: हे भरत! तुम्हारे लिए (तुम्हारी समझ में) यह कलंक है, पर हम सबके लिए तो उपदेश है। श्री रामभक्ति रूपी रस की सिद्धि के लिए यह समय गणेश (बड़ा शुभ) हुआ है ॥
english_translation: Bharat, what seems like a stain to you is instruction for all of us. This is an auspicious moment for the completion of the nectar of devotion to Ram.
essence: What feels like shame can become the doorway to devotion.
simple_meaning: What looks like disgrace to Bharat becomes a teaching for everyone else. Tulsidas says this moment is auspicious because it helps devotion to Ram mature fully.
insight: It shifts you from seeing embarrassment as wasted pain to seeing it as material for devotion and learning.
modern_relevance: You were misunderstood in a family meeting, and the memory still stings. Later, someone else learns courage from that same moment. Pain can become instruction when love is larger than pride.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: नव बिधु बिमल तात जसु तोरा। रघुबर किंकर कुमुद चकोरा॥ उदित सदा अँथइहि कबहूँ ना। घटिहि न जग नभ दिन दिन दूना ॥
translation: हे तात! तुम्हारा यश निर्मल नवीन चन्द्रमा है और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दास कुमुद और चकोर हैं (वह चन्द्रमा तो प्रतिदिन अस्त होता और घटता है, जिससे कुमुद और चकोर को दुःख होता है), परन्तु यह तुम्हारा यश रूपी चन्द्रमा सदा उदय रहेगा, कभी अस्त होगा ही नहीं! जगत रूपी आकाश में यह घटेगा नहीं, वरन दिन-दिन दूना होगा ॥
english_translation: Your spotless fame, dear Bharat, is like a fresh moon. The servants of Raghubar are the kumud and chakor that live by it. It will rise forever, never set, and it will not fade in the world’s sky; day by day it will grow brighter.
essence: Pure devotion turns your name into a light that only grows.
simple_meaning: Bharat's fame is compared to a moon that never sets or wanes. As long as Ram's devotees exist, that glory will keep growing.
insight: It shifts attention from short-term praise to the lasting radiance of a life rooted in Ram.
modern_relevance: You quietly did the right thing when no one was applauding. Months later, people still trust your name because they felt your steadiness. That kind of goodness compounds.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोक तिलोक प्रीति अति करिही। प्रभु प्रताप रबि छबिहि न हरिही॥ निसि दिन सुखद सदा सब काहू। ग्रसिहि न कैकइ करतबु राहू ॥
translation: त्रैलोक्य रूपी चकवा इस यश रूपी चन्द्रमा पर अत्यन्त प्रेम करेगा और प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी का प्रताप रूपी सूर्य इसकी छबि को हरण नहीं करेगा। यह चन्द्रमा रात-दिन सदा सब किसी को सुख देने वाला होगा। कैकेयी का कुकर्म रूपी राहु इसे ग्रास नहीं करेगा ॥
english_translation: The three worlds will love this moon of fame deeply. The sun of the Lord's splendor will never dim its beauty. It will always give joy to everyone, day and night. Rahu's dark deed of Kaikeyi will not swallow it.
essence: True brilliance survives even the darkest blow.
simple_meaning: Rama's fame is like a moon loved by all. Its brightness will never fade, and Kaikeyi's wrongdoing cannot swallow it.
insight: It shifts attention from temporary disgrace to enduring worth.
modern_relevance: A rumor starts after a family argument, and suddenly everyone is speaking as if one cruel moment defines the whole person. This verse refuses that collapse: what is truly noble can survive public damage.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पूरन राम सुपेम पियूषा। गुर अवमान दोष नहिं दूषा॥ राम भगत अब अमिअँ अघाहूँ। कीन्हेहु सुलभ सुधा बसुधाहूँ ॥
translation: यह चन्द्रमा श्री रामचन्द्रजी के सुंदर प्रेम रूपी अमृत से पूर्ण है। यह गुरु के अपमान रूपी दोष से दूषित नहीं है। तुमने इस यश रूपी चन्द्रमा की सृष्टि करके पृथ्वी पर भी अमृत को सुलभ कर दिया। अब श्री रामजी के भक्त इस अमृत से तृप्त हो लें ॥
english_translation: This moon is full of Ram's beautiful nectar of love. It is not stained by disrespect to the guru. You have made nectar easy to find on earth, and now Ram's devotees may drink their fill.
essence: Pure devotion becomes nectar that feeds everyone around it.
simple_meaning: Ram's loving glory is like nectar that remains pure and can satisfy devotees. A life of devotion can become a blessing others freely share.
insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to shared nourishment that others can actually receive.
modern_relevance: You do something beautiful, and people around you quietly feel steadier because of it. A home, a team, or a friendship can become easier to breathe in when your care is clean and generous.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भूप भगीरथ सुरसरि आनी। सुमिरत सकल सुमंगल खानी॥ दसरथ गुन गन बरनि न जाहीं। अधिकु कहा जेहि सम जग नाहीं ॥
translation: राजा भगीरथ गंगाजी को लाए, जिन (गंगाजी) का स्मरण ही सम्पूर्ण सुंदर मंगलों की खान है। दशरथजी के गुण समूहों का तो वर्णन ही नहीं किया जा सकता, अधिक क्या, जिनकी बराबरी का जगत में कोई नहीं है ॥
english_translation: King Bhagirath brought the Ganga, whose remembrance itself is a treasury of all auspiciousness. King Dasharath's countless virtues cannot be described; there is no one in the world equal to him.
essence: True greatness is remembered through the blessings it leaves behind.
simple_meaning: Bhagirath is remembered for bringing the Ganga, and Dasharath is praised as a king whose virtues are beyond description and unmatched in the world.
insight: It shifts attention from public power to the lasting fragrance of virtue and service.
modern_relevance: A funeral conversation turns to the person everyone admired: not their title, but the way their life quietly improved everyone around them. That is the kind of loss this verse prepares you to feel.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जासु सनेह सकोच बस राम प्रगट भए आई। जे हर हिय नयननि कबहुँ निरखे नहीं अघाइ ॥
translation: जिनके प्रेम और संकोच (शील) के वश में होकर स्वयं (सच्चिदानंदघन) भगवान श्री राम आकर प्रकट हुए, जिन्हें श्री महादेवजी अपने हृदय के नेत्रों से कभी अघाकर नहीं देख पाए (अर्थात जिनका स्वरूप हृदय में देखते-देखते शिवजी कभी तृप्त नहीं हुए) ॥
english_translation: Because of their love and modest reserve, Ram himself came and appeared. Mahadev never grew tired of seeing them with his heart and eyes.
essence: Love and modesty can draw Ram himself into view.
simple_meaning: Deep love and humble restraint can draw Ram himself near. Such a person becomes endlessly beautiful to Shiva's heart.
insight: It shifts attention from outward display to the quiet force of love and humility.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who stays gentle even when praised, and the room changes. People trust that kind of quiet dignity — it feels like something higher has entered the space.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कीरति बिधु तुम्ह कीन्ह अनूपा। जहँ बस राम पेम मृगरूपा॥ तात गलानि करहु जियँ जाएँ। डरहु दरिद्रहि पारसु पाएँ ॥
translation: (परन्तु उनसे भी बढ़कर) तुमने कीर्ति रूपी अनुपम चंद्रमा को उत्पन्न किया, जिसमें श्री राम प्रेम ही हिरन के (चिह्न के) रूप में बसता है। हे तात! तुम व्यर्थ ही हृदय में ग्लानि कर रहे हो। पारस पाकर भी तुम दरिद्रता से डर रहे हो! ॥
