english_translation: You created a unique moon of fame, where Ram's love lives like a deer. Dear one, do not feel remorse in your heart. Why fear poverty after finding a touchstone?
essence: Ram's love makes even remorse look unnecessary.
simple_meaning: Bharat has already earned extraordinary honor because Ram's love rests in his fame. Shiva tells him not to feel ashamed or think himself spiritually poor after receiving such grace.
insight: It shifts attention from self-criticism to the grace already present in your life.
modern_relevance: You keep replaying the one mistake that went wrong, even though your life is already carrying real love, trust, and earned respect. Shiva's words tell you not to call yourself poor just because perfection is missing.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सुनहु भरत हम झूठ न कहहीं। उदासीन तापस बन रहहीं॥ सब साधन कर सुफल सुहावा। लखन राम सिय दरसनु पावा ॥
translation: हे भरत! सुनो, हम झूठ नहीं कहते। हम उदासीन हैं (किसी का पक्ष नहीं करते), तपस्वी हैं (किसी की मुँह देखी नहीं कहते) और वन में रहते हैं (किसी से कुछ प्रयोजन नहीं रखते)। सब साधनों का उत्तम फल हमें लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामजी और सीताजी का दर्शन प्राप्त हुआ ॥
english_translation: Listen, Bharat, we do not speak falsely. We are detached, forest-dwelling ascetics who take no side. The best fruit of all spiritual practice is that we have seen Lakshman, Ram, and Sita.
essence: All striving finds its fulfillment in Ram's presence.
simple_meaning: All spiritual effort reaches its highest fruit in the direct sight of Ram, Sita, and Lakshman. Detachment and austerity are not the goal; loving encounter is.
insight: It shifts spiritual effort from self-improvement to loving encounter.
modern_relevance: You finish a long retreat, a year of therapy, or months of discipline and realize the breakthrough wasn't the achievement. It was finally meeting what you had been preparing yourself to receive.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: तेहि फल कर फलु दरस तुम्हारा। सहित प्रयाग सुभाग हमारा॥ भरत धन्य तुम्ह जसु जगु जयऊ। कहि अस प्रेम मगन मुनि भयऊ ॥
translation: (सीता-लक्ष्मण सहित श्री रामदर्शन रूप) उस महान फल का परम फल यह तुम्हारा दर्शन है! प्रयागराज समेत हमारा बड़ा भाग्य है। हे भरत! तुम धन्य हो, तुमने अपने यश से जगत को जीत लिया है। ऐसा कहकर मुनि प्रेम में मग्न हो गए ॥
english_translation: The highest fruit of that great result is your sight. Our good fortune, along with Prayag's, is fulfilled. Bharata, you are blessed; your fame has conquered the world. Saying this, the sage became lost in love.
essence: True devotion makes your presence itself the reward.
simple_meaning: Seeing Bharata is treated as the highest reward of all. The sage says this meeting completes their good fortune and praises Bharata’s fame as world-winning.
insight: It shifts attention from achievement to the grace a devoted presence brings into a place.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone who kept showing up for everyone else, never asking for credit. Their quiet loyalty changes the whole room, and you realize presence itself can be a blessing.
speaker: Bharadvaja

verse_text: सुनि मुनि बचन सभासद हरषे। साधु सराहि सुमन सुर बरषे॥ धन्य धन्य धुनि गगन प्रयागा। सुनि सुनि भरतु मगन अनुरागा॥4
translation: भारद्वाज मुनि के वचन सुनकर सभासद् हर्षित हो गए। 'साधु-साधु' कहकर सराहना करते हुए देवताओं ने फूल बरसाए। आकाश में और प्रयागराज में 'धन्य, धन्य' की ध्वनि सुन-सुनकर भरतजी प्रेम में मग्न हो रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing the sage's words, everyone in the assembly rejoiced. Praising him as noble, the devas showered flowers. The sky and Prayagraj rang with cries of "Blessed! Blessed!" and Bharat, hearing and hearing it all, became lost in love.
essence: Praise ripens devotion when the heart is already surrendered.
simple_meaning: The assembly rejoices at the sage's words, the devas shower flowers, and Bharat is swept deeper into loving devotion.
insight: It shows how sincere recognition can intensify humility and loving absorption rather than self-importance.
modern_relevance: You hear someone describe your quiet sacrifice with more kindness than you expected, and your throat tightens. Being seen rightly can deepen devotion instead of feeding ego.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुलक गात हियँ रामु सिय सजल सरोरुह नैन। करि प्रनामु मुनि मंडलिहि बोले गदगद बैन ॥
translation: भरतजी का शरीर पुलकित है, हृदय में श्री सीता-रामजी हैं और कमल के समान नेत्र (प्रेमाश्रु के) जल से भरे हैं। वे मुनियों की मंडली को प्रणाम करके गद्गद वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: Bharat's body trembles with emotion; Ram and Sita fill his heart, and his lotus-like eyes are wet with tears. He bows to the assembly of sages and speaks in a choked voice.
essence: True reverence makes even your voice bow.
simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed with devotion and tears as he bows to the sages and speaks in a choked voice.
insight: It teaches you that deep devotion first appears in the body, then in speech.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone whose kindness has held you together for years, and your throat closes before you can thank them. Gratitude arrives faster than language.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि समाजु अरु तीरथराजू। साँचिहुँ सपथ अघाइ अकाजू॥ एहिं थल जौं किछु कहिअ बनाई। एहि सम अधिक न अघ अधमाई ॥
translation: मुनियों का समाज है और फिर तीर्थराज है। यहाँ सच्ची सौगंध खाने से भी भरपूर हानि होती है। इस स्थान में यदि कुछ बनाकर कहा जाए, तो इसके समान कोई बड़ा पाप और नीचता न होगी ॥
english_translation: This is the gathering of sages and the king of pilgrimages. Even a true oath taken here loses its value. If you speak falsely in this place, no greater evil or baseness exists.
essence: Falsehood feels smallest nowhere less than before the holy and the wise.
simple_meaning: This sacred place is so holy that speaking falsely here is especially shameful. Even a true oath would be wasted if it were used to hide the truth.
insight: It pushes you to drop performance when the setting demands truth, especially before people who can see through it.
modern_relevance: You’re in a room where everyone can sense you’re hiding something, and the silence is getting heavier by the second. In that moment, polished words only deepen the crack.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: तुम्ह सर्बग्य कहउँ सतिभाऊ। उर अंतरजामी रघुराऊ॥ मोहि न मातु करतब कर सोचू। नहिं दुखु जियँ जगु जानिहि पोचू ॥
translation: मैं सच्चे भाव से कहता हूँ। आप सर्वज्ञ हैं और श्री रघुनाथजी हृदय के भीतर की जानने वाले हैं (मैं कुछ भी असत्य कहूँगा तो आपसे और उनसे छिपा नहीं रह सकता)। मुझे माता कैकेयी की करनी का कुछ भी सोच नहीं है और न मेरे मन में इसी बात का दुःख है कि जगत मुझे नीच समझेगा ॥
english_translation: I speak with complete sincerity. You are all-knowing, and Raghunath knows the heart within. I do not worry about Kaikeyi's deed, nor do I grieve that the world will call me low.
essence: When your heart is already seen, public judgment loses its power.
simple_meaning: Bharat speaks honestly to the sages: Ram knows his heart, so he has no need to hide anything. He is not troubled by Kaikeyi's actions or by public shame.
insight: It shifts attention from managing your image to standing honestly in what you know is true.
modern_relevance: You sit in a family meeting where everyone assumes the worst about you, and you stop trying to win the room. The need to be understood loosens its grip.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: नाहिन डरु बिगरिहि परलोकू। पितहु मरन कर मोहि न सोकू॥ सुकृत सुजस भरि भुअन सुहाए। लछिमन राम सरिस सुत पाए ॥
translation: न यही डर है कि मेरा परलोक बिगड़ जाएगा और न पिताजी के मरने का ही मुझे शोक है, क्योंकि उनका सुंदर पुण्य और सुयश विश्व भर में सुशोभित है। उन्होंने श्री राम-लक्ष्मण सरीखे पुत्र पाए ॥
english_translation: I do not fear any harm to the next world, nor grieve my father's death. His good deeds and good name shine across the world, and he gained sons like Ram and Lakshman.
essence: A life filled with virtue leaves grief less room to grow.
simple_meaning: Bharat says Dasharath’s death does not trouble him deeply, because his father’s virtue and fame are secure, and he was blessed with sons like Ram and Lakshman.
insight: It shifts attention from loss itself to the wholeness of a life already completed in virtue.
modern_relevance: You stand at a funeral and hear people speak of a parent’s kindness, integrity, and the children who carry their values forward. The ache remains, but something in you knows the life was not wasted.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: राम बिरहँ तजि तनु छनभंगू। भूप सोच कर कवन प्रसंगू॥ राम लखन सिय बिनु पग पनहीं। करि मुनि बेष फिरहिं बन बनहीं ॥
translation: फिर जिन्होंने श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विरह में अपने क्षणभंगुर शरीर को त्याग दिया, ऐसे राजा के लिए सोच करने का कौन प्रसंग है? (सोच इसी बात का है कि) श्री रामजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी पैरों में बिना जूती के मुनियों का वेष बनाए वन-वन में फिरते हैं ॥
english_translation: What grief is there to feel for a king who gave up his fragile body in separation from Ram? The real sorrow is that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita wander from forest to forest in the dress of ascetics, without shoes.
essence: The deepest grief is not death, but Ram's exile.
simple_meaning: A king's death is not the real cause for grief, because life is fragile. The deeper sorrow is that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are living in exile, barefoot and dressed like sages.
insight: It teaches you to measure pain by separation from dharma and love, not by the mere ending of a body.
modern_relevance: You miss a funeral and everyone speaks about the loss, but your mind keeps going to the child living far from home, alone and barefoot. This verse teaches you where the deepest sorrow actually lives.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अजिन बसन फल असन महि सयन डासि कुस पात। बसि तरु तर नित सहत हिम आतप बरषा बात ॥
translation: वे वल्कल वस्त्र पहनते हैं, फलों का भोजन करते हैं, पृथ्वी पर कुश और पत्ते बिछाकर सोते हैं और वृक्षों के नीचे निवास करके नित्य सर्दी, गर्मी, वर्षा और हवा सहते हैं। 211॥
english_translation: They wear bark garments, eat fruits, sleep on the ground spread with kusa grass and leaves, and live beneath trees, enduring cold, heat, rain, and wind every day.
essence: Love can make hardship feel bearable.
simple_meaning: The exiled ones live like forest ascetics: simple clothes, simple food, rough sleep, and daily endurance of weather.
insight: It shifts attention from missing comfort to bearing hardship with dignity.
modern_relevance: You unpack a thin mattress in a cold cabin after choosing to stay with someone you love through a difficult season. Comfort is gone, but the choice is clear.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि दुख दाहँ दहइ दिन छाती। भूख न बासर नीद न राती॥ एहि कुरोग कर औषधु नाहीं। सोधेउँ सकल बिस्व मन माहीं ॥
translation: इसी दुःख की जलन से निरंतर मेरी छाती जलती रहती है। मुझे न दिन में भूख लगती है, न रात को नींद आती है। मैंने मन ही मन समस्त विश्व को खोज डाला, पर इस कुरोग की औषध कहीं नहीं है ॥
english_translation: The fire of this sorrow burns my chest day and night. I feel no hunger by day, no sleep by night. I searched the whole world in my mind, but no medicine exists for this illness.
essence: Some grief cannot be cured; it must be borne.
simple_meaning: This grief is so intense that it destroys appetite and sleep. Even after searching everywhere, no remedy can be found for it.
insight: It shifts you from trying to solve every sorrow to meeting some pain with endurance and acceptance.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after a breakup, hoping for one message that will make the ache stop. But some losses do not respond to solutions; they ask for patience and honesty.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मातु कुमत बढ़ई अघ मूला। तेहिं हमार हित कीन्ह बँसूला॥ कलि कुकाठ कर कीन्ह कुजंत्रू। गाड़ि अवधि पढ़ि कठिन कुमंत्रू ॥
translation: माता का कुमत (बुरा विचार) पापों का मूल बढ़ई है। उसने हमारे हित का बसूला बनाया। उससे कलह रूपी कुकाठ का कुयंत्र बनाया और चौदह वर्ष की अवधि रूपी कठिन कुमंत्र पढ़कर उस यंत्र को गाड़ दिया। (यहाँ माता का कुविचार बढ़ई है, भरत को राज्य बसूला है, राम का वनवास कुयंत्र है और चौदह वर्ष की अवधि कुमंत्र है) ॥
english_translation: A mother's wrong-mindedness became the root of sin. She made an axe for our welfare. She forged a crooked device of quarrel, and by reading the harsh spell of fourteen years, she buried it in place.
essence: Wrong intention can turn even help into harm.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi's wrong choice has turned into the source of suffering. What was meant to help has become the tool that cut the family apart and sent Ram into exile.
insight: It shows how one corrupt intention can turn a protective plan into a weapon.
modern_relevance: A family argument starts with one sharp sentence at dinner, and suddenly everyone is choosing sides. Later, you can trace the whole fracture back to that one twisted thought.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: मोहि लगि यहु कुठाटु तेहिं ठाटा। घालेसि सब जगु बारहबाटा॥ मिटइ कुजोगु राम फिरि आएँ। बसइ अवध नहिं आन उपाएँ ॥
translation: मेरे लिए उसने यह सारा कुठाट (बुरा साज) रचा और सारे जगत को बारहबाट (छिन्न-भिन्न) करके नष्ट कर डाला। यह कुयोग श्री रामचन्द्रजी के लौट आने पर ही मिट सकता है और तभी अयोध्या बस सकती है, दूसरे किसी उपाय से नहीं ॥
english_translation: He set this whole trap for me and shattered the world into pieces. This bad alignment can end only when Ram returns, and Ayodhya can be settled by no other means.
essence: Only Ram's return can heal what was broken.
simple_meaning: Bharat says the whole disaster came from a bad scheme, and only Ram's return can restore Ayodhya. No other fix will work.
insight: It shifts you from looking for quick fixes to recognising that some situations need restoration, not adjustment.
modern_relevance: You can rearrange the furniture, change the schedule, and call it progress — but the house still feels wrong after the person who held it together is gone.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: भरत बचन सुनि मुनि सुखु पाई। सबहिं कीन्हि बहु भाँति बड़ाई॥ तात करहु जनि सोचु बिसेषी। सब दुखु मिटिहि राम पग देखी ॥
translation: भरतजी के वचन सुनकर मुनि ने सुख पाया और सभी ने उनकी बहुत प्रकार से बड़ाई की। (मुनि ने कहा-) हे तात! अधिक सोच मत करो। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों का दर्शन करते ही सारा दुःख मिट जाएगा ॥
english_translation: Hearing Bharat's words, the sage felt joy, and everyone praised him in many ways. The sage said, "Dear child, do not grieve so much. Seeing Ram's feet will end all sorrow."
essence: Grief ends when you reach Ram, not when you keep thinking.
simple_meaning: Bharat's words comfort the sage, and the sage tells him not to worry so much. Seeing Ram will end all sorrow.
insight: It shifts attention from mental rumination to the healing power of direct presence.
modern_relevance: You have replayed the same painful conversation all night, trying to make peace with what happened. Sometimes the mind cannot untangle grief — but one real meeting, one true presence, can change everything.
speaker: Muni Bharadvaja

verse_text: करि प्रबोधु मुनिबर कहेउ अतिथि पेमप्रिय होहु। कंद मूल फल फूल हम देहिं लेहु करि छोहु ॥
translation: इस प्रकार मुनिश्रेष्ठ भारद्वाजजी ने उनका समाधान करके कहा- अब आप लोग हमारे प्रेम प्रिय अतिथि बनिए और कृपा करके कंद-मूल, फल-फूल जो कुछ हम दें, स्वीकार कीजिए ॥
english_translation: After giving this reassurance, the great sage said, 'Become our dear guests. Please accept whatever roots, fruits, and flowers we offer.'
essence: Love turns even simple food into a gift.
simple_meaning: Bharadwaj reassures the guests warmly and invites them to accept the simple food offered with affection.
insight: It shifts attention from status and formality to warmth, welcome, and shared human care.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a friend’s home exhausted, apologizing for the trouble, and they smile and say, “Just eat what we have.” That ease is Bharadwaj’s grace.
speaker: Bharadwaj

verse_text: सुनि मुनि बचन भरत हियँ सोचू। भयउ कुअवसर कठिन सँकोचू॥ जानि गुरुइ गुर गिरा बहोरी। चरन बंदि बोले कर जोरी ॥
translation: मुनि के वचन सुनकर भरत के हृदय में सोच हुआ कि यह बेमौके बड़ा बेढब संकोच आ पड़ा! फिर गुरुजनों की वाणी को महत्वपूर्ण (आदरणीय) समझकर, चरणों की वंदना करके हाथ जोड़कर बोले- ॥
english_translation: Hearing the sage's words, Bharata felt a stir of worry in his heart: this awkward hesitation had come at the wrong time. Then, remembering the elders' words as weighty and worthy of respect, he bowed at their feet and spoke with joined hands.
essence: Hesitation yields to humility when you remember what deserves respect.
simple_meaning: Bharata feels awkward and worried, but he still respects the elders' words, bows to them, and speaks humbly with folded hands.
insight: It teaches you to let reverence guide your response even when the moment feels strained.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a tense family argument, and every sentence feels too sharp. Bharata shows the way through: notice the discomfort, honor the people in front of you, and speak only after bowing inwardly.
speaker: Bharata

verse_text: सिर धरि आयसु करिअ तुम्हारा। परम धरम यहु नाथ हमारा॥ भरत बचन मुनिबर मन भाए। सुचि सेवक सिष निकट बोलाए ॥
translation: हे नाथ! आपकी आज्ञा को सिर चढ़ाकर उसका पालन करना, यह हमारा परम धर्म है। भरतजी के ये वचन मुनिश्रेष्ठ के मन को अच्छे लगे। उन्होंने विश्वासपात्र सेवकों और शिष्यों को पास बुलाया ॥
english_translation: Bearing your command on my head and obeying it is our highest duty, O Lord. Bharata's words pleased the sage's mind, and he called his trusted servants and students near.
essence: When duty is loved, obedience becomes joy.
simple_meaning: Bharat says that obeying his lord's command is his highest duty. The sage is pleased by this humility and calls his helpers closer.
insight: It shifts action from self-will to faithful response.
modern_relevance: You get a message from someone you deeply respect, and you stop making it about your preference. You do what needs doing because the relationship and the promise matter more than your convenience.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: चाहिअ कीन्हि भरत पहुनाई। कंद मूल फल आनहु जाई। भलेहिं नाथ कहि तिन्ह सिर नाए। प्रमुदित निज निज काज सिधाए ॥
translation: (और कहा कि) भरत की पहुनाई करनी चाहिए। जाकर कंद, मूल और फल लाओ। उन्होंने 'हे नाथ! बहुत अच्छा' कहकर सिर नवाया और तब वे बड़े आनंदित होकर अपने-अपने काम को चल दिए ॥
english_translation: And he said, "Bharat must be welcomed properly. Go and bring roots, bulbs, and fruits." They bowed their heads and said, "Very well, lord," and then joyfully went off to do their own tasks.
essence: True hospitality begins with simple, sincere service.
simple_meaning: Bharat is to be honored as a guest, so the sages send for simple forest food and then return happily to their work.
insight: It teaches you that honoring someone can be practical, not grand.
modern_relevance: A guest shows up at your door with no warning, and you quietly start chopping fruit, boiling tea, and clearing a place to sit. Care often begins in the simplest actions.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: मुनिहि सोच पाहुन बड़ नेवता। तसि पूजा चाहिअ जस देवता॥ सुनि रिधि सिधि अनिमादिक आईं। आयसु होइ सो करहिं गोसाईं ॥
translation: मुनि को चिंता हुई कि हमने बहुत बड़े मेहमान को न्योता है। अब जैसा देवता हो, वैसी ही उसकी पूजा भी होनी चाहिए। यह सुनकर ऋद्धियाँ और अणिमादि सिद्धियाँ आ गईं (और बोलीं-) हे गोसाईं! जो आपकी आज्ञा हो सो हम करें ॥
english_translation: The sage felt anxious: we have invited a very great guest. Such worship should match such a deity. Hearing this, the powers of attainment came and said, "O Lord, whatever you command, we will do."
essence: Great devotion makes even attainments become servants.
simple_meaning: The sage realizes that a great guest deserves a fitting welcome. The powers of attainment then arrive and offer to obey whatever command is given.
insight: It shifts attention from casual welcome to reverent service that rises to the dignity of the guest.
modern_relevance: A friend you deeply respect walks into your home after months away, and suddenly every small gesture matters. You want your welcome to match the love you feel.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम बिरह ब्याकुल भरतु सानुज सहित समाज। पहुनाई करि हरहु श्रम कहा मुदित मुनिराज ॥
translation: मुनिराज ने प्रसन्न होकर कहा- छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न और समाज सहित भरतजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विरह में व्याकुल हैं, इनकी पहुनाई (आतिथ्य सत्कार) करके इनके श्रम को दूर करो ॥
english_translation: Bharat, along with his younger brother and the whole company, is restless in separation from Ram. O sage-king, honor them as guests and remove their fatigue.
essence: Longing deserves hospitality, not judgment.
simple_meaning: Bharat and his companions are worn out by longing for Ram, so the sage asks that they be welcomed and rested.
insight: It shifts attention from solving sorrow to receiving the sorrowful with care.
modern_relevance: You come home after a hard day, and the person who loves you most notices before you speak. Sometimes the kindest response is not advice, but welcome.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: रिधि सिधि सिर धरि मुनिबर बानी। बड़भागिनि आपुहि अनुमानी॥ कहहिं परसपर सिधि समुदाई। अतुलित अतिथि राम लघु भाई ॥
translation: ऋद्धि-सिद्धि ने मुनिराज की आज्ञा को सिर चढ़ाकर अपने को बड़भागिनी समझा। सब सिद्धियाँ आपस में कहने लगीं- श्री रामचन्द्रजी के छोटे भाई भरत ऐसे अतिथि हैं, जिनकी तुलना में कोई नहीं आ सकता ॥
english_translation: Holding the sage's words on their heads, the Riddhis and Siddhis felt blessed. The whole company said among themselves, 'There is no guest equal to Ram's younger brother Bharat.'
essence: Devotion makes even a guest feel unmatched.
simple_meaning: The divine powers feel honored to serve Bharat and call him an unmatched guest, because he comes in Ram's name and with Ram in his heart.
insight: It shifts attention from social status to the sacredness of service.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at your door who never asks for special treatment, yet everyone in the room feels the quiet weight of their character. Respect follows devotion faster than rank.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि पद बंदि करिअ सोइ आजू। होइ सुखी सब राज समाजू॥ अस कहि रचेउ रुचिर गृह नाना। जेहि बिलोकि बिलखाहिं बिमाना ॥
translation: अतः मुनि के चरणों की वंदना करके आज वही करना चाहिए, जिससे सारा राज-समाज सुखी हो। ऐसा कहकर उन्होंने बहुत से सुंदर घर बनाए, जिन्हें देखकर विमान भी विलखते हैं (लजा जाते हैं) ॥
english_translation: Therefore, today one should bow to the sage's feet and do what makes the whole royal assembly happy. Saying this, they built many beautiful houses, so lovely that even celestial vehicles would feel ashamed seeing them.
essence: True welcome begins with humility and careful preparation.
simple_meaning: Honor the sage first, then do what brings peace to everyone around you. The homes they built were so beautiful that even heavenly chariots would feel outdone.
insight: It shifts attention from status to service: make the setting worthy of the people in it.
modern_relevance: You clean the house before guests arrive, not to impress them, but to make them feel cared for. Small acts of preparation can turn an ordinary welcome into real hospitality.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भोग बिभूति भूरि भरि राखे। देखत जिन्हहि अमर अभिलाषे॥ दासीं दास साजु सब लीन्हें। जोगवत रहहिं मनहि मनु दीन्हें ॥
translation: उन घरों में बहुत से भोग (इन्द्रियों के विषय) और ऐश्वर्य (ठाट-बाट) का सामान भरकर रख दिया, जिन्हें देखकर देवता भी ललचा गए। दासी-दास सब प्रकार की सामग्री लिए हुए मन लगाकर उनके मनों को देखते रहते हैं (अर्थात उनके मन की रुचि के अनुसार करते रहते हैं) ॥
english_translation: They filled the houses with abundant pleasures and luxuries, so tempting that even the immortals would long for them. Servants stood ready with every arrangement, watching and serving according to each mind's wish.
essence: True welcome anticipates every need before it is spoken.
simple_meaning: The houses were stocked with lavish comforts, and servants were ready to meet every wish. It is a scene of complete, welcoming hospitality.
insight: It shows devotion expressed as practical attentiveness, where service adapts itself to another's mind.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home where every detail was handled before you arrived — the food, the room, the timing. Someone cared enough to notice what would make you comfortable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब समाजु सजि सिधि पल माहीं। जे सुख सुरपुर सपनेहुँ नाहीं॥ प्रथमहिं बास दिए सब केही। सुंदर सुखद जथा रुचि जेही ॥
translation: जो सुख के सामान स्वर्ग में भी स्वप्न में भी नहीं हैं, ऐसे सब सामान सिद्धियों ने पल भर में सजा दिए। पहले तो उन्होंने सब किसी को, जिसकी जैसी रुचि थी, वैसे ही, सुंदर सुखदायक निवास स्थान दिए ॥
english_translation: In a moment, the whole assembly was arranged with comforts that even heaven cannot match in dreams. First, everyone was given a beautiful, pleasant dwelling suited to each person's liking.
essence: True welcome makes room for every person exactly as needed.
simple_meaning: A moment later, everyone had been given a beautiful place to stay, each one arranged according to personal taste, with comforts beyond ordinary imagination.
insight: It shifts attention from grandeur to thoughtful care for each person.
modern_relevance: You arrive exhausted at a friend’s home after a hard journey, and they have already set out food, blankets, and a quiet room just for you. Care like that changes everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरि सपरिजन भरत कहुँ रिषि अस आयसु दीन्ह। बिधि बिसमय दायकु बिभव मुनिबर तपबल कीन्ह ॥
translation: और फिर कुटुम्ब सहित भरतजी को दिए, क्योंकि ऋषि भारद्वाजजी ने ऐसी ही आज्ञा दे रखी थी। (भरतजी चाहते थे कि उनके सब संगियों को आराम मिले, इसलिए उनके मन की बात जानकर मुनि ने पहले उन लोगों को स्थान देकर पीछे सपरिवार भरतजी को स्थान देने के लिए आज्ञा दी थी।) मुनि श्रेष्ठ ने तपोबल से ब्रह्मा को भी चकित कर देने वाला वैभव रच दिया ॥
english_translation: Then, for Bharat and his companions, the sage gave such an order. By the power of his austerity, the best of sages created a splendor that astonished even Brahma.
essence: A trained inner power can arrange comfort that ordinary means cannot.
simple_meaning: Bharat and his companions were given a separate, fitting place. Bharadwaj's austerity created a wonder-filled display of comfort and splendor.
insight: It shows how disciplined inner power can create ease for others without effort or display.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a retreat house after a long drive, and every room is already prepared without fuss. That quiet care feels almost impossible — like someone had seen your needs before you spoke.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि प्रभाउ जब भरत बिलोका। सब लघु लगे लोकपति लोका॥ सुख समाजु नहिं जाइ बखानी। देखत बिरति बिसारहिं ग्यानी ॥
translation: जब भरतजी ने मुनि के प्रभाव को देखा, तो उसके सामने उन्हें (इन्द्र, वरुण, यम, कुबेर आदि) सभी लोकपालों के लोक तुच्छ जान पड़े। सुख की सामग्री का वर्णन नहीं हो सकता, जिसे देखकर ज्ञानी लोग भी वैराग्य भूल जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: When Bharat saw the power of the sage, even the realms of the world-lords seemed small. The wealth and comforts cannot be described; even the wise forget non-attachment when they see it.
essence: Great comfort can make even clear-minded people forget restraint.
simple_meaning: Bharat sees the sage's power and the splendor around him, and even wise people can lose their detachment in such abundance.
insight: It shows how atmosphere can overpower resolve and make detachment harder to hold.
modern_relevance: You walk into a beautifully curated retreat, and your resolve melts before the soft lights, food, and quiet luxury. Even your best intentions can blur when comfort is everywhere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आसन सयन सुबसन बिताना। बन बाटिका बिहग मृग नाना॥ सुरभि फूल फल अमिअ समाना। बिमल जलासय बिबिध बिधाना ॥
translation: आसन, सेज, सुंदर वस्त्र, चँदोवे, वन, बगीचे, भाँति-भाँति के पक्षी और पशु, सुगंधित फूल और अमृत के समान स्वादिष्ट फल, अनेकों प्रकार के (तालाब, कुएँ, बावली आदि) निर्मल जलाशय, ॥
english_translation: There were seats, beds, fine clothes, canopies, groves, many birds and animals, fragrant flowers, fruits sweet as nectar, and many kinds of clear water places.
essence: True welcome makes even simple things feel abundant.
simple_meaning: The place was beautifully prepared with comforts, gardens, birds, animals, flowers, fruits, and clean water sources.
insight: It shifts attention from luxury as display to hospitality as spiritual power.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home where the room is already ready for you: clean sheets, fresh fruit, water, and quiet. The care itself makes you soften before anyone speaks.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: असन पान सुचि अमिअ अमी से। देखि लोग सकुचात जमी से॥ सुर सुरभी सुरतरु सबही कें। लखि अभिलाषु सुरेस सची कें ॥
translation: तथा अमृत के भी अमृत-सरीखे पवित्र खान-पान के पदार्थ थे, जिन्हें देखकर सब लोग संयमी पुरुषों (विरक्त मुनियों) की भाँति सकुचा रहे हैं। सभी के डेरों में (मनोवांछित वस्तु देने वाले) कामधेनु और कल्पवृक्ष हैं, जिन्हें देखकर इन्द्र और इन्द्राणी को भी अभिलाषा होती है (उनका भी मन ललचा जाता है) ॥
english_translation: There were pure foods and drinks, nectar-like and even more delightful than nectar. Everyone felt shy, as if they were renunciates. Every home had wish-fulfilling cows and trees, and even Indra and Indrani would long for them.
essence: True abundance makes even desire feel out of place.
simple_meaning: The scene describes a place of effortless abundance, where even heavenly luxuries seem ordinary and people feel humbled by the richness around them.
insight: It shifts attention from wanting more to recognising fullness already present.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home where everything is already set, clean, and generous. There is nothing to grab, nothing to prove. Your hunger quiets before you even speak.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रितु बसंत बह त्रिबिध बयारी। सब कहँ सुलभ पदारथ चारी॥ स्रक चंदन बनितादिक भोगा। देखि हरष बिसमय बस लोगा ॥
translation: वसन्त ऋतु है। शीतल, मंद, सुगंध तीन प्रकार की हवा बह रही है। सभी को (धर्म, अर्थ, काम और मोक्ष) चारों पदार्थ सुलभ हैं। माला, चंदन, स्त्री आदि भोगों को देखकर सब लोग हर्ष और विषाद के वश हो रहे हैं। (हर्ष तो भोग सामग्रियों को और मुनि के तप प्रभाव को देखकर होता है और विषाद इस बात से होता है कि श्री राम के वियोग में नियम-व्रत से रहने वाले हम लोग भोग-विलास में क्यों आ फँसे, कहीं इनमें आसक्त होकर हमारा मन नियम-व्रतों को न त्याग दे) ॥
english_translation: It is springtime. Three kinds of cool, gentle, fragrant breezes are blowing. The four aims of life are easy to find for everyone. Seeing garlands, sandalwood, and pleasures like women, people are filled with both joy and unease.
essence: Pleasure is not the real test; your response to it is.
simple_meaning: Spring has arrived, and everything pleasant is within reach. But the sight of pleasure also stirs mixed feelings in people, because comfort can awaken both delight and doubt.
insight: It shifts attention from outer comfort to the mind's response to comfort.
modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall full of music, perfume, and laughter, but your mind tightens because you promised yourself not to get carried away. Plenty can feel like pressure when you are trying to stay steady.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: संपति चकई भरतु चक मुनि आयस खेलवार। तेहि निसि आश्रम पिंजराँ राखे भा भिनुसार ॥
translation: सम्पत्ति (भोग-विलास की सामग्री) चकवी है और भरतजी चकवा हैं और मुनि की आज्ञा खेल है, जिसने उस रात को आश्रम रूपी पिंजड़े में दोनों को बंद कर रखा और ऐसे ही सबेरा हो गया। (जैसे किसी बहेलिए के द्वारा एक पिंजड़े में रखे जाने पर भी चकवी-चकवे का रात को संयोग नहीं होता, वैसे ही भारद्वाजजी की आज्ञा से रात भर भोग सामग्रियों के साथ रहने पर भी भरतजी ने मन से भी उनका स्पर्श तक नहीं किया।) ॥
english_translation: Wealth was like a female chakwa bird, Bharat like the male chakwa, and the sage's command was the game. That night, the hermitage-cage held them both until dawn.
essence: True non-attachment stays untouched even in the middle of plenty.
simple_meaning: Bharat stayed among comforts, but his mind remained untouched. The verse compares him to a bird that stays near its mate without yielding to desire.
insight: It trains the mind to remain close to pleasure without becoming captive to it.
modern_relevance: You are at a lavish wedding, everyone urging one more indulgence, one more drink, one more purchase. You can smile, stay courteous, and still not let the night own you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कीन्ह निमज्जनु तीरथराजा। नाई मुनिहि सिरु सहित समाजा। रिषि आयसु असीस सिर राखी। करि दंडवत बिनय बहु भाषी ॥
translation: (प्रातःकाल) भरतजी ने तीर्थराज में स्नान किया और समाज सहित मुनि को सिर नवाकर और ऋषि की आज्ञा तथा आशीर्वाद को सिर चढ़ाकर दण्डवत् करके बहुत विनती की ॥
english_translation: At dawn, Bharata bathed at the king of pilgrimages, bowed his head with the sages, placed the sage's command and blessings above his own head, prostrated himself, and spoke many humble words.
essence: True service starts by lowering your head before guidance.
simple_meaning: Bharata bathes, bows to the sage, honors the sage's command and blessings, and humbly asks for guidance.
insight: It teaches you to begin a hard journey by honoring guidance, not asserting control.
modern_relevance: Before a difficult family conversation, you pause, take a breath, and listen fully instead of defending yourself. That quiet respect can change the whole direction of the day.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पथ गति कुसल साथ सब लीन्हें। चले चित्रकूटहिं चितु दीन्हें॥ रामसखा कर दीन्हें लागू। चलत देह धरि जनु अनुरागू ॥
translation: तदनन्तर रास्ते की पहचान रखने वाले लोगों (कुशल पथप्रदर्शकों) के साथ सब लोगों को लिए हुए भरतजी त्रिकूट में चित्त लगाए चले। भरतजी रामसखा गुह के हाथ में हाथ दिए हुए ऐसे जा रहे हैं, मानो साक्षात् प्रेम ही शरीर धारण किए हुए हो ॥
english_translation: With skilled guides leading the way, they all set out, hearts fixed on Chitrakoot. Holding Ram's friend Guha by the hand, Bharat walked as if love itself had taken a body.
essence: Love becomes visible when it walks beside someone.
simple_meaning: Bharat and the group travel toward Chitrakoot with careful guides. Bharat holds Guha's hand, and his whole journey feels like love in human form.
insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to visible companionship and steady movement toward the beloved.
modern_relevance: You leave at dawn with a friend whose family is hurting, and you stay close without needing to fix anything. Sometimes loyalty is just walking beside someone all the way there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नहिं पद त्रान सीस नहिं छाया। पेमु नेमु ब्रतु धरमु अमाया॥ लखन राम सिय पंथ कहानी। पूँछत सखहि कहत मृदु बानी ॥
translation: न तो उनके पैरों में जूते हैं और न सिर पर छाया है, उनका प्रेम नियम, व्रत और धर्म निष्कपट (सच्चा) है। वे सखा निषादराज से लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामचंद्रजी और सीताजी के रास्ते की बातें पूछते हैं और वह कोमल वाणी से कहता है ॥
english_translation: They have no shoes on their feet and no shade over their heads. Their love, vows, and righteousness are utterly sincere. They ask the friendly guide about the path of Lakshman, Ram, and Sita, and he speaks gently.
essence: Love makes hardship feel like the only honest way to travel.
simple_meaning: Bharat and his companions travel humbly, with no comfort or display, and their devotion is genuine. They ask about the path taken by Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, and receive gentle guidance.
insight: It shifts attention from outward comfort to inward sincerity in service.
modern_relevance: You walk into a place bareheaded, tired, and quiet, only wanting directions to someone you love. Even your simplest questions carry your loyalty.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम बास थल बिटप बिलोकें। उर अनुराग रहत नहिं रोकें॥ देखि दसा सुर बरिसहिं फूला। भइ मृदु महि मगु मंगल मूला ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी के ठहरने की जगहों और वृक्षों को देखकर उनके हृदय में प्रेम रोके नहीं रुकता। भरतजी की यह दशा देखकर देवता फूल बरसाने लगे। पृथ्वी कोमल हो गई और मार्ग मंगल का मूल बन गया ॥
english_translation: Seeing the places where Ram had stayed and the trees along the way, Bharat's love could not be held back. Seeing his condition, the gods showered flowers. The earth became soft, and the road itself turned into a source of blessing.
essence: Love makes even a road sacred.
simple_meaning: Bharat sees the places connected with Ram and cannot contain his love. His devotion is so moving that even the world around him seems blessed.
insight: It shows how devotion can sanctify even a road, turning grief and longing into blessing.
modern_relevance: You pass the café where someone once sat across from you, and your chest tightens. A place can hold love so strongly that even ordinary streets feel charged with memory.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: किएँ जाहिं छाया जलद सुखद बहइ बर बात। तस मगु भयउ न राम कहँ जस भा भरतहि जात ॥
translation: बादल छाया किए जा रहे हैं, सुख देने वाली सुंदर हवा बह रही है। भरतजी के जाते समय मार्ग जैसा सुखदायक हुआ, वैसा श्री रामचंद्रजी को भी नहीं हुआ था ॥
english_translation: The clouds gave shade and a pleasant breeze blew. The road for Bharat became as pleasant as it had never been for Ram.
essence: A devoted heart makes even the road feel blessed.
simple_meaning: Nature itself seems to welcome Bharat’s journey. The road becomes gentle and blessed, as if the world is honoring his devotion.
insight: It shifts attention from the physical journey to the moral beauty of the one making it.
modern_relevance: You leave home before sunrise to make a hard trip for someone you love, and even the cold air feels kind. Your heart changes the road.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जड़ चेतन मग जीव घनेरे। जे चितए प्रभु जिन्ह प्रभु हेरे॥ ते सब भए परम पद जोगू। भरत दरस मेटा भव रोगू ॥
translation: रास्ते में असंख्य जड़-चेतन जीव थे। उनमें से जिनको प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी ने देखा, अथवा जिन्होंने प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी को देखा, वे सब (उसी समय) परमपद के अधिकारी हो गए, परन्तु अब भरतजी के दर्शन ने तो उनका भव (जन्म-मरण) रूपी रोग मिटा ही दिया। (श्री रामदर्शन से तो वे परमपद के अधिकारी ही हुए थे, परन्तु भरत दर्शन से उन्हें वह परमपद प्राप्त हो गया) ॥
english_translation: Countless living beings on the road were touched by the sight of Ram. Those who saw him, or whom he saw, reached the highest state. Bharat's sight removed the sickness of rebirth itself.
essence: Pure presence can free others without a word.
simple_meaning: Ram's sight blesses every being he meets, and Bharat's presence is so pure that it also frees others from the pain of repeated birth.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary seeing to the transforming power of a pure presence.
modern_relevance: You enter a room already carrying stress, and one person’s steady kindness changes the whole atmosphere. Some people do not just notice you — they make life feel less heavy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: यह बड़ि बात भरत कइ नाहीं। सुमिरत जिनहि रामु मन माहीं॥ बारक राम कहत जग जेऊ। होत तरन तारन नर तेऊ ॥
translation: भरतजी के लिए यह कोई बड़ी बात नहीं है, जिन्हें श्री रामजी स्वयं अपने मन में स्मरण करते रहते हैं। जगत् में जो भी मनुष्य एक बार 'राम' कह लेते हैं, वे भी तरने-तारने वाले हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: This is no great matter for Bharat. Anyone whom Ram remembers in his mind is already lifted across. In the world, whoever even once says 'Ram' becomes a boat that carries others across too.
essence: Ram's remembrance makes ordinary people into carriers of rescue.
simple_meaning: Being remembered by Ram is no small thing. Even one sincere utterance of his name can lift a person across life's struggle and help others too.
insight: It shifts attention from proving yourself to resting in remembrance, and from self-effort to the power of holy naming.
modern_relevance: You open your phone and see one message from someone you deeply love — and suddenly the whole day feels different. Being held in someone's heart can change everything, and one sacred name can steady you the same way.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भरतु राम प्रिय पुनि लघु भ्राता। कस न होइ मगु मंगलदाता॥ सिद्ध साधु मुनिबर अस कहहीं। भरतहि निरखि हरषु हियँ लहहीं ॥
translation: फिर भरतजी तो श्री रामचंद्रजी के प्यारे तथा उनके छोटे भाई ठहरे। तब भला उनके लिए मार्ग मंगल (सुख) दायक कैसे न हो? सिद्ध, साधु और श्रेष्ठ मुनि ऐसा कह रहे हैं और भरतजी को देखकर हृदय में हर्ष लाभ करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Bharat is dear to Ram and is his younger brother. How could the road not become auspicious for him? Siddhas, saints, and great sages say this, and they feel joy in their hearts when they see Bharat.
essence: Belovedness itself makes the road auspicious.
simple_meaning: Bharat is so dear to Ram that even his path becomes blessed. Saints and sages rejoice just by seeing him.
insight: It shifts attention from status to relationship: closeness to Ram makes ordinary movement feel sacred.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after helping someone you love through a hard week. Nothing about the furniture changed, but the whole place feels lighter. Bharat’s presence works like that.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि प्रभाउ सुरेसहि सोचू। जगु भल भलेहि पोच कहुँ पोचू॥ गुर सन कहेउ करिअ प्रभु सोई। रामहि भरतहि भेंट न होई ॥
translation: भरतजी के (इस प्रेम के) प्रभाव को देखकर देवराज इन्द्र को सोच हो गया (कि कहीं इनके प्रेमवश श्री रामजी लौट न जाएँ और हमारा बना-बनाया काम बिगड़ जाए)। संसार भले के लिए भला और बुरे के लिए बुरा है (मनुष्य जैसा आप होता है जगत् उसे वैसा ही दिखता है)। उसने गुरु बृहस्पतिजी से कहा- हे प्रभो! वही उपाय कीजिए जिससे श्री रामचंद्रजी और भरतजी की भेंट ही न हो ॥
english_translation: Seeing the power of Bharat's love, Indra grew anxious. The world seems good to the good and bad to the bad. He told Brihaspati, 'Do whatever is needed so Ram and Bharat do not meet.'
essence: Love so pure can make control itself feel unsafe.
simple_meaning: Bharat's love is so powerful that even Indra worries. He fears Ram and Bharat meeting, because their love could overturn the situation.
insight: It shows that sincere devotion can disturb worldly arrangements and expose how fragile control really is.
modern_relevance: You finally see two people about to reconcile after a long silence, and someone panics because the truth might undo their control. Love can be more disruptive than power.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामु सँकोची प्रेम बस भरत सप्रेम पयोधि। बनी बात बेगरन चहति करिअ जतनु छलु सोधि ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी संकोची और प्रेम के वश हैं और भरतजी प्रेम के समुद्र हैं। बनी-बनाई बात बिगड़ना चाहती है, इसलिए कुछ छल ढूँढकर इसका उपाय कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Ram is modest and moved by love, while Bharat is a sea of love. The settled matter seems ready to break, so find some trick and a way to set it right.
essence: Love can create peace, and peace can still be fragile.
simple_meaning: Ram is gentle and moved by love, while Bharat is pure love itself. Because the situation is delicate, careful action is needed to keep things from falling apart.
insight: It teaches you to treat a hard-won harmony as something fragile and worth protecting with skill.
modern_relevance: You finally got two estranged siblings to sit in the same room after years of silence. Everyone can feel how fragile it is. One careless sentence could undo weeks of healing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बचन सुनत सुरगुरु मुसुकाने। सहसनयन बिनु लोचन जाने॥ मायापति सेवक सन माया। करइ त उलटि परइ सुरराया ॥
translation: इंद्र के वचन सुनते ही देवगुरु बृहस्पतिजी मुस्कुराए। उन्होंने हजार नेत्रों वाले इंद्र को (ज्ञान रूपी) नेत्रोंरहित (मूर्ख) समझा और कहा- हे देवराज! माया के स्वामी श्री रामचंद्रजी के सेवक के साथ कोई माया करता है तो वह उलटकर अपने ही ऊपर आ पड़ती है ॥
english_translation: At Indra's words, the teacher of the gods smiled. He saw the thousand-eyed king as blind without true sight: anyone who tries trickery against the servant of the master of illusion has that trickery turn back on himself.
essence: What you use against Ram's servant turns back on you.
simple_meaning: Brihaspati smiles at Indra's plan and warns him that any trick used against Ram's devotee will rebound on the trickster.
insight: It shifts the mind from strategic control to reverence for what cannot be manipulated.
modern_relevance: You try to manipulate a loyal friend into changing their mind, and the whole plan collapses in your own hands. Pressure aimed at devotion often reveals your own weakness.
speaker: Brihaspati

verse_text: तब किछु कीन्ह राम रुख जानी। अब कुचालि करि होइहि हानी। सुनु सुरेस रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। निज अपराध रिसाहिं न काऊ ॥
translation: उस समय (पिछली बार) तो श्री रामचंद्रजी का रुख जानकर कुछ किया था, परन्तु इस समय कुचाल करने से हानि ही होगी। हे देवराज! श्री रघुनाथजी का स्वभाव सुनो, वे अपने प्रति किए हुए अपराध से कभी रुष्ट नहीं होते ॥
english_translation: At one time, knowing Ram's mood, some action was taken. But now, if you resort to trickery, it will only bring harm. Listen, lord of the gods: hear the nature of Raghunath. He is never angered by an offense done against himself.
essence: Ram cannot be manipulated by offense; only deceit brings harm back to you.
simple_meaning: Ram does not get angry when someone harms him personally. Trying to deceive him will only backfire and bring loss.
insight: It shifts attention from protecting your ego to trusting a presence that cannot be shaken by insult.
modern_relevance: You replay a harsh message in your head, ready to defend yourself or strike back. This verse says the deepest strength does not need revenge; it cannot be manipulated by your offense.
speaker: Brahma

verse_text: जो अपराधु भगत कर करई। राम रोष पावक सो जरई॥ लोकहुँ बेद बिदित इतिहासा। यह महिमा जानहिं दुरबासा ॥
translation: पर जो कोई उनके भक्त का अपराध करता है, वह श्री राम की क्रोधाग्नि में जल जाता है। लोक और वेद दोनों में इतिहास (कथा) प्रसिद्ध है। इस महिमा को दुर्वासाजी जानते हैं ॥
english_translation: Anyone who wrongs Ram's devotee is burned by Ram's fire of anger. This story is known in the world and in the Vedas; Durvasa knows this greatness.
essence: Ram's anger rises for anyone who harms his devotee.
simple_meaning: Harming a devoted follower of Ram brings Ram's fierce response. The verse says this is a well-known truth, remembered in tradition and scripture.
insight: It shifts the mind from casual contempt to reverence for those who serve with sincerity.
modern_relevance: You mock someone because they are gentle, faithful, or deeply devoted, thinking no one will answer for it. This verse says that cruelty toward the devoted does not stay hidden forever.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत सरिस को राम सनेही। जगु जप राम रामु जप जेही ॥
translation: सारा जगत् श्री राम को जपता है, वे श्री रामजी जिनको जपते हैं, उन भरतजी के समान श्री रामचंद्रजी का प्रेमी कौन होगा? ॥
english_translation: Who loves Ram like Bharat? The whole world chants Ram, and Ram chants the name of Bharat.
essence: Bharat's devotion is so pure that Ram himself returns it.
simple_meaning: Bharat's love for Ram is so complete that it becomes the standard for devotion. The verse also says Ram holds Bharat in equal affection.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to relationship, showing that true love is recognised and answered.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone who never forgets your kindness. In a world full of noisy affection, this verse honors the bond where care is returned without calculation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मनहुँ न आनिअ अमरपति रघुबर भगत अकाजु। अजसु लोक परलोक दुख दिन दिन सोक समाजु ॥
translation: हे देवराज! रघुकुलश्रेष्ठ श्री रामचंद्रजी के भक्त का काम बिगाड़ने की बात मन में भी न लाइए। ऐसा करने से लोक में अपयश और परलोक में दुःख होगा और शोक का सामान दिनोंदिन बढ़ता ही चला जाएगा ॥
english_translation: O lord of the gods, do not even think of harming the work of Ram's devotee. It brings disgrace in this world, sorrow in the next, and a growing burden of grief day by day.
essence: Hurt Ram's devotee, and sorrow follows you home.
simple_meaning: Do not interfere with the work of Ram's devotee. Doing so brings shame now and sorrow later, and grief keeps increasing.
insight: It teaches you to stop opposing sincere devotion, because resistance to it rebounds as inner and outer pain.
modern_relevance: You try to sabotage someone who is quietly doing the right thing, and it backfires. The damage is not just to them — your own name, mind, and sleep start to unravel.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सुनु सुरेस उपदेसु हमारा। रामहि सेवकु परम पिआरा॥ मानत सुखु सेवक सेवकाईं। सेवक बैर बैरु अधिकाईं ॥
translation: हे देवराज! हमारा उपदेश सुनो। श्री रामजी को अपना सेवक परम प्रिय है। वे अपने सेवक की सेवा से सुख मानते हैं और सेवक के साथ वैर करने से बड़ा भारी वैर मानते हैं ॥
english_translation: Listen, Indra: this is my counsel. Ram is especially dear to a servant. He takes joy in a servant's service, and he counts enmity toward a servant as a great wrong.
essence: Ram is closest to the one who serves him.
simple_meaning: Ram is deeply pleased by the service of his devotee. Helping a devotee brings him joy, and harming a devotee is a serious wrong.
insight: It shifts devotion from a private feeling to a relationship that changes how you act toward others.
modern_relevance: You quietly help someone who can never repay you, and the work itself feels sacred. This verse says such service is seen, honored, and protected.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: जद्यपि सम नहिं राग न रोषू। गहहिं न पाप पूनु गुन दोषू॥ करम प्रधान बिस्व करि राखा। जो जस करइ सो तस फलु चाखा ॥
translation: यद्यपि वे सम हैं- उनमें न राग है, न रोष है और न वे किसी का पाप-पुण्य और गुण-दोष ही ग्रहण करते हैं। उन्होंने विश्व में कर्म को ही प्रधान कर रखा है। जो जैसा करता है, वह वैसा ही फल भोगता है ॥
english_translation: Although they are even-minded, free from attachment and anger, and do not take up anyone's virtue or fault, they have made the world governed by action. Whoever does as they do, tastes that result.
essence: Evenness does not cancel consequence; action still bears its own fruit.
simple_meaning: The divine is beyond attachment, anger, praise, and blame, yet the world still runs on action. What you do returns to you in kind.
insight: It shifts attention from emotional fairness to lawful consequence: what you do matters, even when the higher order is unmoved.
modern_relevance: You can sit in a meeting and stay calm when someone criticises you, but your preparation still shows in the result. The world may not mirror your mood, yet it answers your actions.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तदपि करहिं सम बिषम बिहारा। भगत अभगत हृदय अनुसारा॥ अगनु अलेप अमान एकरस। रामु सगुन भए भगत प्रेम बस ॥
translation: तथापि वे भक्त और अभक्त के हृदय के अनुसार सम और विषम व्यवहार करते हैं (भक्त को प्रेम से गले लगा लेते हैं और अभक्त को मारकर तार देते हैं)। गुणरहित, निर्लेप, मानरहित और सदा एकरस भगवान् श्री राम भक्त के प्रेमवश ही सगुण हुए हैं ॥
english_translation: Still, they behave differently according to the hearts of devotees and non-devotees. Though without form, untouched, self-respecting, and ever one, Ram took form only because of a devotee's love.
essence: Love makes the formless one meet you in form.
simple_meaning: Ram responds differently to devotees and non-devotees, and his own form appears because of a devotee's love.
insight: It shifts devotion from abstract belief to lived relationship: your inner state shapes how presence is experienced.
modern_relevance: You sit in a quiet room after a hard day, and the same prayer feels distant one night and near the next. This verse says the difference is not in Ram's care, but in the heart that calls.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: राम सदा सेवक रुचि राखी। बेद पुरान साधु सुर साखी॥ अस जियँ जानि तजहु कुटिलाई। करहु भरत पद प्रीति सुहाई ॥
translation: श्री रामजी सदा अपने सेवकों (भक्तों) की रुचि रखते आए हैं। वेद, पुराण, साधु और देवता इसके साक्षी हैं। ऐसा हृदय में जानकर कुटिलता छोड़ दो और भरतजी के चरणों में सुंदर प्रीति करो ॥
english_translation: Ram has always favored those who serve him. The Vedas, Puranas, sages, and radiant beings all bear witness. Knowing this in your heart, let go of crookedness and hold lovely love for Bharat.
essence: Love for Ram shows itself as clean loyalty, not cleverness.
simple_meaning: Ram naturally favors those who serve him. Knowing that, drop all duplicity and offer sincere love to Bharat.
insight: It shifts attention from rivalry to sincere service, especially where loyalty is being tested.
modern_relevance: You’re tempted to judge someone who stayed loyal while others chased status. Then you remember: real devotion does not compete. It bows, trusts, and loves cleanly.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: राम भगत परहित निरत पर दुख दुखी दयाल। भगत सिरोमनि भरत तें जनि डरपहु सुरपाल ॥
translation: हे देवराज इंद्र! श्री रामचंद्रजी के भक्त सदा दूसरों के हित में लगे रहते हैं, वे दूसरों के दुःख से दुःखी और दयालु होते हैं। फिर भरतजी तो भक्तों के शिरोमणि हैं, उनसे बिलकुल न डरो ॥
english_translation: Ram's devotees are devoted to others' welfare, pained by others' pain, and full of compassion. Bharata, the best among devotees, is even more beyond fear, O king of the gods.
essence: Devotion shows itself as compassion for other people's pain.
simple_meaning: True devotees care for other people's good, feel their pain, and act with compassion. Bharata is held up as the finest example, so even Indra need not fear him.
insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to outward care and shared suffering.
modern_relevance: Your friend texts at midnight after a breakup, and you stop scrolling to listen. You don't fix everything. You stay present, and their pain matters to you. That's the shape of real devotion here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सत्यसंध प्रभु सुर हितकारी। भरत राम आयस अनुसारी॥ स्वारथ बिबस बिकल तुम्ह होहू। भरत दोसु नहिं राउर मोहू ॥
translation: प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी सत्यप्रतिज्ञ और देवताओं का हित करने वाले हैं और भरतजी श्री रामजी की आज्ञा के अनुसार चलने वाले हैं। तुम व्यर्थ ही स्वार्थ के विशेष वश होकर व्याकुल हो रहे हो। इसमें भरतजी का कोई दोष नहीं, तुम्हारा ही मोह है ॥
english_translation: The Lord is true to His vow and works for the good of the radiant beings. Bharat follows Ram's command. You are only agitated by selfish attachment; Bharat has no fault here. Your delusion is the problem.
essence: True duty is clear; blame often comes from your own attachment.
simple_meaning: Ram stays true to his promise, and Bharat simply follows Ram's command. The real problem is not Bharat's conduct but the speaker's selfish confusion.
insight: It shifts attention from blaming another person's conduct to noticing your own attachment and confusion.
modern_relevance: You blame the coworker who followed the plan exactly, while your own attachment to control keeps burning underneath. The verse asks you to see the real source of the upset.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुनि सुरबर सुरगुर बर बानी। भा प्रमोदु मन मिटी गलानी॥ बरषि प्रसून हरषि सुरराऊ। लगे सराहन भरत सुभाऊ ॥
translation: देवगुरु बृहस्पतिजी की श्रेष्ठ वाणी सुनकर इंद्र के मन में बड़ा आनंद हुआ और उनकी चिंता मिट गई। तब हर्षित होकर देवराज फूल बरसाकर भरतजी के स्वभाव की सराहना करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Hearing the excellent words of the best of the gods and the teacher of the gods, Indra felt great joy and his worry disappeared. Then, delighted, the lord of the gods showered flowers and began praising Bharat's nature.
essence: Bharat's character is so pure it wins praise from heaven itself.
simple_meaning: Indra hears Brihaspati's words, feels relieved, showers flowers, and praises Bharat's noble nature.
insight: It shifts attention from suspicion to recognition of virtue.
modern_relevance: You hear someone defend a person you had misjudged, and your resistance softens. The tension drops, and you finally see the goodness you had overlooked.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि बिधि भरत चले मग जाहीं। दसा देखि मुनि सिद्ध सिहाहीं॥ जबहि रामु कहि लेहिं उसासा। उमगत प्रेमु मनहुँ चहु पासा ॥
translation: इस प्रकार भरतजी मार्ग में चले जा रहे हैं। उनकी (प्रेममयी) दशा देखकर मुनि और सिद्ध लोग भी सिहाते हैं। भरतजी जब भी 'राम' कहकर लंबी साँस लेते हैं, तभी मानो चारों ओर प्रेम उमड़ पड़ता है ॥
english_translation: In this way Bharat kept walking along the road. Seeing his condition, sages and perfected beings felt humbled. Whenever Bharat sighs and says 'Ram,' love seems to overflow from every direction.
essence: Love for Ram makes even longing feel luminous.
simple_meaning: Bharat walks on with such love and longing for Ram that even holy beings are awed. Every breath and mention of Ram seems to spread devotion all around him.
insight: It shifts attention from outward achievement to the radiance created by wholehearted devotion.
modern_relevance: You sit in the back seat after a long train ride to see someone you love, exhausted but unable to stop thinking their name. That kind of longing changes the whole room before you even speak.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: द्रवहिं बचन सुनि कुलिस पषाना। पुरजन पेमु न जाइ बखाना॥ बीच बास करि जमुनहिं आए। निरखि नीरु लोचन जल छाए ॥
translation: उनके (प्रेम और दीनता से पूर्ण) वचनों को सुनकर वज्र और पत्थर भी पिघल जाते हैं। अयोध्यावासियों का प्रेम कहते नहीं बनता। बीच में निवास (मुकाम) करके भरतजी यमुनाजी के तट पर आए। यमुनाजी का जल देखकर उनके नेत्रों में जल भर आया ॥
english_translation: Hearing those tender words, even thunderbolts and stone would melt. The love of the people of Ayodhya cannot be fully described. After resting along the way, Bharat came to the bank of the Yamuna. Seeing the water, his eyes filled with tears.
essence: Humility melts hardness, and grief rises at the sight of home.
simple_meaning: Bharat's humble words move everyone deeply. The people of Ayodhya love him beyond words. When he reaches the Yamuna, the sight of water brings tears to his eyes.
insight: It shows how sincerity disarms resistance and how grief can surface through ordinary sensory moments.
modern_relevance: You say something honest and humble in a family conversation, and the room changes. Later, a simple sight — a river, a cup, a place you shared — suddenly opens the grief you were carrying.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रघुबर बरन बिलोकि बर बारि समेत समाज। होत मगन बारिधि बिरह चढ़े बिबेक जहाज ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी के (श्याम) रंग का सुंदर जल देखकर सारे समाज सहित भरतजी (प्रेम विह्वल होकर) श्री रामजी के विरह रूपी समुद्र में डूबते-डूबते विवेक रूपी जहाज पर चढ़ गए (अर्थात् यमुनाजी का श्यामवर्ण जल देखकर सब लोग श्यामवर्ण भगवान के प्रेम में विह्वल हो गए और उन्हें न पाकर विरह व्यथा से पीड़ित हो गए, तब भरतजी को यह ध्यान आया कि जल्दी चलकर उनके साक्षात् दर्शन करेंगे, इस विवेक से वे फिर उत्साहित हो गए) ॥
english_translation: Seeing the lovely dark-blue sight of Raghubar, Bharata and the whole company were lost in love, then climbed back onto the boat of discernment in the ocean of separation.
essence: Love can flood you, and discernment can still carry you forward.
simple_meaning: The sight of Ram's dark beauty overwhelms Bharata and everyone with love, then the pain of separation reminds them to keep moving with clear judgment.
insight: It shows how devotion and discernment can work together: feeling deeply without losing your direction.
modern_relevance: You see a photo, a place, or a message that brings someone back all at once. Your chest tightens, then you remember what needs to be done next.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जमुन तीर तेहि दिन करि बासू। भयउ समय सम सबहि सुपासू॥ रातिहिं घाट घाट की तरनी। आईं अगनित जाहिं न बरनी ॥
translation: उस दिन यमुनाजी के किनारे निवास किया। समयानुसार सबके लिए (खान-पान आदि की) सुंदर व्यवस्था हुई (निषादराज का संकेत पाकर) रात ही रात में घाट-घाट की अगणित नावें वहाँ आ गईं, जिनका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
english_translation: That day they stayed on the Yamuna bank, and everything was arranged in time for everyone. At night, countless boats came to every landing, beyond counting.
essence: Quiet service makes impossible crossings feel effortless.
simple_meaning: They camped by the Yamuna, and the people were comfortably provided for. At night, so many boats arrived that no one could count them.
insight: It highlights how true service anticipates need and removes friction before anyone has to plead.
modern_relevance: You arrive exhausted at a riverside stop after a long family trip, and someone quietly brings food, blankets, and transport before you even ask. That kind of care changes everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रात पार भए एकहि खेवाँ। तोषे रामसखा की सेवाँ॥ चले नहाइ नदिहि सिर नाई। साथ निषादनाथ दोउ भाई ॥
translation: सबेरे एक ही खेवे में सब लोग पार हो गए और श्री रामचंद्रजी के सखा निषादराज की इस सेवा से संतुष्ट हुए। फिर स्नान करके और नदी को सिर नवाकर निषादराज के साथ दोनों भाई चले ॥
english_translation: At dawn, everyone crossed in a single boat, and Ram's friend Nishadraj was pleased by this service. Then they bathed, bowed to the river, and the two brothers set out with Nishadraj.
essence: Service becomes complete when it asks for nothing back.
simple_meaning: Everyone crosses the river in one boat, and Nishadraj is pleased to serve Ram's party. After bathing and honoring the river, the two brothers continue with him.
insight: It highlights service that quietly carries others forward without asking for recognition.
modern_relevance: You drop everything to help a friend move across town before sunrise, then walk them to the door yourself. No applause, just care that makes the whole day lighter.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आगें मुनिबर बाहन आछें। राजसमाज जाइ सबु पाछें॥ तेहि पाछें दोउ बंधु पयादें। भूषन बसन बेष सुठि सादें ॥
translation: आगे अच्छी-अच्छी सवारियों पर श्रेष्ठ मुनि हैं, उनके पीछे सारा राजसमाज जा रहा है। उसके पीछे दोनों भाई बहुत सादे भूषण-वस्त्र और वेष से पैदल चल रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Ahead, the best sages ride in fine conveyances; behind them goes the whole royal company. Behind that, the two brothers walk on foot in very simple ornaments, clothes, and appearance.
essence: Simplicity can stand behind honor without losing dignity.
simple_meaning: The sages and royal company travel ahead, while Ram and Lakshman walk behind them in simple dress.
insight: It shifts attention from status and display to humility and restraint.
modern_relevance: You show up to a formal event in plain clothes while everyone else arrives polished and important. You don't need the spotlight to carry your dignity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सेवक सुहृद सचिवसुत साथा। सुमिरत लखनु सीय रघुनाथा॥ जहँ जहँ राम बास बिश्रामा। तहँ तहँ करहिं सप्रेम प्रनामा ॥
translation: सेवक, मित्र और मंत्री के पुत्र उनके साथ हैं। लक्ष्मण, सीताजी और श्री रघुनाथजी का स्मरण करते जा रहे हैं। जहाँ-जहाँ श्री रामजी ने निवास और विश्राम किया था, वहाँ-वहाँ वे प्रेमसहित प्रणाम करते हैं ॥
english_translation: The servants, friends, and ministers' sons stayed with them. Lakshman, Sita, and Raghunath kept remembering each other. Wherever Ram had lived or rested, they bowed there with love.
essence: Love makes every remembered place worthy of bowing.
simple_meaning: Lakshman, Sita, and the others walk together, remembering Ram and bowing lovingly at every place he stayed.
insight: It shifts attention from movement itself to the tenderness of remembering and honoring what mattered.
modern_relevance: You pass the café where someone once sat across from you, and the memory hits before the coffee does. Certain places keep a person's presence alive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मगबासी नर नारि सुनि धाम काम तजि धाइ। देखि सरूप सनेह सब मुदित जनम फलु पाइ ॥
translation: मार्ग में रहने वाले स्त्री-पुरुष यह सुनकर घर और काम-काज छोड़कर दौड़ पड़ते हैं और उनके रूप (सौंदर्य) और प्रेम को देखकर वे सब जन्म लेने का फल पाकर आनंदित होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, men and women living along the road ran out, leaving home and work. Seeing their beauty and love, all of them felt they had gained the fruit of being born.
essence: Their presence makes people feel their lives have meaning.
simple_meaning: People along the road forget their routines and hurry out to see Ram and Lakshman. Their beauty and affection make everyone feel life has become worthwhile.
insight: It shifts attention from tasks and schedules to the transforming effect of a noble presence.
modern_relevance: A crowd gathers outside a train station because someone beloved has arrived. People stop errands, forget their plans, and just want one glimpse. Some presences make the whole day feel blessed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहहिं सप्रेम एक एक पाहीं। रामु लखनु सखि होहिं कि नाहीं॥ बय बपु बरन रूपु सोइ आली। सीलु सनेहु सरिस सम चाली ॥
translation: गाँवों की स्त्रियाँ एक-दूसरे से प्रेमपूर्वक कहती हैं- सखी! ये राम-लक्ष्मण हैं कि नहीं? हे सखी! इनकी अवस्था, शरीर और रंग-रूप तो वही है। शील, स्नेह उन्हीं के सदृश है और चाल भी उन्हीं के समान है ॥
english_translation: The village women lovingly ask one another, “Are these Ram and Lakshman or not? Dear friend, their age, bodies, color, beauty, character, affection, and manner of walking are just like theirs.”
essence: Love sees the beloved before certainty arrives.
simple_meaning: The women are so struck by the brothers that they compare every detail of them to Ram and Lakshman, yet they are still unsure.
insight: It captures a moment of near-recognition, where longing and familiarity rise before certainty.
modern_relevance: You see someone in a crowd who feels strangely familiar, and you keep asking friends, “Is that really them?” The heart recognizes before the mind does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बेषु न सो सखि सीय न संगा। आगें अनी चली चतुरंगा॥ नहिं प्रसन्न मुख मानस खेदा। सखि संदेहु होइ एहिं भेदा ॥
translation: परन्तु सखी! इनका न तो वह वेष (वल्कल वस्त्रधारी मुनिवेष) है, न सीताजी ही संग हैं और इनके आगे चतुरंगिणी सेना चली जा रही है। फिर इनके मुख प्रसन्न नहीं हैं, इनके मन में खेद है। हे सखी! इसी भेद के कारण संदेह होता है ॥
english_translation: But, friend, they do not wear that ascetic dress, nor is Sita with them. And an army of four divisions marches ahead of them. Their faces are not cheerful, and their minds are troubled. Friend, because of these differences, doubt arises.
essence: Doubt grows when reality does not match expectation.
simple_meaning: The women notice that this is not the ascetic-looking Ram they expected. Sita is absent, an army is marching ahead, and Ram's face looks troubled, so doubt begins to grow.
insight: It trains the mind to notice concrete signs before accepting a conclusion.
modern_relevance: You see a friend arrive in the same car, but their expression is tight and they are not with the person you expected. The details don't fit the story, and your mind starts searching for what changed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तासु तरक तियगन मन मानी। कहहिं सकल तेहि सम न सयानी॥ तेहि सराहि बानी फुरि पूजी। बोली मधुर बचन तिय दूजी ॥
translation: उसका तर्क (युक्ति) अन्य स्त्रियों के मन भाया। सब कहती हैं कि इसके समान सयानी (चतुर) कोई नहीं है। उसकी सराहना करके और 'तेरी वाणी सत्य है' इस प्रकार उसका सम्मान करके दूसरी स्त्री मीठे वचन बोली ॥
english_translation: Her reasoning pleased the women’s minds. They all said, “No one is as clever as she is.” After praising her and honoring her words as true, another woman spoke sweetly.
essence: A clear voice can settle a room before the full story is known.
simple_meaning: The women are convinced by her argument and praise her as the wisest among them. Another woman responds with respectful, sweet speech.
insight: It shows how shared uncertainty often resolves when one person speaks with clarity and confidence.
modern_relevance: In a group chat, one person finally names what everyone has been half-thinking. The room relaxes, and the conversation moves forward because someone put the feeling into words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहि सप्रेम बस कथाप्रसंगू। जेहि बिधि राम राज रस भंगू॥ भरतहि बहुरि सराहन लागी। सील सनेह सुभाय सुभागी ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के राजतिलक का आनंद जिस प्रकार से भंग हुआ था, वह सब कथाप्रसंग प्रेमपूर्वक कहकर फिर वह भाग्यवती स्त्री श्री भरतजी के शील, स्नेह और स्वभाव की सराहना करने लगी ॥
english_translation: After lovingly recounting how Ram's coronation joy was broken, she again began praising Bharat's character, affection, and noble nature.
essence: Loss reveals the depth of Bharat's gentleness and love.
simple_meaning: She lovingly tells the story of how Ram's coronation was disrupted, then turns to praising Bharat's character and loving nature.
insight: It keeps attention on character, not just on the event that caused sorrow.
modern_relevance: At a family gathering, someone retells the moment everything went wrong, then quietly says who stayed kind through it. Pain and character are being measured at the same time.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चलत पयादें खात फल पिता दीन्ह तजि राजु। जात मनावन रघुबरहि भरत सरिस को आजु ॥
translation: (वह बोली-) देखो, ये भरतजी पिता के दिए हुए राज्य को त्यागकर पैदल चलते और फलाहार करते हुए श्री रामजी को मनाने के लिए जा रहे हैं। इनके समान आज कौन है? ॥।
english_translation: See how Bharat has renounced the kingdom his father gave him, walking on foot and living on fruit as he goes to appease Ram. Who is like him today?
essence: Devotion becomes undeniable when it walks away from comfort.
simple_meaning: Bharat has left behind the throne, travels on foot, eats only fruit, and goes to win Ram back. His devotion is being praised as unmatched.
insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to visible sacrifice and loyal action.
modern_relevance: You turn down a promotion because it would pull you away from someone you promised to stand by. That quiet refusal tells the truth about what matters most.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भायप भगति भरत आचरनू। कहत सुनत दुख दूषन हरनू॥ जो किछु कहब थोर सखि सोई। राम बंधु अस काहे न होई ॥
translation: भरतजी का भाईपना, भक्ति और इनके आचरण कहने और सुनने से दुःख और दोषों के हरने वाले हैं। हे सखी! उनके संबंध में जो कुछ भी कहा जाए, वह थोड़ा है। श्री रामचंद्रजी के भाई ऐसे क्यों न हों ॥
english_translation: Bharat's brotherly love, devotion, and conduct remove sorrow and fault when spoken of or heard. O friend, whatever can be said is still too little. Why would Ram's brother be any less than this?
essence: Pure devotion makes sorrow lighter just by being seen.
simple_meaning: Bharat's love, devotion, and conduct are so pure that even hearing about them eases sorrow. His greatness feels too vast for words, and Ram's brother could not be otherwise.
insight: It shifts attention from Bharat's sacrifice alone to the healing power of witnessing selfless conduct.
modern_relevance: You hear about someone who gave up comfort to keep a promise, and your chest loosens. Their integrity doesn't just impress you — it restores something in you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हम सब सानुज भरतहि देखें। भइन्ह धन्य जुबती जन लेखें॥ सुनि गुन देखि दसा पछिताहीं। कैकइ जननि जोगु सुतु नाहीं ॥
translation: छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न सहित भरतजी को देखकर हम सब भी आज धन्य (बड़भागिनी) स्त्रियों की गिनती में आ गईं। इस प्रकार भरतजी के गुण सुनकर और उनकी दशा देखकर स्त्रियाँ पछताती हैं और कहती हैं- यह पुत्र कैकयी जैसी माता के योग्य नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Seeing Bharata with his younger brother Shatrughna, we all count ourselves among the blessed women. Hearing of his virtues and seeing his condition, the women regret and say, 'This son is not worthy of Kaikeyi as a mother.'
essence: Bharata's virtue makes even sorrow feel like blessing.
simple_meaning: The women feel blessed just by seeing Bharata and Shatrughna. But when they hear Bharata's virtues and see his hardship, they lament that such a son does not deserve a mother like Kaikeyi.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance to the moral weight of a person's conduct and suffering.
modern_relevance: You watch someone carry family pain with dignity at a funeral, and the room goes quiet. Their goodness makes everyone feel both grateful and heartbroken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोउ कह दूषनु रानिहि नाहिन। बिधि सबु कीन्ह हमहि जो दाहिन॥ कहँ हम लोक बेद बिधि हीनी। लघु तिय कुल करतूति मलीनी ॥
translation: कोई कहती है- इसमें रानी का भी दोष नहीं है। यह सब विधाता ने ही किया है, जो हमारे अनुकूल है। कहाँ तो हम लोक और वेद दोनों की विधि (मर्यादा) से हीन, कुल और करतूत दोनों से मलिन तुच्छ स्त्रियाँ, ॥
english_translation: Some say the queen is not at fault. Fate has done all this to us, to our liking. What are we, poor women lacking both social order and scriptural rule, lowly in family and conduct?
essence: Sorrow can make blame dissolve into self-condemnation.
simple_meaning: The women say the queen may not be to blame; they feel fate has brought this sorrow. They also call themselves lowly, lacking both social and scriptural standing.
insight: It reveals how sorrow distorts judgment: blame, pity, and self-condemnation all blur together.
modern_relevance: After a family blowup, people start saying, 'Maybe it wasn't just her fault' — and then immediately shrink into self-blame, as if the pain proves their own worthlessness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बसहिं कुदेस कुगाँव कुबामा। कहँ यह दरसु पुन्य परिनामा॥ अस अनंदु अचिरिजु प्रति ग्रामा। जनु मरुभूमि कलपतरु जामा ॥
translation: जो बुरे देश (जंगली प्रान्त) और बुरे गाँव में बसती हैं और (स्त्रियों में भी) नीच स्त्रियाँ हैं! और कहाँ यह महान् पुण्यों का परिणामस्वरूप इनका दर्शन! ऐसा ही आनंद और आश्चर्य गाँव-गाँव में हो रहा है। मानो मरुभूमि में कल्पवृक्ष उग गया हो ॥
english_translation: Those living in bad lands, bad villages, and low homes! And yet, where is this sight? It is the fruit of great merit. Such joy and wonder spread through every village, as if a wish-fulfilling tree had grown in a desert.
essence: Bharat's presence feels like a miracle in a barren world.
simple_meaning: Bharat's presence is so beautiful that even ordinary people feel amazed and blessed by seeing him, as if a miracle has appeared in a barren place.
insight: It shifts attention from status to the blessing of a person whose presence quietly transforms everyone around them.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after someone kind and steady arrives, and the whole mood changes. People feel lighter without knowing why. Some people do that just by being present.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत दरसु देखत खुलेउ मग लोगन्ह कर भागु। जनु सिंघलबासिन्ह भयउ बिधि बस सुलभ प्रयागु ॥
translation: भरतजी का स्वरूप देखते ही रास्ते में रहने वाले लोगों के भाग्य खुल गए! मानो दैवयोग से सिंहलद्वीप के बसने वालों को तीर्थराज प्रयाग सुलभ हो गया हो! ॥
english_translation: Just seeing Bharat, the people along the road felt their fortune open. It was as if, by fate, the people of Lanka had found Prayag within reach.
essence: A pure presence can feel like a sacred meeting place.
simple_meaning: Bharat's presence blesses everyone who sees him. The people along the road feel as if a rare holy blessing has come to them.
insight: It shifts attention from what Bharat is doing to what his presence awakens in others.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a funeral, and their quiet steadiness calms everyone in the room. Without saying much, they make grief feel less lonely.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निज गुन सहित राम गुन गाथा। सुनत जाहिं सुमिरत रघुनाथा॥ तीरथ मुनि आश्रम सुरधामा। निरखि निमज्जहिं करहिं प्रनामा ॥
translation: (इस प्रकार) अपने गुणों सहित श्री रामचंद्रजी के गुणों की कथा सुनते और श्री रघुनाथजी को स्मरण करते हुए भरतजी चले जा रहे हैं। वे तीर्थ देखकर स्नान और मुनियों के आश्रम तथा देवताओं के मंदिर देखकर प्रणाम करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Bharat keeps walking while hearing the praises of Ram's virtues and remembering Raghunath. Seeing holy places, sages' hermitages, and shrines of radiant beings, he bathes and bows down.
essence: Devotion makes every step an offering.
simple_meaning: Bharat walks on, thinking of Ram and hearing Ram's praise. Whenever he sees a holy place, a sage's hermitage, or a shrine, he bathes and bows.
insight: It shifts travel from movement through space into continuous remembrance and respect.
modern_relevance: You pass a temple on the way to work, step in for a minute, and leave quieter than you entered. Bharat carries that same reflex of reverence wherever he goes.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मनहीं मन मागहिं बरु एहू। सीय राम पद पदुम सनेहू॥ मिलहिं किरात कोल बनबासी। बैखानस बटु जती उदासी ॥
translation: और मन ही मन यह वरदान माँगते हैं कि श्री सीता-रामजी के चरण कमलों में प्रेम हो। मार्ग में भील, कोल आदि वनवासी तथा वानप्रस्थ, ब्रह्मचारी, संन्यासी और विरक्त मिलते हैं ॥
english_translation: And in their hearts they ask for only this blessing: love for the lotus feet of Sita and Ram. Along the way they meet forest-dwellers, ascetics, celibates, renunciants, and wandering seekers.
essence: The journey is already sacred when your heart wants only Ram.
simple_meaning: Bharat and his companions keep asking for one thing in their hearts: love for Ram and Sita. As they travel, they meet many forest people and renunciants.
insight: It shifts attention from outward travel to inward devotion, showing that the real destination is the heart's orientation.
modern_relevance: You keep moving through a difficult season, and all you really want is one thing: to feel love again for what truly matters. Even the people you meet along the way can become reminders of that longing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि प्रनामु पूँछहिं जेहि तेही। केहि बन लखनु रामु बैदेही॥ ते प्रभु समाचार सब कहहीं। भरतहि देखि जनम फलु लहहीं ॥
translation: उनमें से जिस-तिस से प्रणाम करके पूछते हैं कि लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामजी और जानकीजी किस वन में हैं? वे प्रभु के सब समाचार कहते हैं और भरतजी को देखकर जन्म का फल पाते हैं ॥
english_translation: They bow to each person they meet and ask, "Which forest are Lakshman, Ram, and Sita in?" Those people tell them everything about the Lord, and seeing Bharat, they feel they have gained the fruit of life.
essence: A devoted heart makes everyone it meets feel blessed.
simple_meaning: Bharat keeps asking everyone where Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are. People who answer him feel blessed just by seeing him.
insight: It shifts attention from the search itself to the purity of the seeker’s love.
modern_relevance: You stop strangers on a long road and ask one name again and again because someone you love is missing. Even the answer feels holy when your heart is that devoted.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जे जन कहहिं कुसल हम देखे। ते प्रिय राम लखन सम लेखे॥ एहि बिधि बूझत सबहि सुबानी। सुनत राम बनबास कहानी ॥
translation: जो लोग कहते हैं कि हमने उनको कुशलपूर्वक देखा है, उनको ये श्री राम-लक्ष्मण के समान ही प्यारे मानते हैं। इस प्रकार सबसे सुंदर वाणी से पूछते और श्री रामजी के वनवास की कहानी सुनते जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who say, “We have seen him safe and well” are cherished as dearly as Ram and Lakshman. In this way, they ask everyone with sweet words and keep hearing the story of Ram’s exile.
essence: When love is waiting, even news becomes a blessing.
simple_meaning: Anyone who can tell Bharata that Ram and Lakshman are safe becomes dear to him. He keeps asking people gently and listening to the story of Ram’s exile.
insight: It shows how longing makes ordinary information feel sacred and turns every listener into a devotee of the beloved’s safety.
modern_relevance: You refresh your phone again and again, hoping for one reassuring message. When someone you love is away, even a small update feels priceless.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहि बासर बसि प्रातहीं चले सुमिरि रघुनाथ। राम दरस की लालसा भरत सरिस सब साथ ॥
translation: उस दिन वहीं ठहरकर दूसरे दिन प्रातःकाल ही श्री रघुनाथजी का स्मरण करके चले। साथ के सब लोगों को भी भरतजी के समान ही श्री रामजी के दर्शन की लालसा (लगी हुई) है ॥
english_translation: After staying there that day, they set out at dawn the next morning, remembering Raghunath. Everyone in the group longs to see Ram just as Bharata does.
essence: Shared longing turns the whole group toward one beloved presence.
simple_meaning: They spend the night there and leave at dawn, all of them longing to see Ram just as Bharata does.
insight: It shows how shared longing can unify action and keep a group moving together.
modern_relevance: You leave before sunrise after a sleepless night on the road, replaying one meeting in your mind. Everyone with you feels the same pull: get there, see them, and let the waiting end.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंगल सगुन होहिं सब काहू। फरकहिं सुखद बिलोचन बाहू॥ भरतहि सहित समाज उछाहू। मिलिहहिं रामु मिटिहि दुख दाहू ॥
translation: सबको मंगलसूचक शकुन हो रहे हैं। सुख देने वाले (पुरुषों के दाहिने और स्त्रियों के बाएँ) नेत्र और भुजाएँ फड़क रही हैं। समाज सहित भरतजी को उत्साह हो रहा है कि श्री रामचंद्रजी मिलेंगे और दुःख का दाह मिट जाएगा ॥
english_translation: All signs are auspicious. Pleasant twitches move the eyes and arms. Bharat and the whole gathering feel joy, knowing Ram will meet them and the fire of sorrow will be quenched.
essence: Hope itself can begin healing before the meeting arrives.
