simple_meaning: Everyone sees hopeful signs, and Bharat’s group feels joy because Ram is about to meet them and their suffering will ease.
insight: It shifts attention from grief to anticipation, showing how hope can steady a shaken mind.
modern_relevance: You’re waiting outside a hospital room, and someone finally texts that the doctor is coming. Your chest loosens before the door even opens.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करत मनोरथ जस जियँ जाके। जाहिं सनेह सुराँ सब छाके। सिथिल अंग पग मग डगि डोलहिं। बिहबल बचन प्रेम बस बोलहिं ॥
translation: जिसके जी में जैसा है, वह वैसा ही मनोरथ करता है। सब स्नेही रूपी मदिरा से छके (प्रेम में मतवाले हुए) चले जा रहे हैं। अंग शिथिल हैं, रास्ते में पैर डगमगा रहे हैं और प्रेमवश विह्वल वचन बोल रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Whatever is in a person's heart, that becomes the person's desire. Everyone moves forward, drunk on the wine of affection; their limbs grow weak, their feet stagger on the path, and love makes them speak in a dazed way.
essence: Longing turns the whole body into a sign of the heart.
simple_meaning: Love and longing make people act differently: their bodies weaken, their steps falter, and their words come out overwhelmed.
insight: It captures how emotion can overtake the body and speech before the mind catches up.
modern_relevance: You leave a message unread because your heart is racing, then reread it ten times on the walk. When longing takes over, even your body starts to show it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामसखाँ तेहि समय देखावा। सैल सिरोमनि सहज सुहावा॥ जासु समीप सरित पय तीरा। सीय समेत बसहिं दोउ बीरा ॥
translation: रामसखा निषादराज ने उसी समय स्वाभाविक ही सुहावना पर्वतशिरोमणि कामदगिरि दिखलाया, जिसके निकट ही पयस्विनी नदी के तट पर सीताजी समेत दोनों भाई निवास करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram's friend Nishadraj showed them the lovely mountain at that moment. Near it, on the bank of the Payaswini river, the two brothers live with Sita.
essence: A simple place becomes precious because Ram and Sita live there.
simple_meaning: Nishadraj points out the beautiful hill near the river where Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are staying.
insight: It shifts attention from scenery alone to the presence that gives a place meaning.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a quiet hillside after hearing stories about it for months. The view matters, but what really moves you is knowing someone you love once stood there too.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि करहिं सब दंड प्रनामा। कहि जय जानकि जीवन रामा॥ प्रेम मगन अस राज समाजू। जनु फिरि अवध चले रघुराजू ॥
translation: सब लोग उस पर्वत को देखकर 'जानकी जीवन श्री रामचंद्रजी की जय हो।' ऐसा कहकर दण्डवत प्रणाम करते हैं। राजसमाज प्रेम में ऐसा मग्न है मानो श्री रघुनाथजी अयोध्या को लौट चले हों ॥
english_translation: Seeing the mountain, everyone bowed down and said, 'Victory to Rama, the life of Janaki.' The royal assembly was so immersed in love that it seemed as if the lord of Raghu had returned to Ayodhya.
essence: Deep love makes absence feel like return.
simple_meaning: Everyone bows to the sight of the mountain and praises Rama. The whole royal gathering feels so full of love that it seems as if Rama has already returned home.
insight: It turns memory into living presence and shows how devotion reshapes perception.
modern_relevance: You walk into a place tied to someone you love, and the whole room changes. Their memory is so strong it feels like they are there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत प्रेमु तेहि समय जस तस कहि सकइ न सेषु। कबिहि अगम जिमि ब्रह्मसुखु अह मम मलिन जनेषु ॥
translation: भरतजी का उस समय जैसा प्रेम था, वैसा शेषजी भी नहीं कह सकते। कवि के लिए तो वह वैसा ही अगम है, जैसा अहंता और ममता से मलिन मनुष्यों के लिए ब्रह्मानंद! ॥
english_translation: At that moment, Bharat's love could not be fully spoken even by Shesha. For a poet, it is as inaccessible as the bliss of Brahman is to a mind stained by ego and possessiveness.
essence: Love can become so pure that words fail completely.
simple_meaning: Bharat's love at that moment was beyond description. Even the greatest speaker could not fully capture it, just as some joys are unreachable to a restless, self-centered mind.
insight: It shifts the mind from trying to justify devotion to simply recognising its depth.
modern_relevance: You try to explain why you stayed loyal to someone who gave you nothing back, and the explanation sounds thin. Some bonds are felt more deeply than they can ever be argued.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकल सनेह सिथिल रघुबर कें। गए कोस दुइ दिनकर ढरकें॥ जलु थलु देखि बसे निसि बीतें। कीन्ह गवन रघुनाथ पिरीतें ॥
translation: सब लोग श्री रामचंद्रजी के प्रेम के मारे शिथिल होने के कारण सूर्यास्त होने तक (दिनभर में) दो ही कोस चल पाए और जल-स्थल का सुपास देखकर रात को वहीं (बिना खाए-पीए ही) रह गए। रात बीतने पर श्री रघुनाथजी के प्रेमी भरतजी ने आगे गमन किया ॥
english_translation: Because of their love for Raghubar, everyone became weak. They walked only two kos before sunset. Seeing water and land, they stayed there through the night. At dawn, the devoted Bharat went on ahead.
essence: Love for Ram changes exhaustion into forward motion.
simple_meaning: Love for Ram made everyone so weak that they could barely travel. They stopped for the night after only a short distance, and Bharat moved on at dawn.
insight: It shifts attention from physical ease to devotion-powered endurance.
modern_relevance: You leave before sunrise for a long drive to see someone you love. The road feels endless, but you keep going because the heart has already decided.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उहाँ रामु रजनी अवसेषा। जागे सीयँ सपन अस देखा॥ सहित समाज भरत जनु आए। नाथ बियोग ताप तन ताए ॥
translation: उधर श्री रामचंद्रजी रात शेष रहते ही जागे। रात को सीताजी ने ऐसा स्वप्न देखा (जिसे वे श्री रामचंद्रजी को सुनाने लगीं) मानो समाज सहित भरतजी यहाँ आए हैं। प्रभु के वियोग की अग्नि से उनका शरीर संतप्त है ॥
english_translation: There, Ram was still awake while night remained. In sleep, Sita saw a dream: Bharat had come here with his whole company, and his body was burning with the heat of separation from his lord.
essence: Separation burns so deeply it enters even dreams.
simple_meaning: Ram stays awake while night still lingers. Sita dreams that Bharat has arrived with his companions, and that he is burning with grief from separation.
insight: It shows how separation enters both waking life and dreams, turning love into a shared burden.
modern_relevance: You wake before sunrise and the first thought is the person who is missing. Even sleep cannot fully loosen the bond, and the mind keeps carrying their pain.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकल मलिन मन दीन दुखारी। देखीं सासु आन अनुहारी॥ सुनि सिय सपन भरे जल लोचन। भए सोचबस सोच बिमोचन ॥
translation: सभी लोग मन में उदास, दीन और दुःखी हैं। सासुओं को दूसरी ही सूरत में देखा। सीताजी का स्वप्न सुनकर श्री रामचंद्रजी के नेत्रों में जल भर गया और सबको सोच से छुड़ा देने वाले प्रभु स्वयं (लीला से) सोच के वश हो गए ॥
english_translation: Everyone was sad, humble, and grieving. The mothers-in-law seemed changed in a troubling way. Hearing Sita's dream, Ram's eyes filled with tears, and the one who frees others from sorrow became overcome by sorrow himself.
essence: The one who ends sorrow can still weep with those he loves.
simple_meaning: The household is heavy with grief, and Ram is moved to tears after hearing Sita's dream. Even the one who frees others from sorrow is touched by sorrow here.
insight: It shows how shared fear spreads through a family and how even the steady can be pierced by sorrow.
modern_relevance: You notice your family going quiet after a dream or a late-night call. Everyone pretends to stay composed, but one small sign is enough to bring the whole room into grief.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लखन सपन यह नीक न होई। कठिन कुचाह सुनाइहि कोई॥ अस कहि बंधु समेत नहाने पूजि पुरारि साधु सनमाने ॥
translation: (और बोले-) लक्ष्मण! यह स्वप्न अच्छा नहीं है। कोई भीषण कुसमाचार (बहुत ही बुरी खबर) सुनावेगा। ऐसा कहकर उन्होंने भाई सहित स्नान किया और त्रिपुरारी महादेवजी का पूजन करके साधुओं का सम्मान किया ॥
english_translation: Laxman, this dream is not a good sign. Someone will bring terrible news. Saying this, he bathed with his brother, worshipped Lord Shiva, and honored the sages.
essence: A bad sign does not justify panic; begin with reverence and steadiness.
simple_meaning: Ram reads the dream as a bad omen, then begins the day with ritual bathing, worship of Shiva, and respect for holy men.
insight: It shifts the mind from superstition and panic to composed, respectful action.
modern_relevance: You wake from a bad dream before dawn and feel the day tilting wrong. Instead of spiraling, you wash your face, pray, and treat the morning with dignity.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सनमानि सुर मुनि बंदि बैठे उतर दिसि देखत भए। नभ धूरि खग मृग भूरि भागे बिकल प्रभु आश्रम गए॥ तुलसी उठे अवलोकि कारनु काह चित सचकित रहे। सब समाचार किरात कोलन्हि आइ तेहि अवसर कहे॥
translation: देवताओं का सम्मान (पूजन) और मुनियों की वंदना करके श्री रामचंद्रजी बैठ गए और उत्तर दिशा की ओर देखने लगे। आकाश में धूल छा रही है, बहुत से पक्षी और पशु व्याकुल होकर भागे हुए प्रभु के आश्रम को आ रहे हैं। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी यह देखकर उठे और सोचने लगे कि क्या कारण है? वे चित्त में आश्चर्ययुक्त हो गए। उसी समय कोल-भीलों ने आकर सब समाचार कहे।
english_translation: After honoring the gods and bowing to the sages, Ram sat down and looked toward the north. Dust filled the sky, and many birds and animals, frightened and restless, rushed toward the Lord's hermitage. Tulsidas says that seeing this, Ram rose and wondered what had happened. His mind became alert and astonished. Then the Kirat and Kol people came and told the whole news at that moment.
essence: Alert attention comes before understanding.
simple_meaning: Ram notices unusual signs in nature and waits in alert surprise. Soon, the forest people arrive and explain what has happened.
insight: It teaches you to notice the signs before the news becomes clear.
modern_relevance: You hear dogs barking before dawn, then see neighbors stepping outside in confusion. Something is wrong, and you stop talking long enough to pay attention before the explanation arrives.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनत सुमंगल बैन मन प्रमोद तन पुलक भर। सरद सरोरुह नैन तुलसी भरे सनेह जल ॥
translation: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि सुंदर मंगल वचन सुनते ही श्री रामचंद्रजी के मन में बड़ा आनंद हुआ। शरीर में पुलकावली छा गई और शरद् ऋतु के कमल के समान नेत्र प्रेमाश्रुओं से भर गए ॥
english_translation: Hearing the auspicious words, Ram's mind filled with joy. His body thrilled with goosebumps, and his eyes, like autumn lotuses, overflowed with love.
essence: Joy can overflow into tears before the mind explains it.
simple_meaning: Ram hears good news and is instantly filled with joy, love, and tears.
insight: It shows how the heart reveals relief through the body before thought catches up.
modern_relevance: You get the message you've been waiting for after a long, anxious evening. Before you can even speak, your chest loosens and tears come.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरि सोचबस भे सियरवनू। कारन कवन भरत आगवनू॥ एक आइ अस कहा बहोरी। सेन संग चतुरंग न थोरी ॥
translation: सीतापति श्री रामचंद्रजी पुनः सोच के वश हो गए कि भरत के आने का क्या कारण है? फिर एक ने आकर ऐसा कहा कि उनके साथ में बड़ी भारी चतुरंगिणी सेना भी है ॥
english_translation: Rama became worried again: what was the reason for Bharat's arrival? Then another person came and said that he had brought a very large fourfold army with him.
essence: A brother's arrival can carry both love and threat.
simple_meaning: Rama grows uneasy at Bharat's arrival and hears that Bharat has come with a large army.
insight: It sets up the tension between family affection and the fear of political intent.
modern_relevance: You hear that a sibling is coming to talk, but they arrive with lawyers, relatives, and a long silence. Before anyone speaks, your stomach tightens.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सो सुनि रामहि भा अति सोचू। इत पितु बच इत बंधु सकोचू॥ भरत सुभाउ समुझि मन माहीं। प्रभु चित हित थिति पावत नाहीं ॥
translation: यह सुनकर श्री रामचंद्रजी को अत्यंत सोच हुआ। इधर तो पिता के वचन और उधर भाई भरतजी का संकोच! भरतजी के स्वभाव को मन में समझकर तो प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी चित्त को ठहराने के लिए कोई स्थान ही नहीं पाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Ram was deeply troubled: his father’s word on one side, Bharat’s hesitation on the other. Thinking of Bharat’s nature, he could not settle his mind.
essence: Love and obligation can pull the mind apart at once.
simple_meaning: Ram feels torn between keeping his father's promise and understanding Bharat’s loving hesitation. That conflict leaves his mind unsettled.
insight: It shows how duty can become emotionally complicated when family loyalty and promise collide.
modern_relevance: You get a message that your parent expects one thing, but your sibling’s silence says something else. You can feel the tension before anyone even speaks.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समाधान तब भा यह जाने। भरतु कहे महुँ साधु सयाने॥ लखन लखेउ प्रभु हृदयँ खभारू। कहत समय सम नीति बिचारू ॥
translation: तब यह जानकर समाधान हो गया कि भरत साधु और सयाने हैं तथा मेरे कहने में (आज्ञाकारी) हैं। लक्ष्मणजी ने देखा कि प्रभु श्री रामजी के हृदय में चिंता है तो वे समय के अनुसार अपना नीतियुक्त विचार कहने लगे- ॥
english_translation: Then he understood: Bharat is noble and wise, and he speaks with obedience. Lakshman saw the worry in Ram's heart and, at the right moment, began to speak with measured judgment.
essence: Right speech comes from seeing both character and timing clearly.
simple_meaning: Ram feels relief when he realises Bharat is wise and obedient. Lakshman notices Ram's worry and chooses the right moment to speak carefully.
insight: It teaches you to read the room and speak with timing, not impulse.
modern_relevance: You can feel tension in a room before anyone says a word. The wise person notices it, reads the moment, and speaks only when the other heart is ready.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिनु पूछें कछु कहउँ गोसाईं। सेवकु समयँ न ढीठ ढिठाईं॥ तुम्ह सर्बग्य सिरोमनि स्वामी। आपनि समुझि कहउँ अनुगामी ॥
translation: हे स्वामी! आपके बिना ही पूछे मैं कुछ कहता हूँ, सेवक समय पर ढिठाई करने से ढीठ नहीं समझा जाता (अर्थात् आप पूछें तब मैं कहूँ, ऐसा अवसर नहीं है, इसलिए यह मेरा कहना ढिठाई नहीं होगा)। हे स्वामी! आप सर्वज्ञों में शिरोमणि हैं (सब जानते ही हैं)। मैं सेवक तो अपनी समझ की बात कहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: “Without being asked, I say a little, O Lord. A servant is not rude for speaking at the right time. You are the crown jewel of the all-knowing, O master. I speak only according to my understanding, as your follower.”
essence: Humility lets you speak clearly without claiming importance.
simple_meaning: A true servant speaks humbly and at the right time, trusting the master’s wisdom while offering honest understanding.
insight: It teaches you to pair honesty with humility, so your words help rather than wound.
modern_relevance: You’re in a family group chat, typing and deleting a message because the truth matters but tone matters too. This verse gives you that balance: speak honestly, but speak as someone who is serving, not asserting.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: नाथ सुहृद सुठि सरल चित सील सनेह निधान। सब पर प्रीति प्रतीति जियँ जानिअ आपु समान ॥
translation: हे नाथ! आप परम सुहृद् (बिना ही कारण परम हित करने वाले), सरल हृदय तथा शील और स्नेह के भंडार हैं, आपका सभी पर प्रेम और विश्वास है, और अपने हृदय में सबको अपने ही समान जानते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Lord, you are a true well-wisher, utterly simple in heart, a storehouse of virtue and affection. You love and trust everyone, and in your heart you see all as your own equal.
essence: True greatness treats everyone as equal and beloved.
simple_meaning: Ram is described as a deeply kind, simple-hearted presence who trusts and loves everyone equally, seeing all beings as his own.
insight: It shifts your attention from status and suspicion to equal regard and open-hearted trust.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who remembers the names of the quiet people, not just the important ones. They make no one feel lesser, and you leave feeling seen.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: बिषई जीव पाइ प्रभुताई। मूढ़ मोह बस होहिं जनाई॥ भरतु नीति रत साधु सुजाना। प्रभु पद प्रेमु सकल जगु जाना ॥
translation: परंतु मूढ़ विषयी जीव प्रभुता पाकर मोहवश अपने असली स्वरूप को प्रकट कर देते हैं। भरत नीतिपरायण, साधु और चतुर हैं तथा प्रभु (आप) के चरणों में उनका प्रेम है, इस बात को सारा जगत् जानता है ॥
english_translation: But a foolish, desire-driven person reveals their true nature when given power, overcome by delusion. Bharat, by contrast, is devoted to right conduct, noble, wise, and known throughout the world for his love at the Lord's feet.
essence: Power does not transform character; it uncovers what was hidden.
simple_meaning: Power exposes a foolish person's hidden desires. Bharat, however, is known everywhere for right conduct, wisdom, and love for Ram's feet.
insight: It shifts attention from what power gives you to what power reveals about you.
modern_relevance: You get promoted, and suddenly everyone sees how you treat the assistant, the deadline, and the credit. Authority doesn't invent your character; it exposes it.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तेऊ आजु राम पदु पाई। चले धरम मरजाद मेटाई॥ कुटिल कुबंधु कुअवसरु ताकी। जानि राम बनबास एकाकी ॥
translation: वे भरतजी आज श्री रामजी (आप) का पद (सिंहासन या अधिकार) पाकर धर्म की मर्यादा को मिटाकर चले हैं। कुटिल खोटे भाई भरत कुसमय देखकर और यह जानकर कि रामजी (आप) वनवास में अकेले (असहाय) हैं, ॥
english_translation: They have come today to take Ram's place, overturning the bounds of dharma. Seeing the right moment, that crooked brother came knowing Ram was alone in the forest.
essence: A badly timed approach can look like virtue while hiding disruption.
simple_meaning: Bharat has come at the wrong time, when Ram is alone in exile. The verse frames him as taking Ram's place and upsetting rightful conduct.
insight: It trains the mind to read motive, timing, and consequence together instead of trusting appearances.
modern_relevance: A sibling shows up after everyone is exhausted, and the room instantly changes. Even before words are spoken, you can feel whether the visit is care, control, or calculation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि कुमंत्रु मन साजि समाजू। आए करै अकंटक राजू॥ कोटि प्रकार कलपि कुटिलाई। आए दल बटोरि दोउ भाई ॥
translation: अपने मन में बुरा विचार करके, समाज जोड़कर राज्यों को निष्कण्टक करने के लिए यहाँ आए हैं। करोड़ों (अनेकों) प्रकार की कुटिलताएँ रचकर सेना बटोरकर दोनों भाई आए हैं ॥
english_translation: Having formed a wicked plan in the mind, they came with a gathered assembly to make the kingdom secure. After plotting countless kinds of deceit, the two brothers came with assembled forces.
essence: Power guided by crooked intent turns every gathering into suspicion.
simple_meaning: The brothers came with a hidden scheme, trying to secure power by gathering support and force.
insight: It frames political action as suspect when desire for control is hiding underneath it.
modern_relevance: A family meeting starts polite, but everyone can feel the hidden agenda under the careful words. The room gets colder when people are really negotiating power, not peace.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जौं जियँ होति न कपट कुचाली। केहि सोहाति रथ बाजि गजाली॥ भरतहि दोसु देइ को जाएँ। जग बौराइ राज पदु पाएँ ॥
translation: यदि इनके हृदय में कपट और कुचाल न होती, तो रथ, घोड़े और हाथियों की कतार (ऐसे समय) किसे सुहाती? परन्तु भरत को ही व्यर्थ कौन दोष दे? राजपद पा जाने पर सारा जगत् ही पागल (मतवाला) हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: If there were no deceit and crookedness in their hearts, who would enjoy chariots, horses, and elephants at such a time? Who can really blame Bharat? When people get royal power, the whole world goes mad.
essence: Power exposes how quickly judgment bends around status.
simple_meaning: If there were no deceit in the heart, no one would be dazzled by royal display. Don’t single out Bharat; power itself can make people lose judgment.
insight: It shifts judgment from one blamed person to the corrupting pull of power itself.
modern_relevance: A family starts treating someone differently the moment a promotion, inheritance, or title enters the picture. This verse asks you to notice how status changes everyone’s behavior, not just the person at the center.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ससि गुर तिय गामी नघुषु चढ़ेउ भूमिसुर जान। लोक बेद तें बिमुख भा अधम न बेन समान ॥
translation: चंद्रमा गुरुपत्नी गामी हुआ, राजा नहुष ब्राह्मणों की पालकी पर चढ़ा और राजा वेन के समान नीच तो कोई नहीं होगा, जो लोक और वेद दोनों से विमुख हो गया ॥
english_translation: The moon, Nahusha, and Vena all fell when they turned against the moral order and the learned; Vena was the lowest of all.
essence: Power turns rotten the moment it abandons right conduct.
simple_meaning: Even famous rulers fell when they violated right conduct and ignored the guidance of the learned. Vena is named as the worst example.
insight: It shifts attention from public success to the moral direction behind it.
modern_relevance: A celebrated leader ignores every warning, surrounds himself with flatterers, and then acts surprised when everything unravels. This verse names that pattern before it repeats itself.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सहसबाहु सुरनाथु त्रिसंकू। केहि न राजमद दीन्ह कलंकू॥ भरत कीन्ह यह उचित उपाऊ। रिपु रिन रंच न राखब काउ ॥
translation: सहस्रबाहु, देवराज इंद्र और त्रिशंकु आदि किसको राजमद ने कलंक नहीं दिया? भरत ने यह उपाय उचित ही किया है, क्योंकि शत्रु और ऋण को कभी जरा भी शेष नहीं रखना चाहिए ॥
english_translation: Who has not been stained by the intoxication of kingship—Sahasrabahu, Indra, and Trishanku? Bharat has taken the right course: never leave an enemy or a debt even a little unpaid.
essence: Power corrupts; clean duty keeps you from being ruled by it.
simple_meaning: Kingship often corrupts people, so Bharat's choice is praised as the right way to act: do not leave an enemy or a debt unfinished.
insight: It shifts attention from status itself to the moral discipline needed to hold it without corruption.
modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, and suddenly every old rivalry wakes up in your chest. This verse reminds you that status can poison judgment unless you keep your debts, duties, and motives clean.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: एक कीन्हि नहिं भरत भलाई। निदरे रामु जानि असहाई॥ समुझि परिहि सोउ आजु बिसेषी। समर सरोष राम मुखु पेखी ॥
translation: हाँ, भरत ने एक बात अच्छी नहीं की, जो रामजी (आप) को असहाय जानकर उनका निरादर किया! पर आज संग्राम में श्री रामजी (आप) का क्रोधपूर्ण मुख देखकर यह बात भी उनकी समझ में विशेष रूप से आ जाएगी (अर्थात् इस निरादर का फल भी वे अच्छी तरह पा जाएँगे) ॥
english_translation: Bharat did not do one thing well: he insulted Ram, thinking him helpless. Today, seeing Ram's anger in battle, he will understand that clearly.
essence: You can mistake gentleness for weakness only until pressure reveals the truth.
simple_meaning: Bharat once treated Ram as helpless, and that disrespect will soon be answered when he sees Ram in battle.
insight: It shifts you from judging by appearance to respecting hidden strength.
modern_relevance: You dismissed someone as powerless because they stayed quiet. Then one day they stood firm, and your old assumption collapsed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एतना कहत नीति रस भूला। रन रस बिटपु पुलक मिस फूला॥ प्रभु पद बंदि सीस रज राखी। बोले सत्य सहज बलु भाषी ॥
translation: इतना कहते ही लक्ष्मणजी नीतिरस भूल गए और युद्धरस रूपी वृक्ष पुलकावली के बहाने से फूल उठा (अर्थात् नीति की बात कहते-कहते उनके शरीर में वीर रस छा गया)। वे प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणों की वंदना करके, चरण रज को सिर पर रखकर सच्चा और स्वाभाविक बल कहते हुए बोले ॥
english_translation: As he said this, Lakshman forgot all talk of policy and blossomed with heroic fervor. Bowing at his Lord's feet and placing the dust of those feet on his head, he spoke the truth with natural strength.
essence: True strength speaks only after bowing first.
simple_meaning: Lakshman stops speaking like a strategist and shifts into heroic resolve. He bows to Ram, takes the dust of Ram's feet on his head, and speaks from his true strength.
insight: It shifts you from reactive debate into grounded speech rooted in loyalty and inner strength.
modern_relevance: You were arguing in circles until you paused, took a breath, and remembered who you serve. The next words came cleaner, stronger, and without posture.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: अनुचित नाथ न मानब मोरा। भरत हमहि उपचार न थोरा॥ कहँ लगि सहिअ रहिअ मनु मारें। नाथ साथ धनु हाथ हमारें ॥
translation: हे नाथ! मेरा कहना अनुचित न मानिएगा। भरत ने हमें कम नहीं प्रचारा है (हमारे साथ कम छेड़छाड़ नहीं की है)। आखिर कहाँ तक सहा जाए और मन मारे रहा जाए, जब स्वामी हमारे साथ हैं और धनुष हमारे हाथ में है! ॥
english_translation: O Lord, do not take my words as improper. Bharata has not treated me lightly. How long should I keep bearing it and swallowing my anger, when my lord is beside me and my bow is in my hand?
essence: Restraint has a limit; then action becomes the honest answer.
simple_meaning: Lakshman says he has tolerated enough. With Ram beside him and his bow in hand, he will no longer stay silent or passive.
insight: It shifts you from passive endurance to decisive, responsible action.
modern_relevance: You keep swallowing your words in a meeting while someone keeps undermining you. Then your manager is right there, your facts are clear, and you know the moment has come to speak.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: छत्रि जाति रघुकुल जनमु राम अनुग जगु जान। लातहुँ मारें चढ़ति सिर नीच को धूरि समान ॥
translation: क्षत्रिय जाति, रघुकुल में जन्म और फिर मैं श्री रामजी (आप) का अनुगामी (सेवक) हूँ, यह जगत् जानता है। (फिर भला कैसे सहा जाए?) धूल के समान नीच कौन है, परन्तु वह भी लात मारने पर सिर ही चढ़ती है ॥
english_translation: I am born in the Raghu clan, a warrior by birth, and the whole world knows I am Ram's follower. How can I endure this? Even the lowest dust rises to the head when kicked.
essence: Loyalty still has a spine.
simple_meaning: Lakshman says his birth and loyalty to Ram should be respected, and even something lowly reacts when struck. He is warning that humiliation cannot be taken lightly.
insight: It teaches you that loyalty does not mean accepting humiliation forever.
modern_relevance: You keep swallowing disrespect in a meeting, smiling while someone keeps pushing too far. At some point, your dignity asks for a response, not more endurance.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: उठि कर जोरि रजायसु मागा। मनहुँ बीर रस सोवत जागा॥ बाँधि जटा सिर कसि कटि भाथा। साजि सरासनु सायकु हाथा ॥
translation: यों कहकर लक्ष्मणजी ने उठकर, हाथ जोड़कर आज्ञा माँगी। मानो वीर रस सोते से जाग उठा हो। सिर पर जटा बाँधकर कमर में तरकस कस लिया और धनुष को सजाकर तथा बाण को हाथ में लेकर कहा- ॥
english_translation: Laxman rose, joined his hands, and asked for permission. It was as if warrior spirit woke from sleep. He tied his matted hair, tightened his waistcloth, and took up his bow and arrows.
essence: True courage wakes instantly when duty calls.
simple_meaning: Laxman stands up, asks permission, and prepares for battle. His sleeping courage wakes fully as he arms himself.
insight: It shifts attention from hesitation to immediate readiness, showing how disciplined loyalty becomes action.
modern_relevance: Your phone buzzes with bad news, and you stop scrolling. You take a breath, straighten up, and do what needs doing without drama.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आजु राम सेवक जसु लेऊँ। भरतहि समर सिखावन देऊँ॥ राम निरादर कर फलु पाई। सोवहुँ समर सेज दोउ भाई ॥
translation: आज मैं श्री राम (आप) का सेवक होने का यश लूँ और भरत को संग्राम में शिक्षा दूँ। श्री रामचंद्रजी (आप) के निरादर का फल पाकर दोनों भाई (भरत-शत्रुघ्न) रण शय्या पर सोवें ॥
english_translation: Today I will earn the praise of being Ram's servant and teach Bharat a lesson in battle. Let the two brothers, having suffered the fruit of disrespecting Ram, lie on the battlefield together.
essence: True service can look like battle when loyalty is tested.
simple_meaning: Lakshman is ready to prove his devotion by fighting for Ram and confronting Bharat. He sees battle as the way to answer disrespect toward Ram.
insight: It turns devotion into action, showing that service can include fearless confrontation when dharma is challenged.
modern_relevance: You hear a friend insult the person you love most, and your whole body tightens. Before you speak, you know loyalty is about to test your restraint.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: आइ बना भल सकल समाजू। प्रगट करउँ रिस पाछिल आजू॥ जिमि करि निकर दलइ मृगराजू। लेइ लपेटि लवा जिमि बाजू ॥
translation: अच्छा हुआ जो सारा समाज आकर एकत्र हो गया। आज मैं पिछला सब क्रोध प्रकट करूँगा। जैसे सिंह हाथियों के झुंड को कुचल डालता है और बाज जैसे लवे को लपेट में ले लेता है ॥
english_translation: Good that the whole assembly has gathered. Today I will bring out all my anger. Like a lion crushing a herd of elephants, like a hawk folding up a lark.
essence: Anger fed by pride always looks for a crowd to conquer.
simple_meaning: Ravana sees the gathered crowd as a chance to unleash the anger he has been holding back, boasting that he will overpower them completely.
insight: It shows how ego converts conflict into domination, not understanding.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting already burning inside, ready to prove a point instead of solve the problem.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: तैसेहिं भरतहि सेन समेता। सानुज निदरि निपातउँ खेता॥ जौं सहाय कर संकरु आई। तौ मारउँ रन राम दोहाई ॥
translation: वैसे ही भरत को सेना समेत और छोटे भाई सहित तिरस्कार करके मैदान में पछाड़ूँगा। यदि शंकरजी भी आकर उनकी सहायता करें, तो भी, मुझे रामजी की सौगंध है, मैं उन्हें युद्ध में (अवश्य) मार डालूँगा (छोड़ूँगा नहीं) ॥
english_translation: I will trample Bharat and his army, along with his younger brother, in the field. Even if Shankar himself comes to help them, by Ram's name I will kill them in battle.
essence: Anger makes even devotion sound like a threat.
simple_meaning: Lakshman vows to crush Bharat, his army, and anyone who helps them, even Shiva himself. His anger is total, and he swears by Ram's name.
insight: It shows how anger turns a conflict into a vow of destruction, leaving no room for restraint.
modern_relevance: You hear a cutting insult in front of everyone and feel your chest tighten. In that instant, the mind wants total victory, not understanding.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: अति सरोष माखे लखनु लखि सुनि सपथ प्रवान। सभय लोक सब लोकपति चाहत भभरि भगान ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी को अत्यंत क्रोध से तमतमाया हुआ देखकर और उनकी प्रामाणिक (सत्य) सौगंध सुनकर सब लोग भयभीत हो जाते हैं और लोकपाल घबड़ाकर भागना चाहते हैं॥230।
english_translation: Seeing Lakshman blazing with fierce anger and hearing his true oath, everyone grows afraid; even the guardians of the world want to flee in panic.
essence: Fierce anger can make the whole world flinch.
simple_meaning: Lakshman’s fierce anger and solemn vow terrify everyone around him, even the world’s guardians.
insight: It shows how uncontained anger radiates outward and makes even powerful beings lose composure.
modern_relevance: A heated argument in a packed room can change the air instantly. One person’s certainty, when it turns sharp and absolute, makes everyone else step back.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जगु भय मगन गगन भइ बानी। लखन बाहुबलु बिपुल बखानी॥ तात प्रताप प्रभाउ तुम्हारा। को कहि सकइ को जाननिहारा ॥
translation: सारा जगत् भय में डूब गया। तब लक्ष्मणजी के अपार बाहुबल की प्रशंसा करती हुई आकाशवाणी हुई- हे तात! तुम्हारे प्रताप और प्रभाव को कौन कह सकता है और कौन जान सकता है? ॥
english_translation: The whole world fell into fear. Then a voice from the sky praised Lakshman's immense strength: 'Father, who can speak of your glory, and who can truly know it?'
essence: True force is so great that even its measure disappears.
simple_meaning: The world is shaken with fear, and a heavenly voice praises Lakshman's great strength and says his glory cannot be fully known.
insight: It frames Lakshman's power as undeniable, setting up the need for careful judgment in action.
modern_relevance: A room goes silent after the one person who can stop the chaos finally speaks. Everyone feels the force in the moment before they can even explain it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अनुचित उचित काजु किछु होऊ। समुझि करिअ भल कह सबु कोऊ। सहसा करि पाछे पछिताहीं। कहहिं बेद बुध ते बुध नाहीं ॥
translation: परन्तु कोई भी काम हो, उसे अनुचित-उचित खूब समझ-बूझकर किया जाए तो सब कोई अच्छा कहते हैं। वेद और विद्वान कहते हैं कि जो बिना विचारे जल्दी में किसी काम को करके पीछे पछताते हैं, वे बुद्धिमान् नहीं हैं ॥
english_translation: Whatever task it may be, consider carefully whether it is right or wrong. Everyone praises a deed done with understanding. The Vedas and the wise say that those who act in haste and later regret it are not truly wise.
essence: Wise action begins with a pause, not a rush.
simple_meaning: Before doing anything, judge carefully whether it is right. People praise thoughtful action, while rushed action often ends in regret.
insight: It teaches you to interrupt impulse and check the consequences before acting.
modern_relevance: You are one text away from sending the angry message, and your thumb is already hovering. This verse asks for one breath before the damage is done.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि सुर बचन लखन सकुचाने। राम सीयँ सादर सनमाने॥ कही तात तुम्ह नीति सुहाई। सब तें कठिन राजमदु भाई ॥
translation: देववाणी सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी सकुचा गए। श्री रामचंद्रजी और सीताजी ने उनका आदर के साथ सम्मान किया (और कहा-) हे तात! तुमने बड़ी सुंदर नीति कही। हे भाई! राज्य का मद सबसे कठिन मद है ॥
english_translation: Hearing the divine words, Lakshman felt shy. Ram and Sita honored him respectfully. Then Ram said, "Brother, your counsel is excellent. Of all intoxications, the intoxication of power is the hardest to bear."
essence: Power is the most dangerous form of intoxication.
simple_meaning: Lakshman speaks wisely, and Ram agrees that power is the most dangerous kind of pride because it can quietly intoxicate a ruler.
insight: It shifts attention from external power to the inner discipline needed to hold it cleanly.
modern_relevance: You get promoted, people start agreeing with you, and soon every decision feels obviously right. Ram points to the hidden danger: status can make even good judgment wobble.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जो अचवँत नृप मातहिं तेई। नाहिन साधुसभा जेहिं सेई॥ सुनहू लखन भल भरत सरीसा। बिधि प्रपंच महँ सुना न दीसा ॥
translation: जिन्होंने साधुओं की सभा का सेवन (सत्संग) नहीं किया, वे ही राजा राजमद रूपी मदिरा का आचमन करते ही (पीते ही) मतवाले हो जाते हैं। हे लक्ष्मण! सुनो, भरत सरीखा उत्तम पुरुष ब्रह्मा की सृष्टि में न तो कहीं सुना गया है, न देखा ही गया है ॥
english_translation: Those who have not kept company with the good become drunk with royal pride at the first taste of power. Listen, Lakshman: Bharat is so excellent that his like has neither been heard of nor seen in the created world.
essence: Power intoxicates the untrained; Bharat proves nobility can stay untouched.
simple_meaning: People who avoid the company of the good become intoxicated by power, but Bharat is held up as unmatched in virtue.
insight: It shifts attention from status to the moral discipline that keeps status from corrupting you.
modern_relevance: You get promoted, and suddenly everyone laughs a little louder around you. The verse warns that status can distort you unless your circle keeps you honest.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भरतहि होइ न राजमदु बिधि हरि हर पद पाइ। कबहुँ कि काँजी सीकरनि छीरसिंधु बिनसाइ ॥
translation: (अयोध्या के राज्य की तो बात ही क्या है) ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और महादेव का पद पाकर भी भरत को राज्य का मद नहीं होने का! क्या कभी काँजी की बूँदों से क्षीरसमुद्र नष्ट हो सकता (फट सकता) है? ॥
english_translation: Bharat would not become proud of kingship even if he attained the positions of Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh. Can a drop of sour whey ever spoil the ocean of milk?
essence: Greatness cannot inflate a heart already filled with devotion.
simple_meaning: Bharat is so humble that even the highest power would not make him arrogant. His character is too vast to be spoiled by status.
insight: It shifts attention from status itself to the inner steadiness that status can either expose or fail to disturb.
modern_relevance: You get promoted, praised, and suddenly everyone is calling you important. Bharat’s example says the real test is whether success changes your heart at all.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तिमिरु तरुन तरनिहि मकु गिलई। गगनु मगन मकु मेघहिं मिलई॥ गोपद जल बूड़हिं घटजोनी। सहज छमा बरु छाड़ै छोनी ॥
translation: अन्धकार चाहे तरुण (मध्याह्न के) सूर्य को निगल जाए। आकाश चाहे बादलों में समाकर मिल जाए। गो के खुर इतने जल में अगस्त्यजी डूब जाएँ और पृथ्वी चाहे अपनी स्वाभाविक क्षमा (सहनशीलता) को छोड़ दे ॥
english_translation: Darkness may swallow the midday sun. The sky may merge into the clouds. Water in a cow's hoofprint may drown Agastya, and the earth may abandon its natural patience.
essence: Status cannot corrupt a heart already free of craving.
simple_meaning: The poet says impossible things may happen first: darkness may swallow the sun, the sky may vanish into clouds, and even the earth may lose its patience. But Bharat will still not be proud of power.
insight: It teaches you to see Bharat's character as proof that power does not have to corrupt the heart.
modern_relevance: You get handed a promotion that could change how everyone sees you. Even then, the part of you shaped by service can stay untouched by status.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मसक फूँक मकु मेरु उड़ाई। होइ न नृपमदु भरतहि भाई॥ लखन तुम्हार सपथ पितु आना। सुचि सुबंधु नहिं भरत समाना ॥
translation: मच्छर की फूँक से चाहे सुमेरु उड़ जाए, परन्तु हे भाई! भरत को राजमद कभी नहीं हो सकता। हे लक्ष्मण! मैं तुम्हारी शपथ और पिताजी की सौगंध खाकर कहता हूँ, भरत के समान पवित्र और उत्तम भाई संसार में नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Even if Mount Meru were blown away by a mosquito's breath, Bharat would never feel royal pride, brother. Lakshman, I swear by you and by my father's vow: there is no brother in the world as pure and noble as Bharat.
essence: Power cannot corrupt a heart that has no pride.
simple_meaning: Bharat is so pure and humble that even the greatest power would not make him arrogant. Ram also declares him the noblest brother of all.
insight: It shifts admiration away from status and toward character that stays clean under pressure.
modern_relevance: Someone gets promoted and suddenly talks differently, but one person in the circle stays exactly the same — steady, modest, impossible to corrupt. That is the kind of character Ram is praising here.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सगुनु खीरु अवगुन जलु ताता। मिलइ रचइ परपंचु बिधाता॥ भरतु हंस रबिबंस तड़ागा। जनमि कीन्ह गुन दोष बिभागा ॥
translation: हे तात! गुरु रूपी दूध और अवगुण रूपी जल को मिलाकर विधाता इस दृश्य प्रपंच (जगत् ) को रचता है, परन्तु भरत ने सूर्यवंश रूपी तालाब में हंस रूप जन्म लेकर गुण और दोष का विभाग कर दिया (दोनों को अलग-अलग कर दिया) ॥
english_translation: O dear one, the Creator mixes the milk of virtues with the water of faults to make this visible world. Bharat was born like a swan in the lake of the solar dynasty, separating virtue from defect.
essence: Real nobility separates what is worth keeping from what is not.
simple_meaning: The world is a mixture of good and bad, but Bharat is like a swan that knows how to separate them. He does not get confused by appearances.
insight: It trains the mind to discern value without being seduced by confusion.
modern_relevance: A group chat is full of half-truths, gossip, and panic, but you don't have to absorb all of it. Like Bharat, you can keep your judgment clean and choose what deserves your trust.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गहि गुन पय तजि अवगुण बारी। निज जस जगत कीन्हि उजिआरी॥ कहत भरत गुन सीलु सुभाऊ। पेम पयोधि मगन रघुराऊ ॥
translation: गुणरूपी दूध को ग्रहण कर और अवगुण रूपी जल को त्यागकर भरत ने अपने यश से जगत् में उजियाला कर दिया है। भरतजी के गुण, शील और स्वभाव को कहते-कहते श्री रघुनाथजी प्रेमसमुद्र में मग्न हो गए ॥
english_translation: Accepting the milk of virtue and discarding the water of fault, Bharat has brightened the world with his own fame. As he spoke of Bharat's character, conduct, and nature, Raghunath himself became immersed in the ocean of love.
essence: Virtue shines so clearly that even Ram is swept into love.
simple_meaning: Bharat's virtues are being praised as the light that reveals his true greatness. Hearing that praise, Ram becomes lost in love for him.
insight: It shifts attention from judging a person by flaws to seeing the light their character gives others.
modern_relevance: A room full of people is talking about someone who never tries to defend himself. The more honestly his character is named, the more respect he earns without asking for it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि रघुबर बानी बिबुध देखि भरत पर हेतु। सकल सराहत राम सो प्रभु को कृपानिकेतु ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी की वाणी सुनकर और भरतजी पर उनका प्रेम देखकर समस्त देवता उनकी सराहना करने लगे (और कहने लगे) कि श्री रामचंद्रजी के समान कृपा के धाम प्रभु और कौन है? ॥
english_translation: Hearing Ram's words and seeing His love for Bharat, all the radiant beings praised Him, saying: who is a lord more filled with grace than Ram?
essence: True lordship is revealed by compassion, not command.
simple_meaning: Ram's gentle words and his affection for Bharat make the radiant beings praise him as the very home of compassion.
insight: It shifts admiration from achievement to the quality of your care for others.
modern_relevance: You defend someone who has been misunderstood, even when it costs you status. People notice less than you expect, but the ones who see clearly know what grace looks like.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जौं न होत जग जनम भरत को। सकल धरम धुर धरनि धरत को॥ कबि कुल अगम भरत गुन गाथा। को जानइ तुम्ह बिनु रघुनाथा ॥
translation: यदि जगत् में भरत का जन्म न होता, तो पृथ्वी पर संपूर्ण धर्मों की धुरी को कौन धारण करता? हे रघुनाथजी! कविकुल के लिए अगम (उनकी कल्पना से अतीत) भरतजी के गुणों की कथा आपके सिवा और कौन जान सकता है? ॥
english_translation: If Bharat had not been born in the world, who would have carried the pole of all dharma on earth? O Raghunath, who besides you can truly know the immeasurable story of Bharat's virtues?
essence: Bharat's hidden virtue is so deep only Ram can measure it.
simple_meaning: Bharat is praised as the one who upheld all righteous duty on earth, and his virtues are said to be beyond ordinary understanding.
insight: It shifts respect from public achievement to the unseen weight of steadfast character.
modern_relevance: When you quietly keep a promise no one else would notice, the work may look small from outside. But the people who truly matter know what it cost you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: लखन राम सियँ सुनि सुर बानी। अति सुखु लहेउ न जाइ बखानी॥ इहाँ भरतु सब सहित सहाए। मंदाकिनीं पुनीत नहाए ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामचंद्रजी और सीताजी ने देवताओं की वाणी सुनकर अत्यंत सुख पाया, जो वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। यहाँ भरतजी ने सारे समाज के साथ पवित्र मंदाकिनी में स्नान किया ॥
english_translation: Lakshman, Ram, and Sita heard the words of the radiant beings and felt a joy beyond description. Here Bharat, along with everyone present, bathed in the pure Mandakini.
essence: Joy and purity arrive together when the heart is ready.
simple_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita felt indescribable joy on hearing the divine message. Bharat and everyone with him bathed in the holy Mandakini.
insight: It shifts attention from explanation to direct experience, letting joy and reverence arrive before analysis.
modern_relevance: You get a message that changes everything, and for a second you just sit there smiling. Later you can explain it. First, you simply feel it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सरित समीप राखि सब लोगा। मागि मातु गुर सचिव नियोगा॥ चले भरतु जहँ सिय रघुराई। साथ निषादनाथु लघु भाई ॥
translation: फिर सबको नदी के समीप ठहराकर तथा माता, गुरु और मंत्री की आज्ञा माँगकर निषादराज और शत्रुघ्न को साथ लेकर भरतजी वहाँ चले जहाँ श्री सीताजी और श्री रघुनाथजी थे ॥।
english_translation: Then, leaving everyone by the riverbank and asking permission from his mother, his teacher, and his ministers, Bharat went with Nishadraj and Shatrughna to where Sita and Raghurai were.
essence: Devotion does not erase duty; it deepens it.
simple_meaning: Bharat leaves the group safely by the river, seeks permission from his mother, teacher, and ministers, and then goes with Nishadraj and Shatrughna to Ram and Sita.
insight: It teaches you to act with devotion without dropping your responsibilities to others.
modern_relevance: You want to rush into a hard conversation, but you still check in with the people who depend on you. Bharat shows that urgency can stay respectful.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समुझि मातु करतब सकुचाहीं। करत कुतरक कोटि मन माहीं॥ रामु लखनु सिय सुनि मम नाऊँ। उठि जनि अनत जाहिं तजि ठाऊँ ॥
translation: भरतजी अपनी माता कैकेयी की करनी को समझकर (याद करके) सकुचाते हैं और मन में करोड़ों (अनेकों) कुतर्क करते हैं (सोचते हैं) श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीताजी मेरा नाम सुनकर स्थान छोड़कर कहीं दूसरी जगह उठकर न चले जाएँ ॥
english_translation: Thinking of his mother’s deed, Bharata feels shy and keeps turning over countless thoughts in his mind: “If Ram, Lakshman, and Sita hear my name, may they not rise and leave this place, abandoning it.”
essence: Shame makes even your own name feel like a burden.
simple_meaning: Bharat feels ashamed remembering Kaikeyi’s deed and worries that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita might leave if they hear his name.
insight: It shows how deep remorse makes a person watch the effect of their very presence on others.
modern_relevance: You send a message after a family fight, then stare at the screen wondering whether your name will reopen the wound. Bharat knows that ache of being associated with pain.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मातु मते महुँ मानि मोहि जो कछु करहिं सो थोर। अघ अवगुन छमि आदरहिं समुझि आपनी ओर ॥
translation: मुझे माता के मत में मानकर वे जो कुछ भी करें सो थोड़ा है, पर वे अपनी ओर समझकर (अपने विरद और संबंध को देखकर) मेरे पापों और अवगुणों को क्षमा करके मेरा आदर ही करेंगे ॥
english_translation: Considering my mother's counsel, whatever they do is little; they will forgive my faults and honor me, seeing me as their own.
essence: Love can be stronger than the faults it sees.
simple_meaning: Bharat trusts that his family will judge him with compassion, not harshness. Even if they see his faults, they will still honor him as one of their own.
insight: It shifts you from expecting judgment to trusting relationship can hold imperfection.
modern_relevance: You send the message after the awkward family fight, expecting blame. Instead, the person who knows your worst habits still answers with warmth. That kind of mercy changes everything.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जौं परिहरहिं मलिन मनु जानी। जौं सनमानहिं सेवकु मानी॥ मोरें सरन रामहि की पनही। राम सुस्वामि दोसु सब जनही ॥
translation: चाहे मलिन मन जानकर मुझे त्याग दें, चाहे अपना सेवक मानकर मेरा सम्मान करें, (कुछ भी करें), मेरे तो श्री रामचंद्रजी की जूतियाँ ही शरण हैं। श्री रामचंद्रजी तो अच्छे स्वामी हैं, दोष तो सब दास का ही है ॥
english_translation: Even if they cast me off as impure, even if they honor me as a servant, my refuge is only Ram's sandals. Ram is a good master; the fault is all the servant's.
essence: Your worth does not depend on praise when your refuge is Ram.
simple_meaning: Bharat says people may judge him any way they want, but he belongs to Ram alone. He places all fault on himself and all refuge in Ram.
insight: It shifts you from self-defense to surrender, letting Ram be the only court that matters.
modern_relevance: A family group chat is tearing your name apart, and you can feel the urge to explain yourself. This verse says your center does not have to move with their verdict.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जग जग भाजन चातक मीना। नेम पेम निज निपुन नबीना॥ अस मन गुनत चले मग जाता। सकुच सनेहँ सिथिल सब गाता ॥
translation: जगत् में यश के पात्र तो चातक और मछली ही हैं, जो अपने नेम और प्रेम को सदा नया बनाए रखने में निपुण हैं। ऐसा मन में सोचते हुए भरतजी मार्ग में चले जाते हैं। उनके सब अंग संकोच और प्रेम से शिथिल हो रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: In the world, only the chatak bird and the fish are truly praiseworthy, because they keep their vow and love forever fresh. Thinking this in his heart, Bharat keeps walking along the road. All his limbs are softened by modesty and love.
essence: True devotion stays fresh, even as the body grows tender.
simple_meaning: Bharat thinks of the chatak bird and the fish as examples of pure, steady love, then keeps walking with his body weakened by humility and affection.
insight: It shifts devotion from a feeling into a steady, embodied way of moving.
modern_relevance: You keep walking to someone you love after a hard conversation, replaying what they mean to you. The body grows heavy, but the heart stays loyal.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: फेरति मनहुँ मातु कृत खोरी। चलत भगति बल धीरज धोरी॥ जब समुझत रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। तब पथ परत उताइल पाऊ ॥
translation: माता की हुई बुराई मानो उन्हें लौटाती है, पर धीरज की धुरी को धारण करने वाले भरतजी भक्ति के बल से चले जाते हैं। जब श्री रघुनाथजी के स्वभाव को समझते (स्मरण करते) हैं तब मार्ग में उनके पैर जल्दी-जल्दी पड़ने लगते हैं ॥
english_translation: The insult to their mother seems to turn them back, but Bharat carries the weight of patience and moves on through devotion. When they remember Shri Raghunath's nature, their feet hurry along the road.
essence: Devotion can make even wounded feet hurry forward.
simple_meaning: Even when hurt makes you want to turn back, devotion and patience keep you walking forward. Remembering Ram's nature gives Bharat new strength and speeds his steps.
insight: It shifts the mind from injury-driven withdrawal to devotion-driven perseverance.
modern_relevance: You get a message that reopens an old family wound, and for a moment you want to shut down. Then you remember the person you are trying to remain loyal to, and you keep going anyway.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत दसा तेहि अवसर कैसी। जल प्रबाहँ जल अलि गति जैसी॥ देखि भरत कर सोचु सनेहू। भा निषाद तेहि समयँ बिदेहू ॥
translation: उस समय भरत की दशा कैसी है? जैसी जल के प्रवाह में जल के भौंरे की गति होती है। भरतजी का सोच और प्रेम देखकर उस समय निषाद विदेह हो गया (देह की सुध-बुध भूल गया) ॥
english_translation: What was Bharat's state at that moment? Like the movement of a water beetle in flowing water. Seeing Bharat's sorrow and love, Nishad became lost to his body.
essence: Love so pure can make even a witness forget himself.
simple_meaning: Bharat's grief and love are so intense that even Nishad loses all sense of his body while watching him.
insight: It shifts attention from events to the force of devotion they awaken in others.
modern_relevance: You watch someone arrive at a funeral carrying both grief and love, and the room goes quiet. Their sincerity is so complete that everyone feels it before anyone speaks.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लगे होन मंगल सगुन सुनि गुनि कहत निषादु। मिटिहि सोचु होइहि हरषु पुनि परिनाम बिषादु ॥
translation: मंगल शकुन होने लगे। उन्हें सुनकर और विचारकर निषाद कहने लगा- सोच मिटेगा, हर्ष होगा, पर फिर अन्त में दुःख होगा ॥
english_translation: Good omens began to appear. Hearing and considering them, Nishad said, 'Sorrow will fade, joy will arise, but in the end grief will return.'
essence: Hope can arrive first, while grief still waits behind it.
simple_meaning: Nishad notices good omens, but he can already feel the mixed fate ahead: relief now, joy later, sorrow again at the end.
insight: It teaches you to hold joy without pretending pain has vanished.
modern_relevance: You finally get a hopeful message after days of dread, but you still know the hard part isn't over. Relief arrives first; the deeper wound may still remain.
speaker: Nishad

verse_text: सेवक बचन सत्य सब जाने। आश्रम निकट जाइ निअराने॥ भरत दीख बन सैल समाजू। मुदित छुधित जनु पाइ सुनाजू ॥
translation: भरतजी ने सेवक (गुह) के सब वचन सत्य जाने और वे आश्रम के समीप जा पहुँचे। वहाँ के वन और पर्वतों के समूह को देखा तो भरतजी इतने आनंदित हुए मानो कोई भूखा अच्छा अन्न (भोजन) पा गया हो ॥
english_translation: Bharat accepted the servant's words as true and came near the hermitage. Seeing the forest and the hills there, he was delighted like a hungry person who has found fine food.
essence: Love makes even the approach feel like fulfillment.
simple_meaning: Bharat trusts the servant's words and moves closer to the hermitage. Seeing the forest and hills, he feels deep joy, like a hungry person finding a good meal.
insight: It shifts attention from the destination itself to the joy of nearing what you love.
modern_relevance: You finally reach the quiet road outside a place you have long wanted to visit. Even the trees and the gate feel like relief, because your heart has already arrived.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ईति भीति जनु प्रजा दुखारी। त्रिबिध ताप पीड़ित ग्रह मारी॥ जाइ सुराज सुदेस सुखारी। होहिं भरत गति तेहि अनुहारी ॥
translation: जैसे ईति के भय से दुःखी हुई और तीनों (आध्यात्मिक, आधिदैविक और आधिभौतिक) तापों तथा क्रूर ग्रहों और महामारियों से पीड़ित प्रजा किसी उत्तम देश और उत्तम राज्य में जाकर सुखी हो जाए, भरतजी की गति (दशा) ठीक उसी प्रकार हो रही है ॥ (अधिक जल बरसना, न बरसना, चूहों का उत्पात, टिड्डियाँ, तोते और दूसरे राजा की चढ़ाई- खेतों में बाधा देने वाले इन छह उपद्रवों को 'ईति' कहते हैं)।
english_translation: Like a people made miserable by plague, the three kinds of suffering, cruel planets, and disasters becoming happy after reaching a good land and a good kingdom, Bharata is now in exactly that state.
essence: Bharata's grief is like a people escaping disaster into safety.
simple_meaning: Bharata's condition is compared to a suffering people who finally reach a safe, prosperous kingdom and feel relief.
insight: It shifts the reader to feel Bharata's sorrow as a public disaster, not a private mood.
modern_relevance: You finally get home after days of bad news, missed calls, and a stomach that never unclenched. The relief is real, but it arrives after too much strain.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम बास बन संपति भ्राजा। सुखी प्रजा जनु पाइ सुराजा॥ सचिव बिरागु बिबेकु नरेसू। बिपिन सुहावन पावन देसू ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी के निवास से वन की सम्पत्ति ऐसी सुशोभित है मानो अच्छे राजा को पाकर प्रजा सुखी हो। सुहावना वन ही पवित्र देश है। विवेक उसका राजा है और वैराग्य मंत्री है ॥
english_translation: Ram's presence makes the forest shine like a prosperous kingdom. A lovely forest becomes a holy land, with discernment as king and non-attachment as minister.
essence: Ram's presence turns exile into a kingdom of peace.
simple_meaning: Ram's presence transforms the forest into a place of peace and order. The real rulers there are discernment and non-attachment.
insight: It shifts attention from outer conditions to the quality of presence that shapes them.
modern_relevance: You walk into a cramped apartment after a hard week, and somehow it feels calm because one steady person is there. Presence changes a place more than furniture, money, or status ever can.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भट जम नियम सैल रजधानी। सांति सुमति सुचि सुंदर रानी॥ सकल अंग संपन्न सुराऊ। राम चरन आश्रित चित चाऊ ॥
translation: यम (अहिंसा, सत्य, अस्तेय, ब्रह्मचर्य और अपरिग्रह) तथा नियम (शौच, संतोष, तप, स्वाध्याय और ईश्वर प्रणिधान) योद्धा हैं। पर्वत राजधानी है, शांति तथा सुबुद्धि दो सुंदर पवित्र रानियाँ हैं। वह श्रेष्ठ राजा राज्य के सब अंगों से पूर्ण है और श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणों के आश्रित रहने से उसके चित्त में चाव (आनंद या उत्साह) है ॥ (स्वामी, आमत्य, सुहृद, कोष, राष्ट्र, दुर्ग और सेना- राज्य के सात अंग हैं।)
english_translation: The warriors are Yama and Niyama. The capital is a mountain. Peace and wise understanding are the two beautiful, pure queens. The king is complete in every part of a noble kingdom, and his mind delights in shelter at Ram's feet.
essence: A disciplined inner kingdom begins when the mind rests in Ram.
simple_meaning: A well-ordered life has discipline, peace, and wise judgment. When the mind rests at Ram's feet, everything in that inner kingdom comes together.
insight: It shifts you from chasing control to building an inner structure that can actually hold calm.
modern_relevance: After a week of broken sleep, missed meals, and scattered focus, you finally clean your room, fix your routine, and notice your mind softening. Order outside begins to restore order inside.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जीति मोह महिपालु दल सहित बिबेक भुआलु। करत अकंटक राजु पुरँ सुख संपदा सुकालु ॥
translation: मोह रूपी राजा को सेना सहित जीतकर विवेक रूपी राजा निष्कण्टक राज्य कर रहा है। उसके नगर में सुख, सम्पत्ति और सुकाल वर्तमान है ॥
english_translation: Having conquered delusion, the discerning king now rules with his army. In his city, happiness, wealth, and good times flourish without obstruction.
essence: Clear seeing takes power when delusion is defeated.
simple_meaning: When confusion is conquered, clear understanding governs life freely, and peace, prosperity, and good fortune follow.
insight: It shifts attention from mental fog to the quiet authority of discernment.
modern_relevance: You finally stop replaying the same argument in your head at 2 a.m. Once confusion loses its grip, your home, work, and choices all feel less cramped.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: बन प्रदेस मुनि बास घनेरे। जनु पुर नगर गाउँ गन खेरे॥ बिपुल बिचित्र बिहग मृग नाना। प्रजा समाजु न जाइ बखाना ॥
translation: वन रूपी प्रांतों में जो मुनियों के बहुत से निवास स्थान हैं, वही मानो शहरों, नगरों, गाँवों और खेड़ों का समूह है। बहुत से विचित्र पक्षी और अनेकों पशु ही मानो प्रजाओं का समाज है, जिसका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
english_translation: The forest regions, where many sages live, are like a spread of cities, towns, villages, and hamlets. The many varied birds and countless animals are like a population beyond description.
essence: The forest becomes a kingdom when you learn to see its life.
simple_meaning: The forest is described like a living kingdom, full of sages, birds, and animals, as if it were a populated land.
insight: It shifts your attention from seeing wilderness as vacant to seeing it as a full, ordered world.
modern_relevance: You step into a quiet park after a brutal week and notice it is not empty at all. Every tree, bird, and animal feels like part of a larger, breathing community.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: खगहा करि हरि बाघ बराहा। देखि महिष बृष साजु सराहा॥ बयरु बिहाइ चरहिं एक संगा। जहँ तहँ मनहुँ सेन चतुरंगा ॥
translation: गैंडा, हाथी, सिंह, बाघ, सूअर, भैंसे और बैलों को देखकर राजा के साज को सराहते ही बनता है। ये सब आपस का वैर छोड़कर जहाँ-तहाँ एक साथ विचरते हैं। यही मानो चतुरंगिणी सेना है ॥
english_translation: Seeing rhinoceroses, elephants, lions, tigers, boars, buffaloes, and bulls, even a king would praise the splendor. They have given up enmity and roam together everywhere, like a four-part army.
essence: When enmity drops, even wildness looks like order.
simple_meaning: Wild animals are roaming together peacefully, as if they were one army. The scene is being used to describe the forest as orderly and full of life.
insight: It shifts attention from conflict to the hidden order that can appear when hostility falls away.
modern_relevance: You walk into a park where stray dogs, pigeons, and children all share the same path without tension. The scene feels almost arranged, as if nature itself had found its order.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: झरना झरहिं मत्त गज गाजहिं। मनहुँ निसान बिबिधि बिधि बाजहिं॥ चक चकोर चातक सुक पिक गन। कूजत मंजु मराल मुदित मन ॥
translation: पानी के झरने झर रहे हैं और मतवाले हाथी चिंघाड़ रहे हैं। मानो वहाँ अनेकों प्रकार के नगाड़े बज रहे हैं। चकवा, चकोर, पपीहा, तोता तथा कोयलों के समूह और सुंदर हंस प्रसन्न मन से कूज रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Waterfalls tumble down and wild elephants trumpet, as if many kinds of drums are sounding. Chakravaka, chakor, chatak, parrots, cuckoos, and graceful swans all call out joyfully.
essence: Nature itself is singing in celebration.
simple_meaning: The forest is so alive and beautiful that its sounds seem like music: waterfalls, elephants, and birds all create a joyful scene.
insight: It shifts attention from plot to atmosphere, letting the reader feel the forest as a sacred, living place.
modern_relevance: You step off a crowded train into a rain-soaked park, and every sound feels brighter than usual. The world itself seems to be breathing with you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अलिगन गावत नाचत मोरा। जनु सुराज मंगल चहु ओरा॥ बेलि बिटप तृन सफल सफूला। सब समाजु मुद मंगल मूला ॥
translation: भौंरों के समूह गुंजार कर रहे हैं और मोर नाच रहे हैं। मानो उस अच्छे राज्य में चारों ओर मंगल हो रहा है। बेल, वृक्ष, तृण सब फल और फूलों से युक्त हैं। सारा समाज आनंद और मंगल का मूल बन रहा है ॥
english_translation: Bees hum and peacocks dance, as if a noble reign has brought auspiciousness everywhere. Vines, trees, and grasses are full of fruit and flowers; the whole society becomes the source of joy and blessing.
essence: Right order makes even nature look joyful and full.
simple_meaning: The landscape itself seems alive with joy, as if good rule has made everything flourish. Nature and society both look fruitful, harmonious, and blessed.
insight: It shifts attention from private feeling to the atmosphere created by right order and harmony.
modern_relevance: You walk into a neighborhood after the rain and notice children playing, shopkeepers smiling, and even the trees looking brighter. Sometimes a place feels cared for before anyone says a word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम सैल सोभा निरखि भरत हृदयँ अति पेमु। तापस तप फलु पाइ जिमि सुखी सिरानें नेमु ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के पर्वत की शोभा देखकर भरतजी के हृदय में अत्यंत प्रेम हुआ। जैसे तपस्वी नियम की समाप्ति होने पर तपस्या का फल पाकर सुखी होता है ॥
english_translation: Seeing the beauty of Ram's mountain, Bharat felt deep love in his heart, like a ascetic who has gained the fruit of discipline and rests in joy when the vow is complete.
essence: Love can feel like the reward for years of waiting.
simple_meaning: Bharat sees the beauty of the mountain where Ram is staying, and his heart overflows with love. It feels like the joy of a seeker who finally receives the reward of long discipline.
insight: It turns longing into fulfilled devotion, showing that the heart can find joy even before the journey is complete.
modern_relevance: You finally reach the place you have been aching to see — a childhood home, a pilgrimage site, a hospital room after long waiting — and your chest loosens before words can come.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब केवट ऊँचे चढ़ि धाई। कहेउ भरत सन भुजा उठाई॥ नाथ देखिअहिं बिटप बिसाला। पाकरि जंबु रसाल तमाला ॥
translation: तब केवट दौड़कर ऊँचे चढ़ गया और भुजा उठाकर भरजी से कहने लगा- हे नाथ! ये जो पाकर, जामुन, आम और तमाल के विशाल वृक्ष दिखाई देते हैं, ॥
english_translation: Then the boatman climbed up quickly and, raising his arm, said to Bharat, "My lord, look at these great trees: pakar, jamun, mango, and tamal."
essence: The scene pauses to let the forest be seen.
simple_meaning: The boatman points out the names of the large trees around them. It is a scenic detail, not a teaching.
insight: It shifts attention from plot to place, preparing the mind for the fuller image that comes next.
modern_relevance: You slow down on a road trip and someone in the car starts naming the trees, as if the world itself deserves a second look.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जिन्ह तरुबरन्ह मध्य बटु सोहा। मंजु बिसाल देखि मनु मोहा॥ नील सघन पल्लव फल लाला। अबिरल छाहँ सुखद सब काला ॥
translation: जिन श्रेष्ठ वृक्षों के बीच में एक सुंदर विशाल बड़ का वृक्ष सुशोभित है, जिसको देखकर मन मोहित हो जाता है, उसके पत्ते नीले और सघन हैं और उसमें लाल फल लगे हैं। उसकी घनी छाया सब ऋतुओं में सुख देने वाली है ॥
english_translation: Among the finest trees stands a beautiful, विशाल banyan tree. Its sight captivates the mind. Its dense blue leaves and red fruit give cool shade in every season.
essence: The most beautiful thing here is also the most sheltering.
simple_meaning: A huge banyan tree stands out among the other trees, and its beauty draws the eye. Its thick shade stays pleasant through every season.
insight: It trains attention to notice what quietly protects and comforts, not only what is impressive.
modern_relevance: You turn off a dusty road and spot one tree giving shade to everyone waiting nearby. It feels like relief before you even sit down.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मानहुँ तिमिर अरुनमय रासी। बिरची बिधि सँकेलि सुषमा सी॥ ए तरु सरित समीप गोसाँई। रघुबर परनकुटी जहँ छाई ॥
translation: मानो ब्रह्माजी ने परम शोभा को एकत्र करके अंधकार और लालिमामयी राशि सी रच दी है। हे गुसाईं! ये वृक्ष नदी के समीप हैं, जहाँ श्री राम की पर्णकुटी छाई है ॥
english_translation: It looks as if Brahma gathered all beauty together and shaped it into a mass of darkness and red glow. O master, these trees stand by the river, where Ram's leaf-hut rests.
essence: Beauty becomes unforgettable when it surrounds Ram's resting place.
simple_meaning: The forest is so beautiful that it feels like all beauty itself has been gathered into one place. The trees stand near the river where Ram's hut is built.
insight: It trains the eye to see ordinary nature as sacred when it is touched by devotion.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a quiet riverside camp and suddenly notice how the whole place feels charged because someone you love once lived there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तुलसी तरुबर बिबिध सुहाए। कहुँ कहुँ सियँ कहुँ लखन लगाए॥ बट छायाँ बेदिका बनाई। सियँ निज पानि सरोज सुहाई ॥
translation: वहाँ तुलसीजी के बहुत से सुंदर वृक्ष सुशोभित हैं, जो कहीं-कहीं सीताजी ने और कहीं लक्ष्मणजी ने लगाए हैं। इसी बड़ की छाया में सीताजी ने अपने करकमलों से सुंदर वेदी बनाई है ॥
english_translation: There are many beautiful trees there, planted here and there by Sita and Lakshman. Beneath the banyan's shade, Sita herself has made a lovely altar with her own hands.
essence: Love can turn exile into a home.
simple_meaning: Sita and Lakshman have made the forest dwelling beautiful and sacred. Sita has even built a small altar under the banyan tree with her own hands.
insight: It shifts attention from loss to the quiet power of making sacred space through simple acts.
modern_relevance: You move into a bare rented room and slowly make it feel like home — a plant by the window, a clean corner, a place to sit quietly. Care turns hardship into shelter.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहाँ बैठि मुनिगन सहित नित सिय रामु सुजान। सुनहिं कथा इतिहास सब आगम निगम पुरान ॥
translation: जहाँ सुजान श्री सीता-रामजी मुनियों के वृन्द समेत बैठकर नित्य शास्त्र, वेद और पुराणों के सब कथा-इतिहास सुनते हैं ॥
english_translation: Where wise Sita and Ram sit each day with the sages, listening to all the stories and histories of the scriptures, Vedas, and Puranas.
essence: Greatness can sit quietly and still receive wisdom.
simple_meaning: Sita and Ram spend their days among sages, listening respectfully to sacred stories and teachings.
insight: It shifts admiration toward humility: real nobility can include listening deeply.
modern_relevance: You sit in a room full of expertise and still choose to listen instead of perform. That quiet respect can be its own kind of greatness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सखा बचन सुनि बिटप निहारी। उमगे भरत बिलोचन बारी॥ करत प्रनाम चले दोउ भाई। कहत प्रीति सारद सकुचाई ॥
translation: सखा के वचन सुनकर और वृक्षों को देखकर भरतजी के नेत्रों में जल उमड़ आया। दोनों भाई प्रणाम करते हुए चले। उनके प्रेम का वर्णन करने में सरस्वतीजी भी सकुचाती हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing his friend's words and seeing the trees, Bharata's eyes overflowed with tears. The two brothers walked on with bows of reverence, and even Saraswati would feel shy trying to describe their love.
essence: True devotion is so deep that even words fall silent.
simple_meaning: Bharata is overwhelmed with emotion as he sees the sacred place and walks onward with Lakshmana in reverence. Their love is so deep that even language feels inadequate.
insight: It shifts attention from explaining love to embodying it through reverence, tears, and humble action.
modern_relevance: You stand in a place that still holds someone's memory — a park bench, an empty room, a road you once walked together — and your chest tightens before you can explain why.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरषहिं निरखि राम पद अंका। मानहुँ पारसु पायउ रंका॥ रज सिर धरि हियँ नयनन्हि लावहिं। रघुबर मिलन सरिस सुख पावहिं ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणचिह्न देखकर दोनों भाई ऐसे हर्षित होते हैं, मानो दरिद्र पारस पा गया हो। वहाँ की रज को मस्तक पर रखकर हृदय में और नेत्रों में लगाते हैं और श्री रघुनाथजी के मिलने के समान सुख पाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ram's footprints, both brothers rejoice as if a poor man has found a touchstone. They place the dust on their heads, hold it in their hearts and eyes, and feel the joy of meeting Raghubar himself.
essence: A beloved's trace can feel as fulfilling as meeting them.
simple_meaning: Just seeing Ram's footprints fills the brothers with joy. They treat even the dust as sacred and feel as happy as if they had met Ram himself.
insight: It shifts attention from needing direct contact to recognising how love animates every sign.
modern_relevance: You find an old voice note from someone you miss and listen three times. The sound is tiny, but your whole chest changes. Presence can live in a trace.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि भरत गति अकथ अतीवा। प्रेम मगन मृग खग जड़ जीवा॥ सखहि सनेह बिबस मग भूला। कहि सुपंथ सुर बरषहिं फूला ॥
translation: भरतजी की अत्यन्त अनिर्वचनीय दशा देखकर वन के पशु, पक्षी और जड़ (वृक्षादि) जीव प्रेम में मग्न हो गए। प्रेम के विशेष वश होने से सखा निषादराज को भी रास्ता भूल गया। तब देवता सुंदर रास्ता बतलाकर फूल बरसाने लगे ॥
english_translation: Seeing Bharata's utterly indescribable state, the beasts, birds, and even motionless beings were filled with love. Overcome by affection, his companion, the boatman, lost the path. Then the radiant beings showed the right way and showered flowers.
essence: True devotion is so strong it changes the world around it.
simple_meaning: Bharat's love is so overwhelming that even the forest creatures feel it. His companion loses the way, and the radiant beings help guide them and honor the moment with flowers.
insight: It shows how devotion can transform a whole environment, not just the person feeling it.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room carrying real grief, and everyone feels the weight before you speak. Some moods are that powerful.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निरखि सिद्ध साधक अनुरागे। सहज सनेहु सराहन लागे॥ होत न भूतल भाउ भरत को। अचर सचर चर अचर करत को ॥
translation: भरत के प्रेम की इस स्थिति को देखकर सिद्ध और साधक लोग भी अनुराग से भर गए और उनके स्वाभाविक प्रेम की प्रशंसा करने लगे कि यदि इस पृथ्वी तल पर भरत का जन्म (अथवा प्रेम) न होता, तो जड़ को चेतन और चेतन को जड़ कौन करता? ॥
english_translation: Seeing Bharata's love, even perfected sages and seekers were filled with devotion and praised his natural affection: if Bharata's love had not appeared on earth, who could make the lifeless living and the living lifeless?
essence: Selfless love can make the impossible feel natural.
simple_meaning: Bharata's love is so pure that even sages are moved by it. His affection is praised as something that can transform the impossible.
insight: It shifts attention from outward success to the transforming power of selfless devotion.
modern_relevance: You watch someone give up status, comfort, and control just to honor a promise. The room goes quiet, because everyone can feel that this kind of love is rarer than achievement.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पेम अमिअ मंदरु बिरहु भरतु पयोधि गँभीर। मथि प्रगटेउ सुर साधु हित कृपासिंधु रघुबीर ॥
translation: प्रेम अमृत है, विरह मंदराचल पर्वत है, भरतजी गहरे समुद्र हैं। कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने देवता और साधुओं के हित के लिए स्वयं (इस भरत रूपी गहरे समुद्र को अपने विरह रूपी मंदराचल से) मथकर यह प्रेम रूपी अमृत प्रकट किया है ॥
english_translation: Love is nectar, separation is Mount Mandara, and Bharat is the deep ocean. For the good of the gods and holy ones, the ocean of mercy, Raghubir, churned it and brought forth this nectar of love.
essence: Separation can become the very force that reveals devotion.
simple_meaning: Love is compared to nectar, separation to the churning rod, and Bharat to a deep ocean. Ram, moved by mercy, brings out devotion's sweetness through Bharat's intense longing.
insight: It teaches you to see longing not as failure, but as the pressure that reveals the depth of love.
modern_relevance: You miss someone so deeply that the ache feels unbearable, yet that very longing keeps your love alive. Sometimes separation doesn't kill devotion — it distills it.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सखा समेत मनोहर जोटा। लखेउ न लखन सघन बन ओटा॥ भरत दीख प्रभु आश्रमु पावन। सकल सुमंगल सदनु सुहावन ॥
translation: सखा निषादराज सहित इस मनोहर जोड़ी को सघन वन की आड़ के कारण लक्ष्मणजी नहीं देख पाए। भरतजी ने प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के समस्त सुमंगलों के धाम और सुंदर पवित्र आश्रम को देखा ॥
english_translation: Lakshman could not see the beautiful pair with his friend Nishadraj because of the dense forest cover. Bharat saw Lord Ram's holy hermitage, lovely and full of all auspiciousness.
essence: Devotion sees the holy place even before reunion happens.
simple_meaning: Lakshman is blocked by the thick forest, but Bharat sees Ram's pure hermitage, a place filled with auspiciousness and beauty.
insight: It shifts attention from obstruction to sacred presence, showing that devotion perceives meaning before the eyes do.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a quiet retreat after a long, aching journey. One person sees only trees and distance; another sees the place where love has been waiting for them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करत प्रबेस मिटे दुख दावा। जनु जोगीं परमारथु पावा॥ देखे भरत लखन प्रभु आगे। पूँछे बचन कहत अनुरागे ॥
translation: आश्रम में प्रवेश करते ही भरतजी का दुःख और दाह (जलन) मिट गया, मानो योगी को परमार्थ (परमतत्व) की प्राप्ति हो गई हो। भरतजी ने देखा कि लक्ष्मणजी प्रभु के आगे खड़े हैं और पूछे हुए वचन प्रेमपूर्वक कह रहे हैं (पूछी हुई बात का प्रेमपूर्वक उत्तर दे रहे हैं) ॥
english_translation: As soon as he entered the hermitage, Bharat's sorrow and burning vanished, as if a yogi had attained the highest truth. He saw Lakshman standing before the Lord, answering questions with love.
essence: Presence can end sorrow before a single word is spoken.
simple_meaning: Bharat enters the hermitage and his grief instantly falls away. Seeing Lakshman before Ram, speaking with love, brings him a deep inner settling.
insight: It shifts the mind from emotional turbulence to quiet release in the presence of what is trusted.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after days of dread, and the person you feared facing is simply there, calm and kind. Your chest loosens before anyone speaks.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीस जटा कटि मुनि पट बाँधें। तून कसें कर सरु धनु काँधें॥ बेदी पर मुनि साधु समाजू। सीय सहित राजत रघुराजू ॥
translation: सिर पर जटा है, कमर में मुनियों का (वल्कल) वस्त्र बाँधे हैं और उसी में तरकस कसे हैं। हाथ में बाण तथा कंधे पर धनुष है, वेदी पर मुनि तथा साधुओं का समुदाय बैठा है और सीताजी सहित श्री रघुनाथजी विराजमान हैं ॥
english_translation: With matted hair on his head, a sage's cloth tied at his waist, a quiver fastened there; bow and arrows in hand and on his shoulder. On the sacred platform, among sages and holy people, Raghuraj shines with Sita beside him.
essence: Renunciation and kingship can live in the same person.
simple_meaning: Ram appears as both a forest sage and a royal figure at once, seated with Sita among holy people on the sacred platform.
insight: It teaches you that true nobility does not depend on outward luxury.
modern_relevance: You show up at a wedding in plain clothes after a hard year, and somehow your calm carries more dignity than anyone's polished display.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बलकल बसन जटिल तनु स्यामा। जनु मुनिबेष कीन्ह रति कामा॥ कर कमलनि धनु सायकु फेरत। जिय की जरनि हरत हँसि हेरत ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के वल्कल वस्त्र हैं, जटा धारण किए हैं, श्याम शरीर है। (सीता-रामजी ऐसे लगते हैं) मानो रति और कामदेव ने मुनि का वेष धारण किया हो। श्री रामजी अपने करकमलों से धनुष-बाण फेर रहे हैं और हँसकर देखते ही जी की जलन हर लेते हैं (अर्थात जिसकी ओर भी एक बार हँसकर देख लेते हैं, उसी को परम आनंद और शांति मिल जाती है।) ॥
english_translation: He wears bark-cloth, his body is matted-haired and dark. It is as if Desire and Love themselves have taken a sage's form. With lotus hands he turns his bow and arrows, and his smiling glance removes the burning from the heart.
essence: Ram's gentle presence cools what desire has burned.
simple_meaning: Ram looks like a sage, yet his beauty is so powerful it feels like Love itself has taken that form. Even his smiling glance cools the heart's burning.
insight: It turns attention from outer appearance to the healing force of presence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a quiet room after weeks of tension, and one calm smile from the right person undoes the whole knot in your chest.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लसत मंजु मुनि मंडली मध्य सीय रघुचंदु। ग्यान सभाँ जनु तनु धरें भगति सच्चिदानंदु ॥
translation: सुंदर मुनि मंडली के बीच में सीताजी और रघुकुलचंद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी ऐसे सुशोभित हो रहे हैं मानो ज्ञान की सभा में साक्षात् भक्ति और सच्चिदानंद शरीर धारण करके विराजमान हैं ॥
english_translation: Beautifully seated among the sages, Sita and Raghunath shine like devotion itself appearing in the assembly of wisdom, as if the supreme being of consciousness and bliss has taken form.
essence: Devotion becomes visible when wisdom becomes a living presence.
simple_meaning: Ram and Sita sit among the sages like devotion itself taking form inside the world of wisdom.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating wisdom and devotion as separate paths to seeing them as one living reality.
modern_relevance: You can be in a room full of experts and still feel the deepest truth is simple love. The most complete understanding often looks less like argument and more like reverent presence.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सानुज सखा समेत मगन मन। बिसरे हरष सोक सुख दुख गन॥ पाहि नाथ कहि पाहि गोसाईं। भूतल परे लकुट की नाईं ॥
translation: छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न और सखा निषादराज समेत भरतजी का मन (प्रेम में) मग्न हो रहा है। हर्ष-शोक, सुख-दुःख आदि सब भूल गए। हे नाथ! रक्षा कीजिए, हे गुसाईं! रक्षा कीजिए' ऐसा कहकर वे पृथ्वी पर दण्ड की तरह गिर पड़े ॥
english_translation: Along with his younger brother and his friend, Bharata's mind was absorbed. He forgot all counts of joy and sorrow, pleasure and pain. Crying, "Protect me, Lord! Protect me, Master!" he fell to the earth like a staff.
essence: Devotion can be so complete that even joy and sorrow disappear.
simple_meaning: Bharat becomes so overwhelmed with devotion that he forgets every opposite feeling and collapses on the ground, crying out for protection.
insight: It shifts the mind from emotional self-management to wholehearted surrender.
modern_relevance: You finally see the person you’ve been missing after a long silence. For a moment, every other feeling drops away — relief, fear, pride, and hurt all dissolve into one helpless cry.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बचन सप्रेम लखन पहिचाने। करत प्रनामु भरत जियँ जाने॥ बंधु सनेह सरस एहि ओरा। उत साहिब सेवा बस जोरा ॥
translation: प्रेमभरे वचनों से लक्ष्मणजी ने पहचान लिया और मन में जान लिया कि भरतजी प्रणाम कर रहे हैं। (वे श्री रामजी की ओर मुँह किए खड़े थे, भरतजी पीठ पीछे थे, इससे उन्होंने देखा नहीं।) अब इस ओर तो भाई भरतजी का सरस प्रेम और उधर स्वामी श्री रामचन्द्रजी की सेवा की प्रबल परवशता ॥
english_translation: Lakshman recognised Bharat through his loving words and understood in his heart that Bharat was bowing. One side was the sweetness of brotherly love; the other was the force of service binding the lord.
essence: Love may pull your heart one way while service pulls your hands another.
simple_meaning: Lakshman sees Bharat's bowed heart clearly: one side is brotherly affection, the other is devoted service to Ram.
insight: It teaches you to see devotion as a living tension between affection and obligation, not a simple emotion.
