modern_relevance: You’re standing between family loyalty and a promise you made to someone else. Neither side feels wrong, and that tension is exactly what this verse understands.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मिलि न जाइ नहिं गुदरत बनई। सुकबि लखन मन की गति भनई॥ रहे राखि सेवा पर भारू। चढ़ी चंग जनु खैंच खेलारू ॥
translation: न तो (क्षणभर के लिए भी सेवा से पृथक होकर) मिलते ही बनता है और न (प्रेमवश) छोड़ते (उपेक्षा करते) ही। कोई श्रेष्ठ कवि ही लक्ष्मणजी के चित्त की इस गति (दुविधा) का वर्णन कर सकता है। वे सेवा पर भार रखकर रह गए (सेवा को ही विशेष महत्वपूर्ण समझकर उसी में लगे रहे) मानो चढ़ी हुई पतंग को खिलाड़ी (पतंग उड़ाने वाला) खींच रहा हो ॥
english_translation: It neither feels right to meet nor to turn away. Only a great poet can describe Lakshman's state of mind. He stayed weighed down by service, like a kite being pulled by the string of the one flying it.
essence: True service can hold you even when your heart is pulled apart.
simple_meaning: Lakshman is so absorbed in service that he cannot fully meet or turn away. His mind is caught in a devoted tension, like a kite held by its string.
insight: It shows how service can remain steady even when the mind feels split, and how duty can anchor divided attention.
modern_relevance: You are on a video call, but half your mind is with the child crying in the next room. You want to respond fully to both, yet only one can hold your body at a time.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहत सप्रेम नाइ महि माथा। भरत प्रनाम करत रघुनाथा॥ उठे रामु सुनि पेम अधीरा। कहुँ पट कहुँ निषंग धनु तीरा ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी ने प्रेम सहित पृथ्वी पर मस्तक नवाकर कहा- हे रघुनाथजी! भरतजी प्रणाम कर रहे हैं। यह सुनते ही श्री रघुनाथजी प्रेम में अधीर होकर उठे। कहीं वस्त्र गिरा, कहीं तरकस, कहीं धनुष और कहीं बाण ॥
english_translation: Lakshman bowed to the ground with love and said, “Raghunath, Bharata is offering his respects.” Hearing this, Ram rose in love and excitement, dropping his cloth here, his quiver there, his bow and arrows elsewhere.
essence: Love makes Ram rise before anything else can matter.
simple_meaning: Lakshman respectfully tells Ram that Bharata is bowing to him. Ram is so moved by love that he jumps up in eagerness, dropping his clothes and weapons as he rises.
insight: It shows how genuine love dissolves formality and pulls attention straight to the beloved.
modern_relevance: You hear that someone you love has finally arrived, and you stop mid-task without thinking. The body moves before pride can catch up.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बरबस लिए उठाइ उर लाए कृपानिधान। भरत राम की मिलनि लखि बिसरे सबहि अपान ॥
translation: कृपा निधान श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने उनको जबरदस्ती उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया! भरतजी और श्री रामजी के मिलन की रीति को देखकर सबको अपनी सुध भूल गई ॥
english_translation: The treasure of compassion pulled him up and drew him into an embrace. Seeing Bharat and Ram meet, everyone forgot themselves.
essence: Love can be so overwhelming that it makes everyone forget themselves.
simple_meaning: Ram pulled Bharat up and embraced him. Everyone watching was so moved by their reunion that they forgot themselves.
insight: It shows love so complete that even bystanders are pulled out of ordinary awareness.
modern_relevance: You finally see a sibling after years apart, and the room goes quiet. The hug says everything before either of you can speak.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मिलनि प्रीति किमि जाइ बखानी। कबिकुल अगम करम मन बानी॥ परम प्रेम पूरन दोउ भाई। मन बुधि चित अहमिति बिसराई ॥
translation: मिलन की प्रीति कैसे बखानी जाए? वह तो कविकुल के लिए कर्म, मन, वाणी तीनों से अगम है। दोनों भाई (भरतजी और श्री रामजी) मन, बुद्धि, चित्त और अहंकार को भुलाकर परम प्रेम से पूर्ण हो रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: How can the love of this meeting be described? It is beyond the reach of a poet's action, mind, and speech. Both brothers are overflowing with perfect love, having forgotten mind, intellect, consciousness, and the sense of separate self.
essence: True meeting dissolves ego before it can be named.
simple_meaning: Their reunion is so full of love that words cannot capture it. Both brothers are lost in perfect affection, beyond ego and ordinary thought.
insight: It shifts attention from explaining closeness to recognising the depth that makes explanation fail.
modern_relevance: You finally see someone after years apart, and the room goes quiet because nothing you say can match what you feel. Some reunions are larger than language.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहहु सुपेम प्रगट को करई। केहि छाया कबि मति अनुसरई॥ कबिहि अरथ आखर बलु साँचा। अनुहरि ताल गतिहि नटु नाचा ॥
translation: कहिए, उस श्रेष्ठ प्रेम को कौन प्रकट करे? कवि की बुद्धि किसकी छाया का अनुसरण करे? कवि को तो अक्षर और अर्थ का ही सच्चा बल है। नट ताल की गति के अनुसार ही नाचता है! ॥
english_translation: Tell me, who can reveal that supreme love? Whose shadow can the poet's mind follow? The poet has only the true force of words and meaning. The dancer moves only to the rhythm of the drum.
essence: The deepest love can be hinted at, never fully captured.
simple_meaning: The poet says this love is too great to fully describe. Words can only follow its outline, like a dancer following rhythm.
insight: It teaches you to respect the limits of language and let feeling exceed description.
modern_relevance: You try to explain a moment that changed you, and the sentence keeps breaking apart. Some experiences are real before they are speakable.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अगम सनेह भरत रघुबर को। जहँ न जाइ मनु बिधि हरि हर को॥ सो मैं कुमति कहौं केहि भाँति। बाज सुराग कि गाँडर ताँती ॥
translation: भरतजी और श्री रघुनाथजी का प्रेम अगम्य है, जहाँ ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और महादेव का भी मन नहीं जा सकता। उस प्रेम को मैं कुबुद्धि किस प्रकार कहूँ! भला, गाँडर की ताँत से भी कहीं सुंदर राग बज सकता है? ॥ (तालाबों और झीलों में एक तरह की घास होती है, उसे गाँडर कहते हैं।)
english_translation: The love of Bharat and Raghubar is beyond reach, where even the minds of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva cannot go. How can I, with dull understanding, describe that love? Can a reed-string ever produce a sweeter tune than a proper lute?
essence: True devotion is too vast for even the highest minds to contain.
simple_meaning: Bharat’s love for Ram is beyond ordinary understanding, so deep that even the greatest minds cannot fully grasp it.
insight: It shifts the mind from analyzing love to revering its mystery.
modern_relevance: You try to explain why you still care so deeply for someone who changed your life, and every sentence feels too small. Some bonds are larger than explanation.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मिलनि बिलोकि भरत रघुबर की। सुरगन सभय धकधकी धरकी॥ समुझाए सुरगुरु जड़ जागे। बरषि प्रसून प्रसंसन लागे ॥
translation: भरतजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के मिलने का ढंग देखकर देवता भयभीत हो गए, उनकी धुकधुकी धड़कने लगी। देव गुरु बृहस्पतिजी ने समझाया, तब कहीं वे मूर्ख चेते और फूल बरसाकर प्रशंसा करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Seeing the meeting of Bharat and Raghubar, the celestial beings grew fearful and their hearts pounded. When the divine teacher explained, they came to their senses and began showering flowers in praise.
essence: Pure love can overwhelm even the wise before it becomes clear.
simple_meaning: The gods were stunned by the depth of Bharat and Ram's meeting. After Brahma explained, they understood and praised it with flowers.
insight: It shifts attention from surface drama to the hidden greatness of selfless love.
modern_relevance: You watch two siblings reconcile after a family rupture, and the room goes silent. Everyone can feel something sacred has happened, even before anyone finds the words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मिलि सपेम रिपुसूदनहि केवटु भेंटेउ राम। भूरि भायँ भेंटे भरत लछिमन करत प्रनाम ॥
translation: फिर श्री रामजी प्रेम के साथ शत्रुघ्न से मिलकर तब केवट (निषादराज) से मिले। प्रणाम करते हुए लक्ष्मणजी से भरतजी बड़े ही प्रेम से मिले ॥
english_translation: Then, with love, Rama met Shatrughna. Bharata and Lakshmana met with great affection, offering their salutations.
essence: Love returns first as greeting, not argument.
simple_meaning: The brothers meet after long separation, and each greeting is full of love and respect. It is a scene of reunion, not teaching.
insight: It shifts attention from conflict to the healing power of respectful reunion.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering after years of distance, and the first hug says what everyone has been holding back. Some bonds need no speech to feel restored.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भेंटेउ लखन ललकि लघु भाई। बहुरि निषादु लीन्ह उर लाई॥ पुनि मुनिगन दुहुँ भाइन्ह बंदे। अभिमत आसिष पाइ अनंदे ॥
translation: तब लक्ष्मणजी ललककर (बड़ी उमंग के साथ) छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न से मिले। फिर उन्होंने निषादराज को हृदय से लगा लिया। फिर भरत-शत्रुघ्न दोनों भाइयों ने (उपस्थित) मुनियों को प्रणाम किया और इच्छित आशीर्वाद पाकर वे आनंदित हुए ॥
english_translation: Then Lakshman joyfully embraced his younger brother Shatrughna. After that he drew Nishadraj close to his heart. Then both brothers bowed to the sages, and, receiving the blessing they desired, they were filled with joy.
essence: True reunion begins with embrace, humility, and blessing.
simple_meaning: Lakshman greets Shatrughna with joy, embraces Nishadraj, and both brothers bow to the sages and receive blessings.
insight: It shows how reunion naturally moves from affection to respect, especially when old bonds have been tested.
modern_relevance: You finally see your sibling after months apart, and the first thing you do is pull them into a hug before greeting anyone else.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सानुज भरत उमगि अनुरागा। धरि सिर सिय पद पदुम परागा॥ पुनि पुनि करत प्रनाम उठाए। सिर कर कमल परसि बैठाए ॥
translation: छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न सहित भरतजी प्रेम में उमँगकर सीताजी के चरण कमलों की रज सिर पर धारण कर बार-बार प्रणाम करने लगे। सीताजी ने उन्हें उठाकर उनके सिर को अपने करकमल से स्पर्श कर (सिर पर हाथ फेरकर) उन दोनों को बैठाया ॥
english_translation: With Lakshman beside him, Bharat rose in love and placed Sita's lotus dust on his head. Again and again he bowed; Sita lifted them, touched their heads with her lotus hand, and seated them.
essence: Love bows low, and tenderness lifts it back up.
simple_meaning: Bharat and Lakshman bow to Sita with deep love. Sita responds gently, lifting them up and seating them with affection.
insight: It shows respect and affection working together, turning a painful reunion into comfort.
modern_relevance: You see someone after a long family rupture, and no one knows how to speak first. One person bows low in love; the other answers by making the moment safe again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीयँ असीस दीन्हि मन माहीं। मनग सनेहँ देह सुधि नाहीं॥ सब बिधि सानुकूल लखि सीता। भे निसोच उर अपडर बीता ॥
translation: सीताजी ने मन ही मन आशीर्वाद दिया, क्योंकि वे स्नेह में मग्न हैं, उन्हें देह की सुध-बुध नहीं है। सीताजी को सब प्रकार से अपने अनुकूल देखकर भरतजी सोचरहित हो गए और उनके हृदय का कल्पित भय जाता रहा ॥
english_translation: Sita gave her blessing in her heart. Lost in love, she was unaware of her body. Seeing Sita favorable in every way, Bharat became free of worry, and the fear in his heart vanished.
essence: Clear love dissolves the fear you were carrying.
simple_meaning: Sita blesses Bharat inwardly, and Bharat’s fear disappears when he sees her kindness and favor.
insight: It shifts the mind from suspicion to trust when another person’s goodwill becomes unmistakable.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room expecting judgment, then catch one kind look and your shoulders drop. A single sign of goodwill can undo hours of fear.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोउ किछु कहई न कोउ किछु पूँछा। प्रेम भरा मन निज गति छूँछा॥ तेहि अवसर केवटु धीरजु धरि। जोरि पानि बिनवत प्रनामु करि ॥
translation: उस समय न तो कोई कुछ कहता है, न कोई कुछ पूछता है! मन प्रेम से परिपूर्ण है, वह अपनी गति से खाली है (अर्थात संकल्प-विकल्प और चांचल्य से शून्य है)। उस अवसर पर केवट (निषादराज) धीरज धर और हाथ जोड़कर प्रणाम करके विनती करने लगा- ॥
english_translation: No one says anything; no one asks anything. The mind is full of love and empty of restless thoughts. At that moment, the boatman, steady and composed, folded his hands and bowed, then spoke his prayer.
essence: Love silences the mind before it lets anyone speak.
simple_meaning: In a moment of deep love, everyone falls silent. The boatman then gathers himself, bows, and begins to speak with respect.
insight: It shows how reverence creates silence first, then makes humble speech possible.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room where everyone has already cried. Nobody needs explanations. In that quiet, the person who speaks next does so with care, not noise.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ साथ मुनिनाथ के मातु सकल पुर लोग। सेवक सेनप सचिव सब आए बिकल बियोग ॥
translation: हे नाथ! मुनिनाथ वशिष्ठजी के साथ सब माताएँ, नगरवासी, सेवक, सेनापति, मंत्री- सब आपके वियोग से व्याकुल होकर आए हैं ॥
english_translation: O Lord, with the sage Vashishtha, all the mothers, the people of the city, servants, generals, and ministers have come, distressed by separation from you.
essence: Ram's absence is felt by everyone who loves him.
simple_meaning: Everyone from the city has come, overwhelmed by your absence: the mothers, the people, the servants, the generals, and the ministers.
insight: It shifts attention from individual grief to the way one absence can unsettle an entire community.
modern_relevance: A family waiting in a hospital corridor, each person pretending to be steady while the same fear sits in everyone’s chest.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सीलसिंधु सुनि गुर आगवनू। सिय समीप राखे रिपुदवनू॥ चले सबेग रामु तेहि काला। धीर धरम धुर दीनदयाला ॥
translation: गुरु का आगमन सुनकर शील के समुद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सीताजी के पास शत्रुघ्नजी को रख दिया और वे परम धीर, धर्मधुरंधर, दीनदयालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी उसी समय वेग के साथ चल पड़े ॥
english_translation: Hearing that the teacher had arrived, the ocean of virtue Ram placed Shatrughna beside Sita and quickly set out. At that moment, the compassionate one who bears the weight of righteousness went swiftly.
essence: Right conduct moves first, even in the middle of sorrow.
simple_meaning: Ram hears that his teacher has arrived, places Shatrughna by Sita, and immediately goes to greet the teacher.
insight: It teaches you to respond to a rightful call immediately, while still protecting those in your care.
modern_relevance: Your mentor texts that they’ve arrived early, and you stop what you’re doing. You don’t keep them waiting, because respect is shown in movement, not intention.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गुरहि देखि सानुज अनुरागे। दंड प्रनाम करन प्रभु लागे॥ मुनिबर धाइ लिए उर लाई। प्रेम उमगि भेंटे दोउ भाई ॥
translation: गुरुजी के दर्शन करके लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी प्रेम में भर गए और दण्डवत प्रणाम करने लगे। मुनिश्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी ने दौड़कर उन्हें हृदय से लगा लिया और प्रेम में उमँगकर वे दोनों भाइयों से मिले ॥
english_translation: Seeing their guru, Ram and Lakshman were filled with love and bowed fully. The best of sages rushed forward and embraced them to his heart. Overflowing with love, the two brothers met him.
essence: Love deepens when humility and affection meet.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman see their guru, bow deeply, and receive a warm embrace in return. Love moves both sides of the meeting.
insight: It teaches you that reverence can be intimate, and intimacy can still be respectful.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and see the teacher who changed your life. Before any words, your body lowers itself in gratitude, and the distance disappears in one hug.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रेम पुलकि केवट कहि नामू। कीन्ह दूरि तें दंड प्रनामू॥ राम सखा रिषि बरबस भेंटा। जनु महि लुठत सनेह समेटा ॥
translation: फिर प्रेम से पुलकित होकर केवट (निषादराज) ने अपना नाम लेकर दूर से ही वशिष्ठजी को दण्डवत प्रणाम किया। ऋषि वशिष्ठजी ने रामसखा जानकर उसको जबर्दस्ती हृदय से लगा लिया। मानो जमीन पर लोटते हुए प्रेम को समेट लिया हो ॥
english_translation: Then, filled with love and thrill, the boatman bowed from a distance, naming himself. Knowing him as Ram's friend, the sage Vasishtha pulled him into an embrace, as if gathering up love that had rolled on the ground.
essence: Love for Ram turns distance into belonging.
simple_meaning: The boatman bows to Vasishtha from afar, and Vasishtha embraces him warmly because he belongs to Ram's circle of love.
insight: It shifts attention from status to shared devotion, showing that belonging can be immediate and wholehearted.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a temple, a retreat, or a family gathering and feel no need to perform. They already feel familiar because your love for the same center has made you kin.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रघुपति भगति सुमंगल मूला। नभ सराहि सुर बरिसहिं फूला॥ एहि सम निपट नीच कोउ नाहीं। बड़ बसिष्ठ सम को जग माहीं ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी की भक्ति सुंदर मंगलों का मूल है, इस प्रकार कहकर सराहना करते हुए देवता आकाश से फूल बरसाने लगे। वे कहने लगे- जगत में इसके समान सर्वथा नीच कोई नहीं और वशिष्ठजी के समान बड़ा कौन है? ॥
english_translation: Devotion to Raghupati is the root of all auspiciousness. Saying this in praise, the radiant beings showered flowers from the sky. They said, 'In the world there is none more lowly than this one, and none greater than Vashishtha.'
essence: Devotion to Ram makes the overlooked one truly great.
simple_meaning: Devotion to Ram is the source of all good fortune. When that truth is praised, even the heavens respond with flowers.
insight: It shifts respect away from social rank and toward devotion as the real measure of a person.
modern_relevance: You watch someone quietly honor what is sacred while everyone else chases applause. The room feels different around them. That is the kind of greatness this verse points to.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जेहि लखि लखनहु तें अधिक मिले मुदित मुनिराउ। सो सीतापति भजन को प्रगट प्रताप प्रभाउ ॥
translation: जिस (निषाद) को देखकर मुनिराज वशिष्ठजी लक्ष्मणजी से भी अधिक उससे आनंदित होकर मिले। यह सब सीतापति श्री रामचन्द्रजी के भजन का प्रत्यक्ष प्रताप और प्रभाव है ॥
english_translation: Seeing him, the sage Vashishtha was even more delighted than he was with Lakshman. All of this is the clear power and influence of worshiping Sita's lord, Ram.
essence: Devotion to Ram changes how the world receives you.
simple_meaning: Worship of Ram changes how people respond to you. Even a sage felt greater joy meeting this man than meeting Lakshman.
insight: It shifts attention from social charm to the transforming force of devotion and character.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the tension drops before you speak. No performance can explain it — something steadier in you has already done the work.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आरत लोग राम सबु जाना। करुनाकर सुजान भगवाना॥ जो जेहि भायँ रहा अभिलाषी। तेहि तेहि कै तसि तसि रुख राखी ॥
translation: दया की खान, सुजान भगवान श्री रामजी ने सब लोगों को दुःखी (मिलने के लिए व्याकुल) जाना। तब जो जिस भाव से मिलने का अभिलाषी था, उस-उस का उस-उस प्रकार का रुख रखते हुए (उसकी रुचि के अनुसार) ॥
english_translation: Lord Ram knew all the distressed people. The compassionate, wise Lord then met each person according to the desire in their heart.
essence: Compassion becomes real when it takes the shape of each heart.
simple_meaning: Ram sees every distressed person and responds in the way each heart is ready for. His compassion is personal, not one-size-fits-all.
insight: It teaches you to meet people by their actual need, not by your preferred style of helping.
modern_relevance: You open up to a friend after a breakup, but what you need is not advice — just presence. Another person needs practical help. This verse says real care listens first, then responds.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सानुज मिलि पल महुँ सब काहू। कीन्ह दूरि दुखु दारुन दाहू॥ यह बड़ि बात राम कै नाहीं। जिमि घट कोटि एक रबि छाहीं ॥
translation: उन्होंने लक्ष्मणजी सहित पल भर में सब किसी से मिलकर उनके दुःख और कठिन संताप को दूर कर दिया। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के लिए यह कोई बड़ी बात नहीं है। जैसे करोड़ों घड़ों में एक ही सूर्य की (पृथक-पृथक) छाया (प्रतिबिम्ब) एक साथ ही दिखती है ॥
english_translation: Together with Lakshman, he met everyone in a moment and removed their sorrow and burning pain. For Ram, this was no great feat, just as one sun is reflected in countless pots at once.
essence: True presence multiplies itself without losing anything.
simple_meaning: Ram, with Lakshman, quickly meets everyone and removes their suffering. The verse says this is natural for him, like one sun reflected in many pots.
insight: It shifts attention from limited effort to expansive presence: one grounded person can calm many at once.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family room after bad news, and everyone wants your attention at once. The verse reminds you that a steady presence can reach many people without being divided.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मिलि केवटहि उमगि अनुरागा। पुरजन सकल सराहहिं भागा॥ देखीं राम दुखित महतारीं। जनु सुबेलि अवलीं हिम मारीं ॥
translation: समस्त पुरवासी प्रेम में उमँगकर केवट से मिलकर (उसके) भाग्य की सराहना करते हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सब माताओं को दुःखी देखा। मानो सुंदर लताओं की पंक्तियों को पाला मार गया हो ॥
english_translation: The townspeople, filled with love, praised Kevat's good fortune. Ram saw the mothers in sorrow, like rows of lovely vines struck by frost.
essence: Joy and grief can share the same room.
simple_meaning: The people rejoice over Kevat's blessing, and Ram notices the sorrow of the mothers around him.
insight: It keeps attention on the emotional contrast in the scene rather than turning it into a general lesson.
modern_relevance: At a family gathering, one person is being praised in the living room while another quietly wipes away tears in the kitchen. Both truths are real at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रथम राम भेंटी कैकेई। सरल सुभायँ भगति मति भेई॥ पग परि कीन्ह प्रबोधु बहोरी। काल करम बिधि सिर धरि खोरी ॥
translation: सबसे पहले रामजी कैकेयी से मिले और अपने सरल स्वभाव तथा भक्ति से उसकी बुद्धि को तर कर दिया। फिर चरणों में गिरकर काल, कर्म और विधाता के सिर दोष मढ़कर, श्री रामजी ने उनको सान्त्वना दी ॥
english_translation: First, Ram met Kaikeyi. By his simple nature and loving devotion, he softened her mind. Then, bowing at her feet, he comforted her further, placing blame on time, karma, and fate.
essence: Gentleness can soften blame before blame hardens into ruin.
simple_meaning: Ram meets Kaikeyi with such gentleness that her mind softens. He even comforts her by shifting blame away from her and onto time, karma, and fate.
insight: It teaches you to respond to hurt with composure, easing conflict instead of feeding it.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room after a family argument, and everyone is waiting for the next sharp word. Instead, you lower your voice, sit down, and make it safe to breathe again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भेटीं रघुबर मातु सब करि प्रबोधु परितोषु। अंब ईस आधीन जगु काहु न देइअ दोषु ॥
translation: फिर श्री रघुनाथजी सब माताओं से मिले। उन्होंने सबको समझा-बुझाकर संतोष कराया कि हे माता! जगत ईश्वर के अधीन है। किसी को भी दोष नहीं देना चाहिए ॥
english_translation: Then Raghubar met all the mothers, comforted them, and calmed their grief. "Mother, the world is under the divine's rule; do not blame anyone."
essence: When you see a larger order, blame loses its grip.
simple_meaning: Ram comforts his grieving mothers and tells them not to blame anyone, because the world moves under the divine's control.
insight: It shifts the mind from accusation to acceptance, helping you respond with calm instead of resentment.
modern_relevance: You replay a family argument at 1 a.m., searching for who ruined everything. This verse asks you to stop feeding blame and look at the larger forces at work.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गुरतिय पद बंदे दुहु भाईं। सहित बिप्रतिय जे सँग आईं॥ गंग गौरिसम सब सनमानीं। देहिं असीस मुदित मृदु बानीं ॥
translation: फिर दोनों भाइयों ने ब्राह्मणों की स्त्रियों सहित- जो भरतजी के साथ आई थीं, गुरुजी की पत्नी अरुंधतीजी के चरणों की वंदना की और उन सबका गंगाजी तथा गौरीजी के समान सम्मान किया। वे सब आनंदित होकर कोमल वाणी से आशीर्वाद देने लगीं ॥
english_translation: Then both brothers bowed to the wives of the gurus and to the women who had come with Bharata. They honored them all like Ganga and Gauri, and the women, delighted, gave them gentle blessings.
essence: Humility turns a formal meeting into blessing.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman show deep respect to the women who came with Bharata and to the guru's wife. Those women, pleased by their humility, bless them warmly.
insight: It teaches you to treat every person in the room with equal dignity, not just the ones with status.
modern_relevance: You enter a room where the people around your partner are waiting, and you choose respect over self-importance. That small bow changes the whole atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गहि पद लगे सुमित्रा अंका। जनु भेंटी संपति अति रंका॥ पुनि जननी चरननि दोउ भ्राता। परे पेम ब्याकुल सब गाता ॥
translation: तब दोनों भाई पैर पकड़कर सुमित्राजी की गोद में जा चिपटे। मानो किसी अत्यन्त दरिद्र की सम्पत्ति से भेंट हो गई हो। फिर दोनों भाई माता कौसल्याजी के चरणों में गिर पड़े। प्रेम के मारे उनके सारे अंग शिथिल हैं ॥
english_translation: Then both brothers clung to Sumitra's lap, as if a poor man had suddenly found immense wealth. Then the two brothers fell at their mother Kaushalya's feet, their bodies limp with love.
essence: Deep love makes strength dissolve into tenderness.
simple_meaning: The brothers rush to their mothers with overwhelming love and gratitude. Their reunion is so moving that their bodies seem to go weak.
insight: It shifts attention from formal reunion to the physical language of gratitude and love.
modern_relevance: You finally see your mother after months away, and all the words disappear. The body knows what the heart cannot explain.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अति अनुराग अंब उर लाए। नयन सनेह सलिल अन्हवाए॥ तेहि अवसर कर हरष बिषादू। किमि कबि कहै मूक जिमि स्वादू ॥
translation: बड़े ही स्नेह से माता ने उन्हें हृदय से लगा लिया और नेत्रों से बहे हुए प्रेमाश्रुओं के जल से उन्हें नहला दिया। उस समय के हर्ष और विषाद को कवि कैसे कहे? जैसे गूँगा स्वाद को कैसे बतावे? ॥
english_translation: With deep affection, Mother held them to her heart and bathed them in the tears of love from her eyes. How can a poet describe the joy and sorrow of that moment? Like a mute person describing taste.
essence: Love can flood you with joy and sorrow at once.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya holds Ram and Lakshman close, crying tears of love. The moment is so full of mixed joy and sorrow that words cannot capture it.
insight: It teaches you that the deepest moments of love may also carry grief and cannot be neatly explained.
modern_relevance: You finally see someone you have missed for years, and you laugh while crying at the same time. No explanation fits that kind of relief.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मिलि जननिहि सानुज रघुराऊ। गुर सन कहेउ कि धारिअ पाऊ॥ पुरजन पाइ मुनीस नियोगू। जल थल तकि तकि उतरेउ लोगू ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी ने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित माता कौसल्या से मिलकर गुरु से कहा कि आश्रम पर पधारिए। तदनन्तर मुनीश्वर वशिष्ठजी की आज्ञा पाकर अयोध्यावासी सब लोग जल और थल का सुभीता देख-देखकर उतर गए ॥
english_translation: Raghunath met his mother with Lakshman beside him and asked the guru to come in. Then, after the sage Vashishtha's command, the people of Ayodhya began descending, choosing paths through water and land.
essence: The homecoming continues, and the whole city follows.
simple_meaning: Ram meets his mother with Lakshman beside him, invites the teacher, and the people of Ayodhya follow the sage's guidance to go down by land and water.
insight: It shifts attention from reunion to the next step in the journey.
modern_relevance: A group finally reaches the destination after a long trip, and everyone is still figuring out where to stand, who to follow, and what comes next.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: महिसुर मंत्री मातु गुरु गने लोग लिए साथ। पावन आश्रम गवनु किए भरत लखन रघुनाथ ॥
translation: ब्राह्मण, मंत्री, माताएँ और गुरु आदि गिने-चुने लोगों को साथ लिए हुए, भरतजी, लक्ष्मणजी और श्री रघुनाथजी पवित्र आश्रम को चले ॥
english_translation: With a few selected people — brahmins, ministers, mothers, and the teacher — Bharat, Lakshman, and Raghunath went to the sacred hermitage.
essence: The party moves together toward the hermitage.
simple_meaning: Bharat, Lakshman, and Ram set out for the hermitage with a small group of elders and family members.
insight: It keeps attention on the scene’s transition rather than on a teaching.
modern_relevance: A group of relatives and elders quietly walks with you to a place that matters. The moment feels important, but this line is only the movement into it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीय आइ मुनिबर पग लागी। उचित असीस लही मन मागी॥ गुरपतिनिहि मुनितियन्ह समेता। मिली पेमु कहि जाइ न जेता ॥
translation: सीताजी आकर मुनि श्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी के चरणों लगीं और उन्होंने मन माँगी उचित आशीष पाई। फिर मुनियों की स्त्रियों सहित गुरु पत्नी अरुन्धतीजी से मिलीं। उनका जितना प्रेम था, वह कहा नहीं जाता ॥
english_translation: Sita came and bowed at the feet of the noble sage, receiving the blessings her heart desired. Then, along with the wives of the sages, she met the guru’s wife Arundhati. Their affection was beyond words.
essence: Humility receives blessings, and reverence turns meeting into love.
simple_meaning: Sita greets the sages and their wives with humility, receives the blessings she hopes for, and shares a love so deep it cannot be measured.
insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing how respectful conduct creates trust and closeness.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering after a long separation, greet the elders first, and feel the room soften around you. Respect opens the door to affection.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बंदि बंदि पग सिय सबही के। आसिरबचन लहे प्रिय जी के। सासु सकल सब सीयँ निहारीं। मूदे नयन सहमि सुकुमारीं ॥
translation: सीताजी ने सभी के चरणों की अलग-अलग वंदना करके अपने हृदय को प्रिय (अनुकूल) लगने वाले आशीर्वाद पाए। जब सुकुमारी सीताजी ने सब सासुओं को देखा, तब उन्होंने सहमकर अपनी आँखें बंद कर लीं ॥
english_translation: Sita bowed to each of them and received the blessings most dear to her heart. When the delicate Sita saw all her mothers-in-law, she closed her eyes in modest fear.
essence: Grace begins with bowing before you belong.
simple_meaning: Sita respectfully greets everyone, receives their blessings, and lowers her eyes in shy modesty when she sees her mothers-in-law.
insight: It teaches you to meet new relationships with respect first, not self-display.
modern_relevance: You walk into your partner’s family home for the first time, trying to remember every name and every custom. Sita’s grace is in that careful, humble pause.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परीं बधिक बस मनहुँ मरालीं। काह कीन्ह करतार कुचालीं॥ तिन्ह सिय निरखि निपट दुखु पावा। सो सबु सहिअ जो दैउ सहावा ॥
translation: (सासुओं की बुरी दशा देखकर) उन्हें ऐसा प्रतीत हुआ मानो राजहंसिनियाँ बधिक के वश में पड़ गई हों। (मन में सोचने लगीं कि) कुचाली विधाता ने क्या कर डाला? उन्होंने भी सीताजी को देखकर बड़ा दुःख पाया। (सोचा) जो कुछ दैव सहावे, वह सब सहना ही पड़ता है ॥
english_translation: Seeing the in-laws in distress, it seemed to them as if swans had fallen into the hands of a hunter. They thought, “What has the creator done in this crooked way?” Seeing Sita, they felt deep sorrow too. “Whatever fate permits must be borne.”
essence: Some pain cannot be fixed; it can only be carried.
simple_meaning: The elders feel grief on seeing Sita and think that whatever life brings must be endured.
insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to dignified endurance.
modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed and realize there is nothing clever to say. Sometimes love means staying present with what cannot be changed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जनकसुता तब उर धरि धीरा। नील नलिन लोयन भरि नीरा॥ मिली सकल सासुन्ह सिय जाई। तेहि अवसर करुना महि छाई ॥
translation: तब जानकीजी हृदय में धीरज धरकर, नील कमल के समान नेत्रों में जल भरकर, सब सासुओं से जाकर मिलीं। उस समय पृथ्वी पर करुणा (करुण रस) छा गई ॥
english_translation: Then Janaki gathered courage in her heart, filled her lotus-like eyes with tears, and went to meet all her mothers-in-law. At that moment, compassion spread over the earth.
essence: Courage can look like gentle tears and respectful steps.
simple_meaning: Sita steadies herself, wipes her fear into tears, and goes to meet her mothers-in-law with humility and grace.
insight: It teaches you to answer discomfort with grace instead of defensiveness.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone already knows the tension, and your throat tightens. Still, you smile, bow, and meet each person gently anyway.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लागि लागि पग सबनि सिय भेंटति अति अनुराग। हृदयँ असीसहिं पेम बस रहिअहु भरी सोहाग ॥
translation: सीताजी सबके पैरों लग-लगकर अत्यन्त प्रेम से मिल रही हैं और सब सासुएँ स्नेहवश हृदय से आशीर्वाद दे रही हैं कि तुम सुहाग से भरी रहो (अर्थात सदा सौभाग्यवती रहो) ॥
english_translation: Sita lovingly touches everyone's feet, and all the queens bless her from their hearts: “May you always remain blessed in marriage.”
essence: Humility invites blessing faster than rank ever could.
simple_meaning: Sita greets every queen with deep affection, touching their feet, and they bless her warmly in return.
insight: It shows how humility can soften status and turn greeting into grace.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where the people who should have been formal with you suddenly become tender. A respectful gesture opens the door to blessing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिकल सनेहँ सीय सब रानीं। बैठन सबहि कहेउ गुर ग्यानीं॥ कहि जग गति मायिक मुनिनाथा॥ कहे कछुक परमारथ गाथा ॥
translation: सीताजी और सब रानियाँ स्नेह के मारे व्याकुल हैं। तब ज्ञानी गुरु ने सबको बैठ जाने के लिए कहा। फिर मुनिनाथ वशिष्ठजी ने जगत की गति को मायिक कहकर (अर्थात जगत माया का है, इसमें कुछ भी नित्य नहीं है, ऐसा कहकर) कुछ परमार्थ की कथाएँ (बातें) कहीं ॥
english_translation: Sita and all the queens were overcome with emotion. Then the wise teacher asked everyone to sit down. Vashishtha, the sage among sages, spoke of the world's changing nature as illusory and then said a few words about ultimate reality.
essence: What feels permanent is only part of a changing world.
simple_meaning: Sita and the queens are overwhelmed with feeling. Vashishtha settles everyone down and speaks about how the world keeps changing, then turns to deeper spiritual truth.
insight: It shifts the mind from raw feeling to a wider view that can hold grief without being swallowed by it.
modern_relevance: You are in a room where everyone is crying after bad news, and someone finally says, sit down, breathe, and see this clearly before the panic spreads.
speaker: Vashishtha

verse_text: नृप कर सुरपुर गवनु सुनावा। सुनि रघुनाथ दुसह दुखु पावा॥ मरन हेतु निज नेहु बिचारी। भे अति बिकल धीर धुर धारी ॥
translation: तदनन्तर वशिष्ठजी ने राजा दशरथजी के स्वर्ग गमन की बात सुनाई। जिसे सुनकर रघुनाथजी ने दुःसह दुःख पाया और अपने प्रति उनके स्नेह को उनके मरने का कारण विचारकर धीरधुरन्धर श्री रामचन्द्रजी अत्यन्त व्याकुल हो गए ॥
english_translation: Vashistha announced King Dasharatha's passing to the higher realm. Hearing it, Raghunath felt unbearable grief. Thinking of the love Dasharatha held for him as the cause of his death, the steady one became deeply distressed.
essence: Steadiness does not cancel grief when love is real.
simple_meaning: Dasharath's death is announced, and Ram is overwhelmed with grief. He sees his father's love for him as part of what led to that death.
insight: It normalises grief as the natural response to deep attachment, not as a failure of strength.
modern_relevance: You get the call late at night, and the room goes quiet before anyone speaks. What hurts most is not only the loss — it is remembering how much they loved you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कुलिस कठोर सुनत कटु बानी। बिलपत लखन सीय सब रानी॥ सोक बिकल अति सकल समाजू। मानहूँ राजु अकाजेउ आजू ॥
translation: वज्र के समान कठोर, कड़वी वाणी सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी, सीताजी और सब रानियाँ विलाप करने लगीं। सारा समाज शोक से अत्यन्त व्याकुल हो गया! मानो राजा आज ही मरे हों ॥
english_translation: Hearing the words, hard as thunderbolt and bitter as poison, Lakshman, Sita, and all the queens began to wail. The whole assembly was shaken with grief, as if the king had died that very day.
essence: Grief can strike a whole gathering at once.
simple_meaning: The news lands like a blow. Lakshman, Sita, the queens, and everyone else break into grief, as if the king has just died.
insight: It captures how grief spreads through a shared space before anyone can think clearly.
modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after one message changes everything. Nobody knows what to say first; the shock arrives before the words do.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनिबर बहुरि राम समुझाए। सहित समाज सुसरित नहाए॥ ब्रत निरंबु तेहि दिन प्रभु कीन्हा। मुनिहु कहें जलु काहुँ न लीन्हा ॥
translation: फिर मुनिश्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी ने श्री रामजी को समझाया। तब उन्होंने समाज सहित श्रेष्ठ नदी मंदाकिनीजी में स्नान किया। उस दिन प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने निर्जल व्रत किया। मुनि वशिष्ठजी के कहने पर भी किसी ने जल ग्रहण नहीं किया ॥
english_translation: Then the sage Vashistha again explained things to Ram. Together with the group, they bathed in the sacred Mandakini River. That day the Lord kept a waterless fast, and even when the sage said to take water, no one did.
essence: Discipline means keeping the vow even when relief is available.
simple_meaning: Ram follows Vashistha’s guidance, bathes with the gathered group, and keeps a strict fast without water for the day.
insight: It shifts attention from intention alone to the bodily practice that proves commitment.
modern_relevance: You promised yourself one sober day, one honest conversation, one hour without your phone — and then the old pull came back. Discipline is what you keep when comfort asks to be excused.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भोरु भएँ रघुनंदनहि जो मुनि आयसु दीन्ह। श्रद्धा भगति समेत प्रभु सो सबु सादरु कीन्ह ॥
translation: दूसरे दिन सबेरा होने पर मुनि वशिष्ठजी ने श्री रघुनाथजी को जो-जो आज्ञा दी, वह सब कार्य प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने श्रद्धा-भक्ति सहित आदर के साथ किया ॥
english_translation: At dawn, Raghunandan did everything the sage instructed, with reverence and devotion.
essence: Devotion makes even duty feel sacred.
simple_meaning: At daybreak, Ram carried out every instruction from Vashishtha with reverence and devotion.
insight: It shifts action from reluctant compliance to respectful, wholehearted service.
modern_relevance: You are exhausted, grieving, and still have to do what must be done: call the relatives, sign the papers, make the arrangements. This verse honours the dignity of doing it with care.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि पितु क्रिया बेद जसि बरनी। भे पुनीत पातक तम तरनी॥ जासु नाम पावक अघ तूला। सुमिरत सकल सुमंगल मूला ॥
translation: वेदों में जैसा कहा गया है, उसी के अनुसार पिता की क्रिया करके, पाप रूपी अंधकार के नष्ट करने वाले सूर्यरूप श्री रामचन्द्रजी शुद्ध हुए! जिनका नाम पाप रूपी रूई के (तुरंत जला डालने के) लिए अग्नि है और जिनका स्मरण मात्र समस्त शुभ मंगलों का मूल है, ॥
english_translation: Having performed his father's rites as the Vedas prescribe, Rama became purified, the destroyer of the darkness of sin. His name is fire for the cotton of wrongdoing; remembering him is the root of all auspiciousness.
essence: Right action in sorrow can itself become purification.
simple_meaning: Ram completed his father's funeral rites exactly as the sacred law requires, and that act purified him. His name burns away wrongdoing and becomes the source of every good beginning.
insight: It shifts attention from grief alone to the dignity of faithful action under grief.
modern_relevance: You stand at a hospital corridor after a parent dies, signing papers, arranging the last rites, holding yourself together. Doing what must be done can become its own cleansing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुद्ध सो भयउ साधु संमत अस। तीरथ आवाहन सुसरिजस॥ सुद्ध भएँ दुइ बासर बीते। बोले गुर सनराम पिरीते ॥
translation: वे (नित्य शुद्ध-बुद्ध) भगवान श्री रामजी शुद्ध हुए! साधुओं की ऐसी सम्मति है कि उनका शुद्ध होना वैसे ही है जैसा तीर्थों के आवाहन से गंगाजी शुद्ध होती हैं! (गंगाजी तो स्वभाव से ही शुद्ध हैं, उनमें जिन तीर्थों का आवाहन किया जाता है, उलटे वे ही गंगाजी के सम्पर्क में आने से शुद्ध हो जाते हैं। इसी प्रकार सच्चिदानंद रूप श्रीराम तो नित्य शुद्ध हैं, उनके संसर्ग से कर्म ही शुद्ध हो गए।) जब शुद्ध हुए दो दिन बीत गए तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी प्रीति के साथ गुरुजी से बोले- ॥
english_translation: He became purified, as the saints agree. It is like the purification of the Ganga by the calling of holy places. After two days had passed in this purified state, Lord Ram lovingly spoke to the teacher.
essence: Ram does not receive purity; he gives it.
simple_meaning: Ram is already pure, and even the rites around him become pure through contact with him. After two days, he speaks lovingly to his teacher.
insight: It shifts attention from ritual as a requirement to purity as an overflowing quality of Ram’s presence.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm changes the whole room. You came carrying tension, but their presence makes everything feel orderly, clean, and strangely settled.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ लोग सब निपट दुखारी। कंद मूल फल अंबु आहारी॥ सानुज भरतु सचिव सब माता। देखि मोहि पल जिमि जुग जाता ॥
translation: हे नाथ! सब लोग यहाँ अत्यन्त दुःखी हो रहे हैं। कंद, मूल, फल और जल का ही आहार करते हैं। भाई शत्रुघ्न सहित भरत को, मंत्रियों को और सब माताओं को देखकर मुझे एक-एक पल युग के समान बीत रहा है ॥
english_translation: O Lord, everyone here is terribly sorrowful. They live on roots, fruits, and water. Seeing Bharata with his younger brother Shatrughna, the ministers, and all the mothers, every moment feels like an age to me.
essence: Separation makes a single moment feel endless.
simple_meaning: Lakshman tells Ram that Ayodhya is full of sorrow. Everyone is living on very simple food, and seeing Bharata, Shatrughna, the ministers, and the mothers makes even a moment feel unbearably long.
insight: It shifts the focus from argument to the lived pain of separation and loss.
modern_relevance: You walk into a house after a family fight and feel the silence before anyone speaks. Everyone is functioning, but the air itself feels heavy and stretched.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: सब समेत पुर धारिअ पाऊ। आपु इहाँ अमरावति राऊ॥ बहुत कहेउँ सब कियउँ ढिठाई। उचित होइ तस करिअ गोसाँई ॥
translation: अतः सबके साथ आप अयोध्यापुरी को पधारिए (लौट जाइए)। आप यहाँ हैं और राजा अमरावती (स्वर्ग) में हैं (अयोध्या सूनी है)! मैंने बहुत कह डाला, यह सब बड़ी ढिठाई की है। हे गोसाईं! जैसा उचित हो, वैसा ही कीजिए ॥
english_translation: So please return to Ayodhya with everyone. You are here, and yet the king is in Amravati; Ayodhya feels empty. I have spoken too much and acted boldly. O Lord, let what is proper be done.
essence: What is proper matters more than pride, comfort, or delay.
simple_meaning: Vashishtha urges Ram to return to Ayodhya with everyone, saying the city feels empty without him and asking him to do what is right.
insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to responsibility, reminding you that the proper action may already be clear.
modern_relevance: Your family is waiting in a hospital corridor, and everyone keeps looking at the empty chair where the person who holds things together should be. Someone has to come back and make the next right move.
speaker: Vashishtha

verse_text: धर्म सेतु करुनायतन कस न कहु अस राम। लोग दुखित दिन दुइ दरस देखि लहहुँ बिश्राम ॥
translation: (वशिष्ठजी ने कहा-) हे राम! तुम धर्म के सेतु और दया के धाम हो, तुम भला ऐसा क्यों न कहो? लोग दुःखी हैं। दो दिन तुम्हारा दर्शन कर शांति लाभ कर लें ॥
english_translation: O Ram, bridge of dharma and abode of compassion, why would you not say yes? The people are suffering. Let them have your sight for two days and find relief.
essence: Compassion sometimes means letting others rest in your presence.
simple_meaning: Ram is asked to return briefly so the suffering people of Ayodhya can see him and feel relief.
insight: It shifts attention from fixing problems to offering reassuring presence.
modern_relevance: A sick parent asks to hear your voice before sleep, not for advice but for comfort. Sometimes what heals people is simply being near the one they trust.
speaker: Vashishtha

verse_text: राम बचन सुनि सभय समाजू। जनु जलनिधि महुँ बिकल जहाजू॥ सुनि गुर गिरा सुमंगल मूला। भयउ मनहुँ मारुत अनुकूला ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के वचन सुनकर सारा समाज भयभीत हो गया। मानो बीच समुद्र में जहाज डगमगा गया हो, परन्तु जब उन्होंने गुरु वशिष्ठजी की श्रेष्ठ कल्याणमूलक वाणी सुनी, तो उस जहाज के लिए मानो हवा अनुकूल हो गई ॥
english_translation: Hearing Ram's words, the whole assembly grew fearful, like a ship tossed in the middle of the sea. Hearing Guru Vashistha's auspicious words, it was as if the wind turned favorable for that ship.
essence: Wise words can steady what fear has thrown off course.
simple_meaning: The assembly first trembles at Ram's words, then steadies when Vashistha speaks. The scene compares their fear and relief to a ship in rough sea finding favorable wind.
insight: It shows how fear can be reversed by wise counsel, shifting a group from panic back to balance.
modern_relevance: A tense family meeting goes silent after one sharp sentence, then softens when the elder speaks calmly. The room changes not because facts changed, but because steadiness returned.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पावन पयँ तिहुँ काल नहाहीं। जो बिलोकि अघ ओघ नसाहीं॥ मंगलमूरति लोचन भरि भरि। निरखहिं हरषि दंडवत करि करि ॥
translation: सब लोग पवित्र पयस्विनी नदी में (अथवा पयस्विनी नदी के पवित्र जल में) तीनों समय (सबेरे, दोपहर और सायंकाल) स्नान करते हैं, जिसके दर्शन से ही पापों के समूह नष्ट हो जाते हैं और मंगल मूर्ति श्री रामचन्द्रजी को दण्डवत प्रणाम कर-करके उन्हें नेत्र भर-भरकर देखते हैं ॥
english_translation: People bathe in the holy river at all three times, and just seeing Ram destroys a heap of wrongdoing. They bow again and again, then look at the auspicious form of Ram with eyes full of joy.
essence: Ram's presence cleanses more deeply than ritual alone.
simple_meaning: People bathe in holy water all day, but Ram's sight is even more purifying. They keep bowing to him and look at him again and again with joy.
insight: It shifts devotion from ritual alone to direct, repeated seeing of the beloved form.
modern_relevance: You step into a temple after a hard week, but what you really want is the calm that settles when you finally stand before someone who restores you. That is the feeling here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम सैल बन देखन जाहीं। जहँ सुख सकल सकल दुख नाहीं॥ झरना झरहिं सुधासम बारी। त्रिबिध तापहर त्रिबिध बयारी ॥
translation: सब श्री रामचन्द्रजी के पर्वत (कामदगिरि) और वन को देखने जाते हैं, जहाँ सभी सुख हैं और सभी दुःखों का अभाव है। झरने अमृत के समान जल झरते हैं और तीन प्रकार की (शीतल, मंद, सुगंध) हवा तीनों प्रकार के (आध्यात्मिक, आधिभौतिक, आधिदैविक) तापों को हर लेती है ॥
english_translation: People go to see Ram's mountain and forest, where all joy is found and all sorrow is absent. Streams pour out water like nectar, and the three kinds of breeze remove the three kinds of suffering.
essence: Ram's presence turns a place into relief itself.
simple_meaning: Ram's mountain and forest are described as a place of pure comfort: no sorrow, sweet water, and cooling breezes that remove every kind of suffering.
insight: It turns a landscape into a lived experience of relief, showing how environment can calm the whole person.
modern_relevance: You step into a quiet hillside after weeks of noise, and your body loosens before your mind can explain why. Some places seem to hold grief differently.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिटप बेलि तृन अगनित जाती। फल प्रसून पल्लव बहु भाँती॥ सुंदर सिला सुखद तरु छाहीं। जाइ बरनि बन छबि केहि पाहीं ॥
translation: असंख्य जात के वृक्ष, लताएँ और तृण हैं तथा बहुत तरह के फल, फूल और पत्ते हैं। सुंदर शिलाएँ हैं। वृक्षों की छाया सुख देने वाली है। वन की शोभा किससे वर्णन की जा सकती है? ॥
english_translation: There are countless kinds of trees, vines, grasses, fruits, flowers, and leaves. Beautiful rocks and soothing shade fill the forest. Who could ever describe the forest's splendor?
essence: The forest's richness exceeds any single description.
simple_meaning: The forest is overflowing with variety, beauty, and shade. It is so rich and lovely that no description can fully capture it.
insight: It shifts attention from utility to presence, letting beauty be seen before it is explained.
modern_relevance: You step off a crowded train into a quiet hillside trail, and the air changes at once. The details keep coming, and you stop trying to name them all.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सरनि सरोरुह जल बिहग कूजत गुंजत भृंग। बैर बिगत बिहरत बिपिन मृग बिहंग बहुरंग ॥
translation: तालाबों में कमल खिल रहे हैं, जल के पक्षी कूज रहे हैं, भौंरे गुंजार कर रहे हैं और बहुत रंगों के पक्षी और पशु वन में वैररहित होकर विहार कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Lotuses bloom in the lakes, waterbirds call, bees hum, and many-colored birds and animals roam the forest without enmity.
essence: Peace changes the whole world around you.
simple_meaning: The forest around Ram is so beautiful and peaceful that even the animals and birds seem free of conflict.
insight: It shifts attention from danger and loss to the healing order present in a peaceful environment.
modern_relevance: You step into a quiet park after a brutal week, and even the birds seem less frantic. The world can feel different when you finally stop carrying your own tension into it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोल किरात भिल्ल बनबासी। मधु सुचि सुंदर स्वादु सुधा सी॥ भरि भरि परन पुटीं रचि रूरी। कंद मूल फल अंकुर जूरी ॥
translation: कोल, किरात और भील आदि वन के रहने वाले लोग पवित्र, सुंदर एवं अमृत के समान स्वादिष्ट मधु (शहद) को सुंदर दोने बनाकर और उनमें भर-भरकर तथा कंद, मूल, फल और अंकुर आदि की जूड़ियों (अँटियों) को ॥
english_translation: The forest-dwellers of the Kola, Kirata, and Bhilla tribes bring pure, lovely honey as sweet as nectar, filling leaf-bowls with it and gathering roots, tubers, fruits, and tender shoots.
essence: Even the forest offers Ram what it has most lovingly.
simple_meaning: Forest people bring Ram and his companions gifts from the woods: honey, roots, fruits, and tender shoots.
insight: It shifts attention from the size of a gift to the love and effort behind it.
modern_relevance: A neighbor shows up with mangoes from their tree and a jar of homemade honey after you move into a new place. No formal gift could feel more generous.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सबहि देहिं करि बिनय प्रनामा। कहि कहि स्वाद भेद गुन नामा॥ देहिं लोग बहु मोल न लेहीं। फेरत राम दोहाई देहीं ॥
translation: सबको विनय और प्रणाम करके उन चीजों के अलग-अलग स्वाद, भेद (प्रकार), गुण और नाम बता-बताकर देते हैं। लोग उनका बहुत दाम देते हैं, पर वे नहीं लेते और लौटा देने में श्री रामजी की दुहाई देते हैं ॥
english_translation: They greet everyone respectfully, explain the taste, variety, qualities, and names of the goods, and give them away. People offer much money, but they refuse it and send them back, invoking Ram.
essence: True giving asks for nothing back.
simple_meaning: The forest people politely offer their goods, describe them carefully, and refuse payment, sending others back with Ram's name on their lips.
insight: It shifts giving from transaction to offering, where respect matters more than profit.
modern_relevance: At a roadside stall, someone hands you extra fruit, waves away the change, and smiles as if kindness itself were the price. That quiet dignity changes the whole exchange.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहहिं सनेह मगन मृदु बानी। मानत साधु पेम पहिचानी॥ तुम्ह सुकृती हम नीच निषादा। पावा दरसनु राम प्रसादा ॥
translation: प्रेम में मग्न हुए वे कोमल वाणी से कहते हैं कि साधु लोग प्रेम को पहचानकर उसका सम्मान करते हैं (अर्थात आप साधु हैं, आप हमारे प्रेम को देखिए, दाम देकर या वस्तुएँ लौटाकर हमारे प्रेम का तिरस्कार न कीजिए)। आप तो पुण्यात्मा हैं, हम नीच निषाद हैं। श्री रामजी की कृपा से ही हमने आप लोगों के दर्शन पाए हैं ॥
english_translation: Overjoyed with love, they speak softly: “The good understand and honor love. You are virtuous; we are lowly Nishads. By Ram’s grace, we have received your sight.”
essence: Love becomes sacred when it is received with humility.
simple_meaning: True goodness recognizes love and responds with respect. The Nishads humbly say they are lowly and that seeing Ram’s people is itself Ram’s grace.
insight: It shifts you from measuring care by price or status to honoring the love inside the gesture.
modern_relevance: You bring food to someone who is grieving, and they keep trying to pay you back. The deeper gift is not the meal — it is letting love be received without turning it into a transaction.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हमहि अगम अति दरसु तुम्हारा। जस मरु धरनि देवधुनि धारा॥ राम कृपाल निषाद नेवाजा। परिजन प्रजउ चहिअ जस राजा ॥
translation: हम लोगों को आपके दर्शन बड़े ही दुर्लभ हैं, जैसे मरुभूमि के लिए गंगाजी की धारा दुर्लभ है! (देखिए) कृपालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने निषाद पर कैसी कृपा की है। जैसे राजा हैं वैसा ही उनके परिवार और प्रजा को भी होना चाहिए ॥
english_translation: Your sight is as rare to us as a river of Ganga in a desert. See how kindly Ram has blessed Nishad; a king's family and people should be like him.
essence: True grace does not stop with one devotee; it reshapes everyone nearby.
simple_meaning: Nishad says Ram's presence is precious and rare, like water in a desert. He also says a truly good ruler blesses not only himself but his whole people.
insight: It shifts attention from private devotion to the way leadership should shape an entire circle of people.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who treats the cleaner, the driver, and the assistant with the same warmth they give the CEO. That small consistency tells you more than any speech about character.
speaker: Nishad

verse_text: यह जियँ जानि सँकोचु तजि करिअ छोहु लखि नेहु। हमहि कृतारथ करनलगि फल तृन अंकुर लेहु ॥
translation: हृदय में ऐसा जानकर संकोच छोड़कर और हमारा प्रेम देखकर कृपा कीजिए और हमको कृतार्थ करने के लिए ही फल, तृण और अंकुर लीजिए ॥
english_translation: Knowing this in your heart, set aside hesitation and show kindness, seeing our love. To make us fulfilled, please take fruits, grass, and shoots.
essence: Kindness completes the gift, not its size.
simple_meaning: Nishad asks Ram to ignore any hesitation, accept the simple forest gifts, and bless him by receiving them with kindness.
insight: It teaches you to receive simple service as an act of honouring the giver.
modern_relevance: You bring homemade food to someone recovering from illness, and they hesitate to take it because it feels too little. Their acceptance matters more than the meal itself.
speaker: Nishad

verse_text: तुम्ह प्रिय पाहुने बन पगु धारे। सेवा जोगु न भाग हमारे॥ देब काह हम तुम्हहि गोसाँई। ईंधनु पात किरात मिताई ॥
translation: आप प्रिय पाहुने वन में पधारे हैं। आपकी सेवा करने के योग्य हमारे भाग्य नहीं हैं। हे स्वामी! हम आपको क्या देंगे? भीलों की मित्रता तो बस, ईंधन (लकड़ी) और पत्तों ही तक है ॥
english_translation: You have come to the forest as a beloved guest. We are not worthy of serving you. What can we offer you, lord? For forest people, friendship means only firewood and leaves.
essence: Love makes the smallest offering feel complete.
simple_meaning: Shabari welcomes Ram as a beloved guest and humbly says she has nothing worthy to offer except the simple gifts of the forest.
insight: It shifts attention from perfect hospitality to sincere welcome.
modern_relevance: You host a friend in a tiny apartment with mismatched cups and instant tea, worried it feels too little. What matters is that you opened the door with love.
speaker: Shabari

verse_text: यह हमारि अति बड़ि सेवकाई। लेहिं न बासन बसन चोराई॥ हम जड़ जीव जीव गन घाती। कुटिल कुचाली कुमति कुजाती ॥
translation: हमारी तो यही बड़ी भारी सेवा है कि हम आपके कपड़े और बर्तन नहीं चुरा लेते। हम लोग जड़ जीव हैं, जीवों की हिंसा करने वाले हैं, कुटिल, कुचाली, कुबुद्धि और कुजाति हैं ॥
english_translation: This is our great service: we do not steal your clothes or vessels. We are dull beings, killers of living creatures, crooked, deceitful, foolish, and low-born.
essence: True service may be nothing more than not taking what is not yours.
simple_meaning: The speaker humbly says that the best service he can offer is simply not causing harm or taking anything that is not given.
insight: It shifts service from grand gestures to simple non-harm and gratitude.
modern_relevance: You show up at a friend's house after they have already done too much for you. Instead of performing gratitude, you stop taking, stop demanding, and become easy to host.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: पाप करत निसि बासर जाहीं। नहिं पट कटि नहिं पेट अघाहीं॥ सपनेहुँ धरमबुद्धि कस काऊ। यह रघुनंदन दरस प्रभाऊ ॥
translation: हमारे दिन-रात पाप करते ही बीतते हैं। तो भी न तो हमारी कमर में कपड़ा है और न पेट ही भरते हैं। हममें स्वप्न में भी कभी धर्मबुद्धि कैसी? यह सब तो श्री रघुनाथजी के दर्शन का प्रभाव है ॥
english_translation: We spend our days and nights in wrongdoing, yet our waists still lack cloth and our bellies still go hungry. We have no sense of righteousness, even in dreams. This is the power of seeing Raghunandan.
essence: Ram's presence changes even an unworthy heart.
simple_meaning: The forest people admit their lives are full of wrongdoing and poverty, yet Ram's presence has still transformed them. Just seeing him has awakened a new sense of goodness.
insight: It shifts devotion from earning worthiness to receiving transformation through nearness.
modern_relevance: You sit in a room with someone whose calm changes the whole atmosphere. No lecture, no correction — just being near them makes your own habits feel smaller and your better instincts stronger.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जब तें प्रभु पद पदुम निहारे। मिटे दुसह दुख दोष हमारे॥ बचन सुनत पुरजन अनुरागे। तिन्ह के भाग सराहन लागे ॥
translation: जब से प्रभु के चरण कमल देखे, तब से हमारे दुःसह दुःख और दोष मिट गए। वनवासियों के वचन सुनकर अयोध्या के लोग प्रेम में भर गए और उनके भाग्य की सराहना करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Since we beheld the lotus feet of the Lord, our unbearable sorrow and faults have vanished. Hearing the forest dwellers’ words, the people of Ayodhya were filled with love and began praising their good fortune.
essence: Ram’s presence dissolves sorrow and awakens love in everyone around him.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram’s feet removes deep sorrow and inner faults. Hearing the forest dwellers speak, the people of Ayodhya feel love and praise their good fortune.
insight: It shifts attention from complaint to gratitude and shows how devotion changes the heart’s atmosphere.
modern_relevance: You hear someone speak with such sincerity that your own bitterness loosens. A single moment of real presence can make old pain feel lighter.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लागे सराहन भाग सब अनुराग बचन सुनावहीं बोलनि मिलनि सिय राम चरन सनेहु लखि सुखु पावहीं॥ नर नारि निदरहिं नेहु निज सुनि कोल भिल्लनि की गिरा। तुलसी कृपा रघुबंसमनि की लोह लै लौका तिरा॥
translation: सब उनके भाग्य की सराहना करने लगे और प्रेम के वचन सुनाने लगे। उन लोगों के बोलने और मिलने का ढंग तथा श्री सीता-रामजी के चरणों में उनका प्रेम देखकर सब सुख पा रहे हैं। उन कोल-भीलों की वाणी सुनकर सभी नर-नारी अपने प्रेम का निरादर करते हैं (उसे धिक्कार देते हैं)। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि यह रघुवंशमणि श्री रामचन्द्रजी की कृपा है कि लोहा नौका को अपने ऊपर लेकर तैर गया॥
english_translation: All began praising their fortune and speaking words of love. Seeing their speech, meeting, and affection for the feet of Sita and Ram, everyone felt joy. Hearing the speech of those Kol and Bhil people, men and women despised their own lovelessness. Tulsidas says: by the grace of the jewel of Raghu's line, even iron floated across the river.
essence: True love for Ram makes even the hard-hearted feel their own dryness.
simple_meaning: The villagers are moved by the love they see in the forest people for Ram and Sita. Even ordinary people feel ashamed of their own coldness. Tulsidas says Ram's grace can make the impossible happen.
insight: It shifts attention from social approval to the transforming power of genuine devotion.
modern_relevance: You hear a friend speak gently about someone they love, and your own guarded heart suddenly feels thin. Their sincerity exposes how much of your life has been performed without warmth.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: बिहरहिं बन चहु ओर प्रतिदिन प्रमुदित लोग सब। जल ज्यों दादुर मोर भए पीन पावस प्रथम ॥
translation: सब लोग दिनोंदिन परम आनंदित होते हुए वन में चारों ओर विचरते हैं। जैसे पहली वर्षा के जल से मेंढक और मोर मोटे हो जाते हैं (प्रसन्न होकर नाचते-कूदते हैं) ॥
english_translation: Everyone roams through the forest in daily delight, like frogs and peacocks swelling with the first rains.
essence: Shared joy can make exile feel like spring.
simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya now move through the forest happily, as if the first rains have made them bloom with life.
insight: It shows how a blessed presence can make even difficult circumstances feel alive and nourishing.
modern_relevance: A long family trip turns into laughter once the tension lifts and everyone starts enjoying the same roadside tea and rain. The place has not changed, but the mood has.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुर जन नारि मगन अति प्रीती। बासर जाहिं पलक सम बीती॥ सीय सासु प्रति बेष बनाई। सादर करइ सरिस सेवकाई ॥
translation: अयोध्यापुरी के पुरुष और स्त्री सभी प्रेम में अत्यन्त मग्न हो रहे हैं। उनके दिन पल के समान बीत जाते हैं। जितनी सासुएँ थीं, उतने ही वेष (रूप) बनाकर सीताजी सब सासुओं की आदरपूर्वक एक सी सेवा करती हैं ॥
english_translation: The men and women of Ayodhya were utterly absorbed in love. Their days passed like a blink. Sita dressed herself in the form of each mother-in-law and served every one of them with respect.
essence: Love becomes real when it turns into respectful service.
simple_meaning: Everyone in Ayodhya is caught up in loving joy, and time feels like it flies. Sita also takes on each mother-in-law's form and serves them all respectfully.
insight: It shifts attention from enjoying closeness to expressing it through humble care.
modern_relevance: A home full of laughter can make the hours disappear. In the middle of that warmth, someone notices the dishes, the tea, the tired elder in the next room, and serves without making a scene.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लखा न मरमु राम बिनु काहूँ। माया सब सिय माया माहूँ॥ सीयँ सासु सेवा बस कीन्हीं। तिन्ह लहि सुख सिख आसिष दीन्हीं ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के सिवा इस भेद को और किसी ने नहीं जाना। सब मायाएँ (पराशक्ति महामाया) श्री सीताजी की माया में ही हैं। सीताजी ने सासुओं को सेवा से वश में कर लिया। उन्होंने सुख पाकर सीख और आशीर्वाद दिए ॥
english_translation: No one understood the mystery except Ram. All illusion rests within Sita's own power. Sita won over her mothers-in-law through service, and they, pleased, gave her blessings and teachings.
essence: True grace changes others without needing force.
simple_meaning: Only Ram fully knows the hidden mystery. Sita's influence is so complete that even other powers of appearance rest within her, and she wins over her mothers-in-law through humble service.
insight: It shifts attention from control and display to gentle influence through service.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense family gathering and do the dishes without announcement. By the end of the evening, the room feels different. That is the kind of power this verse honors.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लखि सिय सहित सरल दोउ भाई। कुटिल रानि पछितानि अघाई॥ अवनि जमहि जाचति कैकेई। महि न बीचु बिधि मीचु न देई ॥
translation: सीताजी समेत दोनों भाइयों (श्री राम-लक्ष्मण) को सरल स्वभाव देखकर कुटिल रानी कैकेयी भरपेट पछताई। वह पृथ्वी तथा यमराज से याचना करती है, किन्तु धरती बीच (फटकर समा जाने के लिए रास्ता) नहीं देती और विधाता मौत नहीं देता ॥
english_translation: Seeing both brothers with Sita, simple and gentle, the crooked queen Kaikeyi was filled with regret. She begged the earth and Yama for a way out, but the ground would not open and death would not come.
essence: Regret can become so heavy that even death feels too slow.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi sees Ram, Lakshman, and Sita's innocence and feels unbearable regret. She wants the earth to swallow her and death to come, but neither happens.
insight: It shows regret at its most physical: guilt becomes so intense that the body longs for disappearance.
modern_relevance: You replay one decision at 2 a.m. and feel your chest tighten. You wish the floor would open, but the mind keeps you awake with what you cannot undo.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लोकहुँ बेद बिदित कबि कहहीं। राम बिमुख थलु नरक न लहहीं॥ यहु संसउ सब के मन माहीं। राम गवनु बिधि अवध कि नाहीं ॥
translation: लोक और वेद में प्रसिद्ध है और कवि (ज्ञानी) भी कहते हैं कि जो श्री रामजी से विमुख हैं, उन्हें नरक में भी ठौर नहीं मिलती। सबके मन में यह संदेह हो रहा था कि हे विधाता! श्री रामचन्द्रजी का अयोध्या जाना होगा या नहीं ॥
english_translation: It is famous among people and in the Vedas, and wise poets say that those who turn away from Ram find no place even in the lower realm. Everyone’s mind held one doubt: would Ram go to Ayodhya or not?
essence: Turning away from Ram leaves you without refuge.
simple_meaning: Turning away from Ram leaves no true refuge, and everyone is still wondering whether Ram will actually go to Ayodhya.
insight: It links inner exile with outer loss, then shows a city suspended in uncertainty.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you trust walk out of the room, and suddenly the whole day feels unstable. That unsettled feeling is what this verse knows.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निसि न नीद नहिं भूख दिन भरतु बिकल सुचि सोच। नीच कीच बिच मगन जस मीनहि सलिल सँकोच ॥
translation: भरतजी को न तो रात को नींद आती है, न दिन में भूख ही लगती है। वे पवित्र सोच में ऐसे विकल हैं, जैसे नीचे (तल) के कीचड़ में डूबी हुई मछली को जल की कमी से व्याकुलता होती है ॥
english_translation: Bharat has neither sleep at night nor hunger by day. He is shaken by pure sorrowful thought, like a fish trapped in mud and longing for water.
essence: True grief makes even the body feel exiled.
simple_meaning: Bharat is so overwhelmed by pure grief and concern that he cannot sleep or eat. His distress is like a fish trapped in mud, craving water.
insight: It shows how grief can become bodily and total, not just emotional.
modern_relevance: You lie awake after a message changes everything, staring at the ceiling while your body forgets hunger. Bharat's pain is what happens when love and regret become one knot.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कीन्हि मातु मिस काल कुचाली। ईति भीति जस पाकत साली॥ केहि बिधि होइ राम अभिषेकू। मोहि अवकलत उपाउ न एकू ॥
translation: (भरतजी सोचते हैं कि) माता के मिस से काल ने कुचाल की है। जैसे धान के पकते समय ईति का भय आ उपस्थित हो। अब श्री रामचन्द्रजी का राज्याभिषेक किस प्रकार हो, मुझे तो एक भी उपाय नहीं सूझ पड़ता ॥
english_translation: By my mother’s pretext, fate has played a wicked trick, like a blight striking ripening rice. How can Ram's coronation happen now? I can see no way at all.
essence: Grief can make every solution disappear.
simple_meaning: Bharat sees Kaikeyi’s demand as a cruel trick of fate. He feels helpless and cannot see any way to stop Ram’s coronation from being ruined.
insight: It shows how shock narrows attention to loss and blocks clear action.
modern_relevance: You open the email and realize one decision has wrecked the plan you spent months building. Your mind goes straight to panic: no fix, no backup, no way through.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: अवसि फिरहिं गुर आयसु मानी। मुनि पुनि कहब राम रुचि जानी॥ मातु कहेहुँ बहुरहिं रघुराऊ। राम जननि हठ करबि कि काऊ ॥
translation: गुरुजी की आज्ञा मानकर तो श्री रामजी अवश्य ही अयोध्या को लौट चलेंगे, परन्तु मुनि वशिष्ठजी तो श्री रामचन्द्रजी की रुचि जानकर ही कुछ कहेंगे। ( अर्थात वे श्री रामजी की रुचि देखे बिना जाने को नहीं कहेंगे)। माता कौसल्याजी के कहने से भी श्री रघुनाथजी लौट सकते हैं, पर भला, श्री रामजी को जन्म देने वाली माता क्या कभी हठ करेगी? ॥
english_translation: By obeying the teacher's command, Ram will surely return. Vashishtha will speak only after seeing Ram's own wish. Even if mother Kaushalya asks, Raghunath may return—but the mother who gave birth to Ram would never be stubborn.
essence: Love is deepest when it refuses to coerce.
simple_meaning: Ram will return because he follows his teacher's command, and even his family speaks only after understanding his own wish. No one should force him.
insight: It teaches you to honor authority and personal will before trying to influence a decision.
modern_relevance: You're drafting the message that could change everything, then you stop and ask: is this what they want, or just what you want? Sometimes the most loving move is to wait for consent.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मोहि अनुचर कर केतिक बाता। तेहि महँ कुसमउ बाम बिधाता॥ जौं हठ करउँ त निपट कुकरमू। हरगिरि तें गुरु सेवक धरमू ॥
translation: मुझ सेवक की तो बात ही कितनी है? उसमें भी समय खराब है (मेरे दिन अच्छे नहीं हैं) और विधाता प्रतिकूल है। यदि मैं हठ करता हूँ तो यह घोर कुकर्म (अधर्म) होगा, क्योंकि सेवक का धर्म शिवजी के पर्वत कैलास से भी भारी (निबाहने में कठिन) है ॥
english_translation: What am I, your servant, worth? The timing is already bad, and fate is against me. If I act stubbornly, it would be a grave wrong, because a servant’s duty is heavier to bear than Mount Kailash.
essence: Stubborn force is wrong when service itself is the duty.
simple_meaning: Bharat sees himself as a servant who must not act out of stubbornness. For him, forcing things would be wrong, because true service is a serious and difficult duty.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-assertion to humble responsibility, where restraint is part of service.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the angry text, make the dramatic call, or force the meeting to go your way. Bharat’s pause reminds you that not every impulse deserves action.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: एकउ जुगुति न मन ठहरानी। सोचत भरतहि रैनि बिहानी॥ प्रात नहाइ प्रभुहि सिर नाई। बैठत पठए रिषयँ बोलाई ॥
translation: एक भी युक्ति भरतजी के मन में न ठहरी। सोचते ही सोचते रात बीत गई। भरतजी प्रातःकाल स्नान करके और प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को सिर नवाकर बैठे ही थे कि ऋषि वशिष्ठजी ने उनको बुलवा भेजा ॥
english_translation: No one solution stayed in Bharata's mind. The night passed while he kept thinking. At dawn, after bathing and bowing to Lord Ram, he sat down just as Vashishtha had him called.
essence: When the mind finds no answer, humility becomes the next right step.
simple_meaning: Bharat spent the night unable to settle on any answer. In the morning he bathed, bowed to Ram, and came when Vashishtha called him.
insight: It shows the mind exhausted by moral pressure, then returning to reverence before action.
modern_relevance: You stare at your phone all night, trying to decide whether to send the message, resign, or stay silent. By dawn, the problem still exists — but your mind is finally tired enough to listen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गुर पद कमल प्रनामु करि बैठे आयसु पाइ। बिप्र महाजन सचिव सब जुरे सभासद आइ ॥
translation: भरतजी गुरु के चरणकमलों में प्रणाम करके आज्ञा पाकर बैठ गए। उसी समय ब्राह्मण, महाजन, मंत्री आदि सभी सभासद आकर जुट गए ॥
english_translation: Bharat bowed at the guru's lotus feet and sat down after receiving permission. Then Brahmins, nobles, ministers, and all the assembly gathered there.
essence: Humility opens the door before any hard truth can be spoken.
simple_meaning: Bharat shows respect to the teacher, takes permission, and sits down. The court then gathers around him.
insight: It shows how humility and proper order prepare the mind for serious counsel.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a tense family meeting, say nothing first, and wait for the elders to settle the room. That pause changes everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बोले मुनिबरु समय समाना। सुनहु सभासद भरत सुजाना॥ धरम धुरीन भानुकुल भानू। राजा रामु स्वबस भगवानू ॥
translation: श्रेष्ठ मुनि वशिष्ठजी समयोचित वचन बोले- हे सभासदों! हे सुजान भरत! सुनो। सूर्यकुल के सूर्य महाराज श्री रामचन्द्र धर्मधुरंधर और स्वतंत्र भगवान हैं ॥
english_translation: The great sage said at the right moment, “Listen, assembly and wise Bharata. Ram, the sun of the Raghu line, is the upholder of dharma and the Lord who acts by his own will.”
essence: True authority comes from freedom aligned with dharma.
simple_meaning: Ram is described as the perfect king: devoted to dharma, noble like the sun, and completely self-governed. He acts from inner freedom, not pressure.
insight: It shifts respect away from power and toward inner freedom aligned with duty.
modern_relevance: You’re in a meeting where everyone wants quick compliance, but the one person you trust is calm, principled, and impossible to pressure. That’s the kind of authority this verse honors.
speaker: Vashistha

verse_text: सत्यसंध पालक श्रुति सेतू। राम जनमु जग मंगल हेतु॥ गुर पितु मातु बचन अनुसारी। खल दलु दलन देव हितकारी ॥
translation: वे सत्य प्रतिज्ञ हैं और वेद की मर्यादा के रक्षक हैं। श्री रामजी का अवतार ही जगत के कल्याण के लिए हुआ है। वे गुरु, पिता और माता के वचनों के अनुसार चलने वाले हैं। दुष्टों के दल का नाश करने वाले और देवताओं के हितकारी हैं ॥
english_translation: He is true to his word and upholds the boundary of the sacred law. Ram's birth came for the world's welfare. He follows the words of his teacher, father, and mother, and destroys the host of the wicked while bringing benefit to the radiant beings.
essence: Ram's greatness is that his life serves truth, order, and the welfare of all.
simple_meaning: Ram is described as truthful, obedient to his parents and teacher, born for the world's welfare, and a destroyer of harmful forces.
insight: It shifts attention from charisma to character: truthfulness, obedience to rightful guidance, and service to the larger good.
modern_relevance: You sign a contract, call your parents back, and show up for the team even when no one is watching. This verse measures greatness by whether your life can be trusted.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नीति प्रीति परमारथ स्वारथु। कोउ न राम सम जान जथारथु॥ बिधि हरि हरु ससि रबि दिसिपाला। माया जीव करम कुलि काला ॥
translation: नीति, प्रेम, परमार्थ और स्वार्थ को श्री रामजी के समान यथार्थ (तत्त्व से) कोई नहीं जानता। ब्रह्मा, विष्णु, महादेव, चन्द्र, सूर्य, दिक्पाल, माया, जीव, सभी कर्म और काल, ॥
english_translation: No one knows policy, love, supreme purpose, and self-interest as Ram truly does. Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, the moon, the sun, the guardians of the directions, Maya, the living being, karma, the clans, and time itself all stand within his knowing.
essence: Ram alone sees duty, love, and self-interest exactly as they are.
simple_meaning: Ram understands right conduct, love, higher purpose, and self-interest perfectly. Even the great cosmic forces and time itself are within his full awareness.
insight: It shifts attention from self-justification to trusting the clarity of Ram's vision.
modern_relevance: You are trying to justify a choice to three different people, then rereading the message for the tenth time. Ram already sees the clean intention beneath all the noise.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अहिप महिप जहँ लगि प्रभुताई। जोग सिद्धि निगमागम गाई॥ करि बिचार जियँ देखहु नीकें। राम रजाइ सीस सबही कें ॥
translation: शेषजी और (पृथ्वी एवं पाताल के अन्यान्य) राजा आदि जहाँ तक प्रभुता है और योग की सिद्धियाँ, जो वेद और शास्त्रों में गाई गई हैं, हृदय में अच्छी तरह विचार कर देखो, (तो यह स्पष्ट दिखाई देगा कि) श्री रामजी की आज्ञा इन सभी के सिर पर है (अर्थात श्री रामजी ही सबके एक मात्र महान महेश्वर हैं) ॥
english_translation: Wherever there is rule—among serpents, kings of the earth, or the underworld—wherever yoga powers and perfected attainments are praised in the Vedas and scriptures, reflect carefully and see: Ram's command rests above them all.
essence: All power is borrowed; Ram's command is the source.
simple_meaning: All power, mastery, and even spiritual attainments are ultimately under Ram's command. Nothing stands above his will.
insight: It shifts you from chasing control to recognising a higher order already governing it.
modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the title, the authority — and then one bad email reminds you how fragile it all is. This verse puts every kind of power back in its place.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: राखें राम रजाइ रुख हम सब कर हित होइ। समुझि सयाने करहु अब सब मिलि संमत सोइ ॥
translation: अतएव श्री रामजी की आज्ञा और रुख रखने में ही हम सबका हित होगा। (इस तत्त्व और रहस्य को समझकर) अब तुम सयाने लोग जो सबको सम्मत हो, वही मिलकर करो ॥
english_translation: Therefore, keeping Ram's command is what will benefit us all. Understanding this well, you wise ones should now agree together on what is best.
essence: What serves Ram also serves everyone.
simple_meaning: Real welfare comes from following Ram's command. Once you see that clearly, wise people should agree and act together.
insight: It shifts decision-making from personal preference to shared alignment with dharma.
modern_relevance: A family group chat is spiralling over who should make the next decision, and everyone is arguing from ego. This verse points to the relief of choosing the option that serves the whole, not just the loudest voice.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सब कहुँ सुखद राम अभिषेकू। मंगल मोद मूल मग एकू॥ केहि बिधि अवध चलहिं रघुराऊ। कहहु समुझि सोइ करिअ उपाऊ ॥
translation: श्री रामजी का राज्याभिषेक सबके लिए सुखदायक है। मंगल और आनंद का मूल यही एक मार्ग है। (अब) श्री रघुनाथजी अयोध्या किस प्रकार चलें? विचारकर कहो, वही उपाय किया जाए ॥
english_translation: Ram's coronation would bring happiness to everyone. It is the one path from which auspiciousness and joy arise. But how should Lord Raghunath return to Ayodhya? Think carefully and say what plan should be made.
essence: The best outcome still needs the right way home.
simple_meaning: Ram's coronation would bless everyone, so the only question is how to bring him safely back to Ayodhya.
insight: It shifts attention from debating the goal to arranging the most dharmic means.
modern_relevance: You finally know the decision is right, but the hard part is logistics: how do you bring it about without breaking trust, timing, or relationships?
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब सादर सुनि मुनिबर बानी। नय परमारथ स्वारथ सानी॥ उतरु न आव लोग भए भोरे। तब सिरु नाइ भरत कर जोरे ॥
translation: मुनिश्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी की नीति, परमार्थ और स्वार्थ (लौकिक हित) में सनी हुई वाणी सबने आदरपूर्वक सुनी। पर किसी को कोई उत्तर नहीं आता, सब लोग भोले (विचार शक्ति से रहित) हो गए। तब भरत ने सिर नवाकर हाथ जोड़े ॥
english_translation: Everyone respectfully heard the sage's words, mixed with policy, higher purpose, and worldly benefit. No one had an answer; everyone fell silent. Then Bharat bowed his head and joined his hands.
essence: Humility can answer where argument cannot.
simple_meaning: Everyone listens to the sage's wise words but cannot answer. Bharat responds not with debate, but with humility and respect.
insight: It shifts you from argumentative certainty to respectful receptivity, where humility becomes the first right move.
modern_relevance: A tense family meeting goes quiet after the elder finishes speaking. Everyone has opinions, but no one has the heart to force them. Then the person who loves most lowers their head first.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भानुबंस भए भूप घनेरे। अधिक एक तें एक बड़ेरे॥ जनम हेतु सब कहँ कितु माता। करम सुभासुभ देइ बिधाता ॥
translation: (और कहा-) सूर्यवंश में एक से एक अधिक बड़े बहुत से राजा हो गए हैं। सभी के जन्म के कारण पिता-माता होते हैं और शुभ-अशुभ कर्मों को (कर्मों का फल) विधाता देते हैं ॥
english_translation: Many kings have ruled in the Solar dynasty, each greater than the last. Every being has a mother and father for birth, but the supreme being gives the results of good and bad actions.
essence: Birth comes from parents, but consequences come from action.
simple_meaning: Many great kings have ruled before, but birth comes from parents while the results of actions come from the supreme order.
insight: It shifts attention from ancestry and status to moral causation and responsibility.
