modern_relevance: You can trace your family tree for hours, but it won't explain why one choice wrecked trust and another repaired it. The deeper pattern is in what you do, not just where you came from.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: दलि दुख सजइ सकल कल्याना। अस असीस राउरि जगु जाना॥ सो गोसाइँ बिधि गति जेहिं छेंकी। सकइ को टारि टेक जो टेकी ॥
translation: आपकी आशीष ही एक ऐसी है, जो दुःखों का दमन करके, समस्त कल्याणों को सज देती है, यह जगत जानता है। हे स्वामी! आप ही हैं, जिन्होंने विधाता की गति (विधान) को भी रोक दिया। आपने जो टेक टेक दी (जो निश्चय कर दिया) उसे कौन टाल सकता है? ॥
english_translation: Your blessing alone can crush sorrow and arrange every blessing. The world knows this, my lord. You are the one who can even stop the course of fate. Who can turn aside what you have firmly resolved?
essence: Ram's blessing makes sorrow powerless and gives resolve the final word.
simple_meaning: Bharat praises the power of Ram's blessing and steadfast resolve. Ram's grace removes sorrow, brings good fortune, and cannot be resisted once firmly set.
insight: It shifts you from anxiety about outcomes to trust in a steady, protective presence.
modern_relevance: You are spiralling over a decision you cannot control, then someone you trust says, “Leave it to me.” The body relaxes because their steadiness is stronger than your panic.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: बूझिअ मोहि उपाउ अब सो सब मोर अभागु। सुनि सनेहमय बचनगुर उर उमगा अनुरागु ॥
translation: अब आप मुझसे उपाय पूछते हैं, यह सब मेरा अभाग्य है। भरतजी के प्रेममय वचनों को सुनकर गुरुजी के हृदय में प्रेम उमड़ आया ॥
english_translation: Now you ask me for a solution, but all of this is my own misfortune. Hearing Bharat's loving words, the teacher's heart overflowed with affection.
essence: Sincere love can turn misfortune into a moment of grace.
simple_meaning: Bharat says the solution is not in his hands; he sees his situation as misfortune. His loving words move the teacher deeply.
insight: It shows how humility and loving speech can open the way for guidance.
modern_relevance: You finally admit you don't know what to do, and someone answers with kindness instead of correction. That tenderness can change everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तात बात फुरि राम कृपाहीं। राम बिमुख सिधि सपनेहुँ नाहीं॥ सकुचउँ तात कहत एक बाता। अरध तजहिं बुध सरबस जाता॥1।
translation: (वे बोले-) हे तात! बात सत्य है, पर है रामजी की कृपा से ही। राम विमुख को तो स्वप्न में भी सिद्धि नहीं मिलती। हे तात! मैं एक बात कहने में सकुचाता हूँ। बुद्धिमान लोग सर्वस्व जाता देखकर (आधे की रक्षा के लिए) आधा छोड़ दिया करते हैं ॥
english_translation: “Father, the matter is true, but only through Ram’s grace. The one who turns away from Ram finds no success, even in a dream. Father, I hesitate to say one thing: wise people abandon half when they see the whole lost.”
essence: When the whole is lost, wisdom protects the half that remains.
simple_meaning: Success does not come from turning away from Ram, and a wise person saves what can still be saved instead of losing everything.
insight: It shifts you from stubborn attachment to practical discernment when loss is already unavoidable.
modern_relevance: You realize a project is collapsing, but your ego still wants to defend every part of it. This verse says: stop clinging to the whole fantasy; save what remains and let the rest go.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: तुम्ह कानन गवनहु दोउ भाई। फेरिअहिं लखन सीय रघुराई॥ सुनि सुबचन हरषे दोउ भ्राता। भे प्रमोद परिपूरन गाता ॥
translation: अतः तुम दोनों भाई (भरत-शत्रुघ्न) वन को जाओ और लक्ष्मण, सीता और श्री रामचन्द्र को लौटा दिया जाए। ये सुंदर वचन सुनकर दोनों भाई हर्षित हो गए। उनके सारे अंग परमानंद से परिपूर्ण हो गए ॥
english_translation: So you two brothers should go to the forest, and Lakshman, Sita, and Lord Ram should be brought back. Hearing these gracious words, both brothers rejoiced; their whole bodies were filled with bliss.
essence: Love can turn exile into a path home.
simple_meaning: The brothers are told to go to the forest and bring Ram, Sita, and Lakshman back. Hearing this, they become overjoyed.
insight: It shows how a single clear decision can dissolve grief and restore energy at once.
modern_relevance: You hear the text message you have been praying for: come home, it’s settled. Your shoulders drop before you even finish reading.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: मन प्रसन्न तन तेजु बिराजा। जनु जिय राउ रामु भए राजा॥ बहुत लाभ लोगन्ह लघु हानी। सम दुख सुख सब रोवहिं रानी ॥
translation: उनके मन प्रसन्न हो गए। शरीर में तेज सुशोभित हो गया। मानो राजा दशरथजी उठे हों और श्री रामचन्द्रजी राजा हो गए हों! अन्य लोगों को तो इसमें लाभ अधिक और हानि कम प्रतीत हुई, परन्तु रानियों को दुःख-सुख समान ही थे (राम-लक्ष्मण वन में रहें या भरत-शत्रुघ्न, दो पुत्रों का वियोग तो रहेगा ही), यह समझकर वे सब रोने लगीं ॥
english_translation: Their minds grew joyful, and their bodies shone with radiance, as if King Dasharath had risen and Ram had become king. Others saw little loss and much gain, but the queens saw equal grief and joy, and they all wept.
essence: A triumph can still leave the deepest love in tears.
simple_meaning: The family’s mood lifts at the thought of Ram returning to rule, but the queens still feel the pain of separation and begin to cry.
insight: It shows how a single event can be victory for some and sorrow for others.
modern_relevance: You get the promotion you wanted, and everyone celebrates. But at home, the family still feels the strain of what the win cost. Relief and loss can arrive together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहहिं भरतु मुनि कहा सो कीन्हे। फलु जग जीवन्ह अभिमत दीन्हे॥ कानन करउँ जनम भरि बासू। एहि तें अधिक न मोर सुपासू ॥
translation: भरतजी कहने लगे- मुनि ने जो कहा, वह करने से जगतभर के जीवों को उनकी इच्छित वस्तु देने का फल होगा। (चौदह वर्ष की कोई अवधि नहीं) मैं जन्मभर वन में वास करूँगा। मेरे लिए इससे बढ़कर और कोई सुख नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Bharat said, "What the sage said, let that be done. The fruit will be to give every being in the world what they long for. I will live in the forest for my whole life. Nothing is more pleasing to me than this."
essence: True non-attachment can make hardship feel like the sweetest choice.
simple_meaning: Bharat decides to accept the sage's instruction and live in the forest for life. He sees this as the best possible choice, because it serves everyone and removes his own claim to comfort.
insight: It shifts you from chasing personal ease to choosing the life that best honors dharma.
modern_relevance: You turn down a promotion because it would pull you away from what you know is right. The room goes quiet, but inside you feel steady. Bharat knows that refusing ease can be the cleanest form of love.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: अंतरजामी रामु सिय तुम्ह सरबग्य सुजान। जौं फुर कहहु त नाथ निज कीजिअ बचनु प्रवान ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी और सीताजी हृदय की जानने वाले हैं और आप सर्वज्ञ तथा सुजान हैं। यदि आप यह सत्य कह रहे हैं तो हे नाथ! अपने वचनों को प्रमाण कीजिए (उनके अनुसार व्यवस्था कीजिए) ॥
english_translation: Ram and Sita know the heart, and you are all-knowing and wise. If this is truly spoken, then, my lord, make your word real.
essence: A true promise must become visible in action.
simple_meaning: Bharat says Ram and Sita know the heart, so if Ram's promise is true, it should be fulfilled in action.
insight: It shifts you from accepting polished speech to asking whether a promise is actually being honoured.
modern_relevance: You’re in a tense family conversation where everyone says the right thing, but nothing changes. Bharat’s standard is simple: if the promise is real, let life show it.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: भरत बचन सुनि देखि सनेहू। सभा सहित मुनि भए बिदेहू॥ भरत महा महिमा जलरासी। मुनि मति ठाढ़ि तीर अबला सी ॥
translation: भरतजी के वचन सुनकर और उनका प्रेम देखकर सारी सभा सहित मुनि वशिष्ठजी विदेह हो गए (किसी को अपने देह की सुधि न रही)। भरतजी की महान महिमा समुद्र है, मुनि की बुद्धि उसके तट पर अबला स्त्री के समान खड़ी है ॥
english_translation: Hearing Bharat's words and seeing his love, the sage and the whole assembly were left speechless. Bharat's greatness is an ocean; the sage's mind stood at its shore like a helpless woman.
essence: True greatness can leave even wisdom speechless.
simple_meaning: Bharat's love overwhelms everyone present so completely that they lose track of their bodies. His greatness is so vast that even the sage's understanding can only stand at its edge.
insight: It shifts attention from clever explanation to the power of lived devotion.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose sincerity is so complete that the room changes. Nobody argues, performs, or postures anymore — everyone just feels the weight of what is real.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गा चह पार जतनु हियँ हेरा। पावति नाव न बोहितु बेरा॥ औरु करिहि को भरत बड़ाई। सरसी सीपि कि सिंधु समाई ॥
translation: वह (उस समुद्र के) पार जाना चाहती है, इसके लिए उसने हृदय में उपाय भी ढूँढे! पर (उसे पार करने का साधन) नाव, जहाज या बेड़ा कुछ भी नहीं पाती। भरतजी की बड़ाई और कौन करेगा? तलैया की सीपी में भी कहीं समुद्र समा सकता है? ॥
english_translation: She wants to cross to the far shore and has searched for a way in her heart, but she finds no boat, ship, or raft. Who else can praise Bharata’s greatness? Can the ocean fit inside a pond’s shell?
essence: Real greatness cannot be contained by ordinary praise.
simple_meaning: Bharata's virtue is so immense that ordinary praise cannot contain it. The verse says his greatness is as vast as the ocean, while praise is only a tiny shell.
insight: It shifts attention from polished praise to the scale of lived character.
modern_relevance: You try to explain someone who quietly carried a family through crisis, and every sentence feels too small. Their goodness doesn’t fit in compliments, because it was never built for display.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरतु मुनिहि मन भीतर भाए। सहित समाज राम पहिं आए॥ प्रभु प्रनामु करि दीन्ह सुआसनु। बैठे सब सुनि मुनि अनुसासनु ॥
translation: मुनि वशिष्ठजी की अन्तरात्मा को भरतजी बहुत अच्छे लगे और वे समाज सहित श्री रामजी के पास आए। प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने प्रणाम कर उत्तम आसन दिया। सब लोग मुनि की आज्ञा सुनकर बैठ गए ॥
english_translation: Bharat pleased the sage within his heart, and came with his companions to Rama. Lord Rama bowed to him and offered a fine seat. Everyone sat down after hearing the sage's instruction.
essence: Honor and humility create the space where wisdom can be heard.
simple_meaning: Bharat comes to Rama with the assembly. Rama honors him with respect, and everyone sits down to hear the sage's guidance.
insight: It shows that humility and courtesy prepare the mind for guidance.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense family meeting and choose respect first. That single gesture lowers the temperature enough for everyone to actually hear each other.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बोले मुनिबरु बचन बिचारी। देस काल अवसर अनुहारी॥ सुनहु राम सरबग्य सुजाना। धरम नीति गुन ग्यान निधाना ॥
translation: श्रेष्ठ मुनि देश, काल और अवसर के अनुसार विचार करके वचन बोले- हे सर्वज्ञ! हे सुजान! हे धर्म, नीति, गुण और ज्ञान के भण्डार राम! सुनिए- ॥
english_translation: The great sage spoke, considering the place, time, and occasion. 'Listen, Ram, all-knowing and wise, treasury of dharma, policy, qualities, and wisdom.'
essence: Wise speech fits the moment before it seeks to persuade.
simple_meaning: The sage speaks carefully, choosing words suited to the moment, and addresses Ram as the one who knows dharma, right conduct, virtues, and wisdom.
insight: It teaches you to shape speech to context instead of blurting out what is true in general.
modern_relevance: You are about to send a message into a tense family group chat. The right words matter as much as the right intention. Wisdom begins by reading the room.
speaker: Vasishta

verse_text: सब के उर अंतर बसहु जानहु भाउ कुभाउ। पुरजन जननी भरत हित होइ सो कहिअ उपाउ ॥
translation: आप सबके हृदय के भीतर बसते हैं और सबके भले-बुरे भाव को जानते हैं, जिसमें पुरवासियों का, माताओं का और भरत का हित हो, वही उपाय बतलाइए ॥
english_translation: You dwell in every heart and know every good and bad intention. Tell us the course that will benefit the people of the city, the mothers, and Bharata.
essence: Real guidance begins when you care about everyone’s welfare, not just your own.
simple_meaning: Ram is asked to choose the course that will help everyone, because he already knows every heart and every intention.
insight: It shifts you from partial, self-protective thinking to asking for the action that serves the whole circle.
modern_relevance: You’re in a family group chat where everyone is hurt and talking past each other. The wisest person is not the loudest one, but the one who can see what helps everyone most.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: आरत कहहिं बिचारि न काऊ। सूझ जुआरिहि आपन दाऊ॥ सुनि मुनि बचन कहत रघुराऊ॥ नाथ तुम्हारेहि हाथ उपाऊ ॥
translation: आर्त (दुःखी) लोग कभी विचारकर नहीं कहते। जुआरी को अपना ही दाँव सूझता है। मुनि के वचन सुनकर श्री रघुनाथजी कहने लगे- हे नाथ! उपाय तो आप ही के हाथ है ॥
english_translation: The distressed do not think carefully; a gambler sees only his own stake. Hearing the sage's words, Raghunath said, "Lord, the remedy is in your hands."
essence: Distress distorts judgment; the real remedy comes from surrender.
simple_meaning: When people are overwhelmed, they stop thinking clearly. Ram says the solution is not in his own hands but in the Lord's.
insight: It shifts you from self-reliant control to humble release when emotions cloud judgment.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a family crisis at 1 a.m., rereading the same message thread, knowing your mind is too shaken to decide well. The verse reminds you that panic shrinks judgment and some remedies require surrender.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सब कर हित रुख राउरि राखें। आयसु किए मुदित फुर भाषें॥ प्रथम जो आयसु मो कहुँ होई। माथें मानि करौं सिख सोई ॥
translation: आपका रुख रखने में और आपकी आज्ञा को सत्य कहकर प्रसन्नता पूर्वक पालन करने में ही सबका हित है। पहले तो मुझे जो आज्ञा हो, मैं उसी शिक्षा को माथे पर चढ़ाकर करूँ ॥
english_translation: Keeping to your wish is best for everyone. I will gladly carry out whatever order comes first, and I will hold that instruction to my head.
essence: True service starts when your own wish yields to rightful command.
simple_meaning: Serving the other person's will is the best way to help everyone. The speaker says he will gladly follow the first instruction given and treat it as sacred.
insight: It teaches you to treat rightful guidance as more important than personal preference.
modern_relevance: You’re in a family meeting where everyone is tense, and the quietest person says, ‘Tell me what helps most, and I’ll do that first.’ That kind of humility can save a room.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: पुनि जेहि कहँ जस कहब गोसाईं। सो सब भाँति घटिहि सेवकाईं॥ कह मुनि राम सत्य तुम्ह भाषा। भरत सनेहँ बिचारु न राखा ॥
translation: फिर हे गोसाईं! आप जिसको जैसा कहेंगे वह सब तरह से सेवा में लग जाएगा (आज्ञा पालन करेगा)। मुनि वशिष्ठजी कहने लगे- हे राम! तुमने सच कहा। पर भरत के प्रेम ने विचार को नहीं रहने दिया ॥
english_translation: Then, whatever you say, O Lord, will fully turn into service in every way. The sage said, "Ram, what you said is true. But Bharat's love left no room for calculation."
essence: Bharat's love is so pure that calculation cannot survive it.
simple_meaning: True love for Ram turns everything into service. Bharat's devotion is so complete that careful calculation disappears.
insight: It shifts you from measured compliance to wholehearted service shaped by devotion.
modern_relevance: You stop weighing every benefit and cost before helping someone you love. The heart simply moves, and the mind follows later.
speaker: Vashistha

verse_text: तेहि तें कहउँ बहोरि बहोरी। भरत भगति बस भइ मति मोरी॥ मोरें जान भरत रुचि राखी। जो कीजिअ सो सुभ सिव साखी ॥
translation: इसीलिए मैं बार-बार कहता हूँ, मेरी बुद्धि भरत की भक्ति के वश हो गई है। मेरी समझ में तो भरत की रुचि रखकर जो कुछ किया जाएगा, शिवजी साक्षी हैं, वह सब शुभ ही होगा ॥
english_translation: That is why I keep saying it again and again: my mind has been won over by Bharat's devotion. In my understanding, whatever is done while keeping Bharat's wish in view will surely be auspicious, Shiva is my witness.
essence: Devotion can make even judgment bend toward what is right.
simple_meaning: Vasistha says his judgment is now shaped by Bharat's devotion. He believes any decision that respects Bharat's wishes will be auspicious.
insight: It shifts judgment from status and strategy to the moral weight of selfless devotion.
modern_relevance: You watch someone refuse a promotion so a colleague can keep their job, and the room goes quiet. Suddenly, everyone can feel which choice is cleaner.
speaker: Vasistha

verse_text: भरत बिनय सादर सुनिअ करिअ बिचारु बहोरि। करब साधुमत लोकमत नृपनय निगम निचोरि ॥
translation: पहले भरत की विनती आदरपूर्वक सुन लीजिए, फिर उस पर विचार कीजिए। तब साधुमत, लोकमत, राजनीति और वेदों का निचोड़ (सार) निकालकर वैसा ही (उसी के अनुसार) कीजिए ॥
english_translation: First listen to Bharat's request with respect, then reflect on it carefully. After that, take the essence of the wise, public opinion, statecraft, and the Vedas, and act accordingly.
essence: Respectful listening comes before the right decision.
simple_meaning: Bharat's request should be heard respectfully and judged carefully. The right action comes from weighing wisdom, public feeling, leadership, and sacred guidance together.
insight: It shifts you from reacting to a single voice toward making a balanced, responsible decision.
modern_relevance: A family argument is already heated, and everyone is talking over each other. The person who pauses, listens to the quieter request, and weighs the fuller picture often makes the cleanest decision.
speaker: Vasistha

verse_text: गुर अनुरागु भरत पर देखी। राम हृदयँ आनंदु बिसेषी॥ भरतहि धरम धुरंधर जानी। निज सेवक तन मानस बानी ॥
translation: भरतजी पर गुरुजी का स्नेह देखकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी के हृदय में विशेष आनंद हुआ। भरतजी को धर्मधुरंधर और तन, मन, वचन से अपना सेवक जानकर- ॥
english_translation: Seeing the teacher's affection for Bharat, Ram felt special joy in his heart. Knowing Bharat as the upholder of righteousness and as his servant in body, mind, and speech—
essence: A noble heart rejoices when it sees another's devotion and goodness.
simple_meaning: Ram feels deep joy when he sees the teacher's affection for Bharat, because he recognises Bharat as fully devoted to righteousness and service.
insight: It shifts the mind from comparison to appreciation of another's dharma.
modern_relevance: You watch a mentor praise someone you admire, and your first feeling is joy, not envy. That quiet happiness reveals a generous heart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बोले गुरु आयस अनुकूला। बचन मंजु मृदु मंगलमूला॥ नाथ सपथ पितु चरन दोहाई। भयउ न भुअन भरत सम भाई ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी गुरु की आज्ञा अनुकूल मनोहर, कोमल और कल्याण के मूल वचन बोले- हे नाथ! आपकी सौगंध और पिताजी के चरणों की दुहाई है (मैं सत्य कहता हूँ कि) विश्वभर में भरत के समान कोई भाई हुआ ही नहीं ॥
english_translation: Ram spoke words that matched the guru’s command: beautiful, gentle, and full of blessing. “My lord, by your oath and by my father’s feet, I tell the truth: there has never been a brother like Bharat in all the world.”
essence: Gentle speech can honor devotion better than force ever will.
simple_meaning: Ram answers with soft, respectful words and praises Bharat as unmatched among brothers. His speech shows gratitude, humility, and love for family duty.
insight: It teaches you to answer admiration and conflict with language that heals, not hardens.
modern_relevance: When a family argument finally softens and someone speaks without sharpness, the room changes. A respectful sentence can do what anger never could: restore dignity and make love visible again.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जे गुर पद अंबुज अनुरागी। ते लोकहुँ बेदहुँ बड़भागी॥ राउर जा पर अस अनुरागू। को कहि सकइ भरत कर भागू ॥
translation: जो लोग गुरु के चरणकमलों के अनुरागी हैं, वे लोक में (लौकिक दृष्टि से) भी और वेद में (परमार्थिक दृष्टि से) भी बड़भागी होतें हैं! (फिर) जिस पर आप (गुरु) का ऐसा स्नेह है, उस भरत के भाग्य को कौन कह सकता है? ॥
english_translation: Those who love the guru's lotus feet are fortunate in both the world and the Vedas. What can anyone say of Bharat's fortune, on whom you have such love?
essence: Love for the guru makes ordinary and sacred life fruitful.
simple_meaning: People who are devoted to the guru are truly fortunate. Bharat is especially blessed because the guru loves him so deeply.
insight: It shifts attention from public success to the transforming power of loyal reverence.
modern_relevance: You meet a teacher who sees your effort before anyone else does. That steady respect changes how you carry yourself, because being received well can matter more than being praised widely.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: लखि लघु बंधु बुद्धि सकुचाई। करत बदन पर भरत बड़ाई॥ भरतु कहहिं सोइ किएँ भलाई। अस कहि राम रहे अरगाई ॥
translation: छोटा भाई जानकर भरत के मुँह पर उसकी बड़ाई करने में मेरी बुद्धि सकुचाती है। (फिर भी मैं तो यही कहूँगा कि) भरत जो कुछ कहें, वही करने में भलाई है। ऐसा कहकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी चुप हो रहे ॥
english_translation: Seeing his younger brother, his mind felt shy to praise Bharat in his face. Yet he said, "Whatever Bharat says, doing that is best." Saying this, Ram fell silent.
essence: True respect is following the good, not merely praising it.
simple_meaning: Ram feels shy to praise Bharat directly, yet says that doing what Bharat says is the right thing.
insight: It shifts respect from verbal praise to obedient recognition of what is truly right.
modern_relevance: You’re in a meeting and someone younger than you solves the problem before you do. Instead of defending your status, you admit they’re right and let their insight lead.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तब मुनि बोले भरत सन सब सँकोचु तजि तात। कृपासिंधु प्रिय बंधु सन कहहु हृदय कै बात ॥
translation: तब मुनि भरतजी से बोले- हे तात! सब संकोच त्यागकर कृपा के समुद्र अपने प्यारे भाई से अपने हृदय की बात कहो ॥
english_translation: Then the sage said to Bharat, "Cast off all hesitation, dear one, and tell your heart's truth to your beloved brother, the ocean of mercy."
essence: Hesitation falls away before real love.
simple_meaning: The sage urges Bharat to stop holding back and speak honestly to Ram, who is full of mercy and love.
insight: It shifts you from guarded silence to honest self-expression in the presence of trust.
modern_relevance: You rehearse a difficult text message for an hour, then delete it. The moment you finally speak plainly to someone who cares, the weight starts to lift.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुनि मुनि बचन राम रुख पाई। गुरु साहिब अनुकूल अघाई॥ लखि अपनें सिर सबु छरु भारू। कहि न सकहिं कछु करहिं बिचारू ॥
translation: मुनि के वचन सुनकर और श्री रामचन्द्रजी का रुख पाकर गुरु तथा स्वामी को भरपेट अपने अनुकूल जानकर सारा बोझ अपने ही ऊपर समझकर भरतजी कुछ कह नहीं सकते। वे विचार करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Hearing the sage's words and seeing Ram's favorable mood, Bharat felt that his teacher and lord were fully on his side. Seeing the whole burden on his own head, he could say nothing and kept thinking.
essence: Real responsibility can leave you speechless before it lets you speak.
simple_meaning: Bharat feels the sage and Ram are both in his favor, so he takes the whole burden on himself and falls silent, thinking deeply.
insight: It shifts the mind from speaking quickly to carrying the weight of the moment with care.
modern_relevance: You hear a message in a room full of people, and suddenly you know the decision is already resting on you. Your mouth goes dry, not from fear, but from responsibility.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुलकि सरीर सभाँ भए ठाढ़े। नीरज नयन नेह जल बाढ़े॥ कहब मोर मुनिनाथ निबाहा। एहि तें अधिक कहौं मैं काहा ॥
translation: शरीर से पुलकित होकर वे सभा में खड़े हो गए। कमल के समान नेत्रों में प्रेमाश्रुओं की बाढ़ आ गई। (वे बोले-) मेरा कहना तो मुनिनाथ ने ही निबाह दिया (जो कुछ मैं कह सकता था वह उन्होंने ही कह दिया)। इससे अधिक मैं क्या कहूँ? ॥
english_translation: His body thrilled as he stood in the assembly. Tears of love rose in his lotus eyes. He said, "My words have already been fulfilled by the sage. What more can I say now?"
essence: True devotion leaves you with nothing left to prove.
simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed with devotion and gratitude. Tears rise as he realizes the sage has already spoken the truth he wanted to express.
insight: It shifts you from self-conscious explanation to grateful recognition that your truth has already been held.
modern_relevance: You finally sit across from someone who understands your pain before you explain it. The relief is so complete that words feel unnecessary.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: मैं जानउँ निज नाथ सुभाऊ। अपराधिहु पर कोह न काऊ॥ मो पर कृपा सनेहु बिसेषी। खेलत खुनिस न कबहूँ देखी ॥
translation: अपने स्वामी का स्वभाव मैं जानता हूँ। वे अपराधी पर भी कभी क्रोध नहीं करते। मुझ पर तो उनकी विशेष कृपा और स्नेह है। मैंने खेल में भी कभी उनकी रीस (अप्रसन्नता) नहीं देखी ॥
english_translation: I know my Lord’s nature well: he never grows angry, even with one who has done wrong. He has special grace and affection for me. I have never seen him displeased, even in play.
essence: Ram’s grace stays steady even when you fail.
simple_meaning: Ram’s nature is gentle and forgiving. Even when people err, he does not become angry. The speaker feels especially held by Ram’s grace and has never seen him displeased.
insight: It shifts you from fearing divine anger to trusting a mercy that stays steady even when you falter.
modern_relevance: You replay a mistake before sending the apology text, expecting coldness. But some people meet your weakness with steadiness, not punishment.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सिसुपन तें परिहरेउँ न संगू। कबहुँ न कीन्ह मोर मन भंगू॥ मैं प्रभु कृपा रीति जियँ जोही। हारेहूँ खेल जितावहिं मोही ॥
translation: बचपन में ही मैंने उनका साथ नहीं छोड़ा और उन्होंने भी मेरे मन को कभी नहीं तोड़ा (मेरे मन के प्रतिकूल कोई काम नहीं किया)। मैंने प्रभु की कृपा की रीति को हृदय में भलीभाँति देखा है (अनुभव किया है)। मेरे हारने पर भी खेल में प्रभु मुझे जिता देते रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: I have not left his company since childhood, and he has never broken my heart. I have seen the way the Lord's grace works: even when I lose, he still lets me win the game.
essence: Grace can turn even defeat into a hidden victory.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he never left Ram's side since childhood, and Ram never hurt him. He has learned that Ram's grace is such that even in defeat, Ram still lets him win.
insight: It shifts the mind from measuring life by wins and losses to seeing grace inside both.
modern_relevance: You look back at years of loyalty to someone who never used your trust against you. Even the hard moments now feel like they were guided by a kindness you couldn't see then.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: महूँ सनेह सकोच बस सनमुख कही न बैन। दरसन तृपित न आजु लगि प्रेम पिआसे नैन ॥
translation: मैंने भी प्रेम और संकोचवश कभी सामने मुँह नहीं खोला। प्रेम के प्यासे मेरे नेत्र आज तक प्रभु के दर्शन से तृप्त नहीं हुए ॥
english_translation: I too, held back by love and modesty, never spoke face to face. My eyes, thirsty for his sight, have still not been satisfied.
essence: Love can be so deep that even speech feels too small.
simple_meaning: Bharat says his love and modesty kept him from speaking openly, and his eyes have never felt full without Ram's sight.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to longing, showing that love can be quiet, restrained, and still absolute.
modern_relevance: You keep the unread message open because you don't know how to say what matters most. The silence isn't indifference — sometimes it is love mixed with reverence.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: बिधि न सकेऊ सहि मोर दुलारा। नीच बीचु जननी मिस पारा॥ यहउ कहत मोहि आजु न सोभा। अपनीं समुझि साधु सुचि को भा ॥
translation: परन्तु विधाता मेरा दुलार न सह सका। उसने नीच माता के बहाने (मेरे और स्वामी के बीच) अंतर डाल दिया। यह भी कहना आज मुझे शोभा नहीं देता, क्योंकि अपनी समझ से कौन साधु और पवित्र हुआ है? (जिसको दूसरे साधु और पवित्र मानें, वही साधु है) ॥
english_translation: But fate could not bear my affection. It placed a barrier between me and my beloved through the excuse of my lowly mother. Even saying this does not suit me today, for who has become holy and pure by their own judgment?
essence: Self-praise stains the very humility it tries to prove.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he should not praise himself as pure or holy. He sees that self-approval is empty and unworthy, especially when he is speaking about his own family and conduct.
insight: It shifts you away from self-justification and toward humble, quiet conduct.
modern_relevance: You almost type a long message defending yourself after being blamed at family dinner. Then you stop. You know that explaining your own purity usually makes you look smaller, not cleaner.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: मातु मंदि मैं साधु सुचाली। उर अस आनत कोटि कुचाली॥ फरइ कि कोदव बालि सुसाली। मुकता प्रसव कि संबुक काली ॥
translation: माता नीच है और मैं सदाचारी और साधु हूँ, ऐसा हृदय में लाना ही करोड़ों दुराचारों के समान है। क्या कोदों की बाली उत्तम धान फल सकती है? क्या काली घोंघी मोती उत्पन्न कर सकती है? ॥
english_translation: To think, 'My mother is bad and I am noble,' is like committing millions of wrongs in the heart. Can a stalk of kodu grain bear fine rice? Can a black shellfish produce pearls?
essence: Pride that condemns your own mother is already a moral failure.
simple_meaning: Bharat says it is deeply wrong to think he is noble while his mother is blameworthy. He uses simple images to show that a pure result cannot come from a corrupt source.
insight: It shifts you from judgment to responsibility, so you stop using comparison to feel pure.
modern_relevance: You catch yourself telling a friend, 'I would never act like my mother.' The sentence feels clever for a second, then ugly. Bharat shows why self-righteous distance can corrupt the heart.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: सपनेहूँ दोसक लेसु न काहू। मोर अभाग उदधि अवगाहू॥ बिनु समुझें निज अघ परिपाकू। जारिउँ जायँ जननि कहि काकू ॥
translation: स्वप्न में भी किसी को दोष का लेश भी नहीं है। मेरा अभाग्य ही अथाह समुद्र है। मैंने अपने पापों का परिणाम समझे बिना ही माता को कटु वचन कहकर व्यर्थ ही जलाया ॥
english_translation: Even in a dream, no one deserves blame. My own misfortune is an endless ocean. Without understanding the fruit of my own sins, I burned my mother by speaking harshly in vain.
essence: Blame fades when you finally face your own part.
simple_meaning: Bharat says no one else is at fault. His own misfortune and unrecognized wrongdoing led him to speak harshly to his mother and regret it.
insight: It shifts attention from blaming others to owning the harm you helped create.
modern_relevance: After a fight, you replay every line and want to blame the other person. But later, in the quiet of your room, you see the moment you crossed the line too.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: हृदयँ हेरि हारेउँ सब ओरा। एकहि भाँति भलेहिं भल मोरा॥ गुर गोसाइँ साहिब सिय रामू। लागत मोहि नीक परिनामू ॥
translation: मैं अपने हृदय में सब ओर खोज कर हार गया (मेरी भलाई का कोई साधन नहीं सूझता)। एक ही प्रकार भले ही (निश्चय ही) मेरा भला है। वह यह है कि गुरु महाराज सर्वसमर्थ हैं और श्री सीता-रामजी मेरे स्वामी हैं। इसी से परिणाम मुझे अच्छा जान पड़ता है ॥
english_translation: I searched my heart in every direction and found no other way. One thing alone is surely good for me: my teacher is the lord, and Sita-Ram are my masters. Because of this, the outcome feels right to me.
essence: Peace begins when you stop seeking a better master.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he has searched every possibility in his heart and found only one good path: accepting Guru and Sita-Ram as his masters.
insight: It shifts the mind from endless comparison to wholehearted surrender.
modern_relevance: You keep replaying the same decision at 1 a.m., hoping another option will appear. Then you finally choose the one place your heart can truly stand, and the noise drops away.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: साधु सभाँ गुर प्रभु निकट कहउँ सुथल सतिभाउ। प्रेम प्रपंचु कि झूठ फुर जानहिं मुनि रघुराउ ॥
translation: साधुओं की सभा में गुरुजी और स्वामी के समीप इस पवित्र तीर्थ स्थान में मैं सत्य भाव से कहता हूँ। यह प्रेम है या प्रपंच (छल-कपट)? झूठ है या सच? इसे (सर्वज्ञ) मुनि वशिष्ठजी और (अन्तर्यामी) श्री रघुनाथजी जानते हैं ॥
english_translation: In the holy gathering, near the guru and my lord, I speak with true feeling. Is this love or deception? Is it false or true? Only the sages and Raghunath know.
essence: Real devotion does not need to defend itself.
simple_meaning: The speaker admits confusion about whether this is genuine love or just an act, and places the answer in the hands of the guru and Ram.
insight: It shifts you from self-judgment to trust in a wiser witness of your heart.
modern_relevance: You send a message after midnight and wonder if your care was genuine or just neediness. The mind keeps judging itself, but the deepest truth of love is not always visible from inside the ache.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: भूपति मरन प्रेम पनु राखी। जननी कुमति जगतु सबु साखी॥ देखि न जाहिं बिकल महतारीं। जरहिं दुसह जर पुर नर नारीं ॥
translation: प्रेम के प्रण को निबाहकर महाराज (पिताजी) का मरना और माता की कुबुद्धि, दोनों का सारा संसार साक्षी है। माताएँ व्याकुल हैं, वे देखी नहीं जातीं। अवधपुरी के नर-नारी दुःसह ताप से जल रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Keeping the vow of love, the king died; the whole world is witness to the queen's wrong-mindedness. The mothers cannot be looked at in their anguish; the men and women of Ayodhya burn in unbearable heat.
essence: One wrongful choice can make an entire kingdom grieve.
simple_meaning: Dasharath has died after keeping the promise of love, and Kaikeyi's wrong judgment has brought grief to everyone. The women are shattered, and Ayodhya burns with sorrow.
insight: It shifts attention from private regret to the wider damage caused by wrong judgment and broken trust.
modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after one harsh decision, and suddenly everyone is carrying the weight. One person's choice can leave an entire home stunned and scorched.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: महीं सकल अनरथ कर मूला। सो सुनि समुझि सहिउँ सब सूला॥ सुनि बन गवनु कीन्ह रघुनाथा। करि मुनि बेष लखन सिय साथा ॥ बिनु पानहिन्ह पयादेहि पाएँ। संकरु साखि रहेउँ एहि घाएँ॥ बहुरि निहारि निषाद सनेहू। कुलिस कठिन उर भयउ न बेहू ॥
translation: मैं ही इन सारे अनर्थों का मूल हूँ, यह सुन और समझकर मैंने सब दुःख सहा है। श्री रघुनाथजी लक्ष्मण और सीताजी के साथ मुनियों का सा वेष धारणकर बिना जूते पहने पाँव-प्यादे (पैदल) ही वन को चले गए, यह सुनकर, शंकरजी साक्षी हैं, इस घाव से भी मैं जीता रह गया (यह सुनते ही मेरे प्राण नहीं निकल गए)! फिर निषादराज का प्रेम देखकर भी इस वज्र से भी कठोर हृदय में छेद नहीं हुआ (यह फटा नहीं)॥2-3॥
english_translation: Seeing and understanding that I am the root of all misfortune, I have endured every pain. Hearing that Raghunath went to the forest with Lakshman and Sita, dressed like a sage and walking barefoot, I held on by Shiva's witness. Then, even after seeing Nishadraj's love, this heart, harder than lightning, did not break.
essence: Humility lets you survive what pride would shatter you over.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he has survived unbearable pain by understanding that he himself is the root of the disaster. Even hearing of Ram's exile and seeing Nishadraj's love did not break his heart.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-justification to humble endurance, so pain becomes bearable instead of corrosive.
modern_relevance: You replay the argument after midnight and finally admit your part in it. The shame still hurts, but it stops poisoning everything once you stop defending yourself.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: अब सबु आँखिन्ह देखेउँ आई। जिअत जीव जड़ सबइ सहाई॥ जिन्हहि निरखि मग साँपिनि बीछी। तजहिं बिषम बिषु तामस तीछी ॥
translation: अब यहाँ आकर सब आँखों देख लिया। यह जड़ जीव जीता रह कर सभी सहावेगा। जिनको देखकर रास्ते की साँपिनी और बीछी भी अपने भयानक विष और तीव्र क्रोध को त्याग देती हैं- ॥
english_translation: Now I have come and seen it all with my own eyes. Living beings endure only because they are helped by the living. Even snakes and scorpions on the road lay aside their terrible poison and fierce heat when they see such a one.
essence: True presence makes even harshness soften.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he has now seen the full reality for himself: life continues only because others support it, and even fierce dangers soften before truly noble presence.
insight: It shifts attention from power and blame to the fragile support that lets life continue.
modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed after days of bad news, and suddenly the small kindnesses matter most: the water cup, the hand squeeze, the quiet presence that keeps you from breaking.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: तेइ रघुनंदनु लखनु सिय अनहित लागे जाहि। तासु तनय तजि दुसह दुख दैउ सहावइ काहि ॥
translation: वे ही श्री रघुनंदन, लक्ष्मण और सीता जिसको शत्रु जान पड़े, उस कैकेयी के पुत्र मुझको छोड़कर दैव दुःसह दुःख और किसे सहावेगा? ॥
english_translation: Those very Raghunandan, Lakshman, and Sita whom you saw as enemies—why should the unbearable sorrow fall on anyone else when Kaikeyi's son must bear it?
essence: The sorrow of your choice comes home to you.
simple_meaning: Bharat says that the unbearable grief belongs to Kaikeyi's son, because Kaikeyi treated Ram, Lakshman, and Sita like enemies and sent them away.
insight: It shifts blame into responsibility: the one connected to the act must also carry its grief.
modern_relevance: You finally read the message thread where your decision hurt everyone you love. The silence afterward feels heavier than the choice itself.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: सुनि अति बिकल भरत बर बानी। आरति प्रीति बिनय नय सानी॥ सोक मगन सब सभाँ खभारू। मनहुँ कमल बन परेउ तुसारू ॥
translation: अत्यन्त व्याकुल तथा दुःख, प्रेम, विनय और नीति में सनी हुई भरतजी की श्रेष्ठ वाणी सुनकर सब लोग शोक में मग्न हो गए, सारी सभा में विषाद छा गया। मानो कमल के वन पर पाला पड़ गया हो ॥
english_translation: Hearing Bharata's noble words, filled with anguish, love, humility, and moral restraint, everyone in the assembly was overcome with grief. It was as if frost had fallen on a field of lotuses.
essence: Bharata's wounded nobility makes the whole assembly grieve with him.
simple_meaning: Bharat speaks with deep pain, love, humility, and restraint, and everyone present falls into grief. The whole assembly feels cold and heavy, like lotus flowers struck by frost.
insight: It shows how sincere grief and moral dignity can move an entire gathering without argument.
modern_relevance: You hear a friend speak after a family loss, and the room changes at once. Their honesty is so full of feeling that everyone else goes quiet with them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहि अनेक बिधि कथा पुरानी। भरत प्रबोधु कीन्ह मुनि ग्यानी॥ बोले उचित बचन रघुनंदू। दिनकर कुल कैरव बन चंदू ॥
translation: तब ज्ञानी मुनि वशिष्ठजी ने अनेक प्रकार की पुरानी (ऐतिहासिक) कथाएँ कहकर भरतजी का समाधान किया। फिर सूर्यकुल रूपी कुमुदवन के प्रफुल्लित करने वाले चन्द्रमा श्री रघुनंदन उचित वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: Then the wise sage Vashishtha spoke many kinds of ancient stories to comfort Bharat. After that, the Moon of Raghu's line, Ram, spoke fitting words.
essence: Comfort comes first; fitting truth follows only when the heart is ready.
simple_meaning: Vashishtha first comforts Bharat with old stories, and then Ram speaks in a way that fits the moment.
insight: It shows that comfort often needs preparation before instruction can help.
modern_relevance: A friend is crying in your kitchen, and you do not rush to fix it. You sit, you listen, you offer what can actually be heard. Then the right words finally land.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तात जायँ जियँ करहु गलानी। ईस अधीन जीव गति जानी॥ तीनि काल तिभुअन मत मोरें। पुन्यसिलोक तात तर तोरें ॥
translation: हे तात! तुम अपने हृदय में व्यर्थ ही ग्लानि करते हो। जीव की गति को ईश्वर के अधीन जानो। मेरे मत में (भूत, भविष्य, वर्तमान) तीनों कालों और (स्वर्ग, पृथ्वी और पाताल) तीनों लोकों के सब पुण्यात्मा पुरुष तुम से नीचे हैं ॥
english_translation: Father, do not trouble your heart with grief. Know that the fate of a living being rests in the divine. In my view, all the virtuous beings of the three times and three worlds are beneath you.
essence: Grief eases when you stop making yourself the author of everything.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Bharat not to blame himself. Life moves under a higher order, and even the most virtuous people are not above this truth.
insight: It shifts you from self-condemnation to surrendering the burden of control.
modern_relevance: You replay one conversation all night, convinced you ruined everything. Ram’s words meet that spiral: not every outcome belongs to your control, and not every pain is your fault.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: उर आनत तुम्ह पर कुटिलाई। जाइ लोकु परलोकु नसाई॥ दोसु देहिं जननिहि जड़ तेई। जिन्ह गुर साधु सभा नहिं सेई ॥
translation: हृदय में भी तुम पर कुटिलता का आरोप करने से यह लोक (यहाँ के सुख, यश आदि) बिगड़ जाता है और परलोक भी नष्ट हो जाता है (मरने के बाद भी अच्छी गति नहीं मिलती)। माता कैकेयी को तो वे ही मूर्ख दोष देते हैं, जिन्होंने गुरु और साधुओं की सभा का सेवन नहीं किया है ॥
english_translation: Even thinking crookedly about you ruins this world and the next. Only fools blame Mother Kaikeyi; they are the ones who have never sat in the company of teachers and saints.
essence: Private resentment damages both your present life and what follows.
simple_meaning: Even private ill will against someone harms your life now and after death. People who blame Kaikeyi without understanding are ignorant and have not kept company with wise teachers and saints.
insight: It shifts you from blame to discernment, and from judgment to the need for wise company.
modern_relevance: You rehearse blame in your head after a family fight, and the bitterness starts shaping everything you see. This verse says that hidden resentment already damages you before you ever speak.
speaker: Vasistha

verse_text: मिटिहहिं पाप प्रपंच सब अखिल अमंगल भार। लोक सुजसु परलोक सुखु सुमिरत नामु तुम्हार ॥
translation: हे भरत! तुम्हारा नाम स्मरण करते ही सब पाप, प्रपंच (अज्ञान) और समस्त अमंगलों के समूह मिट जाएँगे तथा इस लोक में सुंदर यश और परलोक में सुख प्राप्त होगा ॥
english_translation: O Bharat, by remembering your name, all sins, illusion, and every burden of inauspiciousness are removed. In this world there is good fame, and in the next there is happiness.
essence: Bharat's remembrance is so pure it washes away burden and brings blessing.
simple_meaning: Remembering Bharat's name is said to remove wrongdoing, confusion, and all misfortune, while bringing good reputation here and happiness beyond.
insight: It shifts devotion from ceremony to remembrance as a source of cleansing and strength.
modern_relevance: You hear a friend's name after a hard day and feel your chest loosen. Some people steady you just by being remembered with love.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कहउँ सुभाउ सत्य सिव साखी। भरत भूमि रह राउरि राखी॥ तात कुतरक करहु जनि जाएँ। बैर पेम नहिं दुरइ दुराएँ ॥
translation: हे भरत! मैं स्वभाव से ही सत्य कहता हूँ, शिवजी साक्षी हैं, यह पृथ्वी तुम्हारी ही रखी रह रही है। हे तात! तुम व्यर्थ कुतर्क न करो। वैर और प्रेम छिपाए नहीं छिपते ॥
english_translation: O Bharat, I speak the truth by nature; Shiva himself is my witness. This earth has remained yours alone. Do not go into useless argument, dear one. Enmity and love cannot be hidden.
essence: Love and enmity reveal themselves without disguise.
simple_meaning: Bharat should stop doubting and arguing. Tulsidas says he speaks truthfully, with Shiva as witness, and that love or hostility always reveal themselves.
insight: It shifts attention from verbal defense to the deeper truth already visible in conduct and feeling.
modern_relevance: You're trying to explain your intentions in a long text thread, but the tone already gave you away. No amount of clever wording can hide whether you care, resent, or mean well.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मुनिगन निकट बिहग मृग जाहीं। बाधक बधिक बिलोकि पराहीं॥ हित अनहित पसु पच्छिउ जाना। मानुष तनु गुन ग्यान निधाना ॥
translation: पक्षी और पशु मुनियों के पास (बेधड़क) चले जाते हैं, पर हिंसा करने वाले बधिकों को देखते ही भाग जाते हैं। मित्र और शत्रु को पशु-पक्षी भी पहचानते हैं। फिर मनुष्य शरीर तो गुण और ज्ञान का भंडार ही है ॥
english_translation: Birds and animals go near sages, but they flee when they see hunters. Even animals know friend from foe. Then the human body is a treasure-house of virtue and understanding.
essence: Human life is wasted if it never becomes clear seeing.
simple_meaning: Even birds and animals can sense who is safe and who is dangerous. Human life is far greater, because it can hold virtue and understanding.
insight: It shifts you from reactive fear to thoughtful discernment.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and immediately feel who is steady and who is draining. That instinct is basic. Your human gift is going further: seeing with wisdom, not just sensing risk.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तात तुम्हहि मैं जानउँ नीकें। करौं काह असमंजस जीकें॥ राखेउ रायँ सत्य मोहि त्यागी। तनु परिहरेउ पेम पन लागी ॥
translation: हे तात! मैं तुम्हें अच्छी तरह जानता हूँ। क्या करूँ? जी में बड़ा असमंजस (दुविधा) है। राजा ने मुझे त्याग कर सत्य को रखा और प्रेम-प्रण के लिए शरीर छोड़ दिया ॥
english_translation: Dear brother, I know you well. What should I do? My heart is deeply torn. The king upheld truth by abandoning me, and gave up his body for the sake of love and his vow.
essence: Truth can be honored only at the price of a broken heart.
simple_meaning: Bharat tells Lakshman that he knows him well, but he is confused and heartbroken. He says Dasharath upheld truth and love even by giving up his life.
insight: It shifts the mind from judging grief as weakness to seeing it as the cost of honoring truth.
modern_relevance: You read a text message from someone who chose what they believed was right, and now everything feels both noble and unbearable. Bharat knows that kind of split heart.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: तासु बचन मेटत मन सोचू। तेहि तें अधिक तुम्हार सँकोचू॥ ता पर गुर मोहि आयसु दीन्हा। अवसि जो कहहु चहउँ सोइ कीन्हा ॥
translation: उनके वचन को मेटते मन में सोच होता है। उससे भी बढ़कर तुम्हारा संकोच है। उस पर भी गुरुजी ने मुझे आज्ञा दी है, इसलिए अब तुम जो कुछ कहो, अवश्य ही मैं वही करना चाहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Thinking of their words, my mind feels troubled. Even greater than that is your hesitation. On top of that, the guru has given me this command, so whatever you say, I want to do that for sure.
essence: True duty begins when your own preference stops leading.
simple_meaning: Ram says he has already received a command and now wants to follow Bharat's wishes without hesitation.
insight: It shifts you from defending your own position to aligning with a binding responsibility.
modern_relevance: You’re in a tense family call, everyone talking over each other, and you finally say, “Tell me what you need, and I’ll do it.” That shift can stop the spiral.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: मनु प्रसन्न करि सकुच तजि कहहु करौं सोइ आजु। सत्यसंध रघुबर बचन सुनि भा सुखी समाजु ॥
translation: तुम मन को प्रसन्न कर और संकोच को त्याग कर जो कुछ कहो, मैं आज वही करूँ। सत्य प्रतिज्ञ रघुकुल श्रेष्ठ श्री रामजी का यह वचन सुनकर सारा समाज सुखी हो गया ॥
english_translation: “Set your mind at ease, let go of hesitation, and do today whatever you say. Hearing this vow of truth from the best of the Raghu line, the whole assembly became happy.”
essence: A truthful word can calm everyone before any action begins.
simple_meaning: Speak without hesitation, then do exactly what you promised. Ram's truthfulness makes everyone around him feel safe and happy.
insight: It teaches you to make your promise and your action one thing, so trust can settle in around you.
modern_relevance: You tell a friend, “I’ll be there,” and then you actually show up when it matters. That simple alignment can calm a whole room faster than any explanation.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुर गन सहित सभय सुरराजू। सोचहिं चाहत होन अकाजू॥ बनत उपाउ करत कछु नाहीं। राम सरन सब गे मन माहीं ॥
translation: देवगणों सहित देवराज इन्द्र भयभीत होकर सोचने लगे कि अब बना-बनाया काम बिगड़ना ही चाहता है। कुछ उपाय करते नहीं बनता। तब वे सब मन ही मन श्री रामजी की शरण गए ॥
english_translation: The gods, with Indra at their head, grew fearful and thought, “Now the planned work is about to go wrong.” No remedy seemed to work. Then, in their hearts, they all took refuge in Ram.
essence: Helplessness becomes grace when you turn to Ram.
simple_meaning: The gods panic because their efforts are failing, and they inwardly turn to Ram for refuge.
insight: It shifts the mind from anxious fixing to inward surrender when effort reaches its limit.
modern_relevance: You have three backup plans, two phone calls, and one more spreadsheet, but the problem still won't move. In that moment, the mind finally softens and asks for help beyond its own control.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरि बिचारि परस्पर कहहीं। रघुपति भगत भगति बस अहहीं॥ सुधि करि अंबरीष दुरबासा। भे सुर सुरपति निपट निरासा ॥
translation: फिर वे विचार करके आपस में कहने लगे कि श्री रघुनाथजी तो भक्त की भक्ति के वश हैं। अम्बरीष और दुर्वासा की (घटना) याद करके तो देवता और इन्द्र बिल्कुल ही निराश हो गए ॥
english_translation: Then they reflected together and said, "Raghupati is bound by a devotee's devotion." Remembering Ambarish and Durvasa, the gods and Indra fell completely into despair.
essence: Ram is reached by devotion, not by pressure.
simple_meaning: The gods realise that Ram responds to devotion, not power. Remembering old stories of a devoted king and a proud sage, they feel helpless.
insight: It shifts attention from control to reverent trust, showing that devotion can accomplish what force cannot.
modern_relevance: You’ve tried arguing, proving, and pushing for days, and nothing changes. Then one quiet act of sincerity cuts through the whole mess — the kind of opening this verse points to.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सहे सुरन्ह बहु काल बिषादा। नरहरि किए प्रगट प्रहलादा॥ लगि लगि कान कहहिं धुनि माथा। अब सुर काज भरत के हाथा ॥
translation: पहले देवताओं ने बहुत समय तक दुःख सहे। तब भक्त प्रह्लाद ने ही नृसिंह भगवान को प्रकट किया था। सब देवता परस्पर कानों से लग-लगकर और सिर धुनकर कहते हैं कि अब (इस बार) देवताओं का काम भरतजी के हाथ है ॥
english_translation: The gods endured great sorrow for a long time. Then Prahlada made Narahari appear. Pressing close together, speaking into one another's ears and shaking their heads, they say, “Now the gods’ work is in Bharata’s hands.”
essence: Quiet devotion can become the only force strong enough to move events.
simple_meaning: The gods have suffered for a long time, and now they see Bharata as the one who can help them. Their hope rests on his devotion and purity.
insight: It shifts attention from power and planning to the moral force of devotion and character.
modern_relevance: Everyone in the room has tried to fix the mess, and the loudest voices have failed. Then someone calm, loyal, and unshowy steps in — and suddenly the whole team turns toward them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आन उपाउ न देखिअ देवा। मानत रामु सुसेवक सेवा॥ हियँ सपेम सुमिरहु सब भरतहि। निज गुन सील राम बस करतहि ॥
translation: हे देवताओं! और कोई उपाय नहीं दिखाई देता। श्री रामजी अपने श्रेष्ठ सेवकों की सेवा को मानते हैं (अर्थात उनके भक्त की कोई सेवा करता है, तो उस पर बहुत प्रसन्न होते हैं)। अतएव अपने गुण और शील से श्री रामजी को वश में करने वाले भरतजी का ही सब लोग अपने-अपने हृदय में प्रेम सहित स्मरण करो ॥
english_translation: O gods, no other remedy appears. Ram honors the service of his devoted servants. So remember Bharat with love in your hearts, for his virtues and noble character have won Ram over.
essence: Pure service can win what force never reaches.
simple_meaning: No other solution works here: Ram responds to devoted service. Remember Bharat with love, because his character and virtue have won Ram's heart.
insight: It shifts attention from control to loving service as the real power in relationship.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to persuade someone with arguments, reminders, and pressure, but nothing changes. Then a quiet act of care lands differently, and the relationship softens on its own.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि सुर मत सुरगुर कहेउ भल तुम्हार बड़ भागु। सकल सुमंगल मूल जग भरत चरन अनुरागु ॥
translation: देवताओं का मत सुनकर देवगुरु बृहस्पतिजी ने कहा- अच्छा विचार किया, तुम्हारे बड़े भाग्य हैं। भरतजी के चरणों का प्रेम जगत में समस्त शुभ मंगलों का मूल है ॥
english_translation: Hearing the gods' counsel, the teacher of the gods, Brihaspati, said, 'Good. You are greatly blessed. Love for Bharat's feet is the root of all good fortune in the world.'
essence: Reverence for Bharat is the root of all auspiciousness.
simple_meaning: Brihaspati blesses the gods' idea and says that loving Bharat is itself a source of all auspiciousness.
insight: It shifts attention from visible status to the hidden devotion that sustains a whole world.
modern_relevance: You meet someone quietly holding a family together while everyone else chases credit. Later, you realise the whole room runs on their steadiness. This verse says that kind of devotion is not small — it is the source.
speaker: Brihaspati

verse_text: सीतापति सेवक सेवकाई। कामधेनु सय सरिस सुहाई॥ भरत भगति तुम्हरें मन आई। तजहु सोचु बिधि बात बनाई ॥
translation: सीतानाथ श्री रामजी के सेवक की सेवा सैकड़ों कामधेनुओं के समान सुंदर है। तुम्हारे मन में भरतजी की भक्ति आई है, तो अब सोच छोड़ दो। विधाता ने बात बना दी ॥
english_translation: The service of Rama's servant is as beautiful as hundreds of wish-fulfilling cows. If your mind has turned to Bharata's devotion, let go of worry. The creator has already arranged it well.
essence: Devotion to Ram's devotee is itself a blessing that ends worry.
simple_meaning: Serving a true devotee of Ram is wonderfully rewarding. If your heart has turned toward Bharata's devotion, stop worrying — the situation has already been set right.
insight: It shifts you from anxious fixing to trusting the power of sincere devotion and service.
modern_relevance: You help someone who loves your family, and the atmosphere changes before anyone says thank you. Something honest and generous has entered the room, and the tension starts to loosen.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: देखु देवपति भरत प्रभाऊ। सजह सुभायँ बिबस रघुराऊ॥ मन थिर करहु देव डरु नाहीं। भरतहि जानि राम परिछाहीं ॥
translation: हे देवराज! भरतजी का प्रभाव तो देखो। श्री रघुनाथजी सहज स्वभाव से ही उनके पूर्णरूप से वश में हैं। हे देवताओं ! भरतजी को श्री रामचन्द्रजी की परछाईं (परछाईं की भाँति उनका अनुसरण करने वाला) जानकर मन स्थिर करो, डर की बात नहीं है ॥
english_translation: O lord of the gods, look at Bharat’s greatness. By his very nature, Raghunath is completely under his influence. O beings of light, steady your minds and fear not; know Bharat as Ram’s own shadow.
essence: True devotion can make even the highest heart yield naturally.
simple_meaning: Bharat’s devotion is so great that even Ram naturally responds to it. The gods are told to stop fearing and trust Bharat’s role as Ram’s devoted shadow.
insight: It shifts attention from anxious control to the stabilising power of faithful presence.
modern_relevance: You’re worried about whether your loyalty will be misunderstood. Then someone quietly shows up, takes responsibility, and proves that devotion can hold a whole situation together without drama.
speaker: Brihaspati

verse_text: सुनि सुरगुर सुर संमत सोचू। अंतरजामी प्रभुहि सकोचू॥ निज सिर भारु भरत जियँ जाना। करत कोटि बिधि उर अनुमाना ॥
translation: देवगुरु बृहस्पतिजी और देवताओं की सम्मति (आपस का विचार) और उनका सोच सुनकर अन्तर्यामी प्रभु श्री रामजी को संकोच हुआ। भरतजी ने अपने मन में सब बोझा अपने ही सिर जाना और वे हृदय में करोड़ों (अनेकों) प्रकार के अनुमान (विचार) करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Hearing the gods' and Brihaspati's concern, the all-knowing Lord felt uneasy. Bharat took the whole burden upon his own head and kept turning over countless thoughts in his heart.
essence: True devotion makes even burden feel shared.
simple_meaning: Ram feels a gentle unease after hearing the concern around Bharat, while Bharat carries the whole matter in his heart and turns it over in many ways.
insight: It shows how deep care makes both the giver and the beloved feel responsibility at once.
modern_relevance: You read a tense family message and immediately start carrying everyone's feelings on your own shoulders. Before anyone asks, you are already trying to hold the whole room together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि बिचारु मन दीन्ही ठीका। राम रजायस आपन नीका॥ निज पन तजि राखेउ पनु मोरा। छोहु सनेहु कीन्ह नहिं थोरा ॥
translation: सब तरह से विचार करके अंत में उन्होंने मन में यही निश्चय किया कि श्री रामजी की आज्ञा में ही अपना कल्याण है। उन्होंने अपना प्रण छोड़कर मेरा प्रण रखा। यह कुछ कम कृपा और स्नेह नहीं किया (अर्थात अत्यन्त ही अनुग्रह और स्नेह किया) ॥
english_translation: After thinking it through, he decided in his heart that Ram's command was the best path. He set aside his own vow and upheld mine. That was no small grace or affection.
essence: Your own vow can be surrendered when a truer duty appears.
simple_meaning: Bharat decides that Ram's command is the right guide, even if it means setting aside his own promise. He sees this as a great act of love.
insight: It shifts you from defending your own plan to honoring the obligation that matters most.
modern_relevance: You promised yourself one thing, then a parent, partner, or teacher needed something truer from you. The mature move is not stubborn self-protection; it's knowing which commitment deserves to stand.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कीन्ह अनुग्रह अमित अति सब बिधि सीतानाथ। करि प्रनामु बोले भरतु जोरि जलज जुग हाथ ॥
translation: श्री जानकीनाथजी ने सब प्रकार से मुझ पर अत्यन्त अपार अनुग्रह किया। तदनन्तर भरतजी दोनों करकमलों को जोड़कर प्रणाम करके बोले- ॥
english_translation: Janakinath has shown me boundless grace in every way. Then Bharat joined his hands, bowed, and said:
essence: Grace received with humility becomes the doorway to surrender.
simple_meaning: Bharat bows and says that Ram has shown him limitless grace in every way.
insight: It shifts you from self-justification to humble recognition of the grace you have received.
modern_relevance: You finally get a message from someone you disappointed, and it is kinder than you deserved. The first honest response is not defense — it is gratitude.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: कहौं कहावौं का अब स्वामी। कृपा अंबुनिधि अंतरजामी॥ गुर प्रसन्न साहिब अनुकूला। मिटी मलिन मन कलपित सूला ॥
translation: हे स्वामी! हे कृपा के समुद्र! हे अन्तर्यामी! अब मैं (अधिक) क्या कहूँ और क्या कहाऊँ? गुरु महाराज को प्रसन्न और स्वामी को अनुकूल जानकर मेरे मलिन मन की कल्पित पीड़ा मिट गई ॥
english_translation: O master, what more can I say or make others say? Ocean of grace, inner witness, when the teacher is pleased and the master is favorable, the imagined pain of my impure mind is gone.
essence: Grace can end pain the mind itself created.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he has nothing more to say. When the teacher is pleased and Ram is favorable, the pain created by his own troubled mind disappears.
insight: It shifts attention from self-made suffering to the relief that comes from trust and alignment.
modern_relevance: You finally get the message from someone you deeply respect, and the knot in your chest unwinds. The problem was never only outside you; half of it was the story your mind kept replaying.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: अपडर डरेउँ न सोच समूलें। रबिहि न दोसु देव दिसि भूलें॥ मोर अभागु मातु कुटिलाई। बिधि गति बिषम काल कठिनाई ॥
translation: मैं मिथ्या डर से ही डर गया था। मेरे सोच की जड़ ही न थी। दिशा भूल जाने पर हे देव! सूर्य का दोष नहीं है। मेरा दुर्भाग्य, माता की कुटिलता, विधाता की टेढ़ी चाल और काल की कठिनता, ॥
english_translation: I was frightened by a false fear; there was no real cause for sorrow. If I lost my way, the sun was not at fault. My misfortune, my mother’s crookedness, fate’s crooked course, and the harshness of time—these are to blame.
essence: False fear fades when you stop blaming the innocent.
simple_meaning: Bharat says his fear had no real basis. If he went astray, the blame was not on the sun but on his own misfortune, his mother’s wrongdoing, fate, and the harshness of time.
insight: It teaches you to separate real cause from emotional blame, so you can face loss without distortion.
modern_relevance: You missed the train, then spent the whole ride blaming the app, the traffic, the weather, anything but the real mistake. This verse asks for cleaner seeing: name the cause without turning it into a story of resentment.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: पाउ रोपि सब मिलि मोहि घाला। प्रनतपाल पन आपन पाला॥ यह नइ रीति न राउरि होई। लोकहुँ बेद बिदित नहिं गोई ॥
translation: इन सबने मिलकर पैर रोपकर (प्रण करके) मुझे नष्ट कर दिया था, परन्तु शरणागत के रक्षक आपने अपना (शरणागत की रक्षा का) प्रण निबाहा (मुझे बचा लिया)। यह आपकी कोई नई रीति नहीं है। यह लोक और वेदों में प्रकट है, छिपी नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Everyone joined together and drove me down, but you, protector of those who take refuge, kept your own vow and saved me. This is not your new way. It is known openly in the world and in the Vedas.
essence: The one who surrenders is never abandoned by Ram.
simple_meaning: Bharat says Ram saved him even after others tried to crush him, because Ram always protects anyone who takes refuge in him.
insight: It shifts trust from human approval to steadfast refuge in the one who keeps a vow.
modern_relevance: You were blamed in a group chat, cornered in a meeting, and left with no defence. Then one person stood beside you anyway. Bharat's praise is the feeling of finding a refuge that does not collapse under social pressure.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जगु अनभल भल एकु गोसाईं। कहिअ होइ भल कासु भलाईं॥ देउ देवतरु सरिस सुभाऊ। सनमुख बिमुख न काहुहि काऊ ॥
translation: सारा जगत बुरा (करने वाला) हो, किन्तु हे स्वामी! केवल एक आप ही भले (अनुकूल) हों, तो फिर कहिए, किसकी भलाई से भला हो सकता है? हे देव! आपका स्वभाव कल्पवृक्ष के समान है, वह न कभी किसी के सम्मुख (अनुकूल) है, न विमुख (प्रतिकूल) ॥
english_translation: The whole world may be unkind, but if you alone are kind, whose kindness can make things good? O Lord, your nature is like the wish-fulfilling tree: never favorable to some and hostile to others.
essence: Ram's grace does not favor you; it simply remains good.
simple_meaning: The world may feel hostile, but Ram's nature is always good to everyone. His grace does not depend on whether someone stands near him or turns away.
insight: It shifts the mind from judging events as personal favor or rejection to trusting a steady, impartial grace.
modern_relevance: You watch two friends get the same bad news, and one says life is unfair while the other quietly keeps faith. This verse speaks to that deeper steadiness: not everything around you is kind, but the highest presence is not arbitrary.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जाइ निकट पहिचानि तरु छाहँ समनि सब सोच। मागत अभिमत पाव जग राउ रंकु भल पोच ॥
translation: उस वृक्ष (कल्पवृक्ष) को पहचानकर जो उसके पास जाए, तो उसकी छाया ही सारी चिंताओं का नाश करने वाली है। राजा-रंक, भले-बुरे, जगत में सभी उससे माँगते ही मनचाही वस्तु पाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Approaching that tree and recognizing it, all sorrow ends in its shade. King and beggar, good and bad alike, receive whatever they ask from it.
essence: Near true refuge, worry dissolves and needs are met.
simple_meaning: A truly wish-fulfilling presence removes worry and gives what each person seeks, whether they are powerful or poor.
insight: It shifts the mind from scarcity to confidence in a generous refuge.
modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed, exhausted and scared, and one calm person in the room somehow steadies everyone. Being near that kind of presence changes what you can bear.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: लखि सब बिधि गुर स्वामि सनेहू। मिटेउ छोभु नहिं मन संदेहू॥ अब करुनाकर कीजिअ सोई। जन हित प्रभु चित छोभु न होई ॥
translation: गुरु और स्वामी का सब प्रकार से स्नेह देखकर मेरा क्षोभ मिट गया, मन में कुछ भी संदेह नहीं रहा। हे दया की खान! अब वही कीजिए जिससे दास के लिए प्रभु के चित्त में क्षोभ (किसी प्रकार का विचार) न हो ॥
english_translation: Seeing the love between guru and master, my distress is gone and my mind has no doubt. O source of compassion, now do only what leaves no burden on your servant's heart.
essence: True devotion asks for the beloved's ease, not personal gain.
simple_meaning: Bharat sees the affection between teacher and ruler and feels relieved. He asks Ram to act in a way that causes no pain or worry for his servant.
insight: It shifts devotion from self-protection to selfless concern for the other person's peace.
modern_relevance: You finally hear someone you love speak gently about you after a long misunderstanding. The relief is immediate, and all you want is to respond in a way that doesn't add to their strain.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जो सेवकु साहिबहि सँकोची। निज हित चहइ तासु मति पोची॥ सेवक हित साहिब सेवकाई। करै सकल सुख लोभ बिहाई ॥
translation: जो सेवक स्वामी को संकोच में डालकर अपना भला चाहता है, उसकी बुद्धि नीच है। सेवक का हित तो इसी में है कि वह समस्त सुखों और लोभों को छोड़कर स्वामी की सेवा ही करे ॥
english_translation: A servant who makes the master uneasy for personal gain has poor judgment. A servant's good lies in serving the master, leaving all pleasures and greed behind.
essence: Service becomes pure when your own gain stops mattering.
simple_meaning: A true servant does not put personal gain above the master's ease. Real welfare comes from serving wholeheartedly, without chasing pleasure or greed.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to faithful service, especially when another person's trust is at stake.
modern_relevance: You ask a teammate to cover your mistake so your bonus survives. The verse cuts through that reflex: if your role depends on someone else, protect their ease before your own gain.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: स्वारथु नाथ फिरें सबही का। किएँ रजाइ कोटि बिधि नीका॥ यह स्वारथ परमारथ सारू। सकल सुकृत फल सुगति सिंगारू ॥
translation: हे नाथ! आपके लौटने में सभी का स्वार्थ है और आपकी आज्ञा पालन करने में करोड़ों प्रकार से कल्याण है। यही स्वार्थ और परमार्थ का सार (निचोड़) है, समस्त पुण्यों का फल और सम्पूर्ण शुभ गतियों का श्रृंगार है ॥
english_translation: O Lord, your return is the good of everyone. In obeying your command, countless forms of welfare are fulfilled. This is the essence of self-interest and the highest good: the fruit of all merit and the adornment of every blessed state.
essence: What is good for everyone is also your highest good.
simple_meaning: Real benefit is not selfish gain. It is doing what is right, because that serves everyone and brings the highest good.
insight: It shifts the mind from private gain to actions that serve the whole field of relationships.
modern_relevance: You’re tempted to choose the option that flatters your ego, but the quieter choice would help everyone in the room. Sometimes what is best for you is the same thing that is best for others.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: देव एक बिनती सुनि मोरी। उचित होइ तस करब बहोरी॥ तिलक समाजु साजि सबु आना। करिअ सुफल प्रभु जौं मनु माना ॥
translation: हे देव! आप मेरी एक विनती सुनकर, फिर जैसा उचित हो वैसा ही कीजिए। राजतिलक की सब सामग्री सजाकर लाई गई है, जो प्रभु का मन माने तो उसे सफल कीजिए (उसका उपयोग कीजिए) ॥
english_translation: O divine one, hear my one request. Then do what is fitting. The whole royal coronation has been prepared; if it pleases you, let it be made fruitful.
essence: Prepared plans mean nothing unless they serve the right will.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks Ram to ignore the prepared coronation unless Ram himself approves it. What matters is not the ceremony, but what is fitting to Ram's will.
insight: It shifts you from defending your arrangement to submitting it to what is truly right.
modern_relevance: You have a venue booked, guests invited, and plans printed — then the person at the center says, 'Not like this.' Bharat's response is to stop protecting the plan and honor what is fitting.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: सानुज पठइअ मोहि बन कीजिअ सबहि सनाथ। नतरु फेरिअहिं बंधु दोउ नाथ चलौं मैं साथ ॥
translation: छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न समेत मुझे वन में भेज दीजिए और (अयोध्या लौटकर) सबको सनाथ कीजिए। नहीं तो किसी तरह भी (यदि आप अयोध्या जाने को तैयार न हों) हे नाथ! लक्ष्मण और शत्रुघ्न दोनों भाइयों को लौटा दीजिए और मैं आपके साथ चलूँ ॥
english_translation: Send me to the forest with my younger brother, and make everyone safe by returning. Otherwise, if you will not go back to Ayodhya, Lord, send both brothers back, and I will go with you.
essence: Real loyalty asks for the burden, not the reward.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks to go to the forest with his younger brother, or else asks Ram to send the brothers back and let him go with Ram. He wants everyone else to be सुरक्षित first.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-advantage to shared responsibility, even when the cost is personal.
modern_relevance: You are offered the better seat, the easier role, the cleaner exit — but someone else would be left carrying the burden. Bharat's answer is to move first for everyone else's good.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: नतरु जाहिं बन तीनिउ भाई। बहुरिअ सीय सहित रघुराई॥ जेहि बिधि प्रभु प्रसन्न मन होई। करुना सागर कीजिअ सोई ॥
translation: अथवा हम तीनों भाई वन चले जाएँ और हे श्री रघुनाथजी! आप श्री सीताजी सहित (अयोध्या को) लौट जाइए। हे दयासागर! जिस प्रकार से प्रभु का मन प्रसन्न हो, वही कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Or let us three brothers go to the forest, and let you, O Raghu lord, return with Sita. O ocean of compassion, do whatever brings your heart peace.
essence: Love gives up its own plan so the beloved can be at peace.
simple_meaning: Bharat offers to go to the forest with both brothers if that is what Ram wants, and asks Ram and Sita to return if that will please him.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to wholehearted yielding for another's good.
modern_relevance: You're in a family argument and realise you no longer care about winning the point. You just want the other person to feel safe enough to soften. That is Bharat's heart.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: देवँ दीन्ह सबु मोहि अभारू। मोरें नीति न धरम बिचारू॥ कहउँ बचन सब स्वारथ हेतू। रहत न आरत के चित चेतू ॥
translation: हे देव! आपने सारा भार (जिम्मेवारी) मुझ पर रख दिया। पर मुझमें न तो नीति का विचार है, न धर्म का। मैं तो अपने स्वार्थ के लिए सब बातें कह रहा हूँ। आर्त (दुःखी) मनुष्य के चित्त में चेत (विवेक) नहीं रहता ॥
english_translation: The divine has placed the whole burden on me, yet I have no sense of policy or duty. I speak only for my own gain; a distressed heart cannot keep clear awareness.
essence: A distressed heart cannot judge cleanly.
simple_meaning: Bharat admits that he has been given a heavy responsibility, but he lacks the judgment to handle it purely. He says his words are driven by self-interest because grief clouds the mind.
insight: It teaches you to notice when grief is steering your speech, so you do not mistake emotional pressure for clear judgment.
modern_relevance: You’re trying to write a careful message after a brutal argument, but every sentence is tinted by hurt. Bharat names that exact moment: distress makes even good intentions wobble.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: उतरु देइ सुनि स्वामि रजाई। सो सेवकु लखि लाज लजाई॥ अस मैं अवगुन उदधि अगाधू। स्वामि सनेहँ सराहत साधू ॥
translation: स्वामी की आज्ञा सुनकर जो उत्तर दे, ऐसे सेवक को देखकर लज्जा भी लजा जाती है। मैं अवगुणों का ऐसा अथाह समुद्र हूँ (कि प्रभु को उत्तर दे रहा हूँ), किन्तु स्वामी (आप) स्नेह वश साधु कहकर मुझे सराहते हैं! ॥
english_translation: Hearing his master's command, the servant who gives a reply makes even shame feel ashamed. I am an unfathomable ocean of faults, yet out of affection my master praises me as noble.
essence: Real service answers without ego and receives praise without claiming it.
simple_meaning: A real servant does not feel proud when answering a master's command. Bharat calls himself full of faults and says Ram praises him only out of affection.
insight: It shifts you from self-display to obedient, humble service.
modern_relevance: You get a message from someone you deeply respect, and your first urge is to explain, defend, or polish your image. Bharat shows another way: answer simply, stay humble, and let service speak louder than self-protection.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: अब कृपाल मोहि सो मत भावा। सकुच स्वामि मन जाइँ न पावा॥ प्रभु पद सपथ कहउँ सति भाऊ। जग मंगल हित एक उपाऊ ॥
translation: हे कृपालु! अब तो वही मत मुझे भाता है, जिससे स्वामी का मन संकोच न पावे। प्रभु के चरणों की शपथ है, मैं सत्यभाव से कहता हूँ, जगत के कल्याण के लिए एक यही उपाय है ॥
english_translation: O compassionate one, now only that counsel pleases me by which the master's mind feels no hesitation. By the Lord's feet, I speak truly: this is the only way for the world's welfare.
essence: Real surrender wants the other person's ease, not your own victory.
simple_meaning: Bharat says the best advice is the one that does not make his master uncomfortable. He insists this is the true way to bring good to the world.
insight: It shifts you from pushing your preference to serving what truly eases the other person's heart.
modern_relevance: You're about to send a message that could pressure someone into agreeing just to keep the peace. Bharat's standard is sharper: if your words create hesitation, they are not yet clean.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: प्रभु प्रसन्न मन सकुच तजि जो जेहि आयसु देब। सो सिर धरि धरि करिहि सबु मिटिहि अनट अवरेब ॥
translation: प्रसन्न मन से संकोच त्यागकर प्रभु जिसे जो आज्ञा देंगे, उसे सब लोग सिर चढ़ा-चढ़ाकर (पालन) करेंगे और सब उपद्रव और उलझनें मिट जाएँगी ॥
english_translation: With a pleased heart, set aside hesitation, and whatever order the Lord gives, everyone will carry it on their heads; all obstacles and confusion will dissolve.
essence: Clear obedience dissolves confusion.
simple_meaning: When you receive a rightful command with a willing heart, people will follow it and the confusion around it will clear away.
insight: It teaches you to act with wholehearted clarity instead of dragging hesitation into a necessary task.
modern_relevance: You’re in a tense family group chat, and everyone is waiting for someone to speak clearly. The moment you stop circling and say the right thing plainly, the whole mess starts settling.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: भरत बचन सुचि सुनि सुर हरषे। साधु सराहि सुमन सुर बरषे॥ असमंजस बस अवध नेवासी। प्रमुदित मन तापस बनबासी ॥
translation: भरतजी के पवित्र वचन सुनकर देवता हर्षित हुए और 'साधु-साधु' कहकर सराहना करते हुए देवताओं ने फूल बरसाए। अयोध्या निवासी असमंजस के वश हो गए (कि देखें अब श्री रामजी क्या कहते हैं) तपस्वी तथा वनवासी लोग (श्री रामजी के वन में बने रहने की आशा से) मन में परम आनन्दित हुए ॥
english_translation: Hearing Bharat's pure words, the devas rejoiced. Praising him as noble, they showered flowers. The people of Ayodhya were left in suspense, while ascetics and forest dwellers felt deep joy in their hearts.
essence: Pure words can lift some hearts while leaving the moment unresolved.
simple_meaning: Bharat's sincere words move everyone differently: the devas rejoice, Ayodhya waits in suspense, and holy people feel joy.
insight: It shows how sincere speech can transform a whole atmosphere without resolving the larger conflict yet.
modern_relevance: You send a message that finally says what you mean. Some people breathe easier, some freeze, and everyone feels the room change.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चुपहिं रहे रघुनाथ सँकोची। प्रभु गति देखि सभा सब सोची॥ जनक दूत तेहि अवसर आए। मुनि बसिष्ठँ सुनि बेगि बोलाए ॥
translation: किन्तु संकोची श्री रघुनाथजी चुप ही रह गए। प्रभु की यह स्थिति (मौन) देख सारी सभा सोच में पड़ गई। उसी समय जनकजी के दूत आए, यह सुनकर मुनि वशिष्ठजी ने उन्हें तुरंत बुलवा लिया ॥
english_translation: But Raghunath stayed silent, shy and restrained. Seeing the Lord's silence, the whole assembly fell into thought. Just then, Janak's messengers arrived, and hearing this, sage Vashistha quickly called them in.
essence: Silence can change a whole room before anyone speaks.
simple_meaning: Ram stays silent and the court grows thoughtful. At that moment, Janak's messengers arrive, and Vashistha has them brought in at once.
insight: It keeps the focus on the unfolding scene, not a moral claim.
modern_relevance: You say nothing after a tense family conversation, and everyone in the room starts reading your face. Then a message arrives that shifts the whole evening.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि प्रनाम तिन्ह रामु निहारे। बेषु देखि भए निपट दुखारे॥ दूतन्ह मुनिबर बूझी बाता। कहहु बिदेह भूप कुसलाता ॥
translation: उन्होंने (आकर) प्रणाम करके श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखा। उनका (मुनियों का सा) वेष देखकर वे बहुत ही दुःखी हुए। मुनिश्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी ने दूतों से बात पूछी कि राजा जनक का कुशल समाचार कहो ॥
english_translation: After bowing, they looked at Ram. Seeing his ascetic dress, they were deeply saddened. Then the great sage Vashishtha asked the messengers, “Tell me, how is King Janaka?”
essence: Ram's exile is visible at a glance, and it wounds the heart.
simple_meaning: The messengers bow to Ram, are saddened by his ascetic look, and Vashishtha asks after Janaka's well-being.
insight: It captures how appearance can carry emotional truth before anyone speaks.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room and see someone you love looking thinner, quieter, older. The greeting comes first, but the worry lands before any words do.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि सकुचाइ नाइ महि माथा। बोले चरबर जोरें हाथा॥ बूझब राउर सादर साईं। कुसल हेतु सो भयउ गोसाईं ॥
translation: यह (मुनि का कुशल प्रश्न) सुनकर सकुचाकर पृथ्वी पर मस्तक नवाकर वे श्रेष्ठ दूत हाथ जोड़कर बोले- हे स्वामी! आपका आदर के साथ पूछना, यही हे गोसाईं! कुशल का कारण हो गया ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, they grew shy, bowed their heads to the ground, and spoke with joined hands. "Your respectful inquiry itself, my lord, has become the reason for our welfare, O gracious one."
essence: Respectful concern can itself become comfort.
simple_meaning: The messengers bow respectfully and answer that Ram's own concern for their well-being has already brought them comfort.
insight: It shows how courtesy itself can become a form of care, turning formal speech into relief.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room already tense, and someone asks about your well-being before the agenda begins. That single respectful question softens everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाहिं त कोसलनाथ कें साथ कुसल गइ नाथ। मिथिला अवध बिसेष तें जगु सब भयउ अनाथ ॥
translation: नहीं तो हे नाथ! कुशल-क्षेम तो सब कोसलनाथ दशरथजी के साथ ही चली गई। (उनके चले जाने से) यों तो सारा जगत ही अनाथ (स्वामी के बिना असहाय) हो गया, किन्तु मिथिला और अवध तो विशेष रूप से अनाथ हो गया ॥
english_translation: No, with the lord of Kosala gone, all well-being has left with him. With him gone, the world is orphaned, and Mithila and Ayodhya are especially bereft.
essence: When the protector falls, everyone feels unmoored.
simple_meaning: Dasharath's death is felt not just as one family's loss, but as a loss of protection for the whole world, especially Mithila and Ayodhya.
insight: It shifts the mind from private loss to the shared emptiness created when a steady presence disappears.
modern_relevance: A family loses the person everyone quietly relied on to hold things together. Suddenly the house feels different, the phone calls feel heavier, and even ordinary routines seem unprotected.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोसलपति गति सुनि जनकौरा। भे सब लोक सोकबस बौरा॥ जेहिं देखे तेहि समय बिदेहू। नामु सत्य अस लाग न केहू ॥
translation: अयोध्यानाथ की गति (दशरथजी का मरण) सुनकर जनकपुर वासी सभी लोग शोकवश बावले हो गए (सुध-बुध भूल गए)। उस समय जिन्होंने विदेह को (शोकमग्न) देखा, उनमें से किसी को ऐसा न लगा कि उनका विदेह (देहाभिमानरहित) नाम सत्य है! (क्योंकि देहभिमान से शून्य पुरुष को शोक कैसा?) ॥
