english_translation: Receiving the order from Ram's guru, Janak went to the camp and came to see Sita. Janak embraced Janaki to his heart as a sacred guest of his pure love and life.
essence: Pure love can hold a farewell without trying to stop it.
simple_meaning: Janak comes to see Sita and embraces her with deep love, treating her as a sacred guest of his life.
insight: It shows how affection can be expressed as reverent embrace, not possessiveness.
modern_relevance: You hug someone at the airport and both of you know this goodbye is heavier than words. Love does not always speak; sometimes it simply holds on for one more breath.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उर उमगेउ अंबुधि अनुरागू। भयउ भूप मनु मनहुँ पयागू॥ सिय सनेह बटु बाढ़त जोहा। ता पर राम पेम सिसु सोहा ॥
translation: उनके हृदय में (वात्सल्य) प्रेम का समुद्र उमड़ पड़ा। राजा का मन मानो प्रयाग हो गया। उस समुद्र के अंदर उन्होंने (आदि शक्ति) सीताजी के (अलौकिक) स्नेह रूपी अक्षयवट को बढ़ते हुए देखा। उस (सीताजी के प्रेम रूपी वट) पर श्री रामजी का प्रेम रूपी बालक (बाल रूप धारी भगवान) सुशोभित हो रहा है ॥
english_translation: Love rose like an ocean in Janaka's heart. The king's mind became like Prayag. Within that ocean, he saw Sita's unfading love growing like a banyan tree, and on that love, Ram's childlike love shone beautifully.
essence: Love can make the heart feel vast enough to hold the sacred.
simple_meaning: Janaka's heart overflows with love as he sees Sita's deep affection for Ram and Ram's tender love for Sita.
insight: It shifts attention from outward reunion to the inner power that makes reunion sacred.
modern_relevance: You watch two people meet after months apart, and the room changes. What you feel isn't drama — it's the quiet shock of seeing love that has survived distance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चिरजीवी मुनि ग्यान बिकल जनु। बूड़त लहेउ बाल अवलंबनु॥ मोह मगन मति नहिं बिदेह की। महिमा सिय रघुबर सनेह की ॥
translation: जनकजी का ज्ञान रूपी चिरंजीवी (मार्कण्डेय) मुनि व्याकुल होकर डूबते-डूबते मानो उस श्री राम प्रेम रूपी बालक का सहारा पाकर बच गया। वस्तुतः (ज्ञानिशिरोमणि) विदेहराज की बुद्धि मोह में मग्न नहीं है। यह तो श्री सीता-रामजी के प्रेम की महिमा है (जिसने उन जैसे महान ज्ञानी के ज्ञान को भी विकल कर दिया) ॥
english_translation: The sage of endless life, though wise, was as if drowning and found a childlike support. Janaka's mind was not lost in delusion; this was the greatness of Sita and Raghubar's love.
essence: Love can move even the wisest mind beyond its usual control.
simple_meaning: Even Janaka, a great sage-king, is overwhelmed by Sita and Ram's love. His confusion is not ignorance; it is the force of devotion.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating emotional overwhelm as weakness to seeing it as devotion's power.
modern_relevance: You thought you had yourself together, then one message from someone you love undid you completely. That collapse may not be failure; it may be the depth of what truly matters.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिय पितु मातु सनेह बस बिकल न सकी सँभारि। धरनिसुताँ धीरजु धरेउ समउ सुधरमु बिचारि ॥
translation: पिता-माता के प्रेम के मारे सीताजी ऐसी विकल हो गईं कि अपने को सँभाल न सकीं। (परन्तु परम धैर्यवती) पृथ्वी की कन्या सीताजी ने समय और सुंदर धर्म का विचार कर धैर्य धारण किया ॥
english_translation: Overcome by love for her father and mother, Sita could not steady herself. Yet the daughter of the earth held her patience, considering the time and the demands of right conduct.
essence: Love can shake you without taking away your steadiness.
simple_meaning: Sita is overwhelmed by love for her parents, but she regains herself by choosing patience and right conduct.
insight: It teaches emotional steadiness: feel the wave fully, then choose the response that fits the moment.
modern_relevance: You are crying in the car after a family goodbye, and your chest feels too full to breathe. Even then, you can gather yourself and do what is right.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तापस बेष जनक सिय देखी। भयउ पेमु परितोषु बिसेषी॥ पुत्रि पबित्र किए कुल दोऊ। सुजस धवल जगु कह सबु कोऊ ॥
translation: सीताजी को तपस्विनी वेष में देखकर जनकजी को विशेष प्रेम और संतोष हुआ। (उन्होंने कहा-) बेटी! तूने दोनों कुल पवित्र कर दिए। तेरे निर्मल यश से सारा जगत उज्ज्वल हो रहा है, ऐसा सब कोई कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing Sita in the dress of an ascetic, Janaka felt special love and deep satisfaction. "Daughter, you have purified both families. Your spotless fame brightens the whole world," everyone says.
essence: True greatness makes both your home and the world brighter.
simple_meaning: Janaka sees Sita in ascetic dress and feels deep joy. He praises her for bringing honor to both families and for making her reputation pure and radiant.
insight: It shifts attention from outward appearance to the quiet power of character and family honor.
modern_relevance: You watch your daughter walk into a room in simple clothes, calm and unshowy, and feel something in you settle. Her character is speaking louder than any display ever could.
speaker: Janaka

verse_text: जिति सुरसरि कीरति सरि तोरी। गवनु कीन्ह बिधि अंड करोरी॥ गंग अवनि थल तीनि बड़ेरे। एहिं किए साधु समाज घनेरे ॥
translation: तेरी कीर्ति रूपी नदी देवनदी गंगाजी को भी जीतकर (जो एक ही ब्रह्माण्ड में बहती है) करोड़ों ब्रह्माण्डों में बह चली है। गंगाजी ने तो पृथ्वी पर तीन ही स्थानों (हरिद्वार, प्रयागराज और गंगासागर) को बड़ा (तीर्थ) बनाया है। पर तेरी इस कीर्ति नदी ने तो अनेकों संत समाज रूपी तीर्थ स्थान बना दिए हैं ॥
english_translation: Your fame has crossed even the Ganga and spread through countless worlds. The Ganga makes only three great holy places on earth, but your fame has made many communities of saints into holy places.
essence: A pure life makes whole communities feel sacred.
simple_meaning: Your praise has spread beyond ordinary limits and made many gatherings of holy people sacred. Even the Ganga seems smaller beside the reach of your fame.
insight: It shifts attention from personal achievement to the quiet power of a life that elevates everyone around it.
modern_relevance: You show up for a grieving friend, and the room feels calmer the moment you enter. No speech, no spotlight — just a steady way of being that changes the whole atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पितु कह सत्य सनेहँ सुबानी। सीय सकुच महुँ मनहुँ समानी॥ पुनि पितु मातु लीन्हि उर लाई। सिख आसिष हित दीन्हि सुहाई ॥
translation: पिता जनकजी ने तो स्नेह से सच्ची सुंदर वाणी कही, परन्तु अपनी बड़ाई सुनकर सीताजी मानो संकोच में समा गईं। पिता-माता ने उन्हें फिर हृदय से लगा लिया और हितभरी सुंदर सीख और आशीष दिया ॥
english_translation: Janak spoke true and lovingly; Sita sank into modest silence. Then her parents drew her close again and gave her loving counsel and blessings.
essence: True affection praises you without making you feel exposed.
simple_meaning: Janak praises Sita with loving words, but she grows shy. Her parents embrace her again and bless her with kind advice.
insight: It shows how praise, when rooted in love, can still leave room for humility and care.
modern_relevance: Your parent says something proud about you in front of relatives, and you suddenly want the floor to open. That mix of love, embarrassment, and reassurance feels exactly like this moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहति न सीय सकुचि मन माहीं। इहाँ बसब रजनीं भल नाहीं॥ लखि रुख रानि जनायउ राऊ। हृदयँ सराहत सीलु सुभाऊ ॥
translation: सीताजी कुछ कहती नहीं हैं, परन्तु सकुचा रही हैं कि रात में (सासुओं की सेवा छोड़कर) यहाँ रहना अच्छा नहीं है। रानी सुनयनाजी ने जानकीजी का रुख देखकर (उनके मन की बात समझकर) राजा जनकजी को जना दिया। तब दोनों अपने हृदयों में सीताजी के शील और स्वभाव की सराहना करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Sita says nothing, but in her heart she feels shy: staying here at night is not right. Seeing her mood, Queen Sunaina told King Janaka. Then both of them praised Sita's modesty and gentle nature in their hearts.
essence: True refinement is felt before it is spoken.
simple_meaning: Sita stays quiet, but her hesitation is clear. Sunaina understands her feeling and tells Janaka, and both parents admire Sita's modest, gracious nature.
insight: It trains you to notice unspoken discomfort and honor it with grace.
modern_relevance: You sit at a dinner table where everyone is urging you to stay longer, but your body says it's time to leave. Someone who loves you notices the hesitation without making it awkward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बार बार मिलि भेंटि सिय बिदा कीन्हि सनमानि। कही समय सिर भरत गति रानि सुबानि सयानि ॥
translation: राजा-रानी ने बार-बार मिलकर और हृदय से लगाकर तथा सम्मान करके सीताजी को विदा किया। चतुर रानी ने समय पाकर राजा से सुंदर वाणी में भरतजी की दशा का वर्णन किया ॥
english_translation: The king and queen repeatedly met Sita, embraced her, and sent her off with honour. Then the wise queen spoke at the right time, beautifully describing Bharata's condition to the king.
essence: Kindness and timing can soften even a painful parting.
simple_meaning: Sita is sent away with love and respect, and Queen Sunaina then speaks wisely about Bharata's situation.
insight: It shows how respect and good timing can carry a difficult message without harshness.
modern_relevance: You wait until the room is calm, then say the hard thing kindly. The timing of a truth can change everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि भूपाल भरत ब्यवहारू। सोन सुगंध सुधा ससि सारू॥ मूदे सजन नयन पुलके तन। सुजसु सराहन लगे मुदित मन ॥
translation: सोने में सुगंध और (समुद्र से निकली हुई) सुधा में चन्द्रमा के सार अमृत के समान भरतजी का व्यवहार सुनकर राजा ने (प्रेम विह्वल होकर) अपने (प्रेमाश्रुओं के) जल से भरे नेत्रों को मूँद लिया (वे भरतजी के प्रेम में मानो ध्यानस्थ हो गए)। वे शरीर से पुलकित हो गए और मन में आनंदित होकर भरतजी के सुंदर यश की सराहना करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Hearing of Bharat's conduct, the king's heart filled with wonder. Like fragrance in gold and nectar in the moon, Bharat's character seemed even more precious. His eyes closed in love, his body thrilled, and his mind delighted as he praised Bharat's good fame.
essence: Bharat's character is so rare it feels like treasure inside treasure.
simple_meaning: The king hears about Bharat's character and is overwhelmed with joy and admiration. Bharat's conduct seems as rare and precious as fragrance in gold or nectar in the moon.
insight: It shifts attention from what people possess to the quality of how they live.
modern_relevance: You hear how someone gave up comfort to keep a promise, and suddenly your own complaints feel small. Real character can silence a room without raising its voice.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सावधान सुनु सुमुखि सुलोचनि। भरत कथा भव बंध बिमोचनि॥ धरम राजनय ब्रह्मबिचारू। इहाँ जथामति मोर प्रचारू ॥
translation: (वे बोले-) हे सुमुखि! हे सुनयनी! सावधान होकर सुनो। भरतजी की कथा संसार के बंधन से छुड़ाने वाली है। धर्म, राजनीति और ब्रह्मविचार- इन तीनों विषयों में अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार मेरी (थोड़ी-बहुत) गति है (अर्थात इनके संबंध में मैं कुछ जानता हूँ) ॥
english_translation: (He said:) O graceful and bright-eyed one, listen carefully. The story of Bharat frees you from the bonds of the world. In dharma, politics, and spiritual reflection, I have some understanding according to my own measure.
essence: Bharat's story is meant to free you, not just inform you.
simple_meaning: Bharat's story is presented as deeply freeing. The speaker says he understands enough about duty, leadership, and spiritual reflection to begin telling it.
insight: It frames Bharat's life as a teaching story, not just a family episode, and invites the listener into a freer way of seeing duty and renunciation.
modern_relevance: You hear a friend begin a story by saying, 'This one changed me.' Before the details even start, you feel that something in you may need to shift too.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सो मति मोरि भरत महिमाही। कहै काह छलि छुअति न छाँही॥ बिधि गनपति अहिपति सिव सारद। कबि कोबिद बुध बुद्धि बिसारद ॥
translation: वह (धर्म, राजनीति और ब्रह्मज्ञान में प्रवेश रखने वाली) मेरी बुद्धि भरतजी की महिमा का वर्णन तो क्या करे, छल करके भी उसकी छाया तक को नहीं छू पाती! ब्रह्माजी, गणेशजी, शेषजी, महादेवजी, सरस्वतीजी, कवि, ज्ञानी, पण्डित और बुद्धिमान- ॥
english_translation: My mind can never describe Bharat's greatness. Even in deceit, it cannot touch even his shadow. Brahma, Ganesha, Shesha, Shiva, Saraswati, poets, sages, scholars, and the wise...
essence: Bharat's greatness is so pure that even thought falls short.
simple_meaning: Bharat's greatness is beyond ordinary understanding. Even the speaker's own mind cannot fully describe it, and only the greatest beings and wisest minds can begin to approach it.
insight: It shifts you from measuring worth by cleverness to recognising the depth of lived devotion.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who quietly keeps a promise no one else would notice. When you try to explain why that loyalty moves you, words feel too small. Bharat's example has that kind of weight.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत चरित कीरति करतूती। धरम सील गुन बिमल बिभूती॥ समुझत सुनत सुखद सब काहू। सुचि सुरसरि रुचि निदर सुधाहू ॥
translation: सब किसी को भरतजी के चरित्र, कीर्ति, करनी, धर्म, शील, गुण और निर्मल ऐश्वर्य समझने में और सुनने में सुख देने वाले हैं और पवित्रता में गंगाजी का तथा स्वाद (मधुरता) में अमृत का भी तिरस्कार करने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: Bharat’s character, fame, deeds, righteousness, restraint, virtues, and spotless excellence are pleasing to understand and hear. In purity, they surpass the Ganges; in sweetness, they outshine even nectar.
essence: Bharat’s virtue is so pure it becomes its own reward.
simple_meaning: Bharat’s character is so noble that hearing about him brings joy. His purity and virtue are described as greater than the Ganges and even sweeter than nectar.
insight: It shifts attention from status to character, showing that true excellence is felt in the way a life affects others.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose integrity needs no announcement: they show up, keep faith, and leave a room calmer. Later, people speak of them with the same quiet admiration this verse gives Bharat.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निरवधि गुन निरुपम पुरुषु भरतु भरत सम जानि। कहिअ सुमेरु कि सेर सम कबिकुल मति सकुचानि ॥
translation: भरतजी असीम गुण सम्पन्न और उपमारहित पुरुष हैं। भरतजी के समान बस, भरतजी ही हैं, ऐसा जानो। सुमेरु पर्वत को क्या सेर के बराबर कह सकते हैं? इसलिए (उन्हें किसी पुरुष के साथ उपमा देने में) कवि समाज की बुद्धि भी सकुचा गई! ॥
english_translation: Bharat is a person of limitless virtues, beyond comparison. Bharat can only be known as Bharat himself. Can Mount Sumeru be measured against a seer? Even the minds of poets shrink back from making such a comparison.
essence: True greatness cannot be measured by comparison.
simple_meaning: Bharat's virtues are so vast that no comparison fits him. Even poets feel hesitant trying to measure him against anyone else.
insight: It shifts the mind away from comparison and toward reverence for character that cannot be reduced to a scale.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who quietly carries more grace than any title can show. The urge to rank them, label them, or compare them feels clumsy and inadequate.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अगम सबहि बरनत बरबरनी। जिमि जलहीन मीन गमु धरनी॥ भरत अमित महिमा सुनु रानी। जानहिं रामु न सकहिं बखानी ॥
translation: हे श्रेष्ठ वर्णवाली! भरतजी की महिमा का वर्णन करना सभी के लिए वैसे ही अगम है जैसे जलरहित पृथ्वी पर मछली का चलना। हे रानी! सुनो, भरतजी की अपरिमित महिमा को एक श्री रामचन्द्रजी ही जानते हैं, किन्तु वे भी उसका वर्णन नहीं कर सकते ॥
english_translation: O noble lady, the greatness of Bharat is beyond description, like a fish on dry land. O queen, only Ram knows Bharat's limitless glory, yet even Ram cannot fully describe it.
essence: Bharat's greatness is so deep that even praise cannot contain it.
simple_meaning: Bharat's greatness is beyond ordinary description. Even Ram alone fully knows it, yet its full measure cannot be put into words.
insight: It shifts attention from public reputation to the hidden depth of character that only love can truly know.
modern_relevance: You try to explain why a certain friend stayed loyal when everything would have rewarded betrayal. The explanation feels too small. Some people are larger than the language you have for them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बरनि सप्रेम भरत अनुभाऊ। तिय जिय की रुचि लखि कह राऊ॥ बहुरहिं लखनु भरतु बन जाहीं। सब कर भल सब के मन माहीं ॥
translation: इस प्रकार प्रेमपूर्वक भरतजी के प्रभाव का वर्णन करके, फिर पत्नी के मन की रुचि जानकर राजा ने कहा- लक्ष्मणजी लौट जाएँ और भरतजी वन को जाएँ, इसमें सभी का भला है और यही सबके मन में है ॥
english_translation: After lovingly describing Bharat's greatness, the king saw his wife's wish and said, 'Let Lakshman return and let Bharat go to the forest; that would be best for everyone, and that is what everyone wants in their heart.'
essence: The king tries to heal a wound by naming the wish already living in the family.
simple_meaning: The king, sensing his wife's feelings, says Lakshman should return and Bharat should go to the forest. He believes this would be best for everyone.
insight: It shows how public decisions are often shaped by hidden feelings in the room.
modern_relevance: You are in a tense family group chat, trying to say the one thing that might calm everyone down. The real issue is not logic — it's reading what each person is carrying.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देबि परन्तु भरत रघुबर की। प्रीति प्रतीति जाइ नहिं तरकी॥ भरतु अवधि सनेह ममता की। जद्यपि रामु सीम समता की ॥
translation: परन्तु हे देवि! भरतजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी का प्रेम और एक-दूसरे पर विश्वास, बुद्धि और विचार की सीमा में नहीं आ सकता। यद्यपि श्री रामचन्द्रजी समता की सीमा हैं, तथापि भरतजी प्रेम और ममता की सीमा हैं ॥
english_translation: O goddess, Bharata's love for Raghubara and their mutual trust cannot be measured by reason or thought. Though Ram is the limit of perfect equality, Bharata is the limit of love and affection.
essence: True devotion cannot be measured, only lived.
simple_meaning: Bharata's love and trust in Ram cannot be measured by logic. Ram remains perfectly even-hearted, while Bharata becomes the limit of loving devotion.
insight: It shifts attention from proving love to embodying it. The bond becomes something lived, not argued.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone who cannot fully explain why they matter so much. The relationship stops being about logic and becomes a quiet proof of loyalty.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: परमारथ स्वारथ सुख सारे। भरत न सपनेहुँ मनहुँ निहारे॥ साधन सिद्धि राम पग नेहू। मोहि लखि परत भरत मत एहू ॥
translation: (श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्रति अनन्य प्रेम को छोड़कर) भरतजी ने समस्त परमार्थ, स्वार्थ और सुखों की ओर स्वप्न में भी मन से भी नहीं ताका है। श्री रामजी के चरणों का प्रेम ही उनका साधन है और वही सिद्धि है। मुझे तो भरतजी का बस, यही एक मात्र सिद्धांत जान पड़ता है ॥
english_translation: Bharat has never even dreamed of seeking worldly gain, selfish gain, or pleasure. Love for Ram's feet is his means and his fulfillment. In my view, that is Bharat's only principle.
essence: Love for Ram becomes both the path and the reward.
simple_meaning: Bharat has no interest in personal gain or pleasure. Loving Ram is both his path and his fulfillment.
insight: It shifts your priorities from acquisition to wholehearted devotion.
modern_relevance: You turn down the promotion, the applause, and the shortcut because they would pull you away from what you love. Bharat shows what it looks like when devotion is more satisfying than winning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भोरेहुँ भरत न पेलिहहिं मनसहुँ राम रजाइ। करिअ न सोचु सनेह बस कहेउ भूप बिलखाइ ॥
translation: राजा ने बिलखकर (प्रेम से गद्गद होकर) कहा- भरतजी भूलकर भी श्री रामचन्द्रजी की आज्ञा को मन से भी नहीं टालेंगे। अतः स्नेह के वश होकर चिंता नहीं करनी चाहिए ॥
english_translation: The king, overcome with emotion, said, "Bharat will not even in the slightest disobey Ram's command. Do not worry out of love."
essence: Love that is true does not need suspicion.
simple_meaning: Dasharath says Bharat will never even mentally go against Ram's command, so no one should worry out of affection.
insight: It shifts the mind from anxious doubt to steady trust in another's devotion.
modern_relevance: You keep replaying the text, wondering whether your friend will stay loyal or your partner will understand. This verse softens that fear: true love does not rush to suspicion.
speaker: Dasharath

verse_text: राम भरत गुन गनत सप्रीती। निसि दंपतिहि पलक सम बीती॥ राज समाज प्रात जुग जागे। न्हाइ न्हाइ सुर पूजन लागे ॥
translation: श्री रामजी और भरतजी के गुणों की प्रेमपूर्वक गणना करते (कहते-सुनते) पति-पत्नी को रात पलक के समान बीत गई। प्रातःकाल दोनों राजसमाज जागे और नहा-नहाकर देवताओं की पूजा करने लगे ॥
english_translation: As Ram and Bharat’s virtues were lovingly counted, the night passed like a blink for the couple. At dawn, the royal assembly awoke, bathed, and began worshipping the radiant beings.
essence: Love for Ram and Bharat makes sorrow feel brief.
simple_meaning: Ram and Bharat’s qualities are so dear that talking about them makes the night pass quickly. By morning, everyone is awake, bathed, and ready to worship.
insight: It shows how shared remembrance softens grief and prepares the mind for right action.
modern_relevance: You stay up late with family, remembering the person everyone misses most. Morning comes, and even the silence feels gentler because love was spoken aloud.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गे नहाइ गुर पहिं रघुराई। बंदि चरन बोले रुख पाई॥ नाथ भरतु पुरजन महतारी। सोक बिकल बनबास दुखारी ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी स्नान करके गुरु वशिष्ठजी के पास गए और चरणों की वंदना करके उनका रुख पाकर बोले- हे नाथ! भरत, अवधपुर वासी तथा माताएँ, सब शोक से व्याकुल और वनवास से दुःखी हैं ॥
english_translation: After bathing, Rama went to Guru Vashishtha. Bowing at his feet, he spoke after seeing his mood: "Lord, Bharata, the people of Ayodhya, and the mothers are all shaken with grief and pained by exile."
essence: Before asking for help, Rama names everyone’s suffering.
simple_meaning: Rama bows to his teacher and reports that Bharata, the people of Ayodhya, and the mothers are all suffering from grief and exile.
insight: It shifts you from private emotion to responsible speech, so the real situation can be addressed clearly.
modern_relevance: You finally sit down with the person who can help, after a night of family tension. Before asking for anything, you name who is hurting and why.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सहित समाज राउ मिथिलेसू। बहुत दिवस भए सहत कलेसू॥ उचित होइ सोइ कीजिअ नाथा। हित सबही कर रौरें हाथा ॥
translation: मिथिलापति राजा जनकजी को भी समाज सहित क्लेश सहते बहुत दिन हो गए, इसलिए हे नाथ! जो उचित हो वही कीजिए। आप ही के हाथ सभी का हित है ॥
english_translation: Even King Janaka of Mithila, with his whole assembly, has endured sorrow for many days. So, O Lord, do what is right. The welfare of everyone rests in your hands.
essence: What is right becomes larger when many lives depend on it.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks Ram to do what is proper, saying that the suffering of Janaka and the whole gathering has gone on long enough and that everyone's welfare depends on Ram.
insight: It shifts the mind from personal hesitation to responsibility for the wider good.
modern_relevance: A family has been living in silence after one person's decision shook everyone. At last, someone says the hard thing: stop avoiding it, do what's right, and let the whole house breathe again.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: अस कहि अति सकुचे रघुराऊ। मुनि पुल के लखि सीलु सुभाऊ॥ तुम्ह बिनु राम सकल सुख साजा। नरक सरिस दुहु राज समाजा ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर श्री रघुनाथजी अत्यन्त ही सकुचा गए। उनका शील स्वभाव देखकर (प्रेम और आनंद से) मुनि वशिष्ठजी पुलकित हो गए। (उन्होंने खुलकर कहा-) हे राम! तुम्हारे बिना (घर-बार आदि) सम्पूर्ण सुखों के साज दोनों राजसमाजों को नरक के समान हैं ॥
english_translation: Saying this, Raghunath grew very shy. Seeing his gentle nature, the sage was filled with delight. He said openly: "Without you, Ram, all the comforts of home are like hell to both royal households."
essence: Without Ram, comfort itself becomes misery.
simple_meaning: Ram feels shy after speaking humbly. Vashistha sees his gentle nature and says that without Ram, even royal comfort feels unbearable.
insight: It shifts value from outer comfort to the living presence that makes life feel whole.
modern_relevance: You can have the perfect apartment, the nicest furniture, and a full calendar — and still feel empty if the one person who matters is missing.
speaker: Vashistha

verse_text: प्रान-प्रान के जीव के जिव सुख के सुख राम। तुम्ह तजि तात सोहात गृह जिन्हहि तिन्हहि बिधि बाम ॥
translation: हे राम! तुम प्राणों के भी प्राण, आत्मा के भी आत्मा और सुख के भी सुख हो। हे तात! तुम्हें छोड़कर जिन्हें घर सुहाता है, उन्हे विधाता विपरीत है ॥
english_translation: O Ram, you are the life within life, the joy within joy. Father, those who find comfort in a home without you are set against the right order of things.
essence: Without Ram, even a home becomes out of tune.
simple_meaning: Ram is the deepest source of life and joy. A home feels empty and out of order when he is absent.
insight: It shifts attention from outer comfort to the presence that gives life its meaning.
modern_relevance: You sit in a beautiful apartment after a breakup and nothing feels settled. The furniture is fine, the room is fine, but the warmth is gone. This verse names that ache exactly.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सो सुखु करमु धरमु जरि जाऊ। जहँ न राम पद पंकज भाऊ॥ जोगु कुजोगु ग्यानु अग्यानू। जहँ नहिं राम प्रेम परधानू ॥
translation: जहाँ श्री राम के चरण कमलों में प्रेम नहीं है, वह सुख, कर्म और धर्म जल जाए, जिसमें श्री राम प्रेम की प्रधानता नहीं है, वह योग कुयोग है और वह ज्ञान अज्ञान है ॥
english_translation: Any happiness, action, or duty burns away where love for Ram's lotus feet is absent. Without Ram as the center, yoga becomes misguidance and wisdom becomes ignorance.
essence: Without love for Ram, even virtue and wisdom lose their value.
simple_meaning: Love for Ram is what gives value to happiness, action, duty, yoga, and wisdom. Without that love, even good things lose their worth.
insight: It shifts attention from outer success to the devotion that gives all action meaning.
modern_relevance: You can build the perfect career, follow every wellness rule, and still feel empty if your heart has no center. This verse asks what your life is actually arranged around.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तुम्ह बिनु दुखी सुखी तुम्ह तेहीं। तुम्ह जानहु जिय जो जेहि केहीं॥ राउर आयसु सिर सबही कें। बिदित कृपालहि गति सब नीकें ॥
translation: तुम्हारे बिना ही सब दुःखी हैं और जो सुखी हैं वे तुम्हीं से सुखी हैं। जिस किसी के जी में जो कुछ है तुम सब जानते हो। आपकी आज्ञा सभी के सिर पर है। कृपालु (आप) को सभी की स्थिति अच्छी तरह मालूम है॥2
english_translation: You alone are the source of sorrow and joy. You know what lives in every heart. Your command rests on every head, and the compassionate one knows every state perfectly.
essence: The one who governs your life already knows your heart.
simple_meaning: Ram is the source of both sorrow and joy, and he knows every heart completely. Everyone stands under his authority, and nothing about anyone's condition is hidden from him.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to trust in being known and guided.
modern_relevance: You sit beside someone who cannot say what hurts, yet you already feel the shape of it. This verse speaks to the relief of being understood before you can explain yourself.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आपु आश्रमहि धारिअ पाऊ। भयउ सनेह सिथिल मुनिराऊ॥ करि प्रनामु तब रामु सिधाए। रिषि धरि धीर जनक पहिं आए ॥
translation: अतः आप आश्रम को पधारिए। इतना कह मुनिराज स्नेह से शिथिल हो गए। तब श्री रामजी प्रणाम करके चले गए और ऋषि वशिष्ठजी धीरज धरकर जनकजी के पास आए ॥
english_translation: 'Please return to your hermitage,' he said. The sage-king was then softened by affection. After bowing, Ram departed, and the sage gathered his composure and came to Janak.
essence: Affection can soften the heart without breaking dignity.
simple_meaning: The sage asks Ram to return to his hermitage. Ram bows and leaves, and the sage regains composure before going to Janak.
insight: It shows how reverence and composure can coexist even in emotional transitions.
modern_relevance: You finish a hard conversation, bow your head, and walk out before your emotions spill over. The moment is tender, but the next duty still waits.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: राम बचन गुरु नृपहि सुनाए। सील सनेह सुभायँ सुहाए॥ महाराज अब कीजिअ सोई। सब कर धरम सहित हित होई ॥
translation: गुरुजी ने श्री रामचन्द्रजी के शील और स्नेह से युक्त स्वभाव से ही सुंदर वचन राजा जनकजी को सुनाए (और कहा-) हे महाराज! अब वही कीजिए, जिसमें सबका धर्म सहित हित हो ॥
english_translation: The guru conveyed Ram's words to the king, words shaped by grace and loving nature: "Great king, now do what brings dharma-filled good to everyone."
essence: The best choice is the one that protects dharma for everyone.
simple_meaning: Ram's message is that the king should choose the course of action that is righteous and beneficial for everyone.
insight: It shifts decision-making from personal preference to the wider good of everyone involved.
modern_relevance: A family meeting is stuck because every option benefits one person and hurts another. The wisest voice in the room asks for the choice that leaves the whole group better, not just the loudest person.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ग्यान निधान सुजान सुचि धरम धीर नरपाल। तुम्ह बिनु असमंजस समन को समरथ एहि काल ॥
translation: हे राजन् ! तुम ज्ञान के भंडार, सुजान, पवित्र और धर्म में धीर हो। इस समय तुम्हारे बिना इस दुविधा को दूर करने में और कौन समर्थ है? ॥
english_translation: O king, you are a storehouse of wisdom, discerning, pure, and steadfast in dharma. Without you, who is capable of ending this confusion at this time?
essence: Steady wisdom becomes the authority that ends confusion.
simple_meaning: Janak is praised as wise, pure, and steady in dharma, the one best able to resolve the present confusion.
insight: It shifts attention from noise and hesitation to the person whose clarity can resolve the moment.
modern_relevance: A room full of people is stuck, everyone talking at once, and the one person who stays calm finally names the next step. That is the kind of steadiness this verse honours.
speaker: Vasishta

verse_text: सुनि मुनि बचन जनक अनुरागे। लखि गति ग्यानु बिरागु बिरागे॥ सिथिल सनेहँ गुनत मन माहीं। आए इहाँ कीन्ह भल नाहीं ॥
translation: मुनि वशिष्ठजी के वचन सुनकर जनकजी प्रेम में मग्न हो गए। उनकी दशा देखकर ज्ञान और वैराग्य को भी वैराग्य हो गया (अर्थात उनके ज्ञान-वैराग्य छूट से गए)। वे प्रेम से शिथिल हो गए और मन में विचार करने लगे कि हम यहाँ आए, यह अच्छा नहीं किया ॥
english_translation: Hearing the sage's words, Janaka was filled with love. Seeing his state, even knowledge and detachment seemed to lose their grip. Softened by affection, he thought in his heart, 'Coming here was not a good choice.'
essence: Love can melt the very detachment that once seemed strongest.
simple_meaning: Janaka hears the sage and becomes tender with love. His usual detachment weakens, and he feels that coming there was a mistake.
insight: It shows how love can dissolve even a carefully held stance of detachment.
modern_relevance: You sit in a meeting trying to stay composed, but one sentence from someone you respect changes everything. Your usual distance drops, and the heart speaks first.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामहि रायँ कहेउ बन जाना। कीन्ह आपु प्रिय प्रेम प्रवाना॥ हम अब बन तें बनहि पठाई। प्रमुदित फिरब बिबेक बड़ाई ॥
translation: राजा दशरथजी ने श्री रामजी को वन जाने के लिए कहा और स्वयं अपने प्रिय के प्रेम को प्रमाणित (सच्चा) कर दिया (प्रिय वियोग में प्राण त्याग दिए), परन्तु हम अब इन्हें वन से (और गहन) वन को भेजकर अपने विवेक की बड़ाई में आनन्दित होते हुए लौटेंगे (कि हमें जरा भी मोह नहीं है, हम श्री रामजी को वन में छोड़कर चले आए, दशरथजी की तरह मरे नहीं!) ॥
english_translation: King Dasharatha told Rama to go to the forest and made his own love for his beloved fully real. We will now send him from the forest into deeper forest and return, proud of our wisdom, as if we feel no attachment at all.
essence: Love is tested by how much it can release without becoming false.
simple_meaning: True love is shown when you can release someone you cherish without pretending it does not hurt.
insight: It shifts the mind from proving control to honoring attachment honestly.
modern_relevance: You wave goodbye at the station after helping someone move cities, then force a smile and call it maturity. The verse cuts through that pose and asks whether your detachment is real or just performance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तापस मुनि महिसुर सुनि देखी। भए प्रेम बस बिकल बिसेषी॥ समउ समुझि धरि धीरजु राजा। चले भरत पहिं सहित समाजा ॥
translation: तपस्वी, मुनि और ब्राह्मण यह सब सुन और देखकर प्रेमवश बहुत ही व्याकुल हो गए। समय का विचार करके राजा जनकजी धीरज धरकर समाज सहित भरतजी के पास चले ॥
english_translation: Seeing and hearing this, the ascetics, sages, and priests were overwhelmed by love. Understanding the moment, King Janak steadied himself and went with his whole company to Bharata.
essence: Love can shake you; steadiness lets you respond well.
simple_meaning: The holy men are moved to deep emotion, and Janak keeps his composure before going to Bharata with his attendants.
insight: It teaches you to let feeling move you without letting it scatter your conduct.
modern_relevance: You hear bad news in a crowded room and feel your chest tighten, but you still stand up, smooth your face, and go meet the person who needs you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत आइ आगें भइ लीन्हे। अवसर सरिस सुआसन दीन्हे॥ तात भरत कह तेरहुति राऊ। तुम्हहि बिदित रघुबीर सुभाऊ ॥
translation: भरतजी ने आकर उन्हें आगे होकर लिया (सामने आकर उनका स्वागत किया) और समयानुकूल अच्छे आसन दिए। तिरहुतराज जनकजी कहने लगे- हे तात भरत! तुमको श्री रामजी का स्वभाव मालूम ही है ॥
english_translation: Bharat came forward and welcomed them with fitting seats. King Janaka said, “Dear Bharat, you already know the nature of Raghuvir.”
essence: Courtesy opens the way for truth already known.
simple_meaning: Bharat receives the guests respectfully, and Janaka reminds him that Ram’s nature is already well known.
insight: It shows how dignity and tenderness can steady a difficult gathering before deeper words are spoken.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is carrying grief, and you still make space, offer a chair, and speak gently. Small courtesy can hold a heavy moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम सत्यब्रत धरम रत सब कर सीलु स्नेहु। संकट सहत सकोच बस कहिअ जो आयसु देहु ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी सत्यव्रती और धर्मपरायण हैं, सबका शील और स्नेह रखने वाले हैं, इसीलिए वे संकोचवश संकट सह रहे हैं, अब तुम जो आज्ञा दो, वह उनसे कही जाए ॥
english_translation: Rama is true to his vow and devoted to dharma, full of gentleness and affection for everyone. He is bearing this hardship out of modesty, so please give the command that should be conveyed to him.
essence: True duty stays gentle even under strain.
simple_meaning: Ram stays true to his vows, lives by dharma, and treats everyone with kindness. Even while suffering, he remains humble and waits for the right instruction.
insight: It teaches you to see duty and tenderness as companions, not opposites.
modern_relevance: You’re the one who keeps showing up, even when the job is painful and no one sees the strain. The hardest part is still staying kind while you carry it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि तन पुलकि नयन भरि बारी। बोले भरतु धीर धरि भारी॥ प्रभु प्रिय पूज्य पिता सम आपू। कुलगुरु सम हित माय न बापू ॥
translation: भरतजी यह सुनकर पुलकित शरीर हो नेत्रों में जल भरकर बड़ा भारी धीरज धरकर बोले- हे प्रभो! आप हमारे पिता के समान प्रिय और पूज्य हैं और कुल गुरु श्री वशिष्ठजी के समान हितैषी तो माता-पिता भी नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Bharata’s body thrilled and his eyes filled with tears. Holding firm courage, he said, “My lord is as dear and worthy of worship as my father. My family teacher is my guide; even mother and father are not as helpful.”
essence: True reverence speaks with a full heart and a steady voice.
simple_meaning: Bharata is overwhelmed with emotion, yet he speaks firmly. He says Ram is as dear and worthy of respect as a father, and the family teacher is even more guiding than parents.
insight: It teaches you to let emotion deepen humility, not disrupt it.
modern_relevance: You sit across from an elder who changed your life, and your throat tightens before you can speak. Bharata shows that gratitude can be intense without becoming noisy, and respect can be deeply felt without any self-display.
speaker: Bharata

verse_text: कौसिकादि मुनि सचिव समाजू। ग्यान अंबुनिधि आपुनु आजू॥ सिसु सेवकु आयसु अनुगामी। जानि मोहि सिख देइअ स्वामी ॥
translation: विश्वामित्रजी आदि मुनियों और मंत्रियों का समाज है और आज के दिन ज्ञान के समुद्र आप भी उपस्थित हैं। हे स्वामी! मुझे अपना बच्चा, सेवक और आज्ञानुसार चलने वाला समझकर शिक्षा दीजिए ॥
english_translation: Kausika and the sages are here, along with the ministers. You yourself are here today, ocean of wisdom. O master, regard me as your child, your servant, and one who follows your command, and teach me.
essence: Real wisdom begins when you stop trying to look wise.
simple_meaning: Bharat speaks with humility, asking the wise assembly to teach him as if he were a child and servant. Real learning begins with surrendering pride.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to teachability, making true understanding possible.
modern_relevance: You sit in a room full of experts, your notes half-finished, and your first instinct is to protect your image. Bharat shows another way: ask plainly, listen fully, and let learning begin.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: एहिं समाज थल बूझब राउर। मौन मलिन मैं बोलब बाउर॥ छोटे बदन कहउँ बड़ि बाता। छमब तात लखि बाम बिधाता ॥
translation: इस समाज और (पुण्य) स्थल में आप (जैसे ज्ञानी और पूज्य) का पूछना! इस पर यदि मैं मौन रहता हूँ तो मलिन समझा जाऊँगा और बोलना पागलपन होगा तथापि मैं छोटे मुँह बड़ी बात कहता हूँ। हे तात! विधाता को प्रतिकूल जानकर क्षमा कीजिएगा ॥
english_translation: In this assembly, asking you feels strange. If I stay silent, I look dull; if I speak, I look foolish. Still, I will say a great thing with my small voice. Forgive me, father, if fate seems to oppose it.
essence: Humility can still carry a hard truth.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he feels awkward speaking in such a noble assembly, but he must still say something important and asks to be forgiven if his words seem improper.
insight: It teaches you to speak from responsibility, not confidence, when the moment requires it.
modern_relevance: You’re in a room full of senior people, and your throat tightens before you speak. You know staying quiet would be easier, but the truth in you still needs a voice.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: आगम निगम प्रसिद्ध पुराना। सेवाधरमु कठिन जगु जाना॥ स्वामि धरम स्वारथहि बिरोधू। बैरु अंध प्रेमहि न प्रबोधू ॥
translation: वेद, शास्त्र और पुराणों में प्रसिद्ध है और जगत जानता है कि सेवा धर्म बड़ा कठिन है। स्वामी धर्म में (स्वामी के प्रति कर्तव्य पालन में) और स्वार्थ में विरोध है (दोनों एक साथ नहीं निभ सकते) वैर अंधा होता है और प्रेम को ज्ञान नहीं रहता (मैं स्वार्थवश कहूँगा या प्रेमवश, दोनों में ही भूल होने का भय है) ॥
english_translation: Scripture, the Vedas, the teachings, and the Puranas all say it: service is hard in this world. Duty to a master and self-interest stand opposed; blind attachment and love cannot see clearly.
essence: Service becomes difficult the moment self-interest enters.
simple_meaning: True service is difficult because it often conflicts with personal gain. Loyalty to a master or cause cannot always be mixed with self-interest.
insight: It teaches you to separate genuine service from hidden self-benefit.
modern_relevance: You volunteer to help organize a family event, then quietly hope your effort gets noticed. The verse catches that split: service becomes difficult the moment self-interest slips in.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: राखि राम रुख धरमु ब्रतु पराधीन मोहि जानि। सब कें संमत सर्ब हित करिअ प्रेमु पहिचानि ॥
translation: अतएव मुझे पराधीन जानकर (मुझसे न पूछकर) श्री रामचन्द्रजी के रुख (रुचि), धर्म और (सत्य के) व्रत को रखते हुए, जो सबके सम्मत और सबके लिए हितकारी हो आप सबका प्रेम पहचानकर वही कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Therefore, knowing me to be dependent, keep Ram's will, dharma, and vow in view. Recognize the love that is approved by all and beneficial to all, and act accordingly.
essence: Love becomes clear when it serves everyone, not just your preference.
simple_meaning: Put Ram's will, dharma, and promise first. Then choose the course that everyone can accept and that benefits everyone.
insight: It shifts decision-making from personal insistence to shared welfare and fidelity to what is already right.
modern_relevance: A family group chat is full of opinions about what you should do next. Instead of forcing your preference, you pause and ask which choice respects the bigger good and the promise already made.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: भरत बचन सुनि देखि सुभाऊ। सहित समाज सराहत राऊ॥ सुगम अगम मृदु मंजु कठोरे। अरथु अमित अति आखर थोरे ॥
translation: भरतजी के वचन सुनकर और उनका स्वभाव देखकर समाज सहित राजा जनक उनकी सराहना करने लगे। भरतजी के वचन सुगम और अगम, सुंदर, कोमल और कठोर हैं। उनमें अक्षर थोड़े हैं, परन्तु अर्थ अत्यन्त अपार भरा हुआ है ॥
english_translation: Hearing Bharata's words and seeing his nature, King Janaka and the gathered assembly praised him. Bharata's speech is easy and difficult, gentle and firm. It uses few words, yet holds immense meaning.
essence: True speech can be brief and still carry immense weight.
simple_meaning: Bharata speaks with a rare balance: his words are gentle yet firm, simple yet profound. The assembly admires how so little speech can carry so much meaning.
insight: It teaches you to value speech that is concise, truthful, and rich with intention.
modern_relevance: You send a short message that settles a family conflict better than a long explanation ever could. Bharata's kind of speech is brief, exact, and impossible to dismiss.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ज्यों मुखु मुकुर मुकुरु निज पानी। गहि न जाइ अस अदभुत बानी॥ भूप भरतू मुनि सहित समाजू। गे जहँ बिबुध कुमुद द्विजराजू ॥
translation: जैसे मुख (का प्रतिबिम्ब) दर्पण में दिखता है और दर्पण अपने हाथ में है, फिर भी वह (मुख का प्रतिबिम्ब) पकड़ा नहीं जाता, इसी प्रकार भरतजी की यह अद्भुत वाणी भी पकड़ में नहीं आती (शब्दों से उसका आशय समझ में नहीं आता)। (किसी से कुछ उत्तर देते नहीं बना) तब राजा जनकजी, भरतजी तथा मुनि वशिष्ठजी समाज के साथ वहाँ गए, जहाँ देवता रूपी कुमुदों को खिलाने वाले (सुख देने वाले) चन्द्रमा श्री रामचन्द्रजी थे ॥
english_translation: As a face appears in a mirror held in one’s own hand, yet cannot be grasped, so too this wondrous speech of Bharat cannot be fully caught. Then King Janaka, along with Bharat and the sages, went to where Ram, the moon that delights the celestial lilies, was staying.
essence: True feeling can outgrow the words trying to hold it.
simple_meaning: Bharat’s words are so profound that they cannot be easily captured or explained. After that, Janaka, Bharat, and the sages go to meet Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from clever wording to the force of sincere feeling and presence.
modern_relevance: You read a message from someone who loves you deeply, and you sit there unable to reply. The feeling is bigger than any neat sentence. Some truths move people before they can explain them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि सुधि सोच बिकल सब लोगा। मनहुँ मीनगन नव जल जोगा॥ देवँ प्रथम कुलगुर गति देखी। निरखि बिदेह सनेह बिसेषी ॥
translation: यह समाचार सुनकर सब लोग सोच से व्याकुल हो गए, जैसे नए (पहली वर्षा के) जल के संयोग से मछलियाँ व्याकुल होती हैं। देवताओं ने पहले कुलगुरु वशिष्ठजी की (प्रेमविह्वल) दशा देखी, फिर विदेहजी के विशेष स्नेह को देखा, ॥
english_translation: Hearing the news, everyone was shaken with worry, like fish stirred by the first touch of fresh water. The gods first saw the family teacher Vashishtha in grief, then saw the special tenderness of Videha.
essence: Shared sorrow can ripple through everyone at once.
simple_meaning: The news leaves everyone shaken. The verse compares their distress to fish stirred by fresh water and notes how the gods saw Vashishtha's grief and Janaka's deep affection.
insight: It shows how grief moves through a group before anyone can explain it.
modern_relevance: A phone call arrives before dawn, and the whole family goes silent. Before anyone knows what to do, the shock has already spread through the room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम भगतिमय भरतु निहारे। सुर स्वारथी हहरि हियँ हारे॥ सब कोउ राम प्रेममय पेखा। भए अलेख सोच बस लेखा ॥
translation: और तब श्री रामभक्ति से ओतप्रोत भरतजी को देखा। इन सबको देखकर स्वार्थी देवता घबड़ाकर हृदय में हार मान गए (निराश हो गए)। उन्होंने सब किसी को श्री राम प्रेम में सराबोर देखा। इससे देवता इतने सोच के वश हो गए कि जिसका कोई हिसाब नहीं ॥
english_translation: And then they saw Bharat filled with Ram's devotion. The self-seeking devas lost heart within. They saw everyone drenched in love for Ram, and their minds were thrown into such confusion that it could not be counted.
essence: Devotion makes selfishness lose its footing.
simple_meaning: Bharat is seen as full of devotion to Ram, and everyone else appears overwhelmed by that same love. Even the self-interested devas lose confidence before it.
insight: It shifts attention from calculation to the contagious force of sincere love and loyalty.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where someone has quietly chosen loyalty over advantage. The mood shifts instantly, and all the clever self-interest in the room starts to look thin.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामु सनेह सकोच बस कह ससोच सुरराजु। रचहु प्रपंचहि पंच मिलि नाहिं त भयउ अकाजु ॥
translation: देवराज इन्द्र सोच में भरकर कहने लगे कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी तो स्नेह और संकोच के वश में हैं, इसलिए सब लोग मिलकर कुछ प्रपंच (माया) रचो, नहीं तो काम बिगड़ा (ही समझो) ॥
english_translation: Lord Indra, troubled with worry, said, 'Ram is held back by affection and modesty. All of you together create some scheme; otherwise the plan will surely fail.'
essence: Fear looks for a scheme when it cannot face gentleness directly.
simple_meaning: Indra sees that Ram's gentle nature may stop him from acting, so he urges the other gods to work together and create a plan.
insight: It reveals how anxious minds try to exploit gentleness when they cannot meet it honestly.
modern_relevance: A group chat starts spinning a workaround because the person you need to persuade is too kind to push back. The pressure feels clever, but it is really fear talking.
speaker: Indra

verse_text: सुरन्ह सुमिरि सारदा सराही। देबि देव सरनागत पाही॥ फेरि भरत मति करि निज माया। पालु बिबुध कुल करि छल छाया ॥
translation: देवताओं ने सरस्वती का स्मरण कर उनकी सराहना (स्तुति) की और कहा- हे देवी! देवता आपके शरणागत हैं, उनकी रक्षा कीजिए। अपनी माया रचकर भरतजी की बुद्धि को फेर दीजिए और छल की छाया कर देवताओं के कुल का पालन (रक्षा) कीजिए ॥
english_translation: The devas remembered and praised Saraswati: “O goddess, the devas have taken refuge in you. Protect us. Turn Bharat’s mind with your own power and, through a veil of deception, preserve the lineage of the devas.”
essence: Fear can turn even the powerful toward deception.
simple_meaning: The devas pray to Saraswati to save them by changing Bharat’s mind through her power of illusion.
insight: It exposes the mind’s willingness to use cleverness when it cannot win by honesty.
modern_relevance: A room full of people starts quietly steering the conversation because they fear losing influence. The verse shows how quickly anxiety turns into manipulation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिबुध बिनय सुनि देबि सयानी। बोली सुर स्वारथ जड़ जानी॥ मो सन कहहु भरत मति फेरू। लोचन सहस न सूझ सुमेरू ॥
translation: देवताओं की विनती सुनकर और देवताओं को स्वार्थ के वश होने से मूर्ख जानकर बुद्धिमती सरस्वतीजी बोलीं- मुझसे कह रहे हो कि भरतजी की मति पलट दो! हजार नेत्रों से भी तुमको सुमेरू नहीं सूझ पड़ता! ॥
english_translation: After hearing the gods’ plea, the wise goddess said, knowing the gods were driven by self-interest: “You ask me to turn Bharat’s mind? Even with a thousand eyes, you still cannot see Mount Sumeru.”
essence: A pure mind cannot be bent by selfish schemes.
simple_meaning: The goddess sees that the gods are acting out of self-interest, and she refuses their request. Bharat's mind is so steady and noble that they cannot even understand it, let alone change it.
insight: It shifts you from trying to control noble people to recognising when your own motives are clouding your judgment.
modern_relevance: A group chat starts plotting how to nudge someone into doing what benefits everyone else. One person quietly refuses the manipulation because they can see the motive behind it. That steadiness is what Saraswati defends here.
speaker: Saraswati

verse_text: बिधि हरि हर माया बड़ि भारी। सोउ न भरत मति सकइ निहारी॥ सो मति मोहि कहत करु भोरी। चंदिनि कर कि चंडकर चोरी ॥
translation: ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और महेश की माया बड़ी प्रबल है! किन्तु वह भी भरतजी की बुद्धि की ओर ताक नहीं सकती। उस बुद्धि को, तुम मुझसे कह रहे हो कि, भोली कर दो (भुलावे में डाल दो)! अरे! चाँदनी कहीं प्रचंड किरण वाले सूर्य को चुरा सकती है? ॥
english_translation: Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva's illusion is immense, yet it cannot even look at Bharat's mind. And you ask me to make that mind foolish? Can moonlight steal the blazing sun?
essence: A mind held by Ram cannot be tricked by illusion.
simple_meaning: Even the strongest illusion cannot touch Bharat's understanding, because his heart is already filled with Ram. Saraswati refuses the request to make him foolish.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing devotion as weakness to seeing it as protection against confusion.
modern_relevance: Someone tries to twist your words in a family group chat, but you already know what matters. When your values are anchored, manipulation has less room to enter.
speaker: Saraswati

verse_text: भरत हृदयँ सिय राम निवासू। तहँ कि तिमिर जहँ तरनि प्रकासू॥ अस कहि सारद गइ बिधि लोका। बिबुध बिकल निसि मानहुँ कोका ॥
translation: भरतजी के हृदय में श्री सीता-रामजी का निवास है। जहाँ सूर्य का प्रकाश है, वहाँ कहीं अँधेरा रह सकता है? ऐसा कहकर सरस्वतीजी ब्रह्मलोक को चली गईं। देवता ऐसे व्याकुल हुए जैसे रात्रि में चकवा व्याकुल होता है ॥
english_translation: Bharat's heart is where Sita and Ram dwell. Where sunlight shines, how can darkness remain? Saying this, Saraswati returned to Brahmaloka. The gods were restless, like chakravaka birds at night.
essence: Where Ram dwells in the heart, darkness has no foothold.
simple_meaning: Bharat's heart is already filled with Ram and Sita, so there is no place for darkness there. Saraswati says this and leaves, while the gods remain agitated.
insight: It shifts attention from suspicion to the inner quality that makes devotion unshakeable.
modern_relevance: You are exhausted after defending someone decent from unfair gossip, and the room still feels tense. This verse reminds you that a heart anchored in love and loyalty cannot be easily poisoned.
speaker: Saraswati

verse_text: सुर स्वारथी मलीन मन कीन्ह कुमंत्र कुठाटु। रचि प्रपंच माया प्रबल भय भ्रम अरति उचाटु ॥
translation: मलिन मन वाले स्वार्थी देवताओं ने बुरी सलाह करके बुरा ठाट (षड्यन्त्र) रचा। प्रबल माया-जाल रचकर भय, भ्रम, अप्रीति और उच्चाटन फैला दिया ॥
english_translation: The selfish, impure-minded devas plotted a bad scheme. They wove a powerful web of illusion, spreading fear, confusion, dislike, and restlessness.
essence: Selfish minds can manufacture fear, confusion, and unrest.
simple_meaning: Selfish, impure-minded devas created a harmful plot and used illusion to stir fear, confusion, dislike, and restlessness.
insight: It shows how selfish intent distorts perception and turns collective energy into anxiety.
modern_relevance: A group chat starts spinning rumors before a family meeting, and suddenly everyone feels tense for no clear reason. This verse names that atmosphere: fear and confusion can be manufactured.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि कुचालि सोचत सुरराजू। भरत हाथ सबु काजु अकाजू॥ गए जनकु रघुनाथ समीपा। सनमाने सब रबिकुल दीपा ॥
translation: कुचाल करके देवराज इन्द्र सोचने लगे कि काम का बनना-बिगड़ना सब भरतजी के हाथ है। इधर राजा जनकजी (मुनि वशिष्ठ आदि के साथ) श्री रघुनाथजी के पास गए। सूर्यकुल के दीपक श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सबका सम्मान किया, ॥
english_translation: By crooked means, Indra kept worrying, thinking that everything depended on Bharata's hands. Meanwhile King Janaka went to Raghunatha, and the lamp of Raghu's line honoured everyone.
essence: Crooked power worries; Ram answers with honour.
simple_meaning: Indra schemed and worried, thinking Bharata could shape everything. At the same time, Janaka went to Ram, and Ram honoured everyone with dignity.
insight: It contrasts anxious control with dignified conduct, showing that true authority does not need manipulation.
modern_relevance: A group chat fills with suspicion, one person quietly spins the story, and another walks into the room and treats everyone with calm respect.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समय समाज धरम अबिरोधा। बोले तब रघुबंस पुरोधा॥ जनक भरत संबादु सुनाई। भरत कहाउति कही सुहाई ॥
translation: तब रघुकुल के पुरोहित वशिष्ठजी समय, समाज और धर्म के अविरोधी (अर्थात अनुकूल) वचन बोले। उन्होंने पहले जनकजी और भरतजी का संवाद सुनाया। फिर भरतजी की कही हुई सुंदर बातें कह सुनाईं ॥
english_translation: Then the family priest of Raghu's line spoke words suited to the time, the gathering, and dharma. He first recounted the dialogue between Janaka and Bharata, and then repeated Bharata's lovely words.
essence: Wise speech fits the moment without betraying the truth.
simple_meaning: Vashishtha speaks carefully, choosing words that fit the moment. He retells Janaka and Bharata's conversation and repeats Bharata's noble words.
insight: It shows that wise speech is not just true, but well-timed, socially aware, and aligned with dharma.
modern_relevance: In a family meeting where everyone is already upset, one person slows down, chooses careful words, and repeats the exact sentence that keeps the room from breaking apart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तात राम जस आयसु देहू। सो सबु करै मोर मत एहू॥ सुनि रघुनाथ जोरि जुग पानी। बोले सत्य सरल मृदु बानी ॥
translation: (फिर बोले-) हे तात राम! मेरा मत तो यह है कि तुम जैसी आज्ञा दो, वैसा ही सब करें! यह सुनकर दोनों हाथ जोड़कर श्री रघुनाथजी सत्य, सरल और कोमल वाणी बोले- ॥
english_translation: Then he said, “Father, give me Ram’s command. I think everyone should do only that.” Hearing this, Raghunath joined both palms and spoke with truth, simplicity, and gentleness.
essence: True greatness bows first and speaks gently.
simple_meaning: Janak says that Ram’s command should guide everyone. Ram responds with folded hands and speaks gently and truthfully.
insight: It shifts leadership from control to humility, showing that real dignity does not need to assert itself.
modern_relevance: You’re in a family group chat where everyone waits for the most important person to decide. The calmest voice is the one that lowers itself first.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: बिद्यमान आपुनि मिथिलेसू। मोर कहब सब भाँति भदेसू॥ राउर राय रजायसु होई। राउरि सपथ सही सिर सोई ॥
translation: आपके और मिथिलेश्वर जनकजी के विद्यमान रहते मेरा कुछ कहना सब प्रकार से भद्दा (अनुचित) है। आपकी और महाराज की जो आज्ञा होगी, मैं आपकी शपथ करके कहता हूँ वह सत्य ही सबको शिरोधार्य होगी॥
english_translation: While Mithila's king Janak is still present, anything I say would be improper. Whatever command you and the king give, I swear by your word alone, it will be accepted by all.
essence: Humility lets truth arrive without self-assertion.
simple_meaning: Ram says it is improper for him to speak while Janak is present. He places both authority and truth in the hands of his elders.
insight: It teaches you to step back from ego and let proper authority or context guide the exchange.
modern_relevance: You are in a tense family meeting and everyone keeps interrupting. Instead of forcing your point, you wait, respect the elder voice, and let the right order return.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: राम सपथ सुनि मुनि जनकु सकुचे सभा समेत। सकल बिलोकत भरत मुखु बनइ न ऊतरु देत ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की शपथ सुनकर सभा समेत मुनि और जनकजी सकुचा गए (स्तम्भित रह गए)। किसी से उत्तर देते नहीं बनता, सब लोग भरतजी का मुँह ताक रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing Ram's solemn vow, the sage, Janak, and the whole assembly fell silent. Everyone looked at Bharat, but no one could speak.
essence: Ram's vow leaves even the wise without words.
simple_meaning: Ram's vow leaves everyone in the hall silent and uneasy. They all look to Bharat, but no one can answer.
insight: It shows how a sacred promise can stop argument and force everyone into stillness.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone speaks with complete sincerity. Everyone feels the weight of it, and the real response is not noise but restraint.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सभा सकुच बस भरत निहारी। राम बंधु धरि धीरजु भारी॥ कुसमउ देखि सनेहु सँभारा। बढ़त बिंधि जिमि घटज निवारा ॥
translation: भरतजी ने सभा को संकोच के वश देखा। रामबंधु (भरतजी) ने बड़ा भारी धीरज धरकर और कुसमय देखकर अपने (उमड़ते हुए) प्रेम को संभाला, जैसे बढ़ते हुए विन्ध्याचल को अगस्त्यजी ने रोका था ॥
english_translation: Bharat looked at the assembly with great restraint. Seeing the wrong moment, Ram's brother held back his rising love, just as Agastya stopped the growing Vindhya.
essence: True love can be strongest when it knows when to wait.
simple_meaning: Bharat sees the tense assembly and, though love rises in him, he restrains himself because the moment is not right.
insight: It teaches you to regulate emotion by reading context, not by suppressing feeling altogether.
modern_relevance: You’re about to text back in anger after a family argument, but you pause and reread the room. That restraint can protect what matters most.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सोक कनकलोचन मति छोनी। हरी बिमल गुन गन जगजोनी॥ भरत बिबेक बराहँ बिसाला। अनायास उधरी तेहि काला ॥
translation: शोक रूपी हिरण्याक्ष ने (सारी सभा की) बुद्धि रूपी पृथ्वी को हर लिया जो विमल गुण समूह रूपी जगत की योनि (उत्पन्न करने वाली) थी। भरतजी के विवेक रूपी विशाल वराह (वराह रूप धारी भगवान) ने (शोक रूपी हिरण्याक्ष को नष्ट कर) बिना ही परिश्रम उसका उद्धार कर दिया! ॥
english_translation: Grief had swallowed the mind of the whole assembly, which was the source of pure virtues. Bharat's vast discernment, like a mighty boar, lifted it all without effort.
essence: Clear discernment can rescue minds buried in grief.
simple_meaning: Grief had overwhelmed everyone, but Bharat's discernment cut through it and restored clarity without any struggle.
insight: It shifts you from being absorbed by collective emotion to becoming the stabilizing presence that helps others think clearly.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family room after bad news, and everyone is frozen. You don't fix the loss, but your calm, steady clarity keeps the whole moment from collapsing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि प्रनामु सब कहँ कर जोरे। रामु राउ गुर साधु निहोरे॥ छमब आजु अति अनुचित मोरा। कहउँ बदन मृदु बचन कठोरा ॥
translation: भरतजी ने प्रणाम करके सबके प्रति हाथ जोड़े तथा श्री रामचन्द्रजी, राजा जनकजी, गुरु वशिष्ठजी और साधु-संत सबसे विनती की और कहा- आज मेरे इस अत्यन्त अनुचित बर्ताव को क्षमा कीजिएगा। मैं कोमल (छोटे) मुख से कठोर (धृष्टतापूर्ण) वचन कह रहा हूँ ॥
english_translation: Bharat bowed to everyone with folded hands and humbly begged Ram, King Janak, Guru Vashishtha, and the saints: forgive my utterly improper conduct today. With a gentle face, I am speaking harsh words.
essence: Respect can carry even the hardest words.
simple_meaning: Bharat shows deep humility before speaking. He asks everyone to forgive him because he knows his words may sound harsh, even though his intention is respectful.
insight: It teaches you to frame difficult speech with humility, so truth does not become aggression.
modern_relevance: You’re about to send a message that could sting, so you rewrite it twice and add a softer opening. Bharat’s instinct is the same: respect first, then the hard sentence.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: हियँ सुमिरी सारदा सुहाई। मानस तें मुख पंकज आई॥ बिमल बिबेक धरम नय साली। भरत भारती मंजु मराली ॥
translation: फिर उन्होंने हृदय में सुहावनी सरस्वती का स्मरण किया। वे मानस से (उनके मन रूपी मानसरोवर से) उनके मुखारविंद पर आ विराजीं। निर्मल विवेक, धर्म और नीति से युक्त भरतजी की वाणी सुंदर हंसिनी (के समान गुण-दोष का विवेचन करने वाली) है ॥
english_translation: Then he remembered lovely Saraswati in his heart, and she came from the lake of his mind to his lotus face. Filled with pure discernment, dharma, and wise conduct, Bharat's speech is like a graceful swan.
essence: Clear discernment turns speech into something beautiful and trustworthy.
simple_meaning: Bharat remembers Saraswati, and his speech becomes beautiful because it is guided by clear discernment, dharma, and wise conduct.
insight: It teaches you to let discernment guide speech before emotion takes over.
modern_relevance: You are about to speak in a family meeting after a painful argument. If you pause long enough to remember what is true, your words can calm the room instead of adding fuel.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निरखि बिबेक बिलोचनन्हि सिथिल सनेहँ समाजु। करि प्रनामु बोले भरतु सुमिरि सीय रघुराजु ॥
translation: विवेक के नेत्रों से सारे समाज को प्रेम से शिथिल देख, सबको प्रणाम कर, श्री सीताजी और श्री रघुनाथजी का स्मरण करके भरतजी बोले- ॥
english_translation: Seeing the gathering with the eye of discernment softened by love, he bowed to all and, remembering Sita and the lord of Raghu, Bharata spoke.
essence: Clear seeing lets love replace tension before words begin.
simple_meaning: Bharat looks at everyone with calm discernment and loving respect. He bows to all, remembers Sita and Ram, and begins to speak.
insight: It trains you to meet a charged room with discernment first, reaction second.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone expects tension, but you pause, breathe, and see people clearly before speaking. That small softness changes everything.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: प्रभु पितु मातु सुहृद गुर स्वामी। पूज्य परम हित अंतरजामी॥ सरल सुसाहिबु सील निधानू। प्रनतपाल सर्बग्य सुजानू ॥
translation: हे प्रभु! आप पिता, माता, सुहृद् (मित्र), गुरु, स्वामी, पूज्य, परम हितैषी और अन्तर्यामी हैं। सरल हृदय, श्रेष्ठ मालिक, शील के भंडार, शरणागत की रक्षा करने वाले, सर्वज्ञ, सुजान, ॥
english_translation: O Lord, you are father, mother, friend, teacher, and master. You are worthy of worship, the highest benefactor, and the inner knower. You are simple-hearted, a noble lord, a treasury of character, protector of those who seek refuge, all-knowing, and wise.
essence: Ram is every true refuge you could ever need.
simple_meaning: Bharat praises Ram as the one who fulfills every loving role at once: parent, friend, teacher, master, protector, and inner knower.
insight: It shifts devotion from formal praise to complete dependence on Ram's care and understanding.
modern_relevance: After a family argument, you finally stop defending yourself and say, 'You know what I need better than I do.' That surrender is the mood of this verse.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: समरथ सरनागत हितकारी। गुनगाहकु अवगुन अघ हारी॥ स्वामि गोसाँइहि सरिस गोसाईं। मोहि समान मैं साइँ दोहाईं ॥
translation: समर्थ, शरणागत का हित करने वाले, गुणों का आदर करने वाले और अवगुणों तथा पापों को हरने वाले हैं। हे गोसाईं! आप सरीखे स्वामी आप ही हैं और स्वामी के साथ द्रोह करने में मेरे समान मैं ही हूँ ॥
english_translation: You are powerful, the refuge of those who surrender, one who values virtue, and one who removes faults and sins. O lord, there is no master like you. I alone am the one who has betrayed my master.
essence: Refuge is real, but betrayal is never hidden from the one who knows you.
simple_meaning: Bharat praises Ram as the protector of anyone who takes refuge in him, then blames himself for failing his duty and loyalty.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-justification to honest surrender and responsibility.
modern_relevance: You finally call someone after letting them down, and the first thing you say is not an excuse. It is the truth: they were steady; you were not.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: प्रभु पितु बचन मोह बस पेली। आयउँ इहाँ समाजु सकेली॥ जग भल पोच ऊँच अरु नीचू। अमिअ अमरपद माहुरु मीचू ॥
translation: मैं मोहवश प्रभु (आप) के और पिताजी के वचनों का उल्लंघन कर और समाज बटोरकर यहाँ आया हूँ। जगत में भले-बुरे, ऊँचे और नीचे, अमृत और अमर पद (देवताओं का पद), विष और मृत्यु आदि- ॥
english_translation: Overcome by delusion, I broke my lord's and my father's word and came here with the whole assembly. In this world, there are the good and the bad, the high and the low, nectar and the deathly poison, even the immortal realm and death itself.
essence: Delusion makes you violate what you already know is right.
simple_meaning: Bharat admits that confusion led him to break his father and lord's command and come with the gathered court. He also reflects that the world contains opposites: good and bad, high and low, nectar and poison.
insight: It shifts the mind from excuse-making to clear seeing of how delusion distorts action.
modern_relevance: You replay the text thread where you ignored a clear boundary, then tried to justify it afterward. Bharat's honesty cuts through that self-protection and names the confusion before it hardens into pride.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: राम रजाइ मेट मन माहीं। देखा सुना कतहुँ कोउ नाहीं॥ सो मैं सब बिधि कीन्हि ढिठाई। प्रभु मानी सनेह सेवकाई ॥
translation: किसी को भी कहीं ऐसा नहीं देखा-सुना जो मन में भी श्री रामचन्द्रजी (आप) की आज्ञा को मेट दे। मैंने सब प्रकार से वही ढिठाई की, परन्तु प्रभु ने उस ढिठाई को स्नेह और सेवा मान लिया! ॥
english_translation: I have never seen or heard of anyone who can erase Ram's command even in the mind. I was bold in every way, but the Lord took that boldness as love and service.
essence: Ram can turn even your misstep into loving service.
simple_meaning: No one can erase Ram's command from the heart. Bharat says his own stubborn act was received by Ram as love and service.
insight: It shifts you from self-condemnation to seeing how sincere intention can redeem imperfect action.
modern_relevance: You sent the message too sharply, then worried it ruined everything. But the person who loves you may hear the care beneath the clumsiness.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: कृपाँ भलाईं आपनी नाथ कीन्ह भल मोर। दूषन भे भूषन सरिस सुजसु चारु चहुँ ओर ॥
translation: हे नाथ! आपने अपनी कृपा और भलाई से मेरा भला किया, जिससे मेरे दूषण (दोष) भी भूषण (गुण) के समान हो गए और चारों ओर मेरा सुंदर यश छा गया ॥
english_translation: O Lord, by your grace and kindness you have done me good. My faults have become ornaments, and my beautiful fame now shines everywhere.
essence: Grace can turn your faults into ornaments.
simple_meaning: Ram's kindness has transformed Bharat's shame into honor. What looked like fault has become something beautiful, and his name now shines everywhere.
insight: It shifts self-image from shame to gratitude, showing how loving response can transform guilt into dignity.
modern_relevance: You sent the apology, expecting distance. Instead, the other person answered with warmth, and your worst moment stopped defining you. Grace can do that.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: राउरि रीति सुबानि बड़ाई। जगत बिदित निगमागम गाई॥ कूर कुटिल खल कुमति कलंकी। नीच निसील निरीस निसंकी ॥
translation: हे नाथ! आपकी रीति और सुंदर स्वभाव की बड़ाई जगत में प्रसिद्ध है और वेद-शास्त्रों ने गाई है। जो क्रूर, कुटिल, दुष्ट, कुबुद्धि, कलंकी, नीच, शीलरहित, निरीश्वरवादी (नास्तिक) और निःशंक (निडर) है ॥
english_translation: Your noble conduct and beautiful nature are praised throughout the world and sung by the Vedas. Even the cruel, crooked, wicked, ill-minded, stained, low, shameless, irreverent, and fearless...
essence: Ram’s grace is large enough to include even the fallen.
simple_meaning: Your noble conduct is known everywhere, and even the most fallen people are included in your grace.
insight: It shifts judgment into trust, showing that grace can reach even the lowest person.
modern_relevance: You’ve written someone off because of their worst behavior, then watched them soften when treated with dignity. This verse remembers that character can transform when grace meets it first.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तेउ सुनि सरन सामुहें आए। सकृत प्रनामु किहें अपनाए॥ देखि दोष कबहुँ न उर आने। सुनि गुन साधु समाज बखाने ॥
translation: उन्हें भी आपने शरण में सम्मुख आया सुनकर एक बार प्रणाम करने पर ही अपना लिया। उन (शरणागतों) के दोषों को देखकर भी आप कभी हृदय में नहीं लाए और उनके गुणों को सुनकर साधुओं के समाज में उनका बखान किया ॥
english_translation: Even those who came before you and bowed just once were accepted. You never held their faults in your heart, and when you heard their virtues, you praised them among the noble.
essence: Surrender meets a heart that remembers your goodness, not your flaws.
simple_meaning: Ram accepts anyone who comes to him in surrender, does not dwell on their faults, and speaks well of their good qualities.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to surrender, and from judging others to noticing their goodness.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after making a mess, expecting judgment. Instead, someone meets you without replaying your worst moment. That kind of welcome changes everything.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: को साहिब सेवकहि नेवाजी। आपु समाज साज सब साजी॥ निज करतूति न समुझिअ सपनें। सेवक सकुच सोचु उर अपनें ॥
translation: ऐसा सेवक पर कृपा करने वाला स्वामी कौन है, जो आप ही सेवक का सारा साज-सामान सज दे (उसकी सारी आवश्यकताओं को पूर्ण कर दे) और स्वप्न में भी अपनी कोई करनी न समझकर (अर्थात मैंने सेवक के लिए कुछ किया है, ऐसा न जानकर) उलटा सेवक को संकोच होगा, इसका सोच अपने हृदय में रखे! ॥
english_translation: What master, so gracious to a servant, arranges all the servant’s needs and, without ever thinking, even in a dream, that he has done anything, still worries that the servant may feel shy or troubled?
essence: Grace gives fully without making the receiver feel beholden.
simple_meaning: The highest kind of master gives everything a servant needs and never lets the servant feel that a favor was done.
insight: It shifts devotion from transaction to tenderness, showing care that never turns into debt.
modern_relevance: Someone quietly covers your share of the bill, fixes the form you forgot, and never mentions it again. The kindness feels clean because it leaves your dignity intact.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सो गोसाइँ नहिं दूसर कोपी। भुजा उठाइ कहउँ पन रोपी॥ पसु नाचत सुक पाठ प्रबीना। गुन गति नट पाठक आधीना ॥
translation: मैं भुजा उठाकर और प्रण रोपकर (बड़े जोर के साथ) कहता हूँ, ऐसा स्वामी आपके सिवा दूसरा कोई नहीं है। (बंदर आदि) पशु नाचते और तोते (सीखे हुए) पाठ में प्रवीण हो जाते हैं, परन्तु तोते का (पाठ प्रवीणता रूप) गुण और पशु के नाचने की गति (क्रमशः) पढ़ाने वाले और नचाने वाले के अधीन है ॥
english_translation: I say with raised arms and a firm vow: there is no lord like you. Animals dance, and parrots become skilled in recitation, but the skill of the parrot and the movement of the animal depend on the teacher and trainer.
essence: Your abilities are not self-made; they still rest in Ram's care.
simple_meaning: No one is as gracious and capable as Ram. Even a creature's skill or movement comes from the one who trains it, so all ability ultimately depends on the divine source.
insight: It shifts credit away from ego and toward the source that makes ability possible.
modern_relevance: You finally nail the presentation after weeks of practice, and everyone applauds your talent. This verse quietly reminds you that even your steadiness, timing, and nerve were being supported all along.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: यों सुधारि सनमानि जन किए साधु सिरमोर। को कृपाल बिनु पालिहै बिरिदावलि बरजोर ॥
translation: इस प्रकार अपने सेवकों की (बिगड़ी) बात सुधारकर और सम्मान देकर आपने उन्हें साधुओं का शिरोमणि बना दिया। कृपालु (आप) के सिवा अपनी विरदावली का और कौन जबर्दस्ती (हठपूर्वक) पालन करेगा? ॥
english_translation: In this way, by correcting their faults and honoring them, you made your servants the foremost among the good. Who, except the compassionate one, would forcefully keep to such a vow?
essence: Compassion keeps your promises and raises others with them.
simple_meaning: Ram corrects his servants gently and honors them so fully that they become admirable. Only a deeply compassionate master would keep his promise with such loving force.
insight: It teaches you to lead by refining and honoring others, not by crushing them into obedience.
modern_relevance: A manager notices a mistake in a team member's work and fixes it without embarrassment, then publicly credits them for the improvement. The person leaves stronger, not smaller.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सोक सनेहँ कि बाल सुभाएँ। आयउँ लाइ रजायसु बाएँ॥ तबहुँ कृपाल हेरि निज ओरा। सबहि भाँति भल मानेउ मोरा ॥
translation: मैं शोक से या स्नेह से या बालक स्वभाव से आज्ञा को बाएँ लाकर (न मानकर) चला आया, तो भी कृपालु स्वामी (आप) ने अपनी ओर देखकर सभी प्रकार से मेरा भला ही माना (मेरे इस अनुचित कार्य को अच्छा ही समझा) ॥
english_translation: I came with my order turned aside, whether from grief, affection, or childish nature. Yet the compassionate Lord looked toward me and accepted my mistake as good in every way.
essence: Compassion sees more good in you than your mistake deserves.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he came with his order set aside, but Ram still treated him with kindness and saw the good in him.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to trust in compassionate seeing.
modern_relevance: You sent the apology after the damage was already done, expecting coldness back. Instead, the person you hurt chose generosity, and that changed everything.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: देखेउँ पाय सुमंगल मूला। जानेउँ स्वामि सहज अनुकूला। बड़ें समाज बिलोकेउँ भागू। बड़ीं चूक साहिब अनुरागू ॥
translation: मैंने सुंदर मंगलों के मूल आपके चरणों का दर्शन किया और यह जान लिया कि स्वामी मुझ पर स्वभाव से ही अनुकूल हैं। इस बड़े समाज में अपने भाग्य को देखा कि इतनी बड़ी चूक होने पर भी स्वामी का मुझ पर कितना अनुराग है! ॥
english_translation: I saw your feet, the source of all auspiciousness, and knew my master is naturally kind to me. In this great gathering, I saw my own good fortune: even after such a grave mistake, my master still holds love for me.
essence: True love remains steady even after a grave mistake.
simple_meaning: Bharat feels that seeing Ram's feet has shown him both blessing and mercy. Even after his mistake, Ram's affection has not changed.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to receiving grace without resistance.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family room after saying the wrong thing and expecting distance. Instead, someone meets you with the same warmth. That quiet mercy can undo shame faster than any apology.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: कृपा अनुग्रहु अंगु अघाई। कीन्हि कृपानिधि सब अधिकाई॥ राखा मोर दुलार गोसाईं। अपनें सील सुभायँ भलाई ॥
translation: कृपानिधान ने मुझ पर सांगोपांग भरपेट कृपा और अनुग्रह, सब अधिक ही किए हैं (अर्थात मैं जिसके जरा भी लायक नहीं था, उतनी अधिक सर्वांगपूर्ण कृपा आपने मुझ पर की है)। हे गोसाईं! आपने अपने शील, स्वभाव और भलाई से मेरा दुलार रखा ॥
english_translation: The gracious Lord has poured out complete kindness and favor on me, far more than I deserved. O Lord of kindness, you have kept your affection for me alive through your own character, gentleness, and goodness.
essence: Grace is greater than merit, and gentleness keeps love alive.
simple_meaning: Bharat says Ram has shown him far more grace than he deserved, and that Ram's gentle nature has kept that affection alive.
insight: It shifts you from measuring what you deserve to noticing how generously you have been received.
modern_relevance: You apologized badly, expecting coldness back, and instead the other person answered with patience. That kind of response changes you more than punishment ever could.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: नाथ निपट मैं कीन्हि ढिठाई। स्वामि समाज सकोच बिहाई॥ अबिनय बिनय जथारुचि बानी। छमिहि देउ अति आरति जानी ॥
translation: हे नाथ! मैंने स्वामी और समाज के संकोच को छोड़कर अविनय या विनय भरी जैसी रुचि हुई वैसी ही वाणी कहकर सर्वथा ढिठाई की है। हे देव! मेरे आर्तभाव (आतुरता) को जानकर आप क्षमा करेंगे ॥
english_translation: Lord, I have been utterly bold. I have set aside all hesitation before my master and this assembly. Whether my words were respectful or not, I spoke as I wished. Please forgive me, knowing my distress.
essence: Distress can be more truthful than polished politeness.
simple_meaning: Bharat admits he spoke boldly and without formal restraint. He asks forgiveness, saying his distress made him speak this way.
insight: It shifts you from polishing your speech to revealing your real condition.
modern_relevance: You finally tell a parent, partner, or teacher what you really feel, and your voice shakes. The right listener does not punish the imperfect words; they hear the pain underneath.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: सुहृद सुजान सुसाहिबहि बहुत कहब बड़ि खोरि। आयसु देइअ देव अब सबइ सुधारी मोरि ॥
translation: सुहृद् (बिना ही हेतु के हित करने वाले), बुद्धिमान और श्रेष्ठ मालिक से बहुत कहना बड़ा अपराध है, इसलिए हे देव! अब मुझे आज्ञा दीजिए, आपने मेरी सभी बात सुधार दी ॥
english_translation: It is a great fault to say too much to a wise, kind lord. So now, O divine one, give me your command; you have already set my words right.
essence: True guidance begins when your own explaining stops.
simple_meaning: Speaking too much before a wise, kind master is a mistake. The speaker now asks for instruction and trusts that the master's guidance will correct everything.
insight: It shifts you from self-justification to receptive obedience.
modern_relevance: You keep explaining yourself in a tense conversation, then suddenly realise the other person already understands the heart of it. The next move is not more defending — it is listening.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: प्रभु पद पदुम पराग दोहाई। सत्य सुकृत सुख सीवँ सुहाई॥ सो करि कहउँ हिए अपने की। रुचि जागत सोवत सपने की ॥
translation: प्रभु (आप) के चरणकमलों की रज, जो सत्य, सुकृत (पुण्य) और सुख की सुहावनी सीमा (अवधि) है, उसकी दुहाई करके मैं अपने हृदय को जागते, सोते और स्वप्न में भी बनी रहने वाली रुचि (इच्छा) कहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I invoke the dust of my Lord's lotus feet, the lovely limit of truth, merit, and joy. By that, I speak of the desire that stays in my heart while waking, sleeping, and dreaming.
essence: True devotion keeps returning, even in sleep and dream.
simple_meaning: The speaker bows to Ram's feet and says that his heart's real desire stays fixed on Ram at all times, awake, asleep, and dreaming.
insight: It shifts desire from scattered craving to one steady devotion that follows you through every state.
modern_relevance: You check your phone before bed and again the moment you wake up, and one person or one longing is still there. This verse names that kind of unbroken attachment, then turns it toward loving service.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सहज सनेहँ स्वामि सेवकाई। स्वारथ छल फल चारि बिहाई॥ अग्यासम न सुसाहिब सेवा। सो प्रसादु जन पावै देवा।2॥
translation: वह रुचि है- कपट, स्वार्थ और (अर्थ-धर्म-काम-मोक्ष रूप) चारों फलों को छोड़कर स्वाभाविक प्रेम से स्वामी की सेवा करना। और आज्ञा पालन के समान श्रेष्ठ स्वामी की और कोई सेवा नहीं है। हे देव! अब वही आज्ञा रूप प्रसाद सेवक को मिल जाए ॥
english_translation: The best service to a master is to obey with natural love, leaving behind selfishness, deceit, and the four aims of life. O divine one, may I receive that blessing of obedience.
essence: Love serves best when it gives up bargaining.
simple_meaning: The purest service is loving obedience without selfish motives or hidden deals.
insight: It shifts service from transaction to wholehearted obedience.
modern_relevance: You help a friend move house, even though nobody will notice how much you carried. You don't keep score. That quiet, unadvertised loyalty is what this verse praises.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अस कहि प्रेम बिबस भए भारी। पुलक सरीर बिलोचन बारी॥ प्रभु पद कमल गहे अकुलाई। समउ सनेहु न सो कहि जाई ॥
