translation: भरतजी ऐसा कहकर प्रेम के बहुत ही विवश हो गए। शरीर पुलकित हो उठा, नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया। अकुलाकर (व्याकुल होकर) उन्होंने प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणकमल पकड़ लिए। उस समय को और स्नेह को कहा नहीं जा सकता ॥
english_translation: Saying this, Bharata became overwhelmed with love. His body thrilled with goosebumps, and tears filled his eyes. In distress, he seized Lord Rama's lotus feet. No one can describe that moment or that love.
essence: True love leaves no room for performance.
simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed by love for Ram. His body trembles, tears come, and he clings to Ram's feet because his feelings are too deep for words.
insight: It shows that devotion is not polished emotion; it is the body moving before the mind can explain itself.
modern_relevance: You finally see someone you have missed for years, and all your rehearsed words disappear. Your chest tightens, your eyes fill, and the first thing you do is reach for their hand.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कृपासिंधु सनमानि सुबानी। बैठाए समीप गहि पानी॥ भरत बिनय सुनिदेखि सुभाऊ। सिथिल सनेहँ सभा रघुराऊ ॥
translation: कृपासिन्धु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सुंदर वाणी से भरतजी का सम्मान करके हाथ पकड़कर उनको अपने पास बिठा लिया। भरतजी की विनती सुनकर और उनका स्वभाव देखकर सारी सभा और श्री रघुनाथजी स्नेह से शिथिल हो गए ॥
english_translation: The ocean of compassion honored Bharat with kind words, took his hand, and seated him nearby. Hearing Bharat's plea and seeing his nature, the whole assembly and Raghunath melted with love.
essence: Love deepens when honor is given without hesitation.
simple_meaning: Ram receives Bharat with tenderness, seating him close and honoring him. Bharat's humility moves everyone present, and love softens the whole assembly.
insight: It shifts attention from status to reverent welcome, showing how humility can transform an entire gathering.
modern_relevance: You finally meet the sibling who has no wish to outshine you, only to serve. The room changes when you stop defending your place and simply honor theirs.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रघुराउ सिथिल सनेहँ साधु समाज मुनि मिथिला धनी। मन महुँ सराहत भरत भायप भगति की महिमा घनी॥ भरतहि प्रसंसत बिबुध बरषत सुमन मानस मलिन से। तुलसी बिकल सब लोग सुनि सकुचे निसागम नलिन से॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी, साधुओं का समाज, मुनि वशिष्ठजी और मिथिलापति जनकजी स्नेह से शिथिल हो गए। सब मन ही मन भरतजी के भाईपन और उनकी भक्ति की अतिशय महिमा को सराहने लगे। देवता मलिन से मन से भरतजी की प्रशंसा करते हुए उन पर फूल बरसाने लगे। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- सब लोग भरतजी का भाषण सुनकर व्याकुल हो गए और ऐसे सकुचा गए जैसे रात्रि के आगमन से कमल!
english_translation: Lord Raghunath, the saints, Sage Vashishtha, and King Janaka were softened by affection. In their hearts they praised the greatness of Bharat's brotherhood and devotion. The gods, with hearts made pure, showered flowers in praise of Bharat. Tulsidas says: hearing Bharat's words, everyone was overwhelmed and shy, like lotuses at nightfall.
essence: Sincere devotion can move even the highest hearts.
simple_meaning: Bharat's devotion and brotherly love move everyone present. Even revered elders and the divine beings praise him, while the whole assembly feels overwhelmed by the depth of his heart.
insight: It shifts attention from public performance to the quiet force of sincere devotion and brotherly loyalty.
modern_relevance: You show up for a family crisis with no agenda, no image to protect, and no demand to be praised. People feel it immediately — and their respect changes before you say another word.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: देखि दुखारी दीन दुहु समाज नर नारि सब। मघवा महा मलीन मुए मारि मंगल चहत ॥
translation: दोनों समाजों के सभी नर-नारियों को दीन और दुःखी देखकर महामलिन मन इन्द्र मरे हुओं को मारकर अपना मंगल चाहता है ॥
english_translation: Seeing both communities of men and women grieving and helpless, the utterly impure Indra, even by harming the already fallen, seeks his own gain.
essence: Self-interest can remain blind even in the presence of shared suffering.
simple_meaning: Everyone in both groups is sad and powerless, and Indra is so corrupt that he wants his own benefit even if it means hurting those already suffering.
insight: It sharpens the contrast between collective grief and self-serving calculation, exposing selfishness as a failure of character.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after bad news, and one person still starts calculating what they can get out of it. That instinct reveals a mind untouched by compassion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कपट कुचालि सीवँ सुरराजू। पर अकाज प्रिय आपन काजू॥ काक समान पाकरिपु रीती। छली मलीन कतहुँ न प्रतीती ॥
translation: देवराज इन्द्र कपट और कुचाल की सीमा है। उसे पराई हानि और अपना लाभ ही प्रिय है। इन्द्र की रीति कौए के समान है। वह छली और मलिन मन है, उसका कहीं किसी पर विश्वास नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Indra, king of the gods, is the height of deceit and crookedness. He loves harm to others and benefit for himself. Indra's way is like a crow's. He is deceitful and impure, and no trust can be placed in him.
essence: Cleverness without integrity becomes a crow's way.
simple_meaning: Indra is described as selfish, deceitful, and untrustworthy. He wants others harmed if it helps him.
insight: It warns you to see through polished behavior when the motive is selfish gain.
modern_relevance: A colleague smiles in the meeting and then quietly shifts blame onto you in the email thread. The damage is not just the lie — it's the kind of mind that can live with it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रथम कुमत करि कपटु सँकेला। सो उचाटु सब कें सिर मेला॥ सुरमायाँ सब लोग बिमोहे। राम प्रेम अतिसय न बिछोहे ॥
translation: पहले तो कुमत (बुरा विचार) करके कपट को बटोरा (अनेक प्रकार के कपट का साज सजा)। फिर वह (कपटजनित) उचाट सबके सिर पर डाल दिया। फिर देवमाया से सब लोगों को विशेष रूप से मोहित कर दिया, किन्तु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्रेम से उनका अत्यन्त बिछोह नहीं हुआ (अर्थात उनका श्री रामजी के प्रति प्रेम कुछ तो बना ही रहा) ॥
english_translation: First, they gathered crooked intentions and deceit. Then they spread that restless unease over everyone’s head. By the power of illusion, they bewildered all people, yet their love for Ram Chandr did not break completely.
essence: Illusion can cloud everyone, but love for Ram still survives.
simple_meaning: Deceit and confusion spread across everyone, and people were deeply bewildered. Even so, their love for Ram was not completely destroyed.
insight: It shows how confusion can distort judgment without fully erasing the heart's deepest attachment.
modern_relevance: A rumor spreads through a family group chat, and suddenly everyone is upset, suspicious, and half-lost in fear. Even then, the deepest loyalties do not disappear overnight.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भय उचाट बस मन थिर नाहीं। छन बन रुचि छन सदन सोहाहीं॥ दुबिध मनोगति प्रजा दुखारी। सरित सिंधु संगम जनु बारी ॥
translation: भय और उचाट के वश किसी का मन स्थिर नहीं है। क्षण में उनकी वन में रहने की इच्छा होती है और क्षण में उन्हें घर अच्छे लगने लगते हैं। मन की इस प्रकार की दुविधामयी स्थिति से प्रजा दुःखी हो रही है। मानो नदी और समुद्र के संगम का जल क्षुब्ध हो रहा हो। (जैसे नदी और समुद्र के संगम का जल स्थिर नहीं रहता, कभी इधर आता और कभी उधर जाता है, उसी प्रकार की दशा प्रजा के मन की हो गई) ॥
english_translation: Under fear and agitation, the mind cannot stay steady. One moment it likes the forest, the next it finds the home beautiful. The people suffer from this divided state of mind, like water stirred at the meeting of a river and the sea.
essence: Fear turns the mind into a place with no rest.
simple_meaning: Fear and agitation make people indecisive. Their minds keep swinging between two choices, and that inner split itself becomes suffering.
insight: It shifts attention from the external choice to the inner instability making every choice painful.
modern_relevance: You keep refreshing the message thread, then deleting your reply, then typing again. Fear has split your mind, and even small choices start to hurt.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दुचित कतहुँ परितोषु न लहहीं। एक एक सन मरमु न कहहीं॥ लखि हियँ हँसि कह कृपानिधानू। सरिस स्वान मघवान जुबानू ॥
translation: चित्त दो तरफा हो जाने से वे कहीं संतोष नहीं पाते और एक-दूसरे से अपना मर्म भी नहीं कहते। कृपानिधान श्री रामचन्द्रजी यह दशा देखकर हृदय में हँसकर कहने लगे- कुत्ता, इन्द्र और नवयुवक (कामी पुरुष) एक सरीखे (एक ही स्वभाव के) हैं। (पाणिनीय व्याकरण के अनुसार, श्वन, युवन और मघवन शब्दों के रूप भी एक सरीखे होते हैं) ॥
english_translation: Because their minds are split in two, they find no satisfaction anywhere, and they do not tell one another their real feelings. Seeing this, the treasure of compassion laughed in his heart and said, "A dog, Indra, and a lustful youth are alike."
essence: A divided mind cannot settle or tell the truth.
simple_meaning: A divided mind cannot feel settled or honest. Ram sees this inner split and points out how restless, secretive, and unsatisfied it makes people.
insight: It shifts attention from outer confusion to the inner split that produces it.
modern_relevance: You draft three versions of the same text message, then delete all of them because none feels safe to send. That hesitation is what a split mind looks like: no rest, no honesty, no ease.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: भरतु जनकु मुनिजन सचिव साधु सचेत बिहाइ। लागि देवमाया सबहि जथाजोगु जनु पाइ ॥
translation: भरतजी, जनकजी, मुनिजन, मंत्री और ज्ञानी साधु-संतों को छोड़कर अन्य सभी पर जिस मनुष्य को जिस योग्य (जिस प्रकृति और जिस स्थिति का) पाया, उस पर वैसे ही देवमाया लग गई ॥
english_translation: Except for Bharata, Janaka, the sages, ministers, and wise saints, divine illusion fell on everyone according to each person's nature and capacity.
essence: Illusion lands where awareness is weak.
simple_meaning: Divine illusion affects people differently, finding each person according to their nature and vulnerability. Only the truly aware, like Bharata and the wise, remain untouched.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the condition of the mind receiving it.
modern_relevance: A rumor spreads through a family WhatsApp group and each person reacts differently — panic, anger, denial, blame. The same event does not enter every mind the same way; your inner state decides what takes hold.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कृपासिंधु लखि लोग दुखारे। निज सनेहँ सुरपति छल भारे॥ सभा राउ गुर महिसुर मंत्री। भरत भगति सब कै मति जंत्री ॥
translation: कृपासिंधु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने लोगों को अपने स्नेह और देवराज इन्द्र के भारी छल से दुःखी देखा। सभा, राजा जनक, गुरु, ब्राह्मण और मंत्री आदि सभी की बुद्धि को भरतजी की भक्ति ने कील दिया ॥
english_translation: The ocean of compassion saw the people suffering, weighed down by their own love and by Indra's deep deceit. In the assembly, the king, the teacher, the learned men, and the ministers all stood fixed by Bharat's devotion.
essence: Devotion can steady even the most divided minds.
simple_meaning: Ram sees the people's pain and the weight of deceit around them. Bharat's devotion is so strong that it leaves everyone silent and fixed in reverence.
insight: It shifts attention from status and argument to the quiet authority of selfless devotion.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family meeting where everyone has an opinion and no one is listening. Then one person's steady loyalty changes the room. That is the force Bharat carries here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामहि चितवत चित्र लिखे से। सकुचत बोलत बचन सिखे से॥ भरत प्रीति नति बिनय बड़ाई। सुनत सुखद बरनत कठिनाई ॥
translation: सब लोग चित्रलिखे से श्री रामचन्द्रजी की ओर देख रहे हैं। सकुचाते हुए सिखाए हुए से वचन बोलते हैं। भरतजी की प्रीति, नम्रता, विनय और बड़ाई सुनने में सुख देने वाली है, पर उसका वर्णन करने में कठिनता है ॥
english_translation: Everyone looks at Ram as if they were painted still; they speak with the hesitation of people who have been taught. Bharat's love, humility, reverence, and greatness are sweet to hear, but hard to describe.
essence: True devotion makes even praise feel too small.
simple_meaning: Everyone is so moved by Ram that they look almost frozen and speak carefully. Bharat's love, humility, and greatness are beautiful to hear, but beyond full description.
insight: It shifts attention from explaining devotion to recognising its quiet force.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence changes the room, and suddenly everyone speaks more softly. Some people are so sincere that your usual labels feel too small for them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जासु बिलोकि भगति लवलेसू। प्रेम मगन मुनिगन मिथिलेसू॥ महिमा तासु कहै किमि तुलसी। भगति सुभायँ सुमति हियँ हुलसी ॥
translation: जिनकी भक्ति का लवलेश देखकर मुनिगण और मिथिलेश्वर जनकजी प्रेम में मग्न हो गए, उन भरतजी की महिमा तुलसीदास कैसे कहे? उनकी भक्ति और सुंदर भाव से (कवि के) हृदय में सुबुद्धि हुलस रही है (विकसित हो रही है) ॥
english_translation: Just a glimpse of his devotion sent sages and even Janak into loving rapture. How can Tulsidas describe Bharat's greatness? His devoted nature itself makes wisdom bloom in the heart.
essence: A single glimpse of devotion can transform everyone around it.
simple_meaning: Bharat's devotion is so deep that even great sages and Janak are moved by it. Tulsidas says his praise is beyond words, because such devotion naturally awakens wisdom in the heart.
insight: It shifts attention from performance to the power of lived devotion.
modern_relevance: You watch someone care for an ailing parent without complaint, and the whole room softens. Their love needs no speech; it teaches everyone present what depth looks like.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: आपु छोटि महिमा बड़ि जानी। कबिकुल कानि मानि सकुचानी॥ कहि न सकति गुन रुचि अधिकाई। मति गति बाल बचन की नाई ॥
translation: परन्तु वह बुद्धि अपने को छोटी और भरतजी की महिमा को बड़ी जानकर कवि परम्परा की मर्यादा को मानकर सकुचा गई (उसका वर्णन करने का साहस नहीं कर सकी)। उसकी गुणों में रुचि तो बहुत है, पर उन्हें कह नहीं सकती। बुद्धि की गति बालक के वचनों की तरह हो गई (वह कुण्ठित हो गई)! ॥
english_translation: Knowing herself small and Bharata's greatness vast, the poet's mind grew shy out of respect for poetic tradition. Her delight in his virtues is so great that she cannot fully speak them; her thinking falters like a child's words.
essence: True greatness can make even praise fall silent.
simple_meaning: The poet feels too small to fully describe Bharata's greatness, so she falls silent out of respect and awe.
insight: It teaches humility before genuine virtue: instead of forcing grand language, the mind bows and lets greatness remain greater than speech.
modern_relevance: You try to describe the friend who showed up when everyone else vanished, and your words suddenly feel thin. Some goodness is so large that praise itself becomes shy.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भरत बिमल जसु बिमल बिधु सुमति चकोरकुमारि। उदित बिमल जन हृदय नभ एकटक रही निहारि ॥
translation: भरतजी का निर्मल यश निर्मल चन्द्रमा है और कवि की सुबुद्धि चकोरी है, जो भक्तों के हृदय रूपी निर्मल आकाश में उस चन्द्रमा को उदित देखकर उसकी ओर टकटकी लगाए देखती ही रह गई है (तब उसका वर्णन कौन करे?) ॥
english_translation: Bharat’s spotless fame is a spotless moon, and the poet’s good sense is a chakor bird. Seeing that moon rise in the pure sky of devotees’ hearts, it keeps staring without blinking.
essence: True greatness leaves even praise speechless.
simple_meaning: Bharat’s pure fame is compared to a moon, and the poet’s mind is like a bird that can only stare at it in wonder.
insight: It shifts praise from explanation to reverent witnessing, showing that some virtue can only be admired, not fully captured.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who quietly carried everyone else’s burden and never asked for credit. Words feel clumsy, and admiration turns into silence.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भरत सुभाउ न सुगम निगमहूँ। लघु मति चापलता कबि छमहूँ॥ कहत सुनत सति भाउ भरत को। सीय राम पद होइ न रत को ॥
translation: भरतजी के स्वभाव का वर्णन वेदों के लिए भी सुगम नहीं है। (अतः) मेरी तुच्छ बुद्धि की चंचलता को कवि लोग क्षमा करें! भरतजी के सद्भाव को कहते-सुनते कौन मनुष्य श्री सीता-रामजी के चरणों में अनुरक्त न हो जाएगा ॥
english_translation: Bharat's nature is hard to grasp even for the Vedas. Let the poet's small mind be forgiven for its wavering. Who could hear or speak of Bharat's noble heart and not become devoted to the feet of Sita and Ram?
essence: Bharat's devotion is so pure it makes devotion itself feel natural.
simple_meaning: Bharat's character is so deep that even the Vedas cannot fully describe it. Hearing about his devotion naturally turns the heart toward Sita and Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from clever description to the magnetic power of lived devotion.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who keeps serving quietly while others chase credit. Their steadiness changes the room. Without preaching, they make loyalty feel beautiful and make your own heart want better things.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सुमिरत भरतहि प्रेमु राम को। जेहि न सुलभु तेहि सरिस बाम को॥ देखि दयाल दसा सबही की। राम सुजान जानि जन जी की ॥
translation: भरतजी का स्मरण करने से जिसको श्री रामजी का प्रेम सुलभ न हुआ, उसके समान वाम (अभागा) और कौन होगा? दयालु और सुजान श्री रामजी ने सभी की दशा देखकर और भक्त (भरतजी) के हृदय की स्थिति जानकर, ॥
english_translation: Whoever did not easily receive Ram's love by remembering Bharat is the most unfortunate of all. Seeing everyone's condition with compassion, Ram, wise in the hearts of beings, knew the mind of his devotee.
essence: Bharat's devotion is so pure it should awaken love in you.
simple_meaning: Bharat's devotion is so pure that remembering him should awaken love for Ram. If it does not, something is wrong in the heart. Ram sees everyone's condition and knows the devotee's inner state.
insight: It teaches you to measure your own openness by what devotion in others awakens in you.
modern_relevance: You hear a story of someone who gave up power to honor a promise, and it makes your own excuses feel thin. Some people don't just inspire admiration — they reveal whether your heart is still awake.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: धरम धुरीन धीर नय नागर। सत्य सनेह सील सुख सागर॥ देसु कालु लखि समउ समाजू। नीति प्रीति पालक रघुराजू ॥
translation: धर्मधुरंधर, धीर, नीति में चतुर, सत्य, स्नेह, शील और सुख के समुद्र, नीति और प्रीति के पालन करने वाले श्री रघुनाथजी देश, काल, अवसर और समाज को देखकर, ॥
english_translation: Raghunath is the pillar of dharma, calm, skilled in conduct, and an ocean of truth, affection, character, and joy. He judges the right action by place, time, occasion, and society.
essence: True right action is calm, loving, and perfectly timed.
simple_meaning: Ram is described as the perfect model of steady, wise conduct: truthful, loving, disciplined, and able to judge what fits each situation.
insight: It shifts judgment from rigid rules to wise, timely action shaped by truth and affection.
modern_relevance: You are about to answer a difficult message and you pause, reread it, and notice the person behind the words. Ram's way is that rare mix of firmness and care that keeps a relationship intact.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बोले बचन बानि सरबसु से। हित परिनाम सुनत ससि रसु से॥ तात भरत तुम्ह धरम धुरीना। लोक बेद बिद प्रेम प्रबीना ॥
translation: (तदनुसार) ऐसे वचन बोले जो मानो वाणी के सर्वस्व ही थे, परिणाम में हितकारी थे और सुनने में चन्द्रमा के रस (अमृत) सरीखे थे। (उन्होंने कहा-) हे तात भरत! तुम धर्म की धुरी को धारण करने वाले हो, लोक और वेद दोनों के जानने वाले और प्रेम में प्रवीण हो ॥
english_translation: He spoke words that were the very essence of speech, beneficial in their outcome and sweet as moonlit nectar to hear. “Dear Bharat, you uphold the weight of dharma. You know both worldly conduct and the Vedas, and you are skilled in love.”
essence: True speech helps, soothes, and still carries moral weight.
simple_meaning: Kind, wise speech can be both helpful and beautiful. Bharat is praised as someone who carries dharma, understands life and scripture, and knows how to love well.
insight: It teaches you to make speech useful, gentle, and rooted in discernment.
modern_relevance: You’re drafting a message to someone hurting, and every sentence matters. This verse reminds you that the best words are not just correct — they also heal, steady, and reveal your character.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करम बचन मानस बिमल तुम्ह समान तुम्ह तात। गुर समाज लघु बंधु गुन कुसमयँ किमि कहि जात ॥
translation: हे तात! कर्म से, वचन से और मन से निर्मल तुम्हारे समान तुम्हीं हो। गुरुजनों के समाज में और ऐसे कुसमय में छोटे भाई के गुण किस तरह कहे जा सकते हैं? ॥
english_translation: O dear one, only you are pure in deed, word, and mind like this. In the presence of elders and at such an untimely moment, how can a younger brother's virtues be spoken of?
essence: Purity does not boast; it yields to the rightness of the moment.
simple_meaning: You are pure in action, speech, and mind. In front of elders, and at this bad moment, your younger brother's virtues cannot even be properly spoken of.
insight: It shifts attention from self-display to rightful modesty and respect for the moment.
modern_relevance: You’re being praised in a room full of seniors after a crisis, and you know the compliment belongs elsewhere. The honest response is not to inflate yourself, but to step back with grace.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जानहु तात तरनि कुल रीती। सत्यसंध पितु कीरति प्रीती॥ समउ समाजु लाज गुरजन की। उदासीन हित अनहित मन की ॥
translation: हे तात! तुम सूर्यकुल की रीति को, सत्यप्रतिज्ञ पिताजी की कीर्ति और प्रीति को, समय, समाज और गुरुजनों की लज्जा (मर्यादा) को तथा उदासीन, मित्र और शत्रु सबके मन की बात को जानते हो ॥
english_translation: You know the customs of the solar line, your father's vow and honor, the needs of the time and company, the respect owed to elders, and the thoughts of friends and foes alike.
essence: Real duty sees the whole field before it speaks.
simple_meaning: Bharat reminds the listener that he understands family duty, public respect, timing, and the feelings of others.
insight: It shifts the mind from private impulse to a larger sense of duty, timing, and responsibility.
modern_relevance: You are about to send a message that could change a family relationship forever. Before you hit send, you already know how your words will land, what they owe the moment, and what honor requires.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: तुम्हहि बिदित सबही कर करमू। आपन मोर परम हित धरमू॥ मोहि सब भाँति भरोस तुम्हारा। तदपि कहउँ अवसर अनुसारा ॥
translation: तुमको सबके कर्मों (कर्तव्यों) का और अपने तथा मेरे परम हितकारी धर्म का पता है। यद्यपि मुझे तुम्हारा सब प्रकार से भरोसा है, तथापि मैं समय के अनुसार कुछ कहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: You know everyone’s duties, and you know what serves our highest good. I trust you completely, yet I still speak according to the moment.
essence: Complete trust still speaks with restraint.
simple_meaning: Bharat says Ram already knows everyone’s responsibilities and what is best for both of them. Even with complete trust, he speaks carefully according to the situation.
insight: It teaches you to pair deep trust with measured speech, instead of speaking carelessly just because the bond is strong.
modern_relevance: You already know your partner understands the issue, but you still choose your words carefully before bringing it up. Trust and timing can live together.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: तात तात बिनु बात हमारी। केवल गुरकुल कृपाँ सँभारी॥ नतरु प्रजा परिजन परिवारू। हमहि सहित सबु होत खुआरू ॥
translation: हे तात! पिताजी के बिना (उनकी अनुपस्थिति में) हमारी बात केवल गुरुवंश की कृपा ने ही सम्हाल रखी है, नहीं तो हमारे समेत प्रजा, कुटुम्ब, परिवार सभी बर्बाद हो जाते ॥
english_translation: Father, without Father, our words have only been held together by the grace of the guru's line. Otherwise, with us included, all the people, relatives, and family would have been ruined.
essence: One steady presence can hold a whole family together.
simple_meaning: Bharat says that without his father, only the guru's grace has kept their affairs from falling apart. Without that support, the whole family and people would have been ruined.
insight: It shifts attention from personal drama to the stabilising force that quietly holds a community together.
modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after the one person who always settles arguments is gone. Everyone feels the strain. This verse names how much order can depend on one steady, principled presence.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जौं बिनु अवसर अथवँ दिनेसू। जग केहि कहहु न होइ कलेसू॥ तस उतपातु तात बिधि कीन्हा। मुनि मिथिलेस राखि सबु लीन्हा ॥
translation: यदि बिना समय के (सन्ध्या से पूर्व ही) सूर्य अस्त हो जाए, तो कहो जगत में किस को क्लेश न होगा? हे तात! उसी प्रकार का उत्पात विधाता ने यह (पिता की असामयिक मृत्यु) किया है। पर मुनि महाराज ने तथा मिथिलेश्वर ने सबको बचा लिया ॥
english_translation: If the sun were to set before its proper time, who in the world would not suffer? In the same way, fate has caused this untimely disaster. Yet the sage and the king of Mithila have protected everyone.
essence: Untimely loss feels cosmic, but steady hands can still protect everyone.
simple_meaning: An untimely death is compared to the sun setting too early: it throws the whole world into distress. Yet wise people and the king of Mithila have protected everyone from the full fallout.
insight: It shifts attention from the shock itself to the stabilising role of those who can hold others through it.
modern_relevance: A family gets the call at 6 a.m. that someone died unexpectedly, and the whole day tilts sideways. One calm person starts making the calls, arranging travel, and keeping everyone from unraveling.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: राज काज सब लाज पति धरम धरनि धन धाम। गुर प्रभाउ पालिहि सबहि भल होइहि परिनाम ॥
translation: राज्य का सब कार्य, लज्जा, प्रतिष्ठा, धर्म, पृथ्वी, धन, घर- इन सभी का पालन (रक्षण) गुरुजी का प्रभाव (सामर्थ्य) करेगा और परिणाम शुभ होगा ॥
english_translation: The care of the kingdom, honor, duty, the earth, wealth, and home will all be upheld by the guru's grace, and the result will be good.
essence: Grace can uphold what duty alone cannot.
simple_meaning: Guru's grace can protect every part of life — duty, reputation, home, wealth, and order — and lead things to a good result.
insight: It shifts responsibility from anxious control to trust in a sustaining influence beyond your own effort.
modern_relevance: You're trying to keep a family crisis from falling apart while answering messages, paying bills, and staying composed in front of everyone. This verse reminds you that steadiness does not come only from force; it can come from guidance and grace.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सहित समाज तुम्हार हमारा। घर बन गुर प्रसाद रखवारा॥ मातु पिता गुर स्वामि निदेसू। सकल धरम धरनीधर सेसू ॥
translation: गुरुजी का प्रसाद (अनुग्रह) ही घर में और वन में समाज सहित तुम्हारा और हमारा रक्षक है। माता, पिता, गुरु और स्वामी की आज्ञा (का पालन) समस्त धर्म रूपी पृथ्वी को धारण करने में शेषजी के समान है ॥
english_translation: Your guru's grace protects both your home and your forest life, with all your people around you. Obeying mother, father, guru, and master is like Shesha bearing the earth of all dharma.
essence: Rightful obedience carries the whole burden of dharma.
simple_meaning: A person's safety and right conduct come from following the guidance of guru, parents, and rightful authority. That obedience supports life the way Shesha supports the earth.
insight: It shifts attention from personal preference to responsible alignment with rightful guidance.
modern_relevance: You are torn between your manager's deadline, your parents' expectations, and your own plans for the weekend. This verse asks you to see obligation not as a burden alone, but as the structure that keeps life from collapsing.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सो तुम्ह करहु करावहु मोहू। तात तरनिकुल पालक होहू॥ साधक एक सकल सिधि देनी। कीरति सुगति भूतिमय बेनी ॥
translation: हे तात! तुम वही करो और मुझसे भी कराओ तथा सूर्यकुल के रक्षक बनो। साधक के लिए यह एक ही (आज्ञा पालन रूपी साधना) सम्पूर्ण सिद्धियों की देने वाली, कीर्तिमयी, सद्गतिमयी और ऐश्वर्यमयी त्रिवेणी है ॥
english_translation: Do that and make me do it too, dear one. Be the protector of the solar dynasty. For the seeker, this one discipline gives every success: fame, a blessed end, and a river of prosperity.
essence: Right action carries its own reward and preserves your honour.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks the listener to act in the right way and help him do the same. He says serving one’s duty brings success, good name, and a blessed outcome.
insight: It shifts action from reward-seeking to faithful responsibility, treating duty itself as the source of success.
modern_relevance: Your parent asks you to step up when the family is strained, and you know there will be no applause. You do it anyway, because some responsibilities quietly build the whole life.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: सो बिचारि सहि संकटु भारी। करहु प्रजा परिवारू सुखारी॥ बाँटी बिपति सबहिं मोहि भाई। तुम्हहि अवधि भरि बड़ि कठिनाई ॥
translation: इसे विचारकर भारी संकट सहकर भी प्रजा और परिवार को सुखी करो। हे भाई! मेरी विपत्ति सभी ने बाँट ली है, परन्तु तुमको तो अवधि (चौदह वर्ष) तक बड़ी कठिनाई है (सबसे अधिक दुःख है) ॥
english_translation: Thinking this over, endure the heavy hardship and keep the people and family happy. Brother, everyone has shared my suffering, but you must bear the far greater pain for the full fourteen years.
essence: True duty is carrying the heavier burden so others can live in peace.
simple_meaning: Even in a hard situation, you should keep the people around you safe and steady. Your own burden may be greater, but your role is to hold the family and community together.
insight: It shifts duty from self-protection to protective responsibility for others.
modern_relevance: You are the one holding the family together after the bad news, answering calls, calming relatives, and making sure the children still eat. This verse honours the person who carries the hidden weight so others can breathe.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जानि तुम्हहि मृदु कहउँ कठोरा। कुसमयँ तात न अनुचित मोरा॥ होहिं कुठायँ सुबंधु सहाए। ओड़िअहिं हाथ असनिहु के धाए ॥
translation: तुमको कोमल जानकर भी मैं कठोर (वियोग की बात) कह रहा हूँ। हे तात! बुरे समय में मेरे लिए यह कोई अनुचित बात नहीं है। कुठौर (कुअवसर) में श्रेष्ठ भाई ही सहायक होते हैं। वज्र के आघात भी हाथ से ही रोके जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Knowing you to be gentle, I speak this harsh truth. In a bad time, this is not improper, dear one. In a crisis, only a true brother helps; a hand alone stops a lightning strike.
essence: True care sometimes sounds harsh because crisis needs honesty, not comfort alone.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he is speaking painfully but honestly because difficult times call for clear support, not softness alone. In a crisis, a true brother protects you.
insight: It teaches you to pair tenderness with truth, especially when someone is already under pressure.
modern_relevance: You sit beside a friend after a breakup and tell them the part they do not want to hear. They need comfort, yes — but they also need someone brave enough to be honest.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: सेवक कर पद नयन से मुख सो साहिबु होइ। तुलसी प्रीति कि रीति सुनि सुकबि सराहहिं सोइ ॥
translation: सेवक हाथ, पैर और नेत्रों के समान और स्वामी मुख के समान होना चाहिए। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि सेवक-स्वामी की ऐसी प्रीति की रीति सुनकर सुकवि उसकी सराहना करते हैं ॥
english_translation: A servant should be like hands, feet, and eyes, and the master like the face. Tulsidas says that hearing this way of love between servant and master, even wise poets praise it.
essence: Love is proven by becoming useful to the one you cherish.
simple_meaning: A true servant lives for the master's needs, like hands, feet, and eyes serving the face. Love is shown through useful, selfless service.
insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to embodied service in daily life.
modern_relevance: You answer your mother's call before she finishes the sentence. You don't need applause for that. This verse honours the kind of love that moves first and serves quietly.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सभा सकल सुनि रघुबर बानी। प्रेम पयोधि अमिअँ जनु सानी॥ सिथिल समाज सनेह समाधी। देखि दसा चुप सारद साधी ॥
translation: रघुनाथजी की वाणी सुनकर, जो मानो प्रेम रूपी समुद्र के (मंथन से निकले हुए) अमृत में सनी हुई थी, सारा समाज शिथिल हो गया, सबको प्रेम समाधि लग गई। यह दशा देखकर सरस्वती ने चुप साध ली ॥
english_translation: Hearing Raghubar's words, the whole gathering was as if stirred into nectar from the sea of love. Seeing their state, even Saraswati fell silent.
essence: True affection can silence even the need to speak.
simple_meaning: Ram's words fill the gathering with such love that everyone becomes quiet and absorbed. Even Saraswati, the goddess of speech, falls silent before that scene.
insight: It shifts attention from clever speech to speech that carries genuine feeling.
modern_relevance: You say one honest sentence in a tense family room, and the argument stops mid-breath. Not because you won, but because your care landed before your logic did.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरतहि भयउ परम संतोषू। सनमुख स्वामि बिमुख दुख दोषू॥ मुख प्रसन्न मन मिटा बिषादू। भा जनु गूँगेहि गिरा प्रसादू ॥
translation: भरतजी को परम संतोष हुआ। स्वामी के सम्मुख (अनुकूल) होते ही उनके दुःख और दोषों ने मुँह मोड़ लिया (वे उन्हें छोड़कर भाग गए)। उनका मुख प्रसन्न हो गया और मन का विषाद मिट गया। मानो गूँगे पर सरस्वती की कृपा हो गई हो ॥
english_translation: Bharat felt complete contentment. When he stood before his lord, grief and fault turned away. His face brightened and sorrow left his mind, as if speech itself had been granted to the mute.
essence: Being before the beloved dissolves grief.
simple_meaning: Bharat finds peace the moment he comes face to face with his lord. His sorrow leaves, his face brightens, and he feels unexpectedly blessed.
insight: It shifts attention from internal distress to the healing power of loving presence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room after days of dread, and the person you came to see smiles first. Something in you unclenches before any words are spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कीन्ह सप्रेम प्रनामु बहोरी। बोले पानि पंकरुह जोरी॥ नाथ भयउ सुखु साथ गए को। लहेउँ लाहु जग जनमु भए को ॥
translation: उन्होंने फिर प्रेमपूर्वक प्रणाम किया और करकमलों को जोड़कर वे बोले- हे नाथ! मुझे आपके साथ जाने का सुख प्राप्त हो गया और मैंने जगत में जन्म लेने का लाभ भी पा लिया।3॥
english_translation: He bowed again with love and, palms joined, said: “Lord, I have found the joy of going with you, and I have gained the true benefit of being born in this world.”
essence: Being with Ram is the highest gain life can give.
simple_meaning: Bharat bows again and says that being with Ram is the real joy and the real reward of being born.
insight: It reorders desire around presence, so the mind stops chasing status and starts valuing sacred company.
modern_relevance: You finally sit beside the friend who showed up when everything fell apart. No grand solution appears, but something in you settles: being with them was the point all along.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: अब कृपाल जस आयसु होई। करौं सीस धरि सादर सोई॥ सो अवलंब देव मोहि देई। अवधि पारु पावौं जेहि सेई ॥
translation: हे कृपालु! अब जैसी आज्ञा हो, उसी को मैं सिर पर धर कर आदरपूर्वक करूँ! परन्तु देव! आप मुझे वह अवलम्बन (कोई सहारा) दें, जिसकी सेवा कर मैं अवधि का पार पा जाऊँ (अवधि को बिता दूँ) ॥
english_translation: O gracious one, whatever you command now, I will place on my head and do with reverence. But, O divine one, give me some support to serve, by which I may pass this time.
essence: Surrender can include asking for the strength to keep serving.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he will obey whatever command comes, but he asks for some support so he can keep serving until the waiting period ends.
insight: It teaches you to obey without pride and to ask for what helps you keep serving well.
modern_relevance: You’ve agreed to help through a hard season, but you’re exhausted and need a steadying hand. Bharat shows that asking for support does not weaken loyalty; it makes service sustainable.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: देव देव अभिषेक हित गुर अनुसासनु पाइ। आनेउँ सब तीरथ सलिलु तेहि कहँ काह रजाइ ॥
translation: हे देव! स्वामी (आप) के अभिषेक के लिए गुरुजी की आज्ञा पाकर मैं सब तीर्थों का जल लेता आया हूँ, उसके लिए क्या आज्ञा होती है? ॥
english_translation: O divine one, for your consecration, having received the teacher's command, I have brought water from all the sacred places. What further command is there for me?
essence: Service asks for the next task, not the reward.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he has brought water from all holy places for Ram's consecration, following his teacher's command, and asks what else he should do.
insight: It shifts attention from self-display to obedient service: do the needed work, then wait for the next right step.
modern_relevance: You finish the job no one else wanted, then ask, 'What next?' without needing credit. That is Bharat's way of serving.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: एकु मनोरथु बड़ मन माहीं। सभयँ सकोच जात कहि नाहीं॥ कहहु तात प्रभु आयसु पाई। बोले बानि सनेह सुहाई ॥
translation: मेरे मन में एक और बड़ा मनोरथ है, जो भय और संकोच के कारण कहा नहीं जाता। (श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने कहा-) हे भाई! कहो। तब प्रभु की आज्ञा पाकर भरतजी स्नेहपूर्ण सुंदर वाणी बोले- ॥
english_translation: I have one more great wish in my heart, but fear and hesitation keep me from saying it. Then, after receiving the Lord's permission, Bharat spoke in sweet, loving words.
essence: Love becomes deeper when it waits for permission.
simple_meaning: Bharat has another deep wish, but he is too humble and afraid to say it until Ram invites him to speak.
insight: It teaches you to let devotion speak only after humility has opened the door.
modern_relevance: You have something important to ask, but you wait until the other person is ready to hear it. That restraint can be its own form of love.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: चित्रकूट सुचि थल तीरथ बन। खग मृग सर सरि निर्झर गिरिगन॥ प्रभु पद अंकित अवनि बिसेषी। आयसु होइ त आवौं देखी ॥
translation: आज्ञा हो तो चित्रकूट के पवित्र स्थान, तीर्थ, वन, पक्षी-पशु, तालाब-नदी, झरने और पर्वतों के समूह तथा विशेष कर प्रभु (आप) के चरण चिह्नों से अंकित भूमि को देख आऊँ ॥
english_translation: If you allow it, I would like to go see Chitrakut’s pure holy places, forests, birds and animals, ponds, rivers, streams, and mountains—especially the land marked by your feet.
essence: A place becomes sacred when it bears the trace of the beloved.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks for permission to visit Chitrakut and see the sacred land where Ram’s footprints are found.
insight: It shifts attention from the place itself to what makes the place meaningful: presence, memory, and devotion.
modern_relevance: You visit a place because someone you love once walked there. The street, the park, even the quiet stones feel different because they carry that trace.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: अवसि अत्रि आयसु सिर धरहू। तात बिगतभय कानन चरहू॥ मुनि प्रसाद बनु मंगल दाता। पावन परम सुहावन भ्राता ॥
translation: (श्री रघुनाथजी बोले-) अवश्य ही अत्रि ऋषि की आज्ञा को सिर पर धारण करो (उनसे पूछकर वे जैसा कहें वैसा करो) और निर्भय होकर वन में विचरो। हे भाई! अत्रि मुनि के प्रसाद से वन मंगलों का देने वाला, परम पवित्र और अत्यन्त सुंदर है- ॥
english_translation: Certainly honor the command of Atri and go fearlessly into the forest. Brother, by the sage's grace the forest is a giver of blessings, supremely pure, and very beautiful.
essence: Fearless action begins when you bow to wise guidance.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Bharat to respect Atri's instruction and move through the forest without fear, because the sage's blessing makes the forest pure and auspicious.
insight: It shifts the mind from fear of the setting to trust in right instruction.
modern_relevance: You step into a situation that feels uncertain — a new city, a difficult family visit, a decision you don't fully control. The right counsel steadies you, and the place stops feeling hostile.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: रिषिनायकु जहँ आयसु देहीं। राखेहु तीरथ जलु थल तेहीं॥ सुनि प्रभु बचन भरत सुखु पावा। मुनि पद कमल मुदित सिरु नावा ॥
translation: और ऋषियों के प्रमुख अत्रिजी जहाँ आज्ञा दें, वहीं (लाया हुआ) तीर्थों का जल स्थापित कर देना। प्रभु के वचन सुनकर भरतजी ने सुख पाया और आनंदित होकर मुनि अत्रिजी के चरणकमलों में सिर नवाया ॥
english_translation: And wherever the chief sage Atri gives instruction, place the sacred water and the ritual offerings there. Hearing the Lord's words, Bharata felt joy and bowed his head, delighted, at the sage's lotus feet.
essence: Obedience becomes joy when the instruction is righteous.
simple_meaning: Bharata is told to place the sacred water wherever the sage instructs, and he gladly bows in gratitude when he hears Ram's words.
insight: It teaches you to treat right guidance as a gift, not an interruption.
modern_relevance: You're setting up something important and someone wiser than you changes the plan. Instead of resisting, you feel the ease that comes from trusting good direction.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत राम संबादु सुनि सकल सुमंगल मूल। सुर स्वारथी सराहि कुल बरषत सुरतरु फूल ॥
translation: समस्त सुंदर मंगलों का मूल भरतजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी का संवाद सुनकर स्वार्थी देवता रघुकुल की सराहना करके कल्पवृक्ष के फूल बरसाने लगे ॥
english_translation: Hearing the dialogue between Bharat and Ram, the root of all auspiciousness, the self-interested devas praised the Raghu line and showered flowers from the kalpa tree.
essence: Pure brotherly love becomes a blessing the whole world can recognize.
simple_meaning: Bharat and Ram speak with such goodness that even the devas celebrate the Raghu family and shower flowers.
insight: It shifts attention from dramatic events to the moral beauty of how people treat each other.
modern_relevance: You watch two siblings choose love over status, and the room changes. Even people with hidden agendas can feel the force of a clean, selfless exchange.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धन्य भरत जय राम गोसाईं। कहत देव हरषत बरिआईं॥ मुनि मिथिलेस सभाँ सब काहू। भरत बचन सुनि भयउ उछाहू ॥
translation: 'भरतजी धन्य हैं, स्वामी श्री रामजी की जय हो!' ऐसा कहते हुए देवता बलपूर्वक (अत्यधिक) हर्षित होने लगे। भरतजी के वचन सुनकर मुनि वशिष्ठजी, मिथिलापति जनकजी और सभा में सब किसी को बड़ा उत्साह (आनंद) हुआ ॥
english_translation: ‘Blessed is Bharat, victory to Ram, the Lord of the world!’ Saying this, the devas became deeply joyful. Hearing Bharat’s words, the sage, King Janak, and everyone in the assembly felt great delight.
essence: Bharat’s devotion makes everyone else rejoice too.
simple_meaning: Bharat’s words of devotion to Ram delight everyone, even the devas. The whole assembly feels uplifted by his praise.
insight: It shifts attention from status to the joy created by sincere praise and humility.
modern_relevance: You say one honest sentence about someone you love, and the whole room softens. Real humility has that effect — it gives everyone permission to feel joy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत राम गुन ग्राम सनेहू। पुलकि प्रसंसत राउ बिदेहू॥ सेवक स्वामि सुभाउ सुहावन। नेमु पेमु अति पावन पावन ॥
translation: भरतजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुण समूह की तथा प्रेम की विदेहराज जनकजी पुलकित होकर प्रशंसा कर रहे हैं। सेवक और स्वामी दोनों का सुंदर स्वभाव है। इनके नियम और प्रेम पवित्र को भी अत्यन्त पवित्र करने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: Janaka, the king of Videha, joyfully praises the bond of love between Bharat and Ram, and the many virtues of both. The servant-and-master relationship between them is beautiful; their discipline and love purify even what is already pure.
essence: Devotion makes hierarchy beautiful instead of heavy.
simple_meaning: Janaka praises Bharat and Ram’s beautiful bond. Their servant-and-master relationship is so full of love and discipline that it makes holiness feel even holier.
insight: It shifts you to see discipline and affection as allies, not opposites.
modern_relevance: You watch two people treat each other with such respect that the whole room changes. No one is performing; one serves, one receives, and the love between them feels cleaner than any rulebook.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मति अनुसार सराहन लागे। सचिव सभासद सब अनुरागे॥ सुनि सुनि राम भरत संबादू। दुहु समाज हियँ हरषु विषादू॥3
translation: मंत्री और सभासद् सभी प्रेममुग्ध होकर अपनी-अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार सराहना करने लगे। श्री रामचन्द्रजी और भरतजी का संवाद सुन-सुनकर दोनों समाजों के हृदयों में हर्ष और विषाद (भरतजी के सेवा धर्म को देखकर हर्ष और रामवियोग की सम्भावना से विषाद) दोनों हुए ॥
english_translation: The ministers and assembly members, all filled with affection, began praising him according to their own understanding. Hearing the dialogue between Ram and Bharat again and again, both gatherings felt joy and sorrow in their hearts.
essence: Love can make everyone glad and heartbroken at once.
simple_meaning: Everyone in both groups is moved by Ram and Bharat's exchange. They praise what they understand, while feeling both joy and sorrow at the same time.
insight: It shows how sincere conduct can lift others without erasing grief. The scene carries both admiration and ache.
modern_relevance: You overhear siblings speaking gently after a family rupture, and everyone nearby goes quiet. Their care feels healing, but it also reminds you what has been lost.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम मातु दुखु सुखु सम जानी। कहि गुन राम प्रबोधीं रानी॥ एक कहहिं रघुबीर बड़ाई। एक सराहत भरत भलाई ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की माता कौसल्याजी ने दुःख और सुख को समान जानकर श्री रामजी के गुण कहकर दूसरी रानियों को धैर्य बँधाया। कोई श्री रामजी की बड़ाई (बड़प्पन) की चर्चा कर रहे हैं, तो कोई भरतजी के अच्छेपन की सराहना करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing sorrow and joy as equal, Kaushalya comforted the queens by speaking of Ram's virtues. Some praised the greatness of Raghubir, while others praised Bharat's goodness.
essence: Sorrow eases when you remember the goodness still standing beside it.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya steadies the grieving queens by speaking of Ram's virtues. In the same gathering, some admire Ram's greatness and others praise Bharat's goodness.
insight: It shifts attention from raw hurt to the qualities that can still hold a family together.
modern_relevance: At a family gathering after bad news, someone quietly changes the room by speaking of what is still good in each person. That doesn't erase the pain, but it keeps the heart from hardening.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अत्रि कहेउ तब भरत सन सैल समीप सुकूप। राखिअ तीरथ तोय तहँ पावन अमिअ अनूप ॥
translation: तब अत्रिजी ने भरतजी से कहा- इस पर्वत के समीप ही एक सुंदर कुआँ है। इस पवित्र, अनुपम और अमृत जैसे तीर्थजल को उसी में स्थापित कर दीजिए ॥
english_translation: Then Atri said to Bharat, 'Near this hill is a lovely well. Place this sacred, unmatched, nectar-like pilgrimage water there.'
essence: Precious things also need a proper place.
simple_meaning: Atri points Bharat to a nearby well and asks him to place the sacred water there.
insight: It shifts attention from reverence alone to the practical care that protects what is sacred.
modern_relevance: You carry a bottle of water after a long hike and look for the safest place to set it down. Small acts of care preserve what is precious.
speaker: Atri

verse_text: भरत अत्रि अनुसासन पाई। जल भाजन सब दिए चलाई॥ सानुज आपु अत्रि मुनि साधू। सहित गए जहँ कूप अगाधू ॥
translation: भरतजी ने अत्रिमुनि की आज्ञा पाकर जल के सब पात्र रवाना कर दिए और छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न, अत्रि मुनि तथा अन्य साधु-संतों सहित आप वहाँ गए, जहाँ वह अथाह कुआँ था ॥
english_translation: Having received Atri's instruction, Bharata sent all the water vessels away. Then, with his younger brother Shatrughna, Atri Muni, and the other holy men, he went to the deep well.
essence: True humility turns instruction into immediate service.
simple_meaning: Bharata follows Atri's guidance, clears the vessels, and goes with Shatrughna and the sages to the deep well.
insight: It teaches you to receive guidance quickly and turn it into action without ego or delay.
modern_relevance: You get a clear instruction from someone wiser, and instead of debating it for an hour, you simply make it happen. That kind of clean response keeps a group moving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पावन पाथ पुन्यथल राखा। प्रमुदित प्रेम अत्रि अस भाषा॥ तात अनादि सिद्ध थल एहू। लोपेउ काल बिदित नहिं केहू ॥
translation: और उस पवित्र जल को उस पुण्य स्थल में रख दिया। तब अत्रि ऋषि ने प्रेम से आनंदित होकर ऐसा कहा- हे तात! यह अनादि सिद्धस्थल है। कालक्रम से यह लोप हो गया था, इसलिए किसी को इसका पता नहीं था ॥
english_translation: And the sacred water was placed in that holy site. Then Atri, delighted with love, said, “Dear one, this is an ancient, perfected place. It had been lost over time, so no one knew of it.”
essence: Hidden holiness can survive even when time buries its name.
simple_meaning: Atri rejoices that the sacred water has been restored to an ancient holy place that time had hidden from everyone.
insight: It shifts attention from visible neglect to the deeper sanctity that can remain untouched beneath it.
modern_relevance: You return to a childhood home after years away and feel something still sacred in the cracked walls. Time covered it, but it never erased it.
speaker: Atri

verse_text: तब सेवकन्ह सरस थलुदेखा। कीन्ह सुजल हित कूप बिसेषा॥ बिधि बस भयउ बिस्व उपकारू। सुगम अगम अति धरम बिचारू ॥
translation: तब (भरतजी के) सेवकों ने उस जलयुक्त स्थान को देखा और उस सुंदर (तीर्थों के) जल के लिए एक खास कुआँ बना लिया। दैवयोग से विश्वभर का उपकार हो गया। धर्म का विचार जो अत्यन्त अगम था, वह (इस कूप के प्रभाव से) सुगम हो गया ॥
english_translation: Then the servants saw a water-rich spot and made a special well there for the sacred water. By providence, a blessing for the whole world arose. What is extremely hard to understand about dharma became easy to follow.
essence: A single well can turn difficult duty into shared ease.
simple_meaning: Bharat's servants find a water-rich place and create a special well for pilgrims. What was hard to arrange becomes a blessing for everyone, making a difficult dharmic need easy to meet.
insight: It shifts you from seeing a small practical fix to seeing service that blesses many people.
modern_relevance: A neighborhood volunteers to install a water point near a temple fair, and suddenly elderly visitors, children, and pilgrims all benefit. One careful act quietly makes life easier for everyone.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरतकूप अब कहिहहिं लोगा। अति पावन तीरथ जल जोगा॥ प्रेम सनेम निमज्जत प्रानी। होइहहिं बिमल करम मन बानी ॥
translation: अब इसको लोग भरतकूप कहेंगे। तीर्थों के जल के संयोग से तो यह अत्यन्त ही पवित्र हो गया। इसमें प्रेमपूर्वक नियम से स्नान करने पर प्राणी मन, वचन और कर्म से निर्मल हो जाएँगे ॥
english_translation: People will now call it Bharat's Well. Joined with the waters of holy places, it has become deeply sacred. Anyone who bathes here with love and discipline will become pure in mind, speech, and action.
essence: Love and disciplined devotion make purity possible.
simple_meaning: A well becomes sacred through the waters of holy places, and anyone who bathes there with love and discipline becomes pure in thought, speech, and action.
insight: It shifts attention from outer cleansing alone to the inner state that makes cleansing real.
modern_relevance: You step into a temple after carrying weeks of resentment, and something in you softens. The place matters, but what changes you most is the love and steadiness you bring with you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहत कूप महिमा सकल गए जहाँ रघुराउ। अत्रि सुनायउ रघुबरहि तीरथ पुन्य प्रभाउ ॥
translation: कूप की महिमा कहते हुए सब लोग वहाँ गए जहाँ श्री रघुनाथजी थे। श्री रघुनाथजी को अत्रिजी ने उस तीर्थ का पुण्य प्रभाव सुनाया ॥
english_translation: While speaking of the well’s greatness, everyone went to the place where Raghunath was. Atri then told Raghubar about the sacred power of that holy spot.
essence: Reverence gathers people before the sacred place itself does.
simple_meaning: People gathered around Ram while the greatness of the well and the holiness of the place were being described.
insight: It shifts attention from the object itself to the meaning a community places around it.
modern_relevance: A group stands around a new memorial, passing the story from person to person. The place matters, but the shared reverence is what gives it weight.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहत धरम इतिहास सप्रीती। भयउ भोरु निसि सो सुख बीती॥ नित्य निबाहि भरत दोउ भाई। राम अत्रि गुर आयसु पाई ॥
translation: प्रेमपूर्वक धर्म के इतिहास कहते वह रात सुख से बीत गई और सबेरा हो गया। भरत-शत्रुघ्न दोनों भाई नित्यक्रिया पूरी करके, श्री रामजी, अत्रिजी और गुरु वशिष्ठजी की आज्ञा पाकर, ॥
english_translation: They spent the night happily, talking lovingly about sacred duty and its stories. At dawn, Bharat and Shatrughna completed their morning rites, then received the blessings of Ram, Atri, and Guru Vashistha.
essence: A night of loving remembrance prepares the heart for the next duty.
simple_meaning: The night passed in loving talk about duty and sacred stories. At dawn, Bharat and Shatrughna finished their morning rites and received blessings before moving on.
insight: It places spiritual conversation and daily discipline before action, letting the next step begin from clarity.
modern_relevance: A long night in a quiet guest room, talking with family after a hard decision, can feel strangely light. When the conversation is rooted in what matters, morning arrives without heaviness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सहित समाज साज सब सादें। चले राम बन अटन पयादें॥ कोमल चरन चलत बिनु पनहीं। भइ मृदु भूमि सकुचि मन मनहीं ॥
translation: समाज सहित सब सादे साज से श्री रामजी के वन में भ्रमण (प्रदक्षिणा) करने के लिए पैदल ही चले। कोमल चरण हैं और बिना जूते के चल रहे हैं, यह देखकर पृथ्वी मन ही मन सकुचाकर कोमल हो गई ॥
english_translation: Ram set out barefoot for the forest with the whole company in simple dress. His soft feet touched the ground without shoes, and the earth, shy at heart, became gentle.
essence: Humility can make even exile feel sacred.
simple_meaning: Ram leaves for the forest on foot, dressed simply. His tender feet make even the earth feel shy and soft.
insight: It shifts attention from the fact of leaving to the grace with which you leave.
modern_relevance: You leave home before sunrise with a backpack, no fanfare, and a heavy heart. The way you carry yourself can still make the moment feel sacred.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कुस कंटक काँकरीं कुराईं। कटुक कठोर कुबस्तु दुराईं॥ महि मंजुल मृदु मारग कीन्हे। बहत समीर त्रिबिध सुख लीन्हे ॥
translation: कुश, काँटे, कंकड़ी, दरारों आदि कड़वी, कठोर और बुरी वस्तुओं को छिपाकर पृथ्वी ने सुंदर और कोमल मार्ग कर दिए। सुखों को साथ लिए (सुखदायक) शीतल, मंद, सुगंध हवा चलने लगी ॥
english_translation: Thorns, sharp gravel, roughness, and harsh things were hidden away. The earth made the path lovely and soft, and the wind blew gently, carrying a threefold comfort.
essence: The path softens itself for the one walking in dharma.
simple_meaning: The road becomes soft and pleasant for Ram's walk, as if nature itself removes every rough thing in his way.
insight: It shifts attention from hardship to the quiet support that appears around righteous action.
modern_relevance: You leave home carrying a heavy goodbye, and the street feels strangely quiet, almost kind. Even grief can seem to soften when you walk with the right purpose.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुमन बरषि सुर घन करि छाहीं। बिटप फूलि फलि तृन मृदुताहीं॥ मृग बिलोकि खग बोलि सुबानी। सेवहिं सकल राम प्रिय जानी ॥
translation: रास्ते में देवता फूल बरसाकर, बादल छाया करके, वृक्ष फूल-फलकर, तृण अपनी कोमलता से, मृग (पशु) देखकर और पक्षी सुंदर वाणी बोलकर सभी भरतजी को श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्यारे जानकर उनकी सेवा करने लगे ॥
english_translation: The gods showered flowers and made shade with clouds. Trees blossomed and fruited, grass softened, deer looked on, and birds sang sweetly, all serving Bharat as one dear to Ram.
essence: Pure devotion makes even nature feel like a servant.
simple_meaning: Everything around Bharat responds to him kindly. Flowers fall, shade appears, plants bloom, grass softens, and even animals and birds seem to serve him because he is dear to Ram.
insight: It turns Bharat’s presence into a sign that selfless love changes how the world is experienced.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room carrying no agenda, only love for someone else’s good. Even the atmosphere feels different — softer, kinder, almost welcoming you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुलभ सिद्धि सब प्राकृतहु राम कहत जमुहात। राम प्रानप्रिय भरत कहुँ यह न होइ बड़ि बात ॥
translation: जब एक साधारण मनुष्य को भी (आलस्य से) जँभाई लेते समय 'राम' कह देने से ही सब सिद्धियाँ सुलभ हो जाती हैं, तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्राण प्यारे भरतजी के लिए यह कोई बड़ी (आश्चर्य की) बात नहीं है ॥
english_translation: When even an ordinary person can gain ease by saying Ram while yawning, then for Ram's dearest Bharat, that is no great wonder.
essence: True devotion makes Ram's name feel as natural as breathing.
simple_meaning: Even an ordinary person can find ease by saying Ram's name. For Bharat, who loves Ram more than life itself, this is completely natural.
insight: It shifts remembrance from a practice you force into a love that rises by itself.
modern_relevance: You catch yourself whispering a loved one's name when you're exhausted, and it steadies you without effort. That is the kind of ease Bharat feels with Ram.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: एहि बिधि भरतु फिरत बन माहीं। नेमु प्रेमु लखि मुनि सकुचाहीं॥ पुन्य जलाश्रय भूमि बिभागा। खग मृग तरु तृन गिरि बन बागा ॥
translation: इस प्रकार भरतजी वन में फिर रहे हैं। उनके नियम और प्रेम को देखकर मुनि भी सकुचा जाते हैं। पवित्र जल के स्थान (नदी, बावली, कुंड आदि) पृथ्वी के पृथक-पृथक भाग, पक्षी, पशु, वृक्ष, तृण (घास), पर्वत, वन और बगीचे- ॥
english_translation: In this way Bharat wandered through the forest. His discipline and love made even the sages feel shy. The sacred waters, the separate lands, birds, beasts, trees, grasses, hills, forests, and gardens—
essence: Love held with discipline makes even saints feel humble.
simple_meaning: Bharat wanders through the forest with such disciplined love that even sages feel humbled. The verse then begins listing the sacred and beautiful features of the landscape.
insight: It highlights how disciplined devotion changes the atmosphere around you, even before anyone speaks.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone without asking for credit, and the people around you go quiet. Your consistency speaks louder than praise ever could.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चारु बिचित्र पबित्र बिसेषी। बूझत भरतु दिब्य सब देखी॥ सुनि मन मुदित कहत रिषिराऊ। हेतु नाम गुन पुन्य प्रभाऊ ॥
translation: सभी विशेष रूप से सुंदर, विचित्र, पवित्र और दिव्य देखकर भरतजी पूछते हैं और उनका प्रश्न सुनकर ऋषिराज अत्रिजी प्रसन्न मन से सबके कारण, नाम, गुण और पुण्य प्रभाव को कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing everything as beautiful, wondrous, pure, and divine, Bharata asks. Hearing him, the sage-king speaks with joy about the cause, the name, the qualities, and the power of merit.
essence: Wonder grows when you ask before you assume.
simple_meaning: Bharata looks at the holy places and asks about them. The sage answers happily, explaining their source, names, qualities, and sacred power.
insight: It shifts you from passive seeing to reverent inquiry, where even ordinary places become instructive.
modern_relevance: You stand in a temple courtyard, unsure why each corner matters, and ask the elder beside you. That simple question turns scenery into meaning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कतहुँ निमज्जन कतहुँ प्रनामा। कतहुँ बिलोकत मन अभिरामा॥ कतहुँ बैठि मुनि आयसु पाई। सुमिरत सीय सहित दोउ भाई ॥
translation: भरतजी कहीं स्नान करते हैं, कहीं प्रणाम करते हैं, कहीं मनोहर स्थानों के दर्शन करते हैं और कहीं मुनि अत्रिजी की आज्ञा पाकर बैठकर, सीताजी सहित श्री राम-लक्ष्मण दोनों भाइयों का स्मरण करते हैं ॥ तो इसमें लाभ अधिक और हानि कम प्रतीत हुई, परन्तु रानियों को दुःख-सुख समान ही थे (राम-लक्ष्मण वन में रहें या भरत-शत्रुघ्न, दो पुत्रों का वियोग तो रहेगा ही), यह समझकर वे सब रोने लगीं ॥
english_translation: Bharat moves through the forest, bathing here, bowing there, beholding lovely places, and sitting where the sage permits, remembering Ram and Lakshman with Sita. Seeing this, the queens weep, realizing that loss remains loss whether the sons stay or go.
essence: Sacred routines cannot cancel the pain of separation.
simple_meaning: Bharat spends his time bathing, bowing, looking at holy places, and remembering Ram and Lakshman with Sita. The queens see that whatever happens, separation still hurts.
insight: It shifts attention from outward movement to the deeper fact that grief follows love, not location.
modern_relevance: You can visit every meaningful place, follow every careful ritual, and still feel the same missing person in your chest when you get home.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि सुभाउ सनेहु सुसेवा। देहिं असीस मुदित बनदेवा॥ फिरहिं गएँ दिनु पहर अढ़ाई। प्रभु पद कमल बिलोकहिं आई ॥
translation: भरतजी के स्वभाव, प्रेम और सुंदर सेवाभाव को देखकर वनदेवता आनंदित होकर आशीर्वाद देते हैं। यों घूम-फिरकर ढाई पहर दिन बीतने पर लौट पड़ते हैं और आकर प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणकमलों का दर्शन करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing Bharata's nature, love, and selfless service, the forest spirits gladly give blessings. After wandering for two and a half watches, he returns and again beholds the lotus feet of Lord Raghunatha.
essence: Selfless love earns blessings and keeps turning back to Ram.
simple_meaning: Bharata's loving, selfless conduct wins the blessings of the forest beings, and after wandering for a while he returns to see Ram's feet again.
insight: It highlights how selfless conduct draws goodwill and keeps attention returning to what truly matters.
modern_relevance: You show up for someone with no agenda, no performance, no demand for credit. People feel it. The room softens around that kind of sincerity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखे थल तीरथ सकल भरत पाँच दिन माझ। कहत सुनत हरि हर सुजसु गयउ दिवसु भइ साँझ ॥
translation: भरतजी ने पाँच दिन में सब तीर्थ स्थानों के दर्शन कर लिए। भगवान विष्णु और महादेवजी का सुंदर यश कहते-सुनते वह (पाँचवाँ) दिन भी बीत गया, संध्या हो गई ॥
english_translation: In five days, Bharat visited all the holy places. Speaking and listening to the beautiful fame of Hari and Shiva, the fifth day also passed, and evening fell.
essence: Devotion makes even time feel like worship.
simple_meaning: Bharat spent five days visiting holy places and listening to praises of Hari and Shiva until evening came.
insight: It shifts attention from schedule and distance to reverent presence.
modern_relevance: You spend a whole weekend moving from one sacred place to another, never rushing, never checking the clock. The hours disappear because your attention is fully given.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भोर न्हाइ सबु जुरा समाजू। भरत भूमिसुर तेरहुति राजू॥ भल दिन आजु जानि मन माहीं। रामु कृपाल कहत सकुचाहीं ॥
translation: (अगले छठे दिन) सबेरे स्नान करके भरतजी, ब्राह्मण, राजा जनक और सारा समाज आ जुटा। आज सबको विदा करने के लिए अच्छा दिन है, यह मन में जानकर भी कृपालु श्री रामजी कहने में सकुचा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: At dawn, after bathing, Bharata, the Brahmins, King Janaka, and the whole assembly gathered. Knowing in his heart that today was a good day to send them off, compassionate Ram still felt shy to speak.
essence: Compassion can make the right words hard to say.
simple_meaning: After the morning bath, Bharata, the priests, King Janaka, and everyone gather. Ram knows it is the right day to speak, but he still hesitates out of gentle modesty.
insight: It shows that right action need not be cold; compassion can make even necessary speech feel hesitant.
modern_relevance: You know the meeting should end, the message should be sent, or the goodbye should happen. Even then, your care for people can make the words catch in your throat.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गुर नृप भरत सभा अवलोकी। सकुचि राम फिरि अवनि बिलोकी॥ सील सराहि सभा सब सोची। कहुँ न राम सम स्वामि सँकोची ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने गुरु वशिष्ठजी, राजा जनकजी, भरतजी और सारी सभा की ओर देखा, किन्तु फिर सकुचाकर दृष्टि फेरकर वे पृथ्वी की ओर ताकने लगे। सभा उनके शील की सराहना करके सोचती है कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी के समान संकोची स्वामी कहीं नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Ram looked at Guru Vashishtha, King Janaka, Bharata, and the whole assembly, then, feeling shy, looked down at the ground. The whole assembly praised his humility and thought, "No master is as modest as Ram."
essence: The highest master is the one who stays modest.
simple_meaning: Ram feels shy before the gathered elders and lowers his gaze. The assembly sees his humility and praises him as the most modest master.
insight: It shifts respect away from self-display and toward quiet self-command.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone expects you to speak first, defend yourself, or take credit. Instead, you listen, soften, and let your conduct carry the weight. People remember that far longer than a performance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत सुजान राम रुख देखी। उठि सप्रेम धरि धीर बिसेषी॥ करि दंडवत कहत कर जोरी। राखीं नाथ सकल रुचि मोरी ॥
translation: सुजान भरतजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी का रुख देखकर प्रेमपूर्वक उठकर, विशेष रूप से धीरज धारण कर दण्डवत करके हाथ जोड़कर कहने लगे- हे नाथ! आपने मेरी सभी रुचियाँ रखीं ॥
english_translation: Wise Bharat saw Ram's face, rose with love, and held himself steady. Bowing low with joined hands, he said, “Lord, you have fulfilled all my wishes.”
essence: Love kneels and discovers it was already complete.
simple_meaning: Bharat sees Ram and responds with love, humility, and self-control. He tells Ram that all his wishes are already fulfilled in Ram's presence.
insight: It shifts attention from asking for more to recognising fullness already present in devotion.
modern_relevance: You finally meet the person you have missed for months, and all the rehearsed words disappear. What comes out instead is simple gratitude: just being near them is enough.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: मोहि लगि सहेउ सबहिं संतापू। बहुत भाँति दुखु पावा आपू॥ अब गोसाइँ मोहि देउ रजाई। सेवौं अवध अवधि भरि जाई ॥
translation: मेरे लिए सब लोगों ने संताप सहा और आपने भी बहुत प्रकार से दुःख पाया। अब स्वामी मुझे आज्ञा दें। मैं जाकर अवधि भर (चौदह वर्ष तक) अवध का सेवन करूँ ॥
english_translation: For my sake, everyone has endured sorrow, and you too have suffered in many ways. Now, my lord, give me your command. I will go and serve Ayodhya for the full term.
essence: Real love asks for work, not comfort.
simple_meaning: Bharat says everyone has suffered because of him, including Ram. He asks Ram for permission to return and serve Ayodhya for the full exile period.
insight: It shifts you from self-protection to responsible service after harm has been caused.
modern_relevance: You realize your mistake has cost other people sleep, money, and peace. Instead of defending yourself, you ask how to make things right and keep showing up until the damage is repaired.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जेहिं उपाय पुनि पाय जनु देखै दीनदयाल। सो सिख देइअ अवधि लगि कोसलपाल कृपाल ॥
translation: हे दीनदयालु! जिस उपाय से यह दास फिर चरणों का दर्शन करे- हे कोसलाधीश! हे कृपालु! अवधिभर के लिए मुझे वही शिक्षा दीजिए ॥
english_translation: O compassionate one, by whatever means this servant may again behold your feet, O lord of Kosala and merciful one, teach me that way for the whole period of my stay.
essence: True devotion asks for the way back, not the reward.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks Ram to teach him the one way that will let him see Ram again and remain devoted for the whole exile period.
insight: It shifts devotion from emotion alone into a concrete way of living that keeps return possible.
modern_relevance: You are moving cities, changing jobs, or living far from someone you love, and you keep asking: what keeps this bond alive? Bharat knows the answer is not possession, but faithful direction.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: पुरजन परिजन प्रजा गोसाईं। सब सुचि सरस सनेहँ सगाईं॥ राउर बदि भल भव दुख दाहू। प्रभु बिनु बादि परम पद लाहू ॥
translation: हे गोसाईं! आपके प्रेम और संबंध में अवधपुर वासी, कुटुम्बी और प्रजा सभी पवित्र और रस (आनंद) से युक्त हैं। आपके लिए भवदुःख (जन्म-मरण के दुःख) की ज्वाला में जलना भी अच्छा है और प्रभु (आप) के बिना परमपद (मोक्ष) का लाभ भी व्यर्थ है ॥
english_translation: O Lord, the people of Ayodhya, our family, and the subjects are all pure and filled with sweet affection because of your love. For you, even burning in the fire of worldly suffering is good, and without you, even the highest freedom is meaningless.
essence: Ram’s presence makes suffering bearable and freedom incomplete without him.
simple_meaning: Bharat says Ayodhya’s people, family, and subjects are made pure and joyful by Ram’s presence. Even suffering in the world feels worthwhile for him, while freedom without Ram feels pointless.
insight: It shifts value from external success to the presence that makes life meaningful.
modern_relevance: You leave a family gathering and realize one person made the whole room feel alive. The food, the laughter, even the comfort of being there — none of it feels complete without them.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: स्वामि सुजानु जानि सब ही की। रुचि लालसा रहनि जन जी की॥ प्रनतपालु पालिहि सब काहू। देउ दुहू दिसि ओर निबाहू ॥
translation: हे स्वामी! आप सुजान हैं, सभी के हृदय की और मुझ सेवक के मन की रुचि, लालसा (अभिलाषा) और रहनी जानकर, हे प्रणतपाल! आप सब किसी का पालन करेंगे और हे देव! दोनों ओर अन्त तक निबाहेंगे ॥
english_translation: O wise Lord, you know everyone’s heart. You know the desires and longings that live in each person’s mind. Protector of the surrendered, you will care for everyone and keep faith with both sides until the end.
essence: Real protection begins when nothing in your heart is hidden.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as one who knows every heart and will protect everyone, keeping his promise to all sides.
insight: It shifts trust from self-protection to resting in a presence that sees through you and still protects you.
modern_relevance: You’re trying to explain yourself to someone who already understands your patterns better than you do. The deepest relief is being held by someone who knows your heart and still stays faithful.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: अस मोहि सब बिधि भूरि भरोसो। किएँ बिचारु न सोचु खरो सो॥ आरति मोर नाथ कर छोहू। दुहुँ मिलि कीन्ह ढीठु हठि मोहू ॥
translation: मुझे सब प्रकार से ऐसा बहुत बड़ा भरोसा है। विचार करने पर तिनके के बराबर (जरा सा) भी सोच नहीं रह जाता! मेरी दीनता और स्वामी का स्नेह दोनों ने मिलकर मुझे जबर्दस्ती ढीठ बना दिया है ॥
english_translation: I have such complete trust in every way. After reflection, not even the slightest worry remains. My helplessness and my lord's affection have together made me stubbornly bold.
essence: Complete trust ends hesitation and makes humility steady.
simple_meaning: Bharat says he has complete trust, so deep that even careful thought leaves no worry. His helplessness and Ram's affection together have made him boldly stubborn in devotion.
insight: It shifts the mind from second-guessing to settled confidence in the beloved.
modern_relevance: You keep rereading the message before sending it, then finally stop because you know the relationship is safe. That steadiness is what Bharat is naming: trust that removes the need to keep checking.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: यह बड़ दोषु दूरि करि स्वामी। तजि सकोच सिखइअ अनुगामी॥ भरत बिनय सुनि सबहिं प्रसंसी। खीर नीर बिबरन गति हंसी ॥
translation: हे स्वामी! इस बड़े दोष को दूर करके संकोच त्याग कर मुझ सेवक को शिक्षा दीजिए। दूध और जल को अलग-अलग करने में हंसिनी की सी गति वाली भरतजी की विनती सुनकर उसकी सभी ने प्रशंसा की ॥
english_translation: “My Lord, remove this great fault and, setting aside hesitation, teach me, your servant.” Hearing Bharat's plea, everyone praised him, graceful like a swan separating milk from water.
essence: Humble honesty makes you fit to receive what pride cannot hear.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks Ram to remove hesitation and teach him openly. Everyone praises the purity and clarity of his humble request.
insight: It shifts you from self-protection to open receiving, so guidance can actually reach you.
modern_relevance: You finally admit to a mentor that you are confused and need direct help. The relief comes not from looking capable, but from being honest enough to learn.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दीनबंधु सुनि बंधु के वचन दीन छलहीन। देस काल अवसर सरिस बोले रामु प्रबीन ॥
translation: दीनबन्धु और परम चतुर श्री रामजी ने भाई भरतजी के दीन और छलरहित वचन सुनकर देश, काल और अवसर के अनुकूल वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: Hearing Bharat's humble, deceit-free words, the compassionate and skilled Ram spoke in a way suited to the place, time, and moment.
essence: True closeness speaks with perfect care.
simple_meaning: Ram hears Bharat's humble, sincere words and answers with perfect tact, matching the moment and the need.
insight: It teaches you to answer sincere vulnerability with speech that heals, not speech that wins.
modern_relevance: A tense family conversation after a long silence needs more than honesty. You also need timing, tenderness, and the wisdom to say the right thing without deepening the wound.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तात तुम्हारि मोरि परिजन की। चिंता गुरहि नृपहि घर बन की॥ माथे पर गुर मुनि मिथिलेसू। हमहि तुम्हहि सपनेहूँ न कलेसू ॥
translation: हे तात! तुम्हारी, मेरी, परिवार की, घर की और वन की सारी चिंता गुरु वशिष्ठजी और महाराज जनकजी को है। हमारे सिर पर जब गुरुजी, मुनि विश्वामित्रजी और मिथिलापति जनकजी हैं, तब हमें और तुम्हें स्वप्न नें भी क्लेश नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Father, your worries and mine, the family’s worries, the home’s worries, and the forest’s worries are all on the shoulders of Guru Vashistha and King Janaka. With Guru, sage Vishvamitra, and Janaka above us, neither you nor I have any trouble, even in dreams.
essence: You can release worry when wise hands already hold the burden.
simple_meaning: Ram reassures Bharat that the burden of managing home, forest, and family rests with trusted elders, so neither brother needs to worry.
insight: It shifts you from private panic to shared responsibility, trusting competent elders instead of clutching everything yourself.
modern_relevance: You are lying awake after a family crisis, trying to solve every detail by morning. This verse reminds you that care can be shared, and not every burden belongs to your hands.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: मोर तुम्हार परम पुरुषारथु। स्वारथु सुजसु धरमु परमारथु॥ पितु आयसु पालिहिं दुहु भाईं। लोक बेद भल भूप भलाईं ॥
translation: मेरा और तुम्हारा तो परम पुरुषार्थ, स्वार्थ, सुयश, धर्म और परमार्थ इसी में है कि हम दोनों भाई पिताजी की आज्ञा का पालन करें। राजा की भलाई (उनके व्रत की रक्षा) से ही लोक और वेद दोनों में भला है ॥
english_translation: My and your highest aim, self-interest, good name, duty, and true good all lie in this: that both brothers obey our father's command. The king's welfare is served when both worldly custom and sacred teaching are upheld.
essence: Keeping your father's word is the highest good for both brothers.
simple_meaning: Keeping their father's command is the highest good for both brothers. It is not just obedience; it is their duty, their honor, and what brings real benefit.
insight: It shifts you from chasing convenience to honoring the obligation that preserves your integrity.
modern_relevance: You are tempted to bend a promise because it would make life easier right now. But the deeper relief comes from keeping what you said, even when it costs you comfort.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: गुर पितु मातु स्वामि सिख पालें। चलेहुँ कुमग पग परहिं न खालें॥ अस बिचारि सब सोच बिहाई। पालहु अवध अवधि भरि जाई ॥
translation: गुरु, पिता, माता और स्वामी की शिक्षा (आज्ञा) का पालन करने से कुमार्ग पर भी चलने पर पैर गड्ढे में नहीं पड़ता (पतन नहीं होता)। ऐसा विचार कर सब सोच छोड़कर अवध जाकर अवधिभर उसका पालन करो ॥
english_translation: By following the guidance of your teacher, father, mother, and master, even a wrong road will not make you fall. Thinking this through, let go of sorrow and go to Ayodhya; keep that vow until the end.
essence: Right guidance can keep you steady even on a wrong road.
simple_meaning: Following the guidance of your teacher, parents, and master protects you from losing your way. Keep that instruction in mind and carry it through without worry.
insight: It shifts action from anxious self-direction to disciplined trust in rightful guidance.
modern_relevance: Your phone is buzzing, three people are giving you conflicting advice, and you feel pulled in every direction. This verse says steady yourself by remembering the guidance that deserves your trust.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: देसु कोसु परिजन परिवारू। गुर पद रजहिं लाग छरुभारू॥ तुम्ह मुनि मातु सचिव सिख मानी। पालेहु पुहुमि प्रजा रजधानी ॥
translation: देश, खजाना, कुटुम्ब, परिवार आदि सबकी जिम्मेदारी तो गुरुजी की चरण रज पर है। तुम तो मुनि वशिष्ठजी, माताओं और मन्त्रियों की शिक्षा मानकर तदनुसार पृथ्वी, प्रजा और राजधानी का पालन (रक्षा) भर करते रहना ॥
english_translation: The burden of land, treasury, kin, family, and kingdom rests on the teacher’s feet. You, having followed the counsel of the sages, mothers, and ministers, should simply protect the earth, the people, and the capital.
essence: True rule is light when it serves guidance, not ego.
simple_meaning: Rule the land, people, and capital, but do it by following wise guidance and staying humble. Real authority is light when it listens.
insight: It shifts responsibility from personal control to humble governance guided by trusted wisdom.
modern_relevance: You’re handed a team, a household, or a project, and suddenly every problem feels like it has your name on it. This verse says leadership is not solitary pride; it is stewardship shaped by counsel.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: मुखिआ मुखु सो चाहिऐ खान पान कहुँ एक। पालइ पोषइ सकल अँग तुलसी सहित बिबेक ॥
translation: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) मुखिया मुख के समान होना चाहिए, जो खाने-पीने को तो एक (अकेला) है, परन्तु विवेकपूर्वक सब अंगों का पालन-पोषण करता है ॥
english_translation: A leader should be like the mouth: taking for itself only food and drink, yet wisely nourishing all the limbs.
essence: A leader stays small in need and large in care.
simple_meaning: A true leader takes only what is needed and uses discernment to support everyone else.
insight: It shifts leadership from self-interest to wise care for the whole.
modern_relevance: You’re the manager who grabs the last credit while your team carries the load. Or the parent who keeps the house running by quietly giving more than taking. Real authority nourishes others first.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: राजधरम सरबसु एतनोई। जिमि मन माहँ मनोरथ गोई॥ बंधु प्रबोधु कीन्ह बहु भाँती। बिनु अधार मन तोषु न साँती ॥
translation: राजधर्म का सर्वस्व (सार) भी इतना ही है। जैसे मन के भीतर मनोरथ छिपा रहता है। श्री रघुनाथजी ने भाई भरत को बहुत प्रकार से समझाया, परन्तु कोई अवलम्बन पाए बिना उनके मन में न संतोष हुआ, न शान्ति ॥
english_translation: The whole of righteous rule is this much: like a desire hidden in the mind. Brother Ram explained in many ways, but without a support, Bharat's mind found neither contentment nor peace.
essence: Peace comes only when the mind finds something firm to stand on.
simple_meaning: Even wise advice cannot bring peace if the mind has nothing solid to hold onto. Bharat is still unsettled because he lacks the support he needs.
insight: It shifts you from chasing better explanations to finding the support that lets the mind settle.
modern_relevance: You can read ten messages, get three apologies, and still feel shaky at 1 a.m. What you need is not more explanation, but something steady to hold.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: भरत सील गुर सचिव समाजू। सकुच सनेह बिबस रघुराजू॥ प्रभु करि कृपा पाँवरीं दीन्हीं। सादर भरत सीस धरि लीन्हीं ॥
translation: इधर तो भरतजी का शील (प्रेम) और उधर गुरुजनों, मंत्रियों तथा समाज की उपस्थिति! यह देखकर श्री रघुनाथजी संकोच तथा स्नेह के विशेष वशीभूत हो गए (अर्थात भरतजी के प्रेमवश उन्हें पाँवरी देना चाहते हैं, किन्तु साथ ही गुरु आदि का संकोच भी होता है।) आखिर (भरतजी के प्रेमवश) प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने कृपा कर खड़ाऊँ दे दीं और भरतजी ने उन्हें आदरपूर्वक सिर पर धारण कर लिया ॥
