english_translation: Seeing Bharat's noble conduct and the gathered teachers, ministers, and people, Raghunath was overcome by both shyness and love. In compassion, the Lord gave him the sandals, and Bharat placed them respectfully on his head.
essence: True devotion turns even sandals into something sacred.
simple_meaning: Bharat's love, and the presence of elders and ministers, makes Ram both shy and tender. He gives Bharat his sandals, and Bharat accepts them with reverence.
insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone into a visible act of reverence and surrender.
modern_relevance: You hand back the keys to a home you can no longer keep, and your hands shake a little. What matters most is not possession, but the love with which you release it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चरनपीठ करुनानिधान के। जनु जुग जामिक प्रजा प्रान के॥ संपुट भरत सनेह रतन के। आखर जुग जनु जीव जतन के ॥
translation: करुणानिधान श्री रामचंद्रजी के दोनों ख़ड़ाऊँ प्रजा के प्राणों की रक्षा के लिए मानो दो पहरेदार हैं। भरतजी के प्रेमरूपी रत्न के लिए मानो डिब्बा है और जीव के साधन के लिए मानो राम-नाम के दो अक्षर हैं ॥
english_translation: The pair of wooden sandals of the compassionate Lord are like two guardians for the lives of the people, like a casket for Bharat's jewel of love, and like two letters for the soul's practice.
essence: What is touched by Ram becomes shelter, treasure, and practice.
simple_meaning: Ram's sandals are described as protectors of the people, a container for Bharat's love, and a symbol of the two-letter name that supports spiritual practice.
insight: It shifts attention from the object itself to the love and refuge the object carries.
modern_relevance: You keep a photo, a voice note, or a worn-out letter from someone you love. It seems small, but it holds your whole devotion. Bharat's sandals carry that same weight.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कुल कपाट कर कुसल करम के। बिमल नयन सेवा सुधरम के॥ भरत मुदित अवलंब लहे तें। अस सुख जस सिय रामु रहे तें ॥
translation: रघुकुल (की रक्षा) के लिए दो किवाड़ हैं। कुशल (श्रेष्ठ) कर्म करने के लिए दो हाथ की भाँति (सहायक) हैं और सेवा रूपी श्रेष्ठ धर्म के सुझाने के लिए निर्मल नेत्र हैं। भरतजी इस अवलंब के मिल जाने से परम आनंदित हैं। उन्हें ऐसा ही सुख हुआ, जैसा श्री सीता-रामजी के रहने से होता है ॥
english_translation: The Raghu line has two doors for protection, two hands for good action, and two clear eyes for the noble duty of service. Bharat is overjoyed to have such support, feeling a joy like the presence of Sita and Ram.
essence: True support turns service into joy.
simple_meaning: Service, right action, and clear sight protect the family line. Bharat feels deep joy in having this support, like the joy of being with Sita and Ram.
insight: It reframes support as the condition that lets duty, service, and right action actually happen.
modern_relevance: You finally have a teammate who sees the whole picture, handles the practical work, and protects what matters. That kind of support feels almost sacred because it makes service possible.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मागेउ बिदा प्रनामु करि राम लिए उर लाइ। लोग उचाटे अमरपति कुटिल कुअवसरु पाइ ॥
translation: भरतजी ने प्रणाम करके विदा माँगी, तब श्री रामचंद्रजी ने उन्हें हृदय से लगा लिया। इधर कुटिल इंद्र ने बुरा मौका पाकर लोगों का उच्चाटन कर दिया ॥
english_translation: Bharat bowed and asked to depart; Ram embraced him to his heart. Then, finding a bad opening, the crooked lord of the gods stirred everyone into unease.
essence: Love gives comfort, but unrest can still slip in through a weak moment.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks Ram for permission to leave, and Ram embraces him lovingly. At that moment, a harmful force takes advantage and unsettles the people.
insight: It shows how quickly harmony can be disturbed when a vulnerable moment meets outside interference.
modern_relevance: You finally say goodbye after a painful family visit, and the room feels lighter for a second. Then one sharp comment, one bad mood, and everyone is unsettled again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सो कुचालि सब कहँ भइ नीकी। अवधि आस सम जीवनि जी की॥ नतरु लखन सिय राम बियोगा। हहरि मरत सब लोग कुरोगा ॥
translation: वह कुचाल भी सबके लिए हितकर हो गई। अवधि की आशा के समान ही वह जीवन के लिए संजीवनी हो गई। नहीं तो (उच्चाटन न होता तो) लक्ष्मणजी, सीताजी और श्री रामचंद्रजी के वियोग रूपी बुरे रोग से सब लोग घबड़ाकर (हाय-हाय करके) मर ही जाते ॥
english_translation: That bad turn became good for everyone. Like the hope of a deadline, it became the medicine that kept life going. Otherwise, the pain of separation from Lakshman, Sita, and Ram would have made everyone cry out and die in grief.
essence: A bad delay can become the medicine that prevents a deeper collapse.
simple_meaning: A seemingly bad event turned out to help everyone. It stopped the pain of separation from Lakshman, Sita, and Ram from overwhelming the people.
insight: It shifts you to see delay as possible protection, not always obstruction.
modern_relevance: A meeting gets delayed after a family argument, and the extra hour keeps everyone from saying something unforgivable. What felt like a setback quietly prevents a worse wound.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामकृपाँ अवरेब सुधारी। बिबुध धारि भइ गुनद गोहारी॥ भेंटत भुज भरि भाइ भरत सो। राम प्रेम रसु न कहि न परत सो ॥
translation: श्री रामजी की कृपा ने सारी उलझन सुधार दी। देवताओं की सेना जो लूटने आई थी, वही गुणदायक (हितकरी) और रक्षक बन गई। श्री रामजी भुजाओं में भरकर भाई भरत से मिल रहे हैं। श्री रामजी के प्रेम का वह रस (आनंद) कहते नहीं बनता ॥
english_translation: By Ram's grace, everything was set right. The host of radiant beings, who had come to seize, became helpful and protective. Ram embraced his brother Bharat in his arms, and the sweetness of Ram's love cannot be spoken.
essence: Ram's grace can turn even threat into shelter.
simple_meaning: Ram's grace turns even trouble into help. He welcomes Bharat with a full embrace, and the joy of that love is beyond words.
insight: It shifts attention from the conflict itself to the healing power of wholehearted welcome.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a family fight, expecting tension, and instead someone opens their arms. In that moment, the whole mood changes before a single explanation is given.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तन मन बचन उमग अनुरागा। धीर धुरंधर धीरजु त्यागा॥ बारिज लोचन मोचत बारी। देखि दसा सुर सभा दुखारी ॥
translation: तन, मन और वचन तीनों में प्रेम उमड़ पड़ा। धीरज की धुरी को धारण करने वाले श्री रघुनाथजी ने भी धीरज त्याग दिया। वे कमल सदृश नेत्रों से (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल बहाने लगे। उनकी यह दशा देखकर देवताओं की सभा (समाज) दुःखी हो गई ॥
english_translation: Love surged through body, mind, and speech. Even the steadfast Lord of Raghu let go of composure. He began shedding tears from lotus-like eyes. Seeing this state, the assembly of the devas became sorrowful.
essence: True steadiness can still dissolve in love.
simple_meaning: Ram's love becomes so intense that even his usual calm breaks, and tears flow from his eyes. The devas are moved to sorrow by seeing it.
insight: It reframes tears as an honest sign of love, not a failure of strength.
modern_relevance: You finally see someone you have missed for years, and the careful mask drops in an instant. The body knows what the mind has tried to hold back.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनिगन गुर धुर धीर जनक से। ग्यान अनल मन कसें कनक से॥ जे बिरंचि निरलेप उपाए। पदुम पत्र जिमि जग जल जाए ॥
translation: मुनिगण, गुरु वशिष्ठजी और जनकजी सरीखे धीरधुरन्धर जो अपने मनों को ज्ञान रूपी अग्नि में सोने के समान कस चुके थे, जिनको ब्रह्माजी ने निर्लेप ही रचा और जो जगत् रूपी जल में कमल के पत्ते की तरह ही (जगत् में रहते हुए भी जगत् से अनासक्त) पैदा हुए ॥
english_translation: The sages, the teacher, and King Janak were steady like that. They had tempered their minds in the fire of wisdom, like gold. Brahma created them untouched, like a lotus leaf in water, living in the world yet unstained.
essence: Real freedom is staying untouched while fully present.
simple_meaning: Great sages and Janak stayed steady, purified by wisdom, and untouched by the world, like a lotus leaf in water.
insight: It shifts attention from worldly involvement to inner non-attachment.
modern_relevance: You leave a tense family dinner, phone buzzing with old arguments, and still choose not to carry the bitterness home. That is the kind of inner freedom this verse praises.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेउ बिलोकि रघुबर भरत प्रीति अनूप अपार। भए मगन मन तन बचन सहित बिराग बिचार ॥
translation: वे भी श्री रामजी और भरतजी के उपमारहित अपार प्रेम को देखकर वैराग्य और विवेक सहित तन, मन, वचन से उस प्रेम में मग्न हो गए ॥
english_translation: Seeing the incomparable, boundless love between Raghubar and Bharat, they too became absorbed in it with body, mind, and speech, along with detachment and discernment.
essence: Love at its purest carries both surrender and clear seeing.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram and Bharat's unmatched love, even the wise were moved into a state of loving absorption, while still keeping detachment and clear judgment.
insight: It shows that devotion and discernment can coexist, and that genuine love can awaken both feeling and clarity.
modern_relevance: You watch two siblings protect each other through a family crisis, and something in you softens. Their loyalty doesn't make them naive; it makes them clearer about what matters.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहाँ जनक गुरु गति मति भोरी। प्राकृत प्रीति कहत बड़ि खोरी॥ बरनत रघुबर भरत बियोगू। सुनि कठोर कबि जानिहि लोगू ॥
translation: जहाँ जनकजी और गुरु वशिष्ठजी की बुद्धि की गति कुण्ठित हो, उस दिव्य प्रेम को प्राकृत (लौकिक) कहने में बड़ा दोष है। श्री रामचंद्रजी और भरतजी के वियोग का वर्णन करते सुनकर लोग कवि को कठोर हृदय समझेंगे ॥
english_translation: Where even Janak and the teacher's wisdom falters, calling that love ordinary is a grave mistake. If I describe the separation of Ram and Bharat, people will think the poet is hard-hearted.
essence: True devotion makes ordinary language feel too small.
simple_meaning: The bond between Ram and Bharat is so extraordinary that calling it ordinary would be wrong. Even describing their separation feels impossible and risks sounding heartless.
insight: It teaches you to respect what cannot be flattened into simple labels and to let deep feeling remain deep.
modern_relevance: You try to explain why you still care about someone who hurt you, and every sentence sounds too small. Some bonds are real precisely because they resist neat explanation.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सो सकोच रसु अकथ सुबानी। समउ सनेहु सुमिरि सकुचानी॥ भेंटि भरतु रघुबर समुझाए। पुनि रिपुदवनु हरषि हियँ लाए ॥
translation: वह संकोच रस अकथनीय है। अतएव कवि की सुंदर वाणी उस समय उसके प्रेम को स्मरण करके सकुचा गई। भरतजी को भेंट कर श्री रघुनाथजी ने उनको समझाया। फिर हर्षित होकर शत्रुघ्नजी को हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
english_translation: That shy, indescribable nectar of love made even the poet's beautiful words falter. Ram embraced Bharat and consoled him, then joyfully drew Shatrughna into his heart.
essence: True love can be too deep for speech.
simple_meaning: The love between Ram and Bharat is so deep and restrained that words cannot hold it. Ram comforts Bharat, then lovingly embraces Shatrughna.
insight: It shifts attention from explaining love to embodying it through presence, reassurance, and embrace.
modern_relevance: You finally see a sibling after a long fight, and neither of you knows how to start. One hug says what careful sentences never could.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सेवक सचिव भरत रुख पाई। निज निज काज लगे सब जाई॥ सुनि दारुन दुखु दुहूँ समाजा। लगे चलन के साजन साजा ॥
translation: सेवक और मंत्री भरतजी का रुख पाकर सब अपने-अपने काम में जा लगे। यह सुनकर दोनों समाजों में दारुण दुःख छा गया। वे चलने की तैयारियाँ करने लगे ॥
english_translation: When Bharata's servants and ministers understood Bharata's decision, each returned to their own duties. Hearing this, deep sorrow spread through both groups, and they began preparing to depart.
essence: Love can end a gathering and still leave everyone moving with duty.
simple_meaning: Bharata's people understand his decision and return to their tasks, but everyone feels the pain of separation and starts preparing to leave.
insight: It shows how duty can resume even while grief remains present in the heart.
modern_relevance: The group chat goes quiet after the decision is made. People start packing, booking rides, and pretending they are fine — but the room feels different because everyone knows the visit is ending.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु पद पदुम बंदि दोउ भाई। चले सीस धरि राम रजाई॥ मुनि तापस बनदेव निहोरी। सब सनमानि बहोरि बहोरी ॥
translation: प्रभु के चरणकमलों की वंदना करके तथा श्री रामजी की आज्ञा को सिर पर रखकर भरत-शत्रुघ्न दोनों भाई चले। मुनि, तपस्वी और वनदेवता सबका बार-बार सम्मान करके उनकी विनती की ॥
english_translation: Both brothers bowed at the Lord's lotus feet and left with Ram's command on their heads. They honored the sages, ascetics, and forest spirits again and again, offering respectful requests.
essence: Humility obeys fully and still bows to everyone along the way.
simple_meaning: Bharat and Shatrughna leave after bowing to Ram, carrying his command as their guiding order. Before going, they respectfully honor the sages, ascetics, and forest beings around them.
insight: It teaches you to carry instruction with humility and to honor everyone before moving on.
modern_relevance: You finish the meeting, but before stepping out you thank the people who helped, the assistants, even the quiet ones in the room. Leaving well can be its own form of character.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लखनहि भेंटि प्रनामु करि सिर धरि सिय पद धूरि। चले सप्रेम असीस सुनि सकल सुमंगल मूरि ॥
translation: फिर लक्ष्मणजी को क्रमशः भेंटकर तथा प्रणाम करके और सीताजी के चरणों की धूलि को सिर पर धारण करके और समस्त मंगलों के मूल आशीर्वाद सुनकर वे प्रेमसहित चले ॥
english_translation: Then, greeting Lakshman and bowing, he placed Sita's dust on his head and departed in love after hearing blessings from the source of all auspiciousness.
essence: Respect and love can sanctify even a simple departure.
simple_meaning: They greet Lakshman, bow to Sita, receive blessings, and leave with loving hearts.
insight: It turns departure into an act of reverence, not mere movement.
modern_relevance: You leave a home after a hard conversation, but you still touch the elder's feet, thank the host, and carry the warmth with you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सानुज राम नृपहि सिर नाई। कीन्हि बहुत बिधि बिनय बड़ाई॥ देव दया बस बड़ दुखु पायउ। सहित समाज काननहिं आयउ ॥
translation: छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी समेत श्री रामजी ने राजा जनकजी को सिर नवाकर उनकी बहुत प्रकार से विनती और बड़ाई की (और कहा-) हे देव! दयावश आपने बहुत दुःख पाया। आप समाज सहित वन में आए ॥
english_translation: With Lakshman beside him, Ram bowed to King Janak and praised him in many ways: “By your grace, O noble one, you have suffered much sorrow and come to the forest with your whole assembly.”
essence: True greatness bows first and recognizes another's burden.
simple_meaning: Ram greets King Janak with deep respect and praises his willingness to come into the forest with everyone around him.
insight: It teaches you to begin with reverence, especially when another person has already suffered for others.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a hospital entrance after they have carried their whole family through a hard night. Before asking anything, you honor what they have already endured.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: पुर पगु धारिअ देइ असीसा। कीन्ह धीर धरि गवनु महीसा॥ मुनि महिदेव साधु सनमाने। बिदा किए हरि हर सम जाने ॥
translation: अब आशीर्वाद देकर नगर को पधारिए। यह सुन राजा जनकजी ने धीरज धरकर गमन किया। फिर श्री रामचंद्रजी ने मुनि, ब्राह्मण और साधुओं को विष्णु और शिव के समान जानकर सम्मान करके उनको विदा किया ॥
english_translation: Now, after giving blessings, let the king depart to the city. Hearing this, King Janaka gathered himself and set out with composure. Then Ram honored sages, priests, and holy men, knowing them as equal to Vishnu and Shiva, and bade them farewell.
essence: True dignity is leaving calmly and honoring the worthy fully.
simple_meaning: Janaka leaves with dignity after receiving blessings, and Ram respectfully sends off the sages and holy men as worthy of the highest honor.
insight: It teaches graceful departure and humble honor toward the wise.
modern_relevance: At the end of a wedding, when the elders rise and the room slowly empties, the real beauty is in the way everyone leaves: blessed, composed, and respected.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सासु समीप गए दोउ भाई। फिरे बंदि पग आसिष पाई॥ कौसिक बामदेव जाबाली। पुरजन परिजन सचिव सुचाली ॥
translation: तब श्री राम-लक्ष्मण दोनों भाई सास (सुनयनाजी) के पास गए और उनके चरणों की वंदना करके आशीर्वाद पाकर लौट आए। फिर विश्वामित्र, वामदेव, जाबालि और शुभ आचरण वाले कुटुम्बी, नगर निवासी और मंत्री- ॥
english_translation: Then both brothers went to their mother, bowed at her feet, received her blessing, and returned. After that, Kaushik, Vamadeva, Jabali, the townspeople, relatives, and upright ministers...
essence: Departure stays noble when it begins with respect.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman visit their mother, bow to her feet, receive her blessing, and then greet the assembled sages, relatives, citizens, and ministers.
insight: It shows how to leave without breaking your bonds: honor the people who formed you before you step forward.
modern_relevance: You leave the house for a life-changing move, but first you touch your mother’s feet, thank the elders, and say goodbye properly. Some departures stay clean because they begin with humility.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जथा जोगु करि बिनय प्रनामा। बिदा किए सब सानुज रामा॥ नारि पुरुष लघु मध्य बड़ेरे। सब सनमानि कृपानिधि फेरे ॥
translation: सबको छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित श्री रामचंद्रजी ने यथायोग्य विनय एवं प्रणाम करके विदा किया। कृपानिधान श्री रामचंद्रजी ने छोटे, मध्यम (मझले) और बड़े सभी श्रेणी के स्त्री-पुरुषों का सम्मान करके उनको लौटाया ॥
english_translation: Rama, along with Lakshmana, respectfully took leave of everyone. The treasure of compassion honored all the women and men, young, middle-aged, and old, and sent them back.
essence: True grace honors everyone, not just the important few.
simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana respectfully take leave of everyone, honoring people of every age and rank before sending them back.
insight: It trains you to show equal respect, not just to the people who matter most to you.
modern_relevance: You leave a family gathering and make sure the quiet aunt, the child, and the elder all feel seen before you go.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत मातु पद बंदि प्रभु सुचि सनेहँ मिलि भेंटि। बिदा कीन्ह सजि पालकी सकुच सोच सब मेटि ॥
translation: भरत की माता कैकेयी के चरणों की वंदना करके प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी ने पवित्र (निश्छल) प्रेम के साथ उनसे मिल-भेंट कर तथा उनके सारे संकोच और सोच को मिटाकर पालकी सजाकर उनको विदा किया ॥
english_translation: Lord Ram bowed at Bharata's mother's feet, met her with pure affection, and, removing all her hesitation and worry, had a palanquin prepared and sent her off.
essence: Respect can soften even a painful family bond.
simple_meaning: Ram shows deep respect to Kaikeyi, meets her with sincere affection, removes her awkwardness and worry, and arranges her farewell kindly.
insight: It teaches you to lower conflict through respectful action instead of carrying old heat forward.
modern_relevance: You see someone who hurt your family at a gathering, and everyone stiffens. Ram's response shows another way: meet them with dignity, not poison the room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परिजन मातु पितहि मिलि सीता। फिरी प्रानप्रिय प्रेम पुनीता॥ करि प्रनामु भेंटीं सब सासू। प्रीति कहत कबि हियँ न हुलासू ॥
translation: प्राणप्रिय पति श्री रामचंद्रजी के साथ पवित्र प्रेम करने वाली सीताजी नैहर के कुटुम्बियों से तथा माता-पिता से मिलकर लौट आईं। फिर प्रणाम करके सब सासुओं से गले लगकर मिलीं। उनके प्रेम का वर्णन करने के लिए कवि के हृदय में हुलास (उत्साह) नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: Sita met her parents and relatives, then returned with pure love for her dear husband. She bowed and embraced all her mothers-in-law, and the poet says his heart cannot contain the joy of describing their love.
essence: Love becomes complete when respect flows to everyone.
simple_meaning: Sita lovingly meets her family and in-laws before returning. The verse lingers on the warmth and respect flowing between both sides of the family.
insight: It highlights how affection and proper conduct can coexist without strain.
modern_relevance: You leave a family gathering after hugging both sides of the family, and the room still feels warm behind you. Some goodbyes are made of respect, not distance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि सिख अभिमत आसिष पाई। रही सीय दुहु प्रीति समाई॥ रघुपति पटु पालकीं मगाईं। करि प्रबोध सब मातु चढ़ाईं ॥
translation: उनकी शिक्षा सुनकर और मनचाहा आशीर्वाद पाकर सीताजी सासुओं तथा माता-पिता दोनों ओर की प्रीति में समाई (बहुत देर तक निमग्न) रहीं! (तब) श्री रघुनाथजी ने सुंदर पालकियाँ मँगवाईं और सब माताओं को आश्वासन देकर उन पर चढ़ाया ॥
english_translation: After hearing the advice and receiving the blessing she wanted, Sita remained absorbed in equal affection for both families. Then Lord Raghunath arranged fine palanquins and, reassuring all the mothers, helped them into them.
essence: True affection makes parting gentle, not painful.
simple_meaning: Sita receives the blessing she wanted and stays equally devoted to both families. Ram then arranges palanquins and gently sends the mothers off with reassurance.
insight: It shows how care can smooth a transition, honoring both attachment and departure without forcing either.
modern_relevance: After a wedding weekend, you stand at the doorway while both families linger, reluctant to part. Someone quietly makes sure everyone is cared for, and the farewell becomes tender instead of awkward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बार बार हिलि मिलि दुहु भाईं। सम सनेहँ जननीं पहुँचाईं॥ साजि बाजि गज बाहन नाना। भरत भूप दल कीन्ह पयाना ॥
translation: दोनों भाइयों ने माताओं से समान प्रेम से बार-बार मिल-जुलकर उनको पहुँचाया। भरतजी और राजा जनकजी के दलों ने घोड़े, हाथी और अनेकों तरह की सवारियाँ सजाकर प्रस्थान किया ॥
english_translation: Again and again, both brothers met and embraced their mothers and escorted them with equal affection. Then Bharat's party set out with horses, elephants, and many kinds of vehicles.
essence: Equal affection is shown in the way you escort, not in grand words.
simple_meaning: The brothers lovingly see their mothers off, and Bharat’s group leaves with a grand procession of horses, elephants, and vehicles.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to tenderness: the way you part can reveal the depth of your love.
modern_relevance: You walk your parents to the car after a hard family visit, making sure no one feels left behind. Even small gestures can carry the weight of care.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हृदयँ रामु सिय लखन समेता। चले जाहिं सब लोग अचेता॥ बसह बाजि गज पसु हियँ हारें। चले जाहिं परबस मन मारें ॥
translation: सीताजी एवं लक्ष्मणजी सहित श्री रामचंद्रजी को हृदय में रखकर सब लोग बेसुध हुए चले जा रहे हैं। बैल-घोड़े, हाथी आदि पशु हृदय में हारे (शिथिल) हुए परवश मन मारे चले जा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: With Ram, Sita, and Lakshman in their hearts, everyone walked on in a daze. Even the cattle, horses, elephants, and other animals, with hearts drooping, moved on helplessly, their minds stricken.
essence: When Ram leaves, even the city feels grief.
simple_meaning: Everyone is so overwhelmed by Ram’s departure that they walk on in a daze, and even the animals seem subdued and helpless.
insight: It shows how deeply one departure can affect an entire community, not just one family.
modern_relevance: You leave the hospital after hearing bad news, and the street looks unreal. People keep moving, but your whole world has gone quiet inside.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गुर गुरतिय पद बंदि प्रभु सीता लखन समेत। फिरे हरष बिसमय सहित आए परन निकेत ॥
translation: गुरु वशिष्ठजी और गुरु पत्नी अरुन्धतीजी के चरणों की वंदना करके सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी हर्ष और विषाद के साथ लौटकर पर्णकुटी पर आए ॥
english_translation: After bowing to Guru Vashishtha and Arundhati, Lord Ram returned with Sita and Lakshman, filled with joy and wonder, to the forest hut.
essence: Respect and wonder travel with you even after the moment has passed.
simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman bow to their teachers and return to their forest hut, feeling both joy and wonder.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the humility that frames it.
modern_relevance: You leave your mentor’s house after receiving life-changing advice, still smiling and still stunned. The lesson is not just what you heard — it is how you carry yourself after hearing it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिदा कीन्ह सनमानि निषादू। चलेउ हृदयँ बड़ बिरह बिषादू॥ कोल किरात भिल्ल बनचारी। फेरे फिरे जोहारि जोहारी ॥
translation: फिर सम्मान करके निषादराज को विदा किया। वह चला तो सही, किन्तु उसके हृदय में विरह का भारी विषाद था। फिर श्री रामजी ने कोल, किरात, भील आदि वनवासी लोगों को लौटाया। वे सब जोहार-जोहार कर (वंदना कर-करके) लौटे ॥
english_translation: After honouring Nishad, Ram sent him away. Ram then moved on, but his heart was heavy with separation. He also sent back the Kol, Kirat, Bhil, and other forest people, and they all returned with repeated salutations.
essence: Love makes even a proper farewell feel like loss.
simple_meaning: Ram respectfully sends away the forest people who had accompanied him. Everyone parts with deep sadness, because this journey is marked by love and separation.
insight: It shifts attention from the action of leaving to the emotional cost of separation.
modern_relevance: You wave goodbye after a long visit, then sit in the car before starting the engine. Everyone was smiling, but the silence after the farewell feels heavier than words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु सिय लखन बैठि बट छाहीं। प्रिय परिजन बियोग बिलखाहीं॥ भरत सनेह सुभाउ सुबानी। प्रिया अनुज सन कहत बखानी ॥
translation: प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी, सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी बड़ की छाया में बैठकर प्रियजन एवं परिवार के वियोग से दुःखी हो रहे हैं। भरतजी के स्नेह, स्वभाव और सुंदर वाणी को बखान-बखान कर वे प्रिय पत्नी सीताजी और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी से कहने लगे ॥
english_translation: Lord Ram, Sita, and Lakshman sat under the shade of a banyan tree, grieving the separation from their loved ones. Ram then spoke to his dear wife Sita and younger brother Lakshman, praising Bharat's affection, nature, and sweet speech.
essence: Missing people can deepen, not diminish, the love you feel for them.
simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman sit in sorrow under a tree, missing those they love. Ram begins praising Bharat's loving nature to Sita and Lakshman.
insight: It teaches you to hold separation without hardening, and to let gratitude keep relationships alive across distance.
modern_relevance: You sit in a quiet park after leaving home for a hard move, and the people you miss keep rising in your chest. Naming their goodness is one way grief softens.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रीति प्रतीति बचन मन करनी। श्रीमुख राम प्रेम बस बरनी॥ तेहि अवसर खम मृग जल मीना। चित्रकूट चर अचर मलीना ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी ने प्रेम के वश होकर भरतजी के वचन, मन, कर्म की प्रीति तथा विश्वास का अपने श्रीमुख से वर्णन किया। उस समय पक्षी, पशु और जल की मछलियाँ, चित्रकूट के सभी चेतन और जड़ जीव उदास हो गए ॥
english_translation: Ram, moved by love, spoke from his own mouth about Bharat's love, trust, words, mind, and actions. At that moment, the birds, animals, fish, and all living and still things of Chitrakoot became sorrowful.
essence: Love can make an entire place grieve with you.
simple_meaning: Ram speaks lovingly about Bharat's devotion, and even Chitrakoot's living and still world feels the sorrow of separation.
insight: It shifts attention from outward events to the emotional force moving through everyone present.
modern_relevance: You hear a friend's voice after months apart, and the whole room seems to change. Some bonds are so deep that even silence feels heavy with them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिबुध बिलोकि दसा रघुबर की। बरषि सुमन कहि गति घर घर की॥ प्रभु प्रनामु करि दीन्ह भरोसो। चले मुदित मन डर न खरो सो ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी की दशा देखकर देवताओं ने उन पर फूल बरसाकर अपनी घर-घर की दशा कही (दुखड़ा सुनाया)। प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी ने उन्हें प्रणाम कर आश्वासन दिया। तब वे प्रसन्न होकर चले, मन में जरा सा भी डर न रहा ॥
english_translation: Seeing Raghubar's condition, the gods showered flowers and spoke of their own homes and sorrows. The Lord bowed to them and gave reassurance. Then they left delighted, with no fear left in their minds.
essence: Humility can steady even the ones who came to steady you.
simple_meaning: The gods see Ram's condition, honor him, and receive comfort. He bows back and reassures them, and they leave relieved.
insight: It shows that true dignity does not resist care; it receives it and returns courage to others.
modern_relevance: You visit someone in crisis expecting to comfort them, but their calm steadies you instead. A respectful bow and a few honest words can change the whole room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सानुज सीय समेत प्रभु राजत परन कुटीर। भगति ग्यानु बैराग्य जनु सोहत धरें सरीर ॥
translation: छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी समेत प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी पर्णकुटी में ऐसे सुशोभित हो रहे हैं मानो वैराग्य, भक्ति और ज्ञान शरीर धारण कर के शोभित हो रहे हों ॥
english_translation: The Lord, together with Lakshman and Sita, shines in the leaf-hut as if devotion, wisdom, and detachment have taken human form.
essence: True richness can look like a simple hut.
simple_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita shine in a simple forest hut, and their presence looks like devotion, wisdom, and detachment made visible.
insight: It shifts the mind from measuring life by possessions to recognizing the dignity of inner richness.
modern_relevance: You sit on a floor mattress in a rented room with almost nothing around you, yet the space feels peaceful because the right people are there. Simplicity stops feeling like lack.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि महिसुर गुर भरत भुआलू। राम बिरहँ सबु साजु बिहालू। प्रभु गुन ग्राम गनत मन माहीं। सब चुपचाप चले मग जाहीं ॥
translation: मुनि, ब्राह्मण, गुरु वशिष्ठजी, भरतजी और राजा जनकजी सारा समाज श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विरह में विह्वल है। प्रभु के गुण समूहों का मन में स्मरण करते हुए सब लोग मार्ग में चुपचाप चले जा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The sages, priests, the teacher, Bharata, and King Janaka were all overwhelmed by separation from Ram. Remembering Ram's countless virtues in their minds, they walked on in silence.
essence: Separation from Ram turns even a crowd into a quiet procession.
simple_meaning: Everyone is heartbroken by Ram's absence, and they keep walking while quietly remembering his many virtues.
insight: It shifts attention from conversation to shared grief and remembrance, showing how devotion can silence a crowd.
modern_relevance: You leave a place after saying goodbye to someone who mattered deeply, and the car stays quiet for miles. Everyone is thinking the same thing, but no one wants to break the spell.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जमुना उतरि पार सबु भयऊ। सो बासरु बिनु भोजन गयऊ॥ उतरि देवसरि दूसर बासू। रामसखाँ सब कीन्ह सुपासू ॥
translation: (पहले दिन) सब लोग यमुनाजी उतरकर पार हुए। वह दिन बिना भोजन के ही बीत गया। दूसरा मुकाम गंगाजी उतरकर (गंगापार श्रृंगवेरपुर में) हुआ। वहाँ राम सखा निषादराज ने सब सुप्रबंध कर दिया ॥
english_translation: Everyone crossed the Yamuna and spent that day without food. The next halt was after crossing the Ganga, where Ram's friend Nishadraj arranged everything well.
essence: Exile becomes bearable when loyal friendship meets you on the road.
simple_meaning: The travelers crossed two rivers during exile. They went hungry for a day, then rested at a place where Ram's friend arranged their stay.
insight: It shifts attention from grand events to the human kindness that keeps difficult journeys moving.
modern_relevance: You get off a crowded train after a long day, hungry and tired, and one friend is already there with water, food, and a place to sit. Relief often comes through quiet loyalty.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सई उतरि गोमतीं नहाए। चौथें दिवस अवधपुर आए॥ जनकु रहे पुर बासर चारी। राज काज सब साज सँभारी ॥
translation: फिर सई उतरकर गोमतीजी में स्नान किया और चौथे दिन सब अयोध्याजी जा पहुँचे। जनकजी चार दिन अयोध्याजी में रहे और राजकाज एवं सब साज-सामान को सम्हालकर, ॥
english_translation: Then they crossed the Saryu, bathed in the Gomti, and reached Ayodhya on the fourth day. Janaka stayed in the city for four days, taking care of the kingdom and arranging everything.
essence: Even grief must pause for the duties that keep life in order.
simple_meaning: They crossed the river, bathed, and reached Ayodhya on the fourth day. Janaka stayed four days, managing the kingdom and its arrangements.
insight: It shifts attention from emotion alone to the steady work that follows loss.
modern_relevance: After a funeral, someone still has to book the train, return the keys, and tell the landlord. Grief does not erase the tasks that keep life moving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सौंपि सचिव गुर भरतहिं राजू। तेरहुति चले साजि सबु साजू॥ नगर नारि नर गुर सिख मानी। बसे सुखेन राम रजधानी ॥
translation: तथा मंत्री, गुरुजी तथा भरतजी को राज्य सौंपकर, सारा साज-सामान ठीक करके तिरहुत को चले। नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष गुरुजी की शिक्षा मानकर श्री रामजी की राजधानी अयोध्याजी में सुखपूर्वक रहने लगे ॥
english_translation: Handing the kingdom to the ministers, the teacher, and Bharat, and arranging everything, they departed for Tirhut. The people of the city, men and women alike, followed the teacher's guidance and lived happily in Ram's capital.
essence: Peace returns when each person accepts the right role.
simple_meaning: The kingdom is placed in Bharat's care, everyone prepares to leave, and the people of Ayodhya settle into peaceful life under the teacher's guidance.
insight: It shows how harmony returns when authority is entrusted properly and people choose discipline over confusion.
modern_relevance: A family finally divides responsibilities after weeks of tension: one person handles the accounts, another watches the children, and the house can breathe again. Order returns when everyone accepts their role.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम दरस लगि लोग सब करत नेम उपबास। तजि तजि भूषन भोग सुख जिअत अवधि कीं आस ॥
translation: सब लोग श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन के लिए नियम और उपवास करने लगे। वे भूषण और भोग-सुखों को छोड़-छाड़कर अवधि की आशा पर जी रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: All people fasted and kept vows for Ram's sight. They gave up ornaments and pleasures, living only in hope of the day he would return.
essence: Love makes comfort feel unnecessary.
simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya gave up comfort, beauty, and pleasure. They fasted and kept vows because they longed to see Ram return.
insight: It shifts attention from immediate comfort to faithful waiting for what matters most.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after sending the message that matters most. You skip the snack, the party, the distraction, because one return is all you can think about.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सचिव सुसेवक भरत प्रबोधे। निज निज काज पाइ सिख ओधे॥ पुनि सिख दीन्हि बोलि लघु भाई। सौंपी सकल मातु सेवकाई ॥
translation: भरतजी ने मंत्रियों और विश्वासी सेवकों को समझाकर उद्यत किया। वे सब सीख पाकर अपने-अपने काम में लग गए। फिर छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्नजी को बुलाकर शिक्षा दी और सब माताओं की सेवा उनको सौंपी ॥
english_translation: Bharat instructed the ministers and faithful servants, and each took up their own work. Then he called his younger brother Shatrughna, gave him guidance, and entrusted him with the service of all the mothers.
essence: Bharat serves by giving everyone their proper work.
simple_meaning: Bharat gives everyone a clear role: ministers do their work, Shatrughna serves the mothers, and the household keeps moving with order and care.
insight: It teaches you to lead by clarifying responsibility, not by centering yourself.
modern_relevance: A family emergency hits, and everyone looks to one person for direction. Instead of panicking, you assign tasks, calm the room, and make sure the vulnerable are cared for.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूसुर बोलि भरत कर जोरे। करि प्रनाम बय बिनय निहोरे॥ ऊँच नीच कारजु भल पोचू। आयसु देब न करब सँकोचू ॥
translation: ब्राह्मणों को बुलाकर भरतजी ने हाथ जोड़कर प्रणाम कर अवस्था के अनुसार विनय और निहोरा किया कि आप लोग ऊँचा-नीचा (छोटा-बड़ा), अच्छा-मन्दा जो कुछ भी कार्य हो, उसके लिए आज्ञा दीजिएगा। संकोच न कीजिएगा ॥
english_translation: Calling the Brahmins, Bharata joined his hands and bowed with humble respect. He said, "For any task, great or small, good or difficult, please give your command without hesitation."
essence: Humility makes even authority ready to serve.
simple_meaning: Bharata humbly asks the Brahmins to give him any instruction, for any kind of work, without feeling shy or restrained.
insight: It teaches you to accept guidance and carry out any duty without ego.
modern_relevance: You’re the team lead, but you still ask the senior colleague, "Tell me what needs doing." That kind of humility keeps power clean and service real.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परिजन पुरजन प्रजा बोलाए। समाधानु करि सुबस बसाए॥ सानुज गे गुर गेहँ बहोरी। करि दंडवत कहत कर जोरी ॥
translation: भरतजी ने फिर परिवार के लोगों को, नागरिकों को तथा अन्य प्रजा को बुलाकर, उनका समाधान करके उनको सुखपूर्वक बसाया। फिर छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्नजी सहित वे गुरुजी के घर गए और दंडवत करके हाथ जोड़कर बोले- ॥
english_translation: Bharat called together his family, the townspeople, and the rest of the people, calmed them, and settled them comfortably. Then, along with his younger brother Shatrughna, he went again to the guru's house, bowed fully, and spoke with joined hands.
essence: Steady everyone first, then bow for guidance.
simple_meaning: Bharat restores order among the people, then returns with Shatrughna to bow before the guru and speak respectfully.
insight: It teaches you to restore stability around you before seeking counsel, and to approach guidance without pride.
modern_relevance: A family crisis has shaken everyone, but you still have to answer texts, reassure relatives, and keep the house from falling apart. Bharat shows how to steady others without losing humility.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आयसु होइ त रहौं सनेमा। बोले मुनि तन पुलकि सपेमा॥ समुझब कहब करब तुम्ह जोई। धरम सारु जग होइहि सोई ॥
translation: आज्ञा हो तो मैं नियमपूर्वक रहूँ! मुनि वशिष्ठजी पुलकित शरीर हो प्रेम के साथ बोले- हे भरत! तुम जो कुछ समझोगे, कहोगे और करोगे, वही जगत में धर्म का सार होगा ॥
english_translation: If you permit me, I will live by your command. Sage Vashishtha, thrilled and full of love, said, “Bharat, whatever you understand, say, and do, that will be the essence of dharma in the world.”
essence: A clear, sincere life becomes the measure of dharma.
simple_meaning: Vashishtha tells Bharat that if he acts with understanding, honesty, and care, his life will become a model of righteous conduct for the world.
insight: It shifts responsibility from image to integrity: your inner clarity must match your words and actions.
modern_relevance: You’re asked to lead a team after a crisis, and everyone is watching how you think before they watch what you decide. The way you understand, speak, and act becomes the standard others follow.
speaker: Vashishtha

verse_text: सुनि सिख पाइ असीस बड़ि गनक बोलि दिनु साधि। सिंघासन प्रभु पादुका बैठारे निरुपाधि ॥
translation: भरतजी ने यह सुनकर और शिक्षा तथा बड़ा आशीर्वाद पाकर ज्योतिषियों को बुलाया और दिन (अच्छा मुहूर्त) साधकर प्रभु की चरणपादुकाओं को निर्विघ्नतापूर्वक सिंहासन पर विराजित कराया ॥
english_translation: Having heard the teaching and received great blessings, Bharat called the astrologers, chose an auspicious time, and reverently seated the Lord's sandals on the throne without obstruction.
essence: You can hold power without wanting it for yourself.
simple_meaning: Bharat, after receiving guidance and blessings, arranges the coronation of Ram's sandals on the throne at the right time, with no resistance.
insight: It shifts action from self-claiming to faithful stewardship of what belongs to another.
modern_relevance: You step into a role you never wanted, but you still do it properly: the meeting is scheduled, the chair is set, and the person who truly belongs there is honored.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम मातु गुर पद सिरु नाई। प्रभु पद पीठ रजायसु पाई॥ नंदिगाँव करि परन कुटीरा। कीन्ह निवासु धरम धुर धीरा ॥
translation: फिर श्री रामजी की माता कौसल्याजी और गुरुजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर और प्रभु की चरणपादुकाओं की आज्ञा पाकर धर्म की धुरी धारण करने में धीर भरतजी ने नन्दिग्राम में पर्णकुटी बनाकर उसी में निवास किया ॥
english_translation: After bowing to Ram's mother and to his teacher, and receiving the command from Ram's sandals, steadfast Bharata built a leaf hut in Nandigram and lived there.
essence: You can renounce comfort and still stand taller than a king.
simple_meaning: Bharata honors his mother, his teacher, and Ram's command, then leaves the palace life behind and lives in a simple hut at Nandigram.
insight: It shifts the mind from status-seeking to voluntary simplicity in service of what is right.
modern_relevance: You turn down the bigger apartment, the title, the corner office, because taking it would betray what you value. Bharata shows that dignity can be stronger than ambition.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जटाजूट सिर मुनिपट धारी। महि खनि कुस साँथरी सँवारी॥ असन बसन बासन ब्रत नेमा। करत कठिन रिषिधरम सप्रेमा ॥
translation: सिर पर जटाजूट और शरीर में मुनियों के (वल्कल) वस्त्र धारण कर, पृथ्वी को खोदकर उसके अंदर कुश की आसनी बिछाई। भोजन, वस्त्र, बरतन, व्रत, नियम सभी बातों में वे ऋषियों के कठिन धर्म का प्रेम सहित आचरण करने लगे ॥
english_translation: With matted hair on his head and ascetic garments on his body, they dug the earth and prepared a bed of kusa grass. They began to practice the hard discipline of a sage, with love, in food, clothing, vessels, vows, and rules.
essence: Love can turn hardship into disciplined living.
simple_meaning: They lived like forest sages, with simple clothes, a grass bed, and strict vows. Even the hard discipline of an ascetic life was taken up lovingly.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing hardship as loss to seeing it as chosen training.
modern_relevance: You move into a bare rental after a breakup, with a mattress on the floor and one box of dishes. The simplicity feels harsh at first, until it starts to feel clean.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूषन बसन भोग सुख भूरी। मन तन बचन तजे तिन तूरी॥ अवध राजु सुर राजु सिहाई। दसरथ धनु सुनि धनदु लजाई ॥
translation: गहने-कपड़े और अनेकों प्रकार के भोग-सुखों को मन, तन और वचन से तृण तोड़कर (प्रतिज्ञा करके) त्याग दिया। जिस अयोध्या के राज्य को देवराज इन्द्र सिहाते थे और (जहाँ के राजा) दशरथजी की सम्पत्ति सुनकर कुबेर भी लजा जाते थे, ॥
english_translation: They gave up ornaments, clothes, pleasures, and abundant comforts with body, mind, and speech. Ayodhya's kingdom was so splendid that even Indra coveted it, and hearing of Dasharath's wealth made Kubera ashamed.
essence: True nobility is proven by what you can leave untouched.
simple_meaning: The princes gave up royal luxury completely. Ayodhya was so wealthy and glorious that even heavenly rulers admired it, yet they walked away from all of it.
insight: It shifts attention from status and comfort to the strength needed to release them.
modern_relevance: You sign the promotion letter, then realize the bigger question is what it will cost your peace. This verse remembers the courage to walk away from glitter when your deeper duty asks for less.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहिं पुर बसत भरत बिनु रागा। चंचरीक जिमि चंपक बागा॥ रमा बिलासु राम अनुरागी। तजत बमन जिमि जन बड़भागी ॥
translation: उसी अयोध्यापुरी में भरतजी अनासक्त होकर इस प्रकार निवास कर रहे हैं, जैसे चम्पा के बाग में भौंरा। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्रेमी बड़भागी पुरुष लक्ष्मी के विलास (भोगैश्वर्य) को वमन की भाँति त्याग देते हैं (फिर उसकी ओर ताकते भी नहीं) ॥
english_translation: In that city, Bharat lived without attachment, like a bee in a champak grove. Those devoted to Ram reject the pleasures of wealth like something vomited and never look back.
essence: Real detachment lives in the middle of abundance.
simple_meaning: Bharat lives in Ayodhya without attachment. A person devoted to Ram can enjoy none of the world’s pleasures and still remain fully alive to duty.
insight: It shifts the mind from craving pleasant experiences to remaining free while surrounded by them.
modern_relevance: You walk through a house full of gifts after a breakup, and nothing in the room calls to you anymore. Bharat knows that state: being present where you are, without letting comfort own you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: राम प्रेम भाजन भरतु बड़े न एहिं करतूति। चातक हंस सराहिअत टेंक बिबेक बिभूति ॥
translation: फिर भरतजी तो (स्वयं) श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्रेम के पात्र हैं। वे इस (भोगैश्वर्य त्याग रूप) करनी से बड़े नहीं हुए (अर्थात उनके लिए यह कोई बड़ी बात नहीं है)। (पृथ्वी पर का जल न पीने की) टेक से चातक की और नीर-क्षीर-विवेक की विभूति (शक्ति) से हंस की भी सराहना होती है ॥
english_translation: Bharat is already worthy of Ram's love; this act does not make him great. The chātak is praised for its vow, and the hansa for its discerning power.
essence: Sacrifice reveals worth; it does not create it.
simple_meaning: Bharat's refusal of comfort does not make him great; it only reveals the greatness he already had in Ram's eyes. Like the chātak and hansa, he is praised for a natural excellence.
insight: It shifts the mind from performing goodness to recognising the inner quality that makes selfless action natural.
modern_relevance: You decline the promotion, stay late to help, and quietly give up your own comfort — but the deepest value was never in the visible sacrifice. It was in the character that made that choice possible.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: देह दिनहुँ दिन दूबरि होई। घटइ तेजु बलु मुखछबि सोई॥ नित नव राम प्रेम पनु पीना। बढ़त धरम दलु मनु न मलीना ॥
translation: भरतजी का शरीर दिनों-दिन दुबला होता जाता है। तेज (अन्न, घृत आदि से उत्पन्न होने वाला मेद) घट रहा है। बल और मुख छबि (मुख की कान्ति अथवा शोभा) वैसी ही बनी हुई है। राम प्रेम का प्रण नित्य नया और पुष्ट होता है, धर्म का दल बढ़ता है और मन उदास नहीं है (अर्थात प्रसन्न है) ॥ संस्कृत कोष में 'तेज' का अर्थ मेद मिलता है और यह अर्थ लेने से 'घटइ' के अर्थ में भी किसी प्रकार की खींच-तान नहीं करनी पड़ती।
english_translation: Day by day Bharat's body grows thinner. His vitality and strength decline, yet his face keeps its radiance. His vow of love for Ram grows ever fresh and strong, dharma's force increases, and his mind remains untroubled.
essence: A devoted heart can grow stronger even as the body grows weaker.
simple_meaning: Bharat grows leaner, but his love for Ram grows stronger. His strength and beauty remain, his commitment to dharma increases, and his mind stays cheerful.
insight: It shifts attention from physical condition to the steadiness of commitment, showing that inner discipline can outlast bodily decline.
modern_relevance: You skip meals for weeks while caring for someone in crisis, yet something in you feels cleaner, steadier, more alive. Bharat shows that sacrifice can thin the body without dimming the heart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जिमि जलु निघटत सरद प्रकासे। बिलसत बेतस बनज बिकासे॥ सम दम संजम नियम उपासा। नखत भरत हिय बिमल अकासा ॥
translation: जैसे शरद ऋतु के प्रकाश (विकास) से जल घटता है, किन्तु बेंत शोभा पाते हैं और कमल विकसित होते हैं। शम, दम, संयम, नियम और उपवास आदि भरतजी के हृदयरूपी निर्मल आकाश के नक्षत्र (तारागण) हैं ॥
english_translation: As the autumn light makes the water recede, bamboo shines and lotus blossoms. Calm, self-control, restraint, discipline, and fasting are the stars in Bharat's pure heart-sky.
essence: Restraint can make the heart more radiant, not less.
simple_meaning: Bharat's inner life is so pure that his discipline shines like stars in a clear autumn sky. His restraint doesn't dim him; it makes his character more radiant.
insight: It reframes discipline as something that clarifies character instead of merely denying pleasure.
modern_relevance: You skip the party, eat simply, and keep your routine while everyone else chases noise. Later, people notice your steadiness. What looked like deprivation was quietly polishing you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ध्रुव बिस्वासु अवधि राका सी। स्वामि सुरति सुरबीथि बिकासी॥ राम पेम बिधु अचल अदोषा। सहित समाज सोह नित चोखा ॥
translation: विश्वास ही (उस आकाश में) ध्रुव तारा है, चौदह वर्ष की अवधि (का ध्यान) पूर्णिमा के समान है और स्वामी श्री रामजी की सुरति (स्मृति) आकाशगंगा सरीखी प्रकाशित है। राम प्रेम ही अचल (सदा रहने वाला) और कलंकरहित चन्द्रमा है। वह अपने समाज (नक्षत्रों) सहित नित्य सुंदर सुशोभित है ॥
english_translation: Trust is the fixed star in that sky; remembrance of the Lord is the shining Milky Way. Love for Ram is the steady, spotless moon, always lovely with its companion stars.
essence: Trust and love for Ram become the sky that holds everything in place.
simple_meaning: Trust, remembrance of Ram, and love for Ram are compared to stars and the moon in a night sky. They keep a life steady, bright, and beautiful.
insight: It shifts devotion from emotion alone to a stable inner orientation that can guide your whole life.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone in the dark, waiting for a message that will settle your heart. This verse says something steadier can hold you: trust, remembrance, and love that do not flicker.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत रहनि समुझनि करतूती। भगति बिरति गुन बिमल बिभूती॥ बरनत सकल सुकबि सकुचाहीं। सेस गनेस गिरा गमु नाहीं ॥
translation: भरतजी की रहनी, समझ, करनी, भक्ति, वैराग्य, निर्मल, गुण और ऐश्वर्य का वर्णन करने में सभी सुकवि सकुचाते हैं, क्योंकि वहाँ (औरों की तो बात ही क्या) स्वयं शेष, गणेश और सरस्वती की भी पहुँच नहीं है ॥
english_translation: All good poets hesitate to describe Bharat's way of life, understanding, conduct, devotion, non-attachment, pure virtues, and splendour. Even Shesha, Ganesha, and Saraswati cannot reach the end of it.
essence: Bharat's devotion is so complete that language itself gives up.
simple_meaning: Bharat's life is so full of devotion, virtue, and non-attachment that even the greatest poets cannot fully describe it.
insight: It shifts attention from public achievement to the depth of character revealed in selfless service.
modern_relevance: You watch someone quietly care for a parent, a partner, or a cause for years without asking for credit. Their goodness is hard to summarize because it lives in action, not performance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नित पूजत प्रभु पाँवरी प्रीति न हृदयँ समाति। मागि मागि आयसु करत राज काज बहु भाँति ॥
translation: वे नित्य प्रति प्रभु की पादुकाओं का पूजन करते हैं, हृदय में प्रेम समाता नहीं है। पादुकाओं से आज्ञा माँग-माँगकर वे बहुत प्रकार (सब प्रकार के) राज-काज करते हैं ॥
english_translation: They keep worshipping the Lord's sandals every day; their hearts cannot contain their love. Asking the sandals for permission again and again, they carry out all royal duties in many ways.
essence: Love makes power kneel and duty become worship.
simple_meaning: Bharat worships Ram's sandals every day because his love is too deep to hold inside. Even while ruling, he acts only after seeking their permission.
insight: It shifts leadership from self-importance to reverent service under a higher claim.
modern_relevance: You sit in a meeting chair that should have been someone else's, and every decision still feels borrowed. Bharat shows what it means to lead without claiming the seat as yours.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुलक गात हियँ सिय रघुबीरू। जीह नामु जप लोचन नीरू॥ लखन राम सिय कानन बसहीं। भरतु भवन बसि तप तनु कसहीं ॥
translation: शरीर पुलकित है, हृदय में श्री सीता-रामजी हैं। जीभ राम नाम जप रही है, नेत्रों में प्रेम का जल भरा है। लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामजी और सीताजी तो वन में बसते हैं, परन्तु भरतजी घर ही में रहकर तप के द्वारा शरीर को कस रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The body trembles with love; Sita and Ram live in the heart. The tongue repeats Ram's name; the eyes overflow with tears. Lakshman, Ram, and Sita live in the forest, but Bharat lives at home and burns his body with austerity.
essence: True devotion makes even home feel like exile.
simple_meaning: Bharat's devotion is so intense that his body, speech, and tears all show it. Though he remains in the palace, he lives like an ascetic because his heart is with Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from outward location to inward attachment: where your heart lives matters more than where your body stands.
modern_relevance: You keep your phone on silent at a family wedding because your mind is elsewhere, tied to someone you miss. Bharat knows that kind of divided presence — except his longing has become devotion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दोउ दिसि समुझि कहत सबु लोगू। सब बिधि भरत सराहन जोगू॥ सुनि ब्रत नेम साधु सकुचाहीं। देखि दसा मुनिराज लजाहीं ॥
translation: दोनों ओर की स्थिति समझकर सब लोग कहते हैं कि भरतजी सब प्रकार से सराहने योग्य हैं। उनके व्रत और नियमों को सुनकर साधु-संत भी सकुचा जाते हैं और उनकी स्थिति देखकर मुनिराज भी लज्जित होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Everyone, seeing both sides, says that Bharat is worthy of praise in every way. Hearing of his vows and restraints, even holy people grow modest, and seeing his condition, even great sages feel humbled.
essence: Restraint so complete can make even the wise feel small.
simple_meaning: Everyone sees Bharat as worthy of praise. His vows and self-restraint are so deep that even saints and sages feel humbled before him.
insight: It shifts attention from public success to the quiet authority of disciplined conduct.
modern_relevance: You keep your promise when no one is watching, and later people sense it without being told. A calm, disciplined life can make others feel their own noise.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परम पुनीत भरत आचरनू। मधुर मंजु मुद मंगल कhरनू॥ हरन कठिन कलि कलुष कलेसू। महामोह निसि दलन दिनेसू ॥
translation: भरतजी का परम पवित्र आचरण (चरित्र) मधुर, सुंदर और आनंद-मंगलों का करने वाला है। कलियुग के कठिन पापों और क्लेशों को हरने वाला है। महामोह रूपी रात्रि को नष्ट करने के लिए सूर्य के समान है ॥
english_translation: Bharat's conduct is supremely pure, sweet, beautiful, and a maker of auspicious joy. It removes the harsh stains and suffering of Kali Yuga and is like the sun that drives away the night of great delusion.
essence: Bharat's purity becomes a light that drives out confusion.
simple_meaning: Bharat's way of living is pure, sweet, and deeply uplifting. It removes suffering and confusion, like sunlight ending night.
insight: It shifts attention from loud success to the quiet power of lived integrity.
modern_relevance: You watch someone stay honest in a room full of compromise, and the atmosphere changes. Their steadiness doesn't just help them — it makes everyone else breathe easier.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: पाप पुंज कुंजर मृगराजू। समन सकल संताप समाजू॥ जन रंजन भंजन भव भारू। राम सनेह सुधाकर सारू ॥
translation: पाप समूह रूपी हाथी के लिए सिंह है। सारे संतापों के दल का नाश करने वाला है। भक्तों को आनंद देने वाला और भव के भार (संसार के दुःख) का भंजन करने वाला तथा श्री राम प्रेम रूपी चन्द्रमा का सार (अमृत) है ॥
english_translation: The lion that destroys the elephant of accumulated sin, the remover of all suffering, the delight of devotees, the breaker of the burden of worldly existence, is the essence of the moon of Ram's love.
essence: Ram's love is both fierce protection and deep relief.
simple_meaning: Ram's love is compared to a lion that destroys the elephant of sin, removes all suffering, delights devotees, and breaks the burden of worldly life.
insight: It shifts devotion from sentiment to power: love for Ram becomes the force that clears suffering and steadies the heart.
modern_relevance: You sit beside someone in the hospital waiting room, exhausted by worry and unable to fix anything. The mind softens when love is stronger than panic; that is the kind of relief this verse offers.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सिय राम प्रेम पियूष पूरन होत जनमु न भरत को। मुनि मन अगम जम नियम सम दम बिषम ब्रत आचरत को॥ दुख दाह दारिद दंभ दूषन सुजस मिस अपहरत को। कलिकाल तुलसी से सठन्हि हठि राम सनमुख करत को॥
translation: श्री सीतारामजी के प्रेमरूपी अमृत से परिपूर्ण भरतजी का जन्म यदि न होता, तो मुनियों के मन को भी अगम यम, नियम, शम, दम आदि कठिन व्रतों का आचरण कौन करता? दुःख, संताप, दरिद्रता, दम्भ आदि दोषों को अपने सुयश के बहाने कौन हरण करता? तथा कलिकाल में तुलसीदास जैसे शठों को हठपूर्वक कौन श्री रामजी के सम्मुख करता?
english_translation: If Bharat had not been born, full of the nectar of love for Siya and Ram, who would practice the hard vows of yama, niyama, shama, dama, and the rest that even sages find hard to keep? Who would remove sorrow, burning pain, poverty, pride, and other faults under the pretext of his good fame? And in Kali Yuga, who would stubbornly turn stubborn people like Tulsidas toward Ram?
essence: Bharat's love turns devotion into discipline for everyone around him.
simple_meaning: Bharat's love for Ram becomes a living example that inspires hard self-discipline, removes faults, and even turns stubborn people toward Ram.
insight: It shifts devotion from feeling to transforming force: love becomes the source of conduct, healing, and influence.
modern_relevance: You watch someone keep a painful promise with quiet dignity, and it changes the room. Their loyalty makes self-control look possible instead of harsh.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भरत चरित करि नेमु तुलसी जो सादर सुनहिं। सीय राम पद पेमु अवसि होइ भव रस बिरति ॥
translation: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- जो कोई भरतजी के चरित्र को नियम से आदरपूर्वक सुनेंगे, उनको अवश्य ही श्रीसीतारामजी के चरणों में प्रेम होगा और सांसारिक विषय रस से वैराग्य होगा ॥
english_translation: Tulsidas says: whoever listens to Bharat's character with reverence and discipline will surely develop love for Sita and Ram's feet and grow detached from worldly pleasures.
essence: Bharat's example turns respect into love and loosens attachment to pleasure.
simple_meaning: Careful, respectful listening to Bharat's life awakens love for Ram and weakens attachment to worldly pleasures.
insight: It shifts attention from consuming stories for entertainment to receiving them as training for the heart.
modern_relevance: You hear a story about someone who gave up power for love, and it quietly changes what you admire. That kind of admiration can make ambition feel smaller and devotion feel real.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मूलं धर्मतरोर्विवेकजलधेः पूर्णेन्दुमानन्ददं वैराग्याम्बुजभास्करं ह्यघघनध्वान्तापहं तापहम् । मोहाम्भोधरपूगपाटनविधौ स्वःसम्भवं शंकरं वंदे ब्रह्मकुलं कलंकशमनं श्री रामभूपप्रियम् ॥
translation: धर्म रूपी वृक्ष के मूल, विवेक रूपी समुद्र को आनंद देने वाले पूर्णचन्द्र, वैराग्य रूपी कमल के (विकसित करने वाले) सूर्य, पाप रूपी घोर अंधकार को निश्चय ही मिटाने वाले, तीनों तापों को हरने वाले, मोह रूपी बादलों के समूह को छिन्न-भिन्न करने की विधि (क्रिया) में आकाश से उत्पन्न पवन स्वरूप, ब्रह्माजी के वंशज (आत्मज) तथा कलंकनाशक, महाराज श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्रिय श्री शंकरजी की मैं वंदना करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I bow to Shankar, born of the sky, destroyer of stain, beloved of Sri Ram, who is the root of the tree of dharma, the moon that delights discernment, the sun that makes non-attachment bloom, the remover of the thick darkness of delusion, and the one who burns away all suffering.
essence: Shiva is praised as the force that clears confusion and awakens release.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas praises Shiva as the source of dharma, clarity, non-attachment, and relief from suffering. He bows to Shiva as Ram's beloved and as the one who destroys delusion.
insight: It shifts the mind from emotional fog to steadier seeing through devotion and praise.
modern_relevance: You are spiraling after bad news, and everything feels foggy. This verse points to the kind of reverence that can cut through mental noise and restore your footing.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सान्द्रानन्दपयोदसौभगतनुं पीताम्बरं सुंदरं पाणौ बाणशरासनं कटिलसत्तूणीरभारं वरम् । राजीवायतलोचनं धृतजटाजूटेन संशोभितं सीतालक्ष्मणसंयुतं पथिगतं रामाभिरामं भजे ॥
translation: जिनका शरीर जलयुक्त मेघों के समान सुंदर (श्यामवर्ण) एवं आनंदघन है, जो सुंदर (वल्कल का) पीत वस्त्र धारण किए हैं, जिनके हाथों में बाण और धनुष हैं, कमर उत्तम तरकस के भार से सुशोभित है, कमल के समान विशाल नेत्र हैं और मस्तक पर जटाजूट धारण किए हैं, उन अत्यन्त शोभायमान श्री सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित मार्ग में चलते हुए आनंद देने वाले श्री रामचन्द्रजी को मैं भजता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I worship Ramchandra, radiant and blissful, beautiful in yellow garments, with bow, arrows, and quiver in hand, eyes wide like lotus petals, hair in a matted crown, walking the path with Sita and Lakshman.
essence: Ram is most beautiful when he walks the hard road with his loved ones.
simple_meaning: The speaker offers a devotional praise of Ram: beautiful, armed, radiant, and walking with Sita and Lakshman.
insight: It turns attention from Ram's royal status to his living presence beside those who love him.
modern_relevance: You’re walking through a hard season with two people depending on you, and you still choose dignity, steadiness, and tenderness. That is the image this verse holds up.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: उमा राम गुन गूढ़ पंडित मुनि पावहिं बिरति। पावहिं मोह बिमूढ़ जे हरि बिमुख न धर्म रति॥
translation: हे पार्वती! श्री रामजी के गुण गूढ़ हैं, पण्डित और मुनि उन्हें समझकर वैराग्य प्राप्त करते हैं, परन्तु जो भगवान से विमुख हैं और जिनका धर्म में प्रेम नहीं है, वे महामूढ़ (उन्हें सुनकर) मोह को प्राप्त होते हैं।
english_translation: O Parvati, Ram's qualities are profound. Learned sages gain detachment by understanding them, but those who turn away from Hari and feel no love for dharma fall into delusion.
essence: Ram's nature frees the receptive mind and entangles the resistant one.
simple_meaning: Ram's qualities are so deep that wise people become less attached by reflecting on them. But people who turn away from him and dislike dharma become lost in confusion.
insight: It shifts attention from mere hearing to the inner result of how you receive truth.
modern_relevance: You can sit with a wise teacher's words and feel calmer, or scroll past them in irritation and end up more tangled than before. What you lean toward changes what your mind becomes.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: पुर नर भरत प्रीति मैं गाई। मति अनुरूप अनूप सुहाई॥ अब प्रभु चरित सुनहु अति पावन। करत जे बन सुर नर मुनि भावन ॥
translation: पुरवासियों के और भरतजी के अनुपम और सुंदर प्रेम का मैंने अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार गान किया। अब देवता, मनुष्य और मुनियों के मन को भाने वाले प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के वे अत्यन्त पवित्र चरित्र सुनो, जिन्हें वे वन में कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: I have sung, according to my understanding, the incomparable and lovely love of the people of the city and of Bharat. Now listen to the supremely pure deeds of Lord Ram, which delight gods, humans, and sages, as he lives in the forest.
essence: Praise gives way to the deeds that make devotion visible.
simple_meaning: The poet closes one part of the story and invites you into Ram's pure forest deeds, which please every kind of being.
insight: It shifts the focus from praise of supporters to the living example of Ram's conduct in exile.
modern_relevance: You finish speaking about the people who stood by you, then turn to the harder part: what you must do next, quietly and purely, without applause.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: एक बार चुनि कुसुम सुहाए। निज कर भूषन राम बनाए॥ सीतहि पहिराए प्रभु सादर। बैठे फटिक सिला पर सुंदर ॥
translation: एक बार सुंदर फूल चुनकर श्री रामजी ने अपने हाथों से भाँति-भाँति के गहने बनाए और सुंदर स्फटिक शिला पर बैठे हुए प्रभु ने आदर के साथ वे गहने श्री सीताजी को पहनाए ॥
english_translation: Once, choosing lovely flowers, Lord Ram made ornaments with his own hands. Sitting beautifully on a crystal rock, the Lord respectfully put those ornaments on Sita.
essence: True love adorns the beloved with its own hands.
simple_meaning: Ram lovingly makes ornaments from flowers and places them on Sita himself, showing care, respect, and tenderness.
insight: It shifts love from grand words to humble, visible care.
modern_relevance: You notice someone you love is tired, so you make tea, fix their collar, and quietly help before they ask. Small care can carry the deepest devotion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुरपति सुत धरि बायस बेषा। सठ चाहत रघुपति बल देखा॥ जिमि पिपीलिका सागर थाहा। महा मंदमति पावन चाहा ॥
translation: देवराज इन्द्र का मूर्ख पुत्र जयन्त कौए का रूप धरकर श्री रघुनाथजी का बल देखना चाहता है। जैसे महान मंदबुद्धि चींटी समुद्र का थाह पाना चाहती हो ॥
english_translation: Indra's foolish son took the form of a crow and wanted to test Raghunath's strength. It was like a tiny ant trying to measure the ocean's depth.
essence: Ego makes even a tiny challenge look brave.
simple_meaning: A proud fool tries to test Ram's power, but the effort is absurdly out of scale with his own smallness.
insight: It warns against testing greatness from a place of arrogance and poor judgment.
modern_relevance: Someone with almost no context walks into a room and tries to challenge the person who has spent years mastering the field. The mismatch is obvious before anyone speaks.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीता चरन चोंच हति भागा। मूढ़ मंदमति कारन कागा॥ चला रुधिर रघुनायक जाना। सींक धनुष सायक संधाना ॥
translation: वह मूढ़, मंदबुद्धि कारण से (भगवान के बल की परीक्षा करने के लिए) बना हुआ कौआ सीताजी के चरणों में चोंच मारकर भागा। जब रक्त बह चला, तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने जाना और धनुष पर सींक (सरकंडे) का बाण संधान किया ॥ दोहा :
english_translation: The foolish crow pecked Sita's foot and fled. When blood flowed, Ram noticed and fitted a reed-arrow to his bow.
essence: Ram turns instantly when suffering touches the one he protects.
simple_meaning: A foolish crow attacks Sita and runs away. The moment blood appears, Ram notices and prepares to shoot.
insight: It shows how quickly Ram responds when innocence is harmed.
modern_relevance: Someone you love gets hurt in a careless moment, and your whole body goes alert before you even think. Love notices pain fast.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अति कृपाल रघुनायक सदा दीन पर नेह। ता सन आइ कीन्ह छलु मूरख अवगुन गेह ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी, जो अत्यन्त ही कृपालु हैं और जिनका दीनों पर सदा प्रेम रहता है, उनसे भी उस अवगुणों के घर मूर्ख जयन्त ने आकर छल किया ॥
english_translation: The gracious Lord of Raghu always loves the humble, yet that fool Jayanta came and tried to deceive him.
essence: Ram’s grace welcomes the humble and unmasks the fool.
simple_meaning: Ram is naturally kind to the humble, but Jayanta still came in disguise and tried to deceive him.
insight: It shifts you from testing goodness to trusting it, and from pride to humility.
modern_relevance: You meet someone kind, then still decide to test them with a lie or a game. The verse catches that self-defeating move: grace is not weakness, and deceit only exposes your own fault.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रेरित मंत्र ब्रह्मसर धावा। चला भाजि बायस भय पावा॥ धरि निज रूप गयउ पितु पाहीं। राम बिमुख राखा तेहि नाहीं ॥
translation: मंत्र से प्रेरित होकर वह ब्रह्मबाण दौड़ा। कौआ भयभीत होकर भाग चला। वह अपना असली रूप धरकर पिता इन्द्र के पास गया, पर श्री रामजी का विरोधी जानकर इन्द्र ने उसको नहीं रखा ॥
english_translation: Driven by the mantra, the Brahmastra rushed forward. The crow fled in fear. Taking his true form, he went to his father Indra, but Indra would not shelter one who opposed Ram.
essence: Opposing Ram leaves even refuge unable to hold you.
simple_meaning: The crow escapes the weapon, returns to his father in his real form, and is rejected for opposing Ram.
insight: It shows that wrongdoing strips away protection, no matter how much power or lineage you have.
modern_relevance: You try to hide behind status, family, or connections after crossing a line. But when your actions have broken trust, even your strongest support can refuse you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भा निरास उपजी मन त्रासा। जथा चक्र भय रिषि दुर्बासा॥ ब्रह्मधाम सिवपुर सब लोका। फिरा श्रमित ब्याकुल भय सोका ॥
translation: तब वह निराश हो गया, उसके मन में भय उत्पन्न हो गया, जैसे दुर्वासा ऋषि को चक्र से भय हुआ था। वह ब्रह्मलोक, शिवलोक आदि समस्त लोकों में थका हुआ और भय-शोक से व्याकुल होकर भागता फिरा ॥
english_translation: Then he lost all hope, and fear rose in his mind, just as Durvasa was frightened by the discus. He wandered, exhausted and distressed by fear and sorrow, through Brahmaloka, Shivaloka, and all the worlds.
essence: Fear keeps running even after the danger has passed.
simple_meaning: The frightened being loses hope and runs through every realm, exhausted and shaken. Fear and sorrow keep driving it onward.
insight: It shows how guilt and fear can turn escape into suffering, making the mind restless instead of free.
modern_relevance: You make one mistake, then spend the rest of the day replaying it, checking messages, and imagining worst-case reactions. Fear starts running your whole mind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: काहूँ बैठन कहा न ओही। राखि को सकइ राम कर द्रोही ॥ मातु मृत्यु पितु समन समाना। सुधा होइ बिष सुनु हरिजाना ॥
translation: (पर रखना तो दूर रहा) किसी ने उसे बैठने तक के लिए नहीं कहा। श्री रामजी के द्रोही को कौन रख सकता है? (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं-) है गरुड़ ! सुनिए, उसके लिए माता मृत्यु के समान,
english_translation: No one even offered him a seat. Who can shelter one who is hostile to Ram? Listen, Garuda: for such a person, mother becomes death, father becomes Yama, and nectar turns to poison.
essence: Opposition to Ram makes even nourishment feel like harm.
simple_meaning: A person cut off from Ram loses all support and comfort. Even the most loving things in life can feel hostile and painful.
insight: It shifts attention from outer support to the inner relation that makes support feel alive or dead.
modern_relevance: You can have people around you, food on the table, and a full calendar — yet still feel everything has gone wrong inside. When your heart turns against what is true, even comfort starts to sting.
speaker: Kak Bhushundi

verse_text: पिता यमराज के समान और अमृत विष के समान हो जाता है ॥ मित्र करइ सत रिपु कै करनी। ता कहँ बिबुधनदी बैतरनी॥ सब जगु ताहि अनलहु ते ताता। जो रघुबीर बिमुख सुनु भ्राता ॥
translation: मित्र सैकड़ों शत्रुओं की सी करनी करने लगता है। देवनदी गंगाजी उसके लिए वैतरणी (यमपुरी की नदी) हो जाती है। हे भाई! सुनिए, जो श्री रघुनाथजी के विमुख होता है, समस्त जगत उनके लिए अग्नि से भी अधिक गरम (जलाने वाला) हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: A father becomes like Yama and nectar turns to poison. A friend acts like a hundred enemies, and the sacred river becomes the river of judgment. O brother, listen: for one who turns away from Raghubir, the whole world burns hotter than fire.
essence: Turning away from Ram makes even blessings feel hostile.
simple_meaning: Turning away from Ram distorts everything. What should help you can feel harmful, and even the world itself becomes unbearable.
insight: It shifts attention from outer comforts to the direction of your heart.
modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the praise, the perfect meal — and still feel strangely hollow. When your center is off, even good things lose their sweetness.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: नारद देखा बिकल जयंता। लगि दया कोमल चित संता॥ पठवा तुरत राम पहिं ताही। कहेसि पुकारि प्रनत हित पाही ॥
translation: नारदजी ने जयन्त को व्याकुल देखा तो उन्हें दया आ गई, क्योंकि संतों का चित्त बड़ा कोमल होता है। उन्होंने उसे (समझाकर) तुरंत श्री रामजी के पास भेज दिया। उसने (जाकर) पुकारकर कहा- हे शरणागत के हितकारी! मेरी रक्षा कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Narada saw Jayaanta in distress and felt compassion, for the hearts of saints are tender. He sent him at once to Ram, and Jayaanta cried out, 'O protector of the surrendered, save me.'
essence: Compassion sends the frightened straight to refuge.
simple_meaning: Narada sees Jayaanta in distress, feels compassion, and sends him straight to Ram, who protects the surrendered.
insight: It shifts your response from judgment to rescue, making compassion an action rather than a feeling.
modern_relevance: You notice a friend spiraling after a mistake and resist the urge to lecture. You calm them, point them toward help, and let mercy do what shame never could.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आतुर सभय गहेसि पद जाई। त्राहि त्राहि दयाल रघुराई॥ अतुलित बल अतुलित प्रभुताई। मैं मतिमंद जानि नहीं पाई ॥
translation: आतुर और भयभीत जयन्त ने जाकर श्री रामजी के चरण पकड़ लिए (और कहा-) हे दयालु रघुनाथजी! रक्षा कीजिए, रक्षा कीजिए। आपके अतुलित बल और आपकी अतुलित प्रभुता (सामर्थ्य) को मैं मन्दबुद्धि जान नहीं पाया था ॥
english_translation: Distressed and frightened, Jayaanta fell at Ram's feet and cried, 'Save me, save me, merciful Raghurai! I did not understand your immeasurable strength and immeasurable majesty, foolish as I was.'
essence: Fear dissolves when pride gives way to Ram's feet.
simple_meaning: Jayaanta, shaken and afraid, falls at Ram's feet and asks for protection. He admits he failed to understand Ram's power and greatness.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to surrender, making room for grace and correction.
modern_relevance: After a harsh mistake, you walk into the room with your head down and finally say, 'I was wrong. Please help me fix this.' That honesty changes everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निज कृत कर्म जनित फल पायउँ। अब प्रभु पाहि सरन तकि आयउँ॥ सुनि कृपाल अति आरत बानी। एकनयन करि तजा भवानी ॥
translation: अपने कर्म से उत्पन्न हुआ फल मैंने पा लिया। अब हे प्रभु! मेरी रक्षा कीजिए। मैं आपकी शरण तक कर आया हूँ। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे पार्वती! कृपालु श्री रघुनाथजी ने उसकी अत्यंत आर्त्त (दुःख भरी) वाणी सुनकर उसे एक आँख का काना करके छोड़ दिया ॥ सोरठा :
english_translation: I have received the fruit born of my own actions. Now, Lord, protect me; I have come to your refuge. Hearing his deeply distressed plea, the compassionate Raghunath spared him, leaving him one-eyed, O Parvati.
essence: Taking responsibility opens the door to mercy.
simple_meaning: Jayanta admits he has received the result of his own wrongdoing and asks Ram for protection. Ram hears his desperate plea and shows mercy instead of killing him.
insight: It teaches you to stop self-justifying, accept responsibility, and move toward humble surrender instead of pride.
modern_relevance: You finally admit the mess was partly yours, not just everyone else's. The moment you stop defending yourself and ask for help, the room changes.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: कीन्ह मोह बस द्रोह जद्यपि तेहि कर बध उचित। प्रभु छाड़ेउ करि छोह को कृपाल रघुबीर सम ॥
translation: उसने मोहवश द्रोह किया था, इसलिए यद्यपि उसका वध ही उचित था, पर प्रभु ने कृपा करके उसे छोड़ दिया। श्री रामजी के समान कृपालु और कौन होगा? ॥
english_translation: He acted out of delusion and committed hostility, so his death was deserved; yet the Lord, full of compassion, spared him. Who is as merciful as Raghubir?
essence: Compassion can overrule what punishment demands.
simple_meaning: Even when someone has done wrong and deserves punishment, Ram chooses compassion and lets him go.
insight: It shifts the mind from automatic retaliation to measured mercy.
modern_relevance: Someone lies to you, and every part of you wants to cut them off. You may still choose a response that is firm without becoming cruel.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रघुपति चित्रकूट बसि नाना। चरित किए श्रुति सुधा समाना॥ बहुरि राम अस मन अनुमाना। होइहि भीर सबहिं मोहि जाना ॥
translation: चित्रकूट में बसकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने बहुत से चरित्र किए, जो कानों को अमृत के समान (प्रिय) हैं। फिर (कुछ समय पश्चात) श्री रामजी ने मन में ऐसा अनुमान किया कि मुझे सब लोग जान गए हैं, इससे (यहाँ) बड़ी भीड़ हो जाएगी ॥
english_translation: Dwelling in Chitrakoot, Lord Raghupati performed many deeds, sweet as nectar to the ears. Then Ram thought in his mind, "Now everyone knows me; there will be a great crowd here."
essence: True grace sometimes moves away before it becomes a spectacle.
simple_meaning: Ram lived in Chitrakoot and performed many beautiful deeds there. Then he felt that people had come to know him, so the place would soon become crowded.
insight: It teaches you to protect a sacred space before popularity turns it into noise.
modern_relevance: You finally find a quiet café where you can think, and then the room fills with people who recognize you. Sometimes the right move is to leave before attention destroys the calm you came for.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकल मुनिन्ह सन बिदा कराई। सीता सहित चले द्वौ भाई॥ अत्रि के आश्रम जब प्रभु गयऊ। सुनत महामुनि हरषित भयऊ ॥
translation: (इसलिए) सब मुनियों से विदा लेकर सीताजी सहित दोनों भाई चले! जब प्रभु अत्रिजी के आश्रम में गए, तो उनका आगमन सुनते ही महामुनि हर्षित हो गए ॥
english_translation: After taking leave of all the sages, the two brothers set out with Sita. When the Lord reached Atri's hermitage, the great sage was delighted on hearing of his arrival.
essence: Their presence itself awakens joy before they even arrive.
simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman leave the sages and continue their forest journey. When they reach Atri's hermitage, the sage feels great joy at hearing they have come.
insight: It frames arrival itself as blessing, preparing the emotional warmth of the next encounter.
modern_relevance: You hear that someone you deeply respect is on the way, and your whole day changes before they even arrive. That quiet happiness is already part of the meeting.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुलकित गात अत्रि उठि धाए। देखि रामु आतुर चलि आए॥ करत दंडवत मुनि उर लाए। प्रेम बारि द्वौ जन अन्हवाए ॥
translation: शरीर पुलकित हो गया, अत्रिजी उठकर दौड़े। उन्हें दौड़े आते देखकर श्री रामजी और भी शीघ्रता से चले आए। दण्डवत करते हुए ही श्री रामजी को (उठाकर) मुनि ने हृदय से लगा लिया और प्रेमाश्रुओं के जल से दोनों जनों को (दोनों भाइयों को) नहला दिया ॥
english_translation: Atri's body thrilled with joy as he rose and ran forward. Seeing him hurry toward them, Ram and Lakshman came even faster. The sage bowed down and embraced Ram to his heart, bathing both brothers in the waters of his love-filled tears.
essence: Love runs out first, and tears become welcome.
simple_meaning: Atri greets Ram with overwhelming love, bows down, embraces him, and weeps tears of joy over both brothers.
insight: It shows love as immediate, bodily, and unashamed — devotion that moves before speech.
modern_relevance: You see someone you love after months apart, and your whole body moves before your mind does. That rush of recognition is what this scene holds.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि राम छबि नयन जुड़ाने। सादर निज आश्रम तब आने॥ करि पूजा कहि बचन सुहाए। दिए मूल फल प्रभु मन भाए ॥
translation: श्री रामजी की छवि देखकर मुनि के नेत्र शीतल हो गए। तब वे उनको आदरपूर्वक अपने आश्रम में ले आए। पूजन करके सुंदर वचन कहकर मुनि ने मूल और फल दिए, जो प्रभु के मन को बहुत रुचे ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ram's beauty, the sage's eyes became filled with delight. He then respectfully brought Him to his hermitage. After worshipping Him and speaking gentle words, the sage offered roots and fruits, which pleased the Lord greatly.
essence: Simple offerings become precious when they come from devotion.
simple_meaning: The sage sees Ram, welcomes Him with honor, worships Him, speaks kindly, and offers simple food that Ram gladly accepts.
insight: It shifts attention from lavish display to sincere welcome and heartfelt offering.
modern_relevance: You open the door to someone you deeply respect, and suddenly even tea and fruit feel like an offering. Care changes the ordinary into something memorable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु आसन आसीन भरि लोचन सोभा निरखि। मुनिबर परम प्रबीन जोरि पानि अस्तुति करत ॥
translation: प्रभु आसन पर विराजमान हैं। नेत्र भरकर उनकी शोभा देखकर परम प्रवीण मुनि श्रेष्ठ हाथ जोड़कर स्तुति करने लगे ॥
english_translation: The Lord sat on the seat. The wise sage filled his eyes with that beauty and, joining his hands, began to praise him.
essence: Seeing the divine clearly leaves only praise.
simple_meaning: Ram sits before the sage, and the sage is so moved by his beauty that he joins his hands and begins to praise him.
insight: It shifts attention from analysis to reverent recognition.
