modern_relevance: You finally meet someone whose presence feels bigger than words. Before you can even think, gratitude rises and your hands come together in respect.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नमामि भक्त वत्सलं। कृपालु शील कोमलं॥ भजामि ते पदांबुजं। अकामिनां स्वधामदं ॥
translation: हे भक्त वत्सल! हे कृपालु! हे कोमल स्वभाव वाले! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ। निष्काम पुरुषों को अपना परमधाम देने वाले आपके चरण कमलों को मैं भजता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I bow to the one who loves devotees, who is compassionate and gentle. I worship your lotus feet, which give their own abode to those without desire.
essence: Ram gives his own home to the one who asks for nothing.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as gentle, compassionate, and loving toward devotees. Those who let go of desire receive his own supreme abode.
insight: It shifts devotion from transaction to surrender: release desire, and the heart finds its home.
modern_relevance: You finally stop chasing approval after a long season of proving yourself. In that quiet, you discover that the deepest welcome comes when you are no longer bargaining for it.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: निकाम श्याम सुंदरं। भवांबुनाथ मंदरं॥ प्रफुल्ल कंज लोचनं। मदादि दोष मोचनं ॥
translation: आप नितान्त सुंदर श्याम, संसार (आवागमन) रूपी समुद्र को मथने के लिए मंदराचल रूप, फूले हुए कमल के समान नेत्रों वाले और मद आदि दोषों से छुड़ाने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: You are utterly beautiful and dark-hued, like Mount Mandara for churning the ocean of becoming. Your eyes are like blooming lotuses, and you free people from pride and other flaws.
essence: His beauty does what pride cannot survive.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as dark, beautiful, lotus-eyed, and able to free people from pride and other inner flaws.
insight: It turns admiration into surrender and shows that real greatness clears away self-importance.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm makes your own ego feel loud. Instead of trying to impress, you soften. Some presences do not inflate you; they purify you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: प्रलंब बाहु विक्रमं। प्रभोऽप्रमेय वैभवं॥ निषंग चाप सायकं। धरं त्रिलोक नायकं ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! आपकी लंबी भुजाओं का पराक्रम और आपका ऐश्वर्य अप्रमेय (बुद्धि के परे अथवा असीम) है। आप तरकस और धनुष-बाण धारण करने वाले तीनों लोकों के स्वामी, ॥
english_translation: O Lord, your long-armed valor and immeasurable glory are beyond thought. You bear quiver, bow, and arrows, and you are the lord of the three worlds.
essence: Power becomes holy when it protects without limit.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as mighty, limitless, and armed with bow and arrows. He is the ruler of all three worlds.
insight: It shifts reverence toward power that is disciplined, protective, and beyond calculation.
modern_relevance: A child feels safe because a parent stands at the door after a hard conversation. Strength is not only force; it is the presence that can hold danger without flinching.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: दिनेश वंश मंडनं। महेश चाप खंडनं॥ मुनींद्र संत रंजनं। सुरारि वृंद भंजनं ॥
translation: सूर्यवंश के भूषण, महादेवजी के धनुष को तोड़ने वाले, मुनिराजों और संतों को आनंद देने वाले तथा देवताओं के शत्रु असुरों के समूह का नाश करने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: The ornament of the solar dynasty, the one who broke Shiva's bow, the delight of sages and saints, and the destroyer of the hosts of hostile beings.
essence: True nobility is known by what it can break and whom it can uplift.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the glory of the solar dynasty, the one who broke Shiva's bow, the joy of saints, and the destroyer of hostile forces.
insight: It shifts admiration from status alone to the ability to defend dharma and remove harm.
modern_relevance: At a family gathering, someone keeps retelling your old win like it defines you. This verse reminds you that real stature is not just reputation — it is the power to protect what is good and end what is false.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मनोज वैरि वंदितं। अजादि देव सेवितं॥ विशुद्ध बोध विग्रहं। समस्त दूषणापहं ॥
translation: आप कामदेव के शत्रु महादेवजी के द्वारा वंदित, ब्रह्मा आदि देवताओं से सेवित, विशुद्ध ज्ञानमय विग्रह और समस्त दोषों को नष्ट करने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: You are worshipped by Shiva, served by Brahma and the other radiant beings, a pure embodiment of knowledge, and the remover of every flaw.
essence: Purity itself becomes power when every flaw falls away.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the one worshipped by Shiva, served by Brahma and other radiant beings, pure in wisdom, and free of all faults.
insight: It shifts attention from status to inner purity, showing that true worth is recognised by character, not display.
modern_relevance: When you feel pressured to prove yourself with noise, this verse points to a quieter kind of authority: the kind that needs no self-promotion because its purity speaks for itself.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: नमामि इंदिरा पतिं। सुखाकरं सतां गतिं॥ भजे सशक्ति सानुजं। शची पति प्रियानुजं ॥
translation: हे लक्ष्मीपते! हे सुखों की खान और सत्पुरुषों की एकमात्र गति! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ! हे शचीपति (इन्द्र) के प्रिय छोटे भाई (वामनजी)! स्वरूपा-शक्ति श्री सीताजी और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित आपको मैं भजता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I bow to the Lord of Lakshmi, the source of joy and the refuge of the good. I worship him with his power and his younger brother, the beloved younger brother of Shachi's lord.
essence: Ram is not only majestic; he is the refuge that gathers love around him.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the source of joy and the refuge of good people, and the speaker worships him together with his power and his brother Lakshman.
insight: It shifts worship from abstract greatness to a living relationship of refuge, power, and companionship.
modern_relevance: You reach for something steady after a hard day, and it is not just power you want — it is warmth, loyalty, and a presence that makes life feel held.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: त्वदंघ्रि मूल ये नराः। भजंति हीन मत्सराः॥ पतंति नो भवार्णवे। वितर्क वीचि संकुले ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य मत्सर (डाह) रहित होकर आपके चरण कमलों का सेवन करते हैं, वे तर्क-वितर्क (अनेक प्रकार के संदेह) रूपी तरंगों से पूर्ण संसार रूपी समुद्र में नहीं गिरते (आवागमन के चक्कर में नहीं पड़ते) ॥
english_translation: Those people who worship at your feet without jealousy do not fall into the ocean of becoming, which is full of waves of doubt and argument.
essence: Jealousy keeps you in confusion; devotion carries you through it.
simple_meaning: People who worship Ram without jealousy are not thrown into the endless cycle of confusion and rebirth.
insight: It shifts devotion from mixed motives to a clean, steady trust that can cross confusion.
modern_relevance: You scroll past someone else's success and feel the sting of comparison. The moment you stop measuring yourself, your prayer, work, and attention all become cleaner.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: विविक्त वासिनः सदा। भजंति मुक्तये मुदा॥ निरस्य इंद्रियादिकं। प्रयांतिते गतिं स्वकं ॥
translation: जो एकान्तवासी पुरुष मुक्ति के लिए, इन्द्रियादि का निग्रह करके (उन्हें विषयों से हटाकर) प्रसन्नतापूर्वक आपको भजते हैं, वे स्वकीय गति को (अपने स्वरूप को) प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who live in solitude, restrain the senses, and worship with joy for freedom reach their own true state.
essence: Joyful restraint brings you back to your own true nature.
simple_meaning: People who live quietly, control their senses, and worship with joy reach their own true nature and freedom.
insight: It shifts attention from outer stimulation to inner return, showing freedom as a disciplined homecoming.
modern_relevance: You close the laptop, silence your phone, and sit alone for ten minutes because your mind has been pulled in too many directions. That small withdrawal can become the doorway back to yourself.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तमेकमद्भुतं प्रभुं। निरीहमीश्वरं विभुं॥ जगद्गुरुं च शाश्वतं। तुरीयमेव केवलं ॥
translation: उन (आप) को जो एक (अद्वितीय), अद्भुत (मायिक जगत से विलक्षण), प्रभु (सर्वसमर्थ), इच्छारहित, ईश्वर (सबके स्वामी), व्यापक, जगद्गुरु, सनातन (नित्य), तुरीय (तीनों गुणों से सर्वथा परे) और केवल (अपने स्वरूप में स्थित) हैं ॥
english_translation: I bow to the one, wondrous Lord: desireless, sovereign, all-pervading, teacher of the world, eternal, beyond the three states, alone in true being.
essence: Ram is beyond all passing states and remains complete in himself.
simple_meaning: Ram is described as the one, wondrous, desireless, all-pervading reality who teaches the world and stands beyond ordinary states of mind.
insight: It shifts attention from changing experiences to the unchanging ground beneath them.
modern_relevance: You wake from a dream, check your phone, then sink back into restlessness before the day even starts. This verse points to what remains untouched underneath all three states.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भजामि भाव वल्लभं। कुयोगिनां सुदुर्लभं॥ स्वभक्त कल्प पादपं। समं सुसेव्यमन्वहं ॥
translation: (तथा) जो भावप्रिय, कुयोगियों (विषयी पुरुषों) के लिए अत्यन्त दुर्लभ, अपने भक्तों के लिए कल्पवृक्ष (अर्थात् उनकी समस्त कामनाओं को पूर्ण करने वाले), सम (पक्षपातरहित) और सदा सुखपूर्वक सेवन करने योग्य हैं, मैं निरंतर भजता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I continually worship the one who loves devotion, is hard to reach for those lost in wrong practice, is like a wish-fulfilling tree for his devotees, impartial, and always easy to serve.
essence: Sincere devotion reaches Ram; cleverness and pride do not.
simple_meaning: Ram is easy to approach through sincere devotion, but hard to reach through wrong or selfish practice. He treats all devotees equally and fulfills their needs like a wish-fulfilling tree.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to sincerity, and from earning grace to receiving it through love.
modern_relevance: You stand in front of someone important, rehearsing the perfect words, but what reaches them is your sincerity. This verse says the same is true with Ram: polished performance fails, honest devotion opens everything.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अनूप रूप भूपतिं। नतोऽहमुर्विजा पतिं॥ प्रसीद मे नमामि ते। पदाब्ज भक्ति देहि मे ॥
translation: हे अनुपम सुंदर! हे पृथ्वीपति! हे जानकीनाथ! मैं आपको प्रणाम करता हूँ। मुझ पर प्रसन्न होइए, मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ। मुझे अपने चरण कमलों की भक्ति दीजिए ॥
english_translation: O incomparable beauty, lord of the earth, lord of Janaki, I bow to you. Be pleased with me; I offer my salutations to you. Grant me devotion to your lotus feet.
essence: Devotion begins when you ask for devotion itself.
simple_meaning: The speaker praises Ram, bows down, and asks for devotion to Ram's feet.
insight: It shifts prayer from asking for outcomes to asking for a transformed heart.
modern_relevance: You can be standing in a hospital corridor, frightened and helpless, and still know the real request is larger than rescue: give me the strength to love what is worthy.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: पठंति ये स्तवं इदं। नरादरेण ते पदं॥ व्रजंति नात्र संशयं। त्वदीय भक्ति संयुताः ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य इस स्तुति को आदरपूर्वक पढ़ते हैं, वे आपकी भक्ति से युक्त होकर आपके परम पद को प्राप्त होते हैं, इसमें संदेह नहीं ॥
english_translation: Those who read this praise with reverence, joined to your devotion, surely reach your highest state; there is no doubt.
essence: Reverent devotion carries you to Ram without doubt.
simple_meaning: Anyone who reads this praise respectfully and with devotion will surely reach Ram's highest state.
insight: It shifts practice from casual reading to devotional participation, where reverence itself becomes the vehicle of transformation.
modern_relevance: You open a prayer, a poem, or a line of wisdom before bed and read it with real attention, not as a checkbox. That small reverence changes what reaches you.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: बिनती करि मुनि नाइ सिरु कह कर जोरि बहोरि। चरन सरोरुह नाथ जनि कबहुँ तजै मति मोरि ॥
translation: मुनि ने (इस प्रकार) विनती करके और फिर सिर नवाकर, हाथ जोड़कर कहा- हे नाथ! मेरी बुद्धि आपके चरण कमलों को कभी न छोड़े ॥
english_translation: After bowing and praying, the sage folded his hands and said, "O Lord, may my mind never leave your lotus feet."
essence: The deepest prayer is to never drift from Ram.
simple_meaning: The sage prays for one thing: that his mind never drift away from Ram's feet.
insight: It shifts attention from asking for outcomes to asking for inner steadiness in devotion.
modern_relevance: After a long day of distractions, you finally sit quietly and realize what you keep coming back to. This verse names that returning as the real prayer.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: अनुसुइया के पद गहि सीता। मिली बहोरि सुसील बिनीता॥ रिषिपतिनी मन सुख अधिकाई। आसिष देइ निकट बैठाई ॥
translation: फिर परम शीलवती और विनम्र श्री सीताजी अनसूयाजी (आत्रिजी की पत्नी) के चरण पकड़कर उनसे मिलीं। ऋषि पत्नी के मन में बड़ा सुख हुआ। उन्होंने आशीष देकर सीताजी को पास बैठा लिया ॥
english_translation: Then the noble and humble Sita held Anasuya's feet and greeted her. The sage's wife felt great joy, blessed her, and seated her nearby.
essence: Humility turns a meeting into a blessing.
simple_meaning: Sita humbly greets Anasuya by touching her feet. Anasuya feels delighted, blesses Sita, and invites her to sit close by.
insight: It shows that reverence creates trust, making guidance and blessing possible.
modern_relevance: You meet an elder who has lived through more than you can imagine. Instead of performing confidence, you listen, bow your pride, and receive what they offer.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दिब्य बसन भूषन पहिराए। जे नित नूतन अमल सुहाए॥ कह रिषिबधू सरस मृदु बानी। नारिधर्म कछु ब्याज बखानी ॥
translation: और उन्हें ऐसे दिव्य वस्त्र और आभूषण पहनाए, जो नित्य-नए निर्मल और सुहावने बने रहते हैं। फिर ऋषि पत्नी उनके बहाने मधुर और कोमल वाणी से स्त्रियों के कुछ धर्म बखान कर कहने लगीं ॥
english_translation: She dressed her in divine garments and ornaments, ever new, pure, and lovely. Then the sage's wife spoke in soft, sweet words, using this pretext to explain a woman's proper conduct.
essence: Kindness opens the heart before instruction begins.
simple_meaning: Anusuiya clothes Sita in beautiful divine garments and ornaments, then gently begins teaching her about a woman's conduct.
insight: It shows how warmth and respect can prepare someone to hear guidance.
modern_relevance: A grandmother fixes your collar before giving you advice you did not ask for. The care softens you first, so the lesson can land without resistance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मातु पिता भ्राता हितकारी। मितप्रद सब सुनु राजकुमारी॥ अमित दानि भर्ता बयदेही। अधम सो नारि जो सेव न तेही ॥
translation: हे राजकुमारी! सुनिए- माता, पिता, भाई सभी हित करने वाले हैं, परन्तु ये सब एक सीमा तक ही (सुख) देने वाले हैं, परन्तु हे जानकी! पति तो (मोक्ष रूप) असीम (सुख) देने वाला है। वह स्त्री अधम है, जो ऐसे पति की सेवा नहीं करती ॥
english_translation: Parents, brothers, and all family members are helpful, O princess, but only within limits. O Janaki, a husband gives boundless support. A woman is low who does not serve such a husband.
essence: A committed bond asks for service, not just affection.
simple_meaning: Annsuya teaches Sita that parents and siblings help only in limited ways, while a husband is meant to give boundless support and receive devoted service.
insight: It shifts attention from general affection to the specific obligation of committed partnership.
modern_relevance: You are caring for everyone in the house, but one relationship still asks for your most steady presence. This verse speaks to the quiet discipline of showing up for the person who shares your life.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: धीरज धर्म मित्र अरु नारी। आपद काल परिखिअहिं चारी॥ बृद्ध रोगबस जड़ धनहीना। अंध बधिर क्रोधी अति दीना ॥
translation: धैर्य, धर्म, मित्र और स्त्री- इन चारों की विपत्ति के समय ही परीक्षा होती है। वृद्ध, रोगी, मूर्ख, निर्धन, अंधा, बहरा, क्रोधी और अत्यन्त ही दीन- ॥
english_translation: Patience, duty, friend, and wife are tested in times of hardship. The old, the sick, the dull, the poor, the blind, the deaf, the angry, and the deeply distressed...
essence: Pressure reveals whether your bonds are real.
simple_meaning: Patience, duty, friendship, and marriage are truly tested when life gets difficult. The verse also points to people who are especially vulnerable in such times.
insight: It shifts attention from easy loyalty to loyalty under strain.
modern_relevance: A friend disappears the moment your job is lost. A partner stays. A promise survives the pressure. This verse reminds you that difficulty is not just pain — it is the test that reveals what your bonds are made of.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: ऐसेहु पति कर किएँ अपमाना। नारि पाव जमपुर दुख नाना॥ एकइ धर्म एक ब्रत नेमा। कायँ बचन मन पति पद प्रेमा ॥
translation: ऐसे भी पति का अपमान करने से स्त्री यमपुर में भाँति-भाँति के दुःख पाती है। शरीर, वचन और मन से पति के चरणों में प्रेम करना स्त्री के लिए, बस यह एक ही धर्म है, एक ही व्रत है और एक ही नियम है ॥
english_translation: Even so, if a wife dishonors her husband, she meets many kinds of suffering in Yama's realm. For body, speech, and mind, loving the husband's feet is her one duty, one vow, and one rule.
essence: True devotion shows itself in body, speech, and mind together.
simple_meaning: A wife should not dishonor her husband. Her duty is to love him with body, speech, and mind.
insight: It shifts devotion from a feeling into a total way of relating, where thought, speech, and action must agree.
modern_relevance: A marriage starts to crack when respect disappears from small things: the tone of a reply, the eye-roll, the private contempt. This verse asks for wholeness, not performance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जग पतिब्रता चारि बिधि अहहीं। बेद पुरान संत सब कहहीं॥ उत्तम के अस बस मन माहीं। सपनेहुँ आन पुरुष जग नाहीं ॥
translation: जगत में चार प्रकार की पतिव्रताएँ हैं। वेद, पुराण और संत सब ऐसा कहते हैं कि उत्तम श्रेणी की पतिव्रता के मन में ऐसा भाव बसा रहता है कि जगत में (मेरे पति को छोड़कर) दूसरा पुरुष स्वप्न में भी नहीं है ॥
english_translation: There are four kinds of chaste wives in the world. The Vedas, Puranas, and saints all say that the best kind keeps this thought in her heart: there is no other man in the world, even in a dream.
essence: True fidelity leaves no room for a second claim on the heart.
simple_meaning: The highest kind of devoted wife keeps her mind fixed on her husband alone, with no room for anyone else.
insight: It shifts attention from divided attraction to single-hearted fidelity.
modern_relevance: You keep checking an old message thread, half-hoping for a different answer. This verse points to a love that is no longer divided by comparison, fantasy, or second choices.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मध्यम परपति देखइ कैसें। भ्राता पिता पुत्र निज जैसें॥ धर्म बिचारि समुझि कुल रहई। सो निकिष्ट त्रिय श्रुति अस कहई ॥
translation: मध्यम श्रेणी की पतिव्रता पराए पति को कैसे देखती है, जैसे वह अपना सगा भाई, पिता या पुत्र हो (अर्थात समान अवस्था वाले को वह भाई के रूप में देखती है, बड़े को पिता के रूप में और छोटे को पुत्र के रूप में देखती है।) जो धर्म को विचारकर और अपने कुल की मर्यादा समझकर बची रहती है, वह निकृष्ट (निम्न श्रेणी की) स्त्री है, ऐसा वेद कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: How does a moderate chaste woman see another man's husband? She sees him like her own brother, father, or son. Considering dharma and understanding her family’s honor, the woman who stays restrained is called the lowest by the scriptures.
essence: What you call someone shapes whether desire can take hold.
simple_meaning: A woman of moderate restraint is told to regard another man's husband as a brother, father, or son, and to remain within family honor and dharma.
insight: It trains the mind to redirect desire through disciplined perception, not just through willpower.
modern_relevance: You notice a line is being crossed in a conversation, and you quietly step back before it grows teeth. The mind does not need to chase every attraction; it can choose a cleaner way of seeing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिनु अवसर भय तें रह जोई। जानेहु अधम नारि जग सोई॥ पति बंचक परपति रति करई। रौरव नरक कल्प सत परई ॥
translation: और जो स्त्री मौका न मिलने से या भयवश पतिव्रता बनी रहती है, जगत में उसे अधम स्त्री जानना। पति को धोखा देने वाली जो स्त्री पराए पति से रति करती है, वह तो सौ कल्प तक रौरव नरक में पड़ी रहती है ॥
english_translation: Know the woman who stays faithful only because there was no chance or because fear held her back as low in the world. The woman who betrays her husband and takes desire in another man falls into the Raurava lower realm for a hundred ages.
essence: Fearful restraint is not true fidelity.
simple_meaning: A woman who is faithful only because she had no chance or was afraid is still judged low. Betraying a husband and seeking another man brings severe suffering.
insight: It shifts attention from outward behavior to the motive underneath it.
modern_relevance: Someone stays in line only because cameras are on, then acts differently the moment no one is watching. The verse says hidden intention matters more than public appearance.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: छन सुख लागि जनम सत कोटी। दुख न समुझ तेहि सम को खोटी॥ बिनु श्रम नारि परम गति लहई। पतिब्रत धर्म छाड़ि छल गहई ॥
translation: क्षणभर के सुख के लिए जो सौ करोड़ (असंख्य) जन्मों के दुःख को नहीं समझती, उसके समान दुष्टा कौन होगी। जो स्त्री छल छोड़कर पतिव्रत धर्म को ग्रहण करती है, वह बिना ही परिश्रम परम गति को प्राप्त करती है ॥
english_translation: For a moment of pleasure, she does not understand the suffering of countless births; who could be more blameworthy than she? A woman who abandons deceit and takes up the vow of fidelity attains the highest state without effort.
essence: Brief pleasure can hide a vast cost; fidelity lifts you effortlessly.
simple_meaning: Short-lived pleasure can lead to great suffering, while a woman who gives up deceit and stays faithful reaches the highest state naturally.
insight: It shifts attention from immediate gratification to the long moral weight of a choice.
modern_relevance: You know the text, the flirtation, the secret message you almost sent because it felt harmless for one night. The verse says that tiny thrill can carry a much larger cost, while steady loyalty needs no performance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पति प्रतिकूल जनम जहँ जाई। बिधवा होइ पाइ तरुनाई ॥
translation: किन्तु जो पति के प्रतिकूल चलती है, वह जहाँ भी जाकर जन्म लेती है, वहीं जवानी पाकर (भरी जवानी में) विधवा हो जाती है ॥
english_translation: But the woman who goes against her husband, wherever she is born, becomes a widow in the bloom of youth.
essence: Opposing your bond can turn youth itself into loss.
simple_meaning: Turning against your husband brings ruin instead of security. The verse warns that such a life ends in loss and grief.
insight: It frames marital disloyalty as self-destructive, not liberating.
modern_relevance: A relationship starts unraveling when every disagreement becomes defiance. The verse points to the cost of choosing opposition over loyalty until love itself feels gone.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सहज अपावनि नारि पति सेवत सुभ गति लहइ। जसु गावत श्रुति चारि अजहुँ तुलसिका हरिहि प्रिय ॥
translation: स्त्री जन्म से ही अपवित्र है, किन्तु पति की सेवा करके वह अनायास ही शुभ गति प्राप्त कर लेती है। (पतिव्रत धर्म के कारण ही) आज भी 'तुलसीजी' भगवान को प्रिय हैं और चारों वेद उनका यश गाते हैं ॥
english_translation: A woman, by her nature, is impure; by serving her husband, she attains a noble state. Even today, Tulsidas is dear to Ram, and the four Vedas sing his praise.
essence: Faithful service can elevate a life more than birth can.
simple_meaning: Serving one's husband is presented as a path to a better state, and Tulsidas says this kind of devotion is still honoured by Ram and the Vedas.
insight: It shifts attention from status to the transforming power of loyal service.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up for a partner through illness, stress, and long silence. No applause comes, but the relationship deepens because your care is steady.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सुनु सीता तव नाम सुमिरि नारि पतिब्रत करहिं। तोहि प्रानप्रिय राम कहिउँ कथा संसार हित ॥
translation: हे सीता! सुनो, तुम्हारा तो नाम ही ले-लेकर स्त्रियाँ पतिव्रत धर्म का पालन करेंगी। तुम्हें तो श्री रामजी प्राणों के समान प्रिय हैं, यह (पतिव्रत धर्म की) कथा तो मैंने संसार के हित के लिए कही है ॥
english_translation: Listen, Sita: by remembering your name, women will uphold chastity. You are as dear to Ram as life itself; I have spoken this story for the good of the world.
essence: A beloved example can teach devotion more powerfully than instruction.
simple_meaning: Sita’s name is so pure and powerful that remembering it helps women live with fidelity and devotion. The speaker says this teaching is meant for the good of everyone.
insight: It turns virtue into something contagious: one life of devotion can train many others.
modern_relevance: Someone hears a grandmother speak a name with reverence, and it changes how the whole family behaves. That is how living examples work: they teach without argument and quietly reshape what people think is possible.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुनि जानकीं परम सुखु पावा। सादर तासु चरन सिरु नावा॥ तब मुनि सन कह कृपानिधाना। आयसु होइ जाउँ बन आना ॥
translation: जानकीजी ने सुनकर परम सुख पाया और आदरपूर्वक उनके चरणों में सिर नवाया। तब कृपा की खान श्री रामजी ने मुनि से कहा- आज्ञा हो तो अब दूसरे वन में जाऊँ ॥
english_translation: Sita felt supreme joy on hearing this and bowed her head respectfully at his feet. Then the treasure of grace, Ram, said to the sage, 'If you permit, I will now go to another forest.'
essence: Joy bows naturally before grace, and duty moves only with permission.
simple_meaning: Sita is overjoyed when she hears Ram's words and bows to him. Ram then asks the sage's permission to move on to another forest.
insight: It models a response of gratitude and humility before moving on.
modern_relevance: You finally hear the apology you needed, and your chest loosens before you even answer. Respect returns first, then words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: संतत मो पर कृपा करेहू। सेवक जानि तजेहु जनि नेहू॥ धर्म धुरंधर प्रभु कै बानी। सुनि सप्रेम बोले मुनि ग्यानी ॥
translation: मुझ पर निरंतर कृपा करते रहिएगा और अपना सेवक जानकर स्नेह न छोड़िएगा। धर्म धुरंधर प्रभु श्री रामजी के वचन सुनकर ज्ञानी मुनि प्रेमपूर्वक बोले- ॥
english_translation: “Please keep showing me your grace without end. Seeing me as your servant, do not withdraw your affection.” Hearing the words of Dharma's upholder, the wise sage spoke with love.
essence: Devotion asks for nothing except continued grace.
simple_meaning: The sage asks Ram to keep showing kindness and not stop loving him just because he is a servant.
insight: It shifts devotion from getting something to remaining in loving relation.
modern_relevance: After a hard conversation, you text someone one more time not to ask for anything, just to stay connected. That quiet need to remain held is what this verse understands.
speaker: Muni

verse_text: जासु कृपा अज सिव सनकादी। चहत सकल परमारथ बादी॥ ते तुम्ह राम अकाम पिआरे। दीन बंधु मृदु बचन उचारे ॥
translation: ब्रह्मा, शिव और सनकादि सभी परमार्थवादी (तत्ववेत्ता) जिनकी कृपा चाहते हैं, हे रामजी! आप वही निष्काम पुरुषों के भी प्रिय और दीनों के बंधु भगवान हैं, जो इस प्रकार कोमल वचन बोल रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Brahma, Shiva, and the sages of deep insight all long for your grace. You are the dear one of the desireless and the friend of the humble, yet you speak so gently.
essence: True greatness stays tender and is loved by the desireless.
simple_meaning: Even the highest seekers long for Ram's grace, yet he remains gentle and loving toward the humble and desireless.
insight: It shifts respect away from status and toward gentleness, humility, and inner freedom.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose title could make them cold, but they still speak softly to the cleaner, the child, the overlooked person in the room. That kind of greatness feels like relief.
speaker: Muni

verse_text: अब जानी मैं श्री चतुराई। भजी तुम्हहि सब देव बिहाई॥ जेहि समान अतिसय नहिं कोई। ता कर सील कस न अस होई ॥
translation: अब मैंने लक्ष्मीजी की चतुराई समझी, जिन्होंने सब देवताओं को छोड़कर आप ही को भजा। जिसके समान (सब बातों में) अत्यन्त बड़ा और कोई नहीं है, उसका शील भला, ऐसा क्यों न होगा? ॥
english_translation: Now I understand Lakshmi's wisdom: she abandoned all other radiant beings and worshipped only you. One greater than all others must surely have noble character.
essence: The highest being naturally draws the most complete devotion.
simple_meaning: Lakshmi is praised for leaving aside every other radiant being and choosing Ram alone, because the one who is greatest must also have the noblest character.
insight: It shifts devotion from blind feeling to clear recognition of what deserves your whole heart.
modern_relevance: You keep checking three different options, hoping one will feel right. Then you meet someone whose presence makes the rest feel small. The mind settles because it has recognized what it was really looking for.
speaker: Muni

verse_text: केहि बिधि कहौं जाहु अब स्वामी। कहहु नाथ तुम्ह अंतरजामी॥ अस कहि प्रभु बिलोकि मुनि धीरा। लोचन जल बह पुलक सरीरा ॥
translation: मैं किस प्रकार कहूँ कि हे स्वामी! आप अब जाइए? हे नाथ! आप अन्तर्यामी हैं, आप ही कहिए। ऐसा कहकर धीर मुनि प्रभु को देखने लगे। मुनि के नेत्रों से (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल बह रहा है और शरीर पुलकित है ॥
english_translation: How can I say, "Go now, my Lord"? O Master, you are the inner knower; you yourself speak. Saying this, the steadfast sage looked upon the Lord, and tears flowed from his eyes while his body shivered with love.
essence: When love is complete, even farewell becomes surrender.
simple_meaning: The sage cannot bring himself to ask Ram to leave. Since Ram knows every heart, he can only speak with tears and devotion.
insight: It shifts speech from asking to trusting that the other already understands.
modern_relevance: You sit across from someone who has helped you through your worst week, and the goodbye sticks in your throat. Some feelings are too full for explanation.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तन पुलक निर्भर प्रेम पूरन नयन मुख पंकज दिए। मन ग्यान गुन गोतीत प्रभु मैं दीख जप तप का किए॥ जप जोग धर्म समूह तें नर भगति अनुपम पावई। रघुबीर चरित पुनीत निसि दिन दास तुलसी गावई॥
translation: मुनि अत्यन्त प्रेम से पूर्ण हैं, उनका शरीर पुलकित है और नेत्रों को श्री रामजी के मुखकमल में लगाए हुए हैं। (मन में विचार रहे हैं कि) मैंने ऐसे कौन से जप-तप किए थे, जिसके कारण मन, ज्ञान, गुण और इन्द्रियों से परे प्रभु के दर्शन पाए। जप, योग और धर्म समूह से मनुष्य अनुपम भक्ति को पाता है। श्री रघुवीर के पवित्र चरित्र को तुलसीदास रात-दिन गाता है।
english_translation: My body is bristling with love; my eyes stay fixed on Ram's lotus face. I wonder what penance I performed to see the Lord beyond mind, wisdom, qualities, and senses. Through chanting, yoga, and all duties, a person gains incomparable devotion. Tulsidas sings the pure deeds of Raghuvir day and night.
essence: Devotion gives you what effort alone cannot reach.
simple_meaning: The poet is overwhelmed by Ram's presence and says that true devotion is greater than chanting, yoga, or ritual duty. He keeps singing Ram's pure story day and night.
insight: It shifts the mind from spiritual achievement to loving absorption as the real source of fulfillment.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone whose presence makes your rehearsed lines disappear. In that moment, trying harder feels smaller than simply opening your heart and letting reverence do the work.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कलिमल समन दमन मन राम सुजस सुखमूल। सादर सुनहिं जे तिन्ह पर राम रहहिं अनुकूल ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का सुंदर यश कलियुग के पापों का नाश करने वाला, मन को दमन करने वाला और सुख का मूल है, जो लोग इसे आदरपूर्वक सुनते हैं, उन पर श्री रामजी प्रसन्न रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram's beautiful fame destroys the stains of Kali, calms the mind, and is the root of joy. Those who listen to it with reverence receive Ram's favor.
essence: Reverent listening turns Ram's praise into inner medicine.
simple_meaning: Ram's fame clears away the stains of the age, quiets the mind, and brings joy. Anyone who listens respectfully gains Ram's grace.
insight: It shifts attention from passive hearing to reverent reception, where the mind is purified by what it truly takes in.
modern_relevance: You put on a podcast while cooking, but half your mind is elsewhere. Then one line lands, and the room feels different. What you receive with attention can change you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कठिन काल मल कोस धर्म न ग्यान न जोग जप। परिहरि सकल भरोस रामहि भजहिं ते चतुर नर ॥
translation: यह कठिन कलि काल पापों का खजाना है, इसमें न धर्म है, न ज्ञान है और न योग तथा जप ही है। इसमें तो जो लोग सब भरोसों को छोड़कर श्री रामजी को ही भजते हैं, वे ही चतुर हैं ॥
english_translation: This is the hard age of Kali, full of corruption. Dharma, knowledge, yoga, and chanting are all scarce here. Wise people abandon every other refuge and worship Ram alone.
essence: Real wisdom in a broken age is to lean on Ram alone.
simple_meaning: In this difficult age, ordinary supports are weak. The wise stop leaning on everything else and turn to Ram alone.
insight: It shifts the mind from divided dependence to single-hearted devotion.
modern_relevance: You’ve tried three self-help books, a podcast, and another plan, but the anxiety is still there. This verse says the smartest move may be simpler than your mind wants: stop outsourcing your peace.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मुनि पद कमल नाइ करि सीसा। चले बनहि सुर नर मुनि ईसा॥ आगें राम अनुज पुनि पाछें। मुनि बर बेष बने अति काछें ॥
translation: मुनि के चरण कमलों में सिर नवाकर देवता, मनुष्य और मुनियों के स्वामी श्री रामजी वन को चले। आगे श्री रामजी हैं और उनके पीछे छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी हैं। दोनों ही मुनियों का सुंदर वेष बनाए अत्यन्त सुशोभित हैं ॥
english_translation: Bowing their heads to the sages' lotus feet, they walked into the forest. Ram went first, Lakshman behind him, both dressed beautifully like ascetics.
essence: Humility opens the road before the journey starts.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman respectfully bow to the sages and then walk into the forest, dressed like holy men, with Ram leading and Lakshman following.
insight: It shows that true departure begins with reverence, not haste.
modern_relevance: You leave a mentor's office after asking for guidance, then step back into a hard decision with humility still intact. The respect you showed changes how you carry the road ahead.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उभय बीच श्री सोहइ कैसी। ब्रह्म जीव बिच माया जैसी॥ सरिता बन गिरि अवघट घाटा। पति पहिचानि देहिं बर बाटा ॥
translation: दोनों के बीच में श्री जानकीजी कैसी सुशोभित हैं, जैसे ब्रह्म और जीव के बीच माया हो। नदी, वन, पर्वत और दुर्गम घाटियाँ, सभी अपने स्वामी को पहचानकर सुंदर रास्ता दे देते हैं ॥
english_translation: How beautiful Sita shines between the two, like Maya between Brahman and the individual self. Rivers, forests, mountains, and rough passes all recognise their lord and give him a fine path.
essence: Grace can make even rough ground feel like a path.
simple_meaning: Sita shines beautifully between Ram and Lakshman, like a radiant presence in the middle of a hard journey. Even rivers, forests, mountains, and steep passes seem to recognise their lord and make way.
insight: It shifts attention from hardship itself to the presence that makes hardship bearable.
modern_relevance: You walk into a season that should feel harsh — a hospital corridor, a divorce meeting, a job loss — and something steady in you quietly makes the path feel less hostile.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ जहँ जाहिं देव रघुराया। करहिं मेघ तहँ तहँ नभ छाया॥ मिला असुर बिराध मग जाता। आवतहीं रघुबीर निपाता ॥
translation: जहाँ-जहाँ देव श्री रघुनाथजी जाते हैं, वहाँ-वहाँ बादल आकाश में छाया करते जाते हैं। रास्ते में जाते हुए विराध राक्षस मिला। सामने आते ही श्री रघुनाथजी ने उसे मार डाला ॥
english_translation: Wherever Lord Raghunath goes, clouds spread shade across the sky. On the road, the demon Viradh appeared. As soon as he came near, Raghubir struck him down.
essence: Ram's presence turns the path itself into protection.
simple_meaning: As Ram walks through the forest, nature responds to him, and Viradh the demon appears. Ram defeats him immediately.
insight: It shows Ram's presence as protective and decisive, while also moving the story toward the next encounter.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room and the mood shifts before you say a word. Some presence calms the space; some problems disappear the moment they are faced.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तुरतहिं रुचिर रूप तेहिं पावा। देखि दुखी निज धाम पठावा॥ पुनि आए जहँ मुनि सरभंगा। सुंदर अनुज जानकी संगा ॥
translation: (श्री रामजी के हाथ से मरते ही) उसने तुरंत सुंदर (दिव्य) रूप प्राप्त कर लिया। दुःखी देखकर प्रभु ने उसे अपने परम धाम को भेज दिया। फिर वे सुंदर छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी के साथ वहाँ आए जहाँ मुनि शरभंगजी थे ॥
english_translation: At once he received a beautiful form. Seeing his sorrow, the Lord sent him to his own supreme abode. Then Ram came there with the lovely younger brother Lakshman and Sita, to where the sage Sarabhanga was.
essence: True compassion ends suffering and then lets the soul move on.
simple_meaning: The sage’s suffering ends immediately, and Ram sends him onward. Then Ram, Lakshman, and Sita arrive at Sarabhanga’s hermitage.
insight: It shows that compassion does not merely comfort suffering; it also knows when to release it.
modern_relevance: A hospital room goes quiet after the doctor gives the final answer, and the family finally exhales. What was waiting in pain can now move on with dignity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि राम मुख पंकज मुनिबर लोचन भृंग। सादर पान करत अति धन्य जन्म सरभंग ॥
translation: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का मुखकमल देखकर मुनिश्रेष्ठ के नेत्र रूपी भौंरे अत्यन्त आदरपूर्वक उसका (मकरन्द रस) पान कर रहे हैं। शरभंगजी का जन्म धन्य है ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ram's lotus face, the great sage's eyes, like bees, drink it with reverence. Sarabhanga's birth is truly blessed.
essence: Seeing Ram is itself a blessing that fulfills a life.
simple_meaning: The sage looks at Ram's beautiful face with loving reverence, as bees drink nectar from a lotus. Sarabhanga's life becomes blessed by that sight.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary looking to reverent seeing, where the mind drinks in what it cherishes.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone you deeply love across a crowded station, and everything else fades. That single sight can make a hard day feel sacred.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह मुनि सुनु रघुबीर कृपाला। संकर मानस राजमराला॥ जात रहेउँ बिरंचि के धामा। सुनेउँ श्रवन बन ऐहहिं रामा ॥
translation: मुनि ने कहा- हे कृपालु रघुवीर! हे शंकरजी मन रूपी मानसरोवर के राजहंस! सुनिए, मैं ब्रह्मलोक को जा रहा था। (इतने में) कानों से सुना कि श्री रामजी वन में आवेंगे ॥
english_translation: The sage said, “Listen, compassionate Lord Raghuvir, swan of Shiva’s Manasarovar mind. I was on my way to Brahmaloka when I heard through my ears that Ram would come to the forest.”
essence: Even Brahmaloka can wait when Ram is near.
simple_meaning: The sage tells Ram that he was on his way to Brahmaloka, but the news that Ram would come to the forest made him stop and wait with devotion.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing higher destinations to recognising what is truly worth waiting for.
modern_relevance: You were about to chase the next milestone, then a message came from someone you love and everything else went quiet. Some arrivals matter more than promotion, plans, or prestige.
speaker: Muni

verse_text: चितवत पंथ रहेउँ दिन राती। अब प्रभु देखि जुड़ानी छाती॥ नाथ सकल साधन मैं हीना। कीन्ही कृपा जानि जन दीना ॥
translation: तब से मैं दिन-रात आपकी राह देखता रहा हूँ। अब (आज) प्रभु को देखकर मेरी छाती शीतल हो गई। हे नाथ! मैं सब साधनों से हीन हूँ। आपने अपना दीन सेवक जानकर मुझ पर कृपा की है ॥
english_translation: I kept watching the path day and night. Now that I have seen the Lord, my heart is soothed. O Lord, I am without all means. Seeing me as a humble servant, you have shown me grace.
essence: Meeting the Lord turns waiting into peace and lack into grace.
simple_meaning: A seeker says he watched for the Lord day and night, and now that he has seen him, his heart is calm. He feels unworthy and sees the meeting as grace.
insight: It shifts attention from lack to gratitude, and from self-importance to humble reception.
modern_relevance: You kept checking your phone for one message that mattered more than the rest. When it finally came, the anxiety dropped out of your body. Recognition can feel like grace.
speaker: Sarbhang

verse_text: सो कछु देव न मोहि निहोरा। निज पन राखेउ जन मन चोरा॥ तब लगि रहहु दीन हित लागी। जब लगि मिलौं तुम्हहि तनु त्यागी ॥
translation: हे देव! यह कुछ मुझ पर आपका एहसान नहीं है। हे भक्त-मनचोर! ऐसा करके आपने अपने प्रण की ही रक्षा की है। अब इस दीन के कल्याण के लिए तब तक यहाँ ठहरिए, जब तक मैं शरीर छोड़कर आपसे (आपके धाम में न) मिलूँ ॥
english_translation: O divine one, this is no favor done to me. You have only kept your own vow, O stealer of hearts. Stay here for this helpless one’s welfare until I leave my body and meet you.
essence: Devotion receives grace as the keeping of a sacred promise.
simple_meaning: The sage says Ram has not done him a personal favor; Ram has simply upheld his own promise. He asks Ram to remain until his death, for the sage’s welfare.
insight: It shifts gratitude from feeling indebted to recognising faithful presence.
modern_relevance: You finally hear back from the person you trusted, and they show up exactly when they said they would. The relief is not that they “did you a favor” — it’s that their word held.
speaker: Muni

verse_text: जोग जग्य जप तप ब्रत कीन्हा। प्रभु कहँ देइ भगति बर लीन्हा॥ एहि बिधि सर रचि मुनि सरभंगा। बैठे हृदयँ छाड़ि सब संगा ॥
translation: योग, यज्ञ, जप, तप जो कुछ व्रत आदि भी मुनि ने किया था, सब प्रभु को समर्पण करके बदले में भक्ति का वरदान ले लिया। इस प्रकार (दुर्लभ भक्ति प्राप्त करके फिर) चिता रचकर मुनि शरभंगजी हृदय से सब आसक्ति छोड़कर उस पर जा बैठे ॥
english_translation: The sage performed yoga, sacrifice, chanting, austerity, and vows, and offered them all to the Lord, receiving the boon of devotion. In this way, the sage Sharabhanga built a fire, gave up all attachment in his heart, and sat upon it.
essence: Everything disciplined can be surrendered into devotion.
simple_meaning: Sharabhanga gave Ram all his spiritual practices and received devotion in return. Then he let go of every attachment and turned fully inward toward Ram.
insight: It shifts the goal from accumulating spiritual effort to offering it until only devotion remains.
modern_relevance: You can spend years collecting techniques, rituals, and self-improvement habits, then realize none of them matter unless they open your heart. The real turning point is when practice stops being possession and becomes surrender.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीता अनुज समेत प्रभु नील जलद तनु स्याम। मम हियँ बसहु निरंतर सगुनरूप श्री राम ॥
translation: हे नीले मेघ के समान श्याम शरीर वाले सगुण रूप श्री रामजी! सीताजी और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु (आप) निरंतर मेरे हृदय में निवास कीजिए ॥
english_translation: O Lord Ram, dark as a blue raincloud, with Sita and your younger brother beside you, dwell forever in my heart.
essence: Presence, not possessions, is the devotee's highest request.
simple_meaning: Sarabhanga asks Ram to stay in his heart forever, along with Sita and Lakshman, and praises Ram's beautiful dark form.
insight: It shifts devotion from asking for gifts to asking for abiding presence.
modern_relevance: After a long night of worry, you finally sit quietly and realize you do not need one more answer. What you need is presence — something steady enough to live in your heart.
speaker: Sarabhanga

verse_text: अस कहि जोग अगिनि तनु जारा। राम कृपाँ बैकुंठ सिधारा॥ ताते मुनि हरि लीन न भयऊ। प्रथमहिं भेद भगति बर लयऊ ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर शरभंगजी ने योगाग्नि से अपने शरीर को जला डाला और श्री रामजी की कृपा से वे वैकुंठ को चले गए। मुनि भगवान में लीन इसलिए नहीं हुए कि उन्होंने पहले ही भेद-भक्ति का वर ले लिया था ॥
english_translation: Having said this, he burned his body in the fire of yoga, and by Ram's grace went to Vaikuntha. The sage did not merge into the divine because he had already received the boon of devoted love with distinction.
essence: Love can stay personal and still lead beyond the body.
simple_meaning: Sharabhang did not dissolve into the divine in an impersonal way. He had already received a special kind of devotion that kept his loving relationship with Ram intact.
insight: It shifts devotion from self-erasure to loving relationship, where distinctness is not a flaw but a gift.
modern_relevance: You can spend years trying to disappear into a practice, a cause, or a role. This verse says closeness does not require self-erasure; love can remain personal and still be complete.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रिषि निकाय मुनिबर गति देखी। सुखी भए निज हृदयँ बिसेषी॥ अस्तुति करहिं सकल मुनि बृंदा। जयति प्रनत हित करुना कंदा ॥
translation: ऋषि समूह मुनि श्रेष्ठ शरभंगजी की यह (दुर्लभ) गति देखकर अपने हृदय में विशेष रूप से सुखी हुए। समस्त मुनिवृंद श्री रामजी की स्तुति कर रहे हैं (और कह रहे हैं) शरणागत हितकारी करुणा कन्द (करुणा के मूल) प्रभु की जय हो! ॥
english_translation: The sages saw the rare state of the great ascetic and felt a special joy in their hearts. All the sages praised Ram: victory to the compassionate one who helps those who seek refuge.
essence: Ram is praised as the compassionate refuge of the surrendered.
simple_meaning: The sages are glad to see Sarabhanga reach a blessed state, and they praise Ram as the compassionate one who helps those who take refuge in him.
insight: It turns attention from the ascetic's achievement to Ram's grace as the real source of fulfilment.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you respected finally find peace after years of struggle, and your first feeling is gratitude. Their ending becomes a reminder that mercy can meet sincere effort.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि रघुनाथ चले बन आगे। मुनिबर बृंद बिपुल सँग लागे॥ अस्थि समूह देखि रघुराया। पूछी मुनिन्ह लागि अति दाया ॥
translation: फिर श्री रघुनाथजी आगे वन में चले। श्रेष्ठ मुनियों के बहुत से समूह उनके साथ हो लिए। हड्डियों का ढेर देखकर श्री रघुनाथजी को बड़ी दया आई, उन्होंने मुनियों से पूछा ॥
english_translation: Then Raghunath moved deeper into the forest, and a great company of sages followed him. Seeing a heap of bones, Raghuraya felt deep compassion and asked the sages.
essence: Compassion begins when you truly see what remains after pain.
simple_meaning: Ram walks deeper into the forest with many sages beside him. When he sees a pile of bones, compassion rises immediately, and he asks the sages about it.
insight: It trains attention to move from scenery to suffering, so the heart responds before the mind explains.
modern_relevance: You pass a roadside memorial or an empty chair at a family gathering, and something in you goes quiet. Compassion begins the moment you notice what loss has left behind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जानतहूँ पूछिअ कस स्वामी। सबदरसी तुम्ह अंतरजामी॥ निसिचर निकर सकल मुनि खाए। सुनि रघुबीर नयन जल छाए ॥
translation: (मुनियों ने कहा) हे स्वामी! आप सर्वदर्शी (सर्वज्ञ) और अंतर्यामी (सबके हृदय की जानने वाले) हैं। जानते हुए भी (अनजान की तरह) हमसे कैसे पूछ रहे हैं? राक्षसों के दलों ने सब मुनियों को खा डाला है। (ये सब उन्हीं की हड्डियों के ढेर हैं)। यह सुनते ही श्री रघुवीर के नेत्रों में जल छा गया (उनकी आँखों में करुणा के आँसू भर आए) ॥
english_translation: “You already know everything, Lord. You are the inner knower of all. Yet you ask us anyway? The whole of these sages has been devoured by bands of demons.” Hearing this, Ram’s eyes filled with tears.
essence: Perfect awareness can still weep for suffering.
simple_meaning: The sages remind Ram that he already knows everything, then tell him how demons destroyed their communities. Ram responds with tears of compassion.
insight: It shifts you from detached knowing to felt response, showing that true awareness includes compassion.
modern_relevance: You hear a friend describe the same loss for the third time, and you still feel it in your chest. Real care does not get numb from repetition.
speaker: Muni

verse_text: निसिचर हीन करउँ महि भुज उठाइ पन कीन्ह। सकल मुनिन्ह के आश्रमन्हि जाइ जाइ सुख दीन्ह ॥
translation: श्री रामजी ने भुजा उठाकर प्रण किया कि मैं पृथ्वी को राक्षसों से रहित कर दूँगा। फिर समस्त मुनियों के आश्रमों में जा-जाकर उनको (दर्शन एवं सम्भाषण का) सुख दिया ॥
english_translation: Raising his arm, Ram vowed to rid the earth of all forest-dwelling demons. Then he went from one sage's hermitage to another, giving them the joy of his presence and conversation.
essence: Protection becomes real only when your promise reaches people.
simple_meaning: Ram vows to clear the earth of harmful beings, then visits the sages one by one and gives them comfort through his presence.
insight: It turns compassion into action: first a vow, then repeated presence where help is needed.
modern_relevance: You hear the damage in a friend's voice, then do more than sympathize. You show up, make a clear promise, and keep visiting until the fear loosens.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: मुनि अगस्ति कर सिष्य सुजाना। नाम सुतीछन रति भगवाना॥ मन क्रम बचन राम पद सेवक। सपनेहुँ आन भरोस न देवक ॥
translation: मुनि अगस्त्यजी के एक सुतीक्ष्ण नामक सुजान (ज्ञानी) शिष्य थे, उनकी भगवान में प्रीति थी। वे मन, वचन और कर्म से श्री रामजी के चरणों के सेवक थे। उन्हें स्वप्न में भी किसी दूसरे देवता का भरोसा नहीं था ॥
english_translation: Muni Agastya had a wise disciple named Suteekshna, whose heart was devoted to the Lord. With mind, speech, and body, he served Ram's feet; even in a dream, he trusted no other divine power.
essence: Wholehearted devotion leaves no room for divided trust.
simple_meaning: Suteekshna was a wise disciple of Agastya who loved Ram deeply. He served Ram with mind, speech, and body, and placed no trust in any other divine power.
insight: It shifts you from divided loyalty to undivided trust in Ram.
modern_relevance: You keep a backup plan for your backup plan, then wonder why your heart feels split. Suteekshna shows the peace of giving your trust to one center instead of scattering it everywhere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु आगवनु श्रवन सुनि पावा। करत मनोरथ आतुर धावा॥ हे बिधि दीनबंधु रघुराया। मो से सठ पर करिहहिं दाया ॥
translation: उन्होंने ज्यों ही प्रभु का आगमन कानों से सुन पाया, त्यों ही अनेक प्रकार के मनोरथ करते हुए वे आतुरता (शीघ्रता) से दौड़ चले। हे विधाता! क्या दीनबन्धु श्री रघुनाथजी मुझ जैसे दुष्ट पर भी दया करेंगे? ॥
english_translation: As soon as he heard of the Lord's arrival, he rushed forward in eagerness, full of hopes. 'O Providence, will the compassionate Raghunath show mercy even to a wretch like me?'
essence: Hope runs toward Ram even while doubt lingers.
simple_meaning: Hearing that Ram has arrived, the devotee rushes forward with hope, yet still wonders whether such mercy can reach someone like him.
insight: It shifts you from waiting passively to moving as soon as grace feels near.
modern_relevance: You hear a message saying someone important has finally arrived, and you leave the room before finishing your reply. Your body knows hope before your mind can explain it.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सहित अनुज मोहि राम गोसाईं। मिलिहहिं निज सेवक की नाईं॥ मोरे जियँ भरोस दृढ़ नाहीं। भगति बिरति न ग्यान मन माहीं ॥
translation: क्या स्वामी श्री रामजी छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित मुझसे अपने सेवक की तरह मिलेंगे? मेरे हृदय में दृढ़ विश्वास नहीं होता, क्योंकि मेरे मन में भक्ति, वैराग्य या ज्ञान कुछ भी नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Will Lord Ram come to meet me, along with Lakshman, like a servant? My heart has no firm confidence, and my mind holds no devotion, detachment, or wisdom.
essence: Ram meets the one who longs for him, even without spiritual credentials.
simple_meaning: Sutikshna longs to be met by Ram as a servant, but he feels unworthy because he lacks firm faith, devotion, detachment, and wisdom.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-disqualification to receptive trust.
modern_relevance: You sit in your parked car before walking into a room where everyone seems more composed, more devoted, more certain than you. You feel unready — but the longing to go in is already its own strength.
speaker: Sutikshna

verse_text: नहिं सतसंग जोग जप जागा। नहिं दृढ़ चरन कमल अनुरागा॥ एक बानि करुनानिधान की। सो प्रिय जाकें गति न आन की ॥
translation: मैंने न तो सत्संग, योग, जप अथवा यज्ञ ही किए हैं और न प्रभु के चरणकमलों में मेरा दृढ़ अनुराग ही है। हाँ, दया के भंडार प्रभु की एक बान है कि जिसे किसी दूसरे का सहारा नहीं है, वह उन्हें प्रिय होता है ॥
english_translation: I have done no holy company, no yoga, no chanting, no sacrifice, and no steady love for the lotus feet. Yet the treasure of compassion has one habit: the one with no other support becomes dear to him.
essence: Being helpless can make you most beloved to Ram.
simple_meaning: The speaker admits to having no spiritual practice or steady devotion, yet says Ram is especially kind to those who have nowhere else to turn.
insight: It shifts the mind from earning grace to trusting that need can attract grace.
modern_relevance: You sit in a hospital waiting room, exhausted and stripped of all control. Nothing polished remains — only need. This verse says that is not a disqualification; it may be the very reason mercy comes close.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: होइहैं सुफल आजु मम लोचन। देखि बदन पंकज भव मोचन॥ निर्भर प्रेम मगन मुनि ग्यानी। कहि न जाइ सो दसा भवानी ॥
translation: (भगवान की इस बान का स्मरण आते ही मुनि आनंदमग्न होकर मन ही मन कहने लगे-) अहा! भव बंधन से छुड़ाने वाले प्रभु के मुखारविंद को देखकर आज मेरे नेत्र सफल होंगे। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे भवानी! ज्ञानी मुनि प्रेम में पूर्ण रूप से निमग्न हैं। उनकी वह दशा कही नहीं जाती ॥
english_translation: Today my eyes will bear fruit by seeing the lotus face of the one who frees beings from bondage. O Bhavani, the sage and the wise are so immersed in love that their state cannot be described.
essence: Ram's sight makes longing feel complete before a word is spoken.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram's lotus face will make the sage feel fulfilled. Love has carried the wise so deeply that their condition cannot even be put into words.
insight: It shifts devotion from abstract belief to a lived, overwhelming absorption that changes perception itself.
modern_relevance: You catch sight of someone you have missed for years, and the whole day changes. Some moments do not just please you — they make your waiting feel worth it.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: दिसि अरु बिदिसि पंथ नहिं सूझा। को मैं चलेउँ कहाँ नहिं बूझा॥ कबहुँक फिरि पाछें पुनि जाई। कबहुँक नृत्य करइ गुन गाई ॥
translation: उन्हें दिशा-विदिशा (दिशाएँ और उनके कोण आदि) और रास्ता, कुछ भी नहीं सूझ रहा है। मैं कौन हूँ और कहाँ जा रहा हूँ, यह भी नहीं जानते (इसका भी ज्ञान नहीं है)। वे कभी पीछे घूमकर फिर आगे चलने लगते हैं और कभी (प्रभु के) गुण गा-गाकर नाचने लगते हैं ॥
english_translation: They could not tell east from west, or even which path to take. They did not know who they were or where they were going. Sometimes they turned back, and sometimes they danced while singing the divine qualities.
essence: When devotion deepens, even direction and selfhood dissolve.
simple_meaning: Deep devotion makes a person lose track of direction, self-consciousness, and ordinary purpose. They move without planning, sometimes turning back, sometimes singing and dancing in joy.
insight: It shifts attention from managing the journey to being carried by devotion itself.
modern_relevance: You walk out of a concert or temple with tears in your eyes and no sense of time. For a few minutes, the usual map of self and schedule falls away, and only love remains.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अबिरल प्रेम भगति मुनि पाई। प्रभु देखैं तरु ओट लुकाई॥ अतिसय प्रीति देखि रघुबीरा। प्रगटे हृदयँ हरन भव भीरा ॥
translation: मुनि ने प्रगाढ़ प्रेमाभक्ति प्राप्त कर ली। प्रभु श्री रामजी वृक्ष की आड़ में छिपकर (भक्त की प्रेमोन्मत्त दशा) देख रहे हैं। मुनि का अत्यन्त प्रेम देखकर भवभय (आवागमन के भय) को हरने वाले श्री रघुनाथजी मुनि के हृदय में प्रकट हो गए ॥
english_translation: The sage gained unbroken loving devotion. The Lord hid behind a tree to watch. Seeing such intense love, Raghubir appeared in the sage's heart and removed the fear of rebirth.
essence: Pure love makes Ram appear inside you.
simple_meaning: The sage's love for Ram becomes so intense that Ram reveals himself within the sage's heart and removes fear.
insight: It shifts devotion from external seeking to inward presence, where fear loses its grip.
modern_relevance: You sit alone after a hard prayer, a tearful chant, or a quiet walk, and suddenly the ache feels answered from inside. Love that sincere changes what your heart can hold.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि मग माझ अचल होइ बैसा। पुलक सरीर पनस फल जैसा॥ तब रघुनाथ निकट चलि आए। देखि दसा निज जन मन भाए ॥
translation: (हृदय में प्रभु के दर्शन पाकर) मुनि बीच रास्ते में अचल (स्थिर) होकर बैठ गए। उनका शरीर रोमांच से कटहल के फल के समान (कण्टकित) हो गया। तब श्री रघुनाथजी उनके पास चले आए और अपने भक्त की प्रेम दशा देखकर मन में बहुत प्रसन्न हुए ॥
english_translation: The sage sat motionless in the middle of the path, his body bristling like a jackfruit. Then Raghunath came near and was delighted to see the devotion of his own devotee.
essence: Devotion can freeze the body and still draw Ram closer.
simple_meaning: The sage becomes so absorbed in seeing Ram that he sits frozen in the road. Ram comes close and feels joy at the sight of that devotion.
insight: It shows that devotion can make the body still and the heart vivid at once.
modern_relevance: You catch yourself standing still after hearing a name that matters to you. Your chest tightens, your mind goes quiet, and the one you love feels suddenly near.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनिहि राम बहु भाँति जगावा। जाग न ध्यान जनित सुख पावा॥ भूप रूप तब राम दुरावा। हृदयँ चतुर्भुज रूप देखावा ॥
translation: श्री रामजी ने मुनि को बहुत प्रकार से जगाया, पर मुनि नहीं जागे, क्योंकि उन्हें प्रभु के ध्यान का सुख प्राप्त हो रहा था। तब श्री रामजी ने अपने राजरूप को छिपा लिया और उनके हृदय में अपना चतुर्भुज रूप प्रकट किया ॥
english_translation: Ram tried in many ways to wake the sage, but the sage did not wake, because he was tasting the bliss born of meditation. Then Ram hid his royal form and revealed His four-armed form in the sage’s heart.
essence: When the heart is full of Ram, ordinary waking loses its power.
simple_meaning: The sage is so absorbed in the joy of meditation that he cannot be awakened. Ram then hides His outer royal form and reveals a divine form within the sage’s heart.
insight: It shifts attention from outer interruption to inner absorption, showing that devotion can transform how you perceive presence.
modern_relevance: You finally put your phone down after hours of scrolling, but your mind is still elsewhere. Something deeper has your attention now, and the usual noise can’t quite reach you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि अकुलाइ उठा तब कैसें। बिकल हीन मनि फनिबर जैसें॥ आगें देखि राम तन स्यामा। सीता अनुज सहित सुख धामा ॥
translation: तब (अपने ईष्ट स्वरूप के अंतर्धान होते ही) मुनि ऐसे व्याकुल होकर उठे, जैसे श्रेष्ठ (मणिधर) सर्प मणि के बिना व्याकुल हो जाता है। मुनि ने अपने सामने सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित श्यामसुंदर विग्रह सुखधाम श्री रामजी को देखा ॥
english_translation: Then the sage rose in agitation, like a jewel-less serpent in distress. Before him he saw dark-hued Ram, with Sita and Lakshman, the abode of joy.
essence: Separation itself reveals how precious the beloved is.
simple_meaning: The sage becomes restless when the vision disappears, then sees Ram again with Sita and Lakshman before him.
insight: It shows how intense longing makes absence feel unbearable and return feel like relief.
modern_relevance: You close your eyes after a moment of deep prayer or grief, and the room feels empty for a second. Then the presence you were reaching for feels suddenly near again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परेउ लकुट इव चरनन्हि लागी। प्रेम मगन मुनिबर बड़भागी॥ भुज बिसाल गहि लिए उठाई। परम प्रीति राखे उर लाई ॥
translation: प्रेम में मग्न हुए वे बड़भागी श्रेष्ठ मुनि लाठी की तरह गिरकर श्री रामजी के चरणों में लग गए। श्री रामजी ने अपनी विशाल भुजाओं से पकड़कर उन्हें उठा लिया और बड़े प्रेम से हृदय से लगा रखा ॥
english_translation: The blessed sage fell like a staff at Ram's feet, lost in love. Ram lifted him with His broad arms and held him close to His heart.
essence: The one who falls in devotion is lifted into closeness.
simple_meaning: The sage is so full of love for Ram that he falls at Ram's feet. Ram responds by lifting him up and holding him close.
insight: It turns reverence into intimacy: surrender becomes the doorway to being embraced.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you’ve admired for years, and your voice shakes. Instead of distance, they smile, pull you in, and make your nervousness feel holy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनिहि मिलत अस सोह कृपाला। कनक तरुहि जनु भेंट तमाला॥ राम बदनु बिलोक मुनि ठाढ़ा। मानहुँ चित्र माझ लिखि काढ़ा ॥
translation: कृपालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी मुनि से मिलते हुए ऐसे शोभित हो रहे हैं, मानो सोने के वृक्ष से तमाल का वृक्ष गले लगकर मिल रहा हो। मुनि (निस्तब्ध) खड़े हुए (टकटकी लगाकर) श्री रामजी का मुख देख रहे हैं, मानो चित्र में लिखकर बनाए गए हों ॥
english_translation: The compassionate Ram shone beside the sage like a dark tamala tree embracing a golden tree. The sage stood still, gazing at Ram's face, as if painted in a picture.
essence: A true meeting can leave you motionless in wonder.
simple_meaning: Ram's meeting with the sage is described as a beautiful, striking contrast, and the sage stands spellbound, unable to look away.
insight: It shifts attention from action to reverent seeing, where presence itself becomes the event.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you have admired for years, and your mind goes silent. You just stand there, taking in their face, unable to do anything else.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब मुनि हृदयँ धीर धरि गहि पद बारहिं बार। निज आश्रम प्रभु आनि करि पूजा बिबिध प्रकार ॥
translation: तब मुनि ने हृदय में धीरज धरकर बार-बार चरणों को स्पर्श किया। फिर प्रभु को अपने आश्रम में लाकर अनेक प्रकार से उनकी पूजा की ॥
english_translation: Then the sage steadied his heart, touched the Lord's feet again and again, and brought Him to his hermitage, where he worshipped Him in many ways.
essence: True devotion turns awe into humble service.
simple_meaning: The sage calms himself, bows to Ram's feet again and again, brings Him to his hermitage, and worships Him with many offerings.
insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone into concrete welcome, bowing, and service.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you deeply admire, and your first instinct is not to perform — it's to make room, serve well, and show respect without hurry.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह मुनि प्रभु सुनु बिनती मोरी। अस्तुति करौं कवन बिधि तोरी॥ महिमा अमित मोरि मति थोरी। रबि सन्मुख खद्योत अँजोरी ॥
translation: मुनि कहने लगे- हे प्रभो! मेरी विनती सुनिए। मैं किस प्रकार से आपकी स्तुति करूँ? आपकी महिमा अपार है और मेरी बुद्धि अल्प है। जैसे सूर्य के सामने जुगनू का उजाला! ॥
english_translation: The sage said, “Lord, hear my plea. How can I praise you? Your greatness is boundless, and my mind is small. My light is like a firefly before the sun.”
essence: True devotion knows its own words are too small.
simple_meaning: The sage asks Ram to listen, then admits he cannot properly praise him because Ram's greatness is limitless and his own mind is too small.
insight: It shifts you from performing praise to surrendering into reverence.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who changed your life, and every thank-you sounds too small. That awkward humility is not failure; it is recognition of something larger than language.
speaker: Muni

verse_text: श्याम तामरस दाम शरीरं। जटा मुकुट परिधन मुनिचीरं॥ पाणि चाप शर कटि तूणीरं। नौमि निरंतर श्रीरघुवीरं ॥
translation: हे नीलकमल की माला के समान श्याम शरीर वाले! हे जटाओं का मुकुट और मुनियों के (वल्कल) वस्त्र पहने हुए, हाथों में धनुष-बाण लिए तथा कमर में तरकस कसे हुए श्री रामजी! मैं आपको निरंतर नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: O dark one, with a body like a garland of blue lotuses; with matted hair as your crown and bark garments; with bow and arrows in your hands and a quiver at your waist, I continually bow to Sri Raghubir.
essence: True devotion sees splendor inside simplicity.
simple_meaning: The sage praises Ram's form and bows to him again and again. He sees the Lord of Raghu as both majestic and forest-dwelling.
insight: It trains the mind to honor the sacred form beneath outward simplicity.
modern_relevance: You meet someone in worn-out clothes after a hard year, but their steadiness changes the room. What looks ordinary may carry a dignity you only notice when your heart is quiet.
speaker: Muni

verse_text: मोह विपिन घन दहन कृशानुः। संत सरोरुह कानन भानुः॥ निसिचर करि वरूथ मृगराजः। त्रास सदा नो भव खग बाजः ॥
translation: जो मोह रूपी घने वन को जलाने के लिए अग्नि हैं, संत रूपी कमलों के वन को प्रफुल्लित करने के लिए सूर्य हैं, राक्षस रूपी हाथियों के समूह को पछाड़ने के लिए सिंह हैं और भव (आवागमन) रूपी पक्षी को मारने के लिए बाज रूप हैं, वे प्रभु सदा हमारी रक्षा करें ॥
english_translation: May the Lord who burns the dense forest of delusion, the sun that makes the lotus-forest of saints bloom, the lion that scatters the herd of demon-elephants, and the hawk that strikes down the bird of worldly becoming protect us forever.
essence: Ram destroys confusion and protects the good from fear.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the one who destroys confusion, nourishes the good, defeats destructive forces, and frees people from fear and rebirth.
insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to refuge: Ram is not just praised, he is relied on.
modern_relevance: When your mind feels like a dark room full of anxious thoughts, this verse offers a different center: something steady enough to burn through confusion and quiet the fear underneath it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अरुण नयन राजीव सुवेशं। सीता नयन चकोर निशेशं॥ हर हृदि मानस बाल मरालं। नौमि राम उर बाहु विशालं ॥
translation: हे लाल कमल के समान नेत्र और सुंदर वेश वाले! सीताजी के नेत्र रूपी चकोर के चंद्रमा, शिवजी के हृदय रूपी मानसरोवर के बालहंस, विशाल हृदय और भुजा वाले श्री रामचंद्रजी! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: With red lotus eyes and a beautiful form, you are the moon for Sita's chakor-like gaze. You are the young swan in Shiva's Manasarovar heart. I bow to Ram, whose chest is vast and whose arms are broad.
essence: Ram's beauty is matched by how completely he lives in loving hearts.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised for his beautiful form and for being beloved by Sita and Shiva alike.
insight: It shifts attention from Ram's appearance to his living place in the hearts of devotees.
modern_relevance: You see someone you love in a crowded station and your whole attention softens. This verse names that feeling when devotion makes one presence shine through every heart.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: संशय सर्प ग्रसन उरगादः। शमन सुकर्कश तर्क विषादः॥ भव भंजन रंजन सुर यूथः। त्रातु सदा नो कृपा वरूथः ॥
translation: जो संशय रूपी सर्प को ग्रसने के लिए गरुड़ हैं, अत्यंत कठोर तर्क से उत्पन्न होने वाले विषाद का नाश करने वाले हैं, आवागमन को मिटाने वाले और देवताओं के समूह को आनंद देने वाले हैं, वे कृपा के समूह श्री रामजी सदा हमारी रक्षा करें ॥
english_translation: May Lord Ram, the gracious one, always protect us: he swallows the serpent of doubt, destroys the suffering born of harsh logic, ends the cycle of becoming, and delights the hosts of radiant beings.
essence: Ram destroys doubt before doubt destroys you.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the one who destroys doubt, ends despair born from harsh reasoning, and frees beings from the cycle of reactivity.
insight: It shifts you from compulsive analysis to trust in a presence that can clear confusion.
modern_relevance: You stare at a message for ten minutes, building worst-case stories from one unread reply. This verse names the deeper rescue: a steadier presence that cuts through doubt before it hardens into despair.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: निर्गुण सगुण विषम सम रूपं। ज्ञान गिरा गोतीतमनूपं॥ अमलमखिलमनवद्यमपारं। नौमि राम भंजन महि भारं ॥
translation: हे निर्गुण, सगुण, विषम और समरूप! हे ज्ञान, वाणी और इंद्रियों से अतीत! हे अनुपम, निर्मल, संपूर्ण दोषरहित, अनंत एवं पृथ्वी का भार उतारने वाले श्री रामचंद्रजी! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: O Ram, beyond attributes and beyond words, beyond all opposites, pure, flawless, limitless, and incomparable, I bow to you—the one who lifts the burden of the earth.
essence: Ram is beyond every category, yet still carries the world's burden.
simple_meaning: Ram is beyond qualities, beyond speech, beyond the senses, yet also pure, complete, and without flaw. Tulsidas bows to him as the one who removes the world's burden.
insight: It shifts the mind from naming Ram to bowing before what cannot be fully named.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to define what matters most in a few neat words, then it shows up as something larger than your categories. This verse lets you rest in reverence instead of control.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भक्त कल्पपादप आरामः। तर्जन क्रोध लोभ मद कामः॥ अति नागर भव सागर सेतुः। त्रातु सदा दिनकर कुल केतुः ॥
translation: जो भक्तों के लिए कल्पवृक्ष के बगीचे हैं, क्रोध, लोभ, मद और काम को डराने वाले हैं, अत्यंत ही चतुर और संसार रूपी समुद्र से तरने के लिए सेतु रूप हैं, वे सूर्यकुल की ध्वजा श्री रामजी सदा मेरी रक्षा करें ॥
english_translation: May Ram, the banner of the solar line, always protect me: he is the wish-fulfilling grove for devotees, the one who frightens away anger, greed, pride, and desire, and the skilled bridge across the ocean of worldly existence.
essence: Ram gives devotees refuge and carries them beyond their own inner enemies.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the one who gives devotees everything they truly need, protects them from inner faults, and helps them cross the ocean of worldly struggle.
insight: It shifts devotion from sentiment to protection: Ram is both refuge and the force that dismantles inner disturbance.
modern_relevance: You are staring at your phone at 1:30 a.m., angry, restless, and tempted to spiral. This verse reminds you that real refuge does not just comfort you — it also weakens the habits that keep dragging you down.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अतुलित भुज प्रताप बल धामः। कलि मल विपुल विभंजन नामः॥ धर्म वर्म नर्मद गुण ग्रामः। संतत शं तनोतु मम रामः ॥
translation: जिनकी भुजाओं का प्रताप अतुलनीय है, जो बल के धाम हैं, जिनका नाम कलियुग के बड़े भारी पापों का नाश करने वाला है, जो धर्म के कवच (रक्षक) हैं और जिनके गुण समूह आनंद देने वाले हैं, वे श्री रामजी निरंतर मेरे कल्याण का विस्तार करें ॥
english_translation: May Lord Ram, whose arms have unmatched splendor and whose strength is immense, whose name destroys the great impurities of Kali Yuga, who protects dharma, and whose qualities bring delight, always expand my welfare.
essence: Ram’s name protects, purifies, and strengthens you at once.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as immensely powerful, protective, and purifying. His name destroys the heavy impurities of this age and brings lasting welfare.
insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to reliance: Ram is not only praised, he is taken as shelter.
modern_relevance: When your mind feels polluted by doomscrolling, resentment, and self-doubt, you want something stronger than willpower. This verse points to a steadier refuge: repeated remembrance of Ram as protection and cleansing.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जदपि बिरज ब्यापक अबिनासी। सब के हृदयँ निरंतर बासी॥ तदपि अनुज श्री सहित खरारी। बसतु मनसि मम काननचारी ॥
translation: यद्यपि आप निर्मल, व्यापक, अविनाशी और सबके हृदय में निरंतर निवास करने वाले हैं, तथापि हे खरारि श्री रामजी! लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सहित वन में विचरने वाले आप इसी रूप में मेरे हृदय में निवास कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Although you are pure, all-pervading, imperishable, and always dwelling in everyone's heart, still, O Ravana-slayer, let you, with Lakshman and Sita, dwell in my mind as the forest-wandering Ram.
essence: The all-pervading one is most beloved when he feels near.
simple_meaning: Ram is everywhere and already present in every heart, yet the devotee asks for a personal, loving presence of Ram, Sita, and Lakshman in the mind.
insight: It shifts devotion from abstract reverence to intimate companionship.
modern_relevance: You know someone can be admired by everyone, yet you still want their voice in your own home. This prayer feels like asking for not just respect from afar, but living closeness.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जे जानहिं ते जानहुँ स्वामी। सगुन अगुन उर अंतरजामी॥ जो कोसलपति राजिव नयना। करउ सो राम हृदय मम अयना ॥
translation: हे स्वामी! आपको जो सगुण, निर्गुण और अंतर्यामी जानते हों, वे जाना करें, मेरे हृदय में तो कोसलपति कमलनयन श्री रामजी ही अपना घर बनावें ॥
english_translation: O Lord, those who know You may know You as embodied, formless, and the inner ruler. But for me, may Kosalapati, the lotus-eyed Ram, make His home in my heart.
essence: Let Ram be your inner home, beyond every argument about form.
simple_meaning: The speaker says that others may understand the divine in many forms, but he wants only Ram to dwell in his heart.
insight: It shifts devotion from debate to intimacy, from understanding Ram to making room for Ram.
modern_relevance: You can read a dozen books, compare every path, and still feel empty at night. This verse lands like a quiet decision: stop circling the idea of the divine and let Ram in.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: अस अभिमान जाइ जनि भोरे। मैं सेवक रघुपति पति मोरे॥ सुनि मुनि बचन राम मन भाए। बहुरि हरषि मुनिबर उर लाए ॥
translation: ऐसा अभिमान भूलकर भी न छूटे कि मैं सेवक हूँ और श्री रघुनाथजी मेरे स्वामी हैं। मुनि के वचन सुनकर श्री रामजी मन में बहुत प्रसन्न हुए। तब उन्होंने हर्षित होकर श्रेष्ठ मुनि को हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
english_translation: May this pride never leave you even in a dream: 'I am a servant, and Raghupati is my master.' Hearing the sage's words, Ram was delighted in his heart. Then, pleased, he embraced the great sage.
essence: Pride survives only when it is turned into service.
simple_meaning: The sage says the only pride worth keeping is this: you are a servant of Ram. Ram is pleased by that humility and embraces the sage.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to loving service, showing that humility itself creates closeness.
modern_relevance: You help someone without expecting credit, and the quiet thought arises: 'I am only serving.' That inner humility can feel more powerful than applause.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: परम प्रसन्न जानु मुनि मोही। जो बर मागहु देउँ सो तोही॥ मुनि कह मैं बर कबहुँ न जाचा। समुझि न परइ झूठ का साचा ॥
translation: (और कहा-) हे मुनि! मुझे परम प्रसन्न जानो। जो वर माँगो, वही मैं तुम्हें दूँ! मुनि सुतीक्ष्णजी ने कहा- मैंने तो वर कभी माँगा ही नहीं। मुझे समझ ही नहीं पड़ता कि क्या झूठ है और क्या सत्य है, (क्या माँगू, क्या नहीं) ॥
english_translation: And he said, “O sage, know me to be greatly pleased. Ask for whatever boon you wish, and I will give it to you.” The sage replied, “I have never asked for any boon. I do not even know how to tell what is false and what is true, or what I should ask and what I should not.”
essence: True devotion stops asking for random rewards and trusts what comes.
simple_meaning: Ram offers Suṭīkṣṇa any boon, but the sage replies that he has never learned how to ask for one, or even how to separate false from true desire.
insight: It shifts you from craving and bargaining to honest simplicity about what you truly want.
modern_relevance: Someone finally asks, “What do you want for your birthday?” and you freeze because the honest answer is: you do not know. The verse understands that quiet clarity.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तुम्हहि नीक लागै रघुराई। सो मोहि देहु दास सुखदाई॥ अबिरल भगति बिरति बिग्याना। होहु सकल गुन ग्यान निधाना ॥
translation: ((अतः) हे रघुनाथजी! हे दासों को सुख देने वाले! आपको जो अच्छा लगे, मुझे वही दीजिए। (श्री रामचंद्रजी ने कहा- हे मुने!) तुम प्रगाढ़ भक्ति, वैराग्य, विज्ञान और समस्त गुणों तथा ज्ञान के निधान हो जाओ ॥
english_translation: “O Raghunath, giver of ease to your servants, give me whatever is pleasing to you. May I attain unbroken devotion, non-attachment, clear understanding, and become a storehouse of all virtues and wisdom.”
essence: The best boon is becoming fit for devotion, clarity, and non-attachment.
simple_meaning: The seeker asks Ram for whatever Ram thinks is best, and asks to be filled with steady devotion, non-attachment, understanding, and all good qualities.
insight: It shifts desire from getting outcomes to becoming fit for devotion and wisdom.
modern_relevance: You finally get the chance to ask for what you want — better pay, a shortcut, a favor. Instead, you ask to become steadier, clearer, and harder to shake.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: प्रभु जो दीन्ह सो बरु मैं पावा। अब सो देहु मोहि जो भावा ॥
translation: (तब मुनि बोले-) प्रभु ने जो वरदान दिया, वह तो मैंने पा लिया। अब मुझे जो अच्छा लगता है, वह दीजिए ॥
english_translation: (Then the sage said-) The blessing the Lord gave, I have already received. Now give me what I truly long for.
essence: The real boon is the one your heart still needs.
simple_meaning: The sage says he already has the blessing he needed from Ram, and now asks for the deeper gift his heart truly wants.
insight: It shifts you from asking for external rewards to asking for the deeper grace that satisfies longing.
modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the apology, the thing you asked for — and still feel the ache underneath. This verse names that second request: not more stuff, but what your heart actually needs.
speaker: Sutiksna

verse_text: अनुज जानकी सहित प्रभु चाप बान धर राम। मन हिय गगन इंदु इव बसहु सदा निहकाम ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! हे श्री रामजी! छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सहित धनुष-बाणधारी आप निष्काम (स्थिर) होकर मेरे हृदय रूपी आकाश में चंद्रमा की भाँति सदा निवास कीजिए ॥
english_translation: O Lord Ram, with your younger brother Lakshman and Sita beside you, bow in hand, may you always dwell in my heart-mind like the moon in the sky, without desire.
essence: True devotion asks for Ram's presence, not anything else.
simple_meaning: The speaker asks Ram to stay in the heart forever, along with Lakshman and Sita, like a calm moon in the sky, free from desire.
insight: It shifts devotion from asking for favors to asking for abiding presence.
modern_relevance: After a long day, you finally sit alone and realize what you really want is not more control or praise — just a steady presence in your heart that calms everything else.
speaker: Sutīkshna

verse_text: एवमस्तु करि रमानिवासा। हरषि चले कुंभज रिषि पासा॥ बहुत दिवस गुर दरसनु पाएँ। भए मोहि एहिं आश्रम आएँ ॥
translation: 'एवमस्तु' (ऐसा ही हो) ऐसा उच्चारण कर लक्ष्मी निवास श्री रामचंद्रजी हर्षित होकर अगस्त्य ऋषि के पास चले। (तब सुतीक्ष्णजी बोले-) गुरु अगस्त्यजी का दर्शन पाए और इस आश्रम में आए मुझे बहुत दिन हो गए ॥
english_translation: Saying, “So be it,” Ram, the abode of Lakshmi, went joyfully to Sage Agastya. Then Sutikshna said, “It has been many days since I had the teacher’s darshan and came to this hermitage.”
essence: Joy grows when you move toward the teacher with reverence.
simple_meaning: Ram agrees and goes happily to Agastya’s hermitage. Sutikshna then reflects that it has been a long time since he last saw his teacher and arrived here.
insight: It shows how reverence turns movement into joy and arrival into gratitude.
modern_relevance: You finally get the call from someone wise enough to guide you, and you leave the room lighter than you entered. The meeting itself feels like a reward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अब प्रभु संग जाउँ गुर पाहीं। तुम्ह कहँ नाथ निहोरा नाहीं॥ देखि कृपानिधि मुनि चतुराई। लिए संग बिहसे द्वौ भाई ॥
