translation: अब मैं भी प्रभु (आप) के साथ गुरुजी के पास चलता हूँ। इसमें हे नाथ! आप पर मेरा कोई एहसान नहीं है। मुनि की चतुरता देखकर कृपा के भंडार श्री रामजी ने उनको साथ ले लिया और दोनो भाई हँसने लगे ॥
english_translation: "Now I will go with the Lord to the teacher. O Lord, I owe you no favor." Seeing the sage's cleverness, the treasure of compassion took him along, and both brothers laughed.
essence: Real generosity needs no repayment.
simple_meaning: The sage asks to come along, saying he owes no debt for the kindness. Ram sees the sage's cleverness, takes him with him, and the two brothers laugh together.
insight: It shows that true affection can be given without keeping score.
modern_relevance: A friend says, “I’m coming with you,” pretending it’s no big deal, even though the gesture means everything. Some kindnesses are so natural they don’t need repayment.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: पंथ कहत निज भगति अनूपा। मुनि आश्रम पहुँचे सुरभूपा॥ तुरत सुतीछन गुर पहिं गयऊ। करि दंडवत कहत अस भयऊ ॥
translation: रास्ते में अपनी अनुपम भक्ति का वर्णन करते हुए देवताओं के राजराजेश्वर श्री रामजी अगस्त्य मुनि के आश्रम पर पहुँचे। सुतीक्ष्ण तुरंत ही गुरु अगस्त्य के पास गए और दण्डवत् करके ऐसा कहने लगे ॥
english_translation: While speaking of their incomparable devotion on the way, the king of the gods, Ram, reached the sage's hermitage. Suतीkshan quickly went to Guru Agastya, bowed down, and began to speak.
essence: Devotion becomes real when it turns into immediate bowing and approach.
simple_meaning: Ram reaches Agastya's hermitage while speaking of devotion, and Sutikshan immediately bows before the guru and begins to speak.
insight: It shows devotion as movement toward the teacher, not just feeling or speech.
modern_relevance: You finally arrive at the mentor's door after a long walk of questions. Before you even sit down, your body already knows to bow, listen, and soften.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ कोसलाधीस कुमारा। आए मिलन जगत आधारा॥ राम अनुज समेत बैदेही। निसि दिनु देव जपत हहु जेही ॥
translation: हे नाथ! अयोध्या के राजा दशरथजी के कुमार जगदाधार श्री रामचंद्रजी छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सहित आपसे मिलने आए हैं, जिनका हे देव! आप रात-दिन जप करते रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Lord, the prince of Ayodhya, the support of the world, has come to meet you. Ram has come with his younger brother and Sita, the one you chant day and night.
essence: What you remember with love can one day stand before you.
simple_meaning: The speaker tells Augustya that Ram has arrived with Lakshman and Sita, and reminds him that Augustya has long been remembering Ram day and night.
insight: It shifts longing from private devotion into living encounter.
modern_relevance: You finally meet the person whose name you have been carrying in prayer, memory, and hope. The waiting ends, and recognition arrives before words do.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुनत अगस्ति तुरत उठि धाए। हरि बिलोकि लोचन जल छाए॥ मुनि पद कमल परे द्वौ भाई। रिषि अति प्रीति लिए उर लाई ॥
translation: यह सुनते ही अगस्त्यजी तुरंत ही उठ दौड़े। भगवान् को देखते ही उनके नेत्रों में (आनंद और प्रेम के आँसुओं का) जल भर आया। दोनों भाई मुनि के चरण कमलों पर गिर पड़े। ऋषि ने (उठाकर) बड़े प्रेम से उन्हें हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Agastya rose at once and ran forward. Seeing Hari, tears filled his eyes. The two brothers fell at the sage's lotus feet, and the sage, full of love, drew them into his heart.
essence: Love recognizes the beloved before words begin.
simple_meaning: Agastya rushes to greet Ram and Lakshman with tears of joy. The brothers bow at his feet, and he embraces them with deep affection.
insight: It highlights devotion as an immediate, embodied response to sacred presence.
modern_relevance: You open the door and see someone you have waited months to meet. Your body moves before your words do, and gratitude shows up as tears.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सादर कुसल पूछि मुनि ग्यानी। आसन बर बैठारे आनी॥ पुनि करि बहु प्रकार प्रभु पूजा। मोहि सम भाग्यवंत नहिं दूजा ॥
translation: ज्ञानी मुनि ने आदरपूर्वक कुशल पूछकर उनको लाकर श्रेष्ठ आसन पर बैठाया। फिर बहुत प्रकार से प्रभु की पूजा करके कहा- मेरे समान भाग्यवान् आज दूसरा कोई नहीं है ॥
english_translation: The wise sage respectfully asked after their well-being, brought them in and seated them on a fine seat. Then he worshipped the Lord in many ways and said, "No one is as fortunate as I am today."
essence: Honor the divine presence by welcoming it with your whole heart.
simple_meaning: Agastya greets Ram and his companions with honor, seats them well, worships Ram in many ways, and feels blessed by their arrival.
insight: It shows devotion through hospitality: the sacred guest is welcomed with care, not ceremony alone.
modern_relevance: Someone arrives at your home after a long journey, and you stop everything to make them comfortable, feed them, and give them your best seat. That quiet honor says more than praise ever could.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ लगि रहे अपर मुनि बृंदा। हरषे सब बिलोकि सुखकंदा ॥
translation: वहाँ जहाँ तक (जितने भी) अन्य मुनिगण थे, सभी आनंदकन्द श्री रामजी के दर्शन करके हर्षित हो गए ॥
english_translation: All the other sages there became joyful upon seeing the Lord of bliss.
essence: His presence alone turns reverence into joy.
simple_meaning: The other sages present there felt joy just from seeing Ram.
insight: It shows Ram's presence as enough to transform the mood of everyone around him.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the tension drops before anyone speaks. Some people bring calm just by being there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि समूह महँ बैठे सन्मुख सब की ओर। सरद इंदु तन चितवन मानहुँ निकर चकोर ॥
translation: मुनियों के समूह में श्री रामचंद्रजी सबकी ओर सम्मुख होकर बैठे हैं (अर्थात् प्रत्येक मुनि को श्री रामजी अपने ही सामने मुख करके बैठे दिखाई देते हैं और सब मुनि टकटकी लगाए उनके मुख को देख रहे हैं)। ऐसा जान पड़ता है मानो चकोरों का समुदाय शरत्पूर्णिमा के चंद्रमा की ओर देख रहा है ॥
english_translation: Ram sits facing everyone in the gathering of sages, and they gaze at his moonlike form like a flock of chakors looking toward the autumn moon.
essence: True presence gathers every gaze without asking for it.
simple_meaning: Ram sits facing the gathered sages, and they keep their eyes fixed on his radiant face as if chakors are staring at the autumn moon.
insight: It shifts attention from scattered social chatter to reverent, focused presence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the noise softens because someone you trust finally arrived. Everyone keeps looking up, not out of politeness, but because presence itself has become the event.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब रघुबीर कहा मुनि पाहीं। तुम्ह सन प्रभु दुराव कछु नाहीं॥ तुम्ह जानहु जेहि कारन आयउँ। ताते तात न कहि समुझायउँ ॥
translation: तब श्री रामजी ने मुनि से कहा- हे प्रभो! आप से तो कुछ छिपाव है नहीं। मैं जिस कारण से आया हूँ, वह आप जानते ही हैं। इसी से हे तात! मैंने आपसे समझाकर कुछ नहीं कहा ॥
english_translation: Then Lord Ram said to the sage, “Nothing is hidden from you. You already know why I have come, so, dear one, I did not explain it to you.”
essence: What is truly understood needs very few words.
simple_meaning: Ram tells the sage that nothing is hidden from him. The sage already knows why Ram has come, so no long explanation is needed.
insight: It shifts you from explaining yourself to trusting that the right people can see clearly.
modern_relevance: You sit across from a mentor who can read the silence on your face. Before you defend yourself, they already understand. Some conversations become lighter when you stop performing and let the truth stand on its own.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: अब सो मंत्र देहु प्रभु मोही। जेहि प्रकार मारौं मुनिद्रोही॥ मुनि मुसुकाने सुनि प्रभु बानी। पूछेहु नाथ मोहि का जानी ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! अब आप मुझे वही मंत्र (सलाह) दीजिए, जिस प्रकार मैं मुनियों के द्रोही राक्षसों को मारूँ। प्रभु की वाणी सुनकर मुनि मुस्कुराए और बोले- हे नाथ! आपने क्या समझकर मुझसे यह प्रश्न किया? ॥
english_translation: "Now give me the counsel, Lord, by which I may kill the forest-dwelling demons who oppose the sages." Hearing the Lord's words, the sage smiled and said, "Lord, why would you ask me that?"
essence: A question can hide deeper understanding and invite closer guidance.
simple_meaning: Ram asks the sage for guidance on how to destroy the demons troubling the forest sages. The sage smiles, knowing Ram already understands far more than he is asking aloud.
insight: It shifts the moment from strategy to relationship, showing that true guidance begins in humility.
modern_relevance: You already know the answer, but you still ask someone you trust. The question is not confusion — it is the beginning of a deeper conversation.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तुम्हरेइँ भजन प्रभाव अघारी। जानउँ महिमा कछुक तुम्हारी॥ ऊमरि तरु बिसाल तव माया। फल ब्रह्मांड अनेक निकाया ॥
translation: हे पापों का नाश करने वाले! मैं तो आप ही के भजन के प्रभाव से आपकी कुछ थोड़ी सी महिमा जानता हूँ। आपकी माया गूलर के विशाल वृक्ष के समान है, अनेकों ब्रह्मांडों के समूह ही जिसके फल हैं ॥
english_translation: O destroyer of sins, I know only a little of your greatness through the power of your own devotion. Your illusion is like a vast fig tree, and countless universes are its fruits.
essence: Devotion reveals greatness, but never exhausts it.
simple_meaning: Ram says that even devotion reveals only a small part of his greatness. His cosmic power is so vast that countless universes are only a tiny expression of it.
insight: It shifts the mind from mastery to reverent humility, showing that devotion opens vision without exhausting mystery.
modern_relevance: You pray, meditate, or sit in silence and still feel you have only touched the edge. That feeling is not failure; it is a sign that what you seek is larger than your mind can contain.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जीव चराचर जंतु समाना। भीतर बसहिं न जानहिं आना॥ ते फल भच्छक कठिन कराला। तव भयँ डरत सदा सोउ काला ॥
translation: चर और अचर जीव (गूलर के फल के भीतर रहने वाले छोटे-छोटे) जंतुओं के समान उन (ब्रह्माण्ड रूपी फलों) के भीतर बसते हैं और वे (अपने उस छोटे से जगत् के सिवा) दूसरा कुछ नहीं जानते। उन फलों का भक्षण करने वाला कठिन और कराल काल है। वह काल भी सदा आपसे भयभीत रहता है ॥
english_translation: All moving and unmoving beings are like creatures living inside those fruits; they do not know anything beyond that inner world. The fierce, terrible Time that devours those fruits is always afraid of you.
essence: You are trapped only when you mistake a small world for the whole.
simple_meaning: All beings live inside a limited world and mistake it for everything. Even Time, the great destroyer, remains afraid of the divine.
insight: It shifts you from narrow identification to a wider view of reality and power.
modern_relevance: You spend weeks inside one disappointing email thread and start believing that one room, one boss, one failure is the whole universe. This verse pulls you back into scale.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: ते तुम्ह सकल लोकपति साईं। पूँछेहु मोहि मनुज की नाईं॥ यह बर मागउँ कृपानिकेता। बसहु हृदयँ श्री अनुज समेता ॥
translation: उन्हीं आपने समस्त लोकपालों के स्वामी होकर भी मुझसे मनुष्य की तरह प्रश्न किया। हे कृपा के धाम! मैं तो यह वर माँगता हूँ कि आप श्री सीताजी और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित मेरे हृदय में (सदा) निवास कीजिए ॥
english_translation: You are the lord of all worlds, yet you asked me like a human being. O home of grace, I ask for this boon: dwell in my heart with Sita and your younger brother Lakshman.
essence: The highest boon is not gain, but Ram living in your heart.
simple_meaning: The speaker honours Ram as the lord of all worlds, then asks for the highest blessing: that Ram, Sita, and Lakshman live in his heart forever.
insight: It shifts desire from outer rewards to inward companionship with the divine.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who has changed your life, and they ask what they can give you. You don't ask for money or status — you just want them close. That is this verse.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: अबिरल भगति बिरति सतसंगा। चरन सरोरुह प्रीति अभंगा॥ जद्यपि ब्रह्म अखंड अनंता। अनुभव गम्य भजहिं जेहि संता।6॥
translation: मुझे प्रगाढ़ भक्ति, वैराग्य, सत्संग और आपके चरणकमलों में अटूट प्रेम प्राप्त हो। यद्यपि आप अखंड और अनंत ब्रह्म हैं, जो अनुभव से ही जानने में आते हैं और जिनका संतजन भजन करते हैं ॥
english_translation: May I have unbroken devotion, detachment, good company, and undying love for your lotus feet. Although you are the boundless, endless supreme reality, the saints know you through direct experience and worship you.
essence: Unbroken devotion is the way to know the boundless.
simple_meaning: The speaker asks for steady devotion, non-attachment, holy companionship, and lasting love for Ram's feet. Even the supreme reality is reached through lived devotion.
insight: It shifts the aim from getting spiritual experiences to building a life that can sustain devotion.
modern_relevance: You leave a retreat feeling clear, then lose it by Tuesday morning in traffic and noise. What holds is not a high moment, but steady companionship, discipline, and love that keeps returning.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: अस तव रूप बखानउँ जानउँ। फिरि फिरि सगुन ब्रह्म रति मानउँ॥ संतत दासन्ह देहु बड़ाई। तातें मोहि पूँछेहु रघुराई ॥
translation: यद्यपि मैं आपके ऐसे रूप को जानता हूँ और उसका वर्णन भी करता हूँ, तो भी लौट-लौटकर में सगुण ब्रह्म में (आपके इस सुंदर स्वरूप में) ही प्रेम मानता हूँ। आप सेवकों को सदा ही बड़ाई दिया करते हैं, इसी से हे रघुनाथजी! आपने मुझसे पूछा है ॥
english_translation: Although I know how to describe your form, I keep returning again and again to loving your manifest, beautiful presence. You always honor your servants, and that is why, O Raghunath, you asked me.
essence: Knowing the divine form is not the same as loving it.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he understands Ram's divine form, yet his heart keeps returning to loving that visible, beautiful presence. Ram always honors his servants, so Tulsidas feels invited to speak.
insight: It shifts you from treating reverence as ignorance to seeing it as a chosen return to what matters most.
modern_relevance: You can read the books, name the principles, and still find your heart softening when someone you love walks into the room. Understanding is not the end of devotion; sometimes it is the doorway.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: है प्रभु परम मनोहर ठाऊँ। पावन पंचबटी तेहि नाऊँ॥ दंडक बन पुनीत प्रभु करहू। उग्र साप मुनिबर कर हरहू ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! एक परम मनोहर और पवित्र स्थान है, उसका नाम पंचवटी है। हे प्रभो! आप दण्डक वन को (जहाँ पंचवटी है) पवित्र कीजिए और श्रेष्ठ मुनि गौतमजी के कठोर शाप को हर लीजिए ॥
english_translation: O Lord, there is a most beautiful and sacred place. Its name is Panchavati. Please sanctify the Dandaka forest there, and remove the severe curse of the great sage.
essence: A sacred presence can transform even a cursed place.
simple_meaning: Panchavati is described as a beautiful, holy place, and Ram is asked to purify the forest and remove the sage’s curse.
insight: It shifts attention from scenery to sanctifying presence.
modern_relevance: A room can feel heavy after weeks of stress, arguments, and bad news. Then one calm person enters, and the whole atmosphere changes. Some places are healed by the presence they receive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बास करहु तहँ रघुकुल राया। कीजे सकल मुनिन्ह पर दाया॥ चले राम मुनि आयसु पाई। तुरतहिं पंचबटी निअराई ॥
translation: हे रघुकुल के स्वामी! आप सब मुनियों पर दया करके वहीं निवास कीजिए। मुनि की आज्ञा पाकर श्री रामचंद्रजी वहाँ से चल दिए और शीघ्र ही पंचवटी के निकट पहुँच गए ॥
english_translation: O Lord of Raghu's line, dwell there and show mercy to all the sages. Having received the sage's command, Ram immediately went and soon reached near Panchavati.
essence: Ram's greatness appears in how quickly he answers a righteous request.
simple_meaning: The sage asks Ram to stay in the holy place and bless the sages with mercy. Ram obeys at once and moves on to Panchavati.
insight: It trains the mind to treat a worthy request as a call to serve, not an inconvenience.
modern_relevance: Someone asks you to stay a little longer and help set things right before you leave. You don't make it about your schedule; you simply respond with care.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गीधराज सै भेंट भइ बहु बिधि प्रीति बढ़ाइ। गोदावरी निकट प्रभु रहे परन गृह छाइ ॥
translation: वहाँ गृध्रराज जटायु से भेंट हुई। उसके साथ बहुत प्रकार से प्रेम बढ़ाकर प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी गोदावरीजी के समीप पर्णकुटी छाकर रहने लगे ॥
english_translation: There, Ram met Jatayu and deepened their affection in many ways. Near the Godavari, the Lord lived in a leaf-hut.
essence: Humility and friendship can make a forest home feel complete.
simple_meaning: Ram met Jatayu and grew close to him. Then he stayed in a leaf-hut near the Godavari River.
insight: It shifts attention from grandeur to the quiet dignity of simple living and loyal companionship.
modern_relevance: You move into a small rented room and begin to notice who shows up with warmth, not status. The simplest place can become full of meaning when it holds real friendship.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जब ते राम कीन्ह तहँ बासा। सुखी भए मुनि बीती त्रासा॥ गिरि बन नदीं ताल छबि छाए। दिन दिन प्रति अति होहिं सुहाए ॥
translation: जब से श्री रामजी ने वहाँ निवास किया, तब से मुनि सुखी हो गए, उनका डर जाता रहा। पर्वत, वन, नदी और तालाब शोभा से छा गए। वे दिनोंदिन अधिक सुहावने (मालूम) होने लगे ॥
english_translation: When Ram took up residence there, the sages became happy and their fear disappeared. Mountains, forests, rivers, and lakes all shone with beauty and grew more lovely each day.
essence: Ram's presence turns fear into peace and wilderness into beauty.
simple_meaning: Ram's presence brings peace to the sages and beauty to the whole landscape. Fear fades, and everything feels more alive.
insight: It shows that a truly steady presence can transform both people and place.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the tension drops before anyone speaks. The mood changes because someone steady has arrived.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: खग मृग बृंद अनंदित रहहीं। मधुप मधुर गुंजत छबि लहहीं॥ सो बन बरनि न सक अहिराजा। जहाँ प्रगट रघुबीर बिराजा ॥
translation: पक्षी और पशुओं के समूह आनंदित रहते हैं और भौंरे मधुर गुंजार करते हुए शोभा पा रहे हैं। जहाँ प्रत्यक्ष श्री रामजी विराजमान हैं, उस वन का वर्णन सर्पराज शेषजी भी नहीं कर सकते ॥
english_translation: Birds and animals stay delighted there, and bees hum sweetly, adding to the beauty. Even Shesha, the king of serpents, cannot describe that forest where Raghubir is visibly present.
essence: Ram's presence turns even the forest into something beyond description.
simple_meaning: Ram's presence makes the forest feel alive and beautiful. Birds and animals are joyful there, and even the greatest serpent cannot fully describe it.
insight: It shifts attention from scenery alone to the transforming power of sacred presence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and feel the tension drop before anyone speaks. Some presence quietly changes the whole atmosphere, and everyone in the space feels it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक बार प्रभु सुख आसीना। लछिमन बचन कहे छलहीना॥ सुर नर मुनि सचराचर साईं। मैं पूछउँ निज प्रभु की नाईं ॥
translation: एक बार प्रभु श्री रामजी सुख से बैठे हुए थे। उस समय लक्ष्मणजी ने उनसे छलरहित (सरल) वचन कहे- हे देवता, मनुष्य, मुनि और चराचर के स्वामी! मैं अपने प्रभु की तरह (अपना स्वामी समझकर) आपसे पूछता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Once, the Lord was seated in ease. Then Lakshman spoke words free of deceit: “O master of gods, humans, sages, and all moving and unmoving beings, I ask you as I would ask my own lord.”
essence: Honest questioning opens the door to real guidance.
simple_meaning: Lakshman speaks honestly and respectfully to Ram, asking a question as if speaking to his own master. The verse sets up a sincere inquiry that leads into deeper teaching.
insight: It shifts the mind from guarded speech to sincere seeking.
modern_relevance: You sit beside someone you trust after a hard day and finally ask the question you have been carrying. No performance, no cleverness — just honesty. That is the kind of opening that invites real guidance.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: मोहि समुझाइ कहहु सोइ देवा। सब तजि करौं चरन रज सेवा॥ कहहु ग्यान बिराग अरु माया। कहहु सो भगति करहु जेहिं दाया ॥
translation: हे देव! मुझे समझाकर वही कहिए, जिससे सब छोड़कर मैं आपकी चरणरज की ही सेवा करूँ। ज्ञान, वैराग्य और माया का वर्णन कीजिए और उस भक्ति को कहिए, जिसके कारण आप दया करते हैं ॥
english_translation: O divine one, explain it to me so I may leave everything and serve only the dust of your feet. Speak of knowledge, detachment, and illusion, and speak of the devotion through which you show grace.
essence: Real understanding ends in service, not pride.
simple_meaning: Lakshman asks Ram to explain the path that leads him to give up everything except loving service at Ram's feet. He also asks for teaching on knowledge, detachment, illusion, and the devotion that draws grace.
insight: It shifts inquiry from collecting ideas to seeking the understanding that transforms devotion and conduct.
modern_relevance: You sit with a teacher after a breakup, a job loss, or a family rupture, and you don't want theory. You want the kind of understanding that actually changes what you cling to.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: ईस्वर जीव भेद प्रभु सकल कहौ समुझाइ। जातें होइ चरन रति सोक मोह भ्रम जाइ ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! ईश्वर और जीव का भेद भी सब समझाकर कहिए, जिससे आपके चरणों में मेरी प्रीति हो और शोक, मोह तथा भ्रम नष्ट हो जाएँ ॥
english_translation: O Lord, explain clearly the difference between the supreme being and the individual being, so that my love for your feet may arise and sorrow, delusion, and confusion may vanish.
essence: Clear understanding can turn confusion into love at the feet of the divine.
simple_meaning: Lakshman asks Ram to explain the difference between the supreme being and the individual self, because true understanding will grow devotion and remove sorrow, delusion, and confusion.
insight: It shifts the mind from vague devotion to clear understanding that strengthens devotion.
modern_relevance: You keep rereading the same message, trying to understand what someone really meant. Beneath the confusion is a deeper hunger: once you see clearly, your heart can settle and love without strain.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: थोरेहि महँ सब कहउँ बुझाई। सुनहु तात मति मन चित लाई॥ मैं अरु मोर तोर तैं माया। जेहिं बस कीन्हे जीव निकाया ॥
translation: (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे तात! मैं थोड़े ही में सब समझाकर कहे देता हूँ। तुम मन, चित्त और बुद्धि लगाकर सुनो! मैं और मेरा, तू और तेरा- यही माया है, जिसने समस्त जीवों को वश में कर रखा है ॥
english_translation: I will explain everything briefly. Listen carefully, with your mind and attention fixed. "I" and "mine," "you" and "yours"—this is the veil of appearance that has bound all living beings.
essence: Bondage begins the moment life is divided into mine and yours.
simple_meaning: Ram says the whole trap can be understood quickly: the sense of “I,” “mine,” “you,” and “yours” is what binds living beings.
insight: It shifts attention from external conflict to the mind’s habit of claiming and separating.
modern_relevance: You feel hurt the moment someone touches your idea, your partner, your status, your plan. The pain is often not the event itself, but the grip of ownership around it.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: गो गोचर जहँ लगि मन जाई। सो सब माया जानेहु भाई॥ तेहि कर भेद सुनहु तुम्ह सोऊ। बिद्या अपर अबिद्या दोऊ ॥
translation: इंद्रियों के विषयों को और जहाँ तक मन जाता है, हे भाई! उन सबको माया जानना। उसके भी एक विद्या और दूसरी अविद्या, इन दोनों भेदों को तुम सुनो- ॥
english_translation: Whatever the mind can reach through the senses, know all of that as illusion, brother. Hear now the difference between the two: knowledge and ignorance.
essence: What the mind can reach is not necessarily what is real.
simple_meaning: Everything the mind can reach through the senses is part of appearance, not ultimate reality. Ram then points to two kinds of understanding: one that frees, and one that keeps you trapped.
insight: It trains you to distinguish raw sensory experience from clear understanding, instead of treating every impression as truth.
modern_relevance: You scroll for an hour, feeling like you understand everything because you have seen so much. But seeing more is not the same as seeing clearly. This verse asks you to question what your restless mind keeps collecting.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: एक दुष्ट अतिसय दुखरूपा। जा बस जीव परा भवकूपा॥ एक रचइ जग गुन बस जाकें। प्रभु प्रेरित नहिं निज बल ताकें ॥
translation: एक (अविद्या) दुष्ट (दोषयुक्त) है और अत्यंत दुःखरूप है, जिसके वश होकर जीव संसार रूपी कुएँ में पड़ा हुआ है और एक (विद्या) जिसके वश में गुण है और जो जगत् की रचना करती है, वह प्रभु से ही प्रेरित होती है, उसके अपना बल कुछ भी नही है ॥
english_translation: One is wicked and full of suffering; under its grip, the living being falls into the pit of worldly existence. The other, ruled by virtue, creates the world, yet it acts only when moved by the supreme being and has no power of its own.
essence: One force enslaves; the other works only when the supreme reality moves it.
simple_meaning: Two powers are being described: one traps the living being in suffering, while the other is constructive but has no independent power and works only by the supreme being's prompting.
insight: It shifts you from treating appearances as autonomous to tracing every power back to its source.
modern_relevance: You watch a habit take over your day, then call it "just how I am." This verse cuts through that excuse: some forces enslave, and even the constructive ones are not ultimate.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: ग्यान मान जहँ एकउ नाहीं। देख ब्रह्म समान सब माहीं॥ कहिअ तात सो परम बिरागी। तृन सम सिद्धि तीनि गुन त्यागी ॥
translation: ज्ञान वह है, जहाँ (जिसमें) मान आदि एक भी (दोष) नहीं है और जो सबसे समान रूप से ब्रह्म को देखता है। हे तात! उसी को परम वैराग्यवान् कहना चाहिए, जो सारी सिद्धियों को और तीनों गुणों को तिनके के समान त्याग चुका हो ॥ (जिसमें मान, दम्भ, हिंसा, क्षमाराहित्य, टेढ़ापन, आचार्य सेवा का अभाव, अपवित्रता, अस्थिरता, मन का निगृहीत न होना, इंद्रियों के विषय में आसक्ति, अहंकार, जन्म-मृत्यु-जरा-व्याधिमय जगत् में सुख-बुद्धि, स्त्री-पुत्र-घर आदि में आसक्ति तथा ममता, इष्ट और अनिष्ट की प्राप्ति में हर्ष-शोक, भक्ति का अभाव, एकान्त में मन न लगना, विषयी मनुष्यों के संग में प्रेम- ये अठारह न हों और नित्य अध्यात्म (आत्मा) में स्थिति तथा तत्त्व ज्ञान के अर्थ (तत्त्वज्ञान के द्वारा जानने योग्य) परमात्मा का नित्य दर्शन हो, वही ज्ञान कहलाता है। देखिए गीता अध्याय 13/ 7 से 11)
english_translation: Knowledge is where not even a trace of pride remains, and where you see the supreme reality equally in all. O dear one, call that person truly detached who has cast aside all powers and the three qualities like straw.
essence: Real knowledge ends pride and makes every being look equal.
simple_meaning: Real knowledge removes pride and lets you see the same divine reality in everyone. Real detachment means not clinging to powers, achievements, or the three qualities of nature.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to equal vision, and from spiritual achievement to non-clinging.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who outranks you, and the old urge to compare flares up. This verse asks whether you can still see the same worth in both of you without needing to win the room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: माया ईस न आपु कहुँ जान कहिअ सो जीव। बंध मोच्छ प्रद सर्बपर माया प्रेरक सीव ॥
translation: जो माया को, ईश्वर को और अपने स्वरूप को नहीं जानता, उसे जीव कहना चाहिए। जो (कर्मानुसार) बंधन और मोक्ष देने वाला, सबसे परे और माया का प्रेरक है, वह ईश्वर है ॥
english_translation: One who does not know maya, the divine ruler, or the true self is called a living being. The one beyond all, who gives bondage and freedom and moves maya, is Shiva.
essence: Freedom begins when you see beyond maya and know the true self.
simple_meaning: A person is trapped when they do not understand illusion, the divine ruler, or their own true nature. Real freedom comes from seeing what is beyond all change.
insight: It shifts attention from surface events to the awareness that interprets them.
modern_relevance: You keep reacting to a message thread, a headline, and a private fear, all while forgetting the deeper question: who is actually seeing this? The verse pulls you back to first principles.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: धर्म तें बिरति जोग तें ग्याना। ग्यान मोच्छप्रद बेद बखाना॥ जातें बेगि द्रवउँ मैं भाई। सो मम भगति भगत सुखदाई ॥
translation: धर्म (के आचरण) से वैराग्य और योग से ज्ञान होता है तथा ज्ञान मोक्ष का देने वाला है- ऐसा वेदों ने वर्णन किया है। और हे भाई! जिससे मैं शीघ्र ही प्रसन्न होता हूँ, वह मेरी भक्ति है जो भक्तों को सुख देने वाली है ॥
english_translation: Renunciation comes from duty, and knowledge comes from yoga; the Vedas say knowledge gives freedom. And, brother, what makes me quickly pleased is my devotion, which gives joy to devotees.
essence: Devotion reaches Ram faster than any ladder of practice.
simple_meaning: Right conduct can lead to detachment, yoga can lead to knowledge, and knowledge can lead to freedom. But Ram says devotion is what delights him fastest and brings joy to devotees.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing spiritual status to offering simple, heartfelt devotion.
modern_relevance: You can spend months perfecting your practice, your routine, your arguments, your self-image — and still feel far away. Then one honest prayer, one unguarded act of love, changes the whole atmosphere.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सो सुतंत्र अवलंब न आना। तेहि आधीन ग्यान बिग्याना॥ भगति तात अनुपम सुखमूला। मिलइ जो संत होइँ अनुकूला ॥
translation: वह भक्ति स्वतंत्र है, उसको (ज्ञान-विज्ञान आदि किसी) दूसरे साधन का सहारा (अपेक्षा) नहीं है। ज्ञान और विज्ञान तो उसके अधीन हैं। हे तात! भक्ति अनुपम एवं सुख की मूल है और वह तभी मिलती है, जब संत अनुकूल (प्रसन्न) होते हैं ॥
english_translation: That devotion is independent and needs no other support. Knowledge and discernment are under its sway. O friend, devotion is the unmatched root of joy, and it comes only when the saints are pleased.
essence: Devotion is not the reward of wisdom; wisdom serves devotion.
simple_meaning: Devotion does not depend on any other path. Even knowledge and discernment serve it, and it becomes possible when saints are pleased.
insight: It shifts the mind from treating devotion as a result of insight to seeing insight as subordinate to devotion.
modern_relevance: You have read every book, rehearsed every answer, and still feel dry inside. This verse says the missing piece may not be more analysis, but a heart that can yield to devotion.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भगति कि साधन कहउँ बखानी। सुगम पंथ मोहि पावहिं प्रानी॥ प्रथमहिं बिप्र चरन अति प्रीती। निज निज कर्म निरत श्रुति रीती ॥
translation: अब मैं भक्ति के साधन विस्तार से कहता हूँ- यह सुगम मार्ग है, जिससे जीव मुझको सहज ही पा जाते हैं। पहले तो ब्राह्मणों के चरणों में अत्यंत प्रीति हो और वेद की रीति के अनुसार अपने-अपने (वर्णाश्रम के) कर्मों में लगा रहे ॥
english_translation: Now I will explain the means of bhakti. It is the easy path by which living beings can reach me with ease. First, there should be deep love for the feet of the learned, and one should remain engaged in one's own duties according to the Vedic order.
essence: The easiest way to reach Ram is to honor wisdom and keep your duties.
simple_meaning: Bhakti is presented as an easy path: love the learned, and stay faithful to your own duties. That combination makes reaching Ram natural and direct.
insight: It shifts devotion from private emotion to a disciplined way of living.
modern_relevance: You admire a mentor, then still show up for your work, your family, and your promises. That mix of reverence and responsibility is what makes devotion livable.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: एहि कर फल पुनि बिषय बिरागा। तब मम धर्म उपज अनुरागा॥ श्रवनादिक नव भक्ति दृढ़ाहीं। मम लीला रति अति मन माहीं ॥
translation: इसका फल, फिर विषयों से वैराग्य होगा। तब (वैराग्य होने पर) मेरे धर्म (भागवत धर्म) में प्रेम उत्पन्न होगा। तब श्रवण आदि नौ प्रकार की भक्तियाँ दृढ़ होंगी और मन में मेरी लीलाओं के प्रति अत्यंत प्रेम होगा ॥
english_translation: Its fruit is detachment from worldly objects. Then love for my dharma arises. Then the nine forms of devotion become firm, and the mind grows deeply fond of my divine plays.
essence: Detachment makes devotion stable, and stable devotion makes Ram's presence sweet.
simple_meaning: When attachment to worldly things fades, love for Ram's way appears. Then listening, remembering, and the other forms of devotion become steady, and the mind begins to delight in his stories.
insight: It shifts you from chasing stimulation to building a mind that can stay with devotion.
modern_relevance: You stop checking your phone for one more hit of distraction, and suddenly prayer, music, or quiet reflection feels natural again. The appetite for noise weakens first; deeper love can finally settle in.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: संत चरन पंकज अति प्रेमा। मन क्रम बचन भजन दृढ़ नेमा॥ गुरु पितु मातु बंधु पति देवा। सब मोहि कहँ जानै दृढ़ सेवा ॥
translation: जिसका संतों के चरणकमलों में अत्यंत प्रेम हो, मन, वचन और कर्म से भजन का दृढ़ नियम हो और जो मुझको ही गुरु, पिता, माता, भाई, पति और देवता सब कुछ जाने और सेवा में दृढ़ हो, ॥
english_translation: One who deeply loves the feet of saints, keeps firm devotion in mind, words, and deeds, and sees me alone as teacher, father, mother, brother, husband, and divine, serves with unwavering dedication.
essence: True devotion makes one presence enough for every role in life.
simple_meaning: Deep devotion shows itself as love for holy people, steady worship in thought, speech, and action, and seeing Ram as the one true refuge in every role of life.
insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to a whole-life orientation of service and remembrance.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone for one person’s reply, but your real devotion shows up in what you repeatedly choose, protect, and serve. Love becomes visible in loyalty.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: मम गुन गावत पुलक सरीरा। गदगद गिरा नयन बह नीरा॥ काम आदि मद दंभ न जाकें। तात निरंतर बस मैं ताकें ॥
translation: मेरा गुण गाते समय जिसका शरीर पुलकित हो जाए, वाणी गदगद हो जाए और नेत्रों से (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल बहने लगे और काम, मद और दम्भ आदि जिसमें न हों, हे भाई! मैं सदा उसके वश में रहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: When someone sings my qualities, their body shivers with joy, their voice breaks with emotion, and tears flow from their eyes. One who has no desire, pride, or vanity—dear friend, I always remain under that person's control.
essence: When pride is gone, love can pull the divine close.
simple_meaning: True devotion shows itself in tears, trembling, and speech that breaks with feeling. When pride and selfish desire are absent, Ram says he comes under that person's sway.
insight: It shifts devotion from display to surrender, showing that humility makes the heart receptive.
modern_relevance: You hear your favorite song in a crowded car and suddenly your eyes fill, your voice catches, and nothing in you feels guarded. That kind of unselfconscious love is what this verse points to.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: बचन कर्म मन मोरि गति भजनु करहिं निःकाम। तिन्ह के हृदय कमल महुँ करउँ सदा बिश्राम ॥
translation: जिनको कर्म, वचन और मन से मेरी ही गति है और जो निष्काम भाव से मेरा भजन करते हैं, उनके हृदय कमल में मैं सदा विश्राम किया करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Those whose mind, speech, and action move only toward me, and who worship me without desire for reward — I dwell forever in the lotus of their hearts.
essence: Selfless devotion makes the heart Ram’s resting place.
simple_meaning: When your mind, speech, and actions are all directed toward Ram, and you worship without wanting a reward, Ram lives in your heart.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to wholehearted alignment.
modern_relevance: You show up for someone with no hidden agenda, no need for applause, no secret scorekeeping. That kind of love makes room for something sacred to stay.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: भगति जोग सुनि अति सुख पावा। लछिमन प्रभु चरनन्हि सिरु नावा॥ एहि बिधि कछुक दिन बीती। कहत बिराग ग्यान गुन नीती ॥
translation: इस भक्ति योग को सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी ने अत्यंत सुख पाया और उन्होंने प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणों में सिर नवाया। इस प्रकार वैराग्य, ज्ञान, गुण और नीति कहते हुए कुछ दिन बीत गए ॥
english_translation: Hearing this yoga of devotion, Lakshman felt immense joy and bowed his head at Lord Ram's feet. In this way, some days passed, with talks of detachment, wisdom, virtues, and conduct.
essence: Devotion first moves the heart; then wisdom can be spoken.
simple_meaning: Lakshman feels deep joy on hearing about devotion and bows to Ram. Then the days pass as they keep speaking about detachment, wisdom, virtues, and right conduct.
insight: It shows how devotion can soften the heart before any argument or philosophy begins.
modern_relevance: You finally hear a teaching that feels true, and your whole body relaxes. Then you keep circling the same questions with someone you trust, and the days become lighter.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सूपनखा रावन कै बहिनी। दुष्ट हृदय दारुन जस अहिनी॥ पंचबटी सो गइ एक बारा। देखि बिकल भइ जुगल कुमारा ॥
translation: शूर्पणखा नामक रावण की एक बहिन थी, जो नागिन के समान भयानक और दुष्ट हृदय की थी। वह एक बार पंचवटी में गई और दोनों राजकुमारों को देखकर विकल (काम से पीड़ित) हो गई ॥
english_translation: Sūpanakhā was Rāvaṇa’s sister. Her heart was cruel and wicked, like a serpent’s. Once she went to Panchavati and, seeing the two princes, became agitated with desire.
essence: Desire can enter wearing beauty and still carry danger.
simple_meaning: Surpanakha, Ravana’s sister, comes to Panchavati and becomes unsettled when she sees Ram and Lakshman. The verse introduces her as dangerous and driven by desire.
insight: It prepares the mind to notice how desire can distort judgment before any action begins.
modern_relevance: A stranger’s attention can feel flattering at first, then suddenly unsafe. This verse shows how quickly desire can turn into threat when it is unchecked.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भ्राता पिता पुत्र उरगारी। पुरुष मनोहर निरखत नारी॥ होइ बिकल सक मनहि न रोकी। जिमि रबिमनि द्रव रबिहि बिलोकी ॥
translation: (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं-) हे गरुड़जी! (शूर्पणखा- जैसी राक्षसी, धर्मज्ञान शून्य कामान्ध) स्त्री मनोहर पुरुष को देखकर, चाहे वह भाई, पिता, पुत्र ही हो, विकल हो जाती है और मन को नहीं रोक सकती। जैसे सूर्यकान्तमणि सूर्य को देखकर द्रवित हो जाती है (ज्वाला से पिघल जाती है) ॥
english_translation: A woman, upon seeing a handsome man, becomes agitated even if he is a brother, father, or son. She cannot hold her mind steady, just as a sun-stone melts when it sees the sun.
essence: Desire can seize the mind before reason gets a chance.
simple_meaning: Seeing beauty can stir desire so strongly that the mind loses steadiness and stops obeying reason.
insight: It trains you to notice attraction as it begins, before it turns into action.
modern_relevance: You open a photo, tell yourself it is harmless, and five minutes later your attention has been pulled off course. The mind can slip into craving faster than pride can admit.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: रुचिर रूप धरि प्रभु पहिं जाई। बोली बचन बहुत मुसुकाई॥ तुम्ह सम पुरुष न मो सम नारी। यह सँजोग बिधि रचा बिचारी ॥
translation: वह सुन्दर रूप धरकर प्रभु के पास जाकर और बहुत मुस्कुराकर वचन बोली- न तो तुम्हारे समान कोई पुरुष है, न मेरे समान स्त्री। विधाता ने यह संयोग (जोड़ा) बहुत विचार कर रचा है ॥
english_translation: She took a lovely form, went to the Lord, and spoke with a broad smile: “There is no man like you, and no woman like me. The creator has arranged this meeting with great thought.”
essence: False sweetness can disguise a dangerous intention.
simple_meaning: She approaches him in a beautiful form, smiles, and flatters him by saying their meeting must be fate.
insight: It shows how manipulation often begins with admiration, softness, and a story that makes desire feel ordained.
modern_relevance: Someone sends a polished message that feels too smooth to be real. The praise is flattering, but the intention underneath is not innocent.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मम अनुरूप पुरुष जग माहीं। देखेउँ खोजि लोक तिहु नाहीं॥ तातें अब लगि रहिउँ कुमारी। मनु माना कछु तुम्हहि निहारी ॥
translation: मेरे योग्य पुरुष (वर) जगत् भर में नहीं है, मैंने तीनों लोकों को खोज देखा। इसी से मैं अब तक कुमारी (अविवाहित) रही। अब तुमको देखकर कुछ मन माना (चित्त ठहरा) है ॥
english_translation: No man in the world matched me; I searched the three worlds and found none. That is why I remained unmarried until now. Seeing you, my mind has become steady.
essence: Desire can make you mistake attraction for final certainty.
simple_meaning: She says she searched everywhere for a man equal to her and found none, so she stayed unmarried until seeing Ram.
insight: It shows how desire narrows judgment and turns attraction into a claim of destiny.
modern_relevance: You scroll through endless profiles, convinced no one measures up, until one person catches your eye and the whole story changes. Attraction can feel like certainty before it has any wisdom.
speaker: Shurpanakha

verse_text: सीतहि चितइ कही प्रभु बाता। अहइ कुआर मोर लघु भ्राता॥ गइ लछिमन रिपु भगिनी जानी। प्रभु बिलोकि बोले मृदु बानी ॥
translation: सीताजी की ओर देखकर प्रभु श्री रामजी ने यह बात कही कि मेरा छोटा भाई कुमार है। तब वह लक्ष्मणजी के पास गई। लक्ष्मणजी ने उसे शत्रु की बहिन समझकर और प्रभु की ओर देखकर कोमल वाणी से बोले- ॥
english_translation: Sita looked at him, and the Lord said, "My younger brother is unmarried." Then she went to Lakshman. Seeing her as the enemy's sister and looking at the Lord, Lakshman spoke gently.
essence: Right speech can hold both caution and kindness.
simple_meaning: Ram points Sita toward Lakshman and says his younger brother is unmarried. Lakshman then speaks gently, treating her as the enemy's sister while still looking to Ram.
insight: It shows how loyalty, caution, and courtesy can coexist in a difficult encounter.
modern_relevance: You meet someone in a charged moment and choose your words carefully, not to inflame the situation. That restraint can protect everyone involved.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुंदरि सुनु मैं उन्ह कर दासा। पराधीन नहिं तोर सुपासा॥ प्रभु समर्थ कोसलपुर राजा। जो कछु करहिं उनहि सब छाजा ॥
translation: हे सुंदरी! सुन, मैं तो उनका दास हूँ। मैं पराधीन हूँ, अतः तुम्हे सुभीता (सुख) न होगा। प्रभु समर्थ हैं, कोसलपुर के राजा है, वे जो कुछ करें, उन्हें सब फबता है ॥
english_translation: O beautiful one, listen: I am their servant. I am under another's control, so I cannot help you. The Lord is powerful, the king of Kosala; whatever they do, all suits them.
essence: Serving rightly means refusing what your role cannot permit.
simple_meaning: Lakshman tells Surpanakha that he serves Ram and cannot act independently. Ram is the powerful king, and whatever he does is fitting.
insight: It teaches you to hold your service steady even when someone demands more than you can give.
modern_relevance: Someone asks you for a favor that would cross a line you already know. You feel the pressure to be agreeable, but your role, promise, or loyalty comes first.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: सेवक सुख चह मान भिखारी। ब्यसनी धन सुभ गति बिभिचारी॥ लोभी जसु चह चार गुमानी। नभ दुहि दूध चहत ए प्रानी ॥
translation: सेवक सुख चाहे, भिखारी सम्मान चाहे, व्यसनी (जिसे जुए, शराब आदि का व्यसन हो) धन और व्यभिचारी शुभ गति चाहे, लोभी यश चाहे और अभिमानी चारों फल- अर्थ, धर्म, काम, मोक्ष चाहे, तो ये सब प्राणी आकाश को दुहकर दूध लेना चाहते हैं (अर्थात् असंभव बात को संभव करना चाहते हैं) ॥
english_translation: A servant may want comfort, a beggar may want respect, an addict may want wealth, an adulterer may want a good fate, the greedy may want fame, and the proud may want all four aims of life. They are trying to milk the sky for milk.
essence: Impossible desires collapse when your life contradicts your wishes.
simple_meaning: People often want blessings that their own habits make impossible. A servant wants comfort, a beggar wants respect, and a proud person wants all four aims of life.
insight: It pushes you to notice when your goals and habits are fighting each other.
modern_relevance: You want a calm mind, but you keep doom-scrolling past midnight. You want trust, but you keep feeding suspicion. The verse cuts through that self-contradiction.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि फिरि राम निकट सो आई। प्रभु लछिमन पहिं बहुरि पठाई॥ लछिमन कहा तोहि सो बरई। जो तृन तोरि लाज परिहरई ॥
translation: वह लौटकर फिर श्री रामजी के पास आई, प्रभु ने उसे फिर लक्ष्मणजी के पास भेज दिया। लक्ष्मणजी ने कहा- तुम्हें वही वरेगा, जो लज्जा को तृण तोड़कर (अर्थात् प्रतिज्ञा करके) त्याग देगा (अर्थात् जो निपट निर्लज्ज होगा) ॥
english_translation: She came back again to Ram, and the Lord sent her once more to Lakshman. Lakshman said, "You will choose only the one who casts off shame like a blade of grass."
essence: Repeated disrespect meets a sharper boundary.
simple_meaning: She returns to Ram, and he sends her to Lakshman again. Lakshman answers sharply: only someone with no shame at all would accept her.
insight: It shows that repeated intrusion can be met with direct refusal, not endless politeness.
modern_relevance: Someone keeps pushing past your first no, hoping the second time will be easier. You finally answer plainly, without apology, because the boundary itself matters.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब खिसिआनि राम पहिं गई। रूप भयंकर प्रगटत भई॥ सीतहि सभय देखि रघुराई। कहा अनुज सन सयन बुझाई ॥
translation: तब वह खिसियायी हुई (क्रुद्ध होकर) श्री रामजी के पास गई और उसने अपना भयंकर रूप प्रकट किया। सीताजी को भयभीत देखकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने लक्ष्मण को इशारा देकर कहा ॥
english_translation: Then, angered, she went to Ram and revealed her terrible form. Seeing Sita frightened, Raghunath signaled to Lakshman.
essence: Anger can turn ugly, but calm awareness still sees the real danger.
simple_meaning: The woman returns in anger, shows a frightening form, and Ram notices Sita’s fear and signals Lakshman.
insight: It shifts attention from the aggressor’s performance to the vulnerable person who needs protection.
modern_relevance: Someone storms back into a room after being embarrassed, trying to regain control with intimidation. The calm person notices who is actually shaken and quietly lets the right response begin.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लछिमन अति लाघवँ सो नाक कान बिनु कीन्हि। ताके कर रावन कहँ मनौ चुनौती दीन्हि ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी ने बड़ी फुर्ती से उसको बिना नाक-कान की कर दिया। मानो उसके हाथ रावण को चुनौती दी हो! ॥
english_translation: Lakshman swiftly cut off her nose and ears, as if he had thrown Ravana a challenge.
essence: A swift retaliation turns mockery into a direct challenge.
simple_meaning: Lakshman quickly disfigures the woman by cutting off her nose and ears, and the line compares it to a challenge thrown at Ravana.
insight: It shows how a single retaliatory act can transform insult into open conflict.
modern_relevance: A heated argument can turn into a point of no return in seconds. One sharp response can escalate everything beyond repair.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाक कान बिनु भइ बिकरारा। जनु स्रव सैल गेरु कै धारा॥ खर दूषन पहिं गइ बिलपाता। धिग धिग तव पौरुष बल भ्राता ॥
translation: बिना नाक-कान के वह विकराल हो गई। (उसके शरीर से रक्त इस प्रकार बहने लगा) मानो (काले) पर्वत से गेरू की धारा बह रही हो। वह विलाप करती हुई खर-दूषण के पास गई (और बोली-) हे भाई! तुम्हारे पौरुष (वीरता) को धिक्कार है, तुम्हारे बल को धिक्कार है ॥
english_translation: She became hideous without nose and ears, as if a stream of red ochre flowed from a black mountain. Wailing, she went to Khara and Dushana and cried, "Shame on your manhood, shame on your strength, brother!"
essence: Humiliation, left unchecked, becomes the spark for revenge.
simple_meaning: After Lakshman maimed her, Surpanakha became terrifying to look at and ran crying to her brothers, insulting their courage and strength.
insight: It shows how wounded pride can convert private injury into collective retaliation.
modern_relevance: A heated argument leaves someone humiliated, and instead of cooling down, they call a sibling or friend to rally support. Hurt quickly becomes escalation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहिं पूछा सब कहेसि बुझाई। जातुधान सुनि सेन बनाई॥ धाए निसिचर निकर बरूथा। जनु सपच्छ कज्जल गिरि जूथा ॥
translation: उन्होंने पूछा, तब शूर्पणखा ने सब समझाकर कहा। सब सुनकर राक्षसों ने सेना तैयार की। राक्षस समूह झुंड के झुंड दौड़े। मानो पंखधारी काजल के पर्वतों का झुंड हो ॥
english_translation: She was questioned, and then she explained everything clearly. Hearing it, the demons formed their army. The demon hosts rushed forward in swarms, like flocks of winged black mountains.
essence: Anger multiplies fast when a wound is handed to a crowd.
simple_meaning: After hearing Shurpanakha's report, the demons quickly gather their army and rush out in huge numbers.
insight: It shows how quickly resentment spreads when pain is turned into retaliation.
modern_relevance: One angry message in a family group chat can turn private hurt into a full-blown fight before anyone has cooled down.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाना बाहन नानाकारा। नानायुध धर घोर अपारा॥ सूपनखा आगें करि लीनी। असुभ रूप श्रुति नासा हीनी ॥
translation: वे अनेकों प्रकार की सवारियों पर चढ़े हुए तथा अनेकों आकार (सूरतों) के हैं। वे अपार हैं और अनेकों प्रकार के असंख्य भयानक हथियार धारण किए हुए हैं। उन्होंने नाक-कान कटी हुई अमंगलरूपिणी शूर्पणखा को आगे कर लिया ॥
english_translation: They rode on many kinds of mounts, in many forms, carrying countless terrible weapons. They placed the disfigured, inauspicious Shurpanakha in front.
essence: Power driven by hurt still marches toward ruin.
simple_meaning: The demon army arrives in many forms, on many mounts, with many weapons, and they put Shurpanakha at the front.
insight: It shifts attention from the army's spectacle to the emotion driving it: revenge born from injury.
modern_relevance: A crowd gathers outside a house after one person has been humiliated, and the whole mood turns sharp and reckless. The force looks huge, but it is really just wounded outrage spreading.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: असगुन अमित होहिं भयकारी। गनहिं न मृत्यु बिबस सब झारी॥ गर्जहिं तर्जहिं गगन उड़ाहीं। देखि कटकु भट अति हरषाहीं ॥
translation: अनगिनत भयंकर अशकुन हो रहे हैं, परंतु मृत्यु के वश होने के कारण वे सब के सब उनको कुछ गिनते ही नहीं। गरजते हैं, ललकारते हैं और आकाश में उड़ते हैं। सेना देखकर योद्धा लोग बहुत ही हर्षित होते हैं ॥
english_translation: Countless ominous signs appear, but the warriors, driven by death, pay them no mind. They roar, shout, and fly through the sky. Seeing the army, the fighters are filled with joy.
essence: Fearful omens mean nothing to those already rushing toward ruin.
simple_meaning: Bad omens fill the sky, but the warriors ignore them and rush ahead, roaring and shouting. The sight of the army only makes them more excited.
insight: It shows how collective aggression can override caution and make destruction feel thrilling.
modern_relevance: You’ve seen a group get hyped in a group chat, ignoring every warning sign, and rush straight into a mess. Momentum can make danger feel like celebration.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोउ कह जिअत धरहु द्वौ भाई। धरि मारहु तिय लेहु छड़ाई॥ धूरि पूरि नभ मंडल रहा। राम बोलाइ अनुज सन कहा ॥
translation: कोई कहता है दोनों भाइयों को जीता ही पकड़ लो, पकड़कर मार डालो और स्त्री को छीन लो। आकाशमण्डल धूल से भर गया। तब श्री रामजी ने लक्ष्मणजी को बुलाकर उनसे कहा ॥
english_translation: Some said, “Catch both brothers alive, kill them after capturing them, and take the woman away.” Dust filled the sky. Then Ram called Lakshman and said:
essence: The crisis is now, and Ram answers with command.
simple_meaning: The scene turns chaotic as enemies shout orders to seize Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Dust fills the sky, and Ram turns to Lakshman to respond.
insight: It shifts attention from fear to immediate protective action.
modern_relevance: A crowded street suddenly turns tense, voices rise, and you have seconds to decide who to protect and where to move. Clarity matters more than panic.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लै जानकिहि जाहु गिरि कंदर। आवा निसिचर कटकु भयंकर॥ रहेहु सजग सुनि प्रभु कै बानी। चले सहित श्री सर धनु पानी ॥
translation: राक्षसों की भयानक सेना आ गई है। जानकीजी को लेकर तुम पर्वत की कंदरा में चले जाओ। सावधान रहना। प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी के वचन सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी हाथ में धनुष-बाण लिए श्री सीताजी सहित चले ॥
english_translation: The terrifying army of demons has arrived. Take Janaki to the mountain cave. Stay alert. Hearing Lord Ram's words, Lakshman went with bow and arrows in hand, along with Sita.
essence: Urgency becomes clear service when danger arrives.
simple_meaning: The enemy army has arrived, so Sita should be taken to safety while everyone stays alert. Lakshman obeys Ram at once and leaves with bow in hand.
insight: It shifts attention from fear to immediate protective action.
modern_relevance: A storm alert flashes on your phone, and you move the children to the safest room before grabbing your keys. In a crisis, calm obedience protects more than fear does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि राम रिपुदल चलि आवा। बिहसि कठिन कोदंड चढ़ावा ॥
translation: शत्रुओं की सेना (समीप) चली आई है, यह देखकर श्री रामजी ने हँसकर कठिन धनुष को चढ़ाया ॥
english_translation: Seeing the enemy army advance, Ram smiled and strung the mighty bow.
essence: Fear does not enter where readiness is already complete.
simple_meaning: Ram sees the enemy army approaching and calmly prepares his bow for battle.
insight: It shifts you from fear to composed readiness when pressure arrives.
modern_relevance: You hear the worst possible update just before a meeting, and your chest tightens. Then you breathe, straighten up, and handle the next step without drama.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोदंड कठिन चढ़ाइ सिर जट जूट बाँधत सोह क्यों। मरकत सयल पर लरत दामिनि कोटि सों जुग भुजग ज्यों॥ कटि कसि निषंग बिसाल भुज गहि चाप बिसिख सुधारि कै। चितवत मनहुँ मृगराज प्रभु गजराज घटा निहारि कै॥
translation: कठिन धनुष चढ़ाकर सिर पर जटा का जू़ड़ा बाँधते हुए प्रभु कैसे शोभित हो रहे हैं, जैसे मरकतमणि (पन्ने) के पर्वत पर करोड़ों बिजलियों से दो साँप लड़ रहे हों। कमर में तरकस कसकर, विशाल भुजाओं में धनुष लेकर और बाण सुधारकर प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी राक्षसों की ओर देख रहे हैं। मानों मतवाले हाथियों के समूह को (आता) देखकर सिंह (उनकी ओर) ताक रहा हो।
english_translation: How splendid the Lord looks, bow raised, matted hair tied on his head, like two serpents fighting on a mountain of emerald and lightning. With his quiver tightened at the waist, mighty arms holding the bow, arrows ready, he watches the enemy like a lion watching a herd of elephants.
essence: True courage looks beautiful because it is completely prepared.
simple_meaning: Ram stands ready for battle, beautifully fierce and fully armed, watching the enemy with calm strength.
insight: It shifts attention from fear to poised readiness under pressure.
modern_relevance: You tighten your helmet strap before walking into the room where the hard conversation waits. Your calm is not weakness; it is readiness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आइ गए बगमेल धरहु धरहु धावत सुभट। जथा बिलोकि अकेल बाल रबिहि घेरत दनुज ॥
translation: 'पकड़ो-पकड़ो' पुकारते हुए राक्षस योद्धा बाग छोड़कर (बड़ी तेजी से) दौड़े हुए आए (और उन्होंने श्री रामजी को चारों ओर से घेर लिया), जैसे बालसूर्य (उदयकालीन सूर्य) को अकेला देखकर मन्देह नामक दैत्य घेर लेते हैं ॥
english_translation: The warrior-raksasas rushed in, shouting, “Catch him! Catch him!” and surrounded the lone Ram like demons surrounding the young sun.
essence: Aloneness can still stand unshaken when danger closes in.
simple_meaning: The enemy warriors rushed toward Ram and surrounded him, just as demons would crowd around the rising sun.
insight: It frames crisis as a moment of visible courage, not panic.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room and realize every eye is on you at once. The pressure feels sudden, but the verse holds the image of standing alone without shrinking.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु बिलोकि सर सकहिं न डारी। थकित भई रजनीचर धारी॥ सचिव बोलि बोले खर दूषन। यह कोउ नृपबालक नर भूषन ॥
translation: (सौंदर्य-माधुर्यनिधि) प्रभु श्री रामजी को देखकर राक्षसों की सेना थकित रह गई। वे उन पर बाण नहीं छोड़ सके। मंत्री को बुलाकर खर-दूषण ने कहा- यह राजकुमार कोई मनुष्यों का भूषण है ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ram, the demon army grew tired and could not shoot their arrows. Calling his minister, Khara-Dushana said, "This prince is truly an ornament of humankind."
essence: True majesty can stop violence before it begins.
simple_meaning: Ram's presence leaves the demon army stunned and unable to attack. Even Khara-Dushana recognizes that this prince is extraordinary.
insight: It shows how presence can disarm aggression before force is used.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room ready for conflict, but something about your calm changes the whole atmosphere. Even the people braced against you can feel your steadiness before a word is spoken.
speaker: Khara-Dushana

verse_text: नाग असुर सुर नर मुनि जेते। देखे जिते हते हम केते॥ हम भरि जन्म सुनहु सब भाई। देखी नहिं असि सुंदरताई ॥
translation: जितने भी नाग, असुर, देवता, मनुष्य और मुनि हैं, उनमें से हमने न जाने कितने ही देखे, जीते और मार डाले हैं। पर हे सब भाइयों! सुनो, हमने जन्मभर में ऐसी सुंदरता कहीं नहीं देखी ॥
english_translation: We have seen, defeated, and killed countless serpents, demons, gods, humans, and sages. But listen, brothers: in all our lives, we have never seen such beauty.
essence: Beauty can silence even the proudest enemies.
simple_meaning: Ravana's men boast that they have faced every kind of being and defeated many, yet they admit they have never seen beauty like Ram's.
insight: It shows how true greatness can disarm aggression before any weapon is used.
modern_relevance: You meet someone in a room who makes your usual confidence feel small. The mind that came ready to dominate suddenly has to admit, 'I have never seen this before.'
speaker: Ravana's ministers

verse_text: जद्यपि भगिनी कीन्हि कुरूपा। बध लायक नहिं पुरुष अनूपा॥ देहु तुरत निज नारि दुराई। जीअत भवन जाहु द्वौ भाई ॥
translation: यद्यपि इन्होंने हमारी बहिन को कुरूप कर दिया तथापि ये अनुपम पुरुष वध करने योग्य नहीं हैं। 'छिपाई हुई अपनी स्त्री हमें तुरंत दे दो और दोनों भाई जीते जी घर लौट जाओ' ॥
english_translation: Although they have disfigured our sister, such an incomparable man is not fit to be killed. Hand over your hidden wife at once, and both brothers may return home alive.
essence: Pride can admire greatness and still refuse to yield.
simple_meaning: Ravana admits the brothers are extraordinary, but still demands Sita back and offers them safe return if they comply.
insight: It exposes how ego can speak in compliments while still demanding control.
modern_relevance: A person can praise your talent in one breath and pressure you in the next. Recognition does not always mean respect; sometimes it is just strategy.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: मोर कहा तुम्ह ताहि सुनावहु। तासु बचन सुनि आतुर आवहु॥ दूतन्ह कहा राम सन जाई। सुनत राम बोले मुसुकाई ॥
translation: मेरा यह कथन तुम लोग उसे सुनाओ और उसका वचन (उत्तर) सुनकर शीघ्र आओ। दूतों ने जाकर यह संदेश श्री रामचंद्रजी से कहा। उसे सुनते ही श्री रामचंद्रजी मुस्कुराकर बोले- ॥
english_translation: Tell him my words, and come back quickly after hearing his reply. The messengers carried the message to Ram, and hearing it, Ram smiled.
essence: A steady heart does not lose itself when challenged.
simple_meaning: Ravana tells the messengers to carry his words and return quickly with the reply. When Ram hears the message, he smiles.
insight: It shows how calm presence can answer provocation before any battle begins.
modern_relevance: Someone sends a sharp email meant to provoke you, but you read it once and stay steady. Not every challenge deserves agitation; some only reveal how settled you are.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: हम छत्री मृगया बन करहीं। तुम्ह से खल मृग खोजत फिरहीं॥ रिपु बलवंत देखि नहिं डरहीं। एक बार कालहु सन लरहीं ॥
translation: हम क्षत्रिय हैं, वन में शिकार करते हैं और तुम्हारे सरीखे दुष्ट पशुओं को तो ढ़ूँढते ही फिरते हैं। हम बलवान् शत्रु देखकर नहीं डरते। (लड़ने को आवे तो) एक बार तो हम काल से भी लड़ सकते हैं ॥
english_translation: We are warriors who hunt in the forest. We keep searching for wicked beasts like you. Seeing a strong enemy does not frighten us. If needed, we can even fight Death itself.
essence: Real courage stands firm even before death.
simple_meaning: Lakshman answers with fierce confidence: he and Ram are not afraid of powerful enemies and are ready for battle.
insight: It strengthens the mind to face threat without flinching or self-doubt.
modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a meeting, trying to make you look small. You don't have to match their volume, but you also don't have to fold.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: जद्यपि मनुज दनुज कुल घालक। मुनि पालक खल सालक बालक॥ जौं न होइ बल घर फिरि जाहू। समर बिमुख मैं हतउँ न काहू ॥
translation: यद्यपि हम मनुष्य हैं, परन्तु दैत्यकुल का नाश करने वाले और मुनियों की रक्षा करने वाले हैं, हम बालक हैं, परन्तु दुष्टों को दण्ड देने वाले। यदि बल न हो तो घर लौट जाओ। संग्राम में पीठ दिखाने वाले किसी को मैं नहीं मारता ॥
english_translation: Although we are human, we destroy the race of demons and protect the sages. Though we are boys, we punish the wicked. If you lack strength, go back home. I do not strike anyone who turns away from battle.
essence: Strength protects the good and refuses to chase the fleeing.
simple_meaning: Ram says his side exists to protect sages and defeat evil. He challenges the enemy to leave if they cannot fight with strength.
insight: It shifts the mind from posturing to honest action under pressure.
modern_relevance: A tense argument is already turning into a fight, and someone starts bluffing instead of speaking plainly. This verse cuts through the performance: either stand by what you came for, or step away.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: रन चढ़ि करिअ कपट चतुराई। रिपु पर कृपा परम कदराई॥ दूतन्ह जाइ तुरत सब कहेऊ। सुनि खर दूषन उर अति दहेऊ ॥
translation: रण में चढ़ आकर कपट-चतुराई करना और शत्रु पर कृपा करना (दया दिखाना) तो बड़ी भारी कायरता है। दूतों ने लौटकर तुरंत सब बातें कहीं, जिन्हें सुनकर खर-दूषण का हृदय अत्यंत जल उठा ॥
english_translation: Charging into battle and then using deceitful cleverness, or showing mercy to an enemy, is great cowardice. The messengers quickly reported everything, and hearing it, Khara and Dushana burned with anger.
essence: Deceit and false softness have no place once battle has begun.
simple_meaning: In battle, false cleverness and mercy toward an enemy are called cowardice. The messengers return at once, and Khara and Dushana burn with rage.
insight: It marks the shift from warning to confrontation, where delay only hardens the conflict.
modern_relevance: You replay a tense text thread and realize the other person has already taken your hesitation as weakness. The moment has moved past diplomacy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उर दहेउ कहेउ कि धरहु धाए बिकट भट रजनीचरा। सर चाप तोमर सक्ति सूल कृपान परिघ परसु धरा॥ प्रभु कीन्हि धनुष टकोर प्रथम कठोर घोर भयावहा। भए बधिर ब्याकुल जातुधान न ग्यान तेहि अवसर रहा॥
translation: (खर-दूषण का) हृदय जल उठा। तब उन्होंने कहा- पकड़ लो (कैद कर लो)। (यह सुनकर) भयानक राक्षस योद्धा बाण, धनुष, तोमर, शक्ति (साँग), शूल (बरछी), कृपाण (कटार), परिघ और फरसा धारण किए हुए दौड़ पड़े। प्रभु श्री रामजी ने पहले धनुष का बड़ा कठोर, घोर और भयानक टंकार किया, जिसे सुनकर राक्षस बहरे और व्याकुल हो गए। उस समय उन्हें कुछ भी होश न रहा।
english_translation: Their hearts burned. Then they shouted, "Seize him!" Fierce night-roaming warriors rushed forward with arrows, bows, tomars, spears, daggers, iron clubs, and axes in hand. Lord Ram struck his bow first with a hard, terrible, fearsome twang. The demons became deaf and bewildered, and at that moment they lost all sense.
essence: Presence can shake aggression before the first arrow flies.
simple_meaning: The enemy rushes in armed for attack, and Ram answers first with the sound of his bow. That single strike overwhelms them before the fight even fully begins.
insight: It shifts attention from brute force to presence: composure can disarm aggression before direct conflict escalates.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room where everyone expects you to flinch. Instead, you speak once, clearly and firmly, and the whole mood shifts before the argument starts.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सावधान होइ धाए जानि सबल आराति। लागे बरषन राम पर अस्त्र सस्त्र बहुभाँति ॥
translation: फिर वे शत्रु को बलवान् जानकर सावधान होकर दौड़े और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के ऊपर बहुत प्रकार के अस्त्र-शस्त्र बरसाने लगे ॥
english_translation: Then, knowing Ram was strong, they became alert and rushed forward, hurling many kinds of weapons at Ram.
essence: Recognising strength, the enemy attacks harder.
simple_meaning: The enemy warriors, seeing Ram's strength, rushed in alert and attacked him with many kinds of weapons.
insight: It shifts attention from meaning to motion: this is a combat beat, not a teaching verse.
modern_relevance: A room turns tense the moment one person stops bluffing and stands firm. The noise that follows is often just panic wearing armour.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तिन्ह के आयुध तिल सम करि काटे रघुबीर। तानि सरासन श्रवन लगि पुनि छाँड़े निज तीर ॥
translation: श्री रघुवीरजी ने उनके हथियारों को तिल के समान (टुकड़े-टुकड़े) करके काट डाला। फिर धनुष को कान तक तानकर अपने तीर छोड़े ॥
english_translation: Raghubir cut their weapons into tiny pieces. Then he drew his bow to his ear and released his own arrows.
essence: True strength meets aggression without losing control.
simple_meaning: Rama quickly destroys the enemy's weapons and then answers with his own arrows.
insight: It shifts attention from being attacked to responding with skill and precision.
modern_relevance: A heated argument lands in your lap, and you do not freeze. You cut through the confusion, answer clearly, and keep control of your response.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब चले बान कराल। फुंकरत जनु बहु ब्याल॥ कोपेउ समर श्रीराम। चले बिसिख निसित निकाम ॥
translation: तब भयानक बाण ऐसे चले, मानो फुफकारते हुए बहुत से सर्प जा रहे हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी संग्राम में क्रुद्ध हुए और अत्यन्त तीक्ष्ण बाण चले ॥
english_translation: Then terrible arrows flew, like many hissing serpents. Shri Ram grew fierce in battle and sent out razor-sharp arrows.
essence: The clash turns fiercer as Ram answers force with force.
simple_meaning: Terrible arrows flew like hissing snakes, and Ram answered the attack with fierce, razor-sharp arrows of his own.
insight: It shows battle pressure rising into direct counterattack, not reflection or teaching.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अवलोकि खरतर तीर। मुरि चले निसिचर बीर॥ भए क्रुद्ध तीनिउ भाइ। जो भागि रन ते जाइ ॥
translation: अत्यन्त तीक्ष्ण बाणों को देखकर राक्षस वीर पीठ दिखाकर भाग चले। तब खर-दूषण और त्रिशिरा तीनों भाई क्रुद्ध होकर बोले- जो रण से भागकर जाएगा, ॥
english_translation: Seeing the fierce arrows, the demon warriors turned back and fled. Then the three brothers grew angry and said, 'Whoever runs from the battlefield...'
essence: Pride lashes out when fear makes retreat unavoidable.
simple_meaning: The demon warriors see Ram's deadly arrows and run away. Their three leaders get angry and vow that no one should flee the battle.
insight: It shows how wounded ego reacts when it cannot control the field.
modern_relevance: A team meeting collapses after one hard question, and the loudest person in the room snaps at everyone for backing down. Panic often wears the mask of anger.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहि बधब हम निज पानि। फिरे मरन मन महुँ ठानि॥ आयुध अनेक प्रकार। सनमुख ते करहिं प्रहार ॥
translation: उसका हम अपने हाथों वध करेंगे। तब मन में मरना ठानकर भागते हुए राक्षस लौट पड़े और सामने होकर वे अनेकों प्रकार के हथियारों से श्री रामजी पर प्रहार करने लगे ॥
english_translation: We will kill him with our own hands. Then, resolved to die, the fleeing demons turned back and attacked him from the front with many kinds of weapons.
essence: Pride makes retreat look like courage.
simple_meaning: The demons, determined to die or kill, turn back and attack Ram head-on with every weapon they have.
insight: It shows how ego can turn retreat into reckless aggression.
modern_relevance: A person knows the argument is already lost, but pride keeps them typing longer, sharper messages. They come back swinging, even though the damage is already clear.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रिपु परम कोपे जानि। प्रभु धनुष सर संधानि॥ छाँड़े बिपुल नाराच। लगे कटन बिकट पिसाच ॥
translation: शत्रु को अत्यन्त कुपित जानकर प्रभु ने धनुष पर बाण चढ़ाकर बहुत से बाण छोड़े, जिनसे भयानक राक्षस कटने लगे ॥
english_translation: Seeing the enemy furious, the Lord drew his bow and released many arrows, and the terrible demons began to fall apart.
essence: Clear force meets fury without losing control.
simple_meaning: Ram sees the enemy's rage, nocks his bow, and sends out many arrows. The demons are cut down in battle.
insight: It shifts you from reactive anger to disciplined, targeted action.
modern_relevance: A tense meeting turns hostile, voices rise, and everyone expects you to match the heat. Instead, you stay clear, prepare your response, and answer with exactness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उर सीस भुज कर चरन। जहँ तहँ लगे महि परन॥ चिक्करत लागत बान। धर परत कुधर समान ॥
translation: उनकी छाती, सिर, भुजा, हाथ और पैर जहाँ-तहाँ पृथ्वी पर गिरने लगे। बाण लगते ही वे हाथी की तरह चिंग्घाड़ते हैं। उनके पहाड़ के समान धड़ कट-कटकर गिर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Their chests, heads, arms, hands, and feet fell here and there upon the earth. Hit by arrows, they roared like elephants, and their mountain-like trunks kept crashing down.
essence: The attack is so fierce that bodies fall apart on impact.
simple_meaning: Arrows tear the demons apart, and their limbs and bodies fall across the ground.
insight: It keeps the reader inside the momentum of the fight, not in commentary about it.
modern_relevance: A crisis can leave everything in pieces before you can even make sense of it. Sometimes the moment is just impact, not meaning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भट कटत तन सत खंड। पुनि उठत करि पाषंड॥ नभ उड़त बहु भुज मुंड। बिनु मौलि धावत रुंड ॥
translation: योद्धाओं के शरीर कटकर सैकड़ों टुकड़े हो जाते हैं। वे फिर माया करके उठ खड़े होते हैं। आकाश में बहुत सी भुजाएँ और सिर उड़ रहे हैं तथा बिना सिर के धड़ दौड़ रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Warriors are cut into hundreds of pieces, then rise again through illusion. Many arms and heads fly through the sky, and headless trunks run on.
essence: Violence here multiplies itself into nightmare, not triumph.
simple_meaning: Bodies are sliced apart, but the fighters keep rising in a terrifying display of magical power. The sky fills with severed limbs and heads, and headless bodies keep charging.
insight: It shifts the mind from heroic combat to the horror of destructive force that refuses to end.
modern_relevance: A conflict that should have ended keeps escalating, and every response seems to spawn a worse one. What began as a problem now feels like a nightmare that feeds on itself.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: खग कंक काक सृगाल। कटकटहिं कठिन कराल ॥
translation: चील (या क्रौंच), कौए आदि पक्षी और सियार कठोर और भयंकर कट-कट शब्द कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Crows, hawks, and jackals were making harsh, dreadful clicking sounds.
essence: Even the forest seems to shudder at the violence.
simple_meaning: Birds and jackals are making harsh, ominous noises as the battle rages around them.
insight: It sharpens the battlefield into a full sensory scene, showing how violence infects even the environment.
modern_relevance: You walk past a street after a crash, and even the silence feels disturbed. Some moments are so violent that the whole atmosphere seems to flinch.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कटकटहिं जंबुक भूत प्रेत पिसाच खर्पर संचहीं। बेताल बीर कपाल ताल बजाइ जोगिनि नंचहीं॥ रघुबीर बान प्रचंड खंडहिं भटन्ह के उर भुज सिरा। जहँ तहँ परहिं उठि लरहिं धर धरु धरु करहिं भयंकर गिरा ॥
translation: सियार कटकटाते हैं, भूत, प्रेत और पिशाच खोपड़ियाँ बटोर रहे हैं (अथवा खप्पर भर रहे हैं)। वीर-वैताल खोपड़ियों पर ताल दे रहे हैं और योगिनियाँ नाच रही हैं। श्री रघुवीर के प्रचंड बाण योद्धाओं के वक्षःस्थल, भुजा और सिरों के टुकड़े-टुकड़े कर डालते हैं। उनके धड़ जहाँ-तहाँ गिर पड़ते हैं, फिर उठते और लड़ते हैं और 'पकड़ो-पकड़ो' का भयंकर शब्द करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Jackals, ghosts, wandering spirits, and goblins gather skulls. Fierce spirits beat skulls like drums, and witch-like beings dance. Lord Raghubir's fierce arrows cut warriors' chests, arms, and heads apart. Their bodies fall, rise again, and fight, shouting in terrible voices.
essence: The battlefield has become a nightmare of endless, savage motion.
simple_meaning: The battlefield is so savage that it feels haunted. Arrows tear warriors apart, yet the fighting continues as bodies fall, rise, and clash again.
insight: It shows the war as chaos beyond ordinary description, with violence and horror overtaking the scene.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अंतावरीं गहि उड़त गीध पिसाच कर गहि धावहीं। संग्राम पुर बासी मनहुँ बहु बाल गुड़ी उड़ावहीं॥ मारे पछारे उर बिदारे बिपुल भट कहँरत परे। अवलोकि निज दल बिकल भट तिसिरादि खर दूषन फिरे ॥
translation: अंतड़ियों के एक छोर को पकड़कर गीध उड़ते हैं और उन्हीं का दूसरा छोर हाथ से पकड़कर पिशाच दौड़ते हैं, ऐसा मालूम होता है मानो संग्राम रूपी नगर के निवासी बहुत से बालक पतंग उड़ा रहे हों। अनेकों योद्धा मारे और पछाड़े गए बहुत से, जिनके हृदय विदीर्ण हो गए हैं, पड़े कराह रहे हैं। अपनी सेना को व्याकुल देखर त्रिशिरा और खर-दूषण आदि योद्धा श्री रामजी की ओर मुड़े ॥
english_translation: Ghouls and vultures clutch the intestines and fly, while other demons run with the other end in hand, as if the people of the battlefield city were flying kites. Many warriors are struck down, thrown down, and pierced through the chest, lying groaning. Seeing their own army in confusion, Trishira, Khara, and Dushana turn toward Ram.
essence: Panic in one army forces its leaders to face Ram.
simple_meaning: The battlefield has become a scene of chaos and slaughter. Seeing their army break apart, Trishira, Khara, and Dushana turn toward Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from battlefield spectacle to the collapse of ego under pressure.
modern_relevance: A group chat has turned into a pile-on, and the loudest voices suddenly go quiet when the facts land. Chaos can look powerful for a moment, but it always reveals who still stands.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सरसक्ति तोमर परसु सूल कृपान एकहि बारहीं। करि कोप श्री रघुबीर पर अगनित निसाचर डारहीं॥ प्रभु निमिष महुँ रिपु सर निवारि पचारि डारे सायका। दस दस बिसिख उर माझ मारे सकल निसिचर नायका ॥
translation: अनगिनत राक्षस क्रोध करके बाण, शक्ति, तोमर, फरसा, शूल और कृपाण एक ही बार में श्री रघुवीर पर छोड़ने लगे। प्रभु ने पल भर में शत्रुओं के बाणों को काटकर, ललकारकर उन पर अपने बाण छोड़े। सब राक्षस सेनापतियों के हृदय में दस-दस बाण मारे ॥
english_translation: Countless demons, in rage, hurled arrows, shaktis, toors, axes, spears, and swords at Shri Raghubir all at once. In a moment, the Lord cut down the enemy arrows, charged forward, and loosed his own arrows. He struck ten arrows into the hearts of all the demon commanders.
essence: Calm precision defeats furious chaos.
simple_meaning: The demons attack in a furious shower of weapons, and Ram instantly cuts through them and answers with his own arrows.
insight: It shows how composure and skill can cut through chaos faster than aggression can spread it.
modern_relevance: A meeting turns hostile and everyone starts talking over each other. You stay steady, hear the real issue, and answer only what matters.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: महि परत उठि भट भिरत मरत न करत माया अति घनी। सुर डरत चौदह सहस प्रेत बिलोकि एक अवध धनी॥ सुर मुनि सभय प्रभु देखि मायानाथ अति कौतुक कर् यो। देखहिं परसपर राम करि संग्राम रिपु दल लरि मर् यो ॥
translation: योद्धा पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ते हैं, फिर उठकर भिड़ते हैं। मरते नहीं, बहुत प्रकार की अतिशय माया रचते हैं। देवता यह देखकर डरते हैं कि प्रेत (राक्षस) चौदह हजार हैं और अयोध्यानाथ श्री रामजी अकेले हैं। देवता और मुनियों को भयभीत देखकर माया के स्वामी प्रभु ने एक बड़ा कौतुक किया, जिससे शत्रुओं की सेना एक-दूसरे को राम रूप देखने लगी और आपस में ही युद्ध करके लड़ मरी ॥
english_translation: Warriors fell to the ground, got up, and fought again. They did not die; they created many kinds of illusions. The gods grew afraid seeing fourteen thousand spirits against the lone Lord of Ayodhya. Seeing the gods and sages afraid, the Lord of illusion made a wondrous display: the enemy army began seeing Ram in one another and destroyed itself in battle.
essence: Illusion can make an army destroy itself.
simple_meaning: The battle turns into a strange illusion. Ram's enemies see one another as Ram and end up destroying themselves.
insight: It shows how delusion can make conflict collapse from within.
modern_relevance: A group chat turns into a pile-on, and everyone starts reacting to their own projections. What looked like one threat becomes self-destruction once confusion takes over.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम राम कहि तनु तजहिं पावहिं पद निर्बान। करि उपाय रिपु मारे छन महुँ कृपानिधान ॥
translation: सब ('यही राम है, इसे मारो' इस प्रकार) राम-राम कहकर शरीर छोड़ते हैं और निर्वाण (मोक्ष) पद पाते हैं। कृपानिधान श्री रामजी ने यह उपाय करके क्षण भर में शत्रुओं को मार डाला ॥
english_translation: Saying "Ram, Ram," they leave their bodies and attain the state of freedom. The compassionate Lord used this means and, in a moment, destroyed the enemies.
essence: Ram's name turns even death into release.
simple_meaning: Even enemies can be freed by remembering Ram. His compassion ends violence quickly and turns death into liberation.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing victory as destruction to seeing mercy as the highest victory.
modern_relevance: A room full of anger can shift in one honest moment. Sometimes the same force that stops the harm also softens the heart of everyone caught inside it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरषित बरषहिं सुमन सुर बाजहिं गगन निसान। अस्तुति करि करि सब चले सोभित बिबिध बिमान ॥
translation: देवता हर्षित होकर फूल बरसाते हैं, आकाश में नगाड़े बज रहे हैं। फिर वे सब स्तुति कर-करके अनेकों विमानों पर सुशोभित हुए चले गए ॥
english_translation: The radiant beings rejoice, shower flowers, and beat celestial drums in the sky. After praising again and again, they all depart in splendid flying chariots.
essence: Righteous victory makes even the heavens rejoice.
simple_meaning: The radiant beings celebrate Ram's victory with flowers, drums, and praise before returning to their celestial homes.
insight: It shifts attention from combat to celebration, showing that rightful victory restores harmony beyond the battlefield.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after the hard presentation ends, and then the people who believed in you start clapping first. Some victories deserve witness, not just results.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जब रघुनाथ समर रिपु जीते। सुर नर मुनि सब के भय बीते॥ तब लछिमन सीतहि लै आए। प्रभु पद परत हरषि उर लाए ॥
translation: जब श्री रघुनाथजी ने युद्ध में शत्रुओं को जीत लिया तथा देवता, मनुष्य और मुनि सबके भय नष्ट हो गए, तब लक्ष्मणजी सीताजी को ले आए। चरणों में पड़ते हुए उनको प्रभु ने प्रसन्नतापूर्वक उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
english_translation: When Raghunath defeated the enemy in battle and the fear of gods, humans, and sages had passed, Lakshman brought Sita back. As she fell at his feet, the Lord lifted her up joyfully and held her to his heart.
essence: Victory matters because it makes reunion possible.
simple_meaning: Ram defeats the enemies, fear leaves everyone, and Sita is brought back to him. He welcomes her with joy and embraces her at his heart.
insight: It shifts attention from conquest itself to the restoration that conquest makes possible.
modern_relevance: After a long fight to fix what went wrong, you finally see the person you were trying to protect walk back through the door. The relief is bigger than the victory.
speaker: Narrator
