verse_text: सीता चितव स्याम मृदु गाता। परम प्रेम लोचन न अघाता॥ पंचबटीं बसि श्री रघुनायक। करत चरित सुर मुनि सुखदायक ॥
translation: सीताजी श्री रामजी के श्याम और कोमल शरीर को परम प्रेम के साथ देख रही हैं, नेत्र अघाते नहीं हैं। इस प्रकार पंचवटी में बसकर श्री रघुनाथजी देवताओं और मुनियों को सुख देने वाले चरित्र करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Sita gazes at Ram's dark, gentle form, and her eyes are never satisfied. Dwelling in Panchavati, Shri Raghunath begins the acts that delight the radiant beings and sages.
essence: True love cannot look enough, and Ram's presence turns the forest holy.
simple_meaning: Sita cannot stop looking at Ram. After settling in Panchavati, Ram begins the deeds that bring joy to sages and radiant beings.
insight: It shifts attention from possession to reverent seeing.
modern_relevance: You catch someone you love across a crowded room and forget everything else for a second. That steady looking is what devotion feels like before words arrive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धुआँ देखि खरदूषन केरा। जाइ सुपनखाँ रावन प्रेरा॥ बोली बचन क्रोध करि भारी। देस कोस कै सुरति बिसारी ॥
translation: खर-दूषण का विध्वंस देखकर शूर्पणखा ने जाकर रावण को भड़काया। वह बड़ा क्रोध करके वचन बोली- तूने देश और खजाने की सुधि ही भुला दी ॥
english_translation: Seeing the destruction of Khara and Dushana, Shurpanakha went and provoked Ravana. Enraged, she said, "You have forgotten even your own land and treasury."
essence: Anger makes a ruler forget what protects him.
simple_meaning: Shurpanakha sees her brothers destroyed and rushes to inflame Ravana with angry words, accusing him of neglecting his kingdom and wealth.
insight: It shows how wounded pride can be weaponized, pushing someone already unstable toward worse choices.
modern_relevance: You get one furious voice note after a bad day, and suddenly a small problem becomes a family war. Heat spreads faster than wisdom.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करसि पान सोवसि दिनु राती। सुधि नहिं तव सिर पर आराती॥ राज नीति बिनु धन बिनु धर्मा। हरिहि समर्पे बिनु सतकर्मा ॥ बिद्या बिनु बिबेक उपजाएँ। श्रम फल पढ़ें किएँ अरु पाएँ॥ संग तें जती कुमंत्र ते राजा। मान ते ग्यान पान तें लाजा ॥
translation: शराब पी लेता है और दिन-रात पड़ा सोता रहता है। तुझे खबर नहीं है कि शत्रु तेरे सिर पर खड़ा है? नीति के बिना राज्य और धर्म के बिना धन प्राप्त करने से, भगवान को समर्पण किए बिना उत्तम कर्म करने से और विवेक उत्पन्न किए बिना विद्या पढ़ने से परिणाम में श्रम ही हाथ लगता है। विषयों के संग से संन्यासी, बुरी सलाह से राजा, मान से ज्ञान, मदिरा पान से लज्जा,॥4-5॥
english_translation: You drink and sleep day and night. Do you not know that an enemy stands over your head? Without policy, a kingdom; without dharma, wealth; without offering yourself to the divine, good deeds; and without wisdom, study all end in wasted effort. From bad company, a renunciant falls; from bad counsel, a king; from pride, wisdom; from drink, shame.
essence: Without wisdom and restraint, even success becomes waste.
simple_meaning: Blind habit, bad company, and pride ruin even noble efforts. Work, learning, wealth, and power only bear fruit when guided by wisdom and right conduct.
insight: It teaches you to check the quality of your mind, company, and motives before measuring results.
modern_relevance: You keep scrolling past midnight, telling yourself you will fix it tomorrow. But tiredness, bad inputs, and ego have already started shaping the day before it begins.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: प्रीति प्रनय बिनु मद ते गुनी। नासहिं बेगि नीति अस सुनी ॥
translation: नम्रता के बिना (नम्रता न होने से) प्रीति और मद (अहंकार) से गुणवान शीघ्र ही नष्ट हो जाते हैं, इस प्रकार नीति मैंने सुनी है ॥
english_translation: Without humility, even gifted people quickly perish through pride. This is the policy I have heard.
essence: Talent collapses when pride replaces humility.
simple_meaning: Pride destroys even capable people. Humility is what keeps skill, goodness, and good judgment from collapsing.
insight: It shifts attention from raw ability to the attitude that either preserves or destroys it.
modern_relevance: You get praised for one project, then start believing you’re untouchable. A few weeks later, the same overconfidence makes you careless, defensive, and easy to break.
speaker: Shurpanakha

verse_text: रिपु रुज पावक पाप प्रभु अहि गनिअ न छोट करि। अस कहि बिबिध बिलाप करि लागी रोदन करन ॥
translation: शत्रु, रोग, अग्नि, पाप, स्वामी और सर्प को छोटा करके नहीं समझना चाहिए। ऐसा कहकर शूर्पणखा अनेक प्रकार से विलाप करके रोने लगी ॥
english_translation: Never treat an enemy, disease, fire, sin, a ruler, or a serpent as small. Saying this, she wailed in many ways and began to cry.
essence: Small dangers become disasters when you refuse to respect them.
simple_meaning: Surpanakha warns that dangerous things should never be underestimated, then breaks into grief and tears.
insight: It teaches you to respect danger early, before pride or carelessness turns it into crisis.
modern_relevance: You ignore a small warning sign in a relationship, a body ache, or a risky deal, and suddenly the damage is everywhere. She is naming the cost of contempt.
speaker: Surpanakha

verse_text: सभा माझ परि ब्याकुल बहु प्रकार कह रोइ। तोहि जिअत दसकंधर मोरि कि असि गति होइ ॥
translation: (रावण की) सभा के बीच वह व्याकुल होकर पड़ी हुई बहुत प्रकार से रो-रोकर कह रही है कि अरे दशग्रीव! तेरे जीते जी मेरी क्या ऐसी दशा होनी चाहिए? ॥
english_translation: In the middle of the assembly, she lay there distraught, crying in many ways: 'While you live, O ten-headed one, how could such a fate be mine?'
essence: Humiliation speaks first when hurt has not yet settled.
simple_meaning: She collapses in Ravana's court and cries out in distress, blaming his living presence for her humiliation and suffering.
insight: It shows how humiliation turns into public complaint before clear thinking returns.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room already wounded, and your first words come out as blame. The hurt is real, but it is still speaking through you.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुनत सभासद उठे अकुलाई। समुझाई गहि बाँह उठाई॥ कह लंकेस कहसि निज बाता। केइँ तव नासा कान निपाता ॥
translation: शूर्पणखा के वचन सुनते ही सभासद् अकुला उठे। उन्होंने शूर्पणखा की बाँह पकड़कर उसे उठाया और समझाया। लंकापति रावण ने कहा- अपनी बात तो बता, किसने तेरे नाक-कान काट लिए? ॥
english_translation: When the courtiers heard this, they sprang up in agitation. They consoled her, took her by the arm, and lifted her up. Then the lord of Lanka said, “Tell your story. Who cut off your nose and ears?”
essence: Shock in the court opens the door to the accusation.
simple_meaning: The courtiers rush to help the injured woman, and Ravana asks who mutilated her. It is a scene of shock, not teaching.
insight: It keeps attention on the immediate scene and prepares the listener for the accusation to follow.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone blurts out a shocking complaint, and everyone turns to the person who can explain what happened next. The scene matters, but it is still only the opening of the response.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: अवध नृपति दसरथ के जाए। पुरुष सिंघ बन खेलन आए॥ समुझि परी मोहि उन्ह कै करनी। रहित निसाचर करिहहिं धरनी ॥
translation: (वह बोली-) अयोध्या के राजा दशरथ के पुत्र, जो पुरुषों में सिंह के समान हैं, वन में शिकार खेलने आए हैं। मुझे उनकी करनी ऐसी समझ पड़ी है कि वे पृथ्वी को राक्षसों से रहित कर देंगे ॥
english_translation: She said, "The sons of King Dasharath of Ayodhya have come. They are lions among men, come to play in the forest. I understand their deed: they will rid the earth of demons."
essence: What looks like play can be the beginning of a complete clearing.
simple_meaning: Shurpanakha recognizes that Ram and Lakshman are not ordinary forest visitors. She sees that their arrival will end the rule of demons on earth.
insight: It shifts attention from surface appearance to the deeper force behind a person's actions.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a gathering and think they are just being polite, but their calm presence changes the whole room. Some people arrive quietly and still shift the direction of everything around them.
speaker: Shurpanakha

verse_text: जिन्ह कर भुजबल पाइ दसानन। अभय भए बिचरत मुनि कानन॥ देखत बालक काल समाना। परम धीर धन्वी गुन नाना ॥
translation: जिनकी भुजाओं का बल पाकर हे दशमुख! मुनि लोग वन में निर्भय होकर विचरने लगे हैं। वे देखने में तो बालक हैं, पर हैं काल के समान। वे परम धीर, श्रेष्ठ धनुर्धर और अनेकों गुणों से युक्त हैं ॥
english_translation: By the strength of their arms, the sages have become fearless in the forest, O Ravana. They look like boys, yet they are like Time itself: deeply steady, master archers, and filled with many virtues.
essence: Real power can look young, calm, and unthreatening.
simple_meaning: Ravana admits that Ram and Lakshman have made the forest safe for sages. Though they look young, they are powerful, calm, skilled archers, and full of virtues.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance to actual capacity, showing that steadiness can be more formidable than display.
modern_relevance: You meet the quiet person in the room who says little, but everyone relaxes when they arrive. Their calm changes the atmosphere before they ever speak.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: अतुलित बल प्रताप द्वौ भ्राता। खल बध रत सुर मुनि सुखदाता॥ सोभा धाम राम अस नामा। तिन्ह के संग नारि एक स्यामा ॥
translation: दोनों भाइयों का बल और प्रताप अतुलनीय है। वे दुष्टों का वध करने में लगे हैं और देवता तथा मुनियों को सुख देने वाले हैं। वे शोभा के धाम हैं, 'राम' ऐसा उनका नाम है। उनके साथ एक तरुणी सुंदर स्त्री है ॥
english_translation: The two brothers have unmatched strength and glory. They are devoted to destroying the wicked and giving joy to the gods and sages. Ram is a name of beauty, and with them is a dark-hued woman.
essence: Power and beauty are being introduced, not yet explained.
simple_meaning: The two brothers are unmatched in strength and glory. They protect the good and punish the wicked, and a beautiful dark-hued woman is with them.
insight: It frames the characters before the encounter turns into action, so the verse functions as scene-setting rather than a complete teaching.
modern_relevance: You meet someone in a room and instantly sense their presence before they speak. The real meaning comes only when they begin to act.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रूप रासि बिधि नारि सँवारी। रति सत कोटि तासु बलिहारी॥ तासु अनुज काटे श्रुति नासा। सुनि तव भगिनि करहिं परिहासा ॥
translation: विधाता ने उस स्त्री को ऐसी रूप की राशि बनाया है कि सौ करोड़ रति (कामदेव की स्त्री) उस पर निछावर हैं। उन्हीं के छोटे भाई ने मेरे नाक-कान काट डाले। मैं तेरी बहिन हूँ, यह सुनकर वे मेरी हँसी करने लगे ॥
english_translation: The creator shaped that woman as a treasury of beauty; a hundred million Ratis would offer themselves to her. Her younger brother cut off my nose and ears. When I said, "I am your sister," they mocked me.
essence: Wounded pride turns beauty into resentment.
simple_meaning: Surpanakha describes Sita’s beauty, then complains that Lakshman mutilated her and laughed when she claimed to be Ravana’s sister.
insight: It shows how wounded vanity turns humiliation into a story of grievance and retaliation.
modern_relevance: You felt dismissed in one sharp moment, and now every word sounds like an insult. Hurt can make a small rejection grow teeth.
speaker: Surpanakha

verse_text: खर दूषन सुनि लगे पुकारा। छन महुँ सकल कटक उन्ह मारा॥ खर दूषन तिसिरा कर घाता। सुनि दससीस जरे सब गाता ॥
translation: मेरी पुकार सुनकर खर-दूषण सहायता करने आए। पर उन्होंने क्षण भर में सारी सेना को मार डाला। खर-दूषन और त्रिशिरा का वध सुनकर रावण के सारे अंग जल उठे ॥
english_translation: Hearing the call, Khara and Dushana rushed to help. In a moment, they were all slain. When Khara, Dushana, and Trishira were killed, Ravana's whole body burned with rage.
essence: Revenge arrives fast, but defeat can arrive faster.
simple_meaning: Khara and Dushana rush to help after hearing the call, but Ram's side destroys their army immediately. Ravana burns with anger when he hears they have been killed.
insight: It shows how quickly rash retaliation can be overwhelmed, and how anger spreads when ego is wounded.
modern_relevance: A friend texts, then three people pile into the argument thinking they can fix it. Before the group chat settles, the damage is already done.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सूपनखहि समुझाइ करि बल बोलेसि बहु भाँति। गयउ भवन अति सोचबस नीद परइ नहिं राति ॥
translation: उसने शूर्पणखा को समझाकर बहुत प्रकार से अपने बल का बखान किया, किन्तु (मन में) वह अत्यन्त चिंतावश होकर अपने महल में गया, उसे रात भर नींद नहीं पड़ी ॥
english_translation: After reassuring Surpanakha and boasting in many ways of his strength, he went back to his palace, overwhelmed with worry and unable to sleep all night.
essence: Boasted strength collapses into sleepless fear.
simple_meaning: Ravana tries to calm Surpanakha by boasting about his power, but inside he is shaken and cannot sleep.
insight: It exposes the split between outward bravado and inward insecurity.
modern_relevance: You leave a tense family argument sounding firm and certain, then lie awake replaying every word. The outside voice says control; the inside mind knows better.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सुर नर असुर नाग खग माहीं। मोरे अनुचर कहँ कोउ नाहीं॥ खर दूषन मोहि सम बलवंता। तिन्हहि को मारइ बिनु भगवंता ॥
translation: (वह मन ही मन विचार करने लगा-) देवता, मनुष्य, असुर, नाग और पक्षियों में कोई ऐसा नहीं, जो मेरे सेवक को भी पा सके। खर-दूषण तो मेरे ही समान बलवान थे। उन्हें भगवान के सिवा और कौन मार सकता है? ॥
english_translation: Among gods, humans, demons, serpents, and birds, none can match me. Khara and Dushana were as strong as I am; only the divine could kill them.
essence: Pride makes you imagine yourself beyond correction.
simple_meaning: Ravana is measuring his own power against the world and concluding that only the divine can defeat him. The verse reveals his pride and blindness.
insight: It exposes how the sense of separate self builds a false image of invulnerability.
modern_relevance: You reread the email that proved you wrong and still want to call it a fluke. Ravana's mistake is familiar: when ego feels threatened, it starts rewriting reality.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सुर रंजन भंजन महि भारा। जौं भगवंत लीन्ह अवतारा॥ तौ मैं जाइ बैरु हठि करऊँ। प्रभु सर प्रान तजें भव तरऊँ ॥
translation: देवताओं को आनंद देने वाले और पृथ्वी का भार हरण करने वाले भगवान ने ही यदि अवतार लिया है, तो मैं जाकर उनसे हठपूर्वक वैर करूँगा और प्रभु के बाण (के आघात) से प्राण छोड़कर भवसागर से तर जाऊँगा ॥
english_translation: If the divine has truly taken birth to delight the radiant beings and lift the earth's burden, then I will go and fight him stubbornly. By the Lord's arrow, I will give up my life and cross beyond the cycle of suffering.
essence: Pride can recognise truth and still choose ruin.
simple_meaning: Ravana recognizes that Ram has likely come for a divine purpose, yet his pride pushes him to oppose that truth anyway.
insight: It shows how clear seeing can still be defeated by stubborn self-importance.
modern_relevance: You know you’re wrong, but your jaw tightens anyway and you double down in the meeting. The facts are clear; the ego just wants the last word.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: होइहि भजनु न तामस देहा। मन क्रम बचन मंत्र दृढ़ एहा॥ जौं नररूप भूपसुत कोऊ। हरिहउँ नारि जीति रन दोऊ ॥
translation: इस तामस शरीर से भजन तो होगा नहीं, अतएव मन, वचन और कर्म से यही दृढ़ निश्चय है। और यदि वे मनुष्य रूप कोई राजकुमार होंगे तो उन दोनों को रण में जीतकर उनकी स्त्री को हर लूँगा ॥
english_translation: Devotion will not come from this tamasic body. My resolve is firm in mind, speech, and action: if they are human princes, I will defeat them both in battle and seize their woman.
essence: Ego turns uncertainty into a vow of violence.
simple_meaning: Ravana hardens himself for violence. He dismisses devotion and vows that if the opponents are human princes, he will defeat them and take their wife.
insight: It shows how wounded pride hardens into a destructive plan instead of self-correction.
modern_relevance: Someone hears a warning that they may be outmatched, and instead of pausing, they get more reckless, more defensive, and more determined to prove themselves right.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: चला अकेल जान चढ़ि तहवाँ। बस मारीच सिंधु तट जहवाँ॥ इहाँ राम जसि जुगुति बनाई। सुनहु उमा सो कथा सुहाई ॥
translation: राक्षसों की भयानक सेना आ गई है। जानकीजी को लेकर तुम पर्वत की कंदरा में चले जाओ। सावधान रहना। प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी के वचन सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी हाथ में धनुष-बाण लिए श्री सीताजी सहित चले ॥
english_translation: Laxman went alone up there, to the shore where Maricha lived by the sea. Here Ram made a fitting plan, O Uma, and the story is delightful to hear.
essence: The story moves forward through careful, unseen planning.
simple_meaning: Laxman goes alone to the place where Maricha lives, while Ram quietly makes the right plan. The verse is a bridge in the story, not a teaching by itself.
insight: It shows coordinated action in a larger strategy, with no standalone moral claim.
modern_relevance: You watch someone leave the room to handle the hard part while another person quietly puts the plan in place. The real work is already moving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लछिमन गए बनहिं जब लेन मूल फल कंद। जनकसुता सन बोले बिहसि कृपा सुख बृंद ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी जब कंद-मूल-फल लेने के लिए वन में गए, तब (अकेले में) कृपा और सुख के समूह श्री रामचंद्रजी हँसकर जानकीजी से बोले- ॥
english_translation: When Lakshman went into the forest to gather roots, fruits, and tubers, Janak's daughter, smiling, spoke to him with grace and delight.
essence: Love can speak softly right before hardship begins.
simple_meaning: Lakshman goes to fetch forest food, and Ram speaks lovingly to Sita. It is a quiet moment before the deeper plan is revealed.
insight: It shows how calm affection can prepare the heart for sacrifice.
modern_relevance: You are making tea while the house is tense, and someone you love gives you a small smile before the hard conversation begins.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनहु प्रिया ब्रत रुचिर सुसीला। मैं कछु करबि ललित नरलीला॥ तुम्ह पावक महुँ करहु निवासा। जौ लगि करौं निसाचर नासा ॥
translation: हे प्रिये! हे सुंदर पतिव्रत धर्म का पालन करने वाली सुशीले! सुनो! मैं अब कुछ मनोहर मनुष्य लीला करूँगा, इसलिए जब तक मैं राक्षसों का नाश करूँ, तब तक तुम अग्नि में निवास करो ॥
english_translation: Listen, dear one, pure and noble in vow. I will now enact a beautiful human play. Remain in the fire until I destroy the demons.
essence: What looks like loss can be part of a greater protection.
simple_meaning: Ram asks Sita to stay in the fire while he carries out his human play and destroys the demons.
insight: It shifts the mind from immediate comfort to protecting what is sacred through difficult means.
modern_relevance: You may have to endure a painful separation for a larger purpose, trusting that the hidden cost is not the final truth.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जबहिं राम सब कहा बखानी। प्रभु पद धरि हियँ अनल समानी॥ निज प्रतिबिंब राखि तहँ सीता। तैसइ सील रूप सुबिनीता ॥
translation: श्री रामजी ने ज्यों ही सब समझाकर कहा, त्यों ही श्री सीताजी प्रभु के चरणों को हृदय में धरकर अग्नि में समा गईं। सीताजी ने अपनी ही छाया मूर्ति वहाँ रख दी, जो उनके जैसे ही शील-स्वभाव और रूपवाली तथा वैसे ही विनम्र थी ॥
english_translation: As soon as Ram had explained everything, Sita entered the fire, holding the Lord's feet in her heart. There he placed her reflection, a form just like her—gentle in character, beautiful in form, and equally modest.
essence: Trust can carry you through fire while your true form remains untouched.
simple_meaning: Sita enters the fire only after Ram has explained the plan. A perfect double of her remains behind, so the world sees her as before.
insight: It shows how trust can carry someone through a terrifying transition without breaking their dignity.
modern_relevance: You agree to a painful plan because you trust the person who asked you to do it. Later, everyone sees only the version of you that stayed behind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लछिमनहूँ यह मरमु न जाना। जो कछु चरित रचा भगवाना॥ दसमुख गयउ जहाँ मारीचा। नाइ माथ स्वारथ रत नीचा ॥
translation: भगवान ने जो कुछ लीला रची, इस रहस्य को लक्ष्मणजी ने भी नहीं जाना। स्वार्थ परायण और नीच रावण वहाँ गया, जहाँ मारीच था और उसको सिर नवाया ॥
english_translation: Even Lakshman did not understand this secret: whatever the divine had arranged as the play. Ravana, driven by selfishness, went to where Maricha was and bowed his head before him.
essence: Selfish desire makes you bow to what will harm you.
simple_meaning: Even Lakshman could not see the hidden design behind events. Ravana, trapped in selfishness, went to Maricha and bowed to him.
insight: It shows how desire narrows vision and makes dangerous choices feel respectful or wise.
modern_relevance: You keep chasing the person who flatters your worst impulse, thinking it will help. Later, you see you were already bowing to the very thing that would trap you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नवनि नीच कै अति दुखदाई। जिमि अंकुस धनु उरग बिलाई॥ भयदायक खल कै प्रिय बानी। जिमि अकाल के कुसुम भवानी ॥
translation: नीच का झुकना (नम्रता) भी अत्यन्त दुःखदायी होता है। जैसे अंकुश, धनुष, साँप और बिल्ली का झुकना। हे भवानी! दुष्ट की मीठी वाणी भी (उसी प्रकार) भय देने वाली होती है, जैसे बिना ऋतु के फूल! ॥
english_translation: A low person's bowing is deeply painful, like a goad, a bow, a snake, or a cat bending low. O Bhavani, a wicked person's sweet speech is equally fearsome, like flowers blooming out of season.
essence: Softness can be a mask for danger.
simple_meaning: A wicked person may look humble and speak sweetly, but that can hide danger. Outward softness does not always mean good intent.
insight: It trains you to test appearance against character before trusting what sounds gentle.
modern_relevance: Someone apologizes with the perfect tone after hurting you, but their pattern never changes. The smile is polished; the intention is not.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि पूजा मारीच तब सादर पूछी बात। कवन हेतु मन ब्यग्र अति अकसर आयहु तात ॥
translation: तब मारीच ने उसकी पूजा करके आदरपूर्वक बात पूछी- हे तात! आपका मन किस कारण इतना अधिक व्यग्र है और आप अकेले आए हैं? ॥
english_translation: Then Maricha honored him with worship and respectfully asked, "Dear uncle, what makes your mind so troubled, and why have you come alone?"
essence: Polite words can open the door to harm.
simple_meaning: Maricha greets Ravana with respect and asks why he has come alone in such a troubled state.
insight: It frames the scene as a prelude to manipulation, not a teaching in itself.
modern_relevance: A friend calls you late at night, unusually formal, and asks if you can talk privately. The politeness itself tells you something is already off.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दसमुख सकल कथा तेहि आगें। कही सहित अभिमान अभागें॥ होहु कपट मृग तुम्ह छलकारी। जेहि बिधि हरि आनौं नृपनारी ॥
translation: भाग्यहीन रावण ने सारी कथा अभिमान सहित उसके सामने कही (और फिर कहा-) तुम छल करने वाले कपटमृग बनो, जिस उपाय से मैं उस राजवधू को हर लाऊँ ॥
english_translation: Ravana told the whole story before him, with pride despite his ill fortune, and said, 'Become a deceitful deer, you trickster, by whatever means I may bring away the queen.'
essence: Pride can dress itself as strategy and still be the beginning of collapse.
simple_meaning: Ravana tells Maricha his plan and orders him to take the form of a deceptive deer so he can lure away Sita.
insight: It shows how ego speaks openly while hiding its own destruction.
modern_relevance: A powerful person calls you with a flattering tone and a dangerous request. You can hear the charm, but the real story is the harm underneath it.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: तेहिं पुनि कहा सुनहु दससीसा। ते नररूप चराचर ईसा॥ तासों तात बयरु नहिं कीजै। मारें मरिअ जिआएँ जीजै ॥
translation: तब उसने (मारीच ने) कहा- हे दशशीश! सुनिए। वे मनुष्य रूप में चराचर के ईश्वर हैं। हे तात! उनसे वैर न कीजिए। उन्हीं के मारने से मरना और उनके जिलाने से जीना होता है (सबका जीवन-मरण उन्हीं के अधीन है) ॥
english_translation: Then he said again, "Listen, Ravana. Those are the Lord in human form, the ruler of all moving and unmoving beings. So do not make enmity with him, my friend. Death and life are in his hands: he kills, and he gives life."
essence: Enmity collapses when you see the divine power already standing before you.
simple_meaning: Maricha warns Ravana not to make Ram his enemy. He says Ram is the Lord in human form, and life and death rest with him.
insight: It shifts the mind from reckless opposition to clear recognition of power and consequence.
modern_relevance: You are about to send that angry text, convinced you can win the argument. Then a quieter part of you remembers: this person may be carrying far more power than your ego wants to admit.
speaker: Maricha

verse_text: मुनि मख राखन गयउ कुमारा। बिनु फर सर रघुपति मोहि मारा॥ सत जोजन आयउँ छन माहीं। तिन्ह सन बयरु किएँ भल नाहीं ॥
translation: यही राजकुमार मुनि विश्वामित्र के यज्ञ की रक्षा के लिए गए थे। उस समय श्री रघुनाथजी ने बिना फल का बाण मुझे मारा था, जिससे मैं क्षणभर में सौ योजन पर आ गिरा। उनसे वैर करने में भलाई नहीं है ॥
english_translation: The prince went to protect the sage's sacrifice. Raghupati struck me with a fruitless arrow, and in a moment I fell a hundred leagues away. It is not wise to bear enmity toward them.
essence: Remembering your defeat can save you from repeating it.
simple_meaning: Maricha warns Ravana that Ram once sent him flying with a single arrow, so fighting Ram and Lakshman will only bring harm.
insight: It shifts you from stubborn revenge to sober self-recognition before you escalate harm.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the angry message, even though the last one already blew up in your face. Memory is trying to protect you from repeating a wound.
speaker: Maricha

verse_text: भइ मम कीट भृंग की नाई। जहँ तहँ मैं देखउँ दोउ भाई॥ जौं नर तात तदपि अति सूरा। तिन्हहि बिरोधि न आइहि पूरा ॥
translation: मेरी दशा तो भृंगी के कीड़े की सी हो गई है। अब मैं जहाँ-तहाँ श्री राम-लक्ष्मण दोनों भाइयों को ही देखता हूँ। और हे तात! यदि वे मनुष्य हैं, तो भी बड़े शूरवीर हैं। उनसे विरोध करने में पूरा न पड़ेगा (सफलता नहीं मिलेगी) ॥
english_translation: My condition has become like a worm in a wasp's nest. Everywhere I look, I see only the two brothers, Ram and Lakshman. And, father, if they are only men, they are still very mighty; no one can defeat them.
essence: Fear makes one danger seem to occupy your entire world.
simple_meaning: Ravana says fear has made Ram and Lakshman seem to fill his whole world. He admits they are formidable enough that fighting them may fail.
insight: It shows how fear distorts perception and makes resistance look impossible before the struggle even begins.
modern_relevance: You replay one harsh conversation all night and start seeing that person in every room, every message, every silence. Anxiety makes a single fear feel larger than reality.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: जेहिं ताड़का सुबाहु हति खंडेउ हर कोदंड। खर दूषन तिसिरा बधेउ मनुज कि अस बरिबंड ॥
translation: जिसने ताड़का और सुबाहु को मारकर शिवजी का धनुष तोड़ दिया और खर, दूषण और त्रिशिरा का वध कर डाला, ऐसा प्रचंड बली भी कहीं मनुष्य हो सकता है? ॥
english_translation: Can a mere human be so mighty—one who killed Tadka and Subahu, broke Shiva's bow, and slew Khara, Dushana, and Trisira?
essence: Ram's power is so great that even his enemy cannot call him ordinary.
simple_meaning: Ravana is stunned by Ram's power and lists Ram's victories to question whether such a mighty being can be only human.
insight: It frames Ram's greatness through an enemy's reluctant admiration, raising the stakes before Ravana's anger erupts.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm competence leaves no room for doubt. Their presence makes your excuses feel small, even before they say a word.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: जाहु भवन कुल कुसल बिचारी। सुनत जरा दीन्हिसि बहु गारी॥ गुरु जिमि मूढ़ करसि मम बोधा। कहु जग मोहि समान को जोधा ॥
translation: अतः अपने कुल की कुशल विचारकर आप घर लौट जाइए। यह सुनकर रावण जल उठा और उसने बहुत सी गालियाँ दीं (दुर्वचन कहे)। (कहा-) अरे मूर्ख! तू गुरु की तरह मुझे ज्ञान सिखाता है? बता तो संसार में मेरे समान योद्धा कौन है? ॥
english_translation: Therefore, considering the welfare of your own family, return home. Hearing this, Ravana burned with anger and hurled many abuses. 'Fool! You try to teach me like a guru? Tell me, who in the world is a warrior equal to me?'
essence: Pride cannot hear wisdom without turning defensive.
simple_meaning: Ravana rejects advice, insults the messenger, and boasts that no warrior equals him.
insight: It shows how ego blocks correction and turns guidance into a threat.
modern_relevance: Someone points out a blind spot in your plan, and your first reaction is to defend yourself instead of listening. That instant flare of ego can ruin what careful seeing might have saved.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: तब मारीच हृदयँ अनुमाना। नवहि बिरोधें नहिं कल्याना॥ सस्त्री मर्मी प्रभु सठ धनी। बैद बंदि कबि भानस गुनी ॥
translation: तब मारीच ने हृदय में अनुमान किया कि शस्त्री (शस्त्रधारी), मर्मी (भेद जानने वाला), समर्थ स्वामी, मूर्ख, धनवान, वैद्य, भाट, कवि और रसोइया- इन नौ व्यक्तियों से विरोध (वैर) करने में कल्याण (कुशल) नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: Then Maricha reasoned in his heart that there is no good in opposing these nine: an armed man, one who knows your secrets, a powerful lord, a fool, a wealthy man, a physician, a bard, a poet, and a cook.
essence: Clear seeing can spare you from a fight that cannot be won.
simple_meaning: Maricha sees that opposing certain kinds of people is dangerous and pointless. He understands that some confrontations only lead to harm.
insight: It teaches you to assess power, weakness, and risk before reacting.
modern_relevance: You’re about to send the angry text, jump into the group argument, or challenge the person who already has leverage over you. A pause now can save you from a costly mistake.
speaker: Maricha

verse_text: उभय भाँति देखा निज मरना। तब ताकिसि रघुनायक सरना॥ उतरु देत मोहि बधब अभागें। कस न मरौं रघुपति सर लागें ॥
translation: जब मारीच ने दोनों प्रकार से अपना मरण देखा, तब उसने श्री रघुनाथजी की शरण तकी (अर्थात उनकी शरण जाने में ही कल्याण समझा)। (सोचा कि) उत्तर देते ही (नाहीं करते ही) यह अभागा मुझे मार डालेगा। फिर श्री रघुनाथजी के बाण लगने से ही क्यों न मरूँ ॥
english_translation: Seeing death either way, Maricha took refuge in Raghunath. "If I answer, this wicked one will kill me. Why not die by Raghupati's arrow?"
essence: When escape is impossible, surrender becomes the wisest act.
simple_meaning: Maricha sees that either answer or silence will lead to death, so he chooses Ram's refuge instead of resisting.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to surrender when control is no longer possible.
modern_relevance: You are cornered in a conversation where every reply makes things worse. The moment you stop trying to control the damage and choose the truest response, relief begins.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस जियँ जानि दसानन संगा। चला राम पद प्रेम अभंगा॥ मन अति हरष जनाव न तेही। आजु देखिहउँ परम सनेही ॥
translation: हृदय में ऐसा समझकर वह रावण के साथ चला। श्री रामजी के चरणों में उसका अखंड प्रेम है। उसके मन में इस बात का अत्यन्त हर्ष है कि आज मैं अपने परम स्नेही श्री रामजी को देखूँगा, किन्तु उसने यह हर्ष रावण को नहीं जनाया ॥
english_translation: Thinking this in his heart, he went with Ravana. His love for Ram's feet was unbroken. Joy surged in his mind at the thought, 'Today I will see my dearest Ram,' but he did not show that joy to Ravana.
essence: Devotion can survive even while you walk through danger.
simple_meaning: He walks with Ravana, but his heart belongs to Ram. He hides his joy because he is about to see the one he loves most.
insight: It teaches you to keep your deepest allegiance inwardly intact, even when outward circumstances force you to play along.
modern_relevance: You sit through a tense dinner with people who would mock what you love. Your face stays calm, but inside you hold on to what matters most.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निज परम प्रीतम देखि लोचन सुफल करि सुख पाइहौं। श्रीसहित अनुज समेत कृपानिकेत पद मन लाइहौं॥ निर्बान दायक क्रोध जा कर भगति अबसहि बसकरी। निज पानि सर संधानि सो मोहि बधिहि सुखसागर हरी॥
translation: (वह मन ही मन सोचने लगा-) अपने परम प्रियतम को देखकर नेत्रों को सफल करके सुख पाऊँगा। जानकीजी सहित और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी समेत कृपानिधान श्री रामजी के चरणों में मन लगाऊँगा। जिनका क्रोध भी मोक्ष देने वाला है और जिनकी भक्ति उन अवश (किसी के वश में न होने वाले, स्वतंत्र भगवान) को भी वश में करने वाली है, अब वे ही आनंद के समुद्र श्री हरि अपने हाथों से बाण सन्धानकर मेरा वध करेंगे।
english_translation: Seeing my most beloved, I will make my eyes fruitful and find joy. With Sita and Lakshman beside him, I will place my mind at the feet of the compassionate Lord. His anger grants freedom, and his devotion can bring even the unconstrained under control. Now the blissful Lord Hari himself will draw the arrow and strike me down with his own hand.
essence: Ram’s nearness is so complete that even death becomes joy.
simple_meaning: Maricha thinks that seeing Ram will fulfill his eyes and bring joy. He also sees Ram as so loving and powerful that even being killed by him feels blessed.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to reverent longing, where even punishment becomes a form of blessing.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who once hurt you, and instead of replaying the wound, you feel strangely grateful just to be in their presence. This verse holds that impossible tenderness: even judgment from the beloved can feel like mercy.
speaker: Maricha

verse_text: मम पाछें धर धावत धरें सरासन बान। फिरि फिरि प्रभुहि बिलोकिहउँ धन्य न मो सम आन ॥
translation: धनुष-बाण धारण किए मेरे पीछे-पीछे पृथ्वी पर (पकड़ने के लिए) दौड़ते हुए प्रभु को मैं फिर-फिरकर देखूँगा। मेरे समान धन्य दूसरा कोई नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Holding bow and arrows, the Lord will run behind me on the ground. Again and again I will behold the Lord; no one is as blessed as I am.
essence: Even being chased can feel blessed when the beloved is in sight.
simple_meaning: Ravana imagines Ram chasing him with bow and arrows, yet he feels fortunate because he will keep seeing Ram again and again.
insight: It shifts the mind from fearing encounter to valuing the chance to see what you love.
modern_relevance: You are bracing for a hard conversation, but the other person matters so much that even the tension feels strangely precious.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: तेहि बननिकट दसानन गयऊ। तब मारीच कपटमृग भयऊ॥ अति बिचित्र कछु बरनि न जाई। कनक देह मनि रचित बनाई ॥
translation: जब रावण उस वन के (जिस वन में श्री रघुनाथजी रहते थे) निकट पहुँचा, तब मारीच कपटमृग बन गया! वह अत्यन्त ही विचित्र था, कुछ वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। सोने का शरीर मणियों से जड़कर बनाया था ॥
english_translation: When Ravana reached the edge of that forest, Maricha became the deceitful deer. It was so strange that it cannot be described: its body was golden and set with jewels.
essence: A dazzling disguise can hide a dangerous intention.
simple_meaning: Ravana reached the forest edge, and Maricha took the form of a dazzling golden deer that was hard to describe.
insight: It trains you to notice how beauty can be used as bait.
modern_relevance: A message arrives with perfect grammar, a polished logo, and exactly the promise you wanted. The shine is the point — and that is why you should look twice.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीता परम रुचिर मृग देखा। अंग अंग सुमनोहर बेषा॥ सुनहु देव रघुबीर कृपाला। एहि मृग कर अति सुंदर छाला ॥
translation: सीताजी ने उस परम सुंदर हिरन को देखा, जिसके अंग-अंग की छटा अत्यन्त मनोहर थी। (वे कहने लगीं-) हे देव! हे कृपालु रघुवीर! सुनिए। इस मृग की छाल बहुत ही सुंदर है ॥
english_translation: Sita saw that exceedingly beautiful deer, with every limb charming to the eye. She said, “Listen, O divine, compassionate Raghuvir. This deer’s hide is very beautiful.”
essence: What looks harmless can be the very thing that separates you from what matters most.
simple_meaning: Sita is captivated by the beautiful deer and asks Ram to bring back its lovely hide.
insight: It shows how attraction can override caution and pull attention toward a hidden snare.
modern_relevance: You click on something dazzling because it feels harmless and lovely. Only later do you realize the shine was the bait.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सत्यसंध प्रभु बधि करि एही। आनहु चर्म कहति बैदेही॥ तब रघुपति जानत सब कारन। उठे हरषि सुर काजु सँवारन ॥
translation: जानकीजी ने कहा- हे सत्यप्रतिज्ञ प्रभो! इसको मारकर इसका चमड़ा ला दीजिए। तब श्री रघुनाथजी (मारीच के कपटमृग बनने का) सब कारण जानते हुए भी, देवताओं का कार्य बनाने के लिए हर्षित होकर उठे ॥
english_translation: Sita said, “O truthful Lord, kill this one and bring me its skin.” Then Raghupati, knowing all the reason, rose gladly to complete the gods’ task.
essence: Knowing the trick, he still moves to fulfill the larger plan.
simple_meaning: Sita asks Ram to kill the deer and bring back its skin. Ram already knows the trick, yet he rises gladly to help the divine plan unfold.
insight: It shows that clear seeing does not always lead to refusal; sometimes it leads to purposeful action.
modern_relevance: You can spot the manipulation in the room and still choose the harder, wiser response because protecting what matters is more important than proving you were right.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मृग बिलोकि कटि परिकर बाँधा। करतल चाप रुचिर सर साँधा॥ प्रभु लछिमनहि कहा समुझाई। फिरत बिपिन निसिचर बहु भाई ॥
translation: हिरन को देखकर श्री रामजी ने कमर में फेंटा बाँधा और हाथ में धनुष लेकर उस पर सुंदर (दिव्य) बाण चढ़ाया। फिर प्रभु ने लक्ष्मणजी को समझाकर कहा- हे भाई! वन में बहुत से राक्षस फिरते हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing the deer, Ram tied his waist cloth and fitted a beautiful arrow to his bow. Then the Lord explained to Lakshman, 'Brother, many demons roam this forest.'
essence: Beauty can hide danger, so steady readiness matters.
simple_meaning: Ram gets ready to shoot the deer and warns Lakshman that many dangerous beings roam the forest.
insight: It teaches you to read beneath appearances and respond before danger fully reveals itself.
modern_relevance: You spot the charming offer, but something feels off. Before you commit, you prepare, check the risk, and tell the person beside you to stay alert.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीता केरि करेहु रखवारी। बुधि बिबेक बल समय बिचारी॥ प्रभुहि बिलोकि चला मृग भाजी। धाए रामु सरासन साजी ॥
translation: तुम बुद्धि और विवेक के द्वारा बल और समय का विचार करके सीताजी की रखवाली करना। प्रभु को देखकर मृग भाग चला। श्री रामचन्द्रजी भी धनुष चढ़ाकर उसके पीछे दौड़े ॥
english_translation: Guard Sita with wisdom, discernment, strength, and attention to the moment. Seeing the Lord, the deer ran; Ram also ran after it, bow ready.
essence: Protection works only when wisdom, timing, and strength move together.
simple_meaning: Keep watch over Sita using wisdom, discernment, strength, and good timing. The deer sees Ram and runs; Ram immediately gives chase.
insight: It teaches you to protect what matters by reading the moment clearly, not by reacting late.
modern_relevance: You leave someone you love alone for just a minute, trusting the situation is harmless. Later you realise the danger was never loud — it was clever. This verse asks for alert care, not sleepy confidence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निगम नेति सिव ध्यान न पावा। मायामृग पाछें सो धावा॥ कबहुँ निकट पुनि दूरि पराई। कबहुँक प्रगटइ कबहुँ छपाई ॥
translation: वेद जिनके विषय में 'नेति-नेति' कहकर रह जाते हैं और शिवजी भी जिन्हें ध्यान में नहीं पाते (अर्थात जो मन और वाणी से नितान्त परे हैं), वे ही श्री रामजी माया से बने हुए मृग के पीछे दौड़ रहे हैं। वह कभी निकट आ जाता है और फिर दूर भाग जाता है। कभी तो प्रकट हो जाता है और कभी छिप जाता है ॥
english_translation: The Vedas stop at "not this, not this," and Shiva cannot reach it in meditation. Yet Ram chases the deer made of illusion. Sometimes it comes near, sometimes it goes far away; sometimes it appears, sometimes it hides.
essence: The infinite can still be drawn into a game of appearances.
simple_meaning: Ram is beyond all description, yet he is now chasing the illusion-deer that keeps appearing and disappearing.
insight: It shifts attention from the object’s trickery to the mind’s attachment to what flickers.
modern_relevance: You know that moment when you keep checking your phone because something keeps almost-appearing, then vanishing again. The mind stays hooked by what it cannot quite hold.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रगटत दुरत करत छल भूरी। एहि बिधि प्रभुहि गयउ लै दूरी॥ तब तकि राम कठिन सर मारा। धरनि परेउ करि घोर पुकारा ॥
translation: इस प्रकार प्रकट होता और छिपता हुआ तथा बहुतेरे छल करता हुआ वह प्रभु को दूर ले गया। तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने तक कर (निशाना साधकर) कठोर बाण मारा, (जिसके लगते ही) वह घोर शब्द करके पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा ॥
english_translation: Moving in and out of sight, he used many tricks to lead the Lord farther away. Then Ram aimed carefully and shot a fierce arrow; struck by it, he fell to the earth with a terrible cry.
essence: What keeps deceiving you can still be brought down.
simple_meaning: The deer kept luring Ram farther away by appearing, disappearing, and tricking him. Ram then shot it with a powerful arrow, and it fell down crying out loudly.
insight: It shifts attention from the lure of appearances to the need for decisive action.
modern_relevance: A message keeps pinging, a tab keeps reopening, and you keep getting pulled away from what matters. Eventually, the distraction has to be named and cut off.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लछिमन कर प्रथमहिं लै नामा। पाछें सुमिरेसि मन महुँ रामा॥ प्रान तजत प्रगटेसि निज देहा। सुमिरेसि रामु समेत सनेहा ॥
translation: पहले लक्ष्मणजी का नाम लेकर उसने पीछे मन में श्री रामजी का स्मरण किया। प्राण त्याग करते समय उसने अपना (राक्षसी) शरीर प्रकट किया और प्रेम सहित श्री रामजी का स्मरण किया ॥
english_translation: She first took Lakshman's name, then remembered Ram in her mind. As she gave up her life, she revealed her own body and remembered Ram with love.
essence: What the heart remembers at the end reveals what it truly served.
simple_meaning: At the moment of death, she first called on Lakshman and then remembered Ram with love. Even in that final instant, devotion remained alive.
insight: It shifts attention from outward appearance to the final inward attachment that shapes the heart.
modern_relevance: A person can spend years chasing approval, then suddenly face a hospital room, a breakup, or a grave mistake. In that last raw moment, what the mind returns to shows what truly held it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अंतर प्रेम तासु पहिचाना। मुनि दुर्लभ गति दीन्हि सुजाना ॥
translation: सुजान (सर्वज्ञ) श्री रामजी ने उसके हृदय के प्रेम को पहचानकर उसे वह गति (अपना परमपद) दी जो मुनियों को भी दुर्लभ है ॥
english_translation: The all-knowing Lord recognized his hidden love and gave him the rare state that even sages find hard to attain.
essence: Hidden devotion can receive the highest grace.
simple_meaning: Ram recognized the warrior's hidden devotion and granted him a rare spiritual state beyond ordinary reach.
insight: It shifts attention from outer identity to the sincerity beneath it.
modern_relevance: You do the right thing without anyone noticing, and it still changes you. A quiet act of loyalty, a private prayer, a hidden kindness — none of it is wasted.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिपुल सुमर सुर बरषहिं गावहिं प्रभु गुन गाथ। निज पद दीन्ह असुर कहुँ दीनबंधु रघुनाथ ॥
translation: देवता बहुत से फूल बरसा रहे हैं और प्रभु के गुणों की गाथाएँ (स्तुतियाँ) गा रहे हैं (कि) श्री रघुनाथजी ऐसे दीनबन्धु हैं कि उन्होंने असुर को भी अपना परम पद दे दिया ॥
english_translation: Many radiant beings shower flowers and sing the Lord's praise: Raghunath gave even an asura his highest state, because he is the friend of the humble.
essence: Ram's mercy can raise even an enemy into blessing.
simple_meaning: Heavenly beings celebrate Ram because he gave even an asura a supreme state. Ram is the friend of the humble and the fallen.
insight: It shifts you from judging by outer identity to recognising inner turning and the possibility of transformation.
modern_relevance: You write someone off after their worst mistake, but they surprise everyone with one honest act of remorse. This verse says mercy can see deeper than reputation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: खल बधि तुरत फिरे रघुबीरा। सोह चाप कर कटि तूनीरा॥ आरत गिरा सुनी जब सीता। कह लछिमन सन परम सभीता ॥
translation: दुष्ट मारीच को मारकर श्री रघुवीर तुरंत लौट पड़े। हाथ में धनुष और कमर में तरकस शोभा दे रहा है। इधर जब सीताजी ने दुःखभरी वाणी (मरते समय मारीच की 'हा लक्ष्मण' की आवाज) सुनी तो वे बहुत ही भयभीत होकर लक्ष्मणजी से कहने लगीं ॥
english_translation: Having slain the wicked one, Raghuvira returned at once, with bow in hand and quiver at his waist. Then, hearing the sorrowful cry, Sita became deeply frightened and said to Lakshmana:
essence: A single cry can turn calm into fear.
simple_meaning: Ram returns after killing the demon, and Sita is startled by the cry she hears. She turns to Lakshmana in fear.
insight: It shows how quickly the mind reacts to alarming sound, even without understanding the full situation.
modern_relevance: You hear a panicked voice from another room and your body tightens before you know why. Fear often arrives before facts do.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जाहु बेगि संकट अति भ्राता। लछिमन बिहसि कहा सुनु माता॥ भृकुटि बिलास सृष्टि लय होई। सपनेहुँ संकट परइ कि सोई ॥
translation: तुम शीघ्र जाओ, तुम्हारे भाई बड़े संकट में हैं। लक्ष्मणजी ने हँसकर कहा- हे माता! सुनो, जिनके भ्रृकुटि विलास (भौं के इशारे) मात्र से सारी सृष्टि का लय (प्रलय) हो जाता है, वे श्री रामजी क्या कभी स्वप्न में भी संकट में पड़ सकते हैं? ॥
english_translation: Go quickly, brother, for your brother is in great danger. Lakshman smiled and said, "Listen, Mother: can those on whose brows the mere play of an eyebrow brings about the dissolution of creation ever be in danger, even in a dream?"
essence: Ram's smallest gesture is greater than the danger itself.
simple_meaning: Lakshman reassures Sita that Ram cannot truly be threatened, because even the slightest movement of Ram's brow can dissolve creation itself.
insight: It shifts the mind from immediate panic to trust in a reality larger than the threat.
modern_relevance: Your phone buzzes with bad news, and panic starts to rise before you even know the facts. This verse reminds you to breathe and remember what is actually bigger than the moment.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: मरम बचन जब सीता बोला। हरि प्रेरित लछिमन मन डोला॥ बन दिसि देव सौंपि सब काहू। चले जहाँ रावन ससि राहू ॥
translation: इस पर जब सीताजी कुछ मर्म वचन (हृदय में चुभने वाले वचन) कहने लगीं, तब भगवान की प्रेरणा से लक्ष्मणजी का मन भी चंचल हो उठा। वे श्री सीताजी को वन और दिशाओं के देवताओं को सौंपकर वहाँ चले, जहाँ रावण रूपी चन्द्रमा के लिए राहु रूप श्री रामजी थे ॥
english_translation: When Sita spoke words that struck the heart, Lakshman's mind wavered under the divine's prompting. Entrusting Sita to the forest spirits and all directions, he went where Ravana was like Rahu to the moon.
essence: A shaken mind can still obey what must be done.
simple_meaning: Sita’s painful words unsettle Lakshman, and he leaves at once, placing her under divine and forest protection before going to face Ravana.
insight: It shows loyalty under pressure: feeling shaken does not cancel immediate action.
modern_relevance: Your sibling says one sharp sentence, and your whole body tightens. You still lock the door, hand over the keys, and go do what cannot wait.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सून बीच दसकंधर देखा। आवा निकट जती कें बेषा॥ जाकें डर सुर असुर डेराहीं। निसि न नीद दिन अन्न न खाहीं ॥
translation: रावण सूना मौका देखकर यति (संन्यासी) के वेष में श्री सीताजी के समीप आया, जिसके डर से देवता और दैत्य तक इतना डरते हैं कि रात को नींद नहीं आती और दिन में (भरपेट) अन्न नहीं खाते- ॥
english_translation: Ravana saw the chance when no one was around and came near Sita disguised as a renunciant. Even the radiant beings and shadow beings fear him so much that they lose sleep at night and cannot eat fully by day.
essence: Power without restraint becomes deception.
simple_meaning: Ravana takes advantage of the empty moment and approaches Sita in the disguise of a renunciant. His terrifying power is so great that even the radiant and shadow beings are restless before him.
insight: It shows how danger often enters through disguise, not force.
modern_relevance: A person who seems harmless at the door may be carrying bad intent underneath. This verse feels like the instant your guard drops and you realise the threat was already inside the room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सो दससीस स्वान की नाईं। इत उत चितइ चला भड़िहाईं॥ इमि कुपंथ पग देत खगेसा। रह न तेज तन बुधि बल लेसा ॥
translation: वही दस सिर वाला रावण कुत्ते की तरह इधर-उधर ताकता हुआ भड़िहाई (चोरी) के लिए चला। (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं-) हे गरुड़जी! इस प्रकार कुमार्ग पर पैर रखते ही शरीर में तेज तथा बुद्धि एवं बल का लेश भी नहीं रह जाता ॥ सूना पाकर कुत्ता चुपके से बर्तन-भाँड़ों में मुँह डालकर कुछ चुरा ले जाता है। उसे 'भड़िहाई' कहते हैं।
english_translation: Ravana, the ten-headed one, moved like a dog, looking here and there for a chance to steal. Thus, O Garuda, when one sets foot on the wrong path, even a trace of brilliance, clear judgment, and strength does not remain in the body.
essence: Wrong action quietly strips away the power to see clearly.
simple_meaning: Ravana is described as sneaking around like a dog looking for theft. The deeper point is that choosing the wrong path quickly drains your brilliance, judgment, and strength.
insight: It shifts attention from the outward act to the inner damage that follows unethical movement.
modern_relevance: You tell one small lie to cover another, then notice how quickly your confidence starts to thin out. The verse catches that exact moment when bad choices begin to hollow you from within.
speaker: Kak Bhushundi

verse_text: नाना बिधि करि कथा सुहाई। राजनीति भय प्रीति देखाई॥ कह सीता सुनु जती गोसाईं। बोलेहु बचन दुष्ट की नाईं ॥
translation: रावण ने अनेकों प्रकार की सुहावनी कथाएँ रचकर सीताजी को राजनीति, भय और प्रेम दिखलाया। सीताजी ने कहा- हे यति गोसाईं! सुनो, तुमने तो दुष्ट की तरह वचन कहे॥6।
english_translation: Ravana used many charming stories to show Sita politics, fear, and love. Sita said, “O ascetic and lord, listen: you have spoken like a wicked man.”
essence: False sweetness cannot hide a crooked intent.
simple_meaning: Ravana tries to win Sita with polished words, fear, and false affection. Sita sees through it and calls out the wickedness behind his speech.
insight: It trains you to trust clear seeing over persuasive packaging.
modern_relevance: Someone floods your inbox with polite language, pressure, and flattery to get what they want. You feel the mismatch before you can explain it. Sita shows how to name manipulation without getting pulled in.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: तब रावन निज रूप देखावा। भई सभय जब नाम सुनावा॥ कह सीता धरि धीरजु गाढ़ा। आइ गयउ प्रभु रहु खल ठाढ़ा ॥
translation: तब रावण ने अपना असली रूप दिखलाया और जब नाम सुनाया तब तो सीताजी भयभीत हो गईं। उन्होंने गहरा धीरज धरकर कहा- 'अरे दुष्ट! खड़ा तो रह, प्रभु आ गए' ॥
english_translation: Then Ravana showed his true form, and when he announced his name, Sita became afraid. Gathering deep courage, she said, 'O wicked one, stand still — the Lord has arrived.'
essence: Courage can stand its ground even while fear is present.
simple_meaning: Ravana reveals his true nature, but Sita keeps her courage. Even while afraid, she tells him to stand still because Ram has already arrived.
insight: It teaches you to steady yourself under pressure instead of reacting from panic.
modern_relevance: A threatening email lands in your inbox and your stomach drops, but you take one breath before replying. That pause can keep fear from steering the whole day.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जिमि हरिबधुहि छुद्र सस चाहा। भएसि कालबस निसिचर नाहा॥ सुनत बचन दससीस रिसाना। मन महुँ चरन बंदि सुख माना ॥
translation: जैसे सिंह की स्त्री को तुच्छ खरगोश चाहे, वैसे ही अरे राक्षसराज! तू (मेरी चाह करके) काल के वश हुआ है। ये वचन सुनते ही रावण को क्रोध आ गया, परन्तु मन में उसने सीताजी के चरणों की वंदना करके सुख माना ॥
english_translation: Like a jackal coveting a lioness, you, lord of demons, have fallen under Time’s control. Hearing this, Ravana burned with anger, yet in his mind he bowed to Sita’s feet and found a strange peace.
essence: Courage can expose arrogance so completely that anger and reverence appear together.
simple_meaning: Sita compares Ravana’s desire for her to a jackal wanting a lioness, then says he is already trapped by Time. Ravana outwardly rages, but inwardly feels humbled before her.
insight: It shifts the mind from being intimidated by force to seeing through it instantly.
modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a heated text thread, trying to dominate with bluster. You answer once, cleanly, and their confidence cracks because they know you are not afraid.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: क्रोधवंत तब रावन लीन्हिसि रथ बैठाइ। चला गगनपथ आतुर भयँ रथ हाँकि न जाइ ॥
translation: फिर क्रोध में भरकर रावण ने सीताजी को रथ पर बैठा लिया और वह बड़ी उतावली के साथ आकाश मार्ग से चला, किन्तु डर के मारे उससे रथ हाँका नहीं जाता था ॥
english_translation: Then, in rage, Ravana lifted Sita onto his chariot. He hurried through the sky-route, but fear made him unable to drive the chariot properly.
essence: Rage can seize someone, but fear still drives the chariot.
simple_meaning: Ravana, driven by anger and fear, abducts Sita and rushes away, but his own fear makes him unstable even as he flees.
insight: It shows how domination born of rage is never steady; fear rides inside it and weakens every move.
modern_relevance: You storm out after a cruel argument, heart racing, only to realise your anger has made every next step shaky.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हा जग एक बीर रघुराया। केहिं अपराध बिसारेहु दाया॥ आरति हरन सरन सुखदायक। हा रघुकुल सरोज दिननायक ॥
translation: (सीताजी विलाप कर रही थीं-) हा जगत के अद्वितीय वीर श्री रघुनाथजी! आपने किस अपराध से मुझ पर दया भुला दी। हे दुःखों के हरने वाले, हे शरणागत को सुख देने वाले, हा रघुकुल रूपी कमल के सूर्य! ॥
english_translation: Alas, O unique hero of the world, Raghunath! For what fault have you forgotten your mercy toward me? O remover of suffering, giver of comfort to those who seek refuge, alas, sun of the lotus-clan of Raghu!
essence: Love in exile still calls the beloved by name.
simple_meaning: Sita cries out to Ram, asking why his mercy has been forgotten and pleading to the one who removes suffering and comforts those who take refuge.
insight: It captures how suffering turns longing into direct appeal, not abstraction.
modern_relevance: You sit awake after a cruel message, staring at the person you trusted most. The ache is not just loss — it is the question, why did your care disappear?
speaker: Sita

verse_text: हा लछिमन तुम्हार नहिं दोसा। सो फलु पायउँ कीन्हेउँ रोसा॥ बिबिध बिलाप करति बैदेही। भूरि कृपा प्रभु दूरि सनेही ॥
translation: हा लक्ष्मण! तुम्हारा दोष नहीं है। मैंने क्रोध किया, उसका फल पाया। श्री जानकीजी बहुत प्रकार से विलाप कर रही हैं- (हाय!) प्रभु की कृपा तो बहुत है, परन्तु वे स्नेही प्रभु बहुत दूर रह गए हैं ॥
english_translation: Ha Lakshman, your fault is not here. I earned this result by my own anger. Janaki weeps in many ways: the Lord is full of grace, yet the loving Lord has gone far away.
essence: Your own reaction can hurt you more than anyone else's fault.
simple_meaning: Sita says Lakshman is not at fault. Her own anger brought this suffering, and she laments that the loving Lord has gone far away.
insight: It shifts the mind from blame to responsibility, while naming separation as the real suffering.
modern_relevance: After the argument, you replay every line and want someone to blame. Then you see it more clearly: your own reaction helped create the damage, and the person you most need feels far away.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: बिपति मोरि को प्रभुहि सुनावा। पुरोडास चह रासभ खावा॥ सीता कै बिलाप सुनि भारी। भए चराचर जीव दुखारी ॥
translation: प्रभु को मेरी यह विपत्ति कौन सुनावे? यज्ञ के अन्न को गदहा खाना चाहता है। सीताजी का भारी विलाप सुनकर जड़-चेतन सभी जीव दुःखी हो गए ॥
english_translation: Who can tell the Lord of my distress? A donkey wants to eat the sacred offering. Hearing Sita's deep lament, all moving and unmoving beings became sorrowful.
essence: Grief so deep can make the whole world ache with you.
simple_meaning: Sita cries out in helpless grief, asking who can carry her suffering to Ram. Her sorrow is so deep that all living beings are moved by it.
insight: It shows how grief can become a shared atmosphere, not just a private feeling.
modern_relevance: You sit on the bathroom floor after a message that changes everything, unable to explain the hurt to anyone else. Some pain is so raw it seems to spill into the room.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: गीधराज सुनि आरत बानी। रघुकुलतिलक नारि पहिचानी॥ अधम निसाचर लीन्हें जाई। जिमि मलेछ बस कपिला गाई ॥
translation: गृध्रराज जटायु ने सीताजी की दुःखभरी वाणी सुनकर पहचान लिया कि ये रघुकुल तिलक श्री रामचन्द्रजी की पत्नी हैं। (उसने देखा कि) नीच राक्षस इनको (बुरी तरह) लिए जा रहा है, जैसे कपिला गाय म्लेच्छ के पाले पड़ गई हो ॥
english_translation: King of the birds Jatayu heard Sita’s anguished voice and recognized her as the wife of Ram, the ornament of Raghu’s line. The wicked demon was carrying her away, like a cow seized by an outcaste.
essence: Recognition of suffering becomes the first act of courage.
simple_meaning: Jatayu hears Sita’s cry, recognizes who she is, and sees Ravana carrying her away like a helpless cow seized by a cruel stranger.
insight: It turns perception into duty: once suffering is recognized, action follows.
modern_relevance: You hear a frightened voice from the next room and know something is wrong before anyone explains. Recognition itself can become responsibility.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीते पुत्रि करसि जनि त्रासा। करिहउँ जातुधान कर नासा ॥ धावा क्रोधवंत खग कैसें। छूटइ पबि परबत कहुँ जैसें ॥
translation: (वह बोला-) हे सीते पुत्री! भय मत कर। मैं इस राक्षस का नाश करूँगा। (यह कहकर) वह पक्षी क्रोध में भरकर ऐसे दौड़ा, जैसे पर्वत की ओर वज्र छूटता हो ॥
english_translation: “O Sita, daughter, do not be afraid. I will destroy this demon.” Saying this, the bird rushed in anger, like a thunderbolt striking a mountain.
essence: Love rushes toward danger before fear can speak.
simple_meaning: Jatayu comforts Sita, promises to destroy Ravana, and charges at him with fierce courage.
insight: It shows how devotion turns concern into immediate action, without waiting for safety or advantage.
modern_relevance: You hear a frightened voice from the next room and move before thinking. That instant of protective courage is what Jatayu becomes here.
speaker: Jatayu

verse_text: रे रे दुष्ट ठाढ़ किन हो ही। निर्भय चलेसि न जानेहि मोही॥ आवत देखि कृतांत समाना। फिरि दसकंधर कर अनुमाना ॥
translation: (उसने ललकारकर कहा-) रे रे दुष्ट! खड़ा क्यों नहीं होता? निडर होकर चल दिया! मुझे तूने नहीं जाना? उसको यमराज के समान आता हुआ देखकर रावण घूमकर मन में अनुमान करने लगा- ॥
english_translation: “Hey you villain, why do you stand there? You flew off fearless and still you do not know me!” Seeing him come like Death itself, Ravana turned and thought to himself.
essence: Ego shouts loudest right before fear takes over.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the opponent for daring to come fearlessly, then realizes he is facing someone as terrible as death and begins to reassess.
insight: It shows how arrogance turns into caution when confronted by something greater.
modern_relevance: You swagger into a room sure you control it, then one hard look from the person across from you changes everything. Confidence built on ego collapses fast.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: की मैनाक कि खगपति होई। मम बल जान सहित पति सोई॥ जाना जरठ जटायू एहा। मम कर तीरथ छाँड़िहि देहा ॥
translation: यह या तो मैनाक पर्वत है या पक्षियों का स्वामी गरुड़। पर वह (गरुड़) तो अपने स्वामी विष्णु सहित मेरे बल को जानता है! (कुछ पास आने पर) रावण ने उसे पहचान लिया (और बोला-) यह तो बूढ़ा जटायु है। यह मेरे हाथ रूपी तीर्थ में शरीर छोड़ेगा ॥
english_translation: Is this Mainaka, or the king of birds? But he knows my strength along with his master Vishnu. Ah, this is the old Jatayu. He will leave his body in my hands, like a pilgrim at a holy place.
essence: Pride turns even danger into a joke until it meets resistance.
simple_meaning: Ravana briefly mistakes Jatayu for something harmless, then recognizes the old bird and boasts that Jatayu will die at his hands.
insight: It exposes the ego that assumes it can name and dismiss resistance before the fight begins.
modern_relevance: You spot someone in your way and instantly rank them as weak or irrelevant. That split-second contempt can blind you to the courage already standing there.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सुनत गीध क्रोधातुर धावा। कह सुनु रावन मोर सिखावा॥ तजि जानकिहि कुसल गृह जाहू। नाहिं त अस होइहि बहुबाहू ॥
translation: यह सुनते ही गीध क्रोध में भरकर बड़े वेग से दौड़ा और बोला- रावण! मेरी सिखावन सुन। जानकीजी को छोड़कर कुशलपूर्वक अपने घर चला जा। नहीं तो हे बहुत भुजाओं वाले! ऐसा होगा कि- ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Jatayu rushed forward in anger and said, 'Listen, Ravana, to my warning: leave Janaki and go home safely. Otherwise, O many-armed one, this will happen...'
essence: Real courage speaks up before violence fully begins.
simple_meaning: Jatayu confronts Ravana in anger and warns him to leave Sita and go home safely.
insight: It shows that protecting the vulnerable can begin with a direct warning, not only with force.
modern_relevance: You see someone being cornered in a parking lot and your body moves before your fear catches up. Jatayu is that instant of moral courage.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम रोष पावक अति घोरा। होइहि सकल सलभ कुल तोरा॥ उतरु न देत दसानन जोधा। तबहिं गीध धावा करि क्रोधा ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के क्रोध रूपी अत्यन्त भयानक अग्नि में तेरा सारा वंश पतिंगा (होकर भस्म) हो जाएगा। योद्धा रावण कुछ उत्तर नहीं देता। तब गीध क्रोध करके दौड़ा ॥
english_translation: In Ram's terrible fire of wrath, your whole lineage will be burned to ash. The warrior Ravana gives no answer. Then the vulture, enraged, rushed forward.
essence: Ram's wrath exposes ego as something that cannot endure.
simple_meaning: Ravana is warned that Ram's anger will destroy his entire lineage, but he stays silent. Jatayu then attacks in rage.
insight: It frames Jatayu's charge as righteous fury against Ravana's arrogance, not a random fight.
modern_relevance: A bully keeps talking until someone names the cost clearly. Then the room goes quiet, and the person with courage steps in anyway.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धरि कच बिरथ कीन्ह महि गिरा। सीतहि राखि गीध पुनि फिरा॥ चोचन्ह मारि बिदारेसि देही। दंड एक भइ मुरुछा तेही ॥
translation: उसने (रावण के) बाल पकड़कर उसे रथ के नीचे उतार लिया, रावण पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा। गीध सीताजी को एक ओर बैठाकर फिर लौटा और चोंचों से मार-मारकर रावण के शरीर को विदीर्ण कर डाला। इससे उसे एक घड़ी के लिए मूर्च्छा हो गई ॥
english_translation: He seized Ravana by the hair and threw him to the ground. The eagle set Sita aside and returned again, striking the body with its beak until Ravana lay stunned for a moment.
essence: Protecting the vulnerable can be stronger than brute force.
simple_meaning: Jatayu throws Ravana down, protects Sita, and attacks again until Ravana is stunned.
insight: It shows that dharma can mean repeated, bodily resistance when someone vulnerable is under attack.
modern_relevance: You step between a friend and someone bullying them, even when your voice shakes. Protection is not loudness; it is refusing to move aside.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब सक्रोध निसिचर खिसिआना। काढ़ेसि परम कराल कृपाना॥ काटेसि पंख परा खग धरनी। सुमिरि राम करि अदभुत करनी ॥
translation: तब खिसियाए हुए रावण ने क्रोधयुक्त होकर अत्यन्त भयानक कटार निकाली और उससे जटायु के पंख काट डाले। पक्षी (जटायु) श्री रामजी की अद्भुत लीला का स्मरण करके पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा ॥
english_translation: Then, angered and hostile, the demon king drew a terribly fierce dagger. He cut off the bird's wings, and Jatayu fell to the earth, remembering Ram's wondrous deed.
essence: Anger cuts the body, but remembrance can remain unbroken.
simple_meaning: Ravana, furious, draws a terrible weapon and cuts Jatayu's wings. The wounded bird falls, holding Ram in mind.
insight: It shows how violence springs from wounded pride, while steadfast remembrance can survive physical defeat.
modern_relevance: A person lashes out in anger during a breakup or family fight, saying the cruel thing they can never take back. The wound lands, but the one being hurt may still hold on to what is highest.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीतहि जान चढ़ाइ बहोरी। चला उताइल त्रास न थोरी॥ करति बिलाप जाति नभ सीता। ब्याध बिबस जनु मृगी सभीता ॥
translation: सीताजी को फिर रथ पर चढ़ाकर रावण बड़ी उतावली के साथ चला। उसे भय कम न था। सीताजी आकाश में विलाप करती हुई जा रही हैं। मानो व्याधे के वश में पड़ी हुई (जाल में फँसी हुई) कोई भयभीत हिरनी हो! ॥
english_translation: Ravana hurried on after lifting Sita back onto the chariot. Fear still did not leave him. Sita went through the sky, crying out, like a frightened doe caught by a hunter.
essence: Cruelty runs faster when fear is driving it.
simple_meaning: Ravana rushed onward with Sita after forcing her back onto the chariot. Sita cried out helplessly as she was carried through the sky, like a frightened deer caught by a hunter.
insight: It shows how fear and force can keep a person moving without any inner steadiness.
modern_relevance: A person keeps pushing forward after crossing a line, not slowing down but speeding up. The harm is already done, yet the panic only makes the damage harsher.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गिरि पर बैठे कपिन्ह निहारी। कहि हरि नाम दीन्ह पट डारी॥ एहि बिधि सीतहि सो लै गयऊ। बन असोक महँ राखत भयऊ ॥
translation: पर्वत पर बैठे हुए बंदरों को देखकर सीताजी ने हरिनाम लेकर वस्त्र डाल दिया। इस प्रकार वह सीताजी को ले गया और उन्हें अशोक वन में जा रखा ॥
english_translation: Seeing the monkeys seated on the mountain, Sita uttered Hari's name and let her cloth fall. In this way he carried Sita away and placed her in the Ashoka grove.
essence: Even in captivity, Sita answers with Ram's name.
simple_meaning: Sita sees the monkeys, calls on Ram, and drops her cloth as a sign. Ravana then carries her to the Ashoka grove.
insight: It shows how faith can be signaled quietly, even when direct action is impossible.
modern_relevance: You catch sight of one familiar face in a room where you feel utterly alone. A small sign of trust can still travel farther than fear.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हारि परा खल बहु बिधि भय अरु प्रीति देखाइ। तब असोक पादप तर राखिसि जतन कराइ ॥
translation: सीताजी को बहुत प्रकार से भय और प्रीति दिखलाकर जब वह दुष्ट हार गया, तब उन्हें यत्न कराके (सब व्यवस्था ठीक कराके) अशोक वृक्ष के नीचे रख दिया ॥
english_translation: After showing Sita many kinds of fear and affection and finally being defeated, the wicked one had her carefully placed under the Ashoka tree.
essence: False tenderness is still a cage.
simple_meaning: Ravana used fear and false kindness, but after failing, he had Sita placed under the Ashoka tree with care.
insight: It teaches you to see coercion clearly, even when it comes dressed as kindness.
modern_relevance: Someone corners you with pressure, then suddenly softens their tone to make control feel like concern. You can feel the manipulation even when it arrives wrapped in care.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जेहि बिधि कपट कुरंग सँग धाइ चले श्रीराम। सो छबि सीता राखि उर रटति रहति हरिनाम ॥
translation: जिस प्रकार कपट मृग के साथ श्री रामजी दौड़ चले थे, उसी छवि को हृदय में रखकर वे हरिनाम (रामनाम) रटती रहती हैं ॥
english_translation: Keeping the image of Shri Ram running after the deceptive deer in her heart, Sita keeps chanting Ram's name.
essence: A single remembered act of love can keep devotion breathing.
simple_meaning: Sita remembers the moment Ram ran after the false deer, and that memory keeps her repeating Ram's name.
insight: It teaches you to anchor attention in a sustaining memory so devotion stays alive under pressure.
modern_relevance: You replay one moment of care from someone you love while sitting alone in a quiet room. That memory keeps you from collapsing into panic.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रघुपति अनुजहि आवत देखी। बाहिज चिंता कीन्हि बिसेषी॥ जनकसुता परिहरिहु अकेली। आयहु तात बचन मम पेली ॥
translation: (इधर) श्री रघुनाथजी ने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी को आते देखकर ब्राह्य रूप में बहुत चिंता की (और कहा-) हे भाई! तुमने जानकी को अकेली छोड़ दिया और मेरी आज्ञा का उल्लंघन कर यहाँ चले आए! ॥
english_translation: Seeing his younger brother return, Raghupati showed great concern outwardly and said, 'Brother, you left Janaki alone and came here against my command.'
essence: Fear for someone you love can wear the mask of anger.
simple_meaning: Ram speaks as if he is upset that Lakshman left Sita alone and returned against his order.
insight: It shows how protective concern can appear as blame when danger feels near.
modern_relevance: You hear footsteps at the door after leaving someone vulnerable alone, and your first words come out sharper than you meant. Fear often speaks before calm does.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: निसिचर निकर फिरहिं बन माहीं। मम मन सीता आश्रम नाहीं॥ गहि पद कमल अनुज कर जोरी। कहेउ नाथ कछु मोहि न खोरी ॥
translation: राक्षसों के झुंड वन में फिरते रहते हैं। मेरे मन में ऐसा आता है कि सीता आश्रम में नहीं है। छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी ने श्री रामजी के चरणकमलों को पकड़कर हाथ जोड़कर कहा- हे नाथ! मेरा कुछ भी दोष नहीं है ॥
english_translation: The demons keep roaming the forest, and my mind tells me Sita is not at the hermitage. Lakshman clasped Ram's lotus feet and, with joined hands, said, "Lord, I have done nothing wrong."
essence: Fear can make innocence feel like guilt.
simple_meaning: Ram senses danger in the forest and fears Sita is no longer safe at the hermitage. Lakshman falls at his feet and insists he has done no wrong.
insight: It shows how anxiety distorts trust and turns concern into suspicion.
modern_relevance: You get a text that sounds like something went wrong, and your stomach drops before you even know why. In fear, even loyal people start defending themselves.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: अनुज समेत गए प्रभु तहवाँ। गोदावरि तट आश्रम जहवाँ॥ आश्रम देखि जानकी हीना। भए बिकल जस प्राकृत दीना ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामजी वहाँ गए, जहाँ गोदावरी के तट पर उनका आश्रम था। आश्रम को जानकीजी से रहित देखकर श्री रामजी साधारण मनुष्य की भाँति व्याकुल और दीन (दुःखी) हो गए ॥
english_translation: Ram went there with Lakshman, to the hermitage on the bank of the Godavari. Seeing the hermitage empty of Janaki, Ram became distraught and helpless like an ordinary sorrowful man.
essence: Absence itself can bring even the steady heart to its knees.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman reach the hermitage by the Godavari, but Sita is missing. Seeing the empty place, Ram is overwhelmed with grief like an ordinary person.
insight: It shows how loss can strip away composure and leave only raw feeling.
modern_relevance: You come home and notice the small things first: the untouched cup, the quiet room, the message that never came. In that instant, absence becomes unbearable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हा गुन खानि जानकी सीता। रूप सील ब्रत नेम पुनीता॥ लछिमन समुझाए बहु भाँति। पूछत चले लता तरु पाँती ॥
translation: (वे विलाप करने लगे-) हा गुणों की खान जानकी! हा रूप, शील, व्रत और नियमों में पवित्र सीते! लक्ष्मणजी ने बहुत प्रकार से समझाया। तब श्री रामजी लताओं और वृक्षों की पंक्तियों से पूछते हुए चले ॥
english_translation: Alas, Janaki, mine of virtues! Alas, pure Sita, radiant in beauty, conduct, vows, and discipline! Lakshman tried to console him in many ways. Then Ram walked on, asking the creepers and trees.
essence: Longing does not stop the search.
simple_meaning: Ram grieves for Sita’s absence, praises her virtues, and keeps searching for her despite Lakshman’s efforts to comfort him.
insight: It shows how love keeps looking even when reason knows there is no answer.
modern_relevance: You search an empty room after someone you love has left, still hoping for one more sign. Grief makes you ask the world itself where they went.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: हे खग मृग हे मधुकर श्रेनी। तुम्ह देखी सीता मृगनैनी॥ खंजन सुक कपोत मृग मीना। मधुप निकर कोकिला प्रबीना ॥
translation: हे पक्षियों! हे पशुओं! हे भौंरों की पंक्तियों! तुमने कहीं मृगनयनी सीता को देखा है? खंजन, तोता, कबूतर, हिरन, मछली, भौंरों का समूह, प्रवीण कोयल, ॥
english_translation: O birds, O deer, O rows of bees, have you seen Sita, the doe-eyed one? Khanjan birds, parrots, pigeons, deer, fish, swarms of bees, and clever cuckoos...
essence: Longing makes every creature feel like a witness.
simple_meaning: Ram is so overwhelmed by Sita's absence that he asks birds, animals, and even bees whether they have seen her. The verse is a heartfelt cry of searching, not a teaching on its own.
insight: It turns private grief into a search that reaches outward, making the whole world part of the longing.
modern_relevance: You keep asking everyone in the group chat if they saw the person who left your life without warning. Even strangers start to feel like possible witnesses to your missing piece.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कुंद कली दाड़िम दामिनी। कमल सरद ससि अहिभामिनी॥ बरुन पास मनोज धनु हंसा। गज केहरि निज सुनत प्रसंसा ॥
translation: कुन्दकली, अनार, बिजली, कमल, शरद् का चंद्रमा और नागिनी, अरुण का पाश, कामदेव का धनुष, हंस, गज और सिंह- ये सब आज अपनी प्रशंसा सुन रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Kund blossoms, pomegranate, lightning, lotus, autumn moon, and the serpent-woman; Varuna's noose, Cupid's bow, swan, elephant, and lion — all are hearing their own praise.
essence: Sita's radiance makes every comparison bow.
simple_meaning: The poet piles up images of beauty and power to say that all of them are being outshone by Sita's radiance.
insight: It shifts attention from the objects named to the one they cannot equal.
modern_relevance: You see someone enter a room and every polished detail around them feels ordinary. The verse catches that rare feeling when one presence makes all other beauty look smaller.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: श्री फल कनक कदलि हरषाहीं। नेकु न संक सकुच मन माहीं॥ सुनु जानकी तोहि बिनु आजू। हरषे सकल पाइ जनु राजू ॥
translation: बेल, सुवर्ण और केला हर्षित हो रहे हैं। इनके मन में जरा भी शंका और संकोच नहीं है। हे जानकी! सुनो, तुम्हारे बिना ये सब आज ऐसे हर्षित हैं, मानो राज पा गए हों। (अर्थात् तुम्हारे अंगों के सामने ये सब तुच्छ, अपमानित और लज्जित थे। आज तुम्हें न देखकर ये अपनी शोभा के अभिमान में फूल रहे हैं) ॥
english_translation: The bel, golden flower, and banana trees are rejoicing. There is not even a trace of doubt or shyness in their minds. O Janaki, without you today they are all delighted, as if they have won a kingdom.
essence: Nature itself seems to miss Sita’s beauty and presence.
simple_meaning: The poet imagines plants and trees rejoicing at Sita's absence, as if they feel proud of their own beauty now that she is not there to outshine them.
insight: It turns the search for Sita into a living landscape of longing, not a lesson to apply.
modern_relevance: You step into a room after someone radiant has left, and everything still looks bright — but the brightness feels empty. The scene is really about the ache of their absence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: किमि सहि जात अनख तोहि पाहीं। प्रिया बेगि प्रगटसि कस नाहीं॥ एहि बिधि खोजत बिलपत स्वामी। मनहुँ महा बिरही अति कामी ॥
translation: तुमसे यह अनख (स्पर्धा) कैसे सही जाती है? हे प्रिये! तुम शीघ्र ही प्रकट क्यों नहीं होती? इस प्रकार (अनन्त ब्रह्माण्डों के अथवा महामहिमामयी स्वरूपाशक्ति श्री सीताजी के) स्वामी श्री रामजी सीताजी को खोजते हुए (इस प्रकार) विलाप करते हैं, मानो कोई महाविरही और अत्यंत कामी पुरुष हो ॥
english_translation: How can I bear this rivalry from you? Beloved, why do you not appear at once? In this way, the lord of Sita searches and cries out, like a great lover burning with longing.
essence: Even the lord of Sita is shown as helpless in love.
simple_meaning: Ram searches for Sita in deep longing and cries out for her to appear. His grief is so intense it looks like the pain of a lover separated from the one he loves most.
insight: It shifts the mind from heroic distance to vulnerable devotion.
modern_relevance: You have called, texted, waited, and still no reply comes. The silence starts to feel physical, and you understand how longing can make even dignity tremble.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पूरकनाम राम सुख रासी। मनुजचरित कर अज अबिनासी॥ आगें परा गीधपति देखा। सुमिरत राम चरन जिन्ह रेखा ॥
translation: पूर्णकाम, आनंद की राशि, अजन्मा और अविनाशी श्री रामजी मनुष्यों के चरित्र कर रहे हैं। आगे (जाने पर) उन्होंने गृध्रपति जटायु को पड़ा देखा। वह श्री रामजी के चरणों का स्मरण कर रहा था, जिनमें (ध्वजा, कुलिश आदि की) रेखाएँ (चिह्न) हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram, the source of complete fulfillment and bliss, the unborn and imperishable, was acting out the life of a human. Ahead, he saw Jatayu, lord of the vultures, lying fallen, remembering the footprints of Ram's feet.
essence: The imperishable one walks as a human and is found by devotion.
simple_meaning: Ram, though unborn and imperishable, is moving through a human life. Then he sees Jatayu lying fallen, still remembering Ram's marked feet.
insight: It shifts attention from the tragedy of the body to the endurance of remembrance.
modern_relevance: You find someone collapsed after trying to help and realize they were holding on to the memory of what mattered most. Even at the edge of loss, devotion can remain.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कर सरोज सिर परसेउ कृपासिंधु रघुबीर। निरखि राम छबि धाम मुख बिगत भई सब पीर ॥
translation: कृपा सागर श्री रघुवीर ने अपने करकमल से उसके सिर का स्पर्श किया (उसके सिर पर करकमल फेर दिया)। शोभाधाम श्री रामजी का (परम सुंदर) मुख देखकर उसकी सब पीड़ा जाती रही ॥
english_translation: The ocean of compassion, Raghubir, touched his head with his lotus hand. Seeing Ram's beauty, all his pain vanished.
essence: Ram's touch and sight heal where strength cannot.
simple_meaning: Ram gently touches Jatayu's head, and the sight of his beautiful face removes all suffering.
insight: It shows that compassionate presence can relieve suffering without explanation or argument.
modern_relevance: You sit beside someone hurting and say almost nothing. Then you place a hand on their shoulder, and the room softens. Presence itself can be medicine.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब कह गीध बचन धरि धीरा। सुनहु राम भंजन भव भीरा॥ नाथ दसानन यह गति कीन्ही। तेहिं खल जनकसुता हरि लीन्ही ॥
translation: तब धीरज धरकर गीध ने यह वचन कहा- हे भव (जन्म-मृत्यु) के भय का नाश करने वाले श्री रामजी! सुनिए। हे नाथ! रावण ने मेरी यह दशा की है। उसी दुष्ट ने जानकीजी को हर लिया है ॥
english_translation: Then Gid, gathering himself, spoke: "Listen, Ram, destroyer of the fear of worldly existence. Lord, Ravana has done this to me. That wicked one has taken Janaki away."
essence: Pain becomes useful when it names the wrong clearly.
simple_meaning: Jatayu tells Ram that Ravana has carried Sita away and asks Ram to hear him out.
insight: It teaches you to speak with steadiness even when hurt, so the truth can still help.
modern_relevance: After a hard conversation, you finally say the truth plainly: who did what, what was lost, and what must happen next.
speaker: Jatayu

verse_text: लै दच्छिन दिसि गयउ गोसाईं। बिलपति अति कुररी की नाईं॥ दरस लाग प्रभु राखेउँ प्राना। चलन चहत अब कृपानिधाना ॥
translation: हे गोसाईं! वह उन्हें लेकर दक्षिण दिशा को गया है। सीताजी कुररी (कुर्ज) की तरह अत्यंत विलाप कर रही थीं। हे प्रभो! आपके दर्शनों के लिए ही प्राण रोक रखे थे। हे कृपानिधान! अब ये चलना ही चाहते हैं ॥
english_translation: He has taken her toward the south. Sita was crying bitterly like a kurri bird. 'Lord, I held my breath only to see you. Now, O treasure of grace, I want to leave my body.'
essence: Grief becomes a final message when love is still alive.
simple_meaning: Jatayu tells Ram that Ravana carried Sita southward. Sita cried in pain, and she had stayed alive only to see Ram again before leaving her body.
