translation: सयाना हो जाने पर उस पुत्र पर माता प्रेम तो करती है, परन्तु पिछली बात नहीं रहती (अर्थात् मातृ परायण शिशु की तरह फिर उसको बचाने की चिंता नहीं करती, क्योंकि वह माता पर निर्भर न कर अपनी रक्षा आप करने लगता है)। ज्ञानी मेरे प्रौढ़ (सयाने) पुत्र के समान है और (तुम्हारे जैसा) अपने बल का मान न करने वाला सेवक मेरे शिशु पुत्र के समान है ॥
english_translation: A mother loves her grown son, but she no longer worries over his safety like a child’s. My mature devotee is like that wise son, and the humble servant who does not rely on his own strength is like a child to me.
essence: Humility draws care; pride creates distance.
simple_meaning: A wise person may rely on personal understanding, but a humble devotee depends on the divine completely. Humility brings closeness; self-reliance creates distance.
insight: It shifts devotion from self-display to dependence, showing that humility creates intimacy.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to look capable in front of everyone, even when you are exhausted. This verse says the deeper safety comes when you stop performing strength and allow yourself to be held.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जनहि मोर बल निज बल ताही। दुहु कहँ काम क्रोध रिपु आही॥ यह बिचारि पंडित मोहि भजहीं। पाएहुँ ग्यान भगति नहिं तजहीं ॥
translation: मेरे सेवक को केवल मेरा ही बल रहता है और उसे (ज्ञानी को) अपना बल होता है। पर काम-क्रोध रूपी शत्रु तो दोनों के लिए हैं।(भक्त के शत्रुओं को मारने की जिम्मेवारी मुझ पर रहती है, क्योंकि वह मेरे परायण होकर मेरा ही बल मानता है, परन्तु अपने बल को मानने वाले ज्ञानी के शत्रुओं का नाश करने की जिम्मेवारी मुझ पर नहीं है।) ऐसा विचार कर पंडितजन (बुद्धिमान लोग) मुझको ही भजते हैं। वे ज्ञान प्राप्त होने पर भी भक्ति को नहीं छोड़ते ॥
english_translation: Those who know my strength rely on my strength alone. For both of them, the enemies are lust and anger. Thinking this way, the wise worship me. Even after gaining understanding, they do not abandon devotion.
essence: Knowing your limits makes devotion wiser, not weaker.
simple_meaning: Those who depend on Ram's strength are protected, while lust and anger threaten everyone. Wise people understand this and keep worshipping him even after gaining knowledge.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance to humble dependence, showing that understanding should lead to deeper devotion.
modern_relevance: You can be the smartest person in the room and still feel hijacked by anger in a family argument or desire in a private moment. The deeper move is not pride in insight, but leaning on a source stronger than your impulses.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: काम क्रोध लोभादि मद प्रबल मोह कै धारि। तिन्ह महँ अति दारुन दुखद मायारूपी नारि ॥
translation: काम, क्रोध, लोभ और मद आदि मोह (अज्ञान) की प्रबल सेना है। इनमें मायारूपिणी (माया की साक्षात् मूर्ति) स्त्री तो अत्यंत दारुण दुःख देने वाली है ॥
english_translation: Desire, anger, greed, pride, and the rest are the strong army of delusion. Among them, the woman shaped by illusion is the most terrible source of suffering.
essence: Delusion becomes most dangerous when it feels attractive.
simple_meaning: Desire, anger, greed, and pride are powerful forces of confusion. The verse warns that illusion can take a form that causes especially deep suffering.
insight: It teaches you to recognize the hidden pattern behind emotional overwhelm before it hardens into action.
modern_relevance: A late-night argument starts with one sharp message, then turns into jealousy, defensiveness, and obsession. By morning, you can see the pattern: the mind was never just reacting — it was being pulled by forces you didn't name fast enough.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनु मुनि कह पुरान श्रुति संता। मोह बिपिन कहुँ नारि बसंता॥ जप तप नेम जलाश्रय झारी। होइ ग्रीषम सोषइ सब नारी॥1
translation: हे मुनि! सुनो, पुराण, वेद और संत कहते हैं कि मोह रूपी वन (को विकसित करने) के लिए स्त्री वसंत ऋतु के समान है। जप, तप, नियम रूपी संपूर्ण जल के स्थानों को स्त्री ग्रीष्म रूप होकर सर्वथा सोख लेती है ॥
english_translation: Listen, O sage: the Puranas, the Vedas, and the saints say that woman is like spring for the forest of delusion. She is like summer, drying up all pools of austerity, vows, and discipline.
essence: Desire can look like spring while secretly draining your strength.
simple_meaning: The verse warns that desire can quickly awaken delusion and drain away spiritual practice, vows, and restraint.
insight: It shifts attention from the pleasure of temptation to the damage it can do to your discipline.
modern_relevance: You open one message “just to check,” and an hour later your focus is gone. The pull did not look dangerous at first, but it quietly ate the day you had set aside for practice.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: काम क्रोध मद मत्सर भेका। इन्हहि हरषप्रद बरषा एका॥ दुर्बासना कुमुद समुदाई। तिन्ह कहँ सरद सदा सुखदाई ॥
translation: काम, क्रोध, मद और मत्सर (डाह) आदि मेंढक हैं। इनको वर्षा ऋतु होकर हर्ष प्रदान करने वाली एकमात्र यही (स्त्री) है। बुरी वासनाएँ कुमुदों के समूह हैं। उनको सदैव सुख देने वाली यह शरद् ऋतु है ॥
english_translation: Lust, anger, pride, and jealousy are like frogs. For them, this is the one rain that brings delight. Evil desires are like clusters of water lilies, and this is the autumn season that always pleases them.
essence: Desires grow when you unknowingly keep watering them.
simple_meaning: Certain emotions and bad habits flourish under the right conditions. The verse compares desire, anger, pride, and jealousy to creatures or flowers that thrive in their own season.
insight: It shifts attention from moral blame to pattern recognition: watch the conditions that strengthen reactive habits.
modern_relevance: You open your phone at midnight and the same loop starts again: envy, craving, irritation. The verse points to a hard truth — some habits only grow when the conditions keep favoring them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धर्म सकल सरसीरुह बृंदा। होइ हिम तिन्हहि दहइ सुख मंदा॥ पुनि ममता जवास बहुताई। पलुहइ नारि सिसिर रितु पाई ॥
translation: समस्त धर्म कमलों के झुंड हैं। यह नीच (विषयजन्य) सुख देने वाली स्त्री हिमऋतु होकर उन्हें जला डालती है। फिर ममतारूपी जवास का समूह (वन) स्त्री रूपी शिशिर ऋतु को पाकर हरा-भरा हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: All virtues are like clusters of lotuses. Woman, as winter, burns them with the cold of low pleasure. Then the thicket of attachment grows green again when woman, like winter, arrives.
essence: Outer restraint can fail when attachment quietly returns.
simple_meaning: Virtues are delicate. When attachment and desire return, they can burn away good habits and make old cravings grow again.
insight: It shifts you from trusting temporary restraint to noticing the deeper pull of attachment.
modern_relevance: You delete the app, feel clean for a week, then one familiar message pulls the old pattern back. What looked conquered was only resting.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: पाप उलूक निकर सुखकारी। नारि निबिड़ रजनी अँधियारी॥ बुधि बल सील सत्य सब मीना। बनसी सम त्रिय कहहिं प्रबीना ॥
translation: पाप रूपी उल्लुओं के समूह के लिए यह स्त्री सुख देने वाली घोर अंधकारमयी रात्रि है। बुद्धि, बल, शील और सत्य- ये सब मछलियाँ हैं और उन (को फँसाकर नष्ट करने) के लिए स्त्री बंसी के समान है, चतुर पुरुष ऐसा कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: For the flock of sinful owls, a woman is a delighting, pitch-dark night. Wisdom, strength, virtue, and truth are all fish; clever people say a woman is like a fishing rod that catches and destroys them.
essence: Craving can turn your best qualities into easy prey.
simple_meaning: The verse uses harsh images to warn that desire for women can darken judgment and pull down wisdom, strength, character, and truth.
insight: It shifts attention from attraction itself to the way craving can erode discernment and self-command.
modern_relevance: You open one harmless-looking app and keep scrolling until your judgment feels dull. The verse warns that desire can quietly turn sharpness into helplessness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अवगुन मूल सूलप्रद प्रमदा सब दुख खानि। ताते कीन्ह निवारन मुनि मैं यह जियँ जानि ॥
translation: युवती स्त्री अवगुणों की मूल, पीड़ा देने वाली और सब दुःखों की खान है, इसलिए हे मुनि! मैंने जी में ऐसा जानकर तुमको विवाह करने से रोका था ॥
english_translation: Woman is the root of faults, a thorn that brings pain, and a mine of sorrow. Therefore, sage, I stopped you from marrying her, knowing this in my heart.
essence: What looks sweet can hide the seeds of suffering.
simple_meaning: Desire can seem attractive, but it often becomes the source of suffering. The speaker says he warned the sage from marriage because he saw that danger clearly.
insight: It shifts attention from surface attraction to the hidden consequences of attachment.
modern_relevance: You keep reopening a chat thread because the attention feels sweet, even while you know it leaves you drained. The pull itself can be the warning.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सुनि रघुपति के बचन सुहाए। मुनि तन पुलक नयन भरि आए॥ कहहु कवन प्रभु कै असि रीती। सेवक पर ममता अरु प्रीती ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी के सुंदर वचन सुनकर मुनि का शरीर पुलकित हो गया और नेत्र (प्रेमाश्रुओं के जल से) भर आए। (वे मन ही मन कहने लगे-) कहो तो किस प्रभु की ऐसी रीती है, जिसका सेवक पर इतना ममत्व और प्रेम हो ॥
english_translation: Hearing the gracious words of Lord Raghupati, the sage’s body thrilled and his eyes filled with tears. He thought, “Tell me, what Lord has such a nature—so much affection and love for a servant?”
essence: Ram’s greatness is that he loves his servant like his own.
simple_meaning: Hearing Ram’s gentle words, the sage is overwhelmed with joy and tears. He realises that Ram loves and cares for a servant in a way no ordinary lord would.
insight: It shifts devotion from duty alone to intimate trust in Ram’s loving attention.
modern_relevance: You finally hear a message from someone you admire, and instead of distance, there is warmth. That shock of being seen changes everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जे न भजहिं अस प्रभु भ्रम त्यागी। ग्यान रंक नर मंद अभागी॥ पुनि सादर बोले मुनि नारद। सुनहु राम बिग्यान बिसारद ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य भ्रम को त्यागकर ऐसे प्रभु को नहीं भजते, वे ज्ञान के कंगाल, दुर्बुद्धि और अभागे हैं। फिर नारद मुनि आदर सहित बोले- हे विज्ञान-विशारद श्री रामजी! सुनिए- ॥
english_translation: Those who, after giving up delusion, do not worship such a Lord are poor in wisdom, foolish, and unfortunate. Then Sage Narada spoke respectfully: "Listen, Ram, knower of all knowledge—"
essence: Clarity becomes complete only when it turns into worship.
simple_meaning: Even after seeing through confusion, a person who does not worship Ram remains spiritually poor. Narada then turns to Ram with deep reverence.
insight: It shifts the mind from intellectual clarity alone to devotion as the living completion of understanding.
modern_relevance: You can understand your patterns in therapy, name your habits, and still stay unchanged if you never bow to what is higher than your ego. Insight without reverence can become another kind of pride.
speaker: Narada

verse_text: संतन्ह के लच्छन रघुबीरा। कहहु नाथ भव भंजन भीरा॥ सुनु मुनि संतन्ह के गुन कहऊँ। जिन्ह ते मैं उन्ह कें बस रहऊँ ॥
translation: हे रघुवीर! हे भव-भय (जन्म-मरण के भय) का नाश करने वाले मेरे नाथ! अब कृपा कर संतों के लक्षण कहिए! (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे मुनि! सुनो, मैं संतों के गुणों को कहता हूँ, जिनके कारण मैं उनके वश में रहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: O Raghuvir, destroyer of the fear of becoming and ceasing, please tell me the marks of holy people. The Lord said, "Listen, sage. I will tell you the qualities of the holy, through which I remain under their sway."
essence: The pure heart can hold even the divine in loving sway.
simple_meaning: A sage asks Ram to describe the qualities of holy people. Ram answers that such people are so pure and devoted that even he stays under their influence.
insight: It shifts respect from outer status to inner purity, showing that true influence comes from character, not power.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm changes the whole room. They do not push, perform, or compete — yet you naturally want to be better around them. That quiet gravity is what Ram points to.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: षट बिकार जित अनघ अकामा। अचल अकिंचन सुचि सुखधामा॥ अमित बोध अनीह मितभोगी। सत्यसार कबि कोबिद जोगी ॥
translation: वे संत (काम, क्रोध, लोभ, मोह, मद और मत्सर- इन) छह विकारों (दोषों) को जीते हुए, पापरहित, कामनारहित, निश्चल (स्थिरबुद्धि), अकिंचन (सर्वत्यागी), बाहर-भीतर से पवित्र, सुख के धाम, असीम ज्ञानवान् , इच्छारहित, मिताहारी, सत्यनिष्ठ, कवि, विद्वान, योगी, ॥
english_translation: Saints have conquered the six inner faults, are free from desire, steady, ownerless, and pure. They are homes of peace, boundless understanding, free of wanting, moderate in appetite, rooted in truth, and skilled as poets, scholars, and yogis.
essence: True saintliness is freedom from craving, not just good behaviour.
simple_meaning: A saint has conquered the six inner faults and lives without craving, greed, or restlessness. Such a person is pure, steady, content, and rooted in truth.
insight: It shifts attention from outer respectability to the inner discipline that makes a person trustworthy.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose house is spotless, but their mind is crowded with wanting. This verse points to a different kind of cleanliness: a life with less grasping, less noise, and more steadiness.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सावधान मानद मदहीना। धीर धर्म गति परम प्रबीना ॥
translation: सावधान, दूसरों को मान देने वाले, अभिमानरहित, धैर्यवान, धर्म के ज्ञान और आचरण में अत्यंत निपुण, ॥
english_translation: They are careful, respectful to others, free of pride, patient, and highly skilled in the ways of dharma.
essence: True goodness is humble, patient, and alert in action.
simple_meaning: A true saint is careful, respectful, humble, patient, and deeply skilled in righteous conduct.
insight: It shifts you from performative virtue to steady character shaped by restraint and respect.
modern_relevance: In a tense family conversation, you stay calm, listen fully, and refuse the urge to dominate. That quiet self-command is what this verse praises.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: गुनागार संसार दुख रहित बिगत संदेह। तजि मम चरन सरोज प्रिय तिन्ह कहुँ देह न गेह ॥
translation: गुणों के घर, संसार के दुःखों से रहित और संदेहों से सर्वथा छूटे हुए होते हैं। मेरे चरण कमलों को छोड़कर उनको न देह ही प्रिय होती है, न घर ही ॥
english_translation: They are treasure-houses of virtues, free from the sorrows of the world and completely beyond doubt. Leaving my lotus feet, neither body nor home is dear to them.
essence: Real devotion makes every other attachment feel small.
simple_meaning: Those who truly belong to Ram are full of good qualities, free from worldly sorrow and doubt, and no longer attached to body or home.
insight: It shifts devotion from ritual admiration to total inner belonging.
modern_relevance: You can be surrounded by comfort, yet still feel unrooted. The verse points to a deeper home: the place in your heart where anxiety loosens and your need to possess things falls away.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: निज गुन श्रवन सुनत सकुचाहीं। पर गुन सुनत अधिक हरषाहीं॥ सम सीतल नहिं त्यागहिं नीती। सरल सुभाउ सबहि सन प्रीति ॥
translation: कानों से अपने गुण सुनने में सकुचाते हैं, दूसरों के गुण सुनने से विशेष हर्षित होते हैं। सम और शीतल हैं, न्याय का कभी त्याग नहीं करते। सरल स्वभाव होते हैं और सभी से प्रेम रखते हैं ॥
english_translation: They feel shy hearing praise of their own virtues, but rejoice deeply hearing the virtues of others. They remain calm and balanced, never abandoning righteousness. Their nature is simple, and they love everyone.
essence: Humility makes room for others' goodness and keeps your heart steady.
simple_meaning: A truly noble person is humble about personal praise, happy about others' virtues, steady in conduct, and naturally loving toward everyone.
insight: It shifts you from self-protection to open-heartedness, so praise becomes a chance to rejoice rather than compare.
modern_relevance: You hear someone else get praised in the team meeting, and instead of tightening up, you feel glad. That quiet generosity says more about your character than any self-promotion ever could.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जप तप ब्रत दम संजम नेमा। गुरु गोबिंद बिप्र पद प्रेमा॥ श्रद्धा छमा मयत्री दाया। मुदिता मम पद प्रीति अमाया ॥
translation: वे जप, तप, व्रत, दम, संयम और नियम में रत रहते हैं और गुरु, गोविंद तथा ब्राह्मणों के चरणों में प्रेम रखते हैं। उनमें श्रद्धा, क्षमा, मैत्री, दया, मुदिता (प्रसन्नता) और मेरे चरणों में निष्कपट प्रेम होता है ॥
english_translation: They live in japa, tapas, vows, self-restraint, discipline, and rules. They hold love for the teacher, the supreme being, and the learned, and they possess trust, forgiveness, friendship, compassion, joy, and pure love for my feet.
essence: Devotion becomes visible as disciplined love and humane conduct.
simple_meaning: A devoted person lives with discipline, respect, trust, forgiveness, friendship, compassion, and joyful love for Ram.
insight: It turns devotion into character: self-control, reverence, and compassionate conduct toward others.
modern_relevance: You can say you believe deeply, but the truth shows up when you're patient with your partner, respectful with your mentor, and gentle with people who can offer you nothing back.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: बिरति बिबेक बिनय बिग्याना। बोध जथारथ बेद पुराना॥ दंभ मान मद करहिं न काऊ। भूलि न देहिं कुमारग पाऊ ॥
translation: तथा वैराग्य, विवेक, विनय, विज्ञान (परमात्मा के तत्व का ज्ञान) और वेद-पुराण का यथार्थ ज्ञान रहता है। वे दम्भ, अभिमान और मद कभी नहीं करते और भूलकर भी कुमार्ग पर पैर नहीं रखते ॥
english_translation: They possess renunciation, clear seeing, humility, and true understanding of the scriptures. They never act from pride, ego, or intoxication, and they do not step onto the wrong path even by mistake.
essence: Clear seeing makes pride and wrong action impossible.
simple_meaning: True understanding brings renunciation, humility, and steady conduct. Pride, ego, and intoxication fall away, and the wrong path is avoided.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to steady discernment and clean conduct.
modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, and the first temptation is to start performing your importance. This verse points to the quieter victory: staying humble, clear, and unhooked from ego.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गावहिं सुनहिं सदा मम लीला। हेतु रहित परहित रत सीला॥ मुनि सुनु साधुन्ह के गुन जेते। कहि न सकहिं सादर श्रुति तेते ॥
translation: सदा मेरी लीलाओं को गाते-सुनते हैं और बिना ही कारण दूसरों के हित में लगे रहने वाले होते हैं। हे मुनि! सुनो, संतों के जितने गुण हैं, उनको सरस्वती और वेद भी नहीं कह सकते ॥
english_translation: They always sing and hear My leelas, and remain ever engaged in selfless service to others. O sage, listen: the virtues of saints are so many that even Saraswati and the Vedas cannot fully describe them.
essence: True devotion sings Ram and serves others without asking why.
simple_meaning: Saints keep singing and hearing about Ram, and their nature is to help others without seeking a reason or reward. Their goodness is so vast it cannot be fully described.
insight: It links devotion to action: remembrance of Ram should show up as selfless care for other people.
modern_relevance: You keep replaying the same prayer, name, or song while helping a friend move, cook, or sit through grief. That quiet combination of remembrance and service is what this verse honors.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कहि सक न सारद सेष नारद सुनत पद पंकज गहे। अस दीनबंधु कृपाल अपने भगत गुन निज मुख कहे॥ सिरु नाइ बारहिं बार चरनन्हि ब्रह्मपुर नारद गए। ते धन्य तुलसीदास आस बिहाइ जे हरि रँग रँए॥
translation: 'शेष और शारदा भी नहीं कह सकते' यह सुनते ही नारदजी ने श्री रामजी के चरणकमल पकड़ लिए। दीनबंधु कृपालु प्रभु ने इस प्रकार अपने श्रीमुख से अपने भक्तों के गुण कहे। भगवान् के चरणों में बार-बार सिर नवाकर नारदजी ब्रह्मलोक को चले गए। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि वे पुरुष धन्य हैं, जो सब आशा छोड़कर केवल श्री हरि के रंग में रँग गए हैं।
english_translation: Shesha and Saraswati cannot fully tell it. Hearing this, Narada held Ram's lotus feet. The compassionate lord of the poor spoke the qualities of his devotees from his own mouth. Bowing again and again at those feet, Narada went to Brahmaloka. Blessed are those, says Tulsidas, who leave all hopes behind and are dyed only in Hari's love.
essence: Total devotion begins when all other hopes fall away.
simple_meaning: Even the great sages cannot fully describe Ram's glory. Narada is overwhelmed, bows at Ram's feet, and Tulsidas blesses those who give up all other hopes and live only in loving remembrance of Hari.
insight: It shifts the mind from scattered wanting to single-pointed devotion.
modern_relevance: You keep chasing the next fix, the next reply, the next plan, and still feel hungry. This verse points to a different fullness: the relief of wanting one thing so deeply that everything else loosens.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: रावनारि जसु पावन गावहिं सुनहिं जे लोग। राम भगति दृढ़ पावहिं बिनु बिराग जप जोग ॥
translation: जो लोग रावण के शत्रु श्री रामजी का पवित्र यश गावेंगे और सुनेंगे, वे वैराग्य, जप और योग के बिना ही श्री रामजी की दृढ़ भक्ति पावेंगे ॥
english_translation: Those who sing and hear the pure fame of Ram, the enemy of Ravana, gain firm devotion to Ram without detachment, chanting, or yoga.
essence: Ram’s glory can awaken firm devotion before any formal practice.
simple_meaning: Listening to and singing Ram's pure fame awakens strong devotion in you. You do not need special practices first; the story itself changes the heart.
insight: It shifts the mind from forced spiritual effort to receptive remembrance that naturally deepens devotion.
modern_relevance: You put on a song that reminds you who you want to be, and something in you softens. Repeated, sincere listening can change your loyalties before you even notice it.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: दीप सिखा सम जुबति तन मन जनि होसि पतंग। भजहि राम तजि काम मद करहि सदा सतसंग ॥
translation: युवती स्त्रियों का शरीर दीपक की लौ के समान है, हे मन! तू उसका पतिंगा न बन। काम और मद को छोड़कर श्री रामचंद्रजी का भजन कर और सदा सत्संग कर ॥
english_translation: The body of a young woman is like a lamp flame; mind, do not become a moth. Leave desire and pride, worship Ram, and keep good company always.
essence: What dazzles you can destroy you; Ram and good company protect you.
simple_meaning: Don't let desire pull you toward what will burn you. Turn your mind toward Ram, drop pride and craving, and stay with good company.
insight: It shifts attention from seductive impulse to disciplined devotion and supportive surroundings.
modern_relevance: A message pops up, a photo catches your eye, and you feel the old pull to chase what looks exciting but leaves you emptier. This verse says: step back, choose what strengthens you, and stay in better company.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कुन्देन्दीवरसुन्दरावतिबलौ विज्ञानधामावुभौ शोभाढ्यौ वरधन्विनौ श्रुतिनुतौ गोविप्रवृन्दप्रियौ। मायामानुषरूपिणौ रघुवरौ सद्धर्मवर्मौ हितौ सीतान्वेषणतत्परौ पथिगतौ भक्तिप्रदौ तौ हि नः ॥
translation: कुन्दपुष्प और नीलकमल के समान सुंदर गौर एवं श्यामवर्ण, अत्यंत बलवान् , विज्ञान के धाम, शोभा संपन्न, श्रेष्ठ धनुर्धर, वेदों के द्वारा वन्दित, गौ एवं ब्राह्मणों के समूह के प्रिय (अथवा प्रेमी), माया से मनुष्य रूप धारण किए हुए, श्रेष्ठ धर्म के लिए कवचस्वरूप, सबके हितकारी, श्री सीताजी की खोज में लगे हुए, पथिक रूप रघुकुल के श्रेष्ठ श्री रामजी और श्री लक्ष्मणजी दोनों भाई निश्चय ही हमें भक्तिप्रद हों ॥
english_translation: May the two brothers, Ram and Lakshman, beautiful like a white lotus and a blue lotus, immensely strong, abodes of wisdom, richly radiant, best among archers, praised by the Vedas, dear to cows and learned priests, taking human form through the veil of appearance, protectors of righteous conduct, benefactors of all, eager to search for Sita, and walking the path, surely grant us devotion.
essence: Ram and Lakshman awaken devotion simply by who they are.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are praised as beautiful, strong, righteous, and devoted to finding Sita. The verse asks them to bless the reader with devotion.
insight: It teaches you to see devotion as contagious: noble action and noble presence can awaken it in others.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm strength changes the room before they speak. Their presence makes you want to be better, steadier, more devoted to what matters.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ब्रह्माम्भोधिसमुद्भवं कलिमलप्रध्वंसनं चाव्ययं श्रीमच्छम्भुमुखेन्दुसुन्दरवरे संशोभितं सर्वदा। संसारामयभेषजं सुखकरं श्रीजानकीजीवनं धन्यास्ते कृतिनः पिबन्ति सततं श्रीरामनामामृतम् ॥
translation: वे सुकृती (पुण्यात्मा पुरुष) धन्य हैं जो वेद रूपी समुद्र (के मथने) से उत्पन्न हुए कलियुग के मल को सर्वथा नष्ट कर देने वाले, अविनाशी, भगवान श्री शंभु के सुंदर एवं श्रेष्ठ मुख रूपी चंद्रमा में सदा शोभायमान, जन्म-मरण रूपी रोग के औषध, सबको सुख देने वाले और श्री जानकीजी के जीवनस्वरूप श्री राम नाम रूपी अमृत का निरंतर पान करते रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Blessed are those wise souls who continually drink the nectar of Ram's name — born from the churning of the Vedas, forever destroying the stains of the age of darkness, ever-shining in Shiva's beautiful moonlike mouth, the medicine for the disease of worldly suffering, and the source of joy for Janaki's beloved.
essence: Ram's name is the cure you can keep taking forever.
simple_meaning: Ram's name is described as a healing nectar. It removes the darkness of the age, brings joy, and is praised as something wise people keep drinking again and again.
insight: It shifts repetition from compulsion to nourishment, teaching you to return to what cleanses rather than what numbs.
modern_relevance: You keep opening the same app, the same chat, the same distraction, hoping it will soothe you. This verse points to a different repetition — one that actually restores you instead of draining you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मुक्ति जन्म महि जानि ग्यान खान अघ हानि कर। जहँ बस संभु भवानि सो कासी सेइअ कस न ॥
translation: जहाँ श्री शिव-पार्वती बसते हैं, उस काशी को मुक्ति की जन्मभूमि, ज्ञान की खान और पापों का नाश करने वाली जानकर उसका सेवन क्यों न किया जाए?
english_translation: Knowing Kashi as the birthplace of freedom, a mine of wisdom, and the destroyer of sins, why would you not serve it, where Shiva and Bhavani dwell?
essence: A place becomes priceless when it holds freedom, wisdom, and divine presence.
simple_meaning: Kashi is praised as a sacred place where Shiva and Bhavani live, and where freedom, wisdom, and cleansing from wrongdoing are found. Such a place deserves your reverence.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary geography to sacred presence and the transformation that comes from serving it.
modern_relevance: You walk into a temple courtyard after a brutal week, and your chest loosens before anyone speaks. Some places do not entertain you; they reset you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जरत सकल सुर बृंद बिषम गरल जेहिं पान किय। तेहि न भजसि मन मंद को कृपाल संकर सरिस॥
translation: जिस भीषण हलाहल विष से सब देवतागण जल रहे थे उसको जिन्होंने स्वयं पान कर लिया, रे मन्द मन! तू उन शंकरजी को क्यों नहीं भजता? उनके समान कृपालु (और) कौन है?
english_translation: Why don’t you worship Shankar, who drank the terrible poison that burned all the radiant beings? O dull mind, who is more compassionate than him?
essence: The one who carried poison for others deserves your worship.
simple_meaning: Shiva took the deadly poison for everyone’s sake, so the speaker asks why a dull mind would not worship him.
insight: It shifts devotion from abstract praise to recognising sacrificial care as the real measure of greatness.
modern_relevance: You remember the person who stayed up all night with the sick child, while everyone else slept. That kind of care changes how you trust someone.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: आगें चले बहुरि रघुराया। रिष्यमूक पर्बत निअराया॥ तहँ रह सचिव सहित सुग्रीवा। आवत देखि अतुल बल सींवा ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी फिर आगे चले। ऋष्यमूक पर्वत निकट आ गया। वहाँ (ऋष्यमूक पर्वत पर) मंत्रियों सहित सुग्रीव रहते थे। अतुलनीय बल की सीमा श्री रामचंद्रजी और लक्ष्मणजी को आते देखकर- ॥
english_translation: Raghunath moved ahead again. Rishyamuk Mountain came near. There Sugriva lived with his ministers. Seeing Ram and Lakshman coming, whose strength was unmatched—
essence: Arrival can begin the turning point before a single word is spoken.
simple_meaning: Ram moves closer to Rishyamuk Mountain, where Sugriva lives with his ministers. Sugriva sees Ram and Lakshman approaching, and their unmatched strength is immediately noticed.
insight: It sets the stage for alliance by showing that arrival itself can change the mood of a whole place.
modern_relevance: You spot the person you’ve been waiting to meet across a crowded station platform. Nothing has been said yet, but the moment already feels decisive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अति सभीत कह सुनु हनुमाना। पुरुष जुगल बल रूप निधाना॥ धरि बटु रूप देखु तैं जाई। कहेसु जानि जियँ सयन बुझाई ॥
translation: सुग्रीव अत्यंत भयभीत होकर बोले- हे हनुमान् ! सुनो, ये दोनों पुरुष बल और रूप के निधान हैं। तुम ब्रह्मचारी का रूप धारण करके जाकर देखो। अपने हृदय में उनकी यथार्थ बात जानकर मुझे इशारे से समझाकर कह देना ॥
english_translation: Sugriva, greatly afraid, said, “Listen, Hanuman. These two men are treasure-houses of strength and beauty. Go in the form of a celibate student, look at them, and understand their true nature in your heart; then tell me by sign.”
essence: Careful seeing comes before safe action.
simple_meaning: Sugriva, frightened, asks Hanuman to approach the two men in disguise, observe them carefully, understand who they really are, and report back silently.
insight: It shifts the mind from fearful assumption to careful observation before response.
modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with an unknown caller and your mind starts writing stories. Before you react, you check, listen, and understand what is actually there.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: पठए बालि होहिं मन मैला। भागौं तुरत तजौं यह सैला॥ बिप्र रूप धरि कपि तहँ गयऊ। माथ नाइ पूछत अस भयऊ ॥
translation: यदि वे मन के मलिन बालि के भेजे हुए हों तो मैं तुरंत ही इस पर्वत को छोड़कर भाग जाऊँ (यह सुनकर) हनुमान् जी ब्राह्मण का रूप धरकर वहाँ गए और मस्तक नवाकर इस प्रकार पूछने लगे- ॥
english_translation: If they are Bali's men, I will quickly flee this hill. Hanuman then took the form of a Brahmin, went there, bowed his head, and began to ask in fear.
essence: Careful disguise can open a door that fear would keep shut.
simple_meaning: Sugriva fears strangers and Hanuman goes to meet them in a harmless disguise. The verse shows caution, quick thinking, and careful approach.
insight: It teaches you to assess danger first, then approach with tact instead of raw suspicion.
modern_relevance: You spot two unfamiliar people at the edge of a tense meeting, and your first instinct is to protect yourself. The verse shows the value of cautious, respectful inquiry before you reveal too much.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: को तुम्ह स्यामल गौर सरीरा। छत्री रूप फिरहु बन बीरा ॥ कठिन भूमि कोमल पद गामी। कवन हेतु बिचरहु बन स्वामी ॥
translation: हे वीर! साँवले और गोरे शरीर वाले आप कौन हैं, जो क्षत्रिय के रूप में वन में फिर रहे हैं? हे स्वामी! कठोर भूमि पर कोमल चरणों से चलने वाले आप किस कारण वन में विचर रहे हैं? ॥
english_translation: O hero, who are you, with dark and fair bodies, wandering the forest in a warrior's form? O master, why do you move through the forest with soft feet on hard ground?
essence: A stranger's grace can make even fear pause and ask questions.
simple_meaning: Sugriva asks the strangers who they are, why they look so noble, and why they are walking in the forest like princes.
insight: It frames the meeting as cautious recognition, not instant trust.
modern_relevance: You notice someone polished and out of place in a rough situation, and your first instinct is to ask: who are they, really?
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: मृदुल मनोहर सुंदर गाता। सहत दुसह बन आतप बाता ॥ की तुम्ह तीनि देव महँ कोऊ। नर नारायन की तुम्ह दोऊ ॥
translation: मन को हरण करने वाले आपके सुंदर, कोमल अंग हैं और आप वन के दुःसह धूप और वायु को सह रहे हैं क्या आप ब्रह्मा, विष्णु, महेश- इन तीन देवताओं में से कोई हैं या आप दोनों नर और नारायण हैं ॥
english_translation: Your body is soft and beautiful, yet you endure the unbearable heat and wind of the forest. Are you one among the three radiant beings, or are you both Nara and Narayana?
essence: True greatness can look soft while enduring what breaks others.
simple_meaning: The speaker sees a stranger whose beautiful body is enduring the forest's harsh conditions and wonders whether he is a radiant being or a divine incarnation.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance alone to the quiet power that lets someone remain graceful under hardship.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who stays gentle under pressure, never showing the strain. Their steadiness makes you wonder what kind of strength they are drawing from.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: जग कारन तारन भव भंजन धरनी भार। की तुम्ह अखिल भुवन पति लीन्ह मनुज अवतार ॥
translation: अथवा आप जगत् के मूल कारण और संपूर्ण लोकों के स्वामी स्वयं भगवान् हैं, जिन्होंने लोगों को भवसागर से पार उतारने तथा पृथ्वी का भार नष्ट करने के लिए मनुष्य रूप में अवतार लिया है? ॥
english_translation: Or are you the original cause of the world, the lord of all worlds, who has taken human form to carry beings across the cycle of suffering and relieve the earth's burden?
essence: The divine may arrive looking entirely human.
simple_meaning: Hanuman wonders if this stranger is actually the supreme being who has taken human form to rescue beings and relieve the world's burden.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance to hidden divine identity in human form.
modern_relevance: You meet someone quiet in a crowded room, and something about them feels larger than their role. This verse captures that moment when respect turns into reverence.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: कोसलेस दसरथ के जाए। हम पितु बचन मानि बन आए॥ नाम राम लछिमन दोउ भाई। संग नारि सुकुमारि सुहाई ॥
translation: (श्री रामचंद्रजी ने कहा-) हम कोसलराज दशरथजी के पुत्र हैं और पिता का वचन मानकर वन आए हैं। हमारे राम-लक्ष्मण नाम हैं, हम दोनों भाई हैं। हमारे साथ सुंदर सुकुमारी स्त्री थी ॥
english_translation: We are Dasharath's sons from Kosala, and we came to the forest obeying our father's command. Our names are Ram and Lakshman, the two brothers. A beautiful, gentle woman was with us.
essence: Keeping your father's word can define your path more than a crown ever could.
simple_meaning: Ram identifies himself and Lakshman as Dasharath's sons who came to the forest because they obeyed their father's command, with Sita accompanying them.
insight: It shifts attention from self-presentation to faithful action under pressure.
modern_relevance: You leave for the airport with a packed bag and a heavy chest because you promised you would show up. No applause, no reward — just the weight of keeping your word.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: इहाँ हरी निसिचर बैदेही। बिप्र फिरहिं हम खोजत तेही॥ आपन चरित कहा हम गाई। कहहु बिप्र निज कथा बुझाई ॥
translation: यहाँ (वन में) राक्षस ने (मेरी पत्नी) जानकी को हर लिया। हे ब्राह्मण! हम उसे ही खोजते फिरते हैं। हमने तो अपना चरित्र कह सुनाया। अब हे ब्राह्मण! अपनी कथा समझाकर कहिए ॥
english_translation: Here in the forest, a demon has carried off Sita. We keep searching for her. We have told our own story; now, noble one, please tell us yours and help us understand.
essence: Loss can coexist with openness.
simple_meaning: Ram explains that Sita has been taken by a demon and that he is searching for her. He asks the stranger to share his own story too.
insight: It teaches you to name your situation plainly, without shutting down curiosity about the person in front of you.
modern_relevance: You meet someone at a train station while carrying private heartbreak. Even then, you can still speak honestly and invite the other person to be real too.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: प्रभु पहिचानि परेउ गहि चरना। सो सुख उमा जाइ नहिं बरना॥ पुलकित तन मुख आव न बचना। देखत रुचिर बेष कै रचना ॥
translation: प्रभु को पहचानकर हनुमान् जी उनके चरण पकड़कर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े (उन्होंने साष्टांग दंडवत् प्रणाम किया)। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे पार्वती! वह सुख वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। शरीर पुलकित है, मुख से वचन नहीं निकलता। वे प्रभु के सुंदर वेष की रचना देख रहे हैं! ॥
english_translation: Recognizing the Lord, he fell at his feet and held them fast. O Uma, that joy cannot be described. His body thrilled, his voice would not come, and he gazed at the Lord's beautiful form.
essence: Recognizing the Lord leaves you speechless and bowed.
simple_meaning: Hanuman recognizes Ram and falls at his feet in overwhelming joy. The sight leaves him speechless, trembling, and completely absorbed.
insight: It shifts devotion from thought to embodied response — recognition becomes humility, stillness, and praise.
modern_relevance: You meet someone you have admired from afar, and the room suddenly feels different. The rehearsed words disappear, and all that remains is awe, relief, and the urge to bow inwardly.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: पुनि धीरजु धरि अस्तुति कीन्ही। हरष हृदयँ निज नाथहि चीन्ही॥ मोर न्याउ मैं पूछा साईं। तुम्ह पूछहु कस नर की नाईं ॥
translation: फिर धीरज धर कर स्तुति की। अपने नाथ को पहचान लेने से हृदय में हर्ष हो रहा है। (फिर हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे स्वामी! मैंने जो पूछा वह मेरा पूछना तो न्याय था, (वर्षों के बाद आपको देखा, वह भी तपस्वी के वेष में और मेरी वानरी बुद्धि इससे मैं तो आपको पहचान न सका और अपनी परिस्थिति के अनुसार मैंने आपसे पूछा), परंतु आप मनुष्य की तरह कैसे पूछ रहे हैं? ॥
english_translation: After calming himself, he offered praise. Joy rose in his heart as he recognized his own Lord. "My question was fair, my Lord. But why are you asking like an ordinary man?"
essence: Knowing the Lord turns hesitation into praise.
simple_meaning: Hanuman calms himself, praises Ram, and feels joy at recognizing his own Lord. He then says his earlier question was reasonable, but Ram is speaking like an ordinary man.
insight: It shifts attention from social formality to reverent recognition of what is truly present.
modern_relevance: You finally understand the person in front of you is the one you were looking for. The tension drops, your chest opens, and even your awkward question feels forgiven.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: तव माया बस फिरउँ भुलाना। ताते मैं नहिं प्रभु पहिचाना ॥
translation: मैं तो आपकी माया के वश भूला फिरता हूँ इसी से मैंने अपने स्वामी (आप) को नहीं पहचाना ॥
english_translation: I wander lost under your veil of appearance, and because of that I did not recognize you, Lord.
essence: Confusion can hide even the one you most need to see.
simple_meaning: Hanuman admits that he failed to recognize Ram because he was caught in the divine veil of appearance and confusion.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame to humility, showing that clear seeing can arrive only when confusion is admitted.
modern_relevance: You stare at a message from someone you care about and still miss what they mean because your own confusion is louder. Sometimes the obstacle is not the person in front of you, but the haze you are carrying.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: एकु मैं मंद मोहबस कुटिल हृदय अग्यान। पुनि प्रभु मोहि बिसारेउ दीनबंधु भगवान ॥
translation: एक तो मैं यों ही मंद हूँ, दूसरे मोह के वश में हूँ, तीसरे हृदय का कुटिल और अज्ञान हूँ, फिर हे दीनबंधु भगवान् ! प्रभु (आप) ने भी मुझे भुला दिया! ॥
english_translation: I am dull, deluded, crooked of heart, and ignorant; and yet, O Lord of the lowly, you too have forgotten me.
essence: Even your forgetting cannot erase Ram's remembrance of you.
simple_meaning: Hanuman admits his own dullness, delusion, crooked heart, and ignorance, yet still says that Ram did not forget him.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to grateful trust in a mercy that outlasts your mistakes.
modern_relevance: You sent the apology after days of avoiding the message, convinced you had ruined everything. This verse says the deeper bond may still hold even when you feel unworthy.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: जदपि नाथ बहु अवगुन मोरें। सेवक प्रभुहि परै जनि भोरें॥ नाथ जीव तव मायाँ मोहा। सो निस्तरइ तुम्हारेहिं छोहा ॥
translation: एहे नाथ! यद्यपि मुझ में बहुत से अवगुण हैं, तथापि सेवक स्वामी की विस्मृति में न पड़े (आप उसे न भूल जाएँ)। हे नाथ! जीव आपकी माया से मोहित है। वह आप ही की कृपा से निस्तार पा सकता है ॥
english_translation: Even though I have many faults, Lord, do not let your servant be forgotten. Lord, a living being is deluded by your veil of appearance. That being can cross beyond only through your grace.
essence: Faults do not block grace; grace is what carries you through.
simple_meaning: Hanuman admits his faults and asks Ram not to forget him. He says every living being is confused by the veil of appearance and can cross beyond it only through Ram's grace.
insight: It shifts you from self-condemnation to humble reliance on grace.
modern_relevance: You miss the deadline, forget the message, and still feel ashamed to ask for help. This verse says your flaws do not cancel your worth; what lifts you out is still grace.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: ता पर मैं रघुबीर दोहाई। जानउँ नहिं कछु भजन उपाई॥ सेवक सुत पति मातु भरोसें। रहइ असोच बनइ प्रभु पोसें ॥
translation: उस पर हे रघुवीर! मैं आपकी दुहाई (शपथ) करके कहता हूँ कि मैं भजन-साधन कुछ नहीं जानता। सेवक स्वामी के और पुत्र माता के भरोसे निश्चिंत रहता है। प्रभु को सेवक का पालन-पोषण करते ही बनता है (करना ही पड़ता है) ॥
english_translation: Then, O Raghubir, I swear by you: I do not know any way of devotion. A servant rests in the trust of the master, a son in the trust of the mother. So the Lord must sustain the servant.
essence: Real devotion begins when you stop pretending you can carry yourself.
simple_meaning: Hanuman admits he does not know any special method of devotion. He says a servant lives by the master's care, just as a child lives by the mother's care.
insight: It shifts devotion from technique to dependence, from self-management to trust in Ram's care.
modern_relevance: You are sitting in the car outside the hospital, too tired to hold yourself together. This verse gives you permission to stop performing control and lean into care.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: अस कहि परेउ चरन अकुलाई। निज तनु प्रगटि प्रीति उर छाई॥ तब रघुपति उठाई उर लावा। निज लोचन जल सींचि जुड़ावा ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर हनुमान् जी अकुलाकर प्रभु के चरणों पर गिर पड़े, उन्होंने अपना असली शरीर प्रकट कर दिया। उनके हृदय में प्रेम छा गया। तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने उन्हें उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया और अपने नेत्रों के जल से सींचकर शीतल किया ॥
english_translation: Having said this, Hanuman fell in agitation at the Lord's feet. He revealed his true form, and love filled his heart. Then Raghupati lifted him into his arms, embraced him to his chest, and soothed him with the water of his own eyes.
essence: The one who falls in love with Ram is gathered, not rejected.
simple_meaning: Hanuman overflows with devotion and falls at Ram's feet. Ram responds with tenderness, lifting him up and comforting him like a beloved child.
insight: It shifts devotion from self-effacement to intimate belonging: surrender is met by embrace, not distance.
modern_relevance: After a hard apology, you expect cold silence. Instead, the person you feared most reaches out, holds your shoulder, and lets the tension break. That is the warmth this verse carries.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनु कपि जियँ मानसि जनि ऊना। तैं मम प्रिय लछिमन ते दूना॥ समदरसी मोहि कह सब कोऊ। सेवक प्रिय अनन्य गति सोऊ ॥
translation: (फिर कहा-) हे कपि! सुनो, मन में ग्लानि मत मानना (मन छोटा न करना)। तुम मुझे लक्ष्मण से भी दूने प्रिय हो। सब कोई मुझे समदर्शी कहते हैं (मेरे लिए न कोई प्रिय है न अप्रिय) पर मुझको सेवक प्रिय है, क्योंकि वह अनन्यगति होता है (मुझे छोड़कर उसको कोई दूसरा सहारा नहीं होता) ॥
english_translation: Listen, monkey, do not feel small in your heart. You are dearer to me than Lakshman. Everyone says I am equal to all, but I especially love the servant who has no other refuge.
essence: Single-hearted dependence draws the closest love.
simple_meaning: Ram reassures Hanuman that he should not feel lesser. He says Hanuman is even dearer to him than Lakshman, and that he especially values a servant who has nowhere else to turn.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to dependence: the less divided your refuge, the nearer you are held.
modern_relevance: You finally admit you don't have it all together, and someone answers with warmth instead of judgment. That is the kind of closeness this verse points to.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सो अनन्य जाकें असि मति न टरइ हनुमंत। मैं सेवक सचराचर रूप स्वामि भगवंत ॥
translation: और हे हनुमान् ! अनन्य वही है जिसकी ऐसी बुद्धि कभी नहीं टलती कि मैं सेवक हूँ और यह चराचर (जड़-चेतन) जगत् मेरे स्वामी भगवान् का रूप है ॥
english_translation: O Hanuman, only that person is truly devoted whose mind never wavers from this understanding: “I am the servant, and the moving and unmoving world is the form of the Lord.”
essence: One-pointed devotion sees everything as the Lord's form and the self as servant.
simple_meaning: True devotion stays steady in one insight: you are a servant, and everything around you belongs to the divine.
insight: It shifts identity from ownership to service, and from separation to sacred belonging.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room full of people, but the old habit still whispers, “How do I look?” This verse cuts through that noise: you are not the center, and nothing you meet is outside the divine.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: देखि पवनसुत पति अनुकूला। हृदयँ हरष बीती सब सूला॥ नाथ सैल पर कपिपति रहई। सो सुग्रीव दास तव अहई ॥
translation: स्वामी को अनुकूल (प्रसन्न) देखकर पवन कुमार हनुमान् जी के हृदय में हर्ष छा गया और उनके सब दुःख जाते रहे। (उन्होंने कहा-) हे नाथ! इस पर्वत पर वानरराज सुग्रीव रहते हैं, वह आपका दास है ॥
english_translation: Seeing his master favorable, Hanuman's heart filled with joy and all his sorrow vanished. He said, “Lord, on this mountain lives the king of the monkeys. Sugriva is your servant.”
essence: Grace received turns anxiety into clear, helpful action.
simple_meaning: Hanuman sees that Ram is kindly disposed toward him, and his grief disappears. Then he points out that Sugriva lives on the mountain and is Ram's servant.
insight: It shifts attention from self-protection to service once acceptance is felt.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room expecting judgment, but the first smile changes everything. The tension leaves your chest, and you can finally speak plainly.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: तेहि सन नाथ मयत्री कीजे। दीन जानि तेहि अभय करीजे॥ सो सीता कर खोज कराइहि। जहँ तहँ मरकट कोटि पठाइहि ॥
translation: हे नाथ! उससे मित्रता कीजिए और उसे दीन जानकर निर्भय कर दीजिए। वह सीताजी की खोज करवाएगा और जहाँ-तहाँ करोड़ों वानरों को भेजेगा ॥
english_translation: O Lord, make friendship with him and treat him as humble and fearless. He will arrange the search for Sita and send millions of monkeys everywhere.
essence: Trust the humble one, and hidden power begins to move.
simple_meaning: Treat Sugriva kindly and without fear. Once he feels safe, he will help search for Sita and send the monkey army everywhere.
insight: It shifts you from control to relationship: make the other person feel safe, and cooperation becomes possible.
modern_relevance: You meet someone guarded after a betrayal. Instead of pressing harder, you lower your voice, offer safety, and suddenly they start helping in ways you never expected.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: एहि बिधि सकल कथा समुझाई। लिए दुऔ जन पीठि चढ़ाई॥ जब सुग्रीवँ राम कहुँ देखा। अतिसय जन्म धन्य करि लेखा ॥
translation: इस प्रकार सब बातें समझाकर हनुमान् जी ने (श्री राम-लक्ष्मण) दोनों जनों को पीठ पर चढ़ा लिया। जब सुग्रीव ने श्री रामचंद्रजी को देखा तो अपने जन्म को अत्यंत धन्य समझा ॥
english_translation: In this way, Hanuman explained everything and carried both of them on his back. When Sugriva saw Ram, he felt that his birth had become truly blessed.
essence: Seeing Ram makes Sugriva’s whole life feel fulfilled.
simple_meaning: Hanuman carried Ram and Lakshman on his back to Sugriva. The moment Sugriva saw Ram, he felt his life had become blessed.
insight: It shifts attention from the journey to the transforming power of a single right encounter.
modern_relevance: You finally meet the person who can change everything, and your chest loosens before a single word is spoken. Recognition itself feels like grace.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सादर मिलेउ नाइ पद माथा। भेंटेउ अनुज सहित रघुनाथा॥ कपि कर मन बिचार एहि रीती। करिहहिं बिधि मो सन ए प्रीती ॥
translation: सुग्रीव चरणों में मस्तक नवाकर आदर सहित मिले। श्री रघुनाथजी भी छोटे भाई सहित उनसे गले लगकर मिले। सुग्रीव मन में इस प्रकार सोच रहे हैं कि हे विधाता! क्या ये मुझसे प्रीति करेंगे? ॥
english_translation: Sugriva bowed his head to the feet and met Ram with respect. Raghunath embraced him along with Lakshman. In his mind, the monkey king wondered, “Will they truly care for me?”
essence: Kindness can arrive before trust is fully ready to believe it.
simple_meaning: Sugriva bows respectfully to Ram, and Ram embraces him with Lakshman. Sugriva still wonders whether this kindness will last.
insight: It shows how trust often begins as a gesture before it becomes certainty.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems kind, but part of you still waits for the catch. The body relaxes before the mind does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब हनुमंत उभय दिसि की सब कथा सुनाइ। पावक साखी देइ करि जोरी प्रीति दृढ़ाइ ॥
translation: तब हनुमान् जी ने दोनों ओर की सब कथा सुनाकर अग्नि को साक्षी देकर परस्पर दृढ़ करके प्रीति जोड़ दी (अर्थात् अग्नि की साक्षी देकर प्रतिज्ञापूर्वक उनकी मैत्री करवा दी) ॥
english_translation: Then Hanuman told both sides the whole story and, taking fire as witness, firmly joined their friendship.
essence: Truth, spoken to both sides, can turn alliance into trust.
simple_meaning: Hanuman explains everything to both sides and uses fire as witness to seal their friendship.
insight: It shifts conflict resolution from partial loyalty to transparent, trust-building speech.
modern_relevance: You’re mediating between two friends who both feel wronged. Instead of choosing sides, you tell the whole story honestly until something solid can begin again.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: कीन्हि प्रीति कछु बीच न राखा। लछिमन राम चरित् सब भाषा॥ कह सुग्रीव नयन भरि बारी। मिलिहि नाथ मिथिलेसकुमारी ॥
translation: दोनों ने (हृदय से) प्रीति की, कुछ भी अंतर नहीं रखा। तब लक्ष्मणजी ने श्री रामचंद्रजी का सारा इतिहास कहा। सुग्रीव ने नेत्रों में जल भरकर कहा- हे नाथ! मिथिलेशकुमारी जानकीजी मिल जाएँगी ॥
english_translation: They shared friendship with nothing held back. Then Lakshman recounted all of Ram's story. With tears in his eyes, Sugriva said, "My lord, Janaki of Mithila will be found."
essence: Friendship deepens when both sides stop holding anything back.
simple_meaning: The friendship between Ram's group and Sugriva becomes complete and open. Lakshman tells Ram's story, and Sugriva, moved to tears, says Sita will be found.
insight: It shifts relationship from formal alliance to shared feeling and mutual trust.
modern_relevance: You finally speak honestly with someone after weeks of careful distance. The conversation changes everything, not because of strategy, but because both hearts are now open.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंत्रिन्ह सहित इहाँ एक बारा। बैठ रहेउँ मैं करत बिचारा॥ गगन पंथ देखी मैं जाता। परबस परी बहुत बिलपाता ॥
translation: मैं एक बार यहाँ मंत्रियों के साथ बैठा हुआ कुछ विचार कर रहा था। तब मैंने पराए (शत्रु) के वश में पड़ी बहुत विलाप करती हुई सीताजी को आकाश मार्ग से जाते देखा था ॥
english_translation: I was once sitting here with my ministers, thinking. Then I saw Sita, weeping helplessly, being carried through the sky.
essence: Seeing helpless suffering makes all other concerns shrink.
simple_meaning: Sugriva recalls sitting in counsel when he saw Sita being carried helplessly through the sky, crying in misery.
insight: It shifts attention from strategy to urgency when suffering is seen directly.
modern_relevance: You’re in a meeting, trying to sort out practical next steps, when a message arrives that someone you care about is in obvious distress. Everything else drops away.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: राम राम हा राम पुकारी। हमहि देखि दीन्हेउ पट डारी॥ मागा राम तुरत तेहिं दीन्हा। पट उर लाइ सोच अति कीन्हा ॥
translation: हमें देखकर उन्होंने 'राम! राम! हा राम!' पुकारकर वस्त्र गिरा दिया था। श्री रामजी ने उसे माँगा, तब सुग्रीव ने तुरंत ही दे दिया। वस्त्र को हृदय से लगाकर रामचंद्रजी ने बहुत ही सोच किया ॥
english_translation: Seeing us, he cried, 'Ram! Ram! Ha Ram!' and dropped the cloth. When Ram asked for it, Sugriva gave it at once. Ram pressed the cloth to his heart and fell into deep thought.
essence: A humble offering becomes precious when love is present.
simple_meaning: Sugriva is so moved by Ram's presence that he cries out and offers a cloth immediately. Ram receives it and falls into thought.
insight: It shows how devotion turns even a simple object into a sign of deep connection.
modern_relevance: You hand someone a note, a scarf, or a keepsake, and they hold it like it matters more than the object itself. Some gestures carry the whole weight of trust.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह सुग्रीव सुनहु रघुबीरा। तजहु सोच मन आनहु धीरा॥ सब प्रकार करिहउँ सेवकाई। जेहि बिधि मिलिहि जानकी आई ॥
translation: सुग्रीव ने कहा- हे रघुवीर! सुनिए। सोच छोड़ दीजिए और मन में धीरज लाइए। मैं सब प्रकार से आपकी सेवा करूँगा, जिस उपाय से जानकीजी आकर आपको मिलें ॥
english_translation: Sugriva said, "Listen, Raghubir. Let go of sorrow and bring steadiness to your mind. I will serve you in every way, by whatever means Sita may come to you."
essence: True alliance says: calm down, and let me carry the search with you.
simple_meaning: Sugriva asks Ram to stop worrying and stay calm. He promises full service until Sita is found and brought back.
insight: It shifts devotion from sympathy into active help: calming another person and taking responsibility for the next step.
modern_relevance: You’re spiraling after a painful text, and a friend says, “Breathe. I’m with you. We’ll handle this.” That is Sugriva’s role here.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: सखा बचन सुनि हरषे कृपासिंधु बलसींव। कारन कवन बसहु बन मोहि कहहु सुग्रीव ॥
translation: कृपा के समुद्र और बल की सीमा श्री रामजी सखा सुग्रीव के वचन सुनकर हर्षित हुए। (और बोले-) हे सुग्रीव! मुझे बताओ, तुम वन में किस कारण रहते हो? ॥
english_translation: Saying this, the ocean of compassion and strength rejoiced. "Friend Sugriva, tell me: why do you live in the forest?"
essence: Compassion begins by asking the right question.
simple_meaning: Ram is pleased by Sugriva's words and asks why Sugriva is living in the forest.
insight: It shifts attention from surface talk to the wound that needs attention.
modern_relevance: Someone finally sits across from you and asks, not what happened in the meeting, but what happened to you. That one honest question can change everything.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: नाथ बालि अरु मैं द्वौ भाइ। प्रीति रही कछु बरनि न जाई॥ मयसुत मायावी तेहि नाऊँ। आवा सो प्रभु हमरें गाऊँ ॥
translation: (सुग्रीव ने कहा-) हे नाथ! बालि और मैं दो भाई हैं, हम दोनों में ऐसी प्रीति थी कि वर्णन नहीं की जा सकती। हे प्रभो! मय दानव का एक पुत्र था, उसका नाम मायावी था। एक बार वह हमारे गाँव में आया ॥
english_translation: —Sugriva said— "O Lord, Bali and I were two brothers. The love between us cannot be described. O Lord, there was a son of Maya named Mayavi. He came once to our village."
essence: A broken brotherhood hurts most because it once held real love.
simple_meaning: Sugriva recalls that he and Bali were once very close brothers, and he begins explaining how the trouble started when Mayavi came to their village.
insight: It shifts attention from the quarrel itself to the earlier bond that made the loss so painful.
modern_relevance: You can be speaking to someone who wants the whole truth, yet still find yourself circling the wound that changed everything. Old family pain rarely starts with hatred; it starts with love that got broken.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: अर्ध राति पुर द्वार पुकारा। बाली रिपु बल सहै न पारा॥ धावा बालि देखि सो भागा। मैं पुनि गयउँ बंधु सँग लागा ॥
translation: उसने आधी रात को नगर के फाटक पर आकर पुकारा (ललकारा)। बालि शत्रु के बल (ललकार) को सह नहीं सका। वह दौड़ा, उसे देखकर मायावी भागा। मैं भी भाई के संग लगा चला गया ॥
english_translation: He came shouting at the city gate in the middle of the night. Bali could not bear the enemy's challenge. Bali ran after him; seeing him, the illusionist fled. I too went along with my brother.
essence: Loyalty can drag you into danger before you understand it.
simple_meaning: Sugriva describes how Bali chased the stranger who challenged him at night, and how Sugriva followed his brother.
insight: It sets up the betrayal that made Sugriva afraid and displaced, preparing the case for Ram's help.
modern_relevance: A friend pulls you into a fight you never wanted, and suddenly you are running on loyalty instead of choice. Later, all you can do is explain how it started.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: गिरिबर गुहाँ पैठ सो जाई। तब बालीं मोहि कहा बुझाई॥ परिखेसु मोहि एक पखवारा। नहिं आवौं तब जानेसु मारा ॥
translation: वह मायावी एक पर्वत की गुफा में जा घुसा। तब बालि ने मुझे समझाकर कहा- तुम एक पखवाड़े (पंद्रह दिन) तक मेरी बाट देखना। यदि मैं उतने दिनों में न आऊँ तो जान लेना कि मैं मारा गया ॥
english_translation: He entered a mountain cave. Then Bali told me, "Wait for me for half a month. If I do not return by then, know that I have been killed."
essence: A promise to return can become a weapon when fear enters the waiting.
simple_meaning: Sugriva recalls how Bali entered a cave and told him to wait fifteen days. If Bali did not return, Sugriva was to assume Bali had died.
insight: It shows how a delayed return can turn hope into anxiety and suspicion.
modern_relevance: You wait outside a hospital room while someone says, "I'll be back soon," and the silence stretches into dread. A simple promise can become the hinge of your whole trust.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: मास दिवस तहँ रहेउँ खरारी। निसरी रुधिर धार तहँ भारी॥ बालि हतेसि मोहि मारिहि आई। सिला देइ तहँ चलेउँ पराई ॥
translation: हे खरारि! मैं वहाँ महीने भर तक रहा। वहाँ (उस गुफा में से) रक्त की बड़ी भारी धारा निकली। तब (मैंने समझा कि) उसने बालि को मार डाला, अब आकर मुझे मारेगा, इसलिए मैं वहाँ (गुफा के द्वार पर) एक शिला लगाकर भाग आया ॥
english_translation: O Kharaari, I stayed there for a month. A great stream of blood flowed out from there. Then I thought, "He has killed Bali and will come to kill me," so I placed a stone there and fled.
essence: Fear fills gaps with disaster and pushes you into flight.
simple_meaning: Sugriva says he waited a month in the cave, saw a stream of blood, feared Bali had been killed and would return to kill him, and so he sealed the cave and fled.
insight: It shows how quickly the mind turns partial signs into certainty and then acts from panic.
modern_relevance: You get one alarming text, see one unfinished email thread, and your mind writes the worst ending before the facts are clear.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: मंत्रिन्ह पुर देखा बिनु साईं। दीन्हेउ मोहि राज बरिआईं॥ बाली ताहि मारि गृह आवा। देखि मोहि जियँ भेद बढ़ावा ॥
translation: मंत्रियों ने नगर को बिना स्वामी (राजा) का देखा, तो मुझको जबर्दस्ती राज्य दे दिया। बालि उसे मारकर घर आ गया। मुझे (राजसिंहासन पर) देखकर उसने जी में भेद बढ़ाया (बहुत ही विरोध माना)। (उसने समझा कि यह राज्य के लोभ से ही गुफा के द्वार पर शिला दे आया था, जिससे मैं बाहर न निकल सकूँ और यहाँ आकर राजा बन बैठा) ॥
english_translation: The ministers saw the city without a ruler and forcibly gave me the kingdom. Bali killed him and came home. Seeing me on the throne, he grew deeply suspicious and thought I had left the cave door sealed out of greed for power.
essence: A rightful placement can look like greed to a wounded mind.
simple_meaning: Sugriva says he was made king when the city was left without a ruler, but Bali misread that as greed and became suspicious.
insight: It shows how power, fear, and suspicion can turn a practical decision into a moral accusation.
modern_relevance: You finally step into a role after someone disappears, and the returning person assumes you schemed for it. Misunderstanding hardens instantly.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: रिपु सम मोहि मारेसि अति भारी। हरि लीन्हसि सर्बसु अरु नारी॥ ताकें भय रघुबीर कृपाला सकल भुवन मैं फिरेउँ बिहाला ॥
translation: उसने मुझे शत्रु के समान बहुत अधिक मारा और मेरा सर्वस्व तथा मेरी स्त्री को भी छीन लिया। हे कृपालु रघुवीर! मैं उसके भय से समस्त लोकों में बेहाल होकर फिरता रहा ॥
english_translation: He struck me terribly, like an enemy, and took away all my wealth and my wife. O compassionate Raghubir, I wandered through all the worlds in misery, afraid of him.
essence: Fear turns a single injury into a whole life of exile.
simple_meaning: Sugriva says Vali beat him badly, took his wife and kingdom, and left him wandering in fear everywhere.
insight: It shows how trauma traps attention in threat, making the whole world feel unsafe.
modern_relevance: After one humiliating betrayal, you start checking doors, rereading messages, and expecting the worst from everyone. Fear can keep you living in exile long after the event is over.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: इहाँ साप बस आवत नाहीं। तदपि सभीत रहउँ मन माहीं॥ सुन सेवक दुःख दीनदयाला फरकि उठीं द्वै भुजा बिसाला ॥
translation: वह शाप के कारण यहाँ नहीं आता, तो भी मैं मन में भयभीत रहता हूँ। सेवक का दुःख सुनकर दीनों पर दया करने वाले श्री रघुनाथजी की दोनों विशाल भुजाएँ फड़क उठीं ॥
english_translation: He does not come here because of the curse, yet I still remain afraid in my mind. Hearing the grief of a servant, the arms of the compassionate Raghunath trembled.
essence: Fear can remain in the mind even after danger has passed.
simple_meaning: Sugriva says that even though Bali cannot come here because of a curse, fear still lives in his mind. When Ram hears a servant's pain, his powerful arms stir with compassion.
insight: It shifts attention from abstract safety to the lived reality of fear and the healing force of immediate compassion.
modern_relevance: You know the person is blocked from reaching you, yet your body still stays tense. Then someone you trust hears your pain and instantly moves to help. That contrast is this verse.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: सुनु सुग्रीव मारिहउँ बालिहि एकहिं बान। ब्रह्म रुद्र सरनागत गएँ न उबरिहिं प्रान ॥
translation: (उन्होंने कहा-) हे सुग्रीव! सुनो, मैं एक ही बाण से बालि को मार डालूँगा। ब्रह्मा और रुद्र की शरण में जाने पर भी उसके प्राण न बचेंगे ॥
english_translation: Saying, "Listen, Sugriva: I will kill Bali with a single arrow. Even if he seeks refuge in Brahma and Rudra, his life will not be saved."
essence: True refuge is not in escape, but in Ram's protection.
simple_meaning: Ram promises Sugriva that he will kill Bali with one arrow, and no refuge will save Bali from that fate.
insight: It shifts the mind from helplessness to trust in decisive protection.
modern_relevance: You are backing a friend who has been cornered by a bully and every excuse has already failed. A clear promise from someone steady can change panic into courage.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जे न मित्र दुख होहिं दुखारी। तिन्हहि बिलोकत पातक भारी॥ निज दुख गिरि सम रज करि जाना। मित्रक दुख रज मेरु समाना ॥
translation: जो लोग मित्र के दुःख से दुःखी नहीं होते, उन्हें देखने से ही बड़ा पाप लगता है। अपने पर्वत के समान दुःख को धूल के समान और मित्र के धूल के समान दुःख को सुमेरु (बड़े भारी पर्वत) के समान जाने ॥
english_translation: Those who do not feel sorrow at a friend's sorrow are deeply blameworthy to even look upon. Treat your own mountain-sized grief as dust, and your friend's dust-sized grief as Mount Sumeru.
essence: True friendship makes your friend's pain heavier than your own.
simple_meaning: Real friendship means feeling your friend's pain as your own and shrinking your own suffering in comparison.
insight: It shifts friendship from polite concern to shared burden and shared feeling.
modern_relevance: Your best friend texts at 1am from a hospital waiting room, and you answer with advice instead of presence. This verse asks for something harder: let their pain matter to you more than your own discomfort.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जिन्ह कें असि मति सहज न आई। ते सठ कत हठि करत मिताई॥ कुपथ निवारि सुपंथ चलावा। गुन प्रगटै अवगुनन्हि दुरावा ॥
translation: जिन्हें स्वभाव से ही ऐसी बुद्धि प्राप्त नहीं है, वे मूर्ख हठ करके क्यों किसी से मित्रता करते हैं? मित्र का धर्म है कि वह मित्र को बुरे मार्ग से रोककर अच्छे मार्ग पर चलावे। उसके गुण प्रकट करे और अवगुणों को छिपावे ॥
english_translation: Those who do not naturally have this kind of wisdom—why do they stubbornly call it friendship? A true friend turns you away from the wrong road and leads you to the right one. They reveal your virtues and hide your faults.
essence: True friendship protects your best path, not your ego.
simple_meaning: A real friend does not flatter you. They stop you from going wrong, guide you toward what is right, and protect your good qualities.
insight: It shifts friendship from approval-seeking to moral care: a friend helps you choose better, not just feel better.
modern_relevance: You text the friend who tells you the uncomfortable truth before you make the mistake. The one who protects your best self is worth more than the one who only agrees.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: देत लेत मन संक न धरई। बल अनुमान सदा हित करई॥ बिपति काल कर सतगुन नेहा। श्रुति कह संत मित्र गुन एहा ॥
translation: देने-लेने में मन में शंका न रखे। अपने बल के अनुसार सदा हित ही करता रहे। विपत्ति के समय तो सदा सौगुना स्नेह करे। वेद कहते हैं कि संत (श्रेष्ठ) मित्र के गुण (लक्षण) ये हैं ॥
english_translation: Keep no doubt in giving or receiving. Always do what is helpful within your power. In hardship, multiply your affection a hundredfold. The Vedas say these are the qualities of a true friend.
essence: True friendship gives more when life gets harder.
simple_meaning: A true friend gives and receives without suspicion, helps within their ability, and becomes even more loving when trouble comes.
insight: It shifts friendship from exchange to steadfast care, especially when the other person is in pain.
modern_relevance: You answered a late-night call from a friend who was falling apart, even though you were exhausted. You didn't tally effort or ask what you'd get back. That is the kind of loyalty this verse praises.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: आगें कह मृदु बचन बनाई। पाछें अनहित मन कुटिलाई॥ जाकर िचत अहि गति सम भाई। अस कुमित्र परिहरेहिं भलाई ॥
translation: जो सामने तो बना-बनाकर कोमल वचन कहता है और पीठ-पीछे बुराई करता है तथा मन में कुटिलता रखता है- हे भाई! (इस तरह) जिसका मन साँप की चाल के समान टेढ़ा है, ऐसे कुमित्र को तो त्यागने में ही भलाई है ॥
english_translation: If someone speaks sweetly in front but hides harm behind your back, and their mind twists like a snake's path, it is better to leave such a false friend.
essence: A friend who hides harm is safer left behind.
simple_meaning: A false friend may speak gently in front of you while planning harm behind your back. The wise choice is to let that person go.
insight: It teaches you to judge friendship by consistency, not charm, and to step back from relationships that conceal harm.
modern_relevance: You notice a friend praising you in the group chat, then quietly undermining you in private. The sting is not just the betrayal — it is realizing you kept calling it loyalty.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सेवक सठ नृप कृपन कुनारी। कपटी मित्र सूल सम चारी॥ सखा सोच त्यागहु बल मोरें। सब बिधि घटब काज मैं तोरें ॥
translation: मूर्ख सेवक, कंजूस राजा, कुलटा स्त्री और कपटी मित्र- ये चारों शूल के समान पीड़ा देने वाले हैं। हे सखा! मेरे बल पर अब तुम चिंता छोड़ दो। मैं सब प्रकार से तुम्हारे काम आऊँगा (तुम्हारी सहायता करूँगा) ॥
english_translation: A foolish servant, a miserly king, an unchaste woman, and a deceitful friend — these four are like spears of pain. O friend, now drop your worry; with my strength, I will handle everything for you.
essence: True friendship replaces fear with help.
simple_meaning: A deceitful friend hurts like a spear, but a true friend removes fear and takes care of your task with full support.
insight: It shifts friendship from social closeness to dependable support under pressure.
modern_relevance: You finally tell a trusted friend what is overwhelming you, and they don’t flinch. They don’t just listen — they step in. That is the relief Sugriva offers here.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: कह सुग्रीव सुनहु रघुबीरा। बालि महाबल अति रनधीरा॥ दुंदुभि अस्थि ताल देखराए। बिनु प्रयास रघुनाथ ढहाए ॥
translation: सुग्रीव ने कहा- हे रघुवीर! सुनिए, बालि महान् बलवान् और अत्यंत रणधीर है। फिर सुग्रीव ने श्री रामजी को दुंदुभि राक्षस की हड्डियाँ व ताल के वृक्ष दिखलाए। श्री रघुनाथजी ने उन्हें बिना ही परिश्रम के (आसानी से) ढहा दिया।
english_translation: Sugriva said, "Listen, Raghubira: Bali is immensely powerful and fierce in battle. I showed you the bones of the demon Dundubhi and the palm trees, and Ragunath toppled them without effort."
essence: Real power proves itself without strain.
simple_meaning: Sugriva points to Bali's huge strength, then reminds Ram how easily he knocked down Dundubhi's bones and palm trees. The message is clear: Ram's power is enough for the coming fight.
insight: It shifts you from fear of the challenge to confidence in tested capability.
modern_relevance: Before a high-stakes interview, you replay the one presentation where you handled pressure beautifully. That memory steadies you. Sugriva is doing the same for Ram: proving readiness through evidence.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: देखि अमित बल बाढ़ी प्रीती। बालि बधब इन्ह भइ परतीती॥ बार-बार नावइ पद सीसा। प्रभुहि जानि मन हरष कपीसा ॥
translation: श्री रामजी का अपरिमित बल देखकर सुग्रीव की प्रीति बढ़ गई और उन्हें विश्वास हो गया कि ये बालि का वध अवश्य करेंगे। वे बार-बार चरणों में सिर नवाने लगे। प्रभु को पहचानकर सुग्रीव मन में हर्षित हो रहे थे ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ram's immeasurable strength, Sugriva's love grew and he became convinced that Ram would surely kill Bali. Again and again he bowed his head at Ram's feet, and knowing the Lord, the king of monkeys felt joy in his heart.
essence: Seeing true strength makes trust effortless.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram's power, Sugriva trusted him more and bowed again and again in joy.
insight: It shifts trust from hope to recognition, and turns reverence into joyful surrender.
modern_relevance: You watch someone handle the crisis you were dreading, and your chest finally loosens. The proof isn't in promises anymore — it's in what they can actually do.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उपजा ग्यान बचन तब बोला। नाथ कृपाँ मन भयउ अलोला॥ सुख संपति परिवार बड़ाई। सब परिहरि करिहउँ सेवकाई ॥
translation: जब ज्ञान उत्पन्न हुआ तब वे ये वचन बोले कि हे नाथ! आपकी कृपा से अब मेरा मन स्थिर हो गया। सुख, संपत्ति, परिवार और बड़ाई (बड़प्पन) सबको त्यागकर मैं आपकी सेवा ही करूँगा ॥
english_translation: When understanding arose, he spoke these words: “Lord, by your grace my mind has become steady. Leaving behind comfort, wealth, family, and status, I will serve you alone.”
essence: Grace makes every other claim on you feel smaller.
simple_meaning: Sugriva says that by Ram's grace his mind is calm, and he will give up comfort, wealth, family, and status to serve Ram.
insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to a complete reordering of life around service.
modern_relevance: You finally realize the promotion, the praise, and the polished image were never the center of your life. Something deeper has settled, and you want to serve what matters.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: ए सब राम भगति के बाधक। कहहिं संत तव पद अवराधक॥ सत्रु मित्र सुख, दुख जग माहीं। मायाकृत परमारथ नाहीं ॥
translation: क्योंकि आपके चरणों की आराधना करने वाले संत कहते हैं कि ये सब (सुख-संपत्ति आदि) राम भक्ति के विरोधी हैं। जगत् में जितने भी शत्रु-मित्र और सुख-दुःख (आदि द्वंद्व) हैं, सब के सब मायारचित हैं, परमार्थतः (वास्तव में) नहीं हैं ॥
english_translation: Because saints who worship your feet say that these things are obstacles to Ram's devotion. In this world, enemies and friends, pleasure and pain are all made by illusion; in ultimate reality, they are not real.
essence: The world’s opposites lose power when devotion becomes your center.
simple_meaning: Saints say that comfort, status, friends, enemies, pleasure, and pain all distract from devotion. These opposites belong to appearance, not ultimate reality.
insight: It shifts attention away from emotional opposites and toward what remains steady beneath them.
modern_relevance: You get praised at work one day and ignored the next. A friend cheers you, then disappoints you. This verse says both swings are temporary patterns, not the center of your life.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: बालि परम हित जासु प्रसादा। मिलेहु राम तुम्ह समन बिषादा॥ सपनें जेहि सन होइ लराई। जागें समुझत मन सकुचाई ॥
translation: हे श्री रामजी! बालि तो मेरा परम हितकारी है, जिसकी कृपा से शोक का नाश करने वाले आप मुझे मिले और जिसके साथ अब स्वप्न में भी लड़ाई हो तो जागने पर उसे समझकर मन में संकोच होगा (कि स्वप्न में भी मैं उससे क्यों लड़ा) ॥
english_translation: Bali is my greatest well-wisher, by whose grace I met you, Ram, the remover of sorrow. Even a dream-fight with him would make my heart hesitate in shame when I wake.
essence: Even your worst conflict can become the road to grace.
simple_meaning: Sugriva says Bali is still his greatest benefactor, because the conflict with Bali led him to Ram. Even the memory of fighting Bali now feels shameful to him.
insight: It shifts you from blaming the wound to noticing the help hidden inside it.
modern_relevance: You look back at a breakup, a firing, or a humiliating argument and realise it pushed you toward the people who truly changed your life.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: अब प्रभु कृपा करहु एहि भाँति। सब तजि भजनु करौं दिन राती॥ सुनि बिराग संजुत कपि बानी। बोले बिहँसि रामु धनुपानी ॥
translation: हे प्रभो अब तो इस प्रकार कृपा कीजिए कि सब छोड़कर दिन-रात मैं आपका भजन ही करूँ। सुग्रीव की वैराग्ययुक्त वाणी सुनकर (उसके क्षणिक वैराग्य को देखकर) हाथ में धनुष धारण करने वाले श्री रामजी मुस्कुराकर बोले- ॥
english_translation: “O Lord, now grant me this grace: let me leave everything and spend day and night in your devotion.” Hearing the monkey’s words of renunciation, bow in hand, Ram smiled and spoke.
essence: Renunciation becomes complete when it turns into love.
simple_meaning: Sugriva asks for grace to give up everything else and spend day and night in devotion. Ram hears the sincere longing and smiles at the words.
insight: It shifts the mind from scattered wanting to single-hearted devotion.
modern_relevance: You finally stop chasing the next promotion, the next distraction, the next excuse — and realize you want a life that actually points somewhere. That quiet turn is what this verse honors.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: जो कछु कहेहु सत्य सब सोई। सखा बचन मम मृषा न होई॥ नट मरकट इव सबहि नचावत। रामु खगेस बेद अस गावत ॥
translation: तुमने जो कुछ कहा है, वह सभी सत्य है, परंतु हे सखा! मेरा वचन मिथ्या नहीं होता (अर्थात् बालि मारा जाएगा और तुम्हें राज्य मिलेगा)। (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं कि-) हे पक्षियों के राजा गरुड़! नट (मदारी) के बंदर की तरह श्री रामजी सबको नचाते हैं, वेद ऐसा कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Whatever you have said is entirely true, friend; my word is never false. Like a puppeteer making monkeys dance, Ram moves everyone, as the Vedas declare.
essence: Ram's promise is true, and everything moves in his hands.
simple_meaning: Ram reassures Sugriva that his promise is true, then teaches that Ram moves all beings just as a puppeteer moves monkeys.
insight: It shifts you from anxious self-management to trust in a larger, reliable order.
modern_relevance: You finally tell the one person you trust what you need, and they answer without hesitation. The relief is not just in their promise — it's in knowing the whole situation is held by something steadier than your fear.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: लै सुग्रीव संग रघुनाथा। चले चाप सायक गहि हाथा॥ तब रघुपति सुग्रीव पठावा। गर्जेसि जाइ निकट बल पावा ॥
translation: तदनन्तर सुग्रीव को साथ लेकर और हाथों में धनुष-बाण धारण करके श्री रघुनाथजी चले। तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने सुग्रीव को बालि के पास भेजा। वह श्री रामजी का बल पाकर बालि के निकट जाकर गरजा ॥
english_translation: Then, taking Sugriva along, Raghunath set out with bow and arrows in hand. Then Raghupati sent Sugriva near Bali, and Sugriva, empowered by Ram's strength, went close and roared.
essence: Ram's backing makes Sugriva bold enough to face Bali.
simple_meaning: Ram and Sugriva move toward Bali together. Ram arms himself, sends Sugriva forward, and Sugriva confronts Bali with Ram's strength behind him.
insight: It turns private support into public courage and moves the ally from promise to action.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hard conversation with someone backing you up. Their presence changes your voice before you even speak.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनत बालि क्रोधातुर धावा। गहि कर चरन नारि समुझावा॥ सुनु पति जिन्हहि मिलेउ सुग्रीवा। ते द्वौ बंधु तेज बल सींवा ॥
translation: बालि सुनते ही क्रोध में भरकर वेग से दौड़ा। उसकी स्त्री तारा ने चरण पकड़कर उसे समझाया कि हे नाथ! सुनिए, सुग्रीव जिनसे मिले हैं वे दोनों भाई तेज और बल की सीमा हैं ॥
english_translation: As soon as Bali heard it, he rushed out in a rage. His wife Tara caught his feet and tried to warn him: "Listen, my lord. The two brothers whom Sugriva has joined are beyond measure in valor and strength."
essence: Anger can outrun wisdom even when danger is plain.
simple_meaning: Bali hears the news and charges forward in anger, while Tara tries to stop him by warning that Sugriva has joined two brothers of immense power.
insight: It shows how rage blinds judgment and how warning is wasted on a heated mind.
modern_relevance: You get one text, feel insulted, and fire back before reading the whole message. The calmer voice beside you sees the danger, but anger has already started driving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोसलेस सुत लछिमन रामा। कालहु जीति सकहिं संग्रामा ॥
translation: वे कोसलाधीश दशरथजी के पुत्र राम और लक्ष्मण संग्राम में काल को भी जीत सकते हैं ॥
english_translation: Rama and Lakshmana, sons of King Dasharatha of Kosala, can defeat even death in battle.
essence: Some courage is so complete that even death yields.
simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana are so powerful in battle that even death cannot stand against them.
insight: It frames courage as a power that can face even death without hesitation.
modern_relevance: Before a hard conversation, you feel your chest tighten because the stakes are real. This verse meets that moment with steadiness: some people enter conflict with such force and clarity that fear itself loses.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह बाली सुनु भीरु प्रिय समदरसी रघुनाथ। जौं कदाचि मोहि मारहिं तौ पुनि होउँ सनाथ ॥
translation: बालि ने कहा- हे भीरु! (डरपोक) प्रिये! सुनो, श्री रघुनाथजी समदर्शी हैं। जो कदाचित् वे मुझे मारेंगे ही तो मैं सनाथ हो जाऊँगा (परमपद पा जाऊँगा) ॥
english_translation: Bali said, “Listen, dear and timid one: Raghunath sees all beings equally. If he should kill me, I will at last be truly sheltered.”
essence: Even death becomes refuge in the hands of one who sees equally.
simple_meaning: Bali recognizes that Ram judges no one by bias. Even if Ram kills him, Bali believes that death will bring him shelter, not ruin.
insight: It shifts the mind from fear of punishment to trust in fair seeing.
modern_relevance: When someone you respect corrects you sharply, your first reaction is to defend yourself. But sometimes the harder truth is also the safer one: being honestly seen can be a kind of rescue.
speaker: Bali

verse_text: अस कहि चला महा अभिमानी। तृन समान सुग्रीवहि जानी॥ भिरे उभौ बाली अति तर्जा। मुठिका मारि महाधुनि गर्जा ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर वह महान् अभिमानी बालि सुग्रीव को तिनके के समान जानकर चला। दोनों भिड़ गए। बालि ने सुग्रीव को बहुत धमकाया और घूँसा मारकर बड़े जोर से गरजा ॥
english_translation: Saying this, the greatly arrogant Bali went on, seeing Sugriva as no more than a blade of grass. The two clashed; Bali threatened Sugriva fiercely, struck him with a fist, and roared loudly.
