essence: Pride makes an opponent seem smaller than human.
simple_meaning: Bali, full of pride, treats Sugriva as nothing and attacks him. The fight begins with threats, a blow, and a furious roar.
insight: It shows how arrogance turns conflict into humiliation before the fight is even over.
modern_relevance: A heated argument starts when someone decides the other person doesn't matter. The insult comes first; the blow, whether spoken or physical, follows.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब सुग्रीव बिकल होइ भागा। मुष्टि प्रहार बज्र सम लागा॥ मैं जो कहा रघुबीर कृपाला। बंधु न होइ मोर यह काला ॥
translation: तब सुग्रीव व्याकुल होकर भागा। घूँसे की चोट उसे वज्र के समान लगी (सुग्रीव ने आकर कहा-) हे कृपालु रघुवीर! मैंने आपसे पहले ही कहा था कि बालि मेरा भाई नहीं है, काल है ॥
english_translation: Then Sugriva, overwhelmed, fled. The blow of the fist struck like a thunderbolt. “I told you, merciful Raghubir, that Bali is not my brother — he is my death.”
essence: Fear turns a brother into a force of death.
simple_meaning: Sugriva runs in fear after Bali's blow lands hard. He cries out to Ram that Bali is not a brother to him, but death itself.
insight: It shows how fear strips away polite language and reveals raw dependence on help.
modern_relevance: You freeze in a confrontation, then blurt out the truth to the one person you trust. In panic, even family can feel like a threat.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक रूप तुम्ह भ्राता दोऊ तेहि भ्रम तें नहिं मारेउँ सोऊ॥ कर परसा सुग्रीव सरीरा। तनु भा कुलिस गई सब पीरा ॥
translation: (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) तुम दोनों भाइयों का एक सा ही रूप है। इसी भ्रम से मैंने उसको नहीं मारा। फिर श्री रामजी ने सुग्रीव के शरीर को हाथ से स्पर्श किया, जिससे उसका शरीर वज्र के समान हो गया और सारी पीड़ा जाती रही ॥
english_translation: (Lord Ram said:) Your two brothers look exactly alike. Because of that confusion, I did not kill him. Then Ram touched Sugriva's body with his hand, and his body became like thunderbolt; all pain disappeared.
essence: Mercy can heal even the confusion it did not cause.
simple_meaning: Ram explains that he mistook the brothers for each other, so he did not kill the wrong one. Then his touch restores Sugriva's strength and removes his pain.
insight: It shows that clarity and compassion can follow confusion without shame.
modern_relevance: You misread a situation, say the wrong thing, and someone is hurt. A calm explanation and a caring touch can repair what panic made worse.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: मेली कंठ सुमन कै माला। पठवा पुनि बल देइ बिसाला॥ पुनि नाना बिधि भई लराई। बिटप ओट देखहिं रघुराई ॥
translation: तब श्री रामजी ने सुग्रीव के गले में फूलों की माला डाल दी और फिर उसे बड़ा भारी बल देकर भेजा। दोनों में पुनः अनेक प्रकार से युद्ध हुआ। श्री रघुनाथजी वृक्ष की आड़ से देख रहे थे ॥
english_translation: Then Ram placed a garland of flowers around Sugriva's neck and gave him great strength. The two fought again in many ways, while Raghunath watched from behind a tree.
essence: Real help empowers action, then steps back.
simple_meaning: Ram blesses Sugriva, strengthens him, and sends him back into battle. Then the two fight again while Ram watches from hiding.
insight: It shows support followed by restraint: strengthen the ally, then wait for the right opening.
modern_relevance: A coach gives you one last pep talk before the match, then steps back and lets the contest unfold. Help can steady you, but it cannot replace the moment of action.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहु छल बल सुग्रीव कर हियँ हारा भय मानि। मारा बालि राम तब हृदय माझ सर तानि ॥
translation: सुग्रीव ने बहुत से छल-बल किए, किंतु (अंत में) भय मानकर हृदय से हार गया। तब श्री रामजी ने तानकर बालि के हृदय में बाण मारा ॥
english_translation: Sugriva used many tricks and displays of strength, but in the end he was overcome by fear and admitted defeat. Then Ram drew his bow and shot an arrow into Bali's chest.
essence: Fear breaks the contest; Ram's arrow ends it.
simple_meaning: Sugriva finally gave in, and Ram shot Bali with an arrow to end the fight.
insight: It shifts attention from the struggle itself to the decisive act that ends it.
modern_relevance: A tense argument has gone on too long, and everyone knows the real decision is about to land. This is the moment when the outcome changes, not the talking.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परा बिकल महि सर के लागें। पुनि उठि बैठ देखि प्रभु आगे॥ स्याम गात सिर जटा बनाएँ। अरुन नयन सर चाप चढ़ाएँ ॥
translation: बाण के लगते ही बालि व्याकुल होकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा, किंतु प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी को आगे देखकर वह फिर उठ बैठा। भगवान् का श्याम शरीर है, सिर पर जटा बनाए हैं, लाल नेत्र हैं, बाण लिए हैं और धनुष चढ़ाए हैं ॥
english_translation: Struck by the arrow, Bali fell to the ground in distress, then rose and sat up when he saw Lord Ram before him. The Lord has a dark body, matted hair on his head, red eyes, a drawn bow, and an arrow ready.
essence: Seeing Ram turns pain into recognition.
simple_meaning: Bali is hit, falls down, then sits up again when he sees Ram standing before him. Ram is shown as a poised warrior with bow and arrow.
insight: It slows the scene to show that recognition comes before surrender. The wounded mind must first see clearly.
modern_relevance: You get the bad news, sit frozen for a second, then look up and see the person you most needed to face. The moment changes because presence changes everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि पुनि चितइ चरन चित दीन्हा। सुफल जन्म माना प्रभु चीन्हा॥ हृदयँ प्रीति मुख बचन कठोरा। बोला चितइ राम की ओरा ॥
translation: बालि ने बार-बार भगवान् की ओर देखकर चित्त को उनके चरणों में लगा दिया। प्रभु को पहचानकर उसने अपना जन्म सफल माना। उसके हृदय में प्रीति थी, पर मुख में कठोर वचन थे। वह श्री रामजी की ओर देखकर बोला- ॥
english_translation: Again and again he looked at Ram's feet and fixed his mind there. Recognizing the Lord, he felt his birth had become fruitful. His heart held love, but his mouth spoke harshly. Looking toward Ram, he said:
essence: Recognition can soften the heart without fully healing the wound.
simple_meaning: Bali sees Ram clearly and feels blessed by the encounter, even as he speaks with bitterness on the outside. It is the moment before his final words of accusation.
insight: It shows how devotion and injury can coexist, and why the next words still carry pain.
modern_relevance: You can be deeply moved by someone and still speak from old hurt. Recognition and resentment can live in the same heart for a moment.
speaker: Bali

verse_text: धर्म हेतु अवतरेहु गोसाईं। मारेहु मोहि ब्याध की नाईं॥ मैं बैरी सुग्रीव पिआरा। अवगुन कवन नाथ मोहि मारा ॥
translation: हे गोसाईं। आपने धर्म की रक्षा के लिए अवतार लिया है और मुझे व्याध की तरह (छिपकर) मारा? मैं बैरी और सुग्रीव प्यारा? हे नाथ! किस दोष से आपने मुझे मारा? ॥
english_translation: O Lord, you have incarnated to uphold dharma, yet you struck me like a hunter from hiding? I am your enemy, and Sugriva is dear to you—by what fault did you kill me?
essence: Wounded pride can make justice feel like betrayal.
simple_meaning: Vali, dying, accuses Ram of killing him from hiding and questions why Ram favored Sugriva over him.
insight: It shows how wounded pride turns a moral event into a personal grievance.
modern_relevance: You get blamed in a group chat after someone cuts you off mid-sentence, and your first reaction is, 'Why did you do that to me?' Hurt often speaks before understanding.
speaker: Vali

verse_text: अनुज बधू भगिनी सुत नारी। सुनु सठ कन्या सम ए चारी॥ इन्हहि कुदृष्टि बिलोकइ जोई। ताहि बधें कछु पाप न होई ॥
translation: (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे मूर्ख! सुन, छोटे भाई की स्त्री, बहिन, पुत्र की स्त्री और कन्या- ये चारों समान हैं। इनको जो कोई बुरी दृष्टि से देखता है, उसे मारने में कुछ भी पाप नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: O fool, listen: your younger brother’s wife, your sister, your son’s wife, and your daughter are all the same. Whoever looks at them with lustful intent deserves no blame if punished.
essence: Right seeing protects both the other person and your own character.
simple_meaning: Ram says that a younger brother’s wife, a sister, a son’s wife, and a daughter must all be seen as equal and protected from lustful looking.
insight: It shifts the mind from consuming others to protecting them through disciplined seeing.
modern_relevance: You notice your eyes lingering where they should not, then feel the quiet shame afterward. This verse draws a hard line: train your gaze before desire trains you.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: मूढ़ तोहि अतिसय अभिमाना। नारि सिखावन करसि न काना॥ मम भुज बल आश्रित तेहि जानी। मारा चहसि अधम अभिमानी ॥
translation: हे मूढ़! तुझे अत्यंत अभिमान है। तूने अपनी स्त्री की सीख पर भी कान (ध्यान) नहीं दिया। सुग्रीव को मेरी भुजाओं के बल का आश्रित जानकर भी अरे अधम अभिमानी! तूने उसको मारना चाहा ॥
english_translation: You are utterly proud, fool. You would not even listen to your wife’s counsel. Knowing that Sugriva was protected by my arms, you still wanted to kill him, arrogant wretch.
essence: Pride makes you deaf to the counsel that could save you.
simple_meaning: Ravana is being called out for his arrogance. He ignored wise counsel, forgot Sugriva was under Ram’s protection, and still tried to harm him.
insight: It shifts attention from outward blame to the inner pride that blocks clear hearing.
modern_relevance: You keep arguing in the group chat even after three people warn you to stop. Later, you realize the real problem was not the advice — it was the part of you that refused to hear it.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनहु राम स्वामी सन चल न चातुरी मोरि। प्रभु अजहूँ मैं पापी अंतकाल गति तोरि ॥
translation: (बालि ने कहा-) हे श्री रामजी! सुनिए, स्वामी (आप) से मेरी चतुराई नहीं चल सकती। हे प्रभो! अंतकाल में आपकी गति (शरण) पाकर मैं अब भी पापी ही रहा? ॥
english_translation: Listen, Ram, my cleverness cannot work against my Lord. O Lord, even now at the end, I remain sinful while taking refuge in you.
essence: Cleverness dies at the feet of surrender.
simple_meaning: Bali admits that his tricks cannot work against Ram. He also admits that, at the end, only Ram's refuge remains for him.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to humble surrender when control has already failed.
modern_relevance: You’ve rehearsed the apology, the excuse, the workaround — and then the moment arrives when none of it matters. What remains is honesty and asking for help.
speaker: Bali

verse_text: सुनत राम अति कोमल बानी। बालि सीस परसेउ निज पानी॥ अचल करौं तनु राखहु प्राना। बालि कहा सुनु कृपानिधाना ॥
translation: बालि की अत्यंत कोमल वाणी सुनकर श्री रामजी ने उसके सिर को अपने हाथ से स्पर्श किया (और कहा-) मैं तुम्हारे शरीर को अचल कर दूँ, तुम प्राणों को रखो। बालि ने कहा- हे कृपानिधान! सुनिए ॥
english_translation: Hearing Bali's gentle words, Ram touched his head with his own hand. "I can make your body still; keep your life," Bali said. "Listen, treasure of compassion..."
essence: Mercy does not disappear when justice is done.
simple_meaning: Bali speaks with humility after Ram’s response. Ram shows mercy even in the middle of a fatal confrontation, and Bali recognises that compassion.
insight: It teaches you to meet conflict without losing gentleness.
modern_relevance: A tense conversation after a breakup, firing, or family conflict can still hold dignity. Even when someone has been hurt, the response does not have to become hard or humiliating.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जन्म जन्म मुनि जतनु कराहीं। अंत राम कहि आवत नाहीं॥ जासु नाम बल संकर कासी। देत सबहि सम गति अबिनासी ॥
translation: मुनिगण जन्म-जन्म में (प्रत्येक जन्म में) (अनेकों प्रकार का) साधन करते रहते हैं। फिर भी अंतकाल में उन्हें 'राम' नहीं कह आता (उनके मुख से राम नाम नहीं निकलता)। जिनके नाम के बल से शंकरजी काशी में सबको समान रूप से अविनाशिनी गति (मुक्ति) देते हैं ॥
english_translation: Sages practice countless disciplines across many births, yet at the end they still cannot utter Ram's name. By the power of whose name, Shankar in Kashi grants everyone the same undying liberation.
essence: Effort may fail; Ram's name does not.
simple_meaning: Even great sages may practice for life after life and still fail to remember Ram at the end. Ram's name is so powerful that even Shankar gives everyone liberation through it.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-made spiritual effort to trust in Ram's saving name.
modern_relevance: You can spend years perfecting your routine, your discipline, your self-control — and still feel strangely empty when life turns serious. This verse points to a refuge deeper than achievement.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मम लोचन गोचर सोई आवा। बहुरि कि प्रभु अस बनिहि बनावा ॥
translation: वह श्री रामजी स्वयं मेरे नेत्रों के सामने आ गए हैं। हे प्रभो! ऐसा संयोग क्या फिर कभी बन पड़ेगा ॥
english_translation: He has come before my eyes. O Lord, will such a meeting happen again?
essence: True nearness is precious because it may not return.
simple_meaning: The speaker sees Ram directly and feels wonder that such a blessed meeting may never happen again.
insight: It shifts attention from possession to reverent noticing of a rare encounter.
modern_relevance: You finally sit across from someone you have longed to meet, and the room goes quiet. A part of you already knows this moment will never feel ordinary again.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सो नयन गोचर जासु गुन नित नेति कहि श्रुति गावहीं। जिति पवन मन गो निरस करि मुनि ध्यान कबहुँक पावहीं॥ मोहि जानि अति अभिमान बस प्रभु कहेउ राखु सरीरही। अस कवन सठ हठि काटि सुरतरु बारि करिहि बबूरही ॥
translation: श्रुतियाँ 'नेति-नेति' कहकर निरंतर जिनका गुणगान करती रहती हैं तथा प्राण और मन को जीतकर एवं इंद्रियों को (विषयों के रस से सर्वथा) नीरस बनाकर मुनिगण ध्यान में जिनकी कभी क्वचित् ही झलक पाते हैं, वे ही प्रभु (आप) साक्षात् मेरे सामने प्रकट हैं। आपने मुझे अत्यंत अभिमानवश जानकर यह कहा कि तुम शरीर रख लो, परंतु ऐसा मूर्ख कौन होगा जो हठपूर्वक कल्पवृक्ष को काटकर उससे बबूर के बाड़ लगाएगा (अर्थात् पूर्णकाम बना देने वाले आपको छोड़कर आपसे इस नश्वर शरीर की रक्षा चाहेगा?) ॥
english_translation: The sages sing of you with endless "not this, not that." By conquering breath and mind and draining the taste from the senses, they glimpse you only sometimes in meditation. Yet you, the Lord, stand before me now. Knowing me proud, you told me to keep this body—but who would foolishly cut down a wish-fulfilling tree to make a thorn fence?
essence: What seekers chase in thought stands before the devotee in person.
simple_meaning: The divine reality is beyond description and hard to reach through meditation, yet Hanuman sees Ram directly. He refuses to keep a fragile body instead of the one who fulfills every wish.
insight: It shifts the mind from abstract searching to direct recognition and wholehearted surrender.
modern_relevance: You spend years trying to name what matters, then one meeting makes everything else feel too small. A mentor, a beloved, a calling — once it appears, you stop bargaining with lesser things.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: अब नाथ करि करुना बिलोकहु देहु जो बर मागऊँ। जेहि जोनि जन्मौं कर्म बस तहँ राम पद अनुरागऊँ॥ यह तनय मम सम बिनय बल कल्यानप्रद प्रभु लीजिये। गहि बाँह सुर नर नाह आपन दास अंगद कीजिये ॥
translation: हे नाथ! अब मुझ पर दयादृष्टि कीजिए और मैं जो वर माँगता हूँ उसे दीजिए। मैं कर्मवश जिस योनि में जन्म लूँ, वहीं श्री रामजी (आप) के चरणों में प्रेम करूँ! हे कल्याणप्रद प्रभो! यह मेरा पुत्र अंगद विनय और बल में मेरे ही समान है, इसे स्वीकार कीजिए और हे देवता और मनुष्यों के नाथ! बाँह पकड़कर इसे अपना दास बनाइए ॥
english_translation: O Lord, now show me your compassion and grant the boon I ask. Wherever I am born by the force of my deeds, let me love Ram's feet there. O gracious Lord, please accept this son of mine, Angad, equal to me in humility and strength, and taking him by the arm, make him your servant, O lord of gods and humans.
essence: Love for Ram can survive every birth and every change.
simple_meaning: Bali asks for one blessing: no matter where he is born in future lives, he wants love for Ram to remain in his heart. He also asks Ram to accept Angad as a servant.
insight: It shifts the mind from protecting a temporary life to protecting devotion itself.
modern_relevance: You lose a job, move cities, and everything familiar drops away. What stays with you is what you have truly loved. Bali asks for that kind of love to survive every change.
speaker: Bali

verse_text: राम चरन दृढ़ प्रीति करि बालि कीन्ह तनु त्याग। सुमन माल जिमि कंठ ते गिरत न जानइ नाग ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के चरणों में दृढ़ प्रीति करके बालि ने शरीर को वैसे ही (आसानी से) त्याग दिया जैसे हाथी अपने गले से फूलों की माला का गिरना न जाने ॥
english_translation: Bali gave up his body with firm love for Ram's feet, just as an elephant does not notice a flower garland slipping from its neck.
essence: Total love makes release feel effortless.
simple_meaning: Bali died with such deep love for Ram that leaving the body felt effortless, like something slipping away unnoticed.
insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to surrendering without resistance.
modern_relevance: You finally let go of a job, a relationship, or an identity you had outgrown. It hurts less than you feared because something deeper in you has already chosen peace.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम बालि निज धाम पठावा। नगर लोग सब व्याकुल धावा॥ नाना बिधि बिलाप कर तारा। छूटे केस न देह सँभारा ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी ने बालि को अपने परम धाम भेज दिया। नगर के सब लोग व्याकुल होकर दौड़े। बालि की स्त्री तारा अनेकों प्रकार से विलाप करने लगी। उसके बाल बिखरे हुए हैं और देह की सँभाल नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Ram sent Bali to his own divine abode. The people of the city rushed about in distress. Tara wept in many ways, her hair undone and her body no longer composed.
essence: A righteous act can still leave sorrow in its wake.
simple_meaning: Ram has killed Bali, and the whole city is thrown into grief and confusion. Tara is overwhelmed with lamentation.
insight: It shifts attention from the triumph of action to the grief that follows it.
modern_relevance: The meeting ends, the decision is made, and everyone walks out quietly shaken. One person has won, but another family is still standing in the shock of loss.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तारा बिकल देखि रघुराया। दीन्ह ग्यान हरि लीन्ही माया॥ छिति जल पावक गगन समीरा। पंच रचित अति अधम सरीरा ॥
translation: तारा को व्याकुल देखकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने उसे ज्ञान दिया और उसकी माया (अज्ञान) हर ली। (उन्होंने कहा-) पृथ्वी, जल, अग्नि, आकाश और वायु- इन पाँच तत्वों से यह अत्यंत अधम शरीर रचा गया है ॥
english_translation: Seeing Tara distressed, Raghuraya gave her understanding and removed the veil of confusion. He said: this body is made from earth, water, fire, sky, and air — a very lowly composition.
essence: Clear seeing dissolves grief’s grip on what is temporary.
simple_meaning: Ram comforts Tara by showing her that the body is only a temporary mix of five elements, so her grief should ease.
insight: It shifts attention from the body’s collapse to the deeper reality behind it.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a hospital bed, unable to accept how quickly a strong body can fail. This verse meets that shock with a hard, tender clarity: what changes was never the whole person.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रगट सो तनु तव आगे सोवा। जीव नित्य केहि लगि तुम्ह रोवा॥ उपजा ग्यान चरन तब लागी। लीन्हेसि परम भगति बर मागी ॥
translation: वह शरीर तो प्रत्यक्ष तुम्हारे सामने सोया हुआ है, और जीव नित्य है। फिर तुम किसके लिए रो रही हो? जब ज्ञान उत्पन्न हो गया, तब वह भगवान् के चरणों लगी और उसने परम भक्ति का वर माँग लिया ॥
english_translation: That body lies visibly before you, and the living being is eternal. Then why are you crying for it? When knowledge arose, she bowed at Ram's feet and asked for the boon of supreme devotion.
essence: What you truly mourn is not what can be seen.
simple_meaning: The visible body is not the whole person. Once true understanding appears, grief softens and turns into devotion.
insight: It shifts attention from the body’s ending to the deeper continuity behind it.
modern_relevance: You’re standing by a hospital bed after hearing the worst news, staring at a still face. This verse speaks to the part of you that knows love is larger than the body it inhabited.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: उमा दारु जोषित की नाईं। सबहि नचावत रामु गोसाईं॥ तब सुग्रीवहि आयसु दीन्हा। मृतक कर्म बिधिवत सब कीन्हा ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! स्वामी श्री रामजी सबको कठपुतली की तरह नचाते हैं। तदनन्तर श्री रामजी ने सुग्रीव को आज्ञा दी और सुग्रीव ने विधिपूर्वक बालि का सब मृतक कर्म किया ॥
english_translation: (Shiva says:) O Uma, Lord Ram moves everyone like a puppet. Then Ram gave Sugriva the order, and Sugriva duly performed all the funeral rites for Bali.
essence: Ram guides even the hands that seem to act on their own.
simple_meaning: Ram quietly directs everyone’s actions. After that, Sugriva carries out Bali’s funeral rites exactly as required.
insight: It shifts attention from visible control to the deeper force guiding events and responsibilities.
modern_relevance: A family is stunned after a sudden death, yet someone still has to call the priest, arrange the rites, and keep everyone steady. This verse reminds you that even chaos has an unseen order.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: राम कहा अनुजहि समुझाई। राज देहु सुग्रीवहि जाई॥ रघुपति चरन नाइ करि माथा। चले सकल प्रेरित रघुनाथा ॥
translation: तब श्री रामचंद्रजी ने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण को समझाकर कहा कि तुम जाकर सुग्रीव को राज्य दे दो। श्री रघुनाथजी की प्रेरणा (आज्ञा) से सब लोग श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों में मस्तक नवाकर चले ॥
english_translation: Then Lord Ram explained to his younger brother Lakshman: go and give the kingdom to Sugriva. Everyone bowed their heads at Raghunath's feet and departed, moved by Raghunath's command.
essence: Power becomes righteous when it gives back what it won.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Lakshman to restore Sugriva's kingdom, and everyone leaves after bowing to Ram's feet.
insight: It teaches you to complete an obligation cleanly and release ownership once the promise is fulfilled.
modern_relevance: You finally get the keys, the credit, or the control everyone fought for — and then you return what was never meant to stay with you. That kind of restraint changes everything.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: लछिमन तुरत बोलाए पुरजन बिप्र समाज। राजु दीन्ह सुग्रीव कहँ अंगद कहँ जुबराज ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी ने तुरंत ही सब नगरवासियों को और ब्राह्मणों के समाज को बुला लिया और (उनके सामने) सुग्रीव को राज्य और अंगद को युवराज पद दिया ॥
english_translation: Lakshman quickly summoned the townspeople and the assembly of Brahmins, and in their presence gave Sugriva the kingdom and Angada the crown prince's seat.
essence: Fairness becomes complete only when it is publicly carried out.
simple_meaning: Lakshman gathers the people and formally installs Sugriva as king and Angada as crown prince.
insight: It teaches you to complete responsibility openly, so fairness becomes visible and real.
modern_relevance: A manager signs the transfer papers in front of the whole team instead of dragging it out in private. Clear, timely action restores trust faster than speeches do.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उमा राम सम हत जग माहीं। गुरु पितु मातु बंधु प्रभु नाहीं॥ सुर नर मुनि सब कै यह रीती। स्वारथ लागि करहिं सब प्रीति ॥
translation: हे पार्वती! जगत में श्री रामजी के समान हित करने वाला गुरु, पिता, माता, बंधु और स्वामी कोई नहीं है। देवता, मनुष्य और मुनि सबकी यह रीति है कि स्वार्थ के लिए ही सब प्रीति करते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Parvati, in the world there is no benefactor like Ram, no teacher, father, mother, brother, or lord like him. Gods, humans, and sages all follow this rule: they love only for their own sake.
essence: Ram's love is pure because it asks for nothing in return.
simple_meaning: Ram alone loves without self-interest. Everyone else usually loves with some hidden need or benefit in mind.
insight: It shifts your trust away from transactional affection toward selfless care.
modern_relevance: You know the difference between the friend who checks in because they care and the one who only calls when they need something. This verse points to the rare kind of love that gives without keeping score.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: बालि त्रास ब्याकुल दिन राती। तन बहु ब्रन चिंताँ जर छाती॥ सोइ सुग्रीव कीन्ह कपि राऊ। अति कृपाल रघुबीर सुभाऊ ॥
translation: जो सुग्रीव दिन-रात बालि के भय से व्याकुल रहता था, जिसके शरीर में बहुत से घाव हो गए थे और जिसकी छाती चिंता के मारे जला करती थी, उसी सुग्रीव को उन्होंने वानरों का राजा बना दिया। श्री रामचंद्रजी का स्वभाव अत्यंत ही कृपालु है ॥
english_translation: The same Sugriva who lived in fear of Bali day and night, whose body bore many wounds and whose chest burned with worry, Ram made king of the monkeys. The nature of Raghubir is deeply compassionate.
essence: Compassion restores what fear has taken away.
simple_meaning: Ram lifts Sugriva from fear and suffering into kingship because compassion is his nature.
insight: It shifts attention from pity to restorative action: help should return agency, not just comfort.
modern_relevance: You know the friend who has been shaking through every phone call, carrying old hurt in the body. Then someone finally gives them a real chance, not just sympathy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जानतहूँ अस प्रभु परिहरहीं। काहे न बिपति जाल नर परहीं॥ पुनि सुग्रीवहि लीन्ह बोलाई। बहु प्रकार नृपनीति सिखाई ॥
translation: जो लोग जानते हुए भी ऐसे प्रभु को त्याग देते हैं, वे क्यों न विपत्ति के जाल में फँसें? फिर श्री रामजी ने सुग्रीव को बुला लिया और बहुत प्रकार से उन्हें राजनीति की शिक्षा दी ॥
english_translation: Those who knowingly abandon such a Lord fall into the net of trouble. Then Ram called Sugriva back and taught him statecraft in many ways.
essence: Rejecting Ram is itself the path into suffering.
simple_meaning: Turning away from a true helper leads straight into suffering. Ram then calls Sugriva close and teaches him how to rule wisely.
insight: It shifts the mind from casual neglect of guidance to active reliance on what protects and orders life.
modern_relevance: You keep ignoring the friend who always gives the clearest advice, then wonder why the same mess keeps returning. Wisdom is not just hearing good counsel — it is staying close enough to let it shape your choices.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह प्रभु सुनु सुग्रीव हरीसा। पुर न जाउँ दस चारि बरीसा॥ गत ग्रीषम बरषा रितु आई। रहिहउँ निकट सैल पर छाई ॥
translation: फिर प्रभु ने कहा- हे वानरपति सुग्रीव! सुनो, मैं चौदह वर्ष तक गाँव (बस्ती) में नहीं जाऊँगा। ग्रीष्मऋतु बीतकर वर्षाऋतु आ गई। अतः मैं यहाँ पास ही पर्वत पर टिक रहूँगा ॥
english_translation: Then the Lord said, “Listen, Sugriva, king of the monkeys. I will not stay in the town for fourteen years. Summer has passed and the rainy season has arrived, so I will remain nearby on the mountain.”
essence: True commitment stays near the task, not the comfort.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Sugriva he will stay near the mountain, not in the town, during the rainy season and for the years of exile.
insight: It teaches you to stay aligned with your commitment even when comfort is available.
modern_relevance: You’ve been offered a comfortable seat, but you choose the hard edge of the room because your promise still matters.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: अंगद सहित करहु तुम्ह राजू। संतत हृदयँ धरेहु मम काजू॥ जब सुग्रीव भवन फिरि आए। रामु प्रबरषन गिरि पर छाए ॥
translation: तुम अंगद सहित राज्य करो। मेरे काम का हृदय में सदा ध्यान रखना। तदनन्तर जब सुग्रीवजी घर लौट आए, तब श्री रामजी प्रवर्षण पर्वत पर जा टिके ॥
english_translation: You and Angada should rule, keeping my work always in your heart. Then, when Sugriva returned home, Rama stayed on Mount Pravarshana.
essence: Help fully, then step back and let others rule.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Sugriva and Angada to rule, while keeping his work in mind. After Sugriva returns home, Ram stays on Mount Pravarshana.
insight: It shifts the mind from controlling the outcome to supporting the right people at the right time.
modern_relevance: You finish helping a friend rebuild their business, then step back and let them lead. Real support knows when to stay involved and when to leave room.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: प्रथमहिं देवन्ह गिरि गुहा राखेउ रुचिर बनाइ। राम कृपानिधि कछु दिन बास करहिंगे आइ ॥
translation: देवताओं ने पहले से ही उस पर्वत की एक गुफा को सुंदर बना (सजा) रखा था। उन्होंने सोच रखा था कि कृपा की खान श्री रामजी कुछ दिन यहाँ आकर निवास करेंगे ॥
english_translation: The gods had already made a lovely cave in the mountain, thinking that Ram, the treasure of grace, would come and stay there for some days.
essence: The right refuge is ready before you arrive.
simple_meaning: The mountain cave was prepared in advance, because the devas expected Ram to stay there for a while.
insight: It frames the stay as divinely prepared, not improvised.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a friend's empty hill cabin and find the firewood stacked, the bed made, the lights on. Someone prepared for your coming before you even asked.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुंदर बन कुसुमित अति सोभा। गुंजत मधुप निकर मधु लोभा॥ कंद मूल फल पत्र सुहाए। भए बहुत जब ते प्रभु आए ॥
translation: सुंदर वन फूला हुआ अत्यंत सुशोभित है। मधु के लोभ से भौंरों के समूह गुंजार कर रहे हैं। जब से प्रभु आए, तब से वन में सुंदर कन्द, मूल, फल और पत्तों की बहुतायत हो गई ॥
english_translation: The beautiful forest is in full bloom, shining with great splendor. Swarms of bees hum, drawn by the sweetness of nectar. Since the Lord arrived, roots, fruits, and leaves have become abundant and lovely.
essence: His arrival makes the forest bloom.
simple_meaning: The forest has become lush and beautiful since Ram arrived there.
insight: It shows Ram’s presence as life-giving, turning even wilderness into abundance.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home after good news has arrived, and the whole place feels lighter. Nothing changed on the walls, yet everything seems to breathe differently.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि मनोहर सैल अनूपा। रहे तहँ अनुज सहित सुरभूपा॥ मधुकर खग मृग तनु धरि देवा। करहिं सिद्ध मुनि प्रभु कै सेवा ॥
translation: मनोहर और अनुपम पर्वत को देखकर देवताओं के सम्राट् श्री रामजी छोटे भाई सहित वहाँ रह गए। देवता, सिद्ध और मुनि भौंरों, पक्षियों और पशुओं के शरीर धारण करके प्रभु की सेवा करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Seeing the beautiful, unmatched mountain, the lord of the gods stayed there with his younger brother. The devas, siddhas, and sages took the forms of bees, birds, and animals and served the Lord.
essence: Ram's presence turns even nature into service.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman stay on a beautiful mountain, and celestial beings take forms of bees, birds, and animals to serve them.
insight: It shifts attention from the setting itself to the way devotion transforms the entire atmosphere around Ram.
modern_relevance: You walk into a place that somehow feels different the moment someone deeply grounded arrives. People soften, help appears, and the whole atmosphere starts leaning toward service.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंगलरूप भयउ बन तब ते। कीन्ह निवास रमापति जब ते॥ फटिक सिला अति सुभ्र सुहाई। सुख आसीन तहाँ द्वौ भाई ॥
translation: जब से रमापति श्री रामजी ने वहाँ निवास किया तब से वन मंगलस्वरूप हो गया। सुंदर स्फटिक मणि की एक अत्यंत उज्ज्वल शिला है, उस पर दोनों भाई सुखपूर्वक विराजमान हैं ॥
english_translation: From the moment Rama took residence there, the forest became auspicious. A beautiful, bright crystal slab was there, and the two brothers sat there in comfort.
essence: Rama's presence turns ordinary ground into a place of blessing.
simple_meaning: Rama's presence makes the forest feel blessed, and he and Lakshman sit together on a bright crystal slab.
insight: It shifts attention from scenery to presence: the sacred quality of a place comes from who dwells there.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a hard day, and the tension drops because one steady person is already there. Some places change not by decoration, but by presence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहत अनुज सन कथा अनेका। भगति बिरत नृपनीति बिबेका॥ बरषा काल मेघ नभ छाए। गरजत लागत परम सुहाए ॥
translation: श्री राम छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी से भक्ति, वैराग्य, राजनीति और ज्ञान की अनेकों कथाएँ कहते हैं। वर्षाकाल में आकाश में छाए हुए बादल गरजते हुए बहुत ही सुहावने लगते हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram speaks with his younger brother about many topics—devotion, renunciation, kingship, and discernment. In the rainy season, clouds fill the sky and their thunder sounds especially lovely.
essence: Quiet conversation can carry the deepest teachings.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman spend time in quiet conversation about devotion, renunciation, wise rule, and clear judgment. The rainy clouds overhead make the scene feel beautiful and alive.
insight: It shifts attention from the setting to the quality of awareness and conversation within it.
modern_relevance: You sit with someone you trust while rain taps the window, and a simple conversation turns serious. What feels ordinary can hold the deepest guidance when the mind is settled.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: लछिमन देखु मोर गन नाचत बारिद पेखि। गृही बिरति रत हरष जस बिष्नुभगत कहुँ देखि ॥
translation: (श्री रामजी कहने लगे-) हे लक्ष्मण! देखो, मोरों के झुंड बादलों को देखकर नाच रहे हैं जैसे वैराग्य में अनुरक्त गृहस्थ किसी विष्णुभक्त को देखकर हर्षित होते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Lakshman, look at my peacocks dancing on seeing the clouds. Householders devoted to renunciation rejoice on seeing a devotee of Vishnu.
essence: Devotion recognizes devotion and answers with joy.
simple_meaning: Ram notices that even peacocks rejoice at the sight of clouds, just as devoted people feel joy when they see someone devoted to Vishnu.
insight: It trains you to recognize devotion as something that calls forth joy and alignment, not just belief.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and feel it immediately: one person is calm, sincere, and inwardly gathered. Without thinking, you relax too. Real devotion changes the atmosphere before anyone speaks.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: घन घमंड नभ गरजत घोरा। प्रिया हीन डरपत मन मोरा॥ दामिनि दमक रह नघन माहीं। खल कै प्रीति जथा थिर नाहीं ॥
translation: आकाश में बादल घुमड़-घुमड़कर घोर गर्जना कर रहे हैं, प्रिया (सीताजी) के बिना मेरा मन डर रहा है। बिजली की चमक बादलों में ठहरती नहीं, जैसे दुष्ट की प्रीति स्थिर नहीं रहती ॥
english_translation: The dark clouds roar fiercely in the sky. My mind trembles without my beloved. Lightning flashes within the clouds and never stays, just like the love of a wicked person never remains steady.
essence: True love stays; false love flashes and disappears.
simple_meaning: Ram sees a storm and feels Sita's absence. He compares lightning to unreliable love: bright for a moment, then gone.
insight: It teaches you to test love by steadiness, not by excitement.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who texts with heat for a week, then disappears when life gets difficult. The intensity felt real, but it was only lightning.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: बरषहिं जलद भूमि निअराएँ। जथा नवहिं बुध बिद्या पाएँ। बूँद अघात सहहिं गिरि कैसे। खल के बचन संत सह जैसें ॥
translation: बादल पृथ्वी के समीप आकर (नीचे उतरकर) बरस रहे हैं, जैसे विद्या पाकर विद्वान् नम्र हो जाते हैं। बूँदों की चोट पर्वत कैसे सहते हैं, जैसे दुष्टों के वचन संत सहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Clouds, coming close to the earth, pour rain; learned people become humble after gaining wisdom. Mountains endure the blows of raindrops; saints endure the words of the wicked.
essence: Real wisdom lowers pride and leaves you unshaken.
simple_meaning: True learning makes a person humble. A steady person can absorb harsh words the way mountains absorb rain.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to humility and steady endurance.
modern_relevance: You finally get praised after years of work, and the first temptation is to puff up. This verse pulls you back down: real growth should make you quieter, not louder.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: छुद्र नदीं भरि चलीं तोराई। जस थोरेहुँ धन खल इतराई॥ भूमि परत भा ढाबर पानी। जनु जीवहि माया लपटानी ॥
translation: छोटी नदियाँ भरकर (किनारों को) तुड़ाती हुई चलीं, जैसे थोड़े धन से भी दुष्ट इतरा जाते हैं। (मर्यादा का त्याग कर देते हैं)। पृथ्वी पर पड़ते ही पानी गंदला हो गया है, जैसे शुद्ध जीव के माया लिपट गई हो ॥
english_translation: Small rivers swell and break their banks, just as a little wealth makes the wicked boastful. When water falls to the ground, it turns muddy, just as maya clings to a pure living being.
essence: Small success can swell ego and blur your clarity.
simple_meaning: Small rivers overflow their banks, just as a little wealth can make bad people arrogant. Water becomes muddy when it falls to the ground, just as maya can cling to a pure living being.
insight: It trains you to notice how pride and confusion attach themselves before they feel permanent.
modern_relevance: You get a bonus and suddenly start speaking louder, spending faster, and feeling untouchable. The change is small, but the distortion is real.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समिटि समिटि जल भरहिं तलावा। जिमि सदगुन सज्जन पहिं आवा॥ सरिता जल जलनिधि महुँ जोई। होइ अचल जिमि जिव हरि पाई ॥
translation: जल एकत्र हो-होकर तालाबों में भर रहा है, जैसे सद्गुण (एक-एककर) सज्जन के पास चले आते हैं। नदी का जल समुद्र में जाकर वैसे ही स्थिर हो जाता है, जैसे जीव श्री हरि को पाकर अचल (आवागमन से मुक्त) हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Water gathers into ponds, just as good qualities gather in a noble person. River water becomes still in the ocean, just as a living being becomes steady upon reaching Hari.
essence: True steadiness comes when the restless life reaches Hari.
simple_meaning: Good qualities naturally gather in a noble person, and a restless life becomes steady when it reaches Hari.
insight: It shifts attention from collecting experiences to finding what truly steadies the mind.
modern_relevance: You keep chasing the next fix, the next approval, the next milestone — and still feel scattered. Then one relationship, one practice, one presence makes everything inside you start to settle.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: हरित भूमि तृन संकुल समुझि परहिं नहिं पंथ। जिमि पाखंड बाद तें गुप्त होहिं सदग्रंथ ॥
translation: पृथ्वी घास से परिपूर्ण होकर हरी हो गई है, जिससे रास्ते समझ नहीं पड़ते। जैसे पाखंड मत के प्रचार से सद्ग्रंथ गुप्त (लुप्त) हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: The earth has turned green and thick with grass, so the path is no longer visible. In the same way, when false teachings spread, true scriptures become hidden.
essence: False noise can hide the path, but it cannot erase it.
simple_meaning: When false ideas spread everywhere, it becomes hard to see the real path, just as thick grass hides a road.
insight: It trains you to notice how confusion can mask what is reliable, and to look past surface noise for what truly guides.
modern_relevance: You open your phone for a simple answer and get buried under ten confident opinions, half-truths, and recycled advice. The real path is still there — but clutter can hide it.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: दादुर धुनि चहु दिसा सुहाई। बेद पढ़हिं जनु बटु समुदाई॥ नव पल्लव भए बिटप अनेका। साधक मन जस मिलें बिबेका ॥
translation: चारों दिशाओं में मेंढकों की ध्वनि ऐसी सुहावनी लगती है, मानो विद्यार्थियों के समुदाय वेद पढ़ रहे हों। अनेकों वृक्षों में नए पत्ते आ गए हैं, जिससे वे ऐसे हरे-भरे एवं सुशोभित हो गए हैं जैसे साधक का मन विवेक (ज्ञान) प्राप्त होने पर हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: The sound of frogs sounds pleasant in all four directions, as if groups of students are reciting the Vedas. Many trees have put forth new leaves, becoming lush and beautiful like a seeker’s mind when clear seeing arrives.
essence: Clear seeing can make the same world feel newly alive.
simple_meaning: Nature is described as becoming fresh and beautiful, just like a seeker’s mind becomes bright and settled when clear understanding arises.
insight: It shifts attention from external conditions to the inner clarity that changes how everything is experienced.
modern_relevance: You step outside after a long, heavy week and notice the air, the trees, even the noise differently. Nothing changed out there — but your mind did.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अर्क जवास पात बिनु भयऊ। जस सुराज खल उद्यम गयऊ॥ खोजत कतहुँ मिलइ नहिं धूरी। करइ क्रोध जिमि धरमहि दूरी ॥
translation: मदार और जवासा बिना पत्ते के हो गए (उनके पत्ते झड़ गए)। जैसे श्रेष्ठ राज्य में दुष्टों का उद्यम जाता रहा (उनकी एक भी नहीं चलती)। धूल कहीं खोजने पर भी नहीं मिलती, जैसे क्रोध धर्म को दूर कर देता है। (अर्थात् क्रोध का आवेश होने पर धर्म का ज्ञान नहीं रह जाता) ॥
english_translation: The madar and javasa plants became leafless, just as the efforts of the wicked fail in a well-ruled kingdom. Dust cannot be found anywhere, just as anger drives dharma far away.
essence: Anger makes right action vanish.
simple_meaning: A peaceful, well-run order leaves wrongdoing powerless. In the same way, anger blinds you and pushes right conduct far away.
insight: It teaches you to interrupt anger before it cuts off clear judgment.
modern_relevance: You get a sharp email, feel your face heat up, and type a reply you will regret. In that tiny gap before sending, your whole course can change.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ससि संपन्न सोह महि कैसी। उपकारी कै संपति जैसी॥ निसि तम घन खद्योत बिराजा। जनु दंभिन्ह कर मिला समाजा ॥
translation: अन्न से युक्त (लहराती हुई खेती से हरी-भरी) पृथ्वी कैसी शोभित हो रही है, जैसी उपकारी पुरुष की संपत्ति। रात के घने अंधकार में जुगनू शोभा पा रहे हैं, मानो दम्भियों का समाज आ जुटा हो ॥
english_translation: The earth looks beautiful when it is full of grain, just as wealth makes a generous person shine. In the dark of night, fireflies glow like a crowd of boastful people gathered together.
essence: Real worth shines quietly; pride only glitters in the dark.
simple_meaning: A fertile earth looks lovely, just as generous wealth looks fitting. Fireflies in the dark are like proud people showing off together.
insight: It trains you to distinguish genuine value from showy appearance.
modern_relevance: A room full of loud voices and shiny clothes can look impressive for a moment. Then you notice who actually helps, who actually feeds people, and who only wants to be seen.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: महाबृष्टि चलि फूटि किआरीं। जिमि सुतंत्र भएँ बिगरहिं नारीं॥ कृषी निरावहिं चतुर किसाना। जिमि बुध तजहिं मोह मद माना ॥
translation: भारी वर्षा से खेतों की क्यारियाँ फूट चली हैं, जैसे स्वतंत्र होने से स्त्रियाँ बिगड़ जाती हैं। चतुर किसान खेतों को निरा रहे हैं (उनमें से घास आदि को निकालकर फेंक रहे हैं।) जैसे विद्वान् लोग मोह, मद और मान का त्याग कर देते हैं ॥
english_translation: Heavy rain has broken the field ridges, just as women become unruly when left independent. Wise farmers weed their fields, just as the learned cast off delusion, pride, and conceit.
essence: Clear seeing begins when pride and delusion are pulled out by the roots.
simple_meaning: A wise person removes inner weeds the way a farmer clears a field. Real understanding means dropping delusion, pride, and self-importance.
insight: It shifts attention from managing appearances to removing the habits that block clear seeing.
modern_relevance: You finally sit down to work, but your mind keeps feeding on comparison, defensiveness, and the need to look smart. Real clarity begins when you start pulling those weeds out.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखिअत चक्रबाक खग नाहीं। कलिहि पाइ जिमि धर्म पराहीं॥ ऊषर बरषइ तृन नहिं जामा। जिमि हरिजन हियँ उपज न कामा ॥
translation: चक्रवाक पक्षी दिखाई नहीं दे रहे हैं, जैसे कलियुग को पाकर धर्म भाग जाते हैं। ऊसर में वर्षा होती है, पर वहाँ घास तक नहीं उगती। जैसे हरिभक्त के हृदय में काम नहीं उत्पन्न होता ॥
english_translation: The chakravaka birds are nowhere to be seen, as dharma flees when Kali arrives. Rain falls on barren ground, yet no grass grows there. In the heart of a devotee of Hari, desire does not arise.
essence: A heart full of Hari leaves no soil for desire.
simple_meaning: A devotee of Hari becomes inwardly barren to desire, just as grass cannot grow on dry land. The verse also says dharma retreats in the age of Kali.
insight: It shifts attention from suppressing desire to cultivating a heart where desire cannot take root.
modern_relevance: You open your phone for one quick check and feel the old hunger return. But when your mind is anchored in something sacred, that restless wanting has nowhere to settle.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: बिबिध जंतु संकुल महि भ्राजा। प्रजा बाढ़ जिमि पाइ सुराजा॥ जहँ तहँ रहे पथिक थकि नाना। जिमि इंद्रिय गन उपजें ग्याना ॥
translation: पृथ्वी अनेक तरह के जीवों से भरी हुई उसी तरह शोभायमान है, जैसे सुराज्य पाकर प्रजा की वृद्धि होती है। जहाँ-तहाँ अनेक पथिक थककर ठहरे हुए हैं, जैसे ज्ञान उत्पन्न होने पर इंद्रियाँ (शिथिल होकर विषयों की ओर जाना छोड़ देती हैं) ॥
english_translation: The earth shines with many kinds of living beings, like a kingdom where the people flourish under good rule. Travelers rest everywhere, like the senses fall quiet when true understanding arises.
essence: Understanding stills the senses the way good rule steadies a kingdom.
simple_meaning: A well-ordered world looks alive and flourishing. In the same way, when understanding arises, the senses stop roaming and become still.
insight: It shifts attention from sensory chasing to inner settling through understanding.
modern_relevance: You finally close ten browser tabs after reading something that actually makes sense. The urge to chase every distraction drops away because your mind has found its footing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कबहुँ प्रबल बह मारुत जहँ तहँ मेघ बिलाहिं। जिमि कपूत के उपजें कुल सद्धर्म नसाहिं ॥
translation: कभी-कभी वायु बड़े जोर से चलने लगती है, जिससे बादल जहाँ-तहाँ गायब हो जाते हैं। जैसे कुपुत्र के उत्पन्न होने से कुल के उत्तम धर्म (श्रेष्ठ आचरण) नष्ट हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Sometimes fierce winds blow and the clouds vanish here and there. In the same way, when a bad son is born, a family’s noble conduct is destroyed.
essence: One corrupted life can darken an entire family.
simple_meaning: A family can lose its good name and conduct when one child goes badly astray. The image is of strong wind scattering clouds.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated misbehavior to the wider damage a corrupting influence can cause.
modern_relevance: You watch one teenager start lying, and soon the whole house is tense, defensive, and ashamed. One person’s choices can change the emotional climate for everyone.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कबहु दिवस महँ निबिड़ तम कबहुँक प्रगट पतंग। बिनसइ उपजइ ग्यान जिमि पाइ कुसंग सुसंग॥15ख॥
translation: कभी (बादलों के कारण) दिन में घोर अंधकार छा जाता है और कभी सूर्य प्रकट हो जाते हैं। जैसे कुसंग पाकर ज्ञान नष्ट हो जाता है और सुसंग पाकर उत्पन्न हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Sometimes thick darkness covers the day; sometimes the sun appears. In the same way, understanding is lost in bad company and born again in good company.
essence: Your mind follows the company you keep.
simple_meaning: Bad company can hide good judgment, while good company helps clear understanding return.
insight: It teaches you to protect your judgment by choosing the people and environments that sharpen, not distort, your mind.
modern_relevance: You leave a group chat feeling smaller, sharper, and strangely convinced of things you didn't believe yesterday. Then one honest friend says a few words, and your mind clears.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बरषा बिगत सरद रितु आई। लछमन देखहु परम सुहाई॥ फूलें कास सकल महि छाई। जनु बरषाँ कृत प्रगट बुढ़ाई ॥
translation: हे लक्ष्मण! देखो, वर्षा बीत गई और परम सुंदर शरद् ऋतु आ गई। फूले हुए कास से सारी पृथ्वी छा गई। मानो वर्षा ऋतु ने (कास रूपी सफेद बालों के रूप में) अपना बुढ़ापा प्रकट किया है ॥
english_translation: The rains have passed, and the lovely autumn has arrived, Lakshman. The blooming kans grass covers the earth, as if the rainy season has shown its old age.
essence: Beauty can also be a sign that time has moved on.
simple_meaning: The rainy season has ended, autumn has arrived, and the white kans grass now covers the land like the season's aging hair.
insight: It trains the mind to notice impermanence through ordinary nature, preparing you for the deeper teaching that follows.
modern_relevance: You notice the first cool morning after weeks of rain, and the street outside looks washed clean. Even the season has turned a page without asking permission.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उदित अगस्ति पंथ जल सोषा। जिमि लोभहिं सोषइ संतोषा॥ सरिता सर निर्मल जल सोहा। संत हृदय जस गत मद मोहा ॥
translation: अगस्त्य के तारे ने उदय होकर मार्ग के जल को सोख लिया, जैसे संतोष लोभ को सोख लेता है। नदियों और तालाबों का निर्मल जल ऐसी शोभा पा रहा है जैसे मद और मोह से रहित संतों का हृदय! ॥
english_translation: The star Agastya rises and dries up the path’s water, just as contentment dries up greed. The clear water of rivers and ponds shines like the hearts of saints free from pride and delusion.
essence: Contentment clears greed, and a humble heart becomes radiant.
simple_meaning: Contentment weakens greed, and a mind free from pride and confusion becomes clear and beautiful.
insight: It shifts attention from craving more to cultivating enough, so the mind becomes transparent and calm.
modern_relevance: You finally stop checking your phone after sending the message, and the urge to chase reassurance loosens. Something steadier takes over — and the mind feels clean again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रस रस सूख सरित सर पानी। ममता त्याग करहिं जिमि ग्यानी॥ जानि सरद रितु खंजन आए। पाइ समय जिमि सुकृत सुहाए ॥
translation: नदी और तालाबों का जल धीरे-धीरे सूख रहा है। जैसे ज्ञानी (विवेकी) पुरुष ममता का त्याग करते हैं। शरद ऋतु जानकर खंजन पक्षी आ गए। जैसे समय पाकर सुंदर सुकृत आ सकते हैं। (पुण्य प्रकट हो जाते हैं) ॥
english_translation: The waters of rivers and ponds slowly dry up, just as wise people let go of possessiveness. Knowing that autumn has arrived, the khanjan birds come, just as good deeds appear when the right time comes.
essence: Wise people release possessiveness, and good things arrive in their own time.
simple_meaning: As the season changes, water dries up and birds arrive at the right time. In the same way, wise people let go of possessiveness and let good things come naturally.
insight: It shifts you from grasping for outcomes to allowing life to unfold in its proper season.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after sending the message, hoping the reply will hurry up. But some things arrive only when you stop squeezing them. Possessiveness dries the moment; patience lets it ripen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पंक न रेनु सोह असि धरनी। नीति निपुन नृप कै जसि करनी॥ जल संकोच बिकल भइँ मीना। अबुध कुटुंबी जिमि धनहीना ॥
translation: न कीचड़ है न धूल? इससे धरती (निर्मल होकर) ऐसी शोभा दे रही है जैसे नीतिनिपुण राजा की करनी! जल के कम हो जाने से मछलियाँ व्याकुल हो रही हैं, जैसे मूर्ख (विवेक शून्य) कुटुम्बी (गृहस्थ) धन के बिना व्याकुल होता है ॥
english_translation: The mud and dust are gone, so the earth shines like a wise king's conduct. With the water reduced, the fish are restless, like a foolish householder without wealth.
essence: What is released can brighten life; what is depended on can create panic.
simple_meaning: When excess is gone, beauty appears. But when resources shrink, the unprepared become anxious and restless.
insight: It shifts attention from outer abundance to inner readiness, showing that removal can refine you while dependence exposes you.
modern_relevance: Your room feels calm after you finally clear the piles from the floor. But if your savings suddenly drop and your whole mood collapses, this verse is showing you where attachment still rules.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिनु घन निर्मल सोह अकासा। हरिजन इव परिहरि सब आसा॥ कहुँ कहुँ बृष्टि सारदी थोरी। कोउ एक भाव भगति जिमि मोरी ॥
translation: बिना बादलों का निर्मल आकाश ऐसा शोभित हो रहा है जैसे भगवद्भक्त सब आशाओं को छोड़कर सुशोभित होते हैं। कहीं-कहीं (विरले ही स्थानों में) शरद् ऋतु की थोड़ी-थोड़ी वर्षा हो रही है। जैसे कोई विरले ही मेरी भक्ति पाते हैं ॥
english_translation: The clear sky shines without clouds, like devotees who have let go of every hope. Scattered showers of autumn fall here and there, just as only a rare few receive my devotion.
essence: Freedom from craving makes the heart clear enough for devotion.
simple_meaning: A mind without clinging becomes bright and open. True devotion is rare, and only a few people receive it deeply.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing outcomes to making inner space for devotion.
modern_relevance: You finally stop refreshing your phone for one message, and the room feels bigger. The quiet that follows is the same clearing Tulsidas points to.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: चले हरषि तजि नगर नृप तापस बनिक भिखारि। जिमि हरिभगति पाइ श्रम तजहिं आश्रमी चारि ॥
translation: (शरद् ऋतु पाकर) राजा, तपस्वी, व्यापारी और भिखारी (क्रमशः विजय, तप, व्यापार और भिक्षा के लिए) हर्षित होकर नगर छोड़कर चले। जैसे श्री हरि की भक्ति पाकर चारों आश्रम वाले (नाना प्रकार के साधन रूपी) श्रमों को त्याग देते हैं ॥
english_translation: Kings, ascetics, merchants, and beggars all left the city gladly. In the same way, when you find devotion to Hari, the weariness of all four life-stages falls away.
essence: Real devotion makes every lesser burden feel light.
simple_meaning: People leave their ordinary work gladly, because devotion to Hari makes all effort feel lighter and less burdensome.
insight: It shifts the mind from scattered striving to a single, steady orientation toward Ram.
modern_relevance: You finally close the laptop after chasing one more task, and the body feels empty but restless. Then something steadier takes over — the relief of caring for what matters most, not everything at once.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सुखी मीन जे नीर अगाधा। जिमि हरि सरन न एकऊ बाधा॥ फूलें कमल सोह सर कैसा। निर्गुन ब्रह्म सगुन भएँ जैसा ॥
translation: जो मछलियाँ अथाह जल में हैं, वे सुखी हैं, जैसे श्री हरि के शरण में चले जाने पर एक भी बाधा नहीं रहती। कमलों के फूलने से तालाब कैसी शोभा दे रहा है, जैसे निर्गुण ब्रह्म सगुण होने पर शोभित होता है ॥
english_translation: Fish are happy in deep water, just as no obstacle remains in Hari's refuge. A blooming lotus beautifies a lake, just as the formless supreme reality shines when it takes form.
essence: Complete refuge makes obstacles disappear and hidden greatness visible.
simple_meaning: Taking refuge in the divine removes all obstacles. The verse also says that the formless supreme reality becomes beautifully manifest through form, like a lotus brightening a lake.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to complete reliance, and from formless abstraction to living presence.
modern_relevance: You finally stop checking your phone after sending the hard message. The fear was in carrying it alone; once you place it where it belongs, the weight changes shape.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: गुंजत मधुकर मुखर अनूपा। सुंदर खग रव नाना रूपा॥ चक्रबाक मन दुख निसि पेखी। जिमि दुर्जन पर संपति देखी ॥
translation: भौंरे अनुपम शब्द करते हुए गूँज रहे हैं तथा पक्षियों के नाना प्रकार के सुंदर शब्द हो रहे हैं। रात्रि देखकर चकवे के मन में वैसे ही दुःख हो रहा है, जैसे दूसरे की संपत्ति देखकर दुष्ट को होता है ॥
english_translation: Bees hum with lovely, unmatched sounds, and birds sing in many beautiful tones. The chakravaka bird feels sorrow at night, just as a wicked person feels pain seeing another's prosperity.
essence: Another person's success only hurts the mind that compares.
simple_meaning: The scene is full of sweet bird calls and bee hums, but the chakravaka bird suffers at night. Tulsidas compares that pain to a bad person's jealousy at another's success.
insight: It trains the mind to notice envy as a self-created wound, not a response caused by the other person's gain.
modern_relevance: You scroll past a friend's promotion announcement and feel a twist in your chest. Their good news has not harmed you, but comparison has made it sting.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चातक रटत तृषा अति ओही। जिमि सुख लहइ न संकर द्रोही॥ सरदातप निसि ससि अपहरई। संत दरस जिमि पातक टरई ॥
translation: पपीहा रट लगाए है, उसको बड़ी प्यास है, जैसे श्री शंकरजी का द्रोही सुख नहीं पाता (सुख के लिए झीखता रहता है) शरद् ऋतु के ताप को रात के समय चंद्रमा हर लेता है, जैसे संतों के दर्शन से पाप दूर हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: The chatak bird keeps crying out in thirst, just as one who turns against Shiva finds no lasting peace. The moon removes the heat of a autumn night, just as the sight of holy people removes sin.
essence: Right company cools the thirst that nothing else can.
simple_meaning: A thirsty bird keeps calling for water. In the same way, the heart finds relief through holy company, and old wrongdoing falls away.
insight: It shifts you from chasing relief alone to seeking the company that naturally restores you.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is calm, and your shoulders drop without effort. The company around you can either inflame your restlessness or quietly wash it away.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि इंदु चकोर समुदाई। चितवहिं जिमि हरिजन हरि पाई॥ मसक दंस बीते हिम त्रासा। जिमि द्विज द्रोह किएँ कुल नासा ॥
translation: चकोरों के समुदाय चंद्रमा को देखकर इस प्रकार टकटकी लगाए हैं जैसे भगवद्भक्त भगवान् को पाकर उनके (निर्निमेष नेत्रों से) दर्शन करते हैं। मच्छर और डाँस जाड़े के डर से इस प्रकार नष्ट हो गए जैसे ब्राह्मण के साथ वैर करने से कुल का नाश हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Seeing the moon, the whole flock of chakoras gazes at it just as devotees gaze at the divine after finding the divine. Mosquitoes and gnats are destroyed by the fear of winter just as a family is ruined by hostility toward a brahmin.
essence: Longing can become a steady, wordless gaze; hostility can erase a whole line.
simple_meaning: The verse gives two similes from nature: chakoras stare at the moon the way devotees gaze at the divine, and small insects vanish in winter just as a family is ruined by hostility toward a brahmin.
insight: It trains the mind to read nature as a mirror for devotion and consequence.
modern_relevance: You notice how a child can stare at a beloved parent without blinking, or how one bitter feud can poison an entire household. The verse turns both into living images.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूमि जीव संकुल रहे गए सरद रितु पाइ। सदगुर मिलें जाहिं जिमि संसय भ्रम समुदाइ ॥
translation: (वर्षा ऋतु के कारण) पृथ्वी पर जो जीव भर गए थे, वे शरद् ऋतु को पाकर वैसे ही नष्ट हो गए जैसे सद्गुरु के मिल जाने पर संदेह और भ्रम के समूह नष्ट हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: The creatures crowded on the earth during the rainy season disappeared when autumn arrived, just as doubt and confusion disappear when a true teacher is found.
essence: A true teacher makes confusion fall away on contact.
simple_meaning: When autumn arrives, the earth is no longer crowded with creatures from the rains. In the same way, meeting a true teacher makes doubt and confusion disappear.
insight: It shifts the mind from wrestling with confusion to seeking clear guidance.
modern_relevance: You’ve been turning the same problem over in your head for weeks, and then one honest conversation cuts through everything. The mess was real, but it was never the whole picture.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: बरषा गत निर्मल रितु आई। सुधि न तात सीता कै पाई॥ एक बार कैसेहुँ सुधि जानौं। कालुह जीति निमिष महुँ आनौं ॥
translation: वर्षा बीत गई, निर्मल शरद्ऋतु आ गई, परंतु हे तात! सीता की कोई खबर नहीं मिली। एक बार कैसे भी पता पाऊँ तो काल को भी जीतकर पल भर में जानकी को ले आऊँ ॥
english_translation: The rains have ended and the clear season has come, but, O father, I have found no news of Sita. If I could learn her whereabouts even once, I would conquer time itself and bring Janaki back in an instant.
essence: A single clue can turn waiting into unstoppable action.
simple_meaning: Hanuman has reached the clear season, but he still has no news of Sita. He says that if he can find even one clue, he will overcome time and bring her back immediately.
insight: It turns longing into decisive action by showing how one clue can release total effort.
modern_relevance: You are waiting for a reply that will decide everything, and the silence is wearing you down. Then one small message arrives, and your whole body changes. Clarity does that.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: कतहुँ रहउ जौं जीवति होई। तात जतन करि आनउँ सोई॥ सुग्रीवहुँ सुधि मोरि बिसारी। पावा राज कोस पुर नारी ॥
translation: कहीं भी रहे, यदि जीती होगी तो हे तात! यत्न करके मैं उसे अवश्य लाऊँगा। राज्य, खजाना, नगर और स्त्री पा गया, इसलिए सुग्रीव ने भी मेरी सुध भुला दी ॥
english_translation: Wherever she may be, if she is still alive, I will search and bring her back with effort. Sugriva has forgotten my help now that he has gained kingdom, treasure, city, and woman.
essence: Love keeps searching even after being forgotten.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says he will search for Sita and bring her back if she is alive, even though Sugriva has forgotten his help after gaining power and comfort.
insight: It shifts attention from gratitude received to duty fulfilled.
modern_relevance: You helped someone through their worst week, and now they barely reply. The hurt is real. This verse reminds you that sincere service does not depend on being remembered.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: जेहिं सायक मारा मैं बाली। तेहिं सर हतौं मूढ़ कहँ काली॥ जासु कृपाँ छूटहिं मद मोहा। ता कहुँ उमा कि सपनेहुँ कोहा ॥
translation: जिस बाण से मैंने बालि को मारा था, उसी बाण से कल उस मूढ़ को मारूँ! (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! जिनकी कृपा से मद और मोह छूट जाते हैं उनको कहीं स्वप्न में भी क्रोध हो सकता है? (यह तो लीला मात्र है) ॥
english_translation: The same arrow with which I struck Bali, I would strike that fool tomorrow. O Uma, can those whom divine grace has freed from pride and delusion ever feel anger, even in a dream?
essence: When pride falls away, anger has no place to land.
simple_meaning: Shiva says the arrow that killed Bali would still be the right one, but only as divine play. Anyone freed from pride and confusion cannot truly feel anger.
insight: It shifts attention from the outer event to the inner distortion that makes anger possible.
modern_relevance: You replay a harsh message in your head and feel your chest tighten. Then you notice the real wound is not the text — it's the pride underneath it. Once that loosens, the anger loses its fuel.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: जानहिं यह चरित्र मुनि ग्यानी। जिन्ह रघुबीर चरन रति मानी॥ लछिमन क्रोधवंत प्रभु जाना। धनुष चढ़ाई गहे कर बाना ॥
translation: ज्ञानी मुनि जिन्होंने श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों में प्रीति मान ली है (जोड़ ली है), वे ही इस चरित्र (लीला रहस्य) को जानते हैं। लक्ष्मणजी ने जब प्रभु को क्रोधयुक्त जाना, तब उन्होंने धनुष चढ़ाकर बाण हाथ में ले लिए ॥
english_translation: Only wise sages who have placed their love at Raghubir’s feet know this secret play. When Lakshman saw the Lord angry, he raised his bow and took an arrow in hand.
essence: Ram’s deepest play opens only to devotion, and loyal love reacts without delay.
simple_meaning: Only those with deep devotion can understand Ram’s hidden play. Lakshman, seeing Ram angry, immediately picked up his bow and arrow.
insight: It shifts you from intellectual distance to devoted understanding and immediate protective action.
modern_relevance: You can read a situation a hundred times and still miss its meaning. The person who loves deeply often understands fastest, and acts before anyone else has finished explaining.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब अनुजहि समुझावा रघुपति करुना सींव। भय देखाइ लै आवहु तात सखा सुग्रीव ॥
translation: तब दया की सीमा श्री रघुनाथजी ने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी को समझाया कि हे तात! सखा सुग्रीव को केवल भय दिखलाकर ले आओ (उसे मारने की बात नहीं है) ॥
english_translation: Then Raghupati, full of compassion, explained to his younger brother: 'Dear brother, bring Sugriva here only by showing him fear.'
essence: Compassion sets the limit on force.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Lakshman to bring Sugriva by frightening him, not by killing him. Compassion guides even the use of force.
insight: It teaches you to apply pressure with restraint, so correction serves the relationship instead of damaging it.
modern_relevance: You catch a teammate hiding from a hard conversation. You do not need to crush them to get their attention; a firm warning can open the door to repair.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: इहाँ पवनसुत हृदयँ बिचारा। राम काजु सुग्रीवँ बिसारा॥ निकट जाइ चरनन्हि सिरु नावा। चारिहु बिधि तेहि कहि समुझावा ॥
translation: यहाँ (किष्किन्धा नगरी में) पवनकुमार श्री हनुमान् जी ने विचार किया कि सुग्रीव ने श्री रामजी के कार्य को भुला दिया। उन्होंने सुग्रीव के पास जाकर चरणों में सिर नवाया। (साम, दान, दंड, भेद) चारों प्रकार की नीति कहकर उन्हें समझाया ॥
english_translation: Here, Hanuman thought in his heart that Sugriva had forgotten Ram's work. He went close, bowed his head at Sugriva's feet, and explained the four methods of policy: conciliation, gifts, division, and force.
essence: True service corrects without pride and acts without noise.
simple_meaning: Hanuman notices that Sugriva has forgotten Ram's task. He approaches respectfully, bows, and gently reminds him using practical counsel.
insight: It teaches you to pair firmness with humility when someone forgets their responsibility.
modern_relevance: A teammate has drifted from the plan, and you need to bring them back without ego or embarrassment. Hanuman shows how to correct with dignity, not dominance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि सुग्रीवँ परम भय माना। बिषयँ मोर हरि लीन्हेउ ग्याना॥ अब मारुतसुत दूत समूहा। पठवहु जहँ तहँ बानर जूहा ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी के वचन सुनकर सुग्रीव ने बहुत ही भय माना। (और कहा-) विषयों ने मेरे ज्ञान को हर लिया। अब हे पवनसुत! जहाँ-तहाँ वानरों के यूथ रहते हैं, वहाँ दूतों के समूहों को भेजो ॥
english_translation: Hearing Hanuman's words, Sugriva felt great fear and said, 'Desires have stolen away my wisdom. Now, O son of the wind, send messengers to the monkey bands wherever they are.'
essence: Seeing your own confusion is the first step back to right action.
simple_meaning: Sugriva admits that desire has clouded his judgment and asks Hanuman to send messengers to all the monkey groups.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-deception to corrective action once distraction is recognised.
modern_relevance: You finally admit that craving has made you sloppy, and then you call the team, send the texts, and fix the mess before it spreads.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: कहहु पाख महुँ आव न जोई। मोरें कर ता कर बध होई॥ तब हनुमंत बोलाए दूता। सब कर करि सनमान बहूता ॥
translation: और कहला दो कि एक पखवाड़े में (पंद्रह दिनों में) जो न आ जाएगा, उसका मेरे हाथों वध होगा। तब हनुमान् जी ने दूतों को बुलाया और सबका बहुत सम्मान करके- ॥
english_translation: And say: whoever does not come within a fortnight will be killed by my hand. Then Hanuman called the messengers and honoured them all greatly.
essence: Firm boundaries can still be delivered with respect.
simple_meaning: Hanuman sends a firm warning: if someone does not return within fifteen days, he will be punished. Then he respectfully sends the messengers away.
insight: It shows how to combine authority with courtesy: enforce the standard, but keep your dignity intact.
modern_relevance: You have to send a hard message to a team that has gone slack, but you still choose your words carefully. Firmness does not require humiliation.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: भय अरु प्रीति नीति देखराई। चले सकल चरनन्हि सिर नाई॥ एहि अवसर लछिमन पुर आए। क्रोध देखि जहँ तहँ कपि धाए ॥
translation: सबको भय, प्रीति और नीति दिखलाई। सब बंदर चरणों में सिर नवाकर चले। इसी समय लक्ष्मणजी नगर में आए। उनका क्रोध देखकर बंदर जहाँ-तहाँ भागे ॥
english_translation: They showed fear, affection, and policy. All the monkeys bowed their heads and left. Just then Lakshman entered the city, and seeing his anger, the monkeys fled here and there.
essence: Lakshman’s anger instantly changes the whole mood of the city.
simple_meaning: The monkeys are brought under control by fear, affection, and good conduct. Then Lakshman arrives in anger, and they scatter.
insight: It shows how quickly a mood can spread through a group when one powerful person enters.
modern_relevance: A calm room can turn tense the moment the manager walks in with a hard face. People who were cooperating a second ago suddenly start looking for the nearest exit.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धनुष चढ़ाइ कहा तब जारि करउँ पुर छार। ब्याकुल नगर देखि तब आयउ बालिकुमार ॥
translation: तदनन्तर लक्ष्मणजी ने धनुष चढ़ाकर कहा कि नगर को जलाकर अभी राख कर दूँगा। तब नगरभर को व्याकुल देखकर बालिपुत्र अंगदजी उनके पास आए ॥
english_translation: Then Lakshman raised his bow and said, 'I will burn the city to ashes now.' Seeing the city in turmoil, Bali's son Angad came to him.
essence: Anger raises the stakes, and courage must answer it.
simple_meaning: Lakshman threatens to burn the city to ashes, and Angad comes forward when he sees the city in distress.
insight: It shows how force can shake people into action, but reconciliation still needs someone to step forward.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone says, 'Fine, I’ll handle this myself.' The threat changes the mood, but it also invites the first real response.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चर नाइ सिरु बिनती कीन्ही। लछिमन अभय बाँह तेहि दीन्ही॥ क्रोधवंत लछिमन सुनि काना। कह कपीस अति भयँ अकुलाना ॥
translation: अंगद ने उनके चरणों में सिर नवाकर विनती की (क्षमा-याचना की) तब लक्ष्मणजी ने उनको अभय बाँह दी (भुजा उठाकर कहा कि डरो मत)। सुग्रीव ने अपने कानों से लक्ष्मणजी को क्रोधयुक्त सुनकर भय से अत्यंत व्याकुल होकर कहा- ॥
english_translation: Angad bowed his head at their feet and pleaded for mercy. Lakshmana then raised his arm and gave him fearlessness. Hearing Lakshmana’s angry words, Sugriva became deeply alarmed and said—
essence: Mercy can calm a moment, but anger can keep fear alive.
simple_meaning: Angad asks for mercy, Lakshmana reassures him, and Sugriva is shaken by Lakshmana’s anger.
insight: It shows how quickly a room can shift from apology to relief to renewed fear.
modern_relevance: A tense group chat goes silent after one harsh message. Someone apologizes, one person softens, but another is still bracing for the next blow.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनु हनुमंत संग लै तारा। करि बिनती समुझाउ कुमारा॥ तारा सहित जाइ हनुमाना। चरन बंदि प्रभु सुजस बखाना ॥
translation: हे हनुमान् सुनो, तुम तारा को साथ ले जाकर विनती करके राजकुमार को समझाओ (समझा-बुझाकर शांत करो)। हनुमान् जी ने तारा सहित जाकर लक्ष्मणजी के चरणों की वंदना की और प्रभु के सुंदर यश का बखान किया ॥
english_translation: Hanuman, take Tara with you. Go with respectful words and calm the prince. Hanuman went with Tara, bowed at the feet of the Lord, and praised his glorious fame.
essence: Humility opens the door that anger has shut.
simple_meaning: Hanuman is sent with Tara to speak gently to Lakshman and calm the situation. He bows first, then praises Ram's glory.
insight: It teaches you to enter conflict with humility, not escalation, and to lead with reverence before persuasion.
modern_relevance: A heated family argument is one message away from exploding. Someone calmer steps in first, speaks with respect, and lowers the temperature before anyone tries to win.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: करि बिनती मंदिर लै आए। चरन पखारि पलँग बैठाए॥ तब कपीस चरनन्हि सिरु नावा। गहि भुज लछिमन कंठ लगावा ॥
translation: वे विनती करके उन्हें महल में ले आए तथा चरणों को धोकर उन्हें पलँग पर बैठाया। तब वानरराज सुग्रीव ने उनके चरणों में सिर नवाया और लक्ष्मणजी ने हाथ पकड़कर उनको गले से लगा लिया ॥
english_translation: They brought him in with a request, washed his feet, and seated him on a couch. Then Sugriva bowed his head at Lakshmana's feet, and Lakshmana embraced him by the arm and held him to his chest.
essence: Humility turns an enemy meeting into friendship.
simple_meaning: Sugriva welcomes Lakshmana with honor, bows to him, and receives a loving embrace in return.
insight: It shifts conflict into trust through visible humility and respect.
modern_relevance: You finally sit down with someone after a tense misunderstanding. One honest gesture — a lowered head, a warm hand, a careful welcome — changes the whole room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ विषय सम मद कछु नाहीं। मुनि मन मोह करइ छन माहीं। सुनत बिनीत बचन सुख पावा। लछिमन तेहि बहु बिधि समुझावा ॥
translation: (सुग्रीव ने कहा-) हे नाथ! विषय के समान और कोई मद नहीं है। यह मुनियों के मन में भी क्षणमात्र में मोह उत्पन्न कर देता है (फिर मैं तो विषयी जीव ही ठहरा)। सुग्रीव के विनययुक्त वचन सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी ने सुख पाया और उनको बहुत प्रकार से समझाया ॥
english_translation: (Sugriva said-) O Lord, there is no pride like desire for pleasure. It can bewilder even the minds of sages in a moment. Hearing his humble words, Lakshman felt pleased and explained many things to him in many ways.
essence: Desire can confuse even the wise; humility restores clear seeing.
simple_meaning: Desire for pleasure is so powerful it can confuse even wise people. Humble words can soften the heart and open the way to understanding.
insight: It shifts attention from judging others to noticing how desire distorts your own mind.
modern_relevance: You know that moment when a craving starts running the whole day — the third scroll, the extra drink, the need to be chosen. A humble conversation can interrupt that spiral before it hardens into conflict.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: पवन तनय सब कथा सुनाई। जेहि बिधि गए दूत समुदाई ॥
translation: तब पवनसुत हनुमान् जी ने जिस प्रकार सब दिशाओं में दूतों के समूह गए थे वह सब हाल सुनाया ॥
english_translation: Then Hanuman, son of the wind, told the whole story of how the envoys had gone out in all directions.
essence: A report moves the alliance toward its next step.
simple_meaning: Hanuman recounts how the messengers had been sent out in every direction.
insight: It keeps attention on the unfolding action rather than on a standalone lesson.
modern_relevance: You finish a briefing and simply pass along what happened so the next step can begin.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरषि चले सुग्रीव तब अंगदादि कपि साथ। रामानुज आगें करि आए जहँ रघुनाथ ॥
translation: तब अंगद आदि वानरों को साथ लेकर और श्री रामजी के छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी को आगे करके (अर्थात् उनके पीछे-पीछे) सुग्रीव हर्षित होकर चले और जहाँ रघुनाथजी थे वहाँ आए ॥
english_translation: Then Sugriva, delighted, set out with Angada and the other monkeys, placing Lakshmana in front, and came to where Raghunath was.
essence: Trust now has legs and is walking toward Ram.
simple_meaning: Sugriva, along with Angada and the monkeys, went happily to meet Ram, with Lakshmana leading the way.
insight: It turns a promise into a meeting, showing trust becoming visible action.
modern_relevance: After days of tense messages, you finally walk into the room where the other side is waiting. The stiffness is gone; respect and relief now do the work.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाइ चरन सिरु कह कर जोरी॥ नाथ मोहि कछु नाहिन खोरी॥ अतिसय प्रबल देव तव माया॥ छूटइ राम करहु जौं दाया ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर हाथ जोड़कर सुग्रीव ने कहा- हे नाथ! मुझे कुछ भी दोष नहीं है। हे देव! आपकी माया अत्यंत ही प्रबल है। आप जब दया करते हैं, हे राम! तभी यह छूटती है ॥
english_translation: Bowing his head to Ram's feet and joining his hands, Sugriva said, 'Lord, I have no fault. Your veil of appearance is very powerful. It falls away only when you show mercy, Ram.'
essence: Only mercy can lift the veil that keeps you confused.
simple_meaning: Sugriva bows to Ram and admits that the power of appearance is overwhelming. He says only Ram's mercy can free someone from it.
insight: It shifts blame away from personal failure and toward the deeper force of appearance that mercy can dissolve.
modern_relevance: You keep circling the same mistake, sure the problem is your weakness. Then one honest conversation reveals how much of the confusion was the mind's own veil.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: बिषय बस्य सुर नर मुनि स्वामी॥ मैं पावँर पसु कपि अति कामी॥ नारि नयन सर जाहि न लागा। घोर क्रोध तम निसि जो जागा ॥
translation: हे स्वामी! देवता, मनुष्य और मुनि सभी विषयों के वश में हैं। फिर मैं तो पामर पशु और पशुओं में भी अत्यंत कामी बंदर हूँ। स्त्री का नयन बाण जिसको नहीं लगा, जो भयंकर क्रोध रूपी अँधेरी रात में भी जागता रहता है (क्रोधान्ध नहीं होता) ॥
english_translation: All radiant beings, humans, sages, and rulers are bound by desire. I am a miserable creature, a lowly monkey, and intensely driven by craving. The arrow from a woman's eyes has not struck me, and I remain awake even in the dark night of fierce anger.
essence: Humility sees its own weakness and becomes ready for mercy.
simple_meaning: Sugriva humbly says that even great beings are often ruled by desire, while he feels even more vulnerable and full of craving.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-justification to clear self-recognition before asking for help.
modern_relevance: You sit in front of someone whose approval could change everything, and instead of pretending, you admit your weakness. That kind of honesty can be the beginning of trust.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: लोभ पाँस जेहिं गर न बँधाया। सो नर तुम्ह समान रघुराया॥ यह गुन साधन तें नहिं होई। तुम्हरी कृपा पाव कोइ कोई ॥
translation: और लोभ की फाँसी से जिसने अपना गला नहीं बँधाया, हे रघुनाथजी! वह मनुष्य आप ही के समान है। ये गुण साधन से नहीं प्राप्त होते। आपकी कृपा से ही कोई-कोई इन्हें पाते हैं ॥
english_translation: A person who has not bound their neck in the noose of greed is like you, Raghunath. Such qualities are not gained by practice; only a rare few receive them by your grace.
essence: Freedom from greed is a gift, not a personal achievement.
simple_meaning: A person who is free from greed is like Ram. Such qualities cannot be forced through practice alone; they come only by grace.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-made virtue to receptive humility before grace.
modern_relevance: You open your banking app after a salary hike and still feel hungry for more. This verse reminds you that some freedom cannot be manufactured by ambition alone.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: तब रघुपति बोले मुसुकाई। तुम्ह प्रिय मोहि भरत जिमि भाई॥ अब सोइ जतनु करह मन लाई। जेहि बिधि सीता कै सुधि पाई ॥
translation: तब श्री रघुनाथजी मुस्कुराकर बोले- हे भाई! तुम मुझे भरत के समान प्यारे हो। अब मन लगाकर वही उपाय करो जिस उपाय से सीता की खबर मिले ॥
english_translation: Then Raghupati smiled and said, "You are dear to me, brother, just as Bharat is. Now apply your mind to the same effort by which Sita's news can be found."
essence: Being dear to Ram means helping with what matters most.
simple_meaning: Ram smiles and tells Hanuman that he is as dear as Bharat, then asks him to use his full attention to find news of Sita.
insight: It links closeness with responsibility: real affection becomes careful, purposeful action.
modern_relevance: A friend trusts you with something precious, not because you bragged, but because you stayed steady. That quiet trust changes everything about how you show up.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: एहि बिधि होत बतकही आए बानर जूथ। नाना बरन सकल दिसि देखिअ कीस बरूथ ॥
translation: इस प्रकार बातचीत हो रही थी कि वानरों के यूथ (झुंड) आ गए। अनेक रंगों के वानरों के दल सब दिशाओं में दिखाई देने लगे ॥
english_translation: While they were talking like this, the monkey troops arrived. Monkey bands of many colors became visible in every direction.
essence: The meeting gives way to a gathering army.
simple_meaning: The conversation is interrupted as monkey troops arrive from all directions in many colors.
insight: It shifts attention from the exchange itself to the gathering force around it.
modern_relevance: You are still talking through the plan when the team starts arriving, each person bringing a different strength. The moment shifts from discussion to momentum.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बानर कटक उमा मैं देखा। सो मूरुख जो करन चह लेखा॥ आइ राम पद नावहिं माथा। निरखि बदनु सब होहिं सनाथा ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! वानरों की वह सेना मैंने देखी थी। उसकी जो गिनती करना चाहे वह महान् मूर्ख है। सब वानर आ-आकर श्री रामजी के चरणों में मस्तक नवाते हैं और (सौंदर्य-माधुर्यनिधि) श्रीमुख के दर्शन करके कृतार्थ होते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Uma, I saw that army of monkeys. Anyone who tries to count it is a fool. They come and bow their heads at Ram's feet, and by seeing his face they feel fulfilled.
essence: Real greatness makes counting irrelevant and devotion natural.
