simple_meaning: The monkey army is too vast to count, and every monkey comes to bow before Ram and feels complete just by seeing him.
insight: It shifts attention from quantity and spectacle to the quiet power of reverent presence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a crowded hall and still notice one person everyone keeps turning toward. It isn't numbers that matter — it's the kind of presence that makes people bow their heads without being asked.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: अस कपि एक न सेना माहीं। राम कुसल जेहि पूछी नाहीं॥ यह कछु नहिं प्रभु कइ अधिकाई। बिस्वरूप ब्यापक रघुराई ॥
translation: सेना में एक भी वानर ऐसा नहीं था जिससे श्री रामजी ने कुशल न पूछी हो, प्रभु के लिए यह कोई बड़ी बात नहीं है, क्योंकि श्री रघुनाथजी विश्वरूप तथा सर्वव्यापक हैं (सारे रूपों और सब स्थानों में हैं) ॥
english_translation: Not a single monkey in the army had been left unasked about by Ram. This is no great feat for the Lord, because Raghunath is all-pervading and of universal form.
essence: What seems impossible to others is effortless for the all-pervading Ram.
simple_meaning: Ram asked after every monkey in the army, and that is natural for him because he is present everywhere in every form.
insight: It shifts reverence from spectacle to presence: true greatness notices everyone without strain.
modern_relevance: You walk into a crowded family gathering and somehow the one person everyone overlooks remembers your name, your work, and the thing you were worried about. That kind of attention feels impossible — until love makes it natural.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: ठाढ़े जहँ तहँ आयसु पाई। कह सुग्रीव सबहि समुझाई॥ राम काजु अरु मोर निहोरा। बानर जूथ जाहु चहुँ ओरा ॥
translation: आज्ञा पाकर सब जहाँ-तहाँ खड़े हो गए। तब सुग्रीव ने सबको समझाकर कहा कि हे वानरों के समूहों! यह श्री रामचंद्रजी का कार्य है और मेरा निहोरा (अनुरोध) है, तुम चारों ओर जाओ ॥
english_translation: Receiving the order, everyone stood where they were. Then Sugriva explained to all of them and said, “This is Ram’s task and my request: O troop of monkeys, go in all directions.”
essence: Clear command turns loyalty into movement.
simple_meaning: Sugriva gives the search party their assignment: this is Ram’s work, and he wants them to spread out in every direction.
insight: It turns intention into coordinated action by giving each person a clear role.
modern_relevance: A team gathers after the plan is finally approved. Instead of more debate, someone assigns the next steps clearly, and the whole room shifts from waiting to moving.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: जनकसुता कहुँ खोजहु जाई। मास दिवस महँ आएहु भाई॥ अवधि मेटि जो बिनु सुधि पाएँ। आवइ बनिहि सो मोहि मराएँ ॥
translation: और जाकर जानकीजी को खोजो। हे भाई! महीने भर में वापस आ जाना। जो (महीने भर की) अवधि बिताकर बिना पता लगाए ही लौट आएगा उसे मेरे द्वारा मरवाते ही बनेगा (अर्थात् मुझे उसका वध करवाना ही पड़ेगा) ॥
english_translation: Go search for Janaka's daughter, and return within a month, brother. If you come back without finding her after the deadline, I will have you put to death.
essence: Urgent duty becomes real only when time is fixed.
simple_meaning: Sugriva sends the monkeys out to search for Sita and gives them a strict time limit. He makes it clear that failure to return with news will bring punishment.
insight: It teaches you to set firm deadlines when a task matters, so effort becomes focused and accountable.
modern_relevance: You tell your team to find the missing file before the client call, not 'sometime today.' Clear urgency changes scattered effort into real search.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: बचन सुनत सब बानर जहँ तहँ चले तुरंत। तब सुग्रीवँ बोलाए अंगद नल हनुमंत ॥
translation: सुग्रीव के वचन सुनते ही सब वानर तुरंत जहाँ-तहाँ (भिन्न-भिन्न दिशाओं में) चल दिए। तब सुग्रीव ने अंगद, नल, हनुमान् आदि प्रधान-प्रधान योद्धाओं को बुलाया (और कहा-) ॥
english_translation: As soon as they heard Sugriva's words, all the monkeys left at once in different directions. Then Sugriva called Angad, Nala, Hanuman, and the others.
essence: Clear command turns many hands into one search.
simple_meaning: The monkeys split up immediately after Sugriva's order, and he then summoned the chief warriors.
insight: It shifts attention from intention to organised action under a trusted leader.
modern_relevance: A team meeting ends, and everyone moves without confusion because the next action is clear. No drama, no delay — just clean execution.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनहु नील अंगद हनुमाना। जामवंत मतिधीर सुजाना॥ सकल सुभट मिलि दच्छिन जाहू। सीता सुधि पूँछेहु सब काहू ॥
translation: हे धीरबुद्धि और चतुर नील, अंगद, जाम्बवान् और हनुमान! तुम सब श्रेष्ठ योद्धा मिलकर दक्षिण दिशा को जाओ और सब किसी से सीताजी का पता पूछना ॥
english_translation: Listen, Neel, Angad, Hanuman, and wise Jambavan. All of you brave warriors should go south and ask everyone for news of Sita.
essence: Urgent service becomes effective when brave people move as one.
simple_meaning: Sugriva sends Hanuman, Angad, Neel, and Jambavan south to search for Sita and ask everyone they meet.
insight: It teaches you to turn concern into organized action instead of scattered worry.
modern_relevance: A group chat fills with panic after someone goes missing. One person calls, another checks the route, another asks neighbors. This verse is about coordinated effort when the situation is urgent.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: मन क्रम बचन सो जतन बिचारेहु। रामचंद्र कर काजु सँवारेहु॥ भानु पीठि सेइअ उर आगी। स्वामिहि सर्ब भाव छल त्यागी ॥
translation: मन, वचन तथा कर्म से उसी का (सीताजी का पता लगाने का) उपाय सोचना। श्री रामचंद्रजी का कार्य संपन्न (सफल) करना। सूर्य को पीठ से और अग्नि को हृदय से (सामने से) सेवन करना चाहिए, परंतु स्वामी की सेवा तो छल छोड़कर सर्वभाव से (मन, वचन, कर्म से) करनी चाहिए ॥
english_translation: Think of a way with mind, words, and action. Carry out Ramchandra's task. Serve the sun from behind and fire from the front, but serve your master with all your being, without deceit.
essence: True service gives Ram your whole mind, not just your hands.
simple_meaning: Use your whole mind, speech, and action for the work in front of you. Serve your master sincerely, without trickery or divided loyalty.
insight: It shifts service from reluctant compliance to wholehearted commitment.
modern_relevance: You agree to help a friend move, but you keep checking your phone and hoping the day ends quickly. This verse calls you back to full presence: do the task cleanly, without hidden resistance.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: तजि माया सेइअ परलोका। मिटहिं सकल भवसंभव सोका॥ देह धरे कर यह फलु भाई। भजिअ राम सब काम बिहाई ॥
translation: माया (विषयों की ममता-आसक्ति) को छोड़कर परलोक का सेवन (भगवान के दिव्य धाम की प्राप्ति के लिए भगवत्सेवा रूप साधन) करना चाहिए, जिससे भव (जन्म-मरण) से उत्पन्न सारे शोक मिट जाएँ। हे भाई! देह धारण करने का यही फल है कि सब कामों (कामनाओं) को छोड़कर श्री रामजी का भजन ही किया जाए ॥
english_translation: Give up illusion and serve the higher realm. Then all sorrow born from becoming and becoming again is erased. O brother, the true fruit of having a body is to छोड़ all desires and worship Ram.
essence: Letting go of craving reveals the real purpose of being alive.
simple_meaning: Let go of attachment to worldly illusion and devote yourself to Ram. That is how sorrow ends and life becomes meaningful.
insight: It shifts attention from chasing wants to anchoring life in devotion.
modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone, hoping one more message will settle your mind. It doesn't. The ache eases when you stop feeding craving and give your attention to what matters most.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सोइ गुनग्य सोई बड़भागी। जो रघुबीर चरन अनुरागी॥ आयसु मागि चरन सिरु नाई। चले हरषि सुमिरत रघुराई ॥
translation: सद्गुणों को पहचानने वाला (गुणवान) तथा बड़भागी वही है जो श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों का प्रेमी है। आज्ञा माँगकर और चरणों में फिर सिर नवाकर श्री रघुनाथजी का स्मरण करते हुए सब हर्षित होकर चले ॥
english_translation: Only the one who loves Raghubir's feet is truly wise and truly fortunate. They asked for permission, bowed their heads to his feet, and departed joyfully, remembering Raghu's lord.
essence: Loving Ram matters more than being clever or fortunate.
simple_meaning: Real wisdom and real good fortune belong to the person who loves Ram deeply. With his permission, they bowed, remembered him, and went away happily.
insight: It shifts value from status or cleverness to loving alignment with Ram.
modern_relevance: You leave a difficult meeting, not with a victory speech, but with quiet relief because you stayed honest. What makes the moment meaningful is not applause — it's that your heart stayed aligned.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पाछें पवन तनय सिरु नावा। जानि काज प्रभु निकट बोलावा॥ परसा सीस सरोरुह पानी। करमुद्रिका दीन्हि जन जानी ॥
translation: सबके पीछे पवनसुत श्री हनुमान् जी ने सिर नवाया। कार्य का विचार करके प्रभु ने उन्हें अपने पास बुलाया। उन्होंने अपने करकमल से उनके सिर का स्पर्श किया तथा अपना सेवक जानकर उन्हें अपने हाथ की अँगूठी उतारकर दी ॥
english_translation: Hanuman bowed his head from behind. Knowing the purpose, the Lord called him near. He touched Hanuman's head like a lotus with his hand and gave him his ring, recognizing him as a servant.
essence: Quiet service is what brings you closest.
simple_meaning: Hanuman bows before Ram, and Ram calls him close, touches his head, and gives him a ring as a sign of trust and service.
insight: It shifts attention from self-display to faithful readiness. Service, not status, becomes the mark of closeness.
modern_relevance: You stay late to help without making noise, and the right person notices. A quiet act of service can open the next door.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहु प्रकार सीतहि समुझाएहु। कहि बल बिरह बेगि तुम्ह आएहु॥ हनुमत जन्म सुफल करि माना। चलेउ हृदयँ धरि कृपानिधाना ॥
translation: (और कहा-) बहुत प्रकार से सीता को समझाना और मेरा बल तथा विरह (प्रेम) कहकर तुम शीघ्र लौट आना। हनुमान् जी ने अपना जन्म सफल समझा और कृपानिधान प्रभु को हृदय में धारण करके वे चले ॥
english_translation: “Tell Sita many things for me. Tell her of my strength and my longing, and come back quickly.” Hanuman considered his birth fulfilled and departed, holding the merciful Lord in his heart.
essence: A life becomes fruitful when it is spent carrying love for Ram.
simple_meaning: Ram asks Hanuman to reassure Sita and return quickly. Hanuman feels his life has succeeded because he has served Ram and carries Ram in his heart.
insight: It shifts service from a task to a sacred fulfillment of relationship.
modern_relevance: You finally get the message that someone you love has been waiting for. The errand is simple, but it feels sacred because it lets you carry care across distance.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जद्यपि प्रभु जानत सब बाता। राजनीति राखत सुरत्राता ॥
translation: यद्यपि देवताओं की रक्षा करने वाले प्रभु सब बात जानते हैं, तो भी वे राजनीति की रक्षा कर रहे हैं (नीति की मर्यादा रखने के लिए सीताजी का पता लगाने को जहाँ-तहाँ वानरों को भेज रहे हैं) ॥
english_translation: Although the Lord who protects the radiant beings knows everything, he still upholds righteous conduct.
essence: Even perfect knowledge still respects the right way to act.
simple_meaning: Ram already knows where Sita is, but he still sends the monkeys out to search so the search follows proper conduct and dignity.
insight: It shifts you from chasing efficiency alone to respecting the integrity of the process.
modern_relevance: You already know the shortcut would work, but you still choose the honest process: the interview, the apology, the careful check, the extra step that keeps your actions clean.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चले सकल बन खोजत सरिता सर गिरि खोह। राम काज लयलीन मन बिसरा तन कर छोह ॥
translation: सब वानर वन, नदी, तालाब, पर्वत और पर्वतों की कन्दराओं में खोजते हुए चले जा रहे हैं। मन श्री रामजी के कार्य में लवलीन है। शरीर तक का प्रेम (ममत्व) भूल गया है ॥
english_translation: The monkey band moved through forests, rivers, lakes, mountains, and caves in search. Their minds were absorbed in Ram's work, and even attachment to the body was forgotten.
essence: When Ram's work fills the mind, personal comfort disappears.
simple_meaning: The monkey army keeps searching everywhere, completely absorbed in Ram's mission. They are so focused that they forget even bodily comfort and attachment.
insight: It shows how wholehearted service can dissolve self-importance and make effort fearless.
modern_relevance: A team stays late combing through messages, documents, and files because someone needs an answer tonight. Nobody is thinking about sleep, snacks, or credit anymore.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कतहुँ होइ निसिचर सैं भेटा। प्रान लेहिं एक एक चपेटा॥ बहु प्रकार गिरि कानन हेरहिं। कोउ मुनि मिलइ ताहि सब घेरहिं ॥
translation: कहीं किसी राक्षस से भेंट हो जाती है, तो एक-एक चपत में ही उसके प्राण ले लेते हैं। पर्वतों और वनों को बहुत प्रकार से खोज रहे हैं। कोई मुनि मिल जाता है तो पता पूछने के लिए उसे सब घेर लेते हैं ॥
english_translation: Sometimes they ran into a demon, and killed him with a single slap. They searched mountains and forests in many ways. If they met a sage, they surrounded him all at once to ask for directions.
essence: The search continues through danger, question, and motion.
simple_meaning: The search party moves through forests and mountains, defeating hostile beings on the way and surrounding any sage they meet to ask for directions.
insight: It shows steady, practical searching under pressure, with no pause for comfort or hesitation.
modern_relevance: You are lost in a new city, checking lane after lane, asking strangers, and getting nowhere fast. The only option is to keep moving and keep asking.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लागि तृषा अतिसय अकुलाने। मिलइ न जल घन गहन भुलाने॥ मन हनुमान् कीन्ह अनुमाना। मरन चहत सब बिनु जल पाना ॥
translation: इतने में ही सबको अत्यंत प्यास लगी, जिससे सब अत्यंत ही व्याकुल हो गए, किंतु जल कहीं नहीं मिला। घने जंगल में सब भुला गए। हनुमान् जी ने मन में अनुमान किया कि जल पिए बिना सब लोग मरना ही चाहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Everyone became terribly thirsty and restless, but no water could be found. Lost in the deep forest, they forgot the way. Hanuman understood in his mind that they seemed ready to die without water.
essence: Clear seeing begins when you notice exhaustion before collapse.
simple_meaning: The search has gone on so long that everyone is thirsty, lost, and close to collapse. Hanuman notices their condition and quietly understands the danger.
insight: It trains attention to read the real condition of a group before the situation turns desperate.
modern_relevance: You keep walking through a long, hot afternoon with no bottle, no shade, and no clear direction. Before panic starts, someone has to notice what exhaustion is doing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चढ़ि गिरि सिखर चहूँ दिसि देखा। भूमि बिबर एक कौतुक पेखा॥ चक्रबाक बक हंस उड़ाहीं। बहुतक खग प्रबिसहिं तेहि माहीं ॥
translation: उन्होंने पहाड़ की चोटी पर चढ़कर चारों ओर देखा तो पृथ्वी के अंदर एक गुफा में उन्हें एक कौतुक (आश्चर्य) दिखाई दिया। उसके ऊपर चकवे, बगुले और हंस उड़ रहे हैं और बहुत से पक्षी उसमें प्रवेश कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: They climbed the mountain peak and looked in all four directions. They saw a curious cave in the earth. Cranes, herons, and swans flew above it, and many birds entered it.
essence: A higher view reveals the hidden opening.
simple_meaning: From the mountain top, they spot a strange cave filled with birds flying in and out.
insight: It trains attention to notice unusual openings that a hurried mind would overlook.
modern_relevance: You climb to the top of a parking garage to get signal and notice a hidden stairwell you had missed below. A clue appears only after you change your vantage point.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गिरि ते उतरि पवनसुत आवा। सब कहुँ लै सोइ बिबर देखावा॥ आगें कै हनुमंतहि लीन्हा। पैठे बिबर बिलंबु न कीन्हा ॥
translation: पवन कुमार हनुमान् जी पर्वत से उतर आए और सबको ले जाकर उन्होंने वह गुफा दिखलाई। सबने हनुमान् जी को आगे कर लिया और वे गुफा में घुस गए, देर नहीं की ॥
english_translation: Hanuman came down from the mountain and showed everyone the cave. They placed Hanuman in front and entered the cave without delay.
essence: The one who sees clearly also leads the way.
simple_meaning: Hanuman leads the others to the cave, and they enter quickly without hesitation.
insight: It shifts attention from the discovery itself to the trust that lets the group move together.
modern_relevance: You spot a narrow stairwell behind a locked door, and the person who noticed it first goes ahead. The group follows because confidence is contagious.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दीख जाइ उपबन बर सर बिगसित बहु कंज। मंदिर एक रुचिर तहँ बैठि नारि तप पुंज ॥
translation: अंदर जाकर उन्होंने एक उत्तम उपवन (बगीचा) और तालाब देखा, जिसमें बहुत से कमल खिले हुए हैं। वहीं एक सुंदर मंदिर है, जिसमें एक तपोमूर्ति स्त्री बैठी है ॥
english_translation: Entering inside, they saw a beautiful garden and a lake with many blooming lotuses. There stood a lovely hermitage, where a woman of great austerity sat.
essence: The search leads them to a hidden presence of purity and patience.
simple_meaning: They go inside and find a beautiful garden, a lotus-filled lake, and a woman absorbed in austerity.
insight: It shifts attention from movement and searching to the quiet revelation waiting inside the unknown.
modern_relevance: You follow a lead into a place you barely understand and suddenly find the clue you were hoping for. The moment is still, clear, and charged with meaning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दूरि ते ताहि सबन्हि सिरु नावा। पूछें निज बृत्तांत सुनावा॥ तेहिं तब कहा करहु जल पाना। खाहु सुरस सुंदर फल नाना ॥
translation: दूर से ही सबने उसे सिर नवाया और पूछने पर अपना सब वृत्तांत कह सुनाया। तब उसने कहा- जलपान करो और भाँति-भाँति के रसीले सुंदर फल खाओ ॥
english_translation: From afar, everyone bowed their heads to him and, when asked, told their whole story. Then he said, "Drink water and eat the many sweet, beautiful fruits."
essence: Respect and hospitality open the door before words do.
simple_meaning: They greet him respectfully, tell him their story, and he welcomes them with food and drink.
insight: It shows how care begins with welcoming the other person before asking anything more.
modern_relevance: You walk into a house where nobody knows you yet, and the first thing offered is water and food. Before any explanation, simple kindness changes the whole mood.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: मज्जनु कीन्ह मधुर फल खाए। तासु निकट पुनि सब चलि आए॥ तेहिं सब आपनि कथा सुनाई। मैं अब जाब जहाँ रघुराई ॥
translation: (आज्ञा पाकर) सबने स्नान किया, मीठे फल खाए और फिर सब उसके पास चले आए। तब उसने अपनी सब कथा कह सुनाई (और कहा-) मैं अब वहाँ जाऊँगी जहाँ श्री रघुनाथजी हैं ॥
english_translation: After bathing and eating sweet fruit, they all came back to him. Then he told them his story and said, “I will now go where Raghunath is.”
essence: Rest is not the end; devotion keeps walking toward Ram.
simple_meaning: After the meal, the group gathers again, listens to the story, and the speaker chooses to go where Ram is.
insight: It shifts attention from temporary comfort to the deeper direction your life is taking.
modern_relevance: You finally sit down after a long day, eat something warm, and the noise in your head softens. But one quiet thought remains: where is the place, or person, your heart is actually moving toward?
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: मूदहु नयन बिबर तजि जाहू। पैहहु सीतहि जनि पछिताहू॥ नयन मूदि पुनि देखहिं बीरा। ठाढ़े सकल सिंधु कें तीरा ॥
translation: तुम लोग आँखें मूँद लो और गुफा को छोड़कर बाहर जाओ। तुम सीताजी को पा जाओगे, पछताओ नहीं (निराश न होओ)। आँखें मूँदकर फिर जब आँखें खोलीं तो सब वीर क्या देखते हैं कि सब समुद्र के तीर पर खड़े हैं ॥
english_translation: Close your eyes and leave the cave. You will find Sita; do not regret it. When the warriors shut their eyes and open them again, they are standing on the seashore.
essence: Trust can carry you where sight alone cannot.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells the search party to trust him and leave the cave. When they obey, they find themselves at the seashore, close to Sita's trail.
insight: It shifts the mind from anxious overthinking to obedient trust in a clearer guide.
modern_relevance: You are stuck in a problem so long that your own thinking starts to feel like the only map. Then someone who sees more clearly says, 'Follow me,' and the next step appears before you can explain it.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: सो पुनि गई जहाँ रघुनाथा। जाइ कमल पद नाएसि माथा॥ नाना भाँति बिनय तेहिं कीन्हीं। अनपायनी भगति प्रभु दीन्हीं ॥
translation: और वह स्वयं वहाँ गई जहाँ श्री रघुनाथजी थे। उसने जाकर प्रभु के चरण कमलों में मस्तक नवाया और बहुत प्रकार से विनती की। प्रभु ने उसे अपनी अनपायिनी (अचल) भक्ति दी ॥
english_translation: She went there where Raghunath was. She bowed her head at his lotus feet and prayed in many ways; the Lord granted her unwavering devotion.
essence: True humility opens the door to lasting devotion.
simple_meaning: She goes to Ram, bows at his feet, and prays sincerely. In response, Ram gives her steady devotion that does not break.
insight: It shifts the reader from self-protection to sincere surrender, showing that humility can receive what pride cannot.
modern_relevance: You finally walk into the room and admit what you need instead of performing strength. That honest bow can change the whole relationship.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बदरीबन कहुँ सो गई प्रभु अग्या धरि सीस। उर धरि राम चरन जुग जे बंदत अज ईस ॥
translation: प्रभु की आज्ञा सिर पर धारण कर और श्री रामजी के युगल चरणों को, जिनकी ब्रह्मा और महेश भी वंदना करते हैं, हृदय में धारण कर वह (स्वयंप्रभा) बदरिकाश्रम को चली गई ॥
english_translation: Taking the Lord's command upon her head, and holding in her heart Ram's twin feet, which even Brahma and Shiva worship, she went to Badarivan.
essence: True devotion obeys outwardly while staying inwardly with Ram.
simple_meaning: She leaves by accepting Ram's command completely and keeping his feet in her heart. Obedience and devotion move together.
insight: It teaches you to let duty and devotion work together, instead of treating obedience as cold and love as vague.
modern_relevance: You get a hard message from someone you trust, and you don't argue with it for three hours. You absorb it, keep your heart steady, and do what needs doing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: इहाँ बिचारहिं कपि मन माहीं। बीती अवधि काज कछु नाहीं॥ सब मिलि कहहिं परस्पर बाता। बिनु सुधि लएँ करब का भ्राता ॥
translation: यहाँ वानरगण मन में विचार कर रहे हैं कि अवधि तो बीत गई, पर काम कुछ न हुआ। सब मिलकर आपस में बात करने लगे कि हे भाई! अब तो सीताजी की खबर लिए बिना लौटकर भी क्या करेंगे! ॥
english_translation: The monkeys were thinking in their hearts: the time limit had passed, and nothing had been done. They all spoke among themselves: Brother, what use is it to return without news of Sita?
essence: Without the one answer that matters, even returning feels empty.
simple_meaning: The search has run out of time, and the monkeys have still found no news of Sita. They wonder what returning would even mean without that news.
insight: It shifts attention from completing the trip to confronting the real unmet need.
modern_relevance: You’ve spent the whole day chasing leads, and the one message that matters still hasn’t come. At some point, the question becomes: what is returning without resolution?
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह अंगद लोचन भरि बारी। दुहुँ प्रकार भइ मृत्यु हमारी॥ इहाँ न सुधि सीता कै पाई। उहाँ गएँ मारिहि कपिराई ॥
translation: अंगद ने नेत्रों में जल भरकर कहा कि दोनों ही प्रकार से हमारी मृत्यु हुई। यहाँ तो सीताजी की सुध नहीं मिली और वहाँ जाने पर वानरराज सुग्रीव मार डालेंगे ॥
english_translation: Angad, eyes full of tears, said, 'We have died in both ways. Here we have found no news of Sita, and if we return there, Sugriva will kill us.'
essence: When the mission fails, even returning home can feel dangerous.
simple_meaning: Angad says the search has failed in every direction: they found no news of Sita, and returning home feels deadly too.
insight: It captures the pressure of a mission where every option seems costly and no outcome feels safe.
modern_relevance: You miss the deadline, and the client is angry either way: stay and keep fixing it, or send it in and risk blame. Angad knows that trapped feeling.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: पिता बधे पर मारत मोही। राखा राम निहोर न ओही॥ पुनि पुनि अंगद कह सब पाहीं। मरन भयउ कछु संसय नाहीं ॥
translation: वे तो पिता के वध होने पर ही मुझे मार डालते। श्री रामजी ने ही मेरी रक्षा की, इसमें सुग्रीव का कोई एहसान नहीं है। अंगद बार-बार सबसे कह रहे हैं कि अब मरण हुआ, इसमें कुछ भी संदेह नहीं है ॥
english_translation: They would have killed me when my father was slain. Ram protected me, not Sugriva. Angad keeps telling everyone again and again: death has come, and there is no doubt about it.
essence: Real rescue makes self-importance disappear.
simple_meaning: Angad says he would have died already if Ram had not protected him. He tells the others that death is certain and there is no doubt left.
insight: It shifts attention from self-credit to the unseen support that made survival possible.
modern_relevance: You look back on a crisis and realise you did not make it through on your own. Someone's protection, timing, or grace carried you farther than pride wants to admit.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: अंगद बचन सुन कपि बीरा। बोलि न सकहिं नयन बह नीरा॥ छन एक सोच मगन होइ रहे। पुनि अस बचन कहत सब भए ॥
translation: वानर वीर अंगद के वचन सुनते हैं, किंतु कुछ बोल नहीं सकते। उनके नेत्रों से जल बह रहा है। एक क्षण के लिए सब सोच में मग्न हो रहे। फिर सब ऐसा वचन कहने लगे- ॥
english_translation: Hearing Angad's words, the monkey warriors could not speak; tears flowed from their eyes. For a moment they sat lost in thought, and then all began to speak thus.
essence: Pain can silence a crowd before it turns into resolve.
simple_meaning: Angad's words leave the monkey warriors speechless and tearful for a moment before they respond together.
insight: It shows grief and resolve arriving together, before the group turns pain into a shared response.
modern_relevance: You hear a hard truth in a room and nobody can speak for a second. The silence itself shows how deeply it landed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हम सीता कै सुधि लीन्हें बिना। नहिं जैहैं जुबराज प्रबीना॥ अस कहि लवन सिंधु तट जाई। बैठे कपि सब दर्भ डसाई ॥
translation: हे सुयोग्य युवराज! हम लोग सीताजी की खोज लिए बिना नहीं लौटेंगे। ऐसा कहकर लवणसागर के तट पर जाकर सब वानर कुश बिछाकर बैठ गए ॥
english_translation: “We will not return without finding Sita.” Saying this, the monkeys went to the shore of the ocean and sat down on kusa grass.
essence: Real loyalty stays put until the search is complete.
simple_meaning: The monkeys refuse to go back until they have found Sita. They go to the seashore and sit down on kusa grass.
insight: It shifts the mind from retreat to steadfast commitment when the task is unfinished.
modern_relevance: You leave the hospital parking lot after another unanswered update, but you still don't drive home. Not until you know what happened, not until you can tell the family something real.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जामवंत अंगद दुख देखी। कहीं कथा उपदेस बिसेषी॥ तात राम कहुँ नर जनि मानहु। निर्गुन ब्रह्म अजित अज जानहु ॥
translation: जाम्बवान् ने अंगद का दुःख देखकर विशेष उपदेश की कथाएँ कहीं। (वे बोले-) हे तात! श्री रामजी को मनुष्य न मानो, उन्हें निर्गुण ब्रह्म, अजेय और अजन्मा समझो ॥
english_translation: Seeing Angad's sorrow, Jambavan spoke a special teaching. "Dear one, do not think of Ram as merely human. Know him as the attributeless supreme reality, unconquerable and unborn."
essence: Ram is not limited by human form or human weakness.
simple_meaning: Jambavan comforts the grieving monkeys by reminding them that Ram is not limited to a human form. He is beyond ordinary nature, beyond defeat, and beyond birth itself.
insight: It shifts the mind from judging Ram by appearance to recognising his limitless nature.
modern_relevance: You start doubting after a setback and begin treating what you love as small, ordinary, or fragile. This verse pulls you back from that reduction and restores reverence.
speaker: Jambavan

verse_text: हम सब सेवक अति बड़भागी। संतत सगुन ब्रह्म अनुरागी ॥
translation: हम सब सेवक अत्यंत बड़भागी हैं, जो निरंतर सगुण ब्रह्म (श्री रामजी) में प्रीति रखते हैं ॥
english_translation: We servants are truly fortunate, for we remain ever devoted to the manifest supreme reality.
essence: Steady love for Ram is itself the greatest good.
simple_meaning: The servants are called fortunate because they keep loving Ram in his visible, personal form.
insight: It shifts devotion from vague admiration to a living relationship with Ram.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone for one message that could change your day. The deeper relief comes when your heart already has a place to rest, not just a goal to chase.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: निज इच्छाँ प्रभु अवतरइ सुर मह गोद्वज लागि। सगुन उपासक संग तहँ रहहिं मोच्छ सब त्यागि ॥
translation: देवता, पृथ्वी, गो और ब्राह्मणों के लिए प्रभु अपनी इच्छा से (किसी कर्मबंधन से नहीं) अवतार लेते हैं। वहाँ सगुणोपासक (भक्तगण सालोक्य, सामीप्य, सारुप्य, सार्ष्टि और सायुज्य) सब प्रकार के मोक्षों को त्यागकर उनकी सेवा में साथ रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: The Lord descends by His own will for the sake of the gods, the earth, cows, and brahmins. There, devotees of the divine form stay with Him in service, abandoning all kinds of freedom in the higher realm.
essence: True devotion would rather stay near Ram than claim release.
simple_meaning: Ram comes of His own will to protect the gods, the earth, cows, and brahmins. Devotees stay near Him in loving service, even if that means giving up all forms of liberation.
insight: It shifts devotion from using the divine for personal gain to choosing loving nearness over spiritual reward.
modern_relevance: You finally get the offer you thought you wanted: the promotion, the exit, the clean break. But your heart says the real prize is staying with what you love and serving it well.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: एहि बिधि कथा कहहिं बहु भाँती। गिरि कंदराँ सुनी संपाती॥ बाहेर होइ देखि बहु कीसा। मोहि अहार दीन्ह जगदीसा ॥
translation: इस प्रकार जाम्बवान् बहुत प्रकार से कथाएँ कह रहे हैं। इनकी बातें पर्वत की कन्दरा में सम्पाती ने सुनीं। बाहर निकलकर उसने बहुत से वानर देखे। (तब वह बोला-) जगदीश्वर ने मुझको घर बैठे बहुत सा आहार भेज दिया! ॥
english_translation: In this way, Jambavan was telling many kinds of stories. Sampati heard them from a mountain cave. Coming outside, he saw many monkeys and thought, "The divine ruler has sent me food right here at home."
essence: Need can turn sight into appetite.
simple_meaning: Sampati overhears the monkeys' conversation, comes out of his cave, sees them, and thinks the monkeys are food sent to him by the divine ruler.
insight: It shows how deprivation distorts perception before any real judgment can happen.
modern_relevance: You overhear a conversation while exhausted and immediately read danger into it. When hunger or fear is driving, even neutral things can look like a threat.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आजु सबहि कहँ भच्छन करऊँ। दिन हबु चले अहार बिनु मरऊँ॥ कबहुँ न मिल भरि उदर अहारा। आजु दीन्ह बिधि एकहिं बारा ॥
translation: आज इन सबको खा जाऊँगा। बहुत दिन बीत गए, भोजन के बिना मर रहा था। पेटभर भोजन कभी नहीं मिलता। आज विधाता ने एक ही बार में बहुत सा भोजन दे दिया ॥
english_translation: Today I will eat all of you. For many days I have gone without food and am dying. I have never once had enough to fill my belly. Today fate has given me a full meal at one stroke.
essence: Desperation can turn a starving mind into a threat.
simple_meaning: Sampati says he will eat the monkeys because he has been starving for a long time and has never had enough food.
insight: It shows how deprivation can warp judgment and make others seem like prey.
modern_relevance: A person who has gone too long without support can start seeing other people as resources instead of lives. Desperation narrows the mind until everything looks like a chance to survive.
speaker: Sampati

verse_text: डरपे गीध बचन सुनि काना। अब भा मरन सत्य हम जाना॥ कपि सब उठे गीध कहँ देखी। जामवंत मन सोच बिसेषी ॥
translation: गीध के वचन कानों से सुनते ही सब डर गए कि अब सचमुच ही मरना हो गया। यह हमने जान लिया। फिर उस गीध (सम्पाती) को देखकर सब वानर उठ खड़े हुए। जाम्बवान् के मन में विशेष सोच हुआ ॥
english_translation: Hearing the vulture's words, everyone was struck with fear: now we know death is certain. Then, seeing that vulture, the monkeys sprang up, and Jambavan felt deep concern.
essence: Fear rises first; understanding comes only after seeing clearly.
simple_meaning: The monkeys hear the vulture's words and panic, thinking death is near. Then they see him clearly, and Jambavan begins to think carefully.
insight: It shows how fear can surge from words alone, but clear seeing brings the mind back to thought.
modern_relevance: Someone sends a terrifying voice note, and your stomach drops before you even read it fully. Then you open the message, see the full context, and your mind finally steadies.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह अंगद बिचारि मन माहीं। धन्य जटायू सम कोउ नाहीं॥ राम काज कारन तनु त्यागी। हरि पुर गयउ परम बड़भागी ॥
translation: अंगद ने मन में विचार कर कहा- अहा! जटायु के समान धन्य कोई नहीं है। श्री रामजी के कार्य के लिए शरीर छोड़कर वह परम बड़भागी भगवान् के परमधाम को चला गया ॥
english_translation: Angada thought to himself, “No one is as blessed as Jatayu. He gave up his body for Ram’s work and went to the supreme abode, most fortunate indeed.”
essence: Selfless service can make a life truly blessed.
simple_meaning: Angada honors Jatayu as the most blessed being because he gave his life for Ram’s cause and reached the supreme abode.
insight: It shifts admiration toward self-giving service instead of status, survival, or reward.
modern_relevance: You remember the friend who showed up when it mattered, gave everything, and asked for nothing back. Some lives shine brightest at the moment they are spent.
speaker: Angada

verse_text: सुनि खग हरष सोक जुत बानी। आवा निकट कपिन्ह भय मानी॥ तिन्हहि अभय करि पूछेसि जाई। कथा सकल तिन्ह ताहि सुनाई ॥
translation: हर्ष और शोक से युक्त वाणी (समाचार) सुनकर वह पक्षी (सम्पाती) वानरों के पास आया। वानर डर गए। उनको अभय करके (अभय वचन देकर) उसने पास जाकर जटायु का वृत्तांत पूछा, तब उन्होंने सारी कथा उसे कह सुनाई ॥
english_translation: Hearing the news filled with joy and sorrow, the bird came close to the monkeys, who were afraid. After giving them reassurance, he went near and asked about Jatayu, and they told him the whole story.
essence: Reassurance opens the door to painful truth.
simple_meaning: The bird came to the monkeys after hearing mixed news. They were afraid, but he reassured them and asked about Jatayu, then heard the full story.
insight: It shows how trust must be restored before painful truth can be shared.
modern_relevance: A tense group chat goes quiet after bad news. Someone finally says, “Take a breath — tell me what happened.” That small reassurance opens the whole story.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि संपाति बंधु कै करनी। रघुपति महिमा बहुबिधि बरनी ॥
translation: भाई जटायु की करनी सुनकर सम्पाती ने बहुत प्रकार से श्री रघुनाथजी की महिमा वर्णन की ॥
english_translation: Hearing about his brother Jatayu's deed, Sampati praised the glory of Raghunath in many ways.
essence: Devotion grows when sacrifice is seen clearly.
simple_meaning: Sampati hears of Jatayu's sacrifice and responds by praising Ram's greatness in many ways.
insight: It shifts the mind from family loss to reverence for a greater purpose.
modern_relevance: You hear what someone did for a cause bigger than themselves, and your cynicism drops. A single story of courage can make you speak differently, trust differently, and act differently.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मोहि लै जाहु सिंधुतट देउँ तिलांजलि ताहि। बचन सहाइ करबि मैं पैहहु खोजहु जाहि ॥
translation: (उसने कहा-) मुझे समुद्र के किनारे ले चलो, मैं जटायु को तिलांजलि दे दूँ। इस सेवा के बदले मैं तुम्हारी वचन से सहायता करूँगा (अर्थात् सीताजी कहाँ हैं सो बतला दूँगा), जिसे तुम खोज रहे हो उसे पा जाओगे ॥
english_translation: Take me to the shore of the ocean. I will offer libations to Jatayu. In return for that service, I will help with my word and tell you where to find the one you seek.
essence: Honor given without calculation returns as guidance.
simple_meaning: Sampati asks the monkeys to take him to the sea so he can honor Jatayu, and promises to help them find Sita.
insight: It links care for the dead with practical help for the living, showing how service can create trust and open doors.
modern_relevance: You stop to help an older man place flowers at a roadside memorial, expecting nothing back. Later, he gives you the exact contact you needed. Respect can become a bridge.
speaker: Sampati

verse_text: अनुज क्रिया करि सागर तीरा। कहि निज कथा सुनहु कपि बीरा॥ हम द्वौ बंधु प्रथम तरुनाई। गगन गए रबि निकट उड़ाई ॥
translation: समुद्र के तीर पर छोटे भाई जटायु की क्रिया (श्राद्ध आदि) करके सम्पाती अपनी कथा कहने लगा- हे वीर वानरों! सुनो, हम दोनों भाई उठती जवानी में एक बार आकाश में उड़कर सूर्य के निकट चले गए ॥
english_translation: After performing the rites for his younger brother at the seashore, Sampati began to tell his own story: "Listen, brave monkeys. We two brothers, in our youth, once flew up into the sky and went near the sun."
essence: A painful loss opens the door to crucial memory.
simple_meaning: Sampati finishes his brother's rites and begins telling the monkeys how he and Jatayu once flew close to the sun in their youth.
insight: It shifts attention from the present loss to the backstory that explains it.
modern_relevance: At a funeral gathering, someone who has lost a sibling starts speaking slowly about the years before everything changed. The memory itself becomes the bridge to what must be heard next.
speaker: Sampati

verse_text: तेज न सहि सक सो फिरि आवा। मैं अभिमानी रबि निअरावा॥ जरे पंख अति तेज अपारा। परेउँ भूमि करि घोर चिकारा ॥
translation: वह (जटायु) तेज नहीं सह सका, इससे लौट आया (किंतु), मैं अभिमानी था इसलिए सूर्य के पास चला गया। अत्यंत अपार तेज से मेरे पंख जल गए। मैं बड़े जोर से चीख मारकर जमीन पर गिर पड़ा ॥
english_translation: He could not bear the brilliance and returned. But I was proud, so I went near the sun. My wings were burned by that immense radiance, and I fell to the ground with a terrible cry.
essence: Pride can send you toward the fire that breaks you.
simple_meaning: Sampati explains that his brother turned back from the sun's heat, but his own pride drove him too close, burning his wings and sending him crashing down.
insight: It shows how ego pushes a person past their limits, creating the very collapse that later makes humility possible.
modern_relevance: You take on the job, the pace, or the relationship that looks dazzling from far away, then realize you were trying to stand too close to what would burn you.
speaker: Sampati

verse_text: मुनि एक नाम चंद्रमा ओही। लागी दया देखि करि मोही॥ बहु प्रकार तेहिं ग्यान सुनावा। देहजनित अभिमान छुड़ावा ॥
translation: वहाँ चंद्रमा नाम के एक मुनि थे। मुझे देखकर उन्हें बड़ी दया लगी। उन्होंने बहुत प्रकार से मुझे ज्ञान सुनाया और मेरे देहजनित (देह संबंधी) अभिमान को छुड़ा दिया ॥
english_translation: There was a sage named Chandrama. He felt deep compassion for me when he saw me. In many ways he taught me wisdom and removed my pride born of the body.
essence: Kindness can remove the pride that blocks understanding.
simple_meaning: A compassionate sage taught Sampati and freed him from bodily pride. Real wisdom began when someone saw him with kindness and helped him drop his false identification.
insight: It shows that clear seeing often arrives through compassionate guidance, not harsh criticism.
modern_relevance: You make a mistake, and instead of being shamed, one calm person explains what you could not see. That gentle correction can do what anger never will.
speaker: Sampati

verse_text: त्रेताँ ब्रह्म मनुज तनु धरिही। तासु नारि निसिचर पति हरिही॥ तासु खोज पठइहि प्रभु दूता। तिन्हहि मिलें तैं होब पुनीता ॥
translation: (उन्होंने कहा-) त्रेतायुग में साक्षात् परब्रह्म मनुष्य शरीर धारण करेंगे। उनकी स्त्री को राक्षसों का राजा हर ले जाएगा। उसकी खोज में प्रभु दूत भेजेंगे। उनसे मिलने पर तू पवित्र हो जाएगा ॥
english_translation: In Treta Yuga, the supreme reality will take a human body. The king of demons will carry off his wife. The Lord will send messengers to search for her. Meeting them will purify you.
essence: Ram's messengers are enough to change you.
simple_meaning: The sage predicts that Ram will be born as a human, Sita will be taken away, and Ram will send messengers to search for her. Even meeting those messengers will purify you.
insight: It shifts you from seeing helpers as ordinary contacts to recognising them as carriers of transformation.
modern_relevance: A stranger gives you directions that later save your day, and you realise the help was never random. Sometimes the people sent your way carry more than information — they carry a turning point.
speaker: Muni

verse_text: जमिहहिं पंख करसि जनि चिंता। तिन्हहि देखाइ देहेसु तैं सीता॥ मुनि कइ गिरा सत्य भइ आजू। सुनि मम बचन करहु प्रभु काजू ॥
translation: और तेरे पंख उग आएँगे, चिंता न कर। उन्हें तू सीताजी को दिखा देना। मुनि की वह वाणी आज सत्य हुई। अब मेरे वचन सुनकर तुम प्रभु का कार्य करो ॥
english_translation: Your wings will grow. Do not worry. Show Sita to them. The sage's words have come true today. Now, hearing my words, do the Lord's work.
essence: Faith turns impossible work into clear service.
simple_meaning: Hanuman is told not to worry; his wings will come, he will show Sita, and he should carry out Ram's task.
insight: It shifts you from anxious hesitation to confident action in service of a larger purpose.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, make the call, or take the leap, and your chest tightens. Then something in you says: keep going, the next step will reveal itself.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: गिरि त्रिकूट ऊपर बस लंका। तहँ रह रावन सहज असंका॥ तहँ असोक उपबन जहँ रहई। सीता बैठि सोच रत अहई ॥
translation: त्रिकूट पर्वत पर लंका बसी हुई है। वहाँ स्वभाव से ही निडर रावण रहता है। वहाँ अशोक नाम का उपवन (बगीचा) है, जहाँ सीताजी रहती हैं। (इस समय भी) वे सोच में मग्न बैठी हैं ॥
english_translation: Lanka stands atop Mount Trikuta. There lives Ravana, naturally fearless. There is the Ashoka grove, where Sita sits, absorbed in sorrowful thought.
essence: A fortress can look fearless while holding deep sorrow within it.
simple_meaning: Lanka sits high on Mount Trikuta, ruled by fearless Ravana. In the Ashoka grove there, Sita sits lost in sorrowful thought.
insight: It shifts attention from the city’s strength to the hidden suffering at its center.
modern_relevance: You walk into a glittering place where everyone seems powerful, yet one person is sitting quietly with a broken heart. This verse holds both images at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मैं देखउँ तुम्ह नाहीं गीधहि दृष्टि अपार। बूढ़ भयउँ न त करतेउँ कछुक सहाय तुम्हार ॥
translation: मैं उन्हें देख रहा हूँ, तुम नहीं देख सकते, क्योंकि गीध की दृष्टि अपार होती है (बहुत दूर तक जाती है)। क्या करूँ? मैं बूढ़ा हो गया, नहीं तो तुम्हारी कुछ तो सहायता अवश्य करता ॥
english_translation: I can see them, but you cannot. A vulture's sight reaches far. What can I do? I have grown old; otherwise I would surely help you.
essence: Clear sight can remain even after strength is gone.
simple_meaning: Jatayu says he can still see Sita, but his age has taken away the strength to help more than this.
insight: It shows that seeing clearly is not the same as being able to act. Age, limits, and love can exist together.
modern_relevance: You know exactly how to fix the problem, but your body or energy won't cooperate. Someone you care about is counting on you, and all you can offer is one clear direction.
speaker: Jatayu

verse_text: जो नाघइ सत जोजन सागर। करइ सो राम काज मति आगर॥ मोहि बिलोकि धरहु मन धीरा। राम कृपाँ कस भयउ सरीरा ॥
translation: जो सौ योजन (चार सौ कोस) समुद्र लाँघ सकेगा और बुद्धिनिधान होगा, वही श्री रामजी का कार्य कर सकेगा। (निराश होकर घबराओ मत) मुझे देखकर मन में धीरज धरो। देखो, श्री रामजी की कृपा से (देखते ही देखते) मेरा शरीर कैसा हो गया (बिना पाँख का बेहाल था, पाँख उगने से सुंदर हो गया) ! ॥
english_translation: Whoever can cross the hundred-yojana ocean and is wise can do Ram's work. Seeing me, keep your mind steady. By Ram's grace, see what has happened to my body.
essence: Ram's work is done by the one who trusts enough to cross fear.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says that only someone wise and bold enough to cross the vast ocean can do Ram's work. He tells the listener to stay calm and trust Ram's grace.
insight: It shifts effort from panic to confident action grounded in grace.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the risky message, take the hard trip, or make the call nobody else wants to make. The task feels impossible until you remember what steadies you.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: पापिउ जाकर नाम सुमिरहीं। अति अपार भवसागर तरहीं॥ तासु दूत तुम्ह तजि कदराई राम हृदयँ धरि करहु उपाई ॥
translation: पापी भी जिनका नाम स्मरण करके अत्यंत पार भवसागर से तर जाते हैं। तुम उनके दूत हो, अतः कायरता छोड़कर श्री रामजी को हृदय में धारण करके उपाय करो ॥
english_translation: Even sinners cross the vast ocean of becoming by remembering that name. You are that divine messenger, so drop your fear, hold Ram in your heart, and find a way.
essence: Ram's name carries even the fallen across the deepest waters.
simple_meaning: Ram's name is so powerful that even people with serious faults can be carried across life's greatest flood. Hanuman is told to stop hesitating and act with courage.
insight: It shifts you from self-doubt to trust in Ram's power working through you.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that could change everything, and your thumb freezes over the screen. This verse says courage is not the absence of fear — it is remembering who you serve.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस कहि गरुड़ गीध जब गयऊ। तिन्ह के मन अति बिसमय भयऊ॥ निज निज बल सब काहूँ भाषा। पार जाइ कर संसय राखा ॥
translation: (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं-) हे गरुड़जी! इस प्रकार कहकर जब गीध चला गया, तब उन (वानरों) के मन में अत्यंत विस्मय हुआ। सब किसी ने अपना-अपना बल कहा। पर समुद्र के पार जाने में सभी ने संदेह प्रकट किया ॥
english_translation: After saying this, the vulture departed, and the hearts of all were filled with wonder. Each one spoke of his own strength, yet everyone still doubted crossing the sea.
essence: Strength without certainty still hesitates before the impossible.
simple_meaning: The monkeys were amazed, but no one was sure they could cross the sea. Each one spoke of his strength, yet doubt remained.
insight: It shows the gap between boasting about ability and meeting an actual obstacle.
modern_relevance: In a team meeting, everyone lists their qualifications, but the room still goes quiet when the hardest problem appears. Confidence is easy until the real threshold shows up.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जरठ भयउँ अब कहइ रिछेसा। नहिं तन रहा प्रथम बल लेसा॥ जबहिं त्रिबिक्रम भए खरारी। तब मैं तरुन रहेउँ बल भारी ॥
translation: ऋक्षराज जाम्बवान् कहने लगे- मैं बूढ़ा हो गया। शरीर में पहले वाले बल का लेश भी नहीं रहा। जब खरारि (खर के शत्रु श्री राम) वामन बने थे, तब मैं जवान था और मुझ में बड़ा बल था ॥
english_translation: I have grown old now, O king of the bears. Not a trace remains of my former strength. When the destroyer of demons became Trivikrama, I was young and full of strength.
essence: Old age does not cancel the strength that once met Ram.
simple_meaning: Jambavan says he is old now and no longer has his former strength, but he remembers the time when Ram appeared as Trivikrama and he was young and powerful.
insight: It shifts attention from present weakness to remembered proof, so courage can return.
modern_relevance: You open a dusty photo album and see the version of yourself that once moved fast, feared little, and believed. The body is older now, but the part that remembers still knows how to rise.
speaker: Jambavan

verse_text: बलि बाँधत प्रभु बाढ़ेउ सो तनु बरनि न जाइ। उभय घरी महँ दीन्हीं सात प्रदच्छिन धाइ ॥
translation: बलि के बाँधते समय प्रभु इतने बढ़े कि उस शरीर का वर्णन नहीं हो सकता, किंतु मैंने दो ही घड़ी में दौड़कर (उस शरीर की) सात प्रदक्षिणाएँ कर लीं ॥
english_translation: When Bali was being bound, the Lord grew so large that his body cannot be described. Yet in two moments I ran around that form seven times.
essence: Ram's form overwhelms description, and devotion moves faster than thought.
simple_meaning: The speaker recalls how Ram became vast when Bali was bound, and how quickly he ran around that immense form seven times.
insight: It turns a past event into reverent astonishment, making Ram's presence feel immeasurable.
modern_relevance: You remember the moment someone walked into the room and changed everything. Later, even the details feel larger than language can hold.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: अंगद कहइ जाउँ मैं पारा। जियँ संसय कछु फिरती बारा॥ जामवंत कह तुम्ह सब लायक। पठइअ किमि सबही कर नायक ॥
translation: अंगद ने कहा- मैं पार तो चला जाऊँगा, परंतु लौटते समय के लिए हृदय में कुछ संदेह है। जाम्बवान् ने कहा- तुम सब प्रकार से योग्य हो, परंतु तुम सबके नेता हो, तुम्हे कैसे भेजा जाए? ॥
english_translation: Angad said, "I can cross over, but my heart still has some doubt about the return journey." Jambavan said, "You are fully capable, but you are the leader of all of us—how can we send you?"
essence: Ability alone does not decide who should carry the mission.
simple_meaning: Angad says he can go across, but he is unsure about coming back. Jambavan then praises his ability, while also noting that he is the leader and should not be sent lightly.
insight: It shifts attention from raw ability to wise assignment of responsibility.
modern_relevance: You may be able to take on the challenge, but still hesitate because others depend on you. The question is not only can you do it, but should you be the one sent?
speaker: Angad

verse_text: कहइ रीछपति सुनु हनुमाना। का चुप साधि रहेहु बलवाना॥ पवन तनय बल पवन समाना। बुधि बिबेक बिग्यान निधाना ॥
translation: ऋक्षराज जाम्बवान् ने श्री हनुमानजी से कहा- हे हनुमान् ! हे बलवान् ! सुनो, तुमने यह क्या चुप साध रखी है? तुम पवन के पुत्र हो और बल में पवन के समान हो। तुम बुद्धि-विवेक और विज्ञान की खान हो ॥
english_translation: Jambavan, lord of the bears, said to Hanuman: "Listen, mighty one—why are you sitting silent? You are the son of the wind, and your strength is like the wind itself. You are a treasure-house of wisdom, clear seeing, and knowledge."
essence: True strength wakes when someone names it clearly.
simple_meaning: Jambavan reminds Hanuman that he is not ordinary: he has great strength and deep wisdom, so he should speak up and act.
insight: It shifts you from hesitation to rightful confidence by recognizing your latent capacity.
modern_relevance: Everyone in the room looks stuck, and you keep quiet because you think someone else is better for the task. Then one trusted person names what you can do, and your whole posture changes.
speaker: Jambavan

verse_text: कवन सो काज कठिन जग माहीं। जो नहिं होइ तात तुम्ह पाहीं॥ राम काज लगि तव अवतारा। सुनतहिं भयउ पर्बताकारा ॥
translation: जगत् में कौन सा ऐसा कठिन काम है जो हे तात! तुमसे न हो सके। श्री रामजी के कार्य के लिए ही तो तुम्हारा अवतार हुआ है। यह सुनते ही हनुमान् जी पर्वत के आकार के (अत्यंत विशालकाय) हो गए ॥
english_translation: What task in the world is too hard for you, dear one? You were born for Ram's work. Hearing this, Hanuman became mountain-sized.
essence: Your real strength appears when your work is named correctly.
simple_meaning: Jambavan reminds Hanuman that no task is beyond him, because he was born for Ram's work. The reminder awakens Hanuman's full power.
insight: It shifts you from self-doubt to decisive action by linking ability with purpose.
modern_relevance: A friend says, "You can do this," right when you've started doubting yourself before a hard call, a move, or a rescue. Sometimes the right reminder unlocks the strength already in you.
speaker: Jambavan

verse_text: कनक बरन तन तेज बिराजा। मानहुँ अपर गिरिन्ह कर राजा॥ सिंहनाद करि बारहिं बारा। लीलहिं नाघउँ जलनिधि खारा ॥
translation: उनका सोने का सा रंग है, शरीर पर तेज सुशोभित है, मानो दूसरा पर्वतों का राजा सुमेरु हो। हनुमान् जी ने बार-बार सिंहनाद करके कहा- मैं इस खारे समुद्र को खेल में ही लाँघ सकता हूँ ॥
english_translation: His golden body shone with radiance, like another king of mountains. Roaring like a lion again and again, Hanuman declared, "I can leap across this salty sea as if it were play."
essence: When your strength is remembered, the impossible becomes a game.
simple_meaning: Hanuman’s body shines like a mountain king, and he boldly declares that crossing the ocean is easy for him.
insight: It shifts you from hesitation to decisive confidence when the right reminder awakens your capacity.
modern_relevance: You stand at the edge of a task that once felt impossible, and something in you finally wakes up. The fear is still there, but it no longer gets to speak first.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: सहित सहाय रावनहि मारी। आनउँ इहाँ त्रिकूट उपारी॥ जामवंत मैं पूँछउँ तोही। उचित सिखावनु दीजहु मोही ॥
translation: और सहायकों सहित रावण को मारकर त्रिकूट पर्वत को उखाड़कर यहाँ ला सकता हूँ। हे जाम्बवान् ! मैं तुमसे पूछता हूँ, तुम मुझे उचित सीख देना (कि मुझे क्या करना चाहिए) ॥
english_translation: I can kill Ravana and his allies and bring Mount Trikuta here. O Jambavan, I ask you to guide me properly.
essence: Great power stays humble enough to ask for direction.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says he can defeat Ravana and even uproot a mountain, but he still asks Jambavan for proper guidance.
insight: It teaches you to pair courage with guidance, so strength does not turn careless.
modern_relevance: You finally solve the hard part of the project, then stop and ask the senior colleague to check your next move. Real confidence can still take correction.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: एतना करहु तात तुम्ह जाई। सीतहि देखि कहहु सुधि आई॥ तब निज भुज बल राजिवनैना। कौतुक लागि संग कपि सेना ॥
translation: (जाम्बवान् ने कहा-) हे तात! तुम जाकर इतना ही करो कि सीताजी को देखकर लौट आओ और उनकी खबर कह दो। फिर कमलनयन श्री रामजी अपने बाहुबल से (ही राक्षसों का संहार कर सीताजी को ले आएँगे, केवल) खेल के लिए ही वे वानरों की सेना साथ लेंगे ॥
english_translation: Go and do only this, dear one: see Sita and come back with news of her. Then lotus-eyed Ram, by his own strength, will destroy the demons and bring her back, taking the monkey army only for sport.
essence: Your task is small; Ram's work is vast.
simple_meaning: Jambavan tells Hanuman to go find Sita, see her, and return with news. Ram himself will then defeat the demons and rescue her.
insight: It shifts you from trying to control the whole outcome to completing the one faithful step in front of you.
modern_relevance: You finally get the courage to call the person you need to help. You do not have to solve everything in one breath — first make contact, then let the larger answer unfold.
speaker: Jambavan

verse_text: कपि सेन संग सँघारि निसिचर रामु सीतहि आनि हैं। त्रैलोक पावन सुजसु सुर मुनि नारदादि बखानि हैं॥ जो सुनत गावत कहत समुक्षत परमपद नर पावई। रघुबीर पद पाथोज मधुकर दास तुलसी गावई॥
translation: वानरों की सेना साथ लेकर राक्षसों का संहार करके श्री रामजी सीताजी को ले आएँगे। तब देवता और नारदादि मुनि भगवान् के तीनों लोकों को पवित्र करने वाले सुंदर यश का बखान करेंगे, जिसे सुनने, गाने, कहने और समझने से मनुष्य परमपद पाते हैं और जिसे श्री रघुवीर के चरणकमल का मधुकर (भ्रमर) तुलसीदास गाता है।
english_translation: With the monkey army, Ram will destroy the demons and bring Sita back. Then the gods, sages, and Narad will sing his pure fame that purifies the three worlds. Whoever hears, sings, speaks, or reflects on it attains the highest state; Tulsidas sings as a bee at the lotus feet of Raghuvir.
essence: Ram's fame purifies you just by being heard.
simple_meaning: Ram will defeat the demons, bring Sita back, and his fame will purify the three worlds. Hearing, singing, speaking, or reflecting on that fame leads a person to the highest state.
insight: It shifts attention from the event to the sacred remembrance behind the event, treating praise itself as transformative practice.
modern_relevance: You hear a story about someone who stayed faithful through loss, and it steadies you more than advice ever could. Some names carry enough purity to reorient a whole heart.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: भव भेषज रघुनाथ जसु सुनहिं जे नर अरु नारि। तिन्ह कर सकल मनोरथ सिद्ध करहिं त्रिसिरारि ॥
translation: श्री रघुवीर का यश भव (जन्म-मरण) रूपी रोग की (अचूक) दवा है। जो पुरुष और स्त्री इसे सुनेंगे, त्रिशिरा के शत्रु श्री रामजी उनके सब मनोरथों को सिद्ध करेंगे ॥
english_translation: The glory of Raghunath is the cure for the cycle of birth and death. Men and women who hear it have all their wishes fulfilled by Ram, the destroyer of the three-headed demon.
essence: Ram's glory heals the restless cycle and fulfills sincere longing.
simple_meaning: Hearing Ram's praise is said to heal the pain of repeated birth and death, and to fulfill the wishes of anyone who listens with faith.
insight: It shifts attention from control to receptive listening, showing that devotion can heal and complete what striving cannot.
modern_relevance: You are exhausted after months of trying to fix everything yourself. Then one song, one prayer, one line of truth lands differently — and something in you loosens before you even understand why.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: नीलोत्पल तन स्याम काम कोटि सोभा अधिक। सुनिअ तासु गुन ग्राम जासु नाम अघ खग बधिक ॥
translation: जिनका नीले कमल के समान श्याम शरीर है, जिनकी शोभा करोड़ों कामदेवों से भी अधिक है और जिनका नाम पापरूपी पक्षियों को मारने के लिए बधिक (व्याधा) के समान है, उन श्री राम के गुणों के समूह (लीला) को अवश्य सुनना चाहिए ॥
english_translation: His body is dark like a blue lotus, his beauty surpasses millions of Cupids, and his name is like a hunter that kills the birds of sin. You should listen to the many virtues of Ram.
essence: Ram's name does what desire and effort cannot: it clears the stain.
simple_meaning: Ram is unimaginably beautiful, and even his name has the power to destroy inner wrongs. The verse urges you to listen to his qualities with attention.
insight: It shifts attention from Ram's outward beauty to the cleansing power of remembering his name.
modern_relevance: You are scrolling past a hundred noisy voices, and one name still stops you. Some words don't just inform you — they purify the mood you were carrying.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: शान्तं शाश्वतमप्रमेयमनघं निर्वाणशान्तिप्रदं ब्रह्माशम्भुफणीन्द्रसेव्यमनिशं वेदान्तवेद्यं विभुम् । रामाख्यं जगदीश्वरं सुरगुरुं मायामनुष्यं हरिं वन्देऽहं करुणाकरं रघुवरं भूपालचूडामणिम् ॥
translation: शान्त, सनातन, अप्रमेय (प्रमाणों से परे), निष्पाप, मोक्षरूप परमशान्ति देने वाले, ब्रह्मा, शम्भु और शेषजी से निरंतर सेवित, वेदान्त के द्वारा जानने योग्य, सर्वव्यापक, देवताओं में सबसे बड़े, माया से मनुष्य रूप में दिखने वाले, समस्त पापों को हरने वाले, करुणा की खान, रघुकुल में श्रेष्ठ तथा राजाओं के शिरोमणि राम कहलाने वाले जगदीश्वर की मैं वंदना करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I bow to Ram, the peaceful, eternal, immeasurable, stainless, giver of freedom and deep stillness, ever served by Brahma, Shiva, and Shesha, known through the end of the Vedas, all-pervading, lord of the world, teacher of the gods, appearing as a human through his own power, remover of suffering, full of compassion, best of the Raghu line, and crown jewel of kings.
essence: Ram is beyond measure, yet close enough to receive your bow.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as peaceful, eternal, beyond measurement, pure, and full of compassion. He is the supreme ruler who appears in human form and is worthy of worship.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing power as distant to seeing it as compassionate and approachable.
modern_relevance: Before a hard meeting, you may feel small and overmatched. This verse reminds you that what is highest can still feel near, personal, and worthy of trust.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: नान्या स्पृहा रघुपते हृदयेऽस्मदीये सत्यं वदामि च भवानखिलान्तरात्मा। भक्तिं प्रयच्छ रघुपुंगव निर्भरां मे कामादिदोषरहितं कुरु मानसं च ॥
translation: हे रघुनाथजी! मैं सत्य कहता हूँ और फिर आप सबके अंतरात्मा ही हैं (सब जानते ही हैं) कि मेरे हृदय में दूसरी कोई इच्छा नहीं है। हे रघुकुलश्रेष्ठ! मुझे अपनी निर्भरा (पूर्ण) भक्ति दीजिए और मेरे मन को काम आदि दोषों से रहित कीजिए ॥
english_translation: O Lord of the Raghu line, I speak truth: there is no other desire in my heart. You are the inner witness of everything. Grant me unwavering devotion and make my mind free of desire and fault.
essence: Full devotion leaves no room for private desire.
simple_meaning: The speaker tells Ram that there is no other desire in the heart, asks for complete devotion, and asks for a mind freed from desire and flaw.
insight: It shifts attention from mixed motives to wholehearted devotion, and from self-interest to inner cleanliness.
modern_relevance: Before sending that text, you check your own motive: are you helping, or hoping to be noticed? This verse asks for cleaner reasons and a quieter mind.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: अतुलितबलधामं हेमशैलाभदेहं दनुजवनकृशानुं ज्ञानिनामग्रगण्यम् । सकलगुणनिधानं वानराणामधीशं रघुपतिप्रियभक्तं वातजातं नमामि ॥
translation: अतुल बल के धाम, सोने के पर्वत (सुमेरु) के समान कान्तियुक्त शरीर वाले, दैत्य रूपी वन (को ध्वंस करने) के लिए अग्नि रूप, ज्ञानियों में अग्रगण्य, संपूर्ण गुणों के निधान, वानरों के स्वामी, श्री रघुनाथजी के प्रिय भक्त पवनपुत्र श्री हनुमान् जी को मैं प्रणाम करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I bow to Hanuman, the son of the Wind, whose strength is unmatched, whose body shines like a golden mountain, who is the fire that burns the forest of demons, foremost among the wise, a treasury of all virtues, lord of the monkeys, and the beloved devotee of Raghupati.
essence: True greatness shines through devoted service.
simple_meaning: Hanuman is praised as unmatched in strength, wisdom, virtue, and service to Ram. He is not just powerful; his greatness comes from devotion.
insight: It teaches you to measure greatness by service, not self-importance.
modern_relevance: You see someone handle impossible pressure without bragging, without panic, and without needing credit. That calm force is what Hanuman embodies.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जामवंत के बचन सुहाए। सुनि हनुमंत हृदय अति भाए॥ तब लगि मोहि परिखेहु तुम्ह भाई। सहि दुख कंद मूल फल खाई ॥
translation: जाम्बवान् के सुंदर वचन सुनकर हनुमान् जी के हृदय को बहुत ही भाए। (वे बोले-) हे भाई! तुम लोग दुःख सहकर, कन्द-मूल-फल खाकर तब तक मेरी राह देखना ॥
english_translation: Jambavan’s gentle words pleased Hanuman deeply. Hanuman said, “Until then, my brothers, endure the hardship and wait for me, eating roots, bulbs, and fruits.”
essence: Love keeps moving while others wait in faith.
simple_meaning: Hanuman asks his companions to wait and endure hardship while he goes ahead to find Sita.
insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to carrying responsibility for others’ hope.
modern_relevance: You leave your friends behind at the train station before a difficult trip, asking them to trust you and hold the line until you return with news. That’s the steadiness in Hanuman’s words.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: जब लगि आवौं सीतहि देखी। होइहि काजु मोहि हरष बिसेषी॥ यह कहि नाइ सबन्हि कहुँ माथा । चलेउ हरषि हियँ धरि रघुनाथा ॥
translation: जब तक मैं सीताजी को देखकर (लौट) न आऊँ। काम अवश्य होगा, क्योंकि मुझे बहुत ही हर्ष हो रहा है। यह कहकर और सबको मस्तक नवाकर तथा हृदय में श्री रघुनाथजी को धारण करके हनुमान् जी हर्षित होकर चले ॥
english_translation: Until I return after seeing Sita, the task will surely succeed, and I feel great joy. Saying this, bowing to everyone, and holding Ram in his heart, Hanuman departed in delight.
essence: Remembering Ram turns a hard mission into joyful certainty.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says he will not rest until he sees Sita, and he feels certain the mission will succeed. He bows to everyone and leaves with Ram in his heart.
insight: It shifts action from anxious effort to joyful resolve rooted in remembrance.
modern_relevance: You leave a difficult conversation, breathe once in the hallway, and remind yourself why you came. The fear is still there, but something steadier is walking with you.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: सिंधु तीर एक भूधर सुंदर। कौतुक कूदि चढ़ेउ ता ऊपर॥ बार-बार रघुबीर सँभारी। तरकेउ पवनतनय बल भारी ॥
translation: समुद्र के तीर पर एक सुंदर पर्वत था। हनुमान् जी खेल से ही (अनायास ही) कूदकर उसके ऊपर जा चढ़े और बार-बार श्री रघुवीर का स्मरण करके अत्यंत बलवान् हनुमान् जी उस पर से बड़े वेग से उछले ॥
english_translation: On the seashore stood a beautiful mountain. Hanuman leapt up playfully and climbed it. Recalling Raghubir again and again, the son of the wind sprang onward with immense force.
essence: Remembering Ram turns impossible distance into a single leap.
simple_meaning: Hanuman reaches a mountain by the sea, leaps onto it, and launches forward by remembering Ram.
insight: It shows devotion as fuel for action, not a separate feeling.
modern_relevance: You grab your bag, take one deep breath, and step into the hard conversation. The body moves first; courage follows the name you keep close.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जेहिं गिरि चरन देइ हनुमंता। चलेउ सो गा पाताल तुरंता॥ जिमि अमोघ रघुपति कर बाना। एही भाँति चलेउ हनुमाना ॥
translation: जिस पर्वत पर हनुमान् जी पैर रखकर चले (जिस पर से वे उछले), वह तुरंत ही पाताल में धँस गया। जैसे श्री रघुनाथजी का अमोघ बाण चलता है, उसी तरह हनुमान् जी चले ॥
english_translation: The mountain sank into the underworld the moment Hanuman stepped on it. Hanuman moved like an unfailing arrow of Raghunath.
essence: True force moves straight through resistance.
simple_meaning: Hanuman’s weight and force are so great that the mountain sinks when he pushes off from it. His movement is compared to Ram’s unstoppable arrow.
insight: It turns raw momentum into a sign of complete alignment with purpose.
modern_relevance: You leave a meeting, and the decision is already made in your body. No second-guessing, no backtracking — just clean movement toward what you came to do.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जलनिधि रघुपति दूत बिचारी। तैं मैनाक होहि श्रम हारी ॥
translation: समुद्र ने उन्हें श्री रघुनाथजी का दूत समझकर मैनाक पर्वत से कहा कि हे मैनाक! तू इनकी थकावट दूर करने वाला हो (अर्थात् अपने ऊपर इन्हें विश्राम दे) ॥
english_translation: Seeing him as the messenger of Raghupati, the ocean told Mainaka, “O Mainaka, become the one who relieves his fatigue.”
essence: True service moves creation itself to help you.
simple_meaning: The ocean recognizes Hanuman as Ram’s messenger and asks Mainaka to give him a place to rest.
insight: It shows how a worthy mission can attract unexpected support, even from the world around you.
modern_relevance: You are racing from one responsibility to the next, and a friend quietly opens the door, brings water, and says, “Sit for a minute.”
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हनूमान तेहि परसा कर पुनि कीन्ह प्रनाम। राम काजु कीन्हें बिनु मोहि कहाँ बिश्राम ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी ने उसे हाथ से छू दिया, फिर प्रणाम करके कहा- भाई! श्री रामचंद्रजी का काम किए बिना मुझे विश्राम कहाँ? ॥
english_translation: Hanuman touched him, then bowed again and said, "Brother, how can I rest before completing Ram's work?"
essence: Devotion makes rest impossible until the beloved's work is complete.
simple_meaning: Hanuman shows complete devotion: even after being honored, he says he cannot rest until Ram's task is finished.
insight: It shifts attention from personal ease to wholehearted service.
modern_relevance: You finish helping a friend move, and they offer tea, a chair, a break. You smile, but your mind is still on the boxes left in the truck. Hanuman knows that feeling of service before comfort.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जात पवनसुत देवन्ह देखा। जानैं कहुँ बल बुद्धि बिसेषा॥ सुरसा नाम अहिन्ह कै माता। पठइन्हि आइ कही तेहिं बाता ॥
translation: देवताओं ने पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी को जाते हुए देखा। उनकी विशेष बल-बुद्धि को जानने के लिए (परीक्षार्थ) उन्होंने सुरसा नामक सर्पों की माता को भेजा, उसने आकर हनुमान् जी से यह बात कही- ॥
english_translation: As Hanuman, son of the wind, was seen passing by, the devas wanted to test his exceptional strength and intelligence. So they sent Surasa, mother of the serpents, who came and spoke to him.
essence: Before a great task opens, a test often appears first.
simple_meaning: The devas notice Hanuman's extraordinary strength and intelligence, so they send Surasa to test him.
insight: It frames success as something that invites examination, not applause.
modern_relevance: You finally get the chance to prove yourself, and the first thing you meet is a test you did not choose.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आजु सुरन्ह मोहि दीन्ह अहारा। सुनत बचन कह पवनकुमारा॥ राम काजु करि फिरि मैं आवौं। सीता कइ सुधि प्रभुहि सुनावौं ॥
translation: आज देवताओं ने मुझे भोजन दिया है। यह वचन सुनकर पवनकुमार हनुमान् जी ने कहा- श्री रामजी का कार्य करके मैं लौट आऊँ और सीताजी की खबर प्रभु को सुना दूँ, ॥
english_translation: The gods have given me food today. Hearing this, Hanuman said, 'I will return only after finishing Ram's work, and I will tell the Lord news of Sita.'
essence: Devotion keeps moving until the work is complete.
simple_meaning: Hanuman refuses to stop for food or comfort. He will return only after completing Ram's task and bringing Sita's news back.
insight: It shifts attention from personal comfort to faithful completion of the task in front of you.
modern_relevance: You are halfway through helping a friend move when someone offers snacks and a break. You can pause, but part of you knows the real relief comes after the job is finished.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: तब तव बदन पैठिहउँ आई। सत्य कहउँ मोहि जान दे माई॥ कवनेहुँ जतन देइ नहिं जाना। ग्रससि न मोहि कहेउ हनुमाना ॥
translation: तब मैं आकर तुम्हारे मुँह में घुस जाऊँगा (तुम मुझे खा लेना)। हे माता! मैं सत्य कहता हूँ, अभी मुझे जाने दे। जब किसी भी उपाय से उसने जाने नहीं दिया, तब हनुमान् जी ने कहा- तो फिर मुझे खा न ले ॥
english_translation: Then I will enter your mouth and come through. I speak the truth, Mother, let me go. When no other way worked, Hanuman said, 'Then eat me if you must.'
essence: Real resolve keeps moving when every normal route is closed.
simple_meaning: Hanuman refuses to be stopped. If the guardian will not let him pass, he is ready to go straight through her mouth to continue his mission.
insight: It teaches you to treat resistance as a problem to route around, not a reason to stop.
modern_relevance: You are at the airport gate, your documents are wrong, and the line is closing. Instead of collapsing, you start looking for the next workable move. That is Hanuman’s energy.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: जोजन भरि तेहिं बदनु पसारा। कपि तनु कीन्ह दुगुन बिस्तारा ॥ सोरह जोजन मुख तेहिं ठयऊ। तुरत पवनसुत बत्तिस भयऊ ॥
translation: उसने योजनभर (चार कोस में) मुँह फैलाया। तब हनुमान् जी ने अपने शरीर को उससे दूना बढ़ा लिया। उसने सोलह योजन का मुख किया। हनुमान् जी तुरंत ही बत्तीस योजन के हो गए ॥
english_translation: She spread her mouth to a span of one yojana. Hanuman doubled his body. She made her mouth sixteen yojanas wide. At once, the Son of Wind became thirty-two yojanas tall.
essence: Real strength grows to meet resistance without panic.
simple_meaning: Surasa keeps enlarging her mouth, and Hanuman keeps doubling his size to match her challenge.
insight: It trains the mind to respond dynamically to resistance instead of shrinking before it.
modern_relevance: A problem keeps getting bigger while you stand there in the middle of it — the deadline, the bill, the conversation. You don't freeze; you adjust fast and stay larger than the obstacle.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जस जस सुरसा बदनु बढ़ावा। तासु दून कपि रूप देखावा॥ सत जोजन तेहिं आनन कीन्हा। अति लघु रूप पवनसुत लीन्हा ॥
translation: जैसे-जैसे सुरसा मुख का विस्तार बढ़ाती थी, हनुमान् जी उसका दूना रूप दिखलाते थे। उसने सौ योजन (चार सौ कोस का) मुख किया। तब हनुमान् जी ने बहुत ही छोटा रूप धारण कर लिया ॥
english_translation: As Surasa kept widening her mouth, Hanuman showed a form twice as large. When she made her mouth one hundred yojanas wide, the son of the wind took a very small form.
essence: Real strength knows when to expand and when to shrink.
simple_meaning: Hanuman keeps adjusting his size to match Surasa's challenge. He first grows larger, then becomes tiny when she opens her mouth huge.
insight: It teaches you to meet resistance with agility instead of stubborn force.
modern_relevance: A tense conversation is going nowhere until you stop pushing the same point and change your approach. Sometimes the smartest move is to adapt instantly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बदन पइठि पुनि बाहेर आवा। मागा बिदा ताहि सिरु नावा॥ मोहि सुरन्ह जेहि लागि पठावा। बुधि बल मरमु तोर मैं पावा ॥
translation: और उसके मुख में घुसकर (तुरंत) फिर बाहर निकल आए और उसे सिर नवाकर विदा माँगने लगे। (उसने कहा-) मैंने तुम्हारे बुद्धि-बल का भेद पा लिया, जिसके लिए देवताओं ने मुझे भेजा था ॥
english_translation: He entered her mouth and came back out at once, then bowed and asked leave. She said, "I have understood the secret of your intelligence and strength—the reason the devas sent me to test you."
essence: Strength proves itself without boasting.
simple_meaning: Hanuman passes Surasa's test, then respectfully asks permission to leave. Surasa recognises that his intelligence and strength are extraordinary and that the devas sent her to test him.
insight: It shows that true power does not need to dominate; it can pass through challenge with composure and courtesy.
modern_relevance: You handled a difficult conversation without raising your voice, then left with grace. The other person may still disagree, but they can feel the steadiness in you.
speaker: Surasa

verse_text: राम काजु सबु करिहहु तुम्ह बल बुद्धि निधान। आसिष देइ गई सो हरषि चलेउ हनुमान ॥
translation: तुम श्री रामचंद्रजी का सब कार्य करोगे, क्योंकि तुम बल-बुद्धि के भंडार हो। यह आशीर्वाद देकर वह चली गई, तब हनुमान् जी हर्षित होकर चले ॥
english_translation: You will accomplish all of Ram's work, for you are a treasury of strength and wisdom. Giving this blessing, she left, and Hanuman went on joyfully.
essence: When your strength serves Ram's work, even obstacles become blessings.
simple_meaning: Surasa blesses Hanuman and recognizes that he has the strength and wisdom to complete Ram's mission.
insight: It shifts your focus from self-doubt to capable service.
modern_relevance: A senior colleague sees your work under pressure and says, quietly, that you can handle the whole project. That recognition steadies you more than praise ever could.
speaker: Surasa

verse_text: निसिचरि एक सिंधु महुँ रहई। करि माया नभु के खग गहई॥ जीव जंतु जे गगन उड़ाहीं। जल बिलोकि तिन्ह कै परिछाहीं ॥
translation: समुद्र में एक राक्षसी रहती थी। वह माया करके आकाश में उड़ते हुए पक्षियों को पकड़ लेती थी। आकाश में जो जीव-जंतु उड़ा करते थे, वह जल में उनकी परछाईं देखकर ॥
english_translation: A demoness lived in the ocean. Using illusion, she caught birds flying in the sky. Any creature that flew above, she spotted by its reflection in the water.
essence: Hidden traps watch for the slightest sign of movement.
simple_meaning: A sea-dwelling demoness uses illusion to trap flying creatures by spotting their reflections in the water.
insight: It prepares the reader for hidden danger and shows how illusion exploits even a shadow of presence.
modern_relevance: A scammer watches the faintest reply time on your phone and knows you're interested. The danger is not the trap itself, but how carefully it studies your movement.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गहइ छाहँ सक सो न उड़ाई। एहि बिधि सदा गगनचर खाई॥ सोइ छल हनूमान् कहँ कीन्हा। तासु कपटु कपि तुरतहिं चीन्हा ॥
translation: उस परछाईं को पकड़ लेती थी, जिससे वे उड़ नहीं सकते थे (और जल में गिर पड़ते थे) इस प्रकार वह सदा आकाश में उड़ने वाले जीवों को खाया करती थी। उसने वही छल हनुमान् जी से भी किया। हनुमान् जी ने तुरंत ही उसका कपट पहचान लिया ॥
english_translation: She would seize the shadow, so they could not fly and would fall into the water. In this way she kept eating the creatures that flew through the sky. She used the same trick on Hanuman, but Hanuman recognized her deceit at once.
essence: Clear seeing breaks a trick before it can work.
simple_meaning: A sea-dwelling ogress traps flying beings by grabbing their shadows. She tries the same trick on Hanuman, but he sees through it immediately.
insight: It trains you to spot deception before reacting, using alert perception rather than brute strength.
modern_relevance: A scam email lands in your inbox with urgent language and a fake logo. You pause, notice the mismatch, and delete it before it can hook you. Quick recognition saves you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ताहि मारि मारुतसुत बीरा। बारिधि पार गयउ मतिधीरा॥ तहाँ जाइ देखी बन सोभा। गुंजत चंचरीक मधु लोभा ॥
translation: पवनपुत्र धीरबुद्धि वीर श्री हनुमान् जी उसको मारकर समुद्र के पार गए। वहाँ जाकर उन्होंने वन की शोभा देखी। मधु (पुष्प रस) के लोभ से भौंरे गुंजार कर रहे थे ॥
english_translation: Hanuman, the brave and steady-minded one, killed that obstacle and crossed the ocean. Then he went and saw the beauty of the forest, where bees hummed for the nectar of flowers.
essence: Once the obstacle falls, the journey can continue.
simple_meaning: Hanuman overcomes the obstacle, crosses the ocean, and reaches a beautiful forest filled with birds, animals, and humming bees.
insight: It moves the scene from struggle to arrival, showing that courage clears the way for the next step.
modern_relevance: You finally get through the airport delay, the traffic jam, the obstacle that almost made you turn back—and then the city opens up in front of you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाना तरु फल फूल सुहाए। खग मृग बृंद देखि मन भाए॥ सैल बिसाल देखि एक आगें। ता पर धाइ चढ़ेउ भय त्यागें ॥
translation: अनेकों प्रकार के वृक्ष फल-फूल से शोभित हैं। पक्षी और पशुओं के समूह को देखकर तो वे मन में (बहुत ही) प्रसन्न हुए। सामने एक विशाल पर्वत देखकर हनुमान् जी भय त्यागकर उस पर दौड़कर जा चढ़े ॥
english_translation: Many kinds of trees stood bright with fruit and flowers. Seeing flocks of birds and herds of animals, he felt delighted. When he saw a huge mountain ahead, Hanuman threw off fear and leapt up it.
essence: Beauty uplifts him, and a mountain only makes him move faster.
simple_meaning: Hanuman sees a beautiful forest, feels happy among the birds and animals, then spots a huge mountain and climbs it without fear.
insight: It shifts you from hesitant looking to fearless forward motion.
modern_relevance: You step out of a tense airport into sunlight, see trees, people, and open space, and your chest loosens. Then the next challenge appears, and you keep moving anyway.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उमा न कछु कपि कै अधिकाई। प्रभु प्रताप जो कालहि खाई॥ गिरि पर चढ़ि लंका तेहिं देखी। कहि न जाइ अति दुर्ग बिसेषी ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! इसमें वानर हनुमान् की कुछ बड़ाई नहीं है। यह प्रभु का प्रताप है, जो काल को भी खा जाता है। पर्वत पर चढ़कर उन्होंने लंका देखी। बहुत ही बड़ा किला है, कुछ कहा नहीं जाता ॥
english_translation: Uma, Hanuman's greatness is nothing of his own. It is the power of the Lord, who devours even death. Climbing the mountain, he saw Lanka. Its special fortifications cannot be fully described.
essence: Your finest feats are often the Lord's power moving through you.
simple_meaning: Hanuman's feat is really the Lord's power working through him. After reaching the hilltop, he sees Lanka as an immense, unbeatable fortress.
insight: It shifts credit away from ego and toward the deeper power that makes action possible.
modern_relevance: You pulled off something impossible and everyone praised your talent. But deep down, you know support, timing, and grace carried you too.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: अति उतंग जलनिधि चहुँ पासा। कनक कोट कर परम प्रकासा ॥
translation: वह अत्यंत ऊँचा है, उसके चारों ओर समुद्र है। सोने के परकोटे (चहारदीवारी) का परम प्रकाश हो रहा है ॥
english_translation: It stands extremely high, with the ocean on all four sides. The golden rampart shines with a brilliant light.
