essence: Lanka is shown as a dazzling fortress before the search begins.
simple_meaning: The verse describes Lanka as a towering city surrounded by the sea, with golden walls shining brightly.
insight: It shifts attention from the task itself to the obstacle's size and strength.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a place that feels impossible to enter — a guarded campus, a locked building, a system built to keep outsiders out. The scale itself is meant to intimidate.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कनक कोटि बिचित्र मनि कृत सुंदरायतना घना। चउहट्ट हट्ट सुबट्ट बीथीं चारु पुर बहु बिधि बना॥ गज बाजि खच्चर निकर पदचर रथ बरूथन्हि को गनै। बहुरूप निसिचर जूथ अतिबल सेन बरनत नहिं बनै ॥
translation: विचित्र मणियों से जड़ा हुआ सोने का परकोटा है, उसके अंदर बहुत से सुंदर-सुंदर घर हैं। चौराहे, बाजार, सुंदर मार्ग और गलियाँ हैं, सुंदर नगर बहुत प्रकार से सजा हुआ है। हाथी, घोड़े, खच्चरों के समूह तथा पैदल और रथों के समूहों को कौन गिन सकता है! अनेक रूपों के राक्षसों के दल हैं, उनकी अत्यंत बलवती सेना वर्णन करते नहीं बनती ॥
english_translation: The city is ringed with a golden wall studded with strange jewels. Inside are many beautiful houses, crossroads, markets, fine roads, and lovely streets, all arranged in splendid ways. Who can count the elephants, horses, mules, foot soldiers, and chariots? Countless demons of many forms fill the mighty army; their strength cannot be fully described.
essence: Lanka looks magnificent, but its power makes it feel unapproachable.
simple_meaning: Lanka is described as a dazzling, heavily fortified city packed with wealth, roads, buildings, and a vast army. The point is its overwhelming scale, not a teaching.
insight: It frames the scene as one of scale and intimidation, preparing the mind for the challenge ahead.
modern_relevance: You step off a train into a city that feels impossible to navigate: glittering towers, crowded roads, security gates, and no clear way in. The verse captures that first stunned look.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बन बाग उपबन बाटिका सर कूप बापीं सोहहीं। नर नाग सुर गंधर्ब कन्या रूप मुनि मन मोहहीं॥ कहुँ माल देह बिसाल सैल समान अतिबल गर्जहीं। नाना अखारेन्ह भिरहिं बहुबिधि एक एकन्ह तर्जहीं ॥
translation: वन, बाग, उपवन (बगीचे), फुलवाड़ी, तालाब, कुएँ और बावलियाँ सुशोभित हैं। मनुष्य, नाग, देवताओं और गंधर्वों की कन्याएँ अपने सौंदर्य से मुनियों के भी मन को मोहे लेती हैं। कहीं पर्वत के समान विशाल शरीर वाले बड़े ही बलवान् मल्ल (पहलवान) गरज रहे हैं। वे अनेकों अखाड़ों में बहुत प्रकार से भिड़ते और एक-दूसरे को ललकारते हैं ॥
english_translation: Gardens, groves, orchards, ponds, wells, and tanks shine there. Humans, serpents, radiant beings, and celestial maidens enchant even the minds of sages with their beauty. Somewhere, mighty wrestlers with mountain-like bodies are roaring. In many arenas, they grapple in many ways and challenge one another.
essence: Lanka gleams with beauty, but its strength is restless and menacing.
simple_meaning: Lanka is shown as a glittering city full of gardens, waterworks, beautiful beings, and powerful wrestlers. The verse is describing its splendor and strength, not teaching a lesson.
insight: It sets the stage by showing a world of luxury, beauty, and force before the real search begins.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करि जतन भट कोटिन्ह बिकट तन नगर चहुँ दिसि रच्छहीं। कहुँ महिष मानुष धेनु खर अज खल निसाचर भच्छहीं॥ एहि लागि तुलसीदास इन्ह की कथा कछु एक है कही। रघुबीर सर तीरथ सरीरन्हि त्यागि गति पैहहिं सही ॥
translation: भयंकर शरीर वाले करोड़ों योद्धा यत्न करके (बड़ी सावधानी से) नगर की चारों दिशाओं में (सब ओर से) रखवाली करते हैं। कहीं दुष्ट राक्षस भैंसों, मनुष्यों, गायों, गदहों और बकरों को खा रहे हैं। तुलसीदास ने इनकी कथा इसीलिए कुछ थोड़ी सी कही है कि ये निश्चय ही श्री रामचंद्रजी के बाण रूपी तीर्थ में शरीरों को त्यागकर परमगति पावेंगे ॥
english_translation: With fierce bodies, countless warriors guard the city on all four sides. Elsewhere, evil beings are devouring buffaloes, humans, cows, donkeys, and goats. Tulsidas mentions only a little of their story because they will surely give up their bodies at Ram's arrow like pilgrims at a sacred crossing and reach the highest state.
essence: Even the strongest cruelty is already headed toward its end.
simple_meaning: Lanka is heavily guarded, and its cruel inhabitants are destroying living beings. Tulsidas says this only briefly because Ram's arrow will end their bodies and send them onward.
insight: It shifts attention from intimidating appearances to the larger force that ends them.
modern_relevance: You walk into a place that feels untouchable — security everywhere, power everywhere, cruelty everywhere — and still something in you knows it will not last.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: दोहा- पुर रखवारे देखि बहु कपि मन कीन्ह बिचार। अति लघु रूप धरों निसि नगर करौं पइसार ॥
translation: नगर के बहुसंख्यक रखवालों को देखकर हनुमान् जी ने मन में विचार किया कि अत्यंत छोटा रूप धरूँ और रात के समय नगर में प्रवेश करूँ ॥
english_translation: Seeing the many guards of the city, Hanuman thought to take a very small form and enter the city at night.
essence: Care beats force when the path is watched.
simple_meaning: Hanuman sees the heavy city guard and decides to shrink his form so he can slip in at night.
insight: It models adaptive action: assess the obstacle first, then choose the least exposed way through.
modern_relevance: You reach a locked building after midnight and realize the front entrance is watched. Instead of forcing your way in, you slow down, change approach, and move quietly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मसक समान रूप कपि धरी। लंकहि चलेउ सुमिरि नरहरी॥ नाम लंकिनी एक निसिचरी। सो कह चलेसि मोहि निंदरी ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी मच्छड़ के समान (छोटा सा) रूप धारण कर नर रूप से लीला करने वाले भगवान् श्री रामचंद्रजी का स्मरण करके लंका को चले (लंका के द्वार पर) लंकिनी नाम की एक राक्षसी रहती थी। वह बोली- मेरा निरादर करके (बिना मुझसे पूछे) कहाँ चला जा रहा है? ॥
english_translation: Hanuman took a tiny form like a mosquito and, remembering Lord Ram, set out for Lanka. At the gate stood a demoness named Lankini, who said, "Why are you passing me by without respect?"
essence: Remembering Ram makes even the smallest form fearless.
simple_meaning: Hanuman shrinks himself, remembers Ram, and heads into Lanka. At the gate, Lankini stops him and complains that he is ignoring her.
insight: It teaches you to enter difficulty lightly, with memory and restraint instead of ego.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room, keep your composure, and ignore the urge to prove yourself. Quiet focus gets you farther than force.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जानेहि नहीं मरमु सठ मोरा। मोर अहार जहाँ लगि चोरा॥ मुठिका एक महा कपि हनी। रुधिर बमत धरनीं ढनमनी ॥
translation: हे मूर्ख! तूने मेरा भेद नहीं जाना जहाँ तक (जितने) चोर हैं, वे सब मेरे आहार हैं। महाकपि हनुमान् जी ने उसे एक घूँसा मारा, जिससे वह खून की उलटी करती हुई पृथ्वी पर ल़ुढक पड़ी ॥
english_translation: You fool! You have not understood my secret. All the thieves here are my food. The great monkey struck her with one blow, and she fell to the ground vomiting blood.
essence: Pride looks fierce until it meets the right blow.
simple_meaning: Lankini boasts that intruders are her prey, but Hanuman knocks her down in one blow.
insight: It shows that arrogant resistance falls quickly before disciplined power.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where one person tries to intimidate everyone with loud confidence. The moment real competence shows up, the performance ends.
speaker: Lankini

verse_text: पुनि संभारि उठी सो लंका। जोरि पानि कर बिनय ससंका॥ जब रावनहि ब्रह्म बर दीन्हा। चलत बिरंच कहा मोहि चीन्हा ॥
translation: वह लंकिनी फिर अपने को संभालकर उठी और डर के मारे हाथ जोड़कर विनती करने लगी। (वह बोली-) रावण को जब ब्रह्माजी ने वर दिया था, तब चलते समय उन्होंने मुझे राक्षसों के विनाश की यह पहचान बता दी थी कि- ॥
english_translation: She then gathered herself and stood up. Terrified, the female guardian of Lanka folded her hands and pleaded. She said, 'When Brahma gave Ravana his boon, as he was leaving he told me this sign: ...'
essence: A small defeat can reveal a much larger danger.
simple_meaning: The guardian of Lanka regains herself, then speaks fearfully. She explains that Brahma once gave Ravana a boon and left behind a warning sign.
insight: It shifts attention from the blow itself to the meaning the blow reveals.
modern_relevance: You get corrected hard, then suddenly realize the other person was never just being difficult. Their fear has history, and now the conversation changes.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिकल होसि तैं कपि कें मारे। तब जानेसु निसिचर संघारे॥ तात मोर अति पुन्य बहूता। देखेउँ नयन राम कर दूता ॥
translation: जब तू बंदर के मारने से व्याकुल हो जाए, तब तू राक्षसों का संहार हुआ जान लेना। हे तात! मेरे बड़े पुण्य हैं, जो मैं श्री रामचंद्रजी के दूत (आप) को नेत्रों से देख पाई ॥
english_translation: When you are thrown into confusion by a monkey's blow, then know that the slaughter of the demons has begun. O dear one, I have great merit indeed, for I have seen with my own eyes the messenger of Ram.
essence: Ram's messenger turns even a blow into a blessing.
simple_meaning: Lankini realizes that Hanuman's blow means her side is in danger, and she feels blessed to have seen Ram's messenger with her own eyes.
insight: It shifts the mind from resisting disruption to recognizing sacred arrival in it.
modern_relevance: You get corrected hard by someone you underestimated, and instead of spiraling, you realize the encounter woke you up. Sometimes the blow is also the blessing.
speaker: Lankini

verse_text: तात स्वर्ग अपबर्ग सुख धरिअ तुला एक अंग। तूल न ताहि सकल मिलि जो सुख लव सतसंग ॥
translation: हे तात! स्वर्ग और मोक्ष के सब सुखों को तराजू के एक पलड़े में रखा जाए, तो भी वे सब मिलकर (दूसरे पलड़े पर रखे हुए) उस सुख के बराबर नहीं हो सकते, जो लव (क्षण) मात्र के सत्संग से होता है ॥
english_translation: O friend, if all the joys of heaven and liberation are placed on one side of a scale, they still cannot equal the joy of even a moment's company with holy fellowship.
essence: Holy company outweighs every reward, even freedom itself.
simple_meaning: Even the greatest rewards cannot equal the joy that comes from a brief moment in the company of the wise and devoted.
insight: It shifts value from external rewards to the company that shapes your mind and heart.
modern_relevance: You leave a noisy party and sit for ten quiet minutes with someone who truly understands you. That relief, that settling, is worth more than all the applause you chased that night.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रबिसि नगर कीजे सब काजा। हृदयँ राखि कोसलपुर राजा॥ गरल सुधा रिपु करहिं मिताई। गोपद सिंधु अनल सितलाई ॥
translation: अयोध्यापुरी के राजा श्री रघुनाथजी को हृदय में रखे हुए नगर में प्रवेश करके सब काम कीजिए। उसके लिए विष अमृत हो जाता है, शत्रु मित्रता करने लगते हैं, समुद्र गाय के खुर के बराबर हो जाता है, अग्नि में शीतलता आ जाती है ॥
english_translation: Enter the city and do all your work while keeping the king of Kosala in your heart. For such a person, poison becomes nectar, enemies become friends, the ocean becomes as small as a cow's hoofprint, and fire turns cool.
essence: Ram in the heart makes danger lose its power.
simple_meaning: Go into the world with Ram held in your heart. Then even what looks harmful, impossible, or hostile can turn helpful.
insight: It shifts attention from outer threat to inner remembrance, so action becomes fearless and clear.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense family gathering with your chest already tight. If you hold on to what is steady inside, the room does not get to define you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गरुड़ सुमेरु रेनु सम ताही। राम कृपा करि चितवा जाही॥ अति लघु रूप धरेउ हनुमाना। पैठा नगर सुमिरि भगवाना ॥
translation: और हे गरुड़जी! सुमेरु पर्वत उसके लिए रज के समान हो जाता है, जिसे श्री रामचंद्रजी ने एक बार कृपा करके देख लिया। तब हनुमान् जी ने बहुत ही छोटा रूप धारण किया और भगवान् का स्मरण करके नगर में प्रवेश किया ॥
english_translation: And Garuda, even Mount Sumeru becomes like a speck of dust for the one whom Ram has once looked upon with grace. Then Hanuman took a very small form and entered the city while remembering the divine.
essence: Ram’s grace makes the impossible feel small.
simple_meaning: Ram’s grace makes the impossible feel small. Hanuman then shrinks his form, keeps Ram in mind, and enters the city quietly.
insight: It shifts attention from your own scale to the protection and courage that grace gives.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone seems bigger, louder, and more certain than you. Then you remember who stands with you, and the fear loses its size.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंदिर मंदिर प्रति करि सोधा। देखे जहँ तहँ अगनित जोधा॥ गयउ दसानन मंदिर माहीं। अति बिचित्र कहि जात सो नाहीं ॥
translation: उन्होंने एक-एक (प्रत्येक) महल की खोज की। जहाँ-तहाँ असंख्य योद्धा देखे। फिर वे रावण के महल में गए। वह अत्यंत विचित्र था, जिसका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता ॥
english_translation: He searched each palace in turn and saw countless warriors everywhere. Then he entered Ravana's palace, which was so strange it cannot be described.
essence: The search continues until the hidden place is reached.
simple_meaning: Hanuman carefully searched every palace, saw many warriors, and finally entered Ravana's extraordinary palace.
insight: It keeps attention on careful searching, not on dramatic discovery yet.
modern_relevance: You check the last room in the house after midnight, still hoping the missing thing is there. The search itself has become a test of patience.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सयन किएँ देखा कपि तेही। मंदिर महुँ न दीखि बैदेही॥ भवन एक पुनि दीख सुहावा। हरि मंदिर तहँ भिन्न बनावा ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी ने उस (रावण) को शयन किए देखा, परंतु महल में जानकीजी नहीं दिखाई दीं। फिर एक सुंदर महल दिखाई दिया। वहाँ (उसमें) भगवान् का एक अलग मंदिर बना हुआ था ॥
english_translation: Hanuman saw him lying down, but did not see Sita in the palace. Then he saw a beautiful separate shrine there, a temple dedicated to Hari.
essence: Ram's presence survives even inside Ravana's palace.
simple_meaning: Hanuman found Ravana asleep, but Sita was not in the palace. Then he noticed a lovely separate shrine to Hari inside the building.
insight: It shifts attention from the search itself to the hidden sign that Ram's presence remains even in enemy territory.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everything feels hostile, and then you notice one small sign of faith on a shelf or wall. Even there, devotion has survived.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामायुध अंकित गृह सोभा बरनि न जाइ। नव तुलसिका बृंद तहँ देखि हरष कपिराई ॥
translation: वह महल श्री रामजी के आयुध (धनुष-बाण) के चिह्नों से अंकित था, उसकी शोभा वर्णन नहीं की जा सकती। वहाँ नवीन-नवीन तुलसी के वृक्ष-समूहों को देखकर कपिराज श्री हनुमान् जी हर्षित हुए ॥
english_translation: The mansion was marked with the emblems of Ram's weapons; its beauty cannot be described. Seeing fresh groves of tulsi there, Hanuman, king of the monkeys, felt joy.
essence: Ram's signs make even an enemy city feel like home.
simple_meaning: Hanuman finds a house marked by Ram's symbols and filled with tulsi, and his joy rises because he recognizes Ram's presence there.
insight: It trains you to notice the quiet signs of shared devotion and feel connection instead of isolation.
modern_relevance: You walk into a stranger's home and spot a small framed image, a prayer corner, a tulsi plant on the balcony. In that instant, the room stops feeling strange. Recognition creates warmth before a single word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लंका निसिचर निकर निवासा। इहाँ कहाँ सज्जन कर बासा॥ मन महुँ तरक करैं कपि लागा। तेहीं समय बिभीषनु जागा ॥
translation: लंका तो राक्षसों के समूह का निवास स्थान है। यहाँ सज्जन (साधु पुरुष) का निवास कहाँ? हनुमान् जी मन में इस प्रकार तर्क करने लगे। उसी समय विभीषणजी जागे ॥
english_translation: Lanka is the dwelling place of hosts of demons. Where could a good person possibly live here? Hanuman began thinking this in his mind, and at that very moment Vibhishana woke up.
essence: A good heart can be hidden inside a corrupt place.
simple_meaning: Hanuman looks at Lanka and wonders how any good person could live there. Just then, Vibhishana wakes up.
insight: It shifts attention from the crowd around you to the one person who does not belong to its corruption.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everything feels off, and then one quiet person changes the whole atmosphere. Recognition often begins before introductions.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम राम तेहिं सुमिरन कीन्हा। हृदयँ हरष कपि सज्जन चीन्हा॥ एहि सन सठि करिहउँ पहिचानी। साधु ते होइ न कारज हानी ॥
translation: उन्होंने (विभीषण ने) राम नाम का स्मरण (उच्चारण) किया। हनमान् जी ने उन्हें सज्जन जाना और हृदय में हर्षित हुए। (हनुमान् जी ने विचार किया कि) इनसे हठ करके (अपनी ओर से ही) परिचय करूँगा, क्योंकि साधु से कार्य की हानि नहीं होती। (प्रत्युत लाभ ही होता है) ॥
english_translation: He remembered Ram's name. Hanuman rejoiced in his heart and recognized him as a good person. He thought, "I will introduce myself to this one, because a good person never causes harm in a task."
essence: Shared reverence reveals who can be trusted.
simple_meaning: Hearing Ram's name, Hanuman feels joy and instantly trusts Vibhishana. He sees that a good person will not spoil the task.
insight: It shifts you from guarded doubt to discerning trust based on character and shared devotion.
modern_relevance: You meet someone in a tense room and they mention the same value you live by. The suspicion eases. Sometimes one honest signal is enough to know who can be trusted.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिप्र रूप धरि बचन सुनाए। सुनत बिभीषन उठि तहँ आए॥ करि प्रनाम पूँछी कुसलाई। बिप्र कहहु निज कथा बुझाई ॥
translation: ब्राह्मण का रूप धरकर हनुमान् जी ने उन्हें वचन सुनाए (पुकारा)। सुनते ही विभीषणजी उठकर वहाँ आए। प्रणाम करके कुशल पूछी (और कहा कि) हे ब्राह्मणदेव! अपनी कथा समझाकर कहिए ॥
english_translation: Taking the form of a Brahmin, Hanuman spoke to him. Hearing that, Vibhishana came there at once. He bowed and asked after his welfare, then said, "Brahmin, please tell me who you are and explain your story."
essence: Trust begins with respectful approach, not immediate revelation.
simple_meaning: Hanuman approaches in disguise, and Vibhishana responds with respect and curiosity, asking him to explain who he is and why he has come.
insight: It shows how humility and courtesy create the first bridge between strangers.
modern_relevance: You meet someone new at a gathering and feel they may understand you. Before you reveal yourself, you ask careful questions and wait for trust to form.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: की तुम्ह हरि दासन्ह महँ कोई। मोरें हृदय प्रीति अति होई॥ की तुम्ह रामु दीन अनुरागी। आयहु मोहि करन बड़भागी ॥
translation: क्या आप हरिभक्तों में से कोई हैं? क्योंकि आपको देखकर मेरे हृदय में अत्यंत प्रेम उमड़ रहा है। अथवा क्या आप दीनों से प्रेम करने वाले स्वयं श्री रामजी ही हैं जो मुझे बड़भागी बनाने (घर-बैठे दर्शन देकर कृतार्थ करने) आए हैं? ॥
english_translation: Are you one of Ram's devotees? My heart is overflowing with love. Or are you Ram himself, who loves the humble and has come to bless me?
essence: Devotion is so real it can feel like Ram has arrived.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana sees Hanuman and feels such deep affection that he wonders whether this visitor is a devotee of Ram or Ram himself.
insight: It teaches you to recognise devotion by its effect: it softens fear and awakens trust before words arrive.
modern_relevance: You meet someone in a hospital corridor and feel calm before they even speak. Some people carry such sincerity that being near them feels like being met by grace.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: तब हनुमंत कही सब राम कथा निज नाम। सुनत जुगल तन पुलक मन मगन सुमिरि गुन ग्राम ॥
translation: तब हनुमान् जी ने श्री रामचंद्रजी की सारी कथा कहकर अपना नाम बताया। सुनते ही दोनों के शरीर पुलकित हो गए और श्री रामजी के गुण समूहों का स्मरण करके दोनों के मन (प्रेम और आनंद में) मग्न हो गए ॥
english_translation: Then Hanuman told the whole story of Ram and revealed his own name. Hearing it, both bodies thrilled, and both minds became absorbed in remembering Ram's countless virtues.
essence: Ram’s story turns strangers into companions.
simple_meaning: Hanuman shares Ram’s story and his own identity, and that remembrance fills everyone with joy and devotion.
insight: It shows that sincere remembrance of Ram creates instant connection and shared joy.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who already loves the same teacher, ideal, or cause you do. One honest sentence about what matters most, and the whole room changes.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनहु पवनसुत रहनि हमारी। जिमि दसनन्हि महुँ जीभ बिचारी॥ तात कबहुँ मोहि जानि अनाथा। करिहहिं कृपा भानुकुल नाथा ॥
translation: (विभीषणजी ने कहा-) हे पवनपुत्र! मेरी रहनी सुनो। मैं यहाँ वैसे ही रहता हूँ जैसे दाँतों के बीच में बेचारी जीभ। हे तात! मुझे अनाथ जानकर सूर्यकुल के नाथ श्री रामचंद्रजी क्या कभी मुझ पर कृपा करेंगे? ॥
english_translation: Listen, son of the wind, to my way of living. I live like a tongue trapped between the teeth. O friend, if the Lord of the solar line knows me as helpless, will he ever show me grace?
essence: Helplessness becomes the doorway to Ram's grace.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana says he feels trapped in Lanka and helpless, like a tongue caught between teeth. He wonders whether Ram will ever take pity on him.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance to honest surrender.
modern_relevance: You know that moment when you finally admit, after months of pretending, that you cannot fix the mess alone? Vibhishana stands there first, asking for mercy instead of control.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: तामस तनु कछु साधन नाहीं। प्रीत न पद सरोज मन माहीं॥ अब मोहि भा भरोस हनुमंता। बिनु हरिकृपा मिलहिं नहिं संता ॥
translation: मेरा तामसी (राक्षस) शरीर होने से साधन तो कुछ बनता नहीं और न मन में श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणकमलों में प्रेम ही है, परंतु हे हनुमान् ! अब मुझे विश्वास हो गया कि श्री रामजी की मुझ पर कृपा है, क्योंकि हरि की कृपा के बिना संत नहीं मिलते ॥
english_translation: My body is born of darkness, so I have no real practice, and my mind holds no love for the lotus feet of Ram. Yet now, Hanuman, I trust that Ram has shown me grace, because without the divine's grace, noble seekers are not found.
essence: Grace can reach you before you feel worthy of it.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana says he feels spiritually unprepared, but he now trusts that Ram's grace has reached him. Noble seekers do not arrive by their own power alone.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-judgment to receptive trust, showing that grace can precede your own readiness.
modern_relevance: You sit in the therapist's waiting room, convinced you waited too long to ask for help. Then you realize the door was open before you found the courage to knock.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: जौं रघुबीर अनुग्रह कीन्हा। तौ तुम्ह मोहि दरसु हठि दीन्हा॥ सुनहु बिभीषन प्रभु कै रीती। करहिं सदा सेवक पर प्रीति ॥
translation: जब श्री रघुवीर ने कृपा की है, तभी तो आपने मुझे हठ करके (अपनी ओर से) दर्शन दिए हैं। (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे विभीषणजी! सुनिए, प्रभु की यही रीति है कि वे सेवक पर सदा ही प्रेम किया करते हैं ॥
english_translation: If Raghubir has shown grace, then you have forced me to reveal myself to you. Listen, Vibhishan: the Lord's way is always to love the servant.
essence: Grace arrives first, and love naturally follows the servant.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Vibhishan that their meeting happened only because Ram was gracious. He says Ram's nature is to always love and care for those who serve him.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-doubt to trust in a relationship that welcomes sincere service.
modern_relevance: You finally call the person who helped you through a hard season, and they act like it was nothing. That quiet warmth is what Hanuman is pointing to: true love moves toward service without keeping score.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: कहहु कवन मैं परम कुलीना। कपि चंचल सबहीं बिधि हीना॥ प्रात लेइ जो नाम हमारा। तेहि दिन ताहि न मिलै अहारा ॥
translation: भला कहिए, मैं ही कौन बड़ा कुलीन हूँ? (जाति का) चंचल वानर हूँ और सब प्रकार से नीच हूँ, प्रातःकाल जो हम लोगों (बंदरों) का नाम ले ले तो उस दिन उसे भोजन न मिले ॥
english_translation: What high birth do I have? I am a restless monkey, lacking every virtue. If someone even names us monkeys at dawn, that person will not get food that day.
essence: The one who drops pride becomes fit for grace.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says he is not noble or impressive by himself. He is a monkey with no special merit, and even his name brings bad luck to others. His worth comes only through Ram's grace.
insight: It shifts the mind from proving status to receiving grace through humility.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone seems polished, connected, and important. Instead of performing, you admit you are not the center. That honesty can open more doors than self-promotion.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: अस मैं अधम सखा सुनु मोहू पर रघुबीर। कीन्हीं कृपा सुमिरि गुन भरे बिलोचन नीर ॥
translation: हे सखा! सुनिए, मैं ऐसा अधम हूँ, पर श्री रामचंद्रजी ने तो मुझ पर भी कृपा ही की है। भगवान् के गुणों का स्मरण करके हनुमान् जी के दोनों नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया ॥
english_translation: O friend, listen: I am so lowly, yet Lord Raghubir has shown mercy even to me. Remembering the Lord's qualities, tears filled Hanuman's eyes.
essence: Ram's grace reaches you before your worthiness does.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says he is unworthy, yet Ram has still shown him kindness. Thinking of Ram's qualities moves him to tears.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-judgment to receptive devotion, where grace matters more than status.
modern_relevance: You sit in a quiet car after a hard day, feeling like you have failed too many times to be loved well. Then one small memory of kindness breaks you open again.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: जानतहूँ अस स्वामि बिसारी। फिरहिं ते काहे न होहिं दुखारी॥ एहि बिधि कहत राम गुन ग्रामा। पावा अनिर्बाच्य बिश्रामा ॥
translation: जो जानते हुए भी ऐसे स्वामी (श्री रघुनाथजी) को भुलाकर (विषयों के पीछे) भटकते फिरते हैं, वे दुःखी क्यों न हों? इस प्रकार श्री रामजी के गुण समूहों को कहते हुए उन्होंने अनिर्वचनीय (परम) शांति प्राप्त की ॥
english_translation: Those who forget such a master even after knowing him still wander after pleasures—why would they not suffer? In this way, speaking the many virtues of Ram, he attained indescribable peace.
essence: Forgetting Ram brings suffering; remembering him brings peace.
simple_meaning: Even after knowing Ram, people who forget him and chase other things end up in suffering. Speaking of Ram's virtues brings Hanuman deep peace.
insight: It shifts attention from scattered wanting back to the source of real steadiness.
modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message and somehow lose an hour. The noise feels normal until you remember what actually holds your life together.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: पुनि सब कथा बिभीषन कही। जेहि बिधि जनकसुता तहँ रही॥ तब हनुमंत कहा सुनु भ्राता। देखी चहउँ जानकी माता ॥
translation: फिर विभीषणजी ने, श्री जानकीजी जिस प्रकार वहाँ (लंका में) रहती थीं, वह सब कथा कही। तब हनुमान् जी ने कहा- हे भाई सुनो, मैं जानकी माता को देखता चाहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Then Vibhishana told the whole story of how Janaki had been living there. Then Hanuman said, "Brother, listen. I want to see Mother Janaki."
essence: Devotion is not satisfied by success; it wants presence.
simple_meaning: After hearing how Sita has been living in Lanka, Hanuman says he wants to see her. His mission is no longer just to find her; it becomes a direct, heartfelt longing to behold her.
insight: It shifts action from mere completion to loving presence.
modern_relevance: You finally reach the hospital room after days of worry, but standing at the door is not enough. You need to see the person you came for, hear their voice, know they are really there.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: हनुमान् जी का अशोक वाटिका में सीताजी को देकर दुःखी होना और रावण का सीताजी को भय दिखलाना जुगुति बिभीषन सकल सुनाई। चलेउ पवन सुत बिदा कराई॥ करि सोइ रूप गयउ पुनि तहवाँ। बन असोक सीता रह जहवाँ ॥
translation: विभीषणजी ने (माता के दर्शन की) सब युक्तियाँ (उपाय) कह सुनाईं। तब हनुमान् जी विदा लेकर चले। फिर वही (पहले का मसक सरीखा) रूप धरकर वहाँ गए, जहाँ अशोक वन में (वन के जिस भाग में) सीताजी रहती थीं ॥
english_translation: Vibhishana explained every way to reach Sita. Then Hanuman took leave and went back in the same form, to the part of Ashoka grove where Sita stayed.
essence: The path is revealed; the meeting is still ahead.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana gives Hanuman the route and method. Hanuman leaves, returns in the same disguise, and goes to the part of Ashoka grove where Sita is kept.
insight: It keeps the focus on preparation and stealth, not on emotional resolution yet.
modern_relevance: You get the address, the timing, and the plan before slipping into the room where someone is waiting for you. The real work is still ahead.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि मनहि महुँ कीन्ह प्रनामा। बैठेहिं बीति जात निसि जामा॥ कृस तनु सीस जटा एक बेनी। जपति हृदयँ रघुपति गुन श्रेनी ॥
translation: सीताजी को देखकर हनुमान् जी ने उन्हें मन ही में प्रणाम किया। उन्हें बैठे ही बैठे रात्रि के चारों पहर बीत जाते हैं। शरीर दुबला हो गया है, सिर पर जटाओं की एक वेणी (लट) है। हृदय में श्री रघुनाथजी के गुण समूहों का जाप (स्मरण) करती रहती हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing Sita, Hanuman bowed to her inwardly. He sat there as the night’s four watches passed. Her body had grown thin, her hair was tied in one braid, and her heart kept repeating the qualities of Raghupati.
essence: True devotion begins with silent respect and steady remembrance.
simple_meaning: Hanuman sees Sita and bows to her inwardly. She sits in deep sorrow, worn thin by waiting, while her mind stays fixed on Ram.
insight: It teaches you to meet suffering with quiet reverence before trying to fix it.
modern_relevance: You finally reach the person you came to help, and they look shattered from waiting. Before words come, respect and tenderness do.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निज पद नयन दिएँ मन राम पद कमल लीन। परम दुखी भा पवनसुत देखि जानकी दीन ॥
translation: श्री जानकीजी नेत्रों को अपने चरणों में लगाए हुए हैं (नीचे की ओर देख रही हैं) और मन श्री रामजी के चरण कमलों में लीन है। जानकीजी को दीन (दुःखी) देखकर पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी बहुत ही दुःखी हुए ॥
english_translation: Sita’s eyes rest on her own feet, while her mind rests on Ram’s lotus feet. Seeing Janaki so helpless, Hanuman became deeply distressed.
essence: Sorrow can bend the body without moving the heart from Ram.
simple_meaning: Sita is physically bowed in sorrow, but inwardly fixed on Ram. Hanuman feels deep pain when he sees her helpless state.
insight: It teaches you to notice both inner faith and outer pain at once, instead of reducing a person to only what you see.
modern_relevance: You visit someone in the hospital and they smile weakly while still asking about the person they love most. Their devotion is intact, and that makes their suffering hit even harder.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तरु पल्लव महँ रहा लुकाई। करइ बिचार करौं का भाई॥ तेहि अवसर रावनु तहँ आवा। संग नारि बहु किएँ बनावा ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी वृक्ष के पत्तों में छिप रहे और विचार करने लगे कि हे भाई! क्या करूँ (इनका दुःख कैसे दूर करूँ)? उसी समय बहुत सी स्त्रियों को साथ लिए सज-धजकर रावण वहाँ आया ॥
english_translation: Hanuman hid among the leaves of a tree and thought, 'Brother, what should I do?' At that moment, Ravana arrived there, adorned and accompanied by many women.
essence: Hidden patience can be the smartest form of strength.
simple_meaning: Hanuman hides in the tree and wonders what to do next. Then Ravana arrives, surrounded by women and dressed up.
insight: It teaches restraint before action, so the next move comes from awareness rather than impulse.
modern_relevance: You spot the person you need to avoid at the same event and stay still behind the crowd, waiting for the right opening instead of rushing in.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहु बिधि खल सीतहि समुझावा। साम दान भय भेद देखावा॥ कह रावनु सुनु सुमुखि सयानी। मंदोदरी आदि सब रानी ॥
translation: उस दुष्ट ने सीताजी को बहुत प्रकार से समझाया। साम, दान, भय और भेद दिखलाया। रावण ने कहा- हे सुमुखि! हे सयानी! सुनो! मंदोदरी आदि सब रानियों को- ॥
english_translation: The wicked one tried many ways to persuade Sita, showing her conciliation, gifts, fear, and division. Ravana said, 'Listen, beautiful and wise one. Mandodari and all the queens...'
essence: Power without reverence turns into coercion.
simple_meaning: Ravana tries every tactic he can think of to win Sita over: kindness, gifts, threats, and manipulation. He speaks as if flattery and power can bend her will.
insight: It exposes how manipulation shifts forms when direct control fails.
modern_relevance: Someone keeps texting after you said no, first sweetly, then angrily, then through mutual friends. The tactics change, but the attempt is the same.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: तव अनुचरीं करउँ पन मोरा। एक बार बिलोकु मम ओरा॥ तृन धरि ओट कहति बैदेही। सुमिरि अवधपति परम सनेही ॥
translation: मैं तुम्हारी दासी बना दूँगा, यह मेरा प्रण है। तुम एक बार मेरी ओर देखो तो सही! अपने परम स्नेही कोसलाधीश श्री रामचंद्रजी का स्मरण करके जानकीजी तिनके की आड़ (परदा) करके कहने लगीं- ॥
english_translation: I will become your servant; that is my vow. Look at me just once. Hiding herself behind a blade of grass, Vaidehi remembered the lord of Ayodhya, her beloved protector.
essence: True loyalty stays with the beloved even under threat.
simple_meaning: Sita, hidden and pleading, asks Ravana to look at her once while she remembers Ram, her beloved protector.
insight: It shifts the mind from outward pressure to inward allegiance.
modern_relevance: Someone keeps pushing you to compromise your values in a room where you feel cornered. You stay inwardly loyal to the person, principle, or love that still protects your heart.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सुनु दसमुख खद्योत प्रकासा। कबहुँ कि नलिनी करइ बिकासा॥ अस मन समुझु कहति जानकी। खल सुधि नहिं रघुबीर बान की ॥
translation: हे दशमुख! सुन, जुगनू के प्रकाश से कभी कमलिनी खिल सकती है? जानकीजी फिर कहती हैं- तू (अपने लिए भी) ऐसा ही मन में समझ ले। रे दुष्ट! तुझे श्री रघुवीर के बाण की खबर नहीं है ॥
english_translation: O ten-faced one, listen: can a water lily ever bloom by the light of a firefly? Understand this in your own mind as well. O wicked one, you do not know the force of Raghubir's arrows.
essence: Tiny force cannot touch what is protected by Ram.
simple_meaning: Sita tells Ravana that his tiny power cannot overcome Ram's strength. She warns him to understand his own weakness before it is too late.
insight: It teaches you to see intimidation clearly and refuse to be overawed by it.
modern_relevance: Someone keeps pushing you in a meeting, acting louder than they are strong. You do not need to match the noise to know the truth of the situation.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सठ सूनें हरि आनेहि मोही। अधम निलज्ज लाज नहिं तोही ॥
translation: रे पापी! तू मुझे सूने में हर लाया है। रे अधम! निर्लज्ज! तुझे लज्जा नहीं आती? ॥
english_translation: You shameless fool, you brought me here in secret.
essence: Hidden cruelty becomes more shameful when it meets clear speech.
simple_meaning: Sita rebukes Ravana for abducting her in secret and for having no shame.
insight: It names wrongdoing directly, refusing to let fear or isolation soften the truth.
modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a private message, a closed room, or a manipulative conversation, hoping silence will make you smaller. Her words remind you that dishonour does not become power just because it hides.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: आपुहि सुनि खद्योत सम रामहि भानु समान। परुष बचन सुनि काढ़ि असि बोला अति खिसिआन ॥
translation: अपने को जुगनू के समान और रामचंद्रजी को सूर्य के समान सुनकर और सीताजी के कठोर वचनों को सुनकर रावण तलवार निकालकर बड़े गुस्से में आकर बोला- ॥
english_translation: Hearing himself compared to a firefly and Ramchandra to the sun, and hearing Sita's harsh words, Ravana drew his sword and spoke in great fury.
essence: Pride cannot bear comparison, so it reaches for force.
simple_meaning: Ravana is insulted by Sita's words and enraged enough to draw his sword.
insight: It shows how wounded ego reacts before reason can return.
modern_relevance: Someone points out your blind spot in a meeting, and your first urge is to snap back. That flash of anger reveals how fragile pride can be.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सीता तैं मम कृत अपमाना। कटिहउँ तव सिर कठिन कृपाना॥ नाहिं त सपदि मानु मम बानी। सुमुखि होति न त जीवन हानी ॥
translation: सीता! तूने मेरा अपनाम किया है। मैं तेरा सिर इस कठोर कृपाण से काट डालूँगा। नहीं तो (अब भी) जल्दी मेरी बात मान ले। हे सुमुखि! नहीं तो जीवन से हाथ धोना पड़ेगा ॥
english_translation: Sita, you have insulted me. I will cut off your head with this sharp sword. Obey my words at once, fair-faced one, or you will lose your life.
essence: Ego, when challenged, reaches for violence.
simple_meaning: Ravana threatens Sita with death unless she obeys him immediately.
insight: It shows how wounded pride tries to regain control through intimidation.
modern_relevance: Someone feels rejected in a relationship and suddenly starts speaking in threats, blame, or ultimatums. The real wound is not the refusal — it is the bruised ego underneath it.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: स्याम सरोज दाम सम सुंदर। प्रभु भुज करि कर सम दसकंधर॥ सो भुज कंठ कि तव असि घोरा। सुनु सठ अस प्रवान पन मोरा ॥
translation: (सीताजी ने कहा-) हे दशग्रीव! प्रभु की भुजा जो श्याम कमल की माला के समान सुंदर और हाथी की सूँड के समान (पुष्ट तथा विशाल) है, या तो वह भुजा ही मेरे कंठ में पड़ेगी या तेरी भयानक तलवार ही। रे शठ! सुन, यही मेरा सच्चा प्रण है ॥
english_translation: Sita said: "O Dashanan, the beautiful arm of the Lord is like a garland of dark lotuses and strong as an elephant's trunk. Either that arm will rest on my neck, or your dreadful sword will. Listen, fool — this is my true vow."
essence: Love becomes unbreakable when fear no longer decides.
simple_meaning: Sita refuses Ravana's threat and declares her vow: only Ram's arm or Ravana's sword will reach her neck.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to vow-keeping under pressure.
modern_relevance: Someone corners you with an ultimatum in a message thread, expecting panic or compromise. You pause, remember what you will not betray, and answer from that center instead of from fear.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: चंद्रहास हरु मम परितापं। रघुपति बिरह अनल संजातं॥ सीतल निसित बहसि बर धारा। कह सीता हरु मम दुख भारा ॥
translation: सीताजी कहती हैं- हे चंद्रहास (तलवार)! श्री रघुनाथजी के विरह की अग्नि से उत्पन्न मेरी बड़ी भारी जलन को तू हर ले, हे तलवार! तू शीतल, तीव्र और श्रेष्ठ धारा बहाती है (अर्थात् तेरी धारा ठंडी और तेज है), तू मेरे दुःख के बोझ को हर ले ॥
english_translation: O Chandrahasa, remove my burning pain. The fire of separation from Raghupati has arisen in me. You flow as a cool, sharp, excellent blade. O Sita says, remove the heavy burden of my sorrow.
essence: Separation burns so hot that even a sword feels like mercy.
simple_meaning: Sita, overwhelmed by separation from Ram, asks a sword to cut away her pain and heavy sorrow.
insight: It reveals how separation can overwhelm the mind, and how devotion can speak through raw pain instead of composure.
modern_relevance: You stare at your phone at 2 a.m., waiting for one message that would calm everything. When longing gets that sharp, even a small sign can feel like rescue.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सुनत बचन पुनि मारन धावा। मयतनयाँ कहि नीति बुझावा॥ कहेसि सकल निसिचरिन्ह बोलाई। सीतहि बहु बिधि त्रासहु जाई ॥
translation: सीताजी के ये वचन सुनते ही वह मारने दौड़ा। तब मय दानव की पुत्री मन्दोदरी ने नीति कहकर उसे समझाया। तब रावण ने सब दासियों को बुलाकर कहा कि जाकर सीता को बहुत प्रकार से भय दिखलाओ ॥
english_translation: Hearing Sita's words, he rushed to kill her. Then Mandodari, daughter of Maya, tried to counsel him with reason. Ravana then called all the female attendants and ordered them to go and frighten Sita in every way.
essence: Pride, when checked, often turns to intimidation.
simple_meaning: Ravana reacts with rage, then shifts to intimidation. Mandodari tries to restrain him, but he orders his attendants to scare Sita instead.
insight: It shows how wounded ego turns from direct attack to calculated cruelty.
modern_relevance: You get a harsh message and instantly want to strike back. A calmer voice tries to interrupt, but your hurt still looks for someone weaker to intimidate.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: मास दिवस महुँ कहा न माना। तौ मैं मारबि काढ़ि कृपाना ॥
translation: यदि महीने भर में यह कहा न माने तो मैं इसे तलवार निकालकर मार डालूँगा ॥
english_translation: If she does not agree within a month, I will draw my sword and kill her.
essence: Threats begin where real influence has ended.
simple_meaning: Ravana threatens Sita with death if she does not give in within a month.
insight: It exposes how coercion replaces persuasion when ego cannot accept refusal.
modern_relevance: A person sends one last message: answer by Friday, or else. The deadline is really a mask for helplessness.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: भवन गयउ दसकंधर इहाँ पिसाचिनि बृंद। सीतहि त्रास देखावहिं धरहिं रूप बहु मंद ॥
translation: (यों कहकर) रावण घर चला गया। यहाँ राक्षसियों के समूह बहुत से बुरे रूप धरकर सीताजी को भय दिखलाने लगे ॥
english_translation: Ravana went home, and there the women-demons took many ugly forms to frighten Sita.
essence: Cruelty tries to win by multiplying fear around the vulnerable.
simple_meaning: Ravana leaves, and his demon attendants try to scare Sita by taking on many ugly forms.
insight: It shows how intimidation multiplies when fear is used as a group tactic.
modern_relevance: A room goes silent after the argument ends, but the pressure still hangs there. Then the people around you start adding their own fear, making the moment feel even smaller.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: त्रिजटा नाम राच्छसी एका। राम चरन रति निपुन बिबेका॥ सबन्हौ बोलि सुनाएसि सपना। सीतहि सेइ करहु हित अपना ॥
translation: उनमें एक त्रिजटा नाम की राक्षसी थी। उसकी श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणों में प्रीति थी और वह विवेक (ज्ञान) में निपुण थी। उसने सबों को बुलाकर अपना स्वप्न सुनाया और कहा- सीताजी की सेवा करके अपना कल्याण कर लो ॥
english_translation: There was a demoness named Trijata who was skilled in clear seeing and loved Ram's feet. She called everyone and told them her dream: serve Sita and do what is good for you.
essence: Clear seeing turns loyalty into service.
simple_meaning: Trijata, a demoness loyal to Ram, sees clearly enough to protect Sita and advise the other women to serve her for their own good.
insight: It shifts you from crowd cruelty to protective action guided by clear seeing.
modern_relevance: At work, everyone is mocking the person under pressure, but one colleague quietly helps instead of joining in. That small act of loyalty changes the room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सपनें बानर लंका जारी। जातुधान सेना सब मारी॥ खर आरूढ़ नगन दससीसा। मुंडित सिर खंडित भुज बीसा ॥
translation: स्वप्न (मैंने देखा कि) एक बंदर ने लंका जला दी। राक्षसों की सारी सेना मार डाली गई। रावण नंगा है और गदहे पर सवार है। उसके सिर मुँडे हुए हैं, बीसों भुजाएँ कटी हुई हैं ॥
english_translation: In the dream, a monkey burned Lanka. The entire army of demons was slain. Ravana rode naked on a donkey, with his head shaved and all twenty arms cut off.
essence: The nightmare of oppression is already breaking in the mind of a true witness.
simple_meaning: Trijata dreams that a monkey destroys Lanka, Ravana is humiliated, and his army is wiped out. The dream is a sign that Sita's suffering will end.
insight: It shifts attention from present fear to a larger pattern of coming reversal.
modern_relevance: You wake before sunrise after a nightmare, still shaken — then one calm message changes everything. Relief can begin before the situation itself has changed.
speaker: Trijata

verse_text: एहि बिधि सो दच्छिन दिसि जाई। लंका मनहुँ बिभीषन पाई॥ नगर फिरी रघुबीर दोहाई। तब प्रभु सीता बोलि पठाई ॥
translation: इस प्रकार से वह दक्षिण (यमपुरी की) दिशा को जा रहा है और मानो लंका विभीषण ने पाई है। नगर में श्री रामचंद्रजी की दुहाई फिर गई। तब प्रभु ने सीताजी को बुला भेजा ॥
english_translation: In this way he went toward the southern direction, as if Lanka had already been won by Vibhishana. The cry of Lord Ram spread through the city. Then the Lord sent for Sita.
essence: Ram's presence has already begun remaking Lanka.
simple_meaning: He moves through Lanka as if it already belongs to Vibhishana, Ram's call spreads everywhere, and then Sita is summoned.
insight: It marks movement from hidden searching to open recognition and the next step in reunion.
modern_relevance: You hear your name called from the next room after days of waiting. Something has shifted, but you still don't know the whole story yet.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: यह सपना मैं कहउँ पुकारी। होइहि सत्य गएँ दिन चारी॥ तासु बचन सुनि ते सब डरीं। जनकसुता के चरनन्हि परीं ॥
translation: मैं पुकारकर (निश्चय के साथ) कहती हूँ कि यह स्वप्न चार (कुछ ही) दिनों बाद सत्य होकर रहेगा। उसके वचन सुनकर वे सब राक्षसियाँ डर गईं और जानकीजी के चरणों पर गिर पड़ीं ॥
english_translation: I declare with certainty that this dream will come true in four days. Hearing her words, they all grew afraid and fell at Janaki's feet.
essence: Fear collapses when truth speaks with certainty.
simple_meaning: The women hear a confident prediction that Sita's rescue is near, and their fear breaks. They bow to her in alarm and respect.
insight: It shifts attention from the crowd's panic to the quiet authority of truth.
modern_relevance: A tense room goes quiet when someone speaks with calm certainty. The people who were mocking you a moment ago suddenly feel how shaky their confidence really was.
speaker: Shurpanakha's attendants

verse_text: जहँ तहँ गईं सकल तब सीता कर मन सोच। मास दिवस बीतें मोहि मारिहि निसिचर पोच ॥
translation: तब (इसके बाद) वे सब जहाँ-तहाँ चली गईं। सीताजी मन में सोच करने लगीं कि एक महीना बीत जाने पर नीच राक्षस रावण मुझे मारेगा ॥
english_translation: Then all of them went away here and there, and Sita thought in her mind: after a month passes, that wicked demon will kill me.
essence: Fear makes waiting feel like punishment.
simple_meaning: After the demon women leave, Sita feels trapped and fears that once a month passes, Ravana will kill her.
insight: It reveals how fear magnifies time and turns waiting into emotional pain.
modern_relevance: You refresh your phone for a message that never comes, and every hour starts to feel like bad news. Waiting under pressure can stretch time into suffering.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: त्रिजटा सन बोलीं कर जोरी। मातु बिपति संगिनि तैं मोरी॥ तजौं देह करु बेगि उपाई। दुसह बिरहु अब नहिं सहि जाई ॥
translation: सीताजी हाथ जोड़कर त्रिजटा से बोलीं- हे माता! तू मेरी विपत्ति की संगिनी है। जल्दी कोई ऐसा उपाय कर जिससे मैं शरीर छोड़ सकूँ। विरह असह्म हो चला है, अब यह सहा नहीं जाता ॥
english_translation: Sita, with folded hands, said to Trijata: “Mother, you are my companion in this suffering. Quickly find some way for me to leave this body. This unbearable separation can no longer be endured.”
essence: Shared suffering can become a plea for release.
simple_meaning: Sita tells Trijata that she feels utterly overwhelmed by separation and asks for any way to end her suffering.
insight: It shifts attention from fixing suffering to staying present with someone who is suffering.
modern_relevance: You sit beside someone in a hospital corridor, and they finally say the pain is too much to carry alone. What they need first is not advice, but a witness.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: आनि काठ रचु चिता बनाई। मातु अनल पुनि देहि लगाई॥ सत्य करहि मम प्रीति सयानी। सुनै को श्रवन सूल सम बानी ॥
translation: काठ लाकर चिता बनाकर सजा दे। हे माता! फिर उसमें आग लगा दे। हे सयानी! तू मेरी प्रीति को सत्य कर दे। रावण की शूल के समान दुःख देने वाली वाणी कानों से कौन सुने? ॥
english_translation: Bring wood and make a pyre. O mother, then set it alight. Wise one, make my love come true. Who can bear these words, sharp as a spear, in the ears?
essence: When suffering becomes unbearable, even hearing more can feel like another wound.
simple_meaning: Sita begs Trijata to build a pyre and light it so she can end her suffering. She says hearing Ravana's painful words is unbearable.
insight: It shows the mind at the edge of endurance, where the wish is not for answers but for escape from suffering.
modern_relevance: You keep the phone face down because one more message from the person who hurt you would break you again. Sometimes pain is so raw that even hearing more feels like injury.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सुनत बचन पद गहि समुझाएसि। प्रभु प्रताप बल सुजसु सुनाएसि॥ निसि न अनल मिल सुनु सुकुमारी। अस कहि सो निज भवन सिधारी।3॥
translation: सीताजी के वचन सुनकर त्रिजटा ने चरण पकड़कर उन्हें समझाया और प्रभु का प्रताप, बल और सुयश सुनाया। (उसने कहा-) हे सुकुमारी! सुनो रात्रि के समय आग नहीं मिलेगी। ऐसा कहकर वह अपने घर चली गई ॥
english_translation: Hearing her words, Trijata took her by the feet and consoled her. She spoke of the Lord's power, strength, and fame. “Listen, gentle one: at night, fire will not be found.” Saying this, she returned to her own home.
essence: Hope returns when someone names the strength still guarding you.
simple_meaning: Trijata comforts Sita by praising Ram’s power and telling her that fire cannot be found at night.
insight: It shifts you from despair to trust in protection that may not be visible yet.
modern_relevance: A friend sits beside you after midnight, when panic feels absolute. They do not argue with your pain; they steady you with a truth bigger than the fear.
speaker: Trijata

verse_text: कह सीता बिधि भा प्रतिकूला। मिलिहि न पावक मिटिहि न सूला॥ देखिअत प्रगट गगन अंगारा। अवनि न आवत एकउ तारा ॥
translation: सीताजी (मन ही मन) कहने लगीं- (क्या करूँ) विधाता ही विपरीत हो गया। न आग मिलेगी, न पीड़ा मिटेगी। आकाश में अंगारे प्रकट दिखाई दे रहे हैं, पर पृथ्वी पर एक भी तारा नहीं आता ॥
english_translation: Sita said inwardly, 'Fate has turned against me. I will not find fire, and my pain will not end. The sky appears filled with burning embers, yet not a single star comes down to the earth.'
essence: Despair can make even a bright sky feel empty.
simple_meaning: Sita feels that even the world has turned against her. She sees no way for her suffering to end, and no relief seems possible.
insight: It captures how suffering narrows perception until even beauty feels unavailable.
modern_relevance: You refresh your phone at 2 a.m. and still see nothing that changes the situation. When fear is this heavy, even ordinary things start to look cruel.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: पावकमय ससि स्रवत न आगी। मानहुँ मोहि जानि हतभागी॥ सुनहि बिनय मम बिटप असोका। सत्य नाम करु हरु मम सोका ॥
translation: चंद्रमा अग्निमय है, किंतु वह भी मानो मुझे हतभागिनी जानकर आग नहीं बरसाता। हे अशोक वृक्ष! मेरी विनती सुन। मेरा शोक हर ले और अपना (अशोक) नाम सत्य कर ॥
english_translation: The moon is made of fire, yet it does not rain fire on me, as if it knows I am unfortunate. Listen to my plea, Ashoka tree: remove my sorrow and make your name truly true.
essence: Even grief can become a prayer for relief.
simple_meaning: Sita feels so abandoned that even the moon seems unwilling to burn her. She pleads with the Ashoka tree to live up to its name and remove her sorrow.
insight: It turns private suffering into a direct plea, showing how devotion can speak to the world itself.
modern_relevance: You sit alone at night after a message that never came, staring at the window like it might answer. Sita knows that feeling: when sorrow is so close, even the world seems to reflect it back.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: नूतन किसलय अनल समाना। देहि अगिनि जनि करहि निदाना॥ देखि परम बिरहाकुल सीता। सो छन कपिहि कलप सम बीता ॥
translation: तेरे नए-नए कोमल पत्ते अग्नि के समान हैं। अग्नि दे, विरह रोग का अंत मत कर (अर्थात् विरह रोग को बढ़ाकर सीमा तक न पहुँचा) सीताजी को विरह से परम व्याकुल देखकर वह क्षण हनुमान् जी को कल्प के समान बीता ॥
english_translation: Your tender new leaves look like fire. Give me fire, but do not end this burning. Seeing Sita utterly overwhelmed by separation, that one moment felt like a world-age to Hanuman.
essence: Compassion makes another's suffering feel like your own clock has stopped.
simple_meaning: Hanuman sees Sita's intense sorrow and feels time slow to a crawl. He is moved by her suffering and the unbearable heat of the Ashoka grove.
insight: It trains you to feel another person's distress as urgent and real, not as a story happening at a distance.
modern_relevance: You sit beside a friend in the emergency room and keep checking the clock, but the minutes barely move. When someone's pain matters to you, time stops behaving normally.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: कपि करि हृदयँ बिचार दीन्हि मुद्रिका डारि तब। जनु असोक अंगार दीन्ह हरषि उठि कर गहेउ ॥
translation: तब हनुमान् जी ने हदय में विचार कर (सीताजी के सामने) अँगूठी डाल दी, मानो अशोक ने अंगारा दे दिया। (यह समझकर) सीताजी ने हर्षित होकर उठकर उसे हाथ में ले लिया ॥
english_translation: Then Hanuman, thinking deeply in his heart, placed the ring there. It was as if the Ashoka tree had handed over a spark; delighted, Sita rose and took it in her hand.
essence: A small sign can turn grief into hope.
simple_meaning: Hanuman places Ram's ring before Sita, and she receives it with joy. The moment feels like a spark of hope in the middle of deep sorrow.
insight: It shows how a single unmistakable sign can break despair and restore trust.
modern_relevance: You open a message from someone you thought had forgotten you, and one small sign changes your whole body. That is this moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब देखी मुद्रिका मनोहर। राम नाम अंकित अति सुंदर॥ चकित चितव मुदरी पहिचानी। हरष बिषाद हृदयँ अकुलानी ॥
translation: तब उन्होंने राम-नाम से अंकित अत्यंत सुंदर एवं मनोहर अँगूठी देखी। अँगूठी को पहचानकर सीताजी आश्चर्यचकित होकर उसे देखने लगीं और हर्ष तथा विषाद से हृदय में अकुला उठीं ॥
english_translation: Then she saw the beautiful ring, engraved with Ram's name, very lovely indeed. Recognizing the ring, Sita stared in wonder, and her heart trembled with joy and sorrow.
essence: A beloved sign can bring joy and grief together.
simple_meaning: Sita recognizes Ram's ring and is shaken by both joy and grief at once.
insight: It shows how a single sign can awaken both memory and longing at the same time.
modern_relevance: You open a message and see a name you had almost stopped hoping for. Relief arrives first, then the ache of everything still missing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जीति को सकइ अजय रघुराई। माया तें असि रचि नहिं जाई॥ सीता मन बिचार कर नाना। मधुर बचन बोलेउ हनुमाना ॥
translation: (वे सोचने लगीं-) श्री रघुनाथजी तो सर्वथा अजेय हैं, उन्हें कौन जीत सकता है? और माया से ऐसी (माया के उपादान से सर्वथा रहित दिव्य, चिन्मय) अँगूठी बनाई नहीं जा सकती। सीताजी मन में अनेक प्रकार के विचार कर रही थीं। इसी समय हनुमान् जी मधुर वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: Who can conquer the unconquerable Raghunath? No one can create such a ring except through divine power. Sita reflected on this in many ways, and then Hanuman spoke sweetly.
essence: Proof arrives before certainty, and the heart knows first.
simple_meaning: Sita recognizes that Ram is unconquerable and that this ring could only come through divine power. While she weighs these thoughts, Hanuman begins speaking gently.
insight: It shows how recognition can arise before certainty, and how gentle speech can meet a mind full of wonder.
modern_relevance: You hold a message that feels too precise to be coincidence, and your mind keeps circling it. Before you can name the feeling, someone speaks and confirms what your heart already sensed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामचंद्र गुन बरनैं लागा। सुनतहिं सीता कर दुख भागा॥ लागीं सुनैं श्रवन मन लाई। आदिहु तें सब कथा सुनाई ॥
translation: वे श्री रामचंद्रजी के गुणों का वर्णन करने लगे, (जिनके) सुनते ही सीताजी का दुःख भाग गया। वे कान और मन लगाकर उन्हें सुनने लगीं। हनुमान् जी ने आदि से लेकर अब तक की सारी कथा कह सुनाई ॥
english_translation: Hanuman began to describe Ramchandra's virtues, and as soon as Sita heard them, her sorrow fell away. She listened with her ears and mind fully focused, and Hanuman told the whole story from the beginning.
essence: Ram's virtues can lift grief before any problem is solved.
simple_meaning: Hanuman praises Ram, and Sita's sorrow fades as she listens with complete attention. Then he tells her the whole story from the beginning.
insight: It shows how remembrance of what is beloved can dissolve despair and restore attention.
modern_relevance: You are shaking after bad news, and one calm voice begins naming what is still true. Your chest loosens before the problem is solved.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: श्रवनामृत जेहिं कथा सुहाई। कही सो प्रगट होति किन भाई॥ तब हनुमंत निकट चलि गयऊ। फिरि बैठीं मन बिसमय भयऊ ॥
translation: (सीताजी बोलीं-) जिसने कानों के लिए अमृत रूप यह सुंदर कथा कही, वह हे भाई! प्रकट क्यों नहीं होता? तब हनुमान् जी पास चले गए। उन्हें देखकर सीताजी फिरकर (मुख फेरकर) बैठ गईं? उनके मन में आश्चर्य हुआ ॥
english_translation: “The one who spoke this sweet story, nectar for the ears — why does he not appear, brother?” Then Hanuman moved close. Seeing him, Sita turned away again, and wonder filled her mind.
essence: The comforted heart longs to meet the one who brought the comfort.
simple_meaning: Sita wonders why the one who spoke such a sweet, comforting story is not visible. Then Hanuman comes closer, and she turns away in surprise.
insight: It shifts attention from the message alone to the living presence that carries it.
modern_relevance: You hear a voice note that calms you after a brutal day, and then you want to see the person behind it. Relief often turns into wonder when comfort becomes real.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: राम दूत मैं मातु जानकी। सत्य सपथ करुनानिधान की॥ यह मुद्रिका मातु मैं आनी। दीन्हि राम तुम्ह कहँ सहिदानी ॥
translation: (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे माता जानकी मैं श्री रामजी का दूत हूँ। करुणानिधान की सच्ची शपथ करता हूँ, हे माता! यह अँगूठी मैं ही लाया हूँ। श्री रामजी ने मुझे आपके लिए यह सहिदानी (निशानी या पहिचान) दी है ॥
english_translation: I am Rama's messenger, Mother Janaki. I swear this truth by the compassionate one. I brought this ring, and Rama gave it to me as your token.
essence: True devotion proves itself by carrying the beloved's token.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita that he is Ram's messenger and proves it by showing the ring Ram gave him.
insight: It teaches you that devotion is made credible through faithful action and recognizable signs.
modern_relevance: You hear from someone after weeks of silence, and the first thing you need is proof it really is them. Sometimes a small token carries more comfort than a thousand promises.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: नर बानरहि संग कहु कैसें। कही कथा भइ संगति जैसें ॥
translation: (सीताजी ने पूछा-) नर और वानर का संग कहो कैसे हुआ? तब हनुमानजी ने जैसे संग हुआ था, वह सब कथा कही ॥
english_translation: How did a man and a monkey come together? Hanuman then told the whole story of how that bond happened.
essence: Trust grows when the hidden story is finally told.
simple_meaning: Sita asks how a human and a monkey came to be together, and Hanuman begins explaining their bond.
insight: It shifts attention from the strange pairing to the story that created trust.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who feels impossible to trust, then one honest conversation changes everything. Sometimes the bond makes sense only after you hear the story behind it.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: कपि के बचन सप्रेम सुनि उपजा मन बिस्वास जाना मन क्रम बचन यह कृपासिंधु कर दास ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी के प्रेमयक्त वचन सुनकर सीताजी के मन में विश्वास उत्पन्न हो गया, उन्होंने जान लिया कि यह मन, वचन और कर्म से कृपासागर श्री रघुनाथजी का दास है ॥
english_translation: Hearing the monkey's loving words, trust arose in Sita's mind. She knew him to be a servant of the merciful Raghunath in mind, action, and speech.
essence: Trust awakens when love, speech, and action all point the same way.
simple_meaning: Sita hears Hanuman speak with love and immediately trusts him. She recognises that his mind, words, and actions all belong to Ram.
insight: It teaches you to look for alignment between intention, speech, and action before giving your trust.
modern_relevance: Someone texts you with perfect words, but their actions feel off. Then one message arrives with warmth, consistency, and no agenda — and you know you can trust them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरिजन जानि प्रीति अति गाढ़ी। सजल नयन पुलकावलि बाढ़ी॥ बूड़त बिरह जलधि हनुमाना। भयहु तात मो कहुँ जलजाना ॥
translation: भगवान का जन (सेवक) जानकर अत्यंत गाढ़ी प्रीति हो गई। नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया और शरीर अत्यंत पुलकित हो गया (सीताजी ने कहा-) हे तात हनुमान् ! विरहसागर में डूबती हुई मुझको तुम जहाज हुए ॥
english_translation: Knowing him as a servant of the divine, her love became intense. Her eyes filled with tears, her body thrilled with joy. (Sita said,) "Hanuman, I was drowning in the ocean of separation; you became the boat that carried me across."
essence: True devotion becomes a boat for someone drowning in separation.
simple_meaning: Sita recognises Hanuman as a devoted servant and feels deep love and relief. His arrival feels like a boat rescuing her from the ocean of separation.
insight: It shifts devotion from abstract admiration to active rescue: love becomes something that helps another person cross suffering.
modern_relevance: You finally hear from the one person who understood your pain without explanation. In that moment, their presence doesn’t just soothe you — it makes survival feel possible again.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: अब कहु कुसल जाउँ बलिहारी। अनुज सहित सुख भवन खरारी॥ कोमलचित कृपाल रघुराई। कपि केहि हेतु धरी निठुराई ॥
translation: मैं बलिहारी जाती हूँ, अब छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित खर के शत्रु सुखधाम प्रभु का कुशल-मंगल कहो। श्री रघुनाथजी तो कोमल हृदय और कृपालु हैं। फिर हे हनुमान् ! उन्होंने किस कारण यह निष्ठुरता धारण कर ली है? ॥
english_translation: I bow to you. Tell me now of the welfare of the Lord of the auspicious home, along with Lakshman, his younger brother. Raghunath is tender-hearted and full of grace. Then, O Hanuman, why has he taken on such harshness?
essence: True tenderness can seem hidden when love is stretched by separation.
simple_meaning: Sita asks Hanuman to tell her whether Ram and Lakshman are well. She remembers Ram as kind and soft-hearted, so his seeming harshness pains her.
insight: It teaches you to notice how separation can make even love feel like hardness.
modern_relevance: You read a short, flat text from someone who once loved you warmly, and your chest tightens. You know their tenderness too well to mistake silence for indifference.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सहज बानि सेवक सुखदायक। कबहुँक सुरति करत रघुनायक॥ कबहुँ नयन मम सीतल ताता। होइहहिं निरखि स्याम मृदु गाता ॥
translation: सेवक को सुख देना उनकी स्वाभाविक बान है। वे श्री रघुनाथजी क्या कभी मेरी भी याद करते हैं? हे तात! क्या कभी उनके कोमल साँवले अंगों को देखकर मेरे नेत्र शीतल होंगे? ॥
english_translation: Service is their natural way of being. Do they ever remember me? O father, will my eyes grow cool when I see his soft dark form?
essence: Ram's servants find comfort because his nature is to remember and soothe them.
simple_meaning: Ram naturally brings comfort to those who serve him. Sita longs for his remembrance and hopes that seeing his gentle form will soothe her grief.
insight: It shifts longing from panic to trust: remembrance itself becomes a refuge.
modern_relevance: You wait by your phone after sending a message that matters. The silence hurts, but part of you still trusts that the person who loves you has not forgotten.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: बचनु न आव नयन भरे बारी। अहह नाथ हौं निपट बिसारी॥ देखि परम बिरहाकुल सीता। बोला कपि मृदु बचन बिनीता ॥
translation: (मुँह से) वचन नहीं निकलता, नेत्रों में (विरह के आँसुओं का) जल भर आया। (बड़े दुःख से वे बोलीं-) हा नाथ! आपने मुझे बिलकुल ही भुला दिया! सीताजी को विरह से परम व्याकुल देखकर हनुमान् जी कोमल और विनीत वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: Her words would not come out; tears filled her eyes. "Ah, Lord, you have completely forgotten me." Seeing Sita overwhelmed by separation, Hanuman spoke gentle, humble words.
essence: Deep grief needs gentle speech, not force.
simple_meaning: Sita is so overwhelmed by separation that she cannot speak clearly, and Hanuman responds with gentle, respectful words.
insight: It teaches you to meet raw grief with restraint, tenderness, and respect before trying to fix anything.
modern_relevance: You call someone at 2 a.m. after a breakup and can barely speak. The right response is not advice first, but a voice gentle enough to hold your shaking.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मातु कुसल प्रभु अनुज समेता। तव दुख दुखी सुकृपा निकेता॥ जनि जननी मानह जियँ ऊना। तुम्ह ते प्रेमु राम कें दूना ॥
translation: हे माता! सुंदर कृपा के धाम प्रभु भाई लक्ष्मणजी के सहित (शरीर से) कुशल हैं, परंतु आपके दुःख से दुःखी हैं। हे माता! मन में ग्लानि न मानिए (मन छोटा करके दुःख न कीजिए)। श्री रामचंद्रजी के हृदय में आपसे दूना प्रेम है ॥
english_translation: Mother, the Lord and Lakshman are well, but they grieve with your grief. Do not feel hurt in your heart; Ram loves you twice as much.
essence: Love stays alive even when separation makes it feel far away.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita that Ram and Lakshman are safe, share her sorrow, and love her deeply. He asks her not to feel diminished in her heart.
insight: It shifts the heart from self-blame and doubt toward reassurance in being remembered and loved.
modern_relevance: You finally get the text you were waiting for after a terrible week: 'We’re okay.' The message doesn’t erase the hurt, but it tells you the bond is still alive.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: रघुपति कर संदेसु अब सुनु जननी धरि धीर। अस कहि कपि गदगद भयउ भरे बिलोचन नीर ॥
translation: हे माता! अब धीरज धरकर श्री रघुनाथजी का संदेश सुनिए। ऐसा कहकर हनुमान् जी प्रेम से गद्गद हो गए। उनके नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया ॥
english_translation: O Mother, now listen with patience to the message of Raghupati. Saying this, the monkey became choked with emotion, and his eyes filled with tears.
essence: Devotion makes even a message feel sacred.
simple_meaning: Hanuman asks Sita to steady herself and listen to Ram's message. He is so moved by devotion that he cannot speak without tears.
insight: It shifts communication from mere words to presence, showing that sincerity can be felt before it is understood.
modern_relevance: You finally call the person who has been waiting for news, and your voice breaks before you even begin. Some messages matter so much that your emotion speaks first.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: कहेउ राम बियोग तव सीता। मो कहुँ सकल भए बिपरीता॥ नव तरु किसलय मनहुँ कृसानू। कालनिसा सम निसि ससि भानू ॥
translation: (हनुमान् जी बोले-) श्री रामचंद्रजी ने कहा है कि हे सीते! तुम्हारे वियोग में मेरे लिए सभी पदार्थ प्रतिकूल हो गए हैं। वृक्षों के नए-नए कोमल पत्ते मानो अग्नि के समान, रात्रि कालरात्रि के समान, चंद्रमा सूर्य के समान ॥
english_translation: Ram said that in separation from you, Sita, everything has become opposite for me. New tender leaves seem like fire, night feels like death-darkness, and the moon seems like the sun.
essence: Separation makes even beauty feel like fire.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Sita that her absence has changed his whole experience of the world. Things that once felt pleasant now feel harsh or wrong.
insight: It shows how longing reshapes perception, turning neutral things into either comfort or pain.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a breakup and every small thing feels altered — the music, the light, the air. This verse names that strange reordering of reality.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कुबलय बिपिन कुंत बन सरिसा। बारिद तपत तेल जनु बरिसा॥ जे हित रहे करत तेइ पीरा। उरग स्वास सम त्रिबिध समीरा ॥
translation: और कमलों के वन भालों के वन के समान हो गए हैं। मेघ मानो खौलता हुआ तेल बरसाते हैं। जो हित करने वाले थे, वे ही अब पीड़ा देने लगे हैं। त्रिविध (शीतल, मंद, सुगंध) वायु साँप के श्वास के समान (जहरीली और गरम) हो गई है ॥
english_translation: The lotus groves have become forests of spears. Clouds now pour down like boiling oil. What once gave comfort now brings pain. Even the breeze of three kinds feels like a snake’s breath.
essence: Love in separation can make comfort feel like pain.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita that everything around him now feels hostile and painful, even things that normally give comfort.
insight: It turns private longing into a shared language of pain, so Sita knows Ram’s love is alive in his absence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room that used to feel safe, but after one painful loss everything feels sharp, cold, and wrong. Grief can change the texture of the whole world.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: कहेहू तें कछु दुख घटि होई। काहि कहौं यह जान न कोई॥ तत्व प्रेम कर मम अरु तोरा। जानत प्रिया एकु मनु मोरा ॥
translation: मन का दुःख कह डालने से भी कुछ घट जाता है। पर कहूँ किससे? यह दुःख कोई जानता नहीं। हे प्रिये! मेरे और तेरे प्रेम का तत्त्व (रहस्य) एक मेरा मन ही जानता है ॥
english_translation: Speaking of it can lessen sorrow a little, but whom can I tell? No one knows this pain. O beloved, the secret of your love and mine is known only to my own mind.
essence: True love can be shared only by hearts that already know it.
simple_meaning: Speaking about sorrow can lessen it, but this love is too deep for anyone else to fully understand. Only the speaker's own mind knows its secret.
insight: It shifts you from demanding perfect understanding to trusting that honest speech can still soften pain.
modern_relevance: You try to explain a heartbreak over tea, and the other person nods but cannot really enter it. Still, naming it aloud can make the ache more bearable.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सो मनु सदा रहत तोहि पाहीं। जानु प्रीति रसु एतनेहि माहीं॥ प्रभु संदेसु सुनत बैदेही। मगन प्रेम तन सुधि नहिं तेही ॥
translation: और वह मन सदा तेरे ही पास रहता है। बस, मेरे प्रेम का सार इतने में ही समझ ले। प्रभु का संदेश सुनते ही जानकीजी प्रेम में मग्न हो गईं। उन्हें शरीर की सुध न रही ॥
english_translation: And my mind always remains with you. Understand the essence of love in this much alone. Hearing the Lord's message, Sita was lost in love; she forgot her body.
essence: True love keeps the mind near the beloved, even across separation.
simple_meaning: Sita says her mind is always with Ram, and hearing his message fills her with such love that she forgets her body.
insight: It shifts devotion from a feeling to a total mental presence that can overpower bodily awareness.
modern_relevance: You hear a voice note from someone you have been missing for weeks, and your whole chest softens. For a moment, your body is still there, but your attention belongs completely to them.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: कह कपि हृदयँ धीर धरु माता। सुमिरु राम सेवक सुखदाता॥ उर आनहु रघुपति प्रभुताई। सुनि मम बचन तजहु कदराई ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी ने कहा- हे माता! हृदय में धैर्य धारण करो और सेवकों को सुख देने वाले श्री रामजी का स्मरण करो। श्री रघुनाथजी की प्रभुता को हृदय में लाओ और मेरे वचन सुनकर कायरता छोड़ दो ॥
english_translation: Hanuman said: "Mother, keep courage in your heart. Remember Ram, the giver of joy to his servants. Hold the greatness of Raghupati in your heart, and hearing my words, let go of your fear."
essence: Remembering Ram gives you courage before the fear can rule.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita to stay brave, remember Ram, and let go of fear. Trust in Ram's greatness is what steadies the heart.
insight: It shifts the mind from fear-driven spiraling to trust anchored in remembrance.
modern_relevance: You are waiting for a difficult call, and your mind keeps inventing the worst outcome. Then one steady reminder arrives: breathe, remember what is larger than this moment, and the panic loses its grip.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: निसिचर निकर पतंग सम रघुपति बान कृसानु। जननी हृदयँ धीर धरु जरे निसाचर जानु ॥
translation: राक्षसों के समूह पतंगों के समान और श्री रघुनाथजी के बाण अग्नि के समान हैं। हे माता! हृदय में धैर्य धारण करो और राक्षसों को जला ही समझो ॥
english_translation: The demons are like moths, and Raghupati's arrows are fire. Mother, keep your heart steady and know the night-demons are already burned.
essence: What looks terrifying is already reduced to ash.
simple_meaning: Hanuman reassures Sita that Ravana's forces are helpless before Ram's power, and she should stay calm because their defeat is already certain.
insight: It shifts attention from the size of the threat to the certainty of divine protection.
modern_relevance: You are waiting for a test result, and your mind keeps replaying worst-case stories. This verse says the threat is not as powerful as it feels; steady yourself before the outcome arrives.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: जौं रघुबीर होति सुधि पाई। करते नहिं बिलंबु रघुराई॥ राम बान रबि उएँ जानकी। तम बरुथ कहँ जातुधान की ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी ने यदि खबर पाई होती तो वे बिलंब न करते। हे जानकीजी! रामबाण रूपी सूर्य के उदय होने पर राक्षसों की सेना रूपी अंधकार कहाँ रह सकता है? ॥
english_translation: If Raghuvir had received the news, Raghu Rai would not have delayed. Janaki, when the sun of Ram's arrow rises, how can the darkness of the demon host remain?
essence: Ram's arrival makes delay and darkness impossible.
simple_meaning: If Ram knew Sita's situation, he would not wait. Just as sunrise ends darkness, Ram's power destroys the demon army.
insight: It shifts the mind from helpless waiting to trust in the force of true support.
modern_relevance: You are waiting for a text that could change everything, and the silence feels endless. This verse speaks to the certainty that real help, once awakened, does not hesitate.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: अबहिं मातु मैं जाउँ लवाई। प्रभु आयुस नहिं राम दोहाई॥ कछुक दिवस जननी धरु धीरा। कपिन्ह सहित अइहहिं रघुबीरा ॥
translation: हे माता! मैं आपको अभी यहाँ से लिवा जाऊँ, पर श्री रामचंद्रजी की शपथ है, मुझे प्रभु (उन) की आज्ञा नहीं है। (अतः) हे माता! कुछ दिन और धीरज धरो। श्री रामचंद्रजी वानरों सहित यहाँ आएँगे ॥
english_translation: Mother, I would take you away right now, but I cannot do so without the Lord's command. So, mother, hold on with courage for a few more days. Lord Ram will come here with the monkeys.
essence: True courage can wait without losing hope.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita he cannot leave immediately because he must wait for Ram's order. He asks her to stay brave a little longer, promising that Ram will come with the monkeys.
insight: It teaches you to restrain impulse until action aligns with rightful authority or purpose.
modern_relevance: You want to send the message, make the move, fix it now — but the wiser step is to wait for the right signal. Courage sometimes means not rushing ahead.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: निसिचर मारि तोहि लै जैहहिं। तिहुँ पुर नारदादि जसु गैहहिं॥ हैं सुत कपि सब तुम्हहि समाना। जातुधान अति भट बलवाना ॥
translation: और राक्षसों को मारकर आपको ले जाएँगे। नारद आदि (ऋषि-मुनि) तीनों लोकों में उनका यश गाएँगे। (सीताजी ने कहा-) हे पुत्र! सब वानर तुम्हारे ही समान (नन्हें-नन्हें से) होंगे, राक्षस तो बड़े बलवान, योद्धा हैं ॥
english_translation: Killing the demons, they will take you back. Narada and others will sing their praise in the three worlds. "Son, all the monkeys are as small as you, while the demons are mighty warriors and very strong."
essence: Doubt sees only size and misses hidden strength.
simple_meaning: Sita says Hanuman would have to defeat the demons before taking her back, but she doubts the monkeys are strong enough for that fight.
insight: It shows how despair can shrink trust, even when rescue is near.
modern_relevance: You finally tell someone you can help, and they still look at your small frame and doubt you. Their fear is real, but it is not the whole story.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: मोरें हृदय परम संदेहा। सुनि कपि प्रगट कीन्हि निज देहा॥ कनक भूधराकार सरीरा। समर भयंकर अतिबल बीरा ॥
translation: अतः मेरे हृदय में बड़ा भारी संदेह होता है (कि तुम जैसे बंदर राक्षसों को कैसे जीतेंगे!)। यह सुनकर हनुमान् जी ने अपना शरीर प्रकट किया। सोने के पर्वत (सुमेरु) के आकार का (अत्यंत विशाल) शरीर था, जो युद्ध में शत्रुओं के हृदय में भय उत्पन्न करने वाला, अत्यंत बलवान् और वीर था ॥
english_translation: Then Sita said, "I have deep doubt in my heart." Hearing this, Hanuman revealed his true form. His body was like a golden mountain, terrifying in battle, immensely strong, and heroic.
essence: A hidden truth becomes believable when it is fully revealed.
simple_meaning: Sita doubts Hanuman at first, so he reveals his enormous, powerful form to reassure her.
insight: It shows that trust can be earned through clear, embodied evidence, not words alone.
modern_relevance: You explain yourself carefully, but the other person still hesitates. Then one honest act, one visible proof, changes everything.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सीता मन भरोस तब भयऊ। पुनि लघु रूप पवनसुत लयऊ ॥
translation: तब (उसे देखकर) सीताजी के मन में विश्वास हुआ। हनुमान् जी ने फिर छोटा रूप धारण कर लिया ॥
english_translation: Then Sita's mind was filled with trust. Hanuman again took on a small form.
essence: Trust grows when fear is answered by visible strength.
simple_meaning: Seeing Hanuman's true power, Sita's fear softens into trust, and Hanuman returns to a smaller form.
insight: It shifts the mind from doubt to confidence through direct experience, not argument.
modern_relevance: You meet someone in a moment of crisis, and they prove themselves by calmly doing what seemed impossible. Your suspicion drops, and the room feels safe again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनु माता साखामृग नहिं बल बुद्धि बिसाल। प्रभु प्रताप तें गरुड़हि खाइ परम लघु ब्याल ॥
translation: हे माता! सुनो, वानरों में बहुत बल-बुद्धि नहीं होती, परंतु प्रभु के प्रताप से बहुत छोटा सर्प भी गरुड़ को खा सकता है। (अत्यंत निर्बल भी महान् बलवान् को मार सकता है) ॥
english_translation: Listen, Mother: monkeys do not have great strength or intelligence, yet by the Lord's power even a tiny serpent can swallow Garuda.
essence: Smallness is no obstacle when the Lord's power is with you.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita that monkeys may seem weak, but the Lord's power can make even the smallest being overcome the greatest one.
insight: It shifts attention from personal capability to the source of strength behind action.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room feeling underqualified, while everyone else seems sharper, louder, and more prepared. Then one calm reminder changes everything: what matters most is not your size, but what power is working through you.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: मन संतोष सुनत कपि बानी। भगति प्रताप तेज बल सानी॥ आसिष दीन्हि राम प्रिय जाना। होहु तात बल सील निधाना ॥
translation: भक्ति, प्रताप, तेज और बल से सनी हुई हनुमान् जी की वाणी सुनकर सीताजी के मन में संतोष हुआ। उन्होंने श्री रामजी के प्रिय जानकर हनुमान् जी को आशीर्वाद दिया कि हे तात! तुम बल और शील के निधान होओ ॥
english_translation: Hearing Hanuman's speech filled with devotion, radiance, power, and strength, Sita felt reassured. Recognising him as dear to Ram, she blessed him: “O child, may you become a storehouse of strength and character.”
essence: Devotion that carries strength also brings comfort.
simple_meaning: Sita feels calm when she hears Hanuman's devoted, powerful speech. Seeing that he is dear to Ram, she blesses him to be full of strength and good character.
insight: It shows that spiritual strength becomes visible as calm, and that calm can awaken blessing in others.
modern_relevance: You hear someone speak with such sincerity that your shoulders drop. No performance, no agenda — just steady goodness. That kind of presence makes trust possible again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अजर अमर गुननिधि सुत होहू। करहुँ बहुत रघुनायक छोहू॥ करहुँ कृपा प्रभु अस सुनि काना। निर्भर प्रेम मगन हनुमाना ॥
translation: हे पुत्र! तुम अजर (बुढ़ापे से रहित), अमर और गुणों के खजाने होओ। श्री रघुनाथजी तुम पर बहुत कृपा करें। 'प्रभु कृपा करें' ऐसा कानों से सुनते ही हनुमान् जी पूर्ण प्रेम में मग्न हो गए ॥
