english_translation: “May you be unborn by decay, deathless, and a treasure-house of virtues. May Lord Raghunath show you great grace.” Hearing the words “the Lord will show grace,” Hanuman was lost in love.
essence: Ram's grace alone is enough to dissolve Hanuman into love.
simple_meaning: Sita blesses Hanuman with long life, virtue, and Ram's grace. The moment he hears that Ram's grace is being spoken of, he is filled completely with love.
insight: It shows how loving attention can move the mind from effort into pure absorption.
modern_relevance: You hear one line from someone you trust — “you’re still in their good graces” — and your chest loosens instantly. That is the kind of devotion this verse captures.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: बार बार नाएसि पद सीसा। बोला बचन जोरि कर कीसा॥ अब कृतकृत्य भयउँ मैं माता। आसिष तव अमोघ बिख्याता ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी ने बार-बार सीताजी के चरणों में सिर नवाया और फिर हाथ जोड़कर कहा- हे माता! अब मैं कृतार्थ हो गया। आपका आशीर्वाद अमोघ (अचूक) है, यह बात प्रसिद्ध है ॥
english_translation: Hanuman bowed again and again at Sita's feet, then spoke with folded hands: "Mother, I am now fulfilled. Your blessing is known to be unfailing."
essence: Bow without pride, and service itself becomes your fulfillment.
simple_meaning: Hanuman bows to Sita with deep respect and says he feels fulfilled by her blessing, which never fails.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeking recognition to feeling complete through selfless service.
modern_relevance: After helping someone through a crisis, you leave the room without needing praise, because the act itself already settled something inside you.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: सुनहु मातु मोहि अतिसय भूखा। लागि देखि सुंदर फल रूखा॥ सुनु सुत करहिं बिपिन रखवारी। परम सुभट रजनीचर भारी ॥
translation: हे माता! सुनो, सुंदर फल वाले वृक्षों को देखकर मुझे बड़ी ही भूख लग आई है। (सीताजी ने कहा-) हे बेटा! सुनो, बड़े भारी योद्धा राक्षस इस वन की रखवाली करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Listen, Mother: I am very hungry. Seeing these beautiful fruit trees has made me eager for them. Listen, my son: mighty night-watchers guard this grove.
essence: A simple excuse opens the door to a dangerous meeting.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita he is hungry after seeing the fruit trees, and Sita warns him that fierce night-guardians protect the grove.
insight: It shows how courage can wear the face of ordinary conversation, even under danger.
modern_relevance: You walk into a place where you do not belong, trying to stay calm while your stomach knots and every sound feels risky. Even then, you keep the conversation gentle.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: तिन्ह कर भय माता मोहि नाहीं। जौं तुम्ह सुख मानहु मन माहीं ॥
translation: (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे माता! यदि आप मन में सुख मानें (प्रसन्न होकर) आज्ञा दें तो मुझे उनका भय तो बिलकुल नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Mother, I have no fear of them. If you are pleased in your heart, then give me your blessing.
essence: Fear disappears when service is rooted in another's approval.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita that the guards do not frighten him. What matters most is whether she is pleased and gives permission.
insight: It shifts courage from self-confidence to faithful service and consent.
modern_relevance: You ask for permission before stepping in to help a friend in crisis. The room is tense, but what steadies you is not confidence in yourself — it is knowing they trust you.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: देखि बुद्धि बल निपुन कपि कहेउ जानकीं जाहु। रघुपति चरन हृदयँ धरि तात मधुर फल खाहु ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी को बुद्धि और बल में निपुण देखकर जानकीजी ने कहा- जाओ। हे तात! श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों को हृदय में धारण करके मीठे फल खाओ ॥
english_translation: Seeing the monkey's skill in intelligence and strength, Sita said, "Go. O dear one, keep Raghupati's feet in your heart and eat the sweet fruits."
essence: Remembrance of Ram turns even eating into bhakti.
simple_meaning: Sita sees Hanuman's skill and gives him permission to eat the fruit, asking him to keep Ram in his heart while doing so.
insight: It shifts action from appetite alone to action guided by devotion and inner recollection.
modern_relevance: You open a snack after a brutal day, but your mind is still racing. This verse says even ordinary relief can begin with remembrance, not distraction.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: चलेउ नाइ सिरु पैठेउ बागा। फल खाएसि तरु तोरैं लागा॥ रहे तहाँ बहु भट रखवारे। कछु मारेसि कछु जाइ पुकारे ॥
translation: वे सीताजी को सिर नवाकर चले और बाग में घुस गए। फल खाए और वृक्षों को तोड़ने लगे। वहाँ बहुत से योद्धा रखवाले थे। उनमें से कुछ को मार डाला और कुछ ने जाकर रावण से पुकार की- ॥
english_translation: He bowed his head and entered the grove. He ate the fruit and began uprooting the trees. Many guards were stationed there. He killed some, and some ran to report it.
essence: Fearless service can look disruptive to those guarding power.
simple_meaning: Hanuman enters the grove, eats the fruit, uproots the trees, and fights the guards who try to stop him.
insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to fearless action when the moment demands it.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone expects you to stay small, but your purpose is bigger than their discomfort. You do the work anyway.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ एक आवा कपि भारी। तेहिं असोक बाटिका उजारी॥ खाएसि फल अरु बिटप उपारे। रच्छक मर्दि मर्दि महि डारे ॥
translation: (और कहा-) हे नाथ! एक बड़ा भारी बंदर आया है। उसने अशोक वाटिका उजाड़ डाली। फल खाए, वृक्षों को उखाड़ डाला और रखवालों को मसल-मसलकर जमीन पर डाल दिया ॥
english_translation: “Lord, a huge monkey has come. He has ruined the Ashoka grove, eaten the fruit, uprooted the trees, and crushed the guards to the ground.”
essence: The search has turned into force.
simple_meaning: A guard reports that Hanuman has torn through the Ashoka grove, eaten the fruit, uprooted trees, and beaten the guards down.
insight: It sets up the next clash by showing that Hanuman is no longer hiding or waiting.
modern_relevance: A colleague bursts into the room saying the quiet plan has already collapsed, and the person everyone underestimated has changed everything.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुनि रावन पठए भट नाना। तिन्हहि देखि गर्जेउ हनुमाना॥ सब रजनीचर कपि संघारे। गए पुकारत कछु अधमारे ॥
translation: यह सुनकर रावण ने बहुत से योद्धा भेजे। उन्हें देखकर हनुमान् जी ने गर्जना की। हनुमान् जी ने सब राक्षसों को मार डाला, कुछ जो अधमरे थे, चिल्लाते हुए गए ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Ravana sent many warriors. Seeing them, Hanuman roared. He killed all the night-walkers; some half-dead ran away crying.
essence: Force without steadiness only creates more defeat.
simple_meaning: Ravana sends more fighters, but Hanuman meets them with fierce force and defeats them all.
insight: It shows that fear-fed resistance can be broken by unflinching strength.
modern_relevance: A group chat turns hostile, and you realize the first sharp reply only invites more noise. Sometimes the strongest response is simply not to be shaken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि पठयउ तेहिं अच्छकुमारा। चला संग लै सुभट अपारा॥ आवत देखि बिटप गहि तर्जा। ताहि निपाति महाधुनि गर्जा ॥
translation: फिर रावण ने अक्षयकुमार को भेजा। वह असंख्य श्रेष्ठ योद्धाओं को साथ लेकर चला। उसे आते देखकर हनुमान् जी ने एक वृक्ष (हाथ में) लेकर ललकारा और उसे मारकर महाध्वनि (बड़े जोर) से गर्जना की ॥
english_translation: Ravana sent Akshayakumar again. He came with countless elite warriors. Seeing him approach, Hanuman seized a tree and challenged him, then struck him down and roared with a thunderous cry.
essence: Fear collapses when you meet force with fearless presence.
simple_meaning: Ravana sends another commander with a huge force. Hanuman grabs a tree, confronts him, kills him, and roars in victory.
insight: It shows that fear is broken by direct, fearless response, not by retreat.
modern_relevance: A problem keeps escalating in your inbox, and then a manager forwards it to someone even tougher. You stop shrinking, face it directly, and the pressure changes.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कछु मारेसि कछु मर्देसि कछु मिलएसि धरि धूरि। कछु पुनि जाइ पुकारे प्रभु मर्कट बल भूरि ॥
translation: उन्होंने सेना में से कुछ को मार डाला और कुछ को मसल डाला और कुछ को पकड़-पकड़कर धूल में मिला दिया। कुछ ने फिर जाकर पुकार की कि हे प्रभु! बंदर बहुत ही बलवान् है ॥
english_translation: He killed some, crushed some, and flung some into the dust. Some ran back crying, “My lord, that monkey is immensely strong!”
essence: Panic spreads when resistance meets unstoppable force.
simple_meaning: Hanuman overwhelms Ravana’s soldiers so completely that the survivors flee and report his immense strength.
insight: It advances the battle by showing that Hanuman’s force has broken the enemy’s confidence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि सुत बध लंकेस रिसाना। पठएसि मेघनाद बलवाना॥ मारसि जनि सुत बाँधेसु ताही। देखिअ कपिहि कहाँ कर आही ॥
translation: पुत्र का वध सुनकर रावण क्रोधित हो उठा और उसने (अपने जेठे पुत्र) बलवान् मेघनाद को भेजा। (उससे कहा कि-) हे पुत्र! मारना नहीं उसे बाँध लाना। उस बंदर को देखा जाए कि कहाँ का है ॥
english_translation: Hearing of his son’s death, Ravana burned with rage and sent the mighty Meghnad. “Do not kill him; bind him and bring him. Let us see what kind of monkey this is.”
essence: Pride does not seek understanding; it seeks to seize and punish.
simple_meaning: Ravana hears that his son has been killed, grows furious, and sends Meghnad with orders to capture Hanuman alive.
insight: It shows how wounded pride turns into a demand to dominate rather than to discern.
modern_relevance: You get the message that someone has crossed a line, and your first impulse is not clarity but retaliation. The mind wants to strike back before it understands.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चला इंद्रजित अतुलित जोधा। बंधु निधन सुनि उपजा क्रोधा॥ कपि देखा दारुन भट आवा। कटकटाइ गर्जा अरु धावा ॥
translation: इंद्र को जीतने वाला अतुलनीय योद्धा मेघनाद चला। भाई का मारा जाना सुन उसे क्रोध हो आया। हनुमान् जी ने देखा कि अबकी भयानक योद्धा आया है। तब वे कटकटाकर गर्जे और दौड़े ॥
english_translation: The incomparable warrior Indrajit advanced. Hearing of his brother's death, anger arose in him. Hanuman saw that a terrible fighter had arrived, and he roared and charged.
essence: Fury meets fearless force on the battlefield.
simple_meaning: Indrajit comes forward in anger after hearing his brother was killed, and Hanuman meets him with a fierce roar and charge.
insight: It keeps the focus on action under pressure, not inner debate.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room after hearing bad news, jaw set and heart hot. Someone else meets that heat without flinching.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अति बिसाल तरु एक उपारा। बिरथ कीन्ह लंकेस कुमारा॥ रहे महाभट ताके संगा। गहि गहि कपि मर्दई निज अंगा ॥
translation: उन्होंने एक बहुत बड़ा वृक्ष उखाड़ लिया और (उसके प्रहार से) लंकेश्वर रावण के पुत्र मेघनाद को बिना रथ का कर दिया। (रथ को तोड़कर उसे नीचे पटक दिया)। उसके साथ जो बड़े-बड़े योद्धा थे, उनको पकड़-पकड़कर हनुमान् जी अपने शरीर से मसलने लगे ॥
english_translation: He uprooted a huge tree and struck Ravana's son, leaving him without a chariot. Then he grabbed the great warriors with him and crushed them against his own body.
essence: Force meets force in a single, unstoppable burst.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tears up a tree, destroys Meghnad's chariot, and overpowers the warriors around him with sheer force.
insight: It shifts attention from strategy to decisive action under pressure.
modern_relevance: A crisis hits fast: the phone rings, the plan collapses, and you stop overthinking and do the one hard thing in front of you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तिन्हहि निपाति ताहि सन बाजा। भिरे जुगल मानहुँ गजराजा॥ मुठिका मारि चढ़ा तरु जाई। ताहि एक छन मुरुछा आई ॥
translation: उन सबको मारकर फिर मेघनाद से लड़ने लगे। (लड़ते हुए वे ऐसे मालूम होते थे) मानो दो गजराज (श्रेष्ठ हाथी) भिड़ गए हों। हनुमान् जी उसे एक घूँसा मारकर वृक्ष पर जा चढ़े। उसको क्षणभर के लिए मूर्च्छा आ गई ॥
english_translation: After defeating them all, he fought with Meghnad again. The two clashed like mighty elephants. Hanuman struck him with a fist, leapt back up into a tree, and Meghnad fell unconscious for a moment.
essence: The fight keeps moving, and Hanuman keeps answering.
simple_meaning: Hanuman defeats Meghnad's men, fights Meghnad like two powerful elephants, lands a fist, and briefly knocks him unconscious.
insight: It shows relentless action under pressure, not reflection or doctrine.
modern_relevance: You’re in the middle of a heated argument and the other person comes back harder than before. You don’t need a grand speech — just enough steadiness to stay standing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उठि बहोरि कीन्हिसि बहु माया। जीति न जाइ प्रभंजन जाया ॥
translation: फिर उठकर उसने बहुत माया रची, परंतु पवन के पुत्र उससे जीते नहीं जाते ॥
english_translation: Rising again, he cast many illusions, but the son of the wind could not be defeated.
essence: Repeated tricks cannot defeat steady courage.
simple_meaning: Ravana's side uses more tricks, but Hanuman still cannot be overcome.
insight: It shows that endurance and clarity can outlast even repeated deception.
modern_relevance: A room full of polished lies can still fail against someone who stays clear and steady. The pressure rises, the tricks multiply, but you do not have to be shaken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ब्रह्म अस्त्र तेहि साँधा कपि मन कीन्ह बिचार। जौं न ब्रह्मसर मानउँ महिमा मिटइ अपार ॥
translation: अंत में उसने ब्रह्मास्त्र का संधान (प्रयोग) किया, तब हनुमान् जी ने मन में विचार किया कि यदि ब्रह्मास्त्र को नहीं मानता हूँ तो उसकी अपार महिमा मिट जाएगी ॥
english_translation: Hanuman then thought: if I do not respect the Brahmastra, its great power will be diminished.
essence: True strength can honour force without losing itself.
simple_meaning: Hanuman sees the Brahmastra coming and decides to honor it, because refusing it would diminish its immense power.
insight: It teaches you to recognize legitimate power without letting ego turn resistance into self-defeat.
modern_relevance: You are in a heated argument and could bulldoze ahead, but you stop and acknowledge the other person's point. That pause keeps your strength from becoming arrogance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ब्रह्मबान कपि कहुँ तेहिं मारा। परतिहुँ बार कटकु संघारा॥ तेहिं देखा कपि मुरुछित भयऊ। नागपास बाँधेसि लै गयऊ ॥
translation: उसने हनुमान् जी को ब्रह्मबाण मारा, (जिसके लगते ही वे वृक्ष से नीचे गिर पड़े), परंतु गिरते समय भी उन्होंने बहुत सी सेना मार डाली। जब उसने देखा कि हनुमान् जी मूर्छित हो गए हैं, तब वह उनको नागपाश से बाँधकर ले गया ॥
english_translation: He struck Hanuman with a Brahma weapon; even as he fell, he destroyed many troops. When he saw Hanuman unconscious, he bound him with the serpent noose and carried him away.
essence: Even when struck down, true resolve keeps fighting.
simple_meaning: Hanuman is struck down, yet even in falling he keeps destroying the enemy. Then the enemy binds him with a serpent noose and takes him away.
insight: It shows that steadfast effort can continue even under collapse, before the body or plan finally yields.
modern_relevance: A project collapses after weeks of effort, yet your work still leaves a mark before it ends. Sometimes the final fall does not cancel the force of what you gave.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जासु नाम जपि सुनहु भवानी। भव बंधन काटहिं नर ग्यानी॥ तासु दूत कि बंध तरु आवा। प्रभु कारज लगि कपिहिं बँधावा ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे भवानी सुनो, जिनका नाम जपकर ज्ञानी (विवेकी) मनुष्य संसार (जन्म-मरण) के बंधन को काट डालते हैं, उनका दूत कहीं बंधन में आ सकता है? किंतु प्रभु के कार्य के लिए हनुमान् जी ने स्वयं अपने को बँधा लिया ॥
english_translation: O Bhavani, listen: by chanting whose name wise people cut through the bonds of worldly becoming, could that being's messenger ever be bound? Yet for the Lord's work, Hanuman allowed himself to be bound.
essence: True devotion can turn even bondage into service.
simple_meaning: Ram's name frees wise people from bondage, so his messenger cannot truly be bound. Hanuman was bound only because he chose to serve Ram's work.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing surrender as weakness to seeing it as chosen service.
modern_relevance: You take the blame in a meeting to protect someone else. It looks like defeat from the outside, but you know exactly why you stayed quiet.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: कपि बंधन सुनि निसिचर धाए। कौतुक लागि सभाँ सब आए॥ दसमुख सभा दीखि कपि जाई। कहि न जाइ कछु अति प्रभुताई ॥
translation: बंदर का बाँधा जाना सुनकर राक्षस दौड़े और कौतुक के लिए (तमाशा देखने के लिए) सब सभा में आए। हनुमान् जी ने जाकर रावण की सभा देखी। उसकी अत्यंत प्रभुता (ऐश्वर्य) कुछ कही नहीं जाती ॥
english_translation: Hearing that the monkey had been bound, the demons rushed out and came to the assembly for a spectacle. Hanuman then went and saw Ravana's court; its immense splendor cannot be fully described.
essence: Power can fill a room and still fail to shake the fearless.
simple_meaning: The demons hurry to see the bound Hanuman, and Hanuman is brought before Ravana's magnificent court.
insight: It sets up the contrast between Ravana's outward grandeur and Hanuman's unshaken presence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a boardroom where everyone already knows your name, and the room is built to intimidate. The size of the place is real, but so is your steadiness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कर जोरें सुर दिसिप बिनीता। भृकुटि बिलोकत सकल सभीता॥ देखि प्रताप न कपि मन संका। जिमि अहिगन महुँ गरुड़ असंका ॥
translation: देवता और दिक्पाल हाथ जोड़े बड़ी नम्रता के साथ भयभीत हुए सब रावण की भौं ताक रहे हैं। (उसका रुख देख रहे हैं) उसका ऐसा प्रताप देखकर भी हनुमान् जी के मन में जरा भी डर नहीं हुआ। वे ऐसे निःशंख खड़े रहे, जैसे सर्पों के समूह में गरुड़ निःशंख निर्भय) रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: The radiant beings and guardians of the directions folded their hands in fear, watching his stern brow. Yet Hanuman felt no fear at all; he stood unshaken, like Garuda among a mass of serpents.
essence: Fear loses its grip when your purpose is steady.
simple_meaning: Even the celestial beings fear Ravana, but Hanuman does not. His courage stays steady in the middle of danger.
insight: It teaches you to stay steady when power tries to make you smaller.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is intimidated by the loudest person there. Your chest tightens, but you keep your footing and speak clearly anyway.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कपिहि बिलोकि दसानन बिहसा कहि दुर्बाद। सुत बध सुरति कीन्हि पुनि उपजा हृदयँ बिसाद ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी को देखकर रावण दुर्वचन कहता हुआ खूब हँसा। फिर पुत्र वध का स्मरण किया तो उसके हृदय में विषाद उत्पन्न हो गया ॥
english_translation: Seeing Hanuman, Ravana laughed hard and spoke abusive words. Then he remembered his son's death, and sorrow rose in his heart.
essence: Mockery can hide grief for only a moment.
simple_meaning: Ravana first mocks Hanuman, then remembers his dead son and feels sudden sorrow.
insight: It shows how quickly ego can turn from mockery to wounded sorrow.
modern_relevance: You snap at someone in public, then one private memory undoes you. The mask of strength drops the moment grief returns.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह लंकेस कवन तैं कीसा। केहि कें बल घालेहि बन खीसा॥ की धौं श्रवन सुनेहि नहिं मोही। देखउँ अति असंक सठ तोही ॥
translation: लंकापति रावण ने कहा- रे वानर! तू कौन है? किसके बल पर तूने वन को उजाड़कर नष्ट कर डाला? क्या तूने कभी मुझे (मेरा नाम और यश) कानों से नहीं सुना? रे शठ! मैं तुझे अत्यंत निःशंख देख रहा हूँ ॥
english_translation: Lankesh Ravana said, “O monkey, who are you? By whose power have you ruined the forest? Have you never heard of me? I see you utterly fearless, fool.”
essence: Arrogance questions what fearless devotion already knows.
simple_meaning: Ravana confronts Hanuman with arrogance, demanding to know who he is and by what power he has acted so boldly.
insight: It shows how ego reacts when it meets courage it cannot control.
modern_relevance: A powerful manager leans back and asks, "Who do you think you are?" when you calmly challenge a bad decision. That question often reveals more insecurity than strength.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: मारे निसिचर केहिं अपराधा। कहु सठ तोहि न प्रान कइ बाधा॥ सुनु रावन ब्रह्मांड निकाया। पाइ जासु बल बिरचति माया ॥
translation: तूने किस अपराध से राक्षसों को मारा? रे मूर्ख! बता, क्या तुझे प्राण जाने का भय नहीं है? (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे रावण! सुन, जिनका बल पाकर माया संपूर्ण ब्रह्मांडों के समूहों की रचना करती है, ॥
english_translation: For what offense did you kill the demons? Tell me, fool—do you not fear for your life? Listen, Ravana: by whose power the countless worlds of the universe are formed through maya.
essence: Real fear disappears when your strength comes from beyond yourself.
simple_meaning: Hanuman answers Ravana's taunt by saying that true power belongs to the one whose strength creates the universe itself. Ravana's threats are small beside that.
insight: It shifts courage away from personal bravado to trust in a power greater than threats.
modern_relevance: A hostile manager corners you in front of the team and tries to make you flinch. Hanuman's answer reminds you that real strength does not come from intimidation, but from what you stand on.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: जाकें बल बिरंचि हरि ईसा। पालत सृजत हरत दससीसा॥ जा बल सीस धरत सहसानन। अंडकोस समेत गिरि कानन ॥
translation: जिनके बल से हे दशशीश! ब्रह्मा, विष्णु, महेश (क्रमशः) सृष्टि का सृजन, पालन और संहार करते हैं, जिनके बल से सहस्रमुख (फणों) वाले शेषजी पर्वत और वनसहित समस्त ब्रह्मांड को सिर पर धारण करते हैं, ॥
english_translation: By whose power, O ten-headed one, Brahma creates, Vishnu preserves, and Shiva destroys. By whose power, Shesha with a thousand hoods holds the entire universe, including mountains and forests, upon his head.
essence: All power belongs to Ram, not to the proud who borrow it.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Ravana that the supreme power behind creation, preservation, and destruction is not Ravana's strength, but Ram's.
insight: It shifts attention from visible authority to the source that makes authority possible.
modern_relevance: A powerful executive storms into the room, expecting everyone to shrink. One calm person doesn't flinch because they know status is borrowed, not owned.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: धरइ जो बिबिध देह सुरत्राता। तुम्ह से सठन्ह सिखावनु दाता॥ हर कोदंड कठिन जेहिं भंजा। तेहि समेत नृप दल मद गंजा ॥
translation: जो देवताओं की रक्षा के लिए नाना प्रकार की देह धारण करते हैं और जो तुम्हारे जैसे मूर्खों को शिक्षा देने वाले हैं, जिन्होंने शिवजी के कठोर धनुष को तोड़ डाला और उसी के साथ राजाओं के समूह का गर्व चूर्ण कर दिया ॥
english_translation: The one who protects the radiant beings takes many forms, teaches fools like you, broke Shiva’s hard bow, and crushed the pride of kings.
essence: Ram’s greatness is proven by both compassion and irresistible power.
simple_meaning: Ram is the protector of the devas, the teacher of the foolish, the breaker of Shiva’s bow, and the destroyer of royal pride.
insight: It shifts reverence from brute strength to the power that protects, teaches, and restores right order.
modern_relevance: A room full of powerful people can still go silent when one person speaks with unshakable clarity. The right presence does not just impress — it exposes arrogance and resets the room.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: खर दूषन त्रिसिरा अरु बाली। बधे सकल अतुलित बलसाली ॥
translation: जिन्होंने खर, दूषण, त्रिशिरा और बालि को मार डाला, जो सब के सब अतुलनीय बलवान् थे, ॥
english_translation: He killed Khara, Dushana, Trisira, and Bali, all of them immeasurably powerful.
essence: Even the strongest foes fall before Ram's power.
simple_meaning: Ram's power is shown through the defeat of four mighty enemies.
insight: It shifts attention from raw force to the source of force behind it.
modern_relevance: Someone dismisses you because you look alone or outnumbered. Then they remember the one time you handled a problem everyone else feared. Reputation changes the room before you speak.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जाके बल लवलेस तें जितेहु चराचर झारि। तास दूत मैं जा करि हरि आनेहु प्रिय नारि ॥
translation: जिनके लेशमात्र बल से तुमने समस्त चराचर जगत् को जीत लिया और जिनकी प्रिय पत्नी को तुम (चोरी से) हर लाए हो, मैं उन्हीं का दूत हूँ ॥
english_translation: I am the messenger of the one whose mere slightest power you have conquered the entire moving and unmoving world, and whose beloved wife you have carried away.
essence: Even the smallest trace of Ram's power makes conquest meaningless.
simple_meaning: Hanuman identifies himself as the messenger of Ram, whose tiny fraction of power has already defeated the entire world. Ravana is being warned that this is no ordinary envoy.
insight: It shifts attention from surface appearance to the source of authority behind an action or message.
modern_relevance: You dismiss the quiet person in the room, not noticing they speak for someone far stronger than they look. The mistake is never about the messenger alone.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: जानउँ मैं तुम्हारि प्रभुताई। सहसबाहु सन परी लराई॥ समर बालि सन करि जसु पावा। सुनि कपि बचन बिहसि बिहरावा ॥
translation: मैं तुम्हारी प्रभुता को खूब जानता हूँ सहस्रबाहु से तुम्हारी लड़ाई हुई थी और बालि से युद्ध करके तुमने यश प्राप्त किया था। हनुमान् जी के (मार्मिक) वचन सुनकर रावण ने हँसकर बात टाल दी ॥
english_translation: I know your power well. You fought Sahasrabahu and won fame by battling Bali. Hearing the monkey's words, Ravana laughed and brushed them aside.
essence: Knowing the truth means nothing if pride refuses to bow.
simple_meaning: Ravana admits Hanuman knows Ram's strength, but he laughs it off and refuses to take the warning seriously.
insight: It shows how ego turns clear warning into entertainment instead of action.
modern_relevance: Someone warns you plainly that your shortcut will backfire, and you smile because you think you're untouchable. Ravana is that moment before the fall.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: खायउँ फल प्रभु लागी भूँखा। कपि सुभाव तें तोरेउँ रूखा॥ सब कें देह परम प्रिय स्वामी। मारहिं मोहि कुमारग गामी ॥
translation: हे (राक्षसों के) स्वामी मुझे भूख लगी थी, (इसलिए) मैंने फल खाए और वानर स्वभाव के कारण वृक्ष तोड़े। हे (निशाचरों के) मालिक! देह सबको परम प्रिय है। कुमार्ग पर चलने वाले (दुष्ट) राक्षस जब मुझे मारने लगे॥2
english_translation: I ate fruit because I was hungry, Lord, and I broke trees by my monkey nature. Dear master of the night-roamers, everyone loves their own body; when the ones who walk the wrong path began to strike me...
essence: You can speak plainly without losing your calm.
simple_meaning: Hanuman explains that he ate fruit because he was hungry and broke trees because of his monkey nature. He reminds the listener that every being loves its own body, even when acting harshly.
insight: It teaches you to answer accusation with clarity, not defensiveness, and to recognise how self-protection drives harsh behaviour.
modern_relevance: You get snapped at in a tense meeting after speaking bluntly. Instead of escalating, you can name what happened plainly, without ego, and see the fear underneath the reaction.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: जिन्ह मोहि मारा ते मैं मारे। तेहि पर बाँधेउँ तनयँ तुम्हारे॥ मोहि न कछु बाँधे कइ लाजा। कीन्ह चहउँ निज प्रभु कर काजा ॥
translation: तब जिन्होंने मुझे मारा, उनको मैंने भी मारा। उस पर तुम्हारे पुत्र ने मुझको बाँध लिया (किंतु), मुझे अपने बाँधे जाने की कुछ भी लज्जा नहीं है। मैं तो अपने प्रभु का कार्य करना चाहता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Those who struck me, I struck back. Then your son bound me, but I feel no shame in being bound. I only wanted to do my Lord's work.
essence: Service makes even humiliation feel small.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says he fought back when attacked, was then bound by Ravan's son, and felt no shame because he only wanted to serve Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from protecting your image to serving your calling.
modern_relevance: You get blamed in a meeting for something you did not start, and your first impulse is to defend your ego. This verse reminds you that dignity can stay intact when your purpose is bigger than embarrassment.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: बिनती करउँ जोरि कर रावन। सुनहु मान तजि मोर सिखावन॥ देखहु तुम्ह निज कुलहि बिचारी। भ्रम तजि भजहु भगत भय हारी ॥
translation: हे रावण! मैं हाथ जोड़कर तुमसे विनती करता हूँ, तुम अभिमान छोड़कर मेरी सीख सुनो। तुम अपने पवित्र कुल का विचार करके देखो और भ्रम को छोड़कर भक्त भयहारी भगवान् को भजो ॥
english_translation: I beg you with folded hands, Ravana. Listen to my teaching and drop your pride. Look at your own noble lineage, cast off confusion, and worship the one who removes fear from devotees.
essence: Pride blinds you to the very refuge that can free you.
simple_meaning: Hanuman asks Ravana to stop being arrogant, think about his lineage, clear his confusion, and turn toward Ram, who frees devotees from fear.
insight: It teaches you to speak truth plainly to ego, and to choose clear seeing over self-protection.
modern_relevance: You're arguing with someone who refuses every warning, even as their choices keep hurting them. Sometimes the kindest thing is to name the pride underneath the mess.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: जाकें डर अति काल डेराई। जो सुर असुर चराचर खाई॥ तासों बयरु कबहुँ नहिं कीजै। मोरे कहें जानकी दीजै ॥
translation: जो देवता, राक्षस और समस्त चराचर को खा जाता है, वह काल भी जिनके डर से अत्यंत डरता है, उनसे कदापि वैर न करो और मेरे कहने से जानकीजी को दे दो ॥
english_translation: Do not make enmity with the one whom even Time fears deeply, who devours gods, demons, and all moving and unmoving beings. In my words, give Sita back.
essence: Even the strongest pride must yield before the one Time fears.
simple_meaning: Hanuman warns Ravana not to oppose Ram, whose power exceeds even Time itself, and tells him to return Sita.
insight: It shifts you from prideful resistance to clear-eyed surrender before damage deepens.
modern_relevance: You keep arguing with a situation that has already outgrown your control. A wiser voice says: stop the fight, face reality, and return what should never have been taken.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: प्रनतपाल रघुनायक करुना सिंधु खरारि। गएँ सरन प्रभु राखिहैं तव अपराध बिसारि ॥
translation: खर के शत्रु श्री रघुनाथजी शरणागतों के रक्षक और दया के समुद्र हैं। शरण जाने पर प्रभु तुम्हारा अपराध भुलाकर तुम्हें अपनी शरण में रख लेंगे ॥
english_translation: Raghu's lord is the protector of those who seek refuge, an ocean of compassion. If you surrender, the Lord will forget your wrongdoing and keep you in his shelter.
essence: Surrender to Ram, and even your past can be released.
simple_meaning: Ram protects anyone who comes to him in surrender. He does not cling to your past mistakes; he receives you fully.
insight: It shifts you from self-protection to surrender, trusting that honest return matters more than past error.
modern_relevance: You finally admit you were wrong in a message you’ve delayed for days. The fear says you’ve ruined everything; this verse says a sincere return can still be received.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: राम चरन पंकज उर धरहू। लंका अचल राजु तुम्ह करहू॥ रिषि पुलस्ति जसु बिमल मयंका। तेहि ससि महुँ जनि होहु कलंका ॥
translation: तुम श्री रामजी के चरण कमलों को हृदय में धारण करो और लंका का अचल राज्य करो। ऋषि पुलस्त्यजी का यश निर्मल चंद्रमा के समान है। उस चंद्रमा में तुम कलंक न बनो ॥
english_translation: Keep Ram's lotus feet in your heart, and rule Lanka firmly. Sage Pulastya's fame is like a spotless moon; do not become a stain upon that moon.
essence: Power remains noble only when it bows to Ram.
simple_meaning: Ravana is told to keep Ram in his heart, rule Lanka steadily, and never stain the pure fame of his lineage.
insight: It shifts ambition from self-display to reverence and restraint.
modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, but everyone is watching how you use it. Power feels bigger when it stays humble, and smaller when ego starts writing the script.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: राम नाम बिनु गिरा न सोहा। देखु बिचारि त्यागि मद मोहा॥ बसन हीन नहिं सोह सुरारी। सब भूषन भूषित बर नारी ॥
translation: राम नाम के बिना वाणी शोभा नहीं पाती, मद-मोह को छोड़, विचारकर देखो। हे देवताओं के शत्रु! सब गहनों से सजी हुई सुंदरी स्त्री भी कपड़ों के बिना (नंगी) शोभा नहीं पाती ॥
english_translation: Without Ram's name, speech has no beauty. See clearly, and let go of pride and delusion. A woman without clothes is not graceful, even if she is adorned with every ornament.
essence: Speech only becomes graceful when pride gives way to Ram's name.
simple_meaning: Speech becomes truly beautiful only when it carries Ram's name. Pride and delusion strip away real grace, no matter how polished things look on the outside.
insight: It shifts attention from performance to the quality of heart behind speech.
modern_relevance: You can sound polished in a meeting, but if your words are inflated by ego, people feel it immediately. The same sentence lands differently when it comes from humility and devotion.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: राम बिमुख संपति प्रभुताई। जाइ रही पाई बिनु पाई॥ सजल मूल जिन्ह सरितन्ह नाहीं। बरषि गएँ पुनि तबहिं सुखाहीं ॥
translation: रामविमुख पुरुष की संपत्ति और प्रभुता रही हुई भी चली जाती है और उसका पाना न पाने के समान है। जिन नदियों के मूल में कोई जलस्रोत नहीं है। (अर्थात् जिन्हें केवल बरसात ही आसरा है) वे वर्षा बीत जाने पर फिर तुरंत ही सूख जाती हैं ॥
english_translation: A person turned away from Ram may keep wealth and power for a while, but they slip away. Like rivers with no source, they dry up as soon as the rains end.
essence: What is cut off from Ram cannot endure, no matter how grand it looks.
simple_meaning: Wealth and authority do not truly stay with someone who turns away from Ram. They may seem present, but they fade quickly like rivers that have no real source.
insight: It shifts attention from holding status to finding what actually sustains it.
modern_relevance: You finally get the title, the money, the praise — and still feel one bad week away from losing it all. Anything built without a deeper center can disappear overnight.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सुनु दसकंठ कहउँ पन रोपी। बिमुख राम त्राता नहिं कोपी॥ संकर सहस बिष्नु अज तोही। सकहिं न राखि राम कर द्रोही ॥
translation: हे रावण! सुनो, मैं प्रतिज्ञा करके कहता हूँ कि रामविमुख की रक्षा करने वाला कोई भी नहीं है। हजारों शंकर, विष्णु और ब्रह्मा भी श्री रामजी के साथ द्रोह करने वाले तुमको नहीं बचा सकते ॥
english_translation: O ten-headed one, listen: I swear that no protector can save one who turns away from Ram. Even thousands of Shankar, Vishnu, and Brahma cannot save you if you oppose Ram.
essence: Opposing Ram leaves you beyond every other shelter.
simple_meaning: Hanuman warns Ravana that anyone who turns away from Ram loses all protection. Even the greatest forces cannot save someone who opposes Ram.
insight: It shifts the mind from relying on external protection to aligning with what is right.
modern_relevance: You keep doubling down on a choice that is clearly breaking trust, then hope status or connections will cover it. This verse says they won't.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: मोहमूल बहु सूल प्रद त्यागहु तम अभिमान। भजहु राम रघुनायक कृपा सिंधु भगवान ॥
translation: मोह ही जिनका मूल है ऐसे (अज्ञानजनित), बहुत पीड़ा देने वाले, तमरूप अभिमान का त्याग कर दो और रघुकुल के स्वामी, कृपा के समुद्र भगवान् श्री रामचंद्रजी का भजन करो ॥
english_translation: Give up the dark pride born of delusion, which brings many pains. Worship Ram, the lord of Raghu, the ocean of grace.
essence: Pride rooted in confusion only hurts; devotion to Ram heals it.
simple_meaning: Pride born from confusion only brings suffering. Let it go and turn toward Ram with devotion.
insight: It shifts you from self-protection to humble remembrance of Ram.
modern_relevance: You replay a harsh text message for hours, building a story around being disrespected. That tightening in the chest is pride doing its work; the release begins when you stop feeding it.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: जदपि कही कपि अति हित बानी। भगति बिबेक बिरति नय सानी॥ बोला बिहसि महा अभिमानी। मिला हमहि कपि गुर बड़ ग्यानी ॥
translation: यद्यपि हनुमान् जी ने भक्ति, ज्ञान, वैराग्य और नीति से सनी हुई बहुत ही हित की वाणी कही, तो भी वह महान् अभिमानी रावण बहुत हँसकर (व्यंग्य से) बोला कि हमें यह बंदर बड़ा ज्ञानी गुरु मिला! ॥
english_translation: Although Hanuman spoke words of great benefit, filled with devotion, discernment, detachment, and wise conduct, the great arrogant Ravana laughed and said, 'We have met a monkey guru, a great scholar!'
essence: Arrogance hears wisdom as an insult and misses its own rescue.
simple_meaning: Hanuman gives Ravana a wise, helpful warning, but Ravana laughs it off because his ego cannot receive advice.
insight: It shows how ego filters out correction, turning counsel into comedy before it can do any work.
modern_relevance: You finally tell a friend the hard truth they asked for, and they smirk like you’re the problem. That moment is Ravana’s blindness in modern clothes.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: मृत्यु निकट आई खल तोही। लागेसि अधम सिखावन मोही॥ उलटा होइहि कह हनुमाना। मतिभ्रम तोर प्रगट मैं जाना ॥
translation: रे दुष्ट! तेरी मृत्यु निकट आ गई है। अधम! मुझे शिक्षा देने चला है। हनुमान् जी ने कहा- इससे उलटा ही होगा (अर्थात् मृत्यु तेरी निकट आई है, मेरी नहीं)। यह तेरा मतिभ्रम (बुद्धि का फेर) है, मैंने प्रत्यक्ष जान लिया है ॥
english_translation: “Your death is near, wicked one. You try to teach me, lowly one? Hanuman replied, “The opposite will happen. I see clearly that your mind is confused.”
essence: Ego mistakes itself for wisdom until clear seeing names the confusion.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Ravana that death is coming for him, not for Hanuman. Ravana’s attempt to lecture him only reveals Ravana’s own confusion.
insight: It teaches you to recognize when confidence is actually confusion, and to answer from clear seeing instead of intimidation.
modern_relevance: Someone in a meeting keeps talking over everyone, certain they understand the situation better than anyone else. You can feel the gap between volume and clarity. Hanuman shows how to name that gap without losing your center.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: सुनि कपि बचन बहुत खिसिआना। बेगि न हरहु मूढ़ कर प्राना॥ सुनत निसाचर मारन धाए। सचिवन्ह सहित बिभीषनु आए ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी के वचन सुनकर वह बहुत ही कुपित हो गया। (और बोला-) अरे! इस मूर्ख का प्राण शीघ्र ही क्यों नहीं हर लेते? सुनते ही राक्षस उन्हें मारने दौड़े उसी समय मंत्रियों के साथ विभीषणजी वहाँ आ पहुँचे ॥
english_translation: Hearing Hanuman's words, Ravana grew very angry and said, "Why not quickly take this fool's life?" As the demons rushed to kill him, Vibhishana arrived with the ministers.
essence: Pride wants instant punishment; dharma arrives with restraint.
simple_meaning: Ravana loses his temper at Hanuman's words and orders him killed. The demons rush in, and Vibhishana arrives with the ministers.
insight: It shows how ego rushes toward retaliation, while a steadier voice arrives to check it.
modern_relevance: A harsh message lands in a group chat, and someone instantly wants to punish the sender. The room fills with heat before anyone asks what is actually right.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाइ सीस करि बिनय बहूता। नीति बिरोध न मारिअ दूता॥ आन दंड कछु करिअ गोसाँई। सबहीं कहा मंत्र भल भाई ॥
translation: उन्होंने सिर नवाकर और बहुत विनय करके रावण से कहा कि दूत को मारना नहीं चाहिए, यह नीति के विरुद्ध है। हे गोसाईं। कोई दूसरा दंड दिया जाए। सबने कहा- भाई! यह सलाह उत्तम है ॥
english_translation: They bowed their heads and spoke with great humility: killing a messenger goes against righteous conduct. My lord, give some other punishment. Everyone said, “Brother, that advice is good.”
essence: Even an enemy must be answered within the limits of conduct.
simple_meaning: A messenger should not be killed. Even in anger, there should be some other punishment instead.
insight: It shifts the mind from revenge to proportion, asking for a response that still respects conduct.
modern_relevance: A furious email lands in your inbox, and your first impulse is to destroy the person who sent it. This verse reminds you that even anger needs boundaries.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनत बिहसि बोला दसकंधर। अंग भंग करि पठइअ बंदर ॥
translation: यह सुनते ही रावण हँसकर बोला- अच्छा तो, बंदर को अंग-भंग करके भेज (लौटा) दिया जाए ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, the ten-headed Ravana laughed and said, "Maim the monkey and send him back."
essence: Mockery can be the first step toward self-destruction.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Hanuman and orders that the monkey be mutilated and sent back.
insight: It shows how ego blocks wise counsel and escalates conflict.
modern_relevance: A boss laughs off a serious warning in a meeting, then doubles down just to save face. That reflex can turn a small problem into a bigger one.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: कपि कें ममता पूँछ पर सबहि कहउँ समुझाइ। तेल बोरि पट बाँधि पुनि पावक देहु लगाइ ॥
translation: मैं सबको समझाकर कहता हूँ कि बंदर की ममता पूँछ पर होती है। अतः तेल में कपड़ा डुबोकर उसे इसकी पूँछ में बाँधकर फिर आग लगा दो ॥
english_translation: I tell everyone after making them understand: a monkey's attachment is to its tail. So soak cloth in oil, tie it to the tail, and then set it on fire.
essence: Pride tries to shame what it cannot control.
simple_meaning: Ravana orders Hanuman's tail to be soaked in oil, wrapped in cloth, and set on fire.
insight: It shows how ego reacts to challenge with humiliation instead of wisdom, creating the very consequence it wants to avoid.
modern_relevance: A manager mocks the person who exposed a mistake and tries to make an example of them. The humiliation feels powerful for a moment, but it often plants the seed of a bigger collapse.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: पूँछहीन बानर तहँ जाइहि। तब सठ निज नाथहि लइ आइहि॥ जिन्ह कै कीन्हिसि बहुत बड़ाई। देखउ मैं तिन्ह कै प्रभुताई ॥
translation: जब बिना पूँछ का यह बंदर वहाँ (अपने स्वामी के पास) जाएगा, तब यह मूर्ख अपने मालिक को साथ ले आएगा। जिनकी इसने बहुत बड़ाई की है, मैं जरा उनकी प्रभुता (सामर्थ्य) तो देखूँ! ॥
english_translation: When this tailless monkey goes there, that fool will bring his master along. Let me see the power of those he has praised so much.
essence: Pride laughs first, then discovers what it feared.
simple_meaning: Ravana thinks Hanuman will return to Ram and prove Ram's power. He mocks the monkey while secretly challenging the strength of Ram and his devotees.
insight: It shows how ego misreads devotion as weakness and treats a challenge as a joke.
modern_relevance: You dismiss someone’s warning at the meeting, then spend the next hour trying to prove they were wrong. Pride can make fear sound like confidence.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: बचन सुनत कपि मन मुसुकाना। भइ सहाय सारद मैं जाना॥ जातुधान सुनि रावन बचना। लागे रचैं मूढ़ सोइ रचना ॥
translation: यह वचन सुनते ही हनुमान् जी मन में मुस्कुराए (और मन ही मन बोले कि) मैं जान गया, सरस्वतीजी (इसे ऐसी बुद्धि देने में) सहायक हुई हैं। रावण के वचन सुनकर मूर्ख राक्षस वही (पूँछ में आग लगाने की) तैयारी करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Hearing these words, Hanuman smiled inwardly, knowing that Saraswati had helped him. Hearing Ravana's words, the foolish demons set about making that very plan.
essence: Clear seeing stays calm while foolishness rushes ahead.
simple_meaning: Hanuman realizes his own cleverness is being guided from beyond, while Ravana's followers blindly turn his words into action.
insight: It shifts attention from reacting to recognizing the hidden stupidity in the situation.
modern_relevance: Someone tries to embarrass you in a meeting, and the whole room starts following their lead. You see the setup instantly, stay calm, and let their own move reveal their mistake.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रहा न नगर बसन घृत तेला। बाढ़ी पूँछ कीन्ह कपि खेला॥ कौतुक कहँ आए पुरबासी। मारहिं चरन करहिं बहु हाँसी ॥
translation: (पूँछ के लपेटने में इतना कपड़ा और घी-तेल लगा कि) नगर में कपड़ा, घी और तेल नहीं रह गया। हनुमान् जी ने ऐसा खेल किया कि पूँछ बढ़ गई (लंबी हो गई)। नगरवासी लोग तमाशा देखने आए। वे हनुमान् जी को पैर से ठोकर मारते हैं और उनकी हँसी करते हैं ॥
english_translation: So much cloth, ghee, and oil were used that the city ran short. Hanuman turned the whole thing into play, and his tail grew long. The townspeople came to watch for fun, then kicked him and mocked him.
essence: Mockery gathers its own undoing.
simple_meaning: The people of Lanka use up cloth, ghee, and oil to wrap Hanuman's tail, then come mockingly to watch him.
insight: It shows how mob laughter can hide fear, and how humiliation often precedes a reversal of power.
modern_relevance: A crowd gathers around someone already embarrassed, turning humiliation into a public event. What feels like a joke in the moment can become the very thing that exposes arrogance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बाजहिं ढोल देहिं सब तारी। नगर फेरि पुनि पूँछ प्रजारी॥ पावक जरत देखि हनुमंता। भयउ परम लघुरूप तुरंता ॥
translation: ढोल बजते हैं, सब लोग तालियाँ पीटते हैं। हनुमान् जी को नगर में फिराकर, फिर पूँछ में आग लगा दी। अग्नि को जलते हुए देखकर हनुमान् जी तुरंत ही बहुत छोटे रूप में हो गए ॥
english_translation: Drums beat and everyone claps. Hanuman is paraded through the city, then his tail is set on fire. Seeing the flame burn, Hanuman instantly takes a very small form.
essence: Humiliation does not control you when your response stays free.
simple_meaning: The city celebrates Hanuman's humiliation, then sets his tail on fire. Hanuman responds by shrinking instantly to a tiny form.
insight: It shows how composure can turn humiliation into readiness.
modern_relevance: You are being laughed at in a room, and your body wants to flare up. Instead, you breathe, adjust, and respond with precision rather than ego.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निबुकि चढ़ेउ कप कनक अटारीं। भईं सभीत निसाचर नारीं ॥
translation: बंधन से निकलकर वे सोने की अटारियों पर जा चढ़े। उनको देखकर राक्षसों की स्त्रियाँ भयभीत हो गईं ॥
english_translation: Free of restraint, he climbed the golden rooftops, and the demon women grew frightened at the sight.
essence: Fearless movement itself becomes a force.
simple_meaning: Hanuman breaks free and moves onto the golden rooftops. The women of Lanka are startled by his presence.
insight: It shows how fearless action can shake a hostile environment without a single speech.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after everyone has written you off, and the whole mood changes. Your calm movement can unsettle fear more than noise ever could.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरि प्रेरित तेहि अवसर चले मरुत उनचास। अट्टहास करि गर्जा कपि बढ़ि लाग अकास ॥
translation: उस समय भगवान् की प्रेरणा से उनचासों पवन चलने लगे। हनुमान् जी अट्टहास करके गर्जे और बढ़कर आकाश से जा लगे ॥
english_translation: At that moment, moved by Ram's will, the forty-nine winds began to blow. Hanuman roared with a loud laugh and leapt up into the sky.
essence: When Ram moves you, even the sky becomes reachable.
simple_meaning: Ram's will sets the winds in motion, and Hanuman rises into the sky with a fearless roar.
insight: It shifts attention from effort alone to the force that rises when you act in alignment.
modern_relevance: You finish the hard part, take one breath, and suddenly the next step feels possible. Confidence changes the whole room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देह बिसाल परम हरुआई। मंदिर तें मंदिर चढ़ धाई॥ जरइ नगर भा लोग बिहाला। झपट लपट बहु कोटि कराला ॥
translation: देह बड़ी विशाल, परंतु बहुत ही हल्की (फुर्तीली) है। वे दौड़कर एक महल से दूसरे महल पर चढ़ जाते हैं। नगर जल रहा है लोग बेहाल हो गए हैं। आग की करोड़ों भयंकर लपटें झपट रही हैं ॥
english_translation: His body was huge yet wonderfully light. He leapt from palace to palace in an instant. The city burned, people were distressed, and countless fierce flames sprang up everywhere.
essence: Great power can move with effortless speed.
simple_meaning: Hanuman’s huge body moved with astonishing lightness as he rushed across the burning city from roof to roof.
insight: It shows unstoppable action: strength, speed, and purpose all working together without hesitation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तात मातु हा सुनिअ पुकारा। एहिं अवसर को हमहि उबारा॥ हम जो कहा यह कपि नहिं होई। बानर रूप धरें सुर कोई ॥
translation: हाय बप्पा! हाय मैया! इस अवसर पर हमें कौन बचाएगा? (चारों ओर) यही पुकार सुनाई पड़ रही है। हमने तो पहले ही कहा था कि यह वानर नहीं है, वानर का रूप धरे कोई देवता है! ॥
english_translation: “Father! Mother! Who will save us now?” That cry is heard everywhere. “We said before that this is no monkey — it must be some radiant being in monkey form!”
essence: Pride breaks first when the truth arrives.
simple_meaning: The people of Lanka panic and call out for help as they realize Hanuman is no ordinary monkey.
insight: It shows how arrogance collapses into fear when reality can no longer be denied.
modern_relevance: A room goes silent after the mistake becomes impossible to hide. The people who were certain a threat was harmless suddenly feel the full weight of what they ignored.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: साधु अवग्या कर फलु ऐसा। जरइ नगर अनाथ कर जैसा॥ जारा नगरु निमिष एक माहीं। एक बिभीषन कर गृह नाहीं ॥
translation: साधु के अपमान का यह फल है कि नगर, अनाथ के नगर की तरह जल रहा है। हनुमान् जी ने एक ही क्षण में सारा नगर जला डाला। एक विभीषण का घर नहीं जलाया ॥
english_translation: The result of insulting a saint is like this: the city burns like a helpless town. In a single moment the whole city was set ablaze, yet not Vibhishana's house.
essence: Disrespect the noble, and ruin follows; honor remains protected.
simple_meaning: Disrespecting a holy person brings ruin. Lanka burns in a moment, but Vibhishana's home is spared.
insight: It teaches you that contempt for the worthy invites destruction, while integrity can remain untouched in the middle of chaos.
modern_relevance: You mock the one person in the room who stayed decent, and suddenly the whole group dynamic turns against you. Respect matters more than you think.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ताकर दूत अनल जेहिं सिरिजा। जरा न सो तेहि कारन गिरिजा॥ उलटि पलटि लंका सब जारी। कूदि परा पुनि सिंधु मझारी ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे पार्वती! जिन्होंने अग्नि को बनाया, हनुमान् जी उन्हीं के दूत हैं। इसी कारण वे अग्नि से नहीं जले। हनुमान् जी ने उलट-पलटकर (एक ओर से दूसरी ओर तक) सारी लंका जला दी। फिर वे समुद्र में कूद पड़े॥
english_translation: O Parvati, the one who created fire also sent Hanuman as his messenger. That is why fire could not burn him. Hanuman turned Lanka upside down and burned it all, then jumped back into the sea.
essence: The fire that should destroy him cannot touch the one sent by its maker.
simple_meaning: Hanuman is beyond fire because the creator of fire sent him. He burns Lanka completely, then returns by leaping into the sea.
insight: It shows that true protection comes from the mission itself, not from external safety.
modern_relevance: You walk into a situation everyone says will burn you out, but your purpose keeps you steady. What should have destroyed you becomes the very thing you pass through.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: पूँछ बुझाइ खोइ श्रम धरि लघु रूप बहोरि। जनकसुता कें आगें ठाढ़ भयउ कर जोरि ॥
translation: पूँछ बुझाकर, थकावट दूर करके और फिर छोटा सा रूप धारण कर हनुमान् जी श्री जानकीजी के सामने हाथ जोड़कर जा खड़े हुए ॥
english_translation: After putting out his tail, shaking off his fatigue, and taking a small form again, Hanuman stood before Janakasuta with folded hands.
essence: Power becomes beautiful when it returns as humility.
simple_meaning: Hanuman cools his tail, recovers from exhaustion, shrinks again, and stands respectfully before Sita with folded hands.
insight: It shifts action into service: after achievement, the next move is respect, not display.
modern_relevance: You finish the hard part, wipe the sweat from your face, and then walk back in humble enough to listen. Real strength knows when to bow.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मातु मोहि दीजे कछु चीन्हा। जैसें रघुनायक मोहि दीन्हा॥ चूड़ामनि उतारि तब दयऊ। हरष समेत पवनसुत लयऊ ॥
translation: (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे माता! मुझे कोई चिह्न (पहचान) दीजिए, जैसे श्री रघुनाथजी ने मुझे दिया था। तब सीताजी ने चूड़ामणि उतारकर दी। हनुमान् जी ने उसको हर्षपूर्वक ले लिया ॥
english_translation: “Mother, give me some token of recognition, just as Raghunath gave me.” Then Sita removed her jeweled hair ornament and gave it. Hanuman received it joyfully.
essence: A true token carries the whole bond within it.
simple_meaning: Hanuman asks Sita for a token from Ram, and she gives him her jeweled ornament. The exchange confirms their bond and sends him back with joy.
insight: It teaches you to value symbols that keep love and trust alive across separation.
modern_relevance: You save a note, a photo, or a voice message because it carries someone’s presence across distance. A small thing can steady you more than a long speech.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: कहेहु तात अस मोर प्रनामा। सब प्रकार प्रभु पूरनकामा॥ दीन दयाल बिरिदु संभारी। हरहु नाथ सम संकट भारी ॥
translation: (जानकीजी ने कहा-) हे तात! मेरा प्रणाम निवेदन करना और इस प्रकार कहना- हे प्रभु! यद्यपि आप सब प्रकार से पूर्ण काम हैं (आपको किसी प्रकार की कामना नहीं है), तथापि दीनों (दुःखियों) पर दया करना आपका विरद है (और मैं दीन हूँ) अतः उस विरद को याद करके, हे नाथ! मेरे भारी संकट को दूर कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Tell him, dear one: offer my प्रणाम. Say that the Lord is complete in every way and has no want. Yet the Lord’s very vow is to protect the lowly; remembering that vow, O Master, remove my great suffering.
essence: Needless strength becomes mercy when it remembers its own vow.
simple_meaning: Sita asks Hanuman to greet Ram respectfully and remind him that, although he needs nothing, his special nature is to protect the helpless. She begs him to end her suffering.
insight: It teaches you to ask for help by appealing to character, not entitlement.
modern_relevance: You text the one person who can help, even though they owe you nothing. You do not flatter them; you remind them of who they are and ask them to act from that.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: तात सक्रसुत कथा सनाएहु। बान प्रताप प्रभुहि समुझाएहु॥ मास दिवस महुँ नाथु न आवा। तौ पुनि मोहि जिअत नहिं पावा ॥
translation: हे तात! इंद्रपुत्र जयंत की कथा (घटना) सुनाना और प्रभु को उनके बाण का प्रताप समझाना (स्मरण कराना)। यदि महीने भर में नाथ न आए तो फिर मुझे जीती न पाएँगे ॥
english_translation: Dear Hanuman, tell him the story of Jayanta, Indra's son, and remind him of the power of his arrow. If my Lord does not come within a month, he will never find me alive again.
essence: Faith waits, but it still asks for Ram to come soon.
simple_meaning: Sita asks Hanuman to tell Ram about Jayanta and his own arrow's power, then says that if Ram does not come within a month, she will not remain alive.
insight: It shifts longing into a clear request: carry the message, strengthen trust, and name the limit of waiting.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after a message that changed everything, then nothing follows. That quiet stretch of waiting is what Sita is living through: hope held together by memory and faith.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: कहु कपि केहि बिधि राखौं प्राना। तुम्हहू तात कहत अब जाना॥ तोहि देखि सीतलि भइ छाती। पुनि मो कहुँ सोइ दिनु सो राती ॥
translation: हे हनुमान् ! कहो, मैं किस प्रकार प्राण रखूँ! हे तात! तुम भी अब जाने को कह रहे हो। तुमको देखकर छाती ठंडी हुई थी। फिर मुझे वही दिन और वही रात! ॥
english_translation: O Hanuman, tell me how I am to keep my life! You too, dear one, are now saying you must go. Seeing you had cooled my heart; now I will face the same day and the same night again.
essence: A brief refuge can make separation hurt even more.
simple_meaning: Sita tells Hanuman that his presence brought her comfort, and his departure will leave her facing the same unbearable loneliness again.
insight: It names how relief can deepen attachment, making separation feel sharper after comfort.
modern_relevance: You finally hear from the person who has been checking on you through the worst week of your life. Then they say they have to go, and the room feels empty again.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: जनकसुतहि समुझाइ करि बहु बिधि धीरजु दीन्ह। चरन कमल सिरु नाइ कपि गवनु राम पहिं कीन्ह ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी ने जानकीजी को समझाकर बहुत प्रकार से धीरज दिया और उनके चरणकमलों में सिर नवाकर श्री रामजी के पास गमन किया ॥ समुद्र के इस पार आना, सबका लौटना, मधुवन प्रवेश, सुग्रीव मिलन,
english_translation: After comforting Janaki in many ways, Hanuman bowed his head to her lotus feet and went to meet Ram.
essence: Devotion first comforts the suffering, then returns to the beloved.
simple_meaning: Hanuman reassures Sita, bows to her feet, and then goes to Ram. His devotion shows itself through comfort, humility, and action.
insight: It teaches you to combine reassurance, humility, and faithful action in one response.
modern_relevance: You finish helping a frightened friend pack their bags, wait until they can breathe again, and only then walk out the door. Real devotion does not rush past the person in front of you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चलत महाधुनि गर्जेसि भारी। गर्भ स्रवहिं सुनि निसिचर नारी॥ नाघि सिंधु एहि पारहि आवा। सबद किलिकिला कपिन्ह सुनावा ॥
translation: चलते समय उन्होंने महाध्वनि से भारी गर्जन किया, जिसे सुनकर राक्षसों की स्त्रियों के गर्भ गिरने लगे। समुद्र लाँघकर वे इस पार आए और उन्होंने वानरों को किलकिला शब्द (हर्षध्वनि) सुनाया ॥
english_translation: As he went, he roared so fiercely that the demon women miscarried at the sound. After crossing the ocean, he came to this shore and gave the monkeys a joyful cry.
essence: A true return carries both thunder and joy.
simple_meaning: Hanuman crossed the ocean, roared in triumph, and reached the monkeys with a cry of joy. The verse mainly describes the scene, not a teaching.
insight: It frames success as something that changes the atmosphere around you before you explain it.
modern_relevance: You come home after the hardest part is over, still buzzing from the win, and your voice gives the good news before your face does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरषे सब बिलोकि हनुमाना। नूतन जन्म कपिन्ह तब जाना॥ मुख प्रसन्न तन तेज बिराजा। कीन्हेसि रामचंद्र कर काजा ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी को देखकर सब हर्षित हो गए और तब वानरों ने अपना नया जन्म समझा। हनुमान् जी का मुख प्रसन्न है और शरीर में तेज विराजमान है, (जिससे उन्होंने समझ लिया कि) ये श्री रामचंद्रजी का कार्य कर आए हैं ॥
english_translation: Everyone rejoiced on seeing Hanuman; the monkeys felt they had been born anew. Hanuman’s face was bright with joy, and his body shone with radiance, showing that he had done Ramchandra’s work.
essence: Completed service leaves a glow others can instantly recognize.
simple_meaning: The monkeys are overjoyed to see Hanuman return, and his shining face shows he has completed Ram's task.
insight: It shifts attention from the feat itself to the visible peace that comes after faithful service.
modern_relevance: You walk into the room after a hard trip, and everyone can read it on your face: the mission is done, and the tension breaks at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मिले सकल अति भए सुखारी। तलफत मीन पाव जिमि बारी॥ चले हरषि रघुनायक पासा। पूँछत कहत नवल इतिहासा ॥
translation: सब हनुमान् जी से मिले और बहुत ही सुखी हुए, जैसे तड़पती हुई मछली को जल मिल गया हो। सब हर्षित होकर नए-नए इतिहास (वृत्तांत) पूछते- कहते हुए श्री रघुनाथजी के पास चले ॥
english_translation: Everyone met Hanuman and became deeply joyful, like a thirsty fish finding water. Rejoicing, they went to Raghunath, asking and telling fresh accounts.
essence: Meeting the one you longed for turns relief into joy.
simple_meaning: The vanaras are overjoyed to see Hanuman, and they hurry to Ram with fresh questions and stories.
insight: It shows how reunion naturally becomes conversation, gratitude, and movement toward what matters most.
modern_relevance: You spot the friend who finally made it through the airport crowd, and your whole body relaxes. Relief turns into rapid-fire questions, because the person you were waiting for is finally here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब मधुबन भीतर सब आए। अंगद संमत मधु फल खाए॥ रखवारे जब बरजन लागे। मुष्टि प्रहार हनत सब भागे ॥
translation: तब सब लोग मधुवन के भीतर आए और अंगद की सम्मति से सबने मधुर फल (या मधु और फल) खाए। जब रखवाले बरजने लगे, तब घूँसों की मार मारते ही सब रखवाले भाग छूटे ॥
english_translation: Then everyone entered the Madhu grove, and with Angad's approval ate the sweet fruits. When the guards tried to stop them, a few punches sent them running.
essence: Bold action can clear the way before resistance gathers.
simple_meaning: Hanuman and the monkeys enter the grove, eat the fruits, and chase away the guards who try to stop them.
insight: It shifts attention from caution to decisive action when the moment calls for it.
modern_relevance: A team walks into a space where they do not feel welcome, gets the job done, and leaves before fear can take over.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जाइ पुकारे ते सब बन उजार जुबराज। सुनि सुग्रीव हरष कपि करि आए प्रभु काज ॥
translation: उन सबने जाकर पुकारा कि युवराज अंगद वन उजाड़ रहे हैं। यह सुनकर सुग्रीव हर्षित हुए कि वानर प्रभु का कार्य कर आए हैं ॥
english_translation: When they went and cried out that Prince Angad was destroying the grove, Sugriva heard it and rejoiced that the monkeys had completed the Lord's work.
essence: What looks like trouble can still be faithful service.
simple_meaning: The guards complain that Angad is wrecking the grove, and Sugriva is pleased because the monkeys have done Ram's work.
insight: It shifts judgment from appearances to the larger purpose behind an action.
modern_relevance: A manager hears that the team caused a stir at a client site, but the real issue was never the noise. What matters is whether the work got done.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जौं न होति सीता सुधि पाई। मधुबन के फल सकहिं कि काई॥ एहि बिधि मन बिचार कर राजा। आइ गए कपि सहित समाजा ॥
translation: यदि सीताजी की खबर न पाई होती तो क्या वे मधुवन के फल खा सकते थे? इस प्रकार राजा सुग्रीव मन में विचार कर ही रहे थे कि समाज सहित वानर आ गए ॥
english_translation: If Sita's news had not been found, could the monkeys have eaten the fruits of the grove? While Sugriva was thinking this in his mind, the monkeys arrived with the whole company.
essence: Enjoyment has meaning only after the real mission is fulfilled.
simple_meaning: Sugriva reflects that the monkeys would not have enjoyed the grove if they had not first found news of Sita. As he thinks this, Hanuman and the others arrive.
insight: It frames pleasure as secondary to completing the true task.
modern_relevance: You finally relax after a long search, but the reward only matters because the real problem was solved first. The relief comes before the celebration.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: आइ सबन्हि नावा पद सीसा। मिलेउ सबन्हि अति प्रेम कपीसा॥ पूँछी कुसल कुसल पद देखी। राम कृपाँ भा काजु बिसेषी ॥
translation: (सबने आकर सुग्रीव के चरणों में सिर नवाया। कपिराज सुग्रीव सभी से बड़े प्रेम के साथ मिले। उन्होंने कुशल पूछी, (तब वानरों ने उत्तर दिया-) आपके चरणों के दर्शन से सब कुशल है। श्री रामजी की कृपा से विशेष कार्य हुआ (कार्य में विशेष सफलता हुई है) ॥
english_translation: All the monkeys bowed their heads at Sugriva’s feet. The king of the monkeys greeted them with great love. He asked after their well-being, and they replied that seeing his feet had made everything well. By Ram’s grace, their mission had been especially successful.
essence: Love received well makes hard work feel blessed.
simple_meaning: The monkeys bow to Sugriva, and he welcomes them warmly. They say that seeing his feet has made them well, and that Ram’s grace has made their mission succeed.
insight: It shows how respect, affection, and grace can confirm that a difficult task has been completed.
modern_relevance: You come home after a hard day, and the first warm face at the door changes everything. Relief often begins with being received well.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ काजु कीन्हेउ हनुमाना। राखे सकल कपिन्ह के प्राना॥ सुनि सुग्रीव बहुरि तेहि मिलेऊ कपिन्ह सहित रघुपति पहिं चलेऊ ॥
translation: हे नाथ! हनुमान ने सब कार्य किया और सब वानरों के प्राण बचा लिए। यह सुनकर सुग्रीवजी हनुमान् जी से फिर मिले और सब वानरों समेत श्री रघुनाथजी के पास चले ॥
english_translation: O Lord, Hanuman has done the task and saved the lives of all the monkeys. Hearing this, Sugriva met him again, and he went with all the monkeys to Raghupati.
essence: True success is when everyone survives the task.
simple_meaning: Hanuman completes the mission and saves the monkey army. Sugriva rejoins him, and everyone goes together to Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from personal triumph to the welfare of the whole group.
modern_relevance: You finish the hard part of a group project at 1 a.m. and quietly keep everyone from falling apart. Only after the crisis passes does the team move together again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम कपिन्ह जब आवत देखा। किएँ काजु मन हरष बिसेषा॥ फटिक सिला बैठे द्वौ भाई। परे सकल कपि चरनन्हि जाई ॥
translation: श्री रामजी ने जब वानरों को कार्य किए हुए आते देखा तब उनके मन में विशेष हर्ष हुआ। दोनों भाई स्फटिक शिला पर बैठे थे। सब वानर जाकर उनके चरणों पर गिर पड़े ॥
english_translation: When Ram saw the monkeys returning after completing the task, his heart filled with special joy. The two brothers sat on a crystal rock, and all the monkeys fell at their feet.
essence: Completed effort becomes sweeter when it is received with love.
simple_meaning: Ram is pleased when the monkeys return after finishing their task. He and Lakshman sit together, and the monkeys bow at their feet.
insight: It shifts attention from the task itself to the bond that gives the task meaning.
modern_relevance: You come home after a hard day and someone sees the effort behind your tired face. That quiet welcome can feel like the real reward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रीति सहित सब भेंटे रघुपति करुना पुंज॥ पूछी कुसल नाथ अब कुसल देखि पद कंज ॥
translation: दया की राशि श्री रघुनाथजी सबसे प्रेम सहित गले लगकर मिले और कुशल पूछी। (वानरों ने कहा-) हे नाथ! आपके चरण कमलों के दर्शन पाने से अब कुशल है ॥
english_translation: Raghupati, a mass of compassion, embraced them all with love and asked after their welfare. Seeing your lotus feet, O Lord, now all is well.
essence: Love makes a simple meeting feel like blessing.
simple_meaning: Ram lovingly greets the monkeys and asks how they are. They reply that simply seeing his feet has made everything feel well.
insight: It shifts attention from achievement to presence: being seen by the beloved is itself the reward.
modern_relevance: You finally walk into the room after a long, hard day, and the person you trust most just looks relieved to see you. No speech is needed. Presence itself becomes the comfort.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जामवंत कह सुनु रघुराया। जा पर नाथ करहु तुम्ह दाया॥ ताहि सदा सुभ कुसल निरंतर। सुर नर मुनि प्रसन्न ता ऊपर ॥
translation: जाम्बवान् ने कहा- हे रघुनाथजी! सुनिए। हे नाथ! जिस पर आप दया करते हैं, उसे सदा कल्याण और निरंतर कुशल है। देवता, मनुष्य और मुनि सभी उस पर प्रसन्न रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Jambavan said: Listen, O Lord of Raghu. Whoever receives your grace lives in lasting well-being. Devas, humans, and sages are pleased with that person.
essence: Ram’s grace makes a person permanently fortunate and universally welcomed.
simple_meaning: Jambavan tells Ram that anyone touched by Ram's grace lives in lasting well-being, and even the higher beings, people, and sages feel pleased with that person.
insight: It shifts attention from self-made success to the quiet power of being supported by grace.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence steadies a whole room. Their confidence isn’t loud, but everyone relaxes around them. Jambavan says that kind of steadiness comes from being touched by Ram’s grace.
speaker: Jambavan

verse_text: सोइ बिजई बिनई गुन सागर। तासु सुजसु त्रैलोक उजागर॥ प्रभु कीं कृपा भयउ सबु काजू। जन्म हमार सुफल भा आजू ॥
translation: वही विजयी है, वही विनयी है और वही गुणों का समुद्र बन जाता है। उसी का सुंदर यश तीनों लोकों में प्रकाशित होता है। प्रभु की कृपा से सब कार्य हुआ। आज हमारा जन्म सफल हो गया ॥
english_translation: He alone is victorious, humble, and an ocean of virtues. His beautiful fame shines through the three worlds. By the Lord's grace, everything was accomplished. Today our birth has become fruitful.
essence: Victory becomes holy when humility and grace stand behind it.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as victorious, humble, and endlessly virtuous. Because of his grace, Hanuman's mission succeeds and his life feels fulfilled.
insight: It shifts credit away from personal achievement toward grace and devotion.
modern_relevance: You finish the hardest part of a project and realize the relief isn't pride — it's gratitude. The outcome feels larger than your effort because something beyond ego carried it through.
speaker: Jambavan

verse_text: नाथ पवनसुत कीन्हि जो करनी। सहसहुँ मुख न जाइ सो बरनी॥ पवनतनय के चरित सुहाए। जामवंत रघुपतिहि सुनाए ॥
translation: हे नाथ! पवनपुत्र हनुमान् ने जो करनी की, उसका हजार मुखों से भी वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। तब जाम्बवान् ने हनुमान् जी के सुंदर चरित्र (कार्य) श्री रघुनाथजी को सुनाए ॥
english_translation: O Lord, the deeds Hanuman performed cannot be described even with a thousand mouths. Then Jambavan told Raghunath the lovely story of the son of the wind.
essence: Real devotion makes a person impossible to fully describe.
simple_meaning: Hanuman’s actions are so great they cannot be fully described. Jambavan then tells Ram about Hanuman’s noble deeds.
insight: It shifts attention from self-advertisement to deeds that speak for themselves.
modern_relevance: You see someone quietly fix the mess, stay late, and carry the whole burden without asking for credit. Later, the room finally understands what that person did.
speaker: Jambavan

verse_text: सुनत कृपानिधि मन अति भाए। पुनि हनुमान हरषि हियँ लाए॥ कहहु तात केहि भाँति जानकी। रहति करति रच्छा स्वप्रान की ॥
translation: (वे चरित्र) सुनने पर कृपानिधि श्री रामचंदजी के मन को बहुत ही अच्छे लगे। उन्होंने हर्षित होकर हनुमान् जी को फिर हृदय से लगा लिया और कहा- हे तात! कहो, सीता किस प्रकार रहती और अपने प्राणों की रक्षा करती हैं? ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, the compassionate Lord was greatly pleased. He embraced Hanuman with joy and said, "Tell me, dear one, in what way does Janaki live and protect her life?"
essence: Devotion makes even the Lord long for news of the beloved.
simple_meaning: Ram is delighted by Hanuman's report and embraces him warmly, then asks how Sita is surviving and protecting herself.
insight: It shifts attention from heroic achievement to the living bond that gives the mission its meaning.
modern_relevance: You finally hear from someone you love after days of silence. Relief comes first, but your next question is the real one: are they safe, and how are they holding up?
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाम पाहरू दिवस निसि ध्यान तुम्हार कपाट। लोचन निज पद जंत्रित जाहिं प्रान केहिं बाट ॥
translation: (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) आपका नाम रात-दिन पहरा देने वाला है, आपका ध्यान ही किंवाड़ है। नेत्रों को अपने चरणों में लगाए रहती हैं, यही ताला लगा है, फिर प्राण जाएँ तो किस मार्ग से? ॥
english_translation: Your name guards me day and night; your meditation is the lock. My eyes stay fixed on your feet—how could my life leave by any other way?
essence: Remembrance becomes protection when your whole attention rests on Ram.
simple_meaning: Ram's name protects Hanuman constantly, and keeping Ram in mind keeps his life secure. With his gaze fixed on Ram's feet, nothing can pull him away.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to refuge in constant remembrance.
modern_relevance: You wake up at 3 a.m. with the same worry looping again. Something steadier than panic can hold you too: a name, a practice, a presence you return to until fear loses the doorway.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: चलत मोहि चूड़ामनि दीन्हीं। रघुपति हृदयँ लाइ सोइ लीन्ही॥ नाथ जुगल लोचन भरि बारी। बचन कहे कछु जनककुमारी ॥
translation: चलते समय उन्होंने मुझे चूड़ामणि (उतारकर) दी। श्री रघुनाथजी ने उसे लेकर हृदय से लगा लिया। (हनुमान् जी ने फिर कहा-) हे नाथ! दोनों नेत्रों में जल भरकर जानकीजी ने मुझसे कुछ वचन कहे- ॥
english_translation: As she left, she gave me her jewel from the hair. Raghupati took it and held it to his heart. Then, with both eyes full of tears, Janak’s daughter spoke a few words to me.
essence: Love turns a small token into living presence.
simple_meaning: Sita gave Hanuman a token for Ram, and Ram received it with deep emotion. Her tears and words show how much she longs to be reunited.
insight: It teaches you to see how devotion turns even a token into presence.
modern_relevance: You find a note, a photo, or a voice message from someone you miss, and your whole chest tightens. A small thing can carry a whole relationship when love is real.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: अनुज समेत गहेहु प्रभु चरना। दीन बंधु प्रनतारति हरना॥ मन क्रम बचन चरन अनुरागी। केहिं अपराध नाथ हौं त्यागी ॥
translation: छोटे भाई समेत प्रभु के चरण पकड़ना (और कहना कि) आप दीनबंधु हैं, शरणागत के दुःखों को हरने वाले हैं और मैं मन, वचन और कर्म से आपके चरणों की अनुरागिणी हूँ। फिर स्वामी (आप) ने मुझे किस अपराध से त्याग दिया? ॥
english_translation: With your younger brother beside you, you held the Lord's feet and said: 'You are the friend of the lowly, the remover of the suffering of those who seek refuge. I am devoted to your feet in mind, speech, and action. O Lord, what fault of mine caused you to cast me aside?'
essence: True devotion can ask hard questions without losing love.
simple_meaning: Sita calls Ram the friend of the helpless and says her mind, speech, and actions are devoted to him. She asks why he has abandoned her.
insight: It shows how devotion can coexist with honest sorrow, without collapsing into bitterness or self-erasure.
modern_relevance: You send a message after being hurt, trying to stay loving without hiding the ache. You still care completely, but you need to know why the distance exists.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: अवगुन एक मोर मैं माना। बिछुरत प्रान न कीन्ह पयाना॥ नाथ सो नयनन्हि को अपराधा। निसरत प्रान करहिं हठि बाधा ॥
translation: (हाँ) एक दोष मैं अपना (अवश्य) मानती हूँ कि आपका वियोग होते ही मेरे प्राण नहीं चले गए, किंतु हे नाथ! यह तो नेत्रों का अपराध है जो प्राणों के निकलने में हठपूर्वक बाधा देते हैं ॥
english_translation: I count one fault of my own: when you were taken from me, my life did not leave. O Lord, that is the fault of my eyes, which stubbornly block my breath from going out.
essence: Separation is so sharp that even survival feels like resistance.
simple_meaning: Sita says her only fault is that separation from Ram did not kill her at once. She blames her eyes for stubbornly keeping her life-breath from leaving.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame to seeing how grief can overwhelm even the body's will to release.
modern_relevance: You get the message you've been waiting for after months of silence, and relief arrives mixed with ache. Part of you wonders why you had to keep going at all.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: बिरह अगिनि तनु तूल समीरा। स्वास जरइ छन माहिं सरीरा॥ नयन स्रवहिं जलु निज हित लागी। जरैं न पाव देह बिरहागी ॥
translation: विरह अग्नि है, शरीर रूई है और श्वास पवन है, इस प्रकार (अग्नि और पवन का संयोग होने से) यह शरीर क्षणमात्र में जल सकता है, परंतु नेत्र अपने हित के लिए प्रभु का स्वरूप देखकर (सुखी होने के लिए) जल (आँसू) बरसाते हैं, जिससे विरह की आग से भी देह जलने नहीं पाती ॥
english_translation: The fire of separation is in the body, the body is like cotton, and breath is like wind; in a moment the body could burn. Yet the eyes pour out tears for their own relief, and so the body does not burn in the fire of separation.
essence: Longing burns, but tears keep the heart from being consumed.
simple_meaning: Separation feels like a fire that could consume the body, but tears from the eyes ease that pain and keep the body from burning up.
insight: It shifts you from resisting grief to letting expression discharge its heat before it overwhelms you.
modern_relevance: You stare at your phone after a message that never came, feeling heat rise in your chest. The tears, the shaking, the quiet release — they are not weakness; they are what keep heartbreak from hardening into collapse.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सीता कै अति बिपति बिसाला। बिनहिं कहें भलि दीनदयाला ॥
translation: सीताजी की विपत्ति बहुत बड़ी है। हे दीनदयालु! वह बिना कही ही अच्छी है (कहने से आपको बड़ा क्लेश होगा) ॥
english_translation: Sita's suffering is immense. O Merciful One, it is better left unspoken.
essence: True compassion hears pain before it is spoken.
simple_meaning: Sita's distress is so severe that even speaking of it feels unbearable. The line turns toward Ram as the one who understands without needing details.
insight: It trains you to respond to suffering with presence first, not explanation.
modern_relevance: You sit beside a friend in the hospital and run out of words. What matters most is not explanation, but the quiet recognition that their pain is real.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: निमिष निमिष करुनानिधि जाहिं कलप सम बीति। बेगि चलिअ प्रभु आनिअ भुज बल खल दल जीति ॥
translation: हे करुणानिधान! उनका एक-एक पल कल्प के समान बीतता है। अतः हे प्रभु! तुरंत चलिए और अपनी भुजाओं के बल से दुष्टों के दल को जीतकर सीताजी को ले आइए ॥
english_translation: O treasure of compassion, for her every moment passes like an age. Please come at once, and by the strength of your arms defeat the enemy host and bring Sita back.
essence: Real devotion cannot watch suffering slowly.
simple_meaning: Sita's suffering feels unbearably long, so Hanuman pleads with Ram to come quickly, defeat the enemy forces, and rescue her.
insight: It turns devotion into immediate action for someone else's suffering, not private emotion.
modern_relevance: You get a voice note from someone you love, and one sentence tells you they are barely holding on. You stop everything. That urgency is what Hanuman feels here.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: सुनि सीता दुख प्रभु सुख अयना। भरि आए जल राजिव नयना॥ बचन कायँ मन मम गति जाही। सपनेहुँ बूझिअ बिपति कि ताही ॥
translation: सीताजी का दुःख सुनकर सुख के धाम प्रभु के कमल नेत्रों में जल भर आया (और वे बोले-) मन, वचन और शरीर से जिसे मेरी ही गति (मेरा ही आश्रय) है, उसे क्या स्वप्न में भी विपत्ति हो सकती है? ॥
english_translation: Hearing of Sita's sorrow, the Lord whose home is joy had tears fill his lotus eyes. He said, “For the one whose refuge in mind, speech, and body is mine, can there be adversity even in a dream?”
essence: Complete refuge makes even adversity feel unreal.
simple_meaning: Ram is moved to tears by Sita's suffering, and he says that anyone who takes refuge in him completely cannot be touched by real danger.
insight: It shifts trust from partial reliance to wholehearted refuge, showing that surrender and protection belong together.
modern_relevance: You call someone in panic after a night of bad news, and they answer with steady care instead of distance. That is the feeling this verse carries: being held completely when you are most vulnerable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह हनुमंत बिपति प्रभु सोई। जब तव सुमिरन भजन न होई॥ केतिक बात प्रभु जातुधान की। रिपुहि जीति आनिबी जानकी ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी ने कहा- हे प्रभु! विपत्ति तो वही (तभी) है जब आपका भजन-स्मरण न हो। हे प्रभो! राक्षसों की बात ही कितनी है? आप शत्रु को जीतकर जानकीजी को ले आवेंगे ॥
english_translation: Hanuman said, "O Lord, the only real trouble is when your remembrance and devotion are absent. What are these demons to you? You will defeat the enemy and bring Sita back."
essence: Separation from Ram is the only real danger.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says the worst suffering is forgetting Ram. With Ram in mind, even demons and danger are not a real problem.
insight: It shifts the mind from outer danger to inner anchoring in devotion.
modern_relevance: You are stuck in traffic, late, and your chest tightens. Then you remember what truly steadies you. The problem is still there, but it no longer owns you.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: सुनु कपि तोहि समान उपकारी। नहिं कोउ सुर नर मुनि तनुधारी॥ प्रति उपकार करौं का तोरा। सनमुख होइ न सकत मन मोरा ॥
