translation: (भगवान् कहने लगे-) हे हनुमान् ! सुन, तेरे समान मेरा उपकारी देवता, मनुष्य अथवा मुनि कोई भी शरीरधारी नहीं है। मैं तेरा प्रत्युपकार (बदले में उपकार) तो क्या करूँ, मेरा मन भी तेरे सामने नहीं हो सकता ॥
english_translation: O monkey, listen: no embodied being among gods, humans, or sages has helped me like you. What can I give you in return? My mind cannot even face you.
essence: Real devotion creates a debt love itself cannot repay.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Hanuman that no one else has served him like this, and he cannot repay such devotion in any ordinary way.
insight: It shifts the mind from transactional giving to devotion that cannot be measured or settled.
modern_relevance: You stay up all night helping a friend through a crisis, and they say, almost helplessly, that they can never make it up to you. Some acts of love simply outgrow accounting.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनु सुत तोहि उरिन मैं नाहीं। देखेउँ करि बिचार मन माहीं॥ पुनि पुनि कपिहि चितव सुरत्राता। लोचन नीर पुलक अति गाता ॥
translation: हे पुत्र! सुन, मैंने मन में (खूब) विचार करके देख लिया कि मैं तुझसे उऋण नहीं हो सकता। देवताओं के रक्षक प्रभु बार-बार हनुमान् जी को देख रहे हैं। नेत्रों में प्रेमाश्रुओं का जल भरा है और शरीर अत्यंत पुलकित है ॥
english_translation: Son, listen: after careful thought, I see that I can never repay you. The protector of the gods keeps looking at Hanuman again and again, with tears in his eyes and his body bristling with joy.
essence: Pure devotion leaves even the beloved unable to repay it.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Hanuman that no amount of thought can make him feel repaid. Hanuman's devotion is so complete that Ram keeps gazing at him with tears and delight.
insight: It shifts the mind from transaction to gratitude, showing that selfless service creates a bond beyond compensation.
modern_relevance: You help someone through a crisis, expecting nothing back. Later, they try to thank you and fall short. Some care changes the relationship so deeply that repayment no longer makes sense.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनि प्रभु बचन बिलोकि मुख गात हरषि हनुमंत। चरन परेउ प्रेमाकुल त्राहि त्राहि भगवंत ॥
translation: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर और उनके (प्रसन्न) मुख तथा (पुलकित) अंगों को देखकर हनुमान् जी हर्षित हो गए और प्रेम में विकल होकर 'हे भगवन् ! मेरी रक्षा करो, रक्षा करो' कहते हुए श्री रामजी के चरणों में गिर पड़े ॥
english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words and seeing His joyful face and thrilled body, Hanuman was filled with delight and, overcome by love, fell at Ram's feet crying, "Protect me, protect me, O Lord."
essence: When love is real, surrender happens before you plan it.
simple_meaning: Hanuman hears Ram's loving words, sees His joy, and is so moved that he falls at Ram's feet in surrender.
insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to embodied surrender, where love becomes action before speech.
modern_relevance: You finally hear the apology you were not expecting, and your chest loosens before you can explain why. Some moments don't call for analysis — only surrender.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बार बार प्रभु चहइ उठावा। प्रेम मगन तेहि उठब न भावा॥ प्रभु कर पंकज कपि कें सीसा। सुमिरि सो दसा मगन गौरीसा ॥
translation: प्रभु उनको बार-बार उठाना चाहते हैं, परंतु प्रेम में डूबे हुए हनुमान् जी को चरणों से उठना सुहाता नहीं। प्रभु का करकमल हनुमान् जी के सिर पर है। उस स्थिति का स्मरण करके शिवजी प्रेममग्न हो गए ॥
english_translation: Again and again, the Lord tries to lift him, but Hanuman, lost in love, does not wish to rise. The Lord’s lotus hand rests on Hanuman’s head; remembering that scene, Shiva becomes absorbed in love.
essence: Love can make even honor feel too small to accept.
simple_meaning: Hanuman is so absorbed in love for Ram that he does not want to get up, even when Ram tries to lift him. Shiva remembers this and is moved by devotion.
insight: It shifts attention from receiving recognition to resting inside devotion itself.
modern_relevance: You finally hear the praise you worked for, but all you feel is gratitude and awe. Some moments are too sacred for self-importance to stand up in them.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सावधान मन करि पुनि संकर। लागे कहन कथा अति सुंदर॥ कपि उठाई प्रभु हृदयँ लगावा। कर गहि परम निकट बैठावा ॥
translation: फिर मन को सावधान करके शंकरजी अत्यंत सुंदर कथा कहने लगे- हनुमान् जी को उठाकर प्रभु ने हृदय से लगाया और हाथ पकड़कर अत्यंत निकट बैठा लिया ॥
english_translation: Then, with his mind made attentive, Shankar began to tell the most beautiful story. The Lord lifted Hanuman, pressed him to His heart, and seated him very close, holding his hand.
essence: Devotion is answered by being brought close, not kept apart.
simple_meaning: Shiva grows attentive and continues the story, while Ram lifts Hanuman, holds him to His heart, and seats him beside Him in deep closeness.
insight: It shifts devotion from effort alone to intimate mutual presence.
modern_relevance: You finally tell someone the truth you've been carrying, and instead of pulling away, they move closer and listen fully. That is the kind of welcome this verse holds.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: कहु कपि रावन पालित लंका। केहि बिधि दहेउ दुर्ग अति बंका॥ प्रभु प्रसन्न जाना हनुमाना। बोला बचन बिगत अभिमाना ॥
translation: हे हनुमान् ! बताओ तो, रावण के द्वारा सुरक्षित लंका और उसके बड़े बाँके किले को तुमने किस तरह जलाया? हनुमान् जी ने प्रभु को प्रसन्न जाना और वे अभिमानरहित वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: Tell me, monkey, how did you burn Lanka, guarded by Ravana, and its vast, crooked fortress? Hanuman knew the Lord was pleased and spoke words free of pride.
essence: Great action stays pure when pride has no place in it.
simple_meaning: Shiva asks Hanuman how he burned Lanka, and Hanuman answers only after sensing Ram's pleasure, with no trace of pride.
insight: It shifts attention from celebrating your own feat to speaking only from humility and devotion.
modern_relevance: You finally finish the project everyone doubted. Before you start telling the story, you check whether you're speaking from gratitude or from ego.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: साखामग कै बड़ि मनुसाई। साखा तें साखा पर जाई॥ नाघि सिंधु हाटकपुर जारा। निसिचर गन बधि बिपिन उजारा ॥
translation: बंदर का बस, यही बड़ा पुरुषार्थ है कि वह एक डाल से दूसरी डाल पर चला जाता है। मैंने जो समुद्र लाँघकर सोने का नगर जलाया और राक्षसगण को मारकर अशोक वन को उजाड़ डाला, ॥
english_translation: The great feat of a monkey is to leap from branch to branch. I crossed the ocean, burned the golden city, killed the demon hosts, and cleared the grove.
essence: Great deeds lose their shine when you refuse to call them yours.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says his real monkey strength is leaping from branch to branch, and everything else he did came from Ram's grace.
insight: It turns achievement into offering, not self-display.
modern_relevance: You finish the hardest part of the project, and someone praises your brilliance. You know the truth: the real strength was never yours alone.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: सो सब तव प्रताप रघुराई। नाथ न कछू मोरि प्रभुताई ॥
translation: यह सब तो हे श्री रघुनाथजी! आप ही का प्रताप है। हे नाथ! इसमें मेरी प्रभुता (बड़ाई) कुछ भी नहीं है ॥
english_translation: All of that is your power, O Raghuvir. Lord, none of it is my own greatness.
essence: True power becomes devotion when you stop calling it your own.
simple_meaning: Hanuman gives all credit to Ram. He says the feat was possible only because of Ram's power, not his own greatness.
insight: It shifts credit away from the separate self and back toward the source of strength.
modern_relevance: You finish a project everyone praises, but you know the late-night help, the timing, and the support around you made it possible. Hanuman's response is the opposite of self-congratulation.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: ता कहुँ प्रभु कछु अगम नहिं जा पर तुम्ह अनुकूल। तव प्रभावँ बड़वानलहि जारि सकइ खलु तूल ॥
translation: हे प्रभु! जिस पर आप प्रसन्न हों, उसके लिए कुछ भी कठिन नहीं है। आपके प्रभाव से रूई (जो स्वयं बहुत जल्दी जल जाने वाली वस्तु है) बड़वानल को निश्चय ही जला सकती है (अर्थात् असंभव भी संभव हो सकता है) ॥
english_translation: For one who has your favor, nothing is impossible. By your power, even cotton can burn the ocean-fire.
essence: Ram's favor makes the impossible feel ordinary.
simple_meaning: When Ram is pleased, no task is too hard. His power can make even the impossible happen.
insight: It shifts you from self-credit to trust in a power beyond ego.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a task everyone says cannot be done — a broken relationship, a failed plan, a deadline that feels too big. This verse reminds you that support, grace, and alignment can change what effort alone cannot.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: नाथ भगति अति सुखदायनी। देहु कृपा करि अनपायनी॥ सुनि प्रभु परम सरल कपि बानी। एवमस्तु तब कहेउ भवानी ॥
translation: हे नाथ! मुझे अत्यंत सुख देने वाली अपनी निश्चल भक्ति कृपा करके दीजिए। हनुमान् जी की अत्यंत सरल वाणी सुनकर, हे भवानी! तब प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी ने 'एवमस्तु' (ऐसा ही हो) कहा ॥
english_translation: O Lord, grant me your unfailing devotion, the one that gives the highest joy. Hearing Hanuman's utterly simple words, O Uma, the Lord said, "So be it."
essence: The purest request is for devotion itself.
simple_meaning: Hanuman asks Ram for unwavering devotion, saying it is the greatest source of joy. Ram is pleased by Hanuman's simple, sincere words and grants the request.
insight: It shifts desire from outer gain to inner devotion, showing that the highest gift is a steady bond with Ram.
modern_relevance: You finally get a chance to ask for what you want, and you stop reaching for status or control. What comes out is simpler: give me a heart that stays loyal.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: उमा राम सुभाउ जेहिं जाना। ताहि भजनु तजि भाव न आना॥ यह संबाद जासु उर आवा। रघुपति चरन भगति सोइ पावा ॥
translation: हे उमा! जिसने श्री रामजी का स्वभाव जान लिया, उसे भजन छोड़कर दूसरी बात ही नहीं सुहाती। यह स्वामी-सेवक का संवाद जिसके हृदय में आ गया, वही श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों की भक्ति पा गया ॥
english_translation: O Uma, whoever has understood Ram's nature finds no taste in anything except devotion. Whoever lets this exchange settle in the heart receives devotion at Raghupati's feet.
essence: Seeing Ram clearly makes every other desire fade.
simple_meaning: When you truly understand Ram's nature, devotion stops feeling like a duty and becomes the only thing your heart wants. Letting this truth settle inside brings devotion at his feet.
insight: It shifts devotion from effortful practice to the natural result of clear recognition.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm, kindness, and integrity quietly rearrange your priorities. After that, shallow thrills lose their pull, and loyalty starts to feel obvious.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सुनि प्रभु बचन कहहिं कपि बृंदा। जय जय जय कृपाल सुखकंदा॥ तब रघुपति कपिपतिहि बोलावा। कहा चलैं कर करहु बनावा ॥
translation: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर वानरगण कहने लगे- कृपालु आनंदकंद श्री रामजी की जय हो जय हो, जय हो! तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने कपिराज सुग्रीव को बुलाया और कहा- चलने की तैयारी करो ॥
english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, the monkey hosts cried, “Victory, victory to the compassionate, bliss-filled one!” Then Raghupati called the lord of the monkeys and said, “Get ready to depart.”
essence: Devotion becomes action the moment Ram gives the word.
simple_meaning: The monkeys rejoice when Ram speaks, and Ram tells Sugriva to prepare to move.
insight: It shifts the moment from celebration to decisive preparation.
modern_relevance: You get the message you were waiting for, and suddenly the room changes. Relief turns into motion, and everyone starts getting ready.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अब बिलंबु केह कारन कीजे। तुरंत कपिन्ह कहँ आयसु दीजे॥ कौतुक देखि सुमन बहु बरषी। नभ तें भवन चले सुर हरषी ॥
translation: अब विलंब किस कारण किया जाए। वानरों को तुरंत आज्ञा दो। (भगवान् की) यह लीला (रावणवध की तैयारी) देखकर, बहुत से फूल बरसाकर और हर्षित होकर देवता आकाश से अपने-अपने लोक को चले ॥
english_translation: Why delay any longer? Give the monkeys their orders at once. Seeing this divine play, many devas showered flowers and, delighted, returned to their own realms from the sky.
essence: The right moment has come; delay only breaks the momentum.
simple_meaning: There is no reason to wait now. The army should be sent immediately, and the devas, delighted by the divine play, shower flowers and leave.
insight: It shifts attention from waiting to immediate execution once the right moment has arrived.
modern_relevance: You’ve already gathered the team, checked the plan, and waited long enough at the door. At some point, delaying again only weakens what is ready to move.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कपिपति बेगि बोलाए आए जूथप जूथ। नाना बरन अतुल बल बानर भालु बरूथ ॥
translation: वानरराज सुग्रीव ने शीघ्र ही वानरों को बुलाया, सेनापतियों के समूह आ गए। वानर-भालुओं के झुंड अनेक रंगों के हैं और उनमें अतुलनीय बल है ॥
english_translation: Sugriva quickly summoned the monkey chiefs, and the troop leaders arrived. The monkey and bear bands were of many colors and had unmatched strength.
essence: A mission begins when many strengths gather at once.
simple_meaning: Sugriva quickly calls the leaders, and the monkey and bear armies gather in many colors and great strength.
insight: It shows how decisive leadership turns scattered allies into a ready force.
modern_relevance: A group chat lights up, and within minutes the right people are on the road, carrying tools, snacks, and urgency. Big work moves when everyone answers at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु पद पंकज नावहिं सीसा। गर्जहिं भालु महाबल कीसा॥ देखी राम सकल कपि सेना। चितइ कृपा करि राजिव नैना ॥
translation: वे प्रभु के चरण कमलों में सिर नवाते हैं। महान् बलवान् रीछ और वानर गरज रहे हैं। श्री रामजी ने वानरों की सारी सेना देखी। तब कमल नेत्रों से कृपापूर्वक उनकी ओर दृष्टि डाली ॥
english_translation: They bow their heads at the Lord's lotus feet. The mighty bears and monkeys roar. Seeing the whole monkey army, Ram looked upon them with compassionate lotus eyes.
essence: Strength becomes complete when it meets compassionate regard.
simple_meaning: The monkey and bear army bows to Ram, roars with strength, and Ram looks at them with kindness.
insight: It shifts attention from raw force to the grace that gathers and directs it.
modern_relevance: Before the team walks into the big presentation, everyone is keyed up and ready. The strongest person in the room still needs to be seen with kindness, not just used for their power.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम कृपा बल पाइ कपिंदा। भए पच्छजुत मनहुँ गिरिंदा॥ हरषि राम तब कीन्ह पयाना। सगुन भए सुंदर सुभ नाना ॥
translation: राम कृपा का बल पाकर श्रेष्ठ वानर मानो पंखवाले बड़े पर्वत हो गए। तब श्री रामजी ने हर्षित होकर प्रस्थान (कूच) किया। अनेक सुंदर और शुभ शकुन हुए ॥
english_translation: Having received the strength of Ram's grace, the chief monkeys became like great mountains with wings. Then Ram set out in joy, and many beautiful, auspicious signs appeared.
essence: Grace makes small strength feel mountain-sized.
simple_meaning: Ram's grace gives the monkeys such strength that they seem like winged mountains. Then Ram departs happily, and auspicious signs appear everywhere.
insight: It shifts attention from personal ability to the empowering force behind it.
modern_relevance: A team walks into a hard meeting after weeks of preparation. The room still feels heavy, but something bigger than nerves is carrying them now.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जासु सकल मंगलमय कीती। तासु पयान सगुन यह नीती॥ प्रभु पयान जाना बैदेहीं। फरकि बाम अँग जनु कहि देहीं ॥
translation: जिनकी कीर्ति सब मंगलों से पूर्ण है, उनके प्रस्थान के समय शकुन होना, यह नीति है (लीला की मर्यादा है)। प्रभु का प्रस्थान जानकीजी ने भी जान लिया। उनके बाएँ अंग फड़क-फड़ककर मानो कहे देते थे (कि श्री रामजी आ रहे हैं) ॥
english_translation: For one whose fame is full of every blessing, auspicious signs accompany departure by nature. Janaki knew the Lord was leaving; her left side fluttered as if announcing his arrival.
essence: Ram's presence is so complete that even departure feels auspicious.
simple_meaning: Ram's departure is naturally accompanied by auspicious signs. Sita senses his leaving immediately, and even her body seems to announce his arrival.
insight: It teaches you to notice how deep connection can be felt before it is explained.
modern_relevance: You are halfway across the city when your phone buzzes and you already know who it is. Some people carry a presence that announces itself before they arrive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जोइ जोइ सगुन जानकिहि होई। असगुन भयउ रावनहिं सोई॥ चला कटकु को बरनैं पारा। गर्जहिं बानर भालु अपारा ॥
translation: जानकीजी को जो-जो शकुन होते थे, वही-वही रावण के लिए अपशकुन हुए। सेना चली, उसका वर्णन कौन कर सकता है? असंख्य वानर और भालू गर्जना कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Whatever signs were auspicious for Sita became inauspicious for Ravana. The army marched on—who could describe it? Countless monkeys and bears roared.
essence: One event can become blessing or warning depending on your side.
simple_meaning: What is lucky for Sita becomes a bad sign for Ravana. Then the army moves forward, with countless monkeys and bears roaring loudly.
insight: It frames the march to battle as a turning point where fate favors dharma and unsettles ego.
modern_relevance: A room can feel like victory to one person and warning to another. The same meeting, the same news, the same moment lands very differently depending on what you stand for.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नख आयुध गिरि पादपधारी। चले गगन महि इच्छाचारी॥ केहरिनाद भालु कपि करहीं। डगमगाहिं दिग्गज चिक्करहीं ॥
translation: नख ही जिनके शस्त्र हैं, वे इच्छानुसार (सर्वत्र बेरोक-टोक) चलने वाले रीछ-वानर पर्वतों और वृक्षों को धारण किए कोई आकाश मार्ग से और कोई पृथ्वी पर चले जा रहे हैं। वे सिंह के समान गर्जना कर रहे हैं। (उनके चलने और गर्जने से) दिशाओं के हाथी विचलित होकर चिंग्घाड़ रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Their only weapons are their nails; they carry mountains and trees. Some move through the sky, some across the earth, all at will. The bears and monkeys roar like lions, and the elephants of the directions tremble and cry out.
essence: Power is already moving before the fight begins.
simple_meaning: The monkey and bear army moves in wild force, carrying mountains and trees, roaring so loudly that even the directions tremble.
insight: It heightens the sense of collective momentum, preparing the reader for the battle that follows.
modern_relevance: A stadium erupts before the final play, and the noise rolls through your chest. Before anything has even happened, you can feel a turning point arriving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चिक्करहिं दिग्गज डोल महि गिरि लोल सागर खरभरे। मन हरष सभ गंधर्ब सुर मुनि नाग किंनर दुख टरे॥ कटकटहिं मर्कट बिकट भट बहु कोटि कोटिन्ह धावहीं। जय राम प्रबल प्रताप कोसलनाथ गुन गन गावहीं ॥
translation: दिशाओं के हाथी चिंग्घाड़ने लगे, पृथ्वी डोलने लगी, पर्वत चंचल हो गए (काँपने लगे) और समुद्र खलबला उठे। गंधर्व, देवता, मुनि, नाग, किन्नर सब के सब मन में हर्षित हुए' कि (अब) हमारे दुःख टल गए। अनेकों करोड़ भयानक वानर योद्धा कटकटा रहे हैं और करोड़ों ही दौड़ रहे हैं। 'प्रबल प्रताप कोसलनाथ श्री रामचंद्रजी की जय हो' ऐसा पुकारते हुए वे उनके गुणसमूहों को गा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The guardian elephants of the directions cried out, the earth shook, the mountains trembled, and the ocean churned. Gandharvas, radiant beings, sages, serpents, and kinnaras rejoiced that their suffering had ended. Countless fierce monkey-warriors roared and rushed forward by the millions, singing the glory of the mighty Lord of Kosala, Ram.
essence: Ram's arrival makes the whole world feel alive with victory.
simple_meaning: Nature and the heavenly beings react as Ram's army advances. The world shakes with the force of the march, while the warriors sing Ram's praise.
insight: It turns a march into a public hymn, showing that true force carries devotion, not just power.
modern_relevance: A stadium erupts, the floor vibrates, and a whole crowd starts chanting one name together. You can feel how shared conviction turns motion into momentum.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सहि सक न भार उदार अहिपति बार बारहिं मोहई। गह दसन पुनि पुनि कमठ पृष्ठ कठोर सो किमि सोहई॥ रघुबीर रुचिर प्रयान प्रस्थिति जानि परम सुहावनी। जनु कमठ खर्पर सर्पराज सो लिखत अबिचल पावनी ॥
translation: उदार (परम श्रेष्ठ एवं महान् ) सर्पराज शेषजी भी सेना का बोझ नहीं सह सकते, वे बार-बार मोहित हो जाते (घबड़ा जाते) हैं और पुनः-पुनः कच्छप की कठोर पीठ को दाँतों से पकड़ते हैं। ऐसा करते (अर्थात् बार-बार दाँतों को गड़ाकर कच्छप की पीठ पर लकीर सी खींचते हुए) वे कैसे शोभा दे रहे हैं मानो श्री रामचंद्रजी की सुंदर प्रस्थान यात्रा को परम सुहावनी जानकर उसकी अचल पवित्र कथा को सर्पराज शेषजी कच्छप की पीठ पर लिख रहे हों ॥
english_translation: The noble king of serpents cannot bear the army's weight; again and again he is bewildered. He bites the tortoise's back, and how does that hard back look beautiful? It is as if, knowing the exquisitely lovely march of Raghubir, the serpent king Shesha is writing that immovable, holy account on the tortoise's shell.
essence: Even the cosmos tries to preserve Ram's departure as holy memory.
simple_meaning: Shesha, the king of serpents, is overwhelmed by Ram's grand departure. The verse imagines him marking that holy event on the tortoise's back, as if preserving its beauty forever.
insight: It turns a physical image into devotion, showing how cosmic beings witness Ram's movement as sacred history.
modern_relevance: You watch a loved one leave for a life-changing journey, and you know words will never hold it. So you remember it in fragments, photos, and tiny rituals.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि बिधि जाइ कृपानिधि उतरे सागर तीर। जहँ तहँ लागे खान फल भालु बिपुल कपि बीर ॥
translation: इस प्रकार कृपानिधान श्री रामजी समुद्र तट पर जा उतरे। अनेकों रीछ-वानर वीर जहाँ-तहाँ फल खाने लगे ॥
english_translation: In this way, the gracious one reached the shore of the ocean. There, the bears and many monkey warriors began eating fruit wherever they could.
essence: Even after a great advance, the army pauses for ordinary relief.
simple_meaning: Ram reaches the ocean shore, and the bear and monkey warriors spread out to eat fruit.
insight: It marks a pause in the journey, not the end of the mission.
modern_relevance: You finally arrive after a long drive, drop your bags, and reach for the first snack you can find. The body needs its small relief before the next hard thing begins.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उहाँ निसाचर रहहिं ससंका। जब तें जारि गयउ कपि लंका॥ निज निज गृहँ सब करहिं बिचारा। नहिं निसिचर कुल केर उबारा।1॥
translation: वहाँ (लंका में) जब से हनुमान् जी लंका को जलाकर गए, तब से राक्षस भयभीत रहने लगे। अपने-अपने घरों में सब विचार करते हैं कि अब राक्षस कुल की रक्षा (का कोई उपाय) नहीं है ॥
english_translation: After Hanuman burned Lanka, the night-dwellers lived in fear. In their own homes, they kept thinking there was no way to save their clan.
essence: A single fearless act can expose an entire kingdom’s weakness.
simple_meaning: Hanuman’s burning of Lanka leaves the night-dwellers terrified and worried that their clan has no protection left.
insight: It shifts attention from outward strength to the insecurity underneath it.
modern_relevance: A company’s biggest team player quits, and suddenly everyone in the building feels exposed. The real shock is not the loss itself, but the feeling that the old safety was never solid.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जासु दूत बल बरनि न जाई। तेहि आएँ पुर कवन भलाई॥ दूतिन्ह सन सुनि पुरजन बानी। मंदोदरी अधिक अकुलानी ॥
translation: जिसके दूत का बल वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता, उसके स्वयं नगर में आने पर कौन भलाई है (हम लोगों की बड़ी बुरी दशा होगी)? दूतियों से नगरवासियों के वचन सुनकर मंदोदरी बहुत ही व्याकुल हो गई ॥
english_translation: The strength of that messenger cannot even be described. If he himself has come to the city, what good can possibly remain? Hearing the city's words from the female messengers, Mandodari became deeply distressed.
essence: When the messenger is unstoppable, the city’s fear is justified.
simple_meaning: Mandodari hears that Hanuman is a messenger so powerful that his strength cannot be described. His arrival inside Lanka feels like a sign that disaster is already at the door.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary alarm to the recognition that a decisive force has already entered the scene.
modern_relevance: You hear that the one person who already exposed every weakness is walking into the meeting. Suddenly everyone in the room knows the situation has changed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रहसि जोरि कर पति पग लागी। बोली बचन नीति रस पागी॥ कंत करष हरि सन परिहरहू। मोर कहा अति हित हियँ धरहू ॥
translation: वह एकांत में हाथ जोड़कर पति (रावण) के चरणों लगी और नीतिरस में पगी हुई वाणी बोली- हे प्रियतम! श्री हरि से विरोध छोड़ दीजिए। मेरे कहने को अत्यंत ही हितकर जानकर हृदय में धारण कीजिए ॥
english_translation: In private, she joined her hands and fell at her husband's feet. Filled with wise feeling, she spoke: “Dear one, give up hostility toward Hari. Take my words as deeply beneficial and keep them in your heart.”
essence: True care tells you to drop the fight that is destroying you.
simple_meaning: Mandodari privately begs Ravana to stop opposing Ram and to take her warning seriously as loving, useful counsel.
insight: It teaches you to recognise wise counsel as an act of care, not control.
modern_relevance: You watch a friend double down on a choice that is clearly breaking their life. Speaking gently may be the most loving thing you can do, even if they resist it.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: समुझत जासु दूत कइ करनी। स्रवहिं गर्भ रजनीचर घरनी॥ तासु नारि निज सचिव बोलाई। पठवहु कंत जो चहहु भलाई ॥
translation: जिनके दूत की करनी का विचार करते ही (स्मरण आते ही) राक्षसों की स्त्रियों के गर्भ गिर जाते हैं, हे प्यारे स्वामी! यदि भला चाहते हैं, तो अपने मंत्री को बुलाकर उसके साथ उनकी स्त्री को भेज दीजिए ॥
english_translation: Just thinking of what this messenger has done makes the women of the demon households miscarry. Dear lord, if you want what is good, call your minister and send his wife along with him.
essence: Ignoring a clear warning only makes the fall harder.
simple_meaning: Even the memory of this messenger's power is terrifying. Mandodari urges Ravana to send Sita back with his minister if he wants safety.
insight: It shows how ego blocks clear seeing, even when the threat is already undeniable.
modern_relevance: You keep dismissing the warning signs because admitting them would bruise your pride. Someone close to you sees the danger first and begs you to act before the damage spreads.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: तव कुल कमल बिपिन दुखदाई। सीता सीत निसा सम आई॥ सुनहु नाथ सीता बिनु दीन्हें। हित न तुम्हार संभु अज कीन्हें ॥
translation: सीता आपके कुल रूपी कमलों के वन को दुःख देने वाली जाड़े की रात्रि के समान आई है। हे नाथ। सुनिए, सीता को दिए (लौटाए) बिना शम्भु और ब्रह्मा के किए भी आपका भला नहीं हो सकता ॥
english_translation: Sita has come like a winter night, bringing sorrow to your lotus-forest of a lineage. Listen, lord: without giving Sita back, even Shiva and Brahma cannot bring you true welfare.
essence: No blessing can grow from a stolen wrong.
simple_meaning: Mandodari warns Ravana that Sita has brought sorrow to his family line, and no blessing can come until he returns her.
insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to a wrongful gain toward restoring what was taken.
modern_relevance: You know the feeling of winning something and then sleeping badly because you got it the wrong way. The relief does not come from defending the mistake. It comes from undoing it.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: राम बान अहि गन सरिस निकर निसाचर भेक। जब लगि ग्रसत न तब लगि जतनु करहु तजि टेक ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के बाण सर्पों के समूह के समान हैं और राक्षसों के समूह मेंढक के समान। जब तक वे इन्हें ग्रस नहीं लेते (निगल नहीं जाते) तब तक हठ छोड़कर उपाय कर लीजिए ॥
english_translation: Ram's arrows are like a flock of snakes, and the demons are like frogs. Before they are swallowed up, abandon stubbornness and make peace with what must be done.
essence: Stubbornness only makes the blow harder to bear.
simple_meaning: Ram's power is overwhelming. The wise response is not stubbornness, but quick, practical action before destruction arrives.
insight: It shifts you from prideful resistance to timely, practical response.
modern_relevance: You keep arguing in a text thread long after the room has already turned against you. The smarter move is to stop defending your ego and deal with the real problem.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: श्रवन सुनी सठ ता करि बानी। बिहसा जगत बिदित अभिमानी॥ सभय सुभाउ नारि कर साचा। मंगल महुँ भय मन अति काचा ॥
translation: मूर्ख और जगत प्रसिद्ध अभिमानी रावण कानों से उसकी वाणी सुनकर खूब हँसा (और बोला-) स्त्रियों का स्वभाव सचमुच ही बहुत डरपोक होता है। मंगल में भी भय करती हो। तुम्हारा मन (हृदय) बहुत ही कच्चा (कमजोर) है ॥
english_translation: The arrogant Ravana, famous across the world, heard her words and laughed. He said, 'Women are naturally timid. Even in a place of good fortune, you are afraid. Your heart is very weak.'
essence: Pride laughs at what it cannot understand.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Sita's fear and dismisses her courage as weakness. His pride blinds him to her strength and to the danger closing in on him.
insight: It shows how ego turns a warning into a joke and blocks clear seeing.
modern_relevance: Someone dismisses your concern in a meeting with a smirk, calling you overreactive. The real issue is not your fear — it's their refusal to see what is already obvious.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: जौं आवइ मर्कट कटकाई। जिअहिं बिचारे निसिचर खाई॥ कंपहिं लोकप जाकीं त्रासा। तासु नारि सभीत बड़ि हासा ॥
translation: यदि वानरों की सेना आवेगी तो बेचारे राक्षस उसे खाकर अपना जीवन निर्वाह करेंगे। लोकपाल भी जिसके डर से काँपते हैं, उसकी स्त्री डरती हो, यह बड़ी हँसी की बात है ॥
english_translation: If the monkey army comes, the poor demons will have to eat them to stay alive. The wife of one whom even the guardians of the worlds fear—how could she possibly be afraid? What a joke.
essence: Pride turns warning into a joke and blinds you to danger.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Hanuman's threat. He says the monkey army is so small that the demons could swallow it, and Sita could never be afraid of someone who frightens even the guardians of the worlds.
insight: It shows how pride distorts judgment, making real danger seem laughable until it is too late.
modern_relevance: You brush off the warning because the problem looks too small to matter. Then it grows teeth, and your confidence was the first thing it ate.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: अस कहि बिहसि ताहि उर लाई। चलेउ सभाँ ममता अधिकाई॥ फमंदोदरी हृदयँ कर चिंता। भयउ कंत पर बिधि बिपरीता ॥
translation: रावण ने ऐसा कहकर हँसकर उसे हृदय से लगा लिया और ममता बढ़ाकर (अधिक स्नेह दर्शाकर) वह सभा में चला गया। मंदोदरी हृदय में चिंता करने लगी कि पति पर विधाता प्रतिकूल हो गए ॥
english_translation: Ravana said this, laughed, and drew her close to his chest. Then, with even more affection, he went back to the court. Mandodari felt worry in her heart: fate had turned against her husband.
essence: Pride keeps smiling even as ruin begins.
simple_meaning: Ravana laughs off the warning, holds Mandodari close, and returns to the court. She alone feels the unease: something has already turned against him.
insight: It shows how ego can stay cheerful while reality is already closing in.
modern_relevance: You brush off the one warning that matters, smile through it, and walk back into the meeting pretending nothing is wrong. Someone beside you can already feel the collapse coming.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बैठेउ सभाँ खबरि असि पाई। सिंधु पार सेना सब आई॥ बूझेसि सचिव उचित मत कहहू। ते सब हँसे मष्ट करि रहहू ॥
translation: ज्यों ही वह सभा में जाकर बैठा, उसने ऐसी खबर पाई कि शत्रु की सारी सेना समुद्र के उस पार आ गई है, उसने मंत्रियों से पूछा कि उचित सलाह कहिए (अब क्या करना चाहिए?)। तब वे सब हँसे और बोले कि चुप किए रहिए (इसमें सलाह की कौन सी बात है?) ॥
english_translation: As soon as he sat in the assembly, he received the news that the entire army had crossed the ocean. He asked his ministers for proper advice, and they all laughed and said, 'Stay quiet—what advice is there in this?'
essence: A ruler in denial cannot summon wise counsel.
simple_meaning: Ravana hears that the enemy has crossed the ocean and asks for advice, but his ministers mock the situation instead of helping.
insight: It shows how denial in leadership turns danger into disaster.
modern_relevance: You finally open the group chat after a crisis hits, hoping someone has a plan. Instead, everyone jokes, deflects, and pretends the problem will vanish.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जितेहु सुरासुर तब श्रम नाहीं। नर बानर केहि लेखे माहीं ॥
translation: आपने देवताओं और राक्षसों को जीत लिया, तब तो कुछ श्रम ही नहीं हुआ। फिर मनुष्य और वानर किस गिनती में हैं? ॥
english_translation: You conquered gods and demons without strain. What are humans and monkeys to you?
essence: Victory can become the reason you misjudge the next threat.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that Hanuman and the vanara army are nothing compared with the beings he has already defeated.
insight: It exposes the blindness of ego: past success can make you underestimate the next challenge.
modern_relevance: You brush off a problem because last month’s crisis felt worse. That same dismissal is often how bigger trouble slips in unnoticed.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सचिव बैद गुर तीनि जौं प्रिय बोलहिं भय आस राज धर्म तन तीनि कर होइ बेगिहीं नास ॥
translation: मंत्री, वैद्य और गुरु- ये तीन यदि (अप्रसन्नता के) भय या (लाभ की) आशा से (हित की बात न कहकर) प्रिय बोलते हैं (ठकुर सुहाती कहने लगते हैं), तो (क्रमशः) राज्य, शरीर और धर्म- इन तीन का शीघ्र ही नाश हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: If ministers, doctors, and teachers speak only what is pleasing out of fear or hope of gain, then kingdom, body, and dharma quickly fall apart.
essence: Pleasing words from trusted guides can quietly ruin everything.
simple_meaning: People who should guide you must tell the truth, not just what feels nice. When they speak to please fear or gain, leadership, health, and right conduct suffer.
insight: It teaches you to value truthful counsel over comfort, because false kindness can become a form of harm.
modern_relevance: A manager tells the team everything is fine because she wants the room to stay calm. A doctor avoids the hard warning. A mentor sugarcoats the feedback. The problem grows quietly while everyone feels reassured.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सोइ रावन कहुँ बनी सहाई। अस्तुति करहिं सुनाइ सुनाई॥ अवसर जानि बिभीषनु आवा। भ्राता चरन सीसु तेहिं नावा ॥
translation: रावण के लिए भी वही सहायता (संयोग) आ बनी है। मंत्री उसे सुना-सुनाकर (मुँह पर) स्तुति करते हैं। (इसी समय) अवसर जानकर विभीषणजी आए। उन्होंने बड़े भाई के चरणों में सिर नवाया ॥
english_translation: The same support had come to Ravana as well. His ministers kept praising him to his face. Just then, seeing the right moment, Vibhishana arrived and bowed his head at his elder brother's feet.
essence: Flattery surrounds power; humility arrives with the truth.
simple_meaning: Ravana is surrounded by flattering ministers, and at the right moment Vibhishana arrives and bows to his brother.
insight: It sets up the contrast between flattering speech and truthful surrender before Vibhishana speaks.
modern_relevance: A meeting where everyone is saying what the boss wants to hear, and one person finally walks in with honesty. The room changes the moment sincerity enters.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि सिरु नाइ बैठ निज आसन। बोला बचन पाइ अनुसासन॥ जौ कृपाल पूँछिहु मोहि बाता। मति अनुरूप कहउँ हित ताता ॥
translation: फिर से सिर नवाकर अपने आसन पर बैठ गए और आज्ञा पाकर ये वचन बोले- हे कृपाल जब आपने मुझसे बात (राय) पूछी ही है, तो हे तात! मैं अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार आपके हित की बात कहता हूँ- ॥
english_translation: He bowed his head again, sat on his own seat, and then spoke after receiving permission: “If you, O gracious one, ask me for advice, then, father, I will speak what I think is for your good.”
essence: Respect opens the door for honest counsel.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana bows respectfully, takes his seat, and says he will speak honestly for Ravana's good if asked.
insight: It teaches you to offer counsel only after permission, and to keep it aligned with what is actually helpful.
modern_relevance: You finally get a chance to speak in a tense family meeting, and everyone expects a safe answer. This verse is the courage to be respectful without becoming false.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: जो आपन चाहै कल्याना। सुजसु सुमति सुभ गति सुख नाना॥ सो परनारि लिलार गोसाईं। तजउ चउथि के चंद कि नाईं ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य अपना कल्याण, सुंदर यश, सुबुद्धि, शुभ गति और नाना प्रकार के सुख चाहता हो, वह हे स्वामी! परस्त्री के ललाट को चौथ के चंद्रमा की तरह त्याग दे (अर्थात् जैसे लोग चौथ के चंद्रमा को नहीं देखते, उसी प्रकार परस्त्री का मुख ही न देखे) ॥
english_translation: One who wants well-being, good fame, right understanding, auspicious progress, and many kinds of happiness should, O lord, avoid another man's wife as one avoids the moon on the fourth night.
essence: What you refuse in private shapes everything you become.
simple_meaning: Real well-being, good name, clear judgment, and lasting happiness come from avoiding another man's wife.
insight: It shifts desire from indulgence to restraint, showing that discipline protects both reputation and inner clarity.
modern_relevance: You are scrolling late at night, and one tempting image could become a habit you hide from everyone. The verse says your future is shaped by what you refuse to entertain.
speaker: Bibhishana

verse_text: चौदह भुवन एक पति होई। भूत द्रोह तिष्टइ नहिं सोई॥ गुन सागर नागर नर जोऊ। अलप लोभ भल कहइ न कोऊ ॥
translation: चौदहों भुवनों का एक ही स्वामी हो, वह भी जीवों से वैर करके ठहर नहीं सकता (नष्ट हो जाता है) जो मनुष्य गुणों का समुद्र और चतुर हो, उसे चाहे थोड़ा भी लोभ क्यों न हो, तो भी कोई भला नहीं कहता ॥
english_translation: Even the ruler of the fourteen worlds cannot endure if he harms living beings. And even a wise, capable person is not praised if even a little greed remains.
essence: Greatness survives only when power stays kind and greed stays absent.
simple_meaning: No ruler can remain secure if he harms living beings. And no matter how capable someone is, even a little greed ruins their goodness.
insight: It shifts judgment from status to conduct: power must be humane, and talent must be free of greed.
modern_relevance: You get promoted, but the way you treat people in meetings starts turning cold. The title grows, yet respect quietly drains away. This verse sees that before anyone says it aloud.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: काम क्रोध मद लोभ सब नाथ नरक के पंथ। सब परिहरि रघुबीरहि भजहु भजहिं जेहि संत ॥
translation: हे नाथ! काम, क्रोध, मद और लोभ- ये सब नरक के रास्ते हैं, इन सबको छोड़कर श्री रामचंद्रजी को भजिए, जिन्हें संत (सत्पुरुष) भजते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Lord, desire, anger, pride, and greed are all paths to ruin. Leave them all behind and worship Raghubir, whom the saints worship.
essence: The saints escape ruin by turning away from the four poisons and toward Ram.
simple_meaning: Desire, anger, pride, and greed pull you toward ruin. Let them go and turn toward Ram, the one the saints worship.
insight: It shifts attention from feeding the four inner poisons to choosing a steadier refuge.
modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message and end up spiraling into comparison, irritation, and wanting more. The verse names that drift before it owns you, then points you back to what steadies you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तात राम नहिं नर भूपाला। भुवनेस्वर कालहु कर काला॥ ब्रह्म अनामय अज भगवंता। ब्यापक अजित अनादि अनंता ॥
translation: हे तात! राम मनुष्यों के ही राजा नहीं हैं। वे समस्त लोकों के स्वामी और काल के भी काल हैं। वे (संपूर्ण ऐश्वर्य, यश, श्री, धर्म, वैराग्य एवं ज्ञान के भंडार) भगवान् हैं, वे निरामय (विकाररहित), अजन्मे, व्यापक, अजेय, अनादि और अनंत ब्रह्म हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram is not merely a human king. He is the lord of all worlds, even the master of time itself. He is the flawless, unborn, all-pervading, unconquerable, beginningless, endless supreme reality.
essence: Ram is not limited by form, time, or defeat.
simple_meaning: Ram is not just a human ruler. He is the supreme reality itself: unborn, all-pervading, beyond change, beyond defeat, without beginning or end.
insight: It shifts devotion from a personal preference to recognition of Ram's boundless nature.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary at first, then realise they carry a steadiness that fear cannot shake. This verse names that deeper reality: the one you trust is larger than the whole mess around you.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: गो द्विज धेनु देव हितकारी। कृपा सिंधु मानुष तनुधारी॥ जन रंजन भंजन खल ब्राता। बेद धर्म रच्छक सुनु भ्राता ॥
translation: उन कृपा के समुद्र भगवान् ने पृथ्वी, ब्राह्मण, गो और देवताओं का हित करने के लिए ही मनुष्य शरीर धारण किया है। हे भाई! सुनिए, वे सेवकों को आनंद देने वाले, दुष्टों के समूह का नाश करने वाले और वेद तथा धर्म की रक्षा करने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: For the welfare of the earth, the learned, cows, and the radiant beings, the ocean of compassion took human form. Listen, brother: he delights his followers, destroys the company of the wicked, and protects the Vedas and dharma.
essence: Ram takes human form to protect, delight, and restore what is right.
simple_meaning: Ram took a human body to help the earth, the learned, cows, and the radiant beings. He brings joy to devotees, removes evil company, and protects dharma.
insight: It shifts you from seeing divinity as remote to seeing it as protective, practical, and close to human life.
modern_relevance: When someone shows up at 2 a.m. to help you move, then quietly fixes the broken lock before leaving, you feel what this verse points to: power that serves, not power that boasts.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ताहि बयरु तजि नाइअ माथा। प्रनतारति भंजन रघुनाथा॥ देहु नाथ प्रभु कहुँ बैदेही। भजहु राम बिनु हेतु सनेही ॥
translation: वैर त्यागकर उन्हें मस्तक नवाइए। वे श्री रघुनाथजी शरणागत का दुःख नाश करने वाले हैं। हे नाथ! उन प्रभु (सर्वेश्वर) को जानकीजी दे दीजिए और बिना ही कारण स्नेह करने वाले श्री रामजी को भजिए ॥
english_translation: Put aside hostility and bow your head to him. Raghunath destroys the suffering of those who take refuge. O Lord, give Janaki to that supreme Lord, and worship Ram, the loving one without cause.
essence: Ram answers surrender by ending suffering.
simple_meaning: Let go of enmity and bow to Ram. He removes the suffering of anyone who takes refuge in him, and he is loved without needing a reason.
insight: It shifts the mind from guarding against hurt to trusting that surrender can meet pain more cleanly than resistance.
modern_relevance: You finally stop rehearsing the argument before sending the message. Instead of protecting your pride, you choose the softer move that makes repair possible.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सरन गएँ प्रभु ताहु न त्यागा। बिस्व द्रोह कृत अघ जेहि लागा॥ जासु नाम त्रय ताप नसावन। सोइ प्रभु प्रगट समुझु जियँ रावन ॥
translation: जिसे संपूर्ण जगत् से द्रोह करने का पाप लगा है, शरण जाने पर प्रभु उसका भी त्याग नहीं करते। जिनका नाम तीनों तापों का नाश करने वाला है, वे ही प्रभु (भगवान् ) मनुष्य रूप में प्रकट हुए हैं। हे रावण! हृदय में यह समझ लीजिए ॥
english_translation: He does not abandon anyone who comes to him for refuge, even one burdened with the sin of betraying the whole world. His name removes the three kinds of suffering. Understand in your heart: that same Lord has appeared in human form, O Ravana.
essence: Surrender is stronger than your worst failure.
simple_meaning: Even someone burdened by terrible wrongdoing is not rejected if they seek refuge. Ram's name also removes the three kinds of suffering, showing that the Lord has come in human form.
insight: It shifts you from self-condemnation to surrender, and from judging others to recognising refuge as available.
modern_relevance: After a brutal argument, you replay the worst thing you said and assume the relationship is over. This verse says the door can still open if you truly come back humble.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बार बार पद लागउँ बिनय करउँ दससीस। परिहरि मान मोह मद भजहु कोसलाधीस॥39क॥ मुनि पुलस्ति निज सिष्य सन कहि पठई यह बात। तुरत सो मैं प्रभु सन कही पाइ सुअवसरु तात॥39ख॥
translation: हे दशशीश! मैं बार-बार आपके चरणों लगता हूँ और विनती करता हूँ कि मान, मोह और मद को त्यागकर आप कोसलपति श्री रामजी का भजन कीजिए ॥ मुनि पुलस्त्यजी ने अपने शिष्य के हाथ यह बात कहला भेजी है। हे तात! सुंदर अवसर पाकर मैंने तुरंत ही वह बात प्रभु (आप) से कह दी ॥
english_translation: "O ten-faced one, I bow to your feet again and again and beg you: give up pride, delusion, and arrogance, and worship the Lord of Kosala. The sage Pulastya sent this message through his disciple. O dear one, I quickly told that to the Lord at the right moment."
essence: Pride keeps you from the very refuge that could save you.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana begs Ravana to abandon pride, delusion, and arrogance and turn to Ram. He says he has passed this message along at the right moment.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to humble surrender before the divine.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that could save a friendship, but your own pride keeps editing it. This verse reminds you that timely honesty matters more than winning the argument.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: माल्यवंत अति सचिव सयाना। तासु बचन सुनि अति सुख माना॥ तात अनुज तव नीति बिभूषन। सो उर धरहु जो कहत बिभीषन ॥
translation: माल्यवान् नाम का एक बहुत ही बुद्धिमान मंत्री था। उसने उन (विभीषण) के वचन सुनकर बहुत सुख माना (और कहा-) हे तात! आपके छोटे भाई नीति विभूषण (नीति को भूषण रूप में धारण करने वाले अर्थात् नीतिमान् ) हैं। विभीषण जो कुछ कह रहे हैं उसे हृदय में धारण कर लीजिए ॥
english_translation: Malyavan, a very wise minister, heard his words and felt great joy. "Dear one, your younger brother is a jewel of good conduct. Hold in your heart what Vibhishana is saying."
essence: Wise words matter most when pride wants to throw them away.
simple_meaning: Malyavan recognizes Vibhishana's advice as wise and urges Ravana to take it seriously.
insight: It shifts you from defending your ego to receiving inconvenient truth.
modern_relevance: A friend texts you the hard truth after you have already decided to ignore it. The relief comes later, when you realize the honest voice was trying to save you from yourself.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रिपु उतकरष कहत सठ दोऊ। दूरि न करहु इहाँ हइ कोऊ॥ माल्यवंत गह गयउ बहोरी। कहइ बिभीषनु पुनि कर जोरी ॥
translation: (रावन ने कहा-) ये दोनों मूर्ख शत्रु की महिमा बखान रहे हैं। यहाँ कोई है? इन्हें दूर करो न! तब माल्यवान् तो घर लौट गया और विभीषणजी हाथ जोड़कर फिर कहने लगे- ॥
english_translation: The two fools keep praising the enemy's greatness. Is there no one here? Drive them away! Then Malyavan went back home, and Vibhishana again spoke with folded hands.
essence: Pride drives away the counsel that could still save you.
simple_meaning: Ravana angrily rejects advice that praises his enemy. Malyavan leaves, and Vibhishana continues pleading with folded hands.
insight: It shifts the mind from defending ego to listening for correction before damage hardens.
modern_relevance: You snap at the one person telling you the hard truth, then wonder why the situation keeps slipping. Pride often throws away the very warning that could have saved you.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सुमति कुमति सब कें उर रहहीं। नाथ पुरान निगम अस कहहीं॥ जहाँ सुमति तहँ संपति नाना। जहाँ कुमति तहँ बिपति निदाना ॥
translation: हे नाथ! पुराण और वेद ऐसा कहते हैं कि सुबुद्धि (अच्छी बुद्धि) और कुबुद्धि (खोटी बुद्धि) सबके हृदय में रहती है, जहाँ सुबुद्धि है, वहाँ नाना प्रकार की संपदाएँ (सुख की स्थिति) रहती हैं और जहाँ कुबुद्धि है वहाँ परिणाम में विपत्ति (दुःख) रहती है ॥
english_translation: Good and bad judgment both live in every heart. The Puranas and Vedas say this, O Lord. Where good judgment lives, many blessings gather; where bad judgment lives, disaster follows.
essence: Your life follows the judgment you choose to trust.
simple_meaning: Good and bad judgment both live in every heart. When clear judgment leads, life becomes fruitful; when confused judgment leads, trouble follows.
insight: It shifts attention from events outside you to the quality of discernment inside you.
modern_relevance: You know that moment when you ignore the quiet, sensible voice and choose the louder impulse instead. Hours later, the mess is not random — it grew from the judgment you fed.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: तव उर कुमति बसी बिपरीता। हित अनहित मानहु रिपु प्रीता॥ कालराति निसिचर कुल केरी। तेहि सीता पर प्रीति घनेरी ॥
translation: आपके हृदय में उलटी बुद्धि आ बसी है। इसी से आप हित को अहित और शत्रु को मित्र मान रहे हैं। जो राक्षस कुल के लिए कालरात्रि (के समान) हैं, उन सीता पर आपकी बड़ी प्रीति है ॥
english_translation: Your heart has been taken over by twisted judgment. That is why you call what helps you harmful, and what harms you friendly. For the race of demons, Sita is like the night of destruction, yet you feel deep affection for her.
essence: Desire can make ruin look like love.
simple_meaning: A corrupted mind reverses values: it mistakes harm for benefit and the enemy for a friend. Ravana’s desire for Sita is proof of that confusion.
insight: It shifts the mind from defending desire to checking whether desire has distorted judgment.
modern_relevance: You keep defending a relationship that keeps draining you. Everyone else can see the pattern, but your mind keeps calling it loyalty. This verse names that dangerous reversal.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: तात चरन गहि मागउँ राखहु मोर दुलार। सीता देहु राम कहुँ अहित न होइ तुम्हारा ॥
translation: हे तात! मैं चरण पकड़कर आपसे भीख माँगता हूँ (विनती करता हूँ)। कि आप मेरा दुलार रखिए (मुझ बालक के आग्रह को स्नेहपूर्वक स्वीकार कीजिए) श्री रामजी को सीताजी दे दीजिए, जिसमें आपका अहित न हो ॥
english_translation: O father, I hold your feet and beg you: keep my love for you. Give Sita to Ram, and no harm will come to you.
essence: Real care sometimes means asking someone to let go before ruin arrives.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana pleads with Ravana as a son and advisor: show affection, return Sita to Ram, and you will not suffer for it.
insight: It teaches you to speak truth with care, even when the other person may resist it.
modern_relevance: You know the conversation where a friend is about to lose everything, and you say the hard thing anyway. This is that moment: affection without honesty becomes cruelty.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: बुध पुरान श्रुति संमत बानी। कही बिभीषन नीति बखानी॥ सुनत दसानन उठा रिसाई। खल तोहिं निकट मृत्यु अब आई ॥
translation: विभीषण ने पंडितों, पुराणों और वेदों द्वारा सम्मत (अनुमोदित) वाणी से नीति बखानकर कही। पर उसे सुनते ही रावण क्रोधित होकर उठा और बोला कि रे दुष्ट! अब मृत्यु तेरे निकट आ गई है! ॥
english_translation: Vibhishana spoke words approved by the wise, the Puranas, and the Vedas, explaining right conduct. Hearing this, Ravana rose in anger and said, “Wretch, death is now near you!”
essence: Pride turns even wise counsel into a threat.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana speaks with support from respected wisdom traditions, but Ravana reacts with rage instead of listening.
insight: It teaches you to notice when defensiveness is blocking clear seeing.
modern_relevance: A friend calmly points out the mistake in your plan, and your chest tightens before they finish the sentence. The verse captures that instant when ego hears correction as attack.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जिअसि सदा सठ मोर जिआवा। रिपु कर पच्छ मूढ़ तोहि भावा॥ कहसि न खल अस को जग माहीं। भुज बल जाहि जिता मैं नाहीं ॥
translation: अरे मूर्ख! तू जीता तो है सदा मेरा जिलाया हुआ (अर्थात् मेरे ही अन्न से पल रहा है), पर हे मूढ़! पक्ष तुझे शत्रु का ही अच्छा लगता है। अरे दुष्ट! बता न, जगत् में ऐसा कौन है जिसे मैंने अपनी भुजाओं के बल से न जीता हो? ॥
english_translation: You fool, you live only because I keep you alive. You side with my enemy. Tell me, is there anyone in the world I have not conquered by my own strength?
essence: Ego boasts of control even while depending on others.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he keeps people alive, insults Vibhishana as foolish, and claims he has conquered everyone by his own strength.
insight: It exposes how ego turns every relationship into a contest and every warning into an insult.
modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in a meeting, then acts as if they alone built the whole project. The louder the boast, the more it hides dependence on others.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: मम पुर बसि तपसिन्ह पर प्रीती। सठ मिलु जाइ तिन्हहि कहु नीती॥ अस कहि कीन्हेसि चरन प्रहारा। अनुज गहे पद बारहिं बारा ॥
translation: मेरे नगर में रहकर प्रेम करता है तपस्वियों पर। मूर्ख! उन्हीं से जा मिल और उन्हीं को नीति बता। ऐसा कहकर रावण ने उन्हें लात मारी, परंतु छोटे भाई विभीषण ने (मारने पर भी) बार-बार उसके चरण ही पकड़े ॥
english_translation: Living in my city, you love ascetics. Fool, go join them and tell them your morals. Saying this, Ravana kicked him, but Vibhishana kept holding his brother's feet again and again.
essence: Loyalty can survive even when it is kicked away.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Vibhishana for loving holy people, kicks him, and Vibhishana still keeps clinging to his feet.
insight: It reveals the contrast between wounded pride and steady loyalty under attack.
modern_relevance: You try to speak calmly to someone who is already furious, and they lash out. The real test is whether your care survives their contempt.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: उमा संत कइ इहइ बड़ाई। मंद करत जो करइ भलाई॥ तुम्ह पितु सरिस भलेहिं मोहि मारा। रामु भजें हित नाथ तुम्हारा ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! संत की यही बड़ाई (महिमा) है कि वे बुराई करने पर भी (बुराई करने वाले की) भलाई ही करते हैं। (विभीषणजी ने कहा-) आप मेरे पिता के समान हैं, मुझे मारा सो तो अच्छा ही किया, परंतु हे नाथ! आपका भला श्री रामजी को भजने में ही है ॥
english_translation: Uma, this is the greatness of the noble: even when harmed, they do good. You are like my father; striking me was for my good. But, Lord, your true welfare lies in worshipping Ram.
essence: True goodness keeps blessing even after being hurt, and points others to Ram.
simple_meaning: Noble people keep wishing well even after being hurt. Vibhishana says Ravana's blow was still for his good, and that real welfare comes from turning to Ram.
insight: It shifts you from reacting to injury toward answering with goodwill and spiritual clarity.
modern_relevance: Someone snaps at you in a family argument, then acts like nothing happened. Instead of matching their bitterness, you see the deeper opening: you can stay kind, and you can still point them toward what heals them.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: सचिव संग लै नभ पथ गयऊ। सबहि सुनाइ कहत अस भयऊ ॥
translation: (इतना कहकर) विभीषण अपने मंत्रियों को साथ लेकर आकाश मार्ग में गए और सबको सुनाकर वे ऐसा कहने लगे- ॥
english_translation: Taking his ministers along, Vibhishana went by the sky path and, making everyone hear it, began to speak thus.
essence: A private break becomes a public declaration.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana leaves with his ministers and goes into the sky, preparing to speak publicly.
insight: It frames the coming declaration as a public turning point, not a philosophical conclusion.
modern_relevance: You draft the message, then stop and decide to send it to the whole group. The real moment is not the typing — it is when you choose to say it out loud.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामु सत्यसंकल्प प्रभु सभा कालबस तोरि। मैं रघुबीर सरन अब जाउँ देहु जनि खोरि ॥
translation: श्री रामजी सत्य संकल्प एवं (सर्वसमर्थ) प्रभु हैं और (हे रावण) तुम्हारी सभा काल के वश है। अतः मैं अब श्री रघुवीर की शरण जाता हूँ, मुझे दोष न देना ॥
english_translation: Ram is the Lord whose resolve never fails, and your court is already under Time's control. I now go to the refuge of Raghubir; do not blame me for this.
essence: Surrender becomes clear when you see which side is already falling.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana says Ram always keeps his promise, while Ravana's court is doomed. So he leaves Ravana and seeks Ram's protection, asking not to be blamed.
insight: It shifts loyalty from a failing power structure to a refuge that can actually hold you.
modern_relevance: You are in a group chat where everyone is mocking the one person telling the truth. The atmosphere has gone rotten, and staying silent would mean joining it. Vibhishana shows the courage to leave and stand elsewhere.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: अस कहि चला बिभीषनु जबहीं। आयू हीन भए सब तबहीं॥ साधु अवग्या तुरत भवानी। कर कल्यान अखिल कै हानी ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर विभीषणजी ज्यों ही चले, त्यों ही सब राक्षस आयुहीन हो गए। (उनकी मृत्यु निश्चित हो गई)। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे भवानी! साधु का अपमान तुरंत ही संपूर्ण कल्याण की हानि (नाश) कर देता है ॥
english_translation: As soon as Vibhishana left, all the demons became lifeless. Then Shiva said to Parvati: the insult of a noble person quickly destroys all well-being.
essence: Disrespecting the noble destroys the very good you depend on.
simple_meaning: When Vibhishana departs, the demons lose their life-force. Shiva then warns Parvati that insulting a noble person instantly harms all that is good.
insight: It shifts you from casual disrespect to careful recognition of character and value.
modern_relevance: You mock the colleague who quietly keeps the team afloat, then wonder why the whole room feels colder. This verse says contempt has a cost long before anyone admits it.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: रावन जबहिं बिभीषन त्यागा। भयउ बिभव बिनु तबहिं अभागा॥ चलेउ हरषि रघुनायक पाहीं। करत मनोरथ बहु मन माहीं ॥
translation: रावण ने जिस क्षण विभीषण को त्यागा, उसी क्षण वह अभागा वैभव (ऐश्वर्य) से हीन हो गया। विभीषणजी हर्षित होकर मन में अनेकों मनोरथ करते हुए श्री रघुनाथजी के पास चले ॥
english_translation: The moment Ravana cast Vibhishana aside, he was left bereft of fortune. Vibhishana then walked joyfully toward Raghunath, holding many hopes in his heart.
essence: Pride loses everything the moment it rejects refuge.
simple_meaning: Ravana loses his greatness the instant he rejects Vibhishana. Vibhishana, by contrast, walks joyfully toward Ram, full of hope.
insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to status toward seeing refuge as real gain.
modern_relevance: The friend you dismissed finally stops trying to save the friendship, and only then do you realize what your pride cost you. The other person walks away lighter, not bitter.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखिहउँ जाइ चरन जलजाता। अरुन मृदुल सेवक सुखदाता॥ जे पद परसि तरी रिषनारी। दंडक कानन पावनकारी ॥
translation: (वे सोचते जाते थे-) मैं जाकर भगवान् के कोमल और लाल वर्ण के सुंदर चरण कमलों के दर्शन करूँगा, जो सेवकों को सुख देने वाले हैं, जिन चरणों का स्पर्श पाकर ऋषि पत्नी अहल्या तर गईं और जो दंडकवन को पवित्र करने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: I will go and behold the lotus feet—soft, red, and full of comfort for devotees. Those feet touched Ahalya and purified the Dandaka forest.
essence: Ram's feet are both tender refuge and transforming power.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana thinks of Ram's beautiful feet with devotion. He sees them as tender, freeing, and purifying—feet that liberated Ahalya and sanctified the Dandaka forest.
insight: It shifts devotion from abstract praise to a concrete longing for Ram's presence and grace.
modern_relevance: You leave a draining conversation and keep thinking about the one person whose presence steadies you. What you are really reaching for is not approval, but the kind of contact that restores you.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: जे पद जनकसुताँ उर लाए। कपट कुरंग संग धर धाए॥ हर उर सर सरोज पद जेई। अहोभाग्य मैं देखिहउँ तेई ॥
translation: जिन चरणों को जानकीजी ने हृदय में धारण कर रखा है, जो कपटमृग के साथ पृथ्वी पर (उसे पकड़ने को) दौड़े थे और जो चरणकमल साक्षात् शिवजी के हृदय रूपी सरोवर में विराजते हैं, मेरा अहोभाग्य है कि उन्हीं को आज मैं देखूँगा ॥
english_translation: The feet that Janaki holds in her heart, that ran across the earth with the deceptive deer, and that rest like lotus feet in Shiva's heart-lake — it is my great fortune to see those feet today.
essence: Ram's feet are precious because love has already claimed them.
simple_meaning: Hanuman feels blessed to see Ram's feet, which Sita holds in her heart and Shiva reveres. The verse turns a sight into a sacred privilege.
insight: It shifts attention from the object seen to the love already gathered around it.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone whose presence has steadied two people you trust most. The room feels different, because you know you are standing near what they have cherished for years.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: जिन्ह पायन्ह के पादुकन्हि भरतु रहे मन लाइ। ते पद आजु बिलोकिहउँ इन्ह नयनन्हि अब जाइ ॥
translation: जिन चरणों की पादुकाओं में भरतजी ने अपना मन लगा रखा है, अहा! आज मैं उन्हीं चरणों को अभी जाकर इन नेत्रों से देखूँगा ॥
english_translation: The feet whose sandals Bharat held in his heart — today I will go and see those very feet with these eyes.
essence: What your heart has cherished from afar can still become immediate.
simple_meaning: Hanuman feels joy that the feet Bharat revered through Ram's sandals are finally before him. He is eager to see with his own eyes what Bharat loved from afar.
insight: It shifts attention from secondhand devotion to direct encounter with what the heart has already trusted.
modern_relevance: You finally meet the mentor, place, or person you have admired only from stories. The anticipation is not curiosity alone — it is reverence meeting reality.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: ऐहि बिधि करत सप्रेम बिचारा। आयउ सपदि सिंदु एहिं पारा॥ कपिन्ह बिभीषनु आवत देखा। जाना कोउ रिपु दूत बिसेषा ॥
translation: इस प्रकार प्रेमसहित विचार करते हुए वे शीघ्र ही समुद्र के इस पार (जिधर श्री रामचंद्रजी की सेना थी) आ गए। वानरों ने विभीषण को आते देखा तो उन्होंने जाना कि शत्रु का कोई खास दूत है ॥
english_translation: Thinking in this loving way, he quickly crossed to the far shore of the ocean. The monkeys saw Vibhishana coming and thought, 'A special envoy from the enemy has arrived.'
essence: A new arrival can change the whole mood in an instant.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana crosses the ocean quickly, and the monkeys notice him as a suspicious messenger from the enemy side.
insight: It trains attention to read context before granting trust.
modern_relevance: A stranger walks into a tense room just after a major conflict. Everyone goes quiet, trying to read whether this person brings help, danger, or both.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ताहि राखि कपीस पहिं आए। समाचार सब ताहि सुनाए॥ कह सुग्रीव सुनहु रघुराई। आवा मिलन दसानन भाई ॥
translation: उन्हें (पहरे पर) ठहराकर वे सुग्रीव के पास आए और उनको सब समाचार कह सुनाए। सुग्रीव ने (श्री रामजी के पास जाकर) कहा- हे रघुनाथजी! सुनिए, रावण का भाई (आप से) मिलने आया है ॥
english_translation: They left him guarded and came to Sugriva, telling him everything. Sugriva said, “Listen, Raghunath: Ravana’s brother has come to meet you.”
essence: News reaches the right hands before the next move begins.
simple_meaning: Hanuman and the others report Vibhishana’s arrival to Sugriva, who then informs Ram that Ravana’s brother has come seeking an audience.
insight: It keeps attention on the chain of communication, not on interpretation or judgment.
modern_relevance: You get the message, check the facts, and pass it to the right person before anyone acts. That quiet relay can change everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह प्रभु सखा बूझिए काहा। कहइ कपीस सुनहु नरनाहा॥ जानि न जाइ निसाचर माया। कामरूप केहि कारन आया ॥
translation: प्रभु श्री रामजी ने कहा- हे मित्र! तुम क्या समझते हो (तुम्हारी क्या राय है)? वानरराज सुग्रीव ने कहा- हे महाराज! सुनिए, राक्षसों की माया जानी नहीं जाती। यह इच्छानुसार रूप बदलने वाला (छली) न जाने किस कारण आया है ॥
english_translation: Lord Ram said, 'Friend, what do you think?' Sugriva replied, 'Listen, king of men. The nature of a demon cannot be known. This shape-shifter has come for some hidden reason.'
essence: What looks friendly may still hide a dangerous purpose.
simple_meaning: Ram asks Sugriva for his opinion, and Sugriva warns that the shape-shifting enemy cannot be understood easily and may have come with a hidden purpose.
insight: It trains you to question appearances and seek the hidden motive before acting.
modern_relevance: A new person joins the group chat and seems helpful, but something feels off. You pause, ask for judgment, and do not rush into trust just because the surface looks friendly.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: भेद हमार लेन सठ आवा। राखिअ बाँधि मोहि अस भावा॥ सखा नीति तुम्ह नीकि बिचारी। मम पन सरनागत भयहारी ॥
translation: (जान पड़ता है) यह मूर्ख हमारा भेद लेने आया है, इसलिए मुझे तो यही अच्छा लगता है कि इसे बाँध रखा जाए। (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे मित्र! तुमने नीति तो अच्छी विचारी, परंतु मेरा प्रण तो है शरणागत के भय को हर लेना! ॥
english_translation: He has come to spy on us, you fool. It seems right to me to keep him bound. Friend, you have thought well about policy, but my vow is to remove the fear of anyone who has come seeking refuge.
essence: A surrendered one is protected, not punished.
simple_meaning: Ram says policy is not the highest rule here. Even if someone seems suspicious, a person who has come seeking shelter should be protected, not punished.
insight: It shifts you from suspicion-first thinking to refuge-first action.
modern_relevance: Someone shows up at your door after a mistake, scared and ashamed, and everyone else wants to shut them out. This verse asks whether you will choose caution or refuge.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनि प्रभु बचन हरष हनुमाना। सरनागत बच्छल भगवाना ॥
translation: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर हनुमान् जी हर्षित हुए (और मन ही मन कहने लगे कि) भगवान् कैसे शरणागतवत्सल (शरण में आए हुए पर पिता की भाँति प्रेम करने वाले) हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, Hanuman was delighted. The Lord is so loving to those who take refuge.
essence: Refuge is not weakness; it is where loving protection begins.
simple_meaning: Hanuman feels joyful hearing Ram's words and recognises that Ram lovingly protects anyone who seeks refuge in him.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to trust in loving surrender.
modern_relevance: You finally admit you need help, and instead of judgment, someone responds with warmth. That moment of being received is what Hanuman feels here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सरनागत कहुँ जे तजहिं निज अनहित अनुमानि। ते नर पावँर पापमय तिन्हहि बिलोकत हानि ॥
translation: (श्री रामजी फिर बोले-) जो मनुष्य अपने अहित का अनुमान करके शरण में आए हुए का त्याग कर देते हैं, वे पामर (क्षुद्र) हैं, पापमय हैं, उन्हें देखने में भी हानि है (पाप लगता है) ॥
english_translation: Those who abandon someone who has come seeking refuge, fearing harm to themselves, are wretched and stained by wrongdoing; even looking at them brings harm.
essence: Refuge loses meaning the moment fear overrides compassion.
simple_meaning: Anyone who turns away a person seeking refuge, just because they fear trouble, is acting shamefully and wrongly.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to sheltering the vulnerable.
modern_relevance: A friend shows up at your door after a breakup, scared and embarrassed, and you think about your own inconvenience. This verse asks whether your comfort matters more than their safety.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कोटि बिप्र बध लागहिं जाहू। आएँ सरन तजउँ नहिं ताहू॥ सनमुख होइ जीव मोहि जबहीं। जन्म कोटि अघ नासहिं तबहीं ॥
translation: जिसे करोड़ों ब्राह्मणों की हत्या लगी हो, शरण में आने पर मैं उसे भी नहीं त्यागता। जीव ज्यों ही मेरे सम्मुख होता है, त्यों ही उसके करोड़ों जन्मों के पाप नष्ट हो जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Even one burdened with the killing of millions of priests is not abandoned if that person comes in refuge. The moment a living being turns toward me, the sins of countless births are destroyed.
essence: Turning toward Ram erases what once seemed unerasable.
simple_meaning: No matter how heavy someone's past may be, coming in refuge changes everything. Turning toward Ram ends the burden of countless wrongs.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to the power of sincere turning and trust.
modern_relevance: You finally admit what you've done to a friend after months of avoiding their calls. The shame feels huge, but the first honest step toward repair matters more than the whole backstory.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: पापवंत कर सहज सुभाऊ। भजनु मोर तेहि भाव न काऊ॥ जौं पै दुष्ट हृदय सोइ होई। मोरें सनमुख आव कि सोई ॥
translation: पापी का यह सहज स्वभाव होता है कि मेरा भजन उसे कभी नहीं सुहाता। यदि वह (रावण का भाई) निश्चय ही दुष्ट हृदय का होता तो क्या वह मेरे सम्मुख आ सकता था? ॥
english_translation: A sinful person's natural tendency is that my devotion never pleases him. If he were truly cruel at heart, could he have come before me?
essence: Coming near Ram already shows the heart has not fully closed.
simple_meaning: A dishonest or cruel heart does not naturally enjoy devotion. Coming close to Ram itself shows some openness, not total evil.
insight: It shifts the mind from judging entry to noticing the seed of sincerity already present.
modern_relevance: You open a prayer app after months away, half out of habit and half out of longing. That mixed motive is not a failure — it may be the first crack in the wall.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: निर्मल मन जन सो मोहि पावा। मोहि कपट छल छिद्र न भावा॥ भेद लेन पठवा दससीसा। तबहुँ न कछु भय हानि कपीसा ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य निर्मल मन का होता है, वही मुझे पाता है। मुझे कपट और छल-छिद्र नहीं सुहाते। यदि उसे रावण ने भेद लेने को भेजा है, तब भी हे सुग्रीव! अपने को कुछ भी भय या हानि नहीं है ॥
english_translation: One with a pure mind finds me. I do not like deceit, trickery, or hidden flaws. Even if Ravana sent him to spy, Sugriva, you need not fear any harm.
essence: Ram is found by purity, not by clever disguise.
simple_meaning: A pure mind is what brings you close to Ram. He does not welcome deceit or hidden motives. Even a spy cannot shake the safety of sincere devotion.
insight: It shifts attention from strategic image-management to inner honesty and trust.
modern_relevance: You finally tell the truth in a relationship after weeks of careful half-sentences. The relief is immediate: what matters most is not polish, but whether your heart is clean.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जग महुँ सखा निसाचर जेते। लछिमनु हनइ निमिष महुँ तेते॥ जौं सभीत आवा सरनाईं। रखिहउँ ताहि प्रान की नाईं ॥
translation: क्योंकि हे सखे! जगत में जितने भी राक्षस हैं, लक्ष्मण क्षणभर में उन सबको मार सकते हैं और यदि वह भयभीत होकर मेरी शरण आया है तो मैं तो उसे प्राणों की तरह रखूँगा ॥
english_translation: O friend, all the demons in the world could be slain by Lakshman in a moment. But if he has come here in fear and sought refuge, I will protect him as I would my own life.
essence: Power becomes mercy when someone comes to you in fear.
simple_meaning: Ram says Lakshman could destroy all the demons quickly, but anyone who comes in fear and seeks refuge will be protected like life itself.
insight: It shifts you from threat-based judgment to refuge-based care.
modern_relevance: A stranger shows up at your door after a frightening night, shaking and ashamed. You do not ask what they deserve first. You decide whether you can be safe enough for them to rest.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: उभय भाँति तेहि आनहु हँसि कह कृपानिकेत। जय कृपाल कहि कपि चले अंगद हनू समेत ॥
translation: कृपा के धाम श्री रामजी ने हँसकर कहा- दोनों ही स्थितियों में उसे ले आओ। तब अंगद और हनुमान् सहित सुग्रीवजी 'कपालु श्री रामजी की जय हो' कहते हुए चले ॥
english_translation: Smiling, the abode of mercy said, "Bring him either way." Then Angad and Hanuman set out, crying, "Victory to the compassionate Lord," and went with Hanuman beside them.
essence: Compassion brings the seeker in before fear can turn them away.
simple_meaning: Ram says Vibhishana should be brought to him no matter which way it happens. Angad and Hanuman leave with joy and reverence.
insight: It shifts the mind from testing a seeker to receiving them with trust.
modern_relevance: Someone finally admits they need help, and you do not make them prove themselves first. You open the door, steady and unguarded, because mercy is stronger than doubt.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सादर तेहि आगें करि बानर। चले जहाँ रघुपति करुनाकर॥ दूरिहि ते देखे द्वौ भ्राता। नयनानंद दान के दाता ॥
translation: विभीषणजी को आदर सहित आगे करके वानर फिर वहाँ चले, जहाँ करुणा की खान श्री रघुनाथजी थे। नेत्रों को आनंद का दान देने वाले (अत्यंत सुखद) दोनों भाइयों को विभीषणजी ने दूर ही से देखा ॥
english_translation: Placing Vibhishana respectfully in front, the monkeys went on to where Raghupati, the compassionate one, was. From a distance, Vibhishana saw the two brothers, the givers of delight to the eyes.
essence: Respect opens the way before devotion speaks.
simple_meaning: The monkeys escort Vibhishana toward Ram, and Vibhishana sees Ram and Lakshman from afar.
insight: It shows how trust, introduction, and presence can create belonging before explanation.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room behind someone who has vouched for you, and the whole atmosphere changes before you say a word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरि राम छबिधाम बिलोकी। रहेउ ठटुकि एकटक पल रोकी॥ भुज प्रलंब कंजारुन लोचन। स्यामल गात प्रनत भय मोचन ॥
translation: फिर शोभा के धाम श्री रामजी को देखकर वे पलक (मारना) रोककर ठिठककर (स्तब्ध होकर) एकटक देखते ही रह गए। भगवान् की विशाल भुजाएँ हैं लाल कमल के समान नेत्र हैं और शरणागत के भय का नाश करने वाला साँवला शरीर है ॥
english_translation: Then he looked again at Ram's radiant form and stood still, eyes fixed without blinking. Ram's long arms, red-lotus eyes, and dark body free the sheltered from fear.
essence: Ram's beauty does what fear cannot: it makes you still and safe.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram's beauty leaves the devotee stunned and motionless. His form is not just beautiful; it brings fearlessness to anyone who seeks refuge in him.
insight: It shifts attention from judging appearance to recognising the peace a presence can carry.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm makes your own panic loosen. Nothing is said, but their presence feels safer than all your planning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सघ कंध आयत उर सोहा। आनन अमित मदन मन मोहा॥ नयन नीर पुलकित अति गाता। मन धरि धीर कही मृदु बाता ॥
translation: सिंह के से कंधे हैं, विशाल वक्षःस्थल (चौड़ी छाती) अत्यंत शोभा दे रहा है। असंख्य कामदेवों के मन को मोहित करने वाला मुख है। भगवान् के स्वरूप को देखकर विभीषणजी के नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया और शरीर अत्यंत पुलकित हो गया। फिर मन में धीरज धरकर उन्होंने कोमल वचन कहे ॥
english_translation: His lion-like shoulders and broad chest were beautiful. His face captivated countless Cupids. Seeing that form, Vibhishana's eyes filled with tears, his body thrilled with love, and then, steadying his mind, he spoke gently.
essence: Beauty worthy of reverence can steady a wavering heart.
simple_meaning: Ram's beauty overwhelms Vibhishana so deeply that he trembles with tears before speaking.
insight: It shows devotion as a bodily response first: tears, trembling, then gentle speech.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence silences you for a second — not because you're intimidated, but because something in you recognizes what is noble.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ दसानन कर मैं भ्राता। निसिचर बंस जनम सुरत्राता॥ सहज पापप्रिय तामस देहा। जथा उलूकहि तम पर नेहा ॥
translation: हे नाथ! मैं दशमुख रावण का भाई हूँ। हे देवताओं के रक्षक! मेरा जन्म राक्षस कुल में हुआ है। मेरा तामसी शरीर है, स्वभाव से ही मुझे पाप प्रिय हैं, जैसे उल्लू को अंधकार पर सहज स्नेह होता है ॥
english_translation: O Lord, I am the brother of ten-headed Ravana. I was born in the race of demons, O protector of the radiant beings. My body is born of darkness, and I naturally love what is evil, just as an owl loves the night.
essence: Honest surrender begins with admitting your own darkness.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana admits his dark lineage and flawed nature, comparing himself to an owl drawn to night. He is confessing his unworthiness before seeking Ram's protection.
insight: It teaches you to stop performing goodness and speak plainly from your real condition.
modern_relevance: After a relapse, you sit in your car outside the house and finally text, “I need help.” The honesty hurts, but it also opens the door.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: श्रवन सुजसु सुनि आयउँ प्रभु भंजन भव भीर। त्राहि त्राहि आरति हरन सरन सुखद रघुबीर ॥
translation: मैं कानों से आपका सुयश सुनकर आया हूँ कि प्रभु भव (जन्म-मरण) के भय का नाश करने वाले हैं। हे दुखियों के दुःख दूर करने वाले और शरणागत को सुख देने वाले श्री रघुवीर! मेरी रक्षा कीजिए, रक्षा कीजिए ॥
english_translation: I have come after hearing your glorious fame, O Lord who destroys the fear of worldly existence. O Raghubir, remover of suffering and giver of peace to those who seek refuge, protect me, protect me.
essence: Hearing Ram's name can bring you all the way home.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana comes to Ram after hearing of his fame and asks for protection. He trusts Ram as the one who ends fear and gives peace to anyone who takes refuge.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to open surrender. Help begins when you stop defending your isolation.
modern_relevance: After months of carrying everything alone, you finally call the one person who can actually help. You do not need a perfect explanation. You need refuge, and you ask for it plainly.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: अस कहि करत दंडवत देखा। तुरत उठे प्रभु हरष बिसेषा॥ दीन बचन सुनि प्रभु मन भावा। भुज बिसाल गहि हृदयँ लगावा ॥
translation: प्रभु ने उन्हें ऐसा कहकर दंडवत् करते देखा तो वे अत्यंत हर्षित होकर तुरंत उठे। विभीषणजी के दीन वचन सुनने पर प्रभु के मन को बहुत ही भाए। उन्होंने अपनी विशाल भुजाओं से पकड़कर उनको हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
english_translation: Seeing him prostrate like that, the Lord was filled with special joy and rose at once. Hearing Vibhishana's humble words, the Lord was pleased in heart. He took him in his broad arms and held him to his chest.
essence: Humility is enough to bring Ram into your arms.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana bows in complete surrender, and Ram responds with immediate joy, acceptance, and a loving embrace.
insight: It shifts the mind from earning acceptance to receiving it through sincerity and surrender.
modern_relevance: You finally tell the truth after weeks of pretending you were fine. Instead of judgment, someone listens and pulls you closer. That relief is the point.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अनुज सहित मिलि ढिग बैठारी। बोले बचन भगत भय हारी॥ कहु लंकेस सहित परिवारा। कुसल कुठाहर बास तुम्हारा ॥
translation: छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित गले मिलकर उनको अपने पास बैठाकर श्री रामजी भक्तों के भय को हरने वाले वचन बोले- हे लंकेश! परिवार सहित अपनी कुशल कहो। तुम्हारा निवास बुरी जगह पर है ॥
english_translation: Embracing him with Lakshman by his side, Ram seated him near himself and spoke words that remove a devotee's fear: “Tell me, Lord of Lanka, how are you and your family? You live in a bad place.”
essence: True welcome makes fear loosen at once.
simple_meaning: Ram welcomes Vibhishana kindly, sits him near himself, and speaks in a way that removes fear. He asks after Vibhishana’s well-being and notices the hardship of living in Lanka.
insight: It teaches you to meet sincere surrender with immediate warmth, not suspicion.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room already braced for judgment, and someone pulls out a chair beside them. Before any explanation, your shoulders drop. That is the kind of welcome Ram gives here.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: खल मंडली बसहु दिनु राती। सखा धरम निबहइ केहि भाँती॥ मैं जानउँ तुम्हारि सब रीती। अति नय निपुन न भाव अनीती ॥
translation: दिन-रात दुष्टों की मंडली में बसते हो। (ऐसी दशा में) हे सखे! तुम्हारा धर्म किस प्रकार निभता है? मैं तुम्हारी सब रीति (आचार-व्यवहार) जानता हूँ। तुम अत्यंत नीतिनिपुण हो, तुम्हें अनीति नहीं सुहाती ॥
english_translation: You live day and night among the wicked. Friend, how can your duty be upheld there? I know all your ways: you are deeply skilled in fairness, and injustice does not please you.
essence: Character weakens when you keep living inside corruption.
