simple_meaning: Bad company makes it hard to live rightly. Vibhishana is telling Ram that he knows Ram values fairness and cannot abide injustice.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated intention to the moral pressure of your environment.
modern_relevance: You keep showing up to a group chat where cruelty passes as humor. After a while, you notice your own voice changing. This verse names that slow drift before it hardens.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: बरु भल बास नरक कर ताता। दुष्ट संग जनि देइ बिधाता॥ अब पद देखि कुसल रघुराया। जौं तुम्ह कीन्हि जानि जन दाया ॥
translation: हे तात! नरक में रहना वरन् अच्छा है, परंतु विधाता दुष्ट का संग (कभी) न दे। (विभीषणजी ने कहा-) हे रघुनाथजी! अब आपके चरणों का दर्शन कर कुशल से हूँ, जो आपने अपना सेवक जानकर मुझ पर दया की है ॥
english_translation: It is better, dear one, to live in hell than to keep company with the wicked. Now that I have seen the feet of Raghunath, I am well, because you have shown mercy to me, knowing me as your servant.
essence: The right company can feel better than comfort itself.
simple_meaning: Bad company is worse than any hardship. Vibhishana says he feels well now because he has seen Ram and received his mercy.
insight: It shifts the mind from tolerating harmful company to valuing the peace that comes from choosing the right presence.
modern_relevance: You leave a group chat full of cruelty and feel your chest unclench at once. Sometimes the real relief is not comfort — it's finally standing near what is clean.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: तब लगि कुसल न जीव कहुँ सपनेहुँ मन बिश्राम। जब लगि भजत न राम कहुँ सोक धाम तजि काम ॥
translation: तब तक जीव की कुशल नहीं और न स्वप्न में भी उसके मन को शांति है, जब तक वह शोक के घर काम (विषय-कामना) को छोड़कर श्री रामजी को नहीं भजता ॥
english_translation: Until a person turns from desire and worships Ram, the mind finds no real well-being or even dreamlike rest.
essence: Desire keeps you homeless; Ram gives the mind a place to rest.
simple_meaning: Real peace doesn't come while desire rules the mind. It comes when you turn away from craving and turn toward Ram.
insight: It shifts you from chasing relief to placing your trust where rest can actually begin.
modern_relevance: You close the app, then open another one, then another, hoping the restlessness will finally settle. It doesn't. This verse names the deeper cure: stop feeding craving, and let Ram become the center.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: तब लगि हृदयँ बसत खल नाना। लोभ मोह मच्छर मद माना॥ जब लगि उर न बसत रघुनाथा। धरें चाप सायक कटि भाथा ॥
translation: लोभ, मोह, मत्सर (डाह), मद और मान आदि अनेकों दुष्ट तभी तक हृदय में बसते हैं, जब तक कि धनुष-बाण और कमर में तरकस धारण किए हुए श्री रघुनाथजी हृदय में नहीं बसते ॥
english_translation: Only then do many vices dwell in the heart: greed, delusion, jealousy, pride, and conceit. Only when Raghunath does not dwell in the heart, bow in hand and quiver at the waist.
essence: Without Ram in the heart, the vices take over.
simple_meaning: Greed, delusion, jealousy, pride, and conceit stay in the heart only until Ram takes that place.
insight: It shifts attention from fighting every flaw separately to placing the heart under Ram's presence.
modern_relevance: You can scroll all day, chase approval, and still feel strangely crowded inside. The mind settles when something worth loving takes the central seat.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ममता तरुन तमी अँधिआरी। राग द्वेष उलूक सुखकारी॥ तब लगि बसति जीव मन माहीं। जब लगि प्रभु प्रताप रबि नाहीं ॥
translation: ममता पूर्ण अँधेरी रात है, जो राग-द्वेष रूपी उल्लुओं को सुख देने वाली है। वह (ममता रूपी रात्रि) तभी तक जीव के मन में बसती है, जब तक प्रभु (आप) का प्रताप रूपी सूर्य उदय नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: Attachment is a dark night. Desire and aversion thrive in it like owls. They live in the mind only until the Lord's radiance rises like the sun.
essence: Attachment survives only where inner light has not risen.
simple_meaning: Attachment clouds the mind like night. Desire and aversion thrive there until Ram's power brings inner light.
insight: It shifts attention from emotional reactivity to the need for clear seeing that dissolves it.
modern_relevance: You scroll through old messages at 1am, replaying what someone said and what they meant. The loop keeps going because the mind is still in darkness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अब मैं कुसल मिटे भय भारे। देखि राम पद कमल तुम्हारे॥ तुम्ह कृपाल जा पर अनुकूला। ताहि न ब्याप त्रिबिध भव सूला ॥
translation: हे श्री रामजी! आपके चरणारविन्द के दर्शन कर अब मैं कुशल से हूँ, मेरे भारी भय मिट गए। हे कृपालु! आप जिस पर अनुकूल होते हैं, उसे तीनों प्रकार के भवशूल (आध्यात्मिक, आधिदैविक और आधिभौतिक ताप) नहीं व्यापते ॥
english_translation: O Shri Ram, seeing your lotus feet, all my fears are gone, and I am now at peace. O compassionate one, whoever you favor is never troubled by the three kinds of suffering.
essence: Fear ends where loving refuge begins.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says that just seeing Ram's lotus feet has removed his fear. He adds that anyone favored by Ram is not struck by the three kinds of suffering.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to refuge in grace.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room after hearing bad news, and your chest is tight. Then someone you trust sits beside you, and the panic eases. Presence changes everything before any solution arrives.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: मैं निसिचर अति अधम सुभाऊ। सुभ आचरनु कीन्ह नहिं काऊ॥ जासु रूप मुनि ध्यान न आवा। तेहिं प्रभु हरषि हृदयँ मोहि लावा ॥
translation: मैं अत्यंत नीच स्वभाव का राक्षस हूँ। मैंने कभी शुभ आचरण नहीं किया। जिनका रूप मुनियों के भी ध्यान में नहीं आता, उन प्रभु ने स्वयं हर्षित होकर मुझे हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
english_translation: I am a vile creature of the night, with no good conduct at all. Yet the Lord, whose form even sages cannot hold in meditation, joyfully drew me close to his heart.
essence: Ram's embrace reaches farther than your failures.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana admits his lowly nature and lack of good conduct, yet says Ram still joyfully accepted him and drew him close.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to grateful surrender before grace.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room convinced you've already been judged, but someone listens without flinching. That quiet welcome can undo years of shame.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: अहोभाग्य मम अमित अति राम कृपा सुख पुंज। देखेउँ नयन बिरंचि सिव सेब्य जुगल पद कंज ॥
translation: हे कृपा और सुख के पुंज श्री रामजी! मेरा अत्यंत असीम सौभाग्य है, जो मैंने ब्रह्मा और शिवजी के द्वारा सेवित युगल चरण कमलों को अपने नेत्रों से देखा ॥
english_translation: O Ram, treasure of grace and joy, my boundless fortune is this: with these eyes I have seen the twin lotus-feet served by Brahma and Shiva.
essence: Seeing Ram's feet is fortune beyond all measure.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says his greatest blessing is seeing Ram's lotus feet with his own eyes, feet even Brahma and Shiva serve.
insight: It shifts the mind from chasing achievement to treasuring direct presence with what is sacred.
modern_relevance: After months of chasing recognition, you finally sit beside someone whose presence steadies your whole mind. In that moment, applause feels small and contact feels priceless.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: सुनहु सखा निज कहउँ सुभाऊ। जान भुसुंडि संभु गिरिजाऊ॥ जौं नर होइ चराचर द्रोही। आवै सभय सरन तकि मोही ॥
translation: (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे सखा! सुनो, मैं तुम्हें अपना स्वभाव कहता हूँ, जिसे काकभुशुण्डि, शिवजी और पार्वतीजी भी जानती हैं। कोई मनुष्य (संपूर्ण) जड़-चेतन जगत् का द्रोही हो, यदि वह भी भयभीत होकर मेरी शरण तक कर आ जाए, ॥
english_translation: Listen, friend, I will tell you my own nature. Kak Bhushundi, Shiva, and Parvati know it. If a person has become an enemy of all that moves and all that does not move, and comes to me in fear seeking refuge,
essence: Fearful surrender is enough to reopen the way home.
simple_meaning: Ram says his nature is to accept even someone who has become hostile to the whole world, as long as that person comes to him in fear and seeks refuge.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-exclusion to return: the act of seeking refuge matters more than past estrangement.
modern_relevance: After a bitter argument, you sit in the car outside someone's house, rehearsing your apology and your pride at the same time. This verse says the first honest step matters more than the mess you carry.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तजि मद मोह कपट छल नाना। करउँ सद्य तेहि साधु समाना॥ जननी जनक बंधु सुत दारा। तनु धनु भवन सुहृद परिवारा ॥
translation: और मद, मोह तथा नाना प्रकार के छल-कपट त्याग दे तो मैं उसे बहुत शीघ्र साधु के समान कर देता हूँ। माता, पिता, भाई, पुत्र, स्त्री, शरीर, धन, घर, मित्र और परिवार ॥
english_translation: If you give up pride, delusion, and all kinds of deceit, I quickly make you like a saint. Mother, father, brother, son, wife, body, wealth, home, friends, and family.
essence: Drop ego and pretense, and transformation comes quickly.
simple_meaning: Ram says that anyone who drops pride, confusion, and trickery can quickly become saint-like. The next line lists the bonds of attachment that usually keep the mind tied down.
insight: It shifts the focus from self-protection to inner honesty, showing that surrender begins with dropping the mask.
modern_relevance: You finally admit you were performing, not living. The relief is immediate: once the mask drops, a cleaner way of being becomes possible.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सब कै ममता ताग बटोरी। मम पद मनहि बाँध बरि डोरी॥ समदरसी इच्छा कछु नाहीं। हरष सोक भय नहिं मन माहीं ॥
translation: इन सबके ममत्व रूपी तागों को बटोरकर और उन सबकी एक डोरी बनाकर उसके द्वारा जो अपने मन को मेरे चरणों में बाँध देता है। (सारे सांसारिक संबंधों का केंद्र मुझे बना लेता है), जो समदर्शी है, जिसे कुछ इच्छा नहीं है और जिसके मन में हर्ष, शोक और भय नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Gathering up all the threads of attachment, you tie your mind to my feet with a single cord. You see all beings equally, want nothing, and keep no joy, sorrow, or fear in your mind.
essence: Gather every attachment into one devotion, and the mind becomes steady.
simple_meaning: Real devotion gathers every scattered attachment and places the mind on Ram alone. In that state, you see everyone equally and are no longer ruled by desire, joy, sorrow, or fear.
insight: It shifts devotion from scattered attachment to single-pointed surrender and steady emotional balance.
modern_relevance: You check your phone, your family group, work chat, and old messages before sunrise, already split into pieces. This verse offers a calmer center: one heart, one anchor, less inner noise.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: अस सज्जन मम उर बस कैसें। लोभी हृदयँ बसइ धनु जैसें॥ तुम्ह सारिखे संत प्रिय मोरें। धरउँ देह नहिं आन निहोरें ॥
translation: ऐसा सज्जन मेरे हृदय में कैसे बसता है, जैसे लोभी के हृदय में धन बसा करता है। तुम सरीखे संत ही मुझे प्रिय हैं। मैं और किसी के निहोरे से (कृतज्ञतावश) देह धारण नहीं करता ॥
english_translation: How can a good person live in my heart, the way wealth lives in the heart of a greedy person? Saints like you are dear to me. I do not take a body because of anyone else's request.
essence: True devotion makes you dear to Ram without bargaining.
simple_meaning: Ram says that true saints are dear to him, and he comes into the world for those who are devoted and pure-hearted.
insight: It shifts attention from asking for favors to becoming the kind of person who naturally draws grace.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose kindness is effortless, whose loyalty costs them something, and you feel instantly at ease. That same quality is what this verse calls dear to Ram.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सगुन उपासक परहित निरत नीति दृढ़ नेम। ते नर प्रान समान मम जिन्ह कें द्विज पद प्रेम ॥
translation: जो सगुण (साकार) भगवान् के उपासक हैं, दूसरे के हित में लगे रहते हैं, नीति और नियमों में दृढ़ हैं और जिन्हें ब्राह्मणों के चरणों में प्रेम है, वे मनुष्य मेरे प्राणों के समान हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who worship the divine in a personal form, work for the good of others, keep to righteous conduct and firm vows, and love the feet of the learned are as dear to me as life itself.
essence: Love for the divine becomes visible as service, discipline, and reverence.
simple_meaning: Ram says that people who worship him, help others, keep righteous discipline, and respect the learned are as dear to him as his own life.
insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to visible character and service.
modern_relevance: You keep your promises when nobody is watching, help without announcing it, and still stay teachable. That combination quietly makes you unforgettable to the people who matter most.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनु लंकेस सकल गुन तोरें। तातें तुम्ह अतिसय प्रिय मोरें॥। राम बचन सुनि बानर जूथा। सकल कहहिं जय कृपा बरूथा ॥
translation: हे लंकापति! सुनो, तुम्हारे अंदर उपर्युक्त सब गुण हैं। इससे तुम मुझे अत्यंत ही प्रिय हो। श्री रामजी के वचन सुनकर सब वानरों के समूह कहने लगे- कृपा के समूह श्री रामजी की जय हो ॥
english_translation: O king of Lanka, listen: all those qualities are yours, and because of them you are very dear to me. Hearing Ram's words, the whole troop of monkeys cried, "Victory to the one whose grace is a host of kindness!"
essence: Virtue makes you naturally dear to the one who sees clearly.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Vibhishana that his virtues make him dear, and the monkey army responds with joyful praise.
insight: It shifts attention from status to character as the basis of trust and belonging.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who quietly does the right thing when no one is watching. People trust them instantly. That kind of steadiness still makes hearts open.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनत बिभीषनु प्रभु कै बानी। नहिं अघात श्रवनामृत जानी॥ पद अंबुज गहि बारहिं बारा। हृदयँ समात न प्रेमु अपारा ॥
translation: प्रभु की वाणी सुनते हैं और उसे कानों के लिए अमृत जानकर विभीषणजी अघाते नहीं हैं। वे बार-बार श्री रामजी के चरण कमलों को पकड़ते हैं अपार प्रेम है, हृदय में समाता नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, Vibhishana never feels satisfied, knowing them as nectar for the ears. Again and again he grasps the lotus feet, and his boundless love cannot fit inside his heart.
essence: Real devotion keeps returning because love cannot be exhausted.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana hears Ram's words as nectar and cannot get enough. His love is so vast that he keeps bowing again and again.
insight: It shifts devotion from a momentary feeling to a repeating act of reverence and closeness.
modern_relevance: You replay a voice note from someone who truly understood you, then listen again just to feel that warmth return. Some words do not get old; they open the heart wider each time.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनहु देव सचराचर स्वामी। प्रनतपाल उर अंतरजामी॥ उर कछु प्रथम बासना रही। प्रभु पद प्रीति सरित सो बही ॥
translation: (विभीषणजी ने कहा-) हे देव! हे चराचर जगत् के स्वामी! हे शरणागत के रक्षक! हे सबके हृदय के भीतर की जानने वाले! सुनिए, मेरे हृदय में पहले कुछ वासना थी। वह प्रभु के चरणों की प्रीति रूपी नदी में बह गई ॥
english_translation: Listen, O divine one, lord of all that moves and does not move, protector of the surrendered, inner knower of every heart. Some desire still remained in my heart; it was carried away by the river of love for the Lord's feet.
essence: Surrender becomes complete when love carries away the last trace of wanting.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana tells Ram that a small trace of desire still remained in his heart, but love for Ram's feet has carried it away.
insight: It shifts the mind from hiding imperfection to letting devotion or trust complete the work of release.
modern_relevance: You finally tell the truth in a therapy session: part of you still wants approval, even while you want to change. Naming it is not failure. Being met with care can loosen what self-criticism could not.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: अब कृपाल निज भगति पावनी। देहु सदा सिव मन भावनी॥ एवमस्तु कहि प्रभु रनधीरा। मागा तुरत सिंधु कर नीरा ॥
translation: अब तो हे कृपालु! शिवजी के मन को सदैव प्रिय लगने वाली अपनी पवित्र भक्ति मुझे दीजिए। 'एवमस्तु' (ऐसा ही हो) कहकर रणधीर प्रभु श्री रामजी ने तुरंत ही समुद्र का जल माँगा ॥
english_translation: “Now, O compassionate one, grant me your pure devotion, ever dear to Shiva’s heart.” Saying “So be it,” the brave Ram at once asked for the ocean’s water.
essence: The highest gift is devotion itself, and Ram grants it at once.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana asks Ram for pure devotion that is always dear to Shiva. Ram agrees immediately and then asks for the ocean’s water.
insight: It shifts desire from external rescue to inner devotion, showing that readiness itself is a gift.
modern_relevance: You finally get a quiet moment after a long crisis, and instead of asking for the problem to vanish, you ask for the strength to stay faithful. That is the turn this verse makes.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: जदपि सखा तव इच्छा नहीं। मोर दरसु अमोघ जग माहीं॥ अस कहि राम तिलक तेहि सारा। सुमन बृष्टि नभ भई अपारा ॥
translation: (और कहा-) हे सखा! यद्यपि तुम्हारी इच्छा नहीं है, पर जगत् में मेरा दर्शन अमोघ है (वह निष्फल नहीं जाता)। ऐसा कहकर श्री रामजी ने उनको राजतिलक कर दिया। आकाश से पुष्पों की अपार वृष्टि हुई ॥
english_translation: And said, "Friend, even if your wish is absent, my sight in the world never goes in vain." Saying this, Ram immediately crowned him, and an endless shower of flowers fell from the sky.
essence: Ram's gaze makes even unasked surrender fruitful.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Vibhishana that even without asking, his sight is never fruitless, then crowns him as king while flowers rain from the sky.
insight: It shifts the mind from earning worthiness to receiving grace and responsibility together.
modern_relevance: You show up for someone who has already given up on being seen, and you give them trust before they can earn it. That is the kind of recognition this verse carries.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: रावन क्रोध अनल निज स्वास समीर प्रचंड। जरत बिभीषनु राखेउ दीन्हेउ राजु अखंड॥49क॥
translation: श्री रामजी ने रावण की क्रोध रूपी अग्नि में, जो अपनी (विभीषण की) श्वास (वचन) रूपी पवन से प्रचंड हो रही थी, जलते हुए विभीषण को बचा लिया और उसे अखंड राज्य दिया ॥
english_translation: Rama rescued Vibhishana, who was burning in Ravana's fire of anger fanned by the fierce wind of his own breath, and gave him an undivided kingdom.
essence: Surrender to Ram turns danger into shelter and loss into belonging.
simple_meaning: Rama protects Vibhishana when Ravana's anger is burning around him, and then gives him lasting kingship.
insight: It shifts the mind from fearing surrender to seeing it as the doorway to safety and rightful place.
modern_relevance: You leave a toxic family meeting, heart pounding, after finally telling the truth. You expect loss, but instead someone steadies you and helps you rebuild with dignity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जो संपति सिव रावनहि दीन्हि दिएँ दस माथ। सोइ संपदा बिभीषनहि सकुचि दीन्हि रघुनाथ॥49ख॥
translation: शिवजी ने जो संपत्ति रावण को दसों सिरों की बलि देने पर दी थी, वही संपत्ति श्री रघुनाथजी ने विभीषण को बहुत सकुचते हुए दी ॥
english_translation: The wealth Shiva gave Ravana for offering his ten heads, that same wealth Raghunath gave Vibhishana with humility.
essence: The same honor becomes sacred when it is given without pride.
simple_meaning: Ram gives Vibhishana the same royal honor that Shiva once gave Ravana, but he does it humbly and with care.
insight: It shifts the mind from earning worth through struggle to receiving honour through surrender and right alignment.
modern_relevance: Someone who once ignored your effort suddenly trusts you with responsibility. The old wound is still there, but this time the respect arrives quietly, without display.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस प्रभु छाड़ि भजहिं जे आना। ते नर पसु बिनु पूँछ बिषाना॥ निज जन जानि ताहि अपनावा। प्रभु सुभाव कपि कुल मन भावा ॥
translation: ऐसे परम कृपालु प्रभु को छोड़कर जो मनुष्य दूसरे को भजते हैं, वे बिना सींग-पूँछ के पशु हैं। अपना सेवक जानकर विभीषण को श्री रामजी ने अपना लिया। प्रभु का स्वभाव वानरकुल के मन को (बहुत) भाया ॥
english_translation: Those who abandon such a gracious Lord and worship someone else are beasts without horns or tails. Recognizing Vibhishana as his own servant, Lord Rama accepted him. The Lord's nature delighted the minds of the monkey race.
essence: Ram's own nature makes surrender feel safe.
simple_meaning: Only Ram deserves full devotion. Those who turn away from him lose their true humanity. Ram welcomed Vibhishana because he saw him as one of his own, and that loving nature pleased the monkey army.
insight: It shifts devotion from fear to confidence: the heart can move toward Ram without holding back.
modern_relevance: You finally tell the one person who can help you the whole truth, even though it makes you feel exposed. The relief is immediate when they respond with welcome instead of judgment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि सर्बग्य सर्ब उर बासी। सर्बरूप सब रहित उदासी॥ बोले बचन नीति प्रतिपालक। कारन मनुज दनुज कुल घालक ॥
translation: फिर सब कुछ जानने वाले, सबके हृदय में बसने वाले, सर्वरूप (सब रूपों में प्रकट), सबसे रहित, उदासीन, कारण से (भक्तों पर कृपा करने के लिए) मनुष्य बने हुए तथा राक्षसों के कुल का नाश करने वाले श्री रामजी नीति की रक्षा करने वाले वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: Then the all-knowing one, dwelling in every heart, present in every form, yet beyond all forms and untouched, spoke words that uphold right conduct: the cause of human birth and the destroyer of the demon clans.
essence: The one beyond all forms still speaks through form to restore right order.
simple_meaning: Ram is all-knowing, present in every heart, and beyond every form. From that place, he speaks as the upholder of right conduct and the destroyer of demonic forces.
insight: It shifts attention from surface appearance to the presence that sees through all appearances without being caught by them.
modern_relevance: You hear a voice in a tense room that is calm, precise, and strangely kind. It does not react from ego; it sees clearly, holds its center, and says exactly what needs to be said.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनु कपीस लंकापति बीरा। केहि बिधि तरिअ जलधि गंभीरा॥ संकुल मकर उरग झष जाती। अति अगाध दुस्तर सब भाँति ॥
translation: हे वीर वानरराज सुग्रीव और लंकापति विभीषण! सुनो, इस गहरे समुद्र को किस प्रकार पार किया जाए? अनेक जाति के मगर, साँप और मछलियों से भरा हुआ यह अत्यंत अथाह समुद्र पार करने में सब प्रकार से कठिन है ॥
english_translation: Listen, lord of the monkeys and warrior of Lanka: how can this deep ocean be crossed? Full of crocodiles, serpents, and fish, it is utterly vast and hard to pass in every way.
essence: The obstacle is so vast that ordinary means are not enough.
simple_meaning: The sea in front of them is huge, dangerous, and seemingly impossible to cross. The speaker is asking how anyone could get across it.
insight: It frames the mission as a real obstacle that requires more than force.
modern_relevance: You open the map and realise the drive is not the problem — the storm, the distance, and the broken bridge are. Before action, you have to face the size of what stands in front of you.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: कह लंकेस सुनहु रघुनायक। कोटि सिंधु सोषक तव सायक॥ जद्यपि तदपि नीति असि गाई। बिनय करिअ सागर सन जाई ॥
translation: विभीषणजी ने कहा- हे रघुनाथजी! सुनिए, यद्यपि आपका एक बाण ही करोड़ों समुद्रों को सोखने वाला है (सोख सकता है), तथापि नीति ऐसी कही गई है (उचित यह होगा) कि (पहले) जाकर समुद्र से प्रार्थना की जाए ॥
english_translation: Vibhishana said, "Listen, Lord of the Raghu clan. Your arrow could dry up millions of oceans. Yet the right course is to go and ask the sea first."
essence: Power becomes righteous when it begins with humility.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana tells Ram that even though Ram could force the sea to part, the proper way is to approach it respectfully first.
insight: It shifts you from brute force to principled action, where power is guided by restraint and etiquette.
modern_relevance: You know you could fire off the angry email and end the matter in ten minutes. But you pause, call first, and try the respectful route. That pause is not weakness; it is discipline.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: प्रभु तुम्हार कुलगुर जलधि कहिहि उपाय बिचारि॥ बिनु प्रयास सागर तरिहि सकल भालु कपि धारि ॥
translation: हे प्रभु! समुद्र आपके कुल में बड़े (पूर्वज) हैं, वे विचारकर उपाय बतला देंगे। तब रीछ और वानरों की सारी सेना बिना ही परिश्रम के समुद्र के पार उतर जाएगी ॥
english_translation: O Lord, your family teacher will think it over and tell a way. Then the whole army of bears and monkeys will cross the sea without effort.
essence: The hardest crossing becomes easy when you trust the right guide.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana says the sea will be crossed easily if the right teacher is consulted and a proper plan is found.
insight: It shifts the mind from panic and force to trust in wise guidance.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a problem too large to brute-force, and someone older, calmer, or wiser knows the route. Relief begins when you stop wrestling and ask the right person.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: सखा कही तुम्ह नीति उपाई। करिअ दैव जौं होइ सहाई। मंत्र न यह लछिमन मन भावा। राम बचन सुनि अति दुख पावा ॥
translation: (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे सखा! तुमने अच्छा उपाय बताया। यही किया जाए, यदि दैव सहायक हों। यह सलाह लक्ष्मणजी के मन को अच्छी नहीं लगी। श्री रामजी के वचन सुनकर तो उन्होंने बहुत ही दुःख पाया ॥
english_translation: Friend, you have suggested a wise plan. Let it be done if fate helps. That advice did not please Lakshman’s mind. Hearing Ram’s words, he felt deep sorrow.
essence: Wise restraint can hurt the part of you that wants instant victory.
simple_meaning: Ram approves Vibhishana’s advice but leaves the outcome to divine help. Lakshman is hurt because he wants bold action, not waiting on fate.
insight: It shows how devotion can include restraint, even when another part of you demands force.
modern_relevance: You’re in a tense group chat, and someone suggests waiting instead of acting now. The calm answer makes sense, but your body still wants to strike immediately.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: नाथ दैव कर कवन भरोसा। सोषिअ सिंधु करिअ मन रोसा॥ कादर मन कहुँ एक अधारा। दैव दैव आलसी पुकारा ॥
translation: (लक्ष्मणजी ने कहा-) हे नाथ! दैव का कौन भरोसा! मन में क्रोध कीजिए (ले आइए) और समुद्र को सुखा डालिए। यह दैव तो कायर के मन का एक आधार (तसल्ली देने का उपाय) है। आलसी लोग ही दैव-दैव पुकारा करते हैं ॥
english_translation: “My Lord, what can fate be trusted for? Dry up the ocean with anger. Fate is only a support for a cowardly mind; only the lazy keep crying, ‘fate, fate.’”
essence: Courage acts first and leaves excuses behind.
simple_meaning: Lakshman rejects passive waiting. He says courage should act directly, not lean on fate as an excuse. A lazy mind blames destiny instead of taking responsibility.
insight: It shifts the mind from passive hoping to decisive effort.
modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your inbox hoping the answer will appear, but the hard conversation still hasn’t happened. Lakshman’s words cut through that delay: stop hiding behind uncertainty and do the thing that actually moves matters forward.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: सुनत बिहसि बोले रघुबीरा। ऐसेहिं करब धरहु मन धीरा॥ अस कहि प्रभु अनुजहि समुझाई। सिंधु समीप गए रघुराई ॥
translation: यह सुनकर श्री रघुवीर हँसकर बोले- ऐसे ही करेंगे, मन में धीरज रखो। ऐसा कहकर छोटे भाई को समझाकर प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी समुद्र के समीप गए ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Raghubir laughed and said, "That is exactly how we will do it. Keep your mind steady." Saying this, the Lord explained to his younger brother and went near the ocean.
essence: Steady calm can turn a crisis into clear action.
simple_meaning: Ram responds with calm confidence, reassures Lakshman, and walks to the ocean with a steady mind.
insight: It teaches you to answer pressure with steadiness, then move forward with composed action.
modern_relevance: You are standing at the edge of a difficult conversation, and your chest is tight. Someone beside you wants urgency; you choose calm, explain clearly, and take the next step without losing yourself.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: प्रथम प्रनाम कीन्ह सिरु नाई। बैठे पुनि तट दर्भ डसाई॥ जबहिं बिभीषन प्रभु पहिं आए। पाछें रावन दूत पठाए ॥
translation: उन्होंने पहले सिर नवाकर प्रणाम किया। फिर किनारे पर कुश बिछाकर बैठ गए। इधर ज्यों ही विभीषणजी प्रभु के पास आए थे, त्यों ही रावण ने उनके पीछे दूत भेजे थे ॥
english_translation: He first bowed his head in reverence and sat down on the shore on a mat of kusa grass. Just then Vibhishana came to the Lord, and behind him Ravana sent messengers.
essence: A true turn toward refuge begins with reverence.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana comes respectfully to Ram and sits near him on the shore, while Ravana sends messengers after him.
insight: It shifts attention from force and reaction to the quiet power of choosing the right company.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where loyalty is already splitting apart a family. One person lowers their head and seeks the right place; another sends pressure behind them. The verse holds both choices in one frame.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकल चरित तिन्ह देखे धरें कपट कपि देह। प्रभु गुन हृदयँ सराहहिं सरनागत पर नेह ॥
translation: कपट से वानर का शरीर धारण कर उन्होंने सब लीलाएँ देखीं। वे अपने हृदय में प्रभु के गुणों की और शरणागत पर उनके स्नेह की सराहना करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Having seen all the events while wearing a monkey disguise, he praised the Lord's virtues in his heart and the Lord's affection for those who take refuge.
essence: Disguise cannot interrupt a heart fixed on Ram.
simple_meaning: Hanuman, disguised as a monkey, saw everything in Lanka and quietly praised Ram's virtues and his care for anyone who seeks refuge.
insight: It shifts attention from outward appearance to inward allegiance, showing that devotion can continue without announcement.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where nobody knows what you're carrying inside. Instead of performing, you stay inwardly loyal to what you love and quietly remember who protects you.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: प्रगट बखानहिं राम सुभाऊ। अति सप्रेम गा बिसरि दुराऊ॥ रिपु के दूत कपिन्ह तब जाने। सकल बाँधि कपीस पहिं आने ॥
translation: फिर वे प्रकट रूप में भी अत्यंत प्रेम के साथ श्री रामजी के स्वभाव की बड़ाई करने लगे उन्हें दुराव (कपट वेश) भूल गया। सब वानरों ने जाना कि ये शत्रु के दूत हैं और वे उन सबको बाँधकर सुग्रीव के पास ले आए ॥
english_translation: Then, openly and with great love, they praised Ram's nature and forgot the disguise. The monkeys recognized them as the enemy's messengers and brought them, bound, to Sugriva.
essence: Love for Ram makes disguise impossible to keep.
simple_meaning: In their true form, they praised Ram with love and forgot their disguise. The monkeys then recognized them as enemy messengers and brought them bound to Sugriva.
insight: It shifts attention from disguise and strategy to the power of heartfelt speech to reveal allegiance.
modern_relevance: You keep acting composed in a room full of strangers, but one sincere conversation makes the mask slip. What you truly love shows before your cover does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह सुग्रीव सुनहु सब बानर। अंग भंग करि पठवहु निसिचर॥ सुनि सुग्रीव बचन कपि धाए। बाँधि कटक चहु पास फिराए ॥
translation: सुग्रीव ने कहा- सब वानरों! सुनो, राक्षसों के अंग-भंग करके भेज दो। सुग्रीव के वचन सुनकर वानर दौड़े। दूतों को बाँधकर उन्होंने सेना के चारों ओर घुमाया ॥
english_translation: Sugriva said, 'Listen, all you monkeys: maim the demons and send them back.' Hearing Sugriva's command, the monkeys rushed forward. They bound the messengers and marched them around the camp on all sides.
essence: A clear command makes scattered strength move as one.
simple_meaning: Sugriva orders the monkeys to punish the enemy messengers, and the monkeys obey at once.
insight: It shows how decisive leadership can instantly organize scattered force into one response.
modern_relevance: A team finally gets the green light after weeks of waiting, and everyone moves at once. The energy changes the moment one person speaks with authority.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: बहु प्रकार मारन कपि लागे। दीन पुकारत तदपि न त्यागे॥ जो हमार हर नासा काना। तेहि कोसलाधीस कै आना ॥
translation: वानर उन्हें बहुत तरह से मारने लगे। वे दीन होकर पुकारते थे, फिर भी वानरों ने उन्हें नहीं छोड़ा। (तब दूतों ने पुकारकर कहा-) जो हमारे नाक-कान काटेगा, उसे कोसलाधीश श्री रामजी की सौगंध है ॥
english_translation: The monkeys beat them in many ways. Even while pleading pitifully, they were not released. Then the envoys cried out, "If anyone cuts our noses and ears, by the oath of the Lord of Kosala, let that be done to him."
essence: Pride collapses fast when fear takes over.
simple_meaning: The monkeys capture and beat the enemy messengers, and the messengers plead for mercy. Then they invoke Ram's oath to protect their faces.
insight: It keeps the focus on the consequences of aggression, not just the thrill of retaliation.
modern_relevance: A group chat turns cruel after one person is publicly mocked. The loud confidence vanishes, and everyone starts searching for the safest words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि लछिमन सब निकट बोलाए। दया लागि हँसि तुरत छोड़ाए॥ रावन कर दीजहु यह पाती। लछिमन बचन बाचु कुलघाती ॥
translation: यह सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी ने सबको निकट बुलाया। उन्हें बड़ी दया लगी, इससे हँसकर उन्होंने राक्षसों को तुरंत ही छुड़ा दिया। (और उनसे कहा-) रावण के हाथ में यह चिट्ठी देना (और कहना-) हे कुलघातक! लक्ष्मण के शब्दों (संदेसे) को बाँचो ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Lakshman called everyone close. Moved by compassion, he smiled and immediately freed them. He said, "Give this letter to Ravana, and tell that clan-destroyer to read Lakshman's words."
essence: Compassion can restrain force without weakening the warning.
simple_meaning: Lakshman feels compassion, frees the captive messengers, and sends Ravana a warning letter. The scene shifts from punishment to a direct message.
insight: It shifts response from retaliation to measured mercy without losing firmness.
modern_relevance: You catch your team piling on someone who made a mistake, and you stop it before the room hardens. Kindness does not cancel the boundary; it gives the boundary dignity.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: कहेहु मुखागर मूढ़ सन मम संदेसु उदार। सीता देइ मिलहु न त आवा कालु तुम्हार ॥
translation: फिर उस मूर्ख से जबानी यह मेरा उदार (कृपा से भरा हुआ) संदेश कहना कि सीताजी को देकर उनसे (श्री रामजी से) मिलो, नहीं तो तुम्हारा काल आ गया (समझो) ॥
english_translation: Then tell that fool in plain words my gracious message: give back Sita and meet Ram, or your end has come.
essence: Mercy still has a deadline.
simple_meaning: Hanuman is told to deliver Ram's final warning to Ravana: return Sita and face Ram, or be destroyed.
insight: It turns hesitation into a clear boundary and makes the next step unmistakable.
modern_relevance: You finally send the message you have been avoiding: enough excuses, enough delay, make it right now or face the consequences.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तुरत नाइ लछिमन पद माथा। चले दूत बरनत गुन गाथा॥ कहत राम जसु लंकाँ आए। रावन चरन सीस तिन्ह नाए ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी के चरणों में मस्तक नवाकर, श्री रामजी के गुणों की कथा वर्णन करते हुए दूत तुरंत ही चल दिए। श्री रामजी का यश कहते हुए वे लंका में आए और उन्होंने रावण के चरणों में सिर नवाए ॥
english_translation: The messengers bowed at Lakshman's feet and left at once, praising Ram's virtues. Speaking of Ram's glory, they entered Lanka and bowed their heads at Ravana's feet.
essence: Honor can travel into enemy territory without losing itself.
simple_meaning: The messengers leave respectfully, speaking only of Ram's greatness. When they reach Lanka, they bow even before Ravana.
insight: It shows how dignity and courtesy can remain intact under pressure.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone expects you to shrink, but you still carry your values with you. Respect does not mean surrendering your center.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिहसि दसानन पूँछी बाता। कहसि न सुक आपनि कुसलाता॥ पुन कहु खबरि बिभीषन केरी। जाहि मृत्यु आई अति नेरी ॥
translation: दशमुख रावण ने हँसकर बात पूछी- अरे शुक! अपनी कुशल क्यों नहीं कहता? फिर उस विभीषण का समाचार सुना, मृत्यु जिसके अत्यंत निकट आ गई है ॥
english_translation: Ravana laughed and asked, "Why do you not speak of your own well-being, Shuka? Tell me about Vibhishana, whose death is now very near."
essence: Arrogance laughs at danger until danger is already at the door.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the messenger and asks about Vibhishana, saying death is already close to him.
insight: It shows how ego turns danger into a joke and blinds you to the truth.
modern_relevance: Someone gets a warning email, smirks at it, and keeps scrolling as if consequences are for other people. That is Ravana's mind in one breath.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: करत राज लंका सठ त्यागी। होइहि जव कर कीट अभागी॥ पुनि कहु भालु कीस कटकाई। कठिन काल प्रेरित चलि आई ॥
translation: मूर्ख ने राज्य करते हुए लंका को त्याग दिया। अभागा अब जौ का कीड़ा (घुन) बनेगा (जौ के साथ जैसे घुन भी पिस जाता है, वैसे ही नर वानरों के साथ वह भी मारा जाएगा), फिर भालु और वानरों की सेना का हाल कह, जो कठिन काल की प्रेरणा से यहाँ चली आई है ॥
english_translation: The fool has abandoned Lanka while ruling it. Now he will be ground down like a cursed grain. Tell me next about the army of bears and monkeys that has come here, driven by harsh fate.
essence: Pride laughs at danger before danger reaches the door.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the supposed traitor and asks for news of the bears and monkeys that have arrived against Lanka.
insight: It shows how ego dismisses warning signs instead of preparing for them.
modern_relevance: You hear bad news in a meeting and immediately brush it off as impossible. That first wave of denial can be the most dangerous part.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: जिन्ह के जीवन कर रखवारा। भयउ मृदुल चित सिंधु बिचारा॥ कहु तपसिन्ह कै बात बहोरी। जिन्ह के हृदयँ त्रास अति मोरी ॥
translation: और जिनके जीवन का रक्षक कोमल चित्त वाला बेचारा समुद्र बन गया है (अर्थात् ) उनके और राक्षसों के बीच में यदि समुद्र न होता तो अब तक राक्षस उन्हें मारकर खा गए होते। फिर उन तपस्वियों की बात बता, जिनके हृदय में मेरा बड़ा डर है ॥
english_translation: And the gentle ocean has become the protector of their lives. Tell me more about those ascetics whose hearts are filled with fear of me.
essence: Pride laughs at danger while secretly feeding on fear.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the sea for protecting the lives of those beyond it, then asks about ascetics who fear him deeply.
insight: It reveals how ego turns fear into mockery and keeps searching for proof of its own power.
modern_relevance: Someone laughs off a problem in a meeting, then spends the rest of the day checking who is against them. That split between swagger and insecurity is Ravana's mind.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: की भइ भेंट कि फिरि गए श्रवन सुजसु सुनि मोर। कहसि न रिपु दल तेज बल बहुत चकित चित तोर ॥
translation: उनसे तेरी भेंट हुई या वे कानों से मेरा सुयश सुनकर ही लौट गए? शत्रु सेना का तेज और बल बताता क्यों नहीं? तेरा चित्त बहुत ही चकित (भौंचक्का सा) हो रहा है ॥
english_translation: Did they meet you, or did they turn back after hearing my fame? Why do you not speak of the enemy army's power and strength? Your mind seems greatly stunned.
essence: Pride hears a challenge, not a truth.
simple_meaning: Ravana asks whether Hanuman met the enemy or merely heard his fame and fled, then demands news of the enemy army. He notices Hanuman looks shaken.
insight: It exposes how ego interrogates others to protect itself instead of facing reality directly.
modern_relevance: Someone storms into a room after a tense meeting and starts asking sharp questions, trying to control the story before hearing it. Pride often talks first because it is afraid to listen.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: नाथ कृपा करि पूँछेहु जैसें। मानहु कहा क्रोध तजि तैसें॥ मिला जाइ जब अनुज तुम्हारा। जातहिं राम तिलक तेहि सारा ॥
translation: (दूत ने कहा-) हे नाथ! आपने जैसे कृपा करके पूछा है, वैसे ही क्रोध छोड़कर मेरा कहना मानिए (मेरी बात पर विश्वास कीजिए)। जब आपका छोटा भाई श्री रामजी से जाकर मिला, तब उसके पहुँचते ही श्री रामजी ने उसको राजतिलक कर दिया ॥
english_translation: O lord, kindly listen and accept my words, setting aside your anger. When your younger brother met Ram, Ram immediately crowned him on arrival.
essence: Ram honors even the one who leaves his side for righteousness.
simple_meaning: The messenger asks Ravana to calm down and trust his report. He says that when Vibhishana met Ram, Ram honored him immediately.
insight: It shows how a messenger appeals to evidence that even a proud listener cannot ignore.
modern_relevance: You’re ready to dismiss bad news because it bruises your ego. Sometimes the most useful message arrives only after you stop defending yourself.
speaker: Ravana's messenger

verse_text: रावन दूत हमहि सुनि काना। कपिन्ह बाँधि दीन्हें दुख नाना॥ श्रवन नासिका काटैं लागे। राम सपथ दीन्हें हम त्यागे ॥
translation: हम रावण के दूत हैं, यह कानों से सुनकर वानरों ने हमें बाँधकर बहुत कष्ट दिए, यहाँ तक कि वे हमारे नाक-कान काटने लगे। श्री रामजी की शपथ दिलाने पर कहीं उन्होंने हमको छोड़ा ॥
english_translation: We said we were Ravana's messengers, and the monkeys bound us and gave us many kinds of pain. They cut our ears and noses, and only released us after we swore by Ram.
essence: Boasting allegiance to power can end in public humiliation.
simple_meaning: The messengers say the monkeys punished them harshly after hearing they came from Ravana, and let them go only when they swore by Ram.
insight: It shifts the mind from boasting about position to respecting the force you are facing.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room expecting to look in control, and leave rattled because the other side saw through you immediately.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: पूँछिहु नाथ राम कटकाई। बदन कोटि सत बरनि न जाई॥ नाना बरन भालु कपि धारी। बिकटानन बिसाल भयकारी ॥
translation: हे नाथ! आपने श्री रामजी की सेना पूछी, सो वह तो सौ करोड़ मुखों से भी वर्णन नहीं की जा सकती। अनेकों रंगों के भालु और वानरों की सेना है, जो भयंकर मुख वाले, विशाल शरीर वाले और भयानक हैं ॥
english_translation: O lord, you asked about Ram's army. It cannot be described even with hundreds of millions of mouths. There are many kinds of bears and monkeys, with terrible faces, huge bodies, and fearsome looks.
essence: Ram's army is beyond counting and beyond tidy description.
simple_meaning: Ram's army is so vast and varied that no one can fully describe it. It includes many kinds of bears and monkeys, all fierce-looking and enormous.
insight: It shifts attention from exact counting to the overwhelming presence of Ram's forces.
modern_relevance: You try to summarize a whole movement, team, or crisis in one neat sentence, and it fails. Some realities are bigger, wilder, and more alive than your labels.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जेहिं पुर दहेउ हतेउ सुत तोरा। सकल कपिन्ह महँ तेहि बलु थोरा॥ अमित नाम भट कठिन कराला। अमित नाग बल बिपुल बिसाला ॥
translation: जिसने नगर को जलाया और आपके पुत्र अक्षय कुमार को मारा, उसका बल तो सब वानरों में थोड़ा है। असंख्य नामों वाले बड़े ही कठोर और भयंकर योद्धा हैं। उनमें असंख्य हाथियों का बल है और वे बड़े ही विशाल हैं ॥
english_translation: The one who burned the city and killed your son has less strength than all the monkeys here. There are countless fierce warriors with the force of countless elephants, vast and terrible.
essence: Even a terrifying enemy is only one part of the larger field of power.
simple_meaning: The enemy who burned your city and killed your son is still weaker than the monkeys here. Their army is full of countless fierce warriors with enormous strength.
insight: It shifts attention from panic to realistic assessment of strength on both sides.
modern_relevance: Before a big presentation, you list the obstacles and realize the room is full of people ready to help. The fear stays real, but it no longer feels larger than your resources.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: द्विबिद मयंद नील नल अंगद गद बिकटासि। दधिमुख केहरि निसठ सठ जामवंत बलरासि ॥
translation: द्विविद, मयंद, नील, नल, अंगद, गद, विकटास्य, दधिमुख, केसरी, निशठ, शठ और जाम्बवान् ये सभी बल की राशि हैं ॥
english_translation: Dvivida, Mainda, Nila, Nala, Angada, Gada, Vikatasya, Dadhimukha, Kesari, Nishatha, Shatha, and Jambavan are all masses of strength.
essence: Strength multiplies when capable allies stand together.
simple_meaning: The verse lists powerful monkey warriors and says each one is a storehouse of strength.
insight: It shifts attention from a single standout to the collective force already present.
modern_relevance: You open a team chat and see names of people who can each handle a crisis. Relief comes from knowing the work is carried by many strong hands, not one exhausted person.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ए कपि सब सुग्रीव समाना। इन्ह सम कोटिन्ह गनइ को नाना॥ राम कृपाँ अतुलित बल तिन्हहीं। तृन समान त्रैलोकहि गनहीं ॥
translation: ये सब वानर बल में सुग्रीव के समान हैं और इनके जैसे (एक-दो नहीं) करोड़ों हैं, उन बहुत सो को गिन ही कौन सकता है। श्री रामजी की कृपा से उनमें अतुलनीय बल है। वे तीनों लोकों को तृण के समान (तुच्छ) समझते हैं ॥
english_translation: These monkeys are all like Sugriva. There are countless more just like them. By Ram's grace they possess unmatched strength, and they count the three worlds as no more than grass.
essence: Grace turns an ordinary army into something immeasurable.
simple_meaning: Ram's army is vast and mighty. These monkeys are all powerful like Sugriva, and their strength comes from Ram's grace.
insight: It shifts attention from visible size to the source of courage and capability.
modern_relevance: A team walks into a crisis with no flashy image, yet everyone moves with quiet confidence. Their courage comes from trust in something larger than personal ego.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस मैं सुना श्रवन दसकंधर। पदुम अठारह जूथप बंदर॥ नाथ कटक महँ सो कपि नाहीं। जो न तुम्हहि जीतै रन माहीं ॥
translation: हे दशग्रीव! मैंने कानों से ऐसा सुना है कि अठारह पद्म तो अकेले वानरों के सेनापति हैं। हे नाथ! उस सेना में ऐसा कोई वानर नहीं है, जो आपको रण में न जीत सके ॥
english_translation: O Ravana, I have heard that there are eighteen crore monkey commanders. In that army, there is no monkey who cannot defeat you in battle.
essence: Pride looks small when it faces a force it cannot count.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Ravana that Ram's army is enormous and full of commanders strong enough to defeat him.
insight: It shifts the focus from Ravana's confidence to the overwhelming strength already gathered against him.
modern_relevance: You walk into a meeting knowing the other side has underestimated you. Calmly, you name the strength they missed — and the room changes.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: परम क्रोध मीजहिं सब हाथा। आयसु पै न देहिं रघुनाथा॥ सोषहिं सिंधु सहित झष ब्याला। पूरहिं न त भरि कुधर बिसाला ॥
translation: सब के सब अत्यंत क्रोध से हाथ मीजते हैं। पर श्री रघुनाथजी उन्हें आज्ञा नहीं देते। हम मछलियों और साँपों सहित समुद्र को सोख लेंगे। नहीं तो बड़े-बड़े पर्वतों से उसे भरकर पूर (पाट) देंगे ॥
english_translation: All of them grind their hands in fierce anger, but Raghunath does not give them the order. We will dry up the ocean, along with its fish and serpents. If not, we will fill it with great mountains.
essence: Power becomes effective only when it waits for the right command.
simple_meaning: The monkey army is furious and ready to destroy the ocean, but Ram has not yet given the command. Their energy is immense, but it still waits for his word.
insight: It shifts attention from strength alone to disciplined action under rightful direction.
modern_relevance: A team is fired up in a late-night war room, ready to smash the problem. But everyone still waits for the one clear call before charging ahead.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मर्दि गर्द मिलवहिं दससीसा। ऐसेइ बचन कहहिं सब कीसा॥ गर्जहिं तर्जहिं सहज असंका। मानहुँ ग्रसन चहत हहिं लंका ॥
translation: और रावण को मसलकर धूल में मिला देंगे। सब वानर ऐसे ही वचन कह रहे हैं। सब सहज ही निडर हैं, इस प्रकार गरजते और डपटते हैं मानो लंका को निगल ही जाना चाहते हैं ॥
english_translation: And they will crush Ravana into dust. All the monkeys speak like this. They roar and threaten without fear, as if they mean to swallow Lanka itself.
essence: Fearless unity can feel like a force that devours everything in its path.
simple_meaning: The monkey army speaks with fearless confidence. They roar as if they can swallow Lanka and crush Ravana completely.
insight: It shows how collective confidence can become its own force before any blow is struck.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is already aligned, loud, and unafraid. Before the meeting even starts, the energy has shifted, and the opposition can feel it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सहज सूर कपि भालु सब पुनि सिर पर प्रभु राम। रावन काल कोटि कहुँ जीति सकहिं संग्राम ॥
translation: सब वानर-भालू सहज ही शूरवीर हैं फिर उनके सिर पर प्रभु (सर्वेश्वर) श्री रामजी हैं। हे रावण! वे संग्राम में करोड़ों कालों को जीत सकते हैं ॥
english_translation: All the bears and monkeys are naturally brave, and Lord Ram stands above them. Ravana, they can defeat even countless deaths in battle.
essence: Devotion turns ordinary strength into victory over death itself.
simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears are naturally fearless, and with Ram above them, they can defeat even countless deaths in battle.
insight: It shifts bravery from personal toughness to courage rooted in surrender to Ram.
modern_relevance: A team walks into the hardest room of the year — a final pitch, a court hearing, a hospital waiting area — and no one is shaking because everyone knows who they are fighting for.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम तेज बल बुधि बिपुलाई। सेष सहस सत सकहिं न गाई॥ सक सर एक सोषि सत सागर। तव भ्रातहि पूँछेउ नय नागर ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी के तेज (सामर्थ्य), बल और बुद्धि की अधिकता को लाखों शेष भी नहीं गा सकते। वे एक ही बाण से सैकड़ों समुद्रों को सोख सकते हैं, परंतु नीति निपुण श्री रामजी ने (नीति की रक्षा के लिए) आपके भाई से उपाय पूछा ॥
english_translation: The splendor, strength, and wisdom of Ram are beyond counting. With one arrow he could dry up hundreds of oceans, yet the master of righteous conduct still asked your brother for a way.
essence: True strength can choose restraint without losing any power.
simple_meaning: Ram's power, strength, and wisdom are beyond measure. Even though he could dry up the ocean with one arrow, he still chose the righteous path and asked for help.
insight: It shifts you from proving power to using power with restraint and respect.
modern_relevance: You know the answer in the meeting, but you let someone else speak first because the room needs trust, not domination. That is the kind of strength this verse praises.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तासु बचन सुनि सागर पाहीं। मागत पंथ कृपा मन माहीं॥ सुनत बचन बिहसा दससीसा। जौं असि मति सहाय कृत कीसा ॥
translation: उनके (आपके भाई के) वचन सुनकर वे (श्री रामजी) समुद्र से राह माँग रहे हैं, उनके मन में कृपा भी है (इसलिए वे उसे सोखते नहीं)। दूत के ये वचन सुनते ही रावण खूब हँसा (और बोला-) जब ऐसी बुद्धि है, तभी तो वानरों को सहायक बनाया है! ॥
english_translation: Hearing that message, Ravana laughed hard: “So this is their intelligence — that’s why they’ve taken monkeys as allies!”
essence: Ego laughs at mercy because it cannot recognize strength without violence.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the message, laughing at the idea that Ram would ask the ocean for a path instead of forcing one open.
insight: It shows how arrogance turns mercy into weakness and blinds you to real strength.
modern_relevance: Someone dismisses a careful plan in a meeting because it looks too gentle to work. Later, that same restraint proves wiser than brute force.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सहज भीरु कर बचन दृढ़ाई। सागर सन ठानी मचलाई॥ मूढ़ मृषा का करसि बड़ाई। रिपु बल बुद्धि थाह मैं पाई ॥
translation: स्वाभाविक ही डरपोक विभीषण के वचन को प्रमाण करके उन्होंने समुद्र से मचलना (बालहठ) ठाना है। अरे मूर्ख! झूठी बड़ाई क्या करता है? बस, मैंने शत्रु (राम) के बल और बुद्धि की थाह पा ली ॥
english_translation: “The timid brother’s words only make me more stubborn. Fool, why boast falsely? I have now measured the strength and intelligence of my enemy.”
essence: Pride mistakes stubbornness for strength and calls it insight.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the messenger’s warning and doubles down on his pride. He thinks he has already measured Ram’s power and intelligence, so he keeps taunting instead of listening.
insight: It shows how contempt for advice becomes self-blindness.
modern_relevance: You get one careful warning before a bad decision, but your ego calls it weakness and pushes ahead anyway. That is the trap Ravana is in.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सचिव सभीत बिभीषन जाकें। बिजय बिभूति कहाँ जग ताकें॥ सुनि खल बचन दूत रिस बाढ़ी। समय बिचारि पत्रिका काढ़ी ॥
translation: जिसके डरपोंक बिभीषण से मंत्री हैं उसके विजय और विभूति कहाँ? || खल रावनके ये वचन सुनकर दूतको बड़ा क्रोध आया| इससे उसने अवसर जानकर लक्ष्मणके हाथकी पत्री निकाली||
english_translation: “How can that world have victory or splendor where the timid Vibhishana serves as minister?” Hearing the villain’s words, the envoy’s anger rose. Seeing the moment, he took out the letter.
essence: Pride speaks loudly; the wiser reply waits for the right moment.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Vibhishana and claims a kingdom led by him cannot truly prosper. The envoy gets angry, then chooses the right moment to reveal the letter he carries.
insight: It teaches you to hold anger briefly and use timing as part of your response.
modern_relevance: Someone insults the person you came to defend, and your face burns. You want to fire back immediately, but the wiser move is to wait for the exact second that serves the truth best.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: रामानुज दीन्हीं यह पाती। नाथ बचाइ जुड़ावहु छाती॥ बिहसि बाम कर लीन्हीं रावन। सचिव बोलि सठ लाग बचावन ॥
translation: (और कहा-) श्री रामजी के छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण ने यह पत्रिका दी है। हे नाथ! इसे बचवाकर छाती ठंडी कीजिए। रावण ने हँसकर उसे बाएँ हाथ से लिया और मंत्री को बुलवाकर वह मूर्ख उसे बँचाने लगा ॥
english_translation: Lakshman sent this letter. O lord, save it and cool your chest. Ravana laughed and took it with his left hand, then called his minister and the fool tried to explain it away.
essence: Mocking a warning only deepens the fall.
simple_meaning: Lakshman’s message reaches Ravana, but Ravana mocks it instead of taking it seriously.
insight: It shows how ego protects itself by mocking what it cannot answer.
modern_relevance: You get a serious text from someone you’ve hurt, and your first instinct is to joke, deflect, or explain it away. That little laugh can be the beginning of a much bigger collapse.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बातन्ह मनहि रिझाइ सठ जनि घालसि कुल खीस। राम बिरोध न उबरसि सरन बिष्नु अज ईस॥56क॥
translation: (पत्रिका में लिखा था-) अरे मूर्ख! केवल बातों से ही मन को रिझाकर अपने कुल को नष्ट-भ्रष्ट न कर। श्री रामजी से विरोध करके तू विष्णु, ब्रह्मा और महेश की शरण जाने पर भी नहीं बचेगा ॥
english_translation: Fool, do not destroy your own family line by soothing your mind with empty words. If you oppose Ram, you will not be saved even by taking refuge in Vishnu, Brahma, and Shiva.
essence: No amount of self-talk can protect you from the cost of opposing Ram.
simple_meaning: False comfort and clever talk cannot protect you. If you stand against Ram, no higher refuge will save you from the consequences.
insight: It pushes you to see self-justification as a danger, not a defense.
modern_relevance: You keep telling yourself the damage is manageable, that one more excuse will fix it, that the fallout will pass. But some choices keep cutting deeper no matter how well you explain them.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: की तजि मान अनुज इव प्रभु पद पंकज भृंग। होहि कि राम सरानल खल कुल सहित पतंग॥56ख॥
translation: या तो अभिमान छोड़कर अपने छोटे भाई विभीषण की भाँति प्रभु के चरण कमलों का भ्रमर बन जा। अथवा रे दुष्ट! श्री रामजी के बाण रूपी अग्नि में परिवार सहित पतिंगा हो जा (दोनों में से जो अच्छा लगे सो कर) ॥
english_translation: Give up pride and become, like Vibhishana, a bee at the Lord’s lotus feet. Or, wicked one, become a moth, along with your whole family, in Ram’s arrow-fire.
essence: Pride leaves only two endings: surrender or destruction.
simple_meaning: Ravana is warned to give up arrogance and surrender like Vibhishana, or else face destruction with his family in Ram’s fiery arrows.
insight: It shifts the mind from protecting ego to choosing humility before consequences harden.
modern_relevance: You keep defending a decision in a family group chat, even as the room goes quiet. At some point, the issue is no longer the argument — it is whether pride is worth the damage.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सुनत सभय मन मुख मुसुकाई। कहत दसानन सबहि सुनाई॥ भूमि परा कर गहत अकासा। लघु तापस कर बाग बिलासा ॥
translation: पत्रिका सुनते ही रावण मन में भयभीत हो गया, परंतु मुख से (ऊपर से) मुस्कुराता हुआ वह सबको सुनाकर कहने लगा- जैसे कोई पृथ्वी पर पड़ा हुआ हाथ से आकाश को पकड़ने की चेष्टा करता हो, वैसे ही यह छोटा तपस्वी (लक्ष्मण) वाग्विलास करता है (डींग हाँकता है) ॥
english_translation: Hearing it, Ravana felt fear in his mind but smiled on his face and spoke so everyone could hear: "It is like someone lying on the ground trying to catch the sky with his hands. This little ascetic is just showing off with words."
essence: Fear hidden by pride turns into ridicule.
simple_meaning: Ravana is afraid inside, but he hides it with a smile and mocks Lakshman’s words as empty boasting.
insight: It reveals how ego protects itself by turning real fear into public mockery.
modern_relevance: You get a hard message in a group chat, feel the sting, then reply with a joke so nobody sees it landed. Ravana’s mask is painfully familiar.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: कह सुक नाथ सत्य सब बानी। समुझहु छाड़ि प्रकृति अभिमानी॥ सुनहु बचन मम परिहरि क्रोधा। नाथ राम सन तजहु बिरोधा ॥
translation: शुक (दूत) ने कहा- हे नाथ! अभिमानी स्वभाव को छोड़कर (इस पत्र में लिखी) सब बातों को सत्य समझिए। क्रोध छोड़कर मेरा वचन सुनिए। हे नाथ! श्री रामजी से वैर त्याग दीजिए ॥
english_translation: Shuk said: O lord, set aside pride and understand every word as true. Listen to my words without anger, and give up your enmity with Ram.
essence: Pride blocks the message that could save you.
simple_meaning: Shuk asks Ravana to drop pride, listen calmly, and stop opposing Ram. The way forward is not more force, but surrender.
insight: It shifts you from defensive reaction to receptive listening, so truth can land before conflict hardens.
modern_relevance: You are halfway through drafting a furious reply when you realize the real issue is your wounded pride. If you can put that down, the conversation may finally become possible.
speaker: Shuk

verse_text: अति कोमल रघुबीर सुभाऊ। जद्यपि अखिल लोक कर राऊ॥ मिलत कृपा तुम्ह पर प्रभु करिही। उर अपराध न एकउ धरिही ॥
translation: यद्यपि श्री रघुवीर समस्त लोकों के स्वामी हैं, पर उनका स्वभाव अत्यंत ही कोमल है। मिलते ही प्रभु आप पर कृपा करेंगे और आपका एक भी अपराध वे हृदय में नहीं रखेंगे ॥
english_translation: Though Lord Raghubir is the ruler of all worlds, his nature is extremely gentle. When he meets you, he will shower you with grace and will not keep even one offense in his heart.
essence: Power becomes lovable when it carries no resentment.
simple_meaning: Ram is gentle, even as the ruler of all worlds. If you meet him, he will show mercy and not keep your faults in his heart.
insight: It shifts the mind from fear of judgment to trust in mercy.
modern_relevance: You finally send the apology text you have avoided for weeks. The reply comes back kinder than you feared. This verse reminds you that real strength can still be tender.
speaker: Shuk

verse_text: जनकसुता रघुनाथहि दीजे। एतना कहा मोर प्रभु कीजे॥ जब तेहिं कहा देन बैदेही। चरन प्रहार कीन्ह सठ तेही ॥
translation: जानकीजी श्री रघुनाथजी को दे दीजिए। हे प्रभु! इतना कहना मेरा कीजिए। जब उस (दूत) ने जानकीजी को देने के लिए कहा, तब दुष्ट रावण ने उसको लात मारी ॥
english_translation: Give Janaki to Raghunath. Tell my Lord only this. When the messenger said to give back Vaidehi, that wicked Ravana kicked him.
essence: Ego does not negotiate; it lashes out at truth.
simple_meaning: Ravana orders Sita to be handed over to Ram, but when the messenger repeats that demand, Ravana kicks him in rage.
insight: It exposes how ego turns a chance to correct course into fresh harm.
modern_relevance: Someone gives you a hard truth in a calm voice, and you snap before they finish the sentence. The reaction itself proves the message was needed.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: नाइ चरन सिरु चला सो तहाँ। कृपासिंधु रघुनायक जहाँ॥ करि प्रनामु निज कथा सुनाई। राम कृपाँ आपनि गति पाई ॥
translation: वह भी (विभीषण की भाँति) चरणों में सिर नवाकर वहीं चला, जहाँ कृपासागर श्री रघुनाथजी थे। प्रणाम करके उसने अपनी कथा सुनाई और श्री रामजी की कृपा से अपनी गति (मुनि का स्वरूप) पाई ॥
english_translation: He bowed his head at the feet and went there, where the ocean of compassion, Raghunath, was. After bowing, he told his own story, and by Ram's grace he attained his rightful state.
essence: Humility opens the way for grace to change your state.
simple_meaning: He approaches Ram with humility, tells his story, and receives his true place through Ram's grace.
insight: It shifts you from self-protection to humble disclosure, trusting grace instead of control.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a mistake, lower your pride, and tell the truth plainly. The moment you stop defending yourself, help can actually reach you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रिषि अगस्ति कीं साप भवानी। राछस भयउ रहा मुनि ग्यानी॥ बंदि राम पद बारहिं बारा। मुनि निज आश्रम कहुँ पगु धारा ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे भवानी! वह ज्ञानी मुनि था, अगस्त्य ऋषि के शाप से राक्षस हो गया था। बार-बार श्री रामजी के चरणों की वंदना करके वह मुनि अपने आश्रम को चला गया ॥
english_translation: (Shiva says to Parvati:) O Bhavani, he was a wise sage who became a demon by the curse of Sage Agastya. Bowing again and again at Ram's feet, the sage went back to his own hermitage.
essence: Repeated bowing to Ram restores what curse had broken.
simple_meaning: A wise sage had once been cursed into a demon. After repeatedly bowing to Ram's feet, he returned to his hermitage.
insight: It shifts the mind from fixed identity to the possibility of return through devotion.
modern_relevance: You can feel trapped by one mistake, one label, or one bad season. But humility can reopen the road home faster than pride ever will.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: बिनय न मानत जलधि जड़ गए तीनि दिन बीति। बोले राम सकोप तब भय बिनु होइ न प्रीति ॥
translation: इधर तीन दिन बीत गए, किंतु जड़ समुद्र विनय नहीं मानता। तब श्री रामजी क्रोध सहित बोले- बिना भय के प्रीति नहीं होती! ॥
english_translation: Three days passed, but the stubborn ocean would not respond to humility. Then Ram spoke in anger: "Without fear, there is no love."
essence: Without respect, even love becomes powerless.
simple_meaning: The ocean ignores Ram's peaceful request, so he warns that love without awe or restraint cannot last.
insight: It shifts you from endless politeness to clear limits when gentleness is being ignored.
modern_relevance: You keep explaining your boundary to someone who keeps crossing it, hoping kindness alone will work. At some point, firmness is not cruelty — it is the condition for respect.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: लछिमन बान सरासन आनू। सोषौं बारिधि बिसिख कृसानु॥ सठ सन बिनय कुटिल सन प्रीति। सहज कृपन सन सुंदर नीति ॥
translation: हे लक्ष्मण! धनुष-बाण लाओ, मैं अग्निबाण से समुद्र को सोख डालूँ। मूर्ख से विनय, कुटिल के साथ प्रीति, स्वाभाविक ही कंजूस से सुंदर नीति (उदारता का उपदेश), ॥
english_translation: “Lakshman, bring the bow and arrows. I will dry up the ocean with fire-arrows. Advice to the foolish, affection for the crooked, and noble conduct from the miserly come naturally.”
essence: Gentleness has limits; some resistance must be met with force.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Lakshman to bring the bow and says he will burn through the ocean. He also says some people do not respond to gentleness, crookedness does not deserve affection, and the miserly do not inspire noble treatment.
insight: It shifts you from endless appeasement to decisive action when persuasion has failed.
modern_relevance: You’ve explained the same boundary three times and the other person still pushes. At some point, kindness stops meaning passivity, and you need a firmer line.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: ममता रत सन ग्यान कहानी। अति लोभी सन बिरति बखानी॥ क्रोधिहि सम कामिहि हरिकथा। ऊसर बीज बएँ फल जथा ॥
translation: ममता में फँसे हुए मनुष्य से ज्ञान की कथा, अत्यंत लोभी से वैराग्य का वर्णन, क्रोधी से शम (शांति) की बात और कामी से भगवान् की कथा, इनका वैसा ही फल होता है जैसा ऊसर में बीज बोने से होता है (अर्थात् ऊसर में बीज बोने की भाँति यह सब व्यर्थ जाता है) ॥
english_translation: Talking about wisdom to someone bound by possessiveness, non-attachment to someone drowning in greed, calmness to someone ruled by anger, and tales of the divine to someone ruled by desire is like sowing seeds in barren ground.
essence: Truth cannot take root in a heart that rejects it.
simple_meaning: A person trapped in possessiveness, greed, anger, or desire cannot receive teachings that ask for wisdom, detachment, peace, or devotion.
insight: It shifts you from forcing advice to noticing whether the listener is ready for it.
modern_relevance: You try to calm a friend who is furious, but every sentence lands like an insult. The message may be right, yet the mind hearing it is too heated to receive it.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: अस कहि रघुपति चाप चढ़ावा। यह मत लछिमन के मन भावा॥ संधानेउ प्रभु बिसिख कराला। उठी उदधि उर अंतर ज्वाला ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने धनुष चढ़ाया। यह मत लक्ष्मणजी के मन को बहुत अच्छा लगा। प्रभु ने भयानक (अग्नि) बाण संधान किया, जिससे समुद्र के हृदय के अंदर अग्नि की ज्वाला उठी ॥
english_translation: After saying this, Raghupati raised his bow. Lakshman was pleased by this resolve. The Lord aimed a terrible arrow, and a fire rose within the ocean's heart.
essence: Resolve can move what patience could not.
simple_meaning: Ram raises his bow and readies a fierce arrow to confront the ocean. Lakshman approves, and the sea is shaken from within by the threat.
insight: It shifts the mind from endless delay to decisive action when a situation refuses to move.
modern_relevance: You’ve tried being reasonable, waiting, and asking nicely. Then you finally set a boundary that cannot be ignored.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मकर उरग झष गन अकुलाने। जरत जंतु जलनिधि जब जाने॥ कनक थार भरि मनि गन नाना। बिप्र रूप आयउ तजि माना ॥
translation: मगर, साँप तथा मछलियों के समूह व्याकुल हो गए। जब समुद्र ने जीवों को जलते जाना, तब सोने के थाल में अनेक मणियों (रत्नों) को भरकर अभिमान छोड़कर वह ब्राह्मण के रूप में आया ॥
english_translation: The crocodiles, snakes, and fish grew restless. When the ocean saw the creatures burning, it came in the form of a Brahmin, giving up pride, with a golden tray full of many gems.
essence: Pride falls away when suffering can no longer be ignored.
simple_meaning: The sea grows troubled when it sees the creatures inside it suffering, and it comes forward humbly with gifts.
insight: It shows that when suffering becomes visible, pride must give way to humility and swift repair.
modern_relevance: A tense meeting is about to explode, and the person who has been defensive suddenly softens, apologises, and brings what is needed. Pressure can strip away ego faster than arguments can.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: काटेहिं पइ कदरी फरइ कोटि जतन कोउ सींच। बिनय न मान खगेस सुनु डाटेहिं पइ नव नीच ॥
translation: (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं-) हे गरुड़जी! सुनिए, चाहे कोई करोड़ों उपाय करके सींचे, पर केला तो काटने पर ही फलता है। नीच विनय से नहीं मानता, वह डाँटने पर ही झुकता है (रास्ते पर आता है) ॥
english_translation: Listen, Garuda: even if you pour effort into a banana plant for a million lifetimes, it fruits only when it is cut; a low-minded person does not respond to gentleness, but to sharp correction.
essence: Some people change only when gentle words become hard truth.
simple_meaning: Some people do not respond to gentle advice. Like a banana plant that fruits only after being cut, they change only through forceful correction.
insight: It shifts you from assuming every problem can be solved by softness to recognizing when firmer correction is needed.
modern_relevance: You keep explaining calmly to someone who keeps repeating the same harmful pattern. After the fifth conversation, you realize kindness alone is not always enough to break denial.
speaker: Kak Bhushundi

verse_text: सभय सिंधु गहि पद प्रभु केरे। छमहु नाथ सब अवगुन मेरे॥। गगन समीर अनल जल धरनी। इन्ह कइ नाथ सहज जड़ करनी ॥
translation: समुद्र ने भयभीत होकर प्रभु के चरण पकड़कर कहा- हे नाथ! मेरे सब अवगुण (दोष) क्षमा कीजिए। हे नाथ! आकाश, वायु, अग्नि, जल और पृथ्वी- इन सबकी करनी स्वभाव से ही जड़ है ॥
english_translation: The ocean, afraid, held the Lord's feet and said, 'Forgive all my faults. O Lord, sky, air, fire, water, and earth are by nature inert.'
essence: True power kneels first and becomes fit to serve.
simple_meaning: The ocean humbles itself before Ram and asks forgiveness. It admits that the elements themselves are naturally inert and depend on divine power.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-justification to surrender, showing that real strength begins with bowing.
modern_relevance: You realize you were wrong in the middle of a tense conversation, and the room changes the moment you stop defending yourself. Humility does what force never can.
speaker: Ocean

verse_text: तव प्रेरित मायाँ उपजाए। सृष्टि हेतु सब ग्रंथनि गाए॥ प्रभु आयसु जेहि कहँ जस अहई। सो तेहि भाँति रहें सुख लहई ॥
translation: आपकी प्रेरणा से माया ने इन्हें सृष्टि के लिए उत्पन्न किया है, सब ग्रंथों ने यही गाया है। जिसके लिए स्वामी की जैसी आज्ञा है, वह उसी प्रकार से रहने में सुख पाता है ॥
english_translation: By your prompting, Maya brought them forth for creation, as all the scriptures declare. Whoever has whatever command the Lord has given them finds ease by living in that way.
essence: Peace comes from living in alignment with your allotted role.
simple_meaning: Everything in creation has its place because the divine power set it in motion. A person finds ease by living according to the role and instruction meant for them.
insight: It shifts you from resistance to alignment: look for the way of living that matches your actual role.
modern_relevance: You keep forcing yourself into someone else’s life plan, then wonder why everything feels tight. The strain softens when you stop arguing with the role that is actually yours.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: प्रभु भल कीन्ह मोहि सिख दीन्हीं। मरजादा पुनि तुम्हरी कीन्हीं॥ ढोल गवाँर सूद्र पसु नारी। सकल ताड़ना के अधिकारी ॥
translation: प्रभु ने अच्छा किया जो मुझे शिक्षा (दंड) दी, किंतु मर्यादा (जीवों का स्वभाव) भी आपकी ही बनाई हुई है। ढोल, गँवार, शूद्र, पशु और स्त्री- ये सब शिक्षा के अधिकारी हैं ॥
english_translation: The Lord did well to teach me, but the code of conduct was also made by you. Drum, fool, low-born, animal, and woman — all are fit for correction.
essence: True correction belongs to the order that also gives it.
simple_meaning: The sea accepts Ram's rebuke as rightful, and says that the boundaries of conduct also come from Ram. The verse then gives a harsh list of those considered fit for correction.
insight: It shifts the mind from taking correction personally to seeing it as part of a larger moral order.
modern_relevance: You get called out by someone you respect, and your first reaction is to bristle. Then you realize the correction was never meant to shame you — it was meant to restore order.
speaker: Sea

verse_text: प्रभु प्रताप मैं जाब सुखाई। उतरिहि कटकु न मोरि बड़ाई॥ प्रभु अग्या अपेल श्रुति गाई। करौं सो बेगि जो तुम्हहि सोहाई ॥
translation: प्रभु के प्रताप से मैं सूख जाऊँगा और सेना पार उतर जाएगी, इसमें मेरी बड़ाई नहीं है (मेरी मर्यादा नहीं रहेगी)। तथापि प्रभु की आज्ञा अपेल है (अर्थात् आपकी आज्ञा का उल्लंघन नहीं हो सकता) ऐसा वेद गाते हैं। अब आपको जो अच्छा लगे, मैं तुरंत वही करूँ ॥
english_translation: By the Lord's power I would dry up, and the army would cross over; that would not be my greatness. The Vedas sing that the Lord's command cannot be disobeyed. I will quickly do whatever pleases you.
essence: Pride vanishes when you place your power under a higher command.
simple_meaning: The sea says it will obey Ram at once. Even if its own power could make the army cross, it does not claim credit. Ram's command must be followed.
insight: It shifts the mind from claiming credit to honouring the right command.
modern_relevance: A senior colleague quietly hands you the final call on a project after days of tension. You stop trying to protect your image and just do what is right.
speaker: Samudra

verse_text: सुनत बिनीत बचन अति कह कृपाल मुसुकाइ। जेहि बिधि उतरै कपि कटकु तात सो कहहु उपाइ ॥
translation: समुद्र के अत्यंत विनीत वचन सुनकर कृपालु श्री रामजी ने मुस्कुराकर कहा- हे तात! जिस प्रकार वानरों की सेना पार उतर जाए, वह उपाय बताओ ॥
english_translation: Hearing the ocean's humble words, the compassionate Lord smiled and said, 'Father, tell me a way by which the monkey army can cross.'
essence: Humility opens the door to help.
simple_meaning: Ram smiles at the ocean's humble request and asks for a practical way to help the monkey army cross.
insight: It shifts the mind from demanding control to inviting wise help.
modern_relevance: You finally admit you need help, and the person across from you doesn't shame you. They lean in, smile, and start thinking with you instead of against you.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: नाथ नील नल कपि द्वौ भाई। लरिकाईं रिषि आसिष पाई॥ तिन्ह कें परस किएँ गिरि भारे। तरिहहिं जलधि प्रताप तुम्हारे ॥
translation: (समुद्र ने कहा)) हे नाथ! नील और नल दो वानर भाई हैं। उन्होंने लड़कपन में ऋषि से आशीर्वाद पाया था। उनके स्पर्श कर लेने से ही भारी-भारी पहाड़ भी आपके प्रताप से समुद्र पर तैर जाएँगे ॥
english_translation: O Lord, Nila and Nala are two monkey brothers. In childhood they received a sage's blessing. By their touch, even heavy mountains will float across the ocean through your power.
essence: Your power makes even mountains float.
simple_meaning: The ocean explains that Nila and Nala, blessed in childhood, can make even heavy mountains float because of Ram's power.
insight: It shifts attention from brute force to the unseen support that makes action succeed.
modern_relevance: A team is stuck on a task everyone calls impossible. Then one person with the right training, the right blessing, or the right backing changes everything. Hidden support can carry what raw effort cannot.
speaker: Ocean

verse_text: मैं पुनि उर धरि प्रभु प्रभुताई। करिहउँ बल अनुमान सहाई॥ एहि बिधि नाथ पयोधि बँधाइअ। जेहिं यह सुजसु लोक तिहुँ गाइअ ॥
translation: मैं भी प्रभु की प्रभुता को हृदय में धारण कर अपने बल के अनुसार (जहाँ तक मुझसे बन पड़ेगा) सहायता करूँगा। हे नाथ! इस प्रकार समुद्र को बँधाइए, जिससे तीनों लोकों में आपका सुंदर यश गाया जाए ॥
english_translation: I will keep your greatness in my heart and help as far as my strength allows. O Lord, in this way bind the ocean so your splendid fame is sung in all three worlds.
essence: True help starts when pride bows to a greater purpose.
simple_meaning: The ocean offers to remember Ram's greatness and help in whatever way it can, so that Ram's fame spreads through all the worlds.
insight: It shifts the mind from ego-driven control to humble, coordinated action.
modern_relevance: You are in a tense meeting, and the problem is bigger than your team. Instead of posturing, you say, 'I'll do what I can, and keep the bigger purpose in view.'
speaker: Ocean

verse_text: एहि सर मम उत्तर तट बासी। हतहु नाथ खल नर अघ रासी॥ सुनि कृपाल सागर मन पीरा। तुरतहिं हरी राम रनधीरा ॥
translation: इस बाण से मेरे उत्तर तट पर रहने वाले पाप के राशि दुष्ट मनुष्यों का वध कीजिए। कृपालु और रणधीर श्री रामजी ने समुद्र के मन की पीड़ा सुनकर उसे तुरंत ही हर लिया (अर्थात् बाण से उन दुष्टों का वध कर दिया) ॥
english_translation: With this arrow, kill the heap of wicked men living on my northern shore. Hearing the ocean's pain, compassionate and battle-hardened Ram quickly removed it.
essence: Compassion can demand decisive force against harm.
simple_meaning: The ocean asks Ram to use his arrow against the wicked people living on its northern shore. Ram hears the ocean's distress and quickly acts.
insight: It shifts the focus from raw force to protective action guided by compassion.
modern_relevance: You finally tell the truth about the person who keeps hurting everyone in the group. The relief is not in revenge, but in ending the damage.
speaker: Ocean

verse_text: देखि राम बल पौरुष भारी। हरषि पयोनिधि भयउ सुखारी॥ सकल चरित कहि प्रभुहि सुनावा। चरन बंदि पाथोधि सिधावा ॥
translation: श्री रामजी का भारी बल और पौरुष देखकर समुद्र हर्षित होकर सुखी हो गया। उसने उन दुष्टों का सारा चरित्र प्रभु को कह सुनाया। फिर चरणों की वंदना करके समुद्र चला गया ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ram's great strength and valour, the ocean became joyful and relieved. It told the Lord the whole story of the wicked ones, then bowed at his feet and departed.
essence: Power that is aligned with dharma ends struggle without further force.
simple_meaning: The ocean sees Ram's power, feels relieved, explains the situation, bows, and leaves.
insight: It shows that truth can emerge once fear and pride are broken.
modern_relevance: After a long argument, you finally hear the other person speak with calm authority. The tension drops, the facts come out, and everyone can breathe again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निज भवन गवनेउ सिंधु श्रीरघुपतिहि यह मत भायऊ। यह चरित कलि मल हर जथामति दास तुलसी गायऊ॥ सुख भवन संसय समन दवन बिषाद रघुपति गुन गना। तजि सकल आस भरोस गावहि सुनहि संतत सठ मना॥
translation: समुद्र अपने घर चला गया, श्री रघुनाथजी को यह मत (उसकी सलाह) अच्छा लगा। यह चरित्र कलियुग के पापों को हरने वाला है, इसे तुलसीदास ने अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार गाया है। श्री रघुनाथजी के गुण समूह सुख के धाम, संदेह का नाश करने वाले और विषाद का दमन करने वाले हैं। अरे मूर्ख मन! तू संसार का सब आशा-भरोसा त्यागकर निरंतर इन्हें गा और सुन।
english_translation: The ocean returned to its home, and this pleased Shri Raghunath. Tulsidas sings this story according to his understanding, for it removes the stains of Kali Yuga. The qualities of Raghupati are a house of joy, the destroyer of doubt, and the end of sorrow. O foolish mind, give up all other hopes and keep singing and listening with steady devotion.
essence: Ram’s praise turns confusion and sorrow into steadiness.
simple_meaning: Ram’s story and qualities are presented as medicine for confusion and sorrow. Tulsidas says that keeping Ram in your heart and hearing his praise brings joy and clears the mind.
insight: It shifts attention from anxious speculation to repeated remembrance of Ram’s qualities.
modern_relevance: You are lying awake after a hard conversation, replaying every line and building worst-case stories. This verse says the mind does not heal by more spinning; it steadies by returning to what is trustworthy.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सकल सुमंगल दायक रघुनायक गुन गान। सादर सुनहिं ते तरहिं भव सिंधु बिना जलजान ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी का गुणगान संपूर्ण सुंदर मंगलों का देने वाला है। जो इसे आदर सहित सुनेंगे, वे बिना किसी जहाज (अन्य साधन) के ही भवसागर को तर जाएँगे ॥
english_translation: The praise of Raghunath brings every blessing. Those who listen with reverence cross the sea of becoming without any boat.
essence: Reverent praise becomes the boat across struggle.
simple_meaning: Listening to Ram's praise with respect brings blessings and helps you cross the cycle of struggle without needing any other support.
insight: It shifts attention from external rescue to inward receptivity, showing that devotion itself becomes the means of crossing.
modern_relevance: You’re exhausted after a long day, and one honest song, prayer, or story steadies you more than another plan ever could. Reverent attention can carry you farther than control.
speaker: Tulsidas
