verse_text: श्लोक: रामं कामारिसेव्यं भवभयहरणं कालमत्तेभसिंहं योगीन्द्रं ज्ञानगम्यं गुणनिधिमजितं निर्गुणं निर्विकारम् । मायातीतं सुरेशं खलवधनिरतं ब्रह्मवृन्दैकदेवं वन्दे कन्दावदातं सरसिजनयनं देवमुर्वीशरूपम् ॥
translation: कामदेव के शत्रु शिवजी के सेव्य, भव (जन्म-मृत्यु) के भय को हरने वाले, काल रूपी मतवाले हाथी के लिए सिंह के समान, योगियों के स्वामी (योगीश्वर), ज्ञान के द्वारा जानने योग्य, गुणों की निधि, अजेय, निर्गुण, निर्विकार, माया से परे, देवताओं के स्वामी, दुष्टों के वध में तत्पर, ब्राह्मणवृन्द के एकमात्र देवता (रक्षक), जल वाले मेघ के समान सुंदर श्याम, कमल के से नेत्र वाले, पृथ्वीपति (राजा) के रूप में परमदेव श्री रामजी की मैं वंदना करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I bow to Ram, served by Shiva, who removes the fear of becoming and death, who is like a lion to the wild elephant of Time, lord of yogis, known through insight, treasure of virtues, unconquered, beyond qualities, beyond change, beyond illusion, lord of the divine beings, ready to destroy the wicked, the one and only divine protector of the learned, beautiful as a dark cloud, with lotus eyes, and appearing as the ruler of the earth.
essence: Ram is the refuge that stands beyond fear, time, and change.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the supreme, unchanging reality who removes fear, defeats time, and stands beyond illusion. He is both the ruler of the world and the refuge of seekers.
insight: It shifts attention from temporary threats to the one reality that cannot be shaken.
modern_relevance: When your phone is full of bad news, deadlines, and family pressure, this verse pulls you out of the panic spiral. It reminds you that what is stable is larger than the storm around you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: शंखेन्द्वाभमतीवसुन्दरतनुं शार्दूलचर्माम्बरं कालव्यालकरालभूषणधरं गंगाशशांकप्रियम् । काशीशं कलिकल्मषौघशमनं कल्याणकल्पद्रुमं नौमीड्यं गिरिजापतिं गुणनिधिं कन्दर्पहं शंकरम् ॥
translation: शंख और चंद्रमा की सी कांति के अत्यंत सुंदर शरीर वाले, व्याघ्रचर्म के वस्त्र वाले, काल के समान (अथवा काले रंग के) भयानक सर्पों का भूषण धारण करने वाले, गंगा और चंद्रमा के प्रेमी, काशीपति, कलियुग के पाप समूह का नाश करने वाले, कल्याण के कल्पवृक्ष, गुणों के निधान और कामदेव को भस्म करने वाले,
english_translation: I bow to Shankara, whose body is beautiful like a conch and moon, who wears tiger skin, who bears dark serpents as ornaments, who loves the Ganga and the moon, who is lord of Kashi, who removes the burdens of this age, who is a wish-fulfilling tree of well-being, who is full of virtues, and who burns desire to ashes.
essence: True greatness can be beautiful, fierce, and merciful at once.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas offers a reverent praise of Shiva, describing his beauty, power, purity, and his ability to remove the heaviness of this age.
insight: It trains the mind to see sacred power as both tender and immense.
modern_relevance: You stand in a crowded temple at dusk, tired and restless, and then the chant begins. Something in you remembers that strength does not have to be harsh, and beauty does not have to be weak.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: पार्वती पति वन्दनीय श्री शंकरजी को मैं नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥ यो ददाति सतां शम्भुः कैवल्यमपि दुर्लभम् । खलानां दण्डकृद्योऽसौ शंकरः शं तनोतु मे ॥
translation: जो सत् पुरुषों को अत्यंत दुर्लभ कैवल्यमुक्ति तक दे डालते हैं और जो दुष्टों को दण्ड देने वाले हैं, वे कल्याणकारी श्री शम्भु मेरे कल्याण का विस्तार करें ॥
english_translation: I bow to Shankar, the husband of Parvati. May auspicious Shambhu, who grants even the hard-to-attain freedom to the good and punishes the wicked, spread blessing over me.
essence: The same presence that blesses the good also restrains what harms.
simple_meaning: Shiva is praised as the one who gives deep freedom to the noble and gives punishment to the wicked. The speaker asks for Shiva's blessing and protection.
insight: It shifts devotion from soft admiration to trust in a power that also judges and corrects.
modern_relevance: Before a hard conversation, you may want only comfort. This verse reminds you that real support can also include correction, boundaries, and the courage to face what is wrong.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: लव निमेष परमानु जुग बरष कलप सर चंड। भजसि न मन तेहि राम को कालु जासु कोदंड॥
translation: लव, निमेष, परमाणु, वर्ष, युग और कल्प जिनके प्रचण्ड बाण हैं और काल जिनका धनुष है, हे मन! तू उन श्री रामजी को क्यों नहीं भजता?
english_translation: O mind, why do you not worship Shri Ram, whose fierce bow is time itself and whose arrows are moments, atoms, years, ages, and cycles?
essence: Even time is only an instrument in Ram's hands.
simple_meaning: Ram is greater than time itself. The mind should turn toward him instead of chasing temporary things.
insight: It shifts attention from fearing time to placing trust in Ram's greater order.
modern_relevance: You are staring at the clock before a medical result, an interview, or a hard conversation. The verse reminds you that time is not the final power in the room.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सिंधु बचन सुनि राम सचिव बोलि प्रभु अस कहेउ। अब बिलंबु केहि काम करहु सेतु उतरै कटकु॥
translation: समुद्र के वचन सुनकर प्रभु श्री रामजी ने मंत्रियों को बुलाकर ऐसा कहा- अब विलंब किसलिए हो रहा है? सेतु (पुल) तैयार करो, जिसमें सेना उतरे।
english_translation: Hearing the ocean's words, Lord Ram called his ministers and said, “Why delay now? Build the bridge so the army can cross.”
essence: Once the way is known, delay becomes waste.
simple_meaning: Ram hears the ocean and immediately tells his ministers to stop delaying and build the bridge for the army to cross.
insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to decisive execution when the path is already clear.
modern_relevance: You have the plan, the team, and the deadline — but everyone is still talking. This verse cuts through the stall and asks for movement, not more discussion.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनहु भानुकुल केतु जामवंत कर जोरि कह। नाथ नाम तव सेतु नर चढ़ि भव सागर तरहिं॥
translation: जाम्बवान् ने हाथ जोड़कर कहा- हे सूर्यकुल के ध्वजास्वरूप (कीर्ति को बढ़ाने वाले) श्री रामजी! सुनिए। हे नाथ! (सबसे बड़ा) सेतु तो आपका नाम ही है, जिस पर चढ़कर (जिसका आश्रय लेकर) मनुष्य संसार रूपी समुद्र से पार हो जाते हैं।
english_translation: Jambavan, with folded hands, said: "Listen, Lord of the solar line. Your name itself is the bridge; by taking refuge in it, people cross the ocean of worldly existence."
essence: Ram's name becomes the bridge that carries you across.
simple_meaning: Ram's name is described as the bridge that carries people across the restless cycle of worldly life.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliant strain to trusting refuge in what is greater than effort alone.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a problem that feels too wide to cross — a broken relationship, a debt, a decision you've delayed for months. Something steadier than your panic can still carry you through.
speaker: Jambavan

verse_text: यह लघु जलधि तरत कति बारा। अस सुनि पुनि कह पवनकुमारा॥ प्रभु प्रताप बड़वानल भारी। सोषेउ प्रथम पयोनिधि बारी ॥
translation: फिर यह छोटा सा समुद्र पार करने में कितनी देर लगेगी? ऐसा सुनकर फिर पवनकुमार श्री हनुमान् जी ने कहा- प्रभु का प्रताप भारी बड़वानल (समुद्र की आग) के समान है। इसने पहले समुद्र के जल को सोख लिया था, ॥
english_translation: How long will it take to cross this small sea? Hearing this, Hanuman spoke again: The power of the Lord is like a great fire that had first dried up the ocean's waters.
essence: Ram's power makes even an ocean feel small.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says Ram's power is so great that it once dried up the ocean itself. He speaks to show that crossing this sea is no real obstacle for Ram's grace.
insight: It shifts the mind from measuring difficulty to remembering the power behind the mission.
modern_relevance: You're staring at a task that feels absurdly large, but someone you trust reminds you of what has already been carried through. The size of the obstacle changes when you remember the source of strength.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: तव रिपु नारि रुदन जल धारा। भरेउ बहोरि भयउ तेहिं खारा॥ सुनि अति उकुति पवनसुत केरी। हरषे कपि रघुपति तन हेरी ॥
translation: परन्तु आपके शत्रुओं की स्त्रियों के आँसुओं की धारा से यह फिर भर गया और उसी से खारा भी हो गया। हनुमान् जी की यह अत्युक्ति (अलंकारपूर्ण युक्ति) सुनकर वानर श्री रघुनाथजी की ओर देखकर हर्षित हो गए ॥
english_translation: But the tears of your enemies' women filled it again, and that made it salty. Hearing Hanuman's bold claim, the monkeys rejoiced, looking at Raghu's lord.
essence: Confidence can turn fear into momentum.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says the sea was filled again by the tears of the enemy women and became salty. The monkeys are delighted by his clever confidence and look toward Ram.
insight: It shows how courage can spread through a team by turning fear into shared momentum.
modern_relevance: You're in a tense group chat before a huge deadline, and one person makes a fearless joke that breaks the fear. The mood changes before the work does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जामवंत बोले दोउ भाई। नल नीलहि सब कथा सुनाई॥ राम प्रताप सुमिरि मन माहीं। करहु सेतु प्रयास कछु नाहीं ॥
translation: जाम्बवान् ने नल-नील दोनों भाइयों को बुलाकर उन्हें सारी कथा कह सुनाई (और कहा-) मन में श्री रामजी के प्रताप को स्मरण करके सेतु तैयार करो, (रामप्रताप से) कुछ भी परिश्रम नहीं होगा ॥
english_translation: Jambavan spoke to the two brothers, Nala and Nila, and told them the whole story. "Remember Ram's power in your heart and build the bridge; then the effort will feel light."
essence: Remember Ram, and the hardest work loses its weight.
simple_meaning: Keep Ram in mind while doing the task, and the work will not feel heavy.
insight: It shifts effort from self-reliance to remembrance of Ram's support.
modern_relevance: You're staring at a task that feels too big to start — a move, a deadline, a family crisis. Remembering what you stand for can make the burden feel workable.
speaker: Jambavan

verse_text: बोलि लिए कपि निकर बहोरी। सकल सुनहु बिनती कछु मोरी॥ राम चरन पंकज उर धरहू। कौतुक एक भालु कपि करहू ॥
translation: फिर वानरों के समूह को बुला लिया (और कहा-) आप सब लोग मेरी कुछ विनती सुनिए। अपने हृदय में श्री रामजी के चरण-कमलों को धारण कर लीजिए और सब भालू और वानर एक खेल कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Hanuman called the monkeys together again and said, "Listen to my request. Hold Ram's lotus feet in your heart, and let all the bears and monkeys join in one play."
essence: Ram in the heart turns hard work into joyful play.
simple_meaning: Hanuman gathers the monkeys and bears, asks them to keep Ram in their hearts, and urges them to begin the work with a playful spirit.
insight: It shifts action from strain to shared devotion, so effort becomes lighter and more unified.
modern_relevance: You walk into a volunteer shift, a family repair job, or a late-night team push already tired. Then someone reminds everyone why it matters, and the whole room changes. The burden softens when the heart is set right.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: धावहु मर्कट बिकट बरूथा। आनहु बिटप गिरिन्ह के जूथा॥ सुनि कपि भालु चले करि हूहा। जय रघुबीर प्रताप समूहा ॥
translation: विकट वानरों के समूह (आप) दौड़ जाइए और वृक्षों तथा पर्वतों के समूहों को उखाड़ लाइए। यह सुनकर वानर और भालू हूह (हुँकार) करके और श्री रघुनाथजी के प्रताप समूह की (अथवा प्रताप के पुंज श्री रामजी की) जय पुकारते हुए चले ॥
english_translation: Run, fierce monkeys, and bring whole trees and mountains. Hearing this, the monkeys and bears moved off with a roar, crying victory to Raghubir's power.
essence: When purpose is shared, even heavy work feels light.
simple_meaning: The monkey and bear army is ordered to fetch trees and mountains for the bridge, and they rush off cheering Ram's power.
insight: It shows how devotion to a shared cause can make hard labor feel like spirited play.
modern_relevance: A team hears the deadline has moved up, and nobody complains. Everyone stands up, grabs what they can, and gets moving because the mission is bigger than discomfort.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अति उतंग गिरि पादप लीलहिं लेहिं उठाइ। आनि देहिं नल नीलहि रचहिं ते सेतु बनाइ ॥
translation: बहुत ऊँचे-ऊँचे पर्वतों और वृक्षों को खेल की तरह ही (उखाड़कर) उठा लेते हैं और ला-लाकर नल-नील को देते हैं। वे अच्छी तरह गढ़कर (सुंदर) सेतु बनाते हैं ॥
english_translation: They lift huge mountains and trees as if playing, bring them to Nala and Neela, and build the bridge with skill.
essence: Shared zeal turns impossible obstacles into building material.
simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears move huge mountains and trees as if they were toys, handing them to Nala and Neela to build the bridge.
insight: It shows coordinated effort: many hands supply the raw material, and skilled builders turn it into structure.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सैल बिसाल आनि कपि देहीं। कंदुक इव नल नील ते लेहीं॥ देखि सेतु अति सुंदर रचना। बिहसि कृपानिधि बोले बचना ॥
translation: वानर बड़े-बड़े पहाड़ ला-लाकर देते हैं और नल-नील उन्हें गेंद की तरह ले लेते हैं। सेतु की अत्यंत सुंदर रचना देखकर कृपासिन्धु श्री रामजी हँसकर वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: The monkeys bring huge mountains, and Nala and Neela take them as if they were balls. Seeing the bridge's beautiful construction, the compassionate Lord smiled and spoke.
essence: Work becomes light when everyone gives their strength to one purpose.
simple_meaning: The monkeys keep bringing mountains, Nala and Neela use them like balls, and Ram smiles at the beautiful bridge being built.
insight: It shifts attention from the burden of the task to the joy created by coordinated service.
modern_relevance: You watch a team move heavy boxes up three flights of stairs, laughing through the strain, and the whole job feels lighter. Shared purpose changes exhaustion into play.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परम रम्य उत्तम यह धरनी। महिमा अमित जाइ नहिं बरनी॥ करिहउँ इहाँ संभु थापना। मोरे हृदयँ परम कलपना ॥
translation: यह (यहाँ की) भूमि परम रमणीय और उत्तम है। इसकी असीम महिमा वर्णन नहीं की जा सकती। मैं यहाँ शिवजी की स्थापना करूँगा। मेरे हृदय में यह महान् संकल्प है ॥
english_translation: This land is supremely beautiful and excellent. Its boundless glory cannot be described. I will establish Shiva here. That great resolve is in my heart.
essence: Victory becomes complete when humility makes room for reverence.
simple_meaning: This place is so beautiful and sacred that its greatness cannot be fully described. Ram resolves to establish Shiva there.
insight: It shifts success from self-congratulation to reverent gratitude.
modern_relevance: You reach the finish line and feel the urge to celebrate yourself. Instead, you pause, honor what made the work possible, and place respect before triumph.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनि कपीस बहु दूत पठाए। मुनिबर सकल बोलि लै आए॥ लिंग थापि बिधिवत करि पूजा। सिव समान प्रिय मोहि न दूजा ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के वचन सुनकर वानरराज सुग्रीव ने बहुत से दूत भेजे, जो सब श्रेष्ठ मुनियों को बुलाकर ले आए। शिवलिंग की स्थापना करके विधिपूर्वक उसका पूजन किया (फिर भगवान बोले-) शिवजी के समान मुझको दूसरा कोई प्रिय नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Hearing Ram's words, Sugriva sent many messengers and brought all the great sages. After establishing the ling and worshipping it properly, the Lord said, 'No one is dearer to me than Shiva.'
essence: True devotion honors what it loves without rivalry.
simple_meaning: Ram has the sages brought in, then honors Shiva by स्थापितing and worshipping the ling properly. He declares that no one is dearer to him than Shiva.
insight: It teaches you to let reverence guide action, even in the middle of urgency.
modern_relevance: Before a big confrontation, you stop, gather the right people, and make space for respect instead of ego. Real strength does not need to dismiss what it honors.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सिव द्रोही मम भगत कहावा। सो नर सपनेहुँ मोहि न पावा॥ संकर बिमुख भगति चह मोरी। सो नारकी मूढ़ मति थोरी ॥
translation: जो शिव से द्रोह रखता है और मेरा भक्त कहलाता है, वह मनुष्य स्वप्न में भी मुझे नहीं पाता। शंकरजी से विमुख होकर (विरोध करके) जो मेरी भक्ति चाहता है, वह नरकगामी, मूर्ख और अल्पबुद्धि है ॥
english_translation: One who opposes Shiva and still calls himself my devotee never finds me, even in dreams. One who wants my devotion while turning away from Shankar is foolish and headed for a lower realm.
essence: You cannot reach Ram by rejecting Shiva.
simple_meaning: Ram says that anyone who hates Shiva cannot truly reach him. Real devotion to Ram includes reverence for Shiva, not opposition to him.
insight: It shifts devotion from selective preference to respectful wholeness, where love for Ram includes honor for Shiva.
modern_relevance: You praise one teacher while sneering at the teacher they honor. That split reveals something in you, not in them. Real reverence doesn't need rivalry.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: संकरप्रिय मम द्रोही सिव द्रोही मम दास। ते नर करहिं कलप भरि घोर नरक महुँ बास ॥
translation: जिनको शंकरजी प्रिय हैं, परन्तु जो मेरे द्रोही हैं एवं जो शिवजी के द्रोही हैं और मेरे दास (बनना चाहते) हैं, वे मनुष्य कल्पभर घोर नरक में निवास करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who love Shankara but are hostile to me, and those who are hostile to Shankara while calling themselves my servants, dwell in terrible lower realms for a full cycle.
essence: Devotion to Ram cannot survive hostility toward Shiva.
simple_meaning: You cannot claim devotion to Ram while opposing Shiva. Real devotion does not split the divine into sides.
insight: It shifts devotion from preference to integrity: reverence must be consistent across what you honor.
modern_relevance: You praise one mentor in public, then mock the other who taught you the same discipline. The split feels clever for a moment, but it reveals divided loyalty, not devotion.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जे रामेस्वर दरसनु करिहहिं। ते तनु तजि मम लोक सिधरिहहिं॥ जो गंगाजलु आनि चढ़ाइहि। सो साजुज्य मुक्ति नर पाइहि ॥
translation: जो मनुष्य (मेरे स्थापित किए हुए इन) रामेश्वरजी का दर्शन करेंगे, वे शरीर छोड़कर मेरे लोक को जाएँगे और जो गंगाजल लाकर इन पर चढ़ावेगा, वह मनुष्य सायुज्य मुक्ति पावेगा (अर्थात् मेरे साथ एक हो जाएगा) ॥
english_translation: Whoever comes to see Rameshwar will leave the body and reach my realm. Whoever brings Ganga water and offers it there will attain union with me.
essence: A sincere offering at Rameshwar can carry you beyond the body.
simple_meaning: Seeing Rameshwar and offering Ganga water there brings the deepest freedom. The body is left behind, and the devotee reaches Ram's own realm.
insight: It shifts devotion from a ritual act to a direct path of belonging and release.
modern_relevance: You stand in a crowded temple queue with a small bottle of water in your hand, tired but sincere. The value is not in the size of the offering; it is in the heart that brings it.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: होइ अकाम जो छल तजि सेइहि। भगति मोरि तेहि संकर देइहि॥ मम कृत सेतु जो दरसनु करिही। सो बिनु श्रम भवसागर तरिही ॥
translation: जो छल छोड़कर और निष्काम होकर श्री रामेश्वरजी की सेवा करेंगे, उन्हें शंकरजी मेरी भक्ति देंगे और जो मेरे बनाए सेतु का दर्शन करेगा, वह बिना ही परिश्रम संसार रूपी समुद्र से तर जाएगा ॥
english_translation: Whoever serves me without desire and without deceit, Shiva will give them devotion to me. Whoever beholds the bridge I built will cross the ocean of becoming without effort.
essence: Clean service opens the door to devotion and release.
simple_meaning: A heart free from desire and deceit receives devotion, and even seeing Ram's bridge becomes a way across life's vast suffering.
insight: It shifts action from self-interest to pure offering, where sincerity itself becomes the path.
modern_relevance: You help someone late at night with no hidden agenda, no need to be praised, no plan to use it later. That clean-heartedness changes what the act becomes.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: राम बचन सब के जिय भाए। मुनिबर निज निज आश्रम आए॥ गिरिजा रघुपति कै यह रीती। संतत करहिं प्रनत पर प्रीती ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के वचन सबके मन को अच्छे लगे। तदनन्तर वे श्रेष्ठ मुनि अपने-अपने आश्रमों को लौट आए। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे पार्वती! श्री रघुनाथजी की यह रीति है कि वे शरणागत पर सदा प्रीति करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram's words pleased everyone's heart. Then the great sages returned to their own hermitages. Parvati, this is Raghu's way: he always loves those who take refuge in him.
essence: Surrender is answered by steady love.
simple_meaning: Ram's words satisfy everyone, and the sages return home. Shiva tells Parvati that Ram always loves and protects those who come to him in surrender.
insight: It shifts the mind from guarded self-protection to confident trust in surrender.
modern_relevance: After a hard conversation, the room goes quiet and you finally hear the one sentence you needed. The fear of being turned away loosens when you realize humility can still be met with warmth.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: बाँधा सेतु नील नल नागर। राम कृपाँ जसु भयउ उजागर॥ बूड़हिं आनहि बोरहिं जेई। भए उपल बोहित सम तेई ॥
translation: चतुर नल और नील ने सेतु बाँधा। श्री रामजी की कृपा से उनका यह (उज्ज्वल) यश सर्वत्र फैल गया। जो पत्थर आप डूबते हैं और दूसरों को डुबा देते हैं, वे ही जहाज के समान (स्वयं तैरने वाले और दूसरों को पार ले जाने वाले) हो गए ॥
english_translation: Nala and Nila built the bridge. By Ram's grace, their fame shone everywhere. The stones that sink and sink others became like ships.
essence: Ram's grace turns even sinking stones into a way across.
simple_meaning: Nala and Nila built the bridge, and Ram's grace made their work famous. Even heavy stones became like boats, carrying others across.
insight: It shifts attention from material limits to the transforming power of grace working through action.
modern_relevance: You fix something no one else can. What should have failed becomes the thing that carries everyone forward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: महिमा यह न जलधि कइ बरनी। पाहन गुन न कपिन्ह कइ करनी ॥
translation: यह न तो समुद्र की महिमा वर्णन की गई है, न पत्थरों का गुण है और न वानरों की ही कोई करामात है ॥
english_translation: The glory is neither the sea's nor the stones' nor the monkeys' alone.
essence: What looks like human achievement is really grace at work.
simple_meaning: The crossing was not only the sea's wonder, the stones' property, or the monkeys' skill. Ram's grace made it happen.
insight: It shifts credit from visible skill to the divine grace behind successful action.
modern_relevance: You finish a project that should have failed, and everyone praises the team, the tools, or the timing. Quietly, you know something larger carried the work through.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: श्री रघुबीर प्रताप ते सिंधु तरे पाषान। ते मतिमंद जे राम तजि भजहिं जाइ प्रभु आन ॥
translation: श्री रघुवीर के प्रताप से पत्थर भी समुद्र पर तैर गए। ऐसे श्री रामजी को छोड़कर जो किसी दूसरे स्वामी को जाकर भजते हैं वे (निश्चय ही) मंदबुद्धि हैं ॥
english_translation: By the power of Lord Raghubir, stones crossed the sea. Those who, abandoning Ram, go to worship another lord are surely dull-minded.
essence: Ram's power carries the impossible; turning elsewhere is self-defeating.
simple_meaning: Ram's power made stones float across the sea. So leaving Ram for another master is called foolish.
insight: It shifts you from divided loyalty to single-hearted refuge in Ram.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a problem that feels heavier than your own strength — a sick parent, a broken plan, a future you cannot engineer. This verse says: remember who has carried you before you start shopping for another anchor.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: बाँधि सेतु अति सुदृढ़ बनावा। देखि कृपानिधि के मन भावा॥ चली सेन कछु बरनि न जाई। गर्जहिं मर्कट भट समुदाई ॥
translation: नल-नील ने सेतु बाँधकर उसे बहुत मजबूत बनाया। देखने पर वह कृपानिधान श्री रामजी के मन को (बहुत ही) अच्छा लगा। सेना चली, जिसका कुछ वर्णन नहीं हो सकता। योद्धा वानरों के समुदाय गरज रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Nala and Nila built the bridge so strong that it pleased the compassionate Lord's heart. The army moved forward beyond description, and the monkey warriors roared as one.
essence: The bridge is ready, and the army can move.
simple_meaning: Nala and Nila finish the bridge, and Ram is pleased. Then the army advances with a roar that cannot be fully described.
insight: It marks the turning point from preparation to action, with no need for reflection or instruction.
modern_relevance: You finally finish the structure everyone depended on, and the room shifts from planning to movement. The real test begins only after the bridge holds.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सेतुबंध ढिग चढ़ि रघुराई। चितव कृपाल सिंधु बहुताई॥ देखन कहुँ प्रभु करुना कंदा। प्रगट भए सब जलचर बृंदा ॥
translation: कृपालु श्री रघुनाथजी सेतुबन्ध के तट पर चढ़कर समुद्र का विस्तार देखने लगे। करुणाकन्द (करुणा के मूल) प्रभु के दर्शन के लिए सब जलचरों के समूह प्रकट हो गए (जल के ऊपर निकल आए) ॥
english_translation: Raghunath climbed onto the bridge's edge and looked over the vast sea. At the sight of the compassionate one, all the creatures of the water emerged.
essence: Compassion makes even the hidden world come forward.
simple_meaning: Ram stands by the bridge and looks out over the sea. His compassionate presence draws all the sea-creatures into view.
insight: It frames stillness and compassion as forces that reveal what is otherwise unseen.
modern_relevance: You stop at the edge of something enormous — a decision, a loss, a future you can't see clearly — and the moment you soften, hidden things begin to surface.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मकर नक्र नाना झष ब्याला। सत जोजन तन परम बिसाला॥ अइसेउ एक तिन्हहि जे खाहीं। एकन्ह कें डर तेपि डेराहीं ॥
translation: बहुत तरह के मगर, नाक (घड़ियाल), मच्छ और सर्प थे, जिनके सौ-सौ योजन के बहुत बड़े विशाल शरीर थे। कुछ ऐसे भी जन्तु थे, जो उनको भी खा जाएँ। किसी-किसी के डर से तो वे भी डर रहे थे ॥
english_translation: There were many kinds of crocodiles, alligators, fish, and serpents, with bodies a hundred yojanas vast. Some creatures could even swallow them, and they too feared others.
essence: Even the fiercest beings live under fear.
simple_meaning: The sea is full of enormous, frightening creatures, and even the biggest ones are afraid of something bigger.
insight: It shifts attention from imagined monsters to the fact that every force has limits.
modern_relevance: Standing at the mouth of a dark tunnel, you notice how every shadow feels larger than the last. What looked dominant a moment ago is already afraid of something else.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभुहि बिलोकहिं टरहिं न टारे। मन हरषित सब भए सुखारे॥ तिन्ह कीं ओट न देखिअ बारी। मगन भए हरि रूप निहारी ॥
translation: वे सब (वैर-विरोध भूलकर) प्रभु के दर्शन कर रहे हैं, हटाने से भी नहीं हटते। सबके मन हर्षित हैं, सब सुखी हो गए। उनकी आड़ के कारण जल नहीं दिखाई पड़ता। वे सब भगवान् का रूप देखकर (आनंद और प्रेम में) मग्न हो गए ॥
english_translation: They all gaze at the Lord and cannot be driven away. Every heart is joyful and at ease. The water is hidden by their bodies. Seeing the form of Hari, they are lost in delight.
essence: Awe makes even the sea forget itself.
simple_meaning: The sea-creatures gather to see Ram and become so delighted that they do not move away, blocking the water from view.
insight: It simply records a shared burst of wonder, with no moral instruction.
modern_relevance: You stop mid-step at a street performance, and the crowd around the stage becomes part of the experience. The moment itself is the point, not what it teaches.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चला कटकु प्रभु आयसु पाई। को कहि सक कपि दल बिपुलाई ॥
translation: प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी की आज्ञा पाकर सेना चली। वानर सेना की विपुलता (अत्यधिक संख्या) को कौन कह सकता है? ॥
english_translation: The army moved forward after receiving the Lord's command. Who can describe the vast monkey host?
essence: Once the command is given, the vast force moves as one.
simple_meaning: After Ram gave the order, the monkey army moved out. Its size was so immense that no one could fully describe it.
insight: It shifts attention from the order itself to the unstoppable momentum that follows clear leadership.
modern_relevance: A team finally gets the green light, and the room shifts from planning to motion. The scale of what follows is bigger than anyone can neatly count.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सेतुबंध भइ भीर अति कपि नभ पंथ उड़ाहिं। अपर जलचरन्हि ऊपर चढ़ि चढ़ि पारहि जाहिं ॥
translation: सेतुबन्ध पर बड़ी भीड़ हो गई, इससे कुछ वानर आकाश मार्ग से उड़ने लगे और दूसरे (कितने ही) जलचर जीवों पर चढ़-चढ़कर पार जा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The bridge grew so crowded that some monkeys flew through the sky, while others climbed over water creatures and crossed the sea.
essence: The crossing is so crowded it turns into a spectacle.
simple_meaning: The crossing became so crowded that some monkeys flew overhead and others crossed by stepping over sea creatures.
insight: It shifts attention from meaning to spectacle, showing the crossing as a living scene.
modern_relevance: A festival crowd pours over a narrow bridge, people squeezing forward from every side. The verse captures motion, not instruction.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस कौतुक बिलोकि द्वौ भाई। बिहँसि चले कृपाल रघुराई॥ सेन सहित उतरे रघुबीरा। कहि न जाइ कपि जूथप भीरा ॥
translation: कृपालु रघुनाथजी (तथा लक्ष्मणजी) दोनों भाई ऐसा कौतुक देखकर हँसते हुए चले। श्री रघुवीर सेना सहित समुद्र के पार हो गए। वानरों और उनके सेनापतियों की भीड़ कही नहीं जा सकती ॥
english_translation: Seeing this strange spectacle, the two brothers laughed and moved on. The compassionate Raghunath crossed over with the army; the crowd of monkeys and their leaders cannot be counted.
essence: The crossing is so immense it becomes a sight to behold.
simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman laugh at the sight, then cross the sea with the army. The monkey hosts are so vast that no one can count them.
insight: It keeps attention on the unfolding scene rather than on interpretation or instruction.
modern_relevance: You watch a crowd pour out of a stadium after midnight, friends and strangers moving in one tide. The moment is bigger than any one person, and all you can do is keep walking.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिंधु पार प्रभु डेरा कीन्हा। सकल कपिन्ह कहुँ आयसु दीन्हा॥ खाहु जाइ फल मूल सुहाए। सुनत भालू कपि जहँ तहँ धाए ॥
translation: प्रभु ने समुद्र के पार डेरा डाला और सब वानरों को आज्ञा दी कि तुम जाकर सुंदर फल-मूल खाओ। यह सुनते ही रीछ-वानर जहाँ-तहाँ दौड़ पड़े ॥
english_translation: The Lord camped beyond the sea and told all the monkeys, "Go eat the lovely fruits and roots." Hearing this, the bears and monkeys rushed off in every direction.
essence: Even in war, Ram gives his followers rest.
simple_meaning: Ram sets up camp beyond the sea and tells the monkeys to go enjoy the fruit and roots nearby. The whole army then scatters happily to forage.
insight: It shifts attention from struggle to restoration without losing the larger mission.
modern_relevance: You finally finish the exhausting trip, drop your bags, and hear, "Go eat, rest, breathe." The job is not victory alone; it is also knowing when to release the strain.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब तरु फरे राम हित लागी। रितु अरु कुरितु काल गति त्यागी॥ खाहिं मधुर फल बिटप हलावहिं। लंका सन्मुख सिखर चलावहिं ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के हित (सेवा) के लिए सब वृक्ष ऋतु-कुऋतु- समय की गति को छोड़कर फल उठे। वानर-भालू मीठे फल खा रहे हैं, वृक्षों को हिला रहे हैं और पर्वतों के शिखरों को लंका की ओर फेंक रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: For Rama's sake, all the trees bore fruit, ignoring season, unseason, and the movement of time. The monkeys and bears ate sweet fruit, shook the trees, and hurled mountain peaks toward Lanka.
essence: When Ram is the aim, even nature seems to serve.
simple_meaning: The forest itself seems to cooperate with Ram's army. Trees bear fruit out of season, and the monkeys and bears use the land's gifts as they prepare for Lanka.
insight: It frames the march to Lanka as a world aligned with dharma, not just an army on the move.
modern_relevance: You're working late on a cause you believe in, and help appears from unexpected places — a friend texts, a tool works, a door opens. Momentum can feel like the world is joining in.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ कहुँ फिरत निसाचर पावहिं। घेरि सकल बहु नाच नचावहिं॥ दसनन्हि काटि नासिका काना। कहि प्रभु सुजसु देहिं तब जाना ॥
translation: घूमते-घूमते जहाँ कहीं किसी राक्षस को पा जाते हैं तो सब उसे घेरकर खूब नाच नचाते हैं और दाँतों से उसके नाक-कान काटकर, प्रभु का सुयश कहकर (अथवा कहलाकर) तब उसे जाने देते हैं ॥
english_translation: Wherever they find a demon wandering, they surround him and make him dance a lot. Then they bite off his nose and ears with their teeth, speak the Lord's fame, and only then let him go.
essence: Ram's fame travels even through the enemy's humiliation.
simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears torment any demon they find, cut off his nose and ears, and only then let him leave after praising Ram.
insight: It shows the enemy's fear spreading through humiliation and word of Ram's power.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जिन्ह कर नासा कान निपाता। तिन्ह रावनहि कही सब बाता॥ सुनत श्रवन बारिधि बंधाना। दस मुख बोलि उठा अकुलाना ॥
translation: जिन राक्षसों के नाक और कान काट डाले गए, उन्होंने रावण से सब समाचार कहा। समुद्र (पर सेतु) का बाँधा जाना कानों से सुनते ही रावण घबड़ाकर दसों मुखों से बोल उठा- ॥
english_translation: The demons whose noses and ears had been cut off told Ravana everything. Hearing that the ocean had been bridged, Ravana grew uneasy and spoke with all ten mouths.
essence: Denial collapses the moment the facts become impossible to ignore.
simple_meaning: Wounded demons report the news to Ravana, and the report of the bridge across the ocean shakes him badly.
insight: It shows how fear spreads when a person can no longer deny the scale of what is coming.
modern_relevance: You keep hearing updates that everything is slipping beyond your control. One message, one headline, one call — and the confidence you built starts to wobble.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बाँध्यो बननिधि नीरनिधि जलधि सिंधु बारीस। सत्य तोयनिधि कंपति उदधि पयोधि नदीस ॥
translation: वननिधि, नीरनिधि, जलधि, सिंधु, वारीश, तोयनिधि, कंपति, उदधि, पयोधि, नदीश को क्या सचमुच ही बाँध लिया? ॥
english_translation: Has the ocean of waters really been bound? The sea, the great river-lord, trembles at the news.
essence: What seemed unbridgeable now trembles before Ram's resolve.
simple_meaning: The verse marvels that the sea itself seems shaken by the news that Ram's army has bound it. It is a poetic question, not a teaching.
insight: It frames a near-impossible achievement as a fact that unsettles pride.
modern_relevance: You hear that the thing everyone called impossible is already underway, and your own certainty wobbles for a moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निज बिकलता बिचारि बहोरी॥ बिहँसि गयउ गृह करि भय भोरी॥ मंदोदरीं सुन्यो प्रभु आयो। कौतुकहीं पाथोधि बँधायो ॥
translation: फिर अपनी व्याकुलता को समझकर (ऊपर से) हँसता हुआ, भय को भुलाकर, रावण महल को गया। (जब) मंदोदरी ने सुना कि प्रभु श्री रामजी आ गए हैं और उन्होंने खेल में ही समुद्र को बँधवा लिया है, ॥
english_translation: After thinking over his own agitation, Ravana laughed it off and went back to the palace, putting fear aside. When Mandodari heard that Lord Ram had arrived and had bound the ocean almost playfully,
essence: Fear can be disguised, but it still follows you home.
simple_meaning: Ravana tries to shake off his fear and return to the palace, while Mandodari hears that Ram has arrived and has bound the ocean easily.
insight: It shows how ego tries to mask fear with laughter, even when reality has already shifted.
modern_relevance: You get alarming news, force a calm face, and walk back into the meeting as if nothing happened. Inside, the fear is still there, waiting.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कर गहि पतिहि भवन निज आनी। बोली परम मनोहर बानी॥ चरन नाइ सिरु अंचलु रोपा। सुनहु बचन पिय परिहरि कोपा ॥
translation: (तब) वह हाथ पकड़कर, पति को अपने महल में लाकर परम मनोहर वाणी बोली। चरणों में सिर नवाकर उसने अपना आँचल पसारा और कहा- हे प्रियतम! क्रोध त्याग कर मेरा वचन सुनिए ॥
english_translation: Then she took her husband by the hand and brought him into her palace. She spoke in a most lovely voice. Bowing her head at his feet, she spread out her garment and said, “My beloved, please set aside your anger and hear me.”
essence: Gentle speech can reach even an angry heart.
simple_meaning: Mandodari gently brings Ravana inside, bows to him, and asks him to drop his anger and listen to her.
insight: It teaches you to lower the temperature before you try to be heard.
modern_relevance: Your partner comes home furious after a humiliating day, and every sharp reply would only deepen the wound. This verse shows the power of soft words when anger is already burning.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: नाथ बयरु कीजे ताही सों। बुधि बल सकिअ जीति जाही सों॥ तुम्हहि रघुपतिहि अंतर कैसा। खलु खद्योत दिनकरहि जैसा ॥
translation: हे नाथ! वैर उसी के साथ करना चाहिए, जिससे बुद्धि और बल के द्वारा जीत सकें। आप में और श्री रघुनाथजी में निश्चय ही कैसा अंतर है, जैसा जुगनू और सूर्य में! ॥
english_translation: O Lord, you should fight only with someone you can defeat by intelligence and strength. What difference is there between you and Raghupati? The wicked are like fireflies before the sun.
essence: Pride fails when it mistakes a firefly for the sun.
simple_meaning: Mandodari warns Ravana that enmity should be chosen only against someone he can actually defeat. She says his power is nothing beside Ram's, like a firefly beside the sun.
insight: It shifts you from ego-driven conflict to clear-eyed judgment about who and what you can truly oppose.
modern_relevance: You send the angry reply, then stare at the screen and realise the other person can ruin your day, not your life. Mandodari's warning says: don't confuse noise with power.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: अति बल मधु कैटभ जेहिं मारे। महाबीर दितिसुत संघारे॥ जेहिं बलि बाँधि सहस भुज मारा। सोइ अवतरेउ हरन महि भारा ॥
translation: जिन्होंने (विष्णु रूप से) अत्यन्त बलवान् मधु और कैटभ (दैत्य) मारे और (वराह और नृसिंह रूप से) महान् शूरवीर दिति के पुत्रों (हिरण्याक्ष और हिरण्यकशिपु) का संहार किया, जिन्होंने (वामन रूप से) बलि को बाँधा और (परशुराम रूप से) सहस्रबाहु को मारा, वे ही (भगवान् ) पृथ्वी का भार हरण करने के लिए (रामरूप में) अवतीर्ण (प्रकट) हुए हैं! ॥
english_translation: The one who destroyed mighty Madhu and Kaitabha, who slew the great warrior sons of Diti, who bound Bali and killed Sahasrabahu, has now appeared as Ram to lift the burden of the earth.
essence: The same power that conquered chaos has arrived in gentle form.
simple_meaning: The speaker praises Ram as the same supreme being who once defeated many mighty enemies and has now appeared on earth to remove its burden.
insight: It shifts the mind from fearing appearances to trusting the power behind them.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a problem that feels ancient and unbeatable, as if it has defeated everyone before you. This verse says the force that can lift it is not new, weak, or uncertain.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: तासु बिरोध न कीजिअ नाथा। काल करम जिव जाकें हाथा ॥
translation: हे नाथ! उनका विरोध न कीजिए, जिनके हाथ में काल, कर्म और जीव सभी हैं ॥
english_translation: O Lord, do not oppose the one in whose hands are time, action, and every living being.
essence: Resistance is foolish before the one who governs time and life.
simple_meaning: Do not oppose Ram, because time, action, and every living being are under his control.
insight: It shifts the mind from defiance to surrender before the power that governs all outcomes.
modern_relevance: You are arguing with a situation that has already moved beyond your control: a diagnosis, a breakup, a deadline, a loss. This verse asks you to stop resisting reality and bow to what is greater than your will.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: रामहि सौंपि जानकी नाइ कमल पद माथ। सुत कहुँ राज समर्पि बन जाइ भजिअ रघुनाथ ॥
translation: (श्री रामजी) के चरण कमलों में सिर नवाकर (उनकी शरण में जाकर) उनको जानकीजी सौंप दीजिए और आप पुत्र को राज्य देकर वन में जाकर श्री रघुनाथजी का भजन कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Bow your head at Ram's lotus feet, entrust Janaki to him, give the kingdom to your son, and go to the forest to worship Raghunath.
essence: True devotion begins when you stop trying to keep what was never yours.
simple_meaning: Bow to Ram, hand over what you love, and stop clinging to power. Real devotion is choosing him over possession.
insight: It shifts the mind from possession to surrender, showing that devotion begins where control ends.
modern_relevance: You finally admit you cannot keep everything: the relationship, the role, the control. Instead of forcing it, you hand over what you cannot hold and choose what matters most.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: नाथ दीनदयाल रघुराई। बाघउ सनमुख गएँ न खाई॥ चाहिअ करन सो सब करि बीते। तुम्ह सुर असुर चराचर जीते ॥
translation: हे नाथ! श्री रघुनाथजी तो दीनों पर दया करने वाले हैं। सम्मुख (शरण) जाने पर तो बाघ भी नहीं खाता। आपको जो कुछ करना चाहिए था, वह सब आप कर चुके। आपने देवता, राक्षस तथा चर-अचर सभी को जीत लिया ॥
english_translation: O Lord, Raghunath is kind to the poor. Even a tiger does not eat when one approaches him in surrender. You have already done all that needed doing. You have conquered the gods, demons, and all moving and unmoving beings.
essence: Surrender to Ram, and even fear loses its power.
simple_meaning: Ram is compassionate to anyone who comes to him openly. The speaker says the listener has already done everything required and has already conquered every being.
insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to surrender, and from self-effort to refuge in Ram.
modern_relevance: You’ve spent the whole night trying to fix what cannot be forced. The moment you stop bracing and ask for help honestly, the room feels less hostile.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: संत कहहिं असि नीति दसानन। चौथेंपन जाइहि नृप कानन॥ तासु भजनु कीजिअ तहँ भर्ता। जो कर्ता पालक संहर्ता ॥
translation: हे दशमुख! संतजन ऐसी नीति कहते हैं कि चौथेपन (बुढ़ापे) में राजा को वन में चला जाना चाहिए। हे स्वामी! वहाँ (वन में) आप उनका भजन कीजिए जो सृष्टि के रचने वाले, पालने वाले और संहार करने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: The saints say this policy, O Ravana: in old age, a king should go to the forest. There, O master, worship the one who creates, sustains, and destroys all.
essence: Power should end in reverence, not in more grasping.
simple_meaning: A ruler should eventually leave worldly power behind and turn toward worship of the one behind creation, preservation, and dissolution.
insight: It shifts the mind from preserving status to preparing for a deeper reckoning.
modern_relevance: You’ve spent decades building a name, a company, a family role, a reputation. Then one day the noise drops, and the deeper question arrives: what have you been serving all along?
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सोइ रघुबीर प्रनत अनुरागी। भजहु नाथ ममता सब त्यागी॥ मुनिबर जतनु करहिं जेहि लागी। भूप राजु तजि होहिं बिरागी ॥
translation: हे नाथ! आप विषयों की सारी ममता छोड़कर उन्हीं शरणागत पर प्रेम करने वाले भगवान् का भजन कीजिए। जिनके लिए श्रेष्ठ मुनि साधन करते हैं और राजा राज्य छोड़कर वैरागी हो जाते हैं- ॥
english_translation: O Lord, worship that Raghubir who loves the surrendered and is loved by those who have given up all attachment. Great sages practice austerity to reach Him, and kings renounce their kingdoms to become detached.
essence: The one you seek comes closest when you stop clinging.
simple_meaning: Ram is reached by letting go of possessiveness. Sages strive for Him, and even kings renounce power to become detached.
insight: It shifts devotion from bargaining to release, showing that attachment itself blocks nearness.
modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone, hoping one message will settle your heart. But the ache only loosens when you stop clinging to control and make room for something deeper.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सोइ कोसलाधीस रघुराया। आयउ करन तोहि पर दाया॥ जौं पिय मानहु मोर सिखावन। सुजसु होइ तिहुँ पुर अति पावन ॥
translation: वही कोसलाधीश श्री रघुनाथजी आप पर दया करने आए हैं। हे प्रियतम! यदि आप मेरी सीख मान लेंगे, तो आपका अत्यंत पवित्र और सुंदर यश तीनों लोकों में फैल जाएगा ॥
english_translation: That Lord of Kosala, Raghu's king, has come to show you mercy. Dear one, if you accept my counsel, your pure fame will spread through all three worlds.
essence: Mercy is already here; your pride decides whether it becomes fame or ruin.
simple_meaning: Ram has come to show mercy, and Mandodari urges Ravana to accept her advice so his name can become pure and honored everywhere.
insight: It shifts the mind from stubborn pride to the possibility of repair through humility.
modern_relevance: A friend calls you after a reckless decision and tells you there is still time to stop. The advice is uncomfortable, but accepting it could save your name and your future.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: अस कहि नयन नीर भरि गहि पद कंपित गात। नाथ भजहु रघुनाथहि अचल होइ अहिवात ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर, नेत्रों में (करुणा का) जल भरकर और पति के चरण पकड़कर, काँपते हुए शरीर से मंदोदरी ने कहा- हे नाथ! श्री रघुनाथजी का भजन कीजिए, जिससे मेरा सुहाग अचल हो जाए ॥
english_translation: After saying this, with tears filling her eyes and clasping her husband's feet, her body trembling, Mandodari said: "O lord, worship Raghunath so that my married life may remain unbroken."
essence: Devotion can become the last shelter when everything else is collapsing.
simple_meaning: Mandodari begs Ravana to worship Ram so her married life can remain secure. Her plea comes from fear, love, and a last hope for protection.
insight: It shifts the mind from control and pride toward humble refuge in Ram.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you love double down on a choice that is clearly разрушing everything. In that moment, you stop negotiating and plead for the one change that could still hold the relationship together.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: तब रावन मयसुता उठाई। कहै लाग खल निज प्रभुताई॥ सुनु तैं प्रिया बृथा भय माना। जग जोधा को मोहि समाना ॥
translation: तब रावण ने मंदोदरी को उठाया और वह दुष्ट उससे अपनी प्रभुता कहने लगा- हे प्रिये! सुन, तूने व्यर्थ ही भय मान रखा है। बता तो जगत् में मेरे समान योद्धा है कौन? ॥
english_translation: Then Ravana lifted Mandodari and began boasting of his own power. "Listen, my dear, your fear is pointless. Tell me, who in the world is my equal as a warrior?"
essence: Pride makes a person dismiss the very warning meant to save them.
simple_meaning: Ravana comforts Mandodari by bragging about his own strength and saying no warrior in the world matches him.
insight: It exposes how self-importance blocks clear seeing and turns warning into a threat to the ego.
modern_relevance: You hear the warning in a partner's voice, but instead of listening, you start listing your achievements. That reflex to defend your ego can blind you to danger.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: बरुन कुबेर पवन जम काला। भुज बल जितेउँ सकल दिगपाला॥ देव दनुज नर सब बस मोरें। कवन हेतु उपजा भय तोरें ॥
translation: वरुण, कुबेर, पवन, यमराज आदि सभी दिक्पालों को तथा काल को भी मैंने अपनी भुजाओं के बल से जीत रखा है। देवता, दानव और मनुष्य सभी मेरे वश में हैं। फिर तुझको यह भय किस कारण उत्पन्न हो गया? ॥
english_translation: Varuna, Kubera, the wind, Yama, and even Time have all been conquered by the strength of my arms. Gods, demons, and humans are all under my control. Then why has fear arisen in you?
essence: Domination is hollow when fear still owns you.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he has conquered all powers and beings, so Mandodari should not fear. His words reveal arrogance, not true strength.
insight: It shifts attention from outward dominance to the hidden insecurity that drives it.
modern_relevance: You have the title, the money, the team, and the reputation — yet one worried thought can still wreck your night. Ravana's speech sounds like control, but it is fear wearing armor.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: नाना बिधि तेहि कहेसि बुझाई। सभाँ बहोरि बैठ सो जाई॥ मंदोदरीं हृदयँ अस जाना। काल बस्य उपजा अभिमाना ॥
translation: मंदोदरी ने उसे बहुत तरह से समझाकर कहा (किन्तु रावण ने उसकी एक भी बात न सुनी) और वह फिर सभा में जाकर बैठ गया। मंदोदरी ने हृदय में ऐसा जान लिया कि काल के वश होने से पति को अभिमान हो गया है ॥
english_translation: Mandodari tried to explain to him in many ways, but he did not listen. He went back and sat in the assembly. Mandodari understood in her heart that, under time's grip, his pride had arisen.
essence: Pride grows fastest when time is already against you.
simple_meaning: Mandodari tries to warn Ravana, but he returns to the assembly unmoved. She sees that time has already fed his pride.
insight: It shows how unchecked pride shuts down counsel and blinds a person to danger.
modern_relevance: Someone you love keeps brushing off every warning, laughing it off as if nothing can touch them. You can see the drift toward disaster long before they can.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सभाँ आइ मंत्रिन्ह तेहिं बूझा। करब कवन बिधि रिपु सैं जूझा॥ कहहिं सचिव सुनु निसिचर नाहा। बार बार प्रभु पूछहु काहा ॥
translation: सभा में आकर उसने मंत्रियों से पूछा कि शत्रु के साथ किस प्रकार से युद्ध करना होगा? मंत्री कहने लगे- हे राक्षसों के नाथ! हे प्रभु! सुनिए, आप बार-बार क्या पूछते हैं? ॥
english_translation: Coming to the assembly, he asked his ministers how the enemy should be fought. The ministers said, 'Listen, lord of the demons, why do you keep asking again and again?'
essence: Pride asks for strategy after it has already refused wisdom.
simple_meaning: Ravana asks his ministers how to fight the enemy, but they answer with impatience, as if he is asking the obvious.
insight: It exposes how ego keeps seeking confirmation instead of correction.
modern_relevance: You call a meeting after ignoring every warning, then ask for advice as if the answer were still missing. The room already knows the real problem: you won't listen.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: कहहु कवन भय करिअ बिचारा। नर कपि भालु अहार हमारा ॥
translation: कहिए तो (ऐसा) कौन-सा बड़ा भय है, जिसका विचार किया जाए? (भय की बात ही क्या है?) मनुष्य और वानर-भालू तो हमारे भोजन (की सामग्री) हैं॥
english_translation: Tell me, what fear should be considered? Human beings, monkeys, and bears are our food.
essence: Arrogance makes real danger look laughably small.
simple_meaning: Ravana dismisses the danger, saying there is no reason to fear because humans, monkeys, and bears are his prey.
insight: It shows how pride blinds judgment and turns caution into mockery.
modern_relevance: A manager laughs off a small competitor, calling them irrelevant, then loses the market because he never took them seriously.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सब के बचन श्रवन सुनि कह प्रहस्त कर जोरि। नीति बिरोध न करिअ प्रभु मंत्रिन्ह मति अति थोरि ॥
translation: कानों से सबके वचन सुनकर (रावण का पुत्र) प्रहस्त हाथ जोड़कर कहने लगा- हे प्रभु! नीति के विरुद्ध कुछ भी नहीं करना चाहिए, मन्त्रियों में बहुत ही थोड़ी बुद्धि है ॥
english_translation: Hearing everyone's words, Prahasta joined his hands and said, "Lord, do not act against policy; your ministers have very little wisdom."
essence: Rash power still needs wise restraint.
simple_meaning: Prahasta warns Ravana not to ignore good judgment. He says the ministers are foolish, but the larger point is that rash action against right conduct is dangerous.
insight: It shifts the mind from crowd confidence to sober judgment before action.
modern_relevance: A group chat is cheering a risky plan, and one person finally says, "Hold on — this is not smart." That pause can save everyone from a mistake.
speaker: Prahasta

verse_text: कहहिं सचिव सठ ठकुर सोहाती। नाथ न पूर आव एहि भाँती॥ बारिधि नाघि एक कपि आवा। तासु चरित मन महुँ सबु गावा॥ ॥
translation: ये सभी मूर्ख (खुशामदी) मन्त्र ठकुरसुहाती (मुँहदेखी) कह रहे हैं। हे नाथ! इस प्रकार की बातों से पूरा नहीं पड़ेगा। एक ही बंदर समुद्र लाँघकर आया था। उसका चरित्र सब लोग अब भी मन-ही-मन गाया करते हैं (स्मरण किया करते हैं) ॥
english_translation: These flattering ministers are speaking like fools. Lord, this kind of talk will not fill the need. One monkey crossed the ocean, and everyone still remembers his story in their hearts.
essence: Real deeds outlast polished talk.
simple_meaning: Empty praise is useless here. What matters is the example of Hanuman, whose crossing of the ocean is still remembered.
insight: It shifts attention from flattering speech to proven action and memorable service.
modern_relevance: A room full of advisors nods politely while the problem keeps growing. Then one person points to the only thing that actually worked, and the whole mood changes.
speaker: Ravana's ministers

verse_text: छुधा न रही तुम्हहि तब काहू। जारत नगरु कस न धरि खाहू॥ सुनत नीक आगें दुख पावा। सचिवन अस मत प्रभुहि सुनावा॥ ॥
translation: उस समय तुम लोगों में से किसी को भूख न थी? (बंदर तो तुम्हारा भोजन ही हैं, फिर) नगर जलाते समय उसे पकड़कर क्यों नहीं खा लिया? इन मन्त्रियों ने स्वामी (आप) को ऐसी सम्मति सुनायी है जो सुनने में अच्छी है पर जिससे आगे चलकर दुःख पाना होगा ॥
english_translation: Weren't you all hungry then? Why didn't you catch and eat him when he was burning the city? The ministers gave their lord advice that sounded pleasant but would bring sorrow later.
essence: Pleasant advice can be the first step toward suffering.
simple_meaning: The speaker mocks the ministers: if the monkeys were so hungry, why didn't they catch and eat Hanuman while he burned the city? Pleasant advice can still lead to later suffering.
insight: It warns you to test advice by consequence, not by how soothing it sounds.
modern_relevance: A friend says, 'Just say yes, keep the peace.' It sounds kind in the moment, but you know it will cost you later.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जेहिं बारीस बँधायउ हेला। उतरेउ सेन समेत सुबेला॥ सो भनु मनुज खाब हम भाई। बचन कहहिं सब गाल फुलाई ॥
translation: जिसने खेल-ही-खेल में समुद्र बँधा लिया और जो सेना सहित सुबेल पर्वत पर आ उतरा है। हे भाई! कहो वह मनुष्य है, जिसे कहते हो कि हम खा लेंगे? सब गाल फुला-फुलाकर (पागलों की तरह) वचन कह रहे हैं! ॥
english_translation: He who, in play, bound the ocean and then descended with an army at Suvela—brother, is that the man you say we can eat? They speak with puffed cheeks like fools.
essence: You cannot reduce great power to a joke.
simple_meaning: Ravana's side is mocking the idea that Hanuman can be eaten. They point out that someone who bound the ocean and arrived with an army is no ordinary man.
insight: It shifts the mind from contempt to recognition of true strength.
modern_relevance: You laugh at the quiet newcomer in the room, then realize they already handled the thing everyone else feared. Mockery fades fast when reality walks in.
speaker: Ravana's warriors

verse_text: तात बचन मम सुनु अति आदर। जनि मन गुनहु मोहि करि कादर। प्रिय बानी जे सुनहिं जे कहहीं। ऐसे नर निकाय जग अहहीं ॥
translation: हे तात! मेरे वचनों को बहुत आदर से (बड़े गौर से) सुनिए। मुझे मन में कायर न समझ लीजिएगा। जगत् में ऐसे मनुष्य झुंड-के-झुंड (बहुत अधिक) हैं, जो प्यारी (मुँह पर मीठी लगने वाली) बात ही सुनते और कहते हैं ॥
english_translation: My dear father, listen to my words with great respect. Do not think of me as a coward in your mind. In this world, people are many who only hear and speak pleasant words.
essence: Pleasant words are common; truthful ones are rare.
simple_meaning: Ravana asks his father to hear him respectfully and not judge him as weak. He says most people only like sweet words and repeat them.
insight: It trains you to value honest speech over approval-seeking language.
modern_relevance: You finally say what needs saying in a family argument, and everyone wants the softer version. Ravana is naming that reflex: people often prefer pleasant words over useful ones.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: बचन परम हित सुनत कठोरे। सुनहिं जे कहहिं ते नर प्रभु थोरे॥ प्रथम बसीठ पठउ सुनु नीती। सीता देइ करहु पुनि प्रीती ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! सुनने में कठोर परन्तु (परिणाम में) परम हितकारी वचन जो सुनते और कहतेहैं,वे मनुष्य बहुत ही थोड़े हैं। नीति सुनिये, (उसके अनुसार) पहले दूत भेजिये, और (फिर) सीता को देकर श्रीरामजी से प्रीति (मेल) कर लीजिये ॥
english_translation: Words that are harsh to hear but deeply beneficial are heard and spoken by very few. Follow policy: first send an envoy, then give Sita and make peace with Ram.
essence: The hardest advice is often the one that saves you.
simple_meaning: Few people can hear and speak words that sting at first but help in the end. The advice here is practical: send a messenger first, then make peace by returning Sita.
insight: It shifts you from pride-driven reaction to strategic restraint and reconciliation.
modern_relevance: A tense family group chat is spiraling, and the one message that could calm everything feels hardest to send. The verse values the advice that stings before it saves you from a bigger mess.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: नारि पाइ फिरि जाहिं जौं तौ न बढ़ाइअ रारि। नाहिं त सन्मुख समर महि तात करिअ हठि मारि ॥
translation: यदि वे स्त्री पाकर लौट जाएँ, तब तो (व्यर्थ) झगड़ा न बढ़ाइये। नहीं तो (यदि न फिरें तो) हे तात! सम्मुख युद्धभूमि में उनसे हठपूर्वक (डटकर) मार-काट कीजिए ॥
english_translation: If they return after finding the woman, do not prolong the quarrel. Otherwise, father, face them in open battle and strike them down with resolve.
essence: Stop the quarrel if the goal is met; fight only when conflict is unavoidable.
simple_meaning: If the enemy leaves after finding Sita, do not drag out the fight. If they refuse, meet them head-on and fight firmly.
insight: It teaches you to separate unnecessary conflict from necessary action, and to respond accordingly.
modern_relevance: A tense family argument is heading toward a blowup. One part of you wants to keep proving a point; another knows when to stop. This verse is about knowing the difference.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: यह मत जौं मानहु प्रभु मोरा। उभय प्रकार सुजसु जग तोरा॥ सुत सन कह दसकंठ रिसाई। असि मति सठ केहिं तोहि सिखाई ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! यदि आप मेरी यह सम्मति मानेंगे, तो जगत् में दोनों ही प्रकार से आपका सुयश होगा। रावण ने गुस्से में भरकर पुत्र से कहा- अरे मूर्ख! तुझे ऐसी बुद्धि किसने सिखायी? ॥
english_translation: “If you accept my advice, your fame will spread in both ways. Ravana, furious, said to his son, ‘Fool, who taught you such thinking?’”
essence: Pride hears counsel as an insult.
simple_meaning: Ravana urges his son to accept his advice, claiming it will protect his reputation either way. Then he angrily insults his son for disagreeing.
insight: It shows how ego converts guidance into threat and shuts down listening.
modern_relevance: You offer careful feedback in a tense family argument, and the other person hears only disrespect. The real issue is no longer the advice — it is wounded pride.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: अबहीं ते उर संसय होई। बेनुमूल सुत भयहु घमोई॥ सुनि पितु गिरा परुष अति घोरा। चला भवन कहि बचन कठोरा ॥
translation: अभी से हृदय में सन्देह (भय) हो रहा है? हे पुत्र! तू तो बाँस की जड़ में घमोई हुआ (तू मेरे वंश के अनुकूल या अनुरूप नहीं हुआ)। पिता की अत्यन्त घोर और कठोर वाणी सुनकर प्रहस्त ये कड़े वचन कहता हुआ घर को चला गया ॥
english_translation: Is doubt already rising in your heart? O son, you are not fitting the line of bamboo. Hearing his father's harsh, terrible words, Prahasta left for his house, speaking hard words.
essence: Pride makes even guidance feel like rejection.
simple_meaning: A father rebukes his son so harshly that the son leaves in anger and hurt. The verse shows a family split by pride and cutting words.
insight: It highlights how criticism without care turns advice into resistance.
modern_relevance: A parent says one sharp sentence at the dinner table, and the room goes cold. No one throws a plate, but the damage is already done.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: हित मत तोहि न लागत कैसें। काल बिबस कहुँ भेषज जैसें॥ संध्या समय जानि दससीसा। भवन चलेउ निरखत भुज बीसा ॥
translation: हित की सलाह आपको कैसे नहीं लगती (आप पर कैसे असर नहीं करती), जैसे मृत्यु के वश हुए (रोगी) को दवा नहीं लगती। संध्या का समय जानकर रावण अपनी बीसों भुजाओं को देखता हुआ महल को चला ॥
english_translation: Why does good advice not affect you, like medicine does not help a person already seized by death? Knowing it was evening, Ravana went home, looking at his twenty arms.
essence: Pride makes even life-saving counsel useless.
simple_meaning: Ravana is beyond advice, like a dying patient beyond medicine. He heads home at dusk, still admiring his twenty arms.
insight: It shifts attention from the advice itself to the ego that refuses to receive it.
modern_relevance: Someone keeps brushing off every warning, even after the third friend, the doctor, and the email all say the same thing. Pride makes the message feel optional.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लंका सिखर उपर आगारा। अति बिचित्र तहँ होइ अखारा॥ बैठ जाइ तेहिं मंदिर रावन। लागे किंनर गुन गन गावन ॥
translation: लंका की चोटी पर एक अत्यन्त विचित्र महल था। वहाँ नाच-गान का अखाड़ा जमता था। रावण उस महल में जाकर बैठ गया। किन्नर उसके गुण समूहों को गाने लगे ॥
english_translation: Atop Lanka's peak stood a wondrous hall. There the arena of music and dance was held. Ravana sat in that palace, and the celestial singers praised his qualities.
essence: Ravana's grandeur is already hollow with self-importance.
simple_meaning: Ravana sits in a magnificent palace on Lanka's peak, where celestial singers praise him and music fills the hall.
insight: It shifts attention from outer splendor to the ego that feeds on it.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is flattering the most powerful person there. The applause sounds grand, but you can already feel how fragile it is.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बाजहिं ताल पखाउज बीना। नृत्य करहिं अपछरा प्रबीना ॥
translation: ताल (करताल), पखावज (मृदंग) और बीणा बज रहे हैं। नृत्य में प्रवीण अप्सराएँ नाच रही हैं ॥
english_translation: Cymbals, drums, and veenas are sounding, and skilled celestial dancers are performing.
essence: Luxury can keep dancing while ruin waits overhead.
simple_meaning: The verse describes the music and dancing happening in Ravana's palace. It is a scene-setting detail, not a teaching.
insight: It shows how pleasure can keep going even when danger is already at the door.
modern_relevance: You walk into a party where the lights are perfect and everyone is laughing, but the room feels strangely hollow. The celebration is real; so is the warning underneath it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनासीर सत सरिस सो संतत करइ बिलास। परम प्रबल रिपु सीस पर तद्यपि सोच न त्रास ॥
translation: वह निरन्तर सैकड़ों इन्द्रों के समान भोग-विलास करता रहता है। यद्यपि (श्रीरामजी-सरीखा) अत्यन्त प्रबल शत्रु सिर पर है, फिर भी उसको न तो चिन्ता है और न डर ही है ॥
english_translation: He keeps enjoying pleasures like a hundred Indras, yet a far stronger enemy stands over his head, and still he feels neither worry nor fear.
essence: Luxury can blind you to the danger already at your door.
simple_meaning: Ravana is still lost in luxury even though Ram, his greatest enemy, is closing in. He feels no fear or concern at all.
insight: It warns you to notice when comfort is covering denial.
modern_relevance: You keep scrolling, shopping, or partying while the deadline, the diagnosis, or the hard conversation waits outside the door. Distraction can feel like power right up to the moment it collapses.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: इहाँ सुबेल सैल रघुबीरा। उतरे सेन सहित अति भीरा॥ सिखर एक उतंग अति देखी। परम रम्य सम सुभ्र बिसेषी ॥
translation: यहाँ श्री रघुवीर सुबेल पर्वत पर सेना की बड़ी भीड़ (बड़े समूह) के साथ उतरे। पर्वत का एक बहुत ऊँचा, परम रमणीय, समतल और विशेष रूप से उज्ज्वल शिखर देखकर- ॥
english_translation: Here, on Mount Suvel, Raghubir descended with a great crowd of his army. Seeing one very high summit, wonderfully beautiful, level, and especially bright—
essence: A single fitting place can shape everything that follows.
simple_meaning: Ram arrives at Mount Suvel with his army and notices a high, beautiful, level, bright summit.
insight: It shifts attention from movement to location, showing that even a war depends on choosing the right ground.
modern_relevance: You arrive at a crowded hillside before a long day’s work, scanning for the one flat spot where everyone can gather and breathe.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तहँ तरु किसलय सुमन सुहाए। लछिमन रचि निज हाथ डसाए॥ ता पर रुचिर मृदुल मृगछाला। तेहिं आसन आसीन कृपाला ॥
translation: वहाँ लक्ष्मणजी ने वृक्षों के कोमल पत्ते और सुंदर फूल अपने हाथों से सजाकर बिछा दिए। उस पर सुंदर और कोमल मृग छाला बिछा दी। उसी आसन पर कृपालु श्री रामजी विराजमान थे ॥
english_translation: There Lakshman arranged tender leaves and lovely flowers with his own hands. On top of that he spread a soft, beautiful deerskin. The compassionate Ram sat on that seat.
essence: A humble seat becomes royal when love prepares it.
simple_meaning: Lakshman prepares a simple, beautiful seat for Ram using leaves, flowers, and deerskin. Ram sits there quietly, showing ease with a humble life in the forest.
insight: It shifts attention from status to service, showing that devotion is expressed through thoughtful preparation.
modern_relevance: You clean a spare room with care before a guest arrives, though nothing about the visit is grand. The welcome itself becomes the gift.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु कृत सीस कपीस उछंगा। बाम दहिन दिसि चाप निषंगा दुहुँ कर कमल सुधारत बाना। कह लंकेस मंत्र लगि काना ॥
translation: प्रभु श्री रामजी वानरराज सुग्रीव की गोद में अपना सिर रखे हैं। उनकी बायीं ओर धनुष तथा दाहिनी ओर तरकस (रखा) है। वे अपने दोनों करकमलों से बाण सुधार रहे हैं। विभीषणजी कानों से लगकर सलाह कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Lord Ram rests his head in Sugriva's lap. His bow is on the left and his quiver on the right. With both lotus hands he readies his arrows, while Vibhishana speaks counsel into his ear.
essence: Readiness can be calm when trust holds the circle around you.
simple_meaning: Ram sits calmly among his allies, ready for battle, while Vibhishana offers advice. The scene shows trust, preparation, and shared purpose before the final fight.
insight: It shifts the mind from solitary strain to supported readiness.
modern_relevance: After a brutal day, you sit on the edge of a couch while a friend quietly helps you think straight. The next step is still hard, but you are no longer carrying it alone.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बड़भागी अंगद हनुमाना। चरन कमल चापत बिधि नाना॥ प्रभु पाछें लछिमन बीरासन। कटि निषंग कर बान सरासन ॥
translation: परम भाग्यशाली अंगद और हनुमान अनेकों प्रकार से प्रभु के चरण कमलों को दबा रहे हैं। लक्ष्मणजी कमर में तरकस कसे और हाथों में धनुष-बाण लिए वीरासन से प्रभु के पीछे सुशोभित हैं ॥
english_translation: Angada and Hanuman, greatly blessed, massage the lotus feet of the Lord in many ways. Behind the Lord stands Lakshmana in a warrior’s stance, with quiver at his waist and bow and arrows in hand.
essence: Love near the beloved becomes service and protection.
simple_meaning: Angada and Hanuman serve Ram by massaging his feet, while Lakshmana stands behind him armed and ready.
insight: It shifts attention from status to service: devotion is shown by what you do around someone, not what you say about them.
modern_relevance: You’re exhausted after a hard day, and the people who love you quietly handle the small things, stay alert, and keep watch without asking for credit.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ऐहि बिधि कृपा रूप गुन धाम रामु आसीन। धन्य ते नर एहिं ध्यान जे रहत सदा लयलीन ॥
translation: इस प्रकार कृपा, रूप (सौंदर्य) और गुणों के धाम श्री रामजी विराजमान हैं। वे मनुष्य धन्य हैं, जो सदा इस ध्यान में लौ लगाए रहते हैं ॥
english_translation: In this way, Ram, the abode of grace, beauty, and virtue, sits there. Blessed are those people who remain forever absorbed in this meditation.
essence: Ram's presence makes steady remembrance feel like a blessing.
simple_meaning: Ram sits there as the source of grace, beauty, and good qualities. People are blessed when they keep their mind steadily fixed on him.
insight: It shifts attention from restless looping to steady remembrance of what ennobles you.
modern_relevance: You are lying awake after a hard day, and your mind keeps replaying noise, fear, and unfinished tasks. This verse offers a gentler anchor: place attention on what is worthy, and the mind begins to settle.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: पूरब दिसा बिलोकि प्रभु देखा उदित मयंक। कहत सबहि देखहु ससिहि मृगपति सरिस असंक ॥
translation: पूर्व दिशा की ओर देखकर प्रभु श्री रामजी ने चंद्रमा को उदय हुआ देखा। तब वे सबसे कहने लगे- चंद्रमा को तो देखो। कैसा सिंह के समान निडर है! ॥
english_translation: Looking toward the east, the Lord saw the moon rise and said to everyone, 'Look at the moon. How fearless it is, like a lion!'
essence: Even the moon becomes a lesson when Ram is the one who sees it.
simple_meaning: Ram notices the rising moon and points it out as a sign of fearless beauty.
insight: It trains attention to pause on what is steady, calm, and fearless.
modern_relevance: You step outside after a long, brutal day and notice the moon above the rooftops. For a second, your mind stops fighting and simply sees beauty.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: पूरब दिसि गिरिगुहा निवासी। परम प्रताप तेज बल रासी॥ मत्त नाग तम कुंभ बिदारी। ससि केसरी गगन बन चारी ॥
translation: पूर्व दिशा रूपी पर्वत की गुफा में रहने वाला, अत्यंत प्रताप, तेज और बल की राशि यह चंद्रमा रूपी सिंह अंधकार रूपी मतवाले हाथी के मस्तक को विदीर्ण करके आकाश रूपी वन में निर्भय विचर रहा है ॥
english_translation: Facing east, the mountain-cave dweller, a storehouse of supreme splendor, radiance, and strength, tears apart the forehead of the drunken elephant of darkness and roams fearlessly through the sky-forest like the moon-lion.
essence: Radiance does not fight darkness — it breaks it apart.
simple_meaning: Ram is described through a vivid moon image: radiant, powerful, fearless, and able to break through darkness.
insight: It shifts attention from darkness itself to the power that makes darkness retreat.
modern_relevance: You look up after a long, draining day and see one clean light cutting through the dark street. Sometimes strength is not loud — it simply makes fear look smaller.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिथुरे नभ मुकुताहल तारा। निसि सुंदरी केर सिंगारा॥ कह प्रभु ससि महुँ मेचकताई। कहहु काह निज निज मति भाई ॥
translation: आकाश में बिखरे हुए तारे मोतियों के समान हैं, जो रात्रि रूपी सुंदर स्त्री के श्रृंगार हैं। प्रभु ने कहा- भाइयो! चंद्रमा में जो कालापन है, वह क्या है? अपनी-अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार कहो ॥
english_translation: The stars scattered across the sky are pearls, the ornaments of the night as a beautiful woman. The Lord said, "Brothers, what is the dark mark in the moon? Tell me according to your own understanding."
essence: Clear seeing begins by asking what others miss.
simple_meaning: Ram points out the moon's dark mark and invites everyone to explain it using their own understanding. The verse values careful seeing and thoughtful questioning.
insight: It trains the mind to pause at appearances and investigate before forming a conclusion.
modern_relevance: You notice a flaw in someone's message, a strange line in a report, or a tense look in a friend's face. Before reacting, Ram's question asks you to look again and think for yourself.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कह सुग्रीव सुनहु रघुराई। ससि महुँ प्रगट भूमि कै झाँई॥ मारेउ राहु ससिहि कह कोई। उर महँ परी स्यामता सोई ॥
translation: सुग्रीव ने कहा- हे रघुनाथजी! सुनिए! चंद्रमा में पृथ्वी की छाया दिखाई दे रही है। किसी ने कहा- चंद्रमा को राहु ने मारा था। वही (चोट का) काला दाग हृदय पर पड़ा हुआ है ॥
english_translation: Sugriva said, “Listen, Raghuraj! The moon seems to show the Earth’s shadow. Someone says Rahu struck the moon. That same dark mark lies in the heart.”
essence: A dark mark on the moon becomes a poetic clue, not a complete idea.
simple_meaning: Sugriva points to a dark mark on the moon and repeats an old explanation for it. The verse is part of a poetic comparison, not a teaching on its own.
insight: It stays with the surrounding verses, using one image to support the next.
modern_relevance: You hear a fragment of a story in the middle of a conversation and try to make it mean more than it does. Some lines are only stepping-stones to the next image.
speaker: Sugriva

verse_text: कोउ कह जब बिधि रति मुख कीन्हा। सार भाग ससि कर हरि लीन्हा॥ छिद्र सो प्रगट इंदु उर माहीं। तेहि मग देखिअ नभ परिछाहीं ॥
translation: कोई कहता है- जब ब्रह्मा ने (कामदेव की स्त्री) रति का मुख बनाया, तब उसने चंद्रमा का सार भाग निकाल लिया (जिससे रति का मुख तो परम सुंदर बन गया, परन्तु चंद्रमा के हृदय में छेद हो गया)। वही छेद चंद्रमा के हृदय में वर्तमान है, जिसकी राह से आकाश की काली छाया उसमें दिखाई पड़ती है ॥
english_translation: Someone says: when Brahma made Rati's face, he took the best part of the moon. That is why a hollow remains in the moon's heart, and the dark shadow of the sky is seen there.
essence: Beauty can still carry the mark of loss.
simple_meaning: People are explaining the moon's dark mark as a hollow left after its best essence was taken away.
insight: It turns a celestial image into a reminder that visible beauty can coexist with hidden absence.
modern_relevance: You smile for the photo, but the tiredness still shows around your eyes. People may see the glow first, yet the crack in you can still be there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु कह गरल बंधु ससि केरा। अति प्रिय निज उर दीन्ह बसेरा॥ बिष संजुत कर निकर पसारी। जारत बिरहवंत नर नारी ॥
translation: प्रभु श्री रामजी ने कहा- विष चंद्रमा का बहुत प्यारा भाई है, इसी से उसने विष को अपने हृदय में स्थान दे रखा है। विषयुक्त अपने किरण समूह को फैलाकर वह वियोगी नर-नारियों को जलाता रहता है ॥
english_translation: The Lord said: poison is the moon's dear brother, and so the moon has given it a place in its heart. Spreading its poisoned rays, it burns men and women who are separated from their beloved.
essence: Longing makes even beauty feel like fire.
simple_meaning: Ram explains the moon's dark mark as something it keeps close, and says its rays burn people suffering separation.
insight: It turns a natural image into a mirror for longing, making separation feel universal rather than private.
modern_relevance: You stare at the moon on a night after a breakup, and it feels almost cruelly beautiful. What shines can still remind you of what hurts.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कह हनुमंत सुनहु प्रभु ससि तुम्हार प्रिय दास। तव मूरति बिधु उर बसति सोइ स्यामता अभास ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी ने कहा- हे प्रभो! सुनिए, चंद्रमा आपका प्रिय दास है। आपकी सुंदर श्याम मूर्ति चंद्रमा के हृदय में बसती है, वही श्यामता की झलक चंद्रमा में है ॥
english_translation: Hanuman said, “Listen, Lord: the moon is your beloved servant. Your beautiful dark form dwells in the moon’s heart; that is why the moon shows a trace of that dark hue.”
essence: Devotion sees the beloved’s mark in all beauty.
simple_meaning: Hanuman praises Ram by saying the moon reflects Ram’s dark beauty because Ram’s form dwells in it.
insight: It trains the mind to see every beauty as an echo of the divine presence.
modern_relevance: You look up at the moon after a long night and feel your chest loosen. In that quiet moment, even beauty feels like it is pointing beyond itself.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: पवन तनय के बचन सुनि बिहँसे रामु सुजान। दच्छिन दिसि अवलोकि प्रभु बोले कृपा निधान ॥
translation: पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी के वचन सुनकर सुजान श्री रामजी हँसे। फिर दक्षिण की ओर देखकर कृपानिधान प्रभु बोले- ॥
english_translation: Hearing Hanuman's words, wise Ram smiled. Looking toward the south, the Lord of grace then spoke.
essence: Ram receives devotion with calm and answers by moving the story forward.
simple_meaning: Ram smiles at Hanuman's words and then turns south to speak. The verse mainly moves the scene forward into the next instruction.
insight: It shifts attention from the messenger's report to the next practical step.
modern_relevance: You hear something hopeful, smile for a second, and then turn toward the harder part of the conversation. Not every meaningful response needs many words.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: देखु विभीषन दच्छिन आसा। घन घमंड दामिनी बिलासा॥ मधुर मधुर गरजइ घन घोरा। होइ बृष्टि जनि उपल कठोरा ॥
translation: हे विभीषण! दक्षिण दिशा की ओर देखो, बादल कैसा घुमड़ रहा है और बिजली चमक रही है। भयानक बादल मीठे-मीठे (हल्के-हल्के) स्वर से गरज रहा है। कहीं कठोर ओलों की वर्षा न हो! ॥
english_translation: Look, Vibhishana, toward the south. Clouds are swelling, and lightning is flashing. The dark clouds rumble softly, softly. May hard hailstones not fall as rain.
essence: The sky darkens before the next turn in the story.
simple_meaning: Ram points out the dark clouds and lightning to Vibhishana, warning that hail may fall. It is a scene-setting verse, not a teaching.
insight: It shifts attention to the immediate scene, not to inner instruction.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कहत विभीषन सुनहू कृपाला। होइ न तड़ित न बारिद माला॥ लंका सिखर उपर आगारा। तहँ दसकंधर देख अखारा ॥
translation: विभीषण बोले- हे कृपालु! सुनिए, यह न तो बिजली है, न बादलों की घटा। लंका की चोटी पर एक महल है। दशग्रीव रावण वहाँ (नाच-गान का) अखाड़ा देख रहा है ॥
english_translation: Vibhishana said, "Listen, O compassionate one. This is neither lightning nor a garland of clouds. On Lanka's summit there is a palace; there, Ravana is watching a dance arena."
essence: What looks like a storm is really Ravana's pride on display.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana points out that the strange sight in Lanka is not a storm. It is Ravana on the palace peak, watching a dance arena.
insight: It shifts attention from appearances to the real source of disorder.
modern_relevance: You glimpse chaos from across the street and assume disaster. Then you get closer and see it is one person making a spectacle, while everyone else pays the price.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: छत्र मेघडंबर सिर धारी। सोइ जनु जलद घटा अति कारी॥ मंदोदरी श्रवन ताटंका। सोइ प्रभु जनु दामिनी दमंका ॥
translation: रावण ने सिर पर मेघडंबर (बादलों के डंबर जैसा विशाल और काला) छत्र धारण कर रखा है। वही मानो बादलों की काली घटा है। मंदोदरी के कानों में जो कर्णफूल हिल रहे हैं, हे प्रभो! वही मानो बिजली चमक रही है ॥
english_translation: Ravana wears a huge black umbrella on his head, like a mass of dark clouds. The earrings in Mandodari's ears flash like lightning.
essence: Ravana is framed as a storm before the battle even begins.
simple_meaning: Ravana is described through vivid comparisons: his umbrella looks like dark clouds, and Mandodari’s earrings look like lightning.
insight: It trains attention to see how imagery can turn a scene into a warning.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet before the boss walks in, and every small detail suddenly feels charged. The mind starts reading power into shadows, shine, and movement.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बाजहिं ताल मृदंग अनूपा। सोइ रव मधुर सुनहू सुरभूपा। प्रभु मुसुकान समुझि अभिमाना। चाप चढ़ाव बान संधाना ॥
translation: हे देवताओं के सम्राट! सुनिए, अनुपम ताल मृदंग बज रहे हैं। वही मधुर (गर्जन) ध्वनि है। रावण का अभिमान समझकर प्रभु मुस्कुराए। उन्होंने धनुष चढ़ाकर उस पर बाण का सन्धान किया ॥
english_translation: O lord of the gods, listen: the drums beat with unmatched rhythm. That very sweet sound is the thunder. Seeing Ravana's pride, the Lord smiled and drew his bow, stringing the arrow.
essence: Pride is met with calm, then decisive action.
simple_meaning: The drums sound like thunder as the battle begins. Ram smiles at Ravana's pride, then lifts his bow and readies an arrow.
insight: It shifts you from reacting to bravado toward seeing clearly and acting cleanly.
modern_relevance: You hear the room get loud before a difficult conversation starts. Someone is posturing, but you stay steady, notice the ego, and prepare your response without losing yourself.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: छत्र मुकुट तांटक तब हते एकहीं बान। सब कें देखत महि परे मरमु न कोऊ जान ॥
translation: और एक ही बाण से (रावण के) छत्र-मुकुट और (मंदोदरी के) कर्णफूल काट गिराए। सबके देखते-देखते वे जमीन पर आ पड़े, पर इसका भेद (कारण) किसी ने नहीं जाना ॥
english_translation: With a single arrow, the crown, umbrella, and earrings were cut down. Everyone saw them fall to the ground, but no one understood how it happened.
essence: Pride falls first; understanding comes later.
simple_meaning: One arrow sent Ravana’s crown, umbrella, and earrings falling to the ground before everyone’s eyes, and no one could tell how it was done.
insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to the hidden force that breaks arrogance.
