modern_relevance: A person walks into the meeting trying to look untouchable, and one calm sentence exposes everything. The room sees the shift before anyone can explain it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस कौतुक करि राम सर प्रबिसेउ आई निषंग। रावन सभा ससंक सब देखि महा रसभंग ॥
translation: ऐसा चमत्कार करके श्री रामजी का बाण (वापस) आकर (फिर) तरकस में जा घुसा। यह महान् रस भंग (रंग में भंग) देखकर रावण की सारी सभा भयभीत हो गई ॥
english_translation: After such a marvel, Ram's arrow returned and entered the quiver again. Seeing this great disruption of their revelry, Ravana's whole assembly was struck with fear.
essence: Ram's power is so complete that even his arrow returns at once.
simple_meaning: Ram's arrow returned to his quiver after the strike, and Ravana's court was thrown into fear by the sudden disruption.
insight: It shows that true force does not need to linger; one precise act can collapse pride completely.
modern_relevance: A room goes silent after one calm sentence lands harder than a shouting match. Everyone who was smirking a second ago suddenly feels the weight of what just happened.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कंप न भूमि न मरुत बिसेषा। अस्त्र सस्त्र कछु नयन न देखा। सोचहिं सब निज हृदय मझारी। असगुन भयउ भयंकर भारी ॥
translation: न भूकम्प हुआ, न बहुत जोर की हवा (आँधी) चली। न कोई अस्त्र-शस्त्र ही नेत्रों से देखे। (फिर ये छत्र, मुकुट और कर्णफूल जैसे कटकर गिर पड़े?) सभी अपने-अपने हृदय में सोच रहे हैं कि यह बड़ा भयंकर अपशकुन हुआ! ॥
english_translation: No earthquake shook the earth, and no strong wind blew. No weapons were seen by anyone's eyes. Yet everyone kept thinking in their own hearts, 'This is a terrible omen.'
essence: Fear turns a mystery into a disaster before facts arrive.
simple_meaning: Nothing outward explains the shock, yet everyone feels a deep fear and reads the moment as a bad omen.
insight: It shows how quickly uncertainty becomes omen when the mind is already shaken.
modern_relevance: A message arrives with no context, and your mind races ahead before anyone has explained a thing. The facts are still small, but fear has already written the story.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दसमुख देखि सभा भय पाई। बिहसि बचन कह जुगुति बनाई। सिरउ गिरे संतत सुभ जाही। मुकुट परे कस असगुन ताही ॥
translation: सभा को भयतीत देखकर रावण ने हँसकर युक्ति रचकर ये वचन कहे- सिरों का गिरना भी जिसके लिए निरंतर शुभ होता रहा है, उसके लिए मुकुट का गिरना अपशकुन कैसा? ॥
english_translation: Seeing the assembly afraid, Ravana laughed and spoke, making a clever excuse. "For one whose heads have always fallen as a blessing, how can the falling of a crown be an omen?"
essence: Pride turns warning signs into excuses.
simple_meaning: Ravana tries to calm the frightened assembly by twisting the situation into confidence. He says that if heads falling has always meant victory for him, then a crown falling cannot be a bad sign.
insight: It reveals how ego protects itself by dressing fear up as certainty.
modern_relevance: You notice a project is slipping, but the boss cracks a joke and calls it fine. Sometimes confidence is just panic wearing a smile.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: मन्दोदरी का फिर रावण को समझाना और श्री राम की महिमा कहना सयन करहु निज निज गृह जाईं। गवने भवन सकल सिर नाई॥ मंदोदरी सोच उर बसेऊ। जब ते श्रवनपूर महि खसेऊ ॥
translation: अपने-अपने घर जाकर सो रहो (डरने की कोई बात नहीं है) तब सब लोग सिर नवाकर घर गए। जब से कर्णफूल पृथ्वी पर गिरा, तब से मंदोदरी के हृदय में सोच बस गया ॥
english_translation: Mandodari again advises Ravana and speaks of Ram's greatness: "Go and sleep in your own homes." Everyone then bowed and went home. But when the earrings fell to the ground, Mandodari's heart filled with worry.
essence: A court can pretend calm, but one falling sign awakens fear.
simple_meaning: Mandodari tries again to calm Ravana and point him toward Ram's greatness. The court disperses, but the fallen earring leaves her heart uneasy.
insight: It shows how a single unsettling sign can break through public confidence and expose private fear.
modern_relevance: You tell everyone the crisis is under control, and the room quiets for a moment. Then one tiny detail—a dropped phone, a missed call, a silence—makes your stomach tighten.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सजल नयन कह जुग कर जोरी। सुनहु प्रानपति बिनती मोरी॥ कंत राम बिरोध परिहरहू। जानि मनुज जनि हठ लग धरहू ॥
translation: नेत्रों में जल भरकर, दोनों हाथ जोड़कर वह (रावण से) कहने लगी- हे प्राणनाथ! मेरी विनती सुनिए। हे प्रियतम! श्री राम से विरोध छोड़ दीजिए। उन्हें मनुष्य जानकर मन में हठ न पकड़े रहिए ॥
english_translation: With tears in her eyes, she folded both hands and said, "Listen to my plea, my beloved lord. O dear one, give up hostility toward Ram. Do not stubbornly cling to the thought that He is only a human."
essence: Stubborn pride fails when it refuses to see Ram clearly.
simple_meaning: Mandodari begs Ravana to stop opposing Ram and to drop the stubborn belief that Ram is merely human.
insight: It shifts the mind from stubborn denial to humble recognition of reality.
modern_relevance: You keep arguing with a truth your partner, friend, or conscience has already made clear. The longer you defend the wrong story, the more damage you do to yourself.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: बिस्वरूप रघुबंस मनि करहु बचन बिस्वासु। लोक कल्पना बेद कर अंग अंग प्रति जासु ॥
translation: मेरे इन वचनों पर विश्वास कीजिए कि ये रघुकुल के शिरोमणि श्री रामचंद्रजी विश्व रूप हैं- (यह सारा विश्व उन्हीं का रूप है)। वेद जिनके अंग-अंग में लोकों की कल्पना करते हैं ॥
english_translation: Believe my words: the jewel of the Raghu clan is the cosmic form, and the Vedas imagine all worlds as parts of him.
essence: Ram is not inside the world; the world rests inside Ram.
simple_meaning: Mandodari tells Ravana to trust her: Ram is not just a prince, but the cosmic form behind all existence, with every world as part of him.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as limited form to seeing him as the ground of all forms.
modern_relevance: You are staring at one person, one problem, one loss, and it feels absolute. This verse widens the frame: what seems small to you may be held inside something much larger.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: पद पाताल सीस अज धामा। अपर लोक अँग अँग बिश्रामा॥ भृकुटि बिलास भयंकर काला। नयन दिवाकर कच घन माला ॥
translation: पाताल (जिन विश्व रूप भगवान् का) चरण है, ब्रह्म लोक सिर है, अन्य (बीच के सब) लोकों का विश्राम (स्थिति) जिनके अन्य भिन्न-भिन्न अंगों पर है। भयंकर काल जिनका भृकुटि संचालन (भौंहों का चलना) है। सूर्य नेत्र हैं, बादलों का समूह बाल है ॥
english_translation: The underworld is his feet, the realm of Brahma is his head, and all the worlds rest in his many limbs. Fearsome Time is the movement of his brow; the sun is his eyes, and clouds are his hair.
essence: Everything rests inside Ram's vast form, even Time.
simple_meaning: Ram's cosmic form contains every realm within itself. The whole universe rests in him, and even Time seems like a small movement within his body.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing the world as fragmented to seeing it as held within one vast order.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a crisis that feels bigger than your control. Then a wider view returns: the pressure, the fear, even time itself are not the whole of reality.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: जासु घ्रान अस्विनीकुमारा। निसि अरु दिवस निमेष अपारा॥ श्रवन दिसा दस बेद बखानी। मारुत स्वास निगम निज बानी ॥
translation: अश्विनी कुमार जिनकी नासिका हैं, रात और दिन जिनके अपार निमेष (पलक मारना और खोलना) हैं। दसों दिशाएँ कान हैं, वेद ऐसा कहते हैं। वायु श्वास है और वेद जिनकी अपनी वाणी है ॥
english_translation: The Ashwini Kumaras are his nostrils; night and day are his endless blinking. The ten directions are his ears, the Vedas declare. Wind is his breath, and the Vedas are his own speech.
essence: Everything sacred and living is already contained in Ram's vast form.
simple_meaning: Ram's cosmic form is being described as vast enough to contain the powers of nature, the Vedas, and the directions themselves.
insight: It shifts your view from seeing Ram as one figure among many to seeing all reality as his form.
modern_relevance: You look up at the night sky after a hard day and feel small, but also strangely held. This verse turns that feeling into devotion: the world is not outside the divine presence; it is inside it.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अधर लोभ जम दसन कराला। माया हास बाहु दिगपाला॥ आनन अनल अंबुपति जीहा। उतपति पालन प्रलय समीहा ॥
translation: लोभ जिनका अधर (होठ) है, यमराज भयानक दाँत हैं। माया हँसी है, दिक्पाल भुजाएँ हैं। अग्नि मुख है, वरुण जीभ है। उत्पत्ति, पालन और प्रलय जिनकी चेष्टा (क्रिया) है ॥
english_translation: Greed is the lips, and Yama's fearsome teeth. Illusion is the smile, and the guardians of the directions are the arms. Fire is the face, Varuna is the tongue. Creation, preservation, and destruction are the movements of that all-encompassing form.
essence: Everything that seems separate is part of one immense form.
simple_meaning: The verse maps the universe onto one vast cosmic form: greed, illusion, death, fire, water, and the powers that govern the world all appear as parts of it.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated forces to the single reality that contains them all.
modern_relevance: You look at a system and see only separate parts: money, fear, power, appetite, control. Then you notice they all feed one larger machine, and your view changes completely.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रोम राजि अष्टादस भारा। अस्थि सैल सरिता नस जारा॥ उदर उदधि अधगो जातना। जगमय प्रभु का बहु कलपना ॥
translation: अठारह प्रकार की असंख्य वनस्पतियाँ जिनकी रोमावली हैं, पर्वत अस्थियाँ हैं, नदियाँ नसों का जाल है, समुद्र पेट है और नरक जिनकी नीचे की इंद्रियाँ हैं। इस प्रकार प्रभु विश्वमय हैं, अधिक कल्पना (ऊहापोह) क्या की जाए? ॥
english_translation: Eighteen kinds of countless plants are his body hair; mountains are his bones, rivers his network of veins, the ocean his belly, and the lower realms his lower organs. The Lord is all-pervading—what more is there to imagine?
essence: The universe is not separate from the Lord.
simple_meaning: The whole universe is described as Ram's body: plants, mountains, rivers, oceans, and even lower regions all belong to him. He fills everything, so there is no need for more speculation.
insight: It shifts attention from fragmented details to a single all-pervading reality.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a night sky after a hard day, feeling small and cut off. Then it hits you that nothing is truly outside the larger order holding it all together.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अहंकार सिव बुद्धि अज मन ससि चित्त महान। मनुज बास सचराचर रूप राम भगवान ॥
translation: शिव जिनका अहंकार हैं, ब्रह्मा बुद्धि हैं, चंद्रमा मन हैं और महान (विष्णु) ही चित्त हैं। उन्हीं चराचर रूप भगवान श्री रामजी ने मनुष्य रूप में निवास किया है ॥
english_translation: Shiva is their ego, Brahma their intellect, the moon their mind, and the great one their inner state. The Lord Ram, whose form is all moving and unmoving beings, dwells in human form.
essence: The highest reality can choose to live as an ordinary person.
simple_meaning: Ram is described as the supreme being present in all moving and unmoving forms, yet also dwelling in human form. The verse points to his cosmic nature and his chosen nearness to people.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as distant power to recognising sacred presence in human form.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary, almost easy to overlook, and later realise their quiet presence changed everything. This verse asks you to look again at the human face in front of you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अस बिचारि सुनु प्रानपति प्रभु सन बयरु बिहाइ। प्रीति करहु रघुबीर पद मम अहिवात न जाइ ॥
translation: हे प्राणपति सुनिए, ऐसा विचार कर प्रभु से वैर छोड़कर श्री रघुवीर के चरणों में प्रेम कीजिए, जिससे मेरा सुहाग न जाए ॥
english_translation: O lord of my life, think this through: give up enmity toward the Lord and love the feet of Raghubir, so my marriage bond may not be broken.
essence: Love for Ram protects what hatred destroys.
simple_meaning: Mandodari tells Ravana to stop opposing Ram and turn to devotion, warning that his wifehood and household will be ruined otherwise.
insight: It shifts you from defending ego to seeing the cost of stubborn opposition.
modern_relevance: You are mid-argument, and the thing you are trying hardest to defend is the thing your anger is breaking. One honest turn could save the relationship.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: बिहँसा नारि बचन सुनि काना। अहो मोह महिमा बलवाना॥ नारि सुभाउ सत्य सब कहहीं। अवगुन आठ सदा उर रहहीं ॥
translation: पत्नी के वचन कानों से सुनकर रावण खूब हँसा (और बोला-) अहो! मोह (अज्ञान) की महिमा बड़ी बलवान् है। स्त्री का स्वभाव सब सत्य ही कहते हैं कि उसके हृदय में आठ अवगुण सदा रहते हैं- ॥
english_translation: Hearing his wife's words, Ravana laughed and said, "Ah, how powerful delusion is! Women’s nature is said to hold eight faults always in the heart."
essence: Delusion makes warning sound like insult.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks his wife's warning and blames delusion, showing that he cannot hear wisdom without turning it into pride and contempt.
insight: It reveals how ego converts feedback into self-justification and blocks clear seeing.
modern_relevance: Someone texts you a careful warning, and you read it as criticism. By the time you start defending yourself, the real message is already lost.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: साहस अनृत चपलता माया। भय अबिबेक असौच अदाया॥ रिपु कर रूप सकल तैं गावा। अति बिसाल भय मोहि सुनावा ॥
translation: साहस, झूठ, चंचलता, माया (छल), भय (डरपोकपन) अविवेक (मूर्खता), अपवित्रता और निर्दयता। तूने शत्रु का समग्र (विराट) रूप गाया और मुझे उसका बड़ा भारी भय सुनाया ॥
english_translation: Courage, falsehood, fickleness, illusion, fear, lack of discernment, impurity, and cruelty — you have described the enemy's whole vast form and filled me with terrible fear.
essence: Fear turns a real threat into a monstrous one.
simple_meaning: Ravana says the woman has described the enemy as a bundle of fear, falsehood, illusion, and cruelty, making him seem terrifyingly vast.
insight: It shifts you from emotional exaggeration to clear seeing, so you can name what is actually there.
modern_relevance: You read a message late at night and suddenly the whole situation feels catastrophic. Half the terror comes from your own mind filling in blanks.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सो सब प्रिया सहज बस मोरें। समुझि परा अब प्रसाद तोरें॥ जानिउँ प्रिया तोरि चतुराई। एहि बिधि कहहु मोरि प्रभुताई ॥
translation: हे प्रिये! वह सब (यह चराचर विश्व तो) स्वभाव से ही मेरे वश में है। तेरी कृपा से मुझे यह अब समझ पड़ा। हे प्रिये! तेरी चतुराई मैं जान गया। तू इस प्रकार (इसी बहाने) मेरी प्रभुता का बखान कर रही है ॥
english_translation: Everything that exists is naturally under my control. By your grace, I now understand this. O beloved, I see your cleverness: in this way, you are praising my greatness.
essence: Ego hears warning as praise.
simple_meaning: Ravana says he now understands that everything is already under his control, and he thinks Mandodari is cleverly praising his power through her words.
insight: It exposes how self-importance distorts listening and turns correction into confirmation.
modern_relevance: Someone points out the risk in your plan, but you hear only criticism of your brilliance. The mind that needs to feel superior can turn every warning into applause.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: तव बतकही गूढ़ मृगलोचनि। समुझत सुखद सुनत भय मोचनि॥ मंदोदरि मन महुँ अस ठयऊ। पियहि काल बस मति भ्रम भयउ ॥
translation: हे मृगनयनी! तेरी बातें बड़ी गूढ़ (रहस्यभरी) हैं, समझने पर सुख देने वाली और सुनने से भय छुड़ाने वाली हैं। मंदोदरी ने मन में ऐसा निश्चय कर लिया कि पति को कालवश मतिभ्रम हो गया है ॥
english_translation: O doe-eyed one, your words are profound: they bring delight when understood and remove fear when heard. Mandodari resolved in her mind that her husband had become deluded by time's power.
essence: Delusion can make even clear truth sound like comfort and warning.
simple_meaning: Mandodari sees that Ravana has become confused by time and pride. She recognizes that wise words can calm fear, but his mind is no longer clear enough to receive them.
insight: It shifts attention from the content of advice to the receiver's state of mind.
modern_relevance: You explain the situation carefully, but the other person is already defending a decision they made in anger. You can feel the conversation landing nowhere, even as your words are perfectly clear.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: ऐहि बिधि करत बिनोद बहु प्रात प्रगट दसकंध। सहज असंक लंकपति सभाँ गयउ मद अंध ॥
translation: इस प्रकार (अज्ञानवश) बहुत से विनोद करते हुए रावण को सबेरा हो गया। तब स्वभाव से ही निडर और घमंड में अंधा लंकापति सभा में गया ॥
english_translation: In this way, while making many idle jokes, dawn arrived for Ravana. Then the lord of Lanka, naturally fearless and blinded by pride, went to the assembly.
essence: Pride keeps you fearless until it blinds you.
simple_meaning: Ravana spends the night in careless amusement, then goes to his council in a state of fearless pride and blindness.
insight: It shows how ego can turn danger into entertainment and block any real self-correction.
modern_relevance: You keep joking in the group chat after the warning signs are obvious. By morning, you walk into the meeting still convinced nothing can touch you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: फूलइ फरइ न बेत जदपि सुधा बरषहिं जलद। मूरुख हृदयँ न चेत जौं गुर मिलहिं बिरंचि सम ॥
translation: यद्यपि बादल अमृत सा जल बरसाते हैं तो भी बेत फूलता-फलता नहीं। इसी प्रकार चाहे ब्रह्मा के समान भी ज्ञानी गुरु मिलें, तो भी मूर्ख के हृदय में चेत (ज्ञान) नहीं होता ॥
english_translation: Even if nectar-like rain falls from the clouds, bamboo never flowers or bears fruit. In the same way, even if a teacher like Brahma is found, a fool's heart does not awaken.
essence: Wisdom cannot bloom in a heart that refuses to receive it.
simple_meaning: A person who refuses to awaken will not change, even with the best guidance. Real understanding needs an open and receptive heart.
insight: It shifts attention from finding better instruction to becoming teachable.
modern_relevance: You keep explaining the same thing to someone who only wants to win the argument. No amount of perfect advice helps until the person is willing to hear it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: इहाँ प्रात जागे रघुराई। पूछा मत सब सचिव बोलाई॥ कहहु बेगि का करिअ उपाई। जामवंत कह पद सिरु नाई ॥
translation: यहाँ (सुबेल पर्वत पर) प्रातःकाल श्री रघुनाथजी जागे और उन्होंने सब मंत्रियों को बुलाकर सलाह पूछी कि शीघ्र बताइए, अब क्या उपाय करना चाहिए? जाम्बवान् ने श्री रामजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर कहा- ॥
english_translation: At dawn, Raghunath woke up, called all the ministers together, and asked what should be done quickly. Jambavan bowed his head at Ram's feet and said:
essence: Real strength asks for guidance before it moves.
simple_meaning: Ram wakes at dawn, gathers his council, and asks for a quick solution. Jambavan responds with reverence and practical advice.
insight: It shifts leadership from reacting alone to seeking grounded counsel before acting.
modern_relevance: You wake up to a crisis message and resist the urge to guess. You gather the right people, ask plainly what should be done, and let wisdom come before speed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनु सर्बग्य सकल उर बासी। बुधि बल तेज धर्म गुन रासी॥ मंत्र कहउँ निज मति अनुसारा। दूत पठाइअ बालि कुमारा ॥
translation: हे सर्वज्ञ (सब कुछ जानने वाले)! हे सबके हृदय में बसने वाले (अंतर्यामी)! हे बुद्धि, बल, तेज, धर्म और गुणों की राशि! सुनिए! मैं अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार सलाह देता हूँ कि बालिकुमार अंगद को दूत बनाकर भेजा जाए! ॥
english_translation: O all-knowing one, who dwells in every heart and is the storehouse of wisdom, strength, radiance, virtue, and goodness, hear me. I offer my counsel according to my understanding: send Angad, the son of Bali, as the messenger.
essence: Reverence and practical counsel can move together.
simple_meaning: Jambavan praises Ram and suggests sending Angad as the messenger. The verse is part of a larger plan, not a complete teaching on its own.
insight: It links devotion with strategy: honor the highest truth, then choose the right messenger for the mission.
modern_relevance: In a tense team meeting, someone who truly respects the leader still brings a concrete solution, not just praise. Reverence and practical judgment can live together.
speaker: Jambavan

verse_text: नीक मंत्र सब के मन माना। अंगद सन कह कृपानिधाना॥ बालितनय बुधि बल गुन धामा। लंका जाहु तात मम कामा ॥
translation: यह अच्छी सलाह सबके मन में जँच गई। कृपा के निधान श्री रामजी ने अंगद से कहा- हे बल, बुद्धि और गुणों के धाम बालिपुत्र! हे तात! तुम मेरे काम के लिए लंका जाओ ॥
english_translation: The wise counsel pleased everyone. The Lord of compassion then said to Angad, "Son of Bali, treasure of strength, wisdom, and virtue, go to Lanka for my task."
essence: True capability is proven when trust becomes responsibility.
simple_meaning: Ram accepts the plan and sends Angad to Lanka on his mission. He praises Angad’s strength, wisdom, and virtue before giving the task.
insight: It shifts attention from debate to execution: the right person is sent for the right task.
modern_relevance: Your team finally agrees on the approach, and then someone turns to you: "Can you handle the hard part?" The moment feels heavy, but it is also trust.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: बहुत बुझाइ तुम्हहि का कहऊँ। परम चतुर मैं जानत अहऊँ॥ काजु हमार तासु हित होई। रिपु सन करेहु बतकही सोई ॥
translation: तुमको बहुत समझाकर क्या कहूँ! मैं जानता हूँ, तुम परम चतुर हो। शत्रु से वही बातचीत करना, जिससे हमारा काम हो और उसका कल्याण हो ॥
english_translation: Why explain much to you? I know you are extremely clever. Speak with the enemy in a way that serves our purpose and his good.
essence: Clever speech should serve both the mission and the other person's good.
simple_meaning: Ram trusts Angad's intelligence and tells him to speak to the enemy in a way that helps their mission and still leaves room for the enemy's welfare.
insight: It teaches you to use intelligence with restraint, aiming for effectiveness without losing goodwill.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting knowing one wrong sentence could shut everyone down. The wisest move is not blunt force, but words that keep the goal alive without needless harm.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: प्रभु अग्या धरि सीस चरन बंदि अंगद उठेउ। सोइ गुन सागर ईस राम कृपा जा कर करहु ॥
translation: प्रभु की आज्ञा सिर चढ़कर और उनके चरणों की वंदना करके अंगदजी उठे (और बोले-) हे भगवान् श्री रामजी! आप जिस पर कृपा करें, वही गुणों का समुद्र हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Aṅgada rose, bowing his head to the Lord's command and worshipping his feet: "O Ram, the ocean of virtues becomes great only by your grace."
essence: True greatness rises only after you bow first.
simple_meaning: Aṅgada rises only after bowing to Ram's command, and he says that real greatness comes from Ram's grace.
insight: It shifts confidence from self-display to grace-filled service.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hard conversation after quietly reminding yourself who you answer to. The steadiness you feel is not self-importance — it's the relief of being aligned with something higher.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: स्वयंसिद्ध सब काज नाथ मोहि आदरु दियउ। अस बिचारि जुबराज तन पुलकित हरषित हियउ ॥
translation: स्वामी सब कार्य अपने-आप सिद्ध हैं, यह तो प्रभु ने मुझ को आदर दिया है (जो मुझे अपने कार्य पर भेज रहे हैं)। ऐसा विचार कर युवराज अंगद का हृदय हर्षित और शरीर पुलकित हो गया ॥
english_translation: All tasks are already self-succeeded, Lord. Thinking this, the prince's heart thrilled and his body shivered with joy.
essence: True service feels like being trusted, not being burdened.
simple_meaning: Angad feels honored, not burdened. He sees the mission as already blessed and takes it as a sign of trust.
insight: It shifts you from self-conscious performance to joyful service.
modern_relevance: You get assigned the difficult presentation and stop seeing it as a test of your worth. The moment you treat it as trust, your body relaxes and your mind sharpens.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: बंदि चरन उर धरि प्रभुताई। अंगद चलेउ सबहि सिरु नाई॥ प्रभु प्रताप उर सहज असंका। रन बाँकुरा बालिसुत बंका ॥
translation: चरणों की वंदना करके और भगवान् की प्रभुता हृदय में धरकर अंगद सबको सिर नवाकर चले। प्रभु के प्रताप को हृदय में धारण किए हुए रणबाँकुरे वीर बालिपुत्र स्वाभाविक ही निर्भय हैं ॥
english_translation: Bowing to the feet and holding the Lord's majesty in his heart, Angad departed, bowing to everyone. With the Lord's glory in his heart, the brave son of Bali is naturally fearless in battle.
essence: True fearlessness comes from carrying the Lord's glory within.
simple_meaning: Angad leaves with respect for everyone, but his heart stays steady because he trusts the Lord's power. That trust makes him naturally fearless.
insight: It shifts courage from personal toughness to inward trust in Ram's power.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room, knowing a hard conversation is coming. Your voice stays steady because you are anchored in something deeper than the reaction you might get.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुर पैठत रावन कर बेटा। खेलत रहा सो होइ गै भेंटा॥ बातहिं बात करष बढ़ि आई। जुगल अतुल बल पुनि तरुनाई ॥
translation: लंका में प्रवेश करते ही रावण के पुत्र से भेंट हो गई, जो वहाँ खेल रहा था। बातों ही बातों में दोनों में झगड़ा बढ़ गया (क्योंकि) दोनों ही अतुलनीय बलवान् थे और फिर दोनों की युवावस्था थी ॥
english_translation: As Angad entered Lanka, he met Ravana's son, who was playing there. In talk after talk, the quarrel grew, because both were unmatched in strength and both were young.
essence: A small meeting turns fierce when pride and strength meet.
simple_meaning: Angad runs into Ravana's son in Lanka, and a small exchange quickly turns into a fight because both are young and powerful.
insight: It shows how quickly unguarded pride can escalate a simple encounter into conflict.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering already tense, and one careless remark from a young cousin turns the whole room sharp. Sometimes strength and ego need only a spark.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहिं अंगद कहुँ लात उठाई। गहि पद पटकेउ भूमि भवाँई॥ निसिचर निकर देखि भट भारी। जहँ तहँ चले न सकहिं पुकारी ॥
translation: उसने अंगद पर लात उठाई। अंगद ने (वही) पैर पकड़कर उसे घुमाकर जमीन पर दे पटका (मार गिराया)। राक्षस के समूह भारी योद्धा देखकर जहाँ-तहाँ (भाग) चले, वे डर के मारे पुकार भी न मचा सके ॥
english_translation: He kicked Angad, and Angad seized his foot, whirled him around, and slammed him to the ground. Seeing the great warrior among the demon host, they scattered everywhere and could not even cry out.
essence: True strength turns aggression back on itself.
simple_meaning: He attacks Angad, but Angad turns the move back and throws him down. The enemy troops panic and flee in every direction.
insight: It shows how steady force can reverse intimidation and break collective panic.
modern_relevance: A bully lunges in front of a crowd, expecting fear. Instead, the calm response knocks the whole room off balance and the noise dies instantly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक एक सन मरमु न कहहीं। समुझि तासु बध चुप करि रहहीं॥ भयउ कोलाहल नगर मझारी। आवा कपि लंका जेहिं जारी ॥
translation: एक-दूसरे को मर्म (असली बात) नहीं बतलाते, उस (रावण के पुत्र) का वध समझकर सब चुप मारकर रह जाते हैं। (रावण पुत्र की मृत्यु जानकर और राक्षसों को भय के मारे भागते देखकर) नगरभर में कोलाहल मच गया कि जिसने लंका जलाई थी, वही वानर फिर आ गया है ॥
english_translation: No one tells the others the real matter. Thinking him already slain, they fall silent. Then the city erupts in uproar: the monkey who burned Lanka has come again.
essence: Fear fills silence with its own story.
simple_meaning: The enemies stay quiet, thinking the young warrior has been killed. Then panic spreads through Lanka when they realize the same monkey has returned.
insight: It shows how fear turns partial information into collective confusion.
modern_relevance: A group chat goes silent after one bad screenshot, then rumors explode before anyone checks the facts. Panic fills the gap where clear seeing should have been.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अब धौं कहा करिहि करतारा। अति सभीत सब करहिं बिचारा॥ बिनु पूछें मगु देहिं दिखाई। जेहि बिलोक सोइ जाइ सुखाई ॥
translation: सब अत्यंत भयभीत होकर विचार करने लगे कि विधाता अब न जाने क्या करेगा। वे बिना पूछे ही अंगद को (रावण के दरबार की) राह बता देते हैं। जिसे ही वे देखते हैं, वही डर के मारे सूख जाता है ॥
english_translation: All were utterly frightened, wondering what fate would do next. Without even asking, they showed Angad the way. Whoever saw him withers in fear.
essence: Fear makes even enemies hand over the path.
simple_meaning: Everyone is so frightened that they stop thinking clearly and even point out the way without being asked. Angad's presence alone makes people lose courage.
insight: It shifts attention from force to presence: steady courage can disarm fear without a fight.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room, and the people who planned to corner you suddenly soften. Sometimes calm courage changes the whole atmosphere before a word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गयउ सभा दरबार तब सुमिरि राम पद कंज। सिंह ठवनि इत उत चितव धीर बीर बल पुंज ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के चरणकमलों का स्मरण करके अंगद रावण की सभा के द्वार पर गए और वे धीर, वीर और बल की राशि अंगद सिंह की सी ऐंड़ (शान) से इधर-उधर देखने लगे ॥
english_translation: Then Angad went to the court, remembering Ram's lotus feet. Like a lion, steady and brave, he looked all around, a mass of strength.
essence: Remembering Ram makes Angad fearless in enemy territory.
simple_meaning: Angad enters Ravana's court with Ram in mind, calm and fearless. His presence itself shows courage and strength.
insight: It shows that remembrance can steady the body and sharpen presence under pressure.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting where everyone expects you to fold. Instead, you breathe, hold your ground, and let calm confidence speak first.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तुरत निसाचर एक पठावा। समाचार रावनहि जनावा॥ सुनत बिहँसि बोला दससीसा। आनहु बोलि कहाँ कर कीसा ॥
translation: तुरंत ही उन्होंने एक राक्षस को भेजा और रावण को अपने आने का समाचार सूचित किया। सुनते ही रावण हँसकर बोला- बुला लाओ, (देखें) कहाँ का बंदर है ॥
english_translation: At once a demon was sent to inform Ravana. Hearing it, Ravana laughed and said, "Bring him here. Let us see what kind of monkey he is."
essence: Pride laughs first, even when danger is already at the door.
simple_meaning: A messenger rushes to Ravana with the news. Ravana laughs and dismisses Angad, mocking him as just a monkey.
insight: It shows how ego reacts to danger with mockery instead of clear seeing.
modern_relevance: You get the text that a difficult conversation is waiting in the next room, and you laugh it off to feel bigger. That joke can be the first sign you're already losing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आयसु पाइ दूत बहु धाए। कपिकुंजरहि बोलि लै आए॥ अंगद दीख दसानन बैसें। सहित प्रान कज्जलगिरि जैसें ॥
translation: आज्ञा पाकर बहुत से दूत दौड़े और वानरों में हाथी के समान अंगद को बुला लाए। अंगद ने रावण को ऐसे बैठे हुए देखा, जैसे कोई प्राणयुक्त (सजीव) काजल का पहाड़ हो! ॥
english_translation: At his command, many messengers ran and brought Angad, the monkey-chief. Angad saw Ravana seated there, like a living mountain of black collyrium.
essence: The confrontation begins with a charged first look.
simple_meaning: Ravana's messengers hurry to bring Angad before him, and Angad sees the king of Lanka sitting there like a dark, living mountain.
insight: It frames the meeting as a face-off, not a conversation, and builds tension before the exchange.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भुजा बिटप सिर सृंग समाना। रोमावली लता जनु नाना॥ मुख नासिका नयन अरु काना। गिरि कंदरा खोह अनुमाना ॥
translation: भुजाएँ वृक्षों के और सिर पर्वतों के शिखरों के समान हैं। रोमावली मानो बहुत सी लताएँ हैं। मुँह, नाक, नेत्र और कान पर्वत की कन्दराओं और खोहों के बराबर हैं ॥
english_translation: His arms were like tree trunks and his head like mountain peaks. His body hair was like many creeping vines. His mouth, nose, eyes, and ears were like mountain caves and hollows.
essence: Angad's body is described as a living mountain to magnify his presence.
simple_meaning: Angad's huge body is described through mountain-and-forest imagery to show his enormous, awe-inspiring form.
insight: It shifts attention from speech to embodied presence: how you enter a space can carry force before you say anything.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting and everyone notices before you open your mouth. The room reads your presence first, your words second.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गयउ सभाँ मन नेकु न मुरा। बालितनय अतिबल बाँकुरा॥ उठे सभासद कपि कहुँ देखी। रावन उर भा क्रोध बिसेषी ॥
translation: अत्यंत बलवान् बाँके वीर बालिपुत्र अंगद सभा में गए, वे मन में जरा भी नहीं झिझके। अंगद को देखते ही सब सभासद् उठ खड़े हुए। यह देखकर रावण के हृदय में बड़ा क्रोध हुआ ॥
english_translation: Angad entered the assembly without the slightest hesitation. When the courtiers saw the mighty son of Bali, they rose to their feet. Ravana's heart filled with intense anger.
essence: Steady courage can shake a room before any speech begins.
simple_meaning: Angad walks into Ravana's court without fear. The courtiers stand up when they see him, and Ravana burns with anger.
insight: It shows how fearless presence can unsettle pride and command attention without force.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting and say nothing yet. Still, everyone notices your steadiness before you open your mouth.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जथा मत्त गज जूथ महुँ पंचानन चलि जाइ। राम प्रताप सुमिरि मन बैठ सभाँ सिरु नाइ ॥
translation: जैसे मतवाले हाथियों के झुंड में सिंह (निःशंक होकर) चला जाता है, वैसे ही श्री रामजी के प्रताप का हृदय में स्मरण करके वे (निर्भय) सभा में सिर नवाकर बैठ गए ॥
english_translation: Like a lion walking into a herd of drunk elephants, he entered the assembly without fear, remembering Ram's power in his heart and bowing before sitting down.
essence: Remember Ram, and fear cannot rule you.
simple_meaning: Remembering Ram's power, Angad entered a hostile assembly with complete fearlessness and sat down respectfully.
insight: It shifts courage from self-confidence to remembrance of a higher support.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is judging you, and your chest tightens. Then you remember who stands behind your work, your word, your values — and your body settles.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह दसकंठ कवन तैं बंदर। मैं रघुबीर दूत दसकंधर॥ मम जनकहि तोहि रही मिताई। तव हित कारन आयउँ भाई ॥
translation: रावण ने कहा- अरे बंदर! तू कौन है? (अंगद ने कहा-) हे दशग्रीव! मैं श्री रघुवीर का दूत हूँ। मेरे पिता से और तुमसे मित्रता थी, इसलिए हे भाई! मैं तुम्हारी भलाई के लिए ही आया हूँ ॥
english_translation: Ravana said, “Hey monkey, who are you? I am the messenger of the mighty Raghu lord, O ten-headed one. My father and you were once friends, so I have come for your good, brother.”
essence: True courage can challenge someone without losing goodwill.
simple_meaning: Angad answers Ravana boldly: he is Ram’s messenger, and he has come for Ravana’s own good, not to insult him.
insight: It teaches you to hold your ground while keeping your intention clean.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room where everyone expects you to back down. Instead, you speak firmly, without venom, because honesty can still be kind.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: उत्तम कुल पुलस्ति कर नाती। सिव बिंरचि पूजेहु बहु भाँती॥ बर पायहु कीन्हेहु सब काजा। जीतेहु लोकपाल सब राजा ॥
translation: तुम्हारा उत्तम कुल है, पुलस्त्य ऋषि के तुम पौत्र हो। शिवजी की और ब्रह्माजी की तुमने बहुत प्रकार से पूजा की है। उनसे वर पाए हैं और सब काम सिद्ध किए हैं। लोकपालों और सब राजाओं को तुमने जीत लिया है ॥
english_translation: You are from an excellent lineage, grandson of Pulastya. You have worshipped Shiva and Brahma in many ways. You have received boons and accomplished all tasks. You have conquered the guardians of the worlds and all kings.
essence: Great power means nothing when it only strengthens ego.
simple_meaning: Ravana is being reminded of his great lineage, devotion, boons, and conquests. The praise is real, but it also sets up the warning that follows.
insight: It separates real accomplishment from the mind that clings to it as identity.
modern_relevance: You’ve built the company, won the promotion, and collected every sign of status — then one honest conversation shows how brittle the ego still is.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: नृप अभिमान मोह बस किंबा। हरि आनिहु सीता जगदंबा॥ अब सुभ कहा सुनहु तुम्ह मोरा। सब अपराध छमिहि प्रभु तोरा ॥
translation: राजमद से या मोहवश तुम जगज्जननी सीताजी को हर लाए हो। अब तुम मेरे शुभ वचन (मेरी हितभरी सलाह) सुनो! (उसके अनुसार चलने से) प्रभु श्री रामजी तुम्हारे सब अपराध क्षमा कर देंगे ॥
english_translation: You may have brought Sita, the mother of the world, here out of pride or confusion. Now hear my good counsel: if you follow it, Lord Ram will forgive all your offenses.
essence: Pride can be undone if you are willing to hear the truth.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana tells Ravana that Sita may have been brought through pride or confusion, but there is still a way back: listen to good counsel, and Ram will forgive everything.
insight: It shifts the mind from defensiveness to receptivity, showing that correction and forgiveness begin with listening.
modern_relevance: You know that moment after a terrible argument when your chest is tight and your phone is in your hand. One honest conversation, one willingness to listen, can still change what happens next.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: दसन गहहु तृन कंठ कुठारी। परिजन सहित संग निज नारी॥ सादर जनकसुता करि आगें। एहि बिधि चलहु सकल भय त्यागें ॥
translation: दाँतों में तिनका दबाओ, गले में कुल्हाड़ी डालो और कुटुम्बियों सहित अपनी स्त्रियों को साथ लेकर, आदरपूर्वक जानकीजी को आगे करके, इस प्रकार सब भय छोड़कर चलो- ॥
english_translation: Hold a blade of grass in your teeth, a noose at your neck, and come with your family and your women. Place Janak's daughter respectfully in front, and come this way, leaving all fear behind.
essence: Fear falls away only when pride is laid down.
simple_meaning: Ravana is being told to abandon pride and fear, bring his family, and approach Sita respectfully as a sign of surrender.
insight: It teaches you to replace defensiveness with humility before conflict hardens into damage.
modern_relevance: After a bitter argument, you finally send the message you should have sent hours ago: no excuses, no posturing, just honesty. The first real step is dropping the armor.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: प्रनतपाल रघुबंसमनि त्राहि त्राहि अब मोहि। आरत गिरा सुनत प्रभु अभय करेंगे तोहि ॥
translation: और 'हे शरणागत के पालन करने वाले रघुवंश शिरोमणि श्री रामजी! मेरी रक्षा कीजिए, रक्षा कीजिए।' (इस प्रकार आर्त प्रार्थना करो।) आर्त पुकार सुनते ही प्रभु तुमको निर्भय कर देंगे ॥
english_translation: Call out, 'O Ram, jewel of the Raghu line, protector of those who seek refuge, save me, save me.' Hearing a cry of distress, the Lord will make you fearless.
essence: Fear loosens when you call on Ram without pretence.
simple_meaning: Call on Ram from a place of need, and he answers by removing fear.
insight: It shifts you from self-protection to direct refuge, trusting that sincere calling changes your inner state.
modern_relevance: Your hands shake before the difficult phone call, and you cannot find the perfect words. Say the honest sentence anyway. This verse says that raw need can become courage.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रे कपिपोत बोलु संभारी। मूढ़ न जानेहि मोहि सुरारी॥ कहु निज नाम जनक कर भाई। केहि नातें मानिऐ मिताई ॥
translation: (रावण ने कहा-) अरे बंदर के बच्चे! सँभालकर बोल! मूर्ख! मुझ देवताओं के शत्रु को तूने जाना नहीं? अरे भाई! अपना और अपने बाप का नाम तो बता। किस नाते से मित्रता मानता है? ॥
english_translation: Ravana said, “Hey, monkey cub, speak carefully. Fool, you do not know me, enemy of the radiant beings. Tell me your own name and your father’s name. On what basis do you claim friendship?”
essence: Pride cannot hear truth without first demanding rank.
simple_meaning: Ravana insults Angad, demands to know who he is, and challenges the basis for calling him a friend.
insight: It reveals how ego reduces every encounter to status and bloodline instead of listening to the message.
modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a meeting and asks, with a smirk, “And who exactly are you to speak?” The need to dominate the room is louder than the words.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: अंगद नाम बालि कर बेटा। तासों कबहुँ भई ही भेंटा॥ अंगद बचन सुनत सकुचाना। रहा बालि बानर मैं जाना ॥
translation: (अंगद ने कहा-) मेरा नाम अंगद है, मैं बालि का पुत्र हूँ। उनसे कभी तुम्हारी भेंट हुई थी? अंगद का वचन सुनते ही रावण कुछ सकुचा गया (और बोला-) हाँ, मैं जान गया (मुझे याद आ गया), बालि नाम का एक बंदर था ॥
english_translation: Angad said, “My name is Angad. I am Bali’s son. Have you ever met him?” Hearing Angad’s words, Ravana became uneasy and said, “Yes, I remember now—there was a monkey named Bali.”
essence: A true name can shake pride before a single blow is struck.
simple_meaning: Angad identifies himself as Bali’s son, and Ravana is startled into remembering Bali. The verse is a step in the larger exchange, not a complete teaching on its own.
insight: It shows how identity and memory can puncture arrogance before any argument begins.
modern_relevance: You introduce yourself in a room where someone expected weakness, and suddenly their confidence shifts. A single name can carry the weight of history.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अंगद तहीं बालि कर बालक। उपजेहु बंस अनल कुल घालक॥ गर्भ न गयहु ब्यर्थ तुम्ह जायहु। निज मुख तापस दूत कहायहु ॥
translation: अरे अंगद! तू ही बालि का लड़का है? अरे कुलनाशक! तू तो अपने कुलरूपी बाँस के लिए अग्नि रूप ही पैदा हुआ! गर्भ में ही क्यों न नष्ट हो गया तू? व्यर्थ ही पैदा हुआ जो अपने ही मुँह से तपस्वियों का दूत कहलाया! ॥
english_translation: Are you Angad, Bali's son? O destroyer of your own line, you were born like fire for the bamboo of your clan. Why were you not lost in the womb? You were born in vain if you call yourself a messenger with your own mouth.
essence: Ravana's insult exposes his own fear, not Angad's weakness.
simple_meaning: Ravana insults Angad, calling him a useless destroyer of his own family and mocking his role as a messenger.
insight: It shows how wounded ego tries to regain control by humiliating the other person.
modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a heated meeting and starts attacking your family, background, and motives instead of answering the point. The insult reveals their panic more than your worth.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: अब कहु कुसल बालि कहँ अहई। बिहँसि बचन तब अंगद कहई॥ दिन दस गएँ बालि पहिं जाई। बूझेहु कुसल सखा उर लाई ॥
translation: अब बालि की कुशल तो बता, वह (आजकल) कहाँ है? तब अंगद ने हँसकर कहा- दस (कुछ) दिन बीतने पर (स्वयं ही) बालि के पास जाकर, अपने मित्र को हृदय से लगाकर, उसी से कुशल पूछ लेना ॥
english_translation: Now tell me, how is Bali doing? Where is he? Angad then said with a smile, "Go to Bali yourself after ten days, hold your friend close to your heart, and ask him about his welfare."
essence: A calm reply can turn pride back on itself.
simple_meaning: Angad answers Ravana with sharp irony: if you want to know how Bali is, go ask him yourself in the next world.
insight: It shows how fearless speech can dismantle arrogance without losing composure.
modern_relevance: Someone corners you with a smug question, expecting you to shrink. You smile, answer indirectly, and make them feel the weight of their own words.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: राम बिरोध कुसल जसि होई। सो सब तोहि सुनाइहि सोई॥ सुनु सठ भेद होइ मन ताकें। श्री रघुबीर हृदय नहिं जाकें ॥
translation: श्री रामजी से विरोध करने पर जैसी कुशल होती है, वह सब तुमको वे सुनावेंगे। हे मूर्ख! सुन, भेद उसी के मन में पड़ सकता है, (भेद नीति उसी पर अपना प्रभाव डाल सकती है) जिसके हृदय में श्री रघुवीर न हों ॥
english_translation: The good that comes from opposing Ram — Angad will tell you that. Listen, fool: only a heart without Shri Raghubir can be split by deceit.
essence: A heart anchored in Ram cannot be broken by deceit.
simple_meaning: Turning against Ram leaves you vulnerable to confusion and ruin. A heart that holds Ram cannot be split by trickery.
insight: It shifts attention from external tricks to the inner condition that lets those tricks work.
modern_relevance: A group chat starts turning poisonous, and one person keeps feeding the worst interpretation of everything. The verse points to a simple test: when your heart is steady, manipulation loses its grip.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: हम कुल घालक सत्य तुम्ह कुल पालक दससीस। अंधउ बधिर न अस कहहिं नयन कान तव बीस ॥
translation: सच है, मैं तो कुल का नाश करने वाला हूँ और हे रावण! तुम कुल के रक्षक हो। अंधे-बहरे भी ऐसी बात नहीं कहते, तुम्हारे तो बीस नेत्र और बीस कान हैं! ॥
english_translation: I am the destroyer of my line, and you, Ravana, are the protector of your line. Even the blind and deaf would not say such a thing; you have twenty eyes and twenty ears.
essence: Power without clear seeing becomes self-destruction.
simple_meaning: Hanuman mocks Ravana’s pride: Ravana claims to protect his own family, while Hanuman calls himself the one who will destroy his own line. The point is that Ravana is blind to his own condition.
insight: It shifts attention from outward capability to inward perception, warning that ego can distort judgment even when the facts are obvious.
modern_relevance: You’re in a meeting, defending a bad decision because backing down feels humiliating. Everyone can see the flaw except you. This verse captures that dangerous blindness of ego.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: सिव बिरंचि सुर मुनि समुदाई। चाहत जासु चरन सेवकाई॥ तासु दूत होइ हम कुल बोरा। अइसिहुँ मति उर बिहर न तोरा ॥
translation: शिव, ब्रह्मा (आदि) देवता और मुनियों के समुदाय जिनके चरणों की सेवा (करना) चाहते हैं, उनका दूत होकर मैंने कुल को डुबा दिया? अरे ऐसी बुद्धि होने पर भी तुम्हारा हृदय फट नहीं जाता? ॥
english_translation: Shiva, Brahma, the gods, and the gathered sages long to serve at his feet. Yet I, his messenger, have ruined my own clan? Even with such understanding, does your heart not break?
essence: Pride collapses when it has to answer to reverence.
simple_meaning: Ravana shames himself for becoming the messenger of one who is worshipped by Shiva, Brahma, gods, and sages. He says this should have shattered Ravana's heart.
insight: It turns humiliation into self-exposure: the real wound is not the insult, but seeing your own arrogance clearly.
modern_relevance: You bragged all week about being untouchable, then had to admit you were wrong in front of everyone. The shame hurts most when your own words corner you.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सुनि कठोर बानी कपि केरी। कहत दसानन नयन तरेरी॥ खल तव कठिन बचन सब सहऊँ। नीति धर्म मैं जानत अहऊँ ॥
translation: वानर (अंगद) की कठोर वाणी सुनकर रावण आँखें तरेरकर (तिरछी करके) बोला- अरे दुष्ट! मैं तेरे सब कठोर वचन इसीलिए सह रहा हूँ कि मैं नीति और धर्म को जानता हूँ (उन्हीं की रक्षा कर रहा हूँ) ॥
english_translation: Hearing the monkey's harsh words, Ravana glared and said, 'Villain, I bear your harsh speech because I know policy and dharma.'
essence: You can speak of dharma while your pride still leads.
simple_meaning: Ravana claims he can tolerate harsh words because he understands policy and dharma, but his reaction shows his pride is still in control.
insight: It separates intellectual knowledge from actual self-control, showing that insight must be embodied to matter.
modern_relevance: You stay calm in the meeting and say, 'I understand the bigger picture,' while your jaw is tight and your mind is burning. The words may be polished; the reaction tells the truth.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: कह कपि धर्मसीलता तोरी। हमहुँ सुनी कृत पर त्रिय चोरी॥ देखी नयन दूत रखवारी। बूड़ि न मरहु धर्म ब्रतधारी ॥
translation: अंगद ने कहा- तुम्हारी धर्मशीलता मैंने भी सुनी है। (वह यह कि) तुमने पराई स्त्री की चोरी की है! और दूत की रक्षा की बात तो अपनी आँखों से देख ली। ऐसे धर्म के व्रत को धारण (पालन) करने वाले तुम डूबकर मर नहीं जाते! ॥
english_translation: Angad said, "I have also heard of your righteousness. You stole another man's wife, and I have seen with my own eyes how you guarded your own messenger. Do not die drowning while claiming to uphold righteousness!"
essence: Your actions expose the truth your pride tries to hide.
simple_meaning: Angad mocks Ravana's claim of righteousness by pointing to his own actions: abducting another man's wife and protecting his messenger. The point is that conduct, not labels, reveals character.
insight: It shifts attention from self-description to self-observation, forcing you to measure yourself by action instead of image.
modern_relevance: You post about integrity, then cut a corner when no one is watching. Angad's words land because they expose the gap between your self-image and your actual behavior.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: कान नाक बिनु भगिनि निहारी। छमा कीन्हि तुम्ह धर्म बिचारी॥ धर्मसीलता तव जग जागी। पावा दरसु हमहुँ बड़भागी ॥
translation: नाक-कान से रहित बहिन को देखकर तुमने धर्म विचारकर ही तो क्षमा कर दिया था! तुम्हारी धर्मशीलता जगजाहिर है। मैं भी बड़ा भाग्यवान् हूँ, जो मैंने तुम्हारा दर्शन पाया? ॥
english_translation: Seeing your sister without her nose and ears, you still forgave her after considering dharma. Your devotion to righteousness is famous in the world. I too am fortunate to have seen you.
essence: Pride can disguise itself as respect when it feels cornered.
simple_meaning: Ravana flatters Angad by saying he once forgave a mutilated sister after thinking about dharma, and that his righteousness is well known.
insight: It shows how ego can use praise as a shield, turning moral language into manipulation.
modern_relevance: Someone argues with you, then suddenly starts complimenting your character to regain control of the room. The praise sounds respectful, but it is really a tactic.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: जनि जल्पसि जड़ जंतु कपि सठ बिलोकु मम बाहु। लोकपाल बल बिपुल ससि ग्रसन हेतु सब राहु ॥
translation: (रावण ने कहा-) अरे जड़ जन्तु वानर! व्यर्थ बक-बक न कर, अरे मूर्ख! मेरी भुजाएँ तो देख। ये सब लोकपालों के विशाल बल रूपी चंद्रमा को ग्रसने के लिए राहु हैं ॥
english_translation: Ravana said, "You foolish monkey, stop babbling and look at my arms. These are all Rahus meant to swallow the great moon of the guardians of the worlds."
essence: Ego mistakes its own force for invincibility.
simple_meaning: Ravana insults Hanuman and boasts that his arms are so powerful they can swallow the might of all the world’s guardians.
insight: It shifts the mind to recognize bravado as a sign of inner blindness, not real power.
modern_relevance: You dominate the meeting with sharp words and a louder voice, but everyone can feel the insecurity underneath. The room hears strength; the wiser eye sees fear.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: पुनि नभ सर मम कर निकर कमलन्हि पर करि बास। सोभत भयउ मराल इव संभु सहित कैलास ॥
translation: फिर (तूने सुना ही होगा कि) आकाश रूपी तालाब में मेरी भुजाओं रूपी कमलों पर बसकर शिवजी सहित कैलास हंस के समान शोभा को प्राप्त हुआ था! ॥
english_translation: Then, as you must have heard, the sky-lake found a swan-like beauty when Shiva and Kailash rested on my arms like lotuses.
essence: Pride turns strength into a story about yourself.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that even Shiva and Kailash once seemed to rest beautifully on his arms, showing off his own strength and grandeur.
insight: It exposes how ego inflates memory into self-worship and blocks real listening.
modern_relevance: Someone in a meeting starts listing old achievements to shut down a challenge. The room goes quiet, but everyone can feel the same thing: insecurity dressed up as power.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: तुम्हरे कटक माझ सुनु अंगद। मो सन भिरिहि कवन जोधा बद॥ तब प्रभु नारि बिरहँ बलहीना। अनुज तासु दुख दुखी मलीना ॥
translation: अरे अंगद! सुन, तेरी सेना में बता, ऐसा कौन योद्धा है, जो मुझसे भिड़ सकेगा। तेरा मालिक तो स्त्री के वियोग में बलहीन हो रहा है और उसका छोटा भाई उसी के दुःख से दुःखी और उदास है ॥
english_translation: Listen, Angad: in your army, tell me, which warrior can fight me? Your lord is weakening from separation from his wife, and his younger brother is sorrowful and dulled by that grief.
essence: Boasting grows loudest when it fears defeat.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that no warrior in Angad's army can match him, then mocks Ram as weakened by separation from Sita and Lakshman as weakened by Ram's sorrow.
insight: It shows how ego attacks by exaggerating itself and reducing others through their pain.
modern_relevance: Someone in a heated argument starts listing their own achievements and then reaches for your weakest wound. The words sound powerful, but they are really panic dressed as confidence.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: तुम्ह सुग्रीव कूलद्रुम दोऊ। अनुज हमार भीरु अति सोऊ॥ जामवंत मंत्री अति बूढ़ा। सो कि होइ अब समरारूढ़ा ॥
translation: तुम और सुग्रीव, दोनों (नदी) तट के वृक्ष हो (रहा) मेरा छोटा भाई विभीषण, (सो) वह भी बड़ा डरपोक है। मंत्री जाम्बवान् बहुत बूढ़ा है। वह अब लड़ाई में क्या चढ़ (उद्यत हो) सकता है? ॥
english_translation: You and Sugriva are both riverside trees. My younger brother Vibhishana is very timid. Jambavan is very old—how can he now be ready for battle?
essence: Arrogance shrinks others so it can feel larger.
simple_meaning: Ravana dismisses the strength of the opposing side by calling Sugriva and Vibhishana timid and Jambavan too old for war.
insight: It exposes how ego misreads weakness and mistakes contempt for insight.
modern_relevance: You brush off a team because one person is quiet, another is new, and another is older. The mistake is not theirs — it's your blind spot.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सिल्पि कर्म जानहिं नल नीला। है कपि एक महा बलसीला॥ आवा प्रथम नगरु जेहिं जारा। सुनत बचन कह बालिकुमारा ॥
translation: नल-नील तो शिल्प-कर्म जानते हैं (वे लड़ना क्या जानें?)। हाँ, एक वानर जरूर महान् बलवान् है, जो पहले आया था और जिसने लंका जलाई थी। यह वचन सुनते ही बालि पुत्र अंगद ने कहा- ॥
english_translation: Nala and Nila know only craftsmanship. There is one monkey of great strength who came first and burned the city. Hearing this, Angada, the son of Bali, said—
essence: One remembered act of courage can outweigh a roomful of boasts.
simple_meaning: Angada points out that Nala and Nila are builders, not warriors, and recalls the one powerful monkey who burned Lanka first.
insight: It shows how reputation can silence arrogance before the fight even begins.
modern_relevance: In a tense meeting, someone dismisses the quiet people in the room. Then one person names the moment everyone remembers — and the whole balance changes.
speaker: Angada

verse_text: सत्य बचन कहु निसिचर नाहा। साँचेहुँ कीस कीन्ह पुर दाहा॥ रावण नगर अल्प कपि दहई। सुनि अस बचन सत्य को कहई ॥
translation: हे राक्षसराज! सच्ची बात कहो! क्या उस वानर ने सचमुच तुम्हारा नगर जला दिया? रावण (जैसे जगद्विजयी योद्धा) का नगर एक छोटे से वानर ने जला दिया। ऐसे वचन सुनकर उन्हें सत्य कौन कहेगा? ॥
english_translation: O lord of the demons, speak truly. Did that monkey really burn your city? Ravana's city was burned by a tiny monkey. Hearing such words, who would believe they are true?
essence: Great deeds can sound unbelievable before they are understood.
simple_meaning: The speaker asks Ravana to confirm the unbelievable report that a tiny monkey burned Lanka. The verse highlights how strange Hanuman's feat sounds.
insight: It frames Hanuman's feat as so extraordinary that even enemies struggle to name it honestly.
modern_relevance: You hear a story so absurd it sounds impossible, yet the damage is already in front of you. Sometimes reality arrives wearing the face of disbelief.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जो अति सुभट सराहेहु रावन। सो सुग्रीव केर लघु धावन॥ चलइ बहुत सो बीर न होई। पठवा खबरि लेन हम सोई ॥
translation: हे रावण! जिसको तुमने बहुत बड़ा योद्धा कहकर सराहा है, वह तो सुग्रीव का एक छोटा सा दौड़कर चलने वाला हरकारा है। वह बहुत चलता है, वीर नहीं है। उसको तो हमने (केवल) खबर लेने के लिए भेजा था ॥
english_translation: O Ravana, the one you praised as a great warrior is only Sugriva’s small messenger. He runs a lot, but he is not a true hero. We sent him only to gather news.
essence: Fear makes a messenger look like a monster.
simple_meaning: The monkey Ravana praised was not a warrior at all, just a messenger sent to gather information.
insight: It shifts the mind from exaggerated fear to clear-eyed proportion.
modern_relevance: A rumor spreads through a group chat, and by noon the quiet person who asked one question has become a threat in everyone’s mind. Fear often inflates what is actually ordinary.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सत्य नगरु कपि जारेउ बिनु प्रभु आयसु पाइ। फिरि न गयउ सुग्रीव पहिं तेहिं भय रहा लुकाइ ॥
translation: क्या सचमुच ही उस वानर ने प्रभु की आज्ञा पाए बिना ही तुम्हारा नगर जला डाला? मालूम होता है, इसी डर से वह लौटकर सुग्रीव के पास नहीं गया और कहीं छिप रहा! ॥
english_translation: Did that monkey burn your city without receiving his Lord's command? It seems he did not return to Sugriva because of fear, but hid somewhere instead.
essence: Pride can make courage look like fear.
simple_meaning: Ravana is still trying to make sense of Hanuman's burning of Lanka, assuming it happened without Ram's command and out of fear.
insight: It exposes how ego distorts evidence to avoid feeling diminished.
modern_relevance: You get a message that clearly shows someone acted with purpose, but you rewrite it as panic or accident because the truth stings your pride.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सत्य कहहि दसकंठ सब मोहि न सुनि कछु कोह। कोउ न हमारें कटक अस तो सन लरत जो सोह ॥
translation: हे रावण! तुम सब सत्य ही कहते हो, मुझे सुनकर कुछ भी क्रोध नहीं है। सचमुच हमारी सेना में कोई भी ऐसा नहीं है, जो तुमसे लड़ने में शोभा पाए ॥
english_translation: Ravana, you speak the truth. I feel no anger at hearing it. There is no one in our army who would be worthy to fight you.
essence: Strength is met best by calm honesty, not wounded pride.
simple_meaning: Ravana is told that his boast is true, and there is no anger in reply. The speaker admits that no one in his army is fit to match Ravana in battle.
insight: It teaches you to meet arrogance with clear seeing, not reactive anger.
modern_relevance: Someone cuts you down in front of a room, expecting a fight. You don't scramble to prove yourself; you answer cleanly, without heat, and the tension changes.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: प्रीति बिरोध समान सन करिअ नीति असि आहि। जौं मृगपति बध मेडुकन्हि भल कि कहइ कोउ ताहि ॥
translation: प्रीति और वैर बराबरी वाले से ही करना चाहिए, नीति ऐसी ही है। सिंह यदि मेंढकों को मारे, तो क्या उसे कोई भला कहेगा? ॥
english_translation: Friendship and hostility belong with equals; that is the proper rule. If a lion kills frogs, who would call that noble?
essence: True conduct does not prove itself by hurting the powerless.
simple_meaning: Ravana says true conduct is to deal with equals, not to attack the weak. A great person does not win praise by harming those beneath them.
insight: It shifts the mind from domination to fairness in conflict.
modern_relevance: You win an argument with someone who has no voice in the room, then call it firmness. The discomfort you feel afterward is this verse: strength is only worthy when it meets strength.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: जद्यपि लघुता राम कहुँ तोहि बधें बड़ दोष। तदपि कठिन दसकंठ सुनु छत्र जाति कर रोष ॥
translation: यद्यपि तुम्हें मारने में श्री रामजी की लघुता है और बड़ा दोष भी है तथापि हे रावण! सुनो, क्षत्रिय जाति का क्रोध बड़ा कठिन होता है ॥
english_translation: Although it would be a slight for Ram to kill you and a great fault, still listen, Ravana: the anger of a kshatriya is hard to restrain.
essence: True strength can choose restraint even when anger is justified.
simple_meaning: Angad says that killing Ravana would be beneath Ram and morally wrong, but a warrior's anger is still fierce and difficult to stop.
insight: It shifts the mind from raw retaliation to disciplined force, showing that power is strongest when it can hold itself back.
modern_relevance: In a heated family argument, you know you could land the final blow with one cruel sentence. But you also know restraint matters more than winning.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: बक्र उक्ति धनु बचन सर हृदय दहेउ रिपु कीस। प्रतिउत्तर सड़सिन्ह मनहुँ काढ़त भट दससीस ॥
translation: वक्रोक्ति रूपी धनुष से वचन रूपी बाण मारकर अंगद ने शत्रु का हृदय जला दिया। वीर रावण उन बाणों को मानो प्रत्युत्तर रूपी सँड़सियों से निकाल रहा है ॥
english_translation: Angad's crooked words, like arrows from a bow, burned the enemy's heart. Ravana, the ten-headed one, was like a warrior pulling those arrows out with iron tongs.
essence: Words can strike harder than arrows when pride is the target.
simple_meaning: Angad's sharp words strike Ravana so hard that they feel like arrows burning his heart. Ravana tries to pull the insult out, but it only exposes his pride.
insight: It shows how verbal truth can expose ego more sharply than force.
modern_relevance: A calm sentence in a tense meeting can hit harder than a raised voice. The other person smiles, but you can see they are still pulling the words out of their chest.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हँसि बोलेउ दसमौलि तब कपि कर बड़ गुन एक। जो प्रतिपालइ तासु हित करइ उपाय अनेक ॥
translation: तब रावण हँसकर बोला- बंदर में यह एक बड़ा गुण है कि जो उसे पालता है, उसका वह अनेकों उपायों से भला करने की चेष्टा करता है ॥
english_translation: Ravana then laughed and said, "Monkeys have one great quality: whoever feeds them, they try to help in many ways."
essence: Pride turns devotion into a joke.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Hanuman by saying a monkey repays care by trying to help its benefactor in every possible way.
insight: It shows how ego can reduce genuine loyalty into something trivial or useful.
modern_relevance: A person smiles in a meeting and says, "You mean well," but the tone cuts deeper than anger. Pride can disguise dismissal as compliment.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: धन्य कीस जो निज प्रभु काजा। जहँ तहँ नाचइ परिहरि लाजा॥ नाचि कूदि करि लोग रिझाई। पति हित करइ धर्म निपुनाई ॥
translation: बंदर को धन्य है, जो अपने मालिक के लिए लाज छोड़कर जहाँ-तहाँ नाचता है। नाच-कूदकर, लोगों को रिझाकर, मालिक का हित करता है। यह उसके धर्म की निपुणता है ॥
english_translation: Blessed is the monkey who, for his own lord's work, forgets shame and dances wherever needed. By dancing and leaping, he delights people and serves his lord well; that is skill in righteous duty.
essence: True service forgets embarrassment and becomes fearless usefulness.
simple_meaning: A devoted servant is praised for setting aside embarrassment, doing whatever helps the master, and using skillful, even playful action to serve well.
insight: It shifts service from image-management to wholehearted usefulness.
modern_relevance: You volunteer to lead the messy part of the event, even if it means looking awkward in front of everyone. What matters is that the work gets done and the people you serve are helped.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अंगद स्वामिभक्त तव जाती। प्रभु गुन कस न कहसि एहि भाँती॥ मैं गुन गाहक परम सुजाना। तव कटु रटनि करउँ नहिं काना ॥
translation: हे अंगद! तेरी जाति स्वामिभक्त है (फिर भला) तू अपने मालिक के गुण इस प्रकार कैसे न बखानेगा? मैं गुण ग्राहक (गुणों का आदर करने वाला) और परम सुजान (समझदार) हूँ, इसी से तेरी जली-कटी बक-बक पर कान (ध्यान) नहीं देता ॥
english_translation: Angad, your nature is to serve your master. How could you not praise your lord's virtues in this way? I am a true appreciator of virtues and deeply wise, so I do not even listen to your bitter taunts.
essence: Pride can wear the mask of wisdom and still remain untouched.
simple_meaning: Ravana tells Angad that a loyal servant naturally praises his master, and he claims he is wise enough not to be bothered by Angad's harsh words.
insight: It shows how wounded ego can sound composed while still resisting the truth.
modern_relevance: Someone makes a cutting remark in a meeting, and you answer with a smile that hides your irritation. Ravana's tone feels like that kind of controlled defensiveness.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: कह कपि तव गुन गाहकताई। सत्य पवनसुत मोहि सुनाई॥ बन बिधंसि सुत बधि पुर जारा। तदपि न तेहिं कछु कृत अपकारा ॥
translation: अंगद ने कहा- तुम्हारी सच्ची गुण ग्राहकता तो मुझे हनुमान् ने सुनाई थी। उसने अशोक वन में विध्वंस (तहस-नहस) करके, तुम्हारे पुत्र को मारकर नगर को जला दिया था। तो भी (तुमने अपनी गुण ग्राहकता के कारण यही समझा कि) उसने तुम्हारा कुछ भी अपकार नहीं किया ॥
english_translation: Angad said, "Hanuman himself told me of your true love for virtue. He had destroyed the Ashoka grove, killed your son, and burned the city, yet you still felt he had done you no harm."
essence: You reveal your own greatness when you can praise the one who hurt you.
simple_meaning: A noble heart can recognize goodness even after being hurt. Angad says Ravana's ability to appreciate Hanuman's qualities proved his own hidden virtue.
insight: It shifts attention from offense to character: a strong mind can recognize excellence even under attack.
modern_relevance: Someone criticizes you harshly, yet still admits, quietly, that you handled the hardest part better than anyone else. That split-second honesty is what Angad notices in Ravana.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: सोइ बिचारि तव प्रकृति सुहाई। दसकंधर मैं कीन्हि ढिठाई॥ देखेउँ आइ जो कछु कपि भाषा। तुम्हरें लाज न रोष न माखा ॥
translation: तुम्हारा वही सुंदर स्वभाव विचार कर, हे दशग्रीव! मैंने कुछ धृष्टता की है। हनुमान् ने जो कुछ कहा था, उसे आकर मैंने प्रत्यक्ष देख लिया कि तुम्हें न लज्जा है, न क्रोध है और न चिढ़ है ॥
english_translation: Thinking of your fine nature, O Ravana, I have acted boldly. I came and saw for myself what Hanuman had said: you feel no shame, no anger, and no embarrassment.
essence: Seeing clearly leaves no room for flattering denial.
simple_meaning: Angad says he spoke boldly only after seeing Ravana's character firsthand. He confirms Hanuman's warning: Ravana has no shame, anger, or restraint.
insight: It teaches you to trust direct observation over reputation or excuses.
modern_relevance: You finally meet the manager everyone warned you about, and the room feels colder than the stories did. The mask is gone; you can see the pattern yourself.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: जौं असि मति पितु खाए कीसा। कहि अस बचन हँसा दससीसा॥ पितहि खाइ खातेउँ पुनि तोही। अबहीं समुझि परा कछु मोही ॥
translation: (रावण बोला-) अरे वानर! जब तेरी ऐसी बुद्धि है, तभी तो तू बाप को खा गया। ऐसा वचन कहकर रावण हँसा। अंगद ने कहा- पिता को खाकर फिर तुमको भी खा डालता, परन्तु अभी तुरंत कुछ और ही बात मेरी समझ में आ गई! ॥
english_translation: Ravana said, "If your mind is like this, you must have eaten your father too." Laughing at those words, Angada replied, "I would have eaten my father and then eaten you too, but just now I understood something else."
essence: Mockery answers mockery until someone remembers the real stakes.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Angada with a cruel insult, and Angada answers with sharp wit, saying he would have destroyed Ravana too if not for a new realization.
insight: It reveals how insult escalates into performance when ego is in charge.
modern_relevance: Someone throws a nasty joke in a group chat, and the room goes quiet. You can feel the old reflex to strike back harder, even when the real issue is someone's wounded pride.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: बालि बिमल जस भाजन जानी। हतउँ न तोहि अधम अभिमानी॥ कहु रावन रावन जग केते। मैं निज श्रवन सुने सुनु जेते ॥
translation: अरे नीच अभिमानी! बालि के निर्मल यश का पात्र (कारण) जानकर तुम्हें मैं नहीं मारता। रावण! यह तो बता कि जगत् में कितने रावण हैं? मैंने जितने रावण अपने कानों से सुन रखे हैं, उन्हें सुन- ॥
english_translation: Knowing you were the kind of man who brought fame to Bali, I did not kill you, arrogant one. Tell me, Ravana: how many Ravanas are there in the world? I have heard many with my own ears.
essence: Ego is not unique; it is the same mask wearing many names.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the enemy's pride and says his arrogance is nothing special. He treats Ravana-like ego as a common pattern, not a unique identity.
insight: It shifts attention from the person to the pattern of ego driving the speech.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who keeps repeating the same boast in a group chat, as if no one has heard that tone before. The room goes quiet when you realize the swagger is just a costume worn by many insecure minds.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: बलिहि जितन एक गयउ पताला। राखेउ बाँधि सिसुन्ह हयसाला॥ खेलहिं बालक मारहिं जाई। दया लागि बलि दीन्ह छोड़ाई ॥
translation: एक रावण तो बलि को जीतने पाताल में गया था, तब बच्चों ने उसे घुड़साल में बाँध रखा। बालक खेलते थे और जा-जाकर उसे मारते थे। बलि को दया लगी, तब उन्होंने उसे छुड़ा दिया ॥
english_translation: One Ravana had gone down to the netherworld to conquer Bali, and the children had tied him up in the stable. The children played by going and striking him, and Bali, moved by compassion, released him.
essence: Power becomes human when it can still release the defeated.
simple_meaning: Bali once caught Ravana and had him tied up in a stable, where children mocked and hit him. Feeling pity, Bali set him free.
insight: It shifts the mind from revenge to mercy, even when the other person has done wrong.
modern_relevance: A bully at school gets cornered, mocked, and suddenly looks smaller than the anger around him. The real test is whether you can still choose mercy when you have the upper hand.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक बहोरि सहसभुज देखा। धाइ धरा जिमि जंतु बिसेषा॥ कौतुक लागि भवन लै आवा। सो पुलस्ति मुनि जाइ छोड़ावा ॥
translation: फिर एक रावण को सहस्रबाहु ने देखा, और उसने दौड़कर उसको एक विशेष प्रकार के (विचित्र) जन्तु की तरह (समझकर) पकड़ लिया। तमाशे के लिए वह उसे घर ले आया। तब पुलस्त्य मुनि ने जाकर उसे छुड़ाया ॥
english_translation: Again, Ravana was seen by Sahasrabahu, who ran and seized him as if he were a strange creature. For amusement, he carried him home. Then the sage Pulastya went and freed him.
essence: Pride shrinks fast when reality grabs hold.
simple_meaning: Sahasrabahu catches Ravana like an odd creature and takes him home as a joke. Pulastya later goes and frees Ravana.
insight: It shifts the mind from inflated self-image to sober self-awareness.
modern_relevance: Someone posts a grand self-image online, then gets exposed by a simple fact everyone else already knows. The humiliation lands hardest because the arrogance was so loud.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक कहत मोहि सकुच अति रहा बालि कीं काँख। इन्ह महुँ रावन तैं कवन सत्य बदहि तजि माख ॥
translation: एक रावण की बात कहने में तो मुझे बड़ा संकोच हो रहा है- वह (बहुत दिनों तक) बालि की काँख में रहा था। इनमें से तुम कौन से रावण हो? खीझना छोड़कर सच-सच बताओ ॥
english_translation: I feel too shy to even mention one Ravana. One stayed in Bali's armpit. Which Ravana are you? Drop the irritation and tell the truth.
essence: Pride softens when truth is demanded without fear.
simple_meaning: The speaker jokes that there have been different Ravanas in strange situations, so the listener should stop getting offended and speak plainly.
insight: It shifts the exchange from ego-protection to honest self-disclosure.
modern_relevance: Someone keeps dodging a straight question with wounded pride and defensive jokes. A calm, teasing line can sometimes do what pressure cannot: make the truth come out.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: चौपाई : : सुनु सठ सोइ रावन बलसीला। हरगिरि जान जासु भुज लीला॥ जान उमापति जासु सुराई। पूजेउँ जेहि सिर सुमन चढ़ाई ॥
translation: (रावण ने कहा-) अरे मूर्ख! सुन, मैं वही बलवान् रावण हूँ, जिसकी भुजाओं की लीला (करामात) कैलास पर्वत जानता है। जिसकी शूरता उमापति महादेवजी जानते हैं, जिन्हें अपने सिर रूपी पुष्प चढ़ा-चढ़ाकर मैंने पूजा था ॥
english_translation: Listen, fool: I am that mighty Ravana, whose arms even Mount Kailash has known. Lord Shiva, husband of Uma, knows my valor, and I have worshiped him by offering my own heads as flowers.
essence: Pride can dress itself up as devotion and still remain pride.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that even Shiva and Mount Kailash know his power, and he claims to have worshiped Shiva by offering his own heads.
insight: It exposes how ego can hijack even sincere devotion and turn it into a performance.
modern_relevance: Someone in a heated argument starts listing every sacrifice they ever made, not to be understood but to win. The story feels familiar because wounded pride loves a résumé.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सिर सरोज निज करन्हि उतारी। पूजेउँ अमित बार त्रिपुरारी॥ भुज बिक्रम जानहिं दिगपाला। सठ अजहूँ जिन्ह कें उर साला ॥
translation: सिर रूपी कमलों को अपने हाथों से उतार-उतारकर मैंने अगणित बार त्रिपुरारि शिवजी की पूजा की है। अरे मूर्ख! मेरी भुजाओं का पराक्रम दिक्पाल जानते हैं, जिनके हृदय में वह आज भी चुभ रहा है ॥
english_translation: I have lifted the lotus-like heads with my own hands and worshipped Tripurari countless times. Fools, the mighty force of my arms is known to the guardians of the directions, and that ache still stings their hearts.
essence: Devotion loses its purity when it becomes proof of superiority.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he has worshipped Shiva many times and that even the guardians of the directions know how powerful his arms are.
insight: It exposes how ego borrows even sacred acts to defend itself.
modern_relevance: You start listing your achievements in a tense conversation, hoping the other person will back down. The words may be true, but the need to prove yourself is already the problem.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: जानहिं दिग्गज उर कठिनाई। जब जब भिरउँ जाइ बरिआई॥ जिन्ह के दसन कराल न फूटे। उर लागत मूलक इव टूटे ॥
translation: दिग्गज (दिशाओं के हाथी) मेरी छाती की कठोरता को जानते हैं। जिनके भयानक दाँत, जब-जब जाकर मैं उनसे जबरदस्ती भिड़ा, मेरी छाती में कभी नहीं फूटे (अपना चिह्न भी नहीं बना सके), बल्कि मेरी छाती से लगते ही वे मूली की तरह टूट गए ॥
english_translation: The great elephants of the directions know my chest's hardness. When I fought them by force again and again, their terrible tusks never broke my chest; instead, they shattered like radishes against it.
essence: Hardness can become a boast that blinds you.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that even the strongest beings could not break his chest in battle; their teeth shattered against him instead.
insight: It exposes how raw force and self-glorification can masquerade as strength while hiding inner blindness.
modern_relevance: You keep listing the times you survived the worst blow, as if toughness proves you are right. Sometimes that very hardness is what keeps you from seeing clearly.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: जासु चलत डोलति इमि धरनी। चढ़त मत्त गज जिमि लघु तरनी॥ सोइ रावन जग बिदित प्रतापी। सुनेहि न श्रवन अलीक प्रलापी ॥
translation: जिसके चलते समय पृथ्वी इस प्रकार हिलती है जैसे मतवाले हाथी के चढ़ते समय छोटी नाव! मैं वही जगत प्रसिद्ध प्रतापी रावण हूँ। अरे झूठी बकवास करने वाले! क्या तूने मुझको कानों से कभी सुना? ॥
english_translation: As he walked, the earth trembled, just as a small boat rocks when a drunken elephant climbs aboard. I am that famous, mighty Ravana known throughout the world. Have you ever heard me with your own ears, you false babbler?
essence: Ego shouts its greatness and cannot hear the truth.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that his power shakes the earth and that his fame is known everywhere. He dismisses the speaker as a liar and pretends his own greatness proves everything.
insight: It exposes how self-importance turns listening into self-defense.
modern_relevance: Someone interrupts you in a meeting and starts listing their achievements instead of hearing the warning in front of them. That reflex to defend status can block the very help that could save them.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: तेहि रावन कहँ लघु कहसि नर कर करसि बखान। रे कपि बर्बर खर्ब खल अब जाना तव ग्यान ॥
translation: उस (महान प्रतापी और जगत प्रसिद्ध) रावण को (मुझे) तू छोटा कहता है और मनुष्य की बड़ाई करता है? अरे दुष्ट, असभ्य, तुच्छ बंदर! अब मैंने तेरा ज्ञान जान लिया ॥
english_translation: Why do you call Ravana small and praise a mere human? O vile, crude, worthless monkey, now I have understood your wisdom.
essence: Pride cannot hear truth without feeling attacked.
simple_meaning: Ravana insults Angad for praising Ram and calling Ravana small. He takes the praise as an attack on his pride and dismisses Angad as foolish.
insight: It shows how ego turns honest challenge into contempt and blocks self-correction.
modern_relevance: Someone points out a blind spot in a meeting, and you snap back at them instead of hearing the truth. Ravana's response is what wounded pride sounds like.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सुनि अंगद सकोप कह बानी। बोलु संभारि अधम अभिमानी॥ सहसबाहु भुज गहन अपारा। दहन अनल सम जासु कुठारा ॥
translation: रावण के ये वचन सुनकर अंगद क्रोध सहित वचन बोले- अरे नीच अभिमानी! सँभलकर (सोच-समझकर) बोल। जिनका फरसा सहस्रबाहु की भुजाओं रूपी अपार वन को जलाने के लिए अग्नि के समान था, ॥
english_translation: Hearing Ravana's words, Angada spoke in anger: "Speak carefully, you shameless fool. Parashurama's axe was like fire, burning through the boundless forest of Sahasrabahu's arms."
essence: Boastful pride meets a voice that refuses to bow.
simple_meaning: Angada angrily tells Ravana to speak carefully and calls him arrogant and lowly. He then praises Parashurama's axe as a fire that burned through Sahasrabahu's vast armory of power.
insight: It shows how righteous anger can interrupt ego before it spreads.
modern_relevance: Someone in a meeting starts bragging so loudly that the room tightens. You don't have to flatter that energy. Sometimes the clean response is a firm correction.
speaker: Angada

verse_text: जासु परसु सागर खर धारा। बूड़े नृप अगनित बहु बारा॥ तासु गर्ब जेहि देखत भागा। सो नर क्यों दससीस अभागा ॥
translation: जिनके फरसा रूपी समुद्र की तीव्र धारा में अनगिनत राजा अनेकों बार डूब गए, उन परशुरामजी का गर्व जिन्हें देखते ही भाग गया, अरे अभागे दशशीश! वे मनुष्य क्यों कर हैं? ॥
english_translation: The fierce stream of Parashurama's axe has sunk countless kings many times. Even his pride fled at the sight of him. Why, then, can that unlucky ten-headed one call him a mere man?
essence: Pride cannot recognize the power that will undo it.
simple_meaning: Angad reminds Ravana that Parashurama is no ordinary man: his axe has destroyed many kings, and even pride itself would flee before him. Ravana is foolish to dismiss such power.
insight: It exposes how pride distorts judgment and invites self-destruction.
modern_relevance: You brush off a warning because you think you already know better. Then the room goes quiet, and you realise the person you dismissed had every reason to be feared.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: राम मनुज कस रे सठ बंगा। धन्वी कामु नदी पुनि गंगा॥ पसु सुरधेनु कल्पतरु रूखा। अन्न दान अरु रस पीयूषा ॥
translation: क्यों रे मूर्ख उद्दण्ड! श्री रामचंद्रजी मनुष्य हैं? कामदेव भी क्या धनुर्धारी है? और गंगाजी क्या नदी हैं? कामधेनु क्या पशु है? और कल्पवृक्ष क्या पेड़ है? अन्न भी क्या दान है? और अमृत क्या रस है? ॥
english_translation: How can you say Ram is merely a man, you fool? Is desire merely an archer, is the Ganges merely a river? Is Kamadhenu merely an animal, is the wish-fulfilling tree merely a tree? Is giving merely food, is nectar merely a drink?
essence: Ram cannot be reduced to an ordinary human life.
simple_meaning: Angad rebukes Ravana for reducing Ram to an ordinary man. He says sacred things cannot be judged by surface appearances, because their true power is far greater.
insight: It shifts the mind from literal appearance to hidden greatness.
modern_relevance: Someone dismisses a mentor, parent, or quiet devotee because they look unimpressive. Later, their strength, grace, or wisdom changes the room. This verse warns you not to mistake appearance for worth.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: बैनतेय खग अहि सहसानन। चिंतामनि पुनि उपल दसानन॥ सुनु मतिमंद लोक बैकुंठा। लाभ कि रघुपति भगति अकुंठा ॥
