translation: गरुड़जी क्या पक्षी हैं? शेषजी क्या सर्प हैं? अरे रावण! चिंतामणि भी क्या पत्थर है? अरे ओ मूर्ख! सुन, वैकुण्ठ भी क्या लोक है? और श्री रघुनाथजी की अखण्ड भक्ति क्या (और लाभों जैसा ही) लाभ है? ॥
english_translation: Is Garuda merely a bird? Is Shesha merely a serpent? O Ravana, is even the wish-fulfilling gem just a stone? O dull-minded one, listen: is Vaikuntha merely a realm, and is devoted love for Raghunath not the greatest gain?
essence: Devotion to Ram makes every lesser prize look small.
simple_meaning: Garuda is not just a bird, Shesha is not just a serpent, and Vaikuntha is not the only prize. Devoted love for Ram is the greatest gain of all.
insight: It shifts the mind from status and objects to the value of unwavering devotion.
modern_relevance: You can chase a promotion, a perfect address, or a bigger bank balance and still feel empty. Then one quiet practice of love and remembrance changes what counts as wealth.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सेन सहित तव मान मथि बन उजारि पुर जारि। कस रे सठ हनुमान कपि गयउ जो तव सुत मारि ॥
translation: सेना समेत तेरा मान मथकर, अशोक वन को उजाड़कर, नगर को जलाकर और तेरे पुत्र को मारकर जो लौट गए (तू उनका कुछ भी न बिगाड़ सका), क्यों रे दुष्ट! वे हनुमान् जी क्या वानर हैं? ॥
english_translation: You fool! After Hanuman, with his army, churned up your pride, ruined the Ashoka grove, burned the city, and killed your son, do you still ask what kind of monkey he is?
essence: Pride keeps asking questions reality has already answered.
simple_meaning: Ravana is mocked for still doubting Hanuman's power after Hanuman has already devastated Lanka and killed his son.
insight: It exposes how ego keeps arguing even after it has been proven wrong.
modern_relevance: You ignore the warning signs, then act shocked when the damage is already done. Pride can make even obvious consequences feel unreal.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनु रावन परिहरि चतुराई। भजसि न कृपासिंधु रघुराई॥ जौं खल भएसि राम कर द्रोही। ब्रह्म रुद्र सक राखि न तोही ॥
translation: अरे रावण! चतुराई (कपट) छोड़कर सुन। कृपा के समुद्र श्री रघुनाथजी का तू भजन क्यों नहीं करता? अरे दुष्ट! यदि तू श्री रामजी का वैरी हुआ तो तुझे ब्रह्मा और रुद्र भी नहीं बचा सकेंगे।
english_translation: Ravana, give up your cleverness and worship compassionate Raghunath. If you become an enemy of Ram, even Brahma and Rudra cannot save you.
essence: Cleverness cannot save you from opposing Ram.
simple_meaning: Ravana is warned to stop being clever and turn to Ram in devotion. If he chooses enmity instead, no higher power can protect him.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection through control to safety through devotion.
modern_relevance: You keep drafting the perfect reply, trying to win the argument by being sharper than everyone else. This verse says that kind of cleverness can still leave you helpless.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: मूढ़ बृथा जनि मारसि गाला। राम बयर अस होइहि हाला॥ तव सिर निकर कपिन्ह के आगें। परिहहिं धरनि राम सर लागें ॥
translation: हे मूढ़! व्यर्थ गाल न मार (डींग न हाँक)। श्री रामजी से वैर करने पर तेरा ऐसा हाल होगा कि तेरे सिर समूह श्री रामजी के बाण लगते ही वानरों के आगे पृथ्वी पर पड़ेंगे, ॥
english_translation: O fool, stop your empty boasting. If you oppose Ram, this will be your end: your heads will fall before the monkeys when Ram's arrows strike you.
essence: Boasting cannot save you from the result of your own defiance.
simple_meaning: Ravana is warned that his empty boasting will end in disaster if he keeps opposing Ram.
insight: It exposes ego as self-destructive and shifts the mind from bravado to consequence.
modern_relevance: You keep arguing in the group chat like words can protect you. But some battles are already lost the moment pride takes over.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: ते तव सिर कंदुक सम नाना। खेलिहहिं भालु कीस चौगाना॥ जबहिं समर कोपिहि रघुनायक। छुटिहहिं अति कराल बहु सायक ॥
translation: और रीछ-वानर तेरे उन गेंद के समान अनेकों सिरों से चौगान खेलेंगे। जब श्री रघुनाथजी युद्ध में कोप करेंगे और उनके अत्यंत तीक्ष्ण बहुत से बाण छूटेंगे, ॥
english_translation: The bears and monkeys will play with your many heads like balls. When Raghunath grows angry in battle, many terrible arrows will fly.
essence: Arrogance is already losing before the arrows fly.
simple_meaning: Angada warns Ravana that his many heads will be treated like balls by the monkeys and bears, and that Ram's arrows will be deadly in battle.
insight: It turns Ravana's swagger into a warning: arrogance invites humiliation and destruction.
modern_relevance: You keep bluffing in a tense meeting, but everyone can see the numbers on the screen. Confidence without reality collapses the moment the hard facts arrive.
speaker: Angada

verse_text: तब कि चलिहि अस गाल तुम्हारा। अस बिचारि भजु राम उदारा॥ सुनत बचन रावन परजरा। जरत महानल जनु घृत परा ॥
translation: तब क्या तेरा गाल चलेगा? ऐसा विचार कर उदार (कृपालु) श्री रामजी को भज। अंगद के ये वचन सुनकर रावण बहुत अधिक जल उठा। मानो जलती हुई प्रचण्ड अग्नि में घी पड़ गया हो ॥
english_translation: Then what will your boasting achieve? Think this through and worship noble Ram. Hearing Angad's words, Ravana burned even hotter, like ghee poured into a blazing fire.
essence: Boasting collapses before truth; pride answers with fire.
simple_meaning: Angad tells Ravana to stop boasting and turn to Ram instead. Ravana only grows angrier when he hears it.
insight: It shows how ego reacts to truth with heat, not humility.
modern_relevance: You get called out in a meeting and feel your face go hot before you even answer. The sharper the truth, the more your ego may resist it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कुंभकरन अस बंधु मम सुत प्रसिद्ध सक्रारि। मोर पराक्रम नहिं सुनेहि जितेऊँ चराचर झारि ॥
translation: (वह बोला- अरे मूर्ख!) कुंभकर्ण- ऐसा मेरा भाई है, इन्द्र का शत्रु सुप्रसिद्ध मेघनाद मेरा पुत्र है! और मेरा पराक्रम तो तूने सुना ही नहीं कि मैंने संपूर्ण जड़-चेतन जगत् को जीत लिया है! ॥
english_translation: My brother is Kumbhakarna, and my son is the famed enemy of Indra. You have not even heard of my power, by which I have conquered all moving and unmoving beings.
essence: Conquest means nothing when the mind still needs to boast.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts about his family and his supposed conquest of the whole world. He is trying to overwhelm Angad with pride instead of answering his challenge honestly.
insight: It shifts attention from outward bragging to the insecurity underneath it.
modern_relevance: You’re in a meeting and someone challenges your plan. Instead of listening, you start listing your wins, your title, your past victories. The louder the defense, the more fragile it feels.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सठ साखामृग जोरि सहाई। बाँधा सिंधु इहइ प्रभुताई॥ नाघहिं खग अनेक बारीसा। सूर न होहिं ते सुनु सब कीसा ॥
translation: रे दुष्ट! वानरों की सहायता जोड़कर राम ने समुद्र बाँध लिया, बस, यही उसकी प्रभुता है। समुद्र को तो अनेकों पक्षी भी लाँघ जाते हैं। पर इसी से वे सभी शूरवीर नहीं हो जाते। अरे मूर्ख बंदर! सुन- ॥
english_translation: You fool! Ram built a bridge across the ocean with the help of the monkey army — that is his true power. Many birds can cross the sea, but that does not make them heroes.
essence: Pride belittles what it cannot equal.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Hanuman by saying Ram's greatness is not real strength, since birds can cross the ocean too.
insight: It exposes the mind of ego: it explains away achievement instead of facing it.
modern_relevance: Someone online dismisses your months of work with one snide comment: 'Anyone could have done that.' Ravana's voice is the voice that cannot bear another's greatness.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: मम भुज सागर बल जल पूरा। जहँ बूड़े बहु सुर नर सूरा॥ बीस पयोधि अगाध अपारा। को अस बीर जो पाइहि पारा ॥
translation: मेरा एक-एक भुजा रूपी समुद्र बल रूपी जल से पूर्ण है, जिसमें बहुत से शूरवीर देवता और मनुष्य डूब चूके हैं। (बता,) कौन ऐसा शूरवीर है, जो मेरे इन अथाह और अपार बीस समुद्रों का पार पा जाएगा? ॥
english_translation: My arms are like oceans, full of the water of strength. Many gods, humans, and heroes have drowned in them. Who is the warrior who can cross my twenty boundless, unfathomable oceans?
essence: Pride turns strength into a boast that cannot save you.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that his strength is immense and that many powerful beings have already fallen before him. He asks who could possibly survive or cross his twenty boundless oceans of power.
insight: It exposes how ego inflates strength into a shield and mistakes intimidation for real power.
modern_relevance: Someone in a heated argument starts listing every win, every influence, every person who has backed down before them. The volume is high because the fear underneath is even higher.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: दिगपालन्ह मैं नीर भरावा। भूप सुजस खल मोहि सुनावा॥ जौं पै समर सुभट तव नाथा। पुनि पुनि कहसि जासु गुन गाथा ॥
translation: अरे दुष्ट! मैंने दिक्पालों तक से जल भरवाया और तू एक राजा का मुझे सुयश सुनाता है! यदि तेरा मालिक, जिसकी गुणगाथा तू बार-बार कह रहा है, संग्राम में लड़ने वाला योद्धा है- ॥
english_translation: I made the guardians of the directions pour water for me, and you boast of a king's fame to me! If your master, whose praises you keep repeating, is a warrior in battle—
essence: Ego hears praise of another as an insult to itself.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he has power over cosmic forces and mocks the messenger for praising a king's fame. He challenges the claim by asking whether that king is really a fighter in battle.
insight: It shows how arrogance turns conversation into a contest of status instead of a search for truth.
modern_relevance: Someone on a group chat keeps mocking the person you admire, waving around their own status like proof. The verse captures that reflex to belittle what threatens your ego.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: तौ बसीठ पठवत केहि काजा। रिपु सन प्रीति करत नहिं लाजा॥ हरगिरि मथन निरखु मम बाहू। पुनि सठ कपि निज प्रभुहि सराहू ॥
translation: तो (फिर) वह दूत किसलिए भेजता है? शत्रु से प्रीति (सन्धि) करते उसे लाज नहीं आती? (पहले) कैलास का मथन करने वाली मेरी भुजाओं को देख। फिर अरे मूर्ख वानर! अपने मालिक की सराहना करना ॥
english_translation: Then why send an envoy? Does he feel no shame making peace with an enemy? Look at my arms that churned Mount Kailash. Then, fool of a monkey, praise your own lord.
essence: Ego cannot meet a challenge without boasting.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Hanuman, asking why anyone would send an envoy to an enemy and boasting of his own strength before telling Hanuman to praise his own lord.
insight: It shows how wounded pride attacks the messenger instead of facing the message.
modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a meeting and turns every answer into a chance to brag about themselves. The real issue disappears under ego.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सूर कवन रावन सरिस स्वकर काटि जेहिं सीस। हुने अनल अति हरष बहु बार साखि गौरीस ॥
translation: रावण के समान शूरवीर कौन है? जिसने अपने हाथों से सिर काट-काटकर अत्यंत हर्ष के साथ बहुत बार उन्हें अग्नि में होम दिया! स्वयं गौरीपति शिवजी इस बात के साक्षी हैं ॥
english_translation: Who is as brave as Ravana, who cut off his own heads with his own hands and offered them into the fire again and again in great joy? Lord Shiva himself is witness to this.
essence: Ego can glorify even its own destruction.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that no one is as brave as he is, because he once cut off his own heads and offered them into fire with delight. He uses Shiva as a witness to his arrogance.
insight: It teaches you to notice when bravado is just ego defending itself.
modern_relevance: You keep replaying the hardest thing you survived like it proves you’re untouchable. Sometimes the mind turns pain into a badge and calls it power.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: जरत बिलोकेउँ जबहि कपाला। बिधि के लिखे अंक निज भाला॥ नर कें कर आपन बध बाँची। हसेउँ जानि बिधि गिरा असाँची ॥
translation: मस्तकों के जलते समय जब मैंने अपने ललाटों पर लिखे हुए विधाता के अक्षर देखे, तब मनुष्य के हाथ से अपनी मृत्यु होना बाँचकर, विधाता की वाणी (लेख को) असत्य जानकर मैं हँसा ॥
english_translation: When I saw the skulls burning, and the marks of fate written on my forehead, I laughed, knowing that death by a human hand had been escaped and that the words of fate were false.
essence: Ego laughs at warning signs until reality answers.
simple_meaning: Ravana laughs at the idea that fate controls him. He believes he has escaped death at human hands and treats destiny itself as false.
insight: It exposes the blindness of ego: when you trust your own invincibility, you stop seeing the truth in front of you.
modern_relevance: You ignore the warning signs because you think you are still untouchable. That confident laugh can be the last thing standing before collapse.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सोउ मन समुझि त्रास नहिं मोरें। लिखा बिरंचि जरठ मति भोरें॥ आन बीर बल सठ मम आगें। पुनि पुनि कहसि लाज पति त्यागें ॥
translation: उस बात को समझकर (स्मरण करके) भी मेरे मन में डर नहीं है। (क्योंकि मैं समझता हूँ कि) बूढ़े ब्रह्मा ने बुद्धि भ्रम से ऐसा लिख दिया है। अरे मूर्ख! तू लज्जा और मर्यादा छोड़कर मेरे आगे बार-बार दूसरे वीर का बल कहता है! ॥
english_translation: Knowing that, I still feel no fear. Old Brahma must have written this in a clouded mind. Fool, you keep speaking before me of another warrior's strength, abandoning shame and restraint again and again!
essence: Pride hears warning as an insult and learns nothing.
simple_meaning: Ravana says he feels no fear, dismisses fate as a confused mistake, and insults the speaker for repeatedly praising another warrior instead of showing proper restraint.
insight: It shows how wounded pride blocks self-correction and turns wise counsel into provocation.
modern_relevance: Someone keeps warning you that your plan is collapsing, but you brush it off and double down. Ravana is that moment when ego turns every correction into an insult.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: कह अंगद सलज्ज जग माहीं। रावन तोहि समान कोउ नाहीं॥ लाजवंत तव सहज सुभाऊ। निज मुख निज गुन कहसि न काऊ ॥
translation: अंगद ने कहा- अरे रावण! तेरे समान लज्जावान् जगत् में कोई नहीं है। लज्जाशीलता तो तेरा सहज स्वभाव ही है। तू अपने मुँह से अपने गुण कभी नहीं कहता ॥
english_translation: Angada said, 'Ravana, there is no one in the world like you in modesty. Shyness is your natural nature. You never speak of your own virtues yourself.'
essence: Mock praise can reveal pride more sharply than accusation.
simple_meaning: Angad sarcastically praises Ravana, mocking his arrogance by calling him modest and saying he never boasts about himself.
insight: It shows how irony can puncture ego without a direct lecture.
modern_relevance: In a tense meeting, someone says, “Of course you never need credit,” and the room goes quiet. Everyone hears the sarcasm. Angad is doing that on a battlefield.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: सिर अरु सैल कथा चित रही। ताते बार बीस तैं कहीं॥ सो भुजबल राखेहु उर घाली। जीतेहु सहसबाहु बलि बाली ॥
translation: सिर काटने और कैलास उठाने की कथा चित्त में चढ़ी हुई थी, इससे तूने उसे बीसों बार कहा। भुजाओं के उस बल को तूने हृदय में ही टाल (छिपा) रखा है, जिससे तूने सहस्रबाहु, बलि और बालि को जीता था ॥
english_translation: The story of cutting off heads and lifting Mount Kailash has stayed in your mind, so you have said it twenty times. You kept that arm-strength hidden in your heart, the strength that defeated Sahasrabahu, Bali, and Vali.
essence: Boasts about old feats mean little without present courage.
simple_meaning: Angad mocks Ravana for repeating old boasts about cutting off heads and lifting mountains. He says Ravana has hidden the real strength of his arms, the strength that once defeated powerful kings and warriors.
insight: It exposes how bravado can hide fear and how past victories do not prove present power.
modern_relevance: Someone keeps bringing up what they did years ago, but the room can feel the gap between memory and current strength. Angad’s words cut through that performance.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: सुनु मतिमंद देहि अब पूरा। काटें सीस कि होइअ सूरा॥ इंद्रजालि कहुँ कहिअ न बीरा। काटइ निज कर सकल सरीरा ॥
translation: अरे मंद बुद्धि! सुन, अब बस कर। सिर काटने से भी क्या कोई शूरवीर हो जाता है? इंद्रजाल रचने वाले को वीर नहीं कहा जाता, यद्यपि वह अपने ही हाथों अपना सारा शरीर काट डालता है! ॥
english_translation: Listen, fool, enough now. Does cutting off a head make someone brave? A magician is not called a hero, even if he cuts up his own body with his own hands.
essence: Courage is not proved by spectacle or self-harm.
simple_meaning: Bravery is not proved by dramatic self-harm or showy tricks. Real courage is something deeper than a violent display.
insight: It separates real courage from theatrical display and self-inflicted damage.
modern_relevance: You post a dramatic apology, a fierce rant, or a self-destructive stunt and hope it proves something. It does not. Performance is not courage.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: जरहिं पतंग मोह बस भार बहहिं खर बृंद। ते नहिं सूर कहावहिं समुझि देखु मतिमंद ॥
translation: अरे मंद बुद्धि! समझकर देख। पतंगे मोहवश आग में जल मरते हैं, गदहों के झुंड बोझ लादकर चलते हैं, पर इस कारण वे शूरवीर नहीं कहलाते ॥
english_translation: Fool, look and understand: moths burn in fire under the spell of delusion, and donkeys carry heavy loads in herds, but they are not called heroes for that.
essence: Extreme behavior is not the same as true courage.
simple_meaning: Doing something extreme does not make you brave. A moth burns itself and a donkey carries weight, but neither becomes heroic because of that.
insight: It separates real courage from compulsive or deluded action, so you stop glorifying self-destructive effort.
modern_relevance: You stayed up all night proving a point, then called it commitment. Or you kept carrying everyone else's load and called it strength. The verse asks you to look harder.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: अब जनि बतबढ़ाव खल करही। सुनु मम बचन मान परिहरही॥ दसमुख मैं न बसीठीं आयउँ। अस बिचारि रघुबीर पठायउँ ॥
translation: अरे दुष्ट! अब बतबढ़ाव मत कर, मेरा वचन सुन और अभिमान त्याग दे! हे दशमुख! मैं दूत की तरह (सन्धि करने) नहीं आया हूँ। श्री रघुवीर ने ऐसा विचार कर मुझे भेजा है- ॥
english_translation: “Do not boast now, wicked one. Hear my words and let go of pride. O ten-faced one, I did not come here as a messenger for a truce. Considering this, Raghuvir sent me.”
essence: Purpose speaks plainly and does not bow to arrogance.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Ravana to stop boasting, listen carefully, and drop his pride. He says he did not come as a peace messenger; Ram sent him for a different purpose.
insight: It teaches you to hold your role firmly and speak without apologising for your purpose.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting where someone is trying to overpower the room with bluster. You do not need to shrink, flatter, or perform. You can say exactly why you are there.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: बार बार अस कहइ कृपाला। नहिं गजारि जसु बंधे सृकाला॥ मन महुँ समुझि बचन प्रभु केरे। सहेउँ कठोर बचन सठ तेरे ॥
translation: कृपालु श्री रामजी बार-बार ऐसा कहते हैं कि स्यार के मारने से सिंह को यश नहीं मिलता। अरे मूर्ख! प्रभु के (उन) वचनों को मन में समझकर (याद करके) ही मैंने तेरे कठोर वचन सहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Again and again the compassionate Lord says this: a jackal does not gain fame by killing a lion. Remembering the Lord's words in my heart, I have endured your harsh speech, fool.
essence: Remembering Ram makes insults bearable.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says he endured Ravana's insults because he remembered Ram's words, and he reminds Ravana that a weak creature does not win glory by attacking the strong.
insight: It teaches you to hold your center under provocation by recalling a higher instruction before reacting.
modern_relevance: Someone snaps at you in a meeting and expects a sharp reply. You remember who you are, let the insult pass, and answer from steadiness instead of ego.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: नाहिं त करि मुख भंजन तोरा। लैं जातेउँ सीतहि बरजोरा॥ जानेउँ तव बल अधम सुरारी। सूनें हरि आनिहि परनारी ॥
translation: नहीं तो तेरे मुँह तोड़कर मैं सीताजी को जबरदस्ती ले जाता। अरे अधम! देवताओं के शत्रु! तेरा बल तो मैंने तभी जान लिया, जब तू सूने में पराई स्त्री को हर (चुरा) लाया ॥
english_translation: Otherwise, I would have smashed your face and carried Sita away by force. I knew your strength, vile enemy of the devas, when you stole another man's wife in secret.
essence: Real strength can choose not to strike.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says he could have used force against Ravana, but chose not to. He also says Ravana's strength was already clear from the way he secretly abducted Sita.
insight: It shifts the mind from reactive aggression to disciplined restraint under pressure.
modern_relevance: Someone keeps pushing you in a tense conversation, trying to make you lose your temper. You do not need to prove strength by exploding; sometimes the stronger move is refusing the bait.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: तै निसिचर पति गर्ब बहूता। मैं रघुपति सेवक कर दूता॥ जौं न राम अपमानहिं डरऊँ। तोहि देखत अस कौतुक करउँ ॥
translation: तू राक्षसों का राजा और बड़ा अभिमानी है, परन्तु मैं तो श्री रघुनाथजी के सेवक (सुग्रीव) का दूत (सेवक का भी सेवक) हूँ। यदि मैं श्री रामजी के अपमान से न डरूँ तो तेरे देखते-देखते ऐसा तमाशा करूँ कि- ॥
english_translation: You are the king of the demons and full of pride, but I am only the servant-messenger of Raghunath's servant. If I do not fear disrespect to Ram, I will do such a feat before you that...
essence: Loyalty to Ram makes fear irrelevant.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Ravana that he is only Ram's servant-messenger, and that his real concern is protecting Ram's honour, not his own safety.
insight: It shifts courage from self-protection to protecting what you stand for.
modern_relevance: You are cornered in a tense meeting and someone tries to intimidate you. The calmest reply comes when you know exactly who you serve and what you will not let be disrespected.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: तोहि पटकि महि सेन हति चौपट करि तव गाउँ। तव जुबतिन्ह समेत सठ जनकसुतहि लै जाउँ ॥
translation: तुझे जमीन पर पटककर, तेरी सेना का संहार कर और तेरे गाँव को चौपट (नष्ट-भ्रष्ट) करके, अरे मूर्ख! तेरी युवती स्त्रियों सहित जानकीजी को ले जाऊँ ॥
english_translation: I would throw you down, wipe out your army, ruin your city, and carry off Janaki along with your women, fool.
essence: Boastful force can threaten ruin, but it is still only boasting.
simple_meaning: He boasts that he could throw Ravana down, destroy his army and city, and carry Sita away with Ravana's women.
insight: It shows how boastful anger tries to dominate with threats instead of restraint.
modern_relevance: Someone in a heated argument starts listing everything they could do if they really lost control. The words sound powerful, but they only reveal how far the clash has gone.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: जौं अस करौं तदपि न बड़ाई। मुएहि बधें नहिं कछु मनुसाई॥ कौल कामबस कृपिन बिमूढ़ा। अति दरिद्र अजसी अति बूढ़ा ॥
translation: यदि ऐसा करूँ, तो भी इसमें कोई बड़ाई नहीं है। मरे हुए को मारने में कुछ भी पुरुषत्व (बहादुरी) नहीं है। वाममार्गी, कामी, कंजूस, अत्यंत मूढ़, अति दरिद्र, बदनाम, बहुत बूढ़ा, ॥
english_translation: If I do this, there is still no greatness in it. There is no manliness in killing one who is already dead. A heretic, ruled by desire, miserly, deluded, extremely poor, disgraced, and very old...
essence: Cruelty toward the helpless is not strength at all.
simple_meaning: Ravana says that attacking someone who is already helpless or defeated is not a brave act. He also piles on insults to belittle the enemy.
insight: It shifts attention from domination to the character revealed by how you treat the vulnerable.
modern_relevance: You win the argument in the group chat, then keep mocking the person after they stop replying. The extra blow doesn't make you stronger; it only shows how little restraint you have.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सदा रोगबस संतत क्रोधी। बिष्नु बिमुख श्रुति संत बिरोधी॥ तनु पोषक निंदक अघ खानी जीवत सव सम चौदह प्रानी ॥
translation: नित्य का रोगी, निरंतर क्रोधयुक्त रहने वाला, भगवान् विष्णु से विमुख, वेद और संतों का विरोधी, अपना ही शरीर पोषण करने वाला, पराई निंदा करने वाला और पाप की खान (महान् पापी)- ये चौदह प्राणी जीते ही मुरदे के समान हैं ॥
english_translation: Those who are always sick, always angry, turned away from Vishnu, hostile to the Vedas and saints, feeding only their own bodies, slandering others, and full of sin — these fourteen kinds of beings are dead while still alive.
essence: A body can keep moving long after the inner life has collapsed.
simple_meaning: A person trapped in illness, anger, arrogance, and criticism is counted as spiritually dead even while breathing.
insight: It shifts attention from outward survival to inner condition, asking whether your habits are making you more awake or more deadened.
modern_relevance: You know that coworker who is always irritated, always mocking, always feeding only their own comfort? Being busy and breathing is not the same as being alive in any meaningful way.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: अस बिचारि खल बधउँ न तोही। अब जनि रिस उपजावसि मोही॥ सुनि सकोप कह निसिचर नाथा। अधर दसन दसि मीजत हाथा ॥
translation: अरे दुष्ट! ऐसा विचार कर मैं तुझे नहीं मारता। अब तू मुझमें क्रोध न पैदा कर (मुझे गुस्सा न दिला)। अंगद के वचन सुनकर राक्षस राज रावण दाँतों से होठ काटकर, क्रोधित होकर हाथ मलता हुआ बोला- ॥
english_translation: Thinking this, I do not kill you. Do not stir anger in me now. Hearing this, the lord of demons spoke in rage, biting his lip with his teeth and rubbing his hands.
essence: Pride pretends restraint, but anger still shows through.
simple_meaning: Ravana says he is sparing Angad for now and warns him not to provoke his anger. Angad's words have made Ravana furious.
insight: It exposes how ego disguises fury as self-control while the body reveals the real state.
modern_relevance: You say, "I'm fine," but your jaw is clenched and your hands won't stay still. The anger is already speaking before you do.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: रे कपि अधम मरन अब चहसी। छोटे बदन बात बड़ि कहसी॥ कटु जल्पसि जड़ कपि बल जाकें। बल प्रताप बुधि तेज न ताकें ॥
translation: अरे नीच बंदर! अब तू मरना ही चाहता है! इसी से छोटे मुँह बड़ी बात कहता है। अरे मूर्ख बंदर! तू जिसके बल पर कड़ुए वचन बक रहा है, उसमें बल, प्रताप, बुद्धि अथवा तेज कुछ भी नहीं है ॥
english_translation: You lowly monkey! Do you now want to die? Small mouth, yet such big talk. Foolish monkey, the power you rely on has no strength, glory, wisdom, or brilliance.
essence: Arrogance mocks what it cannot defeat.
simple_meaning: Ravana insults Hanuman, mocking his size and claiming that the power Hanuman depends on has no real strength or wisdom.
insight: It reveals how arrogance attacks the messenger when it cannot face the message.
modern_relevance: Someone dismisses your warning in a meeting by sneering at your experience instead of answering the point. The insult is loud, but it only reveals their fear of being exposed.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: अगुन अमान जानि तेहि दीन्ह पिता बनबास। सो दुख अरु जुबती बिरह पुनि निसि दिन मम त्रास ॥
translation: उसे गुणहीन और मानहीन समझकर ही तो पिता ने वनवास दे दिया। उसे एक तो वह (उसका) दुःख, उस पर युवती स्त्री का विरह और फिर रात-दिन मेरा डर बना रहता है ॥
english_translation: He was sent to the forest because his father saw him as without qualities and without honor. On top of that came his sorrow, his separation from his young wife, and my fear day and night.
essence: Ravana defends himself by turning Ram's suffering into a weakness.
simple_meaning: Ravana reminds Angad that Ram was sent into exile, suffered separation from Sita, and still remains a threat that keeps Ravana afraid.
insight: It shows how ego clings to comparison and fear when it cannot answer directly.
modern_relevance: A person cornered in an argument reaches for old facts to protect their pride. The tone is less truth-seeking than self-defense.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: जिन्ह के बल कर गर्ब तोहि अइसे मनुज अनेक। खाहिं निसाचर दिवस निसि मूढ़ समुझु तजि टेक ॥
translation: जिनके बल का तुझे गर्व है, ऐसे अनेकों मनुष्यों को तो राक्षस रात-दिन खाया करते हैं। अरे मूढ़! जिद्द छोड़कर समझ (विचार कर) ॥
english_translation: The beings whose strength you boast of are eaten day and night by many others. Fool, let go of stubbornness and understand.
essence: Pride collapses when it meets facts.
simple_meaning: Boasting about power is foolish when that same power is weak against real danger. Clinging to pride only blocks clear thinking.
insight: It shifts you from defending ego to checking reality before you speak.
modern_relevance: You defend a shaky plan in a meeting because you hate admitting it's weak. The louder you sound, the less you want to see what is actually true.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: जब तेहिं कीन्हि राम कै निंदा। क्रोधवंत अति भयउ कपिंदा॥ हरि हर निंदा सुनइ जो काना। होइ पाप गोघात समाना ॥
translation: जब उसने श्री रामजी की निंदा की, तब तो कपिश्रेष्ठ अंगद अत्यंत क्रोधित हुए, क्योंकि (शास्त्र ऐसा कहते हैं कि) जो अपने कानों से भगवान् विष्णु और शिव की निंदा सुनता है, उसे गो वध के समान पाप होता है ॥
english_translation: When he spoke ill of Ram, Angada became fiercely angry. Listening to slander of Hari and Hara is said to be a sin equal to killing a cow.
essence: Disrespect toward the divine is never just talk.
simple_meaning: Angada is enraged when Ravana insults Ram. The verse adds that hearing slander of Hari and Shiva is considered a grave offense.
insight: It shifts attention from clever speech to the moral weight of what you allow into your hearing.
modern_relevance: You hear someone mock what you deeply respect, and your body tightens before you can answer. The verse catches that instant when reverence turns into fierce protection.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कटकटान कपिकुंजर भारी। दुहु भुजदंड तमकि महि मारी॥ डोलत धरनि सभासद खसे। चले भाजि भय मारुत ग्रसे ॥
translation: वानर श्रेष्ठ अंगद बहुत जोर से कटकटाए (शब्द किया) और उन्होंने तमककर (जोर से) अपने दोनों भुजदण्डों को पृथ्वी पर दे मारा। पृथ्वी हिलने लगी, (जिससे बैठे हुए) सभासद् गिर पड़े और भय रूपी पवन (भूत) से ग्रस्त होकर भाग चले ॥
english_translation: The mighty monkey-hero Angada clattered loudly, and with a fierce strike he slammed both arms to the ground. The earth shook, the assembled courtiers fell, and, seized by fear, they fled like beings possessed by panic.
essence: Fear collapses when courage enters the room.
simple_meaning: Angada strikes the ground so hard that the earth shakes, the court collapses, and everyone runs away in fear.
insight: It shows how fearless presence can overturn intimidation without a long speech.
modern_relevance: A tense room goes quiet when someone stops apologizing for taking up space. Before the meeting even begins, everyone feels the shift in power.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गिरत सँभारि उठा दसकंधर। भूतल परे मुकुट अति सुंदर॥ कछु तेहिं लै निज सिरन्हि सँवारे। कछु अंगद प्रभु पास पबारे ॥
translation: रावण गिरते-गिरते सँभलकर उठा। उसके अत्यंत सुंदर मुकुट पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े। कुछ तो उसने उठाकर अपने सिरों पर सुधाकर रख लिए और कुछ अंगद ने उठाकर प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी के पास फेंक दिए ॥
english_translation: Ravana staggered, caught himself, and stood up. His very beautiful crown fell to the ground. He picked up some pieces and fixed them back on his own head, and Angad tossed some of them to Lord Ram.
essence: Pride falls hard, then rushes to cover its own wound.
simple_meaning: Ravana regains his footing after falling, and his crown scatters on the ground. Some pieces go back on his head, and some are flung toward Ram.
insight: It shows how ego tries to repair its image even after being exposed.
modern_relevance: You take a public hit, then immediately try to look composed again. Everyone saw the stumble; the real question is what your pride does next.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आवत मुकुट देखि कपि भागे। दिनहीं लूक परन बिधि लागे॥ की रावन करि कोप चलाए। कुलिस चारि आवत अति धाए ॥
translation: मुकुटों को आते देखकर वानर भागे। (सोचने लगे) विधाता! क्या दिन में ही उल्कापात होने लगा (तारे टूटकर गिरने लगे)? अथवा क्या रावण ने क्रोध करके चार वज्र चलाए हैं, जो बड़े धाए के साथ (वेग से) आ रहे हैं? ॥
english_translation: Seeing the crowns coming toward them, the monkeys ran. They thought, 'Has a meteor shower begun in daylight? Or has Ravana, in anger, hurled four thunderbolts rushing toward us?'
essence: Fear makes even harmless things look like disaster.
simple_meaning: The monkeys see the crowns flying toward them and panic, mistaking them for falling meteors or thunderbolts.
insight: It shows how quickly perception can be distorted by fear, before facts are even checked.
modern_relevance: You see a few urgent messages pop up on your phone and your stomach drops. For a moment, your mind turns them into catastrophe before you even know what they are.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह प्रभु हँसि जनि हृदयँ डेराहू। लूक न असनि केतु नहिं राहू॥ ए किरीट दसकंधर केरे। आवत बालितनय के प्रेरे ॥
translation: प्रभु ने (उनसे) हँसकर कहा- मन में डरो नहीं। ये न उल्का हैं, न वज्र हैं और न केतु या राहु ही हैं। अरे भाई! ये तो रावण के मुकुट हैं, जो बालिपुत्र अंगद के फेंके हुए आ रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The Lord smiled and said, “Do not be afraid in your heart. These are not meteors, not thunderbolts, not Ketu or Rahu. They are Ravana’s crowns, being hurled by Angada, the son of Vali.”
essence: Clear seeing dissolves fear faster than force.
simple_meaning: Ram reassures the frightened monkeys that the flying objects are only Ravana’s crowns, thrown by Angada, not some terrible omen.
insight: It teaches you to replace panic with clear naming of reality.
modern_relevance: A sudden crash in the next room makes everyone freeze. Before panic invents a disaster, someone calm looks, names the facts, and the whole room breathes again.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तरकि पवनसुत कर गहे आनि धरे प्रभु पास। कौतुक देखहिं भालु कपि दिनकर सरिस प्रकास ॥
translation: पवन पुत्र श्री हनुमान् जी ने उछलकर उनको हाथ से पकड़ लिया और लाकर प्रभु के पास रख दिया। रीछ और वानर तमाशा देखने लगे। उनका प्रकाश सूर्य के समान था ॥
english_translation: Hanuman quickly seized them and brought them to the Lord. The bears and monkeys watched in amazement; they shone like the sun.
essence: What looked threatening is revealed as dazzling and harmless.
simple_meaning: Hanuman quickly brings the crowns to Ram, and the bears and monkeys stare in wonder at their sun-like brilliance.
insight: It shifts attention from suspense to revelation: the object of fear becomes an object of wonder.
modern_relevance: You finally finish the thing everyone was doubting, and for a second the room goes quiet. The result speaks before you do.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उहाँ सकोपि दसानन सब सन कहत रिसाइ। धरहु कपिहि धरि मारहु सुनि अंगद मुसुकाइ ॥
translation: वहाँ (सभा में) क्रोधयुक्त रावण सबसे क्रोधित होकर कहने लगा कि- बंदर को पकड़ लो और पकड़कर मार डालो। अंगद यह सुनकर मुस्कुराने लगे ॥
english_translation: There, Ravana grew furious and told everyone in anger, "Seize the monkey, hold him down, and kill him." Angada only smiled when he heard it.
essence: Rage exposes weakness; calm exposes strength.
simple_meaning: Ravana orders his men to seize and kill Hanuman, but Angada remains calm and smiles.
insight: It shows how ego lashes out when challenged, while inner steadiness does not need to shout back.
modern_relevance: A manager snaps in front of the whole team and demands someone be removed. The loudest voice in the room is often the one most threatened.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: एहि बधि बेगि सुभट सब धावहु। खाहु भालु कपि जहँ जहँ पावहु॥ मर्कटहीन करहु महि जाई। जिअत धरहु तापस द्वौ भाई ॥
translation: (रावण फिर बोला-) इसे मारकर सब योद्धा तुरंत दौड़ो और जहाँ कहीं रीछ-वानरों को पाओ, वहीं खा डालो। पृथ्वी को बंदरों से रहित कर दो और जाकर दोनों तपस्वी भाइयों (राम-लक्ष्मण) को जीते जी पकड़ लो ॥
english_translation: Then Ravana said, "Go at once, all warriors. Eat up every bear and monkey wherever you find them. Make the earth free of monkeys, and go seize the two ascetics alive."
essence: Anger makes power self-destructive.
simple_meaning: Ravana orders his warriors to kill the monkeys and bears, clear them from the earth, and capture Ram and Lakshman alive.
insight: It shows how unchecked fury turns strategy into blind violence.
modern_relevance: A person cornered in a meeting starts issuing harsh orders and turning every disagreement into a purge. Anger makes the mind think in enemies, not solutions.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: पुनि सकोप बोलेउ जुबराजा। गाल बजावत तोहि न लाजा॥ मरु गर काटि निलज कुलघाती। बल बिलोकि बिहरति नहिं छाती ॥
translation: (रावण के ये कोपभरे वचन सुनकर) तब युवराज अंगद क्रोधित होकर बोले- तुझे गाल बजाते लाज नहीं आती! अरे निर्लज्ज! अरे कुलनाशक! गला काटकर (आत्महत्या करके) मर जा! मेरा बल देखकर भी क्या तेरी छाती नहीं फटती! ॥
english_translation: Then Angada, the young prince, spoke in anger: “Do you have no shame, still boasting like this? Die, you shameless destroyer of your line! Even after seeing my strength, does your chest not split open?”
essence: Angada answers arrogance with fearless contempt.
simple_meaning: Angada angrily rebukes Ravana for his shameless boasting and tells him he should die for disgracing his own line.
insight: It shows how fearless speech can break the spell of bluster and force false pride into the open.
modern_relevance: Someone keeps talking big in a meeting, hoping volume will hide weakness. A calm, fearless reply can puncture the performance without needing to shout louder.
speaker: Angada

verse_text: रे त्रिय चोर कुमारग गामी। खल मल रासि मंदमति कामी॥ सन्यपात जल्पसि दुर्बादा। भएसि कालबस खल मनुजादा ॥
translation: अरे स्त्री के चोर! अरे कुमार्ग पर चलने वाले! अरे दुष्ट, पाप की राशि, मन्द बुद्धि और कामी! तू सन्निपात में क्या दुर्वचन बक रहा है? अरे दुष्ट राक्षस! तू काल के वश हो गया है! ॥
english_translation: O thief of another man's wife, walker of the wrong path, heap of evil, dull-minded and lustful one! Why do you babble these foul words in a fit of madness? O wicked one, you are under time's power.
essence: Raging abuse can be the sign of fear already losing.
simple_meaning: Ravana is being insulted as wicked, lustful, and deluded. The speaker says his filthy speech shows he is already under death's power.
insight: It turns aggression into evidence of inner defeat, not power.
modern_relevance: Someone sends a furious voice note full of insults, but the anger only exposes how cornered they feel. The louder they get, the less control they have.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: याको फलु पावहिगो आगें। बानर भालु चपेटन्हि लागें॥ रामु मनुज बोलत असि बानी। गिरहिं न तव रसना अभिमानी ॥
translation: इसका फल तू आगे वानर और भालुओं के चपेटे लगने पर पावेगा। राम मनुष्य हैं, ऐसा वचन बोलते ही, अरे अभिमानी! तेरी जीभें नहीं गिर पड़तीं? ॥
english_translation: You will pay for this later, when monkeys and bears strike you down. You call Ram a mere human—how do your arrogant tongues not fall to the ground?
essence: Arrogant speech plants the seed of its own defeat.
simple_meaning: Angada warns Ravana that his insult will bring a painful result. He says that calling Ram merely human is such arrogance that Ravana's own tongue should fall away.
insight: It shifts the mind from careless speech to awareness that contempt has consequences.
modern_relevance: You make a cruel joke in a room full of people, and the silence after it lands heavier than the laugh. Some words return to you as consequence, not applause.
speaker: Angada

verse_text: गिरिहहिं रसना संसय नाहीं। सिरन्हि समेत समर महि माहीं ॥
translation: इसमें संदेह नहीं है कि तेरी जीभें (अकेले नहीं वरन) सिरों के साथ रणभूमि में गिरेंगी ॥
english_translation: There is no doubt: your tongues will fall on the battlefield together with your heads.
essence: Pride answers reason with threats.
simple_meaning: Ravana threatens that the offending tongues will be cut down along with the heads in battle.
insight: It shows how ego answers challenge with domination instead of reflection.
modern_relevance: A heated argument on a group chat can suddenly turn cruel, with threats and insults replacing any real listening. Pride makes the mouth promise violence before the mind has cooled.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सो नर क्यों दसकंध बालि बध्यो जेहिं एक सर। बीसहुँ लोचन अंध धिग तव जन्म कुजाति जड़ ॥
translation: रे दशकन्ध! जिसने एक ही बाण से बालि को मार डाला, वह मनुष्य कैसे है? अरे कुजाति, अरे जड़! बीस आँखें होने पर भी तू अंधा है। तेरे जन्म को धिक्कार है ॥
english_translation: O ten-headed one, how can he be called a man who killed Bali with a single arrow? You have twenty eyes and still you are blind. Shame on your birth, you fool.
essence: Pride can make even obvious truth invisible.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Ram, refusing to see his divinity. He points to Bali's death and uses it as proof that Ram is no ordinary man, while his own pride makes him blind.
insight: It shifts attention from external proof to the way ego distorts perception.
modern_relevance: You read the same message three times, but your anger decides what it means. The facts are there; your pride is what refuses them.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: तव सोनित कीं प्यास तृषित राम सायक निकर। तजउँ तोहि तेहि त्रास कटु जल्पक निसिचर अधम ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी के बाण समूह तेरे रक्त की प्यास से प्यासे हैं। (वे प्यासे ही रह जाएँगे) इस डर से, अरे कड़वी बकवाद करने वाले नीच राक्षस! मैं तुझे छोड़ता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Ram's arrows are thirsty for your blood. I would spare you only because I fear that, you foul-tongued low creature.
essence: Power becomes clean when it waits for the right command.
simple_meaning: The speaker says Ram's arrows are eager to drink the enemy's blood, but he will spare the enemy only because of Ram's command.
insight: It shifts force from personal vengeance to obedience to dharma.
modern_relevance: You are furious in a meeting and have the perfect comeback ready. Then you remember you do not need to win the room to prove your strength.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: मैं तव दसन तोरिबे लायक। आयसु मोहि न दीन्ह रघुनायक॥ असि रिस होति दसउ मुख तोरौं। लंका गहि समुद्र महँ बोरौं ॥
translation: मैं तेरे दाँत तोड़ने में समर्थ हूँ। पर क्या करूँ? श्री रघुनाथजी ने मुझे आज्ञा नहीं दी। ऐसा क्रोध आता है कि तेरे दसों मुँह तोड़ डालूँ और (तेरी) लंका को पकड़कर समुद्र में डुबो दूँ ॥
english_translation: I am capable of breaking your teeth. But what can I do? Raghunath has not given me orders. Such anger rises that I would smash all ten of your mouths and sink Lanka into the sea.
essence: Power becomes pure when it waits for the right command.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says he has the power to destroy Lanka, but he will not act until Ram gives the order.
insight: It teaches you to hold capability inside obedience, so action stays clean and purposeful.
modern_relevance: You know the email could end the argument in one sharp sentence. You have the power to win — but you pause because winning is not the same as serving what matters.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: गूलरि फल समान तव लंका। बसहु मध्य तुम्ह जंतु असंका॥ मैं बानर फल खात न बारा। आयसु दीन्ह न राम उदारा ॥
translation: तेरी लंका गूलर के फल के समान है। तुम सब कीड़े उसके भीतर (अज्ञानवश) निडर होकर बस रहे हो। मैं बंदर हूँ, मुझे इस फल को खाते क्या देर थी? पर उदार (कृपालु) श्री रामचंद्रजी ने वैसी आज्ञा नहीं दी ॥
english_translation: Your Lanka is like a fig fruit. All you creatures live inside it, fearless and unaware. I am a monkey; I could have eaten this fruit long ago, but noble Ram did not give me that order.
essence: True power can strike, but chooses restraint until duty speaks.
simple_meaning: Angad mocks Lanka as an easy fruit to crack open, but says he is restrained only because Ram has not ordered him to act.
insight: It shifts strength from raw impulse to disciplined obedience.
modern_relevance: You know the moment you could fire off the message, make the sharp remark, or take the win by force. Real control is holding back until your action is truly right.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: जुगुति सुनत रावन मुसुकाई। मूढ़ सिखिहि कहँ बहुत झुठाई॥ बालि न कबहुँ गाल अस मारा। मिलि तपसिन्ह तैं भएसि लबारा ॥
translation: अंगद की युक्ति सुनकर रावण मुस्कुराया (और बोला-) अरे मूर्ख! बहुत झूठ बोलना तूने कहाँ से सीखा? बालि ने तो कभी ऐसा गाल नहीं मारा। जान पड़ता है तू तपस्वियों से मिलकर लबार हो गया है ॥
english_translation: Ravana smiled at Angad's strategy and said, "Fool, where did you learn so much lying? Bali never spoke like this. You seem to have become a liar by mixing with ascetics."
essence: Pride laughs at warning because it cannot bear correction.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Angad's words and calls him a liar, saying Bali never spoke like that and ascetics must have taught him falsehood.
insight: It shows how ego protects itself by mocking the messenger instead of answering the message.
modern_relevance: You point out a hard truth in a meeting, and someone smiles it away as nonsense. The problem is not your words — it's their refusal to face them.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: साँचेहुँ मैं लबार भुज बीहा। जौं न उपारिउँ तव दस जीहा॥ समुझि राम प्रताप कपि कोपा। सभा माझ पन करि पद रोपा ॥
translation: (अंगद ने कहा-) अरे बीस भुजा वाले! यदि तेरी दसों जीभें मैंने नहीं उखाड़ लीं तो सचमुच मैं लबार ही हूँ। श्री रामचंद्रजी के प्रताप को समझकर (स्मरण करके) अंगद क्रोधित हो उठे और उन्होंने रावण की सभा में प्रण करके (दृढ़ता के साथ) पैर रोप दिया ॥
english_translation: Angad said, “If I do not tear out your ten tongues, O twenty-armed one, then I am truly a liar.” Remembering Ram’s power, Angad grew angry and planted his foot firmly in Ravana’s assembly.
essence: Firmness comes from remembering Ram, not from personal pride.
simple_meaning: Angad vows to rip out Ravana’s ten tongues if he keeps insulting him, and he stands firm in Ravana’s court after remembering Ram’s power.
insight: It shifts confidence from personal ego to remembrance of a higher cause.
modern_relevance: Someone dismisses your work in a meeting, and your chest tightens. You don’t need noise or panic — you need the steadiness that comes from remembering who you represent.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: जौं मम चरन सकसि सठ टारी। फिरहिं रामु सीता मैं हारी॥ सुनहु सुभट सब कह दससीसा। पद गहि धरनि पछारहु कीसा ॥
translation: (और कहा-) अरे मूर्ख! यदि तू मेरा चरण हटा सके तो श्री रामजी लौट जाएँगे, मैं सीताजी को हार गया। रावण ने कहा- हे सब वीरो! सुनो, पैर पकड़कर बंदर को पृथ्वी पर पछाड़ दो ॥
english_translation: “If you can move my foot, fool, then Ram will return and I will have lost Sita.” Ravana said, “Hear me, all warriors: seize the monkey’s feet and throw him to the ground.”
essence: Pride mocks danger until it is forced to command violence.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that if Hanuman can move his foot, then Ram will return and he will have lost Sita. He then orders his warriors to grab Hanuman and throw him down.
insight: It shows how ego answers humiliation with bluster instead of seeing reality.
modern_relevance: Someone mocks your boundary in a meeting, then suddenly calls in three colleagues to pressure you into backing down. The real issue was never the gesture — it was the ego behind it.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: इंद्रजीत आदिक बलवाना। हरषि उठे जहँ तहँ भट नाना॥ झपटहिं करि बल बिपुल उपाई। पद न टरइ बैठहिं सिरु नाई ॥
translation: इंद्रजीत (मेघनाद) आदि अनेकों बलवान् योद्धा जहाँ-तहाँ से हर्षित होकर उठे। वे पूरे बल से बहुत से उपाय करके झपटते हैं। पर पैर टलता नहीं, तब सिर नीचा करके फिर अपने-अपने स्थान पर जा बैठ जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Indrajit and other mighty warriors rose up, delighted, from here and there. They rushed forward with great force and many different tactics, but their feet could not move Angad's stance; then they sat back down, bowing their heads.
essence: Powerful resistance collapses when it meets unshakable steadiness.
simple_meaning: Many powerful warriors rush in with confidence and clever tactics, but they cannot dislodge Angad. Defeated, they lower their heads and sit back down.
insight: It shifts attention from aggressive effort to the unshakeable center that effort cannot move.
modern_relevance: A room full of senior people keeps arguing, sending in smarter plans, sharper objections, better numbers — yet the one calm person in the corner doesn't budge. Force keeps changing shape; resolve stays put.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि उठि झपटहिं सुर आराती। टरइ न कीस चरन एहि भाँती॥ पुरुष कुजोगी जिमि उरगारी। मोह बिटप नहिं सकहिं उपारी ॥
translation: (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं-) वे देवताओं के शत्रु (राक्षस) फिर उठकर झपटते हैं, परन्तु हे सर्पों के शत्रु गरुड़जी! अंगद का चरण उनसे वैसे ही नहीं टलता जैसे कुयोगी (विषयी) पुरुष मोह रूपी वृक्ष को नहीं उखाड़ सकते ॥
english_translation: They rise and lunge again, but the monkey's foot does not move. In the same way, misguided people cannot uproot the tree of delusion.
essence: What is firmly rooted cannot be shaken by repeated force.
simple_meaning: A firm devotee does not get shaken by repeated attacks, just as confused people cannot uproot delusion’s hold by force alone.
insight: It shifts attention from reactive struggle to inner firmness. The verse teaches that some forces break against unwavering presence.
modern_relevance: You keep getting pulled into the same argument, the same craving, the same panic — and yet a part of you can stay unmoved. That steadiness is the real victory.
speaker: Kak Bhushundi

verse_text: कोटिन्ह मेघनाद सम सुभट उठे हरषाइ। झपटहिं टरै न कपि चरन पुनि बैठहिं सिर नाइ ॥
translation: करोड़ों वीर योद्धा जो बल में मेघनाद के समान थे, हर्षित होकर उठे, वे बार-बार झपटते हैं, पर वानर का चरण नहीं उठता, तब लज्जा के मारे सिर नवाकर बैठ जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Millions of warriors as mighty as Meghnad rose up in joy. They kept lunging, but the monkey's foot never moved; then, ashamed, they sat down bowing their heads.
essence: Unmoved steadiness makes force collapse on its own.
simple_meaning: Countless powerful warriors rise and attack, but the monkey warrior does not budge. Their force fails, and they sit down in shame.
insight: It teaches you that rooted steadiness can defeat frantic aggression without a larger fight.
modern_relevance: A room full of people pushes back against your boundary, expecting you to fold. You stay calm, unmoved, and the pressure loses its power.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भूमि न छाँड़त कपि चरन देखत रिपु मद भाग। कोटि बिघ्न ते संत कर मन जिमि नीति न त्याग ॥
translation: जैसे करोड़ों विघ्न आने पर भी संत का मन नीति को नहीं छोड़ता, वैसे ही वानर (अंगद) का चरण पृथ्वी को नहीं छोड़ता। यह देखकर शत्रु (रावण) का मद दूर हो गया! ॥
english_translation: Like a saint who never abandons righteous conduct even through countless obstacles, Angada's foot did not leave the ground. Seeing this, Ravana's pride fell away.
essence: Firm conduct can break pride more than force can.
simple_meaning: Angada stands so firmly that even Ravana's pride breaks. The image compares that steadiness to a saint who never drops righteous conduct, no matter how many obstacles appear.
insight: It shifts attention from force to unshakable conduct under pressure.
modern_relevance: You stay calm in a room where everyone expects you to fold. Your silence, more than your argument, exposes the other person's bluster.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कपि बल देखि सकल हियँ हारे। उठा आपु कपि कें परचारे॥ गहत चरन कह बालिकुमारा। मम पद गहें न तोर उबारा ॥
translation: अंगद का बल देखकर सब हृदय में हार गए। तब अंगद के ललकारने पर रावण स्वयं उठा। जब वह अंगद का चरण पकड़ने लगा, तब बालि कुमार अंगद ने कहा- मेरा चरण पकड़ने से तेरा बचाव नहीं होगा! ॥
english_translation: Seeing Angad's strength, everyone lost heart. Then, at Angad's challenge, Ravana himself rose. When he tried to seize Angad's foot, the son of Bali said, 'Holding my foot will not save you!'
essence: Bravado collapses when courage refuses to bow.
simple_meaning: Angad's strength shakes the enemy force, and Ravana rises to face him. But Angad makes it clear that grabbing his foot cannot save Ravana.
insight: It shows that intimidation may bend pride, but it cannot replace true surrender.
modern_relevance: Someone finally calls out the person dominating the room, and the whole mood changes. But the real turning point still comes only when ego stops bargaining and faces the truth.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गहसि न राम चरन सठ जाई॥ सुनत फिरा मन अति सकुचाई॥ भयउ तेजहत श्री सब गई। मध्य दिवस जिमि ससि सोहई ॥
translation: अरे मूर्ख- तू जाकर श्री रामजी के चरण क्यों नहीं पकड़ता? यह सुनकर वह मन में बहुत ही सकुचाकर लौट गया। उसकी सारी श्री जाती रही। वह ऐसा तेजहीन हो गया जैसे मध्याह्न में चंद्रमा दिखाई देता है ॥
english_translation: “Why don’t you go and grasp Ram’s feet, fool?” Hearing this, he turned back in deep shame. All his radiance vanished, and he looked like the moon at midday.
essence: Ego loses its shine the moment surrender is demanded.
simple_meaning: He is told to surrender to Ram, but shame makes him retreat. His pride collapses, and his former brilliance disappears.
insight: It shifts the mind from defending pride to seeing surrender as the only real opening.
modern_relevance: You rehearse your defense in the car, then hear one sentence that exposes everything. Your face goes hot, your certainty drops, and the part of you that wanted to stay untouchable suddenly feels small.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सिंघासन बैठेउ सिर नाई। मानहुँ संपति सकल गँवाई॥ जगदातमा प्रानपति रामा। तासु बिमुख किमि लह बिश्रामा ॥
translation: वह सिर नीचा करके सिंहासन पर जा बैठा। मानो सारी सम्पत्ति गँवाकर बैठा हो। श्री रामचंद्रजी जगत् भर के आत्मा और प्राणों के स्वामी हैं। उनसे विमुख रहने वाला शांति कैसे पा सकता है? ॥
english_translation: He sat on the throne with his head bowed, as if he had lost all his wealth. Lord Ram is the soul of the world and the master of life itself; how can anyone turned away from him find peace?
essence: Separation from Ram leaves even power unable to rest.
simple_meaning: Ram is the life of everything, so turning away from him leaves a person unable to find peace.
insight: It shifts the mind from outer status to inner alignment with Ram.
modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the title, the bigger apartment — and still feel strangely unsettled at night. Something deeper than success is missing, and this verse names it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उमा राम की भृकुटि बिलासा। होइ बिस्व पुनि पावइ नासा॥ तृन ते कुलिस कुलिस तृन करई। तासु दूत पन कहु किमि टरई ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! जिन श्री रामचंद्रजी के भ्रूविलास (भौंह के इशारे) से विश्व उत्पन्न होता है और फिर नाश को प्राप्त होता है, जो तृण को वज्र और वज्र को तृण बना देते हैं (अत्यंत निर्बल को महान् प्रबल और महान् प्रबल को अत्यंत निर्बल कर देते हैं), उनके दूत का प्रण कहो, कैसे टल सकता है? ॥
english_translation: O Uma, by Ram's glance alone the world arises and then returns to ruin. He can turn straw into thunderbolt and thunderbolt into straw; how can his messenger's pledge ever be turned aside?
essence: Ram's backing makes a messenger unstoppable.
simple_meaning: Ram's smallest glance shapes creation and destruction. If his messenger is sent on a mission, no force can block that vow.
insight: It shifts confidence from personal ability to the authority behind your action.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where every person has already decided against you. Still, something in you stays unshaken because you know who sent you and why.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: पुनि कपि कही नीति बिधि नाना। मान न ताहि कालु निअराना॥ रिपु मद मथि प्रभु सुजसु सुनायो। यह कहि चल्यो बालि नृप जायो ॥
translation: फिर अंगद ने अनेकों प्रकार से नीति कही। पर रावण नहीं माना, क्योंकि उसका काल निकट आ गया था। शत्रु के गर्व को चूर करके अंगद ने उसको प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी का सुयश सुनाया और फिर वह राजा बालि का पुत्र यह कहकर चल दिया- ॥
english_translation: Then Angada spoke many kinds of wise counsel. But Ravana did not agree, because his time of death was near. Crushing the enemy's pride, Angada spoke the glory of Lord Ram, and then, saying this, he left, the son of Bali.
essence: Pride can make even clear counsel useless.
simple_meaning: Angada tried many kinds of counsel, but Ravana would not listen. His pride was already too strong, and his end was close. Angada then praised Ram and left.
insight: It shows that counsel has limits when ego has already hardened into refusal.
modern_relevance: You explain the consequences clearly, but the other person keeps defending a bad choice. At some point, the healthiest move is to speak truth once and step back.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हतौं न खेत खेलाइ खेलाई। तोहि अबहिं का करौं बड़ाई॥ प्रथमहिं तासु तनय कपि मारा। सो सुनि रावन भयउ दुखारा ॥
translation: रणभूमि में तुझे खेला-खेलाकर न मारूँ तब तक अभी (पहले से) क्या बड़ाई करूँ। अंगद ने पहले ही (सभा में आने से पूर्व ही) उसके पुत्र को मार डाला था। वह संवाद सुनकर रावण दुःखी हो गया ॥
english_translation: How can I boast now unless I first make you fight and kill you in battle? Hearing that Angad had already killed his son before coming to the assembly, Ravana was stricken with grief.
essence: Boasting means nothing until victory is real.
simple_meaning: Angad taunts Ravana, saying he cannot claim victory unless he defeats him in battle. The mention of Ravana's son being killed earlier only deepens Ravana's grief.
insight: It shows how taunts can expose false pride by forcing it to face loss.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone makes a smug claim, and you answer with one sentence that exposes how little they can actually prove. The air changes because the boast has nowhere left to stand.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: जातुधान अंगद पन देखी। भय ब्याकुल सब भए बिसेषी ॥
translation: अंगद का प्रण (सफल) देखकर सब राक्षस भय से अत्यन्त ही व्याकुल हो गए ॥
english_translation: Seeing Angad's vow succeed, all the demons became especially terrified and agitated with fear.
essence: Fear spreads fast when pride is publicly defeated.
simple_meaning: The demons saw Angad's challenge succeed, and fear spread through all of them.
insight: It shows how a single fearless act can break collective arrogance.
modern_relevance: A quiet person speaks one clear truth in a tense meeting, and the whole room shifts. What looked like confidence was only bluster.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रिपु बल धरषि हरषि कपि बालितनय बल पुंज। पुलक सरीर नयन जल गहे राम पद कंज ॥
translation: शत्रु के बल का मर्दन कर, बल की राशि बालि पुत्र अंगदजी ने हर्षित होकर आकर श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणकमल पकड़ लिए। उनका शरीर पुलकित है और नेत्रों में (आनंदाश्रुओं का) जल भरा है ॥
english_translation: Having crushed the enemy's power, Angad, son of Bali and a mass of strength, came rejoicing and grasped Ram's lotus feet. His body thrilled, and tears filled his eyes.
essence: Strength becomes complete when it returns to Ram's feet.
simple_meaning: Angad defeats the enemy's pride and then comes joyfully to Ram, overwhelmed with devotion. Victory leads him not to self-display, but to Ram's feet.
insight: It shifts success from self-importance to surrender, showing that real power bows down.
modern_relevance: You finally win the argument, close the deal, or prove your point — and the real relief is not being right. It is coming back to what you serve.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: साँझ जानि दसकंधर भवन गयउ बिलखाइ। मंदोदरीं रावनहिं बहुरि कहा समुझाइ ॥
translation: सन्ध्या हो गई जानकर दशग्रीव बिलखता हुआ (उदास होकर) महल में गया। मन्दोदरी ने रावण को समझाकर फिर कहा- ॥
english_translation: Knowing that evening had fallen, Ravana went sorrowfully back to the palace. Mandodari then tried again to counsel him.
essence: Defeat becomes dangerous when pride refuses counsel.
simple_meaning: Ravana returns to his palace in distress after dusk, and Mandodari tries once more to reason with him.
insight: It shifts attention from the outer defeat to the inner collapse that follows stubbornness.
modern_relevance: You come home after a meeting where your plan fell apart, and the silence feels heavier than the failure. Someone who loves you still tries to reach you before you harden.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कंत समुझि मन तजहु कुमतिही। सोह न समर तुम्हहि रघुपतिही॥ रामानुज लघु रेख खचाई। सोउ नहिं नाघेहु असि मनुसाई ॥
translation: हे कान्त! मन में समझकर (विचारकर) कुबुद्धि को छोड़ दो। आप से और श्री रघुनाथजी से युद्ध शोभा नहीं देता। उनके छोटे भाई ने एक जरा सी रेखा खींच दी थी, उसे भी आप नहीं लाँघ सके, ऐसा तो आपका पुरुषत्व है ॥
english_translation: O dear one, think carefully in your mind and abandon foolish thinking. A war with Raghupati does not suit you. You could not even cross the small line drawn by Lakshmana, so is that your manliness?
essence: Ego cannot see its own limits until it is already trapped.
simple_meaning: Mandodari urges Ravana to drop his bad judgment and avoid fighting Ram. She reminds him that he could not even cross Lakshmana's small line, so his pride is misplaced.
insight: It shifts the mind from bravado to honest self-assessment before acting.
modern_relevance: You are about to send the angry text that will end the relationship. A quieter voice in you already knows the argument is bigger than your ego.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: पिय तुम्ह ताहि जितब संग्रामा। जाके दूत केर यह कामा॥ कौतुक सिंधु नाघि तव लंका। आयउ कपि केहरी असंका ॥
translation: हे प्रियतम! आप उन्हें संग्राम में जीत पाएँगे, जिनके दूत का ऐसा काम है? खेल से ही समुद्र लाँघकर वह वानरों में सिंह (हनुमान् ) आपकी लंका में निर्भय चला आया! ॥
english_translation: Dear one, how can you win a battle against the one whose messenger did this? Crossing the ocean was play for him; that fearless monkey-lion entered your Lanka without hesitation.
essence: Fearless action exposes the futility of arrogance.
simple_meaning: Mandodari tells Ravana that he cannot defeat Ram in battle when Ram's messenger has already crossed the ocean and entered Lanka fearlessly.
insight: It shifts the mind from swagger to sober recognition of strength already demonstrated.
modern_relevance: You dismiss the quiet person in the room, then discover they already handled the hardest part without asking permission. The warning came too late to save your pride.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: रखवारे हति बिपिन उजारा। देखत तोहि अच्छ तेहिं मारा॥ जारि सकल पुर कीन्हेसि छारा। कहाँ रहा बल गर्ब तुम्हारा ॥
translation: रखवालों को मारकर उसने अशोक वन उजाड़ डाला। आपके देखते-देखते उसने अक्षयकुमार को मार डाला और संपूर्ण नगर को जलाकर राख कर दिया। उस समय आपके बल का गर्व कहाँ चला गया था? ॥
english_translation: He killed the guards and laid waste to the grove. In front of your own eyes, he killed Akshayakumar. He burned the whole city to ashes. Where did your boast of strength go then?
essence: Pride sounds powerful until events prove otherwise.
simple_meaning: Hanuman has already destroyed the grove, killed the guards, slain Akshayakumar, and burned Lanka. Ravana's boast about his strength is exposed as empty.
insight: It forces the mind to face consequences instead of hiding behind pride.
modern_relevance: You bragged you had it under control, then the mess was already on fire. A single hard fact can expose how fragile your confidence really was.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: अब पति मृषा गाल जनि मारहु। मोर कहा कछु हृदयँ बिचारहु॥ पति रघुपतिहि नृपति जनि मानहु। अग जग नाथ अतुलबल जानहु ॥
translation: अब हे स्वामी! झूठ (व्यर्थ) गाल न मारिए (डींग न हाँकिए) मेरे कहने पर हृदय में कुछ विचार कीजिए। हे पति! आप श्री रघुपति को (निरा) राजा मत समझिए, बल्कि अग-जगनाथ (चराचर के स्वामी) और अतुलनीय बलवान् जानिए ॥
english_translation: Now, husband, do not hurl empty insults. Think carefully about what I am saying in your heart. Do not take Raghupati for a mere king; know Him as the lord of all worlds and of immeasurable strength.
essence: Pride is dangerous because it refuses to see power clearly.
simple_meaning: Mandodari warns Ravana not to insult Ram. She tells him to think seriously and stop treating Ram like an ordinary king, because Ram is the lord of all worlds and immeasurably powerful.
insight: It shifts the mind from contempt to clear seeing before arrogance becomes ruin.
modern_relevance: You keep dismissing the warning because admitting it would bruise your ego. A friend, a partner, or a colleague is trying to save you from a choice you still call harmless.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: बान प्रताप जान मारीचा। तासु कहा नहिं मानेहि नीचा॥ जनक सभाँ अगनित भूपाला। रहे तुम्हउ बल अतुल बिसाला ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के बाण का प्रताप तो नीच मारीच भी जानता था, परन्तु आपने उसका कहना भी नहीं माना। जनक की सभा में अगणित राजागण थे। वहाँ विशाल और अतुलनीय बल वाले आप भी थे ॥
english_translation: Even lowly Maricha knew the power of Rama's arrow, yet you did not heed his warning. In Janaka's assembly there were countless kings; you too were there, mighty and immeasurable in strength.
essence: Pride can hear the truth and still refuse it.
simple_meaning: Ravana is being reminded that even Maricha knew Rama's power, and that Ravana was also present in Janaka's court among many kings.
insight: It shifts the mind from defending ego to remembering earlier evidence and hard lessons.
modern_relevance: You ignore the one colleague who quietly sees the risk clearly, then act surprised when the plan collapses. The warning was never hidden; your pride was louder.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: भंजि धनुष जानकी बिआही। तब संग्राम जितेहु किन ताही॥ सुरपति सुत जानइ बल थोरा। राखा जिअत आँखि गहि फोरा ॥
translation: वहाँ शिवजी का धनुष तोड़कर श्री रामजी ने जानकी को ब्याहा, तब आपने उनको संग्राम में क्यों नहीं जीता? इंद्रपुत्र जयन्त उनके बल को कुछ-कुछ जानता है। श्री रामजी ने पकड़कर, केवल उसकी एक आँख ही फोड़ दी और उसे जीवित ही छोड़ दिया ॥
english_translation: When Ram broke Shiva's bow and married Janaki, why did you not defeat him in battle then? Jayant, the son of Indra, knows something of Ram's strength; Ram seized him, broke only one of his eyes, and left him alive.
essence: Even Ravana admits Ram's power, yet his pride still will not bend.
simple_meaning: Ravana reminds Sita's captor that Ram already proved his power by breaking Shiva's bow and sparing Jayant after wounding him.
insight: It exposes how ego can acknowledge reality and still refuse to submit to it.
modern_relevance: You keep arguing with someone whose record already speaks for itself. The facts are plain, but your ego still wants the last word.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सूपनखा कै गति तुम्ह देखी। तदपि हृदयँ नहिं लाज बिसेषी ॥
translation: शूर्पणखा की दशा तो आपने देख ही ली। तो भी आपके हृदय में (उनसे लड़ने की बात सोचते) विशेष (कुछ भी) लज्जा नहीं आती! ॥
english_translation: You saw what happened to Shurpanakha, and still your heart feels no special shame.
essence: Seeing the warning means nothing if pride stays untouched.
simple_meaning: You saw Shurpanakha’s condition, yet you still feel no shame about what happened next.
insight: It shifts attention from facts to self-correction: seeing clearly means letting the lesson change you.
modern_relevance: You watch a friend ignore every warning sign, then repeat the same mistake anyway. The hard part is not lack of information — it is refusing to feel the lesson.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: बधि बिराध खर दूषनहि लीलाँ हत्यो कबंध। बालि एक सर मार् यो तेहि जानहु दसकंध ॥
translation: जिन्होंने विराध और खर-दूषण को मारकर लीला से ही कबन्ध को भी मार डाला और जिन्होंने बालि को एक ही बाण से मार दिया, हे दशकन्ध! आप उन्हें (उनके महत्व को) समझिए! ॥
english_translation: O ten-headed one, understand their power: they killed Viradh, Khara, and Dushana, slew Kabandha effortlessly, and struck Bali down with a single arrow.
essence: Past victories should end your false confidence.
simple_meaning: Ravana is reminded that Ram has already destroyed powerful foes with ease, so he should not underestimate him.
insight: It shifts attention from Ravana's pride to Ram's proven power and the danger of underestimating it.
modern_relevance: You keep dismissing the person you hurt with one careless remark, forgetting how steadily they have handled harder blows before.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जेहिं जलनाथ बँधायउ हेला। उतरे प्रभु दल सहित सुबेला॥ कारुनीक दिनकर कुल केतू। दूत पठायउ तव हित हेतू ॥
translation: जिन्होंने खेल से ही समुद्र को बँधा लिया और जो प्रभु सेना सहित सुबेल पर्वत पर उतर पड़े, उन सूर्यकुल के ध्वजास्वरूप (कीर्ति को बढ़ाने वाले) करुणामय भगवान् ने आप ही के हित के लिए दूत भेजा ॥
english_translation: He who, by a mere play, bound the ocean and descended with his army to Mount Suvela— that compassionate banner of the solar line sent a messenger for your own good.
essence: True power still leaves room for one last warning.
simple_meaning: Ram, who effortlessly bridged the ocean and came with his army to Suvela, even sent a messenger for Ravana's welfare.
insight: It teaches you to let strength be guided by mercy before it becomes force.
modern_relevance: You finally have the leverage to crush someone who has been blocking you for months. Instead, you send one last message that says, 'Step back now and this can still end well.'
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सभा माझ जेहिं तव बल मथा। करि बरूथ महुँ मृगपति जथा॥ अंगद हनुमत अनुचर जाके। रन बाँकुरे बीर अति बाँके ॥
translation: जिसने बीच सभा में आकर आपके बल को उसी प्रकार मथ डाला जैसे हाथियों के झुंड में आकर सिंह (उसे छिन्न-भिन्न कर डालता है) रण में बाँके अत्यंत विकट वीर अंगद और हनुमान् जिनके सेवक हैं, ॥
english_translation: He who, in the middle of the assembly, churned up your strength like a lion in an elephant herd; Angad and Hanuman are his attendants, and his warriors are fierce and unbending.
essence: Real strength makes pride collapse in public.
simple_meaning: Ravana is boasting that Ram openly crushed his pride in the court, and that powerful warriors like Angad and Hanuman serve Ram.
insight: It shifts the mind from boasting about power to recognizing power that cannot be faked.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room ready to dominate, and one calm person changes the whole atmosphere. Their quiet strength exposes how thin your confidence really was.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: तेहि कहँ पिय पुनि पुनि नर कहहू। मुधा मान ममता मद बहहू॥ अहह कंत कृत राम बिरोधा। काल बिबस मन उपज न बोधा ॥
translation: हे पति! उन्हें आप बार-बार मनुष्य कहते हैं। आप व्यर्थ ही मान, ममता और मद का बोझ ढो रहे हैं! हा प्रियतम! आपने श्री रामजी से विरोध कर लिया और काल के विशेष वश होने से आपके मन में अब भी ज्ञान नहीं उत्पन्न होता ॥
english_translation: O husband, you keep calling him only a human being. You carry the burden of pride, possessiveness, and intoxication in vain. Ah, beloved, you have opposed Ram, and under the grip of time, understanding no longer arises in your mind.
essence: Pride makes you blind before defeat arrives.
simple_meaning: Mandodari tells Ravana that he keeps dismissing Ram as merely human while carrying pride and attachment. By opposing Ram, he has lost clear understanding.
insight: It shifts the mind from defending ego to noticing how ego destroys discernment.
modern_relevance: You are in the middle of a heated argument and keep repeating your point just to win. Later, you realise the need to be right was the very thing that made you unable to listen.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: काल दंड गहि काहु न मारा। हरइ धर्म बल बुद्धि बिचारा॥ निकट काल जेहि आवत साईं। तेहि भ्रम होइ तुम्हारिहि नाईं ॥
translation: काल दण्ड (लाठी) लेकर किसी को नहीं मारता। वह धर्म, बल, बुद्धि और विचार को हर लेता है। हे स्वामी! जिसका काल (मरण समय) निकट आ जाता है, उसे आप ही की तरह भ्रम हो जाता है ॥
english_translation: Death does not strike with a staff. It takes away righteousness, strength, discernment, and judgment. O master, when death draws near, confusion arises in you as well.
essence: Death begins by stealing your clarity, not your body.
simple_meaning: Death is not a physical blow. It first weakens your judgment, strength, and sense of right, leaving you confused when the end approaches.
insight: It shifts attention from external danger to the inner erosion that makes bad choices inevitable.
modern_relevance: You know that moment when panic hits and your sharpest thinking disappears? This verse names that collapse: pressure can take away judgment before it takes anything else.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: दुइ सुत मरे दहेउ पुर अजहुँ पूर पिय देहु। कृपासिंधु रघुनाथ भजि नाथ बिमल जसु लेहु ॥
translation: आपके दो पुत्र मारे गए और नगर जल गया। (जो हुआ सो हुआ) हे प्रियतम! अब भी (इस भूल की) पूर्ति (समाप्ति) कर दीजिए (श्री रामजी से वैर त्याग दीजिए) और हे नाथ! कृपा के समुद्र श्री रघुनाथजी को भजकर निर्मल यश लीजिए ॥
english_translation: Your two sons are dead and the city has burned. Even now, end this feud, and worship Raghunath, the ocean of grace, to earn spotless fame.
essence: Even after ruin, you can still choose Ram and begin again.
simple_meaning: Even after terrible loss, the speaker urges reconciliation and devotion to Ram instead of continuing revenge.
insight: It shifts you from retaliation to reconciliation, showing that humility can begin after damage is done.
modern_relevance: You just got the message that the deal collapsed, the money is gone, and the relationship is shattered. Even then, you can stop feeding the feud and choose the path that restores you.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: नारि बचन सुनि बिसिख समाना। सभाँ गयउ उठि होत बिहाना॥ बैठ जाइ सिंघासन फूली। अति अभिमान त्रास सब भूली ॥
translation: स्त्री के बाण के समान वचन सुनकर वह सबेरा होते ही उठकर सभा में चला गया और सारा भय भुलाकर अत्यंत अभिमान में फूलकर सिंहासन पर जा बैठा ॥
english_translation: Hearing the woman's words, he rose at dawn and went to the assembly. Sitting on the throne, he forgot all fear and swelled with great pride.
essence: Pride can make danger feel distant until it is too late.
simple_meaning: He heard sharp, stinging words, went to the court at daybreak, sat on the throne, and let pride erase all fear.
insight: It exposes how wounded ego turns warning into self-inflation instead of self-correction.
modern_relevance: You get one harsh message before sunrise, then spend the morning rehearsing your own importance instead of hearing the warning. Pride can feel like strength right before it becomes blindness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: इहाँ राम अंगदहि बोलावा। आइ चरन पंकज सिरु नावा॥ अति आदर समीप बैठारी। बोले बिहँसि कृपाल खरारी ॥
translation: यहाँ (सुबेल पर्वत पर) श्री रामजी ने अंगद को बुलाया। उन्होंने आकर चरणकमलों में सिर नवाया। बड़े आदर से उन्हें पास बैठाकर खर के शत्रु कृपालु श्री रामजी हँसकर बोले ॥
english_translation: Here, on Suvela Mountain, Ram called Angad. Angad came and bowed his head at Ram's lotus feet. Ram seated him nearby with great respect and, smiling, the compassionate destroyer of evil spoke.
essence: Respect turns an enemy meeting into a human one.
simple_meaning: Ram calls Angad close, honors him, and speaks to him kindly.
insight: It shows that dignity can disarm conflict before a single argument begins.
modern_relevance: A tense meeting gets easier the moment someone offers respect first — the shoulders drop, the guard softens, and real conversation becomes possible.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बालितनय कौतुक अति मोही। तात सत्य कहुँ पूछउँ तोही॥ रावनु जातुधान कुल टीका। भुज बल अतुल जासु जग लीका ॥
translation: हे बालि के पुत्र! मुझे बड़ा कौतूहल है। हे तात! इसी से मैं तुमसे पूछता हूँ, सत्य कहना। जो रावण राक्षसों के कुल का तिलक है और जिसके अतुलनीय बाहुबल की जगत् भर में धाक है, ॥
english_translation: O son of Bali, I am deeply curious. Tell me the truth, father, I ask you this: Ravana is the ornament of the race of the demons, and his unmatched arm-strength is feared throughout the world.
essence: Great reputation still has to face a truthful question.
simple_meaning: Ram asks Angad to tell the truth about Ravana’s great strength and fame. The verse sets up a challenge: how was such a mighty ruler humbled?
insight: It shifts attention from public image to the facts underneath it.
modern_relevance: In a tense meeting, someone names the most intimidating person in the room and asks for the real story. The question is calm, but it cuts through fear and reputation.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तासु मुकुट तुम्ह चारि चलाए। कहहु तात कवनी बिधि पाए॥ सुनु सर्बग्य प्रनत सुखकारी। मुकुट न होहिं भूप न गुन चारी ॥
translation: उसके चार मुकुट तुमने फेंके। हे तात! बताओ, तुमने उनको किस प्रकार से पाया! (अंगद ने कहा-) हे सर्वज्ञ! हे शरणागत को सुख देने वाले! सुनिए। वे मुकुट नहीं हैं। वे तो राजा के चार गुण हैं ॥
english_translation: You threw down his four crowns. Tell me, dear one, how did you get them? Listen, all-knowing one who brings comfort to the surrendered: those are not crowns at all. They are the four qualities of a king.
essence: Power is real only when it rests on four inner qualities.
simple_meaning: Angad explains that the four items Ram threw down are not real crowns. They represent the four qualities a king should have.
insight: It shifts attention from outward symbols of authority to the inner qualities that make authority real.
modern_relevance: A team celebrates the flashy title on a business card, but the room falls silent when the person cannot lead, protect, or decide. Angad would say the real crown is character.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: साम दान अरु दंड बिभेदा। नृप उर बसहिं नाथ कह बेदा॥ नीति धर्म के चरन सुहाए। अस जियँ जानि पहिं आए ॥
translation: हे नाथ! वेद कहते हैं कि साम, दान, दण्ड और भेद- ये चारों राजा के हृदय में बसते हैं। ये नीति-धर्म के चार सुंदर चरण हैं, (किन्तु रावण में धर्म का अभाव है) ऐसा जी में जानकर ये नाथ के पास आ गए हैं ॥
english_translation: O Lord, the Vedas say that conciliation, gifts, punishment, and division dwell in a king's heart. These are the four beautiful limbs of righteous policy. Knowing this in their hearts, they have come to you.
essence: Power becomes wise only when it knows how to respond.
simple_meaning: A king should know how to use persuasion, generosity, firmness, and strategy. Angad says these royal qualities are what brought him here.
insight: It teaches you to choose the right form of response instead of defaulting to force.
modern_relevance: You are leading a tense family meeting, and everyone wants a different answer. Before you speak, you need to know whether this moment calls for softness, generosity, firmness, or a strategic pause.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: धर्महीन प्रभु पद बिमुख काल बिबस दससीस। तेहि परिहरि गुन आए सुनहु कोसलाधीस ॥
translation: दशशीश रावण धर्महीन, प्रभु के पद से विमुख और काल के वश में है, इसलिए हे कोसलराज! सुनिए, वे गुण रावण को छोड़कर आपके पास आ गए हैं ॥
english_translation: Ravana is without dharma, turned away from the feet of the Lord, and helpless in the grip of time. Leaving him aside, those virtues have come to you, O Lord of Kosala.
essence: Power without dharma empties itself; virtue moves toward what is aligned.
simple_meaning: Ravana has abandoned dharma and turned away from Ram, so his good qualities no longer belong to him. They now rest with Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from outer power to the alignment that makes power meaningful.
modern_relevance: A talented manager keeps winning praise while breaking trust with everyone around them. Slowly, the team stops seeing strength and starts seeing emptiness. Character, not image, decides where respect lives.
speaker: Angad

verse_text: परम चतुरता श्रवन सुनि बिहँसे रामु उदार। समाचार पुनि सब कहे गढ़ के बालिकुमार ॥
translation: अंगद की परम चतुरता (पूर्ण उक्ति) कानों से सुनकर उदार श्री रामचंद्रजी हँसने लगे। फिर बालि पुत्र ने किले के (लंका के) सब समाचार कहे ॥
english_translation: Hearing Angad's wonderfully clever words, generous Ram laughed. Then Bali's son told him all the news of the fortress.
essence: Grace lets you hear hard news without losing composure.
simple_meaning: Ram smiles at Angad's clever words, and Angad then reports everything happening inside Lanka.
insight: It shows how steadiness and wit can hold pressure without collapse.
modern_relevance: You get a message that could spark panic, but you read it twice and stay steady. That pause lets you see clearly instead of reacting on impulse.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रिपु के समाचार जब पाए। राम सचिव सब निकट बोलाए॥ लंका बाँके चारि दुआरा। केहि बिधि लागिअ करहु बिचारा ॥
translation: जब शत्रु के समाचार प्राप्त हो गए, तब श्री रामचंद्रजी ने सब मंत्रियों को पास बुलाया (और कहा-) लंका के चार बड़े विकट दरवाजे हैं। उन पर किस तरह आक्रमण किया जाए, इस पर विचार करो ॥
english_translation: When news of the enemy arrived, Ram called all his ministers close and said, “Lanka has four strong gates. Think carefully about how to attack them.”
