english_translation: Blood has pooled in the pits and hardened there; dust whirls over it, like ash settling on heaps of embers.
essence: War leaves the ground looking like dying fire.
simple_meaning: The battlefield is so soaked with blood and dust that it looks like ash covering burning coals.
insight: It keeps the moment in view as raw aftermath, not heroic victory.
modern_relevance: You walk past the aftermath of a major accident and see the road marked by shattered glass, dust, and stillness. The mind goes quiet before it can explain anything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: घायल बीर बिराजहिं कैसे। कुसुमति किंसुक के तरु जैसे॥ लछिमन मेघनाद द्वौ जोधा। भिरहिं परसपर करि अति क्रोधा ॥
translation: घायल वीर कैसे शोभित हैं, जैसे फूले हुए पलास के पेड़। लक्ष्मण और मेघनाद दोनों योद्धा अत्यंत क्रोध करके एक-दूसरे से भिड़ते हैं ॥
english_translation: Wounded warriors still look splendid, like blossoming palash trees. Lakshman and Meghnad, both furious, clash with each other.
essence: Battle can still look beautiful even while it is savage.
simple_meaning: Even wounded warriors can look striking, like blooming palash trees. Here, Lakshman and Meghnad rush at each other in fierce anger.
insight: It keeps attention on the clash itself, building the tension before the next blow.
modern_relevance: You see two exhausted rivals still forcing themselves into one more round, faces set, pride intact. The moment is all collision, not reflection.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एकहि एक सकइ नहिं जीती। निसिचर छल बल करइ अनीती॥ क्रोधवंत तब भयउ अनंता। भंजेउ रथ सारथी तुरंता ॥
translation: एक-दूसरे को (कोई किसी को) जीत नहीं सकता। राक्षस छल-बल (माया) और अनीति (अधर्म) करता है, तब भगवान् अनन्तजी (लक्ष्मणजी) क्रोधित हुए और उन्होंने तुरंत उसके रथ को तोड़ डाला और सारथी को टुकड़े-टुकड़े कर दिया! ॥
english_translation: He could not defeat the other. The demon fought with deceit, force, and unrighteousness. Then, in anger, the endless one quickly smashed the chariot and destroyed the charioteer.
essence: The duel turns savage when deceit meets fury.
simple_meaning: Neither warrior can defeat the other. Meghnada fights with deceit and force, so Lakshman grows fierce and destroys the chariot and charioteer at once.
insight: It shows the battle escalating from matched strength into destructive retaliation.
modern_relevance: A shouting match in a family argument can become the same thing: no one is trying to understand, only to overpower. This verse just drives the clash forward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाना बिधि प्रहार कर सेषा। राच्छस भयउ प्रान अवसेषा॥ रावन सुत निज मन अनुमाना। संकठ भयउ हरिहि मम प्राना ॥
translation: शेषजी (लक्ष्मणजी) उस पर अनेक प्रकार से प्रहार करने लगे। राक्षस के प्राणमात्र शेष रह गए। रावणपुत्र मेघनाद ने मन में अनुमान किया कि अब तो प्राण संकट आ बना, ये मेरे प्राण हर लेंगे ॥
english_translation: Sesha attacked him in many ways. The demon was left with barely any life. Ravana's son thought to himself, "Now my life is in danger; he will take it away."
essence: The fight turns when the enemy realizes his own life is at stake.
simple_meaning: Laxman keeps pressing the enemy until he is nearly finished. Meghnad realizes his life is now in danger.
insight: It marks the point where battle pressure becomes personal fear.
modern_relevance: A tense meeting turns when the other person realizes you are not bluffing. The room changes the moment the pressure becomes real.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बीरघातिनी छाड़िसि साँगी। तेजपुंज लछिमन उर लागी॥ मुरुछा भई सक्ति के लागें। तब चलि गयउ निकट भय त्यागें ॥
translation: तब उसने वीरघातिनी शक्ति चलाई। वह तेजपूर्ण शक्ति लक्ष्मणजी की छाती में लगी। शक्ति लगने से उन्हें मूर्छा आ गई। तब मेघनाद भय छोड़कर उनके पास चला गया ॥
english_translation: Then Meghnad hurled the weapon called Veerghatini. The blazing weapon struck Lakshman in the chest. When the weapon hit him, Lakshman fell unconscious. Then Meghnad, throwing off his fear, came near him.
essence: One blow changes the whole battle’s rhythm.
simple_meaning: Meghnad fires a deadly weapon at Lakshman, knocking him unconscious, and then moves in closer without fear.
insight: It shows how battle can shift from distance to immediate danger in a single strike.
modern_relevance: A sudden email lands like a blow, and for a moment you go blank. Then the person on the other side keeps pressing forward, and the situation becomes real.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मेघनाद सम कोटि सत जोधा रहे उठाइ। जगदाधार सेष किमि उठै चले खिसिआइ ॥
translation: मेघनाद के समान सौ करोड़ (अगणित) योद्धा उन्हें उठा रहे हैं, परन्तु जगत् के आधार श्री शेषजी (लक्ष्मणजी) उनसे कैसे उठते? तब वे लजाकर चले गए ॥
english_translation: Even after hundreds of millions of warriors tried to lift him like Meghnad, how could the bearer of the world, Shesh, rise? Ashamed, they turned away.
essence: True weight cannot be lifted by force.
simple_meaning: Even an endless crowd of warriors cannot lift Lakshman now. The scene ends in shame for the enemy, not victory.
insight: It shifts the mind from brute force to reverence for what cannot be overpowered.
modern_relevance: You keep pushing a locked door with all your strength, then finally step back and realize the problem was never effort alone.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनु गिरिजा क्रोधानल जासू। जारइ भुवन चारिदस आसू॥ सक संग्राम जीति को ताही। सेवहिं सुर नर अग जग जाही ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे गिरिजे! सुनो, (प्रलयकाल में) जिन (शेषनाग) के क्रोध की अग्नि चौदहों भुवनों को तुरंत ही जला डालती है और देवता, मनुष्य तथा समस्त चराचर (जीव) जिनकी सेवा करते हैं, उनको संग्राम में कौन जीत सकता है? ॥
english_translation: Listen, Girija: whose fire of anger burns the fourteen worlds to ashes, and whom gods, humans, and all beings serve—who can defeat that one in battle?
essence: No ordinary force can overcome what all beings already serve.
simple_meaning: Shiva tells Parvati that the one whose anger can burn the worlds and who is served by all beings cannot be defeated in battle.
insight: It shifts attention from the visible fight to the deeper power behind the scene.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone lashes out, and everyone feels the heat in the air. Some people carry a force so large that casual opposition only reveals how little you can grasp them.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: यह कौतूहल जानइ सोई। जा पर कृपा राम कै होई॥ संध्या भय फिरि द्वौ बाहनी। लगे सँभारन निज निज अनी ॥
translation: इस लीला को वही जान सकता है, जिस पर श्री रामजी की कृपा हो। संध्या होने पर दोनों ओर की सेनाएँ लौट पड़ीं, सेनापति अपनी-अपनी सेनाएँ संभालने लगे ॥
english_translation: Only one who has received Ram's grace can understand this wonder. As evening fell, both armies withdrew, and the commanders began gathering their forces.
essence: Only grace lets you see the meaning hidden inside the scene.
simple_meaning: Ram's grace lets you understand the wonder of this scene. By evening, both armies pull back and regroup.
insight: It shifts attention from surface events to the deeper force that makes them intelligible.
modern_relevance: You watch a tense meeting end with everyone pretending calm, then feel the room still buzzing afterward. Some situations only make sense when your mind is quiet enough to receive them.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: व्यापक ब्रह्म अजित भुवनेस्वर। लछिमन कहाँ बूझ करुनाकर॥ तब लगि लै आयउ हनुमाना। अनुज देखि प्रभु अति दुख माना ॥
translation: व्यापक, ब्रह्म, अजेय, संपूर्ण ब्रह्मांड के ईश्वर और करुणा की खान श्री रामचंद्रजी ने पूछा- लक्ष्मण कहाँ है? तब तक हनुमान् उन्हें ले आए। छोटे भाई को (इस दशा में) देखकर प्रभु ने बहुत ही दुःख माना ॥
english_translation: The all-pervading, unborn, unconquerable lord of the universe, compassionate Ram, asked, “Where is Lakshman?” Then Hanuman brought him. Seeing his younger brother in that condition, the Lord felt deep sorrow.
essence: True greatness still aches for the one it loves.
simple_meaning: Ram is described as the all-pervading lord, yet he still asks where Lakshman is. When Hanuman brings him, Ram is overwhelmed by grief at his brother's condition.
insight: It shifts the reader from seeing greatness as emotional distance to seeing greatness as deep capacity to care.
modern_relevance: You can hold a whole room together and still feel undone when your brother, child, or closest friend is hurt. Strength does not cancel tenderness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जामवंत कह बैद सुषेना। लंकाँ रहइ को पठई लेना॥ धरि लघु रूप गयउ हनुमंता। आनेउ भवन समेत तुरंता ॥
translation: जाम्बवान् ने कहा- लंका में सुषेण वैद्य रहता है, उसे लाने के लिए किसको भेजा जाए? हनुमान् जी छोटा रूप धरकर गए और सुषेण को उसके घर समेत तुरंत ही उठा लाए ॥
english_translation: Jambavan said, "Sushena the physician lives in Lanka. Who should be sent to bring him?" Hanuman took a small form, went, and quickly brought Sushena along with his house.
essence: Real service is quick, humble, and exactly what the moment needs.
simple_meaning: Jambavan asks who can bring Sushena from Lanka, and Hanuman instantly goes in a small form and returns with him.
insight: It shifts attention from heroics to useful action done without delay or self-display.
modern_relevance: Someone in the group chat says, "We need a specialist now." You don't argue, hesitate, or make it about you. You just go, get what is needed, and come back.
speaker: Jambavan

verse_text: राम पदारबिंद सिर नायउ आइ सुषेन। कहा नाम गिरि औषधी जाहु पवनसुत लेन ॥
translation: सुषेण ने आकर श्री रामजी के चरणारविन्दों में सिर नवाया। उसने पर्वत और औषध का नाम बताया, (और कहा कि) हे पवनपुत्र! औषधि लेने जाओ ॥
english_translation: Sushena came and bowed his head at Ram's lotus feet. He named the mountain and the herbs, and said, 'Pawanputra, go bring them.'
essence: Clear guidance turns grief into the next step.
simple_meaning: Sushena bows to Ram and identifies the mountain and herbs needed to heal Lakshman. Hanuman is then sent to bring them.
insight: It shifts attention from panic to precise action.
modern_relevance: When someone is injured or overwhelmed, the turning point is often simple: the right expert, the right diagnosis, the right next step. Relief begins when confusion ends.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम चरन सरसिज उर राखी। चला प्रभंजनसुत बल भाषी॥ उहाँ दूत एक मरमु जनावा। रावनु कालनेमि गृह आवा ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के चरणकमलों को हृदय में रखकर पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी अपना बल बखानकर (अर्थात् मैं अभी लिए आता हूँ, ऐसा कहकर) चले। उधर एक गुप्तचर ने रावण को इस रहस्य की खबर दी। तब रावण कालनेमि के घर आया ॥
english_translation: Keeping Ram's lotus feet in his heart, Hanuman, the son of the wind, set off, praising his own strength. Meanwhile, a spy revealed the secret to Ravana, and Ravana came to the house of Kalanemi.
essence: Hanuman moves forward; Ravana scrambles to respond.
simple_meaning: Hanuman leaves with Ram in his heart, and a spy informs Ravana about the search for the healing herb. Ravana then goes to Kalanemi's house.
insight: It shifts the scene from Hanuman's confident departure to Ravana's reactive counter-move.
modern_relevance: You leave a hospital room with one urgent task in mind, while someone else is already calling to block your path. The next obstacle is already moving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दसमुख कहा मरमु तेहिं सुना। पुनि पुनि कालनेमि सिरु धुना॥ देखत तुम्हहि नगरु जेहिं जारा। तासु पंथ को रोकन पारा ॥
translation: रावण ने उसको सारा मर्म (हाल) बतलाया। कालनेमि ने सुना और बार-बार सिर पीटा (खेद प्रकट किया)। (उसने कहा-) तुम्हारे देखते-देखते जिसने नगर जला डाला, उसका मार्ग कौन रोक सकता है? ॥
english_translation: Ravana told him the whole matter. Kalnemi heard it and kept shaking his head in regret. "The one who burned the city before your eyes — who can block his path?"
essence: A threat already proven cannot be dismissed.
simple_meaning: Ravana explains the situation to Kalnemi, and Kalnemi admits that the one who burned the city cannot be stopped.
insight: It keeps the focus on consequence and recognition, not strategy or moral reflection.
modern_relevance: You watch a problem grow past the point of polite denial: the evidence is already smoking in front of you, and everyone knows the easy fix is gone.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भजि रघुपति करु हित आपना। छाँड़हु नाथ मृषा जल्पना॥ नील कंज तनु सुंदर स्यामा। हृदयँ राखु लोचनाभिरामा ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी का भजन करके तुम अपना कल्याण करो! हे नाथ! झूठी बकवाद छोड़ दो। नेत्रों को आनंद देने वाले नीलकमल के समान सुंदर श्याम शरीर को अपने हृदय में रखो ॥
english_translation: Take refuge in Raghupati and do what is good for you. Leave behind false talk, and keep the beautiful dark form of the beloved of the eyes in your heart.
essence: Your real good begins when you turn toward Ram and drop false speech.
simple_meaning: Choose Ram for your own good. Stop empty, false speech. Keep his beautiful form in your heart with love.
insight: It shifts attention from verbal display to inward refuge and right action.
modern_relevance: You are halfway through a tense argument and know the conversation has turned into posturing. The verse asks you to stop the performance, return to what is good, and hold onto what steadies you.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: मैं तैं मोर मूढ़ता त्यागू। महा मोह निसि सूतत जागू॥ काल ब्याल कर भच्छक जोई। सपनेहुँ समर कि जीतिअ सोई ॥
translation: मैं-तू (भेद-भाव) और ममता रूपी मूढ़ता को त्याग दो। महामोह (अज्ञान) रूपी रात्रि में सो रहे हो, सो जाग उठो, जो काल रूपी सर्प का भी भक्षक है, कहीं स्वप्न में भी वह रण में जीता जा सकता है? ॥
english_translation: Give up the delusion of “I” and “mine.” Wake up from the night of deep confusion. Can the one who is devoured by Time, the serpent, ever win a battle, even in a dream?
essence: Ego sleeps through danger; clear seeing wakes before it is too late.
simple_meaning: Let go of ego and possessiveness. Stay awake in awareness, because someone lost in confusion cannot win against Time.
insight: It shifts you from ego-driven reaction to clear seeing before action.
modern_relevance: You keep replaying a fight in your head after the meeting is over, still defending your pride. The real loss happened earlier, when you stopped seeing clearly.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सुनि दसकंठ रिसान अति तेहिं मन कीन्ह बिचार। राम दूत कर मरौं बरु यह खल रत मल भार ॥
translation: उसकी ये बातें सुनकर रावण बहुत ही क्रोधित हुआ। तब कालनेमि ने मन में विचार किया कि (इसके हाथ से मरने की अपेक्षा) श्री रामजी के दूत के हाथ से ही मरूँ तो अच्छा है। यह दुष्ट तो पाप समूह में रत है ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Ravana became very angry. Then he thought: better to die at the hands of Rama's messenger than by this wretch, who is steeped in filth and evil.
essence: Pride would rather face death than accept insult.
simple_meaning: Ravana hears the insult and burns with anger. He thinks it would be better to die at the hands of Rama's messenger than by this wicked man's.
insight: It shows how ego can make a person choose danger over humiliation.
modern_relevance: Someone mocks you in a group chat, and your first impulse is not safety but pride. You'd rather face the harder blow than look weak.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस कहि चला रचिसि मग माया। सर मंदिर बर बाग बनाया॥ मारुतसुत देखा सुभ आश्रम। मुनिहि बूझि जल पियौं जाइ श्रम ॥
translation: वह मन ही मन ऐसा कहकर चला और उसने मार्ग में माया रची। तालाब, मंदिर और सुंदर बाग बनाया। हनुमान् जी ने सुंदर आश्रम देखकर सोचा कि मुनि से पूछकर जल पी लूँ, जिससे थकावट दूर हो जाए ॥
english_translation: Saying this to himself, he went on and created an illusion along the road. He made a lake, a temple, and a beautiful garden. Seeing the lovely hermitage, Hanuman thought, "Let me ask the sage and drink water, so I can rest from my fatigue."
essence: A pleasant appearance can hide a trap.
simple_meaning: A demon disguises his trickery as a peaceful hermitage to trap Hanuman. Hanuman, tired from travel, sees the place as a chance to rest and ask for water.
insight: It teaches you to stay alert even when something looks harmless and inviting.
modern_relevance: You stop at a roadside café after a long drive, relieved by the quiet and the trees. Sometimes the most welcoming place is designed to lower your guard.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राच्छस कपट बेष तहँ सोहा। मायापति दूतहि चह मोहा॥ जाइ पवनसुत नायउ माथा। लाग सो कहै राम गुन गाथा ॥
translation: राक्षस वहाँ कपट (से मुनि) का वेष बनाए विराजमान था। वह मूर्ख अपनी माया से मायापति के दूत को मोहित करना चाहता था। मारुति ने उसके पास जाकर मस्तक नवाया। वह श्री रामजी के गुणों की कथा कहने लगा ॥
english_translation: A demon sat there disguised as a holy man, hoping to delude the divine messenger through his tricks. Hanuman went to him, bowed his head, and began speaking of Ram's virtues.
essence: False appearances lose power when your mind stays with Ram.
simple_meaning: A demon in disguise tries to trick Hanuman, but Hanuman bows first and answers with Ram's praise.
insight: It teaches you to meet deception without losing your center or your devotion.
modern_relevance: You walk into a meeting where someone is clearly performing sincerity. Instead of getting pulled into the act, you stay respectful, steady, and anchored in what you know is real.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: होत महा रन रावन रामहिं। जितिहहिं राम न संसय या महिं॥ इहाँ भएँ मैं देखउँ भाई। ग्यान दृष्टि बल मोहि अधिकाई ॥
translation: (वह बोला-) रावण और राम में महान् युद्ध हो रहा है। रामजी जीतेंगे, इसमें संदेह नहीं है। हे भाई! मैं यहाँ रहता हुआ ही सब देख रहा हूँ। मुझे ज्ञानदृष्टि का बहुत बड़ा बल है ॥
english_translation: A great war is raging between Ravana and Ram. Ram will surely win; there is no doubt in this. Here, I can see everything myself, brother. I have great power of wisdom-vision.
essence: Clear seeing knows Ram's victory before the battle ends.
simple_meaning: The speaker says Ram is certain to win and claims he can see this clearly through wisdom.
insight: It shifts you from reacting to appearances to trusting clear discernment.
modern_relevance: You are in a room full of confident opinions, but one person quietly sees the larger pattern. Their calm certainty is not arrogance — it comes from seeing past the noise.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: मागा जल तेहिं दीन्ह कमंडल। कह कपि नहिं अघाउँ थोरें जल॥ सर मज्जन करि आतुर आवहु। दिच्छा देउँ ग्यान जेहिं पावहु ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी ने उससे जल माँगा, तो उसने कमण्डलु दे दिया। हनुमान् जी ने कहा- थोड़े जल से मैं तृप्त नहीं होने का। तब वह बोला- तालाब में स्नान करके तुरंत लौट आओ तो मैं तुम्हे दीक्षा दूँ, जिससे तुम ज्ञान प्राप्त करो ॥
english_translation: He asked for water, and the being gave him a water pot. Hanuman said he would not be satisfied with so little water. Then the being said, "Bathe in the lake and return quickly; I will give you initiation so you may gain knowledge."
essence: A false teacher offers knowledge as bait.
simple_meaning: The being offers Hanuman a chance to bathe and return for initiation into knowledge, but this is part of a trap, not a teaching for the reader.
insight: It trains you to pause before trusting guidance that arrives from a suspicious place.
modern_relevance: Someone on a crowded train platform offers you a too-helpful shortcut, a free scan, a quick sign-up. The surface kindness hides a trap, and Hanuman’s caution is the skill you need.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: सर पैठत कपि पद गहा मकरीं तब अकुलान। मारी सो धरि दिब्य तनु चली गगन चढ़ि जान ॥
translation: तालाब में प्रवेश करते ही एक मगरी ने अकुलाकर उसी समय हनुमान् जी का पैर पकड़ लिया। हनुमान् जी ने उसे मार डाला। तब वह दिव्य देह धारण करके विमान पर चढ़कर आकाश को चली ॥
english_translation: As Hanuman entered the lake, a crocodile seized his foot in panic. He killed her, and then she took a divine form and rose into the sky.
essence: The encounter matters, but its meaning is still unfolding.
simple_meaning: Hanuman enters the lake, is seized by a crocodile, kills it, and the crocodile reveals a divine form and ascends into the sky.
insight: It keeps attention on the event itself, not on a lesson that has not yet been spoken.
modern_relevance: A situation turns strange before you understand it: a small danger, a quick response, and only later the reason becomes clear.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कपि तव दरस भइउँ निष्पापा। मिटा तात मुनिबर कर सापा॥ मुनि न होइ यह निसिचर घोरा। मानहु सत्य बचन कपि मोरा ॥
translation: (उसने कहा-) हे वानर! मैं तुम्हारे दर्शन से पापरहित हो गई। हे तात! श्रेष्ठ मुनि का शाप मिट गया। हे कपि! यह मुनि नहीं है, घोर निशाचर है। मेरा वचन सत्य मानो ॥
english_translation: “By seeing you, O monkey, I have become free of stain. O noble one, the curse of the great sage has been removed. O monkey, this is not a sage; he is a terrible night-wanderer. Believe my words as true.”
essence: False holiness can be exposed by clear seeing.
simple_meaning: The woman says Hanuman's presence has freed her from a curse and revealed the truth: the person before him is not a sage but a dangerous demon.
insight: It shifts attention from appearance to discernment, showing that spiritual danger often hides behind respectable form.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who sounds wise, but something feels off. A single clear warning from a person who has seen more than you can save you from trusting the wrong face.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: अस कहि गई अपछरा जबहीं। निसिचर निकट गयउ कपि तबहीं॥ कह कपि मुनि गुरदछिना लेहू। पाछें हमहिं मंत्र तुम्ह देहू ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर ज्यों ही वह अप्सरा गई, त्यों ही हनुमान् जी निशाचर के पास गए। हनुमान् जी ने कहा- हे मुनि! पहले गुरुदक्षिणा ले लीजिए। पीछे आप मुझे मंत्र दीजिएगा ॥
english_translation: As soon as she left, Hanuman went to the demon. Hanuman said, "O sage, take your guru's fee first; after that, give me the mantra."
essence: Power stays clean when humility comes first.
simple_meaning: Hanuman shows humility and respect. Before asking for the mantra, he tells the sage to accept the teacher's fee first.
insight: It shifts you from grabbing for results to honoring the relationship that makes learning possible.
modern_relevance: You want a mentor's help, a recommendation, or a new skill, but you show up acting entitled. This verse reminds you that respect opens doors faster than pressure ever will.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिर लंगूर लपेटि पछारा। निज तनु प्रगटेसि मरती बारा॥ राम राम कहि छाड़ेसि प्राना। सुनि मन हरषि चलेउ हनुमाना ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी ने उसके सिर को पूँछ में लपेटकर उसे पछाड़ दिया। मरते समय उसने अपना (राक्षसी) शरीर प्रकट किया। उसने राम-राम कहकर प्राण छोड़े। यह (उसके मुँह से राम-राम का उच्चारण) सुनकर हनुमान् जी मन में हर्षित होकर चले ॥
english_translation: Hanuman wrapped his tail around her head and threw her down. As she was dying, she revealed her true demonic form. She gave up her life saying "Ram, Ram." Hearing this, Hanuman's heart filled with joy, and he moved on.
essence: Ram's name can surface even at the edge of death.
simple_meaning: Hanuman defeats a demon in disguise, and the demon dies calling on Ram. Hanuman feels pleased and continues his search.
insight: It shifts attention from the fight itself to the unexpected power of Ram's name.
modern_relevance: You finally see through someone's act, and the whole scene changes. Even in conflict, a single sincere word can cut through fear and leave you lighter.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखा सैल न औषध चीन्हा। सहसा कपि उपारि गिरि लीन्हा॥ गहि गिरि निसि नभ धावक भयऊ। अवधपुरी ऊपर कपि गयऊ ॥
translation: उन्होंने पर्वत को देखा, पर औषध न पहचान सके। तब हनुमान् जी ने एकदम से पर्वत को ही उखाड़ लिया। पर्वत लेकर हनुमान् जी रात ही में आकाश मार्ग से दौड़ चले और अयोध्यापुरी के ऊपर पहुँच गए ॥
english_translation: He could not identify the mountain or the herbs. So Hanuman suddenly lifted the whole mountain. Carrying it, the monkey raced through the night across the sky and reached above Ayodhya.
essence: Service does not wait for perfect certainty.
simple_meaning: Hanuman could not tell which mountain held the healing herbs, so he lifted the entire mountain and flew back across the sky.
insight: It shifts you from precision paralysis to decisive service when time matters more than perfect sorting.
modern_relevance: You are staring at a messy problem and cannot tell which detail matters most. Instead of freezing, you grab the whole thing, move fast, and keep the rescue going.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखा भरत बिसाल अति निसिचर मन अनुमानि। बिनु फर सायक मारेउ चाप श्रवन लगि तानि ॥
translation: भरतजी ने आकाश में अत्यंत विशाल स्वरूप देखा, तब मन में अनुमान किया कि यह कोई राक्षस है। उन्होंने कान तक धनुष को खींचकर बिना फल का एक बाण मारा ॥
english_translation: Bharat saw the huge form and thought it was a demon. He drew his bow to his ear and shot a harmless arrow.
essence: First impressions can trigger action before recognition arrives.
simple_meaning: Bharat sees a huge figure in the sky and mistakes it for a demon, so he quickly shoots an arrow without trying to kill.
insight: It shows how quickly the mind labels the unknown and how action can follow before understanding.
modern_relevance: You spot a stranger moving fast toward your house at dusk and tense up before you know who it is. The first reaction is often fear, not truth.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परेउ मुरुछि महि लागत सायक। सुमिरत राम राम रघुनायक॥ सुनि प्रिय बचन भरत तब धाए। कपि समीप अति आतुर आए ॥
translation: बाण लगते ही हनुमान् जी 'राम, राम, रघुपति' का उच्चारण करते हुए मूर्च्छित होकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े। प्रिय वचन (रामनाम) सुनकर भरतजी उठकर दौड़े और बड़ी उतावली से हनुमान् जी के पास आए ॥
english_translation: At the strike of the arrow, Hanuman fell unconscious to the ground, chanting, “Ram, Ram, Raghunath.” Hearing those beloved words, Bharat rushed forward and came anxiously to Hanuman’s side.
essence: Ram’s name wakes love faster than pain can speak.
simple_meaning: Hanuman collapses while repeating Ram’s name, and Bharat runs to him as soon as he hears those beloved words.
insight: It shows how devotion can turn a battlefield into a moment of tenderness and instant response.
modern_relevance: You hear your child whisper a name you love from the next room, and you drop everything. Some words pull the heart forward before the mind catches up.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिकल बिलोकि कीस उर लावा। जागत नहिं बहु भाँति जगावा॥ मुख मलीन मन भए दुखारी। कहत बचन भरि लोचन बारी ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी को व्याकुल देखकर उन्होंने हृदय से लगा लिया। बहुत तरह से जगाया, पर वे जागते न थे! तब भरतजी का मुख उदास हो गया। वे मन में बड़े दुःखी हुए और नेत्रों में (विषाद के आँसुओं का) जल भरकर ये वचन बोले- ॥
english_translation: Seeing Hanuman distressed, Bharata embraced him to his heart. He tried many ways to wake him, but he did not awaken. Bharata's face grew sorrowful. His mind filled with grief, and tears welled in his eyes as he spoke.
essence: Compassion holds first and speaks later.
simple_meaning: Bharata sees Hanuman in distress, holds him close, and becomes deeply saddened when Hanuman will not wake.
insight: It shifts attention from fixing someone quickly to staying present with their suffering.
modern_relevance: You sit beside a friend after bad news, trying every gentle word you know. Nothing changes their face, and your own throat tightens because their pain has become yours.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जेहिं बिधि राम बिमुख मोहि कीन्हा। तेहिं पुनि यह दारुन दुख दीन्हा॥ जौं मोरें मन बच अरु काया॥ प्रीति राम पद कमल अमाया ॥
translation: जिस विधाता ने मुझे श्री राम से विमुख किया, उसी ने फिर यह भयानक दुःख भी दिया। यदि मन, वचन और शरीर से श्री रामजी के चरणकमलों में मेरा निष्कपट प्रेम हो, ॥
english_translation: The same fate that turned me away from Ram has now given me this terrible sorrow. If my mind, speech, and body hold pure love for Ram's lotus feet,
essence: Pain can deepen the love that first seemed to fail.
simple_meaning: Bharat says the same power that kept him away from Ram has now brought this pain. He asks for pure love toward Ram with mind, speech, and body.
insight: It shifts the mind from blaming events to offering the whole self in devotion.
modern_relevance: You realize, halfway through a painful mistake, that the same choices that pulled you away from what matters are now teaching you what devotion costs. The wound becomes a reminder of what you still love.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: तौ कपि होउ बिगत श्रम सूला। जौं मो पर रघुपति अनुकूला॥ सुनत बचन उठि बैठ कपीसा। कहि जय जयति कोसलाधीसा ॥
translation: और यदि श्री रघुनाथजी मुझ पर प्रसन्न हों तो यह वानर थकावट और पीड़ा से रहित हो जाए। यह वचन सुनते ही कपिराज हनुमान् जी 'कोसलपति श्री रामचंद्रजी की जय हो, जय हो' कहते हुए उठ बैठे ॥
english_translation: If Lord Raghupati is pleased with me, may this monkey be freed from fatigue and pain. Hearing these words, Hanuman rose at once and cried, "Victory to the Lord of Kosala, victory!"
essence: Ram's favor restores what effort has spent.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says that if Ram is pleased with him, his fatigue and pain will disappear. Hearing this, he immediately sits up and praises Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from physical exhaustion to the renewing power of devotion and goodwill.
modern_relevance: You are drained after helping someone all day, and one kind message makes you sit up straighter. Being seen with love can restore energy that effort alone cannot.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: लीन्ह कपिहि उर लाइ पुलकित तनु लोचन सजल। प्रीति न हृदय समाइ सुमिरि राम रघुकुल तिलक ॥
translation: भरतजी ने वानर (हनुमान् जी) को हृदय से लगा लिया, उनका शरीर पुलकित हो गया और नेत्रों में (आनंद तथा प्रेम के आँसुओं का) जल भर आया। रघुकुलतिलक श्री रामचंद्रजी का स्मरण करके भरतजी के हृदय में प्रीति समाती न थी ॥
english_translation: Bharat embraced Hanuman to his heart. His body thrilled with joy, his eyes filled with tears. Remembering Ram, the jewel of Raghu's line, love could not fit inside Bharat's heart.
essence: True devotion makes the heart too full to contain itself.
simple_meaning: Bharat's love for Ram is so full that it spills over into tears, joy, and an embrace of Hanuman.
insight: It shifts attention from possession to remembrance: love becomes fuller the more vividly you hold Ram in mind.
modern_relevance: You finally hear from someone you have been missing for months, and your whole body reacts before you can speak. The message is not just information; it is presence returning.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तात कुसल कहु सुखनिधान की। सहित अनुज अरु मातु जानकी॥ लकपि सब चरित समास बखाने। भए दुखी मन महुँ पछिताने ॥
translation: (भरतजी बोले-) हे तात! छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण तथा माता जानकी सहित सुखनिधान श्री रामजी की कुशल कहो। वानर (हनुमान् जी) ने संक्षेप में सब कथा कही। सुनकर भरतजी दुःखी हुए और मन में पछताने लगे ॥
english_translation: “Tell me, father, about the well-being of Ram, the treasure of joy, along with Lakshman, Sita, and his younger brother.” Hanuman briefly told the whole story. Hearing it, Bharat became sorrowful and repented in his heart.
essence: Love makes distance unbearable, even before reunion arrives.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks after Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Hanuman gives a brief account, and Bharat is overcome with sorrow and regret.
insight: It shows how deep attachment makes even good news feel painful when separation has lasted too long.
modern_relevance: You finally get the update you were waiting for, and it lands heavier than you expected. Relief and regret arrive together.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: अहह दैव मैं कत जग जायउँ। प्रभु के एकहु काज न आयउँ॥ जानि कुअवसरु मन धरि धीरा। पुनि कपि सन बोले बलबीरा ॥
translation: हा दैव! मैं जगत् में क्यों जन्मा? प्रभु के एक भी काम न आया। फिर कुअवसर (विपरीत समय) जानकर मन में धीरज धरकर बलवीर भरतजी हनुमान् जी से बोले- ॥
english_translation: Alas! Why was I born in this world? I have not been useful in even one task of the Lord. Knowing the wrong moment, Bharata gathered his courage and spoke again to Hanuman.
essence: Your life feels empty when it serves no one you love.
simple_meaning: Bharat feels he has failed because he has not served Ram in any way. He steadies himself and speaks to Hanuman at the wrong moment, trying to make the next task happen quickly.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to useful action for what matters most.
modern_relevance: You finish a long day and realize you were busy, but not truly helpful to anyone who mattered. That quiet sting is Bharat's: the ache of wanting your effort to count for someone you love.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: तात गहरु होइहि तोहि जाता। काजु नसाइहि होत प्रभाता॥ चढ़ु मम सायक सैल समेता। पठवौं तोहि जहँ कृपानिकेता ॥
translation: हे तात! तुमको जाने में देर होगी और सबेरा होते ही काम बिगड़ जाएगा। (अतः) तुम पर्वत सहित मेरे बाण पर चढ़ जाओ, मैं तुमको वहाँ भेज दूँ जहाँ कृपा के धाम श्री रामजी हैं ॥
english_translation: O dear one, if you delay, it will be too late and the task will fail by dawn. Mount the mountain on my arrow, and I will send you to the abode of grace, where Ram dwells.
essence: True help moves before the moment is lost.
simple_meaning: Bharat tells Hanuman that there is no time to waste. He must go at once, and Bharat offers to send him quickly to Ram.
insight: It teaches you to act decisively when timing matters, and to help others without making them wait.
modern_relevance: You see the last train pulling away while your friend is still tying their bag. Sometimes care means cutting the hesitation short and getting them moving before the moment is lost.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: सुनि कपि मन उपजा अभिमाना। मोरें भार चलिहि किमि बाना॥ राम प्रभाव बिचारि बहोरी। बंदि चरन कह कपि कर जोरी ॥
translation: भरतजी की यह बात सुनकर (एक बार तो) हनुमान् जी के मन में अभिमान उत्पन्न हुआ कि मेरे बोझ से बाण कैसे चलेगा? (किन्तु) फिर श्री रामचंद्रजी के प्रभाव का विचार करके वे भरतजी के चरणों की वंदना करके हाथ जोड़कर बोले- ॥
english_translation: Hearing this, Hanuman felt pride arise in his mind: how could the arrow move with my weight on it? Then, remembering Ram's power, he bowed at Bharat's feet with folded hands.
essence: Pride fades when you remember the power behind your own strength.
simple_meaning: Hanuman briefly feels proud of his own strength, then remembers Ram's power and humbly bows to Bharat.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to reverence, so ability becomes service instead of ego.
modern_relevance: You almost brag about handling the whole project alone, then remember who trained you, supported you, and made the work possible. The chest loosens the moment gratitude returns.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तव प्रताप उर राखि प्रभु जैहउँ नाथ तुरंत। अस कहि आयसु पाइ पद बंदि चलेउ हनुमंत ॥
translation: हे नाथ! हे प्रभो! मैं आपका प्रताप हृदय में रखकर तुरंत चला जाऊँगा। ऐसा कहकर आज्ञा पाकर और भरतजी के चरणों की वंदना करके हनुमान् जी चले ॥
english_translation: O Lord, I will keep your glory in my heart and go at once. Saying this, and receiving permission, Hanuman bowed at Bharata's feet and departed.
essence: Humility lets devotion move without delay.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says he will carry Bharata's greatness in his heart and leave immediately, after bowing and receiving permission.
insight: It teaches you to let reverence dissolve pride and turn praise into action.
modern_relevance: You get praised in the meeting, but you don't linger on it. You thank everyone, do the respectful thing, and get back to the task before the moment turns into ego.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: भरत बाहु बल सील गुन प्रभु पद प्रीति अपार। मन महुँ जात सराहत पुनि पुनि पवनकुमार ॥
translation: भरतजी के बाहुबल, शील (सुंदर स्वभाव), गुण और प्रभु के चरणों में अपार प्रेम की मन ही मन बारंबार सराहना करते हुए मारुति श्री हनुमान् जी चले जा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Hanuman walked on, silently praising Bharat’s strength, character, virtues, and his immense love for the Lord’s feet again and again.
essence: Devotion keeps moving while the mind keeps bowing.
simple_meaning: Hanuman keeps going while admiring Bharat’s strength, good character, virtues, and deep love for Ram.
insight: It shows how a devoted mind can stay active while quietly recognising virtue in another person.
modern_relevance: You leave a difficult conversation and keep replaying the one line that revealed someone’s character. Even while moving forward, your mind keeps bowing to what is noble.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उहाँ राम लछिमनहि निहारी। बोले बचन मनुज अनुसारी॥ अर्ध राति गइ कपि नहिं आयउ। राम उठाइ अनुज उर लायउ ॥
translation: वहाँ लक्ष्मणजी को देखकर श्री रामजी साधारण मनुष्यों के अनुसार (समान) वचन बोले- आधी रात बीत चुकी है, हनुमान् नहीं आए। यह कहकर श्री रामजी ने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी को उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
english_translation: Seeing Lakshman there, Ram spoke as an ordinary human would. "Midnight has passed and Hanuman has not come yet." Saying this, Ram lifted his younger brother and held him to his chest.
essence: Love stays tender even in the middle of worry.
simple_meaning: Ram speaks like an ordinary person and hugs Lakshman while waiting for Hanuman to return.
insight: It shifts attention from heroic distance to intimate care under pressure.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone at 1:30 a.m., waiting for a message that should have come hours ago. In that restless silence, you want to hold someone close and pretend you are not afraid.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकहु न दुखित देखि मोहि काउ। बंधु सदा तव मृदुल सुभाऊ॥ मम हित लागि तजेहु पितु माता। सहेहु बिपिन हिम आतप बाता ॥
translation: (और बोले-) हे भाई! तुम मुझे कभी दुःखी नहीं देख सकते थे। तुम्हारा स्वभाव सदा से ही कोमल था। मेरे हित के लिए तुमने माता-पिता को भी छोड़ दिया और वन में जाड़ा, गरमी और हवा सब सहन किया ॥
english_translation: Brother, you could never bear to see me in pain. Your nature has always been gentle. For my sake, you left your mother and father and endured the forest's cold, heat, and wind.
essence: Love becomes visible when someone endures hardship for your sake.
simple_meaning: Ram praises Lakshman’s tender nature and remembers how Lakshman left his parents and endured the forest’s hardships for Ram’s sake.
insight: It shifts attention from grand gestures to the quiet endurance that proves devotion.
modern_relevance: You stayed up all night with a sibling after a breakup, then went to work exhausted. No one saw the cost, but the love was real. Ram sees that kind of sacrifice completely.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सो अनुराग कहाँ अब भाई। उठहु न सुनि मम बच बिकलाई॥ जौं जनतेउँ बन बंधु बिछोहू। पिता बचन मनतेउँ नहिं ओहू ॥
translation: हे भाई! वह प्रेम अब कहाँ है? मेरे व्याकुलतापूर्वक वचन सुनकर उठते क्यों नहीं? यदि मैं जानता कि वन में भाई का विछोह होगा तो मैं पिता का वचन (जिसका मानना मेरे लिए परम कर्तव्य था) उसे भी न मानता ॥
english_translation: O brother, where is that love now? Why do you not rise at my distressed words? If I had known that exile would mean separation from my brother, I would not have kept my father's word.
essence: Duty can be obeyed and still break your heart.
simple_meaning: Ram grieves Lakshman’s silence and says he would not have obeyed his father if he had known exile would separate him from his brother.
insight: It shows that even the noblest duty can be pierced by human attachment and grief.
modern_relevance: You take a call from the hospital and suddenly every plan feels small. In that moment, duty, family, and love collide exactly the way Ram feels it here.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुत बित नारि भवन परिवारा। होहिं जाहिं जग बारहिं बारा॥ अस बिचारि जियँ जागहु ताता। मिलइ न जगत सहोदर भ्राता ॥
translation: पुत्र, धन, स्त्री, घर और परिवार- ये जगत् में बार-बार होते और जाते हैं, परन्तु जगत् में सहोदर भाई बार-बार नहीं मिलता। हृदय में ऐसा विचार कर हे तात! जागो ॥
english_translation: Children, wealth, wife, house, and family come and go again and again in the world, but a real brother is not found again. Thinking this in your heart, wake up, dear one!
essence: What is replaceable should not outrank what is rare.
simple_meaning: Worldly things like children, wealth, wife, house, and family keep coming and going. A true brother is hard to find, so remember what really matters.
insight: It shifts attention from replaceable comforts to the few bonds that deserve your deepest care.
modern_relevance: You move apartments, change jobs, and replace possessions without much thought. Then one loyal friend shows up when everything falls apart, and you realize how rare real kinship is.
speaker: Lakshman

verse_text: जथा पंख बिनु खग अति दीना। मनि बिनु फनि करिबर कर हीना॥ अस मम जिवन बंधु बिनु तोही। जौं जड़ दैव जिआवै मोही ॥
translation: जैसे पंख बिना पक्षी, मणि बिना सर्प और सूँड बिना श्रेष्ठ हाथी अत्यंत दीन हो जाते हैं, हे भाई! यदि कहीं जड़ दैव मुझे जीवित रखे तो तुम्हारे बिना मेरा जीवन भी ऐसा ही होगा ॥
english_translation: Like a bird without wings, a serpent without a jewel, and a great elephant without its trunk, my life without you, brother, would be the same—if fate somehow kept me alive.
essence: Love can make absence feel like losing your own limbs.
simple_meaning: Ram says that life without Lakshman would be as helpless as a bird without wings or an elephant without its trunk.
insight: It shifts attention from possession to interdependence: some relationships are not additions, but supports your life leans on.
modern_relevance: You look at the empty seat beside you after the hospital visit, the road trip, or the long night of crisis. Some people are not just company; they are part of how you stay upright.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जैहउँ अवध कौन मुहु लाई। नारि हेतु प्रिय भाई गँवाई॥ बरु अपजस सहतेउँ जग माहीं। नारि हानि बिसेष छति नाहीं ॥
translation: स्त्री के लिए प्यारे भाई को खोकर, मैं कौन सा मुँह लेकर अवध जाऊँगा? मैं जगत् में बदनामी भले ही सह लेता (कि राम में कुछ भी वीरता नहीं है जो स्त्री को खो बैठे)। स्त्री की हानि से (इस हानि को देखते) कोई विशेष क्षति नहीं थी ॥
english_translation: How can I return to Ayodhya and face anyone? I have lost my dear brother for a woman. I would rather bear disgrace in the world; the loss of a woman is not a special loss compared to this.
essence: Some losses wound deeper than shame ever could.
simple_meaning: Ram says he could bear public shame more easily than the pain of losing his brother for a woman.
insight: It shifts attention from public image to the cost of breaking a sacred relationship.
modern_relevance: You let someone down who trusted you completely, and the embarrassment sits in your chest all day. What hurts more is not being judged — it is knowing you failed the bond that mattered most.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: अब अपलोकु सोकु सुत तोरा। सहिहि निठुर कठोर उर मोरा॥ निज जननी के एक कुमारा। तात तासु तुम्ह प्रान अधारा ॥
translation: अब तो हे पुत्र! मेरे निष्ठुर और कठोर हृदय यह अपयश और तुम्हारा शोक दोनों ही सहन करेगा। हे तात! तुम अपनी माता के एक ही पुत्र और उसके प्राणाधार हो ॥
english_translation: Now this disgrace and your grief, my hard and cruel heart, will endure. Son, you are your mother’s only child, and the support of her life.
essence: Love can be spoken as duty while hiding deep harm.
simple_meaning: Kaikeyi tells her son that her heart will bear the shame and his sorrow, and reminds him that he is his mother’s only child and life-support.
insight: It exposes how affection can be used to pressure someone into carrying another person’s burden.
modern_relevance: A mother says, “I only want what’s best for you,” but the room already feels poisoned. The pressure to protect family can become a way of controlling it.
speaker: Kaikeyi

verse_text: सौंपेसि मोहि तुम्हहि गहि पानी। सब बिधि सुखद परम हित जानी॥ उतरु काह दैहउँ तेहि जाई। उठि किन मोहि सिखावहु भाई ॥
translation: सब प्रकार से सुख देने वाला और परम हितकारी जानकर उन्होंने तुम्हें हाथ पकड़कर मुझे सौंपा था। मैं अब जाकर उन्हें क्या उत्तर दूँगा? हे भाई! तुम उठकर मुझे सिखाते (समझाते) क्यों नहीं? ॥
english_translation: He entrusted you to me, holding your hand, knowing you were the source of every kind of happiness and supreme good. What answer will I give him now? Brother, why don't you rise and teach me?
essence: Trust becomes unbearable when you cannot honor it.
simple_meaning: The speaker says someone was handed over as a source of happiness and good, and now he cannot face the one who trusted him.
insight: It shifts the mind from pride to accountability, showing how trust creates moral weight.
modern_relevance: You promised to look after a younger brother, a teammate, or a friend, and then let them down. The shame is not just failure — it is having to face the person who trusted you.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: बहु बिधि सोचत सोच बिमोचन। स्रवत सलिल राजिव दल लोचन॥ उमा एक अखंड रघुराई। नर गति भगत कृपाल देखाई ॥
translation: सोच से छुड़ाने वाले श्री रामजी बहुत प्रकार से सोच कर रहे हैं। उनके कमल की पंखुड़ी के समान नेत्रों से (विषाद के आँसुओं का) जल बह रहा है। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! श्री रघुनाथजी एक (अद्वितीय) और अखंड (वियोगरहित) हैं। भक्तों पर कृपा करने वाले भगवान् ने (लीला करके) मनुष्य की दशा दिखलाई है ॥
english_translation: Ram, who frees beings from sorrow, is now sorrowing in many ways. Tears flow from his lotus-petal eyes. Uma, the one and undivided Raghu lord has shown the human condition to his devotees out of compassion.
essence: Compassion can wear the face of grief.
simple_meaning: Ram, who removes sorrow, is shown here weeping like a human being. Shiva explains that this is Ram's compassion at work: he reveals the human condition to help devotees.
insight: It shifts devotion from distant reverence to intimate nearness: the sacred is willing to enter human pain.
modern_relevance: You sit beside someone in the hospital and cannot fix anything. You only stay, listen, and let your eyes fill too. That shared grief is not failure; it is love entering human form.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: प्रभु प्रलाप सुनि कान बिकल भए बानर निकर। आइ गयउ हनुमान जिमि करुना महँ बीर रस ॥
translation: प्रभु के (लीला के लिए किए गए) प्रलाप को कानों से सुनकर वानरों के समूह व्याकुल हो गए। (इतने में ही) हनुमान् जी आ गए, जैसे करुणरस (के प्रसंग) में वीर रस (का प्रसंग) आ गया हो ॥
english_translation: Hearing the Lord's lament, the monkeys grew restless. Then Hanuman arrived, like courage entering a scene of sorrow.
essence: Strength can enter sorrow without breaking its tenderness.
simple_meaning: The monkeys are shaken by Ram's grief, and Hanuman arrives at exactly the right moment, bringing strength into a scene of sorrow.
insight: It shifts attention from the grief itself to the force that can answer it.
modern_relevance: You are sitting beside a friend who has just broken down, and then the one person who knows what to do walks in. Relief can feel like that.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरषि राम भेंटेउ हनुमाना। अति कृतग्य प्रभु परम सुजाना॥ तुरत बैद तब कीन्ह उपाई। उठि बैठे लछिमन हरषाई ॥
translation: श्री रामजी हर्षित होकर हनुमान् जी से गले मिले। प्रभु परम सुजान (चतुर) और अत्यंत ही कृतज्ञ हैं। तब वैद्य (सुषेण) ने तुरंत उपाय किया, (जिससे) लक्ष्मणजी हर्षित होकर उठ बैठे ॥
english_translation: Ram joyfully embraced Hanuman. The Lord is deeply grateful and profoundly wise. Then the physician quickly applied his remedy, and Lakshman rose up, delighted.
essence: Devotion is met with embrace, gratitude, and healing.
simple_meaning: Ram welcomes Hanuman with joy, shows deep gratitude, and Lakshman is healed and sits up again.
insight: It shows that sincere service is answered by recognition, and that healing begins in grateful connection.
modern_relevance: You finally hear back from the friend who showed up when everything was falling apart. The relief is not just in the help — it is in being seen and treasured.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हृदयँ लाइ प्रभु भेंटेउ भ्राता। हरषे सकल भालु कपि ब्राता॥ कपि पुनि बैद तहाँ पहुँचावा। जेहि बिधि तबहिं ताहि लइ आवा ॥
translation: प्रभु भाई को हृदय से लगाकर मिले। भालू और वानरों के समूह सब हर्षित हो गए। फिर हनुमान् जी ने वैद्य को उसी प्रकार वहाँ पहुँचा दिया, जिस प्रकार वे उस बार (पहले) उसे ले आए थे ॥
english_translation: Ram embraced his brother to his heart. The bears and monkeys were all delighted. Then Hanuman carried the physician back there again, just as he had brought him before.
essence: Love rejoices, and service leaves quietly once its work is done.
simple_meaning: Ram warmly embraces Lakshman, and the whole monkey and bear army rejoices. Hanuman then brings the physician back exactly as before.
insight: It closes the healing scene by showing gratitude, relief, and swift selfless service.
modern_relevance: After a long night in the emergency room, your sibling finally opens their eyes. The relief is so complete that even the smallest next task feels light.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: यह बृत्तांत दसानन सुनेऊ। अति बिषाद पुनि पुनि सिर धुनेऊ॥ ब्याकुल कुंभकरन पहिं आवा। बिबिध जतन करि ताहि जगावा ॥
translation: यह समाचार जब रावण ने सुना, तब उसने अत्यंत विषाद से बार-बार सिर पीटा। वह व्याकुल होकर कुंभकर्ण के पास गया और बहुत से उपाय करके उसने उसको जगाया ॥
english_translation: When Ravana heard this news, he was filled with grief and kept striking his head again and again. Agitated, he went to Kumbhakarna and woke him with many efforts.
essence: Fear makes even the powerful reach for help in disorder.
simple_meaning: Ravana hears the bad news, panics, and rushes to wake Kumbhakarna with repeated efforts.
insight: It shows how fear scatters judgment and pushes you into desperate action.
modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with the message you were dreading. You pace the room, then call the one person you think can still fix it. That is Ravana's mind here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जागा निसिचर देखिअ कैसा। मानहुँ कालु देह धरि बैसा॥ कुंभकरन बूझा कहु भाई। काहे तव मुख रहे सुखाई ॥
translation: कुंभकर्ण जगा (उठ बैठा) वह कैसा दिखाई देता है मानो स्वयं काल ही शरीर धारण करके बैठा हो। कुंभकर्ण ने पूछा- हे भाई! कहो तो, तुम्हारे मुख सूख क्यों रहे हैं? ॥
english_translation: What a sight the demon was when he woke up, as if Time itself had taken a body and sat there. Kumbhakarna asked, "Brother, tell me—why does your face look so dry and weary?"
essence: Delayed help arrives after the damage has already deepened.
simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna wakes up looking terrifying, like death itself in a body, and asks Ravana why he looks so drained.
insight: It frames the crisis as already advanced, so the next verse can reveal the full disaster.
modern_relevance: You finally reach the friend who ignored every warning, and now they look shocked that everything has collapsed. The damage was already done before they asked for help.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कथा कही सब तेहिं अभिमानी। जेहि प्रकार सीता हरि आनी॥ तात कपिन्ह सब निसिचर मारे। महा महा जोधा संघारे ॥
translation: उस अभिमानी (रावण) ने उससे जिस प्रकार से वह सीता को हर लाया था (तब से अब तक की) सारी कथा कही। (फिर कहा-) हे तात! वानरों ने सब राक्षस मार डाले। बड़े-बड़े योद्धाओं का भी संहार कर डाला ॥
english_translation: That arrogant one told him the whole story, including how he had carried off Sita. Then he said, "Brother, the monkeys have killed all the demons. They have slain even the greatest warriors."
essence: Pride speaks loudly, even as its world collapses.
simple_meaning: Ravana recounts how he abducted Sita and admits that the monkey army has destroyed his warriors.
insight: It shows how ego keeps narrating its own story even when reality has already overturned it.
modern_relevance: You keep explaining how things went wrong after the loss is already obvious. The longer you defend your pride, the more exposed you feel.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: दुर्मुख सुररिपु मनुज अहारी। भट अतिकाय अकंपन भारी॥ अपर महोदर आदिक बीरा। परे समर महि सब रनधीरा ॥
translation: दुर्मुख, देवशत्रु (देवान्तक), मनुष्य भक्षक (नरान्तक), भारी योद्धा अतिकाय और अकम्पन तथा महोदर आदि दूसरे सभी रणधीर वीर रणभूमि में मारे गए ॥
english_translation: Dumukha, the enemy of the radiant beings, Narantaka the man-eater, the mighty warrior Atikaya and Akampana, along with Mahodara and other brave fighters, all fell on the battlefield.
essence: Great strength means little when it is already falling.
simple_meaning: Several of Ravana's great warriors have been killed in battle.
insight: It frames the war as a collapse of force, not a heroic advance.
modern_relevance: A team that once looked unbeatable starts losing key people one by one. The confidence was loud, but the damage is real.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनि दसकंधर बचन तब कुंभकरन बिलखान। जगदंबा हरि आनि अब सठ चाहत कल्यान ॥
translation: तब रावण के वचन सुनकर कुंभकर्ण बिलखकर (दुःखी होकर) बोला- अरे मूर्ख! जगज्जननी जानकी को हर लाकर अब कल्याण चाहता है? ॥
english_translation: Hearing Ravana's words, Kumbhakarna lamented, "Fool! You brought away the Mother of the world, and now you still want well-being?"
essence: Pride that harms others cannot also secure your good.
simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna rebukes Ravana for abducting Sita and still hoping for good outcomes. He sees that harmful action and real well-being cannot coexist.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-justifying pride to honest recognition of consequence.
modern_relevance: You send a harsh message at midnight, then keep checking your phone for a warm reply. Part of you already knows the damage is done, and pretending otherwise only deepens it.
speaker: Kumbhakarna

verse_text: भल न कीन्ह तैं निसिचर नाहा। अब मोहि आइ जगाएहि काहा॥ अजहूँ तात त्यागि अभिमाना। भजहु राम होइहि कल्याना ॥
translation: हे राक्षसराज! तूने अच्छा नहीं किया। अब आकर मुझे क्यों जगाया? हे तात! अब भी अभिमान छोड़कर श्री रामजी को भजो तो कल्याण होगा ॥
english_translation: O king of the demons, you did not do well. Why have you come to wake me now? Even now, brother, give up pride and worship Ram; you will find welfare.
essence: Pride is not the last word; turning to Ram still is.
simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna rebukes Ravana for waking him and tells him that even now, if he gives up pride and turns to Ram, things can still improve.
insight: It shifts the mind from defending ego to choosing repair before it's too late.
modern_relevance: You get the late-night call after a disastrous decision, and the person on the line still won't admit they were wrong. This verse cuts through that stubbornness: the first healing step is dropping pride.
speaker: Kumbhakarna

verse_text: हैं दससीस मनुज रघुनायक। जाके हनूमान से पायक॥ अहह बंधु तैं कीन्हि खोटाई। प्रथमहिं मोहि न सुनाएहि आई ॥
translation: हे रावण! जिनके हनुमान् सरीखे सेवक हैं, वे श्री रघुनाथजी क्या मनुष्य हैं? हाय भाई! तूने बुरा किया, जो पहले ही आकर मुझे यह हाल नहीं सुनाया ॥
english_translation: O Ravana, are those whose servant is Hanuman truly human? Alas, brother, you did wrong by not telling me this first.
essence: The servant reveals the greatness of the one served.
simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna realises Ram cannot be ordinary if Hanuman serves him. He blames Ravana for not telling him earlier, because this changes everything.
insight: It shifts attention from status to the quality of devotion a person draws out in others.
modern_relevance: You meet someone’s longtime assistant and immediately understand the person better. The way people serve them, speak of them, and stay loyal reveals more than their title ever could.
speaker: Kumbhakarna

verse_text: कीन्हेहु प्रभु बिरोध तेहि देवक। सिव बिरंचि सुर जाके सेवक॥ नारद मुनि मोहि ग्यान जो कहा। कहतेउँ तोहि समय निरबाहा ॥
translation: हे स्वामी! तुमने उस परम देवता का विरोध किया, जिसके शिव, ब्रह्मा आदि देवता सेवक हैं। नारद मुनि ने मुझे जो ज्ञान कहा था, वह मैं तुझसे कहता, पर अब तो समय जाता रहा ॥
english_translation: O Lord, you opposed that supreme being whom Shiva, Brahma, and the radiant beings serve. Narada the sage told me this wisdom, and I would have told it to you, but now the proper time has passed.
essence: Pride can make wisdom arrive too late.
simple_meaning: Mandodari tells Ravana that he has opposed the supreme being served by Shiva, Brahma, and the radiant beings. She says Narada had already warned her of this, but now it is too late.
insight: It shifts the mind from defensive pride to belated recognition of a truth already seen by others.
modern_relevance: You finally read the warning after the contract is signed. The pattern was obvious, but pride kept you from listening until the cost was already real.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: अब भरि अंक भेंटु मोहि भाई। लोचन सुफल करौं मैं जाई॥ स्याम गात सरसीरुह लोचन। देखौं जाइ ताप त्रय मोचन ॥
translation: हे भाई! अब तो (अन्तिम बार) अँकवार भरकर मुझसे मिल ले। मैं जाकर अपने नेत्र सफल करूँ। तीनों तापों को छुड़ाने वाले श्याम शरीर, कमल नेत्र श्री रामजी के जाकर दर्शन करूँ ॥
english_translation: “Brother, now embrace me fully one last time. I will go and make my eyes fruitful by seeing the dark-bodied Ram with lotus eyes, the remover of the three kinds of suffering.”
essence: Even the fallen can find fulfillment in one last sight of Ram.
simple_meaning: Ravana asks his brother for one last embrace and says he will go behold Ram, whose sight brings the eyes true fulfillment and frees one from suffering.
insight: It shifts the mind from pride and possession to longing for direct vision of the divine.
modern_relevance: At a hospital bedside, someone who spent years chasing power suddenly asks to see the person they ignored. The last thing the heart wants is not victory, but a final clear sight.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: राम रूप गुन सुमिरत मगन भयउ छन एक। रावन मागेउ कोटि घट मद अरु महिष अनेक ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी के रूप और गुणों को स्मरण करके वह एक क्षण के लिए प्रेम में मग्न हो गया। फिर रावण से करोड़ों घड़े मदिरा और अनेकों भैंसे मँगवाए ॥
english_translation: Remembering Ram's form and virtues, he became absorbed for a moment. Then he asked Ravana for millions of jars of liquor and many buffaloes.
essence: A glimpse of Ram vanishes when appetite takes over.
simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna briefly remembers Ram with devotion, then asks Ravana for huge amounts of liquor and many buffaloes.
insight: It shows how quickly higher feeling can be swallowed by old craving when discipline is absent.
modern_relevance: You have one clear moment of conscience at midnight, then you open the fridge, the feed, or the bottle again. A brief insight is not the same as a changed life.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: महिषखाइ करि मदिरा पाना। गर्जा बज्राघात समाना॥ कुंभकरन दुर्मद रन रंगा। चला दुर्ग तजि सेन न संगा ॥
translation: भैंसे खाकर और मदिरा पीकर वह वज्रघात (बिजली गिरने) के समान गरजा। मद से चूर रण के उत्साह से पूर्ण कुंभकर्ण किला छोड़कर चला। सेना भी साथ नहीं ली ॥
english_translation: Feasting on buffalo meat and drinking liquor, he roared like a thunderbolt. Drunk with pride, Kumbhakarna left the fortress and marched out in battle fury without even taking an army.
essence: Pride turns strength into reckless noise.
simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna, drunk and furious, storms out of the fortress alone, ready for battle.
insight: It shows how pride and intoxication push action into blind force.
modern_relevance: A person slams the car door after an argument and storms back inside, too angry to think. The body is moving fast, but judgment has already gone missing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि बिभीषनु आगें आयउ। परेउ चरन निज नाम सुनायउ॥ अनुज उठाइ हृदयँ तेहि लायो। रघुपति भक्त जानि मन भायो ॥
translation: उसे देखकर विभीषण आगे आए और उसके चरणों पर गिरकर अपना नाम सुनाया। छोटे भाई को उठाकर उसने हृदय से लगा लिया और श्री रघुनाथजी का भक्त जानकर वे उसके मन को प्रिय लगे ॥
english_translation: Seeing Vibhishana come forward, he fell at his feet and told his name. He lifted his younger brother and held him to his heart; knowing him to be a devotee of Raghupati, he was pleased in his mind.
essence: Ram receives the one who comes bowed, not the one who comes proud.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana approaches with humility, and Ram welcomes him warmly because he recognizes true devotion.
insight: It shifts attention from outer allegiance to the inward quality of devotion and humility.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after making a hard choice that cost you approval. Someone who sees your sincerity doesn’t interrogate your past — they simply make space for you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तात लात रावन मोहि मारा। कहत परम हित मंत्र बिचारा॥ तेहिं गलानि रघुपति पहिं आयउँ। देखि दीन प्रभु के मन भायउँ ॥
translation: (विभीषण ने कहा-) हे तात! परम हितकर सलाह एवं विचार करने पर रावण ने मुझे लात मारी। उसी ग्लानि के मारे मैं श्री रघुनाथजी के पास चला आया। दीन देखकर प्रभु के मन को मैं (बहुत) प्रिय लगा ॥
english_translation: “Dear brother, Ravana kicked me after hearing my well-meaning counsel. Shamed by that, I came to Lord Raghunath. Seeing the humble, I became dear to the Lord’s mind.”
essence: Humility, not status, is what draws Ram close.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana says Ravana insulted him after ignoring good advice, so he came to Ram in shame. Ram welcomes the humble and values their surrender.
insight: It shifts you from protecting ego to approaching with honesty and humility.
modern_relevance: You finally admit you were wrong in a family argument, and the room goes quiet. The apology does not weaken you; it makes real connection possible.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: सुनु भयउ कालबस रावन। सो कि मान अब परम सिखावन॥ धन्य धन्य तैं धन्य विभीषन। भयहु तात निसिचर कुल भूषन ॥
translation: (कुंभकर्ण ने कहा-) हे पुत्र! सुन, रावण तो काल के वश हो गया है (उसके सिर पर मृत्यु नाच रही है)। वह क्या अब उत्तम शिक्षा मान सकता है? हे विभीषण! तू धन्य है, धन्य है। हे तात! तू राक्षस कुल का भूषण हो गया ॥
english_translation: Listen, Ravana has fallen under the power of death. Can he still accept the highest teaching now? Blessed, blessed are you, Vibhishana. You have become the ornament of the demon line, dear son.
essence: Truth honors you even when others are past saving.
simple_meaning: Ravana is already beyond instruction because death has taken hold of him. Vibhishana, by choosing what is right, brings honor to his entire lineage.
insight: It shifts you from trying to fix the unresponsive to honoring the clear choice you can still make.
modern_relevance: You finally tell a friend the hard truth, but they are already too deep in denial to hear it. Still, your honesty matters — sometimes it is the only thing that keeps your own name clean.
speaker: Kumbhakarna

verse_text: बंधु बंस तैं कीन्ह उजागर। भजेहु राम सोभा सुख सागर ॥
translation: हे भाई! तूने अपने कुल को दैदीप्यमान कर दिया, जो शोभा और सुख के समुद्र श्री रामजी को भजा ॥
english_translation: You have made your family shine brightly by worshipping Ram, the ocean of beauty and joy.
essence: Turning to Ram makes your whole lineage radiant.
simple_meaning: Worshipping Ram brings honor not just to you, but to your whole family line.
insight: It shifts pride from bloodline status to moral alignment with Ram.
modern_relevance: You choose honesty over protecting a family secret, and the room goes quiet. Later, people may not praise the choice, but your name carries a different weight because of it.
speaker: Kumbhakarna

verse_text: बचन कर्म मन कपट तजि भजेहु राम रनधीर। जाहु न निज पर सूझ मोहि भयउँ कालबस बीर ॥
translation: मन, वचन और कर्म से कपट छोड़कर रणधीर श्री रामजी का भजन करना। हे भाई! मैं काल (मृत्यु) के वश हो गया हूँ, मुझे अपना-पराया नहीं सूझता, इसलिए अब तुम जाओ ॥
english_translation: Leave deceit in mind, speech, and action, and worship courageous Ram. Brother, I have fallen under death’s power; I can no longer tell friend from foe, so now you must go.
essence: Deceit falls away when death is near; only fearless devotion remains.
simple_meaning: Speak and act without deceit, and turn to Ram with courage. Kumbhakarna says he is now under death’s control and can no longer distinguish friend from foe.
insight: It shifts the mind from divided loyalty to clean, truthful alignment with Ram.
modern_relevance: A family argument has gone too far, and everyone is speaking from hurt instead of honesty. In that moment, the only useful move is to drop the mask and face what is real.
speaker: Kumbhakarna

verse_text: बंधु बचन सुनि चला बिभीषन। आयउ जहँ त्रैलोक बिभूषन॥ नाथ भूधराकार सरीरा। कुंभकरन आवत रनधीरा ॥॥
translation: भाई के वचन सुनकर विभीषण लौट गए और वहाँ आए, जहाँ त्रिलोकी के भूषण श्री रामजी थे। (विभीषण ने कहा-) हे नाथ! पर्वत के समान (विशाल) देह वाला रणधीर कुंभकर्ण आ रहा है ॥
english_translation: Hearing his brother's words, Vibhishana went back and came to where Ram, the ornament of the three worlds, was. He said, "Lord, the mountain-like body of the brave Kumbhakarna is coming into battle."
essence: The battle is about to widen, and Vibhishana sees it first.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana returns to Ram and warns that Kumbhakarna is coming to fight, describing his huge mountain-like body.
insight: It shifts attention from the warning itself to the approaching action that follows.
modern_relevance: You spot the storm before it hits: a message arrives, the room tightens, and everyone braces for what is coming next.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एतना कपिन्ह सुना जब काना। किलकिलाइ धाए बलवाना॥ लिए उठाइ बिटप अरु भूधर। कटकटाइ डारहिं ता ऊपर ॥
translation: वानरों ने जब कानों से इतना सुना, तब वे बलवान् किलकिलाकर (हर्षध्वनि करके) दौड़े। वृक्ष और पर्वत (उखाड़कर) उठा लिए और (क्रोध से) दाँत कटकटाकर उन्हें उसके ऊपर डालने लगे ॥
english_translation: When the monkeys heard this, the mighty ones shouted in delight and rushed forward. They lifted trees and mountains and, grinding their teeth in anger, hurled them down upon him.
essence: Battle energy becomes unstoppable once the army hears the signal.
simple_meaning: The monkeys hear the news, roar with excitement, and rush into battle, tearing up trees and mountains to throw at the enemy.
insight: It shifts the scene from tension to full-force action, showing collective momentum before impact.
modern_relevance: A crowd hears the final call and suddenly moves as one — phones down, chairs pushed back, everyone rushing into the same urgent task.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोटि कोटि गिरि सिखर प्रहारा। करहिं भालु कपि एक एक बारा॥ मुर् यो न मनु तनु टर् यो न टार् यो। जिमि गज अर्क फलनि को मार् यो ॥
translation: रीछ-वानर एक-एक बार में ही करोड़ों पहाड़ों के शिखरों से उस पर प्रहार करते हैं, परन्तु इससे न तो उसका मन ही मुड़ा (विचलित हुआ) और न शरीर ही टाले टला, जैसे मदार के फलों की मार से हाथी पर कुछ भी असर नहीं होता! ॥
english_translation: The bears and monkeys strike him again and again with peaks of mountains, but his mind does not turn and his body does not yield, just as an elephant is unaffected by strikes from madar fruits.
essence: Force can fail completely against a fixed mind.
simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears keep attacking, but the enemy does not flinch. He stays unmoved, like an elephant ignoring weak blows.
insight: It shows that not every obstacle yields to pressure; some must be met differently.
modern_relevance: You keep explaining, pushing, and proving your point in a meeting, but the other person sits there unchanged. Sometimes brute force only reveals how fixed someone already is.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब मारुतसुत मुठिका हन्यो। परयो धरनि ब्याकुल सिर धुन्यो॥ पुनि उठि तेहिं मारेउ हनुमंता। घुर्मित भूतल परेउ तुरंता ॥
translation: तब हनुमान् जी ने उसे एक घूँसा मारा, जिससे वह व्याकुल होकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा और सिर पीटने लगा। फिर उसने उठकर हनुमान् जी को मारा। वे चक्कर खाकर तुरंत ही पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े ॥
english_translation: Then Hanuman struck him with his fist, and he fell to the ground, shaken and clutching his head. Rising again, he struck Hanuman, and Hanuman reeled and fell at once.
essence: The fight keeps surging back and forth.
simple_meaning: Hanuman and the enemy warrior trade blows in fierce combat, each knocking the other down in turn.
insight: It shows a combat beat, not a transferable principle.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि नल नीलहि अवनि पछारेसि। जहँ तहँ पटकि पटकि भट डारेसि॥ चली बलीमुख सेन पराई। अति भय त्रसित न कोउ समुहाई ॥
translation: फिर उसने नल-नील को पृथ्वी पर पछाड़ दिया और दूसरे योद्धाओं को भी जहाँ-तहाँ पटककर डाल दिया। वानर सेना भाग चली। सब अत्यंत भयभीत हो गए, कोई सामने नहीं आता ॥
english_translation: Then he threw Nala and Neela to the ground and hurled warriors here and there. The monkey army fled. Everyone was terrified; no one dared face him.
essence: Overwhelming force can scatter even a brave army.
simple_meaning: The enemy warrior overpowers Nala, Neela, and the monkey army, driving them into fear and retreat.
insight: It shows the battle turning through sheer force, before the next counterattack changes the tide.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अंगदादि कपि मुरुछित करि समेत सुग्रीव। काँख दाबि कपिराज कहुँ चला अमित बल सींव ॥
translation: सुग्रीव समेत अंगदादि वानरों को मूर्छित करके फिर वह अपरिमित बल की सीमा कुंभकर्ण वानरराज सुग्रीव को काँख में दाबकर चला ॥
english_translation: After knocking Angad and the other monkeys unconscious along with Sugriva, Kumbhakarna, with immense strength, carried the monkey king away under his arm.
essence: Raw strength can scatter a whole army in moments.
simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna knocks out Angad and the other monkeys, then picks up Sugriva under his arm and carries him off.
insight: It shifts attention to the scale of the battle rather than a moral instruction.
modern_relevance: A crowd freezes when one person’s anger takes over the room. Nothing is being argued anymore; sheer force has taken the stage.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उमा करत रघुपति नरलीला। खेलत गरुड़ जिमि अहिगन मीला॥ भृकुटि भंग जो कालहि खाई। ताहि कि सोहइ ऐसि लराई ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! श्री रघुनाथजी वैसे ही नरलीला कर रहे हैं, जैसे गरुड़ सर्पों के समूह में मिलकर खेलता हो। जो भौंह के इशारे मात्र से (बिना परिश्रम के) काल को भी खा जाता है, उसे कहीं ऐसी लड़ाई शोभा देती है? ॥
english_translation: O Uma, Raghupati is performing a human drama, just as Garuda plays among a group of snakes. Does such a fight suit one who swallows even Time with a mere movement of his brow?
essence: Ram enters battle as play, not as struggle.
simple_meaning: Ram is only appearing to fight like a human, while remaining far beyond danger. Such a battle cannot touch his true power.
insight: It shifts the mind from taking appearances literally to seeing the larger power beneath them.
modern_relevance: You watch someone handle a crisis with complete ease while everyone else panics. What looks like pressure to others may be only the role they are playing, not their real condition.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: जग पावनि कीरति बिस्तरिहहिं। गाइ गाइ भवनिधि नर तरिहहिं॥ मुरुछा गइ मारुतसुत जागा। सुग्रीवहि तब खोजन लागा ॥
translation: भगवान् (इसके द्वारा) जगत् को पवित्र करने वाली वह कीर्ति फैलाएँगे, जिसे गा-गाकर मनुष्य भवसागर से तर जाएँगे। मूर्च्छा जाती रही, तब मारुति हनुमान् जी जागे और फिर वे सुग्रीव को खोजने लगे ॥
english_translation: He will spread the fame that purifies the world; by singing it again and again, people will cross the ocean of becoming. When the swoon passed, Hanuman woke up and began searching for Sugriva.
essence: Ram's fame saves; Hanuman wakes and serves again.
simple_meaning: Ram's glory will spread through the world and help people cross life's ocean. Meanwhile, Hanuman wakes from the blow and resumes searching for Sugriva.
insight: It shifts attention from personal setback to the next faithful step.
modern_relevance: You get knocked sideways in the middle of a hard day, then remember what matters and get back to it. The work was never about your pride; it was about the mission.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुग्रीवहु कै मुरुछा बीती। निबुकि गयउ तेहि मृतक प्रतीती॥ काटेसि दसन नासिका काना। गरजि अकास चलेउ तेहिं जाना ॥
translation: सुग्रीव की भी मूर्च्छा दूर हुई, तब वे (मुर्दे से होकर) खिसक गए (काँख से नीचे गिर पड़े)। कुम्भकर्ण ने उनको मृतक जाना। उन्होंने कुम्भकर्ण के नाक-कान दाँतों से काट लिए और फिर गरज कर आकाश की ओर चले, तब कुम्भकर्ण ने जाना ॥
english_translation: Sugriva's fainting spell passed too. Kumbhakarna thought he was dead, so he slipped under him. He bit off ears, nose, and teeth, then roared into the sky; only then did Kumbhakarna realize it.
essence: A single misjudgment can turn defeat into sudden escape.
simple_meaning: Sugriva wakes from his fainting spell, and Kumbhakarna mistakes him for dead. Sugriva then attacks fiercely and leaps back into the sky.
insight: It shows how quickly battlefield fortunes can reverse when one fighter misjudges the other.
modern_relevance: In a match where everyone assumes you're finished, you catch one breath, rise, and change the whole rhythm. The moment they relax is the moment you move.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गहेउ चरन गहि भूमि पछारा। अति लाघवँ उठि पुनि तेहि मारा॥ पुनि आयउ प्रभु पहिं बलवाना। जयति जयति जय कृपानिधाना ॥
translation: उसने सुग्रीव का पैर पकड़कर उनको पृथ्वी पर पछाड़ दिया। फिर सुग्रीव ने बड़ी फुर्ती से उठकर उसको मारा और तब बलवान् सुग्रीव प्रभु के पास आए और बोले- कृपानिधान प्रभु की जय हो, जय हो, जय हो ॥
english_translation: He seized Sugriva by the foot and threw him to the ground. Sugriva sprang up swiftly and struck him again. Then the mighty Sugriva came to the Lord and cried, “Victory, victory, victory to the ocean of mercy!”
essence: A setback does not end your strength; you can rise and return in praise.
simple_meaning: Sugriva is knocked down, gets up quickly, strikes back, and then returns to Ram praising His mercy.
insight: It shows resilience in action: fall, recover, respond, then come back to gratitude.
modern_relevance: You get knocked flat in a tough meeting, recover fast, and keep going. The real win is not pretending you never fell — it is rising and returning steady.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाक कान काटे जियँ जानी। फिरा क्रोध करि भइ मन ग्लानी॥ सहज भीम पुनि बिनु श्रुति नासा। देखत कपि दल उपजी त्रासा ॥
translation: नाक-कान काटे गए, ऐसा मन में जानकर बड़ी ग्लानि हुई और वह क्रोध करके लौटा। एक तो वह स्वभाव (आकृति) से ही भयंकर था और फिर बिना नाक-कान का होने से और भी भयानक हो गया। उसे देखते ही वानरों की सेना में भय उत्पन्न हो गया ॥
english_translation: Seeing his nose and ears cut off, he returned in rage, filled with shame. Naturally terrible already, now disfigured without nose and ears, he terrified the monkey army at a glance.
essence: Humiliation can harden into a more frightening force.
simple_meaning: He came back furious and humiliated after being disfigured. His terrifying appearance made the monkey army afraid.
insight: It shows how wounded pride can intensify aggression and unsettle everyone nearby.
modern_relevance: Someone gets publicly embarrassed in a meeting, leaves the room fuming, and comes back sharper and more dangerous. Humiliation often returns as intimidation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जय जय जय रघुबंस मनि धाए कपि दै हूह। एकहि बार तासु पर छाड़ेन्हि गिरि तरु जूह ॥
translation: 'रघुवंशमणि की जय हो, जय हो' ऐसा पुकारकर वानर हूह करके दौड़े और सबने एक ही साथ उस पर पहाड़ और वृक्षों के समूह छोड़े ॥
english_translation: “Victory, victory to the jewel of the Raghu line!” the monkeys cried, and with a roar they rushed forward. In one instant they hurled mountains and trees down upon him.
essence: Praise becomes force when everyone moves together.
simple_meaning: The monkeys shout Ram's praise and attack at once, hurling mountains and trees in a single surge.
insight: It shifts attention to collective action powered by shared devotion, not individual heroics.
modern_relevance: A team hears the final call before a deadline and moves as one—no debate, no delay, just full commitment to the task.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कुंभकरन रन रंग बिरुद्धा। सन्मुख चला काल जनु क्रुद्धा॥ कोटि कोटि कपि धरि धरि खाई। जनु टीड़ी गिरि गुहाँ समाई ॥
translation: रण के उत्साह में कुंभकर्ण विरुद्ध होकर (उनके) सामने ऐसा चला मानो क्रोधित होकर काल ही आ रहा हो। वह करोड़-करोड़ वानरों को एक साथ पकड़कर खाने लगा! (वे उसके मुँह में इस तरह घुसने लगे) मानो पर्वत की गुफा में टिड्डियाँ समा रही हों ॥
english_translation: Kumbhakarna, fierce in battle, strode forward against them like Death itself in anger. He seized and devoured countless monkeys, as if grasshoppers were disappearing into a mountain cave.
essence: Raw force turns battle into terror.
simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna charges into battle like raging death and devours the monkey warriors by the countless.
insight: It frames danger as overwhelming force, not a fair contest, heightening the urgency of the battle.
modern_relevance: A problem walks into the room already bigger than your plan — a deadline, a crisis, a person in full rage. Before you can think, it is already swallowing your options.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोटिन्ह गहि सरीर सन मर्दा। कोटिन्ह मीजि मिलव महि गर्दा॥ मुख नासा श्रवनन्हि कीं बाटा। निसरि पराहिं भालु कपि ठाटा ॥
translation: करोड़ों (वानरों) को पकड़कर उसने शरीर से मसल डाला। करोड़ों को हाथों से मलकर पृथ्वी की धूल में मिला दिया। (पेट में गए हुए) भालू और वानरों के ठट्ट के ठट्ट उसके मुख, नाक और कानों की राह से निकल-निकलकर भाग रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: He seized millions and crushed them in his grip, ground millions into dust with his hands. Crowds of bears and monkeys kept pouring out through his mouth, nose, and ears.
essence: Kumbhakarna’s strength is so wild it turns the battlefield into ruin.
simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna is so huge and violent that he crushes countless bears and monkeys. Even after swallowing them, they spill back out through his face.
insight: It heightens the battle’s scale by showing unstoppable physical violence, not reflective action.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रन मद मत्त निसाचर दर्पा। बिस्व ग्रसिहि जनु ऐहि बिधि अर्पा॥ मुरे सुभट सब फिरहिं न फेरे। सूझ न नयन सुनहिं नहिं टेरे ॥
translation: रण के मद में मत्त राक्षस कुंभकर्ण इस प्रकार गर्वित हुआ, मानो विधाता ने उसको सारा विश्व अर्पण कर दिया हो और उसे वह ग्रास कर जाएगा। सब योद्धा भाग खड़े हुए, वे लौटाए भी नहीं लौटते। आँखों से उन्हें सूझ नहीं पड़ता और पुकारने से सुनते नहीं! ॥
english_translation: Intoxicated by the pride of battle, the demon became arrogant, as if fate had handed him the whole world to devour. The brave warriors ran away and would not turn back. They could not see with their eyes, and they could not hear when called.
essence: Overwhelming rage can make an army lose its senses.
simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna’s battle fury makes everyone panic. The warriors flee, and in the chaos they cannot see or hear clearly.
insight: It shows how raw aggression can paralyze an entire group before any real strategy begins.
modern_relevance: A room goes silent after one furious person starts shouting. Even capable people stop thinking clearly when fear and force take over.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कुंभकरन कपि फौज बिडारी। सुनि धाई रजनीचर धारी॥ देखी राम बिकल कटकाई। रिपु अनीक नाना बिधि आई ॥
translation: कुंभकर्ण ने वानर सेना को तितर-बितर कर दिया। यह सुनकर राक्षस सेना भी दौड़ी। श्री रामचंद्रजी ने देखा कि अपनी सेना व्याकुल है और शत्रु की नाना प्रकार की सेना आ गई है ॥
english_translation: Kumbhakarna scattered the monkey army. Hearing this, the demon army rushed forward. Ram saw his forces in distress and the enemy hosts arrive in many formations.
essence: The battle tightens when one side starts to break.
simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna breaks the monkey ranks, and the demon army surges in response. Ram sees his own army shaken as the enemy advances in many formations.
insight: It shows the turning point where a leader must respond to a weakening front.
modern_relevance: A team meeting goes silent after one hard question, and suddenly everyone can feel the room tilt. The setback is visible before anyone says a word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनु सुग्रीव बिभीषन अनुज सँभारेहु सैन। मैं देखउँ खल बल दलहि बोले राजिवनैन ॥
translation: तब कमलनयन श्री रामजी बोले- हे सुग्रीव! हे विभीषण! और हे लक्ष्मण! सुनो, तुम सेना को संभालना। मैं इस दुष्ट के बल और सेना को देखता हूँ ॥
english_translation: Then lotus-eyed Ram said: "Sugriva, Vibhishana, and Lakshman, hold the army together. I will look at this rogue's strength and forces."
essence: Clear seeing comes before decisive force.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Sugriva, Vibhishana, and Lakshman to hold the army steady while he assesses the enemy's strength.
insight: It shifts you from reactive chaos to calm assessment and organized response.
modern_relevance: Your team is rattled, people are talking over each other, and the room feels close to panic. Instead of rushing blindly, someone has to steady the group and read the situation clearly.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कर सारंग साजि कटि भाथा। अरि दल दलन चले रघुनाथा॥ प्रथम कीन्हि प्रभु धनुष टंकोरा। रिपु दल बधिर भयउ सुनि सोरा ॥
translation: हाथ में शार्गंधनुष और कमर में तरकस सजाकर श्री रघुनाथजी शत्रु सेना को दलन करने चले। प्रभु ने पहले तो धनुष का टंकार किया, जिसकी भयानक आवाज सुनते ही शत्रु दल बहरा हो गया ॥
