translation: दोनों ओर के योद्धा जय-जयकार करके अपनी-अपनी जोड़ी जान (चुन) कर इधर श्री रघुनाथजी का और उधर रावण का बखान करके परस्पर भिड़ गए ॥
english_translation: On both sides, the warriors shouted victory and chose their own champions. Then they fought, praising Ram on one side and Ravana on the other.
essence: War begins when praise turns into allegiance.
simple_meaning: The two armies rush into combat, each side cheering for its own champion and praising its own leader.
insight: It shows how quickly conflict turns people into teams, each defending its own banner.
modern_relevance: A crowd picks sides before the facts are even clear, and the room fills with noise, certainty, and tribal loyalty.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रावनु रथी बिरथ रघुबीरा। देखि बिभीषन भयउ अधीरा॥ अधिक प्रीति मन भा संदेहा। बंदि चरन कह सहित सनेहा ॥
translation: रावण को रथ पर और श्री रघुवीर को बिना रथ के देखकर विभीषण अधीर हो गए। प्रेम अधिक होने से उनके मन में सन्देह हो गया (कि वे बिना रथ के रावण को कैसे जीत सकेंगे)। श्री रामजी के चरणों की वंदना करके वे स्नेह पूर्वक कहने लगे ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ravana on a chariot and Raghubir without one, Vibhishana became restless. His love deepened into doubt, so he bowed at Ram's feet and spoke with affection.
essence: Love sees danger first and cannot stay silent.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana sees Ravana armed and Ram unarmed, and his love turns into anxious doubt. He bows to Ram and speaks lovingly.
insight: It shows how devotion can sharpen perception and move you to speak honestly when danger feels immediate.
modern_relevance: You watch someone you care about walk into a hard meeting with nothing prepared, while the other side looks fully armed. Your concern rises before your confidence does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाथ न रथ नहि तन पद त्राना। केहि बिधि जितब बीर बलवाना॥ सुनहु सखा कह कृपानिधाना। जेहिं जय होइ सो स्यंदन आना ॥
translation: हे नाथ! आपके न रथ है, न तन की रक्षा करने वाला कवच है और न जूते ही हैं। वह बलवान् वीर रावण किस प्रकार जीता जाएगा? कृपानिधान श्री रामजी ने कहा- हे सखे! सुनो, जिससे जय होती है, वह रथ दूसरा ही है ॥
english_translation: O Lord, you have no chariot, no armor for your body, and no shoes. How can the mighty warrior be conquered? The ocean of compassion Ram said, "Listen, friend: the chariot that brings victory is something else."
essence: What wins is not the visible setup, but the inner vehicle.
simple_meaning: Bibhishana worries that Ram has no visible protection or vehicle, but Ram says real victory depends on a different kind of support.
insight: It shifts attention from outward support to the inner qualities that actually carry action through.
modern_relevance: You walk into a difficult meeting with no title, no backup, and no polished script. The room looks stacked against you, but the thing that changes outcomes is not always what people can see.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सौरज धीरज तेहि रथ चाका। सत्य सील दृढ़ ध्वजा पताका॥ बल बिबेक दम परहित घोरे। छमा कृपा समता रजु जोरे ॥
translation: शौर्य और धैर्य उस रथ के पहिए हैं। सत्य और शील (सदाचार) उसकी मजबूत ध्वजा और पताका हैं। बल, विवेक, दम (इंद्रियों का वश में होना) और परोपकार- ये चार उसके घोड़े हैं, जो क्षमा, दया और समता रूपी डोरी से रथ में जोड़े हुए हैं ॥
english_translation: Sauraj and dhiraj are the wheels of that chariot. Truth and good conduct are its strong banner and pennant. Strength, discernment, self-restraint, and service to others are the horses, yoked by forgiveness, compassion, and evenness.
essence: Your real chariot is built from character, not equipment.
simple_meaning: A well-lived life needs courage, patience, truth, good conduct, self-restraint, discernment, and service, all held together by forgiveness, compassion, and balance.
insight: It shifts the mind from outer support to inner formation.
modern_relevance: You are about to walk into a hard conversation with your boss, your partner, or your child. What carries you through is not just confidence, but the steadiness, truth, and self-control you bring with you.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: ईस भजनु सारथी सुजाना। बिरति चर्म संतोष कृपाना॥ दान परसु बुधि सक्ति प्रचंडा। बर बिग्यान कठिन कोदंडा ॥
translation: ईश्वर का भजन ही (उस रथ को चलाने वाला) चतुर सारथी है। वैराग्य ढाल है और संतोष तलवार है। दान फरसा है, बुद्धि प्रचण्ड शक्ति है, श्रेष्ठ विज्ञान कठिन धनुष है ॥
english_translation: Devotion to the divine is the skilled charioteer. Non-attachment is the shield, and contentment the sword. Generosity is the axe, discerning wisdom the fierce power, and true understanding the hard bow.
essence: The real chariot of victory is built from inner qualities, not outer force.
simple_meaning: Inner victory comes from devotion, non-attachment, contentment, generosity, wisdom, and true understanding. These qualities are the real equipment for facing hard struggles.
insight: It shifts the idea of strength from outer power to inner equipment.
modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting with your jaw tight, your phone buzzing, and your chest already braced for attack. What steadies you is not more noise — it is devotion, restraint, and a mind that can see clearly.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अमल अचल मन त्रोन समाना। सम जम नियम सिलीमुख नाना॥ कवच अभेद बिप्र गुर पूजा। एहि सम बिजय उपाय न दूजा ॥
translation: निर्मल (पापरहित) और अचल (स्थिर) मन तरकस के समान है। शम (मन का वश में होना), (अहिंसादि) यम और (शौचादि) नियम- ये बहुत से बाण हैं। ब्राह्मणों और गुरु का पूजन अभेद्य कवच है। इसके समान विजय का दूसरा उपाय नहीं है ॥
english_translation: A pure, steady mind is the quiver. Restraint, discipline, and rules are many arrows. Worship of Brahmins and the teacher is an impenetrable armor. There is no other way to victory.
essence: Victory comes from a trained mind and disciplined character.
simple_meaning: A calm, steady mind becomes your base. Self-control, discipline, and respect for teachers protect you and help you succeed.
insight: It shifts the focus from raw effort to inner preparation, where discipline makes action effective.
modern_relevance: Before a hard exam, a difficult conversation, or a messy family decision, you can feel your mind scatter. This verse says victory begins when your attention is steady and your character is trained.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सखा धर्ममय अस रथ जाकें। जीतन कहँ न कतहुँ रिपु ताकें ॥
translation: हे सखे! ऐसा धर्ममय रथ जिसके हो उसके लिए जीतने को कहीं शत्रु ही नहीं है ॥
english_translation: O friend, for the one who has such a righteous chariot, there is no enemy left to conquer.
essence: A life ordered by dharma cannot be truly defeated.
simple_meaning: A life built on righteousness leaves nothing truly able to defeat you. The real victory comes from having the right inner structure, not from fighting harder.
insight: It shifts victory from external struggle to inner alignment with dharma.
modern_relevance: You walk into a difficult meeting already shaken, but your preparation, values, and calm are in place. The room still matters, but it no longer controls you.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: महा अजय संसार रिपु जीति सकइ सो बीर। जाकें अस रथ होइ दृढ़ सुनहु सखा मतिधीर ॥
translation: हे धीरबुद्धि वाले सखा! सुनो, जिसके पास ऐसा दृढ़ रथ हो, वह वीर संसार (जन्म-मृत्यु) रूपी महान् दुर्जय शत्रु को भी जीत सकता है (रावण की तो बात ही क्या है) ॥
english_translation: O steadfast-minded friend, listen: the hero who has such a firm chariot can conquer the great, hard-to-defeat enemy called the cycle of birth and death.
essence: A firm inner foundation can defeat the hardest enemy.
simple_meaning: A person with a strong, disciplined inner foundation can defeat even the greatest enemy of repeated birth and death.
insight: It shifts the focus from outer power to the disciplined inner structure that makes victory possible.
modern_relevance: You are about to send a message that could start a fight, but you pause, breathe, and choose your words carefully. That inner steadiness is the real weapon.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सुनि प्रभु बचन बिभीषन हरषि गहे पद कंज। एहि मिस मोहि उपदेसेहु राम कृपा सुख पुंज॥80 ख
translation: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर विभीषणजी ने हर्षित होकर उनके चरण कमल पकड़ लिए (और कहा-) हे कृपा और सुख के समूह श्री रामजी! आपने इसी बहाने मुझे (महान् ) उपदेश दिया ॥
english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, Vibhishana rejoiced and clasped the lotus feet, saying, 'O Ram, treasure of mercy and joy, you have taught me through this very moment.'
essence: Ram's mercy teaches the surrendered heart without formal instruction.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana feels joy on hearing Ram and bows at his feet, saying Ram's mercy itself has taught him something important.
insight: It shifts the mind from demanding explanation to recognising grace as guidance.
modern_relevance: You finally hear the calm reply after a painful conversation, and something in you softens. Sometimes the lesson is not the answer — it's the kindness behind it.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: उत पचार दसकंधर इत अंगद हनुमान। लरत निसाचर भालु कपि करि निज निज प्रभु आन ॥
translation: उधर से रावण ललकार रहा है और इधर से अंगद और हनुमान् । राक्षस और रीछ-वानर अपने-अपने स्वामी की दुहाई देकर लड़ रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Ravana roars from one side, Angada and Hanuman from the other. Demons, bears, and monkeys fight, each calling on their own lord.
essence: War becomes a contest of loyalties, not just weapons.
simple_meaning: The battle is split between two sides, with each army fighting under its own leader.
insight: It shifts attention from individual fighters to the larger loyalties driving the battle.
modern_relevance: A crowd argument breaks out at a family gathering, and suddenly everyone is speaking for their side, not for the truth. This verse shows how conflict can turn into tribal allegiance.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुर ब्रह्मादि सिद्ध मुनि नाना। देखत रन नभ चढ़े बिमाना॥ हमहू उमा रहे तेहिं संगा। देखत राम चरित रन रंगा ॥
translation: ब्रह्मा आदि देवता और अनेकों सिद्ध तथा मुनि विमानों पर चढ़े हुए आकाश से युद्ध देख रहे हैं। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! मैं भी उस समाज में था और श्री रामजी के रण-रंग (रणोत्साह) की लीला देख रहा था ॥
english_translation: The gods, Brahma, the perfected beings, and many sages rose into the sky in flying chariots to watch the battle. Shiva says to Uma, "I was there too, watching Ram's war-play."
essence: Heaven itself pauses to watch Ram's battle.
simple_meaning: The heavenly beings and sages are watching the battle from above, and Shiva tells Uma that he was there too, witnessing Ram's battle-play.
insight: It places the reader inside the war's sacred atmosphere before the next clash begins.
modern_relevance: A crowd gathers on a rooftop to watch a final match under floodlights. The moment feels larger than the people in it, but the verse is only setting the scene.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: सुभट समर रस दुहु दिसि माते। कपि जयसील राम बल ताते॥ एक एक सन भिरहिं पचारहिं। एकन्ह एक मर्दि महि पारहिं ॥
translation: दोनों ओर के योद्धा रण रस में मतवाले हो रहे हैं। वानरों को श्री रामजी का बल है, इससे वे जयशील हैं (जीत रहे हैं)। एक-दूसरे से भिड़ते और ललकारते हैं और एक-दूसरे को मसल-मसलकर पृथ्वी पर डाल देते हैं ॥
english_translation: The brave warriors on both sides are drunk with the thrill of battle. The monkeys have Ram's strength, so they keep winning. They clash, challenge each other, and crush one another to the ground.
essence: Battle becomes a force that sweeps everyone into motion.
simple_meaning: Both armies are fully caught up in fierce combat, and Ram's side keeps gaining the upper hand.
insight: It shows battle as total immersion, where strength, challenge, and resistance all hit at once.
modern_relevance: In a crowded sports arena, bodies surge, shouts rise, and every move becomes instinct. This verse captures that raw momentum before anyone has time to think.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मारहिं काटहिं धरहिं पछारहिं। सीस तोरि सीसन्ह सन मारहिं॥ उदर बिदारहिं भुजा उपारहिं। गहि पद अवनि पटकि भट डारहिं ॥
translation: वे मारते, काटते, पकड़ते और पछाड़ देते हैं और सिर तोड़कर उन्हीं सिरों से दूसरों को मारते हैं। पेट फाड़ते हैं, भुजाएँ उखाड़ते हैं और योद्धाओं को पैर पकड़कर पृथ्वी पर पटक देते हैं ॥
english_translation: They strike, cut, seize, and throw down. They break heads and use those very heads to strike again. They tear open bellies, rip up arms, and grab warriors by the feet to slam them to the ground.
essence: The battle has turned into savage, unbroken violence.
simple_meaning: The battle is brutal and chaotic, with fighters killing and maiming each other in many ways.
insight: It shows the war reaching a ferocious, uncontrolled level of close combat.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निसिचर भट महि गाड़हिं भालू। ऊपर ढारि देहिं बहु बालू॥ बीर बलीमुख जुद्ध बिरुद्धे। देखिअत बिपुल काल जनु क्रुद्धे ॥
translation: राक्षस योद्धाओं को भालू पृथ्वी में गाड़ देते हैं और ऊपर से बहुत सी बालू डाल देते हैं। युद्ध में शत्रुओं से विरुद्ध हुए वीर वानर ऐसे दिखाई पड़ते हैं मानो बहुत से क्रोधित काल हों ॥
english_translation: The bear-warriors bury the demon fighters in the ground and cover them with heaps of sand. The brave monkey warriors, fierce in battle, look like many enraged forms of death.
essence: Battle has become a storm of relentless destruction.
simple_meaning: The battle is so fierce that bears bury enemies in the earth while monkey warriors look like many raging figures of death.
insight: It keeps the focus on the sheer violence of the clash, not on strategy or reflection.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: क्रुद्धे कृतांत समान कपि तन स्रवत सोनित राजहीं। मर्दहिं निसाचर कटक भट बलवंत घन जिमि गाजहीं॥ मारहिं चपेटन्हि डाटि दातन्ह काटि लातन्ह मीजहीं। चिक्करहिं मर्कट भालु छल बल करहिं जेहिं खल छीजहीं ॥
translation: क्रोधित हुए काल के समान वे वानर खून बहते हुए शरीरों से शोभित हो रहे हैं। वे बलवान् वीर राक्षसों की सेना के योद्धाओं को मसलते और मेघ की तरह गरजते हैं। डाँटकर चपेटों से मारते, दाँतों से काटकर लातों से पीस डालते हैं। वानर-भालू चिग्घाड़ते और ऐसा छल-बल करते हैं, जिससे दुष्ट राक्षस नष्ट हो जाएँ ॥
english_translation: Angry like death itself, the monkeys’ bodies shine with blood. They crush the strong demon troops and roar like thunderclouds. They strike with slaps, bites, and kicks, and the monkeys and bears shout so that the wicked are destroyed by force and trickery.
essence: The battle surges with savage, unstoppable force.
simple_meaning: The monkey and bear warriors fight with fierce, overwhelming force, crushing the demon army in brutal close combat.
insight: It intensifies the war scene rather than offering a separate lesson.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धरि गाल फारहिं उर बिदारहिं गल अँतावरि मेलहीं। प्रह्लादपति जनु बिबिध तनु धरि समर अंगन खेलहीं॥ धरु मारु काटु पछारु घोर गिरा गगन महि भरि रही। जय राम जो तृन ते कुलिस कर कुलिस ते कर तृन सही ॥
translation: वे राक्षसों के गाल पकड़कर फाड़ डालते हैं, छाती चीर डालते हैं और उनकी अँतड़ियाँ निकालकर गले में डाल लेते हैं। वे वानर ऐसे दिख पड़ते हैं मानो प्रह्लाद के स्वामी श्री नृसिंह भगवान् अनेकों शरीर धारण करके युद्ध के मैदान में क्रीड़ा कर रहे हों। पकड़ो, मारो, काटो, पछाड़ो आदि घोर शब्द आकाश और पृथ्वी में भर (छा) गए हैं। श्री रामचंद्रजी की जय हो, जो सचमुच तृण से वज्र और वज्र से तृण कर देते हैं (निर्बल को सबल और सबल को निर्बल कर देते हैं) ॥
english_translation: They seize the demons by the cheeks, tear open their chests, and stuff their entrails into their throats. The monkeys seem like Lord Narasimha, the protector of Prahlad, playing on the battlefield in many forms. "Seize! Kill! Cut! Throw down!" — fierce cries fill the sky and earth. Victory to Ram, who turns straw into thunderbolt and thunderbolt into straw.
essence: Ram can turn weakness into force and force into weakness.
simple_meaning: The battlefield has become so intense that the monkeys seem like fierce divine forms at play. Ram's power makes the weak strong and the strong weak.
insight: It shifts attention from battlefield fury to Ram's hidden sovereignty over strength itself.
modern_relevance: A situation turns brutal fast: voices rise, tempers snap, and everyone feels the room tilt. In that moment, the verse reminds you that power is never finally yours to control.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निज दल बिचलत देखेसि बीस भुजाँ दस चाप। रथ चढ़ि चलेउ दसानन फिरहु फिरहु करि दाप ॥
translation: अपनी सेना को विचलित होते हुए देखा, तब बीस भुजाओं में दस धनुष लेकर रावण रथ पर चढ़कर गर्व करके 'लौटो, लौटो' कहता हुआ चला ॥
english_translation: Seeing his army wavering, Ravana mounted his chariot with ten bows in his twenty arms and cried, "Turn back, turn back!" in pride.
essence: Ego shouts hardest when it senses weakness.
simple_meaning: Ravana sees his army faltering, climbs onto his chariot, and shouts in pride for the enemy to turn back.
insight: It shows how ego reacts when power begins to slip.
modern_relevance: You spot the room going quiet after your mistake, and you try to cover it with volume. The louder you get, the more everyone sees the fear underneath.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धायउ परम क्रुद्ध दसकंधर। सन्मुख चले हूह दै बंदर॥ गहि कर पादप उपल पहारा। डारेन्हि ता पर एकहिं बारा ॥
translation: रावण अत्यंत क्रोधित होकर दौड़ा। वानर हुँकार करते हुए (लड़ने के लिए) उसके सामने चले। उन्होंने हाथों में वृक्ष, पत्थर और पहाड़ लेकर रावण पर एक ही साथ डाले ॥
english_translation: Ravana, furious beyond measure, charged forward. The monkeys advanced toward him with loud cries. They seized trees, stones, and mountains and hurled them all at once.
essence: Battle surges forward in a storm of fury and flying mountains.
simple_meaning: Ravana rushes into battle, and the monkeys meet him by hurling trees, stones, and mountains together.
insight: It keeps the focus on the raw momentum of battle rather than any inner lesson.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लागहिं सैल बज्र तन तासू। खंड खंड होइ फूटहिं आसू॥ चला न अचल रहा रथ रोपी। रन दुर्मद रावन अति कोपी ॥
translation: पर्वत उसके वज्रतुल्य शरीर में लगते ही तुरंत टुकड़े-टुकड़े होकर फूट जाते हैं। अत्यंत क्रोधी रणोन्मत्त रावण रथ रोककर अचल खड़ा रहा, (अपने स्थान से) जरा भी नहीं हिला ॥
english_translation: Mountains strike his body like thunderbolts and shatter at once. Furious in battle, Ravana stopped his chariot and stood unmoving, not shifting even a little.
essence: Pride can stand unmoved even under overwhelming attack.
simple_meaning: Mountains hit Ravana's body and break apart. He stands unmoved in his chariot, burning with rage.
insight: It shows how ego can turn pain into hardness instead of learning.
modern_relevance: A room full of criticism lands on someone who refuses to bend. They don't soften; they only get more rigid, more defensive, more dangerous.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: इत उत झपटि दपटि कपि जोधा। मर्दै लाग भयउ अति क्रोधा॥ चले पराइ भालु कपि नाना। त्राहि त्राहि अंगद हनुमाना ॥
translation: उसे बहुत ही क्रोध हुआ। वह इधर-उधर झपटकर और डपटकर वानर योद्धाओं को मसलने लगा। अनेकों वानर-भालू 'हे अंगद! हे हनुमान् ! रक्षा करो, रक्षा करो' (पुकारते हुए) भाग चले ॥
english_translation: He grew furious. Leaping here and there, he struck and crushed the monkey warriors. Many monkeys and bears ran away crying, 'Protect us, Angad! Protect us, Hanuman!'
essence: Blind fury can drive even brave hearts into flight.
simple_meaning: Ravana attacks wildly, and the monkey and bear fighters panic and flee, calling for Angad and Hanuman to protect them.
insight: It shows how raw aggression can scatter courage and expose the need for steadier protectors.
modern_relevance: A room full of people goes silent when one person explodes in anger. The force may look powerful, but it also makes everyone else retreat.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पाहि पाहि रघुबीर गोसाईं। यह खल खाइ काल की नाईं॥ तेहिं देखे कपि सकल पराने। दसहुँ चाप सायक संधाने ॥
translation: हे रघुवीर! हे गोसाईं! रक्षा कीजिए, रक्षा कीजिए। यह दुष्ट काल की भाँति हमें खा रहा है। उसने देखा कि सब वानर भाग छूटे, तब (रावण ने) दसों धनुषों पर बाण संधान किए ॥
english_translation: “Protect us, protect us, O Raghubir, O Lord. This villain is devouring us like death itself.” Seeing the monkeys flee, Ravana then strung all ten bows and drew his arrows.
essence: Fear calls for refuge when force becomes overwhelming.
simple_meaning: The monkeys cry out to Ram for protection as Ravana overwhelms them and prepares another fierce arrow attack.
insight: It shows the moment fear turns into a cry for protection, just before the next assault begins.
modern_relevance: You’re in the middle of a group project, messages are failing, and one person is bulldozing everyone else. Panic rises first; clear help comes next.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: संधानि धनु सर निकर छाड़ेसि उरग जिमि उड़ि लागहीं। रहे पूरि सर धरनी गगन दिसि बिदिसि कहँ कपि भागहीं॥ भयो अति कोलाहल बिकल कपि दल भालु बोलहिं आतुरे। रघुबीर करुना सिंधु आरत बंधु जन रच्छक हरे॥
translation: उसने धनुष पर सन्धान करके बाणों के समूह छोड़े। वे बाण सर्प की तरह उड़कर जा लगते थे। पृथ्वी-आकाश और दिशा-विदिशा सर्वत्र बाण भर रहे हैं। वानर भागें तो कहाँ? अत्यंत कोलाहल मच गया। वानर-भालुओं की सेना व्याकुल होकर आर्त्त पुकार करने लगी- हे रघुवीर! हे करुणासागर! हे पीड़ितों के बन्धु! हे सेवकों की रक्षा करके उनके दुःख हरने वाले हरि!
english_translation: Having fitted his bow, he loosed a shower of arrows. They flew like serpents and struck everywhere. Earth, sky, and all directions were filled with arrows. Where could the monkeys run? A terrible uproar rose as the monkey and bear army, shaken and desperate, cried out, "O Raghubir, ocean of compassion, friend of the distressed, protector who removes the suffering of your servants!"
essence: When everything closes in, devotion becomes the only refuge.
simple_meaning: Arrows fill every direction, leaving the monkey and bear army with nowhere to escape. In their panic, they cry out to Ram as the compassionate protector of the suffering.
insight: It shifts the mind from panic and scattering to seeking shelter in what can actually protect you.
modern_relevance: You open your inbox and everything feels like it is hitting at once — messages, deadlines, demands, fear. In that moment, the mind reaches for the one steady refuge it trusts.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निज दल बिकल देखि कटि कसि निषंग धनु हाथ। लछिमन चले क्रुद्ध होइ नाइ राम पद माथ ॥
translation: अपनी सेना को व्याकुल देखकर कमर में तरकस कसकर और हाथ में धनुष लेकर श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों पर मस्तक नवाकर लक्ष्मणजी क्रोधित होकर चले ॥
english_translation: Seeing his own army distressed, Lakshman tightened his quiver, took his bow in hand, bowed his head at Ram's feet, and went out in anger.
essence: True service bows first, then fights without delay.
simple_meaning: Lakshman sees his side in trouble, arms himself, bows to Ram, and rushes into battle in anger.
insight: It shifts loyalty from feeling into immediate, protective action.
modern_relevance: Your team is rattled, the room is tense, and everyone is waiting for someone to move. You steady yourself, remember who you serve, and step in without hesitation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रे खल का मारसि कपि भालू। मोहि बिलोकु तोर मैं कालू॥ खोजत रहेउँ तोहि सुतघाती। आजु निपाति जुड़ावउँ छाती ॥
translation: (लक्ष्मणजी ने पास जाकर कहा-) अरे दुष्ट! वानर भालुओं को क्या मार रहा है? मुझे देख, मैं तेरा काल हूँ। (रावण ने कहा-) अरे मेरे पुत्र के घातक! मैं तुझी को ढूँढ रहा था। आज तुझे मारकर (अपनी) छाती ठंडी करूँगा ॥
english_translation: “You villain, why are you killing monkeys and bears? Look at me — I am your death.” “I have been searching for you, killer of my son. Today I will kill you and cool my burning chest.”
essence: Rage makes the wounded man seek his own ruin.
simple_meaning: Ravana challenges Lakshman in anger, saying he has been looking for him and will kill him to ease his burning rage.
insight: It shows how wounded ego turns loss into aggression instead of reflection.
modern_relevance: Two people trade words after a family fight, and old grief comes out as threat. What should have been sorrow becomes a need to strike back.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: अस कहि छाड़ेसि बान प्रचंडा। लछिमन किए सकल सत खंडा॥ कोटिन्ह आयुध रावन डारे। तिल प्रवान करि काटि निवारे ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर उसने प्रचण्ड बाण छोड़े। लक्ष्मणजी ने सबके सैकड़ों टुकड़े कर डाले। रावण ने करोड़ों अस्त्र-शस्त्र चलाए। लक्ष्मणजी ने उनको तिल के बराबर करके काटकर हटा दिया ॥
english_translation: After saying this, he released fierce arrows. Lakshman shattered them into hundreds of pieces. Ravana hurled millions of weapons, and Lakshman cut them down as if they were sesame seeds.
essence: No barrage can shake the one who stays ready.
simple_meaning: Ravana unleashes weapon after weapon, but Lakshman cuts every attack apart and keeps advancing.
insight: It shifts attention from the volume of opposition to steadiness under pressure.
modern_relevance: A crisis meeting keeps throwing new objections at you, one after another. You stay calm, answer each one, and refuse to be thrown off center.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि निज बानन्ह कीन्ह प्रहारा। स्यंदनु भंजि सारथी मारा॥ सत सत सर मारे दस भाला। गिरि सृंगन्ह जनु प्रबिसहिं ब्याला ॥
translation: फिर अपने बाणों से (उस पर) प्रहार किया और (उसके) रथ को तोड़कर सारथी को मार डाला। (रावण के) दसों मस्तकों में सौ-सौ बाण मारे। वे सिरों में ऐसे पैठ गए मानो पहाड़ के शिखरों में सर्प प्रवेश कर रहे हों ॥
english_translation: Then he struck again with his arrows, shattered the chariot, and killed the charioteer. He shot a hundred arrows into each of Ravana's ten heads, and they pierced them like snakes entering mountain peaks.
essence: Ravana's defenses are shattered in a single, overwhelming strike.
simple_meaning: Ravana is hit hard in battle: his chariot is broken, his charioteer is killed, and arrows pierce all ten heads.
insight: It shows total battlefield collapse, not a moral principle. The focus stays on action, force, and damage.
modern_relevance: A crisis can hit all at once: the plan breaks, the support person disappears, and the pressure lands from every side.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि सुत सर मारा उर माहीं। परेउ धरनि तल सुधि कछु नाहीं॥ उठा प्रबल पुनि मुरुछा जागी। छाड़िसि ब्रह्म दीन्हि जो साँगी ॥
translation: फिर सौ बाण उसकी छाती में मारे। वह पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा, उसे कुछ भी होश न रहा। फिर मूर्च्छा छूटने पर वह प्रबल रावण उठा और उसने वह शक्ति चलाई जो ब्रह्माजी ने उसे दी थी ॥ छंद :
english_translation: Then he shot a hundred arrows into his chest. He fell to the ground, unconscious. When the fainting passed, mighty Ravana rose again and launched the weapon given by Brahma.
essence: Defeat does not end ego; it often makes it reach for stronger force.
simple_meaning: Ravana is struck down, loses consciousness, then rises again and uses a powerful weapon given by Brahma.
insight: It shows how ego can recover quickly and respond with inherited power instead of surrendering.
modern_relevance: You get hit with bad news, sit stunned for a minute, then stand up and reach for the same old defense. The pattern is older than the problem.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सो ब्रह्म दत्त प्रचंड सक्ति अनंत उर लागी सही। पर् यो बीर बिकल उठाव दसमुख अतुल बल महिमा रही॥ ब्रह्मांड भवन बिराज जाकें एक सिर जिमि रज कनी। तेहि चह उठावन मूढ़ रावन जान नहिं त्रिभुअन धनी॥
translation: वह ब्रह्मा की दी हुई प्रचण्ड शक्ति लक्ष्मणजी की ठीक छाती में लगी। वीर लक्ष्मणजी व्याकुल होकर गिर पड़े। तब रावण उन्हें उठाने लगा, पर उसके अतुलित बल की महिमा यों ही रह गई, (व्यर्थ हो गई, वह उन्हें उठा न सका)। जिनके एक ही सिर पर ब्रह्मांड रूपी भवन धूल के एक कण के समान विराजता है, उन्हें मूर्ख रावण उठाना चाहता है! वह तीनों भुवनों के स्वामी लक्ष्मणजी को नहीं जानता।
english_translation: The fierce power given by Brahma struck Lakshmana squarely in the chest. Brave Lakshmana fell in distress. Then Ravana tried to lift him, but his unmatched strength proved useless. The fool does not know the Lord of the three worlds, whose one head bears the universe like a speck of dust.
essence: Pride is weakest when it mistakes greatness for weakness.
simple_meaning: Ravana's blow fells Lakshmana, but even then Ravana cannot lift him. The verse exposes Ravana's blindness: he does not understand Lakshmana's true greatness.
insight: It shifts the mind from raw force to humility before what cannot be mastered.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to control a person who has already slipped beyond your reach. The harder you push, the more your own helplessness shows.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि पवनसुत धायउ बोलत बचन कठोर। आवत कपिहि हन्यो तेहिं मुष्टि प्रहार प्रघोर ॥
translation: यह देखकर पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी कठोर वचन बोलते हुए दौड़े। हनुमान् जी के आते ही रावण ने उन पर अत्यंत भयंकर घूँसे का प्रहार किया ॥
english_translation: Seeing this, Hanuman rushed forward, speaking harsh words. As he came near, Ravana struck him with a fierce blow of his fist.
essence: The next clash begins the moment courage steps forward.
simple_meaning: Hanuman rushes in with sharp words, and Ravana answers with a brutal punch.
insight: It moves the story into direct confrontation, with no pause or reflection.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जानु टेकि कपि भूमि न गिरा। उठा सँभारि बहुत रिस भरा॥ मुठिका एक ताहि कपि मारा। परेउ सैल जनु बज्र प्रहारा ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी घुटने टेककर रह गए, पृथ्वी पर गिरे नहीं और फिर क्रोध से भरे हुए संभलकर उठे। हनुमान् जी ने रावण को एक घूँसा मारा। वह ऐसा गिर पड़ा जैसे वज्र की मार से पर्वत गिरा हो ॥
english_translation: Hanuman knelt, did not fall to the ground, then rose up, full of rage. He struck Ravana with one fist, and Ravana fell like a mountain struck by thunderbolt.
essence: A single retaliatory blow drops Ravana hard.
simple_meaning: Hanuman steadies himself, rises in anger, and lands a crushing blow on Ravana that sends him down hard.
insight: It keeps the focus on immediate combat action, not reflection or principle.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुरुछा गै बहोरि सो जागा। कपि बल बिपुल सराहन लागा॥ धिग धिग मम पौरुष धिग मोही। जौं तैं जिअत रहेसि सुरद्रोही ॥
translation: मूर्च्छा भंग होने पर फिर वह जागा और हनुमान् जी के बड़े भारी बल को सराहने लगा। (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) मेरे पौरुष को धिक्कार है, धिक्कार है और मुझे भी धिक्कार है, जो हे देवद्रोही! तू अब भी जीता रह गया ॥
english_translation: After fainting, he woke again and began praising Hanuman's immense strength. "Shame on my strength, shame on me, if you, enemy of the radiant beings, still live!"
essence: Ego collapses fastest when it meets real strength.
simple_meaning: Ravana regains consciousness, admires Hanuman's power, and then curses his own courage for failing to kill him.
insight: It shows defeat exposing ego, not just weakening the body.
modern_relevance: After a humiliating loss, you replay the moment and hear your own ego cracking. The sting is real, but so is the recognition of someone stronger.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: अस कहि लछिमन कहुँ कपि ल्यायो। देखि दसानन बिसमय पायो॥ कह रघुबीर समुझु जियँ भ्राता। तुम्ह कृतांत भच्छक सुर त्राता ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर और लक्ष्मणजी को उठाकर हनुमान् जी श्री रघुनाथजी के पास ले आए। यह देखकर रावण को आश्चर्य हुआ। श्री रघुवीर ने (लक्ष्मणजी से) कहा- हे भाई! हृदय में समझो, तुम काल के भी भक्षक और देवताओं के रक्षक हो ॥
english_translation: Having said this, Hanuman brought Lakshman to Ram. Ravana was astonished to see it. Then Ram said to his brother, "Understand in your heart: you are the eater of even Time, and the protector of the radiant beings."
essence: Your deepest strength can remain untouched even after defeat.
simple_meaning: Hanuman brings the wounded Lakshman back to Ram, and Ram reassures him with words of strength and honor.
insight: It shifts attention from temporary weakness to the larger courage still intact.
modern_relevance: A teammate comes back from a brutal setback, and everyone is watching to see whether they collapse. The right words can restore courage faster than any bandage.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनत बचन उठि बैठ कृपाला। गई गगन सो सकति कराला॥ पुनि कोदंड बान गहि धाए। रिपु सन्मुख अति आतुर आए ॥
translation: ये वचन सुनते ही कृपालु लक्ष्मणजी उठ बैठे। वह कराल शक्ति आकाश को चली गई। लक्ष्मणजी फिर धनुष-बाण लेकर दौड़े और बड़ी शीघ्रता से शत्रु के सामने आ पहुँचे ॥
english_translation: Hearing those words, the compassionate one rose up. The terrible Shakti went into the sky. Then, taking bow and arrows, he rushed forward and came eagerly before the enemy.
essence: A single word of hope can bring strength back at once.
simple_meaning: Hearing the words, Lakshman rises at once, and the fierce Shakti disappears. He grabs his bow and arrows and rushes toward the enemy.
insight: It shows how restored confidence can dissolve fear and restart decisive action.
modern_relevance: You hear one encouraging message after a crushing setback, and your body changes first. The slump lifts, your hands move, and you are back in the fight.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: आतुर बहोरि बिभंजि स्यंदन सूत हति ब्याकुल कियो। गिर् यो धरनि दसकंधर बिकलतर बान सत बेध्यो हियो॥ सारथी दूसर घालि रथ तेहि तुरत लंका लै गयो। रघुबीर बंधु प्रताप पुंज बहोरि प्रभु चरनन्हि नयो॥
translation: फिर उन्होंने बड़ी ही शीघ्रता से रावण के रथ को चूर-चूर कर और सारथी को मारकर उसे (रावण को) व्याकुल कर दिया। सौ बाणों से उसका हृदय बेध दिया, जिससे रावण अत्यंत व्याकुल होकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा। तब दूसरा सारथी उसे रथ में डालकर तुरंत ही लंका को ले गया। प्रताप के समूह श्री रघुवीर के भाई लक्ष्मणजी ने फिर आकर प्रभु के चरणों में प्रणाम किया।
english_translation: Then, in great haste, he shattered Ravana's chariot and killed the charioteer, throwing him into confusion. He pierced Ravana's heart with a hundred arrows, and Ravana fell to the ground, shaken and helpless. Another charioteer quickly carried him back to Lanka. Lakshman, the shining brother of Raghubir, came again and bowed at the Lord's feet.
essence: Power is complete only when it ends in surrender at the Lord's feet.
simple_meaning: Laxman defeats Ravana in battle, leaving him stunned and carried back to Lanka, then returns to bow before Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from battlefield triumph to the discipline of returning to service.
modern_relevance: A hard-won win at work or in sport can still end with you stepping back quietly, not strutting. The real measure is what you do after the impact.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उहाँ दसानन जागि करि करै लाग कछु जग्य। राम बिरोध बिजय चह सठ हठ बस अति अग्य ॥
translation: वहाँ (लंका में) रावण मूर्छा से जागकर कुछ यज्ञ करने लगा। वह मूर्ख और अत्यंत अज्ञानी हठवश श्री रघुनाथजी से विरोध करके विजय चाहता है ॥
english_translation: There, Ravana woke from his fainting spell and began some ritual. That fool, driven by stubbornness and deep ignorance, still wanted victory while opposing Ram.
essence: Stubborn pride keeps reaching for victory after defeat has already begun.
simple_meaning: Ravana wakes up and starts a ritual, still stubbornly hoping to win by opposing Ram.
insight: It exposes how ego keeps repeating failed methods instead of facing the truth.
modern_relevance: You get a harsh warning from the numbers, but you still double down and call it strategy. That is Ravana's mind at work.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: इहाँ बिभीषन सब सुधि पाई। सपदि जाइ रघुपतिहि सुनाई॥ नाथ करइ रावन एक जागा। सिद्ध भएँ नहिं मरिहि अभागा ॥
translation: यहाँ विभीषणजी ने सब खबर पाई और तुरंत जाकर श्री रघुनाथजी को कह सुनाई कि हे नाथ! रावण एक यज्ञ कर रहा है। उसके सिद्ध होने पर वह अभागा सहज ही नहीं मरेगा ॥
english_translation: Here, Vibhishana learned all the news and quickly went to tell Raghupati: "Lord, Ravana is performing a sacrifice. If it succeeds, that unlucky one will not die."
essence: Early warning can change the whole battle.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana learns that Ravana is trying to complete a sacrifice, and he urgently warns Ram that this would make Ravana harder to defeat.
insight: It teaches you to act on urgent information before a problem hardens.
modern_relevance: You hear the group chat blow up just as a bad decision is about to become irreversible. Speaking up early can stop damage that brute force later can't undo.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पठवहु नाथ बेगि भट बंदर। करहिं बिधंस आव दसकंधर॥ प्रात होत प्रभु सुभट पठाए। हनुमदादि अंगद सब धाए॥2।
translation: हे नाथ! तुरंत वानर योद्धाओं को भेजिए, जो यज्ञ का विध्वंस करें, जिससे रावण युद्ध में आवे। प्रातःकाल होते ही प्रभु ने वीर योद्धाओं को भेजा। हनुमान् और अंगद आदि सब (प्रधान वीर) दौड़े ॥
english_translation: O Lord, quickly send the monkey warriors. Let them destroy the sacrifice so Ravana comes to battle. At dawn the Lord sent out the brave fighters; Hanuman, Angada, and the others rushed forth.
essence: Swift action can stop a danger before it matures.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana asks Ram to send the monkey warriors to stop Ravana’s sacrifice and draw him into battle. Ram then sends Hanuman, Angada, and the others at dawn.
insight: It shifts the mind from passive concern to decisive, timely response.
modern_relevance: You spot a problem before it becomes a disaster, and you act fast instead of hoping it will fix itself.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: कौतुक कूदि चढ़े कपि लंका। पैठे रावन भवन असंका॥ जग्य करत जबहीं सो देखा। सकल कपिन्ह भा क्रोध बिसेषा ॥
translation: वानर खेल से ही कूदकर लंका पर जा चढ़े और निर्भय होकर रावण के महल में जा घुसे। ज्यों ही उसको यज्ञ करते देखा, त्यों ही सब वानरों को बहुत क्रोध हुआ ॥
english_translation: The monkeys leaped onto Lanka as if for sport and entered Ravana's palace without fear. The moment they saw him performing the sacrifice, all the monkeys felt a fierce anger.
essence: Fearless entry becomes fury the moment injustice is seen.
simple_meaning: The monkeys entered Lanka fearlessly, and seeing Ravana's sacrifice made them angry.
insight: It shows how clear sight can convert boldness into righteous action without hesitation.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room expecting a routine meeting, then see someone being cornered unfairly. Your calm turns sharp in an instant, and you know exactly where you stand.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रन ते निलज भाजि गृह आवा। इहाँ आइ बक ध्यान लगावा। अस कहि अंगद मारा लाता। चितव न सठ स्वारथ मन राता ॥
translation: (उन्होंने कहा-) अरे ओ निर्लज्ज! रणभूमि से घर भाग आया और यहाँ आकर बगुले का सा ध्यान लगाकर बैठा है? ऐसा कहकर अंगद ने लात मारी। पर उसने इनकी ओर देखा भी नहीं, उस दुष्ट का मन स्वार्थ में अनुरक्त था ॥
english_translation: “You shameless one, you fled the battlefield and came home, then sat here in monk-like stillness?” Angada said this and kicked him, but the fool did not even look; his mind was fixed on selfish gain.
essence: A selfish mind can stay untouched even by disgrace.
simple_meaning: Angada mocks a coward who fled battle, then kicked him. The man stays unmoved because his mind is absorbed in selfishness.
insight: It shows how selfish fixation can block even shame, warning you that inner attachment can make correction useless.
modern_relevance: A person who has already chosen self-protection over courage can sit through the harshest criticism without blinking. The problem is not lack of hearing; it is a mind already sold.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नहिं चितव जब करि कोप कपि गहि दसन लातन्ह मारहीं। धरि केस नारि निकारि बाहेर तेऽतिदीन पुकारहीं॥ तब उठेउ क्रुद्ध कृतांत सम गहि चरन बानर डारई। एहि बीच कपिन्ह बिधंस कृत मख देखि मन महुँ हारई॥
translation: जब उसने नहीं देखा, तब वानर क्रोध करके उसे दाँतों से पकड़कर (काटने और) लातों से मारने लगे। स्त्रियों को बाल पकड़कर घर से बाहर घसीट लाए, वे अत्यंत ही दीन होकर पुकारने लगीं। तब रावण काल के समान क्रोधित होकर उठा और वानरों को पैर पकड़कर पटकने लगा। इसी बीच में वानरों ने यज्ञ विध्वंस कर डाला, यह देखकर वह मन में हारने लगा। (निराश होने लगा)।
english_translation: When Ravana looked away, the monkeys grew angry, seized him with their teeth, and struck him with kicks. They grabbed the women by the hair and dragged them outside, where the helpless women cried out. Then Ravana rose in rage like Death itself and seized the monkeys by the feet to hurl them down. In the meantime, the monkeys destroyed the sacrifice, and seeing that, he began to lose heart.
essence: Power begins to crack the moment confidence breaks.
simple_meaning: The monkeys attack Ravana's people, Ravana fights back in fury, and the sacrifice is ruined. Seeing the destruction, Ravana starts to lose confidence.
insight: It shows how quickly anger, humiliation, and fear can unravel control.
modern_relevance: A room full of confidence can change in seconds when a plan falls apart and everyone starts reacting at once. The real loss is often not the event itself, but the confidence it shatters.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जग्य बिधंसि कुसल कपि आए रघुपति पास। चलेउ निसाचर कु्रद्ध होइ त्यागि जिवन कै आस ॥
translation: यज्ञ विध्वंस करके सब चतुर वानर रघुनाथजी के पास आ गए। तब रावण जीने की आश छोड़कर क्रोधित होकर चला ॥
english_translation: The clever monkeys returned to Raghupati after ruining the sacrifice. Then Ravana, abandoning all hope of living, went off in anger.
essence: Pride leaves in anger when hope is gone.
simple_meaning: The monkeys returned to Ram after disrupting the sacrifice, and Ravana left in fury, no longer hoping to survive.
insight: It shifts attention from action to aftermath: victory gathers the righteous, while ego leaves in fury.
modern_relevance: A project has gone wrong, the room is tense, and someone storms out after losing control. The verse captures that moment when pride turns into anger because hope has already cracked.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चलत होहिं अति असुभ भयंकर। बैठहिं गीध उड़ाइ सिरन्ह पर॥ भयउ कालबस काहु न माना। कहेसि बजावहु जुद्ध निसाना ॥
translation: चलते समय अत्यंत भयंकर अमंगल (अपशकुन) होने लगे। गीध उड़-उड़कर उसके सिरों पर बैठने लगे, किन्तु वह काल के वश था, इससे किसी भी अपशकुन को नहीं मानता था। उसने कहा- युद्ध का डंका बजाओ ॥
english_translation: As he walked, terrible omens appeared. Vultures circled and sat on his heads, but he was under the sway of time and ignored every sign. He ordered the war drums to sound.
essence: Pride can make even clear warning signs useless.
simple_meaning: Terrible signs appeared, but Ravana ignored them and ordered the war drums sounded.
insight: It shows how a mind captured by ego stops reading reality and rushes toward ruin.
modern_relevance: You keep pushing ahead after the warning lights come on, telling yourself it will be fine. By the time you admit the risk, the decision has already hardened.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: चली तमीचर अनी अपारा। बहु गज रथ पदाति असवारा॥ प्रभु सन्मुख धाए खल कैसें। सलभ समूह अनल कहँ जैसें ॥
translation: निशाचरों की अपार सेना चली। उसमें बहुत से हाथी, रथ, घुड़सवार और पैदल हैं। वे दुष्ट प्रभु के सामने कैसे दौड़े, जैसे पतंगों के समूह अग्नि की ओर (जलने के लिए) दौड़ते हैं॥।2॥
english_translation: The immense army of night-dwellers marched on, with many elephants, chariots, horsemen, and foot soldiers. How could those wicked ones rush before the Lord, like a swarm of moths racing into fire?
essence: Might can rush forward and still be helpless.
simple_meaning: Ravana's vast army advances with every kind of war machine and soldier, but its rush toward Ram is as futile as moths flying into fire.
insight: It shifts the mind from admiring raw force to seeing its fragility before a higher order.
modern_relevance: A room full of people may back the wrong choice, and the momentum can feel unstoppable. But sheer force does not make a thing wise, safe, or lasting.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: इहाँ देवतन्ह अस्तुति कीन्ही। दारुन बिपति हमहि एहिं दीन्ही॥ अब जनि राम खेलावहु एही। अतिसय दुखित होति बैदेही ॥
translation: इधर देवताओं ने स्तुति की कि हे श्री रामजी! इसने हमको दारुण दुःख दिए हैं। अब आप इसे (अधिक) न खेलाइए। जानकीजी बहुत ही दुःखी हो रही हैं ॥
english_translation: Here the gods offered praise: "This has brought us terrible suffering. Now do not keep playing with him; Sita is deeply distressed."
essence: Relief matters more than display.
simple_meaning: The gods praise Ram and ask him to stop prolonging Sita's suffering.
insight: It frames rescue as an act of compassion, not spectacle.
modern_relevance: You finally have the chance to end a painful situation, and everyone is waiting for relief. The kindest move is not to stretch the moment any longer.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देव बचन सुनि प्रभु मुसुकाना। उठि रघुबीर सुधारे बाना॥ जटा जूट दृढ़ बाँधें माथे। सोहहिं सुमन बीच बिच गाथे ॥
translation: देवताओं के वचन सुनकर प्रभु मुस्कुराए। फिर श्री रघुवीर ने उठकर बाण सुधारे। मस्तक पर जटाओं के जूड़े को कसकर बाँधे हुए हैं, उसके बीच-बीच में पुष्प गूँथे हुए शोभित हो रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing the gods' words, the Lord smiled. Rising up, Raghubir adjusted his arrow. His matted hair was tightly bound on his head, with flowers woven through it, shining beautifully.
essence: Calm strength prepares for action without losing gentleness.
simple_meaning: Ram smiles at the gods' plea, then prepares his bow and stands ready for battle, crowned with matted hair and flowers.
insight: It shows that strength and composure can belong to the same moment.
modern_relevance: When a tense message lands on your phone and your chest tightens, you can still pause, breathe, and respond without losing your center.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अरुन नयन बारिद तनु स्यामा। अखिल लोक लोचनाभिरामा॥ कटितट परिकर कस्यो निषंगा। कर कोदंड कठिन सारंगा ॥
translation: लाल नेत्र और मेघ के समान श्याम शरीर वाले और संपूर्ण लोकों के नेत्रों को आनंद देने वाले हैं। प्रभु ने कमर में फेंटा तथा तरकस कस लिया और हाथ में कठोर शार्गं धनुष ले लिया ॥
english_translation: His eyes were red, his body dark like rainclouds, and he delighted the eyes of all the worlds. He tightened the belt at his waist, fastened his quiver, and took up the hard Saranga bow in his hand.
essence: True readiness is calm, beautiful, and already armed.
simple_meaning: Ram is described as beautiful and ready for battle. He tightens his belt and quiver, then lifts his bow.
insight: It shifts attention from drama to composed readiness before decisive action.
modern_relevance: You pause before a hard conversation, straighten your clothes, and take one steady breath. Readiness can be quiet, beautiful, and complete.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सारंग कर सुंदर निषंग सिलीमुखाकर कटि कस्यो। भुजदंड पीन मनोहरायत उर धरासुर पद लस्यो॥ कह दास तुलसी जबहिं प्रभु सर चाप कर फेरन लगे। ब्रह्मांड दिग्गज कमठ अहि महि सिंधु भूधर डगमगे॥
translation: प्रभु ने हाथ में शार्गं धनुष लेकर कमर में बाणों की खान (अक्षय) सुंदर तरकस कस लिया। उनके भुजदण्ड पुष्ट हैं और मनोहर चौड़ी छाती पर ब्राह्मण (भृगुजी) के चरण का चिह्न शोभित है। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं, ज्यों ही प्रभु धनुष-बाण हाथ में लेकर फिराने लगे, त्यों ही ब्रह्माण्ड, दिशाओं के हाथी, कच्छप, शेषजी, पृथ्वी, समुद्र और पर्वत सभी डगमगा उठे।
english_translation: He took the beautiful Saranga bow and the quiver of arrows at his waist. His powerful arms were lovely, and the mark of the brahmin's feet shone on his broad chest. Tulsidas says that as soon as the Lord began to turn the bow and arrow in his hands, the universe, the guardians of the directions, the cosmic turtle, Shesha, the earth, the ocean, and the mountains all trembled.
essence: Ram's smallest movement reveals a power that shakes the cosmos.
simple_meaning: Ram takes up his bow and arrows, and the whole cosmos trembles at the sight of his power.
insight: It shifts attention from visible action to the power beneath it: Ram's mere movement reveals cosmic authority.
modern_relevance: You watch someone calm and unhurried walk into the room, and the mood shifts before they speak. Some presence carries weight without noise.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सोभा देखि हरषि सुर बरषहिं सुमन अपार। जय जय जय करुनानिधि छबि बल गुन आगार ॥
translation: (भगवान् की) शोभा देखकर देवता हर्षित होकर फूलों की अपार वर्षा करने लगे और शोभा, शक्ति और गुणों के धाम करुणानिधान प्रभु की जय हो, जय हो, जय हो (ऐसा पुकारने लगे) ॥
english_translation: Seeing his splendor, the devas rejoiced and showered endless flowers. "Victory, victory, victory to the compassionate one, the source of beauty, strength, and virtues!"
essence: His presence makes praise the only possible response.
simple_meaning: The devas are so moved by Ram's beauty that they shower flowers and praise him as the compassionate source of beauty, strength, and virtue.
insight: It frames true greatness as something that naturally draws reverence, not self-display.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the tension changes before you speak. Sometimes the calm, strength, and kindness you carry announce themselves more clearly than words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहीं बीच निसाचर अनी। कसमसात आई अति घनी॥ देखि चले सन्मुख कपि भट्टा। प्रलयकाल के जनु घन घट्टा ॥
translation: इसी बीच में निशाचरों की अत्यंत घनी सेना कसमसाती हुई (आपस में टकराती हुई) आई। उसे देखकर वानर योद्धा इस प्रकार (उसके) सामने चले जैसे प्रलयकाल के बादलों के समूह हों ॥
english_translation: In that moment, the demon army surged forward in a dense, crashing mass. Seeing it, the monkey warriors advanced like clouds at the end of cosmic dissolution.
essence: The two armies meet like storm clouds before the end.
simple_meaning: The demon army rushes in, and the monkey warriors move to meet it head-on like storm clouds before destruction.
insight: It sets the battle in motion and shows both armies closing in without delay.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहु कृपान तरवारि चमंकहिं। जनु दहँ दिसि दामिनीं दमंकहिं॥ गज रथ तुरग चिकार कठोरा। गर्जहिं मनहुँ बलाहक घोरा ॥
translation: बहुत से कृपाल और तलवारें चमक रही हैं। मानो दसों दिशाओं में बिजलियाँ चमक रही हों। हाथी, रथ और घोड़ों का कठोर चिंग्घाड़ ऐसा लगता है मानो बादल भयंकर गर्जन कर रहे हों ॥
english_translation: Many spears and swords flash like lightning in all ten directions. Elephants, chariots, and horses cry out harshly, as if dark clouds were thundering.
essence: War arrives like a storm of flashing steel and thunder.
simple_meaning: Weapons flash everywhere while elephants, chariots, and horses thunder and cry out. The battlefield feels like a storm made of metal and noise.
insight: It turns battle into a sensory image so the reader feels its scale before the fighting begins.
modern_relevance: You walk into a crowded station at rush hour: horns, shouting, flashing screens, bodies moving everywhere. Before anything even happens, the whole place already feels like pressure.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कपि लंगूर बिपुल नभ छाए। मनहुँ इंद्रधनु उए सुहाए॥ उठइ धूरि मानहुँ जलधारा। बान बुंद भै बृष्टि अपारा ॥
translation: वानरों की बहुत सी पूँछें आकाश में छाई हुई हैं। (वे ऐसी शोभा दे रही हैं) मानो सुंदर इंद्रधनुष उदय हुए हों। धूल ऐसी उठ रही है मानो जल की धारा हो। बाण रूपी बूँदों की अपार वृष्टि हुई ॥
english_translation: The monkeys' tails filled the sky like beautiful rainbows. Dust rose like a stream of water, and arrows fell in an endless shower.
essence: The battlefield becomes a storm of motion and color.
simple_meaning: The battlefield is so crowded and intense that monkey tails seem to fill the sky, dust looks like flowing water, and arrows fall like heavy rain.
insight: It shifts attention from individual fighters to the scale and chaos of the battle.
modern_relevance: A stadium erupts, dust rises from the ground, flags whip overhead, and the noise turns everything into motion. You feel the whole place become one living surge.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दुहुँ दिसि पर्बत करहिं प्रहारा। बज्रपात जनु बारहिं बारा॥ रघुपति कोपि बान झरि लाई। घायल भै निसिचर समुदाई ॥
translation: दोनों ओर से योद्धा पर्वतों का प्रहार करते हैं। मानो बारंबार वज्रपात हो रहा हो। श्री रघुनाथजी ने क्रोध करके बाणों की झड़ी लगा दी, (जिससे) राक्षसों की सेना घायल हो गई ॥
english_translation: On both sides, warriors hurl mountain-like blows, as if thunderbolts are striking again and again. Lord Raghunath grew fierce and sent a rain of arrows, and the demon army was wounded.
essence: Decisive force can break a chaos that force alone created.
simple_meaning: The battle grows more intense on both sides, and Ram answers the enemy attack with a fierce rain of arrows that wounds their army.
insight: It shifts the mind from passive watching to decisive response under pressure.
modern_relevance: You are in the middle of a crisis call, messages flying, everyone talking over each other. Then you stop hesitating, choose a response, and the whole situation changes.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लागत बान बीर चिक्करहीं। घुर्मि घुर्मि जहँ तहँ महि परहीं॥ स्रवहिं सैल जनु निर्झर भारी। सोनित सरि कादर भयकारी ॥
translation: बाण लगते ही वीर चीत्कार कर उठते हैं और चक्कर खा-खाकर जहाँ-तहाँ पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ते हैं। उनके शरीर से ऐसे खून बह रहा है मानो पर्वत के भारी झरनों से जल बह रहा हो। इस प्रकार डरपोकों को भय उत्पन्न करने वाली रुधिर की नदी बह चली ॥
english_translation: As the arrows strike, the warriors cry out and reel to the ground. Their blood flows like a mountain stream, and a fearsome river of blood runs forth.
essence: War turns bodies into a rushing river of blood.
simple_meaning: Arrows strike the warriors, they cry out and fall, and blood pours across the battlefield like a mountain stream.
insight: It sharpens the battlefield into a vivid image of collapse and terror.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कादर भयंकर रुधिर सरिता चली परम अपावनी। दोउ कूल दल रथ रेत चक्र अबर्त बहति भयावनी॥ जलजंतु गज पदचर तुरग खर बिबिध बाहन को गने। सर सक्ति तोमर सर्प चाप तरंग चर्म कमठ घने॥
translation: डरपोकों को भय उपजाने वाली अत्यंत अपवित्र रक्त की नदी बह चली। दोनों दल उसके दोनों किनारे हैं। रथ रेत है और पहिए भँवर हैं। वह नदी बहुत भयावनी बह रही है। हाथी, पैदल, घोड़े, गदहे तथा अनेकों सवारियाँ ही, जिनकी गिनती कौन करे, नदी के जल जन्तु हैं। बाण, शक्ति और तोमर सर्प हैं, धनुष तरंगें हैं और ढाल बहुत से कछुवे हैं।
english_translation: A terrifying, impure river of blood began to flow. The two armies became its two banks; chariots were sand and wheels were whirlpools. It flowed fearfully. Elephants, foot soldiers, horses, donkeys, and countless mounts became its water-creatures. Arrows, spears, tridents, snakes, bows, waves, shields, and many turtles filled it.
essence: War has become a river of blood that swallows everything.
simple_meaning: The battlefield is compared to a terrifying river made of blood, weapons, bodies, and wreckage.
insight: It turns battle into a single overwhelming image of collapse, not a series of separate actions.
modern_relevance: After a fight explodes in a crowded street, broken glass, shouting, and sirens blur together. Nothing looks orderly anymore; everything feels swept into the same violence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बीर परहिं जनु तीर तरु मज्जा बहु बह फेन। कादर देखि डरहिं तहँ सुभटन्ह के मन चेन ॥
translation: वीर पृथ्वी पर इस तरह गिर रहे हैं, मानो नदी-किनारे के वृक्ष ढह रहे हों। बहुत सी मज्जा बह रही है, वही फेन है। डरपोक जहाँ इसे देखकर डरते हैं, वहाँ उत्तम योद्धाओं के मन में सुख होता है ॥
english_translation: Heroes fall like trees on a riverbank; their marrow flows like foam. Cowards are afraid, but brave hearts find comfort there.
essence: The same battlefield frightens the timid and steadies the brave.
simple_meaning: The battlefield is so fierce that fallen warriors look like trees collapsing by a river. Cowards are terrified by it, but true warriors feel calm and steady there.
insight: It shows how courage reshapes perception, letting you remain steady in the middle of violence or crisis.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a brutal argument and feel your stomach tighten. Someone else stays calm, seeing the same chaos without flinching.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मज्जहिं भूत पिसाच बेताला। प्रमथ महा झोटिंग कराला॥ काक कंक लै भुजा उड़ाहीं। एक ते छीनि एक लै खाहीं ॥
translation: भूत, पिशाच और बेताल, बड़े-बड़े झोंटों वाले महान् भयंकर झोटिंग और प्रमथ (शिवगण) उस नदी में स्नान करते हैं। कौए और चील भुजाएँ लेकर उड़ते हैं और एक-दूसरे से छीनकर खा जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Ghosts, fiends, and wandering spirits bathe there. Fierce, wild Shiva-attendants too. Crows and vultures fly off with arms, snatching them from one another and eating them.
essence: Violence has made the battlefield feel inhabited by death itself.
simple_meaning: The battlefield has become so horrific that even ghosts, spirits, and fierce beings seem to swarm there. Birds snatch body parts from the dead as the carnage continues.
insight: It shifts attention from combat as heroics to combat as devastation.
modern_relevance: A news clip shows smoke, sirens, and bodies carried past broken walls. You stop looking for winners because the damage has already outgrown victory.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक कहहिं ऐसिउ सौंघाई। सठहु तुम्हार दरिद्र न जाई॥ कहँरत भट घायल तट गिरे। जहँ तहँ मनहुँ अर्धजल परे ॥
translation: एक (कोई) कहते हैं, अरे मूर्खों! ऐसी सस्ती (बहुतायत) है, फिर भी तुम्हारी दरिद्रता नहीं जाती? घायल योद्धा तट पर पड़े कराह रहे हैं, मानो जहाँ-तहाँ अर्धजल (वे व्यक्ति जो मरने के समय आधे जल में रखे जाते हैं) पड़े हों ॥
english_translation: Someone says, “Fools, is the abundance still not enough to end your poverty?” Wounded warriors lie groaning on the shore, as if half-submerged bodies were scattered everywhere.
essence: War leaves so much ruin that even speech turns bitter.
simple_meaning: The battlefield is so full of wounded men that someone mockingly asks why poverty still remains. The shore looks scattered with half-submerged bodies.
insight: It pulls attention back to the cost of violence, not the spectacle of victory.
modern_relevance: You scroll past headlines of another disaster, and the language starts to sound numb. This verse catches that coldness: suffering becomes so common that even pity can turn sarcastic.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: खैचहिं गीध आँत तट भए। जनु बंसी खेलत चित दए॥ बहु भट बहहिं चढ़े खग जाहीं। जनु नावरि खेलहिं सरि माहीं ॥
translation: गीध आँतें खींच रहे हैं, मानो मछली मार नदी तट पर से चित्त लगाए हुए (ध्यानस्थ होकर) बंसी खेल रहे हों (बंसी से मछली पकड़ रहे हों)। बहुत से योद्धा बहे जा रहे हैं और पक्षी उन पर चढ़े चले जा रहे हैं। मानो वे नदी में नावरि (नौका क्रीड़ा) खेल रहे हों ॥
english_translation: Vultures pull out intestines at the riverbank, as if calmly fishing with a rod. Many warriors float by while birds climb over them, as if they are playing on boats in the river.
essence: War leaves only feeding birds and broken bodies behind.
simple_meaning: The battlefield is so full of death that vultures and birds feed on bodies as if they are casually playing by the river.
insight: It turns the mind away from heroic fantasy and toward the real cost of violence.
modern_relevance: A news feed full of casualty numbers can feel abstract until you picture one body, one family, one loss. This verse refuses abstraction and makes destruction impossible to romanticize.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जोगिनि भरि भरि खप्पर संचहिं। भूति पिसाच बधू नभ नंचहिं॥ भट कपाल करताल बजावहिं। चामुंडा नाना बिधि गावहिं ॥
translation: योगिनियाँ खप्परों में भर-भरकर खून जमा कर रही हैं। भूत-पिशाचों की स्त्रियाँ आकाश में नाच रही हैं। चामुण्डाएँ योद्धाओं की खोपड़ियों का करताल बजा रही हैं और नाना प्रकार से गा रही हैं ॥
english_translation: The yoginis gather blood in their skull-bowls. The wives of ghosts and spirits dance in the sky. The warriors beat skulls like cymbals, and the Chamundas sing in many ways.
essence: Violence fills the world with grotesque celebration.
simple_meaning: The scene turns grotesque and chaotic: blood, skulls, spirits, and wild dancing fill the battlefield.
insight: It turns battle into a vision of disorder, making the cost of violence impossible to ignore.
modern_relevance: A news feed full of wreckage, sirens, and footage of chaos can feel unreal, almost theatrical. This verse captures that sickening moment when destruction stops looking human.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जंबुक निकर कटक्कट कट्टहिं। खाहिं हुआहिं अघाहिं दपट्टहिं॥ कोटिन्ह रुंड मुंड बिनु डोल्लहिं। सीस परे महि जय जय बोल्लहिं ॥
translation: गीदड़ों के समूह कट-कट शब्द करते हुए मुरदों को काटते, खाते, हुआँ-हुआँ करते और पेट भर जाने पर एक-दूसरे को डाँटते हैं। करोड़ों धड़ बिना सिर के घूम रहे हैं और सिर पृथ्वी पर पड़े जय-जय बोल रहे है ॥ छंद :
english_translation: The jackals make a crackling sound as they tear and eat the dead, growling and snapping after they have had enough. Countless headless bodies roam about, while heads fallen on the ground shout, “Victory! Victory!”
essence: Violence keeps moving after victory has already been lost.
simple_meaning: The battlefield is so ruined that jackals feed on the dead, and even severed heads seem to cry victory. It is a scene of total collapse.
insight: It strips away the glamour of war and shows only its emptiness and destruction.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बोल्लहिं जो जय जय मुंड रुंड प्रचंड सिर बिनु धावहीं। खप्परिन्ह खग्ग अलुज्झि जुज्झहिं सुभट भटन्ह ढहावहीं॥ बानर निसाचर निकर मर्दहिं राम बल दर्पित भए। संग्राम अंगन सुभट सोवहिं राम सर निकरन्हि हए॥
translation: मुण्ड (कटे सिर) जय-जय बोल बोलते हैं और प्रचण्ड रुण्ड (धड़) बिना सिर के दौड़ते हैं। पक्षी खोपड़ियों में उलझ-उलझकर परस्पर लड़े मरते हैं, उत्तम योद्धा दूसरे योद्धाओं को ढहा रहे हैं। श्री रामचंद्रजी बल से दर्पित हुए वानर राक्षसों के झुंडों को मसले डालते हैं। श्री रामजी के बाण समूहों से मरे हुए योद्धा लड़ाई के मैदान में सो रहे हैं।
english_translation: Heads shout victory, and fierce headless trunks run on. Birds clash in skulls and warriors strike one another down. Monkeys and demons crush each other, swollen with Ram's power. On the battlefield, brave fighters lie as if asleep, struck by Ram's arrows.
essence: Ram's force leaves the battlefield stunned and still.
simple_meaning: The battlefield is full of violent, surreal destruction. Ram's arrows and power are overwhelming the enemy, and warriors lie fallen everywhere.
insight: It presents war as total collapse, not heroic spectacle.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रावन हृदयँ बिचारा भा निसिचर संघार। मैं अकेल कपि भालु बहु माया करौं अपार ॥
translation: रावण ने हृदय में विचारा कि राक्षसों का नाश हो गया है। मैं अकेला हूँ और वानर-भालू बहुत हैं, इसलिए मैं अब अपार माया रचूँ ॥
english_translation: Ravana thought in his heart: the demons have been destroyed. I am alone, while the monkeys and bears are many, so now I will create immense illusion.
essence: When fear takes over, deception feels like strength.
simple_meaning: Ravana sees that his army is gone and he is outnumbered, so he turns to deception to keep fighting.
insight: It shows how a threatened ego chooses manipulation when honest response would demand humility.
modern_relevance: You realize your plan is failing, your team is shrinking, and instead of facing it cleanly, you start patching with half-truths and spin.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: देवन्ह प्रभुहि पयादें देखा। उपजा उर अति छोभ बिसेषा॥ सुरपति निज रथ तुरत पठावा। हरष सहित मातलि लै आवा ॥
translation: देवताओं ने प्रभु को पैदल (बिना सवारी के युद्ध करते) देखा, तो उनके हृदय में बड़ा भारी क्षोभ (दुःख) उत्पन्न हुआ। (फिर क्या था) इंद्र ने तुरंत अपना रथ भेज दिया। (उसका सारथी) मातलि हर्ष के साथ उसे ले आया ॥
english_translation: The devas saw the Lord fighting on foot and felt deep distress. Then Indra quickly sent his chariot, and Matali brought it joyfully.
essence: Even the victorious need help before the battle is over.
simple_meaning: The devas saw Ram fighting without a chariot and felt concern. Indra immediately sent his chariot, and Matali brought it with joy.
insight: It shows that true strength can still need support, and support can arrive as soon as it is seen.
modern_relevance: You keep doing everything yourself while everyone else watches. Then someone finally notices the load and steps in before you collapse.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेज पुंज रथ दिब्य अनूपा। हरषि चढ़े कोसलपुर भूपा॥ चंचल तुरग मनोहर चारी। अजर अमर मन सम गतिकारी ॥
translation: उस दिव्य अनुपम और तेज के पुंज (तेजोमय) रथ पर कोसलपुरी के राजा श्री रामचंद्रजी हर्षित होकर चढ़े। उसमें चार चंचल, मनोहर, अजर, अमर और मन की गति के समान शीघ्र चलने वाले (देवलोक के) घोड़े जुते थे ॥
english_translation: Ram, the lord of Kosala, joyfully climbed onto that radiant, incomparable, divine chariot. Four lovely, swift horses were yoked to it, moving as fast as the mind itself.
essence: Grace arrives as strength when the struggle is already underway.
simple_meaning: Ram mounts a radiant divine chariot with four beautiful, swift horses.
insight: It shifts attention from strain to divine assistance arriving at the right moment.
modern_relevance: You finally get the right support after carrying too much alone. The burden does not vanish, but the path opens and movement becomes possible again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रथारूढ़ रघुनाथहि देखी। धाए कपि बलु पाइ बिसेषी॥ सही न जाइ कपिन्ह कै मारी। तब रावन माया बिस्तारी ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी को रथ पर चढ़े देखकर वानर विशेष बल पाकर दौड़े। वानरों की मार सही नहीं जाती। तब रावण ने माया फैलाई ॥
english_translation: Seeing Raghunath seated on the chariot, the monkeys surged forward with renewed strength. The monkeys' blows could not be endured, so Ravana spread his illusion.
essence: Steady presence gives others strength; desperation turns to illusion.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram on the chariot, the monkeys rushed in with fresh courage. Ravana then used illusion because the monkeys' attack was too strong to bear.
insight: It shows how visible steadiness can energize a whole group, while panic reaches for tricks when direct resistance fails.
modern_relevance: You spot your team lead step into the chaos and suddenly everyone straightens up. Momentum changes before anyone says a word.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सो माया रघुबीरहि बाँची। लछिमन कपिन्ह सो मानी साँची॥ देखी कपिन्ह निसाचर अनी। अनुज सहित बहु कोसलधनी ॥
translation: एक श्री रघुवीर के ही वह माया नहीं लगी। सब वानरों ने और लक्ष्मणजी ने भी उस माया को सच मान लिया। वानरों ने राक्षसी सेना में भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित बहुत से रामों को देखा ॥
english_translation: Only Raghubir was untouched by that illusion. The monkeys and Lakshman took it as real, and they saw many Rakshasa warriors and many Ramas, with Lakshman and the prince of Kosala among them.
essence: Illusion distorts everyone except the one who is steady.
simple_meaning: Ravana's illusion affected the monkeys and Lakshman, but not Ram. They saw a confusing battlefield image of many enemy warriors and many Ramas.
insight: It shows how confusion spreads through a frightened crowd, while steady awareness stays clear.
modern_relevance: In the middle of a tense group chat, one misleading message can make everyone see a crisis that isn't there. Panic multiplies the illusion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहु राम लछिमन देखि मर्कट भालु मन अति अपडरे। जनु चित्र लिखित समेत लछिमन जहँ सो तहँ चितवहिं खरे॥ निज सेन चकित बिलोकि हँसि सर चाप सजि कोसलधनी। माया हरी हरि निमिष महुँ हरषी सकल मर्कट अनी॥
translation: बहुत से राम-लक्ष्मण देखकर वानर-भालू मन में मिथ्या डर से बहुत ही डर गए। लक्ष्मणजी सहित वे मानो चित्र लिखे से जहाँ के तहाँ खड़े देखने लगे। अपनी सेना को आश्चर्यचकित देखकर कोसलपति भगवान् हरि (दुःखों के हरने वाले श्री रामजी) ने हँसकर धनुष पर बाण चढ़ाकर, पल भर में सारी माया हर ली। वानरों की सारी सेना हर्षित हो गई।
english_translation: Seeing Ram and Lakshman, the monkeys and bears became deeply afraid. They stood frozen, as though painted in a picture, wherever Lakshman was seen. Seeing his own army stunned, the Lord of Kosala smiled, drew his bow, and in an instant removed the illusion. The entire monkey army rejoiced.
essence: Steady presence breaks the spell of fear.
simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears are briefly overwhelmed by Ravana's illusion, but Ram smiles, raises his bow, and breaks the spell at once.
insight: It shows how calm strength can dissolve fear faster than argument or panic.
modern_relevance: A group chat spirals into panic after one alarming message, and everyone starts imagining the worst. Then one steady voice answers clearly, and the whole mood changes in a second.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरि राम सब तन चितइ बोले बचन गँभीर। द्वंदजुद्ध देखहु सकल श्रमित भए अति बीर ॥
translation: फिर श्री रामजी सबकी ओर देखकर गंभीर वचन बोले- हे वीरों! तुम सब बहुत ही थक गए हो, इसलिए अब (मेरा और रावण का) द्वंद्व युद्ध देखो ॥
english_translation: Then Ram looked at everyone and spoke in a grave voice: "O heroes, you are all greatly tired, so now watch the duel."
essence: When everyone is spent, the real battle must be faced directly.
simple_meaning: Ram sees that the warriors are exhausted and tells them to watch the duel instead of fighting on.
insight: It shifts attention from scattered effort to the one निर्णायक confrontation that actually matters.
modern_relevance: After a long day of arguments, deadlines, and half-finished battles, you finally stop trying to do everything yourself and let the main issue stand in the open.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: अस कहि रथ रघुनाथ चलावा। बिप्र चरन पंकज सिरु नावा॥ तब लंकेस क्रोध उर छावा। गर्जत तर्जत सम्मुख धावा ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने ब्राह्मणों के चरणकमलों में सिर नवाया और फिर रथ चलाया। तब रावण के हृदय में क्रोध छा गया और वह गरजता तथा ललकारता हुआ सामने दौड़ा ॥
english_translation: After saying this, Lord Raghunath bowed his head to the feet of the brahmins and drove the chariot forward. Then anger filled Ravana's heart, and he rushed forward roaring and challenging.
essence: Respect steadies Ram; anger drives Ravana into battle.
simple_meaning: Ram bows to the brahmins before moving ahead, while Ravana is filled with anger and rushes to attack.
insight: It contrasts grounded action with ego-driven reaction, preparing the mind for the duel that follows.
modern_relevance: You stay calm, do the respectful thing, and move forward anyway. Someone else may explode in reaction, but their noise does not change your footing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जीतेहु जे भट संजुग माहीं। सुनु तापस मैं तिन्ह सम नाहीं॥ रावन नाम जगत जस जाना। लोकप जाकें बंदीखाना ॥
translation: (उसने कहा-) अरे तपस्वी! सुनो, तुमने युद्ध में जिन योद्धाओं को जीता है, मैं उनके समान नहीं हूँ। मेरा नाम रावण है, मेरा यश सारा जगत् जानता है, लोकपाल तक जिसके कैद खाने में पड़े हैं ॥
english_translation: “Listen, ascetic: I am not like the warriors you have defeated in battle. My name is Ravana, known throughout the world. Even the guardians of the world are prisoners in my fortress.”
essence: Pride speaks loudest when it fears being measured.
simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he is unlike the enemies already defeated, claiming world-famous power and control over even the guardians of the world.
insight: It exposes how ego uses reputation and power as armor against being seen clearly.
modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in a meeting, then starts listing titles, followers, and past wins to shut everyone down. The noise is trying to cover the insecurity underneath.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: खर दूषन बिराध तुम्ह मारा। बधेहु ब्याध इव बालि बिचारा॥ निसिचर निकर सुभट संघारेहु। कुंभकरन घननादहि मारेहु ॥
translation: तुमने खर, दूषण और विराध को मारा! बेचारे बालि का व्याध की तरह वध किया। बड़े-बड़े राक्षस योद्धाओं के समूह का संहार किया और कुंभकर्ण तथा मेघनाद को भी मारा ॥
english_translation: You killed Khara, Dushana, and Viradha; you struck down Bali like a hunter. You destroyed ranks of demons and killed Kumbhakarna and Meghnad.
essence: Even Ravana admits Ram's power before rushing toward defeat.
simple_meaning: Ravana lists Ram's past victories over powerful enemies to boast that he is no easy opponent.
insight: It shows a mind trying to steady itself by naming the opponent's strength before attacking.
modern_relevance: You’re arguing with someone who has already outperformed everyone else in the room. You list their wins, but your voice is really shaking with the size of the challenge.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: आजु बयरु सबु लेउँ निबाही। जौं रन भूप भाजि नहिं जाही॥ आजु करउँ खलु काल हवाले। परेहु कठिन रावन के पाले ॥
translation: अरे राजा! यदि तुम रण से भाग न गए तो आज मैं (वह) सारा वैर निकाल लूँगा। आज मैं तुम्हें निश्चय ही काल के हवाले कर दूँगा। तुम कठिन रावण के पाले पड़े हो ॥
english_translation: Today I will settle this old enmity. If you do not flee the battlefield, I will send you to death today. You have fallen into Ravana's grasp.
essence: Arrogance speaks most loudly when it feels cornered.
simple_meaning: Ravana threatens to finish the fight today and says he will hand the king over to death if he does not run away.
insight: It exposes how ego masks vulnerability with threats.
modern_relevance: Someone cornered in an argument suddenly starts sounding fierce, not because they are strong, but because they feel exposed. The louder they speak, the more fear leaks through.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: सुनि दुर्बचन कालबस जाना। बिहँसि बचन कह कृपानिधाना॥ सत्य सत्य सब तव प्रभुताई। जल्पसि जनि देखाउ मनुसाई ॥
translation: रावण के दुर्वचन सुनकर और उसे कालवश जान कृपानिधान श्री रामजी ने हँसकर यह वचन कहा- तुम्हारी सारी प्रभुता, जैसा तुम कहते हो, बिल्कुल सच है। पर अब व्यर्थ बकवाद न करो, अपना पुरुषार्थ दिखलाओ ॥
english_translation: Hearing Ravana's harsh words and knowing he was under the power of time, the Lord of compassion smiled and said: "Yes, yes, all your greatness is true. But stop the empty boasting and show your real strength."
essence: Real strength does not need bragging; it proves itself in action.
simple_meaning: Ram hears Ravana's insults, laughs, and tells him not to waste time bragging. If Ravana has strength, he should prove it in action.
insight: It shifts attention from verbal aggression to tested capacity. The verse teaches you to meet bluster with calm and let reality speak.
modern_relevance: Someone sends a long angry text, full of threats and self-importance. You read it once, breathe, and realize the noise is bigger than the power behind it.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जनि जल्पना करि सुजसु नासहि नीति सुनहि करहि छमा। संसार महँ पूरुष त्रिबिध पाटल रसाल पनस समा॥ एक सुमनप्रद एक सुमन फल एक फलइ केवल लागहीं। एक कहहिं कहहिं करहिं अपर एक करहिं कहत न बागहीं॥
translation: व्यर्थ बकवाद करके अपने सुंदर यश का नाश न करो। क्षमा करना, तुम्हें नीति सुनाता हूँ, सुनो! संसार में तीन प्रकार के पुरुष होते हैं- पाटल (गुलाब), आम और कटहल के समान। एक (पाटल) फूल देते हैं, एक (आम) फूल और फल दोनों देते हैं एक (कटहल) में केवल फल ही लगते हैं। इसी प्रकार (पुरुषों में) एक कहते हैं (करते नहीं), दूसरे कहते और करते भी हैं और एक (तीसरे) केवल करते हैं, पर वाणी से कहते नहीं॥
english_translation: Do not waste your good name with empty talk. Listen to this policy: in the world there are three kinds of people, like pātal, mango, and jackfruit. One gives only flowers, one gives both flowers and fruit, and one bears fruit without showing flowers. In the same way, one speaks but does not act, one speaks and acts, and one acts without speaking.
essence: Your deeds should outlast your words.
simple_meaning: Empty talk can ruin your reputation. The wise person is not the one who only speaks, but the one whose words and actions match.
insight: It shifts attention from sounding wise to becoming reliable.
modern_relevance: You make a big promise in a family group chat, then disappear when the day comes. The verse cuts through that gap between image and follow-through.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: राम बचन सुनि बिहँसा मोहि सिखावत ग्यान। बयरु करत नहिं तब डरे अब लागे प्रिय प्रान ॥
translation: श्री रामजी के वचन सुनकर वह खूब हँसा (और बोला-) मुझे ज्ञान सिखाते हो? उस समय वैर करते तो नहीं डरे, अब प्राण प्यारे लग रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing Ram's words, he laughed: 'You are teaching me wisdom? You did not fear then, when you fought me; now you call my life dear.'
essence: Pride mocks wisdom until danger makes it flinch.
simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Ram's advice and says Ram was not afraid to fight before, so he should not act concerned now.
insight: It reveals how ego turns guidance into provocation and makes peace harder the moment it is offered.
modern_relevance: You finally call out a friend's destructive pattern, and they smirk, saying you only care now that things are serious. The defensive laugh comes before the regret.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: कहि दुर्बचन क्रुद्ध दसकंधर। कुलिस समान लाग छाँड़ै सर॥॥ नानाकार सिलीमुख धाए। दिसि अरु बिदिसि गगन महि छाए ॥
translation: दुर्वचन कहकर रावण क्रुद्ध होकर वज्र के समान बाण छोड़ने लगा। अनेकों आकार के बाण दौड़े और दिशा, विदिशा तथा आकाश और पृथ्वी में, सब जगह छा गए ॥
english_translation: Ravana, enraged, hurled arrows like thunderbolts after speaking harsh words. Arrows of many kinds rushed forth and filled the sky and earth in every direction.
essence: Rage throws force everywhere and still cannot find a center.
simple_meaning: Ravana, angry after speaking harshly, unleashes a storm of arrows in every direction.
insight: It shows anger as scattered, self-defeating action rather than clear strength.
modern_relevance: Someone fires off three furious texts, then keeps adding more, making the mess bigger with every reply. Rage often feels powerful right before it becomes reckless.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: पावक सर छाँड़ेउ रघुबीरा। छन महुँ जरे निसाचर तीरा॥ छाड़िसि तीब्र सक्ति खिसिआई। बान संग प्रभु फेरि चलाई ॥
translation: श्री रघुवीर ने अग्निबाण छोड़ा, (जिससे) रावण के सब बाण क्षणभर में भस्म हो गए। तब उसने खिसियाकर तीक्ष्ण शक्ति छोड़ी, (किन्तु) श्री रामचंद्रजी ने उसको बाण के साथ वापस भेज दिया ॥
english_translation: Raghubir released a fire-arrow, and in an instant it burned up the demon-king's arrows. Then, in anger, Ravana hurled a fierce weapon, but Lord Ram sent it back along with his own arrow.
essence: Ram's calm power turns Ravana's fury back on itself.
simple_meaning: Ram burns Ravana's arrows at once, then returns Ravana's weapon back at him.
insight: It shows overwhelming skill in battle, where every attack is neutralized and reversed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कोटिन्ह चक्र त्रिसूल पबारै। बिनु प्रयास प्रभु काटि निवारै॥ निफल होहिं रावन सर कैसें। खल के सकल मनोरथ जैसें ॥
translation: वह करोड़ों चक्र और त्रिशूल चलाता है, परन्तु प्रभु उन्हें बिना ही परिश्रम काटकर हटा देते हैं। रावण के बाण किस प्रकार निष्फल होते हैं, जैसे दुष्ट मनुष्य के सब मनोरथ! ॥
english_translation: He hurls millions of discus and tridents, yet the Lord cuts them away without effort. Ravana's arrows fail just like the desires of a wicked heart.
essence: Desire can throw everything and still reach nothing.
simple_meaning: Ravana throws every weapon he has, but Ram effortlessly cuts them down. His attacks fail completely, like selfish desires that never truly satisfy.
insight: It shifts attention from aggressive force to the emptiness of unchecked wanting.
modern_relevance: You keep refreshing the email thread, sending one more message, one more push. But some battles are already over in your mind long before the other side moves.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब सत बान सारथी मारेसि। परेउ भूमि जय राम पुकारेसि॥ राम कृपा करि सूत उठावा। तब प्रभु परम क्रोध कहुँ पावा ॥
translation: तब उसने श्री रामजी के सारथी को सौ बाण मारे। वह श्री रामजी की जय पुकारकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा। श्री रामजी ने कृपा करके सारथी को उठाया। तब प्रभु अत्यंत क्रोध को प्राप्त हुए ॥
english_translation: Then he struck Ram's charioteer with a hundred arrows. He fell to the ground, crying, "Victory to Ram!" Ram, in compassion, lifted the charioteer up. Then the Lord became intensely wrathful.
essence: Mercy can become the fire that ends cruelty.
simple_meaning: Ravana strikes Ram's charioteer down, but the fallen man still cries Ram's victory. Ram lifts him up with compassion, and that mercy turns into fierce anger against Ravana.
insight: It shows that tenderness and fierce action can arise from the same heart.
modern_relevance: You watch someone get humiliated in front of everyone, and the room goes silent. The urge to protect them rises instantly — not from ego, but from care.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भए क्रुद्ध जुद्ध बिरुद्ध रघुपति त्रोन सायक कसमसे। कोदंड धुनि अति चंड सुनि मनुजाद सब मारुत ग्रसे॥ मंदोदरी उर कंप कंपति कमठ भू भूधर त्रसे। चिक्करहिं दिग्गज दसन गहि महि देखि कौतुक सुर हँसे॥
translation: युद्ध में शत्रु के विरुद्ध श्री रघुनाथजी क्रोधित हुए, तब तरकस में बाण कसमसाने लगे (बाहर निकलने को आतुर होने लगे)। उनके धनुष का अत्यंत प्रचण्ड शब्द (टंकार) सुनकर मनुष्यभक्षी सब राक्षस वातग्रस्त हो गए (अत्यंत भयभीत हो गए)। मंदोदरी का हृदय काँप उठा, समुद्र, कच्छप, पृथ्वी और पर्वत डर गए। दिशाओं के हाथी पृथ्वी को दाँतों से पकड़कर चिग्घाड़ने लगे। यह कौतुक देखकर देवता हँसे।
english_translation: In battle, Raghupati grew fierce against his enemies, and the arrows in his quiver seemed eager to spring forth. Hearing the terrible roar of his bow, the man-eating demons were struck with fear. Mandodari's heart trembled, the sea, tortoise, earth, and mountains shook, and the elephants of the directions cried out. Seeing this wonder, the radiant beings laughed.
