essence: Ram's battle fury makes the whole world tremble.
simple_meaning: Ram's anger in battle shakes everything around him. His bow roars, his enemies panic, and even the sea, mountains, and celestial beings react.
insight: It shows how righteous force can expose fear instantly and change the atmosphere around a conflict.
modern_relevance: A room goes silent when the leader finally speaks with force. Everyone feels the shift, not because of volume alone, but because the moment has become undeniable.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तानेउ चाप श्रवन लगि छाँड़े बिसिख कराल। राम मारगन गन चले लहलहात जनु ब्याल ॥
translation: धनुष को कान तक तानकर श्री रामचंद्रजी ने भयानक बाण छोड़े। श्री रामजी के बाण समूह ऐसे चले मानो सर्प लहलहाते (लहराते) हुए जा रहे हों ॥
english_translation: Drawing his bow to his ear, Ram released terrible arrows. His arrows moved like writhing serpents.
essence: Ram's arrows turn the battlefield into a place of sudden terror.
simple_meaning: Ram draws his bow to his ear and releases fierce arrows that move like snakes.
insight: It shifts attention from the person to the force of the strike.
modern_relevance: A tense room goes silent after one sharp decision. The next move lands hard, and everyone feels the change immediately.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चले बान सपच्छ जनु उरगा। प्रथमहिं हतेउ सारथी तुरगा॥ रथ बिभंजि हति केतु पताका। गर्जा अति अंतर बल थाका ॥
translation: बाण ऐसे चले मानो पंख वाले सर्प उड़ रहे हों। उन्होंने पहले सारथी और घोड़ों को मार डाला। फिर रथ को चूर-चूर करके ध्वजा और पताकाओं को गिरा दिया। तब रावण बड़े जोर से गरजा, पर भीतर से उसका बल थक गया था ॥
english_translation: Rama's arrows flew like winged serpents. They first struck down the charioteer and horses. Then they shattered the chariot and brought down the flag and pennants. Ravana roared loudly, but his inner strength was already exhausted.
essence: Ravana's roar remains, but his strength is already spent.
simple_meaning: Rama's arrows cut down Ravana's chariot, horses, and banner. Ravana still roared, but his inner power was already fading.
insight: It shifts attention from loud resistance to the quiet collapse beneath it.
modern_relevance: You keep talking tough in a meeting after your plan has already fallen apart. The volume is still there, but everyone can feel the weakness underneath.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तुरत आन रथ चढ़ि खिसिआना। अस्त्र सस्त्र छाँड़ेसि बिधि नाना॥ बिफल होहिं सब उद्यम ताके। जिमि परद्रोह निरत मनसा के ॥
translation: तुरंत दूसरे रथ पर चढ़कर खिसियाकर उसने नाना प्रकार के अस्त्र-शस्त्र छोड़े। उसके सब उद्योग वैसे ही निष्फल हो गए, जैसे परद्रोह में लगे हुए चित्त वाले मनुष्य के होते हैं ॥
english_translation: He quickly climbed another chariot, irritated, and hurled many kinds of weapons. All his efforts failed, just like the efforts of a mind bent on harming others.
essence: Anger makes even strong effort collapse.
simple_meaning: Ravana jumps to another chariot and attacks again, but his rage only makes his efforts fail. The verse compares that failure to the wasted energy of a harmful mind.
insight: It turns rage into a self-defeating force and shows how hostile intent poisons action.
modern_relevance: You fire off another angry email after the first one backfires, then another. The more you push from irritation, the more your own effort starts working against you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब रावन दस सूल चलावा। बाजि चारि महि मारि गिरावा॥ तुरग उठाइ कोपि रघुनायक। खैंचि सरासन छाँड़े सायक ॥
translation: तब रावण ने दस त्रिशूल चलाए और श्री रामजी के चारों घोड़ों को मारकर पृथ्वी पर गिरा दिया। घोड़ों को उठाकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने क्रोध करके धनुष खींचकर बाण छोड़े ॥
english_translation: Then Ravana hurled ten tridents, killing Ram's four horses and casting them to the ground. Ram lifted the horses, grew angry, drew his bow, and released arrows.
essence: Attack can shake your setup, not your center.
simple_meaning: Ravana attacks Ram's chariot and horses, and Ram responds by lifting the horses, drawing his bow, and firing arrows.
insight: It shows how a true fighter recovers instantly and answers attack without collapse.
modern_relevance: Your plans get wrecked five minutes before the presentation starts. You don't freeze; you reset, steady yourself, and respond with force.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रावन सिर सरोज बनचारी। चलि रघुबीर सिलीमुख धारी॥ दस दस बान भाल दस मारे। निसरि गए चले रुधिर पनारे ॥
translation: रावण के सिर रूपी कमल वन में विचरण करने वाले श्री रघुवीर के बाण रूपी भ्रमरों की पंक्ति चली। श्री रामचंद्रजी ने उसके दसों सिरों में दस-दस बाण मारे, जो आर-पार हो गए और सिरों से रक्त के पनाले बह चले ॥
english_translation: Like bees moving through a lotus forest of Ravana’s heads, the arrows of Raghubir flew on. Ram struck all ten of Ravana’s heads with ten arrows each, and streams of blood poured out.
essence: Relentless force meets relentless resistance in battle.
simple_meaning: Ram’s arrows keep striking Ravana’s ten heads again and again, and blood pours out from the wounds.
insight: It keeps the focus on decisive action under pressure, not on drama or hesitation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: स्रवत रुधिर धायउ बलवाना। प्रभु पुनि कृत धनु सर संधाना॥ तीस तीर रघुबीर पबारे। भुजन्हि समेत सीस महि पारे ॥
translation: रुधिर बहते हुए ही बलवान् रावण दौड़ा। प्रभु ने फिर धनुष पर बाण संधान किया। श्री रघुवीर ने तीस बाण मारे और बीसों भुजाओं समेत दसों सिर काटकर पृथ्वी पर गिरा दिए ॥
english_translation: Ravana, still strong though bleeding, ran on. The Lord drew his bow again. Raghubir loosed thirty arrows and cut down all ten heads along with the twenty arms.
essence: What keeps returning must be cut at the root.
simple_meaning: Ravana keeps charging even while bleeding, and Ram answers again with more arrows, cutting down his many heads and arms.
insight: It shifts attention from the visible symptom to the stubborn source that keeps returning.
modern_relevance: You fix one problem, and the same pattern stands back up wearing a new face. The real work is not just damage control — it is ending what keeps regenerating.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: काटतहीं पुनि भए नबीने। राम बहोरि भुजा सिर छीने॥ प्रभु बहु बार बाहु सिर हए। कटत झटिति पुनि नूतन भए ॥
translation: (सिर और हाथ) काटते ही फिर नए हो गए। श्री रामजी ने फिर भुजाओं और सिरों को काट गिराया। इस तरह प्रभु ने बहुत बार भुजाएँ और सिर काटे, परन्तु काटते ही वे तुरंत फिर नए हो गए ॥
english_translation: Again, as soon as they were cut, new heads and arms appeared. Lord Ram kept cutting off his arms and heads, yet the moment they fell, they became new again. He cut them many times, but they instantly grew back.
essence: What is cut away returns again until its root is ended.
simple_meaning: Ram keeps cutting off Ravana's heads and arms, but they instantly grow back. The fighting continues without end.
insight: It shows a battle that cannot be won by ordinary damage, only by ending the force that keeps returning.
modern_relevance: You finally fix one problem, and three more appear before lunch. The issue is not solved by force alone; it keeps regenerating.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि पुनि प्रभु काटत भुज सीसा। अति कौतुकी कोसलाधीसा॥ रहे छाइ नभ सिर अरु बाहू। मानहुँ अमित केतु अरु राहू ॥
translation: प्रभु बार-बार उसकी भुजा और सिरों को काट रहे हैं, क्योंकि कोसलपति श्री रामजी बड़े कौतुकी हैं। आकाश में सिर और बाहु ऐसे छा गए हैं, मानो असंख्य केतु और राहु हों ॥ छंद :
english_translation: Again and again the Lord cut off his arms and heads. Koshal's lord is full of fierce play. Heads and arms filled the sky, like countless Ketu and Rahu.
essence: Relentless action is needed when resistance keeps returning.
simple_meaning: Ram keeps cutting down Ravana's heads and arms again and again. The battlefield fills with flying limbs, like countless celestial shadows in the sky.
insight: It shifts attention from a single victory to persistent, repeated effort against a stubborn obstacle.
modern_relevance: You fix one problem, and two more seem to grow back by morning. The work can feel endless, but steady action still matters.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जनु राहु केतु अनेक नभ पथ स्रवत सोनित धावहीं। रघुबीर तीर प्रचंड लागहिं भूमि गिरत न पावहीं॥ एक एक सर सिर निकर छेदे नभ उड़त इमि सोहहीं। जनु कोपि दिनकर कर निकर जहँ तहँ बिधुंतुद पोहहीं॥
translation: मानो अनेकों राहु और केतु रुधिर बहाते हुए आकाश मार्ग से दौड़ रहे हों। श्री रघुवीर के प्रचण्ड बाणों के (बार-बार) लगने से वे पृथ्वी पर गिरने नहीं पाते। एक-एक बाण से समूह के समूह सिर छिदे हुए आकाश में उड़ते ऐसे शोभा दे रहे हैं मानो सूर्य की किरणें क्रोध करके जहाँ-तहाँ राहुओं को पिरो रही हों।
english_translation: As if many Rahus and Ketus were rushing through the sky, shedding blood. The mighty arrows of Raghubir strike them so hard that they cannot fall to the ground. Split by one arrow after another, whole clusters of heads fly in the sky, shining as if the sun's rays, in anger, were piercing Rahus everywhere.
essence: Ravana's heads fill the sky like burning celestial bodies.
simple_meaning: The scene compares Ravana's many severed heads to Rahu and Ketu racing through the sky, while Ram's arrows keep striking them before they can fall.
insight: It adds visual force to the battle, but does not introduce a new principle.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जिमि जिमि प्रभु हर तासु सिर तिमि होहिं अपार। सेवत बिषय बिबर्ध जिमि नित नित नूतन मार ॥
translation: जैसे-जैसे प्रभु उसके सिरों को काटते हैं, वैसे ही वैसे वे अपार होते जाते हैं। जैसे विषयों का सेवन करने से काम (उन्हें भोगने की इच्छा) दिन-प्रतिदिन नया-नया बढ़ता जाता है ॥
english_translation: As the Lord cuts off his heads again and again, they become countless. Just as serving the senses makes desire grow anew each day.
essence: What you indulge grows; what you fight without insight returns stronger.
simple_meaning: Ravana's heads keep multiplying as Ram cuts them off, showing that craving only grows stronger when it is fed.
insight: It shifts you from feeding craving to noticing how repetition strengthens it.
modern_relevance: You open your phone for one minute and end up scrolling for forty. The appetite didn't disappear after the first hit — it got louder. This verse names that trap exactly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दसमुख देखि सिरन्ह कै बाढ़ी। बिसरा मरन भई रिस गाढ़ी॥ गर्जेउ मूढ़ महा अभिमानी। धायउ दसहु सरासन तानी ॥
translation: सिरों की बाढ़ देखकर रावण को अपना मरण भूल गया और बड़ा गहरा क्रोध हुआ। वह महान् अभिमानी मूर्ख गरजा और दसों धनुषों को तानकर दौड़ा ॥
english_translation: Seeing the growth of his many heads, Ravana forgot death and was flooded with fierce rage. The great fool, swollen with ego, roared and rushed forward, drawing all ten bows.
essence: Ego turns even near-defeat into blind attack.
simple_meaning: Ravana becomes so swollen with rage and ego that he forgets death itself and charges into battle with all ten bows drawn.
insight: It shows how wounded pride turns a person reckless and blind to consequences.
modern_relevance: You get one harsh email and suddenly everything becomes a fight. The real issue disappears, and your ego takes the wheel.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: समर भूमि दसकंधर कोप्यो। बरषि बान रघुपति रथ तोप्यो॥ दंड एक रथ देखि न परेउ। जनु निहार महुँ दिनकर दुरेऊ ॥
translation: रणभूमि में रावण ने क्रोध किया और बाण बरसाकर श्री रघुनाथजी के रथ को ढँक दिया। एक दण्ड (घड़ी) तक रथ दिखलाई न पड़ा, मानो कुहरे में सूर्य छिप गया हो ॥
english_translation: On the battlefield, Ravana grew furious and showered arrows so thick that he hid Raghupati's chariot. For a moment, the chariot could not be seen, as if the sun had disappeared into fog.
essence: Fury can briefly hide even what cannot be destroyed.
simple_meaning: Ravana's arrows were so dense that Ram's chariot disappeared from view for a moment, like the sun hidden by fog.
insight: It shows how overwhelming force can briefly obscure what is steady and true.
modern_relevance: A meeting turns chaotic, voices overlap, and the main point disappears under noise. For a moment, you cannot even see what matters most.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हाहाकार सुरन्ह जब कीन्हा। तब प्रभु कोपि कारमुक लीन्हा॥ सर निवारि रिपु के सिर काटे। ते दिसि बिदिसि गगन महि पाटे ॥
translation: जब देवताओं ने हाहाकार किया, तब प्रभु ने क्रोध करके धनुष उठाया और शत्रु के बाणों को हटाकर उन्होंने शत्रु के सिर काटे और उनसे दिशा, विदिशा, आकाश और पृथ्वी सबको पाट दिया ॥
english_translation: When the gods cried out in alarm, the Lord angrily took up his bow. He cleared away the enemy's arrows, cut off his heads, and filled the directions, sky, and earth with them.
essence: Protective power can be sudden, total, and unstoppable.
simple_meaning: The divine beings cry out, and Ram responds at once. He takes up his bow, clears the enemy's arrows, and cuts off the heads, filling the sky and earth with them.
insight: It shows decisive action that clears chaos instead of negotiating with it.
modern_relevance: A room goes silent when a crisis finally breaks. You stop explaining, stand up, and do what the moment demands without hesitation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: काटे सिर नभ मारग धावहिं। जय जय धुनि करि भय उपजावहिं॥ कहँ लछिमन सुग्रीव कपीसा। कहँ रघुबीर कोसलाधीसा ॥
translation: काटे हुए सिर आकाश मार्ग से दौड़ते हैं और जय-जय की ध्वनि करके भय उत्पन्न करते हैं। 'लक्ष्मण और वानरराज सुग्रीव कहाँ हैं? कोसलपति रघुवीर कहाँ हैं?' ॥
english_translation: The severed heads rush through the sky, shouting victory and spreading fear. "Where are Lakshman and Sugriva, lord of the monkeys? Where is Raghubir, king of Kosala?"
essence: Defeat still throws out one last wave of fear.
simple_meaning: The severed heads fly through the sky and terrify the battlefield, while the warriors cry out for Lakshman, Sugriva, and Ram.
insight: It keeps the scene in motion and heightens the terror before Ram's next decisive strike.
modern_relevance: A fight keeps replaying in your head long after the argument ends. The body may still be tense, but the decision has already moved on.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहँ रामु कहि सिर निकर धाए देखि मर्कट भजि चले। संधानि धनु रघुबंसमनि हँसि सरन्हि सिर बेधे भले॥ सिर मालिका कर कालिका गहि बृंद बृंदन्हि बहु मिलीं। करि रुधिर सरि मज्जनु मनहुँ संग्राम बट पूजन चलीं॥
translation: 'राम कहाँ हैं?' यह कहकर सिरों के समूह दौड़े, उन्हें देखकर वानर भाग चले। तब धनुष सन्धान करके रघुकुलमणि श्री रामजी ने हँसकर बाणों से उन सिरों को भलीभाँति बेध डाला। हाथों में मुण्डों की मालाएँ लेकर बहुत सी कालिकाएँ झुंड की झुंड मिलकर इकट्ठी हुईं और वे रुधिर की नदी में स्नान करके चलीं। मानो संग्राम रूपी वटवृक्ष की पूजा करने जा रही हों।
english_translation: “Where is Ram?” Crying this, the heads rushed forth; seeing them, the monkeys fled. Then, the jewel of Raghu’s line strung his bow and, smiling, pierced the heads with his arrows. Many groups of dark goddesses gathered, each holding garlands of skulls; bathing in the river of blood, they seemed to go to worship the battle-tree.
essence: War’s horror is met by Ram’s unshaken response.
simple_meaning: The battlefield turns terrifying: severed heads surge forward, the monkeys scatter, and Ram answers by calmly shooting them down again. The scene ends with dark goddesses gathering as if to honor the battle itself.
insight: It shows a battle scene where terror is met with composed force, but no standalone lesson is stated.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि दसकंठ क्रुद्ध होइ छाँड़ी सक्ति प्रचंड। चली बिभीषन सन्मुख मनहुँ काल कर दंड ॥
translation: फिर रावण ने क्रोधित होकर प्रचण्ड शक्ति छोड़ी। वह विभीषण के सामने ऐसी चली जैसे काल (यमराज) का दण्ड हो ॥
english_translation: Then Ravana, furious, hurled a blazing weapon. It rushed toward Vibhishana like the staff of death.
essence: Anger makes even your own brother look like a target.
simple_meaning: Ravana, enraged, launches a terrible weapon straight at Vibhishana, as if death itself were attacking him.
insight: It shows how unchecked rage turns relationship into enemy territory.
modern_relevance: A furious text reply is already typed, and the person on the other end is your own family. In that instant, anger stops being strength and becomes self-damage.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आवत देखि सक्ति अति घोरा। प्रनतारति भंजन पन मोरा॥ तुरत बिभीषन पाछें मेला। सन्मुख राम सहेउ सोइ सेला ॥
translation: अत्यंत भयानक शक्ति को आती देख और यह विचार कर कि मेरा प्रण शरणागत के दुःख का नाश करना है, श्री रामजी ने तुरंत ही विभीषण को पीछे कर लिया और सामने होकर वह शक्ति स्वयं सह ली ॥
english_translation: Seeing the terrible weapon coming, Ram remembered his vow: to protect the one who has surrendered. He quickly moved Vibhishana behind him and took the blow himself.
essence: Refuge is real only when you take the wound yourself.
simple_meaning: Ram keeps his promise to protect anyone who comes to him for refuge. He shields Vibhishana and takes the weapon himself.
insight: It shifts devotion from words to protection: the one who shelters others must be willing to absorb the cost.
modern_relevance: A friend is about to get blamed in a meeting for a mistake you both saw coming. You step in, take the heat, and make sure they are not left exposed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लागि सक्ति मुरुछा कछु भई। प्रभु कृत खेल सुरन्ह बिकलई॥ देखि बिभीषन प्रभु श्रम पायो। गहि कर गदा क्रुद्ध होइ धायो ॥
translation: शक्ति लगने से उन्हें कुछ मूर्छा हो गई। प्रभु ने तो यह लीला की, पर देवताओं को व्याकुलता हुई। प्रभु को श्रम (शारीरिक कष्ट) प्राप्त हुआ देखकर विभीषण क्रोधित हो हाथ में गदा लेकर दौड़े ॥
english_translation: The blow caused him to faint a little. For the Lord, it was all a play, but the gods were unsettled. Seeing the Lord in pain, Vibhishana grew angry, took up his mace, and rushed forward.
essence: Love rushes forward the moment the beloved seems hurt.
simple_meaning: Ravana's weapon briefly stuns Ram, but the moment is only a divine play. The celestial beings are shaken, and Vibhishana rushes to defend Ram when he sees Ram weary.
insight: It shifts attention from the wound itself to the loyalty it awakens in others.
modern_relevance: You see someone you care about flinch after a harsh comment, and something in you tightens at once. Love does that: it turns concern into action before you even think.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रे कुभाग्य सठ मंद कुबुद्धे। तैं सुर नर मुनि नाग बिरुद्धे॥ सादर सिव कहुँ सीस चढ़ाए। एक एक के कोटिन्ह पाए ॥
translation: (और बोले-) अरे अभागे! मूर्ख, नीच दुर्बुद्धि! तूने देवता, मनुष्य, मुनि, नाग सभी से विरोध किया। तूने आदर सहित शिवजी को सिर चढ़ाए। इसी से एक-एक के बदले में करोड़ों पाए ॥
english_translation: “O unlucky fool, dull and misguided one, you have made yourself hostile to gods, humans, sages, and serpents. Yet with reverence you placed Shiva on your head, and from each one you received millions in return.”
essence: Reverence cannot protect a life ruled by arrogance.
simple_meaning: Ravana is mocked for turning against everyone while still honoring Shiva. The verse says that even good acts cannot save a mind ruled by arrogance and bad judgment.
insight: It shifts attention from isolated piety to the overall direction of the heart.
modern_relevance: You can donate generously, pray sincerely, and still sabotage your life with arrogance in every conversation. A few noble acts cannot cover a pattern of contempt.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: तेहि कारन खल अब लगि बाँच्यो। अब तव कालु सीस पर नाच्यो॥ राम बिमुख सठ चहसि संपदा। अस कहि हनेसि माझ उर गदा ॥
translation: उसी कारण से अरे दुष्ट! तू अब तक बचा है, (किन्तु) अब काल तेरे सिर पर नाच रहा है। अरे मूर्ख! तू राम विमुख होकर सम्पत्ति (सुख) चाहता है? ऐसा कहकर विभीषण ने रावण की छाती के बीचों-बीच गदा मारी ॥
english_translation: That is why, you villain, you have survived until now. But now time is dancing on your head. Fool, you want prosperity while turning away from Ram? Saying this, Vibhishana struck Ravana's chest with his mace.
essence: Refusing Ram leaves Ravana with nothing but his own downfall.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana tells Ravana he has survived only by past grace, but now his end is near because he still wants comfort while rejecting Ram. Then he strikes Ravana with his mace.
insight: It shows how refusal to turn back can make a person fight their own ruin.
modern_relevance: You keep doubling down on a choice that is already costing you. The warning has come, the damage is visible, and still the old craving reaches for more.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: उर माझ गदा प्रहार घोर कठोर लागत महि पर् यो। दस बदन सोनित स्रवत पुनि संभारि धायो रिस भर् यो॥ द्वौ भिरे अतिबल मल्लजुद्ध बिरुद्ध एकु एकहि हनै। रघुबीर बल दर्पित बिभीषनु घालि नहिं ता कहुँ गनै॥
translation: बीच छाती में कठोर गदा की घोर और कठिन चोट लगते ही वह पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा। उसके दसों मुखों से रुधिर बहने लगा, वह अपने को फिर संभालकर क्रोध में भरा हुआ दौड़ा। दोनों अत्यंत बलवान् योद्धा भिड़ गए और मल्लयुद्ध में एक-दूसरे के विरुद्ध होकर मारने लगे। श्री रघुवीर के बल से गर्वित विभीषण उसको (रावण जैसे जगद्विजयी योद्धा को) पासंग के बराबर भी नहीं समझते।
english_translation: A fierce, crushing blow of the mace struck his chest, and he fell to the ground. Blood flowed from his ten faces, yet he gathered himself and rushed back in rage. The two mighty warriors clashed, locked in wrestling combat, striking each other. Filled with the power of Raghuvir, Vibhishana did not count him as even a trifle.
essence: Powerful people can still fall; true steadiness comes from Ram.
simple_meaning: This is a battle scene: Ravana is struck, falls, rises again, and keeps fighting. Vibhishana, empowered by Ram, sees Ravana as no great threat.
insight: It shifts attention from damage to endurance, and from intimidation to steadiness.
modern_relevance: A boxer gets knocked to the mat in front of a roaring crowd, wipes the blood away, and stands back up. The point is not the fall — it's the refusal to stay down.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उमा बिभीषनु रावनहि सन्मुख चितव कि काउ। सो अब भिरत काल ज्यों श्री रघुबीर प्रभाउ ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! विभीषण क्या कभी रावण के सामने आँख उठाकर भी देख सकता था? परन्तु अब वही काल के समान उससे भिड़ रहा है। यह श्री रघुवीर का ही प्रभाव है ॥
english_translation: O Uma, could Vibhishana ever even dare to face Ravana? Yet now he fights him like Death itself. Such is the power of Shri Raghubir.
essence: Ram's power can turn fear into fearless action.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana once could not even look at Ravana directly, but now he is fighting him fearlessly. That change comes from Ram's power.
insight: It shifts attention from personal bravery to the transforming power behind brave action.
modern_relevance: Someone who used to shrink in a room finally speaks up and holds their ground. The courage does not come from personality alone; something stronger has steadied them.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: देखा श्रमित बिभीषनु भारी। धायउ हनूमान गिरि धारी॥ रथ तुरंग सारथी निपाता। हृदय माझ तेहि मारेसि लाता ॥
translation: विभीषण को बहुत ही थका हुआ देखकर हनुमान् जी पर्वत धारण किए हुए दौड़े। उन्होंने उस पर्वत से रावण के रथ, घोड़े और सारथी का संहार कर डाला और उसके सीने पर लात मारी ॥
english_translation: Seeing Vibhishana exhausted, Hanuman rushed forward carrying a mountain. With that mountain he destroyed Ravana's chariot, horses, and charioteer, then struck him in the chest with his foot.
essence: True loyalty rushes in before exhaustion becomes defeat.
simple_meaning: Hanuman sees Vibhishana exhausted and rushes in with a mountain, smashing Ravana's chariot and striking him down.
insight: It shows support as immediate action: notice strain, move in, remove pressure.
modern_relevance: A friend is getting overwhelmed in the middle of a hard conversation, and you step in without waiting to be asked. That instinct to protect is this moment's energy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ठाढ़ रहा अति कंपित गाता। गयउ बिभीषनु जहँ जनत्राता॥ पुनि रावन कपि हतेउ पचारी। चलेउ गगन कपि पूँछ पसारी ॥
translation: रावण खड़ा रहा, पर उसका शरीर अत्यंत काँपने लगा। विभीषण वहाँ गए, जहाँ सेवकों के रक्षक श्री रामजी थे। फिर रावण ने ललकारकर हनुमान् जी को मारा। वे पूँछ फैलाकर आकाश में चले गए ॥
english_translation: Ravana stood there, but his body trembled violently. Vibhishana went to where Ram, the protector of servants, was. Then Ravana challenged Hanuman and struck him. Hanuman flew into the sky with his tail spread wide.
essence: Battle pressure exposes fear, refuge, and defiance at once.
simple_meaning: Ravana trembles in battle, Vibhishana goes to Ram for refuge, and Hanuman leaps back into the sky after being struck.
insight: It shifts attention from the blow itself to the larger battle of resolve, refuge, and retaliation.
modern_relevance: In the middle of a heated argument, one person shakes, another reaches for support, and someone else answers with a sharp comeback. Pressure reveals who stands where.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गहिसि पूँछ कपि सहित उड़ाना। पुनि फिरि भिरेउ प्रबल हनुमाना॥ लरत अकास जुगल सम जोधा। एकहि एकु हनत करि क्रोधा ॥
translation: रावण ने पूँछ पकड़ ली, हनुमान् जी उसको साथ लिए ऊपर उड़े। फिर लौटकर महाबलवान् हनुमान् जी उससे भिड़ गए। दोनों समान योद्धा आकाश में लड़ते हुए एक-दूसरे को क्रोध करके मारने लगे ॥
english_translation: Ravana seized Hanuman's tail and carried him upward. Then the mighty Hanuman turned back and clashed with him again. The two equal warriors fought in the sky, each striking the other in anger.
essence: A trapped moment becomes a fierce counterattack.
simple_meaning: Ravana grabs Hanuman's tail, but Hanuman turns and fights back in the sky. Their battle is fierce and evenly matched.
insight: It shows how pressure can be met with instant counterforce instead of panic.
modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a meeting, tries to twist the story, and expects you to freeze. You recover, answer cleanly, and the whole room feels the shift.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सोहहिं नभ छल बल बहु करहीं। कज्जलगिरि सुमेरु जनु लरहीं॥ बुधि बल निसिचर परइ न पारयो। तब मारुतसुत प्रभु संभार् यो ॥
translation: दोनों बहुत से छल-बल करते हुए आकाश में ऐसे शोभित हो रहे हैं मानो कज्जलगिरि और सुमेरु पर्वत लड़ रहे हों। जब बुद्धि और बल से राक्षस गिराए न गिरा तब मारुति श्री हनुमान् जी ने प्रभु को स्मरण किया ॥
english_translation: They shone in the sky, fighting with many tricks and great force, like black mountain and Mount Sumeru battling. When the demon could not be brought down by intelligence or strength, Hanuman remembered the Lord.
essence: When your own power fails, remembrance gives you the next move.
simple_meaning: The two fighters clash in the sky like huge mountains. When brute force and cleverness fail, Hanuman remembers Ram.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance alone to remembrance as the source of real force.
modern_relevance: You keep trying three different fixes on the same broken problem, and nothing moves. Then, in the middle of the mess, you remember who you are fighting for.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: संभारि श्रीरघुबीर धीर पचारि कपि रावनु हन्यो। महि परत पुनि उठि लरत देवन्ह जुगल कहुँ जय जय भन्यो॥ हनुमंत संकट देखि मर्कट भालु क्रोधातुर चले। रन मत्त रावन सकल सुभट प्रचण्ड भुज बल दलमले॥
translation: श्री रघुवीर का स्मरण करके धीर हनुमान् जी ने ललकारकर रावण को मारा। वे दोनों पृथ्वी पर गिरते और फिर उठकर लड़ते हैं, देवताओं ने दोनों की 'जय-जय' पुकारी। हनुमान् जी पर संकट देखकर वानर-भालू क्रोधातुर होकर दौड़े, किन्तु रण-मद-माते रावण ने सब योद्धाओं को अपनी प्रचण्ड भुजाओं के बल से कुचल और मसल डाला।
english_translation: Remembering the steadfast Lord of the Raghu line, Hanuman challenged and struck Ravana. They fell to the ground, rose again, and fought on; the gods cried victory for both. Seeing Hanuman in danger, the monkeys and bears rushed in anger, but the battle-drunk Ravana crushed all the warriors with the force of his mighty arms.
essence: Bravery ignites the fight, but brute force still rules the field.
simple_meaning: Hanuman keeps fighting Ravana with fearless courage, while the monkey and bear army rushes to defend him. Ravana still overwhelms the warriors with his great strength.
insight: It shifts attention from heroic impulse alone to the cost of uncontrolled force in conflict.
modern_relevance: You jump into a heated group chat to defend a friend, and suddenly everyone is shouting at once. Loyalty is noble, but raw force can still flatten the room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब रघुबीर पचारे धाए कीस प्रचंड। कपि बल प्रबल देखि तेहिं कीन्ह प्रगट पाषंड ॥
translation: तब श्री रघुवीर के ललकारने पर प्रचण्ड वीर वानर दौड़े। वानरों के प्रबल दल को देखकर रावण ने माया प्रकट की ॥
english_translation: Then, at Raghubir's challenge, the fierce monkeys rushed forward. Seeing the monkeys' powerful force, Ravana revealed his illusion.
essence: Overmatched pride reaches for illusion.
simple_meaning: At Ram's challenge, the monkey warriors rushed ahead. Ravana saw their strength and answered with illusion.
insight: It shows how ego under pressure reaches for concealment instead of clarity.
modern_relevance: A meeting turns tense, and someone who feels outmatched suddenly starts deflecting, bluffing, or changing the subject. When real strength appears, weak tactics often show themselves.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अंतरधान भयउ छन एका। पुनि प्रगटे खल रूप अनेका॥ रघुपति कटक भालु कपि जेते। जहँ तहँ प्रगट दसानन तेते ॥
translation: क्षणभर के लिए वह अदृश्य हो गया। फिर उस दुष्ट ने अनेकों रूप प्रकट किए। श्री रघुनाथजी की सेना में जितने रीछ-वानर थे, उतने ही रावण जहाँ-तहाँ (चारों ओर) प्रकट हो गए ॥
english_translation: For a moment he disappeared. Then the villain appeared in many forms. In Raghunath's army, wherever there were bears and monkeys, there Ravana appeared as many.
essence: False appearances multiply fear before anyone can see clearly.
simple_meaning: Ravana vanishes, then multiplies himself into many forms to confuse Ram's army.
insight: It shows how illusion can scatter attention and make fear feel larger than it is.
modern_relevance: A crowded group chat suddenly fills with five versions of the same rumor, and panic spreads before anyone checks the source. This verse captures how confusion multiplies when appearance outruns discernment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखे कपिन्ह अमित दससीसा। जहँ तहँ भजे भालु अरु कीसा॥ भागे बानर धरहिं न धीरा। त्राहि त्राहि लछिमन रघुबीरा ॥
translation: वानरों ने अपरिमित रावण देखे। भालू और वानर सब जहाँ-तहाँ (इधर-उधर) भाग चले। वानर धीरज नहीं धरते। हे लक्ष्मणजी! हे रघुवीर! बचाइए, बचाइए, यों पुकारते हुए वे भागे जा रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The monkeys saw countless Ravanas. The bears and monkeys ran everywhere. The monkeys could not keep their courage. Crying, 'Save us, Lakshman! Save us, Raghubir!' they fled.
essence: Illusion makes one enemy feel like many.
simple_meaning: Ravana multiplies into countless forms, and the monkey army panics and runs in every direction, crying out for Lakshman and Ram to save them.
insight: It shows how confusion multiplies fear before reason can regain control.
modern_relevance: You open your phone and see ten urgent messages, three deadlines, and a crisis in the family chat. For a moment, everything feels like it's coming from everywhere at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दहँ दिसि धावहिं कोटिन्ह रावन। गर्जहिं घोर कठोर भयावन॥ डरे सकल सुर चले पराई। जय कै आस तजहु अब भाई ॥
translation: दसों दिशाओं में करोड़ों रावण दौड़ते हैं और घोर, कठोर भयानक गर्जन कर रहे हैं। सब देवता डर गए और ऐसा कहते हुए भाग चले कि हे भाई! अब जय की आशा छोड़ दो! ॥
english_translation: Ravana multiplies into millions, rushing in all ten directions with terrible, harsh roars. All the radiant beings are frightened and flee, saying, “Brother, give up hope of victory now.”
essence: Fear can make one enemy feel endless.
simple_meaning: Ravana seems to be everywhere at once, terrifying everyone so badly that even the radiant beings lose hope and run away.
insight: It shows how fear distorts reality until one obstacle looks like a thousand.
modern_relevance: A project collapses into chaos, every problem seems to arrive at once, and even your confidence starts to shake. This is what panic feels like when it multiplies the threat.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब सुर जिते एक दसकंधर। अब बहु भए तकहु गिरि कंदर॥ रहे बिरंचि संभु मुनि ग्यानी। जिन्ह जिन्ह प्रभु महिमा कछु जानी ॥
translation: एक ही रावण ने सब देवताओं को जीत लिया था, अब तो बहुत से रावण हो गए हैं। इससे अब पहाड़ की गुफाओं का आश्रय लो (अर्थात् उनमें छिप रहो)। वहाँ ब्रह्मा, शम्भु और ज्ञानी मुनि ही डटे रहे, जिन्होंने प्रभु की कुछ महिमा जानी थी ॥
english_translation: One Ravana had already conquered all the radiant beings; now many Ravanas have appeared. So take shelter in mountain caves. Brahma, Shiva, and the wise sages remained fearless because they knew something of the Lord's greatness.
essence: Fear multiplies when Ram's greatness is forgotten.
simple_meaning: Ravana's terror has multiplied so much that only those who know the Lord's greatness stay unafraid.
insight: It shifts attention from multiplying threats to remembering the scale of divine protection.
modern_relevance: You open your phone and see one alarming headline after another until everything feels like the same threat. The panic eases only when you remember there is something larger than the noise.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जाना प्रताप ते रहे निर्भय कपिन्ह रिपु माने फुरे। चले बिचलि मर्कट भालु सकल कृपाल पाहि भयातुरे॥ हनुमंत अंगद नील नल अतिबल लरत रन बाँकुरे। मर्दहिं दसानन कोटि कोटिन्ह कपट भू भट अंकुरे॥
translation: जो प्रभु का प्रताप जानते थे, वे निर्भय डटे रहे। वानरों ने शत्रुओं (बहुत से रावणों) को सच्चा ही मान लिया। (इससे) सब वानर-भालू विचलित होकर 'हे कृपालु! रक्षा कीजिए' (यों पुकारते हुए) भय से व्याकुल होकर भाग चले। अत्यंत बलवान् रणबाँकुरे हनुमान् जी, अंगद, नील और नल लड़ते हैं और कपट रूपी भूमि से अंकुर की भाँति उपजे हुए कोटि-कोटि योद्धा रावणों को मसलते हैं।
english_translation: Those who knew his power stood fearless, but the monkeys mistook the enemies as real. All the monkeys and bears, shaken and crying, rushed away in fear. Yet Hanuman, Angada, Nila, and Nala, mighty and bold in battle, crushed the countless Ravanas, those warriors born from the soil of illusion.
essence: Illusion terrifies the unsteady, but clear courage cuts through it.
simple_meaning: Those who understood Ram's power stayed fearless. The rest were shaken by illusion and ran in fear, while Hanuman, Angada, Nila, and Nala kept fighting and crushed the fake Ravanas.
insight: It trains you to separate appearance from reality before fear starts steering your actions.
modern_relevance: A group chat explodes with worst-case assumptions, and suddenly everyone is reacting to a problem that isn't fully real. One steady person sees through the panic and acts anyway.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुर बानर देखे बिकल हँस्यो कोसलाधीस। सजि सारंग एक सर हते सकल दससीस ॥
translation: देवताओं और वानरों को विकल देखकर कोसलपति श्री रामजी हँसे और शार्गं धनुष पर एक बाण चढ़ाकर (माया के बने हुए) सब रावणों को मार डाला ॥
english_translation: Seeing the gods and monkeys bewildered, the Lord of Kosala smiled. He fitted one arrow to his bow and struck down all the many Ravanas.
essence: One clear strike can end a whole field of confusion.
simple_meaning: Ram sees everyone shaken, smiles, and destroys the many false Ravanas with one arrow.
insight: It shifts attention from the appearance of many problems to the one clear action that resolves them.
modern_relevance: A room full of people is panicking, the problem looks endless, and everyone is waiting for someone to fix it. Then one clear decision cuts through the chaos.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु छन महुँ माया सब काटी। जिमि रबि उएँ जाहिं तम फाटी॥ रावनु एकु देखि सुर हरषे। फिरे सुमन बहु प्रभु पर बरषे ॥
translation: प्रभु ने क्षणभर में सब माया काट डाली। जैसे सूर्य के उदय होते ही अंधकार की राशि फट जाती है (नष्ट हो जाती है)। अब एक ही रावण को देखकर देवता हर्षित हुए और उन्होंने लौटकर प्रभु पर बहुत से पुष्प बरसाए ॥
english_translation: The Lord cut through all the illusion in a moment, just as darkness breaks when the sun rises. Seeing only one Ravana now, the radiant beings rejoiced and showered many flowers on the Lord.
essence: Clarity can end a whole storm of confusion at once.
simple_meaning: Ram instantly ends the magical illusion, and the gods rejoice when they see the real Ravana again.
insight: It shifts the mind from reacting to appearances to seeing what is actually there.
modern_relevance: You panic when a problem looks like ten problems at once, then one clear look shows it was never that large.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भुज उठाइ रघुपति कपि फेरे। फिरे एक एकन्ह तब टेरे॥ प्रभु बलु पाइ भालु कपि धाए। तरल तमकि संजुग महि आए ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी ने भुजा उठाकर सब वानरों को लौटाया। तब वे एक-दूसरे को पुकार-पुकार कर लौट आए। प्रभु का बल पाकर रीछ-वानर दौड़ पड़े। जल्दी से कूदकर वे रणभूमि में आ गए ॥
english_translation: Raghupati raised his arm and sent the monkeys back. Then they returned, calling to one another. Filled with the Lord's strength, the bears and monkeys rushed forward and leapt back into the battle.
essence: A single signal from Ram turns retreat into renewed charge.
simple_meaning: Ram signals the monkeys to pull back, then they regroup and surge into battle again with renewed strength.
insight: It shows how calm leadership restores a scattered group and turns confusion back into coordinated action.
modern_relevance: A team freezes after a failed pitch, then someone raises a hand and resets everyone. The energy comes back not from ego, but from shared trust and a clear signal.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अस्तुति करत देवतन्हि देखें। भयउँ एक मैं इन्ह के लेखें॥ सठहु सदा तुम्ह मोर मरायल। अस कहि कोपि गगन पर धायल ॥
translation: देवताओं को श्री रामजी की स्तुति करते देख कर रावण ने सोचा, मैं इनकी समझ में एक हो गया, (परन्तु इन्हें यह पता नहीं कि इनके लिए मैं एक ही बहुत हूँ) और कहा- अरे मूर्खों! तुम तो सदा के ही मेरे मरैल (मेरी मार खाने वाले) हो। ऐसा कहकर वह क्रोध करके आकाश पर (देवताओं की ओर) दौड़ा ॥
english_translation: Seeing the deities praising Ram, Ravana thought, "I am one in their eyes, but to them I am far too many." He shouted, "You fools, you are always the ones I strike down!" Then, enraged, he rushed through the sky.
essence: Ego turns admiration into insult and then into attack.
simple_meaning: Ravana sees the deities praising Ram and reacts with anger and contempt. He boasts that they are always the ones he defeats, then rushes toward them in fury.
insight: It exposes how wounded pride rushes straight into reckless action.
modern_relevance: You hear someone else being praised for the exact thing you wanted credit for. Your face tightens, and the need to prove yourself starts the next mistake.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: हाहाकार करत सुर भागे। खलहु जाहु कहँ मोरें आगे॥ देखि बिकल सुर अंगद धायो। कूदि चरन गहि भूमि गिरायो ॥
translation: देवता हाहाकार करते हुए भागे। (रावण ने कहा-) दुष्टों! मेरे आगे से कहाँ जा सकोगे? देवताओं को व्याकुल देखकर अंगद दौड़े और उछलकर रावण का पैर पकड़कर (उन्होंने) उसको पृथ्वी पर गिरा दिया ॥
english_translation: The devas fled in panic. Ravana shouted, "O vile ones, where can you go before me?" Seeing the devas distressed, Angada rushed forward, leapt, seized Ravana's foot, and threw him to the ground.
essence: Angada answers fear with immediate force.
simple_meaning: The gods run in fear, Ravana boasts, and Angada jumps in to strike him down.
insight: It shows a sudden act of bravery that interrupts panic and humiliation.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: गहि भूमि पार् यो लात मार् यो बालिसुत प्रभु पहिं गयो। संभारि उठि दसकंठ घोर कठोर रव गर्जत भयो॥ करि दाप चाप चढ़ाइ दस संधानि सर बहु बरषई। किए सकल भट घायल भयाकुल देखि निज बल हरषई॥
translation: उसे पकड़कर पृथ्वी पर गिराकर लात मारकर बालिपुत्र अंगद प्रभु के पास चले गए। रावण संभलकर उठा और बड़े भंयकर कठोर शब्द से गरजने लगा। वह दर्प करके दसों धनुष चढ़ाकर उन पर बहुत से बाण संधान करके बरसाने लगा। उसने सब योद्धाओं को घायल और भय से व्याकुल कर दिया और अपना बल देखकर वह हर्षित होने लगा।
english_translation: Seizing him, Angad threw him to the ground and kicked him before going to the Lord. Ravana recovered, roared with a fierce and harsh voice, drew his ten bows, and showered many arrows. He wounded all the warriors, filled them with fear, and rejoiced in his own strength.
essence: Wounded pride answers humiliation with more violence.
simple_meaning: Angad humbles Ravana, but Ravana quickly rises and attacks with fierce pride, injuring the warriors and delighting in his own power.
insight: It shows how ego reacts to humiliation by escalating conflict and feeding on its own display of strength.
modern_relevance: Someone mocks you in a group chat, and your first urge is to fire back harder. The verse shows how wounded pride reaches for force instead of clarity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब रघुपति रावन के सीस भुजा सर चाप। काटे बहुत बढ़े पुनि जिमि तीरथ कर पाप ॥
translation: तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने रावण के सिर, भुजाएँ, बाण और धनुष काट डाले। पर वे फिर बहुत बढ़ गए, जैसे तीर्थ में किए हुए पाप बढ़ जाते हैं (कई गुना अधिक भयानक फल उत्पन्न करते हैं)! ॥
english_translation: Then Raghu's lord cut off Ravana's heads, arms, arrows, and bow. But they grew back again, just as sins done at sacred places grow into even worse consequences.
essence: What is rooted in ego returns until the root is cut.
simple_meaning: Ravana's heads, arms, arrows, and bow are cut off, but they keep growing back. The image compares this to wrongdoing that only multiplies its own consequences.
insight: It shifts attention from defeating symptoms to removing the underlying cause.
modern_relevance: You keep deleting the same problem from your phone, and it returns through another app, another tab, another habit. Until the source changes, the pattern keeps coming back.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिर भुज बाढ़ि देखि रिपु केरी। भालु कपिन्ह रिस भई घनेरी॥ मरत न मूढ़ कटेहुँ भुज सीसा। धाए कोपि भालु भट कीसा ॥
translation: शत्रु के सिर और भुजाओं की बढ़ती देखकर रीछ-वानरों को बहुत ही क्रोध हुआ। यह मूर्ख भुजाओं के और सिरों के कटने पर भी नहीं मरता, (ऐसा कहते हुए) भालू और वानर योद्धा क्रोध करके दौड़े ॥
english_translation: Seeing the enemy's heads and arms grow back, the bears and monkeys became furious. "That fool does not die even when his heads and arms are cut!" Crying out in anger, the bears and monkey warriors rushed forward.
essence: The battle intensifies when defeat refuses to stay defeated.
simple_meaning: The monkey and bear warriors are enraged because Ravana's cut-off heads and arms keep growing back, so they charge again.
insight: It shifts attention from strategy to escalation: when resistance multiplies, the response becomes collective force.
modern_relevance: You keep fixing the same problem, and it keeps coming back worse. At some point, frustration turns into a harder push.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बालितनय मारुति नल नीला। बानरराज दुबिद बलसीला॥ बिटप महीधर करहिं प्रहारा। सोइ गिरि तरु गहि कपिन्ह सो मारा ॥
translation: बालिपुत्र अंगद, मारुति हनुमान् जी, नल, नील, वानरराज सुग्रीव और द्विविद आदि बलवान् उस पर वृक्ष और पर्वतों का प्रहार करते हैं। वह उन्हीं पर्वतों और वृक्षों को पकड़कर वानरों को मारता है ॥
english_translation: Angada, Hanuman, Nala, Neela, Sugriva, and the mighty monkey warriors, including Dvivida, hurl trees and mountains at him. He seizes those same mountains and trees and kills the monkeys with them.
essence: The battle escalates as each side turns the other's weapons back on them.
simple_meaning: The monkey warriors attack with trees and mountains, but the enemy grabs those weapons and turns them back on them.
insight: It records a violent exchange in the war, with no separate moral claim.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एक नखन्हि रिपु बपुष बिदारी। भागि चलहिं एक लातन्ह मारी। तब नल नील सिरन्हि चढ़ि गयऊ। नखन्हि लिलार बिदारत भयऊ ॥
translation: कोई एक वानर नखों से शत्रु के शरीर को फाड़कर भाग जाते हैं, तो कोई उसे लातों से मारकर। तब नल और नील रावण के सिरों पर चढ़ गए और नखों से उसके ललाट को फाड़ने लगे ॥
english_translation: One monkey tears the enemy’s body with claws and runs off; another strikes with kicks. Then Nala and Nila climbed onto Ravana’s heads and began tearing his forehead with their claws.
essence: The war turns savage as the monkey warriors swarm Ravana.
simple_meaning: The monkey warriors attack Ravana in many ways, clawing, kicking, and tearing at his forehead. This is a vivid battle detail, not a teaching verse.
insight: It stays in the action, showing the battle’s ferocity without shifting into reflection.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रुधिर देखि बिषाद उर भारी। तिन्हहि धरन कहुँ भुजा पसारी॥ गहे न जाहिं करन्हि पर फिरहीं। जनु जुग मधुप कमल बन चरहीं ॥
translation: खून देखकर उसे हृदय में बड़ा दुःख हुआ। उसने उनको पकड़ने के लिए हाथ फैलाए, पर वे पकड़ में नहीं आते, हाथों के ऊपर-ऊपर ही फिरते हैं मानो दो भौंरे कमलों के वन में विचरण कर रहे हों ॥
english_translation: Seeing the blood, grief weighed heavily on his heart. He stretched out his arms to seize them, but they could not be caught; they kept circling just beyond his hands, like two bees moving through a grove of lotuses.
essence: Grief and rage make even power slip through empty hands.
simple_meaning: Ravana is shaken by the sight of blood and keeps reaching for the monkeys, but they slip past his grasp like bees around flowers.
insight: It shows a mind losing command under pressure, turning desperate instead of clear.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to regain control in a meeting that has already slipped away. The harder you reach, the more everything stays just out of grasp.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: कोपि कूदि द्वौ धरेसि बहोरी। महि पटकत भजे भुजा मरोरी॥ पुनि सकोप दस धनु कर लीन्हे। सरन्हि मारि घायल कपि कीन्हे ॥
translation: तब उसने क्रोध करके उछलकर दोनों को पकड़ लिया। पृथ्वी पर पटकते समय वे उसकी भुजाओं को मरोड़कर भाग छूटे। फिर उसने क्रोध करके हाथों में दसों धनुष लिए और वानरों को बाणों से मारकर घायल कर दिया ॥
english_translation: Then, in anger, he sprang up and seized the two again. As they struck the ground, they twisted free by wrenching his arms. Then, angry again, he took up all ten bows and wounded the monkeys with arrows.
essence: Anger only multiplies force; it never restores control.
simple_meaning: Ravana keeps fighting back in fury. He grabs the monkeys, they escape, and then he attacks them with arrows.
insight: It shows how anger feeds on itself and turns every response into escalation.
modern_relevance: A heated argument keeps restarting because nobody wants to back down. Each sharp reply only tightens the knot, and the original problem gets buried under reaction.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हनुमदादि मुरुछित करि बंदर। पाइ प्रदोष हरष दसकंधर॥ मुरुछित देखि सकल कपि बीरा। जामवंत धायउ रनधीरा ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी आदि सब वानरों को मूर्च्छित करके और संध्या का समय पाकर रावण हर्षित हुआ। समस्त वानर-वीरों को मूर्च्छित देखकर रणधीर जाम्बवत् दौड़े ॥
english_translation: Having stunned Hanuman and the other monkeys, Ravana grew delighted as evening fell. Seeing all the monkey-heroes stunned, brave Jambavan rushed forward to the battlefield.
essence: A fallen army still has one last fighter.
simple_meaning: Ravana knocks Hanuman and the other monkey warriors unconscious, then rejoices at dusk. Seeing his allies fallen, Jambavan charges back into the fight.
insight: It shifts attention from the setback to the one who answers it with action.
modern_relevance: You watch a team collapse halfway through a brutal meeting, and the room goes quiet. Then the oldest, steadiest person stands up and keeps the work alive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: संग भालु भूधर तरु धारी। मारन लगे पचारि पचारी॥ भयउ क्रुद्ध रावन बलवाना। गहि पद महि पटकइ भट नाना ॥
translation: जाम्बवान् के साथ जो भालू थे, वे पर्वत और वृक्ष धारण किए रावण को ललकार-ललकार कर मारने लगे। बलवान् रावण क्रोधित हुआ और पैर पकड़-पकड़कर वह अनेकों योद्धाओं को पृथ्वी पर पटकने लगा ॥
english_translation: With Jambavan and the bears carrying mountains and trees, they challenged Ravana again and again and struck at him. The mighty Ravana grew furious and, seizing warriors by the feet, hurled many of them to the ground.
essence: Battle surges on with raw force and fury.
simple_meaning: The battle keeps surging back and forth. The bears attack with mountains and trees, and Ravana answers by seizing warriors and slamming them down.
insight: It shows a combat scene in motion, not a teaching, so it stays as battlefield narration.
modern_relevance: A group chat turns into a pile-on, and everyone starts hitting back harder than before. Nobody is thinking clearly anymore; only impact is spreading.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि भालुपति निज दल घाता। कोपि माझ उर मारेसि लाता ॥
translation: जाम्बवान् ने अपने दल का विध्वंस देखकर क्रोध करके रावण की छाती में लात मारी ॥
english_translation: Seeing his own army struck down, the lord of the bears, in anger, kicked Ravana in the chest.
essence: Battle fury becomes a single decisive blow.
simple_meaning: Jambavan sees his side being battered and answers with a furious kick to Ravana's chest.
insight: It shows how protective anger can become immediate action when someone you stand with is attacked.
modern_relevance: A teammate gets publicly humiliated in front of everyone, and you feel your body tense before you even think. Loyalty can make you stand up faster than fear can sit you down.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उर लात घात प्रचंड लागत बिकल रथ ते महि परा। गहि भालु बीसहुँ कर मनहुँ कमलन्हि बसे निसि मधुकरा॥ मुरुछित बिलोकि बहोरि पद हति भालुपति प्रभु पहिं गयो॥ निसि जानि स्यंदन घालि तेहि तब सूत जतनु करय भयो॥
translation: छाती में लात का प्रचण्ड आघात लगते ही रावण व्याकुल होकर रथ से पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा। उसने बीसों हाथों में भालुओं को पकड़ रखा था। (ऐसा जान पड़ता था) मानो रात्रि के समय भौंरे कमलों में बसे हुए हों। उसे मूर्च्छित देखकर, फिर लात मारकर ऋक्षराज जाम्बवान् प्रभु के पास चले। रात्रि जानकर सारथी रावण को रथ में डालकर उसे होश में लाने का उपाय करने लगा॥
english_translation: The force of the blow to his chest knocked Ravana off the chariot and onto the ground. He clutched the bears with all twenty hands, like bees in lotus flowers at night. Seeing him stunned, Jambavan kicked him again and went to the Lord. Knowing it was night, the charioteer then placed Ravana back in the chariot and tried to revive him.
essence: Pride falls fast when it meets a stronger blow.
simple_meaning: Ravana is battered in battle and falls from his chariot. Jambavan leaves him stunned and returns to Ram, while Ravana's charioteer tries to recover him.
insight: It shows how quickly force and status can collapse when challenged.
modern_relevance: A person who has been performing confidently in a meeting suddenly loses composure after one sharp question. The room changes in a second, and everyone can feel the shift.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुरुछा बिगत भालु कपि सब आए प्रभु पास। निसिचर सकल रावनहि घेरि रहे अति त्रास ॥
translation: मूर्च्छा दूर होने पर सब रीछ-वानर प्रभु के पास आए। उधर सब राक्षसों ने बहुत ही भयभीत होकर रावण को घेर लिया ॥
english_translation: When their faintness passed, all the bears and monkeys came to the Lord. Meanwhile, all the demons, terrified, gathered around Ravana.
essence: The armies regroup around the two centers of fear and trust.
simple_meaning: After the shock passed, the monkey army gathered back around Ram, while Ravana's frightened forces closed in around him.
insight: It keeps the focus on battlefield movement, not on a moral or inner lesson.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेही निसि सीता पहिं जाई। त्रिजटा कहि सब कथा सुनाई॥ सिर भुज बाढ़ि सुनत रिपु केरी। सीता उर भइ त्रास घनेरी ॥
translation: उसी रात त्रिजटा ने सीताजी के पास जाकर उन्हें सब कथा कह सुनाई। शत्रु के सिर और भुजाओं की बढ़ती का संवाद सुनकर सीताजी के हृदय में बड़ा भय हुआ ॥
english_translation: That night Trijata went to Sita and told her the whole story. Hearing that the enemy's head and arms were growing larger, Sita felt deep fear in her heart.
essence: News of the beloved's danger brings fear before any answer arrives.
simple_meaning: Trijata tells Sita about the battle, and Sita becomes very afraid when she hears the enemy is growing stronger.
insight: It shows how deeply Sita is emotionally tied to Ram's struggle, and how quickly hope can turn into anxiety.
modern_relevance: You refresh the news after midnight and see the situation getting worse for someone you love. Your chest tightens before you can even think.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुख मलीन उपजी मन चिंता। त्रिजटा सन बोली तब सीता॥ होइहि कहा कहसि किन माता। केहि बिधि मरिहि बिस्व दुखदाता ॥
translation: (उनका) मुख उदास हो गया, मन में चिंता उत्पन्न हो गई। तब सीताजी त्रिजटा से बोलीं- हे माता! बताती क्यों नहीं? क्या होगा? संपूर्ण विश्व को दुःख देने वाला यह किस प्रकार मरेगा? ॥
english_translation: Her face grew pale and her mind filled with worry. Then Sita spoke to Trijata: "Mother, why do you not tell me? How will the one who brings sorrow to the whole world die?"
essence: Worry rises when justice seems far away.
simple_meaning: Sita grows worried after hearing that Ravana has been wounded and asks Trijata how the world’s tormentor will die.
insight: It shifts attention from the wound itself to the longing for moral resolution.
modern_relevance: You hear that someone who has hurt many people may still escape consequences. Your chest tightens because you want the world made right, not delayed again.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: रघुपति सर सिर कटेहुँ न मरई। बिधि बिपरीत चरित सब करई॥ मोर अभाग्य जिआवत ओही। जेहिं हौं हरि पद कमल बिछोही ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी के बाणों से सिर कटने पर भी नहीं मरता। विधाता सारे चरित्र विपरीत (उलटे) ही कर रहा है। (सच बात तो यह है कि) मेरा दुर्भाग्य ही उसे जिला रहा है, जिसने मुझे भगवान् के चरणकमलों से अलग कर दिया है ॥
english_translation: Even if Raghunath's arrow cuts off his head, he does not die. Fate is making everything run in reverse. My own bad fortune is keeping him alive, the one who separated me from the lotus feet of Hari.
essence: Separation from Ram makes even survival feel like a curse.
simple_meaning: Sita feels that Ravana can survive only because her own misfortune still holds her in separation from Ram. She sees the world as turned upside down by fate.
insight: It shows how separation and fear distort perception, making suffering feel like the force that sustains the problem.
modern_relevance: You watch someone keep escaping consequences while you sit with the mess they caused. In that moment, it can feel as if the whole world is working backward.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: जेहिं कृत कपट कनक मृग झूठा। अजहुँ सो दैव मोहि पर रूठा॥ जेहिं बिधि मोहि दुख दुसह सहाए। लछिमन कहुँ कटु बचन कहाए ॥
translation: जिसने कपट का झूठा स्वर्ण मृग बनाया था, वही दैव अब भी मुझ पर रूठा हुआ है, जिस विधाता ने मुझसे दुःसह दुःख सहन कराए और लक्ष्मण को कड़ुवे वचन कहलाए, ॥
english_translation: The one who made the false golden deer still seems angry with me. The same fate has made me endure unbearable pain and made Lakshman speak harsh words.
essence: Pain turns separate wounds into one enemy.
simple_meaning: Sita blames the same cruel force for both the false golden deer and her present suffering. She feels that this force has kept hurting her and even caused Lakshman to speak harshly.
insight: It shows how pain can make the mind see a single hostile force behind many events.
modern_relevance: After one betrayal, every small delay feels like proof that life is against you. In that state, the mind ties separate hurts into one unbearable pattern.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: रघुपति बिरह सबिष सर भारी। तकि तकि मार बार बहु मारी॥ ऐसेहुँ दुख जो राख मम प्राना। सोइ बिधि ताहि जिआव न आना ॥
translation: जो श्री रघुनाथजी के विरह रूपी बड़े विषैले बाणों से तक-तककर मुझे बहुत बार मारकर, अब भी मार रहा है और ऐसे दुःख में भी जो मेरे प्राणों को रख रहा है, वही विधाता उस (रावण) को जिला रहा है, दूसरा कोई नहीं ॥
english_translation: The sharp arrows of separation from Raghupati strike me again and again, yet my life still remains. The same fate that keeps me alive in this pain keeps Ravana alive too; no one else does.
essence: Separation can keep you alive while feeling like repeated death.
simple_meaning: Ravana says Ram’s absence feels like poisoned arrows hitting him again and again. Even while this pain keeps him alive, the same power is keeping Ram’s enemy alive too.
insight: It shifts the mind from triumphal pride to the unbearable cost of clinging to what is already lost.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after a breakup, and every glance stings. The hurt doesn’t just visit once — it keeps returning, and somehow you are still standing through it.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: बहु बिधि कर बिलाप जानकी। करि करि सुरति कृपानिधान की॥ कह त्रिजटा सुनु राजकुमारी। उर सर लागत मरइ सुरारी ॥
translation: कृपानिधान श्री रामजी की याद कर-करके जानकीजी बहुत प्रकार से विलाप कर रही हैं। त्रिजटा ने कहा- हे राजकुमारी! सुनो, देवताओं का शत्रु रावण हृदय में बाण लगते ही मर जाएगा ॥
english_translation: Sita wept in many ways, remembering the compassionate Lord again and again. Trijata said, “Listen, princess. The enemy of the radiant beings will die the moment an arrow strikes his heart.”
essence: Grief is met here with a promise that the end is near.
simple_meaning: Sita grieves for Ram, and Trijata comforts her by saying Ravana will die when an arrow reaches his heart.
insight: It shifts the mind from helpless grief to patient expectation of relief.
modern_relevance: You sit alone with a message thread unanswered, replaying the same pain. Then one calm friend says, “This won’t last forever,” and your breathing changes.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु ताते उर हतइ न तेही। एहि के हृदयँ बसति बैदेही ॥
translation: परन्तु प्रभु उसके हृदय में बाण इसलिए नहीं मारते कि इसके हृदय में जानकीजी (आप) बसती हैं ॥ छंद :
english_translation: But the Lord does not strike his heart with arrows, because Janaki lives in that heart.
essence: A heart already filled with devotion cannot be easily wounded.
simple_meaning: The Lord does not harm the one whose heart already holds Sita. Love for her becomes a shield.
insight: It shifts the mind from fear of attack to the protecting power of inward devotion.
modern_relevance: You open your messages and see a cruel reply waiting to ruin your mood. But one steady love, one deep commitment, can keep bitterness from taking over your heart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: एहि के हृदयँ बस जानकी जानकी उर मम बास है। मम उदर भुअन अनेक लागत बान सब कर नास है॥ सुनि बचन हरष बिषाद मन अति देखि पुनि त्रिजटाँ कहा। अब मरिहि रिपु एहि बिधि सुनहि सुंदरि तजहि संसय महा॥
translation: वे यही सोचकर रह जाते हैं कि) इसके हृदय में जानकी का निवास है, जानकी के हृदय में मेरा निवास है और मेरे उदर में अनेकों भुवन हैं। अतः रावण के हृदय में बाण लगते ही सब भुवनों का नाश हो जाएगा। यह वचन सुनकर सीताजी के मन में अत्यंत हर्ष और विषाद हुआ देखकर त्रिजटा ने फिर कहा- हे सुंदरी! महान् संदेह का त्याग कर दो, अब सुनो, शत्रु इस प्रकार मरेगा-
english_translation: Because Sita lives in his heart, and Ravana lives in Sita's heart, and countless worlds dwell in Ravana's belly, no arrow can yet destroy him. Hearing this, Sita felt both joy and sorrow. Seeing that, Trijata said again: "O beautiful one, cast away this great doubt. Listen now: the enemy will die in this way."
essence: What holds the enemy alive is the mind's own attachment.
simple_meaning: Trijata explains that Ravana cannot be killed yet because Sita remains in his heart. She comforts Sita by saying the enemy will die only after his attachment to her breaks.
insight: It shifts attention from outer conflict to inner fixation as the real source of bondage.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone because one person still has too much power over your mood. As long as your mind is stuck there, the pattern stays alive.
speaker: Trijata

verse_text: काटत सिर होइहि बिकल छुटि जाइहि तव ध्यान। तब रावनहि हृदय महुँ मरिहहिं रामु सुजान ॥
translation: सिरों के बार-बार काटे जाने से जब वह व्याकुल हो जाएगा और उसके हृदय से तुम्हारा ध्यान छूट जाएगा, तब सुजान (अंतर्यामी) श्री रामजी रावण के हृदय में बाण मारेंगे ॥
english_translation: When his head is cut again and again and he becomes distracted, and your remembrance leaves his heart, then wise Ram will strike Ravana in the heart.
essence: Ego falls only when its grip on attention breaks.
simple_meaning: Ravana can be defeated only after repeated blows make him lose focus. Once his remembrance of Sita slips, Ram will strike at his heart.
insight: It shifts you from seeing victory as force alone to seeing attention and fixation as the real battlefield.
modern_relevance: You keep defending a bad habit until exhaustion cracks your concentration. The moment your grip loosens, the thing that seemed invincible starts to fall.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: अस कहि बहुत भाँति समुझाई। पुनि त्रिजटा निज भवन सिधाई॥ राम सुभाउ सुमिरि बैदेही। उपजी बिरह बिथा अति तेही ॥
translation: ऐसा कहकर और सीताजी को बहुत प्रकार से समझाकर फिर त्रिजटा अपने घर चली गई। श्री रामचंद्रजी के स्वभाव का स्मरण करके जानकीजी को अत्यंत विरह व्यथा उत्पन्न हुई ॥
english_translation: Thus speaking, and after comforting Sita in many ways, Trijata returned to her own home. Remembering Rama's nature, Vaidehi was filled with intense pain of separation.
essence: Remembering what you love can make absence feel sharper.
simple_meaning: Trijata reassures Sita and goes home, but Sita's memory of Rama makes her separation hurt even more.
insight: It shows how remembrance can intensify longing rather than soothe it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: निसिहि ससिहि निंदति बहु भाँति। जुग सम भई सिराति न राती॥ करति बिलाप मनहिं मन भारी। राम बिरहँ जानकी दुखारी ॥
translation: वे रात्रि की और चंद्रमा की बहुत प्रकार से निंदा कर रही हैं (और कह रही हैं-) रात युग के समान बड़ी हो गई, वह बीतती ही नहीं। जानकीजी श्री रामजी के विरह में दुःखी होकर मन ही मन भारी विलाप कर रही हैं ॥
english_translation: She keeps blaming the night and the moon in many ways. The night feels like an age and still does not end. Janaki grieves inwardly, heavy with sorrow over Ram's separation.
essence: Longing makes time itself feel cruel.
simple_meaning: Sita is so heartbroken that the night feels endless, and she quietly laments Ram's absence.
insight: It shifts attention to the lived weight of longing, not just the fact of waiting.
modern_relevance: You keep checking the clock at 2:13 a.m., and the room feels too quiet. When your heart is waiting for someone, even a short night can feel endless.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जब अति भयउ बिरह उर दाहू। फरकेउ बाम नयन अरु बाहू॥ सगुन बिचारि धरी मन धीरा। अब मिलिहहिं कृपाल रघुबीरा ॥
translation: जब विरह के मारे हृदय में दारुण दाह हो गया, तब उनका बायाँ नेत्र और बाहु फड़क उठे। शकुन समझकर उन्होंने मन में धैर्य धारण किया कि अब कृपालु श्री रघुवीर अवश्य मिलेंगे ॥
english_translation: When the pain of separation burned fiercely in her heart, her left eye and arm twitched. Reading it as an omen, she steadied her mind: now the merciful Raghubir will surely come to me.
essence: Hope can arrive first as a sign before it arrives as proof.
simple_meaning: Sita’s separation becomes so intense that her body reacts, but she reads the sign as hope and steadies herself, believing Ram will soon come.
insight: It teaches you to read hope without forcing certainty and to steady yourself before fear takes over.
modern_relevance: You’re staring at your phone after a hard message, trying not to spiral. Then something small—a call back, a missed sign, a sudden calm—lets you breathe again.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: इहाँ अर्धनिसि रावनु जागा। निज सारथि सन खीझन लागा। सठ रनभूमि छड़ाइसि मोही। धिग धिग अधम मंदमति तोही ॥
translation: यहाँ आधी रात को रावण (मूर्च्छा से) जागा और अपने सारथी पर रुष्ट होकर कहने लगा- अरे मूर्ख! तूने मुझे रणभूमि से अलग कर दिया। अरे अधम! अरे मंदबुद्धि! तुझे धिक्कार है, धिक्कार है! ॥
english_translation: Here, in the middle of the night, Ravana woke up and began scolding his charioteer. “Fool! You dragged me away from the battlefield. Shame on you, shame on you, lowly, dull-witted one!”
essence: Pride cannot bear defeat, so it attacks the helper.
simple_meaning: Ravana wakes in the night and angrily abuses his charioteer for pulling him away from battle.
insight: It reveals how ego protects itself by blaming the nearest person.
modern_relevance: You snap at the driver, the assistant, or the teammate who only carried your mistake forward. The anger is loud, but the wound underneath is bruised pride.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: तेहिं पद गहि बहु बिधि समुझावा। भोरु भएँ रथ चढ़ि पुनि धावा॥ सुनि आगवनु दसानन केरा। कपि दल खरभर भयउ घनेरा ॥
translation: सारथि ने चरण पकड़कर रावण को बहुत प्रकार से समझाया। सबेरा होते ही वह रथ पर चढ़कर फिर दौड़ा। रावण का आना सुनकर वानरों की सेना में बड़ी खलबली मच गई ॥
english_translation: The charioteer clasped his feet and tried to persuade him in many ways. At dawn he mounted the chariot and charged again. Hearing Ravana return, the monkey army fell into great confusion.
essence: Reckless return can disturb everyone around you.
simple_meaning: The charioteer tries to calm Ravana, but Ravana rides out again at dawn, and the monkey army is thrown into confusion.
insight: It shows how one impulsive return can spread fear through an entire crowd.
modern_relevance: A tense group chat blows up again after everyone thought the issue was over. One person charges back in, and the whole room tightens at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ तहँ भूधर बिटप उपारी। धाए कटकटाइ भट भारी ॥
translation: वे भारी योद्धा जहाँ-तहाँ से पर्वत और वृक्ष उखाड़कर (क्रोध से) दाँत कटकटाकर दौड़े ॥
english_translation: The mighty warriors rushed from every side, uprooting mountains and trees, grinding their teeth in fury.
essence: The battle surges forward in sheer fury.
simple_meaning: Warriors from all sides tore up mountains and trees and rushed forward in rage.
insight: It shifts attention from inner meaning to the physical violence of the battle scene.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धाए जो मर्कट बिकट भालु कराल कर भूधर धरा। अति कोप करहिं प्रहार मारत भजि चले रजनीचरा॥ बिचलाइ दल बलवंत कीसन्ह घेरि पुनि रावनु लियो। चहुँ दिसि चपेटन्हि मारि नखन्हि बिदारि तन ब्याकुल कियो॥
translation: विकट और विकराल वानर-भालू हाथों में पर्वत लिए दौड़े। वे अत्यंत क्रोध करके प्रहार करते हैं। उनके मारने से राक्षस भाग चले। बलवान् वानरों ने शत्रु की सेना को विचलित करके फिर रावण को घेर लिया। चारों ओर से चपेटे मारकर और नखों से शरीर विदीर्ण कर वानरों ने उसको व्याकुल कर दिया॥
english_translation: The fierce monkeys and bears rushed forward with mountains in their hands. In great rage they struck, and the demons fled. The powerful monkeys scattered the enemy army and then surrounded Ravana again. They lashed him from all sides, clawed him apart, and left him reeling in pain.
essence: The battlefield swings back as Ravana is driven into retreat.
simple_meaning: The monkey and bear army attacks fiercely, scatters the demons, and surrounds Ravana again, leaving him battered and overwhelmed.
insight: It shows the tide of battle turning through coordinated force and relentless counterattack.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि महा मर्कट प्रबल रावन कीन्ह बिचार। अंतरहित होइ निमिष महुँ कृत माया बिस्तार ॥
translation: वानरों को बड़ा ही प्रबल देखकर रावण ने विचार किया और अंतर्धान होकर क्षणभर में उसने माया फैलाई ॥
english_translation: Seeing the mighty monkeys, Ravana thought it over and vanished in a moment, spreading his illusion.
essence: Fear hides, then reaches for illusion.
simple_meaning: Ravana sees the monkey army, hides himself, and creates an illusion to confuse them.
insight: It shows how fear and ego can turn a fight into manipulation.
modern_relevance: A person gets cornered in a meeting, goes quiet, and starts spinning half-truths instead of facing the question directly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जब कीन्ह तेहिं पाषंड। भए प्रगट जंतु प्रचंड॥ बेताल भूत पिसाच। कर धरें धनु नाराच ॥
translation: जब उसने पाखंड (माया) रचा, तब भयंकर जीव प्रकट हो गए। बेताल, भूत और पिशाच हाथों में धनुष-बाण लिए प्रकट हुए! ॥
english_translation: When he created that deception, fierce beings appeared. Vampires, ghosts, and spirits appeared with bows and arrows in their hands.
essence: False appearances can turn fear into a crowd.
simple_meaning: Ravana’s illusion makes terrifying figures appear, each armed and ready to attack. The scene is meant to overwhelm the eye and frighten the enemy.
insight: It shows how deception can manufacture panic by dressing fear in visible forms.
modern_relevance: A rumor hits your phone and suddenly everyone seems dangerous, guilty, or against you. Fear can multiply faster than facts when imagination takes over.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जोगिनि गहें करबाल। एक हाथ मनुज कपाल॥ करि सद्य सोनित पान। नाचहिं करहिं बहु गान ॥
translation: योगिनियाँ एक हाथ में तलवार और दूसरे हाथ में मनुष्य की खोपड़ी लिए ताजा खून पीकर नाचने और बहुत तरह के गीत गाने लगीं ॥
english_translation: Yoginis, with a sword in one hand and a human skull in the other, drank fresh blood, then danced and sang in many ways.
essence: Illusion can turn fear into a weapon.
simple_meaning: The verse describes terrifying magical figures appearing in battle, armed and drinking blood as they dance and sing.
insight: It shows how spectacle and terror can be used to unsettle the mind before real harm arrives.
modern_relevance: A rumor starts in a crowded group chat, and suddenly everyone imagines the worst. Fear spreads faster than facts, just like Ravana's illusion here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धरु मारु बोलहिं घोर। रहि पूरि धुनि चहुँ ओर॥ मुख बाइ धावहिं खान। तब लगे कीस परान ॥
translation: वे 'पक़ड़ो, मारो' आदि घोर शब्द बोल रही हैं। चारों ओर (सब दिशाओं में) यह ध्वनि भर गई। वे मुख फैलाकर खाने दौड़ती हैं। तब वानर भागने लगे ॥
english_translation: They cry out in fierce voices, “Seize! Kill!” The sound fills all directions. With mouths gaping, they rush to devour, and then the monkeys begin to flee.
essence: Chaos can make even the brave run.
simple_meaning: Fierce cries fill the air, and terrifying beings rush forward to devour the monkeys, who panic and run.
insight: It shows how disorder breaks courage by overwhelming the senses before the mind can respond.
modern_relevance: A room erupts in shouting, and before you can think, everyone is reacting at once. Panic becomes contagious the moment danger feels all around you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ जाहिं मर्कट भागि। तहँ बरत देखहिं आगि॥ भए बिकल बानर भालु। पुनि लाग बरषै बालु ॥
translation: वानर भागकर जहाँ भी जाते हैं, वहीं आग जलती देखते हैं। वानर-भालू व्याकुल हो गए। फिर रावण बालू बरसाने लगा ॥
english_translation: Wherever the monkeys ran, they found fire blazing there. The monkeys and bears grew frantic. Then Ravana began raining sand.
essence: Ravana turns escape itself into another wound.
simple_meaning: The fleeing monkey and bear forces keep meeting fire and sand, which leaves them confused and helpless.
insight: It shows how pressure can multiply until even retreat feels impossible.
modern_relevance: You open one app to fix a problem, and three more alerts hit before you finish. Everything you try seems to trigger another obstacle.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ तहँ थकित करि कीस। गर्जेउ बहुरि दससीस॥ लछिमन कपीस समेत। भए सकल बीर अचेत ॥
translation: वानरों को जहाँ-तहाँ थकित (शिथिल) कर रावण फिर गरजा। लक्ष्मणजी और सुग्रीव सहित सभी वीर अचेत हो गए ॥
english_translation: Ravana wearied the monkeys everywhere, then roared again. Lakshmana, Sugriva, and all the heroes fell unconscious.
essence: Pressure can wear down even the bravest.
simple_meaning: Ravana keeps pressuring the monkey army until even Lakshmana and Sugriva lose consciousness.
insight: It shows the cost of sustained pressure: force can exhaust courage itself.
modern_relevance: A long day of crisis leaves everyone frayed: the team is exhausted, the leader is numb, and even the most capable people cannot keep pushing forever.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हा राम हा रघुनाथ। कहि सुभट मीजहिं हाथ॥ ऐहि बिधि सकल बल तोरि। तेहिं कीन्ह कपट बहोरि ॥
translation: हा राम! हा रघुनाथ पुकारते हुए श्रेष्ठ योद्धा अपने हाथ मलते (पछताते) हैं। इस प्रकार सब का बल तोड़कर रावण ने फिर दूसरी माया रची ॥
english_translation: Crying, “Ha Ram! Ha Raghunath!” the great warriors wrung their hands in despair. After breaking everyone’s strength this way, Ravana then used another trick.
essence: Pressure can break strength before the next blow lands.
simple_meaning: The warriors were so exhausted and shaken that they cried out in despair. Ravana then used another deceptive tactic to keep them off balance.
insight: It shows how relentless pressure can weaken resolve before the next move even begins.
modern_relevance: After three brutal meetings, your team is drained, confused, and ready to quit. The hardest part is not the fight itself — it is what pressure does to judgment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रगटेसि बिपुल हनुमान। धाए गहे पाषान॥ तिन्ह रामु घेरे जाइ। चहुँ दिसि बरूथ बनाइ ॥
translation: उसने बहुत से हनुमान् प्रकट किए, जो पत्थर लिए दौड़े। उन्होंने चारों ओर दल बनाकर श्री रामचंद्रजी को जा घेरा ॥
english_translation: He manifested countless Hanumans, who ran forward with stones in hand. They surrounded Ram on all four sides, forming ranks.
essence: The fight tightens as Hanuman's ranks close around Ram.
simple_meaning: Many Hanumans rush in with stones and surround Ram from all sides, forming battle lines.
insight: It shows the battle turning into a full encirclement, with forces gathering around Ram.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मारहु धरहु जनि जाइ। कटकटहिं पूँछ उठाइ॥ दहँ दिसि लँगूर बिराज। तेहिं मध्य कोसलराज ॥
translation: वे पूँछ उठाकर कटकटाते हुए पुकारने लगे, 'मारो, पकड़ो, जाने न पावे'। उनके लंगूर (पूँछ) दसों दिशाओं में शोभा दे रहे हैं और उनके बीच में कोसलराज श्री रामजी हैं ॥
english_translation: Shout, seize him, do not let him go! With tails raised and rattling, they stand in all ten directions, and in their midst is the king of Kosala.
essence: Ram stands secure in the middle of gathered strength.
simple_meaning: The monkey warriors raise their tails and surround Ram from every side, ready for battle.
insight: It frames courage as collective force, with Ram held safe at the center.
modern_relevance: A team crowds around a friend in crisis, all speaking at once, all ready to help. The moment is not quiet, but no one is left unsupported.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहिं मध्य कोसलराज सुंदर स्याम तन सोभा लही। जनु इंद्रधनुष अनेक की बर बारि तुंग तमालही॥ प्रभु देखि हरष बिषाद उर सुर बदत जय जय जय करी। रघुबीर एकहिं तीर कोपि निमेष महुँ माया हरी ॥
translation: उनके बीच में कोसलराज का सुंदर श्याम शरीर ऐसी शोभा पा रहा है, मानो ऊँचे तमाल वृक्ष के लिए अनेक इंद्रधनुषों की श्रेष्ठ बाढ़ (घेरा) बनाई गई हो। प्रभु को देखकर देवता हर्ष और विषादयुक्त हृदय से 'जय, जय, जय' ऐसा बोलने लगे। तब श्री रघुवीर ने क्रोध करके एक ही बाण में निमेषमात्र में रावण की सारी माया हर ली ॥
english_translation: In their midst, the handsome dark form of the Lord of Kosala shone like many rainbows encircling a tall tamala tree. Seeing the Lord, the beings of heaven felt joy and sorrow together and cried, "Victory, victory, victory." Then Raghuvir, in anger, in a single arrow and in a moment, stripped away Ravana's illusion.
essence: One clear strike can end the illusion that multiplies fear.
simple_meaning: Ram stands shining in the battle, and even the heavenly beings are overwhelmed when they see him. With one arrow, he destroys Ravana's illusion at once.
insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle of confusion to the one action that breaks it.
modern_relevance: You finally see the real problem behind the chaos in a tense meeting, and one clear decision dissolves the whole mess. What looked huge was mostly smoke.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: माया बिगत कपि भालु हरषे बिटप गिरि गहि सब फिरे। सर निकर छाड़े राम रावन बाहु सिर पुनि महि गिरे॥ श्रीराम रावन समर चरित अनेक कल्प जो गावहीं। सत सेष सारद निगम कबि तेउ तदपि पार न पावहीं ॥
translation: माया दूर हो जाने पर वानर-भालू हर्षित हुए और वृक्ष तथा पर्वत ले-लेकर सब लौट पड़े। श्री रामजी ने बाणों के समूह छोड़े, जिनसे रावण के हाथ और सिर फिर कट-कटकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े। श्री रामजी और रावण के युद्ध का चरित्र यदि सैकड़ों शेष, सरस्वती, वेद और कवि अनेक कल्पों तक गाते रहें, तो भी उसका पार नहीं पा सकते ॥
english_translation: When the veil of illusion lifted, the monkeys and bears rejoiced and returned, lifting trees and mountains. Lord Ram then loosed volleys of arrows, and Ravana's arms and heads fell again and again to the ground. The deeds of the war between Lord Ram and Ravana are beyond measure: even if hundreds of Shesh, Saraswati, the Vedas, and poets sang for countless ages, they could not reach the far shore.
essence: Some events are so vast that even endless telling cannot finish them.
simple_meaning: The battle surges again: the monkeys and bears return to fighting, Ram keeps cutting down Ravana's arms and heads, and the poem says this war is too vast for anyone to fully describe.
insight: It shifts attention from the battle's details to its overwhelming scale and epic weight.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: ताके गुन गन कछु कहे जड़मति तुलसीदास। जिमि निज बल अनुरूप ते माछी उड़इ अकास ॥
translation: उसी चरित्र के कुछ गुणगण मंदबुद्धि तुलसीदास ने कहे हैं, जैसे मक्खी भी अपने पुरुषार्थ के अनुसार आकाश में उड़ती है ॥
english_translation: Tulsidas, with dull wit, has spoken some qualities of that character, just as a fly flies in the sky according to its own small strength.
essence: Even praise is tiny beside what it tries to name.
simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he has only described a few qualities of Ram's character, and only to the limit of his own small ability.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to humility before greatness.
modern_relevance: You finish a big project and still feel it barely captured what mattered. That quiet honesty — knowing your reach without pretending otherwise — is what this line models.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: काटे सिर भुज बार बहु मरत न भट लंकेस। प्रभु क्रीड़त सुर सिद्ध मुनि ब्याकुल देखि कलेस ॥
translation: सिर और भुजाएँ बहुत बार काटी गईं। फिर भी वीर रावण मरता नहीं। प्रभु तो खेल कर रहे हैं, परन्तु मुनि, सिद्ध और देवता उस क्लेश को देखकर (प्रभु को क्लेश पाते समझकर) व्याकुल हैं ॥
english_translation: His heads and arms were cut off many times, yet the lord of Lanka did not die. The divine one was merely playing, but sages, perfected beings, and radiant beings were distressed to see the suffering.
essence: What looks like suffering may be only divine play.
simple_meaning: Ravana keeps surviving even after repeated attacks, and the onlookers are upset because they think the divine one is suffering.
insight: It shifts attention from visible struggle to the larger meaning hidden inside it.
modern_relevance: You keep trying to fix the same problem, and it only seems to multiply. From the outside, it looks like failure; from a wider view, the pattern is still unfolding.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: काटत बढ़हिं सीस समुदाई। जिमि प्रति लाभ लोभ अधिकाई॥ मरइ न रिपु श्रम भयउ बिसेषा। राम बिभीषन तन तब देखा ॥
translation: काटते ही सिरों का समूह बढ़ जाता है, जैसे प्रत्येक लाभ पर लोभ बढ़ता है। शत्रु मरता नहीं और परिश्रम बहुत हुआ। तब श्री रामचंद्रजी ने विभीषण की ओर देखा ॥
english_translation: As soon as they are cut, the heads multiply, just as greed grows with every gain. The enemy does not die, and the effort has been great. Then Lord Ramchandra looked toward Vibhishana.
essence: Brute force fails when the problem keeps regenerating.
simple_meaning: Cutting down this enemy only makes more heads appear, like greed that grows with every gain. The struggle has been exhausting, and Ram turns toward Vibhishana for help.
insight: It shifts attention from repeated attack to wiser strategy and the right ally.
modern_relevance: You keep deleting spam accounts, and two more appear. You keep patching the leak, and the pipe still bursts. Sometimes force alone only proves that the real answer lies elsewhere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उमा काल मर जाकीं ईछा। सो प्रभु जन कर प्रीति परीछा॥ सुनु सरबग्य चराचर नायक। प्रनतपाल सुर मुनि सुखदायक ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! जिसकी इच्छा मात्र से काल भी मर जाता है, वही प्रभु सेवक की प्रीति की परीक्षा ले रहे हैं। (विभीषणजी ने कहा-) हे सर्वज्ञ! हे चराचर के स्वामी! हे शरणागत के पालन करने वाले! हे देवता और मुनियों को सुख देने वाले! सुनिए- ॥
english_translation: O Uma, the Lord by whose wish even Time can die is testing the devotion of his servant. Listen, all-knowing one, ruler of all moving and unmoving beings, protector of those who surrender, giver of joy to gods and sages.
