essence: Even the all-powerful may test the heart that loves him.
simple_meaning: Ram is so powerful that even Time obeys him, yet he still tests the devotion of his servant. He is also praised as the all-knowing protector of everyone who seeks refuge.
insight: It shifts the mind from demanding immediate proof to staying faithful through the test.
modern_relevance: You finally reach out for help after a long crisis, and the person you trust seems silent. That silence may not be rejection; it may be the moment your sincerity is being refined.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: नाभिकुंड पियूष बस याकें। नाथ जिअत रावनु बल ताकें॥ सुनत बिभीषन बचन कृपाला। हरषि गहे कर बान कराला ॥
translation: इसके नाभिकुंड में अमृत का निवास है। हे नाथ! रावण उसी के बल पर जीता है। विभीषण के वचन सुनते ही कृपालु श्री रघुनाथजी ने हर्षित होकर हाथ में विकराल बाण लिए ॥
english_translation: There is nectar in his navel-cavity, and by that strength Ravana still lives. Hearing Vibhishana's words, the compassionate Lord Raghunath rejoiced and took up a fierce arrow.
essence: Hidden knowledge can turn a long struggle into a single decisive move.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana points out that Ravana survives because of a hidden nectar in his navel. Hearing this, Ram takes up a fierce arrow at once.
insight: It shows that accurate insight turns effort into decisive action.
modern_relevance: You finally learn the real reason a project keeps failing: not the obvious problem, but the hidden one underneath. The whole mood shifts once the truth is named.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: असुभ होन लागे तब नाना। रोवहिं खर सृकाल बहु स्वाना॥ बोलहिं खग जग आरति हेतू। प्रगट भए नभ जहँ तहँ केतू ॥
translation: उस समय नाना प्रकार के अपशकुन होने लगे। बहुत से गदहे, स्यार और कुत्ते रोने लगे। जगत् के दुःख (अशुभ) को सूचित करने के लिए पक्षी बोलने लगे। आकाश में जहाँ-तहाँ केतु (पुच्छल तारे) प्रकट हो गए ॥
english_translation: At that time, many bad omens began to appear. Donkeys, jackals, and many dogs howled. Birds cried out, and comets appeared everywhere in the sky, signaling a world of distress.
essence: The world itself seems to announce approaching ruin.
simple_meaning: Bad omens appear everywhere: animals howl, birds cry out, and comets flash in the sky.
insight: It heightens the sense of approaching collapse by using nature as a warning signal.
modern_relevance: You wake before dawn and something feels wrong before the email arrives, before the call comes, before anyone says it aloud. The air itself seems to know.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दस दिसि दाह होन अति लागा। भयउ परब बिनु रबि उपरागा॥ मंदोदरि उर कंपति भारी। प्रतिमा स्रवहिं नयन मग बारी ॥
translation: दसों दिशाओं में अत्यंत दाह होने लगा (आग लगने लगी) बिना ही पर्व (योग) के सूर्यग्रहण होने लगा। मंदोदरी का हृदय बहुत काँपने लगा। मूर्तियाँ नेत्र मार्ग से जल बहाने लगीं ॥
english_translation: A fierce burning spread in all ten directions. An eclipse appeared without the moon's proper alignment. Mandodari's heart shook hard. Even the statues began to weep through their eyes.
essence: When adharma ripens, even the world seems to grieve.
simple_meaning: The world around Lanka turns ominous: heat, tremors, tears, and unnatural signs all signal disaster.
insight: It shifts attention to warning signs that a situation has crossed into collapse.
modern_relevance: The room goes strangely quiet before bad news lands. A phone keeps buzzing, your stomach tightens, and even small things feel off. You can sense that a structure is breaking before it falls.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रतिमा रुदहिं पबिपात नभ अति बात बह डोलति मही। बरषहिं बलाहक रुधिर कच रज असुभ अति सक को कही॥ उतपात अमित बिलोकि नभ सुर बिकल बोलहिं जय जए। सुर सभय जानि कृपाल रघुपति चाप सर जोरत भए॥
translation: मूर्तियाँ रोने लगीं, आकाश से वज्रपात होने लगे, अत्यंत प्रचण्ड वायु बहने लगी, पृथ्वी हिलने लगी, बादल रक्त, बाल और धूल की वर्षा करने लगे। इस प्रकार इतने अधिक अमंगल होने लगे कि उनको कौन कह सकता है? अपरिमित उत्पात देखकर आकाश में देवता व्याकुल होकर जय-जय पुकार उठे। देवताओं को भयभीत जानकर कृपालु श्री रघुनाथजी धनुष पर बाण सन्धान करने लगे।
english_translation: Idols began to weep, lightning struck the sky, fierce winds blew, the earth trembled, and clouds rained blood, hair, and dust. Who could count such countless omens? Seeing the sky filled with calamities, the gods grew restless and cried out, “Victory! Victory!” Knowing them afraid, compassionate Raghu’s lord drew his bow and prepared his arrows.
essence: True composure shows itself when everything else is shaking.
simple_meaning: The world fills with terrible signs as the battle turns. Even the gods panic, and Ram calmly prepares his bow to protect them.
insight: It shifts attention from reacting to crisis toward becoming the one who can meet it cleanly.
modern_relevance: The group chat is exploding, the deadline has broken, and everyone is spiraling. In the middle of that noise, someone still needs a steady hand.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: खैंचि सरासन श्रवन लगि छाड़े सर एकतीस। रघुनायक सायक चले मानहुँ काल फनीस ॥
translation: कानों तक धनुष को खींचकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने इकतीस बाण छोड़े। वे श्री रामचंद्रजी के बाण ऐसे चले मानो कालसर्प हों ॥
english_translation: Drawing the bow to his ear, Raghunath released thirty-one arrows. Rama's arrows flew like the serpent of time.
essence: Ram's arrows strike with the force of time itself.
simple_meaning: Ram draws his bow to his ear and releases thirty-one arrows with force, as if time itself has become a serpent.
insight: It shows the speed and decisiveness of action in battle.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सायक एक नाभि सर सोषा। अपर लगे भुज सिर करि रोषा॥ लै सिर बाहु चले नाराचा। सिर भुज हीन रुंड महि नाचा ॥
translation: एक बाण ने नाभि के अमृत कुंड को सोख लिया। दूसरे तीस बाण कोप करके उसके सिरों और भुजाओं में लगे। बाण सिरों और भुजाओं को लेकर चले। सिरों और भुजाओं से रहित रुण्ड (धड़) पृथ्वी पर नाचने लगा ॥
english_translation: One arrow dried up the nectar pool in his navel. The other arrows, in anger, struck his heads and arms. The arrows carried away the heads and arms. The headless trunk danced on the ground.
essence: Ravana’s strength is cut down to frantic ruin.
simple_meaning: Rama’s arrows strike Ravana so fiercely that his life source is drained, his heads and arms are severed, and his body thrashes on the ground.
insight: It shows how quickly force and arrogance can turn into helplessness.
modern_relevance: A public argument has already gone too far, and the other person keeps lashing out. You can see the collapse beneath the noise, even before it fully lands.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धरनि धसइ धर धाव प्रचंडा। तब सर हति प्रभु कृत दुइ खंडा॥ गर्जेउ मरत घोर रव भारी। कहाँ रामु रन हतौं पचारी ॥
translation: धड़ प्रचण्ड वेग से दौड़ता है, जिससे धरती धँसने लगी। तब प्रभु ने बाण मारकर उसके दो टुकड़े कर दिए। मरते समय रावण बड़े घोर शब्द से गरजकर बोला- राम कहाँ हैं? मैं ललकारकर उनको युद्ध में मारूँ! ॥
english_translation: The body rushed forward with fierce speed, and the earth seemed to sink. Then the Lord struck with an arrow and cut it into two pieces. As he was dying, Ravana roared in a terrible voice, "Where is Ram? I will challenge him and kill him in battle!"
essence: Ego can keep shouting after defeat has already arrived.
simple_meaning: Ravana’s body lunges forward, but Ram’s arrow cuts him down. Even while dying, Ravana keeps shouting challenges instead of surrendering.
insight: It shows how unchecked ego refuses reality, even when defeat is already complete.
modern_relevance: Someone loses the argument, the job, the relationship — and still keeps texting, defending, and posturing as if nothing has changed. The body may fall before the ego does.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: डोली भूमि गिरत दसकंधर। छुभित सिंधु सरि दिग्गज भूधर॥ धरनि परेउ द्वौ खंड बढ़ाई। चापि भालु मर्कट समुदाई ॥
translation: रावण के गिरते ही पृथ्वी हिल गई। समुद्र, नदियाँ, दिशाओं के हाथी और पर्वत क्षुब्ध हो उठे। रावण धड़ के दोनों टुकड़ों को फैलाकर भालू और वानरों के समुदाय को दबाता हुआ पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा ॥
english_translation: As Ravana fell, the earth trembled. The ocean, rivers, guardian elephants, and mountains were shaken. His two severed halves fell to the ground, crushing the bears and monkeys as they struck the earth.
essence: His fall is so vast it shakes the world around him.
simple_meaning: Ravana's fall shakes the whole world, and his broken body crushes the monkey and bear armies as it hits the ground.
insight: It keeps the focus on the physical aftermath of defeat rather than on victory or moral reflection.
modern_relevance: A powerful person loses everything in public, and the whole room still feels the impact. Even collapse can leave a mess behind.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंदोदरि आगें भुज सीसा। धरि सर चले जहाँ जगदीसा॥ प्रबिसे सब निषंग महुँ जाई। देखि सुरन्ह दुंदुभीं बजाई ॥
translation: रावण की भुजाओं और सिरों को मंदोदरी के सामने रखकर रामबाण वहाँ चले, जहाँ जगदीश्वर श्री रामजी थे। सब बाण जाकर तरकस में प्रवेश कर गए। यह देखकर देवताओं ने नगाड़े बजाए ॥
english_translation: Holding Ravana's arms and heads before Mandodari, the arrows went back to where the Lord of the world was. All the arrows entered the quiver again. Seeing this, the radiant beings beat their drums.
essence: Even victory returns to Ram's hands.
simple_meaning: The arrows finish their work and return to Ram's quiver. The radiant beings celebrate what they see.
insight: It turns a killing blow into a sign of perfect control, not rage.
modern_relevance: After a brutal argument, you realize the sharp words are already gone, and all that's left is the relief of what did not have to continue.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तासु तेज समान प्रभु आनन। हरषे देखि संभु चतुरानन॥ जय जय धुनि पूरी ब्रह्मंडा। जय रघुबीर प्रबल भुजदंडा ॥
translation: रावण का तेज प्रभु के मुख में समा गया। यह देखकर शिवजी और ब्रह्माजी हर्षित हुए। ब्रह्माण्डभर में जय-जय की ध्वनि भर गई। प्रबल भुजदण्डों वाले श्री रघुवीर की जय हो ॥
english_translation: Ravana's power was absorbed into the Lord's face. Seeing this, Shiva and Brahma rejoiced. The cry of victory filled the whole universe: victory to the mighty-armed Raghubir!
essence: Ram's victory is the universe's relief.
simple_meaning: Ravana is defeated, and even the gods rejoice as victory for Ram spreads through the universe.
insight: It shifts attention from the enemy's force to the calm authority that ends it.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after the person who dominated everyone finally loses their grip. The relief is instant — not because someone won, but because the pressure of ego has lifted.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बरषहिं सुमन देव मुनि बृंदा। जय कृपाल जय जयति मुकुंदा ॥
translation: देवता और मुनियों के समूह फूल बरसाते हैं और कहते हैं- कृपालु की जय हो, मुकुन्द की जय हो, जय हो! ॥
english_translation: The gods and sages shower flowers, crying, “Victory to the compassionate one! Victory to Mukunda!”
essence: Ram's victory draws praise because compassion has triumphed.
simple_meaning: The gods and sages celebrate Ram with flowers and praise, calling him compassionate and victorious.
insight: It shifts attention from battle to blessing, showing that true victory invites reverence.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after the hard meeting ends, and the people who saw the struggle finally exhale. Some moments are not for argument anymore — only for recognition.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जय कृपा कंद मुकुंद द्वंद हरन सरन सुखप्रद प्रभो। खल दल बिदारन परम कारन कारुनीक सदा बिभो॥ सुर सुमन बरषहिं हरष संकुल बाज दुंदुभि गहगही। संग्राम अंगन राम अंग अनंग बहु सोभा लही ॥
translation: हे कृपा के कंद! हे मोक्षदाता मुकुन्द! हे (राग-द्वेष, हर्ष-शोक, जन्म-मृत्यु आदि) द्वंद्वों के हरने वाले! हे शरणागत को सुख देने वाले प्रभो! हे दुष्ट दल को विदीर्ण करने वाले! हे कारणों के भी परम कारण! हे सदा करुणा करने वाले! हे सर्वव्यापक विभो! आपकी जय हो। देवता हर्ष में भरे हुए पुष्प बरसाते हैं, घमाघम नगाड़े बज रहे हैं। रणभूमि में श्री रामचंद्रजी के अंगों ने बहुत से कामदेवों की शोभा प्राप्त की ॥
english_translation: Victory to the source of grace, to Mukunda who ends all dualities, to the Lord who gives refuge and happiness! Victory to the destroyer of the wicked host, the supreme cause, the ever-compassionate, the all-pervading one. The devas shower flowers in joy and the drums thunder. On the battlefield, Ram's limbs gained the beauty of many love-gods.
essence: Ram turns the battlefield into a place of grace.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the giver of refuge, the remover of conflict, and the destroyer of evil. The gods rejoice, flowers rain down, and the battlefield itself becomes beautiful around him.
insight: It shifts attention from violence itself to the radiance, mercy, and order that surround right action.
modern_relevance: You step into a room where everything feels tense, and somehow your steady presence lowers the temperature. That is the kind of force this verse celebrates.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सिर जटा मुकुट प्रसून बिच बिच अति मनोहर राजहीं। जनु नीलगिरि पर तड़ित पटल समेत उडुगन भ्राजहीं॥ भुजदंड सर कोदंड फेरत रुधिर कन तन अति बने। जनु रायमुनीं तमाल पर बैठीं बिपुल सुख आपने ॥
translation: सिर पर जटाओं का मुकुट है, जिसके बीच में अत्यंत मनोहर पुष्प शोभा दे रहे हैं। मानो नीले पर्वत पर बिजली के समूह सहित नक्षत्र सुशो भित हो रहे हैं। श्री रामजी अपने भुजदण्डों से बाण और धनुष फिरा रहे हैं। शरीर पर रुधिर के कण अत्यंत सुंदर लगते हैं। मानो तमाल के वृक्ष पर बहुत सी ललमुनियाँ चिड़ियाँ अपने महान् सुख में मग्न हुई निश्चल बैठी हों ॥
english_translation: His hair is matted like a crown, with flowers shining beautifully among the locks, like stars gleaming on a blue mountain with flashes of lightning. Ram moves his bow and arrow with his mighty arms; the drops of blood on his body look beautiful, like flocks of birds resting in delight on a tamala tree.
essence: Beauty can shine even through the marks of battle.
simple_meaning: Ram is shown in the aftermath of battle, radiant and beautiful despite the blood on his body. The verse turns his warlike form into a vision of splendor and calm.
insight: It shifts attention from the wound itself to the radiance that can remain present through conflict.
modern_relevance: You come home exhausted after a hard day, clothes stained, body aching, yet something in you feels steady. The outer mess does not cancel the inner nobility.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कृपादृष्टि करि बृष्टि प्रभु अभय किए सुर बृंद। भालु कीस सब हरषे जय सुख धाम मुकुंद ॥
translation: प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी ने कृपा दृष्टि की वर्षा करके देव समूह को निर्भय कर दिया। वानर-भालू सब हर्षित हुए और सुखधाम मुकुन्द की जय हो, ऐसा पुकारने लगे ॥
english_translation: By showering his gracious glance, the Lord made the celestial hosts fearless. All the monkeys and bears rejoiced and cried, “Victory to Mukunda, the home of bliss!”
essence: A gracious glance can turn fear into celebration.
simple_meaning: Ram’s gracious glance removes fear and fills everyone with joy. Even the monkeys and bears celebrate his victory.
insight: It shifts attention from battle tension to the soothing power of divine presence.
modern_relevance: After a tense family argument, one calm look from the person at the center changes the room. The fear drops first; relief and gratitude follow.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पति सिर देखत मंदोदरी। मुरुछित बिकल धरनि खसि परी॥ जुबति बृंद रोवत उठि धाईं। तेहि उठाइ रावन पहिं आईं ॥
translation: पति के सिर देखते ही मंदोदरी व्याकुल और मूर्च्छित होकर धरती पर गिर पड़ी। स्त्रियाँ रोती हुई दौड़ीं और उस (मंदोदरी) को उठाकर रावण के पास आईं ॥
english_translation: When she saw her husband’s head, Mandodari fainted and fell to the ground. The women ran weeping, lifted her up, and brought her to Ravana.
essence: Grief can strike so hard it drops the body first.
simple_meaning: Mandodari collapses in grief when she sees Ravana’s severed head, and the women rush to help her and bring her to him.
insight: It shows grief as immediate, physical, and overwhelming before any reflection can begin.
modern_relevance: You open a message and realize the relationship is over before you can even sit down. Your body reacts first; grief arrives faster than thought.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पति गति देखि ते करहिं पुकारा। छूटे कच नहिं बपुष सँभारा॥ उर ताड़ना करहिं बिधि नाना। रोवत करहिं प्रताप बखाना ॥
translation: पति की दशा देखकर वे पुकार-पुकारकर रोने लगीं। उनके बाल खुल गए, देह की संभाल नहीं रही। वे अनेकों प्रकार से छाती पीटती हैं और रोती हुई रावण के प्रताप का बखान करती हैं ॥
english_translation: Seeing their husband's condition, they cried out in grief. Their hair came loose and they could not hold themselves together. Beating their chests in many ways, they wept and praised Ravana's power.
essence: Grief can still praise what it has lost.
simple_meaning: The women are overwhelmed by grief at Ravana's fall. They lose control of themselves, weep loudly, and even praise the power he once had.
insight: It shows how collapse can leave people clinging to old images of power even while mourning the loss.
modern_relevance: You stand at a hospital door after hearing news that changes everything. Your mind cannot sort grief from memory, and even praise slips out for what is already gone.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तव बल नाथ डोल नित धरनी। तेज हीन पावक ससि तरनी॥ सेष कमठ सहि सकहिं न भारा। सो तनु भूमि परेउ भरि छारा ॥
translation: (वे कहती हैं-) हे नाथ! तुम्हारे बल से पृथ्वी सदा काँपती रहती थी। अग्नि, चंद्रमा और सूर्य तुम्हारे सामने तेजहीन थे। शेष और कच्छप भी जिसका भार नहीं सह सकते थे, वही तुम्हारा शरीर आज धूल में भरा हुआ पृथ्वी पर पड़ा है! ॥
english_translation: O lord, by your strength the earth always trembled. Fire, the moon, and the sun lost their brilliance before you. Even Shesha and the Tortoise could not bear your burden, and now that same body lies on the ground, covered with dust.
essence: Great power can end in dust in a single moment.
simple_meaning: The women mourn Ravana by recalling how immense his strength once was, then contrast it with his body lying powerless in dust.
insight: It shifts attention from dominance to impermanence, showing how quickly force becomes helplessness.
modern_relevance: You once filled the room with force, certainty, and noise. Now the silence after the fall makes everyone remember how temporary that power was.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: बरुन कुबेर सुरेस समीरा। रन सन्मुख धरि काहुँ न धीरा॥ भुजबल जितेहु काल जम साईं। आजु परेहु अनाथ की नाईं ॥
translation: वरुण, कुबेर, इंद्र और वायु, इनमें से किसी ने भी रण में तुम्हारे सामने धैर्य धारण नहीं किया। हे स्वामी! तुमने अपने भुजबल से काल और यमराज को भी जीत लिया था। वही तुम आज अनाथ की तरह पड़े हो ॥
english_translation: Varuna, Kubera, Indra, and Vayu could not hold their courage before you in battle. Lord, by your own arm strength you conquered even Time and Yama. Today you lie fallen like one without support.
essence: What once looked invincible can collapse into helplessness.
simple_meaning: The queens remember Ravana’s old power: even the great forces of the world once could not face him. Now he lies helpless, and all that strength has vanished.
insight: It shifts the mind from admiring raw power to seeing how fragile ego-driven greatness really is.
modern_relevance: You watch someone who once dominated every room now unable to answer a phone call. The same force that looked unshakable can end in helplessness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जगत बिदित तुम्हारि प्रभुताई। सुत परिजन बल बरनि न जाई॥ राम बिमुख अस हाल तुम्हारा। रहा न कोउ कुल रोवनिहारा ॥
translation: तुम्हारी प्रभुता जगत् भर में प्रसिद्ध है। तुम्हारे पुत्रों और कुटुम्बियों के बल का हाय! वर्णन ही नहीं हो सकता। श्री रामचंद्रजी के विमुख होने से तुम्हारी ऐसी दुर्दशा हुई कि आज कुल में कोई रोने वाला भी न रह गया ॥
english_translation: Your rule was known throughout the world. No one could even describe the strength of your sons and kin. But being opposed to Ram has brought you to this state, where no one in your clan remains to weep for you.
essence: Power without alignment ends in loneliness.
simple_meaning: Ravana's former power was famous everywhere, but turning away from Ram has left him utterly broken, with no family member left to mourn him.
insight: It shifts attention from outward power to the inner cost of resisting what is right.
modern_relevance: You can build a life that looks unbeatable from the outside, then lose its center in one stubborn refusal to listen. By the time the damage is visible, the room is already empty.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: तव बस बिधि प्रचंड सब नाथा। सभय दिसिप नित नावहिं माथा॥ अब तव सिर भुज जंबुक खाहीं। राम बिमुख यह अनुचित नाहीं ॥
translation: हे नाथ! विधाता की सारी सृष्टि तुम्हारे वश में थी। लोकपाल सदा भयभीत होकर तुमको मस्तक नवाते थे, किन्तु हाय! अब तुम्हारे सिर और भुजाओं को गीदड़ खा रहे हैं। राम विमुख के लिए ऐसा होना अनुचित भी नहीं है (अर्थात् उचित ही है) ॥
english_translation: O lord, all creation once stood under your control. The guardians of the directions bowed their heads to you in fear. Now jackals eat your head and arms. For one turned away from Ram, this is not improper.
essence: Greatness collapses fast when it turns away from Ram.
simple_meaning: Even the mightiest ruler can be reduced to ruin. The verse says that turning away from Ram leaves no real protection, and the fall that follows is not surprising.
insight: It shifts the mind from admiring force to seeing the emptiness underneath force without surrender.
modern_relevance: A leader who once filled every room now sits alone after the company collapses. Titles, fear, and status cannot protect what pride has already hollowed out.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: काल बिबस पति कहा न माना। अग जग नाथु मनुज करि जाना ॥
translation: हे पति! काल के पूर्ण वश में होने से तुमने (किसी का) कहना नहीं माना और चराचर के नाथ परमात्मा को मनुष्य करके जाना ॥
english_translation: O husband, under the power of Time, you would not listen to anyone, and you saw the lord of all moving and unmoving beings as merely human.
essence: Pride under Time turns even the highest into something ordinary.
simple_meaning: Mandodari says Ravana was trapped by Time and pride, so he refused wise counsel and failed to recognize Ram's true nature.
insight: It shifts the mind from stubborn self-certainty to clear seeing before damage is done.
modern_relevance: You ignore three people who warn you not to make the same mistake, because you are sure you know better. Later, the truth is obvious — but your certainty had already closed your eyes.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: जान्यो मनुज करि दनुज कानन दहन पावक हरि स्वयं। जेहि नमत सिव ब्रह्मादि सुर पिय भजेहु नहिं करुनामयं॥ आजन्म ते परद्रोह रत पापौघमय तव तनु अयं। तुम्हहू दियो निज धाम राम नमामि ब्रह्म निरामयं॥
translation: दैत्य रूपी वन को जलाने के लिए अग्निस्वरूप साक्षात् श्री हरि को तुमने मनुष्य करके जाना। शिव और ब्रह्मा आदि देवता जिनको नमस्कार करते हैं, उन करुणामय भगवान् को हे प्रियतम! तुमने नहीं भजा। तुम्हारा यह शरीर जन्म से ही दूसरों से द्रोह करने में तत्पर तथा पाप समूहमय रहा! इतने पर भी जिन निर्विकार ब्रह्म श्री रामजी ने तुमको अपना धाम दिया, उनको मैं नमस्कार करती हूँ।
english_translation: You mistook the supreme being for a man, and the one all Shiva, Brahma, and the radiant beings bow to you did not worship. Your life was steeped in betrayal and sin from birth, yet Ram still gave you his own abode. I bow to that flawless Brahman, Ram.
essence: Ram's mercy can still hold the one who rejected him.
simple_meaning: Ravana wrongly saw Ram as only human, ignored the compassionate Lord, lived in harmful pride, yet still received Ram's own abode. The speaker bows to Ram as the flawless supreme reality.
insight: It shifts the mind from deserved punishment to the astonishing reach of grace.
modern_relevance: You keep replaying the one mistake that should have shut every door. This verse says mercy can still arrive after rejection, pride, and a lifetime of wrong turns.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अहह नाथ रघुनाथ सम कृपासिंधु नहिं आन। जोगि बृंद दुर्लभ गति तोहि दीन्हि भगवान ॥
translation: अहह! नाथ! श्री रघुनाथजी के समान कृपा का समुद्र दूसरा कोई नहीं है, जिन भगवान् ने तुमको वह गति दी, जो योगि समाज को भी दुर्लभ है ॥
english_translation: Ah, Lord! There is no other ocean of grace like Raghunath. The Lord has given you a state that is hard even for yogis to attain.
essence: Grace can give what even disciplined striving cannot reach.
simple_meaning: Raghunath alone gives a mercy and spiritual state that even great yogis find hard to reach.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-powered attainment to humble receptivity to grace.
modern_relevance: You can meditate, read, and discipline yourself for years, yet still feel stuck at the edge of change. This verse reminds you that some openings arrive through grace, not force.
speaker: Mandodari

verse_text: मंदोदरी बचन सुनि काना। सुर मुनि सिद्ध सबन्हि सुख माना॥ अज महेस नारद सनकादी। जे मुनिबर परमारथबादी ॥
translation: मंदोदरी के वचन कानों में सुनकर देवता, मुनि और सिद्ध सभी ने सुख माना। ब्रह्मा, महादेव, नारद और सनकादि तथा और भी जो परमार्थवादी (परमात्मा के तत्त्व को जानने और कहने वाले) श्रेष्ठ मुनि थे ॥
english_translation: Hearing Mandodari's words, all the gods, sages, and perfected beings felt joy. Brahma, Mahesh, Narad, and Sanak and other great sages who speak of the highest reality...
essence: Truth spoken at the right moment can calm even the highest minds.
simple_meaning: Mandodari's words moved everyone present, from gods to great sages, into joy and approval.
insight: It shifts attention from conflict to the healing power of clear, truthful speech.
modern_relevance: A tense family meeting finally softens when someone says the honest thing no one wanted to hear. Relief spreads fast when truth enters the room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरि लोचन रघुपतिहि निहारी। प्रेम मगन सब भए सुखारी॥ रुदन करत देखीं सब नारी। गयउ बिभीषनु मनु दुख भारी ॥
translation: वे सभी श्री रघुनाथजी को नेत्र भरकर निरखकर प्रेममग्न हो गए और अत्यंत सुखी हुए। अपने घर की सब स्त्रियों को रोती हुई देखकर विभीषणजी के मन में बड़ा भारी दुःख हुआ और वे उनके पास गए ॥
english_translation: They all gazed at Raghupati with eyes full of tears and became lost in love, filled with bliss. Seeing all the women weeping, Vibhishana felt a great sorrow in his heart and went to them.
essence: Ram's presence awakens love, while another's sorrow still matters.
simple_meaning: Everyone looks at Ram with tears in their eyes and is filled with love. Vibhishana sees the women crying and feels deep sorrow.
insight: It shows how victory in a broken situation can still carry compassion for those who are left mourning.
modern_relevance: You reach the end of a long, painful conflict and finally see the person who ended it. Relief floods the room, but so does grief for everyone who was hurt along the way.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बंधु दसा बिलोकि दुख कीन्हा। तब प्रभु अनुजहि आयसु दीन्हा॥ लछिमन तेहि बहु बिधि समुझायो। बहुरि बिभीषन प्रभु पहिं आयो ॥
translation: उन्होंने भाई की दशा देखकर दुःख किया। तब प्रभु श्री रामजी ने छोटे भाई को आज्ञा दी (कि जाकर विभीषण को धैर्य बँधाओ)। लक्ष्मणजी ने उन्हें बहुत प्रकार से समझाया। तब विभीषण प्रभु के पास लौट आए ॥
english_translation: Seeing his brother's condition, he felt sorrow. Then Lord Ram gave an order to his younger brother. Lakshman explained many things to him in many ways. Then Vibhishana returned to the Lord's side.
essence: Compassion can guide someone back when grief has pulled them away.
simple_meaning: Ram sees Vibhishana's distress, sends Lakshman to comfort him, and Vibhishana returns to Ram.
insight: It shifts you from reacting to another person's pain toward offering calm, patient support.
modern_relevance: You watch a friend go quiet after bad news, then sit beside them instead of fixing them. That steady presence can do more than advice.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कृपादृष्टि प्रभु ताहि बिलोका। करहु क्रिया परिहरि सब सोका॥ कीन्हि क्रिया प्रभु आयसु मानी। बिधिवत देस काल जियँ जानी ॥
translation: प्रभु ने उनको कृपापूर्ण दृष्टि से देखा (और कहा-) सब शोक त्यागकर रावण की अंत्येष्टि क्रिया करो। प्रभु की आज्ञा मानकर और हृदय में देश और काल का विचार करके विभीषणजी ने विधिपूर्वक सब क्रिया की ॥
english_translation: The Lord looked upon him with a merciful gaze and said, "Do the rites, and leave aside all sorrow." Obeying the Lord's command and keeping time and place in mind, Vibhishana performed the funeral rites properly.
essence: Mercy does not remove duty; it makes duty humane.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Vibhishana to set aside grief and complete Ravana's funeral rites properly. Vibhishana obeys and performs the last rites with care and respect.
insight: It teaches you to act with dignity in the middle of grief, instead of letting emotion erase responsibility.
modern_relevance: You are exhausted after a family fight, but the paperwork, the funeral call, or the final goodbye still needs doing. This verse shows how duty can remain gentle even when the heart is breaking.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मंदोदरी आदि सब देह तिलांजलि ताहि। भवन गईं रघुपति गुन गन बरनत मन माहि ॥
translation: मंदोदरी आदि सब स्त्रियाँ उसे (रावण को) तिलांजलि देकर मन में श्री रघुनाथजी के गुण समूहों का वर्णन करती हुई महल को गईं ॥
english_translation: Mandodari and the other women offered the final water ritual to him, then returned to the palace, their minds filled with praise of Raghupati's countless virtues.
essence: Even grief bows before Ram's goodness.
simple_meaning: Ravana's women perform the last rites and leave, inwardly praising Ram's virtues instead of clinging to the fallen king.
insight: It moves attention from mourning power to recognising virtue.
modern_relevance: At a funeral, someone who once defended a powerful person finally sees the cost of that person's pride. In the quiet walk home, their mind keeps returning to the one who ended the harm.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आइ बिभीषन पुनि सिरु नायो। कृपासिंधु तब अनुज बोलायो॥ तुम्ह कपीस अंगद नल नीला। जामवंत मारुति नयसीला ॥ सब मिलि जाहु बिभीषन साथा। सारेहु तिलक कहेउ रघुनाथा॥ पिता बचन मैं नगर न आवउँ। आपु सरिस कपि अनुज पठावउँ ॥
translation: सब क्रिया-कर्म करने के बाद विभीषण ने आकर पुनः सिर नवाया। तब कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामजी ने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी को बुलाया। श्री रघुनाथजी ने कहा कि तुम, वानरराज सुग्रीव, अंगद, नल, नील जाम्बवान् और मारुति सब नीतिनिपुण लोग मिलकर विभीषण के साथ जाओ और उन्हें राजतिलक कर दो। पिताजी के वचनों के कारण मैं नगर में नहीं आ सकता। पर अपने ही समान वानर और छोटे भाई को भेजता हूँ॥1-2॥
english_translation: After the funeral rites were complete, Vibhishana came and bowed again. Then the ocean of compassion, Ram, called his younger brother. Ram said, 'You, Sugriva, Angada, Nala, Neela, Jambavan, and the wise Hanuman should all go with Vibhishana and perform his coronation. Because of my father's word, I cannot enter the city. I send a monkey and a younger brother like myself.'
essence: Keeping a sacred promise matters more than claiming the victory.
simple_meaning: Ram honors his father's word and sends trusted companions to crown Vibhishana. He stays outside the city, but makes sure the right work is done.
insight: It teaches you to protect your commitments while letting others carry out the practical work.
modern_relevance: You could walk into the room and take credit, but you don't. You text the team, hand over the spotlight, and still make sure the job gets finished right.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तुरत चले कपि सुनि प्रभु बचना। कीन्ही जाइ तिलक की रचना॥ सादर सिंहासन बैठारी। तिलक सारि अस्तुति अनुसारी ॥
translation: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर वानर तुरंत चले और उन्होंने जाकर राजतिलक की सारी व्यवस्था की। आदर के साथ विभीषण को सिंहासन पर बैठाकर राजतिलक किया और स्तुति की ॥
english_translation: At the Lord's word, the monkeys went at once and arranged the coronation. With respect, they seated Vibhishana on the throne and performed the coronation with praise.
essence: Victory becomes complete only when rightful order is restored.
simple_meaning: The monkey allies immediately prepare Vibhishana's coronation, seat him on the throne with respect, and complete the ceremony with praise.
insight: It shifts attention from victory itself to the dignified work of restoring order.
modern_relevance: The meeting ends, and everyone quietly shifts from debate to action: chairs are moved, names are called, the room is reset, and the next leader is welcomed without drama.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जोरि पानि सबहीं सिर नाए। सहित बिभीषन प्रभु पहिं आए॥ तब रघुबीर बोलि कपि लीन्हे। कहि प्रिय बचन सुखी सब कीन्हे ॥
translation: सभी ने हाथ जोड़कर उनको सिर नवाए। तदनन्तर विभीषणजी सहित सब प्रभु के पास आए। तब श्री रघुवीर ने वानरों को बुला लिया और प्रिय वचन कहकर सबको सुखी किया ॥
english_translation: Everyone bowed with folded hands. Then they all came before the Lord along with Vibhishana. Raghubir called the monkeys to him and made everyone happy with kind words.
essence: True victory makes room for tenderness.
simple_meaning: Everyone bows to Ram, and Ram responds by calling the monkeys close and speaking kindly so they feel at ease.
insight: It shifts victory away from display and toward gratitude, making leadership feel humane.
modern_relevance: You finish a hard project and walk into the room expecting praise. Instead, the best leader notices the team, pulls everyone close, and speaks in a way that lets the whole room breathe again.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: किए सुखी कहि बानी सुधा सम बल तुम्हारें रिपु हयो। पायो बिभीषन राज तिहुँ पुर जसु तुम्हारो नित नयो॥ मोहि सहित सुभ कीरति तुम्हारी परम प्रीति जो गाइहैं। संसार सिंधु अपार पार प्रयास बिनु नर पाइहैं॥
translation: भगवान् ने अमृत के समान यह वाणी कहकर सबको सुखी किया कि तुम्हारे ही बल से यह प्रबल शत्रु मारा गया और विभीषण ने राज्य पाया। इसके कारण तुम्हारा यश तीनों लोकों में नित्य नया बना रहेगा। जो लोग मेरे सहित तुम्हारी शुभ कीर्ति को परम प्रेम के साथ गाएँगे, वे बिना ही परिश्रम इस अपार संसार का पार पा जाएँगे।
english_translation: After speaking words sweet as nectar, the Lord made everyone happy: "By your strength, this mighty enemy has been slain, and Vibhishana has gained the throne. Your fame will remain ever fresh in the three worlds. Those who sing your noble glory with deep love, along with me, will cross the boundless ocean of worldly struggle without effort."
essence: Love for Ram turns the impossible crossing into an easy passage.
simple_meaning: Ram praises Hanuman and the others, saying their strength won the battle, Vibhishana received the throne, and anyone who sings their glory with love can cross life's vast troubles without struggle.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-made effort to devotion-powered crossing through hardship.
modern_relevance: After the long night of helping a family through a crisis, someone finally says, 'You carried us.' That recognition changes everything. This verse captures how love, gratitude, and praise can become the bridge through exhaustion.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: प्रभु के बचन श्रवन सुनि नहिं अघाहिं कपि पुंज। बार बार सिर नावहिं गहहिं सकल पद कंज ॥
translation: प्रभु के वचन कानों से सुनकर वानर समूह तृप्त नहीं होते। वे सब बार-बार सिर नवाते हैं और चरणकमलों को पकड़ते हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, the monkey hosts are never satisfied. Again and again they bow their heads and hold his lotus feet.
essence: Ram's words create endless gratitude, not satisfaction.
simple_meaning: The monkey army is so moved by Ram's words that they cannot get enough. They keep bowing again and again, holding his feet in devotion.
insight: It shifts attention from achievement to reverent response, showing that love naturally becomes repeated gratitude and surrender.
modern_relevance: You leave a meeting where someone finally spoke with rare kindness, and you keep replaying their words all evening. Something in you wants to bow back to that kind of presence.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि प्रभु बोलि लियउ हनुमाना। लंका जाहु कहेउ भगवाना॥ समाचार जानकिहि सुनावहु। तासु कुसल लै तुम्ह चलि आवहु ॥
translation: फिर प्रभु ने हनुमान् जी को बुला लिया। भगवान् ने कहा- तुम लंका जाओ। जानकी को सब समाचार सुनाओ और उसका कुशल समाचार लेकर तुम चले आओ ॥
english_translation: Then the Lord called Hanuman again and said, "Go to Lanka. Give Janaki my news, and bring back word of her well-being."
essence: True triumph still remembers the one who waited in pain.
simple_meaning: Ram sends Hanuman to Lanka with news for Sita and asks him to return with word of her well-being.
insight: It shifts attention from victory itself to the care that victory should bring to the one who suffered.
modern_relevance: You finally get the chance to text the person who has been waiting for good news. The message is simple, but it carries relief, hope, and the weight of being remembered.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तब हनुमंत नगर महुँ आए। सुनि निसिचरीं निसाचर धाए॥ बहु प्रकार तिन्ह पूजा कीन्ही। जनकसुता देखाइ पुनि दीन्ही ॥
translation: तब हनुमान् जी नगर में आए। यह सुनकर राक्षस-राक्षसी (उनके सत्कार के लिए) दौड़े। उन्होंने बहुत प्रकार से हनुमान् जी की पूजा की और फिर श्री जानकीजी को दिखला दिया ॥
english_translation: Then Hanuman entered the city. Hearing this, the female and male demons rushed out. They honored him in many ways and then showed him Janaki.
essence: A clear mission can turn even an enemy city into a path forward.
simple_meaning: Hanuman enters the city, and the demons rush to receive him. They honor him and then show him Sita.
insight: It keeps the focus on movement in the search: Hanuman enters, is received, and is brought to Sita.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where nobody knows your name, yet your calm changes the atmosphere. Respect arrives before explanation when your purpose is clean.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दूरिहि ते प्रनाम कपि कीन्हा। रघुपति दूत जानकीं चीन्हा॥ कहहु तात प्रभु कृपानिकेता। कुसल अनुज कपि सेन समेता ॥
translation: हनुमान् जी ने (सीताजी को) दूर से ही प्रणाम किया। जानकीजी ने पहचान लिया कि यह वही श्री रघुनाथजी का दूत है (और पूछा-) हे तात! कहो, कृपा के धाम मेरे प्रभु छोटे भाई और वानरों की सेना सहित कुशल से तो हैं? ॥
english_translation: Hanuman bowed from afar. Sita recognized him as Ram's messenger and asked, “Tell me, dear one: is my compassionate Lord well, along with his younger brother and the monkey army?”
essence: Devotion recognizes the messenger before the message is spoken.
simple_meaning: Sita immediately recognizes Hanuman as Ram's messenger and asks about Ram, Lakshman, and the monkey army.
insight: It trains attention toward relationship before self-protection, and toward the beloved's welfare before your own relief.
modern_relevance: You spot a familiar name in a message from someone you miss, and your first question is not about yourself. You want to know whether the person you love is safe.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सब बिधि कुसल कोसलाधीसा। मातु समर जीत्यो दससीसा॥ अबिचल राजु बिभीषन पायो। सुनि कपि बचन हरष उर छायो ॥
translation: (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे माता! कोसलपति श्री रामजी सब प्रकार से सकुशल हैं। उन्होंने संग्राम में दस सिर वाले रावण को जीत लिया है और विभीषण ने अचल राज्य प्राप्त किया है। हनुमान् जी के वचन सुनकर सीताजी के हृदय में हर्ष छा गया ॥
english_translation: The Lord of Kosala is safe in every way. He has defeated the ten-headed Ravana in battle, and Vibhishana has received firm kingship. Hearing Hanuman's words, joy filled Sita's heart.
essence: True news can restore a heart faster than time can.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita that Ram is safe, Ravana has been defeated, and Vibhishana now rules. Sita hears this and feels deep joy.
insight: It shifts the mind from fear and uncertainty to confirmed relief and renewed hope.
modern_relevance: You wait for one message that could change everything, and then it finally arrives: they are safe, the struggle is over, and relief floods your chest.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: अति हरष मन तन पुलक लोचन सजल कह पुनि पुनि रमा। का देउँ तोहि त्रैलोक महुँ कपि किमपि नहिं बानी समा॥ सुनु मातु मैं पायो अखिल जग राजु आजु न संसयं। रन जीति रिपुदल बंधु जुत पस्यामि राममनामयं॥
translation: श्री जानकीजी के हृदय में अत्यंत हर्ष हुआ। उनका शरीर पुलकित हो गया और नेत्रों में (आनंदाश्रुओं का) जल छा गया। वे बार-बार कहती हैं- हे हनुमान् ! मैं तुझे क्या दूँ? इस वाणी (समाचार) के समान तीनों लोकों में और कुछ भी नहीं है! (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे माता! सुनिए, मैंने आज निःसंदेह सारे जगत् का राज्य पा लिया, जो मैं रण में शत्रु को जीतकर भाई सहित निर्विकार श्री रामजी को देख रहा हूँ।
english_translation: Sita was filled with great joy. Her body thrilled and tears filled her eyes. She said again and again, “What can I give you, Hanuman? In all the three worlds, nothing equals this news.” Hanuman replied, “Mother, hear me: today I have truly won the kingdom of the whole world, for I have seen Ram, free from sorrow, after defeating the enemy host and with his brother beside him.”
essence: Seeing Ram safe is greater than owning the world.
simple_meaning: Sita overflows with joy at Hanuman's news, and Hanuman says he has won everything because he has seen Ram safe and victorious.
insight: It shifts value from personal gain to the well-being of the beloved.
modern_relevance: You get the message that someone you love made it home safely after a terrifying night. Suddenly, every other worry shrinks. That is the scale of this moment.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: सुनु सुत सदगुन सकल तव हृदयँ बसहुँ हनुमंत। सानुकूल कोसलपति रहहुँ समेत अनंत ॥
translation: (जानकीजी ने कहा-) हे पुत्र! सुन, समस्त सद्गुण तेरे हृदय में बसें और हे हनुमान् ! शेष (लक्ष्मणजी) सहित कोसलपति प्रभु सदा तुझ पर प्रसन्न रहें ॥
english_translation: “Listen, son. May all virtues dwell in your heart, Hanuman, and may the Lord of Kosala, along with Lakshman, always remain pleased with you.”
essence: Virtue in the heart invites Ram's favor.
simple_meaning: Sita blesses Hanuman that all good qualities may live in his heart, and that Ram and Lakshman may always remain kindly disposed toward him.
insight: It links inner virtue with outer grace, showing that devotion ripens into blessing.
modern_relevance: You help someone through a crisis, then they quietly tell you, 'May goodness stay with you.' That kind of blessing lands deeper than praise because it names character, not performance.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: अब सोइ जतन करहु तुम्ह ताता। देखौं नयन स्याम मृदु गाता॥ तब हनुमान राम पहिं जाई। जनकसुता कै कुसल सुनाई ॥
translation: हे तात! अब तुम वही उपाय करो, जिससे मैं इन नेत्रों से प्रभु के कोमल श्याम शरीर के दर्शन करूँ। तब श्री रामचंद्रजी के पास जाकर हनुमान् जी ने जानकीजी का कुशल समाचार सुनाया ॥
english_translation: O dear one, now do whatever will let me see the dark, gentle form of the Lord with these eyes. Then Hanuman went to Ram and gave news of Janaka's daughter’s well-being.
essence: Devotion becomes simple when all you want is Ram’s presence.
simple_meaning: Sita asks for the means to see Ram again, and Hanuman immediately goes to Ram with her message.
insight: It shifts longing from vague sadness into a clear, devoted request for reunion.
modern_relevance: You stare at your phone after months apart, hoping for one message that says the distance is ending. Sita’s heart knows that feeling exactly.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सुनि संदेसु भानुकुलभूषन। बोलि लिए जुबराज बिभीषन॥ मारुतसुत के संग सिधावहु। सादर जनकसुतहि लै आवहु ॥
translation: सूर्य कुलभूषण श्री रामजी ने संदेश सुनकर युवराज अंगद और विभीषण को बुला लिया (और कहा-) पवनपुत्र हनुमान् के साथ जाओ और जानकी को आदर के साथ ले आओ ॥
english_translation: Hearing the message, Ram, the jewel of the solar dynasty, called Angad and Vibhishan. He said, "Go with Hanuman and bring Janaki back with respect."
essence: Love does not rush recovery; it returns the beloved with honor.
simple_meaning: After hearing Hanuman’s report, Ram immediately sends trusted allies to bring Sita back respectfully.
insight: It shifts rescue from mere success to honorable care.
modern_relevance: You finally hear that the missing person is safe, and the first thing you think is not speed but dignity. Relief is not enough; how you bring them home matters too.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तुरतहिं सकल गए जहँ सीता। सेवहिं सब निसिचरीं बिनीता॥ बेगि बिभीषन तिन्हहि सिखायो। तिन्ह बहु बिधि मज्जन करवायो ॥
translation: वे सब तुरंत ही वहाँ गए, जहाँ सीताजी थीं। सब की सब राक्षसियाँ नम्रतापूर्वक उनकी सेवा कर रही थीं। विभीषणजी ने शीघ्र ही उन लोगों को समझा दिया। उन्होंने बहुत प्रकार से सीताजी को स्नान कराया, ॥
english_translation: They all quickly went to where Sita was. All the female demons served her with humility. Vibhishana promptly instructed them, and they bathed Sita in many ways.
essence: True respect shows itself in immediate, humble care.
simple_meaning: Everyone rushes to Sita, and the women there serve her respectfully. Vibhishana quickly arranges for her bath.
insight: It shifts attention from grand emotion to the dignity of careful service.
modern_relevance: A hospital room after bad news can change in an instant: someone finally brings water, a clean towel, a calmer voice. Respect is sometimes shown through small, urgent acts of care.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहु प्रकार भूषन पहिराए। सिबिका रुचिर साजि पुनि ल्याए॥ ता पर हरषि चढ़ी बैदेही। सुमिरि राम सुखधाम सनेही ॥
translation: बहुत प्रकार के गहने पहनाए और फिर वे एक सुंदर पालकी सजाकर ले आए। सीताजी प्रसन्न होकर सुख के धाम प्रियतम श्री रामजी का स्मरण करके उस पर हर्ष के साथ चढ़ीं ॥
english_translation: They dressed Sita in many kinds of ornaments, then brought a beautiful palanquin. Delighted, she remembered Ram, the abode of joy and her beloved, and climbed into it with joy.
essence: Remembrance of Ram turns departure into joy.
simple_meaning: Sita is honored, placed in a beautiful palanquin, and leaves joyfully while remembering Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from the outward journey to the inward remembrance that makes the journey bearable.
modern_relevance: You finally leave the place that held you too long, and someone has already arranged the ride home. You step in quietly, carrying one name in your heart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बेतपानि रच्छक चहु पासा। चले सकल मन परम हुलासा॥ देखन भालु कीस सब आए। रच्छक कोपि निवारन धाए ॥
translation: चारों ओर हाथों में छड़ी लिए रक्षक चले। सबके मनों में परम उल्लास (उमंग) है। रीछ-वानर सब दर्शन करने के लिए आए, तब रक्षक क्रोध करके उनको रोकने दौड़े ॥
english_translation: Four guards with staves walked on all sides, their hearts full of joy. All the bears and monkeys came to look, and the guards angrily rushed to stop them.
essence: Joyful arrival still needs watchful protection.
simple_meaning: Guards surrounded the procession with sticks in hand, while bears and monkeys gathered to look. The guards ran forward to stop them.
insight: It shows a transition moment where protection, ceremony, and public curiosity all meet.
modern_relevance: You step into a crowded venue with security at every entrance, while curious people crane their necks to catch a glimpse. Joy and control are moving side by side.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह रघुबीर कहा मम मानहु। सीतहि सखा पयादें आनहु॥ देखहुँ कपि जननी की नाईं। बिहसि कहा रघुनाथ गोसाईं ॥
translation: श्री रघुवीर ने कहा- हे मित्र! मेरा कहना मानो और सीता को पैदल ले आओ, जिससे वानर उसको माता की तरह देखें। गोसाईं श्री रामजी ने हँसकर ऐसा कहा ॥
english_translation: Raghubir said, “Do as I say: bring Sita on foot, so the monkeys may see her like a mother.” Laughing, Lord Raghunath said this.
essence: Respect turns a reunion into reverence.
simple_meaning: Ram asks that Sita be brought on foot so the monkeys can see her as a mother. He says it with a smile.
insight: It shifts success from performance to care, showing that how you present someone can be an act of honour.
modern_relevance: You could arrive with all the fanfare, but you choose the kinder entrance. The room feels safer when dignity matters more than spectacle.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनि प्रभु बचन भालु कपि हरषे। नभ ते सुरन्ह सुमन बहु बरषे॥ सीता प्रथम अनल महुँ राखी। प्रगट कीन्हि चह अंतर साखी ॥
translation: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर रीछ-वानर हर्षित हो गए। आकाश से देवताओं ने बहुत से फूल बरसाए। सीताजी (के असली स्वरूप) को पहिले अग्नि में रखा था। अब भीतर के साक्षी भगवान् उनको प्रकट करना चाहते हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, the bears and monkeys rejoiced, and the beings of heaven showered many flowers. Sita had first been placed in fire; now the inner witness wished to reveal her.
essence: What is pure does not need to stay hidden.
simple_meaning: Ram's words fill everyone with joy, flowers fall from the sky, and Sita's hidden purity is revealed.
insight: It shifts attention from private proof to public recognition of what is already true.
modern_relevance: You finally tell the truth in a room that has been tense for days. The air changes at once — relief arrives, and what was quietly known can now be seen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहि कारन करुनानिधि कहे कछुक दुर्बाद। सुनत जातुधानीं सब लागीं करै बिषाद ॥
translation: इसी कारण करुणा के भंडार श्री रामजी ने लीला से कुछ कड़े वचन कहे, जिन्हे सुनकर सब राक्षसियाँ विषाद करने लगीं ॥
english_translation: For that reason, the ocean of compassion spoke a few harsh words in play. Hearing them, all the demon women fell into grief.
essence: Compassion can speak sharply when mercy needs force.
simple_meaning: Ram speaks sternly only to move the scene forward. His words are meant as a dramatic turn, and the women around him fall into sorrow when they hear them.
insight: It shows that sharp speech can be a compassionate tool when the situation calls for it.
modern_relevance: A parent uses a firm tone to stop a child from running into traffic. The voice sounds harsh, but the care underneath is what matters.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु के बचन सीस धरि सीता। बोली मन क्रम बचन पुनीता॥ लछिमन होहु धरम के नेगी। पावक प्रगट करहु तुम्ह बेगी ॥
translation: प्रभु के वचनों को सिर चढ़ाकर मन, वचन और कर्म से पवित्र श्री सीताजी बोलीं- हे लक्ष्मण! तुम मेरे धर्म के नेगी (धर्माचरण में सहायक) बनो और तुरंत आग तैयार करो ॥
english_translation: Holding the Lord's words to her head, Sita spoke, pure in mind, action, and speech: "Lakshman, help me with my dharma and quickly prepare the fire."
essence: True purity can ask for the hardest proof without losing composure.
simple_meaning: Sita accepts Ram's words completely and asks Lakshman to help her prepare the fire right away.
insight: It shows how devotion can stay calm, precise, and obedient even in an unbearable moment.
modern_relevance: You are in a room where everyone is waiting for your answer, and your voice still comes out steady. Even under pressure, you can choose dignity over panic.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: सुनि लछिमन सीता कै बानी। बिरह बिबेक धरम निति सानी॥ लोचन सजल जोरि कर दोऊ। प्रभु सन कछु कहि सकत न ओऊ ॥
translation: श्री सीताजी की विरह, विवेक, धर्म और नीति से सनी हुई वाणी सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी के नेत्रों में (विषाद के आँसुओं का) जल भर आया। वे हाथ जोड़े खड़े रहे। वे भी प्रभु से कुछ कह नहीं सकते ॥
english_translation: Hearing Sita's words, full of separation, discernment, duty, and right conduct, Lakshman’s eyes filled with tears. He stood with both hands folded and could not say anything to the Lord.
essence: True devotion can leave you wordless before duty.
simple_meaning: Lakshman is overwhelmed by Sita’s sorrowful, wise words. Tears fill his eyes, and he stands silently before Ram, unable to speak.
insight: It shows how deep feeling can silence speech and turn attention back to service.
modern_relevance: You hear someone speak with such honesty that your throat tightens. You want to answer, but all you can do is stand there, humbled and quiet.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखि राम रुख लछिमन धाए। पावक प्रगटि काठ बहु लाए॥ पावक प्रबल देखि बैदेही। हृदयँ हरष नहिं भय कछु तेही ॥
translation: फिर श्री रामजी का रुख देखकर लक्ष्मणजी दौड़े और आग तैयार करके बहुत सी लकड़ी ले आए। अग्नि को खूब बढ़ी हुई देखकर जानकीजी के हृदय में हर्ष हुआ। उन्हें भय कुछ भी नहीं हुआ ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ram's look, Lakshman hurried off and brought plenty of wood to kindle the fire. Seeing the fire blaze strongly, Sita's heart filled with joy, and she felt no fear at all.
essence: Fear falls away when trust is fully present.
simple_meaning: Lakshman quickly brings wood for the fire, and Sita feels joy and no fear when she sees it burning strongly.
insight: It shows how decisive support and inner trust can remove fear from a terrifying moment.
modern_relevance: You watch the ambulance lights flash outside the hospital entrance, and your hands stop shaking. In a moment of crisis, someone’s calm action can give your heart back its courage.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जौं मन बच क्रम मम उर माहीं। तजि रघुबीर आन गति नाहीं॥ तौ कृसानु सब कै गति जाना। मो कहुँ होउ श्रीखंड समाना ॥
translation: (सीताजी ने लीला से कहा-) यदि मन, वचन और कर्म से मेरे हृदय में श्री रघुवीर को छोड़कर दूसरी गति (अन्य किसी का आश्रय) नहीं है, तो अग्निदेव जो सबके मन की गति जानते हैं, (मेरे भी मन की गति जानकर) मेरे लिए चंदन के समान शीतल हो जाएँ ॥
english_translation: If, in mind, speech, and action, I have no refuge other than Raghubir in my heart, then may fire, which knows the movements of all minds, become cool to me like sandalwood.
essence: Complete devotion can make even fire feel cool.
simple_meaning: Sita says that if her heart belongs only to Ram in thought, speech, and action, then even fire should become cool and harmless to her.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to complete reliance on Ram.
modern_relevance: You are sitting in a waiting room before hard news, and your chest feels tight. This verse reminds you that when your trust is whole, even fear loses some of its heat.
speaker: Sita

verse_text: श्रीखंड सम पावक प्रबेस कियो सुमिरि प्रभु मैथिली। जय कोसलेस महेस बंदित चरन रति अति निर्मली॥ प्रतिबिंब अरु लौकिक कलंक प्रचंड पावक महुँ जरे। प्रभु चरित काहुँ न लखे नभ सुर सिद्ध मुनि देखहिं खरे ॥
translation: प्रभु श्री रामजी का स्मरण करके और जिनके चरण महादेवजी के द्वारा वंदित हैं तथा जिनमें सीताजी की अत्यंत विशुद्ध प्रीति है, उन कोसलपति की जय बोलकर जानकीजी ने चंदन के समान शीतल हुई अग्नि में प्रवेश किया। प्रतिबिम्ब (सीताजी की छायामूर्ति) और उनका लौकिक कलंक प्रचण्ड अग्नि में जल गए। प्रभु के इन चरित्रों को किसी ने नहीं जाना। देवता, सिद्ध और मुनि सब आकाश में खड़े देखते हैं ॥
english_translation: Remembering Lord Ram, Sita entered the fire that had become cool like sandalwood. She praised the Lord of Kosala, whose feet are worshipped by Shiva and whose pure love is utterly spotless. Her reflection and worldly stain were burned away in the blazing fire. No one understood the Lord's play; gods, perfected beings, and sages stood watching from the sky.
essence: True purity survives fire, while public stain is what burns away.
simple_meaning: Sita enters the fire while remembering Ram. Her shadow and any public stain are burned away, and the divine play remains beyond ordinary understanding.
insight: It shifts attention from outer judgment to the deeper reality that reveals itself through integrity.
modern_relevance: You know the feeling of being misunderstood in front of everyone, while your real truth is invisible. Sometimes the only answer is to stand in what is true and let time burn away the false story.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धरि रूप पावक पानि गहि श्री सत्य श्रुति जग बिदित जो। जिमि छीरसागर इंदिरा रामहि समर्पी आनि सो॥ सो राम बाम बिभाग राजति रुचिर अति सोभा भली। नव नील नीरज निकट मानहुँ कनक पंकज की कली ॥
translation: तब अग्नि ने शरीर धारण करके वेदों में और जगत् में प्रसिद्ध वास्तविक श्री (सीताजी) का हाथ पकड़ उन्हें श्री रामजी को वैसे ही समर्पित किया जैसे क्षीरसागर ने विष्णु भगवान् को लक्ष्मी समर्पित की थीं। वे सीताजी श्री रामचंद्रजी के वाम भाग में विराजित हुईं। उनकी उत्तम शोभा अत्यंत ही सुंदर है। मानो नए खिले हुए नीले कमल के पास सोने के कमल की कली सुशोभित हो ॥
english_translation: Then Fire took a form, held the hand of the true Sita celebrated in the Vedas and the world, and offered her to Ram just as the ocean offered Lakshmi to Vishnu. Sita then shone on Ram's left side with exquisite beauty, like a golden lotus bud beside a fresh blue lotus.
essence: Purity is not only proved; it is welcomed back beside love.
simple_meaning: Fire takes a form and formally returns Sita to Ram. The scene ends with Sita seated beside Ram, glowing like a golden lotus beside a blue one.
insight: It turns vindication into reunion, not just proof.
modern_relevance: After a long public ordeal, you finally hear the words that clear your name. The relief is not just being believed — it is being restored to your place with dignity.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बरषहिं सुमन हरषि सुर बाजहिं गगन निसान। गावहिं किंनर सुरबधू नाचहिं चढ़ीं बिमान ॥
translation: देवता हर्षित होकर फूल बरसाने लगे। आकाश में डंके बजने लगे। किन्नर गाने लगे। विमानों पर चढ़ी अप्सराएँ नाचने लगीं ॥
english_translation: The radiant beings showered flowers in joy. Drums sounded in the sky. Kinnaras sang, and celestial women danced from their flying chariots.
essence: Joy at Ram’s reunion overflows into the whole universe.
simple_meaning: The heavens celebrate with flowers, music, and dancing as the scene turns joyful.
insight: It turns the reunion into a public, cosmic event rather than a private moment.
modern_relevance: You step out of a wedding hall and hear music still ringing behind you, while strangers smile for no reason they can name. Some joy is so full it spills outward.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जनकसुता समेत प्रभु सोभा अमित अपार। देखि भालु कपि हरषे जय रघुपति सुख सार ॥
translation: श्री जानकीजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी की अपरिमित और अपार शोभा देखकर रीछ-वानर हर्षित हो गए और सुख के सार श्री रघुनाथजी की जय बोलने लगे ॥
english_translation: Seeing the immeasurable, boundless splendor of the Lord together with Janak's daughter, the bears and monkeys rejoiced and cried, “Victory to Raghupati, the essence of joy!”
essence: Recognition of the beloved turns relief into celebration.
simple_meaning: Ram and Sita appear in radiant glory, and the bears and monkeys burst into joy and praise him.
insight: It shifts attention from private relief to shared celebration of what has been restored.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a long, painful separation, and the people who love you simply light up. Some moments do not need explanation — only recognition and gratitude.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब रघुपति अनुसासन पाई। मातलि चलेउ चरन सिरु नाई॥ आए देव सदा स्वारथी। बचन कहहिं जनु परमारथी ॥
translation: तब श्री रघुनाथजी की आज्ञा पाकर इंद्र का सारथी मातलि चरणों में सिर नवाकर (रथ लेकर) चला गया। तदनन्तर सदा के स्वार्थी देवता आए। वे ऐसे वचन कह रहे हैं मानो बड़े परमार्थी हों ॥
english_translation: Then, receiving Raghupati's command, Matali bowed his head to the ground and departed. After that, the ever-selfish gods came, speaking as if they were great lovers of duty.
essence: Words can sound selfless while motives stay selfish.
simple_meaning: Matali leaves after bowing to Ram. Then the gods arrive, speaking like selfless seekers even though they are usually self-interested.
insight: It teaches you to look past polished speech and notice whether someone's actions match their claimed virtue.
modern_relevance: A committee meeting ends, and the same people who stayed silent all month suddenly sound noble and principled. You can hear the performance when motives are louder than words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दीन बंधु दयाल रघुराया। देव कीन्हि देवन्ह पर दाया॥ बिस्व द्रोह रत यह खल कामी। निज अघ गयउ कुमारगगामी ॥
translation: हे दीनबन्धु! हे दयालु रघुराज! हे परमदेव! आपने देवताओं पर बड़ी दया की। विश्व के द्रोह में तत्पर यह दुष्ट, कामी और कुमार्ग पर चलने वाला रावण अपने ही पाप से नष्ट हो गया ॥
english_translation: O friend of the lowly, compassionate Raghu king, you showed mercy to the radiant beings. That wicked one, devoted to hostility against the world, lustful, and walking the wrong path, was destroyed by his own sins.
essence: Cruelty collapses from within; compassion protects what is worthy.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as compassionate toward the devas, while Ravana is described as a wicked being destroyed by his own wrongdoing.
insight: It shifts the mind from blaming fate to seeing how harmful choices destroy themselves.
modern_relevance: Someone keeps doubling down on arrogance, blaming everyone else, and acting shocked when everything falls apart. This verse names the pattern: self-made ruin.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तुम्ह समरूप ब्रह्म अबिनासी। सदा एकरस सहज उदासी॥ अकल अगुन अज अनघ अनामय। अजित अमोघसक्ति करुनामय ॥
translation: आप समरूप, ब्रह्म, अविनाशी, नित्य, एकरस, स्वभाव से ही उदासीन (शत्रु-मित्र-भावरहित), अखंड, निर्गुण (मायिक गुणों से रहित), अजन्मे, निष्पाप, निर्विकार, अजेय, अमोघशक्ति (जिनकी शक्ति कभी व्यर्थ नहीं जाती) और दयामय हैं ॥
english_translation: You are the same in every form: the imperishable supreme reality, ever one in taste, naturally detached; whole, without qualities, unborn, flawless, unaging, unconquerable, never-failing in power, and full of compassion.
essence: The highest power is also the most untouched and compassionate.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as changeless, unborn, beyond ordinary qualities, naturally detached, invincible, and full of compassion.
insight: It shifts attention from temporary moods and roles to what remains steady beneath them.
modern_relevance: After a long day of being pulled in every direction, you need something in yourself that cannot be shaken by praise, blame, or pressure.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: मीन कमठ सूकर नरहरी। बामन परसुराम बपु धरी॥ जब जब नाथ सुरन्ह दुखु पायो। नाना तनु धरि तुम्हइँ नसायो ॥
translation: आपने ही मत्स्य, कच्छप, वराह, नृसिंह, वामन और परशुराम के शरीर धारण किए। हे नाथ! जब-जब देवताओं ने दुःख पाया, तब-तब अनेकों शरीर धारण करके आपने ही उनका दुःख नाश किया ॥
english_translation: You took the forms of fish, turtle, boar, man-lion, dwarf, and Parashurama. Whenever the radiant beings suffered, you appeared in many forms and ended their pain.
essence: The divine meets suffering by taking whatever form is needed.
simple_meaning: Ram has appeared again and again in different forms to protect the radiant beings whenever they suffered.
insight: It shifts attention from fixed expectations to the many ways help can arrive.
modern_relevance: You are breaking under pressure, and the help you need arrives in an unexpected form: a blunt friend, a changed plan, a sudden opening. Care does not always look familiar.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: यह खल मलिन सदा सुरद्रोही। काम लोभ मद रत अति कोही। अधम सिरोमनि तव पद पावा। यह हमरें मन बिसमय आवा ॥
translation: यह दुष्ट मलिन हृदय, देवताओं का नित्य शत्रु, काम, लोभ और मद के परायण तथा अत्यंत क्रोधी था। ऐसे अधमों के शिरोमणि ने भी आपका परम पद पा लिया। इस बात का हमारे मन में आश्चर्य हुआ ॥
english_translation: He was vile, filthy, always hostile to the radiant beings, devoted to desire, greed, pride, and fierce anger. Yet even this worst of the low reached your supreme state. That fills our minds with wonder.
essence: Ram's mercy can reach even the most fallen heart.
simple_meaning: A terrible being, full of anger and greed, still reached Ram's feet. That unexpected mercy leaves everyone amazed.
insight: It shifts the mind from moral hopelessness to trust in grace that can still transform the worst case.
modern_relevance: You look at someone who has made a mess of everything and assume the door is shut. Then you remember that mercy can reach farther than judgment ever does.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: हम देवता परम अधिकारी। स्वारथ रत प्रभु भगति बिसारी॥ भव प्रबाहँ संतत हम परे। अब प्रभु पाहि सरन अनुसरे ॥
translation: हम देवता श्रेष्ठ अधिकारी होकर भी स्वार्थपरायण हो आपकी भक्ति को भुलाकर निरंतर भवसागर के प्रवाह (जन्म-मृत्यु के चक्र) में पड़े हैं। अब हे प्रभो! हम आपकी शरण में आ गए हैं, हमारी रक्षा कीजिए ॥
english_translation: We, the radiant beings, though highly privileged, became self-centered and forgot devotion to the Lord. We have long been swept along by the current of repeated birth and death. Now, Lord, we have come seeking your refuge—please protect us.
essence: Pride can trap even the exalted; surrender opens the way home.
simple_meaning: Even the highest beings lost their way through self-interest and were trapped in repeated suffering. Now they turn back and ask the Lord for protection.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance born of ego to humble refuge in what is greater.
modern_relevance: You finally admit you cannot keep carrying everything alone. After months of pride, burnout, and pretending you're fine, you ask for help without dressing it up.
speaker: Brahma

verse_text: दोहा- करि बिनती सुर सिद्ध सब रहे जहँ तहँ कर जोरि। अति सप्रेम तन पु लकि बिधि अस्तुति करत बहोरि ॥
translation: विनती करके देवता और सिद्ध सब जहाँ के तहाँ हाथ जोड़े खड़े रहे। तब अत्यंत प्रेम से पुलकित शरीर होकर ब्रह्माजी स्तुति करने लगे-- ॥
english_translation: After offering their prayers, all the gods and perfected beings stood wherever they were with folded hands. Then, with bodies thrilled by deep love, Brahma began to praise him again.
essence: True greatness makes even the highest bow in love.
simple_meaning: The gods and perfected beings stand with folded hands in prayer, and Brahma begins praising with deep love and awe.
insight: It shifts attention from victory itself to the humility and wonder it awakens in others.
modern_relevance: You finally see someone handle power without arrogance, and your first response is quiet respect. Some moments make admiration feel like the only honest language.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: छंद- जय राम सदा सुख धाम हरे। रघुनायक सायक चाप धरे॥ भव बारन दारन सिंह प्रभो। गुन सागर नागर नाथ बिभो ॥
translation: हे नित्य सुखधाम और (दु:खों को हरने वाले) हरि! हे धनुष-बाण धारण किए हुए रघुनाथजी! आपकी जय हो। हे प्रभो! आप भव (जन्म-मरण) रूपी हाथी को विदीर्ण करने के लिए सिंह के समान हैं। हे नाथ! हे सर्वव्यापक! आप गुणों के समुद्र और परम चतुर हैं ॥
english_translation: Victory to Ram, the ever-abiding home of joy, Hari who holds bow and arrows. Lord of the Raghu line, you are like a lion to the elephant of becoming. O Lord, ocean of virtues, master, all-pervading, supremely wise.
essence: Ram is joy itself and the force that breaks bondage.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the eternal source of joy, the one who destroys the cycle of rebirth, and the master filled with virtues and wisdom.
insight: It shifts attention from Ram as a heroic figure to Ram as the power that ends bondage and steadies devotion.
modern_relevance: You are exhausted after fighting the same fear for the tenth time, and something in you wants a strength bigger than willpower. This praise names that strength and lets your mind rest in it.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: तन काम अनेक अनूप छबी। गुन गावत सिद्ध मुनींद्र कबी॥ जसु पावन रावन नाग महा। खगनाथ जथा करि कोप गहा ॥
translation: आपके शरीर की अनेकों कामदेवों के समान, परंतु अनुपम छवि है। सिद्ध, मुनीश्वर और कवि आपके गुण गाते रहते हैं। आपका यश पवित्र है। आपने रावणरूपी महासर्प को गरुड़ की तरह क्रोध करके पकड़ लिया ॥
english_translation: Your form is unmatched, as lovely as countless gods of desire. Siddhas, sages, and poets keep singing your qualities. Your fame is pure. With a fierce rush, you seized Ravana, the great serpent, just as Garuda seizes a snake.
essence: Ram's beauty and power leave even the wise singing.
simple_meaning: Ram's beauty and fame are beyond compare, and even the greatest sages keep praising him. His power is so great that Ravana is caught like a snake in Garuda's grip.
insight: It joins beauty, praise, and power in one image, showing that true greatness can be both gentle and overwhelming.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone handles a crisis with total calm and absolute force. People do not just notice the result — they feel the presence behind it.
speaker: Brahma

verse_text: जन रंजन भंजन सोक भयं। गत क्रोध सदा प्रभु बोधमयं॥ अवतार उदार अपार गुनं। महि भार बिभंजन ग्यानघनं ॥
translation: हे प्रभो! आप सेवकों को आनंद देने वाले, शोक और भय का नाश करने वाले, सदा क्रोधरहित और नित्य ज्ञान स्वरूप हैं। आपका अवतार श्रेष्ठ, अपार दिव्य गुणों वाला, पृथ्वी का भार उतारने वाला और ज्ञान का समूह है ॥
english_translation: You delight your devotees, destroy sorrow and fear, remain free from anger, and are always full of wisdom. Your incarnation is noble and limitless in virtue, the one who lifts the burden of the world and is pure knowledge itself.
essence: True greatness removes fear and carries burden without anger.
simple_meaning: Ram brings joy to devotees, removes sorrow and fear, never acts in anger, and is full of wisdom. His descent into the world is noble, vast, and meant to lift its burden.
insight: It shifts admiration from outer power to the inner qualities that make power safe.
modern_relevance: You sit beside someone in the hospital waiting room, and their panic starts to soften because you are calm. That quiet steadiness — not force — is what this verse honours.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अज ब्यापकमेकमनादि सदा। करुनाकर राम नमामि मुदा॥ रघुबंस बिभूषन दूषन हा। कृत भूप बिभीषन दीन रहा ॥
translation: (किंतु अवतार लेने पर भी) आप नित्य, अजन्मा, व्यापक, एक (अद्वितीय) और अनादि हैं। हे करुणा की खान श्रीरामजी! मैं आपको बड़े ही हर्ष के साथ नमस्कार करता हूँ। हे रघुकुल के आभूषण! हे दूषण राक्षस को मारने वाले तथा समस्त दोषों को हरने वाले! विभिषण दीन था, उसे आपने (लंका का) राजा बना दिया ॥
english_translation: (Even after taking an incarnation,) you are eternal, unborn, all-pervading, one, and without beginning. O Ram, treasure of compassion, I bow to you with joy. O ornament of the Raghu line, destroyer of the demon Dushan and remover of all faults, Vibhishana was humble, and you made him king of Lanka.
essence: Ram is greatest because his power always serves compassion.
simple_meaning: Ram is beyond birth and beginning, yet full of compassion. He destroys evil, removes faults, and lifts the humble into honor.
insight: It shifts devotion from fear to love by showing power joined with mercy.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems powerful only because they dominate the room. Then they quietly defend the weak and give credit away. That combination of strength and compassion changes how you trust them.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: गुन ध्यान निधान अमान अजं। नित राम नमामि बिभुं बिरजं॥ भुजदंड प्रचंड प्रताप बलं। खल बृंद निकंद महा कुसलं ॥
translation: हे गुण और ज्ञान के भंडार! हे मानरहित! हे अजन्मा, व्यापक और मायिक विकारों से रहित श्रीराम! मैं आपको नित्य नमस्कार करता हूँ। आपके भुजदंडों का प्रताप और बल प्रचंड है। दुष्ट समूह के नाश करने में आप परम निपुण हैं ॥
english_translation: I bow daily to Ram, the treasure of virtues and contemplation, without pride, unborn, all-pervading, and free from blemish. His mighty arms blaze with power, and he is expert at destroying evil forces.
essence: True power stays pure, humble, and undefeated by ego.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as humble, unborn, all-pervading, pure, powerful, and supremely skilled at destroying evil.
insight: It shifts admiration away from raw force and toward force joined with humility and moral clarity.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who can command a room without needing to dominate it. Their strength feels clean, not threatening. That is the kind of power this verse honors.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: बिनु कारन दीन दयाल हितं। छबि धाम नमामि रमा सहितं॥ भव तारन कारन काज परं। मन संभव दारुन दोष हरं ॥
translation: हे बिना ही कारण दीनों पर दया तथा उनका हित करने वाले और शोभा के धाम! मैं श्रीजानकीजी सहित आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ। आप भवसागर से तारने वाले हैं, कारणरूपा प्रकृति और कार्यरूप जगत दोनों से परे हैं और मन से उत्पन्न होने वाले कठिन दोषों को हरने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: I bow to Ram, joined with Sita, who is kind to the humble without cause, the abode of beauty, the savior from becoming, beyond cause and effect, and the remover of the terrible faults born in the mind.
essence: Ram's help arrives without cause and cuts through the mind's worst wounds.
simple_meaning: Ram, with Sita, is praised as the one who helps the humble without any reason, carries beings across the cycle of becoming, and removes deep inner faults.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame to refuge, and from mental distortion to the possibility of being lifted.
modern_relevance: After a day when your thoughts have turned cruel and self-defeating, you remember that mercy is not earned by perfect performance. Some help reaches you before you can clean yourself up.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सर चाप मनोहर त्रोन धरं। जलजारुन लोचन भूपबरं॥ सुख मंदिर सुंदर श्रीरमनं। मद मार मुधा ममता समनं ॥
translation: आप मनोहर बाण, धनुष और तरकस धारण करने वाले हैं। (लाल) कमल के समान रक्तवर्ण आपके नेत्र हैं। आप राजाओं में श्रेष्ठ, सुख के मंदिर, सुंदर, श्री (लक्ष्मीजी) के वल्लभ तथा मद (अहंकार), काम और झूठी ममता के नाश करने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: You hold beautiful arrows, bow, and quiver. Your eyes are red like lotus petals. You are the best among kings, a home of joy, beautiful, beloved of Lakshmi, and the destroyer of pride, desire, and false possessiveness.
essence: Ram's beauty defeats the ego before any weapon is used.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as a beautiful, noble, joy-giving king whose very presence destroys pride, desire, and possessiveness.
insight: It shifts admiration away from surface power and toward the kind of presence that purifies the mind.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm confidence changes the whole room. No one feels smaller — your own posturing simply stops mattering.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: अनवद्य अखंड न गोचर गो। सब रूप सदा सब होइ न गो॥ इति बेद बदंति न दंतकथा। रबि आतप भिन्नमभिन्न जथा ॥
translation: आप अनिन्द्य या दोषरहित हैं, अखंड हैं, इंद्रियों के विषय नहीं हैं। सदा सर्वरूप होते हुए भी आप वह सब कभी हुए ही नहीं, ऐसा वेद कहते हैं। यह (कोई) दंतकथा (कोरी कल्पना) नहीं है। जैसे सूर्य और सूर्य का प्रकाश अलग-अलग हैं और अलग नहीं भी है, वैसे ही आप भी संसार से भिन्न तथा अभिन्न दोनों ही हैं ॥
english_translation: You are flawless, indivisible, and beyond the reach of the senses. Though you are always all forms, you never truly become any of them. The Vedas say this, not mere legend. Like sunlight and the sun, you are both different from the world and not different from it.
essence: Ram is beyond form and still present in every form.
simple_meaning: Ram is beyond the senses, perfect, and whole. He appears as many forms without being trapped by any one form, like sunlight and the sun: distinct, yet inseparable.
insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as one figure among many to recognizing him as present beyond all appearances.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary in the morning, then later realize one choice from them changed the whole room. Some realities are present everywhere without ever being reducible to what you can point at.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कृतकृत्य बिभो सब बानर ए। निरखंति तनानन सादर ए॥ धिग जीवन देव सरीर हरे। तव भक्ति बिना भव भूलि परे ॥
translation: हे व्यापक प्रभो! ये सब वानर कृतार्थ रूप हैं, जो आदरपूर्वक ये आपका मुख देख रहे हैं। (और) हे हरे! हमारे (अमर) जीवन और देव (दिव्य) शरीर को धिक्कार है, जो हम आपकी भक्ति से रहित हुए संसार में (सांसारिक विषयों में) भूले पड़े हैं ॥
english_translation: O all-pervading Lord, these monkeys are fulfilled indeed, for they look upon your face with reverence. And shame on our lives and divine bodies, O Hari, if we remain lost in the world without your devotion.
essence: Without devotion, even a blessed life feels wasted.
simple_meaning: Hanuman says the monkeys are truly fulfilled because they can look at Ram with reverence. Without devotion to Ram, even a divine life and body feel wasted.
insight: It shifts the mind from achievement as success to devotion as fulfillment.
modern_relevance: You finish a huge project, but the room feels hollow because you never cared about what it meant. Then one quiet moment of real love or reverence makes everything feel alive again.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: अब दीनदयाल दया करिऐ। मति मोरि बिभेदकरी हरिऐ॥ जेहि ते बिपरीत क्रिया करिऐ। दुख सो सुख मानि सुखी चरिऐ ॥
translation: हे दीनदयालु! अब दया कीजिए और मेरी उस विभेद उत्पन्न करने वाली बुद्धि को हर लीजिए, जिससे मैं विपरीत कर्म करता हूँ और जो दु:ख है, उसे सुख मानकर आनंद से विचरता हूँ ॥
english_translation: O Lord of the poor, show mercy now and take away this dividing intellect of mine, which makes me do the opposite and call suffering happiness, wandering on in false delight.
essence: Confusion makes suffering look sweet until mercy clears the mind.
simple_meaning: The speaker asks Ram to remove the confused mind that makes him act against his own good and mistake suffering for happiness.
insight: It shifts you from trusting your impulses to asking for clearer seeing before you act.
modern_relevance: You keep returning to the same message thread, the same habit, the same person, even after it hurts. What feels comforting may be the very thing that keeps you confused.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: खल खंडन मंडन रम्य छमा। पद पंकज सेवित संभु उमा॥ नृप नायक दे बरदानमिदं। चरनांबुज प्रेमु सदा सुभदं ॥
translation: आप दुष्टों का खंडन करने वाले और पृथ्वी के रमणीय आभूषण हैं। आपके चरणकमल श्री शिव-पार्वती द्वारा स ेवित हैं। हे राजाओं के महाराज! मुझे यह वरदान दीजिए कि आपके चरणकमलों में सदा मेरा कल्याणदायक (अनन्य) प्रेम हो ॥ दोहा-
english_translation: You destroy evil and remain the beautiful ornament of the world. Shiva and Uma serve your lotus feet. O king of kings, grant me this boon: may I always have blessed love for your lotus feet.
essence: The highest boon is unbroken love for Ram's feet.
simple_meaning: Brahma praises Ram as the beautiful destroyer of evil and asks for one blessing: lasting love for Ram's lotus feet.
insight: It shifts desire from achievement to devotion, from asking for gain to asking for lasting love.
modern_relevance: You finally reach the moment you worked for, and the applause fades fast. What stays is whether your heart has learned where to rest without bargaining for anything else.
speaker: Brahma

verse_text: बिनय कीन्ह चतुरानन प्रेम पुलक अति गात। सोभासिंधु बिलोकत लोचन नहीं अघात ॥
translation: इस प्रकार ब्रह्माजी ने अत्यंत प्रेम-पुलकित शरीर से विनती की। शोभा के समुद्र श्रीरामजी के दर्शन करते-करते उनके नेत्र तृप्त ही नहीं होते थे ॥
english_translation: Brahma bowed with great love, his body thrilled with devotion. Gazing at Ram, the ocean of beauty, his eyes could not drink enough.
essence: Ram's beauty awakens devotion that never reaches enough.
simple_meaning: Brahma offers reverence to Ram and is so moved by Ram's beauty that he cannot stop looking.
insight: It shifts admiration from possession to reverent seeing. The more clearly you look, the less ordinary the beloved becomes.
modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm, kindness, or presence feels deeper every time you look. You don't get tired of them; you feel more devoted, more awake, more grateful.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेहि अवसर दसरथ तहँ आए। तनय बिलोकि नयन जल छाए॥ अनुज सहित प्रभु बंदन कीन्हा। आसिरबाद पिताँ तब दीन्हा ॥
translation: उसी समय दशरथजी वहाँ आए। पुत्र (श्रीरामजी) को देखकर उनके नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल छा गया। छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु ने उनकी वंदना की और तब पिता ने उनको आशीर्वाद दिया ॥
english_translation: At that moment Dasharath arrived there. Seeing his son, tears filled his eyes. The Lord, along with Lakshman, bowed to him, and then the father gave his blessing.
essence: Victory becomes whole only when it is bowed into with love.
simple_meaning: Dasharath arrives, sees Ram and feels overwhelming love, and Ram bows to him with Lakshman before receiving his blessing.
insight: It shifts attention from victory itself to the tenderness and humility that complete it.
modern_relevance: You finally see your child after a long, hard journey, and the first thing you feel is not triumph but tears. Respect still matters, even in joy.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तात सकल तव पुन्य प्रभाऊ। जीत्यों अजय निसाचर राऊ॥ सुनि सुत बचन प्रीति अति बाढ़ी। नयन सलिल रोमावलि ठाढ़ी ॥
translation: (श्रीरामजी ने कहा-) हे तात! यह सब आपके पुण्यों का प्रभाव है, जो मैंने अजेय राक्षसराज को जीत लिया। पुत्र के वचन सुनकर उनकी प्रीति अत्यंत बढ़ गई। नेत्रों में जल छा गया और रोमावली खड़ी हो गई ॥
english_translation: “Father, it is all the power of your merit that I have defeated the unconquerable king of demons.” Hearing his son’s words, his love swelled even more; tears filled his eyes and the hair on his body stood up.
essence: True victory deepens love when it is offered without pride.
