simple_meaning: Ram tells Dasharath that the victory over Ravana came through his merit, not his own pride. Dasharath is overwhelmed with love and emotion at hearing this.
insight: It shifts victory away from ego and turns it into gratitude toward those who made it possible.
modern_relevance: You finally solve the problem everyone thought was impossible, and your first thought is to thank the person who raised you right. That kind of humility changes the whole room.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: रघुपति प्रथम प्रेम अनुमाना। चितइ पितहि दीन्हेउ दृढ़ ग्याना॥ ताते उमा मोच्छ नहिं पायो। दसरथ भेद भगति मन लायो ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी ने पहले के (जीवितकाल के) प्रेम को विचारकर, पिता की ओर देखकर ही उन्हें अपने स्वरूप का दृढ़ ज्ञान करा दिया। हे उमा! दशरथजी ने भेद-भक्ति में अपना मन लगाया था, इसी से उन्होंने (कैवल्य) मोक्ष नहीं पाया ॥
english_translation: Lord of the Raghu clan first remembered the love of earlier times and, looking at his father, gave him firm understanding of his own divine nature. O Uma, Dasharath did not attain liberation, because his mind was absorbed in loving devotion with distinction between lover and beloved.
essence: Even loving devotion can fall short if separateness remains.
simple_meaning: Ram gave his father clear understanding, but Dasharath remained in loving devotion with a sense of separation. Because of that dual feeling, he did not reach liberation.
insight: It shifts devotion from emotional attachment toward a more complete surrender of separateness.
modern_relevance: You can care deeply for someone and still keep them at arm's length in your mind. A relationship changes when love stops being divided into 'me' and 'you'.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सगुनोपासक मोच्छ न लेहीं। तिन्ह कहुँ राम भगति निज देहीं॥ बार बार करि प्रभुहि प्रनामा। दसरथ हरषि गए सुरधामा ॥
translation: (मायारहित सच्चिदानंदमय स्वरूपभूत दिव्यगुणयुक्त) सगुण स्वरूप की उपासना करने वाले भक्त इस प्रकार मोक्ष लेते भी नहीं। उनको श्रीरामजी अपनी भक्ति देते हैं। प्रभु को (इष्टबुद्धि से) बार-बार प्रणाम करके दशरथजी हर्षित होकर देवलोक को चले गए ॥
english_translation: Devotees who worship the divine with form do not seek liberation. Ram gives them his own devotion. Bowing again and again to the Lord, Dasharath went joyfully to the higher realm.
essence: Devotion is richer than liberation, and Ram gives that freely.
simple_meaning: Devotees who love Ram's form are not after liberation as a prize. Ram gives them something even deeper: devotion itself. Dasharath bows again and again, then leaves in joy.
insight: It shifts the goal from escaping experience to deepening devotion.
modern_relevance: You finally get the thing you thought would end your restlessness, but it doesn't. What settles you is not getting out of life — it's being given something to love without bargaining.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: दोहा- अनुज जानकी सहित प्रभु कुसल कोसलाधीस। सोभा देखि हरषि मन अस्तुति कर सुर ईस ॥
translation: छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी और जानकीजी सहित परम कुशल प्रभु श्रीकोसलाधीश की शोभा देखकर देवराज इंद्र मन में हर्षित होकर स्तुति करने लगे- ॥
english_translation: Seeing Lord of Kosala in good health, with Lakshman and Janaki beside him, Indra rejoiced in his mind and began to praise the lord of the gods.
essence: True majesty makes even pride turn into praise.
simple_meaning: Indra sees Ram with Lakshman and Sita, feels joy, and starts praising him.
insight: It shifts attention from victory itself to the reverence victory inspires.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a hard win, and the people who once doubted you fall quiet. Real greatness doesn’t need announcement; it changes the atmosphere.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जय राम सोभा धाम। दायक प्रनत बिश्राम॥ धृत त्रोन बर सर चाप। भुजदंड प्रबल प्रताप ॥
translation: शोभा के धाम, शरणागत को विश्राम देने वाले, श्रेष्ठ तरकस, धनुष और बाण धारण किए हुए, प्रबल प्रतापी भुज दंडों वाले श्रीरामचंद्रजी की जय हो! ॥
english_translation: Victory to Ram, the home of beauty, the giver of rest to those who seek refuge, bearing the finest quiver, bow, and arrows, with mighty and glorious arms.
essence: True greatness protects the one who surrenders.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the source of beauty and the one who gives peace to anyone who takes refuge in him, while also appearing as a mighty warrior ready for battle.
insight: It teaches you to see strength as shelter, not domination.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room carrying a hard decision, and someone steady finally says, “I’ve got you.” The relief is real, but so is the respect. That is the feeling this verse carries.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जय दूषनारि खरारि। मर्दन निसाचर धारि॥ यह दुष्ट मारेउ नाथ। भए देव सकल नाथ ॥
translation: हे खरदूषण के शत्रु और राक्षसों की सेना के मर्दन करने वाले! आपकी जय हो! हे नाथ! आपने इस दुष्ट को मारा, जिससे सब देवता सनाथ (सुरक्षित) हो गए ॥
english_translation: Victory to the enemy of Khara and Dushana, the destroyer of the demon hosts. Victory to the Lord! You killed this wicked one, and all the radiant beings became protected.
essence: True victory is the safety that follows the end of harm.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the one who destroys evil forces and protects everyone who is vulnerable.
insight: It shifts power from aggression to guardianship: strength is measured by the safety it creates.
modern_relevance: You step in when a toxic person is humiliating everyone in the room. The room relaxes the moment the harm stops. That is the kind of protection this verse celebrates.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जय हरन धरनी भार। महिमा उदार अपार॥ जय रावनारि कृपाल। किए जातुधान बिहाल ॥
translation: हे भूमि का भार हरने वाले! हे अपार श्रेष्ठ महिमावाले! आपकी जय हो। हे रावण के शत्रु! हे कृपालु! आपकी जय हो। आपने राक्षसों को बेहाल (तहस-नहस) कर दिया ॥
english_translation: Victory to the remover of the earth's burden, whose glory is vast and limitless. Victory to the enemy of Ravana, the compassionate one, who has left the demon hosts reeling.
essence: True power relieves burden, it does not merely defeat enemies.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the one who lifts the world's burden, destroys evil, and shows compassion while overpowering the forces of chaos.
insight: It shifts attention from raw victory to the deeper relief that comes when destructive pressure is lifted.
modern_relevance: After a long fight, you finally shut the laptop and realise the whole team can breathe because you held the line. Relief and gratitude meet in the same moment.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: लंकेस अति बल गर्ब। किए बस्य सुर गंधर्ब॥ मुनि सिद्ध नर खग नाग। हठि पं सब कें लाग ॥
translation: लंकापति रावण को अपने बल का बहुत घमंड था। उसने देवता और गंधर्व सभी को अपने वश में कर लिया था और वह मुनि, सिद्ध, मनुष्य, पक्षी और नाग आदि सभी के हठपूर्वक (हाथ धोकर) पीछे पड़ गया था ॥
english_translation: Lanka's lord was swollen with pride and had brought gods and celestial beings under his control. He relentlessly harassed sages, perfected beings, humans, birds, and serpents.
essence: Pride makes power violent long before it falls.
simple_meaning: Ravana was arrogant, powerful, and oppressive. He dominated even celestial beings and terrorized every kind of living being.
insight: It frames domination as a warning sign, not a triumph, and prepares the mind to expect consequences.
modern_relevance: A leader who silences criticism, crushes smaller voices, and treats fear as respect may look untouchable for a while. But that kind of power always exposes itself.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परद्रोह रत अति दुष्ट। पायो सो फलु पापिष्ट॥ अब सुनहु दीन दयाल। राजीव नयन बिसाल ॥
translation: वह दूसरों से द्रोह करने में तत्पर और अत्यंत दुष्ट था। उस पापी ने वैसा ही फल पाया। अब हे दीनों पर दया करने वाले! हे कमल के समान विशाल नेत्रों वाले! सुनिए ॥
english_translation: He was eager to harm others and utterly wicked. That sinner has received the fruit of his own deeds. Now listen, O compassionate one to the humble, O wide-eyed one with lotus-like eyes.
essence: Harm ripens into its own consequence, yet mercy is still the final appeal.
simple_meaning: Ravana is condemned as deeply harmful and wicked, and his suffering is presented as the result of his own actions. The verse then turns in prayer to Ram, asking the compassionate, wide-eyed Lord to listen.
insight: It shifts the mind from outrage alone to moral seeing: actions carry their own return, and compassion is still available.
modern_relevance: You watch someone sabotage every relationship, then act shocked when everything collapses. This verse says the damage was never mysterious — and even then, mercy is still worth calling on.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मोहि रहा अति अभिमान। नहिं कोउ मोहि समान॥ अब देखि प्रभु पद कंज। गत मान प्रद दुख पुंज ॥
translation: मुझे अत्यंत अभिमान था कि मेरे समान कोई नहीं है, पर अब प्रभु (आप) के चरण कमलों के दर्शन करने से दु:ख समूह का देने वाला मेरा वह अभिमान जाता रहा ॥
english_translation: I was filled with pride, thinking no one was equal to me. But now, seeing the lotus feet of the Lord, that heap of sorrow called pride has gone.
essence: Seeing what is greater than you ends the ego's spell.
simple_meaning: Ravana admits that his arrogance made him think no one was equal to him, but seeing Ram's feet has destroyed that pride.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to clear seeing, where pride can no longer hide the truth.
modern_relevance: You walk into the room certain you already know the answer, then one honest conversation makes your certainty look small. The humbling is painful, but it frees you.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: कोउ ब्रह्म निर्गुन ध्याव। अब्यक्त जेहि श्रुति गाव॥ मोहि भाव कोसल भूप। श्रीराम सगुन सरूप ॥
translation: कोई उन निर्गुन ब्रह्म का ध्यान करते हैं जिन्हें वेद अव्यक्त (निराकार) कहते हैं। परंतु हे रामजी! मुझे तो आपका यह सगुण कोसलराज-स्वरूप ही प्रिय लगता है ॥
english_translation: Some meditate on the formless Brahman, which the Vedas call unmanifest. But to me, O Ram, your embodied form as the king of Kosala is dear.
essence: The heart chooses the divine it can actually love.
simple_meaning: Ravana admits that some people seek the formless absolute, but he prefers Ram's personal, visible form.
insight: It shifts devotion from abstract idea to living presence.
modern_relevance: You can read a thousand ideas about the ultimate reality, but your heart may still bow to one face, one name, one presence that feels real enough to love.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: बै देहि अनुज समेत। मम हृदयँ करहु निकेत॥ मोहि जानिऐ िनज दास। दे भक्ति रमानिवास ॥
translation: श्रीजानकीजी और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित मेरे हृदय में अपना घर बनाइए। हे रमानिवास! मुझे अपना दास समझिए और अपनी भक्ति दीजिए ॥
english_translation: O Ram, live in my heart together with Janaki and your younger brother. O Raminivasa, know me as your servant and grant me devotion.
essence: Pride ends when the heart asks to become Ram's home.
simple_meaning: Ravana asks Ram to live in his heart with Sita and Lakshman, to accept him as a servant, and to give him devotion.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-assertion to loving surrender and inner belonging.
modern_relevance: After a long argument, you finally stop defending yourself and say, 'I just want this relationship to be whole again.' That is the turn this verse makes.
speaker: Ravana

verse_text: दे भक्ति रमानिवास त्रास हरन सरन सुखदायकं। सुख धाम राम नमामि काम अनेक छबि रघुनायकं॥ सुर बृंद रंजन द्वंद भंजन मनुजतनु अतुलितबलं। ब्रह्मादि संकर सेब्य राम नमामि करुना कोमलं॥
translation: हे रमानिवास! हे शरणागत के भय को हरने वाले और उसे सब प्रकार का सुख देने वाले! मुझे अपनी भक्ति दीजिए। हे सुख के धाम! हे अनेकों कामदेवों की छबिवाले रघुकुल के स्वामी श्रीरामचंद्रजी! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ। हे देवसमूह को आनंद देने वाले, (जन्म-मृत्यु, हर्ष-विषाद, सुख-दु:ख आदि) द्वंद्वों के नाश करने वाले, मनुष्य शरीरधारी, अतुलनीय बलवाले, ब्रह्मा और शिव आदि से सेवनीय, करुणा से कोमल श्रीरामजी! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ।
english_translation: O Ram, dwelling in hearts, remover of fear, giver of refuge and joy, grant me devotion. O abode of bliss, Lord of Raghu, beautiful beyond countless forms, I bow to you. You delight the hosts of radiant beings, break all dualities, wear a human body, possess immeasurable strength, are served by Brahma and Shiva, and are tender with compassion. I bow to you.
essence: Devotion becomes refuge when fear has nowhere left to stand.
simple_meaning: Ram is the one who removes fear, gives refuge, and brings joy. He is praised as beautiful, powerful, compassionate, and worthy of worship by even the highest beings.
insight: It shifts devotion from ritual praise to total inner refuge in Ram.
modern_relevance: You are sitting in a hospital corridor, trying not to panic while waiting for news. This verse speaks to the part of you that wants more than reassurance — it wants refuge, steadiness, and a presence strong enough to hold fear.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: दोहा - अब करि कृपा बिलोकि मोहि आयसु देहु कृपाल। काह करौं सुनि प्रिय बचन बोले दीनदयाल ॥
translation: हे कृपालु! अब मेरी ओर कृपा करके (कृपा दृष्टि से) देखकर आज्ञा दीजिए कि मैं क्या (सेवा) करूँ! इंद्र के ये प्रिय वचन सुनकर दीनदयालु श्रीरामजी बोले ॥ चौपाई
english_translation: “O merciful one, now look upon me with grace and tell me what service I should do.” Hearing these dear words, the compassionate Lord replied.
essence: Real devotion asks, then obeys.
simple_meaning: Hanuman asks Ram for permission to serve and to be told what to do next. Ram, moved by those loving words, answers with compassion.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to responsive service.
modern_relevance: You finish a hard task and resist the urge to announce yourself. Instead, you ask, “What would help most now?” That is Hanuman’s kind of strength.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: सुन सुरपति कपि भालु हमारे। परे भूमि निसिचरन्हि जे मारे॥ मम हित लागि तजे इन्ह प्राना। सकल जिआउ सुरेस सुजाना ॥
translation: हे देवराज! सुनो, हमारे वानर-भालू, जिन्हें निशाचरों ने मार डाला है, पृथ्वी पर पड़े हैं। इन्होंने मेरे हित के लिए अपने प्राण त्याग दिए। हे सुजान देवराज! इन सबको जिला दो ॥
english_translation: O lord of the gods, listen: our monkeys and bears lie on the ground, slain by the demons. They gave up their lives for my sake. O wise lord of the gods, bring all of them back to life.
essence: Ram’s victory includes the lives of those who fought for him.
simple_meaning: Ram asks Indra to revive the monkeys and bears who died fighting for him.
insight: It shifts victory from conquest to responsibility for those who made it possible.
modern_relevance: You watch teammates collapse after carrying your project across the finish line. Before celebrating, you notice who paid the hidden cost and want them whole again.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनु खगेस प्रभु कै यह बानी। अति अगाध जानहिं मुनि ग्यानी॥ प्रभु सक त्रिभुअन मारि जिआई। केवल सक्रहि दीन्हि बड़ाई ॥
translation: (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं -) हे गरुड़! सुनिए प्रभु के ये वचन अत्यंत गहन (गूढ़) हैं। ज्ञानी मुनि ही इन्हें जान सकते हैं। प्रभु श्रीरामजी त्रिलोकी को मारकर जिला सकते हैं। यहाँ तो उन्होंने केवल इंद्र को बड़ाई दी है ॥
english_translation: Listen, king of birds: this statement of the Lord is very profound. Only sages who truly know can understand it. Lord Ram can destroy and restore the three worlds, yet here he has only granted Indra honor.
essence: True power often appears as restraint, not display.
simple_meaning: Ram's words are very deep, and only wise sages can understand them. He can destroy and restore the three worlds, yet here he simply gave Indra honor.
insight: It trains you to look past obvious force and recognise quiet greatness.
modern_relevance: You read a calm reply in a tense group chat and think it means nothing. Later you realise it was the most powerful response in the room.
speaker: Kak Bhushundi

verse_text: सुधा बरषि कपि भालु जियाए। हरषि उठे सब प्रभु पहिं आए॥ सुधाबृष्टि भै दुहु दल ऊपर। जिए भालु कपि नहिं रजनीचर ॥
translation: इंद्र ने अमृत बरसाकर वानर-भालुओं को जिला दिया। सब हर्षित होकर उठे और प्रभु के पास आए। अमृत की वर्षा दोनों ही दलों पर हुई। पर रीछ-वानर ही जीवित हुए, राक्षस नहीं ॥
english_translation: Indra showered nectar and brought the monkeys and bears back to life. Everyone rose in joy and came before the Lord. The nectar fell on both armies, but only the bears and monkeys lived; the demons did not.
essence: The same grace revives the receptive and passes over the closed.
simple_meaning: Indra rains nectar to revive the monkey and bear warriors. The same nectar falls on both sides, but only the righteous fighters return to life.
insight: It shifts attention from the outer event to the inner state that receives it.
modern_relevance: After a brutal argument, two people hear the same apology. One softens and returns; the other stays closed. The same words do not land the same way in every heart.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रामाकार भए तिन्ह के मन। मुक्त भए छूट भव बंधन॥ सुर अंसिक सब कपि अरु रीछा। जिए सकल रघुपति कीं ईछा ॥
translation: क्योंकि राक्षस के मन तो मरते समय रामाकार हो गए थे। अत: वे मुक्त हो गए, उनके भवबंधन छूट गए। किंतु वानर और भालू तो सब देवांश (भगवान् की लीला के परिकर) थे। इसलिए वे सब श्रीरघुनाथजी की इच्छा से जीवित हो गए ॥
english_translation: Their minds took on Ram's form, and they were freed from the bonds of becoming. The monkeys and bears were all sparks of the divine, and all lived by Raghupati's will.
essence: Ram-filled awareness ends bondage, even at the edge of death.
simple_meaning: A mind filled with Ram is freed from worldly bondage. The monkeys and bears survived because they were divine sparks living by Ram's will.
insight: It shifts attention from survival in the struggle to freedom through remembrance.
modern_relevance: At the end of a brutal argument, something in you finally softens and the whole fight loses its grip. The mind that turns toward Ram stops living like a prisoner.
speaker: Kak Bhushundi

verse_text: राम सरिस को दीन हितकारी। कीन्हे मुकुत निसाचर झारी॥ खल मल धाम काम रत रावन। गति पाई जो मुनिबर पाव न ॥
translation: श्रीरामचंद्रजी के समान दीनों का हित करने वाला कौन है? जिन्होंने सारे राक्षसों को मुक्त कर दिया! दुष्ट, पापों के घर और कामी रावण ने भी वह गति पाई जिसे श्रेष्ठ मुनि भी नहीं पाते ॥ दोहा -
english_translation: Who is as kind to the lowly as Ram? He freed even the demons. Ravana, a house of vice and desire, attained a state that great sages do not reach.
essence: Ram's grace reaches even those who seem beyond redemption.
simple_meaning: Ram alone brings real benefit to the fallen. Even Ravana, despite his corruption and desire, reached a state beyond what great sages attain.
insight: It shifts you from judging people as finished to seeing transformation as still possible.
modern_relevance: You look at someone who has wrecked every chance given to them, and still a part of you wonders whether change is possible. This verse says the deepest kindness can reach even there.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: सुमन बरषि सब सुर चले चढ़ि चढ़ि रुचिर बिमान। देखि सुअवसर प्रभु पहिं आयउ संभु सुजान ॥
translation: फूलों की वर्षा करके सब देवता सुंदर विमानों पर चढ़-चढ़कर चले। तब सुअवसर जानकार सुजान शिवजी प्रभु श्रीरामचंद्रजी के पास आए- ॥
english_translation: The gods showered flowers and departed in beautiful flying chariots. Seeing the right moment, wise Shiva came to Lord Ram.
essence: The celebration ends, and the real meeting begins.
simple_meaning: The gods leave after showering flowers, and Shiva approaches Ram at the right moment.
insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to the precise moment a deeper conversation can begin.
modern_relevance: The crowd has moved on, the applause is fading, and one person still waits for the right moment to speak. That quiet timing changes everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परम प्रीति कर जोरि जुग नलिन नयन भरि बारि। पुलकित तन गदगद गिराँ बिनय करत त्रिपुरारि ॥
translation: और परम प्रेम से दोनों हाथ जोड़कर, कमल के समान नेत्रों में जल भरकर, पुलकित शरीर और गद् गद् वाणी से त्रिपुरारी शिवजी विनती करने लगे - ॥ ॥
english_translation: With deepest love, Shiva joined his hands. Tears filled his lotus eyes, his body thrilled, and his voice choked as Tripurari began to pray.
essence: True devotion makes pride dissolve into tears.
simple_meaning: Shiva stands before Ram overwhelmed with love, tears in his eyes, body trembling, and voice breaking as he begins to pray.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to surrender, where feeling becomes more honest than eloquence.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone who changed your life, and all your rehearsed words disappear. What comes out instead is raw gratitude.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: मामभिरक्षय रघुकुल नायक। धृत बर चाप रुचिर कर सायक॥ मोह महा घन पटल प्रभंजन। संसय बिपिन अनल सुर रंजन ॥
translation: हे रघुकुल के स्वामी! सुंदर हाथों में श्रेष्ठ धनुष और सुंदर बाण धारण किए हुए आप मेरी रक्षा कीजिए। आप महामोहरूपी मेघसमूह के (उड़ाने के) लिए प्रचंड पवन हैं, संशयरूपी वन के (भस्म करने के) लिए अग्नि हैं और देवताओं को आनंद देने वाले हैं ॥
english_translation: O Lord of the Raghu line, protect me. You hold the splendid bow and arrows in your beautiful hands. You are the fierce wind that scatters the great cloud of delusion, the fire that burns the forest of doubt, and the delight of the radiant beings.
essence: Ram is the refuge that destroys confusion at its root.
simple_meaning: Shiva asks Ram to protect him, praising Ram as the one who destroys delusion and doubt.
insight: It shifts you from self-protection through control to refuge through surrender.
modern_relevance: You sit in a hospital corridor, rereading the same message, unable to stop your mind from spinning. What you need is not more noise, but something steady enough to cut through fear.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: अगुन सगुन गुन मंदिर सुंदर। भ्रम तम प्रबल प्रताप दिवाकर॥ काम क्रोध मद गज पंचानन। बसहु निरंतर जन मन कानन ॥
translation: आप निर्गुण, सगुण, दिव्य गुणों के धाम और परम सुंदर हैं। भ्रमरूपी अंधकार के (नाश के) लिए प्रबल प्रतापी सूर्य हैं। काम, क्रोध और मदरूपी हाथियों के (वध के) लिए सिंह के समान आप इस सेवक के मनरूपी वन में निरंतर वास कीजिए ॥
english_translation: You are beyond attributes and with attributes: a beautiful abode of virtues. You are a mighty sun that destroys the deep darkness of confusion. Remain forever in this servant’s forest of mind, like a lion against the elephants of desire, anger, and pride.
essence: Ram is both beyond form and the power that clears the mind.
simple_meaning: Ram is praised as beyond form and with form, full of virtues, and powerful enough to destroy confusion, desire, anger, and pride. The speaker asks Ram to stay in the mind forever.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-managed struggle to devotional inner refuge.
modern_relevance: You sit alone after a harsh argument, replaying every line and feeling your temper rise again. This verse sounds like the prayer to make before the spiral takes over: let something steadier live in the mind.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: बिषय मनोरथ पुंज कुंज बन। प्रबल तुषार उदार पार मन॥ भव बारिधि मंदर परमं दर। बारय तारय संसृति दुस्तर ॥
translation: विषयकामनाओं के समूह रूपी कमलवन के (नाश के) लिए आप प्रबल पाला हैं, आप उदार और मन से परे हैं। भवसागर (को मथने) के लिए आप मंदराचल पर्वत हैं। आप हमारे परम भय को दूर कीजिए और हमें दुस्तर संसार सागर से पार कीजिए ॥
english_translation: For the cluster of desire-plants, you are the fierce hail. You are generous and beyond the mind. For churning the ocean of becoming, you are the Mount Mandara. Remove our greatest fear and carry us across the hard-to-cross world-sea.
essence: Ram is the force that cools craving and carries you across fear.
simple_meaning: Ram is asked to destroy the heat of desire, calm the mind, remove fear, and carry the devotee across the hard-to-cross ocean of worldly life.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliant strain to surrendering trust in Ram's power to steady and carry you.
modern_relevance: You are lying awake after a messy breakup, your mind looping through cravings and fears you cannot outthink. This verse gives you a different move: ask to be carried, not just to be tougher.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: स्याम गात राजीव बिलोचन। दीन बंधु प्रनतारति मोचन॥ अनुज जानकी सहित निरंतर। बसहु राम नृप मम उर अंतर॥ मुनि रंजन महि मंडल मंडन। तुलसिदास प्रभु त्रास बिखंडन॥ 4-5॥
translation: हे श्यामसुंदर-शरीर! हे कमलनयन! हे दीनबंधु! हे शरणागत को दु:ख से छुड़ाने वाले! हे राजा रामचंद्रजी! आप छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण और जानकीजी सहित निरंतर मेरे हृदय के अंदर निवास कीजिए। आप मुनियों को आनंद देने वाले, पृथ्वीमंडल के भूषण, तुलसीदास के प्रभु और भय का नाश करने वाले हैं॥ 4-5॥
english_translation: O dark-hued, lotus-eyed Ram, friend of the humble, remover of the suffering of those who seek refuge. O King Ram, stay forever in my heart, along with Lakshman and Sita. You delight sages, adorn the earth, and destroy fear, O Lord of Tulsidas.
essence: Ram becomes home when you ask him to stay within you.
simple_meaning: The speaker prays to Ram to live in the heart forever, together with Sita and Lakshman, and praises him as the friend of the humble and remover of fear.
insight: It shifts devotion from admiration at a distance to living companionship within the heart.
modern_relevance: After a day of noise, you finally sit alone and realize what you want most is not more control. You want one steady presence in the middle of everything that frightens you.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: दोहा नाथ जबहिं कोसलपुरीं हो इहि तिलक तुम्हार। कृपासिंधु मैं आउब देखन चरित उदार ॥
translation: हे नाथ! जब अयोध्यापुरी में आपका राजतिलक होगा, तब हे कृपासागर! मैं आपकी उदार लीला देखने आऊँगा ॥
english_translation: O Lord, when your coronation takes place in Ayodhya, then, ocean of grace, I will come to witness your noble deeds.
essence: Love waits for the moment goodness is publicly crowned.
simple_meaning: The speaker promises to come back and witness Ram’s coronation in Ayodhya, drawn by love and reverence for Ram’s noble life.
insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle of success to the joy of witnessing a loved one’s rightful fulfillment.
modern_relevance: You keep a date in your heart for the moment someone you trust finally gets what they deserve. You want to be there, not for the event, but for them.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: करि बिनती जब संभु सिधाए। तब प्रभु निकट बिभीषनु आए॥ नाइ चरन सिरु कह मृदु बानी। बिनय सुनहु प्रभु सारँगपानी ॥
translation: जब शिवजी विनती करके चले गए, तब विभीषणजी प्रभु के पास आए और चरणों में सिर नवाकर कोमल वाणी से बोले- हे शार्गं धनुष के धारण करने वाले प्रभो! मेरी विनती सुनिए- ॥
english_translation: After Shiva had made his prayer and departed, Vibhishana came near the Lord. Bowing his head at the Lord's feet, he spoke softly: "Listen to my request, Lord who holds the Saranga bow."
essence: Humility is the door through which surrender enters.
simple_meaning: After Shiva leaves, Vibhishana approaches Ram with bowed head and gentle words, asking Him to listen to his plea.
insight: It teaches you to approach what matters with humility first, not self-importance.
modern_relevance: You finally walk into the room and admit you need help, without rehearsing a polished version of the story. The truth reaches people faster when you stop protecting your image.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: सकुल सदल प्रभु रावन मार् यो। पावन जस त्रिभुवन विस्तार् यो॥ दीन मलीन हीन मति जाती। मो पर कृपा कीन्हि बहु भाँती ॥
translation: आपने कुल और सेना सहित रावण का वध किया, त्रिभुवन में अपना पवित्र यश फैलाया और मुझ दीन, पापी, बुद्धिहीन और जातिहीन पर बहुत प्रकार से कृपा की ॥
english_translation: You destroyed Ravana and his army, spread your pure glory through the three worlds, and showed abundant grace to me, lowly, impure, foolish, and outcast.
essence: Victory becomes holy when it is joined with mercy.
simple_meaning: Ram has destroyed Ravana and his forces, and his glory now fills the three worlds. Vibhishana also says Ram has shown him many kinds of mercy despite his lowly state.
insight: It shifts attention from conquest to grace, showing that true power reveals itself in how it treats the vulnerable.
modern_relevance: You finally win the argument, close the deal, or finish the hard fight — and then someone weaker is still waiting for your kindness. This verse reminds you that victory is incomplete without mercy.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: अब जन गृह पुनीत प्रभु कीजे। मज्जन करिअ समर श्रम छीजे॥ देखि कोस मंदिर संपदा। देहु कृपाल कपिन्ह कहुँ मुदा ॥
translation: अब हे प्रभु! इस दास के घर को पवित्र कीजिए और वहाँ चलकर स्नान कीजिए, जिससे युद्ध की थकावट दूर हो जाए। हे कृपालु! खजाना, महल और सम्पत्ति का निरीक्षण कर प्रसन्नतापूर्वक वानरों को दीजिए ॥
english_translation: Now, Lord, make this home pure. Come bathe there and wash away the weariness of battle. O compassionate one, look at the treasury, palace, and wealth, and gladly give them to the monkeys.
essence: Surrender turns your home and wealth into offerings.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana asks Ram to enter his home, bathe, rest after battle, and then gladly share Lanka's wealth with the monkey army.
insight: It shifts devotion from praise into practical hospitality and shared abundance.
modern_relevance: After a long day helping someone move, you open your apartment, hand them water, and insist they eat before leaving. Care is not a speech; it becomes welcome, rest, and generosity.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: सब बिधि नाथ मोहि अपनाइअ। पुनि मोहि सहित अवधपुर जाइअ॥ सुनत बचन मृदु दीनदयाला। सजल भए द्वौ नयन बिसाला ॥
translation: हे नाथ! मुझे सब प्रकार से अपना लीजिए और फिर हे प्रभो! मुझे साथ लेकर अयोध्यापुरी को पधारिए। विभीषणजी के कोमल वचन सुनते ही दीनदयालु प्रभु के दोनों विशाल नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया ॥
english_translation: “O Lord, take me in every way as your own, and then, O compassionate one, take me with you to the city of Ayodhya.” Hearing these gentle words from Vibhishana, the great-eyed Lord’s eyes filled with tears.
essence: Surrender makes you fully accepted, and that acceptance moves the divine.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana asks Ram to accept him completely and take him to Ayodhya. Ram is so moved by his gentle surrender that tears fill his eyes.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to wholehearted belonging.
modern_relevance: After a long fight with your family, you finally say, “Please just let me come home.” The relief in that sentence is bigger than pride. That is Vibhishana’s courage.
speaker: Vibhishana

verse_text: तोर कोस गृह मोर सब सत्य बचन सुनु भ्रात। भरत दसा सुमिरत मोहि निमिष कल्प सम जात ॥
translation: (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे भाई! सुनो, तुम्हारा खजाना और घर सब मेरा ही है, यह सच बात है। पर भरत की दशा याद करके मुझे एक-एक पल कल्प के समान बीत रहा है ॥
english_translation: “Brother, listen: your treasury and house are all truly mine. But remembering Bharat’s condition, each moment feels like an age to me.”
essence: Love owns nothing, yet another’s pain can make time unbearable.
simple_meaning: Ram says the treasury and house belong to him, but what truly weighs on him is Bharat’s suffering. Thinking of Bharat makes even a moment feel unbearably long.
insight: It shifts attention from possession to relationship, showing that devotion feels another’s suffering as your own.
modern_relevance: You’re in a hotel lobby after a hard family call, smiling at people who think you’re fine. Your body is present, but your mind is still with the person you love who is hurting.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तापस बेष गात कृस जपत निरंतर मोहि। देखौं बेगि सो जतनु करु सखा निहोरउँ तोहि ॥
translation: तपस्वी के वेष में कृश (दुबले) शरीर से निरंतर मेरा नाम जप कर रहे हैं। हे सखा! वही उपाय करो जिससे मैं जल्दी से जल्दी उन्हें देख सकूँ। मैं तुमसे निहोरा (अनुरोध) करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: In a hermit's dress, with a lean body, he keeps chanting my name without pause. O friend, find a way so I may see him soon; I beg you.
essence: Pure devotion makes Ram long to see the devotee first.
simple_meaning: Ram speaks of someone who lives like an ascetic, thin from devotion, constantly chanting Ram's name. He asks for a way to see that devotee soon.
insight: It shifts attention from achievement to devotion: the one who remembers with love becomes precious.
modern_relevance: You hear that someone has kept your name in their prayers through a hard season, and suddenly everything else feels smaller. Being remembered with that kind of devotion changes how closeness feels.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: बीतें अवधि जाउँ जौं जिअत न पावउँ बीर। सुमिरत अनुज प्रीति प्रभु पुनि पुनि पुलक सरीर ॥
translation: यदि अवधि बीत जाने पर जाता हूँ तो भाई को जीता न पाऊँगा। छोटे भाई भरतजी की प्रीति का स्मरण करके प्रभु का शरीर बार-बार पुलकित हो रहा है ॥
english_translation: If I leave after the deadline passes, I will not be able to save my brother. Remembering the love of my younger brother Bharata, the Lord's body again and again thrills with emotion.
essence: True devotion makes even Ram tremble with love.
simple_meaning: Ram says he must reach Bharata before the deadline passes, or he will not find him alive. Remembering Bharata's love makes Ram tremble with emotion.
insight: It shifts attention from duty alone to the emotional force of devotion that gives duty its urgency.
modern_relevance: You see a message from someone who has waited patiently for your reply, and your chest tightens. Their care matters so much that delay suddenly feels unbearable.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: करेहु कल्प भरि राजु तुम्ह मोहि सुमिरेहु मन माहिं। पुनि मम धाम पाइहहु जहाँ संत सब जाहिं ॥
translation: (श्री रामजी ने फिर कहा-) हे विभीषण! तुम कल्पभर राज्य करना, मन में मेरा निरंतर स्मरण करते रहना। फिर तुम मेरे उस धाम को पा जाओगे, जहाँ सब संत जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: Rama said, "Rule for ages while remembering me in your heart. Then you will reach my abode, where all the holy ones go."
essence: You can live fully and still be on the way home.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Vibhishan to keep ruling for a long time while remembering him inwardly. That remembrance leads to Ram's abode, the place reached by the holy.
insight: It shifts devotion from withdrawal to inward continuity while living your duties.
modern_relevance: You are still answering emails, paying bills, and caring for family, yet part of you longs for something higher. This verse says ordinary life does not block remembrance; it can become the place where remembrance matures.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनत बिभीषन बचन राम के। हरषि गहे पद कृपाधाम के॥ बानर भालु सकल हरषाने। गहि प्रभु पद गुन बिमल बखाने ॥
translation: श्री रामचंद्रजी के वचन सुनते ही विभीषणजी ने हर्षित होकर कृपा के धाम श्री रामजी के चरण पकड़ लिए। सभी वानर-भालू हर्षित हो गए और प्रभु के चरण पकड़कर उनके निर्मल गुणों का बखान करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Hearing Ram's words, Vibhishana joyfully grasped the feet of the abode of grace. All the monkeys and bears rejoiced, took hold of the Lord's feet, and praised his pure virtues.
essence: Ram's welcome turns surrender into joy.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana feels immediate joy and surrenders to Ram. The monkey and bear allies also rejoice and praise Ram's pure qualities.
insight: It shifts devotion from a private feeling into an outward act of trust and praise.
modern_relevance: You finally hear the apology you needed, and your chest loosens before you can even explain why. Some moments heal you by making surrender feel safe.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरि विभीषन भवन सिधायो। मनि गन बसन बिमान भरायो॥ लै पुष्पक प्रभु आगें राखा। हँसि करि कृपासिंधु तब भाषा ॥
translation: फिर विभीषणजी महल को गए और उन्होंने मणियों के समूहों (रत्नों) से और वस्त्रों से विमान को भर लिया। फिर उस पुष्पक विमान को लाकर प्रभु के सामने रखा। तब कृपासागर श्री रामजी ने हँसकर कहा- ॥
english_translation: Then Vibhishana went to the palace and filled the Pushpak with jewels and garments. He brought the Pushpak aircraft before the Lord, and then the ocean of mercy smiled and spoke.
essence: Surrender opens the door to grace.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana gathers treasures and clothing, brings the Pushpak aircraft before Ram, and Ram smiles before speaking.
insight: It prepares the next act of generosity, showing that surrender is met with welcome, not suspicion.
modern_relevance: You finally bring what you have to offer after a hard apology, and the room softens before anyone says much. The gesture itself already changed the mood.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चढ़ि बिमान सुनु सखा बिभीषन। गगन जाइ बरषहु पट भूषन॥ नभ पर जाइ बिभीषन तबही। बरषि दिए मनि अंबर सबही ॥
translation: हे सखा विभीषण! सुनो, विमान पर चढ़कर, आकाश में जाकर वस्त्रों और गहनों को बरसा दो। तब (आज्ञा सुनते) ही विभीषणजी ने आकाश में जाकर सब मणियों और वस्त्रों को बरसा दिया ॥
english_translation: “Friend Vibhishana, climb the flying chariot and go into the sky to shower down the clothes and ornaments.” At once, Vibhishana went up into the sky and scattered all the jewels and garments.
essence: Trust makes obedience effortless and immediate.
simple_meaning: Ram tells Vibhishana to go up in the flying chariot and scatter the clothes and jewels in the sky. Vibhishana obeys at once.
insight: It shows how trust and service can be so complete that action follows before thought.
modern_relevance: A leader gives one clear instruction in the middle of chaos, and the trusted helper moves without hesitation. The moment works because there is no delay between instruction and service.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जोइ जोइ मन भावइ सोइ लेहीं। मनि मुख मेलि डारि कपि देहीं॥ हँसे रामु श्री अनुज समेता। परम कौतुकी कृपा निकेता ॥
translation: जिसके मन को जो अच्छा लगता है, वह वही ले लेता है। मणियों को मुँह में लेकर वानर फिर उन्हें खाने की चीज न समझकर उगल देते हैं। यह तमाशा देखकर परम विनोदी और कृपा के धाम श्री रामजी, सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित हँसने लगे ॥
english_translation: Whatever each one likes, he takes. The monkeys put the gems in their mouths and then spit them out, not seeing them as food. Seeing this spectacle, Sri Ram, along with his younger brother, laughed with delight; he is the very home of grace.
essence: Possession means little when joy has already arrived.
simple_meaning: The monkeys grab whatever pleases them, then spit out the gems as if they were useless. Ram, Lakshman, and the others laugh at the scene.
insight: It shifts attention from what is valuable on paper to what actually delights the heart.
modern_relevance: You open a box of expensive gifts after a hard-won celebration, and the children care more about the wrapping paper. The moment reminds you that delight often lives in play, not value.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि जेहि ध्यान न पावहिं नेति नेति कह बेद। कृपासिंधु सोइ कपिन्ह सन करत अनेक बिनोद ॥
translation: जिनको मुनि ध्यान में भी नहीं पाते, जिन्हें वेद नेति-नेति कहते हैं, वे ही कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामजी वानरों के साथ अनेकों प्रकार के विनोद कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The sages cannot reach Him in meditation, and the Vedas describe Him as neither this nor that. Yet that ocean of grace is joking with the monkeys in many playful ways.
essence: The highest reality is closest when it is most loving.
simple_meaning: Ram is beyond the reach of even great sages and beyond ordinary description, yet that same limitless grace is joyfully playing with the monkeys.
insight: It shifts the mind from remote abstraction to intimate devotion: the highest reality can be personally near.
modern_relevance: You can spend years trying to pin down what is ultimate, then find it in a moment of laughter with people who love you. The deepest reality is not distant from warmth and play.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उमा जोग जप दान तप नाना मख ब्रत नेम। राम कृपा नहिं करहिं तसि जसि निष्केवल प्रेम ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! अनेकों प्रकार के योग, जप, दान, तप, यज्ञ, व्रत और नियम करने पर भी श्री रामचंद्रजी वैसी कृपा नहीं करते जैसी अनन्य प्रेम होने पर करते हैं ॥
english_translation: O Uma, even many kinds of yoga, chanting, charity, austerity, sacrifices, vows, and disciplines do not draw Ram's grace the way single-minded love does.
essence: Undivided love draws Ram more than any amount of practice.
simple_meaning: Ram's grace comes more readily through undivided love than through many religious practices, rituals, or disciplines.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to sincerity, showing that love matters more than spiritual display.
modern_relevance: You have checked every box, followed every rule, and still feel far away. Then a simple, honest cry from the heart lands more deeply than all the polished effort.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: भालु कपिन्ह पट भूषन पाए। पहिरि पहिरि रघुपति पहिं आए॥ नाना जिनस देखि सब कीसा। पुनि पुनि हँसत कोसलाधीसा ॥
translation: भालुओं और वानरों ने कपड़े-गहने पाए और उन्हें पहन-पहनकर वे श्री रघुनाथजी के पास आए। अनेकों जातियों के वानरों को देखकर कोसलपति श्री रामजी बार-बार हँस रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: The bears and monkeys received clothes and ornaments, and, wearing them again and again, came before Raghupati. Seeing the many kinds of monkeys, the Lord of Kosala kept laughing again and again.
essence: Victory becomes celebration when Ram looks at everyone with delight.
simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears put on the gifts and came to Ram, who laughed at their many different forms.
insight: It shifts attention from formal victory to shared joy and belonging.
modern_relevance: At a family wedding, everyone is dressed badly, beautifully, and hilariously all at once — and the person you love most is laughing with affection, not mockery.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चितइ सबन्हि पर कीन्ही दाया। बोले मृदुल बचन रघुराया॥ तुम्हरें बल मैं रावनु मार् यो। तिलक बिभीषन कहँ पुनि सार् यो ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी ने कृपा दृष्टि से देखकर सब पर दया की। फिर वे कोमल वचन बोले- हे भाइयो! तुम्हारे ही बल से मैंने रावण को मारा और फिर विभीषण का राजतिलक किया ॥
english_translation: Looking at them all with compassion, the Lord of Raghu spoke gently: "By your strength I killed Ravana, and then I crowned Vibhishana."
essence: Victory becomes beautiful when you give the credit away.
simple_meaning: Ram speaks kindly to the monkeys and gives them credit for his victory. He also honors Vibhishana by crowning him king.
insight: It shifts you from self-congratulation to generous acknowledgment, making leadership feel humble and shared.
modern_relevance: Your team stayed late to finish the project, but the public praise went to someone else. The deeper leader is the one who names everyone who made the win possible.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: निज निज गृह अब तुम्ह सब जाहू। सुमिरेहु मोहि डरपहु जनि काहू॥ सुनत बचन प्रेमाकुल बानर। जोरि पानि बोले सब सादर ॥
translation: अब तुम सब अपने-अपने घर जाओ। मेरा स्मरण करते रहना और किसी से डरना नहीं। ये वचन सुनते ही सब वानर प्रेम में विह्वल होकर हाथ जोड़कर आदरपूर्वक बोले- ॥
english_translation: Now all of you go back to your own homes. Keep remembering me, and do not fear anyone. Hearing these words, all the monkeys were overwhelmed with love and, joining their hands, spoke respectfully.
essence: Remembrance of Ram sends fear packing.
simple_meaning: Ram sends the monkeys home with one instruction: keep remembering him and do not be afraid.
insight: It shifts devotion from emotion to protection: remembrance becomes the source of fearlessness.
modern_relevance: You leave a hard season behind, but the nervous system still expects danger. One steady presence in your mind can make the road home feel safe again.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: प्रभु जोइ कहहु तुम्हहि सब सोहा। हमरें होत बचन सुनि मोहा॥ दीन जानि कपि किए सनाथा। तुम्ह त्रैलोक ईस रघुनाथा ॥
translation: प्रभो! आप जो कुछ भी कहें, आपको सब सोहता है। पर आपके वचन सुनकर हमको मोह होता है। हे रघुनाथजी! आप तीनों लोकों के ईश्वर हैं। हम वानरों को दीन जानकर ही आपने सनाथ (कृतार्थ) किया है ॥
english_translation: Whatever you say suits you perfectly, Lord. But hearing your words, we are overcome with wonder. O Raghunath, you are the lord of the three worlds. Seeing us as lowly, you have made us your own.
essence: True greatness makes room for the lowly and calls them its own.
simple_meaning: The monkeys praise Ram’s greatness and feel overwhelmed that he has accepted them despite their lowly state.
insight: It shifts attention from status to grace: what matters is being received, not ranked.
modern_relevance: You get praised for work you barely feel worthy of, and instead of swelling with pride, you feel seen through. That strange mix of humility and love is what this verse holds.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: सुनि प्रभु बचन लाज हम मरहीं। मसक कहूँ खगपति हित करहीं॥ देखि राम रुख बानर रीछा। प्रेम मगन नहिं गृह कै ईछा ॥
translation: प्रभु के (ऐसे) वचन सुनकर हम लाज के मारे मरे जा रहे हैं। कहीं मच्छर भी गरुड़ का हित कर सकते हैं? श्री रामजी का रुख देखकर रीछ-वानर प्रेम में मग्न हो गए। उनकी घर जाने की इच्छा नहीं है ॥
english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, we feel ashamed to the point of death. Can even a mosquito help Garuda? Seeing Ram's face, the bears and monkeys were lost in love and no longer wanted to go home.
essence: Love for Ram can make leaving feel impossible.
simple_meaning: The vanaras and bears feel humbled before Ram's greatness, and Ram's presence fills them with such love that they no longer want to leave.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-consciousness to loving absorption, where Ram's presence matters more than comfort or status.
modern_relevance: You finish helping someone you love, and they tell you to go home. Instead of relief, you feel a quiet ache to stay a little longer. That is what it means to be moved by real devotion.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु प्रेरित कपि भालु सब राम रूप उर राखि। हरष बिषाद सहित चले बिनय बिबिध बिधि भाषि ॥
translation: परन्तु प्रभु की प्रेरणा (आज्ञा) से सब वानर-भालू श्री रामजी के रूप को हृदय में रखकर और अनेकों प्रकार से विनती करके हर्ष और विषाद सहित घर को चले ॥
english_translation: Moved by the Lord's command, all the monkeys and bears kept Ram's form in their hearts and set out for home, speaking many kinds of prayers with joy and sorrow together.
essence: True devotion lets you leave without ever letting go.
simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears leave, holding Ram in their hearts and offering many prayers, feeling both joy and sadness as they go home.
insight: It shifts attention from the trip itself to the heart you carry back home.
modern_relevance: You finish a life-changing retreat, pack your bag, and feel both grateful and empty. The place is behind you, but the presence you found there still travels with you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कपिपति नील रीछपति अंगद नल हनुमान। सहित बिभीषन अपर जे जूथप कपि बलवान ॥
translation: वानरराज सुग्रीव, नील, ऋक्षराज जाम्बवान् , अंगद, नल और हनुमान् तथा विभीषण सहित और जो बलवान् वानर सेनापति हैं, ॥
english_translation: The monkey kings Sugriva, Nila, Jambavan, Angada, Nala, Hanuman, Vibhishana, and the other powerful leaders of the monkey army.
essence: Many strong allies now stand on Ram's side.
simple_meaning: Sugriva, Nila, Jambavan, Angada, Nala, Hanuman, Vibhishana, and other strong leaders stand together.
insight: It shifts attention from individual power to collective alignment.
modern_relevance: A team meeting ends and the people who once worked separately now stand behind one decision. This is the feeling of many strengths gathering into one purpose.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कहि न सकहिं कछु प्रेम बस भरि भरि लोचन बारि॥ सन्मुख चितवहिं राम तन नयन निमेष निवारि ॥
translation: वे कुछ कह नहीं सकते, प्रेमवश नेत्रों में जल भर-भरकर, नेत्रों का पलक मारना छोड़कर (टकटकी लगाए) सम्मुख होकर श्री रामजी की ओर देख रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: They cannot say anything. Overcome by love, their eyes fill again and again with tears. They keep looking straight at Ram, refusing even to blink.
essence: True devotion can make speech disappear and attention become complete.
simple_meaning: Love has filled them so completely that they cannot speak. Tears keep coming, and they cannot look away from Ram.
insight: It shifts devotion from performance to presence: love is proven by attention, not explanation.
modern_relevance: You finally see someone you have missed for years, and your throat closes. Nothing clever comes out — only tears and a steady look that says everything.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अतिसय प्रीति देखि रघुराई। लीन्हे सकल बिमान चढ़ाई॥ मन महुँ बिप्र चरन सिरु नायो। उत्तर दिसिहि बिमान चलायो ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी ने उनका अतिशय प्रेम देखकर सबको विमान पर चढ़ा लिया। तदनन्तर मन ही मन विप्रचरणों में सिर नवाकर उत्तर दिशा की ओर विमान चलाया ॥
english_translation: Seeing their deep affection, Raghurai took them all aboard the aerial chariot. Then, bowing his head inwardly to the feet of the Brahmin, he set the chariot toward the north.
essence: Victory stays pure when humility leads the way.
simple_meaning: Ram notices their devotion, seats everyone in the divine chariot, bows inwardly to the Brahmin’s feet, and sends the chariot north.
insight: It shows that true success includes gratitude, humility, and care for everyone who helped.
modern_relevance: After a hard win, you finally get the group photo, the applause, the relief. The real test is whether you stay humble when everyone else is celebrating.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: चलत बिमान कोलाहल होई। जय रघुबीर कहइ सबु कोई॥ सिंहासन अति उच्च मनोहर। श्री समेत प्रभु बैठे ता पर ॥
translation: विमान के चलते समय बड़ा शोर हो रहा है। सब कोई श्री रघुवीर की जय कह रहे हैं। विमान में एक अत्यंत ऊँचा मनोहर सिंहासन है। उस पर सीताजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी विराजमान हो गए ॥
english_translation: As the विमान moved, there was a great uproar. Everyone cried, "Victory to Raghubir!" In the lofty, beautiful throne, the Lord sat there with Sita.
essence: Victory is now visible, and the whole world is cheering.
simple_meaning: The people celebrate as Ram and Sita ride in a splendid flying chariot and take their seats on a beautiful high throne.
insight: It marks the public arrival of peace after conflict, not a new instruction.
modern_relevance: A stadium erupts when the final whistle blows and your team lifts the trophy. The noise, the relief, the shared shout — all of it is the feeling of a hard victory finally becoming real.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राजत रामु सहित भामिनी। मेरु सृंग जनु घन दामिनी॥ रुचिर बिमानु चलेउ अति आतुर। कीन्ही सुमन बृष्टि हरषे सुर ॥
translation: पत्नी सहित श्री रामजी ऐसे सुशोभित हो रहे हैं मानो सुमेरु के शिखर पर बिजली सहित श्याम मेघ हो। सुंदर विमान बड़ी शीघ्रता से चला। देवता हर्षित हुए और उन्होंने फूलों की वर्षा की ॥
english_translation: Rama, together with his wife, shone like dark clouds with lightning on Mount Meru. The lovely celestial chariot moved swiftly, and the radiant beings rejoiced, showering flowers.
essence: Restored love shines brighter than victory.
simple_meaning: Ram and Sita shine together like lightning on a mountain peak. Their chariot moves swiftly as the radiant beings celebrate and shower flowers.
insight: It shifts attention from battle to restoration, showing victory as harmony returning.
modern_relevance: After a long, brutal project finally ends, you step outside with the person who stood by you. The relief is bigger than success — it feels like the world itself is blessing the moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परम सुखद चलि त्रिबिध बयारी। सागर सर सरि निर्मल बारी॥ सगुन होहिं सुंदर चहुँ पासा। मन प्रसन्न निर्मल नभ आसा ॥
translation: अत्यंत सुख देने वाली तीन प्रकार की (शीतल, मंद, सुगंधित) वायु चलने लगी। समुद्र, तालाब और नदियों का जल निर्मल हो गया। चारों ओर सुंदर शकुन होने लगे। सबके मन प्रसन्न हैं, आकाश और दिशाएँ निर्मल हैं ॥
english_translation: A supremely soothing breeze began to blow in three ways. The sea, ponds, and rivers became clear and pure. Beautiful omens appeared on all sides. Everyone's mind was cheerful; the sky and the directions were bright and clear.
essence: Victory makes the whole world feel purified.
simple_meaning: Nature itself turns calm and auspicious as Ram returns in victory. The world around him seems to share the joy.
insight: It shifts attention from outer noise to the felt harmony that follows right action.
modern_relevance: After a long, tense family gathering finally ends well, the room feels different — lighter, quieter, almost washed clean. Relief can change how everything around you seems to breathe.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कह रघुबीर देखु रन सीता। लछिमन इहाँ हत्यो इँद्रजीता॥ हनूमान अंगद के मारे। रन महि परे निसाचर भारे ॥
translation: श्री रघुवीरजी ने कहा- हे सीते! रणभूमि देखो। लक्ष्मण ने यहाँ इंद्र को जीतने वाले मेघनाद को मारा था। हनुमान् और अंगद के मारे हुए ये भारी-भारी निशाचर रणभूमि में पड़े हैं ॥
english_translation: Raghubir said, "Look at the battlefield, Sita. Lakshman killed Indrajit here. These mighty night-walkers, struck down by Hanuman and Angad, lie on the field."
essence: The battlefield remembers who brought the victory.
simple_meaning: Ram points out the battlefield to Sita and names the fallen enemies and the heroes who struck them down.
insight: It keeps attention on the cost of victory and the people who made it possible.
modern_relevance: You walk past the place where a hard season ended — the office emptied, the argument over, the damage visible. The story is still in the marks left behind.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: कुंभकरन रावन द्वौ भाई। इहाँ हते सुर मुनि दुखदाई ॥
translation: देवताओं और मुनियों को दुःख देने वाले कुंभकर्ण और रावण दोनों भाई यहाँ मारे गए ॥
english_translation: Kumbhakarna and Ravana, the two brothers who tormented the gods and sages, were killed here.
essence: Two feared brothers fell where they once ruled by terror.
simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna and Ravana, the two brothers who caused suffering to the gods and sages, were slain here.
insight: It shifts attention from the drama of battle to the quiet fact of collapse.
modern_relevance: You walk past the place where a long conflict finally ended. The damage is still visible, but so is the fact that what once dominated everything has already fallen.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: इहाँ सेतु बाँध्यों अरु थापेउँ सिव सुख धाम। सीता सहित कृपानिधि संभुहि कीन्ह प्रनाम ॥
translation: मैंने यहाँ पुल बाँधा (बँधवाया) और सुखधाम श्री शिवजी की स्थापना की। तदनन्तर कृपानिधान श्री रामजी ने सीताजी सहित श्री रामेश्वर महादेव को प्रणाम किया ॥
english_translation: I built the bridge here and established the abode of Shiva. Then the treasure of compassion, Ram, bowed with Sita to Lord Shiva.
essence: Even victory bows before the sacred.
simple_meaning: Ram says he built the bridge here, established Shiva's sacred place, and then bowed with Sita to Shiva.
insight: It teaches you to let accomplishment end in gratitude, not self-importance.
modern_relevance: You finish a hard project, then still thank the mentor who shaped it. The victory is real, but so is the humility that keeps it clean.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जहँ जहँ कृपासिंधु बन कीन्ह बास बिश्राम। सकल देखाए जानकिहि कहे सबन्हि के नाम ॥
translation: वन में जहाँ-तहाँ करुणा सागर श्री रामचंद्रजी ने निवास और विश्राम किया था, वे सब स्थान प्रभु ने जानकीजी को दिखलाए और सबके नाम बतलाए ॥
english_translation: Wherever the ocean of compassion had lived and rested in the forest, he showed Janaki all those places and told her the name of each one.
essence: Love turns ordinary places into living remembrance.
simple_meaning: Ram shows Sita the forest places where he had lived and rested, naming each one for her.
insight: It shifts attention from action to memory and shared experience.
modern_relevance: You pass an old street and remember exactly where everything happened. A shared place can hold a whole chapter of love, grief, and return.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तुरत बिमान तहाँ चलि आवा। दंडक बन जहँ परम सुहावा॥ कुंभजादि मुनिनायक नाना। गए रामु सब कें अस्थाना ॥
translation: विमान शीघ्र ही वहाँ चला आया, जहाँ परम सुंदर दण्डकवन था और अगस्त्य आदि बहुत से मुनिराज रहते थे। श्री रामजी इन सबके स्थानों में गए ॥
english_translation: The celestial vehicle quickly arrived there, where the beautiful Dandaka forest lay and many great sages such as Kumbhaja lived. Ram went to the homes of all of them.
essence: Ram's presence turns every sage's home into a sacred stop.
simple_meaning: Ram's aerial vehicle reaches the beautiful Dandaka forest, and Ram visits the homes of many great sages there.
insight: It shifts attention from travel itself to honoring the people and places along the way.
modern_relevance: You finally arrive at a place everyone called meaningful, and you don't rush past the people who live there. You make time to meet the ones who have kept that place alive.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकल रिषिन्ह सन पाइ असीसा। चित्रकूट आए जगदीसा॥ तहँ करि मुनिन्ह केर संतोषा। चला बिमानु तहाँ ते चोखा ॥
translation: संपूर्ण ऋषियों से आशीर्वाद पाकर जगदीश्वर श्री रामजी चित्रकूट आए। वहाँ मुनियों को संतुष्ट किया। (फिर) विमान वहाँ से आगे तेजी के साथ चला ॥
english_translation: After receiving blessings from all the sages, the Lord of the world, Ram, came to Chitrakoot. There he satisfied the sages, and then the aerial chariot moved on quickly from there.
essence: True greatness pauses to bless others before going forward.
simple_meaning: Ram arrives at Chitrakoot, receives the sages’ blessings, gives them joy, and then continues onward.
insight: It teaches you to honor those who support you before moving on.
modern_relevance: You stop by an elder’s home, listen fully, leave them lighter, and still catch your train. Real respect can be brief and complete.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुरि राम जानकिहि देखाई। जमुना कलि मल हरनि सुहाई॥ पुनि देखी सुरसरी पुनीता। राम कहा प्रनाम करु सीता ॥
translation: फिर श्री रामजी ने जानकीजी को कलियुग के पापों का हरण करने वाली सुहावनी यमुनाजी के दर्शन कराए। फिर पवित्र गंगाजी के दर्शन किए। श्री रामजी ने कहा- हे सीते! इन्हें प्रणाम करो ॥
english_translation: Then Ram showed Janaki the lovely Yamuna, remover of the impurities of Kali Yuga. Then he showed the pure Ganga. Ram said, "Bow to them, Sita."
essence: Even Ram teaches reverence by bowing to what purifies.
simple_meaning: Ram shows Sita the sacred Yamuna and Ganga, then asks her to bow to them.
insight: It turns sacred places into living teachers and models reverence through action.
modern_relevance: You pass a river on a road trip and barely look up. This verse reminds you to pause, notice what cleanses you, and meet it with respect.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तीरथपति पुनि देखु प्रयागा। निरखत जन्म कोटि अघ भागा॥ देखु परम पावनि पुनि बेनी। हरनि सोक हरि लोक निसेनी ॥ पुनि देखु अवधपुरि अति पावनि। त्रिबिध ताप भव रोग नसावनि ॥
translation: फिर तीर्थराज प्रयाग को देखो, जिसके दर्शन से ही करोड़ों जन्मों के पाप भाग जाते हैं। फिर परम पवित्र त्रिवेणीजी के दर्शन करो, जो शोकों को हरने वाली और श्री हरि के परम धाम (पहुँचने) के लिए सीढ़ी के समान है। फिर अत्यंत पवित्र अयोध्यापुरी के दर्शन करो, जो तीनों प्रकार के तापों और भव (आवागमन रूपी) रोग का नाश करने वाली है॥4-5॥
english_translation: Then look upon Prayag, lord of pilgrimages, whose sight scatters the sins of countless births. Then behold the supremely pure Triveni, remover of sorrow and the stairway to the realm of Hari. Then look upon the holy city of Ayodhya, destroyer of the threefold heat and the disease of worldly becoming.
essence: Holy places can lighten burdens you have carried for years.
simple_meaning: Ram points out Prayag, the Triveni, and Ayodhya as places so pure that simply seeing them removes burdens, sorrow, and the pain of worldly life.
insight: It shifts attention from ordinary location to places that can reset the mind and soften suffering.
modern_relevance: You arrive in a city after a long train ride and step into a temple lane before dawn. The noise drops away, and for a moment your mind feels lighter than it has in months.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सीता सहित अवध कहुँ कीन्ह कृपाल प्रनाम। सजल नयन तन पुलकित पुनि पुनि हरषित राम ॥
translation: यों कहकर कृपालु श्री रामजी ने सीताजी सहित अवधपुरी को प्रणाम किया। सजल नेत्र और पुलकित शरीर होकर श्री रामजी बार-बार हर्षित हो रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Then the compassionate Lord bowed to Ayodhya along with Sita. With tear-filled eyes and a thrilled body, Ram grew joyful again and again.
essence: Even victory bows before the place that held your life.
simple_meaning: Ram, with Sita beside him, bows to Ayodhya with tears in his eyes and joy in his body.
insight: It shifts the reader from seeing home as possession to seeing it as something worthy of gratitude and honor.
modern_relevance: You come back to the house where your parents still keep your old room untouched. Before you speak to anyone, your chest tightens. Some places deserve reverence, not just arrival.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि प्रभु आइ त्रिबेनीं हरषित मज्जनु कीन्ह। कपिन्ह सहित बिप्रन्ह कहुँ दान बिबिध बिधि दीन्ह ॥
translation: फिर त्रिवेणी में आकर प्रभु ने हर्षित होकर स्नान किया और वानरों सहित ब्राह्मणों को अनेकों प्रकार के दान दिए ॥
english_translation: Then the Lord came to Triveni, bathed with joy, and gave many kinds of gifts to the monkeys and the brahmins.
essence: Blessing is sealed by joy that becomes giving.
simple_meaning: Ram joyfully bathed at Triveni and gave generous gifts to the monkeys and the brahmins.
insight: It shifts the mind from private enjoyment to grateful giving.
modern_relevance: After a long family trip, you finally reach the river everyone had talked about. Before moving on, you pause, wash off the dust, and quietly share what you have.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु हनुमंतहि कहा बुझाई। धरि बटु रूप अवधपुर जाई॥ भरतहि कुसल हमारि सुनाएहु। समाचार लै तुम्ह चलि आएहु ॥
translation: तदनन्तर प्रभु ने हनुमान् जी को समझाकर कहा- तुम ब्रह्मचारी का रूप धरकर अवधपुरी को जाओ। भरत को हमारी कुशल सुनाना और उनका समाचार लेकर चले आना ॥
english_translation: Then the Lord instructed Hanuman: "Go to Ayodhya in the form of a celibate ascetic. Give Bharata our news of well-being, and return bringing word of him."
essence: Even reunion begins with a messenger who knows how to carry love gently.
simple_meaning: Ram sends Hanuman to Ayodhya in disguise. He must tell Bharata that Ram is well and bring back Bharata's news.
insight: It teaches you that even joy can be carried with tact, humility, and care for another person's heart.
modern_relevance: You finally have good news for someone who has been waiting far too long, but you still choose the careful, respectful way to deliver it.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: तुरत पवनसुत गवनत भयऊ। तब प्रभु भरद्वाज पहिं गयऊ॥ नाना बिधि मुनि पूजा कीन्ही। अस्तुति करि पुनि आसिष दीन्ही ॥
translation: पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी तुरंत ही चल दिए। तब प्रभु भरद्वाजजी के पास गए। मुनि ने (इष्ट बुद्धि से) उनकी अनेकों प्रकार से पूजा की और स्तुति की और फिर (लीला की दृष्टि से) आशीर्वाद दिया ॥
english_translation: Hanuman left at once. Then the Lord went to Bharadwaja. The sage honored Him in many ways, praised Him, and then gave blessings.
essence: Devotion deepens when action pauses to honor wisdom.
simple_meaning: Hanuman leaves immediately, and Ram visits Bharadwaja. The sage welcomes Him with worship, praise, and blessings.
insight: It teaches you to honor the people who hold the larger meaning of your work.
modern_relevance: You finish one urgent task and still pause to greet the elder who helped you begin. That respectful pause changes the whole mood of the day.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: मुनि पद बंदि जुगल कर जोरी। चढ़ि बिमान प्रभु चले बहोरी॥ इहाँ निषाद सुना प्रभु आए। नाव नाव कहँ लोग बोलाए ॥
translation: दोनों हाथ जोड़कर तथा मुनि के चरणों की वंदना करके प्रभु विमान पर चढ़कर फिर (आगे) चले। यहाँ जब निषादराज ने सुना कि प्रभु आ गए, तब उसने 'नाव कहाँ है? नाव कहाँ है?' पुकारते हुए लोगों को बुलाया ॥
english_translation: After bowing to the sage and joining both hands, the Lord boarded the aerial car and moved on. When Nishadraj heard that the Lord had arrived here, he called out, "Where is the boat? Bring the boat!"
essence: Humility and prompt service travel together.
simple_meaning: Ram honors the sage, then continues on. News of his arrival reaches Nishadraj, who urgently calls for a boat.
insight: It shows reverence and readiness together: honor what is sacred, then move quickly to serve the moment.
modern_relevance: You finish thanking someone who helped you, then step back into the car. Nearby, a friend hears you’re coming and starts arranging everything before you even ask.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुरसरि नाघि जान तब आयो। उतरेउ तट प्रभु आयसु पायो॥ तब सीताँ पूजी सुरसरी। बहु प्रकार पुनि चरनन्हि परी ॥
translation: इतने में ही विमान गंगाजी को लाँघकर (इस पार) आ गया और प्रभु की आज्ञा पाकर वह किनारे पर उतरा। तब सीताजी बहुत प्रकार से गंगाजी की पूजा करके फिर उनके चरणों पर गिरीं ॥
english_translation: Meanwhile the aerial car crossed the Ganga and, on the Lord's command, landed on the bank. Then Sita worshipped the Ganga in many ways and bowed again at her feet.
essence: Safe arrival deepens humility, not pride.
simple_meaning: The flying car crosses the Ganga, lands on the bank, and Sita honors the river before bowing again.
insight: It teaches you to meet arrival with gratitude, not entitlement.
modern_relevance: You finally reach the other side after a hard trip, but you still stop to thank the people and forces that carried you there.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दीन्हि असीस हरषि मन गंगा। सुंदरि तव अहिवात अभंगा॥ सुनत गुहा धायउ प्रेमाकुल। आयउ निकट परम सुख संकुल ॥
translation: गंगाजी ने मन में हर्षित होकर आशीर्वाद दिया- हे सुंदरी! तुम्हारा सुहाग अखंड हो। भगवान् के तट पर उतरने की बात सुनते ही निषादराज गुह प्रेम में विह्वल होकर दौड़ा। परम सुख से परिपूर्ण होकर वह प्रभु के समीप आया, ॥
english_translation: Ganga blessed Sita in joy: “May your marriage be forever unbroken.” Hearing that the Lord had landed, Guha ran toward him, overwhelmed with love, and came near in bliss.
essence: Love recognises the beloved and rushes toward him.
simple_meaning: Ganga blesses Sita’s married life, and Guha rushes toward Ram with overflowing love when he hears that Ram has arrived.
insight: It shows devotion as an instinctive response: the heart runs toward what it reveres.
modern_relevance: You hear the message that someone you deeply respect has arrived nearby, and your whole body moves before your mind catches up. Some meetings are felt as joy before they are understood.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभुहि सहित बिलोकि बैदेही। परेउ अवनि तन सुधि नहिं तेही॥ प्रीति परम बिलोकि रघुराई। हरषि उठाइ लियो उर लाई ॥
translation: और श्री जानकीजी सहित प्रभु को देखकर वह (आनंद-समाधि में मग्न होकर) पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा, उसे शरीर की सुधि न रही। श्री रघुनाथजी ने उसका परम प्रेम देखकर उसे उठाकर हर्ष के साथ हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
english_translation: And seeing the Lord together with Sita, he fell to the ground and lost all awareness of his body. Seeing that supreme love, Raghunath joyfully lifted him up and drew him to his heart.
essence: Pure devotion collapses the self, and Ram answers by drawing it close.
simple_meaning: Seeing Ram and Sita, Hanuman falls in devotion and loses awareness of his body. Ram responds by lifting him up and holding him close.
insight: It shows that sincere devotion is not ignored; it is received, recognized, and answered with intimacy.
modern_relevance: You finally arrive after a long, exhausting journey and see the person you came for safe. The relief is so complete that your knees give way before your mind can catch up.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लियो हृदयँ लाइ कृपा निधान सुजान रायँ रमापति। बैठारि परम समीप बूझी कुसल सो कर बीनती॥ अब कुसल पद पंकज बिलोकि बिरंचि संकर सेब्य जे। सुख धाम पूरनकाम राम नमामि राम नमामि ते ॥
translation: सुजानों के राजा (शिरोमणि), लक्ष्मीकांत, कृपानिधान भगवान् ने उसको हृदय से लगा लिया और अत्यंत निकट बैठकर कुशल पूछी। वह विनती करने लगा- आपके जो चरणकमल ब्रह्माजी और शंकरजी से सेवित हैं, उनके दर्शन करके मैं अब सकुशल हूँ। हे सुखधाम! हे पूर्णकाम श्री रामजी! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ, नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: The Lord of Lakshmi, the treasure of compassion, drew him to his heart, seated him close, and asked after his well-being. He replied, "Seeing your lotus feet, served by Brahma and Shiva, I am now well. O abode of joy, O one whose every wish is already fulfilled, Lord Ram, I bow to you again and again."
essence: Ram's nearness turns reverence into relief.
simple_meaning: Ram lovingly brings the devotee close, asks after his welfare, and receives a prayer of reverent surrender. Seeing Ram's feet, served even by Brahma and Shiva, the devotee feels fully blessed.
insight: It shifts devotion from distance to intimacy: Ram is not only praised, but personally near and caring.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you admire deeply, and they pull out a chair for you and ask how you're doing. The moment you realize their warmth is real, gratitude turns into tears.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब भाँति अधम निषाद सो हरि भरत ज्यों उर लाइयो। मतिमंद तुलसीदास सो प्रभु मोह बस बिसराइयो॥ यह रावनारि चरित्र पावन राम पद रतिप्रद सदा। कामादिहर बिग्यानकर सुर सिद्ध मुनि गावहिं मुदा ॥
translation: सब प्रकार से नीच उस निषाद को भगवान् ने भरतजी की भाँति हृदय से लगा लिया। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- इस मंदबुद्धि ने (मैंने) मोहवश उस प्रभु को भुला दिया। रावण के शत्रु का यह पवित्र करने वाला चरित्र सदा ही श्री रामजी के चरणों में प्रीति उत्पन्न करने वाला है। यह कामादि विकारों को हरने वाला और (भगवान् के स्वरूप का) विशेष ज्ञान उत्पन्न करने वाला है। देवता, सिद्ध और मुनि आनंदित होकर इसे गाते हैं ॥
english_translation: The Lord embraced that utterly low Nishad like Bharat. Tulsidas says: I, dull and deluded, forgot that Lord through confusion. This pure account of the enemy of Ravana always awakens love for Ram's feet. It destroys desire and other faults, and gives special knowledge of the divine form. Devas, perfected beings, and sages sing it with joy.
essence: Ram's embrace reaches the lowest heart and turns it toward love.
simple_meaning: Ram welcomes the humblest person with the same love he shows Bharat. Tulsidas also admits his own forgetfulness, then says Ram's story purifies the heart, deepens love, and quiets desire.
insight: It shifts the reader from judging worthiness to recognising that devotion grows through being received.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who feels invisible at a funeral, and everyone else walks past. One kind look changes them more than any speech. This verse says that kind of welcome is Ram's nature.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: समर बिजय रघुबीर के चरित जे सुनहिं सुजान। बिजय बिबेक बिभूति नित तिन्हहि देहिं भगवान ॥
translation: जो सुजान लोग श्री रघुवीर की समर विजय संबंधी लीला को सुनते हैं, उनको भगवान् नित्य विजय, विवेक और विभूति (ऐश्वर्य) देते हैं॥।121 (क)॥
english_translation: Those wise ones who hear the victorious battle deeds of Raghubir are always given victory, discernment, and prosperity by the divine.
essence: Ram's victory becomes your own when you truly hear it.
simple_meaning: People who listen deeply to Ram's victorious story receive victory, clear judgment, and prosperity from the divine.
insight: It shifts attention from passive listening to receiving a living force that sharpens judgment and strengthens action.
modern_relevance: You finish reading a story of courage on the train ride home, and something in your chest steadies. Certain stories do more than entertain — they quietly train your mind to win cleanly.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: यह कलिकाल मलायतन मन करि देखु बिचार। श्री रघुनाथ नाम तजि नाहिन आन अधार ॥
translation: अरे मन! विचार करके देख! यह कलिकाल पापों का घर है। इसमें श्री रघुनाथजी के नाम को छोड़कर (पापों से बचने के लिए) दूसरा कोई आधार नहीं है ॥
english_translation: O mind, reflect carefully: this age is a dwelling of impurity. Apart from the name of Shri Raghunath, there is no other support.
essence: Ram's name is the only support that holds in a corrupt age.
simple_meaning: This age is full of corruption and confusion. In such a time, only Ram's name can truly support you.
insight: It shifts you from scattered reliance to inward refuge in Ram's name.
modern_relevance: When your phone is full of bad news, your plans have collapsed, and even your own thoughts feel unreliable, you need something steadier than panic. This verse points you back to the one support that does not shake.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: केकीकण्ठाभनीलं सुरवरविलसद्विप्रपादाब्जचिह्नं शोभाढ्यं पीतवस्त्रं सरसिजनयनं सर्वदा सुप्रसन्नम् । पाणौ नाराचचापं कपिनिकरयुतं बन्धुना सेव्यमानं। नौमीड्यं जानकीशं रघुवरमनिशं पुष्पकारूढरामम् ॥1।
translation: मोर के कण्ठ की आभा के समान (हरिताभ) नीलवर्ण, देवताओं में श्रेष्ठ, ब्राह्मण (भृगुजी) के चरणकमल के चिह्न से सुशोभित, शोभा से पूर्ण, पीताम्बरधारी, कजानकीकरसरोजलालितौ चिन्तकस्य मनभृंगसंगिनौ ॥ कोसलपुरी के स्वामी श्री रामचंद्रजी के सुंदर और कोमल दोनों चरणकमल ब्रह्माजी और शिवजी द्वारा वन्दित हैं, श्री जानकीजी के करकमलों से दुलराए हुए हैं और चिन्तन करने वाले के मन रूपी भौंरे के नित्य संगी हैं अर्थात् चिन्तन करने वालों का मन रूपी भ्रमर सदा उन चरणकमलों में बसा रहता है ॥ कमल नेत्र, सदा परम प्रसन्न, हाथों में बाण और धनुष धारण किए हुए, वानर समूह से युक्त भाई लक्ष्मणजी से सेवित, स्तुति किए जाने योग्य, श्री जानकीजी के पति, रघुकुल श्रेष्ठ, पुष्पक विमान पर सवार श्री रामचंद्रजी को मैं निरंतर नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I bow again and again to Rama, the lord of Janaki, the best of the Raghu line, seated in the Pushpaka विमान, blue like a peacock's neck, marked by the footprints of the best of sages, radiant, clothed in yellow, lotus-eyed, always serene, bearing bow and arrows, served by Lakshmana and a host of monkeys.
essence: Rama's greatness is shown through calm beauty, service, and reverence.
simple_meaning: Rama is beautiful, serene, and worthy of constant reverence. He is the lord of Janaki, served by Lakshmana and the monkey host, and seated in the Pushpaka विमान.
insight: It shifts attention from abstract divinity to the felt beauty of presence, service, and serenity.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a long, hard season and finally notice how peace looks on a face. This verse lingers on that kind of earned radiance.
speaker: Tulsidas

verse_text: कोसलेन्द्रपदकन्जमंजुलौ कोमलावजमहेशवन्दितौ। कुन्दइन्दुदरगौरसुन्दरं अम्बिकापतिमभीष्टसिद्धिदम् । कारुणीककलकन्जलोचनं नौमि शंकरमनंगमोचनम् ॥
translation: कुन्द के फूल, चंद्रमा और शंख के समान सुंदर गौरवर्ण, जगज्जननी श्री पार्वतीजी के पति, वान्छित फल के देने वाले, (दुखियों पर सदा), दया करने वाले, सुंदर कमल के समान नेत्र वाले, कामदेव से छुड़ाने वाले (कल्याणकारी) श्री शंकरजी को मैं नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
english_translation: I bow to Shankar, the husband of Ambika, whose lotus-like feet are worshipped by Mahesh, whose body is fair and beautiful like jasmine, moonlight, and a conch, whose eyes are like lotus petals, who grants desired fruits, is full of compassion, and frees from desire.
essence: Compassionate reverence dissolves desire.
simple_meaning: The verse praises Shiva as beautiful, compassionate, and able to free people from desire while granting what they seek.
insight: It shifts attention from craving to reverence, so the heart becomes less restless.
modern_relevance: Before a difficult conversation, you pause for one quiet breath and remember what steadies you. The mind stops chasing approval, and something calmer takes over.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रहा एक दिन अवधि कर अति आरत पुर लोग। जहँ तहँ सोचहिं नारि नर कृस तन राम बियोग॥
translation: श्री रामजी के लौटने की अवधि का एक ही दिन बाकी रह गया, अतएव नगर के लोग बहुत आतुर (अधीर) हो रहे हैं। राम के वियोग में दुबले हुए स्त्री-पुरुष जहाँ-तहाँ सोच (विचार) कर रहे हैं (कि क्या बात है श्री रामजी क्यों नहीं आए)।
english_translation: One day remained until the promised return, and the people of the city were deeply restless. Men and women, worn thin by separation from Ram, kept wondering what had kept him away.
essence: Longing for Ram makes the whole city ache.
simple_meaning: The city is counting the final day before Ram returns, and everyone is anxious with longing.
insight: It captures how longing distorts time and makes absence physically felt.
modern_relevance: You keep checking the clock before someone you love is due home, and every minute feels stretched. That restless waiting is exactly the city's mood here.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सगुन होहिं सुंदर सकल मन प्रसन्न सब केर। प्रभु आगवन जनाव जनु नगर रम्य चहुँ फेर॥
translation: इतने में सब सुंदर शकुन होने लगे और सबके मन प्रसन्न हो गए। नगर भी चारों ओर से रमणीक हो गया। मानो ये सब के सब चिह्न प्रभु के (शुभ) आगमन को जना रहे हैं।
english_translation: In that moment, all the omens turned beautiful and everyone’s heart became joyful. The whole city looked lovely from every side, as if all these signs were announcing the Lord’s arrival.
essence: Hope makes the whole world look newly alive.
simple_meaning: Good signs appear, everyone feels happy, and the whole city seems to bloom as Ram’s return draws near.
insight: It shows how anticipation can turn an ordinary place into a living sign of hope.
modern_relevance: You hear the front door open after a long wait, and the whole house changes before anyone speaks. Relief arrives first as atmosphere, then as words.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कौसल्यादि मातु सब मन अनंद अस होइ। आयउ प्रभु श्री अनुज जुत कहन चहत अब कोइ॥
translation: कौसल्या आदि सब माताओं के मन में ऐसा आनंद हो रहा है जैसे अभी कोई कहना ही चाहता है कि सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी आ गए।
english_translation: The minds of Kaushalya and the other mothers overflowed with joy, as if someone was about to say that Lord Shri Ram had arrived with his younger brother.
essence: Deep longing can make arrival feel real before it happens.
simple_meaning: The mothers are so happy that it feels as if Ram has already returned with Lakshman.
insight: It captures how longing turns anticipation into felt presence.
modern_relevance: You hear the front door unlock after a long absence, and your whole body lifts before you even see who it is. Hope can make the heart celebrate early.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत नयन भुज दच्छिन फरकत बारहिं बार। जानि सगुन मन हरष अति लागे करन बिचार॥
translation: भरतजी की दाहिनी आँख और दाहिनी भुजा बार-बार फड़क रही है। इसे शुभ शकुन जानकर उनके मन में अत्यंत हर्ष हुआ और वे विचार करने लगे-
english_translation: Bharat's right eye and right arm kept twitching again and again. Taking it as an auspicious sign, his heart filled with joy, and he began to reflect.
essence: A longing heart turns even a twitch into news.
simple_meaning: Bharat notices a repeated auspicious twitch in his body and feels hopeful enough to start thinking about what it means.
insight: It shows how longing makes the mind read meaning into every small sign.
modern_relevance: You catch a small sign in a message, a glance, or a delay, and your whole mood changes. Hope and worry can both begin with the tiniest cue.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रहेउ एक दिन अवधि अधारा। समुझत मन दुख भयउ अपारा॥ कारन कवन नाथ नहिं आयउ। जानि कुटिल किधौं मोहि बिसरायउ ॥
translation: प्राणों की आधार रूप अवधि का एक ही दिन शेष रह गया। यह सोचते ही भरतजी के मन में अपार दुःख हुआ। क्या कारण हुआ कि नाथ नहीं आए? प्रभु ने कुटिल जानकर मुझे कहीं भुला तो नहीं दिया? ॥
english_translation: One day remained in the span that was the support of his life. Thinking this, Bharat felt immense sorrow. "Why has the Lord not come? Has he seen me as crooked and forgotten me?"
essence: Longing turns into self-doubt when love does not return on time.
simple_meaning: Bharat has only one day left before his vow ends, and the delay in Ram's return fills him with grief and self-doubt.
insight: It shifts the mind from neutral delay to the fear of being rejected.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after promising yourself you won't. The silence starts to feel personal, and your mind turns the delay into a verdict.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अहह धन्य लछिमन बड़भागी। राम पदारबिंदु अनुरागी॥ कपटी कुटिल मोहि प्रभु चीन्हा। ताते नाथ संग नहिं लीन्हा ॥
translation: अहा हा! लक्ष्मण बड़े धन्य एवं बड़भागी हैं, जो श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणारविन्द के प्रेमी हैं (अर्थात् उनसे अलग नहीं हुए)। मुझे तो प्रभु ने कपटी और कुटिल पहचान लिया, इसी से नाथ ने मुझे साथ नहीं लिया ॥
english_translation: Ah, Lakshman is truly blessed and fortunate, for he is devoted to Ram's lotus feet. The Lord recognized me as deceitful and crooked, and so he did not take me along.
essence: Ram's nearness reveals love, and exposes what cannot stay close.
simple_meaning: Bharat sees Lakshman as fortunate because he stayed devoted to Ram. He also admits that his own flaws kept him from being taken along.
