insight: It shifts attention from resentment to self-honesty, showing that closeness depends on character, not claim.
modern_relevance: You watch someone else get the trust, the invitation, the closer seat at the table. Instead of blaming the world, you notice the part of you that made distance inevitable.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: जौं करनी समुझै प्रभु मोरी। नहिं निस्तार कलप सत कोरी॥ जन अवगुन प्रभु मान न काऊ। दीन बंधु अति मृदुल सुभाऊ ॥
translation: (बात भी ठीक ही है, क्योंकि) यदि प्रभु मेरी करनी पर ध्यान दें तो सौ करोड़ (असंख्य) कल्पों तक भी मेरा निस्तार (छुटकारा) नहीं हो सकता (परंतु आशा इतनी ही है कि), प्रभु सेवक का अवगुण कभी नहीं मानते। वे दीनबंधु हैं और अत्यंत ही कोमल स्वभाव के हैं ॥
english_translation: If my deeds are truly weighed, even countless ages cannot save me. But the Lord never counts a servant’s faults; the friend of the humble is tender by nature.
essence: Mercy matters more than your self-judgment.
simple_meaning: Bharat feels unworthy if his conduct is judged honestly, but he trusts that Ram does not keep score of a servant’s faults.
insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to trust in compassionate recognition.
modern_relevance: You replay one mistake after another while waiting for a reply you dread. This verse steadies you: the person who truly loves you may not be keeping the same harsh record you are.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: मोरे जियँ भरोस दृढ़ सोई। मिलिहहिं राम सगुन सुभ होई॥ बीतें अवधि रहहिं जौं प्राना। अधम कवन जग मोहि समाना ॥
translation: अतएव मेरे हृदय में ऐसा पक्का भरोसा है कि श्री रामजी अवश्य मिलेंगे, (क्योंकि) मुझे शकुन बड़े शुभ हो रहे हैं, किंतु अवधि बीत जाने पर यदि मेरे प्राण रह गए तो जगत् में मेरे समान नीच कौन होगा? ॥
english_translation: My heart holds firm trust that Ram will meet me, for the signs are all auspicious. But if the time passes and I still live, who in the world would be more lowly than I?
essence: Firm trust can survive the long silence of waiting.
simple_meaning: The speaker is certain Ram will come because the signs are favorable. If the promised time passes and life still remains, that would feel unbearable and shameful.
insight: It shifts the mind from anxious waiting to trust that can endure delay.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after sending the message that matters most. Nothing has arrived yet, but your heart keeps reading small signs as hope.
speaker: Unknown

verse_text: राम बिरह सागर महँ भरत मगन मन होत। बिप्र रूप धरि पवनसुत आइ गयउ जनु पोत॥1क॥
translation: श्री रामजी के विरह समुद्र में भरतजी का मन डूब रहा था, उसी समय पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी ब्राह्मण का रूप धरकर इस प्रकार आ गए, मानो (उन्हें डूबने से बचाने के लिए) नाव आ गई हो ॥
english_translation: While Bharat was sinking in the ocean of separation from Ram, Hanuman arrived in the form of a Brahmin, like a boat coming to rescue him.
essence: Help arrives when longing feels most unbearable.
simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed by longing for Ram, and Hanuman arrives in disguise like a boat that saves someone from drowning.
insight: It frames rescue as timely grace, not self-effort, and prepares the mind for Hanuman’s arrival.
modern_relevance: You are sitting alone after a painful message, staring at your phone, unable to steady yourself. Then a calm friend calls at exactly the right minute.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बैठे देखि कुसासन जटा मुकुट कृस गात॥ राम राम रघुपति जपत स्रवत नयन जलजात॥1ख॥
translation: हनुमान् जी ने दुर्बल शरीर भरतजी को जटाओं का मुकुट बनाए, राम! राम! रघुपति! जपते और कमल के समान नेत्रों से (प्रेमाश्रुओं) का जल बहाते कुश के आसन पर बैठे देखा ॥
english_translation: Seeing him seated on a grass seat, with matted hair as his crown and a lean body, he kept chanting, "Ram, Ram, Raghupati," while tears streamed from his lotus eyes.
essence: What remains when everything else is stripped away is devotion.
simple_meaning: Bharat sits on a simple grass seat, thin and devoted, repeating Ram's name with tears in his eyes.
insight: It shifts attention from outward status to inward devotion as the true measure of a life.
modern_relevance: You open a video call and see someone you love holding themselves together by sheer loyalty. They have almost nothing left, except the name they keep repeating.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: देखत हनूमान अति हरषेउ। पुलक गात लोचन जल बरषेउ॥ मन महँ बहुत भाँति सुख मानी। बोलेउ श्रवन सुधा सम बानी ॥
translation: उन्हें देखते ही हनुमान् जी अत्यंत हर्षित हुए। उनका शरीर पुलकित हो गया, नेत्रों से (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल बरसने लगा। मन में बहुत प्रकार से सुख मानकर वे कानों के लिए अमृत के समान वाणी बोले- ॥
english_translation: Seeing him, Hanuman was overjoyed. His body thrilled with delight, and tears of love fell from his eyes. His mind filled with many kinds of happiness, and he spoke words like nectar to the ears.
essence: Love for Ram overflows before a single word is spoken.
simple_meaning: Hanuman feels overwhelming joy on seeing Bharat, and his love shows in tears, goosebumps, and sweet speech.
insight: It shows how devotion becomes visible as tears, trembling, and gentle speech.
modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you have been worrying about for days, and your chest loosens before you can even say hello. Real care speaks through your body first.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: जासु बिरहँ सोचहु दिन राती। रटहु निरंतर गुन गन पाँती॥ रघुकुल तिलक सुजन सुखदाता। आयउ कुसल देव मुनि त्राता ॥
translation: जिनके विरह में आप दिन-रात सोच करते (घुलते) रहते हैं और जिनके गुण समूहों की पंक्तियों को आप निरंतर रटते रहते हैं, वे ही रघुकुल के तिलक, सज्जनों को दुःख देने वाले और देवताओं तथा मुनियों के रक्षक श्री रामजी सकुशल आ गए ॥
english_translation: The one for whom you grieve day and night, whose virtues you keep repeating, that Raghu-line jewel, friend of the good, protector of the gods and sages, has returned safely.
essence: Devotion turns grief into joy the moment the beloved returns.
simple_meaning: Ram is the one Bharat has missed day and night, and the one whose qualities he keeps repeating. Now that beloved protector has returned safely.
insight: It shifts longing from endless waiting to grateful recognition that the cherished one has returned.
modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after a hard conversation, waiting for the message that says they made it home. The relief is not in solving everything — only in hearing that the one you love is safe.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: रिपु रन जीति सुजस सुर गावत। सीता सहित अनुज प्रभु आवत॥ सुनत बचन बिसरे सब दूखा। तृषावंत जिमि पाइ पियूषा ॥
translation: शत्रु को रण में जीतकर सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु आ रहे हैं, देवता उनका सुंदर यश गा रहे हैं। ये वचन सुनते ही (भरतजी को) सारे दुःख भूल गए। जैसे प्यासा आदमी अमृत पाकर प्यास के दुःख को भूल जाए ॥
english_translation: The Lord is returning with Sita and Lakshman after defeating the enemy in battle; the radiant beings sing his glory. Hearing this, all Bharata's sorrow vanished, like a thirsty man forgetting thirst after drinking nectar.
essence: Joy can erase sorrow the moment hope becomes real.
simple_meaning: News of Ram's return with Sita and Lakshman wipes away Bharata's grief at once. Joy enters like nectar reaching a thirsty person.
insight: It shows how a single true message can dissolve years of heaviness in one moment.
modern_relevance: You hear the text you were waiting for after a sleepless night, and your chest loosens before you can even think. Relief can arrive that suddenly.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: को तुम्ह तात कहाँ ते आए। मोहि परम प्रिय बचन सुनाए॥ मारुत सुत मैं कपि हनुमाना। नामु मोर सुनु कृपानिधाना ॥
translation: (भरतजी ने पूछा-) हे तात! तुम कौन हो? और कहाँ से आए हो? (जो) तुमने मुझको (ये) परम प्रिय (अत्यंत आनंद देने वाले) वचन सुनाए। (हनुमान् जी ने कहा) हे कृपानिधान! सुनिए, मैं पवन का पुत्र और जाति का वानर हूँ, मेरा नाम हनुमान् है ॥
english_translation: “Who are you, dear one? Where have you come from? You have spoken words that gave me great joy. I am Hanuman, son of the wind and a monkey by birth; listen, O treasure of grace, my name is Hanuman.”
essence: Humility and warmth make a stranger instantly trustworthy.
simple_meaning: Hanuman introduces himself to Bharat after speaking words that delight him. The verse shows instant warmth, humility, and devotional connection between them.
insight: It shifts attention from status to the quality of speech and presence.
modern_relevance: You meet someone after a message that already feels kind and safe. Before titles or resumes matter, their tone tells you whether trust is possible.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: दीनबंधु रघुपति कर किंकर। सुनत भरत भेंटेउ उठि सादर॥ मिलत प्रेम नहिं हृदयँ समाता। नयन स्रवतजल पुलकित गाता ॥
translation: मैं दीनों के बंधु श्री रघुनाथजी का दास हूँ। यह सुनते ही भरतजी उठकर आदरपूर्वक हनुमान् जी से गले लगकर मिले। मिलते समय प्रेम हृदय में नहीं समाता। नेत्रों से (आनंद और प्रेम के आँसुओं का) जल बहने लगा और शरीर पुलकित हो गया ॥
english_translation: I am the servant of the Lord of the Raghu clan, friend of the humble. Hearing this, Bharata rose and embraced Hanuman with honor. Their love could not fit in the heart; tears flowed from the eyes and the body thrilled with joy.
essence: Devotion turns strangers into family at once.
simple_meaning: Hanuman identifies himself as a servant of Ram, and Bharata responds with deep honor and affection. Their meeting overflows with tears, love, and joy.
insight: It teaches you to recognize service as sacred and respond with immediate honor.
modern_relevance: You meet someone who quietly served the person you love most, and the room changes. No status game survives that moment — only gratitude, respect, and tears.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: कपि तव दरस सकल दुख बीते। मिले आजुमोहि राम पिरीते॥ बार बार बूझी कुसलाता। तो कहुँ देउँ काह सुन भ्राता ॥
translation: (भरतजी ने कहा-) हे हनुमान् - तुम्हारे दर्शन से मेरे समस्त दुःख समाप्त हो गए (दुःखों का अंत हो गया)। (तुम्हारे रूप में) आज मुझे प्यारे रामजी ही मिल गए। भरतजी ने बार-बार कुशल पूछी (और कहा-) हे भाई! सुनो, (इस शुभ संवाद के बदले में) तुम्हें क्या दूँ? ॥
english_translation: O monkey, seeing you, all my sorrow is gone. Today I have met beloved Ram through you. Again and again I ask after your well-being; tell me, brother, what can I give you?
essence: True devotion makes the messenger feel like the beloved's own arrival.
simple_meaning: Bharat feels that Hanuman’s presence has ended his sorrow, because Hanuman has brought Ram’s presence to him. He is so moved that he asks what gift he can offer.
insight: It shifts attention from the messenger as a person to the beloved they carry with them.
modern_relevance: You open the door to find a message from someone you deeply miss. Before you even read it fully, your chest loosens — because the messenger feels like their presence.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: एहि संदेस सरिस जग माहीं। करि बिचार देखेउँ कछु नाहीं॥ नाहिन तात उरिन मैं तोही। अब प्रभु चरित सुनावहु मोही ॥
translation: इस संदेश के समान (इसके बदले में देने लायक पदार्थ) जगत् में कुछ भी नहीं है, मैंने यह विचार कर देख लिया है। (इसलिए) हे तात! मैं तुमसे किसी प्रकार भी उऋण नहीं हो सकता। अब मुझे प्रभु का चरित्र (हाल) सुनाओ ॥
english_translation: There is nothing in the world equal to this message. After thinking it over, I see nothing else. I can never repay you, dear one. Now tell me about the Lord's deeds.
essence: True devotion sees a message as priceless and answers with gratitude.
simple_meaning: Bharat says Hanuman's message is priceless and cannot be repaid. Overwhelmed with gratitude, he asks to hear Ram's story.
insight: It shifts the mind from measuring kindness to receiving it with humility and longing.
modern_relevance: Someone shows up at your door after months of silence, not with explanations, but with a message that changes everything. You realize gratitude has become too large for payment.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: तब हनुमंत नाइ पद माथा। कहे सकल रघुपति गुन गाथा॥ कहु कपि कबहुँ कृपाल गोसाईं। सुमिरहिं मोहि दास की नाईं ॥
translation: तब हनुमान् जी ने भरतजी के चरणों में मस्तक नवाकर श्री रघुनाथजी की सारी गुणगाथा कही। (भरतजी ने पूछा-) हे हनुमान् ! कहो, कृपालु स्वामी श्री रामचंद्रजी कभी मुझे अपने दास की तरह याद भी करते हैं? ॥
english_translation: Then Hanuman bowed his head at Bharat's feet and spoke the whole story of Ram's virtues. Bharat asked, "Tell me, O gracious Lord, does Ram ever remember me as his servant?"
essence: Real devotion wants only to live in Ram's memory.
simple_meaning: Bharat asks Hanuman whether Ram ever remembers him as a devoted servant. The verse shows Bharat's humility and longing for Ram's remembrance.
insight: It shifts devotion from asking for reward to asking for remembrance.
modern_relevance: You send a message to someone you admire and wait for a simple reply. Not attention, not approval — just the quiet hope that your care is known. Bharat's heart lives there.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: निज दास ज्यों रघुबंसभूषन कबहुँ मम सुमिरन कर् यो। सुनि भरत बचन बिनीत अति कपि पुलकि तन चरनन्हि पर् यो॥ रघुबीर निज मुख जासु गुन गन कहत अग जग नाथ जो। काहे न होइ बिनीत परम पुनीत सदगुन सिंधु सो॥
translation: रघुवंश के भूषण श्री रामजी क्या कभी अपने दास की भाँति मेरा स्मरण करते रहे हैं? भरतजी के अत्यंत नम्र वचन सुनकर हनुमान् जी पुलकित शरीर होकर उनके चरणों पर गिर पड़े (और मन में विचारने लगे कि) जो चराचर के स्वामी हैं, वे श्री रघुवीर अपने श्रीमुख से जिनके गुणसमूहों का वर्णन करते हैं, वे भरतजी ऐसे विनम्र, परम पवित्र और सद्गुणों के समुद्र क्यों न हों?
english_translation: "Has Lord Ram, the ornament of Raghu's line, ever remembered me as his servant?" Hearing Bharat's humble words, Hanuman's body thrilled, and he fell at Bharat's feet. "The Lord of all worlds speaks Bharat's virtues with his own mouth; how could such a bearer of pure virtues and deep goodness not be utterly humble and supremely pure?"
essence: Real greatness bows before humility and recognizes itself in it.
simple_meaning: Hanuman is moved by Bharat's humility and realizes that Ram's praise itself proves Bharat's purity and greatness.
insight: It shifts admiration from status to humility, teaching you to trust the character that doesn't advertise itself.
modern_relevance: Someone quietly deflects praise at a family dinner, and you realize their modesty is not insecurity. It is the mark of a person whose goodness does not need an audience.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: राम प्रान प्रिय नाथ तुम्ह सत्य बचन मम तात। पुनि पुनि मिलत भरत सुनि हरष न हृदयँ समात ॥
translation: (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे नाथ! आप श्री रामजी को प्राणों के समान प्रिय हैं, हे तात! मेरा वचन सत्य है। यह सुनकर भरतजी बार-बार मिलते हैं, हृदय में हर्ष समाता नहीं है ॥
english_translation: O lord, you are as dear to Ram as life itself. My words are true, dear one. Hearing this, Bharat meets again and again, and his heart cannot contain its joy.
essence: Love remembered is joy that cannot stay contained.
simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Bharat that he is as dear to Ram as life itself, and Bharat is so happy hearing this that his heart cannot hold it.
insight: It shifts the heart from anxious doubt to the quiet certainty of being cherished.
modern_relevance: You finally hear that the person you love most still holds you close. The relief is so strong it feels almost too large for your chest.
speaker: Hanuman

verse_text: भरत चरन सिरु नाइ तुरित गयउ कपि राम पहिं। कही कुसल सब जाइ हरषि चलेउ प्रभु जान चढ़ि ॥
translation: फिर भरतजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर हनुमान् जी तुरंत ही श्री रामजी के पास (लौट) गए और जाकर उन्होंने सब कुशल कही। तब प्रभु हर्षित होकर विमान पर चढ़कर चले ॥
english_translation: After bowing his head at Bharata's feet, Hanuman quickly went back to Rama. He told him everything was well, and then the Lord, pleased, set out in the flying chariot.
essence: Devotion moves swiftly and leaves everyone lighter.
simple_meaning: Hanuman bows to Bharata, returns to Rama, reports that all is well, and Rama leaves happily in the chariot.
insight: It shows how devotion becomes action: respect, quick return, clear reporting, and joyful movement.
modern_relevance: You finally get the text that says, 'I'm okay.' The relief is so immediate it changes your whole body.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरषि भरत कोसलपुर आए। समाचार सब गुरहि सुनाए॥ पुनि मंदिर महँ बात जनाई। आवत नगर कुसल रघुराई ॥
translation: इधर भरतजी भी हर्षित होकर अयोध्यापुरी में आए और उन्होंने गुरुजी को सब समाचार सुनाया! फिर राजमहल में खबर जनाई कि श्री रघुनाथजी कुशलपूर्वक नगर को आ रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Bharat joyfully arrived in Kosalpur and told the guru everything. Then he announced in the palace that Raghurai was coming to the city safely.
essence: Bharat's happiness becomes the whole city's hope.
simple_meaning: Bharat returns to Ayodhya, shares the news with his teacher, and spreads word that Ram is safely on the way.
insight: It shifts the moment from waiting alone to shared relief and gathering.
modern_relevance: You get the message that the person you miss is on the way back, and suddenly you are telling everyone — family, friends, the whole house.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनत सकल जननीं उठि धाईं। कहि प्रभु कुसल भरत समुझाईं॥ समाचार पुरबासिन्ह पाए। नर अरु नारि हरषि सब धाए ॥
translation: खबर सुनते ही सब माताएँ उठ दौड़ीं। भरतजी ने प्रभु की कुशल कहकर सबको समझाया। नगर निवासियों ने यह समाचार पाया, तो स्त्री-पुरुष सभी हर्षित होकर दौड़े ॥
english_translation: When they heard the news, all the mothers rushed up. Bharata reassured everyone by saying that the Lord was well. The people of the city received the news, and men and women all ran out in joy.
essence: Relief for Ram becomes joy for everyone.
simple_meaning: The news of Ram's well-being spreads through Ayodhya, and everyone rushes out in joy and relief.
insight: It shows how shared relief can turn a city from waiting into action.
modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with the message you were waiting for: they made it home safely. In that instant, the whole body moves before the mind can speak.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: दधि दुर्बा रोचन फल फूला। नव तुलसी दल मंगल मूला॥ भरि भरि हेम थार भामिनी। गावत चलिं सिंधुरगामिनी ॥
translation: (श्री रामजी के स्वागत के लिए) दही, दूब, गोरोचन, फल, फूल और मंगल के मूल नवीन तुलसीदल आदि वस्तुएँ सोने की थाली में भर-भरकर हथिनी की सी चाल वाली सौभाग्यवती स्त्रियाँ (उन्हें लेकर) गाती हुई चलीं ॥
english_translation: For Ram's welcome, curd, durva grass, rochana, fruits, flowers, and fresh tulsi leaves were filled again and again into golden trays, while fortunate women walked singing with the grace of an elephant.
essence: Welcome becomes worship when love fills the hands.
simple_meaning: Women carried auspicious offerings in golden trays and sang as they went to welcome Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from the gift to the devotion behind the gift.
modern_relevance: You see neighbors carrying sweets, flowers, and lamps to a home after a long-awaited return. The joy is in the gathering itself, not in the objects.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जे जैसेहिं तैसेहिं उठि धावहिं। बाल बृद्ध कहँ संग न लावहिं॥ एक एकन्ह कहँ बूझहिं भाई। तुम्ह देखे दयाल रघुराई ॥
translation: जो जैसे हैं (जहाँ जिस दशा में हैं) वे वैसे ही (वहीं से उसी दशा में) उठ दौड़ते हैं। (देर हो जाने के डर से) बालकों और बूढ़ों को कोई साथ नहीं लाते। एक-दूसरे से पूछते हैं- भाई! तुमने दयालु श्री रघुनाथजी को देखा है? ॥
english_translation: Everyone rushes out just as they are, leaving children and the old behind. Each person asks the other, “Brother, have you seen the compassionate Raghunath?”
essence: Love makes people leave everything and run toward Ram.
simple_meaning: The whole city is so eager to see Ram that people rush out immediately, without waiting to gather anyone else. Everyone is asking who has seen him.
insight: It shows how devotion turns a whole city into one searching, eager movement.
modern_relevance: You get the message that someone you love is finally on the way home, and suddenly nothing else matters. Shoes half-on, phone in hand, you’re already at the door.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अवधपुरी प्रभु आवत जानी। भई सकल सोभा कै खानी॥ बहइ सुहावन त्रिबिध समीरा। भइ सरजू अति निर्मल नीरा ॥
translation: प्रभु को आते जानकर अवधपुरी संपूर्ण शोभाओं की खान हो गई। तीनों प्रकार की सुंदर वायु बहने लगी। सरयूजी अति निर्मल जल वाली हो गईं। (अर्थात् सरयूजी का जल अत्यंत निर्मल हो गया) ॥
english_translation: Knowing that the Lord was coming to Ayodhya, the city became a treasury of beauty. A pleasant breeze from all three directions began to blow, and the Sarayu became extremely clear.
essence: Ram's nearness turns ordinary life radiant.
simple_meaning: Ayodhya is transformed by Ram's arrival. The city, the wind, and the river all seem purified and radiant.
insight: It shifts attention from Ram's arrival as an event to Ram's presence as a transforming force.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home where everyone has been waiting for you, and the whole room changes. The air feels lighter, the water looks clearer, and people stand straighter without meaning to.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हरषित गुर परिजन अनुज भूसुर बृंद समेत। चले भरत मन प्रेम अति सन्मुख कृपानिकेत ॥
translation: गुरु वशिष्ठजी, कुटुम्बी, छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न तथा ब्राह्मणों के समूह के साथ हर्षित होकर भरतजी अत्यंत प्रेमपूर्ण मन से कृपाधाम श्री रामजी के सामने अर्थात् उनकी अगवानी के लिए चले ॥
english_translation: With the guru, family, younger brother, and a group of learned priests, Bharat joyfully set out with a love-filled heart to welcome the gracious Lord Ram.
essence: Love makes the whole city move toward Ram.
simple_meaning: Bharat goes out happily with his teacher, family, brother, and priests to welcome Ram with deep love.
insight: It shows how love turns a public reception into a shared act of reverence.
modern_relevance: You hear someone you love is finally coming home, and you step out with everyone who matters to meet them. The joy is shared before a word is spoken.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बहुतक चढ़ीं अटारिन्ह निरखहिं गगन बिमान। देखि मधुर सुर हरषित करहिं सुमंगल गान ॥
translation: बहुत सी स्त्रियाँ अटारियों पर चढ़ीं आकाश में विमान देख रही हैं और उसे देखकर हर्षित होकर मीठे स्वर से सुंदर मंगल गीत गा रही हैं ॥
english_translation: Many women climbed onto the terraces to look at the aerial chariot in the sky. Seeing it, they rejoiced and sang sweet, auspicious songs.
essence: Joy rises naturally when the beloved comes into view.
simple_meaning: People gather on their terraces to watch the flying chariot and sing joyful songs.
insight: It turns a passing sight into a communal act of celebration.
modern_relevance: You hear the first siren of a parade, and neighbors spill onto balconies with phones raised and smiles breaking through. Joy becomes public before anyone plans it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राका ससि रघुपति पुर सिंधु देखि हरषान। बढ़् यो कोलाहल करत जनु नारि तरंग समान ॥
translation: श्री रघुनाथजी पूर्णिमा के चंद्रमा हैं तथा अवधपुर समुद्र है, जो उस पूर्णचंद्र को देखकर हर्षित हो रहा है और शोर करता हुआ बढ़ रहा है (इधर-उधर दौड़ती हुई) स्त्रियाँ उसकी तरंगों के समान लगती हैं ॥
english_translation: Raghupati is the full moon, and Ayodhya is the sea; seeing that moon, it swells with joy and noise, while the women moving about are like its waves.
essence: Ram's return makes the whole city overflow with joy.
simple_meaning: Ayodhya erupts in joy at Ram's return. The city feels alive, and the women rushing about are compared to waves in a sea.
insight: It turns a return into a shared public celebration, showing how presence can transform an entire place.
modern_relevance: A neighborhood comes alive when the team wins after years of waiting. Doors open, people spill into the street, and even the noise feels like relief.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: इहाँ भानुकुल कमल दिवाकर। कपिन्ह देखावत नगर मनोहर॥ सुनु कपीस अंगद लंकेसा। पावन पुरी रुचिर यह देसा ॥
translation: यहाँ (विमान पर से) सूर्य कुल रूपी कमल को प्रफुल्लित करने वाले सूर्य श्री रामजी वानरों को मनोहर नगर दिखला रहे हैं। (वे कहते हैं-) हे सुग्रीव! हे अंगद! हे लंकापति विभीषण! सुनो। यह पुरी पवित्र है और यह देश सुंदर है ॥
english_translation: Here, Rama, the sun of the Solar dynasty, shows the lovely city to the monkeys. "Listen, Sugriva, Angada, and Lord of Lanka Vibhishana: this city is pure, and this land is beautiful."
essence: Love makes the familiar appear newly pure.
simple_meaning: Rama points out the beauty and purity of Ayodhya to Sugriva, Angada, and Vibhishana as they look down from above.
insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to reverent seeing, where even a city becomes luminous through devotion.
modern_relevance: You return to your old neighborhood after years away and suddenly notice the tree-lined street, the temple bell, the familiar rooftops. What once felt ordinary now feels precious.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जद्यपि सब बैकुंठ बखाना। बेद पुरान बिदित जगु जाना॥ अवधपुरी सम प्रिय नहिं सोऊ। यह प्रसंग जानइ कोउ कोऊ ॥
translation: यद्यपि सबने वैकुण्ठ की बड़ाई की है- यह वेद-पुराणों में प्रसिद्ध है और जगत् जानता है, परंतु अवधपुरी के समान मुझे वह भी प्रिय नहीं है। यह बात (भेद) कई-कोई (बिरले ही) जानते हैं ॥
english_translation: Although everyone praises Vaikuntha, and the Vedas and Puranas make it famous, Ayodhya is still dearer. Only a rare few understand this distinction.
essence: Sacredness deepens when love chooses a place as home.
simple_meaning: Ram says that although Vaikuntha is praised everywhere, Ayodhya is even dearer to him. Only a few people understand this subtle truth.
insight: It shifts reverence from abstract perfection to lived belonging and love.
modern_relevance: You can fly across the world and still feel most alive in the street where your mother called you home. Some places matter not because they are perfect, but because they are yours.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: जन्मभूमि मम पुरी सुहावनि। उत्तर दिसि बह सरजू पावनि॥ जा मज्जन ते बिनहिं प्रयासा। मम समीप नर पावहिं बासा ॥
translation: यह सुहावनी पुरी मेरी जन्मभूमि है। इसके उत्तर दिशा में जीवों को पवित्र करने वाली सरयू नदी बहती है, जिसमें स्नान करने से मनुष्य बिना ही परिश्रम मेरे समीप निवास (सामीप्य मुक्ति) पा जाते हैं ॥
english_translation: This lovely city is my birthplace. To its north flows the purifying Sarayu; by bathing in it, people reach closeness to me without effort.
essence: Grace can make nearness simple, not strenuous.
simple_meaning: Ram says Ayodhya is his beloved birthplace, and the Sarayu there is so pure that bathing in it brings people close to him without effort.
insight: It shifts devotion from effortful striving to receptive purification and place-based remembrance.
modern_relevance: You step into a river at dawn after months of carrying everything alone. For a moment, the noise drops away, and you feel that nearness is not earned by strain alone.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: अति प्रिय मोहि इहाँ के बासी। मम धामदा पुरी सुख रासी॥ हरषे सब कपि सुनि प्रभु बानी। धन्य अवध जो राम बखानी ॥
translation: यहाँ के निवासी मुझे बहुत ही प्रिय हैं। यह पुरी सुख की राशि और मेरे परमधाम को देने वाली है। प्रभु की वाणी सुनकर सब वानर हर्षित हुए (और कहने लगे कि) जिस अवध की स्वयं श्री रामजी ने बड़ाई की, वह (अवश्य ही) धन्य है॥
english_translation: The people here are very dear to me. This city is a treasury of joy and the place of my own highest abode. Hearing the Lord's words, all the monkeys rejoiced and said, "Blessed is Ayodhya, praised by Ram."
essence: Love makes a city feel like the highest home.
simple_meaning: Ram says the people of Ayodhya are very dear to him, and the city is full of joy because it is his own beloved home. The monkeys rejoice at hearing this praise.
insight: It shifts devotion from abstract worship to lived belonging and mutual affection.
modern_relevance: You walk into a neighborhood where everyone knows your name and your burden feels lighter. Ram's words show what it means to be held by a place and a people who truly receive you.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: आवत देखि लोग सब कृपासिंधु भगवान। नगर निकट प्रभु प्रेरेउ उतरेउ भूमि बिमान ॥
translation: कृपा सागर भगवान् श्री रामचंद्रजी ने सब लोगों को आते देखा, तो प्रभु ने विमान को नगर के समीप उतरने की प्रेरणा की। तब वह पृथ्वी पर उतरा ॥
english_translation: Seeing everyone gathered, the compassionate Lord prompted the divine vehicle to descend near the city, and it came down to the earth.
essence: Arrival itself becomes blessing when it comes near the people.
simple_meaning: Ram sees the people and brings the divine vehicle down near the city. The moment is about arrival, not teaching.
insight: It frames the scene as arrival and welcome, not as a doctrinal statement.
modern_relevance: You pull into the neighborhood after a long trip, and everyone is already outside waiting. The real moment is not the vehicle itself, but the nearness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: उतरि कहेउ प्रभु पुष्पकहि तुम्ह कुबेर पहिं जाहु। प्रेरित राम चलेउ सो हरषु बिरहु अति ताहु ॥
translation: विमान से उतरकर प्रभु ने पुष्पक विमान से कहा कि तुम अब कुबेर के पास जाओ। श्री रामचंद्रजी की प्रेरणा से वह चला, उसे (अपने स्वामी के पास जाने का) हर्ष है और प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी से अलग होने का अत्यंत दुःख भी ॥
english_translation: After stepping down, the Lord told Pushpak, “Go now to Kubera.” Moved by Ram’s will, it departed—glad to return, yet aching to leave Ram.
essence: True devotion can make departure feel like both joy and grief.
simple_meaning: Pushpak leaves Ram’s presence because Ram sends it away. It goes gladly, yet it also feels the pain of separation.
insight: It shows how even obedience to what is right can include tenderness and loss.
modern_relevance: You finally end a call with someone who steadies you, and the room feels emptier at once. Relief and longing can arrive together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: आए भरत संग सब लोगा। कृस तन श्रीरघुबीर बियोगा॥ बामदेव बसिष्ट मुनिनायक। देखे प्रभु महि धरि धनु सायक ॥
translation: भरतजी के साथ सब लोग आए। श्री रघुवीर के वियोग से सबके शरीर दुबले हो रहे हैं। प्रभु ने वामदेव, वशिष्ठ आदि मुनिश्रेष्ठों को देखा, तो उन्होंने धनुष-बाण पृथ्वी पर रखकर- ॥
english_translation: Bharat came with all the people. Separated from noble Ram, everyone’s body had grown thin. When the Lord saw Vamadeva, Vashishtha, and the other great sages, he set down his bow and arrows on the ground.
essence: Separation from what you love leaves its mark; true greatness bows first.
simple_meaning: Bharat arrives with the people, and everyone looks worn down by separation from Ram. Ram sees the sages and respectfully lays down his bow and arrows.
insight: It teaches you to notice how separation changes people, and to answer reverence with humility.
modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital waiting room and see how weeks of worry have hollowed everyone out. Then someone important to the family arrives, and the first thing they do is put their phone down and bow their head.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: धाइ धरे गुर चरन सरोरुह। अनुज सहित अति पुलक तनोरुह॥ भेंटि कुसल बूझी मुनिराया। हमरें कुसल तुम्हारिहिं दाया ॥
translation: छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित दौड़कर गुरुजी के चरणकमल पकड़ लिए, उनके रोम-रोम अत्यंत पुलकित हो रहे हैं। मुनिराज वशिष्ठजी ने (उठाकर) उन्हें गले लगाकर कुशल पूछी। (प्रभु ने कहा-) आप ही की दया में हमारी कुशल है ॥
english_translation: Rama and Lakshmana rushed to the guru's lotus feet, their bodies thrilled with joy. Sage Vashishtha embraced them and asked about their welfare. Rama replied, "Our well-being rests in your grace."
essence: True well-being begins when pride bows to grace.
simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana rush to honor their teacher, and Rama says their welfare depends on his grace.
insight: It shifts status into reverence, reminding you that strength stays clean when it remains teachable.
modern_relevance: You finally meet the mentor who helped you through the hardest season, and you don't perform success — you bow, thank them, and admit how much you still need grace.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सकल द्विजन्ह मिलि नायउ माथा। धर्म धुरंधर रघुकुलनाथा॥ गहे भरत पुनि प्रभु पद पंकज। नमत जिन्हहि सुर मुनि संकर अज ॥
translation: धर्म की धुरी धारण करने वाले रघुकुल के स्वामी श्री रामजी ने सब ब्राह्मणों से मिलकर उन्हें मस्तक नवाया। फिर भरतजी ने प्रभु के वे चरणकमल पकड़े जिन्हें देवता, मुनि, शंकरजी और ब्रह्माजी (भी) नमस्कार करते हैं ॥
english_translation: The Lord of Raghu, who upholds the pillar of dharma, bowed to all the learned priests. Then Bharat held the lotus feet of the Lord, feet that devas, sages, Shiva, and Brahma bow to.
essence: True dignity bows first, and reverence deepens when pride disappears.
simple_meaning: Ram bows to the priests, and Bharat bows to Ram's feet. The verse shows mutual humility and reverence in the royal family.
insight: It shifts respect from hierarchy to humility, showing that honour grows when ego steps aside.
modern_relevance: At a wedding, the youngest cousin bows first to the elders, and the room softens. Status drops away for a moment, and love becomes easier to feel.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: परे भूमि नहिं उठत उठाए। बर करि कृपासिंधु उर लाए॥ स्यामल गात रोम भए ठाढ़े। नव राजीव नयन जल बाढ़े ॥
translation: भरतजी पृथ्वी पर पड़े हैं, उठाए उठते नहीं। तब कृपासिंधु श्री रामजी ने उन्हें जबर्दस्ती उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया। (उनके) साँवले शरीर पर रोएँ खड़े हो गए। नवीन कमल के समान नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं के) जल की बाढ़ आ गई ॥
english_translation: Bharat lies on the ground and cannot be lifted. Then the ocean of grace lifts him and holds him to his heart. Ram's dark body bristles with goosebumps, and tears flood his newly lotus-like eyes.
essence: True devotion is met not with distance, but with an embrace that overflows.
simple_meaning: Bharat is too overwhelmed to get up on his own, so Ram lifts him and embraces him. Their love is so intense that Ram trembles with emotion and tears fill his eyes.
insight: It shifts devotion from formal respect to living intimacy, where surrender is met by immediate embrace.
modern_relevance: You finally show up after months of silence, too ashamed to meet someone's eyes. Before you can explain, they pull you in. Some bonds do not need a speech; they need an embrace.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राजीव लोचन स्रवत जल तन ललित पुलकावलि बनी। अति प्रेम हृदयँ लगाइ अनुजहि मिले प्रभु त्रिभुअन धनी॥ प्रभु मिलत अनुजहि सोह मो पहिं जाति नहिं उपमा कही। जनु प्रेम अरु सिंगार तनु धरि मिले बर सुषमा लही ॥
translation: कमल के समान नेत्रों से जल बह रहा है। सुंदर शरीर में पुलकावली (अत्यंत) शोभा दे रही है। त्रिलोकी के स्वामी प्रभु श्री रामजी छोटे भाई भरतजी को अत्यंत प्रेम से हृदय से लगाकर मिले। भाई से मिलते समय प्रभु जैसे शोभित हो रहे हैं, उसकी उपमा मुझसे कही नहीं जाती। मानो प्रेम और श्रृंगार शरीर धारण करके मिले और श्रेष्ठ शोभा को प्राप्त हुए ॥
english_translation: Tears flow from the lotus-like eyes. His beautiful body bristles with joy. The Lord of the three worlds embraced his younger brother with great love. No comparison can capture how splendid the Lord looked when meeting his brother. It was as if love and beauty had taken human form and met in perfect grace.
essence: Love and beauty become visible when reunion finally happens.
simple_meaning: Ram meets Bharat with tears, joy, and an embrace so beautiful that no comparison can fully describe it.
insight: It shifts attention from status to intimacy, showing that true greatness is revealed in loving reunion.
modern_relevance: You see your brother after years apart at the airport, and both of you go silent before the hug. Some reunions carry a beauty words cannot hold.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बूझत कृपानिधि कुसल भरतहि बचन बेगि न आवई॥ सुनु सिवा सो सुख बचन मन ते भिन्न जान जो पावई॥ अब कुसल कौसलनाथ आरत जानि जन दरसन दियो। बूड़त बिरह बारीस कृपानिधान मोहि कर गहि लियो ॥
translation: कृपानिधान श्री रामजी भरतजी से कुशल पूछते हैं, परंतु आनंदवश भरतजी के मुख से वचन शीघ्र नहीं निकलते। (शिवजी ने कहा-) हे पार्वती! सुनो, वह सुख (जो उस समय भरतजी को मिल रहा था) वचन और मन से परे है, उसे वही जानता है जो उसे पाता है। (भरतजी ने कहा-) हे कोसलनाथ! आपने आर्त्त (दुःखी) जानकर दास को दर्शन दिए, इससे अब कुशल है। विरह समुद्र में डूबते हुए मुझको कृपानिधान ने हाथ पकड़कर बचा लिया! ॥
english_translation: The Lord of compassion asks Bharat how he is, but Bharat cannot speak at once in his joy. Shiva says to Parvati: that happiness is beyond words and mind, known only by the one who experiences it. Bharat says: O Lord of Kosala, seeing me in distress, you gave me your sight, and now I am well. The ocean of separation was drowning me, but the Lord of compassion held my hand and saved me.
essence: Love can rescue you before any words are spoken.
simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed when Ram embraces him and asks after his welfare. The joy is so deep it cannot be spoken. Bharat says Ram’s sight itself has rescued him from the pain of separation.
insight: It shifts attention from verbal reassurance to the healing power of loving presence.
modern_relevance: You finally reach the hospital room after a night of fear, and the person you love opens their eyes. Before any explanation, the relief itself says everything.
speaker: Bharat

verse_text: पुनि प्रभु हरषि सत्रुहन भेंटे हृदयँ लगाइ। लछिमन भरत मिले तब परम प्रेम दोउ भाइ ॥
translation: फिर प्रभु हर्षित होकर शत्रुघ्नजी को हृदय से लगाकर उनसे मिले। तब लक्ष्मणजी और भरतजी दोनों भाई परम प्रेम से मिले॥।5॥
english_translation: Then the Lord, delighted, embraced Shatrughna to his heart. Then Lakshman and Bharat met in deep love, both brothers.
essence: Love restores family faster than sorrow can divide it.
simple_meaning: Ram warmly embraces Shatrughna, then Lakshman and Bharat meet in deep affection. The verse simply shows the joy of reunion among the brothers.
insight: It highlights reunion as emotional restoration, not just a social greeting.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after months apart, and the first hug says everything. Some reunions do more than comfort — they repair what grief had split.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरतानुज लछिमन पुनि भेंटे। दुसह बिरह संभव दुख मेटे॥ सीता चरन भरत सिरु नावा। अनुज समेत परम सुख पावा ॥
translation: फिर लक्ष्मणजी शत्रुघ्नजी से गले लगकर मिले और इस प्रकार विरह से उत्पन्न दुःसह दुःख का नाश किया। फिर भाई शत्रुघ्नजी सहित भरतजी ने सीताजी के चरणों में सिर नवाया और परम सुख प्राप्त किया ॥
english_translation: Lakshman and Shatrughna embraced again. The unbearable pain born of separation disappeared. Bharata bowed his head at Sita's feet with his younger brother, and they found complete joy.
essence: Love ends separation faster than words can.
simple_meaning: Lakshman and Shatrughna embrace, and the pain of separation ends. Bharata bows to Sita with his brother, and joy returns.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the healing power of reunion and reverence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a house after months away and no one needs to explain the tears. A single embrace can end a season of loneliness.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु बिलोकि हरषे पुरबासी। जनित बियोग बिपति सब नासी॥ प्रेमातुर सब लोग निहारी। कौतुक कीन्ह कृपाल खरारी ॥
translation: प्रभु को देखकर अयोध्यावासी सब हर्षित हुए। वियोग से उत्पन्न सब दुःख नष्ट हो गए। सब लोगों को प्रेम विह्नल (और मिलने के लिए अत्यंत आतुर) देखकर खर के शत्रु कृपालु श्री रामजी ने एक चमत्कार किया ॥
english_translation: Seeing the Lord, the people of Ayodhya rejoiced. All sorrow born of separation vanished. Seeing everyone overwhelmed with love and longing, the compassionate enemy of Khara performed a wondrous act.
essence: Presence from the beloved ends separation at once.
simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya are overjoyed at Ram's return, and their pain of separation disappears. Seeing their longing, Ram responds with a wondrous act.
insight: It shifts attention from private grief to the healing power of loving presence.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room after months away, and the people who love you light up before you even speak. That relief, that release, is what this verse holds.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अमित रूप प्रगटे तेहि काला। जथाजोग मिले सबहि कृपाला॥ कृपादृष्टि रघुबीर बिलोकी। किए सकल नर नारि बिसोकी ॥
translation: उसी समय कृपालु श्री रामजी असंख्य रूपों में प्रकट हो गए और सबसे (एक ही साथ) यथायोग्य मिले। श्री रघुवीर ने कृपा की दृष्टि से देखकर सब नर-नारियों को शोक से रहित कर दिया ॥
english_translation: At that moment, the compassionate Lord appeared in countless forms and met everyone in the way each needed. Looking with a merciful glance, Raghubir freed every man and woman from sorrow.
essence: Compassion takes the shape each heart can receive.
simple_meaning: Ram appears in many forms so he can meet each person appropriately, and his compassionate glance removes everyone's sorrow.
insight: It teaches you to meet people according to their need, not your script.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is carrying different hurt. One kind look, one careful response, and the whole atmosphere changes.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: छन महिं सबहि मिले भगवाना। उमा मरम यह काहुँ न जाना॥ एहि बिधि सबहि सुखी करि रामा। आगें चले सील गुन धामा ॥
translation: भगवान् क्षण मात्र में सबसे मिल लिए। हे उमा! यह रहस्य किसी ने नहीं जाना। इस प्रकार शील और गुणों के धाम श्री रामजी सबको सुखी करके आगे बढ़े ॥
english_translation: In an instant, Bhagavan met everyone. O Uma, no one understood this mystery. In this way, Ram, the abode of gentleness and virtues, made everyone happy and moved on.
essence: Ram’s presence itself makes people whole.
simple_meaning: Ram met everyone so quickly that no one could even grasp how it happened. He comforted the whole crowd, made them happy, and then moved on.
insight: It shifts attention from dramatic action to the quiet power of presence and graciousness.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room full of people who have been waiting for you, and somehow the tension drops before you say a word. Some people calm others just by arriving.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कौसल्यादि मातु सब धाई। निरखि बच्छ जनु धेनु लवाई ॥
translation: कौसल्या आदि माताएँ ऐसे दौड़ीं मानों नई ब्यायी हुई गायें अपने बछड़ों को देखकर दौड़ी हों ॥
english_translation: Kausalya and the other mothers ran toward them, like cows rushing to their calves.
essence: Love runs before the mind can catch up.
simple_meaning: The mothers ran to meet the children, moved by the same instinct as a mother cow rushing to her calf.
insight: It turns a reunion into a living image of natural, bodily affection.
modern_relevance: You spot your child at the school gate after a long day and move before you even think. Some love is older than language.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जनु धेनु बालक बच्छ तजि गृहँ चरन बन परबस गईं। दिन अंत पुर रुख स्रवत थन हुंकार करि धावत भईं॥ अति प्रेम प्रभु सब मातु भेटीं बचन मृदु बहुबिधि कहे। गइ बिषम बिपति बियोगभव तिन्ह हरष सुख अगनित लहे॥
translation: मानो नई ब्यायी हुई गायें अपने छोटे बछड़ों को घर पर छोड़ परवश होकर वन में चरने गई हों और दिन का अंत होने पर (बछड़ों से मिलने के लिए) हुँकार करके थन से दूध गिराती हुईं नगर की ओर दौड़ी हों। प्रभु ने अत्यंत प्रेम से सब माताओं से मिलकर उनसे बहुत प्रकार के कोमल वचन कहे। वियोग से उत्पन्न भयानक विपत्ति दूर हो गई और सबने (भगवान् से मिलकर और उनके वचन सुनकर) अगणित सुख और हर्ष प्राप्त किए।
english_translation: Like freshly calved cows, leaving their calves at home, they went to graze in helplessness and then at day’s end rushed back lowing, milk flowing from their udders. With great love, the Lord met all the mothers and spoke to them in many gentle ways. The terrible suffering born of separation was removed, and they all received immeasurable joy and delight.
essence: Love meets grief, and grief loses its hold.
simple_meaning: The mothers rush to meet Ram with overwhelming love, and his gentle meeting ends their pain of separation.
insight: It shows how loving presence and gentle words can end separation’s pain.
modern_relevance: You finally reach home after a long, draining trip, and the first familiar face makes your chest loosen. Some exhaustion ends the moment love meets it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भेंटेउ तनय सुमित्राँ राम चरन रति जानि। रामहि मिलत कैकई हृदयँ बहुत सकुचानि ॥
translation: सुमित्राजी अपने पुत्र लक्ष्मणजी की श्री रामजी के चरणों में प्रीति जानकर उनसे मिलीं। श्री रामजी से मिलते समय कैकेयीजी हृदय में बहुत सकुचाईं ॥
english_translation: Sumitra met her son, knowing his love for Ram's feet. Kaikeyi felt deeply shy when she met Ram.
essence: Devotion makes meeting natural; guilt makes it painful.
simple_meaning: Sumitra came to meet Lakshman because she knew his heart belonged to Ram. Kaikeyi, by contrast, felt awkward and ashamed when facing Ram.
insight: It shows how inner devotion creates openness, while inner conflict creates hesitation.
modern_relevance: You walk into a room where one parent beams with pride and another can barely look up. The difference is not the room — it is the heart each person brings into it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लछिमन सब मातन्ह मिलि हरषे आसिष पाइ। कैकइ कहँ पुनि पुनि मिले मन कर छोभु न जाइ ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी भी सब माताओं से मिलकर और आशीर्वाद पाकर हर्षित हुए। वे कैकेयीजी से बार-बार मिले, परंतु उनके मन का क्षोभ (रोष) नहीं जाता ॥
english_translation: Lakshman was delighted after meeting all the mothers and receiving their blessings. He met Kaikeyi again and again, but the hurt in his heart would not go away.
essence: Blessings can soften the moment, but they do not erase old hurt.
simple_meaning: Lakshman is happy to meet the mothers and receive their blessings, but his hurt stays alive when he sees Kaikeyi again.
insight: It shows how unresolved hurt can coexist with outward respect and social grace.
modern_relevance: You smile at the family gathering, but one person’s name still tightens your chest. You can be courteous and still not be healed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सासुन्ह सबनि मिली बैदेही । चरनन्हि लाग हरषु अति तेही॥ देहिं असीस बूझि कुसलाता। होइ अचल तुम्हार अहिवाता ॥
translation: जानकीजी सब सासुओं से मिलीं और उनके चरणों में लगकर उन्हें अत्यंत हर्ष हुआ। सासुएँ कुशल पूछकर आशीष दे रही हैं कि तुम्हारा सुहाग अचल हो ॥
english_translation: Janaki met all her mothers-in-law and bowed at their feet, filling them with great joy. The mothers-in-law asked after her well-being and blessed her: may your married life remain unbroken.
essence: Humility opens the door to blessing.
simple_meaning: Janaki greets all the elder women respectfully, and they bless her with wishes for a lasting marriage.
insight: It shows how humility invites care and restores harmony in a home.
modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering after a long absence, touch the elders' feet, and the whole room relaxes. Respect turns distance into blessing.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब रघुपति मुख कमल बिलोकहिं। मंगल जानि नयन जल रोकहिं॥ कनक थार आरती उतारहिं। बार बार प्रभु गात निहारहिं ॥
translation: सब माताएँ श्री रघुनाथजी का कमल सा मुखड़ा देख रही हैं। (नेत्रों से प्रेम के आँसू उमड़े आते हैं, परंतु) मंगल का समय जानकर वे आँसुओं के जल को नेत्रों में ही रोक रखती हैं। सोने के थाल से आरती उतारती हैं और बार-बार प्रभु के श्री अंगों की ओर देखती हैं ॥
english_translation: All the mothers gaze at Raghupati's lotus face. Knowing this is an auspicious moment, they hold back their tears. They wave lamps in worship from golden trays and keep looking again and again at the Lord's beautiful form.
essence: Joy so full it becomes worship.
simple_meaning: The queens look at Ram with tears of joy, but they hold those tears back because the moment is sacred. They worship him with lamps and cannot stop gazing at him.
insight: It shifts attention from words to reverent seeing, where love is expressed through gaze and offering.
modern_relevance: You finally see someone you have waited months to welcome home. You want to cry, laugh, and speak at once — but first you just look, because presence itself feels sacred.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: नाना भाँति निछावरि करहीं। परमानंद हरष उर भरहीं॥ कौसल्या पुनि पुनि रघुबीरहि। चितवति कृपासिंधु रनधीरहि ॥
translation: अनेकों प्रकार से निछावरें करती हैं और हृदय में परमानंद तथा हर्ष भर रही हैं। कौसल्याजी बार-बार कृपा के समुद्र और रणधीर श्री रघुवीर को देख रही हैं ॥
english_translation: They offer many kinds of gifts and their hearts fill with supreme bliss and joy. Kaushalya keeps looking again and again at Raghubir, the ocean of grace and the fearless warrior.
essence: Victory becomes sweetest when a mother can only keep looking.
simple_meaning: The women keep offering gifts and feeling joy, while Kaushalya keeps gazing at Ram with overflowing love.
insight: It turns victory into tenderness, showing that the deepest response to greatness is grateful love.
modern_relevance: You watch your child come home after years away, and the sight keeps undoing you. Relief, pride, and gratitude all arrive at once.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: हृदयँ बिचारति बारहिं बारा। कवन भाँति लंकापति मारा॥ अति सुकुमार जुगल मेरे बारे। निसिचर सुभट महाबल भारे ॥
translation: वे बार-बार हृदय में विचारती हैं कि इन्होंने लंकापति रावण को कैसे मारा? मेरे ये दोनों बच्चे बड़े ही सुकुमार हैं और राक्षस तो ब़ड़े भारी योद्धा और महान् बली थे ॥
english_translation: She keeps wondering in her heart, again and again: how did they kill the lord of Lanka? My two boys are so tender, while the demons were mighty warriors of great strength.
essence: Tenderness can carry a power that looks impossible until it wins.
simple_meaning: Kausalya cannot stop wondering how Rama and Lakshman defeated Ravana. She sees her sons as tender boys and Ravana's side as powerful warriors.
insight: It shifts attention from visible fragility to the hidden force that made victory possible.
modern_relevance: You watch your quiet child stand up to a bully and feel stunned afterward. The strength was always there, even if you could not see it.
speaker: Kausalya

verse_text: लछिमन अरु सीता सहित प्रभुहि बिलोकति मातु। परमानंद मगन मन पुनि पुनि पुलकित गातु ॥
translation: लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी को माता देख रही हैं। उनका मन परमानंद में मग्न है और शरीर बार-बार पुलकित हो रहा है ॥
english_translation: The mother beholds the Lord with Lakshman and Sita. Her mind is soaked in supreme joy, and her body keeps trembling with delight.
essence: Seeing Ram fills the heart so completely that the body cannot stay still.
simple_meaning: Mother Kaushalya sees Ram with Lakshman and Sita, and her heart overflows with joy. Her whole body shivers with happiness.
insight: It shows how devotion and relief can become a physical experience, not just an emotion.
modern_relevance: You spot your child at the airport after months apart, and your chest tightens before you can speak. Some reunions are felt before they are understood.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: लंकापति कपीस नल नीला। जामवंत अंगद सुभसीला॥ हनुमदादि सब बानर बीरा। धरे मनोहर मनुज सरीरा ॥
translation: लंकापति विभीषण, वानरराज सुग्रीव, नल, नील, जाम्बवान् और अंगद तथा हनुमान् जी आदि सभी उत्तम स्वभाव वाले वीर वानरों ने मनुष्यों के मनोहर शरीर धारण कर लिए ॥
english_translation: Vibhishana, king of Lanka; Sugriva, Nala, Nila, Jambavan, Angada, and Hanuman and all the noble monkey warriors took on charming human forms.
essence: The allies appear together in forms fit for celebration.
simple_meaning: Vibhishana, Sugriva, Nala, Nila, Jambavan, Angada, Hanuman, and the other monkey warriors all took beautiful human forms.
insight: It shifts attention from individual identity to the shared dignity of a united company.
modern_relevance: A wedding hall fills with people you once knew only by role or reputation, and suddenly everyone looks ready for the same joy. The scene matters more than any one face.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: भरत सनेह सील ब्रत नेमा। सादर सब बरनहिं अति प्रेमा॥ देखि नगरबासिन्ह कै रीती। सकल सराहहिं प्रभु पद प्रीती ॥
translation: वे सब भरतजी के प्रेम, सुंदर, स्वभाव (त्याग के) व्रत और नियमों की अत्यंत प्रेम से आदरपूर्वक बड़ाई कर रहे हैं और नगर वासियों की (प्रेम, शील और विनय से पूर्ण) रीति देखकर वे सब प्रभु के चरणों में उनके प्रेम की सराहना कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: They all praise Bharat's love, character, vows, and rules with deep respect. Seeing the way the city people live, they all praise their devotion to the Lord's feet.
essence: True greatness is praised through love, restraint, and humble devotion.
simple_meaning: Everyone respectfully praises Bharat's loving nature, good conduct, vows, and discipline, along with the city's devotion and humble way of living.
insight: It shifts attention from status to the character that earns genuine respect.
modern_relevance: At a family gathering, the person everyone quietly admires is not the loudest one, but the one whose restraint, loyalty, and steadiness make everyone feel safe.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि रघुपति सब सखा बोलाए। मुनि पद लागहु सकल सिखाए॥ गुर बसिष्ट कुलपूज्य हमारे। इन्ह की कृपाँ दनुज रन मारे ॥
translation: फिर श्री रघुनाथजी ने सब सखाओं को बुलाया और सबको सिखाया कि मुनि के चरणों में लगो। ये गुरु वशिष्ठजी हमारे कुलभर के पूज्य हैं। इन्हीं की कृपा से रण में राक्षस मारे गए हैं ॥
english_translation: Then Raghupati called all his companions and taught them to bow at the feet of the sage. "Vashistha, our family teacher, is worthy of worship. It is by his grace that the demons were slain in battle."
essence: Victory stays clean when you credit the grace behind it.
simple_meaning: Ram gathers his companions and reminds them to honor their teacher, Vashistha, because the victory in battle came through his grace, not their own strength alone.
insight: It shifts praise away from ego and toward gratitude, so achievement does not harden into pride.
modern_relevance: You finish a hard project and everyone wants credit to land on the loudest person in the room. Ram’s words pull the spotlight back to the mentor, the support, and the unseen help that made success possible.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: ए सब सखा सुनहु मुनि मेरे। भए समर सागर कहँ बेरे॥ मम हित लागि जन्म इन्ह हारे। भरतहु ते मोहि अधिक पिआरे ॥
translation: (फिर गुरुजी से कहा-) हे मुनि! सुनिए। ये सब मेरे सखा हैं। ये संग्राम रूपी समुद्र में मेरे लिए बेड़े (जहाज) के समान हुए। मेरे हित के लिए इन्होंने अपने जन्म तक हार दिए (अपने प्राणों तक को होम दिया) ये मुझे भरत से भी अधिक प्रिय हैं ॥
english_translation: O sage, listen: all these friends are mine. They have been like boats for me across the ocean of battle. For my sake they have given up even their lives. They are dearer to me than Bharat.
essence: Sacrifice turns friends into the boats that carry you across danger.
simple_meaning: Ram praises his friends as the ones who carried him through danger and gave everything for his welfare. He values their loyalty even above Bharat.
insight: It shifts attention from status and bloodline to the quiet people whose sacrifice actually carried you.
modern_relevance: After a crisis, you finally see who stayed when things were hard, who answered the call, who gave time and strength without keeping score. That loyalty changes how you hold them forever.
speaker: Ram

verse_text: सुनि प्रभु बचन मगन सब भए। निमिष निमिष उपजत सुख नए ॥
translation: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर सब प्रेम और आनंद में मग्न हो गए। इस प्रकार पल-पल में उन्हें नए-नए सुख उत्पन्न हो रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, everyone became absorbed in bliss. Moment by moment, new joy kept arising.
essence: Ram's words don't just please you; they keep creating joy.
simple_meaning: Ram's words fill everyone with fresh delight, and that joy keeps renewing itself every moment.
insight: It shifts attention from the speaker's command to the transforming effect of sacred speech.
modern_relevance: You hear a voice note from someone you love after a hard day, and your chest loosens before the message even ends. Some words don't just inform you — they restore you.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कौसल्या के चरनन्हि पुनि तिन्ह नायउ माथ। आसिष दीन्हे हरषि तुम्ह प्रिय मम जिमि रघुनाथ ॥
translation: फिर उन लोगों ने कौसल्याजी के चरणों में मस्तक नवाए। कौसल्याजी ने हर्षित होकर आशीषें दीं (और कहा-) तुम मुझे रघुनाथ के समान प्यारे हो ॥
english_translation: Then they bowed their heads again at Kaushalya's feet. Kaushalya, delighted, gave her blessings and said, “You are as dear to me as Raghunath himself.”
essence: Love for Ram turns his people into your own.
simple_meaning: Kaushalya blesses the visitors and says they are as dear to her as Ram himself. Their love for Ram has made them part of her own heart.
insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to shared belonging. Loving Ram changes how you see everyone connected to Him.
modern_relevance: You bring home a friend who helped you through your hardest year, and your mother greets them like family. Love for one person quietly expands the whole house.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुमन बृष्टि नभ संकुल भवन चले सुखकंद। चढ़ी अटारिन्ह देखहिं नगर नारि नर बृंद ॥
translation: आनन्दकन्द श्री रामजी अपने महल को चले, आकाश फूलों की वृष्टि से छा गया। नगर के स्त्री-पुरुषों के समूह अटारियों पर चढ़कर उनके दर्शन कर रहे हैं ॥
english_translation: Ram, the source of joy, walked toward his palace. The sky filled with showers of flowers, and men and women in the city climbed onto terraces to see him.
essence: Joy becomes visible when the whole city turns to look.
simple_meaning: Ram returns to his palace while the sky showers flowers and the city watches him from the rooftops.
insight: It shifts attention from private arrival to shared reverence.
modern_relevance: A whole neighborhood leans out of balconies for a glimpse of someone they love and trust. The street itself feels blessed because one beloved person has passed through it.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: कंचन कलस बिचित्र सँवारे। सबहिं धरे सजि निज निज द्वारे॥ बंदनवार पताका केतू। सबन्हि बनाए मंगल हेतू ॥
translation: सोने के कलशों को विचित्र रीति से (मणि-रत्नादि से) अलंकृत कर और सजाकर सब लोगों ने अपने-अपने दरवाजों पर रख लिया। सब लोगों ने मंगल के लिए बंदनवार, ध्वजा और पताकाएँ लगाईं ॥
english_translation: Golden pots, beautifully decorated with jewels, were placed at each home’s doorway. Every house was adorned with festoons, flags, and banners for the celebration.
essence: A beloved arrival turns every doorway into celebration.
simple_meaning: Everyone decorated their doorways with golden pots, festoons, flags, and banners to welcome the celebration.
insight: It shifts attention from one person’s joy to a whole community expressing welcome together.
modern_relevance: You walk into a neighborhood where every balcony has lights, flowers, and flags because someone beloved is coming home. The streets themselves seem to be smiling.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बीथीं सकल सुगंध सिंचाई। गजमनि रचि बहु चौक पुराईं। नाना भाँति सुमंगल साजे। हरषि नगर निसान बहु बाजे ॥
translation: सारी गलियाँ सुगंधित द्रवों से सिंचाई गईं। गजमुक्ताओं से रचकर बहुत सी चौकें पुराई गईं। अनेकों प्रकार के सुंदर मंगल साज सजाए गए और हर्षपूर्वक नगर में बहुत से डंके बजने लगे ॥
english_translation: All the lanes were sprinkled with fragrant liquids. Courtyards were filled and decorated with elephant pearls. Many kinds of auspicious decorations were arranged, and drums sounded joyfully throughout the city.
essence: Joy announces itself before anyone speaks.
simple_meaning: The city is being decorated for a joyful celebration. Streets are scented, courtyards are prepared, and drums sound everywhere.
insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the atmosphere devotion creates around it.
modern_relevance: You catch the smell of fresh flowers in the hallway before guests arrive. The whole house starts feeling different because something precious is coming.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ तहँ नारि निछावरि करहीं। देहिं असीस हरष उर भरहीं॥ कंचन थार आरतीं नाना। जुबतीं सजें करहिं सुभ गाना ॥ `
translation: स्त्रियाँ जहाँ-तहाँ निछावर कर रही हैं और हृदय में हर्षित होकर आशीर्वाद देती हैं। बहुत सी युवती (सौभाग्यवती) स्त्रियाँ सोने के थालों में अनेकों प्रकार की आरती सजाकर मंगलगान कर रही हैं ॥
english_translation: Women everywhere offer gifts, give blessings, and sing auspicious songs with joyful hearts. Many young women arrange different kinds of aarti on golden plates.
essence: Public joy turns into blessing, offering, and song.
simple_meaning: Women across the city are making offerings, blessing others, and singing auspicious songs with full hearts.
insight: It shows how collective joy naturally becomes ritual, song, and offering.
modern_relevance: A neighborhood that has been waiting all week finally sees the guest arrive, and people step out with flowers, lights, and song. Some moments are too full for words alone.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: करहिं आरती आरतिहर कें। रघुकुल कमल बिपिन दिनकर कें॥ पुर सोभा संपति कल्याना। निगम सेष सारदा बखाना ॥
translation: वे आर्तिहर (दुःखों को हरने वाले) और सूर्यकुल रूपी कमलवन को प्रफुल्लित करने वाले सूर्य श्री रामजी की आरती कर रही हैं। नगर की शोभा, संपत्ति और कल्याण का वेद, शेषजी और सरस्वतीजी वर्णन करते हैं- ॥
english_translation: They perform the aarti of Ram, the remover of suffering and the sun that makes the Raghu line bloom. The city's beauty, wealth, and auspiciousness are described by the Vedas, Shesha, and Saraswati.
essence: Ram's presence turns a city into blessing.
simple_meaning: People are worshipping Ram as the one who removes suffering and brings the Raghu line to full bloom. His city is so beautiful and blessed that even the Vedas, Shesha, and Saraswati cannot fully describe it.
insight: It shifts attention from the ceremony itself to the healing presence that makes celebration possible.
modern_relevance: A house fills with light when someone loved returns after a long absence. The decorations matter less than the feeling: relief, joy, and a sense that everything is finally in its place.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तेउ यह चरित देखि ठगि रहहीं। उमा तासु गुन नर किमि कहहीं ॥
translation: परंतु वे भी यह चरित्र देखकर ठगे से रह जाते हैं (स्तम्भित हो रहते हैं)। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! तब भला मनुष्य उनके गुणों को कैसे कह सकते हैं ॥
english_translation: Even they remain stunned after seeing this wondrous play. O Uma, how can any human fully speak of his qualities?
essence: Ram's greatness leaves every mind speechless.
simple_meaning: Even the most perceptive beings are left speechless by Ram's deeds. Human language cannot fully capture his qualities.
insight: It shifts attention from explaining sacred greatness to bowing before it.
modern_relevance: You watch someone quietly hold a family together through grief, and everyone around them goes still. The heart knows their greatness long before language catches up.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: नारि कुमुदिनीं अवध सर रघुपति बिरह दिनेस। अस्त भएँ बिगसत भईं निरखि राम राकेस ॥
translation: स्त्रियाँ कुमुदनी हैं, अयोध्या सरोवर है और श्री रघुनाथजी का विरह सूर्य है (इस विरह सूर्य के ताप से वे मुरझा गई थीं)। अब उस विरह रूपी सूर्य के अस्त होने पर श्री राम रूपी पूर्णचन्द्र को निरखकर वे खिल उठीं ॥
english_translation: Women are like lilies, Ayodhya is the lake, and Raghupati's separation is the sun. When that sun set, they bloomed again at the sight of Ram, the moon.
essence: Ram's return makes what love had wilted bloom again.
simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya, especially the women, had wilted in Ram's absence. Now that Ram has returned, they bloom again with joy.
insight: It turns absence and return into a living image, showing how love can wilt and revive an entire community.
modern_relevance: You walk into a home that has felt heavy for months, and the mood changes the moment the person everyone missed steps through the door.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: होहिं सगुन सुभ बिबिधि बिधि बाजहिं गगन निसान। पुर नर नारि सनाथ करि भवन चले भगवान। 9 ख॥
translation: अनेक प्रकार के शुभ शकुन हो रहे हैं, आकाश में नगाड़े बज रहे हैं। नगर के पुरुषों और स्त्रियों को सनाथ (दर्शन द्वारा कृतार्थ) करके भगवान् श्री रामचंद्रजी महल को चले ॥
english_translation: Many auspicious signs appeared, and drums sounded in the sky. Blessing the men and women of the city with their sight, Bhagavan Shri Ramchandra returned to the palace.
essence: Ram’s presence blesses a city even before he speaks.
simple_meaning: Good omens appear, heavenly drums sound, and Ram returns to the palace after giving the city’s people the blessing of his presence.
insight: It shifts attention from action alone to the blessing carried by presence itself.
modern_relevance: You leave a gathering and everyone is still quieter than before, but somehow steadier. A single gracious presence can change the mood of an entire room.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रभु जानी कैकई लजानी। प्रथम तासु गृह गए भवानी॥ ताहि प्रबोधि बहुत सुख दीन्हा। पुनि निज भवन गवन हरि कीन्हा ॥
translation: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे भवानी! प्रभु ने जान लिया कि माता कैकेयी लज्जित हो गई हैं (इसलिए), वे पहले उन्हीं के महल को गए और उन्हें समझा-बुझाकर बहुत सुख दिया। फिर श्री हरि ने अपने महल को गमन किया ॥
english_translation: Shiva says to Parvati: Knowing that Kaikeyi felt ashamed, the Lord first went to her house and comforted her greatly. Then Hari returned to his own home.
essence: Compassion reaches the ashamed before it returns home.
simple_meaning: Ram noticed Kaikeyi’s shame, went to her first, comforted her, and only then returned home.
insight: It shifts you from self-focus to restorative action after conflict.
modern_relevance: You can win an argument and still leave someone wounded. This verse remembers the deeper victory: noticing the other person’s shame and softening it first.
speaker: Shiva

verse_text: कृपासिंधु जब मंदिर गए। पुर नर नारि सुखी सब भए॥ गुर बसिष्ट द्विज लिए बुलाई। आजु सुघरी सुदिन समुदाई।2॥
translation: कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामजी जब अपने महल को गए, तब नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष सब सुखी हुए। गुरु वशिष्ठजी ने ब्राह्मणों को बुला लिया और कहा आज शुभ घड़ी, सुंदर दिन आदि सभी शुभ योग हैं ॥
english_translation: When the ocean of compassion returned to the palace, all the men and women of the city became happy. Guru Vashistha called the Brahmins and said, "Today is an auspicious hour, a beautiful day, and all signs are favorable."
essence: Ram's return restores ease before the coronation begins.
simple_meaning: Ram returns to the palace, and the whole city feels relieved. Vashistha then gathers the Brahmins and announces that the time is auspicious.
insight: It shifts attention from the ceremony itself to the peace that right order brings.
modern_relevance: The house goes quiet the moment the person everyone trusts walks back in. Even before they speak, the tension drops and everyone breathes easier.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सब द्विज देहु हरषि अनुसासन। रामचंद्र बैठहिं सिंघासन॥ मुनि बसिष्ट के बचन सुहाए। सुनत सकल बिप्रन्ह अति भाए ॥
translation: आप सब ब्राह्मण हर्षित होकर आज्ञा दीजिए, जिसमें श्री रामचंद्रजी सिंहासन पर विराजमान हों। वशिष्ठ मुनि के सुहावने वचन सुनते ही सब ब्राह्मणों को बहुत ही अच्छे लगे ॥
english_translation: Let all the Brahmins joyfully give their approval, so that Ramchandra may sit on the throne. Hearing the pleasing words of sage Vashistha, all the Brahmins were greatly pleased.
essence: Ram's kingship is welcomed through joyful consent, not force.
simple_meaning: The Brahmins are asked to gladly approve Ram's enthronement, and Vashistha's words please them all.
insight: It shifts the focus from private desire to rightful communal approval.
modern_relevance: A family finally agrees on a wedding after weeks of tension, and one calm elder's words settle everyone. Some moments need shared consent before joy can begin.
speaker: Vashistha

verse_text: कहहिं बचन मृदु बिप्र अनेका। जग अभिराम राम अभिषेका॥ अब मुनिबर बिलंब नहिं कीजै। महाराज कहँ तिलक करीजै ॥
translation: वे सब अनेकों ब्राह्मण कोमल वचन कहने लगे कि श्री रामजी का राज्याभिषेक संपूर्ण जगत को आनंद देने वाला है। हे मुनिश्रेष्ठ! अब विलंब न कीजिए और महाराज का तिलक शीघ्र कीजिए ॥
english_translation: Many brahmins spoke gently: "Ram's coronation will delight the whole world. O great sage, do not delay now. Quickly perform the tilak for the king."
essence: Joy should not be held back once the moment is ripe.
simple_meaning: The priests ask Vashishtha to stop delaying and begin Ram's coronation right away, saying it will bring joy to the whole world.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony as delay to ceremony as timely fulfilment.
modern_relevance: You have everyone assembled, the room is ready, and the only thing left is to begin. Sometimes the kindest move is simply not to stall the moment.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: तब मुनि कहेउ सुमंत्र सन सुनत चलेउ हरषाइ। रथ अनेक बहु बाजि गज तुरत सँवारे जाइ ॥
translation: तब मुनि ने सुमन्त्रजी से कहा, वे सुनते ही हर्षित होकर चले। उन्होंने तुरंत ही जाकर अनेकों रथ, घोड़े और हाथी सजाए, ॥
english_translation: Then the sage spoke to Sumantra. Hearing it, he went off rejoicing and quickly arranged many chariots, horses, and elephants.
essence: Joyful obedience turns preparation into worship.
simple_meaning: Sumantra is told to act, and he immediately goes to prepare the royal vehicles and animals with joy.
insight: It shows prompt, joyful service in action rather than reflection.
modern_relevance: A message comes through while you're still tying your shoes, and you move without delay. Some tasks become sacred simply because you answer them fully.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जहँ तहँ धावन पठइ पुनि मंगल द्रब्य मगाइ। हरष समेत बसिष्ट पद पुनि सिरु नायउ आइ ॥
translation: और जहाँ-तहाँ (सूचना देने वाले) दूतों को भेजकर मांगलिक वस्तुएँ मँगाकर फिर हर्ष के साथ आकर वशिष्ठजी के चरणों में सिर नवाया ॥
english_translation: He sent messengers in every direction, brought auspicious items, and then returned joyfully to bow his head at Vashishtha's feet.
essence: Joy becomes rightful only after you bow to what is higher than ceremony.
simple_meaning: The preparations moved quickly and joyfully. Messengers were sent out, auspicious items were gathered, and respect was shown to Vashishtha before the ceremony.
insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle to the humility that makes celebration worthy.
modern_relevance: Before a wedding, launch, or housewarming, someone is still running around for flowers, gifts, and the right arrangements. The real tone of the day is set by whether respect comes before excitement.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अवधपुरी अति रुचिर बनाई। देवन्ह सुमन बृष्टि झरि लाई॥ राम कहा सेवकन्ह बुलाई। प्रथम सखन्ह अन्हवावहु जाई ॥
translation: अवधपुरी बहुत ही सुंदर सजाई गई। देवताओं ने पुष्पों की वर्षा की झड़ी लगा दी। श्री रामचंद्रजी ने सेवकों को बुलाकर कहा कि तुम लोग जाकर पहले मेरे सखाओं को स्नान कराओ ॥
english_translation: Ayodhya was made beautifully splendid. The deities showered a stream of flowers. Ram called the servants and said, "Go first and bathe my friends."
essence: Honor others first, even when everyone is honoring you.
simple_meaning: Ayodhya is beautifully decorated, flowers fall from the sky, and Ram tells his servants to bathe his friends first.
insight: It shifts attention from status to service, showing that true leadership begins by honoring others.
modern_relevance: At a wedding, everyone waits for the guest of honor, but you quietly make sure your friend who traveled far gets water first. That small choice reveals the kind of heart Ram has.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनत बचन जहँ तहँ जन धाए। सुग्रीवादि तुरत अन्हवाए॥ पुनि करुनानिधि भरतु हँकारे। निज कर राम जटा निरुआरे ॥
translation: भगवान् के वचन सुनते ही सेवक जहाँ-तहाँ दौड़े और तुरंत ही उन्होंने सुग्रीवादि को स्नान कराया। फिर करुणानिधान श्री रामजी ने भरतजी को बुलाया और उनकी जटाओं को अपने हाथों से सुलझाया ॥
english_translation: Hearing the command, the servants ran everywhere and quickly bathed Sugriva and the others. Then the ocean of compassion, Ram, called Bharat and untangled his matted hair with his own hands.
essence: True love notices hardship and responds with care.
simple_meaning: Ram’s command is carried out at once. Sugriva and the others are bathed, and Ram lovingly untangles Bharat’s matted hair with his own hands.
insight: It shifts devotion from ceremony to direct, tender service.
modern_relevance: You finally see someone you love after a long, hard season, and the first thing you do is help them clean up, sit down, and breathe.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: अन्हवाए प्रभु तीनिउ भाई। भगत बछल कृपाल रघुराई॥ भरत भाग्य प्रभु कोमलताई। सेष कोटि सत सकहिं न गाई ॥
translation: तदनन्तर भक्त वत्सल कृपालु प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी ने तीनों भाइयों को स्नान कराया। भरतजी का भाग्य और प्रभु की कोमलता का वर्णन अरबों शेषजी भी नहीं कर सकते ॥
english_translation: Then the compassionate Lord, devoted to his devotees, bathed all three brothers. No one, not even countless Sheshas, can fully describe Bharat's fortune or the Lord's tenderness.
essence: True greatness shows itself as tender care for devotees.
simple_meaning: Ram lovingly bathes all three brothers, and the verse says Bharat's good fortune and Ram's tenderness are beyond description.
insight: It shifts attention from status to being cherished, and from grandeur to intimate care.
modern_relevance: You wash off a long, exhausting day and someone you love quietly brings you water, towel, and care without being asked. That small tenderness can feel larger than praise.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: पुनि निज जटा राम बिबराए। गुर अनुसासन मागि नहाए॥ करि मज्जन प्रभु भूषन साजे। अंग अनंग देखि सत लाजे ॥
translation: फिर श्री रामजी ने अपनी जटाएँ खोलीं और गुरुजी की आज्ञा माँगकर स्नान किया। स्नान करके प्रभु ने आभूषण धारण किए। उनके (सुशोभित) अंगों को देखकर सैकड़ों (असंख्य) कामदेव लजा गए ॥
english_translation: Then Ram opened his own matted locks and, seeking the guru's permission, bathed. After bathing, the Lord adorned himself with ornaments. Seeing his radiant limbs, even countless gods of desire felt ashamed.
essence: Grace becomes complete when power bows to guidance.
simple_meaning: Ram first asks his teacher's permission, then bathes and dresses himself beautifully. His radiance is so great that even countless gods of desire are humbled.
insight: It shifts attention from outward beauty to the discipline and reverence that make beauty worthy.
modern_relevance: You finally get dressed for a long-awaited ceremony, but you still pause to check with the elder who taught you how to carry yourself. Real polish begins with humility.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सासुन्ह सादर जानकिहि मज्जन तुरत कराइ। दिब्य बसन बर भूषन अँग अँग सजे बनाइ ॥
translation: (इधर) सासुओं ने जानकीजी को आदर के साथ तुरंत ही स्नान कराके उनके अंग-अंग में दिव्य वस्त्र और श्रेष्ठ आभूषण भली-भाँति सजा दिए (पहना दिए) ॥
english_translation: The mothers respectfully bathed Janaki at once and adorned her body with divine clothes and fine ornaments.
essence: Love can be shown through the way you prepare someone to be honoured.
simple_meaning: The household women quickly bathe Sita and dress her beautifully in fine clothes and ornaments.
insight: It shifts attention to the dignity hidden inside ordinary acts of care.
modern_relevance: A family gets ready for a wedding, and everyone moves around one person with quiet care. That kind of respectful attention can make someone feel truly received.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: राम बाम दिसि सोभति रमा रूप गुन खानि। देखि मातु सब हरषीं जन्म सुफल निज जानि ॥
translation: श्री राम के बायीं ओर रूप और गुणों की खान रमा (श्री जानकीजी) शोभित हो रही हैं। उन्हें देखकर सब माताएँ अपना जन्म (जीवन) सफल समझकर हर्षित हुईं ॥
english_translation: Ram shines on the left, and Rama, the mine of beauty and virtues, shines on his left. Seeing them, all the mothers felt their lives had become fruitful and rejoiced.
essence: True beauty makes even the watcher feel fulfilled.
simple_meaning: Ram stands beside Sita in shining beauty, and the mothers watching them feel their lives have been fulfilled.
insight: It shifts attention from possession to blessed witnessing: seeing wholeness can itself be enough.
modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of two people deeply right for each other, and something in you relaxes. Beauty, love, and rightness can make the heart feel its work is done.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: सुनु खगेस तेहि अवसर ब्रह्मा सिव मुनि बृंद। चढ़ि बिमान आए सब सुर देखन सुखकंद ॥
translation: (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं-) हे पक्षीराज गरुड़जी! सुनिए, उस समय ब्रह्माजी, शिवजी और मुनियों के समूह तथा विमानों पर चढ़कर सब देवता आनंदकंद भगवान् के दर्शन करने के लिए आए ॥
english_translation: Listen, lord of birds: at that time Brahma, Shiva, and groups of sages, along with all the radiant beings riding in celestial vehicles, came to see the source of joy.
essence: Even the highest beings come simply to behold Ram.
simple_meaning: At that moment, Brahma, Shiva, sages, and other radiant beings came in celestial vehicles to see Ram.
insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to reverence: true greatness is recognized, not performed.
modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when someone truly admirable walks in. No announcement is needed; people simply turn, because presence itself has weight.
speaker: Kak Bhushundi

verse_text: प्रभु बिलोकि मुनि मन अनुरागा। तुरत दिब्य सिंघासन मागा॥ रबि सम तेज सो बरनि न जाई। बैठे राम द्विजन्ह सिरु नाई ॥
translation: प्रभु को देखकर मुनि वशिष्ठजी के मन में प्रेम भर आया। उन्होंने तुरंत ही दिव्य सिंहासन मँगवाया, जिसका तेज सूर्य के समान था। उसका सौंदर्य वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। ब्राह्मणों को सिर नवाकर श्री रामचंद्रजी उस पर विराज गए ॥
english_translation: Seeing the Lord, Vashishtha’s heart filled with love. He quickly asked for a divine throne, bright as the sun. Its brilliance could not be described. Bowing to the priests, Ram sat upon it.
essence: Real love for Ram naturally becomes reverent action.
simple_meaning: Vashishtha sees Ram, feels deep love, and arranges a radiant divine throne for him. Ram bows to the priests and sits down.
insight: It turns admiration into respectful action, showing that true honour is expressed, not just felt.
modern_relevance: At a wedding hall, everyone is waiting for the guest of honour. The host sees the person arrive, forgets the protocol, and moves with genuine reverence. Respect is no longer performance; it becomes instinct.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: जनकसुता समेत रघुराई। पेखि प्रहरषे मुनि समुदाई॥ बेद मंत्र तब द्विजन्ह उचारे। नभ सुर मुनि जय जयति पुकारे ॥
translation: श्री जानकीजी के सहित रघुनाथजी को देखकर मुनियों का समुदाय अत्यंत ही हर्षित हुआ। तब ब्राह्मणों ने वेदमंत्रों का उच्चारण किया। आकाश में देवता और मुनि 'जय, हो, जय हो' ऐसी पुकार करने लगे ॥
english_translation: Seeing Ram together with Sita, the gathered sages felt great joy. Then the learned priests chanted Vedic mantras, and in the sky the devas and sages cried, “Victory, victory!”
essence: Joy becomes public when Ram and Sita appear together.
simple_meaning: The sages rejoice at seeing Ram and Sita together. The priests chant sacred mantras, and the heavenly beings join in cries of victory.
insight: It shifts attention from analysis to shared celebration and reverence for a blessed arrival.
modern_relevance: A bride and groom walk into a room and everyone goes quiet for a second, then smiles. The moment itself carries the happiness; no explanation is needed.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: प्रथम तिलक बसिष्ट मुनि कीन्हा। पुनि सब बिप्रन्ह आयसु दीन्हा॥ सुत बिलोकि हरषीं महतारी। बार बार आरती उतारी ॥
translation: (सबसे) पहले मुनि वशिष्ठजी ने तिलक किया। फिर उन्होंने सब ब्राह्मणों को (तिलक करने की) आज्ञा दी। पुत्र को राजसिंहासन पर देखकर माताएँ हर्षित हुईं और उन्होंने बार-बार आरती उतारी ॥
english_translation: First, Vashishtha the sage performed the tilak. Then he gave all the priests the order. Seeing their son on the royal seat, the mothers were overjoyed and kept waving the aarti again and again.
essence: Love celebrates most when blessing becomes visible.
simple_meaning: Vashishtha marks Ram for kingship, then the priests follow. The mothers see their son on the throne and celebrate with repeated aarti.
insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the tenderness of being recognized after long waiting.
modern_relevance: You watch your child walk across the stage in a borrowed gown, and suddenly years of care feel visible at once. Pride, relief, and blessing spill out together.
speaker: Narrator

verse_text: बिप्रन्ह दान बिबिधि बिधि दीन्हे। जाचक सकल अजाचक कीन्हे॥ सिंघासन पर त्रिभुअन साईं। देखि सुरन्ह दुंदुभीं बजाईं ॥
translation: उन्होंने ब्राह्मणों को अनेकों प्रकार के दान दिए और संपूर्ण याचकों को अयाचक बना दिया (मालामाल कर दिया)। त्रिभुवन के स्वामी श्री रामचंद्रजी को (अयोध्या के) सिंहासन पर (विराजित) देखकर देवताओं ने नगाड़े बजाए ॥
